Its political system was based on medieval landlordism.
5.x: The Mature Harappan culture was urban, whereas the Rigvedic culture was predominantly pastoral. The absence of horse, chariot and iron in the Mature Harappan context is also cited in this argument.
5.tq: Use the urban–pastoral contrast to infer the cultural distinction.
xs: The **urban** Harappan culture contrasted with the **pastoral** Rigvedic culture — option **(3)**.
This contrast is the core of the **non-Aryan/pre-Vedic** argument.
**Landlordism** belongs to the **Medieval** period, not the Harappans.
xa: **Continuity view**: **fire altars** and **pipal worship** link the two.
PYQ (**UPPSC 2020**): Indus — **urban**; Rigvedic — **pastoral**; Later Vedic — **agrarian**; Medieval — **landlordism**.
**Seven fire altars** were found at **Kalibangan**; fire altars also at **Lothal**.

5.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the broad social-economic character attributed to the four periods?
o: Indus Valley—urban; Rigvedic—pastoral; Later Vedic—agrarian; Medieval—landlordism
Indus Valley—agrarian; Rigvedic—landlordism; Later Vedic—urban; Medieval—pastoral
Indus Valley—landlordism; Rigvedic—agrarian; Later Vedic—pastoral; Medieval—urban
Indus Valley—pastoral; Rigvedic—urban; Later Vedic—landlordism; Medieval—agrarian
5.x: The stated comparison is: Indus Valley—urban, Rigvedic—pastoral, Later Vedic—agrarian and Medieval—landlordism.
5.tq: Compare all four categories in sequence and reject the options that reverse adjacent stages.
xs: **Indus Valley—urban; Rigvedic—pastoral; Later Vedic—agrarian; Medieval—landlordism** — option **(1)** (**UPPSC 2020**).
The **urban** vs **pastoral** contrast underlies the **non-Aryan/pre-Vedic** view of the Harappans.
xa: Continuity view: **fire altars** and **pipal worship**.
The IVC marks the **first urbanisation in India**.
Mature phase (**2600-1900 BCE**): **planned cities**, **1:2:4 bricks**, **uniform weights**.

5.s: The highest concentration of Harappan settlements was found in which geographical system?
5.x: The Ghaggar–Hakra system had the highest concentration of settlements, with about 250 sites, of which six were cities.
5.tq: Associate the quantitative settlement concentration with the correct river system.
xs: Most settlements lie in the **Ghaggar-Hakra system** — option **(1)**.
Of about **250** sites, **6** were cities.
xa: Scholars stressing these sites use the name "**Sindhu-Sarasvati**".
**Kalibangan** lies on the **Ghaggar**; **Rakhigarhi**, **Mitathal**, **Balu** in the Ghaggar-Hakra basin.
Extent: about **13 lakh sq km**; population about **5 million**.
⚠ Some notes give ~**8 lakh sq km** for the extent.

5.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Boundary site)
a. Manda
b. Daimabad
c. Alamgirpur
d. Sutkagendor

List-II (Direction)
i. East
ii. South
iii. West
iv. North
5.x: Manda is the northern site, Daimabad the southern site, Alamgirpur the eastern site and Sutkagendor the western site.
5.tq: Start from the sure directional pair and eliminate codes containing a wrong boundary.
xs: Correct code is **a–iv, b–ii, c–i, d–iii** — option **(1)**.
**Manda** (J&K) = **North**; **Daimabad** (Maharashtra) = **South**.
**Alamgirpur** (W. UP) = **East**; **Sutkagendor** (Makran coast) = **West**.
xa: ⚠ **N - S - E - W** = **Manda - Daimabad - Alamgirpur - Sutkagendor**.
**Manda** is on the **Chenab**; **Daimabad** on the **Pravara** (Ahmednagar); **Alamgirpur** on the **Hindon** (Meerut).
Eastern limit: some notes give **Rakhigarhi** or **Ropar** instead of Alamgirpur.
**Alamgirpur** as eastern site was asked in **UPPSC 2023**.

5.s: The eastern boundary of the Harappan Civilisation is generally represented by:
5.x: Alamgirpur in western Uttar Pradesh is the standard eastern boundary site. Rakhigarhi and Ropar are sometimes cited in alternative listings, but the standard answer is Alamgirpur.
5.tq: Resolve a known boundary-site confusion by applying the standard directional classification.
xs: The standard eastern limit is **Alamgirpur** in **western UP** — option **(4)** (**UPPSC 2023**).
**Rakhigarhi** and **Ropar** appear only in some notes as the eastern limit.
**Manda** (J&K) is the **northern** limit.
xa: **Alamgirpur** lies on the **Hindon** in **Meerut**; it is a **Late phase** site.
⚠ **N - S - E - W** = **Manda - Daimabad - Alamgirpur - Sutkagendor**.
Other UP sites: **Mandi** (Muzaffarnagar) and **Hulas** (Saharanpur).

5.s: Sutkagendor, the western boundary site of the Harappan Civilisation, is situated on the:
5.x: Sutkagendor is located on the Makran coast in Balochistan, in present-day Pakistan.
5.tq: Discriminate between coastal regions by linking the site with its province.
xs: **Sutkagendor** lies on the **Makran coast** of **Balochistan**, Pakistan — option **(3)**.
It is the **westernmost** coastal town / port.
xa: ⚠ Some notes place Sutkagendor in **Sindh**.
⚠ **N - S - E - W** = **Manda - Daimabad - Alamgirpur - Sutkagendor**.
**Magan** (a Mesopotamian trade stop) = **Oman/Makran**.
Other Pakistan sites: **Harappa**, **Mohenjodaro**, **Chanhudaro**, **Kot Diji**, **Amri**, **Balakot**.

5.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the geographical extent of the Harappan Civilisation is correct?
o: It covered about 1.3 million square kilometres and had an estimated population of about five million.
It was confined to the Indus valley and did not extend towards the Ghaggar-Hakra region.
It covered less than 1 lakh square kilometres and had a population of about one million.
It covered about 5 million square kilometres and had a population of about thirteen lakh.
5.x: The civilisation is estimated to have covered about 1.3 million square kilometres and supported about five million people. Many settlements were located along the Ghaggar-Hakra system.
5.tq: Match the correct area and population combination while rejecting reversed figures.
xs: It covered about **1.3 million sq km** with about **five million** people — option **(1)**.
It was not confined to the Indus: most settlements lie in the **Ghaggar-Hakra** system.
xa: **1.3 million sq km** = **13 lakh sq km**; ⚠ some notes say ~**8 lakh sq km**.
It was the **largest Bronze Age civilisation** by area — larger than **Egypt** and **Mesopotamia**.
Of ~**250** sites, **6** were cities.
Limits: **Manda** (N), **Daimabad** (S), **Alamgirpur** (E), **Sutkagendor** (W).

5.s: Lothal is situated at the confluence of which rivers?
5.x: Lothal lies at the Bhogava–Sabarmati confluence in Ahmedabad district of Gujarat, near the head of the Gulf of Cambay.
5.tq: Test the distinctive river association of a site rather than its general state location.
xs: **Lothal** lies at the confluence of the **Bhogava and Sabarmati** — option **(3)**.
It is in **Ahmedabad** district, Gujarat, at the head of the **Gulf of Cambay**.
**Kalibangan** is on the **Ghaggar**; **Ropar** on the **Sutlej**; **Manda** on the **Chenab**.
xa: ⚠ **Harappa** = **Ravi**; **Mohenjodaro** = **Indus**; **Ropar** = **Sutlej**; **Alamgirpur** = **Hindon**; **Banawali** = **Rangoi**.
Lothal: **dockyard** (world's first **tidal port**), **bead factory**, **rice husks**, **Persian Gulf seal**.
Lothal is "**Mini Harappa**", excavated by **S. R. Rao**.
Indian site among Harappa, Kot Bala, Lothal, Mehrgarh = **Lothal** (**APPSC 2018**).

5.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. Kalibangan — Ghaggar — Hanumangarh
b. Ropar — Sutlej — Punjab
c. Alamgirpur — Hindon — Meerut
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
5.x: All three pairs are correct. Kalibangan is in Hanumangarh, Rajasthan; Ropar is on the Sutlej in Punjab; and Alamgirpur is on the Hindon in Meerut, Uttar Pradesh.
5.tq: Check each site against both its river and present district before choosing the code.
xs: All three pairs **a, b and c** are correct — option **(4)**.
a: **Kalibangan** — **Ghaggar** — **Hanumangarh**, Rajasthan.
b: **Ropar** (Rupnagar) — **Sutlej** — **Punjab** (India).
c: **Alamgirpur** — **Hindon** — **Meerut**, UP.
xa: Older notes put Kalibangan in **Ganganagar**, from which Hanumangarh was carved.
"Kalibangan is located in" — **Hanumangarh** (**APPSC 2018**).
**Banawali** is on the **Rangoi**; **Harappa** on the **Ravi**.
**Ropar** yielded a **dog buried with a human**.

5.s: Which of the following sites is situated in Jammu and Kashmir?
5.x: Manda is located on the Chenab in Jammu and Kashmir. Daimabad is in Maharashtra, Padri in Gujarat and Banawali in Haryana.
5.tq: Use state-based elimination among geographically distinct Harappan sites.
xs: **Manda**, on the **Chenab**, is in **Jammu and Kashmir** — option **(4)**.
**Daimabad** is in **Maharashtra**; **Padri** in **Gujarat**; **Banawali** in **Haryana**.
xa: Manda is the **northern** boundary site.
PYQ (**UPPSC 2020**): **Balu** - Haryana, **Manda** - J&K, **Padri** - Gujarat, **Hulas** - UP.
**Daimabad** (on the **Pravara**, **Ahmednagar**) is the **southern** limit.

5.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Site)
A. Rakhigarhi
B. Banawali
C. Mandi
D. Dholavira
List-II (Present location)
1. Kutch, Gujarat
2. Hisar district, Haryana
3. Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh
4. Hisar–Fatehabad region, Haryana
Select the correct answer using the code below.
5.x: Rakhigarhi is in Hisar district, Banawali in the Hisar–Fatehabad region, Mandi in Muzaffarnagar and Dholavira in Kutch.
5.tq: Start with the distinctive Kutch and Muzaffarnagar locations, then resolve the Haryana pair.
xs: Correct code is **A-2, B-4, C-3, D-1** — option **(1)**.
**Rakhigarhi** — **Hisar district**; **Banawali** — **Hisar-Fatehabad** region (now **Fatehabad** district).
**Mandi** — **Muzaffarnagar**, UP; **Dholavira** — **Kutch**, Gujarat.
xa: **Mandi** yielded a **hoard of gold ornaments**.
**Surkotada** is also in **Kutch**.
**Rakhigarhi** is the **largest Harappan site in India**.
**Banawali** is on the **Rangoi**, excavated by **R. S. Bisht** (**1973-74**).

5.s: Which one of the following States and site combinations is NOT correctly matched?
5.x: Rakhigarhi is in Haryana, not Rajasthan. Kalibangan is the site listed for Rajasthan.
5.tq: Use the state-wise concentration table and identify the swapped site.
xs: **Rakhigarhi** is in **Haryana**, not Rajasthan — the wrong pair is option **(4)**.
**Mitathal** is in **Haryana**; **Daimabad** in **Maharashtra**; **Rangpur** in Saurashtra, **Gujarat**.
**Kalibangan** is the site listed for **Rajasthan**.
xa: Haryana sites: **Rakhigarhi**, **Banawali**, **Mitathal**.
Gujarat sites: **Lothal**, **Dholavira**, **Surkotada**, **Rangpur**, **Rojdi**, **Prabhas Patan**, **Desalpur**.
**Rangpur** lies on the **Bhadar**; **Daimabad** on the **Pravara**.

5.s:
Which of the following sites are located in present-day Pakistan?
1. Harappa
2. Mohenjodaro
3. Chanhudaro
4. Lothal
5.x: Harappa, Mohenjodaro and Chanhudaro are in Pakistan. Lothal is located in Gujarat, India.
5.tq: Classify each site by present national boundary, not by its ancient cultural association.
xs: **Harappa**, **Mohenjodaro** and **Chanhudaro** are in Pakistan — **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
**Lothal** is in **Gujarat** (Ahmedabad district), India.
xa: Other Pakistan sites: **Kot Diji**, **Amri**, **Sutkagendor**, **Balakot** (Kot Bala).
**Harappa** is in Punjab (Pakistan) on the **Ravi**; **Mohenjodaro** and **Chanhudaro** in **Sindh** on the **Indus**.
Indian site among Harappa, Kot Bala, Lothal, Mehrgarh = **Lothal** (**APPSC 2018**).
**Mohenjodaro** is the largest site in Pakistan.

5.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Harappan sites listed in Uttar Pradesh?
o: Rakhigarhi and Banawali are located in Uttar Pradesh.
Dholavira and Surkotada are located in Uttar Pradesh.
Kalibangan and Alamgirpur are both located in Uttar Pradesh.
Mandi and Hulas are located in Uttar Pradesh.
5.x: Mandi is in Muzaffarnagar and Hulas in Saharanpur, both in Uttar Pradesh. Rakhigarhi and Banawali are in Haryana, while Dholavira and Surkotada are in Gujarat.
5.tq: Use paired regional identification and eliminate sites belonging to Haryana, Gujarat and Rajasthan.
xs: **Mandi** and **Hulas** are in **Uttar Pradesh** — option **(4)** (**UPPSC 2025, 2021**).
**Rakhigarhi** and **Banawali** are in **Haryana**.
**Dholavira** and **Surkotada** are in **Gujarat** (Kutch).
**Kalibangan** is in **Rajasthan**; only **Alamgirpur** of that pair is in UP.
xa: **Mandi** = Muzaffarnagar (hoard of **gold ornaments**); **Hulas** = **Saharanpur**.
**Alamgirpur** (Meerut, on the **Hindon**) is the **easternmost** site.

5.s: Surkotada is particularly associated with which archaeological finding?
o: Horse bones, though the identification is disputed
The earliest known gold coin hoard
5.x: Surkotada is a fortified Harappan site in Kutch associated with horse bones; the interpretation is disputed.
5.tq: Identify the distinctive but qualified finding and retain the caution in the wording.
xs: **Surkotada** is linked to **horse bones**, though their identification is **disputed** — option **(3)**.
A **Mauryan copper-plate inscription** belongs to **Sohgaura**, a non-Harappan site.
xa: Surkotada is a **fortified** site in **Kutch**, Gujarat, with a **circular mud-brick fort**.
It was excavated by **J. P. Joshi** in **1964**.
**Mandi** (UP) yielded a **hoard of gold ornaments**.

5.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
A. Sutkagendor — Harappan westernmost coastal town
B. Sohgaura — Mauryan copper-plate site
C. Pataliputra — Harappan city
D. Mehrgarh — Neolithic site
5.x: A, B and D are correct. Pataliputra was a later Magadhan and Mauryan capital, not a Harappan city.
5.tq: Spot the wrong civilizational classification and select the combination of correct pairs.
xs: Pairs **A, B and D** are correct — option **(2)**.
A: **Sutkagendor** — Harappan **westernmost** coastal town / port, Makran coast.
B: **Sohgaura** (Gorakhpur) — **Mauryan copper-plate** inscription site, not Harappan.
C wrong: **Pataliputra** was a later **Magadhan/Mauryan capital**. D: **Mehrgarh** — **Neolithic** (c. **7000 BCE**).
xa: ⚠ **APPSC G2 2024** "not a Harappan site": key "Rakhigarhi" doubtful; only non-Harappan option = **Sohgaura**.
⚠ **Rakhigarhi** = Harappan (largest in India); **Sohgaura** = Mauryan.
**Alamgirpur** (Late phase) is the **easternmost** Harappan site.

5.s: Which one of the following sites is associated with both pre-Harappan and Harappan levels?
5.x: Kot Diji has both pre-Harappan and Harappan levels. Sohgaura is associated with a Mauryan-age copper plate and is not a Harappan site.
5.tq: Use the chronological-level distinction rather than the site's general regional location.
xs: **Kot Diji** has both **pre-Harappan** and **Harappan** levels — option **(1)**.
Kot Diji is an **Early Harappan** (**3300-2600 BCE**) site, on the **Indus** in **Sindh**.
**Sohgaura** is a **Mauryan** copper-plate site, **not Harappan**.
xa: Other Early Harappan sites: **Amri** and **Sothi-Siswal**.
**Siswal** is now one of Haryana's **seven** protected Harappan sites.
⚠ **Rakhigarhi** = Harappan (largest in India); **Sohgaura** = not Harappan.

5.s: Rakhigarhi is notable because it is regarded as which of the following?
o: The largest Harappan site in India
5.x: Rakhigarhi is identified as the largest Harappan site in India and is located in Haryana.
5.tq: Match the site with its size-based distinction rather than its river basin alone.
xs: **Rakhigarhi** is the **largest Harappan site in India** — option **(2)**.
The **westernmost** port is **Sutkagendor**; the non-Harappan Mauryan site is **Sohgaura**.
xa: Rakhigarhi lies in **Hisar district**, Haryana, in the **Ghaggar-Hakra** basin.
It was excavated by **Amarendra Nath** (**1997**).
It is on the UNESCO **Tentative List**; **Mohenjodaro** is the largest site in Pakistan.
It yielded a **4,500-year-old skeleton** and an **ancient DNA** study.

5.s: Dholavira was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in:
5.x: Dholavira was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021.
5.tq: Test the year directly using four closely spaced alternatives.
xs: **Dholavira** was inscribed as a **UNESCO WHS** in **2021** — option **(4)**.
It was India's **40th** and Gujarat's **4th** World Heritage Site.
xa: It is the **first IVC site in India** listed and the only inscribed Harappan site.
Its listing was helped by the **absence of encroachment**.
**Mohenjo-daro** has been a UNESCO site since **1980**; **Rakhigarhi** is only on the **Tentative List**.
It was among the **Budget 2020** five iconic archaeological sites.

5.s:
With reference to Dholavira's UNESCO status, consider the following statements:
1. It became India's 40th UNESCO World Heritage Site.
2. It became Gujarat's fourth UNESCO World Heritage Site.
3. It was the first Indus Valley Civilisation site in India to be listed.
4. It is the only inscribed Harappan site, while Rakhigarhi is on the Tentative List.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
5.x: All four statements are correct. Dholavira was India's 40th and Gujarat's fourth such site, the first Indian IVC site listed, and the only inscribed Harappan site; Rakhigarhi is on the Tentative List.
5.tq: Check each numbered UNESCO-status detail before selecting the comprehensive code.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
1 and 2: Dholavira (**2021**) was India's **40th** and Gujarat's **4th** WHS.
3: It was the **first IVC site in India** to be listed.
4: It is the **only inscribed Harappan site**; **Rakhigarhi** is on the **Tentative List**.
xa: Listing was helped by the **absence of encroachment**.
⚠ Dholavira = inscribed (**2021**); Rakhigarhi = only tentative.
Dholavira is the **fifth-largest** IVC city.
**Mohenjo-daro** (Pakistan) has been a UNESCO site since **1980**.

5.s: Which one of the following was NOT among the five iconic archaeological sites named in the Union Budget of 2020?
5.x: The five sites were Rakhigarhi, Hastinapur, Shivsagar, Dholavira and Adichanallur. Mohenjodaro was not included in that list.
5.tq: Find the outsider from a fixed list by checking every listed member.
xs: **Mohenjodaro** was not among the **Budget 2020** iconic sites — option **(2)**.
The five were **Rakhigarhi**, **Hastinapur**, **Shivsagar**, **Dholavira** and **Adichanallur**.
xa: Of the five, **Rakhigarhi** and **Dholavira** are Harappan sites.
**Mohenjodaro** is in **Sindh**, Pakistan; a UNESCO site since **1980**.
⚠ Dholavira = UNESCO inscribed (**2021**); Rakhigarhi = only tentative.

5.s: Which of the following pairs of Harappan sites was declared protected by Haryana under the Haryana Ancient and Historical Monuments Act, 1964?
5.x: Haryana declared Tighrana and Mitathal protected sites under the Haryana Ancient and Historical Monuments Act, 1964. Both are in Bhiwani district and are about 4,400 years old.
5.tq: Match the newly protected sites with the state law and location.
xs: Haryana declared **Tighrana and Mitathal** protected under the **1964** Act — option **(1)** (Jun **2026**).
Both are in **Bhiwani district** and about **4,400** years old.
**Dholavira** and **Lothal** are in **Gujarat**; **Manda**, **Sutkagendor**, **Alamgirpur**, **Daimabad** lie outside Haryana.
xa: Haryana now has **seven** protected Harappan sites.
They are **Rakhigarhi**, **Banawali**, **Bhirrana**, **Kunal**, **Siswal**, **Mitathal**, **Tighrana**.
Mitathal lies in the **Ghaggar-Hakra** basin.

5.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Mohenjo-daro is inscribed as a UNESCO site
B. Harappa is discovered as the first Indus Valley Civilization site
C. Dholavira becomes the first Indus Valley Civilization site on the UNESCO list
D. Tighrana and Mitathal are notified as protected sites by Haryana
5.x: Harappa was discovered in 1921, Mohenjo-daro became a UNESCO site in 1980, Dholavira later became the first IVC site on the UNESCO list, and Tighrana and Mitathal were protected in June 2026.
5.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the UNESCO milestones between them.
xs: Correct order is **B, A, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**B**: **Harappa** discovered (**1921**); **A**: **Mohenjo-daro** a UNESCO site (**1980**).
**C**: **Dholavira** on the UNESCO list (**2021**); **D**: **Tighrana** and **Mitathal** protected (Jun **2026**).
xa: Dholavira was India's **40th** WHS; **Rakhigarhi** is on the **Tentative List**.
Haryana now has **seven** protected Harappan sites.
ASI moved Rakhigarhi's skeletons to the **Anthropological Survey of India** (**23 Jun 2026**).

5.s: Which one of the following sites has yielded evidence of a ten-sign inscription displayed on a signboard?
5.x: Dholavira is known for its large signboard bearing a ten-sign inscription.
5.tq: Use the unique site-specific finding to eliminate nearby Harappan sites.
xs: **Dholavira** yielded a **signboard** with a **10-sign inscription** — option **(1)**.
**Ropar** is known for a **dog buried with a human**; **Rakhigarhi** for a **4,500-year-old skeleton**.
**Banawali** is known for a **terracotta toy plough**.
xa: Dholavira also has **water reservoirs** and a **three-part town**.
⚠ **Dockyard** = Lothal; **signboard** = Dholavira; **no citadel** = Chanhudaro.
Dholavira is the **fifth-largest** IVC city; local name **Kotada**.

5.s: The discovery of rice husks, fire altars, a Persian Gulf seal and an ivory scale is associated with which Harappan site?
5.x: Lothal has yielded rice husks, fire altars, a Persian Gulf seal and an ivory scale, in addition to its bead-making activity.
5.tq: Cluster several distinctive findings around their common site.
xs: **Lothal** yielded **rice husks**, **fire altars**, a **Persian Gulf seal** and an **ivory scale** — option **(2)**.
**Kalibangan** is known for a **ploughed field** and **seven fire altars**.
**Harappa** for **six granaries** and **Cemetery H**; **Chanhudaro** for a **bead factory** and **no citadel**.
xa: Lothal also had a **dockyard** (world's first **tidal port**) and a **bead factory**.
**Rangpur** too yielded **rice**.
Lothal is "**Mini Harappa**", excavated by **S. R. Rao**.

5.s:
Consider the following statements about Kalibangan:
1. Evidence of a ploughed field has been found there.
2. Seven fire altars were identified at the site.
3. Evidence of an earthquake has been reported from the site.
4. A wooden drain was discovered there.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
5.x: All four statements are correct. Kalibangan is associated with a ploughed field, seven fire altars, earthquake evidence, black bangles and a wooden drain.
5.tq: Check each statement against the complete site profile before selecting the combined code.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(3)**.
**Kalibangan** has a **ploughed field**, **seven fire altars**, **earthquake** evidence and a **wooden drain**.
xa: It also yielded **black bangles** — hence its name.
⚠ **Ploughed field** = Kalibangan; **plough model** = Banawali.
Found by **A. Ghosh** (**1953**); dug by **B. B. Lal and B. K. Thapar** (**1961-69**).
It lies on the **Ghaggar** in **Hanumangarh**, Rajasthan.

5.s: Which Harappan site is particularly associated with the absence of a citadel, an ink-pot and a cart with a seated driver?
5.x: Chanhudaro is distinguished by its bead-making factory, absence of a citadel, ink-pot and cart with a seated driver.
5.tq: Identify the site through its unusual negative and object-based clues.
xs: **Chanhudaro** had **no citadel**, an **ink-pot** and a **cart with a seated driver** — option **(1)**.
**Banawali** = **plough model**; **Dholavira** = **signboard**; **Surkotada** = **horse bones**.
xa: It also had a **bead-making** and **bangle factory** and **lipstick**.
It is the "**Lancashire of India**" for cotton.
Excavated by **N. G. Majumdar** (**1931**); on the **Indus**, Sindh.

5.s: The bronze Dancing Girl, the Priest-King and the Pashupati seal were found at:
5.x: Mohenjodaro has yielded the bronze Dancing Girl, the Priest-King, the Pashupati seal, the Great Bath, the Great Granary and an assembly hall.
5.tq: Apply the famous-object and monument association method.
xs: The **Dancing Girl**, **Priest-King** and **Pashupati seal** come from **Mohenjodaro** — option **(3)**.
**Harappa** gave **six granaries** and a **red sandstone male torso**; **Lothal** a **dockyard**.
**Dholavira** gave **water reservoirs** and a **signboard**.
xa: Mohenjodaro also has the **Great Bath**, **Great Granary** and **assembly hall**.
It means "**Mound of the Dead**"; excavated by **R. D. Banerji** (**1922**).
It is a **UNESCO** site since **1980**.

5.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Harappa — two rows of six granaries
5.x: The ten-sign inscription signboard belongs to Dholavira. Harappa is associated with Cemetery H, a red sandstone male torso and two rows of six granaries.
5.tq: Find the one item belonging to another site rather than the common site in all other pairs.
xs: The **ten-sign signboard** belongs to **Dholavira**, not **Harappa** — option **(4)**.
**Harappa** did yield **two rows of six granaries**, **Cemetery H** and a **red sandstone male torso**.
xa: **Cemetery-H** is also a **Late Harappan** culture.
Harappa lies on the **Ravi**, **Sahiwal/Montgomery** district.
⚠ **Dockyard** = Lothal; **signboard** = Dholavira; **no citadel** = Chanhudaro.

5.s: Dholavira is especially notable for which combination of features?
o: Dog burial and a red sandstone torso
Bronze chariot and an ivory scale
Horse bones and a circular mud-brick fort
Water reservoirs and a three-part town
5.x: Dholavira is known for its water reservoirs, ten-sign signboard and three-part town.
5.tq: Match the settlement’s defining civic features rather than a single portable object.
xs: **Dholavira** is noted for **water reservoirs** and a **three-part town** — option **(4)**.
A **dog burial** = **Ropar**; **red sandstone torso** = **Harappa**; **ivory scale** = **Lothal**.
**Horse bones** and a **circular mud-brick fort** = **Surkotada**.
xa: Dholavira also has a **signboard (10-sign inscription)**.
It lies on **Khadir island**, Kutch, fed by **seasonal streams**.
Inhabited **3000-1800 BCE**; **UNESCO** listing in **2021**.

5.s: A clay model of a plough and a system of radial streets have been found at:
5.x: Banawali is associated with a clay plough model and radial streets. Kalibangan, in contrast, yielded evidence of an actual ploughed field.
5.tq: Separate similar agricultural clues by distinguishing a model from an actual ploughed field.
xs: **Banawali** yielded a **clay plough model** and **radial streets** — option **(2)**.
**Kalibangan** has an actual **ploughed field**, not a model.
**Rakhigarhi** is known for a **skeleton** and **ancient DNA**; **Lothal** for its **dockyard**.
xa: ⚠ **Ploughed field** = Kalibangan; **plough model** = Banawali.
Banawali also gave **barley**; it lies on the **Rangoi**.
It was excavated by **R. S. Bisht** (**1973-74**).

5.s: A 4,500-year-old skeleton and an ancient DNA study are associated with which Harappan site?
5.x: Rakhigarhi has yielded a 4,500-year-old skeleton and has been the subject of an ancient DNA study.
5.tq: Link the distinctive numerical age and scientific study to the correct site.
xs: **Rakhigarhi** yielded a **4,500-year-old skeleton** and an **ancient DNA** study — option **(1)**.
**Ropar** is known for a **dog buried with a human**; **Mohenjodaro** for the **Great Bath**.
xa: ASI moved **56** skeletons from **Mound 7** (incl. a ~**4,600**-year-old woman) to the **Anthropological Survey of India**.
Rakhigarhi is the **largest Indian site**, in **Hisar** district, Haryana.
It is on the UNESCO **Tentative List**.

5.s: The burial of a dog along with a human has been reported from which site?
5.x: Ropar is noted for evidence of a dog buried with a human.
5.tq: Recall the unusual burial association as the decisive clue.
xs: A **dog buried with a human** was found at **Ropar** — option **(3)**.
**Kalibangan** = **ploughed field**; **Rakhigarhi** = **ancient DNA**; **Harappa** = **Cemetery H**.
xa: Ropar (Rupnagar) lies on the **Sutlej** in **Punjab** (India).
It was excavated by **Y. D. Sharma** (**1955-56**).
Some notes give Ropar as the **eastern limit**.

5.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
5.x: Seven fire altars are associated with Kalibangan, not Rangpur. Rangpur is associated with rice and the Late Harappan Rojdi culture.
5.tq: Find the one signature find shifted from its correct site.
xs: **Seven fire altars** belong to **Kalibangan**, not **Rangpur** — option **(4)**.
**Rangpur** gave **rice** and is Late Harappan (**Rojdi culture**).
Surkotada (**horse bones**), Kalibangan (**ploughed field**), Banawali (**toy plough**) are correct.
xa: Rangpur lies on the **Bhadar**, Saurashtra; linked to **M. S. Vats** (**1931**) and **S. R. Rao**.
⚠ **Ploughed field** = Kalibangan; **plough model** = Banawali.
**Lothal** too had **fire altars**.

5.s: Which Harappan site is known for a dockyard regarded as the world's first tidal port?
5.x: Lothal in Gujarat had a dockyard regarded as the world's first tidal port, along with a bead factory. Dholavira is known for its water reservoirs and signboard, Sutkagendor is the westernmost coastal town, and Chanhudaro for its bead factory without a citadel.
5.tq: Dockyard = Lothal.
xs: **Lothal** had a **dockyard**, the **world's first tidal port** — option **(2)**.
**Dholavira** = **reservoirs** and **signboard**; **Sutkagendor** = **westernmost** coastal town.
**Chanhudaro** = **bead factory** and **no citadel**.
xa: ⚠ **Dockyard** = Lothal; **signboard** = Dholavira; **no citadel** = Chanhudaro.
Lothal is at the head of the **Gulf of Cambay**, Bhogava-Sabarmati confluence.
Port towns also: **Sutkagendor** and **Balakot**.

5.s: The Harappan Civilization is significant in Indian history primarily because it represents:
o: The earliest spread of Buddhism across the subcontinent
The first use of iron and iron ploughs in India
The beginning of the Gupta imperial system
The first urbanisation in India and the largest Bronze Age civilization by area
5.x: The civilization is significant for representing the first urbanisation in India and for being the largest Bronze Age civilization by area.
5.tq: Distinguish the civilization’s defining historical significance from developments of later periods.
xs: It is India's **first urbanisation** and the **largest Bronze Age civilisation** by area — option **(4)**.
It was larger than contemporary **Egypt** and **Mesopotamia**.
xa: Extent about **13 lakh sq km**; population about **5 million**.
Mature phase: **planned cities**, **1:2:4 bricks**, **script**, **uniform weights**.
Harappa **urban** vs Rigvedic **pastoral** supports the **pre-Vedic** view.

5.s: The skeletons from Rakhigarhi were transferred under a Memorandum of Understanding to which institution?
o: Archaeological Survey of India, New Delhi
Indian Council of Historical Research, New Delhi
5.x: The Rakhigarhi skeletons were transferred by the Archaeological Survey of India to the Anthropological Survey of India at Kolkata under an MoU.
5.tq: Identify the correct institution and location rather than confusing neighbouring heritage bodies.
xs: Rakhigarhi's skeletons went to the **Anthropological Survey of India** under an **MoU** — option **(4)**.
The **ASI** transferred them; it was the giver, not the receiver.
xa: **56** skeletons from **Mound 7**, incl. a ~**4,600**-year-old woman (**23 Jun 2026**).
Rakhigarhi earlier gave a **4,500-year-old skeleton** and an **ancient DNA** study.
Rakhigarhi is on the UNESCO **Tentative List** (Jun **2026**).

5.s:
Consider the following statements about the current archaeological status of Harappan remains:
1. The skeletons from Rakhigarhi’s Mound 7 were transferred to the Anthropological Survey of India under an MoU.
2. The transferred collection included 56 skeletons.
3. One of the transferred remains was that of a woman approximately 4,600 years old.
4. Tighrana and Mitathal were notified as protected sites by Haryana in June 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
5.x: All four statements are correct. The transfer concerned 56 skeletons from Mound 7, including a woman of about 4,600 years, and Haryana notified Tighrana and Mitathal as protected sites in 2026.
5.tq: Combine institutional action, exact count, approximate age and notification details in one current-affairs statement set.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
1–3: ASI moved **56** skeletons from **Mound 7**, incl. a ~**4,600**-year-old woman, to the **Anthropological Survey of India**.
4: Haryana notified **Tighrana** and **Mitathal** protected in **June 2026**.
xa: The MoU transfer was on **23 Jun 2026**.
Tighrana and Mitathal are in **Bhiwani**, about **4,400** years old; Haryana now has **seven** protected sites.
Only **Dholavira** is on the World Heritage List; **Rakhigarhi** is tentative.

5.s: A researcher is comparing the status of Rakhigarhi with that of Dholavira. Which conclusion is correct?
o: Rakhigarhi is on the World Heritage List, whereas Dholavira is tentative.
Dholavira is on the World Heritage List, whereas Rakhigarhi remains tentative.
Both are on the World Heritage List.
5.x: Dholavira is on the World Heritage List, whereas Rakhigarhi remains on the tentative list.
5.tq: Apply the distinction between a World Heritage listing and tentative-list status.
xs: **Dholavira** is on the **World Heritage List**; **Rakhigarhi** remains **tentative** — option **(2)**.
Dholavira was inscribed in **2021**.
xa: ⚠ Dholavira = inscribed (**2021**); Rakhigarhi = only tentative.
Both were among the **Budget 2020** five iconic sites.
Rakhigarhi = **largest Indian site**; Dholavira = **fifth-largest** IVC city.

5.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the comparative geographical scale of the Harappan Civilization?
o: It was the largest of the contemporary Bronze Age civilizations by area.
It covered less area than the contemporary Egyptian civilization but more than Mesopotamia.
It was confined to the Indus river valley alone.
It was smaller in area than both Egypt and Mesopotamia.
5.x: The Harappan Civilization was the largest of the contemporary Bronze Age civilizations—Egypt and Mesopotamia—when compared by area.
5.tq: Focus on the exact comparative criterion—area—rather than confusing population or urban density.
xs: It was the **largest** contemporary **Bronze Age** civilisation by area — option **(1)**.
It was bigger than both **Egypt** and **Mesopotamia**.
It was not confined to the Indus: most settlements were on the **Ghaggar-Hakra**.
xa: Extent: about **13 lakh sq km** (**1.3 million sq km**).
It marks the **first urbanisation in India**.
Limits: **Manda**, **Daimabad**, **Alamgirpur**, **Sutkagendor**.

5.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the first discovered Indus Valley Civilization site and the year of its discovery?
5.x: Harappa was the first Indus Valley Civilization site discovered, in 1921.
5.tq: Pair the first-in-sequence fact with its exact year and reject swapped milestone dates.
xs: **Harappa** was the first site discovered, in **1921** — option **(2)**.
**Mohenjo-daro** was dug in **1922**; **1980** is its UNESCO year.
**Dholavira** was dug by **R. S. Bisht** in **1990**.
xa: Harappa was found by **Daya Ram Sahni** under **John Marshall**.
**Charles Masson** described its ruins in **1826-38**.
The civilisation is called "**Harappan**" after this first site.

5.s: Mohenjo-daro has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since:
5.x: Mohenjo-daro was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1980.
5.tq: Mohenjo-daro - 1980: 'M' for its early listing in the 80s.
xs: **Mohenjo-daro** has been a UNESCO site since **1980** — option **(3)**.
**2021** is when **Dholavira** was inscribed.
xa: Dholavira is the **first IVC site in India** listed.
**Rakhigarhi** is only on the **Tentative List**.
Mohenjodaro is the largest site in **Pakistan**.

5.s: Which was the first Indus Valley Civilization site in India to be inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List?
5.x: Dholavira is the first (and so far only) IVC site in India on the World Heritage List; Rakhigarhi remains on the tentative list.
5.tq: Dholavira = first Indian Harappan site on the World Heritage list.
xs: **Dholavira** is the **first IVC site in India** on the World Heritage List — option **(4)**.
**Rakhigarhi** is only on the **Tentative List**.
xa: Dholavira (**2021**) was India's **40th** and Gujarat's **4th** WHS.
It is the only inscribed Harappan site in India.
**Mohenjo-daro** (Pakistan) has been listed since **1980**.

6.s: Which one of the following was a hallmark of Harappan town planning?
o: Settlements without drainage or public buildings
Grid-patterned streets and organised civic divisions
Irregular streets centred on royal palaces
6.x: Organised town planning, including grid-patterned streets and civic divisions, is a hallmark of the Indus Valley Civilization.
6.tq: Recognise the broad civilisational feature rather than a minor detail.
xs: The IVC hallmark is **town planning** — **grid-patterned streets** and **organised civic divisions** — option **(2)** (**PYQ APPSC G2 2011**).
**No temples** have been found, and no palaces clearly identified, so options (3) and (4) fail.
Drainage was the **most advanced** feature of IVC towns, so option (1) fails.
xa: Cities were split into a western **citadel** and an eastern **lower town**.
Streets ran **north-south and east-west**, crossing at **right angles**.
⚠ Grid = **Mohenjodaro, Harappa**; **radial** streets = **Banawali** only.

6.s:
Consider the following statements about the street plan of Harappan cities:
1. Streets generally ran north–south and east–west.
2. The streets crossed one another at right angles.
3. The streets divided the city into blocks.
4. Main streets were about 30 feet or approximately 10 metres wide.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: The Harappan grid plan consisted of north–south and east–west streets crossing at right angles, dividing cities into blocks; main streets were about 30 feet or 10 metres wide.
6.tq: Test orientation, geometry and measurement together.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Streets ran **north-south and east-west**, crossing at **right angles**, dividing the city into **blocks**.
**Main streets** were about **30 feet (~10 m)** wide.
xa: **Mohenjodaro** shows the first street layout.
"Main roads about **10 m** wide" was marked **true** in **CGPSC 2022**.
Houses had **doors and windows** onto **side lanes**, not main streets.

6.s: Which Harappan site is associated with the earliest street layout mentioned in the context of Indus town planning?
6.x: Mohenjodaro shows the first street layout referred to in the context of Harappan town planning.
6.tq: Use the site-specific chronological association.
xs: **Mohenjodaro** shows the **first street layout** — option **(4)**.
**Banawali** had **radial** streets, the only such city.
xa: Grid layout is seen at **Mohenjodaro** and **Harappa**.
Mohenjodaro also has the **most wells**.
Main streets: about **30 feet (~10 m)** wide.

6.s: Which Harappan city is noted as the only one with radial streets instead of the usual grid pattern?
6.x: Banawali is the only Harappan city with radial streets; Mohenjodaro and Harappa show the typical grid layout with streets crossing at right angles.
6.tq: Banawali = Radial (B-R): the odd one out in the grid world.
xs: **Banawali** is the only city with **radial streets** — option **(1)**.
**Mohenjodaro** and **Harappa** have the **grid** layout.
xa: Banawali also **lacked systematic drainage**.
**Kalibangan** had **wooden drains**.
**Chanhudaro** is the only city with **no citadel**.

6.s: Which Harappan site is noted for having no citadel?
6.x: Chanhudaro is noted as the only city in the listed comparison without a citadel.
6.tq: Use the unique exception in the site–plan list.
xs: **Chanhudaro** is the only city with **no citadel** — option **(4)**.
**Sutkagendor** has citadel + lower city; **Kalibangan** and **Harappa** have citadel + lower town.
xa: ⚠ **Chanhudaro** = no citadel; **Dholavira** = three parts; **Kalibangan** = lower town also fortified.
**Lothal**: citadel and lower town in **one enclosure**.

6.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. Mohenjodaro — Citadel and lower town
a. Harappa — Citadel and lower town
b. Kalibangan — Citadel and fortified lower town
c. Lothal — Citadel and lower town in one enclosure
d. Sutkagendor — Citadel and lower city
Which of the above pairs are correctly matched?
6.x: All the listed site–plan associations are correct. Kalibangan had a fortified lower town, Lothal had both divisions in one enclosure, and Sutkagendor had a citadel and lower city.
6.tq: Start with the distinctive exceptions and verify the remaining standard pairs.
xs: All the pairs are correct — option **(4) a, b, c and d**.
**Mohenjodaro**, **Harappa** — citadel + lower town; **Kalibangan** — citadel + **fortified lower town**.
**Lothal** — both in **one enclosure**; **Sutkagendor** — citadel + **lower city**.
xa: **Dholavira** = **three parts**: citadel (castle + bailey), **middle town**, lower town.
**Chanhudaro** = no citadel.
The citadel was on the **west**, the lower town on the **east**.

6.s: With reference to the division of Harappan cities, which one of the following is correct?
o: The citadel was a raised and fortified western area, while the lower town lay to the east.
The lower town was always situated on a higher platform than the citadel.
The citadel was generally on the eastern side and the lower town on the western side.
Both the citadel and lower town were exclusively residential areas.
6.x: The western citadel stood on a raised, fortified platform and contained public buildings, while the eastern lower town was associated with commoners’ houses.
6.tq: Check the direction and functional contrast between the two urban divisions.
xs: The **citadel** was the raised, fortified **western** area; the **lower town** lay to the **east** — option **(1)**.
The citadel stood on a **platform** with **public buildings**; the lower town held **commoners' houses**.
Option (3) reverses the sides; option (4) ignores the public buildings.
xa: Seen at **Mohenjodaro**, **Harappa**, **Kalibangan**.
The **Great Bath** and **Great Granary** stood on Mohenjodaro's **citadel**.

6.s: Which one of the following sites is correctly matched with its distinctive town-planning feature?
o: Chanhudaro — Three-part city with a middle town
Lothal — Citadel and lower town in separate distant enclosures
Banawali — Radial streets and no systematic drainage
6.x: Banawali is noted for radial streets, the only such site in the comparison, and for lacking systematic drainage. Dholavira had three parts, Chanhudaro had no citadel, and Lothal had both divisions in one enclosure.
6.tq: Eliminate swapped site–feature combinations by locating the unique features.
xs: **Banawali** — **radial streets** and **no systematic drainage** — option **(4)**.
**Chanhudaro** had **no citadel**; the **three-part** city is **Dholavira**.
**Lothal** had citadel and lower town in **one enclosure**.
xa: Dholavira's three parts: citadel (**castle + bailey**), **middle town**, lower town (**CGPSC 2015**).
**Kalibangan**: lower town also fortified; **wooden drains**.

6.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct regarding Harappan town planning?
o: The cities displayed a grid pattern.
Public buildings were generally associated with the citadel.
The same size of brick was used for every construction.
The main streets were approximately 10 metres wide.
6.x: Brick sizes differed according to construction. House bricks measured about 7 × 14 × 28 cm, while city-wall bricks measured about 10 × 20 × 40 cm, though both followed the same ratio.
6.tq: Find the overgeneralised statement using the exception in brick dimensions.
xs: "**Same size of brick** for every construction" is **NOT correct** — option **(3)** (**CGPSC 2022** trap).
House bricks were **7x14x28 cm**; city-wall bricks **10x20x40 cm** — same **ratio**, different size.
Grid pattern, citadel public buildings and **10 m** main streets are all true.
xa: Standard ratio: **1:2:4** (thickness : width : length).
⚠ Also false in CGPSC 2022: "most houses were **single-storeyed**" — staircases prove multi-storey.

6.s: The standard proportion of Harappan bricks was generally expressed as:
6.x: The standard brick ratio was 1:2:4 in the order of thickness, width and length.
6.tq: Read the numerical ratio in the prescribed order.
xs: The standard brick ratio was **1:2:4** (thickness : width : length) — option **(2)**.
House bricks **7x14x28 cm** and wall bricks **10x20x40 cm** both follow it.
xa: Bricks were **burnt (kiln-fired)**; **mud bricks** for fillings and platforms.
**Dholavira** used **sandstone and limestone** blocks instead.

6.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Harappan bricks:
1. Burnt bricks were the common building material.
2. Mud bricks were used for fillings and platforms.
3. Mud bricks were also used at Kalibangan.
4. Dholavira used sandstone and limestone blocks as an exception.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: Burnt bricks were common, while mud bricks were used for fillings, platforms and at Kalibangan. Dholavira was an exception where sandstone and limestone blocks were used.
6.tq: Combine the general rule with the stated material exceptions.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Burnt (kiln-fired) bricks** were common; **mud bricks** were used for **fillings and platforms** and at **Kalibangan**.
**Dholavira** used **sandstone and limestone** blocks, not baked brick.
xa: Standard ratio **1:2:4**; sizes differ by use.
Mohenjodaro and Harappa used **baked brick**.

6.s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan houses:
1. Rooms were arranged round a central courtyard.
2. Doors and windows usually opened onto the main streets.
3. Staircases show that houses could be multi-storeyed.
4. Housing was fairly uniform, but variation in house size points to social differentiation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: Statement 1 is correct: rooms were built round a central courtyard. Statement 2 is wrong: doors and windows opened onto side lanes, not main streets, for privacy. Statement 3 is correct: staircases prove multi-storey houses. Statement 4 is correct: housing was fairly uniform but house size varied, showing social differentiation. So '1, 3 and 4 only' is right; options A, C and D all include the false statement 2.
6.tq: Side lanes, not main streets; and 'mostly single-storey' is a known false statement (CGPSC 2022).
xs: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct — option **(2) 1, 3 and 4 only**.
Statement 1 correct: rooms round a **central courtyard**.
Statement 2 wrong: **doors and windows opened onto side lanes**, not main streets (privacy).
Statements 3 and 4 correct: **staircases** show multi-storey houses; housing fairly uniform but **house size varied**.
xa: **Bathrooms** had burnt-brick floors connected to the drains.
Wells were inside houses or neighbourhoods at **Mohenjodaro**.

6.s: Which site is associated with the greatest number of wells in the developed stage of the Indus Civilization?
6.x: Wells were found inside houses or neighbourhoods, and Mohenjodaro is noted for having the greatest number of wells.
6.tq: Distinguish the site-specific quantitative association.
xs: **Mohenjodaro** has the **most wells** — option **(4)**.
Wells were inside houses or neighbourhoods in its developed stage (**PYQ UPPSC 2004**).
xa: **Well irrigation** is known from **Allahdino** (Sindh).
Mohenjodaro also shows the first street layout.
Mohenjodaro's **Great Bath**: PYQ UPPSC **2010**.

6.s: Well irrigation in the Harappan context is specifically associated with:
6.x: Well irrigation is associated with Allahdino in Sindh.
6.tq: Match the irrigation practice with its specific site and region.
xs: Well irrigation is linked to **Allahdino** (Sindh) — option **(4)**.
**Kalibangan** is known for **wooden drains**; **Banawali** for radial streets; **Sutkagendor** for citadel + lower city.
xa: **Mohenjodaro** has the most wells.
Wells were inside houses or neighbourhoods (**PYQ UPPSC 2004**).

6.s: Which feature is regarded as the most advanced feature of the Indus Valley Civilization towns?
6.x: The planned drainage system is regarded as the most advanced feature of Indus Valley Civilization towns.
6.tq: Use direct recall for a high-yield superlative fact.
xs: The **planned drainage system** is the **most advanced** feature of IVC towns — option **(1)**.
No **temples** have been found in IVC cities.
xa: Flow: house drains → street drains → **soak pits**/main channels.
IVC drainage was more advanced than contemporary **Mesopotamia/Egypt**.
Even small settlements had planned drainage.

6.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Indus Valley drainage systems:
1. Drains were generally covered.
2. Manholes were provided for cleaning.
3. Burnt bricks and terracotta pipes were used in their construction.
4. Streets were designed with a slope to facilitate natural flow.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: All four statements are correct. Covered drains had manholes for maintenance, were built with burnt bricks and terracotta pipes, and used street slopes for natural flow.
6.tq: Check whether all statements describe connected features of one civic system.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Drains were **covered**, with **manholes** for cleaning.
Built of **burnt brick**, with **terracotta pipes** for wastewater; streets **sloped** for natural flow.
xa: House drains → street drains → **soak pits**.
⚠ **Wooden drains** = Kalibangan; no systematic drainage = Banawali.

6.s: Which one of the following statements about drainage in smaller Indus Valley settlements is correct?
o: Planned drainage was confined to the largest cities.
Kalibangan had wooden drains, whereas Banawali lacked a systematic drainage system.
Banawali had the most elaborate drainage system and Kalibangan had none.
Both Kalibangan and Banawali used only stone drains.
6.x: Planned drainage existed even in small settlements. Kalibangan had wooden drains, while Banawali lacked a systematic drainage system.
6.tq: Separate the two similar settlement examples by assigning each its distinctive feature.
xs: **Kalibangan** had **wooden drains**; **Banawali** lacked **systematic drainage** — option **(2)**.
Even **small settlements** had planned drainage, so option (1) is wrong.
xa: Drains were **covered** with **manholes**.
Banawali is also the only city with **radial** streets.

6.s: The Great Bath at Mohenjodaro was located:
o: Beside the dockyard in the lower town
Inside a residential courtyard at Harappa
On the fortified lower town of Kalibangan
6.x: The Great Bath was situated on the citadel mound of Mohenjodaro.
6.tq: Link the monument to both its site and urban division.
xs: The **Great Bath** stood on the **citadel mound** of **Mohenjodaro** — option **(3)** (**PYQ UPPSC 2010**).
The **dockyard** is at **Lothal**, not Mohenjodaro.
xa: Size: about **12 m x 7 m**, **2.4 m deep**.
The **Great Granary** too is on Mohenjodaro's citadel.

6.s: Which combination of materials was used in the construction and waterproofing of the Great Bath?
o: Burnt bricks, gypsum mortar and bitumen
Mud bricks, lime plaster and clay coating
Limestone, mud mortar and natural resin
6.x: The Great Bath was built with burnt bricks set in gypsum mortar and was waterproofed with a layer of bitumen.
6.tq: Distinguish construction material from the waterproofing agent.
xs: The Great Bath used **burnt bricks** in **gypsum mortar**, sealed with **bitumen** — option **(1)**.
**Sandstone** blocks belong to **Dholavira**; mud bricks were for fillings.
xa: ⚠ **Gypsum** = mortar; **bitumen** = waterproofing layer.
Steps at the **north and south** ends.
Size: about **12 m x 7 m, 2.4 m deep**.

6.s: Which one of the following statements about the Great Bath is correct?
o: It had flights of steps at its northern and southern ends and is generally interpreted as a place for ritual bathing and purification.
It was situated in the lower town and served only as a grain store.
It had no steps and was used exclusively for irrigation.
It had flights of steps at its eastern and western ends and was certainly a royal palace.
6.x: The Great Bath had flights of steps at its north and south ends. It is most commonly interpreted as a place for ritual bathing and purification, although a public water tank interpretation also exists.
6.tq: Combine structural details with the cautious interpretation of purpose.
xs: The Great Bath had **steps at the north and south ends** and is mostly read as **ritual bathing/purification** — option **(1)**.
It is on the **citadel**, not the lower town, and is not a granary.
Steps were not on the east and west ends; no palaces have been clearly identified.
xa: Others read it as a **public water tank**.
Ritual bathing may survive in later **temple tanks** and **ghats**.

6.s: The Great Granary, described as the largest building of the city, has been found at which Harappan site?
6.x: The Great Granary, regarded as the largest building at the site, was found at Mohenjodaro.
6.tq: Use the site–structure association directly.
xs: The **Great Granary**, largest building of the city, is at **Mohenjodaro** — option **(2)** (**PYQ APPSC G2 2008**).
**Harappa** has **two rows of six granaries**; **Lothal** a warehouse beside the dock; **Rakhigarhi** a reported granary.
xa: It stood on the **citadel**.
⚠ **Great Granary** = Mohenjodaro; **two rows of six** = Harappa.

6.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the interpretation of Harappan granaries is correct?
o: They were constructed only for residential purposes.
They were exclusively used as temples.
They are generally read as stores of farm surplus, though the interpretation is debated.
They are universally accepted as royal palaces.
6.x: Granaries are commonly interpreted as storage places for agricultural surplus, but this interpretation remains debated.
6.tq: Distinguish a prevailing interpretation from an absolute conclusion.
xs: Granaries are read as **stores of farm surplus**, but this is **debated** — option **(3)**.
No palaces or temples have been clearly identified in IVC cities.
xa: Mohenjodaro: **Great Granary**; Harappa: **12 units** near the river.
Harappa had the **largest wheat finds**.

6.s: The warehouse on a raised platform beside the dock is associated with which site?
6.x: Lothal had a warehouse on a raised platform beside the dock; seal impressions were also associated with the warehouse.
6.tq: Match the distinctive structure with its site.
xs: **Lothal** had a **warehouse on a raised platform** beside the **dock** — option **(2)**.
It had **seal impressions**.
xa: The Lothal **dockyard** (tidal) is debated — possibly an **irrigation tank**.
Lothal also has **fire altars**.
Lothal: citadel and lower town in **one enclosure**.

6.s: Two rows of six granaries each, with circular working platforms and single-roomed barracks nearby, have been found at
6.x: Harappa had two rows of six granaries (12 units) near the river, with circular working platforms and barracks. Mohenjodaro had the single Great Granary on its citadel, Lothal a warehouse beside the dock, and Rakhigarhi has only a reported granary.
6.tq: Great Granary = Mohenjodaro; 2 x 6 granaries = Harappa.
xs: **Harappa** had **two rows of six granaries** (**12** units) with **circular working platforms** and **single-roomed barracks** — option **(2)**.
**Mohenjodaro** had the single **Great Granary**; **Lothal** a dockside warehouse.
xa: Harappa's granaries stood **near the river**; largest **wheat** finds.
**Rakhigarhi**: granary also reported.

6.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Water reservoirs, dams and embankments — Harappa
6.x: Water reservoirs, dams and embankments are associated with Dholavira, not Harappa.
6.tq: Find the location mismatch by comparing each structure with its known site.
xs: **Water reservoirs, dams, embankments — Harappa** is wrong — option **(2)**; they belong to **Dholavira**.
**Stadium** — Dholavira; **multi-pillared assembly hall** — Mohenjodaro; **dockyard** — Lothal: correct.
xa: Dholavira stadium: ~**283 x 47 m**.
**16 reservoirs** cover about **10%** of Dholavira.

6.s: Fire altars in the Indus Valley Civilization are associated with:
6.x: Fire altars have been identified at Kalibangan, including seven such altars, and at Lothal.
6.tq: Test a paired site association directly.
xs: **Fire altars** are at **Kalibangan** (seven) and **Lothal** — option **(2)**.
**Dholavira** is known for reservoirs and the stadium, **Mohenjodaro** for the Great Bath and Great Granary, **Harappa** for its granaries — not fire altars.
xa: ⚠ At Kalibangan the fire altars belong to the **Mature** phase.
Lothal also has the **dockyard** and a **warehouse**.
Kalibangan: citadel + **fortified lower town**; **wooden drains**.

6.s: The largest Indus Valley inscription, consisting of a ten-sign signboard, has been reported from the:
6.x: The largest inscription is the ten-sign signboard found at the North Gate of Dholavira.
6.tq: Link the numerical detail with its exact site and location.
xs: The largest inscription, a **10-sign signboard**, is at Dholavira's **North Gate** — option **(3)**.
The notes link the **citadel of Mohenjodaro** to the Great Bath and Great Granary, and **Lothal** to the dockyard — not to this inscription.
xa: Dholavira also has a **stadium** (~**283 x 47 m**).
Dholavira's water system: **giant reservoirs**, **bunds**, **dams and embankments** (**UPSC 2021**).
It is the only city in **three parts**.

6.s: Dholavira is distinguished among the known Indus Valley cities because it was divided into:
o: Four parts—citadel, market, temple and lower town
Three parts—citadel, middle town and lower town
6.x: Dholavira is described as the only Indus Valley city divided into three parts: citadel, middle town and lower town.
6.tq: Use the unique qualifier to distinguish Dholavira from other planned cities.
xs: **Dholavira** was divided into **three parts**: **citadel**, **middle town**, **lower town** — option **(3)**.
Other IVC cities had only citadel + lower town.
xa: The citadel had a **castle + bailey**; remnants of **three townships** (**CGPSC 2015**).
**Chanhudaro** = no citadel.

6.s:
Consider the following statements about water management at Dholavira:
1. It included giant reservoirs.
2. Bunds or check-dams and channels fed the reservoirs.
3. Dams and embankments formed part of the system.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: Dholavira had giant reservoirs supplied through bunds, check-dams and channels, along with dams and embankments.
6.tq: Recognise a complete cluster of related water-management features.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** (**UPSC 2021**).
**Giant reservoirs**, partly cut into the rock; **bunds (check-dams)** + **channels** fed them.
**Dams and embankments** formed part of the system.
xa: **16 reservoirs** cover about **10%** of the site (largest ~**73 x 29 m**).
Dholavira also has a **stadium** and the **signboard** inscription.

6.s: Which statement correctly describes the construction materials and techniques associated with Dholavira?
o: Its reservoirs were partly cut into rock, and sandstone and limestone blocks were used for major construction.
It used only baked bricks, unlike Mohenjodaro and Harappa.
Its major structures were built exclusively of iron and copper.
Its reservoirs were entirely made of timber and mud.
6.x: Some Dholavira reservoirs were partly cut into the rock, and sandstone and limestone blocks were used for major construction. Mohenjodaro and Harappa are contrasted with it for their use of baked brick.
6.tq: Use the material contrast to distinguish Dholavira from Mohenjodaro and Harappa.
xs: Dholavira's reservoirs were **partly cut into the rock**, and it used **sandstone and limestone** blocks — option **(1)**.
Unlike **Mohenjodaro** and **Harappa**, it did **not** use baked brick.
xa: Dholavira is one of the **five largest** cities, with **Mohenjodaro, Harappa, Ganweriwala, Rakhigarhi**.
Bunds (**check-dams**) and channels fed the reservoirs.

6.s: Dholavira was occupied through seven stages during approximately which period?
6.x: Dholavira was occupied through seven stages from approximately 3000 to 1500 BCE.
6.tq: Match the duration and date range rather than relying on a single year.
xs: Dholavira was occupied through **seven stages**, c. **3000-1500 BCE** — option **(2)**.
Dholavira is one of the **five largest** Harappan cities, with **Mohenjodaro, Harappa, Ganweriwala, Rakhigarhi**.
xa: ⚠ The **APPSC 2018** key gives **3000-1800 BCE**.
**16 reservoirs** cover about **10%** of the site.
Dholavira is a **three-part** city.

6.s: Which of the following best explains the significance of standardised bricks, grid planning and drainage in the Indus Valley Civilization?
o: They suggest civic authority and early engineering skill.
They prove that all settlements were royal capitals.
They show that the civilization had abandoned urban planning.
They indicate the exclusive control of religious institutions.
6.x: Standardisation of bricks, grid planning and drainage points to civic authority and considerable early engineering skill.
6.tq: Infer the institutional significance from the combination of urban features.
xs: **Standardised bricks**, **grid planning**, streets and **drains** point to **civic authority** and **early engineering skill** — option **(1)**.
No **palaces or temples** have been clearly identified, so royal or religious control is not proven.
xa: Bricks follow the ratio **1:2:4**.
IVC drainage beat contemporary **Mesopotamia/Egypt**.

6.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Indus Valley and contemporary West Asian civilizations:
1. No palaces or temples have been clearly identified in the Indus Valley cities.
2. Indus Valley drainage was more advanced than that of contemporary Mesopotamia and Egypt.
3. The absence of clearly identified palaces or temples proves that the Indus Valley Civilization had no civic authority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The absence of clearly identified palaces or temples does not disprove civic authority; standardised urban planning instead suggests it.
6.tq: Reject an overextended conclusion while retaining the supported comparative statements.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: unlike **Mesopotamia** and **Egypt**, **no palaces or temples** are clearly identified.
Statement 2 correct: IVC **drainage was more advanced** than theirs.
Statement 3 wrong: standardised planning points to **civic authority**.
xa: Drainage = **most advanced** feature of IVC towns.
Standard brick ratio **1:2:4**.

7.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the five largest Harappan cities listed?
7.x: The five largest cities listed are Mohenjodaro, Harappa, Ganweriwala, Rakhigarhi and Dholavira. Lothal is not included in this five-city list.
7.tq: Use the complete list and identify the plausible but excluded city.
xs: **Lothal** is not among the five largest Harappan cities — option **(1)**.
The five: **Mohenjodaro, Harappa, Ganweriwala, Rakhigarhi, Dholavira**.
xa: **Dholavira** is called one of the biggest Harappan townships (**2026**).
Lothal is known for its **tidal dockyard** and the **ship on a seal**.
⚠ Inscribed WHS = **Dholavira**; Tentative List = **Rakhigarhi**.

7.s: A female skeleton from Rakhigarhi lacked the ‘Steppe Pastoralist’ gene. This finding has been interpreted as indicating:
o: Definite Central Asian origin of the Harappans
The absence of agriculture in the Mature Harappan phase
Indigenous ancestry and a challenge to the Aryan-invasion view
A direct Roman connection with Haryana
7.x: The genetic finding has been interpreted as pointing towards indigenous ancestry and challenging the Aryan-invasion view.
7.tq: Translate a scientific finding into its stated historical interpretation without adding an unrelated conclusion.
xs: Lacking the "**Steppe Pastoralist**" gene points to **indigenous ancestry** and **challenges the Aryan-invasion view** — option **(3)** (Jun **2026**).
It does not suggest a Central Asian origin; the finding argues the opposite.
xa: **Rakhigarhi** is one of the **five largest** Harappan cities and is on the **Tentative List**.
Rakhigarhi **Mound 7** has yielded **56 skeletons**, incl. a ~**4,600**-year-old woman.

7.s: Which Harappan site is on the Tentative List rather than the UNESCO World Heritage List?
7.x: Rakhigarhi is on the Tentative List, whereas Dholavira is the only Harappan site on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
7.tq: Discriminate between the World Heritage List and the Tentative List status.
xs: **Rakhigarhi** is on the **Tentative List** — option **(1)**.
**Dholavira** is the **only inscribed** Harappan site (**UNESCO WHS 2021**, India's **40th**).
xa: ⚠ Inscribed = Dholavira; tentative = Rakhigarhi.
Rakhigarhi DNA: no **Steppe Pastoralist** gene → indigenous ancestry.
Five largest cities: Mohenjodaro, Harappa, **Ganweriwala**, Rakhigarhi, Dholavira.

7.s: What was the reported finding concerning the DNA of the female skeleton from Rakhigarhi?
o: It proved that all Indo-Aryan speakers originated in the Arctic.
It showed no Steppe Pastoralist gene.
It showed a Steppe Pastoralist gene in an overwhelming proportion.
It established that Harappans had no genetic continuity with later populations.
7.x: The DNA of a Rakhigarhi female skeleton was reported to show no Steppe Pastoralist gene. This finding has been cited in arguments against invasion theories and in favour of indigenous ancestral continuity.
7.tq: Test the precise genetic finding, not the broader theory attached to it.
xs: The Rakhigarhi female skeleton showed **no Steppe Pastoralist gene** — option **(2)**.
So option (3), an overwhelming share of that gene, is the opposite of the finding.
It is read as **indigenous ancestry**, challenging the **Aryan-invasion** view.
xa: Latest Mound 7 dig: **five complete skeletons** (aged **30-40**) + **three** fragmentary burials (23 Jun **2026**).
Mound 7 total: **56 skeletons**.

7.s: The National Maritime Heritage Complex is being developed at:
7.x: The National Maritime Heritage Complex is being developed at Lothal in Gujarat.
7.tq: Match the heritage complex with its exact location.
xs: The **National Maritime Heritage Complex** is at **Lothal**, Gujarat — option **(1)**.
Lothal fits: it has the Harappan **artificial tidal dockyard**.
xa: ⚠ Some read the Lothal dockyard as an **irrigation tank**.
Lothal finds: **ship on a seal**, **Persian Gulf seal**, **copper dog**.
Other Harappan ports: **Rangpur**, **Somnath (Prabhas Patan)**, **Balakot**.

7.s: The Pashupati seal, depicting a three-faced figure in yogic posture surrounded by animals, was discovered at which Harappan site?
7.x: The Pashupati seal, also called the Proto-Shiva seal, was found at Mohenjodaro. It depicts a three-faced figure in a yogic posture, surrounded by animals.
7.tq: Use the site-specific association directly; distinguish Mohenjodaro from other major urban sites.
xs: The **Pashupati seal** ("**Proto-Shiva**") is from **Mohenjodaro** — option **(2)**.
It shows a **three-faced figure** in **yogic posture**, ringed by **animals**.
**Harappa** gave the **red sandstone male torso**; **Lothal** the **ship on a seal**; **Kalibangan** a **cylindrical seal**.
xa: The **Bronze Dancing Girl** is also from Mohenjodaro.
Most common seal motif: **unicorn**; most depicted tree: **pipal**.

7.s: The Bronze Dancing Girl of the Harappan civilisation was found at
7.x: The Bronze Dancing Girl is one of the best-known sculptures discovered at Mohenjodaro.
7.tq: Test a famous object–site association through direct recall.
xs: The **Bronze Dancing Girl** was found at **Mohenjodaro** — option **(1)**.
**Chanhudaro** gave **carts with seated driver** and toys; **Harappa** the **red sandstone male torso**.
xa: ⚠ Bronze Dancing Girl = Mohenjodaro; red sandstone male torso = Harappa.
Harappa also gave a **bronze dog chasing deer** and **bullock carts**.
The **Pashupati seal** is from Mohenjodaro.

7.s: With reference to cylindrical seals in the Harappan context, which one of the following is correct?
o: They were found only at Lothal and Dholavira.
They were found exclusively at Chanhudaro.
They were found only at Harappa.
They were found at Kalibangan, while a Mesopotamian-linked cylindrical seal was found at Mohenjodaro.
7.x: Cylindrical seals are associated with Kalibangan, and a cylindrical seal indicating a Mesopotamian link was found at Mohenjodaro.
7.tq: Distinguish a general site association from the specific Mesopotamian-linked find.
xs: **Cylindrical seals** come from **Kalibangan**, and one from **Mohenjodaro** shows a **Mesopotamian link** — option **(4)**.
They are not confined to Lothal, Dholavira, Chanhudaro or Harappa.
xa: **Lothal** gave a **Persian Gulf seal** and a **ship on a seal**.
Most common seal motif: **unicorn**.

7.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Harappan seal motifs and plant representation is correct?
o: The rhinoceros is the most common seal motif and the acacia is the most depicted tree.
The unicorn is the most common seal motif and the pipal is the most depicted tree.
The elephant is the most common seal motif and the banyan is the most depicted tree.
The bull is the most common seal motif and the neem is the most depicted tree.
7.x: The unicorn is regarded as the most common Harappan seal motif, while the pipal is the most depicted tree.
7.tq: Test a paired comparison by separating the most common motif from the most depicted tree.
xs: The **unicorn** is the most common **seal motif** and the **pipal** the most depicted **tree** — option **(2)**.
The notes name no rhinoceros, elephant or bull as the top motif, nor acacia, banyan or neem as the top tree.
xa: The **Pashupati seal** shows a figure ringed by animals (Mohenjodaro).
**Lothal** seals: **ship** and **Persian Gulf** types.

7.s:
Arrange the following objects according to their associated Harappan sites from the site-specific associations given below:
A. Pashupati seal
B. Ship on a seal
C. Carts with seated drivers
D. Red sandstone male torso
Which one of the following correctly identifies the sites in the same order?
7.x: The Pashupati seal is from Mohenjodaro, the ship on a seal from Lothal, carts with seated drivers from Chanhudaro, and the red sandstone male torso from Harappa.
7.tq: Use a sure first pair and then map the remaining objects by site association.
xs: Order: **Mohenjodaro, Lothal, Chanhudaro, Harappa** — option **(1)**.
**Pashupati seal** — Mohenjodaro; **ship on a seal** — Lothal.
**Carts with seated driver** — Chanhudaro; **red sandstone male torso** — Harappa.
xa: Mohenjodaro also: **Bronze Dancing Girl**.
Lothal also: **copper dog**; Harappa also: **bronze dog chasing deer**.

7.s: Which Harappan site is especially noted for an elaborate water-management system comprising 16 reservoirs, dams, embankments and sandstone-cut stepwells?
7.x: Dholavira had 16 reservoirs, dams, embankments and stepwells cut in sandstone, demonstrating an elaborate water-management system.
7.tq: Identify the site from the concentration of water-conservation structures.
xs: **Dholavira** had **16 reservoirs**, **dams, embankments** and **stepwells cut in sandstone** — option **(2)**.
**Mohenjodaro** is known for the most **wells**; **Lothal** for the **dockyard**.
xa: The reservoirs cover about **10%** of the site; largest ~**73 x 29 m**.
Dholavira: **UNESCO WHS 2021**, India's **40th**.

7.s: Well irrigation at Allahdino, in Sindh, is an example of:
7.x: Allahdino in Sindh is associated with well irrigation, an example of Harappan water-management practice.
7.tq: Identify the function of a site-specific archaeological feature.
xs: Well irrigation at **Allahdino (Sindh)** is a **Harappan water-management** practice — option **(3)**.
It is not Dholavira's system, which relied on **reservoirs**.
xa: **Mohenjodaro** has the most **wells**.
**Lothal**: artificial **tidal dockyard**.
**Dholavira**: **16 reservoirs**, dams, embankments.

7.s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of Harappan port sites other than Lothal?
7.x: Rangpur, Somnath (Prabhas Patan) and Balakot are listed as other Harappan ports besides Lothal.
7.tq: Test whether every member of the proposed group belongs to the same functional category.
xs: **Rangpur**, **Somnath (Prabhas Patan)** and **Balakot** are the other ports — option **(1)**.
**Dholavira, Harappa, Rakhigarhi** are listed among the **largest cities**, not ports.
xa: **Lothal**'s artificial **tidal dockyard** — some say an irrigation tank.
Lothal finds: **ship on a seal**, **Persian Gulf seal**.

7.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Lothal had an artificial tidal dockyard, though some scholars read it as an irrigation tank.
2. Mohenjodaro has yielded the largest number of wells among Harappan sites.
3. Dholavira's water system relied mainly on wells rather than reservoirs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: Statement 1 is correct: Lothal's tidal dockyard is the standard reading, with an irrigation-tank view as an alternative. Statement 2 is correct: Mohenjodaro has the most wells. Statement 3 is wrong: Dholavira is known for 16 reservoirs, dams and embankments. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses a true statement and options with 3 are wrong.
7.tq: Dockyard = Lothal; most wells = Mohenjodaro; reservoirs = Dholavira.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Lothal** had an **artificial tidal dockyard**; some call it an **irrigation tank**.
Statement 2 correct: **Mohenjodaro** has the most **wells**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Dholavira** relied on **16 reservoirs**, dams and embankments.
xa: Dholavira's reservoirs cover about **10%** of the site.
**Allahdino** (Sindh): well irrigation.

8.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Crop)
a. Wheat
b. Barley
c. Rice
 d. Garlic

List-II (Site of evidence)
i. Banawali
ii. Balu
iii. Harappa and Mehrgarh
iv. Lothal and Rangpur

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
8.x: Wheat is evidenced at Harappa and Mehrgarh, barley at Banawali, rice at Lothal and Rangpur, and garlic at Balu.
8.tq: Start from the sure crop–site pairs and eliminate codes.
xs: The correct match is **a–iii, b–i, c–iv, d–ii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Wheat** → **Harappa** (largest number of wheat grains) and **Mehrgarh**; **barley** → **Banawali**.
**Rice** → **Lothal** (rice husks) and **Rangpur**; **garlic** → **Balu** (Haryana), its earliest evidence.
xa: Lothal's rice husks are the **earliest evidence of rice cultivation in Gujarat**, **c. 1800 BCE**.
**Indigo** → **Rojdi** (Gujarat); **millets and rice as staple** → **Rangpur, Surkotada**.
**Cotton** → **Mohenjodaro**, with Neolithic cotton at **Mehrgarh**.
Other Harappan crops: **peas, lentil, chickpea, horse gram, sesame, mustard**; fruits like **dates, melon, grapes**.

8.s:
With reference to cotton in the Indus Valley Civilization, consider the following statements:
1. Mehrgarh provides Neolithic evidence of cotton.
2. The Harappans were the first to produce cotton textiles.
3. The Greeks referred to cotton as Sindon.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
8.x: Mehrgarh provides Neolithic cotton evidence; the Harappans pioneered cotton textiles; and the Greeks called cotton Sindon.
8.tq: Combine the archaeological, technological and terminology clues.
xs: All three statements are correct — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
Statement 1 is correct: cotton is evidenced at **Mohenjodaro**, with **Neolithic** evidence at **Mehrgarh**.
Statement 2 is correct: the Harappans **pioneered cotton** cultivation and were the **first to produce cotton textiles**.
Statement 3 is correct: the **Greeks** called cotton **Sindon**.
xa: **Chanhudaro** was the **"Lancashire of India"** for its spinning and weaving.
**Spindle-whorls** are common in houses, but **no spinning wheel** has been found.
**Cotton** was also an **export** of Harappan external trade.
⚠ The **Rig Veda** does not mention cotton, rice or wheat.

8.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Chanhudaro — earliest evidence of rice cultivation in Gujarat
Rangpur and Surkotada — millets and rice as staple crops
8.x: Chanhudaro is associated with cotton textiles and craft production. The earliest evidence of rice cultivation in Gujarat is at Lothal, dated to approximately 1800 BCE.
8.tq: Find the mismatched crop and site rather than accepting a familiar site name.
xs: **Chanhudaro — earliest evidence of rice cultivation in Gujarat** is wrongly matched — option **(1)**.
The earliest rice in Gujarat is from **Lothal** (rice husks, **c. 1800 BCE**); Chanhudaro is a **craft centre** (beads, shell, metal, weaving).
**Balu** (Haryana) — earliest **garlic**; **Rojdi** (Gujarat) — **indigo**; **Rangpur and Surkotada** — **millets and rice** as staple: all correct.
xa: Lothal also has the **world's earliest tidal dockyard**.
**Kalibangan** has the **earliest ploughed field**.
**Rice** also comes from **Rangpur**.
**Barley** → **Banawali**; **wheat** → **Harappa** and **Mehrgarh**.

8.s: Which of the following groups consists only of crops cultivated by the Harappans?
o: Tea, coffee, rubber, wheat and barley
Maize, potato, tobacco, cotton and indigo
Jute, sugarcane, tea, rice and coffee
Wheat, barley, peas, sesame and mustard
8.x: Wheat, barley, peas, sesame and mustard are among the crops cultivated by the Harappans. The other groups contain crops not included in the given evidence.
8.tq: Separate the valid crop inventory from later or unrelated crops.
xs: **Wheat, barley, peas, sesame and mustard** were all Harappan crops — option **(4)**.
The notes list Harappan crops as **wheat, barley, peas, lentil, chickpea, horse gram, sesame, mustard, millets, cotton**.
The other groups mix in crops such as **tea, coffee, rubber, maize, potato, tobacco, jute**, which are not in the Harappan crop list.
xa: Fruits and others: **dates, melon, watermelon, grapes, henna**.
**Garlic** → **Balu**; **indigo** → **Rojdi**.
Harappans **pioneered cotton** cultivation; the Greeks called it **Sindon**.
**Surplus** came from **double cropping** and was stored in **granaries**.

8.s: In the crop-wise evidence of the Indus Valley Civilization, cotton from the Mature Harappan period is associated with which site?
8.x: Cotton is evidenced at Mohenjodaro (with earlier Neolithic evidence at Mehrgarh). Banawali is linked with barley, Balu with the earliest garlic and Rojdi with indigo.
8.tq: Cotton = Mohenjodaro (Mehrgarh Neolithic); Greeks called it Sindon.
xs: Cotton is associated with **Mohenjodaro** — option **(2)**.
Earlier, **Neolithic** cotton comes from **Mehrgarh**.
**Banawali** = **barley**; **Balu** = earliest **garlic**; **Rojdi** = **indigo**.
xa: Harappans were the **first to produce cotton textiles**.
**Spinning and weaving** (cotton, wool) centres: **Mohenjodaro** and **Chanhudaro** ("Lancashire of India").
Banawali also gave **terracotta plough models**.
Greeks called cotton **Sindon**.

8.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Evidence)
a. Terracotta plough model
b. Clay plough
c. Well irrigation
d. Reservoirs

List-II (Site)
i. Allahdino
ii. Dholavira
