Statement 2 is wrong: the Ganadharas compiled Mahavira's teaching into **12 Angas**, not 14 — so option **(1) 1 only** is correct.
xa: The canon was arranged into **12 Angas** at the **first council** at **Pataliputra** under **Sthulabhadra**.
Key Angas: **Acharanga Sutra** (code of conduct for monks) and **Bhagavati Sutra** (doctrines).
Other early texts: **Sutrakritanga** and **Kalpasutra**.

27.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the Digambara position from the Svetambara position regarding the Angas?
o: Digambaras hold that all the original Angas were lost, whereas Svetambaras preserve a canon including 12 Angas.
Digambaras preserve all 12 Angas, whereas Svetambaras reject every Anga.
Svetambaras hold that the Angas were lost, whereas Digambaras preserve the complete canon.
Both sects accept the same complete set of original Angas without variation.
27.x: The Svetambara canon includes twelve Angas, while Digambaras maintain that all the original Angas were lost and follow a separate canon.
27.tq: Test the sectarian distinction by reversing the positions as the distractor.
xs: **Digambaras** hold that **all the original Angas were lost**, while **Svetambaras** keep a canon with **12 Angas** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Digambaras therefore follow a **separate canon**.
xa: The Svetambara canon also has **12 Upangas, 10 Prakirnas, 6 Cheda Sutras and 4 Mula Sutras**.
The **Upangas** were added at the **second council** at **Vallabhi** (**512 CE**).
The **Tattvartha Sutra** (Umasvati) is accepted, in two versions, by **both sects**.

27.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Acharanga Sutra — code of conduct for monks
Kalpasutra — code of conduct exclusively for kings
27.x: Acharanga Sutra deals with the code of conduct for Jain monks. Bhagavati Sutra deals with doctrines, while Sutrakritanga and Kalpasutra are also early Jain texts.
27.tq: Use the subject matter of each text to detect the substituted description.
xs: **Acharanga Sutra** is the **code of conduct for monks** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Bhagavati Sutra** deals with **doctrines**, not medicine; the medical treatise is **Kalyanakaraka** by **Ugradityacharya**.
**Sutrakritanga** is an early **Jain** text, not a Buddhist chronicle; **Kalpasutra** is by **Bhadrabahu** (Jinacharitra, Sthaviravali, Samachari).
xa: Jain texts are in **Ardhamagadhi**; the **14 Purvas** came first, then the **12 Angas**.
Exam angle: odd-one-out — Jain texts (**Acharanga**, **Bhagavati**, **Kalpasutra**) vs Buddhist (**Dipavamsa**, **Mahavamsa**, **Divyavadana**, **Milindapanho**).

27.s:
Consider the following statements about the Svetambara Jain canon:
1. It contains 12 Angas and 12 Upangas.
2. It contains 10 Prakirnas.
3. It contains 4 Cheda Sutras and 6 Mula Sutras.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
27.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Svetambara canon has 12 Angas, 12 Upangas and 10 Prakirnas. Statement 3 reverses the numbers: there are 6 Cheda Sutras and 4 Mula Sutras. So '1 and 2 only'.
27.tq: Svetambara canon: 12-12-10-6-4 (Angas, Upangas, Prakirnas, Cheda, Mula).
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the Svetambara canon has **12 Angas** and **12 Upangas**.
Statement 2 is correct: it has **10 Prakirnas**.
Statement 3 is wrong — the numbers are reversed: **6 Cheda Sutras** and **4 Mula Sutras**. So option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
xa: **Digambaras** reject this canon and hold that all the original Angas were lost.
The canon was written down at the **second council**, **Vallabhi**, **512 CE**, under **Devardhi Kshamashramana**.
The earliest texts, the **14 Purvas**, are now mostly lost.

27.s: Which one of the following is NOT a Jain text?
27.x: Acharanga Sutra (monks' code of conduct), Bhagavati Sutra (doctrines) and Kalpasutra are Jain texts. Milindapanho is a Buddhist text, like the Dipavamsa, Mahavamsa and Divyavadana.
27.tq: Odd-one-out: Milindapanho, Dipavamsa, Mahavamsa, Divyavadana are Buddhist.
xs: **Milindapanho** is a **Buddhist** text, not Jain — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Acharanga Sutra** (monks' code of conduct), **Bhagavati Sutra** (doctrines) and **Kalpasutra** are Jain texts.
xa: Other Buddhist texts in the same odd-one-out set: **Dipavamsa**, **Mahavamsa**, **Divyavadana**.
**Nettipakarana** and **Avadanashataka** are also Buddhist (**UPSC 2022**).
**Kalpasutra** = **Bhadrabahu**; it covers Jinacharitra, Sthaviravali and Samachari.

27.s: Which one of the following works is correctly matched with its author?
27.x: Kalpasutra is attributed to Bhadrabahu and includes Jinacharitra, Sthaviravali and Samachari. Parishishtaparvan is by Hemachandra, Mahapurana by Jinasena and Tattvartha Sutra by Umasvati.
27.tq: Start with the known author–work pair and reject the cross-paired scholars.
xs: **Kalpasutra** is by **Bhadrabahu** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Parishishtaparvan** is by **Hemachandra**, not Jinasena; **Mahapurana** is by **Jinasena**, not Umasvati.
**Tattvartha Sutra** is by **Umasvati**, not Hemachandra.
xa: Kalpasutra contains the **Jinacharitra**, **Sthaviravali** and **Samachari**.
**Samayasara**, **Yogasara**, **Pravachanasara** and **Panchastikaya** are by **Kundakundacharya**.
**Kalyanakaraka** (medical) = **Ugradityacharya**; **Yasastilaka Champu** and **Nitivakyamrita** = **Somadeva Suri**.

27.s: The Tattvartha Sutra is significant in Jainism because it:
o: contains core Jain doctrines and is accepted in versions by both major sects
is a Jain version of the Mahabharata composed by Somadeva Suri
records only the biographies of the Svetambara monks
is a medical treatise written for the Rashtrakuta court
27.x: The Tattvartha Sutra, associated with Umasvati, presents core Jain doctrines and is accepted in versions by both the Digambara and Svetambara traditions.
27.tq: Identify the work from its function and cross-sectarian significance.
xs: The Tattvartha Sutra contains **core Jain doctrines** and is **accepted in versions by both** major sects — so option **(1)** is correct.
Its author is **Umasvati**.
The **Harivamsha Purana** is the Jain Mahabharata; **Somadeva Suri** wrote **Yasastilaka Champu**; the medical treatise is **Kalyanakaraka**.
xa: **Kalpasutra** = **Bhadrabahu**; **Parishishtaparvan** = **Hemachandra**.
**Mahapurana** and **Adipurana** (life of Rishabha) = **Jinasena**.
**Jinendra Kalyanabhyudayamu** = **Appayacharya**, dedicated to Kakatiya **Prataparudra**.

27.s: Parishishtaparvan, also known as Sthaviravali Charitra, was written by:
27.x: Parishishtaparvan or Sthaviravali Charitra was written by Hemachandra in the twelfth century. It is regarded as a source for the Svetambara–Digambara split.
27.tq: Combine the alternate title, author and period to avoid author substitution.
xs: **Parishishtaparvan (Sthaviravali Charitra)** was written by **Hemachandra** (12th c.) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Jinasena** wrote the Mahapurana and Adipurana; **Somadeva Suri** the Yasastilaka Champu; **Umasvati** the Tattvartha Sutra.
xa: It is the source for the **Svetambara-Digambara split** and the **12-year famine** story.
Hemachandra's patron was **Kumarapala**, **Chalukya (Solanki)** of Gujarat.
⚠ **Kumarapala** – **Hemachandra**; **Amoghavarsha I** – **Jinasena**.

27.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Harivamsha Purana — Jain version of the Mahabharata
27.x: Jinendra Kalyanabhyudayamu was written by Appayacharya and dedicated to Kakatiya Prataparudra. Adipurana is by Jinasena, Yasastilaka Champu by Somadeva Suri, and Harivamsha Purana is the Jain version of the Mahabharata.
27.tq: Find the work with the swapped author while retaining the correct associations in the other pairs.
xs: The wrong pair is **(4)**: **Jinendra Kalyanabhyudayamu** is by **Appayacharya (Appayaryudu)**, not Hemachandra.
It was dedicated to Kakatiya **Prataparudra**.
The other pairs are right: **Yasastilaka Champu** — Somadeva Suri; **Adipurana** — Jinasena; **Harivamsha Purana** — Jain Mahabharata.
xa: **Hemachandra** wrote the **Parishishtaparvan** (Sthaviravali Charitra).
Somadeva Suri also wrote the **Nitivakyamrita**.
**Kalyanakaraka** (medical treatise) is by **Ugradityacharya**, composed at **Ramatirtham**.

27.s: Which set consists entirely of works associated with Kundakundacharya?
27.x: Yogasara, Pravachanasara and Panchastikaya are associated with Kundakundacharya. The other sets combine works of Bhadrabahu, Hemachandra, Jinasena, Somadeva Suri or Ugradityacharya.
27.tq: Choose the option whose entire group shares one author, not merely one correct pair.
xs: **Yogasara, Pravachanasara and Panchastikaya** are all by **Kundakundacharya** — so option **(1)** is correct.
(2) mixes **Bhadrabahu**, **Hemachandra** and **Umasvati**; (3) has Jinasena's works plus the **Harivamsha Purana**.
(4) mixes **Somadeva Suri** with **Ugradityacharya**'s Kalyanakaraka.
xa: Kundakundacharya also wrote **Samayasara**.
He founded the **Saraswati gachcha** at **Konakondla** (Anantapur).
Exam angle: **Samayasara** (asked **2008** and **2019**), **Yogasara** (**2017**).

27.s: Samayasara, a Jain work asked about in more than one examination, was written by
27.x: Samayasara (like Yogasara, Pravachanasara and Panchastikaya) is by Kundakundacharya, who founded the Saraswati gachcha at Konakondla in Anantapur. Hemachandra wrote Parishishtaparvan, Jinasena the Adipurana/Mahapurana, and Umasvati the Tattvartha Sutra.
27.tq: Samayasara, Yogasara = Kundakundacharya (Konakondla, Anantapur).
xs: **Samayasara** was written by **Kundakundacharya** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Hemachandra** wrote the Parishishtaparvan; **Jinasena** the Adipurana / Mahapurana; **Umasvati** the Tattvartha Sutra.
xa: Samayasara was asked in **2008** and **2019**; **Yogasara** in **2017** — both Kundakundacharya.
His other works: **Pravachanasara** and **Panchastikaya**.
He founded the **Saraswati gachcha** at **Konakondla**, Anantapur.

27.s: Which one of the following is a Buddhist work and NOT a Jain work?
27.x: Nettipakarana (like the Avadanashataka) is a Buddhist text (UPSC 2022). Kalpasutra (Bhadrabahu), Tattvartha Sutra (Umasvati) and Parishishtaparvan (Hemachandra) are Jain works.
27.tq: Nettipakarana, Avadanashataka = Buddhist.
xs: **Nettipakarana** is a **Buddhist** work — so option **(1)** is correct (**UPSC 2022**).
**Kalpasutra** (Bhadrabahu), **Tattvartha Sutra** (Umasvati) and **Parishishtaparvan** (Hemachandra) are Jain works.
xa: **Avadanashataka** is also Buddhist, not Jain.
Other Buddhist texts used as odd-ones-out: **Dipavamsa**, **Mahavamsa**, **Divyavadana**, **Milindapanho**.
Jain texts: **Acharanga**, **Bhagavati**, **Kalpasutra**, **Sutrakritanga**.

27.s:
Consider the following statements about the language and literature of Jainism:
1. Early Jains discarded Sanskrit and preached in the popular Prakrit.
2. The Jain canon was composed in Ardhamagadhi.
3. Jains produced the first grammar of Pali.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
27.x: Statement 1 is correct: early Jains used popular Prakrit instead of Sanskrit, which helped their spread. Statement 2 is correct: the canon is in Ardhamagadhi, an eastern Prakrit. Statement 3 is wrong: Jains wrote the earliest important works in Apabhramsa and its first grammar, not Pali (Pali is the language of the Buddhist Tripitaka). So '1 and 2 only'.
27.tq: Jain = Prakrit/Ardhamagadhi/Apabhramsa; Buddhist = Pali.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: early Jains **discarded Sanskrit** and preached in popular **Prakrit** — key to their spread.
Statement 2 is correct: the canon is in **Ardhamagadhi**.
Statement 3 is wrong: Jains wrote the earliest important works in **Apabhramsa** and its first grammar, not Pali — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
xa: Later Jain literature was rich in **Prakrit**, **Sanskrit** and regional languages (**Kannada**, **Tamil**, **Telugu**).
It covered **grammar**, **poetry** and **mathematics**.
Significance: Jainism enriched **Prakrit**, **Apabhramsa**, **Kannada** and **Telugu**.

27.s: Which social group formed the principal social base of Jainism in urban and commercial centres?
27.x: Traders, merchants and commercial communities supported Jainism, particularly in urban centres.
27.tq: Link the religion with its stated social base.
xs: Jainism's social base was **traders and merchants** (commercial communities) — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was linked with **banking** and **urban growth**.
xa: **Agriculture** was avoided because it **harms life** (strict ahimsa).
**Jain merchant guilds** moved along **Satavahana trade routes**.
In Andhra under the Eastern Chalukyas, **Shudras** adopted Jainism for social advancement.

27.s: Why did strict Jain followers generally avoid agriculture?
o: Agriculture involved harm to living beings.
Agriculture was associated with royal taxation.
Agriculture was considered unsuitable for merchants only.
Agriculture required the use of Sanskrit texts.
27.x: Strict ahimsa made agriculture problematic because ploughing and related activities could injure living organisms.
27.tq: Apply the principle of ahimsa to an economic activity.
xs: Strict Jains avoided agriculture because it **harms life** — so option **(1)** is correct.
This follows from **strict ahimsa**.
xa: Hence their base became **traders and merchants**, with **banking** and **urban growth**.
**Jain merchant guilds** moved on **Satavahana trade routes**.
Jainism also **promoted vegetarianism**.

27.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the social teachings of Jainism:
1. Jainism challenged caste hierarchy.
2. It stressed action over birth.
3. It promoted vegetarianism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: Jainism challenged birth-based hierarchy, emphasised conduct and action, and promoted vegetarianism in accordance with ahimsa.
27.tq: Check whether all three related social principles belong together.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: Jainism **challenged caste hierarchy**.
Statement 2 is correct: it stressed **action over birth**.
Statement 3 is correct: it **promoted vegetarianism** — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
xa: In Andhra under the **Eastern Chalukyas**, **Shudras** adopted Jainism for social advancement.
Its base: **traders and merchants**; agriculture was avoided under **strict ahimsa**.
Decline: loss of **royal patronage**, sect split, **severe austerity**, no missionary zeal, rival **Bhakti** revival.

27.s: In the Eastern Chalukya period in Andhra, which group adopted Jainism for social advancement?
27.x: In Andhra under the Eastern Chalukyas, Shudras adopted Jainism as a means of social advancement.
27.tq: Use the region–period–social group combination.
xs: Under the **Eastern Chalukyas**, **Shudras** adopted Jainism for **social advancement** — so option **(2)** is correct.
This fits Jainism's challenge to **caste hierarchy** and its stress on **action over birth**.
xa: **Potla Cheruvu** was a famous Jain centre of the Eastern Chalukya period (**APPSC G2 2017**).
**Ayyana Mahadevi**, wife of **Vishnuvardhana**, built the **Nedumbasadi** at **Bejawada**.
**Vimaladitya** was a patron; **Durgaraja** built the **Kathikabharana Jinalaya** at **Dharmavaram**.

27.s: Kharavela, the Jain patron associated with the Hathigumpha inscription, belonged to which dynasty?
27.x: Kharavela was a Chedi or Mahameghavahana king of Kalinga in the second century BCE. His activities are known particularly from the Hathigumpha inscription.
27.tq: Use the dynasty–ruler association and reject swapped-ruler traps.
xs: **Kharavela** belonged to the **Chedi (Mahameghavahana)** dynasty of **Kalinga** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He ruled in the **2nd c. BCE** and is known from the **Hathigumpha inscription**.
**Udayin** was **Haryanka**; **Indra III** and **Amoghavarsha I** were **Rashtrakutas**; **Samprati** and **Chandragupta** were **Mauryas**.
xa: His influence reached **Srikakulam-Vizianagaram**; he built a Jain vihara near **Vardhamanapuram**.
The **Udayagiri-Khandagiri** rock-cut caves near **Bhubaneswar** were made under him.
⚠ **Samprati** = "Ashoka of Jainism"; **Kharavela** = Kalinga, Hathigumpha.

27.s: Kharavela's influence, as indicated in the historical tradition associated with him, extended to which present-day Andhra Pradesh districts?
27.x: Kharavela's influence extended to the areas corresponding to present-day Srikakulam and Vizianagaram districts.
27.tq: Apply the location trap by distinguishing neighbouring Andhra regions.
xs: Kharavela's influence extended over **Srikakulam and Vizianagaram** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He was a **Chedi** king of **Kalinga** and a staunch Jain patron.
xa: He built a **Jain vihara** near **Vardhamanapuram**.
**Vaddamanu** had **Samprati**'s vihara (also linked with Kharavela).
⚠ **Kurnool** and **Anantapur** lie on the **Rayalaseema** route of the Jain migration south.

27.s:
Consider the following statements about Chandragupta Maurya:
1. He became a disciple of Bhadrabahu.
2. He migrated to the south.
3. He died by adopting sallekhana at Shravanabelagola.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: Chandragupta Maurya is traditionally described as a disciple of Bhadrabahu who migrated south and ended his life by sallekhana at Shravanabelagola.
27.tq: Check each statement independently before selecting the combined code.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Chandragupta Maurya** was a disciple of **Bhadrabahu**.
Statement 2 is correct: he **migrated south** with him after the **12-year famine**.
Statement 3 is correct: he died by **sallekhana** at **Shravanabelagola** — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
xa: Bhadrabahu was the **6th Thera**; this spread was asked in **APPSC G2 2003**.
**Samprati**, Ashoka's grandson, is the "**Ashoka of Jainism**".
**Udayin** (Haryanka), successor of Ajatashatru, was a devoted Jain per Jain tradition.

27.s: Samprati, the grandson of Ashoka, is popularly described in Jain tradition as the:
27.x: Samprati, the grandson of Ashoka, is known as the “Ashoka of Jainism” because of his role in spreading Jainism.
27.tq: Test the distinctive epithet rather than the dynasty alone.
xs: **Samprati**, Ashoka's grandson, is called the "**Ashoka of Jainism**" — so option **(1)** is correct.
He **spread Jainism in Andhra and the south**.
xa: His vihara was at **Vaddamanu** (Vaddemanu).
He ruled c. **230-215 BCE**; the PM inaugurated the **Samrat Samprati Museum** at **Koba, Gujarat** (Apr **2026**).
⚠ **Kharavela** = Kalinga, **Hathigumpha**; **Chandragupta Maurya** = disciple of **Bhadrabahu**.

27.s:
Consider the following statements about royal patrons of Jainism:
1. Amoghavarsha I, a Rashtrakuta ruler, was a patron of Jinasena.
2. Kumarapala, the patron of Hemachandra, belonged to the Western Ganga dynasty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
27.x: Statement 1 is correct: Rashtrakuta Amoghavarsha I patronised Jinasena. Statement 2 is wrong: Kumarapala was a Chalukya (Solanki) ruler of Gujarat; the Western Gangas are linked with minister Chamundaraya and the Gommateshwara statue. Hence '1 only'.
27.tq: Kumarapala-Hemachandra = Gujarat Solankis; Gangas = Chamundaraya/Gommateshwara.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Amoghavarsha I** (Rashtrakuta) was a patron of **Jinasena**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Kumarapala** was a **Chalukya (Solanki) of Gujarat**, not a Western Ganga — so option **(1) 1 only** is correct.
The **Western Gangas** are linked with minister **Chamundaraya** and the **Gommateshwara** statue.
xa: Kumarapala is linked with 12th-c. councils at **Vallabhi** and **Mathura**, with **Hemachandra** presiding.
Rashtrakuta **Indra III** built a Jain kshetra at **Danavulapadu** (Kadapa).
Jinasena wrote the **Mahapurana** and **Adipurana** (life of Rishabha).

27.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Western Gangas — Jain kshetra at Danavulapadu
27.x: Indra III of the Rashtrakuta dynasty built a Jain kshetra at Danavulapadu in Kadapa. The other monuments are associated with different dynasties or patrons.
27.tq: Start from the sure monument–dynasty pair and eliminate swapped locations.
xs: **Rashtrakuta** Indra III built a **Jain kshetra at Danavulapadu** (Kadapa) — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Kathikabharana Jinalaya** at Dharmavaram was built by **Durgaraja** (Eastern Chalukya), not the Mauryas.
**Gommateshwara** was raised by **Chamundaraya**, a **Western Ganga** minister, not the Eastern Chalukyas.
xa: Rashtrakuta **Amoghavarsha I** was the patron of **Jinasena**.
**Munugodu** had the Svetambara monastery **Pudvithilakavasati**.
⚠ **Nedumbasadi** = Ayyana Mahadevi; **Kadalalaya Basadi** = Mailama; **Kathikabharana Jinalaya** = Durgaraja.

27.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Jainism in Andhra:
1. Srimukha or Simuka is regarded as the first Satavahana patron of Jainism.
2. According to the Kalpa Pradeepa, his 52 army chiefs built 52 Jain temples.
3. The Eastern Chalukyas and the Kakatiyas subsequently followed the Satavahana association with Jainism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: Simuka or Srimukha is identified as the first Satavahana Jain patron; the Kalpa Pradeepa attributes 52 Jain temples to his 52 army chiefs. Eastern Chalukyas and Kakatiyas also followed this tradition.
27.tq: Combine the ruler, numerical detail and dynastic succession before choosing the code.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Srimukha (Simuka)** was the first Satavahana patron of Jainism in Andhra (basadi at **Kandapur**).
Statement 2 is correct: per the **Kalpa Pradeepa** (Jinaprabha Suri), his **52 army chiefs built 52 Jain temples**.
Statement 3 is correct: the order is **Satavahanas → Eastern Chalukyas → Kakatiyas** — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
xa: The early **Kakatiyas** were Jains (**Siddeshwara Charitra**).
Kakatiya minister Betana's wife **Mailama** built the **Kadalalaya Basadi** (**1117 CE** Padmakshi inscription).
Later, **Ganapatideva** persecuted Jains (Siddeshwara Charitra).

27.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
27.x: Indra III built a Jain kshetra at Danavulapadu in Kadapa, not the Gommateshwara statue at Shravanabelagola. Ayyana Mahadevi, Vimaladitya and Durgaraja are correctly associated with the Eastern Chalukya Jain tradition.
27.tq: Find the incorrectly assigned builder rather than the incorrectly named monument.
xs: The wrong pair is **(4)**: **Indra III** (Rashtrakuta) built a Jain kshetra at **Danavulapadu**, not the **Gommateshwara at Shravanabelagola**.
Gommateshwara was raised by **Chamundaraya**, a **Western Ganga** minister.
The other pairs are right: **Vimaladitya** a patron; **Ayyana Mahadevi** — **Nedumbasadi** at Bejawada; **Durgaraja** — **Kathikabharana Jinalaya**.
xa: Ayyana Mahadevi was the wife of **Vishnuvardhana**; the village **Mushinikonda** was donated.
**Potla Cheruvu** was a famous Eastern Chalukya-era Jain centre (**APPSC G2 2017**).
**Ramatirtham** (Vizianagaram) was an Eastern Chalukya Jain hill centre where **Ugraditya** composed Kalyanakaraka.

27.s:
Consider the following statements about the Mahamastakabhisheka:
1. It is performed for the Gommateshwara (Bahubali) statue every 12 years.
2. The 88th Mahamastakabhisheka was held in February 2018.
3. It is performed at Mount Abu in Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
27.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Gommateshwara Mahamastakabhisheka is held every 12 years. Statement 2 is correct: the 88th was in February 2018. Statement 3 is wrong: Gommateshwara is at Shravanabelagola, Karnataka; Mount Abu has the Dilwara temples. So '1 and 2 only'.
27.tq: Gommateshwara = Shravanabelagola; Mount Abu = Dilwara.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Mahamastakabhisheka** of **Gommateshwara (Bahubali)** is held every **12 years**.
Statement 2 is correct: the **88th** was in **February 2018**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it is at **Shravanabelagola**, Karnataka — **Mount Abu** has the **Dilwara** temples. So option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
xa: The statue was raised by **Chamundaraya**, a **Ganga** minister, c. **983 AD**.
The **Dilwara temples** were built by **Vimala Shah**, a Solanki minister, in **1031**.
Shravanabelagola is where **Chandragupta Maurya** died by **sallekhana**.

27.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Site)
 a. Dilwara temples
 b. Shravanabelagola
 c. Udayagiri-Khandagiri
 d. Sammed Shikhar

List-II (Region)
 i. Jharkhand
 ii. Karnataka
 iii. Rajasthan
 iv. Odisha

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
27.x: Dilwara is at Mount Abu in Rajasthan, Shravanabelagola is in Karnataka, Udayagiri-Khandagiri is in Odisha, and Sammed Shikhar is in Jharkhand.
27.tq: Start with the distinctive Shravanabelagola and Sammed Shikhar locations.
xs: **Dilwara temples** — Mount Abu, **Rajasthan** (a–iii); **Shravanabelagola** — **Karnataka** (b–ii).
**Udayagiri-Khandagiri** — **Odisha** (c–iv); **Sammed Shikhar** — **Jharkhand** (d–i).
So option **(1) a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i** is correct.
xa: Sammed Shikhar (on **Parasnath hill**) marks **Parsvanatha's nirvana**.
Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves near **Bhubaneswar** were cut under **Kharavela**.
**Prabhasgiri (Pabhosa)** is near **Kaushambi**, Uttar Pradesh; the **Ellora** Jain caves are in Maharashtra.

27.s: Udayagiri-Khandagari caves are associated with which ruler?
27.x: The rock-cut caves at Udayagiri-Khandagiri were created under Kharavela in Odisha.
27.tq: Apply the ruler–monument association used in history questions.
xs: The **Udayagiri-Khandagiri** caves are linked with **Kharavela** — so option **(1)** is correct.
They are rock-cut caves near **Bhubaneswar**, Odisha.
**Chamundaraya** raised the **Gommateshwara**; **Kumarapala** was the patron of **Hemachandra**; **Chandragupta Maurya** went to **Shravanabelagola**.
xa: Kharavela, a **Chedi (Mahameghavahana)** king of **Kalinga**, is known from the **Hathigumpha inscription**.
His influence reached **Srikakulam-Vizianagaram**.
⚠ **Udayagiri-Khandagiri** = Odisha; **Dilwara** = Rajasthan; **Sammed Shikhar** = Jharkhand.

27.s: Sammed Shikhar, also known as Shikharji, is located on which hill?
27.x: Sammed Shikhar or Shikharji is situated on Parasnath Hill in Jharkhand and is associated with the nirvana of Parsvanatha.
27.tq: Distinguish the pilgrim site from the nearby monument locations.
xs: **Sammed Shikhar (Shikharji)** is on **Parasnath hill** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is in **Jharkhand** and marks **Parsvanatha's nirvana**.
**Mount Abu** has the **Dilwara** temples; **Nallamala** caves held early Jain ascetic camps in Andhra.
xa: ⚠ **Sammed Shikhar** = Jharkhand; **Dilwara** = Mount Abu, Rajasthan; **Udayagiri-Khandagiri** = Odisha.
**Shravanabelagola** (Karnataka) has the **Gommateshwara**, with a **Mahamastakabhisheka** every **12 years**.

27.s: Which one of the following statements about Jain monuments is correct?
o: The Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves are located in Maharashtra and were built by Chamundaraya.
The Jain caves at Ellora are located in Jharkhand.
The Dilwara temples were built at Shravanabelagola by Kharavela.
The Dilwara temples are located at Mount Abu and are associated with Vimala Shah, a Solanki minister.
27.x: The Dilwara temples are at Mount Abu in Rajasthan and are associated with Vimala Shah, a Solanki minister.
27.tq: Reject swapped builders and locations in a monument question.
xs: The **Dilwara temples** are at **Mount Abu** and linked with **Vimala Shah**, a **Solanki minister** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Udayagiri-Khandagiri** is in **Odisha**, cut under **Kharavela** — not Maharashtra or Chamundaraya.
The **Ellora** Jain caves are in **Maharashtra**, not Jharkhand; Dilwara is not at Shravanabelagola.
xa: Dilwara dates to **1031**; **Ranakpur** is also listed with it.
**Chamundaraya**, a Ganga minister, raised the **Gommateshwara** at Shravanabelagola c. **983 AD**.
**Sammed Shikhar** (Parasnath hill, Jharkhand) marks **Parsvanatha's nirvana**.

27.s:
Which of the following statements about Gommateshwara is correct?
1. It is located at Shravanabelagola in Karnataka.
2. It is associated with Bahubali.
3. It was consecrated by Chamundaraya, a Ganga minister, around 983 CE.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: Gommateshwara is the Bahubali statue at Shravanabelagola, associated with Chamundaraya and dated to about 983 CE.
27.tq: Combine monument, identity, patron and date in a coded statement question.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Gommateshwara** stands at **Shravanabelagola**, Karnataka.
Statement 2 is correct: it is the statue of **Bahubali**.
Statement 3 is correct: it was raised by **Chamundaraya**, a **Ganga** minister, c. **983** — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
xa: Its **Mahamastakabhisheka** is held every **12 years**; the **88th** was in **February 2018**.
Chamundaraya served the **Western Gangas**, a Karnataka dynasty.
Shravanabelagola is where **Chandragupta Maurya** died by **sallekhana**, after migrating with **Bhadrabahu**.

27.s: Potla Cheruvu was a famous Jain centre during the reign of which dynasty in Andhra?
27.x: Potla Cheruvu was a prominent Jain centre during the Eastern Chalukya period.
27.tq: Use the dynasty–centre association to eliminate nearby Andhra patrons.
xs: **Potla Cheruvu** was a famous Jain centre in the **Eastern Chalukya** period — so option **(4)** is correct (**APPSC G2 2017**).
The Rashtrakutas are linked with **Danavulapadu**; Vijayanagara with **Devaraya II**'s Jinalaya in Pan Supari Bazar.
xa: Eastern Chalukya Jain sites: **Nedumbasadi** (Bejawada), **Ramatirtham** (Vizianagaram), **Kathikabharana Jinalaya** (Dharmavaram).
Order of Jain dynasties in Andhra: **Satavahanas → Eastern Chalukyas → Kakatiyas**.
Under the Eastern Chalukyas, **Shudras** adopted Jainism for social advancement.

27.s: Nedumba Vasati at Bejawada was built by:
27.x: Nedumba Vasati at Bejawada, or Vijayawada, was built by Ayyana Mahadevi, the wife of Eastern Chalukya Vishnuvardhana.
27.tq: Apply the person–foundation trap by separating the builder from other Jain patrons.
xs: **Nedumba Vasati** at **Bejawada** was built by **Ayyana Mahadevi**, wife of Eastern Chalukya **Vishnuvardhana** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Mailama** built the **Kadalalaya Basadi**; **Durgaraja** built the **Kathikabharana Jinalaya**; **Samprati** is linked with **Vaddamanu**.
xa: The village **Mushinikonda** was donated to the Nedumbasadi.
Bejawada = **Vijayawada**.
⚠ **Nedumbasadi** = Ayyana Mahadevi; **Kadalalaya Basadi** = Mailama; **Kathikabharana Jinalaya** = Durgaraja.

27.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Jain patronage among the Eastern Chalukyas:
1. Vimaladitya was one of the Eastern Chalukya patrons of Jainism.
2. Durgaraja built the Kathikabharana Jinalaya at Dharmavaram.
3. Kathikabharana Jinalaya was built at Danavulapadu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: Vimaladitya was an Eastern Chalukya patron, and Durgaraja built the Kathikabharana Jinalaya at Dharmavaram. The statement placing it at Danavulapadu is false.
27.tq: Find the wrong location while retaining the correctly matched patron and monument.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Vimaladitya** was an Eastern Chalukya patron of Jainism.
Statement 2 is correct: **Durgaraja** built the **Kathikabharana Jinalaya** at **Dharmavaram**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Danavulapadu** (Kadapa) is linked with Rashtrakuta **Indra III** — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
xa: **Ayyana Mahadevi**'s **Nedumbasadi** at Bejawada is another Eastern Chalukya Jain site.
**Potla Cheruvu** was a famous Eastern Chalukya-era Jain centre (**APPSC G2 2017**).
Decline: a Jain monk fled **Rajaraja Narendra**'s persecution to **Hanamkonda** (Orugallu Kaifiyat).

27.s: Ramatirtham, also known as Ramagiri, is located in which district and is associated with which Jain scholar?
27.x: Ramatirtham, or Ramagiri, is a Jain hill centre in Vizianagaram, where Ugraditya composed the Kalyanakaraka.
27.tq: Combine place and associated personality to avoid confusing neighbouring Jain centres.
xs: **Ramatirtham (Ramagiri)** is in **Vizianagaram**, and **Ugraditya** composed the **Kalyanakaraka** there — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was an **Eastern Chalukya-era** Jain hill centre.
**Indra III** is linked with **Danavulapadu** (Kadapa); **Durgaraja** with **Dharmavaram**.
xa: The **Kalyanakaraka** is a **medical treatise** by **Ugradityacharya**.
Other Jain centres: **Aryavatam** (Bikkavolu), **Kolanupaka**, **Munugodu**.
**Kharavela**'s influence covered **Srikakulam-Vizianagaram**.

27.s: Vaddamanu is associated with which of the following descriptions?
o: The Samprati vihara, followed later by Sadavanshiya patronage
27.x: Vaddamanu was associated with Samprati’s vihara and later received Sadavanshiya patronage.
27.tq: Match the centre with its distinctive institutional history.
xs: **Vaddamanu** had **Samprati's vihara**, with later **Sadavanshiya** patronage — so option **(3)** is correct.
The site is also linked with **Kharavela**.
**Nedumbasadi** = Ayyana Mahadevi (Bejawada); **Kadalalaya Basadi** = Mailama; **Devaraya II** built a Jinalaya in Pan Supari Bazar.
xa: **Samprati**, Ashoka's grandson, is the "**Ashoka of Jainism**" and spread Jainism in Andhra and the south.
He ruled c. **230-215 BCE**; the **Samrat Samprati Museum** opened at **Koba**, Gujarat (Apr **2026**).

27.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Jain centre)
a. Danavulapadu
b. Vijayawada
c. Munugodu
 d. Ramatirtham

List-II (Association)
i. Svetambara monastery Pudvithilakavasati
ii. Eastern Chalukya-era centre
iii. Nedumbasadi of Ayyana Mahadevi
iv. Rashtrakuta Indra III

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
27.x: Danavulapadu is associated with Rashtrakuta Indra III; Vijayawada with Ayyana Mahadevi’s Nedumbasadi; Munugodu with Pudvithilakavasati; and Ramatirtham with the Eastern Chalukya period.
27.tq: Start from the sure centre–patron pairs and then complete the remaining matches.
xs: **Danavulapadu** — Rashtrakuta **Indra III** (a–iv); **Vijayawada** — **Nedumbasadi** of Ayyana Mahadevi (b–iii).
**Munugodu** — Svetambara monastery **Pudvithilakavasati** (c–i); **Ramatirtham** — **Eastern Chalukya-era** centre (d–ii).
So option **(1) a–iv, b–iii, c–i, d–ii** is correct.
xa: Danavulapadu is in **Kadapa**; Ramatirtham (Ramagiri) is in **Vizianagaram**.
**Ugraditya** composed the **Kalyanakaraka** at Ramatirtham.
**Potla Cheruvu** was another famous Eastern Chalukya Jain centre (**APPSC G2 2017**).

27.s: Who built a Jinalaya in Pan Supari Bazar?
27.x: Vijayanagara ruler Devaraya II built a Jinalaya in Pan Supari Bazar.
27.tq: Apply the ruler–construction association trap.
xs: **Devaraya II** of **Vijayanagara** built a Jinalaya in **Pan Supari Bazar** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Ganapatideva** persecuted Jains; **Indra III** built a Jain kshetra at **Danavulapadu**; **Vishnuvardhana**'s wife built the Nedumbasadi.
xa: Kakatiya minister Betana's wife **Mailama** built the **Kadalalaya Basadi** (**1117 CE** Padmakshi inscription).
Eastern Chalukya patrons: **Vimaladitya**, and **Durgaraja** (Kathikabharana Jinalaya at Dharmavaram).

27.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the decline and persecution of Jainism in the Andhra region are correct?
1. Ganapatideva persecuted Jains, as indicated in Siddeshwara Charitra.
2. A Jain monk fled the persecution of Rajaraja Narendra to Hanamkonda.
3. The account of the monk’s flight is associated with the Orugallu Kaifiyat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: All three statements are correct. Ganapatideva’s persecution is mentioned in Siddeshwara Charitra, while the flight of a Jain monk to Hanamkonda from Rajaraja Narendra’s persecution is recorded in the Orugallu Kaifiyat.
27.tq: Check whether all three statements refer to the correct source, persecutor and refuge.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Ganapatideva** persecuted Jains (**Siddeshwara Charitra**).
Statement 2 is correct: a Jain monk fled **Rajaraja Narendra**'s persecution to **Hanamkonda**.
Statement 3 is correct: this flight is recorded in the **Orugallu Kaifiyat** — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
xa: The **Siddeshwara Charitra** also says the **early Kakatiyas were Jains**.
Ganapatideva's persecution at **Anmakonda** is tied to **Kalamukha / Vira Shaiva** hostility.
Decline factors: loss of **royal patronage**, sect split, **severe austerity**, no missionary zeal, rival **Bhakti** revival.

27.s: The Kadalalaya Basadi, known from the 1117 CE Padmakshi inscription, was built by
o: Mailama, wife of the Kakatiya minister Betana
27.x: Mailama, wife of the Kakatiya minister Betana, built the Kadalalaya Basadi (1117 CE Padmakshi inscription). Ayyana Mahadevi built the Nedumbasadi at Bejawada, Durgaraja the Kathikabharana Jinalaya at Dharmavaram, and Devaraya II a Jinalaya in Pan Supari Bazar.
27.tq: Kadalalaya Basadi = Mailama (Kakatiya), Padmakshi inscription.
xs: The **Kadalalaya Basadi** was built by **Mailama, wife of the Kakatiya minister Betana** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Its source is the **1117 CE Padmakshi inscription**.
**Ayyana Mahadevi** built the **Nedumbasadi**; **Durgaraja** the **Kathikabharana Jinalaya**; **Devaraya II** a Jinalaya in Pan Supari Bazar.
xa: The **early Kakatiyas** were Jains (**Siddeshwara Charitra**).
Later Kakatiya **Ganapatideva** persecuted Jains.
**Appayacharya**'s **Jinendra Kalyanabhyudayamu** was dedicated to Kakatiya **Prataparudra**.

27.s: Which one of the following correctly expresses the regional distribution of Jainism and Buddhism in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Jainism held the Krishna-Godavari delta, while Buddhism held Rayalaseema.
Jainism was confined to the eastern coast, while Buddhism held the North Coastal borderlands.
Jainism held the rocky Rayalaseema and North Coastal borderlands, while Buddhism held the Krishna-Godavari delta.
Both Jainism and Buddhism were confined exclusively to the Krishna-Godavari delta.
27.x: Jainism was associated with the rocky Rayalaseema and North Coastal borderlands, whereas Buddhism held the Krishna-Godavari delta.
27.tq: Use the reversed-region trap to distinguish the two religious zones.
xs: **Jainism** held the rocky **Rayalaseema** and **North Coastal borderlands**, while **Buddhism** held the **Krishna-Godavari delta** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses the two faiths.
xa: The Jain migration route south passed through **Rayalaseema** (**Kurnool**, **Anantapur**).
Early Jain ascetic camps were in the **Erramala and Nallamala** caves.
**Kharavela**'s influence reached **Srikakulam-Vizianagaram** in the north coast.

27.s: Which of the following was NOT identified as a factor in the decline of Jainism?
27.x: The factors identified were loss of royal patronage, sectarian split, severe austerity, lack of missionary zeal and rival Bhakti revival. Expansion of missionary zeal was not a cause of decline.
27.tq: Look for the reversed meaning of a stated decline factor.
xs: **Expansion of missionary zeal** was NOT a factor — the notes cite **no missionary zeal** as a cause of decline. So option **(2)** is correct.
The real factors: **loss of royal patronage**, **sect split**, **severe austerity**, and a rival **Bhakti revival**.
xa: In Andhra, **Ganapatideva** persecuted Jains at **Anmakonda** (Kalamukha / Vira Shaiva hostility).
A Jain monk fled **Rajaraja Narendra**'s persecution to **Hanamkonda** (Orugallu Kaifiyat).

27.s: Which one of the following correctly states the relationship between Kalamukha/Vira Shaiva hostility and Jainism in the Andhra region?
o: Ganapatideva founded a Jain monastery at Anmakonda, which became a Buddhist refuge.
Ganapatideva persecuted Jains at Anmakonda, while Anmakonda served as a refuge from Eastern Chalukya persecution.
Eastern Chalukyas persecuted Jains only at Danavulapadu, while Anmakonda was a royal Jain capital.
Anmakonda was the site where Samprati built his vihara against Kalamukha hostility.
27.x: The stated regional tradition associates Kalamukha/Vira Shaiva hostility with the persecution of Jains by Ganapatideva at Anmakonda, while Anmakonda also served as a refuge from Eastern Chalukya persecution.
27.tq: Separate the persecuting authority from the place that provided refuge.
xs: **Ganapatideva persecuted Jains at Anmakonda**, while Anmakonda was also a **refuge from Eastern Chalukya persecution** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The hostility is linked with the **Kalamukha / Vira Shaiva** sects.
**Samprati**'s vihara was at **Vaddamanu**, not Anmakonda; **Danavulapadu** is Rashtrakuta Indra III's Jain kshetra.
xa: The source for Ganapatideva's persecution is the **Siddeshwara Charitra**.
A Jain monk fled **Rajaraja Narendra**'s persecution to **Hanamkonda** (**Orugallu Kaifiyat**).

27.s: Jain literature contributed to the enrichment of which group of languages?
27.x: Jain literature enriched Prakrit, Apabhramsa, Kannada and Telugu.
27.tq: Select the complete language group without substituting neighbouring literary languages.
xs: Jain literature enriched **Prakrit, Apabhramsa, Kannada and Telugu** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Pali** is linked with Buddhism; Jains in fact **discarded Sanskrit** early and preached in **Prakrit**.
xa: The Jain canon is in **Ardhamagadhi**.
Jains wrote the **earliest important works in Apabhramsa** and its **first grammar**.
Later works covered **grammar**, **poetry** and **mathematics** in Prakrit, Sanskrit and regional languages.

27.s: Which of the following pairs of architectural sites is associated with Jain architectural significance?
o: Udayagiri and Pan Supari Bazar only
27.x: Jain architectural significance is associated with sites such as Dilwara, Ellora and Udayagiri.
27.tq: Identify the recognised architectural examples rather than regional patronage locations.
xs: **Dilwara and Ellora** are cited for Jain architectural significance — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Udayagiri** is also listed, but **Pan Supari Bazar**, **Anmakonda**, **Hanamkonda**, **Dharmavaram** and **Mushinikonda** are not cited for architectural significance.
xa: **Dilwara** is at **Mount Abu**, Rajasthan, built by **Vimala Shah** (Solanki minister), **1031**.
The **Ellora** Jain caves are in **Maharashtra**.
**Udayagiri-Khandagiri** (Odisha) caves were cut under **Kharavela**.

27.s: In April 2026, the Prime Minister inaugurated the Samrat Samprati Museum connected with Jain heritage at which place?
27.x: The Samrat Samprati Museum was inaugurated at Koba in Gujarat to highlight Jain heritage.
27.tq: Link the current-affairs event with its precise place rather than the broader historical region.
xs: The **Samrat Samprati Museum** was inaugurated at **Koba in Gujarat** (Apr **2026**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Samprati** ruled c. **230-215 BCE**.
xa: Samprati, **Ashoka's grandson**, is the "**Ashoka of Jainism**".
He spread Jainism in **Andhra** and the south; his vihara was at **Vaddamanu**.
⚠ **Kharavela** = Kalinga, **Hathigumpha**; **Samprati** = Maurya.

28.s:
Consider the following statements about the family background of Siddhartha Gautama:
1. His father Suddhodana was the chief of the Sakya clan.
2. His mother Maya was a Koliya princess.
3. He was raised by Mahapajapati Gautami.
4. Yashodhara was his wife and Rahula was his son.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: All four statements correctly describe Siddhartha Gautama's clan, parents, foster mother, wife and son.
28.tq: Treat a biographical cluster as separate statements and verify every relationship.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: father **Suddhodana** was the **Shakya** chief at **Kapilavastu**.
Statement 2 is correct: mother **Maya** was a **Koliya** princess.
Statement 3 is correct: he was raised by foster-mother **Mahapajapati Gautami**.
Statement 4 is correct: wife **Yashodhara**, son **Rahula** — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is correct.
xa: He was **Siddhartha Gautama** of the **Sakya/Shakya** Kshatriya clan.
Charioteer **Channa** and horse **Kanthaka**; teachers **Alara Kalama** and **Uddaka Ramaputta**.
⚠ **Maya** = mother (Koliya); **Mahapajapati Gautami** = foster-mother; **Yashodhara** = wife.

28.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Mahapajapati Gautami — Teacher of Siddhartha's austerities
28.x: Mahapajapati Gautami was Buddha's foster or step-mother, not a teacher of his austerities. Channa, Rahula and Yashodhara are correctly matched.
28.tq: Use a swapped family-role distractor against accurate biographical associations.
xs: The wrong pair is **(4)**: **Mahapajapati Gautami** was his **foster/step-mother**, not a teacher of his austerities.
His teachers were **Alara Kalama** and **Uddaka Ramaputta**.
The rest are right: **Yashodhara** — wife; **Channa** — charioteer; **Rahula** — son.
xa: Mahapajapati Gautami later became the **first nun**, admitted after requests of **Ananda**.
His horse at the Great Renunciation was **Kanthaka**.
Austerities: **six years** with **five ascetics**, later abandoned.

28.s:
Consider the following statements about Siddhartha Gautama before his enlightenment:
1. His teachers were Alara Kalama and Uddaka Ramaputta.
2. He practised austerities with five ascetics for twelve years before abandoning them.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
28.x: Statement 1 is correct: Alara Kalama and Uddaka Ramaputta were his teachers. Statement 2 is wrong: he practised austerities with five ascetics for six years (twelve years of asceticism belongs to Mahavira), then abandoned them and was enlightened at 35. Hence '1 only'.
28.tq: Buddha: 6 years of austerities; Mahavira: 12 years.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: his teachers were **Alara Kalama** and **Uddaka Ramaputta**.
Statement 2 is wrong: he practised austerities with five ascetics for **six years**, not twelve — so option **(1) 1 only** is correct.
He then abandoned them and was enlightened at **35**.
xa: The **four sights** (old man, sick man, corpse, ascetic) led to the **Great Renunciation** at **29**.
Enlightenment came after defeating the temptation of **Mara**, at **Uruvela** under the Bodhi tree.
The **five former companions** later heard his first sermon at **Sarnath** and became Arhats.

28.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the role of Mara in the life of Gautama Buddha?
o: Mara was Buddha's first lay disciple.
Mara presided over the First Buddhist Council.
Mara tempted Buddha before his enlightenment.
Mara was the chief of the Sakya clan.
28.x: Mara is associated with the temptation of Gautama Buddha before his enlightenment.
28.tq: Distinguish a symbolic figure from historical persons in Buddha's biography.
xs: **Mara tempted** the Buddha **before his enlightenment** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He was enlightened at **35** after defeating Mara's temptation.
The first lay disciples were **Tapassu and Bhallika**; **Mahakassapa** presided over the First Council; **Suddhodana** was the Shakya chief.
xa: Enlightenment: **Uruvela**, under the **Bodhi tree**, on the bank of the **Niranjana** — today **Bodh Gaya**, Bihar.
⚠ Ages **29 – 35 – 80** = **Renunciation – Enlightenment – Parinirvana**.

28.s: Which one of the following statements about the succession after Buddha's death is correct?
o: Buddha appointed Bimbisara as the head of the Sangha.
The Dhamma and Vinaya were to serve as the teacher after Buddha's death.
Buddha formally appointed Ajatashatru as his successor.
Buddha nominated Devadatta as the permanent head of the Sangha.
28.x: Buddha did not name an individual successor; the Dhamma and Vinaya were to be the teacher after his death.
28.tq: Apply the distinction between a personal successor and an impersonal institutional authority.
xs: The Buddha named **no successor** — the **Dhamma and Vinaya** were to be the teacher — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Bimbisara** and **Ajatashatru** were **royal disciples** from Magadha, not heads of the Sangha.
xa: **Mahakassapa** presided over the **First Council** and led the Sangha after the Buddha.
At that council **Ananda** recited the **Sutta Pitaka** and **Upali** the **Vinaya Pitaka**.
Last words: "All composite things decay, strive diligently" (**appamadena sampadetha**).

28.s:
With reference to the events in the life of Gautama Buddha, consider the following statements:
1. The Great Renunciation took place at the age of 29.
2. Channa accompanied Siddhartha during the Great Renunciation.
3. Kanthaka was the horse associated with this event.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: The Great Renunciation occurred when Siddhartha was 29 years old, accompanied by the charioteer Channa and the horse Kanthaka.
28.tq: Use a cluster of closely related biographical details and eliminate options by checking each statement.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Great Renunciation (Mahabhinishkramana)** was at age **29**.
Statements 2 and 3 are correct: **Channa** was his charioteer and **Kanthaka** his horse — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
xa: It followed the **four sights**: old man, sick man, corpse, ascetic.
It took place at **Kapilavastu**.
⚠ Ages **29 – 35 – 80** = **Renunciation – Enlightenment – Parinirvana**.

28.s:
Consider the following statements about places in the life of Gautama Buddha:
1. His birth at Lumbini (Rumindei, Nepal) is confirmed by an Ashokan inscribed pillar.
2. He attained enlightenment at Uruvela, on the bank of the Niranjana.
3. Kusinara, where he attained Mahaparinirvana, is identified with present-day Sarnath.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
28.x: Statement 1 is correct: an Ashokan pillar at Lumbini (Rumindei) confirms the birthplace. Statement 2 is correct: enlightenment was at Uruvela (Bodh Gaya) under the Bodhi tree on the Niranjana. Statement 3 is wrong: Kusinara is present-day Kushinagar (UP), capital of the Mallas; Sarnath (Deer Park) is the place of the first sermon. So '1 and 2 only'.
28.tq: Birth-Lumbini, Enlightenment-Bodh Gaya, First sermon-Sarnath, Death-Kushinagar.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Lumbini (Rumindei, Nepal)** is confirmed by an **Ashokan inscribed pillar**.
Statement 2 is correct: enlightenment was at **Uruvela**, on the bank of the **Niranjana** (Bodh Gaya).
Statement 3 is wrong: **Kusinara** is **Kushinagar, UP**; **Sarnath** is the site of the first sermon — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
xa: Birth: **c. 563 BCE**, on Vaishakha Purnima.
Kusinara was the capital of the **Mallas** (Deoria dist.).
Exam angle: "first sermon" = **Sarnath** (APPSC **2012**, **2018**).

28.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
28.x: Sankasya is associated with the descent of Buddha from Trayastrimsa heaven. The First Buddhist Council was held at Rajagriha.
28.tq: Find the one wrong event–place association among nearby Buddhist sites.
xs: The wrong pair is **(4)**: **Sankasya** is the site of the **descent from Trayastrimsa heaven**; the **First Council** was at **Rajagriha**.
The rest are right: **Vaishali** — monkey's honey offering; **Rajagriha** — taming of **Nalagiri**; **Shravasti** — **Twin Miracle**.
xa: **Vaishali** (Bihar) also hosted the **Second Council**.
**Shravasti** (UP) had the **Jetavana Vihara**.
These eight sites are the **Ashtamahasthanas**; **7 of the 8** are in India.

28.s:
With reference to the Ashtamahasthanas, consider the following statements:
1. Seven of the eight places are located in India.
2. Lumbini is one of the eight places.
3. Kushinagar is excluded because it is not associated with Buddha's life.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: Seven of the eight Ashtamahasthanas are in India, and Lumbini is one of them. Kushinagar is included because it is associated with Buddha's Mahaparinirvana.
28.tq: Use an exception-based statement to test both inclusion and geographical distribution.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **7 of the 8** Ashtamahasthanas are in **India**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Lumbini** (Nepal) is one of them.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Kushinagar** is included — it is the site of the **Mahaparinirvana**. So option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
xa: The eight: **Lumbini**, **Bodh Gaya**, **Sarnath**, **Kushinagar**, **Rajagriha**, **Shravasti**, **Vaishali**, **Sankasya**.
Lumbini is the one outside India — **Rumindei, Nepal**.
Kushinagar is in **UP** (Deoria dist.); the Buddha died there at **80**, in **483 BCE**.

28.s: The first sermon of Gautama Buddha, known as Dhammachakra Pravartana, dealt primarily with:
o: The Four Noble Truths and the Noble Eightfold Path
The authority of the Vedas and sacrificial rituals
The theory of the four stages of life
28.x: Dhammachakra Pravartana, the first sermon at Sarnath, expounded the Four Noble Truths and the Noble Eightfold Path.
28.tq: Test the content of a famous event rather than its location, which is a common confusable fact.
xs: The first sermon set out the **Four Noble Truths** and the **Eightfold Path** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was given at the **Deer Park, Sarnath** (Rishipatana), near Varanasi.
The Buddha **rejected Vedic authority and sacrifice**, so (2) is wrong.
xa: **Dhammachakra Pravartana** = "**Turning the Wheel of Dharma**".
Audience: the **five former companions** — **Kondanna, Bhaddiya, Vappa, Mahanama, Assaji** — who became Arhats.
Asked as "first sermon = Sarnath" in APPSC **2012** and **2018**.

28.s: The phrase “Appamadena sampadetha”, associated with the last words of Gautama Buddha, conveys which of the following meanings?
28.x: “Appamadena sampadetha” means “strive diligently” and is associated with Buddha's last words.
28.tq: Translate a distinctive phrase rather than relying on the surrounding historical event.
xs: "**Appamadena sampadetha**" means **strive diligently** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The full last words: "**All composite things decay**, strive diligently".
xa: Mahaparinirvana: **Kusinara** (Kushinagar, UP), age **80**, **483 BCE**; some notes give c. **486** BC.
The Buddha named **no successor** — the **Dhamma and Vinaya** were to be the teacher.
The **last convert** was **Subhadda**, at Kusinara.

28.s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of the five former companions who became arhats after hearing Buddha's first sermon?
o: Bimbisara, Ajatashatru, Prasenajit, Udayana and Pradyota
Kondanna, Bhaddiya, Vappa, Mahanama and Assaji
Alara Kalama, Uddaka Ramaputta, Mara, Subhadda and Mahapajapati
Tapassu, Bhallika, Rahula, Channa and Ananda
28.x: The five former companions were Kondanna, Bhaddiya, Vappa, Mahanama and Assaji; they became arhats after the first sermon.
28.tq: Check completeness of a named list and reject options containing persons from other groups.
xs: The five former companions were **Kondanna, Bhaddiya, Vappa, Mahanama and Assaji** — so option **(2)** is correct.
They heard the first sermon at **Sarnath** and became **Arhats**.
(1) lists **royal** followers; **Tapassu and Bhallika** were the first **lay disciples**; **Alara Kalama** and **Uddaka Ramaputta** were his **teachers**.
xa: They were the five ascetics with whom he had practised austerities for **six years**.
The sermon covered the **Four Noble Truths** and the **Eightfold Path**.

28.s: Gautama Buddha attained Mahaparinirvana at approximately what age and in which year?
28.x: Buddha attained Mahaparinirvana at Kusinara at the age of 80, traditionally dated to 483 BCE; some accounts give an approximate alternative date.
28.tq: Separate the age and date of death from the commonly tested birth and enlightenment figures.
xs: The Buddha attained Mahaparinirvana at **80 years**, in **483 BCE** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**35**, c. **528 BCE** is his enlightenment; **29** is his renunciation; c. **563 BCE** is his birth.
xa: Some notes give c. **486** BC for the Mahaparinirvana.
Place: **Kusinara**, capital of the **Mallas** — Kushinagar, UP (Deoria dist.).
⚠ Ages **29 – 35 – 80** = **Renunciation – Enlightenment – Parinirvana**.

28.s:
Match List-I (Event in the Buddha's life) with List-II (Place):
a. Birth
b. Enlightenment
c. First sermon
d. Mahaparinirvana
i. Kushinagar
ii. Sarnath
iii. Bodh Gaya
iv. Lumbini
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
28.x: Birth = Lumbini (Rumindei, Nepal); Enlightenment = Bodh Gaya (Uruvela); First sermon = Sarnath (Deer Park, Rishipatana); Mahaparinirvana = Kushinagar (Kusinara). The other codes swap Sarnath with Bodh Gaya or Lumbini with Kushinagar.
28.tq: Lumbini - Bodh Gaya - Sarnath - Kushinagar: birth, enlightenment, first sermon, death.
xs: **Birth** — **Lumbini** (a–iv); **Enlightenment** — **Bodh Gaya** (b–iii).
**First sermon** — **Sarnath** (c–ii); **Mahaparinirvana** — **Kushinagar** (d–i).
So option **(1) a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i** is correct.
xa: Lumbini = **Rumindei, Nepal**; Bodh Gaya = ancient **Uruvela**; Kushinagar = **Kusinara**.
This birth-enlightenment-sermon-death match is asked in **APPSC GS**.
**Buddha Purnima / Vesak** marks the birth, enlightenment and death.

28.s: Who were regarded as the first lay disciples of Gautama Buddha?
28.x: The merchants Tapassu and Bhallika are regarded as Buddha's first lay disciples.
28.tq: Separate lay disciples from ordained companions, family members and royal followers.
xs: The first lay disciples were the merchants **Tapassu and Bhallika** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Kondanna** and **Assaji** were among the **five former companions**; **Rahula** was his son and **Channa** his charioteer.
**Bimbisara** and **Ajatashatru** were **royal disciples** of Magadha.
xa: The **last convert** was **Subhadda**, at Kusinara.
**Sariputta** and **Mahamoggallana** were the **chief disciples**.
**Upasaka** = lay follower.

28.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Jina — Mahavira
2. Kevalin — Mahavira
3. Nigantha Nataputta — Mahavira
28.x: Jina, Kevalin and Nigantha Nataputta are all titles or designations associated with Mahavira, not the Buddha.
28.tq: Use confusable religious epithets and identify the person associated with all three terms.
xs: **Jina**, **Kevalin** and **Nigantha Nataputta** are all names of **Mahavira** — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
None of them is a title of the Buddha.
xa: The Buddha's epithets: **Buddha** (Awakened One), **Tathagata** ("thus-gone"), **Shakyamuni** (sage of the Shakyas).
"**Light of Asia**" is the title of **Edwin Arnold**'s poem.
⚠ This is a common **odd-one-out** trap.

28.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Disciple)

a. Ananda
b. Upali
c. Mahakassapa
 d. Subhadda

List-II (Association)
 i. Last convert
 ii. Recited the Vinaya Pitaka
 iii. Personal attendant and reciter of the Sutta Pitaka
 iv. Presided over the First Council

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
28.x: Ananda was the personal attendant and recited the Sutta Pitaka; Upali recited the Vinaya Pitaka; Mahakassapa presided over the First Council; Subhadda was the last convert.
28.tq: Start with the distinctive sure pair and eliminate codes containing swapped disciple roles.
xs: **Ananda** — personal attendant, recited the **Sutta Pitaka** (a–iii); **Upali** — recited the **Vinaya Pitaka** (b–ii).
**Mahakassapa** — presided over the **First Council** (c–iv); **Subhadda** — **last convert** (d–i).
So option **(1) a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i** is correct.
xa: The First Council was held at **Rajagriha** (Rajgir).
Mahakassapa led the Sangha after the Buddha.
⚠ **Ananda** = Sutta; **Upali** = Vinaya; **Mahakassapa** = president.

28.s: The relics of Sariputta and Mahamoggallana are associated with:
28.x: Sariputta and Mahamoggallana were chief disciples, and their relics are associated with Sanchi.
28.tq: Test a disciple-location association without confusing it with a Buddha-life event.
xs: The relics of **Sariputta and Mahamoggallana** are at **Sanchi** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They were the Buddha's **chief disciples**.
xa: The Ministry of Culture sent these relics from Sanchi to **Mongolia** (Jun **2026**).
**Kushinagar** is the site of the Mahaparinirvana; **Vaishali** of the Second Council.
**Ananda** was the personal attendant; **Upali** recited the Vinaya.

28.s: The title 'Light of Asia', used for the Buddha, comes from
28.x: 'Light of Asia' is the title of Edwin Arnold's poem on the Buddha. It is not from an Ashokan inscription, the Mahavamsa or Dharmapala; the Buddha's own epithets are Buddha, Tathagata and Shakyamuni.
28.tq: Light of Asia = Edwin Arnold.
xs: "**Light of Asia**" is the title of **Edwin Arnold's poem** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The Buddha's own epithets are **Buddha**, **Tathagata** and **Shakyamuni**.
**Anagarika Dharmapala** founded the **Maha Bodhi Society** (**1891**); the **Rumindei** pillar confirms the birthplace.
xa: **Tathagata** = "thus-gone"; **Shakyamuni** = sage of the Shakyas.
⚠ **Jina**, **Kevalin** and **Nigantha Nataputta** = **Mahavira**, not the Buddha.

28.s: Which one of the following pairs of a royal disciple of the Buddha and his kingdom is NOT correctly matched?
28.x: Bimbisara and Ajatashatru ruled Magadha, Prasenajit ruled Kosala and Udayana ruled Kausambi. So Ajatashatru - Kosala is wrong.
28.tq: Magadha: Bimbisara, Ajatashatru; Kosala: Prasenajit; Kausambi: Udayana.
xs: The wrong pair is **(4)**: **Ajatashatru** ruled **Magadha**, not Kosala.
The rest are right: **Bimbisara** — Magadha; **Prasenajit** — **Kosala**; **Udayana** — **Kausambi**.
xa: The first lay disciples were the merchants **Tapassu and Bhallika**.
The **First Council** was held at **Rajagriha**, presided over by **Mahakassapa**.
The Buddha tamed the elephant **Nalagiri** at **Rajagriha**.

28.s: Which of the following correctly describes Nirvana in Buddhist teaching?
o: Liberation from suffering and extinction of craving
28.x: Nirvana is liberation from suffering, extinction of craving and freedom from the cycle of rebirth.
28.tq: Distinguish the central Buddhist goal from concepts belonging to other religious traditions.
xs: **Nirvana** is **liberation from suffering** and the **extinction of craving** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It also means freedom from the **cycle of rebirth**; it is the **main goal** (APPSC GS **2012**).
Vedic sacrifice was **rejected**, and God was neither affirmed nor denied.
xa: **Nirodha**, the third Noble Truth, says suffering can end — that cessation is Nirvana.
**Karma**: rebirth continues **till nirvana**.
Three marks: **Anicca**, **Anatta**, **Dukkha**.

28.s: The Buddhist Middle Path primarily rejects which of the following?
o: Both extreme asceticism and sensual indulgence
28.x: The Middle Path avoids both the extreme of severe asceticism and the opposite extreme of sensual indulgence.
28.tq: Identify the principle by applying it to the two extremes it avoids.
xs: The **Middle Path (Madhyama Marga)** rejects both **extreme asceticism** and **sensual indulgence** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The Buddha himself abandoned **six years** of austerities before enlightenment.
xa: The path to the end of suffering is the **Noble Eightfold Path** (**Magga**).
The teaching is likened to a **raft** — **upaya** (skilful means), not dogma.

28.s: Which one of the following statements about Buddhist doctrines is correct?
o: Anicca denotes impermanence and Anatta rejects a permanent self.
Anatta affirms a permanent and unchanging self.
Dukkha means that suffering is impossible.
Anicca denotes the permanence of all things.
28.x: Anicca means impermanence, while Anatta teaches that there is no permanent, unchanging self or atman. Dukkha denotes suffering.
28.tq: Separate the closely related doctrinal terms by their exact meanings.
xs: **Anicca** = impermanence and **Anatta** = no permanent self — so option **(1)** is correct.
Anatta **rejects** a permanent self (**atman**), so (2) is wrong; Anicca is impermanence, so (4) is wrong.
**Dukkha** means suffering — and **Nirodha** says it can end — so (3) is wrong.
xa: Anicca, Anatta and Dukkha are the **three marks**.
The first Noble Truth: life is suffering ("**sabbam dukkham**").

28.s: According to Buddhist teaching, karma is primarily understood as:
o: A ritual sacrifice prescribed in the Vedas
A denial of rebirth and moral causation
Intention-based morality in which present conditions arise from past actions
A divine decree that completely removes human choice
28.x: Buddhist karma is intention-based morality; the present state is linked to past actions, and rebirth continues until nirvana.
28.tq: Distinguish Buddhist moral causation from divine decree and ritual action.
xs: Buddhist karma is **intention-based morality**: the present state comes from **past actions** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Rebirth continues **till nirvana**.
Vedic authority and **sacrifice** were rejected, so (1) is wrong.
xa: The Buddha neither affirmed nor denied **God**.
**Nirvana** brings freedom from the **cycle of rebirth**.

28.s: Which of the following best describes the Buddha’s position regarding God and religious teaching?
o: He definitively denied every form of divine existence.
He definitively affirmed a creator God as the basis of liberation.
He neither affirmed nor denied God, and compared teaching to a raft or skilful means.
He made belief in God the first requirement for Sangha membership.
28.x: The Buddha neither affirmed nor denied God in this formulation. His teaching is compared to a raft and is understood as upaya, or skilful means, rather than dogma.
28.tq: Reject absolute formulations and identify the carefully qualified doctrinal position.
xs: He **neither affirmed nor denied God**, and likened his teaching to a **raft** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The raft stands for **upaya** (skilful means), not dogma.
Sangha membership was open to all **above 15**, regardless of caste — no belief in God was required.
xa: **Vedic authority** and **sacrifice** were rejected.
Significance: a **rational**, moderate, caste-open path.

28.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to the Four Noble Truths?
o: Magga — The permanence of worldly life
28.x: Samudaya identifies the cause of suffering, especially craving, ignorance and attachment. Dukkha is suffering, Nirodha is its cessation and Magga is the path.
28.tq: Match each Pali term with its precise doctrinal meaning rather than a related concept.
xs: **Samudaya** is the **cause of suffering** — craving (**tanha**), ignorance, attachment — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Dukkha** = suffering; **Nirodha** = cessation (Nirvana); **Magga** = the path.
xa: The four truths are called **Arya Satya**.
Magga = the **Noble Eightfold Path**.
⚠ **Samudaya** = cause; **Nirodha** = cessation; **Magga** = path.

28.s: A person seeking the Buddhist path of liberation is advised to cultivate Right View, Right Intention and Right Speech. These belong respectively to:
28.x: Right View and Right Intention belong to wisdom, while Right Speech belongs to ethics.
28.tq: Classify individual elements of the Eightfold Path under the three broader groups.
xs: **Right View** and **Right Intention** are **wisdom** (Prajna); **Right Speech** is **ethics** (Sila) — so option **(4)** is correct.
Sila = Right Speech, Right Action, Right Livelihood.
xa: **Samadhi** (mental discipline) = Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, Right Concentration.
The Eightfold Path is the **Ashtangika Marga**, arranged in **three groups**.

28.s: Which one of the following is NOT included in the ethical discipline component of the Eightfold Path?
28.x: Ethics consists of Right Speech, Right Action and Right Livelihood. Right Mindfulness belongs to mental discipline.
28.tq: Find the element belonging to the neighbouring category of mental discipline.
xs: **Right Mindfulness** is not in the ethics group — so option **(2)** is correct.
It belongs to **Samadhi** (mental discipline) with **Right Effort** and **Right Concentration**.
**Sila** (ethics) = **Right Speech**, **Right Action**, **Right Livelihood**.
xa: **Prajna** (wisdom) = **Right View**, **Right Intention**.
Pali terms: Mindfulness = **sati**; Livelihood = **ajiva**; Action = **kammanta**.

28.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Element of the Eightfold Path)

a. Samma-ditthi
b. Sankappa
c. Vaca
 d. Samadhi

List-II (English rendering)
 i. Right Speech
 ii. Right Concentration
 iii. Right View
 iv. Right Intention

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
28.x: Samma-ditthi means Right View, Sankappa means Right Intention, Vaca means Right Speech and Samadhi means Right Concentration.
28.tq: Use the original terms and their English equivalents, beginning with the unmistakable language term Vaca.
xs: **Samma-ditthi** = **Right View** (a–iii); **Sankappa** = **Right Intention** (b–iv).
**Vaca** = **Right Speech** (c–i); **Samadhi** = **Right Concentration** (d–ii).
So option **(1) a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** is correct.
xa: Others: **Kammanta** = Action, **Ajiva** = Livelihood, **Vayama** = Effort, **Sati** = Mindfulness.
Groups: **Prajna** (wisdom), **Sila** (ethics), **Samadhi** (mental discipline).

28.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
28.x: Kammanta means Right Action. Right Concentration is Samadhi.
28.tq: Detect the swapped Pali equivalents among closely related Eightfold Path terms.
xs: The wrong pair is **(4)**: **Kammanta** is **Right Action**; Right Concentration is **Samadhi**.
The rest are right: **Ajiva** — Right Livelihood; **Vayama** — Right Effort; **Sati** — Right Mindfulness.
xa: Right Action belongs to **Sila** (ethics), with Right Speech and Right Livelihood.
Right Concentration belongs to **Samadhi** (mental discipline).
Right View (**samma-ditthi**) and Right Intention (**sankappa**) form **Prajna**.

28.s:
Assertion (A): The Eightfold Path is regarded as the path leading to the cessation of suffering.
Reason (R): Magga, the fourth Noble Truth, identifies the Eightfold Path as the means to cessation.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
28.x: Both statements are true, and the identification of Magga as the path to cessation directly explains why the Eightfold Path has this role.
28.tq: Check whether the reason supplies the doctrinal basis for the assertion.
xs: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct **explanation** of A — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Magga**, the **fourth Noble Truth**, is the path to cessation: the **Noble Eightfold Path**.
xa: The other truths: **Dukkha** (suffering), **Samudaya** (cause — craving), **Nirodha** (cessation = Nirvana).
The first sermon at **Sarnath** taught the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path.

28.s: The Buddhist doctrine which explains that every phenomenon arises owing to a cause is known as:
28.x: Pratityasamutpada is the doctrine of dependent origination, according to which phenomena arise through causal conditions.
28.tq: Test the exact doctrinal term against closely related Buddhist concepts.
xs: The doctrine that every phenomenon **arises from a cause** is **Pratityasamutpada** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is **dependent origination**, a chain of **12 nidanas**.
**Nirodha** = cessation; **Anicca** = impermanence; **Anatta** = no permanent self.
xa: The chain begins **avidya (ignorance) → samskara → vijnana** and ends in **old age and death**.
Links **9-12**: Upadana → Bhava → Jati → **Jara-marana**.

28.s:
Arrange the following links of Pratityasamutpada in their correct order:

A. Vijnana
B. Samskara
C. Avidya
D. Namarupa
28.x: The first four links are Avidya, Samskara, Vijnana and Namarupa.
28.tq: Start with the first link and follow the fixed doctrinal sequence.
xs: The first four links run **Avidya → Samskara → Vijnana → Namarupa** — C, B, A, D, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Avidya** = ignorance; **Vijnana** = consciousness.
xa: Links **5-8**: **Shadayatana** (six senses) → **Sparsha** (contact) → **Vedana** (feeling) → **Trishna** (craving).
Links **9-12**: **Upadana** → **Bhava** → **Jati** → **Jara-marana**.

28.s: Which one of the following is the correct order of the last four links of Pratityasamutpada?
28.x: The final four links are Upadana, Bhava, Jati and Jara-marana.
28.tq: Use sequence discrimination among adjacent and easily reversed doctrinal terms.
xs: The last four links are **Upadana, Bhava, Jati, Jara-marana** — so option **(2)** is correct.
That is clinging → becoming → **birth** → **old age-death**.
**Trishna** (craving) is link **8**, before Upadana.
xa: Links **1-4**: Avidya → Samskara → Vijnana → Namarupa.
Pratityasamutpada = **dependent origination**, a **12-link** causal chain.

28.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Term)

a. Parivrajaka
b. Shramana
c. Upasaka
 d. Uposatha

List-II (Meaning)
 i. Lay follower
 ii. Wandering ascetic
 iii. Full or new moon confession and rule-recitation
 iv. Striver or ascetic outside the Vedic fold

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
28.x: Parivrajaka means wandering ascetic, Shramana means an ascetic outside the Vedic fold, Upasaka means lay follower and Uposatha is the confession and rule-recitation observance.
28.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes containing a wrong meaning.
xs: **Parivrajaka** = **wandering ascetic** (a–ii); **Shramana** = ascetic **outside the Vedic fold** (b–iv).
**Upasaka** = **lay follower** (c–i); **Uposatha** = **fortnightly confession** and rule-recitation (d–iii).
So option **(1) a–ii, b–iv, c–i, d–iii** is correct.
xa: **Pravrajya** = going forth; **Upasampada** = full ordination.
**Parajika** = grave offence leading to **expulsion**.
**Bhikkhu / Bhikkhuni** = monk / nun living on alms.

28.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
28.x: Pravrajya means leaving lay life or going forth; Upasampada denotes full ordination.
28.tq: Find the swapped meanings in a confusable pair of technical terms.
xs: The wrong pair is **(1)**: **Pravrajya** means **going forth** — leaving lay life (head-shaving, robes) — not full ordination.
Full ordination is **Upasampada**, so (4) is right; **Bhikkhu / Bhikkhuni** are monk / nun on alms.
xa: **Uposatha** = **fortnightly** confession and rule-recitation (full/new moon).
**Vassa** = rainy-season retreat of **3 months**.
⚠ **Pravrajya** = going forth; **Upasampada** = full ordination; **Uposatha** = fortnightly confession.

28.s: In Buddhist monastic terminology, the term ‘Parajika’ refers to:
o: A grave offence resulting in expulsion
28.x: Parajika denotes a grave monastic offence carrying expulsion from the order.
28.tq: Test an exact institutional term rather than its broader religious association.
xs: **Parajika** is a **grave offence** that leads to **expulsion** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The rainy-season retreat is **Vassa**; a lay follower is an **Upasaka**; a wandering ascetic is a **Parivrajaka**.
xa: The Sangha worked **democratically**, with **power to punish**.
**Vinaya** = the monastic code.

28.s: The three refuges or pillars of Buddhism are:
28.x: The Triratna consists of Buddha as teacher, Dhamma as teaching and Sangha as the order.
28.tq: Test a standard three-part list with related doctrinal distractors.
xs: The three refuges (**Triratna**) are **Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Buddha** = teacher; **Dhamma** = teaching; **Sangha** = order of monks and nuns.
xa: The Sangha were the **torch-bearers of Dhamma**; the organised Sangha drove Buddhism's spread.
**Vinaya** = the monastic code; **Uposatha** = fortnightly confession.

28.s:
Which of the following categories was excluded from membership of the Buddhist Sangha?

1. Criminals
2. Lepers
3. Persons with infectious diseases
4. Persons belonging to lower castes
28.x: Criminals, lepers and persons with infectious diseases were excluded. Caste was not a bar to admission for otherwise eligible persons.
28.tq: Separate explicit exclusions from the broad principle of caste-inclusive membership.
xs: **Criminals**, **lepers** and those with **infectious diseases** were excluded — so option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only** is correct.
Statement 4 is wrong: the Sangha was open to all **above 15**, **regardless of caste**.
xa: **Women** were admitted after requests of **Ananda** and **Mahapajapati Gotami**.
Significance: Buddhism was a **caste-open**, socially accessible path.

28.s: The admission of women into the Buddhist Sangha was associated with the requests of:
28.x: Women were admitted after requests associated with Ananda and Mahapajapati Gotami, who became the first nun.
28.tq: Match the institutional development with the persons directly connected to it.
xs: Women were admitted after the requests of **Ananda and Mahapajapati Gotami** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Mahapajapati became the **first nun**.
**Upali** recited the Vinaya; **Mahakassapa** presided over the First Council; **Subhadda** was the last convert.
xa: The **Bhikkhuni Sangha** was taken to Sri Lanka by **Sanghamitta**.
It thrived **1,000+ years** until the Chola invasion of **1017 AD**.

28.s:
Consider the following statements about Buddhist monastic life:
1. Monks shaved their heads, wore yellow or saffron robes and lived on daily alms.
2. Vassa was a two-month rainy-season retreat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
28.x: Statement 1 is correct: shaved heads, yellow/saffron robes and daily alms marked monastic life. Statement 2 is wrong: vassa was a three-month rainy-season retreat. Hence '1 only'.
28.tq: Vassa = 3-month rains retreat.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: monks had **shaved heads**, **yellow/saffron robes** and lived on **daily alms**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Vassa** was a **3-month** rainy-season retreat — so option **(1) 1 only** is correct.
xa: The Sangha had **democratic functioning** with power to punish.
**Uposatha** = fortnightly confession and rule-recitation.
**Parajika** = grave offence — expulsion.

28.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Vinaya and the Bhikkhuni Sangha?

1. Vinaya is the monastic code.
2. The Bhikkhuni Sangha was taken to Sri Lanka by Sanghamitta.
3. It continued there for more than 1,000 years until the Chola invasion of 1017 AD.
28.x: Vinaya denotes the monastic code. Sanghamitta took the Bhikkhuni Sangha to Sri Lanka, where it flourished for more than 1,000 years until the Chola invasion of 1017 AD.
28.tq: Check the authority, destination and date in a compact historical chain.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Vinaya** is the **monastic code**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Sanghamitta** took the **Bhikkhuni Sangha** to Sri Lanka.
Statement 3 is correct: it thrived **1,000+ years** until the **Chola invasion of 1017 AD** — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
xa: Women entered the Sangha after requests of **Ananda** and **Mahapajapati Gotami** (the first nun).
**Upali** recited the **Vinaya Pitaka** at the First Council.

28.s: Membership of the Buddhist Sangha was open to
o: all persons above 15 years of age, regardless of caste
only Kshatriyas and Brahmanas above 20 years
all persons, including criminals and lepers
only men above 15 years of age
28.x: The Sangha was open to all above 15, regardless of caste. Criminals, lepers and those with infectious diseases were excluded, and women were also admitted (after requests of Ananda and Mahapajapati Gotami), so the other options are wrong.
28.tq: Sangha: above 15, caste no bar; criminals, lepers, sick excluded.
xs: The Sangha was open to **all above 15, regardless of caste** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Criminals**, **lepers** and those with **infectious diseases** were excluded, so (3) is wrong.
**Women** were also admitted, so (4) is wrong.
xa: Women were admitted after requests of **Ananda** and **Mahapajapati Gotami**.
**Pravrajya** = going forth; **Upasampada** = full ordination.

28.s:
