(iii) Added canals under Ashoka
(iv) Repaired Sudarshana lake through Suvishakha
43.x: Pushyagupta built the lake, Tushaspha added canals under Ashoka, Rudradaman repaired it through Suvishakha, and Chakrapalita repaired it again during the Gupta period.
43.tq: Start from the sure pair and complete the sequence of repairs.
xs: Correct match: **a–ii, b–iii, c–iv, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Pushyagupta** (Chandragupta Maurya's governor) **built** the lake; **Tushaspha** (Yavanaraja) **added canals under Ashoka**.
**Rudradaman I** repaired it through **Suvishakha**; **Chakrapalita** repaired it again under **Skandagupta**.
xa: Chakrapalita was the son of governor **Parnadatta**.
**Suvishakha** was Rudradaman's **Pahlava** minister.
Exam angle: "repaired Sudarshana lake in a 2nd-century Sanskrit rock inscription" = **Rudradaman** (BPSC **2022**).

43.s:
Which of the following statements about Rudradaman I and the Satavahanas is correct?
1. Rudradaman defeated Satakarni twice.
2. Satakarni was described as lord of Dakshinapatha.
3. Rudradaman spared Satakarni because of a close relationship.
4. Rudradaman’s daughter married Vasishthiputra Satakarni.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
43.x: All four statements are correct. Rudradaman defeated Satakarni twice but spared him because of their close relationship, and Rudradaman’s daughter married Vasishthiputra Satakarni.
43.tq: Verify a connected set of dynastic and military relationships.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Rudradaman I** **twice defeated Satakarni**, described as **lord of Dakshinapatha**.
He **spared** Satakarni as a **close relative**.
His daughter **Rudradamanika** married **Vasishthiputra Satakarni**.
xa: Rudradaman's other conquest: the **Yaudheyas**.
After his defeat of **Pulumavi**, the Satavahana centre shifted to **Amaravati**.
The Satavahana-Kshatrapa **marriage alliance** is examinable (AP angle).

43.s: The greatest ruler of the Parthians in the Indian context was:
43.x: Gondophares is regarded as the greatest ruler among the Parthians or Pahlavas in India.
43.tq: Separate Parthian rulers from Saka and Kshatrapa rulers.
xs: **Gondophares** was the **greatest ruler** of the **Parthians (Pahlavas)** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Nahapana** was a **Kshaharata** Saka; **Maues** the **first Saka king**; **Patika** a north-west Saka ruler at **Taxila**.
xa: Gondophares is linked with the **Takht-i-Bahi inscription** near **Peshawar**.
Christian tradition: **St Thomas** visited his court.
The Parthians came in the **1st c. CE**, after the Sakas.

43.s: The Takht-i-Bahi inscription is associated with which Parthian ruler?
43.x: The Takht-i-Bahi inscription near Peshawar is associated with Gondophares.
43.tq: Match an inscription with the correct ruler and location context.
xs: The **Takht-i-Bahi inscription** (near **Peshawar**) belongs to **Gondophares** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Rudradaman I** and **Chashtana** were **Kardamaka** Sakas; **Bhumaka** a **Kshaharata**.
xa: Gondophares was the **greatest Parthian (Pahlava)** ruler.
Christian tradition: **St Thomas** visited his court.
**Rudradaman's** inscription is the **Junagadh (Girnar)** rock record.

43.s: According to Christian tradition, who visited the court of Gondophares?
43.x: Christian tradition states that St Thomas visited the court of Gondophares.
43.tq: Recall the religious tradition linked with the ruler’s court.
xs: Christian tradition says **St Thomas** visited the court of **Gondophares** — option **(1)** is correct.
Gondophares was the **greatest ruler** of the **Parthians (Pahlavas)**.
xa: His record is the **Takht-i-Bahi inscription** near **Peshawar**.
Sequence: **Indo-Greeks → Sakas → Parthians → Kushanas**.

43.s: Which of the following is NOT regarded as a contribution or feature associated with the Shakas, Parthians and Kushanas?
o: Development of long Sanskrit epigraphic records
43.x: Their military tradition is associated with improved cavalry, not exclusive reliance on elephants. Dated silver coins and Sanskrit epigraphy are also important features.
43.tq: Reject the absolute military claim that contradicts the recorded cavalry contribution.
xs: **Exclusive reliance on elephant-based armies** is not their feature — option **(3)** is the answer.
Shakas and Kushanas had a **better cavalry**, with trousers, long coats, helmets and boots.
**Dated silver coins** (Kardamaka coins with **Saka-era dates**) and the long **Sanskrit** Junagadh record are genuine features.
xa: Rudradaman's **Junagadh** record is the **first long inscription in Sanskrit**.
They patronised art at **Sanchi, Mathura and Gandhara**.
They were absorbed into society as **Vratya Kshatriyas**.

43.s: Which of the following groups of institutions is specifically associated with artistic patronage by the Shakas, Parthians and Kushanas?
43.x: These foreign ruling groups patronised the artistic centres of Sanchi, Mathura and Gandhara.
43.tq: Identify the complete set of associated artistic centres.
xs: They patronised art at **Sanchi, Mathura and Gandhara** — option **(2)** is correct.
This is the UPSC-listed art contribution of the Shakas, Parthians and Kushanas.
xa: **Mathura** was also a **centre of Saka rule** (with Ujjain and Girnar).
Shared dress: **trousers, long coats, helmets, boots**.
Coinage: **numerous silver coins** from western India.

43.s: Which set of articles of dress and military equipment was shared by the Shakas and Kushanas?
o: Kilts, bare feet, helmets and elephants
Trousers, long coats, helmets and boots
43.x: Trousers, long coats, helmets and boots were features shared by the Shakas and Kushanas, along with a stronger cavalry tradition.
43.tq: Recognise the distinctive foreign dress-and-military combination.
xs: Shakas and Kushanas shared **trousers, long coats, helmets and boots** — option **(4)** is correct.
They also had a **better cavalry** (UPSC).
xa: Art patronage: **Sanchi, Mathura and Gandhara**.
Sakas were absorbed into society as **Vratya Kshatriyas**.
The Sakas ruled through the **Satrap system** (Satrapas and Mahasatrapas).

43.s: The foreign ruling groups were absorbed into Indian society as which social category according to the cited tradition?
43.x: The Shakas, Parthians and related foreign groups were absorbed into society as Vratya Kshatriyas.
43.tq: Recall the social assimilation category associated with foreign rulers.
xs: The Sakas were absorbed into society as **Vratya Kshatriyas** — option **(3)** is correct.
This went with their **Satrap system** of administration.
xa: Their titles were **Satrapas and Mahasatrapas**.
**Kolika** = weavers; guild deposits generally earned **12%**.
They patronised **Sanchi, Mathura and Gandhara**.

43.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
43.x: Vikrama Samvat traditionally begins in 57 BC. The Kali Era begins in 3102 BC, the Saka Era in 78 CE and the Gupta Era in 319–20 CE.
43.tq: Start with the sure era–date pair and eliminate shifted dates.
xs: **Vikrama Samvat — 57 BC** is correctly matched — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kali era** began in **3102 BC**, not 78 CE.
**Saka era** began in **78 CE**, not 319–20 CE.
xa: Vikrama Samvat is traditionally linked to **Vikramaditya** of **Ujjain** after defeating the Sakas.
Conversions: **CE = Saka + 78**; **CE = Vikrama - 57**.
⚠ UPSC notes print "**58** CE" for Vikram Samvat — a slip; it began **57 BC**.

43.s: The Saka Era is associated in different historical and examination traditions with which of the following figures?
43.x: The Saka Era is commonly associated with Kanishka, while the Salivahana tradition credits Gautamiputra Satakarni.
43.tq: Handle a historically varied attribution without confusing it with the era’s starting year.
xs: The Saka era (**78 CE**) is credited to **Kanishka** (UPSC) and by APP to **Gautamiputra Satakarni** — option **(4)** is correct.
The Gautamiputra tradition calls it the **Salivahana era**.
xa: **CE = Saka + 78**.
Saka era adopted as the **national calendar** from **22 March 1957**.
First month **Chaitra**; **1 Chaitra = 22 March** (**21 March** in a leap year).

43.s: If a date is given as Saka year 125, its corresponding Common Era year would be:
43.x: The Common Era year is obtained by adding 78 to the Saka year: 125 + 78 = 203 CE.
43.tq: Apply the stated era-conversion formula.
xs: **Saka 125 = 203 CE** — option **(3)** is correct.
xa: Example: Rudradaman's Junagadh record, **Saka 72 = 150 CE**.
For Vikrama Samvat: **CE = Vikrama - 57**.
The Saka era starts in **78 CE** (Kanishka; APP: Gautamiputra Satakarni).

43.s: The national calendar based on the Saka Era was adopted with effect from:
43.x: The Saka-based national calendar was adopted from 22 March 1957.
43.tq: Distinguish the adoption date from the calendar’s annual dates.
xs: The Saka-based **national calendar** was adopted from **22 March 1957** — option **(4)** is correct.
Its first month is **Chaitra**; **1 Chaitra = 22 March**.
xa: In a leap year, **1 Chaitra = 21 March**.
The Saka era begins in **78 CE** (**CE = Saka + 78**).
⚠ Vikrama Samvat begins **57 BC**; Kali era **3102 BC**.

43.s: In a leap year, 1 Chaitra of the Indian National Calendar falls on:
43.x: In a leap year, 1 Chaitra falls on 21 March; in a normal year it falls on 22 March.
43.tq: Separate the normal-year and leap-year calendar dates.
xs: In a leap year, **1 Chaitra** falls on **21 March** — option **(3)** is correct.
In a normal year it falls on **22 March** (option 1 is the non-leap date).
xa: **Chaitra** is the first month of the Saka national calendar.
The calendar was adopted from **22 March 1957**.
Saka era starts **78 CE**.

43.s: Which ruler of the Satavahanas defeated Nahapana of the Kshaharata dynasty and restruck the coins issued by him?
43.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni defeated Nahapana, the Kshaharata ruler, and restruck his coins as an assertion of Satavahana power.
43.tq: Use the ruler–achievement association and distinguish the conqueror from the defeated ruler.
xs: **Gautamiputra Satakarni** defeated **Nahapana (Kshaharata)** and **restruck his silver coins** — option **(4)** is correct.
The restruck coins are in the **Jogalthembi hoard** (APHQ **2000**; **2026**).
**Rudradaman I** was a **Kardamaka** who defeated the Satavahanas; **Nahapana** was the defeated ruler himself.
xa: The **Nasik Prashasti** of **Gautami Balashri** calls him destroyer of the **Shakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas**.
Satavahana capitals: **Pratishthana (Paithan)** and **Amaravati**.
**Chashtana** fought **Vasishthiputra Pulumavi** (Ptolemy).

43.s: Rudradaman I's defeat of Pulumavi is associated with which change in Satavahana political geography?
o: The transfer of the centre from Amaravati to Pratishthana
The transfer of the centre from Amaravati to Junagadh
The transfer of the centre from Paithan to Junagadh
The transfer of the centre from Pratishthana to Amaravati
43.x: Following Rudradaman I's defeat of Pulumavi, the Satavahana centre shifted from Pratishthana, or Paithan, to Amaravati.
43.tq: Apply the stated political event to identify the resulting geographical shift rather than merely recalling a place-name.
xs: After **Rudradaman I** defeated **Pulumavi**, the Satavahana centre shifted from **Pratishthana to Amaravati** — option **(4)** is correct.
The two Satavahana capitals were **Pratishthana (Paithan)** and **Amaravati**; **Junagadh** was a Kshatrapa site, never a Satavahana centre.
xa: Rudradaman **twice defeated Satakarni, lord of Dakshinapatha**.
The **Satavahana-Kshatrapa marriage alliance** is also examinable.
Rudradaman ruled c. **130-150 CE** from **Ujjain**.

43.s: The Satavahana–Kshatrapa relationship included which of the following?
o: A treaty ending the use of coinage
A transfer of the Kshatrapa capital to Amaravati
43.x: The Satavahana–Kshatrapa relationship included a marriage alliance. The other alternatives are not associated with this relationship.
43.tq: Identify the precise form of inter-dynastic relationship and avoid replacing it with an unsupported political arrangement.
xs: The Satavahana–Kshatrapa relationship included a **marriage alliance** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Rudradamanika**, Rudradaman's daughter, married **Vasishthiputra Satakarni**.
Rudradaman spared **Satakarni** after defeating him twice, as a **close relative**.
xa: The Satavahana centre shifted to **Amaravati** after Rudradaman's defeat of **Pulumavi**.
The **Kshatrapa capital** remained **Ujjain**, not Amaravati.
The Sakas were often at war with the **Satavahanas**.

44.s: Who among the following united the five Yuezhi clans and took control of the Kabul valley and Kashmir?
44.x: Kujula Kadphises, also known as Kadphises I, united the five Yuezhi clans and occupied the Kabul valley and Kashmir.
44.tq: Identify the ruler by linking the specific territorial and political achievement.
xs: **Kujula Kadphises** (Kadphises I) united the **five Yuezhi clans** and took the **Kabul valley and Kashmir** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Vima Kadphises** later extended the empire to **Mathura and Varanasi**; **Vima Taktu** came between Kujula and Vima (Rabatak list).
**Huvishka** was Kanishka's successor.
xa: Kujula issued **copper** coins (c. **15-64 CE**, UPSC).
⚠ Copper = **Kujula Kadphises**; large-scale gold = **Vima Kadphises**.
Kujula was keyed as a Kushan ruler in **APPSC G2 2008**.
Kushanas = **Yueh-chi** from north-west China and Central Asia.

44.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Vima Taktu — Successor of Vasudeva I
Vima Kadphises — Extension of the empire to Mathura and Varanasi
Huvishka — Founder of the Kushana dynasty
Vasudeva I — Convenor of the Fourth Buddhist Council
44.x: Vima Kadphises extended Kushana authority to Mathura and Varanasi. The other rulers are associated with different stages of Kushana history.
44.tq: Use the ruler–achievement association and reject swapped deeds.
xs: **Vima Kadphises** extended the empire to **Mathura and Varanasi** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Vima Taktu** came between **Kujula** and **Vima Kadphises**, not after Vasudeva I.
**Kujula Kadphises**, not Huvishka, united the Yuezhi clans; the **Fourth Council** was under **Kanishka**, not Vasudeva I.
xa: Vima Kadphises was a **Shiva devotee** — titles **"Sarvaloka Ishvara"** and **Maheshvara** (RPSC **2024**).
He **first issued gold coins on a large scale** (BPSC **2018**).
**Vasudeva I** was the **last great Kushan**, with **Shiva** on his coins.

44.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kushana rulers:
1. Kanishka is associated with the zenith of the Kushana Empire.
2. Huvishka was a successor of Kanishka and Mathura became a major centre during his reign.
3. Vasudeva I was the first ruler of the Kushana dynasty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
44.x: Kanishka represented the zenith of Kushana power, and Huvishka was his successor with Mathura as an important centre. Vasudeva I was the last great Kushan, not the first ruler.
44.tq: Find the incorrect dynastic-position statement before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Kanishka** marks the **zenith** of the empire.
Statement 2 correct: **Huvishka** succeeded him, with **Mathura** a major centre.
Statement 3 wrong: **Vasudeva I** was the **last great Kushan**; the dynasty began with **Kujula Kadphises**.
xa: Vasudeva I had an **Indian name** and **Shiva** on his coins.
Rabatak genealogy: **Kujula → Vima Taktu → Vima Kadphises → Kanishka**.
Kanishka's capitals: **Purushapura (Peshawar)** and **Mathura**.

44.s: The Kushanas were originally identified with which group?
o: Yueh-chi from north-west China and Central Asia
Scythians from western Europe and Egypt
Huns from the Deccan and Sri Lanka
Parthians from southern Iran and Mesopotamia
44.x: The Kushanas were a branch of the Yueh-chi who came from north-west China and Central Asia.
44.tq: Test the geographical origin of the ruling people against nearby foreign groups.
xs: The Kushanas were the **Yueh-chi** from **north-west China and Central Asia** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Kujula Kadphises** united the **five Yuezhi clans**.
xa: Foreign sequence: Indo-Greeks → Sakas → Parthians → **Kushanas** (1st c. CE).
They became **Silk Road middlemen** between **Han China, Rome and India**.
Kanishka clashed with Chinese general **Pan Chao (Ban Chao)** in Central Asia.

44.s:
The titles adopted by Kushana rulers reflected influences from which of the following regions or traditions?
1. Devaputra — China
2. Shaonano Shao — Persia
3. Kaisara — Rome
4. Maharaja — India
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
44.x: Devaputra reflected Chinese influence, Shaonano Shao Persian influence, Kaisara the Roman Caesar tradition, and Maharaja the Indian tradition.
44.tq: Match each title with its cultural source before choosing the complete combination.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4)**.
**Devaputra** — **China**; **Shaonano Shao** — **Persia**.
**Kaisara** — **Rome's Caesar**; **Maharaja** — **India**.
xa: These four titles belong to **Kanishka**.
**Vima Kadphises** took **"Sarvaloka Ishvara"** and **Maheshvara** as a Shiva devotee.
Kanishka's empire ran from the **Oxus** to the **Ganga**.

44.s: The Kushana ruler who, as a devotee of Shiva, took the titles 'Maheshvara' and 'Sarvaloka Ishvara' was
44.x: Vima Kadphises (Kadphises II), a Shiva devotee, called himself Maheshvara and Sarvaloka Ishvara (RPSC 2024). Kujula united the Yuezhi clans, Kanishka took Devaputra and the other titles, and Huvishka was Kanishka's successor.
44.tq: Maheshvara = Vima Kadphises (Shaiva, large-scale gold).
xs: **Vima Kadphises** (Kadphises II), a **Shiva devotee**, took **Maheshvara** and **Sarvaloka Ishvara** — option **(2)** is correct (RPSC **2024**).
**Kujula Kadphises** united the five Yuezhi clans; **Kanishka** took **Devaputra, Shaonano Shao, Kaisara, Maharaja**.
**Huvishka** was Kanishka's successor.
xa: Vima extended the empire to **Mathura and Varanasi**.
He first issued **gold coins on a large scale**.
Shiva appears with **Nandi** on Kushana coins.

44.s: Which city was the main or winter capital of Kanishka?
44.x: Purushapura, identified with Peshawar, was Kanishka's main or winter capital. Mathura was another capital, while Surkh Kotal was a provincial centre.
44.tq: Distinguish the principal capital from the second capital and provincial centre.
xs: **Purushapura (Peshawar)** was Kanishka's **main/winter capital** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Mathura** was another capital; **Surkh Kotal** a **provincial centre**.
**Sarnath** is known for a **Bodhisattva image** dedicated by **Friar Bala** in **year 3 of Kanishka**.
xa: Empire extent: **Oxus** to **Ganga**, incl. **Kashgar, Khotan and Yarkand**.
Kanishka clashed with Chinese general **Pan Chao**.
**Rabatak inscription** (Afghanistan, in **Bactrian**) gives his genealogy.

44.s: Which of the following correctly describes the territorial extent of Kanishka's empire?
o: Only the Kabul valley and Kashmir
From the Narmada to Sri Lanka, excluding north-western regions
From the Euphrates to the Nile, including Egypt
From the Oxus to the Ganga, including Kashgar, Khotan and Yarkand
44.x: Kanishka's empire extended from the Oxus to the Ganga and included Kashgar, Khotan and Yarkand in the Tarim Basin.
44.tq: Use the two boundary rivers and the named Tarim Basin cities to identify the correct extent.
xs: Kanishka's empire stretched from the **Oxus to the Ganga**, incl. **Kashgar, Khotan and Yarkand** — option **(4)** is correct.
Kashgar, Khotan and Yarkand lie in the **Tarim Basin**.
"Only the Kabul valley and Kashmir" was **Kujula Kadphises'** conquest, not Kanishka's extent.
xa: Rabatak lists his Indian cities: **Saketa, Kaushambi, Pataliputra, Sri-Champa, Ujjain**.
Capitals: **Purushapura** (winter) and **Mathura**; **Surkh Kotal** a provincial centre.
In Central Asia he clashed with **Pan Chao (Ban Chao)**.

44.s: Which of the following sequences represents the genealogy given in the Rabatak inscription?
o: Kujula Kadphises → Vima Taktu → Vima Kadphises → Kanishka
Vima Taktu → Kujula Kadphises → Kanishka → Vima Kadphises
Kanishka → Vima Kadphises → Vima Taktu → Kujula Kadphises
Kujula Kadphises → Kanishka → Huvishka → Vima Taktu
44.x: The Rabatak inscription gives the succession as Kujula Kadphises, Vima Taktu, Vima Kadphises and Kanishka.
44.tq: Arrange the rulers using the inscriptional genealogy rather than general dynastic prominence.
xs: Rabatak genealogy: **Kujula Kadphises → Vima Taktu → Vima Kadphises → Kanishka** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **Rabatak inscription** is in **Afghanistan**, written in **Bactrian**.
**Huvishka** was Kanishka's successor, so he cannot precede Vima Taktu.
xa: Rabatak lists Kanishka's Indian cities: **Saketa, Kaushambi, Pataliputra, Sri-Champa, Ujjain**.
**Sarnath** image inscription: Bodhisattva by **Friar Bala**, **year 3 of Kanishka**.
**Vasudeva I** was the **last great Kushan**.

44.s: The era beginning in 78 CE is commonly credited to Kanishka, but which ruler is credited in some accounts with starting the Salivahana era?
44.x: Although the 78 CE era is commonly credited to Kanishka, some accounts credit Gautamiputra Satakarni with starting the Salivahana era.
44.tq: Separate the commonly accepted attribution from the alternative attribution in the founder debate.
xs: Some notes credit **Gautamiputra Satakarni** with the **Salivahana era (AD 78)** — option **(4)** is correct.
UPSC commonly credits the era of **78 CE** to **Kanishka**.
xa: It is called the **Saka era** because the **Western Kshatrapas (Sakas)** used it on records and coins.
Also known as **Salivahana Saka**.
It became India's **national calendar in 1957**.

44.s: Why did the era beginning in 78 CE come to be known as the Saka era?
o: Because it originated in the Roman Empire
Because the Western Kshatrapas used it in their records and coins
Because Kanishka belonged to the Gupta dynasty
Because it was introduced by the Satavahana navy
44.x: The era became known as the Saka era because the Western Kshatrapas, who were Sakas, used it on their records and coins.
44.tq: Identify the later users responsible for the name rather than the debated founder.
xs: It is the **Saka era** because the **Western Kshatrapas (Sakas)** used it on their **records and coins** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is commonly credited to **Kanishka**, a **Kushana**, not a Gupta.
xa: Some notes credit **Gautamiputra Satakarni** — the **Salivahana era (AD 78)**.
It became India's **national calendar in 1957**.
Also called **Salivahana Saka**.

44.s:
Which of the following statements about the era beginning in 78 CE is correct?
1. It is also called Salivahana Saka.
2. It became India's national calendar in 1957.
3. Its founder attribution is entirely free from historical debate.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
44.x: The era is also called Salivahana Saka and became India's national calendar in 1957. Its attribution is debated, so statement 3 is false.
44.tq: Use the qualified wording about the founder debate to reject an absolute statement.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: it is also called **Salivahana Saka**.
Statement 2 correct: it became India's **national calendar in 1957**.
Statement 3 wrong: the founder is debated — **Kanishka** (UPSC) vs **Gautamiputra Satakarni** (Salivahana era).
xa: Named **Saka era** because the **Western Kshatrapas** used it on records and coins.
It began in **78 CE**.

44.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with the Fourth Buddhist Council?
44.x: Ajatasatru was associated with the First Buddhist Council. The Fourth Council was patronised by Kanishka at Kundalvana in Kashmir and used Sanskrit.
44.tq: Find the council-related person belonging to a different chronological event.
xs: **Ajatasatru — Presiding patron** is wrongly matched — option **(3)** is the answer.
The Fourth Council's patron was **Kanishka**, at **Kundalvana (Harwan), Kashmir**, in **Sanskrit**.
Its president was **Vasumitra**; vice-president **Ashvaghosha**.
xa: Council places: 1st **Rajagriha**, 2nd **Vaishali**, 3rd **Pataliputra**, 4th **Kashmir**.
Date: c. **72 CE**.
Outcome: **Mahavibhasha** compiled; formal split into **Mahayana and Hinayana**.

44.s: Which one of the following was an outcome of the Fourth Buddhist Council?
44.x: The Mahavibhasha was compiled as an important outcome of the Fourth Buddhist Council. The council also dealt with disputes among Sarvastivada teachers.
44.tq: Associate the council with its distinctive textual outcome.
xs: The **Mahavibhasha** was compiled (by **Vasumitra**) at the Fourth Council — option **(2)** is correct.
**Buddhacharita** is by **Ashvaghosha**, not Vasumitra.
The council **settled disputes** among **Sarvastivada** teachers of Kashmir and Gandhara; it did not abolish the school.
xa: It formally split Buddhism into **Mahayana and Hinayana**.
Held at **Kundalvana (Harwan), Kashmir**, c. **72 CE**, under **Kanishka**.
Language: **Sanskrit** (earlier councils used Pali/Prakrit).

44.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Fourth Buddhist Council:
1. It formally marked the division between Mahayana and Hinayana.
2. It settled disputes among Sarvastivada teachers of Kashmir and Gandhara.
3. It was conducted in Sanskrit, whereas earlier councils used Pali or Prakrit.

Two branches of the Mauryan dynasty
46.x: The Puranas refer to them as Andhras or Andhrabhrityas. Andhrabhrityas means ‘servants of the Andhras’ or Andhras who had earlier been feudatories.
46.tq: Distinguish the closely related dynastic labels by their literal meaning.
xs: The Puranas call them **Andhras / Andhrabhrityas** — **Andhras** and the **servants or feudatories of the Andhras** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Andhrabhritya** = "servants of the Andhras", or Andhras who had been **feudatories**.
xa: They began as **feudatories of the Mauryas** and became independent after Mauryan decline.
Scholar views: **V.V. Mirashi, R.G. Bhandarkar** — they were **Andhrabhrityas**; **D.C. Sircar** — **Andhras, not Andhrabhrityas**.
Legendary progenitor: **Satavahana/Shalivahana**.

46.s: The political rise of the Satavahanas took place after they:
o: Began as feudatories of the Mauryas and became independent after the decline of Mauryan power
Were appointed governors by the Western Kshatrapas
Defeated the Kushanas in northern India
Succeeded the Guptas in the Deccan
46.x: The Satavahanas are described as having initially served as Mauryan feudatories and having established independence in the Deccan after the decline of the Mauryas.
46.tq: Identify the political sequence of feudatory status followed by independence.
xs: They **began as feudatories of the Mauryas** and became **independent in the Deccan after Mauryan decline** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **Western Kshatrapas** were their rivals, not their overlords; the **Guptas** came after them.
xa: They were the **first historical ruling dynasty of the Deccan**.
One account makes them **Brahmins** by caste.
Founder **Simuka** overthrew the **Kanvas**.

46.s:
Consider the following statements regarding views on the identity and origin of the Satavahanas:
1. D.C. Sircar held that they were Andhras, not Andhrabhrityas.
2. K.A. Nilakanta Sastri distinguished Andhra as a tribal name, Satavahana as a dynastic name and Satakarni as a family name.
3. R.S. Sharma associated them with the Dravidians.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
46.x: All three statements correctly represent the views attributed to D.C. Sircar, K.A. Nilakanta Sastri and R.S. Sharma respectively.
46.tq: Verify each scholar–theory association before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**D.C. Sircar**: they were **Andhras, not Andhrabhrityas**.
**K.A. Nilakanta Sastri**: **Andhra** = tribal name, **Satavahana** = dynastic, **Satakarni** = family name.
**R.S. Sharma**: they were **Dravidians**.
xa: **V.S. Sukthankar**: "**Andhras and Satavahanas are not the same**" (APPSC **2012** key).
**B.S.L. Hanumantha Rao**: they belonged to the **original Andhra janapada**.
**R.G. Bhandarkar**: original home in **Bellary** (Myakadoni; **2017** key).

46.s: Who associated the Satavahanas with the original Andhra janapada?
46.x: B.S.L. Hanumantha Rao held that the Satavahanas belonged to the original Andhra janapada.
46.tq: Match a specific scholar with the precise homeland theory.
xs: **B.S.L. Hanumantha Rao** linked them with the **original Andhra janapada** — option **(4)** is correct.
**D.C. Sircar**: Andhras, not Andhrabhrityas; **R.S. Sharma**: Dravidians.
**Nilakanta Sastri**: Andhra tribal, Satavahana dynastic, Satakarni family name.
xa: **Sukthankar**: "**Andhras and Satavahanas are not the same**".
⚠ **Bellary** (Myakadoni) home: keyed to **Bhandarkar** in APPSC **2017**, though books often credit Sukthankar.

46.s:
Arrange the following dynasties in the chronological order of their succession in Magadha:
A. Kanvas
B. Mauryas
C. Satavahanas
D. Sungas
46.x: The sequence is Mauryas, Sungas, Kanvas and then Satavahanas. Simuka is associated with the overthrow of the Kanvas.
46.tq: Fix the first and last dynasties, then arrange the intervening succession.
xs: Order: **Mauryas → Sungas → Kanvas → Satavahanas** (B, D, A, C) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Simuka** overthrew the **Kanvas**.
xa: Matsya/Vayu Puranas: a Satavahana king defeated **Kanva Susarma** and held **Magadha**.
Successors: **Ikshvakus** (Andhra), **Abhiras** (Maharashtra), **Vakatakas** (Vidarbha), Chutus, **Pallavas**.
Simuka's period: c. **230-207 BCE** (long chronology).

46.s:
Consider the following statements about the successors of the Satavahanas:
1. The Ikshvakus succeeded them in Andhra.
2. The Abhiras succeeded them in Maharashtra.
3. The Vakatakas succeeded them in Vidarbha.
4. The Pallavas were among their successors.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
46.x: The listed successors include the Ikshvakus in Andhra, Abhiras in Maharashtra, Vakatakas in Vidarbha and Pallavas. Chutus are also included among the successors.
46.tq: Treat each geographical succession as an independent statement before choosing the complete code.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Successors: **Ikshvakus** in **Andhra**, **Abhiras** in **Maharashtra**, **Vakatakas** in **Vidarbha**, and the **Pallavas**.
xa: The **Chutus** were also among the successors.
Later came the **Chalukyas**, then the **Rashtrakutas**.
The last king **Pulomavi III** was defeated by **Ikshvaku Srisantamula**.

46.s: Which of the following is the correct order of later political powers mentioned in connection with the succession after the Satavahanas?
46.x: After the Vakatakas and other immediate successors, the later sequence mentioned is Chalukyas followed by Rashtrakutas.
46.tq: Separate immediate successors from the later powers in the sequence.
xs: Order: **Vakatakas → later Chalukyas → Rashtrakutas** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **Vakatakas** (Vidarbha) were immediate successors; the **Chalukyas** came later, then the **Rashtrakutas**.
xa: Other immediate successors: **Ikshvakus** (Andhra), **Abhiras** (Maharashtra), Chutus, **Pallavas**.
The Satavahanas themselves followed the **Mauryas → Sungas → Kanvas**.

46.s: Which scholar held that 'the Andhras and the Satavahanas are not the same'?
46.x: V.S. Sukthankar held that the Andhras and the Satavahanas were not the same (APPSC 2012). Bhandarkar is keyed to the Bellary original-home view, Sircar held they were Andhras and not Andhrabhrityas, and Nilakanta Sastri treated Andhra as a tribal name and Satavahana as the dynastic name.
46.tq: 'Not the same' = Sukthankar.
xs: **V.S. Sukthankar** held "**Andhras and Satavahanas are not the same**" — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC **2012** key).
**R.G. Bhandarkar** is keyed to the **Bellary** home view; **D.C. Sircar** said **Andhras, not Andhrabhrityas**.
**Nilakanta Sastri**: Andhra = tribal, Satavahana = dynastic, Satakarni = family name.
xa: ⚠ Books often credit Sukthankar with the Bellary (Myakadoni) view — for APPSC **2017**, the key says **Bhandarkar**.
**R.S. Sharma**: **Dravidians**.
**Hanumantha Rao**: original **Andhra janapada**.

46.s: According to the APPSC 2017 key, the view that Bellary, based on the Myakadoni inscription, was the original home of the Satavahanas is attributed to:
46.x: The APPSC 2017 key credits R.G. Bhandarkar with the Bellary (Myakadoni) view. Standard books often name Sukthankar, which is the trap; R.S. Sharma called them Dravidians and Hanumantha Rao placed them in the original Andhra janapada.
46.tq: Bellary home: APPSC key = Bhandarkar, not Sukthankar.
xs: The APPSC **2017** key credits **R.G. Bhandarkar** with the **Bellary** home, based on the **Myakadoni** inscription — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ Trap: standard books often credit **Sukthankar**; his keyed view is "**Andhras and Satavahanas are not the same**".
**R.S. Sharma** called them **Dravidians**; **Hanumantha Rao** placed them in the **original Andhra janapada**.
xa: The 2017 paper called Myakadoni the "**Macedonian inscription**".
**Myakadoni** marks the **final phase** of Satavahana power, under **Pulumavi III**.
The homeland (Maharashtra vs Andhra vs Bellary) remains **unresolved**.

46.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Puranic accounts of the Satavahanas:
1. The Matsya Purana lists 30 Satavahana kings.
2. The Matsya Purana assigns 456 years to their rule.
3. The Vayu and Vishnu Puranas provide a standard chronology of 30 kings.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
46.x: The Matsya Purana lists 30 kings and 456 years. The Vayu and Vishnu Puranas mention 17 kings and 272 years, and their chronology is not treated as standard.
46.tq: Separate the reliable source and figures from the non-standard account.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statements 1, 2: the **Matsya Purana** lists **30 kings** over **456 years** (271 BCE-174 CE).
Statement 3 wrong: **Vayu / Vishnu Puranas** give **17 kings, 272 years**, not treated as standard.
xa: The Matsya list is the **longest, most systematic** and the basis of the political history.
Rulers **1-23** = early Satavahanas; **24-30** = later Satavahanas.
⚠ Vayu is cited by APP; Vishnu by CDX for the 17-king list.

46.s: Which of the following statements regarding the chronology of the Satavahanas is correct?
o: The chronology contains no difference between Puranic and modern scholarly placements.
The dynasty is universally placed only between the fourth and fifth centuries CE.
The Puranic long chronology places Simuka approximately in 230–207 BCE.
The Puranic chronology places Simuka exclusively in the second century CE.
46.x: The Puranic long chronology places Simuka approximately in 230–207 BCE, while another chronology places the dynasty broadly from the first century BCE to the third century CE.
46.tq: Compare the two chronological frameworks instead of treating one disputed date as universal.
xs: The Puranic **long chronology** places **Simuka** c. **230-207 BCE** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **short chronology** places the dynasty c. **1st century BCE-3rd century CE**, so the dates are debated, not fixed.
xa: Long chronology: **271 BC-174 AD** (Puranic).
Long vs short chronology is an **unresolved** debate.
**Matsya Purana**: **30 kings, 456 years**.

46.s: Which Purana provides the longest and most systematic list of Satavahana rulers, forming the basis for reconstructing their political history?
46.x: The Matsya Purana contains the longest and most systematic list of Satavahana kings and is the principal Puranic basis for their political history.
46.tq: Use the source-specific association rather than relying on the familiar name of a Purana.
xs: The **Matsya Purana** gives the longest, most systematic list — option **(3)** is correct.
It lists **30 kings** and **456 years**; the political history is built on it.
The **Vayu** (APP) / **Vishnu** (CDX) list has **17** kings, **272** years and is not treated as standard.
xa: Early Satavahanas: rulers **1-23**; later: **24-30**.
Its long chronology: **271 BCE-174 CE**.

46.s: The Puranic long chronology places the Satavahana rule approximately between:
46.x: The long Puranic chronology places the Satavahana rule from approximately 271 BCE to 174 CE.
46.tq: Distinguish the long chronology from the shorter scholarly chronology.
xs: The Puranic long chronology runs **271 BCE-174 CE** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **1st century BCE-3rd century CE** span is the **short** chronology.
xa: It rests on the **Matsya Purana** — **30 kings, 456 years**.
It dates **Simuka** to c. **230-207 BCE**.

46.s: According to the Matsya Purana's list of 30 Satavahana kings, which rulers are treated as the later Satavahanas?
46.x: Rulers 1-23 of the Matsya list are the early (first) Satavahanas and rulers 24-30 are the later Satavahanas.
46.tq: 23 early + 7 later = 30 kings.
xs: Rulers **24-30** are the **later Satavahanas** — option **(3)** is correct.
Rulers **1-23** are the **early (first)** Satavahanas.
xa: **Gautamiputra Satakarni** was the **23rd** king; **Vasishthiputra Pulumavi** the **24th**.
**Yajna Sri Satakarni** (**27th**) was the greatest of the later rulers.
**Pulomavi III** (**30th**) was the last.

46.s: Which of the following was NOT regarded as a work dealing with the early history of the Satavahanas?
46.x: Kathasaritsagara, Pratishthanapura-kalpa and Dvatrimsatputtalika are associated with the early history of the Satavahanas. Gathasaptasati was not included among them.
46.tq: Find the excluded work among closely related literary titles.
xs: The **Gathasaptasati** does **NOT** narrate early Satavahana history — option **(1)** is the answer (APPSC **2017** key).
**Pratishthanapura-kalpa** and **Dvatrimsatputtalika** are origin traditions; **Kathasaritsagara** (Somadeva Suri) draws on the **Brihatkatha**.
xa: Origin traditions also include **Jain** and **Dipavamsa** traditions.
The Gathasaptasati is linked to **Hala** (**17th** king), titled **Kavivatsala**.
Brihatkatha: **Gunadhya**, in **Paisachi**.

46.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Author)
 a. Pliny
 b. Megasthenes
 c. Ptolemy
 d. Somadeva Suri

List-II (Reference)
 i. Geography
 ii. Natural History
 iii. Kathasaritsagara
 iv. Andhras lived in towns

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
46.x: Pliny wrote Natural History, Megasthenes recorded that the Andhras lived in towns, Ptolemy wrote Geography, and Somadeva Suri composed Kathasaritsagara.
46.tq: Start with the sure author–work pairs and eliminate the remaining codes.
xs: Correct match: **a–ii, b–iv, c–i, d–iii** — option **(1)**.
**Pliny** — **Natural History** (mentions the Andhra kingdom); **Megasthenes** — **Andhras lived in towns**.
**Ptolemy** — **Geography**; **Somadeva Suri** — **Kathasaritsagara** (Sanskrit, from the Brihatkatha).
xa: **Gunadhya** wrote the **Brihatkatha** in **Paisachi**.
**Sharvavarman** wrote the **Katantra** (Kundala Satakarni).
**Kutuhala** wrote **Leelavati Parinayam**.

46.s: Who wrote the Brihatkatha, which is mentioned in connection with Satavahana literary traditions?
46.x: The Brihatkatha is attributed to Gunadhya and was written in Paisachi.
46.tq: Match the literary work with its author and avoid confusing it with later retellings.
xs: **Gunadhya** wrote the **Brihatkatha**, in **Paisachi** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Sharvavarman** wrote the **Katantra**; **Somadeva** the **Kathasaritsagara**; **Kutuhala** the **Leelavati Parinayam**.
xa: Kathasaritsagara is in **Sanskrit**, drawn **from the Brihatkatha**.
⚠ The **Gathasaptasati** does not narrate early Satavahana history.

46.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
46.x: Katantra is associated with Sharvavarman and Kundala Satakarni. Leelavati Parinayam is associated with Kutuhala, while Brihatkatha is associated with Gunadhya.
46.tq: Use the three-part literary association—work, author and Satavahana connection—to eliminate swaps.
xs: **Katantra — Sharvavarman — Kundala Satakarni** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**Leelavati Parinayam** is by **Kutuhala**, not Somadeva.
**Kathasaritsagara** is by **Somadeva Suri**; **Brihatkatha** by **Gunadhya**.
xa: Brihatkatha is in **Paisachi**.
**Hala** (**17th** king) is linked to the **Gathasaptasati**; his queen was **Lilavati**, a Sri Lankan princess.

46.s: Which of the following statements about the Naneghat inscription is correct?
o: It was issued by Pulumavi II and contains the first Telugu word.
It was issued by Rudradaman and records his victories over Satakarni.
It was issued by Devi Naganika, the wife of Satakarni I, and records his victories and Vedic sacrifices.
It was issued by Gautami Balasri in praise of Gautamiputra Satakarni.
46.x: The Naneghat inscription was issued by Devi Naganika, wife of Satakarni I. It records his victories, Vedic sacrifices, gifts to Brahmins and a Maharathi marriage connection.
46.tq: Use the issuer–ruler relationship to eliminate inscriptions belonging to other rulers.
xs: **Naneghat** was issued by **Devi Naganika**, wife of **Satakarni I**, recording his victories and **Vedic sacrifices** — option **(3)** is correct.
The first Telugu word "**Nagabu**" is in **Pulumavi II's Amaravati** record; **Junagadh** is **Rudradaman's**.
**Gautami Balasri** issued the **Nasik Prasasti**, not Naneghat.
xa: It gives Satakarni I's titles **Apratihatachakra** and **Dakshinapathapati**.
It also records **gifts to Brahmins** and a **Maharathi** marriage link.
Naganika co-performed the **Ashvamedha and Rajasuya** with Satakarni I.

46.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Nasik Prasasti?
o: A Prakrit prose record of the conquests and titles of Gautamiputra Satakarni
A Brahmi record of Pulumavi II’s donations at Amaravati
A Sanskrit poetic record of Rudradaman’s conquests
A Tamil record of the victories of Satakarni II
46.x: The Nasik Prasasti is in Prakrit prose and records the conquests and titles of Gautamiputra Satakarni.
46.tq: Separate language, literary form and subject matter when identifying an inscription.
xs: The **Nasik Prasasti** is a **Prakrit prose** record of the conquests and titles of **Gautamiputra Satakarni** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was issued by **Gautami Balasri** in the reign of **Vasishthiputra Pulumavi**.
The **Sanskrit** record of Rudradaman is the **Junagadh** inscription.
xa: All Satavahana inscriptions are in **Prakrit, Brahmi script**.
It praises him as destroyer of the **Sakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas**.
⚠ It is a family eulogy — its conquest claims may be **exaggerated**.

46.s: Which Satavahana ruler is associated with the first Satavahana inscription found at Nasik?
46.x: The inscription associated with Krishna, also called Kanha, is regarded as the first Satavahana inscription and was found at Nasik.
46.tq: Link the earliest record with its issuer rather than with the better-known later ruler.
xs: **Krishna (Kanha)**, the **2nd king**, issued the **first Satavahana inscription**, at **Nasik** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Chanda Satakarni** issued **Kodavali**; **Pulumavi III's** period is linked to **Myakadoni**; **Satakarni II** to the **Sanchi** torana.
xa: Kanha also had a **Dharma Mahamatra**.
The **earliest inscriptions come from Maharashtra** (G2 **2025**).
Founder = **Simuka**; first inscription = **Krishna**.

46.s: The Kodavali inscription is associated with:
o: Chanda Satakarni and the East Godavari region
46.x: The Kodavali inscription is attributed to Chanda Satakarni and was found in the East Godavari region, near Pithapuram.
46.tq: Start with the distinctive inscription–findspot pair and verify the ruler.
xs: **Kodavali** belongs to **Chanda Satakarni**, in the **East Godavari** region — option **(1)** is correct (G2 **2017**).
It is a **later Satavahana** record, near **Pithapuram**.
**Krishna** — Nasik caves; **Pulumavi II** — Amaravati; **Rudradaman** — Junagadh (Gujarat).
xa: **Chinaganjam** (Prakasam) is linked to **Yajnasri** (CDX says **Vijaya Sri**).
**Myakadoni** (Bellary) reflects the **final phase** of Satavahana power.

46.s: The Myakadoni inscription is important for understanding the:
o: Final phase of Satavahana power in the Bellary region
Foundation phase of Mauryan power in the Deccan
Conflict between Rudradaman and the Guptas
46.x: Myakadoni, also called Mekadoni, is associated with the period of Pulumavi III and reflects the final phase of Satavahana power in the Bellary region.
46.tq: Identify the historical significance of an inscription through its period and location.
xs: **Myakadoni (Mekadoni)** reflects the **final phase of Satavahana power** in the **Bellary** region — option **(1)** is correct.
It belongs to **Pulumavi III's** period.
xa: Pulomavi III, the **30th** and last king, spent his last days at **Myakadoni**.
He was defeated by **Ikshvaku Srisantamula**.
⚠ APPSC **2017** keyed the Bellary home view (Myakadoni) to **R.G. Bhandarkar**.

46.s: Which queen is associated with the Kanheri record?
o: Gautami Balasri, mother of Gautamiputra Satakarni
The queen of Yajna Sri Satakarni
Devi Naganika, wife of Satakarni I
46.x: The Kanheri record is associated with the queen of Vasishthiputra Satakarni, who is described as the daughter of the Kshatrapa Rudradaman.
46.tq: Identify the queen through the inscription site and her dynastic relationship.
xs: **Kanheri** is linked with the **queen of Vasishthiputra Satakarni** — option **(3)** is correct.
She is described as the **daughter of the Kshatrapa Rudradaman**.
**Naganika** issued **Naneghat**; **Gautami Balasri** the **Nasik Prasasti**.
xa: Kanheri is in **Mumbai, Maharashtra**.
**Rudradaman's Junagadh** record: he **twice defeated Satakarni**, sparing him as a **near relative**.

46.s: The Junagadh inscription provides evidence of the conflict between Rudradaman and the Satavahanas. According to it, Rudradaman:
o: Defeated Satakarni twice but spared him because he was a near relative
Was defeated twice by Satakarni and later became his feudatory
Issued the first Satavahana inscription at Nasik
Built the Amaravati gateway after marrying a Satavahana princess
46.x: The Junagadh record states that Rudradaman defeated Satakarni twice but spared him because Satakarni was a near relative.
46.tq: Read the relationship clause carefully rather than reversing victor and defeated ruler.
xs: Rudradaman **defeated Satakarni twice but spared him** as a **near relative** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **Junagadh** inscription (Sanskrit, c. **150 CE**) calls Satakarni **lord of Dakshinapatha**.
The **first Satavahana inscription** at Nasik was **Krishna's**; the Amaravati gateway record is **Pulumavi II's**.
xa: Vasishthiputra Pulumavi's rivals: Kardamaka Sakas **Chashtana** and **Rudradaman**.
After these attacks the capital shifted to **Amaravati**.
**Vasishthiputra Satakarni** married Rudradaman's daughter.

46.s: Who studied the Satavahana inscriptions mentioned in this context?
46.x: The Satavahana inscriptions referred to here were studied by Buhler.
46.tq: Identify the epigraphist directly rather than confusing him with travellers or other decipherers.
xs: Satavahana inscriptions were studied by **Buhler** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Megasthenes** wrote that the Andhras **lived in towns**; he did not study inscriptions.
xa: All Satavahana inscriptions are in **Prakrit, Brahmi script**.
The **earliest** come from **Maharashtra** (G2 **2025**).
First Satavahana inscription: **Krishna (Kanha)** at **Nasik**.

46.s: Which statement best expresses the significance of Satavahana inscriptions in Andhra?
o: They were the first records in India to use the Brahmi script.
They were issued in Andhra before the inscriptions of Ashoka.
The Satavahanas were the first kings to issue inscriptions in Andhra itself, although Ashokan inscriptions preceded them chronologically.
They were the first inscriptions of any kind found in India.
46.x: The Satavahanas were the first kings to issue inscriptions in Andhra itself, but Ashoka’s inscriptions were earlier in time.
46.tq: Separate geographical priority from chronological priority.
xs: The Satavahanas were the **first kings to issue inscriptions in Andhra itself**; **Ashoka's** were earlier — option **(3)** is correct.
So option (2) is wrong — Ashokan inscriptions came first.
xa: Their inscriptions are in **Prakrit, Brahmi script**.
First Telugu word "**Nagabu**" is in the **Amaravati** inscription of **Pulumavi II**.
They were the **first historical ruling dynasty of the Deccan**.

46.s: The earliest inscriptions of the Satavahanas have been found in which region?
46.x: The earliest Satavahana inscriptions, such as Naneghat and Kanha's Nasik record, come from Maharashtra (G2 2025). Coastal Andhra (Amaravati), Karnataka (Myakadoni, Bellary) and the Kodavali-type records are later. All were in Prakrit, Brahmi script.
46.tq: Earliest Satavahana inscriptions = Maharashtra.
xs: The **earliest Satavahana inscriptions come from Maharashtra** — option **(2)** is correct (G2 **2025**).
Examples: **Naneghat** (Pune) and **Krishna's Nasik** record.
**Amaravati** (coastal Andhra), **Myakadoni** (Bellary, Karnataka) and **Kodavali** (East Godavari) are later.
xa: All are in **Prakrit, Brahmi script**; studied by **Buhler**.
**Kotilingala** (Karimnagar, Telangana) is claimed as an early political centre.

46.s: Pratishthana, the principal western capital of the Satavahanas, is identified with:
46.x: Pratishthana is identified with Paithan in Maharashtra and was the principal western capital of the Satavahanas on the Godavari.
46.tq: Discriminate between ancient names and their present-day geographical identifications.
xs: **Pratishthana = Paithan, Maharashtra** — the principal **western capital** on the **Godavari** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Amaravati (Dhanyakataka)** was the **eastern capital**; **Kotilingala** an early political centre; **Myakadoni** a Bellary findspot.
xa: The capital shifted to Amaravati under **Vasishthiputra Pulumavi** after Rudradaman's attacks.
**Srikakulam** (Krishna district) was a traditional early Andhra capital.
Amaravati is now the AP state capital (Lok Sabha Bill, **2026**).

46.s: Dhanyakataka or Amaravati became the later eastern political, cultural and Buddhist centre of the Satavahanas. It was shifted there under:
46.x: The eastern centre was shifted to Dhanyakataka or Amaravati under Vasishthiputra Pulumavi after the attacks of Rudradaman.
46.tq: Connect the capital shift with the ruler who presided over it.
xs: The centre shifted to **Dhanyakataka / Amaravati** under **Vasishthiputra Pulumavi** — option **(1)** is correct.
The shift followed **Rudradaman's** attacks.
xa: Pulumavi (**24th** king) also **extended rule into coastal Andhra** and issued **ship-motif coins**.
His titles: **Dakshinapatheshwara**, **Navanagaraswami**.
The eastward shift made the **Krishna valley** the dynasty's centre.

46.s: Which of the following was regarded as an early Satavahana political centre in the capital debate?
46.x: Kotilingala in Karimnagar district of Telangana has been claimed as an early Satavahana political centre. The other places are listed as sites under Satavahana rule in Andhra Pradesh.
46.tq: Distinguish a proposed political centre from sites merely associated with the dynasty.
xs: **Kotilingala** (Karimnagar, Telangana) is claimed as an **early Satavahana political centre** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Ghantasala**, **Bhattiprolu** and **Jaggayyapeta** are listed AP sites, not capitals.
xa: Western capital: **Pratishthana (Paithan)**; eastern capital: **Dhanyakataka / Amaravati**.
**Srikakulam** (Krishna district) is a traditional early Andhra capital.
Other AP sites: **Amaravati**, **Nagarjunakonda**.

46.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the Andhra Pradesh sites associated with Satavahana rule?
46.x: Amaravati, Bhattiprolu, Ghantasala, Jaggayyapeta and Nagarjunakonda are listed as Andhra Pradesh sites under Satavahana rule. Mahishmati was the capital of Anupa.
46.tq: Separate the regional site list from the capital of a subordinate territory.
xs: **Mahishmati** is not an AP site — it was the capital of **Anupa** — option **(4)** is the answer (APPSC **2017** key).
The AP sites are **Amaravati, Bhattiprolu, Ghantasala, Jaggayyapeta, Nagarjunakonda**.
xa: **Anupa** lay in the **Narmada valley** and was ruled by **Gautamiputra Satakarni**.
Other Nasik Prasasti regions: **Aparanta** (North Konkan), **Vidarbha** (Berar).
**Akara** = East Malwa (Vidisha); **Avanti** = West Malwa (Ujjain).

46.s: According to the Puranic tradition, the last Satavahana ruler was:
46.x: Pulomavi III is regarded in the Puranic tradition as the thirtieth and last Satavahana ruler. He was defeated by Ikshvaku Srisantamula.
46.tq: Use the dynastic endpoint and distinguish it from other prominent Satavahana rulers.
xs: The **last** Satavahana per the Puranas is **Pulomavi III** (**30th**) — option **(3)** is correct (G2 **2011**).
**Vasishthiputra Pulumavi** was the **24th**; **Yajna Sri** the **27th** (last great ruler); **Hala** the **17th**.
xa: Pulomavi III was defeated by **Ikshvaku Srisantamula**.
His last days were at **Myakadoni (Bellary)**.
⚠ Founder = **Simuka**; longest reign = **Satakarni II**; last = **Pulomavi III**.

46.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Pulomavi III was defeated by Ikshvaku Srisantamula.
2. The last days of Pulomavi III are associated with Myakadoni in Bellary.
3. Pulomavi III belonged to the early group of the first 23 Satavahana rulers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
46.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Pulomavi III was defeated by the Ikshvaku Srisantamula and spent his last days at Myakadoni (Bellary). Statement 3 is wrong: he was the 30th and last king, one of the later Satavahanas (rulers 24-30), not the early group of rulers 1-23. So 1 and 2 only (A).
46.tq: Check the chronological grouping before accepting the statement about the ruler.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: Pulomavi III was defeated by **Ikshvaku Srisantamula**.
Statement 2 correct: his last days were at **Myakadoni (Bellary)**.
Statement 3 wrong: he was the **30th**, one of the **later** Satavahanas (rulers **24-30**).
xa: Early Satavahanas are rulers **1-23**.
The **Ikshvakus** succeeded the Satavahanas in **Andhra**.

46.s: Who is regarded as the greatest of the later Satavahana rulers?
46.x: Yajna Sri Satakarni is described as the greatest of the later Satavahana rulers.
46.tq: Distinguish between the greatest early ruler and the greatest later ruler.
xs: **Yajna Sri Satakarni** (**27th**) was the **greatest of the later rulers** — the last great ruler — option **(1)** is correct.
He **won back lost territory** (UPSC) and revived **maritime power** (ship coins).
**Satakarni I** was greatest of the early rulers; **Hala** the poet-king.
xa: He was a patron of **Nagarjuna**; linked to the **Nagarjunakonda Mahavihara**.
Titles: **Trisamudradheeshwara**; **Trisamudradhipati** (Banabhatta).
⚠ Trisamudradhipati = **Yajna Sri**; Trisamudra-toya-pita-vahana = **Gautamiputra**.

46.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Satavahana rulers:
1. Satakarni II had the longest reign among the rulers listed.
2. His reign lasted for 56 years.
3. He is associated with the Sanchi torana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
46.x: Satakarni II was the sixth ruler, reigned for 56 years—the longest reign in the listed sequence—and is associated with the Sanchi torana.
46.tq: Combine the ruler’s position, numerical detail and contribution before selecting the code.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Satakarni II** (**6th** king) had the **longest reign — 56 years**.
He is linked with the **Sanchi** south torana.
xa: ⚠ Founder = **Simuka**; longest reign = **Satakarni II**; last = **Pulomavi III**.
The Sanchi south torana names **Siri Satakarni**, not Gautamiputra.
**Satakarni I** (**3rd** king) issued the first silver coins.

46.s: Which ruler is associated with the Ashvamedha sacrifice, expansion into Central India and the issue of the first silver coins among the rulers listed?
46.x: Satakarni I is associated with the Ashvamedha, expansion into Central India and the first silver coins among the listed Satavahana rulers.
46.tq: Combine three distinctive achievements to identify the correct early ruler.
xs: **Satakarni I** (**3rd** king, c. **180 BCE**) performed the **Ashvamedha**, issued the **first silver coins** and expanded into **Central India** — option **(2)** is correct.
He was the **greatest of the early rulers**.
xa: Titles (Naneghat): **Dakshinapathapati**, **Apratihatachakra**.
His queen **Naganika** issued the **Naneghat** inscription.
He was **Kharavela's** contemporary.

46.s: Satakarni I was a contemporary of which ruler?
46.x: Satakarni I is identified as a contemporary of Kharavela.
46.tq: Match the ruler to the contemporary from the same broad historical period.
xs: **Satakarni I** was a contemporary of **Kharavela** — option **(4)** is correct.
Kharavela's **Hathigumpha** inscription says he sent an army west, ignoring Satakarni I.
**Rudradaman** and **Nahapana** clashed with later kings (Gautamiputra, Pulumavi).
xa: Satakarni I performed the **Ashvamedha** and issued the **first silver coins**.
**Nagarjuna** was patronised by **Yajna Sri Satakarni**.

46.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Yajna Sri Satakarni — patronage of Nagarjuna
Vasishthiputra Satakarni — marriage with Rudradaman’s daughter
Pulumavi III — revival of maritime power through ship coins
46.x: Pulumavi III is identified as the last ruler in the Puranic sequence, whereas revival of maritime power and ship coins are associated with Yajna Sri Satakarni.
46.tq: Find the contribution shifted from the last ruler to the last great ruler.
xs: **Pulumavi III — ship coins / maritime revival** is wrongly matched — option **(4)** is the answer.
Maritime revival with **ship coins** belongs to **Yajna Sri Satakarni**; Pulumavi III was the **last ruler**.
The other pairs are right: **Yajna Sri — Nagarjuna**; **Chanda Satakarni — Kodavali**; **Vasishthiputra Satakarni — Rudradaman's daughter**.
xa: **Vasishthiputra Pulumavi** also issued **ship-motif coins** (NextGen).
Pulomavi III was defeated by **Ikshvaku Srisantamula**.

46.s: Which of the following statements regarding Gautamiputra Satakarni is correct?
o: He defeated Nahapana and recovered territories including Malwa, Saurashtra, Konkan and Nasik.
He was the last great ruler of the Satavahana dynasty.
He belonged to the Kshaharata branch of the Western Kshatrapas.
He founded the Kshaharata branch and issued the earliest Nasik inscription.
46.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni defeated Nahapana and recovered Malwa, Saurashtra, Konkan and Nasik. Nahapana belonged to the Kshaharata branch of the Western Kshatrapas.
46.tq: Apply the ruler–enemy–territory relationship and reject swapped identities.
xs: **Gautamiputra Satakarni** defeated **Nahapana** and recovered **Malwa, Saurashtra, Konkan, Nasik** — option **(1)** is correct (APPSC **2000** key).
The **last great ruler** was **Yajna Sri Satakarni**.
The **Kshaharata** branch was **Nahapana's**, not Gautamiputra's; the earliest Nasik inscription was **Krishna's**.
xa: He **restruck Nahapana's coins** — the **Jogalthambi hoard** (Nasik district).
He ruled c. **106-130 CE**; the **23rd** king.
⚠ "28th ruler" in some notes is an error.

46.s: The restriking of whose silver coins by Gautamiputra Satakarni is evidenced by the Jogalthambi hoard?
46.x: The Jogalthambi hoard contains Nahapana’s silver coins restruck by Gautamiputra Satakarni, providing evidence of Gautamiputra’s victory.
46.tq: Use the hoard as archaeological evidence for the ruler defeated and the victor’s action.
xs: The **Jogalthambi hoard** holds silver coins of **Nahapana** **restruck by Gautamiputra** — option **(4)** is correct.
It is in **Nasik district** and confirms the Nasik Prasasti's claims.
**Ushavadata** was Nahapana's son-in-law; **Rudradaman** a Kardamaka; **Kharavela** a contemporary of Satakarni I.
xa: Nahapana was a **Western Kshatrapa** of the **Kshaharata** branch.
The **Periplus** notes the Saka-Satavahana conflict.

46.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kshaharata records:
1. Ushavadata (Rishabhadatta) was the son-in-law of Nahapana.
2. Ayama, the minister, is linked with the Junnar inscription.
3. Ushavadata invested 2,000 karshapanas in a Buddhist monastery at Govardhana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
46.x: Statement 1 is correct: Ushavadata was Nahapana's son-in-law. Statement 2 is correct: Ayama, the minister, issued the Junnar inscription. Statement 3 is wrong: the 2,000 karshapanas were invested in a weavers' guild at Govardhana, not a monastery. So B; A omits 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
46.tq: Govardhana deposit = weavers' guild (a guild, not a monastery).
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Ushavadata (Rishabhadatta)** was **Nahapana's son-in-law**.
Statement 2 correct: **Ayama**, the minister, is linked with the **Junnar** inscription.
Statement 3 wrong: the **2,000 karshapanas** went to a **weavers' guild** at **Govardhana**, not a monastery.
xa: Ushavadata's records are at **Nasik** and **Karle**.
**Gautamiputra's** own Nasik grant re-granted to monks land formerly held by Ushavadata.

46.s: The Periplus refers to which aspect of the history of the Satavahanas?
o: The Kanva conquest of the Deccan
The foundation of the Nagarjunakonda Mahavihara
46.x: The Periplus notes the conflict between the Sakas and the Satavahanas.
46.tq: Match the literary source with the specific historical relationship it records.
xs: The **Periplus** notes the **Saka–Satavahana conflict** — option **(4)** is correct.
The conflict ran from **Gautamiputra's** defeat of **Nahapana** to **Rudradaman's** wars.
xa: **Ptolemy** records clashes with **Chashtana**.
**Rudradaman** twice defeated **Satakarni, lord of Dakshinapatha**.
**Nagarjunakonda Mahavihara** is linked to **Yajna Sri Satakarni**.

46.s: Which inscription is primarily associated with the military victories of Gautamiputra Satakarni?
46.x: The Nasik inscription records the military achievements of Gautamiputra Satakarni. Naneghat is associated with Satakarni I and Naganika, while Junnar and Karle contain Kshaharata records.
46.tq: Use the site–ruler association and reject the nearby inscriptional distractors.
xs: The **Nasik** inscription records **Gautamiputra's military victories** — option **(3)** is correct (G2 **2008**).
**Naneghat** is **Satakarni I and Naganika**; **Junnar** and **Karle** are **Kshaharata (Saka)** records.
xa: The Nasik Prasasti was issued by **Gautami Balasri**.
It praises him as destroyer of the **Sakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas**.
Regions named: **Asika, Asaka, Mulaka, Suratha, Kukura, Aparanta, Anupa, Vidarbha, Akara, Avanti**.

46.s:
With reference to the inscriptions connected with the Satavahanas, consider the following statements:
1. Gautamiputra’s own Nasik grant re-granted to monks land formerly held by Ushavadata.
2. The Naneghat inscription is associated with Gautamiputra Satakarni.
3. Junnar and Karle contain Kshaharata records.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
46.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because the Naneghat inscription is associated with Satakarni I and Naganika, not Gautamiputra.
46.tq: Split the options by identifying the wrongly assigned ruler.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 correct: Gautamiputra's own **Nasik grant** re-granted to monks land formerly held by **Ushavadata**.
Statement 2 wrong: **Naneghat** belongs to **Satakarni I and Naganika**, not Gautamiputra.
Statement 3 correct: **Junnar** and **Karle** are **Kshaharata** records.
xa: Gautamiputra and **Balasri** gave gifts to monks on the **Trirashmi** hill.
He donated **100 nivartanas** of his own land.

46.s: Mahishmati was the capital of which territory mentioned in the Nasik Prasasti?
46.x: Anupa represented the Narmada valley and its capital was Mahishmati.
46.tq: Test the territory–capital relationship directly.
xs: **Mahishmati** was the capital of **Anupa** — option **(4)** is correct (APPSC **2017** key).
Anupa = the **Narmada valley**, ruled by **Gautamiputra Satakarni**.
**Aparanta** = North Konkan; **Suratha** = Saurashtra; **Vidarbha** = Berar.
xa: **Asika, Asaka (Asmaka), Mulaka** = Godavari valley, Paithan area.
**Kukura** = western Malwa-Rajasthan.
**Akara** = East Malwa (Vidisha); **Avanti** = West Malwa (Ujjain).

46.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Region)
 a. Aparanta
 b. Vidarbha
 c. Akara
 d. Avanti

List-II (Modern area)
 i. Berar
 ii. North Konkan

46.x: Aparanta was North Konkan, Vidarbha was Berar, Akara was East Malwa and Avanti was West Malwa.
46.tq: Start from the distinctive pair Aparanta–North Konkan and complete the regional matching.
xs: Correct match: **a–ii, b–i, c–iii, d–iv** — option **(1)**.
**Aparanta** = **North Konkan**; **Vidarbha** = **Berar**.
**Akara** = **East Malwa (Vidisha)**; **Avanti** = **West Malwa (Ujjain)**.
xa: **Anupa** = Narmada valley, capital **Mahishmati**.
**Suratha** = Saurashtra; **Kukura** = western Malwa-Rajasthan.
Gautamiputra recovered **Malwa, Saurashtra, Konkan, Nasik** (APPSC **2000** key).

46.s:
Which of the following statements about the Nasik Prasasti is correct?
1. It was composed in Prakrit prose.
2. It was written in the Brahmi script.
3. It records the expeditions, victories, empire and titles of Gautamiputra Satakarni.
4. It praises him as the destroyer of Sakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
46.x: The Nasik Prasasti is in Prakrit prose and Brahmi script and records Gautamiputra’s expeditions, victories, empire and titles, including his destruction of Sakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas.
46.tq: Treat language, script, contents and titulature as four separate inscriptional clues.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
The **Nasik Prasasti** is in **Prakrit prose**, **Brahmi script**.
It records **expeditions, victories, empire and titles** of Gautamiputra Satakarni.
It praises him as "Destroyer of **Sakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas**".
xa: Issued by **Gautami Balasri** in the reign of **Vasishthiputra Pulumavi**.
⚠ It is a family eulogy — conquest claims may be **exaggerated**.
Restruck coins (**Jogalthambi hoard**) confirm its claims.

46.s: The Nasik Prasasti records gifts made by Gautami Balasri together with her son to monks on which hill?
46.x: The Nasik Prasasti records gifts made by Gautami Balasri and her son to monks on the Trirashmi hill.
46.tq: Identify the specific religious site linked with the recorded donation.
xs: Balasri and her son made gifts to monks on the **Trirashmi hill** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Govardhana** is where **Ushavadata** invested in a weavers' guild; **Naneghat** is **Naganika's** inscription site.
xa: A **village near Trirashmi** was gifted to monks.
**100 nivartanas** of his own land were donated.
Balasri built a Nasik cave for the **Bhadrayaniya** monks.

46.s: In the Nasik Prasasti, Gautami Balasri is described as the wife of a:
46.x: Gautami Balasri is described in the Nasik Prasasti as the wife of a Rajarshi.
46.tq: Recall the precise honorific relationship used for the issuer’s status.
xs: Balasri is called the **wife of a Rajarshi** — option **(2)** is correct.
She was the **queen mother** of Gautamiputra Satakarni.
xa: The Prasasti classes Balasri's line as **Brahmana varna**.
She built a Nasik cave for the **Bhadrayaniya** monks.
It was issued in the reign of her grandson **Vasishthiputra Pulumavi**.

46.s: The Nasik Prasasti presents Gautamiputra Satakarni as belonging to which varna?
46.x: Balasri’s account presents Gautamiputra’s line as Brahmana. The inscription also describes him as the crusher of Kshatriya pride.
46.tq: Test the apparent contradiction between social status and military achievement.
xs: The Prasasti classes Balasri's line as **Brahmana varna** — option **(4)** is correct.
His title **Ekabrahmana** means **Unique Brahmana**.
The "**Crusher of Kshatriya pride**" claim sits beside his Brahmin status → the Satavahanas were **Brahmins, not Kshatriyas**.
xa: He fostered **Brahmin families**, upheld **varnashrama**, and **stopped varna-sankara**.
Title **Varnasankarya-nirodhaka** = stopper of the mixing of varnas.
One account makes the Satavahanas **Brahmins** by caste.

46.s: Which one of the following claims is associated with the Nasik Prasasti regarding Gautamiputra Satakarni’s social policy?
o: He fostered Brahmin families and upheld varnashrama.
He abolished the varna system completely.
He prohibited donations to religious institutions.
He made Buddhism the exclusive state religion.
46.x: The Nasik Prasasti credits him with fostering Brahmin families, upholding varnashrama and stopping varna-sankara.
46.tq: Match the ruler’s social claims with the precise action attributed to him.
xs: He **fostered Brahmin families and upheld varnashrama** — option **(1)** is correct.
He also **stopped varna-sankara**, so he did not abolish varna.
He gave **gifts to monks** (Trirashmi), so donations were not prohibited.
xa: Title: **Varnasankarya-nirodhaka** (stopper of the mixing of varnas).
Title: **Dvijakula-vardhana**; **Agama-nilaya** = abode of traditional learning.
**Kshatriya-darpa-mana-mardana** = crusher of the pride of the Kshatriyas.

46.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the religious patronage attributed to Gautamiputra Satakarni:
1. A village near Trirashmi was gifted to monks.
2. One hundred nivartanas of his own land were donated.
3. The Sanchi toranas are credited to him in the historical tradition.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
46.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Nasik record notes a village near Trirashmi gifted to monks and 100 nivartanas of his own land. Statement 3 is wrong: the Sanchi south torana inscription (gift of Ananda) names the rajan Siri Satakarni, usually taken as Satakarni I/II, not Gautamiputra. So 1 and 2 only (A).
46.tq: Check each separate item of religious patronage before selecting the comprehensive combination.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: a **village near Trirashmi** was gifted to monks.
Statement 2 correct: **100 nivartanas** of his own land were donated.
Statement 3 wrong: the **Sanchi south torana** inscription names **Siri Satakarni** (Satakarni I/II), not Gautamiputra.
xa: The Sanchi torana is linked to **Satakarni II** (longest reign, **56 years**).
Balasri built a Nasik cave for the **Bhadrayaniya** monks.

46.s: In the Puranic sequence of Satavahana rulers, Gautamiputra Satakarni was the:
46.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni was the 23rd king, the last of the early Satavahanas (rulers 1-23). '28th', found in some sources, is an error; the 17th king was Hala and the 30th and last was Pulomavi III.
46.tq: GPS = 23rd (not 28th); Hala 17th; Pulomavi III 30th.
xs: Gautamiputra Satakarni was the **23rd king** — option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ "**28th** ruler" in some notes is an **error**.
The **17th** king was **Hala**; the **30th** and last was **Pulomavi III**.
xa: Rulers **1-23** are the early Satavahanas, so he closes the early group.
His reign: c. **106-130 CE**.
He is called the **greatest of all** Satavahanas.

46.s: Which ruler is associated with ship-motif coins and the extension of Satavahana rule into coastal Andhra?
46.x: Vasishthiputra Pulumavi issued ship-motif coins and extended Satavahana rule into coastal Andhra.
46.tq: Connect the coin motif with the ruler’s maritime and coastal expansion.
xs: **Vasishthiputra Pulumavi** issued **ship-motif coins** and **extended rule into coastal Andhra** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Hala** was the poet-king; **Satakarni II** had the longest reign; **Pulumavi III** was the last ruler.
xa: The **Nasik Prasasti** was engraved in his reign.
The capital shifted to **Amaravati** under him.

46.s:
Which of the following is associated with Yajna Sri Satakarni?
1. Revival of maritime power
2. Ship coins
3. Patronage of Nagarjuna
4. Association with the Nagarjunakonda Mahavihara
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
46.x: Yajna Sri Satakarni is associated with the revival of maritime power, ship coins, patronage of Nagarjuna and the Nagarjunakonda Mahavihara.
46.tq: Recognise the cluster of maritime, religious and architectural associations of one ruler.
xs: All four belong to **Yajna Sri Satakarni** — option **(4)**.
He **revived maritime power** with **ship coins**.
He was a **patron of Nagarjuna** and is linked to the **Nagarjunakonda Mahavihara**.
xa: He was the **27th** king, c. **165-194 CE** (NextGen: **170-199**).
He **won back lost territory** (UPSC) — last great ruler.
Titles: **Trisamudradheeshwara**; **Trisamudradhipati** (Banabhatta).

46.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ptolemy records clashes between Vasishthiputra Pulumavi and Chashtana.
2. The Junagadh inscription of Rudradaman was composed in Sanskrit.
3. The inscription describes Satakarni as lord of Dakshinapatha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
46.x: All three statements are correct. Ptolemy records clashes with Chashtana, while the Sanskrit Junagadh inscription identifies Satakarni as lord of Dakshinapatha.
46.tq: Verify the source, language and political title separately.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Ptolemy** records clashes between **Vasishthiputra Pulumavi** and **Chashtana**.
Rudradaman's **Junagadh** inscription is in **Sanskrit** (c. **150 CE**) and calls Satakarni **lord of Dakshinapatha**.
xa: Rudradaman **twice defeated Satakarni** but spared him because of a **close relationship**.
After these attacks the capital shifted to **Amaravati**.
Pulumavi's rivals: Kardamaka Sakas **Chashtana** and **Rudradaman**.

46.s: Who among the following later recovered territory lost by the Satavahanas?
46.x: Yajnasri Satakarni later won back territory that had been lost by the Satavahanas.
46.tq: Separate the ruler who faced the loss from the ruler who recovered the territory.
xs: **Yajnasri Satakarni** won back lost territory — option **(4)** is correct (UPSC).
**Rudradaman** and **Chashtana** were the Saka rivals who took territory.
xa: He also **revived maritime power** (ship coins).
He was the **last great ruler**, the **27th** king.
He is linked to the **Nagarjunakonda Mahavihara**.

46.s: The title ‘Dakshinapathapati’ was borne by:
46.x: Satakarni I bore the titles Dakshinapathapati and Apratihatachakra.
46.tq: Associate paired royal titles with the correct ruler.
xs: **Dakshinapathapati** was the title of **Satakarni I** — option **(1)** is correct.
It appears with **Apratihatachakra** in the **Naneghat** inscription.
**Hala** = **Kavivatsala**; **Vasishthiputra Pulumavi** = **Dakshinapatheshwara**.
xa: ⚠ Dakshinapathapati (Satakarni I) vs **Dakshinapatheshwara** (Vasishthiputra Pulumavi).
Satakarni I performed the **Ashvamedha** and issued the first silver coins.

46.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
46.x: Kavivatsala was the title of Hala. Gautamiputra Satakarni was associated with titles such as Ekabrahmana, Ekashura and Shakasanhari.
46.tq: Use the swapped-ruler trap in title–person matching.
xs: **Gautamiputra Satakarni — Kavivatsala** is wrongly matched — option **(1)** is the answer.
**Kavivatsala** was **Hala's** title (**17th** king).
**Yajna Sri — Trisamudradheeshwara** and **Vasishthiputra Pulumavi — Dakshinapatheshwara** are correct.
xa: Gautamiputra's titles: **Ekabrahmana**, Ekashura, **Shakasanhari**, **Trisamudratoyapitavahana**.
Hala is linked to the **Gathasaptasati**.

46.s: The title ‘Shakasanhari’, meaning destroyer of the Shakas, is associated with:
46.x: Shakasanhari was one of the titles of Gautamiputra Satakarni, reflecting his association with the defeat of the Shakas.
46.tq: Identify the ruler from the functional meaning of the title.
xs: **Shakasanhari** is a title of **Gautamiputra Satakarni** — option **(1)** is correct.
He defeated the Saka **Nahapana** and restruck his coins.
xa: The Nasik Prasasti calls him destroyer of the **Sakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas**.
Other titles: **Ekabrahmana**, **Varnasankarya-nirodhaka**, **Dakshina-samudradhishwara**.
**Satavahana-kula-yasha** = restorer of Satavahana glory.

46.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Ekabrahmana — Unique Brahmana
2. Agama-nilaya — Abode of traditional learning
3. Varnasankarya-nirodhaka — Stopper of the mixing of varnas
4. Trisamudra-toya-pita-vahana — Restorer of Satavahana glory
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
46.x: The first three pairs are correct. Trisamudra-toya-pita-vahana refers to horses drinking the waters of three seas, not to restoring Satavahana glory.
46.tq: Reject the meaning-swapping trap between similar royal epithets.
xs: Pairs **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(1)**.
**Ekabrahmana** = **Unique Brahmana**; **Agama-nilaya** = **Abode of traditional learning**; **Varnasankarya-nirodhaka** = **Stopper of the mixing of varnas**.
Pair 4 wrong: **Trisamudra-toya-pita-vahana** = **whose horses drank the water of the three seas**.
xa: "Restorer of Satavahana glory" is **Satavahana-kula-yasha**.
⚠ Trisamudra-toya-pita-vahana = **Gautamiputra**; Trisamudradhipati = **Yajna Sri**.

46.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Satavahana queens is correct?
o: Gautami Balasri was the wife of Satakarni I and issued the Naneghat inscription.
Devi Naganika ruled as regent during the minority of her son.
Naganika was the queen of Hala and a Sri Lankan princess.
Lilavati ruled as guardian of the kingdom during the minority of her son.
46.x: Devi Naganika acted as guardian and regent during the minority of her son. Naganika was the wife of Satakarni I, whereas Lilavati was associated with Hala as his queen.
46.tq: Separate the identities and roles of the two prominent Satavahana queens.
xs: **Devi Naganika** ruled as **regent for her minor son** — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC **2019** key).
She was the **wife of Satakarni I** and issued **Naneghat** — not Balasri.
⚠ **Lilavati** (Sri Lankan princess) was **Hala's** queen.
xa: Naganika was the daughter of **Maharathi Tranakayiro**.
She co-performed the **Ashvamedha and Rajasuya** with Satakarni I.
**Gautami Balasri** was the **queen mother** of Gautamiputra.

46.s: Gautami Balasri is best described as:
o: The regent of Yajna Sri Satakarni during his minority
The queen of Hala who composed Gathasaptasati
The queen mother of Gautamiputra Satakarni who built a Nasik cave for Bhadrayaniya monks
The wife of Satakarni I who issued the Naneghat inscription
46.x: Gautami Balasri was the mother of Gautamiputra Satakarni. She built a Nasik cave for Bhadrayaniya monks, and her Nasik Prasasti glorified her son.
46.tq: Use role, relationship and religious patronage together to identify the person.
xs: **Gautami Balasri** was the **queen mother** of Gautamiputra, who built a **Nasik cave for the Bhadrayaniya monks** — option **(3)** is correct.
The wife of Satakarni I who issued Naneghat was **Naganika**; Hala's queen was **Lilavati**.
xa: Her **Nasik Prasasti** glorifies her son.
She is described as the **wife of a Rajarshi**.
She and her son gave gifts to monks on the **Trirashmi** hill.

46.s: The practice of prefixing maternal gotra names to the names of Satavahana kings began with:
46.x: The use of metronymics such as Gautamiputra and Vasishthiputra began with Gautamiputra Satakarni.
