**Pulakeshin II** ended the dynasty; **Ishanavarma** defeated Indrabhattaraka; **Prithvimula** killed him.
xa: Their son **Vikramendra Varma I** was "**Mahakavi**".
**Madhava Varma I** also married a **Vakataka** princess.
**Chikkulla** plates also mention **Vakataka** marriage ties.

54.s:
Consider the following statements about Vishnukundin inscriptions:
1. There were 21 inscriptions in total.
2. Sixteen were copper-plate inscriptions and five were stone inscriptions.
3. All of them were in Sanskrit.
4. Govinda Varma’s Chaitanyapuri record was in Prakrit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
54.x: There were 21 inscriptions, comprising 16 copper-plate and 5 stone records. The general statement that all were in Sanskrit is incorrect because Govinda Varma’s Chaitanyapuri record was in Prakrit.
54.tq: Watch for an absolute statement such as “all” when the material provides a specific exception.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4** are correct — option **(1)**.
**21 inscriptions** = **16 copper-plate + 5 stone**.
3 wrong: not all are Sanskrit — Govinda Varma's **Chaitanyapuri** record is **Prakrit**.
xa: **Tummalagudem** = **first Sanskrit inscription found in Telangana**.
**Chikkulla** has the Telugu phrase "**Vijaya rajya samvatsarambul**".
Records span both Telugu states: **Godavari, Guntur, Telangana**.

54.s: Under which Vishnukundin ruler did Prithvi Maharaja of the Ranadurjayas break away at Pishtapuram?
54.x: Prithvi Maharaja broke away at Pishtapuram during the rule of Vikramendra Varma II, as recorded in the Tandivada inscription.
54.tq: Match the political development with the ruler and inscription under whom it occurred.
xs: **Prithvi Maharaja (Ranadurjaya)** broke away at **Pishtapuram** under **Vikramendra Varma II** — option **(3)**.
Source: the **Tandivada** inscription.
xa: Vikramendra II ruled **555-569** and put down revolts.
Earlier, **Prithvimula** of the Ranadurjayas helped kill **Indrabhattaraka**.
Vikramendra II's title: **Sakala Bhuvana Rakshabharanaikashraya**.

54.s: Who ended Vishnukundin rule by defeating Manchana Bhattaraka at Kunala near Kolleru in 624 CE?
o: Pulakeshin II of the Badami Chalukyas
54.x: Pulakeshin II of the Badami Chalukyas defeated Manchana Bhattaraka at Kunala near Kolleru in 624 CE, ending Vishnukundin rule.
54.tq: Combine the date, place and conqueror to prevent confusion among the several wars involving the dynasty.
xs: **Pulakeshin II** (Badami Chalukya) defeated **Manchana Bhattaraka** at **Kunala (Kolleru)**, **624 CE** — option **(2)**.
**Kubja Vishnuvardhana**, his brother, then founded the **Eastern Chalukyas** — he did not fight this battle.
xa: **Manchana Bhattaraka** = **last** Vishnukundin ruler.
The Eastern Chalukyas took over the Vishnukundin **agrahara system and administration**.
Dynasty dates: **358-569 CE** vs **c. 420-624 CE**.

54.s: Which dynasty was founded by Kubja Vishnuvardhana after the defeat of the Vishnukundins?
54.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana, the brother of Pulakeshin II, founded the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi after the Vishnukundin defeat.
54.tq: Trace the dynastic succession from the conqueror’s brother to the new ruling house.
xs: **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** founded the **Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi** — option **(2)**.
He was the brother of **Pulakeshin II**, who won at **Kunala** in **624 CE**.
xa: The Vishnukundins link the **Ikshvaku age** to the **Eastern Chalukyas**.
**Vengi (Pedavegi)** was earlier the **Salankayana** capital.
**Ranadurjayas** broke away at **Pishtapuram**.

54.s:
Arrange the following events of late Vishnukundin history in chronological order:
A. Indrabhattaraka Varma was killed in the Kalinga war.
B. Prithvi Maharaja of the Ranadurjayas broke away at Pishtapuram under Vikramendra Varma II.
C. Pulakeshin II defeated Manchana Bhattaraka at Kunala.
D. Kubja Vishnuvardhana founded the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi.
54.x: The order is A, B, C, D (option B). Indrabhattaraka (525-555) was killed in the Kalinga war first. Prithvi Maharaja broke away at Pishtapuram under his successor Vikramendra Varma II (555-569). Pulakeshin II defeated Manchana Bhattaraka at Kunala in 624 CE, and his brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana then founded the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi. Option A puts the breakaway before Indrabhattaraka's death. Options C and D put the 624 CE defeat before the breakaway.
54.tq: Indrabhattaraka → Vikramendra II → Manchana (624) → Kubja Vishnuvardhana.
xs: Order: **A, B, C, D** — option **(2)**.
**Indrabhattaraka** (**525-555**) killed in the Kalinga war → **Prithvi Maharaja** breaks away under **Vikramendra II** (**555-569**).
**Pulakeshin II** defeats **Manchana** at **Kunala** (**624 CE**) → **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** founds the **Eastern Chalukyas**.
xa: The breakaway is recorded in the **Tandivada** inscription.
Indrabhattaraka had earlier lost to **Maukhari Ishanavarma** (**Jaunpur** inscription).

54.s: The Vishnukundins are historically significant because they formed a link between which two political phases?
o: The Pallava age and the Maukhari age
The Satavahana age and the Ikshvaku age
The Ikshvaku age and the Eastern Chalukyas
The Gupta age and the Kushana age
54.x: The Vishnukundins link the Ikshvaku age with the Eastern Chalukyas. The Eastern Chalukyas took over their agrahara system and administration.
54.tq: Test the broader historical transition rather than an isolated ruler or inscription.
xs: The Vishnukundins link the **Ikshvaku age** and the **Eastern Chalukyas** — option **(3)**.
The Eastern Chalukyas took over their **agrahara system and administration**.
xa: Dynasty order: Ikshvakus → **Brihatpalayanas** → **Salankayanas** → Vishnukundins → Eastern Chalukyas.
Founder of the Eastern Chalukyas: **Kubja Vishnuvardhana**.
Their records lie across **both Telugu states**.

54.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with the regional distribution of Vishnukundin records?
54.x: The wrong pair is C. The Khanapur plates come from Satara district in Maharashtra, and Ramatirtham is Indravarma's record, so neither belongs to the Guntur region. The other pairs are correct: Ipur and Velpuru are in Guntur, Chikkulla and Polamuru in the Godavari region, and Tummalagudem in Telangana.
54.tq: Use geographical grouping to detect the incorrectly placed inscription pair.
xs: **Khanapur and Ramatirtham — Guntur region** is wrong — option **(3)**.
**Khanapur** plates come from **Satara, Maharashtra**; **Ramatirtham** is **Indravarma's** record, not listed under Guntur.
Correct: **Ipur, Velpuru** = Guntur; **Chikkulla, Polamuru** = Godavari; **Tummalagudem** = Telangana.
xa: Total: **21 inscriptions** (**16 copper-plate + 5 stone**).
**Velpuru** pillar: **Ganapati** in MV II's **33rd** year.

54.s: Which statement best reflects the source-related debates concerning the Vishnukundins?
o: Only the location of their capital is disputed, while all ruler names are certain.
The identity of the Eastern Chalukyas is disputed, but Vishnukundin inscriptions are uniform.
The founder, ruler numbering, dates and some title attributions differ between sources.
The language of every inscription is disputed, but their chronology is fixed.
54.x: Differences among sources concern the founder, numbering of rulers, dates and certain title attributions.
54.tq: Select the comprehensive statement while rejecting options that turn a broad debate into a single disputed issue.
xs: Sources differ on the **founder, ruler numbering, dates and some title attributions** — option **(3)**.
Founder: **Indravarma** vs a note naming **Govindavarma**; dates **358-569 CE** vs **c. 420-624 CE**.
xa: Titles in dispute: **Janasraya** (MV II vs Vikramendra I); **Trikuta-Malayadhipati** (MV II vs MV III).
APPSC keys: **MV II = Janasraya**; **MV II = Amarapuri → Denduluru**.
Some notes add **Deva Varma** and **Madhava Varma III** (**496-510**) after MV II.

55.s: Which of the following is the correct administrative hierarchy?
55.x: The hierarchy was Kingdom, Vishaya, Rashtra and Grama. The Vishayadhipati, Rashtrika or Mahottara, and Gramani were associated with these units respectively.
55.tq: Test the exact sequence of territorial units.
xs: The Vishnukundin hierarchy ran **Kingdom > Vishaya > Rashtra > Grama** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Each unit had its officer: **Vishayadhipati** (Vishaya), **Rashtrika/Mahottara** (Rashtra), **Gramani** (Grama).
Option (1) reflects a minority view: some notes reverse it as **Rashtra > Vishaya > village**; follow the key.
xa: Rashtras named: **Palki** (Vizianagaram-Visakhapatnam), **Velpuru** (Guntur), **Karma**, Pariki and Kalinga.
Vishayas named: **Guddivada**, **Pasanaga** and **Natavadi/Sathrapathi**.
Top officers: **Yuvaraja**, **Mahamatya** (chief minister), **Amatya**, **Senapati**; **Rahasyadhikari** was the secret adviser.

55.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Officer)
 a. Akshapataladhikrita
 b. Rajjuka
 c. Gulmika
 d. Phaladara

List-II (Function)
 i. Measured grain and fixed the king's share
 ii. Keeper of records
 iii. Surveyor who measured land with ropes
 iv. Military officer over border areas

Which of the following is correct?
55.x: Akshapataladhikrita kept records, Rajjuka measured land with ropes, Gulmika supervised border areas, and Phaladara measured grain and fixed the king's share.
55.tq: Start from the sure administrative function and eliminate the codes.
xs: Correct matching is **a–ii, b–iii, c–iv, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Akshapataladhikrita** = keeper of records; **Rajjuka** = surveyor who measured land with ropes.
**Gulmika** = military officer over border areas; **Phaladara** = measured grain and fixed the king's share.
xa: APP notes call the Phaladara **Setty**.
**Rahasyadhikari** and **Antaranga** were the secret / confidential advisers.
The **king** was the highest judge in Vishnukundin justice.
**Amrabad fort** was the biggest fort in the Telugu country, with walls of about **200 km**.

55.s:
Consider the following statements about Vishnukundin military organisation:
1. Hastikosa referred to the elephant corps.
2. Veerakosa was the infantry commander.
3. Bata denoted a spy.
4. Chhata denoted a spy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
55.x: Hastikosa was the elephant corps, Veerakosa was the infantry commander and Chhata was a spy. Bata denoted a soldier, not a spy.
55.tq: Find the swapped military designation.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Hastikosa** = elephant corps. Statement 2 correct: **Veerakosa** = infantry commander.
Statement 3 wrong: **Bata** meant a **soldier**; statement 4 correct: **Chhata** was the **spy**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **Hastikosa** = elephants, **Veerakosa** = infantry — do not swap them.
The army as a whole was called **Chaturanga**.
**Divine ordeals** (boiling oil, fire walk, weighing) are recorded in the **Polamuru** plates.

55.s: Amrabad was noted for being
o: the largest Buddhist centre in Andhra
the biggest fort in the Telugu country
the principal agrahara of the dynasty
55.x: Amrabad was described as the biggest fort in the Telugu country, with walls of about 200 kilometres.
55.tq: Direct identification of a distinctive place-description.
xs: **Amrabad** was the **biggest fort in the Telugu country** — option **(3)**.
Its walls ran about **200 km**.
xa: **Gulmika** was the officer over border areas.
The army was **Chaturanga**; **Hastikosa** = elephant corps, **Veerakosa** = infantry commander.
**Bata** = soldier, **Chhata** = spy.

55.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding Vishnukundin administration?
1. The king was the highest judge.
2. Divine ordeals included boiling oil, fire walk and weighing.
3. Bhaga represented one-sixth of the produce.
4. Vishti referred to forced labour.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
55.x: All four statements are correct. The Polamuru plates record divine ordeals, Bhaga was one-sixth, and Vishti was forced labour, later called vetti in Telugu.
55.tq: Check each administrative and fiscal term independently.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
1: the **king** was the highest judge. 2: **divine ordeals** — boiling oil, fire walk, weighing — appear in the **Polamuru** plates.
3: **Bhaga** (1/6) was the tax. 4: **Vishti** = forced labour, later Telugu **vetti** (Tummalagudem plates).
xa: Land was measured in **Nivartanas** (1 nivartana = **1.5 acres**).
The **Rajjuka** measured land with ropes; the **Phaladara** fixed the king's share of grain.
**Akshapataladhikrita** was the keeper of records.

55.s:
Consider the following statements about Vishnukundin coinage:
1. The coins were made of iron with a thin coating of copper.
2. The coins were brought to light by Rayaprolu Subrahmanyam.
3. About 24 types of Vishnukundin coins have been identified.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
55.x: Statement 1 is correct: the coins were of iron with a thin copper coating (APPSC GS 2018 key). Statement 2 is correct: Rayaprolu Subrahmanyam brought them to light. Statement 3 is wrong: 16 types, not 24, have been identified. So B, C and D, which include statement 3, are wrong; A is right.
55.tq: Fix two anchors: copper-coated iron and 16 types.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
1 correct: coins were of **iron with a thin coating of copper** (**APPSC GS 2018**).
2 correct: they were brought to light by **Rayaprolu Subrahmanyam**. 3 wrong: **16 types** are known, not 24.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **Satavahanas**, **Ikshvakus** and **Eastern Chalukyas** are distractors for the copper-coated iron coinage.
Some notes claim **gold, silver and copper** coins — this conflicts with the key; follow copper-coated iron.
Symbols: **lion** (royal emblem), **Nandi**, **ship**, **trishula**, **conch**, "Sriparvata".
AP find-spots: **Bojjannakonda**, **Yelamanchili** (Anakapalli dt), **Pedavegi** (Eluru dt).

55.s: Which one of the following was NOT mentioned as a symbol on Vishnukundin coins?
55.x: Lion, Nandi, ship, trishula, conch and Sriparvata were mentioned as symbols; lotus was not included in the list.
55.tq: Find the option outside the stated symbol-group.
xs: **Lotus** is not among the listed Vishnukundin coin symbols — option **(4)**.
Listed symbols: **lion with raised paw** (royal emblem), **Nandi** (standard symbol), **ship** and **trishula**.
Others: the **conch** taken by MV II from the **Vasishthas**, and "**Sriparvata**".
xa: Coins were of **iron with a thin coating of copper**; **16 types**, discovered by **Rayaprolu Subrahmanyam**.
Ship coins in coastal Andhra plus MV II's title **Trisamudradhipati** = evidence of **sea trade**.
Telangana find-spots: **Phanigiri**, **Eleshwaram**, **Bhuvanagiri**, **Keesaragutta**, **Sultanabad**.

55.s: The conch symbol on certain Vishnukundin coins is associated with which ruler?
55.x: The conch symbol is associated with Madhava Varma II, who took it from the Vasishthas.
55.tq: Match the distinctive symbol with its associated ruler.
xs: The conch symbol is linked to **Madhava Varma II** — option **(2)**.
MV II took the **conch** emblem from the **Vasishthas**.
xa: MV II's title **Trisamudradhipati**, with ship coins, points to sea trade.
MV II performed **11 Ashvamedhas** and **16 Rajasuyas**, about **1,000 yagas**.
The **lion with raised paw** was the royal emblem; **Nandi** the standard coin symbol.

55.s: Ship-marked Vishnukundin coins found in coastal Andhra, together with the title Trisamudradhipati, indicate the dynasty's association with
55.x: Ship-marked coins and the title Trisamudradhipati point to the importance of sea trade.
55.tq: Infer the economic activity from the symbol and royal title.
xs: Ship-marked coins and the title **Trisamudradhipati** show **sea trade** — option **(2)**.
The ship coins come from **coastal Andhra**; the title belonged to **Madhava Varma II**.
xa: A **Roman gold coin of Constantine** was found at **Kudali Sangameswaram** near Alampur.
**Fahien** noted **cowrie shells (gavvalu)** also used as money.
Outside find-spots: **Nasik**, **Nagpur**, **Khanapur** (Maharashtra) and **Brahmagiri**.

55.s: A Roman gold coin of Constantine associated with the Vishnukundin period was found at
55.x: A Roman gold coin of Constantine was found at Kudali Sangameswaram near Alampur.
55.tq: Direct location-recall question.
xs: The **Roman gold coin of Constantine** was found at **Kudali Sangameswaram near Alampur** — option **(3)**.
**Pedavegi** (Eluru dt), **Phanigiri** (Telangana) and **Yelamanchili** (Anakapalli dt) are Vishnukundin coin find-spots, not the Roman coin site.
xa: Vishnukundin coins: **iron with a thin coating of copper**, **16 types**.
**Fahien** recorded **cowrie shells (gavvalu)** as money.
Ship coins + **Trisamudradhipati** = sea trade evidence.

55.s: Who reported that cowrie shells, locally called gavvalu, were also used as money?
55.x: Fa-hien reported the use of cowrie shells, or gavvalu, as money.
55.tq: Identify the traveller associated with the observation.
xs: **Fa-hien** reported cowrie shells (**gavvalu**) used as money — option **(4)**.
**Rayaprolu Subrahmanyam** discovered the Vishnukundin coins; **Shivavarma** was the scholar given Tundi; **Kumarilabhatta** attacked Jainism.
xa: The main coinage was **iron with a thin coating of copper** (**APPSC GS 2018**).
A **Roman gold coin of Constantine** turned up at **Kudali Sangameswaram** near Alampur.
Coin symbols include **lion**, **Nandi**, **ship**, **trishula** and **conch**.

55.s: The family deity of the Vishnukundin dynasty was
55.x: Sriparvataswami was the family deity, and the kings described themselves as Sriparvataswami-padanudhyata.
55.tq: Direct identification of the dynastic deity.
xs: The family deity was **Sriparvataswami** — option **(1)**.
Kings styled themselves "**Sriparvataswami-padanudhyata**"; the deity is identified with **Srisaila Mallikarjuna**.
**Bhutagrahaka Swami** was Yama; **Dantamukha Swami** was the Ganapati at Velpuru; **Dharmapuri** became a Narasimha kshetra.
xa: "**Sriparvata**" also appears on Vishnukundin coins.
Royal titles: **Paramamaheshwara** (Indrabhattaraka, Vikramendra), **Parama Bhagavata**, **Parama Brahmanya**.
**Ramalingeswara** temples: Keesaragutta, Velpuru, Ipur, Indrapalanagara.

55.s: Which of the following sacrifices was NOT included among those performed by the Vishnukundin rulers?
55.x: Ashvamedha, Rajasuya, Sarvamedha, Hiranyagarbha and Purushamedha or Naramedha were listed; Vajapeya was not included.
55.tq: Identify the sacrifice outside the stated group.
xs: **Vajapeya** is not in the list of Vishnukundin sacrifices — option **(3)**.
Listed: **Ashvamedha**, **Rajasuya**, **Sarvamedha**, **Hiranyagarbha**, **Purushamedha/Naramedha**.
xa: **Madhava Varma II** performed **11 Ashvamedhas**, **16 Rajasuyas** and about **1,000 yagas**.
Family deity: **Sriparvataswami** (Srisaila Mallikarjuna).
Royal titles: **Paramamaheshwara**, **Parama Bhagavata**, **Parama Brahmanya**.

55.s: At which place was Dantamukha Swami installed during the 33rd year of Madhava Varma II?
55.x: Dantamukha Swami was installed at Velpuru in the 33rd year of Madhava Varma II.
55.tq: Combine the deity, place and regnal-year clues.
xs: **Dantamukha Swami** was installed at **Velpuru** — option **(1)**.
It marks the **beginning of Ganapati worship**, in **MV II's 33rd year**.
**Keesaragutta** had a Ramalingeswara temple; **Dharmapuri** became a Narasimha kshetra; **Indrapalanagara** had a vihara and a Ramalingeswara temple.
xa: **Velpuru** (Guntur) was also a **Rashtra**.
**Bhutagrahaka Swami** was identified with **Yama**.
MV II performed **11 Ashvamedhas** and **16 Rajasuyas**.

55.s:
Which of the following statements is correct?
1. Bhutagrahaka Swami was identified with Yama.
2. Ramalingeswara temples stood at Keesaragutta, Velpuru, Ipur and Indrapalanagara.
3. Dharmapuri became a Narasimha kshetra.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
55.x: All three statements are correct. Bhutagrahaka Swami was associated with Yama, Ramalingeswara temples were recorded at the four named places, and Dharmapuri became a Narasimha kshetra.
55.tq: Use the all-inclusive option only after verifying every statement.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
1: **Bhutagrahaka Swami** = **Yama**. 2: **Ramalingeswara** temples at **Keesaragutta, Velpuru, Ipur, Indrapalanagara**.
3: **Dharmapuri** became a **Narasimha kshetra**.
xa: **Ganapati worship** began with **Dantamukha Swami** at Velpuru in MV II's **33rd** year.
Family deity **Sriparvataswami** = **Srisaila Mallikarjuna**.
Sacrifices included **Hiranyagarbha** and **Purushamedha/Naramedha**.

55.s: Madhava Varma II of the Vishnukundin dynasty is credited with performing
55.x: Madhava Varma II performed 11 Ashvamedhas and 16 Rajasuyas, and about 1,000 yagas in all. B reverses the two numbers; C confuses the figure of about 1,000 yagas; D wrongly denies the Ashvamedhas.
55.tq: MV II: 11 Ashvamedha, 16 Rajasuya, ~1,000 yagas.
xs: MV II performed **11 Ashvamedhas and 16 Rajasuyas** — option **(1)**.
Option (2) reverses the figures; option (3) misuses the total of about **1,000 yagas**; option (4) denies the Ashvamedhas.
xa: Other sacrifices: **Sarvamedha**, **Hiranyagarbha**, **Purushamedha/Naramedha**.
MV II installed **Dantamukha Swami** (Ganapati) at **Velpuru** in his **33rd** year.
MV II took the **conch** from the **Vasishthas** and bore the title **Trisamudradhipati**.
His title as scholar: "**Vidyadvijaguru**".

55.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Institution or grant)
 a. Govinda Vihara
 b. Viharas at Gunapashapuram
 c. Grant of Irundhera
 d. Paramabhattarika Mahadevi Vihara

List-II (Associated donor)
 i. Vikramendra Varma II
 ii. Govinda Varma I
 iii. Prithvimula and Harivarma
 iv. Queen of Govinda Varma I

Which of the following is correct?
55.x: Govinda Varma I founded the Govinda Vihara; Prithvimula and Harivarma were associated with the Gunapashapuram viharas; Vikramendra Varma II granted Irundhera; and the queen of Govinda Varma I founded the Paramabhattarika Mahadevi Vihara.
55.tq: Start from the institution–donor pairs that are most distinctive.
xs: Correct matching is **a–ii, b–iii, c–i, d–iv** — option **(1)**.
**Govinda Vihara** (Chaitanyapuri) — **Govinda Varma I**; **Gunapashapuram viharas** — feudatories **Prithvimula and Harivarma**.
**Irundhera** grant — **Vikramendra Varma II** (Tummalagudem-2); **Paramabhattarika Mahadevi Vihara** — **queen of Govinda Varma I**.
xa: The Mahadevi Vihara at **Indrapalanagara** housed **Chaturdasharya bhikshus**; Govinda Varma I granted it **Penkapura and Enmadala**.
Govinda Vihara has a **Prakrit inscription on the Musi**.
Buddhism declined from **MV II** onward.

55.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
55.x: The Govinda Vihara was located at Chaitanyapuri in Hyderabad. The other places were not the locations of the institutions with which they are paired.
55.tq: Use location-based elimination for religious institutions.
xs: **Govinda Vihara — Chaitanyapuri** near Hyderabad is correct — option **(1)**.
The **Paramabhattarika Mahadevi Vihara** stood at **Indrapalanagara**, not Phanigiri.
The **Irundhera** grant was made by **Vikramendra Varma II** to the Mahadevi Vihara, not at Bojjannakonda.
xa: Govinda Vihara was built by **Govinda Varma I**, with a **Prakrit** inscription on the **Musi**.
Gunapashapuram viharas were built by feudatories **Prithvimula** and **Harivarma**.
Buddhist centres of the age: **Bojjannakonda**, **Phanigiri**, **Gajulabanda**, **Nelakondapalli**, **Salihundam**, **Ramatirtham**.

55.s: Which of the following is NOT a Buddhist centre associated with the Vishnukundin age?
55.x: Bojjannakonda, Phanigiri and Salihundam were listed as Buddhist centres. Keesaragutta was associated with the discovery of a bronze Nagarjuna but was not included in that list of Buddhist centres.
55.tq: Distinguish a related archaeological find-spot from the named list.
xs: **Keesaragutta** is not in the listed Buddhist centres — option **(1)**.
Listed centres: **Bojjannakonda**, **Phanigiri**, **Gajulabanda**, **Nelakondapalli**, **Salihundam**, **Ramatirtham**.
Keesaragutta is noted for a **bronze Nagarjuna** find and a **Ramalingeswara** temple.
xa: **Indrabhattaraka** is credited with the **Ghatikeshwara temple at Keesara**.
**MV II**, "destroyer of Buddhism", turned **Undavalli**, **Mogalrajapuram**, **Indrakeeladri**, **Bhairavakonda** into Hindu shrines.
⚠ Some notes say royal grants to monasteries stopped entirely — contradicted by the **Tummalagudem** grants.

55.s: Which development was associated with the decline of Jainism during the Vishnukundin period?
55.x: Jainism declined as Kapalika Shaivism rose; Jain shrines such as Srisailam were converted, and Kumarilabhatta attacked Jainism.
55.tq: Link the religious decline with its stated historical cause.
xs: Jainism declined as **Kapalika Shaivism** rose — option **(2)**.
Jain shrines such as **Srisailam** were converted, and **Kumarilabhatta** attacked Jainism.
xa: Buddhism too declined from **MV II** onward.
MV II turned Buddhist sites at **Undavalli** and **Mogalrajapuram** into Hindu shrines.
Family deity **Sriparvataswami** = **Srisaila Mallikarjuna**.

55.s: A bronze image of Nagarjuna was found at
55.x: A bronze Nagarjuna was found at Keesaragutta.
55.tq: Direct archaeological-site recall.
xs: A **bronze Nagarjuna** was found at **Keesaragutta** — option **(1)**.
**Indrapalanagara** had the Mahadevi Vihara; **Gunapashapuram** had feudatory viharas; **Tummalagudem** is known for its plates.
xa: Keesaragutta is also a Vishnukundin **coin find-spot** and has a **Ramalingeswara** temple.
**Indrabhattaraka** built the **Ghatikeshwara temple at Keesara**.
Buddhist centres of the age: **Bojjannakonda**, **Phanigiri**, **Salihundam**, **Ramatirtham**.

55.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler is called a 'destroyer of Buddhism', from whose reign Buddhism declined and sites such as Undavalli and Mogalrajapuram became Hindu shrines?
55.x: Buddhism declined from Madhava Varma II onward; he is called a destroyer of Buddhism and Buddhist sites became Hindu shrines. Govinda Varma I and his queen founded viharas; Vikramendra Varma II granted Irundhera to a vihara; Indrabhattaraka is linked with Ghatikas.
55.tq: Decline of Buddhism = MV II; patrons = Govinda Varma I and Vikramendra II.
xs: **Madhava Varma II** is called the "destroyer of Buddhism" — option **(2)**.
From his reign Buddhist sites at **Undavalli**, **Mogalrajapuram**, **Indrakeeladri** and **Bhairavakonda** became Hindu shrines.
**Govinda Varma I** and his queen founded viharas; **Vikramendra Varma II** granted **Irundhera** to a vihara; **Indrabhattaraka** is linked with **Ghatikas**.
xa: MV II performed **11 Ashvamedhas** and **16 Rajasuyas**.
⚠ Some notes say royal grants to monasteries stopped entirely — this contradicts the **Tummalagudem** grants.
Jainism declined as **Kapalika** Shaivas rose.

55.s:
Consider the following statements about Vishnukundin Brahmana land grants:
1. Mutukali (Mruthukali) was granted as an agrahara to Indravarma and Agnivarma.
2. The Tundi plates record the grant of Tundi village to the scholar Shivavarma.
3. The Ipur plates name Indravarma and Agnivarma as the donees.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
55.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct as recorded. Statement 3 is wrong: the Ipur plates name Agnisarma and Easwarasarma as donees; Indravarma and Agnivarma received Mutukali. So B, C and D, which include statement 3, are wrong; A is right.
55.tq: Pair each grant with its donees: Mutukali - Indravarma/Agnivarma; Tundi - Shivavarma; Ipur - Agnisarma/Easwarasarma.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
1 correct: **Mutukali (Mruthukali)** agrahara went to **Indravarma and Agnivarma**. 2 correct: **Tundi** plates — Tundi village to scholar **Shivavarma** (Vikramendra II).
3 wrong: the **Ipur plates** name **Agnisarma** and **Easwarasarma** as donees.
xa: The Mutukali grant is assigned to **MV III** in some notes and **Vikramendra I** in others.
Ipur plates granted **cows, gold and land** to Brahmins.
Agraharas were **centres of Vedic learning**.

55.s: Agraharas served not only as land grants but also as
55.x: Agraharas also functioned as centres of Vedic learning.
55.tq: Apply the institutional function of an agrahara to the scenario.
xs: Agraharas were **centres of Vedic learning** — option **(4)**.
They were land grants to Brahmins, e.g. **Mutukali** to Indravarma and Agnivarma, **Tundi** to Shivavarma.
xa: Feudalisation debate: tax-free **Brahmadeyas** with administrative rights created a **landed intermediary class**.
**Ghatikas** were higher Sanskrit/Vedic colleges; special Ghatikas at **Amaravati** and **Vengi**.
**Ipur plates** donees: **Agnisarma**, **Easwarasarma**.

55.s: According to the feudalisation interpretation, tax-free Brahmadeyas with administrative rights contributed to the creation of
o: a class of royal coin inspectors
55.x: The feudalisation interpretation holds that tax-free Brahmadeyas with administrative rights created a landed intermediary class.
55.tq: Identify the social consequence linked to the land-grant system.
xs: Tax-free **Brahmadeyas** with administrative rights created **a landed intermediary class** — option **(4)**.
This is the **feudalisation** reading of Vishnukundin grants.
xa: Agraharas served as **centres of Vedic learning**.
Grants: **Mutukali** (Indravarma, Agnivarma), **Tundi** (Shivavarma), **Ipur** plates (Agnisarma, Easwarasarma).
Social criticism: **varna** rules hardened; women's status fell.

55.s: Ghatikas in the Vishnukundin period were primarily:
o: Residential institutions for Buddhist monks only
Higher colleges of Sanskrit and Vedic learning
55.x: Ghatikas were higher Sanskrit and Vedic colleges concerned with advanced Brahmanical learning.
55.tq: Use the precise institutional definition to distinguish Ghatikas from other contemporary establishments.
xs: Ghatikas were **higher colleges of Sanskrit and Vedic learning** — option **(3)**.
They were Brahmanical, not Buddhist monasteries, military schools or guilds.
xa: First mention in Andhra: **Indrabhattaraka Varma's inscriptions**.
Special Ghatikas: **Amaravati** and **Vengi**.
Curriculum of **14 vidyas**: **4 Vedas**, **6 Vedangas**, Mimamsa, Nyaya, Dharmashastra, Puranas.

55.s: Who is associated with the first mention of Ghatikas in Andhra inscriptions?
55.x: The inscriptions of Indrabhattaraka Varma provide the first mention of Ghatikas in Andhra.
55.tq: Identify the ruler directly associated with the specific epigraphic evidence.
xs: Ghatikas are first mentioned in **Indrabhattaraka Varma's** inscriptions — option **(3)**.
He is also credited with the **Ghatikeshwara temple at Keesara**.
xa: **Govinda Varma** = "**Shadabhigna**"; **MV II** = "**Vidyadvijaguru**".
**Vikramendra Varma I** is called "**Mahakavi**" in the Indrapalanagara plates.
Ghatikas taught **14 vidyas**; special ones at **Amaravati** and **Vengi**.

55.s: Indrabhattaraka Varma is credited with the construction of the Ghatikeshwara temple at:
55.x: Indrabhattaraka Varma is credited with the Ghatikeshwara temple at Keesara.
55.tq: Apply the location-based recall method to separate a temple site from Ghatika centres.
xs: Indrabhattaraka built the **Ghatikeshwara temple at Keesara** — option **(4)**.
**Amaravati** and **Vengi** were special Ghatika centres; **Indrapalanagara** had a vihara.
xa: Indrabhattaraka's inscriptions give the **first mention of Ghatikas** in Andhra.
Indrabhattaraka bore the title **Paramamaheshwara**.
Keesaragutta also yielded a **bronze Nagarjuna**.

55.s: The number of vidyas taught at the special Ghatikas of Amaravati and Vengi was:
55.x: The Ghatikas taught fourteen vidyas: four Vedas, six Vedangas, Mimamsa, Nyaya, Dharmashastra and Puranas.
55.tq: Check the numerical total against the component subjects rather than relying on a rounded figure.
xs: Ghatikas taught **14** vidyas — option **(3)**.
**4 Vedas** + **6 Vedangas** + **Mimamsa** + **Nyaya** + **Dharmashastra** + **Puranas** = 14.
xa: Special Ghatikas: **Amaravati** and **Vengi**.
First mention in Andhra: **Indrabhattaraka Varma's** inscriptions.
Buddhist teacher **Dasabalabali** knew the **four Vedas**.

55.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
55.x: Govinda Varma was known by the title Shadabhigna. Madhava Varma II was called Vidyadvijaguru, while Mahakavi was associated with Vikramendra Varma I; Dasabalabali was a Buddhist teacher who knew the four Vedas.
55.tq: Start with the sure title-person pair and reject the swapped royal epithets.
xs: **Govinda Varma — Shadabhigna** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**MV II** was "**Vidyadvijaguru**"; "**Mahakavi**" was **Vikramendra Varma I**.
**Dasabalabali** was a Buddhist teacher who knew the four Vedas; "**Janasraya**" was MV II's title.
xa: **Janasraya Chhandovichiti** is a Sanskrit work on **prosody** credited to **MV II**.
First mention of **Ghatikas**: **Indrabhattaraka Varma's** inscriptions.
Ghatika curriculum: **14 vidyas**.

55.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the authorship of Janasraya Chhandovichiti:
1. It is credited to Madhava Varma II because of his title Janasraya.
2. Some scholars attribute its composition to the poet Gunaswami, who wrote it in the king's name.
3. It is a Sanskrit work on prosody.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
55.x: All three statements are correct. The work is associated with Madhava Varma II through the title Janasraya, while an alternative view credits the poet Gunaswami with composing it in the king's name; its subject is prosody.
55.tq: Retain both the conventional attribution and the alternative authorship view instead of treating them as mutually exclusive.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
1: credited to **Madhava Varma II** via his title **Janasraya**. 2: some credit poet **Gunaswami (Ganaswami)**, writing in the king's name.
3: it is a **Sanskrit** work on **prosody (chandas)**.
xa: **Vikramendra Varma I** is called "**Mahakavi**" but no surviving Sanskrit work is named.
⚠ **Prabodha Chandrodayam** is a Telugu work by **Nandi Mallaya and Ghanta Singaya**, about a thousand years later — not Vishnukundin.
Official language: **Sanskrit**.

55.s: Which of the following statements about Vikramendra Varma I is correct?
o: He is called Mahakavi in the Indrapalanagara plates, but no surviving Sanskrit work of his is named by the sources.
He wrote Janasraya Chhandovichiti under the title Janasraya.
He composed the Telugu work Prabodha Chandrodayam during the Vishnukundin period.
He was known as Shadabhigna for his mastery of six branches of learning.
55.x: The Indrapalanagara plates call Vikramendra Varma I Mahakavi, but the sources do not name any surviving Sanskrit work by him. The other descriptions confuse him with different persons or with a much later work.
55.tq: Find the option that preserves both parts of the precise epigraphic fact and rejects swapped literary attributions.
xs: Vikramendra Varma I is called **Mahakavi** in the **Indrapalanagara plates**, but **no surviving Sanskrit work** is named — option **(1)**.
**Janasraya Chhandovichiti** is credited to **MV II** (title Janasraya), not him.
⚠ **Prabodha Chandrodayam** is a later Telugu work by **Nandi Mallaya and Ghanta Singaya**; "**Shadabhigna**" was **Govinda Varma**.
xa: MV II's title: "**Vidyadvijaguru**".
Telugu entry: **Chikkulla** plates use "**Vijaya rajya samvatsarambul**".
Official language: **Sanskrit**.

55.s: Which language served as the official language during the Vishnukundin period?
55.x: Sanskrit was the official language of the Vishnukundin period, although Telugu began to enter the records.
55.tq: Separate the official administrative language from the language beginning to appear in records.
xs: The official language was **Sanskrit** — option **(4)**.
**Telugu** only entered records — e.g. Chikkulla plates' "**Vijaya rajya samvatsarambul**" and Telugu village names.
xa: **Prakrit** appears in Govinda Varma I's inscription on the **Musi** (Govinda Vihara).
**Janasraya Chhandovichiti** is a **Sanskrit** work on **prosody**.
Ghatikas were higher **Sanskrit/Vedic** colleges.

55.s: Which of the following provides evidence for the entry of Telugu into Vishnukundin records?
o: The use of the expression “Vijaya rajya samvatsarambul” in the Chikkulla plates and the occurrence of Telugu village names
The replacement of Sanskrit by Telugu as the official language in all inscriptions
The use of Pali terminology in Ghatika curricula
The exclusive use of Telugu in the Indrapalanagara plates
55.x: The Chikkulla plates contain the expression “Vijaya rajya samvatsarambul”, and village names were Telugu, showing Telugu's entry into the records. Sanskrit nevertheless remained the official language.
55.tq: Use concrete epigraphic clues to distinguish emerging regional usage from the official language.
xs: Telugu's entry is shown by "**Vijaya rajya samvatsarambul**" in the **Chikkulla plates** and **Telugu village names** — option **(1)**.
Telugu did not replace Sanskrit: **Sanskrit** stayed the **official language**.
xa: **Vishti** (forced labour) later became Telugu **vetti**.
The **Indrapalanagara plates** call Vikramendra Varma I "**Mahakavi**".
Govinda Vihara has a **Prakrit** inscription on the **Musi**.

55.s: Which of the following was NOT a major feature of the Vishnukundin period in Andhra?
o: Appearance of the first Hindu cave temples
Growth of temple and agrahara economy
55.x: The period witnessed a Vedic-Puranic revival, the temple and agrahara economy, and the first Hindu cave temples. Brahmanical learning did not disappear; Ghatikas were important centres of such learning.
55.tq: Find the option that contradicts the broad historical significance of the period rather than merely changing a detail.
xs: **Complete disappearance of Brahmanical learning** was not a feature — option **(1)**.
The age saw a **Vedic-Puranic revival**, a **temple + agrahara economy** and the **first Hindu cave temples** in Andhra.
Brahmanical learning flourished in **Ghatikas** and **agraharas**.
xa: Debates: **varna** rules hardened; **women's status** fell, with more **child marriage** and **sati**.
Feudalisation view: tax-free **Brahmadeyas** created a **landed intermediary class**.
Ghatikas taught **14 vidyas**.

55.s:
Consider the following statements about social conditions during the Vishnukundin period:
1. Varna rules became more rigid.
2. The status of women declined.
3. Child marriage and sati became more prevalent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
55.x: All three statements are correct. The period is described as one in which varna rules hardened, women's status declined, and practices such as child marriage and sati increased.
55.tq: Check each social consequence separately before selecting the complete combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Varna** rules hardened; **women's status** fell; **child marriage** and **sati** increased.
xa: Positive side: **Vedic-Puranic revival** and **temple + agrahara economy**.
First **Hindu cave temples** in Andhra date to this age.
Tax-free **Brahmadeyas** with administrative rights fed the **feudalisation** debate.

56.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Cave)
 a. Undavalli
 b. Mogalrajapuram
 c. Bhairavakonda
 d. Akkanna-Madanna

List-II (Principal association)
 i. Trimurti, Durga and Nataraja; mainly Shaiva
 ii. Shiva and Kapalika sect
 iii. Ananta Padmanabha Swamy; earlier Jain and Buddhist use
 iv. Shaiva caves at Indrakeeladri

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
56.x: Undavalli is associated with the reclining Ananta Padmanabha Swamy image and earlier Jain-Buddhist use. Mogalrajapuram is associated with Trimurti, Durga and Nataraja, Bhairavakonda with Shiva and the Kapalika sect, and Akkanna-Madanna with Shaivism at Indrakeeladri.
56.tq: Start from the sure cave–deity pair and eliminate codes with mismatched associations.
xs: Correct matching is **a–iii, b–i, c–ii, d–iv** — option **(1)**.
**Undavalli** — **Ananta Padmanabha Swamy**, earlier Jain and Buddhist; **Mogalrajapuram** — **Trimurti, Durga, Nataraja**, mainly Shaiva.
**Bhairavakonda** — **Shiva**, **Kapalika** sect; **Akkanna-Madanna** — Shaiva caves on **Indrakeeladri hill**, Vijayawada.
xa: **Madhava Varma I** is credited with the Undavalli, Bhairavakona and Mogalrajapuram caves.
⚠ **5** caves = Mogalrajapuram; **8** caves = Bhairavakonda; **4** storeys = Undavalli.
**G2 2019**: the "Brahmanical caves" of Moghalrajapuram and Undavalli belong to the **Vishnukundinas** — traps: Ikshvakus, Salankayanas, Pallavas.

56.s: The earliest Hindu cave temples in India, at Udayagiri in Madhya Pradesh, are associated with the:
56.x: The Guptas at Udayagiri in Madhya Pradesh are credited with the earliest Hindu cave temples in India, whereas the Vishnukundins are associated with the first Hindu cave temples in the Telugu states.
56.tq: Distinguish the broader Indian claim from the regional Telugu-states claim.
xs: India's first Hindu cave temples, at **Udayagiri (MP)**, are credited to the **Guptas** — option **(3)**.
The **Vishnukundins** made the first Hindu cave temples of the **Telugu states**, not of India.
xa: Undavalli is a regional form of the **Gupta** rock-cut style, dated **4th-5th c. CE**.
Vishnukundin style blends **Ikshvaku and Vakataka** traditions with Pallava borrowings.
**Pallava** (Mahendravarman I) caves are of the **7th c.**

56.s: Which one of the following cave complexes is specifically associated with Madhava Varma I by the attribution followed in one scholarly tradition?
56.x: Madhava Varma I is credited with the Undavalli, Bhairavakonda and Mogalrajapuram caves in the attribution followed by APP and CDX.
56.tq: Match the ruler with the complete group of monuments, avoiding substitution by a nearby cave site.
xs: **Madhava Varma I** is credited with **Undavalli, Bhairavakonda and Mogalrajapuram** — option **(4)**.
**Mahabalipuram** caves are **Pallava**; **Udayagiri** is **Gupta**; Keesaragutta is not in the attribution.
xa: **APHQ** dates Bhairavakonda to the **Pallava** period (**7th-8th c.**).
Undavalli = **Vishnukundins** (**G2 2025**).
**Vishnukundins** built the first Hindu cave temples in the Telugu states.

56.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the location of the caves:
1. Undavalli is situated on the bank of the Krishna.
2. Mogalrajapuram is presently in NTR district.
3. Akkanna-Madanna caves are located on Indrakeeladri hill.
4. Keesaragutta is located in Medchal-Malkajgiri district of Telangana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
56.x: All four statements are correct. Undavalli and Akkanna-Madanna are associated with the Krishna region, Mogalrajapuram is in present NTR district, and Keesaragutta is in Medchal-Malkajgiri district of Telangana.
56.tq: Verify each location independently, especially the present administrative district.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
1: **Undavalli** is on the **Krishna** bank. 2: **Mogalrajapuram** (Vijayawada) is now in **NTR district**.
3: **Akkanna-Madanna** caves are on **Indrakeeladri hill**. 4: **Keesaragutta** is in **Medchal-Malkajgiri**, Telangana.
xa: Undavalli is in **Tadepalli mandal, Guntur district**, in the **Amaravati** capital area.
**Bhairavakonda**: **Nellore** per the exam key (**G2 2012**); CDI says **Prakasam**.
Keesaragutta has a **brick structural temple** with garbhagriha, antarala-mandapa and mukhamandapa.

56.s: Undavalli caves are situated at:
o: Undavalli in Tadepalli mandal, Guntur district
56.x: Undavalli is located at Undavalli in Tadepalli mandal of Guntur district, in the Amaravati capital area near Vijayawada and Mangalagiri, on the Krishna bank.
56.tq: Separate the exact locality and district from nearby Vijayawada-area cave sites.
xs: Undavalli caves lie at **Undavalli, Tadepalli mandal, Guntur district** — option **(3)**.
They sit in the **Amaravati capital area** near **Vijayawada/Mangalagiri**, on the **Krishna** bank.
**Indrakeeladri** has the Akkanna-Madanna caves; **Bhairavakonda** is in Nellore; **Keesaragutta** is in Medchal-Malkajgiri.
xa: **APPSC GS 2019** asked where Undavalli is: the key is **Vijayawada**; its revenue district is **Guntur**.
Undavalli's deity is now **Vishnu (Ananta Padmanabha Swamy)**.
Undavalli has **four storeys** and **3 main caves**.

56.s: Which one of the following statements correctly reflects the location issue concerning Bhairavakonda?
o: It is located in Medchal-Malkajgiri district, although the examination key places it in Nellore.
It is located in NTR district, although some sources place it in Telangana.
It is uniformly placed in Guntur district by all authorities.
The examination key places it in Nellore district, while another source places it in Prakasam district.
56.x: The examination key places Bhairavakonda in Nellore district, while CDI places it in Prakasam district. This difference is relevant to its administrative identification.
56.tq: Recognise the source-based district distinction instead of treating close regional identifications as identical.
xs: The **exam key** places Bhairavakonda in **Nellore**, while **CDI** places it in **Prakasam** — option **(4)**.
The Nellore placement comes from the **G2 2012** key.
xa: Bhairavakonda has **8 rock-cut caves**, all to **Shiva** — traps 4, 9, 12.
It was a centre of **Shaivism** (**G2 2008**), specifically the **Kapalika** sect.
Attribution: **Madhava Varma I** (most notes) vs **Pallava** period (**7th-8th c.**).

56.s: Which dynasty is associated with the first Hindu cave temples in the Telugu states?
56.x: The Vishnukundins are associated with the first Hindu cave temples in the Telugu states.
56.tq: Use the first-in-sequence clue to distinguish the Vishnukundins from other Andhra dynasties.
xs: The **Vishnukundins** built the **first Hindu cave temples** in the Telugu states — option **(4)**.
Their caves: **Undavalli**, **Mogalrajapuram**, **Bhairavakonda**, **Akkanna-Madanna**.
xa: ⚠ First Hindu cave temples in **India** = **Guptas** at **Udayagiri (MP)**.
**G2 2019** trap options for the Brahmanical caves: **Ikshvakus**, **Salankayanas**, **Pallavas**.
The caves date to the **4th-6th c.**; Undavalli **4th-5th c.**

56.s: The Undavalli cave temples are located near which city?
56.x: Undavalli lies on the Krishna bank near Vijayawada (APPSC GS 2019 key), in Guntur district. Nellore is linked with Bhairavakonda, Visakhapatnam with Bojjannakonda, and Hyderabad with Keesaragutta and Chaitanyapuri.
56.tq: Undavalli: city key Vijayawada; revenue district Guntur.
xs: Undavalli is near **Vijayawada** — option **(1)** (the **APPSC GS 2019** key).
It lies on the **Krishna** bank; its revenue district is **Guntur**.
**Nellore** is linked with **Bhairavakonda**; **Keesaragutta** is in Medchal-Malkajgiri near Hyderabad.
xa: Precisely: **Tadepalli mandal**, inside the **Amaravati** capital area near **Mangalagiri**.
**Mogalrajapuram** is in Vijayawada itself, now **NTR district**.
**Akkanna-Madanna** caves are on **Indrakeeladri hill**, Vijayawada.

56.s: Which of the following statements about Undavalli caves is NOT correct?
o: The ground floor is more finely detailed than the upper levels.
The upper levels are finely detailed, while the ground floor remains crude and unfinished.
They were carved from the top downward.
They have four storeys and three main caves.
56.x: The ground floor is crude and unfinished, whereas the upper levels are finely detailed. Undavalli has four storeys with three main caves and was carved top-down.
56.tq: Find the reversed comparison in the statement about the quality of the storeys.
xs: The false statement is that the **ground floor is more finely detailed** — option **(1)**.
Undavalli was carved **top-down**: upper levels finely detailed, **ground floor crude and unfinished**.
It has **four storeys** and **3 main caves**.
xa: Centrepiece: **monolithic reclining Vishnu, Ananta Padmanabha Swamy**, about **5 m (16 ft)**.
**Purnakumbha** motifs appear throughout.
Date: **4th-5th c. CE**, regional form of the **Gupta** rock-cut style.

56.s: The principal sculpture of Undavalli caves is a monolithic image of:
o: Reclining Vishnu as Ananta Padmanabha Swamy
56.x: The centrepiece of Undavalli is a monolithic reclining Vishnu, identified as Ananta Padmanabha Swamy, approximately 5 metres or 16 feet long.
56.tq: Use the distinctive main sculpture and its iconographic form to eliminate nearby cave images.
xs: The centrepiece is a **monolithic reclining Vishnu as Ananta Padmanabha Swamy** — option **(1)**.
It is about **5 m (16 ft)** long.
**Nataraja** is at **Mogalrajapuram** (Cave 5); **Durga** has Mogalrajapuram Cave 4.
xa: An earlier **Buddha image was replaced by Vishnu** (some notes: padmasana Buddha).
Undavalli: **four storeys**, carved **top-down**.
**Purnakumbha** motifs run throughout.

56.s: Which sequence correctly represents the earlier religious use of Undavalli caves?
o: Buddhist abode → Jain abode → Hindu temple
Jain abode → Buddhist monastic use → Hindu temple
Hindu temple → Buddhist monastery → Jain abode
Jain abode → Hindu temple → Buddhist monastery
56.x: Undavalli was first used as a Jain abode, later by Buddhist monks, and subsequently converted into a Hindu temple.
56.tq: Arrange the stages of religious use in the stated historical sequence.
xs: The sequence is **Jain abode → Buddhist monks → Hindu temple** — option **(2)**.
The Buddha image was later **replaced by Vishnu**.
xa: The present deity is **Ananta Padmanabha Swamy**, about **5 m (16 ft)** long.
⚠ **Aug 2026** test: "built by the **Cholas** as a Hindu temple, later Buddhist" is **false**.
Dated **4th-5th c. CE**.

56.s: Undavalli caves are generally dated to the:
56.x: Undavalli is dated to the fourth–fifth centuries CE and represents a regional form of the Gupta rock-cut style.
56.tq: Distinguish the early date of Undavalli from the later Pallava period.
xs: Undavalli is dated to the **4th–5th centuries CE** — option **(1)**.
It is a regional form of the **Gupta** rock-cut style.
The **7th–8th c.** is the Pallava dating some give for **Bhairavakonda**.
xa: Vishnukundin caves overall: **4th-6th c.**; **Mahendravarman I's** Pallava caves: **7th c.**
First Hindu cave temples of India: **Guptas** at **Udayagiri (MP)**.
Undavalli shows **Pallava influence** too.

56.s:
With reference to the Undavalli caves, consider the following statements:
1. They are situated in Guntur district on the Krishna.
2. Their architecture represents a Vishnukundina adaptation of the Gupta rock-cut style.
3. They contain a five-metre reclining image of Ananta Padmanabha Vishnu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
56.x: All three statements are correct. The Undavalli caves are in Guntur on the Krishna and feature Vishnukundina adaptation of Gupta rock-cut architecture, including the five-metre reclining Ananta Padmanabha Vishnu.
56.tq: Combine location, architectural affiliation and identifying monument details.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
1: Undavalli is in **Guntur district** on the **Krishna**. 2: it is a Vishnukundin regional form of the **Gupta rock-cut style**.
3: it has a **reclining Ananta Padmanabha Vishnu** about **5 m** long.
xa: Earlier use: **Jain** abode, then **Buddhist** monks, then **Hindu** temple.
Undavalli: **four storeys**, carved **top-down**, ground floor **unfinished**.
**Purnakumbha** motifs throughout.

56.s:
Consider the following statements about the Undavalli caves:
1. They were built by the Cholas as a Hindu temple and later used by Buddhists.
2. They are situated on the bank of the Krishna.
3. They contain a monolithic reclining statue of Ananta Padmanabha Swamy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
56.x: Statement 1 is false: Undavalli is a Vishnukundin cave of the 4th-5th c. CE that was a Jain abode, then Buddhist, then a Hindu temple; the Cholas did not build it. Statements 2 and 3 are correct. So A, C and D, which include statement 1, are wrong; B is right.
56.tq: Undavalli: Vishnukundin, not Chola; Jain -> Buddhist -> Hindu.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
1 wrong: Undavalli is **Vishnukundin** (**4th-5th c. CE**), a **Jain** abode, then **Buddhist**, then **Hindu** — not built by the **Cholas**.
2 correct: on the **Krishna** bank. 3 correct: **monolithic reclining Ananta Padmanabha Swamy**.
xa: This exact framing appeared in an **Aug 2026** test.
Undavalli is in **Tadepalli mandal**, Guntur, in the **Amaravati** capital area.
AP held the two-day **Telugu Mahotsavam** at Undavalli on **25-26 Jul 2026**.

56.s: The Mogalrajapuram cave complex consists of how many caves?
56.x: Mogalrajapuram has five caves in all. The fifth cave is the largest and contains the Shiva Tandava Nataraja sculpture.
56.tq: Separate the total number of caves from the numbers associated with individual cave groups.
xs: Mogalrajapuram has **five** caves — option **(2)**.
**Cave 5**, the largest, has **Shiva Tandava Nataraja**.
⚠ **8** caves = **Bhairavakonda**; **4** storeys = **Undavalli**.
xa: **Caves 1-3**: sanctums behind a pillared mandapa for the **Trimurti**.
**Cave 4**: **Durga** cave, **Ardhanarishvara** painted on the back wall.
Some notes file these under "**Akkana-Madanna**" — assign them to **Mogalrajapuram**.

56.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Caves 1–3 — exclusive shrines to the Kapalika sect
Caves 1–3 — sanctums behind a pillared mandapa for the Trimurti
Cave 4 — largest cave with Shiva Tandava Nataraja
Cave 5 — Durga cave with Ardhanarishvara on the back wall
56.x: Caves 1–3 contain sanctums behind a pillared mandapa and are associated with Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva. Cave 4 is the Durga cave, while Cave 5 is the largest and contains Shiva Tandava Nataraja.
56.tq: Match each cave number with its specific feature and reject the swapped descriptions.
xs: **Caves 1–3 — sanctums behind a pillared mandapa for the Trimurti** — option **(2)**.
**Cave 4** is the **Durga** cave with **Ardhanarishvara**; **Cave 5** is the largest, with **Shiva Tandava Nataraja**.
The **Kapalika** sect belongs to **Bhairavakonda**, not Mogalrajapuram.
xa: Trimurti = **Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva**.
Trimurti figures also sit on the **kapota** (eave) above pillar capitals.
Mogalrajapuram is in **Vijayawada**, now **NTR district**.

56.s: In the Mogalrajapuram caves, the Trimurti figures are carved on the:
56.x: Trimurti figures are carved on the kapota, or eave, above the pillar capitals at Mogalrajapuram.
56.tq: Identify the precise architectural location rather than the general shrine area.
xs: The Trimurti figures are on the **kapota above the pillar capitals** — option **(4)**.
The **kapota** is the decorated **eave** above the capitals.
xa: Some notes read these figures as **three goddesses**.
**Dwarapalas** flank shrine entrances, as in Pallava caves.
**Kumbha (pot) capitals** with lion bases mark **Bhairavakonda**.

56.s:
Consider the following statements about the Bhairavakonda caves:
1. There are twelve rock-cut caves, all dedicated to Shiva.
2. The site was a centre of Shaivism, specifically of the Kapalika sect.
3. The pillars rest on lion pedestals and carry pot (kumbha) capitals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
56.x: Statement 1 is wrong: Bhairavakonda has eight rock-cut caves (4, 9 and 12 are the usual traps). Statement 2 is correct: it was a Shaiva centre of the Kapalika sect. Statement 3 is correct: lion pedestals under the pillars with kumbha capitals. So A, C and D, which include statement 1, are wrong; B is right.
56.tq: Bhairavakonda = 8 caves, Shiva, Kapalika, lion pedestals.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
1 wrong: Bhairavakonda has **8** caves, not twelve (traps **4, 9, 12**).
2 correct: a **Shaiva** centre of the **Kapalika** sect. 3 correct: **lion pedestals** with **kumbha (pot) capitals**.
xa: **G2 2012** asked the cave count; **G2 2008** asked the religion (traps: Buddhism, Jainism, Vaishnavism).
Attribution: **Madhava Varma I** vs **Pallava (7th-8th c.)**.
Bhairavakonda is where the **Vishnukundin and Pallava styles overlap**.

56.s: Which statement best describes the debate regarding the dynastic attribution of Bhairavakonda caves?
o: They are attributed to Madhava Varma I by some sources, while another source dates them to the Pallava period.
They are unanimously attributed to the Satavahanas.
They are unanimously attributed to the Guptas of Udayagiri.
They are attributed to the Eastern Chalukyas by all authorities.
56.x: APP and CDX credit Madhava Varma I of the Vishnukundin dynasty, whereas APHQ dates the caves to the Pallava period of the seventh–eighth centuries CE.
56.tq: Identify the disputed attribution rather than selecting an absolute, unanimous claim.
xs: Most notes credit **Madhava Varma I**, while some date it to the **Pallava period** — option **(1)**.
**APP/CDX** say Madhava Varma I; **APHQ** says **Pallava (7th-8th c.)**.
The Pallava case rests on its **close likeness to the early Pallava caves of Mahabalipuram**.
xa: **8 rock-cut caves**, all to **Shiva**.
**Kapalika** Shaiva centre.
District: **Nellore** (exam key) vs **Prakasam** (CDI).

56.s: The close resemblance of Bhairavakonda caves to which monuments is noted in the discussion of their attribution?
56.x: Bhairavakonda closely resembles the early Pallava caves of Mahabalipuram, which is why some sources (APHQ) date it to the Pallava period of the 7th–8th c., although most notes credit Madhava Varma I of the Vishnukundins.
56.tq: Link the debated style to the specific comparison site named in the evidence.
xs: Bhairavakonda closely resembles the **early Pallava caves of Mahabalipuram** — option **(2)**.
This likeness is why some date it to the **Pallava period (7th-8th c.)**; most notes keep **Madhava Varma I**.
**Udayagiri** caves are **Gupta** — the first Hindu cave temples in India.
xa: Pallava (**Mahendravarman I**) caves used **lion-based (simha-mukha) pillars**.
Bhairavakonda pillars: **lion pedestals** + **pot capitals**.
Bhairavakonda = overlap of **Vishnukundin and Pallava** styles.

56.s: Which architectural plan is characteristic of the cave temples described here?
o: A circular stupa without any shrine cell
A free-standing tower enclosing a circumambulatory passage only
A pillared mandapa in front of one or more rock-cut garbhagriha cells
A rectangular palace with no religious chamber
56.x: The typical plan consists of a pillared mandapa or ardhamandapa in front of one or more garbhagriha cells cut into the rock. At Mogalrajapuram, the shrines lie behind the mandapa.
56.tq: Translate the architectural description into a plan-based identification.
xs: The plan is **a pillared mandapa in front of one or more rock-cut garbhagriha cells** — option **(3)**.
The early hall is the **ardhamandapa**; at **Mogalrajapuram** shrines sit behind it.
xa: **Dwarapalas** flank shrine entrances.
**Undavalli** is storeyed (**four storeys**) on the same plan.
**Structural temples** were of **brick**, with garbhagriha, antarala-mandapa and mukhamandapa (**Keesaragutta**).

56.s: Dwarapalas in these cave temples are generally placed:
o: above the roofline of the mandapa
flanking the entrances to the shrines
inside the rear wall of the garbhagriha
at the centre of the pillared hall
56.x: Dwarapalas, or door guardians, flank the entrances to the shrine spaces, a feature also seen in contemporary Pallava caves.
56.tq: Use the functional meaning of the architectural term to locate the figures.
xs: **Dwarapalas** (door guardians) **flank the entrances to the shrines** — option **(2)**.
The same feature appears in contemporary **Pallava** caves.
xa: Plan: **pillared mandapa (ardhamandapa)** before rock-cut **garbhagriha** cells.
**Kapota** = decorated eave above the capitals at Mogalrajapuram.
**Kumbha capitals** on lion-based pillars mark **Bhairavakonda**.

56.s: The cave architecture described combines which traditions and also borrows from the Pallavas?
56.x: The style is described as a blend of Ikshvaku and Vakataka traditions, with additional influence borrowed from the Pallavas.
56.tq: Identify the paired stylistic traditions rather than a single dynastic influence.
xs: The style blends **Ikshvaku and Vakataka traditions** with Pallava borrowings — option **(3)**.
The hills were cut **from the south**.
xa: Undavalli adapts the **Gupta** rock-cut style; base is **Gupta-Vakataka**.
Undavalli shows **Pallava influence**; Vishnukundins "**imitated the Pallava style**".
Structural temples: **brick** (Keesaragutta).

56.s: Which one of the following correctly compares Vishnukundin caves with the rock-cut caves of Mahendravarman I?
o: Vishnukundin caves are generally dated to the 7th century, while the Pallava caves are dated to the 4th–5th centuries.
Vishnukundin caves are generally dated to the 4th–6th centuries, while the Pallava caves are dated to the 7th century.
Vishnukundin caves post-date the Pallava caves by three centuries.
Both groups are confined to the 10th century.
56.x: The Vishnukundin caves are generally dated to the fourth–sixth centuries, with Undavalli in the fourth–fifth century, while Mahendravarman I’s Pallava caves belong to the seventh century.
56.tq: Compare the two date ranges directly before considering the stylistic details.
xs: Vishnukundin caves: **4th–6th c.**; **Mahendravarman I's** Pallava caves: **7th c.** — option **(2)**.
**Undavalli** sits at the early end, **4th-5th c.**
xa: Pallavas introduced **mandapa + garbhagriha** and **lion-based (simha-mukha) pillars**.
Vishnukundin pillars: **lion pedestals**, **pot capitals** (Bhairavakonda).
Pallava style was later taken up by **Telugu Chodas** and **Eastern Chalukyas**.

56.s: Which statement about the relationship between Vishnukundin and Pallava styles is correct?
o: The Vishnukundins imitated or borrowed from Pallava style, and Bhairavakonda reflects an overlap of the two styles.
The Pallavas wholly imitated the Vishnukundins during the fourth century.
The Vishnukundins had no contact with Pallava architectural forms.
Only Buddhist caves show interaction between the two traditions.
56.x: The Vishnukundin style had a Gupta–Vakataka base but also borrowed from or imitated Pallava forms. Bhairavakonda is specifically identified as a zone where the two styles overlap.
56.tq: Distinguish influence and overlap from the false claim of complete stylistic isolation.
xs: Vishnukundins **imitated / borrowed from the Pallava style**, and **Bhairavakonda** shows the overlap — option **(1)**.
**Undavalli** too shows **Pallava influence**.
xa: Vishnukundin base: **Gupta-Vakataka**; also described as an **Ikshvaku and Vakataka** blend.
Vishnukundin caves **4th-6th c.**; Pallava caves **7th c.**
Bhairavakonda resembles the early **Pallava caves of Mahabalipuram**.

56.s: The rock-cut cave style of the Pallava ruler Mahendravarman I, with lion-based pillars, was later taken up by the
56.x: The Pallava (Mahendravarman I) cave style of the 7th c. was later taken up by the Telugu Chodas and Eastern Chalukyas. The Kushanas, Guptas, Mauryas, Sungas, Satavahanas and Ikshvakus all came earlier, so could not take up a 7th-century style.
56.tq: Mahendravarman caves -> later Telugu Chodas, Eastern Chalukyas.
xs: The Pallava style was later taken up by the **Telugu Chodas and Eastern Chalukyas** — option **(3)**.
**Mahendravarman I's** style (**7th c.**) used **lion-based (simha-mukha) pillars** and the **mandapa + garbhagriha** plan.
xa: Vishnukundin caves (**4th-6th c.**) rest on a **Gupta-Vakataka** base.
**Bhairavakonda** is where the two styles overlap.
**Undavalli** shows Pallava influence.

56.s: Who announced that the “Telugu Mahotsavam” would become an annual festival held in every region?
o: The Chief Secretary of Andhra Pradesh
56.x: Minister Kandula Durgesh announced at the close of the festival that it would become an annual festival held in every region.
56.tq: Identify the person associated with the specific announcement rather than the venue or organising authority.
xs: Minister **Kandula Durgesh** announced the festival would become **annual** in every region — option **(2)**.
The **Telugu Mahotsavam** was held at **Undavalli Caves** on **25-26 Jul 2026**.
xa: Undavalli lies inside the **Amaravati capital area**, **Tadepalli mandal**.
Undavalli: **Vishnukundin**, **4th-5th c. CE**, reclining **Ananta Padmanabha Swamy**.
Undavalli is on the **Krishna** bank.

56.s: The two-day Telugu Mahotsavam associated with the Undavalli caves was held in
56.x: The AP government's two-day Telugu Mahotsavam at the Undavalli Caves was held on 25–26 July 2026, so July 2026 is right; the April and 2025 dates are distractors.
56.tq: Separate close current-affairs dates by retaining both the month and year.
xs: The two-day **Telugu Mahotsavam** at Undavalli was held in **July 2026** (**25-26 Jul**) — option **(4)**.
The April and 2025 dates are distractors.
xa: Minister **Kandula Durgesh** said it will be an **annual** festival in every region.
Undavalli is in **Tadepalli mandal** in the **Amaravati** capital area.
Undavalli's centrepiece: **monolithic reclining Vishnu**, about **5 m (16 ft)**.

56.s: Undavalli Caves are situated within which of the following areas?
o: The Visakhapatnam metropolitan region, in Bheemunipatnam mandal
The Tirupati temple area, in Chandragiri mandal
The Kurnool urban area, in Orvakal mandal
The Amaravati capital area, in Tadepalli mandal
56.x: Undavalli Caves lie inside the Amaravati capital area, specifically in Tadepalli mandal.
56.tq: Apply the location test by matching the monument with its mandal and broader regional setting.
xs: Undavalli lies in **the Amaravati capital area, in Tadepalli mandal** — option **(4)**.
Its district is **Guntur**, on the **Krishna** bank near **Vijayawada/Mangalagiri**.
xa: The **Telugu Mahotsavam** was held there on **25-26 Jul 2026**.
**APPSC GS 2019** key for Undavalli's location: **Vijayawada**.
Undavalli is a **Vishnukundin** cave (**G2 2025**).

56.s: The two-day “Telugu Mahotsavam” held at Undavalli Caves in July 2026 was conducted on which dates?
56.x: The two-day “Telugu Mahotsavam” at Undavalli Caves was held on 25–26 July 2026.
56.tq: Use the precise date range and eliminate the options shifted by one day.
xs: The **Telugu Mahotsavam** at Undavalli was held on **25–26 July 2026** — option **(1)**.
It was a **two-day** AP government festival.
xa: Minister **Kandula Durgesh** announced it will become **annual** in every region.
Undavalli is in the **Amaravati** capital area (**Tadepalli mandal**).
Undavalli: **four storeys**, **3 main caves**, carved **top-down**.

57.s: Which statement best describes the social structure of ancient Andhra during the Satavahana period?
o: It was predominantly shaped by the Vedic varna system, with the Satavahanas playing a significant role in its development.
It was based exclusively on tribal organisation and rejected the Vedic varna system.
It was organised only according to Buddhist monastic rules.
It was shaped mainly by Roman administrative institutions.
57.x: The social structure of ancient Andhra was predominantly influenced by the Vedic varna system, and the Satavahanas played a crucial role in it.
57.tq: Identify the broad social feature and reject options using absolute terms such as ‘exclusively’ and ‘only’.
xs: Ancient Andhra society was **predominantly shaped by the Vedic varna system**, with the **Satavahanas** playing a crucial role — option **(1)**.
This statement pair was asked in **APPSC-GS 2024**.
The Satavahana king was **duty-bound to enforce varna-dharma**.
xa: **Gautamiputra Satakarni** claimed he **stopped varna-sankara**; the Nasik prasasti calls him "**Ekabrahmana**".
Brahmins got **tax-free villages**; the **Nanaghat inscription** mentions Brahmins trained in Vedic learning.
The **Vishnukundins** followed **varnasramadharma**.

57.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Satavahana king and the Brahmanical order:
1. The Satavahana king was duty-bound to enforce varna-dharma.
2. Tax-free villages were granted to Brahmins.
3. The Nanaghat inscription refers to Brahmins trained in Vedic learning and rituals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: All three statements are correct. Satavahana kings were associated with the enforcement of varna-dharma, granted tax-free villages to Brahmins, and the Nanaghat inscription mentions Brahmins trained in Vedic learning and ritual.
57.tq: Test all statements against the connected evidence on royal duty, land grants and the Nanaghat inscription.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
1: the king was **duty-bound to enforce varna-dharma**. 2: Brahmins received **tax-free villages**.
3: the **Nanaghat inscription** mentions Brahmins trained in **Vedic learning and ritual**.
xa: **Gautamiputra Satakarni** claimed to have **stopped varna-sankara** (mixing of castes).
Nasik prasasti: "**Ekabrahmana**" and humbler of **Kshatriya pride**.
Agrahara recipients named: **Agnisarma**, **Easwarasarma**.

57.s: Gautamiputra Satakarni claimed in his inscriptions that he had stopped which of the following?
o: The grant of villages to Brahmins
57.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni claimed that he had stopped varna-sankara, or the mixing of castes.
57.tq: Use the exact technical term associated with the ruler’s inscriptional claim.
xs: **Gautamiputra Satakarni** claimed he **stopped varna-sankara** (mixing of castes) — option **(1)**.
His **Nasik prasasti** calls him "**Ekabrahmana**" and humbler of Kshatriya pride.
xa: ⚠ Varna-sankara still happened: with occupational diversification it produced many **sub-castes** (Gathasaptasati, Kamasutra).
His name is a **matronymic** — **Gautamiputra**.
His mother **Gautami Balasri** funded a cave-vihara at **Nasik**.

57.s: The assimilation of which groups into the Kshatriya order is referred to in the context of early Andhra society?
57.x: Greeks, Sakas, Pahlavas and Kushanas adopted Indian names and faiths and were assimilated into the Kshatriya order. The list also includes the Kardhamakas and Western Kshatrapas.
57.tq: Discriminate between the historically associated groups rather than selecting a familiar dynastic list.
xs: **Greeks, Sakas, Pahlavas and Kushanas** took Indian names/faiths and gained **Kshatriya status** — option **(2)**.
The list also includes the **Kardhamakas** and **Western Kshatrapas**.
xa: Examples: Saka **Nahapana's daughter Dakshamitra**, son-in-law **Rishabhadatta**, and **Rudradaman**.
**Vasishthiputra Satakarni** married the daughter of Saka **Rudradaman**.
Kshatriya claims continued later: **Vanniyakula Kshatriya Mahasabha (1888)**, **Akhil Bharatiya Kshatriya Mahasabha (1897)**.

57.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Sub-caste)
 a. Halikas
 b. Sethis
 c. Selavaddikas
 d. Swarnakaras

List-II (Occupation)
 i. Goldsmiths
 ii. Farmers
 iii. Merchants
 iv. Stone sculptors or masons

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
57.x: Halikas were farmers, Sethis were merchants, Selavaddikas were stone sculptors or masons, and Swarnakaras were goldsmiths.
57.tq: Start with the sure occupational pair and eliminate codes that reverse the remaining professions.
xs: Correct matching is **a–ii, b–iii, c–iv, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Halikas** = farmers; **Sethis** = merchants; **Selavaddikas** = stone sculptors/masons; **Swarnakaras** = goldsmiths.
xa: **Gandhikas** = perfumers; **Tailapishakas** = oil pressers; **Golikas** = cowherds.
Sub-castes grew from **varna-sankara** + occupational diversification (**Gathasaptasati**, **Kamasutra**).
Halikas were **the emerging agricultural group**.

57.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
57.x: Halikas were farmers, not goldsmiths. Gandhikas, Tailapishakas and Golikas were respectively perfumers, oil pressers and cowherds.
57.tq: Find the single occupational mismatch among closely related caste-profession pairs.
xs: **Halikas — Goldsmiths** is wrong: Halikas were **farmers** — option **(3)**.
Goldsmiths were **Swarnakaras**.
The others are right: **Tailapishakas** = oil pressers, **Golikas** = cowherds, **Gandhikas** = perfumers.
xa: **Sethis** = merchants; **Selavaddikas** = stone sculptors / masons.
Exam angle: match **sub-caste name → occupation**.
Sources for sub-castes: **Gathasaptasati** and **Kamasutra**.

57.s:
Consider the following statements about the Vishnukundins:
1. Vaisyas were associated with internal and external trade.
2. Sudras such as carpenters, sculptors and handloom weavers had a recognised place in society.
3. Farmers were regarded as the backbone and received land grants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: All three are correct. Under the Vishnukundins, who followed varnasramadharma, Vaisyas carried on internal and external trade, Sudras such as carpenters, sculptors and handloom weavers had a recognised place, and farmers were 'the backbone' and received land grants.
57.tq: Check whether each statement preserves the occupation and social position assigned to the group.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
1: **Vaisyas** handled **internal + external trade**. 2: **Sudras** — carpenters, sculptors, handloom weavers — had a **recognised place**.
3: **Farmers were "the backbone"** and received **land grants**.
xa: The Vishnukundins followed **varnasramadharma**.
They founded **Ghatikasthanas** (Vedic colleges).
Family deity **Sriparvataswamy**; titles **Paramamaheswara**, **Parama Brahmanya**.

57.s: Which evidence is associated with the practice of sati in early Andhra society?
o: A Nagarjunakonda sculpture and the account of the Greek writer Strabo
57.x: A Nagarjunakonda sculpture depicts a woman committing sati, and the Greek writer Strabo also noted the practice.
57.tq: Combine archaeological and literary evidence without adding unrelated inscriptions.
xs: Sati is shown in a **Nagarjunakonda sculpture** and noted by the Greek writer **Strabo** — option **(3)**.
**Amaravati reliefs** show dress and popular worship; the **Nanaghat inscription** mentions Vedic Brahmins.
xa: **Widows** were expected to observe **celibacy**.
**Polygamy** existed among the **upper classes**.
Marriage was a **sacred institution**.

57.s: Which one of the following statements best describes marriage customs in early Andhra society?
o: Marriage was regarded as a sacred institution, polygamy existed among upper classes, and widows were expected to observe celibacy
Marriage was restricted to members of the same occupational group and widowhood had no social regulations
Marriage was regarded as a temporary social contract and widow remarriage was compulsory
Monogamy was compulsory among all social groups and widows were required to enter religious orders
57.x: Marriage was considered a sacred institution. Polygamy was prevalent among the upper classes, while widows were expected to observe celibacy.
57.tq: Use the option containing the complete and precise combination of the three social practices.
xs: Marriage was **sacred**, **polygamy** existed among upper classes, and **widows** observed **celibacy** — option **(1)**.
⚠ Marriage was not limited to one group: **Kathasaritsagara** mentions **inter-caste marriages**.
xa: **Anuloma** (higher man + lower woman) → offspring **Ugra**.
**Viloma/Pratiloma** (lower man + higher woman) → offspring **Chandala**.
**Sati**: a **Nagarjunakonda** sculpture and **Strabo**.

57.s:
With reference to the terms Anuloma and Viloma, consider the following statements:
1. Anuloma refers to the union of a higher-caste man with a lower-caste woman.
2. The offspring of an Anuloma union was termed Ugra.
3. Viloma refers to the union of a lower-caste man with a higher-caste woman.
4. The offspring of a Viloma union was termed Chandala.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: All four statements are correct. Anuloma was a higher-caste man–lower-caste woman union producing offspring termed Ugra, while Viloma or Pratiloma was the reverse union producing offspring termed Chandala.
57.tq: Check each pair separately, especially the reversed social direction in Anuloma and Viloma.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(3)**.
1–2: **Anuloma** = higher-caste man + lower-caste woman; offspring **Ugra**.
3–4: **Viloma (Pratiloma)** = lower-caste man + higher-caste woman; offspring **Chandala**.
xa: ⚠ **Anuloma → Ugra**; **Viloma → Chandala** — a frequent swap trap.
**Kathasaritsagara** mentions inter-caste marriages: caste was **not fully rigid** at first.
**Polygamy** among upper classes; widows kept **celibacy**.

57.s: Which of the following literary works mentions inter-caste marriages, indicating that caste was not completely rigid in the early period?
57.x: Kathasaritsagara mentions inter-caste marriages, showing that caste practices were not completely rigid at that stage.
57.tq: Test the exact literary source rather than the broader theme of social history.
xs: **Kathasaritsagara** mentions inter-caste marriages — option **(4)**.
It shows caste was **not fully rigid** at first.
**Gathasaptasati** is cited for sub-castes and everyday life, not for this point.
xa: **Anuloma** offspring = **Ugra**; **Viloma** offspring = **Chandala**.
Sub-castes arose from **varna-sankara** + occupations.
Marriage = **sacred institution**.

57.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Vasishthiputra Satakarni — Daughter of Saka Rudradaman
Satakarni I — Daughter of Maharathi Tranakayira
57.x: Hala married the Sri Lankan princess Lilavati. The daughter of Saka Rudradaman was married to Vasishthiputra Satakarni.
57.tq: Find the swapped person–marriage connection among otherwise familiar pairs.
xs: **Hala — daughter of Saka Rudradaman** is wrong — option **(4)**.
**Hala** married the Sri Lankan princess **Lilavati**; **Vasishthiputra Satakarni** married **Rudradaman's** daughter.
**Satakarni I** married the daughter of Maharathi **Tranakayira** — correctly matched.
xa: Hala wrote the **Gathasaptasati**, about **700 verses** in **Maharashtri Prakrit**.
**Rudradaman** is an example of foreigners gaining **Kshatriya status**.
Women took titles from husbands: **Mahasenapatni**, **Mahabhojaki**, **Maharathi**.

57.s: Which of the following best characterises the position of women in early Andhra society?
o: Society was patriarchal and based on joint families, but women enjoyed considerable respect and freedom.
Women enjoyed authority only within Buddhist monasteries.
Women were excluded from festivals, assemblies and public life.
Society was entirely matrilineal and had no joint-family system.
57.x: The society was patriarchal and organised around joint families, yet women enjoyed considerable respect and participated in festivals, assemblies and public life.
57.tq: Choose the balanced statement and reject extreme claims that deny one side of the comparison.
xs: Society was **patriarchal with a joint family**, yet women had **considerable respect and freedom** — option **(1)**.
Women joined men in **festivals, assemblies and public life**.
xa: Donative inscriptions record women's gifts on such occasions.
**Matronymics**: **Gautamiputra** Satakarni, **Vasishthiputra** Pulumavi.
Titles from husbands: **Mahasenapatni**, **Mahabhojaki**, **Maharathi**.
Female poets in Hala's Gathasaptasati: **Madhavi**, **Revati**, **Anupamalabdha**, **Anulakshmi**.

57.s: The names Gautamiputra Satakarni and Vasishthiputra Pulumavi illustrate which practice?
o: Use of matronymics by Satavahana kings
Use of occupational surnames by merchants
57.x: Gautamiputra and Vasishthiputra are examples of matronymics, in which the ruler’s name incorporated the name of his mother.
57.tq: Recognise the naming pattern instead of treating the names as ordinary royal titles.
