xs: **Gautamiputra** and **Vasishthiputra** show **matronymics** used by Satavahana kings — option **(2)**.
The king's name carried his **mother's** name — a sign of women's standing.
xa: Women also bore titles from husbands: **Mahasenapatni**, **Mahabhojaki**, **Maharathi**.
**Gautami Balasri** funded a cave-vihara at **Nasik**.
**Vasishthiputra Satakarni** married **Rudradaman's** daughter.

57.s: Which of the following was NOT listed as a female poet associated with Hala’s Gathasaptasati?
57.x: Madhavi, Revati and Anulakshmi are listed as female poets in the Gathasaptasati. Gautami Balasri was a Satavahana woman patron who funded a cave-vihara at Nasik.
57.tq: Separate female literary contributors from female patrons of religious institutions.
xs: **Gautami Balasri** was not a Gathasaptasati poet — option **(4)**.
She was a **Satavahana** patron who funded a cave-vihara at **Nasik**.
The female poets were **Madhavi**, **Revati**, **Anupamalabdha** and **Anulakshmi**.
xa: Gathasaptasati: by **Hala**, about **700 verses**, **Maharashtri Prakrit**.
It is the **most important literary source** of Satavahana society (**APPSC 2019**).
⚠ **Bodhisiri** and **Chantisiri** were **Ikshvaku** patrons, not Satavahana.

57.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Woman)
 a. Gautami Balasri
 b. Bodhisiri
 c. Chantisiri

List-II (Association)
 i. Built the Mahachaitya at Nagarjunakonda
 ii. Greatest woman patron of Buddhism
 iii. Funded a cave-vihara at Nasik for Bhadrayaniya monks

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
57.x: Gautami Balasri funded a cave-vihara at Nasik, Bodhisiri was the greatest woman patron of Buddhism, and Chantisiri built the Mahachaitya at Nagarjunakonda.
57.tq: Begin with the distinctive monument or patronage association and verify the remaining pairs.
xs: Correct matching is **a–iii, b–ii, c–i** — option **(1)**.
**Gautami Balasri** (Satavahana) — cave-vihara at **Nasik** for Bhadrayaniya monks.
**Bodhisiri** (Ikshvaku) — **greatest woman patron of Buddhism**; **Chantisiri** (Ikshvaku) — **Mahachaitya** at Nagarjunakonda.
xa: Chantisiri was the sister of **Vasishthiputra Chantamula**.
CDX says Balasri's cave was "on the **Bhadrayana hill**".
Bodhisiri is known from the **Nagarjunakonda** inscriptions.

57.s: Which of the following correctly matches an educational centre with its nature?
o: Viharas — Centres exclusively for military training
57.x: Viharas were centres of Buddhist monastic learning. Ghatikasthanas were Vedic colleges, while agraharas were land grants to Vedic Brahmins.
57.tq: Distinguish educational institutions by their religious and institutional function.
xs: **Viharas — Buddhist monastic learning** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Ghatikasthanas** were **Vedic colleges**; **Agraharas** were **land grants to Vedic Brahmins**.
xa: **Nagarjunakonda** became a leading Buddhist learning centre of South India under **Ikshvaku** patronage.
Ghatikasthanas were established by the **Vishnukundins**.
Agrahara recipients named: **Agnisarma**, **Easwarasarma**.

57.s: Nagarjunakonda became a leading centre of Buddhist learning in South India primarily through the patronage of which dynasty?
57.x: Nagarjunakonda developed as a leading centre of Buddhist learning in South India under Ikshvaku patronage.
57.tq: Associate the educational centre with the dynasty responsible for its patronage.
xs: Nagarjunakonda grew as a Buddhist learning centre under the patronage of the **Ikshvakus** — option **(1)**.
The **Vishnukundins** are linked instead with **Ghatikasthanas** (Vedic colleges).
xa: Nagarjunakonda = Ikshvaku capital **Vijayapuri**, with an **amphitheatre/stadium**.
Ikshvaku women patrons: **Bodhisiri** and **Chantisiri** (Mahachaitya).
Nagarjunakonda also had Brahmanical shrines such as **Pushpabhadraswami**.

57.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to Vishnukundin scholar-kings?
o: Govindavarma — Shadabhigna, master of six sciences
Vikramendra Varma — Founder of the Mahachaitya at Nagarjunakonda
Indrabhattaraka Varma — Greatest woman patron of Buddhism
57.x: Govindavarma was described as shadabhigna, or a master of six sciences. Vikramendra Varma was called mahakavi and Parama Sogatasya, while Indrabhattaraka Varma was credited with founding ghatikas.
57.tq: Use the ruler-title association and reject swapped roles involving patrons, authors and founders.
xs: **Govindavarma — 'shadabhigna'** (master of six sciences) — option **(1)**.
**Vikramendra Varma** was **'mahakavi'** and **'Parama Sogatasya'**; the **Mahachaitya** was built by **Chantisiri**.
**Bodhisiri** was the greatest woman patron; **Hala** wrote the **Gathasaptasati**.
xa: **Indrabhattaraka Varma**: **'Ghatika Vapta punyasancharya'**, credited with founding ghatikas.
Vishnukundin family deity: **Sriparvataswamy**.
The Vishnukundins also **repaired and built viharas**.

57.s: The expression ‘Ghatika Vapta punyasancharya’ is associated with which Vishnukundin ruler?
57.x: Indrabhattaraka Varma is associated with the expression ‘Ghatika Vapta punyasancharya’ and was credited with founding ghatikas.
57.tq: Recognise the distinctive inscriptional expression linked to the ruler credited with founding ghatikas.
xs: **'Ghatika Vapta punyasancharya'** belongs to **Indrabhattaraka Varma** — option **(3)**.
He is credited with **founding ghatikas**.
**Vasishthiputra Chantamula** was an **Ikshvaku**, not a Vishnukundin.
xa: **Govindavarma** = **'shadabhigna'**; **Vikramendra Varma** = **'mahakavi'**.
**Ghatikasthanas** were Vedic colleges set up by the Vishnukundins.
Vishnukundin titles: **Paramamaheswara**, **Parama Brahmanya**.

57.s:
Consider the following statements about religion under the Vishnukundins:
1. Their family deity was Sriparvataswamy.
2. They used the titles Paramamaheswara and Parama Brahmanya.
3. Their patronage was confined to Shaiva temples such as Ramalingeswara, and they built no viharas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
57.x: Statement 1 is correct: Sriparvataswamy was the family deity. Statement 2 is correct: they bore the titles Paramamaheswara and Parama Brahmanya. Statement 3 is wrong: besides the Ramalingeswara Shiva temple they also repaired and built viharas. So A misses statement 2, and C and D wrongly include statement 3; B is right.
57.tq: Vishnukundins were Shaiva-Brahmanical but still repaired and built viharas.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
1 correct: family deity **Sriparvataswamy**. 2 correct: titles **Paramamaheswara** and **Parama Brahmanya**.
3 wrong: besides the **Ramalingeswara** Shiva temple, they **repaired and built viharas**.
xa: **Vikramendra Varma** was called **'Parama Sogatasya'**.
They followed **varnasramadharma**.
They established **Ghatikasthanas**.

57.s: Which of the following correctly describes the religious policy reflected in the activities of the Ikshvaku kings and queens?
o: Kings patronised Buddhism while queens performed only Vedic sacrifices
Kings performed Vedic sacrifices, while queens patronised Buddhism
Both kings and queens exclusively patronised Jainism
Neither kings nor queens supported organised religious institutions
57.x: Ikshvaku kings performed Vedic sacrifices, whereas Ikshvaku queens patronised Buddhism.
57.tq: Use the contrast between the roles of kings and queens to avoid reversing the patrons.
xs: Ikshvaku **kings performed Vedic sacrifices**, while **queens patronised Buddhism** — option **(2)**.
**Vasishthiputra Chantamula** performed **Asvamedha** and **Vajapeya**.
xa: Queens: **Bodhisiri** (greatest woman patron) and **Chantisiri** (**Mahachaitya**).
Nagarjunakonda had Brahmanical shrines such as **Pushpabhadraswami**.
Nagarjunakonda became a leading Buddhist learning centre under **Ikshvaku** patronage.

57.s: Which of the following sacrifices was performed by Vasishthiputra Chantamula?
57.x: Vasishthiputra Chantamula, an Ikshvaku king, performed the Asvamedha and Vajapeya sacrifices.
57.tq: Recall the exact pair of sacrifices associated with the named ruler.
xs: **Vasishthiputra Chantamula** performed **Asvamedha and Vajapeya** — option **(2)**.
He was an **Ikshvaku** king; his queens and kinswomen patronised Buddhism.
xa: His sister **Chantisiri** built the **Mahachaitya** at Nagarjunakonda.
**Pushpabhadraswami** was a Brahmanical shrine at Nagarjunakonda.
Ikshvaku capital: **Vijayapuri** (Nagarjunakonda).

57.s: Nagarjunakonda is significant for the presence of which of the following religious features?
o: Vedic sacrificial altars without any Buddhist association
Only Jain caves patronised by the Ikshvakus
Only Buddhist monasteries and no Brahmanical shrines
Brahmanical shrines such as Pushpabhadraswami along with Buddhist establishments
57.x: Nagarjunakonda contained Buddhist establishments as well as Brahmanical shrines, including Pushpabhadraswami.
57.tq: Apply the principle of religious coexistence to identify the option that includes both traditions.
xs: Nagarjunakonda had **Brahmanical shrines such as Pushpabhadraswami** along with Buddhist establishments — option **(4)**.
Ikshvaku **kings** did Vedic sacrifices; **queens** patronised Buddhism.
xa: A **Nagarjunakonda sculpture** shows **sati**.
It had an **amphitheatre/stadium** for performances and games.
**Bodhisiri** is known from Nagarjunakonda inscriptions.

57.s: The reliefs at Amaravati depict the popular worship of which of the following, alongside Buddhist symbols?
o: Only Vedic fire altars and sacrificial posts
Jain tirthankaras, yakshas and lion pillars
57.x: Amaravati reliefs show the worship of nagas, yakshas and sacred trees alongside Buddhist symbols.
57.tq: Identify the complete set of folk-cult elements rather than selecting an unrelated religious group.
xs: Amaravati reliefs show worship of **nagas, yakshas and sacred trees** — option **(3)**.
They appear beside **Buddhist symbols**.
xa: **Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda reliefs** are the main visual evidence of dress and adornment.
Men: **lower cloth + turban**; women: **heavy anklets, bangles, girdles, necklaces**.
Early Andhra combined **Vedic varna order** with strong **Buddhist patronage**.

57.s: Which description of Hala’s Gathasaptasati is correct?
o: A Tamil epic dealing only with maritime trade
About 700 verses in Maharashtri Prakrit dealing with everyday social and cultural life
A Buddhist monastic code written in Pali
About 700 Sanskrit verses dealing exclusively with royal genealogy
57.x: The Gathasaptasati contains about 700 verses in Maharashtri Prakrit and discusses family, marriage, women, agriculture, trade, festivals and occupations.
57.tq: Combine the numerical, linguistic and thematic clues to identify the work precisely.
xs: Gathasaptasati: **about 700 verses in Maharashtri Prakrit** on **everyday social and cultural life** — option **(2)**.
It covers family, marriage, women, agriculture, trade, **festivals** and occupations.
xa: Author: King **Hala**, who married Sri Lankan princess **Lilavati**.
Female poets in it: **Madhavi**, **Revati**, **Anupamalabdha**, **Anulakshmi**.
**APPSC 2019**: most important literary source for Satavahana society.

57.s:
Consider the following statements about festivals and amusements in early Andhra society:
1. Women took part equally with men in festivals and gatherings.
2. 'Maiputa' was used by dancers known as Kusuma Lepanam.
3. The amphitheatre at Nagarjunakonda was used mainly for Vedic sacrifices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
57.x: Statement 1 is correct: women joined men in festivals and gatherings, and donative inscriptions record gifts on such occasions. Statement 2 is correct (APPSC 2019 key). Statement 3 is wrong: the amphitheatre at Nagarjunakonda (Ikshvaku capital Vijayapuri) was for performances and games. So B, C and D, which include statement 3, are wrong; A is right.
57.tq: Nagarjunakonda stadium = performances and games, not rituals.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
1 correct: women took part **equally with men** in festivals and gatherings. 2 correct: **'Maiputa'** dancers = **Kusuma Lepanam** (**APPSC 2019** key).
3 wrong: the **Nagarjunakonda amphitheatre** (capital **Vijayapuri**) was for **performances + games**.
xa: Donative inscriptions record women's gifts on such occasions.
**Gathasaptasati** describes festivals among everyday life.
Ikshvaku kings did Vedic sacrifices like **Asvamedha** — not linked to the amphitheatre.

57.s: Nagarjunakonda, which possessed an amphitheatre or stadium, was the capital known as which of the following?
57.x: Nagarjunakonda was identified with Vijayapuri, the capital of the Ikshvakus, and contained an amphitheatre or stadium for performances and games.
57.tq: Distinguish the site-capital-dynasty relationship from other well-known ancient capitals.
xs: Nagarjunakonda was **Vijayapuri**, the **Ikshvaku** capital — option **(3)**.
Its **amphitheatre/stadium** hosted performances and games.
xa: Nagarjunakonda became a leading **Buddhist learning** centre under Ikshvaku patronage.
**Chantisiri** built its **Mahachaitya**.
Brahmanical shrine there: **Pushpabhadraswami**.

57.s: Which of the following correctly describes the sculptural evidence from Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda concerning dress and ornaments?
o: The reliefs provide evidence exclusively about food habits and agricultural tools.
Men and women are uniformly shown in stitched military uniforms.
Women are shown without ornaments, while men wear only necklaces.
Men are shown in a lower cloth with a turban, while women are shown with heavy anklets, bangles, girdles and necklaces.
57.x: Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda reliefs show men wearing a lower cloth and turban, while women are depicted with heavy anklets, bangles, girdles and necklaces.
57.tq: Compare the gender-specific visual details and reject options using unsupported exclusivity.
xs: Men wear a **lower cloth with a turban**; women wear **heavy anklets, bangles, girdles and necklaces** — option **(4)**.
This comes from the **Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda reliefs**, the main visual evidence.
xa: Amaravati reliefs also show worship of **nagas, yakshas and sacred trees**.
A **Nagarjunakonda** sculpture shows **sati**.
**Gathasaptasati** is the main literary source of daily life.

57.s: Which of the following is regarded as the most important literary source for the social and cultural life of the Satavahana period?
57.x: Hala's Gathasaptasati, about 700 verses in Maharashtri Prakrit on family, marriage, agriculture, trade and festivals, is the most important literary source for Satavahana society (APPSC 2019). The Puranas mainly give dynastic lists, while the Aitareya Brahmana and the Dharmasutras are not sources for Satavahana everyday life.
57.tq: Satavahana social life source = Gathasaptasati (Hala).
xs: **Gathasaptasati** is the most important literary source of Satavahana society — option **(3)** (**APPSC 2019**).
**Puranas**, **Aitareya Brahmana** and **Dharmasutras** are the standard wrong options.
It is **Hala's** work of about **700 verses** in **Maharashtri Prakrit**.
xa: It covers family, marriage, women, agriculture, trade, festivals and occupations.
Same **APPSC 2019**: **'Maiputa'** dancers = **Kusuma Lepanam**.
Its female poets: **Madhavi**, **Revati**, **Anupamalabdha**, **Anulakshmi**.

57.s: Which one of the following best expresses the significance of early Andhra society?
o: It rejected the varna order while adopting Buddhism as the exclusive state religion
It followed a rigid caste order and excluded women from religious patronage
It replaced both Vedic traditions and Buddhism with folk worship
It combined the Vedic varna order with strong Buddhist patronage, much of it provided by women
57.x: Early Andhra combined the Vedic varna order with strong Buddhist patronage, and women played a major role in that patronage.
57.tq: Choose the balanced synthesis that preserves both elements of the historical pattern.
xs: Early Andhra **combined the Vedic varna order with strong Buddhist patronage, much of it by women** — option **(4)**.
Women patrons: **Gautami Balasri** (Satavahana), **Bodhisiri** and **Chantisiri** (Ikshvaku).
xa: Women held **considerable respect and freedom** in a **patriarchal joint family**.
Kshatriya-status claims continued in the colonial period: **Vanniyakula Kshatriya Mahasabha (1888)**.
**Akhil Bharatiya Kshatriya Mahasabha** was formed in **1897**.

58.s:
Which of the following statements about the traditional account of the three Sangams is correct?
1. The first Sangam was held at Then Madurai.
2. The second Sangam was held at Kapatapuram.
3. The third Sangam was held at Madurai.
4. All three Sangams were under Pandya patronage.
58.x: The traditional account places the first Sangam at Then Madurai, the second at Kapatapuram and the third at Madurai; all are described as being under Pandya patronage.
58.tq: Combine place-based statements with the common patronage fact.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
First Sangam at **Then Madurai** (submerged); Second at **Kapatapuram** (submerged); Third at **Madurai**.
All three Sangams were under **Pandya** patronage.
xa: ⚠ First and Third both at **Madurai**; Second at **Kapatapuram**.
The tradition comes from the preface of **Iraiyanar Agapporul**.
Presiding scholars: **Agastya** (First), **Agastya / Tolkappiyar** (Second), **Nakkirar** (Third).

58.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Second Sangam — Most of the Sangam corpus survives
58.x: According to the traditional account, nothing survives from the First Sangam. Only Tolkappiyam is said to survive from the Second, while most of the extant Sangam corpus is associated with the Third.
58.tq: Use the survival record to distinguish the three Sangams.
xs: **First Sangam — nothing survives** — option **(1)**.
From the **Second** only **Tolkappiyam** survives; the **Third** gave most of the Sangam corpus.
xa: First Sangam: **Then Madurai**, presided by **Agastya**.
The three-Sangam account with two submerged cities is **traditional, not historical**.
Accepted span: **300 BCE-300 CE**.

58.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Sangam)
a. First Sangam
b. Second Sangam
c. Third Sangam

List-II (Presiding scholar)
i. Nakkirar
ii. Agastya
iii. Agastya and Tolkappiyar
58.x: Agastya presided over the First Sangam; the Second is associated with Agastya and Tolkappiyar; and Nakkirar presided over the Third Sangam.
58.tq: Anchor the matching through the distinctive Third Sangam scholar.
xs: Correct matching is **a–ii, b–iii, c–i** — option **(1)**.
First — **Agastya**; Second — **Agastya / Tolkappiyar**; Third — **Nakkirar**.
xa: **Tolkappiyar** wrote the **Tolkappiyam**, the only survivor of the Second Sangam.
Places: **Then Madurai**, **Kapatapuram**, **Madurai**.
All three were held under **Pandya** patronage.

58.s: The generally accepted chronological span of the Sangam corpus is
58.x: The Sangam corpus is generally placed between approximately the 3rd century BCE and the 3rd century CE, or 300 BCE–300 CE.
58.tq: Select the period that accommodates both the early Tamil-Brahmi evidence and later Sangam works.
xs: The accepted span is **300 BCE–300 CE** (c. **3rd c. BCE-3rd c. CE**) — option **(3)**.
**Tamil-Brahmi** dating to the **3rd c. BCE** supports the early limit.
xa: The three-Sangam chronology is **legendary**, not historical.
**Tirukkural** and the twin epics are **post-Sangam**.
Theban tomb inscriptions (Feb **2026**) date to the **1st-3rd c. CE**.

58.s: Which of the following statements correctly reflects the historical status of the traditional three-Sangam chronology?
o: It is fully confirmed by contemporary inscriptions and archaeological records.
It places the twin epics before the Sangam corpus without dispute.
It was created by Roman writers to describe Tamil ports.
It is a traditional account, and the two submerged cities are not established as historical facts.
58.x: The legendary account of three Sangams and two submerged cities is traditional rather than historically established. The twin epics are generally considered later, post-Sangam works.
58.tq: Distinguish traditional literary memory from firmly corroborated history.
xs: The three-Sangam account with **two submerged cities** is **traditional, not historical** — option **(4)**.
It is not confirmed by inscriptions; the twin epics are **post-Sangam**, not earlier.
xa: The account comes from the preface of **Iraiyanar Agapporul**.
Historians accept **300 BCE-300 CE**, supported by **Tamil-Brahmi** dating.
Submerged sites: **Then Madurai** and **Kapatapuram**.

58.s: The traditional account of the three Tamil Sangams comes from the preface of which work?
58.x: The three-Sangam tradition is given in the preface of Iraiyanar Agapporul. Tolkappiyam is the grammar said to survive from the second Sangam; Pattinappalai describes Puhar; Silappadikaram is the post-Sangam epic of Kannagi.
58.tq: Three-Sangam legend: preface of Iraiyanar Agapporul.
xs: The three-Sangam tradition comes from the preface of **Iraiyanar Agapporul** — option **(2)**.
**Tolkappiyam** is the grammar surviving from the Second Sangam; **Pattinappalai** describes **Puhar**; **Silappadikaram** is the post-Sangam epic of **Kannagi**.
xa: "Sangam" = assemblies/academies of poets under **Pandya** patronage.
Presiding scholar of the Third Sangam: **Nakkirar**.
⚠ First and Third Sangams at **Madurai**; Second at **Kapatapuram**.

58.s:
Consider the following statements about Sangam literature:
1. The Sangams were assemblies of poets held under Chola patronage.
2. The corpus has about 2,400 poems by several hundred poets, including women poets.
3. It is one of the earliest bodies of secular literature in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
58.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the Sangams were assemblies of poets under Pandya patronage. Statements 2 and 3 are correct. So A, C and D, which include statement 1, are wrong; B is right.
58.tq: Sangam patrons = Pandyas, not Cholas or Cheras.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
1 wrong: the Sangams were under **Pandya**, not Chola, patronage.
2 correct: about **2,400 poems** by several hundred poets, **including women poets**. 3 correct: among India's earliest **secular** literature.
xa: Language: **old Tamil**.
Themes divide into **aham** (interior) and **puram** (exterior).
Sangam poets **knew the varna classification** (**UPSC 2022** key).

58.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Aham — Love, personal emotion and nature
58.x: Aham, meaning interior, deals with love, personal emotion and nature. Puram, meaning exterior, concerns war, valour, royal deeds and ethics.
58.tq: Discriminate between the closely related aham and puram categories.
xs: **Aham — love, personal emotion and nature** — option **(3)**.
**Aham** means interior; **Puram** (exterior) covers **war, valour, deeds of kings, ethics**.
xa: Both **Ettuthogai** and **Pattupattu** are divided into aham and puram.
Ettuthogai + Pattupattu = **18 major works (Melkanakku)**.
**Pathinenkilkanakku** = **18 minor works** on ethics.

58.s:
Consider the following statements about the subject matter of Sangam literature:
1. It contains information on polity, trade and cities.
2. It reflects wars, economy and the warrior ethic.
3. It is devoid of references to material culture.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
58.x: Sangam literature is rich in material culture and refers to polity, trade, cities, wars, economy and the warrior ethic. Therefore, statement 3 is false.
58.tq: Find the negative statement that reverses the central content of the literature.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
1 correct: covers **polity, trade, cities**. 2 correct: **wars, economy** and the **warrior ethic**.
3 wrong: it is **rich in material culture**.
xa: Exam angle: "devoid of material culture / no warrior ethic" statements are **false**.
Sangam poets **knew the varna classification** (**UPSC 2022**).
**Pattupattu** = longer poems on kings, cities, trade.

58.s:
Consider the following statements about Sangam literature:
1. It is divided into aham and puram themes.
2. Sangam poets were aware of the varna classification.
3. It contains no references to the warrior ethic.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
58.x: Statement 1 is correct: Ettuthogai and Pattupattu are divided into aham and puram. Statement 2 is correct: Sangam poets knew the varna classification (UPSC 2022 key). Statement 3 is wrong: the literature is rich in the warrior ethic. So A misses statement 2, and C and D include statement 3; B is right.
58.tq: Sangam poems knew varna; full of material culture and warrior ethic.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
1 correct: **Ettuthogai** and **Pattupattu** are divided into **aham and puram**. 2 correct: poets **knew the varna classification** (**UPSC 2022** key).
3 wrong: the literature is rich in the **warrior ethic**.
xa: Corpus: about **2,400 poems**, including women poets.
One of the earliest bodies of **secular** literature in India.
Puram covers **war, valour, deeds of kings, ethics**.

58.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with Ettuthogai?
o: Tirumurugarruppadai — One of the minor ethical works
Mullaippattu — One of the eight anthologies
Pattinappalai — One of the eight anthologies
58.x: Padirruppattu is one of the Ettuthogai anthologies and is associated with Chera kings. Pattinappalai, Mullaippattu and Tirumurugarruppadai belong to Pattupattu.
58.tq: Separate the eight anthologies from the ten idylls and minor works.
xs: **Padirruppattu — Chera kings** is correct for Ettuthogai — option **(3)**.
**Tirumurugarruppadai**, **Mullaippattu** and **Pattinappalai** belong to **Pattupattu**, not Ettuthogai.
xa: Other Ettuthogai: **Ainkurunuru**, **Narrinai**, **Akananuru**, **Purananuru**, **Kuruntogai**, **Kalittogai**, **Paripadal**.
Ettuthogai = **8 anthologies** of **short poems**.
Pattupattu = **10 idylls**, longer poems.

58.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
58.x: Pattinappalai describes the Puhar port and is associated with Karikala. The other descriptions do not correspond to the stated subjects of the Pattupattu works.
58.tq: Match a literary work with its distinctive place and ruler association.
xs: **Pattinappalai — Puhar port and Karikala** — option **(1)**.
It describes **Puhar (Kaveripattinam)** as cosmopolitan with **Yavana settlements**.
xa: Pattupattu (**10 idylls**) also includes **Maduraikkanji**, **Kurinjippattu**, **Malaipadukadam**, **Nedunalvadai**.
The **Arruppadai** works: Tirumurugarruppadai, Porunarruppadai, Sirupanarruppadai, Perumpanarruppadai.
Pattupattu are longer poems on **kings, cities, trade**.

58.s: Ettuthogai and Pattupattu together are known as
o: Melkanakku or the eighteen major works
58.x: Ettuthogai and Pattupattu together constitute the eighteen major works known as Melkanakku.
58.tq: Distinguish the collective title from the names of individual collections.
xs: Ettuthogai + Pattupattu = **Melkanakku**, the **18 major works** — option **(4)**.
**Pathinenkilkanakku** is the **18 minor works** on ethics.
xa: ⚠ Melkanakku = 18 **major**; Pathinenkilkanakku = 18 **minor**.
Ettuthogai = **8 anthologies**; Pattupattu = **10 idylls**.
**Silappadikaram** and **Manimekalai** are the post-Sangam epics.

58.s:
Which of the following statements about Pathinenkilkanakku is correct?
1. It consists of eighteen minor works.
2. It deals mainly with ethics and morals.
3. Tirukkural is included in it.
4. It is largely post-Sangam in character.
58.x: Pathinenkilkanakku comprises eighteen minor works, mainly on ethics and morals, includes Tirukkural and is largely regarded as post-Sangam.
58.tq: Verify all components of a literary classification before selecting the coded option.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Pathinenkilkanakku** = **18 minor works** on **ethics and morals**, including the **Tirukkural**.
It is **largely post-Sangam**.
xa: ⚠ Melkanakku (Ettuthogai + Pattupattu) = **18 major** works.
Tirukkural: **1,330 couplets** by **Tiruvalluvar**.
Other names of the Kural: **Laghuveda**, **Tamil Veda**, **Ulaga Podhumarai**.

58.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Work)
a. Tolkappiyam
b. Tirukkural
c. Silappadikaram
d. Manimekalai

List-II (Author)
i. Ilango Adigal
ii. Tiruvalluvar
iii. Sittalai Sattanar
iv. Tolkappiyar
58.x: Tolkappiyam was written by Tolkappiyar, Tirukkural by Tiruvalluvar, Silappadikaram by Ilango Adigal and Manimekalai by Sittalai Sattanar.
58.tq: Start from the sure author–work pairs and eliminate the codes.
xs: Correct matching is **a–iv, b–ii, c–i, d–iii** — option **(1)**.
**Tolkappiyam** — **Tolkappiyar**; **Tirukkural** — **Tiruvalluvar**.
**Silappadikaram** — **Ilango Adigal**; **Manimekalai** — **Sittalai Sattanar**.
xa: **Sivaga Sindamani (Jivaka Chintamani)**, a Jain epic, is by **Tiruttakkadevar**.
UPPSC 2014 key: Tirukkural = **philosophy**, Tolkappiyam = **grammar**, Silappadikaram = **love story**, Manimekalai = **merchant story**.
Ilango Adigal was the younger brother of **Chera Senguttuvan**.

58.s: Which of the following is the earliest extant Tamil work dealing with grammar and poetics, while also providing information on society and polity?
58.x: Tolkappiyam, attributed to Tolkappiyar, is the earliest extant Tamil work on grammar and poetics and also contains material on society and polity.
58.tq: Identify the work from its combined subject profile.
xs: **Tolkappiyam** is the earliest extant Tamil work, on **grammar and poetics**, also covering society and polity — option **(1)**.
Author: **Tolkappiyar**; it is the only survivor of the **Second Sangam**.
**Sivaga Sindamani** is a Jain epic; **Tirukkural** is ethics; **Manimekalai** is a Buddhist epic.
xa: First Tamil epic = **Silappadikaram**.
Tolkappiyar is linked with **Agastya** as presiding scholar of the Second Sangam.
Second Sangam site: **Kapatapuram** (submerged).

58.s:
Consider the following statements about the Tirukkural:
1. It has 1,330 couplets arranged in three books.
2. Its book Porul deals with love.
3. It is also called Laghuveda, Tamil Veda and Ulaga Podhumarai.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
58.x: Statement 1 is correct: 1,330 couplets in three books. Statement 2 is wrong: Porul deals with wealth; Aram is virtue and Inbam is love. Statement 3 is correct: Laghuveda (UPPSC 2013 key), Tamil Veda and Ulaga Podhumarai are its other names. So A, B and D, which include statement 2, are wrong; C is right.
58.tq: Aram-Porul-Inbam = virtue-wealth-love, in that order.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(3)**.
1 correct: **1,330 couplets** in **3 books**. 2 wrong: **Porul** = wealth; **Aram** = virtue, **Inbam** = love.
3 correct: also called **Laghuveda** (**UPPSC 2013** key), **Tamil Veda**, **Ulaga Podhumarai**.
xa: Author: **Tiruvalluvar**.
The Kural is part of **Pathinenkilkanakku** and is **post-Sangam**.
UPPSC 2014 key: Tirukkural = **philosophy**.

58.s: Silappadikaram is best described as
o: The first Tamil epic centred on Kannagi and Kovalan
A collection of ten idylls on Chola ports
A Buddhist grammar composed by Tolkappiyar
A Jain epic concerning Jivaka Chintamani
58.x: Silappadikaram, written by Ilango Adigal, is regarded as the first Tamil epic and tells the story of Kannagi and Kovalan through the motif of the anklet.
58.tq: Match the work with its distinctive story and literary status.
xs: Silappadikaram is **the first Tamil epic**, about **Kannagi and Kovalan** — option **(1)**.
The story turns on **the anklet**; author **Ilango Adigal**.
**Jivaka Chintamani** is the Jain epic; **Tolkappiyar** wrote the grammar.
xa: Kovalan is executed by the **Pandya** king; **Kannagi burns Madurai**.
Characters: merchant **Kovalan**, wife **Kannagi**, dancer **Madhavi**.
Sequel: **Manimekalai** by **Sittalai Sattanar**.

58.s: Who was the younger brother of Chera king Senguttuvan and the author of Silappadikaram?
58.x: Ilango Adigal, identified as the younger brother of Chera Senguttuvan, composed Silappadikaram.
58.tq: Apply the author–relationship clue to distinguish similar literary figures.
xs: **Ilango Adigal**, younger brother of **Chera Senguttuvan**, wrote Silappadikaram — option **(1)**.
**Sittalai Sattanar** wrote **Manimekalai**; **Tiruttakkadevar** wrote **Sivaga Sindamani**; **Nakkirar** presided over the Third Sangam.
xa: Silappadikaram = **first Tamil epic**, post-Sangam.
Its heroine **Kannagi** burns **Madurai**.
UPPSC 2014 key: Silappadikaram = **love story**.

58.s: Which of the following correctly describes Manimekalai?
o: Kovalan becomes a Buddhist monk after becoming a merchant
The daughter of Kovalan and Madhavi becomes a Buddhist nun
Kannagi becomes a Jain nun after the burning of Madurai
Madhavi becomes the queen of Senguttuvan
58.x: Manimekalai relates how the daughter of Kovalan and Madhavi becomes a Buddhist nun and reflects Buddhist philosophy.
58.tq: Avoid confusing the principal characters of the two twin epics.
xs: In Manimekalai, **the daughter of Kovalan and Madhavi becomes a Buddhist nun** — option **(2)**.
It reflects **Buddhist philosophy** and is the **sequel to Silappadikaram**.
xa: Author: **Sittalai Sattanar**.
UPPSC 2014 key: Manimekalai = **merchant story**.
Kannagi, not Madhavi, is Kovalan's wife; she **burns Madurai**.

58.s: Silappadikaram and Manimekalai are generally regarded as
58.x: Both Silappadikaram and Manimekalai are considered post-Sangam works.
58.tq: Separate the chronology of the twin epics from that of the Sangam corpus.
xs: Silappadikaram and Manimekalai are **post-Sangam works** — option **(3)**.
The **Tirukkural** too is post-Sangam.
xa: Silappadikaram = **first Tamil epic** (Ilango Adigal).
Manimekalai = **Buddhist epic** (Sittalai Sattanar).
Oldest Tamil work = **Tolkappiyam**.

58.s: Which classical account is associated with information on Muziris, pepper and Arikamedu?
58.x: The anonymous Greek work Periplus of the Erythraean Sea provides information on ports, Muziris, pepper and Arikamedu.
58.tq: Match the source with its distinctive geographical and commercial references.
xs: **Periplus of the Erythraean Sea** records **Muziris** pepper and **Arikamedu** — option **(3)**.
It is by an **anonymous Greek** and describes the **ports**.
**Iraiyanar Agapporul** gives the three-Sangam tradition; **Pliny** records spices, pearls, muslin.
xa: Periplus calls Arikamedu the **"market street of the Romans"**.
**Ptolemy's Geography** is another classical account.
Other classical writers: **Megasthenes**, **Strabo**.

58.s:
Which of the following statements about Pliny’s Natural History is correct?
1. It refers to spices from the Chera region.
2. It associates pearls with the Pandya region.
3. It mentions muslin from the Chola region.
4. It refers to the drain of Roman gold.
58.x: Pliny’s Natural History refers to Chera spices, Pandya pearls, Chola muslin and the outflow or drain of Roman gold.
58.tq: Check the complete source-specific list rather than one isolated association.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Pliny's **Natural History**: **spices from Chera**, **pearls from Pandya**, **muslin from Chola**.
It also records the **Roman gold drain**.
xa: **Periplus** records ports, **Muziris** pepper, Arikamedu.
**Ptolemy** wrote the **Geography**.
Later travellers: **Fa Xian**, **Xuanzang**, **Marco Polo**.

58.s: The Ashokan inscriptions mention which southern polities as neighbours south of the Mauryan Empire?
58.x: Ashokan inscriptions identify the Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas as southern neighbours of the Mauryan Empire; Satiyaputras and Keralaputras are also mentioned in Rock Edict II.
58.tq: Recall the political geography recorded in the imperial inscriptions.
xs: Ashokan inscriptions name the **Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas** as southern neighbours — option **(3)**.
**Rock Edict II** also names the **Satiyaputras** and **Keralaputras**.
xa: The **Pugalur inscription** (**1st c. CE**) records three generations of **Chera** rulers.
**Tamil-Brahmi** of the **3rd c. BCE** supports the early Sangam limit.
Indirect sources: **Buddhist-Jain texts** and later travellers.

58.s: Which archaeological site is described as an Indo-Roman trading settlement near Puducherry?
58.x: Arikamedu, near Puducherry, was an Indo-Roman trading settlement and is described in the Periplus as the ‘market street of the Romans’.
58.tq: Use the location and trade description to identify the site.
xs: **Arikamedu**, near Puducherry, was an **Indo-Roman trading settlement** — option **(4)**.
The Periplus calls it the **"market street of the Romans"**.
**Kaveripattinam** was a Chola port; **Keezhadi** is the key Sangam urban site.
xa: **Puhar** had **Yavana settlements** (Pattinappalai).
**Keezhadi** shows urbanisation contemporary with the **Gangetic Second Urbanisation**.
**Muziris** was known for **pepper**.

58.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Kaveripattinam — Chola port with Yavana settlements
Keezhadi — Chera capital described by Pliny
Mangulam — Roman market street near Puducherry
58.x: Kaveripattinam or Puhar was a Chola port described in Pattinappalai as cosmopolitan and containing Yavana settlements.
58.tq: Match each archaeological site with its political and commercial setting.
xs: **Kaveripattinam — Chola port with Yavana settlements** — option **(1)**.
**Pattinappalai** describes Puhar as **cosmopolitan**.
**Keezhadi** is an urban excavation; **Arikamedu** is the Roman "market street" near Puducherry.
xa: Pattinappalai is linked with **Karikala**.
**Pugalur inscription** (**1st c. CE**): three generations of Chera rulers.
Pliny: **muslin from Chola**.

58.s: Keezhadi is particularly important because it provides evidence of
o: The earliest Roman settlement in northern India
The first Gupta capital in the Tamil region
South Indian urbanisation contemporary with the Gangetic Second Urbanisation
The exclusive use of Sanskrit in the Pandya country
58.x: Keezhadi is considered the most important Sangam urban excavation and indicates South Indian urbanisation contemporary with the Gangetic Second Urbanisation.
58.tq: Infer the historical significance from the excavation’s comparative context.
xs: Keezhadi shows **South Indian urbanisation contemporary with the Gangetic Second Urbanisation** — option **(3)**.
It is the **most important Sangam urban excavation** (NextGen CA **2026**).
xa: **Arikamedu** = Indo-Roman trading settlement near Puducherry.
**Kaveripattinam (Puhar)** = Chola port with Yavana settlements.
Jul **2025**: a Tamil Nadu dig gave **Tamil-Brahmi potsherds**, **carnelian beads**, **weaving tools**.

58.s: The Pugalur inscription of the 1st century CE is important because it records
o: the founding of Arikamedu by Roman traders
58.x: The Pugalur inscription (1st c. CE) records three generations of Chera rulers. The Pandya embassy to Augustus is known from classical accounts; Arikamedu was an Indo-Roman trading settlement, not founded by an inscription's record; the Battle of Venni is known from Sangam poems on Karikala.
58.tq: Pugalur = Chera genealogy (3 generations).
xs: The **Pugalur inscription** (**1st c. CE**) records **three generations of Chera rulers** — option **(1)**.
**Arikamedu** was an Indo-Roman trading settlement known from the **Periplus**.
xa: **Padirruppattu** (Ettuthogai) is about **Chera kings**.
**Ilango Adigal** was brother of **Chera Senguttuvan**.
Pliny: **spices from Chera**.

58.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Researchers documented approximately 30 Indian inscriptions, mostly in Tamil-Brahmi, in the Theban tombs of Egypt.
2. These inscriptions belong mainly to the period from the 1st to the 3rd century CE.
3. The evidence indicates the mobility associated with Indo-Roman trade.
4. A Tamil Nadu excavation recapped in July 2025 yielded Tamil-Brahmi potsherds, carnelian beads and weaving tools.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
58.x: All four statements are correct. In February 2026 about 30 Indian inscriptions, mostly Tamil-Brahmi, of the 1st–3rd c. CE were documented in the Theban tombs of Egypt, showing the mobility of Indo-Roman trade; a July 2025 Tamil Nadu excavation yielded Tamil-Brahmi potsherds, carnelian beads and weaving tools.
58.tq: Test the full cluster of current facts by checking the number, script, date, location, evidence and reported excavation finds.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Feb **2026**: **~30 Indian inscriptions, mostly Tamil-Brahmi**, of the **1st-3rd c. CE**, documented in the **Theban tombs** of Egypt.
They show **Indo-Roman trade mobility**; Jul **2025** Tamil Nadu dig: Tamil-Brahmi potsherds, **carnelian beads**, weaving tools.
xa: Pliny records the **Roman gold drain**.
**Arikamedu** = "market street of the Romans" (Periplus).
**Keezhadi** = most important Sangam urban excavation.

58.s: The importance of the Sangam Age sources in reconstructing early South Indian history lies chiefly in the fact that they provide
o: the first detailed description of the Vedic sacrificial tradition
the earliest record of the administrative structure of the Mauryan Empire
the earliest detailed picture of South Indian society, economy and polity
the earliest complete account of the Gupta administrative system
58.x: Sangam Age sources are significant because they offer the earliest detailed picture of South Indian society, economy and polity. The other alternatives relate to historical contexts outside the stated significance of Sangam sources.
58.tq: Identify the precise significance rather than choosing a broader but historically unrelated description.
xs: Sangam sources give **the earliest detailed picture of South Indian society, economy and polity** — option **(3)**.
The literature covers **polity, trade, cities, wars, economy**.
xa: Corpus: about **2,400 poems**, among India's earliest **secular** literature.
Oldest Tamil work = **Tolkappiyam**; first Tamil epic = **Silappadikaram**.
Span: **300 BCE-300 CE**.

58.s: Which one of the following correctly expresses the linguistic distinction between Sangam literature and the contemporary Satavahana tradition?
o: Sangam literature was composed in Prakrit, whereas the Satavahanas used Tamil for literature.
Tamil and Prakrit were used interchangeably by both traditions for literary purposes.
Tamil was used for Sangam literature, whereas the contemporary Satavahanas used Prakrit.
Both Sangam literature and Satavahana records were composed exclusively in Sanskrit.
58.x: Tamil was the language of Sangam literature, while the contemporary Satavahanas used Prakrit. The other options either reverse this distinction or introduce an unsupported linguistic claim.
58.tq: Use the comparison-table method by checking which option preserves the correct direction of the linguistic contrast.
xs: **Tamil** was used for Sangam literature, while the contemporary **Satavahanas** used **Prakrit** — option **(3)**.
Options (1) and (2) reverse or blur this; Sanskrit was not the medium of either.
xa: Sangam corpus: about **2,400 poems** in old Tamil.
**Tamil-Brahmi** dating to the **3rd c. BCE** supports the early limit.
Oldest Tamil work: **Tolkappiyam** (grammar and poetics).

59.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
59.x: Korkai was the Pandya port, whereas the Chola port was Kaveripattinam or Puhar. The Chola capital was Uraiyur and its emblem was the tiger.
59.tq: Find the single wrong combination by checking the port against the kingdom.
xs: **Chola — Uraiyur — Korkai — Tiger** is wrong — option **(3)**.
**Korkai** was the **Pandya** port; the Chola port was **Kaveripattinam (Puhar)**.
The other rows are right: Pandya **Madurai–Korkai–Fish**; Chera **Vanji–Muziris–Bow**; Chola **Puhar–Kaveripattinam–Tiger**.
xa: Chera **Vanji** is identified with **Karur (Karuvur)**; Chera ports also include **Tondi**.
Chola capital shifted **Uraiyur → Puhar**.
Heartland rivers: Chola **Kaveri**, Pandya **Vaigai**.

59.s: The Chola territory during the Sangam period was primarily centred on the:
o: Southern Tamil Nadu around Madurai and Korkai
Central and northern Kerala and Kongu region
Kaveri delta, extending from Tiruchi up to southern Andhra
59.x: The Chola heartland was the Kaveri delta, extending from Tiruchi up to southern Andhra. Central and northern Kerala and Kongu were associated with the Cheras.
59.tq: Use territorial boundaries to distinguish the three Sangam kingdoms.
xs: Chola territory centred on the **Kaveri delta (Tiruchi) up to southern Andhra** — option **(4)**.
**Central/north Kerala + Kongu** was **Chera**; **southern Tamil Nadu** (Madurai, Korkai) was **Pandya**.
xa: Chola capital: **Uraiyur**, later **Puhar**; emblem **tiger**.
Chola port: **Kaveripattinam (Puhar)**.
**Telugu Choda** families (Renati, Pottapi, Nellore) claimed descent from **Karikala Chola**.

59.s: The three crowned kings of early Tamilakam were collectively known as:
59.x: Chera, Chola and Pandya rulers were collectively called the Muvendar, meaning the three crowned kings.
59.tq: Identify the collective political term from a group of related institutions and titles.
xs: The three crowned kings were the **Muvendar** — option **(1)**.
**Aimperunkulu** = five-member advisory body; **Velir** = minor hill/forest chiefs; **Kadai ezhu vallals** = seven great patrons.
xa: Muvendar = **Chera** (bow), **Chola** (tiger), **Pandya** (fish).
Muvendar rivalry + **Roman trade** shaped early Tamil polity.
**Pallavas** were not a Sangam dynasty.

59.s: Which one of the following was NOT a Sangam dynasty?
59.x: The Pallavas were not a Sangam dynasty; they rose from the fourth century CE. The Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas were the three major Sangam dynasties.
59.tq: Remove the outsider from the established triad of Sangam dynasties.
xs: The **Pallava** dynasty was not a Sangam dynasty — option **(3)**.
They rose from the **4th c. CE** (**UPPSC 2010**).
**Chera**, **Chola** and **Pandya** were the three Muvendar.
xa: Capitals: **Vanji** (Chera), **Uraiyur/Puhar** (Chola), **Madurai** (Pandya).
Ports: **Muziris** (Chera), **Kaveripattinam** (Chola), **Korkai** (Pandya).
Pandya power waned under the **Kalabhra** invasion.

59.s: The Cheras are associated with which of the following developments?
o: Establishing Korkai as the Chola capital
Building a temple of Augustus near Muziris
Founding the Pattini cult at Madurai
59.x: The Cheras traded with Rome and are said to have built a temple of Augustus near Muziris.
59.tq: Match the foreign-trade connection with the correct kingdom and port.
xs: The Cheras are said to have built **a temple of Augustus near Muziris** — option **(3)**.
They **traded with Rome** through **Muziris (Musiri)**.
**Korkai** was a Pandya port; **Kallanai** was on the **Kaveri** (Karikala); the **Pattini cult** was founded by Chera **Senguttuvan**, not at Madurai.
xa: Chera capital **Vanji (Karur)**; emblem **bow**.
Chera territory: **central/north Kerala + Kongu**.
**Senguttuvan** ("Red Chera", **2nd c. CE**) founded the Pattini cult.

59.s: The heartland river of the Sangam-age Pandya kingdom was the
59.x: The Pandya heartland, around Madurai, lay on the Vaigai. The Kaveri was the Chola river and the Periyar the Chera river. Vengi is a region in Andhra, not a river; it was the misleading option keyed in UPPSC 2010.
59.tq: Rivers: Chera-Periyar, Chola-Kaveri, Pandya-Vaigai.
xs: The Pandya heartland river was the **Vaigai** — option **(3)**.
⚠ Trap: **UPPSC 2010** keyed the Pandya "lifeline" as option "**Vengi**".
**Kaveri** was the Chola river; **Periyar** the Chera river.
xa: Pandya capital **Madurai**, port **Korkai**, emblem **fish**.
Pandya territory: **southern Tamil Nadu**.
Last renowned Pandya: **Ugra Peruvaludhi**.

59.s: In the polity of the Sangam age, the terms Ko, Kon, Mannan and Vendan denoted the:
59.x: Ko, Kon, Mannan and Vendan were terms used for the king.
59.tq: Discriminate among closely related administrative and political terms.
xs: **Ko, Kon, Mannan, Vendan** all meant **King** — option **(2)** (**RPSC 2010**).
**Avai** = royal court; **Aimperunkulu** = five-member advisory body; **Velir** = minor hill chiefs.
xa: Polity: **hereditary monarchy** + subordinate chieftains.
**Enadi** = title of army commanders.
Velir chiefs: **Pari**, **Athiyaman**, **Ay**.

59.s: Aimperunkulu was a:
o: Military unit under the Velir chiefs
Royal court consisting only of poets
59.x: Aimperunkulu was a five-member advisory body consisting of ministers, priests, commanders, envoys and spies.
59.tq: Identify an institution from its numerical composition and functions.
xs: **Aimperunkulu** was a **five-member advisory body** — option **(4)**.
Members: **ministers, priests, commanders, envoys, spies**.
The court with poets was the **Avai**; the seven great patrons were the **Kadai ezhu vallals**.
xa: King = **Ko, Kon, Mannan, Vendan**.
Army commanders' title: **Enadi**.
**Velir** = minor hill/forest chieftains.

59.s: The Avai in Sangam polity referred to the:
o: Army of the three crowned kings
59.x: Avai was the royal court, in which poets were also present.
59.tq: Match the institutional term with its precise function.
xs: **Avai** was the **royal court, including poets** — option **(2)**.
The advisory council was the **Aimperunkulu**; forest chiefs were the **Velir**.
xa: Aimperunkulu: ministers, priests, commanders, envoys, spies.
**Enadi** = army commanders.
Seven great patrons: **Pari, Kari, Ori, Pegan, Ay, Athiyaman, Nalli**.

59.s: The title borne by army commanders in the Sangam polity was:
59.x: Army commanders bore the title Enadi. Velir referred to minor hill or forest chieftains, while Vendan denoted a king.
59.tq: Separate military titles from royal and chieftain titles.
xs: Army commanders bore the title **Enadi** — option **(4)**.
**Vendan** = king; **Velir** = minor hill/forest chiefs; **Muvendar** = the three crowned kings.
xa: **Aimperunkulu** included **commanders** among its five members.
**Avai** = royal court with poets.
Velir chiefs **Pari**, **Athiyaman**, **Ay** were allies or rivals of the Muvendar.

59.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
59.x: Nalli was one of the seven great patrons, not a minister of Aimperunkulu. Pari, Athiyaman and Ay were Velir chiefs.
59.tq: Detect the category error by separating chieftains from ministers.
xs: **Nalli — Minister of Aimperunkulu** is wrong — option **(4)**.
**Nalli** was one of the **seven great patrons (Kadai ezhu vallals)**.
**Pari**, **Athiyaman** and **Ay** were **Velir** chiefs.
xa: Seven patrons: **Pari, Kari, Ori, Pegan, Ay, Athiyaman, Nalli**.
Aimperunkulu: ministers, priests, commanders, envoys, spies.
Velir chiefs were **allies or rivals** of the Muvendar.

59.s: Who among the following was NOT included among the seven great patrons, or Kadai ezhu vallals?
59.x: The seven great patrons were Pari, Kari, Ori, Pegan, Ay, Athiyaman and Nalli. Nedunjeliyan was a Pandya ruler and was not one of them.
59.tq: Find the outsider by distinguishing a king from the listed patron chieftains.
xs: **Nedunjeliyan** was not one of the seven great patrons — option **(3)**.
He was a **Pandya** king, victor of **Talaiyalanganam**.
The **Kadai ezhu vallals**: **Pari, Kari, Ori, Pegan, Ay, Athiyaman, Nalli**.
xa: **Pari**, **Athiyaman** and **Ay** were also **Velir** chiefs.
Velir = minor hill/forest chieftains.
Other Pandyas: **Nediyon**, **Mudukudumi Peruvaludhi**, **Mudathirumaran**.

59.s: Which one of the following rulers is correctly matched with his dynasty and achievement?
o: Senguttuvan — Pandya — Won the Battle of Talaiyalanganam
Karikala — Chola — Built Kallanai on the Kaveri
Udiyanjeral — Chola — Established the Chola capital at Puhar
Nedunjeliyan — Chera — Founded the Pattini cult
59.x: Karikala was a Chola ruler associated with the construction of Kallanai across the Kaveri. Senguttuvan was a Chera ruler, Nedunjeliyan was a Pandya ruler, and Udiyanjeral was an early Chera ruler.
59.tq: Match the ruler with the correct dynasty and achievement while rejecting swapped-deed traps.
xs: **Karikala — Chola — built Kallanai on the Kaveri** — option **(2)**.
**Senguttuvan** was **Chera**; **Talaiyalanganam** was won by Pandya **Nedunjeliyan**.
**Udiyanjeral** was **Chera**, not Chola; the **Pattini cult** was Senguttuvan's.
xa: Kallanai = **Grand Anicut**, with irrigation canals.
Karikala won **Venni** and **Vahaipparandalai**.
Karikala is the subject of **Pattinappalai**.

59.s: The Battle of Venni was won by:
59.x: Karikala Chola won the Battle of Venni, defeating the Cheras, Pandyas and eleven chieftains.
59.tq: Directly identify the ruler associated with a particular battle.
xs: **Karikala Chola** won the **Battle of Venni** — option **(3)**.
He defeated the **Cheras, Pandyas and 11 chieftains**.
**Nedunjeliyan** won **Talaiyalanganam**; **Senguttuvan** led the Himalayan expedition; **Ugra Peruvaludhi** was the last renowned Pandya.
xa: At **Vahaipparandalai**, **9 chieftains** submitted to Karikala.
Karikala reclaimed **forest land**.
**Kallanai** across the **Kaveri** is attributed to him.

59.s:
Consider the following statements about Karikala Chola:
1. He won the battles of Venni and Vahaipparandalai.
2. He reclaimed forest land.
3. He is associated with the subject matter of Pattinappalai.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: All three statements are correct. Karikala won both battles, reclaimed forest land and is associated with Pattinappalai.
59.tq: Check each achievement separately before selecting the combined statement code.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
1: Karikala won **Venni** and **Vahaipparandalai**. 2: he **reclaimed forest land**.
3: he is the subject of **Pattinappalai**.
xa: Venni: Cheras, Pandyas and **11** chieftains defeated.
**Kallanai (Grand Anicut)** across the **Kaveri**.
Telugu Choda families claimed descent from **Karikala**.

59.s: At the Battle of Vahaipparandalai, which of the following occurred?
o: The Cheras established control over the Tamil country
Kovalan was executed by the victorious ruler
59.x: At Vahaipparandalai, nine chieftains submitted to Karikala.
59.tq: Use the distinctive numerical result to identify the correct battle.
xs: At **Vahaipparandalai**, **nine chieftains submitted to Karikala** — option **(2)**.
**Eleven** chieftains were defeated at **Venni**, not Vahaipparandalai.
Control over the Tamil country came from Pandya **Nedunjeliyan's** win at **Talaiyalanganam**.
xa: At **Venni** Karikala also beat the **Cheras** and **Pandyas**.
Kovalan was executed by **Arya Padai Kadantha Nedunjeliyan**.
Karikala reclaimed **forest land**.

59.s: Kallanai, also known as the Grand Anicut, was constructed across the:
59.x: Kallanai was constructed across the Kaveri and is attributed to Karikala Chola. It was associated with irrigation canals.
59.tq: Reject swapped builder–river combinations by identifying both elements together.
xs: **Kallanai (Grand Anicut)** was built across the **Kaveri by Karikala Chola** — option **(1)**.
It came with **irrigation canals**.
xa: **15 Aug 2026**: remains of a **Sangam-period water-management structure** found in the **Kollidam**.
Kollidam = Kaveri distributary branching at the **Upper Anicut (Mukkombu)**.
Karikala won **Venni** and **Vahaipparandalai**.

59.s: The ancient Sangam-period water-management structure whose remains were reported in August 2026 was found in the:
59.x: The remains were found in the Kollidam, a distributary of the Kaveri that branches off at the Upper Anicut or Mukkombu.
59.tq: Identify the precise river while distinguishing a distributary from the main river.
xs: The remains were found in the **Kollidam River** — option **(1)** (**15 Aug 2026**).
The **Kollidam** is a **Kaveri distributary** branching off at the **Upper Anicut (Mukkombu)**.
**Vengi** is not a river.
xa: **Kallanai (Grand Anicut)** on the **Kaveri** is attributed to **Karikala Chola**.
Pandya river: **Vaigai**; Chola river: **Kaveri**.
Karikala also **reclaimed forest land**.

59.s: Senguttuvan is known in early Tamil history as the:
o: Chola king who shifted the capital to Puhar
Pandya king who defeated the Cheras at Venni
Chera king who founded the Chola dynasty
Red Chera who founded the Pattini cult
59.x: Senguttuvan, known as the Red Chera, founded the Pattini cult centred on Kannagi.
59.tq: Use the title and distinctive achievement to distinguish closely associated rulers.
xs: Senguttuvan was the **Red Chera** who **founded the Pattini cult** — option **(4)**.
He ruled in the **2nd c. CE**; his brother **Ilango Adigal** wrote **Silappadikaram**.
xa: Pattini cult = worship of **Kannagi** as the **ideal wife**.
The idol stone was brought from the **Himalayas**.
Sri Lankan king **Gajabahu** is said to have attended the consecration.

59.s: The Pattini cult founded by Senguttuvan centred on the worship of Kannagi as the:
59.x: The Pattini cult centred on Kannagi, regarded as the ideal wife. Senguttuvan brought stone from the Himalayas for her idol.
59.tq: Identify the central idea of a cult rather than its political or geographical setting.
xs: The Pattini cult worshipped **Kannagi** as the **ideal wife** — option **(1)**.
It was founded by **Chera Senguttuvan**.
xa: The idol stone came from the **Himalayas** (Himalayan expedition).
Sri Lankan king **Gajabahu** is said to have attended the consecration.
Kannagi's husband Kovalan was executed by **Arya Padai Kadantha Nedunjeliyan**.

59.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the consecration of the Pattini idol is correct?
o: It was conducted by the seven great patrons at Korkai.
The Roman emperor Augustus attended it at Muziris.
Karikala attended it after the Battle of Venni.
The Sri Lankan king Gajabahu is said to have attended it.
59.x: The Sri Lankan king Gajabahu is said to have attended the consecration of the Pattini idol.
59.tq: Use the named foreign participant to distinguish the consecration tradition.
xs: The Sri Lankan king **Gajabahu** is said to have attended the consecration — option **(4)**.
The idol was of **Kannagi**, made from **Himalayan** stone, by **Senguttuvan**.
**Augustus** is linked with a Chera temple near **Muziris**; **Karikala** with **Venni**.
xa: The Pattini cult honours Kannagi as the **ideal wife**.
Senguttuvan = "**Red Chera**", **2nd c. CE**.
His brother **Ilango Adigal** wrote **Silappadikaram**.

59.s: Udiyanjeral (Perum Sorru Udhiyan Cheralathan) of the Sangam age was an early ruler of which dynasty?
59.x: Udiyanjeral was an early Chera ruler; the pair 'Udiyanjeral - Chola' was the wrong pair in UPSC 2026. The Cholas and Pandyas were the other Muvendar, and the Pallavas were not a Sangam dynasty.
59.tq: Udiyanjeral = Chera, not Chola.
xs: **Udiyanjeral** (Perum Sorru Udhiyan Cheralathan) was an early **Chera** ruler — option **(2)**.
⚠ **UPSC 2026**: "Udiyanjeral-Chola" was the **wrong pair**.
**Pallavas** were not a Sangam dynasty.
xa: Other Chera: **Imayavaramban Nedunjeral Adan** — boundary up to the **Himalayas**.
**Senguttuvan** ("Red Chera") founded the **Pattini cult**.
Chera capital **Vanji (Karur)**; port **Muziris**.

59.s: Who among the following rulers is associated with both the title ‘Arya Padai Kadantha’ and the execution of Kovalan?
59.x: Arya Padai Kadantha Nedunjeliyan was the Pandya ruler who executed Kovalan. Imayavaramban Nedunjeral Adan bore a different title connected with the Himalayas.
59.tq: Separate rulers by their distinctive titles and associated deeds.
xs: **Arya Padai Kadantha Nedunjeliyan**, a **Pandya**, executed **Kovalan** — option **(3)**.
**Senguttuvan** was Chera; **Karikala** was Chola; **Imayavaramban Nedunjeral Adan** was a Chera whose title refers to the **Himalayas**.
xa: Another **Nedunjeliyan** won **Talaiyalanganam** (Tanjore) — title Talaiyalanganattu Cheruvenra Nedunjeliyan.
Other Pandyas: **Nediyon**, **Mudathirumaran**; last renowned: **Ugra Peruvaludhi**.
After Kovalan's execution, **Kannagi** burnt Madurai and became the Pattini deity.

59.s: The power of the Pandyas declined under the:
59.x: Pandya power waned under the Kalabhra invasion.
59.tq: Identify the cause of political decline from a set of nearby historical events.
xs: Pandya power declined under the **Kalabhra invasion** — option **(4)**.
The **Himalayan expedition** was Senguttuvan's; **Vahaipparandalai** was a Karikala victory.
xa: Last renowned Pandya: **Ugra Peruvaludhi**.
Pandya capital **Madurai**, port **Korkai**, emblem **fish**.
**Nedunjeliyan's** win at **Talaiyalanganam** gave control over the Tamil country.

59.s: The Battle of Talaiyalanganam resulted in:
o: Chera control over the Kaveri delta
The establishment of Roman authority at Muziris
Pandya control over the Tamil country under Nedunjeliyan
Chola defeat by nine Velir chiefs
59.x: Nedunjeliyan of the Pandyas won at Talaiyalanganam and gained control over the Tamil country.
59.tq: Match the battle with its victor and political result.
xs: Talaiyalanganam gave **Pandya control over the Tamil country under Nedunjeliyan** — option **(3)**.
The battle was fought at **Tanjore**.
xa: His title: **Talaiyalanganattu Cheruvenra Nedunjeliyan**.
⚠ **Venni** (Karikala): Cheras, Pandyas and **11** chieftains defeated; **Vahaipparandalai**: **9** chieftains submitted.
Last renowned Pandya: **Ugra Peruvaludhi**.

59.s: Who is regarded as the last renowned Pandya ruler of the Sangam age?
59.x: Ugra Peruvaludhi was the last renowned Sangam Pandya. Mudathirumaran and Nediyon were other Pandya rulers, and Karikala was a Chola king.
59.tq: Last great Sangam Pandya = Ugra Peruvaludhi.
xs: **Ugra Peruvaludhi** was the **last renowned Pandya** — option **(2)**.
**Mudathirumaran** and **Nediyon** were other Pandyas; **Karikala** was Chola.
xa: Other Pandyas: **Palyagasalai Mudukudumi Peruvaludhi**, **Nedunjeliyan**.
Pandya power waned under the **Kalabhra** invasion.
Pandya river: **Vaigai**.

59.s: The Leiden copper plates are significant in relation to early Tamil history because their ring seal depicts the:
o: Chola tiger with the Pandya two fish and the Chera bow
Tiger and fish together as symbols of Roman authority
Chera bow alone, signifying Chera independence from Rome
Pandya fish with the Chola elephant and Pallava lion
59.x: The seal shows the Chola tiger with the Pandya two fish and the Chera bow, marking Chola victory over both the Pandyas and Cheras.
59.tq: Interpret a symbol-bearing historical artefact by linking each emblem to its dynasty.
xs: The ring seal shows the **Chola tiger with the Pandya two fish and the Chera bow** — option **(1)**.
It marks a **Chola victory over both** Pandyas and Cheras.
xa: **Leiden copper plates** (**18 May 2026**) record Chola grants to the **Chulamanivarma vihara, Nagapattinam**.
Muvendar emblems: Chera **bow**, Chola **tiger**, Pandya **fish**.
Muvendar rivalry + Roman trade shaped early Tamil polity.

59.s: Which one of the following best expresses the historical significance of the Muvendar rivalry?
o: It ended all foreign trade in the Kaveri delta.
It replaced hereditary monarchy with village autonomy.
It led directly to Pallava control over all Sangam kingdoms.
It, along with Roman trade, shaped early Tamil polity.
59.x: Rivalry among the Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas, together with Roman trade, shaped early Tamil political organisation.
59.tq: Select the option that combines the two stated forces shaping political development.
xs: **Muvendar rivalry**, along with **Roman trade**, **shaped early Tamil polity** — option **(4)**.
The polity stayed a **hereditary monarchy** with chieftains; **Pallavas** came only from the **4th c. CE**.
xa: Chera-Rome link: a temple of **Augustus** near **Muziris**.
Rivalry battles: **Venni**, **Vahaipparandalai**, **Talaiyalanganam**.
The **Leiden** seal shows Chola victory over Pandyas and Cheras.

59.s: The Telugu Choda families of Renati, Pottapi and Nellore claimed descent from:
59.x: The Renati, Pottapi and Nellore Choda families claimed descent from Karikala Chola.
59.tq: Link regional dynastic claims with the ancestor named in the tradition.
xs: The **Renati, Pottapi and Nellore Chodas** claimed descent from **Karikala Chola** — option **(2)**.
Karikala won **Venni** and built **Kallanai** across the **Kaveri**.
xa: Chola territory reached **southern Andhra**.
Chola capital shifted **Uraiyur → Puhar**.
Karikala is the subject of **Pattinappalai**.

59.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the shift in the Chola capital?
59.x: The Chola capital shifted from Uraiyur to Puhar. Vanji and Madurai were associated with the Cheras and Pandyas respectively.
59.tq: Test the direction of a capital shift rather than merely naming the two places.
xs: The Chola capital shifted **Uraiyur to Puhar** — option **(4)**.
**Vanji** was Chera; **Madurai** was Pandya; **Korkai** was a Pandya port.
xa: Chola port: **Kaveripattinam (Puhar)**.
Chera **Vanji** is identified with **Karur**.
Chola emblem **tiger**, river **Kaveri**.

60.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Tinai)
A. Kurinji
B. Mullai
C. Marutam
D. Neidal

List-II (Deity)
1. Varunan
2. Murugan
3. Mayon
4. Vendan

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
60.x: Kurinji was associated with Murugan, Mullai with Mayon, Marutam with Vendan and Neidal with Varunan.
60.tq: Start from the sure deity-landscape pair and eliminate incompatible codes.
xs: Correct matching is **A-2, B-3, C-4, D-1** — option **(1)**.
**Kurinji** (hilly) — **Murugan (Seyon)**; **Mullai** (pastoral/forest) — **Mayon (Vishnu)**.
**Marutam** (agricultural) — **Vendan (Indra)**; **Neidal** (coastal) — **Varunan**.
xa: The fifth tinai, **Palai** (desert/dry land), had **Korravai** as deity and **robbery** as occupation.
The five-fold division of land is given in the **Tolkappiyam**.
Occupations: Kurinji **hunting, honey**; Mullai **cattle rearing**; Neidal **fishing, salt making**.

60.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
60.x: Marutam was associated with agriculture in riverine plains. Fishing and salt making belonged to Neidal, the coastal landscape.
60.tq: Find the occupation shifted from one landscape to another.
xs: **Marutam — fishing and salt making** is wrong — option **(1)**.
**Marutam** (riverine plains) = **agriculture**; fishing and salt making belong to **Neidal** (coastal).
The rest are right: **Kurinji** hunting/honey, **Mullai** cattle rearing, **Palai** robbery.
xa: Marutam's deity: **Vendan (Indra)**; Neidal's: **Varunan**.
Palai = **desert / dry land**, deity **Korravai**.
Source of the scheme: **Tolkappiyam**.

60.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the five-fold division of land is correct?
1. Kurinji was a hilly region associated with Murugan.
2. Mullai represented pastoral or forest country associated with Mayon.
3. Palai represented desert or dry land associated with Korravai.
4. The classification is given in the Tolkappiyam.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
60.x: All four statements are correct. The Tolkappiyam gives the five-fold division, including Kurinji, Mullai and Palai with their respective landscapes and deities.
60.tq: Check the named source along with the landscape-deity associations before choosing the complete combination.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
1: **Kurinji** = hilly, **Murugan**. 2: **Mullai** = pastoral/forest, **Mayon**. 3: **Palai** = desert/dry land, **Korravai**.
4: the five-fold division is given in the **Tolkappiyam**.
xa: **Marutam** = agricultural plains, **Vendan (Indra)**.
**Neidal** = coastal, **Varunan**; fishing and salt making.
**Korravai** is the goddess of **war/victory**.

60.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Vellalar — Rich peasants and agricultural landowners
60.x: Vellalar were rich peasants and agricultural landowners. Anthanar were Brahmins, Vanigar were traders, and Panar were wandering bards.
60.tq: Start from the occupation that is most clearly associated with the group.
xs: **Vellalar — rich peasants and agricultural landowners** — option **(3)**.
**Anthanar** = Brahmins (priests); **Vanigar** = traders; **Kadaisiyar** = landless labourers and slaves.
Wandering bards were the **Panar**.
xa: Vellalar were the **fourth caste** in the Tolkappiyam's list (**APPSC-G1 2024**).
⚠ **Vellalar** = landowners; **Uzhavar** = tillers; **Kadaisiyar** = labourers.
**Arasar** = ruling class; **Parayar** = drummers.

60.s:
Consider the following statements regarding social classification in the Tolkappiyam:
1. Arasar, Anthanar, Vanigar and Vellalar are listed as four castes.
2. Vellalar occupied the fourth position in this list.
3. The rigid varna system had fully developed in early Sangam society.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
60.x: The Tolkappiyam lists Arasar, Anthanar, Vanigar and Vellalar, with Vellalar as the fourth group. The rigid varna system had not fully developed in early Sangam society.
60.tq: Reject the extreme claim that a social system had fully developed when the qualification is significant.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
1 correct: Tolkappiyam's four castes — **arasar, anthanar, vanigar, vellalar**. 2 correct: **Vellalar** are the **fourth**.
3 wrong: the **rigid varna system had not fully developed** — social mobility was possible.
xa: **APPSC-G1 2024**: "Vellalars were rich peasants who formed the fourth caste".
Distractors in that question: poets, labourers, forest tribes.
**Brahmins** were present and respected.

60.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Vanigar — Ruling class responsible for law and order
Parayar — Drummers and workers with animal skins
60.x: Vanigar were traders or merchants. The ruling class responsible for governance and law and order was the Arasar.
60.tq: Find the occupation-status pair that belongs to a neighbouring group.
xs: **Vanigar — ruling class** is wrong — option **(3)**.
**Vanigar** were **traders/merchants**; the ruling class for governance and law and order was the **Arasar**.
The rest are right: **Uzhavar** tillers, **Kadaisiyar** labourers/slaves, **Parayar** drummers.
xa: **Anthanar** = Brahmin priests with political and religious influence.
**Panar** = wandering bards.
**Vellalar** = rich peasants, the fourth caste.

60.s: In Sangam literature, ‘Kalavu’ refers to:
o: A hero stone erected for a warrior
60.x: Kalavu denotes pre-marital or secret love, whereas Karpu denotes married life or wedded chastity.
60.tq: Separate the two closely related terms concerning love and marriage.
xs: **Kalavu** means **pre-marital (secret) love** — option **(3)**.
**Karpu** = married life / wedded chastity; **Vattakirutal** = ritual starvation; **Nadukal** = hero stone.
xa: **Viraliyar** were court dancers patronised by kings and nobles.
Women poets: **Avvaiyar**, **Nachchellaiyar**, **Kakkaipadiniyar**.
**Sati** existed among the upper strata.

60.s: Which one of the following correctly explains the term ‘Karpu’?
60.x: Karpu means married life or wedded chastity.
60.tq: Identify the exact meaning of the term rather than its related pre-marital counterpart.
xs: **Karpu** means **wedded chastity and married life** — option **(4)**.
**Kalavu** was pre-marital love; **Vattakirutal** was a defeated king's ritual suicide.
xa: Widows led a **hard life**; **sati** in upper strata.
**Viraliyar** = court dancers.
**Mullai** tinai = **cattle rearing** (not Karpu).

60.s:
Which of the following women poets contributed to Sangam poetry?
1. Avvaiyar
2. Nachchellaiyar
3. Kakkaipadiniyar
4. Korravai
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
60.x: Avvaiyar, Nachchellaiyar and Kakkaipadiniyar are identified as women poets of Sangam literature. Korravai was a goddess associated with war and victory, not a poetess in this list.
60.tq: Separate named poetesses from a similarly prominent female religious figure.
xs: **Avvaiyar, Nachchellaiyar and Kakkaipadiniyar** were women poets — option **(3)**.
**Korravai** was a **goddess** of war/victory, the **Palai** deity.
xa: The Sangam corpus includes **women poets** among several hundred poets.
**Sati** was practised in the upper strata; widows led a hard life.
**Viraliyar** were female court dancers.

60.s:
With reference to the position of women in Sangam society, consider the following statements:
1. Sati was practised among the upper strata.
2. Widows generally led an easy and privileged life.
3. Women poets made contributions to Sangam poetry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
60.x: Sati was practised in the upper strata, while widows led a hard life. Women poets such as Avvaiyar, Nachchellaiyar and Kakkaipadiniyar contributed to Sangam poetry.
60.tq: Use the contrast between the true social-practice statement and the reversed condition of widows.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
1 correct: **sati** in the **upper strata**. 2 wrong: **widows led a hard life**.
3 correct: women poets **Avvaiyar**, **Nachchellaiyar**, **Kakkaipadiniyar**.
xa: **Viraliyar** were dancers patronised by kings and nobles.
**Kalavu** = pre-marital love; **Karpu** = wedded chastity.
Rigid **varna** had not fully developed — social mobility possible.

60.s: The viraliyar of the Sangam age were primarily associated with which of the following?
o: Performance as dancers at royal and aristocratic courts
60.x: Viraliyar were dancers who performed at courts and received patronage from kings and nobles.
60.tq: Identify the social role associated with a specific Sangam term.
xs: **Viraliyar** were **dancers who performed at courts** — option **(1)**.
They were **patronised by kings and nobles**.
xa: **Panar** = wandering bards who sang for chiefs.
**Avvaiyar** was a noted woman poet.
**Avai** was the royal court with poets.

60.s: In the Sangam age, the practice of 'Vattakirutal' referred to
o: a king defeated in battle committing ritual suicide by starving himself
the erection of hero stones for fallen warriors
the dance performance of viraliyar at court
60.x: Vattakirutal was the ritual suicide by starvation of a king defeated in battle (UPSC 2023 key). Hero stones are nadukal; secret love is kalavu; viraliyar were court dancers.
60.tq: Vattakirutal = defeated king starves to death.
xs: **Vattakirutal**: a **king defeated in battle** commits **ritual suicide by starving** — option **(1)** (**UPSC 2023** key).
Hero stones are **nadukal**; secret love is **kalavu**; court dancers are **viraliyar**.
xa: **Nadukal** honour warriors who fell in battle, carved with deeds + inscriptions.
**UPSC 2023** also keyed **Korkai, Poompuhar, Muchiri** as **ports**.
**Karpu** = married life.

60.s: Who was regarded as the chief Tamil deity during the Sangam age?
60.x: Seyon, identified with Murugan, was regarded as the chief Tamil deity in the Sangam tradition.
60.tq: Direct deity-identification tests precise recall of the principal religious figure.
xs: The chief deity was **Seyon / Murugan** — option **(3)**.
His six abodes are the **Arupadai Veedu**; his festivals appear in Sangam texts.
**Vendan** = Indra, **Varunan** = Neidal deity, **Mayon** = Vishnu.
xa: Murugan is the **Kurinji** (hilly) deity.
**Korravai** = goddess of war/victory.
Burials: **megalithic** cist and urn burials.

60.s: The six abodes of Murugan are collectively known as which of the following?
60.x: Murugan's six sacred abodes are known collectively as Arupadai Veedu.
60.tq: Look for the exact traditional term associated with a numerical religious grouping.
xs: Murugan's six abodes = **Arupadai Veedu** — option **(4)**.
**Vattakirutal** = ritual starvation; **Nadukal** = hero stones; **Tinai** = landscape division.
xa: Murugan (**Seyon**) was the chief deity; **Kurinji** god.
Murugan's festivals are recorded in Sangam texts.
Other deities: **Mayon**, **Vendan**, **Varunan**, **Korravai**.

60.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Korravai — Goddess of war and victory
Varunan — Goddess of war and victory
60.x: Korravai, not Varunan, was associated with war and victory. Mayon was Vishnu, Vendan was Indra, and Varunan was another deity of the Sangam tradition.
60.tq: Find the swapped deity association in a not-correctly-matched pair.
xs: **Varunan — goddess of war and victory** is wrong — option **(4)**.
The war goddess was **Korravai**; **Varunan** is the **Neidal** (coastal) deity.
**Mayon = Vishnu** and **Vendan = Indra** are correct.
xa: Korravai is the deity of **Palai** (desert).
Chief deity: **Seyon / Murugan**.
**Hero stones (Nadukal)** commemorated fallen warriors.

60.s:
Consider the following statements about hero stones in the Sangam tradition:
1. They were erected in memory of warriors who died in battle.
2. They depicted the deeds of the deceased warriors.
3. They sometimes carried inscriptions.
4. They were found only in the capital cities of Tamil rulers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
60.x: Nadukal were set up for warriors who fell in battle and could contain carvings of their deeds and inscriptions. They were found across Tamil Nadu, not only in royal capitals.
60.tq: Reject the extreme location claim and retain the cluster of specific features.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(1)**.
**Nadukal** honoured warriors who **fell in battle**, carved with their **deeds** and **inscriptions**.
4 wrong: they are **found across Tamil Nadu**, not only in capitals.
xa: Burials were **megalithic** — **cist and urn**.
**Vattakirutal** = a defeated king's ritual starvation.
**Korravai** = goddess of war/victory.

60.s: Which port was associated with the Cheras and was situated on the Malabar coast?
60.x: Muziris, also known as Musiri, was a Chera port on the west or Malabar coast.
60.tq: Identify the port by combining its kingdom and coast.
xs: **Muziris (Musiri)** was the **Chera** port on the **Malabar** (west) coast — option **(1)**.
**Puhar** = Chola, **Korkai** = Pandya, **Arikamedu** = near Puducherry — all east coast.
xa: Muziris = **Pattanam, Ernakulam** (KCHR excavations); the **pepper** port.
Periplus: Muziris "**abounding with ships**".
Other Chera port: **Tondi (Tyndis)**.

60.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
60.x: Muziris has been associated with Pattanam. Tondi was known as Tyndis, while Arikamedu was known as Poduke.
60.tq: Use the classical-name clue to distinguish closely related ports.
xs: **Muziris — Pattanam** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Tondi** = **Tyndis**; **Arikamedu** = **Poduke**; **Korkai** is a separate Pandya port.
xa: **KCHR's** Pattanam excavations (Ernakulam) identify Muziris (Jun **2026**).
Arikamedu = "**market street of the Romans**" (Periplus).
Other ports: **Nelkynda**, **Bakare** (Kerala), **Marakkanam**.

60.s: Korkai was particularly famous in the Sangam period for:
o: Iron manufacture and inland craft production
Pearl fishery and export of pearls and shells
The Yavana quarter dealing in silk
60.x: Korkai was a Pandya port on the east coast, noted for pearl fishing and the export of pearls and shells.
60.tq: Link the port with its distinctive economic speciality.
xs: **Korkai** was famed for its **pearl fishery** and export of **pearls and shells** — option **(2)**.
It was the **Pandya** port on the east coast.
The Roman "market street" was **Arikamedu**; the Yavana quarter was at **Puhar**.
xa: Pliny: **pearls from Pandya**.
**UPSC 2023**: Korkai, Poompuhar, Muchiri were **ports**.
Pandya embassy went to **Augustus**.

60.s: Which one of the following statements about Puhar or Kaveripattinam is correct?
o: It was a Chola port on the east coast where a Yavana quarter prospered.
It was an inland Chera capital with no maritime connections.
It was a Pandya port famous exclusively for pearl fishing.
