66.tq: Use the person–patron association to eliminate rulers from the same dynasty.
xs: **Kalidasa** was a **Navaratna** of **Chandragupta II** — option **(1)**.
He was the **greatest Sanskrit poet-dramatist**.
xa: Dramas: **Abhijnana Shakuntalam, Malavikagnimitram, Vikramorvashiyam**.
Mahakavyas: **Raghuvamsha, Kumarasambhava**; lyrics: **Meghaduta, Ritusamhara**.
⚠ The Navaratna list is **traditional** — members were not all contemporaries.

66.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
66.x: Kiratarjuniya was composed by Bharavi. Sriharsha was the author of Naishadhiyacharita.
66.tq: Check the author of each work and identify the deliberate author swap.
xs: **Kiratarjuniya — Sriharsha** is wrong — option **(1)**; Kiratarjuniyam is by **Bharavi** (Arjuna vs Shiva).
**Sriharsha** wrote **Naishadhiyacharita** (Nala-Damayanti).
**Shishupalavadha — Magha**, **Kamasutra — Vatsyayana**, **Nitisara — Kamandaka** are correct.
xa: Naishadhiyacharita is a **12th-century** work; **Magha** and **Sriharsha** are post-Gupta.
**Nitisara** is a Gupta treatise on **polity / statecraft**.
Kamasutra is placed in the Gupta period by some notes, later **Satavahana** by others.

66.s:
Arrange the following works in the order in which their authors are conventionally placed from earlier to later:
A. Plays of Bhasa
B. Works of Kalidasa
C. Naishadhiyacharita of Sriharsha
D. Shishupalavadha of Magha
66.x: Bhasa is earlier than Kalidasa; Magha is later than Kalidasa, and Sriharsha's Naishadhiyacharita is later still. Hence the order is A, B, D, C.
66.tq: Fix the earliest and latest entries first, then place the middle authors.
xs: Order: **Bhasa → Kalidasa → Magha → Sriharsha** (A, B, D, C) — option **(1)**.
**Bhasa** was **earlier than Kalidasa**; **Magha** and **Sriharsha** are **post-Gupta**.
**Naishadhiyacharita** is a **12th-century** work — the latest.
xa: Bhasa wrote **13 plays** (UPSC notes say **12**); **Charudatta** is the most famous.
⚠ Some notes list all five mahakavyas as "Gupta" — a trap.
**Bharavi** wrote **Kiratarjuniyam**.

66.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the five Mahakavyas listed in relation to classical Sanskrit literature?
66.x: The five listed Mahakavyas are Raghuvamsha, Kumarasambhava, Kiratarjuniya, Shishupalavadha and Naishadhiyacharita. Abhijnana Shakuntalam is a play, not one of these five Mahakavyas.
66.tq: Separate dramatic works from epic poems before choosing the exception.
xs: **Abhijnana Shakuntalam** is a **drama**, not a mahakavya — option **(1)**.
The five mahakavyas: **Raghuvamsha, Kumarasambhava** (Kalidasa), **Kiratarjuniyam** (Bharavi), **Shishupalavadha** (Magha), **Naishadhiyacharita** (Sriharsha).
xa: Kalidasa's other dramas: **Malavikagnimitram, Vikramorvashiyam**.
Naishadhiyacharita = **Nala-Damayanti** theme.
Kalidasa's lyrics: **Meghaduta, Ritusamhara**.

66.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists.
List-I (Work)
a. Abhijnana Shakuntalam
b. Vikramorvashiyam
c. Kumarasambhava
d. Meghaduta
List-II (Genre)
i. Mahakavya
ii. Drama
iii. Lyric poem
iv. Drama
66.x: Abhijnana Shakuntalam and Vikramorvashiyam are dramas; Kumarasambhava is a Mahakavya; and Meghaduta is a lyric poem.
66.tq: Classify each work by genre before selecting the matching code.
xs: Correct match: **a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii** — option **(1)**.
**Abhijnana Shakuntalam** and **Vikramorvashiyam** = **dramas**.
**Kumarasambhava** = **Mahakavya**; **Meghaduta** = **lyric poem**.
xa: **Raghuvamsha** is Kalidasa's other mahakavya.
**Ritusamhara** is his other lyric poem.
⚠ **Shringara Shataka** is **Bhartrihari's**, not Kalidasa's (UPPSC **2025**).

66.s: Malavikagnimitram centres on the love of Agnimitra and Malavika. Agnimitra was a
66.x: Malavikagnimitram portrays the love of Agnimitra, a Shunga king of Vidisha, and Malavika.
66.tq: Use the plot to identify the historical ruler and dynasty.
xs: **Agnimitra** was the **Shunga king of Vidisha** — option **(4)**.
**Malavikagnimitram** is Kalidasa's drama on his love for **Malavika**.
xa: Kalidasa's other dramas: **Abhijnana Shakuntalam, Vikramorvashiyam**.
Kalidasa was a **Navaratna** of **Chandragupta II**.
Usual "NOT by Kalidasa" distractors: **Mudrarakshasa, Mrichchhakatika, Kiratarjuniya**.

66.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
66.x: Shringara Shataka is attributed to Bhartrihari, not Kalidasa. Kiratarjuniyam, Shishupalavadha and Naishadhiyacharita are associated with Bharavi, Magha and Sriharsha respectively.
66.tq: Detect the deliberate wrong attribution among works commonly grouped with classical Sanskrit literature.
xs: **Shringara Shataka — Kalidasa** is wrong — option **(4)**; it is **Bhartrihari's** (UPPSC **2025**).
**Naishadhiyacharita — Sriharsha**, **Kiratarjuniyam — Bharavi**, **Shishupalavadha — Magha** are correct.
xa: Kiratarjuniyam = **Arjuna vs Shiva**; Naishadhiyacharita = **Nala-Damayanti**.
Naishadhiyacharita is a **12th-century** work.
Kalidasa's mahakavyas: **Raghuvamsha, Kumarasambhava**.

66.s: Which of the following works is associated with a post-Gupta author rather than Kalidasa?
66.x: Naishadhiyacharita was written by Sriharsha, who belongs to the post-Gupta period. The other three works are associated with Kalidasa.
66.tq: Separate works of Kalidasa from later Sanskrit mahakavyas through author attribution.
xs: **Naishadhiyacharita** is by the post-Gupta **Sriharsha** — option **(2)**.
**Abhijnana Shakuntalam, Raghuvamsha, Kumarasambhava** are **Kalidasa's**.
xa: Naishadhiyacharita is a **12th-century** work on **Nala-Damayanti**.
**Magha** (Shishupalavadha) is also post-Gupta.
**Bharavi** wrote **Kiratarjuniyam**.

66.s: The work Devichandraguptam, which provides information about Ramagupta and Dhruvadevi, was written by
66.x: Devichandraguptam is attributed to Vishakhadatta and deals with events connected with Ramagupta and Dhruvadevi.
66.tq: Use the author–work–theme chain rather than relying on the name of the ruler alone.
xs: **Devichandraguptam** was written by **Vishakhadatta** — option **(1)**.
It gives Gupta court history (**Ramagupta–Dhruvadevi**) — a political source.
**Amarasimha** = Amarakosha; **Bhasa** = Charudatta; **Kamandaka** = Nitisara.
xa: Vishakhadatta also wrote **Mudrarakshasa** (**Chanakya vs Rakshasa**).
**Sudraka** wrote **Mrichchhakatika** ("Little Clay Cart").
**Harishena** wrote the **Prayaga (Allahabad) Prashasti**.

66.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
66.x: Nitisara is a treatise on polity and statecraft. Amarakosha is a lexicon, Kamasutra deals with human relationships and conduct, and Panchatantra contains animal fables on statecraft.
66.tq: Match each work with its subject, not merely with its author.
xs: **Nitisara — Statecraft** is correct — option **(2)**; it is **Kamandaka's** Gupta treatise on polity.
**Panchatantra** = animal fables on statecraft, not grammar; **Amarakosha** = Sanskrit **lexicon**.
**Kamasutra** is by **Vatsyayana** — not astronomy.
xa: Panchatantra by **Vishnu Sharma** is a **Gupta-period** work (APPSC **2012**).
**Hitopadesha** (Narayana Pandita) is later, based on the Panchatantra.
Amarakosha's author **Amarasimha** was a Navaratna.

66.s:
With reference to Sanskrit literature, consider the following statements:
1. Hitopadesha was composed later and was based on the Panchatantra.
2. Bhasa was earlier than Kalidasa.
3. Charudatta is regarded as the most famous among the plays associated with Bhasa.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: All three statements are correct. Hitopadesha is a later work based on the Panchatantra, while Bhasa predates Kalidasa and Charudatta is his best-known play in this context.
66.tq: Treat each statement independently and select the complete combination when all three fit.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Hitopadesha** is later, **based on the Panchatantra**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Bhasa** was **earlier than Kalidasa**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Charudatta** is Bhasa's most famous play — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: Bhasa wrote **13 plays** (UPSC notes say **12**), including **Svapnavasavadattam**.
Hitopadesha: **Narayana Pandita** (some notes credit Vishnu Sharma).
Panchatantra: **Vishnu Sharma**.

66.s: Which of the following Smritis is associated with the legal literature of the Gupta age?
66.x: Narada Smriti is one of the legal works associated with the age. Yajnavalkya, Katyayana and Brihaspati Smritis are also listed among such legal texts.
66.tq: Identify the legal text rather than a literary or scientific work.
xs: **Narada Smriti** is a Gupta-age law book — option **(2)**.
**Aryabhatiya** = maths/astronomy; **Panchasiddhantika** = Varahamihira's astronomy.
xa: Other Smritis: **Yajnavalkya, Katyayana, Brihaspati** (also **Vishnu**).
**Amarakosha** (Amarasimha) is the Sanskrit lexicon.
**Chandra Vyakarana** by **Chandragomin**, a Buddhist, **5th c.**

66.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Bhasa — Charudatta
2. Shudraka — Mrichchhakatika
3. Vishakhadatta — Devichandraguptam
4. Harishena — Prayaga Prashasti
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
66.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Bhasa wrote Charudatta, Shudraka wrote Mrichchhakatika, Vishakhadatta wrote Devichandraguptam, and Harishena composed the Prayaga Prashasti of Samudragupta.
66.tq: Start from the sure author–work pairs and eliminate codes that omit them.
xs: All four pairs are correct — **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
**Bhasa — Charudatta**; **Shudraka — Mrichchhakatika**.
**Vishakhadatta — Devichandraguptam**; **Harishena — Prayaga Prashasti** of Samudragupta.
xa: ⚠ The **Harishena** of **Brihatkatha Kosha** is a different, later **Jain** author.
Mrichchhakatika = "**Little Clay Cart**", a social drama.
Vishakhadatta also wrote **Mudrarakshasa**.

66.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Harishena of the Brihatkatha Kosha was a later Jain author.
2. The Harishena who composed the Prayaga Prashasti belonged to the same literary work tradition as the author of Brihatkatha Kosha.
3. The Prayaga Prashasti records the achievements of Samudragupta.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The Harishena associated with Brihatkatha Kosha was a different, later Jain author; therefore statement 2 is incorrect.
66.tq: Separate identical names by testing the associated work and historical context.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the Brihatkatha Kosha **Harishena** was a **later Jain author**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the two **Harishenas** are **different** people.
Statement 3 is correct: the **Prayaga Prashasti** is of **Samudragupta** — **1 and 3 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Prayaga = **Allahabad** Prashasti.
⚠ Another pair: **Panchatantra** (Vishnu Sharma) vs **Hitopadesha** (Narayana Pandita).
Vishakhadatta's **Devichandraguptam** is another Gupta political source.

66.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Grammar or lexicon)
 a. Amarakosha
 b. Chandra Vyakarana
 c. Prakrit Prakasha
 d. Katantra

List-II (Author)
 i. Vararuchi
 ii. Sharvavarman
 iii. Amarasimha
 iv. Chandragomin

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
66.x: Amarakosha was written by Amarasimha, Chandra Vyakarana by Chandragomin, Prakrit Prakasha by Vararuchi, and Katantra by Sharvavarman.
66.tq: Begin with the distinctive lexicon–author pair and verify the remaining pairs.
xs: Correct match: **a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** — option **(1)**.
**Amarakosha — Amarasimha**; **Chandra Vyakarana — Chandragomin**.
**Prakrit Prakasha — Vararuchi**; **Katantra — Sharvavarman** (Satavahana age).
xa: **Chandragomin** was a **Buddhist**, **5th c.**
Amarasimha and Vararuchi were **Navaratnas**.
Satavahana-era Sanskrit works also include **Kamasutra** and Aryadeva's **Chittashuddhi Prakaranam**.

66.s: Chandragomin, associated with Chandra Vyakarana, belonged to which religious tradition?
66.x: Chandragomin was a Buddhist grammarian of the fifth century and is associated with Chandra Vyakarana.
66.tq: Combine the author, work and biographical qualifier precisely.
xs: **Chandragomin** of **Chandra Vyakarana** was a **Buddhist** (**5th c.**) — option **(3)**.
The **Harishena** of Brihatkatha Kosha was the **Jain** author in these notes.
xa: **Amarakosha** = Amarasimha's Sanskrit lexicon.
**Katantra** = Sharvavarman, **Satavahana age**.
**Prakrit Prakasha** = Vararuchi.

66.s: Which of the following groups contains only works correctly associated with Dandin and Bhatti respectively?
66.x: Dandin wrote Dasakumaracharita and Kavyadarsha, while Bhatti wrote Ravanavadha. The other groups contain works associated with different authors.
66.tq: Split the option into author groups and verify each work before accepting it.
xs: **Dandin** wrote **Dasakumaracharita and Kavyadarsha**; **Bhatti** wrote **Ravanavadha** — option **(1)**.
**Mrichchhakatika** = Sudraka; **Charudatta** = Bhasa; **Mudrarakshasa** = Vishakhadatta.
xa: **Nitisara** = Kamandaka.
**Panchatantra** = Vishnu Sharma.
**Kamasutra** = Vatsyayana.

66.s: The Panchatantra, a collection of animal fables teaching statecraft, is a Gupta-period work composed by:
66.x: The Panchatantra is attributed to Vishnu Sharma and is placed in the Gupta period (APPSC 2012). Narayana Pandita wrote the later Hitopadesha, which was based on the Panchatantra; Kamandaka wrote the Nitisara on polity; Vishakhadatta wrote Mudrarakshasa and Devichandraguptam.
66.tq: Panchatantra = Vishnu Sharma; Hitopadesha = Narayana Pandita
xs: The **Panchatantra** was composed by **Vishnu Sharma** — option **(2)** (APPSC **2012**; APPSC GS **2012**).
**Narayana Pandita** wrote the later **Hitopadesha**, based on the Panchatantra.
**Kamandaka** = **Nitisara**; **Vishakhadatta** = **Mudrarakshasa, Devichandraguptam**.
xa: Panchatantra = **animal fables on statecraft**.
Some notes credit Hitopadesha to Vishnu Sharma — a trap.
**Dandin** wrote **Dasakumaracharita**.

66.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Kalidasa — Sanskrit poetry and drama
2. Dhanvantari — Ayurveda
3. Vararuchi — Prakrit grammar
4. Vetala Bhatta — Mantrashastra
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
66.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Kalidasa was a poet-dramatist, Dhanvantari represented Ayurveda, Vararuchi was associated with Prakrit grammar, and Vetala Bhatta with Mantrashastra.
66.tq: Check every field carefully because the distractors are created by swapping neighbouring Navaratna disciplines.
xs: All four pairs are correct — **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
**Kalidasa** = poetry and drama; **Dhanvantari** = **Ayurveda** ("Father of Ayurveda").
**Vararuchi** = grammar (**Prakrit Prakasha**); **Vetala Bhatta** = magic (**Mantrashastra**).
xa: **Kshapanaka** = astrology (**Jyotishyashastra**).
**Ghatakarpara, Shanku** = sculpture and architecture.
**Amarasimha** = lexicographer (**Amarakosha**).

66.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
66.x: Amarasimha was a lexicographer associated with the Amarakosha. Ayurveda is associated with Dhanvantari, not Amarasimha.
66.tq: Find the field belonging to another member of the same traditional list.
xs: **Amarasimha — Ayurveda** is wrong — option **(4)**; Amarasimha was a **lexicographer** (**Amarakosha**).
Ayurveda belongs to **Dhanvantari**.
**Ghatakarpara** (sculpture/architecture), **Varahamihira** (astronomy/astrology), **Kshapanaka** (Jyotishyashastra) are correct.
xa: ⚠ **Kshapanaka** = astrology; **Vetala Bhatta** = magic; **Vararuchi** = grammar.
**Kalidasa** = poet-dramatist.
**Shanku** shares sculpture and architecture with Ghatakarpara.

66.s: Which of the following statements best explains the historical qualification attached to the Navaratna tradition of Chandragupta II?
o: All nine members are securely proven to have been contemporaries of Chandragupta II.
The list is traditional, and its members were not necessarily contemporaries.
The list was compiled by Harishena during the reign of Samudragupta.
The list contains only military commanders of the Gupta Empire.
66.x: The Navaratna list is a traditional association. Its members were not all contemporaries; Varahamihira, for example, belonged to the sixth century, later than Chandragupta II.
66.tq: Watch the absolute claim that all members must have lived at the same time.
xs: The Navaratna list is **traditional**; members were **not all contemporaries** — option **(2)**.
**Varahamihira** (**505–587 CE**, **6th c.**) falls after **Chandragupta II** (**380–413 AD**).
**Harishena** wrote the **Prayaga Prashasti**, not this list; the gems were scholars, not commanders.
xa: Gems: **Kalidasa, Amarasimha, Varahamihira, Dhanvantari, Kshapanaka, Vararuchi, Vetala Bhatta, Ghatakarpara, Shanku**.
**Dhanvantari** = "Father of Ayurveda".
**Vararuchi** = Prakrit Prakasha.

66.s:
Consider the following statements about Aryabhata:
1. His Aryabhatiya was composed in 499 CE.
2. He held that the Earth is spherical and rotates on its axis, and gave a scientific cause of eclipses.
3. He gave an accurate value of pi.
4. He laid down the rules of arithmetic with zero and negative numbers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct for Aryabhata. Statement 4 belongs to Brahmagupta, who gave rules of arithmetic with zero and negative quantities. So A misses statement 3, and C and D include statement 4.
66.tq: Aryabhata = rotation, eclipses, pi; Brahmagupta = zero and negative-number rules.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Aryabhatiya** dates to **499 CE**.
Statement 2 is correct: Earth **spherical**, **rotates on its axis**; scientific cause of **eclipses**.
Statement 3 is correct: accurate **pi** (**3.1416**); statement 4 belongs to **Brahmagupta** — **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Aryabhata first treated **mathematics as a distinct subject** — **Ganitapada** (APPSC **2012**).
He **used zero and place value**.
Clear claim = Earth's **daily rotation**; some notes add the Sun is stationary.

66.s: Varahamihira was associated with which of the following places and period?
66.x: Varahamihira is placed in Avanti and is dated approximately to 505–587 CE.
66.tq: Combine the place and date to distinguish the scholar from nearby ancient figures.
xs: **Varahamihira** belongs to **Avanti**, **505–587 CE** — option **(1)**.
**Karnataka** (9th c.) fits **Mahavira** of Ganitasarasangraha, not Varahamihira.
xa: Works: **Panchasiddhantika, Brihat Samhita, Brihat Jataka**.
He improved **Aryabhata's sine tables**.
He is a Navaratna though later than **Chandragupta II**.

66.s:
Consider the following statements about Varahamihira:
1. He improved Aryabhata's sine tables.
2. He treated termites as a sign of underground water.
3. He wrote the Brahmasphutasiddhanta.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
66.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Brahmasphutasiddhanta is by Brahmagupta; Varahamihira wrote the Panchasiddhantika, Brihat Samhita and Brihat Jataka. So A is incomplete and C and D include statement 3.
66.tq: Varahamihira's books all start with Pancha- or Brihat-.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: he **improved Aryabhata's sine tables**.
Statement 2 is correct: **termites** as a sign of **underground water**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Brahmasphutasiddhanta** is **Brahmagupta's** — **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Other ideas: **shifting of equinoxes**, **earthquake** theories.
**Brihat Samhita** = encyclopaedia (astronomy, astrology, geography, botany, architecture).
**Brihat Jataka** = standard work on astrology.

66.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
66.x: Brahmasphutasiddhanta was written by Brahmagupta. Lilavati was written by Bhaskara II, Khandakhadyaka by Brahmagupta, and Sushruta Samhita by Sushruta.
66.tq: Use the work–author association and watch for works exchanged between Brahmagupta and the Bhaskaracharyas.
xs: **Brahmagupta — Brahmasphutasiddhanta** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Lilavati** = **Bhaskara II**; **Khandakhadyaka** = **Brahmagupta**; **Sushruta Samhita** = **Sushruta**.
xa: Brahmagupta gave **rules of arithmetic with zero and negative quantities**.
**Bhaskara I** wrote a **commentary on Aryabhatiya**.
⚠ **Bhaskara II** = **12th c.**, not Gupta.

66.s: Brahmagupta is especially associated with rules of arithmetic involving
66.x: Brahmagupta formulated rules of arithmetic involving zero and negative quantities. He also wrote Brahmasphutasiddhanta and Khandakhadyaka.
66.tq: Identify the distinctive mathematical contribution rather than the scholar's astronomical context.
xs: **Brahmagupta** gave rules of arithmetic with **zero and negative quantities** — option **(2)**.
**Sine tables** were improved by **Varahamihira**; surgery = **Sushruta**.
xa: Works: **Brahmasphutasiddhanta, Khandakhadyaka**.
He **formalised zero arithmetic** and hinted at the **law of gravitation**.
⚠ **Aryabhata** = rotation, pi; **Brahmagupta** = zero rules.

66.s:
Consider the following statements about Bhaskara I:
1. He wrote a commentary on the Aryabhatiya.
2. In 629 CE he wrote numbers in decimal place value using a circle for zero.
3. He wrote the Lilavati.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
66.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Lilavati is by Bhaskara II (12th century). So A is incomplete and C and D include statement 3.
66.tq: Bhaskara I = Aryabhata's commentator (7th c.); Bhaskara II = Lilavati (12th c.).
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Bhaskara I** wrote a **commentary on Aryabhatiya**.
Statement 2 is correct: in **629 CE** he wrote numbers in **decimal place value** with a **circle for zero**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Lilavati** is by **Bhaskara II** (**12th c.**) — **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Bhaskara I **spread Aryabhata's school**.
Zero as a circle in an inscription: **Gwalior, 876 CE**.
Bhaskara II also wrote **Siddhanta Shiromani**.

66.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes Bhaskara II from Bhaskara I?
o: Bhaskara II belonged to the sixth century and wrote Aryabhatiya.
Bhaskara II belonged to the twelfth century and wrote Siddhanta Shiromani.
Bhaskara II was an astronomer of the Gupta court who wrote Brihat Samhita.
Bhaskara II was a physician who wrote Charaka Samhita.
66.x: Bhaskara II belonged to the twelfth century and authored Siddhanta Shiromani, in addition to Lilavati. Bhaskara I was the commentator on Aryabhatiya.
66.tq: Separate similarly named scholars by date and principal work.
xs: **Bhaskara II** belonged to the **12th century** and wrote **Siddhanta Shiromani** — option **(2)**.
**Aryabhatiya** = Aryabhata; **Brihat Samhita** = Varahamihira; **Charaka Samhita** = Charaka.
xa: Bhaskara II also wrote **Lilavati** (ideas of **calculus**); he worked on Earth's circumference.
**Bhaskara I** wrote a commentary on the **Aryabhatiya**.
⚠ **Charaka** (Kushana) and **Bhaskara II** are frequent "not Gupta" distractors.

66.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
66.x: Mahavira wrote Ganitasarasangraha, not Brihat Jataka. Ashtangahridaya, Hastyayurveda and Sushruta Samhita are associated respectively with Vagbhata, Palakapya and Sushruta.
66.tq: Find the one work belonging to a different disciplinary and authorial group.
xs: **Mahavira — Brihat Jataka** is wrong — option **(1)**; Mahavira (9th c., Karnataka) wrote **Ganitasarasangraha**.
**Brihat Jataka** is **Varahamihira's** astrology work.
**Sushruta Samhita**, **Hastyayurveda** (Palakapya) and **Ashtangahridaya** (Vagbhata) are correct.
xa: Hastyayurveda = **veterinary**, on **elephant diseases**.
Vagbhata also wrote **Ashtanga Sangraha**.
Sushruta Samhita = **surgery**.

66.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Varahamihira — Brihat Samhita
2. Brahmagupta — Khandakhadyaka
3. Bhaskara II — Siddhanta Shiromani
4. Dhanvantari — Hastyayurveda
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
66.x: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correctly matched. Hastyayurveda was written by Palakapya, not Dhanvantari.
66.tq: Check each work against its specialist author and isolate the medical-work substitution.
xs: Pairs 1–3 are correct: **Varahamihira — Brihat Samhita**; **Brahmagupta — Khandakhadyaka**; **Bhaskara II — Siddhanta Shiromani**.
Pair 4 is wrong: **Hastyayurveda** is **Palakapya's** — **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **Dhanvantari** = "Father of Ayurveda", a Navaratna.
Brahmagupta also wrote **Brahmasphutasiddhanta**.
Bhaskara II also wrote **Lilavati**.

66.s: Which one of the following statements about Aryabhata is correct?
o: He treated mathematics as a distinct subject and included a separate Ganitapada in Aryabhatiya.
He wrote Siddhanta Shiromani in the twelfth century.
He rejected the use of place value in astronomical calculations.
He treated mathematics only as an auxiliary branch of medicine.
66.x: Aryabhata is regarded as the first Indian scholar to treat mathematics as a distinct subject; Aryabhatiya contains a separate Ganitapada. Siddhanta Shiromani belongs to Bhaskara II.
66.tq: Identify the precise distinction between a scholar's method and later works wrongly attributed to him.
xs: **Aryabhata** first treated **mathematics as a distinct subject**, with a separate **Ganitapada** — option **(1)** (APPSC **2012**).
**Siddhanta Shiromani** is **Bhaskara II's** (**12th c.**).
Aryabhata **used zero and place value** — he did not reject it.
xa: **Aryabhatiya** dates to **499 CE**.
Earth **spherical**, rotates on its **axis**.

66.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the siddhantas summarised in the Panchasiddhantika?
66.x: The five siddhantas are Surya, Romaka, Paulisa, Vasishtha and Paitamaha. Charaka is not included in the list.
66.tq: Find the outsider in a named technical list.

66.s: Which one of the following statements about the development of the decimal system in India is correct?

xs: The Gupta age developed the **decimal system** and the **concept of zero** — option **(3)**.

xa: **Aryabhata** used zero and place value; **Brahmagupta** formalised zero arithmetic.

3. The Sankheda copper plate is dated 876 CE.

66.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Sankheda copper plate is dated 594 CE (cited by some sources as the earliest dated place-value numeral); 876 CE is the Gwalior inscription. So A is incomplete and C and D include statement 3.

xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Mankani plates (AD 595–596)** = earliest place-value evidence (UPSC **2026**).

66.s: The Dashavatara Temple at Deogarh is associated with which combination?

xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.

Statement 2: the earliest paintings (**Satavahana-era**) are in **Caves 9 and 10** — correct.
Statement 3: the later phase was patronised by the **Vakataka** king **Harishena** (5th c.) — correct.
xa: **Cave 16** was excavated by Harishena's minister **Varahadeva**.
**Cave 10** has the **Chhaddanta Jataka** = first "completely evolved painting" (APPSC G2 2012).
Some notes count **25 viharas + 4 chaityas**; **5 Hinayana**, rest Mahayana.

66.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
66.x: The Dying Princess is associated with Cave 16. The Mother and Child panel is in Cave 17, Mahaparinirvana is in Cave 26, and Padmapani is associated with Cave 1.
66.tq: Start from the sure panel–cave pair and eliminate the swapped cave numbers.
xs: **Dying Princess — Cave 16** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Mother and Child** is in **Cave 17**, not 26.
**Mahaparinirvana** is in **Cave 26**, not 17; **Padmapani** is in **Cave 1**, not 19.
xa: **Cave 19** is a chaitya with a **standing Buddha and two Yakshas**.
**Cave 17** also has a Brahmi inscription and the **Bhava-chakra** (wheel of life).
The Dying Princess is a **secular theme**; Cave 16 was excavated by **Varahadeva**.

66.s:
With reference to Ajanta paintings, consider the following statements:
1. Padmapani and Vajrapani are represented as Bodhisattvas.
2. The Mahaparinirvana at Ajanta is a painting of the dying Buddha.
3. The Mother and Child panel is associated with Cave 17.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: Padmapani and Vajrapani are Bodhisattvas, and the Mother and Child panel is associated with Cave 17. The Mahaparinirvana is a sculpture, not a painting.
66.tq: Use the painting–sculpture distinction to detect the false statement.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: **Padmapani** and **Vajrapani** are **Bodhisattvas** — correct (BPSC 2023).
Statement 2: the **Mahaparinirvana** (Cave 26) is a **sculpture** of the dying Buddha, **not a painting** — wrong.
Statement 3: **Mother and Child** (before the Buddha) is in **Cave 17** — correct.
xa: Padmapani is in **Cave 1**; the **Dying Princess** in **Cave 16**.
Technique: tempera on dry lime plaster (**fresco secco**), outlines drawn in red.
Themes: **Jataka tales**, secular life, Bodhi-tree worship and group dances.

66.s: Which one of the following is NOT a theme represented in the Ajanta paintings?
66.x: Ajanta contains themes from Jataka tales, secular life, Bodhi-tree worship and group dances. Chola naval battles are unrelated to these paintings.
66.tq: Find the odd thematic category while avoiding a famous-word association trap.
xs: **Naval battles of the Cholas** are not an Ajanta theme — option **(1)** is the answer.
Ajanta themes are **Jatakas / Jataka tales** plus **secular life**.
**Bodhi-tree worship** and **group dances** also appear.
xa: Famous panels: **Padmapani**, **Vajrapani**, **Dying Princess**, **Mother and Child**.
**Cave 10**: Shwetagaja / **Chhaddanta Jataka** = first "completely evolved painting".
**Cave 17**: **Bhava-chakra** (wheel of life).

66.s:
Consider the following statements about the technique of the Ajanta paintings:
1. They are tempera on dry lime plaster (fresco secco), not true fresco.
2. Outlines were first drawn in red and then filled with colour.
3. Blue pigment was not used at Ajanta.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
66.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: lapis-lazuli blue is in fact used at Ajanta, though some sources claim otherwise. So A is incomplete and C and D include statement 3.
66.tq: Ajanta = fresco secco, red outline, lapis blue present.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: tempera on dry lime plaster (**fresco secco**), **not true fresco** — correct.
Statement 2: **outlines drawn in red**, then filled with colour — correct.
Statement 3: wrong — **lapis-lazuli blue** is in fact used at Ajanta.
xa: ⚠ Trap: some notes say blue is absent at Ajanta — it is not.
Earliest paintings (**Caves 9 and 10**) are **Satavahana-era**; some notes link them to the **Amaravati** style.
**Ashwin Prabhu**'s book on Ajanta's murals (**3 Apr 2026**) is a current-affairs hook.

66.s: Ajanta was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in
66.x: Ajanta was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983, among the early Indian sites to receive that status.
66.tq: Use the chronological range of UNESCO inscriptions and select the historically central date.
xs: Ajanta became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in **1983** — option **(2)** is correct.
It was inscribed **with Ellora**, among India's **first** UNESCO sites.
xa: Ajanta was discovered in **1819** by **John Smith**.
It lies in **Aurangabad district, Maharashtra**, on the **Waghora** river.
**Ellora**'s Buddhist caves are **Caves 1-12** (Dhedwada group).

66.s: The Shwetagaja (Chhaddanta) Jataka painting, regarded as the first completely evolved painting at Ajanta, is found in which cave?
66.x: The Chhaddanta Jataka is in Cave 10, one of the earliest (Satavahana-era) painted caves (APPSC G2 2012). Cave 1 has the Padmapani, Cave 16 the Dying Princess, and Cave 17 the Mother and Child and the Bhava-chakra.
66.tq: Caves 9-10 earliest; Chhaddanta = Cave 10
xs: The Shwetagaja / **Chhaddanta Jataka** painting is in **Cave 10** — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC G2 2012).
**Caves 9 and 10** hold the earliest, **Satavahana-era** paintings.
**Cave 1** has **Padmapani**; **Cave 16** the **Dying Princess**; **Cave 17** the **Mother and Child** and Bhava-chakra.
xa: It is counted the first "**completely evolved painting**" in India.
Later caves (e.g. **Cave 16**) came under the **Vakataka** king **Harishena**.
Some notes link the earliest Ajanta paintings to the **Amaravati** style.

66.s:
Consider the following statements about the Gupta-period Udayagiri caves:
1. They are located in Madhya Pradesh near Vidisha.
2. They contain twenty caves, of which nineteen are Hindu and one is Jain.
3. They include representations of Vishnu as Varaha and Shiva.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: All three statements are correct. The Udayagiri caves near Vidisha in Madhya Pradesh comprise twenty caves, including nineteen Hindu and one Jain cave, with Varaha and Shiva representations.
66.tq: Check site, numerical composition and religious imagery together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: the Gupta Udayagiri caves are at **Vidisha**, near **Sanchi**, **MP** — correct.
Statement 2: **20** caves — **19 Hindu**, **1 Jain** — correct.
Statement 3: deities include **Vishnu (Varaha)** and **Shiva** — correct.
xa: Carved under **Chandragupta II**; a colossal **Varaha (boar) Vishnu** panel.
**Virasena**'s inscription there records Chandragupta II's conquests.
⚠ Not the **Odisha** Udayagiri, which is **Kharavela**'s Jain site.

66.s: The Gupta-period Udayagiri caves should NOT be confused with the Udayagiri caves of which region?
66.x: The Gupta Udayagiri caves are in Madhya Pradesh near Vidisha. They are distinct from the Jain Udayagiri caves of Odisha.
66.tq: Discriminate between two sites with the same name by religion and region.
xs: The Gupta Udayagiri caves (MP) must not be confused with the Jain Udayagiri caves of **Odisha** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **Odisha Udayagiri** is **Kharavela**'s **Jain** site.
The Gupta caves are in **Madhya Pradesh**, near **Vidisha** — some notes blur the two.
xa: Gupta Udayagiri: **20** caves (**1** Jain, **19** Hindu), carved under **Chandragupta II**.
**Virasena**'s inscription records Chandragupta II's conquests.
The **Mehrauli pillar** originally stood at **Udayagiri** near Vidisha.

66.s: The Bagh caves are best described as
o: nine Buddhist viharas in Dhar district, with paintings having secular and local themes
twenty Hindu caves at Vidisha, all devoted to Vishnu
a group of Jain caves at Odisha associated with Kharavela
a group of royal Gupta temples constructed entirely of brick
66.x: The Bagh caves in Dhar district of Madhya Pradesh comprise nine Buddhist viharas, generally dated to the fifth–sixth centuries CE, and their paintings include secular and local themes.
66.tq: Combine cave number, religious function, location and painting character.
xs: Bagh caves = **nine Buddhist viharas** in **Dhar district** with **secular and local** paintings — option **(1)** is correct.
They are **Gupta-age**, dated **5th-6th c. CE**.
**Twenty caves at Vidisha** = **Udayagiri**; **Jain caves of Odisha** = **Kharavela**'s Udayagiri; brick temple = **Bhitargaon**.
xa: **Cave 4** at Bagh is called **Rang Mahal**.
Bagh's famous **Hallisaka** panel = women dancing around a man, a joyous folk dance.
Some notes place Bagh in **Hoshangabad** instead of Dhar.

66.s: The Hallisaka painting at Bagh caves depicts
66.x: The Hallisaka painting at Bagh is known for depicting a joyous folk dance.
66.tq: Identify the subject of a named painting rather than its location alone.
xs: The Hallisaka painting at Bagh depicts **a joyous folk dance** — option **(4)** is correct (UPSC 2026).
The panel shows **women dancing around a man**.
xa: Bagh = **9 Buddhist viharas**, **Dhar district**, MP, **5th-6th c. CE**.
**Cave 4** at Bagh = **Rang Mahal**.
Bagh paintings are **secular and local** in theme.

66.s: Which inscriptional and historical association is connected with the Udayagiri caves?
o: Kharavela’s inscription recording the construction of Buddhist viharas
Virasena’s inscription recording the conquests of Chandragupta II
Ashoka’s edict recording the spread of Jainism
Rudradaman’s inscription recording the reign of Samudragupta
66.x: An inscription of Virasena at Udayagiri records the conquests of Chandragupta II.
66.tq: Match the inscription’s author with the ruler and site.
xs: **Virasena**'s inscription at Udayagiri records the **conquests of Chandragupta II** — option **(2)** is correct.
The caves were carved under **Chandragupta II**.
**Kharavela** belongs to the **Odisha** Udayagiri (Jain), not the Gupta caves.
xa: Udayagiri (Vidisha, MP): **20** caves — **19** Hindu, **1** Jain.
Colossal **Varaha (boar) Vishnu** panel.
The **Mehrauli iron pillar** of Chandragupta II originally stood at **Udayagiri**.

66.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched?
1. Ellora Caves 1–12 — Buddhist group
2. Mandapeshwar — later Christian cave
3. Udayagiri near Vidisha — nineteen Hindu and one Jain cave
4. Bagh — five Buddhist viharas only
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
66.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Bagh had nine Buddhist viharas, not five, so statement 4 is false.
66.tq: Find the numerical distortion in an otherwise familiar list of cave complexes.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**Ellora Caves 1-12** = Buddhist group (Dhedwada group) — correct; **Mandapeshwar** (Mumbai) = Buddhist, later a **Christian** cave — correct.
**Udayagiri** near Vidisha = **19 Hindu**, **1 Jain** — correct.
**Bagh** had **9 Buddhist viharas**, not five — statement 4 is wrong.
xa: Bagh **Cave 4** = **Rang Mahal**; famous **Hallisaka** dance panel.
Ajanta and Ellora became **UNESCO** sites together in **1983**.
⚠ Odisha's Udayagiri is **Kharavela**'s Jain site, not the Gupta one.

66.s: Gupta silver coins introduced after the conquest of the Western Kshatrapas were modelled on
66.x: The silver coins introduced after the Saka conquest were modelled on Saka silver issues.
66.tq: Distinguish the model of the silver issues from the materials and coinage of other dynasties.
xs: Gupta silver coins were modelled on **Saka silver issues** — option **(4)** is correct.
Silver coinage began after **Chandragupta II** conquered the **Sakas** (Western Kshatrapas) of **Gujarat** (MPPSC 2023).
xa: ⚠ Trap: some notes say "gold coins modelled on Saka silver" — read **silver**.
The gold **dinara** was issued in the largest numbers.
Chandragupta II's coin types: **Archer** and **lion-slayer**.

66.s:
Consider the following pairs of Gupta coin types and rulers:
1. Veena-player (lyrist) type - Samudragupta
2. Kartikeya / king feeding peacock type - Chandragupta II
3. Archer and lion-slayer types - Chandragupta II
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
66.x: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct. Pair 2 is wrong: the Kartikeya / king feeding peacock type (and an Ashvamedha type) belongs to Kumaragupta I. So A is incomplete and C and D include pair 2.
66.tq: Kumaragupta = Kartikeya (Kumara is Kartikeya's name).
xs: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Pair 1: **Veena-player (lyrist)** — **Samudragupta** — correct.
Pair 2: **Kartikeya / king feeding peacock** belongs to **Kumaragupta I**, not Chandragupta II — wrong.
Pair 3: **Archer** and **lion-slayer** — **Chandragupta II** — correct.
xa: ⚠ **Tiger-slayer** = Samudragupta; **lion-slayer** = Chandragupta II; **peacock** = Kumaragupta I.
**Skandagupta**: bow, arrow, **Garuda** standard, Lakshmi.
**Ashvamedha** type appears under both **Samudragupta** and **Kumaragupta I**.

66.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists.
List-I (Coin type)
a. King-queen
b. Tiger-slayer
c. Lion-slayer
d. Garuda standard
List-II (Ruler)
i. Chandragupta I
ii. Samudragupta
iii. Chandragupta II
iv. Skandagupta
66.x: The king-queen type belongs to Chandragupta I; tiger-slayer to Samudragupta; lion-slayer to Chandragupta II; and Garuda standard to Skandagupta.
66.tq: Start with the distinctive king-queen and lion-slayer types, then complete the code.
xs: Correct code: **a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv** — option **(1)**.
**King-queen** (Chandragupta I-Kumaradevi) — **Chandragupta I**; **Tiger-slayer** — **Samudragupta**.
**Lion-slayer** — **Chandragupta II**; **Garuda standard** — **Skandagupta**.
xa: Samudragupta also issued **Veena-player** and **Ashvamedha** types.
**Kumaragupta I**: **Kartikeya / king feeding peacock** type.
Silver coins began after Chandragupta II's conquest of the **Sakas** of Gujarat.

66.s:
The description of the Gupta period as a ‘Classical’ or ‘Golden’ age is supported by which of the following developments?
1. Peak of Sanskrit literature
2. Advances in mathematics and astronomy
3. Ajanta painting and Sarnath sculpture
4. Emergence of the first structural temples
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
66.x: All four developments are cited as grounds for regarding the Gupta period as a classical age.
66.tq: Group the positive cultural and scientific indicators before checking the coded options.
xs: All four developments support the "classical age" label — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
The notes list: peak of **Sanskrit literature**, **mathematics and astronomy**, **Ajanta painting**, **Sarnath sculpture** and the **first structural temples**.
xa: Gupta legacy: the **decimal system** and **concept of zero**.
Sanskrit became the language of **inscriptions and courts**.
Against the label: **land grants**, **vishti**, decline of trade and towns — "golden" mainly for the **elite**.

66.s:
Which of the following is cited as a criticism of describing the Gupta period as a ‘Golden Age’?
1. Growth of land grants and feudatories
2. Expansion of vishti or forced labour
3. Decline of trade and towns
4. Falling status of women
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
66.x: All four conditions are cited as limitations of the Golden Age label. The period’s prosperity and cultural achievements were not equally experienced by all sections of society.
66.tq: Contrast elite cultural achievement with social and economic criticisms.
xs: All four are cited against the "Golden Age" label — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Land grants and feudatories** and **vishti** (forced labour) are listed.
**Decline of trade and towns**, **rigid caste** and **falling status of women** are listed too.
xa: Conclusion: the age was "golden" **mainly for the elite**.
For the label: peak of **Sanskrit literature**, maths and astronomy, Ajanta, Sarnath, first structural temples.
**Nalanda** drew students from China, Tibet, Korea and South-East Asia.

66.s: The expression that the Gupta ‘Golden Age’ was mainly a golden age for the elite reflects which of the following conditions?
o: Permanent expansion of trade and towns
Rigid caste practices and unequal social benefits
Universal prosperity among peasants and labourers
66.x: The criticism highlights rigid caste distinctions, forced labour, declining trade and towns, and the falling status of women, showing that benefits were unevenly distributed.
66.tq: Apply the criticism of an historical label to its social implications.
xs: "Golden mainly for the elite" reflects **rigid caste** and **unequal social benefits** — option **(3)** is correct.
The criticism lists **land grants**, **vishti** (forced labour), **decline of trade and towns**, rigid caste and falling status of women.
So trade **declined** (not expanded) and **land grants grew** (not disappeared) — options 1 and 2 are wrong.
xa: For the label: **Sanskrit literature**, maths, astronomy, Ajanta painting, **Sarnath** sculpture.
Gupta legacy to world mathematics: **decimal system** and **zero**.
Arab contact carried decimal place-value notation to the **Islamic world → Europe**.

66.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Gupta age:
1. Sanskrit became established as a language of inscriptions and courts.
2. Nalanda attracted students from China, Tibet, Korea and South-East Asia.
3. Gupta intellectual culture developed without any external influence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because works such as the Romaka and Paulisa Siddhantas show Greek input into Indian science.
66.tq: Identify the absolute claim that conflicts with the evidence of cultural exchange.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: Sanskrit was fixed as the language of **inscriptions and courts** — correct.
Statement 2: **Nalanda** drew students from **China, Tibet, Korea and South-East Asia** — correct.
Statement 3: wrong — Varahamihira's **Romaka/Paulisa siddhantas** show **Greek input**.
xa: **Panchasiddhantika** summarises five systems: **Surya, Romaka, Paulisa, Vasishtha, Paitamaha**.
Arab contact carried decimal place-value notation **→ Islamic world → Europe**.
The Gupta age is the "classical age" of Sanskrit, maths (**zero, decimal**) and art.

66.s: The earliest paintings in Ajanta, particularly in Caves 9 and 10, are associated with the
66.x: The earliest Ajanta paintings, especially those in Caves 9 and 10, are associated with the Satavahana period and are linked to the Amaravati style.
66.tq: Use the cave-number and period combination to avoid confusing later Ajanta patronage.
xs: Ajanta's earliest paintings (Caves **9-10**) are **Satavahana** work, linked to the **Amaravati style** — option **(1)** is correct.
The later phase came under the **Vakatakas** (Harishena), not the earliest one.
xa: **Cave 10**: **Chhaddanta Jataka** = first "completely evolved painting" (APPSC G2 2012).
**4th-5th c.**: **Vishnukundina** adaptation of the Gupta rock-cut style.
Standard date for Ajanta's start: c. **2nd century BCE**, Satavahana era.

66.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with a regional cave-temple site of the Gupta-age cultural context in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Mogalrajapuram — Sarnath Buddha in Dhyan mudra
Mogalrajapuram — five caves and Nataraja image
66.x: Mogalrajapuram is known for five caves and a Nataraja image. Bhairavakonda is associated with eight Kapalika caves, while Undavalli has a different architectural and religious profile.
66.tq: Match each regional site with its distinctive number, deity or sectarian association.
xs: **Mogalrajapuram** has **5 caves** and a **Nataraja** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Bhairavakonda** has the **8 Kapalika caves** — not Undavalli.
The **Sarnath Buddha in Dhyan mudra** was the PM's gift to Thailand's King — not Mogalrajapuram.
xa: **4th-5th c.**: **Vishnukundina** adaptation of the Gupta rock-cut style.
Satavahana-era Sanskrit works: **Katantra** (Sharvavarman), **Kamasutra** (Vatsyayana).
Ajanta's earliest paintings (Caves **9-10**) are Satavahana work.

66.s: In April 2025, the Prime Minister gifted to the King of Thailand a
o: reclining Ananta Padmanabha image from Undavalli
Buddha image from Sarnath in Dhyan mudra
66.x: The gift was a Sarnath Buddha in Dhyan mudra presented to Thailand's King in April 2025.
66.tq: Identify the exact object and provenance in a current cultural-diplomacy question.
xs: The PM gifted a **Sarnath Buddha** in **Dhyan mudra** to Thailand's King (**Apr 2025**) — option **(4)** is correct.
**Mogalrajapuram** is known for **5 caves** and a **Nataraja** — not a gift.
xa: ⚠ Classic Sarnath seated Buddha = **Dharmachakra mudra**; the gift was in **Dhyan mudra**.
Sarnath images used polished **Chunar (buff) sandstone**.
Current relevance: **Ashwin Prabhu**'s book on Ajanta's murals (**3 Apr 2026**).

66.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
66.x: Charaka is associated with the Kushana period, not exclusively with the Gupta period. Bhaskara II belonged to the twelfth century and Vagbhata wrote Ashtanga Hridaya.
66.tq: Apply the period distinction to detect the misleading Gupta association.
xs: **Charaka — Gupta period exclusively** is wrong — option **(3)** is the answer.
**Charaka** (Charaka Samhita) was **Kushana-era**, **Kanishka's physician** — so option 4 is correct.
**Bhaskara II** is **12th c.**; **Vagbhata** wrote **Ashtanga Hridaya** — both correct.
xa: Charaka and Bhaskara II are frequent "**not Gupta**" distractors.
**Sushruta**: Sushruta Samhita (surgery); **Palakapya**: **Hastyayurveda** (elephant diseases).
**Bhaskara II** wrote **Lilavati** (maths) and **Siddhanta Shiromani** (astronomy).
Gupta physicians used **iron and mercury** preparations.

67.s: Who founded the Vakataka dynasty?
67.x: Vindhyashakti is regarded as the founder of the Vakataka dynasty.
67.tq: Use the founder–dynasty association directly; do not confuse founder with a later great ruler.
xs: **Vindhyashakti** founded the Vakataka dynasty — option **(4)** is correct.
**Pravarasena I** was his **son**; **Rudrasena II** married **Prabhavatigupta**; **Harishena** patronised Ajanta.
xa: Pravarasena I was the only Vakataka to take the title **Samrat**.
Two branches: main **Nandivardhana/Pravarapura** and **Vatsagulma (Basim)**.
Vishnukundin founder **Indra Varma** began as a **Vakataka vassal**.

67.s:
With reference to Pravarasena I, consider the following statements:
1. He was the son of Vindhyashakti.
2. He was the only Vakataka ruler to assume the title Samrat.
3. He performed Vajapeya and Ashvamedha sacrifices.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: Pravarasena I was Vindhyashakti’s son, the only Vakataka ruler to take the title Samrat, and performed Vajapeya and Ashvamedha sacrifices.
67.tq: Combine lineage, title and ritual facts in one coded question.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **Pravarasena I** was the **son** of **Vindhyashakti** — correct.
Statement 2: he was the only Vakataka to take the title **Samrat** — correct.
Statement 3: he performed **Vajapeya** and **Ashvamedhas** — correct (BPSC 2024).
xa: ⚠ **Pravarasena I** = Samrat, Ashvamedhas; **Pravarasena II** = Prakrit **Setubandha**.
**Rudrasena II** married **Prabhavatigupta**, daughter of **Chandragupta II**.
**Harishena** (Vatsagulma) patronised **Ajanta Caves 16-17**.

67.s:
Consider the following statements about Prabhavatigupta:
1. She was a daughter of Chandragupta II.
2. She was married to the Vakataka ruler Pravarasena I.
3. Her regency after her husband's death gave the Guptas indirect control of the Deccan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
67.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: she married Rudrasena II; Pravarasena I was the son of the founder Vindhyashakti. So A is incomplete and C and D include statement 2.
67.tq: Prabhavatigupta: Chandragupta II's daughter, Rudrasena II's queen, regent.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: **Prabhavatigupta** was the daughter of **Chandragupta II** — correct.
Statement 2: she married **Rudrasena II**, not Pravarasena I — wrong.
Statement 3: her **regency** after Rudrasena II's death gave the Guptas **indirect control of the Deccan** — correct.
xa: **Pravarasena I** was the son of founder **Vindhyashakti** and took the title **Samrat**.
**Pravarasena II** wrote the Prakrit **Setubandha**.
Vakataka branches: **Nandivardhana/Pravarapura** and **Vatsagulma (Basim)**.

67.s: Who wrote the Prakrit work Setubandha?
67.x: Pravarasena II wrote the Prakrit work Setubandha.
67.tq: Apply the author–work pairing without confusing Pravarasena I and II.
xs: **Pravarasena II** wrote the Prakrit **Setubandha** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Pravarasena I** is known for the title **Samrat** and **Ashvamedhas**, not Setubandha.
**Bana** wrote **Harshacharita** and **Kadambari**; **Harishena** patronised Ajanta.
xa: ⚠ Do not swap the two Pravarasenas.
**Rudrasena II** married **Prabhavatigupta**, Chandragupta II's daughter.
Founder of the dynasty: **Vindhyashakti**.

67.s: Harishena of the Vatsagulma branch is associated with the patronage of which Ajanta caves through his minister Varahadeva?
67.x: Harishena patronised Ajanta Caves 16 and 17 through his minister Varahadeva.
67.tq: Test the exact cave-number pair rather than the general Ajanta association.
xs: **Harishena** patronised **Ajanta Caves 16-17** through minister **Varahadeva** — option **(4)** is correct.
He belonged to the **Vatsagulma (Basim)** branch.
xa: The other Vakataka branch = **Nandivardhana/Pravarapura**.
**Pravarasena II** wrote **Setubandha**; **Pravarasena I** took the title **Samrat**.
Prabhavatigupta's regency gave the Guptas **indirect control of the Deccan**.

67.s:
Consider the following statements about Harsha's accession:
1. He came to power at the age of 16 after his brother Rajyavardhana was killed by Sasanka.
2. His father was Prabhakaravardhana and his mother Yashomati.
3. The Harsha era began in 647 CE.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
67.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Harsha era began in 606 CE, the year of his accession; 647 CE is the year of his death. So A is incomplete and C and D include statement 3.
67.tq: 606 = accession and era; 647 = death.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: Harsha came to power aged **16** after **Rajyavardhana** was killed by **Sasanka** — correct.
Statement 2: father **Prabhakaravardhana**, mother **Yashomati** — correct.
Statement 3: the **Harsha era** began in **606 CE**; **647** is the year of his death — wrong.
xa: Harsha reigned **606-647 CE**.
Yashomati became **sati** in **605**.
He died in **647 AD** without heir → the **Pushyabhuti** line ended.

67.s: Which of the following titles was borne by Harsha?
67.x: Harsha used the titles Siladitya and Sakalottarapathanatha, meaning lord of all North India. Paramesvara was assumed by Pulakesin II after his victory over Harsha.
67.tq: Use the ruler–title association and watch for the opponent's title as a trap.
xs: Harsha bore the title **Sakalottarapathanatha** (lord of all North India) — option **(2)** is correct.
His other title was **Siladitya / Shiladitya** (APPSC G1 2012).
**Paramesvara** was taken by **Pulakesin II** after defeating Harsha.
xa: Also styled **Uttarapathanatha**.
Harsha moved his capital from **Thanesar** to **Kannauj**.
Pulakesin's victory is recorded in the **Aihole inscription**.

67.s: Harsha died in 647 CE without an heir. What was the immediate dynastic consequence mentioned in connection with his death?
o: The Badami Chalukya dynasty came to an end.
The Valabhi kingdom became the new imperial dynasty.
The Pushyabhuti line came to an end.
67.x: Harsha died without an heir in 647 CE, bringing the Pushyabhuti line to an end.
67.tq: Link the succession fact to its direct dynastic consequence.
xs: Harsha's heirless death ended the **Pushyabhuti line** — option **(4)** is correct.
He died in **647 AD** without heir.
xa: Harsha was the **last great Buddhist patron-king** of the north before the rise of Rajput states.
His was the **last great empire** / unified north India of ancient times.
Founder of the line: **Pushyabhuti** (BPSC 2022 key); once **Gupta feudatories**.

67.s:
Arrange the following members of the Vardhana line in chronological order:
A. Adityavardhana
B. Prabhakaravardhana
C. Rajyavardhana
D. Harshavardhana
67.x: The sequence is Adityavardhana, Prabhakaravardhana, Rajyavardhana and Harshavardhana.
67.tq: Fix the father–elder brother–younger brother succession before checking the options.
xs: Order: **Adityavardhana → Prabhakaravardhana → Rajyavardhana → Harshavardhana** — option **(1) A, B, C, D**.
**Adityavardhana** was an early ruler; **Prabhakaravardhana** was Harsha's father.
**Rajyavardhana**, the elder brother, was killed by **Sasanka**; then **Harsha** ruled **606-647 CE**.
xa: Some notes call **Prabhakaravardhana** the founder — he was the first great ruler.
Other founder names: **Pushyabhuti** (BPSC 2022 key) and **Naravardhana**.
Harsha came to power aged **16**.

67.s:
Which of the following statements about the Vardhana lineage is correct?
1. Prabhakaravardhana was the father of Rajyavardhana and Harsha.
2. Yashomati, the queen of Prabhakaravardhana, became sati in 605 CE.
3. Rajyavardhana was killed by Sasanka.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
67.x: All three statements are correct: Prabhakaravardhana was their father, Yashomati became sati in 605 CE, and Rajyavardhana was killed by Sasanka.
67.tq: Combine family relationship, date and political event in a single statement set.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **Prabhakaravardhana** was the father of **Rajyavardhana** and **Harsha** — correct.
Statement 2: queen **Yashomati** became **sati** in **605** — correct.
Statement 3: **Rajyavardhana** was killed by **Sasanka** — correct.
xa: ⚠ **Sasanka** killed Rajyavardhana; **Devagupta** killed **Grahavarman** — do not swap.
Harsha's sister **Rajyashri** married the Maukhari **Grahavarman**.
**Harsha era** begins **606 CE**.

67.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the early capitals of Harsha and the Maukharis is correct?
o: Valabhi was the first capital of Harsha, while Kannauj was the Kamarupa capital.
Pataliputra was the first capital of Harsha, while Vengi was the Maukhari capital.
Thanesar was the first capital of Harsha, while Kannauj was the Maukhari capital.
Kannauj was Harsha's first capital, while Thanesar was the Maukhari capital.
67.x: Thanesar was Harsha's first capital, and Kannauj was the capital of the Maukharis. Harsha later shifted his capital to Kannauj.
67.tq: Compare two dynastic capitals instead of treating the later capital as the original one.
xs: **Thanesar** was Harsha's first capital and **Kannauj** the **Maukhari capital** — option **(3)** is correct (CGPSC 2011).
Harsha later moved from **Thanesar → Kannauj**, shifting power to the **Ganga-Yamuna doab**.
**Valabhi** was the Maitraka kingdom; **Vengi** was the Andhra capital in Hiuen Tsang's account.
xa: Kannauj **replaced Pataliputra** as the premier city (Hiuen Tsang).
Kamarupa (Assam) was ruled by **Bhaskaravarman**, Harsha's ally.
Harsha's court at **Kannauj** became an intellectual centre.

67.s: Who was Grahavarman?
o: A ruler of Kamarupa and ally of Shashanka
A Valabhi ruler made feudatory by Harsha
A Chalukyan ruler and brother of Pulakesin II
A Maukhari ruler and husband of Rajyashri
67.x: Grahavarman was a Maukhari ruler and the husband of Rajyashri. He was killed by Devagupta of Malwa.
67.tq: Test identity through dynasty, relationship and political context.
xs: **Grahavarman** was a **Maukhari** ruler and husband of **Rajyashri** — option **(4)** is correct.
He was killed by **Devagupta of Malwa**, who held Rajyashri at Kannauj.
**Kamarupa** = **Bhaskaravarman**; **Valabhi** = **Dhruvasena II**.
xa: Harsha freed **Rajyashri** and drove **Shashanka** from Kannauj.
Kannauj was the **Maukhari capital** (CGPSC 2011).
⚠ **Devagupta** killed Grahavarman; **Sasanka** killed **Rajyavardhana**.

67.s: Who killed Grahavarman and held Rajyashri at Kannauj?
67.x: Devagupta of Malwa killed Grahavarman and held Rajyashri at Kannauj.
67.tq: Use the wrong-ruler-for-the-deed trap with closely associated contemporary rulers.
xs: **Devagupta of Malwa** killed Grahavarman and held Rajyashri at Kannauj — option **(3)** is correct.
**Shashanka** of Gauda killed **Rajyavardhana**, not Grahavarman.
**Bhaskaravarman** of Kamarupa was Harsha's **ally**; **Pulakesin II** defeated Harsha.
xa: Harsha freed his sister **Rajyashri**.
Shashanka's capital was **Karnasuvarna**; he cut the **Bodhi tree** at Gaya.
Alliance: Harsha + **Bhaskaravarman** vs **Shashanka**.

67.s: Harshavardhana is also known by which of the following titles?
67.x: Harsha bore the title Siladitya (APPSC G1 2012) and also Sakalottarapathanatha, lord of all North India. Vikramaditya was the title of Chandragupta II, Paramesvara was taken by Pulakesin II after defeating Harsha, and Shakraditya was Kumaragupta I.
67.tq: Harsha = Siladitya
xs: Harsha bore the title **Siladitya** — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC G1 2012).
His other title was **Sakalottarapathanatha** (lord of all North India).
**Paramesvara** was taken by **Pulakesin II** after defeating Harsha.
xa: Harsha's reign: **606-647 CE**.
Pulakesin's victory is recorded in the **Aihole inscription** (**634 CE**).
The **Banskhera** inscription bears **Harsha's signature**.

67.s: The Vardhana dynasty of Thanesar, to which Harsha belonged, is also named after its founder. Who was he?
67.x: The line is called the Pushyabhuti dynasty after its founder Pushyabhuti (BPSC 2022 key); its rulers were once Gupta feudatories. Grahavarman was a Maukhari, Vindhyashakti founded the Vakatakas, and Bhaskaravarman ruled Kamarupa.
67.tq: Pushyabhuti = Vardhana line of Thanesar
xs: The line is named after its founder **Pushyabhuti** — option **(1)** is correct (BPSC 2022 key).
**Grahavarman** was a **Maukhari**; **Vindhyashakti** founded the **Vakatakas**; **Bhaskaravarman** ruled **Kamarupa**.
xa: The Pushyabhutis were once **Gupta feudatories**.
Some notes name **Naravardhana** (late **5th/early 6th c.**) as founder.
Some call **Prabhakaravardhana** the founder — he was the first great ruler.

67.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the political result of Harsha's conflict with Dhruvasena II of Valabhi?
o: Dhruvasena II defeated Harsha and annexed Kannauj.
Dhruvasena II succeeded Sasanka in Gauda.
Dhruvasena II became Harsha's vassal and married Harsha's daughter.
Dhruvasena II became the ruler of Kamarupa under Harsha's protection.
67.x: Dhruvasena II of Valabhi was made a vassal of Harsha and married Harsha's daughter.
67.tq: Identify the specific result of a campaign instead of confusing it with Harsha's other conquests.
xs: **Dhruvasena II** became Harsha's **vassal** and married **Harsha's daughter** — option **(3)** is correct.
Dhruvasena II (Dhruvabhata) ruled **Valabhi** (Maitrakas) and became Harsha's **son-in-law**.
**Gauda** was Sasanka's; **Kamarupa** was Bhaskaravarman's — not Dhruvasena's.
xa: ⚠ **Bhaskaravarman** = ally; **Dhruvasena II** = vassal and son-in-law; **Pulakesin II** = defeated Harsha.
After Shashanka's death Harsha took **Magadha** and Gauda.
**Nepal** and **Kashmir** accepted Harsha's overlordship / sent tribute.

67.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Kingdom or ruler)
a. Maukharis
b. Gauda
c. Kamarupa
d. Valabhi

List-II (Association)
i. Bhaskaravarman
 ii. Dhruvasena II
 iii. Grahavarman
 iv. Sasanka

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
67.x: The Maukharis were associated with Grahavarman, Gauda with Sasanka, Kamarupa with Bhaskaravarman and Valabhi with Dhruvasena II.
67.tq: Begin with the distinctive Kamarupa–Bhaskaravarman pair and complete the matching.
xs: Correct code: **a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** — option **(1)**.
**Maukharis** — **Grahavarman**; **Gauda** — **Sasanka**.
**Kamarupa** — **Bhaskaravarman**; **Valabhi** — **Dhruvasena II**.
xa: Sasanka's capital = **Karnasuvarna**.
Bhaskaravarman was Harsha's **ally** (BPSC 2024).
Grahavarman was killed by **Devagupta of Malwa**.

67.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship of the listed rulers or kingdoms with Harsha?
o: Grahavarman of Kannauj was Harsha’s ally and survived the Malwa attack.
Sasanka of Gauda was Harsha’s enemy and killed Rajyavardhana.
Dhruvasena II of Valabhi was Harsha’s principal enemy.
Bhaskaravarman of Kamarupa killed Rajyavardhana and opposed Harsha.
67.x: Sasanka of Gauda was Harsha’s enemy and was responsible for the killing of Rajyavardhana. Grahavarman was Harsha’s brother-in-law, Bhaskaravarman was his ally and Dhruvasena II was his vassal and son-in-law.
67.tq: Use the ruler–relationship trap by checking who was ally, enemy, vassal or victim.
xs: **Sasanka of Gauda** was Harsha's enemy and **killed Rajyavardhana** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Grahavarman** was killed by **Devagupta of Malwa** — he did not survive.
**Dhruvasena II** was a **vassal and son-in-law**; **Bhaskaravarman** was an **ally**.
xa: Sasanka also **cut the Bodhi tree** at Gaya and was **driven from Kannauj**.
Harsha's real check came from **Pulakesin II** on the **Narmada**.
Sasanka's capital = **Karnasuvarna**.

67.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Harsha allied with Bhaskaravarman against Shashanka.
2. Shashanka's capital was Karnasuvarna.
3. Bhaskaravarman ruled Gauda (Bengal).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
67.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Bhaskaravarman ruled Kamarupa (Assam); Gauda was Shashanka's kingdom. So A is incomplete and C and D include statement 3.
67.tq: Kamarupa = Bhaskaravarman (ally); Gauda = Shashanka (rival, Karnasuvarna).
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: Harsha allied with **Bhaskaravarman** against **Shashanka** — correct.
Statement 2: Shashanka's capital was **Karnasuvarna** — correct.
Statement 3: **Bhaskaravarman** ruled **Kamarupa (Assam)**, not Gauda — wrong.
xa: **Gauda (Bengal)** was Sasanka's kingdom.
After Sasanka's death Harsha took **Magadha** and Gauda.
Sasanka **killed Rajyavardhana**.

67.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Harsha's relations with neighbouring regions:
1. Nepal and Kashmir acknowledged his overlordship or sent tribute.
2. Kamarupa acknowledged his authority.
3. Pulakesin II of Badami was defeated and made a vassal by Harsha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: Nepal, Kashmir and Kamarupa acknowledged Harsha's authority or sent tribute. Pulakesin II defeated Harsha on the Narmada and was not made his vassal.
67.tq: Use the reversed-result trap in the Harsha–Pulakesin conflict.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Nepal** and **Kashmir** accepted overlordship / sent tribute — correct.
Statement 2: **Kamarupa** acknowledged Harsha — correct.
Statement 3: **Pulakesin II** **defeated Harsha** — he was never his vassal — wrong.
xa: Pulakesin's victory is recorded in the **Aihole inscription**; he took the title **Paramesvara**.
**Valabhi** (Dhruvasena II) was a vassal.
Harsha's empire: Rajasthan, Punjab, UP, Bihar, Orissa.

67.s:
Assertion (A): Harsha's southward expansion was checked on the Narmada.
Reason (R): Pulakesin II of the Badami Chalukyas defeated Harsha.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
67.x: Both statements are true, and Pulakesin II's victory explains why Harsha's southward advance stopped at the Narmada.
67.tq: Test whether the military result directly explains the geographical limit of expansion.
xs: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A — option **(1)**.
**Pulakesin II** of the **Badami Chalukyas** defeated Harsha, stopping him at the **Narmada**.
The **Aihole inscription** records it; Hiuen Tsang confirms.
xa: Pulakesin took the title **Paramesvara**.
Date: some notes say **637 AD**, but the Aihole inscription is of **634 CE** → war c. **618-619 CE**.
Hiuen Tsang praised **Pulakesin II** along with Harsha and **Narasimhavarman**.

67.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the nature of Harshacharita?
o: A Sanskrit romantic comedy by Harsha
A hymn to the Sun composed by Mayura
67.x: Harshacharita, written by Banabhatta, is a semi-historical biography of Harsha and an important literary source for his reign.
67.tq: Distinguish a work about the ruler from works written by the ruler.
xs: **Harshacharita** is a **semi-historical biography** of Harsha — option **(1)** is correct.
It was written by court poet **Banabhatta** and is the chief literary source for the reign.
**Ratnavali / Priyadarshika** are romantic comedies, **Nagananda** a Buddhist play — all by Harsha; the Sun hymn is **Mayura**'s.
xa: Bana also wrote **Kadambari**, completed by son **Bhushanabhatta**.
"Not written by Harsha" = **Harshacharita** (APPSC G2 2025).
Bana's village: **Pritikuta** on the **Sona** river.

67.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
67.x: Nagananda is a Buddhist-themed play centred on self-sacrifice. Ratnavali and Priyadarshika are romantic comedies, while Harshacharita is Banabhatta's biography of Harsha.
67.tq: Match each work with its literary nature before eliminating swapped descriptions.
xs: **Nagananda — Buddhist theme of self-sacrifice** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Harshacharita** is Bana's **biography**, not a comedy.
**Kadambari** is a **prose romance**, not a hymn; **Ratnavali** is Harsha's **romantic comedy**, not a biography.
xa: Harsha's three dramas: **Ratnavali**, **Priyadarshika**, **Nagananda**.
**Mayura** wrote **Suryashataka** (hymn to the Sun).
**Matanga Divakara** was also a court poet of Harsha.

67.s: Who completed Banabhatta's Kadambari?
67.x: Kadambari, a prose romance begun by Banabhatta, was completed by his son Bhushanabhatta.
67.tq: Use the author–work–successor relationship rather than confusing court poets.
xs: **Bhushanabhatta**, Bana's son, completed **Kadambari** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Mayura** and **Matanga Divakara** were other court poets; **Silabhadra** headed **Nalanda**.
xa: Kadambari is among the world's **earliest Sanskrit novels** (APPSC G1 2018).
Bana also wrote **Harshacharita**.
Bana was Harsha's **Asthana Kavi**.

67.s:
Consider the following statements regarding sources for the reign of Harsha:
1. The Madhuban plate is useful for establishing chronology.
2. The Sonpat seal is an inscriptional source for Harsha's reign.
3. The Banskhera inscription bears Harsha's signature.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: The Madhuban plate, Sonpat seal and Banskhera inscription are all sources for Harsha's reign; the Banskhera record is noted for bearing Harsha's signature.
67.tq: Check each source independently before selecting the combined code.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: the **Madhuban plate** (land grant) is used for **chronology** — correct.
Statement 2: the **Sonpat seal** is an epigraphic source — correct.
Statement 3: the **Banskhera** inscription bears **Harsha's signature** — correct.
xa: The **Aihole** inscription (Chalukya) records Harsha's defeat on the **Narmada**.
Literary source: **Harshacharita**; foreign account: **Si-Yu-Ki**.
Hiuen Tsang visited Harsha's court in **631 CE**.

67.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Source)
A. Harshacharita
B. Si-Yu-Ki
C. Banskhera inscription
D. Madhuban plate

List-II (Type or feature)
1. Foreign account
2. Epigraphic land grant and chronology
3. Literary Sanskrit biography
4. Epigraphic record bearing Harsha's signature

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
67.x: Harshacharita is a literary Sanskrit biography, Si-Yu-Ki is a foreign account, Banskhera bears Harsha's signature and the Madhuban plate is an epigraphic land-grant record useful for chronology.
67.tq: Start with the distinctive Banskhera and Madhuban clues, then complete the source classification.
xs: Correct code: **A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2** — option **(1)**.
**Harshacharita** — literary Sanskrit biography; **Si-Yu-Ki** — foreign account (Hiuen Tsang).
**Banskhera** — bears **Harsha's signature**; **Madhuban plate** — land grant and **chronology**.
xa: The **Sonpat seal** is another epigraphic source.
The **Aihole** inscription records the defeat on the Narmada.
Si-Yu-Ki = "**Records of the Western World**".

67.s: Which of the following is an epigraphic source associated with the defeat of Harsha on the Narmada?
67.x: The Aihole inscription is a Chalukyan epigraphic source recording Pulakesin II's victory over Harsha on the Narmada.
67.tq: Link the historical event to the source category and political issuer.
xs: The **Aihole inscription** of **Pulakesin II** records Harsha's defeat on the **Narmada** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Madhuban plate** = land grant / chronology; **Harshacharita** = Bana's biography; **Si-Yu-Ki** = Hiuen Tsang's account.
xa: The Aihole inscription is of **634 CE**; the war is placed c. **618-619 CE**.
Pulakesin took the title **Paramesvara**.
The **Banskhera** inscription bears Harsha's signature.

67.s: Which one of the following works was NOT written by Harshavardhana?
67.x: Harshacharita, the semi-historical biography of Harsha, was written by his court poet Banabhatta (APPSC G2 2025). Ratnavali and Priyadarshika (romantic comedies) and Nagananda (a Buddhist play on self-sacrifice) are the three Sanskrit dramas written by Harsha himself.
67.tq: Harsha wrote 3 plays; Bana wrote Harshacharita and Kadambari
xs: **Harshacharita** was not written by Harsha — option **(4)** is the answer (APPSC G2 2025).
It was written by his court poet **Banabhatta**.
**Ratnavali**, **Priyadarshika** (romantic comedies) and **Nagananda** (Buddhist play) are Harsha's own.
xa: Bana also wrote **Kadambari**.
Bana is paired with **Harsha**, not the Guptas or Kanishka.
**Mayura** wrote **Suryashataka**.

67.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Matanga Divakara — Court poet of Harsha
67.x: Vakpatiraja was associated with Yashovarman of Kannauj, not Harsha's court. Banabhatta, Mayura and Matanga Divakara were associated with Harsha's court.
67.tq: Find the swapped patron–poet association.
xs: **Vakpatiraja — court poet of Harsha** is wrong — option **(1)** is the answer.
**Vakpatiraja** belonged to **Yashovarman** of Kannauj.
**Matanga Divakara**, **Mayura** (Suryashataka) and **Banabhatta** (Harshacharita) were Harsha's court poets.
xa: **Padmagupta** is another distractor — he belongs to the **Paramaras**.
Bana was Harsha's **Asthana Kavi**.
Bana's village: **Pritikuta** on the **Sona**.

67.s: The Suryashataka, a hymn dedicated to the Sun, was composed by which court poet of Harsha?
67.x: Mayura, a court poet of Harsha, composed Suryashataka, a hymn to the Sun.
67.tq: Separate the court poet's own work from Banabhatta's literary works.
xs: **Mayura** composed the **Suryashataka** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Banabhatta** wrote Harshacharita and Kadambari; **Matanga Divakara** was another court poet; **Padmagupta** belongs to the **Paramaras**.
xa: ⚠ **Harsha** = Ratnavali, Priyadarshika, Nagananda; **Bana** = Harshacharita, Kadambari; **Mayura** = Suryashataka.
**Vakpatiraja** was the poet of **Yashovarman** of Kannauj.

67.s: Banabhatta's native village was located on the bank of which river?
67.x: Banabhatta's native village was Pritikuta, situated on the Sona River.
67.tq: Test the place–river association directly.
xs: Bana's native village **Pritikuta** was on the **Sona** river — option **(1)** is correct.
Banabhatta was Harsha's court poet (**Asthana Kavi**).
xa: He wrote **Harshacharita** and **Kadambari** (APPSC G1 2018).
Kadambari was completed by his son **Bhushanabhatta**.

67.s: Kadambari, regarded as one of the earliest Sanskrit novels, was written by:
67.x: Banabhatta, Harsha's court poet, wrote Kadambari, one of the earliest Sanskrit novels, as well as Harshacharita.
67.tq: Bana = Harshacharita + Kadambari (biography + novel).
xs: **Banabhatta** wrote **Kadambari** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is a **prose romance** and among the **earliest Sanskrit novels** (APPSC G1 2018).
**Mayura** wrote Suryashataka; **Vakpatiraja** belonged to **Yashovarman**.
xa: Kadambari was completed by Bana's son **Bhushanabhatta**.
Bana also wrote **Harshacharita**, the chief literary source for Harsha's reign.
**Matanga Divakara** was another court poet of Harsha.

67.s: The poet Padmagupta is associated with which dynasty?
67.x: Padmagupta was associated with the Paramaras, not with Harsha's court; Vakpatiraja was associated with Yashovarman of Kannauj.
67.tq: Padmagupta - Paramara (P-P).
xs: **Padmagupta** is associated with the **Paramaras** — option **(1)** is correct.
He is a distractor in Harsha questions — not a Pushyabhuti court poet.
xa: **Vakpatiraja** = poet of **Yashovarman** of Kannauj.
Harsha's court poets: **Banabhatta**, **Mayura**, **Matanga Divakara**.

67.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Kannauj assembly from the Prayag assembly?
o: Kannauj was held every five years for charity, whereas Prayag honoured Hiuen Tsang.
Prayag was a one-time debate attended only by Buddhist scholars.
Kannauj honoured Hiuen Tsang and promoted Mahayana, whereas Prayag was associated with charity.
Both assemblies were held at the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna.
67.x: The Kannauj assembly honoured Hiuen Tsang and propagated Mahayana, while the Prayag assembly was primarily a charitable gathering held periodically.
67.tq: Split the alternatives by purpose and frequency before considering location.
xs: **Kannauj** honoured **Hiuen Tsang** and spread **Mahayana**; **Prayag** was for **charity** — option **(3)** is correct.
Kannauj was a **one-time** assembly (**643 CE**); Prayag was held **every five years**.
Only Prayag was at the **Ganga-Yamuna confluence**; Prayag had representatives of **all religions**.
xa: Kannauj attendance: **20 kings**, 1000 Nalanda scholars, 3000 Brahmins and Jains.
At Prayag, Harsha gave away his **whole treasury**, keeping only personal clothes.
Prayag is called the **Moksha Parishad**.

67.s: The Kannauj assembly convened by Harshavardhana was held in
67.x: The Kannauj assembly is dated to 643 CE.
67.tq: Distinguish the assembly year from Hiuen Tsang’s court date and Harsha’s other chronological markers.
xs: The Kannauj assembly was held in **643 CE** — option **(3)** is correct.
**605** = Yashomati's sati; **631** = Hiuen Tsang at Harsha's court; **647** = Harsha's death.
xa: It honoured **Hiuen Tsang** and propagated **Mahayana**.
It lasted **23 days** (some notes: 21-day debate) and saw an **assassination attempt** on Harsha.
⚠ **Kannauj** = 643, one-time; **Prayag** = every five years, charity.

67.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kannauj assembly:
1. It was held to honour Hiuen Tsang and propagate Mahayana doctrine.
2. It lasted for 23 days according to the stated APP account.
3. It ended without any disturbance or attempt on Harsha’s life.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: The assembly honoured Hiuen Tsang, propagated Mahayana and lasted 23 days in the stated account. It was followed by violence, arson and an attempt on Harsha’s life, so statement 3 is false.
67.tq: Identify the negative event that reverses an otherwise correct account of the assembly.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: it honoured **Hiuen Tsang** and propagated **Mahayana** — correct.
Statement 2: it lasted **23 days** — correct.
Statement 3: there was **violence, arson** and an **assassination attempt** on Harsha — wrong.
xa: Attendance: **20 kings** (some notes: kings of **18 countries**).
Also 1000 **Nalanda** scholars and 3000 Hinayanists/Mahayanists.
Figures on the Kannauj assembly **differ across sources**.

67.s: The Prayag assembly, also known as the Moksha Parishad, was held at
o: The confluence of the Narmada and Tapti
Kannauj on the banks of the Ganga
The confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna
67.x: The Prayag assembly was held at the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna at Prayag, also known as Allahabad.
67.tq: Use the location-specific geographical clue to distinguish the two assemblies.
xs: The Prayag assembly met at the **confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna** — option **(4)** is correct.
Prayag = **Allahabad**; the assembly was called the **Moksha Parishad**.
**Kannauj** hosted the separate **643 CE** assembly.
xa: Held **every five years**; a charity (dana) assembly.
Hiuen Tsang attended the **sixth** such assembly.
Buddha, Sun and Shiva were worshipped on **successive days**.

67.s:
With reference to the Prayag assembly, consider the following statements:
