89.tq: Test the alternate-name trap by separating titles of closely related Chola temples.
xs: **Brihadeeswara** (Rajarajeshwara) is also called **"Dakshina Meru"**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**Airavatesvara** (Darasuram) and **Kampaharesvara** (Tribhuvanam) are separate temples.
xa: It was completed by **Rajaraja I** in **1010 CE**.
The great **Nandi** was **added later by the Nayakas**.
Its frescoes show **Shiva as Tripurantaka**.

89.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Brihadeeswara Temple:
1. Its vimana is about 216 feet high.
2. Its capstone is monolithic and weighs approximately 80 tonnes.
3. The entire vimana was constructed exclusively of brick and mortar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
89.x: The vimana is about 216 feet high and has a monolithic capstone of approximately 80 tonnes. Statement 3 is false because the vimana, like the whole temple, is built of granite, not brick and mortar.
89.tq: Split the material claim from the height and weight figures to identify the overstatement.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the vimana is **216 ft** high.
Statement 2 is correct: the **monolithic capstone** weighs about **80 tonnes**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the capstone sits on a **granite** vimana, not brick and mortar.
xa: ⚠ **216 ft** = Thanjavur; **180 ft** = Gangaikondacholapuram.
Completed by **Rajaraja I** in **1010 CE**.
The shikhara at Thanjavur is **monolithic**.

89.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
89.x: Koranganatha, an early Chola structural temple, is located at Srinivasanallur. Airavatesvara is at Darasuram and Kampaharesvara is at Tribhuvanam.
89.tq: Start from the sure site–temple pair and eliminate swapped locations.
xs: **Koranganatha** = **Srinivasanallur** is correctly matched, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Airavatesvara** is at **Darasuram**, **Kampaharesvara** at **Tribhuvanam** and **Brihadeeswara** at **Thanjavur**.
xa: Koranganatha is an **early Chola** structural temple.
**Gangaikondacholapuram** was **Rajendra I's** temple and new capital.
**Kampaharesvara** is a **late Chola** temple of **Kulottunga III**.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about later Chola temples:
1. The Airavatesvara temple at Darasuram was built by Rajaraja II.
2. The 'Musical Steps' and the stone chariot drawn by horses are features of the Kampaharesvara temple.
3. The Kampaharesvara temple at Tribhuvanam was built by Kulottunga III.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x: Statement 1 is correct: Rajaraja II built Airavatesvara at Darasuram. Statement 2 is wrong: the Musical Steps and horse-drawn stone chariot belong to Airavatesvara, not Kampaharesvara. Statement 3 is correct: Kulottunga III built Kampaharesvara at Tribhuvanam. So '1 only' misses 3, and options with 2 are wrong.
89.tq: Darasuram = Rajaraja II + Musical Steps; Tribhuvanam = Kulottunga III.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Rajaraja II** built **Airavatesvara**, Darasuram.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **"Musical Steps"** and the horse-drawn **stone chariot** belong to **Airavatesvara**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Kulottunga III** built **Kampaharesvara**, Tribhuvanam.
xa: Airavatesvara is called a **miniature masterpiece**.
Airavatesvara is one of the UNESCO **Great Living Chola Temples**.
The other two in the group are **Thanjavur** and **Gangaikondacholapuram**.

89.s: Gangaikondacholapuram was established by Rajendra I primarily to commemorate his
89.x: Rajendra I established Gangaikondacholapuram as a new capital to mark his Ganga expedition.
89.tq: Match the ruler’s achievement with the purpose behind the foundation of the capital.
xs: **Rajendra I** founded **Gangaikondacholapuram** as his new capital to mark his **Ganga expedition**, so option **(2)** is correct.
His Southeast Asian expedition (**Kadaram**, **1025**) is a separate event, and **Chidambaram** was enlarged by Chola kings in general.
xa: Its vimana is **180 ft**, with a **concave curvilinear** ("feminine") profile.
The temple has a **bronze well** and a giant **Nandi**.
Rajendra I (**1012-1044**) was highlighted as its builder in **Aug 2025**.

89.s: Which of the following correctly describes the vimana of the Gangaikondacholapuram Temple?
o: It is 216 feet high and has a straight, rigid profile.
It is 216 feet high and has a circular plan.
It is 180 feet high and is entirely made of brick and mortar.
It is 180 feet high and has a concave curvilinear profile.
89.x: The vimana of Gangaikondacholapuram is about 180 feet high and has a curvilinear concave profile.
89.tq: Use the height and profile together to distinguish it from Thanjavur’s vimana.
xs: The Gangaikondacholapuram vimana is **180 ft** high with a **concave curvilinear** profile, so option **(4)** is correct.
**216 ft** is the **Thanjavur** vimana, which has a "masculine" bulk.
xa: ⚠ **216 ft – 180 ft** = **Thanjavur – Gangaikondacholapuram**.
Its profile is said to show "feminine" grace.
Built by **Rajendra I** to mark the **Ganga expedition**.

89.s:
Arrange the following monuments in chronological order of the sequence given:
A. Brihadeeswara Temple
B. Shore Temple
C. Gangaikondacholapuram Temple
D. Seven Pagodas of Mahabalipuram
89.x: The sequence is Seven Pagodas of Mahabalipuram, Shore Temple, Brihadeeswara, and Gangaikondacholapuram.
89.tq: Fix the Pallava pair first, then place the two later Chola monuments.
xs: The order is **Seven Pagodas** → **Shore Temple** → **Brihadeeswara** → **Gangaikondacholapuram** (D, B, A, C), so option **(1)** is correct (**UPPSC 2018**).
The first two are **Pallava** monuments at **Mahabalipuram**; the last two are Chola temples of **Rajaraja I** (**1010 CE**) and **Rajendra I**.
xa: "Seven Pagodas" = **"Sapta pagoda"** = the Pallava Mahabalipuram **rathas**.
This kind of question mixes **Pallava** and **Chola** monuments in a 4-temple order.
Later Chola: **Airavatesvara** (Rajaraja II), **Kampaharesvara** (Kulottunga III).

89.s: The Chit Sabha, containing carvings of 108 classical dance poses, is associated with the
89.x: The Chit Sabha of the Thillai Nataraja Temple at Chidambaram contains carvings of 108 classical dance poses.
89.tq: Identify the shrine through its distinctive dance-related architectural feature.
xs: The **Chit Sabha** (Hall of Consciousness), with **108 classical dance poses**, is in the **Thillai Nataraja temple, Chidambaram**, so option **(4)** is correct.
The temple is a shrine of **Shiva as Nataraja**, enlarged by **Chola kings**.
xa: ⚠ Chidambaram is **not** among the UNESCO **Great Living Chola Temples**.
**APPSC-GS 2018**: Chidambaram, Thanjavur and Gangaikondacholapuram were built by the **Cholas**.
**Airavatesvara** has the **"Musical Steps"**.

89.s: Which of the following statements about the great Nandi at Thanjavur is correct?
o: It is the original monolithic capstone of the vimana.
It was constructed by Rajendra I to mark the Ganga expedition.
It was added later by the Nayakas.
It was installed by Kulottunga III at Tribhuvanam.
89.x: The great Nandi at Thanjavur was added at a later stage by the Nayakas.
89.tq: Watch for the chronology trap separating the original Chola construction from later additions.
xs: The great **Nandi** at Thanjavur was **added later by the Nayakas**, so option **(3)** is correct.
The capstone is a separate **monolith** of about **80 tonnes**. **Rajendra I's** temple is at Gangaikondacholapuram, and **Kulottunga III's** is at Tribhuvanam.
xa: Thanjavur was completed by **Rajaraja I** in **1010 CE**.
**Gangaikondacholapuram** also has a giant **Nandi**.
Thanjavur has **frescoes** in the dark ambulatory passage.

89.s:
Which of the following constitutes the UNESCO group known as the ‘Great Living Chola Temples’?
1. Thanjavur
2. Gangaikondacholapuram
3. Darasuram
4. Chidambaram

91.x: Jaitugi killed Rudradeva, held Ganapatideva captive, released him in 1199, and married Somaladevi to him.

xs: All three statements are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Jaitugi (Jaitrapala)** killed Kakatiya **Rudradeva**; **Mahadeva** also died fighting him.
He held **Ganapatideva** captive, released him in **1199**, and married his daughter **Somaladevi** to him.
xa: The **Paithan copper plate** of Ramachandra confirms Jaitugi killed Rudradeva and imprisoned Ganapatideva.
Court poet **Hemadri** claimed Jaitugi captured and **sacrificed** Rudra.
Ganapatideva was released as a **counterweight** to Hoysala **Veera Ballala**.

91.s: Which Yadava ruler was known as the greatest of the Yadava rulers and assumed the title ‘Teluguraya Sthapanacharya’?
91.x:
Singhana II, who ruled from 1200 to 1247, was regarded as the greatest Yadava ruler and bore the title ‘Teluguraya Sthapanacharya’.
⚠ Sources differ: Singhana II's reign is given as 1200-1247 in some sources and c.1210-1246 in others. This key follows the notes.
91.tq: Link the title with the ruler who held it.
xs: **Singhana II** (**1200-1247**), the **greatest Yadava**, took the title **'Teluguraya Sthapanacharya'**, so option **(4)** is correct.
The title means **installer of the Telugu king**.
**Bhillama V** founded Devagiri, **Jaitugi** killed Rudradeva, and **Mahadeva** was repulsed by Rudramadevi.
xa: Singhana II **defeated the Hoysalas**.
His court musician **Sarngadeva** wrote the **Sangita Ratnakara**.
His son **Sarangapanideva** later served at **Rudramadevi's** court.

91.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ramachandra — Defeated by Delhi forces in 1295
Shankaradeva — Founded Devagiri as the Yadava capital
91.x: Devagiri was founded as the Yadava capital by Bhillama V, not Shankaradeva. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
91.tq: Find the wrong ruler–achievement association.
xs: **Shankaradeva** did not found Devagiri: **Bhillama V** did. So option **(4)** is the wrong pair.
The other pairs are correct: **Ramachandra** was defeated by Delhi in **1295**; **Krishna** fought the Hoysalas; **Mahadeva** was defeated by the Hoysalas.
xa: **Shankaradeva** (**1311-1313**) died in **Malik Kafur's** invasion.
**Harapaladeva** (**1313-1317**) died in **Mubarak Khalji's** invasion, ending the kingdom.
After **1295**, Ramachandra became a **feudatory** of Delhi.

91.s:
Arrange the following Yadava rulers in chronological order of their reigns:
A. Mahadeva
B. Singhana II
C. Ramachandra
D. Krishna
91.x: Singhana II ruled from 1200, followed by Krishna, Mahadeva and Ramachandra.
91.tq: Place rulers in sequence using the given reign periods.
xs: The order is **Singhana II** (**1200-1247**) → **Krishna** (**1246-1261**) → **Mahadeva** (**1261-1271**) → **Ramachandra** (**1271-1311**), i.e. B, D, A, C. So option **(1)** is correct.
Krishna's reign overlaps Singhana's last year, so **Singhana II** comes first.
xa: Before Singhana: **Bhillama V**, then **Jaitugi**.
After Ramachandra: **Shankaradeva** (**1311-1313**), then **Harapaladeva** (**1313-1317**).
**Hemadri** served **Mahadeva and Ramachandra** as **Shrikaranadhipa**.

91.s: Which Yadava ruler’s attack on the Kakatiyas was repulsed by Rudramadevi?
91.x: Rudramadevi repulsed the attack launched by Yadava ruler Mahadeva against the Kakatiyas.
91.tq: Identify the ruler involved in the specific military encounter.
xs: The Yadava ruler **Mahadeva** attacked the Kakatiyas and was **repulsed by Rudramadevi**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Jaitugi** killed **Rudradeva**, and **Ramachandra** was defeated by Delhi in **1295**.
xa: Mahadeva (**1261-1271**) was also defeated by the **Hoysalas**.
AP angle: **Rudrama beat Mahadeva**.
**Hemadri** served Mahadeva as **Shrikaranadhipa**.

91.s: Which of the following correctly represents the final Yadava rulers and the circumstances of their deaths?
o: Shankaradeva — Malik Kafur’s invasion; Harapaladeva — Mubarak Khalji’s invasion
Shankaradeva — Alauddin Khalji’s first raid; Harapaladeva — Veera Ballala II’s attack
Shankaradeva — Rudramadevi’s attack; Harapaladeva — Jaitugi’s invasion
Shankaradeva — Muhammad bin Tughlaq’s invasion; Harapaladeva — Malik Kafur’s campaign
91.x: Shankaradeva died during Malik Kafur’s invasion in 1313, and Harapaladeva was killed during Mubarak Khalji’s invasion in 1317–18.
91.tq: Match each ruler with the invading commander responsible for his death.
xs: **Shankaradeva** died in **Malik Kafur's** invasion, and **Harapaladeva** died in **Mubarak Khalji's** invasion, so option **(1)** is correct.
Harapaladeva's death (**1317-18**) marked the **end of the Yadava kingdom**.
xa: Shankaradeva reigned **1311-1313**; Harapaladeva **1313-1317**.
The first invasion (**1295**) was by **Alauddin Khalji** for **Jalaluddin**.
Kafur's earlier **1307-08** campaign made **Ramachandra** submit.

91.s: Which statement about Hemadri’s account of Kakatiya Rudra is correct?
o: He claimed that Jaitugi captured and sacrificed Rudra.
He stated that Rudra founded the Hemadpanti style.
He recorded that Rudra served as Shrikaranadhipa.
He claimed that Rudra captured and sacrificed Jaitugi.
91.x: The Yadava court poet Hemadri claimed that Jaitugi captured and sacrificed Kakatiya Rudra.
91.tq: Watch for the swapped subject and object in a historical claim.
xs: Court poet **Hemadri** claimed that **Jaitugi captured and sacrificed** Kakatiya Rudra, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Hemadri** himself is credited with the **Hemadpanti** style and served as **Shrikaranadhipa**. Neither is Rudra's.
xa: The **Paithan copper plate** confirms Jaitugi killed **Rudradeva**.
Hemadri wrote the **Chaturvarga Chintamani**.
Hemadri was a **minister** of the Devagiri Yadavas (**APHQ**).

91.s: Jaitugi released Ganapatideva primarily because he intended to
o: make him the successor to the Yadava throne
secure control over the Delhi Sultanate
appoint him as the governor of Devagiri
use him as a counterweight to Hoysala Veera Ballala’s advance
91.x: Jaitugi released Ganapatideva (1199) to use him as a counterweight to Veera Ballala’s push into the Krishna–Tungabhadra region.
91.tq: Infer the political purpose behind the release of a captive.
xs: **Ganapatideva** was released as a **counterweight** to Hoysala **Veera Ballala's** push into the **Krishna-Tungabhadra** region, so option **(4)** is correct.
He was released in **1199** and married to **Somaladevi**.
xa: **Jaitugi** had killed Kakatiya **Rudradeva**.
**Singhana II** styled himself installer of the Telugu king (**Teluguraya Sthapanacharya**).
**Veera Ballala II** had defeated **Bhillama V**.

91.s: Who was Sarangapanideva in relation to the Yadava–Kakatiya political context?
o: Hemadri’s teacher who composed the Dnyaneshwari
Singhana II’s son who later served at Rudramadevi’s court
Ganapatideva’s son who defeated Singhana II
91.x: Sarangapanideva, the son of Singhana II, later served at the court of Rudramadevi.
91.tq: Identify the person through a family and court association.
xs: **Sarangapanideva**, son of **Singhana II**, later served at **Rudramadevi's** court, so option **(3)** is correct.
**Devagiri** was founded by **Bhillama V**, and the **Dnyaneshwari** was written by **Dnyaneshwar**.
xa: Singhana II = the **greatest Yadava**.
He **defeated the Hoysalas**.
**Rudramadevi** repulsed **Mahadeva's** attack.

91.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Sarngadeva — Music
2. Changadeva — Astronomy
3. Changadeva — Grandson of Bhaskaracharya
4. Sarngadeva — Founder of the school at Patan for teaching Bhaskara’s works
91.x: Sarngadeva was associated with music. Changadeva was an astronomer, grandson of Bhaskaracharya, and established the school at Patan; statement 4 wrongly assigns that act to Sarngadeva.
91.tq: Separate closely associated scholars by their disciplines and deeds.
xs: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Sarngadeva** = **music** (court musician of Singhana II); **Changadeva** = **astronomer**, grandson of **Bhaskaracharya**.
Pair 4 is wrong: the school at **Patan** to teach Bhaskara's works was **Changadeva's**.
xa: Sarngadeva wrote the **Sangita Ratnakara**.
⚠ **Sangita Ratnakara** = **Sarngadeva**; **Chaturvarga Chintamani** = **Hemadri**.
**Lilacharitra** (by **Mhaimbhat**) is the first Marathi prose work.

91.s: Who wrote the Sangita Ratnakara?
91.x: Sangita Ratnakara was written by Sarngadeva, the court musician of Singhana II.
91.tq: Match the classical work with its author.
xs: **Sarngadeva**, court musician of **Singhana II**, wrote the **Sangita Ratnakara**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Changadeva** was an astronomer, **Hemadri** wrote the **Chaturvarga Chintamani** and **Dnyaneshwar** wrote the **Dnyaneshwari**.
xa: It is the basic text for both **Hindustani** and **Carnatic** music.
⚠ Don't confuse **Sarngadeva** (music) with **Sarangapanideva** (Singhana's son).
**Singhana II** reigned **1200-1247**.

91.s: Sarngadeva wrote the Sangita Ratnakara while serving as the court musician of
91.x: Sarngadeva was the court musician of Singhana II.
91.tq: Use the author–patron relationship rather than the work title alone.
xs: **Sarngadeva** was the court musician of **Singhana II**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Hemadri** served **Mahadeva** and **Ramachandra**. **Bhillama V** was the founder of Devagiri.
xa: His **Sangita Ratnakara** is a basic text for **Hindustani + Carnatic** music.
Singhana II took the title **Teluguraya Sthapanacharya**.
Singhana II **defeated the Hoysalas**.

91.s: The Sangita Ratnakara is regarded as a basic text for
91.x: The Sangita Ratnakara is considered a basic text for both Hindustani and Carnatic music.
91.tq: Distinguish a shared foundational text from an exclusive tradition.
xs: The **Sangita Ratnakara** is a basic text for **both Hindustani and Carnatic** music, so option **(3)** is correct.
It was written by **Sarngadeva**, court musician of **Singhana II**.
xa: Astronomer **Changadeva** set up a school at **Patan**.
**Hemadri's Chaturvarga Chintamani** is a **Sanskrit** encyclopaedia.
The **Dnyaneshwari** is a **Marathi** Gita commentary.

91.s: Hemadri served as Shrikaranadhipa under which Yadava rulers?
91.x: Hemadri served Mahadeva and Ramachandra as Shrikaranadhipa, the head of the secretariat or records.
91.tq: Associate an office-holder with the rulers under whom he served.
xs: **Hemadri** served **Mahadeva and Ramachandra** as **Shrikaranadhipa**, head of the secretariat/records, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Singhana II's** court is linked with **Sarngadeva**, not Hemadri.
xa: Hemadri wrote the **Chaturvarga Chintamani** (**APPSC G2 2000**).
He is credited with the **Hemadpanti** style.
Mahadeva reigned **1261-1271**; Ramachandra **1271-1311**.

91.s: Hemadri’s Chaturvarga Chintamani is best described as a Sanskrit work dealing with
o: dharma, rituals, charity, pilgrimage and vratas
91.x: Chaturvarga Chintamani is a Sanskrit encyclopaedia dealing with dharma, rituals, charity, pilgrimage and vratas.
91.tq: Identify the subject coverage of the named work.
xs: The **Chaturvarga Chintamani** is a **Sanskrit encyclopaedia** on **dharma, rituals, charity, pilgrimage and vratas**, so option **(1)** is correct (**APPSC G2 2000**).
Music was **Sarngadeva's** field (**Sangita Ratnakara**), and astronomy was **Changadeva's**.
xa: Its author **Hemadri** was a scholar, administrator and minister.
He served as **Shrikaranadhipa**.
He is credited with the **Hemadpanti** temple style.

91.s: Which architectural style is traditionally credited to Hemadri?
91.x: Hemadri is credited with the Hemadpanti style of temple architecture.
91.tq: Match the architect-scholar with the architectural style.
xs: **Hemadri** is credited with the **Hemadpanti** style of temple architecture, so option **(4)** is correct (**APHQ**).
**Nagara**, **Vesara** and **Dravida** are the three broad temple styles. None is credited to Hemadri.
xa: Hemadpanti uses local **black basalt**.
Its dressed stones are **interlocked without mortar** (dry masonry).
Hemadri wrote the **Chaturvarga Chintamani**.

91.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Hemadpanti architecture:
1. It used local black basalt.
2. Its dressed stones were interlocked without mortar.
3. Its masonry is therefore described as dry masonry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
91.x: Hemadpanti construction used local black basalt and interlocked dressed stones without mortar, a technique known as dry masonry.
91.tq: Test material, construction method and technical description as one chain.
xs: All three statements are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
Hemadpanti temples used local **black basalt**.
Dressed stones were **interlocked without mortar**, i.e. **dry masonry**.
xa: The style is credited to **Hemadri**, minister of the Devagiri Yadavas.
Hemadri served as **Shrikaranadhipa**.
He wrote the **Chaturvarga Chintamani**.

91.s: The Dnyaneshwari, composed by the saint-poet Dnyaneshwar, is a
o: Marathi prose biography of Chakradhar Swami
91.x: Dnyaneshwari is Dnyaneshwar’s Marathi commentary on the Bhagavad Gita.
91.tq: Identify the language and subject of the literary work.
xs: The **Dnyaneshwari** is a **Marathi commentary on the Gita**, so option **(2)** is correct.
The Sanskrit encyclopaedia of rituals is **Hemadri's Chaturvarga Chintamani**.
xa: It was written in **1290** at **Nevasa**, in **Ramachandra's** reign.
Bhakti saints **Dnyaneshwar**, **Namdev**, **Tukaram** and **Ramdas** took Upanishad and Gita ideas into **Marathi**.
**Lilacharitra** is the first Marathi prose work.

91.s: In which year and at which place was the Dnyaneshwari written?
91.x: The Dnyaneshwari was written in 1290 at Nevasa during the reign of Ramachandra.
91.tq: Combine the year, place and reigning ruler associated with a work.
xs: The **Dnyaneshwari** was written in **1290** at **Nevasa**, so option **(2)** is correct.
It was written in **Ramachandra's** reign. **1187** is Devagiri's founding, and **1199** is Ganapatideva's release.
xa: It is a **Marathi** commentary on the Gita.
The Yadavas encouraged **Marathi** (**APHQ**).
**Chakradhar Swami** founded the **Mahanubhava** sect.

91.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Chakradhar Swami — Founder of the Mahanubhava sect
Dnyaneshwar — Founder of the Mahanubhava sect
91.x: The Mahanubhava sect was founded by Chakradhar Swami. Dnyaneshwar composed the Dnyaneshwari; he did not found the Mahanubhava sect.
91.tq: Separate the founder, author and literary work in a cultural movement.
xs: **Dnyaneshwar** did not found the **Mahanubhava** sect, so option **(4)** is the wrong pair.
The founder was **Chakradhar Swami**. Dnyaneshwar wrote the **Dnyaneshwari**.
The other pairs are correct: **Lilacharitra** = first Marathi prose work, by the Mahanubhava author **Mhaimbhat**.
xa: The Dnyaneshwari was written in **1290** at Nevasa.
Other Bhakti saints: **Namdev**, later **Tukaram** and **Ramdas**.
The Yadavas' mother tongue was **Marathi**.

91.s:
Consider the following statements about the Delhi Sultanate and the Yadavas:
1. In 1295, Alauddin Khalji, acting for Sultan Jalaluddin, defeated Ramachandra at Devagiri, and the Yadavas became Delhi vassals.
2. During Malik Kafur's campaign of 1307-08, Harapaladeva submitted and was taken to Delhi.
3. After 1323, Devagiri's vizier Malik Burhanuddin was given charge of conquered Andhra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
91.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 1295 raid by Alauddin (for Jalaluddin) made the Yadavas Delhi vassals. Statement 2 is wrong: in 1307-08 it was Ramachandra who submitted and was taken to Delhi; Harapaladeva was killed in Mubarak Khalji's invasion of 1317-18. Statement 3 is correct: Malik Burhanuddin got charge of Andhra after 1323. So options with 2 are wrong.
91.tq: 1295 Alauddin; 1307-08 Ramachandra submits; 1317-18 Harapaladeva killed.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: in **1295** **Alauddin Khalji** (for **Jalaluddin**) defeated **Ramachandra**, and the Yadavas became Delhi vassals.
Statement 2 is wrong: in **1307-08** it was **Ramachandra** who submitted. **Harapaladeva** was killed in **1317-18**.
Statement 3 is correct: after **1323** **Malik Burhanuddin** got charge of Andhra.
xa: The **1295** raid also took **Ellichpur**. Many texts date it **1296**.
After 1323, **Devagiri** was the Sultanate's **Deccan base**.
Harapaladeva was killed in **Mubarak Khalji's** invasion.

91.s: Which sequence correctly represents the major Delhi Sultanate interventions in the Yadava kingdom?
o: 1295 first invasion; 1307–08 Malik Kafur’s campaign; 1313 Shankaradeva killed; 1317–18 Harapaladeva killed
1307–08 first invasion; 1295 Shankaradeva killed; 1317–18 Malik Kafur’s campaign; 1313 kingdom founded
1313 first invasion; 1295 Harapaladeva killed; 1307–08 kingdom restored; 1317–18 Ramachandra crowned
1295 Harapaladeva killed; 1313 Malik Kafur appointed vizier; 1307–08 Devagiri founded; 1317–18 Ramachandra submits
91.x: The sequence was the 1295 first invasion, Malik Kafur’s 1307–08 campaign, Shankaradeva’s death in 1313, and Harapaladeva’s death in 1317–18.
91.tq: Use the dated invasion sequence from first defeat to dynastic extinction.
xs: The sequence is **1295** first invasion → **1307-08** Kafur's campaign → **1313** Shankaradeva killed → **1317-18** Harapaladeva killed, so option **(1)** is correct.
Shankaradeva (**1311-1313**) died in **Malik Kafur's** invasion, and Harapaladeva in **Mubarak Khalji's**.
xa: The 1295 invasion was the **first Muslim invasion of the South**.
In 1307-08 **Ramachandra** submitted and was taken to Delhi.
Devagiri was the first southern kingdom to fall, opening the road to **Warangal**, **Dwarasamudra** and **Madurai**.

91.s: Who led the first Muslim invasion of the South on Devagiri in 1295?
o: Alauddin Khalji on behalf of Sultan Jalaluddin
Muhammad bin Tughlaq on behalf of Alauddin Khalji
Malik Kafur on behalf of Alauddin Khalji
Mubarak Khalji on behalf of Ramachandra
91.x: In 1295, Alauddin Khalji, acting for Sultan Jalaluddin, defeated Ramachandra at Devagiri and took Ellichpur.
91.tq: Distinguish the commander, nominal sovereign and year of the first raid.
xs: **Alauddin Khalji**, acting for Sultan **Jalaluddin**, led the **1295** raid on **Devagiri**, so option **(1)** is correct.
He defeated **Ramachandra** and took **Ellichpur**. **Malik Kafur** came later, in **1307-08**.
xa: It was the **first Muslim invasion of the South**.
The Yadavas then became **Delhi vassals**.
Many texts date this raid **1296**.

91.s: During Malik Kafur’s campaign of 1307–08, which of the following occurred?
o: Ramachandra submitted and was taken to Delhi.
Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted his capital to Devagiri.
Bhillama founded Devagiri and defeated Veera Ballala II.
91.x: During the 1307–08 campaign, Ramachandra submitted to Malik Kafur and was taken to Delhi.
91.tq: Match the campaign year with its immediate event.
xs: In **1307-08** **Ramachandra** submitted to **Malik Kafur** and was taken to Delhi, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Harapaladeva** ended the dynasty only in **1317-18**, and **Bhillama V** founded Devagiri c. **1187**.
xa: Ramachandra had already become a **feudatory** after **1295**.
**Shankaradeva** died in Kafur's later invasion.
**Dnyaneshwari** (**1290**) was written in Ramachandra's reign.

91.s: After 1323, who was given charge of the conquered Andhra region?
o: Malik Burhanuddin, the vizier of Devagiri
Sarngadeva, the court musician of Singhana
91.x: After 1323, Devagiri’s vizier Malik Burhanuddin was placed in charge of conquered Andhra.
91.tq: Identify the administrator appointed over the conquered region.
xs: After **1323**, Devagiri's vizier **Malik Burhanuddin** was given charge of conquered **Andhra**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Hemadri** was the Yadava **Shrikaranadhipa**, **Sarngadeva** a musician and **Sarangapanideva** Singhana's son.
xa: Devagiri became the Sultanate's **Deccan base**.
Devagiri was the **first southern kingdom** to fall to Delhi.
The Yadava kingdom ended with **Harapaladeva** (**1317-18**).

91.s: The importance of Devagiri in the expansion of the Delhi Sultanate lay in the fact that it
o: was the first southern kingdom to fall to Delhi and opened routes towards major southern kingdoms
prevented all further Delhi campaigns into the Deccan
was the first capital established by the Hoysalas in northern India
served as the original capital of the Kakatiyas
91.x: Devagiri was the first southern kingdom to fall to Delhi, opening the road to Warangal, Dwarasamudra and Madurai.
91.tq: Apply the historical significance of a strategic conquest.
xs: **Devagiri** was the **first southern kingdom to fall to Delhi** and opened the road to **Warangal**, **Dwarasamudra** and **Madurai**, so option **(1)** is correct (**UPSC**).
Devagiri was the **Yadava** capital, founded by **Bhillama V**, not a Hoysala or Kakatiya capital.
xa: First raid: **1295**, by **Alauddin Khalji**.
After **1323**, Devagiri = the Sultanate's **Deccan base**.
**Malik Burhanuddin** was the vizier of Devagiri.

91.s: Which set correctly represents the Yadava–Kakatiya rivalry?
o: Jaitugi killed Rudradeva; Singhana used the title ‘Teluguraya Sthapanacharya’; Rudramadevi defeated Mahadeva
Rudradeva killed Jaitugi; Mahadeva installed Singhana; Ganapatideva defeated Rudramadevi
Singhana founded Devagiri; Rudramadevi defeated Bhillama; Jaitugi served under Ramachandra
Mahadeva killed Ganapatideva; Rudradeva founded the Yadava kingdom; Singhana defeated Rudramadevi
91.x: The rivalry included Jaitugi’s killing of Rudradeva, Singhana’s claim to be the installer of the Telugu king, and Rudramadevi’s repulse of Mahadeva’s attack.
91.tq: Start from the sure ruler–event pairs in an inter-dynastic rivalry.
xs: **Jaitugi** killed **Rudradeva**, **Singhana** styled himself **Teluguraya Sthapanacharya**, and **Rudramadevi** beat **Mahadeva**, so option **(1)** is correct.
The other options reverse the roles. For example, **Bhillama V**, not Singhana, founded Devagiri.
xa: Jaitugi held **Ganapatideva** captive, then released him (**1199**).
**Sarangapanideva** (Singhana's son) served at **Rudramadevi's** court.
**Hemadri** claimed Jaitugi **sacrificed** Rudra.

92.s: Which one of the following correctly states the two principal views regarding the progenitor of the Kakatiyas?
o: Prola I of Hanamkonda and Beta I of Orugallu
Kakara Gundana of Magallu and Venna Bhupati of Bayyaram
Rudradeva of Anumakonda and Ganapatideva of Motupalli
Danarnava of Vengi and Durjaya of Pithapuram
92.x: The progenitor is identified in different traditions as Kakara Gundana of Magallu or Venna Bhupati of Bayyaram.
92.tq: Compare competing origin traditions without treating one disputed view as exclusive.
xs: The progenitor is either **Kakara Gundana** (**Magallu**) or **Venna Bhupati** (**Bayyaram**), so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Magallu grant** (**956 CE**) of Eastern Chalukya **Danarnava** names Gundana, and the **Bayyaram** inscription names Venna.
**Danarnava** issued the Magallu grant and was not a Kakatiya progenitor.
xa: The Bayyaram inscription traces the line from **Durjaya**.
The **Bayyaram tank** inscription (**1219**), by **Mailamba**, gives the best genealogy of the early Kakatiyas.
First mention of the Kakatiyas = **Magallu 956**.

92.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kakatiyas:
1. Their Samanta (feudatory) phase lasted from 956 to 1162 and their sovereign phase from 1163 to 1323.
2. The early Kakatiyas were Shaivas who later became Jains.
3. They were Shudras by caste, and Sanskrit was their official language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
92.x: Statement 1 is correct: Samanta 956-1162, sovereign 1163-1323. Statement 2 is wrong: the early Kakatiyas were Jains who later became Shaivas (APPSC G2 2011). Statement 3 is correct: their caste is given as Shudras and their official language as Sanskrit. So '1 only' is incomplete and options with 2 are wrong.
92.tq: Jain first, Shaiva later - the order is the trap.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct, so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **Samanta** phase ran **956-1162**, and the **sovereign** phase **1163-1323**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the early Kakatiyas were **Jains** who later became **Shaivas** (**APPSC G2 2011**).
Statement 3 is correct: they were **Shudras**, with **Sanskrit** as their official language.
xa: Emblem: **Garuda** (Rashtrakuta phase) → **Varaha** (Kalyani Chalukya phase).
Clan deity **Kakatamma (Kakati Devi)** = the Jain **Kushmandini** absorbed into Hinduism.
**Telugu** replaced Sanskrit in inscriptions from **Ganapatideva's** reign.

92.s: ‘Kakati’ in the explanation of the Kakatiya clan deity is associated with which meaning?
92.x: Kakati means gourd. Kakatamma, or Kakati Devi, was associated with the Jain Kushmandini before being absorbed into Hindu tradition.
92.tq: Discriminate the exact etymological meaning from emblem and deity associations.
xs: **"Kakati"** means **gourd**, so option **(1)** is correct.
The clan deity **Kakatamma (Kakati Devi)** was the Jain **Kushmandini**, absorbed into Hinduism.
xa: The early Kakatiyas were **Jains** (**APPSC G2 2011**), later **Shaivas**.
The **Varaha** (boar) was their emblem in the Kalyani Chalukya phase.
The **Garuda** was their emblem in the Rashtrakuta phase.

92.s: The early territorial base of the Kakatiyas was known as:
92.x: The early Kakatiya base was Hanamkonda Vishaya, corresponding broadly to modern Karimnagar, Warangal and Khammam areas.
92.tq: Distinguish the early territorial base from later campaign regions.
xs: The early Kakatiya base was **Hanamkonda Vishaya**, so option **(2)** is correct.
It covered modern **Karimnagar**, **Warangal** and **Khammam**.
xa: **Beta I** got **Anumakonda Vishaya** through his aunt **Viriyala Kamasani**.
**Prola I** made Anumakonda (**Hanamkonda**) the capital.
**Rudradeva** shifted the capital to **Orugallu (Warangal)**.

92.s: Which sequence correctly represents the principal overlordship of the early Kakatiyas?
o: Rashtrakutas followed by Eastern Chalukyas only
92.x: The early Kakatiyas were first feudatories of the Rashtrakutas and later of the Kalyani Chalukyas. The Eastern Chalukya association occurs in the context of the Magallu grant and may appear as an alternative in some questions.
92.tq: Separate the general sequence of overlordship from the issuer of the first inscription.
xs: The Kakatiyas were first under the **Rashtrakutas**, then the **Kalyani Chalukyas**, so option **(2)** is correct (**APPSC G2 2005**).
⚠ Another key (**APHQ 2017 / APPSC 2017**) answers **Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi**, from Danarnava's **Magallu** grant.
xa: ⚠ Write **Eastern Chalukyas** only if **Rashtrakutas** is not among the options.
The emblem changed with the overlord: **Garuda** → **Varaha**.
Feudatory title under the Kalyani Chalukyas: **Mahamandaleswara**.

92.s: Which of the following statements about Beta I is correct?
o: He was known as Garuda Beta and obtained Anumakonda Vishaya through his aunt Viriyala Kamasani.
He invaded the Yadavas to avenge Rudradeva.
He was known as Arigajakesari and built Kesamudram tank.
He founded Orugallu and composed Nitisara.
92.x: Beta I (Garuda Beta) obtained Anumakonda Vishaya through his aunt Viriyala Kamasani. The other options belong to other rulers: avenging Rudradeva by invading the Yadavas was Mahadeva (B), Arigajakesari and the Kesamudram tank were Prola I (C), and founding Orugallu and writing Nitisara were Rudradeva (D).
92.tq: Use the ruler-achievement association and reject deeds belonging to neighbouring rulers.
xs: **Beta I (Garuda Beta)** got **Anumakonda Vishaya** through his aunt **Viriyala Kamasani**, so option **(1)** is correct.
Avenging Rudradeva was **Mahadeva**; **Arigajakesari** and the **Kesamudram** tank were **Prola I**; **Orugallu** and the **Nitisara** were **Rudradeva**.
xa: Beta I was the first Kakatiya to come to **Hanamkonda** (**Bayyaram** inscription).
He attacked **Kanchi** (**1051**) for **Someshwara I**.
His title: **Chola Chamuvardhi Pramadhana** ('Cholachamu Vari Pramathana').

92.s: Prola I is associated with which combination of titles and achievement?
o: Arigajakesari; Samadhigata Panchamahasabda; construction of Kesamudram tank
Cholachamu Vari Pramathana; Vidyabhushana; construction of the Thousand Pillar Temple
Vidyabhushana; Kanchi Churakara; construction of Arikesari Samudram
Samadhigata Panchamahasabda; Rayagaja Kesari; construction of Ramappa temple
92.x: Prola I bore the titles Arigajakesari and Samadhigata Panchamahasabda and built Kesamudram tank.
92.tq: Start from the sure title and verify the achievement attached to the same ruler.
xs: **Prola I** bore the titles **Arigajakesari** and **Samadhigata Panchamahashabda** and built the **Kesamudram** tank, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Vidyabhushana** was **Rudradeva's** title, and **Rayagajakesari** was **Rudramadevi's**.
xa: ⚠ **Kesamudram** = Prola I; **Kesari Samudram** = Rudradeva; **Arikesari Samudram** = Prola II.
⚠ **APPSC 2025** treated "Prolaraja bore the title Arikesari" as **incorrect**.
Prola I made **Anumakonda** the capital (**1052-1076**).

92.s: Which change is associated with Prola I during the development of the Kakatiya polity?
o: The capital changed from Orugallu to Anumakonda.
The emblem changed from Varaha to Garuda.
The capital changed from Hanamkonda to Kanchi.
The emblem changed from Garuda to Varaha.
92.x: During Prola I’s period, the Kakatiya emblem changed from Garuda to Varaha.
92.tq: Discriminate between the two directions of an emblem change.
xs: Under **Prola I** the emblem changed from **Garuda to Varaha**, so option **(4)** is correct.
Option (2) reverses the change. Prola I also made **Anumakonda**, not Orugallu or Kanchi, the capital.
xa: Garuda belonged to the **Rashtrakuta** phase; Varaha to the **Kalyani Chalukya** phase.
Prola I served **Someshwara I** and **Vikramaditya VI**.

92.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Beta II — Shivapura and Betesvaralayam
2. Durgaraja — donations to the Betesvara temple
3. Prola II — victory pillar at Srisailam
4. Mahadeva — construction of Ramappa temple
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
92.x: Beta II built Shivapura and Betesvaralayam, Durgaraja made donations to the Betesvara temple, and Prola II erected a victory pillar at Srisailam. Ramappa temple belongs to the reign of Ganapatideva, not Mahadeva.
92.tq: Find the swapped ruler–achievement statement before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Beta II** built **Shivapura** and **Betesvaralayam**; **Durgaraja** made donations to the **Betesvara** temple (**Kazipet Dargah** inscription).
**Prola II** set up a **victory pillar at Srisailam**.
Pair 4 is wrong: the **Ramappa** temple was built by **Recherla Rudra** (**1213**) in **Ganapatideva's** reign.
xa: Beta II's title: **Vikrama Chakri**.
**Mahadeva** (**1195-1199**) died in the revenge war against the Yadavas.
Ramappa = UNESCO World Heritage Site, **2021**.

92.s: Beta II was initiated into Saivism by Rameswara Pandita of which institution?
92.x: Beta II was initiated into Saivism by Rameswara Pandita of the Srisailam Mallikarjuna matha.
92.tq: Identify the religious teacher through the institution associated with him.
xs: **Beta II** was initiated into Saivism by **Rameswara Pandita** of the **Srisailam Mallikarjuna matha**, so option **(1)** is correct (**APPSC 2025**).
He gave his guru **Vaijanapalli**, as recorded in the **Thousand Pillar** inscription.
xa: Beta II ruled **1076-1108**.
His title was **Vikrama Chakri**.
**Mahadeva's** guru was **Dhruveshwara Pandita**.

92.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Prola II — victory pillar at Srisailam
92.x: The Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam of 1244 belongs to Ganapatideva. Prola II is associated with Arikesari Samudram, the Swayambhu temple and the victory pillar at Srisailam.
92.tq: Find the achievement belonging to a different ruler.
xs: The **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** (**1244**) belongs to **Ganapatideva**, so option **(3)** is the wrong pair.
**Prola II** is credited with the **Swayambhu** temple, **Arikesari Samudram** and the **victory pillar at Srisailam**.
xa: Motupalli gave **protection to foreign traders**.
Prola II (**1116-1157**) was killed fighting the **Velanati** kings.
Arikesari Samudram was asked in **APPSC 2012**.

92.s:
Consider the following statements about Rudradeva (Prataparudra I):
1. He declared Kakatiya independence in 1163, as recorded in the Thousand Pillar inscription.
2. The APPSC 2019 key credits him with building Kesari Samudram.
3. He was killed by the Hoysala ruler Veera Ballala II.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
92.x: Statement 1 is correct: Rudradeva declared independence in 1163 (Thousand Pillar inscription). Statement 2 is correct: the APPSC 2019 key gives Kesari Samudram to Rudradeva. Statement 3 is wrong: he was killed by the Yadava Jaitugi, not a Hoysala. So '1 only' is incomplete and options with 3 are wrong.
92.tq: Rudradeva: 1163 independence, Thousand Pillar temple, Kesari Samudram, killed by Jaitugi.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Rudradeva** declared **independence in 1163** (Thousand Pillar/Anumakonda inscription).
Statement 2 is correct: the **APPSC 2019** key gives **Kesari Samudram** to Rudradeva.
Statement 3 is wrong: he was killed by the Yadava **Jaitugi**, not a Hoysala.
xa: He founded **Orugallu** and wrote the **'Nitisara'**.
The inscription was found by **J.S. Fleet** and composed by **Achitendru**.
Titles: **Vidyabhushana**, **Vinaya Vibhushanudu**.

92.s: Which of the following statements regarding Mahadeva is correct?
o: He built the Jain Kadalalaya at Anumakonda.
He invaded the Yadavas to avenge Rudradeva and died in battle while crossing a river on an elephant.
He issued the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam in 1244.
He founded Orugallu and completed its fortifications.
92.x: Mahadeva invaded the Yadavas to avenge Rudradeva and died in battle, reportedly on an elephant while crossing a river.
92.tq: Use the unusual detail of the ruler’s death to identify the correct statement.
xs: **Mahadeva** invaded the Yadavas to **avenge Rudradeva** and died fighting, on an **elephant**, while crossing a river, so option **(2)** is correct.
The Kadalalaya was built by **Chetanamatya**, Motupalli is **Ganapatideva's** and Orugallu was founded by **Rudradeva**.
xa: Mahadeva ruled **1195-1199**.
His guru was **Dhruveshwara Pandita**.
His son **Ganapatideva** was held captive by **Jaitugi**.

92.s: Which one of the following combinations relating to Ganapatideva is correctly matched?
o: 63-year reign; Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam of 1244; Ramappa temple built during his reign
44-year reign; Draksharamam inscription of 1158; Thousand Pillar Temple built during his reign
19-year reign; Bayyaram inscription; Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya at Sanigaram
8-year reign; Kazipet Dargah inscription; Swayambhu temple built during his reign
92.x: Ganapatideva ruled for 63 years, issued the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam in 1244, and Ramappa temple was built during his reign by Recherla Rudra.
92.tq: Match the ruler with the period length, charter and monumental achievement.
xs: **Ganapatideva** ruled **63 years**, issued the **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** (**1244**), and **Ramappa** was built in his reign, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Draksharamam** (**1158**) describes Rudradeva's accession, and the **Thousand Pillar** temple is Rudradeva's (**1163**).
xa: His reign: **1199-1262**; title **Andhra Deshadhiswara**.
He granted the **Ganapavaram** villages.
He built the **Lakkavaram** and **Ghanapur** tanks.

92.s: Ramappa temple was built during the reign of Ganapatideva by:
92.x: Ramappa temple was built during Ganapatideva’s reign by Recherla Rudra in 1213.
92.tq: Separate the builder of the monument from ministers and inscription authors.
xs: **Recherla Rudra** built the **Ramappa** temple and tank at **Palampet** (**1213**), in Ganapatideva's reign, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Naranayya** built the Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya, **Brahma Reddi** issued the Draksharamam inscription and **Chetanamatya** built the Kadalalaya.
xa: Ramappa: UNESCO World Heritage Site, **2021**; star-shaped platform, **floating bricks**.
Recherla Rudra's title: **'Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya'**.
He saved the kingdom during **Ganapati's captivity**.

92.s: Which of the following set contains only works or grants associated with Ganapatideva’s reign?
o: Ramappa temple, Lakkavaram tank, Ghanapur tank and Ganapavaram villages
Arikesari Samudram, victory pillar at Srisailam and Betesvaralayam
Thousand Pillar Temple, Kadalalaya Jainavasadi and Kesamudram tank
Kesamudram tank, Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya and Swayambhu temple
92.x: Ramappa temple, the Lakkavaram and Ghanapur tanks, and the grant of Ganapavaram villages are associated with Ganapatideva’s reign.
92.tq: Eliminate sets containing achievements of different Kakatiya rulers.
xs: **Ramappa** temple, the **Lakkavaram** and **Ghanapur** tanks and the **Ganapavaram** villages all belong to **Ganapatideva's** reign, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Arikesari Samudram** and the Srisailam pillar are **Prola II's**; **Kesamudram** is **Prola I's**; the **Thousand Pillar** temple is **Rudradeva's**.
xa: **Chouda Samudram** was built by **Malyala Chauda Senani**.
**Betesvaralayam** was built by **Beta II**.
Exam angle: match **tank → builder** and **ruler → temple**.

92.s:
Arrange the following Kakatiya rulers in chronological order of their reigns:
A. Prola II
B. Beta II
C. Rudradeva
D. Mahadeva
92.x: The order is Beta II (1076–1108), Prola II (1116–1157), Rudradeva (1158–1195), and Mahadeva (1195–1199).
92.tq: Fix the sequence using the beginning and end of each ruler’s reign.
xs: The order is **Beta II** (**1076-1108**) → **Prola II** (**1116-1157**) → **Rudradeva** (**1158-1195**) → **Mahadeva** (**1195-1199**), i.e. B, A, C, D. So option **(1)** is correct.
**Durgaraja** (**1108-1116**) came between Beta II and Prola II.
xa: **Ganapatideva** followed (**1199-1262**).
Then **Rudrama Devi** (**1262-1289**).
Last ruler: **Prataparudra II**.

92.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the ruler who united the Telugu lands and is regarded as the greatest Kakatiya ruler?
92.x: Ganapatideva is regarded as the greatest Kakatiya ruler and is credited with uniting the Telugu lands.
92.tq: Identify the ruler from the broad political achievement rather than a single monument.
xs: **Ganapatideva** is the **greatest Kakatiya**, who **united the Telugu lands**, so option **(3)** is correct.
He took the title **'Andhra Deshadhiswara'** and unified "**Telugudesam**".
xa: The Kakatiyas were the **2nd dynasty after the Satavahanas** to unify Telugu-speaking regions.
**Telugu** replaced Sanskrit in inscriptions from his reign.

92.s: The ancient name ‘Orugallu’, associated with the later Kakatiya capital, literally means:
92.x: Orugallu is the ancient name of Warangal and means ‘single rock’.
92.tq: Use the exact meaning of the place-name rather than its later political association.
xs: **Orugallu**, the ancient name of **Warangal**, means **"single rock"**, so option **(4)** is correct.
It became the later Kakatiya capital in place of **Anumakonda (Hanamkonda)**.
xa: **Rudradeva** shifted the capital there from Hanamkonda (**APPSC G2 2019**).
Under **Ganapatideva** it was called **Andhranagari**.
After the **1323** conquest it was named **Sultanpur**.

92.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the names associated with the Kakatiya capital:
1. Andhranagari was a name used for Orugallu under Ganapatideva.
2. Sultanpur was the name given to Orugallu after the conquest of 1323.
3. Orugallu was the early capital made by Prola I.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Andhranagari was used under Ganapatideva, and Sultanpur was the name given after the conquest of 1323. The early capital was Anumakonda or Hanamkonda, not Orugallu.
92.tq: Split the statements by distinguishing the successive names and stages of the capital.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Andhranagari** was used under **Ganapatideva**.
Statement 2 is correct: it was renamed **Sultanpur** after **1323**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Prola I's** capital was **Anumakonda (Hanamkonda)**, not Orugallu.
xa: **Prola II** developed Hanamkonda.
⚠ "Who shifted the capital to Orugallu?" → **Rudradeva**.
**Ganapatideva** completed Orugallu.

92.s: With reference to the development of the Kakatiya capital, which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Prola I — made Orugallu the capital
Rudradeva — gave Orugallu the name Sultanpur
92.x: Prola II developed Hanamkonda. Prola I made Anumakonda the capital, Rudradeva shifted the capital to Orugallu, and Sultanpur was the post-1323 name.
92.tq: Match each ruler with the correct stage in the evolution of the capital.
xs: **Prola II** = **developed Hanamkonda** is correctly matched, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Prola I** made **Anumakonda**, not Orugallu, the capital; **Rudradeva** shifted the capital to Orugallu; **Sultanpur** was the post-**1323** name.
xa: Rudradeva began the **Warangal fort**.
**Ganapatideva** completed Orugallu and moved the court there.
Orugallu = "**single rock**".

92.s: Which of the following correctly describes the respective roles of Rudradeva and Ganapatideva in relation to Orugallu?
o: Rudradeva began fortifying Orugallu, while Ganapatideva completed it and fully moved the court there.
Ganapatideva shifted the capital to Orugallu, while Rudradeva renamed it Sultanpur.
Rudradeva abandoned Orugallu, while Ganapatideva restored Hanamkonda as the capital.
Rudradeva completed the city and Ganapatideva began its fortification.
92.x: Rudradeva shifted the capital and began fortifying Orugallu. Ganapatideva completed the city and fully transferred the court there.
92.tq: Separate the initiating ruler from the ruler who completed the work.
xs: **Rudradeva** began fortifying **Orugallu**, and **Ganapatideva** completed it and fully moved the court there, so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ The "who shifted" answer is **Rudradeva** (**APPSC G2 2019**). Some notes say Ganapati made the final transfer.
xa: The fortification became the **Warangal fort**.
Under Ganapatideva the city was called **Andhranagari**.
After **1323** it was **Sultanpur**.

92.s: Ganapatideva was released from Yadava captivity in which year?
92.x: Ganapatideva was released from Yadava captivity in 1199.
92.tq: Use the date as the direct discriminator among closely related reign events.
xs: **Ganapatideva** was released from Yadava captivity in **1199**, so option **(2)** is correct.
His first inscription is from **Manthena**, dated **26 Dec 1199**.
xa: He had been held captive as a boy by Yadava **Jaitugi**.
General **Recherla Rudra** crushed revolts and installed him.
**1210** was the year **Prithviswara** was killed; his coastal campaign began in **1201**.

92.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Ganapatideva and the Velanati Chodas:
1. Ganapatideva and Choda Tikka of Nellore jointly killed Prithviswara in 1210.
2. Both rulers assumed the title Prithviswara Shirakhandika Kreeda Vinoda.
3. The Velanati kingdom came to an end in 1210.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: All three statements are correct. Prithviswara was killed in 1210, the joint title was adopted by Ganapatideva and Choda Tikka, and the Velanati kingdom ended in that year.
92.tq: Check the linked event, title and consequence as one chronological cluster.
xs: All three statements are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Ganapatideva** and Nellore's **Choda Tikka** jointly killed **Prithviswara** in **1210**.
Both took the title **"Prithviswara Shirakhandika Kreeda Vinoda"**, and the **Velanati** kingdom ended in **1210**.
xa: Final end of the Velanati Chodas: **Mummadi Rajendra Chola** killed in **1257**.
Prithviswara's **Pithapuram** inscription names **Kolleru Lake**.
General **Mutyalachaundaraya** took **Divi**.

92.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the political arrangements made by Ganapatideva after the coastal campaign?
o: He married the daughters of Prithviswara and appointed Akkana as Gajasahani.
He married the daughters of Pinnachodi and appointed their brother Jayapa as Gajasahani.
He married the daughters of Mummadi Rajendra Chola and appointed Bayyana as Gajasahani.
He married the daughters of Manumasiddhi and appointed Tikkana as Gajasahani.
92.x: Ganapatideva married Pinnachodi's daughters Narama and Perama, and appointed their brother Jayapa as Gajasahani, the chief of the elephant forces.
92.tq: Test a multi-person relationship by separating family ties from political office.
xs: Ganapatideva married **Pinnachodi's** daughters **Narama** and **Perama** and made their brother **Jayapa** **'Gajasahani'**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Gajasahani** = chief of the **elephant force**.
**Akkana** and **Bayyana** were allies against **Manumasiddhi**, and **Tikkana** was a poet-envoy.
xa: The coastal campaign began **from 1201**.
**Mutyalachaundaraya** took **Divi**.
Ganapatideva held coastal Andhra firmly.

92.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In 1257, Ganapatideva allied with Akkana and Bayyana and killed Mummadi Rajendra Chola, finally ending the Velanati Chodas.
2. Tikkana dedicated his Nirvachanottara Ramayana to Ganapatideva.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
92.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 1257 alliance killed Mummadi Rajendra Chola, the final end of the Velanati Chodas. Statement 2 is wrong: Tikkana dedicated the Nirvachanottara Ramayana to Manumasiddhi of Nellore. So '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' are wrong.
92.tq: Tikkana's patron = Manumasiddhi; he went as envoy to Ganapatideva.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: in **1257** Ganapatideva allied with **Akkana** and **Bayyana** and killed **Mummadi Rajendra Chola**, the final end of the Velanati Chodas.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Tikkana** dedicated his **Nirvachanottara Ramayana** to **Manumasiddhi**, not Ganapatideva.
xa: Ganapatideva restored **Manumasiddhi II** to the Nellore throne.
**Tikkana** went as envoy to seek his help.
**Akkana** and **Bayyana** were enemies of Manumasiddhi.

92.s: Which of the following correctly describes the consequence of the Battle of Muttukur?
o: Nellore fell to the Pandyas in 1263.
The Kakatiyas captured Divi from the Pandyas in 1263.
The Velanati kingdom was founded in 1263.
Ganapatideva was released from Yadava captivity in 1263.
92.x: The Pandyas defeated Ganapatideva in 1263, and Nellore fell to them after the Battle of Muttukur.
92.tq: Link the battle with its immediate territorial consequence.
xs: After the **Battle of Muttukur** (**1263**), **Nellore fell** to the **Pandyas**, so option **(1)** is correct (**APPSC G2 2017**).
The **Pandyas** defeated **Ganapatideva** there.
xa: Despite this, he still held **coastal Andhra** firmly.
The battle is also spelt **Muthukuru**.
He had earlier restored **Manumasiddhi II** at Nellore.

92.s: Who restored Manumasiddhi II of Nellore to his throne?
92.x: Ganapatideva intervened in Nellore affairs and restored Manumasiddhi II to the throne. The poet Tikkana went as envoy to seek Ganapatideva’s help.
92.tq: Match the political intervention with the ruler who carried it out.
xs: **Ganapatideva** restored **Manumasiddhi II** of Nellore to his throne, so option **(3)** is correct.
The poet **Tikkana** went as envoy to seek his help.
xa: Tikkana dedicated his **Nirvachanottara Ramayana** to **Manumasiddhi**.
Nellore later fell to the **Pandyas** after **Muttukur** (**1263**).
In **1257** Ganapati allied with **Akkana** and **Bayyana**, Manumasiddhi's enemies.

92.s: Who went as an envoy to seek Ganapatideva’s help for Manumasiddhi II?
92.x: The poet Tikkana went as an envoy to request Ganapatideva’s intervention on behalf of Manumasiddhi II.
92.tq: Distinguish the literary figure acting as envoy from military commanders and feudatories.
xs: The poet **Tikkana** went as **envoy** to seek Ganapatideva's help for **Manumasiddhi II**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Pedarudru** was Prataparudra's commander, **Prasadaditya** a Kayastha feudatory, and **Vellanki Gangadhara** Rudradeva's viceroy of Sabbinadu.
xa: Tikkana dedicated the **Nirvachanottara Ramayana** to Manumasiddhi.
Ganapatideva restored Manumasiddhi II.
Nellore fell to the **Pandyas** in **1263**.

92.s: Which one of the following statements is correct about Ganapatideva?
o: After the Muttukur defeat, he nevertheless retained firm control over coastal Andhra.
After the Muttukur defeat, he abandoned all control over coastal Andhra.
He ruled only the Nellore region after restoring Manumasiddhi II.
He transferred coastal Andhra to the Yadavas after his release.
92.x: Although Ganapatideva was defeated at Muttukur, he continued to hold coastal Andhra firmly.
92.tq: Watch for the extreme reversal in statements claiming complete loss of territory.
xs: Even after the **Muttukur** defeat (**1263**), Ganapatideva **still held coastal Andhra firmly**, so option **(1)** is correct.
He bore the title **'Andhra Deshadhiswara'** and unified "**Telugudesam**".
xa: Coastal marriages: **Narama** and **Perama**, daughters of **Pinnachodi**.
**Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** (**1244**) protected foreign traders.
**Jayapa** was made **Gajasahani**.

92.s: Which title was borne by Ganapatideva in recognition of his authority over the Telugu country?
92.x: Ganapatideva bore the title Andhra Deshadhiswara and is associated with the unification of Telugudesam.
92.tq: Separate a ruler’s sovereign title from the titles of his feudatories.
xs: **Ganapatideva** bore the title **'Andhra Deshadhiswara'**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**'Raya Pitamahanka'** and **'Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya'** belong to **Prasadaditya**; **'Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya'** to **Recherla Rudra**.
xa: ⚠ A [GK] table instead gives **Sthapanacharya** to **Recherla Rudra**.
**Rayagajakesari** = **Rudramadevi** (**APPSC-GS 2018**).
**Kumara Rudradeva** = **Prataparudra II** at accession.

92.s: Who killed Rudradeva and captured Ganapatideva?
92.x: Yadava ruler Jaitugi killed Rudradeva and captured Ganapatideva during the Kakatiya-Yadava conflict.
92.tq: Use the ruler–event association and eliminate opponents belonging to other conflicts.
xs: Yadava **Jaitugi** killed **Rudradeva** and captured **Ganapatideva**, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Veera Ballala II's** push into the Krishna-Tungabhadra region was the reason Ganapati was freed. **Tailapa III** was defeated by Rudradeva.
xa: The **Paithan copper plate** of Ramachandra confirms this.
**Mahadeva** was killed in the revenge war.
Ganapati was released in **1199**.

92.s: Which development contributed to Yadava Jaitugi releasing Ganapatideva?
o: The invasion of the Krishna-Tungabhadra region by Veera Ballala II
The revolt of the Nellore Chodas
The defeat of the Pandyas at Muttukur
The capture of Kanchi by Rudramadevi
92.x: Hoysala Veera Ballala II pushed into the Krishna-Tungabhadra region, compelling Jaitugi to release Ganapatideva.
92.tq: Identify the cause-and-effect link rather than merely recalling the names of the rulers.
xs: **Veera Ballala II** pushed into the **Krishna-Tungabhadra** region, which is why **Jaitugi** freed Ganapatideva, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Muttukur** (**1263**) came much later and was a Pandya victory over Ganapati.
xa: Ganapati was released in **1199**.
General **Recherla Rudra** crushed revolts and installed him.
Jaitugi married his daughter **Somaladevi** to Ganapati.

92.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the later Kakatiya conflicts?
o: Rudramadevi repulsed the Yadava Mahadeva, while Pedarudru defeated Hoysala Ballala III after 1316.
Rudramadevi was defeated by Yadava Mahadeva, while Pedarudru supported Hoysala Ballala III.
Mahadeva defeated Rudramadevi and captured the Kakatiya capital after 1316.
Pedarudru defeated Yadava Jaitugi and installed Rudramadevi on the throne.
92.x: Rudramadevi repulsed Yadava Mahadeva, and Prataparudra’s commander Pedarudru defeated Hoysala Ballala III after 1316.
92.tq: Split the paired ruler–opponent relationships before selecting the precisely matched statement.
xs: **Rudramadevi** repulsed Yadava **Mahadeva**, and **Pedarudru** defeated Hoysala **Ballala III** after **1316**, so option **(1)** is correct.
Pedarudru was **Prataparudra's** commander. He fought Ballala III and did not support him.
xa: Rudramadevi's title **Rayagajakesari** marks her victory over the **Yadavas of Devagiri** (**APPSC-GS 2018**).
Supporters of Rudrama: **Malyala Gundiya**, **Viriyala Suri**.
Rudrama ruled **1262-1289**.

92.s: The conflict with which opponent began during the reign of Prola II?
92.x: The Kakatiya conflict with the Yadavas, also called the Sevunas of Devagiri, began during the reign of Prola II.
92.tq: Link the beginning of the conflict to the correct opponent and period.
xs: The conflict with the **Yadavas** (Sevunas of **Devagiri**) began under **Prola II**, so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Velanati Chodas** killed Prola II; the **Kalachuris** were defeated by Rudradeva (**1159**); the **Pandyas** won at Muttukur (**1263**).
xa: Prola II backed **Someshwara III**.
Prola II set up a victory pillar at **Srisailam**.
Later, **Jaitugi** killed **Rudradeva**.

92.s: Who killed Prola II?
92.x: The Velanati Chodas killed Prola II. Rudradeva later avenged him and appointed Vellanki Gangadhara as viceroy of Sabbinadu.
92.tq: Apply the strongest history trap: match the ruler with the correct opponent responsible for his death.
xs: The **Velanati Chodas** killed **Prola II**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Rudradeva** avenged him and made **Vellanki Gangadhara** viceroy of **Sabbinadu**.
xa: Ganapatideva and Choda Tikka killed **Prithviswara** in **1210**.
The Velanati Chodas finally ended in **1257**.
Prola II reigned **1116-1157**.

92.s: Which of the following was defeated by Rudradeva?
92.x: Rudradeva defeated the Telugu Chodas and Tailapa III. The Muttukur victory over Ganapatideva belonged to the Pandyas, while Ballala III was defeated later by Pedarudru.
92.tq: Find the option assigning a later or different ruler’s victory to Rudradeva.
xs: **Rudradeva** defeated the **Telugu Chodas** and **Tailapa III**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Ballala III** was defeated by **Pedarudru** after **1316**, and the **Pandyas** defeated Ganapati at **Muttukur** (**1263**).
xa: Rudradeva defeated the **Kalachuri** confederacy (**Mailagi**, **Medaraja**, **Dommaraja**) in **1159**.
He avenged Prola II against the **Velanati Chodas**.
He declared independence in **1163**.

92.s: Which statement regarding the succession after Ganapatideva is correct?
o: Ganapatideva had no son, and Rudrama Devi succeeded him after being raised as a son or putrika.
Ganapatideva’s son succeeded him, while Rudrama Devi remained outside the succession.
Ganapatideva was succeeded by his sister Mailamba after appointing Rudrama Devi as a feudatory.
Rudrama Devi succeeded only after the Kakatiya kingdom was annexed by the Yadavas.
92.x: Ganapatideva had no son. Rudrama Devi was raised as a son, or putrika, and succeeded him.
92.tq: Use the succession exception—daughter raised as a son—to reject the conventional son-successor trap.
xs: Ganapatideva had **no son**, so **Rudrama Devi**, raised as a son (**putrika**), succeeded him. Option **(1)** is correct.
Rudrama ruled **1262-1289**. **Mailamba** was Ganapati's sister, not his successor.
xa: Daughters: **Rudramamba** married **Veerabhadra** (Nidadavolu Eastern Chalukya); **Ganapamba** married the **Kota** chief.
**Kupama Devi** guided her training.
Ganapati's sisters **Mailamba** and **Kundamamba** married sons of **Natavadi Buddharaja**.

92.s: Rudrama Devi ruled during which period?
92.x: Rudrama Devi succeeded Ganapatideva and ruled from 1262 to 1289.
92.tq: Compare the closely spaced reign periods and select the one belonging to Rudrama Devi.
xs: **Rudrama Devi** ruled **1262-1289**, so option **(1)** is correct.
She succeeded **Ganapatideva** (**1199-1262**).
xa: She was raised as a son (**putrika**).
Title **Rayagajakesari** for her victory over the Yadavas.
She repulsed Yadava **Mahadeva**.

92.s: Who guided Rudrama Devi’s training?
92.x: Kupama Devi, Rudrama Devi’s mother, guided her training when she was being raised as a son.
92.tq: Distinguish the mother who guided training from the sisters and daughter mentioned in the succession account.
xs: **Kupama Devi**, Rudrama's mother, guided her training, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Mailamba** and **Kundamamba** were Ganapatideva's **sisters**, and **Ganapamba** was Rudrama's sister.
xa: Rudrama was raised as a **putrika** (son).
**Mailamba** issued the **Bayyaram tank** inscription (**1219**).
**Ganapamba** married the **Kota** chief.

92.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Recherla Rudra — Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya
2. Prasadaditya — Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya
3. Malyala Chauda Senani — Chouda Samudram
4. Kamasani — Gudur inscription
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
92.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Recherla Rudra bore the title Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya; Prasadaditya was Sthapanacharya; Chauda Senani built Chouda Samudram; and Kamasani’s role is recorded in the Gudur inscription.
92.tq: Verify each family–member–title or achievement pair independently before using the coded options.
xs: All four pairs are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Recherla Rudra** = **'Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya'**; **Prasadaditya** (Kayastha) = **'Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya'**.
**Malyala Chauda Senani** built **Chouda Samudram**; **Kamasani** is recorded in the **Gudur** inscription.
xa: Prasadaditya was also **'Raya Pitamahanka'**.
Kamasani (**Viriyala**) made **Garuda Beta** a Chalukya vassal.
**Malyala Gundiya** and **Viriyala Suri** backed **Rudrama**.

92.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kamasani — Made Garuda Beta a Chalukya vassal
Malyala Chauda Senani — Built Ramappa temple
92.x: Malyala Chauda Senani built Chouda Samudram. The Ramappa temple and tank at Palampet are associated with Recherla Rudra.
92.tq: Find the swapped achievement among closely related Kakatiya feudatories.
xs: **Malyala Chauda Senani** built **Chouda Samudram**, not the Ramappa temple, so option **(3)** is the wrong pair.
The **Ramappa** temple was built by **Recherla Rudra** (**1213**).
The other pairs are correct: **Viriyala Suri** and **Malyala Gundiya** backed **Rudrama**; **Kamasani** made **Garuda Beta** a Chalukya vassal.
xa: Ramappa is at **Palampet**.
Ramappa: UNESCO site, **2021**.
Kamasani's role is in the **Gudur** inscription.

92.s: Which family of Kakatiya feudatories is associated with Kamasani?
92.x: Kamasani belonged to the Viriyala family and made Garuda Beta a Chalukya vassal, as recorded in the Gudur inscription.
92.tq: Use the family–member association to separate the four feudatory groups.
xs: **Kamasani** belonged to the **Viriyala** family, so option **(3)** is correct.
She made **Garuda Beta** a Chalukya vassal (**Gudur** inscription).
xa: **Beta I** got **Anumakonda Vishaya** through his aunt **Viriyala Kamasani**.
**Viriyala Suri** backed **Rudrama**.
**Recherla** = Rudra; **Kayastha** = Prasadaditya; **Malyala** = Gundiya, Chauda Senani.

92.s: Recherla Rudra is associated with which combination?
o: Saving the kingdom during Ganapati’s captivity and constructing the Ramappa temple and tank at Palampet
Restoring Manumasiddhi II and serving as an envoy to the Pandyas
Building Chouda Samudram and making Garuda Beta a Chalukya vassal
Defeating Hoysala Ballala III and ruling the Nellore region
92.x: Recherla Rudra saved the kingdom during Ganapati’s captivity and is associated with the Ramappa temple and tank at Palampet.
92.tq: Start from the sure achievement and reject combinations assembled from different feudatories.
xs: **Recherla Rudra** saved the kingdom during **Ganapati's captivity** and built the **Ramappa** temple and tank at **Palampet**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Chouda Samudram** was **Malyala Chauda Senani's**, and **Kamasani** made Garuda Beta a vassal.
xa: His title was **'Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya'** (bearer of the Kakatiya realm's burden).
The **Palampet** inscription is dated **1213**.
He crushed revolts and installed **Ganapatideva**.

92.s: The Pithapuram inscription of Velanati Prithvishvara mentions which geographical feature?
92.x: The Pithapuram inscription of Velanati Prithvishvara mentions Kolleru Lake.
92.tq: Match the inscription with its distinctive geographical reference.
xs: The **Pithapuram** inscription of Velanati **Prithvisvara** names **Kolleru Lake**, so option **(1)** is correct (**APPSC G2 2017**).
It is a **Velanati Choda** record, not a Kakatiya one.
xa: Prithviswara was killed in **1210** by **Ganapatideva** and **Choda Tikka**.
The **Dharmasagara** inscription mentions the instrument **'Jalakaranda'** (**APPSC 2019**).
The **Motupalli** Abhaya Sasanam (**1244**) protected foreign traders.

92.s: Which inscription is correctly matched with its issuer and historical significance?
o: Magallu grant — Eastern Chalukya Danarnava — first mention of the Kakatiya family
Bayyaram inscription — Rudradeva — protection to foreign traders
Motupalli inscription — Mailamba — best genealogy of the early Kakatiyas
Thousand Pillar inscription — Ganapatideva — first mention of Gundyana
92.x: The Magallu grant of Eastern Chalukya Danarnava, dated 956, contains the first mention of the Kakatiya family through Gundyana.
92.tq: Start from the distinctive first-mention fact and eliminate exchanged issuers.
xs: The **Magallu grant** of Eastern Chalukya **Danarnava** (**956**) has the **first mention** of the Kakatiyas (Gundyana), so option **(1)** is correct.
**Bayyaram** was issued by **Mailamba** and gives the genealogy; **Motupalli** was **Ganapatideva's** grant protecting foreign traders.
The **Thousand Pillar** inscription is **Rudradeva's** (**1163**) declaration of independence.
xa: The Magallu grant names **Kakara Gundana** as progenitor; Bayyaram names **Venna**.
Phases: **Samanta 956-1162**, sovereign **1163-1323**.
First sovereign = **Rudradeva 1163**; last = **Prataparudra II**.

92.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bayyaram tank inscription — 1219 — genealogy of the early Kakatiyas
Palampet inscription — 1213 — Ramappa temple during Ganapati's reign
Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam — 1244 — Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya
92.x: The Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam of 1244 concerns protection for foreign traders. Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya is associated with the Sanigaram inscription.
92.tq: Find the one exchanged fact in an inscription–date–content set.
xs: The **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** (**1244**) gave **protection to foreign traders**. It is not about the Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya, so option **(3)** is the wrong pair.
The **Juddha Mallajinalaya** is linked to the **Sanigaram** inscription, built by **Beta I's** minister **Naranayya**.
The other pairs are correct: **Bayyaram 1219**, **Palampet 1213**, **Draksharamam 1158**.
xa: Motupalli was issued by **Ganapatideva**.
**APPSC 2025** key matched Sanigaram to **Rudradeva**.
The **Draksharamam** inscription was issued by minister **Inangala Brahma Reddi**.

92.s: The Draksharamam inscription of 1158 was issued by:
92.x: The Draksharamam inscription of 1158 was issued by Minister Inangala Brahma Reddi and records Rudradeva's accession.
92.tq: Distinguish an inscription issued by a minister from those issued by rulers.
xs: The **Draksharamam** inscription (**1158**) was issued by minister **Inangala (Unagalla) Brahma Reddi**, so option **(4)** is correct.
It describes **Rudradeva's accession**. **Danarnava** issued the Magallu grant, **Recherla Rudra** the Palampet inscription and **Mailamba** the Bayyaram one.
xa: Rudradeva was a feudatory **1158-1162** and sovereign **1163-1195**.
He declared independence in **1163**.
He founded **Orugallu**.

92.s:
Which of the following statements about the Thousand Pillar inscription is correct?
1. It is also known as the Anumakonda inscription.
2. It is dated 1163.
3. It is associated with Rudradeva.
4. It records the declaration of independence.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
92.x: All four statements are correct. The Anumakonda or Thousand Pillar inscription of 1163 is associated with Rudradeva and records Kakatiya independence.
92.tq: Combine alternative names, date, ruler and political significance before selecting the code.
xs: All four statements are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Anumakonda / Thousand Pillar** inscription is **Rudradeva's**, dated **1163**.
It declares **independence** and records **Prola II's conquests**.
xa: It was found by **J.S. Fleet** and composed by **Achitendru**.
⚠ The **APPSC 2025** key matched Anumakonda to **Prolaraja**, because it records Prola II's conquests.
The **Thousand Pillar (Rudreshwara)** temple was built by Rudradeva in **1163**.

92.s: The Bayyaram tank inscription of 1219 was issued by:
92.x: The Bayyaram tank inscription of 1219 was issued by Mailamba, Ganapatideva's sister, and provides the best genealogy of the early Kakatiyas.
92.tq: Test kinship relations together with the inscription issuer.
xs: The **Bayyaram tank** inscription (**1219**) was issued by **Mailamba**, **Ganapatideva's sister**, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Narama** was Pinnachodi's daughter and Ganapati's wife, and **Rudramadevi** was his daughter. Neither issued it.
xa: It gives the **best genealogy** of the early Kakatiyas.
Mailamba and **Kundamamba** married sons of **Natavadi Buddharaja**.
The Bayyaram inscription traces the line from **Durjaya**.

92.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched?
1. Sanigaram — Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya
2. Palampet — Ramappa temple
3. Dharmasagara — Jalakaranda
4. Pithapuram — Kolleru Lake
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
92.x: All four pairs are correct. These inscriptions respectively refer to Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya, the Ramappa temple, Jalakaranda and Kolleru Lake.
92.tq: Use distinctive cultural and geographical references to secure the inscription pairs.
xs: All four pairs are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Sanigaram** = Jain **Juddha Mallajinalaya**; **Palampet** = **Ramappa** temple (**1213**).
**Dharmasagara** = the instrument **'Jalakaranda'** (**APPSC 2019**); **Pithapuram** = **Kolleru Lake** (**APPSC G2 2017**).
xa: Pithapuram is a **Velanati** (Prithvisvara) record.
**Motupalli** (**1244**) = protection for foreign traders.
**Bayyaram** (**1219**) = best early genealogy.

92.s: In the APPSC 2025 matching question on Kakatiya inscriptions, which pairing of inscription and ruler was given in the key?
92.x: The APPSC 2025 key matched Anumakonda with Prolaraja, Motupalli with Ganapatideva, Bayyaram with Mailamba and Sanigaram with Rudradeva. So Motupalli-Rudradeva, Bayyaram-Ganapatideva and Sanigaram-Mailamba are all wrong pairings.
92.tq: APPSC 2025 key: Anumakonda-Prolaraja, Motupalli-Ganapati, Bayyaram-Mailamba, Sanigaram-Rudradeva.
xs: The **APPSC 2025** key matched the **Anumakonda** inscription to **Prolaraja**, so option **(1)** is correct.
The other key pairs were **Motupalli** = **Ganapatideva**, **Bayyaram** = **Mailamba**, **Sanigaram** = **Rudradeva**.
xa: ⚠ The Anumakonda inscription was issued by **Rudradeva** but records **Prola II's** conquests.
⚠ APPSC 2025 also treated "Prolaraja bore the title Arikesari" as **incorrect**.
Beta II's Saiva initiation by **Rameswara Pandita** was also an **APPSC 2025** point.

92.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
92.x: Prola I bore the title Arigajakesari. Vikrama Chakri belonged to Beta II, Vidyabhushana to Rudradeva, and Andhra Deshadhiswara to Ganapatideva.
92.tq: Start from the sure title–ruler pair and eliminate swapped holders.
xs: **Arigajakesari** = **Prola I** is correctly matched, so option **(1)** is correct (Bayyaram inscription).
**Vikrama Chakri** = **Beta II**; **Vidyabhushana** = **Rudradeva**; **Andhra Deshadhiswara** = **Ganapatideva**.
xa: Prola I also bore **Samadhigata Panchamahashabda**.
**Beta I's** title: **Chola Chamuvardhi Pramadhana**.
⚠ **APPSC 2025** read "Arikesari" as Prola II and marked it incorrect.

92.s: Mahamandaleswara, in the Kakatiya context, was primarily:
o: A feudatory title of the Samanta Kakatiyas under the Kalyani Chalukyas
A title given to generals of the Nellore Chodas
A title of the sovereign Kakatiya emperor only
A religious title of Jain teachers
92.x: Mahamandaleswara was a feudatory title used by the Samanta Kakatiyas under the Kalyani Chalukyas.
92.tq: Distinguish a feudatory designation from a sovereign royal title.
xs: **Mahamandaleswara** was the **feudatory title** of the **Samanta Kakatiyas** under the **Kalyani Chalukyas**, so option **(1)** is correct.
It was not a sovereign or Jain title.
xa: The Samanta phase ran **956-1162**.
Overlords: **Rashtrakutas** first, then **Kalyani Chalukyas**.
Under the Kalyani Chalukyas the emblem was the **Varaha**.

92.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Chola Chamuvardhi — Beta I
2. Vikrama Chakri — Beta II
3. Vinaya Vibhushanudu — Rudradeva
4. Andhra Deshadhiswara — Ganapatideva
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
92.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. These titles belonged respectively to Beta I, Beta II, Rudradeva and Ganapatideva.
92.tq: Verify each title–ruler pair before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All four pairs are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Chola Chamuvardhi** = **Beta I**; **Vikrama Chakri** = **Beta II**.
**Vinaya Vibhushanudu** = **Rudradeva**; **Andhra Deshadhiswara** = **Ganapatideva**.
xa: Rudradeva was also **Vidyabhushana**.
**Arigajakesari** = **Prola I**.
**Rayagajakesari** = **Rudramadevi**.

92.s: The title ‘Samadhigata Panchamahashabda’ was held by:
92.x: Prola I bore the title Samadhigata Panchamahashabda, along with Arigajakesari.
92.tq: Test an exact royal title against nearby Kakatiya rulers.
xs: **Samadhigata Panchamahashabda** was **Prola I's** title, along with **Arigajakesari**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**Beta I** was **Chola Chamuvardhi**, **Rudradeva** **Vidyabhushana**, and **Ganapatideva** **Andhra Deshadhiswara**.
xa: Prola I built the **Kesamudram** tank.
He changed the emblem from **Garuda to Varaha**.
He made **Anumakonda** the capital.

92.s: Which of the following statements regarding the title Kumara Rudradeva is correct?
o: It was the feudatory title of the Samanta Kakatiyas.
It was held by Rudradeva during his accession.
It was the title of Ganapatideva after his victory over the Pandyas.
It was held by Prataparudra II at the time of his accession.
92.x: Kumara Rudradeva was the title borne by Prataparudra II at his accession.
92.tq: Separate a personal accession title from titles of earlier Kakatiya rulers.
xs: **Kumara Rudradeva** was **Prataparudra II's** title at **accession**, so option **(4)** is correct.
The feudatory title was **Mahamandaleswara**. **Rudradeva's** titles were **Vidyabhushana** and **Vinaya Vibhushanudu**.
xa: Prataparudra II was the **last** Kakatiya.
His commander **Pedarudru** defeated Hoysala **Ballala III** after **1316**.
An **APPSC 2017** key gives **Rayagajakesari** to **Prataparudra**.

92.s: Which Kakatiya ruler bore the title 'Rayagajakesari' for her victory over the Yadavas of Devagiri?
92.x: Rudramadevi bore the title Rayagajakesari for her victory over the Yadavas of Devagiri.
