Land classes: **Magani** (wet), **Metta/Velipolam** (dry), **Thotapolam** (garden), **Podu** (newly cultivated).
**Bayyaram** tank (Khammam) was built by **Mailamba**, Ganapati's sister.

94.s: Land revenue during the Kakatiya period was generally fixed at what fraction of the produce?
94.x: Land revenue, referred to as bhaga or Ari, was generally one-sixth of the produce.
94.tq: Identify the precise revenue fraction and reject nearby traditional shares.
xs: Land revenue (**bhaga / Ari**) was generally **one-sixth (1/6)** of the produce — option **(2)** is correct.
Tax-paying farmers were called **Arigapulu**.
xa: ⚠ **One-fourth** is the share of land held by the **Nayankaras**, not the revenue rate.
**Koru** was the tax on wet (Magani) land; **Putti Pahindi** the tax on dry land.
Exempt: **temple lands**, **Brahmin grants**, **Ayagar lands** and tank-maintenance lands.

94.s: Which one of the following statements about land rights and taxation is correct?
o: All forest land was permanently exempt from taxation.
Temple, Brahmin and Ayagar lands paid the highest land revenue.
Dashabandhamu referred to lands maintained for tanks.
94.x: Dashabandhamu referred to lands connected with tank maintenance. Arigapulu were tax-paying farmers, while temple, Brahmin and Ayagar lands were tax-exempt.
94.tq: Match the land category with its fiscal treatment and reject absolute claims.
xs: **Dashabandhamu** was **tax-free land for tank upkeep** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Temple, Brahmin and Ayagar lands** were **exempt**, not the highest payers.
**Arigapulu** were **tax-paying farmers**, not exempt temple servants; forest clearance only got **tax concessions**.
xa: Land revenue (**Ari**) was generally **1/6** of produce.
**Golusukattu cheruvulu** (chain tanks) passed surplus water to the next tank.
Tank-building was one of the **Sapta Santanalu** (seven meritorious acts).

94.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
94.x: Ari denoted land revenue or Bhumi sistu. Koru was levied on wet land, Pullari was a grazing tax, and Kanika was a customary gift.
94.tq: Start from the sure meaning and eliminate the swapped tax descriptions.
xs: **Ari — Land revenue** (Bhumi sistu) is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**Koru** was the tax on **wet (Magani)** land, not dry land; **Pullari** was a **grazing** tax, not a road toll.
**Kanika** was a **customary gift** to the king or officials; the weekly-market tax was **Angadi Sunkam**.
xa: **Putti Pahindi** = dry-land tax; **Dari Sunkam** = road toll.
**Pellipannu** = wedding tax; **Alam** = tax on vegetables/produce.
Tax-paying farmers = **Arigapulu**.

94.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Putti Pahindi — Tax on dry land
94.x: Pellipannu was a wedding tax, not a cattle tax. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
94.tq: Find the one wrong description among closely related taxes and cesses.
xs: **Pellipannu — Tax on cattle** is wrongly matched — option **(3)** is the answer; Pellipannu was the **wedding (marriage) tax**.
The rest are right: **Angadi Sunkam** – weekly-market tax; **Putti Pahindi** – dry-land tax; **Dari Sunkam** – road toll.
xa: **Pullari** = grazing / grass-land tax.
**Koru** = tax on wet (Magani) land.
Other sunkams: **Burra**, **Madiga**, **Gandi**, **Revu**.

94.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Pullari — Grazing or grass-land tax
2. Kanika — Customary gift to the king or officials
3. Alam — Tax on vegetables or produce
4. Angadi Sunkam — Wedding tax
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
94.x: Pullari, Kanika and Alam are correctly matched. Angadi Sunkam was a weekly-market tax, whereas Pellipannu was the wedding tax.
94.tq: Split the options by checking the easily confused market and wedding cesses.
xs: Pairs 1–3 are right: **Pullari** – grazing tax; **Kanika** – customary gift; **Alam** – tax on vegetables/produce.
Pair 4 is wrong: **Angadi Sunkam** was the **weekly-market tax**; the wedding tax was **Pellipannu** — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: **Sunkam** = customs/tolls, collected by the **Sunkamanya Garlu**.
**Dari Sunkam** = road toll.
Other levies: **Siddhayam**, **Sangam**, **Pannu**, **Darshanam**, **Niruvidi**, **Ardhayam**; other tax **Antharayam**.

94.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Arikesari Samudram — Prola II
2. Ramappa tank — Recherla Rudra
3. Pakhala tank — Mummadi Nayaka
4. Laknavaram — Ganapatideva
94.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Arikesari Samudram was built by Prola II, Ramappa tank by Recherla Rudra, Pakhala tank by Mummadi Nayaka, and Laknavaram by Ganapatideva.
94.tq: Start with the sure builder-tank pairs and eliminate codes containing a swapped ruler or tank.
xs: All four pairs are right: **Arikesari Samudram** – **Prola II**; **Ramappa** tank – **Recherla Rudra**.
**Pakhala** tank – **Mummadi Nayaka** (son of Bayyana Nayaka); **Laknavaram** – **Ganapatideva** — so option **(4)**.
xa: ⚠ **Kesari Samudram** = **Rudradeva**; **Arikesari Samudram** = **Prola II** (APPSC G2 2012).
**Ghanapuram** was also built by **Ganapatideva**.
**Bayyaram** (Khammam) – **Mailamba**; **Kunda Samudram** – **Kundamamba**.

94.s: Who constructed the Ghanapuram tank?
94.x: Ghanapuram tank was constructed by Ganapatideva.
94.tq: Test a direct builder-tank association from the irrigation record.
xs: The **Ghanapuram** tank was built by **Ganapatideva** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Mailamba** built **Bayyaram**; **Kundamamba** built **Kunda Samudram**; **Surambika** built **Govardhana Samudram** (Reddi period).
xa: Ganapatideva also built **Laknavaram** (Lakkavaram).
**Pakhala** tank was built by **Mummadi Nayaka**, son of Ganapatideva's minister Bayyana Nayaka.
**Chouda Samudram** – **Malyala Chauda Senani**.

94.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
94.x: Pakhala tank was built by Mummadi Nayaka, son of Bayyana Nayaka, not by Mailamba. Mailamba was associated with Bayyaram tank.
94.tq: Find the swapped builder by comparing patrons of neighbouring tanks.
xs: **Pakhala tank — Mailamba** is wrong — option **(1)** is the answer; Pakhala was built by **Mummadi Nayaka**, son of **Bayyana Nayaka**.
**Mailamba**, Ganapati's sister, built the **Bayyaram** tank (Khammam).
The rest are right: **Ramappa** – **Recherla Rudra**; **Chouda Samudram** – **Malyala Chauda Senani**; **Govardhana Samudram** – **Surambika**.
xa: Surambika was the wife of **Peda Komati Vema** (Reddi period, **APPSC 2019**).
**Laknavaram** and **Ghanapuram** – **Ganapatideva**.
**Kesari Samudram** – **Rudradeva** (APPSC G2 2019 key).

94.s:
Which one of the following statements about tank irrigation is correct?

1. Large tanks were called Samudrams.
2. Golusukattu cheruvulu were linked chain tanks.
3. Surplus water could pass downhill from one tank to the next.
4. Dashabandhamu referred to tax-free land assigned for tank maintenance.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
94.x: All four statements are correct. Samudrams were large tanks, Golusukattu cheruvulu formed linked chains, surplus flowed to lower tanks, and Dashabandhamu was tax-free land for upkeep.
94.tq: Confirm the complete irrigation-system description, including the maintenance arrangement.
xs: Statement 1 correct: large tanks were called **Samudrams**.
Statements 2 and 3 correct: **Golusukattu cheruvulu** were **chain tanks** that passed **surplus water** to the next tank.
Statement 4 correct: **Dashabandhamu** was **tax-free land for tank upkeep** — so all four, option **(4)**.
xa: Tank-building was one of the **Sapta Santanalu** (seven meritorious acts).
The **Porumamilla** tank inscription (**1369**) lists **12 requisites of a good tank**.
The Kakatiya tank network still irrigates **Telangana**.

94.s: Tank-building was counted among the Sapta Santanalu, which refers to
94.x: Sapta Santanalu means seven meritorious works. The list included a son, temple, garden, tank, agrahara, literature and treasure.
94.tq: Distinguish a cultural-religious classification from administrative and fiscal categories.
xs: **Sapta Santanalu** means **seven meritorious works** — option **(1)** is correct.
The seven: **son**, **temple**, **garden**, **tank**, **agrahara**, **literature**, **treasure**.
xa: **Dashabandhamu** was tax-free land for tank upkeep.
Large tanks were called **Samudrams**; chain tanks were **Golusukattu cheruvulu**.
Women donors: **Mailamba** (Bayyaram) and **Kundamamba** (Kunda Samudram).

94.s: The Porumamilla tank inscription is associated with which combination?
o: 1369, Bhaskara, son of Bukka I, Vijayanagara period
1416, Deva Raya I, Motupalli, Reddi period
94.x: The Porumamilla tank inscription dates to 1369 and was issued by Bhaskara, son of Vijayanagara ruler Bukka I. It belongs to the Vijayanagara period and lists twelve requisites of a good tank.
94.tq: Combine date, person, dynasty and inscription subject to separate similar records.
xs: The **Porumamilla** (Kadapa) tank inscription is of **1369**, by **Bhaskara, son of Bukka I** — **Vijayanagara period**, option **(1)**.
**1244** is Ganapatideva's **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam**; **1282** is the **Tripurantakam inscription** on **Virabanajam**.
**1416** is the **Motupalli Dharma Sasanam** of **Deva Raya I** — a Vijayanagara record, not Reddi.
xa: The Porumamilla inscription lists **12 requisites of a good tank**.
It is often asked alongside the **Kakatiya tanks**.
Tank-building was one of the **Sapta Santanalu**.

94.s: Which one of the following pairs of women donors and tanks is correctly matched?
o: Mailamba — Bayyaram tank; Kundamamba — Kunda Samudram
Mailamba — Kunda Samudram; Kundamamba — Bayyaram tank
Mailamba — Warangal fort; Kundamamba — Bayyaram tank
94.x: Mailamba is associated with the Bayyaram tank and Kundamamba with Kunda Samudram.
94.tq: Start with the sure donor–tank pair and avoid swapping the two women.
xs: **Mailamba — Bayyaram tank** and **Kundamamba — Kunda Samudram** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Kesari Samudram** was built by **Rudradeva**, not Mailamba.
xa: Mailamba was **Ganapati's sister**; Bayyaram is in **Khammam**.
⚠ Some notes call Mailama the wife of **Recherla Rudra**; others say she married **Rudru**, son of **Natavadi Buddharaja**.
**Govardhana Samudram** – **Surambika**, wife of **Peda Komati Vema** (Reddi period).

94.s: According to the APPSC Group 2 (2019) answer key, the Kesari Samudram tank was built by
94.x: The APPSC G2 2019 key credits Kesari Samudram to Rudradeva (some sources give Prola I). Prola II built Arikesari Samudram (APPSC 2012), Ganapatideva built Laknavaram and Ghanapuram, and Mailamba built the Bayyaram tank.
94.tq: Kesari Samudram = Rudradeva; Arikesari Samudram = Prola II.
xs: The **APPSC G2 2019** key credits **Kesari Samudram** to **Rudradeva** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Prola II** built **Arikesari Samudram** (APPSC G2 2012); **Ganapatideva** built **Laknavaram** and **Ghanapuram**; **Mailamba** built **Bayyaram**.
xa: ⚠ One source credits Kesari Samudram to **Prola I** — follow the APPSC key.
Rudradeva also built the **Hanamkonda** tank.
**Ramappa** tank (Palampet) – **Recherla Rudra**.

94.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Ratna kambalu — Warangal
2. Knives — Nirmal
3. Diamonds — Golconda region
4. Iron — Warangal

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
94.x: Ratna kambalu was associated with Warangal, knives with Nirmal and diamonds with the Golconda region. Iron was associated with Guthikonda and Palnadu, not Warangal.
94.tq: Start from the sure industry–centre pairs and identify the reversed association.
xs: Pairs 1–3 are right: **Ratna kambalu** – **Warangal**; **knives** – **Nirmal**; **diamonds** – **Golconda region**.
Pair 4 is wrong: **iron** came from **Guthikonda and Palnadu**, not Warangal — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Warangal was also famed for **carpets/rugs** and **Mukkul vastralu**.
The Golconda diamonds were noted by **Marco Polo**.
Exports: textiles, spices, **diamonds**, gold, iron, rubies; imports: **Arabian war horses**, pearls, silk.

94.s: Marco Polo is said to have remarked that the fineness of which Kakatiya textile was such that a seven-yard saree could fit into a matchbox?
94.x: Marco Polo is said to have described the extremely fine cloth of the region in this manner; the material is identified as fine muslin.
94.tq: Test the distinctive traveller–observation association directly.
xs: The cloth so fine that a **7-yard saree** fitted in a **matchbox** was **fine muslin** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Ratna kambalu** (diamond blankets) and **Mukkul vastralu** were Warangal products, not the matchbox cloth.
xa: Cotton growing and **weaving** were major industries; fine muslin was exported.
Warangal was famed for **carpets/rugs** and fine textiles.
Trade partners: **China**, **Persia**, **Arabia**, **Ceylon**, **East Indies**.

94.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding painting in Orugallu during the Kakatiya period?
o: Machaladevi was a male court painter of the Kalyani Chalukyas.
Painting was confined to the Golconda region and had no association with Orugallu.
Orugallu had about 1,500 painters' houses, and Machaladevi was a woman painter.
Orugallu had about 150 painters' houses, led by Machaladevi.
94.x: Orugallu is described as having 1,500 painters' houses, and Machaladevi is identified as a woman painter.
94.tq: Separate the precise number from the nearby wrong figure and swapped identity.
xs: Orugallu had about **1,500 painters' houses**, and **Machaladevi** was a **woman painter** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **1,500** figure comes from **Palnati Veeracharitra**; Machaladevi was a woman, not a male court painter.
xa: Warangal was famed for **carpets/rugs** and **Ratna kambalu**.
**Orugallu** was the main inland trade centre.
Knives were made at **Nirmal**; iron at **Guthikonda** and **Palnadu**.

94.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Nakaram — Domestic trade
2. Nanadesi Pekkandru — Foreign trade
3. Ubhaya Nanadesi Pekkandru — Domestic and foreign trade
4. Ayyavali Ainuraru — Guild of 500

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
94.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Nakaram handled domestic trade, Nanadesi foreign trade, Ubhaya Nanadesi both types of trade, and Ayyavali Ainuraru was the guild of 500.
94.tq: Check every pair against the guild’s specialised scope or numerical identity.
xs: All four are right: **Nakaram** – **domestic** trade; **Nanadesi Pekkandru** – **foreign** trade.
**Ubhaya Nanadesi** – **both** domestic and foreign; **Ayyavali Ainuraru** – the great guild **"of 500"** — so option **(4)**.
xa: ⚠ **Chitrameli** was the samaya of **agricultural farmers** (APPSC G2 2019 key).
**Virabanajam** was licensed for Pakanadu, Vengi and Hanumakonda (**1282**).
Guild head: elected **Setti / Sreshthi**.

94.s: Virabanajam was licensed to operate in which of the following regions?
94.x: The Virabanajam guild was licensed for Pakanadu, Vengi and Hanumakonda, as recorded in the Tripurantakam inscription of 1282.
94.tq: Recall the specific licensed regions rather than confusing them with ports or foreign trading partners.
xs: **Virabanajam** was licensed for **Pakanadu, Vengi and Hanumakonda** — option **(3)** is correct.
The licence is recorded in the **Tripurantakam inscription** of **1282**.
**China, Persia, Arabia** were overseas trade partners; **Motupalli**, **Krishnapatnam**, **Hamsaladeevi** were ports.
xa: **Nakaram** = domestic-trade guild; **Nanadesi** = foreign; **Ubhaya Nanadesi** = both.
**Ayyavole 500** was the great trans-regional guild.
**Tripurantakam** was also one of the trade centres.

94.s: Which of the following was NOT a function or characteristic of the Kakatiya merchant guilds?
o: Exercising an exclusive royal monopoly over all trade
Maintaining their own seal or emblem
94.x: Guilds maintained seals or emblems, settled disputes and kept private military forces, but they did not possess an exclusive royal monopoly over all trade.
94.tq: Find the overbroad and exclusive statement that goes beyond the guild functions.
xs: Guilds had **no exclusive royal monopoly over all trade** — option **(1)** is the answer.
They did have their **own seal and emblem**, **settled disputes**, and kept a **private militia**.
xa: Guilds gave part of their profit to temples and acted as **bankers** and local administrators.
They bargained with the king for **tax concessions**, e.g. the **Motupalli** charter.
Samayas met in **temple mandapams** and had an emblem.

94.s:
Consider the following statements regarding merchant guilds:

1. A merchant was called a Behari.
2. Trade was referred to as Vyavaharam.
3. The head of a guild was called Setti or Sreshthi.
4. Guild members were drawn exclusively from Vaishyas.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
94.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Guild members came from several communities, including Settis, Reddis, Nayakulu, Boyas, Dasaris and Vaishyas, so statement 4 is false.
94.tq: Reject the exclusive-membership statement and retain the precise occupational terms.
xs: Statements 1–3 correct: a merchant was a **Behari**, trade was **Vyavaharam**, and the guild head was the elected **Setti / Sreshthi**.
Statement 4 wrong: members came from many castes — **Settis**, **Reddis**, **Nayakulu**, **Boyas**, **Dasaris** besides **Vaishyas (Komatis)** — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: **Samayas** were caste/occupational groups (APPSC G2 2019 key) that allowed **caste mobility**.
The Kakatiyas were themselves **Shudras**; Cynthia Talbot called it the **"Golden Age of the Shudras"**.
**Chitrameli** was the samaya of agricultural farmers.

94.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents the economic and administrative functions of merchant guilds?
o: Temple priests, military commanders and village headmen
Bankers, local administrators and negotiators for tax concessions
Coin minters, irrigation engineers and royal ambassadors
Judges, royal tax collectors and hereditary governors only
94.x: Merchant guilds acted as bankers and local administrators and negotiated with the king for tax concessions. The Motupalli charter illustrates this interaction.
94.tq: Identify the option that combines the guild’s economic, administrative and negotiating roles.
xs: Merchant guilds acted as **bankers**, **local administrators** and **negotiators for tax concessions** with the king — option **(2)** is correct.
The **Motupalli** charter is the example of guilds bargaining with the king for concessions.
xa: Guilds had their own **seal and emblem**, **settled disputes** and kept a **private militia**.
They gave part of their profit to **temples**; samayas met in **temple mandapams**.
Guild head: the elected **Setti / Sreshthi**.

94.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kakatiya period:
1. Samayas were caste or occupational groups.
2. Chitrameli was a samaya of agricultural farmers.
3. Nakaram was the guild that conducted foreign trade.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
94.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct (both APPSC G2 2019 key). Statement 3 is wrong: Nakaram was the domestic-trade guild, and Nanadesi Pekkandru handled foreign trade. So '1 only' is incomplete, and the options that include 3 are wrong.
94.tq: Chitrameli = farmers' samaya; Nakaram = domestic; Nanadesi = foreign.
xs: Statement 1 correct: **Samayas** were caste/occupational groups (**APPSC G2 2019** key).
Statement 2 correct: **Chitrameli** was the samaya of **agricultural farmers** (APPSC G2 2019 key).
Statement 3 wrong: **Nakaram** was the **domestic**-trade guild; **Nanadesi Pekkandru** did foreign trade — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **Ubhaya Nanadesi** Pekkandru traded in both domestic and foreign markets.
**Ayyavole 500** (Ayyavali Ainuraru) was the great trans-regional guild.
The Kakatiyas were themselves **Shudras**; samayas allowed **caste mobility**.

94.s: Which of the following was included among the exports of the Kakatiya period?
o: Iron tools, salt and timber only
Perfumes, horses, porcelain and silk alone
Grain, copper and medicinal herbs alone
94.x: The listed exports were textiles, spices, diamonds and gold. Perfumes and spices were mentioned among the imports.
94.tq: Distinguish the export list from the shorter list of imports.
xs: Kakatiya exports were **textiles, spices, diamonds and gold** (also iron, rubies) — option **(4)** is correct.
**Perfumes**, **horses** and **silk** were **imports**, not exports.
xa: Imports: **Arabian war horses** (for the cavalry), **pearls**, **silk**, **perfumes**, spices.
Textile exports included **fine muslin**; diamonds came from the **Golconda region**.
⚠ Export = **diamonds**, textiles; import = **Arabian war horses**.

94.s:
The Kakatiya trade network had commercial links with which of the following regions or countries?

1. China
2. Persia
3. Arabia
4. Ceylon
5. East Indies

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
94.x: The recorded trading partners included China, Persia, Arabia, Ceylon and the East Indies.
94.tq: Verify the complete list instead of stopping after identifying the first few familiar partners.
xs: Kakatiya trade partners were **China, Persia, Arabia, Ceylon and the East Indies** — all five, option **(4)**.
The main inland trade centre was **Orugallu**.
xa: Other trade centres: **Pedaganjam**, **Ghantasala**, **Gudivada**, **Macharla**, **Tripurantakam**, **Peruru**, **Manthena**.
Chief port: **Motupalli** (Desiyakonda Pattanam).
The Kakatiyas controlled routes between the **Deccan interior and the eastern coast**.

94.s: Which one of the following was imported for use by the Kakatiya cavalry?
94.x: Arabian war horses were imported for the cavalry. Fine muslin, rubies and iron were among the listed exports.
94.tq: Link the imported commodity to its stated military use.
xs: **Arabian war horses** were imported for the cavalry — option **(4)** is correct.
**Fine muslin**, **rubies** and **iron** were **exports**, not imports.
xa: Other imports: **pearls**, **silk**, **perfumes**, spices.
Prataparudra's army had **20,000 cavalry**, **100 elephants** and **900,000 infantry**.
The cavalry head was the **Ashwa Sahini** (Gangaya Sahini under Ganapatideva, Maraya under Prataparudra II).

94.s: The Kakatiyas controlled routes connecting the
o: Tamil interior and the Arabian Peninsula exclusively
Deccan interior and the eastern coast
Western coast and the Himalayan region
94.x: Kakatiya control extended over routes between the Deccan interior and the eastern coast.
94.tq: Identify the broad geographical direction of the controlled trade routes.
xs: The Kakatiyas controlled routes between the **Deccan interior and the eastern coast** — option **(2)** is correct.
Sources name only **ports** and **licensed regions** — no highway list.
xa: Main inland centre: **Orugallu**; chief port: **Motupalli**.
**Virabanajam** was licensed for **Pakanadu**, **Vengi** and **Hanumakonda** (Tripurantakam inscription, **1282**).
Ports: **Krishnapatnam** (Nellore coast), **Hamsaladeevi** (Krishna delta), **Machilipatnam** (Krishna).

94.s: Ports collecting import and export duties were known as
94.x: Ports that collected import and export duties were called Kara Pattanam.
94.tq: Distinguish the technical term for duty-collecting ports from names of actual ports and guilds.
xs: Ports that collected import/export duties were called **Kara Pattanam** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Abhaya** refers to the **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** (assurance of safety); **Samudram** means a large tank; **Nanadesi** was the foreign-trade guild.
xa: Motupalli, the chief port, was also called **Desiyakonda Pattanam** (APPSC G2 2019 key).
Customs/tolls = **Sunkam**, collected by the **Sunkamanya Garlu**.
Other ports: **Krishnapatnam**, **Hamsaladeevi**, **Machilipatnam**.

94.s: The Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam was issued by Ganapatideva in
94.x: Ganapatideva issued the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam in 1244 CE at Motupalli.
94.tq: Place the inscription date among the nearby dates associated with other inscriptions and periods.
xs: Ganapatideva issued the **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** in **1244 CE** — option **(2)** is correct.
**1282** is the **Tripurantakam inscription** (Virabanajam); **1369** is the **Porumamilla** tank inscription.
xa: It is also called the **Motupalli pillar inscription** / Abhaya Sasana.
⚠ **1244** Abhaya Sasanam = **Ganapatideva**; **1416** Dharma Sasanam = **Deva Raya I**.
"Abhaya" = assurance of **safety**; the issuer was **Ganapatideva**, not Rudrama.

94.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam:

1. It guaranteed safety to foreign merchants.
2. It remitted arbitrary taxes.
3. It promised compensation for losses caused by shipwreck or theft.
4. It authorised harassment of merchants by local officials.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
94.x: The charter protected foreign merchants, remitted arbitrary taxes and promised compensation for losses from shipwreck or theft. It stopped, rather than authorised, harassment by officials.
94.tq: Identify the reversed negative statement concerning official harassment.
xs: Statement 1 correct: it gave **safety to foreign merchants**.
Statements 2 and 3 correct: it **remitted arbitrary taxes** and promised **compensation for losses** from shipwreck or theft.
Statement 4 wrong: it **stopped harassment** by officials — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Issued by **Ganapatideva** in **1244 CE**; beneficiaries were **foreign and seafaring traders**.
**Siddayya Devudu** was the official posted at Motupalli (APPSC PYQ).
It is rated the **most important commercial document** of the period.

94.s: Who was appointed at Motupalli under the Abhaya Sasanam of Ganapatideva?
94.x: Siddayya Devudu was the official posted at Motupalli under Ganapatideva’s charter.
94.tq: Match the official with the charter and port, avoiding confusion with later rulers and builders.
xs: **Siddayya Devudu** was the official posted at **Motupalli** (APPSC PYQ) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Anavota Reddi** issued a later bilingual Motupalli charter (Reddi period); **Bhaskara** issued the **Porumamilla** tank inscription (**1369**).
**Malyala Chauda Senani** built the **Chouda Samudram** tank.
xa: The Abhaya Sasanam was issued by **Ganapatideva** in **1244 CE**.
Motupalli was also called **Desiyakonda Pattanam**.
The **Motupalli Dharma Sasanam (1416)** belongs to Vijayanagara's **Deva Raya I**.

94.s:
Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the two Motupalli protection charters?

1. Ganapatideva’s Abhaya Sasanam was issued in 1244 CE.
2. A later bilingual Telugu-Tamil charter was issued by Anavota Reddi.
3. The Motupalli Dharma Sasanam of 1416 was associated with Deva Raya I.
4. The 1416 Dharma Sasanam belonged to the reign of Ganapatideva.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
94.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The 1416 Motupalli Dharma Sasanam belonged to Vijayanagara ruler Deva Raya I, not Ganapatideva.
94.tq: Separate similar charters by issuer, date and dynasty.
xs: Statement 1 correct: **Ganapatideva's Abhaya Sasanam** dates to **1244 CE**.
Statement 2 correct: a later bilingual **Telugu-Tamil** charter was issued by **Anavota Reddi** (Reddi period).
Statement 3 correct, 4 wrong: the **1416 Dharma Sasanam** was **Deva Raya I's**, not Ganapatideva's — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Deva Raya I issued it after taking Motupalli from **Kondavidu**.
The Abhaya Sasanam assured **safety** to foreign merchants and remitted arbitrary taxes.
Motupalli's long life: a **Vishnukundin-era** port and later one of **Vijayanagara's** Andhra ports.

94.s: Which one of the following ports was located on the Nellore coast?
94.x: Krishnapatnam was situated on the Nellore coast. Hamsaladeevi was associated with the Krishna delta, while Machilipatnam was associated with Krishna.
94.tq: Use coastal-location discrimination among the listed ports.
xs: **Krishnapatnam** lay on the **Nellore coast** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Hamsaladeevi** was in the **Krishna delta**; **Machilipatnam** in **Krishna**; **Motupalli** was the chief port.
xa: Motupalli was also called **Desiyakonda Pattanam** (APPSC G2 2019 key).
**Kara Pattanam** = ports collecting import/export duties.
⚠ One source places **Hamsaladeevi** in **Guntur**.

94.s: Motupalli, the chief port of the Kakatiyas, was also known as
94.x: Motupalli was also called Desiyakonda (Deseeyakkonda) Pattanam (APPSC G2 2019 key). Kara Pattanam is a general term for ports that collected import and export duties. Hamsaladeevi (Krishna delta) and Krishnapatnam (Nellore coast) were separate ports.
94.tq: Motupalli = Desiyakonda Pattanam = Marco Polo's Mutfili.
xs: Motupalli was also called **Desiyakonda Pattanam** (Deseeyakkonda Pattanam; **APPSC G2 2019** key) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kara Pattanam** is a general term for ports collecting duties; **Hamsaladeevi** and **Krishnapatnam** were separate ports.
xa: Ganapatideva issued the **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** there in **1244 CE**.
**Siddayya Devudu** was the official posted at Motupalli.
Vishnukundin-era ports: **Motupalli and Kodur**.

94.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the metal or nature of the coin?
94.x: Gadya or Gadyana was a gold coin. Ruka was silver, Mada was a gold Kakatiya-period coin, and Visa was a small fraction.
94.tq: Match the denomination with its metal while separating full coins from fractions.
xs: **Gadya (Gadyana) — Gold** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**Ruka** was **silver**, not gold; **Mada** was a **gold** coin, not silver.
**Visa** was a **small fraction**, not a full gold coin.
xa: **Mada** was the Kakatiya-period gold coin; **Nishka** was also gold.
**Adduga** and **Padika** are other types named in inscriptions.
Few Kakatiya coins survive; types are known mainly from **inscriptions**.

94.s: Which of the following groups contains only coin types named in Kakatiya inscriptions?
94.x: Adduga, Padika, Ruka and Visa were all named as coin types or denominations. The other options mix coins with taxes and cesses.
94.tq: Separate monetary denominations from taxation terms in a mixed list.
xs: **Adduga, Padika, Ruka, Visa** are all coin types — option **(1)** is correct.
The other options mix in taxes: **Kanika** (customary gift), **Pellipannu** (wedding tax), **Dari Sunkam** (road toll), **Ari** (land revenue), **Koru** (wet-land tax), **Pullari** (grazing tax).
xa: Gold coins: **Gadya (Gadyana)**, **Mada**, **Nishka**.
**Ruka** = silver; **Visa** = small fraction.
Coin types are known mainly from **inscriptions**, as few coins survive.

94.s: Which of the following was described as a small fraction among Kakatiya-period coin denominations?
94.x: Visa was described as a small fraction. Gadya, Mada and Nishka were associated with gold coinage.
94.tq: Use the denomination description rather than assuming every named coin had equal value.
xs: **Visa** was a **small fraction** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Nishka**, **Gadya** and **Mada** were **gold** coins.
xa: **Mada** was the Kakatiya-period gold coin.
**Ruka** was silver.
**Adduga** and **Padika** were other types named in inscriptions.

94.s: Our knowledge of Kakatiya coin types such as Mada, Gadyana and Ruka comes mainly from:
94.x: Few Kakatiya coins survive, so their types are known mainly from inscriptions.
94.tq: Few coins, many inscriptions.
xs: Kakatiya coin types are known mainly from **inscriptions**, as **few coins survive** — option **(3)** is correct.
So there are no large surviving hoards to rely on.
xa: **Mada** = gold, the Kakatiya-period coin; **Gadyana** = gold; **Ruka** = silver.
**Visa** = small fraction; **Adduga** and **Padika** are other types.
The **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** (**1244**) is itself an inscription — a pillar inscription.

94.s:
Consider the following statements regarding interpretations of the Kakatiya state:
1. Burton Stein used the label ‘segmentary state’.
2. Romila Thapar described it as a ‘metropolitan state’.
3. Both labels represent identical interpretations of the nature of the Kakatiya state.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
94.x: Burton Stein’s interpretation is associated with the term ‘segmentary state’, while Romila Thapar used the expression ‘metropolitan state’. Statement 3 is false because the two labels reflect different interpretations.
94.tq: Separate the two scholars’ distinctive labels and reject the statement that erases their difference.
xs: Statement 1 correct: **Burton Stein** compared the Kakatiya state to a **segmentary state**.
Statement 2 correct: **Romila Thapar** called it a **"metropolitan state"**.
Statement 3 wrong: the two are **different, competing** labels — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: Most scholars call it a **"decentralised monarchy"**.
Cynthia Talbot called the period the **"Golden Age of the Shudras"**.
Under the Kakatiyas, religion and politics became **non-Brahmin** (APPSC 2019 key).

94.s: With reference to the social and political significance of the Kakatiya period, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Religion and politics became exclusively Brahmin, and Cynthia Talbot called it the ‘Metropolitan Age’
Religion and politics became non-Brahmin, and Cynthia Talbot called the period the ‘Golden Age of the Shudras’
Religion and politics became exclusively royal, and Romila Thapar called it the ‘Golden Age of the Shudras’
Religion and politics became non-Brahmin, and Burton Stein called it the ‘Golden Age of the Shudras’
94.x: Under the Kakatiyas, religion and politics became non-Brahmin. Cynthia Talbot referred to this period as the ‘Golden Age of the Shudras’.
94.tq: Match the correct scholar with the exact interpretive phrase instead of the nearby scholars’ labels.
xs: Religion and politics became **non-Brahmin** (**APPSC 2019** key), and **Cynthia Talbot** called it the **"Golden Age of the Shudras"** — option **(2)** is correct.
**"Metropolitan state"** is **Romila Thapar's** label; **Burton Stein** used the **segmentary state** comparison.
xa: The Kakatiyas were themselves **Shudras**; samayas allowed **caste mobility**.
Guild membership included **Settis**, **Reddis**, **Nayakulu**, **Boyas**, **Dasaris** besides Vaishyas.
Most scholars call the state a **"decentralised monarchy"**.

94.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Military-land arrangement)

a. Kakatiya
b. Vijayanagara
c. Mughal

List-II (Institution or linkage)

i. Jagir linking land with military duty
 ii. Nayankara
 iii. Amaranayaka

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
94.x: The Kakatiya arrangement was called Nayankara, the comparable Vijayanagara arrangement was Amaranayaka, and the Mughal parallel was the jagir linkage between land and military duty.
94.tq: Start with the sure dynasty–institution pairs and then identify the Mughal parallel.
xs: Correct match **a–ii, b–iii, c–i** — option **(1)**.
**Kakatiya** – **Nayankara**; **Vijayanagara** – **Amaranayaka**; **Mughal** – **jagir** linking land with military duty.
xa: The break-up of the Amaranayaka system produced the **Poligars**.
Under Vijayanagara the land was **Amaram** and the tribute **Kappam/kist**.
Kakatiya Nayakas held villages called **Nayakasthalam** in lieu of salary.

94.s: A dispute relating to the Gonugu canal during the Kakatiya period was settled after the minister consulted the villagers. What does this episode primarily illustrate?
o: People’s participation in resolving a water dispute
The replacement of tank irrigation by sea trade
The centralisation of all village decisions in the royal court
Exclusive control of irrigation by military commanders
94.x: Minister Mancharaju settled the Gonugu canal water dispute after consulting the villagers. The episode illustrates people’s participation in local water management.
94.tq: Identify the administrative principle illustrated by the action taken in the specific local dispute.
xs: The **Gonugu canal** episode shows **people's participation in resolving a water dispute** — option **(1)** is correct.
Minister **Mancharaju** settled it after **consulting the villagers**.
xa: The Kakatiya tank network still irrigates **Telangana**.
**Dashabandhamu** was tax-free land for tank upkeep.
Chain tanks (**Golusukattu cheruvulu**) passed surplus water to the next tank.

94.s: The Motupalli charter is regarded by the CDI as which of the following?
o: The most important religious document of the Kakatiya period
The earliest document describing the Nayankara system
The principal record of the Gonugu canal dispute
The most important commercial document of the period, showing the state’s stake in sea trade
94.x: The CDI considers the Motupalli charter the most important commercial document of the period. It demonstrates the state’s interest in sea trade.
94.tq: Distinguish the document’s commercial significance from other Kakatiya administrative and irrigation themes.
xs: The **Motupalli charter** is the **most important commercial document of the period**, showing the **state's stake in sea trade** — option **(4)** is correct.
The Nayankara system's sources are **Neeti Sastra Muktavali** and **Pratapa Charitra**; the Gonugu canal episode is a separate record.
xa: Issued by **Ganapatideva** in **1244 CE**; it assured **safety to foreign merchants**.
It remitted arbitrary taxes and promised compensation for **shipwreck or theft**.
⚠ Not to be confused with **Deva Raya I's** **Motupalli Dharma Sasanam (1416)**.

94.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the long continuity of Motupalli as a port?
o: It was associated only with Vijayanagara and not with the Vishnukundins
It belonged exclusively to the Mughal jagir system
It was a Vishnukundin-era port but disappeared before the Vijayanagara period
It appears among Vishnukundin-era ports and later among Vijayanagara’s Andhra ports
94.x: Motupalli was among the Vishnukundin-era ports and also appears among Vijayanagara’s Andhra ports, along with Pulicat and Machilipatnam. This indicates its long continuity as a port.
94.tq: Compare the port lists across the two periods and identify the common name.
xs: Motupalli appears among **Vishnukundin-era ports** and later among **Vijayanagara's Andhra ports** — option **(4)** is correct.
That shows its **long life** as a port; it was not exclusive to any one dynasty.
xa: Vishnukundin-era ports: **Motupalli and Kodur**.
Vijayanagara's Andhra ports: **Pulicat**, **Motupalli**, **Machilipatnam**.
Under the Kakatiyas it was the **chief port**, also called **Desiyakonda Pattanam**.

95.s: During the Kakatiya period, caste associations were known as:
95.x: Caste associations were called Samayas.
95.tq: Test the exact institutional term.
xs: Kakatiya caste associations were called **Samayas** (**APPSC G2 2019** answer) — option **(3)** is correct.
**Nakaram** was the body of the **Vaishyas (Komatis)**; **Mahajanas** were the **Brahmins**.
**Simha** and **Shakti Parishat** were the two Kalamukha divisions, not caste bodies.
xa: Each samaya elected a **senior head** who settled disputes; members paid dues to the caste head.
**Ashtadasha kulas** = **18 occupational groups** inside Warangal fort (Kreedabhiramam).
Rising Sudra warrior-peasant groups: **Reddis**, **Kammas**, **Velamas** (Padmanayakas).

95.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Group)
 a. Brahmins
 b. Vaishyas or Komatis
 c. Panchavarmavaru
 d. Panchanamuvaru

List-II (Body or identity)
 i. Five artisan groups
 ii. Nakaram
 iii. Mahajanas
 iv. Saaminumani vaaru

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
95.x: Brahmins were identified as Mahajanas, Komatis as Nakaram, Panchavarmavaru as Saaminumani vaaru, and Panchanamuvaru as the five artisan groups.
95.tq: Start from the sure group–identity pairs and eliminate the codes.
xs: Correct match **a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Brahmins** – **Mahajanas**; **Vaishyas (Komatis)** – **Nakaram**.
**Panchavarmavaru** – **Saaminumani vaaru**; **Panchanamuvaru** – the **five artisan (smith) groups**.
xa: Brahmins were split into **Vaidikas** and **Niyogis**.
Other castes: **Telikas**, **Gollas**, **Sales** (weavers), **Boyas**, **Medharas**, **Gandla**, **Upparas**.
⚠ Veerashaiva castes = **Lingayats, Balijas, Jangamas**; Vaishnava = **Satanis, Dasaris**.

95.s: The term 'Ashtadasha kulas' in the Kakatiya context refers to:
o: Eighteen royal dynasties of the Deccan
Eighteen occupational groups living inside Warangal fort
95.x: Ashtadasha kulas denotes the 18 occupational groups that lived inside Warangal fort, as mentioned in Kreedabhiramam.
95.tq: Decode the numerical social classification from its context.
xs: **Ashtadasha kulas** were the **18 occupational groups** living **inside Warangal fort** — option **(4)** is correct.
The term comes from **Kreedabhiramam**.
xa: Caste associations were called **Samayas**, each with an elected senior head.
Weavers were called **Sales**; other castes included **Telikas**, **Gollas**, **Boyas**, **Gandla**.
⚠ **Eighteen** = Ashtadasha kulas; **twelve** = Ayagars; **72** = Niyogas.

95.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
95.x: Veerashaivism contributed to the rise of Lingayats, Balijas and Jangamas. Vaishnavism was associated with Satanis and Dasaris.
95.tq: Separate the caste groups associated with Veerashaivism and Vaishnavism.
xs: **Veerashaivism — Lingayats, Balijas and Jangamas** is correctly matched — option **(3)**.
**Satanis and Dasaris** came from **Vaishnavism**, not Veerashaivism.
**Komatis** had the **Nakaram**; the **Kalamukhas** were a Shaiva sect, not a caste source.
xa: Reform sects (**Veerashaiva**, **Veeravaishnava**) opposed Brahminical practice and produced new caste groups.
In Veerashaivism, followers were **Lingayats** and gurus were **Jangamas**.
Founder of Veerashaivism: **Basaveshwara**.

95.s: Which one of the following groups was identified as a rising Sudra warrior-peasant group under the Kakatiyas?
95.x: Reddis, Kammas and Velamas, also referred to as Padmanayakas, emerged as Sudra warrior-peasant groups.
95.tq: Use the group-composition clue to distinguish social categories.
xs: The rising Sudra warrior-peasant groups were the **Reddis, Kammas and Velamas** (Padmanayakas) — option **(1)** is correct.
They served as **Nayakas** under the Kakatiyas.
**Satanis, Dasaris** (Vaishnava) and **Jangamas** (Veerashaiva) were sect-based groups; **Mahajanas/Niyogis** were Brahmins.
xa: The **Kakatiyas were Sudras** (originally of **Pulinda** origin) — the culmination of the non-Brahmanical trend.
**Komatis** (Vaishyas) had the **Nakaram**.
**Sales** were weavers; **Medharas** and **Upparas** were other castes.

95.s: The rise of Sudra kingship among the Kakatiyas is regarded as:
o: The beginning of Jain political rule in Andhra
The revival of exclusive Brahminical monarchy
The decline of all peasant-warrior groups
The culmination of the non-Brahmanical trend
95.x: The Kakatiyas, described as Sudras of originally Pulinda origin who adopted the Varna order, represented the culmination of the non-Brahmanical trend.
95.tq: Connect the political development with its historical interpretation.
xs: Sudra kingship of the Kakatiyas is the **culmination of the non-Brahmanical trend** — option **(4)** is correct.
The **Kakatiyas were Sudras**, originally of **Pulinda** origin before adopting the Varna order.
It strengthened peasant-warrior groups (**Reddis**, **Kammas**, **Velamas**) as Nayakas, rather than ending them.
xa: Reform sects (**Veerashaiva**, **Veeravaishnava**) also opposed Brahminical practice.
Cynthia Talbot's phrase for the period: **"Golden Age of the Shudras"**.
Early Kakatiyas were **Jains**; they became Shaivas from **Prola II / Rudradeva**.

95.s: The legal principle recorded in the Purushartha Saramu provided that a woman's property passed to her:
o: The king after the woman's death
Sons alone through the male line
95.x: Purushartha Saramu records that a woman's property passed to her daughters and daughter's daughters, indicating a comparatively progressive legal outlook.
95.tq: Identify the precise inheritance rule rather than a nearby legal text.
xs: **Purushartha Saramu** says a woman's property passed to her **daughters and daughter's daughters** — option **(1)** is correct.
This shows a comparatively **progressive** Kakatiya legal outlook (**APPSC G2 2019**).
xa: Author: **Sivadevayya**.
The same book describes the **72 Niyogas** and the king's daily council routine.
⚠ Distractors: **Vignaneswaram** (Ketana), **Nitisara** (Rudradeva), **Niti Shastra Muktavali** (Baddena).

95.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
95.x: Niti Shastra Muktavali is associated with Baddena, not Sivadevayya. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
95.tq: Find the swapped author–work pair.
xs: **Niti Shastra Muktavali — Sivadevayya** is wrong — option **(4)** is the answer; Niti Shastra Muktavali is by **Baddena**.
Correct pairs: **Nitisara** – **Rudradeva**; **Purushartha Saramu** – **Sivadevayya**; **Vignaneswaram** – **Ketana**.
xa: Purushartha Saramu records that a woman's property passed to her **daughters and daughter's daughters**.
It also describes the **72 Niyogas** and the king's daily council routine.
**Panditaradhya Charitra** tells of Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya's debate with a Buddhist acharya.

95.s: Besides its legal content, Purushartha Saramu is an important administrative source because it gives information about:
o: The military conquests of the Reddi kings
The 72 Niyogas and the king's daily council routine
The 18 occupational groups inside Warangal fort only
The division of Kalamukha sects into two parishads
95.x: Purushartha Saramu also describes the 72 Niyogas, or departments, and the daily routine of the king's council.
95.tq: Distinguish the administrative content of the text from unrelated social facts.
xs: **Purushartha Saramu** also describes the **72 Niyogas** (departments) and the **king's daily council routine** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **18 occupational groups** inside Warangal fort come from **Kreedabhiramam**, not this book.
xa: Author: **Sivadevayya**.
Its legal content: a woman's property passed to her **daughters and daughter's daughters** (APPSC G2 2019).
Kalamukha divisions: **Simha Parishat** (Andhra) and **Shakti Parishat** (Karnataka).

95.s: Which of the following practices is recorded as widespread in the Kakatiya social context?
o: Exclusive practice of Jain monastic fasting by all communities
Superstition, animal sacrifice and self-sacrifice by devotees of Shiva
Abandonment of all forms of religious observance
Complete prohibition of animal sacrifice and ritual worship
95.x: The period witnessed widespread superstition, animal sacrifice and self-sacrifice by devotees of Shiva.
95.tq: Identify the cluster of customs associated with the period.
xs: Widespread **superstition**, **animal sacrifice** and **self-sacrifice by devotees of Shiva** marked the period — option **(2)** is correct.
So animal sacrifice was not prohibited, and religious observance was not abandoned.
xa: **Hero-stones (viragallu)** commemorated warriors who died in battle or cattle raids.
Temple women and courtesans (**Kalavatis**) sustained dance and music.
⚠ **Veerashaivism** itself rejected animal sacrifice.

95.s: Hero-stones, or viragallu, commemorated warriors who died:
95.x: Viragallu were memorial stones for warriors who died in battle or during cattle raids.
95.tq: Link the memorial object with the two stated circumstances of death.
xs: **Viragallu** (hero-stones) commemorated warriors who died **in battle or cattle raids** — option **(3)** is correct.
Temple women (**Kalavatis**) were linked to dance and music, not to hero-stones.
xa: Social customs included **superstition**, **animal sacrifice** and **self-sacrifice by devotees of Shiva**.
Festivals were royal occasions.
Kalamukhas gave **anna dana** at feeding houses.

95.s: The early Kakatiyas were followers of which religion before becoming Shaivas from the time of Prola II or Rudradeva?
95.x: The early Kakatiyas were Jains; they later became Shaivas from the period of Prola II or Rudradeva.
95.tq: Test the religious transition in chronological form.
xs: The **early Kakatiyas** followed **Jainism** (**APPSC G2 2011**) — option **(3)** is correct.
They became **Shaivas** from **Prola II / Rudradeva**.
xa: **Prola II** built the **Padmakshi temple**, originally a **Jain shrine**.
Jainism declined under **Kalamukha** and **Veerashaiva** hostility.
**Visveshwara Shambhu**, Ganapatideva's guru, destroyed **36 Jain villages**.

95.s: Hanumakonda, also known as Anmakonda, was important to Jainism because it:
o: Contained the headquarters of the Simha Parishat in Karnataka
Served as a refuge for Jains persecuted under the Eastern Chalukyas
Was the only centre of Pasupata Shaivism
95.x: Hanumakonda provided refuge to Jains persecuted under the Eastern Chalukyas.
95.tq: Link the centre with its distinctive historical function.
xs: **Hanumakonda (Anmakonda)** was a **refuge for Jains persecuted under the Eastern Chalukyas** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Simha Parishat** was the **Andhra** Kalamukha division (Karnataka had Shakti Parishat); **Lakulisa** founded Pasupata.
xa: **Padmakshi temple** at Hanumakonda was built by **Prola II**; originally a Jain shrine.
**Ganapati** later persecuted Jains at **Anmakonda**.
Jain centres: **Bodhan**, **Vemulawada**, **Patancheru**, **Kolanupaka**, **Potlacheruvu**.

95.s: The Padmakshi temple at Hanumakonda was originally:
o: A Pasupata temple built by Lakulisa
95.x: The Padmakshi temple, built by Prola II, was originally a Jain shrine.
95.tq: Use the temple's original religious identity rather than its later association.
xs: The **Padmakshi temple** was originally a **Jain shrine** — option **(4)** is correct.
It was built by **Prola II**, from whose time the Kakatiyas turned Shaiva.
xa: **Hanumakonda** was a refuge for Jains persecuted under the **Eastern Chalukyas**.
Jain deities were absorbed as Hindu goddesses: **Kakitamma** and **Jogulamba**.
The Kakatiyas are credited with the **final eradication of Jainism** in the region.

95.s: Which one of the following is NOT listed as a Jain centre in the Kakatiya region?
95.x: Bodhan, Vemulawada and Kolanupaka were Jain centres. Tripurantakam is listed among the centres of Kalamukha and Pasupata sects.
95.tq: Separate Jain centres from the Shaiva sect centres.
xs: **Tripurantakam** is not a Jain centre — option **(2)** is the answer; it was a **Kalamukha / Shaiva** centre.
Jain centres: **Bodhan**, **Vemulawada**, **Patancheru**, **Kolanupaka**, **Potlacheruvu**.
xa: ⚠ **Vemulawada** appears in both lists — a Jain centre and a Kalamukha / Shaiva centre.
Kalamukha / Shaiva centres: **Srisailam**, **Alampur**, **Kaleshwaram**, **Tripurantakam**, **Mahanandi**.
**Hanumakonda** sheltered Jains persecuted under the Eastern Chalukyas.

95.s: Which of the following contributed to the decline of Jainism in the Kakatiya region?
o: The decline of all temple institutions
The spread of Vaishnava temple festivals alone
The rise of the Aradhya stream alone
95.x: The decline of Jainism was associated with hostility from Kalamukha and Veerashaiva groups and persecution by certain Kakatiya authorities.
95.tq: Identify the stated cause rather than an adjacent religious development.
xs: Jainism declined because of **Kalamukha and Veerashaiva hostility** — option **(3)** is correct.
Temple institutions did not decline — temples were **landed corporations**.
xa: **Visveshwara Shambhu** destroyed **36 Jain villages**; **Brahmayya** destroyed Jain settlements.
**Ganapati** persecuted Jains at **Anmakonda**.
The Kakatiyas are credited with the **final eradication** of Jainism in the region.

95.s: Jain deities were absorbed into Hindu worship in the form of goddesses such as:
95.x: Jain deities were absorbed as Hindu goddesses, including Kakitamma and Jogulamba.
95.tq: Recall the named examples of religious assimilation.
xs: Jain deities were absorbed as the Hindu goddesses **Kakitamma and Jogulamba** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Padmakshi** and **Ramanatha** are temples; **Simha / Shakti Parishat** are Kalamukha divisions.
xa: The **Padmakshi temple** was originally a Jain shrine, built by **Prola II**.
Early Kakatiyas were **Jains** (APPSC G2 2011).
The Kakatiya age shows **religious tolerance and syncretism**.

95.s: Who is regarded as the founder of the Pasupata sect?
95.x: Pasupata is identified as the oldest Shaiva sect and is associated with Lakulisa, also called Nakulisa.
95.tq: Use the founder–sect association directly.
xs: **Pasupata**, the oldest Shaiva sect, was founded by **Lakulisa (Nakulisa)** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Basaveshwara** founded **Veerashaivism**; **Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya** led the **Aradhya** stream.
**Kalasana/Kalanana**, Lakulisa's disciple, is linked to the **Kalamukha** sect.
xa: **Kapalikas** (skull-bowl ascetics) were an offshoot of **Pasupata** (APPSC G2 2019).
Pasupata Shaivism stayed popular into the **Reddi** period (APPSC G2 2011) and declined under Vijayanagara.
The Kakatiyas patronised the "extremist" **Pasupata and Kalamukha** sects.

95.s: The Kalamukha sect was associated with which of the following characteristics?
o: It was founded by Kalasana or Kalanana and its members managed temples.
It rejected all temple institutions and opposed Shaivism.
It was led by Brahmin Shaivas who retained Vedic ritual.
It was an offshoot of Pasupata consisting of skull-bowl ascetics.
95.x: Kalamukha was associated with Kalasana or Kalanana, a disciple of Lakulisa, and its members acted as temple managers.
95.tq: Separate the Kalamukha description from the Kapalika description.
xs: The **Kalamukha** sect was founded by **Kalasana/Kalanana**, and its members were **temple managers** — option **(1)** is correct.
Brahmin Shaivas keeping Vedic ritual were the **Aradhyas**; skull-bowl ascetics from Pasupata were the **Kapalikas**.
xa: Kalasana was a disciple of **Lakulisa**.
Kalamukha divisions: **Simha Parishat** (Andhra) vs **Shakti Parishat** (Karnataka).
Kalamukhas gave **anna dana** (food charity).

95.s:
Consider the following statements about Shaiva sects in the Kakatiya period:
1. The Kakatiyas patronised the 'extremist' Pasupata and Kalamukha sects.
2. The Kapalikas, the skull-bowl ascetics, were an offshoot of the Kalamukha sect.
3. Pasupata Shaivism remained a popular faith into the Reddi period and declined under Vijayanagara.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
95.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Kapalikas were an offshoot of the Pasupata sect (APPSC G2 2019), not of the Kalamukhas. So A, C and D, which include statement 2, are wrong.
95.tq: Kapalika and 'religion of the Reddi Rajas' both answer Pasupata.
xs: Statement 1 correct: the Kakatiyas patronised the "extremist" **Pasupata and Kalamukha** sects.
Statement 2 wrong: the **Kapalikas** were an offshoot of **Pasupata** (APPSC G2 2019), not Kalamukha.
Statement 3 correct: **Pasupata** stayed popular into the **Reddi** period and declined under **Vijayanagara** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Exam angle: "Kapalikas arose from which doctrine" and "popular religion of the Reddi Rajas" — both **Pasupata**.
Pasupata founder: **Lakulisa (Nakulisa)**.
⚠ **Simha Parishat** = Andhra; **Shakti Parishat** = Karnataka.

95.s: Betaraja and Durgaraja were disciples of:
o: A Kalamukhacharya of the Srisailam Shila matha
95.x: Betaraja and Durgaraja were disciples of a Kalamukhacharya belonging to the Srisailam Shila matha.
95.tq: Use the ruler–guru–institution relationship without substituting a famous religious teacher.
xs: **Betaraja and Durgaraja** were disciples of a **Kalamukhacharya of the Srisailam Shila matha** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Basaveshwara** was the founder of Veerashaivism, minister of **Kalachuri Bijjala**.
xa: **Srisailam** was also the main **Veerashaiva** centre in Andhra.
**Srisailam Mallikarjuna** temple held lands in **70 villages** (some notes say **52**).
Other Shaiva gurus: **Rameshwara Pandita**, **Dharmashiva**.

95.s: Which of the following is NOT listed as a centre of the Kalamukha and Pasupata sects?
95.x: Alampur, Kaleshwaram and Mahanandi are listed as centres of the Kalamukha and Pasupata sects. Patancheru is listed among Jain centres.
95.tq: Separate the Shaiva-centre list from the Jain-centre list.
xs: **Patancheru** is a **Jain** centre, not Kalamukha / Pasupata — option **(2)** is the answer.
Kalamukha / Shaiva centres: **Srisailam**, **Alampur**, **Vemulawada**, **Kaleshwaram**, **Tripurantakam**, **Mahanandi**.
xa: Jain centres: **Bodhan**, **Vemulawada**, **Patancheru**, **Kolanupaka**, **Potlacheruvu**.
**Srisailam**, **Alampur**, **Draksharama** formed the Shaiva-Shakta axis of Andhra.
The Kakatiyas patronised the **Pasupata and Kalamukha** sects.

95.s:
Consider the following statements about Veerashaivism:
1. Its founder Basaveshwara was a minister of Kalachuri Bijjala in Karnataka.
2. Its followers were called Jangamas and its gurus were called Lingayats.
3. Its motto 'Kayakave Kailasa' means 'work is worship'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
95.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 swaps the terms: followers were Lingayats and the gurus were Jangamas (its texts were the Agamas). So A misses statement 3, and B and D wrongly include statement 2.
95.tq: Lingayats follow, Jangamas teach.
xs: Statement 1 correct: **Basaveshwara** was a minister of **Kalachuri Bijjala** (Karnataka).
Statement 2 wrong: it swaps the terms — followers were **Lingayats**, gurus were **Jangamas**.
Statement 3 correct: **"Kayakave Kailasa"** = **work is worship** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: Veerashaivism's texts were the **Agamas**; it was the **first social-reform religion** in Andhra.
Followers wore the **Ishtalinga** on the body.
It rejected **Vedas**, **caste**, **untouchability**, **child marriage** and **animal sacrifice**.

95.s: Which of the following was NOT a tenet or practice associated with Veerashaivism?
o: Acceptance of child marriage as a religious obligation
Wearing the Ishtalinga on the body
95.x: Veerashaivism rejected child marriage. It also rejected untouchability and animal sacrifice and required the wearing of the Ishtalinga.
95.tq: Spot the practice that contradicts the reformist character of the sect.
xs: **Acceptance of child marriage** was not a Veerashaiva tenet — option **(1)** is the answer; Veerashaivism **rejected child marriage**.
It did reject **untouchability** and **animal sacrifice**, and followers wore the **Ishtalinga**.
xa: It also rejected the **Vedas** and **caste**.
Motto: **"Kayakave Kailasa"** (work is worship).
⚠ The **Aradhyas** kept varna; radical Veerashaivas rejected caste.

95.s:
Consider the following statements about Veerashaivism in Andhra:
1. The word 'Veerashaiva' is absent from Andhra inscriptions; its followers are called Veeravratulu or Asankhyakulu.
2. It was the first social-reform religion in Andhra.
3. Its main centre in Andhra was Kolanupaka.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
95.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the main Veerashaiva centre in Andhra was Srisailam; Kolanupaka is listed among Jain centres. So A misses statement 2, and C and D wrongly include statement 3.
95.tq: Veerashaiva centre = Srisailam; Kolanupaka is a Jain-centre distractor.
xs: Statement 1 correct: "Veerashaiva" is absent from Andhra inscriptions; followers are called **Veeravratulu / Asankhyakulu**.
Statement 2 correct: it was the **first social-reform religion** in Andhra.
Statement 3 wrong: the main Andhra centre was **Srisailam**; **Kolanupaka** was a Jain centre — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Founder: **Basaveshwara**, minister of **Kalachuri Bijjala**.
Followers = **Lingayats**; gurus = **Jangamas**; texts = **Agamas**.
The Kakatiyas stayed **neutral** and did not persecute Lingayats.

95.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Aradhya stream:
1. It was led by Brahmin Shaivas.
2. Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya was its prominent leader.
3. It rejected Vedic ritual and the Varna order.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Aradhya stream retained Vedic ritual and the Varna order, so statement 3 is false.
95.tq: Locate the false statement by comparing the Aradhya and radical Veerashaiva positions.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 correct: the **Aradhya** stream was of **Brahmin Shaivas**, led by **Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya**.
Statement 3 wrong: Aradhyas **kept Vedic ritual and varna**, unlike radical Veerashaivas — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: **Panditaradhya Charitra** tells of his debate with a **Buddhist acharya**.
⚠ **Aradhyas** kept varna; radical **Veerashaivas** rejected caste.
Veerashaivism's founder was **Basaveshwara**.

95.s: Which policy best describes the attitude of the Kakatiyas towards religious sects?
o: They prohibited all Shaiva sects from receiving grants.
They took no sides, granted support to orthodox Brahmin sects and did not persecute Lingayats.
They persecuted Lingayats while granting privileges only to Jains.
They imposed Veerashaivism as the exclusive state religion.
95.x: The Kakatiyas supported orthodox Brahmin sects through grants but did not persecute Lingayats and generally did not take sides among these sects.
95.tq: Infer religious policy from the combination of patronage and non-persecution.
xs: The Kakatiyas **took no sides**: they gave grants to **orthodox Brahmin sects** and **did not persecute Lingayats** — option **(2)** is correct.
They patronised Shaiva sects (**Pasupata**, **Kalamukha**), so Shaiva grants were not prohibited; Veerashaivism was not imposed.
xa: **Svayambhu Shiva** was the dynastic deity, yet Vaishnava shrines (**Thousand Pillar Temple**) were endowed — tolerance and syncretism.
**Prataparudra II** endowed **Chennakeshava** (**1321**).
⚠ Jains, however, faced persecution — e.g. **36 Jain villages** destroyed by **Visveshwara Shambhu**.

95.s: Kakatiya temples functioned economically as:
o: Temporary festival structures without permanent staff
Purely private family shrines without endowments
Military cantonments controlled by the Nayakas
95.x: Temples functioned as landed corporations, possessing lands and employing organised staff.
95.tq: Identify the institutional character of the temple.
xs: Kakatiya temples functioned as **landed corporations** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Srisailam Mallikarjuna** held lands in **70 villages** (some notes say **52**).
They had permanent staff: **Sthanapatis**, **Manulas**, **Sanus**, **Nibandhakaras**.
xa: Temples also ran **monasteries** and **feeding houses**; Kalamukhas gave **anna dana**.
Temple women and courtesans (**Kalavatis**) sustained dance and music.
Festivals were **royal occasions**.

95.s:
Which of the following statements about Kakatiya temple institutions is correct?
1. Temples were associated with monasteries and feeding houses.
2. Kalamukhas provided anna dana.
3. Temple women and courtesans sustained dance and music.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: All three statements are correct. Temples included monasteries and feeding houses, Kalamukhas supported food charity, and Kalavatis sustained dance and music.
95.tq: Check the temple as a religious, charitable and cultural institution.
xs: Statement 1 correct: temples ran **monasteries and feeding houses**.
Statement 2 correct: the **Kalamukhas** gave **anna dana**.
Statement 3 correct: temple women and courtesans (**Kalavatis**) sustained **dance and music** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: Temples were **landed corporations**; **Srisailam Mallikarjuna** held lands in **70 villages**.
Temple staff: **Sthanapatis**, **Manulas**, **Sanus**, **Nibandhakaras**.
Kalamukhas were also **temple managers**.

95.s: Royal endowments mentioned in connection with Kakatiya temples include:
o: Prataparudra II's grant to Chennakeshava and Lakshmidevi's grant to Ramanatha at Yelledu
Ganapatideva's grant to Padmakshi and Basava's grant to Srisailam
Prola II's grant to Tripurantakam and Brahmayya's grant to Vemulawada
Rudradeva's grant to Nakaram and Durgaraja's grant to Warangal fort
95.x: Prataparudra II endowed the Chennakeshava temple in 1321, while his queen Lakshmidevi endowed the Ramanatha temple at Yelledu.

xs: **Prataparudra II** endowed **Chennakeshava** (**1321**) and his queen **Lakshmidevi** endowed the **Ramanatha temple at Yelledu** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Basaveshwara** was a Karnataka minister of **Kalachuri Bijjala**; **Brahmayya** destroyed Jain settlements; **Nakaram** was a Vaishya body.
xa: Royal women were active donors to **temples and tanks**.
**Prola II** built the **Padmakshi temple**.
Vaishnava shrines like the **Thousand Pillar Temple** were also endowed.

95.s: Royal women during the Kakatiya period were active donors primarily to which of the following?
o: Guild halls and royal mint houses
95.x: Royal women of the Kakatiya period made donations to temples and tanks, contributing to both religious institutions and public water works.
95.tq: Identify the precise institutional pair instead of being distracted by other public and religious establishments.
xs: Royal women were active donors to **temples and tanks** — option **(1)** is correct.
Example: Prataparudra II's queen **Lakshmidevi** endowed the **Ramanatha temple, Yelledu**.
xa: **Prataparudra II** himself endowed **Chennakeshava** (**1321**).
Temples were **landed corporations** with organised staff.
Temple women and **Kalavatis** sustained dance and music.

95.s: The Kakatiya age is often characterised as the:
95.x: The Kakatiya age is called the Shaiva era because Shaivism had a prominent position during the period.

xs: The Kakatiya age is called the **"Shaiva era"** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Svayambhu Shiva** was the dynastic deity; the Kakatiyas patronised **Pasupata** and **Kalamukha** sects.
Jainism was the faith of the **early Kakatiyas** only, and it declined under the dynasty.
xa: Vaishnava shrines (**Thousand Pillar Temple**) were still endowed — **religious tolerance and syncretism**.
The Kakatiyas turned Shaiva from **Prola II / Rudradeva**.
Shaiva-Shakta axis: **Srisailam**, **Alampur**, **Draksharama**.

95.s: Which one of the following was the dynastic deity of the Kakatiyas?
95.x: Svayambhu Shiva was the dynastic deity of the Kakatiyas.
95.tq: Test the exact deity associated with the ruling dynasty rather than a prominent regional shrine.
xs: The Kakatiya dynastic deity was **Svayambhu Shiva** — option **(1)** is correct.
The period is thus called the **"Shaiva era"**.
xa: Yet Vaishnava shrines (**Thousand Pillar Temple**) were endowed — tolerance and syncretism.
**Prataparudra II** endowed **Chennakeshava** in **1321**.
Early Kakatiyas were **Jains** before becoming Shaivas from **Prola II / Rudradeva**.

95.s: In the dispute concerning Sri Swamy Hathiramji Mutt at Tirupati, the courts clarified the power of the State regarding interim management of old religious endowments under which legal framework?
o: The AP Endowments Act, 1987 and Articles 25–26 of the Constitution
The AP Endowments Act, 1966 and Articles 14–15 of the Constitution
The AP Charitable Trusts Act, 1990 and Articles 36–39 of the Constitution
The Religious Institutions Act, 1987 and Articles 32–35 of the Constitution

xs: Courts clarified state powers under the **AP Endowments Act, 1987** and **Articles 25–26** — option **(1)** is correct.
The case concerned the **Sri Swamy Hathiramji Mutt** (Tirupati) dispute of **May 2026**.
xa: The issue was the State's powers over **interim management** of **old religious endowments**.
Temples have long functioned as **landed corporations** — e.g. **Srisailam Mallikarjuna** with lands in **70 villages**.
Shaiva-Shakta axis of Andhra: **Srisailam**, **Alampur**, **Draksharama**.

95.s: Which of the following groups correctly represents the Shaiva-Shakta axis of Andhra that continued through the Kakatiya period?
95.x: Srisailam, Alampur and Draksharama remained important centres of the Shaiva-Shakta axis of Andhra during the period.
95.tq: Use the geographic cluster as a group and eliminate combinations drawn from unrelated regional or dynastic centres.
xs: The Shaiva-Shakta axis of Andhra was **Srisailam, Alampur and Draksharama** — option **(1)** is correct.
It continued through the Kakatiya period, the **"Shaiva era"**.
xa: **Srisailam** was the main **Veerashaiva** centre in Andhra and a **Kalamukha** centre.
Betaraja and Durgaraja were disciples of a Kalamukhacharya of the **Srisailam Shila matha**.
**Alampur** was also a Kalamukha / Shaiva centre.

96.s:
Which of the following statements regarding religious patronage under the Kakatiyas is correct?
1. Jain–Shaiva conflicts began under Rudradeva.
2. Ganapatideva was a devout Shaivite.
3. Vellanki Gangadhara, a Vaishnava minister of Rudradeva, built the Prasanna Keshava Temple at Hanamkonda.

xs: Statement 1 correct: **Jain-Shaiva conflicts** began under **Rudradeva**, to Jainism's cost.
Statement 2 correct: **Ganapatideva** was a **devout Shaivite**.
Statement 3 correct: Rudradeva's **Vaishnava** minister **Vellanki Gangadhara** built the **Prasanna Keshava** temple, Hanamkonda — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: Rudradeva built the **Thousand Pillar Temple** (**1163 CE**) and gave **Maddi Cheruvu** village for its upkeep.
Ganapatideva built the **Swayambhu Shiva** temple (**1254**) in Warangal fort.
The **Dharmasagara inscription** mentions the instrument **'Jalakaranda'** (APPSC 2019).

96.s: The musical instrument 'Jalakaranda' is mentioned in which Kakatiya-period inscription?
96.x: The Dharmasagara inscription mentions the instrument Jalakaranda (APPSC 2019). The Motupalli inscription (1244) protected foreign traders, the Magallu grant (956) first mentions the Kakatiyas, and the Chandupatla inscription records Rudrama Devi's death.
96.tq: Jalakaranda = Dharmasagara inscription.
xs: **'Jalakaranda'** is mentioned in the **Dharmasagara inscription** (**APPSC 2019**) — option **(1)** is correct.
The notes link no musical instrument to the other inscriptions.
xa: Temple counts: **1,300 Vaishnava**, **2,400 Mallara Devudu**, **4,400 Bhairava/Durga/Ganesha** temples.
**52 villages** were endowed to the **Srisailam Mallikarjuna** temple.
Music treatises: **Gita Ratnavali** and **Vadya Ratnavali** of **Jayapa Senani** (now lost).

96.s:
Which of the following temple-count combinations is correctly matched with the Kakatiya period?
1. Vaishnava temples — 1,300
2. Mallara Devudu temples — 2,400
3. Bhairava, Durga and Ganesha temples — 4,400

96.x: The recorded figures are 1,300 Vaishnava temples, 2,400 Mallara Devudu temples, 4,400 Bhairava/Durga/Ganesha temples and 52 villages endowed to Srisailam Mallikarjuna.
96.tq: Check each numerical row individually before accepting the cumulative option.
xs: All four figures are right: **1,300 Vaishnava**, **2,400 Mallara Devudu**, **4,400 Bhairava/Durga/Ganesha** temples.
And **52 villages** endowed to the **Srisailam Mallikarjuna** temple — so **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(2)**.
xa: **Ganapatideva** was a devout Shaivite; Jain-Shaiva conflicts began under **Rudradeva**.
Vaishnava minister **Vellanki Gangadhara** built **Prasanna Keshava** temple, Hanamkonda.
**Ghanapur (Kota Gullu)** has about **22 temples** of Ganapatideva's time.

96.s: Kakatiya temple architecture is principally associated with which style?
96.x: Kakatiya temple architecture follows the Chalukyan, or Vesara, style and is also described as transitional between early Chalukyan and Vijayanagara styles.
96.tq: Distinguish the named architectural style from broad regional alternatives.
xs: Kakatiya temples follow the **Chalukyan (Vesara)** style — option **(2)** is correct.
Other notes call it a **transitional style** between **early Chalukyan and Vijayanagara**.
The main influence was the **Western Chalukyas of Kalyani**: carved pillars, star-shaped platforms, ornate doorways, sculptured ceilings.

**Early Kakatiya kings built Jain temples** (APPSC G2 2025 statement I).
Other features: high **adhisthana**, **jaali** parapets, **toranas**, **rangamandapas**, swan and lotus motifs.

96.s: The sandbox foundation technology of Kakatiya temples involved
o: pits filled with sand, stone chips and earth to absorb shocks
a timber framework surrounded by lime mortar
floating bricks placed beneath the temple platform without any earth filling
solid granite blocks laid directly on black cotton soil
96.x: Sandbox foundations consisted of deep pits filled with sand, stone chips and earth, creating a shock-absorbing base on black cotton soil.
96.tq: Apply the engineering principle to the described construction method.
xs: The **sandbox foundation** was **deep pits filled with sand, stone chips and earth** acting as a **shock absorber** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was laid on **black cotton soil**, not granite blocks placed directly on it.
**Floating bricks** were used in Ramappa's **vimana**, not under the platform.
xa: The sandbox foundation is why **Ramappa** has survived earthquakes.
⚠ **Floating bricks** = lighter tower; **sandbox foundation** = earthquake cushion.
**Stellate (star) plan** = raised star-shaped platform giving more wall surface for sculpture.

96.s: The survival of Ramappa Temple through earthquakes is particularly associated with its
96.x: The shock-absorbing sandbox foundation is cited as a major reason for Ramappa Temple’s survival through earthquakes.
96.tq: Match a structural feature with its functional consequence.
xs: Ramappa's survival through earthquakes is due to its **sandbox foundation** — option **(4)** is correct.
Deep pits of **sand, stone chips and earth** absorb shocks on **black cotton soil**.
xa: It is a cited **heritage-engineering** example.
Its **vimana** uses **floating bricks** — light, porous bricks that reduce the dead weight of the tower.
Ramappa became a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** on **25 July 2021**.

96.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Kakatiya architectural innovations are correct?
1. Floating bricks reduce the dead weight of the tower.
2. Stellate plans provide greater wall surface for sculpture.
3. Ekasila denotes monolithic carving.

xs: Statement 1 correct: **floating bricks** reduce the **dead weight of the tower**.
