98.tq: Check each statement separately, especially the ruler–minister relationship and the work’s subject matter.
xs: Statement 1 correct: **Anavota Reddi** developed the **Motupalli** dock.
Statement 2 correct: **Somaya** was Anavota's **minister**.
Statement 3 correct: **Srinatha's Haravilasam** describes Reddi-age **imports and exports** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: Haravilasam is the literary source asked in **APPSC 2019** (PYQ **2018**, **2019**).
It was dedicated to merchant **Tippayya Setti**.
The Abhaya Sasanam protected merchants from **sea pirates**.

98.s: Srinatha dedicated Haravilasam to which merchant associated with overseas trade?
98.x: Haravilasam was dedicated to Tippayya Setti, who was famous for overseas trade.
98.tq: Match the literary work with its named dedicatee rather than its author or political patron.
xs: **Haravilasam** was dedicated to merchant **Tippayya Setti**, famous for **overseas trade** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Somaya** was Anavota's minister; **Mallaya Reddy** took Motupalli; **Hasan Gangu** was the Bahmani founder.
xa: The same merchant (**Avachi Tippayya Setti**) funded the **Vasantotsavams**.
Haravilasam describes Reddi sea trade and **imports and exports**.
Srinatha's title: **Kavi Sarvabhauma**.

98.s: Who was the brother of Prolaya Vema Reddi associated with the capture of Motupalli?
98.x: Mallareddi, the brother of Prolaya Vema Reddi, took Motupalli from Hasan Gangu of the Bahmani Sultanate.
98.tq: Separate a family relationship from ministerial and military offices.
xs: **Mallareddi (Mallaya Reddy)**, Prolaya Vema's brother, took **Motupalli** by defeating **Hasan Gangu** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kataya Vema** was Kumaragiri's brother-in-law; **Chennamanayaka** and **Mamidi Peddanamatya** were **Anavema's** army chief and minister.
xa: Hasan Gangu was the **Bahmani** founder.
**Anavota** later developed the Motupalli dock.
The **Kandukur** branch was Mallareddi's line.

98.s: The 'Andhra Path', an earlier trade route, is mentioned in which Buddhist text?
98.x: The Buddhist text Vinayavatthu mentions the 'Andhra Path' (APPSC 2019). Mahavamsa, Dipavamsa and Divyavadana are other Buddhist texts not linked to the Andhra Path.
98.tq: Andhra Path = Vinayavatthu; Reddi sea trade = Haravilasam.
xs: The **'Andhra Path'** is mentioned in the Buddhist text **Vinayavatthu** (**APPSC 2019**) — option **(2)** is correct.
It is an **earlier trade route** that preceded the Reddi port trade at Motupalli.
xa: **Motupalli** was the chief Reddi port.
**Srinatha's Haravilasam** describes Reddi sea trade (APPSC 2019).
The **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** of **Somaya** encouraged trade.

98.s: The Kaluvacheru inscription of 1423 was issued after which event?
o: The seizure of Kondavidu by Pedakomati Vema
The construction of Patala Ganga steps at Srisailam
The abolition of the gold tax by Anavota
98.x: Anitalli issued the Kaluvacheru inscription in 1423 after the recapture of Rajahmundry. It also provides information on the Musunuri-led liberation and Prolaya Vema Reddi’s service under the Nayakas.
98.tq: Associate an inscription with its date and the event immediately preceding its issue.
xs: **Anitalli** issued the **Kaluvacheru inscription** in **1423** after the **recapture of Rajahmundry** — option **(1)** is correct.
**1402** was Pedakomati's seizure of Kondavidu; the **Patala Ganga** steps were finished in **1346**.
xa: Kaluvacheru is a key source on the **Musunuri-led liberation**.
It also records **Prolaya Vema Reddi's** service under the **Nayakas**.
**Veerabhadra** and his brother **Vema** recovered Rajahmundry in **1423**.

98.s: Which of the following statements about Anitalli is correct?
o: She was the ruler who abolished the gold tax.
She was the minister who issued the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam.
She was the queen who dug the tank associated with Pedakomati Vema.
She was regarded as the rightful heir after her father Kataya Vema Reddi.
98.x: Anitalli, the daughter of Kataya Vema Reddi and wife of Veerabhadra Reddi, was regarded as the rightful heir after her father.
98.tq: Separate succession claims from the administrative and welfare activities of other figures.
xs: **Anitalli** was the **rightful heir** after her father **Kataya Vema Reddi** — option **(4)** is correct.
The gold tax was abolished by **Anavota**; the Abhaya Sasanam was issued by **Somaya**; the tank was dug by **Surambika**.
xa: She married **Veerabhadra Reddi**, Allada's second son.
⚠ Some notes call her "**Allada Reddi's** wife"; most say wife of **Veerabhadra**.
She issued the **Kaluvacheru inscription** (**1423**).

98.s: Who constructed the Jaganobbaganda canals to supply water to the tank dug by Surambika?
o: Somaya, the minister of Anavota Reddi
98.x: Racha Vema, the son of Surambika, constructed the Jaganobbaganda canals to feed water into the tank dug by his mother.
98.tq: Identify the family relationship first, then connect the person with the associated irrigation work.
xs: **Racha Vema**, Surambika's **son**, cut the **'Jaganobbaganda'** canals to feed her tank — option **(3)** is correct.
**Surambika** was the wife of **Pedakomati Vema Reddi**.
xa: Tank name: **Govardhana Samudram** (APPSC G2 2019) or **Santana Sagaram** (APPSC GS 2018).
Royal women took an active part in welfare works such as tanks.
Racha Vema was the last Kondaveedu ruler, killed over the **Puriti** tax.

98.s: Which of the following statements is NOT correctly matched?
o: Patala Ganga steps — Pedakomati Vema Reddi
98.x: The Patala Ganga steps at Srisailam were associated with Prolaya Vema Reddi, not Pedakomati Vema Reddi. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
98.tq: Find the swapped ruler–work pair while checking the location and person together.
xs: **Patala Ganga steps — Pedakomati Vema Reddi** is wrong — option **(3)** is the answer; the steps (**1346**) were **Prolaya Vema Reddi's**.
The rest are right: **Kaluvacheru** – **Anitalli**; **Abhaya Sasanam** – **Somaya**; **Jaganobbaganda** canals – **Racha Vema**.
xa: Prolaya Vema also built steps to **Ahobilam** hill.
The **Srisailam** inscription (**1346**) records the Patala Ganga steps.
**Anavema** built the **Veerashiro Mantapa** at Srisailam.

98.s: Which community was primarily associated with inland and coastal trade during the Reddi period?
98.x: The Komatis were mainly engaged in inland and coastal trade.
98.tq: Distinguish occupational roles among the major social groups.
xs: The **Komatis** ran **inland and coastal trade** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Kammas, Kapus, Reddis and Velamas** were the **warrior-farmer** backbone, supplying most soldiers.
xa: The Brahmin-warrior-merchant order survived into **Gajapati** rule.
Merchant **Tippayya Setti** was famed for overseas trade.
**Motupalli** was the chief Reddi port.

98.s:
Consider the following statements about society during the Kakatiya–Reddi period:
1. Kammas, Kapus, Reddis and Velamas formed the warrior-farmer backbone.
2. These groups supplied most of the soldiers.
3. The Brahmin-warrior-merchant social order disappeared completely under Gajapati rule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
98.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Brahmin-warrior-merchant order survived into Gajapati rule.
98.tq: Reject the extreme word 'completely' and retain the two connected social facts.
xs: Statement 1 correct: **Kammas, Kapus, Reddis and Velamas** were the **warrior-farmer backbone**.
Statement 2 correct: they **supplied most soldiers**.
Statement 3 wrong: the **Brahmin-warrior-merchant** order **survived into Gajapati rule** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **Komatis** ran inland and coastal trade.
Village administration also continued in the same decentralised pattern under the Gajapatis.
Village servants: the **12 Ayagars**.

98.s: Which statement regarding women during the Reddi period is correct?
o: Queens were prohibited from issuing inscriptions.
Queens were educated in the arts.
Queens were excluded from formal artistic education.
Queens were confined exclusively to temple service.
98.x: Queens were educated in the arts. The period also records royal women associated with public works and inscriptions.
98.tq: Prefer the precise positive statement over absolute exclusionary distractors.
xs: Reddi **queens were educated in the arts** — option **(2)** is correct.
Royal women also issued inscriptions (**Anitalli's Kaluvacheru**) and built tanks (**Surambika**).
xa: Royal women took an active part in **welfare works** — tanks, canals, reservoirs.
**Devadasis** were trained in music, dance and ritual.
Court dancer **Lakumadevi** was renowned in **Bharatanatyam**.

98.s: The Kaluvacheru inscription was issued by Anithalli, the wife of which ruler?
98.x: Anithalli, wife of Veerabhadra Reddi, issued the Kaluvacheru inscription.
98.tq: Apply the relationship trap by matching the named queen with the correct husband.
xs: **Anithalli** was the wife of **Veerabhadra Reddi** — option **(1)** is correct.
She was the daughter of **Kataya Vema Reddi** and his **rightful heir**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes call her "**Allada Reddi's** wife" — most say Veerabhadra's, which is followed.
Veerabhadra was **Allada's second son** and nominal king (restored **1423** and **1429**).
The **Kaluvacheru inscription** dates to **1423**.

98.s:
Consider the following statements about Devadasis during the Reddi period:
1. They were trained in music, dance and ritual.
2. They were respected performers at Shiva temples.
3. Their activities were associated with the Pancharama temples.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
98.x: Devadasis were trained in music, dance and ritual and were respected performers at Shiva temples, including the Pancharamas.
98.tq: Combine the training, social role and temple association before selecting the coded option.
xs: Statement 1 correct: **Devadasis** were trained in **music, dance and ritual**.
Statements 2 and 3 correct: they were respected performers at **Shiva temples** such as the **Pancharamas** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: The Reddis **renovated and endowed** the Pancharama shrines.
Reddi-era renovations: **Draksharama Bhimesvara**, **Samarlakota Kumararama**.
Court dancer **Lakumadevi** served **Kumaragiri**.

98.s: Surambika, the queen of Pedakomati Vema Reddi, dug a tank known as:
98.x: According to the APPSC G2 2019 key, Surambika's tank was Govardhana Samudram (the APPSC GS 2018 key calls it Santana Sagaram), and her son Racha Vema cut the Jaganobbaganda canals to feed it. Pakhal and Ramappa lakes are Kakatiya-era tanks, and Kambham Cheruvu is a later tank.
98.tq: Surambika's tank: Govardhana Samudram or Santana Sagaram. Pick whichever one is offered.
xs: **Surambika's** tank is **Govardhana Samudram** per the **APPSC G2 2019** key — option **(1)** is correct.
She was the wife of **Pedakomati Vema Reddi**.
xa: ⚠ The **APPSC GS 2018** key calls it **Santana Sagaram**; some notes **Santana Payonidhi** — read the options.
Her son **Rachavema** cut the **'Jaganobbaganda'** canals to feed it.
Reddi rulers built tanks, canals and reservoirs.

98.s: Which religious combination is correctly associated with the Reddi period?
98.x: The Reddi kings followed Pashupata Shaivism, while the people largely followed Veerashaivism.
98.tq: Use the kings-versus-people comparison to avoid reversing the two sectarian affiliations.
xs: Reddi **kings** followed **Pashupata Shaivism**; the **people** followed **Veerashaivism** — option **(4)** is correct.
Option 2 swaps them; Buddhism and Jainism are not the Reddi faiths.
xa: **Bhairava** and **Mailara** worship were common.
Reddi kings were disciples of **Ghoderayacharulu** (Tripurantakam).
Later the Reddis moved towards **Vaishnavism** (Kumaragiri, Kataya Vema).

98.s:
Consider the following statements about religion under the Reddis:
1. The Ghoderayas propagated Shaivism from Tripurantakam.
2. The Reddi kings were disciples of Ghoderayacharulu.
3. The Vadagalai sect of Vedanta Desika's line set up a matha at Srisailam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
98.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Ghoderayas spread Shaivism from Tripurantakam. Statement 2 is correct: Reddi kings were disciples of Ghoderayacharulu. Statement 3 is wrong: the Vadagalai matha was set up at Ahobilam, not Srisailam. Hence B, C and D are wrong.
98.tq: Shaiva centre = Tripurantakam (Ghoderayas); Vaishnava Vadagalai matha = Ahobilam.
xs: Statement 1 correct: the **Ghoderayas** spread Shaivism from **Tripurantakam**.
Statement 2 correct: Reddi kings were disciples of **Ghoderayacharulu**.
Statement 3 wrong: the **Vadagalai** matha was set up at **Ahobilam**, not Srisailam — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Vadagalai is **Vedanta Desika's** line.
**Kumaragiri** and **Kataya Vema** were Vaishnava patrons.
Kings: **Pashupata Shaivism**; people: **Veerashaivism**.

98.s: Which of the following pairs of rulers were patrons of Vaishnavism?
98.x: Kumaragiri and Kataya Vema were patrons of Vaishnavism. The Reddis gradually moved from Shaivism towards Vaishnavism in the later period.
98.tq: Identify the correct ruler pair before considering the broader religious transition.
xs: **Kumaragiri and Kataya Vema** were **Vaishnava** patrons — option **(1)** is correct.
The Reddis moved from **Shaivism towards Vaishnavism** later.
xa: The **Vadagalai** sect set up a matha at **Ahobilam**.
Reddi endowments went to **Srisailam**, **Simhachalam**, **Ahobilam**.
Earlier kings were **Pashupata Shaivas**.

98.s: Which of the following statements about religious endowments under the Reddis is correct?
o: Only Buddhist monasteries received royal endowments.
Srisailam, Simhachalam and Ahobilam received donations, while Pancharama temples also received renovations and land grants.
Donations were made only to Ahobilam and not to Shaiva centres.
The Reddis prohibited land grants to temples.
98.x: Reddi donations reached Srisailam, Simhachalam and Ahobilam, and the Pancharama Shiva temples received renovations and land grants.
98.tq: Prefer the option that preserves both the named centres and the additional temple-support detail.
xs: **Srisailam, Simhachalam and Ahobilam** received endowments, and the **Pancharama** Shiva temples got **renovations and land grants** — option **(2)** is correct.
So both Shaiva and Vaishnava centres were endowed.
xa: Prolaya Vema: **Patala Ganga** steps and **Vasatulas** (rest-houses).
Anavema: **Veerashiro Mantapa** (Srisailam), **Anavemagiri mandapas** (Simhachalam).
Reddi-era renovations: **Draksharama Bhimesvara**, **Samarlakota Kumararama**, **Bikkavolu** temples.

98.s: Which ruler is associated with the construction of pilgrim rest-houses at Ahobilam and Srisailam and the rebuilding of the ramparts of Ahobilam and Mahanandi?
98.x: Prolaya Vema Reddi built the pilgrim rest-houses at Ahobilam and Srisailam and rebuilt the ramparts of Ahobilam and Mahanandi.
98.tq: Match the cluster of related temple works with the ruler rather than relying on one isolated monument.
xs: **Prolaya Vema Reddi** built the pilgrim **rest-houses (Vasatulas)** at **Ahobilam and Srisailam** and rebuilt the ramparts of **Ahobilam** and **Mahanandi** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Anavema** built the Veerashiro Mantapa; **Vallaya Vemana** restored the Amareswara temple.
xa: Prolaya Vema also built steps to **Patala Ganga** (**1346**) and **Ahobilam** hill.
He restored **agraharas** to Brahmins.
Title: **Nissivu Bhudana Parasurama**.

98.s: Who restored the Amareswara temple at Amaravati after it had suffered damage from the Bahmanis?
98.x: Vallaya Vemana, the minister of Anavota Reddi, restored the Amareswara temple at Amaravati after Bahmani damage.
98.tq: Watch for the APPSC swapped-authority trap involving a minister and a ruling king.
xs: **Vallaya Vemana**, minister of **Anavota Reddi**, restored the **Amareswara temple**, Amaravati, after Bahmani damage — option **(3)** is correct.
Senani **Mallareddy** drove the Bahmani forces from **Amaravati**.
xa: **Anavema** built the **Veerashiro Mantapa** at Srisailam.
Anavota's other minister **Somaya** issued the **Motupalli Abhaya Shasana**.
**Bala Saraswati** composed Anavota's Sanskrit inscriptions.

98.s: Which of the following works was authored by Pedakomati Vema Reddi and deals with the Srngara aspect of Amaru Shatakam?
98.x: Srngara Dipika was authored by Pedakomati Vema Reddi and deals with Amaru Shatakam. Tatva Prakashika was written by Sivalinga Reddi, while Kridabhiramam was written by Vinukonda Vallabhamatya.
98.tq: Use author–work association and eliminate works belonging to the same literary period.
xs: **Srngara Dipika**, on **Amaru Shatakam**, is by **Pedakomati Vema Reddi** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kridabhiramam** – **Vinukonda Vallabhamatya**; **Harivamsa** – **Errana**; **Tatva Prakashika** – **Sivalinga Reddi**.
xa: Pedakomati also wrote **Sangeeta Chintamani**, **Sahitya Chintamani**, **Saptasati Saratika**, **Bhava Dipika**.
Title: **Sarvajna Chakravarti**.
**Vamana Bhatta Bana** wrote his biography, **Vema Bhupala Charitra**.

98.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Pedakomati Vema Reddi — Saptasati Saratika
2. Pedakomati Vema Reddi — Bhava Dipika
3. Sivalinga Reddi — Tatva Prakashika
4. Vinukonda Vallabhamatya — Kridabhiramam
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
98.x: All four pairs are correct. Pedakomati Vema Reddi wrote Saptasati Saratika (on Gatha Saptashati) and Bhava Dipika, Sivalinga Reddi of Kandukuru wrote Tatva Prakashika, and Vinukonda Vallabhamatya wrote the Telugu Kridabhiramam.
98.tq: Verify each author–work pair independently before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All four are right: **Saptasati Saratika** and **Bhava Dipika** – **Pedakomati Vema Reddi**.
**Tatva Prakashika** – **Sivalinga Reddi** (Kandukuru); **Kridabhiramam** – **Vinukonda Vallabhamatya** — so option **(3)**.
xa: Saptasati Saratika is on **Gatha Saptashati**.
Kridabhiramam is in **Telugu**, of the same era.
Pedakomati's **Sahitya Chintamani** is on **Alankara Shastra** (poetics).

98.s: 'Sangeeta Chintamani', a work on music, was written by which Reddi ruler?
98.x: Pedakomati Vema Reddi, the scholar-king (1402-1420), wrote Sangeeta Chintamani (PYQ 2011, 2019) as well as Sahitya Chintamani and Srngara Dipika. Kumaragiri wrote Vasantarajiyam on dance, and Kataya Vema wrote Kumaragiri Rajiyam. No work is credited to Anavema.
98.tq: Sangeeta Chintamani = Pedakomati Vema. Do not confuse it with Sangeeta Sudhakaram, which is Velama Singabhupala's.
xs: **Sangeeta Chintamani** (music) was written by **Pedakomati Vema Reddi** (PYQ **2011**, **2019**) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kumaragiri** wrote **Vasanta Rajiyam** (dance); **Kataya Vema** wrote **Kumaragiri Rajiyam**.
xa: Pedakomati (**1402-1420**) also wrote **Sahitya Chintamani** and **Srngara Dipika**.
⚠ **Sangeeta Sudhakaram** is by **Singabhupala II**, a **Recherla Velama** ruler, not a Reddi.
His court had **Srinatha** and **Vamana Bhatta Bana**.

98.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Vasantarajiyam, a Sanskrit work on dance, was written by Kumaragiri Reddi.
2. Kumaragiri Rajiyam, a commentary on Kalidasa's three plays, was written by Kumaragiri Reddi himself.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
98.x: Statement 1 is correct: Kumaragiri wrote Vasantarajiyam on dance. Statement 2 is wrong, and it is the trap: Kumaragiri Rajiyam was written by his brother-in-law Kataya Vema Reddi, and was only named after Kumaragiri.
98.tq: Kumaragiri Rajiyam is by Kataya Vema, not Kumaragiri.
xs: Statement 1 correct: **Kumaragiri** wrote **Vasantarajiyam**, a Sanskrit work on **dance**.
Statement 2 wrong: **Kumaragiri Rajiyam** was written by his brother-in-law **Kataya Vema Reddi** — so **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes credit Kumaragiri Rajiyam to Kumaragiri himself — the trap.
Kumaragiri Rajiyam is a commentary on **Kalidasa's three plays**.
Kumaragiri's title: **Karpura Vasanta Rayalu**.

98.s: Errana's Harivamsam was dedicated to which ruler?
98.x: Errana dedicated his Harivamsam to Prolaya Vema Reddi.
98.tq: This tests the author–patron relationship directly, a common history question pattern.
xs: **Errana's Harivamsam** was dedicated to **Prolaya Vema Reddi** — option **(2)** is correct.
Errana was his court poet at **Addanki** (PYQ G2 2011).
xa: Errana also wrote **Nrisimha Puranam** (PYQ G2 2017) and a **Ramayana**.
Titles: **Prabandha Parameswara**, **Sambhudasa**.
He completed the Telugu **Mahabharata** — last of the **Kavitrayam**.

98.s: Which of the following works was NOT associated with Errana?
98.x: Errana is associated with Aranya Parva shesham, Harivamsam and Nrusimha Puranam. Palnati Veera Charitra was one of Srinatha's works.
98.tq: Identify the one work belonging to another poet in the same literary tradition.
xs: **Palnati Veera Charitra** is **Srinatha's**, not Errana's — option **(3)** is the answer.
Errana's works: **Aranya Parva shesham**, **Harivamsam**, **Nrusimha Puranam**.
xa: Srinatha's other works: **Sringara Naishadham**, **Kasikhandam**, **Bhimakhandam**, **Haravilasam**.
Srinatha also wrote **Maruttarat Charitra** and **Sivaratri Mahatyam**.
Errana bridges **Nannaya** and **Tikkana**.

98.s: Errana is regarded as a link between which two literary styles?
o: Nannaya’s classical style and Tikkana’s style
98.x: Errana is regarded as a bridge between Nannaya’s classical style and Tikkana’s style.
98.tq: Distinguish the literary relationship from other poet–style combinations.
xs: Errana bridges **Nannaya's classical style and Tikkana's style** — option **(1)** is correct.
He is called the **greatest Telugu translator**.
xa: He translated the remaining part (**Seshabhaga**) of the **Aranya Parva**.
He is the third of the **Kavitrayam**.
Titles: **Prabandha Parameswara**, **Sambhudasa**.

98.s: Which of the following descriptions of Errana is correct?
o: He was the first of the Kavitrayam and initiated the Telugu Mahabharata.
He was the last of the Kavitrayam and completed the Telugu Mahabharata.
He opened the Kavya Yuga through his independent Sanskrit compositions.
He was a court poet of the Vijayanagara emperor who translated the entire Sanskrit Mahabharata.
98.x: Errana was the last of the Kavitrayam and completed the Telugu Mahabharata by translating the remaining portion of the Aranya Parva.
98.tq: Use the first/last distinction to separate Errana from the other members and from Srinatha.
xs: Errana was the **last of the Kavitrayam** and **completed the Telugu Mahabharata** — option **(2)** is correct.
He translated the remaining part of the **Aranya Parva**.
**Srinatha**, not Errana, opened the **Kavya Yuga**.
xa: Errana was court poet of **Prolaya Vema Reddi**, not of Vijayanagara.
He bridges **Nannaya** and **Tikkana**.
Harivamsa was dedicated to **Prolaya Vema**.

98.s: Which of the following titles was borne by the poet Errana?
98.x: Errana was called Prabandha Parameswara and Sambhudasa. Kavi Sarvabhauma was Srinatha's title, and Sahitya Chudamani was Vamana Bhatta Bana's. Andhra Suratrana was a royal title (Anavema in the APPSC key, first borne by Kapaya Nayaka), not a poet's.
98.tq: Errana = Prabandha Parameswara, Sambhudasa; Srinatha = Kavi Sarvabhauma.
xs: Errana bore the title **Prabandha Parameswara** (also **Sambhudasa**) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kavi Sarvabhauma** was **Srinatha's**; **Sahitya Chudamani** was **Vamana Bhatta Bana's**.
**Andhra Suratrana** was a royal title — **Anavema** in the APPSC G2 2011 key, first borne by **Kapaya Nayaka**.
xa: Vamana Bhatta Bana was also **Sahitya Samrajya Dhurandhara**.
Srinatha was honoured with **Kanakabhishekam** and **Ganda Penderam**.
Errana completed the Telugu Mahabharata.

98.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Poet — Ruler

1. Errana — Prolaya Vema Reddi
2. Bala Saraswati — Anavota Reddi
3. Srinatha — Pedakomati Vema Reddi
4. Vamana Bhatta Bana — Pedakomati Vema Reddi
98.x: Errana was associated with Prolaya Vema, Bala Saraswati with Anavota, and both Srinatha and Vamana Bhatta Bana were associated with Pedakomati Vema. Hence all four pairs are correctly matched.
98.tq: Start from the sure poet–ruler pairs and eliminate codes containing a swapped court.
xs: All four are right: **Errana** – **Prolaya Vema Reddi**; **Bala Saraswati** – **Anavota Reddi**.
**Srinatha** and **Vamana Bhatta Bana** – **Pedakomati Vema Reddi** — so option **(4)**.
xa: Srinatha was **Vidyadhikari** (minister of education) and composed Pedakomati's Sanskrit inscriptions.
Bala Saraswati composed **Anavota's** Sanskrit inscriptions.
Srinatha defeated **Gauda Dindima Bhatta**, court poet of **Devaraya II**.

98.s:
Consider the following statements about Srinatha:

1. His Sringara Naishadham was based on Sriharsha's Naishadhiyacharita.
2. He dedicated Sringara Naishadham to Mamidi Singana.
3. He dedicated Haravilasam to Tippayya Setti.
4. He wrote only devotional works and did not compose historical narratives.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
98.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because Srinatha also composed works such as Palnati Veeracharitra and Maruttarat Charitra.
98.tq: Reject the extreme word ‘only’ and verify each work with its dedication or source.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Sringara Naishadham** was rendered from **Sriharsha's Naishadhiyacharita**.
Statement 2 is correct: Srinatha dedicated **Sringara Naishadham** to **Mamidi Singana**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Haravilasam** was dedicated to merchant **Tippayya Setti**, famous for overseas trade.
Statement 4 is wrong: Srinatha also wrote narratives such as **Palnati Veeracharitra** and **Maruttarat Charitra**.
xa: Other Srinatha works: **Kasikhandam**, **Bhimakhandam / Bhimeswara Puranam** and **Sivaratri Mahatyam**.
**Haravilasam** describes the **sea trade** and the **imports and exports** of the Reddi age (APPSC 2019).
Srinatha bore the title **Kavi Sarvabhauma** (c. **1365-1441**) and was court poet of **Pedakomati Vema Reddi**.
⚠ **Kasikhandam**: some notes say it was written at **Kataya Vema's** request.

98.s: Which one of the following works of Srinatha is specifically associated with Bhimeswara of Draksharamam?
98.x: Bhimakhandam, also known as Bhimeswara Puranam, praises Bhimeswara of Draksharamam.
98.tq: Use the work–theme association rather than confusing similarly named literary titles.
xs: **Bhimakhandam**, also called **Bhimeswara Puranam**, praises **Bhimeswara of Draksharamam** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Haravilasam** describes the **Motupalli sea trade** and was dedicated to **Tippayya Setti**.
**Sringara Naishadham** is based on **Sriharsha's Naishadhiyacharita**, dedicated to **Mamidi Singana**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say Bhimakhandam is about the **Bhima river** — the main reading is the **Draksharamam** deity.
**Draksharama Bhimesvara** is one of the **Pancharama** shrines renovated in the Reddi era (Godavari region).
Other Srinatha works: **Palnati Veeracharitra**, **Maruttarat Charitra**, **Sivaratri Mahatyam**, **Kasikhandam**.

98.s:
Consider the following statements about Srinatha:
1. He belongs to the Kavya Yuga and prepared the way for the Prabandha style.
2. He is cited as evidence that birch bark was used for writing in the 15th century.
3. At Vijayanagara he defeated Gauda Dindima Bhatta, court poet of Devaraya II, and received Kanakabhishekam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
98.x: Statement 1 is correct: Srinatha's era is the Kavya Yuga and he prepared the way for the Prabandha style. Statement 2 is wrong: he is cited as evidence for the use of paper, not birch bark. Statement 3 is correct: he defeated Gauda Dindima Bhatta of Devaraya II's court and was honoured with Kanakabhishekam and Ganda Penderam. So only C fits; A, B and D include the false statement 2.
98.tq: Srinatha + 15th century writing material = paper (PYQ G2 2012).
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: Srinatha belongs to the **Kavya Yuga** and prepared the way for the **Prabandha** style.
Statement 2 is wrong: Srinatha is cited (APPSC G2 2012) as evidence that **paper**, not birch bark, was used for writing in the **15th century**.
Statement 3 is correct: he defeated **Gauda Dindima Bhatta** of **Devaraya II's** court and got **Kanakabhishekam** and **Ganda Penderam**.
xa: Srinatha was **Vidyadhikari** (minister of education) to **Pedakomati Vema Reddi** and composed his Sanskrit inscriptions.
After Kondaveedu fell (**1424**) he joined the Rajahmundry Reddis (patron **Veerabhadra Reddi**) with **Bendapudi Annamatya's** help.
After Rajahmundry fell (**1448**) he lived in **poverty in Palnadu**.
He wrote more kavyas than any other Telugu poet.

98.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with Vamana Bhatta Bana?

1. Nalabhyudayam
2. Raghunatha Charitam
3. Hamsa Sandesam
4. Vema Bhupala Charitra
98.x: All four works are associated with Vamana Bhatta Bana. Vema Bhupala Charitra, also called Veeranarayana Charitra, is a biography of Pedakomati Vema.
98.tq: Check the complete author–works list before selecting the inclusive combination.
xs: All four — **Nalabhyudayam, Raghunatha Charitam, Hamsa Sandesam and Vema Bhupala Charitra** — are by **Vamana Bhatta Bana**, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Vema Bhupala Charitra** (also Veeranarayana Charitra) is a **prose biography of Pedakomati Vema Reddi**.
xa: Some notes also credit him with the dictionaries **Shabda Ratnakaram** and **Shabda Chandrika**.
His titles: **Sahitya Samrajya Dhurandhara** and **Sahitya Chudamani**.
He was at the court of **Pedakomati Vema Reddi**, alongside **Srinatha**.
Pedakomati himself wrote **Sangeeta Chintamani** (music) and **Sahitya Chintamani** (poetics).

98.s:
Vamana Bhatta Bana was known by which of the following titles?

1. Sahitya Samrajya Dhurandhara
2. Sahitya Chudamani
3. Kavi Sarvabhauma
4. Dharma Pratishthana Guru
98.x: Vamana Bhatta Bana, at Pedakomati Vema Reddi's court, held the titles Sahitya Samrajya Dhurandhara and Sahitya Chudamani. Kavi Sarvabhauma was Srinatha's title, and Dharma Pratishthana Guru was not a title of Vamana Bhatta Bana.
98.tq: Separate a poet's titles from the titles of other poets and rulers.
xs: Vamana Bhatta Bana held the titles **Sahitya Samrajya Dhurandhara** and **Sahitya Chudamani** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Kavi Sarvabhauma** was the title of **Srinatha**, not Vamana Bhatta Bana.
"Dharma Pratishthana Guru" is not his title; the similar **Dharma Pratishtana Nagarudu** belonged to **Prolaya Vema Reddi**.
xa: Vamana Bhatta Bana was court poet of **Pedakomati Vema Reddi**.
His works: **Nalabhyudayam**, **Raghunatha Charitam**, **Hamsa Sandesam** and the prose **Vema Bhupala Charitra**.
**Bala Saraswati** composed **Anavota Reddi's** Sanskrit inscriptions.

98.s: Singabhupala II, the author of Sangeeta Sudhakaram, belonged to which political group?
98.x: Singabhupala II was a Recherla Velama ruler of Rachakonda, not a Reddi ruler, and he wrote Sangeeta Sudhakaram.
98.tq: Discriminate between a work associated with the Reddi period and its non-Reddi author.
xs: **Singabhupala II** was a **Recherla Velama ruler of Rachakonda** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He wrote **Sangeeta Sudhakaram** on musicology (PYQ 2012).
⚠ He was **not a Reddi** of Addanki, although he appears in Reddi-era book lists.
xa: Do not confuse with **Sangeeta Chintamani**, the music work of **Pedakomati Vema Reddi** (PYQ 2011, 2019).
The **Recherla Velamas** and the **Musunuris** were the other two successor states after **1323**, with the Reddis.
**Vasanta Rajiyam** (on dance) was by **Kumaragiri Reddi**.

98.s: Srinatha held which office at the court of Pedakomati Vema Reddi?
98.x: Srinatha (Kavi Sarvabhauma) was Vidyadhikari, the minister of education, at Pedakomati Vema Reddi's court, and he composed Pedakomati's Sanskrit inscriptions. He held no post as chief minister, commander or royal preceptor.
98.tq: Srinatha = Vidyadhikari under Pedakomati.
xs: Srinatha was **Vidyadhikari (minister of education)** at **Pedakomati Vema Reddi's** court — so option **(1)** is correct.
In that office he composed **Pedakomati's Sanskrit inscriptions**.
The notes record no post for him as chief minister, commander or royal preceptor.
xa: Srinatha's title: **Kavi Sarvabhauma** (c. **1365-1441**); court poet of Pedakomati (PYQ 2002).
He defeated **Gauda Dindima Bhatta**, court poet of **Devaraya II**, and got **Kanakabhishekam**.
Pedakomati was a scholar-king titled **Sarvajna Chakravarti**.

98.s: Which one of the following records is correctly matched with its historical association?
o: Srisailam record — Prolaya Vema Reddi’s Patala Ganga steps
Sarpavaram record — Anavota Reddi’s capital shift
Motupalli record — Pedakomati Vema’s seizure of Kondavidu
98.x: The 1346 Srisailam record refers to the Patala Ganga steps built by Prolaya Vema Reddi. The Manyapuram record concerns Anavota’s capital shift, and the Sarpavaram record concerns Kataya Vema’s family.
98.tq: Find the correctly matched place–record association and reject swapped locations.
xs: The **Srisailam record (1346)** records **Prolaya Vema Reddi's Patala Ganga steps** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Sarpavaram** record concerns **Kataya Vema's family**, not a capital shift.
The **Manyapuram** record concerns **Anavota's capital shift** to Kondavidu.
The **Motupalli Abhaya Shasana** was issued by Anavota's minister **Somaya** to encourage trade.
xa: The **Kaluvacheru inscription (1423)** was issued by **Anitalli** after the recapture of Rajahmundry.
Sarpavaram also records the treaty: **Harihara II** married his daughter **Vijayalakshmi** to Kataya's son.
Prolaya Vema also built steps to **Ahobilam** hill and pilgrim rest-houses (**Vasatulas**).

98.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Title)
(a) Dharma Pratishtana Nagarudu
(b) Dweepa Vijetha
(c) Karpura Vasanta Rayalu
(d) Sarvajna Chakravarti

List-II (Ruler)

(ii) Prolaya Vema Reddi

(iv) Pedakomati Vema Reddi

Choose the correct answer using the code given below:
98.x: Dharma Pratishtana Nagarudu was Prolaya Vema Reddi’s title; Dweepa Vijetha belonged to Anavota Reddi; Karpura Vasanta Rayalu to Kumaragiri Reddi; and Sarvajna Chakravarti to Pedakomati Vema Reddi.
98.tq: Start from the sure title–ruler pair and eliminate codes that misplace the remaining titles.
xs: Correct match: **a–ii, b–iii, c–i, d–iv** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Dharma Pratishtana Nagarudu** → **Prolaya Vema Reddi**.
**Dweepa Vijetha** (for taking **Talagada island**) → **Anavota Reddi**.
**Karpura Vasanta Rayalu** → **Kumaragiri Reddi**; **Sarvajna Chakravarti** → **Pedakomati Vema Reddi**.
xa: Prolaya Vema also bore **Nissivu Bhudana Parasurama**, stressing land gifts.
**Anavema Reddi**: **Rajashri Ramani**, **Rachuru Durga Vibhala** and **Andhra Suratrana**.
**Kataya Vema Reddi**: **Kataka Churakara**; **Sivalinga Reddi**: **Bharatamata Patanga**.

98.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
98.x: Kumaragiri Reddi was known as Karpura Vasanta Rayalu. Rajashri Ramani was a title of Anavema Reddi.
98.tq: Find the swapped title–ruler pair while retaining the correctly matched neighbouring titles.
xs: **Kumaragiri Reddi — Rajashri Ramani** is wrongly matched — so option **(1)** is the answer.
**Rajashri Ramani** was a title of **Anavema Reddi**; Kumaragiri was **Karpura Vasanta Rayalu**.
The others are correct: **Sivalinga Reddi — Bharatamata Patanga**, **Kataya Vema — Kataka Churakara**, **Anavema — Vasantarayadu**.
xa: **Anavema** also bore **Rachuru Durga Vibhala** (APPSC G2 2017) and **Andhra Suratrana** (APPSC G2 2011).
**Anavota Reddi**: **Dweepa Vijetha** and **Veeranna Pothu**.
**Pedakomati Vema Reddi**: **Sarvajna Chakravarti**.

98.s:
Consider the following statements about the titles of Reddi rulers:
1. Anavota Reddi assumed the title Veeranna Pothu.
2. Anavema Reddi bore the title Andhra Suratrana.
3. Kumaragiri Reddi was known as Karpura Vasantaraya.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
98.x: All four statements are correct. Veeranna Pothu belonged to Anavota Reddi, Andhra Suratrana and Vasantaraya were associated with Anavema Reddi, Karpura Vasantaraya with Kumaragiri, and Bharatamata Patanga with Sivalinga Reddi.
98.tq: Verify each title independently and watch for confusion between the similar Vasantaraya titles.
xs: All four statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statement 1: **Veeranna Pothu** (with **Dweepa Vijetha**) belonged to **Anavota Reddi**.
Statement 2: **Andhra Suratrana** was borne by **Anavema Reddi** (APPSC G2 2011).
Statements 3 and 4: **Karpura Vasantaraya** → **Kumaragiri**; **Bharatamata Patanga** → **Sivalinga Reddi of Kandukuru**.
xa: ⚠ **Andhra Suratrana** was first borne by **Musunuri Kapaya Nayaka**.
Anavema's other titles: **Rajashri Ramani**, **Vasantarayadu**, **Rachuru Durga Vibhala**.
**Sivalinga Reddi** also wrote **Tatva Prakashika**.

98.s: According to the APPSC Group 2 (2017) key, the title 'Rachuru Durga Vibhala' belonged to which Reddi ruler?
98.x: The APPSC G2 2017 key gives Rachuru Durga Vibhala to Anavema Reddi, who also bore Rajashri Ramani and Andhra Suratrana. Prolaya Vema bore Dharma Pratishtana Nagarudu and Nissivu Bhudana Parasurama, Anavota bore Dweepa Vijetha, and Kataya Vema bore Kataka Churakara.
98.tq: Rachuru Durga Vibhala = Anavema (APPSC 2017).
xs: The APPSC G2 2017 key gives **Rachuru Durga Vibhala** to **Anavema Reddi** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Prolaya Vema** bore **Dharma Pratishtana Nagarudu** and **Nissivu Bhudana Parasurama**.
**Anavota** bore **Dweepa Vijetha**; **Kataya Vema** bore **Kataka Churakara**.
xa: Anavema also bore **Rajashri Ramani**, **Vasantarayadu** and **Andhra Suratrana**.
**Anavema Reddi** (**1364-1386**) was the **greatest Reddi**, with the widest conquests.
He built the **Veerashiro Mantapa at Srisailam** (APPSC G2 2011) and mandapas at **Simhachalam**.
He was the **most charitable** Reddi king, guided by **Vemadri Pandit**.

98.s: Who is traditionally associated with opening the Kavya Yuga in Telugu literature?
98.x: Srinatha is described as the poet who opened the Kavya Yuga, whereas Errana completed the Andhra Mahabharata as the last of the Kavitrayam.
98.tq: Separate the literary-period milestone from the Mahabharata-completion milestone.
xs: **Srinatha** opened the **Kavya Yuga** in Telugu literature — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Errana** completed the **Andhra Mahabharata** as the **last of the Kavitrayam**, so he closes the Bharata phase.
Errana is said to bridge **Nannaya's** classical style and **Tikkana's** style.
xa: Srinatha wrote more kavyas than any other Telugu poet and prepared the way for the **Prabandha** style.
Errana translated the **Seshabhaga of the Aranya Parva**; titles **Prabandha Parameswara** and **Sambhudasa**.
Errana was court poet of **Prolaya Vema Reddi** (PYQ G2 2011); his **Harivamsa** is dedicated to him.

98.s: The Reddi kingdoms emerged as one of the three successor states after 1323 along with which two states?
98.x: The Reddis were one of three successor political formations after 1323, the other two being the Musunuris and the Recherla Velamas.
98.tq: Use the three-state comparison and eliminate dynasties that belonged to different political contexts.
xs: The Reddis were one of three successor states after **1323**, with the **Musunuris and Recherla Velamas** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The other options (Cholas, Hoysalas, Vijayanagara, Bahmanis) are not the post-**1323** successor trio named in the notes.
xa: The Reddi period is **c. 1325-1448**: Kondaveedu line **1325-1424**, Rajamahendravaram line **1402-1448**.
**Prolaya Vema Reddi** expelled **Tughluq** forces from coastal Andhra c. **1325**.
⚠ **Singabhupala II** (Sangeeta Sudhakaram) was a **Recherla Velama** of **Rachakonda**, not a Reddi.
The Reddis expelled the **Velamas** from Palnadu at the **Battle of Bhimavaram** (APPSC G2 2019 key).

98.s: The Reddi rule, approximately dated from 1325 to 1448, is described as which of the following?
o: The beginning of the Bahmani golden age
The second golden age of Telugu culture
The final age of Chola imperial expansion
The first golden age of Sanskrit culture in the Deccan
98.x: Reddi rule, approximately from 1325 to 1448, is called the second golden age of Telugu culture.
98.tq: Combine the date range with the distinctive historical label instead of selecting a generic golden-age description.
xs: Reddi rule (**c. 1325-1448**) is called the **second golden age of Telugu culture** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was the **peak of Telugu literature before Vijayanagara**, and the kings were themselves authors.
xa: Court poets: **Errana** and **Srinatha**.
Royal language **Sanskrit**; emblem the **bull**; faith **Pashupata Shaivism**.
Lineage: **Panta Vamsam** (**Deseti kula**); family deity **Mula Guramma**.
Capitals in sequence: **Addanki → Kondavidu → Rajahmundry**.

98.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the Godavari-region heritage sites associated with Reddi-era renovations?
o: Bikkavolu, Draksharama Bhimesvara and Samarlakota Kumararama
98.x: Bikkavolu temples, Draksharama Bhimesvara and Samarlakota Kumararama are identified as Godavari-region sites carrying Reddi-era renovations.
98.tq: Use the geographical clue to distinguish Godavari sites from other Andhra locations.
xs: **Bikkavolu** temples, **Draksharama Bhimesvara** and **Samarlakota Kumararama** are the Godavari-region sites with Reddi-era renovations — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Kondaveedu, Motupalli and Tripurantakam** are listed AP-angle sites, not Godavari renovations.
**Addanki, Kondaveedu and Rajamahendravaram** were the Reddi **capitals**.
xa: The Reddis were ardent Shaivas who restored the **Pancharama** shrines.
**Bhimakhandam** of **Srinatha** praises **Bhimeswara of Draksharamam**.
Other AP sites: **Kondavidu** hill fort (Guntur/Palnadu), **Srisailam**, **Ahobilam**.

98.s:
Which of the following literary works is associated with Rajahmundry as a literary hub?
1. Kashikhandam of Srinatha
2. Sivalila Vilasamu of Sivaleka Kommana
3. Kavyalankara Chudamani of Vinnakota Peddana

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
98.x: Rajahmundry was associated with all three works: Srinatha’s Kashikhandam, Sivaleka Kommana’s Sivalila Vilasamu and Vinnakota Peddana’s Kavyalankara Chudamani.
98.tq: Check each author–work pair independently before selecting the complete combination.
xs: All three works are tied to **Rajahmundry as a literary hub** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Kashikhandam** of **Srinatha** (some notes: at **Kataya Vema's** request).
**Sivalila Vilasamu** of **Sivaleka Kommana** and **Kavyalankara Chudamani** of **Vinnakota Peddana**.
xa: The Rajahmundry court under **Kataya Vema** was a competitive literary centre.
**Kataya Vema Reddi** wrote **Kumaragiri Rajiyam**, a commentary on Kalidasa's three plays.
After Kondaveedu fell (**1424**), Srinatha joined the Rajahmundry court under **Veerabhadra Reddi**.

98.s: Which statement best expresses the cultural significance of the Reddi courts?
o: They are remembered mainly for ending temple patronage in Andhra.
They discouraged Telugu literary activity in favour of exclusive Persian patronage.
They marked the peak of Telugu literature before Vijayanagara, and the kings themselves also authored works.
They confined literary patronage to Sanskrit and prohibited regional languages.
98.x: The Reddi court represented the peak of Telugu literature before Vijayanagara, and several Reddi kings were themselves authors.
98.tq: Select the option that combines the literary-patronage and royal-authorship features without an absolute distortion.
xs: The Reddi courts marked the **peak of Telugu literature before Vijayanagara**, and **kings themselves authored works** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Examples: **Kumaragiri** wrote **Vasanta Rajiyam**; **Pedakomati** wrote **Sangeeta Chintamani**.
Options on ending temple patronage or banning regional languages are wrong: the Reddis endowed **Srisailam, Simhachalam, Ahobilam**.
xa: **Sanskrit** was the official language; many kings were **scholar-poets**.
Court poets **Errana** and **Srinatha** worked under Reddi patronage.
The Reddi age is called the **second golden age** of Telugu culture.

98.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the religious and political significance of Reddi temple patronage?
o: It was limited to military forts and had no connection with religious institutions.
It replaced all Shaiva shrines with Vaishnava temples and ended royal literary patronage.
It was directed exclusively towards Buddhist monasteries.
It strengthened political legitimacy through literary patronage and expressed Shaiva devotion through restoration of Pancharama shrines.
98.x: Literary patronage gave the Reddis political legitimacy, while their Shaiva devotion was expressed through the restoration and endowment of Pancharama shrines.
98.tq: Connect the cause-and-effect relationship between cultural patronage, political legitimacy and religious restoration.
xs: Reddi patronage gave **political legitimacy through literature** and expressed **Shaiva devotion by restoring Pancharama shrines** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was not exclusive to Buddhism or forts: the Reddis endowed **Srisailam, Simhachalam, Ahobilam** with land grants.
xa: Kings followed **Pashupata Shaivism**; people **Veerashaivism**.
The **Ghoderayas** propagated Shaivism from **Tripurantakam**.
Later the Reddis moved towards **Vaishnavism**; the **Vadagalai** sect set up a **matha at Ahobilam**.
**Kumaragiri** and **Kataya Vema** were Vaishnava patrons.

99.s: After the fall of Warangal, which of the following combinations is correct?
o: Sultanpurti—Malik Burhanuddin, assisted by Malik Maqbul
Rekapalli—Malik Maqbul, assisted by Malik Burhanuddin
Orugallu—Malik Kafur, assisted by Malik Ambar
Rachakonda—Malik Burhanuddin, assisted by Alauddin Khalji
99.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq renamed Warangal Sultanpurti and placed Andhra under Malik Burhanuddin, with Malik Maqbul assisting him.

xs: Warangal was renamed **Sultanpurti** (Sultanpur) and Andhra placed under **Malik Burhanuddin**, assisted by **Malik Maqbul** — so option **(1)** is correct.

xa: Of Prataparudra's **75 generals**, only **Prolaya Nayaka, Recherla Singama and Prolaya Vema Reddi** survived.
Tughluq misrule (from **1326**) and revolts freed Andhra within about **2 years**.
**Kapaya Nayaka** took **Orugallu** back from **Malik Maqbool** in **1336**.

99.s:
Consider the following statements about the surviving generals of Prataparudra:
1. Prolaya Nayaka survived the fall of Warangal.
2. Recherla Singama survived the fall of Warangal.
3. Prolaya Vema Reddi survived the fall of Warangal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

99.tq: Test a complete named list through the all-inclusive option.
xs: All three — **Prolaya Nayaka, Recherla Singama and Prolaya Vema Reddi** — survived, so option **(4)** is correct.
They were the only three survivors of **Prataparudra's 75 generals** after the fall of Warangal (**1323**).

99.s: Which one of the following best describes the Vimochanodyamam?
o: A religious movement founded by the Velamas
The first organised resistance to Muslim rule in Andhra
A military expedition of the Cholas into Telangana
A revenue settlement introduced by the Reddis

99.tq: Identify the movement by its character and historical significance.
xs: **Vimochanodyamam** was the **first organised resistance to Muslim rule in Andhra** — so option **(2)** is correct.

xa: Chiefs involved: **Prolaya Vema Reddi, Recherla Singama, Koppula Prolaya Nayaka**, Kolani Rudra, Vengi Bhupala, Kapaya Nayaka.

99.s: The Musunuri kingdom is generally associated with which period?
99.x: The Musunuri kingdom is dated approximately from 1325 to 1368 CE.
99.tq: Distinguish the kingdom’s duration from the dates of individual rulers and battles.
xs: The Musunuri kingdom is dated **1325–1368 CE** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**1325-1475** is the span of the **Recherla Velamas**, and **1323** is the fall of Warangal.
xa: Successor states: **Musunuri (1325-1368)**, **Recherla Velama (1325-1475)**, **Reddi (1325-1448)**.
It ended at the **Battle of Bhimavaram (1367-68)**, where **Kapaya Nayaka** was killed.
**Prolaya Nayaka** ruled from **Rekapalli** from **1325**; **Kapaya Nayaka** ruled **1336-1368**.

99.s: Which of the following sets contains only chiefs associated with the Musunuri liberation effort?
o: Anapotha Nayaka, Devaraya II, Prolaya Vema Reddi and Ganapati Deva
Anapota Reddy, Kumaragiri Reddy, Pedakomati Vema and Kapaya Nayaka
Rajaraja Narendra, Kulottunga Chola, Kolani Rudra and Kapaya Nayaka
Prolaya Vema Reddi, Recherla Singama, Kolani Rudra and Kapaya Nayaka
99.x: Option D is right: Prolaya Vema Reddi, Recherla Singama, Kolani Rudra and Kapaya Nayaka are all listed among the chiefs of the Musunuri-led liberation confederacy. The other sets include rulers outside it, such as Devaraya II, Ganapati Deva, Kumaragiri, Pedakomati Vema, Rajaraja Narendra and Kulottunga Chola.
99.tq: Find the option whose entire membership belongs to the specified confederacy.
xs: **Prolaya Vema Reddi, Recherla Singama, Kolani Rudra and Kapaya Nayaka** are all listed chiefs of the liberation confederacy — so option **(4)** is correct.
The other sets include outsiders: **Devaraya II**, **Ganapati Deva** (a Kakatiya), **Kumaragiri** and **Pedakomati** (later Reddis), **Rajaraja Narendra**, **Kulottunga Chola**.
xa: Other chiefs: **Koppula Prolaya Nayaka**, **Vengi Bhupala**, **Manchikonda Ganapati Nayaka**.
The leader was **Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka**.
The movement is called **Vimochanodyamam**.

99.s: Who led the confederacy of Nayakas that freed Andhra from Tughluq rule after the fall of Warangal in 1323?
99.x: Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka led the liberation confederacy, the Vimochanodyamam (APPSC GS 2018; G2 2019). Recherla Singama, Prolaya Vema Reddi and Kolani Rudra were chiefs who took part in the movement but did not lead it.
99.tq: Leader of the liberation = Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka; Kaluvacheru grant names 75 Nayakas who backed him.
xs: **Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka** led the liberation confederacy (APPSC GS 2018; G2 2019) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Recherla Singama**, **Prolaya Vema Reddi** and **Kolani Rudra** were participating chiefs, not the leader.
xa: Prolaya Nayaka was son of **Potinayaka**, of the **Kamma** clan.
He ruled from **Rekapalli** on the Godavari, near **Bhadrachalam** (APPSC G2 2017).
His **Vilasa copper-plate grant (1330)** records Tughluq atrocities and his relief measures.
Childless, he was succeeded by **Kapaya Nayaka**.

99.s: The Musunuri Nayaks belonged primarily to which community?
99.x: The Musunuris belonged to the Kamma community, also described as Chaturthanvayas.
99.tq: Distinguish the Musunuri community from the neighbouring ruling groups.
xs: The Musunuris belonged to the **Kamma** clan (the **Chaturthanvaya** lineage) — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Velamas** were their rivals (Recherla of Rachakonda), and the **Reddis** formed a separate successor state.
xa: The surname comes from **Musunuru** village near **Vuyyuru** (Krishna district).
Prolaya Nayaka was the son of **Potinayaka**.
Velamas are also called **Padmanayakas**.

99.s: The name ‘Musunuri’ was derived from:
o: A village near Vuyyuru in Krishna district
A temple town near Sri Kalahasti
A port near Rajahmundry in Godavari district
A fort near Rachakonda in Nalgonda district
99.x: The surname Musunuri was derived from Musunuru village near Vuyyuru in Krishna district.
99.tq: Apply the place-name origin clue to identify the correct location.
xs: The surname comes from **Musunuru village near Vuyyuru in Krishna district** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Sri Kalahasti** was the seat of the **Damerla** Velamas, and **Rachakonda** that of the Recherla Velamas.
xa: The Musunuris were **Kammas** (Chaturthanvaya lineage).
Their first capital was **Rekapalli** on the Godavari.
**Kapaya Nayaka** ruled from **Orugallu (Warangal)** from **1336**.

99.s: Which territory was cleared by Prolaya Nayaka during the initial Musunuri resistance?
o: The region between the Pennar and Tungabhadra rivers
The tract between the Krishna and Godavari rivers
The plateau between the Bhima and Krishna rivers
The coastal tract between the Mahanadi and Godavari rivers
99.x: Prolaya Nayaka cleared the Krishna–Godavari tract and established his authority there.
99.tq: Use river boundaries to identify the precise territorial unit.
xs: Prolaya Nayaka freed **the land between the Krishna and Godavari** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He then ruled from **Rekapalli** on the Godavari from **1325**.
xa: Rekapalli lay in the forest near **Bhadrachalam** (capital: APPSC G2 2017).
In **1336** **Singama** cleared **Nalgonda-Mahabubnagar**, and **Prolaya Vema Reddi** cleared **Kammanadu-Pakanadu** south of the Krishna.
His **Vilasa grant (1330)** records **restoration of agraharas** to Brahmins.

99.s: Prolaya Nayaka ruled from which place?
99.x: Prolaya Nayaka ruled from Rekapalli, situated on the Godavari in the forest region near Bhadrachalam.
99.tq: Separate the capital of Prolaya from the later Musunuri capital of Kapaya.
xs: Prolaya Nayaka ruled from **Rekapalli** — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC G2 2017).
**Orugallu** was **Kapaya Nayaka's** capital from **1336**; **Rachakonda** and **Devarakonda** were **Recherla Velama** capitals.
xa: Rekapalli lay **on the Godavari**, in forest near **Bhadrachalam**.
The Velamas moved their capital from **Amanagallu to Rachakonda** under **Anapota Nayaka**.
Reddi capitals: **Addanki → Kondavidu → Rajahmundry**.

99.s:
Consider the following statements about the Vilasa copper-plate grant of 1330:
1. It describes the sufferings of the people under Tughluq rule.
2. It records Prolaya Nayaka's restoration of agraharas to Brahmins.
3. It was issued by the Reddi queen Anitalli.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
99.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Vilasa grant (1330) of Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka describes the Tughluq atrocities and his relief measures, including the restoration of agraharas. Statement 3 is wrong: Anitalli issued the Kaluvacheru grant of 1423, not the Vilasa grant.
99.tq: Vilasa 1330 = Prolaya Nayaka; Kaluvacheru 1423 = Anitalli.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **Vilasa grant (1330)** describes sufferings under **Tughluq** rule.
Statement 2 is correct: it records agrarian relief and **restoration of agraharas** to Brahmins.
Statement 3 is wrong: Reddi queen **Anitalli** issued the **Kaluvacheru grant (1423)**, not the Vilasa grant.
xa: The Vilasa grant was issued by **Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka**.
The **Kaluvacheru grant** names **75 Nayakas** who backed Prolaya.
**Polavaram, Ganapeshwaram and Palasamarri** records belong to **Kapaya Nayaka**.

99.s: Kapaya Nayaka appointed whom to govern Vengi?
99.x: Kapaya Nayaka appointed his nephew Anapotha Nayaka to govern Vengi.
99.tq: Test the appointment relationship rather than the broader list of confederate chiefs.
xs: Kapaya Nayaka appointed his nephew **Anapotha Nayaka** as governor at **Vengi** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Manchikonda Ganapati Nayaka** and **Kolani Rudra** were liberation chiefs; **Prolaya Vema Reddi** founded the Reddi kingdom.
xa: ⚠ Do not confuse with **Anapota Nayaka**, the Recherla Velama who killed Kapaya at **Bhimavaram (1367-68)**.
Kapaya's **Polavaram inscription** names **14** members of the lineage, only **3** of whom ruled.
Kapaya extended power to **Kaulas (Bidar)**.

99.s: Which of the following was NOT a title associated with Kapaya Nayaka?
99.x: Andhradeshadhiswara, Katakachurakara and Andhra Suratrana were associated with Kapaya Nayaka. Kavirajamarga is not one of his titles.
99.tq: Identify the unrelated famous term among titles belonging to the same historical setting.
xs: **Kavirajamarga** is not a title of Kapaya Nayaka — so option **(3)** is the answer.
His titles were **Andhra Suratrana**, **Andhradeshadhiswara** and **Katakachurakara**.
xa: Kapaya was the **first** to bear **Andhra Suratrana** (APPSC GS 2019); later **Anavema Reddi** too (APPSC G2 2011 key).
**Andhradesadhisvara** had earlier been held by Kakatiya **Ganapatideva**.
⚠ "First borne by" → **Kapaya**; "popular title of" with Anavema in the options → **Anavema Reddi**.

99.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Fall of Warangal
B. Issue of the Vilasa grant
C. Kapaya Nayaka’s capture of Orugallu
D. Battle of Bhimavaram
99.x: Warangal fell in 1323, the Vilasa grant was issued in 1330, Orugallu was captured in 1336, and the Battle of Bhimavaram occurred in 1367–68.
99.tq: Place the events by their stated years before checking the sequence options.
xs: Order: **A, B, C, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Fall of Warangal (1323)** → **Vilasa grant (1330)** → **Kapaya's capture of Orugallu (1336)** → **Battle of Bhimavaram (1367-68)**.
xa: Kapaya helped found the **Bahmani** kingdom in **1347** (Gulbarga).
Bahmani gains: **Kaulas (1350)**, **Bhuvanagiri (1356)**, **Golconda (1364-65)**.
Bhimavaram was the **last battle** of the Musunuri kingdom.

99.s:
Consider the following statements about the titles associated with Kapaya Nayaka:
1. He was known by the title Andhradesadhisvara.
2. He was known by the title Katakachurakara.
3. Andhradesadhisvara had earlier been held by Kakatiya Ganapatideva.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
99.x: Kapaya Nayaka is associated with both Andhradesadhisvara and Katakachurakara. The title Andhradesadhisvara had earlier been used by Kakatiya Ganapatideva.
99.tq: Check the title-holder details and the earlier association separately before selecting the combined code.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statements 1 and 2: Kapaya Nayaka bore **Andhradesadhisvara** and **Katakachurakara**.
Statement 3: **Andhradesadhisvara** was earlier held by Kakatiya **Ganapatideva**.
xa: Kapaya was the **first holder** of **Andhra Suratrana** (APPSC GS 2019).
⚠ **Kataka Churakara** is also listed as a title of Reddi **Kataya Vema** in Reddi notes.
Kapaya ruled **1336-1368** from **Orugallu**.

99.s: In the recovery of Warangal in 1336, Kapaya Nayaka acted together with
o: Hoysala Veera Ballala III, Prolaya Vema Reddi and Singama
Bukka I, Mahmud Gawan and Sultan Quli Qutb Shah
Annadevu, Kataya Vema and Pedakomati Vema Reddi
Hasan Gangu, Firoz Shah Tughlaq and Vinayaka Deva
99.x: In 1336, Kapaya Nayaka, Hoysala Veera Ballala III, Prolaya Vema Reddi and Singama took Warangal from Malik Maqbul.
99.tq: Start with the sure association of the liberation coalition and reject later-period figures.
xs: In **1336** Kapaya took Warangal with **Hoysala Veera Ballala III, Prolaya Vema Reddi and Singama** — so option **(1)** is correct.
They took **Orugallu** from **Malik Maqbool**.
**Bukka I** was sought later against the Bahmanis; **Hasan Gangu** was helped by Kapaya in **1347**; **Sultan Quli Qutb Shah** came much later.
xa: Kapaya then ruled the old **Kakatiya** realm from **Orugallu**.
Simultaneously **Singama** cleared Nalgonda-Mahabubnagar and **Prolaya Vema Reddi** cleared Kammanadu-Pakanadu.

99.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the simultaneous territorial activities of the three leaders in 1336?
o: Kapaya took Warangal, Singama cleared Nalgonda–Mahabubnagar, and Prolaya Vema Reddi cleared Kammanadu–Pakanadu
Singama took Warangal, Kapaya cleared Kammanadu–Pakanadu, and Prolaya Vema Reddi cleared Nalgonda–Mahabubnagar
Prolaya Vema Reddi took Warangal, Kapaya cleared Nalgonda–Mahabubnagar, and Singama cleared Vengi
Kapaya took Vengi, Singama cleared Kammanadu–Pakanadu, and Prolaya Vema Reddi took Warangal
99.x: Kapaya recovered Warangal, Singama cleared Nalgonda and Mahabubnagar, and Prolaya Vema Reddi cleared Kammanadu and Pakanadu south of the Krishna.
99.tq: Match each leader with the correct region and detect the swapped assignments.
xs: **Kapaya** took Warangal, **Singama** cleared **Nalgonda–Mahabubnagar**, and **Prolaya Vema Reddi** cleared **Kammanadu–Pakanadu** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Kammanadu-Pakanadu lay **south of the Krishna**.
xa: Kapaya's ally was **Hoysala Veera Ballala III**; Warangal was taken from **Malik Maqbul** in **1336**.
Kapaya appointed **Anapota Nayaka** as governor at **Vengi**.
**Singama Nayaka I** later expanded up to the **Krishna** and into the **Krishna-Tungabhadra doab**.

99.s: Kapaya Nayaka extended his power up to
99.x: Kapaya Nayaka extended his authority to Kaulas in the Bidar region.
99.tq: Test the northern extent of power through the place-region association.
xs: Kapaya Nayaka extended his power to **Kaulas (Bidar)** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Golconda** was later ceded by Kapaya to the Bahmanis; **Jallipalli** is where **Singama** was killed.
xa: Kaulas Durgam was lost to the Bahmanis in **1350**.
**Bhuvanagiri Durgam** was lost in **1356**.
**Golconda Durgam** was lost in **1364-65** with **33 lakhs** in treasure.

99.s: The title 'Andhra Suratrana' was first borne by:
99.x: Musunuri Kapaya Nayaka was the first to bear Andhra Suratrana (APPSC GS 2019). Anavema Reddi used it later and is the APPSC G2 2011 key answer for 'popular title of'. Prolaya Vema and Singama Nayaka I did not bear it.
99.tq: 'First borne by' = Kapaya; 'popular title of', with Anavema among the options = Anavema.
xs: **Kapaya Nayaka** was the first to bear **Andhra Suratrana** (APPSC GS 2019) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Anavema Reddi** bore it later (APPSC G2 2011 key for "popular title of").
**Prolaya Vema Reddi** and **Singama Nayaka I** are not recorded with this title.
xa: Kapaya's other titles: **Andhradeshadhiswara** and **Katakachurakara**.
⚠ "First borne by" → Kapaya; "popular title of" with Anavema in options → Anavema.
Kapaya was paternal nephew (some notes: cousin) of **Prolaya Nayaka**.

99.s: The Battle of Bhimavaram of 1367–68 resulted in which of the following?
o: The Reddis capturing Rachakonda from the Velamas
The Cholas restoring the Kakatiya kingdom
Prolaya Nayaka defeating Malik Maqbul at Rekapalli
Kapaya Nayaka defeated and killed by the Recherla Velamas under Anapota Nayaka
99.x: At Bhimavaram, near Orugallu, Kapaya Nayaka was defeated and killed by the Recherla Velamas led by Anapota Nayaka, after which Telangana passed to the Velamas of Rachakonda.
99.tq: Use the outcome and opposing leaders to identify the battle correctly.
xs: At **Bhimavaram (1367–68)** Kapaya Nayaka was **defeated and killed by the Recherla Velamas under Anapota Nayaka** — so option **(4)** is correct.
This ended the **Musunuri** line; **Telangana** passed to the Velamas of Rachakonda.
xa: Bhimavaram lay **near Orugallu**.
⚠ A PYQ (aph2019_11) explanation says the **Reddis** beat the Velamas at Bhimavaram and drove them out of **Palnadu** — learn it as a Velama-Musunuri battle.
**Anapota Nayaka** moved the Velama capital from **Amanagallu to Rachakonda**.

99.s: Kapaya Nayaka helped Hasan Gangu in founding the Bahmani kingdom in
99.x: Kapaya Nayaka helped Hasan Gangu, also known as Zafar Khan, establish the Bahmani kingdom at Gulbarga in 1347.
99.tq: Keep the year and place together to avoid confusing the Bahmani foundation with later territorial losses.
xs: Kapaya helped **Hasan Gangu (Zafar Khan)** found the **Bahmani** kingdom in **1347 at Gulbarga** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**1356** is the loss of **Bhuvanagiri**, **1367** Bhimavaram, and **1336** the recovery of Warangal.
xa: Kapaya then lost to the Bahmanis: **Kaulas (1350)**, **Bhuvanagiri (1356)**, **Golconda (1364-65)**.
His son **Vinayaka Deva** was burnt alive by **Muhammad Shah I** (1361-62).
Same wave: **Harihara-Bukka** founded Vijayanagara in **1336**.

99.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Kapaya Nayaka received help from Bukka I of Vijayanagara.
2. Kapaya Nayaka sought assistance from Firoz Shah Tughlaq.
3. Kapaya Nayaka remained permanently allied with the Bahmanis after helping to establish their kingdom.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
99.x: Kapaya received help from Bukka I and sought help from Firoz Shah Tughlaq. He later came into conflict with the Bahmanis, so statement 3 is false.
99.tq: Reject the absolute word ‘permanently’ and identify the two documented alliances or requests for aid.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: Kapaya allied with/sought help from **Bukka I** of Vijayanagara against the Bahmanis.
Statement 2: he also sought help from **Firoz Shah Tughlaq**.
Statement 3 is wrong: after helping found the Bahmani kingdom (**1347**) he **lost** forts and his son to it.
xa: The truce of **1364-65** ceded **Golconda**, which became the boundary.
A **turquoise throne** was among the gifts.
He lost **400 elephants**, **250 horses** and **33 lakhs** with Golconda.

99.s:
Arrange the following events associated with Kapaya Nayaka in chronological order:
A. Loss of Bhuvanagiri Durgam
B. Recovery of Warangal from Malik Maqbul
C. Founding of the Bahmani kingdom with Hasan Gangu’s assistance
D. Loss of Golconda Durgam
99.x: Warangal was recovered in 1336, the Bahmani kingdom was founded in 1347, Bhuvanagiri was lost in 1356, and Golconda was lost in 1364–65.
99.tq: Place the two foundation events first, then order the dated territorial losses.
xs: Order: **B, C, A, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Recovery of Warangal (1336)** → **Bahmani founding (1347)** → **loss of Bhuvanagiri (1356)** → **loss of Golconda (1364-65)**.
xa: **Kaulas Durgam** was lost in **1350**.
Son **Vinayaka Deva** was killed in **1361/1362**.
Kapaya died at **Bhimavaram (1367-68)**.

99.s: The Bahmanis acquired Kaulas and Bhuvanagiri from Kapaya Nayaka in which respective years?
99.x: Kaulas was lost in 1350 and Bhuvanagiri was lost in 1356.
99.tq: Separate paired dates by preserving the order in which the events occurred.
xs: **Kaulas** was lost in **1350** and **Bhuvanagiri** in **1356** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option (4) reverses the order; **1361** and **1364-65** relate to Vinayaka Deva and Golconda.
xa: **1361/1362**: son **Vinayaka Deva** killed by **Muhammad Shah I**.
**1364-65**: **Golconda Durgam** ceded with **400 elephants**, **250 horses** and **33 lakhs**.
Kapaya had extended his power to **Kaulas (Bidar)** before losing it.

99.s: Which one of the following events occurred in 1361–62 during the conflict between Kapaya Nayaka and the Bahmanis?
o: Golconda was ceded under a truce
Bhuvanagiri was lost to the Bahmanis
Kaulas was lost to the Bahmanis
Vinayaka Deva was captured and burnt alive by Muhammad Shah I
99.x: Muhammad Shah I captured and burnt Vinayaka Deva, the son of Kapaya Nayaka, alive in 1361–62. This severely weakened Kapaya’s morale.
99.tq: Link a precise date with the person and event associated with it.
xs: In **1361–62** **Vinayaka Deva**, Kapaya's son, was **captured and burnt alive by Muhammad Shah I** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Golconda** was ceded in **1364-65**, **Bhuvanagiri** lost in **1356**, and **Kaulas** in **1350**.
xa: The killing broke **Kapaya's morale**.
APP notes: burned alive at 'Velama town', **1361**; CDX notes: **1362**.
The Bahmani kingdom had been founded in **1347** with Kapaya's help.

99.s: Which of the following correctly describes the truce of 1364–65 between Kapaya Nayaka and the Bahmanis?
o: Bhuvanagiri was ceded along with the turquoise throne
Kaulas was restored to Kapaya and Bhuvanagiri was made the boundary
The Bahmanis abandoned Telangana and recognised Kapaya’s sovereignty over Golconda
Golconda fort was ceded along with substantial wealth and Golconda became the boundary
99.x: Under the truce of 1364–65, Kapaya ceded Golconda fort with huge wealth, and Golconda became the boundary between the powers.
99.tq: Use the terms of a settlement rather than the earlier military events.
xs: Under the **1364–65 truce**, **Golconda fort was ceded with huge wealth** and **Golconda became the boundary** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Bhuvanagiri** had been lost earlier, in **1356**, and **Kaulas** in **1350**; neither was restored.
xa: Wealth ceded: **400 elephants**, **250 horses** and **33 lakhs** in treasure.
A **turquoise throne** was among the gifts.
Kapaya sought help from **Bukka I** and **Firoz Shah Tughlaq** against the Bahmanis.

99.s: Which statement regarding the Velamas is correct?
o: They are also called Padmanayakas and are traditionally said to have originated from Vishnu’s lotus feet.
They are also called Agraharikas and are traditionally said to have originated from Brahma’s crown.

99.x: Velamas are also called Padmanayakas, and their tradition connects their origin with the lotus feet of Vishnu.
99.tq: Separate the Velama designation and origin legend from the similar Musunuri lineage term.
xs: Velamas are also called **Padmanayakas**, said to be born from the **lotus feet of Vishnu** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Chaturthanvaya** is the lineage of the **Kamma** Musunuris, and **Suratrana** is a title, not a Velama name.
xa: The Rachakonda and Devarakonda kings were of the **Recherla gotra**.
Family history: **Velugoti Varivamsavali**; founder of lineage: **Betala Nayudu**.

99.s: The Rachakonda and Devarakonda rulers belonged to which gotra?
99.x: The rulers of Rachakonda and Devarakonda belonged to the Recherla gotra and had earlier been Kakatiya feudatories.
99.tq: Distinguish the ruling gotra from the names of other Velama families.
xs: The Rachakonda and Devarakonda kings were of the **Recherla** gotra — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Damerla** ruled **Sri Kalahasti**; **Velugoti** → **Venkatagiri**; **Ravu** → **Bobbili**.
xa: The Recherlas began as **feudatories of the early Kakatiyas**.
They ruled **Telangana** for about **150 years (1325-1475)**.

99.s: Who founded the Recherla Velama lineage?
99.x: Betala Nayudu is identified as the founder of the Recherla lineage.
99.tq: Use the founder-versus-successor distinction, a common dynasty trap.
xs: **Betala Nayudu** founded the Recherla Velama lineage — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Singama Nayudu I** founded the **independent kingdom**; **Anapota Nayaka** moved the capital to **Rachakonda**.
**Sarvagna Singa Bhupala** was a later Sanskrit **scholar-king** of Rachakonda.
xa: Family history: **Velugoti Varivamsavali**.
Velamas are also called **Padmanayakas**.
The kingdom ended when **Sultan Quli Qutb Shah** annexed Rachakonda and Devarakonda.

99.s: Which one of the following statements about Singama Nayaka I is correct?
o: He founded the independent kingdom and expanded towards the Krishna and the Krishna-Tungabhadra doab
He shifted the capital from Rachakonda to Amanagallu
He founded the Bahmani kingdom at Gulbarga
He defeated Sultan Quli Qutb Shah and recovered Devarakonda
99.x: Singama Nayaka I founded the independent Velama kingdom and expanded to the Krishna and into the Krishna-Tungabhadra doab.
99.tq: Reject options assigning later rulers’ actions to the kingdom’s founder.
xs: **Singama Nayaka I** founded the **independent kingdom** and expanded up to the **Krishna** and into the **Krishna-Tungabhadra doab** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The capital shift (**Amanagallu → Rachakonda**) was by his son **Anapota Nayaka**, not from Rachakonda to Amanagallu.
The **Bahmani** kingdom was founded by **Hasan Gangu**.
xa: In **1336** Singama expelled the Muslims from **Nalgonda and Mahabubnagar**.
**Kapaya Nayaka** failed to subdue him.
He was **killed fighting the chiefs of Jallipalli**.

99.s:
Consider the following statements about the Recherla Velama kingdom:
1. It began as a kingdom of loyal feudatories under the early Kakatiyas.
2. Its duration is generally placed between 1325 and 1475.
3. It lasted for approximately 150 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

99.tq: Combine institutional origin with dates and duration before selecting the coded option.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.

99.s: Which Sultan defeated the Velama chiefs and annexed both Rachakonda and Devarakonda?
o: Muhammad I of the Bahmani dynasty
99.x: Sultan Quli Qutb Shah, who ruled at Golconda from 1518 to 1543, defeated the Velama chiefs and annexed Rachakonda and Devarakonda.
99.tq: Distinguish the final conqueror from earlier Bahmani opponents and ministers.
xs: **Sultan Quli Qutb Shah** (Golconda, **1518-43**) defeated the Velama chiefs and annexed **Rachakonda and Devarakonda** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Mahmud Gawan** was a Bahmani minister who crushed Telangana revolts **with Velama help**.
**Muhammad I** burnt **Vinayaka Deva**; **Firoz Shah Tughlaq** was approached by Kapaya for help.
xa: The Velamas later sided with the **Bahmanis and Gajapatis** against Vijayanagara and the Reddis.
**Devarakonda** (Nalgonda) was the second Velama branch capital.

99.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Betala Nayudu — Founder of the Recherla lineage
Singama Nayaka I — Killed in the Battle of Bhimavaram
Anapota Nayaka — Shifted the capital to Rachakonda

xa: The princess was **Bhadradevi** (Tukkadevi/Jaganmohini).
Prataparudra remained a **feudatory**.
Settlement: c. **1518-19**.

100.s: The Madala Panji is best described as which of the following?
o: A temple chronicle of Jagannath at Puri dealing with Gajapati history
A Persian history of the Deccan sultans
A military account of Kapileswara's attack on Andhra
An inscription describing Vijayanagara assistance to the Reddis
100.x: Madala Panji is the temple chronicle of Jagannath at Puri and contains material on Gajapati history.
100.tq: Use the source–content association and distinguish the chronicle from the Persian history and inscriptions.
xs: **Madala Panji** is the **temple chronicle of Jagannath, Puri**, on Gajapati history — so option **(1)** is correct.
A Persian history of the Deccan sultans is **Ferishta**; Vijayanagara help to the Reddis is in the **Draksharama inscription (1444)**.
Kapileswara's attack on Tiran Andhra is recorded in the **Penugonda inscription**.
xa: **Anantavaram inscription** (Prataparudra): the **Virupaksharayas** defeated and made to pay **Kappam**.
Victory pillars at **Simhachalam** and **Potnuru** mark **Krishnadevaraya's** triumph.

100.s: Ferishta's account is particularly important for studying which aspect of the history of the Deccan?
o: The temple administration of Jagannath at Puri
The Gajapati inscriptions at Srikurmam and Simhachalam
The assistance given by Vijayanagara to the Reddis
The Bahmani side of the conflicts, through a Persian history of the Deccan sultans
100.x: Ferishta wrote a Persian history of the Deccan sultans, making his account especially significant for the Bahmani side.
100.tq: Match the historian or source with its viewpoint and subject.
xs: **Ferishta** is a **Persian history of the Deccan sultans** — the **Bahmani side** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Jagannath temple history is the **Madala Panji**; Vijayanagara help to the Reddis is the **Draksharama inscription**.
xa: The **Anantavaram inscription** records the **Virupaksharayas** paying tribute (**Kappam**).

The kingdom was largest under **Mahmud Gawan**.

100.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

 d. Victory pillars at Simhachalam and Potnuru

100.s: Which of the following pairs consists of sites in present-day Andhra Pradesh associated with the Gajapati wars?
o: Srikurmam, Puri, Delhi, Agra and Rajahmundry
Warangal, Hampi, Bidar, Gulbarga and Daulatabad
Udayagiri, Kondaveedu, Kondapalli, Rajahmundry and Simhachalam
Penugonda, Anantavaram, Draksharama, Potnuru and Puri

100.tq: Separate the regional war sites from source locations and places outside Andhra Pradesh.
xs: **Udayagiri, Kondaveedu, Kondapalli, Rajahmundry and Simhachalam** are the AP sites of the Gajapati wars — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Puri** is in Odisha; **Warangal, Bidar, Gulbarga** lie outside the listed AP sites.

100.s: The Gajapatis ruled approximately during which period?

**Uttarandhra** culture shows their influence.

100.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the cultural significance of Gajapati rule in the Andhra region?
o: Uttarandhra culture shows the influence of Gajapati rule.
Its influence was confined exclusively to the Deccan sultanates.

xs: **Uttarandhra culture shows the influence of Gajapati rule** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The notes say nothing of Persian replacement or of influence confined to forts.
xa: The Gajapatis ruled c. **1434** to **1541**.
The whole of **north coastal Andhra** was under them.

101.s: Who coined the epithet “Italian of the East” for Telugu?
101.x: The Venetian traveller Niccolo de' Conti, who visited in the fifteenth century, is associated with the epithet “Italian of the East” for Telugu.
101.tq: Match the famous epithet with the traveller who coined it.
xs: The Venetian traveller **Niccolo de' Conti** (**15th c.**) called Telugu the **"Italian of the East"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Sri Krishnadevaraya** coined a different praise: **"Desa bhashalandu Telugu lessa"** in **Amuktamalyada**.
The reason given: Telugu's **rounded, vowel-ending, highly phonetic** character.
xa: It was asked in **APPSC GS 2021** (key: Italian of the East).
⚠ **Italian of the East** = a foreign traveller; **Desa bhashalandu Telugu lessa** = a king.
Telugu is a **South-Central Dravidian** language, official language of AP.

101.s: The expression “Desa bhashalandu Telugu lessa” is associated with which person and work?
o: Niccolo de' Conti — a travel account
101.x: Sri Krishnadevaraya used the expression “Desa bhashalandu Telugu lessa” in Amuktamalyada, meaning that Telugu is the finest among regional languages.
101.tq: Use the author–work–quotation triad to distinguish two famous statements about Telugu.
xs: **"Desa bhashalandu Telugu lessa"** is **Sri Krishnadevaraya's** line in **Amuktamalyada** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It means Telugu is the **finest of the regional languages**.
**Niccolo de' Conti** coined **"Italian of the East"**, not this line.
xa: Krishnadevaraya also wrote **Jambavati Kalyanam** (Sanskrit).
The **Ashtadiggajas** at his court mark the peak of the **Prabandha** age.
**Telugu Language Day** is **29 August**, the birth anniversary of **Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy**.

101.s: Telugu belongs to which sub-branch of the Dravidian language family?
101.x: Telugu belongs to the South-Central Dravidian sub-branch.
101.tq: Test the exact linguistic sub-classification rather than the broader family name.
xs: Telugu belongs to the **South-Central Dravidian** sub-branch — so option **(2)** is correct.
Its family is **Dravidian** (CDCA 2026).
xa: Sister languages include **Gondi** and **Kui**.
It is one of the **22 Eighth Schedule languages** and the official language of AP.
It has been a **classical language since 2008**.

101.s: Which of the following are identified as sister languages of Telugu within the South-Central Dravidian group?
101.x: Gondi and Kui are identified among the sister languages of Telugu in the South-Central Dravidian sub-branch.
101.tq: Distinguish sister languages from other Dravidian languages outside the stated sub-branch.
xs: **Gondi and Kui** are named as sister languages of Telugu — so option **(4)** is correct.
They sit with Telugu in the **South-Central Dravidian** sub-branch.
xa: Telugu grew out of the **Desi bhasha (Paisachi)** of Prakrit.
**D.C. Sircar** found Desi words very close to Telugu.
Other names of the language: **Andhra**, **Andhrika**, **Tenugu**.

101.s:
