103.x: The Maru-Gurjara style, associated with the Solanki tradition of Gujarat and Rajasthan, often includes a Kirti-torana.
103.tq: Identify the specific architectural feature attached to the regional style, not merely its geographical location.
xs: The Maru-Gurjara sub-style often has a **Kirti-torana** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Rekha deul** belongs to the **Odisha/Kalinga** school; **Valabhi** is just a barrel-vaulted tower type.
xa: Maru-Gurjara = **Solanki**, **Gujarat-Rajasthan**, **11th-13th c.**, fusing **Maha-Maru** + **Maha-Gurjara**.
Shikhara types: **Latina** (single curvilinear), **Phamsana** (sloping, stepped), **Valabhi** (barrel-vaulted).

103.s: The Vijaya Stambha at Chittor was built by Rana Kumbha to commemorate his victory over
103.x: Rana Kumbha built the Vijaya Stambha at Chittor to commemorate his victory over Mahmud Khalji of Malwa.
103.tq: Separate the builder from the opponent associated with the monument.
xs: Rana Kumbha built the **Vijaya Stambha** at Chittor for his victory over **Mahmud Khalji of Malwa** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The builder Rana Kumbha is an APPSC G2 **2011** question.
⚠ **Alauddin Khalji** of Delhi is the **Rani Padmini** jauhar story, not this tower.
xa: ⚠ **Vijaya Stambha** = Rana Kumbha; **Kirti Stambha** = Jain merchant **Jijaji**.
Rana Kumbha also built **Kumbhalgarh** fort.

103.s: Who constructed the Kirti Stambha at Chittor in the twelfth century?
103.x: The Kirti Stambha at Chittor was constructed in the twelfth century by Jijaji, also known as Jeeja, a Jain merchant.
103.tq: Monument–builder recall with a social-identity clue.
xs: The **Kirti Stambha** at Chittor was built by **Jijaji (Jeeja), a Jain merchant**, in the **12th c.** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Rana Kumbha** built the other tower, the **Vijaya Stambha**.
xa: Vijaya Stambha commemorates Kumbha's victory over **Mahmud Khalji of Malwa**.
**Chittorgarh** was the **Guhila/Gehlot (Sisodia)** stronghold of **Mewar**.

103.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
103.x: Kumbhalgarh Fort was built by Rana Kumbha. Chittorgarh was a Guhila or Gehlot, later Sisodia, stronghold of Mewar, while the Kirti Stambha was built by Jijaji.
103.tq: Use builder–monument pairs and eliminate swapped builders.
xs: **Kumbhalgarh Fort — Rana Kumbha** is correct — so option **(1)** is the answer.
**Chittorgarh** was a **Guhila/Gehlot (Sisodia)** stronghold of **Mewar**, not Tomara.
The **Kirti Stambha** was built by **Jijaji**, and the **Vijaya Stambha** by **Rana Kumbha**.
xa: Vijaya Stambha marks Kumbha's victory over **Mahmud Khalji of Malwa** (APPSC G2 **2011**).
**Paramardi** was a **Chandela** ruler, hero of **Alha Khand**.

103.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Bhojshala:
1. The Madhya Pradesh High Court declared Bhojshala a Hindu temple on the strength of Archaeological Survey of India findings.
2. The ASI survey of Bhojshala was ordered in 2024.
3. Under a 2003 ASI arrangement, members of both communities worshipped there on separate days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: All three statements are correct. The Madhya Pradesh High Court relied on ASI findings in declaring Bhojshala a Hindu temple; the survey was ordered in 2024, while the 2003 arrangement provided for worship by the two communities on separate days.
103.tq: Combine judicial finding, survey year and administrative arrangement without confusing their sequence.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
1: the **Madhya Pradesh High Court** declared Bhojshala a **Hindu temple** on **ASI findings** (**May 2026**).
2: the ASI survey was ordered in **2024**.
3: under a **2003** ASI arrangement both communities worshipped on **separate days**.
xa: Bhojshala at **Dhar** has a **Saraswati (Vagdevi)** temple and was linked to **Bhoja**.
It was turned into a mosque in the **14th century**; Muslims call it **Kamal Maula Mosque**.

103.s: Modhera, site of the Solanki Sun temple, is in the news because it:
o: Was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2022
Was fully solarised under an MNRE scheme, inaugurated on 9 October 2022
Was declared a Hindu temple by the Gujarat High Court
Became the site of the Somnath Swabhiman Parv
103.x: Modhera was fully solarised under an MNRE scheme (6 MW plant with 15 MWh storage), inaugurated on 9 October 2022. The court ruling on a temple concerned Bhojshala (MP High Court); Somnath Swabhiman Parv concerns Somnath; there was no 2022 UNESCO listing for Modhera.
103.tq: Modhera = solar village, 9 Oct 2022
xs: Modhera was **fully solarised under an MNRE scheme**, inaugurated **9 October 2022** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The project: a **6 MW** plant with **15 MWh** storage, costing **₹76.66 crore**.
The court ruling was on **Bhojshala** by the **Madhya Pradesh High Court**, not Gujarat.
xa: The **Modhera Sun temple** (Surya) was built by Solanki **Bhima I**, in Mehsana, Gujarat.
⚠ The Solanki UNESCO site in the notes is **Rani-ki-Vav**, built by queen **Udayamati**.

103.s: With reference to the solarisation of Modhera, which one of the following is correct?
o: A 6 MW plant with 15 MWh storage was inaugurated on 9 October 2022 at a cost of ₹76.66 crore.
A 60 MW plant with 15 MWh storage was inaugurated on 9 October 2022 at a cost of ₹766.6 crore.
A 6 MW plant with 15 MWh storage was inaugurated on 18 May 2026 at a cost of ₹76.66 crore.
A 15 MW plant with 6 MWh storage was inaugurated on 9 October 2024 at a cost of ₹67.66 crore.
103.x: Modhera was fully solarised under an MNRE scheme through a 6 MW plant and 15 MWh storage system. The project, costing ₹76.66 crore, was inaugurated on 9 October 2022.
103.tq: Check the plant capacity, storage capacity, date and cost as a combined numerical set.
xs: A **6 MW** plant with **15 MWh** storage, inaugurated **9 October 2022** at **₹76.66 crore** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The other options swap the figures (60 MW, ₹766.6 crore) or the dates (2024, 2026).
The work was done under an **MNRE** scheme and made Modhera **fully solarised**.
xa: Modhera's **Sun temple** was built by **Bhima I** (Solanki) for **Surya**.
⚠ **May 2026** is the Bhojshala court ruling, not Modhera.

103.s: The debates associated with the study of Rajput states and society include debates over:
o: Rajput origin theories and the Indian feudalism thesis
Only the chronology of Chola naval expeditions
The authorship of Sangam literature alone
Only the classification of Buddhist stupas
103.x: The principal debates identified here concern the competing theories of Rajput origin and the Indian feudalism thesis.
103.tq: Select the option that preserves both elements of the stated historiographical debate.
xs: The debates are over **Rajput origin theories** and the **Indian feudalism thesis** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Origin theories: **Agnikula** (Chand Bardai), **foreign origin** (Col. James Tod, V.A. Smith), **Kshatriya descent** (G.H. Ojha, C.V. Vaidya).
**R.S. Sharma's** thesis: **sub-infeudation**, **vishti** (forced labour) and **closed village economies**.
xa: Rajput **land grants** carried revenue, judicial and police rights.
The Rajput states rose after the collapse of the **Pratihara** empire.

104.s: Which pair is NOT correctly matched?
104.x: Kitab-ul-Hind was written by Al-Biruni, not Firdausi. The other three source-author pairs are correctly matched.
104.tq: Find the swapped author in a list of medieval sources.
xs: **Kitab-ul-Hind — Firdausi** is wrong — so option **(2)** is the answer.
**Kitab-ul-Hind (Tahqiq-i-Hind)** was written in Arabic by **Al-Biruni**; **Firdausi** wrote the **Shahnama**.
The rest are correct: **Prithviraj Raso** by **Chand Bardai**, **Tabaqat-i-Nasiri** by **Minhaj-us-Siraj**, **Taj-ul-Maasir** by **Hasan Nizami**.
xa: ⚠ **Mahmud of Ghazni** patronised **Al-Biruni**, **Firdausi** and **Utbi** — all three, so they are easily mixed up.
**Utbi**, Mahmud's court historian, wrote **Kitab-ul-Yamini**.
⚠ **Prithviraj Raso** = Chand Bardai; **Prithviraja Vijaya** = **Jayanaka**.

104.s:
Consider the following statements regarding medieval Persian chronicles:
1. Taj-ul-Maasir was written by Hasan Nizami and relates to the early Sultanate.
2. Hasan Nizami was patronised by Qutbuddin Aibak.
3. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri was dedicated to Nasiruddin Mahmud.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
104.x: All three statements are correct. Hasan Nizami wrote Taj-ul-Maasir on the early Sultanate under the patronage of Qutbuddin Aibak, and Minhaj-us-Siraj dedicated Tabaqat-i-Nasiri to Nasiruddin Mahmud.
104.tq: Combine author, patron and dedication facts while checking whether all statements belong to the same source cluster.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
1: **Taj-ul-Maasir** by **Hasan Nizami** covers the **early Sultanate**.
2: Hasan Nizami was patronised by **Qutbuddin Aibak**.
3: **Minhaj-us-Siraj** dedicated **Tabaqat-i-Nasiri** to **Nasiruddin Mahmud**.
xa: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri covers the **Ghurids** and early **Delhi Sultans**.
Chronological order: **Kitab-ul-Hind** → **Taj-ul-Maasir** → **Tabaqat-i-Nasiri** → **Futuh-us-Salatin** → **Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi**.

104.s: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri primarily deals with which of the following periods?
o: The Bahmani rulers and the Qutb Shahis
The reigns of the later Mughals
The Ghurids and the early Delhi Sultans
The reigns of Akbar and Jahangir
104.x: Minhaj-us-Siraj’s Tabaqat-i-Nasiri covers the Ghurids and the early Delhi Sultans.
104.tq: Use the period covered as the distinguishing clue when several Sultanate works are listed.
xs: **Tabaqat-i-Nasiri** covers **the Ghurids and the early Delhi Sultans** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Its author **Minhaj-us-Siraj** dedicated it to **Nasiruddin Mahmud**.
Akbar's reign is covered by **Tabaqat-i-Akbari** (Nizamuddin Ahmad); the Qutb Shahis by works like **Hadikat-us-Salatin**.
xa: The earlier **Taj-ul-Maasir** (Hasan Nizami) also covers the early Sultanate.
Exam angle: **Minhaj: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri**; **Barani: Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi**; **Al-Biruni: Tahqiq-i-Hind**.

104.s: Who wrote Futuh-us-Salatin, a work covering the Ghaznavids to Muhammad bin Tughlaq and written at the Bahmani court around 1350?
104.x: Futuh-us-Salatin was written by Isami at the Bahmani court around 1350 and covers the period from the Ghaznavids to Muhammad bin Tughlaq, including the Tughlaq campaigns against Warangal.
104.tq: Distinguish similar Sultanate historians by matching the work with its author and historical range.
xs: **Futuh-us-Salatin** was written by **Isami** at the **Bahmani court c. 1350** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It runs from the **Ghaznavids** to **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**, including the Tughlaq campaigns against **Warangal**.
**Nizamuddin Ahmad** wrote **Tabaqat-i-Akbari**, **Sarhindi** wrote **Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi** and **Barani** wrote **Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes credit Futuh-us-Salatin to **Amir Khusrau** — the standard answer is Isami.
AP angle: **Isami** and **Firishta** are the sources asked for **Warangal**.

104.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi — Yahiya bin Ahmad Sarhindi
104.x: Tabaqat-i-Akbari was written by Nizamuddin Ahmad. Badauni’s own historical work was Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh.
104.tq: Find the wrong author–work pairing, especially where a neighbouring historian is substituted.
xs: **Tabaqat-i-Akbari — Badauni** is wrong — so option **(4)** is the answer.
**Tabaqat-i-Akbari** was written by **Nizamuddin Ahmad**; ⚠ some notes wrongly credit Badauni.
**Badauni's** own history is **Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh**.
The rest are correct: **Ziauddin Barani** wrote both **Fatawa-i-Jahandari** and **Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi**; **Sarhindi** wrote **Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi**.
xa: Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi is the main account of **Alauddin's market regulations**.
Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi was written under the **Sayyid** Sultan **Mubarak Shah**.

104.s: Fatawa-i-Jahandari is primarily a work on which subject?
o: The postal system of the Delhi Sultanate
104.x: Fatawa-i-Jahandari, written by Ziauddin Barani, deals with political theory and kingship.
104.tq: Identify the subject of a text rather than confusing it with the author’s historical chronicle.
xs: **Fatawa-i-Jahandari** deals with the **political theory of kingship** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Its author is **Ziauddin Barani**, who wrote from an **orthodox Sunni** viewpoint.
The postal system is in **Ibn Battuta's Rihla**; Golconda's conquest in **Khafi Khan's Muntakhab-ul-Lubab**; astronomy in **Al-Biruni**.
xa: Barani also wrote **Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi** (Balban to early Firoz Tughlaq).
Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi is the main account of **Alauddin's market regulations and ordinances**.

104.s: Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi was written during the reign of which ruler?
o: Mubarak Shah of the Sayyid dynasty
Nasiruddin Mahmud of the Slave dynasty
104.x: Yahiya bin Ahmad Sarhindi wrote Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi during the reign of Sayyid Sultan Mubarak Shah.
104.tq: Use the title and reign association to separate similarly named Sultanate chronicles.
xs: **Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi** was written in the reign of **Mubarak Shah of the Sayyid dynasty** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Its author is **Yahiya bin Ahmad Sarhindi**.
**Nasiruddin Mahmud** received **Tabaqat-i-Nasiri**; **Firoz Tughlaq** is in **Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi**; **Akbar** in **Tabaqat-i-Akbari**.
xa: In chronological order it comes after **Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi** and before **Tabaqat-i-Akbari**.
**Tabaqat-i-Akbari** = **Nizamuddin Ahmad** (not Badauni).

104.s:
Arrange the following works in chronological order of the periods they primarily cover:
A. Tabaqat-i-Akbari
B. Taj-ul-Maasir
C. Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi
D. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri
104.x: Taj-ul-Maasir belongs to the early Sultanate, followed by Tabaqat-i-Nasiri, Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi and finally Tabaqat-i-Akbari up to Akbar’s reign.
104.tq: Place the earliest and latest works first, then distinguish the two intervening Sultanate chronicles.
xs: The order is **B, D, C, A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Taj-ul-Maasir** (early Sultanate, Aibak) → **Tabaqat-i-Nasiri** (Ghurids, early Sultans, Nasiruddin Mahmud).
→ **Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi** (Balban to early Firoz Tughlaq) → **Tabaqat-i-Akbari** (up to Akbar).
xa: The earliest work in the list is **Al-Biruni's Kitab-ul-Hind** (c. **1030** CE).
**Futuh-us-Salatin** (Isami, c. **1350**) sits between Tabaqat-i-Nasiri and Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.
**Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi** (Sayyid period) comes just before Tabaqat-i-Akbari.

104.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding Amir Khusrau?
o: He wrote Kitab-ul-Yamini as court historian of Mahmud of Ghazni.
He wrote Rihla in Arabic after visiting Muhammad bin Tughlaq’s court.
He wrote Shahnama under the patronage of Akbar.
He wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh and accompanied Malik Kafur’s 1310 invasion of Warangal.
104.x: Amir Khusrau, court poet of Alauddin Khalji, wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh and accompanied Malik Kafur’s 1310 expedition to Warangal. Kitab-ul-Yamini was written by Utbi, Shahnama by Firdausi and Rihla by Ibn Battuta.
104.tq: Apply the author–ruler–work trap to distinguish famous medieval writers.
xs: Amir Khusrau **wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh and accompanied Malik Kafur's 1310 invasion of Warangal** — so option **(4)** is correct.
He was the **court poet of Alauddin Khalji**; Khazain-ul-Futuh describes 14th-century **Deccan** conditions.
**Kitab-ul-Yamini** is **Utbi's**, **Rihla** is **Ibn Battuta's**, **Shahnama** is **Firdausi's**.
xa: ⚠ As a court poet his history glorifies the patron — the **court bias** problem.
Muslim sources (**Amir Khusrau**, **Wassaf**) count **5** Warangal invasions; Telugu sources count **8**.

104.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
104.x: Utbi was the court historian of Mahmud of Ghazni and wrote Kitab-ul-Yamini. Firdausi wrote Shahnama, Ibn Battuta wrote Rihla and Amir Khusrau wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh.
104.tq: Use the famous title as the anchor and reject swapped authors.
xs: **Utbi — Kitab-ul-Yamini** is correct — so option **(1)** is the answer.
Utbi was **Mahmud of Ghazni's** court historian.
**Firdausi** wrote **Shahnama**, **Ibn Battuta** wrote **Rihla**, and **Amir Khusrau** wrote **Khazain-ul-Futuh**.
xa: Mahmud patronised **Al-Biruni**, **Firdausi** and **Utbi**.
Mahmud's **Lahore dirhams** carry an Arabic legend with a **Sanskrit** translation in **Sharada** script.

104.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Source)
A. Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi
B. Khazain-ul-Futuh
C. Futuh-us-Salatin

List-II (Author)
I. Isami
II. Amir Khusrau
III. Ziauddin Barani

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
104.x: Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi was written by Ziauddin Barani, Khazain-ul-Futuh by Amir Khusrau, and Futuh-us-Salatin by Isami.
104.tq: Start from the sure author–work pair and eliminate the remaining codes.
xs: The correct code is **A-III, B-II, C-I** — so option **(1)** is the answer.
**Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi** — **Ziauddin Barani**; **Khazain-ul-Futuh** — **Amir Khusrau**.
**Futuh-us-Salatin** — **Isami**, written at the **Bahmani court c. 1350**.
xa: Barani also wrote **Fatawa-i-Jahandari** on the theory of kingship.
Amir Khusrau went with **Malik Kafur's 1310** invasion of **Warangal**.

104.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ramacharitam — Sandhyakara Nandi — Life of Ramapala
Prithviraja Vijaya — Gangadevi — Life of Prithviraj Chauhan
Madhura Vijayam — Jayanaka — Conquest of Madurai
104.x: Ramacharitam was written by Sandhyakara Nandi and deals with the life of Pala king Ramapala. Prithviraja Vijaya was by Jayanaka, Madhura Vijayam by Gangadevi and Siddhesvara Charitam by Kase Siddhappa.
104.tq: Start with the author–work pair and check the subject attached to each regional source.
xs: **Ramacharitam — Sandhyakara Nandi — life of Ramapala** is correct — so option **(1)** is the answer.
Ramapala was a **Pala** king.
**Prithviraja Vijaya** is by **Jayanaka**, **Madhura Vijayam** by **Gangadevi**, **Siddhesvara Charitam** by **Kase Siddhappa**.
**Kalhana** wrote **Rajatarangini**, the history of Kashmir.
xa: Rajatarangini: **12th c.**, in **8 tarangas (books)**.
⚠ **Prithviraj Raso** = **Chand Bardai**; **Prithviraja Vijaya** = **Jayanaka**.

104.s: Madhura Vijayam provides information chiefly about which of the following?
o: Kampana’s conquest of Madurai and conditions under Tughlaq rule
The conquest of Golconda by Aurangzeb
The life of Pala king Ramapala
104.x: Madhura Vijayam, written by Gangadevi, describes Kampana’s conquest of Madurai and conditions under Tughlaq rule.
104.tq: Associate the regional biography with its protagonist, campaign and political context.
xs: **Madhura Vijayam** describes **Kampana's conquest of Madurai and conditions under Tughlaq rule** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was written by **Gangadevi**.
Golconda's conquest is in **Muntakhab-ul-Lubab**; Ramapala in **Ramacharitam**; Kashmir in **Rajatarangini**.
xa: **Kumara Ramana Charitam** (Kannada) covers **South India after the fall of Warangal**.
**Siddhesvara Charitam** (Telugu, **Kase Siddhappa**) covers **Kakatiya-era society and religion**.

104.s: Siddhesvara Charitam, written in Telugu by Kase Siddhappa, is a source for the study of which subject?
104.x: Siddhesvara Charitam is a Telugu work by Kase Siddhappa that provides information on Kakatiya-era society and religion.
104.tq: Match the language and author with the regional historical theme.
xs: **Siddhesvara Charitam** is a source for **Kakatiya-era society and religion** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is a **Telugu** work by **Kase Siddhappa**.
Kingship theory is **Barani's Fatawa-i-Jahandari**; Akbar's reign is in **Tabaqat-i-Akbari**.
xa: **Marco Polo** visited Kakatiya **Rudramadevi** (**1289-93**), landing at **Motupalli**.
**Kumara Ramana Charitam** (Kannada) deals with **South India after the fall of Warangal**.

104.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Tarikh-i-Firishta — Muhammad Qasim Firishta — Deccan history
Hadikat-us-Salatin — Ali bin Tahir Bustani — Qutb Shahis
Kumara Ramana Charitam — Kannada — South India after the fall of Warangal
104.x: Muntakhab-ul-Lubab was written by Khafi Khan and deals with Aurangzeb’s conquest of Golconda. Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam.
104.tq: Detect the swapped author in a list of regional and Deccan sources.
xs: **Muntakhab-ul-Lubab — Gangadevi — conquest of Madurai** is wrong — so option **(3)** is the answer.
**Muntakhab-ul-Lubab** was written by **Khafi Khan** on **Aurangzeb's conquest of Golconda**.
**Gangadevi** wrote **Madhura Vijayam** on **Kampana's** conquest of Madurai.
The other three are correct: **Firishta** on the **Deccan**, **Bustani** on the **Qutb Shahis**, **Kumara Ramana Charitam** (Kannada) on post-Warangal South India.
xa: Other Qutb Shahi sources: **Tarikh Muhammad Qutb Shah** (anonymous, **1617**), **Basatin-us-Salatin** (**Mirza Ibrahim Zuberi**).
Modern work: **H.K. Sherwani's** History of the Qutb Shahi Dynasty.

104.s:
Consider the following statements about Muhammad Qasim Firishta and his work:
1. His Tarikh-i-Firishta is also known as Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi.
2. He dedicated his work to Ibrahim Qutb Shah of Golconda.
3. He was born at Astarabad in Iran in 1552.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
104.x: Statement 1 is correct: Tarikh-i-Firishta is also called Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi. Statement 2 is wrong: it was dedicated to Ibrahim Adil Shah of Bijapur, not a Qutb Shahi ruler. Statement 3 is correct: Firishta was born at Astarabad, Iran, in 1552. So '1 and 3 only' is right; options with 2 are wrong and '1 and 2 only' omits a true statement.
104.tq: Gulshan-i-IBRAHIMI = Ibrahim ADIL Shah of Bijapur; don't fall for the Qutb Shahi swap.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 3 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: **Tarikh-i-Firishta** is also called **Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi**.
2 is wrong: it was dedicated to **Ibrahim Adil Shah of Bijapur**, not a Qutb Shahi.
3 is correct: Firishta was born at **Astarabad, Iran, in 1552**.
xa: Firishta calls **Telangana "Tilang"**.
⚠ His story of **Deva Raya kidnapping Nehal** is rejected by modern historians.
AP angle: **Isami** and **Firishta** → **Warangal**.

104.s: Rajatarangini, a 12th-century history of Kashmir in eight tarangas, was written by:
104.x: Kalhana wrote Rajatarangini, the 12th-century history of Kashmir in 8 tarangas (books). Jayanaka wrote Prithviraja Vijaya, Sandhyakara Nandi Ramacharitam and Gangadevi Madhura Vijayam.
104.tq: Rajatarangini = Kalhana, Kashmir
xs: **Rajatarangini** was written by **Kalhana** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is a **12th c.** history of **Kashmir** in **8 tarangas (books)**.
**Jayanaka** wrote **Prithviraja Vijaya**, **Sandhyakara Nandi** wrote **Ramacharitam**, **Gangadevi** wrote **Madhura Vijayam**.
xa: **Chachnama** (Persian) was written by **Muhammad Ali bin Abu Bakr Kufi**.
**Ramacharitam** is the life of the **Pala** king **Ramapala**.

104.s: Al-Biruni came to India in approximately which year and century?
o: Around 1030 CE in the eleventh century
Around 1450 CE in the fifteenth century
Around 1300 CE in the fourteenth century
Around 1150 CE in the twelfth century
104.x: Al-Biruni came to India around 1030 CE, during the eleventh century, under Mahmud of Ghazni.
104.tq: Distinguish the century and approximate date using the middle-period historical sequence.
xs: Al-Biruni came **around 1030 CE in the eleventh century** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He came with **Mahmud of Ghazni**, under whose patronage he wrote **Kitab-ul-Hind**.
xa: He was from **Khwarazm, Central Asia** (present **Uzbekistan**).
⚠ Later travellers: **Marco Polo** (**1289-93**), **Ibn Battuta** (born **1304**), **Abdur Razzaq** (**1443-44**).

104.s: Which one of the following statements about Al-Biruni is correct?
o: He confined his study of India exclusively to military campaigns.
He wrote in Persian without learning any Indian language.
He was patronised by Deva Raya II of Vijayanagara.
He wrote in Arabic after learning Sanskrit and studied Indian religion, philosophy, astronomy and caste.
104.x: Al-Biruni learned Sanskrit and wrote in Arabic on Indian religion, philosophy, astronomy and the caste system. He was associated with Mahmud of Ghazni, not Vijayanagara.
104.tq: Use the language, subjects and patron together to identify the correct biographical statement.
xs: Al-Biruni **wrote in Arabic after learning Sanskrit** and studied **religion, philosophy, astronomy and caste** — so option **(4)** is correct.
His work is **Kitab-ul-Hind / Tahqiq-i-Hind** on **Indian sciences and society**, not just military campaigns.
His patron was **Mahmud of Ghazni**; **Deva Raya II** received **Abdur Razzaq**.
xa: He records **Diwali** on **Kartika Amavasya**.
He found Indians **unwilling to share learning with outsiders**.

104.s: According to Al-Biruni’s account, which of the following was observed on Kartika Amavasya?
o: The conquest of Madurai by Kampana
The coronation of Muhammad bin Tughlaq
The annual court of the Qutb Shahis
104.x: Al-Biruni recorded the celebration of Diwali on Kartika Amavasya.
104.tq: Match the festival and its calendrical occasion with the appropriate chronicler.
xs: Al-Biruni records **the celebration of Diwali** on **Kartika Amavasya** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Kampana's** Madurai conquest is in **Gangadevi's Madhura Vijayam**, not Al-Biruni.
xa: Vision PT365 cites **Al-Biruni**, **Nicolo Conti** and **Ain-i-Akbari** as early evidence of Diwali (UNESCO topic, **Apr 2026**).
**Nicolo Conti** described **"innumerable oil lamps"** at Diwali in Vijayanagara.

104.s: Which one of the following was Al-Biruni’s observation about Indian society?
o: Indians had abandoned Sanskrit learning entirely.
Indian society was free from caste distinctions.
Indians were unwilling to share learning with outsiders.
Indian scholars refused to study astronomy.
104.x: Al-Biruni observed that Indians were unwilling to share their learning with outsiders. He nevertheless studied Indian religion, philosophy, astronomy and caste through Sanskrit sources.
104.tq: Identify the precise social observation without reversing its meaning.
xs: Al-Biruni found **Indians unwilling to share learning with outsiders** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He himself **learned Sanskrit** and wrote on **caste**, **astronomy**, religion and philosophy — so the other options contradict his account.
xa: His work: **Kitab-ul-Hind / Tahqiq-i-Hind**, in **Arabic**, c. **1030** CE.
He came from **Khwarazm** with **Mahmud of Ghazni**.

104.s: Al-Biruni, who came to India with Mahmud of Ghazni, was a native of:
104.x: Al-Biruni came from Khwarazm in Central Asia, in present Uzbekistan. Tangiers was Ibn Battuta's birthplace, Balkh was Mahmud Wali Balkhi's home, and Astarabad was Firishta's birthplace.
104.tq: Al-Biruni = Khwarazm (Uzbekistan)
xs: Al-Biruni was from **Khwarazm in Central Asia (present Uzbekistan)** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Tangiers (Morocco)** was **Ibn Battuta's** birthplace; **Balkh** was **Mahmud Wali Balkhi's** home; **Astarabad** was **Firishta's**.
xa: He came with **Mahmud of Ghazni** in the **11th century**.
Mahmud's other protégés: **Firdausi** and **Utbi**.

104.s: Rihla, the travel account of Ibn Battuta, was written in which language?
104.x: Ibn Battuta’s travel account, Rihla, was written in Arabic.
104.tq: Test the exact language of a source rather than its author’s place of origin.
xs: **Rihla** was written in **Arabic** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Ibn Battuta** was from **Morocco**, born at **Tangiers** in **1304**.
xa: He served **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**, who made him **qazi of Delhi** and sent him as **envoy to China**.
Rihla describes **espionage**, the **postal system**, **sati** and **slave markets**.
⚠ **Al-Biruni's Kitab-ul-Hind** is also in Arabic.

104.s: Marco Polo, who landed at Motupalli, visited the kingdom of which ruler?
104.x: Marco Polo visited the Kakatiya kingdom during the reign of Rudramadevi in 1289–93 and landed at Motupalli.
104.tq: Link the traveller’s landing place with the ruler and kingdom visited.
xs: Marco Polo visited the kingdom of **Rudramadevi of the Kakatiyas** (**1289-93**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
He landed at **Motupalli**.
**Abdullah Qutb Shah** received **Tavernier**; **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**, **Ibn Battuta**; **Deva Raya II**, **Abdur Razzaq**.
xa: He described the **diamond trade**, **no oppressive taxes on merchants**, and praised the **Kakatiya army**.
His is the **first foreign reference to a female ruler** in India.
⚠ Two Venetians: **Marco Polo** → Kakatiyas; **Nicolo Conti** → Vijayanagara.

104.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ibn Battuta — Morocco — Muhammad bin Tughlaq
Abdur Razzaq — Portugal — Deva Raya II
104.x: Ibn Battuta was from Morocco and visited the court of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. Marco Polo was from Venice, Abdur Razzaq from Persia and Duarte Barbosa from Portugal.
104.tq: Begin with the country–traveller pair and verify the ruler visited.
xs: **Ibn Battuta — Morocco — Muhammad bin Tughlaq** is correct — so option **(1)** is the answer.
**Marco Polo** was from **Venice (Italy)**, not France — **Tavernier** was French.
**Abdur Razzaq** was from **Persia**, a Timurid envoy of **Shah Rukh**.
xa: Other traveller-country pairs: **Afanasy Nikitin** — **Russia**; **Seydi Ali Reis** — **Turkey**; **Mahmud Wali Balkhi** — **Balkh (Afghanistan)**.
Ibn Battuta was made **qazi of Delhi** and sent as **envoy to China**.

104.s: Which traveller is associated with observations on espionage, the postal system, sati and slave markets in the Delhi Sultanate?
104.x: Ibn Battuta’s account of Muhammad bin Tughlaq’s reign contains observations on espionage, the postal system, sati and slave markets.
104.tq: Match the distinctive subject described with the traveller who recorded it.
xs: **Ibn Battuta**, in his **Rihla**, describes **espionage**, the **postal system**, **sati** and **slave markets** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He served **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** as **qazi of Delhi**.
**Tavernier** wrote on **Golconda diamonds**; **Nicolo Conti** on **Diwali lamps** in Vijayanagara.
xa: Rihla is in **Arabic**; Ibn Battuta was born at **Tangiers** in **1304**.
⚠ "Who mentioned sati" at Vijayanagara = **Abdur Razzaq**.

104.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Nicolo Conti was a traveller from Venice.
2. He described innumerable oil lamps at Diwali in Vijayanagara.
3. The APPSC-associated account places him at the court of Deva Raya II.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
104.x: All three statements are correct. Nicolo Conti was a Venetian who described the innumerable oil lamps at Diwali in Vijayanagara. Some sources place him at the end of Deva Raya I's reign, but the APPSC 2011 key placed this Italian traveller in Deva Raya II's reign.
104.tq: Combine origin, court and distinctive observation to identify one traveller precisely.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
1: **Nicolo Conti** was from **Venice (Italy)**.
2: he described **"innumerable oil lamps"** at **Diwali** in Vijayanagara.
3: the **APPSC 2011** key places this Italian traveller in **Deva Raya II's** reign.
xa: ⚠ Notes place Conti at the end of **Deva Raya I's** reign — follow the key's version in APPSC.
⚠ Two Venetians: **Marco Polo** → Kakatiyas; **Nicolo Conti** → Vijayanagara.

104.s: Abdur Razzaq visited Vijayanagara in 1443–44 as an envoy sent by which ruler?
104.x: Abdur Razzaq was a Persian envoy of Shah Rukh and visited the court of Deva Raya II in 1443–44.
104.tq: Distinguish the envoy’s sending ruler from the ruler whose court he visited.
xs: **Abdur Razzaq** was the Timurid envoy of **Shah Rukh of Persia** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He visited **Deva Raya II** at Vijayanagara in **1443-44**.
**Ibrahim Adil Shah** was **Firishta's** patron; **Muhammad Qutb Shah** received **Mir Zainul Abidin** (**1614**).
xa: He called Vijayanagara among the **largest, richest cities**, with **diamonds sold in heaps**.
He mentions **sati** and **"300 ports"**.

104.s: Robert Sewell’s A Forgotten Empire is based principally on the accounts of which group?
o: Barbosa, Seydi Ali Reis and Mahmud Wali Balkhi
Marco Polo, Ibn Battuta and Tavernier
104.x: Robert Sewell’s A Forgotten Empire draws chiefly on the accounts of Paes, Nuniz and Abdur Razzaq.
104.tq: Recognise the specific cluster of sources associated with a modern historical reconstruction.
xs: Sewell's **A Forgotten Empire** is built on the accounts of **Paes, Nuniz and Abdur Razzaq** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is a history of **Vijayanagara**, which all three described.
xa: **Abdur Razzaq** visited **Deva Raya II** in **1443-44**.
AP angle: **Abdur Razzaq** and **Barbosa** → **Vijayanagara**; **Tavernier** → **Golconda**.

104.s: Which one of the following foreign travellers described diamonds being sold in heaps at Vijayanagara?
104.x: Abdur Razzaq described the sale of diamonds in heaps during his visit to Vijayanagara under Deva Raya II.
104.tq: Identify the traveller from a distinctive observation recorded in the travel account.
xs: **Abdur Razzaq** described **diamonds sold in heaps** at Vijayanagara — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Marco Polo** described the Kakatiya **diamond trade**; **Afanasy Nikitin** was a **horse merchant**.
xa: Abdur Razzaq ranked Vijayanagara among the **largest, richest cities** and mentions **sati**.
**Tavernier** wrote on **Golconda diamonds** under **Abdullah Qutb Shah**.

104.s: Afanasy Nikitin, a horse merchant who visited India during the reign of Virupaksha Raya II, belonged to which country?
104.x: Afanasy Nikitin was a Russian traveller from Tver, situated on the Volga. He visited Vijayanagara during the reign of Virupaksha Raya II.
104.tq: Test the traveller’s nationality through the associated ruler and occupation.
xs: **Afanasy Nikitin** was from **Russia** (**Tver**, on the **Volga**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
He was a **horse merchant** at Vijayanagara under **Virupaksha Raya II**.
**Persia** = Abdur Razzaq, **Afghanistan (Balkh)** = Mahmud Wali Balkhi, **Turkey** = Seydi Ali Reis.
xa: **Nicolo Conti** and **Marco Polo** were both from **Venice**.
**Tavernier** was from **France**.

104.s: Which one of the following statements about Mahmud Wali Balkhi is correct?
o: He was a Moroccan qazi at Muhammad bin Tughlaq’s court.
He was a Persian envoy to Vijayanagara in 1443.
He belonged to Balkh and lived for some time as a kind of sanyasi.
He was a Venetian visitor to the Kakatiya kingdom.
104.x: Mahmud Wali Balkhi belonged to Balkh in Afghanistan and travelled in the 1620s. He is noted for having lived as a kind of sanyasi for some time.
104.tq: Find the statement that combines the correct origin with the distinctive biographical detail.
xs: **Mahmud Wali Balkhi** was from **Balkh** and **lived for some time as a kind of sanyasi** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He was a **17th-century** visitor who travelled in the **1620s**.
The Moroccan qazi was **Ibn Battuta**; the Persian envoy (**1443**) was **Abdur Razzaq**; the Venetian was **Marco Polo**.
xa: **Balkh** is in **Afghanistan**.
**Seydi Ali Reis** was an Ottoman admiral from **Turkey**.

104.s: Which foreign traveller is associated with the mention of '300 ports'?
104.x: Abdur Razzaq, the Timurid envoy to Deva Raya II's Vijayanagara, is credited with mentioning '300 ports'. ⚠ The APPSC key said Barbosa, so recognise that answer if it appears in an APPSC paper. Nikitin was a Russian horse merchant, and Tavernier described the diamonds of Golconda.
104.tq: 300 ports = Barbosa; sati = Abdur Razzaq
xs: **Abdur Razzaq** is credited with mentioning **"300 ports"** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ The **APPSC key** said **Barbosa** — know both answers.
**Afanasy Nikitin** was a Russian horse merchant; **Tavernier** wrote on **Golconda** diamonds.
xa: Abdur Razzaq also mentions **sati** and describes **diamonds sold in heaps**.
He visited **Deva Raya II** in **1443-44** as **Shah Rukh's** envoy.

104.s: The Nizami Mosque inscription at Golconda is significant because it dates Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk's independence to:
104.x: The Nizami Mosque inscription at Golconda dates the independence of Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk to 1518.
104.tq: Test the precise date attached to a political event in an inscription.
xs: The **Nizami Mosque** inscription at Golconda dates **Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk's** independence to **1518** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**1576** is the **Ghazinagar** inscription (Nalgonda, **Ibrahim Quli**, **1576-77**); **1595** is the **Daru-Shifa** inscription.
xa: **Badshahi Ashurkhana** inscription: **1592-96**.
These Qutb Shahi inscriptions are in **Persian**.

104.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Vilasa copper plate — Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka
Palam Baoli inscription — Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka
104.x: The Palam Baoli inscription is a Sanskrit record praising Balban and dates to 1276. The Vilasa copper plate is associated with Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka.
104.tq: Find the wrongly assigned person by checking the inscription–issuer relationship.
xs: **Palam Baoli inscription — Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka** is wrong — so option **(4)** is the answer.
The **Palam Baoli** inscription (**1276**) is bilingual and praises **Balban** in **Sanskrit**.
**Vilasa copper plate** — **Prolaya Nayaka** (c. **1330**); **Kaluvacheru** — **Anitalli**; **Warangal** — **Shitab Khan** (**1504-06**).
xa: The Telugu sources **Vilasa**, **Kaluvacheru** and **Pratapa Charitra** count **8** Warangal invasions.
Muslim sources count **5**.

104.s: Mahmud of Ghazni's Lahore dirhams are especially significant as medieval sources because they contain:
o: An Arabic legend and its Sanskrit translation in Sharada script
A Telugu inscription and an Arabic translation
A Sanskrit legend and its Persian translation in Devanagari script
Only a Persian inscription in Nastaliq script
104.x: The Lahore dirhams of Mahmud of Ghazni carry an Arabic legend along with a Sanskrit translation written in Sharada script.
104.tq: Use the script–language combination to distinguish bilingual numismatic evidence.
xs: Mahmud's **Lahore dirhams** carry **an Arabic legend and its Sanskrit translation in Sharada script** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ Mahmud's coins = Arabic + **Sanskrit**; **Iltutmish's** coins = purely **Arabic**.
xa: Iltutmish issued the silver **tanka** and copper **jital**.
The **Palam Baoli** inscription (**1276**) is another bilingual record, praising **Balban** in Sanskrit.

104.s: The Palam Baoli inscription of 1276 praises which ruler in Sanskrit?
104.x: The Palam Baoli inscription, dated 1276, praises Balban in Sanskrit.
104.tq: Link the inscription's date with the ruler praised in it.
xs: The **Palam Baoli** inscription of **1276** praises **Balban** in Sanskrit — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is a **bilingual** record.
**Mahmud of Ghazni** is linked with bilingual **Lahore dirhams**; **Iltutmish's** coins are purely **Arabic**.
xa: ⚠ Iltutmish: silver **tanka** and copper **jital**.
**Barani's Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi** covers **Balban** to early Firoz Tughlaq.

104.s: The transition from trabeate to arcuate construction in Sultanate architecture is marked by the increasing use of:
o: Wooden pillars and flat roofs only
Timber frames and corbelled balconies only
True arches, domes and lime mortar
104.x: Sultanate buildings demonstrate the shift from trabeate construction to arcuate construction through the use of true arches, domes and lime mortar.
104.tq: Identify the architectural system from its characteristic structural elements.
xs: The **trabeate → arcuate** shift used **true arches, domes and lime mortar** — so option **(3)** is correct.
That change marks Sultanate buildings.
xa: **Naskh** script was used for Quranic verses, e.g. the **Jami Masjid mihrab**.
**Nastaliq** was used for **Persian** texts.

104.s:
With reference to Qutb Shahi calligraphy, consider the following statements:
1. Naskh was used for Quranic verses, including those in the Jami Masjid mihrab.
2. Nastaliq was used for Persian texts.
3. Naskh and Nastaliq were forms of architectural construction.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
104.x: Naskh was used for Quranic verses, while Nastaliq was used for Persian texts. They are calligraphic scripts, not forms of architectural construction.
104.tq: Separate the two related scripts from the unrelated architectural term.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: **Naskh** was used for **Quranic verses** (e.g. **Jami Masjid mihrab**).
2 is correct: **Nastaliq** was used for **Persian texts**.
3 is wrong: both are **calligraphy** styles, not building methods.
xa: Architecture shifted from **trabeate** to **arcuate** (true arch, dome, lime mortar).
The **Golconda school** of painting was founded by **Mir Hashimi**.

104.s: Who founded the Golconda school of painting?
104.x: The Golconda school of painting was founded by Mir Hashimi.
104.tq: Test the founder of an artistic tradition against prominent literary figures.
xs: The Golconda school of painting was founded by **Mir Hashimi** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Amir Khusrau** was a court poet; **Abul Fazl** wrote the official history of **Akbar**.
xa: The **"Quliyat Quli"** manuscript has **14** miniatures.
Qutb Shahi calligraphy: **Naskh** (Quranic), **Nastaliq** (Persian).

104.s: Which of the following statements correctly reflects the nature of court histories in medieval India?
o: They avoided all religious and political viewpoints.
They were entirely independent of royal patronage.
They were written exclusively by foreign travellers.
They generally glorified the ruler who patronised the writer.
104.x: Court histories were influenced by royal patronage and generally glorified the patron ruler. Their authors could also reflect particular religious or political viewpoints.
104.tq: Apply the source-criticism principle of patronage bias.
xs: Court histories **generally glorified the ruler who patronised the writer** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Abul Fazl** wrote the official history of **Akbar**; **Amir Khusrau** was a court poet.
**Barani** wrote from an **orthodox Sunni** viewpoint — so they were not free of views.
xa: Foreign accounts **supplement** Indian texts and must be **cross-verified** with inscriptions and archaeology.
Sources also **disagree** — e.g. on the number of **Warangal invasions** (**8** vs **5**).

104.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Ziauddin Barani?
o: He wrote from an orthodox Sunni viewpoint and theorised kingship.
He was a Persian ambassador to Vijayanagara and described its markets.
He founded the Golconda school of painting.
He composed the royal memoirs of Jahangir.
104.x: Ziauddin Barani wrote from an orthodox Sunni viewpoint and also theorised about kingship. The other descriptions belong to different figures or traditions.
104.tq: Use the writer's viewpoint and intellectual contribution to identify him.
xs: Barani **wrote from an orthodox Sunni viewpoint and theorised kingship** — so option **(1)** is correct.
His kingship theory is in **Fatawa-i-Jahandari**.
The Persian envoy to Vijayanagara was **Abdur Razzaq**; the Golconda school was founded by **Mir Hashimi**.
xa: Barani's **Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi** covers **Balban** to early **Firoz Tughlaq**.
It is the main account of **Alauddin's market regulations** and Sultanate attacks on **south Indian kingdoms**.

104.s: Telugu sources and Muslim sources differ in their accounts of the number of invasions of Warangal. Which statement is correct?
o: Telugu sources record 5 invasions, while Muslim sources record 8.
Telugu sources record 8 invasions, while Muslim sources record 5.
Both groups of sources record 8 invasions.
Both groups of sources record 5 invasions.
104.x: The Telugu sources Pratapa Charitra, Vilasa and Kaluvacheru record eight invasions of Warangal, whereas Muslim sources associated with Amir Khusrau and Wassaf record five.
104.tq: Compare conflicting numerical claims by source tradition.
xs: **Telugu sources record 8 invasions, while Muslim sources record 5** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Telugu: **Pratapa Charitra**, **Vilasa**, **Kaluvacheru** — **8**.
Muslim: **Amir Khusrau**, **Wassaf** — **5**.
xa: Amir Khusrau went with **Malik Kafur's 1310** invasion of Warangal.
**Isami's Futuh-us-Salatin** covers the **Tughlaq campaigns against Warangal**.

104.s: Which of the following statements regarding Firishta's account of Deva Raya is correct?
o: His story that Deva Raya kidnapped Nehal has been rejected by modern historians.
Modern historians regard Firishta as the author of the Ain-i-Akbari.
His story that Deva Raya kidnapped Nehal is accepted without reservation by modern historians.
Firishta did not write about Deva Raya.
104.x: Firishta's story that Deva Raya kidnapped Nehal is rejected by modern historians. This illustrates the need to critically evaluate chronicle narratives.
104.tq: Identify the historically qualified statement rather than accepting a dramatic anecdote.
xs: Firishta's story that **Deva Raya kidnapped Nehal** has been **rejected by modern historians** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It shows that chronicle stories must be checked, not accepted wholesale.
Firishta wrote **Tarikh-i-Firishta**, not the **Ain-i-Akbari**.
xa: Tarikh-i-Firishta (**Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi**) was dedicated to **Ibrahim Adil Shah** of Bijapur.
Firishta was born at **Astarabad, Iran, 1552**; he calls Telangana **"Tilang"**.

104.s: Foreign travellers' accounts of medieval India should generally be used by historians in which manner?
o: They should replace inscriptions and archaeological evidence.
They should be ignored because they were written outside India.
They should be accepted as accurate in every detail.
They should supplement Indian texts and be cross-verified with inscriptions and archaeology.
104.x: Foreign accounts supplement Indian textual evidence, but their statements must be cross-verified with inscriptions and archaeological evidence.
104.tq: Apply the principle of corroboration across different source types.
xs: Foreign accounts **supplement Indian texts** and must be **cross-verified with inscriptions and archaeology** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They neither replace other evidence nor are accurate in every detail; nor are they to be ignored.
xa: ⚠ Court histories have their own bias — they **glorify the patron**.
**Taj Mahal** case (**Jul 2026**): evidence that **Shah Jahan** built it includes **European travellers' accounts**.

104.s: Which of the following combinations correctly associates an AP-linked source with the place or polity described?
o: Marco Polo — Motupalli; Abdur Razzaq — Vijayanagara; Tavernier — Golconda
Marco Polo — Golconda; Abdur Razzaq — Warangal; Tavernier — Motupalli
Barbosa — Motupalli; Isami — Vijayanagara; Firishta — Golconda
Tavernier — Vijayanagara; Marco Polo — Warangal; Barbosa — Golconda
104.x: Marco Polo is associated with Motupalli, Abdur Razzaq and Barbosa with Vijayanagara, and Tavernier with Golconda. Isami and Firishta are associated with Warangal.
104.tq: Start with the sure place–traveller pair and complete the matching set.
xs: **Marco Polo — Motupalli; Abdur Razzaq — Vijayanagara; Tavernier — Golconda** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Isami** and **Firishta** are the sources asked for **Warangal**; **Barbosa** goes with **Vijayanagara**, not Motupalli or Golconda.
The other options shuffle these places.
xa: Marco Polo landed at **Motupalli** and visited Kakatiya **Rudramadevi** (**1289-93**).
Tavernier wrote on **Golconda diamonds** under **Abdullah Qutb Shah**.
Abdur Razzaq visited **Deva Raya II** in **1443-44**.

104.s: Which of the following set of sources is cited as early evidence of Diwali in the context of its UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage discussion?
104.x: Al-Biruni, Nicolo Conti and the Ain-i-Akbari are cited as early evidence of Diwali in the referenced UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage discussion.
104.tq: Distinguish the exact evidence set from other medieval source combinations.
xs: **Al-Biruni, Nicolo Conti and Ain-i-Akbari** are cited as early evidence of Diwali — so option **(1)** is correct.
Vision PT365 cites them in the **UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage** topic (**Apr 2026**).
xa: Al-Biruni records **Diwali** on **Kartika Amavasya**.
Nicolo Conti described **"innumerable oil lamps"** at Diwali in **Vijayanagara**.
⚠ Two Venetians: **Marco Polo** → Kakatiyas; **Nicolo Conti** → Vijayanagara.

104.s: In the suit claiming that the Taj Mahal was a temple, the Allahabad High Court sought responses from which authorities?
o: The UNESCO and the World Bank
The Centre and the Archaeological Survey of India
The Centre and the Reserve Bank of India
The Election Commission and the Archaeological Survey of India
104.x: The Allahabad High Court sought responses from the Centre and the Archaeological Survey of India. The evidence that Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal rests on chronicles, records and European travellers' accounts.
104.tq: Identify the institutions involved by separating them from unrelated constitutional and international bodies.
xs: The **Allahabad HC** sought responses from **the Centre and the Archaeological Survey of India** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The suit claims the **Taj Mahal** was a temple (**Jul 2026**).
Evidence that **Shah Jahan** built it = **chronicles**, **records** and **European travellers' accounts**.
xa: Foreign accounts **supplement** Indian texts and must be **cross-verified** with inscriptions and archaeology.
⚠ Court histories **glorify the patron** — e.g. **Abul Fazl**, official history of **Akbar**.

105.s: Which of the following correctly represents the three names used for the dynasty founded by Qutbuddin Aibak?
105.x: The dynasty is known as the Slave or Mamluk dynasty; the ruling line is also associated with the Ilbari Turks.
105.tq: Discriminate among overlapping dynasty names and later ruling houses.
xs: The dynasty is called **Slave**, **Mamluk** and **Ilbari** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It had three lines: **Qutbi** (**1206-1211**, Aibak), **First Ilbari** (**1211-1266**, Iltutmish), **Second Ilbari** (**1266-1290**, Balban).
**Khalji**, **Tughlaq**, **Sayyid** and **Lodi** are later dynasties.
xa: **Mamluk** is Arabic for "owned" — a **military slave**, not a domestic one.
Iltutmish was an **Ilbari** Turk, slave and son-in-law of Aibak.
The dynasty ruled **1206-1290**.

105.s: The term ‘Mamluk’ literally refers to:
105.x: Mamluk is an Arabic term meaning ‘owned’. In this context it denotes a military slave, distinct from a domestic slave.
105.tq: Test the precise meaning of a technical historical term.
xs: **Mamluk** is Arabic for "owned" — **an owned military slave** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It means a **military** slave as opposed to a **domestic** slave.
xa: The **Slave / Mamluk** dynasty ruled **1206-1290**.
Aibak was a slave of **Muhammad Ghori** (APPSC G1 **2004**).
Balban was captured by the Mongols and **bought by Iltutmish**.

105.s: Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the major Delhi Sultanate dynasties?
105.x: The sequence was Mamluk (1206–1290), Khalji (1290–1320), Tughlaq (1320–1414), Sayyid (1414–1451) and Lodi (1451–1526).
105.tq: Use the dynasty transition sequence to eliminate reversals.
xs: The order is **Mamluk, Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, Lodi** — so option **(1)** is correct.
xa: **Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji** crowned himself at **Kilokhari** in **1290**, ending Mamluk rule.
The Mamluks were the **first Muslim dynasty** to rule north India from Delhi.

105.s: Which of the following does NOT belong to the Mamluk dynasty?
105.x: Jalaluddin Khalji belonged to the Khalji dynasty. Alauddin Masud, Nasiruddin Mahmud and Ruknuddin Firuz were rulers of the Mamluk dynasty.
105.tq: Identify the outsider from a list of rulers belonging to one dynasty.
xs: **Jalaluddin Khalji** was not a Mamluk — so option **(4)** is the answer.
He founded the **Khalji** dynasty at **Kilokhari** in **1290**.
**Ruknuddin Firuz** (**1236**), **Alauddin Masud** (**1242-46**) and **Nasiruddin Mahmud** (**1246-66**) were Mamluks.
xa: ⚠ Odd one out: **Jalaluddin Khalji** and the **Tughlaqs** are NOT Mamluks.
The last Mamluks after Balban: grandson **Kaiqubad**, then infant **Kaimurs**.

105.s: Arrange the following Mamluk rulers in chronological order: 1. Razia  2. Balban  3. Iltutmish  4. Nasiruddin Mahmud
105.x: Iltutmish (1210-36) was followed, after Ruknuddin Firuz, by Razia (1236-40); after Bahram Shah and Alauddin Masud came Nasiruddin Mahmud (1246-66) and then Balban (1266-86). The other orders misplace Razia, Nasiruddin or Balban.
105.tq: Iltutmish - Razia - Nasiruddin - Balban
xs: The order is **3, 1, 4, 2** — Iltutmish, Razia, Nasiruddin Mahmud, Balban — so option **(1)** is correct.
→ **Nasiruddin Mahmud (1246-66)** → **Balban (1266-86)**.
xa: Between them: **Ruknuddin Firuz** (**1236**), **Bahram Shah** (**1240-42**), **Alauddin Masud** (**1242-46**).
Before Iltutmish: **Aibak**, then **Aram Shah**.

105.s:
Consider the following statements about Qutbuddin Aibak:
1. He was born in Turkestan and was first sold to the Qazi of Nishapur.
2. His title 'Lakh Bakhsh' means 'shadow of God'.
3. He died in 1210 after falling from his horse while playing chaugan (polo).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
105.x: Statement 1 is correct: Aibak was born in Turkestan and first sold to the Qazi of Nishapur. Statement 2 is wrong: Lakh Bakhsh means 'giver of lakhs'; 'shadow of God' (Zil-i-Ilahi) is Balban's idea of the Sultan. Statement 3 is correct: he died in 1210 in a chaugan accident. Hence '1 and 3 only'; any option including 2 is wrong, and '1 and 2 only' drops a true statement.
105.tq: Lakh Bakhsh = giver of lakhs (Aibak); Zil-i-Ilahi = shadow of God (Balban).
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 3 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: Aibak was born in **Turkestan** and first sold to the **Qazi of Nishapur**.
2 is wrong: **Lakh Bakhsh** means **"giver of lakhs"**; **Zil-i-Ilahi** ("shadow of God") is **Balban's** theory.
3 is correct: he died in **1210** falling from his horse playing **chaugan** (polo).
xa: He was then a slave of **Muhammad Ghori** and rose to **Amir-i-Akhur** (Master of Stables).
His son **Aram Shah** ruled only about **8** months.

105.s: Before becoming a general, Qutbuddin Aibak held the office of:
105.x: Aibak rose to the position of Amir-i-Akhur, or Master of Stables, and subsequently became a general.
105.tq: Test an earlier post through an official Persian title.
xs: Aibak rose to **Amir-i-Akhur** (**Master of Stables**) before becoming a general — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Diwan-i-Arz** is the military department later created by **Balban**, not an office of Aibak.
xa: After **Tarain II (1192)** Aibak was **Ghori's** representative in India.
He became Sultan on Ghori's death and ruled **1206-1210** from **Lahore**.

105.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
105.x: The Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque was built at Delhi. Arhai-din-ka-Jhonpra is at Ajmer, while Sultan Ghari was built by Iltutmish.
105.tq: Start from the sure location and reject swapped monument-place pairs.
xs: **Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque — Delhi** is correct — so option **(3)** is the answer.
**Arhai-din-ka-Jhonpra** is at **Ajmer**, not Delhi; Quwwat-ul-Islam is not at Ajmer.
**Sultan Ghari** tomb was built by **Iltutmish**, not at Lahore.
xa: Quwwat-ul-Islam = the **first mosque in India**, built with **reused temple pillars**.
Both Quwwat-ul-Islam and Arhai-din-ka-Jhonpra were built by **Aibak**.

105.s: Which statement about the monuments associated with Qutbuddin Aibak is NOT correct?
o: The Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque was built using reused temple pillars.
Aibak completed the Qutb Minar during his own reign.
The Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque is regarded as the first mosque in India.
Aibak began the construction of the Qutb Minar.
105.x: Aibak began the Qutb Minar, but it was completed by Iltutmish. The Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque used reused temple pillars and is regarded as the first mosque in India.
105.tq: Find the wrong completion claim in a sequence of monument-related facts.
xs: "**Aibak completed the Qutb Minar**" is wrong — so option **(2)** is the answer.
Aibak **began** the Qutb Minar; **Iltutmish completed** it.
Quwwat-ul-Islam used **reused temple pillars** and is the **first mosque in India** — both true.
xa: The Qutb Minar is dedicated to **Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki**.
The **Qutb complex** is now a **UNESCO** site.

105.s: The Qutb Minar was dedicated to:
105.x: Qutbuddin Aibak began the Qutb Minar and dedicated it to Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki.
105.tq: Separate the dedicatee of a monument from other well-known Sufi figures.
xs: The Qutb Minar is dedicated to **Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki** — so option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ It is named after the saint **Bakhtiyar Kaki**, not after Aibak.
xa: It was **begun by Aibak** and **completed by Iltutmish**.
Iltutmish's **Sultan Ghari** tomb made him the **"Father of tomb building"**.

105.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Qutbuddin Aibak became Sultan
B. Second Battle of Tarain
C. Death of Muhammad Ghori
D. Death of Qutbuddin Aibak
105.x: The Second Battle of Tarain occurred in 1192, followed by Ghori's death and Aibak's accession in 1206; Aibak died in 1210.
105.tq: Fix the first and last events, then place the two 1206 events correctly.
xs: The order is **B, C, A, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Tarain II (1192)** made Aibak **Ghori's** representative in India.
On **Ghori's death** Aibak became Sultan (**1206**); he died in **1210**.
xa: ⚠ **Tarain II (1192)** = Ghori's win; Tarain **1216** = Iltutmish defeats **Yildiz**.
Aibak died falling from his horse while playing **chaugan** (polo).

105.s: Qutbuddin Aibak, Sultan from 1206 to 1210, ruled from which capital?
105.x: Aibak's capital was Lahore; Iltutmish later moved the capital from Lahore to Delhi. Ajmer has his Arhai-din-ka-Jhonpra, and Badaun was a governorship held by Iltutmish.
105.tq: Aibak = Lahore; Iltutmish moved to Delhi
xs: Aibak ruled from **Lahore** — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ **Iltutmish** later moved the capital from **Lahore to Delhi**.
**Ajmer** has Aibak's **Arhai-din-ka-Jhonpra**; **Badaun** was a governorship held by Iltutmish.
xa: Aibak patronised **Hasan Nizami**.
His title **Lakh Bakhsh** means **"giver of lakhs"**.

105.s:
Consider the following statements about Iltutmish:
1. He was an Ilbari Turk and the slave and son-in-law of Qutbuddin Aibak.
2. He moved the capital from Delhi to Lahore.
3. Before becoming Sultan he was iqtadar of Gwalior and governor of Baran and Badaun.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
105.x: Statement 1 is correct: Iltutmish was an Ilbari Turk, Aibak's slave and son-in-law. Statement 2 is wrong: he moved the capital the other way, from Lahore (Aibak's capital) to Delhi. Statement 3 is correct: he was iqtadar of Gwalior, then governor of Baran and Badaun. So '1 and 3 only'.
105.tq: Aibak = Lahore; Iltutmish shifted to Delhi. Reversed direction is the trap.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 3 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: Iltutmish was an **Ilbari** Turk, **slave and son-in-law** of Aibak.
2 is wrong: he moved the capital from **Lahore to Delhi**, not the reverse.
3 is correct: he was **iqtadar of Gwalior**, then governor of **Baran** and **Badaun**.
xa: His title was **Shamsuddin**.
He received investiture (**"mansur"**) from the **Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad** in **1229**.

105.s: Iltutmish defeated Taj-ud-din Yildiz at Tarain in:
105.x: Iltutmish defeated Taj-ud-din Yildiz at Tarain in 1216. Nasiruddin Qubacha was another important rival of Iltutmish.
105.tq: Use a middle-value year option to distinguish related events in the early Sultanate.
xs: Iltutmish defeated **Taj-ud-din Yildiz** at Tarain in **1216** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1206** was Aibak's accession, **1210** Aibak's death, and **1229** the Caliph's investiture.
xa: His other rival was **Nasiruddin Qubacha**.
⚠ **Tarain II (1192)** was Ghori's victory — a different battle at the same place.

105.s:
Consider the following statements about the institutions of Iltutmish:
1. He received investiture (mansur) from the Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad in 1229.
2. Under the iqta system, officers (muqtis) were given revenue assignments instead of cash salaries.
3. The Turkan-i-Chahalgani was a body of Persian revenue clerks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
105.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Abbasid Caliph's mansur came in 1229. Statement 2 is correct: iqtas were revenue assignments to muqtis in place of cash pay. Statement 3 is wrong: the Turkan-i-Chahalgani (the Forty) was the Turkish military elite. So '1 and 2 only'.
105.tq: Chahalgani = Forty TURKISH nobles; mansur 1229; iqta = revenue assignment, not cash.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: investiture (**mansur**) from the **Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad** in **1229**.
2 is correct: **iqta** = revenue assignments to officers (**muqtis**) instead of cash salaries.
3 is wrong: **Turkan-i-Chahalgani** (the Forty / **Chalisa**) was the **Turkish military elite**.
xa: ⚠ Iltutmish **created** the Forty; **Balban broke** its power.
1229 is the **first Caliphal investiture** of a Delhi Sultan.

105.s: Which statement regarding Iltutmish and the Mongols is correct?
o: He sheltered Jalaluddin Mangbarni and invited Chengiz Khan to India.
He made Jalaluddin Mangbarni a member of the Forty.
He refused shelter to Jalaluddin Mangbarni, helping keep Chengiz Khan out of India.
He defeated Chengiz Khan at Tarain in 1216.
105.x: Iltutmish refused shelter to Jalaluddin Mangbarni of Khwarazm. This diplomatic decision helped prevent Chengiz Khan from entering India.
105.tq: Use the cause-and-effect relationship in a diplomatic episode.
xs: Iltutmish **refused shelter to Jalaluddin Mangbarni**, keeping **Chengiz Khan** out of India — so option **(3)** is correct.
Mangbarni was the prince of **Khwarazm**, fleeing the Mongols.
**1216** at Tarain was Iltutmish's victory over **Yildiz**, not Chengiz Khan.
xa: Balban later built **outposts and forts** against the **Mongols**.
Balban's son **Prince Muhammad** died fighting the Mongols (**1285**).

105.s: Which monument led to Iltutmish being called the ‘Father of tomb building’?
105.x: Iltutmish built the Sultan Ghari tomb and is consequently called the Father of tomb building. He also completed the Qutb Minar.
105.tq: Match an architectural work with the historical epithet associated with its builder.
xs: The **Sultan Ghari tomb** made Iltutmish the **"Father of tomb building"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Arhai-din-ka-Jhonpra** at Ajmer was built by **Aibak** and is not a tomb.
xa: Iltutmish **completed** the **Qutb Minar** begun by Aibak.
Aibak's **Quwwat-ul-Islam** mosque, Delhi, is the **first mosque in India**.

105.s: Razia Sultan ruled the Delhi Sultanate during which period?
105.x: Razia ruled from 1236 to 1240. She was the first and only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.
105.tq: Distinguish closely spaced reign periods of early Sultanate rulers.
xs: Razia ruled **1236-1240** — so option **(2)** is correct.
She was the **first and only woman ruler** of the Delhi Sultanate.
**1246-1266** is **Nasiruddin Mahmud** and **1266-1286** is **Balban**.
xa: She discarded **purdah**, wore **male attire** and **led the army**.
She was overthrown in **1240** after **Altuniya's** revolt at **Bhatinda**.

105.s: Which of the following was a distinctive feature of Razia Sultan's rule?
o: She accepted the authority of Bahram Shah throughout her reign.
She maintained purdah and never appeared before the army.
She discarded purdah, wore male attire and led the army.
She ruled only through Balban as her regent.
105.x: Razia discarded purdah, wore male attire and personally led the army. Her conduct challenged the expectations of the Turkish nobles.
105.tq: Identify the correct application of a ruler's known social and military policy.
xs: Razia **discarded purdah, wore male attire and led the army** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Bahram Shah** was the noble's choice who replaced her; **Balban** was **naib** to Nasiruddin Mahmud, not her regent.
xa: Razia made Balban **Amir-i-Shikar**.
Turkish nobles resented her favour to **Yaqut** (Abyssinian).

105.s: The Turkish nobles opposed Razia primarily because she favoured:
105.x: The Turkish nobles resented Razia's favour towards Yaqut, an Abyssinian. Their opposition contributed to the revolt led by Altuniya.
105.tq: Use the person–identity association to resolve a confusable court-politics question.
xs: The nobles resented her favour to **Yaqut, an Abyssinian** — so option **(4)** is correct.
In **1240** **Altuniya**, governor of **Bhatinda (Sirhind)**, revolted; Yaqut was killed and Razia imprisoned.
**Minhaj-us-Siraj** and **Hasan Nizami** were chroniclers; **Yildiz** was Iltutmish's rival.
xa: The nobles then enthroned **Bahram Shah**.
Razia married Altuniya, marched on Delhi, and was **defeated and killed** (**1240**).

105.s:
Arrange the following events relating to Razia Sultan in chronological order:
A. Altuniya revolted at Bhatinda
B. Yaqut was killed and Razia was imprisoned
C. Razia married Altuniya
D. Razia was defeated and killed
105.x: Altuniya's revolt was followed by Yaqut's death and Razia's imprisonment; Razia then married Altuniya, marched towards Delhi, and was defeated and killed in 1240.
105.tq: Follow the causal sequence from revolt to imprisonment, alliance and final defeat.
xs: The order is **A, B, C, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Altuniya** revolted at **Bhatinda** → **Yaqut killed**, Razia **imprisoned**.
Razia **married Altuniya** → marched on Delhi → **defeated and killed** (**1240**).
xa: Meanwhile the nobles enthroned **Bahram Shah** (**1240-42**).
Razia, **1236-1240**, was the first and only woman Sultan.

105.s: Balban was born as:
105.x: Balban was born around 1205 as Bahauddin. He was later known by the title Ulugh Khan.
105.tq: Distinguish a ruler's birth name from his title and regnal names.
xs: Balban was born c. **1205** as **Bahauddin** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Shamsuddin** was **Iltutmish's** title; **Ruknuddin** Firuz was Iltutmish's successor.
His title was **Ulugh Khan**, not "Ulughuddin".
xa: Captured by the **Mongols**, he was **bought by Iltutmish**.
He rose from **water-carrier** to the **Forty**; Razia made him **Amir-i-Shikar**.

105.s: Which sequence correctly describes Balban's early rise?
o: Slave of Iltutmish → water-carrier → member of the Forty → Amir-i-Shikar
Water-carrier → slave of Aibak → Amir-i-Akhur → member of the Forty
Member of the Forty → slave of Iltutmish → water-carrier → governor of Bhatinda
105.x: Balban was captured by the Mongols, bought by Iltutmish, rose from water-carrier to the Forty, and was made Amir-i-Shikar by Razia.
105.tq: Arrange biographical stages rather than merely recalling an isolated title.
xs: **Slave of Iltutmish → water-carrier → member of the Forty → Amir-i-Shikar** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Balban was captured by the **Mongols** and **bought by Iltutmish**.
**Razia** made him **Amir-i-Shikar**; title **Ulugh Khan**.
xa: **Amir-i-Akhur** (Master of Stables) was **Aibak's** post, not Balban's.
Under Nasiruddin Mahmud he became **principal minister (naib)** and leader of the Forty.

105.s: Which statement about Nasiruddin Mahmud is correct?
o: He ruled from 1236 to 1240 and opposed Razia.
He founded the Khalji dynasty in 1290.
He ruled from 1246 to 1266 and was regarded as pious but weak.
He ruled from 1266 to 1286 and introduced the blood-and-iron policy.
105.x: Nasiruddin Mahmud ruled from 1246 to 1266 and was considered a pious and weak Sultan. Balban served as his principal minister and naib.
105.tq: Distinguish a ruler's reign and character from those of his powerful minister.
xs: Nasiruddin Mahmud **ruled 1246-1266** and was **pious but weak** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1236-1240** was **Razia**; **1266-1286** and the **blood-and-iron** policy were **Balban**.
The **Khalji** dynasty was founded in **1290** by **Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji**.
xa: **Balban** was his **principal minister (naib)** and leader of the Forty.
**Minhaj-us-Siraj's Tabaqat-i-Nasiri** is named after him.

105.s: During the reign of Nasiruddin Mahmud, Balban served as:
105.x: Balban was Nasiruddin Mahmud's principal minister, or naib, and leader of the Forty. He was briefly displaced by Imaduddin Raihan before returning to power.
105.tq: Test the exact office held by a powerful minister during a weak ruler's reign.
xs: Balban was Nasiruddin Mahmud's **principal minister and naib** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was also **leader of the Forty**.
He was briefly displaced by **Imaduddin Raihan**, then returned.
xa: **Altuniya** was governor of **Bhatinda**; **Amir-i-Akhur** was **Aibak's** post.
Balban became Sultan in **1266**.

105.s: The work Tabaqat-i-Nasiri was named after:
105.x: Minhaj-us-Siraj's Tabaqat-i-Nasiri was named after Sultan Nasiruddin Mahmud.
105.tq: Match a historical work with the ruler after whom it was named.
xs: **Tabaqat-i-Nasiri** was named after Sultan **Nasiruddin Mahmud** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was written by **Minhaj-us-Siraj**.
xa: Nasiruddin Mahmud (**1246-66**) was pious and weak; **Balban** was his naib.
Aibak patronised **Hasan Nizami**.

105.s:
Consider the following statements about Balban's theory of kingship:
1. He regarded the Sultan as Zil-i-Ilahi (shadow of God).
2. He required sijda (prostration) and paibos (kissing the feet) at court.
3. He abolished the Persian festival of Nauroz at court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
105.x: Statement 1 is correct: Balban held the Sultan to be Zil-i-Ilahi. Statement 2 is correct: sijda and paibos were required. Statement 3 is wrong: Balban introduced the Persian Nauroz festival with strict court etiquette, he did not abolish it. So '1 and 2 only'; options with 3 are wrong and '1 only' is incomplete.
105.tq: Balban's court was Persian in style: Nauroz, sijda, paibos, Zil-i-Ilahi.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: Balban saw the Sultan as **Zil-i-Ilahi** (shadow of God).
2 is correct: **sijda** (prostration) and **paibos** (kissing the feet) were required.
3 is wrong: Balban **adopted** the Persian **Nauroz** festival with strict court etiquette.
xa: ⚠ **Sijda** = prostration; **paibos** = kissing the feet.
He created the military department **Diwan-i-Arz**.

105.s:
Consider the following statements about Balban's 'blood and iron' policy:
1. He ruthlessly suppressed the Mewatis and rebellious villages.
2. He strengthened the Forty by promoting only senior Turks.
3. He broke the power of the Forty by promoting junior Turks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
105.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Mewatis and rebel villages were ruthlessly suppressed. Statement 2 is wrong: he did not strengthen the Forty. Statement 3 is correct: he broke the Forty's power by promoting junior Turks. Hence '1 and 3 only'; any option with 2 is wrong.
105.tq: Balban ended the Chahalgani; he did not build it up.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 3 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: **ruthless suppression** of the **Mewatis** and rebellious villages.
2 is wrong: he did not strengthen the Forty.
3 is correct: he **broke the power of the Forty** by promoting **junior Turks**.
xa: ⚠ Iltutmish **created** the Forty; Balban **broke** it.
UPPSC **2024**: Balban centralised authority AND guarded the north-west, but the second is not the reason for the first.

105.s: The military department reorganised by Balban was known as:
105.x: Balban reorganised the army and created the military department Diwan-i-Arz. He also built outposts and forts against the Mongols.
105.tq: Use the function of an institution to distinguish it from neighbouring departments.
xs: Balban created the military department **Diwan-i-Arz** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He reorganised the army and built **outposts and forts** against the **Mongols**.
xa: His son **Prince Muhammad** died fighting the Mongols (**1285**).
Diwan-i-Arz is one of the dynasty's **core institutions**, with iqta, the Forty and **tanka/jital**.

105.s: Who among the following died while fighting the Mongols in 1285?
105.x: Prince Muhammad, Balban's son, died fighting the Mongols in 1285. Balban had built forts and outposts to guard the north-west.
105.tq: Link the precise year with the correct member of the ruling family.
xs: **Prince Muhammad, son of Balban**, died fighting the **Mongols** in **1285** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Aram Shah** was Aibak's son; **Qubacha** was Iltutmish's rival; **Kaiqubad** was Balban's grandson, murdered.
xa: Balban guarded the north-west with **outposts and forts**.
Balban died in **1286**.

105.s: Which sequence correctly describes the end of Mamluk rule?
o: Balban → Kaiqubad → Kaimurs → Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji
Kaiqubad → Balban → Kaimurs → Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji
Balban → Kaimurs → Kaiqubad → Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji
Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji → Balban → Kaiqubad → Kaimurs
105.x: Balban died in 1286 and was followed by his grandson Kaiqubad, who was murdered. The infant Kaimurs succeeded him briefly before Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji ended Mamluk rule in 1290.
105.tq: Arrange succession events by fixing the transition from the last Mamluk ruler to the Khaljis.
xs: **Balban → Kaiqubad → Kaimurs → Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Balban died in **1286**; grandson **Kaiqubad** was murdered (body thrown into the **Yamuna**).
Then the infant **Kaimurs**, until **Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji** took over in **1290**.
xa: Jalaluddin crowned himself at **Kilokhari**.
The **Khalji** dynasty ruled **1290-1320**.

105.s: Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji crowned himself at which place in 1290?
105.x: Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji crowned himself at Kilokhari in 1290, thereby ending Mamluk rule and beginning the Khalji dynasty.
105.tq: Match the accession event with its precise location and year.
xs: Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji crowned himself at **Kilokhari** in **1290** — so option **(2)** is correct.
That ended **Mamluk** rule.
**Bhatinda** is linked with **Altuniya**, **Badaun** with Iltutmish's governorship and **Lahore** with **Aibak's** capital.
xa: The last Mamluks were **Kaiqubad** and the infant **Kaimurs**.
The **Khalji** dynasty ruled **1290-1320**.

105.s: Which dynasty is regarded as the first Muslim dynasty to rule North India from Delhi?
105.x: The Slave or Mamluk dynasty was the first Muslim dynasty to rule North India from Delhi and laid the institutional foundation of the Delhi Sultanate.
105.tq: Use direct dynasty identification while distinguishing the founding dynasty from later Sultanate dynasties.
xs: The **Slave or Mamluk** dynasty was the **first Muslim dynasty** to rule north India from Delhi — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Khalji**, **Tughlaq** and **Lodi** dynasties came after it (**1290** onwards).
xa: Its core institutions: **iqta**, **the Forty**, **tanka/jital**, **Diwan-i-Arz**.
FIRSTS: first mosque **Quwwat-ul-Islam**; only woman Sultan **Razia**; first Caliphal investiture **Iltutmish, 1229**.

105.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the contributions of the Slave or Mamluk dynasty:
1. It created the iqta institution as a core institution of the Sultanate.
2. It developed the institution known as the Forty.
3. It introduced the tanka and jital as important Sultanate coins.
4. It established the Diwan-i-Arz as a core institution.
5. The Qutb complex associated with this dynasty is now a UNESCO site.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
105.x: All five statements are correct. The dynasty helped establish the iqta, Forty, tanka-jital and Diwan-i-Arz institutions, while the Qutb complex is now a UNESCO site.
105.tq: Check each institutional contribution separately before selecting the comprehensive combination.
xs: All five statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5** is the answer.
Core institutions: **iqta**, **the Forty**, **tanka/jital** and **Diwan-i-Arz**.
The **Qutb complex** is now a **UNESCO** site.
xa: **Iqta** and the **Forty** came from **Iltutmish**; **Diwan-i-Arz** from **Balban**.
**Iqta** = revenue assignments to **muqtis** instead of cash salaries.

105.s: The first Caliphal investiture of a Delhi Sultan took place in which year?
105.x: Iltutmish received the first Caliphal investiture in 1229.
105.tq: Anchor the event to its exact year and distinguish it from the accession years of early Delhi Sultans.
xs: The first Caliphal investiture came in **1229** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Iltutmish** received it (**"mansur"**) from the **Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad**.
**1206** was Aibak's accession, **1211** the start of the First Ilbari line, **1236** Iltutmish's death.
xa: Iltutmish's title was **Shamsuddin**; he moved the capital to **Delhi**.
He created the **Turkan-i-Chahalgani** (the Forty).

106.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Jalaluddin Khalji's policy towards rebels and Hindus?
o: He imposed severe punishments on every rebel without exception.
He adopted a benevolent attitude and was lenient towards rebels such as Malik Chhajju.
He adopted a policy of complete exclusion of Hindus from administration.
He transferred the capital to Ranthambore to control Hindu chiefs.
106.x: Jalaluddin Khalji was the first Sultan described as having a benevolent attitude towards Hindus, and he was lenient towards rebels including Malik Chhajju.
106.tq: Identify the policy statement that combines the ruler's general approach with its specific example.
xs: Jalaluddin **adopted a benevolent attitude** and was **lenient towards rebels such as Malik Chhajju** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was the **first Sultan** with a benevolent attitude to **Hindus**.
His attack on **Ranthambore** failed; he never moved his capital there.
xa: He crowned himself at **Kilokhari** in **1290**, aged about **70**.
He was a **Khalji** from **Turkestan** who had fought the Mongols.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about Jalaluddin Khalji:
1. He crowned himself at Kilokhari.
2. His attack on Ranthambore failed.
3. He was murdered at Kara by his nephew and son-in-law Alauddin.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: All three statements are correct. Jalaluddin crowned himself at Kilokhari, failed in his attack on Ranthambore, and was murdered at Kara by Alauddin in 1296.
106.tq: Check the event, outcome and place separately before selecting the combined option.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
1: he crowned himself at **Kilokhari** (**1290**).
2: his attack on **Ranthambore** failed.
3: his nephew and son-in-law **Alauddin** murdered him at **Kara (1296)**.
xa: Before the murder Alauddin raided **Devagiri** (**1294-96**) — the **first Turkish invasion of the south**.
Jalaluddin was lenient to rebels like **Malik Chhajju**.

106.s: The raid on Devagiri by Alauddin Khalji, which preceded his accession to the throne, took place during which period?
106.x: Alauddin Khalji raided Devagiri during 1294–1296, before murdering Jalaluddin and becoming Sultan.
106.tq: Distinguish the date-range of a preliminary campaign from the date of accession.
