xs: **Haji Iliyas** made Bengal independent, and **Firoz** failed to recover it in **two campaigns** — option **(3)**.
The second campaign was in **1359-60** and failed, so Firoz did not annex Bengal (4).
**Tughril Khan** only revolted (**1279**) and was crushed by **Balban**.
xa: **Jaunpur (Sharqi)** also broke away and was annexed back by **Bahlol Lodi** in **1476**.
**Vijayanagara** arose in **1336** from **Harihara** and **Bukka**.

110.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the origins of Vijayanagara:
1. Muhammad bin Tughluq sent Harihara and Bukka against the Deccan rebels.
2. After their defeat, Harihara and Bukka returned to Hinduism under Vidyaranya.
3. Anegondi founded by them later grew into Vijayanagara.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
110.x: All three statements are correct. Harihara and Bukka were sent against Deccan rebels, later returned to Hinduism under Vidyaranya, and founded Anegondi, which developed into Vijayanagara.
110.tq: Check the complete causal chain from the Deccan expedition to the foundation of Vijayanagara.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** sent **Harihara and Bukka** against Deccan rebels.
Statement 2 is correct: after defeat they returned to **Hinduism** under **Vidyaranya**.
Statement 3 is correct: they founded **Anegondi**, which grew into **Vijayanagara (1336)** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: **Bengal** broke away under **Haji Iliyas**.
**Jaunpur** was annexed back by **Bahlol Lodi** in **1476**.
AP angle: **Ulugh Khan** (future MBT) captured **Prataparudra II** in **1323**.

110.s: Jaunpur, which had broken away as a Sharqi kingdom, was annexed back to the Delhi Sultanate by Bahlol Lodi in:
110.x: Bahlol Lodi re-annexed the breakaway Sharqi kingdom of Jaunpur in 1476.
110.tq: Match the annexation year with the correct Lodi ruler and kingdom.
xs: **Bahlol Lodi** annexed **Jaunpur (Sharqi)** back in **1476** — option **(3)**.
**1359** relates to Firoz's second Bengal campaign; **1398** is **Timur's** invasion; **1526** is **Panipat**.
xa: Bahlol reigned **1451-1489** (**38 years**), the longest reign.
Bahlol = **first Afghan** Sultan.

110.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
110.x: Gulrukhi was the pen-name of Sikandar Lodi. Alauddin Khalji was known as Sikandar-i-Sani, while Ghazi Malik was the pre-accession name of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq.
110.tq: Look for a title transferred to a famous ruler of another dynasty.
xs: **Gulrukhi – Alauddin Khalji** is wrong: Gulrukhi was **Sikandar Lodi's** pen-name — option **(1)**.
Alauddin's title was **Sikandar-i-Sani**; **Ghazi Malik** = Ghiyasuddin, **Zillillah** = Balban, **Lakh Baksh** = Aibak.
xa: **Lakh Baksh** = "giver of lakhs".
Balban also took **Niyabat-i-Khudai**.
Ghazi Malik was Ghiyasuddin's name **before he took the throne**.

110.s: The title ‘Zillillah’, meaning ‘Shadow of God’, was associated with which ruler?
110.x: Balban adopted the titles Zil-i-Ilahi or Zillillah, meaning Shadow of God, and Niyabat-i-Khudai.
110.tq: Translate the epithet mentally and connect it with the ruler’s theory of kingship.
xs: **Zillillah** (**Zil-i-Ilahi**, "**shadow of God**") was the title of **Balban** — option **(1)**.
Ghiyasuddin was **Ghazi Malik**; Aibak was **Lakh Baksh**; Sikandar Lodi wrote as **Gulrukhi**.
xa: Balban's other title: **Niyabat-i-Khudai**.
Balban crushed **Tughril Khan's** Bengal revolt (**1279**).
Balban led the **Second Ilbari** phase (**1266-1290**).

110.s: The title ‘Lakh Bakhsh’ associated with Qutbuddin Aibak means:
110.x: Lakh Bakhsh means ‘giver of lakhs’, referring to Aibak's generosity. He also patronised the historian Hasan Nizami.
110.tq: Discriminate between a ruler's title and the meanings of other Sultanate titles.
xs: **Lakh Baksh** means "**giver of lakhs**" — option **(4)**.
"**Shadow of God**" (**Zillillah**) was Balban's title, not Aibak's.
xa: **Aibak** = first Sultan; took the title when **Ghori** died in **1206**.
Ghori left him in charge in India after **1192**.
Aibak founded the **Mamluk / Slave** dynasty (**1206-1290**).

110.s: Who among the following was earlier known as Ghazi Malik?
110.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq was earlier known as Ghazi Malik. He became Sultan in 1320 after killing Khusrau Shah.
110.tq: Test the earlier name of the ruler directly, while using nearby dynastic rulers as distractors.
xs: **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq** was earlier known as **Ghazi Malik** — option **(4)**.
**Muhammad bin Tughlaq** was earlier **Ulugh Khan**.
xa: Ghiyasuddin founded the **Tughlaq** dynasty (**1320-1414**).
Origin: father a **Turkish slave**, mother a **Jat**.
The last Khalji was killed by the usurper **Khusrau Khan (Nasiruddin Khusrau Shah)**.

110.s: The title 'Sikandar-i-Sani' (the Second Alexander) was assumed by:
110.x: Alauddin Khalji assumed the title Sikandar-i-Sani. Sikandar Lodi is linked with the pen-name Gulrukhi, not this title.
110.tq: Alauddin dreamed of world conquest like Alexander.
xs: **Alauddin Khalji** took the title **Sikandar-i-Sani** — option **(1)**.
⚠ **Sikandar Lodi** is linked to the pen-name **Gulrukhi**, not this title.
xa: Alauddin completed **Balban's** frontier policy of forts.
Balban's titles: **Zillillah**, **Niyabat-i-Khudai**.
Aibak = **Lakh Baksh**.

110.s: Who was the last ruler of the Mamluk or Slave dynasty in the Delhi Sultanate?
110.x: Kaiqubad was the last effective ruler of the Mamluk dynasty and was killed in 1290. His infant son Kayumars was only the nominal last ruler.
110.tq: Separate the effective last ruler from the nominal child successor.
xs: **Kaiqubad**, killed in **1290**, was the last Slave ruler — option **(4)**.
His infant son **Kayumars** was only the **nominal** last ruler.
**Ruknuddin Firoz** and **Nasiruddin Mahmud** ruled earlier in the line, before **Balban**.
xa: Last rulers: **Khalji – Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah**; **Tughlaq – Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah**; **Sayyid – Alam Shah**; **Lodi – Ibrahim**.
Slave dynasty: **1206-1290**.

110.s: When Vasco da Gama reached Calicut on 17 May 1498, who was the Sultan of Delhi?
110.x: Sikandar Lodi was the Delhi Sultan when Vasco da Gama arrived at Calicut. The Zamorin ruled Calicut and Immadi Narasimha ruled Vijayanagara at that time.
110.tq: Anchor the event to its date and then identify the ruler in office.
xs: **Sikandar Lodi (1489-1517)** was Sultan when **Vasco da Gama** reached **Calicut** on **17 May 1498** — option **(3)**.
xa: Rajon ki Baoli was built by **Daulat Khan Lodi** in **1506**, in Sikandar's reign.
Sikandar's pen-name: **Gulrukhi**.

110.s: Which statement regarding the early Delhi Sultanate is correct?
o: Razia was the first Afghan ruler of Delhi.
Bahlol Lodi was the first Afghan ruler of Delhi.
Ibrahim Lodi was the first woman ruler of the Sultanate.
Qutbuddin Aibak was the first Afghan Sultan.
110.x: Bahlol Lodi was the first Afghan ruler of Delhi; the rulers before him were Turks. Razia was the first and only woman to rule the Delhi Sultanate.
110.tq: Use nationality and gender distinctions to reject familiar but reversed claims.
xs: **Bahlol Lodi** was the **first Afghan ruler** of Delhi; all before him were **Turks** — option **(2)**.
**Razia** was the first woman ruler; **Ibrahim** was the last Sultan; **Aibak** was the first Sultan (a Turk).
xa: Lodi dynasty: **1451-1526**.
Bahlol reigned **1451-89** (**38 years**).
Razia = **first and only** woman to rule the Sultanate.

110.s:
Consider the following statements about Rajon ki Baoli in Mehrauli Archaeological Park:
1. It is a four-tier stepwell.
2. It was built by Daulat Khan Lodi in 1506 during the reign of Ibrahim Lodi.
3. Its restoration was completed under the ASI, World Monuments Fund India and TCS Foundation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
110.x: Statement 1 is correct: it is a four-tier stepwell. Statement 2 is wrong: 1506 falls in Sikandar Lodi's reign (1489-1517), not Ibrahim's. Statement 3 is correct: ASI, WMF India and TCS Foundation restored it. So '1 and 3 only' (C); A omits 3, B and D include the false statement 2.
110.tq: Check the year against reign dates: 1506 = Sikandar Lodi.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Rajon ki Baoli** is a **four-tier stepwell** in **Mehrauli Archaeological Park**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Daulat Khan Lodi** built it in **1506**, in **Sikandar Lodi's** reign (**1489-1517**), not Ibrahim's.
Statement 3 is correct: restored under **ASI**, **World Monuments Fund India** and **TCS Foundation** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: Reported by **PIB**.
**Ibrahim Lodi** reigned **1517-26**.

110.s:
Consider the following statements about the Delhi invasions of Andhra:
1. Delhi invaded Andhra five times between 1303 and 1323.
2. Ulugh Khan captured Prataparudra II in 1323.
3. The capture resulted in the annexation of the Kakatiya kingdom.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
110.x: Delhi forces invaded Andhra five times during 1303–1323. In 1323, Ulugh Khan captured Prataparudra II, leading to the annexation of the Kakatiya kingdom.
110.tq: Verify the number, date, person and political consequence together.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: Delhi invaded Andhra **five times** (**1303-1323**).
Statement 2 is correct: **Ulugh Khan** captured **Prataparudra II** in **1323**.
Statement 3 is correct: the **Kakatiya** kingdom was then **annexed** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: Ulugh Khan = the future **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** (**1325-51**).
MBT later sent **Harihara and Bukka** to the Deccan; they founded **Vijayanagara (1336)**.

110.s: Ulugh Khan, who captured Prataparudra II in 1323, later became known as:
110.x: Ulugh Khan was the earlier name of Muhammad bin Tughluq, who captured Prataparudra II in 1323.
110.tq: Discriminate between an earlier personal name and a later regnal identity.
xs: **Ulugh Khan** later became **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** — option **(1)**.
He captured **Prataparudra II** in **1323**, annexing the **Kakatiya** kingdom.
xa: MBT reigned **1325-51**.
⚠ **Timur** invaded under **Nasiruddin Mahmud**, not MBT.
⚠ **Ghazi Malik** = Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, MBT's predecessor.

110.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Razia — First Afghan ruler of Delhi
Bahlol Lodi — First woman ruler of Delhi
Ibrahim Lodi — Founder of the Slave dynasty
110.x: Qutbuddin Aibak was the first Sultan of Delhi. Razia was the first woman ruler, Bahlol Lodi the first Afghan ruler, and Ibrahim Lodi the last Sultan.
110.tq: Use the first-and-last distinctions to reject swapped titles and identities.
xs: **Aibak – first Sultan of Delhi** is correct — option **(2)**.
**Razia** = first woman ruler; **Bahlol Lodi** = first Afghan ruler; **Ibrahim Lodi** = last Sultan, not founder.
xa: Aibak took the title when **Ghori** died in **1206**.
Aibak's title: **Lakh Baksh** ("giver of lakhs").
Last Sultan **Ibrahim Lodi** fell at **Panipat (1526)**.

110.s: Which ruler was the last Sultan of Delhi before the establishment of Mughal rule?
110.x: Ibrahim Lodi was the last Sultan of Delhi and was defeated at the Battle of Panipat in 1526.
110.tq: Use the final-ruler and transition-to-Mughal relationship.
xs: **Ibrahim Lodi** was the last Sultan of Delhi, defeated at **Panipat (1526)** — option **(2)**.
**Sikandar** (**1489-1517**) and **Bahlol** ruled before him; **Nasiruddin Mahmud** was the last **Tughlaq**.
xa: Ibrahim reigned **1517-26**.
**Rana Sanga** defeated him at **Khatoli (1517)**.
Lodi dynasty: **1451-1526**.

111.s: Under whose theory of kingship was the Sultan described as Zil-i-Ilahi, or the Shadow of God?
111.x: Balban propounded the concept of the Sultan as Zil-i-Ilahi, or Shadow of God, along with Niyabat-i-Khudai, or divine deputyship.
111.tq: Match the distinctive political doctrine with its proponent.
xs: The theory of kingship of **Balban** called the Sultan **Zil-i-Ilahi** (Shadow of God) — option **(4)**.
He paired it with **Niyabat-i-Khudai** (divine deputyship), **sijda and paibos**, **Nauroz** and a "**blood and iron**" policy.
**Iltutmish** sought legitimacy through **caliphal investiture**; **Alauddin** put state interest above the ulema; **MBT** followed **rationalist absolutism**.
xa: Balban allowed **no low-born men** in office.
Balban, himself one of the **Forty**, destroyed the **Chalisa**.
He set up the **Diwan-i-Arz** (army department) — **RPSC 2018**.

111.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Alauddin Khalji — Kingship knows no kinship
Muhammad bin Tughlaq — Exclusion of non-Turks from high office
111.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq followed rationalist absolutism and appointed non-Turks and low-born persons. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
111.tq: Look for the reversed policy statement, especially where a ruler's inclusionary policy is made exclusionary.
xs: **MBT – exclusion of non-Turks** is wrong: MBT **appointed non-Turks and low-born men** — option **(4)**.
The rest are correct: **Alauddin** – "kingship knows no kinship"; **Balban** – "blood and iron"; **Iltutmish** – created the **Turkan-i-Chahalgani** (the Forty).
xa: MBT's theory: **rationalist absolutism**.
MBT sought investiture from the Abbasid Caliph in **Egypt**.
MBT set up the **Diwan-i-Kohi** (agriculture).

111.s:
Consider the following statements about the theory of kingship:
1. Alauddin Khalji placed the interests of the state above the authority of the ulema and religious law.
2. Alauddin Khalji used the title Sikandar-i-Sani.
3. Balban permitted low-born men to occupy high offices as a central feature of his theory of kingship.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
111.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Balban excluded low-born men from high office, whereas the appointment of non-Turks and low-born men is associated with Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
111.tq: Use the contrast between the social policies of Balban and Muhammad bin Tughlaq to identify the false statement.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Alauddin** put **state interest above the ulema** and law.
Statement 2 is correct: Alauddin took the title **Sikandar-i-Sani** (some notes: Sikander-i-Azam).
Statement 3 is wrong: **Balban** allowed **no low-born men** in office; appointing them was **MBT's** policy — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Alauddin's maxim: "**kingship knows no kinship**".
Alauddin took **Yamin-ul-Khilafat Nasir-i-Amir-ul-Mominin** but did **not** seek investiture (**UPPSC 2023**).
Balban's titles: **Zil-i-Ilahi** and **Niyabat-i-Khudai**.

111.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sultan in the Delhi Sultanate:
1. The Sultan was supreme in military, legal and political matters and was the highest court of appeal.
2. There was a fixed rule of succession by which the eldest son always succeeded.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
111.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Sultan was supreme in military, legal and political matters and the highest court of appeal. Statement 2 is wrong: there was no fixed rule; succession rested on acceptance by nobles and ulema or on military strength. So A; B and C accept the false statement 2, D rejects the true statement 1.
111.tq: No fixed succession rule in the Sultanate.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the Sultan was supreme in **military, legal and political** matters and the **highest court of appeal**.
Statement 2 is wrong: there was **no fixed rule of succession** — it rested on backing of **nobles, ulema and army**, or military strength — so **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Sultans saw themselves as the **Caliph's representatives**.
The state was essentially a **military, centralised** state.
**Barids** formed the intelligence network.

111.s: The investiture received by Iltutmish from the Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad took place in approximately which year?
111.x: Iltutmish received a letter of investiture, or mansur, from the Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad in approximately 1229.
111.tq: Test a precise date with closely spaced medieval Sultanate dates as distractors.
xs: Iltutmish received the letter of investiture (**mansur**) from the **Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad** in **c.1229** — option **(2)**.
**1206** is the Sultanate's start; **1290** the Khalji revolution; **MBT** later sought investiture from the Caliph in **Egypt**.
xa: ⚠ **Baghdad** Caliph = Iltutmish; **Egypt** Caliph = MBT; **Mubarak Shah Khalji** = proclaimed himself Caliph.
Iltutmish's wazir: **Nizam-ul-Mulk Junaidi** (**APPSC-GS 2023**).
**BPSC 2022** asked who "opposed the Khalifa's power" — key: "**more than one of the above**".

111.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Delhi Sultans and the Caliphate is correct?
o: The Caliph directly appointed all provincial governors in India.
Every Sultan obtained investiture before occupying the throne.
The Sultans saw themselves as representatives of the Caliph.
The Sultans generally regarded themselves as independent successors of the Caliphs.
111.x: The Sultans generally saw themselves as representatives of the Caliph. There was no rule that every Sultan obtained investiture, and the Caliph did not directly appoint all provincial governors.
111.tq: Reject absolute statements such as “every” and identify the general constitutional relationship.
xs: The Sultans **saw themselves as the Caliph's representatives** — option **(3)**.
Not every Sultan sought investiture: **Alauddin** did not, and **Mubarak Shah Khalji** proclaimed himself Caliph.
xa: **Iltutmish** got investiture from **Baghdad (c.1229)**; **MBT** sought it from **Egypt**.
**Firoz** respected the Caliph.
The Caliph's **nominal authority** was a **Perso-Arabic** element of the state.

111.s: Who among the following proclaimed himself the Caliph?
111.x: Mubarak Shah Khalji proclaimed himself Caliph. This was distinct from Iltutmish's receipt of investiture and Alauddin's adoption of Caliphal titles without seeking investiture.
111.tq: Distinguish a self-proclaimed Caliph from a Sultan who merely received investiture or adopted titles.
xs: **Mubarak Shah Khalji** **proclaimed himself Caliph** — option **(1)**.
**Iltutmish** received investiture from Baghdad; **Firoz** respected the Caliph; Balban is given "**Nasir-amir-ul-momin**" in some notes.
xa: **Alauddin Khalji** took caliphal titles but **did not seek investiture**.
**MBT** sought investiture from the Caliph in **Egypt**.
⚠ **Baghdad** = Iltutmish; **Egypt** = MBT.

111.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the position of Muhammad bin Tughlaq in relation to the Abbasid Caliphate?
o: He proclaimed himself the only Caliph of India.
He received investiture from the Caliph of Baghdad in 1229.
He sought investiture from the Abbasid Caliph in Egypt.
He rejected every form of association with the Caliphate.
111.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq sought investiture from the Abbasid Caliph in Egypt. The 1229 investiture from the Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad was received by Iltutmish.
111.tq: Separate the similar investiture episodes of Iltutmish and Muhammad bin Tughlaq by place and event.
xs: **MBT** **sought investiture from the Abbasid Caliph in Egypt** — option **(3)**.
The **1229** investiture from **Baghdad** was **Iltutmish's**; **Mubarak Shah Khalji** proclaimed himself Caliph.
xa: MBT's theory: **rationalist absolutism**; he appointed **non-Turks and low-born men**.
MBT promoted **foreigners** in the nobility.
**Firoz** respected the Caliph.

111.s: Which Delhi Sultan took the titles 'Yamin-ul-Khilafat Nasir-i-Amir-ul-Mominin' without seeking investiture from the Caliph?
111.x: Alauddin Khalji took these titles but did not seek investiture. Iltutmish received investiture from the Caliph of Baghdad (c.1229), Mubarak Shah Khalji proclaimed himself Caliph, and Muhammad bin Tughlaq sought investiture from the Caliph in Egypt.
111.tq: Yamin-ul-Khilafat = Alauddin (UPPSC 2023).
xs: **Alauddin Khalji** took **Yamin-ul-Khilafat Nasir-i-Amir-ul-Mominin** without seeking investiture — option **(2)** (**UPPSC 2023** key).
**Iltutmish** received investiture (**c.1229**); **Mubarak Shah Khalji** proclaimed himself Caliph; **MBT** sought investiture from **Egypt**.
xa: Alauddin put **state interest above the ulema** and law.
His title: **Sikandar-i-Sani**.
He set up **Diwan-i-Mustakhraj** and **Diwan-i-Riyasat**.

111.s: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between sharia and zawabit in the Delhi Sultanate?
o: Zawabit replaced sharia in all civil and criminal matters.
Sharia governed all criminal matters, while zawabit governed only Hindu personal law.
Sharia applied only to the Sultan and his nobles, whereas zawabit applied to the general population.
Sharia covered Muslims’ civil matters, while royal decrees called zawabit supplemented it.
111.x: Sharia covered the civil matters of Muslims, while royal decrees or zawabit supplemented the legal order. Criminal law followed the Sultan’s rules, and Hindus retained their personal law.
111.tq: Separate civil law, personal law, criminal rules and royal decrees rather than treating them as one system.
xs: **Sharia** covered **Muslims' civil matters**, and royal decrees called **zawabit** supplemented it — option **(4)**.
**Criminal law** followed the **Sultans' rules**, and **Hindus** kept their own personal law — so (1), (2) and (3) are wrong.
xa: The state was a **composite of Perso-Arabic, Turko-Mongol and Indian** elements (**JPSC 2021**).
The Sultan was the **highest court of appeal**.
**Qazi-ul-Quzat** = chief justice.

111.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the legal and administrative nature of the Delhi Sultanate:
1. Hindus generally retained their own personal law.
2. Criminal law followed the rules made by the Sultans.
3. The Sultan was the supreme commander and the highest court of appeal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
111.x: All three statements are correct. Hindu personal law was retained, criminal law was governed by the Sultan’s rules, and the Sultan combined supreme military and appellate authority.
111.tq: Test the institutional features separately and select the complete combination.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Hindus** kept their own **personal law**.
Statement 2 is correct: **criminal law** followed the **Sultans' rules**.
Statement 3 is correct: the Sultan was **supreme commander** and **highest court of appeal** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: **Sharia** covered Muslims' civil matters; **zawabit** (royal decrees) supplemented it.
The state was comparatively **centralised**, with **Barids** as an intelligence network.

111.s: The state under the Delhi Sultanate was described as a composite structure because it combined which of the following elements?
111.x: The Delhi Sultanate combined Perso-Arabic, Turko-Mongol and Indian elements and was comparatively centralised.
111.tq: Recall the exact three-part composition instead of substituting neighbouring cultural influences.
xs: The Sultanate was a **composite of Perso-Arabic, Turko-Mongol and Indian** elements — option **(4)** (**JPSC 2021**).
**Perso-Arabic**: title Sultan, the Caliph's nominal authority, **sijda, paibos, Nauroz**.
**Turko-Mongol**: army in **decimal units** (khan, malik, amir, sipahsalar), **mounted archers**.
xa: It was comparatively **centralised** — essentially a **military, centralised state**.
**Barids** = intelligence network.

111.s:
Consider the following statements about the composite nature of the Delhi Sultanate state:
1. The title Sultan and Persian court rituals such as sijda, paibos and Nauroz were Perso-Arabic elements.
2. An army organised in decimal units with mounted archers was an Indian element.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
111.x: Statement 1 is correct: the title Sultan and sijda, paibos and Nauroz were Perso-Arabic. Statement 2 is wrong: decimal army units and horse warfare with mounted archers were Turko-Mongol elements. So A; B and C accept the false statement 2, D rejects the true statement 1.
111.tq: Decimal army + mounted archers = Turko-Mongol.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the title **Sultan** and **sijda, paibos, Nauroz** were **Perso-Arabic**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **decimal army units** and **mounted archers** were **Turko-Mongol**, not Indian — so **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Decimal ranks: **khan, malik, amir, sipahsalar**.
The state was a composite of **Perso-Arabic, Turko-Mongol and Indian** elements (**JPSC 2021**).
Sijda and paibos were part of **Balban's** court ritual.

111.s: Which department was responsible for recruitment, inspection and payment of the army and was headed by the Ariz-i-Mumalik?
111.x: Diwan-i-Arz dealt with army recruitment, inspection and pay, under the Ariz-i-Mumalik.
111.tq: Identify the department from its function and head together.
xs: **Diwan-i-Arz**, under the **Ariz-i-Mumalik**, handled army **recruitment, inspection and pay** — option **(1)**.
**Diwan-i-Risalat** = religious affairs; **Diwan-i-Qaza** = justice; **Diwan-i-Insha** = royal correspondence.
xa: Diwan-i-Arz was set up by **Balban** (**RPSC 2018**).
⚠ "Alauddin first set up a separate Ariz's department" is **false** (**UPSC 2002**).
**Imad-ul-Mulk** headed the army department under Balban.

111.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Diwan-i-Wizarat dealt with finance and revenue.
2. Diwan-i-Insha handled royal correspondence and drafting of decrees.
3. Diwan-i-Qaza was concerned with justice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
111.x: All three statements are correct. Diwan-i-Wizarat dealt with finance and revenue, Diwan-i-Insha with royal correspondence and decrees, and Diwan-i-Qaza with justice.
111.tq: Verify each department against its distinct administrative function before selecting the combined code.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Diwan-i-Wizarat** (under the **Wazir**) = **finance and revenue**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Diwan-i-Insha** (under the **Dabir-i-Khas**) = **royal correspondence** and decrees.
Statement 3 is correct: **Diwan-i-Qaza** = **justice** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: The Wazir was assisted by the **Auditor-General** and **Accountant-General**.
**Qazi-ul-Quzat** = chief justice.
**Diwan-i-Risalat** under the **Sadr-us-Sudur** = religious affairs.

111.s: Which Sultan is associated with the establishment of Diwan-i-Arz?
111.x: Diwan-i-Arz, the department dealing with army recruitment and inspection, was set up by Balban.
111.tq: Separate the founder of a department from later rulers who expanded military administration.
xs: **Balban** set up the **Diwan-i-Arz** — option **(2)** (**RPSC 2018**).
⚠ "Alauddin first set up a separate Ariz's department" is **false** (**UPSC 2002**).
xa: Alauddin set up **Diwan-i-Mustakhraj** and **Diwan-i-Riyasat**.
**Firoz**: **Diwan-i-Bandagan** and **Diwan-i-Khairat**.
Head of Diwan-i-Arz: **Ariz-i-Mumalik**.

111.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
111.x: Diwan-i-Bandagan, the department dealing with slaves, was established by Firoz Tughlaq, not Balban. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
111.tq: Find the single founder swapped with a neighbouring Sultan.
xs: **Diwan-i-Bandagan – Balban** is wrong: the department of **slaves** was set up by **Firoz** (**UPSC 2002**) — option **(4)**.
The rest are correct: **Kohi** = **MBT**; **Mustakhraj** and **Riyasat** = **Alauddin**.
xa: **Mustakhraj** recovered arrears from revenue officials.
**Kohi** aimed at extending cultivation.
Firoz also set up **Diwan-i-Khairat**.

111.s: The Diwan-i-Riyasat was primarily concerned with which of the following?
111.x: Diwan-i-Riyasat was the department of market control, functioning under the Naib-i-Riyasat, during Alauddin Khalji's reign.
111.tq: Distinguish the two Alauddin departments by their separate functions: market control and arrears recovery.
xs: **Diwan-i-Riyasat** dealt with **market control**, under the **Naib-i-Riyasat** — option **(3)**.
Revenue arrears = **Diwan-i-Mustakhraj**; religious grants = **Diwan-i-Risalat**; correspondence = **Diwan-i-Insha**.
xa: Both Riyasat and Mustakhraj were set up by **Alauddin**.
⚠ **Kohi** = MBT; **Bandagan + Khairat** = Firoz.

111.s: The Sadr-us-Sudur in the Delhi Sultanate was primarily associated with which of the following functions?
111.x: The Sadr-us-Sudur supervised religious affairs and endowments; the Chief Sadr was also the Chief Qazi.
111.tq: Discriminate between officials whose functions belonged to religion, intelligence and court administration.
xs: The **Sadr-us-Sudur** headed the **Diwan-i-Risalat**: **religious affairs and endowments** — option **(4)**.
News and intelligence = **Barid-i-Mumalik**; despatch of decrees = **Khareetadar**; court decorum and household = **Wakil-i-Dar**.
xa: The Chief Sadr was also the **Chief Qazi**.
Risalat made grants to **mosques and madrasas**.
Older notes call Diwan-i-Risalat the **foreign ministry**; learn the religious-affairs meaning first.

111.s:
Consider the following statements about the central administration of the Delhi Sultanate:
1. The Naib ranked next to the Sultan and in practice could control all departments.
2. The wizarat reached its heyday under Balban.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
111.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Naib ranked next to the Sultan and in practice controlled all departments. Statement 2 is wrong: the wizarat's heyday was under Firoz Tughlaq, when Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul ran the government. So '1 only' (A); B and C accept the false statement 2, D rejects the true statement 1.
111.tq: Heyday of wazir = Firoz Tughlaq with Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Naib** ranked next to the Sultan and in practice **controlled all departments**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the wizarat's heyday was under **Firoz Tughlaq**, not Balban — so **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: **Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul** ran Firoz's government as **wazir**.
**Malik Kafur** was **Naib Malik** of Alauddin.
The Wazir headed the **Diwan-i-Wizarat** (finance and revenue).

111.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Dabir-i-Khas — Royal correspondence and drafting of decrees
111.x: The Dabir-i-Khas headed the Diwan-i-Insha and dealt with royal correspondence and the drafting of decrees. The Barid ran intelligence and the Wakil-i-Dar maintained court decorum.
111.tq: Use the official–function association and reject swapped responsibilities.
xs: **Dabir-i-Khas – royal correspondence and drafting of decrees** is correct — option **(3)**.
The **Barid** ran **intelligence**; the **Wakil-i-Dar** kept **court decorum**; market control was the **Naib-i-Riyasat's**, not the Qazi's.
xa: Dabir-i-Khas headed the **Diwan-i-Insha**.
**Khareetadar** = despatcher of royal decrees (**UPPSC 2023**).
Qutb Shahi **Dabir** = Diwan-i-Insha.

111.s:
With reference to the central officials of the Delhi Sultanate, consider the following statements:
1. Qazi-ul-Quzat was the Chief Justice.
2. Barid-i-Mumalik headed the news and intelligence system.
3. Wakil-i-Dar was responsible for court decorum and the royal household.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
111.x: All three statements are correct. Qazi-ul-Quzat was the Chief Justice, Barid-i-Mumalik headed intelligence, and Wakil-i-Dar supervised the court and royal household.
111.tq: Use the official-function pairings and check all three statements independently.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Qazi-ul-Quzat** = **chief justice**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Barid-i-Mumalik** = head of **news and intelligence**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Wakil-i-Dar** = **court decorum** and **royal household** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: **Amir-i-Hajib** = master of ceremonies.
**Khareetadar** = despatcher of royal decrees.
**Naib** = second only to the Sultan.

111.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Barid-i-Mumalik — Head of news and intelligence
111.x: Wakil-i-Dar was responsible for court decorum and the royal household. The Chief Justice was the Qazi-ul-Quzat.
111.tq: Find the official whose duty has been swapped with that of another official.
xs: **Wakil-i-Dar – Chief Justice** is wrong: the Wakil-i-Dar handled **court decorum and the royal household** — option **(1)**.
The chief justice was the **Qazi-ul-Quzat**; the other three pairs are correct.
xa: **Khareetadar** asked in **UPPSC 2023**.
**Barids** ran the intelligence network.
**Naib** in practice controlled all departments.

111.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Imad-ul-Mulk — Balban
2. Malik Kafur — Alauddin Khalji
3. Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul — Firoz Tughlaq
4. Nizam-ul-Mulk Junaidi — Muhammad bin Tughlaq
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
111.x: Imad-ul-Mulk served Balban, Malik Kafur was the Naib Malik of Alauddin Khalji, and Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul was the wazir of Firoz Tughlaq. Nizam-ul-Mulk Junaidi served Iltutmish, not Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
111.tq: Split the options by identifying the swapped Sultan in the fourth pair.
xs: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct: **Imad-ul-Mulk – Balban**, **Malik Kafur – Alauddin**, **Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul – Firoz** — option **(2)**.
Pair 4 is wrong: **Nizam-ul-Mulk Junaidi** was **Iltutmish's** wazir (**APPSC-GS 2023**).
xa: Malik Kafur was Alauddin's **Naib Malik**.
**Ain-ul-Mulk Multani** conquered **Malwa** in **1305** for Alauddin.
Imad-ul-Mulk headed Balban's **army department**.

111.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul?
o: A Rajput general who served as Naib Malik under Alauddin Khalji
A Turkish noble who headed the army under Balban
A Persian scholar who headed the Diwan-i-Insha under Iltutmish
A Telugu Brahmin convert who served as wazir under Firoz Tughlaq
111.x: Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul was a Telugu Brahmin convert and served as wazir under Firoz Tughlaq.
111.tq: Discriminate among closely associated nobles by combining office, ruler and background.
xs: **Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul** — some notes call him a **Telugu Brahmin convert** — was **Firoz Tughlaq's wazir** — option **(4)**.
**Naib Malik** of Alauddin was **Malik Kafur**; Balban's army head was **Imad-ul-Mulk**.
xa: Under him the wizarat reached its **heyday**.
A **Malik Maqbul** is recorded at **Warangal** after **1323**.
After 1323 Andhra was run from **Devagiri** (**Malik Burhanuddin**).

111.s: Who among the following served as the wazir of Iltutmish?
111.x: Nizam-ul-Mulk Junaidi served as the wazir of Iltutmish.
111.tq: Use the noble–Sultan association directly; APPSC commonly tests the wrong-person-with-the-deed trap.
xs: **Nizam-ul-Mulk Junaidi** was **Iltutmish's** wazir — option **(3)** (**APPSC-GS 2023**).
**Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul** served **Firoz**; **Ain-ul-Mulk Multani** served **Alauddin**; **Imad-ul-Mulk** served **Balban**.
xa: Iltutmish received investiture from the **Baghdad** Caliph in **c.1229**.
Iltutmish created the **Chalisa** (the Forty).

111.s: The wizarat reached its heyday during the reign of which Sultan?
111.x: The wizarat reached its heyday under Firoz Tughlaq, when Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul effectively ran the government.
111.tq: Test the period of maximum importance of an institution rather than merely its origin.
xs: The wizarat's heyday was under **Firoz Tughlaq** — option **(1)**.
His wazir **Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul** **ran the government**.
xa: Firoz made iqtas **hereditary**, strengthening the nobles.
Firoz set up **Diwan-i-Bandagan** (slaves, **UPSC 2002**) and **Diwan-i-Khairat**.
Firoz **respected the Caliph**.

111.s: Malwa was conquered in 1305 for Alauddin Khalji by:
111.x: Ain-ul-Mulk Multani conquered Malwa for Alauddin Khalji in 1305.
111.tq: Multani took Malwa (both M).
xs: **Ain-ul-Mulk Multani** conquered **Malwa** in **1305** for **Alauddin** — option **(2)**.
**Malik Kafur** was Alauddin's **Naib Malik**; **Imad-ul-Mulk** served **Balban**; **Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul** served **Firoz**.
xa: Ain-ul-Mulk also served **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**.
⚠ Qutb Shahi **Ain-ul-Mulk** = the army office — a different use of the name.

111.s:
Which of the following practices were introduced by Balban to enhance the dignity of the Sultan?
1. Sijda
2. Paibos
3. Nauroz
4. Turkan-i-Chahalgani
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
111.x: Balban introduced sijda, paibos and the Persian festival Nauroz. Turkan-i-Chahalgani, the Forty, was created by Iltutmish.
111.tq: Separate the practices of Balban from the institution created by Iltutmish.
xs: **Sijda**, **paibos** and **Nauroz** were Balban's court practices — **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
The **Turkan-i-Chahalgani** ("The Forty") was created by **Iltutmish**; Balban **destroyed** it.
xa: Balban's theory: **Zil-i-Ilahi** + **Niyabat-i-Khudai**.
These rituals were **Perso-Arabic** elements of the state.
Balban's policy: "**blood and iron**".

111.s:
Consider the following statements about the Turkan-i-Chahalgani:
1. It was created by Iltutmish.
2. It consisted of forty Turkish slave-nobles.
3. Balban ultimately destroyed its political influence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
111.x: Iltutmish created the Turkan-i-Chahalgani, or the Forty, of Turkish slave-nobles. They influenced the succession after him, but Balban destroyed their power.
111.tq: Check the institution through its founder, composition and later fate.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Iltutmish** created the **Turkan-i-Chahalgani**.
Statement 2 is correct: it was "**The Forty**" Turkish **slave-nobles**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Balban**, himself one of the Forty, **destroyed it** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: The Forty made and unmade Sultans after Iltutmish, including over **Razia**.
⚠ **Iltutmish** created the Forty; **Balban** destroyed it.
After Balban, nobles set aside his nominee **Kai Khusrau** and raised **Kaiqubad**.

111.s: Which development is associated with the Khalji Revolution of 1290?
o: The Sultan was reduced to a ceremonial position.
All nobles were made hereditary landholders.
High offices were opened to non-Turks and Indian Muslims.
High offices were restricted to Turkish slave-nobles.
111.x: The Khalji Revolution opened high office to non-Turks and Indian Muslims, breaking the earlier Turkish monopoly.
111.tq: Use the date and institutional change together to identify the correct development.
xs: The **Khalji revolution (1290)** **opened high office to non-Turks and Indian Muslims** — option **(3)**.
It ended the earlier **Turkish monopoly** of the Slave nobility, so (4) is the opposite.
xa: **Alauddin** crushed the **Balbani and Jalali** nobles.
He **banned noble gatherings** and **spied** on the nobility.
**Jalaluddin Khalji** took power in **1290**.

111.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with the policy concerning nobility?
o: Muhammad bin Tughluq — Promoted foreigners and low-born men
Alauddin Khalji — Crushed the Balbani and Jalali nobles
Lodi Sultans — Treated Afghan nobles as subordinate officials without tribal equality
111.x: Lodi rulers dealt with an Afghan tribal nobility that treated the Sultan as first among equals. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
111.tq: Detect the reversed description in a dynasty-wise comparison of nobility.
xs: **Lodis – nobles as subordinate officials** is wrong: the **Afghan tribal nobility** treated the Sultan as "**first among equals**" — option **(4)**.
The rest are correct: **Firoz** made iqtas **hereditary**; **MBT** promoted **foreigners and low-born men**; **Alauddin** crushed **Balbani and Jalali** nobles.
xa: Khalji revolution (**1290**) opened office to **non-Turks** and **Indian Muslims**.
Slave dynasty nobility = **Turkish monopoly**.

111.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Iltutmish created the Turkan-i-Chahalgani.
B. Jalaluddin Khalji came to power.
C. Alauddin Khalji banned noble gatherings and spied on the nobility.
D. Balban destroyed the power of the Forty.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
111.x: Iltutmish created the Forty, Balban destroyed its power, Jalaluddin Khalji came to power in 1290, and Alauddin later imposed restrictions on the nobility.
111.tq: Fix the founder and the later destroyer first, then place the Khalji developments.
xs: Order: **Iltutmish** creates the Forty → **Balban** destroys it → **Jalaluddin** takes power (**1290**) → **Alauddin** curbs nobles (**A, D, B, C**) — option **(1)**.
**Balban** was himself one of the Forty, so its destruction preceded the **Khalji revolution of 1290**.
xa: After Balban, nobles raised **Kaiqubad** over **Kai Khusrau**.
Alauddin **banned noble gatherings** and spied on the nobility.
The Khalji revolution opened office to **non-Turks**.

111.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Muqti or wali — Governor of an iqta
Amil — Revenue officer of a pargana
111.x: A Khut was a hereditary rural landholder. The despatcher of royal decrees was the Khareetadar.
111.tq: Identify the official whose role has been replaced by a central court function.
xs: **Khut – despatcher of royal decrees** is wrong: the khut was a **hereditary rural landholder** — option **(4)**.
The despatcher of royal decrees was the **Khareetadar**; the other three pairs are correct.
xa: **Alauddin** abolished the **khut's cess**.
**Shiqdar** = in charge of a **shiq** (division/district).
**Muqaddam / Chaudhari** = village headman (**BPSC 2022**).

111.s:
With reference to rural officials of the Delhi Sultanate, consider the following statements:
1. Muqaddam or Chaudhari was the village headman.
2. The Chaudhari was regarded as the chief rural land-revenue official.
3. Alauddin Khalji abolished the cess of the khut.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
111.x: All three statements are correct. The muqaddam or chaudhari headed the village, the chaudhari had a major rural revenue role, and Alauddin abolished the khut’s cess.
111.tq: Combine the village hierarchy with the specific revenue measure associated with Alauddin.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Muqaddam / Chaudhari** = **village headman** (**BPSC 2022**).
Statement 2 is correct: the **UPSC 2004** key made the chaudhari the **chief rural land-revenue official**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Alauddin** abolished the **khut's cess** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: **Patwari** = village accountant.
**Amil** = revenue officer of a **pargana** (**UPSC 2019**).

111.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
111.x: A pargana, comprising a group of villages, was placed under an amil for revenue collection. A province was under a muqti or wali, a shiq under a shiqdar, and a village under a muqaddam or chaudhari.
111.tq: Match each territorial unit with its corresponding officer.
xs: **Pargana – Amil** is correct: the amil was **in charge of revenue collection** in a pargana — option **(3)** (**UPSC 2019**).
A province (iqta) was under a **muqti / wali**, a shiq under a **shiqdar**, a village under a **muqaddam / chaudhari**.
xa: A **pargana** = group of villages.
**Patwari** = village accountant.
**Khut** = hereditary rural landholder.

111.s: Which one of the following offices did NOT exist under the Delhi Sultans?
111.x: Mir Bakshi was a Mughal office and did not exist under the Delhi Sultans. The other offices belonged to the Sultanate administrative or military structure.
111.tq: Use the dynasty-specific office trap.
xs: The office of **Mir Bakshi** did **not** exist under the Sultans; it is **Mughal** — option **(4)** (**UPSC 2019**).
**Shiqdar** (shiq), **Ariz-i-Mumalik** (Diwan-i-Arz) and **Muqti** (iqta) were Sultanate offices.
xa: Sultanate diwans prefigured the Mughal **Diwan**, **Mir Bakshi** and **Sadr-us-Sudur**.
The Ariz-i-Mumalik's department was set up by **Balban**.

111.s: Which of the following statements best expresses the significance of the Delhi Sultanate’s administrative institutions for the Mughal Empire?
o: The Sultanate diwans anticipated institutions such as the Mughal Diwan, Mir Bakshi and Sadr-us-Sudur.
The Sultanate had no specialised departments that could influence later administrations.
Only the Sultanate’s village institutions survived in the Mughal system.
The Mughal Empire rejected all Sultanate administrative institutions.
111.x: The Sultanate diwans prefigured important Mughal institutions, including the Diwan, Mir Bakshi and Sadr-us-Sudur.
111.tq: Recognise institutional continuity across two successive imperial systems.
xs: The Sultanate diwans **prefigured the Mughal Diwan, Mir Bakshi and Sadr-us-Sudur** — option **(1)**.
The Sultanate had many specialised **diwans** (Wizarat, Arz, Insha, Risalat), so (2) and (4) are wrong.
xa: ⚠ **Mir Bakshi** itself did not exist under the Sultans (**UPSC 2019**).
The **Bahmani** and **Qutb Shahi** states also inherited the Delhi model.
Bahmani institutions: **Majlis-i-Malakat**, **Wakil-us-Saltanat**, **Amir-i-Jumla**.

111.s:
Consider the following statements about Qutb Shahi administration:
1. The Peshwa functioned as the Prime Minister.
2. Under Tana Shah, the title Peshwa was renamed Diwan.
3. Madanna was the last holder of the Peshwa office.
4. Majumdar was an auditor and was mostly drawn from Hindus.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
111.x: All four statements are correct. The Peshwa was the Prime Minister, was renamed Diwan under Tana Shah, was last held by Madanna, and the Majumdar served as auditor, mostly from the Hindu community.
111.tq: Check the office, renaming, last holder and community detail separately.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: Qutb Shahi **Peshwa** = **PM**, renamed **Diwan** under **Tana Shah**, last held by **Madanna**.
Statement 4 is correct: **Majumdar** = **auditor**, mostly **Hindus** — so **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
xa: Qutb Shahi **Mir Jumla** = finance; **Ain-ul-Mulk** = army.
**Dabir** = Diwan-i-Insha.
Bahmani PM = **Wakil-us-Saltanat**.

111.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched in the Qutb Shahi administration?
111.x: Mir Jumla was associated with finance. The master of ceremonies in the Delhi Sultanate was the Amir-i-Hajib.
111.tq: Detect the office transferred from the Delhi Sultanate to the wrong Qutb Shahi official.
xs: **Mir Jumla – master of ceremonies** is wrong: Qutb Shahi **Mir Jumla** handled **finance** — option **(1)**.
The rest are correct: **Dabir** = **Diwan-i-Insha**; **Ain-ul-Mulk** = **army**; **Majumdar** = **auditor**.
xa: The Sultanate master of ceremonies was the **Amir-i-Hajib**.
Qutb Shahi **Peshwa** = PM; last holder **Madanna**.
Bahmani counterpart: **Amir-i-Jumla**.

111.s: The Prime Minister of the Bahmani state was known as the:
111.x: The Bahmani Prime Minister was known as the Wakil-us-Saltanat.
111.tq: Separate the Bahmani title from the similarly placed Qutb Shahi offices.
xs: The Bahmani Prime Minister was the **Wakil-us-Saltanat** — option **(1)**.
**Peshwa** was the **Qutb Shahi** PM; **Dabir** headed the Qutb Shahi **Diwan-i-Insha**.
xa: Bahmani state also had the **Majlis-i-Malakat** and **Amir-i-Jumla**.
These states **inherited the Delhi model**.
Qutb Shahi Peshwa was renamed **Diwan** under **Tana Shah**.

112.s: Which statement regarding the development of the iqta system is correct?
o: Firoz Tughluq abolished the iqta system completely.
Iltutmish built the iqta into a systematic administrative institution.
Alauddin Khalji converted every iqta into private property.
Qutbuddin Aibak first introduced it as a hereditary system in India.
112.x: Iltutmish developed the iqta into a system. Under the Sultanate, it remained a revenue assignment rather than private ownership.
112.tq: Identify the ruler associated with institutional consolidation, not later modification.
xs: **Iltutmish** built the iqta into a **systematic institution** — option **(2)** (**UPPSC 2010** key: Iltutmish).
**Firoz** did not abolish iqtas — he made them **hereditary**; iqtas were **not ownership of land**, so (3) is wrong.
**Aibak** received the **first iqta** (**Hansi**) from **Ghori**, but it was **transferable**, not hereditary.
xa: Holder = **iqtadar / muqti** (or **wali** for a province).
Iqta = a **Turkish, non-indigenous** institution (**UPSC 2019**).
Some notes credit **Aibak** with introducing it.

112.s: What did the term ‘fawazil’ signify in the iqta system?
o: The hereditary right of the muqti over the land
The military contingent permanently stationed at the capital
The surplus revenue remaining after the muqti’s costs, which was sent to the treasury
The tax imposed on village artisans
112.x: Fawazil was the surplus revenue left after meeting the muqti’s costs, and it had to be remitted to the treasury.
112.tq: Distinguish surplus revenue from the assignment, officer and military obligations of an iqta.
xs: **Fawazil** was the **surplus revenue** left after the muqti's costs, which had to go to the **treasury** — option **(3)**.
The muqti had **no hereditary right** until **Firoz** made iqtas hereditary.
xa: Muqti duties: kept **troops**, collected **revenue**, kept **law and order**, sent the **fawazil** to the centre.
Iqta = **land revenue** assigned instead of a **cash salary**.
**Balban** appointed **khwajas** (auditors) to check muqtis' accounts.

112.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the responsibilities of a muqti:
1. He maintained troops.
2. He collected revenue.
3. He sent the surplus revenue to the central government.
4. He was exempt from maintaining law and order.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
112.x: A muqti maintained troops, collected revenue, preserved law and order, and remitted the surplus to the centre. Therefore, statement 4 is false.
112.tq: Find the statement that reverses a duty of the office-holder.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: the muqti **kept troops**, **collected revenue** and sent the **surplus (fawazil)** to the centre.
Statement 4 is wrong: he also **kept law and order** — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: The muqti held an **iqta**, a revenue assignment, **not ownership of land**.
Iqtas were **transferable**; muqtis moved periodically until **Firoz** made them hereditary.
**Alauddin** tightened the **audit** of muqtis.

112.s: Which one of the following statements about the nature of the iqta system is correct?
o: It was an ancient indigenous Indian institution.
It was exclusively a religious endowment system.
It was introduced only in the Mughal period.
It was a Turkish, non-indigenous institution.
112.x: The iqta was a Turkish institution and was not an ancient indigenous Indian institution.
112.tq: Discriminate between a foreign administrative institution and an indigenous one.
xs: The iqta was a **Turkish, non-indigenous** institution — option **(4)**.
⚠ Trap: "ancient indigenous institution" is **false** (**UPSC 2019**).
It began under **Ghori** (**Hansi** to **Aibak**), long before the Mughals, and was a revenue assignment, not a religious endowment.
xa: **Iltutmish** institutionalised it.
Iqta = ancestor of the Mughal **jagir/mansab** system.

112.s: The first iqta grant in India, of Hansi, is credited to:
o: Muhammad Ghori, granted to Qutbuddin Aibak
Alauddin Khalji, granted to Malik Kafur
112.x: Muhammad Ghori granted Hansi (some sources say Kuhram) to Qutbuddin Aibak, the first iqta. Iltutmish later built the iqta into a system; Balban and Alauddin are not linked with the first grant.
112.tq: First iqta: Hansi, Ghori to Aibak.
xs: The first iqta, **Hansi**, was granted by **Muhammad Ghori** to **Qutbuddin Aibak** — option **(2)**.
Some notes say **Kuhram** instead of Hansi.
xa: **Iltutmish** later built the iqta into a system (**UPPSC 2010**).
Some notes credit **Aibak** with introducing it.
Iqta = a **Turkish, non-indigenous** institution.

112.s:
Consider the following statements about changes in the iqta system:
1. Balban appointed khwajas (auditors) to check the muqtis' accounts.
2. Alauddin Khalji paid the standing army in cash and enlarged the khalisa.
3. Ghiyasuddin Tughluq made the iqtas hereditary.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
112.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Balban appointed khwajas, and Alauddin paid the army in cash and enlarged the khalisa. Statement 3 is wrong: Firoz Tughlaq made iqtas hereditary; Ghiyasuddin held an inquiry into grants and seized unlawful ones. So B; A omits 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
112.tq: Hereditary iqtas = Firoz Tughlaq only.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Balban** appointed **khwajas** (auditors) to check muqtis' accounts.
Statement 2 is correct: **Alauddin** paid a **standing army in cash** and enlarged the **khalisa**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Firoz** made iqtas **hereditary**; **Ghiyasuddin** held an **inquiry into grants** and seized unlawful ones — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: ⚠ **Alauddin** = cash pay; **Firoz** = hereditary iqtas.
**Balban** tried to resume the iqtas of **old soldiers**.

112.s: With reference to the iqta system, which of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: Firoz Tughlaq abolished the jagir system to improve army efficiency.
Ghiyasuddin Tughluq ordered an inquiry into grants and jagirs.
Unlawful grants were seized during the reign of Ghiyasuddin Tughluq.
112.x: Firoz Tughlaq revived the jagir system and made iqtas hereditary. This revival adversely affected army efficiency; he did not abolish the system.
112.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated policy and its consequence.
xs: "**Firoz abolished the jagir system**" is NOT correct: he **revived** the jagir and made iqtas **hereditary** — option **(2)**.
That revival **hurt army efficiency**, as nobles controlled recruitment, promotion and discipline.
Statements (3) and (4) are correct: **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq** inquired into **grants/jagirs** and seized **unlawful grants**.
xa: Before Firoz, iqtas were **transferable**.
⚠ **Alauddin** = cash pay; **Firoz** = back to assignments.

112.s:
Arrange the following developments in the iqta system in chronological order:
A. Iqtas were made hereditary under Firoz Tughlaq.
B. Iltutmish organised the iqta system.
C. Balban appointed khwajas to audit muqtis' accounts.
D. Alauddin Khalji enlarged the khalisa and paid the standing army in cash.
112.x: The correct sequence is Iltutmish, Balban, Alauddin Khalji and Firoz Tughlaq.
112.tq: Use the rulers' chronological order to arrange administrative changes.
xs: Order: **Iltutmish** organises the iqta → **Balban** appoints **khwajas** → **Alauddin** pays cash and enlarges **khalisa** → **Firoz** makes iqtas **hereditary** (**B, C, D, A**) — option **(1)**.
Each change is tied to the Sultan's own reign, so the dynastic order fixes the sequence.
xa: **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq** (between Alauddin and Firoz) inquired into grants.
**Ghori** made the first iqta grant (**Hansi**) to **Aibak**.
⚠ **Alauddin** = cash pay; **Firoz** = hereditary iqtas.

112.s: What was the position of iqtas before the policy of Firoz Tughlaq?
o: They were permanently owned by the muqtis.
They were administered exclusively as khalisa lands.
They were granted only to religious leaders.
They were periodically transferable between muqtis.
112.x: Before Firoz Tughlaq made iqtas hereditary, muqtis were transferred periodically from one iqta to another.
112.tq: Distinguish a transferable assignment from a hereditary one.
xs: Before Firoz, iqtas were **transferable** and muqtis were **moved periodically** — option **(4)**.
Iqtas were **not ownership of land**; **khalisa** was the separate crown land; grants to religious men were **inam**.
xa: **Firoz Tughlaq** made iqtas **hereditary**.
Iqta = **land revenue** assigned instead of a **cash salary**.
Muqti sent the **fawazil** (surplus) to the treasury.

112.s: Which Sultan maintained the first large permanent standing army paid in cash from the royal treasury?
112.x: Alauddin Khalji maintained the first large permanent standing army paid in cash from the royal treasury. Market control helped keep the purchasing power of the pay adequate.
112.tq: Link a distinctive army-pay innovation with its ruler.
xs: **Alauddin Khalji** kept the **first large permanent standing army paid in cash** from the royal treasury — option **(3)**.
**Iltutmish** and **Balban** paid through **iqtas**; **Firoz** went back to assignments.
xa: **Market control** kept that cash pay adequate.
Ferishta put Alauddin's cavalry at about **4,75,000**.
Alauddin introduced **dagh** and **huliya**.

112.s:
Consider the following statements regarding army pay:
1. Iltutmish and Balban used iqtas for paying officers and troopers.
2. Alauddin Khalji paid his standing army in cash.
3. Firoz Tughlaq restored assignment-based payment through the revival of the jagir system.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
112.x: Iltutmish and Balban used iqtas for payment, Alauddin Khalji introduced large-scale cash payment, and Firoz Tughlaq returned to assignment-based payment through the jagir revival.
112.tq: Compare payment systems across successive rulers.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Iltutmish** and **Balban** gave **iqtas to officers and troopers**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Alauddin** paid his **standing army in cash**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Firoz** went back to assignments through the **jagir** revival — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: Firoz also made iqtas **hereditary**.
Alauddin enlarged the **khalisa** to fund cash pay.

112.s: The revival of the jagir system under Firoz Tughlaq adversely affected army efficiency because it allowed nobles to control
o: Only the royal treasury and market prices
The appointment of village accountants alone
112.x: The jagir revival enabled nobles to control recruitment, promotion and discipline, which weakened the efficiency of the army.
112.tq: Connect an institutional arrangement with its administrative consequence.
xs: The jagir revival let nobles control **recruitment, promotion and discipline** — option **(1)**.
This **hurt army efficiency** under **Firoz Tughlaq**.
xa: Firoz **reinstated iqtas** and made them **hereditary**.
⚠ Contrast **Alauddin**: a **standing army paid in cash** from the treasury.
**Shivaji** later **avoided jagir grants** and paid a standing army in cash.

112.s: Who introduced the branding of horses and the descriptive roll of soldiers in the Delhi Sultanate?
112.x: Alauddin Khalji introduced dagh, the branding of horses, and huliya, the descriptive roll of each soldier. Sher Shah later revived dagh.
112.tq: Match paired military controls with the ruler who introduced them.
xs: **Alauddin Khalji** introduced **dagh** (branding of horses) and **huliya** (descriptive roll) — option **(3)**.
**Sher Shah** only **revived** the dagh later.
⚠ "**Balban** introduced the branding of horses" is **false** (**UPSC 2002**).
xa: Purpose: stop **substandard horses** or **proxies** at the muster.
The army was run by the **Ariz-i-Mumalik**.

112.s: The primary purpose of dagh and huliya was to
o: Record the revenue of each iqta
Determine the hereditary rights of military officers
Prevent the presentation of substandard horses and substitute soldiers at muster
Classify villages according to agricultural production
112.x: Branding horses and maintaining descriptive rolls helped prevent soldiers from bringing inferior horses or sending proxies in their place during inspection.
112.tq: Infer the administrative purpose from the control mechanism.
xs: Dagh and huliya stopped **substandard horses** and **proxy soldiers** at the muster — option **(3)**.
**Dagh** = branding of horses; **huliya** = descriptive roll of each soldier.
xa: Introduced by **Alauddin Khalji**; dagh revived by **Sher Shah**.
The **Ariz's department** recruited, inspected and paid the army.

112.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correctly matched?
o: Huliya — Descriptive roll of a soldier
112.x: Balban did not introduce horse branding. Dagh and huliya were introduced by Alauddin Khalji, while Sher Shah later revived dagh.
112.tq: Catch the swapped-ruler trap in a military reform question.
xs: **Balban – introduction of horse branding** is wrong: **Alauddin Khalji** introduced it — option **(1)** (**UPSC 2002** trap).
The rest are correct: **Sher Shah** revived dagh; **huliya** = descriptive roll; **dagh** = branding of horses.
xa: Balban set up the **Diwan-i-Arz** and appointed **khwajas**.
Alauddin kept a **standing army paid in cash**.

112.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the Sultanate military hierarchy from the lowest listed rank to the highest?
112.x: The order was sar-i-khail, sipah-salar, amir, malik and khan. Khan was the highest listed rank.
112.tq: Arrange a graded hierarchy by its internal sequence.
xs: Lowest to highest: **Sar-i-khail → Sipah-salar → Amir → Malik → Khan** — option **(1)**.
A **Sar-i-khail** commanded **10 horsemen**; each higher rank commanded **10** of the rank below; **Khan** was highest.
xa: Ranks followed a **decimal** pattern — a **Turko-Mongol** feature.
Cavalry = **core arm**; also infantry and elephants.

112.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the decimal military organisation is correct?
o: A Khan commanded ten horsemen directly as the lowest rank.
112.x: An Amir commanded ten sipah-salars. The hierarchy rose from sar-i-khail to Khan, with each higher rank commanding ten units or officers of the next lower level.
112.tq: Check the direction of command in a decimal hierarchy.
xs: An **Amir commanded ten Sipah-salars** — option **(1)**.
A **Malik** commanded **10 amirs** (not khans); the **Khan** was the **highest** rank; a **Sar-i-khail** commanded **10 horsemen**.
xa: **Sipah-salar** = **10 sar-i-khails**.
**Khan** = **10 maliks**.

112.s:
Which of the following constituted the principal arms of the Sultanate army?
1. Cavalry
2. Infantry
3. Elephants
Which of the statements given above are correct?
112.x: Cavalry was the core arm of the army, which also included infantry and elephants.
112.tq: Distinguish the core arm from the other recognised components.
xs: **Cavalry** was the core arm, with **infantry** and **elephants** too — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
**War elephants** were a **royal preserve**.
xa: Alauddin's cavalry: about **4,75,000** (Ferishta).
Horses were **imported from West Asia**.
Ranks were **decimal**, from **Sar-i-khail** to **Khan**.

112.s:
Which combination of military innovations is associated with the Turks in medieval India?
1. Horse-based warfare
2. Mounted archery
3. Iron stirrup
4. Stronger fortifications
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
112.x: The Turks introduced or strengthened horse-based warfare, mounted archery, the iron stirrup, armour and stronger fortifications. Therefore, all four statements are correct.
112.tq: Identify the complete set of related military features before eliminating partial combinations.
xs: Turkish innovations: **horse-based warfare**, **mounted archers**, the **iron stirrup**, **armour** and **stronger fortification** — **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
So every listed item — horse-based warfare, mounted archery, iron stirrup and stronger fortifications — is a **Turkish** innovation.
xa: The **horse** became a key military and economic resource, **imported from West Asia**.
**War elephants** = a royal preserve.

112.s: Why did the horse become a key military and economic resource during the period under consideration?
o: Because war elephants were no longer used by royal armies
Because horses were reserved exclusively for provincial governors
Because the Turks introduced horse-based warfare and horses were imported from West Asia
Because horses were used mainly for transporting agricultural produce
112.x: The importance of horses increased with the spread of Turkish horse-based warfare. Since suitable horses were imported from West Asia, they also acquired major economic importance.
112.tq: Link the military development with its economic consequence and source of supply.
xs: The Turks brought **horse-based warfare**, and horses were **imported from West Asia** — option **(3)**.
**War elephants** remained in use as a **royal preserve**, so (1) is wrong.
xa: Other Turkish innovations: **mounted archers**, the **iron stirrup**, **armour**.
**Dagh** (branding of horses) stopped **substandard horses** at the muster.
Cavalry = **core arm** of the army.

112.s: Which one of the following is correctly associated with war elephants in the medieval military system?
o: They were maintained exclusively by village communities
They were imported only from West Asia
They were used only for carrying fruits of Khorasan
112.x: War elephants were regarded as a royal preserve. The other alternatives wrongly assign them to village control, West Asian importation or commercial transport.
112.tq: Use the precise institutional association rather than a broad military description.
xs: **War elephants** were a **royal preserve** — option **(3)**.
Horses, not elephants, came from **West Asia**; **Khorasan fruit** came by the **ulaq** (horse post).
xa: The army: **cavalry** (core), **infantry**, **elephants**.
Kakatiya posts: **Gajasahini**, **Ashwasahini**.

112.s: Alauddin Khalji received daily market reports from
112.x: Alauddin Khalji obtained daily market reports from barids and munhiyans, the latter functioning as secret spies.
112.tq: Match information sources with the ruler who used them.
xs: Alauddin got daily market reports from **barids and munhiyans** (secret spies) — option **(3)**.
**Barids** were news-reporters and intelligence agents under the **barid-i-mumalik**.
xa: **Khwajas** were **Balban's** auditors; **amils** were pargana revenue officers.
Alauddin's **market control** kept the army's cash pay adequate.

112.s: Who improved the postal system by using runners and horsemen?
112.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughluq improved the postal system by employing both runners and horsemen.
112.tq: Associate a communication reform with the correct Sultan.
xs: **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq** improved the post with **runners and horsemen** — option **(1)**.
**Sher Shah** later set up the **dak chowki**.
xa: **Ibn Battuta** described two relays: **ulaq** (horse) and **dawa** (foot).
⚠ **Ulaq** = horse; **dawa** = foot.
Ghiyasuddin also held an **inquiry into grants/jagirs**.

112.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Sultanate postal system?
o: The horse post, ulaq, was used to bring Khorasan fruit to Delhi.
The ulaq was a system of village revenue collection.
The foot post, dawa, was exclusively used for military recruitment.
The dawa was the department responsible for horse branding.
112.x: The horse post, called ulaq, was used to bring fruit from Khorasan to Delhi. Dawa referred to the foot post.
112.tq: Apply the functional distinction between the two postal relays.
xs: The horse post **ulaq** brought **Khorasan fruit** to Delhi — option **(1)** (**APPSC-G1 2017**).
**Dawa** was the **foot post**, not recruitment or branding; ulaq was a relay, not revenue collection.
xa: Both relays are from **Ibn Battuta's** account.
⚠ **Ulaq** = horse; **dawa** = foot.
**Sher Shah's dak chowki** = precursor of the modern post.

112.s: Sher Shah's dak chowki is regarded as
o: The accounting office of the khalisa
The later precursor of the modern post
The earliest form of the iqta system
The military department of the Delhi Sultanate
112.x: Sher Shah's dak chowki is regarded as a later precursor of the modern postal system.
112.tq: Identify the historical predecessor from its institutional legacy.
xs: **Sher Shah's dak chowki** is a **later precursor of the modern post** — option **(2)**.
It was a postal system, not an accounting office or a military department.
xa: Earlier: **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq** improved the post with **runners and horsemen**.
**Ulaq** (horse) and **dawa** (foot) relays per **Ibn Battuta**.
Sher Shah also **revived the dagh**.

112.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Iqta — Delhi Sultanate
2. Jagir — Mughal Empire
3. Amaram — Vijayanagara Empire
4. Mokasa — Bahmani and later Deccan
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
112.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Iqta, jagir, amaram and mokasa belonged respectively to the Delhi Sultanate, Mughal Empire, Vijayanagara and Bahmani-later Deccan contexts.
112.tq: Compare the four revenue assignments by both region and administrative nature.
xs: All four pairs are correct: **Iqta – Sultanate**, **Jagir – Mughal**, **Amaram – Vijayanagara**, **Mokasa – Bahmani and later Deccan** — option **(4)**.
So **1, 2, 3 and 4** are all correctly matched.
xa: The **jagir** also appears in **Bahmani** and **Qutb Shahi** usage.
Bahmanis used **iqta** as a synonym for **jagir**.
**Amaram** holders paid **kappam**.

112.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
112.x: Mahrousa meant a protected town. Khalisa referred to land under state administration, shiq to a portion or division, and iqta to a revenue assignment.
112.tq: Start with the sure terminological pair and eliminate the swapped meanings.
xs: **Mahrousa – protected town** is correct — option **(1)** (**UPPSC 2023**).
**Khalisa** = land under **direct state administration**; **Shiq** = "**a portion**", a division; **Iqta** = assignment of **land revenue**.
xa: A shiq was under a **shiqdar**.
**Inam** = land granted to religious leaders/institutions.

112.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Khalisa in the Bahmani context is correct?
o: Its revenue was used to maintain the central army.
It was a grant made only to Sufi saints.
It denoted a division of a province under a shiqdar.
It was the hereditary estate of an Amaranayaka.
112.x: In the Bahmani system, revenue from Khalisa lands was used to maintain the central army.
112.tq: Apply the same administrative term to its specified regional context.
xs: Bahmani **Khalisa** revenue **paid the central army** — option **(1)**.
A division under a **shiqdar** is a **shiq**; the **Amaranayaka's** land is the **amaram**.
xa: In the Sultanate, khalisa revenue went to the **royal treasury, court and household**.
**Alauddin** enlarged the khalisa.
Bahmanis used **iqta** as a synonym for **jagir**.

112.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Shiq — Division of a province
2. Inam — Grant to religious leaders or institutions
3. Jagir — Revenue assignment to a noble or officer
4. Amaram — Land given to Amaranayakas for maintaining troops
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
112.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Shiq, inam, jagir and amaram had the meanings and institutional associations stated.
112.tq: Verify each term against both its meaning and institutional setting.
xs: All four pairs are correct: **Shiq** = division of a province; **Inam** = religious grant; **Jagir** = revenue assignment to a noble; **Amaram** = land to **Amaranayakas** for troops — option **(4)**.
So **1, 2, 3 and 4** are all correctly matched.
xa: The Mughal jagir was tied to **mansab** rank and was transferable.
**Mokasa** = revenue assignment for military service in the **Deccan**.
**Mahrousa** = protected town.

112.s: Amaram in the Vijayanagara administrative system was associated with
o: Land under direct administration of the royal treasury
Land given to Amaranayakas for maintaining troops and paying kappam
A group of villages under an amil
A grant to religious institutions without military obligations
112.x: Amaram was land assigned to Amaranayakas, who maintained troops and paid kappam.
112.tq: Link a regional land assignment to its beneficiary and obligation.
xs: **Amaram** was land given to **Amaranayakas** for keeping **troops** and paying **kappam** — option **(2)**.
Crown land = **khalisa**; a pargana under an **amil** is a different unit; religious grants = **inam**.
xa: Amaram is also called **nayankara**.
Vijayanagara army: standing **Siddha Sainyam** + feudal **Amara Nayankara** army.

112.s: Which one of the following best describes an iqta under the Delhi Sultanate?
o: A hereditary ownership of agricultural land by a military officer
An assignment of land revenue to an officer in lieu of a cash salary
A tax-free grant exclusively to religious institutions
A village unit administered directly by the Sultan
112.x: An iqta was an assignment of land revenue to an officer, usually an iqtadar or muqti, instead of a cash salary. It did not confer ownership of the land.
112.tq: Distinguish a revenue assignment from ownership of land.
xs: An iqta was an **assignment of land revenue** to an officer **instead of a cash salary** — option **(2)**.
It was **not ownership of land** and was **transferable**; religious grants were **inam**.
xa: Holder = **iqtadar / muqti**; sent the **fawazil** to the treasury.
**UPPSC 2023** asked iqta = assignment of land revenue.
Iqta financed the army and **integrated distant provinces**.

112.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Land category)
 a. Khalisa
 b. Iqta
 c. Inam
List-II (Meaning)
 i. Land assigned to officials in place of salary
 ii. Land granted to religious men and institutions
 iii. Crown land whose revenue supported the court and royal household

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
112.x: Khalisa was crown land, iqta was assigned to officials in place of salary, and inam was granted to religious men and institutions.
112.tq: Start from the sure meaning of Khalisa and then distinguish official assignments from religious grants.
xs: **Khalisa** = crown land (iii), **Iqta** = land in place of salary (i), **Inam** = religious grants (ii) — option **(1)**.
Khalisa revenue went to the **royal treasury, court and household**; inam went to **religious leaders/institutions**.
xa: **UPPSC 2025**: Sultanate territory broadly **Khalisa and Iqta**.
Bahmani khalisa **paid the central army**.
**Alauddin** enlarged the **khalisa**.

112.s:
Assertion (A): The territory of the Delhi Sultanate was broadly divided into Khalisa and Iqta lands.
Reason (R): The territory of the Delhi Sultanate was broadly divided into Khalsa and Jagirs.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
112.x: A is true: Sultanate land was broadly khalisa (crown land) and iqta (revenue assignments). R is false: the jagir belongs to the Bahmani, Qutb Shahi and Mughal systems, not the Sultanate's basic division. So A is true and R is false, as in the UPPSC 2025 key.
112.tq: Sultanate = Khalisa + Iqta; jagir is Mughal/Deccan.
xs: **A is true**: Sultanate territory was broadly **Khalisa and Iqta**.
**R is false**: "**Khalsa and Jagirs**" is wrong; the **jagir** belongs to **Bahmani, Qutb Shahi and Mughal** usage — so option **(3)**, as in the **UPPSC 2025** key.
xa: Khalisa revenue went to the **royal treasury, court and household**.
The **Mughal jagir** was tied to **mansab** rank.

112.s:
Assertion (A): The iqta system helped the Delhi Sultanate finance its army.
Reason (R): Revenue assignments under the system linked military obligations with the administration of distant territories.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
112.x: Both statements are correct. The iqta system provided the financial basis for maintaining troops while also connecting military service with the administration of assigned territories.
112.tq: Check whether the reason explains the administrative and military function stated in the assertion.
xs: **A is true**: the **iqta** financed the army.
**Both A and R are true**, and **R is the correct explanation** of A: revenue assignments linked **military service** with **integrating distant provinces** — option **(1)**.
xa: The muqti **kept troops** and sent the **fawazil** to the centre.
The iqta is the ancestor of the Mughal **jagir/mansab** system.

112.s: The iqta system is regarded as the ancestor of which later Mughal arrangement?
o: Amara Nayankara and Siddha Sainyam system
112.x: The iqta system is considered the ancestor of the Mughal jagir and mansab system. The other combinations belong to different administrative or military contexts.
112.tq: Discriminate between related administrative and military institutions of different periods.
xs: The iqta is the ancestor of the Mughal **jagir and mansab** system — option **(1)**.
**Amara Nayankara** and **Siddha Sainyam** belong to **Vijayanagara**.
xa: The Mughal jagir was tied to **mansab** rank and was **transferable**.
The iqta financed the army and integrated **distant provinces**.

112.s:
The military organisation of Vijayanagara comprised which of the following?
1. A standing Siddha Sainyam
2. A feudal Amara Nayankara army
3. A Jagirdar Sainyam headed by the Ain-ul-Mulk
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
112.x: Vijayanagara had a standing Siddha Sainyam and a feudal Amara Nayankara army. The Jagirdar Sainyam headed by the Ain-ul-Mulk belonged to the Qutb Shahi military organisation, not Vijayanagara.
112.tq: Separate institutions belonging to neighbouring kingdoms before selecting the combination.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Vijayanagara had a standing **Siddha Sainyam** and a feudal **Amara Nayankara** army.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **Jagirdar Sainyam** and **Ain-ul-Mulk** belong to the **Qutb Shahis** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **Nuniz**: Siddha Sainyam about **50,000**, paid every **4 months**.
**Thevenot** records Ain-ul-Mulk heading the Qutb Shahi army.
Kakatiya royal bodyguards = **Lenkas**.

112.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Military feature)
A. Vijayanagara
B. Qutb Shahis
C. Kakatiyas
D. Shivaji

List-II (Associated feature)
I. Lenkas as royal bodyguards
II. Standing army paid in cash
III. Siddha Sainyam and Amara Nayankara army
IV. Siddha Sainyam and Jagirdar Sainyam

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
112.x: Vijayanagara had the Siddha Sainyam and Amara Nayankara army; the Qutb Shahis had the Siddha Sainyam and Jagirdar Sainyam; Kakatiya royal bodyguards were Lenkas; and Shivaji maintained a cash-paid standing army.
112.tq: Start from the sure institutional pairs and eliminate codes with a swapped military feature.
xs: **Vijayanagara – Siddha Sainyam + Amara Nayankara** (III); **Qutb Shahis – Siddha + Jagirdar Sainyam** (IV) — option **(1)**.
**Kakatiyas – Lenkas** (I); **Shivaji – standing army paid in cash** (II).
xa: Kakatiya posts: **Gajasahini**, **Ashwasahini**.
Shivaji set up **Sindhudurg** and **Vijaydurg** naval bases.

112.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Shivaji — dependence on jagir grants for the standing army
112.x: Shivaji avoided jagir grants and maintained a standing army paid in cash. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
112.tq: Find the single reversed policy or institutional association among otherwise correct pairs.
xs: **Shivaji – dependence on jagir grants** is wrong: he **avoided jagir grants** and kept a **standing army paid in cash** — option **(3)**.
The rest are correct: **Qutb Shahis – Ain-ul-Mulk**, **Kakatiyas – Lenkas**, **Vijayanagara – Amara Nayankara**.
xa: Shivaji's naval bases: **Sindhudurg** and **Vijaydurg**.
⚠ Like **Alauddin**, Shivaji paid in cash; **Firoz** revived the jagir.

113.s: Which one of the following taxes was levied on land and was generally assessed at one-third of the produce, though it could vary from one-tenth to one-half?
113.x: Kharaj was a land tax, usually assessed at one-third of the produce, with the rate varying according to crop and region from one-tenth to one-half.
113.tq: Use the nature of the tax to distinguish land revenue from personal and religious taxes.
xs: **Kharaj** was the land tax, usually **1/3** of produce, varying from **1/10 to 1/2** by crop and region — option **(3)**.
**Khams** = **1/5** of war booty; **Zakat** = religious tax on **Muslims** (about **2.5%** of wealth); **Jizya** = poll tax on non-Muslims.
xa: Kharaj was paid by **non-Muslim cultivators** (mainly Hindu peasants).
