118.s: Which of the following commodities were state monopolies?
118.x: Salt, betel leaf and tobacco were state monopolies.
118.tq: Select the complete commodity group rather than a partially correct combination.
xs: **Salt, betel leaf and tobacco** were **state monopolies** — option **(4)**.
Diamonds came from **leased mines**, traded at **Moti Darwaza**.
xa: Other sources: **trade taxes**, **port customs**, taxes on courtesans and professions.
Chief source: **land revenue**.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about Akkanna and Madanna:
1. They were Pingali Brahmin brothers from Hanamkonda.
2. Madanna served as Mir Jumla or Diwan.
3. Akkanna served as Sar Lashkar.
4. Madanna held the titles Surya Prakasa Rao and Alampana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: All four statements are correct. Madanna was the Diwan or prime minister, while Akkanna was the Sar Lashkar or army chief.
118.tq: Check the family, offices and titles together, while avoiding the documented reversal of their roles.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Madanna and Akkanna** were **Pingali Brahmin** brothers from **Hanamkonda**.
**Madanna** = **Mir Jumla / Diwan**, titles **Surya Prakasa Rao** + **Alampana**; **Akkanna** = **Sar Lashkar**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: some notes (Block 03) **reverse** their roles.
They made an alliance with **Shivaji** (**1677**); were **murdered in 1686**.

118.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the nephews of Akkanna and Madanna?
o: Podili Linganna — governor of the Karnatak; Gopanna — tahsildar of Palvancha
Podili Linganna — tahsildar of Palvancha; Gopanna — governor of the Karnatak
Podili Linganna — Sar Lashkar; Gopanna — Mir Jumla
Podili Linganna — governor of Golconda; Gopanna — commander of the Karnatak
118.x: Podili Linganna was the governor of the Karnatak, while Kancherla Gopanna was the tahsildar of Palvancha.
118.tq: Match each nephew with his office, using the distinct administrative locations as clues.
xs: **Podili Linganna** = **governor of the Karnatak**; **Kancherla Gopanna** = **Tahsildar of Palvancha** — option **(1)**.
Option (2) swaps them; **Sar Lashkar** and **Mir Jumla** were Akkanna and Madanna themselves.
xa: Gopanna is **Bhakta Ramadasu** (Palvancha/**Bhadrachalam**), under **Abul Hasan**.
Madanna's titles: **Surya Prakasa Rao**, **Alampana**.

118.s: The murder of Akkanna and Madanna in 1686 weakened Golconda because it occurred
o: before the Qutb Shahis acquired coastal Andhra
during the establishment of the Nizam Shahi dynasty
immediately after the founding of Khirki
just before the Mughal fall of Golconda
118.x: The brothers were murdered in 1686, shortly before Golconda fell to Aurangzeb in 1687, thereby weakening the state’s administration and defence.
118.tq: Connect the event’s timing with its political consequence rather than treating it as an isolated date.
xs: The brothers were **murdered in 1686**, **just before the Mughal fall of Golconda** — option **(4)**.
**Aurangzeb** took Golconda on **21 September 1687**.
xa: Aurangzeb annexed **Bijapur** the same year (**1686**).
⚠ **1633** Nizam Shahis – **1686** Bijapur – **1687** Golconda.

118.s: The city of Hyderabad was planned by which official?
118.x: Peshwa Mir Momin Astarabadi planned Hyderabad after its foundation by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.
118.tq: Use the official–institution or official–project association.
xs: Hyderabad was planned by Peshwa **Mir Momin Astarabadi** — option **(2)**.
**Hussain Shah Wali** built Hussain Sagar; **Mir Jumla** gave the Kohinoor to Shah Jahan; **Firishta** was a historian.
xa: Capital shifted from **Golconda** in **1592**.
Original name **Bhagyanagar**; founded by **Muhammad Quli** in **1591**.

118.s:
Which statement best reflects the differing traditions concerning the name Bhagyanagar?
1. One account names Bhagirathi as the consort of Ibrahim.
2. A common legend names Bhagmati in association with Muhammad Quli.
3. Both traditions uniformly identify the same person as the source of the name.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
118.x: The two traditions identify different persons: Bhagirathi in one account and Bhagmati in the common legend. Therefore, statement 3 is incorrect.
118.tq: Spot the false statement that incorrectly merges two confusable traditions.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: one account names **Bhagirathi**, consort of **Ibrahim** — correct.
Statement 2: the common legend names **Bhagmati**, of **Muhammad Quli** — correct.
Statement 3: wrong — the two traditions name **different** persons.
xa: Full name: **Bhagyanagar-Bhagirathapuram**, linked to a Hindu consort.
**Mir Momin Astarabadi** planned the city.

118.s: The foundation stone of the Charminar was laid in which year?
118.x: The Charminar was founded in 1591; the foundation stone is specifically associated with 8 February 1591.
118.tq: Retain the exact year attached to a monument’s foundation.
xs: The **Charminar** foundation stone was laid in **1591** (**8 Feb 1591**) — option **(2)**.
Built by **Muhammad Quli** to mark the **end of a plague**.
**1562** = Hussain Sagar; **1614** = Mecca Masjid begun.
xa: It has four **Char Kaman** gateways.
⚠ **Mecca Masjid** = Muhammad Qutb Shah / Aurangzeb; **Charminar** = Muhammad Quli.

118.s:
Match List-I (Monument) with List-II (Feature):
List-I
a. Charminar
b. Golconda fort
c. Qutb Shahi tombs at Ibrahim Bagh
List-II
i. Four Char Kaman gateways
ii. Acoustics: a handclap at the gate carries to the Bala Hisar
iii. Onion domes on square bases with charbagh gardens
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
118.x: Charminar is linked with the four Char Kaman gateways, Golconda fort is famous for its acoustics (handclap at the gate heard at the Bala Hisar), and the Qutb Shahi tombs at Ibrahim Bagh have onion domes on square bases with charbagh gardens. So A. B swaps Charminar and Golconda; C swaps Charminar and the tombs; D swaps the fort and the tombs.
118.tq: Fix the unique one first: the handclap acoustics belong only to Golconda fort.
xs: **a-i, b-ii, c-iii** — option **(1)**.
**Charminar — four Char Kaman gateways**; **Golconda fort — acoustics** (handclap heard at **Bala Hisar**).
**Qutb Shahi tombs (Ibrahim Bagh) — onion domes on square bases**, charbagh gardens.
xa: Golconda fort also had **piped water**; old name **Mangalavaram/Mankal**.
**Ibrahim** built Golconda's **high walls**.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about Urdu/Dakhni literature under the Qutb Shahis:
1. Urdu literature is said to have reached its peak under Abdullah Qutb Shah.
2. Muhammad Qutb Shah is called the 'Chaucer of Urdu' in some notes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x: Statement 1 is correct: Urdu peaked under Abdullah Qutb Shah. Statement 2 is wrong: the 'Chaucer of Urdu' label found in some sources is for Ibrahim, not Muhammad Qutb Shah (whose pen name was Zillullah). Hence 1 only (A); B and C accept the wrong attribution, D rejects a correct statement.
118.tq: Chaucer of Urdu = Ibrahim; Urdu peak = Abdullah; do not confuse the similar Muhammad names.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: **Urdu** literature peaked under **Abdullah** — correct.
Statement 2: wrong — some notes call **Ibrahim** the "**Chaucer of Urdu**"; Muhammad Qutb Shah's pen name was **Zillullah**.
xa: **Muhammad Quli** wrote Dakhni/Urdu poetry as "**Maani**" (**Kulliyat-e-Quli Qutb Shah**).
Abdullah also patronised **Kshetrayya**.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about the early names associated with Hyderabad and Golconda:
1. Hyderabad was originally known as Bhagyanagar.
2. Golconda was also known by the name Mankal.
3. Mangalavaram is another name associated with old Golconda.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: Bhagyanagar is identified as the original name of Hyderabad, while Mankal and Mangalavaram are names associated with old Golconda.
118.tq: Combine closely related alternative names and test all listed associations.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Hyderabad's original name was **Bhagyanagar**.
Golconda fort's old name was **Mangalavaram / Mankal**.
xa: Golconda was the Qutb Shahi capital from **Sultan Quli**, who renamed it **Muhammadnagar**.
Capital moved to Hyderabad in **1592**.

118.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Mecca Masjid — Begun by Muhammad Qutb Shah
2. Charminar — Founded by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah
3. Hussain Sagar — Built by Hussain Shah Wali
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
118.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Mecca Masjid was begun by Muhammad Qutb Shah, the Charminar was founded by Muhammad Quli, and Hussain Sagar was built by Hussain Shah Wali.
118.tq: Verify each monument–builder pair before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All three pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Mecca Masjid** — begun by **Muhammad Qutb Shah** (**1614**); **Charminar** — **Muhammad Quli** (**1591**).
**Hussain Sagar** — built by **Hussain Shah Wali** (**1562**), in Ibrahim's reign.
xa: Mecca Masjid was completed by **Aurangzeb (1692-93)**.
Hussain Sagar = UNWTO "**Heart of the World**" (**2012**).

118.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the construction of the Mecca Masjid?
o: It was begun in 1591 and completed in 1614 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.
It was begun in 1614 by Muhammad Qutb Shah and completed by Aurangzeb in 1692–93.
It was begun by Aurangzeb in 1692 and completed by Muhammad Qutb Shah.
It was built in 1562 by Hussain Shah Wali.
118.x: Muhammad Qutb Shah began the Mecca Masjid in 1614, and Aurangzeb completed it in 1692–93.
118.tq: Separate the initiator, successor and completion date in a long construction history.
xs: Begun in **1614** by **Muhammad Qutb Shah**, completed by **Aurangzeb** in **1692-93** — option **(2)**.
Option (3) reverses the two; **1591** is the Charminar; **1562** is Hussain Sagar.
xa: **Tavernier** saw **4,000** workers on it.
Muhammad Qutb Shah's pen name: **Zillullah**.

118.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah — Kulliyat-e-Quli Qutb Shah
Ibrahim Adil Shah II — Six Travels
118.x: Kulliyat-e-Quli Qutb Shah is associated with Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah. Kitab-i-Nauras was written by Ibrahim Adil Shah II, while Six Travels was written by Tavernier.
118.tq: Discriminate between authors and works by using the sure author–title pair.
xs: **Muhammad Quli — Kulliyat-e-Quli Qutb Shah** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Kitab-i-Nauras** is by **Ibrahim Adil Shah II**; **Six Travels** by **Tavernier**; **Firishta** wrote Tarikh-i-Firishta.
xa: Muhammad Quli's pen name: **Maani**.
Ibrahim Adil Shah II invoked **Saraswati** in Kitab-i-Nauras.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about monuments associated with Hyderabad:
1. Golconda Fort was the Qutb Shahi capital from the time of Sultan Quli.
2. Ibrahim Qutb Shah built the high walls of Golconda Fort.
3. Hussain Sagar was built in 1562 during Ibrahim’s reign.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: All three statements are correct. Golconda served as the Qutb Shahi capital from Sultan Quli, Ibrahim built its high walls, and Hussain Sagar was built by Hussain Shah Wali in 1562 during Ibrahim’s reign.
118.tq: Check ruler, monument and date together instead of treating them as isolated facts.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Golconda fort** was the Qutb Shahi capital from **Sultan Quli**; **Ibrahim** built its **high walls**.
**Hussain Sagar** was built by **Hussain Shah Wali** in **1562**, in Ibrahim's reign.
xa: Golconda fort: **acoustics** (handclap heard at **Bala Hisar**) and **piped water**.
Hussain Sagar date: **1562** / **1563** — notes differ.

118.s: Tavernier visited the Andhra diamond mines during the reign of:
118.x: Tavernier visited the mines during the reign of Abdullah Qutb Shah.
118.tq: Apply the traveller–ruler association while avoiding a neighbouring ruler trap.
xs: **Tavernier** visited the Andhra diamond mines in **Abdullah Qutb Shah's** reign — option **(1)** (APPSC G2 2019).
He was a **French jeweller / diamond merchant** (**17th century**) and wrote **Six Travels**.
xa: He recorded the **Kohinoor** and saw **4,000** workers at the Mecca Masjid.
Mines: **Kollur** (Guntur), **Paritala** (Krishna), **Ramallakota** (Kurnool), **Vajrakarur** (Anantapur).

118.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kohinoor diamond:
1. It came from the Kollur mines on the Krishna.
2. It is stated to have been found in 1656.
3. Tavernier presented it to Shah Jahan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x:
Statement 1 is correct: the Kohinoor came from the Kollur mines (Guntur district, on the Krishna). Statement 2 is correct: it was found in 1656. Statement 3 is wrong: Tavernier only recorded it; Mir Jumla presented it to Shah Jahan. So 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
⚠ Sources differ: the Kohinoor's origin is uncertain; exam texts give the Kollur mine / Mir Jumla 1656 tradition. This key follows the standard view.
118.tq: Tavernier recorded, Mir Jumla presented: separate the chronicler from the giver.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: the **Kohinoor** came from the **Kollur mines** (Guntur, on the Krishna) — correct (APPSC G2 2011).
Statement 2: found in **1656** — correct.
Statement 3: wrong — **Tavernier** only recorded it; **Mir Jumla** presented it to Shah Jahan.
xa: It is now in the **British crown**, in British hands since **1849**.
Pakistan's **1976** claim was recalled in the news.

118.s: At which places were diamonds traded and polished respectively in the Golconda region?
118.x: Diamonds were traded at Moti Darwaza and polished at Karwan.
118.tq: Separate the marketplace from the place of processing in a paired-location question.
xs: Diamonds were **traded at Moti Darwaza** and **polished at Karwan** — option **(2)**.
Option (1) reverses the two; **Kollur** and **Paritala** are mines.
xa: Other mines: **Ramallakota** (Kurnool), **Vajrakarur** (Anantapur), **Malapalli**, **Gollapalli**, **Banaganapalli**.
**Golconda Blue** diamond (**23.24 ct**) was in the news **May 2025**.

118.s:
Consider the following pairs concerning European factories at Machilipatnam:
1. Dutch — 1605
2. English — 1611
3. Captain Hippon — Ship Globe
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
118.x: The Dutch factory dates to 1605, the English factory to 1611, and Captain Hippon arrived in the ship Globe. All three pairs are correct.
118.tq: Start with the sure company–year pair and verify the associated agent and vessel.
xs: All three pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Dutch** factory at Machilipatnam **1605**; **English** **1611**.
The English came under **Captain Hippon** in the ship **Globe**.
xa: The Dutch factory was the **first European factory in Andhra**.
The English came with **Muhammad Quli's** permission.

118.s: The English obtained permission to establish their presence at Machilipatnam from:
118.x: The English came to Machilipatnam with the permission of Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah. The attribution to Ibrahim Qutb Shah is chronologically inconsistent because he died in 1580.
118.tq: Use chronology to reject a ruler who could not have granted the permission.
xs: The English came to Machilipatnam with **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah's** permission — option **(1)**.
APPSC 2025 accepted "**Quli Qutub Shah**".
xa: ⚠ Trap: the **APPSC G2 2008** key gave **Ibrahim Qutb Shah**, though he died in **1580** — choose him only if Muhammad Quli is absent.
The English factory dates to **1611** (Captain **Hippon**, ship **Globe**).

118.s: Machilipatnam was particularly famous for the manufacture and trade of:
118.x: Machilipatnam was famed for muslin and Kalamkari, in addition to its importance as a trading centre.
118.tq: Identify the characteristic goods associated with a historic port.
xs: **Machilipatnam** was famed for **muslin** and **Kalamkari** — option **(1)**.
Diamonds came from the **Kollur** and other mines, traded at **Moti Darwaza**.
xa: It was leased for **1,80,000 pagodas** a year.
Port works revive the old **Gilakaladindi** port.

118.s:
Which of the following travellers, apart from Tavernier, described Golconda?
1. Thevenot
2. Bernier
3. Manucci
Select the correct answer using the code below.
118.x: Thevenot, Bernier and Manucci also described Golconda. Thevenot’s account is associated with 1666–67.
118.tq: Test a complete named list by checking all members rather than one familiar name.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Thevenot** (**1666-67**), **Bernier** and **Manucci** also described Golconda.
xa: **Tavernier**, a French jeweller, visited in **Abdullah's** reign and wrote **Six Travels**.
Tavernier also recorded the **Kohinoor**.

118.s: Who captured Ahmadnagar city and Asirgarh respectively in 1600 and 1601?
118.x: Akbar captured Ahmadnagar city in 1600 and Asirgarh of Khandesh in 1601.
118.tq: Use the ruler–conquest association to eliminate rulers connected with later Deccan campaigns.
xs: **Akbar** took **Ahmadnagar city (1600)** and **Asirgarh/Khandesh (1601)** — option **(1)**.
**Shah Jahan** ended the Nizam Shahis (**1633**); **Aurangzeb** took Bijapur (**1686**) and Golconda (**1687**).
xa: **Chand Bibi** died when Ahmadnagar fell in **1600**.
⚠ **1633** Nizam Shahis – **1686** Bijapur – **1687** Golconda.

118.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Annexation of Bijapur by Aurangzeb
B. Ahmadnagar city captured by Akbar
C. Golconda annexed as the 21st Mughal Suba
D. Nizam Shahi dynasty ended by Shah Jahan
118.x: The correct order is Ahmadnagar’s capture in 1600, the end of the Nizam Shahis in 1633, Bijapur’s annexation in 1686 and Golconda’s annexation in 1687.
118.tq: Place the events by their dates before comparing the middle positions.
xs: Order: **Ahmadnagar captured (1600) → Nizam Shahis ended (1633) → Bijapur annexed (1686) → Golconda annexed (1687)** — option **(1) B, D, A, C**.
Golconda became the Mughals' **21st Suba**.
xa: In **1636** Bijapur and Golconda signed **ahdnamas** under Shah Jahan.
Aurangzeb first attacked Golconda in **1656** as Deccan subedar.

118.s: Who opened the gates of Golconda Fort to Aurangzeb on 21 September 1687?
118.x: The gates were opened by the traitor Abdullah Khan Pani, also referred to as Abdullah Phani in the accounts.
118.tq: Use the person–deed trap by associating the gate-opening with the named traitor rather than the defender.
xs: The traitor **Abdullah Khan Pani** (Abdullah Phani) opened the gates on **21 September 1687** — option **(4)**.
**Abul Razak Lari** was honoured for **defending** Golconda; **Fath Khan** was Malik Ambar's son.
xa: Golconda became the Mughals' **21st Suba**.
Last ruler **Abul Hasan Tana Shah** was imprisoned at Bidar, then **Daulatabad**.

118.s: Abul Razak Lari was honoured for
o: negotiating the 1636 treaty with Shah Jahan
118.x: Abul Razak Lari was honoured for his defence of Golconda during the Mughal siege.
118.tq: Match the military personality with the specific deed for which he was honoured.
xs: **Abul Razak Lari** was honoured for **defending Golconda against Aurangzeb** — option **(4)**.
**Khirki** was founded by **Malik Ambar**; the **1636** deed was Abdullah's.
xa: The gates were opened by the traitor **Abdullah Khan Pani** (**21 Sept 1687**).
**Akkanna and Madanna** had been murdered in **1686**.

118.s: After the fall of Golconda in 1687, Abul Hasan Tana Shah was finally imprisoned at:
118.x: Abul Hasan Tana Shah, the last Qutb Shahi ruler, was imprisoned first at Bidar and then at Daulatabad, where he died in 1699; he was buried at Khuldabad. Gwalior, Asirgarh and Ahmadnagar were not his place of imprisonment.
118.tq: Tana Shah: Bidar -> Daulatabad; buried Khuldabad.
xs: **Abul Hasan Tana Shah** was imprisoned at **Bidar**, then **Daulatabad** — option **(2)**.
He died in **1699** (some notes **1700**) and was buried at **Khuldabad**.
**Asirgarh** and **Ahmadnagar** were taken by **Akbar**, not his prison.
xa: He was the **last** Qutb Shahi ruler (**1672-87**).
He made a treaty with **Shivaji** (**1677**).

118.s: The first European factory established in Andhra was set up by the:
118.x: The Dutch established the first European factory in Andhra at Machilipatnam in 1605.
118.tq: Test the combined identity-place-year link directly.
xs: The **Dutch** set up the first European factory in Andhra at **Machilipatnam in 1605** — option **(4)**.
The **English** came to Machilipatnam later, in **1611**.
xa: Both came with **Muhammad Quli's** permission.
**First Qutb Shahi to mint coins**: **Ibrahim**.

118.s: Machilipatnam port works are associated with the revival of which historical port facility of the Golconda period?
118.x: The revival of Machilipatnam port is linked with the historical Gilakaladindi port, which functioned as a transshipment hub under the Golconda dynasty.
118.tq: Connect the present development with its historical institution and location.
xs: Machilipatnam port works revive the old **Gilakaladindi** port — option **(1)**.
It was a **transhipment hub** under the **Golconda dynasty**.
xa: Machilipatnam was famed for **muslin** and **Kalamkari**.
It had the **Dutch (1605)** and **English (1611)** factories.

118.s: With reference to the Kohinoor, which of the following statements is correct?
o: Pakistan claimed it in 1976, and it has been in British hands since 1849.
Afghanistan claimed it in 1976, and it has been in British hands since 1849.
Pakistan claimed it in 1984, and it has been in British hands since 1947.
Pakistan claimed it in 1947, and it has been in British hands since 1857.
118.x: Pakistan made a claim to the Kohinoor in 1976, while the diamond has been in British hands since 1849.
118.tq: Discriminate between closely related claim-year and possession-year pairs.
xs: **Pakistan** claimed the Kohinoor in **1976**; it has been in **British** hands since **1849** — option **(1)**.
The claim was recalled on **8 Sep 2026**.
xa: The Kohinoor came from the **Kollur mines** (APPSC G2 2011), found in **1656**.
**Mir Jumla** presented it to **Shah Jahan**; **Tavernier** recorded it.

118.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Hussain Sagar:
1. It was named after Hussain Shah Wali.
2. It was built under Ibrahim.
3. It was declared the UNWTO ‘Heart of the World’ in 2012.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: Hussain Sagar was named after Hussain Shah Wali, built under Ibrahim, and received the UNWTO designation ‘Heart of the World’ in 2012.
118.tq: Check each statement independently, especially the name, patron, and recognition-year details.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Hussain Sagar** is named after **Hussain Shah Wali** and was built under **Ibrahim**.
It was declared the UNWTO "**Heart of the World**" (**2012**).
xa: Date given as **1562** / **1563** — notes differ.
The **Ibrahimpatnam** tank also dates from Ibrahim's reign.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about the Bonalu festival of Telangana:
1. It began at the Jagadamba Mahankali temple inside Golconda fort.
2. Its roots are traced to the Vijayanagara and Mughal periods.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x: Statement 1 is correct: Bonalu began at the Jagadamba Mahankali temple inside Golconda fort. Statement 2 is wrong: its roots go back to the Kakatiya and Qutb Shahi periods, not Vijayanagara and Mughal. So 1 only (A); B and C accept the wrong period, D rejects the correct temple link.
118.tq: Bonalu: Golconda fort temple, Kakatiya + Qutb Shahi roots - both Telangana-centred.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: **Bonalu** began at the **Jagadamba Mahankali temple inside Golconda fort** — correct.
Statement 2: wrong — it goes back to the **Kakatiya + Qutb Shahi** periods.
xa: Muharram was celebrated as **Peerla Panduga**.
Golconda fort's old name: **Mangalavaram / Mankal**.

118.s: Which of the following sets consists entirely of Hindus who held high office under the Qutb Shahis?
o: Murari Rao, Jagadeva Rao and Madanna
Hussain Shah Wali, Ibrahim and Madanna
Murari Rao, Abul Hasan and Jagadeva Rao
Madanna, Muhammad Quli and Jagadeva Rao
118.x: Murari Rao, Jagadeva Rao and Madanna are identified as Hindus who held high office under the Qutb Shahis.
118.tq: Eliminate options containing rulers or other non-matching personalities and retain the complete administrative trio.
xs: **Murari Rao**, **Jagadeva Rao** and **Madanna** were Hindus in high office — option **(1)**.
**Hussain Shah Wali**, **Ibrahim**, **Abul Hasan** and **Muhammad Quli** were Muslims.
xa: Madanna was **Mir Jumla / Diwan**; his brother **Akkanna** was **Sar Lashkar**.
**Mustajirs** (tax farmers) were also **mostly Hindus**.

118.s: During the Qutb Shahi period, Muharram came to be celebrated in Andhra as:
118.x: Muharram came to be celebrated as Peerla Panduga during the Qutb Shahi period.
118.tq: Separate closely associated regional festival names by linking the specific festival with its religious occasion.
xs: **Muharram** was celebrated as **Peerla Panduga** — option **(2)**.
**Bonalu** is a separate Telangana festival begun at Golconda fort.
xa: Hindus held high office (**Murari Rao**, **Jagadeva Rao**, **Madanna**).
The Qutb Shahis united the Telugu lands for the **third time**.

119.s: Who was the father of Harihara and Bukka, the founders of the Vijayanagara ruling house?
119.x: Sangama, the father of Harihara and Bukka, was a Kakatiya chief. The brothers had served the Kakatiyas before founding Vijayanagara in 1336.
119.tq: Use the dynastic legacy link rather than confusing the Kakatiya chief with a later ruler.
xs: Harihara and Bukka were sons of **Sangama** — option **(4)**; hence the **Sangama dynasty**.
On the **Kakatiya** theory, **Sangama** was a **Kakatiya chief** (APPSC G2 2005 key).
xa: Sangama came from "**Mangalanilaya**"; placed in the **Kuruba** clan (also given as Kuruba/Yadava).
The brothers founded Vijayanagara in **1336** on the **southern bank of the Tungabhadra**.
Exam angle: **APPSC** treats the **Kakatiya link** as the correct answer.

119.s: The Kakatiya-service theory regarding Harihara and Bukka holds that they had served under:
119.x: The Kakatiya theory states that Harihara and Bukka served Prataparudra of Warangal before being taken to Delhi after 1323.
119.tq: Apply the ruler–regional power association without confusing it with the Kampili or Hoysala theories.
xs: The Kakatiya-service theory says they served **Prataparudra of Warangal** — option **(1)**.
After **1323** they were taken to **Delhi** and converted.
Service under **Veera Ballala III** is the **Kannada/Hoysala** theory; service to **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** is the Delhi version.
xa: **APPSC G2 2005** key: Sangama was "**a Kakatiya chief**".
There are **7 theories** of origin; **Sewell** records **seven** local traditions.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about the versions of Harihara and Bukka's early career:
1. In the Kampili version, they governed Kampili, were captured by Muhammad bin Tughlaq, converted in Delhi and sent back as Sultanate governors.
2. In the Delhi-service version, Muhammad bin Tughlaq sent them to crush Deccan rebels such as Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka and Prolaya Vema.
3. In the Kampili version, they were officers of Veera Ballala III.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statement 1 is correct: this is the Kampili version. Statement 2 is correct: the Delhi-service version has Tughlaq sending them against Deccan rebels (Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka, Prolaya Vema). Statement 3 is wrong: service under Veera Ballala III is the Kannada/Hoysala theory, not the Kampili version. So 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include statement 3.
119.tq: Keep each theory to its patron: Kampili/Tughlaq, Kakatiya/Prataparudra, Hoysala/Ballala III.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Kampili** version — governed Kampili, captured by **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**, converted, sent back as governors — correct.
Statement 2: **Delhi-service** version — sent against **Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka** and **Prolaya Vema** — correct.
Statement 3: wrong — service under **Veera Ballala III** is the **Kannada/Hoysala** theory.
xa: After defeat they met **Vidyaranya** near **Pampa** and returned to Hinduism.
They founded **Anegondi** in the name of **Virupaksha**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about the theories concerning the origin of the Vijayanagara founders:
1. The Kannada or Hoysala theory associates them with Veera Ballala III.
2. The Andhra theory is associated with scholars such as N. Venkataramanaiah, Sewell and Nilakanta Sastri.
3. Robert Sewell recorded seven local founding traditions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: All three statements are correct. The Kannada/Hoysala theory links them with Veera Ballala III, the Andhra theory has the listed scholarly supporters, and Sewell recorded seven local traditions.
119.tq: Test several competing origin theories together rather than relying on one familiar association.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Kannada/Hoysala** theory: officers of **Veera Ballala III** — correct.
**Andhra** theory: **N. Venkataramanaiah, Sewell, Nilakanta Sastri** — correct; **Sewell** recorded **seven** traditions — correct.
xa: ⚠ **Sewell** appears twice: records the seven traditions + backs the **Andhra** theory.
Kannada theory backers: **Father Heras**, **Rice**, **S.K. Ayyangar**, **H. Krishna Sastri**, **P.B. Desai**.

119.s: Who among the following is associated with the Kannada or Hoysala theory of the origin of Harihara and Bukka?
119.x: Father Heras, Rice, S. K. Ayyangar, H. Krishna Sastri and P. B. Desai supported the Kannada or Hoysala theory.
119.tq: Separate the scholars supporting the Kannada/Hoysala theory from those associated with the Andhra theory.
xs: **Father Heras** backs the **Kannada/Hoysala** theory — option **(2)**.
**N. Venkataramanaiah**, **Nilakanta Sastri** and **Sewell** back the **Andhra** theory.
xa: Other Kannada-theory backers: **Rice**, **S.K. Ayyangar**, **H. Krishna Sastri**, **P.B. Desai**.
The theory makes them officers of **Veera Ballala III**.
Heras also wrote **The Aravidu Dynasty of Vijayanagara**.

119.s: The first inscription to call Harihara I a king was the:
119.x: The Nellore inscription is regarded as the first inscription to call Harihara I a king; it dates his reign to 1336–1355.
119.tq: Match the inscription with the precise historical claim associated with it.
xs: The first record to call Harihara I king is the **Nellore inscription** — option **(3)**.
It dates his reign **1336-1355**.
xa: First seat of the kingdom: **Anegondi**.
Harihara I was crowned on **18 April 1336** at the **Virupaksha** temple.
The city was completed by **1343** (some notes: entered **1344**).

119.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the founding location of Vijayanagara?
o: It was founded on the northern bank of the Tungabhadra in 1323.
It was founded on the southern bank of the Godavari in 1346.
It was founded on the northern bank of the Krishna near Warangal.
It was founded on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra in 1336.
119.x: The Vijayanagara kingdom was founded in 1336 on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra.
119.tq: Use the river-bank and year together to reject reversed-location options.
xs: Vijayanagara was founded in **1336** on the **southern bank of the Tungabhadra** — option **(4)**.
**1323** is the fall of Warangal; **1346** is the Sringeri visit after the Hoysala victory.
xa: ⚠ **1336** = founding + coronation (**18 April**); **1343** = city completed; **1346** = Sringeri visit.
It was built as a **Giri Durga** on **Ramadurga** hill; ruins at **Hampi**.

119.s: In the founding legend, after being defeated while suppressing the Deccan rebellion, Harihara and Bukka met Vidyaranya near:
119.x: The legend places their meeting with Vidyaranya near Pampa after their defeat in the Deccan campaign.
119.tq: Link the event in the legend with its geographical setting.
xs: They met **Vidyaranya** near **Pampa** — option **(3)**.
Vidyaranya headed the **Sringeri** math and returned them to Hinduism.
**Penukonda** and **Chandragiri** were later capitals after Talikota; **Kalyani** is the Saluva home.
xa: They then founded **Anegondi** in the name of **Virupaksha**.
**Hampi (Pampa)**: family deity **Virupaksha**; ruins of Vijayanagara.

119.s: Vidyaranya, who is associated with the reconversion of Harihara and Bukka, was the head of the:
119.x: Vidyaranya headed the Sringeri Shankara Math and is associated with the brothers' return to Hinduism.
119.tq: Match the religious institution with its associated spiritual leader.
xs: **Vidyaranya** headed the **Sringeri Shankara Math** — option **(4)**.
He **reconverted** the brothers to Hinduism before the **1336** coronation.
xa: The brothers visited **Sringeri** in **1346** after the **Hoysala** victory.
He wrote the **Vidyaranya Kalajnana**; his brother **Sayana** was minister of Harihara II.
⚠ **Madhava-Vidyaranya** (Advaita head) ≠ **Madhava** the minister who took **Goa**.

119.s: Which of the following correctly represents the sequence in the founding legend?
o: Fall of Warangal → conversion in Delhi → dispatch against Deccan rebels → meeting with Vidyaranya → return to Hinduism
Meeting with Vidyaranya → fall of Warangal → conversion in Delhi → foundation of Anegondi
Conversion in Delhi → fall of Warangal → visit to Sringeri → appointment by Prataparudra
Foundation of Anegondi → conversion in Delhi → fall of Warangal → meeting with Vidyaranya
119.x: The legend proceeds from the fall of Warangal and conversion in Delhi to the Deccan campaign, meeting Vidyaranya, and return to Hinduism.
119.tq: Arrange the narrative by identifying the first event and following the linked sequence.
xs: Sequence: **fall of Warangal → conversion in Delhi → sent against Deccan rebels → met Vidyaranya → return to Hinduism** — option **(1)**.
Then they founded **Anegondi** in the name of **Virupaksha**.
xa: The meeting took place near **Pampa**.
Harihara I was crowned **18 April 1336**.

119.s: Anegondi is significant in the early history of Vijayanagara because it was:
o: The site of the Sringeri Shankara Math
The place where Saluva Narasimha began the first usurpation
The first seat of the kingdom, established in the name of Sri Virupaksha
The final capital of the Aravidu dynasty
119.x: Anegondi was the first seat of the kingdom, and it was set up in the name of Sri Virupaksha.
119.tq: Distinguish the founders' first seat from later dynastic capitals and religious centres.
xs: **Anegondi** was the **first seat** of the kingdom, set up "**in the name of Sri Virupaksha**" — option **(3)**.
**Harihara I** later moved the capital from Anegondi to **Vijayanagara**.
**Saluva Narasimha** was lord of **Chandragiri**; the Aravidu capitals were **Penukonda, Chandragiri, Vellore**.
xa: Vidyaranya headed **Sringeri**, not Anegondi.
City completed by **1343**.

119.s: According to the legend associated with the selection of the capital site, a hare:
o: Turned on the royal hunting dogs
Was offered to the deity Virupaksha
Led the royal hunting party to Sringeri
Crossed the Tungabhadra during a battle
119.x: The site was considered a place of valour because a hare reportedly turned on the royal hunting dogs.
119.tq: Use the unusual legend detail to distinguish the correct option from plausible religious associations.
xs: In the legend, a **hare turned on the royal hunting dogs** — option **(1)**.
So the site was chosen as a **place of valour**.
xa: Emblem: **Varaha** (boar).
Founded **1336** on the **southern bank of the Tungabhadra**.

119.s: The ruins of Vijayanagar are located at which present-day site?
119.x: The ruins of Vijayanagar are located at Hampi.
119.tq: Ancient capital–present archaeological site association.
xs: The ruins of Vijayanagara are at **Hampi** — option **(3)**.
**Anegondi** was the first seat; **Penukonda** and **Chandragiri** were later capitals.
xa: The city had **7 stone ramparts** and measured **14 x 10 miles**.
Hampi (**Pampa**): family deity **Virupaksha**.

119.s: Who built a dam across the Tungabhadra and arranged canals to carry water to the capital?
119.x: Devaraya I built a dam across the Tungabhadra and canals to carry water to Vijayanagar.
119.tq: Identify the ruler responsible for a specific public-works project.
xs: **Devaraya I** built a **dam on the Tungabhadra** with canals to the city — option **(3)**.
He also strengthened the city **walls**.
xa: He fought **Firuz Shah** at **Mudgal**; **Nicolo Conti** visited.
One source calls him the **first to recruit Muslims**.

119.s: After the battle of Talikota, the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire was shifted in which sequence?
119.x: After Talikota, the capital moved from Hampi to Penukonda and subsequently to Chandragiri; both later capitals were in present-day Andhra Pradesh.
119.tq: Follow the first and second capital shifts in sequence.
xs: After Talikota: **Hampi → Penukonda → Chandragiri** — option **(2)**.
Both **Penukonda** and **Chandragiri** are in **AP**.
xa: The **Aravidu** capitals were **Penukonda, Chandragiri, Vellore**.
**Talikota (1565)**: Deccan sultanates defeated **Rama Raya**.

119.s: The name 'Vijayanagara', the capital built by Harihara and Bukka on the south bank of the Tungabhadra, means:
119.x: Vijayanagara means 'City of Victory'; it was built on the south bank of the Tungabhadra and its ruins lie at Hampi. 'City of Learning', 'City of Gold' and 'City of the Boar' are not meanings of the name (the boar, Varaha, was the royal emblem, not the city's name).
119.tq: Vijaya = victory, nagara = city.
xs: **Vijayanagara** means "**City of Victory**" — option **(1)**.
The **boar (Varaha)** was the royal **emblem**, not the city's name.
xa: Built on the **south bank of the Tungabhadra**; ruins at **Hampi**.
**7 stone ramparts**; completed by **1343**.

119.s:
Arrange the following Vijayanagara dynasties in chronological order of their rule:
A. Tuluva
B. Aravidu
C. Sangama
D. Saluva
119.x: The dynastic order was Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva and Aravidu.
119.tq: Fix the first dynasty and then place the successive dynasties in their established order.
xs: Order: **Sangama → Saluva → Tuluva → Aravidu** — option **(1) C, D, A, B**.
xa: ⚠ **S-S-T-A**; Sangama + Aravidu = **Andhra** origin.
**Sangama** ruled longest.

119.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Dynasty)
a. Sangama
b. Saluva
c. Tuluva
d. Aravidu

List-II (Founder)
i. Tirumala Raya
ii. Saluva Narasimha
iii. Harihara I and Bukka I
iv. Vira Narasimha

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
119.x: Sangama was founded by Harihara I and Bukka I, Saluva by Saluva Narasimha, Tuluva by Vira Narasimha, and Aravidu by Tirumala Raya.
119.tq: Start with the sure founder–dynasty pair and complete the one-to-one matching.
xs: **a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i** — option **(1)**.
**Sangama — Harihara I and Bukka I**; **Saluva — Saluva Narasimha**.
**Tuluva — Vira Narasimha** (APPSC G2 2002 key); **Aravidu — Tirumala Raya**.
xa: Some notes call **Tuluva Narasa Nayaka** (his father) the Tuluva founder.
Aravidu origin: **Araviti**, Kurnool.

119.s: The first usurpation in the history of the Vijayanagara Empire is associated with:
o: Saluva Narasimha and the Saluva dynasty
Harihara I and the Sangama dynasty
Tirumala Raya and the Aravidu dynasty
Vira Narasimha and the Tuluva dynasty
119.x: Saluva Narasimha ended the Sangama line and established the Saluva dynasty, an event described as the first usurpation.
119.tq: Match the political event ‘first usurpation’ with its ruler and dynasty.
xs: The **first usurpation** = **Saluva Narasimha**, founding the **Saluva** dynasty — option **(1)**.
In **1485** he expelled **Praudha Raya** with **Tuluva Narasa Nayaka's** help.
xa: He was lord of **Chandragiri**; clan from **Kalyana**.
**Annamacharya** (**1408-1503**) was his contemporary.

119.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Tuluva dynasty is correct?
o: Tirumala Raya founded the Tuluva dynasty at Chandragiri.
Krishnadevaraya founded the Tuluva dynasty in 1570.
Vira Narasimha was crowned in 1505 after executing Immadi Narasimha.
Tuluva Narasa Nayaka was crowned in 1485 after defeating Saluva Narasimha.
119.x: The APPSC-associated account identifies Vira Narasimha as the founder; he was crowned in 1505 after executing Immadi Narasimha. Tuluva Narasa Nayaka was his father and is also called the dynasty founder in another historiographical usage.
119.tq: Separate the formal APPSC founder attribution from the alternative genealogical description of Tuluva Narasa Nayaka.
xs: **Vira Narasimha** was crowned in **1505** after executing **Immadi Narasimha** — option **(3)**.
**Tirumala Raya** founded the **Aravidu**; **Krishnadevaraya** reigned **1509-29**; **1485** is Saluva Narasimha's usurpation.
xa: ⚠ APPSC key names **Veera Narasimha** as Tuluva founder; some notes give his father **Tuluva Narasa Nayaka**.

119.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the Aravidu dynasty?
o: Founder—Tirumala Raya; capitals—Penukonda, Chandragiri and Vellore
119.x: Tirumala Raya founded the Aravidu dynasty, whose capitals included Penukonda, Chandragiri and Vellore.
119.tq: Check both the founder and the capital list before selecting the complete pair.
xs: **Aravidu**: founder **Tirumala Raya**; capitals **Penukonda, Chandragiri, Vellore** — option **(1)**.
**Saluva Narasimha** founded the Saluva; **Vira Narasimha** the Tuluva; **Bukka I** co-founded the Sangama.
xa: Aravidu origin: **Andhra** (**Araviti**, Kurnool).
Span **1570-1680** in one source.

119.s: Which dynasty of Vijayanagara ruled for the longest period and had Devaraya II as its greatest ruler and Praudha Raya as its last ruler?
119.x: The Sangama dynasty was the longest-ruling dynasty; Devaraya II was regarded as its greatest ruler and Praudha Raya as its last ruler.
119.tq: Combine the duration, greatest ruler and last ruler to identify the dynasty.
xs: The **Sangama** dynasty ruled longest; greatest king **Devaraya II**, last **Praudha Raya** — option **(3)**.
xa: ⚠ **Harihara II** = longest-reigning Sangama king; **Sangama** = longest-ruling dynasty.
Praudha Raya was expelled by **Saluva Narasimha** in **1485**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the religious affiliation and emblem of the Vijayanagara dynasties:
1. The emblem was the Varaha or boar.
2. The Sangamas were Shaiva.
3. The later three dynasties were Vaishnava.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: The Vijayanagara emblem was the Varaha. The Sangama rulers were Shaiva, while the Saluva, Tuluva and Aravidu dynasties were associated with Vaishnavism.
119.tq: Test the common emblem separately from the Shaiva–Vaishnava dynastic distinction.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The emblem was the **Varaha** (boar); the **Sangamas** were **Shaiva**; the later **three** dynasties were **Vaishnava**.
xa: **Devaraya I's** coronation copper plates (Apr **2025**) carry a **Vamana** seal instead of the usual **Varaha**.
The family deity was **Virupaksha**.

119.s: Which ruler shifted the capital of the Vijayanagara kingdom from Anegondi to Vijayanagara?
119.x: Harihara I shifted the capital from Anegondi to Vijayanagara.
119.tq: Direct ruler–achievement recall.
xs: **Harihara I** moved the capital from **Anegondi** to **Vijayanagara** — option **(1)**.
**Bukka I** completed the city; **Devaraya I** built the dam.
xa: Harihara I annexed the **Hoysala** kingdom (**1346**) and the **Kadambas** (**1347**).
Title: **Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Harihara I:
1. He annexed the Hoysala kingdom in 1346.
2. He annexed the Kadamba territory in 1347.
3. He took Udayagiri himself in 1343.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Harihara I annexed the Hoysala kingdom in 1346 and the Kadambas in 1347. Udayagiri was taken by Bukka, not Harihara I, in 1343.
119.tq: Separate the ruler from the achievement attributed to his associate.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Harihara I annexed the **Hoysala** kingdom (**1346**) and the **Kadambas** (**1347**).
Statement 3 is wrong: **Bukka** took **Udayagiri** (**1343**).
xa: **Ibn Battuta** visited in Harihara I's reign — the first foreign traveller.
Title: **Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati**.

119.s: The title ‘Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati’ was assumed by which Vijayanagara ruler?
119.x: Harihara I bore the title ‘Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati’.
119.tq: Direct title–ruler matching.
xs: **Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati** was **Harihara I's** title — option **(4)**.
**Devaraya II** = **Gajabetekara**; **Bukka I** = **Vedamarga Pratishthapaka**; **Harihara II** = **Rajavyasa, Rajavalmiki**.
xa: ⚠ **Dakshina Samudradhipati** = **Lakkanna Dandanayaka**.
Harihara I reigned **1336-56**.

119.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
119.x: Devaraya I ruled from 1406 to 1422. The period 1422–1446 belongs to Devaraya II.
119.tq: Check the reign-period pair before accepting the familiar ruler name.
xs: **Devaraya I — 1422-1446** is wrong — option **(4)**; Devaraya I ruled **1406-22**.
**1422-46** is **Devaraya II's** reign.
Others correct: **Harihara II 1377-1404**, **Harihara I 1336-56**, **Bukka I 1356-77**.
xa: One source dates Bukka I from **1351/52**.
Harihara II = **longest-reigning** Sangama king.

119.s:
Bukka I is associated with which combination of achievements?
1. Completion of the city of Vijayanagara
2. Conquest of Madurai
3. Reconciliation of Jains and Vaishnavas
4. Construction of the Ganigitti Jain temple
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
119.x: Bukka I completed the city, conquered Madurai and reconciled Jains and Vaishnavas. The Ganigitti Jain temple was built by Irugappa, minister of Harihara II.
119.tq: Identify the one achievement shifted from one Sangama ruler to another.
xs: Items 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**Bukka I** **completed the city**, conquered **Madurai** and **reconciled Jains and Vaishnavas** (Shravanabelagola inscription).
Item 4 is wrong: the **Ganigitti Jain temple** was built by **Irugappa**, minister of Harihara II.
xa: Bukka sent an **embassy to Ming China (1374)**.
He took **Srisailam** and **Dupadu**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about Harihara II:
1. He was the longest-reigning Sangama king.
2. He bore the titles Rajavyasa and Rajavalmiki.
3. He bore the title Gajabetekara.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statement 1 is correct: Harihara II (1377-1404) had the longest Sangama reign. Statement 2 is correct: Rajavyasa and Rajavalmiki were his titles. Statement 3 is wrong: Gajabetekara (elephant hunter) was the title of Devaraya II. So 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include statement 3.
119.tq: Literary titles (Vyasa, Valmiki) = Harihara II; elephant hunter = Devaraya II.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
**Harihara II** (**1377-1404**) was the **longest-reigning** Sangama king, titled **Rajavyasa** and **Rajavalmiki**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Gajabetekara** was **Devaraya II's** title.
xa: He was the **first to attack Sri Lanka**.
His minister was **Sayana**.

119.s: Who built the Ganigitti Jain temple and wrote the Navaratnamala?
119.x: Irugappa, the minister of Harihara II, built the Ganigitti Jain temple and wrote Navaratnamala.
119.tq: Match the minister with both his architectural and literary work.
xs: **Irugappa**, minister of Harihara II, built the **Ganigitti Jain temple** and wrote **Navaratnamala** — option **(4)**.
**Sayana** wrote Vedartha Prakasha; **Saluva Mangu** killed the Madurai Sultan; **Lakkanna** collected Sri Lankan tribute.
xa: Harihara II's reign saw the famine "**Durgadevi Karamu**".
**Bukka I** reconciled **Jains and Vaishnavas**.

119.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Devaraya I — Dam across the Tungabhadra
2. Devaraya I — War with Firuz Shah
3. Devaraya I — First recruitment of Muslims into the army
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
119.x: Devaraya I built a dam and canals, fought Firuz Shah and is recorded as the first Sangama ruler to recruit Muslims into the army.
119.tq: Combine several achievements of one ruler before selecting the code.
xs: All three pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Devaraya I** built the **Tungabhadra dam**, fought **Firuz Shah** (Mudgal), and one source calls him **first to recruit Muslims**.
xa: He gave his daughter to **Firoz Shah Bahmani** with **Bankapur** as dowry — "**War of the Goldsmith's Daughter**".
**Devaraya II** enrolled **10,000 Muslim soldiers**.

119.s: Who led the conquest of Madurai during the reign of Bukka I?
119.x: Kumara Kampana, son of Bukka I, overthrew Sambhuvaraya in 1366 and destroyed the Madurai Sultanate.
119.tq: Direct identification of the commander in a dynastic conquest.
xs: **Kumara Kampana**, Bukka I's son, led the **Madurai** conquest — option **(1)**.
He overthrew **Sambhuvaraya** (**1366**) and destroyed the **Madurai Sultanate**.
xa: General **Saluva Mangu** killed the Sultan — title "**Parapakshi Saluva**".
Kampana's wife **Gangadevi** wrote **Madhura Vijayam**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Kumara Kampana overthrew Sambhuvaraya in 1366.
2. Saluva Mangu killed the Sultan of Madurai.
3. Saluva Mangu received the title ‘Parapakshi Saluva’.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: All three statements are correct. Kampana led the conquest, while General Saluva Mangu killed the Sultan and received the title ‘Parapakshi Saluva’.
119.tq: Test a conquest through its date, commander and associated title.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Kumara Kampana** overthrew **Sambhuvaraya** in **1366**.
**Saluva Mangu** killed the **Sultan of Madurai** and got the title "**Parapakshi Saluva**".
xa: Saluva Mangu was an **ancestor of Saluva Narasimha**.
The campaign is told in **Madhura Vijayam** by **Gangadevi**.

119.s: Who wrote Madhura Vijayam?
119.x: Madhura Vijayam, a Sanskrit work describing the Madurai conquest, was written by Gangadevi, the wife of Kumara Kampana.
119.tq: Author–work recall with nearby literary distractors.
xs: **Madhura Vijayam** (Sanskrit) was written by **Gangadevi** — option **(4)** (PYQ 2012).
**Rajanatha Dindima** wrote **Saluvabhyudayam**; **Pinaveerabhadra** wrote **Jaimini Bharatam**; **Nachana Somana** wrote **Uttara Harivamsam**.
xa: Gangadevi was the wife of **Kumara Kampana**, daughter-in-law of **Bukka I**, a **disciple of Agastya**.
It narrates the defeat of **Champaraya of Tondaimandalam**, the advance to **Kanchi** and the conquest of Madurai.

119.s: Bukka I sent an embassy to the Ming emperor of China in which year?
119.x: Bukka I sent an embassy to the Ming emperor in 1374.
119.tq: Direct year recall using four distinct chronological values.
xs: **Bukka I** sent an embassy to the **Ming emperor of China** in **1374** — option **(2)**.
**1366** = Kampana overthrew Sambhuvaraya; **1424** = Kondaveedu annexed; **1443** = Abdur Razzaq's visit.
xa: Bukka's title: **Vedamarga Pratishthapaka**.
He patronised **Nachana Somana**.

119.s: The title 'Vedamarga Pratishthapaka' was borne by which Sangama ruler?
119.x: Bukka I (1356-77) bore the title Vedamarga Pratishthapaka. Harihara I's title was Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati; Harihara II was called Rajavyasa and Rajavalmiki; Devaraya II was Gajabetekara.
119.tq: Bukka - Vedas (Sayana-Madhava commentaries began under him) - Vedamarga.
xs: **Vedamarga Pratishthapaka** was **Bukka I's** title — option **(2)**.
**Harihara I** = Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati; **Harihara II** = Rajavyasa, Rajavalmiki; **Devaraya II** = Gajabetekara.
xa: Bukka patronised **Nachana Somana** (Uttara Harivamsam), granted agrahara **Penchikaladinne**.
The **Sayana-Madhava** Vedic commentaries began **under Bukka Raya I** (APPSC G2 2008 key).

119.s:
Match List-I (Author) with List-II (Work):
List-I
a. Sayana
b. Vidyaranya
c. Nachana Somana
List-II
i. Uttara Harivamsam
ii. Vedartha Prakasha
iii. Vidyaranya Kalajnana
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
119.x: Sayana (brother of Vidyaranya, minister of Harihara II) wrote the Vedic commentary Vedartha Prakasha; Vidyaranya wrote the Vidyaranya Kalajnana; Nachana Somana, patronised by the first two Sangama kings, wrote Uttara Harivamsam. So A. B swaps Sayana and Vidyaranya; C and D give the Telugu Uttara Harivamsam to the wrong author.
119.tq: Vedic commentary = Sayana; the Kalajnana carries Vidyaranya's own name; Uttara Harivamsam is the Telugu work.
xs: **a-ii, b-iii, c-i** — option **(1)**.
**Sayana — Vedartha Prakasha**; **Vidyaranya — Vidyaranya Kalajnana**; **Nachana Somana — Uttara Harivamsam**.
xa: Sayana was **Vidyaranya's brother** and **minister of Harihara II**.
Nachana Somana was patronised by the **first two** Sangama kings.

119.s:
With reference to the Vedic commentaries associated with the early Vijayanagara rulers, consider the following statements:
1. The work was initiated under Bukka Raya I.
2. The work continued under Harihara II.
3. Sayana served as a minister of Harihara II.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: The Vedic commentaries were produced under Bukka Raya I and continued under Harihara II, during whose reign Sayana served as minister.
119.tq: Combine the ruler, continuation and minister facts before selecting the coded option.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Sayana + Madhava's** Vedic commentaries began **under Bukka Raya I** (APPSC G2 2008 key) and continued under **Harihara II**.
**Sayana** was **minister of Harihara II**.
xa: Sayana's commentary: **Vedartha Prakasha**.
Bukka's title **Vedamarga Pratishthapaka** fits this Vedic patronage.

119.s: Madhava, the minister and general associated with the conquest of Goa, was known by which title?
119.x: Madhava was known by the title Bhuvanaikavira in connection with his military achievement and conquest of Goa.
119.tq: Test the title–person association rather than the broader event.
xs: **Madhava**, minister/general who conquered **Goa**, was titled **"Bhuvanaikavira"** — option **(1)**.
He is distinct from **Madhava-Vidyaranya**, Advaita head of Sringeri; some notes merge the two.
xa: Goa was taken in **1366** and lost to the Bahmanis in **1472**.
Sayana and Madhava wrote **Vedic commentaries**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about Gangadevi and Madhura Vijayam:
1. Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam in Sanskrit.
2. Gangadevi was the wife of Bukka I.
3. Madhura Vijayam describes Kumara Kampana's southern campaign, including the defeat of Champaraya of Tondaimandalam and the conquest of Madurai.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statement 1 is correct: Madhura Vijayam is a Sanskrit work by Gangadevi. Statement 2 is wrong: she was the wife of Kumara Kampana and the daughter-in-law of Bukka I. Statement 3 is correct: the work narrates Kampana's campaign, the defeat of Champaraya of Tondaimandalam, the advance to Kanchi and the conquest of Madurai. So 1 and 3 only (C); A, B and D include statement 2.
119.tq: Gangadevi = Kampana's wife, Bukka's daughter-in-law: the relation is the usual trap.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: **Gangadevi** wrote **Madhura Vijayam** in **Sanskrit** — correct.
Statement 2: wrong — she was the wife of **Kumara Kampana**, **daughter-in-law** of Bukka I.
Statement 3: it narrates Kampana's campaign, defeat of **Champaraya of Tondaimandalam** and conquest of **Madurai** — correct.
xa: She was a **disciple of Agastya**.
Kampana overthrew **Sambhuvaraya** in **1366**.

119.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Devaraya II’s military policy is correct?
1. He enrolled 10,000 Muslim soldiers.
2. Muslims received jagirs and a mosque.
3. He kept a Quran near his throne.
4. He improved cavalry and archery.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
119.x: All four statements describe Devaraya II’s army reforms and accommodation of Muslim soldiers.
119.tq: Use the complete military-policy cluster rather than an isolated reform.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Devaraya II** enrolled **10,000 Muslim soldiers** (APPSC G2 2011 key), gave them **jagirs** and a **mosque**.
He kept a **Quran** near his throne and improved **cavalry and archery**.
xa: Titles: **Gajabetekara**, **Praudha Devaraya**, **Ilanti Raikonda**.
He was the **greatest** Sangama ruler (**1422-46**).

119.s:
Which of the following observations is associated with Abdur Razzaq’s account of Vijayanagara?
1. Open diamond bazaars
2. Three hundred ports
3. Taxation of prostitution
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
119.x: Abdur Razzaq described the open diamond bazaars, the large number of ports and the taxation of prostitution.
119.tq: Cluster the distinctive details of one foreign traveller’s account.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Abdur Razzaq** noted **open diamond bazaars**, **300 ports** and **taxed prostitution**.
xa: He was the Persian envoy of **Shah Rukh**, **1443**, in **Devaraya II's** reign.
**Paes** and **Barbosa** came under **Krishnadevaraya**; **Nuniz** under **Achyutaraya**.

119.s: Which statement best resolves the association of Nicolo Conti with the Vijayanagara rulers?
o: He visited under Devaraya I, while some examination references associate him with Devaraya II.
He visited only during the reign of Bukka I and never during the Sangama period.
He visited Vijayanagara after the Talikota battle.
He was a Persian envoy of Shah Rukh in 1443.
119.x: Nicolo Conti’s visit is dated 1420–21, during Devaraya I, although an APPSC association places him under Devaraya II. He was an Italian traveller, not Abdur Razzaq.
119.tq: Resolve a close visitor–reign confusion through the date and nationality.
xs: **Nicolo Conti** is dated **1420-21** under **Devaraya I**, though the **APPSC G2 2011** key places him under **Devaraya II** — option **(1)**.
He was an **Italian**; the Persian envoy of Shah Rukh (**1443**) was **Abdur Razzaq**.
xa: **Cesare Federici** (Italy) came under **Sadasivaraya**.
**Ibn Battuta** was the first foreign traveller, under **Harihara I**.

119.s: Which of the following titles was NOT associated with Devaraya II?
119.x: Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati was the title of Harihara I. Devaraya II was known as Gajabetekara, Praudha Devaraya and Ilanti Raikonda.
119.tq: Find the title belonging to a different ruler.
xs: **Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati** is NOT Devaraya II's — option **(2)**; it was **Harihara I's**.
Devaraya II's titles: **Gajabetekara** (elephant hunter), **Praudha Devaraya**, **Ilanti Raikonda**.
xa: ⚠ **Dakshina Samudradhipati** = **Lakkanna Dandanayaka**.
Devaraya II wrote **Mahanataka Sudhanidhi**.

119.s:
Which of the following achievements is associated with Devaraya II?
1. Annexation of Kondaveedu in 1424
2. Collection of tribute from Sri Lanka through Lakkanna Dandanayaka
3. Repulsion of the Gajapatis, recorded in the Draksharama inscription of 1444
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
119.x: Devaraya II annexed Kondaveedu, received Sri Lankan tribute through Lakkanna Dandanayaka and repelled the Gajapatis, as recorded at Draksharama.
119.tq: Link ruler, date, inscription and military achievement.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Devaraya II** annexed **Kondaveedu (1424)** and got **Sri Lankan** tribute via **Lakkanna Dandanayaka**.
He repelled the **Gajapatis**, sending **Mallappa Odayar** to Rajahmundry (**Draksharama inscription, 1444**).
xa: He honoured **Srinatha** with a **kanakabhishekam** after he beat **Gauda Dindima**.
**Vinukonda Vallabharaya** (Kridabhiramam) was his governor of **Vinukonda**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about culture under Devaraya II:
1. Srinatha received kanakabhishekam after defeating Gauda Dindima.
2. Devaraya II wrote the Navaratnamala.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
119.x: Statement 1 is correct: Srinatha was honoured with kanakabhishekam after beating Gauda Dindima. Statement 2 is wrong: Devaraya II's own work is Mahanataka Sudhanidhi; Navaratnamala was written by Irugappa, minister of Harihara II. So 1 only (A); B and C accept the wrong statement, D rejects the correct one.
119.tq: Devaraya II wrote Mahanataka Sudhanidhi; Navaratnamala belongs to Irugappa.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct, so option **(1) 1 only** is the answer.
Statement 1 is correct: **Srinatha** received the **kanakabhishekam** after defeating **Gauda Dindima**, under the patronage of **Devaraya II**.
Statement 2 is wrong: Devaraya II's own work is **Mahanataka Sudhanidhi**; the **Navaratnamala** was written by **Irugappa**, minister of **Harihara II**.
xa: **Vinukonda Vallabharaya**, author of **Kridabhiramam**, was governor of **Vinukonda** under Devaraya II.
Devaraya II's titles: **Gajabetekara** (elephant hunter), **Praudha Devaraya**, **Ilanti Raikonda**.
Irugappa also built the **Ganigitti Jain temple**.

119.s: Abdur Razzaq, who visited Vijayanagara in 1443 during the reign of Devaraya II, came as the envoy of:
119.x: Abdur Razzaq was the Persian envoy of Shah Rukh and visited in 1443 under Devaraya II. Firuz Shah Bahmani fought Devaraya I; the Ming emperor received Bukka I's embassy (1374); the Portuguese came later, under the Tuluvas.
119.tq: Razzaq - Persia - Shah Rukh - 1443 - Devaraya II.
xs: **Abdur Razzaq** came as the Persian envoy of **Shah Rukh** in **1443** — option **(1)**.
**Firuz Shah Bahmani** fought **Devaraya I** (War of the Goldsmith's Daughter), not Devaraya II.
The **Ming emperor of China** received **Bukka I's** embassy of **1374**.
xa: Abdur Razzaq described open **diamond bazaars**, **300 ports**, and a tax on prostitution.
Travellers by reign: **Paes** and **Barbosa** (Portugal) → **Krishnadevaraya**; **Nuniz** → **Achyutaraya**; **Cesare Federici** (Italy) → **Sadasivaraya**.
⚠ **Nicolo Conti**: APPSC G2 **2011** key places him under **Devaraya II**; some notes date his visit **1420-21** under **Devaraya I**.

119.s: Harihara II advanced towards the Krishna in alliance with which of the following?
119.x: Harihara II pushed towards the Krishna in alliance with the Reddis.
119.tq: Identify the allied power by separating Harihara II’s campaign from Devaraya I’s alliances.
xs: **Harihara II** pushed towards the **Krishna** in alliance with **the Reddis** — option **(4)**.
The **Kandukuru Reddis** were fought and made feudatories by **Devaraya I**, and the **Velamas** were Devaraya I's allies.
xa: **Bukka I** captured **Srisailam** and **Dupadu** (near **Markapur**).
Harihara II was the **longest-reigning** Sangama king (**1377-1404**) and the **first to attack Sri Lanka**.
Harihara II gave a daughter to **Kataya Vema's** son; his reign saw the famine **"Durgadevi Karamu"**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Devaraya I:
1. He fought the Kandukuru Reddis and made them feudatories.
2. He allied with the Velamas and Kataya Vema.
3. He captured Srisailam and Dupadu near Markapur.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the capture of Srisailam and Dupadu is attributed to Bukka I.
119.tq: Find the wrong ruler–achievement pairing before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Devaraya I** fought the **Kandukuru Reddis** and made them **feudatories**.
Statement 2 is correct: he allied with the **Velamas** and **Kataya Vema**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Srisailam** and **Dupadu** (near **Markapur**) were captured by **Bukka I**.
xa: Devaraya I took southern **Kondaveedu**, including **Motupalli**, recorded in his **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam**.
Devaraya I built a **dam on the Tungabhadra** with canals to carry water to the city.
**Nicolo Conti** visited in his reign; CDX calls him the first to recruit Muslims.

119.s: Devaraya I’s capture of southern Kondaveedu, including Motupalli, is recorded in which inscription?
119.x: Devaraya I’s capture of southern Kondaveedu, including Motupalli, is recorded in the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam.
119.tq: Match the specific inscription with the ruler’s territorial achievement.
xs: Devaraya I's capture of southern **Kondaveedu**, including **Motupalli**, is recorded in the **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** — option **(1)**.
The **Draksharama inscription** (**1444**) belongs to **Devaraya II**, recording help sent to **Rajahmundry** against the Gajapatis.
xa: Devaraya I also fought the **Kandukuru Reddis** and allied with the **Velamas** and **Kataya Vema**.
**Devaraya II** annexed **Kondaveedu** fully in **1424**.
Devaraya I gave his daughter to **Firoz Shah Bahmani** with **Bankapur** as dowry.

119.s: Devaraya II sent Mallappa Odayar to assist which place?
119.x: Devaraya II sent Mallappa Odayar to help Rajahmundry, as recorded in the Draksharama inscription of 1444.
119.tq: Use the person–place association to distinguish Devaraya II’s intervention in Andhra.
xs: Devaraya II sent **Mallappa Odayar** to help **Rajahmundry** — option **(2)**.
This is recorded in the **Draksharama inscription** of **1444**, when Devaraya II repelled the **Gajapatis**.
xa: Devaraya II annexed **Kondaveedu** in **1424**.
He received tribute from **Sri Lanka** through **Lakkanna Dandanayaka**, titled **"Dakshina Samudradhipati"**.
He enrolled **10,000 Muslim soldiers** (APPSC G2 **2011** key), gave them **jagirs** and a mosque.

119.s: Who among the following was the author of Kridabhiramam and served as governor of Vinukonda under Devaraya II?
119.x: Vinukonda Vallabharaya wrote Kridabhiramam and was the governor of Vinukonda under Devaraya II.
119.tq: Link the author, work and office rather than confusing the poet with a military officer or ally.
xs: **Vinukonda Vallabharaya** wrote **Kridabhiramam** and was governor of **Vinukonda** under **Devaraya II** — option **(1)**.
**Srinatha** was the poet honoured with **kanakabhishekam**; **Mallappa Odayar** was sent to help **Rajahmundry**.
**Kataya Vema** was an ally of **Devaraya I**, not a governor-poet.
xa: Srinatha's kanakabhishekam followed his victory over **Gauda Dindima**.
Devaraya II's own work: **Mahanataka Sudhanidhi**.
⚠ **Gajabetekara** = Devaraya II; **Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati** = **Harihara I**.

119.s: The principal bone of contention between the Vijayanagara and Bahmani kingdoms was the Raichur Doab, situated between which two rivers?
119.x: The Raichur Doab, or Raichur Antarvedi, lies between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers and was the main cause of the recurring wars.
119.tq: Test the geographical boundaries of a disputed region.
xs: The **Raichur Doab** lies between the **Krishna and Tungabhadra** — option **(1)**.
Also called the **Raichur Antarvedi**, it was the main cause of the Vijayanagara-Bahmani wars (APPSC G2 **2000**, **2003**; PYQ **2017**).
xa: The two kingdoms also fought over the **Krishna-Godavari delta** and **Marathwada**.
Key contested points: **Mudgal** and **Raichur**.
**Krishnadevaraya** retook Raichur in the **Gobburi/Raichur war (1520)** with Portuguese help.

119.s:
With reference to the conflict at Mudgal in 1358, consider the following statements:
1. Bukka I took Mudgal.
2. It was regarded as the first Indian war involving artillery.
3. A truce was concluded to spare civilians.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: The 1358 Mudgal conflict occurred under Bukka I, who took Mudgal; it is noted as the first Indian war involving artillery, followed by a truce intended to spare civilians.
119.tq: Verify the date, military innovation and stated consequence as a single event cluster.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **Bukka I** took **Mudgal** in **1358**.
Statement 2: it is called the **first Indian war with artillery**, used by the **Bahmanis**.
Statement 3: a **truce** was concluded to spare civilians.
xa: In **1347**, the Bahmani general **Mubarak Khan** took land west of Raichur.
Under **Devaraya I**, the **"War of the Goldsmith's Daughter"** (Nehal of Mudgal) was fought against **Firuz Shah**.
**Devaraya II** fought two wars over **Mudgal**, **Raichur** and **Bijapur**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about the 'War of the Goldsmith's Daughter':
1. It was fought between Devaraya I and Firuz Shah Bahmani.
2. After his defeat, Devaraya I gave his daughter and Bankapur as dowry.
3. Bankapur was never regained by Vijayanagara.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statement 1 is correct: the war (over Nehal of Mudgal) was between Devaraya I and Firuz Shah. Statement 2 is correct: the defeated Devaraya I gave his daughter and Bankapur as dowry. Statement 3 is wrong: Bankapur was later regained. So 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include statement 3.
119.tq: Goldsmith's daughter = Devaraya I vs Firuz Shah; Bankapur lost as dowry, later regained.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: the war, over **Nehal of Mudgal**, was between **Devaraya I** and **Firuz Shah** Bahmani.
Statement 2 is correct: the defeated Devaraya I gave his **daughter** and **Bankapur** as dowry.
Statement 3 is wrong: Bankapur was **later regained** (CDX).
xa: The **Mudgal (1358)** war under **Bukka I** was the **first Indian war with artillery**.
Main bone of contention: the **Raichur Doab** between the **Krishna and Tungabhadra**.
**Nicolo Conti** visited Vijayanagara under Devaraya I (per some notes, **1420-21**).

119.s: Goa was taken by Madhava in 1366 and was lost to the Bahmanis in which year?
119.x: Goa, taken in 1366 by Madhava, was lost to the Bahmanis in 1472.
119.tq: Pair the two close historical dates and identify the later reversal.
xs: Goa, taken by minister **Madhava** in **1366**, was lost to the Bahmanis in **1472** — option **(2)**.
⚠ Memory hook: Goa taken **1366**, lost **1472**; Raichur retaken **1520**, Gulbarga **1523**.
xa: Madhava the minister/general bore the title **"Bhuvanaikavira"**; some notes place the Goa conquest under **Harihara II**.
⚠ Do not confuse him with **Madhava-Vidyaranya**, the **Advaita** head of **Sringeri**.
Goa had been part of the **Raichur Doab**-centred Bahmani wars, which ended at **Talikota (1565)**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Krishnadevaraya’s campaigns:
1. He retook Raichur in the Gobburi or Raichur war of 1520.
2. Portuguese assistance was received in that campaign.
3. He took Gulbarga in 1523.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Krishnadevaraya retook Raichur in 1520 with Portuguese help and took Gulbarga in 1523.
119.tq: Combine the campaign, foreign assistance and successive dates before choosing the code.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Krishnadevaraya** retook **Raichur** in the **Gobburi/Raichur war (1520)**, with **Portuguese** help.
He then took **Gulbarga** in **1523**.
xa: Krishnadevaraya (**1509-29**, Tuluva) marked the empire's **zenith**.
**Paes** and **Barbosa** (Portugal) visited during his reign.
The conflict ended at **Talikota (1565)**, where the Deccan sultanates defeated **Rama Raya**.

119.s: The conflict between Vijayanagara and the Deccan sultanates finally culminated in the Battle of Talikota in 1565. What was its principal outcome?
o: Rama Raya defeated the Deccan sultanates and annexed Bijapur.
The Deccan sultanates defeated Rama Raya.
The Bahmanis recovered Goa from Madhava.
119.x: At Talikota in 1565, the Deccan sultanates defeated Rama Raya, bringing the major phase of the conflict to an end.
119.tq: Connect the terminal date of the conflict with its actual victor.
xs: At **Talikota (1565)**, **the Deccan sultanates defeated Rama Raya** — option **(2)**.
Goa was lost to the Bahmanis in **1472**, and **Krishnadevaraya** captured **Gulbarga** in **1523** — neither is Talikota's outcome.
xa: Talikota came in the reign of **Sadasivaraya**, with **Rama Raya** as regent.
After Talikota the capital moved to **Penukonda** and then **Chandragiri** (both in AP).
The **Aravidu** dynasty (Andhra origin, **Araviti**, Kurnool) followed, with capitals Penukonda, Chandragiri and **Vellore**.

119.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Krishnadevaraya took Gulbarga.
B. Bukka I took Mudgal.
C. Goa was lost to the Bahmanis.
D. The Battle of Talikota was fought.
119.x: The correct sequence is Mudgal in 1358, Goa’s loss in 1472, the capture of Gulbarga in 1523, and Talikota in 1565.
119.tq: Place the dated events first and then compare the middle positions.
xs: The order is **B, C, A, D** — option **(1)**.
**B**: **Bukka I** took **Mudgal** in **1358**; **C**: **Goa** lost to the Bahmanis in **1472**.
**A**: **Krishnadevaraya** took **Gulbarga** in **1523**; **D**: **Talikota** in **1565**.
xa: Goa had been taken in **1366** by minister **Madhava**.
**Raichur** was retaken in the **Gobburi war (1520)**, three years before Gulbarga.
In **1347**, the Bahmani general **Mubarak Khan** took land west of Raichur.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about Saluva Narasimha:
1. He was originally the lord of Chandragiri.
2. He seized the throne in 1485 with the help of Tuluva Narasa Nayaka.
3. He expelled Devaraya II to seize the throne.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statement 1 is correct: Saluva Narasimha was lord of Chandragiri. Statement 2 is correct: in 1485 he seized the throne with Tuluva Narasa Nayaka's help (the First Usurpation). Statement 3 is wrong: he expelled Praudha Raya, the last Sangama ruler, not Devaraya II. So 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include statement 3.
119.tq: First Usurpation 1485: Chandragiri lord + Tuluva Narasa Nayaka against Praudha Raya.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Saluva Narasimha** was lord of **Chandragiri**.
Statement 2 is correct: in **1485** he seized the throne with **Tuluva Narasa Nayaka's** help — the **First Usurpation**.
Statement 3 is wrong: he expelled **Praudha Raya**, the last Sangama ruler, not Devaraya II.
xa: His clan came from **Kalyana**; ancestor **Saluva Mangu** served **Kumara Kampana**.
He took the **Machilipatnam** area and repelled a **Bahmani raid on Kanchi (1481)**.
The **Saluva** dynasty ruled **1485-1505**.

119.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the background of Saluva Narasimha is correct?
1. His clan came from Kalyana.
2. His ancestor Saluva Mangu served Kumara Kampana.
3. He was a ruler of the Tuluva dynasty.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
119.x: The Saluva clan came from Kalyana and Saluva Mangu served Kumara Kampana. Saluva Narasimha belonged to the Saluva dynasty, not the Tuluva dynasty.
119.tq: Reject the dynasty substitution while retaining the correct lineage facts.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: the Saluva clan came from **Kalyana**.
Statement 2 is correct: ancestor **Saluva Mangu** served **Kumara Kampana**, killed the Madurai Sultan and took the title **"Parapakshi Saluva"**.
Statement 3 is wrong: he founded the **Saluva** dynasty; the **Tuluva** dynasty was founded by **Vira Narasimha** in **1505**.
xa: Saluva Narasimha was lord of **Chandragiri** and expelled **Praudha Raya** in **1485** (**First Usurpation**).
Court works: **Saluvabhyudayam** by **Rajanatha Dindima**; **Jaimini Bharatam** by **Pillalamarri Pinaveerabhadra**, dedicated to him.
Order of dynasties: **Sangama – Saluva – Tuluva – Aravidu**.

119.s: Annamacharya, born in 1408 and deceased in 1503, was a contemporary of which ruler?
119.x: Annamacharya (1408–1503) was a contemporary of Saluva Narasimha and is also placed in his court.
119.tq: Use overlapping life dates to identify the contemporary ruler.
xs: **Annamacharya (1408-1503)** was a contemporary of **Saluva Narasimha** — option **(3)**.
Some notes even place him in Saluva Narasimha's **court** (PYQ **2011**).
xa: Saluva Narasimha seized the throne in **1485** from **Praudha Raya** — the **First Usurpation**.
He repelled a **Bahmani raid on Kanchi (1481)** and took the **Machilipatnam** area.
**Jaimini Bharatam** by **Pillalamarri Pinaveerabhadra** was dedicated to him.

119.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
119.x: Jaimini Bharatam was written by Pillalamarri Pinaveerabhadra and dedicated to Saluva Narasimha. Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam.
119.tq: Detect the swapped author–work pair.
xs: **Gangadevi — Jaimini Bharatam** is wrongly matched — option **(1)**.
**Jaimini Bharatam** is by **Pillalamarri Pinaveerabhadra**, dedicated to **Saluva Narasimha**.
**Saluvabhyudayam** is by **Rajanatha Dindima**, from Saluva Narasimha's court.
**Gangadevi** wrote **Madhura Vijayam** (Sanskrit).
xa: Gangadevi was wife of **Kumara Kampana** and daughter-in-law of **Bukka I**; a **disciple of Agastya**.
Madhura Vijayam's theme: Kampana's defeat of **Champaraya of Tondaimandalam**, advance to **Kanchi** and conquest of **Madurai**.
**Annamacharya (1408-1503)** was Saluva Narasimha's contemporary.

119.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: The Aravidu Dynasty of Vijayanagara — Father H. Heras
Peasant State and Society in Medieval South India — Burton Stein
Social and Political Life in the Vijayanagara Empire — B.A. Saletore
119.x: Kampili and Vijayanagara was written by Nelaturi Venkataramanaiah, not Robert Sewell. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
119.tq: Find the swapped author–title pair among closely related historical works.
xs: **Kampili and Vijayanagara — Robert Sewell** is wrong — option **(4)**; it was written by **Nelaturi Venkataramanaiah**.
The other pairs are correct: **Father H. Heras** (The Aravidu Dynasty), **Burton Stein** (Peasant State and Society), **B.A. Saletore** (Social and Political Life).
xa: Robert Sewell wrote **A Forgotten Empire**, translating **Paes** and **Nuniz** (APPSC G2 **2011**, **2017**).
Burton Stein called Vijayanagara a **"segmentary state"**.
⚠ **Sewell** backs the **Andhra theory**; **Heras** backs the **Kannada** theory of origin.

119.s: A Forgotten Empire: Vijayanagar is best described as which of the following?
o: A Sanskrit poem describing the conquest of Madurai
A Telugu account of the twelve Sangama kings
A Persian chronicle presenting the Bahmani view of the wars
An English translation of the accounts of Domingo Paes and Fernao Nuniz
119.x: Robert Sewell’s A Forgotten Empire: Vijayanagar is an English translation of the Portuguese accounts of Domingo Paes and Fernao Nuniz.
119.tq: Distinguish the nature and source-language tradition of the work from other historical sources.
xs: **A Forgotten Empire** is **Robert Sewell's** English translation of the accounts of **Domingo Paes and Fernao Nuniz** — option **(4)**.
The Sanskrit poem on Madurai's conquest is **Madhura Vijayam** by **Gangadevi**.
The list of **12 Sangama kings** is in **Virupakshaya Kalajnana**; the Bahmani view comes from **Ferishta**.
xa: Asked in APPSC G2 **2011** and **2017**.
**Paes** visited under **Krishnadevaraya**; **Nuniz** under **Achyutaraya**.
Sewell also records the **seven** founding traditions of Vijayanagara.
