124.x: Burrakatha was earlier called Jangam Katha (APPSC-GS 2018 key). It is also known as Jamukula Kathalu and as Thandana Katha in Rayalaseema. Harikatha is a solo form with Chidatalu, Oggu Katha is the Telangana shepherd ballad, and Pichukuntla Katha sings Palnati Veeracharitra.
124.tq: Jangam Katha -> Burrakatha
xs: **Burrakatha** was earlier called **Jangam Katha** (APPSC-GS **2018** key) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Harikatha** is a solo form with **Chidatalu**.
**Oggu Katha** is the **Telangana** shepherd (Golla/Kuruma) ballad.
**Pichukuntla Katha** sings **Palnati Veeracharitra**.

124.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the material and technique used in Tolu Bommalata?

xs: Tolu Bommalata uses **thin, translucent leather figures painted on both sides**, moved behind a **white screen** lit by an **oil lamp** — so option **(4)** is correct.

xa: The puppeteer **sings verses and dialogue** from behind the screen.

1. Janapada Kalalu are the arts of the Janapadam (village).
2. The first book on the theory of folk knowledge was written by Annamacharya.
3. The period 1857-1956 is called the 'golden era' of dance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
125.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the first folk-knowledge theory book was by Biruduraju Ramaraju; Annamacharya wrote Kolatam kirtanas. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 2.
125.tq: Biruduraju Ramaraju = folk theory; Annamacharya = kirtanas.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Janapada Kalalu** are the arts of the **Janapadam (village)**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the first folk-knowledge theory book was by **Biruduraju Ramaraju**; **Annamacharya** wrote Kolatam kirtanas.
Statement 3 is correct: **1857-1956** is the **"golden era"** of dance.
xa: **World Folk Day** is **22 August**.
**Jola patalu** = lullabies.
The **Gathasaptasati** records couple and choir dances of rural folk.

125.s: World Folk Day is observed on which date?
125.x: World Folk Day is observed on 22 August.
125.tq: Recall the exact date from the set of cultural observances.
xs: **World Folk Day** is observed on **22 August** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**21 April** (**2026**) is when the **Kondapalli Toys Festival** was made annual; **13 May** relates to a report on **Gangamma Jatara**.
xa: Folk arts = **Janapada Kalalu**.
First folk-knowledge theory book: **Biruduraju Ramaraju**.
**1857-1956** = "golden era" of dance.

125.s:
Consider the following statements about Kuchipudi:
1. The village of Kuchipudi is associated with Krishna district.
2. Kuchipudi is one of India’s eight classical dance forms.
3. It has been described as a global ambassador of Indian culture.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
125.x: All three statements are correct. Kuchipudi village is associated with Krishna district, and the dance is among India’s eight classical forms and is regarded as a global ambassador of Indian culture.
125.tq: Combine geographical, classificatory and cultural-status statements without confusing the village with the wider region.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statement 1: Kuchipudi is named after **Kuchipudi village, Krishna district** (APPSC-GS **2024**: "originated in Krishna district" = correct).
Statement 2: it is one of India's **eight classical dance forms**.
Statement 3: it is called a **"global ambassador of Indian culture"**.
xa: PYQ option key: "**Krishna and Guntur**" (APPSC-GS **2019**).
Kuchipudi is a dance-drama from the **Bhagavata Mela**; dancers also **speak/sing**.
**Tarangam** = dancing on the rim of a **brass plate**.

125.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Kuchipudi from Bharatanatyam?
o: Bharatanatyam originated in Andhra, whereas Kuchipudi belongs to Tamil Nadu.
Kuchipudi is a strictly geometric solo repertoire without dialogue, whereas Bharatanatyam uses spoken dialogue.
Kuchipudi is a dance-drama tradition from Andhra, whereas Bharatanatyam is associated with Tamil Nadu and a solo temple-dance tradition.
Both are exclusively group dance-dramas performed by male troupes.
125.x: Kuchipudi is an Andhra dance-drama tradition, while Bharatanatyam is associated with Tamil Nadu and a solo temple-dance tradition.
125.tq: Split the comparison into region, performance format and tradition before selecting the precise pair.
xs: **Kuchipudi** is an **Andhra dance-drama**, whereas **Bharatanatyam** is a **Tamil Nadu** solo temple-dance tradition — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses the states; option (2) reverses the features — it is **Bharatanatyam** that has **no dialogue** and a geometric solo repertoire.
Bharatanatyam is **solo**, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: Kuchipudi grew from the **Bhagavata Mela** of Brahmin male troupes.
In Kuchipudi, dancers also **speak/sing**; **Tarangam** is dancing on a **brass plate** rim.
⚠ **Lakumadevi**, court dancer of Kumaragiri Reddy, was famed for **Bharatanatyam**, not Kuchipudi.

125.s: In Kuchipudi performance, ‘Tarangam’ refers to:
o: A sequence performed only with geometric movements
Dancing on the rim of a brass plate
125.x: Tarangam is a distinctive Kuchipudi feature in which the dancer performs while dancing on the rim of a brass plate.
125.tq: Recognise the technical performance term through its distinctive physical action.
xs: **Tarangam** is **dancing on the rim of a brass plate** — so option **(3)** is correct.
A geometric, dialogue-free solo repertoire describes **Bharatanatyam**, not Tarangam.
xa: In Kuchipudi, dancers also **speak and sing**.
Kuchipudi is a dance-drama from the **Bhagavata Mela** (Brahmin male troupes).
Kuchipudi is one of India's **eight classical dance forms**.

125.s: Lakumadevi, famed for Bharatanatyam, was a court dancer of
125.x: Lakumadevi was the court dancer of the Reddi king Kumaragiri Reddy. Krishnadevaraya was the Vijayanagara emperor, Tana Shah gifted the Kuchipudi village to performers, and Prolaya Vema Reddi founded the Reddi kingdom.
125.tq: Lakuma - Kumaragiri (Karpura Vasantarayalu)
xs: **Lakumadevi**, famed for **Bharatanatyam**, was the court dancer of **Kumaragiri Reddy** — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ Lakumadevi = **Bharatanatyam**, not Kuchipudi.
xa: Kumaragiri Reddy styled himself **Karpura Vasantarayalu**.
**Vasantotsavam** was the most popular festival under the **Reddi kings** (APPSC G2 **2019** key).
Merchant **Avachi Tippayashetti** headed the **Sugandhabhandagara** that supplied Vasantotsavam.

125.s:
Consider the following statements about Kolattam:
1. It is also called Dandalasyam and is a stick dance of 8 or 12 dancers.
2. Its leader is called Pennadi.
3. It was the main dance of the Kakatiya era.
4. Its Karnataka version is known as Jadakollu.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
125.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Kolattam was the main dance of the Eastern Chalukya era, not the Kakatiya era. Hence A; B and C include statement 3, and D treats all four as correct.
125.tq: Kolattam = Dandalasyam, Pennadi, Eastern Chalukya, Jadakollu.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Kolattam** (**Dandalasyam**) is a stick dance of **8 or 12**.
Statement 2 is correct: its leader is the **Pennadi**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it was the main dance of the **Eastern Chalukya** era, not the Kakatiya.
Statement 4 is correct: its Karnataka version is **Jadakollu**.
xa: **Annamacharya** wrote **Kolatam kirtanas** for this group dance.
⚠ **Dhimsa** origin is traced to **Koraput** (Odisha).
**Tappeta Gullu** belongs to the **north coastal** districts.

125.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Puli Veshalu — Namala village solo dance
125.x: Tappeta Gullu is associated with the north coastal districts. Dhimsa is associated with tribal women of Araku, Keelugurram is popular in Guntur and Puli Veshalu is the Vizianagaram tiger dance.
125.tq: Start with the sure regional association and reject swapped dance descriptions.
xs: **Tappeta Gullu — North coastal districts** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Dhimsa** is the dance of tribal women of **Araku / ASR district**, not Guntur.
**Keelugurram** is the **dummy-horse dance** popular in **Guntur**, not Araku.
**Puli Veshalu** is the tiger dance of **Vizianagaram Dasara**; the Namala solo is **Namala Singadu Nrutyam**.
xa: Tappeta Gullu: shepherds invoke **rain** and appease **Gangamma**, with drums strapped to the chest.
Keelugurram is also called **Ashwa Nrutyam**.
**Namala Singadu Nrutyam** comes from Namala village, **Anantapur**.

125.s: Tappeta Gullu is traditionally performed by shepherd communities mainly to:
o: Celebrate the arrival of spring alone
125.x: Shepherd communities perform Tappeta Gullu to invoke rain and appease Gangamma. Drums are strapped to the chest and ankle bells are also used.
125.tq: Infer the ritual purpose from the community, deity and performance setting.
xs: Shepherd communities perform **Tappeta Gullu** to **invoke rain and appease Gangamma** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Performers wear **drums strapped to the chest** and **ankle bells**.
xa: It belongs to the **north coastal** districts.
**Gangamma Jatara** of **Tirupati** is a **nine-day** festival with **Perantalu Vesham**.
**Kolla Pandalu** (cockfights) belong to **Sankranti**.

Which of the following statements about selected Andhra folk dances is correct?
1. Butta Bommalu performers wear large hollow figures or masks.
2. Dappu is percussion-led.
3. Garagalu involves decorated pots carried on the head for the village goddess.
4. Gangireddulu features a decorated bull and is associated with Sankranti.

125.x: All four statements are correct. These features distinguish Butta Bommalu, Dappu, Garagalu and Gangireddulu respectively.
125.tq: Group the characteristic costume, instrument, prop and festival associations accurately.
xs: All four statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Butta Bommalu**: dancers wear large hollow figures/masks; **Dappu**: percussion-led.
**Garagalu**: decorated pots on the head for the **village goddess**.
**Gangireddulu**: a decorated bull at **Sankranti**.
xa: **Dommarata** = acrobatics; **Chekka Bhajana** = wooden clappers.
**Lambadi** is the dance of the **Banjara**.
**Puli Veshalu** = tiger dance of **Vizianagaram Dasara**.

125.s: Dhimsa, performed by tribal women of the Araku or Alluri Sitarama Raju district, is traced to which place?
125.x: The origin of Dhimsa is traced to Koraput in Odisha, although it is strongly associated with the tribal women of the Araku and ASR region.
125.tq: Separate the present performance region from the stated origin place.
xs: The origin of **Dhimsa** is traced to **Koraput in Odisha** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is danced by tribal women of **Araku / ASR district**.
**Bidar (Karnataka)** is the origin of **Bidri** work, not Dhimsa.
xa: ⚠ **Kolattam** (AP) = **Jadakollu** (Karnataka); **Dhimsa** origin = **Koraput**.
**Puli Veshalu** is the tiger dance of **Vizianagaram** Dasara.
**Tappeta Gullu** belongs to the north coastal districts.

125.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Vasantotsavam under the Reddi kings is correct?

2. Avachi Tippayashetti headed the Sugandhabhandagara.

xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.

125.s: Which of the following festivals and associated features is correctly matched?
o: Sankranti — January; Gangireddulaata, Kolla Pandalu and Pottella Pandalu
Atla Taddi — Chaitra month; exclusively a harvest festival
Vasantotsavam — January; festival of Telangana identity
125.x: Sankranti falls in January and features Gangireddulaata, Kolla Pandalu (cockfights) and Pottella Pandalu (ram fights). Atla Taddi is a women's festival of Ashwayuja, Ugadi is the Telugu New Year (19 March in 2026), and Vasantotsavam was the most popular festival under the Reddi kings.
125.tq: Use the month and the cluster of associated rural practices to identify the festival.
xs: **Sankranti — January; Gangireddulaata, Kolla Pandalu and Pottella Pandalu** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Atla Taddi** is a women's festival of **Ashwayuja**, not Chaitra.
**Ugadi** is the **Telugu** New Year (**19 March 2026**), not October or Tamil.
**Vasantotsavam** was the Reddi kings' festival; **Bathukamma, Bonalu** mark Telangana identity.
xa: ⚠ **Kolla Pandalu** = cockfights; **Pottella Pandalu** = ram fights.
Sankranti falls in **January, Magh**.
Ugadi 2026 = **Sri Parabhava** samvatsara.

125.x: Atla Taddi is a women’s festival observed during the Ashwayuja month.

xs: **Atla Taddi** is a women's festival of the **Ashwayuja** month — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Magha** is linked to **Sankranti** (January, Magh).
xa: **Ugadi** is the Telugu New Year; in **2026** it was **Sri Parabhava** samvatsara, on **19 March**.
**Bathukamma, Bonalu** = Telangana identity.

xs: **Vasantotsavam** was the most popular festival under the **Reddi kings** (APPSC G2 **2019** key) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Sankranti** is the January festival; **Atla Taddi** is a women's festival of **Ashwayuja**; **Bathukamma** marks **Telangana identity**.

125.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
125.x: Dwaraka Tirumala is known as Dakshina Dwaraka. Draksharamam is Dakshina Kasi and Srikalahasti is Dakshina Kailasam.

Consider the following statements about the Gangamma Jatara of Tirupati:
1. It is a nine-day festival in which men appear in women's attire (Perantalu Vesham).
2. Chapparalu, bamboo structures, are a feature of this jatara.
3. Its chief ritual is the Sirimanu utsavam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
125.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Sirimanu utsavam belongs to Paidithalli Ammavaru of Vizianagaram. So 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include the false statement 3.
125.tq: Gangamma = Tirupati, Perantalu Vesham, Chapparalu; Sirimanu = Paidithalli.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Gangamma Jatara** of **Tirupati** lasts **nine days**; men appear in women's attire (**Perantalu Vesham**).
Statement 2 is correct: **Chapparalu** bamboo structures are a feature.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Sirimanu utsavam** belongs to **Paidithalli Ammavaru** of **Vizianagaram**.

**Kotappakonda Jatra** lies in the Guntur region, now **Palnadu**.
**Tappeta Gullu** dancers also appease **Gangamma** while invoking rain.

xs: **Sirimanu utsavam** is associated with **Paidithalli Ammavaru** of **Vizianagaram** — so option **(4)** is correct.

xs: **Kotappakonda Jatra** lies in the **Guntur region**, now **Palnadu** district — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Nandyal** district has the **Mahanandi** Shivaratri fair; **Vizianagaram** has **Paidithalli Ammavaru**.

125.s: Which of the following statements about Kalamkari traditions in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Srikalahasti is associated with pen or freehand Kalamkari, whereas Machilipatnam-Pedana is associated with block printing.
Kalamkari in Andhra Pradesh is confined to Kondapalli.
Srikalahasti is associated only with block printing, whereas Pedana is associated with freehand painting.

xs: **Srikalahasti** = **pen/freehand** Kalamkari; **Machilipatnam-Pedana** = **block-printed** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option (3) reverses the two styles.
**Kondapalli** is known for **toys**, and lacquerware belongs to **Etikoppaka**.
xa: Srikalahasti is also called **Dakshina Kailasam**.

125.s:
Consider the following statements about Lepakshi:

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
125.x: Statement 1 is correct: Lepakshi (APHDC) is the state handicrafts nodal agency. Statement 2 is wrong: the portal exports AP GI products such as Kondapalli toys and Dharmavaram sarees; Bidri and Nirmal are Telangana crafts. So 1 only (A); B, C and D misjudge one or both statements.
125.tq: Lepakshi sells AP crafts; Bidri/Nirmal/Cherial are Telangana traps.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Lepakshi (APHDC)** is the **state handicrafts nodal agency**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the portal exports AP GI products like **Kondapalli toys** and **Dharmavaram sarees**; **Bidri** and **Nirmal** are **Telangana** crafts.
xa: AP GI crafts are marketed through Lepakshi under **"Vocal for Local"**.

**Lepakshi Utsav** at Lepakshi celebrates Vijayanagara heritage.

125.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a Telangana craft or art tradition?
125.x: Dharmavaram sarees are an Andhra Pradesh tradition. Bidri, Cherial scroll paintings and Nirmal paintings are associated with Telangana.
125.tq: Find the out-of-state item by separating Andhra and Telangana traditions.
xs: **Dharmavaram sarees** are an **Andhra Pradesh** GI product, not a Telangana craft — so option **(4)** is the answer.
**Bidri** (Hyderabad), **Cherial scroll paintings** and **Nirmal paintings** are Telangana traditions.
xa: Telangana crafts also include **banjara needle craft** and **dokra metal craft**.
APPSC-GS **2022** key: the craft NOT traditional to AP = **Bidri work**.
Dharmavaram sarees are exported via **Lepakshi (APHDC)**'s portal.

125.s: Which of the following sets consists entirely of crafts associated with Telangana?
o: Bidri, Banjara needle craft, dokra metal craft and Nirmal art
Crochet lace, wooden cutlery, carpets and Etikoppaka toys
Lepakshi textiles, Srikalahasti Kalamkari, Cherial paintings and Dharmavaram sarees
Kondapalli toys, Kalamkari, Dharmavaram sarees and Budithi bell metal

125.tq: Check whether every item belongs to the same state rather than accepting a partly correct list.
xs: **Bidri, Banjara needle craft, dokra metal craft and Nirmal art** are all Telangana crafts — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) lists AP crafts: crochet (**Narasapur**), cutlery (**Udayagiri**), carpets (**Eluru**), **Etikoppaka** toys.
Option (4) lists AP crafts: **Kondapalli**, **Kalamkari**, **Dharmavaram**, **Budithi**; option (3) mixes in Telangana's **Cherial**.
xa: Telangana crafts also include **bronze castings** and **lacquerware**.
**Bidri** = Hyderabad, from **Bidar** (Karnataka).
Telangana markers: **Bathukamma, Bonalu, Oggu Katha**.

125.s: Bidri work in Hyderabad is historically associated with Bidar, which is in:
125.x: Hyderabad’s Bidri tradition is derived from Bidar, which is in Karnataka.
125.tq: Distinguish the present production centre from the historical place of origin.
xs: **Bidri** of Hyderabad comes from **Bidar**, in **Karnataka** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ Bidri is a **Telangana** craft, not AP.
xa: APPSC-GS **2022** key: of bamboo / Bidri / Cherial / Nirmal, the one NOT traditional to AP = **Bidri work**.
**Cherial scroll paintings** and **Nirmal paintings** are Telangana arts.
Other Telangana crafts: **banjara needle craft**, **dokra metal craft**.

125.s: Which sequence correctly represents the three forms of Bihu with their months?
o: Rongali — April; Kongali — October; Bhogali — January
Rongali — January; Kongali — April; Bhogali — October
Rongali — October; Kongali — January; Bhogali — April
Rongali — March; Kongali — June; Bhogali — December
125.x: Rongali Bihu is celebrated in April, Kongali Bihu in October and Bhogali Bihu in January.

**Ugadi**, the Telugu New Year, fell on **19 March 2026**.

125.s: In APPSC-GS 2022, which one of the following crafts was keyed as NOT traditional to Andhra Pradesh?
125.x: The APPSC-GS 2022 key marks Bidri work as the one NOT traditional to AP; Bidri is a Hyderabad craft that came from Bidar in Karnataka. Bamboo work, Cherial and Nirmal were the other options; Cherial and Nirmal are now listed under Telangana.

xs: The APPSC-GS **2022** key marked **Bidri work** as NOT traditional to AP — so option **(2)** is correct.
Bidri is a **Hyderabad** craft that came from **Bidar, Karnataka**.
**Cherial** and **Nirmal** paintings are now listed as **Telangana** arts too.
xa: Other Telangana crafts: **banjara needle craft, dokra metal craft**, bronze castings.

AP GI crafts are marketed through **Lepakshi (APHDC)**.

125.s:

Select the correct answer using the code given below.

125.tq: Separate current Andhra cultural developments from neighbouring-state markers.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statements 1 and 2: the **Kondapalli Toys Festival** was made **annual** (**21 Apr 2026**).
Statement 3 is wrong: Kondapalli (**NTR district**) is an **AP** craft, not a Telangana marker.

Telangana markers: **Bathukamma, Bonalu, Oggu Katha, Bidri, Cherial, Nirmal**.

125.s: Which one of the following is NOT a marker of Telangana culture?
125.x: Bathukamma, Oggu Katha and Cherial are listed as Telangana markers. Kolatam kirtanas are associated with group dance in the Andhra folk-song context.
125.tq: Find the item belonging to the neighbouring cultural context rather than the listed group.
xs: **Kolatam kirtanas** are not a Telangana marker — so option **(1)** is the answer.
Kolatam kirtanas were written by **Annamacharya** for group dance (Andhra).
**Cherial**, **Bathukamma** and **Oggu Katha** are listed Telangana markers.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about Rama Raya’s Deccan policy:
1. In 1546–47, he supported Ahmadnagar against Bijapur and Bidar.
2. He acquired the Raichur doab during that phase.
3. From 1557 to 1563, he supported Bijapur and razed Ahmadnagar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: All three are correct: in 1546-47 Rama Raya backed Ahmadnagar against Bijapur and Bidar and took the Raichur doab, and in 1557-63 he backed Bijapur and razed Ahmadnagar - playing the Sultans against each other.
126.tq: Track the dates and changing allies carefully; the reversal of alliances is the key trap.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statements 1 and 2: in **1546-47** Rama Raya backed **Ahmadnagar** against **Bijapur and Bidar** and took the **Raichur doab**.
Statement 3: in **1557-63** he backed **Bijapur** and **razed Ahmadnagar**.
This was his policy of **playing the Sultans against each other**.
xa: This **divide-and-rule** diplomacy is listed as a cause that **united the Sultans** against him.
Rama Raya had earlier served under **Golconda** and the **Bahmanis**.
He also sheltered **Jagadeva Rao**, a rebel from Golconda.

126.s: What was the Turka Vada established by Rama Raya?
126.x: Rama Raya established a Muslim quarter known as the Turka Vada.
126.tq: Discriminate between a place-name and administrative or military terminology.
xs: **Turka Vada** was a **Muslim quarter** set up by Rama Raya — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was not a tax, a factory or a temple corridor.
xa: Rama Raya's guru was **Tatacharya**.
He married **Krishnadevaraya's daughter** — hence **Aliya** (son-in-law).
At Talikota, the **Muslim contingents** in the Vijayanagara army withdrew/deserted.

126.s: Who was the guru of Rama Raya?
126.x: Tatacharya was the guru of Rama Raya.
126.tq: Match the ruler with the associated religious teacher.
xs: **Tatacharya** was Rama Raya's **guru** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Babanathu** was the Muslim saint given villages by **Venkatapati II**.
**Appayya Dikshita** (Shaivarka Mani Dipika) was at Venkatapati II's court; **Ramaraja Bhushanudu** wrote **Vasucharitra**.
xa: Rama Raya set up the **Turka Vada**, a Muslim quarter.
He was **regent** for nominal king **Sadashiva Raya** (**1543**-).

126.s: The Battle of Talikota was fought between which two villages, according to local historical tradition?
126.x: Local histories place the battle between the villages of Rakshasi and Tangadi, on the north bank of the Krishna.
126.tq: Use the location clue to identify the correct pair of villages.
xs: The battle was fought between the villages of **Rakshasi and Tangadi**, on the north bank of the **Krishna** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Bannihatti** is the name used by **H.K. Sherwani**; **Kondavidu** went to Golconda after the battle.
After defeat, Sadashiva and Tirumala fled from **Hampi** to **Penukonda**.
xa: **Talikota** is Robert **Sewell**'s name; **Rakshasi-Tangadi** is used by **Fr. Heras** and **Nilakanta Sastri**.
Date: **23 January 1565** (some notes: **26 January**).
The **Dutch** traded at **Pulicat**; **Chandragiri** later became a capital.

126.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Vijayanagara side in the Battle of Talikota:
1. Sadasiva Raya was the Tuluva king.
2. Aliya Rama Raya acted as his regent.
3. Tirumala and Venkatadri fought alongside Rama Raya.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: Sadasiva Raya was the nominal Tuluva king, while Rama Raya was his regent; Rama Raya's brothers Tirumala and Venkatadri fought with him.
126.tq: Combine the nominal ruler, regent and military associates in one statement set.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statements 1 and 2: **Sadasiva Raya** was the Tuluva king; **Aliya Rama Raya** was his regent and the de-facto ruler.
Statement 3: Rama Raya's brothers **Tirumala and Venkatadri** fought alongside him.
xa: Rama Raya was **captured and killed**; **Venkatadri** was also killed.
**Sadashiva and Tirumala** fled to **Penukonda**.
Last Tuluva ruler = **Sadasiva**; first Aravidu = **Tirumala**.

126.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Sultanate)
A. Bijapur
B. Ahmadnagar
C. Golconda
D. Bidar

List-II (Ruler)
1. Ali Barid Shah
2. Ibrahim Qutb Shah
3. Ali Adil Shah
4. Hussain Nizam Shah

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
126.x: Bijapur was ruled by Ali Adil Shah, Ahmadnagar by Hussain Nizam Shah, Golconda by Ibrahim Qutb Shah and Bidar by Ali Barid Shah.
126.tq: Start from the sure ruler–Sultanate pairs and eliminate the codes.
xs: **A-3, B-4, C-2, D-1** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Bijapur — Ali Adil Shah**; **Ahmadnagar — Hussain Nizam Shah**.
**Golconda — Ibrahim Qutb Shah**; **Bidar — Ali Barid Shah**.
xa: **Ibrahim Qutb Shah** was the key organiser of the alliance.
**Hussain Nizam Shah** beheaded Rama Raya.
**Berar** (Imad Shahi) stayed out.

126.s: Who is associated with the organisation of the Deccan Sultanates' coalition against Vijayanagara at Talikota?
126.x: Ibrahim Qutb Shah of Golconda is identified as the key organiser or leader of the coalition.
126.tq: Match the political role with the correct Sultan rather than merely identifying an ally.
xs: **Ibrahim Qutb Shah** of **Golconda** was the key organiser of the alliance — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Ali Adil Shah** ruled **Bijapur**; **Hussain Nizam Shah** ruled **Ahmadnagar**; **Ali Barid Shah** ruled **Bidar**.
xa: The Sultans are called the **"Pancha Padushas"**.
**Bibi Jamal** married Ibrahim; **Chand Bibi** married Ali Adil.
Golconda gained **Kondavidu and Machilipatnam** after the battle.

126.s: Who beheaded Aliya Rama Raya after his capture in the Battle of Talikota?
126.x: Hussain Nizam Shah of Ahmadnagar is stated to have beheaded the captured Rama Raya.
126.tq: Use the deed–person association trap common in medieval history questions.
xs: **Hussain Nizam Shah** of **Ahmadnagar** beheaded **Rama Raya** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Ibrahim Qutb Shah** (Golconda) organised the alliance; **Ali Barid Shah** ruled **Bidar**; **Ali Adil Shah** ruled **Bijapur**.
xa: Rama Raya had **razed Ahmadnagar** in **1557-63**.
**Venkatadri** was also killed in the battle.
After an early Vijayanagara lead came **deceptive peace talks** and a **surprise attack**.

126.s: Which one of the following Deccan Sultanates did NOT participate in the alliance against Vijayanagara at Talikota?
126.x: Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda and Bidar formed the alliance; Berar, ruled by the Imad Shahi dynasty, stayed out.
126.tq: Find the excluded member by separating the four participating Sultanates from Berar.
xs: **Berar** (Imad Shahi) did not take part — so option **(1)** is the answer.
The alliance: **Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda and Bidar**.
⚠ Some notes add Berar's **Burhan Imad-ul-Mulk** to the "Pancha Padushas"; others (incl. **Sherwani**) exclude Berar.
xa: **Ibrahim Qutb Shah** of Golconda organised the alliance.
Vijayanagara faced the **Deccan Sultanates**, not the Bahmani kingdom (G1 **2018**).

126.s: The Sultanate that stayed out of the Talikota alliance was ruled by which dynasty?
126.x: Berar stayed out of the alliance and was ruled by the Imad Shahi dynasty.
126.tq: Connect the excluded state with its ruling dynasty.
xs: **Berar**, which stayed out, was ruled by the **Imad Shahi** dynasty — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Adil Shahi** = Bijapur, **Nizam Shahi** = Ahmadnagar, **Qutb Shahi** = Golconda — all joined the alliance.
xa: The fourth member, **Bidar**, was ruled by **Ali Barid Shah**.
⚠ Some notes list Berar's **Burhan Imad-ul-Mulk** among the "Pancha Padushas".
**Hussain Nizam Shah** beheaded Rama Raya.

126.s: In the Battle of Talikota (1565), the Vijayanagara Empire fought against
o: A confederacy of the Deccan Sultanates
126.x: Vijayanagara under Aliya Rama Raya fought the confederacy of the Deccan Sultanates (Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar). The Bahmani kingdom had already broken up into these Sultanates, so 'Bahmani' is a common trap. The Mughals and the Gajapatis were not parties to the battle.
126.tq: 1565 = Deccan Sultanates, not Bahmanis
xs: At Talikota, Vijayanagara fought **a confederacy of the Deccan Sultanates** — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ Trap: it was **NOT the Bahmani kingdom** (G1 **2018**; UPPSC **2014**).
Members: **Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar**.
xa: Vijayanagara's de-facto ruler was **Aliya Rama Raya**, regent of **Sadasiva Raya**.
Date: **23 January 1565**.
After victory, the Sultanates **went back to fighting each other**.

126.s: Which historian called the battle of 1565 'Bannihatti'?
126.x: H.K. Sherwani called it Bannihatti. Robert Sewell called it Talikota, while Fr. Heras and Nilakanta Sastri called it Rakshasi-Tangadi.
126.tq: Sewell-Talikota; Heras/Sastri-Rakshasi-Tangadi; Sherwani-Bannihatti
xs: **H.K. Sherwani** called the battle **Bannihatti** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Robert Sewell** called it **Talikota**.
**Fr. Heras** and **Nilakanta Sastri** called it **Rakshasi-Tangadi**.
xa: Sherwani also excludes **Berar** from the alliance.
Sewell's **"graveyard"** account of Hampi may exaggerate the damage.
Sewell wrote **A Forgotten Empire** (**1900**).

126.s: The Battle of Talikota (Rakshasi-Tangadi) was fought in
126.x: It was fought in January 1565 (APPSC-GS 2022 answer). 1556 is Panipat II, 1576 Haldighati, and 1526 Panipat I.
126.tq: Talikota 1565; Panipat II 1556
xs: The Battle of Talikota was fought in **1565** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Date: **23 January 1565** (some notes: **26 January**); APPSC-GS **2022** answer: **1565**.
**1576** is one date given for **Sadasiva Raya's** death, not the battle.
xa: Place: north bank of the **Krishna**, between **Rakshasi and Tangadi**.
Tirumala was crowned at **Penukonda** in **1570**.
Venetian **Caesar Frederick** saw the ruined capital in **1567**.

126.s: Which one of the following was NOT a principal cause contributing to the formation of the Deccan coalition against Vijayanagara?
o: Rama Raya's policy of playing the Sultans against one another
Rama Raya's interference in the affairs of the Sultanates
Rama Raya's sheltering of Jagadeva Rao, a rebel from Golconda
The permanent military union created by the Bahmani emperor
126.x: The coalition is attributed to Rama Raya's diplomacy, interference, earlier attacks and sheltering of Jagadeva Rao; no Bahmani emperor created the coalition.
126.tq: Find the historically unrelated cause among closely connected political factors.
xs: No **Bahmani emperor** created a military union — so option **(4)** is the answer.
Real causes: Rama Raya's **divide-and-rule** diplomacy, **interference** in the Sultanates' affairs and sheltering **Jagadeva Rao**.
⚠ The enemy was the **Deccan Sultanates**, not the Bahmani kingdom.
xa: Marriage links: **Bibi Jamal** married Ibrahim; **Chand Bibi** married Ali Adil.
**Ferishta** also alleges religious insults.
Rama Raya **sacked Ahmadnagar** in **1557-63**.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about the causes of the Battle of Talikota:
1. Rama Raya sacked Ahmadnagar during 1557-63.
2. Bibi Jamal married Ali Adil, while Chand Bibi married Ibrahim.
3. Ferishta also alleges religious insults as a cause.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 reverses the marriages: Bibi Jamal married Ibrahim and Chand Bibi married Ali Adil. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 2.
126.tq: Marriage links: Bibi Jamal-Ibrahim, Chand Bibi-Ali Adil; watch for swaps.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: Rama Raya sacked **Ahmadnagar** in **1557-63**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Bibi Jamal** married **Ibrahim**, and **Chand Bibi** married **Ali Adil**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Ferishta** also alleges **religious insults**.
xa: Rama Raya sheltered **Jagadeva Rao**, a rebel from Golconda.
In **1546-47** he took the **Raichur doab**.

126.s: Which sequence best represents the principal course of the Battle of Talikota?
o: Surprise attack, Vijayanagara success, peace talks, capture of Rama Raya
Vijayanagara successes, deceptive peace talks, surprise attack, withdrawal of Muslim contingents
Peace treaty, Vijayanagara retreat, Sultanate division, capture of Rama Raya
Withdrawal of Muslim contingents, Vijayanagara successes, peace talks, Sultanate attack
126.x: The battle initially saw Vijayanagara successes, followed by deceptive peace talks, a surprise attack and the withdrawal of Muslim contingents from the Vijayanagara army.
126.tq: Arrange the stages of the battle by identifying the first and final developments.
xs: **Vijayanagara successes → deceptive peace talks → surprise attack → withdrawal of Muslim contingents** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The Muslim contingents in Vijayanagara's army **withdrew/deserted**.
**Rama Raya** was then **captured and killed**; **Venkatadri** too.
xa: **Hussain Nizam Shah** beheaded Rama Raya.
Hampi was looted for about **six months**.
Sadashiva and Tirumala fled to **Penukonda**.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about the consequences of the Battle of Talikota:
1. Hampi was looted for about six months.
2. The damage to the capital was severe but not total.
3. The Nayakas became autonomous and later developed into zamindars and poligars.
4. The Deccan Sultanates permanently stopped fighting one another after their victory.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: Hampi was looted for about six months, the destruction was severe but not total, and the Nayakas became autonomous. The Sultanates resumed fighting among themselves after the victory.
126.tq: Reject the extreme claim that a temporary alliance became permanent.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statements 1 and 2: **Hampi** was looted for about **six months**; damage was **severe but not total**.
Statement 3: the **Nayakas** became autonomous → later **zamindars and poligars**.
Statement 4 is wrong: the Sultanates **went back to fighting each other**.
xa: Sewell's **"graveyard"** account may exaggerate.
Golconda gained **Kondavidu and Machilipatnam** + coastal tracts.
Sadashiva and Tirumala fled to **Penukonda**.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about the results of the Battle of Talikota:
1. Golconda gained Kondavidu and Machilipatnam along with coastal tracts.
2. Sadasiva and Tirumala fled to Chandragiri after the defeat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Sadasiva and Tirumala fled to Penukonda (Chandragiri became a capital later, under Venkata II). So 1 only (A); B, C and D misjudge the statements.
126.tq: First refuge after 1565 = Penukonda.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Golconda** gained **Kondavidu and Machilipatnam** with coastal tracts.
Statement 2 is wrong: Sadasiva and Tirumala fled to **Penukonda**; **Chandragiri** became capital later, under **Venkata II**.
xa: Capital order: **Penukonda (1570) → Chandragiri → Vellore (1600)**.
After **1565**, the empire's centre moved into AP.
**Sriranga Raya I** later lost **Kondaveedu** to Ibrahim Qutb Shah.

126.s: The Aravidu dynasty of Vijayanagara derived its name from which place?
126.x: The dynasty was named after Araviti, also called Aravidu, a village in Kurnool district.
126.tq: Use the place-name clue to distinguish the dynasty from similarly named ruling houses.
xs: The Aravidu dynasty is named after **Araviti (Aravidu) village, Kurnool district** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Penukonda** was its first capital (**1570**), not its namesake.
**Gandikota** is where **Mir Jumla** melted temple idols into cannon (**1657**).
xa: Aravidus ruled **1570-1680**, with **7** rulers.
Founder: **Tirumala Raya**, crowned at **Penukonda** at about age **90**.
Last ruler: **Sriranga III**, died **1680**.

126.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Aravidu dynasty:
1. It ruled the Vijayanagara Empire from 1570 to 1680.
2. It had seven rulers.

3. The Aravidu rulers originated from Kurnool.

126.x: All three statements are correct. After Talikota, the political centre shifted towards the Telugu country, particularly Penukonda and Chandragiri, while the Aravidus were associated with Kurnool.
126.tq: Test a regional shift through multiple connected consequences rather than a single place-name.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statements 1 and 2: after Talikota, the centre of gravity shifted to the **Telugu country** — **Penukonda, Chandragiri**.
Statement 3: the **Aravidus** came from **Kurnool** (Araviti village).
xa: The **Madras** grant came from a **Chandragiri-era Nayaka**.
Capital order: **Penukonda (1570) → Chandragiri → Vellore (1600)**.
After **1565**, the empire's centre moved into AP.

126.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Caesar Frederick visited the ruined Vijayanagara capital.
B. Tirumala founded the Aravidu line.
C. The Battle of Talikota was fought.
D. Tirumala shifted the capital to Penukonda.
126.x: The correct sequence is Talikota in 1565, Caesar Frederick’s visit in 1567, and Tirumala’s foundation of the Aravidu line and shift to Penukonda in 1570.
126.tq: Fix the sequence using the anchor years 1565, 1567 and 1570.
xs: **C, A, B, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Talikota** (**1565**) → **Caesar Frederick**'s visit (**1567**).
Then **Tirumala** founded the Aravidu line in **1570** and moved the capital to **Penukonda**.
xa: Tirumala was crowned at about age **90**.
Sadasiva Raya's reign is given as **1542-1570**.
Vellore became capital in **1600**.

126.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Caesar Frederick — Founder of the Aravidu dynasty
126.x: Caesar Frederick was a Venetian merchant who recorded an eyewitness account in 1567; Tirumala, not Caesar Frederick, founded the Aravidu line.
126.tq: Find the wrong person–achievement pairing by checking founders against visitors.
xs: **Caesar Frederick — Founder of the Aravidu dynasty** is wrongly matched — so option **(3)** is the answer.
Caesar Frederick was a **Venetian merchant** who saw the ruined capital in **1567**.
The other pairs are correct: **Tirumala** = first Aravidu, **Sriranga III** = last Aravidu, **Sadasiva** = last Tuluva.
xa: Tirumala founded the line in **1570** and moved the capital to **Penukonda**.
Sriranga III died in **1680**, ending the empire.

126.s:
Assertion (A): The dating of Sadasiva Raya’s death is subject to chronological debate.
Reason (R): Different accounts give 1570 and 1576 as the year of his death.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
126.x: Both statements are true, and the existence of the two dates, 1570 and 1576, explains the debate regarding Sadasiva Raya’s death.
126.tq: Check whether the stated evidence directly explains the historical uncertainty.
xs: Both **A and R are true**, and R is the **correct explanation** of A — so option **(1)** is correct.
Some notes give **1570** and others **1576** for **Sadashiva's death** — hence the debate.
xa: Tirumala's accession is dated **1570**, after Sadashiva died.
Some notes date the empire's end to **1646**, others to **1680**.
Talikota is dated **23 January 1565**; some notes give **26 January**.

126.s: Which of the following statements regarding interpretations of the aftermath of Talikota is correct?
o: The sack is universally accepted as having caused the complete disappearance of Vijayanagara culture.
Sewell denied that the Vijayanagara capital suffered any destruction.
Sewell described the sack as a “graveyard”, but this description may be exaggerated.
The description of the sack was written by Tirumala in 1570.
126.x: Sewell used the expression “graveyard” for the sack, although that assessment may be exaggerated. The other statements do not reflect the stated historical interpretation.
126.tq: Distinguish a historian’s vivid interpretation from an absolute claim about historical consequences.
xs: **Sewell** called the sack a **"graveyard"**, but this **may be exaggerated** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Hampi was looted for about **six months**: damage was **severe but not total**.
So the sack neither ended Vijayanagara culture completely, nor did Sewell deny destruction.
xa: Sewell wrote **A Forgotten Empire** (**1900**).
**Caesar Frederick** gave an eyewitness account in **1567**.
Nayaka courts later spread **Raya gopurams** and **kalyana mandapas** across Andhra.

127.s: Babur was born in 1483 at
127.x: Babur was born in 1483 at Farghana in Central Asia.
127.tq: Pair the birth year with the correct Central Asian birthplace.
xs: Babur was born in **1483** at **Farghana** (Central Asia) — so option **(4)** is correct.
He took **Kabul** only in **1504**; he **won and lost Samarkand**; he **died at Agra** (**1530**).
xa: He became ruler of Farghana as a boy in **1494**.
Descent: **Timur** (father's side) + **Chingiz Khan** (mother's side).
First Indian raid: **1519** (Bajaur, Bhera).

127.s: Babur’s descent was traced to which of the following combinations?
o: Timur on his father’s side and Chingiz Khan on his mother’s side
Chingiz Khan on his father’s side and Timur on his mother’s side
Sher Shah on his father’s side and Timur on his mother’s side
Ibrahim Lodi on his father’s side and Chingiz Khan on his mother’s side
127.x: Babur was descended from Timur through his father and from Chingiz Khan through his mother.
127.tq: Check the direction of descent carefully; the two ancestors are deliberately placed in opposite sides.
xs: Babur descended from **Timur on his father's side** and **Chingiz Khan on his mother's side** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) reverses the two lines.
xa: Born **1483**, **Farghana**.
His coins were silver **Shahrukhi** in **Timurid** style.
He wrote the **Tuzuk-i-Baburi** in **Chagatai Turki**.

127.s: Babur’s first raid into India is associated with which places and year?
127.x: Babur’s first raid into India took place in 1519 and involved Bajaur and Bhera. Some accounts give 1522, but the stated exam-oriented date is 1519.
127.tq: Match the event with both its places and year instead of accepting a nearby Babur date.
xs: Babur's first Indian raid was on **Bajaur and Bhera** in **1519** — so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes give **1522**.
**1504** is when he took **Kabul**; **1527** is **Khanwa**; **1526** is **Panipat**, which gave him **Delhi and Agra**.
xa: He was invited by **Daulat Khan Lodi**, **Alam Khan** and **Rana Sanga**.
He became ruler of Farghana in **1494**.

127.s:
Consider the following statements about those who invited Babur to India:
1. Daulat Khan Lodi, Governor of Punjab, invited him.
2. Alam Khan, Ibrahim Lodi's uncle, invited him.
3. Bahadur Shah of Gujarat invited him.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
127.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the third inviter was Rana Sanga of Mewar, not Bahadur Shah. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
127.tq: Inviters: Daulat Khan Lodi, Alam Khan, Rana Sanga.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Daulat Khan Lodi**, Governor of **Punjab**, invited him.
Statement 2 is correct: **Alam Khan**, Ibrahim's uncle, invited him.
Statement 3 is wrong: the third inviter was **Rana Sanga** of **Mewar**; **Bahadur Shah** united **Gujarat-Malwa**.
xa: Rana Sanga later fought Babur at **Khanwa (1527)**.
Babur's first raid: **1519**.

127.s: Which statement correctly describes Babur’s early political career?
o: He ruled Samarkand continuously from 1494 until his death in Agra.
He became ruler of Kabul in 1494, conquered Delhi in 1504, and never contested Samarkand.
He became ruler of Farghana as a boy in 1494, lost and regained Samarkand, and took Kabul in 1504.
He inherited Delhi in 1494 and took Farghana after the Battle of Panipat.
127.x: Babur became ruler of Farghana in 1494, experienced repeated success and failure at Samarkand, and captured Kabul in 1504.
127.tq: Choose the precise sequence of early political milestones and reject continuous-rule exaggerations.
xs: Babur became ruler of **Farghana** as a boy in **1494**, won and lost **Samarkand**, and took **Kabul** in **1504** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He got **Delhi** only after **Panipat (1526)**, and he died at **Agra**.
xa: Born **1483**, Farghana.
First Indian raid: **1519** (Bajaur, Bhera).
Buried at **Kabul** (Bagh-e-Babur).

127.s:
Consider the following statements about Babur's military methods:
1. Tulughma, of Uzbek origin, had flanking units wheel round to encircle the enemy.
2. The Rumi method used war elephants chained together as a barrier.
3. Babur's artillery was commanded by the Ottoman gunners Ustad Ali and Mustafa.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
127.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Rumi method (araba) chained carts as a barrier for matchlockmen and guns; the elephant version is a known error. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 2.
127.tq: Tulughma = Uzbek; Rumi = Ottoman carts, never elephants.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Tulughma**, of **Uzbek** origin, had flanking units wheel round to encircle the enemy.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **Rumi method (araba)** chained **carts** as a barrier for matchlockmen and guns; ⚠ the elephant version is a known error.
Statement 3 is correct: Ottoman gunners **Ustad Ali** and **Mustafa** commanded his artillery.
xa: The Rumi method is an **Ottoman** field-defence system.
Panipat = first large-scale use of **field artillery** in North Indian warfare.

127.s: Which statement regarding Babur’s use of artillery at Panipat is correct?
o: It was commanded by Ibrahim Lodi’s Ottoman officers.
It was used exclusively against cavalry and not infantry.
It marked the first large-scale use of field artillery in North Indian warfare.
It was the first use of any firearm ever known in India.
127.x: Panipat marked the first large-scale use of field artillery in North Indian warfare. Firearms were not wholly unknown in India before Babur.
127.tq: Avoid the extreme claim that a first large-scale use means the first knowledge of firearms.
xs: Panipat was the **first large-scale use of field artillery in North Indian warfare** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Firearms were **not wholly unknown** in India before Babur — so option (4) is wrong.
The guns were Babur's, under Ottoman gunners **Ustad Ali** and **Mustafa**, not Ibrahim Lodi's.
xa: The **Rumi method / araba**: carts chained as a barrier for matchlockmen and guns.
Artillery was decisive again at **Khanwa** (**1527**).

127.s: At the First Battle of Panipat, Babur’s approximately 12,000 troops defeated an army of Ibrahim Lodi numbering about
127.x: Babur’s force of about 12,000 defeated approximately 1,00,000 troops of Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat.
127.tq: Use the numerical contrast between the two armies to identify the correct figure.
xs: Babur's **12,000** defeated about **1,00,000** of Ibrahim's troops — so option **(4)** is correct.
His edge came from **Tulughma** and the **Rumi method** with field artillery.
xa: Ottoman gunners **Ustad Ali** and **Mustafa** commanded the artillery.
Panipat gave him **Delhi and Agra** + the **Lodi treasure** (APPSC-GS **2023**).
**Ibrahim Lodi** was the **last Delhi Sultan**.

127.s:
Consider the following statements about Babur after Panipat:
1. The victory gave Babur Delhi and Agra along with the treasure of the Lodis.
2. His lavish sharing of the treasure earned him the nickname 'Ghazi'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
127.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: lavish distribution earned him the nickname 'Qalandar'; 'Ghazi' was the title he took after Khanwa. So 1 only (A).
127.tq: Qalandar = generosity; Ghazi = Khanwa.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: Panipat gave Babur **Delhi and Agra** + the **treasure of the Lodis** (APPSC-GS **2023**).
Statement 2 is wrong: lavish sharing earned him **"Qalandar"**; **"Ghazi"** was his title after **Khanwa**.
xa: The lavish sharing left the treasury **depleted for Humayun**.
The **Kabuli Bagh mosque** at Panipat commemorates the **1526** victory.

127.s: At the Battle of Khanwa, the Rajput confederacy led by Rana Sanga was joined by
o: Daulat Khan Lodi and Medini Rai
Mahmud Lodi and Hasan Khan Mewati
127.x: Rana Sanga’s coalition included the Afghan Mahmud Lodi and Hasan Khan Mewati.
127.tq: Identify the members of the coalition rather than confusing them with Babur’s earlier opponents.
xs: Rana Sanga's Rajput confederacy was joined by **Mahmud Lodi** and **Hasan Khan Mewati** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Daulat Khan Lodi** had invited Babur; **Ibrahim Lodi** was already defeated at Panipat (**1526**).
xa: Babur used **trenches and barricades** against Sanga's **elephants**.
Before Khanwa he declared a **jihad**, renounced wine and remitted the **tamgha**.
Khanwa **broke Rajput power**; Babur took the title **"Ghazi"**.

127.s:
Consider the following statements about the Battle of Khanwa:
1. Before the battle Babur declared a jihad and renounced wine.
2. He remitted the tamgha for Muslims.
3. After the victory he took the title 'Padshah'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
127.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: after Khanwa Babur took the title 'Ghazi'. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
127.tq: Khanwa: jihad, wine renounced, tamgha remitted, title Ghazi.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: before Khanwa, Babur declared a **jihad** and **renounced wine**.
Statement 2 is correct: he remitted the **tamgha** for Muslims.
Statement 3 is wrong: after victory he took the title **"Ghazi"**.
xa: ⚠ **"Qalandar"** = for sharing the Lodi treasure; **"Ghazi"** = after Khanwa.
Rana Sanga was wounded and retreated.

127.s: Babur used trenches and barricades at Khanwa primarily to counter
127.x: Babur used trenches and barricades against the elephants of Rana Sanga. His artillery also played a decisive role in the battle.
127.tq: Infer the defensive measure from the battlefield threat it was designed to neutralise.
xs: Babur's **trenches and barricades** at Khanwa countered **Rana Sanga's elephants** — so option **(2)** is correct.
His **artillery** was decisive again; Sanga was **wounded** and retreated.
xa: Sanga's allies: **Mahmud Lodi** and **Hasan Khan Mewati**.
Khanwa (**1527**) broke **Rajput power**.
Babur then took the title **"Ghazi"**.

127.s: Which of the following best describes the extent of Babur’s dominions at the time of his death?
o: From Kabul and Badakhshan through Punjab, Delhi and Agra to the borders of Bihar
Only Kabul, Punjab and Delhi, without Agra
From Gujarat and Malwa to Bengal and the Deccan
From Afghanistan to the entire Indian subcontinent
127.x: At his death, Babur’s dominions extended from Kabul and Badakhshan through Punjab, Delhi and Agra to the borders of Bihar.
127.tq: Reject both the exaggerated all-India claim and the underestimation of the actual extent.
xs: At his death, Babur's empire ran from **Kabul and Badakhshan** through **Punjab, Delhi and Agra** to the **borders of Bihar** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Bengal** stayed unconquered and **Gujarat-Malwa** was under **Bahadur Shah**, so options (3) and (4) are wrong.
xa: The Bihar border was reached after **Ghaghra**.
He died in **1530** at Agra; **Humayun** took the throne on **29 Dec 1530**.
Mughal authority had **shallow roots**.

127.s: Where was Babur buried?
127.x: Babur was buried at Kabul in Bagh-e-Babur, although he died at Agra.
127.tq: Separate the place of death from the place of burial.
xs: Babur was buried at **Kabul** (**Bagh-e-Babur**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
He **died at Agra** in **1530**, but was not buried there.
xa: **Humayun** took the throne on **29 Dec 1530**.
**Ram Bagh (Aram Bagh)** at Agra was the first Mughal garden.
He took **Kabul** in **1504**.

127.s: Which one of the following was NOT a limitation of Babur’s rule in India?
o: The Afghans continued to claim Delhi
Gujarat and Malwa were united under Bahadur Shah
A fully developed administrative system was established
127.x: D is the answer because Babur set up no administrative system at all (his rule had shallow roots and the treasury was empty), so 'a fully developed administrative system' was not one of his limitations. A, B and C are listed limits: the Afghans still claimed Delhi, Bengal stayed unconquered, and Gujarat-Malwa was united under Bahadur Shah.
127.tq: Find the option that reverses a stated weakness of Babur’s administration.
xs: **A fully developed administrative system** was not something Babur had — so option **(4)** is the answer.
He left **no administrative system** and an **empty treasury**.
The others are real limits: **Afghans** still claimed Delhi, **Bengal** unconquered, **Gujarat-Malwa** under **Bahadur Shah**.
xa: Mughal authority had **shallow roots** in his **4-year** rule.
⚠ The **Mansabdari system** is **Akbar's**, not Babur's.

127.s:
Consider the following statements about the foundations of Mughal rule under Babur:
1. Babur’s victory at Panipat I displaced the Lodis.
2. The victory at Khanwa weakened Rajput power.
3. Babur introduced the Mansabdari system during his four-year rule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
127.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Mansabdari system was introduced under Akbar, not Babur.
127.tq: Use the ruler–institution trap to identify the statement assigning Akbar’s system to Babur.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Panipat I (1526)** displaced the **Lodis**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Khanwa** broke **Rajput power**.
Statement 3 is wrong: ⚠ the **Mansabdari system** is **Akbar's**.
xa: Babur left no administrative system; the treasury was empty.
Panipat ended the **Delhi Sultanate**.

127.s: Tuzuk-i-Baburi, also known as Baburnama, was written in
127.x: Baburnama was written in Chagatai Turki. Persian, rather than Turki, was the language of the Mughal court.
127.tq: Distinguish the language of the autobiography from the language of the Mughal court.
xs: The **Tuzuk-i-Baburi (Baburnama)** was written in **Chagatai Turki** — so option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ The Mughal **court language** was **Persian**, not Turki (UPPSC **2025**: A true, R false).
xa: English translators: **Leyden and Erskine** (**1826**); **Annette Beveridge**.
It counts **five Muslim and two Hindu powers** in India.
It praises **Krishnadevaraya** as the most powerful ruler.

127.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with an English translation of Baburnama?
o: Annette Beveridge — Persian translation under Akbar
Rana Sanga and Mahmud Lodi — 1826 translation
127.x: Leyden and Erskine produced an English translation in 1826. Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan was associated with the Persian translation, while Annette Beveridge was an English translator.
127.tq: Use the language–translator–date combination to eliminate swapped associations.
xs: **Leyden and Erskine — 1826** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Annette Beveridge** was an **English** translator, not a Persian one under Akbar.
**Rana Sanga** and **Mahmud Lodi** were Babur's enemies at **Khanwa**, not translators.
xa: The Baburnama was written in **Chagatai Turki**.
Its two Hindu powers: **Vijayanagara and Mewar**.

127.s:
Consider the following statements about Babur's account of India:
1. He counted five Muslim and two Hindu powers, the Hindu ones being Vijayanagara and Mewar.
2. He praised Rana Sanga as the most powerful ruler in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
127.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Babur praised Krishnadevaraya as the most powerful ruler. So 1 only (A).
127.tq: Baburnama praises Krishnadevaraya.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: Babur counted **five Muslim and two Hindu powers** — **Vijayanagara and Mewar**.
Statement 2 is wrong: he praised **Krishnadevaraya**, not Rana Sanga, as the most powerful.
xa: Babur was a contemporary of **Krishnadevaraya** and Golconda's **Sultan Quli**.
The Baburnama is in **Chagatai Turki**; translated by **Leyden and Erskine** (**1826**).

127.s: The first Mughal garden is generally identified as
o: Ram Bagh or Aram Bagh at Agra
127.x: Ram Bagh, also called Aram Bagh, at Agra was the first Mughal garden. It reflected the charbagh, or four-quartered, design.
127.tq: Match the garden with its location and historical distinction.
xs: **Ram Bagh (Aram Bagh)** at **Agra** was the first Mughal garden — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Bagh-e-Babur** at Kabul is Babur's **burial place**.
xa: Babur also built the **Kabuli Bagh mosque** at **Panipat**, for the **1526** victory.
He built a mosque at **Agra** too.
His coins: silver **Shahrukhi**, Timurid style.

127.s: The Kabuli Bagh mosque at Panipat commemorates
127.x: The Kabuli Bagh mosque at Panipat commemorates Babur’s victory in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.
127.tq: Match the monument with the event and year it commemorates.
xs: The **Kabuli Bagh mosque** at **Panipat** commemorates Babur's victory of **1526** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Khanwa** (**1527**) earned him the title **"Ghazi"**, not this mosque.
xa: Panipat gave him **Delhi and Agra** and the Lodi treasure.
Kabuli Bagh mosque is a **practice MCQ** theme, with Tulughma and the Rumi method.
**Ram Bagh** at Agra was the first Mughal garden.

127.s: Which of the following statements about Babur’s architectural and monetary contributions is correct?
o: He introduced the Mansabdari system and issued gold dinars in the Ottoman style.
He built only forts and issued copper coins in the Rajput style.
He introduced the charbagh and issued silver Shahrukhi coins in the Timurid style.
He introduced Persian as the language of Baburnama and issued silver rupees in the Safavid style.
127.x: Babur introduced the charbagh garden and issued silver Shahrukhi coins in the Timurid style.
127.tq: Select the option that combines two independently correct contributions without importing later institutions.
xs: Babur's garden and silver **Shahrukhi** coins in **Timurid** style — option **(3)** — is correct.
His garden **Ram Bagh (Aram Bagh)** at **Agra** was the **first Mughal garden**.
⚠ The **Mansabdari system** is **Akbar's**; the Baburnama is in **Chagatai Turki**, not Persian.
xa: He built the **Kabuli Bagh mosque** at Panipat and a mosque at **Agra**.
His paternal descent was from **Timur**.

127.s: Which of the following statements correctly explains the historical significance of the First Battle of Panipat?
o: It ended Mughal rule and restored the Delhi Sultanate.
It ended Lodi rule and initiated Mughal rule in India.
It marked the beginning of Akbar’s reign.
It established Rajput supremacy over northern India.
127.x: Panipat I ended the rule of the Lodis, the last dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, and began Mughal rule in India.
127.tq: Identify the political transition caused by the battle rather than a later Mughal event.
xs: **Panipat I** ended **Lodi** rule and began **Mughal rule** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Lodis** were the last Delhi Sultanate dynasty; **Ibrahim Lodi** was the last Delhi Sultan.
**Khanwa**, not Panipat, broke **Rajput** power.
xa: Panipat = first major **field-artillery** battle in North India.
Babur's **12,000** beat about **1,00,000** troops.
Panipat gave him **Delhi and Agra** (APPSC-GS **2023**).

127.s: Which of the following statements about Babur’s relations with the Deccan is correct?
o: Babur made Golconda his provincial capital.
Babur defeated Sultan Quli of Golconda at Ghaghra.
The Mughals did not interfere in the Deccan during Babur’s time.
Babur conquered the Deccan before the Battle of Khanwa.
127.x: The Mughals did not interfere in the Deccan during Babur’s time. Babur was a contemporary of Krishnadevaraya and Golconda’s Sultan Quli.
127.tq: Reject the exaggerated conquest claim and retain the stated scope of Babur’s activity.
xs: The **Mughals did not interfere in the Deccan** in Babur's time — so option **(3)** is correct.
Babur's empire reached only the **borders of Bihar**.
xa: Babur was a contemporary of **Krishnadevaraya** and Golconda's **Sultan Quli**.
In the Baburnama he praised **Krishnadevaraya** as the most powerful ruler.
His two Hindu powers: **Vijayanagara and Mewar**.

127.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ibrahim Lodi was the last Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate.
2. Panipat I was the first major field-artillery battle in North India.
3. Babur’s victory at Panipat immediately created a fully consolidated Mughal administrative system.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
127.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Ibrahim Lodi was the last Delhi Sultan, and Panipat I was the first major field-artillery battle in North India. Statement 3 is false: Babur's authority had shallow roots and he left no administrative system, so Panipat did not create a consolidated Mughal administration.
127.tq: Combine two significance statements with a deliberately overstated administrative conclusion.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Ibrahim Lodi** was the **last Delhi Sultan**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Panipat I** was the first major **field-artillery** battle in North India.
Statement 3 is wrong: Babur's authority had **shallow roots** and he left **no administrative system**.
xa: His treasury was **empty**, depleted by lavish gifts that earned him the nickname **"Qalandar"**.
⚠ The Mansabdari system is **Akbar's**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Babur:
1. He was born in Farghana and descended from Timur on his father's side and Genghis Khan on his mother's side.
2. He had held Samarkand and Kabul.
3. After Panipat he occupied Lahore and Kabul.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: after Panipat Babur occupied Delhi and Agra. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
128.tq: Panipat gains = Delhi and Agra.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: Babur was born in **Farghana**, descended from **Timur** (father) and **Genghis Khan** (mother).
Statement 2 is correct: he had held **Samarkand** and **Kabul**.
Statement 3 is wrong: after Panipat he occupied **Delhi and Agra** (APPSC **2023**).
xa: His memoir **Tuzuk-i-Baburi** is in **Chaghatai Turkish** and praises **Krishnadevaraya**.
Panipat was the first large-scale use of **gunpowder artillery** in Indian warfare.
Babur's battles in order: **Panipat I → Khanwa → Chanderi → Ghaghra** (UKPSC **2024**).

128.s:
Consider the following statements about the Tuzuk-i-Baburi:
1. It was written in Persian.
2. It praises Krishnadevaraya.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the Baburnama was written in Chaghatai Turkish (Persian was the Mughal court language). Statement 2 is correct. So 2 only (B).
128.tq: Baburnama = Chaghatai Turkish, not Persian.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is wrong: the **Tuzuk-i-Baburi** was written in **Chaghatai Turkish**, not Persian.
Statement 2 is correct: it **praises Krishnadevaraya**.
xa: Babur's tactics: **Tulughma** (cavalry flanking) and the **Rumi (Ottoman) method**.
After Panipat he occupied **Delhi and Agra**.
**Sultan Quli Qutb Shah** of Golconda (**1518-43**) was Babur's contemporary.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Babur's tactics:
1. Tulughma was rapid cavalry flanking and encircling.
2. The Rumi method linked carts into a barrier sheltering matchlockmen and artillery.
3. The Rumi method was of Uzbek origin.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Rumi method was Ottoman. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
128.tq: Rumi = Rome/Ottoman.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Tulughma** = rapid cavalry **flanking and encircling**.
Statement 2 is correct: the **Rumi method** linked **carts** into a barrier sheltering matchlockmen and artillery.
Statement 3 is wrong: the Rumi method was **Ottoman**, not Uzbek.
xa: Panipat I (**21 Apr 1526**): Babur beat **Ibrahim Lodi**; artillery decisive.
These tactics were tested in a PMF IAS practice item (**Apr 2026**).
**Kabuli Bagh Mosque** at Panipat marks **1526**.

128.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with Babur’s architectural or garden works?
o: Charbagh — a system of horse branding
128.x: Babur built the Kabuli Bagh Mosque at Panipat to commemorate the events of 1526. He also introduced the Charbagh and built Ram Bagh at Agra.
128.tq: Start with the sure monument–place pair and eliminate shifted locations or meanings.
xs: **Kabuli Bagh Mosque — Panipat** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Ram Bagh** is at **Agra**, not Delhi; it is the **first Mughal garden**.
The **Charbagh** is a garden plan Babur introduced; horse branding is **dagh**.
**Sasaram** has **Sher Shah's tomb**, not the Kabuli Bagh Mosque.
xa: The mosque marks the **1526** victory at Panipat.
After Panipat Babur occupied **Delhi and Agra**.

128.s: Which one of the following was NOT mentioned as one of Humayun's initial problems?
o: Rivalry of Kamran, Askari and Hindal
The challenge from Bahadur Shah of Gujarat-Malwa
128.x: Humayun's initial problems included his rival brothers, the Afghans, Bahadur Shah of Gujarat-Malwa and an empty treasury. Rana Sanga was not listed among these problems.
128.tq: Find the option outside the closely related group of contemporary challenges.
xs: A conflict with **Rana Sanga** was not one of Humayun's initial problems — so option **(1)** is the answer.
His problems: rival brothers **Kamran, Askari, Hindal**; the **Afghans**; **Bahadur Shah** of Gujarat-Malwa; an **empty treasury**.
Rana Sanga was **Babur's** enemy at **Khanwa (1527)**.
xa: Humayun acceded on **29 Dec 1530**, three days after Babur's death.
At **Dourah** he drove **Mahmud Lodi** from **Jaunpur**.

128.s: At Dourah, Humayun defeated the Afghans and drove which person from Jaunpur?
128.x: Humayun defeated the Afghans at Dourah and drove Mahmud Lodi from Jaunpur.
128.tq: Match the battlefield with the specific opponent or consequence.
xs: At **Dourah**, Humayun beat the Afghans and drove **Mahmud Lodi** from **Jaunpur** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He also lifted the siege of **Kalinjar**.
**Sikandar Sur** was beaten later at **Sirhind** (**1555**); **Sher Khan** beat Humayun; **Hemu** fought Akbar.
xa: Mahmud Lodi earlier joined Rana Sanga at **Khanwa**.
In **Gujarat (1535)**, Bahadur Shah let the **Portuguese** fortify **Diu**.
Sher Khan won at **Surajgarh** and took **Gaur** (**1538**).

128.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Gujarat, 1535 — Bahadur Shah allowed the Portuguese to fortify Diu
128.x: When pressed by Humayun in Gujarat in 1535, Bahadur Shah allowed the Portuguese to fortify Diu. Humayun was defeated at Chausa and Kannauj, while he defeated Sikandar Sur at Sirhind.
128.tq: Separate victories from defeats by checking the result attached to each event.
xs: **Gujarat, 1535 — Bahadur Shah let the Portuguese fortify Diu** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
At **Chausa (1539)** and **Kannauj (1540)**, **Sher Khan** defeated Humayun, not the reverse.
At **Sirhind (1555)**, **Humayun** defeated **Sikandar Sur**.
xa: After Kannauj, Humayun went into **exile**.
He returned in **July 1555**, retaking **Delhi and Agra**.
⚠ "Jahangir - Chausa" is a planted wrong pair (APPSC G2 **2025**).

128.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Kannauj and Bilgram:
1. They refer to the same battle fought in 1540.
2. The battle was won by Sher Khan.
3. Humayun was driven into exile after the battle.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: Kannauj and Bilgram are two names for the same 1540 battle. Sher Khan won it, and Humayun was consequently driven into exile.
128.tq: Test whether apparently different names denote the same historical event.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statement 1: **Kannauj** and **Bilgram** are one battle (**1540**).
Statement 2: **Sher Khan** won it.
Statement 3: Humayun was driven into **exile**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes wrongly list "Bilgram (1540)" as a Humayun victory.
After Kannauj, Sher Shah **took the throne**.
In exile, **Akbar** was born at **Amarkot** (**1542**).

128.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding Samugarh?
o: It was fought in 1539 between Babur and Mahmud Lodi.
It was fought in 1540 between Humayun and Sher Khan.
It was fought in 1555 between Humayun and Hemu.
It was fought in 1658 between Aurangzeb and Dara Shikoh.
128.x: The Battle of Samugarh was fought in 1658 between Aurangzeb and Dara Shikoh. It was not a battle of Humayun's return in 1555.
128.tq: Discriminate between closely placed Mughal dates and similarly named battles.
xs: **Samugarh** was fought in **1658** between **Aurangzeb and Dara** — so option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes wrongly list a "Battle of Samugarh (**1555**) Humayun vs Hemu".
**1540** was **Kannauj/Bilgram** (Humayun vs Sher Khan); **1555** was **Sirhind** (Humayun vs Sikandar Sur).
xa: **Hemu** fought Akbar/Bairam Khan at **Second Panipat** (**5 Nov 1556**).
**Panipat III (1761)**: Marathas vs **Ahmad Shah Abdali**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Sher Shah's early life:
1. He was born Farid, of the Afghan Sur tribe.
2. Babur gave him the title 'Sher Khan' for slaying a tiger.
3. He served Babur and later became the de facto ruler of Bihar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the title 'Sher Khan' was given by Bahar Khan of Bihar. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 2.
128.tq: Sher Khan title = Bahar Khan of Bihar.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: he was born **Farid**, of the Afghan **Sur** tribe.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Bahar Khan** of Bihar gave him the title **"Sher Khan"** for slaying a tiger.
Statement 3 is correct: he served Babur and became **deputy regent (de facto ruler)** of Bihar.
xa: He studied at **Jaunpur** and managed his father's jagir from **1511**.
⚠ **"Sher Shah"** was assumed after **Chausa (1539)**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Sher Shah's rise:
1. Surajgarh was the turning point, after which he took Gaur (1538).
2. He assumed the title 'Sher Shah' after the Battle of Kannauj (1540).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: he took the title Sher Shah after Chausa (1539); after Kannauj (1540) he took the throne. So 1 only (A).
128.tq: Chausa = title; Kannauj = throne.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Surajgarh** was the turning point; he took **Gaur** (**1538**).
Statement 2 is wrong: he became **"Sher Shah"** after **Chausa (1539)**; after **Kannauj (1540)** he **took the throne**.
xa: ⚠ **"Sher Khan"** = from **Bahar Khan** (tiger).
Sher Shah's reign: **1540-45**.
He died in **1545** during the siege of **Kalinjar**.

128.s: Which of the following places was NOT included among Sher Shah's listed conquests?
128.x: The listed conquests were Malwa, Raisen and Marwar. Kandahar was associated with Humayun's recovery with Safavid help.
128.tq: Find the geographically related but historically separate place.
xs: **Kandahar** was not among Sher Shah's conquests — so option **(3)** is the answer.
His conquests: **Malwa**, **Raisen** (Puran Mal) and **Marwar** (Maldeo).
Kandahar was retaken by **Humayun** with help from **Shah Tahmasp** of Persia.
xa: At **Samel (1544)**, Maldeo's generals **Jaita and Kumpa** nearly beat Sher Shah.
Sher Shah said he nearly lost Hindustan **"for a handful of bajra"**.

128.s: Raisen was conquered by Sher Shah from
128.x: Sher Shah's conquest of Raisen was associated with Puran Mal.
128.tq: Match the conquered centre with the ruler or chief connected with it.
xs: Sher Shah took **Raisen** from **Puran Mal** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Maldeo** was the ruler of **Marwar**; **Sikandar Sur** was a later Sur rival; **Medini Rai** fought Babur at **Chanderi**.
xa: Other conquests: **Malwa** and **Marwar**.
At **Samel (1544)**, Maldeo's generals **Jaita and Kumpa** fought hard.

128.s: Sher Shah's remark about nearly losing Hindustan 'for a handful of bajra' was made in connection with the battle of
128.x: The remark referred to the hard-fought Battle of Samel against Maldeo of Marwar.
128.tq: Use a memorable quotation as a clue to the associated battle and opponent.
xs: The **"handful of bajra"** remark refers to **Samel** (**Sammel/Giri-Sumel**, **1544**) against **Maldeo** of Marwar — so option **(3)** is correct.
Maldeo's generals **Jaita and Kumpa** fought so hard that Sher Shah said he nearly lost Hindustan.
**Chausa** was against Humayun, **Sirhind** was Humayun vs Sikandar Sur, and **Bahar Khan** gave him the "Sher Khan" title.
xa: Other conquests: **Malwa**, **Raisen** (Puran Mal).
Sher Shah died in **1545** at **Kalinjar**.

128.s: Which pair is correctly matched regarding the Rajput resistance to Sher Shah?
o: Jaita and Kumpa — generals of Maldeo of Marwar
Jaita and Kumpa — generals of Bahadur Shah of Gujarat
Puran Mal and Maldeo — generals of Sher Shah
Maldeo and Sikandar Sur — generals of Hemu
128.x: Jaita and Kumpa were associated with Maldeo of Marwar and fought with great valour against Sher Shah at Samel.
128.tq: Start from the sure person–place association and eliminate swapped commanders.
xs: **Jaita and Kumpa** were the generals of **Maldeo of Marwar** — so option **(1)** is correct.
They fought at **Samel (1544)** so hard that Sher Shah nearly lost Hindustan "for a handful of bajra".
**Puran Mal** (Raisen) and **Maldeo** were Sher Shah's enemies, not his generals.
**Hemu** was the general of **Muhammad Adil Shah**; Sikandar Sur was Adil Shah's rival.
xa: The battle is also called **Sammel/Giri-Sumel**.
Sher Shah's other conquests: **Malwa** and **Raisen**.

128.s: Sher Shah died in 1545 in a gunpowder explosion during the siege of
128.x: Sher Shah died in 1545 in a gunpowder explosion during the siege of Kalinjar.
128.tq: Associate the ruler's death with the exact military operation rather than merely the year.
xs: Sher Shah died in **1545** in a gunpowder explosion during the siege of **Kalinjar** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Raisen** was taken from Puran Mal; **Gaur** was taken in **1538**.
xa: Humayun had earlier lifted a siege of **Kalinjar** after **Dourah**.
Successor: **Islam Shah** (**Jalal Khan**, **1545-53**).
Sher Shah's tomb is at **Sasaram** (Bihar), an **octagonal tomb in a tank**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Humayun's exile:
1. He married Hamida Banu Begum.
2. Akbar was born at Amarkot in 1542.
3. Bahadur Shah of Gujarat helped him retake Kandahar and Kabul.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Safavid Shah Tahmasp of Persia helped him retake Kandahar and Kabul. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
128.tq: Exile help came from Persia (Shah Tahmasp).
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: Humayun married **Hamida Banu Begum**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Akbar** was born at **Amarkot** (**1542**).
Statement 3 is wrong: Safavid **Shah Tahmasp** of Persia helped him retake **Kandahar and Kabul**; Bahadur Shah was an enemy.
xa: Humayun went to **Persia**, forming an alliance with the **Safavids**.
He returned in **July 1555**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Humayun's return and death:
1. He returned in July 1555, exploiting quarrels among Sher Shah's successors.
2. He defeated Sikandar Sur at Machhiwara and Sirhind and then took Delhi and Agra.
3. He died in January 1556 after falling from the stairs of the library in Agra Fort.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: he fell from the stairs of the Sher Mandal library in the Purana Qila, Delhi. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
128.tq: Humayun's fatal fall = Sher Mandal, Purana Qila.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: he returned in **July 1555**, exploiting quarrels among Sher Shah's successors.
Statement 2 is correct: he beat **Sikandar Sur** at **Machhiwara and Sirhind**, then took **Delhi and Agra**.
Statement 3 is wrong: he fell from the stairs of the **Sher Mandal** library in the **Purana Qila**, Delhi (**January 1556**).
xa: The **Purana Qila** was begun by Humayun and rebuilt by Sher Shah.
**Humayun-nama** was written by his sister **Gulbadan Begum**.

128.s: Which of the following statements about Muhammad Adil Shah is correct?
o: He ruled in the east and his general and minister was Hemu.
He ruled Delhi throughout Humayun's exile and appointed Bairam Khan.
He was the ruler of Marwar who resisted Sher Shah.
He helped Humayun recover Kandahar from the Safavids.
128.x: Muhammad Adil Shah ruled in the east, and Hemu served as his general and minister.
128.tq: Test the ruler–region–minister relationship while avoiding swapped roles.
xs: **Muhammad Adil Shah** ruled in the **east**, and **Hemu** was his Hindu minister-general — so option **(1)** is correct.
He fought **Sikandar Sur**; he did not rule Delhi during Humayun's exile (that was **Sher Shah**, then **Islam Shah**).
The ruler of **Marwar** who resisted Sher Shah was **Maldeo**.
xa: Hemu seized **Agra and Delhi** (**1556**) and took the title **"Vikramaditya"**.
Hemu lost **Panipat II (5 Nov 1556)**.
