128.s: Hemu seized Agra and Delhi in 1556 and assumed the title
128.x: After occupying Agra and Delhi in 1556, Hemu took the title Vikramaditya.
128.tq: Match a political achievement with the title assumed immediately thereafter.
xs: **Hemu** took the title **"Vikramaditya"** after seizing **Agra and Delhi** (**1556**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**"Sher Shah"** was Farid's title after **Chausa (1539)**.
xa: Hemu was **Adil Shah's** Hindu minister-general.
At **Panipat II (5 Nov 1556)** an arrow struck his eye; he was captured.
Panipat II ended **Afghan power**.

128.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the political situation after Sher Shah's death?
o: Bahadur Shah of Gujarat became the undisputed successor.
Islam Shah succeeded him, followed by rival claims involving Adil Shah and Sikandar Sur.
Humayun immediately succeeded him without opposition and ruled continuously.
Hemu succeeded him as Sultan and ended all Afghan rivalry.
128.x: Islam Shah succeeded Sher Shah. Later, Muhammad Adil Shah in the east and Sikandar Sur fought each other amid the fragmentation of Sur power.
128.tq: Infer the succession pattern from the sequence of rulers and competing claimants.
xs: **Islam Shah** succeeded Sher Shah; later **Muhammad Adil Shah** and **Sikandar Sur** fought each other — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Humayun** returned only in **July 1555**, exploiting these quarrels.
**Hemu** was Adil Shah's general, not Sultan; his defeat at Panipat II ended Afghan power.
xa: Islam Shah = **Jalal Khan**, **1545-53**.
Surs = **last Afghan dynasty** to rule Delhi.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about the Second Battle of Panipat:
1. It was fought on 5 November 1556.
2. Hemu was struck in the eye by an arrow and captured.
3. It marked the end of Afghan power in the relevant political context.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: All three statements are correct. The defeat and capture of Hemu at the battle helped end Afghan power in north India.
128.tq: Combine the date, battlefield incident and political consequence in one statement set.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statement 1: **Panipat II** was fought on **5 Nov 1556**.
Statement 2: an **arrow struck Hemu's eye**; he was captured.
Statement 3: it marked the **end of Afghan power**.
xa: The Mughal side was led by **Akbar/Bairam Khan**.
⚠ "Tipu vs Marathas" is **not** Panipat II.
**Panipat III (1761)**: Marathas vs **Ahmad Shah Abdali**.

128.s: The Humayun-nama was written by
128.x: The Humayun-nama was written by Humayun's sister Gulbadan Begum. Hamida Banu Begum was Humayun's wife and Akbar's mother; Abul Fazl wrote the Akbarnama; Babur wrote the Tuzuk-i-Baburi.
128.tq: Gulbadan = Humayun's sister = Humayun-nama
xs: The **Humayun-nama** was written by Humayun's sister **Gulbadan Begum** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Hamida Banu Begum** was Humayun's wife and **Akbar's** mother.
**Babur** wrote the **Tuzuk-i-Baburi**.
xa: Akbar was born at **Amarkot** (**1542**).
Humayun died in **January 1556** at the **Sher Mandal** library, **Purana Qila**.

128.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Sher Shah's army and administration is correct?
o: Hindus were excluded from all important military positions
Hindus were appointed to high posts in the army
Only Persian merchants could hold army offices
High army posts were reserved for foreign cavalrymen
128.x: Sher Shah's administration included Hindus in high army posts, reflecting a practical and inclusive policy.
128.tq: Watch for the absolute exclusion trap in statements about official appointments.
xs: In Sher Shah's army, **Hindus held high posts** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The army was **regular**, **directly recruited** and **strictly disciplined**.
xa: **Dagh** (horse branding) and **chehra/huliya** (descriptive roll) prevented fraud.
Hemu, a Hindu, was later **Adil Shah's** minister-general.
Officers were **frequently transferred**.

128.s: Sher Shah opened maktabs and provided stipends primarily to
128.x: The opening of maktabs with stipends was an educational measure intended to support learning.
128.tq: Match an institution and financial provision with their social purpose.
xs: Sher Shah opened **maktabs** (schools) with **scholarships/stipends** to **support education** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Coin weights, horse branding (**dagh**) and roadside trees were separate reforms.
xa: Sarais along roads had **shady trees** planted.
Justice was **uniform and harsh**.
Local headmen were responsible for **detecting crime**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Sur sarkar administration:
1. The Chief Shiqdar (shiqdar-i-shiqdaran) looked after law and order in a sarkar.
2. The Chief Munsif (munsif-i-munsifan) was the treasurer of a pargana.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Chief Munsif was the sarkar-level revenue/civil officer; the pargana treasurer was the fotedar. So 1 only (A).
128.tq: Sarkar: Chief Shiqdar + Chief Munsif; pargana treasurer = fotedar.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **Chief Shiqdar** (shiqdar-i-shiqdaran) handled **law and order** in a sarkar.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **Chief Munsif** (munsif-i-munsifan) was the sarkar's **revenue/civil** officer; the pargana treasurer was the **fotedar**.
xa: Pargana officers: **Shiqdar**, **Amin** (munsif), **fotedar**, **Hindi and Persian writers** (karkuns).
Officers were **frequently transferred**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the officers of a Sur-era pargana:
1. The Shiqdar was an officer of the pargana.
2. The Fotedar functioned as treasurer.
3. Karkuns included Hindi and Persian writers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: All three statements are correct. The pargana had a Shiqdar, Amin, Fotedar and Hindi and Persian-writing Karkuns.
128.tq: Check each statement against the composition of the pargana administration.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statement 1: the **Shiqdar** was a pargana officer.
Statement 2: the **fotedar** was the treasurer.
Statement 3: **karkuns** were **Hindi and Persian writers**.
xa: The pargana also had an **Amin** (munsif).
Sarkar level: **Chief Shiqdar** (law and order) and **Chief Munsif** (revenue/civil).

128.s: Which administrative practice was adopted to prevent local officials from developing entrenched interests under the Sur rulers?
o: Election of officers by village assemblies
128.x: Sur officers were frequently transferred, limiting the growth of local personal power and vested interests.
128.tq: Infer the administrative purpose from the stated institutional practice.
xs: Sur officers were **frequently transferred** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Life, elected or hereditary posts are not in the Sur system.
xa: Sarkar level: **Chief Shiqdar** and **Chief Munsif**.
The army was **directly recruited**, with **dagh** and **chehra** against fraud.
An efficient **espionage** system backed the administration.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sur army:
1. It was a regular army, directly recruited and strictly disciplined.
2. 'Dagh' meant the descriptive roll of soldiers, while 'chehra' meant the branding of horses.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 reverses the terms: dagh was horse branding and chehra/huliya the descriptive roll of soldiers. So 1 only (A).
128.tq: Dagh = horse brand; chehra = face/description of soldier.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the army was **regular**, **directly recruited** and **strictly disciplined**.
Statement 2 is wrong — it reverses the terms: **dagh** = **horse branding**; **chehra/huliya** = **descriptive roll** of soldiers.
xa: Both measures were aimed **against fraud**.
**Hindus** held high army posts.

128.s: Which statement about policing under the Sur administration is correct?
o: Public morals were regulated only by village accountants.
Local headmen were made responsible for detecting crime.
Crime detection was entrusted exclusively to the central army.
The Sur rulers had no organised espionage system.
128.x: Local headmen were held responsible for detecting crime. The system also included censors of public morals and an efficient espionage network.
128.tq: Test the responsible authority and reject the exclusive or negative claims.
xs: **Local headmen** were made responsible for **detecting crime** — so option **(2)** is correct.
There were **censors of public morals** and an efficient **espionage** system — so options (1) and (4) are wrong.
xa: Justice was **uniform** and **harsh**.
Sarkar law and order lay with the **Chief Shiqdar**.
Officers were **frequently transferred**.

128.s: The unit of measurement used in Sher Shah's land-revenue survey was known as
128.x: Sher Shah introduced a uniform system of land measurement using the sikandari gaz, also called gaz-i-Sikandari.
128.tq: Use the exact official term to distinguish closely related measurement units.
xs: Sher Shah's survey used the **gaz-i-Sikandari** (sikandari gaz) — so option **(2)** is correct.
Land was measured under a **uniform system**, with a rope/**jarib**.
xa: Land had **three categories**: good, middling, bad.
State share: **one-third** of average produce.
His system was the model for **Todar Mal's Bandobast**.

128.s: Sher Shah classified agricultural land into which of the following categories on the basis of its produce?
128.x: Land was classified as good, middling or bad according to its productivity.
128.tq: Test the precise three-part classification rather than a familiar alternative classification.
xs: Land was classed **good, middling and bad** by produce — so option **(1)** is correct.
This is the **three**-category system; **Akbar-Todar Mal** used **four** classes (**polaj, parauti, chachar, banjar**).
xa: APPSC-G1 **2024** key: "three categories" and "uniform measurement" true.
State share: **one-third** of average produce, in **cash or grain**.
Akbar used **ten-year averages**.

128.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with Sher Shah's revenue administration?
o: Qanungo — command of the royal cavalry
128.x: The amin made the revenue assessment in Sher Shah's system. The shiqdar, qanungo and patwari were also revenue/local officials; none of them prepared manuscripts, commanded the cavalry or minted coins, so B, C and D are false pairs.
128.tq: Use the 'who would do this job?' method to identify the official function.
xs: **Amin — assessment of revenue** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
The Amin assessed revenue together with the **shiqdar, qanungo and patwari** — all revenue/local officials.
None of them prepared manuscripts, commanded cavalry or minted coins.
xa: **Jaribana** = surveyor's fee; **Muhasilana** = collector's fee.
**Patta** = title deed; **Qabuliyat** = peasant's deed of acceptance.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Sher Shah's land revenue system:
1. His direct settlement with cultivators removed illegal demands and recognised tenant rights.
2. It became the model for Todar Mal's Bandobast.
3. The state's share was fixed at one-fourth of the average produce.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the state share was one-third of average produce (APPSC-G1 2024 key marks 'one-fourth' false). So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
128.tq: Sher Shah's share = one-third; 'one-fourth' is the trap.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **direct settlement** with cultivators removed illegal demands and recognised **tenant rights**.
Statement 2 is correct: it was the model for **Todar Mal's Bandobast**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the share was **one-third**; APPSC-G1 **2024** key marks "one-fourth" false.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say "one-fourth to one-third".
Some notes call Sher Shah the first to introduce a **ryotwari**-type system.

128.s: Under Sher Shah's revenue system, the state's share was generally fixed at
o: One-fourth of the average produce, payable only in cash
One-half of the actual produce, payable only in grain
One-sixth of the assessed produce, payable in cash or kind
One-third of the average produce, payable in cash or grain
128.x: The state demand was one-third of the average produce and could be paid either in cash or in grain.
128.tq: Separate the correct fraction from the payment mode; both details must be matched.
xs: The state's share was **one-third of the average produce**, payable in **cash or grain** — so option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ "One-fourth" is the trap; APPSC-G1 **2024** marks it false.
xa: Land was classed **good, middling, bad**.
**Akbar-Todar Mal** kept **1/3** but used **ten-year averages**.
The **Patta** stated each peasant's revenue dues.

128.s: In Sher Shah's revenue system, the Qabuliyat was
o: the title deed given to the peasant stating his revenue dues
the deed of agreement signed by the peasant accepting the revenue demand
the fee paid to the surveyor
the fee paid to the revenue collector
128.x: The Qabuliyat was the peasant's deed of acceptance of the revenue demand, signed by him. The Patta was the title deed given to the cultivator. Jaribana was the surveyor's fee and muhasilana the collector's fee.
128.tq: Patta given to peasant; Qabuliyat signed by peasant
xs: The **Qabuliyat** was the peasant's **deed of agreement** accepting the revenue demand, **signed by him** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Patta** was the **title deed** given to the cultivator.
**Jaribana** = surveyor's fee; **Muhasilana** = collector's fee.
xa: ⚠ **Patta** = given by the state; **Qabuliyat** = signed by the peasant.
Assessment was by the **Amin**, with shiqdar, qanungo and patwari.

128.s: Which one of the following pairs relating to Sher Shah's currency is correctly matched?
128.x: The rupiya was a silver coin. The dam was copper, while the mohur or ashrafi was a gold coin.
128.tq: Use metal–coin pairing to separate the three denominations.
xs: **Rupiya — silver** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **dam** was **copper**; the **mohur / ashrafi** was **gold**.
xa: The rupiya weighed about **178 grains**, introduced **1540-45** (APPSC-GS **2019**).
It remained standard for centuries (APPSC-G2 **2017**).
Sher Shah minted **pure** gold and silver coins.

128.s: The approximate weight of Sher Shah's silver rupiya was
128.x: Sher Shah's rupiya was a silver coin weighing approximately 178 grains.
128.tq: Recall the distinctive numerical value and reject nearby altered figures.
xs: The silver **rupiya** weighed about **178 grains** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was introduced **1540-45** (APPSC-GS **2019**).
xa: The rupiya remained standard for centuries (APPSC-G2 **2017**).
**Dam** = copper; **mohur/ashrafi** = gold.
**Rupiya** began with Sher Shah — a FIRST.

128.s: Sher Shah's currency reform is considered important because his coinage
o: included pure gold and silver coins and outlived the Sur dynasty
replaced all metallic currency with paper notes
was confined to copper and disappeared with the Sur dynasty
was issued only for payment to foreign merchants
128.x: Sher Shah minted pure gold and silver coins, and the monetary system continued to influence currency after the Sur dynasty ended.
128.tq: Test the lasting significance of a reform rather than only its individual denominations.
xs: Sher Shah minted **pure gold and silver** coins, and the reform **outlived the Sur dynasty** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He also minted copper (**dam**), so his coinage was not copper-only.
xa: The silver **rupiya** (about **178 grains**) remained standard for centuries.
His rupiya, roads and revenue system were the base for **Akbar's** administration.

128.s: The Sadak-e-Azam constructed or restored by Sher Shah connected
o: Sonargaon in Bengal with the Indus
128.x: The major road, also called the Grand Trunk Road, ran from Sonargaon in Bengal to the Indus.
128.tq: Distinguish the principal imperial highway from the other roads associated with Sher Shah.
xs: The **Sadak-e-Azam (Grand Trunk Road)** ran from **Sonargaon (Bengal) to the Indus** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Lahore-Multan** and **Agra-Burhanpur** were his other, shorter roads.
xa: APPSC-G1 **2022** answer: "Indus to Sonargaon"; APPSC-GS **2018**: he **restored** it.
⚠ Some notes say **Chittagong-Kabul**, about **1,500 miles**.
Another road: **Agra-Jodhpur-Chittor**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Sher Shah's sarais:
1. They were built along roads, with shady trees planted for travellers.
2. They gave common lodging with no separate arrangement for Hindus and Muslims.
3. They served as dak-chowkis for relaying news and mail.
4. Market towns grew around them.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the sarais had separate lodging for Hindus and Muslims. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 2.
128.tq: Sarais: roads + trees, separate lodging, dak-chowki, market towns.
xs: Statements **1, 3 and 4 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: sarais stood along roads, with **shady trees**.
Statement 2 is wrong: there was **separate lodging for Hindus and Muslims**.
Statements 3 and 4 are correct: they served as **dak-chowkis** and **market towns** grew around them.
xa: Dak-chowkis were post stations relaying news and mail, with **horses**.
The **Grand Trunk Road** ran from **Sonargaon** to the **Indus**.

128.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Road)
a. Sadak-e-Azam
b. Agra–Burhanpur
c. Agra–Jodhpur–Chittor
d. Lahore–Multan

List-II (Association)
i. Major road from Bengal to the Indus
ii. Road linking Lahore and Multan
iii. Road linking Agra and Burhanpur
iv. Road linking Agra, Jodhpur and Chittor
128.x: Sadak-e-Azam was the Bengal–Indus highway; the remaining pairs reproduce the three other routes correctly.
128.tq: Start from the sure route pair and eliminate codes that repeat or misplace the roads.
xs: **a–i, b–iii, c–iv, d–ii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Sadak-e-Azam** = the Bengal-to-Indus highway (**Sonargaon to the Indus**).
The other three roads link exactly the places named: **Agra-Burhanpur**, **Agra-Jodhpur-Chittor**, **Lahore-Multan**.
xa: The Grand Trunk Road still exists.
Sarais along the roads doubled as **dak-chowkis**.

128.s: Sher Shah's tomb at Sasaram is notable for being
o: a four-domed marble mausoleum in Agra
an octagonal tomb set in a tank
a circular tomb built inside the Purana Qila
128.x: The tomb at Sasaram is an octagonal monument surrounded by water in a tank.
128.tq: Use the distinctive architectural feature to distinguish the monument from other Sur structures.
xs: **Sher Shah's tomb** at **Sasaram** (Bihar) is an **octagonal tomb in a tank** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Rohtas fort** is in present-day **Pakistan**; the **Purana Qila** is in **Delhi**.
xa: Sher Shah rebuilt the **Purana Qila** (Dinpanah), begun by **Humayun**.
He built the **Qila-i-Kuhna mosque** inside it.
**Humayun's Tomb** is the first **garden tomb**, with a **double dome**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Rohtas fort:
1. It is located at Sasaram in Bihar.
2. It is known for its angled walls and bastions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statement 1 is wrong: Rohtas fort is in present-day Pakistan; Sasaram has Sher Shah's tomb. Statement 2 is correct. So 2 only (B); A, C and D misjudge the statements.
128.tq: Sasaram = tomb in a tank; Rohtas = Pakistan fort.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is wrong: **Rohtas fort** is in present-day **Pakistan**; **Sasaram** has **Sher Shah's tomb**.
Statement 2 is correct: Rohtas has **angled walls and bastions**.
xa: Sasaram tomb: **octagonal**, set in a **tank**.
**Qila-i-Kuhna mosque** stands inside the **Purana Qila**, Delhi.

128.s: Humayun's Tomb is regarded as
o: the first garden tomb of the Indian subcontinent
the first Mughal building constructed entirely of copper
the first stone fort built by Sher Shah
128.x: Humayun's Tomb is considered the first garden tomb of the Indian subcontinent.
128.tq: Use the monument's architectural classification to distinguish it from nearby Mughal and Sur structures.
xs: **Humayun's Tomb** is the **first garden tomb** of the subcontinent — so option **(2)** is correct.
It has a **double dome** and uses **red sandstone + white marble**.
xa: Humayun died in **January 1556** at the **Sher Mandal** library, **Purana Qila**.
The **Purana Qila** was begun by Humayun and rebuilt by **Sher Shah**.
**Ram Bagh**, Agra, was the first Mughal **garden**.

128.s: The Qila-i-Kuhna mosque built by Sher Shah is located in
128.x: Sher Shah built the Qila-i-Kuhna mosque inside the Purana Qila in Delhi; Humayun began the fort and Sher Shah rebuilt it. Sasaram has Sher Shah's tomb, Rohtas fort is in present-day Pakistan, and Agra Fort is not linked to this mosque.
128.tq: Qila-i-Kuhna = inside Purana Qila
xs: Sher Shah's **Qila-i-Kuhna mosque** stands inside the **Purana Qila, Delhi** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Sasaram** (Bihar) has **Sher Shah's tomb**, an octagonal tomb in a tank.
**Rohtas fort** is in present-day **Pakistan**, known for angled walls and bastions.
xa: The **Purana Qila** (Old Fort; **Dinpanah**) was begun by **Humayun** and rebuilt by **Sher Shah**.
Humayun died in **January 1556**, falling from the stairs of the **Sher Mandal** library in the Purana Qila.
**Humayun's Tomb** is the first **garden tomb**, with a **double dome**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Babur's battles:
1. At Chanderi (1528) Babur fought Medini Rai.
2. Ghaghra (1529), fought against the Afghans under Mahmud Lodi, was Babur's last battle.
3. Babur's battles in order were Panipat I, Chanderi, Khanwa and Ghaghra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the order is Panipat I (1526), Khanwa (1527), Chanderi (1528), Ghaghra (1529). So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
128.tq: Babur's order: Panipat-Khanwa-Chanderi-Ghaghra (1526-29).
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: at **Chanderi (1528)** Babur fought **Medini Rai**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Ghaghra (1529)**, against the Afghans of Bihar-Bengal (**Mahmud Lodi**), was Babur's **last battle**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the order is **Panipat I (1526) → Khanwa (1527) → Chanderi (1528) → Ghaghra (1529)** (UKPSC **2024**).
xa: Panipat I (**21 Apr 1526**): Babur beat **Ibrahim Lodi**; Mughal Empire founded.
**Khanwa** broke **Rajput** power (Babur vs **Rana Sanga**).

128.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Panipat II — Akbar and Sher Shah
128.x: Panipat II was fought in 1556 between Akbar, represented by Bairam Khan, and Hemu. Sher Shah was the opponent of Humayun at Kannauj.
128.tq: Find the wrong ruler–opponent pairing by checking the battle chronology.
xs: **Panipat II — Akbar and Sher Shah** is wrongly matched — so option **(4)** is the answer.
**Panipat II (5 Nov 1556)** was **Akbar/Bairam Khan vs Hemu**; Sher Shah had died in **1545**.
The others are correct: **Haldighati** (Akbar's general **Man Singh** vs **Maharana Pratap**), **Chausa** and **Kannauj** (Humayun vs **Sher Khan**).
xa: Panipat II ended **Afghan power**.
⚠ "Tipu vs Marathas" is not Panipat II.
Kannauj is also called **Bilgram** (**1540**).

128.s: The result of the Battle of Haldighati in 1576 was that it was
o: a decisive victory of Maharana Pratap over Man Singh
a decisive Mughal victory ending all resistance
a defeat of Akbar by Sher Khan
128.x: The Battle of Haldighati in 1576, fought between Man Singh and Maharana Pratap, was not decisive.
128.tq: Watch for exaggerated outcome words such as decisive and all.
xs: **Haldighati (1576)** was **not decisive** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was fought by Akbar's general **Man Singh** against **Maharana Pratap**.
**Sher Khan** fought Humayun, not Akbar.
xa: **Panipat II (1556)**: Akbar/Bairam Khan vs **Hemu**; Mughals won.
**Khanwa (1527)** broke Rajput power under Babur.
**Panipat III (1761)**: Marathas vs **Ahmad Shah Abdali**.

128.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
128.x: Chausa (1539) was fought by Humayun against Sher Khan, so 'Chausa - Jahangir' is the wrong pair (APPSC G2 2025). Babur fought Rana Sanga at Khanwa (1527), Humayun beat Sikandar Sur at Sirhind (1555), and the Marathas fought Ahmad Shah Abdali at Panipat III (1761).
128.tq: Chausa = Humayun vs Sher Khan, never Jahangir
xs: **Chausa - Jahangir** is the wrong pair — so option **(1)** is the answer (APPSC G2 **2025**).
**Chausa (1539)** was **Humayun vs Sher Khan**.
Correct pairs: **Khanwa — Babur** (**1527**), **Sirhind — Humayun** (**1555**), **Panipat III — Ahmad Shah Abdali** (**1761**).
xa: At Sirhind Humayun beat **Sikandar Sur** and retook Delhi and Agra.
After **Chausa**, Sher Khan assumed the title **Sher Shah**.
⚠ "Wrong pair" questions: Jahangir-Chausa is the planted mismatch.

128.s: Sher Shah’s short reign is regarded as significant for the later Mughal administration because it established a pattern in
o: maritime trade, gunpowder manufacture and temple construction
naval warfare, printing and parliamentary government
hereditary mansabdari, European diplomacy and sea power
128.x: Sher Shah’s reign set patterns for Mughal land revenue administration, the rupee-based coinage system and roads.
128.tq: Identify the correct cluster of long-term administrative influences.
xs: Sher Shah's short reign (**1540-45**) set the pattern for Mughal **land revenue**, **coinage** and **roads** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Revenue passed on via **Todar Mal**; coinage via the **rupee**.
⚠ The **Mansabdari system** is **Akbar's**, not Sher Shah's.
xa: His **rupiya**, roads and revenue system were the base for **Akbar's** administration.
**Rupiya** began with Sher Shah.
The **Grand Trunk Road** ran **Sonargaon to the Indus**.

128.s:
Which statement correctly compares the revenue systems of Sher Shah and Akbar under Todar Mal?
1. Sher Shah assessed revenue at one-third of average produce.
2. Sher Shah classified land into three categories.
3. Akbar-Todar Mal retained the one-third share but used ten-year averages.
4. Akbar-Todar Mal used four land classes: polaj, parauti, chachar and banjar.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
128.x: All four statements are correct. Sher Shah used three land classes and a one-third rate, while Akbar’s system used ten-year averages and four classes while retaining the one-third share.
128.tq: Compare the systems across both the rate and the classification method.
xs: All four statements are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statements 1 and 2: **Sher Shah** = **1/3** of average produce + **three** land classes.
Statements 3 and 4: **Akbar-Todar Mal** kept **1/3** but used **ten-year averages** + **four** classes — **polaj, parauti, chachar, banjar**.
xa: Sher Shah's classes: **good, middling, bad**.
His system was the model for **Todar Mal's Bandobast**.
⚠ APPSC-G1 **2024**: "one-fourth" for Sher Shah's share is false.

128.s: The Sur dynasty is described as the last Afghan dynasty to rule
128.x: The Surs were the last Afghan dynasty to rule Delhi.
128.tq: Distinguish the geographical centre of the dynasty from regions associated with other medieval powers.
xs: The **Surs** were the **last Afghan dynasty to rule Delhi** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Their end came at **Panipat II (5 Nov 1556)**, which ended **Afghan power**.
xa: Sur successors: **Islam Shah** (**1545-53**), then **Muhammad Adil Shah** and **Sikandar Sur**.
**Hemu**, Adil Shah's general, took the title **"Vikramaditya"**.
**Ibrahim Lodi**'s Lodis were the last **Delhi Sultanate** dynasty.

128.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sultan Quli Qutb Shah of Golconda was contemporary with Babur, Humayun and Sher Shah.
2. The Mughal rulers did not interfere in the Deccan during this period.
3. Sultan Quli Qutb Shah ruled Golconda from 1518 to 1543.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: All three statements are correct. Sultan Quli Qutb Shah ruled Golconda from 1518 to 1543 and was contemporary with the early Mughals and Sher Shah, while Mughal interference in the Deccan had not yet begun.
128.tq: Combine chronology, contemporary rulers and regional-policy facts in one check.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statements 1 and 3: **Sultan Quli Qutb Shah** of Golconda (**1518-43**) was contemporary with **Babur, Humayun and Sher Shah**.
Statement 2: the **Mughals did not interfere in the Deccan** then.
xa: Babur's **Tuzuk-i-Baburi** praises **Krishnadevaraya**.
Sher Shah's reign: **1540-45**.
Humayun acceded on **29 Dec 1530**.

129.s: Akbar was enthroned at Kalanaur in February 1556 when he was approximately:
129.x: Akbar was enthroned at Kalanaur in February 1556 at the age of 14. The ceremony took place in a garden under the supervision of Bairam Khan.
129.tq: Use the age and date together to identify the correct early-reign detail.
xs: Akbar was **14 years old** when enthroned at **Kalanaur** (**Feb 1556**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
He was enthroned in a **garden** by **Bairam Khan**.
xa: Bairam Khan's regency lasted **1556-60**.
**Panipat II (5 Nov 1556)**: Hemu hit in the eye, captured; Afghan power ended.
**Petticoat government** (**1560-64**): **Maham Anaga** and her son **Adham Khan**.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about Bairam Khan:
1. He was Akbar's regent from 1556 to 1560.
2. He was dismissed in 1560 and killed on the way to Mecca in 1561.
3. Akbar gave him the title 'Khan-i-Khanan' as part of his appointment as wazir.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
129.x: Statement 1 is correct: Bairam Khan's regency lasted 1556-60. Statement 2 is correct: he was dismissed in 1560 and killed on the way to Mecca in 1561. Statement 3 is wrong: Akbar did give him the title Khan-i-Khanan, but it was not tied to his appointment as wazir (UPPSC 2024). So '1 only' is incomplete and options with 3 are wrong.
129.tq: Regency 1556-60, dismissed 1560, killed 1561; petticoat government 1560-64 follows.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Bairam Khan's regency** lasted **1556-60**.
Statement 2 is correct: he was **dismissed in 1560** and **killed on the way to Mecca** in **1561**.
Statement 3 is wrong: Akbar gave him the title **"Khan-i-Khanan"**, but it was **not tied to his appointment as wazir** (UPPSC **2024**).
xa: Bairam Khan enthroned Akbar at **Kalanaur**.
His son **Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan** translated the **Baburnama** into Persian.

129.s: The expression 'petticoat government' in Akbar's early reign refers to the dominance of:
o: Ruqaiya Sultan Begum and Man Singh I
Hamida Banu Begum and Salima Sultan Begum
Maham Anaga and her son Adham Khan
129.x: The term refers to the period from 1560 to 1564 when Maham Anaga and her son Adham Khan exercised considerable influence.
129.tq: Match the political expression with the persons and period it denotes.
xs: **Petticoat government** (**1560-64**) was the dominance of **Maham Anaga** and her son **Adham Khan** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It followed **Bairam Khan's regency** (**1556-60**).
xa: Bairam Khan was dismissed in **1560** and killed in **1561**.
**Man Singh I** was a Kachhwaha general; **Todar Mal** was the revenue minister.
Akbar married the daughter of **Raja Bharmal of Amber** in **1562**.

129.s: The Second Battle of Panipat (5 November 1556), which ended Afghan power, was fought between Akbar's forces and:
129.x: At Panipat II (1556) Hemu was hit in the eye by an arrow and captured, ending Afghan power. Daud Khan Karrani opposed Akbar in Bengal (1576), Baz Bahadur in Malwa (1561), and Ibrahim Lodi lost the First Battle of Panipat (1526) to Babur.
129.tq: Panipat II = 1556 = Hemu (arrow in the eye).
xs: At **Panipat II (5 Nov 1556)**, Akbar's forces fought **Hemu** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Hemu was **hit in the eye by an arrow** and captured; **Afghan power ended**.
**Daud Khan Karrani** opposed Akbar in **Bengal** (**1576**); **Baz Bahadur** in **Malwa** (**1561**).
xa: Akbar was then **14**, under **Bairam Khan**.
Malwa (**1561**) was Akbar's first listed conquest.

129.s:
Match the following conquests of Akbar with the rulers opposed:

List-I (Region)
 a. Malwa
 b. Gondwana
 c. Chittor
 d. Ranthambore

List-II (Ruler)
 i. Rani Durgavati
 ii. Surjan Rai
 iii. Baz Bahadur
 iv. Rana Udai Singh

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
129.x: Baz Bahadur opposed Akbar in Malwa, Rani Durgavati in Gondwana, Rana Udai Singh at Chittor, and Surjan Rai at Ranthambore.
129.tq: Begin with a known ruler–region pair and check the remaining regional matches.
xs: **a–iii, b–i, c–iv, d–ii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Malwa** (**1561**) — **Baz Bahadur**; **Gondwana** (**1564**) — **Rani Durgavati**.
**Chittor** (**1568**) — **Rana Udai Singh**; **Ranthambore** (**1569**) — **Surjan Rai** (Hada).
xa: ⚠ Women who resisted: **Rani Durgavati** (Gondwana) and **Chand Bibi** (Ahmednagar).
In **Marwar**, **Rao Chandrasena** resisted.
Last campaign: **Asirgarh (1601)**.

129.s:
Arrange the following conquests of Akbar in chronological order:
A. Conquest of Gujarat
B. Conquest of Gondwana
C. Conquest of Kabul
D. Conquest of Chittor
129.x: Gondwana was conquered in 1564, Chittor in 1568, Gujarat in 1572–73 and Kabul in 1581.
129.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the middle conquests by year.
xs: **B, D, A, C** — so option **(1)** is correct.
xa: **Buland Darwaza** marks the Gujarat conquest.
Kabul was taken from **Mirza Hakim**, Akbar's half-brother.
**Kashmir** followed in **1586**.

129.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
129.x: Akbar conquered Gujarat in 1572–73, opposing Muzaffar Shah III. Daud Khan Karrani was associated with Bengal, Mirza Hakim with Kabul, and Chand Bibi with Ahmednagar.
129.tq: Use the region–year–ruler triple and reject swapped opponents.
xs: **Gujarat — 1572–73 — Muzaffar Shah III** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Bengal** (**1576**) was taken from **Daud Khan Karrani**, not Mirza Hakim.
**Kabul** (**1581**) was taken from **Mirza Hakim**, not Daud Khan.
**Kashmir** (**1586**) was **Yusuf Shah Chak**'s; **Chand Bibi** defended **Ahmednagar** (**1600**).
xa: **Buland Darwaza** commemorates the Gujarat conquest.
The Bengal campaign ran **1574-76**.

129.s: Akbar's last campaign was associated with the conquest of:
o: Gujarat, where Buland Darwaza was built
Khandesh, including the capture of Asirgarh fort
129.x: Akbar's last campaign was the conquest of Khandesh in 1601, during which the Asirgarh fort was taken from Miran Bahadur.
129.tq: Identify the last event in a sequence of conquests rather than the most famous one.
xs: Akbar's **last campaign** was **Khandesh**, taking **Asirgarh** fort (**1601**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was taken from **Miran Bahadur**.
**Gujarat** (Buland Darwaza), **Bengal** and **Kashmir** were earlier conquests.
xa: **Ahmednagar** fell in **1600**, resisted by **Chand Bibi**.
Akbar's empire reached the **Godavari** in the south.

129.s: Which one of the following statements about the extent of Akbar's empire is correct?
o: It extended from the Indus to the Narmada and from Gujarat to Bengal.
It extended from Kabul to Tamil Nadu and from Gujarat to Assam.
It extended from Bengal to Afghanistan and from Kashmir to the Godavari.
It was confined to northern India and did not reach the Deccan.
129.x: The extent of Akbar's empire is described as stretching from Bengal to Afghanistan and from Kashmir to the Godavari.
129.tq: Test a geographical extent through both of its stated boundaries.
xs: Akbar's empire ran from **Bengal to Afghanistan** and from **Kashmir to the Godavari** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It did reach the Deccan: **Ahmednagar** (**1600**) and **Khandesh** (**1601**).
xa: **Kashmir** was taken in **1586** from Yusuf Shah Chak.
**Kabul** was taken in **1581** from Mirza Hakim.
Golconda's **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah** kept friendly relations with Akbar.

129.s: The Battle of Haldighati formed part of Akbar's campaign against:
129.x: The Battle of Haldighati was part of Akbar's Mewar campaign. It was fought between the Mughal forces led by Man Singh and Maharana Pratap.
129.tq: Distinguish the broader campaign from nearby Rajput regions.
xs: **Haldighati** was part of Akbar's campaign against **Mewar** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes wrongly place it in the **Gujarat** campaign.
In **Marwar** it was **Rao Chandrasena** who resisted; **Khandesh** and **Malwa** were separate campaigns.
xa: Haldighati (**1576**): **Maharana Pratap** vs Mughals under **Man Singh**; not decisive.
Mewar submitted only under **Jahangir** (**Amar Singh**).
The siege of **Chittor** (**1568**) was against **Rana Udai Singh**.

129.s: Akbar's Rajput policy is best characterised as a combination of:
o: military defeat and confiscation of all autonomy
129.x: Akbar followed a twin policy of conquest and conciliation, accepting submission while restoring autonomy and honour in suitable cases.
129.tq: Choose the formulation that combines the two complementary elements of the policy.
xs: Akbar's Rajput policy combined **conquest and conciliation** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Submission was accepted, and **autonomy and honour** returned.
xa: Rajputs got **high posts**, **matrimonial alliances**, **religious toleration**, autonomy.
Equal treatment + toleration → **lasting loyalty**.
Top mansabdars: **Man Singh** and **Bhagwan Das**.

129.s: In 1562, Akbar entered into a matrimonial alliance with the daughter of:
129.x: In 1562, Akbar married the daughter of Raja Bharmal of Amber, a Kachhwaha ruler.
129.tq: Test the exact person and state connected with the matrimonial alliance.
xs: In **1562** Akbar married the daughter of **Raja Bharmal of Amber** (Kachhwaha) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Miran Bahadur** lost Asirgarh; **Rao Chandrasena** resisted in Marwar; **Rana Udai Singh** defended Chittor.
xa: **Man Singh** and **Bhagwan Das** were top mansabdars.
**Man Singh I**, Kachhwaha of Amber, led the Mughals at **Haldighati**.

129.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Akbar's Rajput policy:
1. Rajputs were appointed to high posts.
2. Matrimonial alliances formed part of the policy.
3. Religious toleration helped secure lasting Rajput loyalty.
4. Every Rajput state was immediately deprived of its autonomy after submission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: Akbar appointed Rajputs to high posts, formed matrimonial alliances and followed religious toleration. Submission could be followed by restoration of autonomy and honour, so statement 4 is false.
129.tq: Reject the absolute statement that conflicts with the conquest-plus-conciliation approach.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statements 1 and 2: Rajputs got **high posts** and **matrimonial alliances**.
Statement 3: **religious toleration** and equal treatment won **lasting loyalty**.
Statement 4 is wrong: after submission, **autonomy and honour were returned**.
xa: The policy was **conquest and conciliation**.
Prominent Rajputs: **Raja Man Singh**, **Raja Todarmal**, **Raja Birbal**.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about the Rajput holdouts against Akbar:
1. Mewar submitted to Akbar soon after the Battle of Haldighati.
2. Rao Chandrasen resisted Akbar in Marwar.
3. Mewar submitted only under Jahangir, through Amar Singh, whose son Karan Singh became a mansabdar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
129.x: Statement 1 is wrong: Mewar never submitted under Akbar; Rana Pratap fought on after Haldighati (1576). Statement 2 is correct: Rao Chandrasen resisted in Marwar. Statement 3 is correct: Mewar submitted under Jahangir (Amar Singh; son Karan Singh made a mansabdar). Hence only '2 and 3 only' fits; '1 and 2 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement, and '3 only' misses statement 2.
129.tq: Mewar = never under Akbar; submitted under Jahangir. Marwar holdout = Rao Chandrasen.
xs: Statements **2 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is wrong: **Mewar never submitted** under Akbar; **Rana Pratap** fought on after **Haldighati (1576)**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Rao Chandrasen** resisted in **Marwar**.
Statement 3 is correct: Mewar submitted under **Jahangir** (**Amar Singh**); his son **Karan Singh** became a mansabdar.
xa: Haldighati was **not decisive**.
Haldighati is a UPPSC **2023** question.

129.s: Who among the following was associated with revenue administration under Akbar?
129.x: Raja Todarmal was prominent in revenue administration under Akbar, while Man Singh was a leading Rajput military officer.
129.tq: Match the individual with the specific administrative field rather than general service.
xs: **Raja Todarmal** handled **revenue** under Akbar — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Raja Bharmal** of Amber gave his daughter in marriage (**1562**); **Man Singh** was a general.
**Karan Singh** of Mewar became a mansabdar under Jahangir.
xa: Todar Mal earlier served **Sher Shah**.
He designed the **Zabti / Bandobast (dahsala)** system (**1580**).
He died in **1589**.

129.s: The Zabti or Dahsala system was designed by
129.x: Raja Todar Mal designed the Zabti, also called Bandobast or Dahsala, revenue system.
129.tq: Test the administrator–revenue-system association.
xs: **Raja Todar Mal** designed the **Zabti / Bandobast / Dahsala** system — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Abul Fazl** wrote the **Akbarnama**; **Man Singh** was a general; **Birbal** a wit and adviser.
xa: It was modelled on **Sher Shah's** survey-based system.
Land was measured with the bamboo **Gaz-i-Ilahi** (about **82** cm).
Revenue = **one-third** of average produce of the last **10** years.

129.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Dahsala system?
o: Revenue was based on one-third of the average produce and prices of the preceding ten years and was paid in cash.
Revenue was collected as a fixed one-fifth of war booty.
Revenue was fixed solely by dividing the standing crop at harvest.
Revenue was assessed only from the peasant's past payments.
129.x: Under Dahsala, revenue was fixed at one-third of the average produce and prices of the previous ten years and was generally paid in cash.
129.tq: Choose the option containing the complete and precise revenue formula.
xs: Under **Dahsala**, revenue was **one-third** of the **average produce and prices of the last 10 years**, **paid in cash** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**One-fifth of war booty** is **Khums**.
Dividing the crop at harvest is **Batai**; assessing from past payments is **Nasaq**.
xa: Designed by **Raja Todar Mal** (**1580**).
Land classes: **Polaj, Parauti, Chachar, Banjar**.
Relief: **Taccavi** loans and remissions.

129.s: The Gaz-i-Ilahi used for measuring land under the Zabti system was made of
129.x: One account describes the Gaz-i-Ilahi (about 82 cm) used under Zabti as bamboo, so C. Other sources say the bamboo item was the jarib, made of bamboo pieces joined with iron rings in place of hemp rope; either way, the material was bamboo, not copper, stone or iron.
129.tq: Recall the material and approximate size of the measuring unit.
xs: The **Gaz-i-Ilahi** was a **bamboo** measure — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was about **82** cm long, used under Todar Mal's **Zabti (1580)**.
xa: Sher Shah's earlier measure was the **gaz-i-Sikandari**.
Revenue was fixed at **one-third**, paid in **cash**.
⚠ Gaz-i-Ilahi = Zabti measure; do not confuse with Sher Shah's yard.

129.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Batai — crop-sharing
2. Kankut — estimation of standing crop
3. Nasaq — rough assessment based on past payments
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
129.x: Batai involved division of the harvested crop, Kankut estimated the standing crop, and Nasaq relied roughly on the peasant's past payments.
129.tq: Match each revenue term with its defining assessment method.
xs: All three pairs are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Batai / Ghallabakshi** = **crop-sharing** between state and peasant.
**Kankut** = revenue by **estimation** of the standing crop; **Nasaq** = rough assessment from **past payments**.
xa: **Zabti** used measurement and **10**-year averages, paid in cash.
Relief came through **Taccavi** loans.

129.s: Taccavi loans and remissions under the revenue arrangements were particularly associated with relief during
129.x: Taccavi loans and remissions provided relief to cultivators during famines or floods.
129.tq: Apply the relief measure to the appropriate agricultural crisis.
xs: **Taccavi** loans and remissions gave relief in **famine or floods** — so option **(3)** is correct.
They were part of Akbar's revenue arrangements under **Todar Mal**.
xa: Revenue under Zabti was **one-third**, paid in **cash**.
Land classes ran from **Polaj** (cultivated yearly) to **Banjar** (uncultivated **5** years or more).
**Mansabdari-jagirdari** and **Zabti** were the core of Mughal governance for **150 years**.

129.s: Which statement regarding Raja Todar Mal is correct?
o: He served Aurangzeb and had earlier served Murshid Quli Khan.
He served only the Qutb Shahis and introduced the Pargana system.
He was a provincial Qazi who designed the Mansabdari system.
He served Akbar and had earlier served Sher Shah.
129.x: Todar Mal was Akbar's revenue minister and had earlier served Sher Shah. His system was modelled on Sher Shah's survey-based arrangements.
129.tq: Use the predecessor-service link to distinguish Todar Mal from other administrative figures.
xs: **Todar Mal** served **Akbar** and had earlier served **Sher Shah** — so option **(4)** is correct.
His Zabti was modelled on **Sher Shah's survey-based system**.
xa: He designed the **Zabti / Bandobast (dahsala)** in **1580**.
He is listed among the prominent Rajputs with **Man Singh** and **Birbal**.
He died in **1589**.

129.s: Under Akbar's Zabti system, land that had been left fallow for three to four years was classified as:
129.x: Chachar was land fallow for 3-4 years. Polaj was cultivated every year, Parauti was fallow for 1-2 years, and Banjar was uncultivated for 5 years or more.
129.tq: Polaj (every year) -> Parauti (1-2) -> Chachar (3-4) -> Banjar (5+).
xs: Land fallow for **3-4 years** was **Chachar** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Polaj** = cultivated every year; **Parauti** = fallow **1-2** years; **Banjar** = uncultivated **5** years or more.
xa: Sher Shah had only **three** land classes.
Akbar-Todar Mal used **four** classes and **ten-year averages**.

129.s: Who among the following was killed in 1586 while fighting the Yusufzai?
129.x: Birbal, whose original name was Mahesh Das, was killed in 1586 while fighting the Yusufzai.
129.tq: Match the court figure with the specific military fate.
xs: **Birbal** (Mahesh Das) was killed in **1586** fighting the **Yusufzai** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Faizi** died in **1595**; **Abul Fazl** was murdered in **1602**; **Todar Mal** died in **1589**.
xa: Birbal was the **only Hindu** in **Din-i-Ilahi**.
**Kashmir** was also conquered in **1586**.

129.s: Abul Fazl was murdered in 1602 by:
o: Man Singh I at Akbar's instance
Adham Khan at Bairam Khan's instance
Bir Singh Bundela at Salim's instance
129.x: Abul Fazl was murdered in 1602 by Bir Singh Bundela at the instance of Prince Salim.
129.tq: Use the wrong-person and wrong-instigator trap in a court event.
xs: **Abul Fazl** was murdered in **1602** by **Bir Singh Bundela** at **Salim's** instance — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Adham Khan** belongs to the **petticoat government**; **Hemu** died at **Panipat II**.
xa: Abul Fazl wrote the **Akbarnama** and **Ain-i-Akbari**.
He was the chief exponent of **Din-i-Ilahi**.
Order of deaths: **Sheikh Mubarak → Faizi → Abul Fazl → Prince Daniyal** (UPPSC **2024**).

129.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Person)
a. Faizi
b. Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan (son of Bairam Khan)
c. Badauni
d. Nizamuddin Ahmad
List-II (Work)
i. Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh
ii. Tabaqat-i-Akbari
iii. Persian translation of Lilavati
iv. Persian translation of the Baburnama
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
129.x: Faizi, the poet laureate, made the Persian Lilavati (a–iii); Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan, son of Bairam Khan, translated the Baburnama into Persian (b–iv); Badauni wrote the Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh (c–i); Nizamuddin Ahmad wrote the Tabaqat-i-Akbari (d–ii). The second option swaps Faizi and Rahim, the third credits Tabaqat-i-Akbari to Badauni (the common trap), and the fourth gives Faizi Badauni's work.
129.tq: Trap: Tabaqat-i-Akbari is Nizamuddin's, not Badauni's.
xs: **a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Faizi** — Persian **Lilavati**; **Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan** — Persian **Baburnama**.
**Badauni** — **Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh**; **Nizamuddin Ahmad** — **Tabaqat-i-Akbari**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes wrongly credit **Tabaqat-i-Akbari** to Badauni.
Faizi was **poet laureate** and Abul Fazl's brother.
The **Razmnama** is the translation of the **Mahabharata**.

129.s:
Arrange the following persons in the order of their deaths:
A. Faizi
B. Prince Daniyal
C. Sheikh Mubarak
D. Abul Fazl
129.x: The order of deaths was Sheikh Mubarak, Faizi, Abul Fazl and Prince Daniyal.
129.tq: Identify the earliest and latest deaths first, then place the two middle figures.
xs: **C, A, D, B** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Sheikh Mubarak → Faizi (1595) → Abul Fazl (1602) → Prince Daniyal** (UPPSC **2024**).
xa: Abul Fazl was murdered by **Bir Singh Bundela** at Salim's instance.
**Shaikh Mubarak** drafted the **Mahzar** (**1579**).
Abul Fazl, Faizi and Shaikh Mubarak were members of **Din-i-Ilahi**.

129.s: Who wrote the official history of Akbar and was one of Akbar's Navaratnas?
129.x: Abul Fazl wrote the official history of Akbar and was one of Akbar's Navaratnas.
129.tq: Identify the court historian through both office and patronage association.
xs: **Abul Fazl** wrote Akbar's official history, the **Akbarnama** (and **Ain-i-Akbari**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
He was one of Akbar's **Navratnas** and the chief exponent of **Din-i-Ilahi**.
xa: He was murdered in **1602** by **Bir Singh Bundela**.
His brother **Faizi** was poet laureate.
Other histories: **Badauni**'s **Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh**, **Nizamuddin Ahmad**'s **Tabaqat-i-Akbari**.

129.s: Which one of Akbar's court figures, originally named Ramtanu Pandey, is associated with the ragas Miyan ki Malhar and Miyan ki Todi?
129.x: Tansen (Ramtanu Pandey) was the court musician credited with Miyan ki Malhar and Miyan ki Todi. Faizi was the poet laureate, Birbal (Mahesh Das) the wit and adviser, and Abdur Rahim a poet known for Hindi dohas.
129.tq: 'Miyan ki' ragas = Miyan Tansen.
xs: **Tansen** (Ramtanu Pandey) is linked to **Miyan ki Malhar** and **Miyan ki Todi** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Faizi** was the **poet laureate**; **Birbal** (Mahesh Das) the wit and adviser; **Abdur Rahim** a poet of Hindi **dohas**.
xa: Tansen is credited with a **gharana** tradition and linked to **Gwalior**.
**Man Singh I** led the Mughals at Haldighati.

129.s: Which one of the following pairs regarding Akbar's religious measures is correctly matched?
129.x: The pilgrimage tax was abolished in 1563 and jizya was abolished in 1564 according to the commonly used chronology. Some accounts place both abolitions in 1564.
129.tq: Use the numerical comparison and distinguish two closely dated measures.
xs: **Pilgrimage tax — 1563; Jizya — 1564** — so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ Some older notes give **1564** for both.
xa: **Aurangzeb** reimposed jizya in **1679**.
**Shah Jahan** abolished the pilgrim tax at **Banaras and Allahabad** after **Kavindracharya**'s deputation.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about Akbar's Ibadat Khana:
1. It was built at Fatehpur Sikri in 1575 for interfaith debates.
2. Its debates were opened to Hindus, Jains, Christians and Zoroastrians.
3. It was built in 1582, the year Din-i-Ilahi was proclaimed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
129.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Ibadat Khana was built at Fatehpur Sikri in 1575 as a forum for interfaith debate. Statement 2 is correct: it was opened to Hindus, Jains, Christians and Zoroastrians. Statement 3 is wrong: 1582 is the year of Din-i-Ilahi, not of the Ibadat Khana. So '1 only' is incomplete and options with 3 are wrong.
129.tq: Sequence: 1575 Ibadat Khana -> 1579 Mahzar -> 1582 Din-i-Ilahi.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **Ibadat Khana** was built at **Fatehpur Sikri** in **1575** for interfaith debate.
Statement 2 is correct: it was opened to **Hindus, Jains, Christians and Zoroastrians**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **1582** is the year of **Din-i-Ilahi**.
xa: **1579**: the **Mahzar** made Akbar supreme arbiter.
Guiding principle: **Sulh-i-Kul**.

129.s:
With reference to the Mahzar of 1579, consider the following statements:
1. It made Akbar the supreme arbiter in religious disputes.
2. It was drafted by Shaikh Mubarak.
3. It transferred the Mughal capital to Fatehpur Sikri.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: The Mahzar of 1579 made Akbar the supreme arbiter in religious disputes and was drafted by Shaikh Mubarak. It had no connection with transferring the capital.
129.tq: Separate the constitutional-religious effect of a decree from an unrelated administrative change.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **Mahzar (1579)** made Akbar **supreme arbiter** in religious disputes.
Statement 2 is correct: it was drafted by **Shaikh Mubarak**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it had nothing to do with the capital; the **Ibadat Khana** was at **Fatehpur Sikri**.
xa: It is also called the so-called **Infallibility Decree**.
**Din-i-Ilahi** followed in **1582**.

129.s: Which one of the following represents the central meaning of Sulh-i-Kul?
o: Compulsory conversion to a single faith
129.x: Sulh-i-Kul means universal peace or peace with all and served as a guiding principle of Akbar's policy.
129.tq: Discriminate the exact meaning of a Persian administrative-religious term.
xs: **Sulh-i-Kul** means **"peace with all"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was the **guiding principle** of Akbar's religious policy.
**Din-i-Ilahi** was **never forced** on anyone, so compulsory conversion is wrong.
xa: Measures: abolition of **jizya** (**1564**) and **pilgrimage tax** (**1563**), **Ibadat Khana**, **Mahzar**.
Shaikh Ahmad **Sirhindi** attacked Sulh-i-kul and Din-i-Ilahi.
Akbar's coins showed **Rama and Sita** with the legend **'Rama-Siya'**.

129.s: Which of the following taxes was re-imposed by Aurangzeb in 1679?
129.x: Aurangzeb re-imposed jizya in 1679. Zakat, ushr and khums are distinct taxes or levies.
129.tq: Distinguish jizya from the other named Islamic taxes.
xs: **Aurangzeb** reimposed **jizya** in **1679** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Zakat** = alms tax on Muslims; **Ushr** = land tax on Muslims; **Khums** = **one-fifth of war booty**.
xa: **Akbar** abolished jizya in **1564**.
Aurangzeb also banned festivals like **Navroz**.
The reversal alienated **Rajputs, Marathas and Sikhs**.

129.s:
Match the following taxes with their descriptions.
List-I
(a) Zakat
(b) Ushr
(c) Khums
(d) Jizya
List-II
(i) Poll tax on non-Muslims
(ii) Alms tax on Muslims
(iii) Land tax on Muslims
(iv) One-fifth of war booty
Choose the correct answer using the code given below.
129.x: Zakat was an alms tax on Muslims, ushr was a land tax on Muslims, khums represented one-fifth of war booty, and jizya was imposed on non-Muslims.
129.tq: Start with the sure jizya pair and complete the tax classifications.
xs: **a–ii, b–iii, c–iv, d–i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Zakat** = alms tax on Muslims; **Ushr** = land tax on Muslims.
**Khums** = one-fifth of war booty; **Jizya** = poll tax on non-Muslims.
xa: Jizya: abolished by Akbar (**1564**), reimposed by Aurangzeb (**1679**).
Pilgrim tax: abolished by Akbar in **1563**.

129.s: The pilgrim tax at Banaras and Allahabad was abolished by Shah Jahan after a deputation led by
129.x: Shah Jahan abolished the pilgrim tax at Banaras and Allahabad after a deputation of Banaras pandits led by Kavindracharya.
129.tq: Link the ruler, tax centres and leader of the deputation.
xs: **Shah Jahan** abolished the pilgrim tax at **Banaras and Allahabad** after a deputation of Banaras pandits led by **Kavindracharya** — so option **(4)** is correct.
This was asked in UPPSC **2000**.
xa: **Akbar** had abolished the pilgrim tax in **1563**.
Shah Jahan was **slightly more orthodox** but kept many Hindu nobles.
**Aurangzeb** had the **highest number of Hindu nobles** in absolute terms (UPPSC **2000** key).

129.s:
Arrange the following measures in chronological order:
A. Mahzar
B. Abolition of jizya
C. Construction of Ibadat Khana
D. Proclamation of Din-i-Ilahi
129.x: The sequence is abolition of jizya in 1564, construction of the Ibadat Khana in 1575, Mahzar in 1579 and Din-i-Ilahi in 1582.
129.tq: Fix the first and last events, then arrange the middle dates.
xs: **B, C, A, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Jizya abolished (1564)** → **Ibadat Khana (1575)**.
xa: The **pilgrimage tax** went in **1563**.
The Mahzar was drafted by **Shaikh Mubarak**.
Jizya was reimposed in **1679** by **Aurangzeb**.

129.s: Which Mughal emperor issued coins bearing figures of Rama and Sita with the Devanagari legend 'Rama-Siya'?
129.x: Akbar, in keeping with Sulh-i-Kul, issued coins with Rama and Sita and the legend 'Rama-Siya' (UPPSC 2011). Babur was an orthodox Sunni who took the title Ghazi, Jahangir is known for his own portrait/zodiac coinage, and Aurangzeb reversed tolerance.
129.tq: Rama-Siya coins = Akbar's Sulh-i-Kul.
xs: **Akbar** issued coins with **Rama and Sita** and the Devanagari legend **'Rama-Siya'** (UPPSC **2011**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Babur** was an orthodox Sunni who took the title **Ghazi**; **Aurangzeb** reversed tolerance.
xa: The coins reflect **Sulh-i-Kul** ("peace with all").
**Jahangir** broadly continued Akbar's tolerance.
Akbar was the **unlettered** emperor, yet a great patron.

129.s: The first Jesuit mission to Akbar's court in 1580 was led by:
o: Dastur Meherji Rana and Guru Ram Das
Jerome Xavier and Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi
129.x: The first Jesuit mission from Goa in 1580 was led by Rudolf Acquaviva and Antonio Monserrate.
129.tq: Match the mission year with its correct representatives.
xs: The **first** Jesuit mission (**1580**) was led by **Rudolf Acquaviva** and **Antonio Monserrate** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Dastur Meherji Rana** (Parsi) and **Guru Ram Das** (Sikh) got land grants.
**Hiravijaya Suri** and **Jinachandra Suri** were Jains; **Jerome Xavier** led the **third** mission.
xa: The second mission came in **1591**.
The missions came from **Goa**.

129.s: The third Jesuit mission to Akbar's court in 1595 was conducted under the leadership of:
129.x: The third Jesuit mission, sent in 1595, was under Jerome Xavier.
129.tq: Distinguish the leader of the later mission from those of the first mission.
xs: The **third** Jesuit mission (**1595**) was led by **Jerome Xavier** (CGPSC **2022**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Rudolf Acquaviva** and **Antonio Monserrate** led the **first** (**1580**).
**Dastur Meherji Rana** was a **Parsi** leader.
xa: The second mission came in **1591**.
The Ibadat Khana was opened to **Christians** among others.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about Akbar's contacts with religious leaders:
1. The Jain scholar Hiravijaya Suri was given the title 'Jagat Guru'.
2. Jinachandra Suri was also given the title 'Jagat Guru'.
3. Akbar granted land to the Parsi leader Dastur Meherji Rana.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
129.x: Statement 1 is correct: Hiravijaya Suri was 'Jagat Guru'. Statement 2 is wrong: Jinachandra Suri was given the title 'Yuga Pradhan'. Statement 3 is correct: Akbar granted land to Dastur Meherji Rana. So '1 only' misses statement 3, and options with 2 are wrong.
129.tq: Hiravijaya = Jagat Guru; Jinachandra = Yuga Pradhan.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Hiravijaya Suri** got the title **"Jagat Guru"** (CGPSC **2024**).
Statement 2 is wrong: **Jinachandra Suri** got **"Yuga Pradhan"**.
Statement 3 is correct: Akbar gave land to Parsi **Dastur Meherji Rana**.
xa: ⚠ "Jagat Guru" = Hiravijaya Suri; "Yuga Pradhan" = Jinachandra Suri.
Land to **Guru Ram Das** → growth of **Amritsar**.

129.s: Akbar's grant of land to Guru Ram Das is associated with the growth of:
129.x: Land granted to Guru Ram Das became associated with the growth of Amritsar.
129.tq: Link the religious leader with the place connected to the grant.
xs: Akbar's land grant to **Guru Ram Das** is where **Amritsar** grew — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Fatehpur Sikri** housed the **Ibadat Khana**.
xa: **Guru Arjan Dev** built the **Golden Temple (Harmandir)** at Amritsar.
Guru Arjan Dev was **executed by Jahangir (1606)**.
Akbar also gave land to Parsi **Dastur Meherji Rana**.

129.s: Din-i-Ilahi, also known as Tauhid-i-Ilahi, is best described as a:

xs: **Din-i-Ilahi (Tauhid-i-Ilahi)** was a **syncretic moral order** — so option **(4)** is correct.

xa: Features: **one God**, greeting **"Allah-hu-Akbar"**, reverence for **sun and fire**, no meat-eating.

xs: Orthodox criticism of Akbar's religious innovations came from **Badauni** and the Naqshbandi **Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi** — so option **(1)** is correct.

xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.

129.s: Banda Singh Bahadur, originally known as Lachhman Dev, was a disciple of
129.x: Banda Singh Bahadur, originally Lachhman Dev, became a disciple of Guru Gobind Singh.
129.tq: Use the disciple–Guru relationship directly.
xs: **Banda Singh Bahadur** (Lachhman Dev) was a disciple of **Guru Gobind Singh** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Guru Tegh Bahadur** was executed in **1675**, **Guru Arjan Dev** in **1606**, and **Guru Hargobind** was the 6th Guru — all before Banda's campaigns of **1709-10**.
xa: Banda founded the **first sovereign Sikh state** with capital **Lohgarh**.
He abolished **zamindari** and issued coins in the Gurus' names.
He was executed in Delhi in **1716** by **Farrukhsiyar**.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about the religious and social composition of the Mughal nobility:
1. Shah Jahan retained a high number of Hindu nobles despite being more orthodox.
2. Aurangzeb had the highest number of Hindu nobles and generals in absolute terms.
3. Many of Aurangzeb's Hindu nobles were Marathas and Rajputs recruited during the Deccan wars.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: All three statements are correct. Shah Jahan retained many Hindu nobles, and Aurangzeb had the highest absolute number, including Marathas and Rajputs recruited during the Deccan wars.
129.tq: Handle the counter-intuitive comparison by checking absolute number rather than presumed religious orientation.
xs: All three statements — **1, 2 and 3** — are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statement 1: **Shah Jahan**, though slightly more orthodox, **retained a high number of Hindu nobles**.
Statement 2: **Aurangzeb** had the **highest number of Hindu nobles/generals** in absolute terms (UPPSC **2000** key).
Statement 3: they were largely **Marathas and Rajputs** taken in during the **Deccan wars**.
xa: This is the counter-intuitive tested fact, since Aurangzeb **reversed tolerance** (jizya **1679**).
Aurangzeb also banned **Navroz** and patronised the **Fatawa-i-Alamgiri**.
Shah Jahan destroyed some **newly built temples**.

129.s: Babur's religious policy is best described as
o: Sulh-i-kul; he abolished jizya and established the Ibadat Khana
complete neutrality towards all religions and prohibition of warfare in the name of religion
orthodox Sunni; he proclaimed jihad at Khanwa and assumed the title Ghazi
129.x: Babur followed an orthodox Sunni outlook, proclaimed jihad at Khanwa and adopted the title Ghazi.
129.tq: Match the ruler with the precise policy rather than a later Mughal feature.
xs: **Babur** was an **orthodox Sunni**; he proclaimed **jihad at Khanwa** and took the title **Ghazi** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Sulh-i-kul**, jizya abolition and the **Ibadat Khana** belong to **Akbar**.
The **Fatawa-i-Alamgiri** was patronised by **Aurangzeb**.
xa: Babur also took the title **Padshah**.
His autobiography, **Tuzuk-i-Baburi**, was written in **Chaghatai Turkish**.
The orthodox **Naqshbandi** order came to India with **Babur**.

129.s: Which one of the following statements best describes Jahangir's religious policy?
o: He broadly continued Akbar's tolerance, though Guru Arjan Dev was executed for political reasons.
He entirely abandoned Akbar's policy of tolerance.
129.x: Jahangir broadly continued Akbar's tolerant approach, but Guru Arjan Dev was executed for political reasons related to support for rebel prince Khusrau.
129.tq: Avoid the extreme claim and retain the ruler-specific qualification.
xs: **Jahangir** broadly **continued Akbar's tolerance**; Guru Arjan Dev's execution was **for political reasons** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Khalsa (1699)** was founded by **Guru Gobind Singh**.
**Jizya** was reimposed in **1679** by **Aurangzeb**.
xa: **Guru Arjan Dev** was executed in **1606** for supporting rebel prince **Khusrau**.
Jahangir imprisoned **Guru Hargobind** at **Gwalior**.
Jahangir gave Prince Khurram the title **"Shah Jahan"**.

129.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Shah Jahan's religious policy:
1. It was slightly more orthodox than Akbar's policy.
2. Some newly built temples were destroyed during his reign.
3. Hindu nobles were completely excluded from his administration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: Shah Jahan was slightly more orthodox and destroyed some newly built temples, but he continued to employ many Hindu nobles. Therefore, statement 3 is false.
129.tq: Reject the absolute exclusion claim while retaining the qualified policy description.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Shah Jahan** was **slightly more orthodox** than Akbar.
Statement 2 correct: he **destroyed some newly built temples**.
Statement 3 wrong: he **retained a high number of Hindu nobles**.
xa: Shah Jahan abolished the **pilgrim tax at Banaras and Allahabad** after a deputation led by **Kavindracharya**.
**Aurangzeb** had the highest number of Hindu nobles in absolute terms.
Shah Jahan got his title from **Jahangir**.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about Aurangzeb's religious policy:
1. He reimposed jizya in 1679 and banned festivals such as Navroz.
2. He patronised the Fatawa-i-Alamgiri and was called 'Zinda Pir'.
3. He executed Guru Arjan Dev.
4. His reversal of tolerance alienated the Rajputs, Marathas and Sikhs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Guru Arjan Dev was executed by Jahangir; Aurangzeb executed Guru Tegh Bahadur. So '1 and 2 only' misses 4, and options with 3 are wrong.
129.tq: Match Guru to emperor: Arjan Dev - Jahangir; Tegh Bahadur - Aurangzeb.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Aurangzeb** reimposed **jizya in 1679** and banned **Navroz**.
Statement 2 correct: he patronised the **Fatawa-i-Alamgiri** and was called **"Zinda Pir"**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Guru Arjan Dev** was executed by **Jahangir**; Aurangzeb executed **Guru Tegh Bahadur**.
Statement 4 correct: the reversal **alienated Rajputs, Marathas and Sikhs**.
xa: The reversal is cited among the **causes of decline**.
Akbar had abolished jizya in **1564**.
⚠ Aurangzeb still had the **highest number of Hindu nobles** in absolute terms.

129.s: Which development most directly helped transform the Mughal state from a conquest state into a durable empire?
o: The withdrawal from Rajput affairs and restriction of Hindu participation
The exclusive use of Persian in local administration
The abolition of the mansabdari system
The combination of Sulh-i-Kul with partnership with the Rajputs
129.x: Sulh-i-Kul and the Rajput partnership broadened support and helped turn the conquest state into a durable empire.
129.tq: Link the stated policy with its institutional and political consequence.
xs: **Sulh-i-Kul** combined with the **Rajput partnership** turned a conquest state into a durable empire — so option **(4)** is correct.
It underpinned **Rajput and Hindu support**; Rajputs got high posts, matrimonial alliances and autonomy.
Akbar did not withdraw from Rajput affairs, and **mansabdari** was a core of governance, not abolished.
xa: **1562**: Akbar married the daughter of **Raja Bharmal of Amber** (Kachhwaha).
Top Rajput mansabdars: **Man Singh** and **Bhagwan Das**.
**Mewar** never submitted under Akbar; it submitted under **Jahangir** (**Amar Singh**).
Aurangzeb's reversal (jizya **1679**) alienated Rajputs, Marathas and Sikhs.

129.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Din-i-Ilahi has been debated as either a new religion or a discipleship order.
2. Only a handful of people joined it.
3. It continued as a major institution after Akbar’s death.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
129.x: The first two statements are correct. Din-i-Ilahi lapsed with Akbar and did not continue as a major institution after his reign.
129.tq: Reject the overstatement about the size and continuity of a short-lived institution.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: debated as a **new religion or a discipleship order**.
Statement 2 correct: only a **handful** joined (about **18**).
Statement 3 wrong: Din-i-Ilahi **lapsed with Akbar**.
xa: Proclaimed **1582**; features: one God, greeting **"Allah-hu-Akbar"**, avoiding meat, reverence for **sun and fire**.
Members included **Abul Fazl**, **Faizi** and **Shaikh Mubarak**; **Birbal** was the only Hindu.
It was never forced on anyone.

129.s: The core components of Mughal governance that remained significant for about 150 years were
o: Maktab Khana, Ibadat Khana and Razmnama
129.x: Mansabdari, jagirdari and Zabti formed the core of Mughal governance for about 150 years.
129.tq: Identify the administrative cluster rather than a religious or cultural cluster.
xs: **Mansabdari-jagirdari** and **Zabti** were the core of Mughal governance for **150 years** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Sulh-i-Kul** and **Din-i-Ilahi** were religious policies; Din-i-Ilahi **lapsed with Akbar**.
**Qadiri** and **Naqshbandi** are Sufi orders, not governance systems.
xa: **Zabti** (dahsala) was designed by **Raja Todar Mal** (**1580**): revenue = **one-third** of average produce of the last **10** years.
Land was measured with the bamboo **Gaz-i-Ilahi** (about **82** cm).
Under Aurangzeb, the **jagirdari crisis** pressed the peasantry.

129.s: What condition is described as the jagirdari crisis under Aurangzeb?
o: Too many jagirdars competing for too few jagirs, placing pressure on the peasantry
The complete abolition of jagirs by Akbar
The transfer of all jagirs to Rajput rulers
Too few mansabdars controlling an excessive number of jagirs
129.x: The jagirdari crisis arose because too many mansabdars chased too few jagirs, which increased pressure on the peasantry.
129.tq: Translate the economic consequence into an administrative scenario.
xs: The **jagirdari crisis**: **too many mansabdars chased too few jagirs**, pressing the peasantry — so option **(1)** is correct.
It arose under **Aurangzeb**, not Akbar; jagirs were not abolished or handed to Rajput rulers.
xa: **Mansabdari-jagirdari** and **Zabti** were the core of Mughal governance for **150 years**.
Aurangzeb's reversal of tolerance (jizya **1679**) is also cited among **causes of decline**.
Many of Aurangzeb's Hindu nobles were **Marathas and Rajputs** taken in during the **Deccan wars**.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about Golconda (AP angle):
1. Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah kept friendly relations with Akbar, who sent Masud Beg with gifts.
2. Abul Hasan Tana Shah followed religious tolerance and appointed Madanna and Akkanna to high office.
3. Bhakta Ramadasu was the son of Madanna.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
129.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Bhakta Ramadasu was the nephew of Madanna and Akkanna, not a son. So '1 only' misses 2, and options with 3 are wrong.
129.tq: Ramadasu = nephew of Madanna-Akkanna.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah** kept friendly ties with Akbar, who sent **Masud Beg** with gifts.
Statement 2 correct: **Abul Hasan Tana Shah** was tolerant and appointed **Madanna and Akkanna**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Bhakta Ramadasu** was their **nephew**, not Madanna's son.
xa: Akbar's southern limit reached the **Godavari**.
**Ahmednagar (1600)**: Akbar's forces opposed **Chand Bibi**.
Akbar's **last campaign**: **Asirgarh (1601)** in Khandesh.

129.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Baisakhi — Banda Singh Bahadur’s conquest of Sirhind
Baisakhi — foundation day of the Khalsa
Shaheedi Divas — martyrdom of Guru Tegh Bahadur
Sirhind Fateh Diwas — Banda Singh Bahadur’s conquest of Sirhind
129.x: Baisakhi is associated with the foundation of the Khalsa, not Banda Singh Bahadur’s conquest of Sirhind. The conquest is commemorated by Sirhind Fateh Diwas.
129.tq: Find the event–observance swap among related Sikh commemorations.
xs: **Baisakhi — conquest of Sirhind** is wrongly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Baisakhi** is the Khalsa foundation day (**13 April 1699**).
Banda Singh Bahadur's **1710** conquest of Sirhind is marked by **Sirhind Fateh Diwas (12-14 May)**.
**Shaheedi Divas (24 Nov)** marks Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom.
xa: Banda took Sirhind after defeating **Wazir Khan** at **Chappar Chiri**.
Guru Tegh Bahadur was beheaded at **Chandni Chowk** in **1675**; **Sis Ganj** marks the site.
The **Chali Mukte** at **Muktsar** are commemorated as **Maghi**.

130.s: Todar Mal’s revenue arrangements built upon the earlier survey-based system of:
130.x: Todar Mal had earlier served Sher Shah and built upon Sher Shah’s survey-based system.
130.tq: Use the predecessor–administrator relationship instead of the later Mughal succession.
xs: Todar Mal built on the survey-based system of **Sher Shah** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Raja Todar Mal** had earlier **served Sher Shah** before becoming Akbar's revenue chief.
xa: Todar Mal was Akbar's **Diwan** (finance minister) and one of the **Navratnas**.
His **dahsala** (bandobast) reform came in **1580**.
Units: **Gaz-i-Ilahi** (about **82 cm**) for length; the **jarib** of bamboo joined with iron rings.
⚠ **1574** = Karori experiment; **1580** = dahsala.

130.s: What was the principal advantage of the bamboo jarib used in land measurement?
o: It was a rope treated with oil to increase its elasticity.
It was made of bamboo pieces joined with iron rings and avoided the shrinkage or stretching of hemp rope.
It consisted exclusively of a single iron rod and could measure only irrigated land.
It was made of wooden pieces joined with leather and used only for crop sharing.
130.x: The jarib was made from bamboo pieces joined with iron rings, avoiding the shrinkage or stretching associated with hemp rope.
130.tq: Identify the material-based improvement and reject altered construction details.
xs: The **jarib** was **bamboo pieces joined with iron rings**, avoiding the shrinking or stretching of **hemp rope** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The older **hemp rope** shrank or stretched, making measurements unreliable; bamboo with iron rings fixed this.
xa: The **Gaz-i-Ilahi** was the unit of length, about **82 cm**.
⚠ Some notes call the **gaz** itself a bamboo rod.
Measurement underpinned **Zabti**: land measured and cash rates fixed per crop per **bigha**.

130.s: Todar Mal held which office in the Mughal Empire?
130.x: Todar Mal served as the Diwan, or finance minister, of the empire and was also counted among the Navratnas.
130.tq: Use the office–portfolio association while avoiding neighbouring central offices.
xs: **Raja Todar Mal** was the **Diwan (finance minister)** of the empire — so option **(1)** is correct.
He was also one of Akbar's **Navratnas** and designed the **dahsala** system.
xa: He had earlier served **Sher Shah** and built on his survey-based system.
Before dahsala, the **Karori experiment (1574)** put circles yielding **one crore dams** under **karoris**.
Under dahsala, the state share was **one-third** of average produce, paid in cash (**dam**).

130.s: The Karori experiment was launched in:
130.x: In 1574, the core provinces were divided into revenue circles under karoris.
130.tq: Distinguish the experimental year from the subsequent year of Dahsala.
xs: The **Karori experiment** was launched in **1574** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Core provinces were split into circles under officers called **karoris**.
**1580** is the year of **dahsala**, which this experiment prepared.
xa: Each circle was to yield **one crore dams**.
Karoris **collected revenue and reported cultivation data** — the groundwork for dahsala.
**1580**: there were **12** subas.

130.s: Under the Karori experiment, each revenue circle was intended to yield:
130.x: Each circle was designed to yield one crore dams and was placed under a karori.
130.tq: Use the scale of the revenue circle as the central numerical clue.
xs: Each Karori circle was to yield **one crore dams** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The officers over these circles were therefore called **karoris** (Karori experiment, **1574**).
xa: The data the karoris gathered laid the groundwork for **dahsala (1580)**.
The **dam** was the cash unit in which revenue was paid.
⚠ **1574** = Karori experiment; **1580** = dahsala.

130.s: Which one of the following best explains the importance of the Karori experiment?
o: It replaced all mansabs with hereditary offices.
It collected revenue and cultivation data that laid the groundwork for the Dahsala system.
It introduced the du-aspa sih-aspa system for trusted nobles.
It converted every jagir into khalisa land.
130.x: Karoris collected revenue and reported cultivation data. This information helped lay the groundwork for Dahsala, introduced in 1580.
130.tq: Link the administrative experiment to its later policy outcome.
xs: The Karori experiment **collected revenue and cultivation data** that laid the groundwork for **Dahsala** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Karoris (**1574**) collected revenue and reported cultivation data; dahsala followed in **1580**.
It did not make offices hereditary or convert jagirs to khalisa; it was a revenue experiment.
