136.s: Which Mughal emperor discontinued the practice of Jharokha darshan and stopped Nauroz?
136.x: Aurangzeb ended Jharokha darshan and stopped the celebration of Nauroz.
136.tq: Identify the ruler associated with the discontinuation of two customs.
xs: **Aurangzeb** ended **Jharokha darshan** and stopped **Nauroz** — option **(4)**.
Jharokha darshan, the emperor showing himself daily at a balcony, had been **begun by Akbar**.
xa: **Nauroz** = **Persian New Year**, adopted from the **Zoroastrians**.
**Sijda** (prostration) and **paibos** (kissing the feet) were introduced by **Akbar**.
**Tuladan** was a **Hindu** custom adopted by Akbar.

136.s: Sijda and paibos, introduced by Akbar, respectively signified
o: weighing the emperor and distributing alms
136.x: Sijda meant prostration, while paibos meant kissing the feet; Akbar introduced both practices at court.
136.tq: Separate two paired court terms by their exact meanings.
xs: **Sijda** = **prostration**; **paibos** = **kissing the feet** — option **(3)**.
Both were court customs **introduced by Akbar**.
xa: Weighing the emperor against gold on his birthday = **Tuladan**.
Daily public appearance at a balcony = **Jharokha darshan** (begun by Akbar, ended by **Aurangzeb**).
**Nauroz** = Persian New Year, from the **Zoroastrians**.

136.s: Which approach is most appropriate while using foreign travellers’ accounts for reconstructing Mughal social history?
o: Use only their descriptions of court ceremonies and disregard society.
Use them as a major source but read them critically alongside Persian chronicles.
Treat every observation as completely objective and ignore Persian chronicles.
Reject them entirely because foreign observers never recorded social conditions.
136.x: Travellers’ accounts are a major source for Mughal social history, but their observations should be read critically alongside Persian chronicles.
136.tq: Apply source criticism rather than accepting or rejecting an entire source category.
xs: Travellers' accounts are the **main source** for Mughal social history but must be **read against Persian chronicles** — option **(2)**.
Bernier's "**no private property**" and "**bleak India**" view reflects **European bias**, so they cannot be taken as fully objective.
Yet they do record society: **Sati**, **child marriage**, **polygamy**, purdah, Delhi's class gap.
xa: Bernier still conceded a **prosperous merchant class**.
**Pelsaert** contrasted nobles' luxury with the misery of servants and workmen.
**John Fryer**: Hindu women in the Deccan **moved freely**.

136.s: Which of the following Mughal customs was also shared by Qutb Shahi Golconda?
o: Jharokha darshan exclusively as an imperial Mughal practice
Sijda as a practice confined to Delhi
136.x: Qutb Shahi Golconda shared Mughal customs such as Nauroz. The other options incorrectly make broader or different practices exclusive to the Mughal court.
136.tq: Apply a cultural comparison between the Mughal and Qutb Shahi courts.
xs: **Qutb Shahi Golconda** shared the Mughal custom of **Nauroz** — option **(4)**.
It also shared **Muharram**, known as **Peerla Panduga**.
xa: **14** national festivals were held under **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah**.
Tavernier recorded **20,000** registered prostitutes in Hyderabad under **Abdullah Qutb Shah**.
Nauroz = **Persian New Year**, from the **Zoroastrians**; stopped by **Aurangzeb** in the Mughal court.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about the Qutb Shahi kingdom of Golconda:
1. Muharram was popularly known as Peerla Panduga.
2. Fourteen national festivals were observed under Abdullah Qutb Shah.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
136.x: Statement 1 is correct: Muharram was known as Peerla Panduga in Golconda. Statement 2 is wrong: the 14 national festivals are associated with Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, not Abdullah Qutb Shah. Hence '1 only'; '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' are wrong.
136.tq: Check the ruler's name: 14 festivals = Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Muharram** was known as **Peerla Panduga** in Golconda.
Statement 2 wrong: the **14 national festivals** belong to **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah**, not Abdullah Qutb Shah.
xa: **Abdullah Qutb Shah**'s Hyderabad had **20,000** registered prostitutes (Tavernier).
Golconda also shared the Mughal **Nauroz**.

137.s: The Tomb of Salim Chishti at Fatehpur Sikri is situated in the courtyard of the:
137.x: The Tomb of Salim Chishti is situated in the courtyard of the Jami Masjid at Fatehpur Sikri.
137.tq: Test the exact architectural location within a monument complex.
xs: The **Tomb of Salim Chishti** lies in the courtyard of the **Jami Masjid**, Fatehpur Sikri — option **(3)**.
It is a **white-marble** tomb built by **Akbar** (c. **1580-81**), part of the city's religious core.
**Diwan-i-Khas** = hall of private audience; **Ibadat Khana** = house of worship; **Panch Mahal** = five-storeyed pavilion.
xa: **Buland Darwaza** is the **southern entrance** to the Jami Masjid.
Fatehpur Sikri was built in honour of **Sheikh Salim Chishti** (**1571-1585**).
Akbar's reign set (APPSC-G1 **2024**): Salim Chishti's tomb, Buland Darwaza, Humayun's tomb, Jami Masjid (Fatehpur Sikri).

137.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Tomb of Salim Chishti — Fatehpur Sikri
137.x: The Taj Mahal is situated at Agra, not Delhi. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
137.tq: Find the wrong location among familiar monument–place pairs.
xs: **Taj Mahal — Delhi** is wrongly matched; the Taj is at **Agra** — option **(4)**.
**Akbar's Tomb** — **Sikandra** near Agra; **Salim Chishti's tomb** — **Fatehpur Sikri**; **Char Minar** — **Hyderabad**: all correct.
xa: APPSC G1 **2018** pairs: Charminar - **Hyderabad**; Akbar's Tomb - **Sikandara**; Humayun's Tomb - **Delhi**; Taj Mahal - **Agra**.
⚠ **Char Minar** (**1591**) is **Qutb Shahi**, not Mughal — a common distractor.
Jahangir's tomb is at **Shahdara, Lahore**; Aurangzeb's at **Khuldabad**.

137.s: Who began the construction of Akbar's Tomb, and who completed it?
o: Jahangir began it and Shah Jahan completed it
Akbar began it and Jahangir completed it
Humayun began it and Akbar completed it
Shah Jahan began it and Aurangzeb completed it
137.x: Akbar began the construction of his tomb, and his son Jahangir completed it. The tomb is located at Sikandra near Agra.
137.tq: Use the succession-based builder trap in which the initiator and completer are different rulers.
xs: **Akbar began** his tomb and **Jahangir completed** it — option **(2)**.
It stands at **Sikandra** (Sikandara) near **Agra**, c. **1613**.
It shows the **Persian-Indian synthesis**, like Fatehpur Sikri.
xa: **Jahangir Mahal at Orchha** (MP) continues Akbar's style.
Other emperors' tombs: Babur — **Kabul**; Humayun — **Delhi**; Jahangir — **Shahdara, Lahore**.
**Sher Shah's tomb** at Sasaram was finished under his son **Islam Shah**.

137.s: Char Minar at Hyderabad was built by:
137.x: Char Minar was built at Hyderabad in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah of the Qutb Shahi dynasty. It is not a Mughal monument.
137.tq: Discriminate between rulers of the Qutb Shahi dynasty and Mughal builders.
xs: **Char Minar** at Hyderabad was built by **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah** in **1591** — option **(4)**.
It is a **Qutb Shahi**, not a Mughal, monument; it marked the **end of a plague**.
xa: Style: **Persian arches** + **Deccani stucco**.
**Golconda Fort**: acoustic warning system, piped water.
**Qutb Shahi tombs** at **Ibrahim Bagh**: onion domes on square bases, in gardens.

137.s:
Arrange the following monuments in chronological order of their construction:
A. Humayun's Tomb
B. Jami Masjid, Fatehpur Sikri
C. Tomb of Salim Chishti
D. Char Minar
137.x: The order is Humayun's Tomb (1565–1572), Jami Masjid at Fatehpur Sikri (1571–1574), Tomb of Salim Chishti (1580–1581), and Char Minar (1591).
137.tq: Fix the earliest and latest monuments first, then compare the closely dated middle entries.
xs: Correct order **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**Humayun's Tomb** (c. **1565-72**) → **Jami Masjid, Fatehpur Sikri** (c. **1571-74**).
→ **Tomb of Salim Chishti** (c. **1580-81**) → **Char Minar** (**1591**).
xa: The first three belong to **Akbar's reign**; Char Minar is **Qutb Shahi**.
**Buland Darwaza** (c. **1575**) commemorates Akbar's **Gujarat** victory.
**Agra Fort** was begun in **1565**.

137.s:
Arrange the following monuments in chronological order of construction:
A. Akbar's Tomb
B. Taj Mahal
C. Red Fort, Delhi
D. Jama Masjid, Delhi
137.x: Akbar's Tomb was completed around 1613, followed by the Taj Mahal (1632–1648), Red Fort (1639–1648), and Jama Masjid of Delhi (1650–1656).
137.tq: Arrange monuments by their beginning or completion periods, paying attention to overlapping ranges.
xs: Correct order **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
xa: **Itimad-ud-Daula** (**1622-1628**) falls between Akbar's tomb and the Taj.
The Red Fort's **Diwan-i-Khas** housed the **Peacock Throne**.
Shah Jahan's reign = "**Golden Age**" of Mughal architecture.

137.s: Bibi ka Maqbara at Aurangabad was built by Prince Azam Shah for:
137.x: Prince Azam Shah built Bibi ka Maqbara during Aurangzeb's reign for his mother, Dilras Banu Begum. It is popularly called the Taj of the Deccan.
137.tq: Link the monument with its patron, dedicatee and popular description.
xs: Prince **Azam Shah** built Bibi ka Maqbara for his mother **Dilras Banu Begum** — option **(4)**.
It was built in **Aurangzeb's** reign at **Aurangabad** and is called the "**Taj of the Deccan**".
The Taj Mahal is for **Mumtaz Mahal**; Nur Jahan built Itimad-ud-Daula.
xa: It is the **last major imitation** in the tomb tradition.
⚠ "**Baby Taj**" = Itimad-ud-Daula; "**Taj of the Deccan**" = Bibi ka Maqbara.
Aurangzeb's own tomb is a **simple grave** at **Khuldabad** near Aurangabad.

137.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
137.x: Ram Bagh at Agra was established by Babur around 1528. Itimad-ud-Daula was built under Nur Jahan, Bibi ka Maqbara under Prince Azam Shah, and Akbar's Tomb is at Sikandra.
137.tq: Start with the sure monument–builder pair and eliminate reversed ruler associations.
xs: **Ram Bagh, Agra — Babur** is correct (c. **1528**) — option **(1)**.
**Itimad-ud-Daula** was built by **Nur Jahan**, not Akbar; **Bibi ka Maqbara** by Prince **Azam Shah**, not Shah Jahan.
**Akbar's Tomb** is at **Sikandra**, not Aurangabad.
xa: Ram Bagh = **first Mughal garden**; Babur introduced the **charbagh**.
Babur is buried at **Kabul** (Bagh-e-Babur), first buried at Agra.

137.s:
Which of the following monuments were built during the reign of Akbar?
1. Humayun's tomb, Delhi
2. Buland Darwaza, Fatehpur Sikri
3. Tomb of Itimad-ud-Daula, Agra
4. Tomb of Salim Chishti, Fatehpur Sikri
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
137.x: Humayun's tomb (c.1565-72, commissioned by Haji Begum in Akbar's reign), Buland Darwaza (c.1575, for the Gujarat victory) and Salim Chishti's tomb (c.1580-81) all belong to Akbar's reign. Itimad-ud-Daula's tomb was built by Nur Jahan in 1622-28, in Jahangir's reign. Option A leaves out the Salim Chishti tomb; options C and D wrongly include Itimad-ud-Daula.
137.tq: Humayun's tomb is Akbar-era; Buland Darwaza is Akbar's, never Shah Jahan's.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Humayun's tomb** (c. **1565-72**) and **Buland Darwaza** (c. **1575**) belong to Akbar's reign.
**Salim Chishti's tomb** (c. **1580-81**) was built by **Akbar**.
**Itimad-ud-Daula** (**1622-1628**) was built by **Nur Jahan** — not Akbar's reign.
xa: APPSC-G1 **2024**: Salim Chishti's tomb, Buland Darwaza, Humayun's tomb and Jami Masjid (Fatehpur Sikri) — all Akbar's reign.
⚠ "Not built by Shah Jahan" = **Buland Darwaza** (APPSC GS **2019**).

137.s: Humayun’s tomb in Delhi was built by
o: Haji Begum, also known as Bega Begum
137.x: The standard answer is Humayun's widow Haji Begum (Bega Begum), who commissioned the tomb in Akbar's reign (c.1565-72). Some sources name Hamida Banu Begum, Akbar's mother, but not as the sole builder; Gulbadan Begum wrote the Humayun-nama and Jahanara built the Jama Masjid at Agra.
137.tq: Separate the patron or builder traditionally identified in the standard answer from a closely associated royal figure.
xs: Humayun's widow **Haji Begum (Bega Begum)** built the tomb — option **(1)**, the standard answer.
Some notes name **Hamida Banu Begum** (Akbar's mother), so "Hamida Banu alone" is the trap.
**Gulbadan Begum** wrote the **Humayun-nama**; **Jahanara** built the Jama Masjid, Agra.
xa: The tomb was built in **Akbar's** reign, c. **1565-72**.
It was the **first garden tomb** in the subcontinent and introduced the **double dome**.
UNESCO site since **1993**.

137.s: Which one of the following features is associated with Humayun’s tomb?
o: It was built entirely of black basalt without a dome.
It was the first garden tomb in the subcontinent and used red sandstone with white marble inlay.
It introduced the first rock-cut chaitya design in Delhi.
It was constructed only of timber and glazed tiles.
137.x: Humayun’s tomb was the first garden tomb in the subcontinent, introduced the double dome and used red sandstone with white marble inlay.
137.tq: Select the option combining the distinctive architectural features stated for the monument.
xs: Humayun's tomb was the **first garden tomb in the subcontinent** and used **red sandstone with white marble inlay** — option **(2)**.
It also introduced the **double dome** (inner and outer shells).
xa: Its **jali (lattice)** work is a hallmark.
It inspired the **Taj Mahal** (garden tomb, double dome).
UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed **1993**.

137.s: Who completed the tomb of Sher Shah Suri at Sasaram after Sher Shah's death?
137.x: Sher Shah Suri's tomb at Sasaram was completed under his son Islam Shah.
137.tq: Use the builder-successor distinction to avoid swapping the patron with the person who completed the work.
xs: Sher Shah's tomb was finished under his son **Islam Shah** — option **(3)**.
It is at **Sasaram**, Bihar, **set in a tank**.
xa: It marks the **Sur transition** in tomb architecture.
Earlier **Sayyid-Lodi** tombs used Hindu-style gates and facades, plaster ornament and drip-stones.

137.s: Which development is associated with the Sayyid-Lodi tomb tradition?
o: Introduction of Hindu-style gates and facades
Construction of the first double dome
Exclusive use of white marble and pietra dura
137.x: Sayyid-Lodi tombs incorporated Hindu elements such as Hindu-style gates and facades, plaster ornament and drip-stones.
137.tq: Identify the distinctive architectural contribution rather than the later Mughal features.
xs: **Sayyid-Lodi** tombs show **Hindu-style gates and facades** — option **(1)**.
They also used **plaster ornament** and **drip-stones**.
The **double dome** came at **Humayun's tomb**; **mirror work** is in the **Sheesh Mahal**.
xa: Evolution: Sayyid-Lodi → **Sher Shah's tomb** (Sur transition) → **Itimad-ud-Daula** → **Taj Mahal** (climax) → **Bibi ka Maqbara** (late imitation).
White marble with **pietra dura** first appeared at **Itimad-ud-Daula**.

137.s: Which monument marked the transition from the Lodi tradition to the Mughal architectural tradition under the Sur rulers?
137.x: Sher Shah's tomb at Sasaram marks the Sur transition in the evolution of Indo-Islamic tomb architecture.
137.tq: Use the historical transition clue to connect the monument with the correct dynasty.
xs: **Sher Shah's tomb** marks the **Sur transition** — option **(1)**.
It is at **Sasaram**, Bihar, set in a tank; finished under **Islam Shah**.
The **Taj Mahal** is the climax and **Bibi ka Maqbara** the late imitation of the tradition.
xa: Sayyid-Lodi tombs: **Hindu-style gates**, plaster ornament, drip-stones.
**Itimad-ud-Daula** = first Mughal tomb in **white marble** with **pietra dura**.

137.s: Which of the following is correctly associated with Itimad-ud-Daula's tomb?
o: It was built by Aurangzeb at Khuldabad as a simple grave.
It was built by Prince Azam Shah for his mother at Aurangabad.
It was built by Sher Shah at Sasaram and set in a tank.
It was built by Nur Jahan for her father and is known as the “Baby Taj”.
137.x: Itimad-ud-Daula's tomb at Agra was built by Nur Jahan for her father, Mirza Ghiyas Beg, and is popularly called the “Baby Taj”.
137.tq: Separate similar tomb traditions by matching the builder, beneficiary, place and popular title.
xs: **Itimad-ud-Daula** was built by **Nur Jahan for her father** and is called the "**Baby Taj**" — option **(4)**.
Her father was **Mirza Ghiyas Beg**; the tomb is at **Agra**, **1622-1628**.
Khuldabad = **Aurangzeb**'s grave; Aurangabad = **Bibi ka Maqbara**; Sasaram = **Sher Shah's tomb**.
xa: It was the **first Mughal tomb in white marble** with **pietra dura**.
It marks the transition to white marble under **Jahangir**.

137.s: Fatehpur Sikri was built in honour of which Sufi saint, after whom Prince Salim was named?
137.x: Fatehpur Sikri was built in honour of Sheikh Salim Chishti, after whom Prince Salim was named.
137.tq: Use the direct saint–monument association.
xs: Fatehpur Sikri was built in honour of **Sheikh Salim Chishti** — option **(2)**.
**Akbar** planned it as his capital, **1571-1585**.
xa: Salim Chishti's white-marble tomb lies in the **Jami Masjid** courtyard.
Main material: **red sandstone**; UNESCO site since **1986**.
Style: blend of **Persian, Indian and Central Asian**.

137.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with Fatehpur Sikri?
137.x: Panch Mahal, the Jama Masjid and Jodha Bai's palace are at Fatehpur Sikri. The Moti Masjids are in Agra Fort (Shah Jahan) and the Red Fort, Delhi (Aurangzeb), not at Fatehpur Sikri.
137.tq: Find the structure that does not belong to the monument group.
xs: **Moti Masjid** is not at Fatehpur Sikri — option **(4)**.
The Moti Masjids are in **Agra Fort** (**Shah Jahan**) and the **Red Fort** (**Aurangzeb**).
**Panch Mahal**, **Jama Masjid** and **Jodha Bai's palace** are all at Fatehpur Sikri.
xa: Other Fatehpur Sikri buildings: **Buland Darwaza**, **Ibadat Khana**, **Diwan-i-Khas**, Salim Chishti's tomb.
⚠ Moti Masjid: **Red Fort** = Aurangzeb; **Agra Fort** = Shah Jahan.

137.s: The Panch Mahal at Fatehpur Sikri was influenced by which architectural feature?
137.x: The Panch Mahal was influenced by Persian wind towers.
137.tq: Identify the distinctive architectural influence.
xs: The **Panch Mahal** was influenced by **Persian wind towers** — option **(2)**.
It is a **five-storeyed pavilion** at Fatehpur Sikri.
xa: **Jodha Bai's palace** blends Hindu **trabeate** and Islamic **arcuate** styles.
**Diwan-i-Khas**: single central carved pillar supporting a throne platform.
Fatehpur Sikri introduced the **Tudor (four-centred) arch**.

137.s: The principal material used in the construction of Fatehpur Sikri was:
137.x: Fatehpur Sikri was constructed mainly of red sandstone.
137.tq: Use the material contrast between Akbar's red-sandstone phase and Shah Jahan's marble phase.
xs: Fatehpur Sikri was built mainly of **red sandstone** — option **(4)**.
**Akbar's** phase is the red-sandstone phase (Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri); **white marble** dominated under **Shah Jahan**.
xa: Salim Chishti's tomb within it is in **white marble**.
Fatehpur Sikri: **1571-1585**; UNESCO **1986**.
Style: **Persian, Indian and Central Asian** blend.

137.s: Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri was constructed to commemorate Akbar's:
o: Victory at the Second Battle of Panipat
Accession to the throne at Kalanaur
137.x: Buland Darwaza, meaning the “Gate of Magnificence”, commemorated Akbar's victory in the Gujarat conquest.
137.tq: Distinguish the commemorated event from other major events of Akbar's reign.
xs: **Buland Darwaza** commemorates Akbar's **victory in the Gujarat conquest** — option **(4)**.
It is the "**Gate of Magnificence**" (c. **1575**), the **southern entrance** to the Jami Masjid.
xa: ⚠ "Not built by Shah Jahan" = **Buland Darwaza** (APPSC GS **2019**).
Fatehpur Sikri was built in honour of **Sheikh Salim Chishti**.

137.s: Which building at Fatehpur Sikri served as a house of worship where scholars of different religions held philosophical debates?
137.x: The Ibadat Khana was the House of Worship used for philosophical debates among scholars of various religions.
137.tq: Match the building with its precise institutional purpose.
xs: The **Ibadat Khana** was the **House of Worship** for debates among scholars of various religions — option **(2)**.
It was built in **1575** and was part of the religious core of Fatehpur Sikri.
**Jodha Bai's palace** = trabeate + arcuate; **Diwan-i-Khas** = private audience; **Panch Mahal** = five-storeyed pavilion.
xa: The religious core also had the **Jama Masjid** and **Salim Chishti's tomb**.
**Buland Darwaza** was also built c. **1575**.

137.s: Jodha Bai's palace at Fatehpur Sikri illustrates the combination of:
o: Hindu trabeate and Islamic arcuate styles
Buddhist stupa and Jain temple styles
Persian dome and Turkish minaret styles only
137.x: Jodha Bai's palace combines Hindu trabeate construction, based on beams and lintels, with Islamic arcuate construction, based on arches and domes.
137.tq: Distinguish trabeate and arcuate systems by their structural elements.
xs: Jodha Bai's palace blends **Hindu trabeate** and **Islamic arcuate** styles — option **(1)**.
**Trabeate** = **beam and lintel** (Hindu); **arcuate** = **arch and dome** (Islamic).
xa: The **Persian-Indian synthesis**: arch and dome + trabeate, **chhatris**, **Hindu motifs** (Fatehpur Sikri, Akbar's tomb).
**Panch Mahal** shows **Persian wind tower** influence.

137.s: Which feature is characteristic of the Diwan-i-Khas at Fatehpur Sikri?
o: A five-storeyed pavilion with Persian wind towers
A single central carved pillar supporting a throne platform
A gateway commemorating the Gujarat conquest
A white-marble tomb in the Jami Masjid courtyard
137.x: The Diwan-i-Khas is known for its single central carved pillar supporting a throne platform.
137.tq: Use the unique central-pillar feature to identify the correct building.
xs: The **Diwan-i-Khas** has a **single central carved pillar supporting a throne platform** — option **(2)**.
It was the **hall of private audience**.
Five-storeyed pavilion = **Panch Mahal**; Gujarat gateway = **Buland Darwaza**; white-marble tomb = **Salim Chishti's tomb**.
xa: The Red Fort's Diwan-i-Khas housed the **Peacock Throne** (taken by **Nadir Shah**, **1739**).
**Agra Fort** also has a Diwan-i-Am and Diwan-i-Khas.

137.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Fatehpur Sikri:
1. It was planned as Akbar's capital during 1571–1585.
2. Its buildings show Persian, Indian and Central Asian influences.
3. Akbar introduced the Tudor or four-centred arch in his buildings.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
137.x: All three statements are correct. Fatehpur Sikri was Akbar's planned capital during 1571–1585 and reflects multiple architectural influences, including the Tudor arch introduced by Akbar.
137.tq: Test chronology, stylistic synthesis and a specific architectural innovation together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1: Fatehpur Sikri was **Akbar's** planned capital, **1571-1585**.
Statement 2: its style blends **Persian, Indian and Central Asian** elements.
Statement 3: it introduced the **Tudor (four-centred) arch**.
xa: Built in honour of **Sheikh Salim Chishti**, mainly in **red sandstone**.
**Jahangir Mahal at Orchha** (MP) continues Akbar's style.
UNESCO World Heritage Site (**1986**).

137.s: Who is identified as the chief architect of the Taj Mahal?
137.x: Ustad Ahmad Lahori is identified as the chief architect of the Taj Mahal.
137.tq: Test the specific architect associated with the monument rather than a general Mughal architect.
xs: The chief architect of the Taj Mahal was **Ustad Ahmad Lahori** — option **(2)**.
The Taj was built by **Shah Jahan** at **Agra**, **1632-1648**.
xa: Its marble came from **Makrana** (Rajasthan) (APPSC GS **2016**).
It is the mausoleum of **Mumtaz Mahal (Arjumand Banu Begum)**.
**V.A. Smith**: combination of **European and Asiatic genius**.

137.s: The design of the Taj Mahal was particularly inspired by which earlier Mughal monument?
137.x: Humayun's Tomb provided an important design ancestry for the Taj Mahal, particularly through the garden-tomb form and use of a double dome.
137.tq: Trace architectural influence from an earlier monument rather than selecting a later or contemporary structure.
xs: **Humayun's Tomb** inspired the Taj Mahal's design — option **(1)**.
It gave the **garden tomb**, **double dome** and red sandstone with marble.
xa: Humayun's tomb = **first garden tomb** in the subcontinent.
The Taj stands at the **river end** of its **charbagh**, not the centre.
The Taj = **climax** of the tomb tradition; Bibi ka Maqbara = late imitation.

137.s: Which statement correctly describes the position of the Taj Mahal within its charbagh?
o: The tomb stands at the southern entrance of the garden.
The tomb stands at the exact centre of the garden.
The tomb stands outside the charbagh on the western side.
The tomb stands at the river end of the charbagh.
137.x: Unlike the usual central placement in a charbagh, the Taj Mahal's tomb stands at the river end of the garden, near the Yamuna.
137.tq: Distinguish the Taj Mahal's exceptional garden placement from the usual central-tomb arrangement.
xs: The Taj stands at the **river end of the charbagh** — option **(4)**.
It is not at the garden's centre; it is on the right bank of the **Yamuna**.
xa: **Charbagh** = four-quartered garden, introduced by **Babur** (Ram Bagh, Agra).
Garden-tomb line: **Humayun's tomb** (first garden tomb) → **Taj Mahal**.

137.s: Which one of the following statements about the Taj Mahal is NOT correct?
o: It was built entirely of red sandstone.
It is associated with the mausoleum of Mumtaz Mahal.
It was built at Agra by Shah Jahan.
It represents a high point of pietra dura and symmetry.
137.x: The Taj Mahal is principally constructed of white marble, not entirely of red sandstone. It is the mausoleum of Mumtaz Mahal and is noted for pietra dura and symmetry.
137.tq: Reject the material-based reversal between the Taj Mahal and earlier red-sandstone Mughal monuments.
xs: "**Built entirely of red sandstone**" is wrong — the Taj is in **white marble** — option **(1)**.
It is the mausoleum of **Mumtaz Mahal**, built at **Agra** by **Shah Jahan**.
It is the **pinnacle of pietra dura** and **symmetry**.
xa: Marble source: **Makrana** (Rajasthan).
UNESCO **1983**; among the **New Seven Wonders** (**2007**).

137.s: The Taj Mahal was constructed approximately during which period, while the whole complex is sometimes dated to 1653 in older accounts?
137.x: The main construction period of the Taj Mahal is given as 1632–1648. Older accounts sometimes cite 1653 as the year in which the entire complex was completed.
137.tq: Separate the principal construction period from a later date associated with completion of the whole complex.
xs: The Taj was built in **1632-1648** — option **(4)**.
Older notes give **1653**, the year the whole complex was finished.
**1565-1572** = Humayun's tomb; **1650-1656** = Jama Masjid, Delhi.
xa: Chief architect: **Ustad Ahmad Lahori**.

137.s: The Taj Mahal is threatened by the phenomenon popularly known as ‘marble cancer’, which is primarily associated with:
137.x: Sulphur dioxide emitted by the Mathura refinery, industries and traffic contributes to yellowing and the deterioration popularly called marble cancer.
137.tq: Apply the environmental cause to the monument affected by pollution.
xs: "**Marble cancer**" is yellowing from **sulphur dioxide** pollution — option **(1)**.
Sources: the **Mathura refinery**, industries and traffic.
xa: The Supreme Court's **Taj Trapezium Zone (TTZ)** rulings came in the **M.C. Mehta** case (**1996**).
Allahabad HC issued notices to Centre and **ASI** on a Taj Mahal survey petition (21 Jul **2026**).

137.s: The Taj Trapezium Zone (TTZ) rulings concerning protection of the Taj Mahal are associated with the case of:
137.x: The Supreme Court's Taj Trapezium Zone rulings, including those concerning industrial pollution, were associated with the M.C. Mehta case in 1996.
137.tq: Match an environmental protection measure with the relevant legal case.
xs: The **TTZ** rulings came in the **M.C. Mehta** case — option **(1)**.
The Supreme Court ruled in **1996** against pollution threatening the Taj.
xa: Threat: **marble cancer**, yellowing from **sulphur dioxide** (Mathura refinery, industries, traffic).
The Taj is a UNESCO site since **1983**.

137.s: The white marble used in the construction of the Taj Mahal was obtained mainly from
137.x: The Taj Mahal's marble came from Makrana in Rajasthan. Sasaram is the site of Sher Shah's tomb, Fatehpur Sikri was built mainly of red sandstone, and Kollur is known for diamond mines (the Koh-i-Noor).
137.tq: Taj marble = Makrana (Rajasthan).
xs: The Taj's marble came from **Makrana in Rajasthan** — option **(1)**.
This was the APPSC GS **2016** key.
**Sasaram** = Sher Shah's tomb; **Fatehpur Sikri** = red sandstone.
xa: Taj features: **pietra dura**, symmetry, white marble.
Architect: **Ustad Ahmad Lahori**.

137.s: Which historian described the Taj Mahal as the product of a combination of European and Asiatic genius?
137.x: V.A. Smith saw the Taj Mahal as a combination of European and Asiatic genius (APPSC-G1 2022 key). Fergusson and Percy Brown treated it as a product of the Indo-Persian tradition, and R.C. Majumdar is a distractor here.
137.tq: European + Asiatic genius = V.A. Smith.
xs: **V.A. Smith** saw the Taj as a combination of **European and Asiatic genius** — option **(3)**.
This is the APPSC-G1 **2022** key.
**James Fergusson** and **Percy Brown** saw it as a product of the **Indo-Persian tradition**.
xa: Chief architect: **Ustad Ahmad Lahori**; marble from **Makrana**.
Built **1632-1648** for **Mumtaz Mahal**.

137.s: Shah Jahan's new capital, Shahjahanabad, included which of the following principal monuments?
o: Sasaram tomb and Bibi ka Maqbara
Agra Fort and Ram Bagh only
137.x: Shahjahanabad in Delhi included the Red Fort and the Jama Masjid. Shah Jahan's reign is regarded as the Golden Age of Mughal architecture.
137.tq: Identify the components of the capital rather than confusing them with monuments at Fatehpur Sikri or Agra.
xs: **Shahjahanabad** included the **Red Fort and Jama Masjid** — option **(4)**.
It was **Shah Jahan's** new capital at **Delhi**.
**Panch Mahal** and **Ibadat Khana** are at Fatehpur Sikri; **Bibi ka Maqbara** is at Aurangabad.
xa: Shah Jahan's reign = "**Golden Age**" of Mughal architecture.
Red Fort: **1639-48**; Jama Masjid, Delhi: **1650-1656**.
Red Fort Complex: UNESCO **2007**.

137.s: Which one of the following statements about the Diwan-i-Khas of the Red Fort is correct?
o: It was the residence of the royal women and was called the Palace of Colours.
It housed the Peacock Throne, which was taken by Nadir Shah in 1739.
It was built by Aurangzeb as the Moti Masjid.
It was the public audience hall of Shah Jahan.
137.x: The Diwan-i-Khas was the private audience hall and housed the Peacock Throne, which was taken by Nadir Shah in 1739.
137.tq: Use the famous object-event association while distinguishing the two audience halls.
xs: The Red Fort's **Diwan-i-Khas** housed the **Peacock Throne**, taken by **Nadir Shah** in **1739** — option **(2)**.
It was the **hall of private audience**.
**Rang Mahal** = Palace of Colours for royal women; **Diwan-i-Am** = public audience.
xa: The Red Fort's **Moti Masjid** was built by **Aurangzeb**.
**Sheesh Mahal** = mirror-work chambers.

137.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the two Mughal structures named Moti Masjid?
o: The Moti Masjid in the Red Fort was built by Aurangzeb, whereas the Moti Masjid in Agra Fort was built by Shah Jahan.
The Red Fort Moti Masjid was built by Shah Jahan, whereas the Agra Fort Moti Masjid was built by Aurangzeb.
Both Moti Masjids were built by Akbar in Agra Fort.
Both Moti Masjids were built by Aurangzeb in Delhi.
137.x: Aurangzeb built the Moti Masjid in the Red Fort, while Shah Jahan built the Moti Masjid in Agra Fort.
137.tq: Resolve the look-alike monument pair by comparing location and builder.
xs: **Red Fort** Moti Masjid = **Aurangzeb**; **Agra Fort** Moti Masjid = **Shah Jahan** — option **(1)**.
Options 2–4 swap or merge the builders; neither Moti Masjid is **Akbar's**.
xa: Shah Jahan also built the **Red Fort** and **Jama Masjid, Delhi**.
Red Fort uses **red sandstone** for structure + **marble** for decoration.

137.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Rang Mahal — hall of public audience
137.x: Sheesh Mahal is associated with mirror-work chambers. Rang Mahal was for the royal women, Diwan-i-Am was for public audience and Diwan-i-Khas was for private audience.
137.tq: Match each Red Fort component with its specific function or decorative treatment.
xs: **Sheesh Mahal — mirror-work chambers** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Rang Mahal** = Palace of Colours for the **royal women**; **Diwan-i-Am** = **public** audience; **Diwan-i-Khas** = **private** audience.
xa: Diwan-i-Khas housed the **Peacock Throne**.
⚠ Moti Masjid: Red Fort = **Aurangzeb**; Agra Fort = **Shah Jahan**.

137.s:
Consider the following statements about forts associated with the Mughal rulers:
1. Agra Fort was begun by Akbar in 1565.
2. Allahabad Fort was built by Akbar in 1583.
3. Lahore Fort was rebuilt by Akbar.
4. The Red Fort at Delhi was built by Shah Jahan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
137.x: All four statements are correct. Agra Fort was begun in 1565, Allahabad Fort was built in 1583, Lahore Fort was rebuilt by Akbar and the Red Fort at Delhi was built by Shah Jahan.
137.tq: Check the ruler, date and location of each fort before selecting the complete code.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Agra Fort**: Akbar, begun **1565**; **Allahabad Fort**: Akbar, **1583**.
**Lahore Fort** rebuilt by **Akbar**; **Red Fort, Delhi** built by **Shah Jahan**.
xa: Agra Fort: **red sandstone**, on the **Yamuna**; has Diwan-i-Am and Diwan-i-Khas.
Agra Fort and Taj Mahal: UNESCO **1983**.

137.s: Agra Fort, associated with Akbar, was constructed mainly of:
o: Red sandstone and is situated on the Yamuna
Black stone and is situated on the Narmada
Granite and is situated on the Godavari
White marble and is situated on the Ganga
137.x: Akbar's Agra Fort was begun in 1565, constructed of red sandstone and situated on the Yamuna. It contains the Diwan-i-Am and Diwan-i-Khas.
137.tq: Combine builder, material and river-location clues to identify the correct fort description.
xs: Agra Fort is of **red sandstone** and **on the Yamuna** — option **(1)**.
Akbar began it in **1565**; it contains the **Diwan-i-Am** and **Diwan-i-Khas**.
xa: The **Moti Masjid** in Agra Fort is **Shah Jahan's**.
Akbar also built **Allahabad Fort** (**1583**) and rebuilt **Lahore Fort**.

137.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Jami Masjid, Fatehpur Sikri — Akbar
2. Jama Masjid, Delhi — Shah Jahan
3. Moti Masjid, Agra Fort — Shah Jahan
4. Buland Darwaza — Shah Jahan
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
137.x: The Jami Masjid at Fatehpur Sikri was built by Akbar, while the Jama Masjid of Delhi and Moti Masjid of Agra Fort were built by Shah Jahan. Buland Darwaza was built by Akbar, not Shah Jahan.
137.tq: Find the swapped builder in a monument–ruler pairing.
xs: Pairs **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Jami Masjid, Fatehpur Sikri** — **Akbar**; **Jama Masjid, Delhi** — **Shah Jahan**; **Moti Masjid, Agra Fort** — **Shah Jahan**.
Pair 4 wrong: **Buland Darwaza** was built by **Akbar** (Gujarat victory).
xa: ⚠ "Not built by Shah Jahan" = **Buland Darwaza** (APPSC GS **2019**).
Shah Jahan: **Red Fort**, Jama Masjid (Delhi), Moti Masjid (Agra Fort).

137.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pietra dura — inlay of semi-precious stones
Double dome — inner and outer shells
137.x: Jali refers to lattice work. Mirror-work chambers are associated with the Sheesh Mahal.
137.tq: Separate related decorative terms by their exact meanings and locations.
xs: **Jali — mirror-work chambers** is wrong — option **(1)**.
**Jali** = **lattice** work (Humayun's tomb); mirror work is in the **Sheesh Mahal**.
**Pietra dura** = semi-precious stone inlay; **charbagh** = four-quartered garden; **double dome** = inner and outer shells — all correct.
xa: Other hallmarks: **calligraphy**, **arabesque**.
Double dome introduced at **Humayun's tomb**.

137.s: The charbagh garden tradition in Mughal architecture was introduced by:
137.x: Babur introduced the charbagh, or four-quartered garden, tradition; Ram Bagh at Agra is an example.
137.tq: Match the architectural innovation with the earliest Mughal ruler associated with it.
xs: **Babur** introduced the **charbagh** (four-quartered garden) — option **(4)**.
Example: **Ram Bagh**, Agra (c. **1528**), the **first Mughal garden**.
xa: Shalimar: **Srinagar** = **Jahangir**; **Lahore** = **Shah Jahan**.
**Nishat Bagh** (Srinagar) was built by **Asaf Khan**, Nur Jahan's brother.
**Pinjore garden** (Haryana): Fidai Khan, under Aurangzeb.

137.s: Which of the following correctly describes the development of pietra dura in Mughal architecture?
o: It began under Jahangir, appeared on a large scale at Itimad-ud-Daula and reached its peak at the Taj Mahal.
It began under Babur and reached its peak at Sher Shah's tomb.
It began under Akbar and was confined to red sandstone buildings.
It began under Aurangzeb and reached its peak at Bibi ka Maqbara.
137.x: Pietra dura began during Jahangir's reign, was first used on a large scale at Itimad-ud-Daula and reached its peak at the Taj Mahal.
137.tq: Arrange the beginning, large-scale use and culmination of a style in sequence.
xs: Pietra dura **began under Jahangir**, appeared on a large scale at **Itimad-ud-Daula** and peaked at the **Taj Mahal** — option **(1)**.
**Pietra dura** = inlay of **semi-precious stones**.
xa: Itimad-ud-Daula ("**Baby Taj**") = first Mughal tomb in white marble with pietra dura.
White marble: transition under **Jahangir**, dominant under **Shah Jahan**.

137.s: The Persian-Indian synthesis in Mughal architecture is best represented by the combination of:
o: Only European columns and Gothic vaults
Arches and domes with trabeate forms, chhatris and Hindu motifs
Only Buddhist stupas and Jain shikharas
137.x: The Persian-Indian synthesis combined arches and domes with trabeate forms, chhatris and Hindu motifs, as seen at Fatehpur Sikri and Akbar's tomb.
137.tq: Translate the stylistic definition into its constituent architectural elements.
xs: The **Persian-Indian synthesis** = **arches and domes** with **trabeate forms, chhatris and Hindu motifs** — option **(2)**.
Best seen at **Fatehpur Sikri** and **Akbar's tomb**.
xa: ⚠ **Trabeate** = beam and lintel (Hindu); **arcuate** = arch and dome (Islamic).
Mughal architecture blends **Persian**, **Timurid** and **Indian** elements.

137.s: Which comparison between the architectural phases of Akbar and Shah Jahan is correct?
o: Akbar is associated mainly with red sandstone, whereas Shah Jahan is associated mainly with white marble.
Akbar is associated mainly with white marble, whereas Shah Jahan is associated mainly with red sandstone.
Both rulers used only white marble.
Both rulers used only red sandstone.
137.x: Akbar's phase is represented by red-sandstone structures such as Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri, while Shah Jahan's phase is dominated by white marble, as in the Taj Mahal.
137.tq: Use the material contrast to distinguish the architectural phases of the two rulers.
xs: **Akbar** = mainly **red sandstone**; **Shah Jahan** = mainly **white marble** — option **(1)**.
Red sandstone: **Agra Fort**, **Fatehpur Sikri**; white marble: **Taj Mahal**.
The transition came under **Jahangir** (**Itimad-ud-Daula**).
xa: The **Red Fort** combines red sandstone structure with marble decoration.
Humayun's tomb: **red sandstone with white marble inlay**.

137.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the relevant architectural feature?
o: Humayun's tomb — double dome, calligraphy, arabesque and jali work
Taj Mahal — first use of the double dome
137.x: Humayun's tomb introduced the double dome and shows calligraphy, arabesque and jali work. The Sheesh Mahal is known for mirror work (the charbagh is the four-quartered garden), Ram Bagh is Babur's first garden while pietra dura peaked at the Taj Mahal, and the double dome first appeared at Humayun's tomb, not the Taj.
137.tq: Combine material, structural and decorative clues to identify the correct monument-feature pair.
xs: **Humayun's tomb** shows the **double dome, calligraphy, arabesque and jali work** — option **(1)**.
**Sheesh Mahal** = **mirror work**; the four-quartered garden is the **charbagh**.
**Ram Bagh** is Babur's first garden; **pietra dura** peaked at the **Taj Mahal**.
The double dome was introduced at **Humayun's tomb**, not the Taj.
xa: Humayun's tomb = **first garden tomb**; red sandstone with **white marble inlay**.
**Pietra dura** began under **Jahangir**, first on a large scale at **Itimad-ud-Daula**.

137.s: Nishat Bagh, situated on the banks of Dal Lake, was built by whom?
137.x: Nishat Bagh at Srinagar, on Dal Lake, was built by Asaf Khan, the brother of Nur Jahan.
137.tq: Discriminate between closely associated Mughal garden builders.
xs: **Nishat Bagh** was built by **Asaf Khan**, Nur Jahan's brother — option **(1)**.
It lies at **Srinagar** on **Dal Lake**.
**Jahangir** built Shalimar Bagh (Srinagar); **Fidai Khan** built Pinjore garden; **Babur** built Ram Bagh.
xa: ⚠ Shalimar: **Srinagar** = Jahangir; **Lahore** = Shah Jahan.
**Pinjore garden** (Haryana) was built under **Aurangzeb**.

137.s: Shalimar Gardens at Lahore were built under which Mughal ruler?
137.x: The Shalimar Gardens at Lahore were built under Shah Jahan. The Shalimar Bagh at Srinagar is associated with Jahangir.
137.tq: Separate the similarly named Shalimar gardens by location and builder.
xs: The **Shalimar Gardens at Lahore** were built under **Shah Jahan** — option **(4)**.
The **Shalimar Bagh at Srinagar** is **Jahangir's**.
xa: ⚠ Shalimar: **Srinagar** = Jahangir; **Lahore** = Shah Jahan.
**Nishat Bagh** (Srinagar, Dal Lake) = **Asaf Khan**.
**Charbagh** introduced by **Babur** (Ram Bagh, Agra).

137.s: Which of the following best describes the relationship between Humayun's Tomb and the Taj Mahal?
o: The Taj Mahal was the first garden tomb and Humayun's Tomb imitated it
Humayun's Tomb was the first garden tomb, while the Taj Mahal stands within a charbagh tradition
Both were constructed as fortifications along the Yamuna
Both monuments were built as congregational mosques
137.x: Humayun's Tomb is regarded as the first garden tomb, and the Taj Mahal represents the later development of the garden-tomb and charbagh tradition.
137.tq: Trace the architectural evolution from the earlier monument to the later one.
xs: **Humayun's Tomb** was the **first garden tomb**; the **Taj Mahal** stands within its **charbagh** — option **(2)**.
The line runs **Humayun's tomb → Taj Mahal**; the Taj did not come first.
The Taj stands at the **river end** of its charbagh, not the centre.
xa: Humayun's tomb gave the Taj its **double dome** and garden-tomb form.
**Charbagh** = four-quartered garden, introduced by **Babur**.

137.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
137.x: Ram Bagh was built by Babur at Agra, not Lahore. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
137.tq: Find the wrong location while keeping the builder association in view.
xs: **Ram Bagh — Lahore — Babur** is wrong: Ram Bagh is at **Agra** — option **(3)**.
**Nishat Bagh** — Srinagar — **Asaf Khan**; **Pinjore** — Haryana — **Fidai Khan**; **Shalimar Bagh** — Srinagar — **Jahangir**: all correct.
xa: Ram Bagh (c. **1528**) = **first Mughal garden**.
Lahore has Shah Jahan's **Shalimar Gardens** and **Jahangir's tomb** (Shahdara).

137.s: Babur's final tomb is located at:
137.x: Babur's tomb is at Bagh-e-Babur in Kabul, although he was first buried at Agra.
137.tq: Watch the distinction between the first burial place and the final tomb location.
xs: Babur's final tomb is at **Kabul** (**Bagh-e-Babur**) — option **(1)**.
He was **first buried at Agra**.
xa: Humayun — **Delhi**; Akbar — **Sikandra**; Jahangir — **Shahdara, Lahore**.
Shah Jahan — **Taj Mahal, Agra**; Aurangzeb — **Khuldabad**.

137.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
137.x: Shah Jahan is buried in the Taj Mahal at Agra beside Mumtaz Mahal. Sikandra near Agra is associated with Akbar's tomb.
137.tq: Find the wrongly shifted emperor-location pair among otherwise familiar tomb sites.
xs: **Shah Jahan — Sikandra** is wrong — option **(4)**.
Shah Jahan lies in the **Taj Mahal, Agra**, beside **Mumtaz Mahal**; **Sikandra** is **Akbar's** tomb.
Aurangzeb — **Khuldabad**; Jahangir — **Shahdara, Lahore**; Humayun — **Delhi**: correct.
xa: Babur — **Kabul** (Bagh-e-Babur), first buried at Agra.
Akbar's tomb was begun by Akbar and **completed by Jahangir**.

137.s: Which of the following statements about the tombs of Mughal emperors is correct?
o: Jahangir's tomb is at Shahdara in Lahore.
Humayun's tomb is at Sikandra near Agra.
Babur's final tomb is at Shahdara in Lahore.
Aurangzeb's tomb is beside Mumtaz Mahal in Agra.
137.x: Jahangir's tomb is located at Shahdara in Lahore. Humayun's tomb is in Delhi, Babur's final tomb is in Kabul and Aurangzeb's grave is at Khuldabad.
137.tq: Discriminate among closely related emperor-tomb locations rather than relying on the city alone.
xs: **Jahangir's tomb** is at **Shahdara, Lahore** — option **(1)**.
Humayun's tomb is in **Delhi**; **Sikandra** is Akbar's.
Babur's final tomb is at **Kabul**; Aurangzeb's is at **Khuldabad**, not Agra.
xa: Shah Jahan lies in the **Taj Mahal** beside Mumtaz Mahal.
Lahore also has Shah Jahan's **Shalimar Gardens**.

137.s: Aurangzeb's tomb is distinguished from the grand Mughal mausoleums because it is:
o: A marble tomb at Agra beside Mumtaz Mahal
A simple grave at Khuldabad near Aurangabad
137.x: Aurangzeb was buried in a simple grave at Khuldabad near Aurangabad.
137.tq: Use the contrast between Aurangzeb's simple grave and the monumental Mughal tombs.
xs: Aurangzeb lies in **a simple grave at Khuldabad near Aurangabad** — option **(4)**.
The tank-set tomb at **Sasaram** is Sher Shah's; the garden tomb at **Delhi** is Humayun's; the tomb beside Mumtaz Mahal is **Shah Jahan's**.
xa: **Bibi ka Maqbara** at Aurangabad was built by Prince **Azam Shah** in Aurangzeb's reign.
Aurangzeb built the **Moti Masjid** in the **Red Fort**.

137.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Monument)
a. Charminar
b. Akbar's Tomb
c. Humayun's Tomb
d. Taj Mahal
List-II (Place)
i. Agra
ii. Delhi
iii. Sikandara
iv. Hyderabad
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
137.x: Charminar is in Hyderabad, Akbar's Tomb at Sikandara, Humayun's Tomb in Delhi and the Taj Mahal at Agra.
137.tq: Akbar rests at Sikandara near Agra, not in Agra itself.
xs: Correct code **a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i** — option **(4)**.
**Charminar** — **Hyderabad**; **Akbar's Tomb** — **Sikandara**.
**Humayun's Tomb** — **Delhi**; **Taj Mahal** — **Agra**.
xa: This is the APPSC G1 **2018** pairs question.
⚠ Charminar (**1591**) is **Qutb Shahi** — **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah**.

137.s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents UNESCO inscription years of Mughal sites in India?
o: Agra Fort and Taj Mahal—1993; Fatehpur Sikri—2007; Humayun's Tomb—1983; Red Fort Complex—1986
Agra Fort and Taj Mahal—1986; Fatehpur Sikri—1983; Humayun's Tomb—2007; Red Fort Complex—1993
Agra Fort and Taj Mahal—1983; Fatehpur Sikri—1986; Humayun's Tomb—1993; Red Fort Complex—2007
Agra Fort and Taj Mahal—2007; Fatehpur Sikri—1993; Humayun's Tomb—1986; Red Fort Complex—1983
137.x: Agra Fort and the Taj Mahal were inscribed in 1983, Fatehpur Sikri in 1986, Humayun's Tomb in 1993 and the Red Fort Complex in 2007.
137.tq: Anchor the sequence using the four distinct inscription years.
xs: **Agra Fort and Taj Mahal—1983; Fatehpur Sikri—1986; Humayun's Tomb—1993; Red Fort Complex—2007** — option **(3)**.
The order follows the sequence **1983 → 1986 → 1993 → 2007**.
xa: The Taj was also named among the **New Seven Wonders** in **2007**.
Fatehpur Sikri: Akbar's capital, **1571-1585**.

137.s: The Taj Mahal was included among the New Seven Wonders of the World in which year?
137.x: The Taj Mahal was included among the New Seven Wonders of the World in 2007.
137.tq: Distinguish the UNESCO inscription year from the New Seven Wonders year.
xs: The Taj joined the **New Seven Wonders** in **2007** — option **(3)**.
**1983** is its UNESCO inscription year (with Agra Fort); **1993** is Humayun's Tomb.
xa: **Red Fort Complex** was also inscribed in **2007**.
The Taj was built **1632-1648** by **Shah Jahan**.

137.s: Which one of the following is NOT included in the listed UNESCO Mughal sites in India?
137.x: Golconda Fort is a Qutb Shahi monument and is not included in the listed UNESCO Mughal sites. Humayun's Tomb, the Red Fort Complex and Fatehpur Sikri are included.
137.tq: Use the dynasty distinction to eliminate the non-Mughal monument.
xs: **Golconda Fort** is not among the listed UNESCO Mughal sites — option **(4)**.
It is a **Qutb Shahi** fort, known for its **acoustic warning system** and **piped water**.
**Humayun's Tomb** (**1993**), **Red Fort Complex** (**2007**) and **Fatehpur Sikri** (**1986**) are listed.
xa: Agra Fort and Taj Mahal were inscribed in **1983**.
**Qutb Shahi tombs** at Ibrahim Bagh: onion domes on square bases.

137.s: Mughal architecture is generally regarded as the zenith of which architectural tradition?
137.x: Mughal architecture is regarded as the peak or zenith of Indo-Islamic architecture, combining Persian, Timurid and Indian elements.
137.tq: Identify the broad architectural classification rather than a monument-specific feature.
xs: Mughal architecture is the **zenith of Indo-Islamic architecture** — option **(2)**.
It blends **Persian, Timurid and Indian** elements.
xa: Hallmarks: **red sandstone** + **white marble**, **charbagh**, **double dome**, **pietra dura**, **calligraphy**.
Shah Jahan's reign = "**Golden Age**" of Mughal architecture.

137.s: The architectural synthesis represented by Mughal monuments primarily blended which traditions?
137.x: Mughal architecture blended Persian, Timurid and Indian architectural elements.
137.tq: Test the exact components of a cultural synthesis without confusing them with general influences.
xs: Mughal architecture blended **Persian, Timurid and Indian** traditions — option **(3)**.
It is the **zenith of Indo-Islamic architecture**.
xa: **Persian-Indian synthesis**: arch and dome + trabeate, **chhatris**, Hindu motifs (Fatehpur Sikri, Akbar's tomb).
Fatehpur Sikri: **Persian, Indian and Central Asian** blend.

137.s: Which of the following is regarded as the last major imitation in the Mughal garden-tomb tradition?
137.x: Bibi ka Maqbara is regarded as the last major imitation in the Mughal garden-tomb tradition.
137.tq: Distinguish the terminal example from the first example in an architectural sequence.
xs: **Bibi ka Maqbara** is the **last major imitation** — option **(4)**.
It is the "**Taj of the Deccan**" at Aurangabad, built by **Azam Shah**.
**Ram Bagh** = first Mughal garden; **Humayun's Tomb** = first garden tomb.
xa: FIRST/LAST: first Mughal garden = **Ram Bagh**; pietra dura first under **Jahangir**.
⚠ "**Baby Taj**" = Itimad-ud-Daula; "**Taj of the Deccan**" = Bibi ka Maqbara.

137.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Bahmani Jama Masjid at Gulbarga from Mughal open-court mosques?
o: It follows a charbagh garden plan, unlike Mughal tombs
It is built entirely of white marble, unlike all Mughal mosques
It has no domes, unlike every Mughal mosque
It has a fully covered courtyard, unlike the open-court pattern of Mughal mosques
137.x: The Bahmani Jama Masjid at Gulbarga is notable for its fully covered courtyard, whereas Mughal mosques generally followed an open-court arrangement.
137.tq: Focus on the precise structural contrast rather than broad stylistic similarities.
xs: The **Bahmani Jama Masjid at Gulbarga** has a **fully covered courtyard**, unlike the **open-court** Mughal mosques — option **(4)**.
**Charbagh** plans belong to garden tombs, not mosques; the notes give no basis for the "white marble" or "no domes" claims.
xa: Shah Jahan's **Jama Masjid, Delhi** (**1650-1656**) is part of Shahjahanabad.
Akbar's **Jami Masjid, Fatehpur Sikri** (c. **1571-74**) has Buland Darwaza as its southern entrance.

137.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Qutb Shahi tombs — onion domes on square bases in gardens
Golconda Fort — acoustic warning system and piped water
Charminar — Persian arches with Deccani stucco
137.x: Charminar is not a fully covered courtyard mosque; that feature is associated with the Bahmani Jama Masjid at Gulbarga. The other pairs are correctly matched.
137.tq: Reject the option that imports a distinctive feature from a different monument.
xs: **Charminar — fully covered courtyard mosque** is wrong — option **(1)**.
The fully covered courtyard belongs to the **Bahmani Jama Masjid at Gulbarga**.
**Qutb Shahi tombs** (onion domes), **Golconda Fort** (acoustic warning, piped water) and **Charminar** (Persian arches + Deccani stucco) are correct.
xa: Charminar (**1591**), by **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah**, marked the **end of a plague**.
Qutb Shahi tombs are at **Ibrahim Bagh**.

137.s: Which of the following monuments is a common distractor when identifying Mughal architectural monuments but is actually a Qutb Shahi work?
137.x: Charminar is a Qutb Shahi monument of Hyderabad, not a Mughal monument. Humayun's Tomb, the Taj Mahal and Agra Fort belong to the Mughal architectural tradition.
137.tq: Separate Mughal monuments from the nearby Deccan Qutb Shahi example.
xs: **Charminar** is a **Qutb Shahi** work, a common distractor in Mughal lists — option **(4)**.
**Taj Mahal**, **Agra Fort** and **Humayun's Tomb** are Mughal.
xa: Charminar: **1591**, **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah**, Hyderabad.
Style: **Persian arches** + **Deccani stucco**.

137.s:
Consider the following statements regarding a current legal development:
1. The Allahabad High Court issued notices to the Centre and the Archaeological Survey of India.
2. The notices related to a petition challenging an Agra court's refusal to permit a survey of the Taj Mahal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
137.x: Both statements are correct. The Allahabad High Court issued notices in connection with the petition challenging the Agra court's refusal to allow a survey of the Taj Mahal.
137.tq: Link the authority, legal action and subject of the petition without reversing the procedural sequence.
xs: Both statements are correct — option **(3)**.
The **Allahabad HC** issued notices to the **Centre and ASI** (21 Jul **2026**).
The petition challenged an **Agra court's refusal** to permit a **Taj Mahal survey**.
xa: The Supreme Court's **TTZ** rulings came in the **M.C. Mehta** case (**1996**).
Taj threat: **marble cancer** from **sulphur dioxide**.

138.s:
Who among the following Persian masters was brought to India by Humayun and helped lay the foundation of the Mughal school of painting?
1. Mir Sayyid Ali
2. Abdus Samad
3. Ustad Mansur
4. Basawan
138.x: Humayun brought the Persian masters Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad, who founded the Mughal school (statements 1 and 2). Basawan was an Akbar-era master and Ustad Mansur a painter of Jahangir's court, so neither was brought by Humayun.
138.tq: Identify the two associated names before eliminating painters from later reigns.
xs: **Humayun** brought the Persian masters **Mir Sayyid Ali** and **Abdus Samad** (**1 and 2 only**) — option **(1)**.
They **founded the Mughal school** (APPSC-G2 **2025**, statement a).
**Basawan** was an **Akbar**-era master; **Ustad Mansur** was **Jahangir's** painter.
xa: Both masters supervised the **Hamzanama** in turn: first Mir Sayyid Ali, then Abdus Samad.
Abdus Samad's title = **Shirin Qalam**.
FIRST: **Humayun** first brought Persian painters.

138.s: The Mughal school of painting gradually developed from Persian miniature painting into which type of style?
o: A geometric style based exclusively on Central Asian art
A symbolic style without human figures
A purely religious and monochromatic style
138.x: The style gradually moved from Persian miniature painting towards a realistic and colourful Indian style.
138.tq: Choose the precise description of the artistic transition rather than an extreme or exclusive alternative.
xs: Mughal painting evolved from **Persian miniature** into **a realistic, colourful Indian style** — option **(3)**.
Under **Akbar** it gained **3-D figures** and **realism**; under **Jahangir** it peaked in **naturalism**.
xa: Mughal colour was **muted, naturalistic**, with **perspective and shading** (European influence).
Rajput painting, by contrast, was **indigenous, vivid, decorative**.

138.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Emperor)
a. Humayun
b. Akbar
c. Jahangir
d. Shah Jahan

List-II (Emphasis)
i. Formal court scenes, albums and floral borders
ii. Foundation through Persian masters
iii. Illustrated manuscripts and a large painting atelier
iv. Portraits, albums, flora, fauna and naturalism

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
138.x: Humayun is associated with the Persian masters; Akbar with illustrated manuscripts; Jahangir with naturalism; and Shah Jahan with formal court scenes and floral decoration.
138.tq: Start from the sure pair and match the distinctive artistic emphasis of each emperor.
xs: Correct code **a–ii, b–iii, c–iv, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Humayun** → foundation through Persian masters; **Akbar** → **illustrated manuscripts** and a large atelier.
**Jahangir** → **portraits**, albums, flora, fauna, **naturalism**; **Shah Jahan** → formal court scenes, **albums (muraqqas)**, floral borders.
xa: Shah Jahan's style also made **heavy use of gold**.
**Aurangzeb** withdrew patronage → **Rajput and Pahari** schools grew.

138.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Akbar's painting atelier:
1. It was known as the Tasvir Khana.
2. It had more than 100 painters.
3. It produced illustrated versions of the Hamzanama, Tutinama, Akbarnama and Razmnama.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: All three statements are correct. Akbar's Tasvir Khana was a large atelier of more than 100 painters and worked on the listed illustrated manuscripts.
138.tq: Check whether all the components of the atelier description belong to the same reign.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Statements 1 and 2: Akbar's atelier was the **Tasvir Khana**, with **100+ painters**.
Statement 3: it produced the **Hamzanama**, **Tutinama**, **Akbarnama** and **Razmnama**.
xa: Leading painters: **Daswant**, **Basawan**, **Mukand**.
**Hamzanama** = tales of **Amir Hamza**, supervised first by **Mir Sayyid Ali**, then **Abdus Samad**.

138.s: The introduction of the halo or nimbus behind the emperor's head in Mughal painting is associated with the reign of:
138.x: Jahangir's painters introduced the halo or nimbus behind the emperor's head, reflecting the period's refined and naturalistic style.
138.tq: Test a distinctive visual innovation against neighbouring emperors.
xs: The **halo (nimbus)** behind the emperor's head was introduced under **Jahangir** — option **(4)**.
Jahangir's reign was the **zenith / golden age** of Mughal painting, with **portraits** and peak **naturalism**.
xa: Jahangir's painters: **Manohar**, **Bishandas**, **Mansur**, **Abul Hasan**.
European influence also marked his reign.

138.s:
The withdrawal of imperial patronage to painters during the reign of Aurangzeb contributed to the growth of painting centres in which of the following regions?
1. Rajasthan
2. Punjab Hills
3. Bihar
4. Bengal
138.x: Painters moved to Rajasthan, the Punjab Hills and Bihar after Aurangzeb withdrew patronage. Bengal is not included in this association.
138.tq: Find the one geographically added region that does not belong to the stated dispersal pattern.
xs: Painters moved to **Rajasthan, the Punjab Hills and Bihar** (**1, 2 and 3 only**) — option **(1)**.
**Aurangzeb** **withdrew patronage**, fuelling the **Rajput and Pahari** schools.
The notes do not list **Bengal** among these destinations.
xa: **Pahari** school: Sub-Himalayan belt, **17th-19th c.**
**Aurangzeb** also ended court music.

138.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Basawan — Jahangir's specialist in flora and fauna
Ustad Mansur — Akbar's leading manuscript illustrator
138.x: Abdus Samad was a Persian master associated with Humayun and Akbar and was given the title Shirin Qalam. Ustad Mansur was associated with Jahangir and Basawan with Akbar.
138.tq: Use the title–painter association while rejecting swapped reigns and specialities.
xs: **Abdus Samad — Shirin Qalam** is correct — option **(2)**.
**Basawan** belongs to **Akbar's** reign; flora and fauna = **Ustad Mansur**.
**Ustad Mansur** was **Jahangir's** painter; **Bishandas** was Jahangir's **portrait** painter.
xa: ⚠ **Nadir-ul-Asr** = Mansur; **Nadir-uz-Zaman** = Abul Hasan; **Shirin Qalam** = Abdus Samad.
Abdus Samad served **Humayun-Akbar**.

138.s: Ustad Mansur is particularly associated with which aspect of Mughal painting?
138.x: Ustad Mansur, a painter of Jahangir's court, was renowned for depicting flora and fauna.
138.tq: Separate a painter's artistic speciality from literary and architectural activities.
xs: **Ustad Mansur** is known for **flora and fauna** — option **(1)**.
He was **Jahangir's** painter, titled **Nadir-ul-Asr**.
xa: ⚠ **Nadir-uz-Zaman** = **Abul Hasan**, Jahangir's court painter.
Jahangir's reign: peak of **naturalism** and precision.

138.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Manohar was the son of Basawan.
2. Manohar was associated with portrait painting in the Akbar–Jahangir period.
3. Basawan was one of the leading masters of Akbar's court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: All three statements are correct. Manohar, the son of Basawan, worked in the Akbar–Jahangir period and was known for portraits, while Basawan was a leading Akbar-era master.
138.tq: Link family relationship, artistic speciality and reign without confusing the two painters.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1 and 2: **Manohar**, **son of Basawan**, painted court **portraits** in the **Akbar-Jahangir** era.
Statement 3: **Basawan** was a **leading Akbar-era master**.
xa: ⚠ **Basawan** = Akbar's reign, not Jahangir's (UKPSC **2025** trap).
Jahangir's painters: **Manohar**, **Bishandas**, **Mansur**.

138.s:
Consider the following statements about Mughal painting under Jahangir:
1. Jahangir's reign is regarded as the golden period of Mughal painting.
2. Abul Hasan, Jahangir's court painter, received the title Nadir-uz-Zaman.
3. Basawan was the leading master of Jahangir's atelier.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
138.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Jahangir's reign was the zenith or golden period of Mughal painting, and Abul Hasan was titled Nadir-uz-Zaman. Statement 3 is wrong: Basawan belongs to Akbar's reign; Jahangir's painters included Manohar, Bishandas and Mansur. Option A leaves out statement 2; options C and D include the false statement 3.
138.tq: Jahangir = golden age; Abul Hasan Nadir-uz-Zaman, Mansur Nadir-ul-Asr; Basawan is Akbar's.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: Jahangir's reign = **golden period** of Mughal painting.
Statement 2: **Abul Hasan** was titled **Nadir-uz-Zaman**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Basawan** belongs to **Akbar's** reign.
xa: Jahangir's painters: **Manohar, Bishandas and Mansur** (UKPSC **2025**).
Jahangir introduced the **halo (nimbus)**.

138.s: Which one of the following features is most closely associated with Rajput painting?
o: Bold colours, flat two-dimensional treatment and Hindu themes
Muted colours, deep perspective and European naturalism
Heavy use of gold and Persian court imagery
Exclusive depiction of battles fought in the Deccan
138.x: Rajput paintings are known for bold colours, a flat two-dimensional style, and subjects such as Hindu epics, love legends and daily life.
138.tq: Separate the indigenous and vivid Rajput style from Mughal naturalism.
xs: Rajput painting = **bold colours**, **flat, 2-D** treatment, **Hindu themes** — option **(1)**.
Themes: **Hindu epics**, love legends, daily life.
Muted colour and European naturalism = **Mughal**; heavy gold = **Deccani** / Shah Jahan.
xa: Rajput painting was **indigenous, vivid, decorative**.
It grew when **Aurangzeb** withdrew patronage.

138.s:
With reference to the Pahari school of painting, consider the following statements:
1. It flourished mainly between the seventeenth and nineteenth centuries.
2. It was associated with the Sub-Himalayan region.
3. It originated in the Bahmani court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: The Pahari school flourished in the seventeenth to nineteenth centuries in the Sub-Himalayan region. Its association with the Bahmani court belongs to Deccani painting, not Pahari painting.
138.tq: Find the statement carrying the wrong school-origin association.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
The **Pahari** school belongs to the **Sub-Himalayan** belt (Himachal, Jammu, Almora, Garhwal), **17th-19th c.**
Statement 3 wrong: the **Bahmani** court origin belongs to the **Deccani** school.
xa: Pahari painting grew from painters dispersed after **Aurangzeb** withdrew patronage.
Deccani school: **heavy use of gold**.

138.s: The Deccani school of painting began in the court of the
138.x: Deccani painting began in the Bahmani court and continued in the successor states of the Bahmani kingdom.
138.tq: Identify the institutional origin of the school.
xs: Deccani painting began in the court of the **Bahmanis** — option **(3)**.
It continued in the **successor states**; at **Golconda** the founder was **Mir Hashim**.
xa: Deccani painting made **heavy use of gold**.
Qutb Shahi Deccani painting was **independent of Mughal style**.

138.s: Who is associated with the founding of the Deccani painting tradition at Golconda?
138.x: At Golconda, Mir Hashim is identified as the founder of the Deccani painting tradition; he was later invited to the Mughal court.
138.tq: Use the artist-founder association rather than the later Mughal connection.
xs: **Mir Hashim** founded the Deccani tradition at **Golconda** — option **(4)**.
He was later **invited to the Mughal court**.
xa: Deccani painting began in the **Bahmani** court.
**Sherwani** called the **14** miniatures (incl. Battle of **Rakshasi-Tangadi**) the Deccan's first coloured miniatures.

138.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes Mughal painting from Rajput painting?
o: Mughal painting was indigenous and decorative, whereas Rajput painting was cosmopolitan and naturalistic.
Rajput painting alone reflected European influence and a cosmopolitan outlook.
Mughal painting generally used muted naturalistic colours, perspective and shading, whereas Rajput painting was vivid and decorative.
Both schools used identical styles and differed only in the language of captions.
138.x: Mughal painting generally displayed muted naturalistic colours, perspective, shading and a cosmopolitan outlook, while Rajput painting was indigenous, vivid and decorative.
138.tq: Read both sides of the reversed comparison carefully.
xs: Mughal = **muted, naturalistic colour**, **perspective and shading**; Rajput = **vivid and decorative** — option **(3)**.
Mughal painting was **cosmopolitan** with **European influence**; Rajput was **indigenous** — option 1 reverses this.
xa: Rajput: **bold colours**, flat **2-D**, Hindu epics.
Pahari school: Sub-Himalayan, **17th-19th c.**

138.s: Sherwani regarded the miniatures including the Battle of Rakshasi-Tangadi as the
o: first coloured miniatures of the Deccan
138.x: Historian Sherwani called the fourteen miniatures, including the Battle of Rakshasi-Tangadi, the Deccan's first coloured miniatures.
138.tq: Link the historian's assessment with the distinctive miniature group.
xs: **Sherwani** called them the **first coloured miniatures of the Deccan** — option **(1)**.
There are **14** miniatures, including the **Battle of Rakshasi-Tangadi**.
xa: Some notes place them in the **Tarikh-i-Hussain Badshahi Deccan**; others credit a **Quli Qutb Shah** manuscript.
Deccani painting began in the **Bahmani** court.

138.s: Tansen, who became one of the Navaratnas of Akbar, was originally known as
138.x: Tansen's original name was Ramtanu Pande. He first served at the court of Raja Ramchandra of Rewa before joining Akbar's court.
138.tq: Use the exact-name distinction to reject the look-alike personal name.
xs: Tansen's original name was **Ramtanu Pande** — option **(2)**.
**Makaranda Pande** is the APPSC-G2 **2011** distractor.
xa: He was a disciple of **Swami Haridas**, first at Raja Ramchandra of **Rewa**'s court.
Title **Mian**; ragas **Mian ki Todi**, **Mian ki Malhar**, **Darbari Kanada**.

138.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Baiju Bawra — Court of Raja Man Singh Tomar
Baz Bahadur — Court musician of Akbar from the beginning of his career
138.x: Pair D is wrong: Baz Bahadur was the Sultan of Malwa (famed with Rupmati), who served Akbar only after Akbar's forces defeated him in 1561, not from the start of his career. Baiju Bawra sang at Raja Man Singh Tomar's court, and Mian ki Malhar and Darbari Kanada are Tansen's ragas.
138.tq: Find the swapped role and sequence in the incorrectly matched pair.
xs: **Baz Bahadur — court musician of Akbar from the start** is wrong — option **(4)**.
Baz Bahadur was **Sultan of Malwa**, famed with **Rupmati**; defeated by Akbar's forces (**1561**), he served Akbar **later**.
**Baiju Bawra** sang at **Raja Man Singh Tomar**'s court; **Mian ki Malhar** and **Darbari Kanada** are Tansen's.
xa: Tansen sang in the **dhrupad** style.
Tansen was one of **Akbar's Navaratnas**.

138.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Tansen:
1. He first served in the court of Raja Ramchandra of Rewa.
2. He was given the title ‘Mian’.
3. He was one of Akbar’s Navaratnas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: All three statements are correct. Tansen moved from Raja Ramchandra of Rewa's court to Akbar's court and was honoured with the title ‘Mian’.
138.tq: Test the whole biographical chain rather than relying on a single association.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Tansen first served **Raja Ramchandra of Rewa**, then became one of **Akbar's Navaratnas**.
He held the title **Mian**.
xa: Original name: **Ramtanu Pande**; from **Gwalior**, disciple of **Swami Haridas**.
**Dhrupad** style; ragas **Mian ki Todi**, **Darbari Kanada**.

138.s: Which one of the following musical forms is correctly matched with its Mughal-era patronage?
o: Tappa — Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior
138.x: Khayal flourished at the court of Muhammad Shah ‘Rangeela’, particularly through Sadarang and Adarang. Dhrupad was associated with Raja Man Singh Tomar, while Tappa was refined by Shori Miyan.
138.tq: Start from the sure form–court association and eliminate the swapped pairs.
xs: **Khayal — Muhammad Shah 'Rangeela'** is correct — option **(2)**.
It flourished there with **Sadarang** and **Adarang**.
**Dhrupad** = **Raja Man Singh Tomar**, Gwalior; **Tappa** = refined by **Shori Miyan**.
xa: Tappa was refined at Muhammad Shah's court (UPPSC **2023**).
**Tansen** and **Baiju** were masters of dhrupad.

138.s: Who among the following refined Tappa in the late eighteenth-century Awadh–Lucknow milieu?
138.x: Tappa was refined by Shori Miyan in the late eighteenth-century Awadh–Lucknow milieu.
138.tq: Distinguish the composer associated with Tappa from those associated with Khayal.
xs: **Shori Miyan** (Shori Mian) refined **Tappa** — option **(2)**.
This was in the **late 18th century** (Awadh/Lucknow milieu).
**Sadarang** and **Adarang** are linked with **Khayal**; **Baiju Bawra** with **dhrupad**.
xa: Tappa refined at **Muhammad Shah**'s court (UPPSC **2023**).
Khayal flourished at **Muhammad Shah 'Rangeela'**'s court.

138.s:
Consider the following statements about music under Aurangzeb:
1. Aurangzeb ended court music.
2. His reign witnessed the production of several Persian works on classical music.
3. Aurangzeb himself played the veena.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: All three statements are correct. Although Aurangzeb ended court music, Persian treatises on classical music were produced during his reign, and he played the veena.
138.tq: Recognise the apparent contradiction between royal policy and developments during the same reign.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Aurangzeb** ended (banned) **court music**.
Yet many **Persian works and treatises on classical music** date from his reign, and he played the **veena**.
xa: He also **withdrew patronage** from painting.
FIRST/LAST: Aurangzeb withdrew patronage from **painting and music**.

138.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the languages of the Sultanate period:
1. Persian became the language of administration, diplomacy and high culture.
2. Persian replaced Sanskrit and Arabic in these official and elite functions.
3. Hindavi developed in camps and bazaars through interaction between Perso-Arabic and indigenous linguistic elements.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: All three statements are correct. Persian acquired elite official status, while Hindavi developed through the interaction of Perso-Arabic script and indigenous grammar and vocabulary.
138.tq: Check whether each statement describes a separate stage or feature of linguistic development.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Persian** replaced **Sanskrit and Arabic** as the language of **administration, diplomacy and high culture**.
**Hindavi** (→ Urdu) grew out of **military camps and bazaars**, mixing Perso-Arabic and indigenous elements.
xa: Persian linked Delhi with **Isfahan** and **Central Asia**.
Urdu = **Perso-Arabic script** + **indigenous grammar**.

138.s:
With reference to Dakhni Urdu, consider the following statements:
1. It became a lingua franca of Deccan camps and bazaars.
2. It developed as a literary medium under the Qutb Shahis.
3. Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah is associated with the first Urdu poetic diwan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: Dakhni Urdu served as the common language of Deccan camps and bazaars, became a literary medium under the Qutb Shahis, and Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah is known for the first Urdu poetic diwan.
138.tq: Combine the language’s social role, literary role and associated poet.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Dakhni Urdu** was the **lingua franca of Deccan camps and bazaars** and a literary medium under the **Qutb Shahis**.
**Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah** = **first Urdu poet with a diwan**.
xa: **Mulla Khiali** = first Deccani poetry in Telangana.
**Abdullah Qutb Shah**'s era = **Golden Age of Urdu**.

138.s: The use of local vernaculars by Sufi saints primarily helped them to:
o: Replace all regional languages with Persian
Restrict religious teaching to court scholars
138.x: Sufi saints used local vernaculars to communicate their ideas and teachings to ordinary people.
138.tq: Infer the social purpose of a linguistic choice from its audience.
xs: Sufi saints wrote in local vernaculars to **reach common people** — option **(4)**.
**Persian** stayed the court and elite language; vernaculars carried teaching to ordinary people.
xa: **Urdu** grew out of **military camps and bazaars**.
**Dakhni Urdu** was the lingua franca of **Deccan** camps and bazaars.

138.s: Urdu developed historically through the stages represented by which sequence?
138.x: The development is described as Hindavi followed by Rekhta, Lashkari and Urdu. Urdu grew in military camps and bazaars.
138.tq: Arrange the successive names of the language in the stated historical sequence.
xs: **Hindavi → Rekhta → Lashkari → Urdu** — option **(2)**.
Urdu grew out of **military camps and bazaars**.
xa: Mix = **Persian, Arabic, Turkic**, local **Prakrits**, **Braj**.
Script: **Perso-Arabic**; grammar: **indigenous**.

138.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Urdu as characterised in the Mughal-period linguistic context?
o: It uses the Devanagari script and excludes local Prakrit influence.
It consists exclusively of Persian vocabulary and Persian grammar.
It developed only in royal courts and not in military camps or bazaars.
It uses the Perso-Arabic script and retains an indigenous grammar.
138.x: Urdu mixes Persian, Arabic, Turkic, local Prakrits and Braj, uses the Perso-Arabic script, and retains an indigenous grammar.
138.tq: Choose the precise composite description and reject exclusive claims.
xs: Urdu uses the **Perso-Arabic script** and keeps an **indigenous grammar** — option **(4)**.
It mixes **Persian, Arabic, Turkic**, local **Prakrits** and **Braj** — not purely Persian.
It grew in **military camps and bazaars**, not only courts.
xa: Stages: **Hindavi → Rekhta → Lashkari → Urdu**.
**Dakhni Urdu** flourished under the **Qutb Shahis**.

138.s: Who was the first writer of Deccani poetry in Telangana?
138.x: Mulla Khiali was the first to write Deccani poetry in Telangana.
138.tq: Identify the pioneer rather than the later court poet associated with the same tradition.
xs: **Mulla Khiali** wrote the **first Deccani poetry in Telangana** — option **(2)**.
**Ghavvasi** was a later court poet (**Tuti Nama**, **1657**); **Keshavdas** was a Hindi poet of **Orchha**; **Sadarang** a Khayal musician.
xa: **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah** = first Urdu poet with a **diwan**.
**Abdullah Qutb Shah**'s era = **Golden Age of Urdu**.

138.s: The Golden Age of Urdu is associated with the reign of
138.x: The era of Abdullah Qutb Shah is described as the Golden Age of Urdu.
138.tq: Distinguish Deccani Urdu’s regional golden age from North Indian Mughal patronage.
xs: The **Golden Age of Urdu** was the era of **Abdullah Qutb Shah** — option **(2)**.
Court poet **Ghavvasi** wrote the **Tuti Nama** (**1657**) in that era.
xa: **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah** = first Urdu poet with a diwan.
Under the Qutb Shahis, **Persian** was official and **Telugu** the people's language.

138.s: Ghavvasi, the court poet associated with Deccani Urdu, wrote
138.x: Ghavvasi wrote Tuti Nama in 1657, rendering the Sanskrit Shuka Saptati.
138.tq: Link the regional court poet to his specific work and date.
xs: **Ghavvasi** wrote the **Tuti Nama** in **1657** — option **(1)**.
It renders the Sanskrit **Shuka Saptati**.
**Sirr-i-Akbar** (**1657**) and **Majma-ul-Bahrain** are **Dara Shikoh's**; **Kavindra-kalpalata** is **Kavindracharya Saraswati's**.
xa: Ghavvasi was court poet in **Abdullah Qutb Shah**'s era (**Golden Age of Urdu**).
**Mulla Khiali** = first Deccani poetry in Telangana.

138.s: The Tuzuk-i-Baburi, also known as Baburnama, was written by Babur in which language?
138.x: Babur wrote the Tuzuk-i-Baburi in Turki. It is one of the important royal memoirs of the Mughal period.
138.tq: Test the exact language associated with a royal memoir.
