With reference to the attribution of Palnati Veera Charitra, consider the following statements:
1. It is traditionally attributed to Srinatha.
2. It is a dvipada ballad concerning the Palnadu war.
3. The APPSC 2025 key treated it as the work not written by Srinatha in a particular comparative question.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
145.x: All three statements are correct. The work is traditionally credited to Srinatha and is a dvipada account of the Palnadu war, although the cited APPSC key used it as the exception in an attribution-based question.
145.tq: Handle an attribution trap by separating traditional attribution from an examination-key treatment.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Palnati Veera Charitra** is traditionally credited to **Srinatha**; it is a heroic **dvipada ballad** of the **Palnadu war (1182)**.
⚠ The **APPSC 2025** key made it the "not written by Srinatha" answer.
xa: Most notes and **C.P. Brown**'s list credit it to Srinatha.
It mirrors the **martial culture** of the Reddi-era courts.

145.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Veerabhadra Vijayam is correct?
o: It was written by Madiki Singana at the Rajahmundry court.
It is a translation of Sriharsha's Naishadham by Srinatha.
It was Srinatha's last work composed at Srisailam.
It is regarded in the cited literary accounts as Potana's first work, written at the request of Ivaturi Somanaradhya.
145.x: Veerabhadra Vijayam is regarded by the cited accounts as Potana's first work, written at the request of his guru Ivaturi Somanaradhya, though an older APPSC key attributed it to Srinatha.
145.tq: Separate the later literary attribution from the older examination-key attribution.
xs: **Veerabhadra Vijayam** is **Potana's first work**, written for his guru **Ivaturi Somanaradhyudu** — option **(4)**.
⚠ The **APPSC 2011** key answered **Srinatha**.
Sriharsha's Naishadham was rendered in **Sringara Naishadhamu**.
xa: Potana's other works: **Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu**, **Bhogini Dandakam**, **Narayana Satakam** (lost).
Potana's title: **Sahaja Panditudu**.

145.s: Palnati Veera Charitra is associated with which event?
o: The establishment of the Gajapati kingdom
145.x: Palnati Veera Charitra is a heroic dvipada narrative of the Palnadu war, dated to 1182.
145.tq: Match the literary work with its distinctive historical event and date.
xs: **Palnati Veera Charitra** is about **the Palnadu war of 1182** — option **(1)**.
It is a heroic **dvipada ballad**, traditionally credited to **Srinatha**.
The fall of Rajahmundry (**1448**) relates to Srinatha's last years, not this ballad.
xa: **Brahmanayudu** led **Veeravaishnavism** in Palnadu.
⚠ **APPSC 2025** key treated it as not by Srinatha.

145.s: What does Palnati Veera Charitra reveal about the social and artistic life of the period?
o: It gives a complete list of Vijayanagara emperors.
It records houses painted with Rama and Krishna avatars and mentions 1,500 painters' houses at Orugallu.
It records the first printing press at Rajahmundry.
It describes only the revenue system of the Delhi Sultanate.
145.x: The text records houses decorated with Rama and Krishna avatars and refers to 1,500 painters' houses at Orugallu, making it a source for social life.
145.tq: Infer the historical value of a literary text from its concrete social details.
xs: The Palnadu source records **houses painted with Rama and Krishna avatars** and **1,500 painters' houses at Orugallu** — option **(2)**.
This makes it a source for **Palnadu social life**.
xa: The ballad deals with the **Palnadu war (1182)**.
**C.P. Brown** printed Palnati Veera Charitra.

145.s: Annamacharya composed his sankirtanas primarily in praise of:
145.x: Annamacharya composed about 32,000 sankirtanas to Lord Venkateswara.
145.tq: Use the deity association to distinguish Annamacharya from other devotional composers.
xs: Annamacharya's sankirtanas were to **Lord Venkateswara** of **Tirumala** — option **(2)**.
He composed about **32,000**; only about **12,000** survive.
**Rama** was the deity of **Ramadasu** and **Tyagaraja**; **Krishna** (Muvva Gopala) of **Kshetrayya**.
xa: Born at **Tallapaka**; dates **1408-1503**.
Contemporary ruler: **Saluva Narasimha** (APPSC-G2 **2011**).

145.s:
Consider the following statements about Annamacharya's sankirtanas:
1. He composed about 32,000 sankirtanas, of which only about 12,000 survive.
2. The surviving songs were preserved on copper plates at Tirumala.
3. C.P. Brown recovered and edited these copper-plate songs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
145.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: about 32,000 sankirtanas were composed, about 12,000 survive, preserved on copper plates at Tirumala. Statement 3 is wrong: it was Veturi Prabhakara Sastry who recovered and edited the copper-plate songs (C.P. Brown is linked with Vemana and the Bhagavatamu). So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
145.tq: 32,000 composed / 12,000 survive / copper plates at Tirumala / Veturi Prabhakara Sastry.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
About **32,000** sankirtanas, about **12,000** survive, preserved on **copper plates at Tirumala**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Veturi Prabhakara Sastry** recovered and edited them; **C.P. Brown** edited **Vemana (1829)** and printed the **Bhagavatamu (1840)**.
xa: Veturi said Annamacharya **created the science of sankirtana**.
**Annamayya district** is named after him.

145.s: Which of the following is NOT a title associated with Annamacharya?
145.x: Padakavita Pitamaha, Sankirtanacharya and Harikirtanacharya are titles of Annamacharya. Ashtabhasha Kavi Chakravarti was the title of China Tirumalacharya.
145.tq: Find the title belonging to another member of the literary family.
xs: **Ashtabhasha Kavi Chakravarti** is NOT Annamacharya's title — option **(3)**; it belongs to **China Tirumalacharya**.
Annamacharya's titles: **Padakavita Pitamaha**, **Sankirtanacharya**, **Harikirtanacharya**.
xa: China Tirumalacharya was the **eldest son of Peda Tirumalacharya**; he wrote **Sankirtana Lakshanamu**.
Praise: "**Right hand to Telugu words**" (Puttaparthi Narayanacharyulu); "**Incarnated Telugu**" (Arudra).

145.s: Annamacharya is known in Telugu literary history as the:
o: Author of the first Telugu Dandakam
Father of the Telugu keertana and pioneer of padakavita
First translator of the Ramayana into Telugu
Founder of the Sanskrit court epic tradition
145.x: Annamacharya is regarded as the father of the Telugu keertana and a pioneer of the padakavita or pada form.
145.tq: Identify the exact literary contribution rather than a related but incorrect achievement.
xs: Annamacharya is the **Father of the Telugu keertana** and **pioneer of padakavita** — option **(2)**.
The first Telugu **Dandakam** is **Potana's Bhogini Dandakam**; the first woman Ramayana translator is **Molla**.
xa: His **Sri Venkateswara Satakam** = first Telugu **Shringara Satakam**.
⚠ Sri Venkateswara Satakam is **Annamacharya's**, not Pedda Tirumalacharya's.

145.s: Which Kannada saint is stated to have met Annamacharya?
145.x: The Kannada saint Purandara Dasa is stated to have met Annamacharya.
145.tq: Discriminate among associated saints by the specific meeting relationship.
xs: Annamacharya was met by the Kannada saint **Purandara Dasa** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Basavanna** was the 12th-century founder of the **Veerashaiva** movement in Karnataka, not a contemporary of Annamacharya.
xa: Annamacharya (**1408-1503**) was born at **Tallapaka** (Annamayya district); parents **Lakkamamba** and **Narayanasuri**; guru **Ghana Vishnu**.
His contemporary ruler was **Saluva Narasimha** (APPSC-G2 2011).
He composed about **32,000 sankirtanas** to **Lord Venkateswara**; only about **12,000** survive, on **copper plates at Tirumala**.

145.s:
Consider the following statements about praise of Annamacharya:
1. Arudra described him as 'Incarnated Telugu'.
2. Veturi Prabhakara Sastry described him as 'Right hand to Telugu words'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
145.x: Statement 1 is correct: Arudra called Annamacharya 'Incarnated Telugu'. Statement 2 is wrong: 'Right hand to Telugu words' was said by Puttaparthi Narayanacharyulu; Veturi Prabhakara Sastry recovered the copper-plate songs. Hence 1 only (A).
145.tq: Arudra = Incarnated Telugu; Puttaparthi = Right hand to Telugu words.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Arudra** called Annamacharya **"Incarnated Telugu"**.
Statement 2 wrong: **"Right hand to Telugu words"** was said by **Puttaparthi Narayanacharyulu**, not Veturi Prabhakara Sastry.
xa: **Veturi Prabhakara Sastry** recovered and edited the **copper-plate songs** and said Annamacharya created the **science of sankirtana**.
Titles of Annamacharya: **Padakavita Pitamaha**, **Sankirtanacharya**, **Harikirtanacharya**; called the **Father of the Telugu keertana**.
⚠ Praise pairs: Arudra = **Incarnated Telugu**; Puttaparthi = **Right hand to Telugu words**.

145.s: Annamacharya, the composer of sankirtanas on Lord Venkateswara, was a contemporary of which ruler?
145.x: Annamacharya (1408-1503) was a contemporary of Saluva Narasimha (APPSC-G2 2011). Pedakomati Vema Reddy was Srinatha's patron, Abul Hasan Tana Shah imprisoned Bhakta Ramadasu, and Krishnadevaraya is not the ruler linked with Annamacharya.
145.tq: Annamacharya - Saluva Narasimha (APPSC-G2 2011).
xs: Annamacharya (**1408-1503**) was a contemporary of **Saluva Narasimha** (APPSC-G2 2011) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Pedakomati Vema Reddy** was **Srinatha's** patron at Kondaveedu, not Annamacharya's.
**Abul Hasan Tana Shah** imprisoned **Bhakta Ramadasu** in Golconda fort.
xa: Annamacharya was met by the Kannada saint **Purandara Dasa**.
Some notes give his dates as **1424-1508**.
**Annamayya district** is named after Annamacharya of **Tallapaka**.

145.s: Who is regarded as the founder of the Tallapaka line of poets?
145.x: Annamacharya is identified as the founder of the Tallapaka line of poets.
145.tq: Distinguish the founder of a literary lineage from its later members.
xs: **Annamacharya** (Tallapaka Annamayya) was the **founder of the Tallapaka line** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Peda Tirumalacharya** was his son; **China Tirumalacharya** and **Chinnanna** were sons of Peda Tirumalacharya.
xa: **China Tirumalacharya** (eldest son of Peda Tirumalacharya) held the title **Ashtabhasha Kavi Chakravarti**.
**Chinnanna** (Tiruvenkatanatha), the **4th son**, wrote **Annamacharya Charitra**, a biography in **Dvipada**.
Annamacharya's first wife **Timmakka** wrote **Subhadra Kalyanam** — the **first woman poet** of the Andhra region.

145.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Peda Tirumalacharya?
o: He was Annamacharya's son and wrote Vairagya Vachanamalika.
He was the fourth son of Peda Tirumalacharya and wrote Annamacharya Charitra.
He was Annamacharya's first wife and wrote Subhadra Kalyanam.
He was a contemporary Kannada saint who met Annamacharya.
145.x: Peda Tirumalacharya was Annamacharya's son. His works included Vairagya Vachanamalika, Seesa padya satakam, Sudarshana Ragada and Chakravala Manjari.
145.tq: Use family relationships to reject swapped identities within the Tallapaka lineage.
xs: **Peda Tirumalacharya** was **Annamacharya's son** and wrote **Vairagya Vachanamalika** — option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) describes **Chinnanna**, the 4th son of Peda Tirumalacharya, who wrote **Annamacharya Charitra**.
Option (3) describes **Timmakka** (Subhadra Kalyanam); option (4) describes **Purandara Dasa**.
xa: Peda Tirumalacharya's other works: **Sankirtanas**, **Seesa padya satakam**, **Sudarshana Ragada**, **Chakravala Manjari**.
⚠ **Trap:** **Sri Venkateswara Satakam** is **Annamacharya's**, not Pedda Tirumalacharya's.

145.s:
Consider the following statements about China Tirumalacharya (China Tirumalayya):
1. He held the title Ashtabhasha Kavi Chakravarti.
2. He wrote the Ashtabhasha Dandakam.
3. He was the son of Annamacharya.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
145.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: China Tirumalacharya held the title Ashtabhasha Kavi Chakravarti and wrote Ashtabhasha Dandakam (and Sankirtana Lakshanamu). Statement 3 is wrong: he was the eldest son of Peda Tirumalacharya, Annamacharya's son, i.e. Annamacharya's grandson. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
145.tq: Tallapaka line: Annamacharya -> Peda Tirumalacharya -> China Tirumalacharya (eldest) and Chinnanna (4th son).
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: China Tirumalacharya held the title **Ashtabhasha Kavi Chakravarti**.
Statement 2 correct: he wrote the **Ashtabhasha Dandakam**.
Statement 3 wrong: he was the **eldest son of Peda Tirumalacharya**, i.e. Annamacharya's grandson.
xa: He also wrote **Sankirtana Lakshanamu**.
⚠ **Trap:** Do not credit China Tirumalayya with the **first Telugu Dandakam** — that was Potana's **Bhogini Dandakam**.

145.s: Which of the following works was written by Chinnanna?
145.x: Chinnanna wrote Annamacharya Charitra, a biography of Annamacharya in the Dvipada form, along with Paramayogi Vilasam, Ashtamahishi Kalyanam and Usha Kalyanam.
145.tq: Match the later family member with his distinctive biographical work.
xs: **Chinnanna** wrote **Annamacharya Charitra**, a biography in **Dvipada** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Vairagya Vachanamalika** is **Peda Tirumalacharya's**; **Sankirtana Lakshanamu** is **China Tirumalacharya's**.
**Venkateswara Satakam** is **Annamacharya's** own work.
xa: Chinnanna (**Tiruvenkatanatha**) was the **4th son** of Peda Tirumalacharya.
His other works: **Paramayogi Vilasam**, **Ashtamahishi Kalyanam**, **Usha Kalyanam**.

145.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the first Telugu Dandakam?
o: It was written by Chinnanna in Annamacharya Charitra.
It was written by China Tirumalayya.
It was written by Peda Tirumalacharya.
145.x: The first Telugu Dandakam was Potana's Bhogini Dandakam; it should not be attributed to China Tirumalayya.
145.tq: Separate the similar-sounding Dandakam title from the wrong Tallapaka attribution.
xs: The **first independent Dandakam in Telugu** was **Potana's Bhogini Dandakam** — option **(3)** is correct.
Crediting it to **China Tirumalayya** is the classic trap; he wrote the **Ashtabhasha Dandakam**.
Chinnanna's **Annamacharya Charitra** is a **Dvipada** biography, not a Dandakam.
xa: **Bhogini Dandakam** is about **Sarvajna Singabhupala** and **Bhogini**.
Other FIRSTs: **Sri Venkateswara Satakam** (Annamacharya) = first Telugu **Shringara Satakam**; **Vrushadhipa Satakam** = first full-featured satakam.
**Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya** = originator of the **Sataka form** in Telugu.

145.s: Sri Venkateswara Satakam, regarded as the first Telugu Shringara Satakam, was written by
145.x: Sri Venkateswara Satakam is Annamacharya's work and the first Telugu Shringara Satakam. Crediting it to his son Peda Tirumalacharya is the common trap; China Tirumalacharya wrote Ashtabhasha Dandakam and Chinnanna wrote Annamacharya Charitra.
145.tq: Venkateswara Satakam = Annamacharya, not Pedda Tirumalacharya.
xs: **Sri Venkateswara Satakam**, the first Telugu Shringara Satakam, was written by **Annamacharya** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ Crediting it to his son **Peda Tirumalacharya** is the common trap.
**China Tirumalacharya** wrote Ashtabhasha Dandakam; **Chinnanna** wrote Annamacharya Charitra.
xa: Annamacharya's other Telugu works: **Sringara Manjari** (**258 dvipadas**), **Dvipada Ramayanam**, **Alivelumangamma Satakam**.
His Sanskrit works: **Sankirtana Lakshanam**, **Venkatachala Mahatyam**.

145.s: Which one of the following pairs of titles is associated with Bammera Potana?
145.x: Potana was known by the titles Sahaja Panditudu and Nigarva Chudamani.
145.tq: Use exact title-pair recognition to eliminate titles belonging to other poets.
xs: Potana's titles were **Sahaja Panditudu** and **Nigarva Chudamani** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Andhra Kavita Pitamaha** is **Allasani Peddana's** title; **Padakavita Pitamaha** is **Annamacharya's**.
**Kavibrahma** is **Tikkana's** title.
xa: Potana (c. **1450-1510**) was a native of **Bammera** (Janagama district, Telangana).
He was a contemporary of **Srinatha** (Kavi Sarvabhauma); some notes make him Srinatha's brother-in-law.
Other titles: **Nannaya** = Adikavi; **Errapragada** = Prabandha Parameswara.

145.s:
With reference to Potana’s Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu, consider the following statements:
1. It is the Telugu version of the Bhagavata Purana.
2. Potana dedicated it to Lord Rama.
3. Potana wrote all the twelve skandhas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
145.x: Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu is the Telugu Bhagavata Purana and was offered to Lord Rama. Potana wrote eight of its twelve skandhas, not all twelve.
145.tq: Find the overstatement in the claim that one author completed the entire work.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: it is the **Telugu version of the Bhagavata Purana**.
Statement 2 correct: Potana dedicated it to **Lord Rama**.
Statement 3 wrong: of **12 skandhas**, Potana wrote only **8**.
xa: Other skandhas: **Bopparaju Gangana** (5th), **Erchuri Singana** (6th), **Veligandala Narayana** (11th-12th).
**C.P. Brown** printed Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu in **1840**.
Potana vowed **never to dedicate his work to a human king**.

145.s: Which work of Potana is described as the first independent Dandakam in Telugu?
145.x: Bhogini Dandakam is regarded as the first independent Dandakam in Telugu.
145.tq: Match the superlative description with the exact literary work.
xs: **Bhogini Dandakam** is the **first independent Dandakam in Telugu** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Veerabhadra Vijayam** was Potana's **first work**, written for his guru **Ivaturi Somanaradhyudu**.
**Narayana Satakam** is lost; **Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu** is his Telugu Bhagavata Purana.
xa: Bhogini Dandakam is about **Sarvajna Singabhupala** and **Bhogini**.
⚠ **Trap:** not China Tirumalayya — the first Telugu Dandakam is Potana's.

145.s: Which one of the following works of Potana is described as lost?
145.x: Narayana Satakam is listed as a lost work of Potana.
145.tq: Test the exceptional status in a list of surviving works.
xs: **Narayana Satakam** is listed as Potana's **lost** work — option **(1)** is correct.
**Veerabhadra Vijayam**, **Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu** and **Bhogini Dandakam** all survive in the notes' list.
xa: **Veerabhadra Vijayam** = his first work; ⚠ **APPSC 2011** key gave it to **Srinatha**.
**Bhogini Dandakam** = first independent **Dandakam** in Telugu.
Of **12** skandhas of the Bhagavatamu, Potana wrote **8**.

145.s:
Potana’s refusal to dedicate his Bhagavatamu to a human king primarily reflects his:
1. Refusal to dedicate the work to Sarvajna Singabhupala.
2. Dedication of the work to Sri Rama.
3. Dependence on royal patronage as the central principle of his literary outlook.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
145.x: Potana refused to dedicate the work to Sarvajna Singabhupala and offered it to Sri Rama. This represents independence from, rather than dependence on, royal patronage.
145.tq: Reject the reversed interpretation of a poet’s refusal of royal patronage.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: he refused **Sarvajna Singabhupala** of **Rachakonda**.
Statement 2 correct: he offered the Bhagavatam to **Sri Rama**.
Statement 3 wrong: his vow shows **independence from** royal patronage, not dependence on it.
xa: Interpretation: **quiet independence from Gajapati overlordship**.
⚠ **Trap:** some notes still call him **Sarvajna Singa Bhupala's** court poet.

145.s: Potana is described as a contemporary of which poet?
145.x: Potana was a contemporary of Srinatha.
145.tq: Use the contemporary-pair relationship rather than the literary work association.
xs: Potana was a **contemporary of Srinatha** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Palkuriki Somanatha** belonged to the **Kakatiya** period; **Tyagaraja** and **Kshetrayya** were later composers.
xa: Some notes even make Potana **Srinatha's brother-in-law**.
Srinatha (**c. 1385-1475**) = **Kavi Sarvabhauma**; Potana = **Sahaja Panditya**.
**Veerabhadra Vijayam** (Potana's first work) was credited to Srinatha by the **APPSC 2011** key.

145.s: Vemana is best described as which of the following?
o: A devotional poet who composed only Sanskrit hymns
A yogi-philosopher poet who wrote satakam-style verses in colloquial Telugu
A royal historian who wrote chronicles in Persian
A court poet who composed Sanskrit epics
145.x: Vemana was a yogi-philosopher poet whose satakam-style verses were written in colloquial Telugu for common people.
145.tq: Use the precise identity and literary form to distinguish the poet from nearby medieval writers.
xs: Vemana was a **yogi-philosopher poet** who wrote **satakam-style verses in colloquial Telugu** — option **(2)** is correct.
His verses were for **common people**, not Sanskrit hymns or court epics.
xa: Themes: satire on **empty ritual**, **caste discrimination by birth**, **idol worship**, superstition and hypocrisy.
Metre: mostly **Ataveladi**; refrain **"Vishwadabhirama Vinura Vema"**.
**Dating disputed:** **17th c.** vs **14th-15th c.**

145.s: Which one of the following was NOT a major social or religious theme in Vemana's poetry?
o: Advocacy of humanism and equal treatment of castes
Criticism of caste discrimination by birth
Glorification of superstition and ritual formalism
Opposition to empty ritual and hypocrisy
145.x: Vemana criticised superstition, empty ritual, idol worship and hypocrisy; he advocated humanism, inner wisdom and equality.
145.tq: Find the option that reverses the poet's central social message.
xs: Vemana never glorified **superstition and ritual formalism** — he satirised them, so option **(3)** is the answer.
He satirised **empty ritual**, **idol worship**, **superstition** and **hypocrisy**.
He stood for **humanism**, **inner wisdom (Jnana)** and **equal treatment of all castes** — options (1), (2), (4) are genuine themes.
xa: **C.P. Brown** edited and translated his verses as **Verses of Vemana** (**1829**).
Vemana is paired with **Potuluri Veerabrahmam** as Andhra's **anti-caste voices**.

145.s:
Consider the following statements about Vemana's verses:
1. C.P. Brown collected them from manuscripts, edited them and translated them into English as 'Verses of Vemana' (1829).
2. They are mostly composed in the Dvipada metre.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
145.x: Statement 1 is correct: C.P. Brown collected, edited and translated Vemana's verses, published as Verses of Vemana in 1829. Statement 2 is wrong: Vemana mostly used the Ataveladi metre with the refrain 'Vishwadabhirama Vinura Vema'. Hence 1 only (A).
145.tq: Vemana = Ataveladi + C.P. Brown 1829.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **C.P. Brown** collected, edited and translated them as **Verses of Vemana** (**1829**).
Statement 2 wrong: Vemana mostly used the **Ataveladi** metre, not Dvipada.
xa: Refrain: **"Vishwadabhirama Vinura Vema"**.
⚠ C.P. Brown dates: Verses of Vemana **1829**; Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu **1840**.

145.s: Vemana's verses are mostly composed in which metre and commonly end with which refrain?
145.x: Vemana mainly used the Ataveladi metre, and his verses commonly conclude with the refrain “Vishwadabhirama Vinura Vema.”
145.tq: Pair the distinctive metre with its recurring refrain rather than recognising either in isolation.
xs: Vemana mostly used the **Ataveladi** metre with the refrain **"Vishwadabhirama Vinura Vema"** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Dvipada** is the metre of works like **Basava Puranam** and **Annamacharya Charitra**, not Vemana's verses.
xa: His verses are short, **satakam-style**, in **colloquial Telugu**.
**Dating disputed:** **17th c.** vs **14th-15th c.** — learn both.

145.s: Vemana is often paired with which figure as an Andhra voice against caste discrimination?
145.x: Vemana is paired with Potuluri Veerabrahmam, whose Kaalagnanam also represents an important anti-caste voice in Andhra.
145.tq: Identify the related reformist voice rather than a contemporary ruler or devotional musician.
xs: Vemana is paired with **Potuluri Veerabrahmam** (Kalagnanam) as Andhra's anti-caste voices — option **(3)** is correct.
**Saluva Narasimha** was Annamacharya's contemporary ruler; **Purandara Dasa** was the Kannada saint who met Annamacharya.
**Kumara Kampana** was **Gangadevi's** husband who conquered **Madurai**.
xa: Veerabrahmam's disciples crossed castes and faiths, e.g. **Siddaiah**, a Muslim.
Caste critique in the wider bhakti: **Alvars**, **Nayanars**, **Basava**.

145.s: The prophecies of Potuluri Veerabrahmam are contained in:
145.x: Potuluri Veerabrahmam’s prophecies are contained in Kalagnanam.
145.tq: Use the author–work association and reject works belonging to other traditions.
xs: Potuluri Veerabrahmam's prophecies are in the **Kalagnanam** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Tevaram** is the Nayanar canon; **Basava Puranam** is **Palkuriki Somanatha's**; **Dasarathi Satakam** is **Bhakta Ramadasu's**.
xa: Veerabrahmendra Swamy **strongly condemned caste differences**.
His disciple **Siddaiah** was a **Muslim**.

145.s: Which one of the following best reflects the social message of Veerabrahmendra Swamy?
o: He condemned caste differences and accepted disciples across castes and faiths.
He rejected vernacular literature in favour of Sanskrit.
He supported ritual hierarchy as the basis of social order.
He defended caste distinctions and restricted discipleship to one community.
145.x: Veerabrahmendra Swamy strongly condemned caste differences and accepted disciples from different castes and faiths, including Siddaiah, a Muslim.
145.tq: Apply the reformer’s stated social principles to a concrete description.
xs: Veerabrahmendra Swamy **condemned caste differences** and **accepted disciples across castes and faiths** — option **(1)** is correct.
His disciple **Siddaiah** was a **Muslim**, so options (3) and (4) are the opposite of his message.
xa: His prophecies are in **Kalagnanam**.
He is paired with **Vemana** as Andhra's anti-caste voices.

145.s: Kshetrayya was primarily associated with which deity?
145.x: Kshetrayya composed Shringara padams dedicated to Muvva Gopala, a form of Krishna.
145.tq: Distinguish the deity associated with each Andhra bhakti poet.
xs: Kshetrayya is associated with **Muvva Gopala** (Krishna) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Rama of Bhadrachalam** = **Bhakta Ramadasu**; **Venkateswara of Tirumala** = **Annamacharya**.
**Srikalahasteeswara Satakam** is **Dhurjati's** work.
xa: Kshetrayya was **Varadayya of Movva** (Krishna dt.).
He composed over a thousand **Movva Gopala padams** at **Abdullah Qutb Shah's** court.

145.s: Which statement regarding Kshetrayya is correct?
o: He composed over a thousand Movva Gopala padams at Abdullah Qutb Shah’s court.
He wrote the Basava Puranam in Dwipada metre at the Kakatiya court.
He composed the Pancharatna kritis at Tiruvaiyaru.
145.x: Kshetrayya composed over a thousand Movva Gopala padams and is associated with Abdullah Qutb Shah’s court.
145.tq: Use the court–composer–work combination to separate closely related bhakti figures.
xs: Kshetrayya composed **over a thousand Movva Gopala padams** at **Abdullah Qutb Shah's court** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Srikalahasteeswara Satakam** = **Dhurjati**; **Basava Puranam** = **Palkuriki Somanatha**.
**Pancharatna kritis** at **Tiruvaiyaru** = **Tyagaraja**.
xa: His padams are **Shringara padams** to **Muvva Gopala** (Krishna).
⚠ Ramadasu = Golconda prison under **Tana Shah**; Kshetrayya = **Abdullah Qutb Shah's** court.

145.s:
Consider the following statements about Bhakta Ramadasu:
1. He served as a Golconda revenue official under Tana Shah.
2. He built the Bhadrachalam temple.
3. He was jailed in connection with the construction of the temple.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
145.x: All three statements are correct. Bhakta Ramadasu (Kancharla Gopanna), a Golconda revenue official under Tana Shah, used state revenue to rebuild the Bhadrachalam Rama temple. For this, Abul Hasan Tana Shah imprisoned him in Golconda fort for 12 years.
145.tq: Verify a complete chain of office, religious construction and punishment.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: Ramadasu was a **Golconda revenue official under Tana Shah**.
Statement 2: he used revenue to rebuild the **Bhadrachalam Rama temple**.
Statement 3: **Abul Hasan Tana Shah** jailed him for **12 years** in **Golconda fort**.
xa: Bhakta Ramadasu = **Kancharla Gopanna**, born **1620** at **Nelakondapalli** (Khammam).
Guru **Raghunatha Bhattacharya**; nephew of **Akkanna and Madanna**.
He wrote **Dasarathi Satakam** in prison.

145.s: Tyagaraja’s compositions are predominantly devoted to:
145.x: Tyagaraja composed Telugu kritis predominantly in devotion to Rama.
145.tq: Separate the principal deity of Tyagaraja from those of other Telugu bhakti poets.
xs: Tyagaraja's compositions are devoted to **Rama** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Krishna** (Muvva Gopala) = **Kshetrayya**; **Venkateswara** = **Annamacharya**.
xa: He composed **Telugu kritis** and the **Pancharatna kritis** at **Tiruvaiyaru**.
He is one of the **Carnatic Trinity** with **Dikshitar** and **Syama Sastri**.

145.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the members of the Carnatic Trinity other than Tyagaraja?
145.x: The Carnatic Trinity consists of Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri.
145.tq: Complete a well-defined triad by identifying the two associated names.
xs: The Carnatic Trinity is Tyagaraja with **Dikshitar** and **Syama Sastri** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Dhurjati** wrote Srikalahasteeswara Satakam; **Kshetrayya** and **Ramadasu** are Andhra bhakti composers, not the Trinity.
xa: Tyagaraja's deity was **Rama**; he composed at **Tiruvaiyaru**.
Telugu bhakti forms (padams, keertanas) became the base of **Carnatic music's Telugu repertoire**.

145.s: Dhurjati is associated with which work?
145.x: Dhurjati wrote Srikalahasteeswara Satakam, regarded as a foremost Shaiva satakam.
145.tq: Distinguish similarly named satakams by their author and deity.
xs: Dhurjati wrote the **Srikalahasteeswara Satakam**, the foremost **Shaiva satakam** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Venkateshwara Satakam** = **Annamacharya**; **Narayana Satakam** = **Potana** (lost); **Vrushadhipa Satakam** = **Palkuriki Somanatha**.
xa: **Vrushadhipa Satakam** = first Telugu satakam with all satakam features.
**Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya** = originator of the **Sataka form** in Telugu.

145.s: Bhakta Ramadasu is the popular name of:
145.x: Bhakta Ramadasu was Kancherla Gopanna, a prominent devotee and composer associated with Bhadrachalam.
145.tq: Test the popular name–historical name pair directly.
xs: Bhakta Ramadasu was **Kancherla Gopanna** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Potuluri Veerabrahmam** wrote the Kalagnanam; **Palkuriki Somanatha** wrote Basava Puranam; **Brahmanayudu** led **Veeravaishnavism** in Palnadu.
xa: Born **1620** at **Nelakondapalli** (Khammam); deity **Rama**.
Rebuilt the **Bhadrachalam Rama temple**; jailed **12 years** in **Golconda fort** by **Abul Hasan Tana Shah**.

145.s: For how many years was Bhakta Ramadasu imprisoned in Golconda Fort by Abul Hasan Tana Shah?
145.x: Bhakta Ramadasu was imprisoned for 12 years in Golconda Fort by Abul Hasan Tana Shah.
145.tq: Test the exact duration with nearby numerical distractors.
xs: Ramadasu was imprisoned for **12 years** in **Golconda fort** by **Abul Hasan Tana Shah** — option **(2)** is correct.
He had used revenue to rebuild the **Bhadrachalam Rama temple**.
xa: In prison he wrote the **Dasarathi Satakam**.
**Dr. Bhanumathi Ramakrishna** translated it into English (APPSC-G2 2001).
⚠ Ramadasu = **Tana Shah**; Kshetrayya = **Abdullah Qutb Shah's** court.

145.s: Which of the following works is associated with Bhakta Ramadasu?
145.x: Dasarathi Satakam, written in prison, and the Ramadasu kirtanas are associated with Bhakta Ramadasu.
145.tq: Match the devotional author with his literary work.
xs: **Dasarathi Satakam**, written in prison, is Bhakta Ramadasu's — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kalagnanam** = **Potuluri Veerabrahmam**; **Nalayira Divya Prabandham** = **Alvars**; **Molla Ramayanam** = **Molla**.
xa: He also composed the **Ramadasu kirtanas / keertanas**.
English translation of Dasarathi Satakam: **Dr. Bhanumathi Ramakrishna** (APPSC-G2 2001).

145.s: Bhakta Ramadasu's Dasarathi Satakam was translated into English by
145.x: Dr. Bhanumathi Ramakrishna translated Dasarathi Satakam into English (APPSC-G2 2001). C.P. Brown translated Vemana's verses, Veturi Prabhakara Sastry recovered Annamacharya's copper-plate songs, and Arudra called Annamacharya 'Incarnated Telugu'.
145.tq: Dasarathi Satakam (English) = Bhanumathi Ramakrishna (APPSC-G2 2001).
xs: **Dr. Bhanumathi Ramakrishna** translated the Dasarathi Satakam into English (APPSC-G2 2001) — option **(3)** is correct.
**C.P. Brown** translated **Vemana's** verses (**1829**).
**Veturi Prabhakara Sastry** recovered Annamacharya's **copper-plate songs**; **Arudra** called Annamacharya **"Incarnated Telugu"**.
xa: Ramadasu wrote the Dasarathi Satakam **in prison** in **Golconda fort**.
Ramadasu = **Kancharla Gopanna**, nephew of **Akkanna and Madanna**.

145.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
145.x: Timmakka, the wife of Annamacharya, wrote Subhadra Kalyanam in Telugu.
145.tq: Start from the sure poet–work pair and reject swapped literary associations.
xs: **Timmakka — Subhadra Kalyanam** is correctly matched — option **(3)** is correct.
**Tirumalamba** wrote **Varadambika Parinayam**; **Raghunathabhyudayam** is **Ramabhadramba's**.
**Gangadevi** wrote **Madhura Vijayam**, not Varadambika Parinayam.
xa: **Timmakka** (Tirumalamma) was **Annamacharya's first wife** and the **first woman poet** of the Andhra region.
**Subhadra Kalyanam** (Subhadra Parinayam) is a **Dvipada kavya**.

145.s: Varadambika Parinayam deals with the marriage of:
145.x: Tirumalamba's Sanskrit work describes the marriage of Achyutaraya to Varadambika.
145.tq: Distinguish the subject of a work from its author and language.
xs: **Varadambika Parinayam** deals with the marriage of **Achyuta Deva Raya and Varadambika** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Kumara Kampana** was **Gangadevi's** husband (Madhura Vijayam); **Timmakka** was **Annamacharya's** wife.
xa: It was written by **Oduva Tirumalamba** as a **Sanskrit court epic**.
**Ramabhadramba** wrote **Raghunathabhyudayam** (Sanskrit).

145.s: Which of the following statements regarding Tallapaka Timmakka is correct?
o: She was the wife of Kumara Kampana and wrote Madhura Vijayam.
She was an eighteenth-century devotee of Venkateswara from Tirumala.
She was the daughter of Achyuta Deva Raya and wrote Varadambika Parinayam.
She was Annamacharya's first wife and is regarded as the first woman poet of the Andhra region.
145.x: Tallapaka Timmakka, also called Tirumalamma, was Annamacharya's first wife and is regarded as the first woman poet of the Andhra region.
145.tq: Use the relation and distinction between women poets to avoid author–work substitution.
xs: **Timmakka** was **Annamacharya's first wife** and the **first woman poet of the Andhra region** — option **(4)** is correct.
Option (1) describes **Gangadevi**; option (2) describes **Tarigonda Vengamamba**; option (3) mixes up **Oduva Tirumalamba's** work.
xa: Timmakka's work: **Subhadra Kalyanam** (Subhadra Parinayam), a **Dvipada kavya**.
⚠ **Molla** was the first Telugu woman poet to **translate the Ramayana**.

145.s: Madhura Vijayam, also known as Veera Kamparaya Charitam, describes:
o: The conquest of Madurai by Kumara Kampana
The marriage of Achyuta Deva Raya and Varadambika
The legends of Rama in Telugu
The life of Venkateswara at Tirumala
145.x: Gangadevi's Sanskrit work Madhura Vijayam describes her husband Kumara Kampana's conquest of Madurai.
145.tq: Link the literary work to its historical subject rather than merely its author.
xs: **Madhura Vijayam** describes the **conquest of Madurai by Kumara Kampana** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was written in **Sanskrit** by **Gangadevi**, a **Sangama princess**, about her husband.
The marriage of Achyuta Deva Raya is **Varadambika Parinayam** (Oduva Tirumalamba).
xa: ⚠ PYQ (APPSC-G2 2023 and 2025): wrong match = **Gangadevi — Marichi Parinayam**.
**Molla Ramayanam** gives Rama's story in simple, elegant **Telugu**.

145.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Gangadevi — Madhura Vijayam
2. Oduva Tirumalamba — Varadambika Parinayam
3. Tarigonda Vengamamba — Venkatachala Mahatyamu
4. Molla — Molla Ramayanam
145.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. These works represent important contributions of Telugu and Sanskrit women poets.
145.tq: Verify each author–work pair before accepting the all-inclusive code.
xs: All four pairs are correctly matched — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Gangadevi — Madhura Vijayam** (Sanskrit); **Oduva Tirumalamba — Varadambika Parinayam**.
**Tarigonda Vengamamba — Venkatachala Mahatyamu**; **Molla — Molla Ramayanam**.
xa: **Vengamamba** was an **18th-century** poet-devotee of Venkateswara, **Tirumala**.
**Molla** (Atukuri Molla), of the **potter community**, was the first Telugu woman poet to translate the **Ramayana**.

145.s: Which one of the following pairs of woman poet and work is NOT correctly matched?
145.x: Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam (Veera Kamparaya Charitam) in Sanskrit, so 'Gangadevi — Marichi Parinayam' is the wrong match (APPSC-G2 2023 and 2025). Molla wrote Molla Ramayanam, Timmakka wrote Subhadra Kalyanam and Vengamamba wrote Venkatachala Mahatyamu.
145.tq: Gangadevi = Madhura Vijayam; 'Marichi Parinayam' is the wrong match.
xs: **Gangadevi — Marichi Parinayam** is the wrong match (APPSC-G2 2023 and 2025) — option **(2)** is the answer.
Gangadevi wrote **Madhura Vijayam** (Veera Kamparaya Charitam) in **Sanskrit**.
**Molla — Molla Ramayanam**, **Timmakka — Subhadra Kalyanam**, **Vengamamba — Venkatachala Mahatyamu** are all correct.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** the **2025** answer key marked **Molla-Ramayanam** instead, but the explanation confirms Molla-Ramayanam is correct.
**Gangadevi** was a **Sangama princess**; husband **Kumara Kampana**.

145.s: Which of the following languages replaced Sanskrit as vehicles for the spread of Bhakti among common people?
145.x: Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam became important vernacular vehicles that carried Bhakti ideas to common people instead of relying exclusively on Sanskrit.
145.tq: Recall the complete language list rather than selecting a partially correct combination.
xs: **Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam** replaced Sanskrit as Bhakti's vehicles — option **(3)** is correct.
Options with **Persian**, **Arabic**, **Sanskrit**, **Pali** or **Prakrit** are not the vernaculars the notes list.
xa: **Satakam** and **dwipada** forms spread bhakti to common people.
The Alvars and Nayanars sang **Tamil hymns**; Basava's movement spread through Kannada **Vachanas**.

145.s: Which literary forms helped spread Bhakti ideas among common people in Andhra?
145.x: The satakam and dwipada forms helped communicate Bhakti ideas to common people in Telugu-speaking regions.
145.tq: Identify the regional literary forms associated with popular religious communication.
xs: The **Satakam and dwipada** forms spread bhakti to common people — option **(2)** is correct.
**Vachanas** are Kannada prose-poems and **Tevaram** is the Tamil Shaiva canon — not Andhra's forms.
xa: **Desi kavita**: simple native metres (**dwipada, ragada, manjari, kanda**) vs the Sanskritised **Marga** style.
**Palkuriki Somanatha** wrote **Basava Puranam** in simple Telugu **Dwipada** metre.

145.s:
Consider the following statements about the social impact of the Bhakti traditions:
1. Alvars, Nayanars and Basava criticised caste distinctions.
2. Vemana and Potuluri Veerabrahmam expressed caste critique in Andhra.
3. Some saints promoted the practice of feeding people of all castes together.
4. Bhakti traditions uniformly upheld Brahmanical dominance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
145.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because these traditions challenged caste and Brahmanical dominance rather than uniformly upholding it.
145.tq: Find the one sweeping reversal among otherwise reform-oriented statements.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
Statements 1 and 2: caste critique came from **Alvars, Nayanars, Basava**, and in Andhra **Vemana** and **Potuluri Veerabrahmam**.
Statement 3: some saints **fed all castes together**.
Statement 4 wrong: bhakti **challenged caste and Brahmanical dominance**.
xa: **Women saints**: **Andal**, **Karaikkal Ammaiyar**, **Akka Mahadevi**, **Atukuri Molla**.
Spread factors: **Chola patronage** and the **"little-great tradition"** fusion (Jagannath at Puri).

145.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Tirumala — Annamacharya and the Tallapaka family
145.x: Tirumala is associated with Annamacharya and the Tallapaka family. Bhadrachalam is associated with Ramadasu, Muvva with Kshetrayya, and Srikurmam with Narahari Tirtha.
145.tq: Start from the temple–saint pair that is most firmly associated and eliminate shifted pairings.
xs: **Tirumala — Annamacharya and the Tallapaka family** is correctly matched — option **(1)** is correct.
**Bhadrachalam = Ramadasu**, not Kshetrayya; **Muvva = Kshetrayya**, not Tyagaraja.
**Srikurmam = Narahari Tirtha**, who spread **Dvaita**.
xa: **Tiruvaiyaru** = **Tyagaraja**.
**Tarigonda Vengamamba** is also linked with **Tirumala**.

145.s: Tarigonda Vengamamba is associated with which sacred place?
145.x: Tarigonda Vengamamba is included among the saints associated with Tirumala and the Venkateswara tradition.
145.tq: Test the less prominent name in a temple–saint association list.
xs: **Tarigonda Vengamamba** is associated with **Tirumala** (Venkateswara) — option **(4)** is correct.
**Bhadrachalam** = **Ramadasu**; **Srikurmam** = **Narahari Tirtha**.
xa: She was an **18th-century** poet-devotee who wrote **Venkatachala Mahatyamu**.
**Annamacharya and the Tallapaka family** are also linked with Tirumala.

145.s: Narahari Tirtha, associated with Srikurmam, is remembered for spreading:
145.x: Narahari Tirtha is associated with Srikurmam and spread the Dvaita tradition.
145.tq: Distinguish the philosophical affiliation from the nearby Shaiva traditions.
xs: **Narahari Tirtha** at **Srikurmam** spread **Dvaita** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Dvaita** (dualism) was **Madhvacharya's** philosophy; **Advaita** was **Shankaracharya's**.
**Aradhya Saivism** was founded by **Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya**; **Virashaivism** by **Basavanna**.
xa: Andhra's contributions: **Dvaita at Srikurmam**, Aradhya Saivism, Tallapaka sankirtana, Bhadrachalam, Kshetrayya's padams.
**Ramanuja** (**1017-1137**) = **Vishishtadvaita**.

145.s: Which of the following correctly matches Telugu poets with their titles?
o: Nannaya — Adikavi; Tikkana — Kavibrahma; Errapragada — Prabandha Parameswara
Nannaya — Kavi Sarvabhauma; Tikkana — Andhra Kavita Pitamaha; Errapragada — Sahaja Panditya
Potana — Adikavi; Srinatha — Kavibrahma; Allasani Peddana — Prabandha Parameswara
Nannaya — Sahaja Panditya; Tikkana — Kavi Sarvabhauma; Potana — Andhra Kavita Pitamaha
145.x: Nannaya was Adikavi, Tikkana was Kavibrahma and Errapragada was Prabandha Parameswara. The other titles include those of Potana, Srinatha and Allasani Peddana in incorrect combinations.
145.tq: Begin with the distinctive title–poet pairs and check every remaining pair.
xs: **Nannaya — Adikavi; Tikkana — Kavibrahma; Errapragada — Prabandha Parameswara** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Kavi Sarvabhauma** = **Srinatha**; **Andhra Kavita Pitamaha** = **Allasani Peddana**; **Sahaja Panditya** = **Potana**.
xa: **Annamacharya** = **Padakavita Pitamaha**.
**China Tirumalacharya** = **Ashtabhasha Kavi Chakravarti**.

145.s: The poets associated with the Bhakti tradition in Telugu contributed to Carnatic music chiefly through:
o: Only Persian ghazals and court chronicles
Padams, keertanas, satakas and dvipada compositions
Only Sanskrit inscriptions and copper plates
145.x: Telugu Bhakti poets carried devotional expression through padams, keertanas, satakas and dvipada compositions, helping establish the Telugu base of the Carnatic music repertoire.
145.tq: Identify the common cultural contribution across different literary forms.
xs: Telugu Bhakti was carried through **padams, keertanas, satakas and dvipada** compositions — option **(3)** is correct.
These became the **base of Carnatic music's Telugu repertoire**; Persian ghazals, military ballads and Sanskrit inscriptions are not the channel.
xa: **Annamacharya** = **Father of the Telugu keertana**; about **32,000 sankirtanas** to **Lord Venkateswara**.
**Kshetrayya** composed over a thousand **Movva Gopala padams** at **Abdullah Qutb Shah's** court.
**Tyagaraja** composed Telugu kritis and the **Pancharatna kritis** at **Tiruvaiyaru**; Carnatic Trinity with **Dikshitar** and **Syama Sastri**.
**Bhakta Ramadasu** composed the **Ramadasu kirtanas** and **Dasarathi Satakam**.

145.s: The district named after Annamacharya is:
145.x: Annamayya district is named after Annamacharya of Tallapaka.
145.tq: Use the place-name derivation to identify the poet commemorated in the district name.
xs: **Annamayya district** is named after **Annamacharya of Tallapaka** — option **(4)** is correct.
There is no Kshetrayya, Srinatha or Tallapaka district in the notes; **Tallapaka** is his birthplace, in Annamayya district.
xa: Annamacharya (**1408-1503**) was a contemporary of **Saluva Narasimha** (APPSC-G2 2011).
His songs are preserved on **copper plates at Tirumala**; **Veturi Prabhakara Sastry** recovered and edited them.
Titles: **Padakavita Pitamaha**, **Sankirtanacharya**, **Harikirtanacharya**.

145.s: Which of the following statements regarding firsts in Telugu literature is correct?
o: Timmakka was the first Telugu woman poet, and Bhogini Dandakam was the first Telugu Dandakam.
Timmakka was the first Telugu woman poet, and Sri Venkateswara Satakam was the first Telugu Dandakam.
Bhogini Dandakam was the first Telugu Shringara Satakam.
Sri Venkateswara Satakam was the first Telugu woman poet's work.
145.x: Timmakka is identified as the first Telugu woman poet, while Bhogini Dandakam is identified as the first Telugu Dandakam. Sri Venkateswara Satakam is associated with the first Telugu Shringara Satakam.
145.tq: Keep separate literary ‘firsts’ distinct instead of transferring the label between forms.
xs: **Timmakka** was the **first Telugu woman poet** and **Bhogini Dandakam** the **first Telugu Dandakam** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Sri Venkateswara Satakam** (Annamacharya) is the first Telugu **Shringara Satakam**, not a Dandakam — so options (2), (3), (4) mix up the firsts.
xa: **Bhogini Dandakam** is **Potana's**; ⚠ do not credit **China Tirumalayya** with the first Dandakam.
**Molla** = first Telugu woman poet to **translate the Ramayana**.
**Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya** = originator of the **Sataka form**; **Vrushadhipa Satakam** = first full-featured satakam.
**Srinatha** = first reference to **paper** as writing material in Andhra (**15th century**, APPSC 2012).

145.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with an Andhra religious or devotional tradition?
145.x: Kshetrayya is associated with padams, not with the Dvaita tradition at Srikurmam. The listed Andhra associations include Dvaita at Srikurmam, Aradhya Saivism, Tallapaka sankirtana and Bhadrachalam through Ramadasu.
145.tq: Find the mismatched religious tradition rather than merely recognising familiar names.
xs: **Kshetrayya — Dvaita philosophy** is the wrong pair — option **(3)** is the answer.
Kshetrayya is known for **padams** to **Muvva Gopala**; Dvaita was spread at **Srikurmam** by **Narahari Tirtha**.
**Srikurmam — Dvaita**, **Tallapaka — Sankirtana** and **Andhra — Aradhya Saivism** are all correct.
xa: Andhra's contributions: Dvaita at **Srikurmam**, **Aradhya Saivism**, **Tallapaka sankirtana**, **Bhadrachalam (Ramadasu)**, **Kshetrayya's padams**.
**Aradhya Saivism** was founded by **Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya**; it kept Vedic learning and varna while preaching Shiva bhakti.
**Dvaita** (dualism) is the philosophy of **Madhvacharya**.

145.s:
Which social ideals are highlighted as important features of the Bhakti tradition described here?
1. Assertion of women's spiritual authority
2. Dignity of labour through the idea of Kayaka
3. Rejection of all forms of devotional poetry
Which of the statements given above are correct?
145.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Bhakti tradition asserted women's spiritual authority and the dignity of labour through Kayaka; it did not reject devotional poetry.
145.tq: Identify the two positive social ideals and reject the reversed negative statement.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: bhakti asserted **women's spiritual authority** centuries before modern reform.
Statement 2 correct: it asserted the **dignity of labour** through **Kayaka** (honest labour).
Statement 3 wrong: bhakti spread through **devotional poetry** — padams, keertanas, satakas, dvipada.
xa: ⚠ **Kayaka** = labour; **Dasoha** = sharing surplus.
**Women saints**: **Andal**, **Karaikkal Ammaiyar**, **Akka Mahadevi**, **Atukuri Molla**.
Virashaivas **supported widow remarriage** and condemned **child marriage**.

146.s:
Consider the following statements about Sufism:
1. The ulema stood for legalistic orthodoxy and the Shariat, whereas the Sufis stressed inner experience over ritual.
2. The Sufis rejected the Quran and the Prophet in favour of yogic teachings.
3. Sufism absorbed ideas from Vedanta, Yoga and Neo-Platonism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
146.x: Statement 1 is correct: the ulema were legalistic, the Sufis valued inner experience. Statement 2 is wrong: Sufis accepted the Quran and the Prophet. Statement 3 is correct: Sufism absorbed Vedanta, Yoga and Neo-Platonism. So '1 and 3 only'; every other option includes the false statement 2 or leaves out 1 or 3.
146.tq: Sufis absorbed outside ideas but never gave up the Quran and the Prophet.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Ulema** = legalistic orthodoxy + the **Shariat**; **Sufis** = **inner experience over ritual**.
Statement 2 wrong: Sufis **accepted the Quran and the Prophet**.
Statement 3 correct: Sufism absorbed **Vedanta**, **Yoga** and **Neo-Platonism**.
xa: Sufis freely used **music**, which orthodox Islam did not generally sanction.
**Ba-shara** orders followed Sharia; **Be-shara** ones (wandering **Qalandars**, Madaris) were not bound by it.
Origin of 'Sufi': **Suf** (coarse wool), **Safa** (purity) or Greek **Sophia**.

146.s:
The word ‘Sufi’ has been associated with which of the following origins?
1. Suf, meaning coarse wool
2. Safa, meaning purity
3. Greek Sophia
Which of the statements given above are correct?
146.x: The term Sufi has been explained through Suf, Safa and the Greek word Sophia. All three proposed origins are mentioned in this context.
146.tq: Treat each proposed etymology as an independent statement.
xs: All three origins are given — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
'Sufi' is traced to **Suf** (coarse wool), **Safa** (purity) or Greek **Sophia**.
xa: First prominent Sufi in India: **Ali Hujwiri (Data Ganj Bakhsh)**, author of **Kashf-ul-Mahjub**.
Most popular order in India: **Chishti**.
Sufis accepted the **Quran and the Prophet** but absorbed **Vedanta, Yoga, Neo-Platonism**.

146.s: Who is considered the first prominent Sufi in India?
146.x: Ali Hujwiri is considered the first prominent Sufi in India. Moinuddin Chishti later founded the Chishti order in India at Ajmer.
146.tq: Distinguish the first prominent Sufi from the founder of a particular Sufi order in India.
xs: **Ali Hujwiri** (Data Ganj Bakhsh) was the **first prominent Sufi in India** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Moinuddin Chishti** came later as the Chishti founder in India, settling at **Ajmer**.
**Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehlavi** was the **last great Chishti of Delhi**; **Nizamuddin Auliya** was Baba Farid's disciple.
xa: Ali Hujwiri wrote **Kashf-ul-Mahjub**; its themes are love and knowledge of God and **fana**.
⚠ FIRST = **Ali Hujwiri**; LAST great Chishti of Delhi = **Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehlavi**.

146.s: Who wrote the Sufi text ‘Kashf-ul-Mahjub’?
146.x: ‘Kashf-ul-Mahjub’ was written by Ali Hujwiri, also known as Data Ganj Bakhsh.
146.tq: Direct author–work recall.
xs: **Kashf-ul-Mahjub** was written by **Ali Hujwiri** (Data Ganj Bakhsh) — option **(4)** is correct.
**Mir Khwurd Kirmani** wrote **Siyar-ul-Auliya** (a tazkira); **Abdul Haqq Muhaddis Dehlavi** wrote **Akhbar-ul-Akhyar**.
xa: Its themes: **love and knowledge of God** and **fana**.
**Maktubat-i-Imam Rabbani** = letters of **Ahmad Sirhindi**; **Radd-i-Khawafiq** = his anti-Shia tract.
⚠ **malfuzat** = conversations; **maktubat** = letters; **tazkiras** = biographies.

146.s: A khanqah in the Sufi tradition was primarily a place that
o: served as a hospice where disciples lived and trained, while also providing food and shelter to the poor
was a military camp maintained by Sufi rulers
functioned exclusively as a court for settling criminal disputes
served only as a shrine over a saint’s tomb
146.x: A khanqah was a Sufi hospice for the residence and training of disciples, and it also provided food and shelter to the poor.
146.tq: Identify the institution from its combined training and charitable functions.
xs: A **khanqah** was a **Sufi hospice** where disciples lived and trained, also giving **food and shelter to the poor** — option **(1)** is correct.
A shrine at a saint's tomb is a **Dargah**, not a khanqah.
xa: At **Golconda**, khanqahs served as **higher-education centres**.
Khanqahs served as **welfare centres**, giving Islam in India a tolerant face.
**Nizamuddin Auliya's** hospice drew both **common people and nobles**.

146.s: Sama in Sufi practice refers to
o: the spiritual path leading through the maqamat
devotional music intended to produce ecstasy
the death anniversary of a saint
146.x: Sama means devotional music intended to produce spiritual ecstasy. Raqs refers to the ritual dance associated with it.
146.tq: Distinguish closely related Sufi technical terms by their precise meanings.
xs: **Sama** is **devotional music meant to produce ecstasy** — option **(2)** is correct.
The spiritual path is **Tariqa**; repetition of God's name is **Zikr**; a saint's death anniversary is **Urs**.
xa: **Raqs** = ritual dance; **'Majlis-i-Sama'** of **Chishtis and Suhrawardis**.
⚠ **Chishtis encouraged** sama and qawwali; **Naqshbandis opposed** sama.
**Amir Khusrau** introduced **Qaul**, the opening hymn of Qawwali.

146.s: The bond between a spiritual master and his disciple in Sufism is known as
146.x: The pir–murid relationship is called Piri-Muridi. The pir or murshid is the spiritual master and the murid is the disciple.
146.tq: Test the exact term for a relationship rather than for an individual role.
xs: The pir-murid bond (preceptorship) is called **Piri-Muridi** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Wahdat-ush-Shuhud** is Sirhindi's doctrine; **Fana-Baqa** is annihilation / subsistence in God; **Ba-shara** means following the Shariat.
xa: **Pir / Murshid** = spiritual master or guide.
**Murid** = disciple pledged in **absolute submission** to the pir.

146.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Urs — Saint’s death anniversary viewed as union with God
Wali — Friend of God or saint
Dargah — Shrine at a saint’s tomb
Tariqa — Legalistic orthodoxy of the ulema
146.x: Tariqa means a spiritual path and also an order. The ulema represented legalistic orthodoxy and the Shariat; tariqa is not their legalistic doctrine.
146.tq: Locate the definition that belongs to a different religious category.
xs: **Tariqa — legalistic orthodoxy of the ulema** is wrong — option **(4)** is the answer.
**Tariqa** means the **spiritual path through stages**, and also an **order** (Silsila).
**Urs**, **Wali** and **Dargah** are matched correctly.
xa: The **ulema** stood for **legalistic orthodoxy and the Shariat**.
**Chilla** = solitude or retreat; **Zikr** = continuous remembrance of God's name.

146.s: Fana and Baqa respectively signify
o: remembrance of God and ritual dance
annihilation of the self in God and subsistence in God
146.x: Fana denotes annihilation of the self or ego in God, while Baqa denotes subsistence in God.
146.tq: Test the paired terms together to prevent reversal of their meanings.
xs: **Fana** = **annihilation of the self in God**; **Baqa** = **subsistence in God** — option **(4)** is correct.
Remembrance of God = **Zikr**; ritual dance = **Raqs**; guide and disciple = **Pir and Murid**.
xa: **Kashf-ul-Mahjub** of Ali Hujwiri treats **fana** as a theme.
The **10 maqamat** run from **Tauba** (repentance) to **Riza** (submission).

146.s: The terms Ba-shara and Be-shara refer respectively to Sufis who
o: belong to the Chishti and Suhrawardi orders
accept state patronage and reject state patronage
follow the Shariat and remain outside it
146.x: Ba-shara Sufis follow the Shariat, whereas Be-shara Sufis remain outside it; qalandars are given as an example of the latter.
146.tq: Separate paired terms by the presence or absence of adherence to the Shariat.
xs: **Ba-shara** Sufis **follow the Shariat**; **Be-shara** Sufis **remain outside it** — option **(4)** is correct.
Ba-shara orders: **Chishti, Suhrawardi, Qadiri, Naqshbandi, Firdausi**.
xa: Be-shara: wandering **Qalandars** and **Madaris**.
Both types **coexisted in India**.

146.s: The ‘Majlis-i-Sama’ was associated with which two Sufi orders?
146.x: Majlis-i-Sama was associated with the Chishti and Suhrawardi orders, both of which accepted sama in the form specified.
146.tq: Identify the two orders linked with the named devotional assembly.
xs: **'Majlis-i-Sama'** belonged to the **Chishtis and Suhrawardis** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **Naqshbandis opposed sama**, so options with them are wrong.
xa: Chishtis **encouraged** sama and **qawwali**; Suhrawardis adopted **sama and raqs**.
**Raqs** = ritual dance accompanying sama.

146.s: Which one of the following practices is NOT listed among the general practices of Sufis?
146.x: Zikr, meditation, fasting, asceticism, sama and solitude or chilla were Sufi practices. Compulsory military service was not one of them.
146.tq: Find the unrelated activity among the recognised spiritual practices.
xs: **Compulsory military service** is not a Sufi practice — option **(2)** is the answer.
Listed practices: **zikr**, **meditation**, fasting, asceticism, **sama**, and **chilla** (solitude or retreat).
xa: The Hatha-yogic text **Amritakund** was translated into Arabic and Persian in the **13th c.**
After it, **breath control** became vital in almost every order **except the Naqshbandis**.

146.s: The Hatha-yogic text Amritakund was translated into Arabic and Persian during which century?
146.x: Amritakund was translated into Arabic and Persian in the 13th century, after which breath control became important in almost every Sufi order except the Naqshbandis.
146.tq: Use the century as the decisive numerical clue.
xs: **Amritakund** was translated into Arabic and Persian in the **13th century** — option **(1)** is correct.
Afterwards **breath control** became vital in almost every order **except the Naqshbandis**.
xa: Sufis met the **Kanphata (Nath) yogis** of **Gorakhnath's** tradition.
**Alberuni** noted similarities with **Patanjali's Yoga Sutra** and the **Gita**.

146.s:
With reference to breath control in Sufi practice, consider the following statements:
1. It became vital in almost every order after the translation of Amritakund.
2. The Naqshbandis were the principal exception.
3. It was derived exclusively from orthodox Islamic legal practice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
146.x: Breath control became important in almost every order after the translation of Amritakund, with the Naqshbandis as the exception. Its association here is with yogic borrowing, not exclusively with Islamic legal practice.
146.tq: Reject the extreme word ‘exclusively’ and identify the stated exception.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: breath control became vital in almost every order after **Amritakund** was translated.
Statement 2: the **Naqshbandis** were the exception.
Statement 3 wrong: it came from a **Hatha-yogic** text, a yogic borrowing, not Islamic legal practice.
xa: Amritakund was translated into **Arabic and Persian** in the **13th c.**
**Shattaris** were liberal and **absorbed yogic practices**.

146.s: The Kanphata yogis whom Sufis encountered belonged to the tradition associated with
146.x: The Kanphata yogis belonged to the Nath tradition associated with Gorakhnath. Sufis interacted with these yogis and adopted or discussed certain yogic ideas.
146.tq: Identify the founder-associated tradition from the community name.
xs: The **Kanphata (Nath) yogis** belonged to the tradition of **Gorakhnath** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Ibn Arabi** is linked to **Wahdat-ul-Wujud**; **Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki** was a Chishti saint of Delhi.
xa: **Alberuni** linked Sufi ideas with **Patanjali's Yoga Sutra** and the **Gita**.
**Amritakund**, a Hatha-yogic text, entered Sufi practice in the **13th c.**

146.s:
Alberuni noted similarities between Sufi ideas and which of the following?
1. Patanjali’s Yoga Sutra
2. The Gita
3. The Arthashastra
Which of the statements given above are correct?
146.x: Alberuni noted similarities between Sufi ideas and Patanjali’s Yoga Sutra and the Gita. The Arthashastra is not included in this comparison.
146.tq: Separate the two stated comparative texts from the unrelated distractor.
xs: Alberuni noted similarities with **Patanjali's Yoga Sutra** and the **Gita** — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
The **Arthashastra** is not part of that comparison.
xa: Sufis also met the **Kanphata (Nath) yogis** of **Gorakhnath**.
Sufism absorbed **Vedanta**, **Yoga** and **Neo-Platonism**.

146.s: In the Sufi scheme of ten stages (maqamat), the first and the last stages are respectively
146.x: The ten maqamat begin with Tauba (repentance) and end with Riza (submission), passing through Wara, Zuhd, Faqr, Sabr, Shukr, Khauf, Raja and Tawakkul. Zuhd, Faqr, Sabr and Shukr are intermediate stages, and 'Riza and Tauba' reverses the order.
146.tq: Maqamat: Tauba first, Riza last.
xs: The maqamat begin with **Tauba** (repentance) and end with **Riza** (submission) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Zuhd, Faqr, Sabr, Shukr** are intermediate stages; option (4) reverses the order.
xa: The **10 stages**: Tauba → **Wara, Zuhd, Faqr, Sabr, Shukr, Khauf, Raja, Tawakkul** → Riza.
**Tariqa** = spiritual path through stages.

146.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Wahdat-ul-Wujud — Unity of Being; Haq and Khalq are one
Wahdat-ush-Shuhud — Creator and creation are identical
Wahdat-ush-Shuhud — Doctrine associated with Ibn Arabi
146.x: Wahdat-ul-Wujud means Unity of Being and identifies Haq, the Creator, with Khalq, creation. Wahdat-ush-Shuhud means Unity of Appearance or Witness and holds that creation reflects God rather than being identical with Him.
146.tq: Distinguish the two doctrines by comparing identity with reflection.
xs: **Wahdat-ul-Wujud** = **"Unity of Being"**: **Haq** (Creator) and **Khalq** (creation) are one — option **(1)** is correct.
**Wahdat-ush-Shuhud** = **"Unity of Appearance/Witness"**: creation **only reflects God** — so options (2) and (3) swap the meanings.
Wahdat-ush-Shuhud belongs to **Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi**, not **Ibn Arabi**.
xa: ⚠ **Wujud** = Being (Ibn Arabi, **Qadiri**, **Chishti**); **Shuhud** = Appearance (Sirhindi, **Naqshbandi**).
Sirhindi, the **Naqshbandi** saint, framed Wahdat-ush-Shuhud as his **counter-doctrine**.

146.s: Wahdat-ush-Shuhud, the counter-doctrine to Wahdat-ul-Wujud, was associated with
146.x: Wahdat-ush-Shuhud, or Unity of Appearance/Witness, was associated with Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi of the Naqshbandi order.
146.tq: Use the doctrine–thinker association to distinguish the two competing formulations.
xs: **Wahdat-ush-Shuhud** was the counter-doctrine of **Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi** (Naqshbandi) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Ibn Arabi** is linked to **Wahdat-ul-Wujud**; **Bahauddin Zakariya** was Suhrawardi; **Shah Raju Qattal** was a Chishti at Golconda.
xa: Sirhindi = **Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**; criticised Akbar's **Sulh-i-Kul**; **imprisoned by Jahangir**.
His letters: **Maktubat-i-Imam Rabbani**.

146.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Wahdat-ul-Wujud was associated with Ibn Arabi.
2. Qadiris and Chishtis followed Wahdat-ul-Wujud.
3. Wahdat-ush-Shuhud was associated with Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi of the Naqshbandi order.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
146.x: All three statements are correct. Wahdat-ul-Wujud was associated with Ibn Arabi and followed by Qadiris and Chishtis, while Sirhindi represented the Naqshbandi-associated Wahdat-ush-Shuhud.
146.tq: Verify the doctrine, associated thinker and associated orders as separate components.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Wahdat-ul-Wujud** is associated with **Ibn Arabi** and followed by the **Qadiris and Chishtis**.
**Wahdat-ush-Shuhud** belongs to **Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi** (Naqshbandi).
xa: Wujud = **Unity of Being** (Haq and Khalq are one); Shuhud = **Unity of Appearance/Witness**.
The **Qadiri** order **backed Wahdat-ul-Wujud**.

146.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of saints belonging to the Chishti Silsila?
o: Miyan Mir, Muhibullah Shah, Dara Shikoh and Burhanuddin Gharib
Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehlavi, Burhanuddin Gharib, Gesudaraz and Hamiduddin of Nagaur
Khwaja Baqi Billah, Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi, Shah Waliullah and Hamiduddin Nagori
Bahauddin Zakariya, Ruknuddin Abul Fath, Jalaluddin Tabrizi and Gesudaraz
146.x: Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehlavi, Burhanuddin Gharib, Gesudaraz and the Chishti Hamiduddin of Nagaur are all associated with the Chishti order.
146.tq: Use group identification to separate closely related saints belonging to different Sufi orders.
xs: **Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehlavi, Burhanuddin Gharib, Gesudaraz and Hamiduddin of Nagaur** are all Chishtis — option **(2)** is correct.
**Miyan Mir, Muhibullah Shah, Dara Shikoh** = **Qadiri**; **Baqi Billah, Sirhindi, Shah Waliullah** = **Naqshbandi**.
**Bahauddin Zakariya, Ruknuddin Abul Fath, Jalaluddin Tabrizi** = **Suhrawardi**.
xa: ⚠ **APPSC-G1 2018:** **Gesudaraz** = the Chishti in the list.
Other Chishtis: **Moinuddin**, **Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki**, **Baba Farid**, **Nizamuddin Auliya**.

146.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Bahauddin Zakariya — Suhrawardi
2. Ruknuddin Abul Fath — Suhrawardi
3. Qazi Hamiduddin Nagori — Suhrawardi
4. Jalaluddin Tabrizi — Suhrawardi

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
146.x: All four persons listed—Bahauddin Zakariya, Ruknuddin Abul Fath, Qazi Hamiduddin Nagori and Jalaluddin Tabrizi—belonged to the Suhrawardi Silsila.
146.tq: Check whether all members of a named Silsila have been correctly grouped before selecting the complete combination.
xs: All four are Suhrawardis — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Bahauddin Zakariya**, **Ruknuddin Abul Fath**, **Qazi Hamiduddin Nagori** and **Jalaluddin Tabrizi** belong to the **Suhrawardi** silsila.
xa: Founder: **Shihabuddin Suhrawardi** (Baghdad); centre **Sindh, Multan, Punjab** (khanqah at Multan).
⚠ The other Hamiduddin of Nagaur was a **Chishti**, disciple of Moinuddin.

146.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Sufi order)
A. Qadiri
B. Qadiri
C. Naqshbandi
D. Naqshbandi

List-II (Saint)
1. Shah Abdul Aziz
2. Dara Shikoh
3. Miyan Mir
4. Shah Waliullah

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
146.x: Miyan Mir and Dara Shikoh belonged to the Qadiri order, while Shah Abdul Aziz and Shah Waliullah belonged to the Naqshbandi order.
146.tq: Separate the two paired orders first, then match the saints within each order.
xs: **A-3, B-2, C-4, D-1** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Qadiri**: **Miyan Mir** and **Dara Shikoh**; **Naqshbandi**: **Shah Waliullah** and **Shah Abdul Aziz**.
xa: Qadiri founder: **Abdul Qadir Jilani** (Baghdad); also **Muhibullah Shah**.
Naqshbandi in India: **Khwaja Baqi Billah**, **Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi**.

146.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Muhammad Ghaus of Gwalior — Shattari order
146.x: Abdul Qadir Jilani founded the Qadiri order; he was not a Chishti saint. Shah Abdullah Shattari, Muhammad Ghaus and Sharafuddin Yahya Maneri are correctly associated with the orders shown.
146.tq: The wrong-founder trap distinguishes Abdul Qadir Jilani from the Chishti order.
xs: **Abdul Qadir Jilani — Chishti** is wrong — option **(1)** is the answer; he **founded the Qadiri order** (RPSC 2016).
**Shah Abdullah Shattari** founded the **Shattari** order; **Muhammad Ghaus of Gwalior** was Shattari.
**Sharafuddin Yahya Maneri** belongs to the **Firdausi** order of **Bihar**.
xa: Chishti founder at Chisht (Herat): **Khwaja Abu Ishaq Shami**; in India **Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti**.
**Mahdawi** order = **Syed Muhammad of Jaunpur**.

146.s:
With reference to the two Hamiduddins associated with medieval Sufism, consider the following statements:
1. Hamiduddin of Nagaur, a disciple of Moinuddin Chishti, belonged to the Chishti order.
2. Qazi Hamiduddin Nagori belonged to the Suhrawardi order.
3. Both Hamiduddins belonged to the same Sufi order.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
146.x: The Chishti Hamiduddin of Nagaur was a disciple of Moinuddin Chishti, whereas Qazi Hamiduddin Nagori was a Suhrawardi. Therefore, they did not belong to the same order.
146.tq: Discriminate between two persons with similar names by checking their Silsila affiliation.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(4) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Hamiduddin of Nagaur** was **Moinuddin's disciple**, a **Chishti**.
Statement 2: **Qazi Hamiduddin Nagori** was a **Suhrawardi**.
Statement 3 wrong: they belonged to **different orders**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes list "Hamiduddin Nagori" under the Suhrawardis — keep the two apart.
Moinuddin Chishti (**1143-1235**) has his dargah at **Ajmer**.

146.s:
Which of the following statements correctly describes the spread of the Chishti order in India?

1. Its important centres included Ajmer and Delhi.
2. It later spread to the Deccan, including Gulbarga and Bijapur.
3. Its growth was aided by adaptation to local traditions and vernacular languages.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
146.x: The Chishti order developed around Ajmer and Delhi, later reached Deccan centres such as Gulbarga and Bijapur, and gained popularity by adapting to local traditions and vernacular languages.
146.tq: The complete option is appropriate when all three geographical and cultural features are correct.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Centres: **Delhi-Ajmer**; later the **Deccan** (**Gulbarga**, **Bijapur**).
It grew by **adapting to local traditions and vernacular languages**.
xa: Founder in India came with **Muhammad Ghori in 1192** and settled at **Ajmer**.
**Burhanuddin Gharib** took the order to the Deccan at **Khuldabad** (**14th c.**).
Chishti adaptation made Sufism the **bridge for Indo-Islamic composite culture**.

146.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Qadiri order:
1. It was founded by Abdul Qadir Jilani.
2. It reached India in the fourteenth century according to the stated chronological account.
3. Miyan Mir and Dara Shikoh were associated with it.
4. It was centred mainly in Bihar.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
146.x: Abdul Qadir Jilani founded the Qadiri order; it reached India in the fourteenth century in the stated account, and Miyan Mir and Dara Shikoh were Qadiri figures. Bihar was associated with the Firdausi order, not the Qadiri order.
146.tq: Reject the geographically misplaced statement while retaining the founder, date and saint associations.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: founded by **Abdul Qadir Jilani** (Baghdad).
Statement 2: reached India in the **14th century** (many books say 15th).
Statement 3: **Miyan Mir** and **Dara Shikoh** were Qadiris; statement 4 wrong — **Bihar** is the **Firdausi** centre.
xa: The Qadiris **backed Wahdat-ul-Wujud**.
⚠ "Sind and Lahore" and "Sheikh Nizamat-ullah" belong to the **Qadiri** spread in Sindh-Punjab, not the Firdausi.

146.s: The Mahdawi order is associated with:
146.x: The Mahdawi order was associated with Syed Muhammad of Jaunpur. The other persons named belonged to or represented different Sufi traditions.
146.tq: Distinguish the Mahdawi order from the better-known Chishti, Suhrawardi and Shattari Silsilas.
xs: The **Mahdawi** order is associated with **Syed Muhammad of Jaunpur** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Shah Abdullah Shattari** founded the **Shattari** order; **Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri** = **Firdausi**; **Bahauddin Zakariya** = **Suhrawardi**.
xa: **Shattari** centres: **Mandu** and **Gwalior**.
Shattari saint **Muhammad Ghaus of Gwalior** was **Tansen's guru**.

146.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Sufi order — Founder or Indian introducer
o: Qadiri — Khwaja Baqi Billah in India
Firdausi — Abdul Qadir Jilani in India
146.x: Bahauddin Zakariya was the Indian introducer of the Suhrawardi order. Baqi Billah introduced the Naqshbandi order in India, Moinuddin Chishti the Chishti order, and Abdul Qadir Jilani founded the Qadiri order.
146.tq: Apply the founder-versus-Indian-introducer distinction to avoid swapped-person traps.
xs: **Suhrawardi — Bahauddin Zakariya** in India is correct — option **(3)**.
**Baqi Billah** brought the **Naqshbandi** order; **Moinuddin Chishti** brought the **Chishti** order.
**Abdul Qadir Jilani** founded the **Qadiri** order; the **Firdausi** saint is **Sharafuddin Yahya Maneri**.
xa: Suhrawardi founder: **Shihabuddin Suhrawardi** (Baghdad).
Bahauddin Zakariya backed **Iltutmish against Qabacha** and got the title **Shaikh-ul-Islam**.

146.s: Regarding the Naqshbandi order, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Bahauddin Zakariya established its main khanqah at Multan.
Bahauddin Naqshband himself established the order in India during Akbar's reign.
Moinuddin Chishti brought the order to India with Muhammad Ghori.
Khwaja Baqi Billah brought the order to India in the late sixteenth century.
146.x: Bahauddin Naqshband was the Central Asian founder and was revered by Babur, but he did not come to India. Khwaja Baqi Billah brought the Naqshbandi order to India in the late sixteenth century.
146.tq: Separate the original founder outside India from the person who introduced the order in India.
xs: **Khwaja Baqi Billah** brought the Naqshbandi order to India in the **late 16th c.** — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ **Bahauddin Naqshband** founded it in Central Asia but **never came to India**.
**Bahauddin Zakariya** (Multan) was **Suhrawardi**; **Moinuddin Chishti** came with **Muhammad Ghori** as the **Chishti** founder.
xa: The order was revered by **Babur**.
Indian Naqshbandis: **Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi**, **Shah Waliullah**, **Shah Abdul Aziz**.

146.s: Which one of the following Sufi orders was centred in Bihar and is described as a branch of the Kubrawiya order?
146.x: The Firdausi order was centred in Bihar and is described as a branch of the Kubrawiya order. Its important saint was Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri.
146.tq: Use the centre and parent-order clues together to identify the correct Silsila.
xs: The **Firdausi** order was centred in **Bihar** and is also given as a branch of the **Kubrawiya** order — option **(2)** is correct.
Its key saint: **Sharafuddin Yahya Maneri**.
xa: It is also described as a **branch of the Suhrawardis**; it was **Ba-shara**.
⚠ BPSC 2024: Firdausi = **founded in Bihar** — not "Sind and Lahore".

146.s:
Consider the following statements about the major Sufi orders:
1. The Chishtis generally kept aloof from the court and were liberal in outlook.
2. The Suhrawardis accepted royal service, wealth and patronage.
3. The Naqshbandis were strictly orthodox and opposed Akbar's Sulh-i-Kul.
4. The Shattaris absorbed certain yogic practices.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
146.x: All four statements correctly describe the characteristic stances of the Chishti, Suhrawardi, Naqshbandi and Shattari orders respectively.
146.tq: Compare the orders by their attitude to political authority, orthodoxy and local religious practices.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Chishti** = liberal, aloof from court; **Suhrawardi** = accepted royal service, wealth, patronage.
**Naqshbandi** = strictly orthodox, opposed Akbar's **Sulh-i-Kul**; **Shattari** = liberal, **absorbed yogic practices**.
xa: ⚠ Chishti (aloof, sama) vs Suhrawardi (close to court) = **most-asked contrast**; Naqshbandi = the **orthodox pole**.
Naqshbandis also opposed **Shia influence**.

146.s:
Which of the following statements about the Naqshbandi order is correct?

1. It originated with Bahauddin Naqshband in Central Asia.
2. It was revered by Babur.
3. In India, it was associated with Khwaja Baqi Billah and Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi.
4. It supported Akbar's Sulh-i-Kul.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
146.x: The first three statements are correct. The Naqshbandis were strictly orthodox and opposed Akbar's Sulh-i-Kul, so statement 4 is false.
146.tq: Find the reversed ideological comparison: opposition to Sulh-i-Kul is a Naqshbandi feature.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
Founded by **Baha-ud-din Naqshband** in **Central Asia**; revered by **Babur**.
In India: **Khwaja Baqi Billah** and **Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi**.
Statement 4 wrong: it **opposed** Akbar's **Sulh-i-Kul**.
xa: Naqshbandis were the **most orthodox** (JPSC 2016); **opposed sama** and visits to saints' tombs.
Sirhindi was **imprisoned by Jahangir**.

146.s: Muhammad Ghaus of Gwalior, described as Tansen's guide, belonged to which Sufi order?
146.x: Muhammad Ghaus of Gwalior belonged to the Shattari order and is identified as Tansen's guide.
146.tq: Use the distinctive cultural association with Tansen to identify the correct Silsila.
xs: **Muhammad Ghaus of Gwalior**, **Tansen's guru**, belonged to the **Shattari** order — option **(2)** is correct.
Shattari founder: **Shah Abdullah Shattari** (**15th c.**); centres **Mandu, Gwalior**.
xa: Shattaris were **liberal** and **absorbed yogic practices**.
**Salim Chishti**, Akbar's saint, has his dargah at **Fatehpur Sikri**.

146.s: Which of the following is NOT a Ba-shara Sufi order?
146.x: The Qalandars were wandering Be-shara groups. Chishti, Suhrawardi and Qadiri were Ba-shara orders.
146.tq: Find the odd category in a listed group.
xs: The **Qalandar** groups were wandering **Be-shara** Sufis, not bound by Sharia — option **(4)** is the answer.
**Chishti, Qadiri, Suhrawardi** (and Naqshbandi, Firdausi) were **Ba-shara**, following Sharia.
xa: **Madaris** were also Be-shara.
