151.x: Job Charnock settled at Sutanuti in 1690; the three zamindaris were bought in 1698, and Fort William was built in 1700.
151.tq: Check the sequence of settlement, acquisition of zamindaris and fort construction.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Job Charnock** settled at **Sutanuti in 1690**.
The zamindari of **Sutanuti, Gobindapur and Kalikata** was bought in **1698**.
**Fort William** was built at Calcutta in **1700**.
xa: **Madras:** Fort St. George, **1639**, by **Francis Day**.
**Farrukhsiyar's farman (1717):** duty-free trade in Bengal.
**Hooghly** was earlier a Portuguese settlement, expelled by **Shah Jahan (1632)**.

151.s: The rival English companies were merged in 1707 into the
o: United Company of the East Indies
151.x: In 1707, the rival English companies merged into the United Company of Merchants.
151.tq: Recall the exact official name rather than a descriptive substitute.
xs: In **1707** the rival English companies merged into the **United Company of Merchants** — option **(2)**.
The merged company continued the EIC's trade under the **1600** charter's monopoly, later made perpetual.
xa: EIC charter: **31 Dec 1600**, **Elizabeth I**; **15-year** monopoly, later perpetual.
Monopoly zone: between the **Cape of Good Hope** and the **Magellan Straits**.
First voyage **1602** (**James Lancaster**, Bantam).

151.s: With reference to Thomas Best, which one of the following is correct?
o: He represented the Danish Company at the court of Shah Jahan.
He defeated the Portuguese at Swally and obtained the Surat farman in 1613.
He was refused permission for trade under Portuguese pressure in 1608.
He secured the right to establish factories throughout the Mughal Empire in 1615.
151.x: Thomas Best defeated the Portuguese at Swally in 1612, and the English obtained the Surat farman in 1613.
151.tq: Separate closely associated English envoys by their specific achievement.
xs: **Thomas Best** beat the **Portuguese at Swally (1612)** and secured the **Surat farman (1613)** — option **(2)**.
Revocation under Portuguese pressure (1608) relates to **William Hawkins**; factories across the empire (**1615**) to **Sir Thomas Roe**.
Best was English, at **Jahangir's** court — not Danish or at Shah Jahan's.
xa: **Swally** was near **Surat**; the English won.
English vs Portuguese again at **Jask / Ormuz** (**1620 / 1622**) — Ormuz taken for the Shah of Persia.
**Roe** got factories at **Agra, Ahmedabad, Broach** but no treaty.

151.s: The farman issued by Farrukhsiyar in 1717 is associated with which concession to the English East India Company?
o: Transfer of Bombay at nominal rent
Permission to build a fort at Bhatkal
151.x: Farrukhsiyar’s farman of 1717 granted the English East India Company the privilege of duty-free trade in Bengal.
151.tq: Link the ruler and year with the precise commercial concession.
xs: **Farrukhsiyar's farman (1717)** gave **duty-free trade in Bengal** — option **(4)**.
**Bombay** at nominal rent came from the Crown in **1668**; **Bhatkal** was a Portuguese fort; Hooghly was Portuguese, expelled by Shah Jahan.
xa: **Golden Farman ('Bangaru Farmana'):** **1636** (many books say **1632**), from **Abdullah Qutb Shah** of Golconda.
**Surat farman 1613** followed Best's victory at Swally.
**Sir Thomas Roe (1615):** right to set up factories across the empire.

151.s:
Arrange the following English visitors to the Mughal court in chronological order of their association with the court:
A. Sir Thomas Roe
B. Ralph Fitch
C. William Hawkins
D. Edward Terry
151.x: Ralph Fitch visited Akbar in the 1580s, William Hawkins was at Jahangir’s court from 1608 to 1611, Sir Thomas Roe arrived in 1615, and Edward Terry accompanied Roe as chaplain.
151.tq: Arrange visitors by the dates of their Mughal-court association.
xs: Order: **Ralph Fitch** (Akbar, 1580s), **William Hawkins** (**1608-09**), **Sir Thomas Roe** (**1615**), **Edward Terry** — **B, C, A, D**, option **(1)**.
**Edward Terry** was **Roe's chaplain**, so he comes with/after Roe.
xa: **Thomas Best** came in **1612** and won at **Swally**.
Hawkins was envoy of **James I**; title "**English Khan**".
Roe got factories at **Agra, Ahmedabad, Broach** — but **no treaty**.

151.s: William Hawkins visited the court of Jahangir as the envoy of:
151.x: William Hawkins came to Jahangir’s court during 1608–11 as the envoy of James I. He was given the title ‘English Khan’.
151.tq: Link an envoy to the monarch who sent him.
xs: **William Hawkins** came as the envoy of **James I** — option **(1)** is correct.
He came to **Surat** and reached **Jahangir's** court in **1608-09**; he was in India **1608-11**.
xa: First English trade mission; title "**English Khan**".
Permission for Surat revoked under **Portuguese pressure**; he left in **Nov 1611**.
**Sir Thomas Roe (1615)** was also an envoy of **James I**.

151.s: Which one of the following statements regarding William Hawkins is correct?
o: He negotiated a permanent treaty with Jahangir and established the Presidency of Calcutta.
He led the English victory at Swally in 1612.
He served as the chaplain of Sir Thomas Roe.
His permission for Surat trade was revoked under Portuguese pressure.
151.x: Hawkins obtained permission for Surat trade, but it was revoked under Portuguese pressure; he left in November 1611. Edward Terry, not Hawkins, was Roe’s chaplain, and Thomas Best led the Swally victory.
151.tq: Reject options that transfer the deeds of nearby historical figures.
xs: Hawkins's **Surat trade permission was revoked under Portuguese pressure** — option **(4)**.
**Thomas Best** led the victory at **Swally (1612)**; **Edward Terry** was Roe's chaplain.
Hawkins made no treaty; even **Roe** got **no treaty**.
xa: Hawkins was envoy of **James I** to **Jahangir** (**1608-09**); left **Nov 1611**.
Title "**English Khan**".
**Surat farman 1613** came after Best's win.

151.s: Sir Thomas Roe’s mission to Jahangir in 1615 resulted in:
o: The defeat of the Portuguese at Swally
The establishment of the first English factory at Machilipatnam
A formal treaty and the transfer of Bombay to the Company
Factories at Agra, Ahmedabad and Broach, though no treaty was concluded
151.x: Sir Thomas Roe concluded no treaty with Jahangir, but factories were established at Agra, Ahmedabad and Broach during his mission.
151.tq: Distinguish the actual result of a diplomatic mission from military and territorial events.
xs: **Roe's** mission (**1615**) won factories at **Agra, Ahmedabad and Broach**, but **no treaty** — option **(4)**.
He was envoy of **James I** and got the **right to set up factories** across the empire.
**Swally** was **Thomas Best's** victory (**1612**); **Bombay** came via dowry (**1661**) to the EIC (**1668**).
xa: The **Dutch**, not the English, had the first factory at **Masulipatnam (1605)**.
Edward Terry was **Roe's chaplain**.
Order of envoys: Fitch → Hawkins → Best → Roe.

151.s: The Battle of Swally, fought near Surat in 1612, was fought between the
151.x: At Swally in 1612, the English under Thomas Best defeated the Portuguese near Surat.
151.tq: Match the battle with its two European participants.
xs: Swally (**1612**) was fought between the **English** and the **Portuguese** — option **(4)**.
The English under **Thomas Best** won near **Surat**, leading to the **Surat farman 1613**.
xa: **Jask / Ormuz (1620 / 1622):** English beat the Portuguese again.
**Colachel (1741):** **Travancore** beat the **Dutch**.
**Wandiwash (1760):** English (**Eyre Coote**) beat French (**Lally**).

151.s: The Battle of Jask/Ormuz is correctly associated with which of the following?
o: English victory over the Portuguese in 1620/1622
English victory over the Dutch at Chinsura in 1759
French victory over the English at Wandiwash in 1760
151.x: The English fought the Portuguese at Jask in 1620 and Ormuz in 1622 and emerged victorious; Ormuz was taken for the Shah of Persia.
151.tq: Use the battle–year–participants combination to reject swapped European powers.
xs: **Jask / Ormuz (1620 / 1622)** was an **English victory over the Portuguese** — option **(1)**.
**Ormuz** was taken for the **Shah of Persia**.
**Colachel (1741)** was a **Travancore** win over the Dutch; **Wandiwash (1760)** an **English** win over the French.
xa: **Swally (1612):** English (**Thomas Best**) beat the Portuguese.
Albuquerque had earlier taken **Hormuz** for the Portuguese.
Portuguese naval monopoly ended by the **Dutch and English**.

151.s: Who led the Travancore side in the Battle of Colachel against the Dutch in 1741?
151.x: Travancore, under Marthanda Varma, defeated the Dutch at Colachel in 1741.
151.tq: Avoid the ruler–commander swap by linking the regional ruler with the battle.
xs: **Marthanda Varma** led **Travancore** against the **Dutch** at **Colachel (1741)** — option **(1)**.
**Eyre Coote** (English) and **Lally** (French) fought at **Wandiwash (1760)**.
xa: Dutch headquarters: **Pulicat (1610)**, later **Nagapatnam**.
Dutch **VOC 1602** had sovereign powers to make war.
**Swally (1612):** English vs Portuguese.

151.s: The Danish settlements of Serampore and Tranquebar were sold to the British in
151.x: The Danes sold Serampore and Tranquebar to the British in 1845.
151.tq: Use the date-range elimination method for a late colonial transaction.
xs: The Danes sold **Serampore and Tranquebar** to the British in **1845** — option **(3)**.
**1739** is the Maratha capture of Salsette and Bassein; **1760** is Wandiwash.
xa: Danish company formed **1616**; Tranquebar (**1620**); **Serampore (1755)**.
Portuguese: **first to come, last to leave** — **1961**.
Danes came fourth in arrival, before the French.

151.s: The Battle of Wandiwash (1760) was fought between:
o: The English under Eyre Coote and the French under Lally
The English under Thomas Best and the Portuguese
Travancore under Marthanda Varma and the Dutch
The English under Francis Forde and the Dutch
151.x: Wandiwash (1760): English (Eyre Coote) defeated French (Lally). Thomas Best vs Portuguese was Swally 1612; Marthanda Varma vs Dutch was Colachel 1741; Forde vs Dutch was Bedara 1759.
151.tq: Wandiwash 1760 = Coote beats Lally.
xs: **Wandiwash (1760):** English under **Eyre Coote** beat the French under **Lally** — option **(1)**.
**Thomas Best vs Portuguese** was **Swally (1612)**; **Marthanda Varma vs Dutch** was **Colachel (1741)**.
xa: French company: **1664**, state-controlled; HQ **Pondicherry**.
French first factory: **Surat 1668**.
**Yanam** was one of the **4 French enclaves**.

151.s: According to the APPSC examination key, the first European factory in Andhra was established by the:
151.x: The APPSC key identifies the Portuguese as the founders of the first European factory in Andhra at Machilipatnam. Other accounts identify a Dutch factory at Masulipatnam in 1605, so the examination convention must be noted.
151.tq: Distinguish the APPSC key from an alternative account concerning the first Andhra factory.
xs: The APPSC key names the **Portuguese at Machilipatnam** as the first European factory in Andhra — option **(3)**.
This was the **APPSC G2 2019** key.
⚠ Some notes say the **Dutch** set up the first factory (Masulipatnam **1605**) and the Portuguese came last (**1670**) — **follow the key** in APPSC.
xa: **Masulipatnam:** busiest Coromandel port, **textiles**; later English and French too.
**Pulicat:** Portuguese, captured by the Dutch (HQ **1610**).
Portuguese influence faded by the mid-**17**th century (religious intolerance alienated Golconda).

151.s: Which one of the following statements regarding European settlements in Andhra is correct?
o: Nizampatnam was exclusively a Portuguese settlement.
Bheemunipatnam was a Dutch settlement in North Coastal Andhra.
Yanam was a Danish settlement on the Coromandel coast.
Pulicat was established as the French headquarters in Andhra.
151.x: Bheemunipatnam was a Dutch settlement in North Coastal Andhra. Yanam was French, while Nizampatnam and Pulicat were associated with more than one European power.
151.tq: Use the place–company association and reject one-company simplifications.
xs: **Bheemunipatnam** was a **Dutch** settlement in **North Coastal Andhra** — option **(2)**.
**Nizampatnam** was Dutch, then English (**1611**) — not Portuguese only.
**Yanam** was **French**, not Danish; **Pulicat** was the **Dutch** headquarters, not French.
xa: **Masulipatnam:** Portuguese first (APPSC key), Dutch factory **1605**, later English and French.
**Yanam:** one of the **4 French enclaves**.
AP angle also includes the **Golden Farman** and **Kalamkari** export trade.

151.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the sequence of European control at Nizampatnam?
151.x: Nizampatnam was first associated with the Dutch and later with the English, who were present there by 1611.
151.tq: Test the sequence of control rather than merely identifying one company.
xs: **Nizampatnam** was **Dutch, then English** (**1611**) — option **(4)**.
It was a **textile port**.
xa: **Bheemunipatnam:** Dutch, North Coastal Andhra.
**Pulicat:** Portuguese → Dutch HQ (**1610**); pepper and cloth.
**Masulipatnam:** Dutch factory **1605**; busiest Coromandel port.

151.s: Pulicat was important in the European trade network because it was
o: the English capital of the Madras Presidency
the French headquarters and a centre for indigo
a Portuguese settlement captured by the Dutch and later their headquarters
the Danish headquarters after the acquisition of Serampore
151.x: Pulicat was initially Portuguese, was captured by the Dutch and became the Dutch headquarters in 1610; pepper and cloth were important commodities there.
151.tq: Combine the place, change of control, headquarters and commodities clues.
xs: **Pulicat** was a **Portuguese** settlement captured by the **Dutch**, who made it their **headquarters (1610)** — option **(3)**.
It traded in **pepper and cloth**.
The French headquarters was **Pondicherry**; Danish bases were Tranquebar and **Serampore**.
xa: Dutch HQ later moved to **Nagapatnam**.
Dutch first factory: **Masulipatnam 1605**.
**Madras** (Fort St. George, **1639**) was the English base.

151.s: The Golden Farman of 1636 granting English trade concessions was issued by
151.x: Abdullah Qutb Shah of Golconda issued the Golden Farman in 1636, granting trade concessions to the English.
151.tq: Use the ruler–grant association and distinguish Golconda from neighbouring Deccan powers.
xs: The **Golden Farman (1636)** was issued by **Abdullah Qutb Shah of Golconda** — option **(4)**.
The **Raja of Chandragiri** gave Francis Day the **Madras** site; the **Bijapur** Sultan lost Goa (**1510**).
xa: Telugu name: **'Bangaru Farmana'**; many books date it **1632**.
**Farrukhsiyar's farman (1717):** duty-free trade in Bengal.
Portuguese religious intolerance alienated **Golconda**.

151.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
151.x: The Portuguese were called Budata Keechu by local people. Bangaru Farmana was the Golden Farman, and Pulicat became the Dutch headquarters.
151.tq: Test the local name and distinguish it from the grant and headquarters terms.
xs: **Portuguese — 'Budata Keechu'** is correct — option **(1)**; it is what locals in **Andhra** called them.
**'Bangaru Farmana'** is the **Golden Farman (1636)** to the **English**, not the Dutch.
**Pulicat (1610)** was the **Dutch** headquarters, not English.
xa: Portuguese influence in Andhra faded by the mid-**17**th century.
Golden Farman issued by **Abdullah Qutb Shah**.
**Yanam** was **French**.

151.s: Which of the following best explains an important reason for the ultimate success of the British in India?
o: The British relied exclusively on naval power and did not use Indian alliances.
The British avoided all involvement in the internal disputes of Indian rulers.
The English East India Company was a private joint-stock company with steady finance and exploited rivalries among Indian rulers.
The English East India Company was directly financed and administered by every Indian ruler.
151.x: The British benefited from the steady finances of a private joint-stock company and from using the rivalries among Indian rulers.
151.tq: Choose the option that combines both stated causal factors without an extreme claim.
xs: The EIC was a **private joint-stock company with steady finance** and **used Indian rulers' rivalries** — option **(3)**.
So the options denying use of Indian alliances or rivalries are wrong.
xa: The EIC was run by a **Court of Directors**.
The **Portuguese** naval monopoly was ended by the **Dutch and English**.
**Wandiwash (1760)** sealed the English victory over the French.

151.s: Which development most directly marked the end of the Portuguese naval monopoly in the Indian Ocean?
o: The expulsion of the Portuguese from Hooghly by Shah Jahan alone
The rise of the Dutch and English as competing maritime powers
The establishment of the French settlement at Yanam
The sale of Serampore and Tranquebar by the Danes
151.x: The Portuguese naval monopoly ended with the emergence of the Dutch and English as competing maritime powers.
151.tq: Identify the broad historical significance rather than a single local event.
xs: The Portuguese **naval monopoly** was ended by the **Dutch and English** as competing maritime powers — option **(2)**.
Hooghly's loss (**1632**), Yanam and the Danish sale (**1845**) are local events, not the cause.
xa: **Swally (1612)** and **Jask / Ormuz (1620 / 1622)**: English beat the Portuguese.
The Dutch captured **Pulicat** from the Portuguese.
Portuguese monopoly tools: **Cartaz**, **Caes**, customs duties.

151.s: Which one of the following sets consists entirely of places associated with the Andhra angle of European trade?
151.x: Masulipatnam, Pulicat, Nizampatnam and Bheemunipatnam are the Andhra-linked places listed in connection with European trade; Yanam is another such place.
151.tq: Use the regional grouping to eliminate places belonging to other European centres.
xs: **Masulipatnam, Pulicat, Nizampatnam and Bheemunipatnam** are all Andhra-angle places — option **(1)** is correct.
**Goa, Diu, Bassein, Salsette** are Portuguese gains on the west coast; **Serampore, Tranquebar** were Danish; **Colachel** and **Ormuz** were battle sites.
xa: **Yanam** (French) completes the AP list; it was one of the **4 French enclaves**.
AP angle also covers the **Golden Farman** and the **calico / Kalamkari** export trade.
⚠ First European factory at **Machilipatnam** = **Portuguese** per the APPSC G2 **2019** key; some notes say **Dutch (1605)**.

151.s: Which of the following is associated with the Andhra region’s export trade under the European companies?
151.x: Andhra’s calico and Kalamkari were important articles connected with the region’s export trade.
151.tq: Distinguish the regional export products from commodities associated with other trade centres.
xs: Andhra's export trade under the companies was in **calico and Kalamkari** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Masulipatnam** was the busiest Coromandel port for **textiles**; **Nizampatnam** too was a **textile port**.
xa: **Pulicat** traded in **pepper and cloth**.
**Golden Farman ('Bangaru Farmana', 1636)** gave the English trade concessions in Golconda.
Andhra ports: Masulipatnam, Pulicat, Nizampatnam, Bheemunipatnam, **Yanam**.

152.s: Cochin and Cannanore became Portuguese bases in:
152.x: Cochin and Cannanore were bases from 1503; the Zamorin had earlier welcomed the Portuguese at Calicut.
152.tq: Distinguish the early base date from later conquest dates.
xs: **Cochin and Cannanore** became Portuguese bases in **1503** — option **(2)**.
The **Zamorin** had earlier welcomed the Portuguese at **Calicut**; **1510** is Goa and **1534** is Bassein.
xa: **Goa** (**1510**, from Bijapur) became the main HQ.
Conflict with the **Zamorin** arose from Portuguese **monopoly and heavy duties**.
The Portuguese lost **Cochin** to the Dutch in **1663**.

152.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Goa — 1510, taken from Bijapur
2. Bassein — 1534, obtained from Bahadur Shah
3. Diu — treaty fort in 1535 and conquered in 1546
4. Daman — obtained in 1559 by treaty
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
152.x: All four pairs are correct. Goa was taken from Bijapur in 1510, Bassein was obtained in 1534, Diu was secured by treaty in 1535 and conquered in 1546, and Daman was obtained in 1559.
152.tq: Check each settlement against both its date and grantor or political source.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Goa 1510** from **Bijapur**; **Bassein 1534** from **Bahadur Shah**.
**Diu:** treaty fort **1535** (Bahadur Shah, pressed by **Humayun**), conquered **1546**.
**Daman:** first attacked **1523**, obtained **1559** by treaty with the Shah.
xa: **Hugli** was granted by **Akbar (1579)**.
**Diu Fort** was built **1535-41**.
Other settlements: **San Thome** (near Madras) and **Salsette**.

152.s: Which Portuguese settlement was granted by Akbar in 1579?
152.x: Akbar granted the Portuguese permission to establish themselves at Hugli in 1579.
152.tq: Identify the settlement from the Mughal grantor and year.
xs: **Hugli** was granted to the Portuguese by **Akbar** in **1579** — option **(4)**.
**Bassein (1534)** came from **Bahadur Shah**; **Daman (1559)** by treaty with the Shah.
xa: **Shah Jahan** captured Hugli in **1632**.
Portuguese raided the Bay of Bengal from **Hugli and Chittagong** with **Arakanese pirates**.
**Shaista Khan** later took **Sondip and Chittagong**.

152.s: In the Battle of Diu fought in 1509, Almeida defeated the combined fleet of:
o: Gujarat, the Egyptian Mamluks and the Zamorin
The English, the Persians and Bijapur
152.x: Almeida defeated the combined fleet of Gujarat, the Egyptian Mamluks and the Zamorin at Diu in 1509.
152.tq: Recall the complete composition of the opposing coalition.
xs: At **Diu (1509)** **Almeida** beat the combined fleet of **Gujarat**, the **Egyptian Mamluks** and the **Zamorin** — option **(1)**.
The **English**, **Persians**, **Marathas**, **Arakanese** and **Dutch** were not part of that fleet.
xa: Almeida was the **first Viceroy**.
The **Zamorin of Calicut** clashed constantly with the Portuguese over **monopoly and heavy duties**.
⚠ Battle of Diu (**1509**) ≠ Diu fort by treaty (**1535**) ≠ Diu conquered (**1546**).

152.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding Bahadur Shah of Gujarat?
o: He conquered Goa from Bijapur in 1510.
He ceded Diu to the Dutch in 1663.
Pressed by Humayun, he allowed Nino da Cunha to build the fort at Diu in 1535.
152.x: Pressed by Humayun, Bahadur Shah of Gujarat permitted Nino da Cunha to build the Diu fort in 1535.
152.tq: Trace the political pressure and concession to identify the correct sequence.
xs: **Pressed by Humayun**, **Bahadur Shah** let **Nino da Cunha** build the **Diu** fort in **1535** — option **(3)**.
Goa was taken from **Bijapur (1510)** by the Portuguese; **Shah Jahan** took Hugli (**1632**); the Dutch took **Cochin (1663)**, not Diu.
xa: Bahadur Shah also gave **Bassein (1534)**.
Diu was **conquered** by the Portuguese in **1546**.
**Diu Fort** dates **1535-41**.

152.s: The constant conflict between the Portuguese and the Zamorin of Calicut was mainly caused by Portuguese:
o: Alliance with the Arakanese pirates against Calicut
152.x: The Portuguese monopoly over trade and their heavy duties led to continuing conflict with the Zamorin of Calicut.
152.tq: Identify the stated economic cause behind the political conflict.
xs: Portuguese **monopoly and heavy duties** caused constant conflict with the **Zamorin of Calicut** — option **(4)**.
The Zamorin had **welcomed** them at Calicut at first.
xa: The Zamorin's fleet joined Gujarat and the Mamluks against **Almeida** at **Diu (1509)**.
The Portuguese shifted to **Cochin and Cannanore (1503)**.
The **Cartaz** enforced the monopoly — ships without it were **confiscated or sunk**.

152.s: The term 'Cartaz' in the context of Portuguese rule in India refers to:
o: A naval trade licence or pass
152.x: A Cartaz was a Portuguese naval trade licence or pass required for ships sailing in the Indian Ocean.
152.tq: Discriminate the exact administrative meaning of a Portuguese term.
xs: The **Cartaz** was a **naval trade licence (pass)** — option **(2)**; asked in **APPSC-GS 2018**.
Every ship sailing the **Indian Ocean** had to buy one.
xa: It was backed by the **Caes** (convoy system) and **customs duties**.
Ships without it were **confiscated or sunk**.
It was used in the **Bay of Bengal** too.

152.s: A ship sailing in the Indian Ocean without a Portuguese Cartaz was liable to be:
152.x: Ships without the required Cartaz could be confiscated or sunk by the Portuguese.
152.tq: Apply the definition of a licence to its enforcement consequence.
xs: A ship without a **Cartaz** was **confiscated or sunk** — option **(2)**.
Every ship sailing the **Indian Ocean** had to buy this **naval trade licence**.
xa: Backed by the **Caes** convoy system and customs duties.
The system also ran in the **Bay of Bengal**.
Cartaz was asked in **APPSC-GS 2018**.

152.s:
Consider the following statements about the Cartaz system:
1. It was supported by convoy arrangements known as Caes.
2. It was connected with the collection of customs duties.
3. It was restricted to the western coast and was not used in the Bay of Bengal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
152.x: The Cartaz system was backed by the Caes convoy system and customs duties. It was also used in the Bay of Bengal, making statement 3 false.
152.tq: Spot the geographically restrictive false statement.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: the Cartaz was backed by the **Caes** convoy system.
Statement 2 correct: it went with **customs duties**.
Statement 3 wrong: the Cartaz was also used in the **Bay of Bengal**.
xa: Every Indian Ocean ship had to buy one; without it, **confiscated or sunk**.
**Goa Inquisition (16th c.)** acted against religious dissent.
Telugu name for the Portuguese: **Budata Keechu**.

152.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Wheat — Portuguese New World crop introduced into India
152.x: Tobacco, chilli and tomato (to Telugu soil) are Portuguese introductions. Wheat is the wrong pair: it is not a New World crop and is not among the crops the Portuguese introduced.
152.tq: Find the item outside the specified crop group.
xs: **Wheat** is the wrong pair — it is not among the Portuguese New World crops — option **(4)**.
Portuguese crops: **tobacco**, potato, lady's finger, **chilli**, pineapple, sapota, groundnut.
**Tomato** was introduced to **Telugu soil** (APPSC-G2 **2025** key).
xa: **Printing press (1556)**; Bible printed in **Kannada and Malayalam**.
**Vindaloo** comes from **vinha d'alhos**.
New World crops **reshaped Indian cuisine**.

152.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Bible was printed in Kannada and Malayalam under Portuguese influence.
2. St. Francis Xavier arrived in Goa in 1542.
3. St. Francis Xavier's remains are preserved in the Basilica of Bom Jesus, Goa.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
152.x: All three statements are correct: Kannada and Malayalam Bible printing is associated with the Portuguese, Xavier reached Goa in 1542, and his remains are at the Basilica of Bom Jesus.
152.tq: Verify the language, date and place details independently.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The **Bible** was printed in **Kannada and Malayalam** after the **printing press (1556)**.
**St. Francis Xavier** arrived in Goa in **1542**; his remains lie in the **Basilica of Bom Jesus**, Goa.
xa: Other missionaries: **Father Rudolf** and **Father Monserrate**.
**Goa Inquisition (16th c.):** state machinery used for conversions.
Forts: **Aguada**, Bassein, **Diu Fort (1535-41)**.

152.s: Which one of the following was associated with the Goa Inquisition?
o: Use of state machinery for conversions and action against religious dissent
Suppression of Arakanese piracy by Shaista Khan
Promotion of religious dissent by Portuguese officials
152.x: The Goa Inquisition in the sixteenth century acted against religious dissent and used state machinery for conversions.
152.tq: Identify the institutional function from the action described.
xs: The **Goa Inquisition** acted **against religious dissent** and used **state machinery for conversions** — option **(2)**.
It belonged to the **16th century**.
**Hugli** was granted by **Akbar (1579)**; **Shaista Khan** suppressed Arakanese pirates — unrelated.
xa: Forced conversion and inter-marriage **alienated Indians** — an internal cause of decline.
Religious intolerance alienated the **Golconda Sultans**.
**St. Francis Xavier** arrived in Goa in **1542**.

152.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
152.x: Vindaloo derives from the Portuguese expression vinha d'alhos. Balcaos refers to features of Indo-Portuguese houses, while Aguada and Bassein are forts.
152.tq: Distinguish cultural terms from administrative and military terms.
xs: **Vindaloo** derives from **vinha d'alhos** — option **(1)**.
**Balcaos** are a feature of **Indo-Portuguese houses**, not naval licences.
**Aguada** and **Bassein** are Portuguese **forts**.
xa: The naval licence was the **Cartaz**, backed by the **Caes**.
**Diu Fort** was built **1535-41**.
**Tomato** reached Telugu soil via the Portuguese.

152.s: The Portuguese set up the first printing press in India at Goa in the year:
152.x: The printing press came to Goa in 1556. 1510 is the capture of Goa, 1542 the arrival of St. Francis Xavier, and 1661 the Bombay dowry.
152.tq: Press 1556; Xavier 1542.
xs: The Portuguese set up the printing press at Goa in **1556** — option **(3)**.
**1510** is the capture of **Goa**; **1542** the arrival of **St. Francis Xavier**.
xa: The Bible was printed in **Kannada and Malayalam**.
Xavier's remains: **Basilica of Bom Jesus**, Goa.
Crops: **tobacco**, **chilli**, groundnut, sapota, pineapple.

152.s: The Portuguese raids from Hugli and Chittagong were conducted in association with:
152.x: Portuguese raiders operating from Hugli and Chittagong acted with Arakanese pirates in the Bay of Bengal.
152.tq: Identify the allied group linked with the activity.
xs: Raids from **Hugli and Chittagong** were made with the **Arakanese pirates** — option **(1)**.
They raided the **Bay of Bengal**.
xa: **Shah Jahan** took **Hugli (1632)**.
**Shaista Khan** took **Sondip and Chittagong** and suppressed the pirates.
Hugli had been granted by **Akbar (1579)**.

152.s: Who captured Hugli in 1632 in response to Portuguese activities?
152.x: Shah Jahan captured Hugli in 1632 in response to Portuguese piracy and related activities.
152.tq: Match the Mughal ruler with the punitive action.
xs: **Shah Jahan** captured **Hugli in 1632** — option **(4)**.
**Akbar** had granted Hugli in **1579**; **Humayun** pressed Bahadur Shah, leading to the Diu fort (**1535**).
xa: **Shaista Khan** (Aurangzeb era) took **Sondip and Chittagong**.
Portuguese pirates from Hugli acted with the **Arakanese**.
Mughal response ended Portuguese power in **Bengal**.

152.s: Which Mughal-era official captured Sondip and Chittagong and suppressed the Arakanese pirates?
152.x: During Aurangzeb's reign, Bengal governor Shaista Khan captured Sondip and Chittagong and suppressed the Arakanese pirates.
152.tq: Use the office-holder and action pairing rather than the emperor alone.
xs: **Shaista Khan**, Bengal governor in the **Aurangzeb** era, captured **Sondip and Chittagong** — option **(3)**.
**Nino da Cunha** was a Portuguese governor; **Bahadur Shah** ruled Gujarat.
xa: He **suppressed the Arakanese pirates**.
**Shah Jahan** captured **Hugli (1632)**.
Portuguese raids came from **Hugli and Chittagong**.

152.s:
Arrange the following Portuguese losses to the English in chronological order:
A. Ormuz
B. Swally
C. Off Jask

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
152.x: The Portuguese suffered defeat at Swally in 1612, off Jask in 1620, and lost Ormuz in 1622 to the English and the Shah of Persia.
152.tq: Arrange events by their stated years, fixing the earliest English victory first.
xs: Ormuz fell to the **English + Shah of Persia**.
xa: Losses to the **Dutch**: **Pulicat (1610)**, Nagapattinam, **Cochin (1663)**.
**Dutch and English competition** was an external cause of decline.
**Goa statehood:** **May 1987**.

152.s: Which one of the following was NOT a major factor in the decline of Portuguese power in India?
o: A sustained increase in support from the Dutch and English
The merger of Portugal with Spain in 1580
152.x: Dutch and English competition contributed to Portuguese decline rather than supporting Portugal. Weak successors, official corruption and the 1580 merger with Spain were among the causes of decline.
152.tq: Find the option that reverses the direction of a stated historical cause.
xs: **Support from the Dutch and English** is NOT a factor — they were **competitors** — option **(1)**.
Real causes: **weak successors** after Albuquerque, **corrupt, poorly paid officials**, Portugal's **merger with Spain (1580)**.
xa: Discovery of **Brazil** diverted attention.
**Forced conversion and inter-marriage** alienated Indians.
Losses to the Dutch: **Pulicat (1610)**, **Cochin (1663)**.

152.s: Which of the following territories was lost by the Portuguese to the Dutch in 1663?
152.x: The Portuguese lost Cochin to the Dutch in 1663. Their other losses to the Dutch were Pulicat (1610) and Nagapattinam (1658); Daman, Diu and Hugli were not lost to the Dutch (Hugli fell to Shah Jahan in 1632).
152.tq: Distinguish the territory associated with the specific year.
xs: The Portuguese lost **Cochin** to the **Dutch** in **1663** — option **(1)**.
Other losses to the Dutch: **Pulicat (1610)** and **Nagapattinam**.
**Hugli** fell to **Shah Jahan (1632)**, not the Dutch.
xa: Losses to the English: **Swally (1612)**, off **Jask (1620)**, **Ormuz (1622)**.
Cochin had been a Portuguese base since **1503**.
Daman (**1559**) and Diu (**1546**) stayed Portuguese till **1961**.

152.s: Which one of the following correctly states the later status of Goa?
o: Goa became a state in May 1987.
Goa became a state in December 1961.
Goa was transferred to the Dutch in May 1987.
Goa became a Portuguese state in 1961.
152.x: Goa attained statehood in May 1987; Portuguese rule had ended earlier through Operation Vijay on 19 December 1961.
152.tq: Separate the date of liberation from the later date of statehood.
xs: **Goa** became a **state** in **May 1987** — option **(1)**.
Portuguese rule had ended in **1961** — the Portuguese were the **last to leave**.
xa: Goa was taken in **1510** — the first European territory since **Alexander**.
Goa was the main **Portuguese HQ**.
**St. Francis Xavier's** remains lie in the **Basilica of Bom Jesus**, Goa.

152.s: Which of the following places formed part of the Portuguese presence on the Andhra coast?
152.x: Portuguese posts existed at Masulipatnam, Pulicat and San Thome on or near the Andhra coast.
152.tq: Identify the complete regional cluster of Portuguese posts.
xs: Portuguese posts on the Andhra / Coromandel coast: **Masulipatnam, Pulicat and San Thome** — option **(3)**.
**Bassein, Diu, Daman** are west-coast gains; **Hugli, Sondip, Chittagong** are in Bengal.
xa: **Pulicat** was a **pepper and cloth** centre before the Dutch took it (**1610**).
First Andhra factory at **Machilipatnam (1670)** with **Abdullah Qutb Shah's** permission (some notes).
Influence waned by the mid-**17th c.** — religious intolerance alienated Golconda.

152.s: Before the Dutch took it, Pulicat was particularly known as a centre of:
152.x: Pulicat was a centre of pepper and cloth trade before it passed to the Dutch.
152.tq: Match the trading centre with its characteristic commodities.
xs: Before the Dutch took it, **Pulicat** was a **pepper and cloth** centre — option **(1)**.
The Portuguese lost Pulicat to the **Dutch** in **1610**.
xa: Other Andhra-coast posts: **Masulipatnam**, **San Thome**.
Dutch also took **Nagapattinam** and **Cochin (1663)**.
Telugu name for the Portuguese: **Budata Keechu**.

152.s: Which statement correctly describes the Portuguese factory at Machilipatnam?
o: It was established in 1670 with permission from Abdullah Qutb Shah.
It was established in 1663 after the Dutch conquest of Cochin.
It was established in 1579 with permission from Akbar.
It was established in 1503 with permission from Bahadur Shah.
152.x: The Portuguese obtained permission from Abdullah Qutb Shah and established their first Andhra factory at Machilipatnam in 1670.
152.tq: Combine the correct year, grantor and location instead of accepting a single matching detail.
xs: The Portuguese **Machilipatnam** factory was set up in **1670** with **Abdullah Qutb Shah's** permission — option **(1)**.
Some notes call the Portuguese the **last Europeans in Andhra**.
**1663** is the Dutch capture of Cochin; **1579** Akbar's Hugli grant; **1503** the Cochin base.
xa: AP angle: Machilipatnam factory under **Qutb Shahi** permission.
Influence waned by the mid-**17th c.** — religious intolerance alienated the **Golconda Sultans**.
Posts also at **Pulicat** and **San Thome**.

152.s: Why did Portuguese influence wane in the Golconda region by the middle of the seventeenth century?
o: They transferred Masulipatnam to the English voluntarily.
Their religious intolerance alienated the Golconda Sultans.
Their alliance with the Golconda Sultans became too strong.
They abandoned all maritime trade in the Bay of Bengal.
152.x: Portuguese religious intolerance alienated the Golconda Sultans, contributing to the waning of their influence by the mid-seventeenth century.
152.tq: Identify the stated cause of regional political decline.
xs: Their **religious intolerance alienated the Golconda Sultans** — option **(2)**.
So Portuguese influence waned by the **mid-17th century**.
xa: **Goa Inquisition (16th c.)** — state machinery for conversions.
Forced conversion and inter-marriage alienated Indians — an internal cause of decline.
Permission for the Machilipatnam factory came from **Abdullah Qutb Shah**.

152.s: In the Telugu country the Portuguese were popularly called:
152.x: Locals called the Portuguese Budata Keechu. Bangaru Farmana is the Golden Farman given to the English, Kalamkari is a painted textile, and Petapoli is another name for Nizampatnam.
152.tq: Budata Keechu = Portuguese.
xs: In the Telugu country the Portuguese were called **Budata Keechu** — option **(1)**.
**Bangaru Farmana** is the **Golden Farman** given to the English; **Kalamkari** is an Andhra textile.
xa: **Tomato, chilli, groundnut** came to Telugu country via the Portuguese.
Portuguese Andhra posts: **Masulipatnam, Pulicat, San Thome**.
Influence waned by mid-**17th c.**

152.s: Which of the following group of crops was introduced by the Portuguese into the Telugu country?
152.x: Tomato, chilli and groundnut were among the New World crops introduced by the Portuguese into the Telugu country. These crops significantly influenced Indian cuisine and agriculture.
152.tq: Group the three region-specific crops before eliminating unrelated crop combinations.
xs: **Tomato, chilli and groundnut** came to the Telugu country via the Portuguese — option **(4)**.
**Tomato** to Telugu soil was the APPSC-G2 **2025** key.
xa: Full list: **tobacco**, potato, lady's finger, **chilli**, pineapple, sapota, groundnut.
New World crops **reshaped Indian cuisine**.
**Vindaloo** from **vinha d'alhos**.

152.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the first European territory in India since the time of Alexander?
152.x: Goa became the first European territory in India since the time of Alexander in 1510.

xs: **Goa, 1510** was the first European territory in India since **Alexander** — option **(4)**.
It was taken from **Bijapur** and became the main **HQ**.

Goa became a state in **May 1987**.

152.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Portuguese were the first Europeans to come to India.
2. The Portuguese were the last European power to leave India.
3. The Portuguese departure from India took place in 1510.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
152.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: the Portuguese left India in 1961; 1510 is associated with Goa becoming the first European territory in India since the time of Alexander.
152.tq: Find the incorrect date by separating the Portuguese departure year from the Goa territorial milestone.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statements 1 and 2: the Portuguese were the **first Europeans to come** and the **last to leave**.
Statement 3 wrong: they left in **1961**; **1510** is when **Goa** was taken.
xa: Goa: first European territory since **Alexander**.
**Goa statehood:** **May 1987**.
New World crops **reshaped Indian cuisine**.

152.s: Who was the first Portuguese Viceroy in India?
152.x: Francisco de Almeida (1505-09) was the first Viceroy. Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in 1498, Albuquerque followed Almeida (1509-15), and Nuno da Cunha later moved the HQ to Goa.
152.tq: First Viceroy = Almeida (Blue Water).
xs: **Francisco de Almeida** was the **first Portuguese Viceroy** — option **(3)**.
He won the **Battle of Diu (1509)** against Gujarat, the Mamluks and the Zamorin.
xa: First European territory since Alexander = **Goa 1510**.
Decline began with **weak successors after Albuquerque**.
**Nino da Cunha** built the **Diu** fort (**1535**) by treaty with Bahadur Shah.

153.s: The Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie (VOC) was formed on:
153.x: The VOC was formed on 20 March 1602 by merging Dutch companies. The year 1592 is a commonly noted misprint.
153.tq: Reject the near-date trap by retaining the exact formation date.
xs: The VOC was formed on **20 March 1602** by **merging Dutch companies** — option **(2)**.
⚠ "**1592**" in some notes is a **misprint**; **1610** is Pulicat and **1605** is Machilipatnam.
xa: Full name: **Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie**.
Charter from the **Dutch States-General** — sovereign powers.
Asian HQ: **Batavia** (Jakarta).

153.s: Which of the following powers was NOT granted to the VOC by the Dutch States-General?
153.x: The VOC received sovereign powers to wage war, build forts and sign treaties; it had no power to crown the British monarch.
153.tq: Find the authority that lies outside the charter’s sovereign commercial powers.
xs: **Crowning the British monarch** was NOT a VOC power — option **(4)**.
The **Dutch States-General** gave it **sovereign powers**: to **wage war**, **build forts** and **sign treaties**.
xa: VOC formed **20 March 1602**.
Focus: **Spice Islands**, not India.
Dutch were the first to get the right to **mint coins** in Andhra.

153.s: What was the headquarters of the VOC in Asia?
153.x: Batavia, now Jakarta, was the Asian headquarters of the VOC.
153.tq: Distinguish the Asian headquarters of the VOC from its Indian headquarters.
xs: The VOC's Asian headquarters was **Batavia** (Jakarta) — option **(1)**.
**Pulicat** was the Coromandel HQ till **1690**, then **Nagapattinam**; **Chinsura** was a Bengal factory (**1653**).
xa: Focus on the **Spice Islands**, not India.
**Pulicat** was a hub of the **slave trade** to Batavia.
After **Bedara (1759)** the Dutch withdrew to **Indonesia**.

153.s: The principal focus of the VOC in Asia was the:
153.x: The VOC primarily focused on the Spice Islands, while India was not its central strategic focus.
153.tq: Identify the company’s strategic priority rather than its secondary Indian activities.
xs: The VOC's main focus in Asia was the **Spice Islands** — option **(3)**.
India was secondary; the **Indonesian spice monopoly** came first.
xa: Asian HQ: **Batavia** (Jakarta).
Malabar was **less profitable** than **Coromandel cloth**.
Carrying trade: **textiles** exchanged for East Indies **spices**.

153.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the background of Dutch expansion in Asia?
o: Philip II — ban on Lisbon trade
Philip II — formation of the VOC in 1602
153.x: Philip II’s ban on Lisbon trade formed part of the background to Dutch expansion. Linschoten wrote the Itinerario, while Cornelis de Houtman reached Bantam in 1596.
153.tq: Match each person or event with the correct role in the background sequence.
xs: **Philip II — ban on Lisbon** trade is correct — option **(1)**; it was the background to Dutch voyages.
**Linschoten** wrote the **Itinerario (1595-96)**; **Cornelis de Houtman** reached **Bantam (1596)** — options 2 and 3 swap them.
The VOC was formed in **1602** by merging Dutch companies, not by Philip II.
xa: **Van der Haghen** set up the **Machilipatnam** factory (**1605**).
**Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah** (Golconda) gave permission for Machilipatnam.
**J.B. Russell** led the Dutch at **Bedara**.

153.s:
Consider the following statements about the Dutch at Pulicat:
1. The Dutch took Pulicat from the Portuguese in 1610.
2. The Dutch settled at Pulicat with the permission of the Sultan of Golconda.
3. Fort Geldria at Pulicat was the Dutch Coromandel headquarters until 1690.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
153.x: Statement 1 is correct: Pulicat was taken from the Portuguese in 1610. Statement 2 is wrong: Pulicat was granted by the Chandragiri king; Golconda (Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah) gave Machilipatnam. Statement 3 is correct: Fort Geldria at Pulicat was the Coromandel headquarters till 1690, when it moved to Nagapattinam. So '1 only' misses statement 3, and options with statement 2 are wrong.
153.tq: Pulicat = Chandragiri king; Machilipatnam = Golconda.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: the Dutch took **Pulicat** from the **Portuguese** in **1610** (UPSC says **1609**).
Statement 2 wrong: Pulicat came with the **Chandragiri king's** permission; Golconda's **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah** permitted Machilipatnam.
Statement 3 correct: **Fort Geldria**, Pulicat, was the **Coromandel HQ till 1690**.
xa: After **1690** the HQ moved to **Nagapattinam** (APPSC G2 **2005** key).
Pulicat: hub of the **slave trade to Batavia**.
Pulicat was ceded under the **Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824**.

153.s: Who permitted the Dutch to establish their factory at Machilipatnam?
153.x: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah of Golconda permitted Van der Haghen to establish the Dutch factory at Machilipatnam.
153.tq: Identify the local ruler associated with the trading privilege.
xs: **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah** of **Golconda** permitted the Machilipatnam factory — option **(4)**.
It was set up by **Van der Haghen** in **1605**.
The **Chandragiri king** permitted **Pulicat**; **Marthanda Varma** of **Travancore** fought the Dutch at **Colachel**.
xa: Machilipatnam = first Dutch (and first formal European) factory in Andhra (APPSC G2 **2017**).
APPSC-GS **2024** match: Dutch **1605**, British **1611**.
Machilipatnam's textile trade = **most-asked AP fact**.

153.s: Which of the following was a subordinate Dutch factory in the Krishna–Godavari weaving belt?
153.x: Draksharama was one of the subordinate Dutch factories in the Krishna–Godavari weaving belt. Colachel was the 1741 battle where Travancore defeated the Dutch, Batavia was the VOC's Asian headquarters, and Bantam was where de Houtman reached in 1596.
153.tq: Distinguish subordinate Andhra factories from major overseas centres and battle sites.
xs: **Draksharama** was a subordinate Dutch factory in the **Krishna-Godavari weaving belt** — option **(4)**.
**Colachel** was the **1741** battle; **Batavia** the VOC's Asian HQ; **Bantam** where de Houtman reached (**1596**).
xa: Other belt factories: **Nizampatnam**, **Narsapuram**, **Gollapalem**, **Petapoli**.
**Palakollu** and Draksharama are old Dutch settlements.
**Palakollu (1652)** was a **Godavari delta** weaving centre.

153.s: Which European power had traded at Machilipatnam before the establishment of the first Dutch factory there?
153.x: The Portuguese had traded at Machilipatnam before the Dutch established their factory there.
153.tq: Use the earlier-presence distinction rather than the later factory chronology.
xs: The **Portuguese** traded at Machilipatnam before the Dutch (APPSC **2019** key) — option **(4)**.
The **British** came to Machilipatnam later, in **1611**.
xa: First Dutch factory in AP: **Machilipatnam (1605)** (APPSC G2 **2017**).
Set up by **Van der Haghen**.
Dutch were also first to **mint coins** in Andhra.

153.s: The Dutch were the first European traders in Andhra to obtain the right to do which of the following?
o: Issue farmans in their own name
153.x: The Dutch were the first to obtain the right to mint coins in Andhra.
153.tq: Match the distinctive privilege with the correct European power.
xs: The Dutch were the first to get the right to **mint coins** in Andhra — option **(2)**.
It was a **privilege granted by local rulers**.
xa: First Dutch factory: **Machilipatnam (1605)**.
The VOC's charter gave powers to **wage war, build forts, sign treaties**.
Dutch Andhra network ran from **Machilipatnam to Bheemunipatnam**.

153.s: Which monument is associated with the Dutch presence at Bheemunipatnam?
153.x: Bheemunipatnam is associated with a Dutch cemetery, while Fort Geldria is located at Pulicat.
153.tq: Match the monument with the correct Andhra location.
xs: **Bheemunipatnam** has the **Dutch cemetery** — option **(2)**.
**Fort Geldria** is at **Pulicat**, not Bheemunipatnam.
xa: Bheemunipatnam factory: **1641** (UPSC).
Old Dutch settlements: **Palakollu** and **Draksharama**.
Dutch network: **Machilipatnam to Bheemunipatnam**.

153.s: Fort Geldria is located at:
153.x: Fort Geldria was established at Pulicat, the major Dutch centre on the Coromandel Coast.
153.tq: Use the monument-location association to distinguish Pulicat from other Dutch settlements.
xs: **Fort Geldria** is at **Pulicat** — option **(2)**.
Pulicat (**1610**) was the Dutch **Coromandel HQ till 1690**.
xa: Pulicat was taken from the **Portuguese** with the **Chandragiri king's** permission.
**Bheemunipatnam:** Dutch cemetery.
Pulicat ceded by the **Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824**.

153.s: Which Dutch settlement was a weaving centre in the Krishna delta?
153.x: Nizampatnam, also called Petapoli, was a Dutch weaving centre in the Krishna delta.

xs: **Nizampatnam (Petapoli)** was a **Krishna delta** weaving centre — option **(4)**.
**Palakollu (Palicol)** was in the **Godavari delta**; **Bheemunipatnam** is known for the Dutch cemetery.

**Jagannathapuram / Koringa:** **1736 / 1802**.
Exports included **Kalamkari**, coarse cloth and fine muslins.

153.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
153.x: Nizampatnam was a Krishna delta weaving centre, not the Dutch headquarters. Pulicat was the headquarters until 1690.
153.tq: Reject the option that swaps a settlement's economic role with the headquarters.
xs: **Nizampatnam — HQ until 1690** is wrong; that was **Pulicat** — option **(3)**.
Nizampatnam (Petapoli) was a **Krishna delta weaving centre**.
**Draksharama** (trading post), **Bheemunipatnam** (**1641**) and **Palakollu** (Godavari weaving) are correct.
xa: HQ moved from Pulicat to **Nagapattinam** in **1690**.
Fort at Pulicat: **Fort Geldria**.

153.s: Which one of the following pairs (European company - first factory in Andhra) is correctly matched as per the APPSC key?
153.x: The Dutch set up their first factory in Andhra at Machilipatnam in 1605; the British came there in 1611. Pulicat was taken by the Dutch in 1610, and Bheemunipatnam was a Dutch factory of 1641.
153.tq: Dutch 1605, British 1611 - both Machilipatnam.
xs: **Dutch — Machilipatnam, 1605** is correct — option **(1)**.
APPSC-GS **2024** match: Dutch first factory at Masulipatnam **1605**, British **1611**.
**Pulicat** was taken in **1610**; **Bheemunipatnam (1641)** was Dutch, not English.

153.s:
Arrange the following Dutch factories in chronological order of establishment:
A. Surat
B. Chinsura
C. Karaikal
D. Nagapattinam
153.x: The correct sequence is Surat (1616), Karaikal (1645), Chinsura (1653) and Nagapattinam (1658).

xs: Order: **Surat (1616)**, **Karaikal (1645)**, **Chinsura (1653)**, **Nagapattinam (1658)** — **A, C, B, D**, option **(1)**.
Nagapattinam was **taken from the Portuguese**.
xa: **Cochin** followed in **1663**.
Other factories: **Kasimbazar**, **Baranagar**, **Balasore**, **Patna**, **Vengurla**.
**Chinsura** was the site of the **Bedara** battle (**1759**).

153.s: Nagapattinam became the chief Dutch factory after the decline of which centre in 1690?
153.x: Pulicat was the chief Dutch centre until 1690, after which Nagapattinam became the chief factory.
153.tq: Test the succession between the former and later chief centres.
xs: **Pulicat** was the chief centre until **1690**, when HQ moved to **Nagapattinam** — option **(3)**.
APPSC G2 **2005** key: Dutch HQ in India = **Nagapattinam**.
xa: Pulicat's fort: **Fort Geldria**.
Nagapattinam was taken from the **Portuguese** in **1658**.
⚠ **Mahe** is wrongly listed as Dutch in some notes — it was **French**.

153.s: Which one of the following is NOT a Dutch centre mentioned in connection with their Indian establishments?
153.x: Mahe was a French centre, although it is sometimes incorrectly included in lists of Dutch centres. Kasimbazar, Balasore and Vengurla were associated with Dutch establishments.
153.tq: Use the confusable European-centre distinction to identify the exception.
xs: **Mahe** was **French**, not Dutch — option **(2)**.
**Kasimbazar**, **Balasore** and **Vengurla** are Dutch factories (UPSC list).
xa: Other Dutch factories: **Baranagar**, **Patna**.
Elsewhere: **Surat (1616)**, **Karaikal (1645)**, **Chinsura (1653)**.
HQ: Pulicat till **1690**, then **Nagapattinam**.

153.s: Which statement regarding the Dutch establishment at Cochin is correct?
o: It was founded by the Dutch in 1605 and abandoned in 1690.
It was taken from Travancore in 1741 and returned to Portugal in 1824.
It was taken from the Portuguese in 1663 and passed to the British in 1795.
It was taken from the English in 1663 and ceded to the French in 1795.
153.x: The Dutch took Cochin from the Portuguese in 1663; it later passed to the British in 1795.
153.tq: Keep the predecessor, takeover year and later successor together as one sequence.
xs: The Dutch took **Cochin** from the **Portuguese** in **1663**; it passed to the **British (1795)** — option **(3)**.
**1605** is Machilipatnam; **1741** is Colachel; **1824** the Anglo-Dutch Treaty.
xa: **Pulicat** was ceded under the **Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824**.
Dutch occupation period: **1605-1825**.
Travancore's win at **Colachel (1741)** ended Dutch ambitions in **Malabar**.

153.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
153.x: Pulicat was a hub of the slave trade to Batavia, not a centre of porcelain production. Koringa was associated with shipbuilding and Chittavalasa with jute.
153.tq: Find the option that substitutes a trade activity not associated with the stated port.
xs: **Pulicat — porcelain** is wrong: Pulicat was a hub of the **slave trade to Batavia** — option **(3)**.
**Porcelain** was an **import**, with silk.
**Koringa — shipbuilding** and **Chittavalasa — jute** are correct.
xa: Exports: gems, **diamonds**, **indigo**, cotton, **Kalamkari**, fine muslins.
Carrying trade: **saltpetre** (Bihar), opium, rice; pepper from Malabar.
**Koringa** factory: **1802**.

153.s: Which of the following commodities was imported into the Coromandel ports by the Dutch?
153.x: Silk and porcelain were imported, whereas gems, diamonds, indigo, cotton, Kalamkari and cloth were among the exports.
153.tq: Separate imports from the longer list of export commodities.
xs: The Dutch imported **silk and porcelain** — option **(2)**.
**Diamonds, indigo, cotton, Kalamkari** were **exports**.
**Saltpetre** (Bihar) and **rice** were part of the **carrying trade**.
xa: Coromandel **textiles** were exchanged for East Indies **spices**.
**Pepper** came from **Malabar**.
Industry: shipbuilding at **Koringa**; jute at **Chittavalasa**.

153.s: In the Dutch carrying trade, Coromandel textiles were exchanged particularly for which commodity from the East Indies?
153.x: The Dutch carried textiles from the Coromandel in exchange for spices from the East Indies.
153.tq: Trace the direction and purpose of the carrying trade instead of memorising isolated commodities.
xs: Coromandel **textiles** were exchanged for East Indies **spices** — option **(3)**.
**Saltpetre**, **opium** and rice were other carrying-trade goods; **pepper** came from **Malabar**.
xa: VOC's focus: the **Spice Islands**.
Imports: **silk and porcelain**.
Malabar was less profitable than **Coromandel cloth**.

153.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Battle of Colachel of 1741?
o: The English defeated the Dutch and captured Chinsura.
The Dutch defeated Travancore and secured Malabar.
The Portuguese defeated Travancore and recovered Cochin.
Travancore defeated the Dutch and ended their ambitions in Malabar.
153.x: Travancore under Marthanda Varma defeated the Dutch at Colachel in 1741, ending Dutch ambitions in Malabar.
153.tq: Match the battle with its opponents and strategic consequence.
xs: At **Colachel (1741)** **Travancore** beat the Dutch and **ended their ambitions in Malabar** — option **(4)**.
Travancore's ruler was **Marthanda Varma**.
The English beat the Dutch at **Bedara / Chinsura (1759)** — a different battle.
xa: **Bedara (1759):** **Francis Forde** vs **J.B. Russell**; Dutch withdrew to Indonesia.
Dutch took **Cochin** from the Portuguese in **1663**.
Defeats plus loss of **Andhra strongholds** in the Anglo-French wars ended Dutch power.

153.s:
Consider the following statements about the Battle of Bedara or Chinsura:
1. It was fought in 1759.
2. The English defeated the Dutch.
3. Francis Forde commanded the English forces.
4. The Dutch subsequently withdrew to Indonesia.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
153.x: All four statements are correct. The English defeated the Dutch at Bedara/Chinsura in 1759, with Francis Forde as commander, after which the Dutch withdrew to Indonesia.
153.tq: Verify the date, opponents, commander and consequence as a connected battle profile.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Bedara / Chinsura** was fought in **1759**; the **English** defeated the **Dutch**.
**Francis Forde** commanded the English (with **Clive**); the Dutch then **withdrew to Indonesia**.
xa: The Dutch side was led by **J.B. Russell**.
**Colachel (1741):** Travancore beat the Dutch.
**Chinsura** factory: **1653**.

153.s: Who commanded the Dutch forces at the Battle of Bedara or Chinsura?
153.x: J.B. Russell commanded the Dutch forces at the Battle of Bedara/Chinsura in 1759.
153.tq: Separate the commanders of the opposing forces in the same battle.
xs: **J.B. Russell** commanded the Dutch at **Bedara / Chinsura** — option **(3)**.
**Clive** and commander **Francis Forde** were on the **English** side; **Marthanda Varma** fought at **Colachel**.
xa: Bedara was fought in **1759**; Dutch withdrew to **Indonesia**.
Anglo-Dutch conferences of **1613** and **1615** failed.
Occupation period: **1605-1825**.

153.s: Which of the following was a major reason for the decline of Dutch power in India?
o: Their Coromandel cloth trade was always more profitable than Indonesian spices.
They were supported by the English against all Indian powers.
They completely abandoned maritime trade after 1605.
Their priority was the Indonesian spice monopoly rather than Indian territorial expansion.
153.x: The Dutch prioritised their spice monopoly in Indonesia, while Malabar was less profitable to them than the Coromandel cloth trade. This weakened their long-term commitment to India.
153.tq: Choose the strategic explanation that links commercial priority with imperial decline.
xs: Their priority was the **Indonesian spice monopoly** — option **(4)**.
**Malabar** was less profitable than **Coromandel cloth** — but the spice monopoly came first, not cloth.
The English were **rivals**, not supporters (conferences of **1613** and **1615** failed).
xa: Defeats at **Colachel** and **Bedara**.
Lost **Andhra strongholds** in the Anglo-French wars.
Asian HQ: **Batavia**.

153.s: The Anglo-Dutch conferences of 1613 and 1615 were significant because they:
o: failed to resolve the rivalry between the English and the Dutch
ended the Dutch spice monopoly in Indonesia
established Dutch control over all Indian ports
153.x: The conferences of 1613 and 1615 failed to settle the fierce Anglo-Dutch rivalry.
153.tq: Identify the outcome of the diplomatic efforts rather than their purpose alone.
xs: The **Anglo-Dutch conferences of 1613 and 1615** **failed** to settle the rivalry — option **(1)**.
The Dutch kept their **Indonesian spice monopoly**; Batavia stayed Dutch.
xa: English beat the Dutch at **Bedara (1759)**.
Pulicat ceded under the **Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824**.
Cochin passed to the British in **1795**.

153.s: The Dutch occupation in India is generally stated to have lasted from:
153.x: The period of Dutch occupation in India is stated as 1605–1825.
153.tq: Distinguish the broad occupation period from the separate dates of treaty-based cession.
xs: Dutch occupation in India lasted **1605-1825** — option **(1)**.
It began with **Machilipatnam (1605)**.
xa: **Pulicat** ceded under the **Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824**.
**Cochin** passed to the British in **1795**.
After **Bedara (1759)** the Dutch withdrew to **Indonesia**.

153.s: Under which agreement was Pulicat ceded by the Dutch?
153.x: Pulicat was ceded by the Dutch under the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824.
153.tq: Match the settlement with the treaty that determined its later transfer.
xs: **Pulicat** was ceded under the **Anglo-Dutch Treaty, 1824** — option **(1)**.
All remaining settlements went with it.
xa: **Fort Geldria** stands at Pulicat.
Pulicat was Coromandel HQ till **1690**.
Occupation period: **1605-1825**.

153.s: The Dutch Andhra network extended broadly from:
153.x: The Dutch network in Andhra extended from Machilipatnam in the south-western part of the network to Bheemunipatnam in the north-east.
153.tq: Test the geographical span of the regional network using its endpoints.
xs: The Dutch Andhra network ran from **Machilipatnam to Bheemunipatnam** — option **(3)**.
**Machilipatnam's textile trade** is the **most-asked AP fact**.
xa: **Machilipatnam (1605)** — first Dutch factory in Andhra.
**Bheemunipatnam (1641)** — Dutch cemetery.
Weaving belt: **Draksharama**, **Nizampatnam**, **Narsapuram**, **Palakollu**.

154.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the charter granted to the English East India Company in 1600:
1. It initially granted a fifteen-year monopoly over East Indies trade.
2. It conferred territorial governance and legislative power over India.
3. The monopoly was subsequently made perpetual.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
154.x: The charter initially granted a fifteen-year monopoly, later made perpetual. It granted exclusive trading rights, not territorial governance or legislative power.
154.tq: Separate commercial privileges from territorial and legislative authority.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 correct: a **15-year monopoly** between the **Cape of Good Hope and the Magellan Straits**.
Statement 2 wrong: APPSC-GS **2024** key — **exclusive trading rights**, not territorial governance or legislative power.
Statement 3 correct: the monopoly was **later made perpetual**.
xa: Granted on **31 December 1600** by **Queen Elizabeth I**.
Name: "The **Governor and Company of Merchants of London** Trading into the East Indies".
"**Merchant Adventurers**" had formed the association c.**1599**.

154.s: Who was the Mughal emperor in 1600, when the English East India Company received its charter?
154.x: Akbar was the Mughal emperor in 1600.
154.tq: Use the date to identify the contemporary ruler.
xs: **Akbar** was the Mughal emperor in **1600** — option **(3)**.
**Jahangir** came later — he issued the Surat farman in **1613**; **Aurangzeb** crushed **Child's War (1686-90)**.
xa: Charter: **31 December 1600**, **Queen Elizabeth I**.
APPSC-G2 **2025**: EIC founded **1600**.
First voyage **1602** under **James Lancaster** → factory at **Bantam**.

154.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the internal organisation of the early English East India Company?
o: A Governor and a 24-member committee, with shareholders forming the General Court
A President and a 40-member committee, with merchants forming the Royal Court
A Governor and a 12-member committee, with the Crown forming the General Court
A Viceroy and a 24-member committee, with Parliament forming the General Court
154.x: The Company was run by a Governor and a 24-member committee, later known as the Court of Directors. Shareholders constituted the General Court, or Court of Proprietors.
154.tq: Match institutional structure with the correct body and membership.
xs: A **Governor + 24-member committee**, with **shareholders** forming the **General Court** — option **(1)**.
The committee became the **Court of Directors** (elected annually); the General Court became the **Court of Proprietors**.
xa: The EIC was a **private joint-stock** company, unlike the state-run Portuguese and French ventures.
**1657:** **Cromwell's** charter — permanent joint stock.
**1635 / 1649:** **Courten's** rival association, licensed by Charles I, merged in **1649**.

154.s: Which of the following was NOT among the powers later delegated to the English East India Company by Charles II and James II?
o: Electing members of the British Parliament
Declaring war and peace with non-Christians
154.x: Charles II and James II delegated powers including coining money, exercising jurisdiction, and making war and peace with non-Christians. Parliamentary elections were not among these powers.
154.tq: Find the authority or power that does not belong to the group.
xs: **Electing members of Parliament** was NOT a delegated power — option **(1)**.
**Charles II** and **James II** delegated sovereignty: **coin money**, **jurisdiction**, **war and peace with non-Christians**.
xa: **1657:** Cromwell's charter made the joint stock **permanent**.
**1708:** merged into the **United Company** (APP gives **1707**).
Bombay was leased from **Charles II** in **1668**.

154.s: The English East India Company received its charter on 31 December 1600 from:
154.x: Queen Elizabeth I granted the charter on 31 December 1600. James I sent Hawkins and Roe to Jahangir, Charles II received Bombay as dowry and delegated sovereign powers, and Cromwell gave the 1657 charter for a permanent joint stock.
154.tq: 1600 = Elizabeth I; 1657 = Cromwell.
xs: The charter of **31 December 1600** came from **Queen Elizabeth I** — option **(2)**.
**Charles II** later delegated sovereign powers; **Cromwell** gave the **1657** charter.
xa: It gave a **15-year monopoly**, later perpetual.
Mughal emperor then: **Akbar**.
First voyage: **1602**, **James Lancaster**, capital **£68,000**.

154.s:
Which of the following sequence of events is correct?

1. Thomas Best defeated the Portuguese at Swally.
2. Jahangir issued a farman to the English.
3. The English achieved further victories off Jask, Ormuz and elsewhere.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
154.x: The Swally victory occurred in 1612, Jahangir’s farman followed in 1613, and further English victories occurred in 1615, off Jask in 1620 and at Ormuz in 1622.
154.tq: Test a connected military-commercial sequence rather than isolated dates.
xs: All three are in correct order — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Swally (1612):** Best defeated the Portuguese off Surat.
**Jahangir's farman (1613)** followed.
xa: The Surat factory was the **first English factory in India**.
**Child's War (1686-90):** EIC attacked Mughal shipping.
**Shivaji** sacked Surat twice.

154.s:
Consider the following statements about Child’s War:
1. It lasted from 1686 to 1690.
2. Josiah Child’s East India Company attacked Mughal shipping.
3. Aurangzeb defeated the Company and pardoned it after payment of a fine.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
154.x: Child’s War lasted from 1686 to 1690. The Company attacked Mughal shipping, but Aurangzeb crushed the conflict and pardoned the Company after it paid a fine.
154.tq: Check the duration, initiator, opponent and consequence of a conflict.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Child's War** ran **1686-90**; **Josiah Child's** EIC attacked **Mughal shipping**.
**Aurangzeb** crushed it and **pardoned the Company** on payment of a **fine**.
xa: **1691** imperial order: trade in Bengal for **Rs 3,000** a year in lieu of dues.
Job Charnock founded Calcutta at **Sutanuti (1690)**.
**Shivaji** threatened the English factory at **Surat**.

154.s: Shivaji’s attacks on Surat had which effect on the English East India Company?
o: He transferred the Surat factory to Madras.
He twice sacked Surat and threatened the English factory there.
He helped the English defeat the Portuguese at Swally.
He granted the English a monopoly over Surat trade.
154.x: Shivaji sacked Surat twice and threatened the English factory located there.
154.tq: Apply the consequence of a regional military event to the Company’s settlement.
xs: **Shivaji** **sacked Surat twice** and threatened the English factory — option **(2)**.
**Swally (1612)** was Thomas Best's victory, not Shivaji's.
xa: **Bombay** replaced **Surat** as the chief west-coast settlement.
Bombay came to the Company in **1668** for **£10 a year**.
Surat factory followed **Jahangir's farman (1613)**.

154.s: The English ship Globe reached Machilipatnam in 1611 under the command of:
154.x: The Globe reached Machilipatnam in 1611 under Captain Anthony Hippon, marking the establishment of the first English factory in Andhra.
154.tq: Distinguish between the similarly associated English captains.
xs: The **"Globe"** reached Machilipatnam in **1611** under **Captain Anthony Hippon** — option **(2)**.
⚠ APPSC-G2 **2025** A-R said "Globe under Captain **Hawkins**" — the bank key marks it **false**.
**Thomas Best** won at **Swally (1612)**.
xa: This was the **first English factory in Andhra** (APPSC G2 **2025** key).
Permission came from **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah**.
UPSC dates the Masulipatnam factory to **1616**.

154.s: Permission for the English to establish their first factory at Machilipatnam in 1611 was granted by:
154.x: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah permitted the English to establish their first factory at Machilipatnam in 1611.
154.tq: Use the founder-or-grantor trap in a regional history question.
xs: **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah** gave permission — option **(3)**; he ruled **1580-1612**, so it fits **1611**.
⚠ APPSC G2 **2008** key named **Ibrahim Qutb Shah** — but Ibrahim died in **1580**.
**Abdullah Qutb Shah** issued the **Golden Farman** later.
xa: **Captain Anthony Hippon** came in the ship **"Globe"**.
First English factory: **Surat** (India), **Machilipatnam** (Andhra).
Next Andhra moves: **Pulicat (1621)**, **Armagaon (1626)**.

154.s: The Golden Farman issued by the Sultan of Golconda granted the English:
o: A monopoly over the diamond mines of Golconda
The right to collect land revenue in Golconda
Free trade in Golconda ports on payment of 500 pagodas annually
Exclusive control over all ports of the Coromandel Coast without payment
154.x: The Golden Farman permitted free trade in Golconda ports in return for an annual payment of 500 pagodas.
154.tq: Identify the precise commercial privilege and its financial condition.
xs: The **Golden Farman** allowed **free trade in Golconda ports** for **500 pagodas** a year — option **(3)**.
It was a **fixed payment**, not free control, revenue rights or a diamond monopoly.
xa: Dated **1632** (UPSC); some notes give **1636** under **Abdullah Qutb Shah**.
It **brought the English back to Machilipatnam**.
**Diamonds and rubies** came from **Golconda** as trade goods.

154.s:
Arrange the following English settlements on the Andhra coast in chronological order:
A. Armagaon
B. Visakhapatnam
C. Machilipatnam
D. Pulicat
154.x: The settlements were established at Machilipatnam in 1611, Pulicat in 1621, Armagaon in 1626 and Visakhapatnam in 1682.
154.tq: Fix the first and last events, then arrange the middle dates.
xs: Order: **Machilipatnam (1611)**, **Pulicat (1621)**, **Armagaon (1626)**, **Visakhapatnam (1682)** — **C, D, A, B**, option **(1)**.
Pulicat was **abandoned** due to Dutch hostility.
xa: After Armagaon, back to Machilipatnam, then **Madras (1639)**.
Other factories: **Nizampatnam**, **Narsapuram**, **Veeravasaram**, **Bheemunipatnam**.
**Bhimili** = first municipality in Andhra (**1861**).

154.s: Which one of the following statements about Armagaon is correct?
o: It was established in 1611 at Machilipatnam by Captain Anthony Hippon.
It was established in 1639 at Madras by Francis Day.
It was established in 1626 at Dugarajapatnam and was named after Karanam Armugam Mudali.
It was established in 1682 at Visakhapatnam by Job Charnock.
154.x: Armagaon was established in 1626 at Dugarajapatnam, now in Tirupati district, and was named after Karanam Armugam Mudali.
154.tq: Combine place, date and names to defeat swapped-founder options.
xs: **Armagaon (1626)**, at **Dugarajapatnam**, was named after **Karanam Armugam Mudali** — option **(3)**.
**1611** is Machilipatnam (Hippon); **1639** Madras (Francis Day); **1682** Visakhapatnam.
xa: Armagaon was the **3rd** Andhra settlement, now in **Tirupati district**.
It lay **35 miles north of Pulicat**.
Job Charnock founded Calcutta, not any Andhra post.

154.s:
Consider the following statements regarding early English settlements in Andhra:
1. Pulicat was the second English settlement on the Andhra coast.
2. Pulicat was abandoned because of Dutch hostility.
3. Visakhapatnam became an English settlement in 1682.
4. Bhimili was the first municipality in Andhra, established in 1861.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
154.x: Pulicat was the second settlement, was abandoned due to Dutch hostility, Visakhapatnam was established in 1682, and Bhimili became the first municipality in Andhra in 1861.
154.tq: Verify multiple regional facts without confusing the first municipality with Madras.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Pulicat (1621)** was the **2nd** settlement (Chandragiri king) and was **abandoned due to Dutch hostility**.
**Visakhapatnam** factory came in **1682**.
**Bhimili** was the **first municipality in Andhra (1861)**.
xa: **Madras** = India's first municipality (**1687**).
**Armagaon (1626)** was the 3rd settlement.
Andhra coast = the EIC's **first home in the south**.

154.s: The English abandoned Pulicat after establishing themselves there in 1621 mainly because of:
o: Dutch rivalry and harassment by Golconda officials
a famine in the Krishna delta
a Portuguese ban on all inland trade
154.x: The English faced Dutch rivalry and harassment by Golconda officials, leading them to move from Pulicat. They later established themselves at Armagaon in 1626.
154.tq: Match the movement of a European power with its stated cause.
xs: **Dutch rivalry** and **harassment by Golconda officials** drove the English from **Pulicat** — option **(1)**.
They moved to **Armagaon (1626)**, then back to Machilipatnam, then **Madras (1639)**.
xa: Pulicat (**1621**) was granted by the **Chandragiri king**.
The **Golden Farman** brought them back to Machilipatnam.
Madras land also came from the **Chandragiri** ruler.

154.s: The Golden Farman issued by Abdullah Qutb Shah to the English is dated in the relevant account to:
154.x: The Golden Farman was issued by Abdullah Qutb Shah in 1636. Some standard accounts give 1632, but the date used here is 1636.
154.tq: Handle a close-date question by retaining the date specified for the event.
xs: The Golden Farman under **Abdullah Qutb Shah** is dated **1636** — option **(3)**.
UPSC dates it **1632**.
**1611** is the Machilipatnam factory; **1626** Armagaon.
xa: Privilege: free trade in **Golconda ports** for **500 pagodas** a year.
It **brought the English back to Machilipatnam**.
**Farrukhsiyar's 1717** farman was the **"Magna Carta"** of Company trade.

154.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Settlement — Year
1. Surat — 1612–13
2. Madras — 1639
3. Bombay — 1668
4. Calcutta — 1690/1700

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
154.x: Surat, Madras, Bombay and Calcutta are associated respectively with 1612–13, 1639, 1668 and 1690/1700 in the early English settlement chronology.
154.tq: Use a settlement-year table and check every pair before selecting the code.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Bombay 1668** (leased from Charles II); **Calcutta 1690 / 1700** (Job Charnock; Fort William).
xa: **Hariharpur, Balasore (1633)** on the **Odisha** coast.
**Masulipatnam (1611)** under Hippon.
Presidency of **Fort William in Bengal** dates **1700**.

154.s:
Consider the following statements about early English settlements:
1. The Surat factory followed Jahangir's farman of 1613, after Thomas Best's victory.
2. Bombay was leased to the Company by Charles II in 1668.
3. Calcutta (Fort William) is associated with Francis Day.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
154.x: Statement 1 is correct: Jahangir's farman of 1613, after Best's victory, gave the Surat factory. Statement 2 is correct: Bombay was leased from Charles II in 1668. Statement 3 is wrong: Calcutta is associated with Job Charnock; Francis Day founded Madras (Fort St. George, 1639). So '1 only' misses statement 2, and options with statement 3 are wrong.
154.tq: Francis Day = Madras; Job Charnock = Calcutta.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Jahangir's farman (1613)** after **Best's** victory gave the **Surat** factory.
Statement 2 correct: **Bombay** was leased from **Charles II** in **1668**.
Statement 3 wrong: Calcutta is **Job Charnock's**; **Francis Day** founded **Madras (1639)**.
xa: Bombay rent: **£10 a year** (some notes print **1688**).
Calcutta: zamindari of three villages bought **1698**; **Fort William (1700)**.
Surat was the first English factory in India (UPSC, APP).

154.s: Madras, including Fort St. George, was founded in 1639 by:
o: Francis Day after obtaining a grant from Venkatapati Raya III
Job Charnock after a grant from Aurangzeb
Thomas Best after obtaining a farman from Jahangir
Anthony Hippon after obtaining permission from Abdullah Qutb Shah
154.x: Francis Day founded Madras in 1639 after obtaining a grant from the Chandragiri ruler Venkatapati Raya III, with the efforts of the Damerla brothers, Venkatadri and Ayyappa.
154.tq: Apply the founder–grantor distinction to a settlement question.
xs: **Francis Day** founded **Madras (1639)** with a grant from **Venkatapati Raya III** — option **(1)**.
Venkatapati Raya III was the **Chandragiri** ruler; the **Damerla brothers** (**Venkatadri, Ayyappa**) urged the grant.
**Job Charnock** founded Calcutta; **Hippon** came to Machilipatnam.
xa: Fort St. George became a **Presidency seat**.
Madras = **India's first municipality (1687)**.
Some notes call Madras the **Company's HQ** in India.

154.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the three principal Presidency seats of the English East India Company?
o: Calcutta–Fort St. George; Madras–Fort William; Bombay–Bantam
Surat–Fort St. George; Bombay–Fort William; Madras–Bantam
Madras–Fort St. George; Bombay; Calcutta–Fort William in Bengal
Machilipatnam–Fort St. George; Surat–Fort William; Calcutta–Bantam
