154.x: The Presidency seats were Madras at Fort St. George, Bombay, and Calcutta at the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal. Bombay replaced Surat as the western Presidency seat.
154.tq: Match each Presidency with its fort or administrative identity.
xs: Presidency seats: **Madras (Fort St. George)**, **Bombay**, **Calcutta (Fort William in Bengal)** — option **(3)**.
**Bombay** replaced **Surat**; **Bantam** was the first-voyage factory (**1602**), not a Presidency.
xa: Presidency of Fort William in Bengal: **1700**.
Bombay transfer: **1668**, **£10 a year**.
Fort St. George: **1639**.

154.s: Bombay was handed over to the East India Company by the English Crown in 1668 in return for an annual rent of
154.x: In 1668, Bombay was transferred to the East India Company for an annual rent of £10.
154.tq: Use the exact monetary figure to distinguish the Company transfer from the earlier dowry transaction.
xs: Bombay went to the Company in **1668** for **£10 a year** — option **(4)**.
⚠ Some notes print **1688** — use **1668**.
xa: It was **leased from Charles II**.
It **replaced Surat** as chief west-coast settlement.
It became one of the three **Presidency seats**.

154.s: Job Charnock is associated with the foundation of the English settlement at
154.x: Job Charnock founded the English settlement at Sutanuti in 1690.
154.tq: Match the Company agent with the specific settlement linked to him.
xs: **Job Charnock** founded Calcutta at **Sutanuti (1690)** — option **(4)**.
**Armagaon** and **Machilipatnam** were Andhra settlements; **Surat** came by Jahangir's farman.
xa: Zamindari of **Sutanuti, Gobindapur, Kalikata** bought **1698**.
**Fort William (1700)** — nucleus of Calcutta.
Presidency of **Fort William in Bengal**.

154.s: The zamindari of which group of villages was acquired by the East India Company in 1698, forming the basis of Calcutta?
154.x: In 1698, the Company bought the zamindari rights of Sutanuti, Gobindapur and Kalikata.
154.tq: Recall the complete three-village group instead of identifying only one settlement.
xs: In **1698** the Company bought the zamindari of **Sutanuti, Gobindapur and Kalikata** — option **(2)**.
These three villages became the nucleus of **Calcutta**, fortified as **Fort William (1700)**.
xa: Job Charnock had founded Calcutta at **Sutanuti (1690)**.
It later became the Presidency of **Fort William in Bengal** — one of three Presidency seats.
**1691** imperial order: Bengal trade for **Rs 3,000** a year.

154.s: The early settlement that became the nucleus of Calcutta was fortified as
154.x: The settlement formed from the three villages was fortified as Fort William in 1700.
154.tq: Use the settlement–fort association to distinguish Calcutta from the other English centres.
xs: The nucleus of Calcutta was fortified as **Fort William (1700)** — option **(3)**.
**Fort St. George** is at **Madras (1639)**.
xa: Built on the three villages bought in **1698**.
It became the Presidency of **Fort William in Bengal**.
**Job Charnock** founded the settlement (**1690**).

154.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Marcara — acquisition of Madras from Chandragiri
Francis Day — acquisition of the Madras site
154.x: Marcara was associated with the French factory at Machilipatnam, not with the acquisition of Madras. Francis Day obtained the Madras site from Venkatapati Raya III.
154.tq: Find the wrongly assigned person and deed.
xs: **Marcara — Madras acquisition** is wrong — option **(1)**.
The Madras site was got by **Francis Day** from the Chandragiri ruler **Venkatapati Raya III** (**1639**).
The **Damerla brothers** — **Venkatadri** and **Ayyappa** — urged the grant.
xa: Fort St. George became a **Presidency seat**.
Madras = **India's first municipality (1687)**.
Pulicat (**1621**) was also granted by the **Chandragiri king**.

154.s: Which one of the following pairs correctly gives the first English factory in India and in Andhra respectively?
154.x: The first English factory in India was at Surat (Jahangir's farman, 1613); in Andhra it was Machilipatnam (Globe under Hippon, 1611). Armagaon (1626) was the third Andhra settlement and Madras (1639) came later.
154.tq: India = Surat; Andhra = Machilipatnam.
xs: First English factory: **Surat** in India, **Machilipatnam** in Andhra — option **(1)**.
Surat came by **Jahangir's farman (1613)**; Machilipatnam by the "Globe" under **Hippon (1611)**.
**Armagaon (1626)** was the 3rd Andhra settlement; **Madras (1639)** came later.
xa: Exam angle: first English factory — **Surat** (India) vs **Machilipatnam** (Andhra).
UPSC dates the Masulipatnam factory to **1616**.
Andhra coast = the EIC's **first home in the south**.

154.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Saltpetre and opium — Bihar and Bengal
154.x: Silk and cotton piece-goods were obtained from Bengal, not Gujarat. Chintz, diamonds and saltpetre were associated respectively with the Coromandel-Andhra region, Golconda and Bihar-Bengal.
154.tq: Find the reversed goods-and-source pair.
xs: **Silk and cotton piece-goods — Gujarat** is wrong; they came from **Bengal** — option **(4)**.
**Saltpetre, opium — Bihar / Bengal**; **chintz — Coromandel / Andhra**; **diamonds, rubies — Golconda** are correct.
xa: **Indigo** came from **Gujarat** and **Coromandel**.
Andhra goods: chintz, **calicoes**, muslins, **palampores** (Machilipatnam).
Goods were paid for with imported **bullion**.

154.s: Indigo was obtained by the English from:
154.x: The main sources of indigo mentioned are Gujarat and the Coromandel region.
154.tq: Distinguish a commodity with more than one regional source.
xs: **Indigo** came from **Gujarat** and the **Coromandel** — option **(3)**.
**Saltpetre and opium** came from **Bihar / Bengal**; **diamonds** from **Golconda**.
xa: **Silk, cotton piece-goods** from **Bengal**.
**Calicoes**, chintz, palampores from Machilipatnam.
Paid for with imported **bullion**.

154.s: The English East India Company largely paid for Indian goods during its early trade with:
154.x: Imported bullion was used to pay for Indian goods in the early period of Company trade.
154.tq: Identify the financial basis of early European trade.
xs: The Company paid for Indian goods with imported **bullion** — option **(2)**.
Land revenue in Bengal came only after **Plassey (1757)** and **Buxar (1764)**.
xa: Goods: **calicoes**, chintz (Coromandel), **indigo** (Gujarat), **saltpetre** (Bihar).
**Diamonds, rubies** from **Golconda**.
Golden Farman: free trade for **500 pagodas** a year.

154.s: The Farman of 1717, regarded as the “Magna Carta” of the East India Company’s trade, was issued by which Mughal emperor?
154.x: The Farman of 1717 was issued by Mughal emperor Farrukhsiyar and substantially enhanced the Company’s trading privileges.
154.tq: Use the ruler–deed association to distinguish the issuer from other Mughal emperors.
xs: The **1717** farman — the **"Magna Carta"** of Company trade — was issued by **Farrukhsiyar** — option **(4)**.
**Aurangzeb** had earlier crushed **Child's War** and pardoned the Company.
xa: The mission was led by **John Surman**.
Bengal: **duty-free trade** for **Rs 3,000** a year and the right to issue **dastaks**.
**Bombay-minted coins** made valid across the empire.

154.s: The mission that secured the Farman of 1717 from Farrukhsiyar was led by
154.x: The Company’s mission to Farrukhsiyar’s court was led by John Surman.
154.tq: Match the diplomatic mission with its leader rather than with an earlier or later Company agent.
xs: **John Surman** led the mission to **Farrukhsiyar** — option **(1)**.
**Hawkins** and **Roe** were envoys to **Jahangir**; **Job Charnock** founded Calcutta.
xa: The farman (**1717**) was the **"Magna Carta"** of Company trade.
Surat: all duties waived for **Rs 10,000** a year.
Madras: only the **prevailing rent**.

154.s:
Consider the following statements about Farrukhsiyar's Farman of 1717:
1. Madras-minted coins were made valid throughout the Mughal Empire.
2. At Surat, all duties were waived for Rs 10,000 a year.
3. In Bengal, the Company got duty-free trade for Rs 3,000 a year and the right to issue dastaks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
154.x: Statement 1 is wrong: it was Bombay-minted coins that became valid across the empire; for Madras the Company paid only the prevailing rent. Statement 2 is correct: Surat duties were waived for Rs 10,000 a year. Statement 3 is correct: Bengal duty-free trade for Rs 3,000 a year with dastaks. So '3 only' misses statement 2, and options with statement 1 are wrong.
154.tq: Bengal Rs 3,000; Surat Rs 10,000; coins = Bombay.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 wrong: it was **Bombay-minted coins** that became valid across the empire; for Madras only the prevailing rent.
Statement 2 correct: **Surat** duties waived for **Rs 10,000** a year.
Statement 3 correct: **Bengal** duty-free trade for **Rs 3,000** a year, with **dastaks**.
xa: Issued by **Farrukhsiyar**; mission under **John Surman**.
Called the **"Magna Carta"** of Company trade.
**Dastak misuse** drained Nawab revenue → a root cause of **Plassey**.

154.s: Under the Farman of 1717, the East India Company was authorised to issue which instrument for duty-free trade in Bengal?
154.x: The Farman granted the Company the right to issue dastaks, or passes for duty-free trade in Bengal.
154.tq: Discriminate between closely associated Mughal administrative and commercial terms.
xs: The **1717** farman let the Company issue **dastaks** for duty-free trade in **Bengal** — option **(4)**.
Bengal duty-free trade cost **Rs 3,000** a year.
xa: **Dastak misuse** through private trade drained the **Nawab's** revenue.
That became **a root cause of Plassey**.
**Bombay-minted coins** made valid across the empire.

154.s: Which one of the following was a consequence of the misuse of dastaks by the East India Company?
o: Draining of the Nawab’s revenue through private trade
Transfer of Bombay to the Portuguese
Increase in the revenue of the Nawab of Bengal
Abolition of the Company’s trade privileges in Surat
154.x: Company servants misused dastaks for private trade, depriving the Nawab of Bengal of revenue. This became one of the underlying causes leading to the Battle of Plassey.
154.tq: Trace the cause-and-effect link from a commercial privilege to its political consequence.
xs: Dastak misuse in **private trade** **drained the Nawab's revenue** — option **(1)**.
This was **a root cause of Plassey** — so the Nawab's revenue fell, not rose.
xa: Dastaks came under **Farrukhsiyar's farman (1717)**.
After **Plassey (1757)** and **Buxar (1764)** the Company became a ruler.
Surat duties waived for **Rs 10,000** a year — unaffected.

154.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the broad political transformation of the English East India Company?
o: It changed directly from a ruling power in 1600 into a trading company after 1757.
It developed from a trading company in 1600 into a ruling power after Plassey and Buxar.
It became a ruling power after the acquisition of Bombay in 1661 alone.
It remained exclusively a trading company until the Government of India Act, 1858.
154.x: The Company was established as a trading company in 1600 and emerged as a territorial ruling power after the Battles of Plassey in 1757 and Buxar in 1764.
154.tq: Track the institutional change across the key dates rather than focusing on a single settlement.
xs: The EIC grew from a **trading company (1600)** into a **ruling power** after **Plassey (1757)** and **Buxar (1764)** — option **(2)**.
Its rule ended with the **GoI Act 1858**.
**Bombay** passed to the Crown as dowry in **1661** — that alone made no ruler.
xa: The **1600** charter gave only **exclusive trading rights**.
**Dastak misuse** was a root cause of Plassey.
Charles II and James II delegated **sovereignty** — coining money, jurisdiction, war and peace.

154.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Battle of Buxar
B. Establishment of the East India Company
C. Battle of Plassey
D. End of Company rule under the Government of India Act

Select the correct sequence.
154.x: The correct order is establishment of the Company in 1600, Plassey in 1757, Buxar in 1764 and the end of Company rule in 1858.
154.tq: Identify the fixed first and last events, then place Plassey before Buxar.
xs: The Company went from **trading company** to **ruler** after Plassey and Buxar; its rule ended under the **GoI Act 1858**.
xa: The EIC charter came from **Queen Elizabeth I**.
**Farrukhsiyar's farman (1717)** came before Plassey.
Madras = India's first municipality (**1687**).

154.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
154.x: Bhimili became the first municipality in Andhra in 1861, whereas Madras was the first municipality in India in 1687.
154.tq: Find the single date-place mismatch by separating the Indian-wide and Andhra-specific municipal facts.
xs: **Bhimili — 1687** is wrong; Bhimili became Andhra's **first municipality** in **1861** — option **(1)**.
**1687** is **Madras**, India's **first municipality**.
**Madras 1639**, **Armagaon 1626**, **Machilipatnam 1611** are correct.
xa: **Visakhapatnam** factory: **1682**.
Madras land came from the **Chandragiri** ruler.
Andhra coast = EIC's **first home in the south**.

155.s:
Consider the following statements about the French East India Company:
1. It was founded in 1664 by Jean-Baptiste Colbert, minister of Louis XIV.
2. It was named the Compagnie des Indes Orientales.
3. It was the first European company to arrive in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
155.x: Statement 1 is correct: Colbert, minister of Louis XIV, founded it in 1664. Statement 2 is correct: its name was the Compagnie des Indes Orientales. Statement 3 is wrong: the French were the last European company to arrive; the Portuguese came first. So '1 only' misses statement 2, and options with statement 3 are wrong.
155.tq: French = last to arrive (1664), state-owned, Colbert under Louis XIV.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: founded in **1664** by **Jean-Baptiste Colbert**, minister of **Louis XIV**.
Statement 2 correct: its name was **Compagnie des Indes Orientales**.
Statement 3 wrong: the French were the **last** European company to arrive.
xa: It was **state-owned** and dependent on subsidies → vulnerable.
Charter: **50**-year monopoly in the Indian + Pacific Oceans, plus rights over **Madagascar**.
First French factory: **Surat (1668)**, under **François Caron**.

155.s: Which of the following correctly describes the charter of the French East India Company?
o: It received a permanent monopoly only over the Indian mainland
It received a 50-year monopoly in the Indian and Pacific Oceans and rights over Madagascar
It received a 25-year monopoly only in the Atlantic Ocean
It received a 100-year monopoly in the Mediterranean Sea
155.x: The company received a 50-year monopoly in the Indian and Pacific Oceans together with rights over Madagascar.
155.tq: Check the duration, geographical scope and additional territorial right as one combined proposition.
xs: It got a **50-year monopoly** in the **Indian and Pacific Oceans** and rights over **Madagascar** — option **(2)**.
This is the UPSC-noted charter of the **1664** company.
xa: Founder: **Colbert**, minister of **Louis XIV**.
**State-owned**, dependent on subsidies.
The French were the **last** European company to arrive.

155.s: The French East India Company was vulnerable primarily because it was:
o: Controlled by the Dutch and financed by English merchants
Organised only as a temporary military alliance
Privately owned and independent of the French Crown
155.x: The French East India Company was state-owned and depended on subsidies, making it vulnerable when sustained state support was lacking.
155.tq: Identify the institutional cause behind the company’s weakness.
xs: The French company was **state-owned and dependent on subsidies** — option **(3)**.
So it was vulnerable when state support was not steady; it was not privately owned.
xa: The French lost for want of **naval supremacy** + steady **state support**.
French = the **only serious European rival** to the British.
By contrast, the EIC was a **private joint-stock** company.

155.s: The first French factory in India was established at which place in 1668 under François Caron?
155.x: Surat was the site of the first French factory in India, established in 1668 under François Caron.
155.tq: Use the direct place-year association and distinguish the first factory from later settlements.
xs: The first French factory was at **Surat (1668)** under **François Caron** — option **(3)**.
Some notes give **1667**.
**Masulipatnam** followed in **1669**; **Pondicherry** in **1673-74**; **Chandernagore** in **1673 / 1690**.
xa: Order key: **Surat > Pondicherry > Yanam > Mahe > Karaikal** (APPSC-G1 **2024**).
Other factories: **Balasore**, **Kasimbazar**.
Pondicherry became the **HQ** of the French in India.

155.s: Which French settlement was established in 1669 by François Caron with Marcara under a patent granted by the Sultan of Golconda?
155.x: Masulipatnam was established in 1669 by François Caron with Marcara under a patent from the Sultan of Golconda.
155.tq: Match the settlement with its year, personnel and granting authority.
xs: **Masulipatnam (1669)** was set up by **Caron** with **Marcara** under a **Golconda** patent — option **(3)**.
**Yanam (1723)**, **Mahe (1725)** and **Karaikal (1739)** came much later.
xa: Machilipatnam was the **first French trading centre in Andhra** (APPSC G2 **2002**; APPSC-GS **2025**).
Permission came from **Abdullah Qutb Shah**.
The French were the **third Europeans** in Andhra.

155.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
155.x: Chandernagore was not situated in Malabar; Mahe was the French settlement on the Malabar coast.
155.tq: Find the geographically misplaced settlement among otherwise correct regional associations.
xs: **Chandernagore — Malabar** is wrong — option **(4)**; Chandernagore was permitted by **Shaista Khan** (Bengal).
**Mahe** is the French settlement in **Malabar**.
**Yanam — Godavari delta** and **Karaikal — Coromandel** are correct.
xa: Chandernagore joined India by **plebiscite (1950)**.
Five enclaves after **1763**: Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam, Chandernagore.

155.s: The French settlement at Chandernagore was permitted by Shaista Khan in 1673 and became settled in which year?
155.x: Shaista Khan permitted the French presence at Chandernagore in 1673, and it was settled in 1690.
155.tq: Separate the year of permission from the later year of actual settlement.
xs: **Chandernagore** was permitted by **Shaista Khan (1673)** and settled in **1690** (APP) — option **(3)**.
**1669** is Masulipatnam; **1674** is Pondicherry; **1725** is Mahe.
xa: Chandernagore → India by **plebiscite (1950)**.
Other Bengal factory: **Kasimbazar**.
Pondicherry's land grant also came in **1673** (Sher Khan Lodi).

155.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the French settlements established in the years 1723, 1725 and 1739 respectively?
155.x: Yanam was established in 1723, Mahe in 1725 and Karaikal in 1739.
155.tq: Arrange the three late French settlements by their stated years.
xs: Yanam is in the **Godavari delta**; Mahe in **Malabar**; Karaikal on the **Coromandel**.
xa: Order key: **Surat > Pondicherry > Yanam > Mahe > Karaikal** (APPSC-G1 **2024**).
**Dumas (1735-41)** acquired Karaikal.
Yanam = **only French territory in Andhra** (APPSC-G2 **2025**).

155.s: Which authority granted permission for the establishment of the French trading centre at Machilipatnam?
155.x: Abdullah Qutb Shah granted permission for the French trading centre at Machilipatnam.
155.tq: Use the authority-location association and avoid confusing Qutb Shah with the later Deccan rulers.
xs: **Abdullah Qutb Shah** permitted the French trading centre at **Machilipatnam (1669)** — option **(3)**.
**Sher Khan Lodi** gave the **Pondicherry** land; **Shaista Khan** permitted **Chandernagore**; **Salabat Jang** granted the **Northern Circars (1753)**.
xa: Machilipatnam = first French centre in Andhra (APPSC G2 **2002**).
French = **third Europeans** in Andhra.
**Colonel Forde** took Machilipatnam in **1759**.

155.s:
With reference to the French presence in Andhra, consider the following statements:
1. The French were the third Europeans to arrive in Andhra.
2. Yanam was the only French territory in Andhra.
3. Yanam became part of the Union Territory of Puducherry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
155.x: The French were the third Europeans in Andhra, Yanam was their only territory there, and it is now part of the Union Territory of Puducherry.
155.tq: Verify the historical status, relative arrival and present administrative association together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The French were the **third Europeans** in Andhra.
**Yanam (1723)** was the **only French territory in Andhra** (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
Yanam merged de facto **1954**, de jure **1962** → UT of **Puducherry**.
xa: First French centre in Andhra: **Machilipatnam (1669)**.
Yanam = **last French enclave** on Andhra soil.
**Chandernagore** joined by plebiscite (**1950**).

155.s: Arrange the following French settlements in chronological order: 1. Yanam 2. Surat 3. Karaikal 4. Pondicherry 5. Mahe
155.x: Surat 1668, Pondicherry 1673-74, Yanam 1723, Mahe 1725, Karaikal 1739. Pondicherry came after Surat; Yanam came before Mahe; and Yanam came after Pondicherry.
155.tq: S-P-Y-M-K (APPSC-G1 2024).
xs: This is the APPSC-G1 **2024** order key.
xa: **Masulipatnam (1669)** came between Surat and Pondicherry.
Pondicherry was founded by **François Martin**; **Fort St. Louis**.
**Chandernagore** settled **1690**.

155.s: Who gave the land on which Pondicherry was founded to François Martin in 1673?
155.x: Sher Khan Lodi, the Bijapur governor of Valikondapuram, gave the land to François Martin in 1673. Pondicherry was founded there in 1674.
155.tq: Use the founder-grantor distinction and identify the regional office held by the grantor.
xs: **Sher Khan Lodi**, **Bijapur governor of Valikondapuram**, gave the land in **1673** — option **(1)**.
He gave it to **François Martin**, then director at **Masulipatnam**.
**Shaista Khan** permitted Chandernagore; **Abdullah Qutb Shah** permitted Machilipatnam.
xa: Pondicherry was founded in **1674**; fort: **Fort St. Louis**.
Pondicherry was the **HQ** of the French in India.
The **Dutch** captured Pondicherry in **1693**.

155.s: Which fort became the headquarters of the French in India at Pondicherry?
155.x: François Martin built Fort St. Louis at Pondicherry, which became the headquarters of the French in India.
155.tq: Distinguish the French fort from the English and Dutch forts associated with other settlements.
xs: The French HQ at Pondicherry was **Fort St. Louis** — option **(2)**.
**Fort William** is Calcutta's and **Fort St. George** Madras's English forts.
xa: Pondicherry founded **1674** by **François Martin**.
Restored by **Ryswick (1697)** and **Paris (1763)**.
Martin was the **first French governor**.

155.s: Which treaty restored Pondicherry to the French in 1697?
155.x: The Treaty of Ryswick restored Pondicherry to the French in 1697, although the Dutch remained there for two more years.
155.tq: Match the restoration year with the correct treaty rather than the later Treaty of Paris.
xs: The **Treaty of Ryswick** restored Pondicherry in **1697** — option **(4)** (APPSC-G1 **2018** key).
The **Dutch** stayed **two more years**.
The **Treaty of Paris** restored it in **1763**, after the British took it in **1761**.
xa: The Dutch, with English support, captured it in **1693**.
**Treaty of Pondicherry (1754)** led to Dupleix's recall.
Pondicherry: French **HQ**, **Fort St. Louis**.

155.s:
Consider the following sequence of events concerning Pondicherry:
1. The Dutch captured Pondicherry.
2. Pondicherry was restored by the Treaty of Ryswick.
3. The British took Pondicherry after the Battle of Wandiwash.
4. Pondicherry was restored by the Treaty of Paris.
Which one of the following is the correct chronological order?
155.x: The sequence is 1693, 1697, 1761 and 1763: Dutch capture, Treaty of Ryswick restoration, British capture and Treaty of Paris restoration.
155.tq: Use the four dates as anchors and preserve the two capture-restoration pairs.
xs: Order: **Dutch capture (1693)**, **Ryswick (1697)**, **British capture (1761)**, **Paris (1763)** — **1, 2, 3, 4**, option **(1)**.
The British took it after **Wandiwash**.
xa: After the Treaty of Paris the French kept only **trading enclaves**.
Pondicherry was founded in **1674**.
It merged with India de facto **1954**, de jure **1962**.

155.s:
Arrange the following French governors in chronological order of their tenure:
A. Dupleix
B. François Martin
C. Count de Lally
D. Dumas
155.x: François Martin was followed by Dumas, Dupleix and Count de Lally. Their relevant periods were Martin’s early tenure, Dumas in 1735–41, Dupleix in 1742–54 and Lally during the later Carnatic conflict.
155.tq: Place the governors by tenure rather than by the importance of their military achievements.
xs: Order: **François Martin**, **Dumas (1735-41)**, **Dupleix (1742-54)**, **Lally** — **B, D, A, C**, option **(1)**.
Lally lost at **Wandiwash (1760)**.
xa: Martin died **31 Dec 1706**.
Dumas acquired **Karaikal**.
**Godeheu (1754)** replaced Dupleix.

155.s: Who was the first French governor and the builder of Pondicherry?
155.x: François Martin was the first French governor and built Pondicherry. He died on 31 December 1706.
155.tq: Link the earliest governor with the foundational development at Pondicherry.
xs: **François Martin** was the **first French governor** and built **Pondicherry** — option **(2)**.
He died on **31 Dec 1706**.
**Dumas** (**1735-41**) and **Dupleix** (**1742-54**) came later; **Godeheu** replaced Dupleix.
xa: He got the land from **Sher Khan Lodi** in **1673**.
He had been director at **Masulipatnam**.
Fort at Pondicherry: **Fort St. Louis**.

155.s:
Consider the following statements about the later French governors:
1. Dupleix served as governor from 1742 to 1754.
2. Godeheu replaced Dupleix.
3. Godeheu was recalled at the beginning of the Third Carnatic War.
4. Count de Lally was defeated at Wandiwash by Eyre Coote.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
155.x: All four statements are correct. Dupleix served from 1742 to 1754, Godeheu replaced him and was recalled at the start of the Third Carnatic War, while Lally lost at Wandiwash to Eyre Coote.
155.tq: Combine tenure, succession, recall and military defeat to test the full governor sequence.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Dupleix** governed **1742-54** — the peak of French power.
**Godeheu (1754)** replaced him and was recalled at the start of the **Third Carnatic War**.
**Count de Lally** lost at **Wandiwash (1760)** to **Eyre Coote**.
xa: **Treaty of Pondicherry (1754)** → Dupleix recalled.
Dupleix's title: **Nawab** of Mughal territory south of the **Krishna**; jagir **Valapadu**.
**Dumas (1735-41)** came before Dupleix.

155.s: After the death of Nizam-ul-Mulk in 1748, Dupleix exploited which succession disputes?
155.x: Dupleix intervened in the Hyderabad succession between Nasir Jang and Muzaffar Jang and in the Carnatic succession between Anwaruddin and Chanda Sahib.
155.tq: Identify the two linked succession struggles used by Dupleix for intervention.
xs: Dupleix exploited the **Hyderabad and Carnatic** successions — option **(1)**.
**Hyderabad:** after **Nizam-ul-Mulk's** death (**1748**) — **Nasir Jang** vs **Muzaffar Jang**.
**Carnatic:** **Anwaruddin** vs **Chanda Sahib**.
xa: **Ambur (1749):** Dupleix + Muzaffar Jang + Chanda Sahib killed **Anwaruddin**.
**Bussy** escorted **Muzaffar Jang**.
Turning point: Clive's **siege of Arcot (1751)**.

155.s: The Battle of Ambur in 1749 resulted in which of the following outcomes?
o: Anwaruddin was killed, Muzaffar Jang became Subedar and Chanda Sahib became Nawab
Chanda Sahib was killed and Nasir Jang became Nawab of the Carnatic
Salabat Jang became Nizam and Dupleix was recalled
Muzaffar Jang was killed, Anwaruddin became Subedar and Chanda Sahib was imprisoned
155.x: At Ambur, Anwaruddin was killed; Muzaffar Jang was made Subedar and Chanda Sahib became Nawab.
155.tq: Trace the consequence of the alliance instead of recalling only the battle name.
xs: At **Ambur (1749)** **Anwaruddin** was killed; **Muzaffar Jang** became **Subedar** and **Chanda Sahib** **Nawab** — option **(1)**.
The winning alliance was **Dupleix + Muzaffar Jang + Chanda Sahib**.
xa: Muzaffar Jang was later murdered at **Rayachoti**; **Salabat Jang** made Subedar.
Clive's **Arcot** siege (**1751**) turned the tide.
**Dupleix** was recalled after the **Treaty of Pondicherry (1754)**.

155.s: Dupleix was declared Nawab of the Mughal territory south of the Krishna with which place as his jagir?
155.x: Dupleix was declared Nawab of the Mughal territory south of the Krishna, with Valapadu as his jagir.
155.tq: Distinguish the title-holder’s jagir from the other territories granted as rewards.
xs: Dupleix's jagir was **Valapadu** — option **(1)**.
He was declared **Nawab of the Mughal territory south of the Krishna**.
xa: Dupleix was governor from **1742**; peak of French power.
**Bussy** guarded **Salabat Jang** in **Hyderabad** for seven years.
Dupleix was recalled after **1754**.

155.s: The siege of Arcot by Clive in 1751 lasted for:
155.x: Clive held Arcot for 53 days in 1751. This success turned the tide against the French-supported position in the Carnatic.
155.tq: Use the specific duration as the decisive numerical clue.
xs: Clive held **Arcot (1751)** for **53** days — option **(3)**.
It was the **turning point** of the Carnatic struggle.
xa: **Ambur (1749)** had made **Chanda Sahib** Nawab.
**Treaty of Pondicherry (1754):** neither side to meddle in princes' quarrels.
**Wandiwash (1760):** **Eyre Coote** beat **Lally**.

155.s: Which treaty provided that the French and the English should not interfere in the quarrels of Indian princes and led to the recall of Dupleix?
155.x: The Treaty of Pondicherry was concluded in 1754. It required both sides not to meddle in the quarrels of Indian princes, and Dupleix was recalled.
155.tq: Match the non-intervention clause with the treaty that ended Dupleix’s tenure.
xs: The **Treaty of Pondicherry (1754)** barred meddling in princes' quarrels and led to **Dupleix's recall** — option **(2)**.
**Ryswick (1697)** and **Paris (1763)** restored Pondicherry.
xa: **Godeheu (1754)** replaced Dupleix.
Clive's **Arcot** siege (**1751**) held **53** days.
Dupleix governed **1742-54**.

155.s: After the murder of Muzaffar Jang at Rayachoti, whom did Bussy help establish as Subedar of the Deccan?
155.x: Following Muzaffar Jang’s murder at Rayachoti, Bussy helped establish Salabat Jang as Subedar of the Deccan.
155.tq: Apply the succession sequence and distinguish Salabat Jang from the rival claimants.
xs: After **Muzaffar Jang's** murder at **Rayachoti**, **Bussy** made **Salabat Jang** Subedar — option **(1)**.
Bussy guarded him in **Hyderabad** for seven years.
**Nasir Jang** was Muzaffar's rival; **Chanda Sahib** and **Anwaruddin** were Carnatic rivals.
xa: **1753:** Salabat Jang gave the French the **Northern Circars** to pay Bussy's troops.
**1758-59:** Salabat Jang switched to the **British**.
Bussy helped **Vijayaramaraju** at **Bobbili (1757)**.

155.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the Northern Circars granted by Salabat Jang to meet the expenses of the French army?
155.x: The Northern Circars granted in 1753 comprised Mustafanagar or Kondapalli, Eluru, Rajahmundry and Chicacole or Srikakulam. Nellore was not included in this list.
155.tq: Recall the complete four-part list and identify the outside district.
xs: **Nellore** was NOT among the Circars — option **(4)**.
The **1753** grant: **Mustafanagar (Kondapalli), Eluru, Rajahmundry** and **Chicacole (Srikakulam)**.
xa: It paid for **Bussy's** troops — **peak** of French power in the region.
**1759** treaty gave the British **Machilipatnam, Nizampatnam, Vakal Mannar** and part of Kondapalli.
Other Circars British in **1768**; **Guntur** in **1788**.

155.s:
Consider the following statements about the Battle of Bobbili:
1. It was fought on 24 January 1757.
2. Vijayaramaraju of Vizianagaram received French assistance under Bussy.
3. Ranga Rao of Bobbili was killed in the battle.
4. Vijayaramaraju was later killed by Tandra Papayya.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
155.x: All four statements are correct. The battle took place on 24 January 1757; French forces under Bussy supported Vijayaramaraju, Ranga Rao was killed, and Vijayaramaraju was later killed by Ranga Rao’s brother-in-law Tandra Papayya.
155.tq: Build the answer from the date, alliance, casualty and subsequent retaliation in the same episode.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Bobbili** was fought on **24 Jan 1757**.
**Vijayaramaraju** of Vizianagaram had **French (Bussy)** help; **Ranga Rao** of Bobbili was killed.
Vijayaramaraju was later killed by Ranga Rao's brother-in-law **Tandra Papayya**.
xa: APPSC G2 **2019**: Vijayaramaraju took **French** help.
**Tumnapalem (1756):** Bussy + Vijayaramaraju vs **Jafar Ali**.
Bobbili is a key AP-linked French event.

155.s: The grant of the Northern Circars to the French in 1753 was primarily intended to
o: establish a French capital at Guntur
finance the troops maintained by Bussy
compensate the British for the fall of Machilipatnam
secure French control over the port of Surat
155.x: Salabat Jang granted the Northern Circars to the French to pay for Bussy's troops. The grant represented the high point of French influence in the region.
155.tq: Identify the purpose behind a political-territorial arrangement rather than merely recalling its date.
xs: The **1753** grant was **to pay for Bussy's troops** — option **(2)**.
Granted by **Salabat Jang**; it marked the **peak** of French power in the region.
**Guntur** was never a French capital; it became British in **1788**.
xa: Circars: **Mustafanagar (Kondapalli), Eluru, Rajahmundry, Chicacole**.
Lost after **Chendurthi** and the fall of **Machilipatnam (1759)**.
The **1759** treaty = **first British-Hyderabad agreement**.

155.s: Yanam was transferred to India de facto in 1954 and de jure in:
155.x: Yanam was transferred de facto in 1954 and de jure in 1962.
155.tq: Distinguish the dates of practical transfer and formal legal transfer.
xs: **Yanam** merged de facto in **1954** and **de jure in 1962** — option **(4)**.
**1950** is Chandernagore's plebiscite.
xa: It became part of the UT of **Puducherry**.
Yanam (**1723**) was the **only French territory in Andhra**.
Yanam = last French enclave on Andhra soil.

155.s: After the Battle of Wandiwash and the Treaty of Paris, which of the following best describes the territorial position of the French in India?
o: They transferred all settlements immediately to the British
They retained the entire Northern Circars but lost Pondicherry
They retained only trading enclaves at Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam and Chandernagore
They retained all their former territorial possessions under direct rule
155.x: After Wandiwash and the Treaty of Paris of 1763, the French retained only the trading enclaves of Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam and Chandernagore.
155.tq: Contrast retained enclaves with the wider territorial ambitions of the earlier period.
xs: After **Wandiwash** and the **Treaty of Paris (1763)** the French kept only **trading enclaves** — option **(3)**.
The five: **Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam, Chandernagore**.
They had already lost the Northern Circars (**1759**).
xa: Chandernagore → India by **plebiscite (1950)**.
The other four: de facto **1954**, de jure **1962**.
**Lally** lost Wandiwash (**1760**) to **Eyre Coote**.

155.s: Chandernagore joined India through a plebiscite in:
155.x: Chandernagore went to India by plebiscite in 1950.
155.tq: Distinguish Chandernagore’s plebiscite from the later de facto and de jure transfers of the other enclaves.
xs: **Chandernagore** joined India by **plebiscite** in **1950** — option **(2)**.
The other four enclaves joined de facto in **1954**, de jure **1962**.
xa: Chandernagore: **Shaista Khan's** permission (**1673**); settled **1690**.
The other four formed the UT of **Puducherry**.
Five enclaves remained after the **Treaty of Paris (1763)**.

155.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Danish settlements mentioned in relation to European expansion in India?
o: The Danish company was founded in 1616, Tranquebar was acquired in 1620, and the Danish settlements were sold to the British in 1845
The Danish company was founded in 1616, Serampore was acquired in 1739, and the settlements were sold to France in 1845
The Danish company was founded in 1690, Tranquebar was acquired in 1725, and the settlements were sold in 1763
The Danish company was founded in 1664, Tranquebar was acquired in 1673, and the settlements were sold in 1954
155.x: The Danish company was founded in 1616; Tranquebar was established in 1620, Serampore was another Danish settlement, and the settlements were sold to the British in 1845.
155.tq: Separate the Danish chronology and settlements from the corresponding French dates and possessions.
xs: Danish company **1616**, **Tranquebar (1620)**, sold to the **British in 1845** — option **(1)**.
**Serampore** was the other Danish settlement; they were sold to the British, not France.
xa: The French company came in **1664**.
French enclaves joined India **1950** / **1954** / **1962**.
**Mahe** (**1725**) and **Karaikal** (**1739**) were French, not Danish.

155.s: Which event correctly describes the loss of French possessions in the Third Carnatic War?
o: Forde took Machilipatnam in 1759, after which Salabat Jang gave Machilipatnam, Nizampatnam and part of Kondapalli to the English
Bussy took Nizampatnam in 1753, after which Salabat Jang restored it to the French
Law took Machilipatnam in 1754, after which Dupleix transferred it to England
Clive took Machilipatnam in 1751, after which Muzaffar Jang gave the Circars to the English
155.x: Forde captured Machilipatnam in 1759. Salabat Jang then granted Machilipatnam, Nizampatnam and part of Kondapalli to the English.
155.tq: Use the commander–place–year chain to avoid swapping the two Carnatic wars.
xs: **Forde** took **Machilipatnam (1759)**; **Salabat Jang** then gave **Machilipatnam, Nizampatnam** and part of **Kondapalli** to the English — option **(1)**.
This followed the French defeat at **Chendurthi**.
Clive's **1751** action was the siege of Arcot, not Machilipatnam.
xa: **Vakal Mannar** was also given to the British.
The **1759** treaty = **first British-Hyderabad agreement**.
French power ended **north of the Krishna**, except **Guntur**.

155.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the transfer of the Northern Circars is correct?
o: It was the first French-Hyderabad agreement, and French power south of the Krishna ended except in Guntur.
It was the first British-Mysore agreement, and the French retained all territories north of the Krishna.
It was the second British-Hyderabad agreement, and French power throughout Andhra ended immediately.
It was the first British-Hyderabad agreement, and French power north of the Krishna ended except in Guntur.
155.x: The transfer was the first British-Hyderabad agreement. French power north of the Krishna ended, except in Guntur.
155.tq: Discriminate among similar agreements by checking both the parties and the geographical exception.
xs: It was the **first British-Hyderabad agreement**; French power **north of the Krishna** ended except in **Guntur** — option **(4)**.
The **1759** treaty followed **Chendurthi** and the fall of **Machilipatnam**.
xa: **Salabat Jang** switched to the British in **1758-59**.
Other Circars became British in **1768**; Guntur in **1788**.
The French had got the Circars in **1753**.

155.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The other Northern Circars became British in 1768.
2. Guntur became British in 1788.
3. Guntur became British before the other Circars.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
155.x: The other Circars became British in 1768, while Guntur followed in 1788. Therefore, the statement that Guntur became British earlier is false.
155.tq: Catch the reversed chronological comparison between the general transfer and the later exception.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: the **other Circars** became British in **1768**.
Statement 2 correct: **Guntur** became British in **1788**.
Statement 3 wrong: Guntur came **after** the other Circars.
xa: **1759** treaty ended French power north of the Krishna except **Guntur**.
Circars granted to the French in **1753**: **Mustafanagar, Eluru, Rajahmundry, Chicacole**.
**Colonel Forde** took Machilipatnam (**1759**).

155.s: The French were the only serious European rival to the British in India, but ultimately lost mainly because of:
o: Their refusal to intervene in Indian succession disputes
Lack of commercial settlements and absence of Indian allies
The immediate surrender of Pondicherry without resistance
Lack of naval supremacy and steady state support
155.x: The French challenge weakened because they lacked naval supremacy and consistent state support.
155.tq: Identify the paired structural causes instead of focusing only on an individual battle.
xs: The French lost for want of **naval supremacy** and **steady state support** — option **(4)**.
They did intervene in successions (**Dupleix**) and had allies and settlements, so the other options are wrong.
xa: French = **only serious European rival** to the British.
The company was **state-owned**, **dependent on subsidies**.
Decisive defeat: **Wandiwash (1760)**.

155.s: Which one of the following is the last French enclave on Andhra soil?
155.x: Yanam was the last French enclave on Andhra soil and remained French de facto until 1954 and de jure until 1962.
155.tq: Apply the last-enclave clue to distinguish Yanam from the earlier trading centre at Machilipatnam.
xs: **Yanam** is the **last French enclave on Andhra soil** — option **(3)**.
**Chicacole** and **Rajahmundry** were Northern Circars lost by the French; **Machilipatnam** fell to **Forde (1759)**.
xa: Yanam (**1723**) — Godavari delta; only French territory in Andhra.
Merged de facto **1954**, de jure **1962**.
Part of the UT of **Puducherry**.

155.s: The grant of the Northern Circars to the French in 1753 is regarded as which of the following?
o: The beginning of English power in Bengal
The end of French influence in Hyderabad
The high point of French power in India
The immediate cause of the Battle of Ambur
155.x: The Northern Circars grant in 1753 represented the high point of French power in India.
155.tq: Match the territorial achievement with its broader historical significance.
xs: The **1753** Northern Circars grant marked the **peak of French power** — option **(3)**.
It came from **Salabat Jang** to pay **Bussy's** troops.
**Ambur** (**1749**) came earlier, so the grant could not cause it.
xa: Circars: **Mustafanagar (Kondapalli), Eluru, Rajahmundry, Chicacole (Srikakulam)**.
Lost after **Chendurthi** and the fall of Machilipatnam (**1759**).
AP angle: Machilipatnam, Circars grant (**1753**), Bobbili (**1757**), Yanam.

155.s: Among the major European trading companies in India, the French East India Company was the:
o: Only company to receive a royal charter
155.x: The French East India Company was the last European company to arrive in India; it was founded in 1664.
155.tq: Apply the first/last distinction without confusing the company’s founding date with earlier arrivals.
xs: The French were the **last** European company to arrive — option **(2)**.
They were founded in **1664**, after the Portuguese, Dutch, English and Danes.
xa: Founder: **Colbert**; minister of **Louis XIV**.
First factory: **Surat (1668)**.
Danish company: **1616**.

155.s: The Battle of Bobbili, an Andhra event linked with the French, took place in:
155.x: The Battle of Bobbili was fought in 1757, the same year as Plassey, and is among the AP-linked French events.
155.tq: Bobbili and Plassey share 1757.
xs: **Bobbili** was fought in **1757** (**24 Jan**) — option **(2)**.
**1753** is the Circars grant; **1749** is Ambur; **1761** the British capture of Pondicherry.
xa: **Vijayaramaraju + French (Bussy)** vs **Bobbili Ranga Rao**.
Ranga Rao was killed; Vijayaramaraju later killed by **Tandra Papayya**.
APPSC G2 **2019** asked about French help at Bobbili.

156.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the order of arrival of the European powers in India?
156.x: The Portuguese were the first among these powers to arrive, followed by the Dutch, British, Danish and French. The French arrived last in 1664.
156.tq: Use the first-and-last positions before fixing the middle sequence.
xs: Order of arrival: **Portuguese → Dutch → British → Danish → French** — option **(1)**.
The **French** came **last (1664)**; the Portuguese first (**1498**).
xa: ⚠ The order **in Andhra** is different: the **Dutch** set up the first factory (**Machilipatnam**); the French were **third**.
Danish East India Company: **1616**.
Portuguese were the last to leave (**1961**); Danes left **1845**.

156.s: Who founded the French settlement at Pondicherry in 1673–74?
156.x: Pondicherry was founded as a French headquarters in 1673–74 by Francois Martin.
156.tq: Match the settlement with its founder rather than with a missionary associated with another centre.
xs: **Francois Martin** founded **Pondicherry (1673-74)** as the French HQ — option **(1)**.
**Ziegenbalg** and **Benjamin Schulz** were Danish-Halle missionaries; **William Carey** was of the **Serampore Trio**.
xa: Pondicherry — French; **Chandernagore** — French.
The French were the **last** to arrive (**1664**).
UPPSC **2016** asked Pondicherry–French, Goa–Portuguese, Tranquebar–Danish, Sadras–Dutch.

156.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
156.x: Chinsura was a Dutch settlement, not a Danish one. Pondicherry and Chandernagore were French, while Tranquebar was Danish.
156.tq: Find the settlement whose European power has been swapped with a nearby power.
xs: **Chinsura — Danish** is wrong: **Chinsura (Chinsurah)** was **Dutch** — option **(1)**.
**Pondicherry** and **Chandernagore** were French; **Tranquebar** was Danish.
xa: Danish settlements: **Tranquebar (Tharangambadi)** and **Serampore**.
**Sadras** was also Dutch.
**Goa, Daman, Diu** were Portuguese — taken by India in **1961**.

156.s: Which European power was the third to arrive in Andhra?
156.x: The French were the third European power to arrive in Andhra, although the general order of arrival in India placed them last among the listed powers.
156.tq: Distinguish the regional order in Andhra from the broader Indian order.
xs: The **French** were the **third** Europeans to arrive in **Andhra** — option **(4)**.
⚠ In India overall they were **last (1664)** — the Andhra order is different.
xa: The **Dutch** were first to set up a factory in Andhra (**Machilipatnam**).
All-India order: **Portuguese → Dutch → British → Danish → French**.
**Pondicherry (1673-74)** was the French HQ.

156.s: Which one of the following pairs (settlement - European power) is correctly matched?
156.x: Sadras was Dutch. Tranquebar and Serampore were Danish, and Chandernagore was French.
156.tq: Sadras + Chinsura = Dutch.
xs: **Sadras — Dutch** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Tranquebar** and **Serampore** were **Danish**; **Chandernagore** was **French**.
xa: UPPSC **2016** match: Pondicherry-French, Goa-Portuguese, Tranquebar-Danish, Sadras-Dutch.
**Chinsura** was also Dutch.
**Goa, Daman, Diu** were Portuguese.

156.s:
Consider the following statements about the Danes in India:
1. The Danish East India Company was founded in 1616.
2. Their first settlement, Tranquebar, lies on the Malabar coast.
3. Tranquebar was set up in 1620.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
156.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Danish East India Company was founded in 1616. Statement 2 is wrong: Tranquebar lies near Tanjore on the south-eastern Coromandel coast, not Malabar. Statement 3 is correct: Tranquebar was set up in 1620. So '1 only' misses statement 3, and options with statement 2 are wrong.
156.tq: Danes: company 1616, Tranquebar 1620 (Coromandel), Serampore 1699 (Bengal), sold 1845.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: the **Danish East India Company** was founded in **1616**.
Statement 2 wrong: **Tranquebar** is near **Tanjore** on the south-eastern **Coromandel** coast, not Malabar.
Statement 3 correct: Tranquebar was set up in **1620**.
xa: Second major settlement: **Serampore (1699)** near Calcutta.
Tranquebar = **Tharangambadi**, in **Tamil Nadu**.
Danes sold both to the British in **1845**.

156.s: Which one of the following was the second major Danish settlement in India and the centre of Danish activity in Bengal?
156.x: Serampore, established in 1699 near Calcutta, became the second major Danish settlement and the focus of Danish activity in Bengal.
156.tq: Link the settlement with both its date and regional role.
xs: **Serampore (1699)**, near **Calcutta**, was the second major Danish settlement and focus of **Bengal** activity — option **(1)**.
**Chinsura** was **Dutch**; **Covelong** was an **Ostend Company** post near Madras.
xa: Serampore = **Srirampur**, West Bengal.
The **Serampore Trio** worked from Danish Serampore.
**Serampore College** founded **1818**.

156.s:
Consider the following statements about Danish settlements in India:
1. Tranquebar is presently in Tamil Nadu.
2. Serampore is presently in West Bengal.
3. Balasore is presently in Odisha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
156.x: All three statements are correct. Tranquebar is in Tamil Nadu, Serampore is near Kolkata in West Bengal, and Balasore is in Odisha.
156.tq: Read present-day locations separately from the historical European affiliations.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Tranquebar / Tharangambadi** — **Tamil Nadu**; **Serampore (Srirampur)** — **West Bengal** (near Kolkata).
**Balasore** — **Odisha**.
xa: Danish first settlement: **Tranquebar (1620)**.
Serampore: **1699**.
Sold to the British in **1845** under **Hardinge I**.

156.s: Which of the following best describes the principal historical importance of the Danish settlements in India?
o: Their extensive military conquest of the Deccan
Their Protestant missionary, educational and linguistic work
Their establishment of the first British administrative capital
Their dominant share in Indian maritime commerce
156.x: The commercial impact of the Danish settlements was negligible, but their Protestant missionary, educational and linguistic work was historically important.
156.tq: Choose the option that captures the stated long-term significance rather than commercial size.
xs: The Danes mattered mainly for **Protestant missionary**, educational and linguistic work — option **(2)**.
Their **commercial impact was negligible**.
xa: Legacy: **printing**, **vernacular Bible**, **Serampore College**.
**Danish-Halle Mission (1706)** — earliest sustained Protestant mission in South India.
AP angle: start of **printed Telugu prose**.

156.s: The sale of the Danish settlements in India in 1845 took place under Governor-General:
156.x: The sale of Serampore and Tranquebar to the British in 1845 took place under Governor-General Hardinge I.
156.tq: Use the office-holder trap by distinguishing the Governor-General connected with the transaction.
xs: The **1845** sale took place under Governor-General **Hardinge I** — option **(2)**.
Denmark, in **financial difficulty**, sold **Serampore and Tranquebar** to the British.
xa: It ended the Danish presence in India.
Price: some notes **Rs 1,20,000**, others "Rs **120** lakhs" — learn the **year + buyer**.
The Danes had come in **1616**.

156.s: The Danish-Halle Mission at Tranquebar was founded in 1706 as the earliest sustained Protestant mission in:
156.x: Founded in 1706, the Danish-Halle Mission at Tranquebar was the earliest sustained Protestant mission in South India.
156.tq: Associate the mission’s foundation date with its regional field of activity.
xs: The **Danish-Halle Mission (1706)** at Tranquebar was the earliest sustained **Protestant** mission in **South India** — option **(3)**.
It was founded by **Ziegenbalg** (Danish-German).
xa: Ziegenbalg translated the New Testament into **Tamil**.
**Benjamin Schulz** of the same mission did the first **Telugu** Bible.
⚠ Some notes say "the Dutch" propagated religion from Tranquebar — it was the **Danes**.

156.s: Bartholomaeus Ziegenbalg, associated with the Tranquebar Mission, was a:
o: Danish naval commander working in Telugu
156.x: Ziegenbalg was a German pietist who worked in Tamil at the Tranquebar Mission. He lived from 1682 to 1719.
156.tq: Distinguish the missionary’s nationality, religious background and language from those of later workers.
xs: **Ziegenbalg (1682-1719)** was a **German pietist** working in **Tamil** — option **(2)**.
He founded the **Danish-Halle Mission** and translated the Bible (New Testament) into Tamil.
xa: His method: learn the language, vernacular Bible, schools.
That method became a **template for later missions in Andhra**.
The mission was founded in **1706**.

156.s:
Which of the following was central to Ziegenbalg’s missionary method?
1. Learning the local language
2. Preparing a vernacular Bible
3. Establishing schools
Which of the statements given above are correct?
156.x: Ziegenbalg’s method combined learning the local language, producing a vernacular Bible and establishing schools. This approach later influenced missions in Andhra.
156.tq: Recognise the complete three-part method instead of selecting only its linguistic element.
xs: All three were central — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Ziegenbalg's method: **learn the language**, prepare a **vernacular Bible**, set up **schools**.
xa: This became the **template** for later missions in **Andhra**.
Andhra missions: Lutheran — **Guntur**; Baptist — **Ongole**.
Ziegenbalg worked in **Tamil**.

156.s:
Consider the following statements about Benjamin Schulz:
1. He was the first to translate the Bible into Telugu, completed and published in 1746-47 at Halle.
2. He began the Telugu translation in 1727.
3. He prepared a Tamil grammar and dictionary.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
156.x: Statement 1 is correct: Schulz of the Danish-Halle Mission was the first to translate the Bible into Telugu, completed/published in 1746-47 at Halle (APPSC G2 2019). Statement 2 is correct: he began the translation in 1727. Statement 3 is wrong: he prepared a Telugu grammar and dictionary; it was Ziegenbalg who worked in Tamil. So '1 only' misses statement 2, and options with statement 3 are wrong.
156.tq: Schulz = Telugu (1727 begun, 1746-47 Halle); Ziegenbalg = Tamil.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Schulz** made the **first Telugu Bible**, published **1746-47** at **Halle** (APPSC G2 **2019**).
Statement 2 correct: he began the translation in **1727**.
Statement 3 wrong: he prepared a **Telugu** grammar and dictionary; **Ziegenbalg** worked in Tamil.
xa: Schulz learnt Telugu from **1719** at **Madras, Cuddalore, Pulicat**.
His grammar was a landmark in early **Telugu prose**.
**Subbarayudu (Anandarao)** helped with the Telugu Bible.

156.s:
Subbarayudu, also known as Anandarao, is associated with which of the following?
1. Assistance with the Telugu Bible
2. Running a mission school in Visakhapatnam
3. Writing Vedanta Rasayanam
Which of the statements given above are correct?
156.x: Subbarayudu assisted with the Telugu Bible, ran a mission school in Visakhapatnam and wrote Vedanta Rasayanam.
156.tq: Group the person’s translation, educational and literary contributions before choosing the complete set.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Subbarayudu (Anandarao)** helped with the **Telugu Bible** and ran a mission school in **Visakhapatnam**.
He wrote **Vedanta Rasayanam**.
xa: The Telugu Bible was by **Benjamin Schulz** (**1746-47**).
First Telugu Bible printed in India: **Serampore press (1807-1810)**.
Schulz also wrote a **Telugu grammar + dictionary**.

156.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the Danish and Dutch roles at Tranquebar?
o: The Dutch founded the Danish-Halle Mission at Tranquebar.
The Danes established the Ostend Company at Tranquebar.
The Dutch founded Serampore College at Tranquebar.
The Danes founded the Danish-Halle Mission at Tranquebar.
156.x: The Danish-Halle Mission at Tranquebar was founded by the Danes in 1706. The attribution of this missionary work to the Dutch is incorrect.
156.tq: Resolve the look-alike European-power confusion by matching the mission to its actual sponsor.
xs: The **Danes** founded the **Danish-Halle Mission** at Tranquebar — option **(4)**.
⚠ Some notes say "the Dutch" propagated religion from Tranquebar — it was the **Danes**.
The **Ostend Company** was Austrian; **Serampore College** was in Serampore, not Tranquebar.
xa: The mission was founded in **1706** by **Ziegenbalg**.
Earliest sustained **Protestant** mission in South India.
⚠ The Serampore press too is wrongly called "Dutch" in some notes — it was **Danish** Serampore.

156.s: Who constituted the Serampore Trio?
o: William Carey, Joshua Marshman and William Ward
William Carey, Benjamin Schulz and Bartholomaeus Ziegenbalg
Joshua Marshman, Francois Martin and William Ward
William Ward, Subbarayudu and Benjamin Schulz
156.x: The Serampore Trio consisted of the Baptist missionaries William Carey, Joshua Marshman and William Ward.
156.tq: Match all three names as a missionary group instead of mixing members from the Tranquebar mission.
xs: The **Serampore Trio**: **William Carey, Joshua Marshman, William Ward** — option **(1)**.
They were **Baptists**; **Schulz** and **Ziegenbalg** were of the **Danish-Halle Mission**.
xa: They worked from Danish Serampore to bypass **EIC bans** on missionaries.
Founded **Serampore College (1818)**.
Ran the **Serampore Mission Press**.

156.s: The Serampore Trio worked from Danish Serampore primarily in order to:
o: bypass the early East India Company bans on missionaries
replace Tamil with Persian in missionary education
establish a Dutch trading monopoly in Bengal
156.x: Carey, Marshman and Ward operated from Danish Serampore to bypass the early bans imposed by the East India Company on missionary activity.
156.tq: Identify the cause-and-effect link between the location and missionary activity.
xs: They worked from **Danish Serampore** to **bypass early EIC bans on missionaries** — option **(2)**.
The **Ostend Company** was Austrian; Serampore was Danish, not Dutch.
xa: They translated the Bible into many **vernaculars**.
They led early **social reform + education**.
**Serampore College (1818)**.

156.s: Which one of the following was NOT a major activity associated with the Serampore Mission?
o: Formation of a permanent Danish military empire in southern India
Translation of the Bible into vernacular languages
Operation of the Serampore Mission Press
156.x: The Serampore Mission was associated with printing, vernacular Bible translation, social reform and education. It did not establish a Danish military empire in southern India.
156.tq: Reject the option that changes a missionary institution into a political or military power.
xs: A **Danish military empire** was NOT a Serampore activity — option **(1)**.
The Mission did **vernacular Bible** translation, **social reform and education**, and ran the **Serampore Mission Press**.
xa: The press printed the first **Telugu Bible** in India (**1807-1810**).
**Serampore College** founded **1818**.
Danish legacy = **educational/linguistic**, not commercial.

156.s: The Serampore College was founded by the Serampore Trio in:
156.x: Serampore College was founded by Carey, Marshman and Ward in 1818.
156.tq: Distinguish the college date from the dates of Telugu Bible printing at the Serampore press.
xs: **Serampore College** was founded in **1818** — option **(3)**.
**1807** and **1810** frame the Telugu Bible printing; **1845** is the Danish sale.
xa: Founders: **Carey, Marshman, Ward**.
The Trio were **Baptists**.
Serampore (**1699**) was the Danish Bengal settlement.

156.s: The first Telugu Bible printed in India was produced at the Serampore press during:
156.x: The Telugu Bible was printed at the Serampore press during 1807–1810, making it the first Telugu Bible printed in India.
156.tq: Separate the printing period at Serampore from the earlier translation and publication period at Halle.
xs: The first **Telugu Bible printed in India** came from the **Serampore press (1807-1810)** — option **(1)**.
**1746-47** was **Schulz's** Telugu Bible published at **Halle**; **1727** its start; **1706** the Danish-Halle Mission.
xa: AP angle: start of **printed Telugu prose**.
The press was the **Baptist** mission press in Danish Serampore.
Schulz's Telugu grammar + dictionary — early Telugu prose landmark.

156.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Swedish East India Company — founded in 1616
Danish East India Company — chartered in 1731
156.x: The Ostend Company of the Austrian Netherlands was chartered in 1722. The Swedish East India Company dates from 1731, the Danish East India Company from 1616, and the Danish-Halle Mission from 1706.
156.tq: Match the organisation with its correct date while rejecting swapped dates from nearby institutions.
xs: **Ostend Company — 1722** is correct — option **(1)**.
The **Swedish** company dates from **1731**; the **Danish** from **1616**; the **Danish-Halle Mission** from **1706**.
xa: Ostend Company was of the **Austrian Netherlands**.
Its posts: **Banquibazar** (Bengal) and **Covelong** near Madras.
**1845** is the Danish sale.

156.s: The Ostend Company’s activities in India were suspended within a decade mainly because of:
156.x: The Ostend Company’s Indian activities were suspended within a decade under British-Dutch pressure.
156.tq: Identify the nearby European powers responsible for the pressure rather than regional Indian powers.
xs: The **Ostend Company** was suspended within a decade under **British-Dutch pressure** — option **(1)**.
Its presence was small: posts in Bengal and near Madras only.
xa: Chartered **1722**, from the **Austrian Netherlands**.
Posts: **Banquibazar** (Bengal) and **Covelong** (near Madras).
The **Swedish** company (**1731**) traded mainly with **China**.

156.s:
With regard to the Swedish East India Company, consider the following statements:
1. It was established in 1731.
2. It traded mainly with China.
3. It had a negligible presence in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
156.x: All three statements are correct. The Swedish East India Company was established in 1731, focused mainly on trade with China, and had only a negligible presence in India.
156.tq: Combine the organisation’s date, principal trading area and Indian significance.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The **Swedish East India Company** was set up in **1731**, traded mainly with **China**, and had a **negligible presence in India**.
xa: **Ostend Company:** chartered **1722**; suspended within a decade.
Ostend posts: **Banquibazar** and **Covelong**.
Danish company: **1616**.

156.s: Which one of the following correctly expresses the broad significance of the Danish legacy in India?
o: It was primarily commercial and military.
It was mainly educational, linguistic and missionary.
It was limited to naval warfare against the Portuguese.
It consisted exclusively of territorial expansion in Bengal.
156.x: The Danish legacy was primarily educational and linguistic, reflected in printing, vernacular Bible translation and Serampore College, rather than commercial dominance.
156.tq: Choose the option that correctly contrasts cultural influence with commercial power.
xs: The Danish legacy was **educational, linguistic and missionary** — option **(2)**.
Its **commercial impact was negligible**.
xa: Legacy: **printing**, **vernacular Bible**, **Serampore College**.
**Danish-Halle Mission (1706)** at Tranquebar.
Danes left in **1845**.

156.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Portuguese, Danish and French presence in India is correct?
o: The Portuguese were the first to arrive in 1498 and the last to leave in 1961.
The French arrived in 1498 and were the last to leave in 1961.
The Danes were the first to arrive in 1498 and left in 1961.
The Portuguese arrived in 1664 and the Danes left in 1845.
156.x: The Portuguese arrived first in 1498 and were the last of the listed European powers to leave, in 1961. The Danes left in 1845, while the French were the last to arrive in 1664.
156.tq: Combine the two endpoint dates instead of confusing arrival order with departure order.
xs: The **Portuguese** were **first to arrive (1498)** and **last to leave (1961)** — option **(1)**.
The **Danes** left in **1845**; the **French** were **last to arrive (1664)**.
xa: **Goa, Daman, Diu** were taken by India in **1961**.
Danish company founded **1616**.
The Danes sold Serampore and Tranquebar under **Hardinge I**.

156.s: Following the Tranquebar methods, which Protestant missions became associated with Guntur and Ongole respectively in Andhra?
156.x: Lutheran missions centred on Guntur and Baptist missions on Ongole. The second option reverses them, and the Jesuits were a Catholic order linked with the Portuguese, not with the Tranquebar Protestant tradition.
156.tq: Guntur Lutheran, Ongole Baptist.
xs: **Lutheran — Guntur** and **Baptist — Ongole** — option **(1)**.
Option 2 reverses them.
These Andhra missions followed **Tranquebar methods** (learn the language, vernacular Bible, schools).
xa: **Schulz** (Lutheran, Danish-Halle) made the first **Telugu Bible**.
The **Serampore Trio** were **Baptists**.
AP angle: start of **printed Telugu prose**.

157.s: Which Qutb Shahi ruler permitted the French to establish their factory at Machilipatnam in 1669?
157.x: Abdullah Qutb Shah permitted the French to establish their factory at Machilipatnam in 1669.
157.tq: Apply the ruler–European power matching trap.
xs: **Abdullah Qutb Shah** permitted the French factory at **Machilipatnam (1669)** — option **(3)**.
**Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah** permitted the **Dutch (1605)** and **English (1611)** factories.
xa: The French factory was set up by **Marcara**.
Abdullah Qutb Shah also permitted the **Portuguese** factory (**1670**).
**Yanam (1723)** was the only French territorial possession in Andhra.

157.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the order of establishment of the four European factories at Machilipatnam?
157.x: The order was Dutch in 1605, English in 1611, French in 1669 and Portuguese in 1670.
157.tq: Arrange the events by their dates, using the first and last entries as anchors.
xs: Order of factories at Machilipatnam: **Dutch (1605)**, **English (1611)**, **French (1669)**, **Portuguese (1670)** — option **(1)**.
⚠ The **APPSC 2019 key** makes the **Portuguese** the first Europeans at Machilipatnam (soon after **1498**) — answer by the question's wording.
xa: Dutch and English: permission of **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah**.
French and Portuguese: permission of **Abdullah Qutb Shah**.
The **Dutch** were also first to get the right to **mint coins**.

157.s: The English East India Company's factory at Armagaon was established in 1626. Armagaon is identified with:
157.x: Armagaon was located at Durgarajapatnam, about 35 miles north of Pulicat.
157.tq: Discriminate between similarly situated coastal factories and settlements.
xs: **Armagaon (1626)** is **Durgarajapatnam** — option **(4)**.
It lies **35 miles north of Pulicat**, in old **Nellore district**, now **Tirupati** district.
xa: English factory at Machilipatnam came earlier, in **1611**.
**Madras (1639)** became the English base that later controlled Andhra.
Masulipatnam (**1611**) began the EIC's territorial expansion in the south.

157.s: The East India Company's factory at Masulipatnam in 1611 is significant because it marked the beginning of its:
o: naval monopoly over the Arabian Sea
control over the Bengal textile trade
157.x: The Masulipatnam factory of 1611 marked the beginning of the Company's territorial expansion in the south.
157.tq: Link a historical establishment with its stated wider significance.
xs: The **1611** Masulipatnam factory began the EIC's **territorial expansion in the south** (2026 notes) — option **(4)**.
The **Arabian Sea** monopoly was **Portuguese**, not English.
xa: The English were **2nd** at Machilipatnam, with **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah's** permission.
**Armagaon (1626)** followed.
Machilipatnam's **chintz + diamond** trade drew all four powers.

157.s: According to the APPSC 2019 key, which European power was the first to come to Machilipatnam?
157.x: The APPSC 2019 key names the Portuguese, who came soon after 1498. Some sources instead make the Dutch (factory 1605) first. The English came in 1611 and the French in 1669.
157.tq: APPSC key: Portuguese first at Machilipatnam.
xs: The **APPSC 2019 key** names the **Portuguese**, who came **soon after 1498** — option **(4)**.
⚠ Some notes instead make the **Dutch (1605)** first and the Portuguese last (**1670**) — answer by the question's wording.
The **English** came in **1611** and the **French** in **1669**.
xa: FIRST/LAST: first factory in AP = **Dutch, 1605**; last = **Portuguese, 1670**.
First right to **mint coins** = **Dutch**.
Portuguese decline began with the **Dutch arrival in 1605**.

157.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Policy)
A. Blue Water Policy
B. Spice monopoly and own coins
C. Dadni advances and dubashes

List-II (European power)
1. Portuguese
2. Dutch
3. English

Codes:
a. A-1, B-2, C-3
b. A-2, B-3, C-1
c. A-3, B-1, C-2
d. A-1, B-3, C-2
157.x: The Blue Water Policy belonged to the Portuguese, spice monopoly and own coins to the Dutch, and dadni advances and dubashes to the English.
157.tq: Start from the sure policy–power pair and complete the matching code.
xs: **Blue Water Policy** — **Portuguese** (Francisco de Almeida): control the sea, not land.
**Spice monopoly, own coins, no middlemen** — **Dutch**.
**Dadni advances, dubashes** — **English**.
xa: Dadni = **advance payments to weavers** through local intermediaries.
The Dutch **traded directly** for profit.
The Portuguese held the **Arabian Sea** trade monopoly until the **17th century**.

157.s: The English system of giving dadni advances involved:
o: granting horses to the Deccan rulers
advance payments to weavers through local intermediaries called dubashes
payment of 500 pagodas to the Golconda authorities
direct purchase of spices without any local intermediary
157.x: The English gave dadni advances to weavers through local intermediaries known as dubashes.
157.tq: Distinguish the English commercial practice from Dutch direct trade and Portuguese maritime policy.
xs: **Dadni** meant **advance payments to weavers** through local intermediaries, the **dubashes** — option **(2)**.
**Direct purchase without middlemen** describes the **Dutch** approach.
xa: The English **paid less** and **demanded high quality** → weavers avoided them.
Dutch, Portuguese and French advanced money and **paid fairly**.
Machilipatnam's **chintz** drew all four powers.

157.s: Which statement regarding Portuguese maritime power is correct?
o: The Portuguese held the Arabian Sea trade monopoly until the seventeenth century.
The Portuguese monopoly began only after the Dutch arrival in 1605.
The Portuguese controlled the Arabian Sea trade until the nineteenth century.
The Portuguese never competed with the Dutch in maritime trade.
157.x: The Portuguese held the Arabian Sea trade monopoly until the seventeenth century, and their decline began with the Dutch arrival in 1605.
157.tq: Use the time-limit and cause-of-decline details to reject altered chronology.
xs: The Portuguese held the **Arabian Sea** trade monopoly **until the 17th century** — option **(1)**.
Their **decline** — not their monopoly — began with the **Dutch arrival in 1605**.
xa: **Blue Water Policy:** control the sea, not land.
The Portuguese were the **last (4th)** to set up a Machilipatnam factory (**1670**).
**Abdullah Qutb Shah** permitted that factory.

157.s: The French East India Company was established in 1664 under the initiative of:
157.x: The French Company was established in 1664 under Colbert's initiative.
157.tq: Apply the founder–institution association without confusing later French officials.
xs: The French Company was founded in **1664** under **Colbert** — option **(2)**.
**Marcara** set up the Machilipatnam factory; **Francois Martin** founded Pondicherry; **Bussy** secured the Circars.
xa: **Surat 1668** = first French factory.
**Machilipatnam 1669** with **Abdullah Qutb Shah's** permission.
**Pondicherry 1673-74**.

157.s: Which of the following correctly presents the early French settlements and their dates?
157.x: The French established themselves at Surat in 1668, Machilipatnam in 1669 and Pondicherry during 1673–74.
157.tq: Arrange related settlements by date and eliminate reversed date pairs.
xs: **Surat 1668**, **Machilipatnam 1669**, **Pondicherry 1673-74** — option **(1)**.
**1664** is the year the Company was formed, not Surat.
xa: Machilipatnam was set up by **Marcara**.
Pondicherry by **Francois Martin**.
**Yanam (1723)** was the only French territorial possession in Andhra.

157.s: Yanam was important in the history of French expansion because it was:
o: the place where the English founded Madras
the headquarters of the Dutch in India
the only French territorial possession in Andhra
the first Dutch factory in Andhra
157.x: Yanam, acquired in 1723, was the only French territorial possession in Andhra.
157.tq: Identify the exceptional territorial possession among otherwise commercial settlements.
xs: **Yanam (1723)** was the **only French territorial possession in Andhra** — option **(3)**.
**Madras** was English (**1639**); **Machilipatnam (1605)** was the first Dutch factory.
xa: After **Wandiwash** only **Pondicherry, Karaikal, Yanam, Mahe** + Chandernagore remained French.
First French centre in Andhra: **Machilipatnam (1669)**.
French Company: **1664**, **Colbert**.

157.s: Who defeated Count de Lally at the Battle of Wandiwash in 1760?
157.x: Eyre Coote defeated the French commander Count de Lally at Wandiwash in 1760.
157.tq: Apply the commander–battle trap by distinguishing Eyre Coote from Robert Clive.
xs: **Eyre Coote** beat **Count de Lally** at **Wandiwash (1760)** — option **(4)**.
This marked the **end of French power in India**.
**Almeida** and **Albuquerque** were Portuguese governors.
xa: **Col. Forde** won at **Chandurthi (1758)** and took **Masulipatnam (1759)**.
Remaining French enclaves: **Pondicherry, Karaikal, Yanam, Mahe** + Chandernagore.
**Bussy** had secured the Circars in **1753**.

157.s: Bussy secured the Northern Circars from Salabat Jung in 1753 primarily for:
o: the establishment of a Telugu missionary school
157.x: Bussy obtained the Northern Circars from Salabat Jung in 1753 for maintaining the French troops.
157.tq: Connect a territorial grant with its stated military purpose.
xs: **Bussy** got the **Northern Circars** from **Salabat Jung** in **1753** for the **upkeep of French troops** — option **(2)**.
**Fort Geldria** was Dutch (Pulicat) — unrelated.
xa: **Bobbili War (1757):** **Vijayarama Raju** took Bussy's help.
After **Chandurthi (1758)** and Masulipatnam's fall (**1759**), Salabat Jung switched to the British.
**Wandiwash (1760)** ended French power.

157.s: The Second Carnatic War was fought during which period?
157.x: The Second Carnatic War took place from 1749 to 1754. During this conflict, the British installed Muhammad Ali as the Nawab of the Carnatic.
157.tq: Use the chronological range directly and distinguish the war from the later battles of Chandurthi and Wandiwash.
xs: The **Second Carnatic War** was **1749-1754** — option **(3)**.
The British installed **Muhammad Ali** as **Nawab of the Carnatic**.
xa: **1753:** Bussy secured the **Northern Circars**.
**Wandiwash (1760)**: **Eyre Coote** beat **Lally**.
**Chandurthi (1758):** **Col. Forde** defeated the French.

157.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Bussy obtained the Circars for the French through a grant from Salabat Jung.
2. The grant of the Circars to the French took place in 1753.
3. The grant was made by Muhammad Ali, the Nawab of the Carnatic.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
157.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Bussy secured the Circars for the French through Salabat Jung’s grant in 1753. Statement 3 is false because Muhammad Ali was not the grantor.
157.tq: Identify the correct authority behind the grant and reject the swapped-ruler trap.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statements 1 and 2: **Bussy** secured the Circars through **Salabat Jung's** grant in **1753**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Muhammad Ali** was the British-installed **Nawab of the Carnatic**, not the grantor.
xa: The grant was for the **upkeep of French troops**.
In **1759** Salabat Jung gave **Machilipatnam, Nizampatnam, Vakal Mannar** and part of **Kondapalli** to the British.
**Second Carnatic War:** **1749-1754**.

157.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the political alignment during the Bobbili War of 1757?
o: Muhammad Ali backed Vizianagaram against the British
Salabat Jung backed Bobbili against the French
The British backed Bobbili against Vizianagaram
157.x: In the Bobbili War of 1757, the French supported Vizianagaram. The other alternatives incorrectly change the parties or their alliances.
157.tq: Use the alliance-based trap by matching the correct power with its supported side.
xs: In the **Bobbili War (1757)** the **French** backed **Vizianagaram** — option **(4)**.
**Vijayarama Raju** of Vizianagaram took **Bussy's** help against Bobbili (APPSC **2019**).
xa: **1753:** Bussy got the **Northern Circars**.
**1758:** **Col. Forde** beat the French at **Chandurthi**.
**1759:** Masulipatnam fell to Forde.

157.s: Who defeated the French under Conflans in the Battle of Chandurthi?
157.x: Colonel Forde, who was sent from Bengal, defeated the French forces commanded by Conflans at Chandurthi in 1758.
157.tq: Apply the commander–battle association and avoid confusing Forde with Bussy or Conflans.
xs: **Colonel Forde**, sent from **Bengal**, beat the French under **Conflans** at **Chandurthi (1758)** — option **(2)**.
**Bussy** led the French; **Salabat Jung** and **Muhammad Ali** were Indian rulers.
xa: Forde then took **Masulipatnam (1759)**.
Salabat Jung gave the British **Machilipatnam, Nizampatnam, Vakal Mannar** and part of Kondapalli.
**Wandiwash (1760)** ended French power in India.

157.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Battle of Chandurthi
B. Grant of the Circars to the French
C. Bobbili War
D. Fall of Masulipatnam
157.x: The correct order is the grant of the Circars to the French in 1753, the Bobbili War in 1757, the Battle of Chandurthi in 1758, and the fall of Masulipatnam in 1759.
