Statement 2: Siraj was the **last independent Nawab**.
Statement 3: Siraj **had French support**.
xa: Conspirators inside his army: **Mir Jafar**, **Rai Durlabh**, **Jagat Seth**, **Omichund**, **Manik Chand**.
Loyal: **Mir Madan** + **Mohan Lal**.

164.s: Which of the following was NOT a cause of the conflict between the English East India Company and Siraj-ud-Daulah?
o: The French refusal to obey the Nawab's order to stop fortification
Fortification of Calcutta by the English without the Nawab's consent
Misuse of dastaks by Company servants
Sheltering of the Nawab's enemies by the Company
164.x: The French obeyed the Nawab's order to stop fortification; it was the English who continued fortifying Calcutta without his consent. Misuse of dastaks and sheltering enemies were causes of conflict.
164.tq: Find the reversed statement among otherwise relevant causes.
xs: "The **French refusal** to obey" is NOT a cause — the **French obeyed** his order to stop; the **English did not** — option **(1)**.
Real causes: English **fortified Calcutta without consent**, **misused dastaks**, **sheltered his enemies**.
xa: **Black Hole (June 1756)**: Siraj took **Qasim Bazar** → **Calcutta (Fort William)**.
Governor **Drake** fled to **Fulta**.

164.s: The British used the Black Hole episode primarily as
o: a reason for supporting Mir Madan
a pretext for war against Siraj-ud-Daulah
a justification for restoring the 1717 farman
a settlement mechanism with the French
164.x: The British used the deaths of prisoners in the Black Hole episode as a pretext for launching war against Siraj-ud-Daulah.
164.tq: Connect an event with the political use made of it.
xs: The British used the **Black Hole** as a **pretext for war** against Siraj — option **(2)**.
**Mir Madan** was loyal to Siraj; the **1717 farman** was restored by the **Treaty of Alinagar**.
xa: Prisoners including **Holwell** were shut in a small cell; many died (**June 1756**).
It followed Siraj's capture of **Calcutta (Fort William)**.

164.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the conspiracy surrounding the Battle of Plassey?
o: Mir Madan — principal conspirator against Siraj
Governor Drake — leader of the anti-Company faction
164.x: Mir Jafar, who held the office of Mir Bakshi, was a principal conspirator against Siraj-ud-Daulah. Mir Madan was loyal to Siraj, while Holwell and Drake were associated with the British side.
164.tq: Use the person-office relationship to eliminate swapped roles.
xs: **Mir Jafar — Mir Bakshi** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**Mir Madan** was **loyal** to Siraj, not a conspirator.
**Holwell** was a European prisoner in the Black Hole; **Drake** was the Governor who fled to **Fulta**.
xa: Other conspirators: **Rai Durlabh**, **Jagat Seth**, **Amir Chand (Omichund)**, **Manik Chand**.
Mir Jafar paid **Rs 1.77 crore** on becoming Nawab.

164.s: Following the Battle of Plassey, which one of the following combinations of concessions was obtained by the Company?
o: Kora and Allahabad, together with the Nizamat of Bengal
Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa and control of Awadh
The whole of Bengal without the appointment of a Nawab
Zamindari of the 24 Parganas, duty-free trade and resources to fight the French
164.x: After Plassey, the Company obtained the zamindari of the 24 Parganas, duty-free trade in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, and resources to fight the French.
164.tq: Group the immediate commercial, territorial and strategic results of one event.
xs: After Plassey the Company got the **zamindari of the 24 Parganas**, **duty-free trade** in Bengal, Bihar, Orissa, and **resources to beat the French** — option **(4)**.
**Diwani** and **Awadh's** dependence came after **Buxar**; **Kora and Allahabad** went to **Shah Alam II** in **1765**.
xa: Mir Jafar became Nawab and paid **Rs 1.77 crore**.
Plassey: **puppet Nawab, 24 Parganas**; Buxar: **Diwani**, Awadh dependent.

164.s: Which of the following correctly represents the two periods of Mir Jafar's tenure as Nawab of Bengal?
164.x: Mir Jafar served as Nawab from 1757 to 1760 and again from 1763 to 1765, after the fall of Mir Qasim.
164.tq: Test the two-tenure pattern instead of treating the office as a single continuous term.
xs: Mir Jafar ruled **1757-1760** and again **1763-1765** — option **(4)**.
**1760-63** was **Mir Qasim**; **1756-57** was **Siraj-ud-Daulah**.
xa: First term: after Plassey; removed in **1760** — could not meet Company demands.
Second term: restored after **Mir Qasim's fall**; accepted **limits on his army**; died soon after **Buxar**.

164.s: Mir Jafar's intrigue with which European power led to the Company's victory at Chinsura or Bidara in 1759?
164.x: Mir Jafar plotted with the Dutch against the English, but Clive defeated the Dutch at Chinsura or Bidara in 1759, after which the Dutch left India.
164.tq: Match the Indian political actor with the European ally involved in the intrigue.
xs: Mir Jafar plotted with the **Dutch**; Clive beat them at **Chinsura/Bidara (1759)** — option **(4)**.
After this the **Dutch left India**.
xa: Mir Jafar was removed in **1760** — he could not meet **Company demands**.
Pension: **Rs 15,000 a month** (some notes print "Rs 1,500 annually").

164.s: Which one of the following was a reason for Mir Jafar's removal from office in 1760?
o: He surrendered Bengal to the Dutch.
He refused to accept the grant of Diwani to the Company.
He could not meet the Company's demands.
164.x: Mir Jafar was removed in 1760 because he could not meet the increasing demands of the Company.
164.tq: Identify the stated cause rather than a later consequence of his rule.
xs: Mir Jafar was removed in **1760** because he **could not meet the Company's demands** — option **(4)**.
He was a **conspirator** against Siraj at Plassey, not a supporter; **Diwani** was granted only in **1765**.
xa: He got a pension of **Rs 15,000 a month**.
**Vansittart** put **Mir Qasim**, his son-in-law, on the throne in **1760**.

164.s: During his second tenure, Mir Jafar accepted which limitation imposed by the Company?
o: The transfer of his capital to Calcutta
A ban on collecting land revenue
A limit on the size of his army
164.x: During his second tenure, Mir Jafar accepted restrictions on the size of his army, reflecting the Company's control over Bengal's political and military affairs.
164.tq: Identify the concession that directly reduced the Nawab's military autonomy.
xs: In his second term, Mir Jafar **accepted limits on the size of his army** — option **(3)**.
Second term: **1763-1765**, restored after **Mir Qasim's fall**.
xa: He was the Nawab at the time of **Buxar** (**October 1764**).
His son **Najm-ud-Daula** became Nawab from **1765**.

164.s: Mir Qasim was placed on the throne of Bengal in 1760 by
164.x: Mir Qasim, the son-in-law of Mir Jafar, was placed on the throne in 1760 by Governor Vansittart.
164.tq: Use the ruler–appointing authority pair rather than confusing the successive Governors of Bengal.
xs: **Governor Vansittart** put **Mir Qasim** on the throne in **1760** — option **(1)**.
Mir Qasim was **Mir Jafar's son-in-law**.
**Warren Hastings** came in **1772**; **Clive** returned in **May 1765**.
xa: **Treaty of 1760**: ceded **Burdwan, Midnapur and Chittagong**.
He moved the capital **Murshidabad to Monghyr (Munger), Bihar**.

164.s:
Under the Treaty of 1760, which of the following concessions were made by Mir Qasim?
1. Cession of Burdwan, Midnapur and Chittagong
2. Half share of the Sylhet chunam trade
3. Payment of Rs 5 lakh for the Company’s southern wars
4. Annual tribute of Rs 26 lakh to Shah Alam II
Which of the statements given above are correct?
164.x: The Treaty of 1760 involved the cession of the three districts, a half share in the Sylhet chunam trade and Rs 5 lakh for the Company’s southern wars. The Rs 26 lakh annual tribute belonged to the later Diwani settlement.
164.tq: Separate the monetary and territorial terms of the 1760 treaty from the Diwani tribute.
xs: Concessions **1, 2 and 3** belong to the **Treaty of 1760** — option **(1)**.
He ceded **Burdwan, Midnapur and Chittagong**, gave **half of Sylhet chunam trade**, and paid **Rs 5 lakh** for southern wars.
Item 4 is wrong: the **Rs 26 lakh** tribute to **Shah Alam II** came with the **Diwani (1765)**.
xa: Mir Qasim was put on the throne by **Vansittart**.
He **abolished all internal trade duties** (APPSC G2 2017).

164.s: Which of the following best describes Mir Qasim’s administrative measures after he became Nawab?
o: He modernised the army and reformed the finances of Bengal.
He restored all internal duties and ended the use of revenue administration.
He shifted the capital to Delhi and surrendered Bengal to Awadh.
He disbanded the army and transferred financial control to the Mughal Emperor.
164.x: Mir Qasim moved the capital to Monghyr and undertook army modernisation and financial reforms.
164.tq: Select the option containing the historically connected administrative measures without an invented transfer of power.
xs: Mir Qasim **modernised the army** and **improved Bengal's finances** — option **(1)**.
He **abolished** (not restored) internal duties, and moved the capital to **Monghyr**, not Delhi.
xa: Capital shift: **Murshidabad to Monghyr (Munger), Bihar**.
Defeated in **1763**, he fled to **Awadh**.

164.s: Why did the abolition of internal trade duties by Mir Qasim lead to conflict with the Company’s servants?
o: It prevented Indian merchants from trading outside Bengal.
It made Indian merchants compete on equal terms with English merchants and removed the advantage derived from dastaks.
It transferred the Company’s Diwani rights to the Nawab.
It imposed a new uniform duty exclusively on English merchants.
164.x: By abolishing internal duties, Mir Qasim placed Indian merchants on an equal footing with English merchants and removed the advantage that Company servants obtained through misuse of dastaks.
164.tq: Trace the economic consequence of equal trade treatment to identify the cause of the conflict.
xs: Abolishing internal duties made **Indian merchants pay the same as the English**, ending the **dastak** advantage — option **(2)**.
**Company servants**, angry at lost **private-trade profits**, went to war.
xa: Asked in **APPSC G2 2017**.
Mir Qasim was **defeated in 1763** and fled to **Awadh**.

164.s: The immediate result of the Company’s conflict with Mir Qasim in 1763 was that he
o: was restored to the throne of Bengal
surrendered directly to Shah Alam II at Delhi
fled to Awadh after being defeated
joined the British and became Governor of Bengal
164.x: The Company defeated Mir Qasim in 1763, after which he fled to Awadh and later became one of the allies against the British at Buxar.
164.tq: Link the defeat year with the correct subsequent movement of the defeated ruler.
xs: Mir Qasim was **defeated in 1763** and **fled to Awadh** — option **(3)**.
**Mir Jafar**, not Mir Qasim, was **restored** in **1763**.
xa: At **Buxar (1764)** he fought as the **deposed Nawab of Bengal** alongside **Shuja-ud-Daulah** and **Shah Alam II**.
Mir Qasim ruled **1760-63**.

164.s: Which Nawab of Bengal shifted his capital from Murshidabad to Monghyr and abolished all internal trade duties?
164.x: Mir Qasim (1760-63) moved the capital to Monghyr (Munger) in Bihar and abolished all inland duties, so Indian merchants paid the same as the English. Mir Jafar was the puppet after Plassey, Siraj lost Plassey, and Najm-ud-Daula was Nawab from 1765 in name only.
164.tq: Mir Qasim = Monghyr + abolished internal duties (APPSC G2 2017)
xs: **Mir Qasim** moved the capital to **Monghyr (Munger)** and **abolished all internal trade duties** — option **(2)**.
**Mir Jafar** was a **puppet**; **Siraj** lost Plassey; **Najm-ud-Daula** kept the **Nizamat** in name only from **1765**.
xa: He also **modernised the army**.
He was **Mir Jafar's son-in-law**.

164.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Leader)
 a. Mir Qasim
 b. Shuja-ud-Daulah
 c. Shah Alam II
 d. Hector Munro

List-II (Position or role at Buxar)
 i. British commander
 ii. Mughal Emperor
 iii. Deposed Nawab of Bengal
 iv. Nawab of Awadh

Which of the following is the correct code?
164.x: Mir Qasim was the deposed Nawab of Bengal, Shuja-ud-Daulah was Nawab of Awadh, Shah Alam II was the Mughal Emperor, and Hector Munro commanded the British forces.
164.tq: Start with the commander–role pair and then match the three allied leaders by position.
xs: **a–iii, b–iv, c–ii, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Mir Qasim** — deposed Nawab of Bengal; **Shuja-ud-Daulah** — Nawab of Awadh.
**Shah Alam II** — Mughal emperor; **Major Hector Munro** — British commander.
xa: Buxar: **October 1764** (22-23 Oct), Bihar.
The Nawab of Bengal at the time was **Mir Jafar** (restored **1763**).

164.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the consequences of the Battle of Buxar:
1. Shuja-ud-Daulah fled and subsequently sought help from the Rohillas and the Marathas.
2. He ultimately surrendered.
3. Awadh and Allahabad were occupied by the British.
4. Shah Alam II joined the English.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
164.x: All four statements describe the consequences recorded after the English victory at Buxar: Shuja fled, sought assistance, surrendered, Awadh and Allahabad were occupied, and Shah Alam II joined the English.
164.tq: Check each consequence separately before selecting the comprehensive combination.
xs: All four statements are correct — **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
**Shuja** fled, sought **Rohilla** + **Maratha** help, then **surrendered**.
**Awadh + Allahabad** were occupied; **Shah Alam joined the English**.
xa: Buxar was a **decisive English win** under **Major Hector Munro**.
**Most decisive battle:** **Buxar** (UPPSC 2016).

164.s: Who was the Nawab of Bengal at the time of the Battle of Buxar (October 1764)?
164.x: Mir Jafar had been restored in 1763 and was Nawab during Buxar. Mir Qasim fought at Buxar as the deposed ex-Nawab, Siraj died after Plassey (1757), and Najm-ud-Daula became Nawab only in 1765.
164.tq: Buxar: Mir Qasim = ex-Nawab; Mir Jafar = sitting Nawab
xs: **Mir Jafar**, restored in **1763**, was Nawab during Buxar — option **(4)**.
**Mir Qasim** fought as the **deposed** Nawab; **Siraj** was executed after **Plassey**.
**Najm-ud-Daula** became Nawab only from **1765**.
xa: Mir Jafar's second term: **1763-1765**; he died soon after Buxar.
In this term he accepted **limits on the size of his army**.

164.s: The Battle of Buxar was fought on 22 October in which year?
164.x: The Battle of Buxar was fought at Buxar in Bihar on 22 October 1764; some accounts place the engagement across 22–23 October.
164.tq: Distinguish the battle year from the subsequent year of the Treaty of Allahabad and Diwani grant.
xs: **Buxar** was fought in **October 1764** (22-23 Oct) — option **(3)**.
**1757** = **Plassey**; **1760** = Mir Qasim's accession; **1765** = **Treaty of Allahabad**.
xa: Place: **Buxar** (Bihar).
Chronology (UPPSC 2016): **Buxar (Oct 1764) → Clive returns (May 1765) → Allahabad (1765) → Warren Hastings (1772)**.

164.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Battle of Buxar from the Battle of Plassey?
o: Buxar occurred before Plassey and established Mir Qasim’s rule.
Buxar ended in a defeat of the English and restoration of Shah Alam II’s independent rule.
Buxar was won through open fighting, whereas Plassey is associated with treachery.
Buxar was fought against the French, whereas Plassey was fought against the Marathas.
164.x: Buxar was a decisive victory achieved through fighting, unlike Plassey, which is traditionally associated with treachery. Buxar strengthened British control in eastern and northern India.
164.tq: Use the contrast in the character of the two victories rather than their common British outcome.
xs: **Buxar** was an **open military victory**, while **Plassey** was won by **treachery** — option **(3)**.
Buxar (**1764**) came after Plassey (**1757**) and was an **English win**.
Buxar's enemies were **Bengal + Awadh + Mughal Emperor** — not the French or Marathas.
xa: Plassey laid the **foundation**; Buxar made the British **masters** of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
Plassey was called "**a transaction**", won through conspiracy.

164.s: The principal historical significance of the English victory at Buxar was that it
o: made the British masters of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa and a major power in North India
established French supremacy over the eastern provinces
transferred the capital of Bengal from Munger to Murshidabad
ended the Company’s authority in Bengal and restored the Nawab’s independence
164.x: The victory at Buxar made the British masters of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa and established them as a major power in North India.
164.tq: Choose the broad political consequence rather than a local administrative change or an opposite outcome.
xs: Buxar made the British **masters of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa** and a **major power in North India** — option **(1)**.
It was a **decisive English win**, not a French or Nawab gain.
xa: It led to the **Diwani of Bengal, Bihar, Orissa**; **Awadh made dependent**.
**Most decisive battle:** **Buxar** (UPPSC 2016).

164.s: Which one of the following was a consequence specifically associated with the Battle of Buxar rather than the Battle of Plassey?
o: The Company restored the privileges of the 1717 farman.
The Company obtained the zamindari of the 24 Parganas.
Mir Jafar became Nawab of Bengal.
The Company secured the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa and made Awadh dependent.
164.x: Buxar led to the grant of Diwani over Bengal, Bihar and Orissa and reduced Awadh to a dependent position. The other consequences relate to Plassey or the Treaty of Alinagar.
164.tq: Separate the consequences of two closely connected events.
xs: **Diwani of Bengal, Bihar, Orissa** and a **dependent Awadh** came from **Buxar** — option **(4)**.
**1717 farman privileges** were restored at **Alinagar (Feb 1757)**.
**24 Parganas** and **Mir Jafar as Nawab** were results of **Plassey**.
xa: Buxar's enemy: **Bengal + Awadh + Mughal Emperor** together.
Plassey's result: **puppet Nawab**, **24 Parganas**.

164.s: The grant of the Diwani rights to the English East India Company was formally made on which date?
164.x: The Diwani was formally granted to the Company on 12 August 1765 under the Treaty of Allahabad.
164.tq: Use the exact-date distinction between the Battle of Buxar and the grant of Diwani.
xs: The Diwani was formally granted on **12 August 1765** — option **(1)**.
**22 October 1764** is **Buxar**.
xa: Grantor: **Shah Alam II** under the **Treaty of Allahabad**; recipient: Company under **Robert Clive**.
Year **1765** asked in **APPSC G2 2017**.
Tribute: **Rs 26 lakh** a year to the Emperor.

164.s: The annual tribute associated with the grant of Diwani to the East India Company was payable to the Mughal Emperor at the rate of
164.x: The Company agreed to pay an annual tribute of Rs 26 lakh to Shah Alam II.
164.tq: Distinguish the fixed annual tribute from other monetary payments connected with Bengal politics.
xs: The tribute was **Rs 26 lakh a year** to **Shah Alam II** — option **(2)**.
**Rs 5 lakh** was Mir Qasim's **1760** payment; **Rs 50 lakh** was Shuja-ud-Daulah's **war indemnity**.
xa: Shah Alam II became a **Company pensioner** — the **first Mughal ruler** to do so.
**Warren Hastings (1772)** **stopped the tribute** to Shah Alam.

164.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Diwani granted to the East India Company?
o: The right to collect revenue and administer civil justice in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa
The right to appoint the Mughal Emperor and control Delhi
The right to conduct foreign affairs on behalf of Awadh
The right to administer criminal justice and maintain the police in Bengal alone
164.x: Diwani comprised revenue collection and civil justice in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
164.tq: Discriminate between Diwani functions and the Nizamat functions retained by the Nawab.
xs: **Diwani** = **revenue collection and civil justice** in **Bengal, Bihar and Orissa** — option **(1)**.
**Criminal justice and police** form the **Nizamat**, kept by the Nawab.
xa: Granted by **Shah Alam II** under the **Treaty of Allahabad (1765)**.
**Naib diwans**: **Muhammad Reza Khan** (Bengal) + **Raja Shitab Rai** (Bihar).

164.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Dual Government in Bengal:
1. The Company held the Diwani.
2. The Nawab retained the Nizamat.
3. The arrangement continued from 1765 to 1772.
4. The Mughal Emperor ceased to be the nominal sovereign immediately after its introduction.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
164.x: The Company held revenue and civil justice, while the Nawab retained law and order and criminal justice during 1765–1772. The Mughal Emperor remained the nominal sovereign, so statement 4 is false.
164.tq: Find the single wrong statement by checking the retained nominal status of the Mughal sovereign.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statements 1-2: Company = **Diwani**; Nawab = **Nizamat**.
Statement 3: Dual Government lasted **1765-72**.
Statement 4 wrong: the **Mughal emperor** stayed the **nominal sovereign**.
xa: Criticism: **power without responsibility** → **1770 Bengal famine** (**John Cartier**'s time).
**Warren Hastings (1772)** ended it.

164.s: The expression “power without responsibility” in the context of Bengal referred to the arrangement under which
o: the Company abandoned all administrative functions in Bengal
the Nawab collected revenue but the Company controlled the army
the Company controlled revenue while the Nawab formally retained administration of law and order
the Mughal Emperor directly administered Bengal through the Company
164.x: Under the Dual Government, the Company enjoyed the financial power of Diwani, while the Nawab formally retained Nizamat and associated responsibilities.
164.tq: Apply the division of Diwani and Nizamat to identify who possessed power and who bore formal responsibility.
xs: "**Power without responsibility**" = **Dual Government**: Company held **revenue** (Diwani), Nawab kept **law and order** (Nizamat) — option **(3)**.
The Company did not abandon administration; the Nawab did not collect revenue.
xa: Period **1765-72**; ended by **Warren Hastings (1772)**.
Result blamed for the **1770 Bengal famine**.

164.s: The Treaty of Allahabad was concluded in 1765 by Robert Clive after he had returned as
o: Governor of Madras for the first time
Governor of Bengal for the second time
Resident at the court of Shah Alam II
Governor-General of India for the first time
164.x: Robert Clive returned as Governor of Bengal for the second time in May 1765 and concluded the Treaty of Allahabad later that year.
164.tq: Link the treaty to the office and tenure of the British negotiator.
xs: Clive signed Allahabad after returning as **Governor of Bengal for the second time** (**May 1765**) — option **(2)**.
His governorships: **1758-60** and **1765-67**.
xa: Other parties: **Shah Alam II** + **Shuja-ud-Daulah**.
Clive = "**founder of the British Empire in India**" (APPSC 2019).

164.s: Which of the following was a term imposed on Shuja-ud-Daula under the Treaty of Allahabad?
o: He received Kora and Allahabad from the Emperor.
He paid an indemnity of Rs 50 lakh and received the remainder of his dominions back.
He surrendered all his territories to the Company.
He obtained the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
164.x: Shuja-ud-Daula paid a war indemnity of Rs 50 lakh and recovered the rest of his dominions, while Kora and Allahabad were given to Shah Alam II.
164.tq: Separate the terms granted to Awadh from those granted to the Mughal Emperor.
xs: **Shuja-ud-Daulah** paid a **Rs 50 lakh** war indemnity and got his **dominions back** — option **(2)**.
**Kora and Allahabad** went to **Shah Alam II**, not Shuja.
The **Diwani** went to the **Company**.
xa: Awadh became a **buffer state** under Company protection.
**Balwant Singh** of **Banaras** was confirmed in his estate.

164.s: Under the Treaty of Allahabad, Awadh was converted into
o: a buffer state under Company protection
a Mughal jagir under Shah Alam II
164.x: Awadh was restored to Shuja-ud-Daula, subject to its becoming a buffer state under the protection of the Company.
164.tq: Infer the political status from the treaty's territorial and protective arrangements.
xs: Awadh became a **buffer state under Company protection** — option **(1)**.
Shuja-ud-Daulah got his dominions back **except Kora and Allahabad**.
xa: He paid a war indemnity of **Rs 50 lakh**.
After Buxar, **Awadh + Allahabad** had been occupied by the English.

164.s: Which treaty followed the Battle of Buxar (1764)?
164.x: The Treaty of Allahabad (1765) followed Buxar and gave the Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa. Salbai (1782) ended the First Anglo-Maratha War, Bassein (1802) was the Peshwa's subsidiary treaty, and Sugauli (1816) ended the Anglo-Nepal War.
164.tq: After Buxar = Allahabad
xs: The **Treaty of Allahabad (1765)** followed Buxar — option **(2)**.
**Salbai** belongs to **1782**; the notes stress **Allahabad**, not **Salbai, Bassein or Sugauli**.
xa: It gave the **Diwani of Bengal, Bihar, Orissa** for **Rs 26 lakh** a year.
Treaty chronology: **Allahabad (1765)**, **Madras (1769)**, **Salbai (1782)**, **Mangalore (1784)**.

164.s: Who among the following was the son of Mir Jafar and became Nawab of Bengal from 1765?
164.x: Najm-ud-Daula, the son of Mir Jafar, became Nawab of Bengal from 1765.
164.tq: Use the family relationship and accession year together to identify the ruler.
xs: **Najm-ud-Daula**, **son of Mir Jafar**, became Nawab from **1765** — option **(1)**.
**Muhammad Reza Khan** was the **Naib Subahdar**; **Balwant Singh** was zamindar of **Banaras**; **Mir Qasim** was Mir Jafar's son-in-law.
xa: Under the **1765 treaty** he handed **defence + administration** to the Naib Subahdar.
He kept the **Nizamat in name only**.

164.s: Under the arrangement made in 1765, the defence and administration of Bengal were handed over to
o: the Nawab of Awadh through the buffer-state system
a Company-nominated Naib Subahdar, Muhammad Reza Khan
Mir Jafar as hereditary military governor
the Mughal Emperor through the Diwan
164.x: Najm-ud-Daula handed defence and administration to the Company-nominated Naib Subahdar, Muhammad Reza Khan, while retaining the Nizamat only nominally.
164.tq: Ask which authority actually exercised power rather than which office remained nominally.
xs: Defence and administration went to a **Company-nominated Naib Subahdar, Muhammad Reza Khan** — option **(2)**.
**Najm-ud-Daula** was left with the **Nizamat** in name only.
xa: **Muhammad Reza Khan** was also **naib diwan** of Bengal; **Raja Shitab Rai** of Bihar.
**Nizamat** = police, criminal justice / law and order.

164.s: Which development in 1772 is associated with Warren Hastings?
o: Restoration of Mir Jafar for a second tenure
Formation of Awadh as a buffer state
End of Mughal pretence and rule by right of conquest
Grant of the Diwani to Shah Alam II
164.x: In 1772, Warren Hastings ended the Mughal pretence and ruled Bengal by right of conquest.
164.tq: Match the administrator with the institutional change associated with his tenure.
xs: **Warren Hastings (1772)** "**tore the mask of Mughal sovereignty**" and ruled **by right of conquest** — option **(3)**.
He ended the **Dual Government** (**1765-72**).
xa: He **stopped the tribute** to Shah Alam.
**Awadh** became a buffer state in **1765**, not **1772**.

164.s:
Consider the following statements about Robert Clive:
1. He is called the 'founder of the British Empire in India'.
2. William Pitt called him a 'heaven-born general'.
3. He was Governor of Bengal only once, during 1765-67.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
164.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Clive is called the founder of the British Empire in India (APPSC 2019), and William Pitt called him a 'heaven-born general'. Statement 3 is wrong: he was Governor of Bengal twice, 1758-60 and 1765-67. So 1 and 2 only.
164.tq: Clive: two terms (1758-60, 1765-67)
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: "**founder of the British Empire in India**" (APPSC 2019; BPSC 2020).
Statement 2: **William Pitt** called him a "**heaven-born general**".
Statement 3 wrong: he was Governor of Bengal **twice** — **1758-60** and **1765-67**.
xa: Record: **Arcot (1751)**, **Chandannagar (1757)**, **Plassey (1757)**, **Condore (1758)**.
Treaty of Allahabad was signed in his **second term**.

164.s:
Arrange the following treaties in chronological order:
A. Treaty of Mangalore
B. Treaty of Allahabad
C. Treaty of Salbai
D. Treaty of Madras associated with Haidar Ali
164.x: The treaties were concluded in the order Allahabad (1765), Madras (1769), Salbai (1782) and Mangalore (1784).
164.tq: Arrange the treaties by their years, using the earliest and latest as anchors.
xs: The order is **B, D, C, A** — option **(1)**.
**Allahabad (1765)** → **Madras with Haidar Ali (1769)** → **Salbai (1782)** → **Mangalore (1784)**.
xa: Allahabad followed **Buxar (Oct 1764)**.
**Warren Hastings** became Governor in **1772**.

164.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Nawab)
A. Shuja-ud-din
B. Sarfaraz Khan
C. Alivardi Khan
D. Siraj-ud-Daulah

List-II (Description)
1. Killed by Alivardi
2. Killed Shaukat Jang at Manihari
3. Too powerful to heed court orders favouring the English in 1735
4. Stopped both companies from fortifying Calcutta and Chandannagar
164.x: Shuja-ud-din was too powerful to heed the court orders of 1735; Sarfaraz Khan was killed by Alivardi; Alivardi stopped the fortifications; and Siraj-ud-Daulah killed Shaukat Jang at Manihari.
164.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes containing mismatched descriptions.
xs: **Shuja-ud-din** — too powerful to heed court orders (**1735**); **Sarfaraz Khan** — killed by Alivardi.
**Alivardi Khan** — stopped fortification of **Calcutta and Chandannagar**; **Siraj** — killed **Shaukat Jang** at **Manihari**.
xa: **Murshid Quli Khan** = last Subahdar appointed by the Mughal emperor (**UPPSC 2021**).
**Siraj-ud-Daulah** was **Alivardi's grandson**.

164.s:
Consider the following statements about Alivardi Khan:
1. He served as Deputy Governor of Bihar.
2. He permitted both the English and French companies to fortify Calcutta and Chandannagar.
3. He ruled Bengal during 1740–1756.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
164.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because Alivardi Khan stopped both companies from fortifying Calcutta and Chandannagar.
164.tq: Find the reversed action in the statement about fortification.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1: **Alivardi Khan** was **Deputy Governor of Bihar**.
Statement 2 wrong: he **stopped** both companies fortifying **Calcutta and Chandannagar**.
Statement 3: he ruled **1740-56**.
xa: He came to power after killing **Sarfaraz Khan**.
Successor: grandson **Siraj-ud-Daulah** (**1756-57**).

164.s: Which of the following correctly describes Mir Qasim?
o: He was the last Subahdar appointed by the Mughal emperor.
He stopped both companies from fortifying Calcutta and Chandannagar.
He was a reformer who ruled Bengal from 1760 to 1763 and fought at Buxar.
He was killed by Alivardi at the Battle of Manihari.
164.x: Mir Qasim was regarded as a reformer, ruled Bengal from 1760 to 1763 and fought at the Battle of Buxar.
164.tq: Use the ruler–role–period association to distinguish Mir Qasim from other Nawabs.
xs: **Mir Qasim** was a **reformer**, ruled **1760-63** and **fought at Buxar** — option **(3)**.
The **last Mughal-appointed Subahdar** was **Murshid Quli Khan**; **Alivardi** stopped the fortifications.
**Siraj** killed **Shaukat Jang** at **Manihari**; Alivardi killed **Sarfaraz**.
xa: Mir Qasim moved the capital to **Monghyr** and **abolished internal trade duties**.
At Buxar he allied with **Shuja-ud-Daulah** and **Shah Alam II**.

164.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Treaty of Allahabad
B. Warren Hastings becomes Governor of Bengal
C. Battle of Buxar
D. Clive returns to Bengal as Governor
164.x: Buxar (October 1764), Clive's return (May 1765), the Treaty of Allahabad (1765) and Warren Hastings as Governor (1772): C, D, A, B. The other orders put Allahabad before Clive's return, Clive before Buxar, or Hastings before Allahabad.
164.tq: UPPSC 2016: Buxar -> Clive back -> Allahabad -> Hastings
xs: The order is **C, D, A, B** — option **(1)**.
**Buxar (Oct 1764)** → **Clive returns (May 1765)** → **Treaty of Allahabad (1765)** → **Warren Hastings Governor (1772)**.
This chronology was asked in **UPPSC 2016**.
xa: Allahabad was signed in Clive's **second term** (**1765-67**); his first was **1758-60**.
Hastings ended the **Dual Government (1765-72)** and **stopped the tribute** to Shah Alam.

164.s: Which Nawab of Bengal was the last Subahdar of Bengal appointed by the Mughal Emperor?
164.x: Murshid Quli Khan (1717-27) was the last Subahdar appointed by the Mughal Emperor (UPPSC 2021 key). Shuja-ud-din, Alivardi Khan and Mir Jafar came later; Alivardi seized power and Mir Jafar was installed by the Company.
164.tq: Last Mughal-appointed = Murshid Quli
xs: **Murshid Quli Khan** was the **last Subahdar of Bengal appointed by the Mughal emperor** — option **(2)**.
This is the **UPPSC 2021** key.
**Shuja-ud-din**, **Alivardi Khan** and **Mir Jafar** came later; Mir Jafar was a **puppet** after Plassey.
xa: Murshid Quli **asked the English to pay customs duties**.
**Alivardi Khan** was **Deputy Governor of Bihar** and killed **Sarfaraz Khan**.

164.s: Which one of the following correctly explains the relationship between the Dual Government and the Bengal Famine of 1770?
o: The Dual Government combined revenue collection and administrative responsibility in one authority, preventing famine relief.
The Dual Government ended Company revenue collection and restored the Nawab's fiscal authority.
The Dual Government separated power from responsibility, while revenue was squeezed as the famine spread.
The Dual Government was introduced after the famine solely to regulate private European trade.
164.x: The Dual Government separated power from responsibility. At the same time, revenue was squeezed even as the famine spread, contributing to the disastrous conditions.
164.tq: Apply the power–responsibility distinction to the famine context.
xs: The **Dual Government** separated **power from responsibility** while revenue was squeezed as the famine spread — option **(3)**.
It did not combine revenue and administration; Company = **Diwani**, Nawab = **Nizamat**.
It ran **1765-72**, so it came **before** the **1770 Bengal famine**, not after.
xa: The famine came in **John Cartier**'s time.
**Warren Hastings (1772)** ended the Dual Government.

164.s: The combined significance of the Battles of Buxar and the Treaty of Allahabad was that they:
o: restored the independent authority of the Mughal Emperor over Bengal and Bihar
transferred the administration of Bengal entirely to the French
ended the Company's right to collect revenue in eastern India
made the Company the real ruler of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa and reduced the Mughal Emperor to a pensioner
164.x: Buxar and Allahabad made the Company the real ruler of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, while the Mughal Emperor became its pensioner.
164.tq: Identify the broad political consequence rather than an individual military event.
xs: **Buxar** + **Allahabad** made the Company the **real ruler of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa** and the **Mughal Emperor its pensioner** — option **(4)**.
They gave the Company the **Diwani**, not ended its revenue rights.
xa: **Shah Alam II** = **first Mughal ruler** to become a Company **pensioner**.
Buxar made the British a **major power in North India**; **Awadh** became a **buffer state**.

164.s: Which one of the following best describes the economic significance of the Company's control over Bengal's revenue?
o: It made the Company dependent on subsidies from the Mughal Emperor.
It enabled the Company to abandon all later military expansion.
It transformed the Company from a territorial power into a purely commercial body.
It turned the Company from a trader into a territorial power and financed its later conquests.
164.x: Control over Bengal's revenue transformed the Company from a trader into a territorial power and provided funds for its subsequent conquests.
164.tq: Trace the stated cause-and-effect link from revenue control to territorial expansion.
xs: Control of Bengal's revenue turned the Company from **trader → territorial power** and **paid for later conquests** — option **(4)**.
Option (3) reverses the direction of the change.
xa: The Diwani came with an annual tribute of **Rs 26 lakh** to the Emperor.
Criticism: **Dual Government** separated power from responsibility → **1770 Bengal famine**.

165.s: Who introduced the system of Dual Government in Bengal?
165.x: Robert Clive introduced the Dual Government in Bengal during his second term as Governor of Bengal from 1765 to 1767.
165.tq: Use the direct architect–institution link and distinguish Clive from Hastings.
xs: **Robert Clive** was the **architect** of the Dual Government — option **(1)**.
He was Governor of Bengal for the 2nd term, **1765-67**.
**Warren Hastings** **abolished** it (**1772**); **John Cartier** was Governor during the **1770** famine.
xa: Exam angle: "The dual system was enforced by" — **Robert Clive**, not Warren Hastings.
⚠ **Clive** enforced (**1765**); **Hastings** abolished (**1772**).

165.s: The Dual Government in Bengal continued during which period?
165.x: The Dual Government was introduced in 1765 and continued until its abolition in 1772.
165.tq: Fix both the starting and ending years of the arrangement.
xs: The Dual Government lasted **1765-1772** — option **(1)**.
It began with the **Second Treaty of Allahabad (1765)** and ended with **Warren Hastings (1772)**.
xa: **Shah Alam II** granted the **Diwani** of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa for **₹26 lakh** a year.
Verdict: "**a sham**" → economic ruin of Bengal + **famine of 1770**.

165.s: The grant of Diwani rights to the East India Company in 1765 was associated with which treaty?
165.x: The Second Treaty of Allahabad in 1765 enabled Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II to grant the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa to the Company.
165.tq: Match the constitutional arrangement with the treaty that created its basis.
xs: The Diwani came under the **Second Treaty of Allahabad (1765)** — option **(4)**.
Grantor: Mughal Emperor **Shah Alam II**; recipient: the **EIC**.
xa: It covered **Bengal, Bihar and Orissa**; annual tribute = **₹26 lakh**.
**Mohd. Reza Khan** was appointed by **Clive** as Deputy Diwan of **Murshidabad** after the treaty (BPSC 2001).

165.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Nizamat — Power and funds without responsibility
165.x: Nizamat involved responsibility without effective power or funds. Diwani represented real power without corresponding responsibility.
165.tq: Find the reversed comparison in the power–responsibility relationship.
xs: "**Nizamat — power and funds without responsibility**" is NOT correctly matched — option **(3)**.
**Nizamat** (with Nawab) had **responsibility, but no power or funds**.
**Diwani** (with EIC) had **real power, no responsibility**; it meant **revenue collection**.
xa: Nizamat = **police, criminal justice, general administration**.
⚠ **Diwani** = revenue (with EIC); **Nizamat** = police and criminal justice (with Nawab).

165.s: Which of the following was NOT a reason for establishing the Dual Government in Bengal?
o: To avoid scrutiny by the British Parliament
To provide the Company with adequate British manpower for civil administration
To keep other European companies paying duties to the Nawab
To conceal British imperial ambitions from Indian rulers
165.x: B is the odd one out: the Dual Government arose from a LACK of British manpower for civil administration, not to provide adequate manpower. Avoiding Parliament's scrutiny, keeping other Europeans paying duties to the 'Nawab' and hiding imperial ambitions were the actual reasons.
165.tq: Identify the option that reverses a stated administrative limitation.
xs: The system arose from a **lack of British manpower** for civil administration — so option **(2)** is NOT a reason.
Real reasons: **hide imperial ambitions**, **avoid British Parliament's scrutiny**, keep other Europeans **paying duties to the "Nawab"**.
xa: The Company worked through **Naib Diwans** and a **Naib Nazim**.
Verdict: "**a sham**".

165.s: During the Dual Government, the East India Company collected revenue primarily through which arrangement?
o: Direct collection by British district collectors
Indian deputies acting on behalf of the Company
Village panchayats appointed by the Nawab
165.x: The Company did not initially collect revenue itself; it operated through Indian deputies.
165.tq: Apply the institutional distinction between nominal control and the actual collection mechanism.
xs: The Company worked through **Indian deputies** — **Naib Diwans** and a **Naib Nazim** — option **(3)**.
It **did not collect revenue itself** under the Dual Government.
xa: **Muhammad Reza Khan** = Naib Diwan, **Bengal (Murshidabad)**; **Raja Shitab Rai** = **Bihar (Patna)**.
After **1772** the Company collected revenue **directly through its own servants**.

165.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Person)
(a) Muhammad Reza Khan
(b) Raja Shitab Rai
(c) Robert Clive
(d) Warren Hastings

List-II (Association)
(i) Abolished Dual Government
(ii) Naib Diwan in Bihar
(iii) Introduced Dual Government
(iv) Naib Diwan at Murshidabad

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
165.x: Muhammad Reza Khan was Naib Diwan at Murshidabad, Shitab Rai was Naib Diwan in Bihar, Clive introduced the system, and Hastings abolished it.
165.tq: Start from the sure deputy–region pairs and then complete the ruler–action pairs.
xs: **a–iv, b–ii, c–iii, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Muhammad Reza Khan** — Naib Diwan at **Murshidabad**; **Raja Shitab Rai** — Naib Diwan in **Bihar**.
**Robert Clive** — **architect**; **Warren Hastings** — **abolished** it (**1772**).
xa: Both deputies were **removed + tried** in **1772**.
BPSC **1996** asked "who abolished Dual Government" — **Warren Hastings**.

165.s: Muhammad Reza Khan held which combination of positions during the Dual Government?
o: Naib Diwan at Murshidabad and Naib Nazim for the minor Nawab
Naib Nazim at Calcutta and Diwan of Orissa
Naib Diwan at Allahabad and Nawab of Bengal
Naib Diwan at Patna and Governor of Bihar
165.x: Muhammad Reza Khan served as Naib Diwan at Murshidabad and also as Naib Nazim for the minor Nawab of Bengal.
165.tq: Test a distinctive combination of offices held by one official.
xs: **Muhammad Reza Khan** was **Naib Diwan at Murshidabad** and **Naib Nazim for the minor Nawab** — option **(1)**.
**Patna** was the seat of **Raja Shitab Rai**, Naib Diwan of **Bihar**.
xa: Reza Khan was appointed by **Clive** after the **Treaty of Allahabad** (BPSC 2001 key).
He was **removed + tried** in **1772**.

165.s: What happened to Muhammad Reza Khan and Raja Shitab Rai when the Dual Government ended?
o: They were appointed as Company servants in Calcutta.
They were transferred to the Mughal court.
They were promoted as Governors of Bengal and Bihar.
165.x: Both Muhammad Reza Khan and Raja Shitab Rai were removed and tried when the Dual Government ended in 1772.
165.tq: Recall the administrative consequence associated with the termination of the system.
xs: Both were **removed and tried** when the dual system ended in **1772** — option **(2)**.
**Warren Hastings** had the Company collect revenue **directly through its own servants**.
xa: The **treasury** shifted **Murshidabad → Calcutta**.
⚠ **Reza Khan** = Bengal (Murshidabad); **Shitab Rai** = Bihar (Patna).

165.s: The conflict between the Nizamat and the Diwani under the Dual Government primarily resulted in which consequence?
o: Sidelining of local nobility and the growth of resentment
Transfer of political power to peasants
165.x: The conflict between the two authorities sidelined the local nobility and generated resentment.
165.tq: Infer the political consequence from divided authority and responsibility.
xs: The **Nizamat** vs **Diwani** conflict **sidelined the local nobility** → **resentment** — option **(1)**.
It did not strengthen the nobility or end Company privileges.
xa: **Revenue extortion** ruined the Bengal economy.
**Weavers** were forced to sell to Company agents at low prices.

165.s:
Consider the following statements about the drain of wealth from Bengal after 1765:
1. Bengal's surplus revenue was used by the Company to buy Indian goods for export.
2. This belongs to R.P. Dutt's mercantilist phase, which he dated 1813-1858.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
165.x: Statement 1 is correct: surplus revenue bought Indian goods for export. Statement 2 is wrong: R.P. Dutt's mercantilist phase is 1757-1813, not 1813-1858. Hence 1 only; '2 only', 'both' and 'neither' are wrong.
165.tq: Mercantilist phase starts with Plassey (1757) and ends with the Charter Act of 1813.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: Bengal's **surplus revenue** bought **Indian goods for export**.
Statement 2 wrong: **R.P. Dutt**'s **Mercantilist phase** is **1757-1813**, not 1813-1858.
xa: R.P. Dutt described **three stages**.
Scholars trace the **drain of wealth** + **deindustrialisation** to the Dual Government.

165.s: What was the immediate effect of Company policies on Bengal weavers?
o: They were exempted from all contractual obligations.
They received tax-free access to European markets.
They were compelled to sell to Company agents at low prices.
They were appointed as Company revenue officers.
165.x: Company agents forced weavers to sell their products at low prices, contributing to the decline of handicrafts.
165.tq: Test the producer–Company agent relationship and its economic effect.
xs: **Weavers** were **forced to sell to Company agents at low prices** — option **(3)**.
Result: **handicrafts declined**.
xa: Company servants also misused the **dastak** for inland trade.
In under two decades Bengal fell into **acute poverty, famines, epidemics**.

165.s: Which of the following correctly explains the misuse of dastaks by Company servants?
o: They used them to appoint the Nawab’s ministers.
They used duty-free trade passes for private inland trade.
They used them to regulate pilgrimages to holy places.
They used them to collect land revenue from peasants.
165.x: Company servants misused the duty-free dastak, or trade pass, for private inland trade.
165.tq: Decode the specific commercial privilege associated with the term dastak.
xs: Company servants misused the **duty-free dastak (trade pass)** for **private inland trade** — option **(2)**.
Dastaks had nothing to do with appointing ministers, pilgrimages or land revenue.
xa: **Mir Qasim** had earlier **abolished internal duties for everyone** in protest.
Wealth drain = **Mercantilist phase (1757-1813)** of R.P. Dutt.

165.s: Mir Qasim had earlier abolished internal duties for everyone primarily as a protest against:
o: The Company’s use of duty-free dastaks for private trade
The famine relief measures of the Nawab
The transfer of the treasury to Calcutta
The abolition of the Diwani by Shah Alam II
165.x: Mir Qasim abolished internal duties for all traders in protest against the Company servants’ misuse of duty-free dastaks.
165.tq: Link a reform measure with the commercial grievance that prompted it.
xs: **Mir Qasim** abolished internal duties for everyone in protest against the Company's **duty-free dastaks** for **private trade** — option **(1)**.
The **treasury shift to Calcutta** came only in **1772**, under Hastings.
xa: Dastak = **duty-free trade pass**.
**Weavers** too were exploited — forced sales at low prices.

165.s: By the period following the establishment of Dual Government, Bengal, formerly regarded as India’s richest province, was reduced to:
o: A province free from Company intervention
165.x: In under two decades, Bengal was reduced to acute poverty, famines and epidemics despite its earlier wealth.
165.tq: Use the before–after comparison to identify the correct historical consequence.
xs: Bengal, **India's richest province**, fell into **acute poverty, famines, epidemics** — option **(4)**.
This happened **in under two decades**.
xa: Causes: **revenue extortion**, **wealth drain**, decline of **weavers**' handicrafts.
Climax: the **famine of 1770**.

165.s: The Great Bengal Famine of 1770 occurred during the term of:
165.x: The Great Bengal Famine of 1770 occurred during John Cartier's term as governor, which lasted from 1769 to 1772.
165.tq: Match the event with the correct contemporary administrator.
xs: The **1770** famine fell in **John Cartier**'s term (**1769-72**) — option **(2)**.
**Warren Hastings** came in **1772**; **Robert Clive**'s 2nd term was **1765-67**.
xa: Exam angle: "Governor during the 1770 famine" — **John Cartier**.
"Famine and Dual Government" — direct **cause-effect**.

165.s: The Bengal Famine of 1770 mainly affected which areas?
o: Punjab and Sindh in north-western India
Bengal and Bihar in the lower Gangetic plain
Madras and Mysore in the southern peninsula
Bombay and Gujarat in western India
165.x: The famine affected Bengal and Bihar, particularly the lower Gangetic plain.
165.tq: Distinguish the famine region from other major Company-controlled areas.
xs: The famine hit **Bengal and Bihar** (**lower Gangetic plain**) — option **(2)**.
Governor at the time: **John Cartier (1769-72)**.
xa: Causes: **monsoon failure**, **high land revenue in cash**, **grain exported**.
⚠ Andhra famines were separate: **Guntur (Dokkala) 1832-33** and **Kurnool 1866**.

165.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the causes of the Bengal Famine of 1770:
1. The monsoon failed.
2. High land revenue was collected in cash.
3. Peasants were forced to sell grain.
4. Grain was exported from Bengal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
165.x: The famine was associated with monsoon failure, high cash revenue demands that forced grain sales, and the export of grain from Bengal.
165.tq: Combine environmental, fiscal and commercial causes in a single statement set.
xs: All four causes are correct — **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
**Failure of the monsoon**; **high land revenue collected in cash**.
Peasants **forced to sell grain**; **grain exported** out of Bengal.
xa: Governor: **John Cartier (1769-72)**.
Company response: **little or no relief**; revenue collection continued.

165.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Company’s response to the Bengal Famine of 1770?
o: It provided little or no relief while revenue collection continued.
It stopped all exports and remitted land revenue permanently.
It transferred famine administration to the Nawab without conditions.
It provided extensive relief and suspended revenue collection.
165.x: The Company offered little or no relief and continued collecting revenue during the famine.
165.tq: Test the contrast between humanitarian response and continued fiscal extraction.
xs: The Company gave **little or no relief** and **revenue collection continued** — option **(1)**.
Revenue was **squeezed even as famine spread**.
xa: This **hurt the Company's reputation** + **increased local opposition**.
Deaths: about **10 million** (UPSC notes); "**about two million lives**" (APP); textbook: about **one-third**.

165.s: The Company’s handling of the Bengal Famine of 1770 had which political consequence?
o: It reduced local opposition to Company rule.
It improved the Company’s reputation among the population.
It damaged the Company’s reputation and increased local opposition.
It resulted in the restoration of complete Nawabi authority.
165.x: The lack of relief and continuation of revenue collection damaged the Company’s reputation and increased local opposition.
165.tq: Infer the political consequence from the stated administrative response.
xs: It **hurt the Company's reputation** and **increased local opposition** — option **(3)**.
Cause: **little or no relief** while revenue was still collected.
xa: The famine fed the **Sanyasi (Fakir) Revolt (1763-1800)**.
Its memory lives in **Anandamath** (**1882**).

165.s: The common textbook estimate of mortality in the Bengal Famine of 1770 is approximately:
165.x: A common textbook estimate places the deaths at about one-third of Bengal’s population.
165.tq: Recall the proportional estimate separately from absolute death figures.
xs: The common textbook figure is about **one-third** of Bengal's population — option **(1)**.
Other sources differ: about **10 million** (UPSC notes); "**about two million lives**" (APP).
xa: Mortality figures for **1770** differ widely between sources — a known debate.
It was **one of the deadliest famines**.

165.s: The Bengal Famine of 1770 is directly linked, as cause and effect, with which arrangement?
165.x: The famine came under the Dual Government (1765-72), when the Company held revenue power without responsibility and kept squeezing revenue as the famine spread. The Permanent Settlement (1793), Subsidiary Alliance (1798) and Ryotwari came later.
165.tq: 1770 famine <-> Dual Government
xs: The **1770** famine is a direct **cause-effect** of the **Dual Government** — option **(3)**.
The Dual Government (**1765-72**) gave "**power without responsibility**"; revenue was **squeezed** as famine spread.
xa: Verdict on the Dual Government: "**a sham**" → economic ruin of Bengal.
Governor at the time: **John Cartier**.

165.s: The Dual Government in Bengal was abolished in which year?
165.x: Warren Hastings abolished the Dual Government in 1772.
165.tq: Anchor the abolition to the precise year rather than to the famine year.
xs: The Dual Government was abolished in **1772** — option **(3)**.
It was abolished by **Warren Hastings** on becoming **Governor of Bengal**.
**1765** is when it began; **1769** is the start of **John Cartier**'s term.
xa: Hastings "**tore the mask of Mughal sovereignty**"; ruled by **right of conquest**.
Treasury shifted **Murshidabad → Calcutta**.

165.s:
Consider the following statements about the steps taken by Warren Hastings after abolishing the Dual Government in 1772:
1. The treasury was shifted from Murshidabad to Calcutta.
2. The annual payment of ₹26 lakh to Shah Alam II was continued.
3. Allahabad and Kora were taken back from Shah Alam II and sold to the Nawab of Awadh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
165.x: Statement 1 is correct: the treasury moved from Murshidabad to Calcutta. Statement 2 is wrong: Hastings stopped the ₹26 lakh payment to Shah Alam II. Statement 3 is correct: Allahabad and Kora were taken back and sold to the Nawab of Awadh. So only 1 and 3 are correct; options with 2 are wrong.
165.tq: Hastings 'tore the mask' of Mughal sovereignty, so anything that keeps paying the Emperor is the false statement.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: the treasury moved **Murshidabad → Calcutta**.
Statement 2 wrong: Hastings **stopped** the **₹26 lakh** payment to **Shah Alam II**.
Statement 3 correct: **Allahabad** and **Kora** were taken back and **sold to the Nawab of Awadh**.
xa: Revenue was now collected **directly through Company servants**.
Hastings = **last Governor of Bengal (1772-73)**, **first Governor-General (1773)**.

165.s: Warren Hastings’ abolition of the Dual Government has been described as an act by which he:
o: Restored the authority of the Nawab over revenue collection
Placed Bengal under the direct administration of Shah Alam II
Transferred Bengal to the French East India Company
Tore the mask of Mughal sovereignty and ruled Bengal by right of conquest
165.x: Hastings’ action was described as tearing the mask of Mughal sovereignty and asserting rule over Bengal by right of conquest.
165.tq: Recognise the historical interpretation attached to a specific administrative change.
xs: Hastings "**tore the mask of Mughal sovereignty**" and ruled Bengal **by right of conquest** — option **(4)**.
He did not restore the Nawab's revenue role — the **Company collected directly**.
xa: He abolished the Dual Government in **1772** (BPSC **1996**).
He stopped the **₹26 lakh** to **Shah Alam II**.

165.s: Which combination correctly identifies the principal causes of the Sanyasi-Fakir Revolt?
o: The famine of 1770, Company insensitivity and restrictions on pilgrims
The Subsidiary Alliance, the Doctrine of Lapse and missionary education
The Carnatic Wars, salt taxation and the Ilbert Bill
The Permanent Settlement, the Revolt of 1857 and railway construction
165.x: The revolt was caused by the famine of 1770, Company insensitivity and restrictions on pilgrims visiting holy places.
165.tq: Group the causes of a revolt and reject causes belonging to later periods.
xs: Causes: the **famine of 1770**, **Company insensitivity** and **restrictions on pilgrims** — option **(1)**.
The other options list later policies unrelated to this revolt in the notes.
xa: **Sanyasi (Fakir) Revolt** = **1763-1800**.
Leaders: **Majnum Shah, Bhawani Pathak, Devi Chaudhurani**.

165.s: The Sanyasi-Fakir Revolt is generally dated to which period?
165.x: The Sanyasi-Fakir Revolt lasted approximately from 1763 to 1800.
165.tq: Distinguish the revolt’s long time span from the single famine year.
xs: The **Sanyasi-Fakir Revolt** is dated **1763-1800** — option **(3)**.
Its causes included the **famine of 1770** and **restrictions on pilgrims**.
xa: Participants: **Hindu Sanyasis, Muslim Fakirs, dispossessed zamindars, peasants**.
**Anandamath** (**1882**) is set against the **1770 famine + Sanyasi revolt**.

165.s:
Who among the following participated in the Sanyasi-Fakir Revolt?
1. Hindu Sanyasis
2. Muslim Fakirs
3. Dispossessed zamindars
4. Peasants

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
165.x: The participants included Hindu Sanyasis, Muslim Fakirs, dispossessed zamindars and peasants.
165.tq: Identify the broad social composition of the revolt rather than a single leadership group.
xs: All four took part — **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
**Hindu Sanyasis**, **Muslim Fakirs**, **dispossessed zamindars** and **peasants**.
xa: Leaders: **Majnum Shah, Bhawani Pathak, Devi Chaudhurani**.
Causes: **famine of 1770**, Company insensitivity, **restrictions on pilgrims**.

165.s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with the leadership of the Sanyasi-Fakir Revolt?
165.x: Majnum Shah, Bhawani Pathak and Devi Chaudhurani were associated with the revolt; Shah Alam II was not a leader of it.
165.tq: Find the unrelated historical figure among the revolt’s named leaders.
xs: **Shah Alam II** was not a leader of the revolt — option **(4)**.
He was the **Mughal Emperor** who granted the **Diwani (1765)**.
Leaders: **Majnum Shah, Bhawani Pathak, Devi Chaudhurani**.
xa: Revolt period: **1763-1800**.
Shah Alam II lost the **₹26 lakh** payment in **1772**.

165.s:
Consider the following statements about Anandamath:
1. It was written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay and published in 1882.
2. It is set against the background of the Revolt of 1857.
3. It contains the song Vande Mataram.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
165.x: Statement 1 is correct: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, 1882. Statement 2 is wrong: the novel is set against the Bengal Famine of 1770 and the Sanyasi revolt, not 1857. Statement 3 is correct: it contains Vande Mataram. So 1 and 3 only.
165.tq: Anandamath = Sanyasis + 1770 famine; 1857 is the classic distractor.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **Anandamath** by **Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay**, **1882**.
Statement 2 wrong: it is set against the **1770 famine + Sanyasi revolt**, not 1857.
Statement 3: it contains **Vande Mataram**.
xa: Sanyasi revolt leaders include **Bhawani Pathak** and **Devi Chaudhurani**.
Revolt period: **1763-1800**.

165.s:
Assertion (A): The origins of the drain of wealth and deindustrialisation in India are traced by scholars to the Dual Government.
Reason (R): The Dual Government marked the first formal Company control of revenue in India.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
165.x: Both statements are true, and the Company's formal control over revenue provides the basis for tracing the drain of wealth and deindustrialisation to the arrangement.
165.tq: Test whether the stated revenue-control feature explains the broader economic consequence.
xs: **Both A and R are true** and **R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
R: the Dual Government was the **first formal Company control of revenue** in India.
A: scholars trace the **drain of wealth** + **deindustrialisation** to it.
xa: Wealth drain = R.P. Dutt's **Mercantilist phase (1757-1813)**.
**Weavers** forced to sell cheap → **handicrafts declined**.

165.s: The criticism that the Dual Government created “power without responsibility” refers to the:
o: Financial loan sought by the Company from Britain
Separation of revenue authority from effective administrative responsibility
Subordination of Bombay and Madras to Bengal
Establishment of the Supreme Court at Calcutta
165.x: The phrase “power without responsibility” criticised the arrangement in which authority over revenue was exercised without corresponding responsibility for administration and welfare.
165.tq: Interpret the constitutional criticism by linking the phrase to the distribution of power and responsibility.
xs: "**Power without responsibility**" = **separation of revenue authority** (Diwani) from **administrative responsibility** (Nizamat) — option **(2)**.
**Diwani (EIC)**: real power, no responsibility; **Nizamat (Nawab)**: responsibility, no power or funds.
xa: Result: economic ruin + **famine of 1770**.
Ended by **Warren Hastings (1772)**.

165.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the famines mentioned in relation to Bengal and Andhra:
1. The Guntur or Dokkala famine occurred in 1832–33 and caused about two lakh deaths.
2. The Kurnool famine occurred in 1866.
3. Both these Andhra famines were the same event as the Bengal Famine of 1770.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
165.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Guntur famine of 1832–33 and the Kurnool famine of 1866 were separate Andhra famines, distinct from the Bengal Famine of 1770.
165.tq: Use dates and location to separate similar famine references and reject the conflation of distinct events.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **Guntur (Dokkala) famine 1832-33** — about **2 lakh** deaths.
Statement 2: **Kurnool famine of 1866**.
Statement 3 wrong: Andhra famines were **separate** from the **1770** Bengal famine.
xa: The 1770 famine hit **Bengal and Bihar** (lower Gangetic plain).
Governor in 1770: **John Cartier**.

165.s: Which of the following correctly describes Warren Hastings in relation to Bengal administration?
o: He was the first Governor of Bengal in 1773 and the last Governor-General in 1774.
He was the first Governor of Bengal in 1758 and the last Governor in 1772–73.
He was the first Governor-General of Bengal in 1758 and the first Viceroy in 1773.
He was the last Governor of Bengal in 1772–73 and the first Governor-General of Bengal in 1773.
165.x: Warren Hastings was the last Governor of Bengal from 1772 to 1773 and became the first Governor-General of Bengal in 1773.
165.tq: Discriminate between closely related offices and dates by tracking the change from Governor to Governor-General.
xs: **Warren Hastings** was the **last Governor of Bengal (1772-73)** and **first Governor-General of Bengal (1773)** — option **(4)**.
The **first Governor of Bengal** was **Clive** (**1758**).
xa: Hastings **abolished** the Dual Government in **1772**.
⚠ **Clive** enforced (**1765**); **Hastings** abolished (**1772**).

166.s:
Consider the following statements about the rise of Haidar Ali:
1. He rose to prominence under the Wodeyar kingdom of Mysore.
2. He became Faujdar of Dindigul in 1755 under the minister Nanjaraja.
3. He became the de facto ruler of Mysore in 1782.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
166.x: Statement 1 is correct: he rose under the Wodeyars. Statement 2 is correct: Faujdar of Dindigul in 1755 under Nanjaraja. Statement 3 is wrong: he became de facto ruler in 1761, not 1782. So 1 and 2 only; '1 only' misses statement 2, and options with 3 are wrong.
166.tq: Haidar's timeline: 1755 Dindigul, 1761 de facto ruler.
xs: Only statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **Haidar Ali** rose under the **Wodeyar** kingdom of Mysore.
Statement 2: he became **Faujdar of Dindigul in 1755** under minister **Nanjaraja**.
Statement 3 wrong: he became **de facto ruler** in **1761**, not 1782.
xa: He adopted **Western techniques** and set up a **modern arsenal at Dindigul** with French help.
In the 1st war he **won over the Marathas** and **detached the Nizam** from the British.

166.s: Which development at Dindigul is associated with Haidar Ali?
o: A naval dockyard was established under British supervision.
A modern arsenal was established with French help.
The Ryotwari system was first introduced by Read and Munro.
A Jacobin Club was established with Maratha help.
166.x: Haidar Ali adopted Western military techniques and established a modern arsenal at Dindigul with French help.
166.tq: Use the military institution and foreign assistance as the identifying pair.
xs: Haidar Ali set up a **modern arsenal at Dindigul** with **French help** — option **(2)**.
**Ryotwari** began in the **Bara Mahal** (Read and Munro); the **Jacobin Club** was Tipu's, at **Seringapatam (1797)**.
xa: Haidar was **Faujdar of Dindigul in 1755**.
⚠ **Dindigul** arsenal = Haidar; **French embassy + navy + Jacobin Club** = Tipu.

166.s: During the First Anglo-Mysore War, Haidar Ali weakened the British position by
o: winning over the Marathas and detaching the Nizam from the British
restoring the Wodeyar dynasty to the Madras Presidency
forming a permanent alliance with Lord Cornwallis
166.x: Haidar Ali used diplomacy to win over the Marathas and detach the Nizam from the British during the First Anglo-Mysore War.
166.tq: Identify the diplomatic combination that changed the balance of the war.
xs: Haidar **won over the Marathas** and **detached the Nizam** from the British — option **(2)**.
The **Wodeyar** restoration came in **1799**; **Cornwallis** belongs to the **Third** war.
xa: The Nizam had first **joined the British**, and the Marathas had **joined against Haidar** (UPSC).
The war ended with the **Treaty of Madras (1769)** with Haidar.

166.s: Which ruler of Sivaganga took Haidar Ali's help to recover her kingdom and is called the first queen to wage war against the British?
166.x: Velu Nachiyar of Sivaganga recovered her kingdom with Haidar Ali's help and is called the first queen to wage war against the British (APPSC-G1 2022). Chennamma (Kittur) and Lakshmibai (Jhansi) fought later, and Durgavati fought the Mughals.
166.tq: Velu Nachiyar + Haidar Ali
xs: **Velu Nachiyar** of **Sivaganga** took Haidar Ali's help to recover her kingdom — option **(2)**.
She is called the **first queen to wage war against the British** (**APPSC-G1 2022** key).
xa: Haidar Ali was **de facto ruler** of Mysore from **1761**.
Haidar's allies-and-diplomacy also turned the **Marathas** and **Nizam** in the 1st war.

166.s: Tipu Sultan sent an envoy to Afghanistan to seek relations with
166.x: Tipu Sultan sent envoys to Afghanistan, including to Zaman Shah.
166.tq: Match the diplomatic destination with the named contemporary ruler.
xs: Tipu's envoy to **Afghanistan** went to **Zaman Shah** — option **(1)**.
He also sent envoys to **Turkey (Constantinople)** and **Mauritius**.
xa: His ambassadors to **France** sought European technology → built a **navy** (APPSC-G1 2018).
Capital: **Seringapatam (Srirangapatna)**.

166.s:
Consider the following statements about Tipu Sultan's association with the Jacobin Club:
1. It was established at Seringapatam in 1797.
2. Tipu Sultan became a member of the club.
3. Tipu Sultan called himself ‘Citizen Tipu’.
4. A Tree of Liberty was planted there.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
166.x: All four statements are correct. Tipu Sultan supported the Jacobin Club at Seringapatam, became a member, used the title ‘Citizen Tipu’ and planted a Tree of Liberty.
166.tq: Confirm the complete cluster of associated details before selecting the inclusive option.
xs: All four statements are correct — **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
Tipu helped French soldiers set up a **Jacobin Club at Seringapatam (1797)** and **became a member**.
He called himself **"Citizen Tipu"** and planted a **Tree of Liberty**.
xa: Other titles: **"Tiger of Mysore"**, **Padshah**.
He sent ambassadors to **France** and built a **navy**.

166.s:
Which of the following sets contains only measures or military innovations associated with Tipu Sultan?
1. New calendar
2. New coinage
3. New weights and measures
4. War rockets
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
166.x: Tipu Sultan introduced a new calendar, new coinage, and new weights and measures, and used war rockets. Therefore, all four statements are correct.
166.tq: Group all the listed innovations under their correct ruler.
xs: All four are Tipu's — **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
He brought a **new calendar**, **new coinage**, **new weights and measures**, and used **war rockets**.
xa: He also introduced **sericulture** in Mysore.
He built a **navy** with **French** technology.

166.s: Which one of the following statements about Tipu Sultan is NOT correct?
o: He supported the establishment of a Jacobin Club at Seringapatam.
He sent envoys to Turkey, Afghanistan and Mauritius.
He discontinued the use of war rockets in military operations.
166.x: Tipu Sultan used war rockets; he did not discontinue their use. The other three statements are correct.
166.tq: Find the statement that reverses a documented military or administrative measure.
xs: "He **discontinued** the use of **war rockets**" is NOT correct — Tipu **used** war rockets — option **(3)**.
The rest are true: **Jacobin Club** at Seringapatam; envoys to **Turkey, Afghanistan, Mauritius**; **sericulture**.
xa: He also brought a **new calendar**, **coinage**, **weights and measures**.
He was killed on **4 May 1799** defending Seringapatam.

166.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
166.x: Tipu Sultan was associated with the titles ‘Tiger of Mysore’, ‘Citizen Tipu’ and ‘Padshah’. ‘Lion of Mysore’ is not among the stated titles.
166.tq: Find the look-alike title that does not belong to the stated set.
xs: "**Lion of Mysore — Tipu Sultan**" is NOT correctly matched — option **(1)**.
Tipu's titles: **"Tiger of Mysore"**, **"Citizen Tipu"** and **Padshah**.
xa: "Citizen Tipu" came from the **Jacobin Club at Seringapatam (1797)**.
His **Gumbaz** at Srirangapatna is the **mausoleum of Haidar and Tipu**.

166.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding monuments at Srirangapatna:

List-I (Monument)
 a. Daria Daulat Bagh
 b. Gumbaz
 c. Jamia Masjid

List-II (Description)
 i. Masjid-e-Ala
 ii. Mausoleum of Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan
 iii. Summer palace containing war murals

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
166.x: Daria Daulat Bagh was a summer palace with war murals, the Gumbaz is the mausoleum of Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan, and Jamia Masjid is also known as Masjid-e-Ala.
166.tq: Begin with the distinctive monument–description pair and use elimination for the remaining pairs.
xs: **a–iii, b–ii, c–i** — option **(1)**.
**Daria Daulat Bagh** — **summer palace with war murals**.
**Gumbaz** — **mausoleum of Haidar and Tipu**; **Jamia Masjid** — **Masjid-e-Ala**.
xa: Srirangapatna = **Seringapatam**, Tipu's capital.
Tipu was killed there on **4 May 1799**.

166.s: Which Mysore ruler sent ambassadors to France for European technology and used it to build a navy?
166.x: Tipu Sultan sent ambassadors to France and built a navy (APPSC-G1 2018 key). Statement questions on the 'French embassy + navy' point to Tipu, not Haidar Ali or the Wodeyars.
166.tq: French embassy + navy = Tipu
xs: **Tipu Sultan** sent ambassadors to **France** and built a **navy** — option **(3)**.
This is the **APPSC-G1 2018** key; "French embassy + navy" points to Tipu, **not Haidar or the Wodeyars**.
xa: **Haidar**'s French link was the **arsenal at Dindigul**.
**Krishnaraja Wodeyar III** was the **boy ruler** restored in **1799**.

166.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Pollilur — Eyre Coote defeated Haidar Ali
Porto Novo — Haidar Ali and Tipu defeated Colonel Baillie
166.x: Cornwallis's coalition won at Seringapatam in 1792 and Tipu sued for peace. A and B swap the battles: Pollilur (1780) was Haidar and Tipu's defeat of Baillie, Porto Novo (1781) was Eyre Coote's win over Haidar; D is wrong because the British won in 1799 and Tipu was killed.
166.tq: Check the victor first, then verify the year and war.
xs: **Seringapatam (1792)** — **Cornwallis's coalition won** — option **(3)**.
**Pollilur (1780)**: Haidar and Tipu beat **Col. Baillie**; **Porto Novo (1781)**: **Eyre Coote** beat Haidar — options (1) and (2) swap them.
**Seringapatam (1799)**: the **British won** and Tipu was killed.
xa: After 1792 Tipu **sued for peace** — Treaty of Seringapatam.
Pollilur and Porto Novo were **2nd war** battles.

166.s: In 1790, Tipu Sultan defeated the British army commanded by
166.x: In 1790, Tipu Sultan defeated the British army under General Meadows during the Third Anglo-Mysore War.
166.tq: Avoid swapping commanders from different battles and years.
xs: In **1790** Tipu defeated the British army under **General Meadows** — option **(1)**.
**Col. Baillie** was beaten at **Pollilur (1780)**; **Hector Munro** and **Sir Eyre Coote** were early-wars commanders.
xa: In **1791** **Cornwallis** took **Bangalore (March 1791)** via **Ambur** and **Vellore**.
The 3rd war ended with Cornwallis's coalition win at **Seringapatam (1792)**.

166.s:
Which of the following statements about British commanders in the early Anglo-Mysore Wars is correct?
1. Hector Munro was among the British commanders.
2. Sir Eyre Coote was among the British commanders.
3. Thomas Munro served under both Hector Munro and Sir Eyre Coote.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
166.x: Hector Munro and Sir Eyre Coote were British commanders in the early wars, and Thomas Munro served under both of them.
166.tq: Verify each person’s role before choosing the comprehensive combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
**Hector Munro** and **Sir Eyre Coote** were early-wars commanders.
**Thomas Munro** **served under both**.
xa: ⚠ Don't confuse **Hector Munro** (commander) with **Thomas Munro**.
**Eyre Coote** defeated Haidar at **Porto Novo (1781)**.

166.s: Under the Treaty of Seringapatam of 1792, Tipu Sultan was required to
o: transfer his capital to Bangalore and join the Maratha confederacy
surrender the whole of Mysore and abdicate permanently
cede about half his territory, pay ₹3 crore and give two sons as hostages
cede Dindigul alone and pay no indemnity
166.x: Tipu Sultan ceded about half his territory, paid a war indemnity of ₹3 crore and gave two sons as hostages under the Treaty of Seringapatam.
166.tq: Combine the territorial, financial and hostage terms of the treaty.
xs: Tipu ceded about **half his territory**, paid **₹3 crore** and gave **two sons as hostages** — option **(3)**.
**Half the indemnity** was paid at once; the sons returned after the rest was paid.
xa: **Nizam** gained from the **Krishna to beyond the Pennar**; **Marathas** around the **Tungabhadra**.
**British** gained **Malabar, Coorg, Dindigul and the Bara Mahal**.

166.s:
Match the gainers under the Treaty of Seringapatam (1792) with their shares:
List-I (Gainer)
a. Nizam
b. Marathas
c. British
List-II (Share)
i. Malabar, Coorg (as protectorate), Dindigul and the Bara Mahal
ii. Areas from the Krishna to beyond the Pennar
iii. Areas around the Tungabhadra and its tributaries
Select the correct code:
166.x: The Nizam got the areas from the Krishna to beyond the Pennar (ii), the Marathas got the areas around the Tungabhadra (iii), and the British got Malabar, Coorg, Dindigul and the Bara Mahal (i). Option 2 swaps the Nizam and the Marathas; options 3 and 4 give the British share to an Indian ally.
166.tq: Nizam = Krishna-Pennar (Rayalaseema), Marathas = Tungabhadra, British = coast and Bara Mahal.
xs: **a–ii, b–iii, c–i** — option **(1)**.
**Nizam** — **Krishna to beyond the Pennar**; **Marathas** — around the **Tungabhadra** and tributaries.
**British** — **Malabar, Coorg (protectorate), Dindigul, Bara Mahal**.
xa: The Nizam's share included half of **Rayalaseema**: **Bellary, Gurramkonda, Gandikota, Kambham, Kadapa**.
**Bara Mahal** (Salem region) is where **Read and Munro** began **Ryotwari**.

166.s:
Which of the following places formed part of the Nizam's share under the Treaty of Seringapatam?
1. Bellary
2. Gurramkonda
3. Gandikota
4. Kadapa
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
166.x: Bellary, Gurramkonda, Gandikota and Kadapa were among the territories in the Nizam's share, which included about half of Rayalaseema.
166.tq: Test the complete membership of the territorial list.
xs: All four — **Bellary, Gurramkonda, Gandikota, Kadapa** — were in the Nizam's share, option **(4)**.
The Nizam's share (**Krishna to beyond the Pennar**) included **half of Rayalaseema**.
xa: **Kambham** was also part of it.
These lands later became the **Ceded Districts**, handed to the Company in **1800**.

166.s: The Bara Mahal, obtained by the British after the Treaty of Seringapatam, is associated with the beginning of the Ryotwari system by
166.x: The Bara Mahal, identified with the Salem region, was where Read and Thomas Munro began the Ryotwari system.
166.tq: Match the administrative experiment with the place and officials associated with it.
xs: **Read and Munro** began the **Ryotwari** system in the **Bara Mahal** — option **(4)**.
Bara Mahal = **Salem region**, gained by the **British** in **1792**.
xa: **Arthur Wellesley** served in the **1799** campaign; **Cornwallis** won the **3rd war**.
British share in 1792 also included **Malabar**, **Coorg** and **Dindigul**.

166.s: On which date was Tipu Sultan killed while defending Seringapatam?
166.x: Tipu Sultan was killed on 4 May 1799 while defending Seringapatam during the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.
166.tq: Distinguish the exact date of the event from the year of the earlier treaty.
xs: Tipu was killed on **4 May 1799** defending **Seringapatam** — option **(3)**.
**1792** was the **Treaty of Seringapatam**; **1800** the **Ceded Districts**.
xa: This was the **4th war**; the **British won**.
**Arthur Wellesley** (later **Duke of Wellington**) served in this campaign.

166.s:
Which statement correctly describes the settlement of Mysore after the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War?
1. Mysore was partitioned.
2. The Hindu Wodeyar dynasty was restored.
3. Krishnaraja Wodeyar III was placed on the throne as a boy ruler.
