The Company retained the Circars for a reduced peshkash of 9 lakh rupees annually and provided military help to the Nizam.
168.x: The Treaty of Masulipatnam allowed the Company to retain the Circars for a reduced annual peshkash of 9 lakh rupees, along with military assistance to the Nizam.
168.tq: Separate the terms of the 1768 treaty from the earlier lease and later cession.
xs: By the **Treaty of Masulipatnam (1768)** the Company **retained the Circars for a reduced peshkash of 9 lakh** a year plus **military help** to the Nizam — option **(4)**.
**15 lakh** was the **1766** lease; **7 lakh** was the **Guntur** payment of **1788**; the **Ceded Districts** came in **1800**.
xa: The 1768 treaty settled the dispute over the Mughal firman of **1765**.
**Guntur** was excepted from the Circar lease until **1788**.
⚠ **15 lakh** = 1766 lease; **9 lakh** = 1768; **7 lakh** = Guntur.

168.s: The Ceded Districts were given to the Company in 1800 in lieu of:
o: The expenses of the Carnatic War
The annual lease payment of 15 lakh rupees
The subsidy payable for the British subsidiary force
The reduced peshkash of the Northern Circars
168.x: In 1800, the Ceded Districts were transferred to the Company in lieu of the subsidy payable for the subsidiary force.
168.tq: Distinguish the compensation arrangement from the separate peshkash and lease payments.
xs: The **Ceded Districts** were given in **1800** in lieu of **the subsidy for the British subsidiary force** — option **(3)**.
Under the **Subsidiary Alliance (1798)** the Nizam could not pay in cash, so he **ceded** territory.
xa: Districts: **Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur, Bellary** = today's **Rayalaseema**.
**Hyder Ali** and **Tipu Sultan** had taken these lands from Hyderabad; **Nizam Ali** regained them in the Mysore wars of **1790-92** and **1799**.
**Munro** became their first **Principal Collector** (**1800**).

168.s: The first Indian ruler to accept Lord Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance was:
168.x: The Nizam of Hyderabad accepted the Subsidiary Alliance first, by the Treaty of Hyderabad in 1798, and kept a British subsidiary force at his own cost. Baji Rao II accepted it later, in 1802, by the Treaty of Bassein. Tipu Sultan refused it. The Nawab of Awadh accepted it after the Nizam.
168.tq: Nizam 1798 = first SA ally (APPSC 2002).
xs: The **Nizam of Hyderabad** was the first ruler to accept **Wellesley's** Subsidiary Alliance (**1798**) — option **(2)** (**APPSC 2002**).
Under the **Treaty of Hyderabad (1798)** the Nizam kept a British subsidiary force and paid for it.
xa: In **1800** he gave up the **Ceded Districts** in lieu of the subsidy.
Earlier treaties with the Nizam: **1766** lease, **1768** Masulipatnam, **1788** Guntur.

168.s: In the Bobbili War, Vijayarama Raju sought the assistance of:
168.x: Vijayarama Raju took French help through Bussy during the Bobbili War, fought in 1757.
168.tq: Identify the external ally associated with the specific conflict.
xs: In the Bobbili war, **Vijayaramaraju** of Vizianagaram took the help of the **French under Bussy** — option **(1)**.
Together they destroyed **Bobbili** on **24 Jan 1757**; **Bobbili Ranga Rao** was killed.
xa: Ranga Rao's brother-in-law **Tandra Papayya** later killed Vijayaramaraju.
**Bobbili** = **Velama** family; **Vizianagaram** = **Pusapati** — rivals.
⚠ **Vijayaramaraju** = Bobbili 1757; **Chinna Vijayaramaraju** = Padmanabham 1794.

168.s: When and where was Chinna Vijayarama Raju defeated by the British?
168.x: Chinna Vijayarama Raju was defeated by the British at Padmanabham on 10 July 1794.
168.tq: Combine the exact date and place to avoid confusing the Bobbili and Padmanabham events.
xs: **Chinna Vijayaramaraju** was defeated and killed by the British at **Padmanabham** on **10 July 1794** — option **(1)**.
**1757 at Bobbili** was the earlier war of **Vijayaramaraju** with **Bussy**.
xa: After Padmanabham, his minor son **Narayana Babu** was made zamindar; **George Russell** took charge of the forts.
**1794** also saw the **Collector system** begin in the Circars.
**APPSC 2025** order: Guntur → Padmanabham → Ryotwari in Madras → abolition of zamindari.

168.s: What arrangement followed the defeat of Chinna Vijayarama Raju at Padmanabham?
o: His minor son Narayana Babu was sent to Vengi, while Bussy was placed over Vizianagaram’s forts.
Kakatiya Ganapatideva made Narayana Babu a Mandaleswara and retained the forts.
The British abolished the Vizianagaram estate and transferred it to the Velanati Chodas.
His minor son Narayana Babu was made zamindar, while George Russell was placed over Vizianagaram’s forts.
168.x: After the defeat, the minor son Narayana Babu was made zamindar and George Russell was placed in charge of Vizianagaram’s forts.
168.tq: Link the political consequence to the correct ruler and administrative officer.
xs: After **Padmanabham (1794)**, minor son **Narayana Babu** was made **zamindar**, and **George Russell** took charge of the forts — option **(4)**.
**Bussy** belongs to the **Bobbili** war of **1757**, not Padmanabham.
xa: The British defeated and killed **Chinna Vijayaramaraju** on **10 July 1794**.
**Vizianagaram** (Pusapati) later became a Northern Circars zamindari under the **Permanent Settlement (1802)**.
**Gajapati Vijayarama** belonged to the Vizianagaram kingdom (**APPSC GS 2022**).

168.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its historical description?
168.x: Vizianagaram was associated with the Pusapati family. Bobbili and Venkatagiri were associated with Velama families, while Peddapuram belonged to the Vatsavayi dynasty.
168.tq: Separate similar zamindari houses through family-name associations.
xs: **Vizianagaram — Pusapati** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**Bobbili** was a **Velama** estate; **Venkatagiri** = **Velugoti**; **Peddapuram** = **Vatsavayi**.
xa: Bobbili was destroyed in the **1757** war by Vizianagaram and the French.
Venkatagiri was a Velama zamindari in **Nellore**.
⚠ **Pusapati** = Vizianagaram; **Velugoti** = Venkatagiri; **Vatsavayi** = Peddapuram.

168.s: Which of the following statements regarding the zamindaris of the Northern Circars is correct?
o: The Permanent Settlement abolished fixed revenue for zamindars.
The Northern Circars had no hereditary zamindari families.
Only Venkatagiri was brought under the Permanent Settlement.
Vizianagaram, Bobbili and Pithapuram were pre-existing estates brought under the Permanent Settlement.
168.x: Vizianagaram, Bobbili and Pithapuram were pre-existing estates brought under the Permanent Settlement. The settlement made zamindars fixed-revenue holders.
168.tq: Reject the absolute statement and identify the precise estate group.
xs: **Vizianagaram, Bobbili and Pithapuram** were **pre-existing estates** brought under the **Permanent Settlement** — option **(4)**.
The settlement made zamindars **fixed-revenue** holders — it did not abolish fixed revenue.
The Circars did have hereditary families — **Velamas, Reddis, Kshatriya Rajus**.
xa: **Permanent Settlement**: **Cornwallis**, **1793**; applied in Andhra in **1802**.
Effect: **absentee landlordism**; tenants impoverished.
Zamindari abolished by the **Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948**, in force **7 Sep 1949**.

168.s: Which of the following communities formed the hereditary zamindari families of the Northern Circars?
168.x: The hereditary zamindari families of the Northern Circars included Velamas, Reddis and Kshatriya Rajus.
168.tq: Recall the exact social composition of the regional zamindari houses.
xs: The hereditary zamindari families were **Velamas, Reddis and Kshatriya Rajus** — option **(4)**.
Their heartland was the **Northern Circars**.
xa: **Bobbili** and **Venkatagiri** = Velama; **Vizianagaram** = **Pusapati**; **Peddapuram** = **Vatsavayi**.
Before **1802** zamindaris were given by **auction**.
Peshkash = tribute zamindars paid to the British; **Korunu** = what they collected from farmers.

168.s: The hereditary zamindari of Venkatagiri was associated with which family?
168.x: Venkatagiri in Nellore was the zamindari of the Velugoti family.
168.tq: Match the estate with its ruling family.
xs: **Venkatagiri** was the zamindari of the **Velugoti** family — option **(4)**.
**Vatsavayi** = **Peddapuram**; **Pusapati** = **Vizianagaram**.
xa: Venkatagiri was a **Velama** estate in **Nellore**.
**Peddapuram — Vatsavayi** was an **APPSC GS 2022** question.
**Bobbili**, also Velama, was the rival of Vizianagaram.

168.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Bobbili — British Permanent Settlement Act of 1948
168.x: Peddapuram was associated with the Vatsavayi dynasty. Vizianagaram was associated with the Pusapati family, while Venkatagiri belonged to the Velugoti family.
168.tq: Start with the sure estate-family pair and eliminate swapped associations.
xs: **Peddapuram — Vatsavayi dynasty** is correctly matched — option **(1)** (**APPSC GS 2022**).
**Vizianagaram** = **Pusapati**, not Velugoti; **Venkatagiri** = **Velugoti**, not Pusapati.
**Bobbili** came under the **Permanent Settlement (1802)**; the **1948** Act abolished zamindaris.
xa: Other Permanent Settlement estates: **Vizianagaram, Pithapuram**.
⚠ Mnemonic pairs: Pusapati–Vizianagaram, Velugoti–Venkatagiri, Vatsavayi–Peddapuram.

168.s: The Battle of Bobbili took place on
168.x: The Battle of Bobbili was fought on 24 January 1757.
168.tq: Test the precise day and year by separating consecutive years associated with the Andhra conflict.
xs: The **Battle of Bobbili** was fought on **24 January 1757** — option **(4)**.
**Vijayaramaraju** of Vizianagaram and the **French under Bussy** destroyed Bobbili.
xa: **Bobbili Ranga Rao** was killed; **Tandra Papayya** later killed Vijayaramaraju.
**1759** was **Salabat Jung's** grant of Machilipatnam to the British — a confusable date.
⚠ **Padmanabham** (**10 July 1794**) was a different battle, against **Chinna Vijayaramaraju**.

168.s: In the aftermath of the Battle of Bobbili (1757), who killed Vijayaramaraju of Vizianagaram?
168.x: Tandra Papayya, brother-in-law of Bobbili Ranga Rao, later killed Vijayaramaraju to avenge the destruction of Bobbili. Bussy led the French who fought alongside Vijayaramaraju. Ranga Rao himself was killed in the battle. George Russell took charge of the Vizianagaram forts after Padmanabham in 1794.
168.tq: Ranga Rao killed; Papayya took revenge.
xs: **Tandra Papayya**, brother-in-law of **Bobbili Ranga Rao**, killed **Vijayaramaraju** after the battle — option **(3)**.
**Ranga Rao** himself was killed at Bobbili; **Bussy** was Vijayaramaraju's French ally; **George Russell** took the forts after **1794**.
xa: Battle date: **24 Jan 1757**.
**Bobbili** = **Velama** estate; **Vizianagaram** = **Pusapati**.

168.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the territories included in the Ceded Districts in 1800?
168.x: The Ceded Districts comprised Kadapa, Kurnool and Anantapur in present-day Andhra Pradesh, together with Bellary, now in Karnataka.
168.tq: Check membership in a historically defined regional group.
xs: The **Ceded Districts (1800)** = **Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary** — option **(1)**.
**Nellore** and **Chittoor** came from the **Carnatic** in **1801**; **Guntur** and **Krishna** were Circar lands.
xa: **Bellary** is now in **Karnataka**; the rest form today's **Rayalaseema** (**APPSC GS 2024**).
Old name: **Dattamandalam / Dattamandalalu**; **Rayalaseema** adopted at **Nandyal, 1928**.
Ceded in lieu of the **Subsidiary Alliance** subsidy.

168.s: The old name used for the Ceded Districts was:
168.x: The region was known as Dattamandalam or Dattamandalalu, meaning the ceded lands, until 1928.
168.tq: Discriminate between the old regional name and the later political name.
xs: The old name was **Dattamandalam / Dattamandalalu** ("ceded lands") — option **(2)**.
It was used until **1928**, when **Rayalaseema** was adopted.
xa: **Rayalaseema** was suggested by **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** (**APPSC G2 2012** key).
Adopted at the **Andhra Mahasabha, Nandyal**, presided over by **S. Radhakrishnan**.
⚠ Some notes say **1927**; others credit **Chilukuri Narayana Rao**.

168.s: The name ‘Rayalaseema’ was adopted at the Andhra Mahasabha held at Nandyal in:
168.x: The name Rayalaseema was adopted at Nandyal in 1928. The meeting was presided over by S. Radhakrishnan.
168.tq: Test the year and venue together rather than the name alone.
xs: **Rayalaseema** was adopted at the **Andhra Mahasabha, Nandyal**, in **1928** — option **(3)**.
The name was suggested by **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao**; **S. Radhakrishnan** presided.
xa: Old name: **Dattamandalalu** (Ceded Districts).
⚠ Some notes give **1927**.
Current angle: sericulture in Rayalaseema traces to British promotion in the "Ceded Districts"; silk hubs **Dharmavaram** and **Madanapalle**.

168.s:
Consider the following statements about the Ceded Districts:
1. Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan had taken these territories from Hyderabad.
2. Nizam Ali regained them as a British ally during the Mysore wars.
3. The Nizam ceded them in 1800 because he could not pay the Subsidiary Alliance subsidy in cash.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
168.x: All three statements are correct. The territories changed hands during the Mysore conflicts and were finally ceded by the Nizam in 1800 under the Subsidiary Alliance arrangement.
168.tq: Trace a territorial change through successive political causes.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **Hyder Ali** and **Tipu Sultan** took these lands from Hyderabad.
Statement 2: **Nizam Ali** regained them as a British ally in the Mysore wars of **1790-92** and **1799**.
Statement 3: unable to pay the **Subsidiary Alliance** subsidy in cash, the Nizam **ceded** them in **1800**.
xa: Districts: **Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur, Bellary**.
First Principal Collector: **Sir Thomas Munro**, with four sub-collectors at **Harpanahalli, Kadapa, Adoni, Kurnool**.

168.s: Before the 1808 division, the single Ceded collectorate was centred at:
168.x: The Ceded region functioned as one collectorate centred at Anantapur under Munro until 1808. Bellary became the seat of one of the two districts after the split.
168.tq: Distinguish the original headquarters from the later headquarters after reorganisation.
xs: Before **1808**, the single Ceded collectorate (**1800**) was centred at **Anantapur** under **Munro** — option **(1)**.
In **1808** it was split into **Bellary** and **Cuddapah**.
xa: ⚠ **APPSC 2011** key = **Bellary** — that refers to the post-1808 period.
**Anantapur** district itself was formed in **1882**; **Kurnool** in **1858**.
Munro surveyed the districts **1802-07**.

168.s: The name 'Rayalaseema' for the Ceded Districts was suggested by:
168.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao suggested the name, which was adopted at the Andhra Mahasabha at Nandyal in 1928 (APPSC G2 2012 key). Jogipantulu was a dubashi in the Circar lease of 1766. Munro was the first Principal Collector of the Ceded Districts. C.P. Brown was a Telugu scholar.
168.tq: Rayalaseema name: Gadicherla, Nandyal 1928.
xs: **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** suggested **Rayalaseema** — option **(1)** (**APPSC G2 2012** key).
**Jogipantulu** was the dubashi of the Circar lease; **Munro** was the first Principal Collector; **C.P. Brown** published **Vemana**.
xa: Adopted at the **Andhra Mahasabha, Nandyal, 1928**, under **S. Radhakrishnan**.
Earlier name: **Dattamandalalu**.
⚠ Other notes credit **Chilukuri Narayana Rao**.

168.s: Nellore and Chittoor were once under which ruler before becoming part of the Carnatic?
168.x: Nellore and Chittoor were once under Aravidu Sriranga Raya III and later formed part of the Carnatic.
168.tq: Match the earlier regional ruler with the territory before its Carnatic association.
xs: **Nellore** and **Chittoor** were under Aravidu **Sriranga Raya III** before they became part of the **Carnatic** — option **(1)**.
**Basalat Jung** held **Guntur**; **Salabat Jung** made the **1759** grant; **Shah Alam II** issued the firman.
xa: The Company annexed the Carnatic districts in **1801**, after **Muhammad Ali's** death.
The **Carnatic Treaty** was signed with Nawab **Azim-ud-Daula**.
By **1801** Andhra was merged into the **Madras Presidency**.

168.s: After the Second Carnatic War, the British installed whom as the Nawab of the Carnatic?
168.x: After the Second Carnatic War, the British installed Muhammad Ali as Nawab of the Carnatic, though his position became secure only after 1763.
168.tq: Distinguish the ruler installed after the war from the later Nawab who signed the treaty.
xs: The British installed **Muhammad Ali** as Nawab after the **Second Carnatic War** — option **(1)**.
His position was secure only after **1763**.
xa: He was shielded from **Najibullah** of Nellore, the **Marathas** and **Hyder Ali**.
After his death, the Carnatic districts were annexed in **1801**.
⚠ **Azim-ud-Daula** signed the **Carnatic Treaty**; Muhammad Ali was the one installed.

168.s: The Carnatic Treaty was signed with which Nawab?
168.x: The Carnatic Treaty was signed with Nawab Azim-ud-Daula.
168.tq: Avoid the ruler-swapping trap between Muhammad Ali and Azim-ud-Daula.
xs: The **Carnatic Treaty** was signed with Nawab **Azim-ud-Daula** — option **(2)**.
**Muhammad Ali** was the earlier Nawab installed after the Second Carnatic War; **Basalat Jung** and **Salabat Jung** were of the Nizam's house.
xa: Under it the Company annexed the Carnatic districts — **Nellore, Prakasam area, part of Chittoor** — in **1801**.
Andhra was then merged into the **Madras Presidency**.

168.s: Before the Northern Circars were acquired, the East India Company’s factories in the region were located at:
168.x: Before acquiring the Circars, the East India Company maintained factories at Machilipatnam and Visakhapatnam.
168.tq: Identify the correct pair of early Company centres.
xs: Before acquisition, the Company's factories and godowns were at **Machilipatnam and Visakhapatnam** — option **(2)**.
A supervising revenue body — called the "**Board of Revenue**" in some notes — sat over them, abolished in **1794**.
xa: **Provincial Chiefs and Councils** at these stations governed the Circars until **1794**.
Dutch (**1605**) and English (**1611**) factories at **Machilipatnam**.

168.s: Which body governed the Circars at the stations of Masulipatnam and Vizagapatnam before district Collectors replaced it?
168.x: Provincial Chiefs and Councils at Masulipatnam and Vizagapatnam governed the Circars before the district Collector system replaced them.
168.tq: Identify the administrative body by its station-level composition and function.
xs: **Provincial Chiefs and Councils** governed the Circars at **Masulipatnam** and **Vizagapatnam** — option **(4)**.
They were replaced by district **Collectors** in **1794**.
xa: The **Chief-in-Council at Masulipatnam** governed the Circars until then.
The **Circuit Committee** reviewed Circar revenue and opposed the **auction** system.
The **Madras Native Association** petitioned in **1861** against **Moturpha** — unconnected.

168.s:
Consider the following statements about the early administration of the Circars:
1. Provincial Chiefs and Councils governed the Circars at the principal Company stations.
2. The body was also referred to as the Board of Revenue.
3. District Collectors replaced this arrangement in 1794.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
168.x: All three are correct: Provincial Chiefs and Councils at Masulipatnam and Vizagapatnam governed the Circars; the supervising revenue body over these stations is called the 'Board of Revenue' in some sources; and district Collectors replaced the arrangement in 1794, when that body was abolished.
168.tq: Verify the institutional name, function and date as separate administrative facts.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **Provincial Chiefs and Councils** governed the Circars at the Company stations.
Statement 2: some notes call the supervising body the "**Board of Revenue**".
Statement 3: **Collectors** replaced them in **1794**.
xa: The Collector handled **land revenue** + law and order + magistracy.
The **Madras Board of Revenue** (state apex) was set up in **1786**.

168.s: The Circuit Committee, while examining revenue administration in the Andhra region, recommended which of the following?
o: Replacement of ryotwari by permanent settlement
Abolition of the auction system of revenue collection
Continuation of the auction system with higher minimum bids
Transfer of revenue collection entirely to village panchayats
168.x: The Circuit Committee recommended against the highest-bidder auction system because it harmed both the government and the ryots. Munro subsequently abolished auctions in Rayalaseema.
168.tq: Identify the recommendation by linking the committee with the administrative problem it addressed.
xs: The **Circuit Committee** recommended **against the auction (highest-bidder) system** — option **(2)**.
Auctions hurt both the government and the **ryots**.
xa: **Munro** then abolished auctions in **Rayalaseema**.
Before **1802**, zamindaris were given by **auction**; the **Permanent Settlement** replaced auctions with a fixed demand.

168.s:
Consider the following statements about the District Collector in coastal Andhra:
1. From 1794 each district had a Collector in charge of land revenue, law and order and magisterial duties.
2. The Board of Revenue that ran the Company's factories was abolished in 1794.
3. The Collector's judicial powers were taken away in 1794 itself.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
168.x: Statement 1 is correct: from 1794 the Collector handled land revenue, law and order and acted as magistrate. Statement 2 is correct: the Board of Revenue was abolished in 1794. Statement 3 is wrong: judicial powers were taken away only in 1816. So 1 and 2 only.
168.tq: 1794 = Collectors arrive; 1816 = Collectors lose judicial powers.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: from **1794** each district had a **Collector** for revenue, law and order and magistracy.
Statement 2 correct: the **Board of Revenue** over the factories was abolished in **1794**.
Statement 3 wrong: the Collector's **judicial powers** were taken away in **1816**, not 1794.
xa: Under ryotwari, some magisterial powers returned to Collectors; civil justice stayed with the **District Judge**.
⚠ **APPSC G2 2012** key gives **1786** for "Collector's administration in place of the Revenue Board".

168.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the separation of judicial and revenue functions in 1816 is correct?
o: Collectors received all criminal and civil powers in the same year.
Munsiffs were abolished and replaced by District Collectors.
Collectors lost their judicial powers, while civil justice remained with District Judges.
District Judges lost civil powers, which were transferred entirely to Collectors.
168.x: Collectors lost their judicial powers in 1816, and civil justice remained with District Judges. Under the ryotwari arrangement, some magisterial powers later returned to Collectors.
168.tq: Watch for the reversed authority trap involving Collectors and District Judges.
xs: In **1816**, **Collectors lost their judicial powers**, and **civil justice** stayed with **District Judges** — option **(3)**.
**Munsiff courts** were created, not abolished, by the **Madras Regulations of 1816**.
xa: **Munro** headed the Judicial Commission (**1814**); report submitted **April 1816**.
Munro (**1816**) moved **police supervision from judges to Collectors**.
**1818**: magistrates got powers to punish.

168.s: The Madras Board of Revenue was established in:
168.x: The Madras Board of Revenue was set up in 1786 and became the state-level apex of the revenue hierarchy.
168.tq: Distinguish the Board's establishment year from the years of territorial acquisition and judicial reform.
xs: The **Madras Board of Revenue** was set up in **1786** — option **(2)**.
It was the **state-level apex** of the revenue hierarchy.
xa: Hierarchy: Board of Revenue → **Collector** → Sub-Collector → **Tahsildar** → Firka Revenue Inspector → **Karanam, Munsab**.
**Andhra Board of Revenue** formed in **1953** after Andhra State was created.
⚠ **1793** = Cornwallis' Permanent Settlement and Code.

168.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Revenue level)
A. State
B. District
C. Taluk
D. Village

List-II (Officer)
1. Tahsildar
2. Collector
3. Board of Revenue
4. Karanam and Munsab

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
168.x: The Board of Revenue was at the state level, the Collector at the district level, the Tahsildar at the taluk level and the Karanam and Munsab at the village level.
168.tq: Start from the sure state and village pairs, then complete the intermediate levels.
xs: **State — Board of Revenue**, **District — Collector**, **Taluk — Tahsildar**, **Village — Karanam and Munsab** = **A-3, B-2, C-1, D-4** — option **(1)**.
The **Board of Revenue** sat at the apex, the **Collector** was the district pivot, and the **Tahsildar** ran the taluk.
xa: Division: **Sub-Collector / Revenue Officer**; Firka: **Deputy Tahsildar / Firka Revenue Inspector**.
Karanam and Munsab were **hereditary** village officers.
The **Madras Board of Revenue** dates from **1786**.

168.s: The Andhra Board of Revenue was formed in 1953 primarily to:
o: link the government with the districts after the creation of Andhra State
transfer the Ceded Districts to the Nizam
abolish the office of the District Collector
168.x: The Andhra Board of Revenue was formed in 1953 after Andhra State was created. It served as a link between the government and the districts.
168.tq: Identify the institution's purpose from the administrative transition that produced it.
xs: The **Andhra Board of Revenue (1953)** was formed after **Andhra State** was created, to **link the government and the districts** — option **(1)**.
It continued the Board-at-the-top structure; the **Collector** stayed the district pivot.
xa: The **Madras Board of Revenue** was set up in **1786**.
The **District Collector** (revenue + magisterial + police powers) was the pivot of British rule.
Current angle: the Supreme Court (CJI **Surya Kant**) issued notice on a plea for a separate "revenue judicial service", under **Art. 14**.

168.s: In the Madras Presidency, the Collector's administration was introduced in place of the Revenue Board in the year:
168.x: The APPSC Group 2 (2012) key gives 1786, the year the Madras Board of Revenue was set up. 1766 is the Circar lease. 1802 is when the Permanent Settlement and Ryotwari were applied in Andhra. 1816 is when Collectors lost their judicial powers.
168.tq: PYQ wording 'Collector in place of Revenue Board' = 1786.
xs: In the PYQ wording, the Collector's administration replaced the Revenue Board in **1786** — option **(2)** (**APPSC G2 2012** key).
The notes date the **Collector system** in coastal Andhra to **1794**; for this exact wording, answer **1786**.
xa: **1786** is also the year of the **Madras Board of Revenue**.
**1816**: Collectors lost judicial powers.
**1802**: Permanent Settlement in Andhra; Ryotwari in the Ceded Districts.

168.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
168.x: West Godavari was created in 1925, not 1911. Kurnool, Anantapur, and Guntur with East Godavari were associated with 1858, 1882, and 1904 respectively.
168.tq: Find the one incorrect district-formation year.
xs: **West Godavari — 1911** is wrong: it was formed in **1925** — option **(4)**.
Correct: **Guntur and East Godavari — 1904**, **Kurnool — 1858**, **Anantapur — 1882**.
xa: **1911** = **Chittoor** carved out, giving **Kadapa** its present area.
Coastal Andhra had **5 districts**: **Ganjam, Visakhapatnam, Godavari, Krishna, Nellore**.
⚠ Exam angle: the **Kadapa 1911** trap.

168.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the five coastal collectorates?
168.x: The five coastal collectorates were Ganjam, Visakhapatnam, Godavari, Krishna and Nellore. Kurnool belonged to the Ceded Territory.
168.tq: Separate coastal districts from Ceded Territory districts.
xs: **Kurnool** was not a coastal collectorate — option **(2)**.
The five coastal ones: **Ganjam, Visakhapatnam, Godavari, Krishna, Nellore**.
xa: Krishna's HQ was **Machilipatnam**.
**Kurnool** district was formed in **1858**.
By **1856**, 8 collectorates: the five coastal + **Bellary, Cuddapah, Kurnool**.

168.s:
Consider the following statements about the initial collectorates of the Andhra region:
1. Ganjam was one of them.
2. Bellary was one of them.
3. Kurnool was one of them.
4. Chittoor was one of them.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
168.x: The initial eight collectorates included Ganjam, Bellary and Kurnool, but not Chittoor. Chittoor was formed later in 1911.
168.tq: Test membership in a historically specific administrative list.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**Ganjam**, **Bellary** and **Kurnool** were among the 8 collectorates (with Visakhapatnam, Godavari, Krishna, Nellore, Cuddapah).
**Chittoor** was carved out only in **1911** — statement 4 is wrong.
xa: The Ceded collectorate was split into **Bellary and Cuddapah** in **1808**.
Some notes list **Kadapa** for Cuddapah among the initial 8.

168.s: Chittoor district was carved out, giving Kadapa its present area, in the year:
168.x: Chittoor was carved out in 1911, which gave Kadapa its present area. 1858 is when Kurnool district was created, 1882 Anantapur, and 1904 Guntur and East Godavari.
168.tq: Chittoor 1911; WG 1925 is the last.
xs: **Chittoor** was carved out in **1911**, giving **Kadapa** its present area — option **(4)**.
**1858** = Kurnool; **1882** = Anantapur; **1904** = Guntur and East Godavari.
xa: **West Godavari** followed in **1925**.
Chittoor and Nellore had been taken from the Carnatic in **1801**.

168.s: ‘Peshkash’ refers to:
o: The share of revenue paid by zamindars to the British
Revenue collected by zamindars from farmers
168.x: Peshkash was the share of revenue paid by zamindars to the British.
168.tq: Discriminate among closely related colonial revenue terms.
xs: **Peshkash** = the share of revenue / tribute **zamindars paid to the British** — option **(2)**.
**Haveli lands** = land under direct British control; **Korunu** = revenue zamindars collected from farmers; **Moturpha** = tax on looms.
xa: **APP** spells it "**peshcush**"; "Peshcush is the revenue collected from zamindars" is true (**PYQ 2025**).
Zamindari lands: **9/10** of estimated revenue to government, **1/10** to the zamindar.
⚠ "**Moturpha** is a salt tax" is false — it was a **tax on looms** (**APPSC G2 2011**).

168.s: Haveli lands in coastal Andhra were lands:
o: Assigned to the Nizam as military grants
168.x: Haveli lands were under the direct control of the British in coastal Andhra.
168.tq: Identify the exact ownership or control category.
xs: **Haveli lands** were lands **held directly under British control** in coastal Andhra — option **(3)**.
Lands held by zamindars were **zamindari lands**, a separate category.
xa: Zamindari lands: **9/10** of estimated revenue to government, **1/10** to the zamindar; agreements ran for **10** years.
**Peshkash** = tribute zamindars paid to the British; **Korunu** = revenue zamindars collected from farmers.
⚠ **Peshkash** = zamindar → British; **Korunu** = farmer → zamindar.

168.s: Which tax was imposed on inland transit and customs duties on goods?
168.x: Sayer was the tax imposed on inland transit and customs duties on goods.
168.tq: Discriminate among the four revenue terms by the taxable activity.
xs: **Sayer** = inland **transit and customs duties** on goods — option **(2)**.
**Moturpha** = tax on **looms** (trades and occupations); **Abkari** = excise on **liquor and toddy**; **Peshcush** = zamindars' tribute.
xa: **Haveli lands** = lands under **direct British control**.
The **Madras Native Association's 1861** petition complained about **Moturpha**.
⚠ "**Moturpha** is a salt tax" is false (**APPSC G2 2011** key: tax on looms).

168.s: Abkari was primarily an excise imposed on:
168.x: Abkari was the excise levied on liquor and toddy.
168.tq: Match the tax name with the specific commodity or activity on which it was imposed.
xs: **Abkari** = excise on **liquor and toddy** — option **(4)**.
Looms and shops were taxed by **Moturpha**; zamindars' tribute was **Peshkash**; inland transit by **Sayer**.
xa: **Korunu** = revenue zamindars collected from farmers.
"**Peshcush** is the revenue collected from zamindars" — true (**PYQ 2025**).

168.s: Moturpha was levied mainly on which of the following?
o: Trades and occupations such as looms, shops and artisan activities
168.x: Moturpha was imposed on trades and occupations, including looms, shops and artisans. It was not a salt tax.
168.tq: Separate the look-alike revenue terms by identifying the actual taxable activity.
xs: **Moturpha** was a tax on **trades and occupations — looms, shops, artisans** — option **(1)**.
It was **not a salt tax**; liquor and toddy fell under **Abkari**, and zamindars' land revenue was **Peshkash**.
xa: **APPSC G2 2011** key: Moturpha = **tax on looms**.
The **Madras Native Association's 1861** petition complained about it.
**Sayer** = inland transit and customs duties.

168.s: The 1861 petition of the Madras Native Association complained specifically about which tax?
168.x: The Madras Native Association's petition of 1861 complained about the burden of Moturpha.
168.tq: Link the dated petition to the particular tax rather than to a general revenue category.
xs: The **Madras Native Association's 1861** petition complained about **Moturpha** — option **(3)**.
Moturpha was a **tax on looms** and other trades and occupations.
xa: ⚠ Moturpha was **NOT a salt tax** — a favourite statement trap.
**Sayer** = transit duties; **Abkari** = liquor excise; **Peshcush** = zamindars' tribute.

168.s: Under the Coastal Andhra Zamindari arrangement, approximately what proportion of the estimated revenue went to the government and the zamindar respectively?
168.x: About nine-tenths of the estimated revenue went to the government and one-tenth to the zamindar.
168.tq: Read the revenue-sharing ratio carefully and avoid reversing the parties.
xs: On zamindari lands, **nine-tenths (9/10)** of the estimated revenue went to the **government** and **one-tenth (1/10)** to the **zamindar** — option **(1)**.
These agreements ran for **10** years.
xa: **Korunu** = what zamindars collected from farmers; **Peshkash** = what they paid the British.
**Haveli lands** were under **direct British control**.
The **Permanent Settlement** (applied **1802**) made zamindars **fixed-revenue** holders.

168.s: The Permanent Settlement replaced the earlier practice of auctioning zamindaris with:
o: A tax collected only from artisans
168.x: The Permanent Settlement introduced a fixed revenue demand in place of the auctioning of zamindaris.
168.tq: Distinguish the reform measure from unrelated revenue practices.
xs: The **Permanent Settlement** replaced the **auction** of zamindaris with a **fixed revenue demand** — option **(2)**.
Introduced by **Cornwallis** in **1793**; applied in Andhra in **1802**.
xa: Estates under it: **Vizianagaram, Bobbili, Pithapuram**.
Effect: **absentee landlordism**; tenants impoverished.
The **Circuit Committee** had opposed the **auction (highest-bidder)** system.

168.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the revenue systems in the Andhra region:
1. Vizianagaram, Bobbili and Pithapuram were estates under the Zamindari system.
2. Ryotwari settlement was made directly with the cultivator.
3. Mahalwari settlement was associated with village headmen collecting revenue.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
168.x: All three statements are correct. Zamindari applied to estates such as Vizianagaram, Bobbili and Pithapuram; Ryotwari dealt directly with the ryot; and Mahalwari involved collection through village headmen.
168.tq: Test a comparison table by separating the settlement unit and collecting agency.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **Vizianagaram, Bobbili, Pithapuram** were **zamindari** (Permanent Settlement) estates.
Statement 2: **Ryotwari** was settled with the **ryot (cultivator)** directly.
Statement 3: **Mahalwari** = village headmen collect; placed in **Nellore**.
xa: Ryotwari began in **Rayalaseema** and later spread to most of Coastal Andhra.
Zamindari abolished by the **Madras Estates Act, 1948**.

168.s: Which one of the following best describes an important effect of the Zamindari system in the Northern Circars?
o: Uniform assessment limited to one-fourth of the produce
Transfer of all land rights to village headmen
Absentee landlordism and impoverishment of tenants
168.x: The Zamindari system encouraged absentee landlordism and contributed to the impoverishment of tenants.
168.tq: Identify the consequence rather than the formal structure of the system.
xs: The zamindari system led to **absentee landlordism** and **impoverished tenants** — option **(3)**.
Zamindars remained **intermediaries** — the system did not abolish them.
xa: Estates: **Vizianagaram, Bobbili, Pithapuram**, under the **Permanent Settlement (1802)**.
Ryotwari's effect, by contrast: **over-assessment** (often **50%+** of produce), moneylenders and land alienation.
Abolished by the **Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948**.

168.s: Which of the following was a major consequence associated with the Ryotwari system in the Andhra region?
o: Abolition of direct contact between cultivator and government
Over-assessment, indebtedness to moneylenders and land alienation
Fixed revenue payable only by zamindars
168.x: Ryotwari areas experienced heavy assessment, often exceeding 50 percent of the produce, along with dependence on moneylenders and alienation of land.
168.tq: Link the revenue arrangement with its stated economic consequences.
xs: **Ryotwari** brought **over-assessment** (often **50%+** of produce), **moneylenders** and **land alienation** — option **(2)**.
Ryotwari was settled with the **ryot directly** — it did not abolish that contact or work through zamindars.
xa: First region: **Baramahal (1792)** under **Captain Alexander Read** with **Munro**.
In Andhra it began in the **Ceded Districts in 1802**; extended across Madras in **1820**.
Zamindari's effect: absentee landlordism, impoverished tenants.

168.s: Mahalwari settlement, in the classification used for the Andhra region, was associated with which area?
168.x: The Mahalwari system, under which village headmen collected revenue, is placed in Nellore in the stated classification.
168.tq: Use location-based discrimination among neighbouring revenue systems.
xs: **Mahalwari** (village headmen collect) is placed in **Nellore** — option **(3)**.
**Vizianagaram** and **Pithapuram** were **zamindari** estates; **Bellary** was a Ceded District under **Ryotwari**.
xa: Zamindari: Northern Circars estates; Ryotwari: Rayalaseema first, then most of Coastal Andhra.
Nellore came from the **Carnatic** in **1801**.

168.s: The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948 came into force on:
168.x: The 1948 Act abolishing the Zamindari system came into force on 7 September 1949.
168.tq: Distinguish the year of an Act from the date on which it came into force.
xs: The **Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948** came into force on **7 September 1949** — option **(4)**.
It converted the zamindari estates into **Ryotwari** — settlement directly with the cultivator.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say "**1952**", but exam keys use the **1948** Act.
It ended the zamindari of estates like **Vizianagaram, Bobbili, Pithapuram** brought under the Permanent Settlement in **1802**.
**APPSC 2025** order: Guntur → Padmanabham → Ryotwari in Madras → abolition of zamindari.

168.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Officer)
A. Alexander Read with Thomas Munro
B. Thomas Munro

List-II (Region and year)
1. Ceded Districts, 1802
2. Baramahal, 1792

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
168.x: Read and Munro conducted the Baramahal experiment in 1792, while Munro's experiment in the Ceded Districts dates to 1802.
168.tq: Start from the officer-region pair that is most distinctive, then eliminate the remaining codes.
xs: **Alexander Read with Munro — Baramahal, 1792**; **Munro — Ceded Districts, 1802** = **A–2, B–1** — option **(2)**.
**Baramahal** (now **Salem/Krishnagiri**, Tamil Nadu) was the first Ryotwari region.
xa: Munro brought **Ryotwari** from the **Bara Mahals** to the Ceded Districts.
Ryotwari extended across **Madras** in **1820** under Governor Munro.
Munro surveyed the Ceded Districts **1802-07**.

168.s: Which of the following correctly represents the regional distribution of Zamindari and Ryotwari in Andhra?
o: Zamindari in the Northern Circars and Ryotwari in Rayalaseema, later extending to most of Andhra
Zamindari in Rayalaseema and Ryotwari in the Northern Circars
Ryotwari in the Northern Circars and Zamindari in the Ceded Districts
Both Zamindari and Ryotwari were confined to Nellore
168.x: Zamindari prevailed in the Northern Circars, while Ryotwari was associated with Rayalaseema and later covered most of Andhra.
168.tq: Use the AP regional contrast as the decisive clue.
xs: **Zamindari** in the **Northern Circars**; **Ryotwari** in **Rayalaseema**, later most of Andhra — option **(1)**.
Circar estates: **Vizianagaram, Bobbili, Pithapuram**; Ryotwari began in the **Ceded Districts in 1802**.
xa: **Mahalwari** is placed in **Nellore**.
Zamindari settled with the zamindar (intermediary); Ryotwari with the ryot directly.
Effects: zamindari → absentee landlordism; ryotwari → over-assessment, moneylenders.

168.s: The Permanent Settlement, introduced by Cornwallis in 1793, was applied to the Andhra zamindaris in:
168.x: It was applied in Andhra in 1802, replacing the earlier auction of zamindaris with a fixed demand. 1794 is when the Collector system began. 1800 is the cession of the Ceded Districts. 1820 is when Ryotwari was extended across Madras under Munro.
168.tq: Cornwallis 1793 Bengal; Andhra 1802.
xs: The **Permanent Settlement** (**Cornwallis**, **1793**) was applied in Andhra in **1802** — option **(3)**.
**1802** is also when **Ryotwari** began in the **Ceded Districts**.
xa: Before **1802**, zamindaris were given by **auction**.
**1794** = Collector system; **1800** = Ceded Districts; **1820** = Ryotwari across Madras.

168.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the judicial hierarchy in the Madras Presidency?
168.x: The Munsiff Court functioned at the taluk level, while the Zilla Court functioned at the district level. Sadar Adalats were apex courts for natives at Madras.
168.tq: Use the administrative level as the anchor for matching the court.
xs: **Taluk — Munsiff Court** is correct — option **(3)**.
The **Zilla Court** was at the **district** level; **Sadar Adalat** was the apex civil court at Madras.
xa: Appeal: **Provincial Courts of Appeal / Circuit courts** (powers expanded in **1820**).
Apex criminal court: **Sadar Faujdari Adalat**.
**Madras Supreme Court (1801)** for British subjects in Madras town.

168.s: The Zilla or District Court functioned under a District Judge. The post of District Judge was created by the:
168.x: The post of District Judge was created under the Cornwallis Code of 1793. The Madras Regulations of 1816 related chiefly to Munsiff and Panchayat courts.
168.tq: Use the legislation–office association and reject neighbouring judicial enactments.
xs: The **District Judge** post was created by the **Cornwallis Code, 1793** — option **(1)**.
The **Madras District Police Act** came in **1859**; the **Madras Regulations of 1816** set up **Munsiff** and **Panchayat** courts.
xa: District courts were also called **Zilla** courts.
After the **1816** separation, civil justice stayed with the District Judge.

168.s: The Madras Supreme Court established in 1801 primarily exercised jurisdiction over:
o: All village panchayats in the Ceded Districts
Revenue disputes only in the Northern Circars
Native subjects throughout the Madras Presidency
168.x: The Madras Supreme Court, established in 1801, dealt with British subjects in Madras town. It was distinct from the Sadar courts for natives.
168.tq: Distinguish courts by their subject jurisdiction and territorial coverage.
xs: The **Madras Supreme Court (1801)** served **British subjects in Madras town** — option **(2)**.
For natives, the apex courts were the **Sadar Adalat** (civil) and **Sadar Faujdari Adalat** (criminal).
xa: Taluk: **Munsiff court**; district: **Zilla court**.

168.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. CPC — 1859
2. IPC — 1860
3. CrPC — 1861
168.x: The Civil Procedure Code was associated with 1859, the Indian Penal Code with 1860 and the Criminal Procedure Code with 1861.
168.tq: Test the coded year associations individually rather than relying on the sequence alone.
xs: All three pairs are correct: **CPC — 1859**, **IPC — 1860**, **CrPC — 1861** — option **(4)**.
Civil procedure came first (**1859**), the penal code next (**1860**), and criminal procedure last (**1861**).
xa: **Madras District Police Act** — also **1859**.
Criticism: slow, costly British procedure displaced village **panchayats** → litigation and debt.

168.s: The introduction of British judicial procedure in place of village panchayats was criticised mainly because it:
o: was slow and costly and contributed to litigation and debt
made justice quicker and less expensive
reduced litigation and eliminated rural debt
transferred all judicial powers to hereditary village officers
168.x: British judicial procedure displaced village panchayats and was criticised as slow and costly. It increased litigation and contributed to indebtedness.
168.tq: Select the option that combines all the stated consequences without reversing the criticism.
xs: British procedure was **slow and costly** and fed **litigation and debt**, displacing village panchayats — option **(1)**.
It did not make justice quicker or cheaper, nor reduce rural debt.
xa: **Munro**'s **1816** Regulations set up **Munsiff** and **Panchayat** courts as courts of first instance.
Village officials handled **petty thefts**.
The **District Collector** became the pivot of British rule and ended village autonomy.

168.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Thomas Munro:
1. He was the President of the Judicial Commission in 1814.
2. The report of the Judicial Commission was submitted in April 1816.
3. Most of the recommendations in the report were accepted.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
168.x: All three statements are correct. Munro presided over the Judicial Commission in 1814, whose report was submitted in April 1816 and was largely accepted.
168.tq: Combine office, date and outcome in a single administrative sequence.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **Munro** was **President** of the Judicial Commission in **1814**.
Statement 2: the report was submitted in **April 1816**.
Statement 3: its recommendations were **mostly accepted**.
xa: Result: the **Madras Regulations of 1816** — Munsiff and Panchayat courts.
**1818**: magistrates got powers to punish.

168.s: The Madras Regulations of 1816 provided for:
o: Abolition of all village-level judicial institutions
Munsiff and Panchayat courts as courts of first instance
Transfer of civil justice from District Judges to Collectors
Creation of the Madras High Court
168.x: The Madras Regulations of 1816 established Munsiff courts and Panchayat courts in every large village and district as courts of first instance.
168.tq: Match the regulation with its immediate institutional reform.
xs: The **Madras Regulations of 1816** set up **Munsiff and Panchayat courts** as **courts of first instance** — option **(2)**.
They strengthened, not abolished, village-level justice: village officials handled **petty thefts**.
xa: Panchayat courts were set up in every large village and district.
Same year (**1816**): Collectors lost judicial powers; civil justice stayed with **District Judges**.
Munro (**1816**) moved **police supervision** from judges to **Collectors**.

168.s: Who created thanas under the supervision of darogas in the early British police administration?
168.x: Cornwallis created thanas under darogas, who were Indian officers assisted by constables. Darogas were criticised for abusing their power.
168.tq: Use the founder–institution association and avoid swapping judicial and police reformers.
xs: **Lord Cornwallis** created **thanas** under **darogas** (Indian officers) with constables — option **(4)**.
Darogas were known for **abuse of power**.
xa: In **Madras**, village watchmen were supplemented by central police under a **District Superintendent**.
**Munro (1816)** moved police supervision from judges to **Collectors**.
**Madras District Police Act**: **1859**.

168.s: In the Madras Presidency, the traditional village watchmen were:
o: placed directly under the Sadar Adalat
abolished and replaced by military courts
supplemented by a central police force under a District Superintendent
168.x: Traditional village watchmen continued but were supplemented by a central police force under a District Superintendent. The force was feared because of corruption.
168.tq: Distinguish supplementation from abolition or replacement.
xs: In **Madras**, village watchmen were **supplemented by a central police force under a District Superintendent** — option **(4)**.
This police too was feared for **corruption**.
xa: **Cornwallis** created **thanas** under **darogas**.
**Munro (1816)**: police supervision from judges to **Collectors**.
**Madras District Police Act**, **1859**.

168.s: Munro's police reforms of 1816 transferred police supervision from:
o: Darogas to the Board of Revenue
168.x: Munro's changes in 1816 transferred police supervision from judges to Collectors. This was part of the reorganisation of administrative powers.
168.tq: Test the direction of transfer by identifying both the former and new authority.
xs: **Munro**'s **1816** reform moved police supervision **from judges to Collectors** — option **(1)**.
**Darogas** belonged to **Cornwallis'** thana system; the **District Superintendent** headed the central police.
xa: Munro presided over the **Judicial Commission (1814)**; report **April 1816**.
Under ryotwari, some magisterial powers returned to Collectors.
The Collector combined **revenue + magisterial + police** powers — the pivot of British rule.

168.s: The Madras District Police Act was enacted in:
168.x: The Madras District Police Act dates to 1859. 1816 is when Munro moved police supervision from judges to Collectors, and 1820 is when the appeal courts' powers were expanded and Munro became Governor.
168.tq: Use the year-specific legislation trap and distinguish it from the judicial enactments.
xs: The **Madras District Police Act** was passed in **1859** — option **(3)**.
**1816** = Munro's reforms; **1820** = Ryotwari across Madras and expanded appeal-court powers.
xa: **1859** is also the year of the **CPC**; **IPC 1860**, **CrPC 1861**.
Earlier, **Cornwallis** created **thanas** under **darogas**.

168.s: Who became the first Collector of the Ceded Districts in 1800?
168.x: Thomas Munro became the first Collector of the Ceded Districts in 1800, with sub-collectors stationed at Harpanahalli, Kadapa, Adoni and Kurnool.
168.tq: Identify the official associated with the first administrative appointment.
xs: **Sir Thomas Munro** became the **first Principal Collector of the Ceded Districts** in **1800** — option **(1)**.
**Arthur Cotton** was an irrigation engineer; **C.P. Brown** a Telugu scholar; **George Russell** took the Vizianagaram forts after **1794**.
xa: Munro had **four sub-collectors** at **Harpanahalli, Kadapa, Adoni, Kurnool**.
⚠ Some notes say "first Collector … in **1802**" (CDX).
He suppressed the **palegars**, introduced **Ryotwari**, and died at **Pattikonda** on **6 July 1827**.

168.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Thomas Munro — Introduced Ryotwari and surveyed the districts from 1802 to 1807
C.P. Brown — Built the Dowleswaram anicut
George Russell — Governor of Madras from 1820 to 1827
168.x: Munro introduced Ryotwari and surveyed the Ceded Districts during 1802–07. Arthur Cotton was the irrigation engineer, C.P. Brown was the Telugu scholar, and Munro—not George Russell—was Governor of Madras from 1820 to 1827.
168.tq: Catch the swapped official-and-work trap.
xs: **Munro** introduced **Ryotwari** and surveyed the districts **1802-07** — option **(1)**.
**Cotton** built the **Dowleswaram anicut**; **Brown** published **Vemana**'s verses; **Munro**, not Russell, was Governor of Madras **1820-27**.
xa: **George Russell** took charge of the Vizianagaram forts after Padmanabham.
⚠ **Cotton**'s assistant = **Veenam Veeranna**; **Brown** = Vemana.

168.s: Thomas Munro served as Governor of Madras during:
168.x: Thomas Munro was Governor of Madras from 1820 to 1827.
168.tq: Use the official’s career dates to distinguish administrative posts.
xs: **Munro** was **Governor of Madras 1820-27** — option **(2)**.
He died in office at **Pattikonda** (Kurnool) on **6 July 1827**.
xa: Under him **Ryotwari** was extended across **Madras** in **1820**.
**1800-1808**: Principal Collector of the single Ceded collectorate at **Anantapur**.

168.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Veenam Veeranna — Andhra assistant to Arthur Cotton
168.x: The Dowleswaram anicut was built across the Godavari. Arthur Cotton built the Krishna anicut at Vijayawada, and Veenam Veeranna served as his Andhra assistant.
168.tq: Find the reversed river-location association.
xs: **Dowleswaram anicut — Krishna** is wrong: Dowleswaram is on the **Godavari** — option **(1)**.
The others are correct: **Veenam Veeranna** was Cotton's Andhra assistant; the **Krishna anicut** is at **Vijayawada**.
xa: **Sir Arthur Cotton** built both anicuts.
**Veenam Veeranna** = **APPSC G2 2019** key.

168.s: Which work is associated with C.P. Brown?
o: The construction of the Krishna anicut
Publication of Vemana’s verses and a Telugu-English dictionary
A survey of the Ceded Districts from 1802 to 1807
Suppression of the palegars of Rayalaseema
168.x: C.P. Brown studied Telugu thoroughly and published Vemana’s verses as well as a Telugu-English dictionary.
168.tq: Match the scholar with his literary contribution.
xs: **C.P. Brown** published **Vemana**'s verses and a **Telugu-English dictionary** — option **(2)**.
The **Krishna anicut** was **Cotton's**; the **1802-07** survey and the suppression of **palegars** were **Munro's**.
xa: Brown studied Telugu thoroughly; with **Munro**, a rare Telugu-learning official.
⚠ **Brown** = Vemana; **Cotton** = anicuts.

168.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Shah Alam II issued the firman relating to the Northern Circars in 1765.
2. The Northern Circars were transferred under a treaty in 1766.
3. The Treaty of Masulipatnam settled the dispute in 1768.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
168.x: All three statements are correct: the firman was issued in 1765, the treaty transferring the Circars was concluded in 1766, and the Treaty of Masulipatnam settled the dispute in 1768.
168.tq: Link successive constitutional and political events in a dated sequence.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **Shah Alam II**'s firman for the Northern Circars — **1765**.
Statement 2: the Circars were leased by **Nizam Ali** (Guntur excepted) under the **1766** treaty.
Statement 3: the **Treaty of Masulipatnam (1768)** settled the dispute.
xa: **Guntur** was handed over in **1788**.
The firman was secured by **Robert Clive**.

168.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam
B. Guntur handed over to the British
C. Treaty of Masulipatnam
D. Battle of Padmanabham
168.x: The correct order is Treaty of Masulipatnam (1768), Guntur handed over (1788), Battle of Padmanabham (1794), and Subsidiary Alliance (1798).
168.tq: Arrange events by their dates, beginning with the earliest sure event.
xs: Order: **Masulipatnam (1768)** → **Guntur (1788)** → **Padmanabham (1794)** → **Subsidiary Alliance (1798)** = **C, B, D, A** — option **(1)**.
**Guntur** was excepted from the **1766** lease and handed over only in **1788**, for **7 lakh**.
xa: **1800**: Ceded Districts; **1801**: Nellore and Chittoor.
Masulipatnam (**1768**) fixed a **peshkash of 9 lakh** plus military help to the Nizam.

168.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. 1794 — Battle of Padmanabham
2. 1800 — Ceded Districts obtained from the Nizam
3. 1801 — Nellore and Chittoor annexed
4. 1802 — Ryotwari introduced in the Ceded Districts
168.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. These events occurred in 1794, 1800, 1801 and 1802 respectively.
168.tq: Check each year–event pair rather than relying on one familiar date.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**1794** Padmanabham; **1800** Ceded Districts; **1801** Nellore and Chittoor; **1802** Ryotwari in the Ceded Districts.
xa: **1794** also saw the **Collector system** begin.
**1801**: Andhra merged into the **Madras Presidency**.
**1808**: Ceded Districts split into **Bellary and Cuddapah**.

168.s: The Ceded Districts were divided into Bellary and Cuddapah in:
168.x: The Ceded Territory was divided into the districts of Bellary and Cuddapah in 1808.
168.tq: Separate the date of acquisition from the date of territorial division.
xs: The Ceded Districts were split into **Bellary and Cuddapah** in **1808** — option **(3)**.
Until then a single collectorate (**1800**) was centred at **Anantapur** under **Munro**.
xa: ⚠ **APPSC 2011** key = **Bellary** as HQ — refers to the post-1808 period.
**Kurnool** district came in **1858**; **Anantapur** in **1882**.

168.s:
Which one of the following was the correct sequence of the four events?
A. Ryotwari extended across Madras
B. Abolition of zamindari in Madras
C. Guntur handed over to the British
D. Battle of Padmanabham
168.x: The events occurred in 1788, 1794, 1820 and 1948 respectively: Guntur, Padmanabham, extension of Ryotwari, and abolition of zamindari.
168.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest and latest dates.
xs: Order: **Guntur (1788)** → **Padmanabham (1794)** → **Ryotwari across Madras (1820)** → **zamindari abolition (1948 Act)** = **C, D, A, B** — option **(1)**.
This was the **APPSC 2025** sequence question.
xa: The 1948 Act came into force on **7 Sep 1949**.
Ryotwari was extended across Madras under Governor **Munro**.

168.s: During the early administration of the Northern Circars, collectors relied on which intermediaries?
168.x: Collectors relied on dubashis for administrative and local assistance. Munro and C.P. Brown were noted as rare Company officials who learned Telugu.
168.tq: Identify the local intermediary rather than the formal revenue officer.
xs: Collectors who did not know Telugu depended on corrupt **dubashis** — option **(2)**.
**Munro** and **Brown** were the exceptions — rare Telugu learners; Munro needed no interpreters.
xa: The famous dubashi **Kandregula Jogipantulu** negotiated the Circar lease.
The **District Collector** held revenue, magisterial and police powers.

168.s:
Consider the following statements regarding sericulture in Rayalaseema:
1. British promotion of the crop in the Ceded Districts dates to the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.
2. Dharmavaram and Madanapalle are present-day silk hubs.
3. The crop was introduced into Rayalaseema only after the formation of Andhra State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
168.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The historical association is with British promotion in the Ceded Districts during the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, not only after Andhra State was formed.
168.tq: Reject the absolute time claim and retain the two historically precise statements.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: British promotion in the "**Ceded Districts**" dates to the late 19th-early 20th centuries.
Statement 2: today's silk hubs are **Dharmavaram** and **Madanapalle**.
Statement 3 is wrong: sericulture predates Andhra State.
xa: Ceded Districts = **Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur, Bellary**.
Name **Rayalaseema** adopted in **1928**.

168.s:
Which of the following is the correct chronological order in which major territorial components of present-day Andhra took shape under Company rule?

A. Ceded Districts
B. Circars
C. Nellore-Chittoor
D. Guntur
168.x: The Circars came under Company control in 1766, Guntur in 1788, the Ceded Districts in 1800 and Nellore-Chittoor in 1801.
168.tq: Fix the earliest and latest territorial changes first, then place the middle events by year.
xs: Order: **Circars (1766)** → **Guntur (1788)** → **Ceded Districts (1800)** → **Nellore-Chittoor (1801)** = **B, D, A, C** — option **(1)**.
The **Circars** were leased in **1766**, **Guntur** followed in **1788**, and the **Ceded Districts** came in lieu of the subsidy in **1800**.
xa: The Circars and Ceded Districts came from the Nizam; **Nellore-Chittoor** from the **Carnatic**.
**Telangana** stayed under the Nizam.

168.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the territorial contrast under British and Nizam rule?
o: The coast and Rayalaseema passed to the Company, while Telangana remained under the Nizam.
Telangana passed to the Company, while the coast remained with the Nizam.
Rayalaseema remained under the Nizam, while Telangana passed to the Company.
The entire Andhra region remained under the Nizam until 1953.
168.x: The coast and Rayalaseema came under Company rule, whereas Telangana remained under the Nizam. This produced an important political and administrative contrast within the Telugu-speaking regions.
168.tq: Use the paired regional contrast and beware of reversing the two territories.
xs: The **coast and Rayalaseema** passed to the **Company**, while **Telangana** stayed under the **Nizam** — option **(1)**.
**Northern Circars** + **Ceded Districts** = almost all of today's **Coastal Andhra** and **Rayalaseema**.
xa: Coast: Circars (**1766**), Guntur (**1788**), Nellore-Chittoor (**1801**); Rayalaseema: Ceded Districts (**1800**).
By **1801** all this was merged into the **Madras Presidency**.

168.s: The growing divergence between the fertile and educated Circars and the arid and neglected Ceded Districts later influenced debates surrounding the:
168.x: The contrasting development of the Circars and the Ceded Districts later shaped the Sri Bagh Pact debate. The other pacts belong to different political contexts.
168.tq: Link a regional socio-economic contrast with the agreement it later influenced.
xs: The divergence between the **fertile, educated Circars** and the **arid, neglected Ceded Districts** later shaped the **Sri Bagh Pact** debate — option **(2)**.
The Circars came to the Company in **1766**; the Ceded Districts only in **1800**, and they grew apart under British rule.
xa: Ceded Districts = today's **Rayalaseema**; name adopted at **Nandyal, 1928**.
The Circars correspond to **Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, East and West Godavari, Krishna + Guntur**.

168.s: Which of the following statements about Thomas Munro in the Andhra region is correct?
o: He introduced mahalwari settlement from Punjab into the Ceded Districts and died at Hyderabad in 1827.
He introduced permanent settlement from Bengal into the Circars and died at Madras in 1801.
He introduced zamindari in Rayalaseema and died at Nellore in 1816.
He introduced ryotwari from the Bara Mahals into the Ceded Districts and died at Pattikonda as Governor in 1827.
168.x: Munro brought the ryotwari system from the Bara Mahals to the Ceded Districts. He died at Pattikonda in Kurnool district in 1827 while serving as Governor.
168.tq: Combine the reformer's policy, source region, destination and death details without swapping settlement systems.
xs: **Munro** brought **Ryotwari** from the **Bara Mahals** to the Ceded Districts and died as Governor at **Pattikonda** in **1827** — option **(4)**.
The **Permanent Settlement** was Cornwallis's, not Munro's; Munro died at Pattikonda (**Kurnool**), not Hyderabad.
xa: In Baramahal (**1792**) he worked with **Captain Alexander Read**.
Date of death: **6 July 1827**; Governor of Madras **1820-27**.

168.s: The concentration of revenue, magisterial and police powers in the office of the District Collector made the Collector the:
o: pivot of British rule and an agent of the end of village autonomy
hereditary head of the Board of Revenue
chief appellate judge of the Madras Supreme Court
168.x: By combining revenue, magisterial and police powers, the District Collector became the pivot of British administration. This concentration of authority weakened village autonomy.
168.tq: Infer institutional importance from the combination of powers held by one office.
xs: With **revenue, magisterial and police** powers, the Collector became the **pivot of British rule** and **ended village autonomy** — option **(1)**.
He was neither a hereditary officer nor a judge of the **Madras Supreme Court** — he was the district head of the revenue hierarchy.
xa: From **1794** each district had a **Collector**; judicial powers were removed in **1816**.
**Munro (1816)** moved police supervision to Collectors.
District → **Collector**; State → **Board of Revenue (1786)**.

168.s: A plea before the Supreme Court sought a separate revenue judicial service cadre on the ground that revenue officers without legal training should not decide land-title disputes. The plea invoked which constitutional provision?
168.x: The plea invoked Article 14 and argued that officers without legal training should not adjudicate land-title disputes. The Supreme Court issued notice on the plea.
168.tq: Identify the constitutional article directly linked to the stated legal argument.
xs: The plea for a separate "**revenue judicial service**" invoked **Article 14** (**Art. 14**) — option **(3)**.
It argues that revenue officers **without legal training** should not decide **land-title** disputes; the Supreme Court (CJI **Surya Kant**) issued notice.
xa: After **1816**, civil justice stayed with the **District Judge**, apart from the Collector.
The **Andhra Board of Revenue** was formed in **1953**.

169.s: After Crown rule, Rajahmundry and Machilipatnam were reorganised into Godavari and Krishna districts in:
169.x: In 1859, Rajahmundry and Machilipatnam were reorganised into Godavari and Krishna districts respectively.
169.tq: Test the chronology of district renaming and reorganisation.
xs: In **1859** (Crown rule), **Rajahmundry** and **Machilipatnam** were reorganised into **Godavari** and **Krishna** districts — option **(3)**.
**1802** was the union of Rajahmundry and **Kakinada** collectorates; **1904** was Guntur and East Godavari.
xa: The new names were given on the suggestion of **Cotton**.
**West Godavari** followed in **1925**.
⚠ **1904** = Guntur + East Godavari; **1925** = West Godavari; **1859** = Godavari + Krishna.

169.s:
Arrange the following district developments in chronological order:
A. Formation of West Godavari district
B. Union of Rajahmundry and Kakinada collectorates
C. Reorganisation into Godavari and Krishna districts
D. Formation of Guntur and East Godavari districts
169.x: The correct order is 1802, 1859, 1904 and 1925: union of collectorates, reorganisation into Godavari and Krishna, formation of Guntur and East Godavari, and formation of West Godavari.
169.tq: Fix the first and last events, then arrange the two middle reorganisation stages.
xs: Order: **Rajahmundry + Kakinada (1802)** → **Godavari and Krishna (1859)** → **Guntur and East Godavari (1904)** → **West Godavari (1925)** = **B, C, D, A** — option **(1)**.
The **1859** change came under **Crown rule**, on **Cotton**'s suggestion.
xa: **Ganjam** Collector was also **Agent to the Governor** for the Agency tracts from **1819**.
The Godavari and Krishna deltas are the "**Rice Bowl of Andhra**".

169.s: In Ganjam, the Collector also acted as Agent to the Governor for the Agency tracts from:
169.x: From 1819, the Collector in Ganjam also acted as Agent to the Governor for the Agency tracts.
169.tq: Test the exceptional regional role and its starting year.
xs: The **Ganjam Collector** was also **Agent to the Governor** for the **Agency tracts** from **1819** — option **(3)**.
**1802** = Rajahmundry district formed; **1815** = Mackenzie became first Surveyor General.
xa: District changes: **1802** Rajahmundry, **1859** Godavari and Krishna, **1904** Guntur and East Godavari, **1925** West Godavari.
⚠ **1904** = Guntur + East Godavari; **1925** = West Godavari.

169.s: C.P. Brown served as Collector of:
169.x: C.P. Brown served as the Collector of Kadapa.
169.tq: Test the administrator–district association without confusing it with other postings.
xs: **C.P. Brown** was **Kadapa Collector** — option **(3)**.
He led the **Telugu revival**, edited the **Madras Literary Journal** and was Curator of the **Madras Manuscript Library**.
xa: Brown lived **1798-1884**.
**G.N. Taylor** was **Rajahmundry** Sub-Collector — started **Anglo-Vernacular schools**.
⚠ **Mackenzie** = first Surveyor General; **Brown** = Madras Literary Journal; **Taylor** = Anglo-Vernacular schools.

169.s: Which of the following was associated with C.P. Brown?
o: Serving as the first Surveyor General in 1815
Introducing ryotwari and suppressing the palegars
Editing the Madras Literary Journal and serving as Curator of the Madras Manuscript Library
169.x: C.P. Brown contributed to Telugu revival, edited the Madras Literary Journal and served as Curator of the Madras Manuscript Library.
169.tq: Use a contribution cluster to distinguish one administrator from neighbouring personalities.
xs: **C.P. Brown** edited the **Madras Literary Journal** and was **Curator of the Madras Manuscript Library** — option **(4)**.
**Anglo-Vernacular schools** = **G.N. Taylor**; first **Surveyor General (1815)** = **Colin Mackenzie**.
xa: Brown was **Kadapa Collector** and a leader of the **Telugu revival**.
**Mackenzie** (**1754-1821**) preserved manuscripts and records.
**Taylor**'s schools were a **PYQ 2017** question.

169.s: Colin Mackenzie became the first Surveyor General in:
169.x: Colin Mackenzie was the first Surveyor General in 1815 and also preserved manuscripts and records.
169.tq: Separate the appointment year from the administrator’s lifespan and other dates.
xs: **Colin Mackenzie** became the **first Surveyor General** in **1815** — option **(2)**.
He lived **1754-1821**; **1798** is C.P. Brown's birth year.
xa: Mackenzie **preserved manuscripts and records**.
⚠ **Mackenzie** = Surveyor General; **Brown** = Manuscript Library curator.

169.s: G.N. Taylor is associated with which of the following contributions?
169.x: G.N. Taylor, Rajahmundry Sub-Collector, started Anglo-Vernacular schools across Andhra.
169.tq: Avoid the swapped-contribution trap among British administrators.
xs: **G.N. Taylor**, **Rajahmundry Sub-Collector**, started **Anglo-Vernacular schools** across Andhra — option **(1)** (**PYQ 2017**).
**Dowleswaram** = **Cotton**; Surveyor General = **Mackenzie**.
xa: **C.P. Brown** = Telugu revival, **Madras Literary Journal**.
**M.G. Ranade** called **Veeresalingam** "South India's **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**".

169.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Administrator)
a. Arthur Cotton
b. C.P. Brown
c. Colin Mackenzie
d. Thomas Munro
List-II (Contribution)
i. Ryotwari and suppression of the palegars
ii. Godavari and Krishna anicuts
iii. Telugu revival and manuscript-library work
iv. Surveyor General and preservation of records
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
169.x: Arthur Cotton built the major anicuts; C.P. Brown contributed to Telugu revival and manuscript work; Colin Mackenzie preserved records; and Thomas Munro introduced ryotwari and suppressed the palegars.
169.tq: Start with the distinctive anicuts–Cotton pair and complete the administrative matches.
xs: **Cotton — anicuts**, **Brown — Telugu revival and manuscript library**, **Mackenzie — Surveyor General and records**, **Munro — Ryotwari and palegars** = **a–ii, b–iii, c–iv, d–i** — option **(1)**.
Cotton built the **Godavari and Krishna anicuts**; Mackenzie was first Surveyor General in **1815**.
xa: Cotton was knighted in **1861** and called "**Apara Bhagiratha**" and "**Cotton Dora**".
Brown was **Kadapa** Collector and Curator of the **Madras Manuscript Library**.

169.s: The proposal for constructing an anicut near Rajahmundry was urged by Arthur Cotton before the Board of Revenue in which year?
169.x: Arthur Cotton reported to the Board of Revenue in 1844, urging the construction of an anicut near Rajahmundry.
169.tq: Test the precise year associated with the administrative proposal.
xs: **Cotton** reported to the **Board of Revenue** in **1844**, urging an anicut near **Rajahmundry** — option **(2)**.
It was **sanctioned late 1846** and **begun in 1847**; main work completed **April 1852**.
xa: Trigger: the **Guntur famine (1832-33)**.
Cost: **Rs 1.5 lakh**; assistant **Veenam Veeranna**.

169.s: The immediate trigger for Arthur Cotton's proposal for an anicut near Rajahmundry was the:
169.x: The Guntur famine of 1832–33 prompted the proposal for an anicut near Rajahmundry.
169.tq: Link a public-works proposal with its immediate historical cause.
xs: The trigger was the **Guntur famine (1832-33)** — option **(2)**.
Cotton's report followed in **1844**, leading to the **Dowleswaram** anicut.
xa: The **Buckingham Canal** was extended as famine relief in **1876-78**.
Reduced land under food crops made the region **famine-prone**.

169.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Dowleswaram anicut:
1. It was sanctioned in 1844, the year Arthur Cotton reported to the Board of Revenue.
2. It was begun in 1847 and its main work was completed in April 1852.
3. Its Indian assistant, Veenam Veeranna, was made Rao Bahadur and Assistant Engineer.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
169.x: Statement 1 is wrong: Cotton reported to the Board of Revenue in 1844, but the anicut was sanctioned only in late 1846. Statement 2 is correct: work began in 1847 and the main work was completed in April 1852. Statement 3 is correct: Veenam Veeranna was made Rao Bahadur and Assistant Engineer. Hence 2 and 3 only; options with 1 are wrong.
169.tq: 1844 = proposal, 1846 = sanction, 1847 = start, 1852 = completion.
xs: Statements 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 2 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 wrong: **1844** was Cotton's report; the anicut was **sanctioned late 1846**.
Statement 2 correct: begun **1847**, main work completed **April 1852**.
Statement 3 correct: **Veenam Veeranna** was made "**Rao Bahadur**" and Assistant Engineer.
xa: Cost: **Rs 1.5 lakh**.
⚠ **PYQ key = 1855** (**APPSC G2 2012**) for the Dowleswaram year.

169.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Anicut or work)
a. Krishna anicut, Bezwada
b. Penna anicut, Nellore
c. K.C. Canal
d. Sangam anicut
List-II (River or location)
i. Penna, Nellore district
ii. Tungabhadra at Sunkesula
iii. Krishna
iv. Penna
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
169.x: The Krishna anicut was on the Krishna, the Penna anicut was at Nellore, the K.C. Canal was associated with the Tungabhadra at Sunkesula, and the Sangam anicut was on the Penna.
169.tq: Start from the sure river-location pairs and eliminate incompatible codes.
xs: **Krishna anicut — Krishna**, **Penna anicut — Penna, Nellore district**, **K.C. Canal — Tungabhadra at Sunkesula**, **Sangam anicut — Penna** = **a–iii, b–i, c–ii, d–iv** — option **(1)**.
The **Sangam anicut** is also on the **Penna** in **Nellore** district.
xa: Penna anicut (**1860**) and Krishna anicut were both on **Cotton**'s plan.

169.s: The Krishna anicut at Bezwada, now associated with the Prakasam Barrage, was built by Charles Orr on the plan of:
169.x: Charles Orr built the Krishna anicut on Arthur Cotton's plan. Col. Henry Atlock (Lake) had proposed it.
169.tq: Use the builder–plan–proposal distinction to avoid a swapped-person trap.
xs: **Charles Orr** built the **Krishna anicut** at Bezwada on the plan of **Arthur Cotton** — option **(1)**.
It was **proposed** by **Col. Henry Atlock (Lake)** and built **1852/53-1855**.
xa: It is now the **Prakasam Barrage**.
In **Feb 2026**, automated crest-gate telemetry + **SCADA** were installed there.
The **Penna anicut**, Nellore (**1860**), also followed Cotton's plan.

169.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
169.x: The Krishna anicut at Bezwada was constructed during 1852–55, not in 1872. The K.C. Canal dates to 1872, while Dowleswaram was begun in 1847 and the Penna anicut dates to 1860.
169.tq: Find the single wrong date among closely related irrigation works.
xs: **Krishna anicut — 1872** is wrong: it was built **1852/53-1855** — option **(1)**.
Correct: **Penna anicut — 1860**, **K.C. Canal — 1872**, **Dowleswaram begun 1847**.
xa: The Krishna anicut was built by **Charles Orr** on **Cotton**'s plan.
The **K.C. Canal** draws from the **Tungabhadra** at **Sunkesula**.

169.s:
Consider the following statements about Sir Arthur Cotton:
1. He was knighted in 1861.
2. He was popularly called "Apara Bhagiratha" and "Cotton Dora".
3. On his suggestion, Rajahmundry and Machilipatnam districts were renamed Krishna and Godavari respectively.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
169.x: Statement 1 is correct: Cotton was knighted in 1861. Statement 2 is correct: he was called Apara Bhagiratha and Cotton Dora. Statement 3 is wrong: Rajahmundry became Godavari and Machilipatnam became Krishna, not the reverse. So 1 and 2 only; '1 only' misses statement 2, and the options with 3 are wrong.
169.tq: Rajahmundry sits on the Godavari, so it became Godavari district.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: Cotton was **knighted in 1861**.
Statement 2: he was called "**Apara Bhagiratha**" and "**Cotton Dora**".
Statement 3 wrong: in **1859** Rajahmundry became **Godavari** and Machilipatnam **Krishna** — the statement swaps them.
xa: Cotton's **1844** report urged an anicut near **Rajahmundry**.
His assistant: **Veenam Veeranna** at **Dowleswaram**.

169.s: In the APPSC Group 2 (2012) answer key, the Dowleswaram anicut across the Godavari is dated to:
169.x: The key gives 1855. The main work was finished in April 1852, so if both 1852 and 1855 appear among the options, follow the PYQ key. 1832 is the start of the Guntur famine that triggered the scheme. 1844 is the year Cotton reported to the Board of Revenue. 1872 is the K.C. Canal.
169.tq: Dowleswaram: built 1847-52, PYQ key 1855.
xs: The **APPSC G2 2012** key dates Dowleswaram to **1855** — option **(3)**.
Most notes give **1852** as the commissioning year (some **1850**); answer **1855** when the options force it.
xa: Begun **1847**; main work completed **April 1852**; cost **Rs 1.5 lakh**.
**1844** = Cotton's report; **1872** = K.C. Canal.

169.s: The Ramapada Sagaram project, the forerunner of today's Polavaram project, was proposed by:
