169.x: Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy proposed Ramapada Sagaram (PYQ 2019). Cotton built the Dowleswaram anicut. Veenam Veeranna was Cotton's Indian assistant there. Charles Orr built the Krishna anicut at Bezwada.
169.tq: Ramapada Sagaram = Polavaram, Venkataramamurthy.
xs: **Ramapada Sagaram** was proposed by **Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy** — option **(3)** (**PYQ 2019**).
It is the forerunner of today's **Polavaram** project.
xa: **Veenam Veeranna** was Cotton's assistant at **Dowleswaram**.
**Charles Orr** built the **Krishna anicut**.

169.s: The principal role of the railways that reached Andhra in the late nineteenth century was to:
o: Link the interior with the Madras port
Link Andhra exclusively with Bombay port
Connect only the Agency tracts with Calcutta
169.x: The railways linked the interior of Andhra with the port of Madras, facilitating movement and trade.
169.tq: Test the direction and commercial purpose of an early transport link.
xs: Railways reaching Andhra in the late 19th century **linked the interior to Madras port** — option **(1)**.
They did not replace coastal waterways — the **Buckingham Canal** was still extended in **1876-78**.
xa: **Vizagapatnam port** began developing for **iron ore + farm exports**.
The **Buckingham Canal** ran along the coast through **Pulicat Lake**.

169.s: During the British period, Vizagapatnam port began developing particularly for the export of:
169.x: Vizagapatnam port developed for the movement of iron ore and agricultural exports.
169.tq: Match a port with its stated export commodities.
xs: **Vizagapatnam port** began developing for **iron ore** and **farm** exports — option **(1)**.
Railways meanwhile linked the interior to **Madras** port.
xa: Cash revenue pushed farmers to **commercial crops** — **tobacco (Guntur)**, indigo, cotton, oilseeds.
The **Buckingham Canal** is now part of **NW-4 (Kakinada-Puducherry)**.

169.s:
Consider the following statements about the Buckingham Canal:
1. It is a salt-water navigation canal running along the coast through Pulicat Lake.
2. Along with the Eluru and Kakinada canals, it is now part of National Waterway-5.
3. It was extended as a famine-relief measure during 1876-78.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
169.x: Statement 1 is correct: it is a salt-water navigation canal along the coast through Pulicat Lake. Statement 2 is wrong: it is part of NW-4 (Kakinada-Puducherry), not NW-5. Statement 3 is correct: it was extended as famine relief in 1876-78. Hence 1 and 3 only; '1 only' misses 3 and the options with 2 are wrong.
169.tq: NW-4 = Kakinada-Puducherry, the Andhra-Tamil coast waterway.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: a **salt-water navigation canal** along the coast through **Pulicat Lake**.
Statement 2 wrong: with the **Eluru** and **Kakinada** canals it is part of **NW-4**, not NW-5.
Statement 3: extended as **famine relief** in **1876-78**.
xa: NW-4 runs **Kakinada-Puducherry**.
Railways linked Andhra's interior to **Madras** port.

169.s: Which one of the following was a major feature of the economic impact of British rule on handicrafts in Andhra?
o: Handicrafts were protected by complete prohibition of imported goods.
Artisans received increased traditional patronage from local courts.
British manufactured goods entered the market duty-free and artisans lost patronage.
Artisans were shifted exclusively to government employment.
169.x: Deindustrialisation occurred because artisans lost traditional patronage and British goods entered duty-free.
169.tq: Identify the correct cause-effect explanation for deindustrialisation.
xs: **British goods entered duty-free** and **artisans lost patronage** — option **(3)** (deindustrialisation).
Imports were not banned, and local patronage shrank rather than grew.
xa: Revenue payable in **cash** pushed a shift to **commercial crops**.
Less land under food made the region **famine-prone**.

169.s: Why did the cash revenue demand encourage farmers to shift towards commercial crops?
o: Food crops were exempt from revenue, so farmers abandoned all commercial crops.
Farmers received fixed cash subsidies for growing only cotton.
Revenue had to be paid in cash, encouraging cultivation of tobacco, indigo, cotton and oilseeds.
The government prohibited the cultivation of rice throughout Andhra.
169.x: Since land revenue had to be paid in cash, farmers increasingly cultivated commercial crops such as tobacco, indigo, cotton and oilseeds.
169.tq: Apply the cash-revenue mechanism to the observed change in cropping pattern.
xs: Because **revenue had to be paid in cash**, farmers grew **tobacco, indigo, cotton and oilseeds** — option **(3)**.
**Tobacco** was the classic **Guntur** cash crop.
xa: Less land under food crops → region **famine-prone**.
Most people still depended on agriculture; **rice** was the main crop.

169.s: The reduction of land under food crops made the region more:
169.x: The shift from food crops to commercial crops reduced food availability and made the region more vulnerable to famines.
169.tq: Follow the chain from commercialisation to food insecurity and famine vulnerability.
xs: Less land under food crops made the region **famine-prone** — option **(4)**.
Cash revenue had pushed farmers to **commercial crops** — tobacco, indigo, cotton, oilseeds.
xa: **Guntur famine (1832-33)** triggered Cotton's anicut proposal.
**Buckingham Canal** extended as famine relief in **1876-78**.

169.s:
Consider the following statements about agriculture in Andhra under British rule:
1. Most people depended on agriculture.
2. Rice was the main crop.
3. Commercial crops completely replaced food crops in all districts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
169.x: Most people depended on agriculture and rice was the main crop. Commercial crops did not completely replace food crops in all districts.
169.tq: Reject the absolute statement while retaining the two supported agricultural facts.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **most people depended on agriculture**; statement 2: **rice** was the main crop.
Statement 3 wrong: commercial crops spread, but **reduced** rather than replaced food crops.
xa: Commercial crops: **tobacco (Guntur)**, indigo, cotton, oilseeds.
Godavari and Krishna deltas = "**Rice Bowl of Andhra**".

169.s: Who called Kandukuri Veeresalingam the 'Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar of South India'?
169.x: M.G. Ranade gave Veeresalingam this title (APPSC G2 2019). Dadabhai Naoroji and Tilak were nationalist leaders, and neither gave the title. Ram Mohan Roy died in 1833, before Veeresalingam was born.
169.tq: Ranade: Veeresalingam = Vidyasagar of the South.
xs: **M.G. Ranade** called **Veeresalingam** "South India's **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**" — option **(1)** (**APPSC G2 2019**).
The link: both were leading social reformers.
xa: **G.N. Taylor** started **Anglo-Vernacular schools** across Andhra.
**C.P. Brown** led the **Telugu revival**.

169.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage:
1. Its length is 5.837 kilometres.
2. It was rebuilt in 1969.
3. It irrigates approximately 10 lakh acres.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
169.x: All three statements are correct: the barrage is 5.837 kilometres long, was rebuilt in 1969, and irrigates about 10 lakh acres.
169.tq: Verify each numerical statement independently before selecting the combined option.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: length **5.837-km**; statement 2: rebuilt in **1969**; statement 3: irrigates **10 lakh acres**.
xa: Foundation laid **13 Jul 2026** for replacing **117 gates**, at **₹152.95 crore**, due by **July 2028**.
July 2026 floods: over **5.2 lakh cusecs** discharged.
The original **Dowleswaram** anicut: begun **1847**, cost **Rs 1.5 lakh**.

169.s: Automated crest-gate telemetry and SCADA were installed at which barrage in February 2026?
169.x: Automated crest-gate telemetry and SCADA were installed at the Prakasam Barrage in February 2026.
169.tq: Apply the location-and-year pair to distinguish similar irrigation structures.
xs: Telemetry and **SCADA** were installed at the **Prakasam Barrage** in **Feb 2026** — option **(3)**.
The Prakasam Barrage stands on the old **Krishna anicut** at **Bezwada**.
xa: The **Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage** (Godavari) is getting **117** new gates.
The Krishna anicut was built by **Charles Orr** on Cotton's plan, **1852/53-1855**.

169.s: Which of the following correctly describes the significance of the Godavari and Krishna deltas in Andhra Pradesh?
o: They are known as the Cotton Bowl of Andhra.
They are known as the Mineral Bowl of Andhra.
They are known as the Rice Bowl of Andhra.
They are known as the Industrial Bowl of Andhra.
169.x: The Godavari and Krishna deltas are collectively known as the “Rice Bowl of Andhra” because of their importance for rice cultivation.
169.tq: Match the distinctive regional title with the correct geographical area.
xs: The **Godavari** and **Krishna** deltas are the "**Rice Bowl of Andhra**" — option **(3)**.
Cotton's **Dowleswaram** and **Krishna** anicuts irrigated them.
xa: **Rice** was the main crop under British rule.
The Cotton Barrage irrigates **10 lakh acres**.

170.s: Which one of the following series of wars covered the period 1746–1763?
170.x: The Carnatic Wars were fought during the period 1746–1763.
170.tq: Match the war series with its span and distinguish overlapping conflicts.
xs: The **Carnatic Wars** spanned **1746-63** — option **(4)**.
xa: **Anglo-Sikh Wars** = **1845-49**.
**Wandiwash (1760)** fell within the Carnatic Wars.
Order of the big three: **Mysore → Maratha → Sikh**.

170.s: Which statement best explains the historical significance of the Anglo-Maratha Wars?
o: The wars ended before the Mysore Wars began.
The British effectively acquired India from the Marathas rather than from the Mughals.
The Marathas were defeated by the Sikhs in these wars.
The Marathas established British rule over Bengal.

Maratha wars: **3** wars; Mysore wars: **4** wars in **32** years.

170.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the broad order of the three major series of wars?
o: Anglo-Maratha Wars, Anglo-Mysore Wars, Anglo-Sikh Wars

Anglo-Mysore Wars, Anglo-Sikh Wars, Anglo-Maratha Wars

xs: The Maratha wars began during the Mysore wars, but ended later.

170.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:

170.s:
Consider the following statements about the First Anglo-Mysore War:
1. It was fought during 1767-69 against Haidar Ali.

170.tq: No Governor-General before 1773 - any 1760s event with a 'GG' is a trap.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.

Nizam + Marathas + British had allied against **Hyder**.

Consider the following statements about the Second Anglo-Mysore War:

xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.

**Porto Novo (1781)**: **Eyre Coote** defeated Hyder.

170.s: Why did the Second Anglo-Mysore War break out, according to the stated circumstances?

170.s: Tipu Sultan's attack on Travancore in 1789 was significant because Travancore was

the capital of the Nizam's dominions
a French possession and Mysore's principal naval base
a British ally and the Company's only pepper supplier

170.s: Which of the following correctly states the British concern behind the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War?

170.s: Under the Treaty of Seringapatam (1792), which ended the Third Anglo-Mysore War, Tipu Sultan:

The British surrendered Salsette and recognised Raghunath Rao
The Marathas accepted the Subsidiary Alliance
The Peshwaship was abolished and Poona was annexed
170.x: The Treaty of Salbai restored the status quo, allowed the British to retain Salsette and ushered in approximately twenty years of peace.
170.tq: Separate the settlement terms of Salbai from those of Bassein and the later war.
xs: At **Salbai** the **status quo** was restored, the British kept **Salsette**, and **20 years of peace** followed — option **(1)**.
The Subsidiary Alliance came with **Bassein (1802)**; the Peshwa-ship ended in **1818**.
xa: Signed by **Warren Hastings and Mahadji Scindia**.
Some notes add **Bassein** to Salsette.

170.s: The Treaty of Salbai (1782) was concluded between:
170.x: Salbai was signed by the British (Warren Hastings) and the Marathas (Mahadji Scindia), and it ended the First Anglo-Maratha War (APPSC 2018). The British made peace with Mysore at Mangalore in 1784. The Marathas fought the Nizam at Kharda in 1795. The Nizam's treaties with the British came at Masulipatnam (1768) and Hyderabad (1798).
170.tq: Salbai = British + Marathas, 1782.
xs: **Salbai (1782)** was between the **British and the Marathas** — option **(1)** (**APPSC 2018**).
Signed by **Warren Hastings** and **Mahadji Scindia**.
xa: It ended the First Anglo-Maratha War; status quo, **Salsette** kept.
**APPSC-G2 2023** match: Hastings → **Salbai**; Minto I → **Amritsar**; Hardinge I → **Lahore**.

170.s:
With reference to the political status of Indian states under British paramountcy, consider the following statements:
1. Indian states retained their internal administration.
2. They possessed complete international freedom.
3. The British interfered in internal matters to fulfil their international commitments.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
170.x: Indian states generally retained internal administration but had no independent international life. British intervention in internal matters was justified partly by their international commitments.
170.tq: Spot the reversed meaning of the phrase ‘no international life’.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: states kept their **internal administration**.
Statement 2 wrong: they had **"no international life"**.
Statement 3: the British intervened **to give effect to their international commitments** (**APPSC-G2 2017**).
xa: Another ground: **misgovernance** (**Coorg, Awadh**).
**Lord Hastings** turned subsidiary alliances into **paramountcy**.

170.s: The British intervened in the internal administration of Indian states on the ground of misgovernance in the case of:
170.x: Misgovernance was cited as a ground for intervention and annexation in Coorg and Awadh.
170.tq: Pair the stated ground of intervention with the two associated territories.
xs: **Coorg and Awadh** were taken on the ground of **misgovernance** — option **(1)**.
**Coorg** (**1834**, **Bentinck**); **Sikkim** was over two detained doctors; **Berar** was assigned by treaty; **Sindh** and **Punjab** were conquests.
xa: Four grounds: **conquest**, **lapse**, **misgovernance**, **abolition of titles**.
**Central Cachar** was also annexed in **1834**.

170.s: Who converted the policy of subsidiary alliances into a wider system of paramountcy?
170.x: Lord Hastings developed subsidiary alliances into the system of British paramountcy and imposed humiliating treaties on the Peshwa and Scindia.
170.tq: Distinguish the architect of paramountcy from the Governor-General associated with the Doctrine of Lapse.
xs: **Lord Hastings** turned subsidiary alliances into **paramountcy** — option **(2)**.
**Wellesley** began the Subsidiary Alliance; **Hardinge** and **Dalhousie** fought the Sikh wars.
xa: He imposed humiliating treaties on the **Peshwa** and **Scindia**.
**Rajputana (1818)**: Udaipur, Jaipur, Jodhpur accepted subordinate alliances.

170.s: Under the subordinate alliances accepted by Rajputana states in 1818, the states:
o: surrendered their internal administration but retained foreign relations
were exempted from all British political control
gave up their external relations in return for British protection
became directly administered provinces of the Company
170.x: The Rajputana states accepted British protection and surrendered control over their external relations under subordinate alliances in 1818.
170.tq: Apply the protection-for-external-control structure of a subordinate alliance.
xs: Rajputana states **gave up external relations in return for British protection** — option **(3)**.
They kept their **internal administration**, but had **"no international life"**.
xa: States: **Udaipur, Jaipur, Jodhpur** and others (**1818**).
Lord Hastings' era: Anglo-Nepalese War (**1814-16**), 3rd Anglo-Maratha, Pindaris.

170.s: Sindh was annexed by the British in 1843 during the Governor-Generalship of:
170.x: The conquest and annexation of Sindh took place in 1843 under Lord Ellenborough.
170.tq: Link the annexation year with the correct Governor-General rather than with Dalhousie’s later expansion.
xs: **Sindh** was annexed in **1843** under **Lord Ellenborough** — option **(4)**.
**Auckland** = 1st Anglo-Afghan; **Hardinge** = 1st Anglo-Sikh; **Dalhousie** = 2nd Anglo-Sikh.
xa: Ellenborough (**1842-44**) also fought a war with **Gwalior**.
**Sir Charles Napier** annexed Sindh after **Miani and Dabo**.

170.s: Which of the following was NOT an objective of the British conquest of Sindh?
o: Recovering prestige lost in the First Afghan War
Securing the trade of the Indus
Introducing the Doctrine of Lapse in Sindh
170.x: The stated objectives were recovery of prestige after the First Afghan War, countering Russia and securing Indus trade. The Doctrine of Lapse was not an objective of the conquest of Sindh.
170.tq: Eliminate the policy that belongs to Dalhousie’s annexations rather than Sindh.
xs: **Introducing the Doctrine of Lapse** was not an aim — Sindh was a **conquest** — option **(3)**.
Real aims: recover prestige lost in the **1st Afghan War**, counter **Russia**, secure the **Indus** trade.
xa: Annexed **1843**, under **Ellenborough**.
Nickname: "**Tail of the Afghan Storm**".

170.s: Who adopted a bullying policy towards the Amirs of Sindh and annexed Sindh after the battles of Miani and Dabo?
170.x: Sir Charles Napier used coercive diplomacy against the Amirs and annexed Sindh after the battles of Miani and Dabo.
170.tq: Use the commander-deed association and avoid confusing Napier with the Governors-General.
xs: **Sir Charles Napier** bullied the **Amirs of Sindh** and annexed it after **Miani and Dabo** — option **(2)**.
**Bentinck** annexed **Coorg (1834)**; **Lord Hastings** fought the Third Maratha War.
xa: GG: **Lord Ellenborough** (**1843**).
Nickname: "**Tail of the Afghan Storm**".

170.s: The annexation of Sindh was described as the:
170.x: The British annexation of Sindh was called the ‘Tail of the Afghan Storm’.
170.tq: Test the exact historical expression rather than a plausible geographical description.
xs: Sindh's annexation was called the "**Tail of the Afghan Storm**" — option **(1)**.
It aimed to recover prestige lost in the **1st Afghan War** (**1839-42**).
xa: Annexed **1843** under **Ellenborough**, by **Charles Napier**.
Other aims: counter **Russia**; secure **Indus** trade.

170.s: Who was the Governor-General of India during the First Anglo-Sikh War (1845–46)?
170.x: Lord Hardinge was the Governor-General during the First Anglo-Sikh War, fought in 1845–46.
170.tq: Use the ruler-period association and distinguish Hardinge from Dalhousie.
xs: **Lord Hardinge** was GG during the **First Anglo-Sikh War (1845-46)** — option **(3)**.
**Dalhousie** = Second Anglo-Sikh war; **Ellenborough** = Sindh.
xa: Battles: **Mudki, Ferozeshah**, Aliwal, **Sobraon (1846)**.
Ended by **Lahore (1846)**; **Amritsar (Mar 1846)** sold **Kashmir** to **Gulab Singh**.

170.s: Which one of the following was the immediate cause of the First Anglo-Sikh War?
o: The murder of Vans Agnew and Anderson at Multan
The refusal of the Nizam to assign Berar
The Sikh army crossing the Sutlej
The detention of two British doctors in Sikkim
170.x: The First Anglo-Sikh War began when the Sikh army crossed the Sutlej, whose boundary had been fixed by the Treaty of Amritsar of 1809.
170.tq: Identify the immediate cause rather than a later Anglo-Sikh event.
xs: The **Sikh army crossed the Sutlej**, the boundary fixed at **Amritsar (1809)** — option **(3)**.
The **Multan** murders of **Vans Agnew and Anderson** caused the **Second** war.
xa: Punjab fell into chaos after **Ranjit Singh**'s death (**1839**, not 1836).
**Sobraon** was lost through the betrayal of **Lal Singh and Tej Singh**.

170.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the Lists.
List-I (Battle)
A. Mudki
B. Chillianwala
C. Gujrat
D. Sobraon
List-II (War)
1. First Anglo-Sikh War
2. Second Anglo-Sikh War

Codes:
170.x: Mudki and Sobraon belonged to the First Anglo-Sikh War, while Chillianwala and Gujrat belonged to the Second.
170.tq: Start from the sure battle-war pairs and use them to eliminate the mixed codes.
xs: **Mudki** and **Sobraon** = **First** Sikh war; **Chillianwala** and **Gujrat** = **Second** = **A-1, B-2, C-2, D-1** — option **(1)**.
First war (**1845-46**): **Mudki, Ferozeshah**, Aliwal, **Sobraon (1846)**; Second (**1848-49**): **Ramnagar, Chillianwala** (Jan 1849), **Gujrat** (21 Feb 1849).
xa: Sobraon was lost through the betrayal of **Lal Singh and Tej Singh**.
**Sir Hugh Gough** commanded at **Mudki** and **Chillianwala** (costly, indecisive).
GGs: **Hardinge** (first war), **Dalhousie** (second).

170.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the outcome of the Second Anglo-Sikh War?
o: Kashmir was annexed directly by the British in 1846.
Punjab was annexed by the British in 1849.
Punjab accepted a subsidiary alliance but retained complete sovereignty.
The Sikh army occupied territory south of the Sutlej.
170.x: The Second Anglo-Sikh War ended with the annexation of Punjab by the British in 1849.
170.tq: Match the war with its final political result and reject reversed outcomes.
xs: The Second Anglo-Sikh War ended with **Punjab annexed in 1849** — option **(2)**.
The **Kohinoor** was taken and **Duleep Singh** pensioned.
**Kashmir** was not annexed: it was sold to **Gulab Singh** in **1846**; crossing the **Sutlej** was the First war's cause.
xa: Trigger: murder of **Vans Agnew and Anderson** at **Multan**.
GG: **Lord Dalhousie** (**1848-56**).

170.s:
Which of the following events occurred after the First Anglo-Sikh War?
1. Treaty of Bhairowal
2. Transfer of Kashmir to Gulab Singh under a separate Treaty of Amritsar
3. Annexation of Punjab
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
170.x: The Treaties of Bhairowal and Amritsar followed the First Anglo-Sikh War. Punjab was annexed only after the Second Anglo-Sikh War in 1849.
170.tq: Use the sequence of treaties and annexation to reject the later event.
xs: Events 1 and 2 followed the First war — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
**Bhairowal (Dec 1846)**: the British **Resident** became virtual ruler.
**Amritsar (Mar 1846)**: **Kashmir** → **Gulab Singh** for **Rs 75 lakh**.
**Annexation of Punjab (1849)** came after the **Second** war.
xa: **Lahore (1846)**: land south of the Sutlej ceded, indemnity paid, Kashmir handed over.
⚠ Kashmir price: **Rs 75 lakh**; some notes say **Rs 1 crore**.

170.s: After the death of Ranjit Singh, Punjab fell into chaos in:
170.x: Ranjit Singh died in 1839, after which Punjab entered a period of political chaos.
170.tq: Distinguish the correct date from the tempting but incorrect 1836 reference.
xs: Punjab fell into chaos after **Ranjit Singh**'s death in **1839** — option **(2)**.
⚠ **1836** is a trap — the year is **1839**.
xa: The Sikh wars followed: **1845-46** and **1848-49**.
**Amritsar (1809)** had fixed the **Sutlej** as the boundary — under **Minto I**.

170.s: The Second Anglo-Sikh War (1848-49) was triggered by:
o: the Sikh army crossing the Sutlej
the murder of British officers Vans Agnew and Anderson at Multan
the death of Maharaja Ranjit Singh
the sale of Kashmir to Gulab Singh
170.x: It began after the British officers Vans Agnew and Anderson were murdered at Multan, under Dalhousie. The Sutlej crossing caused the First war (1845). Ranjit Singh's death in 1839 was the background to both wars. Kashmir went to Gulab Singh in 1846, after the First war.
170.tq: 1st war: Sutlej; 2nd war: Multan.
xs: The **murder of Vans Agnew and Anderson at Multan** triggered the Second war — option **(2)**.
Crossing the **Sutlej** was the First war's cause; Ranjit Singh died in **1839**; Kashmir was sold in **1846**.
xa: Battles: **Ramnagar, Chillianwala, Gujrat (1849)**.
Result: **Punjab annexed 1849**; **Kohinoor** taken.

170.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Coorg was annexed in 1834 by William Bentinck on the plea of misgovernance.
2. Central Cachar was taken along with Coorg.
3. Parts of Sikkim were annexed by Lord Hardinge in 1850 after two British doctors were detained.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
170.x: Statement 1 is correct: Bentinck took Coorg in 1834 citing misgovernance. Statement 2 is correct: Central Cachar was taken together with Coorg. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1850 Sikkim annexation was by Dalhousie, not Hardinge. So 1 and 2 only; '1 only' misses statement 2 and options with 3 are wrong.
170.tq: 1850 is inside Dalhousie's term (1848-56).
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Coorg** annexed **1834** by **Bentinck** for **misgovernance**.
Statement 2: **Central Cachar** was taken with it.
Statement 3 wrong: parts of **Sikkim** were taken in **1850** by **Dalhousie**, not Hardinge.
xa: The Sikkim pretext: two British doctors detained.
Misgovernance cases: **Coorg, Awadh**.

170.s: In 1855, the titles and pensions of the rulers of which territories were abolished?
170.x: The titles and pensions of the rulers of Karnataka, or Carnatic, and Tanjore were abolished in 1855.
170.tq: Test the exact territories associated with abolition of titles and pensions.
xs: In **1855**, rulers' titles and pensions were abolished in **Karnataka (Carnatic) and Tanjore** — option **(4)**.
**Coorg and Central Cachar** = **1834** misgovernance; **Awadh** and **Jhansi** = annexed; **Punjab** = conquest.
xa: Ground: **abolition of titles** — distinct from conquest, lapse and misgovernance.
**Nana Sahib** and the **Mughal house** also lost titles and pensions.

170.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The pension of Nana Sahib was stopped after the death of Baji Rao II.
2. Baji Rao II died in 1851.
3. Nana Sahib was the adopted son of Baji Rao II.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
170.x: All three statements are correct. Nana Sahib, the adopted son of Baji Rao II, was denied continuation of the Peshwa pension after Baji Rao II died in 1851.
170.tq: Combine relationship, date and policy consequence before choosing the complete code.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **Nana Sahib**'s **Peshwa pension** was stopped after **Baji Rao II** died.
Statement 2: Baji Rao II died in **1851**; statement 3: Nana Sahib was his **adopted son**.
xa: Baji Rao II had been deposed and pensioned after the **Third Maratha War**.
Loss of pensions turned **princes** against the Company before **1857**.

170.s: Berar was assigned to the British by the Nizam under the:
170.x: Berar was assigned by the Nizam under the Berar Treaty in 1853.
170.tq: Identify the treaty by its direct territorial association and avoid Anglo-Sikh treaty names.
xs: **Berar** was assigned by the **Nizam** under the **Berar Treaty (1853)** — option **(1)**.
**Bhairowal, Amritsar** and **Lahore** were Sikh treaties of **1846**.
xa: **Lower Burma (Pegu)** was annexed in **1852**.
**1855**: titles of **Carnatic** and **Tanjore** rulers abolished.

170.s:
Which of the following developments contributed to resentment against the East India Company before the Revolt of 1857?
1. Annexation of Awadh
2. Withdrawal of titles and pensions
3. Fear of further annexations among princes and taluqdars
4. Discontent among many Awadh sepoys
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
170.x: All four developments contributed to the growth of resentment. Awadh’s annexation, loss of privileges, fear of annexation and sepoy discontent helped create conditions for the Revolt of 1857.
170.tq: Recognize the cumulative nature of several connected causes rather than selecting a single grievance.
xs: All four contributed — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Annexation of Awadh** and **lapse** (Jhansi) bred resentment.
Loss of **titles and pensions** (**Nana Sahib**, the **Mughal house**) and fear of annexation turned **princes** and **taluqdars** against the Company.
Many **Awadh sepoys** were alienated.
xa: Lapse annexations **1848-54** + Awadh (**1856**) = grievances behind **1857**.
By **1856** British India stretched from the **Hindukush** to **Burma**.

170.s: Awadh was annexed by the British primarily because of its:
o: adoption of a foreign policy hostile to Russia
cotton market and agrarian wealth, with misgovernance also invoked
refusal to accept the Treaty of Amritsar
strategic control over the Indus trade alone
170.x: Awadh’s cotton market and agrarian wealth were important motives, while misgovernance was used as the formal justification. Its annexation generated immense resentment and contributed to the Revolt of 1857.
170.tq: Distinguish the economic motive from the formal administrative justification.
xs: Awadh was coveted for its **cotton market and agrarian wealth**, with **misgovernance** invoked as the ground — option **(2)**.
Its annexation "sparked immense resentment, leading to the **1857 Revolt**".
xa: Misgovernance was also the plea for **Coorg (1834)**.
**Indus trade** and countering **Russia** were aims behind **Sindh (1843)**.

170.s:
Consider the following statements about British territorial expansion by 1856:
1. British India extended from the Hindukush to Burma.
2. It gave India geographical unity and a basis for common resistance.
3. It ended the political resentment of Indian princes and taluqdars.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
170.x: Statement 1 is correct: by 1856 British India stretched from the Hindukush to Burma. Statement 2 is correct: this created geographical unity and a basis for common resistance. Statement 3 is wrong: annexations, Lapse and loss of titles and pensions turned princes, taluqdars and Awadh sepoys against the Company. Hence 1 and 2 only.
170.tq: Expansion fed 1857 - it did not calm resentment.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: by **1856** British India ran from the **Hindukush** to **Burma**.
Statement 2: this gave **geographical unity** and a basis for **common resistance**.
Statement 3 wrong: resentment of **princes** and **taluqdars** grew, feeding **1857**.
xa: Lapse (**Jhansi**) and lost pensions (**Nana Sahib**) alienated the princes.
After **1818** British **paramountcy** was unchallenged.

170.s: Who among the following was associated with the Rohilla War of 1774, the First Anglo-Maratha War and the Second Anglo-Mysore War?
170.x: Warren Hastings was Governor-General from 1772 to 1785 and his tenure included the Rohilla War, the First Anglo-Maratha War and the Second Anglo-Mysore War.
170.tq: Match the Governor-General with the cluster of wars fought during his tenure.
xs: **Warren Hastings** (**1772-85**) — **Rohilla War (1774)**, First Anglo-Maratha, Second Anglo-Mysore — option **(1)**.
**Cornwallis** = 3rd Mysore; **Wellesley** = 4th Mysore + 2nd Maratha; **Lord Hastings** = 3rd Maratha.
xa: Warren Hastings was impeached in **1787** (**Burke**).
He concluded **Salbai (1782)**.

170.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Cornwallis was Governor-General from 1786 to 1793.
2. The Third Anglo-Mysore War was fought during his tenure.
3. The Treaty of Seringapatam was concluded in 1792.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
170.x: All three statements are correct. Cornwallis's tenure covered the Third Anglo-Mysore War, which ended with the Treaty of Seringapatam in 1792.
170.tq: Check the tenure, war and treaty as one connected sequence.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **Cornwallis** was GG **1786-93**.
Statement 2: the **Third Anglo-Mysore War** fell in his tenure.
Statement 3: the **Treaty of Seringapatam** was signed in **1792**.
xa: Tipu gave up **half his territory**, paid **Rs 3 crore**, sent **two sons** as hostages.
Trigger: Tipu's attack on **Travancore (1789)**.

170.s: At the Battle of Kharda in 1795, the Marathas defeated the Nizam while the Governor-General was
170.x: Sir John Shore, Governor-General from 1793 to 1798, followed a policy of neutrality at Kharda, where the Marathas defeated the Nizam.
170.tq: Use the neutral-policy clue to identify the Governor-General.
xs: **Sir John Shore** (**1793-98**) stayed **neutral** at **Kharda (1795)** — option **(2)**.
The Nizam blamed Shore's neutrality and hired French troops under **Raymond**.
xa: This led to the Nizam's **Subsidiary Alliance (1798)** under **Wellesley**.
Resident **Kirkpatrick** reported the French battalions.

170.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Wellesley — Fourth Anglo-Mysore War and Second Anglo-Maratha War
2. Lord Hastings — Anglo-Nepalese War and Third Anglo-Maratha War
3. Ellenborough — Annexation of Sindh and war with Gwalior
4. Dalhousie — First Anglo-Sikh War and annexation of Lower Burma
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
170.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correctly matched. The First Anglo-Sikh War belonged to Hardinge; Dalhousie was associated with the Second Anglo-Sikh War and the annexation of Lower Burma.
170.tq: Detect the swapped war in the final Governor-General pairing.
xs: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**Wellesley** = 4th Mysore + 2nd Maratha; **Lord Hastings** = Nepal + 3rd Maratha; **Ellenborough** = Sindh + Gwalior.
Pair 4 wrong: **Dalhousie** fought the **Second** Anglo-Sikh War; the First was under **Hardinge**.
xa: Dalhousie did annex **Lower Burma (Pegu)**.
Nepal war: **1814-16** — ⚠ **1813-23** is Lord Hastings' tenure.

170.s: The Battle of Porto Novo, fought in 1781, belonged to the
170.x: Porto Novo was fought in 1781 during the Second Anglo-Mysore War. Eyre Coote defeated Haidar Ali in this battle.
170.tq: Match the battle year and war rather than the commander alone.
xs: **Porto Novo (1781)** belonged to the **Second Anglo-Mysore War** — option **(4)**.
**Eyre Coote** defeated Hyder there.
xa: Second war: **1780-84**; GG **Warren Hastings**.
Hyder died in **1782**; the war ended with **Mangalore (1784)**.

170.s: The battles of Assaye, Delhi and Laswari were associated with the
170.x: Assaye, Delhi and Laswari were important battles of the Second Anglo-Maratha War in 1803.
170.tq: Group battles by the war to which they belong.
xs: **Assaye, Delhi, Laswari** (all **1803**) = **Second Anglo-Maratha War** — option **(3)**.
**Arthur Wellesley** won at **Assaye**; **Lord Lake** at **Delhi** and **Laswari**.
xa: ⚠ **Arthur Wellesley** (later **Duke of Wellington**) ≠ Lord Wellesley the GG.

170.s:
Which of the following statements is correct?
1. Arthur Wellesley commanded the British forces at Assaye.
2. Lord Lake commanded the British forces at Delhi and Laswari.
3. Sir Hugh Gough commanded at Mudki and Chillianwala.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
170.x: All three statements are correct. Arthur Wellesley commanded at Assaye, Lord Lake at Delhi and Laswari, and Sir Hugh Gough at Mudki and Chillianwala.
170.tq: Verify repeated commander associations across different battles.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Arthur Wellesley** at **Assaye (1803)**; **Lord Lake** at **Delhi, Laswari (1803)**; **Sir Hugh Gough** at **Mudki (1845)** and **Chillianwala (1849)**.
xa: **Eyre Coote** commanded at **Porto Novo (1781)**.
Chillianwala was **costly and indecisive**.

170.s: Chillianwala was a battle of the
o: Second Anglo-Maratha War and was fought under Lord Lake
First Anglo-Sikh War and was decisive for the British
Second Anglo-Sikh War and was costly and indecisive
Anglo-Nepalese War and was fought under Lord Hastings
170.x: Chillianwala was fought in 1849 during the Second Anglo-Sikh War. The battle under Sir Hugh Gough was costly and indecisive.
170.tq: Reject the wrong war and the reversed assessment of the battle.
xs: **Chillianwala** was in the **Second Anglo-Sikh War** and was **costly and indecisive** — option **(3)**.
Fought **Jan 1849** under **Sir Hugh Gough**; **Lord Lake** belongs to the Maratha war.
xa: The decisive battle was **Gujrat** (21 Feb 1849).
Result: **Punjab annexed 1849**.

170.s: The Anglo-Nepal War of 1814–1816 and the Treaty of Sugauli were associated with:
170.x: The Anglo-Nepal War took place during the tenure of Marquess Hastings, and the Treaty of Sugauli was concluded in 1816.
170.tq: Use the war period and treaty year together to identify the correct tenure.
xs: The **Anglo-Nepal War (1814-16)** and **Sugauli (1816)** belong to **Marquess (Lord) Hastings** — option **(4)** (**APPSC-GS 2018**).
**Amherst** = 1st Burmese; **Minto I** = Amritsar (1809); **Auckland** = 1st Afghan.
xa: Lord Hastings also fought the **3rd Anglo-Maratha** war and the **Pindaris**.
⚠ **1813-23** is his tenure, not the war's dates.

170.s: The Treaty of Yandabo, which ended the First Anglo-Burmese War, was concluded during the tenure of:
170.x: The First Anglo-Burmese War occurred from 1824 to 1826 during Amherst’s tenure, and the Treaty of Yandabo transferred Assam, Manipur, Arakan and Tenasserim to the British sphere.
170.tq: Match the treaty with the war and the Governor-General in office.
xs: **Yandabo** ended the **1st Anglo-Burmese War (1824-26)** under **Amherst** — option **(2)**.
Gains: **Assam, Manipur, Arakan, Tenasserim**.
xa: The **2nd Burmese war (1852)** was under **Dalhousie** — Lower Burma annexed.
**Auckland** = 1st Anglo-Afghan (**1839-42**).

170.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
170.x: The Second Anglo-Burmese War was fought during Dalhousie’s tenure. Auckland was associated with the First Anglo-Afghan War, Ellenborough with the war with Gwalior and Dalhousie with the Second Anglo-Sikh War.
170.tq: Find the campaign assigned to the wrong Governor-General among otherwise correct pairings.
xs: **Hardinge I — Second Anglo-Burmese War** is wrong — option **(4)**.
The 2nd Burmese war (**1852**) was under **Dalhousie**; Hardinge fought the **1st Anglo-Sikh** war.
The rest are correct: **Dalhousie** — 2nd Sikh; **Auckland** — 1st Afghan; **Ellenborough** — Gwalior.
xa: Hardinge's treaty: **Lahore (1846)**.
Ellenborough also annexed **Sindh (1843)**.

170.s:
Match List-I (Treaty) with List-II (Governor-General):
List-I
a. Treaty of Salbai (1782)
b. Treaty of Amritsar (1809)
c. Treaty of Lahore (1846)
List-II
1. Hardinge I
2. Warren Hastings
3. Minto I
Select the correct answer:
170.x: Salbai (1782) was signed under Warren Hastings, Amritsar (1809) with Ranjit Singh under Minto I, and Lahore (1846) after the First Anglo-Sikh War under Hardinge I (APPSC-G2 2023). Option B swaps Hastings and Minto. Option C swaps Minto and Hardinge. Option D swaps Hastings and Hardinge.
170.tq: Salbai-Hastings, Amritsar-Minto, Lahore-Hardinge.
xs: **Salbai — Warren Hastings**, **Amritsar (1809) — Minto I**, **Lahore (1846) — Hardinge I** = **a-2, b-3, c-1** — option **(1)** (**APPSC-G2 2023**).
**Amritsar 1809** fixed the **Sutlej** boundary.
xa: ⚠ **Amritsar 1846** = Kashmir sale to **Gulab Singh**.
**Bassein (1802)** = Wellesley.

170.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the major grounds of British territorial expansion?
o: Sindh and Punjab—misgovernance; Satara to Nagpur—abolition of titles; Awadh and Coorg—lapse; Carnatic and Tanjore—conquest
Sindh and Punjab—lapse; Satara to Nagpur—conquest; Awadh and Coorg—abolition of titles; Carnatic and Tanjore—misgovernance
Sindh and Punjab—conquest; Satara to Nagpur—lapse; Awadh and Coorg—misgovernance; Carnatic and Tanjore—abolition of titles
Sindh and Punjab—abolition of titles; Satara to Nagpur—misgovernance; Awadh and Coorg—conquest; Carnatic and Tanjore—lapse
170.x: The classification is: conquest for Sindh and Punjab, Doctrine of Lapse for Satara to Nagpur, misgovernance for Awadh and Coorg, and abolition of titles for Carnatic and Tanjore.
170.tq: Keep the four legal and political grounds separate instead of swapping them.
xs: **Conquest** — Sindh, Punjab; **lapse** — Satara to Nagpur; **misgovernance** — Awadh, Coorg; **abolition of titles** — Carnatic, Tanjore — option **(3)**.
Each option shuffles these four grounds; only (3) keeps them in place.
xa: **Sindh 1843**, **Punjab 1849**; **Coorg 1834**; Carnatic and Tanjore **1855**.

170.s: The lapse annexations of 1848–1854 and the annexation of Awadh in 1856 contributed to the grievances that fed the
170.x: The annexations carried out between 1848 and 1854 and the annexation of Awadh in 1856 were among the princely grievances that contributed to the Revolt of 1857.
170.tq: Link the annexation policy with its stated political consequence.
xs: Lapse annexations (**1848-54**) and Awadh (**1856**) fed the grievances behind the **Revolt of 1857** — option **(1)**.
Princes, **taluqdars** and many **Awadh sepoys** were alienated.
xa: Lost pensions: **Nana Sahib**, the **Mughal house**.
By **1856** British India stretched from the **Hindukush** to **Burma**.

170.s: The lands of the Carnatic Nawab in Nellore and Chittoor were annexed in 1801 on the charge of
170.x: Nellore and Chittoor were taken from the Carnatic Nawab in 1801 on the charge of collusion with Tipu Sultan, an early pretext annexation.
170.tq: Match the Andhra territories with the specific annexation pretext.
xs: **Nellore and Chittoor** were annexed in **1801** on a charge of **collusion with Tipu** — option **(3)**.
It was an early "**pretext**" annexation.
xa: **Rayalaseema** had come to the Company in **1800** through the subsidiary alliance.
**Wellesley** merged Andhra into the **Madras Presidency**.

170.s: After the acquisition of Rayalaseema and the annexation of Nellore and Chittoor, Wellesley merged the Andhra region into the
170.x: Wellesley merged the Andhra region into the Madras Presidency after the Company obtained Rayalaseema in 1800 and Nellore and Chittoor in 1801.
170.tq: Match the Andhra territorial change with the correct Presidency.
xs: **Wellesley** merged the Andhra region into the **Madras Presidency** — option **(3)**.
This followed **Rayalaseema (1800)** and **Nellore and Chittoor (1801)**.
xa: Ceded Districts: **Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur, Bellary** = **Dattamandalalu**.
Wellesley (**1798-1805**) also fought the 4th Mysore and 2nd Maratha wars.

170.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding British paramountcy in India?
o: It became unchallenged after 1818 following the removal of the last strong Indian powers.
It became unchallenged immediately after the Treaty of Amritsar in 1809.
It ended after the Third Anglo-Maratha War.
It was established only after the annexation of Punjab in 1849.
170.x: The Anglo-Mysore, Anglo-Maratha and other conflicts removed the last strong Indian powers; after 1818, British paramountcy was unchallenged.
170.tq: Use the broader consequence of the wars rather than one individual treaty or annexation.
xs: British **paramountcy** became **unchallenged after 1818**, when the last strong Indian powers were removed — option **(1)**.
**1818** ended the **Third Maratha War** — paramountcy began, not ended, there; **Punjab (1849)** came later.
xa: **Lord Hastings** turned subsidiary alliances into **paramountcy**.
**Rajputana** states accepted subordinate alliances in **1818**.

171.s: The office of Governor-General of Bengal was created by the:
171.x: The Regulating Act of 1773 created the office of Governor-General of Bengal, with Warren Hastings as its first holder.
171.tq: Match the constitutional title with the Act that created it.
xs: The title **Governor-General of Bengal** dates from **1773** — the **Regulating Act, 1773** — option **(4)**.
The **Government of India Act 1858** created the **Viceroy and GG**; **1833** made the GG of Bengal the **GG of India**.
xa: Title sequence: **Governor of Bengal** → **GG of Bengal (1773)** → **GG of India (1833)** → **Viceroy (1858)**.
The office of Governor of Bengal existed **1757-1772**; first holder **Robert Clive (1758)**.
First GG: **Warren Hastings** (**1773-85**).

171.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Robert Clive was the first Governor of Bengal.
2. Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal.
3. Lord Canning was the first Viceroy and Governor-General.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
171.x: Robert Clive was the first Governor of Bengal, Warren Hastings the first Governor-General of Bengal and Lord Canning the first Viceroy and Governor-General.
171.tq: Distinguish the first holders of three successive constitutional titles.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **Robert Clive** was first **Governor of Bengal** (**1758**).
Statement 2: **Warren Hastings** was first **GG of Bengal** (**1773-85**).
Statement 3: **Lord Canning** was first **Viceroy and GG**, under the **Government of India Act 1858**.
xa: **Bentinck** = first GG of India and last GG of Bengal.
Clive is called the founder of British power in India.

171.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Before 1773, the head of the Company's administration in Bengal was called the Governor of Bengal.
2. William Bentinck was the first Governor-General of India.
3. Lord Canning was the last Governor-General of Bengal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
171.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct (APPSC-GS 2019): the office was Governor of Bengal from 1757 to 1772, and Bentinck became the first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act of 1833. Statement 3 is wrong: Bentinck, not Canning, was the last Governor-General of Bengal; Canning was the first Viceroy. '1 only' misses statement 2, and the options containing 3 are wrong.
171.tq: Bentinck = last GG of Bengal + first GG of India.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only** (**APPSC-GS 2019**).
Statement 1: before **1773** the office was **Governor of Bengal** (**1757-1772**).
Statement 2: **Bentinck** was the first **GG of India**.
Statement 3 wrong: the **last GG of Bengal** was **Bentinck**; **Canning** was the first Viceroy.
xa: Bentinck: GG **1828-35**, GG of India from **1833**.
First **Governor of Bengal**: **Robert Clive (1758)**.

171.s: Who among the following served as Governor-General immediately after Sir John Shore?
171.x: Sir John Shore served from 1793 to 1798, and Wellesley succeeded him in 1798.
171.tq: Test succession through the boundary years of adjoining tenures.
xs: **Wellesley** (**1798-1805**) followed **Sir John Shore** (**1793-98**) — option **(3)**.
**Cornwallis** came before Shore (**1786-93**); **Minto I** and **Hastings** came later.
xa: Wellesley: **Subsidiary Alliance (1798)**, **College of Fort William (1800)**, Anti-Infanticide Act (**1802**).
Shore stayed neutral at **Kharda (1795)**.

171.s:
Arrange the following Governor-Generals in chronological order:
A. Sir George Barlow
B. Minto I
C. Cornwallis, second term
D. Wellesley
171.x: Wellesley served before Cornwallis’s second term; Cornwallis’s second term was followed by Sir George Barlow and then Minto I.
171.tq: Fix Wellesley as the earliest and Minto I as the latest, then arrange the middle pair.
xs: Order: **Wellesley (1798-1805)** → **Cornwallis, 2nd term (1805)** → **Barlow (1805-07)** → **Minto I (1807-13)** = **D, C, A, B** — option **(1)**.
Cornwallis died at **Ghazipur** in his second term.
xa: **Vellore Mutiny (1806)** fell under **Barlow**.
**Treaty of Amritsar (1809)** fell under **Minto I**.

171.s: Which Governor-General died at Ghazipur during his second term in office?
171.x: Cornwallis returned for a second term in 1805 and died at Ghazipur during that term.
171.tq: Use the exceptional second tenure to distinguish Cornwallis from the regular succession.
xs: **Cornwallis** died at **Ghazipur** during his **second term (1805)** — option **(3)**.
His first term was **1786-93** (Permanent Settlement, **Cornwallis Code**, **1793**).
xa: **Sir George Barlow** (**1805-07**) succeeded him.
Cornwallis created the post of **District Judge** and reformed the civil service.

171.s: Which one of the following is the correct tenure of Marquess Hastings as Governor-General?
171.x: Marquess Hastings was Governor-General from 1813 to 1823. 1805-07 was Sir George Barlow, 1823-28 was Amherst and 1807-13 was Minto I.
171.tq: Match the exact tenure with nearby consecutive administrations.
xs: **Marquess Hastings** was GG **1813-23** — option **(4)**.
xa: Real name: **Francis Rawdon-Hastings** (**Lord Moira**).
**Mahalwari** (**Holt Mackenzie**) came under him in **1822**.
His era: policy of intervention and wars; humiliating treaties on the **Peshwa** and **Scindia**.

171.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding William Bentinck’s tenure?
o: He served from 1823 to 1828 and was followed by Amherst.
He served from 1835 to 1836 and was followed by Auckland.
He served as Governor-General from 1828 to 1835 and became Governor-General of India from 1833.
He served as Governor-General only from 1833 to 1835.
171.x: Bentinck served from 1828 to 1835; after the Charter Act of 1833, he held the title Governor-General of India from 1833 onward.
171.tq: Separate the full tenure from the shorter period after the title changed.
xs: **Bentinck** was GG **1828-35**, and **GG of India from 1833** — option **(3)**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: some notes print Bentinck "**1833-35**" — only his time as GG of India.
Other wrong tenures in notes: Amherst "**1823-33**", Metcalfe "**1834-36**".

171.s: Which one of the following measures is associated with Warren Hastings?
171.x: Warren Hastings abolished the Dual Government in 1772. The Permanent Settlement was introduced by Cornwallis, the Subsidiary Alliance by Wellesley and Sindh was annexed during Ellenborough’s tenure.
171.tq: Use the ruler–measure association and reject measures belonging to neighbouring administrations.
xs: **Warren Hastings** abolished the **Dual Government** (**1772**) — option **(1)**.
**Permanent Settlement** = **Cornwallis**; **Sindh** = **Ellenborough**; **Subsidiary Alliance** = **Wellesley**.
xa: Hastings also set up the **Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774)** and the **Code of Gentoo Laws (1776)**.
He founded the **Asiatic Society of Bengal**.

171.s:
Consider the following statements about Warren Hastings:
1. He stopped the Rs 26 lakh tribute paid to Shah Alam.
2. He founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal.
3. He founded the College of Fort William.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
171.x: Statement 1 is correct: Hastings stopped the Rs 26 lakh tribute to Shah Alam. Statement 2 is correct: he founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal. Statement 3 is wrong: the College of Fort William (1800) was Wellesley's. Hence 1 and 2 only.
171.tq: Fort William College 1800 = Wellesley, not Hastings.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: Hastings stopped the **₹26 lakh** tribute to **Shah Alam**.
Statement 2: he founded the **Asiatic Society of Bengal**.
Statement 3 wrong: the **College of Fort William (1800)** was **Wellesley's**.
xa: Hastings moved the treasury to **Calcutta** and set up **Diwani and Fauzdari Adalats**.
He set up a bank in **Calcutta**.

171.s:
Consider the following statements about Lord Cornwallis:
1. The Cornwallis Code of 1793 separated revenue administration from justice.
2. He created the post of District Judge.
3. He introduced the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
171.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Cornwallis Code (1793) separated revenue and justice. Statement 2 is correct: he created the post of District Judge. Statement 3 is wrong: the Subsidiary Alliance (1798) was Wellesley's. Hence 1 and 2 only.
171.tq: 1793 = Cornwallis (Permanent Settlement + Code); 1798 = Wellesley.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: the **Cornwallis Code (1793)** separated revenue and justice.
Statement 2: Cornwallis created the post of **District Judge**.
Statement 3 wrong: the **Subsidiary Alliance (1798)** was **Wellesley's**.
xa: **Permanent Settlement (1793)** was also Cornwallis'.
He reformed the **civil service**.

171.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
171.x: Wellesley established the College of Fort William in 1800. The Anti-Slavery Act was associated with Ellenborough, while the Permanent Settlement and Cornwallis Code belonged to Cornwallis.
171.tq: Start with the sure institution–Governor-General pair and eliminate swapped measures.
xs: **Wellesley — College of Fort William (1800)** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Anti-Slavery Act (1843)** = **Ellenborough**; **Permanent Settlement** and **Cornwallis Code** = **Cornwallis**.
xa: **Auckland** extended irrigation and started famine relief.
**Minto I** = **Treaty of Amritsar (1809)**.

171.s: The Treaty of Amritsar of 1809 was concluded during the tenure of:
171.x: Minto I concluded the Treaty of Amritsar with Ranjit Singh in 1809.
171.tq: Discriminate between similarly named or successive Governors-General through the treaty year.
xs: The **Treaty of Amritsar (1809)** with **Ranjit Singh** was under **Minto I** — option **(1)** (**APPSC-G2 2023**).
**Hardinge I** = **Lahore (1846)**; **Wellesley** = Subsidiary Alliance.
xa: Minto I's real name: **Gilbert Elliot**.
**Bentinck** signed the treaty of perpetual friendship with Ranjit Singh in **1831**.

171.s: Which of the following was NOT a measure of William Bentinck?
o: Treaty of perpetual friendship with Ranjit Singh
Introduction of the Mahalwari system in 1822
171.x: The Mahalwari system was introduced in 1822 during the tenure of Marquess Hastings. Bentinck abolished Sati, suppressed female infanticide and concluded a treaty of perpetual friendship with Ranjit Singh in 1831. ⚠ APPSC key said Mahalwari was a Bentinck measure (APPSC-G1 2024, for the Regulation IX of 1833 revision); the 1822 introduction was under Hastings.
171.tq: Find the measure belonging to the preceding administration rather than the named Governor-General.
xs: **Mahalwari (1822)** was introduced under **Hastings**, not Bentinck — option **(4)**.
Bentinck's: **female infanticide** suppressed, **Sati abolished (1829)**, **perpetual friendship** with Ranjit Singh (**1831**).
xa: Bentinck revised Mahalwari by the **1833 Regulation IX** (**APPSC-G1 2024**).
Mahalwari was devised by **Holt Mackenzie**.

171.s:
Consider the following statements about William Bentinck:
1. He took Coorg in 1834.
2. He took over the administration of Mysore.
3. He established universities for the first time in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
171.x: Bentinck took Coorg in 1834 and took over Mysore’s administration. The first universities were established in 1857 during Canning’s tenure, not during Bentinck’s tenure.
171.tq: Reject the later institutional development inserted into a list of genuine Bentinck measures.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: Bentinck took **Coorg** in **1834**; statement 2: he took over **Mysore**'s administration.
Statement 3 wrong: the first universities came in **1857**, under **Canning**.
xa: Bentinck also suppressed **Thuggee** with **Sleeman**.
Called the **Father of Modern Western Education in India**.

171.s:
Consider the following statements about Lord Ellenborough:
1. He ended the Afghan War.
2. Sindh was annexed in 1843 during his tenure.
3. The Anti-Slavery Act of 1843 was passed under his successor, Hardinge I.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
171.x: Statement 1 is correct: Ellenborough ended the Afghan War. Statement 2 is correct: Sindh was annexed in 1843 under him. Statement 3 is wrong: the Anti-Slavery Act of 1843 was Ellenborough's own; Hardinge I is linked to the Anti-Human-Sacrifice Act of 1845. Hence 1 and 2 only.
171.tq: 1843 twice for Ellenborough: Sindh + slavery.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Ellenborough** ended the **Afghan War**.
Statement 2: **Sindh** was annexed in **1843** under him.
Statement 3 wrong: the **Anti-Slavery Act (1843)** was Ellenborough's own.
xa: **Hardinge I** passed the **Anti-Human-Sacrifice Act (1845)**.
Ellenborough: **1842-44**.

171.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
171.x: The Treaty of Lahore of 1846 was concluded during Hardinge I’s tenure. Auckland started famine relief, Hardinge I was associated with the Anti-Human-Sacrifice Act and Dalhousie with the Widow Remarriage Act.
171.tq: Identify the swapped Governor-General in a group of closely dated administrative measures.
xs: **Ellenborough — Treaty of Lahore** is wrong: **Lahore (1846)** was **Hardinge I** — option **(4)**.
The rest are correct: **Dalhousie — Widow Remarriage Act (1856)**, **Auckland — famine relief**, **Hardinge I — Anti-Human-Sacrifice Act (1845)**.
xa: Hardinge I preferred **English education**.
Ellenborough = **Sindh** and **Anti-Slavery Act (1843)**.

171.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with Lord Dalhousie?
171.x: The Permanent Settlement was introduced by Cornwallis in 1793. Dalhousie was associated with the Doctrine of Lapse, the Caste Disabilities Removal Act and railway, post and telegraph development.
171.tq: Locate the historical outlier among measures of a single Governor-General.
xs: The **Permanent Settlement (1793)** was **Cornwallis'**, not Dalhousie's — option **(1)**.
Dalhousie's: **Caste Disabilities Removal Act (1850)**, railway, post and telegraph, **Doctrine of Lapse**.
xa: Also **Widow Remarriage Act (1856)**, **Public Works Department**.
He annexed **Punjab**, **Lower Burma** and **Awadh**.

171.s: The Vellore Mutiny of 1806 occurred during the tenure of:
171.x: The Vellore Mutiny occurred in 1806 during the tenure of Sir George Barlow.
171.tq: Use the event year to identify the Governor-General in office.
xs: The **Vellore Mutiny (1806)** fell under **Sir George Barlow** — option **(1)** (**APPSC-GS 2019**).
Barlow served **1805-07**, after Cornwallis' brief second term.
xa: **Minto I** followed (**1807-13**).
Wellesley's **Anti-Infanticide Act** was **1802**.

171.s:
Match List-I (Event) with List-II (Governor-General):
List-I
a. Code of Gentoo Laws (1776)
b. Thuggee suppression with Sleeman
c. Public Works Department
d. Liberation of the press
List-II
1. Sir Charles Metcalfe
2. Dalhousie
3. Warren Hastings
4. William Bentinck
Select the correct answer:
171.x: The Code of Gentoo Laws (1776) was compiled under Warren Hastings, Thuggee was suppressed by Bentinck with Sleeman, the PWD was set up under Dalhousie and the press was liberated by Metcalfe: a-3, b-4, c-2, d-1. Option B swaps Hastings and Bentinck, option C swaps Dalhousie and Metcalfe, option D swaps Bentinck and Dalhousie.
171.tq: Press = Metcalfe (1835-36), the short-term GG who is often mixed up.
xs: **Gentoo Laws — Warren Hastings**, **Thuggee — Bentinck**, **PWD — Dalhousie**, **press — Metcalfe** = **a-3, b-4, c-2, d-1** — option **(1)**.
The **Code of Gentoo Laws** dates from **1776**; Thuggee was suppressed with **Sleeman**.
xa: **Metcalfe** served **1835-36**.
Dalhousie also brought railway, post and telegraph.

171.s: The Ring Fence policy of Warren Hastings was intended primarily to:
o: Introduce direct British rule in Punjab
Create Awadh as a buffer state
171.x: The Ring Fence policy treated Awadh as a buffer state to protect British territories from external threats.
171.tq: Infer the purpose of a policy from its strategic description rather than its name alone.
xs: The **Ring Fence** policy made **Awadh a buffer state** — option **(4)**.
**Mahalwari** was **Holt Mackenzie**'s (**1822**), under Hastings — unrelated.
xa: **Warren Hastings** also stopped the **₹26 lakh** tribute to **Shah Alam**.
He was impeached partly over the plunder of the **Begums of Awadh**.

171.s: The Charter Act of 1813 was passed during the tenure of:
171.x: The Charter Act of 1813 was passed at the transition between Minto I and Marquess Hastings, whose tenure began in 1813.
171.tq: Handle an event falling at the boundary between two consecutive tenures.
xs: The **Charter Act 1813** fell in the time of **Minto I** and **Marquess Hastings** — option **(3)**.
Minto I served **1807-13**; Hastings **1813-23**.
xa: Often mixed up with other GGs' acts — a known trap.
Hastings introduced **Mahalwari** in **1822**.

171.s: Which Governor-General is credited with easing the entry of British investors and traders into India?
171.x: The APPSC-GS 2025 key names William Bentinck. Warren Hastings is known for abolishing the Dual Government and for the Ring Fence policy. Wellesley is known for the Subsidiary Alliance. Ellenborough annexed Sindh and passed the Anti-Slavery Act.
171.tq: Bentinck: Sati, Thuggee, British investors.
xs: **Bentinck** "eased the entry of **British investors and traders** into India" — option **(2)** (**APPSC-GS 2025**).
**Warren Hastings**, **Wellesley** and **Ellenborough** are tied to wars and annexations, not this opening to investors.
xa: Bentinck also abolished **Sati (1829)** and took **Coorg (1834)**.
First **GG of India** (**1833**).

171.s:
With reference to the impeachment of Warren Hastings, consider the following statements:
1. Edmund Burke and the Whigs impeached Warren Hastings in the British Parliament in 1787.
2. The impeachment was connected with alleged administrative excesses.
3. The trial ended in his conviction in 1795.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
171.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The trial ran from 1788 to 1795 and ended in Hastings's acquittal, so statement 3 is false.
171.tq: Find the outcome trap: acquittal has been changed to conviction.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Edmund Burke** and the **Whigs** impeached Hastings in **1787**.
Statement 2: the charges were **administrative excesses**.
Statement 3 wrong: the trial (**1788 to 1795**) ended in **acquittal**.
xa: Charges: **Rohilla War (1774)**, **Chait Singh**, **Begums of Awadh**, **Nand Kumar** (**1775**).
Hastings was the first **GG of Bengal** (**1773-85**).

171.s: The trial of Warren Hastings on impeachment charges continued from 1788 until:
171.x: The impeachment trial of Warren Hastings ran from 1788 to 1795 and ended in his acquittal.
171.tq: Distinguish the duration of the trial from the earlier year of impeachment.
xs: The trial ran from **1788 to 1795** — option **(3)**.
It ended in **acquittal**.
xa: Impeached in **1787** by **Edmund Burke** and the **Whigs**.
Charges included the judicial murder of **Nand Kumar** (**1775**).

171.s: Which one of the following was NOT among the charges associated with the impeachment of Warren Hastings?
o: Treatment of Chait Singh of Benares
Plunder of the Begums of Awadh
Introduction of the Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam
171.x: The charges included the Rohilla War, the treatment of Chait Singh, the plunder of the Begums of Awadh and the judicial murder of Nand Kumar. The Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam was associated with Wellesley, not with the impeachment charges against Hastings.
171.tq: Find the item belonging to a different Governor-General and policy context.
xs: The **Subsidiary Alliance** with the Nizam was **Wellesley's** (**1798**) — not a charge against Hastings — option **(4)**.
Real charges: **Chait Singh** of Benares, the **Begums of Awadh**, **Nand Kumar**, the **Rohilla War**.
xa: Impeachment **1787**; trial **1788 to 1795**; **acquittal**.
Impeached by **Edmund Burke** and the **Whigs** for administrative excesses.

171.s: Who among the following was popularly described as the "Bengal Tiger" in his own description?
171.x: Lord Wellesley described himself as the "Bengal Tiger".
171.tq: Use the exact title rather than associating the description with a neighbouring Governor-General.
xs: **Wellesley** described himself as the "**Bengal Tiger**" — option **(3)**.
**Robert Clive** was the "**Heaven-born general**".
xa: Wellesley's real name: **Richard Colley Wellesley** (Earl of Mornington).
**Bentinck** = Father of Modern Western Education in India.

171.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Richard Colley Wellesley — Earl of Mornington
2. Francis Rawdon-Hastings — Lord Moira
3. Gilbert Elliot — Minto I
4. James Andrew Broun-Ramsay — Dalhousie

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
171.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Wellesley was Richard Colley Wellesley, Hastings was Francis Rawdon-Hastings, Minto I was Gilbert Elliot, and Dalhousie was James Andrew Broun-Ramsay.
171.tq: Check each real-name and title pairing independently before selecting the complete combination.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Richard Colley Wellesley** (Mornington); **Francis Rawdon-Hastings** (Moira); **Gilbert Elliot** (Minto I); **James Andrew Broun-Ramsay** (Dalhousie).

171.s: Which one of the following pairs of popular titles is correctly matched?
o: Founder of British power in India - William Bentinck
Father of Modern Western Education in India - William Bentinck
171.x: Bentinck is called the Father of Modern Western Education in India. Robert Clive, not Bentinck, is the founder of British power in India and was also called the 'heaven-born general'. Wellesley called himself the 'Bengal Tiger'.
171.tq: Clive = founder + heaven-born; Wellesley = Bengal Tiger.
xs: **Bentinck — Father of Modern Western Education in India** is correct — option **(2)**.
**Robert Clive** = founder of British power and "**Heaven-born general**"; **Wellesley** = "**Bengal Tiger**".
xa: ⚠ Bentinck did not set up universities — those came in **1857** under **Canning**.
**Hardinge I** preferred **English education**.

171.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the successive changes in the title of the head of British administration in India?
o: Governor of Bengal → Governor-General of Bengal → Governor-General of India → Viceroy
Governor-General of Bengal → Governor of Bengal → Viceroy → Governor-General of India
Governor of Bengal → Governor-General of India → Governor-General of Bengal → Viceroy
Governor of Bengal → Viceroy → Governor-General of Bengal → Governor-General of India
171.x: The sequence was Governor of Bengal, Governor-General of Bengal from 1773, Governor-General of India from 1833, and Viceroy from 1858.
171.tq: Fix the first and last titles, then place the two intermediate constitutional changes in order.
xs: **Governor of Bengal** → **GG of Bengal (1773)** → **GG of India (1833)** → **Viceroy (1858)** — option **(1)**.
The office of Governor of Bengal existed **1757-1772**; the Viceroy title came with the **Government of India Act 1858**.
xa: First holders: **Clive**, **Warren Hastings**, **Bentinck**, **Canning**.
The title changes by Act are a common statement question.

171.s: Which of the following sets of measures is correctly associated with Lord Wellesley in the Andhra-related context?
o: Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam in 1798, Ceded Districts in 1800 and merger of Andhra into Madras in 1801
Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam in 1801, Ceded Districts in 1798 and merger of Andhra into Madras in 1800
Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam in 1829, Ceded Districts in 1833 and merger of Andhra into Madras in 1858
Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam in 1843, Ceded Districts in 1845 and merger of Andhra into Madras in 1856
171.x: Under Wellesley, the Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam was concluded in 1798, the Ceded Districts followed in 1800, and Andhra was merged into Madras in 1801.
171.tq: Use the sequence of the three dated measures to eliminate the shifted-year alternatives.
xs: Under **Wellesley**: **Subsidiary Alliance (1798)**, **Ceded Districts (1800)**, **merger of Andhra into Madras (1801)** — option **(1)**.
The other options scramble these years.
xa: Wellesley: **1798-1805**; also the **College of Fort William (1800)**.
Anti-Infanticide Act: **1802**.

171.s:
Arrange the following social measures in chronological order:
A. Infanticide-related measure under Wellesley
B. Abolition of Sati under Bentinck
C. Abolition of slavery under Ellenborough
D. Prohibition of human sacrifice under Hardinge I
171.x: The measures are dated 1802, 1829, 1843 and 1845 respectively. Therefore, the correct order is A, B, C, D.
171.tq: Arrange the events by their stated years, beginning with the earliest reform.
xs: Order: **infanticide (1802)** → **Sati (1829)** → **slavery (1843)** → **human sacrifice (1845)** = **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**Wellesley**, **Bentinck**, **Ellenborough** and **Hardinge I** served in that order.
xa: Then **Dalhousie**: caste disabilities **1850**, widow remarriage **1856**.
Bentinck also suppressed **female infanticide** and **Thuggee**.

171.s:
Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?

Governor-General — Social measure
171.x: The prohibition of human sacrifice in 1845 is associated with Hardinge I. Dalhousie is associated with caste disabilities legislation in 1850 and widow remarriage in 1856.
171.tq: Watch for the swapped Governor-General in a ruler–measure pairing.
xs: **Dalhousie — human sacrifice, 1845** is wrong: that was **Hardinge I** — option **(1)**.
The others are correct: **Ellenborough — slavery (1843)**, **Wellesley — infanticide (1802)**, **Bentinck — Sati (1829)**.
xa: Dalhousie's: **Caste Disabilities Removal Act (1850)**, **Widow Remarriage Act (1856)**.
Hardinge I also signed **Lahore (1846)**.

172.s: Who was the only Viceroy of India to be murdered while in office?
172.x: Lord Mayo was the only Viceroy murdered in office. He was killed in 1872 in the Andamans by the convict Sher Ali Afridi.
172.tq: Use the uniqueness clue and verify it with the place, year and assassin.
xs: **Lord Mayo** is the only Viceroy murdered in office — option **(3)**.
He was killed by the convict **Sher Ali Afridi** in the **Andamans (1872)**.
**Hardinge II** survived the **Delhi Conspiracy** bomb of **1912**.
xa: Mayo (**1869-72**): **financial decentralisation (1870)**, **Mayo College**, statistical survey.
First census under Mayo, **1872** (some notes **1871**) — non-synchronous.
FIRST/LAST: first Viceroy **Canning**; last Viceroy **Mountbatten**.

172.s: Lord Mayo was assassinated by Sher Ali Afridi in
o: Calcutta during the Partition of Bengal
172.x: Sher Ali Afridi, a convict, murdered Lord Mayo in the Andamans in 1872 while Mayo was on tour.
172.tq: Combine the assassin, location and year to avoid confusing two separate assassination conspiracies.
xs: Mayo was killed by **Sher Ali Afridi** in **the Andamans in 1872** — option **(2)**.
**1911/1912 Delhi** relates to **Hardinge II**; **Shimla 1864** to **John Lawrence**.
xa: Mayo set up the **Dept of Agriculture and Commerce** and a **state railway**.
His **1870** resolution began **financial decentralisation**.

172.s:
Arrange the following Viceroys and associated measures in chronological order:
A. Lord Lytton — Royal Titles Act
B. Lord Mayo — Resolution on financial decentralisation
C. Lord Ripon — First Factory Act
D. Lord Canning — Indian Councils Act
172.x: The correct order is Canning's Indian Councils Act of 1861, Mayo's 1870 resolution, Lytton's Royal Titles Act of 1876 and Ripon's First Factory Act of 1881.
172.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place Mayo and Lytton between them.
xs: Order: **Canning — Councils Act (1861)** → **Mayo — decentralisation (1870)** → **Lytton — Royal Titles Act (1876)** → **Ripon — First Factory Act (1881)** = **D, B, A, C** — option **(1)**.
⚠ Some notes date the First Factory Act to **1882**; it still comes last.
xa: Lytton also passed the **Vernacular Press Act** and **Arms Act (1878)**.
Ripon repealed the **VPA (1882)**.

172.s:
Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the later part of the chronological order of Viceroys given below?
A. Lord Curzon
B. Lord Minto II
C. Lord Hardinge II
D. Lord Chelmsford
E. Lord Reading
172.x: The correct order is Curzon, Minto II, Hardinge II, Chelmsford and Reading. Their sequence corresponds broadly to the period from 1899 to the early 1920s.
172.tq: Arrange successive Viceroys by anchoring the known 1909, 1911 and 1919 measures.
xs: Order: **Curzon (1899-1905)** → **Minto II (1905-10)** → **Hardinge II (1910-16)** → **Chelmsford (1916-21)** → **Reading** = **A, B, C, D, E** — option **(1)**.
Anchor years: **1905** Partition, **1909** Councils Act, **1911** Durbar, **1919** Rowlatt Act.
xa: **Irwin** (**1926-31**) followed Reading.
**21 Viceroys** ruled from **1858** to **1947**.

172.s:
Which of the following is the correct final sequence of Viceroys of India?
1. Lord Linlithgow
2. Lord Wavell
3. Lord Mountbatten
4. Lord Willingdon
172.x: The correct sequence is Willingdon, Linlithgow, Wavell and Mountbatten. Mountbatten was the last Viceroy of India.
172.tq: Identify the final successor chain and use Mountbatten as the fixed last item.
xs: Order: **Willingdon** → **Linlithgow (1936-43)** → **Wavell (1943-47)** → **Mountbatten (1947)** = **4, 1, 2, 3** — option **(1)**.
Willingdon came after **Irwin** (**1926-31**).
xa: Linlithgow: **August Offer 1940**, Cripps Mission, **Quit India 1942**.
Wavell: **Simla Conference (1945)**, **Cabinet Mission 1946**.

172.s: The office of Viceroy of India was created by the Government of India Act, 1858, and its first holder was:
172.x: The Government of India Act, 1858 created the designation Viceroy, and Lord Canning became its first holder.
172.tq: Distinguish the first Viceroy from the first Secretary of State and earlier Governors-General.
xs: **Lord Canning** was the first **Viceroy**, under the **GoI Act 1858** — option **(2)**.
He was also the **last Governor-General** of the Company era.
xa: Canning (**1856-62**): Revolt of 1857, Doctrine of Lapse withdrawn, **Indian Councils Act 1861**.
Universities at **Calcutta, Bombay, Madras (1857)**.

172.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy of India.
2. Lord Mountbatten was the first Governor-General of free India.
3. C. Rajagopalachari was the first and the last Indian Governor-General.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
172.x: All three statements are correct. Mountbatten was the last Viceroy and stayed on as the first Governor-General of independent India. C. Rajagopalachari succeeded him as the only Indian to hold the office, which makes him both the first and the last Indian Governor-General. Options A, B and C each leave out at least one true statement.
172.tq: Mountbatten: last Viceroy, first GG; Rajaji: only Indian GG.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Mountbatten** was the **last Viceroy** and the **first Governor-General of free India**.
**C. Rajagopalachari** was the **first and last Indian GG**.
xa: The **Indian Independence Act (18 July 1947)** abolished the offices of **Viceroy** and **Secretary of State**.
Mountbatten replaced Wavell after **Attlee's statement (20 Feb 1947)**.

172.s:
Which of the following measures was associated with Lord Canning?

1. Passage of the Indian Councils Act, 1861
2. Introduction of the portfolio system
3. Establishment of universities at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras
4. Passage of the Indian Penal Code

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
172.x: All four measures are associated with Lord Canning's tenure. His period also witnessed the Revolt of 1857 and the introduction of income tax.
172.tq: Group the measures belonging to one viceroy and reject no unsupported item.
xs: All four are Canning's — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Indian Councils Act 1861**, **portfolio system**, universities at **Calcutta, Bombay, Madras (1857)**, and the **IPC**.
xa: He also withdrew the **Doctrine of Lapse** and introduced **income tax**.
The 1861 Act nominated **3** Indians: **Raja of Benaras, Maharaja of Patiala, Sir Dinkar Rao**.
The **ASI** was set up in **1861** under Canning.

172.s:
Which of the following was NOT associated with Lord John Lawrence?

(a) Establishment of the Indian Forest Department
(b) Telegraph link with Europe
(c) Development of canals and state-managed railways
(d) Introduction of the Indian Councils Act, 1909
o: Development of canals and state-managed railways
Introduction of the Indian Councils Act, 1909
Establishment of the Indian Forest Department
172.x: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 was associated with Minto II. The other three measures belong to the tenure of John Lawrence.
172.tq: Identify the measure separated from the surrounding viceroy-specific cluster.
xs: The **Indian Councils Act 1909** belonged to **Minto II** (Morley-Minto), not Lawrence — option **(3)**.
**John Lawrence** (**1864-69**): telegraph link with **Europe**, **Indian Forest Department**, canals and **state-managed railways**.
xa: Lawrence declared **Shimla** the summer capital in **1864** (**APPSC 2018**).
Minto II's Act was followed by protests; Minto and Morley were later replaced.

172.s:
Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?

(a) Lord Mayo — Financial decentralisation
(b) Lord Northbrook — Abolition of income tax
(c) Lord Lytton — Vernacular Press Act
(d) Lord Ripon — Second Factory Act
o: Lord Northbrook — Abolition of income tax
172.x: The Second Factory Act was passed during the tenure of Lord Lansdowne in 1891. Financial decentralisation, abolition of income tax and the Vernacular Press Act were associated respectively with Mayo, Northbrook and Lytton.
172.tq: Look for the swapped viceroy in a set of otherwise correctly matched measures.
xs: **Ripon — Second Factory Act** is wrong: the **Second Factory Act (1891)** was **Lansdowne's** — option **(2)**.
Ripon passed the **First Factory Act**; the other pairs are correct.
xa: **Mayo** = financial decentralisation; **Northbrook** = abolished income tax; **Lytton** = **VPA**.
Ripon repealed the **VPA (1882)**.

172.s: The term 'Magna Carta of Local Self-Government' is associated with the
o: Financial decentralisation resolution of Lord Mayo
Local Self-Government Resolution of Lord Ripon
Indian Councils Act of Lord Lansdowne
172.x: Lord Ripon's Local Self-Government Resolution of 1882 is described as the Magna Carta of Local Self-Government. Ripon is consequently called the Father of Local Self-Government.
172.tq: Connect the famous title with the exact resolution and viceroy.
xs: The "**Magna Carta**" of local self-government = **Ripon's Local Self-Government Resolution (1882)** — option **(2)**.
Ripon is the "**Father of Local Self-Government**"; **Mayo**'s **1870** resolution was financial decentralisation.
xa: Ripon also: **Hunter Commission (1882)**, **Ilbert Bill (1883)**, repeal of **VPA**.
First synchronous census: **1881** under Ripon.

172.s:
Match List-I (Event) with List-II (Viceroy):
List-I
a. Foundation of the INC (1885)
b. Durand Commission (1893)
c. Killing of Rand and Ayerst by the Chapekar brothers (1897)
d. Police Commission under Andrew Frazer (1902)
List-II
1. Elgin II
2. Curzon
3. Dufferin
4. Lansdowne
Select the correct answer:
172.x: The INC was founded under Dufferin, the Durand Commission came under Lansdowne, the Chapekar killings under Elgin II and the Frazer Police Commission under Curzon: a-3, b-4, c-1, d-2. Option B swaps Dufferin and Lansdowne, option C swaps Lansdowne and Elgin II, option D swaps Elgin II and Curzon.
172.tq: Successive viceroys 1884-1905: Dufferin, Lansdowne, Elgin II, Curzon - the events follow the same order.
