1. The Viceroy dealt particularly with the princely states.
2. The Governor-General administered British India.
3. The two titles referred to entirely separate office-holders after 1858.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
186.x: The same office-holder functioned as Viceroy in relation to the princely states and as Governor-General in British India. Therefore, statement 3 is false.
186.tq: Use the distinction between two functions of one office-holder to reject the absolute statement.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: as **Viceroy** he dealt with the **princely states**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: as **Governor-General** he governed **British India**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: the GG simply got the **additional title** Viceroy — one office-holder — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: First Viceroy: **Lord Canning** (**1858**).
The title GG of India dates from the **Charter Act 1833**.

186.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the fate of the East India Company after 1857?
o: It retained political rule until 1874 and was then transferred to the Crown.
It was dissolved immediately in 1858 without any formal legal process.
It continued to rule India under the Crown until 1901.
It lost its rule under the Act of 1858 and was finally dissolved in 1874.
186.x: The Government of India Act, 1858 ended the Company’s political rule, while the East India Company was formally dissolved in 1874.
186.tq: Separate the year of loss of political power from the later year of formal dissolution.
xs: The Company **lost its rule** under the **1858 Act** and was finally **dissolved in 1874** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It did not keep political rule till **1874**, nor was it dissolved at once in 1858.
xa: It had been chartered by **Elizabeth I** on **31 December 1600**.
The **1858** Act was titled the **Act for the Good Government of India**.

186.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Bahadur Shah II was proclaimed Shahenshah-e-Hindustan by the rebels.
2. He was tried and exiled to Rangoon.
3. His exile marked the formal end of Mughal rule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
186.x: All three statements are correct. The rebels proclaimed Bahadur Shah II as Shahenshah-e-Hindustan, after which the British tried and exiled him to Rangoon, ending the Mughal dynasty in practice and form.
186.tq: Combine title, consequence and sequence in a single historical event cluster.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: rebels proclaimed **Bahadur Shah II** **Shahenshah-e-Hindustan**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: he was **tried and exiled to Rangoon**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: the **Mughal dynasty formally ended** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: He died in Rangoon in **1862**.
LAST: **Bahadur Shah II** — last Mughal emperor.

186.s: Bahadur Shah II, also called Zafar, died in which year after his exile to Rangoon?
186.x: Bahadur Shah II was exiled to Rangoon after 1857 and died there in 1862.
186.tq: Distinguish the year of exile-related events from the year of death.
xs: **Bahadur Shah II** died in **Rangoon** in **1862** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1857** was the revolt itself; the Company lost its rule in **1858**.
xa: The rebels had proclaimed him **Shahenshah-e-Hindustan**.
His exile formally ended **Mughal rule**; he was the **last Mughal emperor**.

186.s: Which of the following statements regarding the English East India Company is correct?
o: It was established by the States-General of the Netherlands in 1602.
Its charter was issued by Elizabeth I on 31 December 1600.
It was a state-controlled Portuguese organisation.
Its original charter gave it legislative authority over all Indian territories.
186.x: Elizabeth I granted the English East India Company its charter on 31 December 1600. The charter granted trading privileges, not territorial or legislative authority.
186.tq: Use the charter date and distinguish trading privileges from territorial powers.
xs: The English East India Company was chartered by **Elizabeth I** on **31 December 1600** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was an English, not Dutch or Portuguese, body.
xa: It **lost its rule in 1858** under the **1858 Act**.
It was finally **dissolved in 1874**.
The **Charter Act 1833** had made it a purely administrative organisation.

186.s:
Which of the following was NOT an object associated with the Queen’s Proclamation of 1858?
1. Disclaiming further annexation of Indian States
2. Placing the administration of India under the Crown
3. Regulating the commercial activities of the East India Company
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
186.x: The Proclamation disclaimed further annexation and placed Indian administration under the Crown. Regulation of Company trade was not one of its objects.
186.tq: Find the unrelated commercial objective among constitutional and political purposes.
xs: **Regulating Company trade** was **not** an object — so **3 only**, option **(1)**.
Its objects: **disclaim annexation** of Indian States and **place administration under the Crown** (UPSC **2014**: "1 and 2 only").
xa: ⚠ Trap: "regulating Company trade" is the planted wrong object.
The Proclamation was read by **Lord Canning** at **Allahabad**, **1 November 1858**.
It is called the "**Magna Carta of the Indian people**".

186.s:
Which of the following were promised in the Queen's Proclamation of 1858?
1. Treaties made by the East India Company with the princes would be honoured.
2. Appointments to public service by merit and qualifications, without discrimination of race or creed.
3. Protection of the commercial monopoly of the East India Company.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
186.x: 1 is correct: Company treaties would be honoured. 2 is correct: equal opportunity in public service by merit. 3 is wrong: the Proclamation protected property, succession and peasants' land rights, not any Company monopoly. So B; A omits 2, C and D include the false 3.
186.tq: Proclamation: princes, religion, merit, property - never Company trade.
xs: Item 1 is **correct**: **Company treaties** with the princes would be **honoured**.
Item 2 is **correct**: **equal opportunity in public service** — appointments by **merit**, without discrimination of race or creed.
Item 3 is **wrong**: it protected **property, succession** and peasants' land rights, not any Company monopoly — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Other promises: **no further annexation**, Doctrine of Lapse abolished, **no interference in religion**.
Concluding line: "Their **satisfaction** is our **security**. Their **gratitude** is our **reward**."

186.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the religious assurance in the Queen’s Proclamation:
1. The Government promised non-interference in religious and social affairs.
2. Forced conversions were rejected.
3. The State withdrew its patronage from missionary conversion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
186.x: The Proclamation promised religious neutrality, rejected forced conversion and was followed by the withdrawal of state patronage from missionary conversion.
186.tq: Confirm whether all statements describe the same neutrality-based policy.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **no interference in religion** and social customs.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **no forced conversions**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: the state **withdrew patronage from missionary conversion** — a promise **kept** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: Kept: **no annexation**, **adoption**, **religious neutrality**.
Not kept: **equal employment** — the **ICS** stayed European-dominated.

186.s:
Consider the following statements about the Queen's Proclamation:
1. Its promise of equal employment was not kept, as the ICS stayed European-dominated.
2. The period 1858-1885 is called the 'Era of Constitutional Experiments'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
186.x: Statement 1 is correct: equal employment was not kept; SoS Kimberley said an adequate number of civil servants 'shall always be Europeans'. Statement 2 is wrong: 1858-1885 is the 'Era of Broken Promises'. So A; B, C and D are wrong.
186.tq: 1858-1885 = Era of Broken Promises.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **equal employment** was **not kept** — the **ICS** stayed European-dominated.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: **1858-1885** is the "**Era of Broken Promises**" — so **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: SoS **Kimberley**: an adequate number of civil servants "**shall always be Europeans**".
Promises **kept**: no annexation, adoption, religious neutrality.
The **Madras Native Association** (**1852**) first petitioned over non-implementation of the Proclamation.

186.s: The Queen’s Proclamation of 1858 is often regarded as the:
o: Magna Carta of the Indian people
Magna Carta of the East India Company
186.x: The Queen’s Proclamation is often called the Magna Carta of the Indian people because of its wide-ranging assurances concerning rulers, religion, public service, property and land rights.
186.tq: Recall the historically used descriptive title rather than the constitutional Act title.
xs: The Queen's Proclamation is called the "**Magna Carta of the Indian people**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
It promised the **princes**, **religious neutrality**, **equal public service** and **property** rights.
xa: **Gandhi** too cited Victoria's **1858** Proclamation as a "**Magna Carta**" (**12 May 2026**, on Magna Carta's legacy).
Read by **Lord Canning** at a **Durbar at Allahabad**, **1 November 1858**.

186.s: The Queen's Proclamation of 1858 was read out by Lord Canning at:
o: a Durbar at Delhi on 1 January 1858
a Durbar at Allahabad on 1 November 1858
a Durbar at Lucknow on 1 January 1859
186.x: Lord Canning read the Proclamation at a Durbar in Allahabad on 1 November 1858 (UPPSC 2009). Delhi is the venue of the 1877 Durbar that proclaimed Victoria Empress of India. Calcutta and Lucknow were not the venue, and the dates in A and D are wrong.
186.tq: Allahabad, 1 November 1858, Canning.
xs: **Lord Canning** read it at a **Durbar at Allahabad** on **1 November 1858** (UPPSC **2009**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Delhi** is the **1877** Durbar that proclaimed Victoria **Empress of India** (under **Lytton**).
xa: ⚠ **Allahabad 1858** = Proclamation (Canning); **Delhi 1877** = Empress of India (Lytton).
It is called the "**Magna Carta of the Indian people**".

186.s: Queen Victoria became 'Empress of India' in:
o: 1858, under the Government of India Act, 1858
1877, under the Royal Titles Act 1876, proclaimed at the Delhi Durbar under Lytton
1911, at the Delhi Durbar of George V
186.x: The Royal Titles Act 1876 gave Victoria the title, and it was proclaimed at the Delhi Durbar of 1 January 1877 under Lord Lytton. The 1858 Act only transferred power to the Crown; some sources wrongly place the title at the 1858 Allahabad Durbar. The 1861 Act and the 1911 Durbar have nothing to do with the title.
186.tq: Empress of India = 1877 (Act of 1876), Lytton, Delhi.
xs: Victoria became **Empress of India** in **1877**, under the **Royal Titles Act 1876**, proclaimed at the **Delhi Durbar** under **Lytton** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **1858** Act only transferred power to the **Crown**.
xa: The Delhi Durbar was held on **1 Jan 1877**.
⚠ Some notes wrongly place the title at the **Allahabad Durbar** of **1858**.
⚠ **1833** = GG of India; **1858** = Viceroy + SoS; **1876** = Empress title.

186.s: Who withdrew the Doctrine of Lapse and recognised the right of adoption by childless Indian rulers?
186.x: Lord Canning withdrew the Doctrine of Lapse and recognised adoption rights after 1857. This marked the abandonment of Dalhousie’s annexation policy.
186.tq: Use the ruler-policy trap by separating the policy’s originator from the person who ended it.
xs: **Lord Canning** **withdrew the Doctrine of Lapse** and recognised the **right of adoption** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Dalhousie**'s annexation policy was thereby **abandoned**.
xa: Princes' territorial integrity was guaranteed if they accepted **British paramountcy**.
Canning also called the loyal princes "**breakwaters to the storm**" (some notes: **Lord Elgin**).
**Rani Avantibai Lodhi** of Ramgarh had fought the Doctrine of Lapse.

186.s:
Consider the following statements about the post-1857 policy towards Indian princes:
1. Princes were assured that their states would not ordinarily be annexed.
2. Their acceptance of British paramountcy was required.
3. They became subordinate allies and supports of British rule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
186.x: All three statements are correct. The princes retained their states subject to British paramountcy and were converted into loyal subordinate allies of the Crown.
186.tq: Test the relationship between territorial assurance, paramountcy and political dependence.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: Dalhousie's **annexation policy** was abandoned.
Statement 2 is **correct**: integrity was guaranteed if princes accepted **British paramountcy** (the Crown as **ultimate sovereign**).
Statement 3 is **correct**: they became **subordinate allies and props** of British rule — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: They had **stayed loyal in 1857**.
**Canning** withdrew the **Doctrine of Lapse**; adoption fully recognised.

186.s: The policy of annexation associated with Lord Dalhousie was officially abandoned after 1857 mainly through the recognition of
o: the election of rulers by legislative councils
the complete independence of princely states
the right of adoption by childless rulers
186.x: The British recognised the right of childless rulers to adopt heirs, thereby withdrawing the Doctrine of Lapse and ending the annexation policy associated with Dalhousie.
186.tq: Identify the constitutional-political consequence of a policy change.
xs: Dalhousie's annexation was abandoned by recognising the **right of adoption by childless rulers** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Canning** withdrew the **Doctrine of Lapse**.
**Paramountcy** was not abolished — princes had to accept it.
xa: The Proclamation promised **no further annexation** and to honour **Company treaties**.
Princes became **subordinate allies** of the Crown.

186.s: The Indian princes, who stayed loyal in 1857, were described as 'breakwaters to the storm' by:
186.x: Lord Canning described the loyal princes as breakwaters to the storm, though some accounts credit Lord Elgin.
186.tq: Canning, the 1857 Viceroy, saw princes as breakwaters.
xs: **Lord Canning** called the loyal princes "**breakwaters to the storm**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
Some notes credit **Lord Elgin**; **Dalhousie** was the annexer whose policy was abandoned.
xa: Post-1857 princes became **subordinate allies** under **British paramountcy**.
Canning also withdrew the **Doctrine of Lapse**.

186.s: Which of the following correctly describes the recommendation of the Peel Commission of 1859?
o: Increase of the European share in the army and retention of artillery for Europeans
Recruitment exclusively from Awadh and Bihar
Abolition of all presidency armies immediately
Reduction of the European share in the army
186.x: The Peel Commission recommended a greater European share in the army and reserved artillery and key positions for Europeans.
186.tq: Identify the post-1857 military measure rather than a later army-merger proposal.
xs: The **Peel Commission** (**1859**) **raised the European share** and kept **artillery exclusively European** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Recruitment shifted **away from Awadh and Bihar**; presidency armies were merged only after the **Eden Commission** (**1879**).
xa: Bengal Army ratio from **1:5 to 1:2**; Madras and Bombay **2:5**.
Regiments organised by **caste, community and region** — "**divide and counterpoise**".
Recruitment shifted to **Gurkhas, Sikhs and Pathans**.

186.s: After the reorganisation recommended by the Peel Commission, the ratio of European to Indian troops was:
o: 1:2 in the Bengal Army and 2:5 in the Madras and Bombay armies
2:5 in the Bengal Army and 1:2 in the Madras and Bombay armies
2:1 in the Bengal Army and 5:2 in the Madras and Bombay armies
186.x: The ratio of European to Indian troops was fixed at 1:2 in the Bengal Army and 2:5 in the Madras and Bombay armies.
186.tq: Read the ratios in the stated presidency order and watch for reversal of numerator and denominator.
xs: Ratios: **1:2** in the **Bengal Army** and **2:5** in **Madras and Bombay** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option 2 swaps them; option 4 inverts them.
xa: The Bengal Army ratio was earlier **1:5**.
⚠ Some notes give Madras and Bombay as **1:3**.
These came from the **Peel Commission** (**1859**).

186.s:
Which of the following statements regarding army reorganisation after 1857 is correct?
1. Artillery and key positions were reserved for Europeans.
2. Recruitment shifted towards groups described as martial races.
3. Recruitment was shifted away from Awadh and Bihar towards Punjab, Gorkhas and the NWFP.
4. Regiments were organised without regard to caste or region.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
186.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the policy of “divide and counterpoise” involved mixing regiments by caste and region, not ignoring those identities.
186.tq: Find the reversed statement hidden among correct military-reorganisation features.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **artillery** and key positions reserved for **Europeans**.
Statements 2 and 3 are **correct**: recruitment shifted to "**martial races**" — Punjab, **Gorkhas**, **NWFP** — away from **Awadh and Bihar**.
Statement 4 is **wrong**: regiments were organised **by caste, community and region** — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Aim: stop **cross-regional fraternising** — "**divide and counterpoise**".
The favoured groups had **stayed loyal in 1857**.

186.s: The policy of “divide and counterpoise” in the post-1857 army was reflected in the:
o: Abolition of all regional distinctions in recruitment
Mixing of regiments by caste and region
Replacement of Indian troops by police constables
186.x: The policy involved mixing regiments by caste and region to prevent unified opposition within the army.
186.tq: Apply the phrase to the organisational measure it describes.
xs: "**Divide and counterpoise**" meant **mixing regiments by caste and region** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It aimed to **prevent fraternisation** across regions.
xa: Exam angle: "**divide and rule**" inside the army — the counterpoise principle.
Regiments: **Sikh**, **Gurkha**, **Rajput**.
Recommended by the **Peel Commission** (**1859**).

186.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Eden Commission (1879) recommended abolishing the separate presidency armies.
2. The presidency armies were merged into a single Indian Army with three commands in 1895.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
186.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the merged Indian Army of 1895 had four commands, not three. So A; B, C and D are wrong.
186.tq: Eden 1879 -> single army, FOUR commands, 1895.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: the **Eden Commission** (**1879**) recommended abolishing the separate **presidency armies**.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: the single Indian Army of **1895** had **four commands**, not three — so **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: The three presidency armies: **Bengal**, **Madras**, **Bombay**.
The earlier **Peel Commission** (**1859**) reshaped the army's ratios and recruitment.

186.s: The recommendations for the reorganisation of the Indian Army after the Revolt of 1857 were associated with which commission?
186.x: The Peel Commission, constituted in 1859, recommended major changes in the composition, organisation and recruitment of the Indian Army.
186.tq: Identify the commission associated with a specific administrative measure.
xs: Army reorganisation after 1857 came from the **Peel Commission** (**1859**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
It raised the **European share**, reserved **artillery** for Europeans and shifted recruitment to "**martial races**".
xa: The **Eden Commission** (**1879**) recommended a **single Indian Army** (formed **1895**).
⚠ **Bengal 1:2**; **Madras and Bombay 2:5**.

186.s: The recruitment policy of the British after the Revolt of 1857 increasingly favoured which groups as so-called “martial races”?
186.x: The British increasingly recruited Sikhs, Gurkhas and Pathans, describing them as martial races, while reducing dependence on recruits from Awadh and Bihar.
186.tq: Distinguish the favoured recruitment groups from the groups deliberately reduced.
xs: Recruitment favoured **Gurkhas, Sikhs and Pathans** as "**martial races**" — so option **(2)** is correct.
These communities had **stayed loyal in 1857**; **Awadh and Bihar** were dropped.
xa: Regions: **Punjab**, **Gorkhas**, **NWFP**.
Regiments were organised by **caste, community and region**.

186.s: Which of the following best describes the change in British policy towards Muslims after 1857?
o: The British transferred all administrative posts exclusively to Muslims.
The British consistently treated Muslims as their principal allies from the beginning.
The British initially blamed and targeted Muslims, but later cultivated them against the educated Hindu middle class.
The British abandoned all communal distinctions and promoted joint political representation.
186.x: The British initially held Muslims chiefly responsible for the revolt and adopted anti-Muslim measures, but later cultivated Muslim support against the rising educated Hindu middle class.
186.tq: Follow the chronological shift rather than selecting an absolute statement.
xs: The British first held **Muslims chiefly responsible** (first **anti-Muslim policies**), then **cultivated them against the educated Hindu middle class** — so option **(3)** is correct.
This was **divide and rule**: Hindus and Muslims played against each other.
xa: **Bahadur Shah II** was exiled to **Rangoon**, ending Mughal rule.
English-educated "**Babus**" were viewed with suspicion.

186.s: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of British policy towards social and landed interests after 1857?
o: Withdrawal from missionary and reforming activity
Continued aggressive interference in Indian social customs
Recognition of proprietary rights of zamindars and taluqdars
186.x: The British abandoned their earlier reforming zeal and adopted a policy of non-interference in social customs. They nevertheless protected landed interests and stepped back from missionary activity.
186.tq: Identify the reversed policy by testing the word “continued” against the historical shift.
xs: **Continued aggressive interference** in social customs is the odd one — **reforming zeal was abandoned** — so option **(2)** is the answer.
The state **stepped back from missionary activity**, **protected zamindars and landlords**, and gave **proprietary rights** to zamindars and taluqdars.
xa: Result: a **conservative, loyalist** landed class (Awadh especially).
Racial arrogance **hardened**; Indians kept out of higher posts.

186.s: The reversal of the annexation of large estates in Awadh after 1857 resulted in zamindars and taluqdars being granted
o: exclusive authority over the British Indian Army
the right to reject British paramountcy
proprietary rights and transformed into a conservative loyalist class
186.x: In Awadh, zamindars and taluqdars were restored to proprietary rights and became a conservative and loyal landed class supporting British rule.
186.tq: Link an administrative concession to its political consequence.
xs: Zamindars and taluqdars got **proprietary rights** and became a **conservative, loyalist class** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Annexation of large estates** was **reversed**, especially in **Awadh**.
xa: Policies now **protected zamindars and landlords**.
Princes too became **subordinate allies** under **British paramountcy**.

186.s: Which of the following correctly reflects British racial attitudes after the Revolt of 1857?
o: Indians were admitted freely to the highest administrative posts.
Rebels were generally tried through transparent constitutional procedures.
Racial arrogance hardened, rebels were publicly executed after mock trials, and Indians were excluded from higher posts.
Missionary activity was expanded as the central instrument of reconciliation.
186.x: Racial arrogance intensified after 1857. Rebels were publicly executed after mock trials, while Indians continued to be excluded from higher administrative positions.
186.tq: Prefer the precise combined description over options containing absolute reversals.
xs: **Racial arrogance hardened**; rebels were **publicly executed after mock trials**; Indians **kept out of higher posts** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The state **stepped back** from missionary activity — it did not expand it.
xa: **Equal employment** (Proclamation) was **not kept** — the ICS stayed European-dominated.
**1858-1885** = "**Era of Broken Promises**".

186.s: The period of direct Crown rule in India, as stated in the historical context of the 1857 Revolt, was
186.x: Direct Crown rule in India began in 1858 after the end of East India Company rule and continued until independence in 1947.
186.tq: Use the precise beginning and ending years of a constitutional transition.
xs: Crown rule lasted **1858-1947** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1858** = watershed between **Company rule** and **Crown rule**.
xa: The submarine cable of **1870** let **London** control administration more directly.
The Proclamation fixed policy on **princes and religion** till **1947**.

186.s: Which development enabled the administration of India to be controlled more directly from London during the period of Crown rule?
o: The opening of the Suez Canal in 1869
The establishment of the Indian National Congress in 1885
The introduction of the submarine cable in 1870
The construction of the first railway in India
186.x: The submarine cable introduced in 1870 facilitated faster communication between India and London, strengthening control from Britain.
186.tq: Identify the specific technological development linked to administrative control.
xs: The **submarine cable** (**1870**) let administration be **controlled from London** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It made **London's** grip on Crown rule closer after the **1858** transfer of power.
xa: The **Secretary of State**, a British cabinet minister, could issue orders to the **Viceroy**.

186.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Gazula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty — Madras Native Association
2. Madras Native Association — 1852
3. Madras Native Association — First petition regarding non-implementation of the Allahabad Proclamation

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
186.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Gazula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty’s Madras Native Association was established in 1852 and was the first to petition against the non-implementation of the Allahabad Proclamation.
186.tq: Verify a person, organisation, year and associated activity together.
xs: All three pairs are **correct** — option **(4)**.
**Gazula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty** founded the **Madras Native Association** in **1852**.
It was the **first to petition** over **non-implementation of the Allahabad Proclamation**.
xa: The broken promise: **equal employment** — the ICS stayed European-dominated.
AP angle: **Coastal Andhra** and **Rayalaseema** stayed in the **Madras Presidency**.

186.s: Which aspect of British policy was fixed by the Proclamation of 1858 and continued until 1947?
o: Policy towards Indian princes and religion
Policy of complete military disarmament of the princes
Policy of abolishing all princely states
186.x: The Proclamation of 1858 established British policy towards the Indian princes and religion, and this broad policy continued until independence in 1947.
186.tq: Select the option that precisely combines the two policy areas covered by the proclamation.
xs: The **1858** Proclamation fixed British policy on **princes and religion** till **1947** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Princes were not abolished: **no further annexation**, **adoption** allowed, **paramountcy** accepted.
xa: Religion: **no interference** and **no forced conversions**.
Called the "**Magna Carta of the Indian people**".

186.s: Rani Avantibai Lodhi of Ramgarh is associated with which of the following?
o: Opposition to the Doctrine of Lapse and victory at the Battle of Kheri
Support for the Subsidiary Alliance and victory at Plassey
Opposition to the Permanent Settlement and victory at Buxar
Support for Crown rule and victory at Kanpur
186.x: Rani Avantibai Lodhi opposed the Doctrine of Lapse and won the Battle of Kheri during the Revolt of 1857.
186.tq: Match the historical personality with both the cause resisted and the battle associated with her.
xs: **Rani Avantibai Lodhi** of **Ramgarh** fought the **Doctrine of Lapse** and won the **Battle of Kheri** (**1857**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Plassey**, **Buxar** and the **Subsidiary Alliance** have no link to her.
xa: She is remembered on her martyrdom day (**1 Sep 2026**).
After 1857 **Canning withdrew the Doctrine of Lapse** and recognised adoption.

186.s:
With reference to the territorial arrangement after the establishment of Crown rule, consider the following statements:

1. Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema remained parts of the Madras Presidency.
2. Telangana remained under the Nizam, subject to British suzerainty.
3. Both Coastal Andhra and Telangana were directly administered from London as separate provinces.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
186.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema remained in the Madras Presidency, while Telangana remained under the Nizam’s authority under British suzerainty until independence.
186.tq: Separate direct Crown administration from indirect control over a princely state.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema** stayed in the **Madras Presidency**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **Telangana** stayed **under the Nizam** (British suzerainty) till independence.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: neither became a separate London-run province — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: AP angle: Andhra came under **direct Crown rule**.
**Madras Native Association** (**1852**) first petitioned over the Allahabad Proclamation.

187.s:
With reference to the Battle of Bobbili, consider the following statements:
1. Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram attacked Bobbili under Ranga Rao.
2. The attack was supported by Bussy.
3. The women of the fort committed mass self-immolation after its fall.
4. Tandra Paparayudu later assassinated Vijayarama Raju in his camp.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
187.x: All four statements correctly describe the parties, French assistance, fall of the fort, mass self-immolation and the subsequent assassination of Vijayarama Raju.
187.tq: Check each statement against the sequence of parties, outcome and aftermath.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are **correct**: **Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram**, helped by the **French (Bussy)**, attacked Bobbili under **Ranga Rao**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: Ranga Rao was killed, the fort fell and the women committed **mass self-immolation**.
Statement 4 is **correct**: **Tandra Paparayudu** later assassinated Vijayarama Raju in his camp — so **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
xa: Date: **24 January 1757**; primary source: the play **Bobbili Yuddham**.
PYQ **2019**: the **French** helped Vizianagaram at Bobbili.
⚠ **Bobbili 1757** = Vizianagaram + French vs Bobbili; **Padmanabham 1794** = Company vs Vizianagaram.

187.s: Which one of the following correctly explains the significance of the Treaty of Aurangabad of 1753 in the context of the Battle of Bobbili?
o: It ended the revolt of the Palegars.
It granted the Circars to the British Crown.
It transferred Kurnool to the Nizam.
It gave the Circars to the French.
187.x: The Treaty of Aurangabad of 1753 gave the Circars to the French. It forms part of the political context of the Battle of Bobbili.
187.tq: Match the treaty with its specific territorial consequence.
xs: The **Treaty of Aurangabad** (**1753**) **gave the Circars to the French** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was the French, not the British Crown, who got the Circars; it had nothing to do with Kurnool or the palegars.
xa: The **Battle of Tummala** (**1757**) confirmed French control.
That is why **Bussy** backed **Vizianagaram** at **Bobbili** (**24 January 1757**).

187.s: Which event confirmed French control in the political context of the Battle of Bobbili?
187.x: The Battle of Tummala in 1757 confirmed French control. The other battles belong to different contexts.
187.tq: Distinguish similarly named battles by their historical consequence.
xs: The **Battle of Tummala** (**1757**) confirmed **French control** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Mundlapadu** and **Pairamalla Konda** belong to the **Uyyalawada revolt** (**1846**); **Padmanabham** was **1794**.
xa: The **Treaty of Aurangabad** (**1753**) had given the **Circars** to the French.
At **Bobbili** the French under **Bussy** helped **Vijayarama Raju**.

187.s: The primary source associated with the Battle of Bobbili is which of the following?
187.x: The play Bobbili Yuddham is identified as the primary source associated with the Battle of Bobbili.
187.tq: Discriminate between a literary source and administrative records.
xs: The primary source for Bobbili is the play **Bobbili Yuddham** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Faujdari Adalat** record and **Kadapa Collector's** reports relate to **Uyyalawada** (**1846-47**); the **Queen's Proclamation** is **1858**.
xa: **Ranga Rao** and **Tandra Paparayudu** remain symbols of **Telugu valour**.
Battle date: **24 January 1757**.

187.s: The British officer associated with the command of the Company forces at the Battle of Padmanabham was
187.x: Colonel Pendergast commanded the English East India Company forces at the Battle of Padmanabham.
187.tq: Match the military commander with the correct battle, avoiding names from other suppressive operations.
xs: The Company's commander at **Padmanabham** was **Col. Pendergast** ("**Fender Gast**" in CDX's spelling) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**George Russell** was made **special officer over the forts** after the battle.
**Capt. Wilson** suppressed **Dandasena**; **Capt. Abbat** suppressed **Mir Fida Ali** at Aurangabad.
xa: Date: **10 July 1794** (CDI gives **8 July**).
The Raja and about **1,000** Kshatriya warriors were killed — compared to **Culloden**.

187.s:
Consider the following statements about the events before the Battle of Padmanabham:
1. The Company demanded a tribute of Rs 3 lakh and the disbanding of the Raja's troops, which Chinna Vijayarama Raju refused.
2. On 2 August 1793 the British seized the Vizianagaram fort and split the estate into three parts.
3. The Raja was then ordered to live at Bobbili on a pension of Rs 1,200.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
187.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the Raja was ordered to live in Machilipatnam, not Bobbili. The other two are correct: the Company demanded Rs 3 lakh and disbanding of troops, which the Raja refused; on 2 August 1793 the fort was seized and the estate split into three parts. So '1 and 2 only' is right; every other option either includes statement 3 or leaves out a correct statement.
187.tq: Rs 3 lakh = demand before the battle; Rs 6 lakh = peshkash for restoration; exile = Machilipatnam.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: the Company demanded **Rs 3 lakh** tribute and **disbanding of troops**; **Chinna Vijayarama Raju** refused.
Statement 2 is **correct**: on **2 Aug 1793** the British seized the **Vizianagaram fort** and split the estate into **3 parts**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: the Raja was sent to **Machilipatnam**, not Bobbili, on a **Rs 1,200** pension — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Background: the Raja had removed his step-brother and Diwan **Sitarama Raju** for misrule (**1784**); Sitarama Raju bribed his way back.
Some notes say the estate was split into **three collectorates**.

187.s: The Battle of Padmanabham was fought between the English East India Company and
o: the Pusapati Vizianagaram zamindar Chinna Vijayarama Gajapati Raju II
the Munsubar of Rampachodavaram supported by the Rohillas
the Nizam's forces led by Turrebaz Khan
the Raja of Bobbili supported by Nana Saheb
187.x: The battle was fought between the English East India Company and Pusapati Chinna Vijayarama Gajapati Raju II, the Vizianagaram zamindar.
187.tq: Use the parties to the conflict to distinguish Padmanabham from other Andhra and Hyderabad episodes.
xs: **Padmanabham** was fought between the Company and **Pusapati (Chinna) Vijayarama Gajapati Raju (II)**, Vizianagaram zamindar — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Turrebaz Khan** belongs to **Hyderabad 1857**; Bobbili's **Ranga Rao** fell in **1757**.
xa: Site: between **Bhimunipatnam** and **Vizianagaram**; date **10 July 1794**.
Exam angle: "Padmanabham decided whose defeat?" — **Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram**, not Bobbili.

187.s:
Consider the following statements about Vizianagaram after the Battle of Padmanabham (1794):
1. Vizianagaram was reduced to an ordinary zamindari.
2. The estate was restored to the minor son Narayana Babu on accepting a Rs 3 lakh peshkash under the Permanent Settlement of 1793.
3. Narayana Babu had hidden at Makkuva before the restoration.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
187.x: Statement 2 is wrong: the estate was restored on accepting the Permanent Settlement (1802) and a Rs 6 lakh peshkash; Rs 3 lakh was the earlier tribute demand. The other two are correct: Vizianagaram was reduced to an ordinary zamindari, and Narayana Babu had hidden at Makkuva. So '1 and 3 only' is right; every other option either includes statement 2 or leaves out a correct statement.
187.tq: Restoration = Permanent Settlement 1802 + Rs 6 lakh peshkash.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: Vizianagaram was reduced to an **ordinary zamindari**.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: restoration came on accepting the **Permanent Settlement (1802)** and a **Rs 6 lakh peshkash**; **Rs 3 lakh** was the earlier tribute demand.
Statement 3 is **correct**: minor son **Narayana Babu** hid at **Makkuva** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: **George Russell** was made special officer over the forts.
The battle (**10 July 1794**) was compared to **Culloden**.

187.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: George Russell — special officer over the forts
Culloden — comparison used for the Battle of Padmanabham
Madhava Bhupati Dev — British commander at Padmanabham
187.x: Madhava Bhupati Dev was not the British commander at Padmanabham: the Company forces there were commanded by Col. Pendergast ("Fender Gast" in CDX). The other pairs are correct: George Russell was made special officer over the forts, the battle was compared to Culloden, and Padmanabham lies between Bhimunipatnam and Vizianagaram.
187.tq: Spot the swapped official and battle commander from otherwise correct associations.
xs: **Madhava Bhupati Dev** was not the British commander — that was **Col. Pendergast** — so option **(3)** is the mismatch.
**George Russell** — special officer over the forts; **Culloden** comparison; site between **Bhimunipatnam** and **Vizianagaram**: all correct.
xa: About **1,000** Kshatriya warriors died with the Raja.
Date: **10 July 1794** (CDI gives **8 July**).

187.s: The Battle of Padmanabham, in which the English East India Company defeated the Vizianagaram zamindar Chinna Vijayarama Raju, was fought in:
187.x: Padmanabham was fought on 10 July 1794 (CDI gives 8 July). 1757 is the Battle of Bobbili, 1802 is when Narayana Babu was restored under the Permanent Settlement, and 1846 is the Uyyalawada revolt.
187.tq: Bobbili 1757, Padmanabham 1794.
xs: **Padmanabham** was fought on **10 July 1794** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**1757** is **Bobbili**; **1802** is Narayana Babu's restoration under the **Permanent Settlement**; **1846** is the **Uyyalawada** revolt.
xa: ⚠ CDI gives **8 July**; CDX and APHQ give **10 July**.
The British had seized the Vizianagaram fort on **2 Aug 1793**.

187.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Place — Nature of resistance
o: Ghumsur — Resistance by zamindars against the Company
Kurnool — Resistance led by French officers
Parlakimedi — Revolt by the Nizam's army
Bhupayya — Resistance confined to the Madras Presidency
187.x: The zamindars of Ghumsur and Parlakimedi (Ganjam) resisted the Company, so A is right. The Kurnool Nawabs (descended from Golconda nobles) were reduced and deposed in 1839 with no French role; Parlakimedi's resistance was by zamindars, not the Nizam's army; and Bhupayya was driven out of the Vizag hills into the Nizam's territory, so his resistance was not confined to Madras.
187.tq: Start from the sure place–event pair and eliminate swapped descriptions.
xs: **Ghumsur** — the **zamindars resisted the Company** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Kurnool**'s Nawabs (from **Golconda nobles**) were **deposed in 1839** — no French role.
**Parlakimedi**'s resistance was by **zamindars**; **Bhupayya** was driven into the **Nizam's territory**, so not confined to Madras.
xa: Ghumsur and Parlakimedi lie in **Ganjam**, now **Odisha**.
Bhupayya had about **2,000** followers in the Vizag hills and died **1796**.

187.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Kurnool:
1. The Nawabs of Kurnool were descended from Golconda nobles.
2. They were reduced and deposed in 1839.
3. Their resistance was organised with the help of Bussy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
187.x: The Kurnool Nawabs were descended from Golconda nobles and were reduced and deposed in 1839. Bussy was associated with the Battle of Bobbili, not with this Kurnool fact.
187.tq: Separate the correct regional facts from a nearby historical association.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: the **Kurnool Nawabs** descended from **Golconda nobles**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: they were **reduced and deposed in 1839**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: **Bussy** belongs to **Bobbili** (**1757**) — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: **Kurnool** was later the base of **Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy** (**1846**).
Kurnool was among the **Ceded Districts** (**1800**).

187.s: Which of the following statements about Bhupayya is correct?
o: He led the French forces at Bobbili and died in 1757.
He organised the Godavari Agency movement from Errannagudem.
He was a British officer who suppressed the Kurnool revolt.
He led about 2,000 followers in the Vizag hills and was driven into Nizam's territory.
187.x: Bhupayya operated in the Vizag hills with about 2,000 followers, was driven into Nizam's territory and died in 1796.
187.tq: Use the person–region–movement combination to reject swapped identities.
xs: **Bhupayya** led about **2,000 followers** in the **Vizag hills** and was **driven into the Nizam's territory** — so option **(4)** is correct.
He died in **1796**; **Errannagudem** belongs to **Korukonda Subba Reddy** (**1857**).
xa: Other zamindari resistance: **Ghumsur**, **Parlakimedi** (Ganjam).
**Kurnool** Nawabs deposed in **1839**.

187.s: The term ‘Poligars’ or ‘Palegars’ in the context of the early South Indian resistance referred primarily to:
o: Local military chiefs and long-time revenue farmers
187.x: Poligars were local military chiefs who had also functioned as long-time revenue farmers.
187.tq: Use the exact institutional meaning of a historical office.
xs: **Poligars** were **local military chiefs** and **long-time revenue farmers** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They were neither missionaries, judges nor merchants.
xa: In Rayalaseema they were **fortified military chiefs** under the **Nizam's nominal suzerainty**.
The Company's **1781** deal letting the **Nawab of Arcot** manage revenue hit their rights.
Leaders: **Veerapandya Kattabomman**, **Marudu brothers**.

187.s: Which development adversely affected the traditional rights of the Poligars in the Carnatic and Tirunelveli region?
o: The introduction of Ryotwari settlement in 1847
The Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam in 1798 alone
The recall of William Bentinck from Madras
The Company's 1781 arrangement allowing the Nawab of Arcot to manage revenue
187.x: The Company's 1781 arrangement allowed the Nawab of Arcot to manage the revenues of Tirunelveli and the Carnatic, affecting the rights of the Poligars.
187.tq: Link a policy arrangement with its institutional consequence.
xs: The Company's **1781** deal letting the **Nawab of Arcot** manage **Tirunelveli** and **Carnatic** revenue hit the poligars' rights — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Subsidiary Alliance** (**1798**) relates to the Nizam's **1800** cession; **Bentinck**'s recall followed **Vellore** (**1806**).
xa: **Kattabomman** (Panchalankurichi) was hanged **1799**.
**Marudu brothers** (Sivaganga) were executed **1801**.

187.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
187.x: Velu Thampi Dalawa was the Diwan of Travancore. Kattabomman was associated with Panchalankurichi, while the Marudu brothers were associated with Sivaganga.
187.tq: Start from the sure leader–region pair and eliminate swapped locations.
xs: **Velu Thampi Dalawa** was **Diwan of Travancore** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Kattabomman** — **Panchalankurichi** (Tirunelveli); **Marudu brothers** — **Sivaganga**: options 1 and 2 are swapped.
xa: Velu Thampi's revolt: **1808-09** (UPSC notes: **1809-10**), the **Kundara Proclamation**.
Kattabomman hanged **1799**; Marudu brothers executed **1801**.

187.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Veerapandya Kattabomman — Hanged in 1799
2. Marudu brothers — Executed in 1801
3. Velu Thampi Dalawa — Kundara Proclamation
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
187.x: All three pairs are correct. Kattabomman was hanged in 1799, the Marudu brothers were executed in 1801, and Velu Thampi Dalawa was associated with the Kundara Proclamation.
187.tq: Combine leader, date and associated event in a compact statement set.
xs: All three pairs are **correct** — option **(4)**.
**Kattabomman** hanged **1799**; **Marudu brothers** executed **1801**.
**Velu Thampi Dalawa** — **Kundara Proclamation**.
xa: Kattabomman's seat: **Panchalankurichi** (Tirunelveli); Marudu brothers: **Sivaganga** (South Indian rebellion).
Velu Thampi was **Diwan of Travancore**; revolt **1808-09**.

187.s: Palegars in the Ceded Districts were best described as:
o: British civil servants appointed by the Madras Governor
Religious heads controlling the Wahabi Movement
Fortified military chiefs exercising autonomous power under the Nizam's nominal suzerainty
187.x: Palegars were fortified military chiefs who exercised autonomous power under the nominal suzerainty of the Nizam.
187.tq: Test the nature of the office through its political and military attributes.
xs: Palegars were **fortified military chiefs** with **autonomous power** under the **Nizam's nominal suzerainty** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They were not **village accountants** or **British civil servants**; the **Wahabi Movement** belongs to **Mubariz-ud-Daula** (**1839**).
xa: Dozens existed in **Kurnool**, **Cuddapah**, **Bellary** and **Anantapur**.
Collector **Thomas Munro** made them **disarm** and **pay peshkash**.

187.s: Palegars were found in considerable numbers in which group of districts?
187.x: There were dozens of Palegars in Kurnool, Cuddapah, Bellary and Anantapur.
187.tq: Recall the complete geographical cluster instead of selecting a partially related region.
xs: Palegars were numerous in **Kurnool, Cuddapah, Bellary and Anantapur** — so option **(1)** is correct.
These are the **Ceded Districts** given up by the Nizam in **1800**.
xa: The cession came under the **Subsidiary Alliance** (**1798**).
About **80** Rayalaseema palegars rose in **1800**.

187.s:
Consider the following statements about palegar revolts in the Ceded Districts:
1. In 1800, about 80 Rayalaseema palegars resisted Munro's order to disarm and pay peshkash.
2. Mutakuri Goudappa, who attacked the Sub-Collector's office, was captured and hanged by Collector Thomas Munro.
3. In 1801, village Patel Mutakuri Goudappa attacked the Sub-Collector's office at Taranikallu in the Adoni division.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
187.x: Statement 2 is wrong: Goudappa was captured and hanged by Sub-Collector Dhakar, not by Munro. The other two are correct: about 80 palegars resisted Munro's order in 1800, and Goudappa attacked the Taranikallu Sub-Collector's office in 1801. So '1 and 3 only' is right; every other option either includes statement 2 or leaves out a correct statement.
187.tq: Taranikallu 1801: Goudappa vs Sub-Collector Dhakar.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: in **1800** about **80 Rayalaseema palegars** resisted **Munro**'s order to disarm and pay peshkash.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: **Goudappa** was captured and hanged by **Sub-Collector Dhakar**, not Munro.
Statement 3 is **correct**: in **1801** **Mutakuri Goudappa** attacked the Sub-Collector's office at **Taranikallu** (Adoni) — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: Munro's suppression took **18 months** of military action.
The **Palakonda** poligars (Srikakulam) rebelled against heavy taxes.

187.s: The Palakonda Poligars, located in present-day Srikakulam region, rebelled mainly against:
o: The establishment of the Agency system
187.x: The Palakonda Poligars rebelled against heavy taxes and were brutally suppressed.
187.tq: Match the local revolt with its immediate grievance.
xs: The **Palakonda** poligars (Srikakulam) rebelled against **heavy taxes** — so option **(3)** is correct.
They were **brutally suppressed**.
The **Kundara Proclamation** is **Velu Thampi**'s; new uniforms caused **Vellore** (**1806**).
xa: Other risings: **Taranikallu** (**1801**, Goudappa), **Rayalaseema** (**1800**, 80 palegars).
The **Agency system** grew out of the **1830s** Vizianagaram-Visakhapatnam hill unrest.

187.s: Which of the following was NOT among the principal causes of resistance by Palegars and other local groups?
o: The Company's order to disarm the Palegars
The introduction of the Kundara Proclamation by Thomas Munro
Forfeiture of estates under the Permanent Settlement
187.x: Heavy revenue and peshkash demands, estate forfeiture and the order to disarm Palegars were causes of resistance. The Kundara Proclamation was associated with Velu Thampi, not Thomas Munro's Palegar policy.
187.tq: Find the wrongly attributed policy among several genuine causes.
xs: The **Kundara Proclamation** was **Velu Thampi Dalawa**'s (Travancore), not Munro's — so option **(3)** is the answer.
Real causes: the **disarm order**, heavy **revenue and peshkash**, **forfeiture of estates** under the Permanent Settlement.
xa: Territorial cessions: **Guntur** (**1788**) and the **Ceded Districts** (**1800**).
Munro was **Principal Collector** (PYQ **2011**).

187.s:
Which of the following statements about the territorial changes preceding Palegar resistance is correct?
1. The Company took Guntur from Nizam Ali in 1788 for Rs 7 lakh.
2. The Nizam ceded Cuddapah, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary in 1800.
3. The 1800 cession occurred under the Subsidiary Alliance of 1798.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
187.x: All three statements are correct. Guntur was taken in 1788 for Rs 7 lakh, and the four Ceded Districts were ceded by the Nizam in 1800 under the Subsidiary Alliance of 1798.
187.tq: Combine date, amount, territory and treaty in a coded statement question.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: the Company took **Guntur** in **1788** from **Nizam Ali** for **Rs 7 lakh**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: the Nizam ceded **Cuddapah, Kurnool, Anantapur, Bellary** in **1800**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: the cession came under the **Subsidiary Alliance (1798)** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: The ceded area is **Rayalaseema** (Ceded Districts).
The cession bred **discontent**, behind the **1800** palegar rising.

187.s: Who was the principal officer responsible for suppressing the Palegar revolts in the Ceded Districts?
187.x: Thomas Munro, serving as Principal Collector, was chiefly responsible for suppressing the Palegar revolts.
187.tq: Identify the correct administrative officer rather than a military or neighbouring official.
xs: **Thomas Munro**, **Principal Collector** (PYQ **2011**), suppressed the palegars — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was helped by military officer **Campbell**.
**Bentinck** was Madras Governor at **Vellore** (**1806**); **Cochrane** was **Kadapa Collector** in **1846**.
xa: He introduced **Ryotwari** in the Ceded Districts.
Methods: proclamations, **18 months** of military action, **confiscation** of estates.

187.s:
Which of the following correctly describes the methods used to suppress the Palegars?
1. Proclamations called upon them to lay down their arms.
2. Military action continued over eighteen months.
3. Rebel estates were confiscated.
4. Loyal heirs were given small pensions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
187.x: All four measures formed part of the suppression and settlement policy: disarmament proclamations, military action for eighteen months, confiscation of rebel estates and small pensions for loyal heirs.
187.tq: Use a comprehensive option to test the full sequence of coercion and settlement.
xs: All four are **correct** — option **(4)**.
**Proclamations** to lay down arms and military action over **18 months**.
**Confiscation of rebel estates**; **loyal heirs** got small pensions.
xa: Officers: **Thomas Munro** and **Campbell**.
Settlement that followed: **Ryotwari**.

187.s: The settlement introduced in the Ceded Districts after the suppression of the Palegars was:
187.x: The settlement introduced in the Ceded Districts was Ryotwari. Permanent Settlement is an incorrect attribution in this context.
187.tq: Discriminate between closely associated revenue-settlement terms.
xs: The Ceded Districts got **Ryotwari** — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes write "**Permanent Settlement**" here — an error; every other source gives Ryotwari.
xa: The Ryotwari was introduced by **Thomas Munro**.
Vizianagaram, by contrast, was restored under the **Permanent Settlement (1802)**.

187.s: What was the principal cause of the Vellore Mutiny?
o: The Company's takeover of Guntur from the Nizam
The introduction of Ryotwari settlement in the Ceded Districts
Confiscation of the estates of the Marudu brothers
New dress regulations that offended caste and religious sentiments
187.x: The new uniform regulations, including changes concerning the turban and a ban on caste marks, hurt the caste and religious sentiments of the sepoys.
187.tq: Identify the specific policy cause instead of confusing it with revenue grievances.
xs: **Vellore** (**1806**) broke out over **new dress/uniform regulations** hurting **caste and religious sentiment** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The turban change and the **ban on caste marks** offended sepoys.
xa: Second cause: **Tipu's family** lodged in the fort.
Vellore = **first major sepoy revolt**, half a century before **1857**.

187.s: Which of the following factors is associated with the outbreak of the Vellore Mutiny?
o: The takeover of the Nosam estate
The presence of Tipu Sultan's family in Vellore Fort
The imprisonment of Mubariz-ud-Daula in Golconda Fort
187.x: Tipu Sultan's family was lodged in Vellore Fort, which was an associated factor in the mutiny.
187.tq: Distinguish a contextual factor of Vellore from causes of other regional revolts.
xs: **Tipu's family** lodged in **Vellore Fort** was a cause — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Nosam** belongs to **Uyyalawada**; **Mubariz-ud-Daula** to Hyderabad; the **Kundara Proclamation** to Travancore.
xa: Main cause: new **dress/uniform regulations**.
Date: **10 July 1806**; sepoys seized **Vellore Fort**.

187.s: Which consequence followed the Vellore Mutiny?
o: The Agency system was abolished immediately.
Thomas Munro was appointed Principal Collector of the Ceded Districts.
Mubariz-ud-Daula was released from Golconda Fort.
Madras Governor William Bentinck and Commander-in-Chief Cradock were recalled.
187.x: Following the mutiny, Madras Governor William Bentinck and the Commander-in-Chief Cradock were recalled.
187.tq: Match a revolt with its administrative consequence and avoid authority swaps.
xs: After Vellore, Madras Governor **William Bentinck** and C-in-C **Cradock** were **recalled** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Munro's Ceded Districts work came earlier (**1800-01**).
xa: Vellore (**1806**) = first major sepoy revolt.
Causes: **uniform regulations**; **Tipu's family** in the fort.

187.s: Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy belonged to which district of present-day Andhra Pradesh?
187.x: Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy belonged to the Palegar family of Uyyalawada in Koilakuntla taluk of Kurnool district.
187.tq: Use the direct place-based recall of the rebel leader.
xs: **Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy** was born in **Koilakuntla taluk, Kurnool district** — so option **(2)** is correct.
PYQ **2022**: "born in **Kurnool** district" is correct.
xa: Uyyalawada is now in **Nandyal district** after the **2022** reorganisation.
Father: **Pedda Mallareddy**, Palegar of Uyyalawada.

187.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the immediate cause of Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy's revolt?
o: A ban on podu cultivation and toddy tapping
Takeover of his estate, reduction to a meagre pension, and the order to disarm and pay peshkash
Introduction of new military uniforms at Vellore
Forcible conversion of local chiefs to Christianity
187.x: His estate was taken over under Munro, he was offered only a meagre pension, and he was ordered to lay down arms and pay peshkash.
187.tq: Separate the specific revenue and disarmament cause from causes of other revolts.
xs: His grievance: the **estate taken over**, a **meagre pension** (**Rs 35**) and the order to **disarm and pay peshkash** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Podu** and **toddy** restrictions belong to **Rampa 1879**; uniforms belong to **Vellore 1806**.
xa: The disarm order dates from **1800-02** → read as the **root grievance** behind **1846**.
His grandfather's **Nosam** estate became government land by **1802** without a pension.

187.s:
Consider the following statements about the family background of Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy:
1. He was the younger son of Pedda Mallareddy, Palegar of Uyyalawada.
2. He was the maternal grandson of Nosam Palegar Jayarama Reddy.
3. When the Nosam estate became government land by 1802, its heirs were given a generous pension.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
187.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the Nosam heirs were left without any pension. The other two are correct: he was the younger son of Pedda Mallareddy and the maternal grandson of Nosam Palegar Jayarama Reddy. So '1 and 2 only' is right; every other option either includes statement 3 or leaves out a correct statement.
187.tq: The grievance theme: estates taken, no or meagre pension.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: he was the younger son of **Pedda Mallareddy**, Palegar of Uyyalawada.
Statement 2 is **correct**: maternal grandson of **Nosam Palegar Jayarama Reddy**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: Nosam became government land by **1802** **without a pension** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: The **three sons** got only **Rs 35** pension from the Uyyalawada estate.
Birthplace: **Koilakuntla taluk**, **Kurnool**.

187.s: During Munro's time, what was the immediate financial grievance associated with the Uyyalawada estate?
o: The sons were granted a pension of Rs 1,000 each.
The estate was transferred to the French and its zamindar was imprisoned.
The estate was restored but the sons were denied all land revenue.
The estate was taken over and the three sons were paid only Rs 35 as pension.
187.x: The government took over the Uyyalawada estate during Munro's time and paid the three sons a meagre pension of Rs 35.
187.tq: Use the precise amount and administrative action to identify the grievance.
xs: In **Munro**'s time the **Uyyalawada estate** was taken over and the **three sons** got only **Rs 35** pension — so option **(4)** is correct.
No **Rs 1,000** pension, French transfer or restoration — **₹1,000** was the later reward for his capture.
xa: The **Nosam** estate went to government by **1802** with no pension.
Munro also ordered palegars to **disarm** and **pay peshkash**.

187.s: Which group best represents the support base of the revolt?
o: Only officials from the Godavari Agency
Farmers, Yanadis, tribal people and people from the Uyyalawada and Nosam estates
Only zamindars from Parlakimedi and Ghumsur
French soldiers, British sepoys and Madras judges
187.x: The movement had about 5,000 followers, including farmers, Yanadis, tribal people and people from the Uyyalawada and Nosam estates.
187.tq: Identify the broad social base rather than an exclusive elite group.
xs: His base: **farmers**, **Yanadis**, **tribal people** and people of the **Uyyalawada and Nosam estates** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It numbered about **5,000 followers**.
xa: Comparison: the **1800-01** rising was **80 palegars** under Munro; **1846** was a single-leader guerrilla revolt with a peasant and tribal base.
It was the **last major palegar rising** in Rayalaseema, a decade before **1857**.

187.s: Approximately how many followers were associated with the revolt?
187.x: About 5,000 followers supported the revolt.
187.tq: Separate the follower count from the smaller figure associated with Bhupayya.
xs: The revolt had about **5,000 followers** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**2,000** was **Bhupayya**'s following in the Vizag hills; **35** was the pension in rupees.
xa: Followers: **farmers**, **Yanadis**, tribal people, Uyyalawada and **Nosam** estates.
A **₹1,000 reward** was announced for his capture.

187.s: Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy was publicly hanged at Koilakuntla on:
187.x: Captured on 7 October 1846 and sentenced to death by the Faujdari Adalat in January 1847, he was publicly hanged near Koilakuntla on 22 February 1847. 22 February 1846 is a year too early (the revolt began only in July 1846), and 10 July 1806 is the Vellore Mutiny.
187.tq: Test the exact date through close year-and-day distractors.
xs: He was **publicly hanged near Koilakuntla** on **22 February 1847** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**1846** is too early — the revolt began only in **July 1846**; **10 July 1806** is **Vellore**.
xa: Captured **7 Oct 1846**; death sentence by the **Faujdari Adalat** in **January 1847**.
Memorial: **Orvakal airport** renamed **Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy Airport**.

187.s:
Arrange the following events of the 1846 revolt in chronological order:
A. The rebels were ambushed at Mundlapadu.
B. The revolt began and nine government sepoys were killed.
C. Rudravaram and the treasury at Kasba Koilakuntla were looted.
D. The leader was captured at the Jagannatha Swamy temple, Pairamalla Konda.
187.x: The revolt began in July, the treasury was looted on 12 July, the Mundlapadu ambush occurred on 24 July, and the capture took place on 7 October 1846.
187.tq: Fix the sequence using the dated events and the final capture.
xs: Order **B, C, A, D** — option **(1)**.
B: revolt began, **July 1846** (**9** sepoys killed) → C: **Rudravaram** and **Koilakuntla** treasury looted, **12 July 1846**.
A: **Mundlapadu** ambush, **24 July 1846** → D: capture at **Pairamalla Konda**, **7 Oct 1846**.
xa: After the treasury raid he marched towards **Cumbum**.
In mid-**1846** he escaped to the **Nizam's dominions**, returning about **6 weeks** later.

187.s: On 12 July 1846, the rebels looted which of the following?
o: The Nizam's treasury and the Mundlapadu cantonment
The treasury at Kasba Koilakuntla and Rudravaram
The Jagannatha Swamy temple and Cumbum fort
The Kadapa Collectorate and Kurnool treasury
187.x: On 12 July 1846, the rebels looted Rudravaram and the treasury at Kasba Koilakuntla.
187.tq: Associate the exact date with the places attacked.
xs: On **12 July 1846** the rebels looted **Rudravaram** and the treasury at **(Kasba) Koilakuntla** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Mundlapadu** was the ambush site; the **Jagannatha Swamy temple** the capture site.
xa: After the raid he marched towards **Cumbum**.
The revolt began in **July 1846**, with **9** government sepoys killed.

187.s: What happened at Mundlapadu on 24 July 1846?
o: The Godavari movement came to an end.
The rebels were ambushed; 25 rebels and the Kambam Tahsildar were killed.
The rebels crossed into French territory with Bussy's support.
The leader was publicly hanged after trial.
187.x: At Mundlapadu, Captain Nott ambushed the rebels. Twenty-five rebels were killed and the Kambam Tahsildar also died.
187.tq: Match the place and date with the military outcome.
xs: At **Mundlapadu** (**24 July 1846**) **Captain Nott** ambushed the rebels: **25** rebels killed and the **Kambam Tahsildar** died — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was **not hanged** there — that came on **22 February 1847** near Koilakuntla.
xa: APP spells the officer "**Nolt**".
The final capture came on **7 Oct 1846**: **50** rebels killed, **90** captured.

187.s: The final capture on 7 October 1846 took place at which location?
o: The Jagannatha Swamy temple at Pairamalla Konda
187.x: The leader was captured at the Jagannatha Swamy temple, Pairamalla Konda, after suffering a leg wound.
187.tq: Use the exact capture site to distinguish it from earlier places of attack.
xs: He was captured at the **Jagannatha Swamy temple**, **Pairamalla Konda**, after a **leg wound** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Errannagudem** is **Korukonda Subba Reddy**'s centre; **Koilakuntla** treasury was looted on **12 July 1846**.
xa: At the capture **50** rebels were killed and **90** captured.
Hanged near **Koilakuntla** on **22 February 1847**.

187.s: Who raised the alarm regarding the revolt associated with Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy?
187.x: Kadapa Collector J. H. Cockrane raised the alarm. Captain Nott, Captain Russell and Lieutenant Moore were deployed subsequently.
187.tq: Separate the civil official who raised the alarm from the military officers deployed.
xs: **Kadapa Collector J.H. Cockrane** raised the alarm and pursued him — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Captain Nott**, **Captain Russell** and **Lt. Moore** were the officers deployed.
xa: Some notes spell him **Cochrane**.
Main official record: the **Kadapa Collector's reports** and the **Faujdari Adalat** trial record.

187.s:
Consider the following statements about the capture and trial of Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy:
1. Captain Nott, Captain Russell and Lt. Moore were deployed against him.
2. A reward of Rs 1,000 was announced for his capture.
3. The Faujdari Adalat passed the death sentence on him in January 1846.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
187.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the death sentence came in January 1847 (the revolt itself began only in July 1846); he was hanged on 22 February 1847. The other two are correct: Captain Nott, Captain Russell and Lt. Moore were deployed, and a Rs 1,000 reward was announced. So '1 and 2 only' is right; every other option either includes statement 3 or leaves out a correct statement.
187.tq: Revolt 1846, sentence and hanging 1847.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Captain Nott**, **Captain Russell** and **Lt. Moore** were deployed.
Statement 2 is **correct**: a **₹1,000 reward** was announced.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: the sentence came in **January 1847** — the revolt began only in **July 1846** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Charges: **rebellion**, **murder**, **looting**.
Hanged on **22 February 1847** near Koilakuntla.

187.s: The captured leader was tried by which institution?
187.x: He was tried by the Faujdari Adalat for rebellion, murder and looting.
187.tq: Match the legal body with the offences and proceedings.
xs: He was tried by the **Faujdari Adalat** for **rebellion, murder and looting** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Madras High Court** came only in **1862**, replacing Company courts.
xa: Sentence: death, **January 1847**; hanged **22 February 1847**.
The trial record is a main official source, with **Cockrane**'s reports.

187.s: Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy is associated with which of the following events?
o: Capturing the treasury at Koilkuntla and being hanged after his revolt
Signing the Carnatic Treaty with Azim-ud-Daula
Establishing the Board of Revenue at Masulipatnam
Negotiating the lease of the Northern Circars from the Nizam
187.x: Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy, a Kurnool poligar, revolted in the 1840s, looted the treasury at Koilkuntla and was later hanged.
187.tq: Match the local leader with his specific action and place.
xs: He **looted the treasury at Koilakuntla** and was **hanged** after his revolt — so option **(1)** is correct.
The loot was on **12 July 1846**; the hanging on **22 February 1847**.
xa: Film: **Sye Raa Narasimha Reddy** (**2019**).
Listed as "**Rayalaseema freedom fighter, Palegar**".
It was the **last major palegar rising** in Rayalaseema.

187.s: Which one of the following statements about Orvakal airport is correct?
o: It was renamed Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy Airport and became operational on 25 March 2021.
It is located in the Godavari district and began operation in 1862.
It was built by the French and transferred to the state in 1757.
It was renamed after Tandra Paparayudu in 2019.
187.x: Orvakal airport in Kurnool was operational from 25 March 2021 and was renamed Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy Airport.
187.tq: Combine the place, renaming and operational date precisely.
xs: **Orvakal airport** (Kurnool), operational since **25 March 2021**, was renamed **Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy Airport** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Tandra Paparayudu** is the hero of **Bobbili** (**1757**), not the airport's namesake.
xa: Film: **Sye Raa Narasimha Reddy** (**2019**).
Uyyalawada is now in **Nandyal district** (**2022** reorganisation).

187.s: The film associated with the memory of Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy is titled:
187.x: Sye Raa Narasimha Reddy, released in 2019, is the film associated with him.
187.tq: Distinguish the modern film title from the historical play and honours.
xs: The film on Uyyalawada is **Sye Raa Narasimha Reddy** (**2019**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Bobbili Yuddham** is the play on the **Battle of Bobbili** (**1757**); the **Star of India** went to **Afzal-ud-Daula**.
xa: **Orvakal airport** (Kurnool) was renamed **Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy Airport** (operational **25 March 2021**).
He is listed as "**Rayalaseema freedom fighter, Palegar**".
Hanged near **Koilakuntla** on **22 February 1847**.

187.s: Who succeeded Nizam Nasir-ud-Daula in Hyderabad in 1857?
187.x: Afzal-ud-Daula succeeded Nasir-ud-Daula in 1857 and ruled Hyderabad from 1857 to 1869.
187.tq: Use the direct succession clue and distinguish the Nizam from the other Hyderabad figures.
xs: **Afzal-ud-Daula** (**1857-69**), son of **Nasir-ud-Daula**, succeeded him — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Mubariz-ud-Daula** was the Nizam's brother who led the **Wahabi Movement** (**1839**); **Mir Fida Ali** led the **Aurangabad** outbreak.
xa: Nasir-ud-Daula died on **16 May 1857**.
APPSC G2 **2001**: Nizam of 1857 = **Afzal-ud-Daula**.
He was **pro-British** and later got the "**Star of India**".

187.s:
Consider the following statements about Hyderabad in 1857:
1. Nizam Nasir-ud-Daula died on 16 May 1857 and was succeeded by Afzal-ud-Daula.
2. Mir Turab Ali Khan, the Diwan retained by the new Nizam, was known as Salar Jung I.
3. Salar Jung I sided with the rebels while the Nizam stayed pro-British.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
187.x: Statement 3 is wrong: both the Nizam and Salar Jung I were pro-British. The other two are correct: Nasir-ud-Daula died on 16 May 1857 and Afzal-ud-Daula succeeded him; he retained Mir Turab Ali Khan (Salar Jung I) as Diwan. So '1 and 2 only' is right; every other option either includes statement 3 or leaves out a correct statement.
187.tq: Nizam and Diwan were both loyal in 1857 - a statement making either a rebel is false.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Nasir-ud-Daula** died **16 May 1857**; **Afzal-ud-Daula** succeeded.
Statement 2 is **correct**: the retained Diwan **Mir Turab Ali Khan** was **Salar Jung I**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: both the Nizam and **Salar Jung I** were **pro-British** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Their loyalty kept the revolt from spreading in the **Deccan**.
Rewards: **Star of India** for Afzal-ud-Daula; Salar Jung honoured.

187.s: The outbreak at Aurangabad in June 1857 was associated with which of the following combinations?
o: Mir Fida Ali and Amir Khan
187.x: The Aurangabad outbreak was associated with Mir Fida Ali and Amir Khan. It was suppressed by Captain Abbot, and Fida Ali was hanged.
187.tq: Start from the sure person-event pair and reject leaders belonging to other risings.
xs: The **Aurangabad** outbreak (**June 1857**) was led by **Mir Fida Ali** with **Amir Khan** — so option **(1)** is correct.

**Turrebaz Khan** and **Maulvi Allauddin** attacked the **Residency** (**17 July 1857**); **Korra Mallayya** and **Chinna Bhupathi** led the **Ganjam Agency** rising (**1845-48**); **Bapurao** and **Venkatarao** — **Chanda**.
xa: It was suppressed by **Capt. Abbot** and **Fida Ali was hanged**.
The **1st Cavalry** of the **Hyderabad Contingent** came under suspicion and was disarmed.

187.s:
With reference to the Aurangabad outbreak of June 1857, consider the following statements:
1. The 1st Cavalry of the Hyderabad Contingent came under suspicion.
2. The suspected cavalry unit was disarmed.
3. Mir Fida Ali was transported for life to the Andamans.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
187.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The 1st Cavalry came under suspicion and was disarmed; Mir Fida Ali was hanged, whereas Maulvi Allauddin was transported to the Andamans.
187.tq: Separate the punishments of Fida Ali and Allauddin before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: the **1st Cavalry** of the **Hyderabad Contingent** came under suspicion.
Statement 2 is **correct**: it was **disarmed**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: **Fida Ali was hanged**; transportation to the **Andamans** was **Allauddin**'s fate — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Suppressor: **Capt. Abbot** (also spelt **Abbat**).
APPSC G1 **2023** chronology: Mubariz-ud-Daula's imprisonment → **Aurangabad** → **Turrebaz Khan**'s attack.

187.s: The immediate objective of Turrebaz Khan and Maulvi Allauddin in attacking the British Residency at Hyderabad was to
187.x: The attack was undertaken to free Jamedar Chida Khan, who had been arrested and held at Hyderabad.
187.tq: Identify the immediate purpose of an action rather than the broader background grievance.
xs: They attacked the Residency to **free Jamedar Chida Khan** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Chida Khan had been **arrested and held at Hyderabad**.
xa: Date: **17 July 1857**; repulsed by Resident **Davidson**.
**Capt. Abbot** was the suppressor at **Aurangabad**, not a target of the attack.
**Turrebaz Khan** was later caught and **shot near Toopran** (**1859**).

187.s:
Consider the following statements about the attack on the British Residency, Hyderabad (17 July 1857):
1. The attack was repulsed by Resident Davidson.
2. Maulvi Allauddin was captured and hanged at Aurangabad.
3. Turrebaz Khan escaped but was later caught and shot near Toopran.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
187.x: Statement 2 is wrong: Maulvi Allauddin was transported for life to the Andamans; hanging after the Aurangabad outbreak was Mir Fida Ali's fate. The other two are correct: Resident Davidson repulsed the attack, and Turrebaz Khan escaped, was caught and shot near Toopran (1859). So '1 and 3 only' is right; every other option either includes statement 2 or leaves out a correct statement.
187.tq: Fates: Allauddin - Andamans; Turrebaz Khan - shot near Toopran; Fida Ali - hanged.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: Resident **Davidson** repulsed the attack.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: **Allauddin** was **transported for life to the Andamans**; hanging was **Mir Fida Ali**'s fate.
Statement 3 is **correct**: **Turrebaz Khan** escaped, was caught and **shot near Toopran** (**1859**) — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: Aim: to free **Jamedar Chida Khan**.
AP angle: Turrebaz Khan is the key **Hyderabad** leader of 1857.

187.s:
Arrange the following events in Hyderabad in chronological order:
A. Arrest of Mubariz-ud-Daula
B. Aurangabad outbreak and disarming of the 1st Cavalry
C. Arrest and detention of Jamedar Chida Khan
D. Attack on the British Residency by Turrebaz Khan and Maulvi Allauddin
187.x: Mubariz-ud-Daula was arrested in 1839, the Aurangabad episode occurred in June 1857, Chida Khan was then detained, and the Residency was attacked on 17 July 1857.
187.tq: Fix the earliest event first and then distinguish the June episode from the July attack.
xs: Order **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)** — the APPSC G1 **2023** key.
A: **Mubariz-ud-Daula** imprisoned in **Golconda Fort** (Wahabi, **1839**) → B: **Aurangabad**, **June 1857**.
C: **Chida Khan** arrested → D: **Residency attack**, **17 July 1857**.
xa: The Residency attack was led by **Turrebaz Khan** and **Maulvi Allauddin**.
The new Nizam **Afzal-ud-Daula** had come in after **16 May 1857**.

187.s: Mubariz-ud-Daula, associated with the Wahabi conspiracy, was imprisoned in
187.x: Mubariz-ud-Daula, a Wahabi leader, was imprisoned in Golconda Fort in 1839.
187.tq: Link the leader with the specific place of imprisonment rather than with the later Residency episode.
xs: **Mubariz-ud-Daula** was imprisoned in **Golconda Fort** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Toopran** is where **Turrebaz Khan** was shot (**1859**); **Kanpur** is where **Peshwa Rao** was caught (**1862**).
xa: He was the **Nizam's brother** and organised the **Wahabi Movement (1839)** — **anti-British** (PYQ **2011**).
The **Wahabi conspiracy of 1839** is a background grievance of 1857.

187.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with a 1857-era rising in Hyderabad State?
187.x: Ramji Gond was associated with the Adilabad rising. Rangarao Pagi belonged to Nanded, Rohilla to Nirmal, and Bapurao with Venkatarao to Chanda.
187.tq: Start with the sure regional association and eliminate leaders assigned to neighbouring risings.
xs: **Adilabad — Ramji Gond** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Ajanta** — **Bhils**; **Rangarao Pagi** — **Nanded**; **Bapurao** — **Chanda**; **Rohilla** — **Nirmal**.
xa: **Sholapur** — **Raja Venkatappa Naik**.
Chanda's leaders: **Bapurao** and **Venkatarao**.

187.s: The rising led by Mir Fida Ali in June 1857 was suppressed by
187.x: Mir Fida Ali's rising at Aurangabad in June 1857 was suppressed by Captain Abbat, and Mir Fida Ali was hanged.
187.tq: Distinguish the suppressing officer from commanders connected with other revolts.
xs: **Mir Fida Ali**'s Aurangabad rising (**June 1857**) was put down by **Capt. Abbat** (Abbot) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Capt. Wilson** suppressed **Dandasena**; **Col. Pendergast** fought at **Padmanabham** (**1794**).
xa: Fida Ali was **hanged**.
His associate was **Amir Khan**; the **1st Cavalry** was disarmed.
