187.s: The Wahabi Movement referred to in the context of anti-British resistance was organised in 1839 by:
187.x: The Wahabi Movement of 1839 was organised by Mubariz-ud-Daula, the brother of the Nizam, and was anti-British.
187.tq: Test the organiser of the movement while using nearby historical figures as traps.
xs: The **Wahabi Movement (1839)** was organised by **Mubariz-ud-Daula**, the Nizam's brother — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Munro** suppressed the **palegars**; **Velu Thampi** led **Travancore**; **Bentinck** was recalled after **Vellore**.
xa: It was **anti-British** (PYQ **2011**).
He was imprisoned in **Golconda Fort** — first item in the APPSC G1 **2023** chronology.

187.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Leader)
a. Dandasena
b. Korukonda Subba Reddy
c. Turrebaz Khan
 d. Mubariz-ud-Daula

List-II (Place or event)
i. Imprisoned in Golconda Fort
ii. Rebellion at Errannagudem
iii. Attack on the British Residency
iv. Rising at Paralakimidi

Codes:
187.x: Dandasena rose at Paralakimidi, Korukonda Subba Reddy led the rebellion at Errannagudem, Turrebaz Khan attacked the British Residency, and Mubariz-ud-Daula was imprisoned in Golconda Fort.
187.tq: Start from the sure leader–place pairs and eliminate codes containing a swapped association.
xs: Correct code: **a–iv, b–ii, c–iii, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Dandasena** — **Paralakimidi**; **Korukonda Subba Reddy** — **Errannagudem**.
**Turrebaz Khan** — **Residency attack**; **Mubariz-ud-Daula** — **Golconda Fort**.
xa: Dandasena's rising: **9 Aug 1857**, Savara tribals, ban on forest produce.
Subba Reddy acted on rumours of **Nana Saheb**'s army.

187.s: Who among the following was associated with the suppression of the uprising at Paralakimidi in the Ganjam region during the Revolt of 1857?
187.x: Captain Wilson suppressed the uprising led by Radhakrishna Dandasena at Paralakimidi and Dandasena was subsequently hanged.
187.tq: Match the person with the deed rather than with a nearby military name.
xs: **Capt. Wilson** (Wilson Nolt) suppressed **Dandasena**'s rising at **Paralakimidi** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**George Russell** was **special officer over the forts** after **Padmanabham**; **Capt. Abbat** suppressed **Aurangabad**.
xa: Dandasena was **hanged**.
Paralakimidi lies in **Ganjam** (now **Gajapati, Odisha**).

187.s: Radhakrishna Dandasena led a revolt in which of the following places during 1857?
187.x: Radhakrishna Dandasena led the Girijan revolt at Paralakimidi in Ganjam, now in Gajapati district of Odisha.
187.tq: Use the area-of-operation clue to distinguish similarly placed Andhra and South Indian leaders.
xs: **Radhakrishna Dandasena** led the revolt at **Paralakimidi** in **Ganjam** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Errannagudem** was **Subba Reddy**'s; **Cuddapah** was **Sheikh Peer Sahib**'s; **Aurangabad** was **Mir Fida Ali**'s.
xa: It was a **Girijan** revolt of **Savara** tribals against a **ban on forest produce**.
Date: **9 Aug 1857**; suppressed by **Capt. Wilson**; Dandasena **hanged**.

187.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Korukonda Subba Reddy:
1. He operated in Errannagudem in the Godavari Agency.
2. His rising was influenced by rumours about Nana Saheb's army.
3. He was released after being arrested by the British.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
187.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Subba Reddy was captured and executed, not released.
187.tq: Find the single false outcome statement among otherwise related facts.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: he operated at **Errannagudem**, **Godavari Agency**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: he acted on **rumours that Nana Saheb was coming** and would reward participants.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: he was **captured and hanged** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: He was village official of **Karaturu**; informer: **Musset Sunkaraswamy** of Buttayigudem.
His movement: **1857-58**, "in the spirit of **Nana Saheb**".

187.s: Who assisted the British in putting down the rising led by Korukonda Subba Reddy?
187.x: Buttaigudem Munsab Shankar Swamy helped the British suppress Korukonda Subba Reddy's rising in the Godavari Agency.
187.tq: Test the local collaborator associated with a particular uprising.
xs: **Buttaigudem Munsab Shankar Swamy** helped put down **Subba Reddy**'s rising — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Capt. Wilson** suppressed **Dandasena**; **George Russell** belongs to **Vizianagaram** (**1794**).
xa: Other notes name the informer **Musset Sunkaraswamy** of Buttayigudem.
Subba Reddy was **hanged** → the movement ended.

187.s: On 28 August 1857, Sheikh Peer Sahib of Cuddapah was reported to have
o: attacked the British Residency at Hyderabad
preached jihad and prayed for the success of the Mughal Emperor
raised a green flag at Machilipatnam
187.x: Sheikh Peer Sahib preached jihad at Cuddapah on 28 August 1857 and prayed for the success of the Mughal Emperor; he was later arrested.
187.tq: Combine the date with the precise action to separate closely related 1857 incidents.
xs: On **28 Aug 1857** **Sheikh Peer Sahib** of **Kadapa** **preached jihad** and **prayed for the Mughal Emperor's success** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Jaggayyapeta** — treasury looted; **Machilipatnam** — green flag; **Hyderabad Residency** — Turrebaz Khan.
xa: He was **arrested**.
A **2024** A/R on his jihad was keyed "**both true, R not the explanation**".

187.s: Which of the following statements regarding incidents in the Andhra region during the Revolt of 1857 is correct?
o: A Telugu placard at Visakhapatnam called for renaming the town Mohammed Pattanam.
The treasury at Jaggayyapeta was used to store weapons for the Company.
A green flag was raised at Machilipatnam in support of the British Crown.
The unrest was confined to Visakhapatnam and did not spread to Narsipatnam.
187.x: A Telugu placard displayed at Visakhapatnam during Muharram called for renaming the town Mohammed Pattanam. The Jaggayyapeta treasury was looted, and unrest also spread to Narsipatnam.
187.tq: Reject reversed or exaggerated descriptions of separate local incidents.
xs: At **Visakhapatnam** a **Telugu placard** at **Muharram** urged renaming the town **Mohammed Pattanam** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Jaggayyapeta** treasury was **looted**; the **Machilipatnam** green flag came with prayers for the **Mughal Emperor**.
Unrest also spread to **Narsipatnam**.
xa: Loyalty meetings were held at **Visakhapatnam**, **Rajahmundry**, **Vijayawada**.
**Kadiri** (Rayalaseema) saw an attempt to incite rebellion (APPSC G2 **2008**).

187.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Faujdari Adalat — Centre of the Godavari Agency movement
Korukonda Subba Reddy — Leader in the Godavari Agency
187.x: The Faujdari Adalat was the court that tried the Uyyalawada rebel leader; it was not the centre of the Godavari Agency movement. Errannagudem was the centre, and Musset Sunkaraswamy was the informer.
187.tq: Find the institution that belongs to the judicial episode rather than the regional movement.
xs: **Faujdari Adalat** was the court that tried **Uyyalawada** (**1847**), not a centre of the Godavari movement — so option **(3)** is the mismatch.
**Errannagudem** — centre; **Musset Sunkaraswamy** — informer; **Korukonda Subba Reddy** — leader: all correct.
xa: Subba Reddy was village official of **Karaturu**.
Motive: **rumours that Nana Saheb was coming**.

187.s: Korukonda Subba Reddy, leader of the Godavari Agency movement, was a village official of which place?
187.x: Korukonda Subba Reddy was the village official of Karaturu in Godavari district. Errannagudem was the centre of his movement.
187.tq: Distinguish the leader's official village from the movement's centre.
xs: **Korukonda Subba Reddy** was village official of **Karaturu**, Godavari district — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Errannagudem** was his movement's **centre**; **Buttayigudem** was the informer's home; **Nosam** is linked to **Uyyalawada**.
xa: He was **hanged** → movement ended.
It lasted **1857-58** in the **Godavari Agency**.

187.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the limited response in Andhra:
1. Public meetings expressing loyalty were held at Visakhapatnam, Rajahmundry and Vijayawada.
2. Many people preferred the stability of Company rule to the earlier anarchy.
3. Andhra had no local leaders capable of organising resistance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
187.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because local leaders and disturbances, including Turrebaz Khan, Korukonda Subba Reddy and Dandasena, did exist.
187.tq: Reject the absolute claim that the region had no local leaders while retaining the documented loyalty factors.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **loyalty meetings** at **Visakhapatnam**, **Rajahmundry**, **Vijayawada**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: people valued Company **stability** over the "**earlier anarchy**".
Statement 3 is **wrong**: **Turrebaz Khan**, **Subba Reddy**, **Dandasena** etc. existed — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Other reasons: **Nizam and Salar Jung loyal**; **zamindars gained** from the Permanent Settlement.
APPSC-G2 **2025** key: "no local leaders" = **false**.

187.s: Which of the following places was NOT mentioned as a venue of loyalty meetings in Andhra during the Revolt of 1857?
187.x: Loyalty meetings were held at Visakhapatnam, Rajahmundry and Vijayawada. Kadiri was associated with an attempt to incite rebellion in Rayalaseema, not with the listed loyalty meetings.
187.tq: Distinguish places linked with loyalty from a place associated with an attempted rebellion.
xs: **Kadiri** saw an **attempt to incite rebellion** (APPSC G2 **2008**), not a loyalty meeting — so option **(4)** is the answer.
Loyalty meetings: **Visakhapatnam**, **Rajahmundry**, **Vijayawada**.
xa: Kadiri lies in **Rayalaseema**.
Andhra saw only **scattered disturbances** and stayed **loyal**.

187.s: Which of the following sets contains the principal background grievances connected with discontent in Hyderabad State and Andhra before or during 1857?
o: The 1794 battle, the 1846–47 rising and the 1879 Rampa rebellion only
The Permanent Settlement, the Star of India and the restoration of Dharaseo
The 1800 cession, the 1839 Wahabi conspiracy and the 1853 Berar treaty
The 1857 Residency attack, the 1862 conspiracy and the 1801 hanging only
187.x: The major background grievances identified were the 1800 cession, the Wahabi conspiracy of 1839 and the 1853 Berar treaty, involving Berar, Raichur and Osmanabad/Dharashiv.
187.tq: Group the underlying grievances together rather than confusing them with later events or rewards.
xs: Background grievances: the **1800 cession**, the **Wahabi conspiracy of 1839** and the **1853 Berar treaty** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The Berar treaty took **Berar**, **Raichur**, **Osmanabad/Dharashiv**.
xa: After 1857 **Raichur Doab** and **Dharashiv** were **restored** to Hyderabad.
The **1800** cession covered **Cuddapah, Kurnool, Anantapur, Bellary**.

187.s:
Assertion (A): The response to the Revolt of 1857 in Andhra was limited and scattered.
Reason (R): Afzal-ud-Daula and Salar Jung I remained pro-British.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
187.x: Both statements are true, and the pro-British position of the Nizam and his Diwan was an important reason why the revolt did not spread widely in Andhra.
187.tq: Test whether the political alignment stated in the Reason directly accounts for the limited regional response.
xs: **Both A and R are true** and R is the **correct explanation** of A — option **(1)**.
A: Andhra saw only **scattered disturbances** and stayed **loyal**.
R: **Afzal-ud-Daula** and **Salar Jung I** were **pro-British**, and the notes list "**Nizam and Salar Jung loyal**" as a reason for loyalty.
xa: Other reasons: **Madras Presidency quiet**; **zamindars gained** from the Permanent Settlement.
⚠ Contrast the **2025** A/R: "no local leaders" as A is **false**.

187.s:
Assertion (A): Andhra was unaffected by the Revolt of 1857 because it had no local leaders.
Reason (R): Nizam Afzal-ud-Daula remained pro-British during the revolt.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
187.x: A is false: Andhra did have local leaders and risings, such as Turrebaz Khan, Korukonda Subba Reddy, Dandasena and the attempt at Kadiri. R is true: Afzal-ud-Daula stayed pro-British. So D (the APPSC G2 2025 key). A and B treat A as true, and C wrongly calls R false.
187.tq: 'No local leaders' is the trap: false.
xs: A is **false**, R is **true** — option **(4)** (APPSC-G2 **2025** key).
A is false: **Turrebaz Khan**, **Subba Reddy**, **Dandasena** and the **Kadiri** attempt existed.
R is true: **Afzal-ud-Daula** stayed **pro-British**.
xa: He received the "**Star of India**".
Andhra stayed loyal partly because people valued Company **stability**.

187.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the repression of the movements?
o: Subba Reddy, Dandasena and Fida Ali — Hanged
Sheikh Peer Sahib — Awarded the Star of India
Salar Jung — Executed after a mock trial
Afzal-ud-Daula — Arrested as the chief rebel
187.x: Subba Reddy, Dandasena and Fida Ali were hanged. Sheikh Peer Sahib was arrested, while Afzal-ud-Daula and Salar Jung were associated with rewards or honours.
187.tq: Use the difference between execution, arrest and loyalist honours.
xs: **Subba Reddy**, **Dandasena** and **Fida Ali** were **hanged** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Sheikh Peer Sahib** was **arrested**; **Afzal-ud-Daula** got the **Star of India**; **Salar Jung** was **honoured**.
xa: Across India, **thousands executed after mock trials**.
**Allauddin** was transported to the **Andamans**; **Turrebaz Khan** shot near **Toopran**.

187.s: Which loyalist received the Star of India after the revolt?
187.x: Afzal-ud-Daula received the Star of India, while Salar Jung was honoured separately.
187.tq: Distinguish the named award from the general statement of honour.
xs: **Afzal-ud-Daula** received the "**Star of India**" — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Salar Jung** (Mir Turab Ali Khan) was **honoured** separately; **Fida Ali** and **Dandasena** were **hanged**.
xa: Hyderabad also got **Raichur Doab** and **Dharashiv** back; its **debt written off**.
Afzal-ud-Daula ruled **1857-69**.

187.s: Which of the following was a territorial and financial concession associated with the rewards to loyalists?
o: Godavari district was transferred to the Nizam and the High Court was abolished.
The Circars were restored to Bobbili and all pensions were cancelled.
The Raichur Doab and Dharashiv were restored to Hyderabad and its debt was written off.
Kurnool was transferred to France and Madras debt was increased.
187.x: The Raichur Doab and Dharashiv were restored to Hyderabad, and Hyderabad's debt was written off.
187.tq: Identify the combined territorial and financial concession without reversing the beneficiary.
xs: **Raichur Doab** and **Dharashiv** (Dharaseo, Osmanabad) were **restored to Hyderabad** and its **debt written off** — so option **(3)** is correct.
These areas had been lost under the **1853 Berar treaty**.
xa: **Afzal-ud-Daula** received the **Star of India**.
**Salar Jung** was honoured.

187.s: Which of the following was NOT included among the assurances of the Queen's Proclamation of 1 November 1858?
187.x: The Proclamation promised no further annexations, respect for Indian religions and protection for zamindars and princes. It did not provide for compulsory conversion.
187.tq: Find the extreme and contradictory option among the stated assurances.
xs: **Compulsory conversion to Christianity** was **not** promised — so option **(3)** is the answer.
Promised: **no further annexations**, **respect for Indian religions**, **protection for zamindars and princes**.
xa: Then **IPC 1860**, **CrPC 1861**, **Madras High Court 1862**.

187.s:
Arrange the following developments in the Madras Presidency in chronological order:
A. The Madras High Court replaced the Company courts.
B. The Indian Penal Code came into force.
C. The Code of Criminal Procedure was introduced.
D. The Queen's Proclamation was issued.
187.x: The Queen's Proclamation was issued in 1858, the IPC arrived in 1860, the CrPC in 1861, and the Madras High Court replaced Company courts in 1862.
187.tq: Arrange the items by their stated years: 1858, 1860, 1861 and 1862.
xs: Order **D, B, C, A** — option **(1)**.
**Queen's Proclamation** (**1 Nov 1858**) → **IPC** (**1860**) → **CrPC** (**1861**) → **Madras High Court** (**1862**).
xa: The High Court replaced the **Company courts** in the Madras Presidency.
The army was recast on the "**martial races**" theory.

187.s: The reorganisation of the British Indian Army after 1857 was based on which theory?
187.x: After the revolt, the Army was recast on the 'martial races' theory.
187.tq: Identify the exact administrative theory rather than a related imperial policy.
xs: The army was recast on the "**martial races**" theory — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Subsidiary alliance** and **paramountcy** concern the princes, not army recruitment.
xa: Other Crown-rule changes in Madras: **Madras High Court** (**1862**), **IPC 1860**, **CrPC 1861**.
The **Queen's Proclamation** (**1 Nov 1858**) promised no further annexations.

187.s:
Arrange the following agency disturbances in chronological order:
A. Vizianagaram–Visakhapatnam hill unrest
B. Korra Mallayya and Chinna Bhupathi's movement
C. Korukonda Subba Reddy's movement
D. Rampa rebellion led by Tammandora
187.x: The correct order is Vizianagaram–Visakhapatnam hill unrest in the 1830s, Korra Mallayya and Chinna Bhupathi in 1845–48, Korukonda Subba Reddy in 1857–58, and the Rampa rebellion in 1879.
187.tq: Fix the first and last events, then arrange the two middle movements by year.
xs: Order **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**Vizianagaram-Visakhapatnam hill unrest** (**1830s**) → **Korra Mallayya / Chinna Bhupathi** (**1845-48**).
**Korukonda Subba Reddy** (**1857-58**) → **Rampa**, **Tammandora** (**1879**).
xa: Later: **Alluri Sitarama Raju**'s Rampa rebellion, **1922-24**.
**Koya** rebellions also in the **1840s**, **1860s** and **1879**.

187.s: The Vizianagaram–Visakhapatnam hill unrest of the 1830s was directed against:
o: The imprisonment of local rulers in Golconda
187.x: The hill unrest of the 1830s was directed against zamindari exactions and led to the establishment of the Agency system.
187.tq: Link the specific grievance with the correct phase of agency unrest.
xs: The **1830s** hill unrest was against **zamindari exactions** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It led to the **Agency system** (CDI).
**Caste marks** and **dress regulations** belong to **Vellore** (**1806**).
xa: Next phase: **Korra Mallayya / Chinna Bhupathi** (**1845-48**) against **plains moneylenders**.
⚠ The Agency system did **not** come from **Rampa 1879**.

187.s:
Consider the following statements about the Rampa rebellion of 1879:
1. It led to the creation of the Agency system.
2. It was a Koya uprising in the East Godavari Agency.
3. It was directed against forest and toddy restrictions affecting podu cultivation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
187.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the Agency system came out of the 1830s Vizianagaram-Visakhapatnam hill unrest against zamindari exactions. The other two are correct: the 1879 rising was a Koya uprising in the East Godavari Agency against forest and toddy restrictions on podu cultivation. So '2 and 3 only' is right; every other option either includes statement 1 or leaves out a correct statement.
187.tq: 1830s hill unrest -> Agency system; 1879 Rampa -> Koyas, forest and toddy rules.
xs: Statement 1 is **wrong**: the **Agency system** came from the **1830s** hill unrest.
Statement 2 is **correct**: a **Koya uprising** in the **East Godavari Agency**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: against **forest and toddy restrictions** on **podu** cultivation — so **2 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Leader: **Tammandora**.
⚠ CDI wrongly names **Alluri** for **1879**.

187.s: Who led the Rampa rebellion of 1879?
187.x: The 1879 Rampa rebellion was led by Tammandora. Alluri Sitarama Raju led the later Rampa rebellion of 1922–24.
187.tq: Discriminate between two Rampa rebellions separated by several decades.
xs: The **1879** Rampa rebellion was led by **Tammandora** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Alluri Sitarama Raju** led the later Rampa rebellion of **1922-24**; **Korra Mallayya** — **1845-48**.
xa: ⚠ **Rampa 1879** = **Tammandora**; **Rampa 1922-24** = **Alluri**.
Exam angle: the year of the Rampa revolution is **1879**, not Alluri's **1922**.

187.s: Alluri Sitarama Raju fought a direct battle with the British at which place during his Rampa rebellion?
187.x: During the 1922–24 Rampa rebellion, Alluri Sitarama Raju fought the British directly at Panjerighat.
187.tq: Test the place associated with a specific episode of the later Rampa rebellion.
xs: **Alluri Sitarama Raju** fought the British directly at **Panjerighat** (PYQ **2012**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Rudravaram** and **Koilakuntla** belong to **Uyyalawada** (**1846**); **Errannagudem** to **Subba Reddy**.
xa: His rebellion: **1922-24**.
The earlier Rampa rebellion (**1879**) was **Tammandora**'s.

187.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gulugonda/Ganjam agency rising — Korra Mallayya and Chinna Bhupathi
187.x: The Rampa rebellion occurred in 1879, whereas Mubariz-ud-Daula was associated with the 1839 Wahabi conspiracy. Taranikallu, Gulugonda/Ganjam and Uyyalawada are correctly matched with the persons shown.
187.tq: Look for the swapped leader-event association among otherwise familiar regional rebellions.
xs: **Rampa — Mubariz-ud-Daula** is wrong — so option **(4)** is the mismatch.
**Rampa** (**1879**) was **Tammandora**'s; Mubariz-ud-Daula led the **Wahabi** conspiracy (**1839**).
**Uyyalawada** — Narasimha Reddy; **Taranikallu** — **Goudappa** (**1801**); **Gulugonda/Ganjam** — **Korra Mallayya**, **Chinna Bhupathi**: correct.
xa: **Rekapalle** rebellion was also **1879**.
**1846-47**: Uyyalawada.

187.s: The Gulugonda/Ganjam Agency rising of 1845–48 was associated with
187.x: Korra Mallayya and Chinna Bhupathi were associated with the Gulugonda/Ganjam Agency rising of 1845–48.
187.tq: Match the regional rising with its local leaders while eliminating names from other Hyderabad risings.
xs: The **Gulugonda/Ganjam** agency rising (**1845-48**) was led by **Korra Mallayya** and **Chinna Bhupathi** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was against **plains moneylenders** (CDX).
xa: **Venkatappa Naik** — **Sholapur**; **Rohilla** — **Nirmal**; **Ramji Gond** — **Adilabad**.
**Peshwa Rao** — **1862** conspiracy, caught at **Kanpur**.

187.s: Which of the following events occurred in 1853?
o: The Residency at Hyderabad was attacked.
187.x: Opposition to the Berar assignment occurred in 1853. The Residency attack was in 1857, the Rampa rebellion in 1879, and Mubariz-ud-Daula's imprisonment in 1839.
187.tq: Use the year-event pair and reject events belonging to nearby but different dates.
xs: In **1853** the **Berar assignment** was **opposed** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Mubariz-ud-Daula** — **1839**; **Rampa** — **1879**; **Residency attack** — **1857**.
xa: The **1853 Berar treaty** covered **Berar**, **Raichur**, **Osmanabad/Dharashiv**.
It is listed among the **background grievances** of 1857.

187.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with an event of 1857 in the Hyderabad State or Andhra region?
187.x: The Dandasena disturbance occurred on 9 August 1857. The Residency attack was on 17 July, and the Peer Saheb episode at Kadapa was on 28 August.
187.tq: Separate the closely spaced dates of the 1857 regional disturbances.
xs: **Dandasena — 9 August** is correct — option **(2)**.
**Residency attack** — **17 July**; **Peer Saheb**, Kadapa — **28 Aug**; **Aurangabad** — **June**.
xa: **Korukonda Subba Reddy** — **Aug 1857**.
Dandasena's area: **Paralakimidi**, Ganjam.

187.s: Peshwa Rao, also referred to as Ramarao, was associated with the conspiracy of
187.x: Peshwa Rao, or Ramarao, was associated with the 1862 conspiracy and was caught at Kanpur.
187.tq: Match the person with the distinct year of the conspiracy, avoiding the more prominent 1857 events.
xs: **Peshwa Rao** (Ramarao) belongs to the **1862** conspiracy — so option **(3)** is correct.
He was **caught at Kanpur**.
xa: **1839** = Wahabi conspiracy; **1879** = **Rampa** and **Rekapalle**.
**1857** in Hyderabad: **Aurangabad** (June) and the **Residency attack** (**17 July**).

187.s: Which one of the following best explains the limited impact of the Revolt of 1857 in South India?
o: The British had withdrawn their forces from the Deccan before 1857
The rulers of all South Indian states openly supported the revolt
The revolts in South India were local and scattered, while the Nizam's loyalty kept the Deccan from joining the revolt
South India had already achieved complete independence from the East India Company
187.x: The revolts in South India were local and scattered. The Nizam's loyalty to the British also prevented the revolt from spreading across the Deccan.
187.tq: Identify the combined significance of two linked causes rather than selecting an absolute statement.
xs: South India's revolts were **local and scattered**, and the **Nizam's loyalty** kept the **Deccan** closed to 1857 — so option **(3)** is correct.
The British had not withdrawn, and southern rulers like the **Nizam** stayed **pro-British**.
xa: The revolt lacked **central leadership**, a **programme** and a **base in the south**.
It took the Company **50-60 years** to consolidate Andhra (coastal zamindars + Rayalaseema palegars).

187.s: The Vellore Mutiny of 1806 is significant because it was:
o: the first organised peasant revolt in coastal Andhra
the last major palegar rising in Rayalaseema
the first revolt led by the Nizam against the British
the first major sepoy mutiny in India, occurring half a century before 1857
187.x: The Vellore Mutiny of 1806 is regarded as the first major sepoy mutiny and occurred about fifty years before the Revolt of 1857.
187.tq: Distinguish the first major sepoy mutiny from later regional and peasant uprisings.
xs: **Vellore 1806** was the **first big sepoy mutiny**, half a century before **1857** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **last major palegar rising** in Rayalaseema was **Uyyalawada** (**1846**).
xa: Causes: new **dress/uniform regulations**; **Tipu's family** in the fort.
Madras Governor **William Bentinck** and C-in-C **Cradock** were recalled.

187.s: Ranga Rao and Tandra Paparayudu are remembered in Andhra history primarily as symbols of:
187.x: Ranga Rao and Tandra Paparayudu of Bobbili remain enduring symbols of Telugu valour.
187.tq: Match the historical personalities with the regional cultural significance attached to them.
xs: **Ranga Rao** and **Tandra Paparayudu** remain symbols of **Telugu valour**, from **Bobbili** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Bobbili (**24 January 1757**): Ranga Rao killed defending it; Paparayudu later killed **Vijayarama Raju**.
xa: The attackers were **Vizianagaram** + the **French (Bussy)**.
Primary source: the play **Bobbili Yuddham**.

187.s:
Consider the following statements about the palegar risings in Rayalaseema:
1. The 1800–01 rising involved about 80 palegars.
2. Thomas Munro was associated with the suppression of the 1800–01 rising.
3. The 1846 rising was a single-leader guerrilla revolt with a peasant and tribal base.
4. The 1846 rising was the last major palegar rising in Rayalaseema, about a decade before 1857.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
187.x: All four statements are correct. The 1800–01 movement involved about 80 palegars and Munro, whereas the 1846 movement was a single-leader guerrilla revolt supported by peasants and tribal groups and was the last major palegar rising before 1857.
187.tq: Compare the two risings across leadership, scale, social base and chronology.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are **correct**: the **1800-01** rising involved about **80 palegars**, suppressed by **Thomas Munro**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: **1846** was a **single-leader guerrilla revolt** with a **peasant and tribal base**.
Statement 4 is **correct**: it was the **last major palegar rising** in Rayalaseema, a decade before **1857** — so **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(1)**.
xa: The 1846 leader was **Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy**, with about **5,000 followers**.
Munro's suppression took **18 months** and ended in **Ryotwari** for the Ceded Districts.
In **1801** **Mutakuri Goudappa** attacked the Sub-Collector's office at **Taranikallu**.

187.s: Uyyalawada, associated with the Andhra resistance tradition, is presently located in:
187.x: After the 2022 district reorganisation, Uyyalawada is in Nandyal district.
187.tq: Apply the post-reorganisation district boundary rather than an older regional association.
xs: **Uyyalawada** is now in **Nandyal district**, after the **2022** reorganisation — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was earlier in **Koilakuntla taluk**, **Kurnool district**.
xa: PYQ **2022**: "born in **Kurnool** district" is correct.
**Orvakal airport** (Kurnool) was renamed **Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy Airport**.
**Bobbili** is linked with **Ranga Rao** and **Tandra Paparayudu**, symbols of Telugu valour.

187.s: The Revolt of 1857 was criticised for lacking:
o: central leadership, a programme and a base in South India
a military dimension, regional causes and opposition to British rule
support from the Deccan, a programme and any local centres
popular participation, military resistance and regional leaders
187.x: A major criticism of the revolt was that it lacked central leadership, a coherent programme and a substantial base in the south.
187.tq: Find the precise combination of shortcomings rather than an option using sweeping exaggeration.
xs: The revolt lacked **central leadership**, a **programme** and a **base in the south** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It did have military resistance, popular participation and local leaders, so options 2 and 4 fail.
xa: South India's revolts were **local and scattered**; the **Nizam's loyalty** kept the **Deccan** closed to 1857.
Andhra leaders who did rise: **Turrebaz Khan**, **Korukonda Subba Reddy**, **Dandasena**.
APPSC-G2 **2025**: "Andhra had **no local leaders**" = **false**.

188.s:
Consider the following statements about Raja Rammohan Roy:
1. He lived from 1772 to 1833.
2. He knew Persian, Arabic, Sanskrit and English.
3. He died at Bristol.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
188.x: All three statements are correct. Rammohan Roy lived from 1772 to 1833, knew the four languages mentioned and died at Bristol in 1833.
188.tq: Confirm each biographical statement independently before selecting the combined option.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: Rammohan Roy lived **1772-1833**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: he knew **Persian, Arabic, Sanskrit, English**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: he died at **Bristol**, **1833** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: He was influenced by **Vedanta** and **Western rationalism**.
Titles: "**Father of Modern India**", "**Father of the Indian Renaissance**", first "**Modern Man of India**".
He left for England in **1830** as envoy of **Akbar II**.

188.s: Raja Rammohan Roy’s journey to England is generally placed in which year in the commonly used account?
188.x: Rammohan Roy left for England in 1830; some accounts associate the mission and title with 1831, but the commonly cited departure year is 1830.
188.tq: Distinguish the departure year from the year of his death and from the closely associated 1831 reference.
xs: Rammohan Roy left for England in **1830** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Some notes date the trip and title to **1831**; **1833** is the year he **died at Bristol**; **1828** is the **Brahmo Sabha**.
xa: He went as envoy of Mughal emperor **Akbar II**, who gave him the title "**Raja**".
He was among the first Indians to go abroad on such a mission.

188.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the title and mission associated with Rammohan Roy?
o: Akbar II conferred the title ‘Raja’ and sent him to England as his envoy.
William Bentinck conferred the title ‘Raja’ and sent him to England as his envoy.
Keshab Chandra Sen conferred the title ‘Raja’ and sent him to England as his envoy.
Debendranath Tagore conferred the title ‘Raja’ and sent him to England as his envoy.
188.x: Mughal emperor Akbar II conferred the title ‘Raja’ on Rammohan Roy and sent him to England as his envoy.
188.tq: Ask who would perform the act, using the authority-and-person trap.
xs: Mughal emperor **Akbar II** conferred the title "**Raja**" and sent him to England as his **envoy** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Bentinck** was the GG who abolished **Sati** (**1829**); **Debendranath** and **Keshab** were later Brahmo leaders.
xa: He left in **1830** and died at **Bristol**, **1833**.
⚠ "**Maharishi**" is **Debendranath Tagore**'s title, not Roy's.

188.s: Which one of the following titles is NOT associated with Raja Rammohan Roy?
188.x: Rammohan Roy is called the Father of Modern India, the Father of the Indian (or Bengal) Renaissance and the first Modern Man of India. 'Maharishi' was the title of Debendranath Tagore. 'Raja' was given to Rammohan Roy by Akbar II.
188.tq: Maharishi = Debendranath, not Rammohan.
xs: "**Maharishi**" is **Debendranath Tagore**'s title — so option **(4)** is the answer.
Roy is "**Father of Modern India**", "**Father of the Indian Renaissance**" and the first "**Modern Man of India**".
xa: Also called **Father of Bengal Renaissance** and **Harbinger** of the modern Indian Renaissance.
Title → person: **Lokahitawadi** — **Gopal Hari Deshmukh** (PYQ **2021**).
"Raja" was given by **Akbar II**.

188.s: Which one of the following statements about Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin is correct?
o: It was an English work defending idolatry.
It was a Persian work written against idolatry.
It was a Bengali journal dealing with social reform.
It was a Sanskrit work on the rituals of the Brahmo Samaj.
188.x: Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin, meaning A Gift to Monotheists, was a Persian book of Rammohan Roy written against idolatry.
188.tq: Combine the work’s exact title, language and theme to defeat look-alike book options.
xs: **Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin** (A Gift to Monotheists) was a **Persian** book **against idolatry** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was not English, Bengali or Sanskrit, and it attacked idolatry rather than defending it.
xa: ⚠ **Tuhfat** + **Mirat-ul-Akhbar** = Persian; **Sambad Kaumudi** = Bengali; **Precepts of Jesus** = English.

188.s: Rammohan Roy’s work titled Precepts of Jesus — the Guide to Peace and Happiness was written in:
188.x: Precepts of Jesus — the Guide to Peace and Happiness was written in English and presented a rational ethical interpretation of Jesus’s teachings.
188.tq: Discriminate among the languages associated with Rammohan Roy’s different books and journals.
xs: **Precepts of Jesus — the Guide to Peace and Happiness** was in **English** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It set out the **rational ethics of Jesus** (**1820**).
xa: **Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin** and **Mirat-ul-Akhbar** — **Persian**.
**Sambad Kaumudi** — **Bengali** weekly.

188.s: Which one of the following pairs relating to Raja Rammohan Roy's educational institutions is correctly matched?
188.x: Rammohan Roy started an English school in 1822, so A is right. Hindu College was 1817 and Vedanta College 1825 (the years in B and C are swapped), and the Atmiya Sabha dates from 1815, not 1822.
188.tq: Separate the closely spaced dates of the English school, Hindu College and Vedanta College.
xs: Roy's **English school** dates from **1822** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Hindu College** is **1817** and **Vedanta College** **1825** — options 2 and 3 swap them.
The **Atmiya Sabha** dates from **1815**, not 1822.
xa: Hindu College was co-founded with **David Hare**.
Vedanta College **blended Indian and Western learning**.

188.s:
Consider the following statements about Raja Rammohan Roy:
1. His Vedanta College (1825) blended Indian and Western learning.
2. He welcomed the Jury Act of 1827 because it removed religious discrimination from the courts.
3. The Calcutta Unitarian Association was linked to inter-faith dialogue.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
188.x: Statement 2 is wrong: he opposed the Jury Act of 1827 because it brought religious discrimination into the courts. The other two are correct: Vedanta College (1825) blended Indian and Western learning, and the Calcutta Unitarian Association served inter-faith dialogue. So '1 and 3 only' is right; every other option either includes statement 2 or leaves out a correct statement.
188.tq: Roy protested both the Jury Act 1827 and the 1823 press curbs.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Vedanta College** (**1825**) blended Indian and Western learning.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: he **opposed** the **Jury Act 1827**, which brought religious discrimination into the courts.
Statement 3 is **correct**: the **Calcutta Unitarian Association** served **inter-faith dialogue** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: He also protested the **1823 Press Ordinance**.
Hindu College: **1817**, with **David Hare**.

188.s:
Consider the following statements about Raja Rammohan Roy's public campaigns:
1. He protested the press curbs imposed through the Press Ordinance of 1823.
2. He demanded fixed maximum rents for peasants against Bengali zamindars.
3. He supported the continuation of the Company's exclusive trading rights.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
188.x: Rammohan Roy opposed press restrictions and advocated fixed maximum rents for peasants. He also sought an end to the Company's trading rights, so statement 3 is false.
188.tq: Find the statement that reverses the reformer's economic and political demands.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: he protested the **1823 Press Ordinance**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: he demanded **fixed maximum rents** for peasants against Bengali zamindars.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: he wanted the **end of the Company's trading rights** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Other demands: **lower export duties**, **Indianisation of the services**.
Campaigns: against **sati**, **child marriage**, **polygamy**; for **widow remarriage**, **women's property rights**.

188.s: Which one of the following pairs of a work by Rammohan Roy and its language is correctly matched?
188.x: Mirat-ul-Akhbar was a Persian weekly, so A is right. Sambad Kaumudi was a Bengali weekly, Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin was written in Persian, and Precepts of Jesus was written in English.
188.tq: Mirat = Persian; Kaumudi = Bengali.
xs: **Mirat-ul-Akhbar** was a **Persian** weekly — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Sambad Kaumudi** was **Bengali**; **Tuhfat** was **Persian**; **Precepts of Jesus** was **English**.
xa: Exam angle: journal-language matching.
**Tattvabodhini Patrika** (Debendranath's Sabha) was also **Bengali**.

188.s: Raja Rammohan Roy established the Atmiya Sabha at which place and in which year?
188.x: The Atmiya Sabha was established by Raja Rammohan Roy in Calcutta in 1815.
188.tq: Pair the institution with both its location and year to avoid confusion with later educational initiatives.
xs: The **Atmiya Sabha** was set up in **Calcutta**, **1815** — so option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ APP and LENS May **2026** say **1814**.
**Rajahmundry** is the Andhra **Prarthana Samaj** centre (**1878**); **1825** is **Vedanta College**.
xa: It was called the "**Society of Friends**".
It translated the **Upanishads/Vedanta** into Bengali and English.

188.s: The Brahmo Sabha, founded in Calcutta in 1828 and later renamed the Brahmo Samaj, was founded by:
188.x: Rammohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha in August 1828 with Dwarkanath Tagore (APPSC-GS 2018). It grew out of his Atmiya Sabha of 1815. Dayananda founded the Arya Samaj (1875). Ramakrishna was a mystic, not the founder of a Samaj, and Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission (1897).
188.tq: Brahmo Sabha = Rammohan, 1828.
xs: **Raja Rammohan Roy** founded the **Brahmo Sabha** (Calcutta, **1828**) — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-GS **2018**).
⚠ Not **Vivekananda**, **Dayananda** or **Ramakrishna**: Dayananda founded the **Arya Samaj** (**1875**).
xa: Co-founder: **Dwarkanath Tagore**.
APPSC-G1 **2008** offered **1826/1829/1834/1836** — the correct **1828** was missing (keyed "-").

188.s: Which one of the following was the principal objective of the Atmiya Sabha associated with Rammohan Roy?
o: Translation of the Upanishads and Vedanta into Bengali and English
Promotion of military education among Indians
Campaign for the exclusive use of Sanskrit in education
Organisation of peasant resistance in Bengal
188.x: The Atmiya Sabha, or Society of Friends, was associated with translating the Upanishads and Vedanta into Bengali and English.
188.tq: Identify the institution from its distinctive activity rather than from its founder alone.
xs: The **Atmiya Sabha** **translated the Upanishads and Vedanta into Bengali and English** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It had no military, Sanskrit-only or peasant agenda.
xa: Founded **Calcutta**, **1815** (some notes **1814**).
It was followed by the **Brahmo Sabha** (**1828**).

188.s: The Brahmo Sabha founded in Calcutta in 1828 was established by Rammohan Roy in association with:
188.x: Rammohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha in association with Dwarkanath Tagore in Calcutta in 1828.
188.tq: Use the founder-associate distinction to avoid confusing different Tagores connected with the movement.
xs: Roy founded the **Brahmo Sabha** (**1828**) with **Dwarkanath Tagore** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Radhakant Deb** founded the rival **Dharma Sabha** (**1830**); **Debendranath** renamed it the **Brahmo Samaj**.
xa: **Keshab Chandra Sen** founded the **Brahmo Samaj of India** in **1866**.
Founded in **August** (**20 Aug**).

188.s: The institution originally known as the Brahmo Sabha came to be known as the Brahmo Samaj after it was renamed by:
188.x: The Brahmo Sabha was later renamed the Brahmo Samaj by Maharishi Debendranath Tagore.
188.tq: Discriminate between the founder of an organisation and the later person associated with its renaming.
xs: **Maharishi Debendranath Tagore** renamed the Brahmo Sabha the **Brahmo Samaj** (CDI) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Dwarkanath Tagore** co-founded the Sabha; **Keshab** came later; **Radhakant Deb** opposed it.
xa: Debendranath **revived** the Samaj through the **Tattvabodhini Sabha** (**1839**).
Debendranath lived **1817-1905**.

188.s:
Which of the following statements correctly describes the religious position of the Brahmo Samaj?
1. It worshipped one formless and eternal God.
2. It treated a particular scripture as the final authority.
3. It rejected belief in avatars.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
188.x: The Brahmo Samaj believed in one formless, eternal God and rejected belief in avatars. It did not treat any scripture as the final authority.
188.tq: Locate the false statement by testing the absolute claim about scriptural authority.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: worship of **one formless, eternal God**.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: **no scripture** was treated as final authority.
Statement 3 is **correct**: **no belief in avatars** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: It drew on the **Upanishads, Bible and Koran**.
A theistic (**Astika**) reform within Hinduism, not a new religion.

188.s:
Consider the following statements about Brahmo religious practice:
1. Idols and animal sacrifice were banned in its halls.
2. Priestly ritualism and caste distinctions were rejected.
3. Collective prayer formed part of its practice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
188.x: The Brahmo Samaj opposed idols, animal sacrifice, priestly ritualism and caste distinctions, and encouraged collective prayer.
188.tq: Recognise a cluster of related reform principles and test whether any statement reverses them.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **idols, animal sacrifice and sectarian symbols** were banned.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **priestly ritualism** and **caste distinctions** were rejected.
Statement 3 is **correct**: **collective prayer** was practised — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: It held **no heaven or hell**.
**Jivatma** and **Paramatma** are not one.

188.s: Which one of the following statements about the Brahmo Samaj is INCORRECT?
o: It drew rational teachings from the Upanishads, Bible and Koran.
It distinguished the individual soul from the Supreme Soul.
It accepted sectarian symbols as essential to worship.
It was a theistic reform movement within Hinduism.
188.x: The Brahmo Samaj rejected sectarian symbols in its halls. It was a theistic reform within Hinduism, drew on the Upanishads, Bible and Koran, and distinguished Jivatma from Paramatma.
188.tq: Spot the statement that reverses the movement's opposition to sectarian ritual.
xs: The Samaj **banned sectarian symbols** in its halls — so option **(3)** is the incorrect statement.
It did draw on the **Upanishads, Bible and Koran**, separated **Jivatma** from **Paramatma**, and was a **theistic** reform within Hinduism.
xa: It also banned **idols** and **animal sacrifice**.
No scripture was final; **no avatars**.

188.s: Which of the following social reform measures was NOT associated with the programme of the Brahmo Samaj?
188.x: The Brahmo Samaj opposed polygamy and child marriage and supported widow remarriage, women's education and women's property rights.
188.tq: Use the reform movement's social programme to identify the reversed position.
xs: The Samaj **opposed polygamy** — so "defence of polygamy" (option **(3)**) is the answer.
It stood for **widow remarriage**, **women's education** and **property rights**.
xa: It was also against **child marriage**, **female infanticide** and **caste**.
Brahmo Samaj = **reformist** (reason), unlike the revivalist **Arya Samaj**.

188.s:
With reference to Raja Rammohan Roy, consider the following statements:
1. He respected the traditional philosophies of the East.
2. He wanted Indians to adopt a rational and scientific approach.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
188.x: Both are correct (UPSC 2025 key). He drew on the Upanishads and Vedanta and also stood for a rational, scientific approach. A and B leave out one true statement, and D rejects both.
188.tq: Rammohan combined Eastern philosophy with Western rationalism.
xs: **Both 1 and 2** are correct — option **(3)** (UPSC **2025** key).
He **respected the traditional philosophies** of the East (Upanishads, Vedanta) **and** wanted a **rational, scientific approach**.
xa: Influences: **Vedanta** + **Western rationalism**.
His **Vedanta College** (**1825**) blended Indian and Western learning.

188.s: The Bengal Sati Regulation of 1829 was issued as which Regulation of the Bengal Code?
188.x: The Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829, was Regulation XVII of the Bengal Code. It declared Sati illegal and punishable.
188.tq: Use the exact-number trap by distinguishing the regulation number from nearby legal provisions.
xs: The **Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829** was **Regulation XVII** of the Bengal Code — so option **(3)** is correct.
It declared Sati **illegal and punishable**.
xa: Passed **4 December 1829** under **Lord William Bentinck**.
Exam angle: "Sati was abolished by ..." — **Bentinck**; regulation number **XVII**.

188.s:
Consider the following statements about the Bengal Sati Regulation:
1. It was passed on 4 December 1829.
2. It was extended to the Madras and Bombay Presidencies in 1830.
3. It was passed under Governor-General Lord Minto.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
188.x: Statement 3 is wrong: it was passed under Lord William Bentinck. The other two are correct: it was passed on 4 December 1829 and extended to Madras and Bombay in 1830. So '1 and 2 only' is right; every other option either includes statement 3 or leaves out a correct statement.
188.tq: Sati: Bentinck, Regulation XVII, 1829; Madras and Bombay 1830.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: passed on **4 December 1829**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: extended to **Madras and Bombay** in **1830**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: it was under **Lord William Bentinck**, not Minto — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: not **Munro**, **Minto**, **Curzon**, **Hastings**, **Cornwallis** or **Shore** (APPSC-GS **2019**, **2025**).
**Rammohan Roy**'s long campaign made the ban possible.

188.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the abolition of Sati:
1. Rammohan Roy conducted a long campaign against the practice.
2. Raja Radhakant Deb supported the Sati ban through the Dharma Sabha.
3. The Dharma Sabha was founded in 1830.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
188.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Raja Radhakant Deb founded the orthodox Dharma Sabha in opposition to the Brahmo propaganda and the Sati ban, so statement 2 is false.
188.tq: Find the swapped stance: the orthodox organisation opposed, rather than supported, the reform.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Rammohan Roy** ran a long campaign against Sati.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: **Radhakant Deb** **opposed** the ban through the orthodox **Dharma Sabha**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: the **Dharma Sabha** was founded in **1830** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: The ban: **Regulation XVII**, **4 December 1829**, under **Bentinck**.
The Dharma Sabha opposed both **Brahmo propaganda** and the Sati ban.

188.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Debendranath Tagore — Tattvabodhini Sabha and Tattvabodhini Patrika
Keshab Chandra Sen — Dharma Sabha and Tattvabodhini Patrika
Radhakant Deb — Tattvabodhini Sabha and Brahmo Samaj of India
Dwarkanath Tagore — Deva Samaj and Tattvabodhini Patrika
188.x: Debendranath Tagore founded the Tattvabodhini Sabha in 1839, whose Bengali organ was the Tattvabodhini Patrika.
188.tq: Match the reformer with both the organisation and its publication rather than with a rival institution.
xs: **Debendranath Tagore** founded the **Tattvabodhini Sabha** (**1839**), whose Bengali organ was the **Tattvabodhini Patrika** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Dharma Sabha** — **Radhakant Deb**; **Brahmo Samaj of India** — **Keshab**; **Deva Samaj** — **Agnihotri**.
xa: Through it he **spread Rammohan's ideas** and **revived** the Samaj.
His title: "**Maharishi**".

188.s: Debendranath Tagore revived the Brahmo Samaj after Rammohan Roy’s death by stressing:
o: The restoration of Sati as a religious duty
Rejection of idolatry and rituals and worship of the formless God
188.x: Debendranath Tagore stressed rejection of idolatry and rituals and advocated worship of the formless God while reviving the Brahmo Samaj.
188.tq: Select the option that preserves the reform movement’s defining religious principle and reject the reversed alternatives.
xs: Debendranath stressed **rejection of idolatry and rituals** and **worship of the formless God** — so option **(4)** is correct.
He revived the Samaj through the **Tattvabodhini Sabha** after Rammohan's death.
xa: Tattvabodhini Sabha: **Calcutta**, **1839**.
He made **Keshab** acharya in **1862**.

188.s: The title ‘Maharishi’ is associated with:
188.x: Debendranath Tagore was known by the title ‘Maharishi’.
188.tq: Use the title-person association while distinguishing it from Rammohan Roy’s title ‘Raja’.
xs: "**Maharishi**" was **Debendranath Tagore**'s title (CDI) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Rammohan Roy**'s title was "**Raja**" (from **Akbar II**).
xa: Debendranath lived **1817-1905**.
His youngest son **Rabindranath Tagore** is remembered on his death anniversary (**10 Aug 2026**).

188.s: Keshab Chandra Sen was appointed Acharya of the Brahmo Samaj by Debendranath Tagore in which year?
188.x: Debendranath Tagore made Keshab Chandra Sen the Acharya, or minister, of the Brahmo Samaj in 1862. He was regarded as its first non-Brahmin Acharya.
188.tq: Use the precise year associated with an appointment rather than the later year of organisational split.
xs: **Debendranath** made **Keshab Chandra Sen** **acharya** (minister) in **1862** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was the **first non-Brahmin acharya**.
**1866** is the first split; **1870** the **Indian Reform Association**.
xa: Keshab lived **1838-1884**.
He took the Brahmo Samaj to **South India**.

188.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Native Marriage Act of 1872:
1. It is also known as the Brahmo Marriage Act.
2. It legalised inter-caste marriage.
3. It fixed minimum ages for marriage.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
188.x: The Native Marriage Act, also called the Brahmo Marriage Act or Act III of 1872, legalised inter-caste marriage and prescribed minimum marriage ages.
188.tq: Check whether all the statutory details belong to the same law before selecting the combined option.
xs: All three are **correct** — option **(4)**.
The **Native Marriage Act** is the **Brahmo Marriage Act** (**Act III of 1872**).
It **legalised inter-caste marriage** and **fixed minimum marriage ages**.
xa: It came from **Keshab Chandra Sen**'s efforts.
Ironically, Keshab's **under-age daughter**'s marriage to the **Cooch Behar** prince caused the **1878** split.

188.s: Keshab Chandra Sen's lectures in Bombay contributed to the emergence of which reform organisation?
188.x: Keshab Chandra Sen's lectures in Bombay inspired the formation of the Prarthana Samaj. He also helped carry Brahmo ideas to South India.
188.tq: Link the reformer's activity in a particular region with the organisation it inspired.
xs: **Keshab**'s **lectures in Bombay** inspired the **Prarthana Samaj** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Paramahansa Mandali** (**1849**) and **Tattvabodhini Sabha** (**1839**) came earlier; the **Sadharan Samaj** broke from Keshab.
xa: The Prarthana Samaj (**1867**) was founded by **Atmaram Pandurang**.
Keshab also took the Brahmo Samaj to **South India**.

188.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Keshab Chandra Sen became Acharya of the Brahmo Samaj
B. Brahmo Samaj of India was formed
C. Indian Reform Association was founded
D. Nava Vidhan was introduced
188.x: Keshab became Acharya in 1862, formed the Brahmo Samaj of India in 1866, founded the Indian Reform Association in 1870 and introduced Nava Vidhan in 1880–81.
188.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the intermediate organisational developments.
xs: Order **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**Acharya** (**1862**) → **Brahmo Samaj of India** (**1866**).
**Indian Reform Association** (**1870**) → **Nava Vidhan** (**1880-81**).
xa: The **Native Marriage Act** came in **1872**.
The **Sadharan Brahmo Samaj** broke away in **1878**.

188.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Brahmo Samaj of India — Keshab Chandra Sen
Sadharan Brahmo Samaj — Ananda Mohan Bose and Shivnath Shastri
188.x: Nava Vidhan, or New Dispensation, was associated with Keshab Chandra Sen and emerged in 1880–81. The other three pairings are correct.
188.tq: Find the swapped leader by distinguishing Keshab's Nava Vidhan from Debendranath's Adi Brahmo Samaj.
xs: **Nava Vidhan — Debendranath** is wrong: the **New Dispensation** (**1880**) was **Keshab's** — so option **(3)** is the mismatch.
**Brahmo Samaj of India** — Keshab; **Sadharan** — **Ananda Mohan Bose** and **Shivnath Shastri**; **Adi Brahmo Samaj** — Debendranath: correct.
xa: ⚠ Some notes wrongly credit Debendranath with the New Dispensation.
⚠ Some notes wrongly label Keshab's body "**Adi Dharm**".

188.s: The first major split of the Brahmo Samaj in 1866 resulted in which of the following combinations?
o: Debendranath Tagore — Brahmo Samaj of India; Keshab Chandra Sen — Adi Brahmo Samaj
Debendranath Tagore — Adi Brahmo Samaj; Keshab Chandra Sen — Brahmo Samaj of India
Ananda Mohan Bose — Adi Brahmo Samaj; Shivnath Shastri — Brahmo Samaj of India
Keshab Chandra Sen — Sadharan Brahmo Samaj; Debendranath Tagore — Nava Vidhan
188.x: After the 1866 split, Debendranath Tagore's body became the Adi Brahmo Samaj, while Keshab Chandra Sen led the Brahmo Samaj of India.
188.tq: Use the leader–body pairing to distinguish the first split from the later Sadharan split.
xs: The **1866** split: **Debendranath** — **Adi Brahmo Samaj**; **Keshab** — **Brahmo Samaj of India** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Cause: Keshab's **radicalism** — inter-caste marriage and eclectic, Christian-influenced worship.
xa: The **Adi Brahmo Samaj** was the **parent body**.
The second split (**1878**) produced the **Sadharan Brahmo Samaj**.

188.s: The Sadharan Brahmo Samaj was formed in 1878 primarily because of which development?
o: Debendranath Tagore's rejection of the Upanishads
The introduction of English education by Raja Rammohan Roy
Keshab Chandra Sen's marriage of his under-age daughter to the Cooch Behar prince
Keshab Chandra Sen's opposition to monotheism
188.x: The 1878 split followed Keshab Chandra Sen's marriage of his under-age daughter to the Maharaja or prince of Cooch Behar. The Sadharan Brahmo Samaj was associated with Ananda Mohan Bose and Shivnath Shastri.
188.tq: Identify the immediate cause of a split rather than confusing it with the ideology of the earlier split.
xs: The **1878** split followed **Keshab**'s **marriage of his under-age daughter** to the **Cooch Behar** prince — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Sadharan Brahmo Samaj** was led by **Ananda Mohan Bose** and **Shivnath Shastri**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes wrongly say it was founded "under **Debendranath**".
Keshab's own **Native Marriage Act** (**1872**) had fixed minimum marriage ages.

188.s: Prarthana Samaj was established in which year?
188.x: Prarthana Samaj was established in 1867. It became an important reformist organisation in Maharashtra.
188.tq: Use the numerical options to distinguish the founding year from nearby reform milestones.
xs: The **Prarthana Samaj** was founded in **1867** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**1873** = **Satyashodhak Samaj**; **1878** = Prarthana Samaj at **Rajahmundry**; **1887** = **National Social Conference**.
xa: Founder: **Atmaram Pandurang**; leaders **M.G. Ranade**, **R.G. Bhandarkar**.
It was inspired by **Keshab**'s Bombay lectures.

188.s: Which of the following reforms was NOT associated with the activities of the Prarthana Samaj?
o: Use of violent confrontation against orthodox groups
188.x: Prarthana Samaj promoted widow remarriage, women's education and inter-caste dining through persuasion rather than confrontation. Violent confrontation was not its method.
188.tq: Find the option that reverses the organisation's method of gradual persuasion.
xs: **Violent confrontation** was not its method — it used **persuasion** — so option **(2)** is the answer.
It worked for **widow remarriage**, **women's education** and **inter-caste dining**.
xa: Leaders: **M.G. Ranade**, **R.G. Bhandarkar**.
Brahmo + Prarthana Samaj = **reformist**; Arya Samaj, Deoband = **revivalist**.

188.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
188.x: Balshastri Jambhekar was associated with Darpan, Karsandas Mulji with Satya Prakash, and Gopal Hari Deshmukh was known as Lokahitawadi. Therefore, all the pairs are correctly matched.
188.tq: Start from a sure newspaper–reformer pair and verify the remaining associations.
xs: All three pairs are **correct** — **All of the above**, option **(4)**.
**Balshastri Jambhekar** — **Darpan**; **Karsandas Mulji** — **Satya Prakash**.
**Gopal Hari Deshmukh** — **Lokahitawadi** (PYQ **2021**).
xa: These are the **Bombay/Poona** press reformers.
APPSC-GS **2022** founder match: **Derozio** → Young Bengal; **Dayanand** → Arya Samaj.

188.s:
Consider the following statements about M.G. Ranade:
1. He was associated with the Widow Marriage Association and the Deccan Education Society.
2. He founded the National Social Conference in 1887 with Raghunath Rao.
3. The National Social Conference served as the political wing of the Prarthana Samaj.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
188.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the National Social Conference was the social wing of the Congress sessions. The other two are correct: Ranade was linked to the Widow Marriage Association and the Deccan Education Society, and founded the Conference in 1887 with Raghunath Rao. So '1 and 2 only' is right; every other option either includes statement 3 or leaves out a correct statement.
188.tq: National Social Conference = social wing of the Congress.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Ranade** — **Widow Marriage Association**, **Deccan Education Society**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **National Social Conference** (**1887**) with **Raghunath Rao**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: it was the **social wing of the Congress sessions** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Ranade was a leader of the **Prarthana Samaj** (**1867**).
Other leader: **R.G. Bhandarkar**.

188.s: The Arya Samaj worked mainly from which place after its foundation in Bombay in 1875?
188.x: Arya Samaj was founded by Dayananda Saraswati in Bombay in 1875 but worked mainly from Lahore. Its Shuddhi programme was a prominent feature of its activities.
188.tq: Use the movement's operational centre as a location-based discriminator.
xs: The **Arya Samaj** (**Dayananda Saraswati**, **1875**, **Bombay**) worked mainly from **Lahore** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Rajahmundry** was the Andhra **Prarthana Samaj** centre (**1878**).
xa: The Arya Samaj was **revivalist**, unlike the reformist Brahmo Samaj.
APPSC-GS **2025** order: Rammohan → Vidyasagar → Phule → **Dayanand**.

188.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Prarthana Samaj (1867) was founded by Atmaram Pandurang.
2. The earliest Prarthana Samaj centre in Andhra was set up at Rajahmundry in 1878 by Veeresalingam.
3. The Arya Samaj was founded at Lahore in 1875.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
188.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct (APPSC-GS 2022 and APPSC 2019). Statement 3 is wrong: Dayananda founded the Arya Samaj at Bombay in 1875, and it later worked mainly from Lahore. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
188.tq: Arya Samaj founded at Bombay; Lahore came later.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Atmaram Pandurang** founded the **Prarthana Samaj** (**1867**).
Statement 2 is **correct**: earliest Andhra centre — **Rajahmundry**, **1878**, **Veeresalingam** (APPSC **2019**).
Statement 3 is **wrong**: the Arya Samaj was founded at **Bombay**, **1875**, and later worked from **Lahore** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: First Andhra Brahmo: **Mannava Buchayya Pantulu**.
Andhra "Trinity": **Veeresalingam**, **Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu**, **Desiraju Peda Bapaiah**.

188.s:
Consider the following statements about the early Brahmo organisations:
1. The Brahmo Sabha was later renamed the Brahmo Samaj by Keshab Chandra Sen.
2. The Atmiya Sabha (1815) translated the Upanishads and Vedanta into Bengali and English.
3. Rammohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha in Calcutta in 1828 with Dwarkanath Tagore.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
188.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the Brahmo Sabha was renamed the Brahmo Samaj by Debendranath Tagore. The other two are correct: the Atmiya Sabha translated the Upanishads and Vedanta, and the Brahmo Sabha was founded in 1828 with Dwarkanath Tagore. So '2 and 3 only' is right; every other option either includes statement 1 or leaves out a correct statement.
188.tq: Dwarkanath = co-founder; Debendranath = renamed and revived; Keshab = later splits.
xs: Statement 1 is **wrong**: the Brahmo Sabha was renamed by **Debendranath Tagore**, not Keshab.
Statement 2 is **correct**: the **Atmiya Sabha** (**1815**) translated the **Upanishads and Vedanta**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: **Brahmo Sabha**, Calcutta, **1828**, with **Dwarkanath Tagore** — so **2 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **Keshab** founded the **Brahmo Samaj of India** (**1866**).
The Atmiya Sabha was the "**Society of Friends**".

188.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
188.x: Dharma Sabha was founded by Raja Radhakant Deb, not Keshab Chandra Sen. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
188.tq: Find the wrong founder-organisation pair by applying the swapped-person trap.
xs: **Dharma Sabha — Keshab** is wrong: it was founded by **Radhakant Deb** (**1830**) — so option **(1)** is the mismatch.
**Deva Samaj** — **Agnihotri**; **Seva Sadan** — **Behramji Malabari**; **Paramahansa Mandali** — **Dadoba Pandurang**: correct.
xa: Seva Sadan: **Bombay**, **1908**, with **Dayaram Gidumal**.
The Dharma Sabha opposed **Brahmo** propaganda and the **Sati ban**.

188.s: Which one of the following organisations was founded in Poona in 1849 to oppose caste distinctions and promote women’s education?
188.x: Paramahansa Mandali was founded by Dadoba Pandurang in 1849 and was associated with opposition to caste distinctions and support for women’s education.
188.tq: Identify the organisation by combining its place, year and reform objective.
xs: The **Paramahansa Mandali** was founded in **Poona** in **1849** against caste and for women's education — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC-GS **2023**).
**Tattvabodhini** (**1839**) and **Dharma Sabha** (**1830**) were in **Calcutta**; the **Prarthana Samaj** dates from **1867**.
xa: Founder: **Dadoba Pandurang** (APP: "**Tadoba Panduranga Tarkad**").
**1848**: the **Phules' girls' school**, Pune.

188.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Atmiya Sabha was established
B. Hindu College was founded
C. Vedanta College was founded
D. The Sati abolition regulation was enacted
188.x: The sequence is Atmiya Sabha in 1815, Hindu College in 1817, Vedanta College in 1825 and the abolition of Sati in 1829.
188.tq: Arrange the events by their dates, beginning with the earliest institutional initiative.
xs: Order **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**Atmiya Sabha** (**1815**) → **Hindu College** (**1817**).
**Vedanta College** (**1825**) → **Sati abolished** (**1829**).
xa: The **English school** came in **1822** and the **Brahmo Sabha** in **1828**.
Sati ban: **Regulation XVII**, **4 December 1829**.

188.s: Which one of the following chronological sequences is correct?
o: Tattvabodhini Sabha — Widow Remarriage Act — Brahmo Samaj of India — Satyashodhak Samaj
Widow Remarriage Act — Tattvabodhini Sabha — Satyashodhak Samaj — Brahmo Samaj of India
Brahmo Samaj of India — Tattvabodhini Sabha — Widow Remarriage Act — Satyashodhak Samaj
Tattvabodhini Sabha — Brahmo Samaj of India — Widow Remarriage Act — Satyashodhak Samaj
188.x: The Tattvabodhini Sabha was founded in 1839, the Widow Remarriage Act was passed in 1856, the Brahmo Samaj of India emerged in 1866 and the Satyashodhak Samaj was founded in 1873.
188.tq: Place the middle events by their years before checking the complete sequence.
xs: Order: **Tattvabodhini Sabha** (**1839**) → **Widow Remarriage Act** (**1856**) → **Brahmo Samaj of India** (**1866**) → **Satyashodhak Samaj** (**1873**) — option **(1)**.
Options 2, 3 and 4 misplace the **Widow Remarriage Act** or the **Brahmo Samaj of India**.
xa: The Widow Remarriage Act is linked with **Vidyasagar**; the Satyashodhak Samaj with **Phule**.
**1867**: Prarthana Samaj; **1875**: Arya Samaj.
**1878**: Sadharan Brahmo Samaj.

188.s:
The correct sequence of the following major contributions is:
1. Raja Rammohan Roy
2. Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
3. Jyotiba Phule
4. Swami Dayanand Saraswati
188.x: The chronological order is Raja Rammohan Roy, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, Jyotiba Phule and Swami Dayanand Saraswati.
188.tq: Arrange reformers by the dates of their principal reform contributions rather than by fame or movement size.
xs: Order **1, 2, 3, 4**: **Rammohan Roy → Vidyasagar → Jyotiba Phule → Dayanand Saraswati** — option **(1)**.
APPSC-GS **2025** key (C-A-D-B).
xa: Markers: **Sati** **1829**; **Widow Remarriage Act** **1856**; **Satyashodhak Samaj** **1873**; **Arya Samaj** **1875**.
Phule also ran a **girls' school** in Pune (**1848**).

188.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Organisation)
a. Brahmo Samaj of India
b. Sadharan Brahmo Samaj
c. Prarthana Samaj
 d. Paramahansa Mandali

List-II (Year)
i. 1849
ii. 1866
iii. 1867
iv. 1878
188.x: The Brahmo Samaj of India was formed in 1866, the Sadharan Brahmo Samaj in 1878, the Prarthana Samaj in 1867 and the Paramahansa Mandali in 1849.
188.tq: Start from the sure year-pair and eliminate codes containing a conflicting chronological association.
xs: Correct code: **a–ii, b–iv, c–iii, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Brahmo Samaj of India** — **1866**; **Sadharan Brahmo Samaj** — **1878**.
**Prarthana Samaj** — **1867**; **Paramahansa Mandali** — **1849**.
xa: The 1866 body was **Keshab**'s; the 1878 body was led by **Ananda Mohan Bose** and **Shivnath Shastri**.
⚠ **1849** (Mandali) vs **1867** (Prarthana) — the usual swap trap.
The **Prarthana Samaj** reached **Rajahmundry** in **1878**.

188.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Reform body)
A. Brahmo Samaj
B. Prarthana Samaj
C. Satyashodhak Samaj
D. Ramakrishna Mission

List-II (Year)
1. 1828
2. 1867
3. 1873
4. 1897

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
188.x: Brahmo Samaj was founded in 1828, Prarthana Samaj in 1867, Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 and Ramakrishna Mission in 1897.
188.tq: Start from the sure chronological pair and eliminate the remaining codes.
xs: Correct code: **A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4** — option **(1)**.
**Brahmo Samaj** (as Brahmo Sabha) **1828**; **Prarthana Samaj** **1867**.
**Satyashodhak Samaj** **1873**; **Ramakrishna Mission** **1897**.
xa: **Arya Samaj** came in **1875**.
**Tattvabodhini Sabha** **1839**; **Paramahansa Mandali** **1849**.

188.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Like the Brahmo Samaj, the Arya Samaj is classed as a reformist rather than a revivalist movement.
2. The Brahmo Samaj and the Prarthana Samaj were reformist movements based on reason.
3. The Arya Samaj and Deoband are classed as revivalist movements.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
188.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the Arya Samaj is classed as revivalist, unlike the reformist Brahmo Samaj. The other two are correct: Brahmo and Prarthana Samaj were reformist (reason), while Arya Samaj and Deoband were revivalist. So '2 and 3 only' is right; every other option either includes statement 1 or leaves out a correct statement.
188.tq: Reformist: Brahmo, Prarthana. Revivalist: Arya, Deoband.
xs: Statement 1 is **wrong**: the **Arya Samaj** is **revivalist**, unlike the reformist Brahmo Samaj.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **Brahmo** and **Prarthana Samaj** were **reformist** (reason).
Statement 3 is **correct**: **Arya Samaj** and **Deoband** are **revivalist** — so **2 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: The Brahmo Samaj stood for **reason** and **modern ideas**.
It **attacked superstition** and laid the base for **nationalism**.

188.s: Which of the following statements best expresses the broader significance of the Brahmo Samaj?
o: It confined its activities entirely to ritual worship.
It attacked superstition, promoted education and women's rights, and helped create the base for nationalism.
It sought to preserve caste restrictions without modification.
It opposed modern education and social reform.
188.x: The Brahmo Samaj opposed superstition, supported education and women's rights, and contributed to the intellectual and social foundations of nationalism.
188.tq: Choose the option that captures the movement's multiple social and national consequences.
xs: The Brahmo Samaj **attacked superstition**, **promoted education and women's rights**, and **laid the base for nationalism** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It **rejected priestly ritualism** and **caste distinctions**, so options 1 and 3 fail.
xa: It was **reformist**, unlike the revivalist **Arya Samaj**.
Social programme: against **child marriage**, **polygamy**, **female infanticide**; for **widow remarriage**.

188.s: Which region is regarded as the first Indian region to experience a renaissance?
188.x: Bengal is identified as the first Indian region to experience a renaissance. Within Andhra, Rajahmundry is associated with the first renaissance.
188.tq: Distinguish the all-India regional first from the corresponding Andhra location.
xs: **Bengal** was the first Indian region to have a **renaissance** — so option **(4)** is correct.
In **Andhra**, the counterpart centre was **Rajahmundry**.
xa: **Rammohan Roy** is called **Father of Bengal Renaissance** and **Father of the Indian Renaissance**.
He is also the first "**Modern Man of India**".

188.s: In the context of the Andhra renaissance, which place is identified as its centre?
188.x: Rajahmundry is identified as the place associated with the first renaissance in Andhra.
188.tq: Separate the Andhra-specific first from the later Brahmo Samaj centres and dates.
xs: **Rajahmundry** is the Andhra renaissance centre — so option **(2)** is correct.
The earliest Andhra **Prarthana Samaj** came up there in **1878** under **Veeresalingam** (APPSC **2019**).
xa: Andhra "**Trinity of the Brahma Samaj**": **Veeresalingam**, **Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu**, **Desiraju Peda Bapaiah**.
First Andhra Brahmo: **Mannava Buchayya Pantulu**.

188.s: Rabindranath Tagore, remembered in the cited anniversary reference, was the youngest son of which Brahmo leader?
188.x: Rabindranath Tagore was the youngest son of Debendranath Tagore, a leader of the Brahmo movement.
188.tq: Distinguish the family relationship from the other named Brahmo and Maharashtra reformers.
xs: **Rabindranath Tagore** was the youngest son of **Debendranath Tagore** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He is remembered on his death anniversary (**10 Aug 2026**).
xa: Debendranath (**1817-1905**) was called "**Maharishi**".
He founded the **Tattvabodhini Sabha** (**1839**) and later led the **Adi Brahmo Samaj**.

188.s: Who was the first Andhra associated with the Brahmo Samaj?
188.x: Mannava Buchayya Pantulu is identified as the first Andhra associated with the Brahmo Samaj.
188.tq: Distinguish the first Andhra associate from the later Andhra Trinity and organisational promoters.
xs: The first Andhra Brahmo was **Mannava Buchayya Pantulu** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Veeresalingam** and **Desiraju Peda Bapaiah** belong to the Andhra **Trinity**, not the first Brahmo.
xa: Trinity: **Veeresalingam**, **Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu**, **Desiraju Peda Bapaiah**.
Andhra renaissance centre: **Rajahmundry**.

188.s: Who among the following formed the Andhra 'Trinity of the Brahma Samaj'?
o: Veeresalingam, Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu and Desiraju Peda Bapaiah
Mannava Buchayya Pantulu, Gurajada Apparao and Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham
Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu, Tanguturi Prakasam and Mannava Buchayya Pantulu
Desiraju Peda Bapaiah, Komarraju Lakshmana Rao and Gurajada Apparao
188.x: The Andhra Trinity of the Brahma Samaj was Veeresalingam, Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu and Desiraju Peda Bapaiah, so A. Mannava Buchayya Pantulu was the first Andhra Brahmo but not one of the Trinity. The other names in B, C and D are not part of it.
188.tq: Trinity = Veeresalingam, Venkataratnam Naidu, Peda Bapaiah.
xs: The Andhra "**Trinity of the Brahma Samaj**" = **Veeresalingam**, **Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu**, **Desiraju Peda Bapaiah** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Mannava Buchayya Pantulu** was the **first Andhra Brahmo**, not one of the Trinity.
xa: **Veeresalingam** set up the earliest Andhra Prarthana Samaj at **Rajahmundry** (**1878**).
Bengal was the first region to have a renaissance; in Andhra, **Rajahmundry**.

189.s: The followers of Henry Vivian Derozio were popularly known as:
189.x: The followers of Derozio were known as Derozians.
189.tq: Test the exact label used for the followers of a reform leader.
xs: Derozio's followers were the "**Derozians**" — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Brahmos** followed the Brahmo Samaj; the others are not terms in the notes.
xa: Derozio taught at **Hindu College, Calcutta**.
Their forum was the **Academic Association** (**1828**).

189.s: Which of the following best describes the ideas of the Young Bengal Movement?
o: Radical rationalism and criticism of social orthodoxy
Opposition to women's education and rights
Exclusive loyalty to idol worship and caste hierarchy
Revival of decadent customs without criticism
189.x: Young Bengal stood for radical rationalism, opposed idol worship, casteism and decadent customs, and supported women's rights and education.
189.tq: Select the option that combines the movement's intellectual and social objectives.
xs: **Young Bengal** stood for **radical, rationalist, iconoclastic** ideas against social orthodoxy — so option **(1)** is correct.
It attacked **idol worship**, **casteism** and **decadent customs**, and strongly backed **women's rights and education**.
xa: It was inspired by the **French Revolution**.
Comparative note: **Young Bengal = radical**; Prarthana Samaj = milder.

189.s: Henry Louis Vivian Derozio was a teacher at which institution?
189.x: Derozio was a teacher at Hindu College, Calcutta, where he influenced the Young Bengal Movement.
189.tq: Identify the movement through its institutional centre.
xs: **Derozio** taught at **Hindu College, Calcutta** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He was **dismissed** from it in **1831** and died that year.
xa: He was of **Anglo-Indian** (Indo-Portuguese) descent.
His followers formed the **Academic Association** (**1828**).

189.s: Henry Louis Vivian Derozio belonged to which background?
189.x: Derozio was of Anglo-Indian, or Indo-Portuguese, descent.
189.tq: Test the leader’s exact nationality or community background rather than his place of work.
xs: Derozio was of **Anglo-Indian** (**Indo-Portuguese**) descent — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was not Scottish, French or Persian in origin.
xa: He was inspired by the **French Revolution**.
He taught at **Hindu College, Calcutta** until his dismissal in **1831**.

189.s: The Young Bengal Movement was particularly inspired by the—
189.x: The ideas of the Young Bengal Movement were inspired by the French Revolution and its emphasis on reason and liberty.
189.tq: Link the intellectual movement with its stated historical inspiration.
xs: **Young Bengal** was inspired by the **French Revolution** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Its ideas were **radical, rationalist, iconoclastic**.
xa: It attacked **idol worship** and **casteism**.
Leader: **Henry Louis Vivian Derozio**; followers: **Derozians**.

189.s:
Consider the following statements about Henry Vivian Derozio:
1. He was dismissed from Hindu College in 1831.
2. He died in 1831.
3. He continued as a teacher at Hindu College until 1857.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
189.x: Derozio was dismissed from Hindu College in 1831 and died in the same year. Statement 3 is false because he did not continue there until 1857.
189.tq: Use the paired date facts and reject the exaggerated continuation of service.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: Derozio was **dismissed from Hindu College in 1831**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: he **died** that same year.
