Statement 3 is **wrong**: he could not have taught till 1857 — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: He taught at Hindu College in the **late 1820s**.
The **Academic Association** was set up in **1828**.

189.s: The forum associated with the followers of Derozio was the—
189.x: The Derozians used the Academic Association as their forum for discussion and intellectual activity.
189.tq: Match the movement’s followers with their specific forum.
xs: The Derozians' forum for debate was the **Academic Association** (Calcutta, **1828**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Manav Dharma Sabha** was **Durgaram Mancharam**'s (Surat); the **National Social Conference** and **Poona Sarvajanik Sabha** were **Ranade**'s.
xa: Founder: **Henry Louis Vivian Derozio**.
APPSC-GS **2022** match: **Derozio — Young Bengal**.

189.s: Who started the Marathi paper Darpan in 1832?
189.x: Bal Shastri Jambhekar started the Marathi paper Darpan in 1832 and attacked Brahmanical orthodoxy.
189.tq: Match the journal with its reformer and use the associated year as confirmation.
xs: **Bal Shastri Jambhekar** started the Marathi paper **Darpan** (**1832**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
He attacked **Brahmanical orthodoxy** in **Bombay** (APPSC-G2 **2017**).
xa: **Gopal Hari Deshmukh** = "**Lokahitawadi**"; **Ranade** — **Induprakash**.
**Dnyanodaya** was a Marathi **Christian missionary** journal.

189.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
189.x: Induprakash, an Anglo-Marathi journal, was linked to M.G. Ranade. Prabhakar carried Deshmukh’s Shatapatre, Darpan was started by Jambhekar, and Dnyanodaya was a Marathi Christian missionary journal.
189.tq: Start from the sure journal–reformer pair and eliminate the swapped associations.
xs: **Induprakash** — **M.G. Ranade** (Anglo-Marathi) is correct — option **(1)**.
**Prabhakar** carried **Deshmukh**'s **Shatapatre**; **Darpan** was **Jambhekar**'s.
**Dnyanodaya** was a Marathi **Christian missionary** journal (American Marathi Mission).
xa: **R.G. Bhandarkar** was a **Sanskrit scholar**, not a journalist in this list.
Jambhekar's Darpan dates from **1832**.

189.s: Prabhakar was the weekly that carried—
189.x: Prabhakar carried Gopal Hari Deshmukh’s Shatapatre, or ‘hundred letters’.
189.tq: Distinguish a journal from the work published in it.
xs: **Prabhakar** carried **Gopal Hari Deshmukh**'s **Shatapatre** (hundred letters) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Darpan** was **Jambhekar**'s own paper; the **Academic Association** was the Derozian forum.
xa: Deshmukh wrote as "**Lokahitawadi**" (APPSC-GS **2021**, G2 **2008**).
**Induprakash** was linked to **Ranade**.

189.s: The pen-name 'Lokahitawadi' is associated with:
189.x: Gopal Hari Deshmukh wrote as Lokahitawadi, and his Shatapatre (hundred letters) appeared in the weekly Prabhakar. Jambhekar started Darpan, Ranade was linked to Induprakash, and Bhandarkar was a Sanskrit scholar.
189.tq: Lokahitawadi = Gopal Hari Deshmukh.
xs: "**Lokahitawadi**" was **Gopal Hari Deshmukh** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC-GS **2021**, G2 **2008**).
**Jambhekar** started **Darpan**; **Ranade** — **Induprakash**; **Bhandarkar** was a **Sanskrit scholar**.
xa: His **Shatapatre** appeared in the weekly **Prabhakar**.
Jambhekar's **Darpan** dates from **1832**.

189.s:
Consider the following statements about the Paramahansa Mandali:
1. It was a secret society that believed in one God.
2. Its members strictly kept caste rules and refused food cooked by lower castes.
3. It opposed caste discrimination and supported women's education and widow remarriage.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
189.x: Statement 2 is wrong: its members broke caste rules by eating food cooked by lower castes. The other two are correct: it was a secret society believing in one God, and it opposed caste discrimination while supporting women's education and widow remarriage. So '1 and 3 only' is right; every other option either includes statement 2 or leaves out a correct statement.
189.tq: Paramahansa Mandali = secret; inter-dining with lower castes.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: a **secret society** believing in **one God**.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: members **broke caste rules** by eating food cooked by lower castes.
Statement 3 is **correct**: against **caste discrimination**; for **women's education** and **widow remarriage** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: Founded **1849** by **Dadoba Pandurang**.
⚠ **1849** = Paramahansa Mandali (secret); **1867** = Prarthana Samaj.

189.s: Who were associated with the founding of Paramahansa Mandali?
189.x: Paramahansa Mandali was founded by Dadoba Pandurang along with Durgaram Mancharam of the Manav Dharma Sabha of Surat.
189.tq: Use the paired-founder clue and distinguish it from leaders of other reform movements.
xs: **Dadoba Pandurang** with **Durgaram Mancharam** (Manav Dharma Sabha, **Surat**) founded the **Paramahansa Mandali** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Ranade** and **Bhandarkar** led the **Prarthana Samaj**; **Tilak** and **Agarkar** the **Deccan Education Society**.
xa: Founded **1849** in **Bombay**, with branches at **Poona** and **Satara**.
It was a **secret society**.

189.s: Which statement correctly describes the location of Paramahansa Mandali?
o: It was founded in Bombay and had branches at Poona and Satara.
It was founded in Pune and had branches only in Bengal.
It was founded in Calcutta and had branches at Bombay and Pune.
It was founded in Surat and had branches at Calcutta and Satara.
189.x: Paramahansa Mandali was founded in Bombay and had branches at Poona and Satara. Some accounts refer to its establishment at Poona in 1849 in examination questions.
189.tq: Separate the founding city from the cities where branches were established.
xs: The Mandali was founded in **Bombay** with branches at **Poona** and **Satara** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ APPSC-GS **2023** frames it as "established in **Poona** in **1849**" — follow the key if options force a choice.
xa: Aims: against **caste discrimination**; for **women's education** and **widow remarriage**.
**Surat** was the home of **Durgaram Mancharam**'s Manav Dharma Sabha.

189.s: R.G. Bhandarkar, associated with the Prarthana Samaj, was primarily known as a—
189.x: R.G. Bhandarkar was known as a Sanskrit scholar and joined the Prarthana Samaj in 1870.
189.tq: Test a precise biographical description rather than a broad organisational association.
xs: **R.G. Bhandarkar** was a **Sanskrit scholar** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He joined the **Prarthana Samaj** in **1870**.
xa: With **Justice M.G. Ranade** he led the Prarthana Samaj.
⚠ Some notes misspell him "**R.C.**" Bhandarkar.

189.s: Prarthana Samaj emerged as—
o: an offshoot of the Brahmo Samaj and a reform movement within Hinduism
a Christian missionary society founded in Pune
a political organisation formed by the Indian National Congress
a branch of the Arya Samaj opposed to all social reform
189.x: Prarthana Samaj was an offshoot of the Brahmo Samaj and functioned as a reform movement within Hinduism.
189.tq: Identify the institutional relationship and reject nearby but incorrect reform traditions.
xs: The **Prarthana Samaj** was an **offshoot of the Brahmo Samaj**, a **reform within Hinduism** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was not missionary, political or anti-reform.
xa: It was inspired by **Keshab Chandra Sen**'s visit.
Comparative note: **Brahmo-inspired but milder**.

189.s: The establishment of Prarthana Samaj in Bombay in 1867 was influenced by the visit of—
189.x: Prarthana Samaj was inspired by the visit of Keshab Chandra Sen and was established in Bombay in 1867.
189.tq: Use the inspiration–organisation association rather than confusing different reform leaders.
xs: The **Prarthana Samaj** (**1867**, Bombay) was inspired by **Keshab Chandra Sen**'s visit — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Derozio** led **Young Bengal**; **Dayananda** founded the **Arya Samaj** (**1875**).
xa: Founder: **Dr. Atmaram Pandurang**.
Leaders: **M.G. Ranade**, **R.G. Bhandarkar**.

189.s: Who were the principal leaders of the Prarthana Samaj in Maharashtra?
189.x: M.G. Ranade and R.G. Bhandarkar were prominent leaders of the Prarthana Samaj in Maharashtra.
189.tq: Identify the correct leadership pair instead of its founder alone.
xs: **M.G. Ranade** and **R.G. Bhandarkar** led the **Prarthana Samaj** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Dadoba Pandurang** and **Durgaram Mancharam** founded the **Paramahansa Mandali**; **Tilak** and **Chiplunkar** the **Deccan Education Society**.
xa: Bhandarkar joined in **1870**.
Founder: **Dr. Atmaram Pandurang** (**1867**).

189.s:
Consider the following statements about the Prarthana Samaj:
1. Its four-point agenda included raising the age of marriage for men and women.
2. It worked through persuasion and social work rather than confrontation.
3. Its aims excluded the uplift of the depressed classes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
189.x: Statement 3 is wrong: uplift of the depressed classes was among its aims, along with inter-dining and inter-marriage. The other two are correct: its four-point agenda included raising the age of marriage, and it worked through persuasion and social work. So '1 and 2 only' is right; every other option either includes statement 3 or leaves out a correct statement.
189.tq: Four points: caste, women's education, widow remarriage, marriage age.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: the four-point agenda included raising the **age of marriage**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: it worked by **persuasion and social work**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: **uplift of the depressed classes** was an aim — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Four points: against **caste**; **women's education**; **widow remarriage**; **age of marriage**.
Other aims: **inter-dining**, **inter-marriage**.

189.s: Which statement best distinguishes the Prarthana Samaj from the Brahmo Samaj in the context of social reform?
o: Prarthana Samaj focused mainly on social reform and did not outright forbid idol worship or abandon caste practices.
Prarthana Samaj completely rejected all forms of social reform.
Prarthana Samaj was exclusively a political body with no religious connection.
Prarthana Samaj required the abandonment of Hindu society before permitting reform.
189.x: The exam-safe distinction is that Prarthana Samaj focused more on social reform and did not outright forbid idol worship or abandon caste in the manner described for the Brahmos.
189.tq: Compare the practical social emphasis of two related reform traditions without using an absolute claim.
xs: Unlike the Brahmos, the Prarthana Samaj focused on **social reform** and did **not outright forbid idol worship or abandon caste** — so option **(1)** is correct.
This is the exam-safe version (p.**84**).
xa: ⚠ p.**83** claims it rejected idol worship — treat p.84 as safe.
Its method: **persuasion and social work**, not confrontation.

189.s: Who among the following was associated with the Prarthana Samaj, Widow Remarriage Association, Poona Sarvajanik Sabha, Deccan Education Society and National Social Conference?
189.x: Justice M.G. Ranade was associated with all the listed reform organisations and bodies. He also advocated the close connection between religious and social reform.
189.tq: Identify the reformer from a cluster of institutional associations.
xs: **Justice M.G. Ranade** links all these bodies — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Widow Remarriage Association** (**1861**), **Poona Sarvajanik Sabha** (**1870**), **National Social Conference** (**1887**).
He supported the **Deccan Education Society** (Pune, **1884**) and led the **Prarthana Samaj**.
xa: His view: **social and religious reform go together**.
**Bhandarkar** joined the Prarthana Samaj but not these other bodies in the notes.

189.s:
Consider the following statements about Justice M.G. Ranade’s views:
1. Rigid religious belief obstructs social, economic and political progress.
2. Social reform and religious reform should be treated as unrelated spheres.
3. Social and religious reform should proceed together.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
189.x: Ranade held that rigid religious belief obstructed progress and that social and religious reform were interrelated. Statement 2 is false because he did not regard them as unrelated.
189.tq: Find the statement that reverses the reformer’s central argument.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **rigid religious belief** blocks social, economic and political progress.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: he did not treat them as unrelated.
Statement 3 is **correct**: **social and religious reform go together** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: He founded the **National Social Conference** (**1887**).
He was linked to **Induprakash**.

189.s: The National Social Conference was founded in 1887 mainly because—
o: the Young Bengal Movement had shifted its headquarters to Pune
the Arya Samaj refused to discuss educational questions
the Prarthana Samaj had been dissolved by the colonial government
the Indian National Congress concentrated on political issues and did not adequately address social reform
189.x: M.G. Ranade founded the National Social Conference with Raghunath Rao because the Congress largely confined itself to political issues. The Conference provided a forum for social reform.
189.tq: Test the cause behind the creation of an organisation rather than merely its date.
xs: The **INC kept to political issues**, so the **National Social Conference** (**1887**) was set up for social reform — so option **(4)** is correct.
It met at the **same time and place** as the Congress sessions.
xa: Founders: **M.G. Ranade** with **Raghunath Rao**.
Ranade: **social and religious reform go together**.

189.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Social Conference:
1. It was founded by M.G. Ranade with Raghunath Rao.
2. It met at the same time and place as the sessions of the Indian National Congress.
3. It was created to discuss social reform.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
189.x: All three statements are correct. The National Social Conference was founded in 1887 and met alongside the Congress to discuss social reform.
189.tq: Verify founder, institutional arrangement and purpose together.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: founded by **M.G. Ranade** with **Raghunath Rao**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: it met at the **same time and place** as **INC** sessions.
Statement 3 is **correct**: it existed to **discuss social reform** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: Reason: the INC kept to **political issues**.

189.s: The Widow Remarriage Association associated with M.G. Ranade was established in—
189.x: The Widow Remarriage Association associated with M.G. Ranade was established in 1861.
189.tq: Distinguish the year of an associated institution from the years of later reform bodies.
xs: Ranade's **Widow Remarriage Association** dates from **1861** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**1849** = **Paramahansa Mandali**; **1870** = **Poona Sarvajanik Sabha**; **1887** = **National Social Conference**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say Ranade set up the **Deccan Education Society** in **1861**; the main date is **1884**.
**Widow remarriage** was also a Prarthana Samaj aim.

189.s: Which of the following combinations correctly describes the Deccan Education Society?
o: Founded in 1884 at Pune by Tilak, Agarkar and Chiplunkar, with Ranade’s support
Founded in 1861 at Bombay by Ranade and Bhandarkar without other associates
Founded in 1873 at Pune by Jyotiba Phule and Derozio
Founded in 1887 at Calcutta by Raghunath Rao and Keshab Chandra Sen
189.x: The Deccan Education Society was founded in Pune in 1884 by Tilak, Agarkar, Chiplunkar and others, with the support of M.G. Ranade.
189.tq: Check the institution through its year, place, founders and supporter together.
xs: The **Deccan Education Society** was founded in **Pune**, **1884**, by **Tilak**, **Agarkar**, **Chiplunkar** and others, with **Ranade's support** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes say Ranade set it up in **1861**.
xa: Ranade's other bodies: **Poona Sarvajanik Sabha** (**1870**), **National Social Conference** (**1887**).
**1861** is the **Widow Remarriage Association**.

189.s: The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha, associated with M.G. Ranade, was established in—
189.x: The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha was established in 1870 and was associated with M.G. Ranade.
189.tq: Separate closely spaced institutional dates by linking each year to its organisation.
xs: The **Poona Sarvajanik Sabha** dates from **1870** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1861** = Widow Remarriage Association; **1867** = Prarthana Samaj; **1884** = Deccan Education Society.
xa: **1870** is also when **Bhandarkar** joined the Prarthana Samaj.
Linked to **M.G. Ranade**.

189.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
189.x: Atmaram Pandurang founded the Prarthana Samaj (Bombay, 1867), so A is right. The Brahmo Samaj was founded by Rammohan Roy, the Satyashodhak Samaj by Jyotiba Phule, and the Ramakrishna Mission by Vivekananda.
189.tq: Watch for the swapped founder trap in reform movements.
xs: **Prarthana Samaj — Atmaram Pandurang** is correct — option **(1)**.
APPSC-GS **2022** key: **Dayananda** — Arya Samaj; **Rammohan** — **Brahmo Samaj**; **Atmaram Pandurang** — Prarthana Samaj; **Derozio** — Young Bengal.
So **Brahmo Samaj — Phule** and **Ramakrishna Mission — Rammohan Roy** are wrong.
xa: Prarthana Samaj: **Bombay**, **1867**.
The **Satyashodhak Samaj** worked for social justice for the "**untouchables**".

189.s: Which one of the following pairs of a reform body and its work is NOT correctly matched?
o: Arya Samaj — true knowledge of the Vedas
Satyashodhak Samaj — social justice for the 'untouchables'
Sharada Sadan — secret society against caste rules
Prarthana Samaj — improvement of women and depressed classes
189.x: Pandita Ramabai's Sharada Sadan was a home for widows, so C is the wrong pair. The secret society against caste was the Paramahansa Mandali. A, B and D match the APPSC-GS 2023 key.
189.tq: Sharada Sadan = home for widows (Pandita Ramabai).
xs: **Sharada Sadan** (**Pandita Ramabai**) was **a home for widows**, not a secret society — so option **(3)** is the mismatch.
The **secret society** against caste rules was the **Paramahansa Mandali**.
The other pairs match the APPSC-GS **2023** key.
xa: **Arya Samaj** — true knowledge of the **Vedas**; **Satyashodhak** — social justice for "**untouchables**".
**Prarthana Samaj** — improvement of **women** and **depressed classes**.

189.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Young Bengal Movement — Henry Louis Vivian Derozio
189.x: The Satyashodhak Samaj was founded by Jyotiba Phule, not Dayananda Saraswati. Dayananda Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj.
189.tq: Find the swapped founder among otherwise familiar reform organisations.
xs: **Satyashodhak Samaj — Dayananda Saraswati** is wrong — so option **(3)** is the mismatch.
**Dayananda** founded the **Arya Samaj** (APPSC-GS **2022**); the Satyashodhak Samaj was **anti-Brahmanical**, with a **lower-caste focus**.
**Derozio** — Young Bengal; **Dadoba Pandurang** — Paramahansa Mandali; **Atmaram Pandurang** — Prarthana Samaj: correct.
xa: ⚠ The **Arya Samaj** was founded in **Bombay (1875)**, not Calcutta.
It **rejects** idol worship and ritualism.

189.s:
Consider the following statements about the Prarthana Samaj:
1. It worked through persuasion and social work rather than confrontation.
2. Its activities included support for inter-dining and inter-marriage.
3. It sought the uplift of depressed classes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
189.x: Prarthana Samaj pursued reform through persuasion and social work and also supported inter-dining, inter-marriage and the uplift of depressed classes.
189.tq: Combine the organisation’s method of reform with its additional social objectives.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **persuasion and social work**, not confrontation.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **inter-dining** and **inter-marriage**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: **uplift of the depressed classes** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: Four-point agenda: against **caste**; **women's education**; **widow remarriage**; **age of marriage**.
It did **not outright forbid idol worship**.

189.s: Who organised the women's wing associated with the first Prarthana Samaj in Andhra?
189.x: K. Seethamma organised the women's wing of the Prarthana Samaj in Andhra.
189.tq: Directly identify the person associated with a specific organisational role.
xs: **K. Seethamma** organised the women's wing of the first Andhra Prarthana Samaj — so option **(2)** is correct.
It held **weekly prayers for women of all castes**.
**Pandita Ramabai** ran the **Sharada Sadan**, a home for widows.
xa: The Samaj was founded by **Kandukuri Veeresalingam** at **Rajahmundry**, **1878** (APHQ **2019**).
The Prarthana Samaj's agenda included **women's education** and **widow remarriage**.

189.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Arya Samaj is correct?
o: It was founded as a secret organisation against social reform.
It rejected idol worship and ritualism.
It primarily advocated the interests of the lower castes through an anti-Brahmanical programme.
It accepted idol worship and ritualism as essential practices.
189.x: The Arya Samaj rejected idol worship and ritualism. A secret organisational character was associated with Paramahansa Mandali, while the anti-Brahmanical lower-caste focus belonged to Satyashodhak Samaj.
189.tq: Use nearby reform movements to distinguish their defining features.
xs: The **Arya Samaj** **rejects idol worship and ritualism** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **secret** body was the **Paramahansa Mandali**; the **anti-Brahmanical, lower-caste** focus was the **Satyashodhak Samaj**'s.
xa: ⚠ Trap (Nov **2025** practice question): Arya Samaj was founded in **Bombay (1875)**, not Calcutta.
Its work: **true knowledge of the Vedas** (APPSC-GS **2023**).

189.s:
Consider the following statements about the reform movements:
1. Prarthana Samaj was influenced by the Brahmo Samaj but followed a milder approach.
2. Young Bengal represented a radical reform tendency.
3. Paramahansa Mandali functioned as a secret organisation.
4. Satyashodhak Samaj focused on anti-Brahmanical reform and the uplift of lower castes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
189.x: All four statements are correct: Prarthana Samaj was a milder Brahmo-inspired movement, Young Bengal was radical, Paramahansa Mandali was secret, and Satyashodhak Samaj had an anti-Brahmanical, lower-caste focus.
189.tq: Separate movements by their distinctive character, method and social objective.
xs: All four are **correct** — option **(4)**.
**Prarthana Samaj** = Brahmo-inspired but **milder**; **Young Bengal** = **radical**.
**Paramahansa Mandali** = **secret**; **Satyashodhak** = **anti-Brahmanical**, lower-caste focus.
xa: Prarthana Samaj worked by **persuasion and social work**.
Young Bengal was **radical, rationalist, iconoclastic**.

189.s: Kandukuri Veeresalingam founded the first Prarthana Samaj in Andhra in 1878 at:
189.x: Veeresalingam founded it at Rajahmundry in 1878 (APHQ 2019), and K. Seethamma later organised its women's wing. Machilipatnam, Guntur and Visakhapatnam were not the site of the first centre.
189.tq: Rajahmundry 1878 = first Andhra Prarthana Samaj.
xs: **Kandukuri Veeresalingam** founded the first Andhra Prarthana Samaj at **Rajahmundry** in **1878** — so option **(3)** is correct (APHQ **2019**).
**Machilipatnam**, **Guntur** and **Visakhapatnam** were not its site.
xa: **K. Seethamma** organised its **women's wing**.
It held **weekly prayers for women of all castes**.

190.s: Dayananda Saraswati was born as:
190.x: Dayananda Saraswati’s original name was Mool Shankar Tiwari.
190.tq: Discriminate between the original names of Arya Samaj personalities.
xs: Dayananda Saraswati was born as **Mool Shankar Tiwari** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He was born at **Tankara** in **Kathiawar, Gujarat**, and lived **1824-1883**.
xa: His guru was **Swami Virajananda** (Virjanand) of **Mathura**.
He died at **Ajmer** in **1883**.
Titles: **"Martin Luther of India"** (given by **Lala Lajpat Rai**) and **"Grandfather of the Indian Nation"**.

190.s:
Consider the following statements about Dayananda Saraswati:
1. His guru was Swami Virajananda of Mathura.
2. He lived from 1824 to 1883.
3. He died at Lahore, where the Arya Samaj later shifted its headquarters.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
190.x: Statement 3 is wrong: he died at Ajmer in 1883; Lahore was only the later headquarters of the Arya Samaj. The other two are correct: his guru was Swami Virajananda of Mathura and he lived 1824-1883. So '1 and 2 only' is right; every other option either includes statement 3 or leaves out a correct statement.
190.tq: Born Tankara, guru at Mathura, died at Ajmer.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: his guru was **Swami Virajananda** of **Mathura**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: he lived **1824-1883**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: he died at **Ajmer** in **1883**; **Lahore** was only where the Arya Samaj later shifted its HQ.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: His original name was **Mool Shankar** (Tiwari), born at **Tankara**, Kathiawar, **Gujarat**.
He founded the **Arya Samaj** at **Bombay** in **1875**; its strongest base became **Punjab**.
⚠ Trap: Arya Samaj was founded in **Bombay**, not Calcutta or Lahore.

190.s: Tankara, the birthplace of Dayananda Saraswati, is located in:
190.x: Dayananda Saraswati was born at Tankara in the Kathiawar region of Gujarat.
190.tq: Use the specific birthplace rather than the broader reform centre.
xs: **Tankara**, Dayananda's birthplace, lies in **Kathiawar, Gujarat** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He was born **Mool Shankar Tiwari** in **1824**.
xa: His guru was **Swami Virajananda** of **Mathura**; he died at **Ajmer** in **1883**.
Slogans: **"India for the Indians"** and **"Back to the Vedas"**.
He is credited as the first to use the term **Swaraj**.

190.s:
Consider the following statements about Dayananda Saraswati:
1. He gave the slogan 'India for the Indians'.
2. Bal Gangadhar Tilak called him the 'Martin Luther of India'.
3. He is credited as the first to use the term Swaraj.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
190.x: Statement 2 is wrong: it was Lala Lajpat Rai who called him the 'Martin Luther of India'. The other two are correct: he gave the slogan 'India for the Indians' and is credited as the first to use the term Swaraj. So '1 and 3 only' is right; every other option either includes statement 2 or leaves out a correct statement.
190.tq: Martin Luther of India - said by Lala Lajpat Rai.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: he gave the slogan **"India for the Indians"**.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: it was **Lala Lajpat Rai**, not Tilak, who called him the **"Martin Luther of India"**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: he is credited as the first to use the term **Swaraj**.
So **1 and 3 only** — option **(3)** is correct.
xa: His other title: **"Grandfather of the Indian Nation"**.
His other slogan: **"Back to the Vedas"** ("Go Back to the Vedas").
He wrote his main work, **Satyarth Prakash**, in **Hindi**.

190.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Dayananda Saraswati’s contribution to language policy?
o: He wrote his main work in Hindi and promoted Hindi as a link language.
He confined his writings to Telugu and Tamil.
He promoted English as the sole link language.
He wrote exclusively in Persian and opposed vernacular languages.
190.x: Dayananda wrote his main work in Hindi and promoted Hindi as a link language.
190.tq: Select the complete and precise language-related statement.
xs: Dayananda **wrote his main work in Hindi** and **promoted Hindi as a link language** — so option **(1)** is correct.
His main work, **Satyarth Prakash** (**1875**), was written in **Hindi** — not Telugu, Tamil, English or Persian.
xa: **Satyarth Prakash** means **"The Light of Truth"** (also "The True Exposition").
It critiqued Hindu orthodoxy: **idolatry**, **caste by birth**, **child marriage**.
His slogans: **"India for the Indians"** and **"Back to the Vedas"**.

190.s: Arya Samaj was founded at which place in 1875?
190.x: Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati at Bombay in 1875. Its headquarters were later shifted to Lahore.
190.tq: Distinguish the place of founding from the later headquarters.
xs: The Arya Samaj was founded at **Bombay** in **1875** (April) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Lahore** became its HQ only later; **Calcutta** is a classic trap.
xa: Founding date: some notes give **7 April 1875**; many texts give **10 April 1875**.
Founder: **Swami Dayananda Saraswati**; name means **"Society of Nobles"**.
Strongest base: **Punjab**; also strong in **Rajasthan** and **United Provinces**.
⚠ Statement traps: "founded in Calcutta" (wrong) and "promotes idol worship" (wrong; it rejects it).

190.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Arya Samaj:
1. Its name means ‘Society of Nobles’.
2. Its strongest base became Punjab.
3. Its headquarters were originally established at Lahore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
190.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Arya Samaj was founded at Bombay, while its headquarters were later shifted to Lahore.
190.tq: Find the wrong location by separating the founding place from the later headquarters.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: Arya Samaj means **"Society of Nobles"**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: its strongest base was **Punjab**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: it was founded at **Bombay** (**1875**); the HQ was **later** shifted to **Lahore**.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: It was also strong in **Rajasthan** and the **United Provinces**.
**Ten Principles** drafted by Dayananda: truth, rational thought, moral action, well-being of all.
Called a **"nursery of militant nationalists"** — **Lala Lajpat Rai**, **Swami Shraddhanand**, Bhagat Singh's family.

190.s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with the programme of Arya Samaj?
190.x: Arya Samaj rejected idol worship, polytheism and ritualism. It opposed child marriage and supported widow remarriage and women’s education.
190.tq: Identify the negative statement among reform measures.
xs: **Promotion of idol worship** was NOT part of the programme — the Arya Samaj **rejected** idol worship — so option **(3)** is correct.
It **supported widow remarriage** and **women's education** and **opposed child marriage** — options (1), (2), (4) were part of it.
xa: It also rejected **polytheism**, **ritualism** and **caste by birth**.
It opposed **untouchability** and **purdah**; supported **inter-caste marriage**.
⚠ Trap: "promotes idol worship" is a standard wrong statement.

190.s:
The Ten Principles of Arya Samaj, drafted by Dayananda Saraswati, emphasised which of the following?
1. Truth and rational thought
2. Moral action
3. Welfare of all
4. Caste by birth
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
190.x: The Ten Principles emphasised truth, rational thought, moral conduct and the well-being of all. Arya Samaj rejected caste based on birth.
190.tq: Reject the swapped reform principle involving caste by birth.
xs: The Ten Principles stressed **truth and rational thought**, **moral action** and **well-being of all** — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(1)**.
**Caste by birth** was **rejected** by the Arya Samaj, so item 4 is wrong.
xa: The **Ten Principles** were drafted by **Dayananda Saraswati** himself.
The Samaj also rejected **idol worship**, **polytheism** and **ritualism**.
It supported **widow remarriage**, **inter-caste marriage** and **women's education**.

190.s:
The Arya Samaj came to be regarded as a ‘nursery of militant nationalists’ mainly because it influenced personalities and groups such as:
1. Lala Lajpat Rai
2. Swami Shraddhanand
3. Bhagat Singh’s family
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
190.x: Arya Samaj influenced Lala Lajpat Rai, Swami Shraddhanand and the family of Bhagat Singh, contributing to militant nationalist attitudes.
190.tq: Recognise the combined list of nationalist associations.
xs: The Samaj influenced **Lala Lajpat Rai**, **Swami Shraddhanand** and **Bhagat Singh's family** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
Hence it is called the **"nursery of militant nationalists"**.
xa: **Lala Lajpat Rai** called Dayananda the **"Martin Luther of India"**.
**Swami Shraddhanand** led the 1920s **Shuddhi** campaign via the **Bharatiya Hindu Shuddhi Sabha (1923)**; assassinated in **1926**.
Significance: revivalism + reform; built **Hindu self-confidence**; fed **militant nationalism**.

190.s: The slogan ‘Back to the Vedas’ implied that Dayananda Saraswati regarded the Vedas as:
o: Political documents of the colonial state
Texts limited exclusively to ritual practices
Infallible and the primordial word of God
190.x: The slogan expressed the belief that the four Vedas were infallible and constituted the primordial word of God.
190.tq: Infer the doctrine from the exact meaning of the slogan.
xs: "Back to the Vedas" held the four Vedas **infallible** — the **primordial word of God** — so option **(4)** is correct.
He **rejected** later **Puranic** accretions (myths, rituals, idol worship), so option (2) is the opposite.
xa: He claimed the Vedas contained **all true knowledge, including science**.
This countered the colonial idea of **Western intellectual superiority**.
The slogan is set out in **Satyarth Prakash** (**1875**, **Hindi**).

190.s: Which of the following was rejected by Dayananda Saraswati as a later accretion rather than part of the original Vedic truth?
190.x: Dayananda rejected later Puranic accretions, including myths, ritualism and idol worship, while supporting rational thought and moral action.
190.tq: Distinguish rejected later accretions from accepted reform principles.
xs: Dayananda rejected **Puranic myths and ritualism** (and idol worship) as later accretions — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Welfare of all**, **rational thought** and **moral action** were part of his **Ten Principles**, not rejected.
xa: He held the **four Vedas** infallible — the **primordial word of God**.
He claimed the Vedas contained all true knowledge, **including science**.
Slogan: **"Back to the Vedas"** ("Go Back to the Vedas").

190.s: Satyarth Prakash was written in which language?
190.x: Dayananda Saraswati wrote Satyarth Prakash in Hindi in 1875.
190.tq: Test the exact language rather than the author, which is a common distractor target.
xs: **Satyarth Prakash** was written in **Hindi** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Dayananda wrote it in **1875** and promoted **Hindi as a link language**.
xa: Title meaning: **"The Light of Truth"** (also "The True Exposition").
Themes: critique of **idolatry**, **caste by birth**, **child marriage**, and of other religions.
Same year **1875**: Arya Samaj founded at **Bombay**.

190.s: The title ‘Satyarth Prakash’ is generally translated as:
190.x: Satyarth Prakash means ‘The Light of Truth’; it is also rendered as ‘The True Exposition’.
190.tq: Choose the precise translation of the title.
xs: **Satyarth Prakash** means **"The Light of Truth"** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is also rendered as **"The True Exposition"**.
xa: Author: **Dayananda Saraswati**, **1875**, in **Hindi**.
It set out his religious and social philosophy and critiqued **Hindu orthodoxy** and other religions.
Its core idea: **"Back to the Vedas"** — Vedas infallible, Puranic accretions rejected.

190.s: Which of the following subjects was NOT a theme of Satyarth Prakash?
o: Critique of idolatry and caste by birth
Religious and social philosophy of Dayananda
190.x: Satyarth Prakash presented Dayananda’s religious and social philosophy and criticised Hindu orthodoxy, idolatry, caste by birth and child marriage.
190.tq: Use the reversal trap involving orthodoxy and reform.
xs: **Advocacy of unquestioned Hindu orthodoxy** was NOT a theme — the book **critiqued** orthodoxy — so option **(4)** is correct.
It did set out his **religious and social philosophy** and attacked **idolatry**, **caste by birth** and **child marriage** — options (1)-(3).
xa: It also critiqued **other religions**.
Written in **Hindi** in **1875**; title means **"The Light of Truth"**.
It rejected the **Puranas'** later accretions — myths, rituals, idol worship.

190.s:
With reference to the Shuddhi movement, consider the following statements:
1. It aimed to reconvert persons who had converted to Islam or Christianity.
2. It also sought to admit outsiders into the Hindu fold.
3. It was initiated by the Brahmo Samaj.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
190.x: Shuddhi was started by Arya Samaj to reconvert converts and admit outsiders into the Hindu fold. It was not initiated by the Brahmo Samaj.
190.tq: Identify the wrong organisation associated with the movement.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: Shuddhi aimed to **reconvert** those who had converted to **Islam or Christianity**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: it also admitted **outsiders** into the Hindu fold.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: Shuddhi was started by the **Arya Samaj**, not the Brahmo Samaj.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: ⚠ "Shuddhi was started by ___" → **Arya Samaj** (not Brahmo Samaj, Satyashodhak Samaj or Ramakrishna Mission).
Later leader: **Swami Shraddhanand**, via the **Bharatiya Hindu Shuddhi Sabha (1923)**.
Impact: contributed to the **communalisation** of social life.

190.s: Who led the Shuddhi campaign of the 1920s through the Bharatiya Hindu Shuddhi Sabha?
190.x: Swami Shraddhanand led the Shuddhi campaign of the 1920s through the Bharatiya Hindu Shuddhi Sabha, formed in 1923.
190.tq: Match the later leader with the specific organisation and campaign.
xs: **Swami Shraddhanand** led the 1920s Shuddhi campaign through the **Bharatiya Hindu Shuddhi Sabha** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The Sabha was formed in **1923**; Shraddhanand was **assassinated in 1926**.
xa: Shuddhi was started by the **Arya Samaj** — ritual "purification" to reconvert converts to **Islam or Christianity**.
Shraddhanand is among the **"militant nationalists"** the Samaj nurtured, with **Lala Lajpat Rai**.
Impact: Shuddhi fed **communal political consciousness**.

190.s: Which of the following statements best describes a later consequence attributed to the Shuddhi movement?
o: It confined itself exclusively to women’s education.
It contributed to communalisation of social life and communal political consciousness.
It ended all communal differences in Indian society.
It rejected all forms of religious reconversion.
190.x: The Shuddhi movement contributed to the communalisation of social life and later communal political consciousness.
190.tq: Select the precise consequence rather than an absolute claim.
xs: Shuddhi **contributed to communalisation of social life** and later **communal political consciousness** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was itself a **reconversion** movement, so option (4) is the opposite of the truth.
xa: Aim: reconvert Hindus who converted to **Islam or Christianity** and admit outsiders.
Criticism: **Shuddhi** plus aggressive attacks on other faiths **sharpened communal divides**.
Leader in the **1920s**: **Swami Shraddhanand** (**Bharatiya Hindu Shuddhi Sabha, 1923**).

190.s: The Arya Samaj satyagraha in Hyderabad State during 1938–39 was directed against:
o: The Nizam’s curbs on religious and civil rights
The educational policies of the Government of India
The abolition of zamindari in coastal Andhra
190.x: In 1938–39, Arya Samaj conducted a satyagraha in Hyderabad State against the Nizam’s restrictions on religious and civil rights.
190.tq: Link the movement, region, period and immediate grievance.
xs: The **1938-39** Hyderabad satyagraha opposed **the Nizam's curbs on religious and civil rights** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was led by the **Arya Samaj** in **Hyderabad State**.
xa: It ran alongside the **Hyderabad State Congress** satyagraha.
Impact: built **political awakening against Nizam rule** in the **Telangana** region.
AP angle: Arya Samaj had great influence on **women's upliftment in Andhra**.

190.s: The Arya Samaj satyagraha in Hyderabad State ran alongside the satyagraha conducted by the:
190.x: The Arya Samaj satyagraha ran alongside the Hyderabad State Congress satyagraha in 1938–39.
190.tq: Identify the parallel organisation rather than a similarly named national body.
xs: The Arya Samaj satyagraha ran alongside the **Hyderabad State Congress** satyagraha — so option **(2)** is correct.
Both were in **1938-39**, against the **Nizam's** curbs on religious and civil rights.
xa: Result: **political awakening against Nizam rule** in the **Telangana** region.
The Samaj's other movement: **Shuddhi** (reconversion), led in the 1920s by **Swami Shraddhanand**.
AP angle: great influence on **women's upliftment in Andhra**.

190.s: One important consequence of Arya Samaj activity in the Telangana region was that it:
o: Ended all political activity in Hyderabad State
Built political awakening against Nizam rule
Strengthened the authority of the Nizam over civil society
190.x: Arya Samaj activity helped build political awakening against Nizam rule in the Telangana region.
190.tq: Select the consequence that follows from the regional political role.
xs: Arya Samaj activity **built political awakening against Nizam rule** in **Telangana** — so option **(2)** is correct.
This came through the **1938-39 satyagraha** against the **Nizam's** curbs on religious and civil rights.
xa: It ran alongside the **Hyderabad State Congress** satyagraha.
The Samaj was strongest in **Punjab**, but was also active in **Hyderabad State**.
AP angle: great influence on **women's upliftment in Andhra**.

190.s: Which of the following correctly captures the dual significance of Arya Samaj?
o: It supported caste by birth and ritualism as essential institutions.
It rejected both Vedic tradition and social reform.
It combined religious revivalism with social reform and contributed to Hindu self-confidence.
It confined itself to literary activity without political influence.
190.x: Arya Samaj combined revivalism with reform, built Hindu self-confidence and contributed to militant nationalism.
190.tq: Choose the balanced statement over extreme descriptions.
xs: The Arya Samaj **combined religious revivalism with social reform** and built **Hindu self-confidence** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It **rejected caste by birth** and ritualism (not option 1) and fed **militant nationalism** (not option 4).
xa: Revivalism: **"Back to the Vedas"** — Vedas infallible.
Reform: opposed **untouchability**, **child marriage**, **purdah**; supported **widow remarriage**.
Criticism: **Shuddhi** and aggressive attacks on other faiths sharpened **communal divides**.

190.s: Which development associated with Arya Samaj was criticised for sharpening communal divisions?
o: Shuddhi and aggressive attacks on other faiths
190.x: Shuddhi and aggressive attacks on other faiths were criticised for sharpening communal divides.
190.tq: Separate reform measures from activities linked to communal tension.
xs: **Shuddhi and aggressive attacks on other faiths** were criticised for sharpening **communal divides** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Women's education, widow remarriage and rational thought were part of its **reform** programme, not the criticism.
xa: Shuddhi: reconversion of those converted to **Islam or Christianity**, started by the **Arya Samaj**.
**Swami Shraddhanand** led it via the **Bharatiya Hindu Shuddhi Sabha (1923)**.
It contributed to the **communalisation of social life**.

190.s: The International Aryan Summit 2025 in New Delhi was associated with which combination of commemorations?
o: 75th birth anniversary of Dayananda and 100 years of Arya Samaj
200th birth anniversary of Dayananda and 150 years of Arya Samaj
150th birth anniversary of Dayananda and 200 years of Arya Samaj
100th birth anniversary of Dayananda and 75 years of Arya Samaj
190.x: The 2025 International Aryan Summit, also associated with the Jnana Jyoti Festival or International Arya Mahasammelan, marked Dayananda’s 200th birth anniversary and 150 years of Arya Samaj.
190.tq: Keep the two commemorative numbers in their correct order.
xs: The **International Aryan Summit 2025** marked the **200th birth anniversary of Dayananda** and **150 years of Arya Samaj** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Dayananda was born in **1824**; the Arya Samaj was founded in **1875**.
xa: The summit, in **New Delhi** (Nov **2025**), is also called the **Jnana Jyoti Festival** / **International Arya Mahasammelan**.
Arya Samaj was founded at **Bombay**, April **1875**.
Dayananda died at **Ajmer** in **1883**.

191.s: Ramakrishna Paramahansa was associated as a mystic and priest with the:
191.x: Ramakrishna Paramahansa served as a mystic and priest at the Dakshineswar Kali Temple near Calcutta.
191.tq: Identify the religious figure through his principal place of association.
xs: Ramakrishna Paramahansa was a mystic and priest of the **Kali Temple at Dakshineswar**, near Calcutta — so option **(4)** is correct.
xa: Original name: **Gadadhar Chattopadhyaya**; wife: **Sarada Devi**.
Gurus: **Bhairavi Brahmani** (Tantra) and **Totapuri** (Advaita).
His saying **"as many faiths, so many paths"** — all religions lead to the same truth.

191.s: What was the original name of Ramakrishna Paramahansa?
191.x: Ramakrishna Paramahansa was born as Gadadhar Chattopadhyaya.
191.tq: Separate the original names of closely associated nineteenth-century religious figures.
xs: Ramakrishna was born **Gadadhar Chattopadhyaya** — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ **Narendranath Datta** = Vivekananda; **Mool Shankar** = Dayanand Saraswati; **Munshi Ram** = Swami Shraddhanand.
xa: Ramakrishna (**1836-1886**) was priest of the **Dakshineswar Kali Temple**.
His wife was **Sarada Devi**.
His chief disciple **Vivekananda** named the **Ramakrishna Mission** (**1897**) after him.

191.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
191.x: Bhairavi Brahmani instructed Ramakrishna in Tantra, while Totapuri was his teacher in Advaita. Sarada Devi was his wife.
191.tq: Start from the sure teacher–school pair and eliminate the swapped associations.
xs: **Bhairavi Brahmani** taught Ramakrishna **Tantra** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Totapuri** taught him **Advaita**, not Tantra; so options (1) and (2) swap the pairs.
**Sarada Devi** was his **wife**, not an Advaita guru.
xa: Ramakrishna's original name: **Gadadhar Chattopadhyaya**.
He was a mystic at the **Dakshineswar Kali Temple** near Calcutta.
Teaching: salvation through **devotion, meditation, renunciation**.

191.s: Who was the wife of Ramakrishna Paramahansa?
191.x: Sarada Devi was the wife of Ramakrishna Paramahansa.
191.tq: Directly identify the associated family relationship.
xs: Ramakrishna's wife was **Sarada Devi** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Margaret Noble** (**Sister Nivedita**) was Vivekananda's Western disciple; **Annie Besant** led the Theosophical Society.
xa: Ramakrishna's gurus: **Bhairavi Brahmani** (Tantra) and **Totapuri** (Advaita).
He lived **1836-1886**, at the **Dakshineswar Kali Temple**.
⚠ Options (1) and (4) are the same person — Margaret Noble = Sister Nivedita.

191.s:
Consider the following statements about the teachings of Ramakrishna Paramahansa:
1. His saying 'as many faiths, so many paths' expresses the belief that all religions lead to the same truth.
2. He held that salvation could be pursued through devotion, meditation and renunciation.
3. He held that salvation was possible only through renunciation and never through devotion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
191.x: Statement 1 is correct: 'as many faiths, so many paths' means all religions lead to the same truth. Statement 2 is correct: he named devotion, meditation and renunciation as paths to salvation. Statement 3 is wrong: devotion was itself one of the paths, not excluded. So '1 only' misses 2, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include 3.
191.tq: Ramakrishna = universalism; words like 'only' or 'never' clash with 'as many faiths, so many paths'.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **"as many faiths, so many paths"** means all religions lead to the **same truth**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: salvation through **devotion, meditation, renunciation**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: **devotion** was itself one of the paths.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(3)** is correct.
xa: Vivekananda's **Practical Vedanta**: serving the poor = serving God (**"Daridra Narayana"**).
RKM motto: **"Atmano Mokshartham Jagat Hitaya Cha"** — for one's own liberation and the welfare of the world.

191.s:
Consider the following statements about Swami Vivekananda:
1. His original name was Narendranath Datta.
2. He was born in Calcutta on 12 January 1863.
3. He was the chief disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa.
4. He was born as Gadadhar Chattopadhyaya.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
191.x: Vivekananda was born Narendranath Datta in Calcutta on 12 January 1863 and became Ramakrishna’s chief disciple. Gadadhar Chattopadhyaya was the birth name of Ramakrishna, not Vivekananda.
191.tq: Use the look-alike personal-name trap to separate the disciple’s name from the guru’s birth name.
xs: Statements 1, 2, 3 are **correct**: born **Narendranath Datta**, **Calcutta**, **12 January 1863**; chief disciple of **Ramakrishna**.
Statement 4 is **wrong**: **Gadadhar Chattopadhyaya** was Ramakrishna's birth name.
So **1, 2 and 3 only** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: Vivekananda died in **1902**.
His birthday, **12 January**, is **National Youth Day**.
Titles: **"Prophet of Indian Nationalism"**, **"Maker of Modern India"**.

191.s: Swami Vivekananda’s birthday is observed in India as:
191.x: 12 January, the birthday of Swami Vivekananda, is observed as National Youth Day.
191.tq: Link the precise date-based observance with the correct national day.
xs: Vivekananda's birthday, **12 January**, is observed as **National Youth Day** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was born **Narendranath Datta** in **Calcutta** in **1863**.
xa: His ideas stressed **strength, self-confidence, youth** for national regeneration.
Titles: **"Prophet of Indian Nationalism"** and **"Maker of Modern India"**.
He died in **1902**.

191.s:
Swami Vivekananda is described by which of the following titles?
1. Prophet of Indian Nationalism
2. Maker of Modern India
3. Father of the Indian Constitution
4. Grand Old Man of India
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
191.x: Vivekananda is described as the ‘Prophet of Indian Nationalism’ and the ‘Maker of Modern India’. The other titles refer to different personalities.
191.tq: Separate attributed titles from famous titles belonging to other national figures.
xs: Vivekananda is called the **"Prophet of Indian Nationalism"** and **"Maker of Modern India"** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
The other two titles belong to other personalities, not Vivekananda.
xa: His Western disciple: **Margaret Noble (Sister Nivedita)**.
He set up **Vedanta Societies** in the **USA and Britain** — **Vedanta Society of New York (1894)**.
He made **humanitarian relief** a monastic duty.

191.s:
Arrange the following events associated with Vivekananda and the institutions connected with him in chronological order:
A. Founding of the Vedanta Society of New York
B. Establishment of Belur Math
C. Birth of Vivekananda
D. Death of Vivekananda
191.x: Vivekananda was born in 1863, founded the Vedanta Society of New York in 1894, Belur Math was established in 1898, and he died in 1902.
191.tq: Fix the sequence by placing the dated personal event first and the two institutions before the death date.
xs: Order: **C, A, B, D** — option **(1)** is correct.
Birth **1863** → **Vedanta Society of New York 1894** → **Belur Math 1898** → death **1902**.
xa: **Chicago** Parliament of Religions: **1893**.
**Ramakrishna Mission**: **1 May 1897**, soon after his return from the West.
⚠ **1898** twice: **Belur Math** and Besant's **Central Hindu College**.

191.s:
Match the participants at the Chicago Parliament of Religions with their affiliations.
List-I (Participant)
a. P.C. Mozoomdar
b. Virchand Gandhi
c. Anagarika Dharmapala
 d. Swami Vivekananda
List-II (Affiliation)
i. Buddhism, Ceylon
ii. Hinduism
iii. Jainism
iv. Brahmo Samaj
Options:
191.x: P.C. Mozoomdar was associated with the Brahmo Samaj, Virchand Gandhi with Jainism, Anagarika Dharmapala with Buddhism from Ceylon, and Vivekananda with Hinduism.
191.tq: Begin with the distinctive Ceylon–Buddhism pair and then match the remaining religious affiliations.
xs: Correct match: **a–iv, b–iii, c–i, d–ii** — option **(1)**.
**P.C. Mozoomdar** – **Brahmo Samaj**; **Virchand Gandhi** – **Jain**; **Anagarika Dharmapala** – **Buddhist, Ceylon**; **Vivekananda** – **Hinduism**.
xa: The event: **World's Parliament of Religions, Chicago, 1893**.
Vivekananda opened with **"Sisters and Brothers of America"** on **11 Sep 1893**.
Before Chicago he meditated on the **Kanyakumari** rock (**Dec 1892**).

191.s: Swami Vivekananda’s opening words at the Chicago Parliament of Religions were:
191.x: Vivekananda began his address with ‘Sisters and Brothers of America’, which received wide acclaim.
191.tq: Recall the exact famous opening phrase instead of a synonymous greeting.
xs: His opening words were **"Sisters and Brothers of America"** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Delivered at the **World's Parliament of Religions, Chicago**, on **11 Sep 1893**; it won wide acclaim.
xa: He represented **Hinduism** there.
Other participants: **P.C. Mozoomdar** (Brahmo Samaj), **Virchand Gandhi** (Jain), **Anagarika Dharmapala** (Buddhist, Ceylon).
In **Feb 1893** he spoke at **Mahboob College, Secunderabad**.

191.s: The address beginning with ‘Sisters and Brothers of America’ was delivered by Swami Vivekananda on:
191.x: Vivekananda delivered the famous opening address on 11 September 1893 at the Chicago Parliament of Religions.
191.tq: Separate the event date from Vivekananda’s birth, Mission-foundation and death dates.
xs: The address was delivered on **11 September 1893** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**12 January 1863** is his birth; **1 May 1897** is the founding of the **Ramakrishna Mission**.
xa: Venue: **World's Parliament of Religions, Chicago**.
He returned in **1897** via **Colombo, Ramnad, Madras** — **Lectures from Colombo to Almora**.
**Vedanta Society of New York**: **1894**.

191.s: Swami Vivekananda established Vedanta Societies in:
191.x: Vivekananda established Vedanta Societies in the United States of America and Britain.
191.tq: Recall the two-country institutional association given for the reformer.
xs: Vivekananda set up Vedanta Societies in **the USA and Britain** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The first was the **Vedanta Society of New York** (**1894**).
xa: He spoke at **Chicago** in **1893**, representing **Hinduism**.
His Western disciple: **Margaret Noble (Sister Nivedita)**.
On return he founded the **Ramakrishna Mission** (**1897**).

191.s:
Arrange the following events associated with Swami Vivekananda in chronological order:
A. Meditation on the Kanyakumari rock
B. Address at the World’s Parliament of Religions
C. Speech at Mahboob College, Secunderabad
D. Return through Colombo, Ramnad and Madras
191.x: Vivekananda meditated at Kanyakumari in December 1892, spoke at Secunderabad in February 1893, addressed the Chicago Parliament in 1893, and returned through the southern route in 1897.
191.tq: Fix the first and last events, then arrange the two intervening 1893 events.
xs: Order: **A, C, B, D** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Kanyakumari** rock (**Dec 1892**) → **Mahboob College, Secunderabad** (**Feb 1893**) → **Chicago** (**11 Sep 1893**) → return via **Colombo, Ramnad, Madras** (**1897**).
xa: The return speeches form **Lectures from Colombo to Almora**.
**Ramakrishna Mission** founded **1 May 1897**, soon after the return.

191.s: At which of the following places did Swami Vivekananda speak in February 1893?
191.x: Swami Vivekananda spoke at Mahboob College in Secunderabad in February 1893.
191.tq: Match the speaker with the specific South Indian venue.
xs: In **February 1893** Vivekananda spoke at **Mahboob College, Secunderabad** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Dakshineswar** was Ramakrishna's temple; **BT College, Madanapalle** dates from **1916**; **Gurukul Kangri** from **1902**.
xa: Before that he meditated on the **Kanyakumari** rock (**Dec 1892**).
Later that year: **Chicago** Parliament of Religions (**1893**).
⚠ **Gurukul Kangri, Haridwar** = Arya Samaj **Gurukul party** (Shraddhanand).

191.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
191.x: My Master was written by Swami Vivekananda. Annie Besant is not its author.
191.tq: Find the swapped author among otherwise correctly matched books and authors.
xs: **My Master — Annie Besant** is wrongly matched; **My Master** is by **Vivekananda** — so option **(4)** is the answer.
**The Secret Doctrine** is by **Blavatsky**; **Karma Yoga** and **Raja Yoga** are by **Vivekananda** — correctly matched.
xa: Vivekananda also wrote **Jnana Yoga** and **Lectures from Colombo to Almora**.
Besant's papers: **New India** and **Commonweal**.
Blavatsky's other book: **Isis Unveiled**; Krishnamurti wrote **At the Feet of the Master** (**1910**).

191.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the social ideas of Swami Vivekananda:
1. He condemned caste-based discrimination.
2. He regarded humanitarian relief as a monastic duty.
3. He supported empty ritual as the basis of national regeneration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
191.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Vivekananda condemned empty ritual, so statement 3 is false.
191.tq: Split the options by testing the reformer's positive and negative positions separately.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: Vivekananda **condemned caste**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: he made **humanitarian relief a monastic duty**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: he **condemned empty ritual**.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: He stressed **strength, self-confidence, youth** for national regeneration.
**Practical Vedanta**: serving the poor = serving God (**"Daridra Narayana"**).

191.s: Who among the following was the Western disciple of Swami Vivekananda known as Sister Nivedita?
191.x: Margaret Noble became the well-known Western disciple of Vivekananda under the name Sister Nivedita.
191.tq: Match the adopted religious name with the original personal name.
xs: **Margaret Noble** was Vivekananda's Western disciple, known as **Sister Nivedita** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Blavatsky** co-founded the Theosophical Society; **Annie Besant** led it; **Sarada Devi** was Ramakrishna's wife.
xa: Vivekananda set up **Vedanta Societies** in the **USA and Britain** (New York, **1894**).
Titles: **"Prophet of Indian Nationalism"**, **"Maker of Modern India"**.
Born **Narendranath Datta** (**1863**); died **1902**.

191.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the two journals associated with the Ramakrishna movement?
o: Prabuddha Bharata was in English and Udbodhan was in Bengali
Prabuddha Bharata was in Bengali and Udbodhan was in English
Both Prabuddha Bharata and Udbodhan were in English
Both Prabuddha Bharata and Udbodhan were in Bengali
191.x: Prabuddha Bharata was an English journal, whereas Udbodhan was published in Bengali.
191.tq: Discriminate between two similar entries by pairing each with its language.
xs: **Prabuddha Bharata** was in **English** and **Udbodhan** in **Bengali** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Both journals are associated with **Vivekananda**.
xa: ⚠ Classic swap trap: **Prabuddha Bharata = English**; **Udbodhan = Bengali**.
Vivekananda's books: **Karma Yoga**, **Raja Yoga**, **Jnana Yoga**, **My Master**.
Besant's papers, by contrast: **New India** and **Commonweal**.

191.s: Lectures from Colombo to Almora is associated with speeches delivered by Swami Vivekananda after his return in 1897 through:
191.x: The work is based on speeches delivered after Vivekananda’s 1897 return through Colombo, Ramnad and Madras.
191.tq: Identify the correct travel route attached to a published work.
xs: **Lectures from Colombo to Almora** are speeches after his **1897** return via **Colombo, Ramnad and Madras** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He had been in the West since the **Chicago** Parliament of **1893**.
xa: Soon after this return he founded the **Ramakrishna Mission** (**1 May 1897**).
His journals: **Prabuddha Bharata** (English) and **Udbodhan** (Bengali).
Other works: **Karma Yoga**, **Raja Yoga**, **Jnana Yoga**, **My Master**.

191.s: Ramakrishna Mission has its headquarters at which of the following places?
o: Belur Math on the Hooghly near Howrah
191.x: The headquarters of the Ramakrishna Mission is at Belur Math, situated on the Hooghly near Howrah.
191.tq: Use the location clue to distinguish the headquarters from the founder’s temple and other reform institutions.
xs: The RKM headquarters is **Belur Math on the Hooghly near Howrah** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Adyar** is the Theosophical Society's Indian HQ; **Dakshineswar** was Ramakrishna's temple; the **Central Hindu College** was Besant's.
xa: **Belur Math** was established in **1898**; permanent HQ of the **Ramakrishna Order**.
Its architecture blends **Hindu, Islamic and Christian** motifs → unity of religions.
**Ramakrishna Mission** founded **1 May 1897** at **Belur (Howrah)**.

191.s: The motto of the Ramakrishna Mission, ‘Atmano Mokshartham Jagat Hitaya Cha’, signifies:
o: For one’s own liberation and the welfare of the world
191.x: The motto means ‘for one’s own liberation and the welfare of the world’.
191.tq: Test the exact meaning of a distinctive institutional motto rather than its general theme.
xs: **"Atmano Mokshartham Jagat Hitaya Cha"** means **for one's own liberation and the welfare of the world** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Universal brotherhood** and comparative religion were **Theosophical** aims, not this motto.
xa: RKM's **Practical Vedanta**: **"Service to mankind is service to God"**.
**Daridra narayana** = God in the poor.
⚠ **"Back to the Vedas"** = Arya Samaj slogan, not RKM.

191.s:
Which of the following activities is associated with the practical work of the Ramakrishna Mission?
1. Running schools and colleges
2. Operating hospitals and orphanages
3. Providing famine and disaster relief
4. Promoting exclusively ritualistic worship
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
191.x: The Mission runs educational and medical institutions, orphanages and relief programmes. Its work is not exclusively ritualistic.
191.tq: Find the one extreme and incompatible statement among several practical-service activities.
xs: The Mission runs **schools and colleges**, **hospitals and orphanages**, and **famine and disaster relief** — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(1)**.
It is not exclusively ritualistic: it combines **renunciation** with **practical spirituality**.
xa: Two wings: a **monastic order** and **lay disciples** doing preaching, philanthropy, humanitarian work.
Vivekananda made **humanitarian relief** a monastic duty.
Current: RKM's **Vivekananda Human Excellence Centre**, **Vijayawada** (**₹8.5 crore**), inaugurated **1 Feb 2026**.

191.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the two broad components of the Ramakrishna Mission’s work?
o: A political party and a constitutional body engaged in legislative reform
A literary society and an educational department of the colonial government
A missionary organisation devoted exclusively to conversion and a trading corporation
A monastic order devoted to renunciation and practical spirituality, and lay disciples engaged in preaching and humanitarian work
191.x: The Mission combines a monastic order devoted to renunciation and practical spirituality with lay work involving preaching, philanthropy and humanitarian service.
191.tq: Compare the two institutional components and reject options that impose an exclusive or unrelated purpose.
xs: The Mission has **a monastic order devoted to renunciation and practical spirituality** and **lay disciples** doing **preaching and humanitarian work** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Lay disciples also carry out **philanthropy**.
xa: Works: **schools, colleges, hospitals, orphanages**; **famine and disaster relief**.
Motto: **"Atmano Mokshartham Jagat Hitaya Cha"**.
Comparative: **RKM = service and universalism**; Arya Samaj = revivalist; Theosophy = foreign-founded Hindu revival.

191.s: The expression ‘daridra narayana’, associated with the practical Vedanta of the Ramakrishna Mission, refers to:
191.x: ‘Daridra narayana’ expresses the idea that service to the poor is service to God.
191.tq: Discriminate between a service-oriented expression and the philosophical doctrines of the Theosophical Society.
xs: **Daridra narayana** means **God manifest in the poor** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It underlies **Practical Vedanta**: **"Service to mankind is service to God"**.
xa: Vivekananda: serving the poor = **serving God**.
⚠ **Rebirth** and **study of ancient religions** are Theosophical beliefs, not this idea.
RKM motto: **"for one's own liberation and the welfare of the world"**.

191.s: The architecture of Belur Math symbolically combines which of the following traditions?
191.x: Belur Math blends Hindu, Islamic and Christian architectural motifs to express the unity of religions.
191.tq: Recall a distinctive three-part cultural combination.
xs: **Belur Math** blends **Hindu, Islamic and Christian** motifs — so option **(2)** is correct.
The blend expresses the **unity of religions**.
xa: **Belur Math** (est. **1898**) on the **Hooghly**, Howrah = permanent HQ of the **Ramakrishna Order**.
It echoes Ramakrishna's **"as many faiths, so many paths"**.
⚠ **1898** also = Besant's **Central Hindu College, Benaras**.

191.s: In which year did Swami Vivekananda found the Ramakrishna Mission?
191.x: Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission on 1 May 1897, soon after returning from the West, and named it after his guru. 1879 is a common wrong version of 1897; 1875 is the founding year of the Arya Samaj and the Theosophical Society; 1902 is the year Vivekananda died.
191.tq: RKM = 1 May 1897, not 1879; Belur Math HQ came in 1898.
xs: Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission in **1897** (**1 May 1897**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1879** is the classic wrong version; **1875** = Arya Samaj and Theosophical Society; **1902** = Vivekananda's death.
xa: He founded it soon after returning from the West and **named it after his guru**.
Place: **Belur (Howrah)**; **Belur Math** followed in **1898**.
⚠ "Founded the Ramakrishna Mission in **1879**" is a WRONG statement.

191.s:
With reference to the Theosophical Society, consider the following statements:
1. Its Indian headquarters is at Adyar.
2. The headquarters was shifted to Adyar in 1882.
3. Its original headquarters was established at Madras in 1875.
4. Its major beliefs included karma and reincarnation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
191.x: Adyar became the Indian headquarters in 1882, and karma and reincarnation were among the Society’s beliefs. The Society was originally founded at New York, not Madras.
191.tq: Spot the location reversal between the original foundation and the later Indian headquarters.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are **correct**: Indian HQ at **Adyar**, Madras, moved in **1882**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: it was founded at **New York** in **1875**, not Madras.
Statement 4 is **correct**: it believed in **karma and reincarnation**.
So **1, 2 and 4 only** — option **(2)** is correct.
xa: Founders: **Madame H.P. Blavatsky** (Russian) and **Col. H.S. Olcott** (American).
⚠ **1875** twice: **Arya Samaj (Bombay)** and **Theosophical Society (New York)**.

191.s: Which of the following was NOT a belief or objective associated with the Theosophical Society?
o: Exclusive propagation of one revealed religion
Study of ancient religions and philosophical traditions
191.x: The Theosophical Society promoted universal brotherhood and comparative study of religions; it did not advocate the exclusive propagation of one revealed religion.
191.tq: Reject the exclusive formulation when the organisation’s defining principle is comparative and universal.
xs: **Exclusive propagation of one revealed religion** was NOT a Theosophical aim — so option **(3)** is correct.
Its aims were **universal brotherhood** and **comparative religion / study of ancient religions**.
xa: Beliefs: **karma and reincarnation**.
It drew on the **Upanishads, Samkhya, Yoga, Vedanta**.
Social stand: condemned **child marriage**; upliftment of **outcastes and widows**.

191.s:
With reference to the Theosophical Society, consider the following statements:
1. It drew upon the Upanishads, Samkhya, Yoga and Vedanta.
2. It condemned child marriage and worked for the uplift of outcastes and widows.
3. It rejected the doctrines of karma and reincarnation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
191.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Society drew on the Upanishads, Samkhya, Yoga and Vedanta. Statement 2 is correct: it condemned child marriage and worked for outcastes and widows. Statement 3 is wrong: karma and reincarnation were among its core beliefs. So '1 only' misses statement 2, '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include statement 3.
191.tq: Theosophy = Hindu revival: it accepted karma and rebirth, so any statement that it rejected them is false.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: it drew on the **Upanishads, Samkhya, Yoga and Vedanta**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: it condemned **child marriage** and worked for **outcastes and widows**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: **karma and reincarnation** were core beliefs.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)** is correct.
xa: Aims: **universal brotherhood**; comparative religion.
Theosophy led straight into **Home Rule** politics.

191.s: The Telugu name of the Theosophical Society is:
191.x: The Theosophical Society is known in Telugu as Divya Gnana Samajam.
191.tq: Test the exact regional-language equivalent of a well-known organisation.
xs: The Theosophical Society's Telugu name is **Divya Gnana Samajam** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Its Indian HQ at **Adyar (Madras)** put Andhra in the Society's **core area**.
xa: **Krishna Divyajnana Lodge** set up the first public library in **Guntur** district (**1882**).
**Madanapalle** = Theosophy's Andhra centre (**BT College**, **1916**).
**Veeresalingam** set up the **first Theosophical High School** in Andhra.

191.s: The Theosophical Society was founded in 1875 by:
o: Madame H.P. Blavatsky and Col. H.S. Olcott
Annie Besant and Madan Mohan Malaviya
Swami Dayanand Saraswati and Col. H.S. Olcott
191.x: The Theosophical Society was founded at New York in 1875 by the Russian Madame H.P. Blavatsky and the American Col. H.S. Olcott. Annie Besant joined only in 1889 and became President in 1907; Malaviya worked with her on the Central Hindu College; Jiddu Krishnamurti was her adopted son; Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj.
191.tq: Theosophy founders = Blavatsky (Russian) + Olcott (American), New York 1875.
xs: The Theosophical Society was founded by **Madame H.P. Blavatsky** (Russian) and **Col. H.S. Olcott** (American) — option **(1)**.
It was founded at **New York** in **1875**.
**Annie Besant** joined in **1889**; **Malaviya** worked with her on BHU; **Krishnamurti** was her adopted son; **Dayanand** founded the Arya Samaj.
xa: Indian HQ moved to **Adyar, Madras** in **1882**.
Besant became President after Olcott's death (**1907**).
Blavatsky's books: **Isis Unveiled**, **The Secret Doctrine**.

191.s: The Central Hindu College at Benaras later became the nucleus of which institution?
191.x: The Central Hindu College founded by Annie Besant became the nucleus of Banaras Hindu University in 1916, with Madan Mohan Malaviya.
191.tq: Distinguish an institutional precursor from similarly prominent universities.
xs: The **Central Hindu College** became the nucleus of **Banaras Hindu University** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Besant founded it in **1898**; it became **BHU** in **1916** with **Madan Mohan Malaviya**.
xa: ⚠ **1916** twice: **BHU** and **BT College, Madanapalle**.
⚠ **1898** twice: **Central Hindu College** and **Belur Math**.
APPSC-GS **2025**: "Along with Malaviya, founder of Benaras Hindu College" → **Annie Besant**.

191.s: Which of the following statements about the Besant Theosophical College is correct?
o: It was founded at Lahore in 1886 and its first Principal was Hansraj.
It was founded at Haridwar in 1902 and its first Principal was Swami Shraddhanand.
It was founded at Adyar in 1882 and its first Principal was H.S. Olcott.
It was founded at Madanapalle in 1916 and its first Principal was H.J. Cousins.
191.x: The Besant Theosophical College was founded by Annie Besant at Madanapalle in 1916; H.J. Cousins was its first Principal.
191.tq: Use the founder, location, year and first office-holder together to defeat swapped institutional details.
xs: **BT College** was founded at **Madanapalle** in **1916**; first Principal **H.J. Cousins** — option **(4)**.
**Lahore 1886** = first **DAV School**; **Haridwar 1902** = **Gurukul Kangri**; **Adyar 1882** = Theosophical HQ.
xa: Founder: **Annie Besant**; also called **Besant Theosophical (National) College**.
There **Rabindranath Tagore** translated **Jana Gana Mana** as **"Morning Song of India"** at Cousins' request.
**Madanapalle** = Theosophy's Andhra centre.

191.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Annie Besant is correct?
o: She came to India in 1882 and became President in 1893.
She joined the Society in 1907 and became President in 1916.
She founded the Society at New York in 1875 and became President in 1882.
She came to India in 1893 and became President of the Theosophical Society in 1907.
191.x: Annie Besant came to India in 1893 and became President of the Theosophical Society in 1907 after the death of Olcott.
191.tq: Separate the dates of joining, arrival in India and assumption of the presidency.
xs: Annie Besant **came to India in 1893** and **became President in 1907** — so option **(4)** is correct.
She **joined** the Society in **1889**; became President after **Olcott's** death.
xa: ⚠ **1889** joined; **1893** came to India; **1907** President; **1916** Home Rule League; **1917** INC President.
**1882** = HQ moved to **Adyar**; **1875** = founding at **New York** by Blavatsky and Olcott.

191.s:
Which of the following statements about Annie Besant is correct?
1. She became the first woman President of the Indian National Congress at Calcutta in 1917.
2. She launched the Home Rule movement in 1916.
3. She was associated with the papers New India and Commonweal.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
191.x: All three statements are correct. Annie Besant was associated with Home Rule in 1916, the papers New India and Commonweal, and the 1917 Calcutta Congress presidency.
191.tq: Combine a leader’s political role, publications and organisational activity.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: first woman **INC President**, **Calcutta 1917**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **Home Rule League (1916)** (one note says 1915).
Statement 3 is **correct**: papers **New India** and **Commonweal**.
So **1, 2 and 3** — option **(4)** is correct.
xa: Andhra Home Rule workers: **Konda Venkatappayya**, **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**, **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** (Secretary).
She founded **Central Hindu College** (**1898**) and **BT College, Madanapalle** (**1916**).

191.s: Who, along with Madan Mohan Malaviya, is regarded as a founder of the Central Hindu College at Benaras?
191.x: Annie Besant founded the Central Hindu College at Benaras in 1898; with Madan Mohan Malaviya it became the nucleus of Banaras Hindu University (1916). Olcott co-founded the Theosophical Society, Sister Nivedita was Vivekananda's disciple, and Shraddhanand led the Gurukul party of the Arya Samaj.
191.tq: Benaras Hindu College + Malaviya -> Annie Besant (APPSC-GS 2025).
xs: **Annie Besant** founded the **Central Hindu College** (**1898**), which with **Malaviya** became BHU — option **(1)**.
**Olcott** co-founded the Theosophical Society; **Sister Nivedita** was Vivekananda's disciple; **Shraddhanand** led the Gurukul party.
xa: APPSC-GS **2025** asked exactly this: answer **Annie Besant**.
Besant's adopted son: **Jiddu Krishnamurti** (**At the Feet of the Master**, **1910**).

191.s: Jiddu Krishnamurti, the adopted son of Annie Besant, wrote:
o: At the Feet of the Master
191.x: Jiddu Krishnamurti, adopted by Annie Besant, wrote At the Feet of the Master (1910). Isis Unveiled and The Secret Doctrine are by H.P. Blavatsky; My Master is by Swami Vivekananda.
191.tq: Krishnamurti = At the Feet of the Master; Blavatsky = Isis Unveiled, Secret Doctrine.
xs: **Jiddu Krishnamurti** wrote **At the Feet of the Master** (**1910**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Isis Unveiled** and **The Secret Doctrine** are by **Blavatsky**; **My Master** is by **Vivekananda**.
xa: Krishnamurti was **Annie Besant's adopted son**.
Besant's papers: **New India**, **Commonweal**.
Vivekananda's journals: **Prabuddha Bharata** (English), **Udbodhan** (Bengali).

191.s: At Madanapalle, Rabindranath Tagore translated ‘Jana Gana Mana’ into English under which title?
191.x: Tagore translated ‘Jana Gana Mana’ into English at Madanapalle as ‘Morning Song of India’.
191.tq: Test the exact translated title rather than a plausible descriptive substitute.
xs: Tagore translated **Jana Gana Mana** into English as **"Morning Song of India"** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He did so at **BT College, Madanapalle**, at **H.J. Cousins'** request.
xa: **BT College** was founded by **Annie Besant** in **1916**; Cousins was first Principal.
**Madanapalle** = Theosophy's Andhra centre.
Other AP Theosophy link: **Krishna Divyajnana Lodge** library, **Guntur** (**1882**).

191.s: The Adyar headquarters of the Theosophical Society was important in Andhra because it:
o: Transferred the Arya Samaj headquarters to Andhra
Excluded Andhra from the Society’s activities
Placed Andhra within the Society’s core area
191.x: The Adyar headquarters placed Andhra within the core area of the Theosophical Society.
191.tq: Identify the institutional effect of a regional headquarters.
xs: The **Adyar (Madras)** HQ **placed Andhra within the Society's core area** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Besant's **New India**, **Commonweal** and her **Madras Home Rule League (1916)** reached Andhra.
xa: HQ moved to **Adyar** in **1882**.
Telugu name of the Society: **Divya Gnana Samajam**.
**Veeresalingam** set up the **first Theosophical High School** in Andhra.

191.s: Which of the following publications of Annie Besant reached Andhra and helped spread Home Rule ideas?
191.x: Annie Besant’s New India and Commonweal reached Andhra, along with the activities of her Madras Home Rule League.
191.tq: Discriminate between reform and nationalist journals by their editor and context.
xs: Besant's **New India and Commonweal** reached Andhra — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Prabuddha Bharata** and **Udbodhan** were **Vivekananda's** journals.
xa: Her **Madras Home Rule League (1916)** also reached Andhra.
Andhra Home Rule Secretary: **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao**.
