193.s: Which one of the following was NOT a characteristic practice of the Kuka or Namdhari followers?
193.x: Kuka followers rejected Brahmin-led rituals. They commonly wore white clothes, abstained from meat and carried a lathi.
193.tq: Find the practice that conflicts with the reform movement's stated principles.
xs: **Performing Brahmin-led rituals** was NOT a Kuka practice — they **rejected** them — so option **(4)** is correct.
Kukas wore **white clothes**, gave up **meat** and carried a **lathi** — options (1)-(3).
xa: They also rejected **idol worship** and worship of **tombs, trees and snakes**.
They revived **Guru Gobind Singh's Khalsa** ceremonies.
Region: **Punjab**; centre **Bhaini, Ludhiana**.

193.s:
Consider the following statements about the methods adopted by the Kuka movement:
1. It boycotted British goods.
2. It boycotted English education.
3. It rejected British law courts and the postal system.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
193.x: The Kuka movement advocated boycott of British goods, English education, law courts and the postal system. Therefore, all three statements are correct.
193.tq: Combine several connected boycott measures and check whether any item is outside the list.
xs: The Kukas boycotted **British goods**, **English education**, **law courts** and the **postal system** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
Hence **Satguru Ram Singh** is called the **first to use boycott and non-cooperation** against British rule.
xa: The Kuka boycott **anticipated Swadeshi and non-cooperation**.
Suppression: after the **1872 Malerkotla** clash, dozens **blown from cannons**.
APPSC **2025** asked Ram Singh as first to use non-cooperation and boycott.

193.s: Who is regarded as the first to use non-cooperation and boycott as a political weapon against British rule?
193.x: Satguru Ram Singh is regarded as the first to use boycott and non-cooperation against British rule as political weapons.
193.tq: Identify the person associated with a distinctive political method.
xs: **Satguru Ram Singh** was the first to use **non-cooperation and boycott** as a political weapon — option **(4)** (APPSC **2025**).
**Malabari** was a Parsi reformer; **Bhagat Jawahar Mal** only began the Kuka movement; **Jhabbar** led the **Akalis**.
xa: He organised the **Namdhari** movement in **1857**.
He was **deported to Rangoon (Burma)**.
The Kuka boycott anticipated **Swadeshi** and **non-cooperation**.

193.s: Which of the following correctly describes the British suppression of the Kukas after the Malerkotla clash?
o: They were executed at Nankana Sahib and Ram Singh retired to Amritsar.
Dozens were blown from cannons and Ram Singh was deported to Rangoon.
They were sent to the Andaman Islands and Ram Singh remained in Punjab.
They were imprisoned at Lahore and Ram Singh was deported to London.
193.x: After the 1872 Malerkotla clash, dozens of Kukas were blown from cannons and Ram Singh was deported to Rangoon in Burma.
193.tq: Match the punishment with the correct leader and location.
xs: After **Malerkotla**, **dozens were blown from cannons** and **Ram Singh was deported to Rangoon** — option **(2)**.
The clash was in **1872**; Rangoon is in **Burma**.
xa: ⚠ **Nankana Sahib** (**1921**) is an **Akali** flashpoint, not Kuka.
Kukas boycotted **British goods**, **English education**, **law courts**, **postal system**.
Practices: **white clothes**, no meat, a **lathi**.

193.s: The principal objective of the Akali or Gurdwara Reform Movement of 1920–25 was to:
o: Establish English education in Punjab courts
Free gurdwaras from corrupt Udasi mahants
Revive worship of trees and snakes
193.x: The Akali movement sought to free Sikh gurdwaras from corrupt Udasi mahants. It was led by figures including Kartar Singh Jhabbar.
193.tq: Identify the institutional grievance that gave rise to the movement.
xs: The Akali movement aimed to **free gurdwaras from corrupt Udasi mahants** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was led by **Kartar Singh Jhabbar** (**1920-25**).
xa: It later became a political party — the **Akali Dal**.
**SGPC** formed **1920**.
Flashpoints: **Nankana Sahib (1921)**, **Guru-ka-Bagh (1922)**.

193.s: Who was a leader of the Akali or Gurdwara Reform Movement?
193.x: Kartar Singh Jhabbar was a leader of the Akali or Gurdwara Reform Movement during 1920–25.
193.tq: Avoid swapping leaders among contemporary religious and social reform bodies.
xs: **Kartar Singh Jhabbar** led the **Akali (Gurdwara Reform) Movement** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Dadabhai Naoroji** = Parsi Sabha; **Agnihotri** = **Dev Samaj**; **Radhakant Deb** = **Dharma Sabha**.
xa: Movement period: **1920-25**.
Aim: free gurdwaras from **Udasi mahants**.
⚠ **1920** SGPC; **1921** Nankana Sahib; **1922** Guru-ka-Bagh.

193.s: The Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) was formed in:
193.x: The SGPC was formed in 1920 during the Gurdwara Reform Movement.
193.tq: Distinguish the body's formation year from the later legislation that gave it statutory control.
xs: The **SGPC** was formed in **1920** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1920** is also when the **Akali** movement began; **1902** is the **Bharat Dharma Mahamandal**.
xa: **1921** = **Nankana Sahib** massacre; **1922** = **Guru-ka-Bagh**.
Akali leader: **Kartar Singh Jhabbar**.
Akali aim: free gurdwaras from corrupt **Udasi mahants**.

193.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with a flashpoint of the Akali movement?
193.x: The Nankana Sahib massacre of 1921 was one of the flashpoints of the Akali movement. Guru-ka-Bagh was another flashpoint in 1922.
193.tq: Match each event with its exact year before checking the alternatives.
xs: **Nankana Sahib massacre — 1921** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**Guru-ka-Bagh** was **1922**, not 1919; **Malerkotla** was a **Kuka** clash of **1872**.
xa: **1920**: **SGPC** formed and Akali movement begins.
The Akalis fought **corrupt Udasi mahants**.
Leader: **Kartar Singh Jhabbar**; later the **Akali Dal**.

193.s:
Consider the following statements about the Radhasoami Satsang:
1. It was founded by Shiv Dayal Singh (Soamiji Maharaj) at Agra in 1861.
2. Its teaching stressed inner realisation through the guru.
3. It was founded by Radhakant Deb at Calcutta in 1830.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
193.x: Statement 1 is correct: Shiv Dayal Singh founded it at Agra in 1861. Statement 2 is correct: it stressed inner realisation through the guru. Statement 3 is wrong: Radhakant Deb founded the Dharma Sabha at Calcutta in 1830. So '2 only' misses 1, and the options with 3 are wrong.
193.tq: Radhasoami = Shiv Dayal Singh, Agra 1861; Dharma Sabha = Radhakant Deb, Calcutta 1830.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Shiv Dayal Singh** (Soamiji Maharaj) founded it at **Agra**, **1861**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: it stressed **inner realisation through the guru**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: **Radhakant Deb** founded the **Dharma Sabha**, Calcutta, **1830**.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: The **Dharma Sabha** **opposed abolition of sati**.
**Dev Samaj**: **Shiv Narain Agnihotri**, **Lahore, 1887**.

193.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Dev Samaj — Shiv Narain Agnihotri — Lahore, 1887
Dharma Sabha — Shiv Dayal Singh — Agra, 1861
Bharat Dharma Mahamandal — Naoroji Furdonji — Bombay, 1851
193.x: Dev Samaj was founded by Shiv Narain Agnihotri at Lahore in 1887. The other combinations exchange founders, places or organisations.
193.tq: Use the founder-place-year triple to expose swapped reform bodies.
xs: **Dev Samaj — Shiv Narain Agnihotri — Lahore, 1887** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Dharma Sabha** = **Radhakant Deb**, Calcutta, **1830**; **Radhasoami** = **Shiv Dayal Singh**, Agra, **1861**; **Bombay 1851** = Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha.
xa: Dev Samaj text: **Deva Shastra**.
**Bharat Dharma Mahamandal** (**1902**): orthodox Hindu body; **Madan Mohan Malaviya** a leading figure.
Dev Samaj stressed **eternity of the soul** and **supremacy of the guru**.

193.s: The text associated with Dev Samaj was:
193.x: Dev Samaj was associated with the text Deva Shastra. Rast Goftar was a journal of the Parsi reform movement, while hukamnamas were issued by the Nirankaris.
193.tq: Separate a reform text from journals and religious directives of other movements.
xs: The **Dev Samaj** text was the **Deva Shastra** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Rast Goftar** and **Jagat Mithra** were **Parsi** journals; **hukamnamas** were issued by the **Nirankaris**.
xa: Dev Samaj: **Shiv Narain Agnihotri**, **Lahore, 1887**.
It stressed **good deeds** and abstaining from **alcohol and meat**.
**Radhasoami**: inner realisation through the guru.

193.s: Which of the following was NOT among the principles stressed by Dev Samaj?
193.x: Dev Samaj stressed abstaining from alcohol and meat, along with the eternity of the soul, supremacy of the guru and good deeds.
193.tq: Identify the reversed form of a stated reform principle.
xs: **Consumption of alcohol and meat** was NOT a Dev Samaj principle — it urged **abstaining** from them — so option **(4)** is correct.
It did stress **eternity of the soul**, **supremacy of the guru** and **good deeds**.
xa: Founder: **Shiv Narain Agnihotri**, **Lahore, 1887**.
Text: **Deva Shastra**.
The **Kukas** also gave up meat.

193.s: Which one of the following statements about the Dharma Sabha is correct?
o: It was founded by Naoroji Furdonji in Bombay in 1851 and promoted girls' education.
It was founded by Madan Mohan Malaviya in 1902 and led the Gurdwara Reform Movement.
It was founded by Radhakant Deb at Calcutta in 1830 and opposed abolition of sati.
It was founded by Shiv Narain Agnihotri at Lahore in 1887 and promoted abolition of sati.
193.x: Radhakant Deb founded the Dharma Sabha at Calcutta in 1830, and it opposed the abolition of sati.
193.tq: Watch for swapped founders, places and reform objectives in long options.
xs: **Radhakant Deb** founded the **Dharma Sabha** at **Calcutta** in **1830**; it **opposed abolition of sati** — option **(3)**.
**Bombay 1851** = Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha; **1902** = **Bharat Dharma Mahamandal**; **Lahore 1887** = **Dev Samaj**.
xa: **Radhasoami Satsang**: **Shiv Dayal Singh**, **Agra**, **1861**.
**Malaviya** was a leading figure of the **Bharat Dharma Mahamandal**.
The Gurdwara Reform Movement was led by **Kartar Singh Jhabbar**.

193.s: The Bharat Dharma Mahamandal was established in 1902 as:
o: A Sikh body for gurdwara administration
193.x: Bharat Dharma Mahamandal was an orthodox all-India Hindu body established in 1902. Madan Mohan Malaviya was a leading figure associated with it.
193.tq: Identify the institutional character of the organisation before considering its associated personality.
xs: The **Bharat Dharma Mahamandal** (**1902**) was **an orthodox all-India Hindu body** — option **(1)**.
**Madan Mohan Malaviya** was a leading figure in it.
xa: Another orthodox body: **Dharma Sabha** (**Radhakant Deb**, **1830**), which opposed abolition of sati.
Sikh gurdwara body: **SGPC** (**1920**).
Parsi reform body: **Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha** (**1851**).

193.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Reform body)
 a. Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha
 b. Singh Sabha
 c. Deoband
 d. Kuka or Namdhari

List-II (Community)
 i. Muslims
 ii. Parsis
 iii. Sikhs

Choose the correct answer using the code given below.
193.x: Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha reformed the Parsis; Singh Sabha and Kuka/Namdhari were Sikh movements; Deoband was associated with Muslims.
193.tq: Start with the distinctive Parsi pair and eliminate codes with swapped communities.
xs: Correct match: **a–ii, b–iii, c–i, d–iii** — option **(1)**.
**Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha** – **Parsis**; **Singh Sabha** – **Sikhs**; **Deoband** – **Muslims**; **Kuka/Namdhari** – **Sikhs**.
xa: Other Sikh bodies: **Nirankari** and the **Akali** movement.
**Aligarh** too was a Muslim reform movement.
APPSC G2 **2017**: Mazdayasnan Sabha reformed the **Parsees**.

193.s: The Kuka movement anticipated which later methods of the Indian national movement?
o: Individual satyagraha and the Cabinet Mission
Home Rule and the Cripps proposals
193.x: The Kuka boycott anticipated the later Swadeshi and non-cooperation methods used in the national movement.
193.tq: Link an early movement's method with the later movements it foreshadowed.
xs: The Kuka boycott anticipated **Swadeshi and non-cooperation** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Kukas boycotted **British goods**, **English education**, **law courts** and the **postal system**.
xa: **Satguru Ram Singh** = first to use **boycott and non-cooperation** against British rule.
Sikh reform → **Sikh political mobilisation**.
Suppression after the **1872 Malerkotla** clash.

193.s: Which comparison between the Namdhari and Nirankari movements is correct?
o: Namdharis controlled gurdwaras through the SGPC, whereas Nirankaris led the Akali Dal.
Namdharis stressed the formless God, whereas Nirankaris wore white and carried a lathi.
Namdhari followers wore white and carried a lathi, whereas Nirankaris stressed the formless God.
Both movements rejected all forms of worship and cooperated with the British.
193.x: Namdhari practices included white dress and carrying a lathi, while Nirankari teaching centred on worship of the formless God.
193.tq: Split the paired movements by their distinctive practices and beliefs.
xs: **Namdharis** wore **white** and carried a **lathi**; **Nirankaris** stressed the **formless God** — option **(3)**.
Option (2) swaps them; only the Nirankaris **cooperated with the British**, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: Namdharis were **anti-British**; Nirankaris **pro-British cooperation**.
**SGPC** and the **Akali Dal** came from the **Akali** movement.
Nirankari founder: **Baba Dayal Das**; Namdhari: **Baba Ram Singh**.

193.s:
Which of the following statements best expresses the broader significance of Sikh reform movements in the period under consideration?
1. The Kuka boycott anticipated later Swadeshi and non-cooperation methods.
2. Sikh reform contributed to Sikh political mobilisation.
3. The Akali movement later became the Akali Dal.
193.x: All three statements are correct. The Kuka methods foreshadowed later nationalist techniques, Sikh reform encouraged political mobilisation, and the Akali movement later developed into the Akali Dal.
193.tq: Combine method, social consequence and political evolution to test the movement's overall significance.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: the Kuka boycott anticipated **Swadeshi and non-cooperation**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: Sikh reform → **Sikh political mobilisation**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: the Akali movement became the **Akali Dal**.
So **1, 2 and 3** — option **(4)** is correct.
xa: Akali flashpoints: **Nankana Sahib (1921)**, **Guru-ka-Bagh (1922)**.
**SGPC** formed **1920**.

194.s: Which of the following was NOT an objective of the Satyashodhak Samaj?
o: Breaking Brahminical dominance and priestly monopoly over rituals
Promoting education among lower castes and women
Strengthening the exclusive authority of Brahmin priests
194.x: The Satyashodhak Samaj opposed Brahminical dominance and priestly monopoly; it did not seek to strengthen them.
194.tq: Identify the option that reverses the movement’s anti-caste objective.
xs: **Strengthening the exclusive authority of Brahmin priests** was NOT a Samaj objective — it fought priestly monopoly — so option **(4)** is correct.
Its objectives: end **caste and untouchability**, break **Brahmanical** dominance and **priestly monopoly** over ritual, educate **women, Shudras, Ati-Shudras**.
xa: Founded by **Jyotiba Phule** at **Pune** in **1873**.
Name means **"Society of Truth Seekers"**.
**Satyashodhak marriages**: inter-caste, **without priests** (**1873**).

194.s: Satyashodhak marriages were significant because they:
o: Were restricted to members of one caste
Required the exclusive participation of Brahmin priests
Could be conducted without priests and permitted inter-caste marriage
Were intended only for upper-caste widows
194.x: Satyashodhak marriages rejected priestly control and allowed inter-caste marriage.
194.tq: Apply the movement’s anti-priestly and anti-caste principles to a social institution.
xs: Satyashodhak marriages were **conducted without priests** and allowed **inter-caste marriage** — so option **(3)** is correct.
They date from **1873** (UPSC), the year the **Satyashodhak Samaj** was founded.
xa: Compare **Self-respect marriages** (Periyar) — also without priests, from **1928**.
Samaj aim: free lower castes from **Brahmin priests** and religious exploitation.
Phule also opened a **home for upper-caste widows** (**1854**).

194.s: Jyotiba Phule belonged to the:
194.x: Jyotiba Phule belonged to the Mali community of Maharashtra.
194.tq: Distinguish the reformer’s community identity from those of other anti-caste leaders.
xs: **Jyotiba Phule** belonged to the **Mali community** of Maharashtra — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ **Ezhavas** = SNDP (Kerala); **Nadars** = southern Tamil Nadu / Travancore; **Vellalas** were in the Justice Party's base.
xa: Phule lived **1827-1890**.
He founded the **Satyashodhak Samaj** at **Pune**, **1873**.
Called **"Father of Indian Social Revolution"**.

194.s: The title ‘Mahatma’ was conferred on Jyotiba Phule by:
194.x: Vithalrao Krishnaji Vandekar gave Jyotiba Phule the title ‘Mahatma’ in 1888.
194.tq: Match the honorific with the person who conferred it, not with a fellow reformer.
xs: **Vithalrao Krishnaji Vandekar** gave Phule the title **"Mahatma"** in **1888** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Savitribai** was Phule's wife, India's first woman teacher; **Periyar** led the **Self-Respect Movement**.
xa: Phule is also called **"Father of Indian Social Revolution"**.
Phule's **200th birth anniversary** was marked on **11 April 2026**.
⚠ **1888** is also the **Aruvippuram** consecration by Narayana Guru.

194.s: Jyotiba Phule is described in the material as the:
o: Father of the Indian Social Revolution
Father of constitutional government in India
194.x: Jyotiba Phule is described as the Father of the Indian Social Revolution.
194.tq: Identify the exact title associated with the reformer rather than a broader historical label.
xs: Phule is called the **"Father of the Indian Social Revolution"** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Dravidian** stream came from **Periyar** (Self-Respect → **DK**).
xa: Title **"Mahatma"** from **Vithalrao Krishnaji Vandekar** (**1888**).
⚠ **"Father of the Indian Constitution"** = **Ambedkar**.
Phule's girls' school, **Pune**, **1848**.

194.s: Which symbolic pairing did Jyotiba Phule use in his critique of Brahminical dominance?
194.x: Phule used King Bali as a symbol representing the oppressed, in opposition to the Brahmanical symbol of Rama.
194.tq: Test the distinctive symbolic contrast rather than the general theme of anti-caste reform.
xs: Phule set **King Bali** against the **Brahmanical** symbol of **Rama** — so option **(4)** is correct (UPSC).
King Bali stood for the oppressed.
xa: ⚠ **Phule symbol** = **King Bali**; **Justice Party symbol** = **Scales**.
**Gulamgiri** (**1873**) compared lower castes' condition to **slavery**.
Samaj aim: break **priestly monopoly** over ritual.

194.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
A. Satyashodhak Samaj
B. Gulamgiri
C. Sarvajanik Satyadharma
D. Shetkaryacha Asud

List-II
1. Society of Truth Seekers
2. Slavery
3. A work on public true religion
4. The Cultivator’s Whipcord

Select the correct answer using the code below.
194.x: Satyashodhak Samaj means Society of Truth Seekers; Gulamgiri means Slavery; Sarvajanik Satyadharma concerns public true religion; and Shetkaryacha Asud means The Cultivator’s Whipcord.
194.tq: Start with the sure translation of Gulamgiri and verify the remaining title pairs.
xs: Correct match: **A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4** — option **(1)**.
**Satyashodhak Samaj** = **Society of Truth Seekers**; **Gulamgiri** = **Slavery**; **Sarvajanik Satyadharma** = public true religion; **Shetkaryacha Asud** = **The Cultivator's Whipcord**.
xa: All the works are by **Jyotiba Phule**; others: **Tritiya Ratna**, **Brahmananche Kasab**.
**Gulamgiri** and the Samaj both date from **1873**.
⚠ **The Orion** is by **Tilak** — a regular distractor.

194.s: Who wrote Sarvajanik Satyadharma Pustak, Shetkaryacha Asud, Tritiya Ratna and Brahmananche Kasab?
194.x: All four works were written by Jyotiba Phule.
194.tq: Group multiple works under their common author.
xs: All four works are by **Jyotiba Phule** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Ambedkar** wrote **Who Were the Shudras?** and **Annihilation of Caste**; **Jala Rangaswamy** wrote **Nimna Jatula Charitra**; **Periyar** ran **Kudi Arasu**.
xa: Phule's best-known book: **Gulamgiri** (Slavery), **1873**.
**Shetkaryacha Asud** = **The Cultivator's Whipcord**.
⚠ **The Orion** = **Tilak**.

194.s: In 1848 Jyotiba Phule opened a girls' school at Pune, where the first woman teacher of India taught. Who was she?
194.x: Savitribai Phule taught at the girls' school opened by Jyotiba Phule at Pune in 1848 and is called India's first woman teacher. Pandita Ramabai and Tarabai Shinde were other Maharashtrian women reformers not named in this context; Sarada Devi was Ramakrishna's wife.
194.tq: 1848 Pune girls' school -> Savitribai = first woman teacher.
xs: **Savitribai Phule** taught at Phule's girls' school, **Pune**, **1848** — India's **first woman teacher** — option **(2)**.
**Sarada Devi** was **Ramakrishna's** wife (not in this topic).
xa: In **1854** Phule opened a **home for upper-caste widows**.
Phule founded the **Satyashodhak Samaj** in **1873**.
Samaj aim: education for **women, Shudras, Ati-Shudras**.

194.s: The proportion of Brahmins in the population of the Madras Presidency and their share in government employment were approximately:
o: 3% of the population and over 90% of government jobs
15% of the population and over 75% of government jobs
10% of the population and 50% of government jobs
25% of the population and 60% of government jobs
194.x: Brahmins constituted only about 3% of the Madras Presidency population but held over 90% of government jobs, contributing to the emergence of the non-Brahmin movement.
194.tq: Pair the two numerical proportions precisely rather than relying on a general impression.
xs: Brahmins were about **3%** of the Madras Presidency population but held **over 90%** of government jobs — option **(1)**.
This imbalance drove non-Brahmins to meet at **Madras** in **1916**.
xa: The **Justice Party** aimed to protect **non-Brahmin** interests (APPSC **2008**).
It sought **reservation** in jobs, education and legislatures.
Result: the **Communal G.O. (1921)**.

194.s: The South Indian Liberal Federation was founded at Madras on:
194.x: The South Indian Liberal Federation was founded at Madras on 20 November 1916.
194.tq: Use the exact date attached to the organisation’s formation.
xs: The organisation was founded at **Madras** on **20 November 1916** — so option **(4)** is correct.
About **30** non-Brahmin leaders met at the **Victoria Memorial Hall** → **South Indian People's Association**; its political wing was the **SILF**.
xa: **17 December 1920** = first Justice ministry under **A. Subbarayalu Reddiar**.
**Non-Brahmin Manifesto**: **Dec 1916**, signed by **P. Thyagaraya Chetty**.
Daily **Justice**: **26 Feb 1917**.

194.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the original organisation of the Justice Party:
1. It was also associated with the South India Peoples Association.
2. It was founded by T.M. Nair, P. Theagaraya Chetty and C. Natesa Mudaliar.
3. Its English newspaper Justice began publication in February 1917.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
194.x: All three statements are correct. The organisation was linked with the South India Peoples Association, had the three stated founders, and its English paper Justice began in February 1917.
194.tq: Check each institutional detail separately before selecting the combined code.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: the **20 Nov 1916** meeting formed the **South Indian People's Association**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: founders **T.M. Nair**, **P. Theagaraya Chetty**, **C. Natesa Mudaliar**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: the daily **Justice** started on **26 Feb 1917**.
So **1, 2 and 3** — option **(4)** is correct.
xa: Political wing: **South Indian Liberal Federation (SILF)**; symbol **Scales**.
First general meeting: **Coimbatore, 19 Jul 1917** (**Panagal Raja** presiding).

194.s: The name ‘Justice Party’ was derived from:
o: A resolution passed by the Madras Legislative Council
The title of its English newspaper Justice
The Justice League formed in Madras
194.x: The English paper Justice, started in February 1917, gave the organisation its popular name, the Justice Party.
194.tq: Identify the naming source rather than confusing the name with an objective.
xs: The name came from **its English newspaper Justice** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The daily started on **26 Feb 1917**; the **SILF** then became the "Justice Party".
xa: Founders: **T.M. Nair**, **Theagaraya Chetty**, **Natesa Mudaliar**.
Symbol: **Scales**.
First Andhra meeting: **Bikkavolu**.

194.s: The first Andhra meeting associated with the Justice Party was held at:
194.x: The first Andhra meeting of the Justice Party was held at Bikkavolu.
194.tq: Distinguish the organisational meeting place from the later university locations.
xs: The first Andhra meeting of the Justice Party was at **Bikkavolu** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Bezawada** was **Andhra University's** first HQ, later moved to **Waltair**; **Annamalai** University dates from **1929**.
xa: First general meeting: **Coimbatore, 19 Jul 1917**.
Andhra base: **Reddys, Kammas, Kapus**.
Andhra leaders: **Panagal Raja**, **K.V. Reddy Naidu**, **Bobbili Raja**, **A.P. Patro**.

194.s: Which one of the following was NOT an objective of the Justice Party?
o: Obtaining reservation in government employment and education
Securing representation for non-Brahmins in legislatures
Establishing exclusive political representation for Brahmins
194.x: The Justice Party sought to protect non-Brahmin interests through representation and reservation; it did not seek exclusive political representation for Brahmins.
194.tq: Find the option that reverses the movement’s social and political objective.
xs: **Establishing exclusive political representation for Brahmins** was NOT an aim — so option **(4)** is correct.
Aims: protect **non-Brahmins**; **reservation** in jobs and education; **representation** in legislatures.
xa: It sought to end Brahmin dominance in **jobs, education, politics and religion**.
APPSC **2008**: aim = protect interests of **non-Brahmins**.
It secured the **Communal G.O. (1921)**.

194.s: The political wing of the South Indian People's Association was known as the:
194.x: The South Indian Liberal Federation was the political wing of the South Indian People's Association and later became popularly known as the Justice Party.
194.tq: Test the relationship between a parent association and its political wing.
xs: The political wing was the **South Indian Liberal Federation** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **ILP** (**1936**) was Ambedkar's; the **Swaraj Party** its rival; the **DK** (**1944**) came later under **Periyar**.
xa: SILF became popularly the **"Justice Party"** after the daily **Justice** (**1917**).
Founded **Madras, 1916**.
Symbol: **Scales**.

194.s: Who signed the Non-Brahmin Manifesto of December 1916?
194.x: The Non-Brahmin Manifesto issued in December 1916 was signed by P. Thyagaraya Chetty.
194.tq: Use the signatory–document association rather than the founder list.
xs: The **Non-Brahmin Manifesto** (**Dec 1916**) was signed by **P. Thyagaraya Chetty** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**T.M. Nair** and **Natesa Mudaliar** were co-founders; **Panagal Raja** presided over the first general meeting.
xa: Thyagaraya Chetty died on **25 Apr 1925** — a blow to the party.
Founding meeting: **20 Nov 1916**, Victoria Memorial Hall.
Daily **Justice**: **26 Feb 1917**.

194.s: What was the symbol of the Justice Party?
194.x: The symbol of the Justice Party was the Scales.
194.tq: Test a distinctive organisational symbol directly.
xs: The Justice Party's symbol was the **Scales** — so option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ **Phule's** symbol was **King Bali**.
xa: Political wing: **South Indian Liberal Federation**.
Founders: **T.M. Nair**, **Theagaraya Chetty**, **Natesa Mudaliar**.
It won **63 of 98** elected seats in **1920**.

194.s:
Consider the following statements about the social base of the Justice Party:
1. Its base included non-Brahmin landed gentry.
2. In Andhra, Reddys, Kammas and Kapus formed part of this social base.
3. Brahmins constituted approximately 90 per cent of the Presidency’s population.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
194.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Brahmins were approximately 3 per cent of the Presidency’s population, not 90 per cent; the 90 per cent-plus figure referred to their share of government jobs.
194.tq: Catch the reversed population-versus-employment comparison.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: its base was **non-Brahmin landed gentry**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: in Andhra, **Reddys, Kammas, Kapus**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: Brahmins were about **3%** of the population; **90%+** was their share of government jobs.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: This base secured the **Communal G.O. (1921)**.
Dalits built a parallel **"Adi"** movement.

194.s: The colonial government used the Justice Party primarily as a counter to:
o: the Swadeshi movement and the Khilafat movement
the Andhra University movement and the Dalit movement
the Round Table Conferences and the Simon Commission
194.x: The government used the Justice Party against the Home Rule movement and Gandhi’s movements.
194.tq: Identify the political movements against which an organisation was deployed.
xs: The British used the Justice Party against **Home Rule and Gandhi's movements** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They backed it partly to **weaken Home Rule**.
xa: Criticism: **pro-British**, **landlord-led**, weak among Andhra masses.
It **opposed both the freedom struggle and the Andhra movement**.
Congress **boycotted** the **1920** elections, letting the Justice Party win.

194.s:
The non-Brahmin movement in the Madras Presidency primarily sought to end Brahmin dominance in which of the following spheres?
1. Jobs
2. Education
3. Politics
4. Religion
Which of the statements given above are correct?
194.x: The movement aimed to end Brahmin dominance in jobs, education, politics and religion, besides safeguarding the interests of non-Brahmins.
194.tq: Use the complete-list option when every listed sphere belongs to the movement’s stated objective.
xs: The movement sought to end Brahmin dominance in **jobs, education, politics and religion** — so **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
Background: Brahmins (**3%**) held **over 90%** of government jobs.
xa: Means: **reservation and representation** in jobs, education, legislatures.
**Communal G.O. (1921)**: proportional representation in jobs and education.
**Temple entry** campaign for non-Brahmins and Dalits.

194.s:
With reference to the Communal G.O. of 1921, consider the following statements:
1. It was secured by the intermediate landed castes associated with the non-Brahmin movement.
2. It is regarded as a root or forerunner of reservation policy in South India.
3. It was intended exclusively for Dalit organisations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
194.x: The Communal G.O. of 1921 was secured by the intermediate landed castes and became a forerunner of South Indian reservation policy. It was not intended exclusively for Dalit organisations.
194.tq: Find the single over-exclusive statement among otherwise connected historical facts.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: the **intermediate landed castes** secured the **Communal G.O. (1921)**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: it is the **root/forerunner** of South Indian **reservation** policy.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: it was for **non-Brahmins**; Dalits built a separate **"Adi"** movement.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)** is correct.
xa: CDX dates it **Dec 1921**.
Caste-based roster: **50%** of educational seats for non-Brahmins.

194.s: The Andhra Mahasabha session associated with the demand for reserved seats for non-Brahmins was held at:
194.x: The Andhra Mahasabha met at Vijayawada in 1917 and sought reserved seats for non-Brahmins.
194.tq: Separate a place-year combination from nearby organisation and session dates.
xs: The **Andhra Mahasabha** at **Vijayawada** in **1917** sought **reserved seats for non-Brahmins** — option **(4)**.
**Machilipatnam 1919** = 2nd Adi-Andhra conference; **Hyderabad 1923** = **Andhra Jana Kendra Sangham**.
xa: Demand echoed by **Ponaka Pattabhirama Reddy** and **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary**.
Also **1917, Vijayawada**: **First Panchama Mahajana Sabha** (**4-6 Nov**).
**Krishna district** was the hub of these sessions.

194.s:
The demand for reserved seats for non-Brahmins in the Andhra Mahasabha was echoed by:
1. Ponaka Pattabhirama Reddy
2. Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary
3. Gora
4. Periyar
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
194.x: Ponaka Pattabhirama Reddy and Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary echoed the demand. Gora and Periyar are associated with other strands of rationalist and anti-caste activity.
194.tq: Match individuals to the specific regional demand rather than to the broader reform movement.
xs: **Ponaka Pattabhirama Reddy** and **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary** echoed the demand — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
**Gora** (atheist, **Atheist Centre**) and **Periyar** (**Self-Respect**) belong to other strands.
xa: Tripuraneni = **Kavi Raju**; rationalist attack on **Puranic** caste stories.
His works: **Kurukshetra Sangramam**, **Sambuka Vadha**, **Suta Puranam**.
The demand came at the **Andhra Mahasabha**, **Vijayawada**, **1917**.

194.s: The parallel movement built by Dalits alongside the non-Brahmin movement was known as the:
194.x: Dalits built a parallel movement identified with the prefix ‘Adi’, asserting a distinct social identity.
194.tq: Distinguish the Dalit parallel stream from the broader non-Brahmin and rationalist movements.
xs: Dalits built a parallel **"Adi" movement** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**"Adi"** = original inhabitants; it rejected the term **Panchama**.
xa: **Adi Andhra** = Dalits of the Andhra (Madras) region; **Adi Hindu** = Dalits of Hyderabad State.
**Bhagya Reddy Varma** popularised both terms.
"Adi Andhra" name (**1917**) = first Dalit identity assertion in Telugu country.

194.s: In the 1920 Madras elections, the Justice Party won:
194.x: After the Congress boycotted the Montagu-Chelmsford elections, the Justice Party won 63 of the 98 elected seats in 1920.
194.tq: Separate the seat total from the number of seats won.
xs: In **1920** the Justice Party won **63 of the 98** elected seats — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Congress boycotted** the **Montagu-Chelmsford** elections; this formed the **first Justice ministry**.
xa: **1937**: routed by the **Congress** (Rajaji ministry).
First CM: **A. Subbarayalu Reddiar**, **17 Dec 1920**.

194.s: Who became the first Chief Minister of the first Justice Party ministry formed on 17 December 1920?
194.x: A. Subbarayalu Reddiar became the first Chief Minister of the first Justice Party ministry on 17 December 1920; he was later succeeded by the Raja of Panagal.
194.tq: Distinguish the first ministry head from later Justice Party ministers.
xs: **A. Subbarayalu Reddiar** became the first Chief Minister on **17 Dec 1920** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He served until **Jul 1921** (ill health); then **Panagal Raja** (**1921-1926**).
xa: Ministry rested on **63 of 98** seats.
⚠ **17 Dec 1933** = Siddhantam temple entry move.

194.s: Which Justice Party Premier served from 1921 to 1926 and headed two ministries?
194.x: Panagal Raja, also known as P. Ramarayaningar, served as Premier from 1921 to 1926 and headed two ministries.
194.tq: Associate the tenure with the correct premier rather than the party founder.
xs: **Panagal Raja** (**P. Ramarayaningar**) was Premier **1921-1926**, heading **two ministries** — option **(2)**.
**Subbarayalu Reddiar** was first CM; **Munuswamy Naidu** **1930-1932**; **K.V. Reddy Naidu** **Apr-Jul 1937**.
xa: Panagal was **party president**; the **Andhra University Act (1926)** came in his time.
He died on **16 Dec 1928**.
**26 Nov 1923**: no-confidence motion against him by **C.R. Reddy**.

194.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the tenure of a Justice Party Premier?
194.x: B. Munuswamy Naidu served from 1930 to 1932. Bobbili Raja served from 1932 to 1937, Panagal Raja from 1921 to 1926, and Subbarayalu Reddiar from December 1920 to July 1921.
194.tq: Use tenure overlap and sequence to eliminate swapped office-holders.
xs: **Munuswamy Naidu — 1930–1932** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**Bobbili Raja** = **1932-1937**; **Panagal Raja** = **1921-1926**; **Apr-Jul 1937** = **K.V. Reddy Naidu**.
xa: **Subbarayalu Reddiar**: **17 Dec 1920 - Jul 1921**.
**1926-30**: independent **P. Subbarayan** ministry with Justice support.
**P.T. Rajan** acted **Apr-Aug 1936**.

194.s: The independent P. Subbarayan ministry of 1926–1930 functioned with the support of the:
194.x: P. Subbarayan headed an independent ministry from 1926 to 1930 with the support of the Justice Party.
194.tq: Identify the supporting party rather than the formal label of the ministry.
xs: The **P. Subbarayan** ministry (**1926-30**) ran with **Justice Party** support — so option **(2)** is correct.
In **1926** the Justice Party won only **22** seats; Swaraj leader **C.V.S. Narasimha Raju** declined to form a ministry.
xa: Panagal could not form one either in **1926**.
Swaraj Party won **41**, independents **36** in **1926**.
Justice returned with **Munuswamy Naidu** (**1930-1932**).

194.s: Who moved the no-confidence motion against Panagal Raja on 26 November 1923?
194.x: C.R. Reddy moved the no-confidence motion against Panagal Raja on 26 November 1923.
194.tq: Match the parliamentary action with its mover and date.
xs: **C.R. Reddy** moved the no-confidence motion against Panagal on **26 Nov 1923** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**C.V.S. Narasimha Raju** was the **Swaraj** leader who declined a ministry in **1926**.
xa: **C.R. (Kattamanchi Ramalinga) Reddy** was also **Andhra University's** first VC.
Justice won **44** seats in **1923**.
Panagal: Premier **1921-1926**.

194.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Communal Government Order of 1921?
o: It introduced proportional representation for non-Brahmins in jobs and education.
It reserved government posts exclusively for Brahmins.
It introduced universal adult franchise in the Madras Presidency.
It abolished all forms of reservation in education.
194.x: The 1921 Communal G.O. provided proportional representation for non-Brahmins in government employment and education and became a basis for reservation in South India.
194.tq: Match the order with its specific policy content, avoiding reversed beneficiaries.
xs: The **Communal G.O.** gave **proportional representation for non-Brahmins in jobs and education** — option **(1)**.
It is the base of **reservation in South India**.
xa: Secured by the intermediate landed castes: **Reddys, Kammas, Kapus**.
**Women's franchise resolution** (**1921**) — Madras first province to let women vote.

194.s:
Consider the following statements about reforms associated with the Justice Party:
1. It campaigned for temple entry for non-Brahmins and Dalits.
2. It promoted schools and scholarships for non-Brahmin students.
3. It introduced a caste-based roster in the 1920s.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
194.x: The Justice Party supported temple entry, educational assistance for non-Brahmins, and a caste-based roster during the 1920s.
194.tq: Combine social, educational and administrative reforms only after verifying all three.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **temple entry** campaign for non-Brahmins and Dalits.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **schools and scholarships** for non-Brahmin students.
Statement 3 is **correct**: a **caste-based roster** in the **1920s** — **50%** of educational seats for non-Brahmins.
So **1, 2 and 3** — option **(4)** is correct.
xa: Also: **Communal G.O. (1921)**; **Andhra University Act (1926)**.
**Bobbili Raja's** ministry amended the **Estate Land Act (1908)** for zamindari tenants.

194.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
A. Andhra University Act — 1926
B. Madras Hindu Religious Endowments Act — 1926
C. Women’s franchise resolution in Madras — 1921
D. Annamalai University — 1929
194.x: All four year associations are correct: the Andhra University Act and Madras Hindu Religious Endowments Act were in 1926, the women’s franchise resolution was in 1921, and Annamalai University was founded in 1929.
194.tq: Verify each year independently because the options differ only through combinations.
xs: All four are **correct**: **Andhra University Act 1926**; **Hindu Religious Endowments Act 1926**; **women's franchise 1921**; **Annamalai University 1929**.
So **A, B, C and D** — option **(4)** is correct.
xa: ⚠ **Andhra University 1926** vs **Annamalai University 1929**.
APPSC G2 **2025** asked "Justice Party helped create which university?" → **Andhra University** (three times).
**Periyar** supported the **Hindu Religious Endowments Act** even in his Congress years.

194.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra University:
1. Its first Chancellor was Lord Goschen.
2. Its first headquarters was at Waltair, later shifted to Bezawada (Vijayawada).
3. A.P. Patro, as Education Minister of the Justice Party ministry, drove the Andhra University Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
194.x: Statement 1 is correct: Lord Goschen was the first Chancellor. Statement 2 is wrong: the first HQ was at Bezawada (Vijayawada) and it later shifted to Waltair, not the reverse. Statement 3 is correct: A.P. Patro as Education Minister drove the 1926 Act. So '1 and 3 only' is right; '1 only' misses Patro, while the options with 2 include the reversed HQ.
194.tq: Remember the move direction: Bezawada first, Waltair later.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: first Chancellor **Lord Goschen**.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: first HQ was **Bezawada (Vijayawada)**, later shifted to **Waltair** — the reverse.
Statement 3 is **correct**: Education Minister **A.P. Patro** drove the Act.
So **1 and 3 only** — option **(2)** is correct.
xa: First VC: **C.R. (Kattamanchi Ramalinga) Reddy**.
Act passed in **1926** under **Panagal Raja**.

194.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Andhra legacy of the Justice Party?
o: It established the Viswa Brahmana Sangham in 1907.
It organised the Aruvippuram consecration in 1888.
Its lasting Andhra legacy was Andhra University, established in 1926.
Its lasting Andhra legacy was the Atheist Centre, established in 1940.
194.x: Andhra University, established in 1926, is identified as the lasting Andhra legacy of the Justice Party.
194.tq: Identify the correct institutional legacy while rejecting achievements belonging to other movements.
xs: The Justice Party's lasting Andhra legacy is **Andhra University** (**1926**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1907** = **Prabhodini**, journal of the **Viswa Brahmana Sangham**; **1888** = **Aruvippuram** consecration (Narayana Guru); **1940** = **Gora's** Atheist Centre.
xa: Act driven by **A.P. Patro**; first VC **C.R. Reddy**.
First HQ **Bezawada**, later **Waltair**.
APPSC G2 **2025** asked it three times.

194.s: Who was the first Vice-Chancellor of Andhra University, created under the Justice Party government in 1926?
194.x: C.R. (Kattamanchi Ramalinga) Reddy was the first Vice-Chancellor of Andhra University. Lord Goschen was its first Chancellor, A.P. Patro the Education Minister who drove the Act, and Panagal Raja the Premier in whose time it was set up.
194.tq: Andhra Univ 1926: VC C.R. Reddy, Chancellor Goschen, HQ Bezawada -> Waltair.
xs: **C.R. (Kattamanchi Ramalinga) Reddy** was the first **Vice-Chancellor** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Lord Goschen** was first **Chancellor**; **A.P. Patro** drove the Act; **Panagal Raja** was Premier.
xa: Andhra University Act: **1926**.
First HQ: **Bezawada (Vijayawada)**, later **Waltair**.
C.R. Reddy also moved the **26 Nov 1923** no-confidence motion against Panagal.

194.s:
Panagal Raja was associated with which combination of offices and facts?
1. President of the Justice Party
2. Premier from 1921 to 1926
3. Association with Andhra University in 1926
4. Death on 16 December 1928
Which of the statements given above are correct?
194.x: All four statements are correct. Panagal Raja was party president, served as Premier from 1921 to 1926, was associated with Andhra University in 1926 and died on 16 December 1928.
194.tq: Verify a personality through office, institutional association and date.
xs: All four are **correct**: Panagal was **party president**, Premier **1921-26**, linked to **Andhra University (1926)**, died **16 Dec 1928**.
So **1, 2, 3 and 4** — option **(4)** is correct.
xa: Real name: **Panuganti Ramarayaningar**.
Origin: some notes say Zamindar of **Srikalahasti**; others trace him to **Nalgonda** (Panagal).
He presided over the first general meeting, **Coimbatore, 19 Jul 1917**.

194.s: Which statement correctly describes K.V. Reddy Naidu in relation to the Justice Party?
o: He was the first Premier in 1920 and resigned due to ill health.
He acted as Premier from April to August 1936.
He founded the South Indian Liberal Federation in 1916.
He was a minister in the first ministry and became Premier in 1937.
194.x: Kurma Venkata Reddy Naidu of Eluru was a minister in the first ministry in 1920 and became Premier in 1937.
194.tq: Match the leader with the two offices held at different times.
xs: **K.V. Reddy Naidu** was **a minister in the first ministry** (**1920**) and **became Premier in 1937** — option **(4)**.
**Subbarayalu Reddiar** was first Premier; **P.T. Rajan** acted **Apr-Aug 1936**.
xa: He was from **Eluru**; Premier **Apr-Jul 1937** (interim).
He backed an Andhra province only with a **non-Brahmin majority** guaranteed.
SILF founders were **T.M. Nair**, **Theagaraya Chetty**, **Natesa Mudaliar**.

194.s: Bobbili Raja, also known as Ramakrishna Ranga Rao, was the:
194.x: Ramakrishna Ranga Rao was the 13th Raja of Bobbili and served as Premier from 1932 to 1937. He was also a delegate to the Second Round Table Conference.
194.tq: Use the hereditary title to identify the correct political personality.
xs: **Bobbili Raja** (Ramakrishna Ranga Rao) was the **13th Raja of Bobbili** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was CM **1932-37**; the first Premier was **Subbarayalu Reddiar**.
xa: He was a delegate to the **2nd Round Table Conference**.
His ministry amended the **Estate Land Act (1908)** for zamindari tenants.
**P.T. Rajan** acted for him **Apr-Aug 1936**.

194.s: Who moved the separate Andhra resolution in 1922, which was later withdrawn at A.P. Patro’s urging?
194.x: M. Suryanarayana moved the separate Andhra resolution in 1922, and it was withdrawn at the urging of A.P. Patro.
194.tq: Separate the mover of a resolution from the person who urged its withdrawal.
xs: **M. Suryanarayana** moved the separate Andhra resolution in **1922**, withdrawn at **Patro's** urging — option **(2)**.
**Munukuru Rama Rao** was a **Krishna** organiser; **Koka Appa Rao Naidu** and **P. Ramachandra Reddy** were other leaders.
xa: M. Suryanarayana was from **Visakhapatnam**.
Some notes date a Suryanarayana resolution to **1937**.
The party **opposed the Andhra movement** — a cause of decline.

194.s:
Consider the following statements about the decline of the Justice Party:
1. It lacked a mass base.
2. Andhra–Tamil differences weakened it.
3. The deaths of Theagaraya Chetty and the Raja of Panagal affected its leadership.
4. It lost to the Congress in 1937.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
194.x: All four statements describe important factors in the Justice Party’s decline: lack of mass support, regional rifts, leadership losses, and defeat by the Congress in 1937.
194.tq: Treat political decline as a cumulative process and test each stated factor.
xs: All four are **correct**: **no mass base**; **Andhra-Tamil rivalry**; deaths of **Thyagaraya Chetty (25 Apr 1925)** and **Panagal (16 Dec 1928)**; **1937** defeat.
So **1, 2, 3 and 4** — option **(4)** is correct.
xa: It also **opposed the freedom struggle and the Andhra movement**.
**Natesa Mudaliar** attacked its neglect of the **poor and Harijans**.
After **1937**, **Periyar** turned it into the **Dravidar Kazhagam** (**1944**).

194.s: The Justice Party was transformed into the Dravidar Kazhagam under the leadership of Periyar in:
194.x: Periyar transformed the Justice Party into the Dravidar Kazhagam in 1944.
194.tq: Distinguish the year of organisational transformation from the year of electoral defeat.
xs: Periyar turned the Justice Party into the **Dravidar Kazhagam** in **1944** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1937** = anti-Hindi agitation and Justice defeat; **1940** = **Dravidistan** demand (Erode); **1947** = Atheist Centre moved to Vijayawada.
xa: **1949**: DK split → **C.N. Annadurai** formed the **DMK** (**17 Sept 1949**).
DMK in power from **1967**.
Periyar's **Self-Respect Movement**: **1925**.

194.s: Which of the following was a major reason for the decline of the Justice Party?
o: Its refusal to participate in provincial elections
Its opposition to both the freedom struggle and the Andhra movement
Its strong mass base among all sections in Andhra
Its merger with the Congress before 1920
194.x: B is correct: the Justice Party opposed both the freedom struggle and the Andhra movement, which, along with Andhra-Tamil rivalry, cost it support. Option C is the reverse of the truth, since it had no mass base in Andhra.
194.tq: Select the historically stated cause while rejecting absolute organisational claims.
xs: The party **opposed both the freedom struggle and the Andhra movement** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It had **no mass base** in Andhra, so option (3) is the reverse; it **fought elections** from **1920**.
xa: **Andhra-Tamil rivalry** also weakened it.
Criticism: **pro-British**, **landlord-led**.
End: **1937** defeat → **Periyar** dominant.

194.s: Which development followed the Justice Party’s defeat in 1937?
o: It merged with the Independent Labour Party.
Periyar became dominant and the political stream later ran into the Dravidar Kazhagam.
It formed the first ministry under Rajaji.
C.R. Das became its leader and renamed it the Swaraj Party.
194.x: After the 1937 defeat, Periyar became dominant, and the stream later developed into the Dravidar Kazhagam.
194.tq: Test the later transformation of an organisation after electoral decline.
xs: After **1937**, **Periyar became dominant** and the stream became the **Dravidar Kazhagam** — option **(2)**.
The **1937** Congress ministry was under **Rajaji** — the Congress, not the Justice Party.
xa: DK formed **1944**; **Annadurai's DMK** **1949**.
**Anti-Hindi agitation**: **1937**.
The Hindu (**16 Jun 2026**): Justice Party formed government **four times** from **1920**.

194.s: Who criticised the neglect of the poor and Harijans within the Justice Party?
194.x: C. Natesa Mudaliar criticised the Justice Party for neglecting the poor and Harijans.
194.tq: Distinguish internal criticism from external political opposition.
xs: **C. Natesa Mudaliar** attacked the party's **neglect of the poor and Harijans** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He was himself a co-founder, with **T.M. Nair** and **P. Thyagaraya Chetty**.
xa: **P.T. Rajan** acted as CM **Apr-Aug 1936**.
Decline causes: **Andhra-Tamil rivalry**, **no mass base** in Andhra.
Leaders' deaths: **Thyagaraya Chetty (25 Apr 1925)**, **Panagal Raja (16 Dec 1928)**.

194.s: The Self-Respect Movement was launched in 1925 by whom?
194.x: The Self-Respect Movement was launched in 1925 by E.V. Ramasamy Naicker, popularly known as Periyar.
194.tq: Use the founder-year association directly.
xs: The **Self-Respect Movement** (**1925**) was launched by **E.V. Ramasamy Naicker** (**Periyar**) — option **(2)**.
**T.M. Nair** co-founded the **Justice Party**; **Narayana Guru** inspired the **SNDP**; **Ambedkar** led the **Mahar** movement.
xa: Aims: attack **caste hierarchy**, **Brahmin priests** and religion.
Journals: **Kudi Arasu**, **Viduthalai**; **Revolt** (English).
It later became the **Dravidar Kazhagam** (**1944**).

194.s: Self-respect marriages, generally conducted without priests, were introduced from which year?
194.x: Self-respect marriages without priests began from 1928 as part of the movement's challenge to caste and religious hierarchy.
194.tq: Distinguish the movement's launch year from the year of a specific reform.
xs: **Self-respect marriages** without priests began from **1928** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**1925** is the launch of the **Self-Respect Movement** itself; **1937** = anti-Hindi agitation; **1940** = **Dravidistan** demand.
xa: Compare **Satyashodhak marriages** (Phule) — inter-caste, without priests, **1873**.
The movement also stood for **women's equality and property rights**.
Founder: **Periyar**.

194.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Self-Respect Movement:
1. It advocated women's equality and property rights.
2. It attacked caste hierarchy and the role of Brahmin priests.
3. It promoted marriages requiring the presence of priests.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
194.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because self-respect marriages were intended to be conducted without priests.
194.tq: Identify the statement that reverses a distinctive feature of the movement.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: it advocated **women's equality and property rights**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: it attacked **caste hierarchy** and **Brahmin priests**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: self-respect marriages were **without priests**.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: Self-respect marriages: from **1928**.
Movement launched **1925** by **Periyar**.

194.s: Which one of the following sets contains the journals associated with Periyar's Self-Respect Movement?
o: Jai Bheem, Veera Bharati and Adi Hindu
Din Bandhu, Vital-Vidhvansak and Kudi Arasu
194.x: Periyar was associated with Kudi Arasu and Viduthalai, while Revolt was his English journal.
194.tq: Separate one reformer's journal group from similarly themed journals.
xs: Periyar's journals were **Kudi Arasu**, **Viduthalai** and **Revolt** (English) — option **(1)**.
**Mooknayak**, **Bahishkrit Bharat** = **Ambedkar**; **Harijan** = **Gandhi**; **Jai Bheem**, **Veera Bharati** = **Jala Rangaswamy**; **Adi Hindu** = **Bhagya Reddy Varma**.
xa: **Din Bandhu** (**1877**) = **Krishnarao Bhalekar**; **Vital-Vidhvansak** (**1888**) = **Gopal Baba Walangkar**.
⚠ **Kudi Arasu** = Periyar; **Mooknayak** = Ambedkar.
**Harijan** weekly: **1933**.

194.s:
Consider the following statements about E.V. Ramasamy (Periyar)'s years in the Congress:
1. He served as president and secretary of the provincial Congress.
2. While in the Congress, he opposed the Hindu Religious Endowments Act.
3. He broke with the Congress in 1925 over non-Brahmin communal representation and caste segregation at the Cheranmadevi Gurukulam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
194.x: Statement 1 is correct: he held both posts in the provincial Congress. Statement 2 is wrong: even as a Congressman he supported the Hindu Religious Endowments Act. Statement 3 is correct: he left in 1925 over communal representation and the Cheranmadevi Gurukulam segregation. So '1 and 3 only'; every other option either includes the false statement 2 or omits statement 3.
194.tq: Periyar 'even then supported' the Endowments Act; break year 1925 = Self-Respect year.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: he was **president and secretary** of the provincial Congress.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: even then he **supported** the **Hindu Religious Endowments Act**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: he broke away in **1925** over **communal representation** and the **Cheranmadevi Gurukulam**.
So **1 and 3 only** — option **(2)** is correct.
xa: The same year (**1925**) he launched the **Self-Respect Movement**.
Earlier he joined **Vaikom** and was jailed → **"Vaikom Veerar"**.

194.s:
Arrange the following developments associated with Periyar and the Dravidian movement in chronological order:
A. Anti-Hindi agitation
B. Launch of the Self-Respect Movement
C. Demand for Dravidistan at Erode
D. Formation of the DMK by C.N. Annadurai
194.x: The Self-Respect Movement was launched in 1925, the anti-Hindi agitation occurred in 1937, the Dravidistan demand was made in 1940, and the DMK was formed in 1949.
194.tq: Place the dated developments first and last before resolving the middle sequence.
xs: Order: **B, A, C, D** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Self-Respect 1925** → **anti-Hindi agitation 1937** → **Dravidistan**, Erode **1940** → **DMK 1949**.
xa: **Dravidar Kazhagam** formed from the Justice Party in **1944**.
DMK founded **17 Sept 1949** by **C.N. Annadurai**; in power from **1967**.
**1937** also = Justice Party's defeat.

194.s:
Consider the following statements about the DMK:
1. It was formed by C.N. Annadurai on 17 September 1949 after a split in the Dravidar Kazhagam.
2. It was founded by Periyar in 1944 from the Justice Party.
3. It came to power in 1967.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
194.x: Statement 1 is correct: Annadurai formed the DMK in 1949 when the DK split. Statement 2 is wrong: Periyar formed the Dravidar Kazhagam (not the DMK) from the Justice Party in 1944. Statement 3 is correct: the DMK came to power in 1967. Hence '1 and 3 only'; options with 2 confuse DK with DMK, and '1 only' omits 1967.
194.tq: 1944 = DK (Periyar); 1949 = DMK (Annadurai); 1967 = DMK in power.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **C.N. Annadurai** formed the **DMK** on **17 Sept 1949** after the DK split.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: Periyar formed the **Dravidar Kazhagam** (not the DMK) from the Justice Party in **1944**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: the DMK came to power in **1967**.
So **1 and 3 only** — option **(2)** is correct.
xa: **Dravidistan** demand: Erode, **1940**.
Self-Respect/DK stream **separated religion and caste from politics**.

194.s: The Self-Respect Movement influenced which Andhra social reformers to adopt the 'Adi' identity and demand temple entry?
o: V.R. Shinde and Gopal Baba Walangkar
T.M. Nair and P. Theagaraya Chetty
Bhagya Reddy Varma and Jala Rangaswamy
194.x: In Andhra, the movement influenced Bhagya Reddy Varma and Jala Rangaswamy to adopt the 'Adi' identity and demand temple entry.
194.tq: Identify the regional impact and the associated reformers.
xs: Self-Respect ideas inspired **Bhagya Reddy Varma** and **Jala Rangaswamy** to adopt the **"Adi"** identity and demand temple entry — option **(3)**.
**V.R. Shinde** (Depressed Classes Mission) and **Walangkar** were Maharashtrian; **Nair/Chetty** founded the Justice Party.
xa: Bhagya Reddy Varma = **"Father of the Dalit movement"** in Hyderabad/Andhra.
Jala Rangaswamy = **Adi Andhra Mahatma**, **Seva Durandhara**.
Contrast: Periyar's movement **anti-religious**; Andhra's mostly **reformist and education-led**.

194.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the Self-Respect Movement and Justice Party politics?
o: The movement strengthened Brahminical dominance within the Justice Party.
The Justice Party opposed all forms of communal representation promoted by the movement.
Its anti-caste and anti-Brahmanical ideas fed the Justice Party's non-Brahmin politics.
The movement was formed from the Justice Party in 1916.
194.x: The Self-Respect Movement's rejection of caste hierarchy and Brahmanical dominance fed the Justice Party's non-Brahmin political orientation.
194.tq: Apply the ideological relationship rather than merely recalling an organisation's date.
xs: Its anti-caste, anti-Brahmanical ideas **fed the Justice Party's non-Brahmin politics** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The Justice Party dates from **1916**; the Self-Respect Movement from **1925**, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: After **1937**, Periyar turned the Justice Party into the **DK** (**1944**).
In Andhra it inspired **Adi-Andhra** leaders.
Non-Brahmin politics helped **Reddys, Kammas and Kapus** rise.

194.s: The Vaikom Satyagraha of 1924–25 primarily demanded:
o: The right of lower castes to use roads around the Vaikom temple
The abolition of the zamindari system in Travancore
The right to draw water from the Chavdar tank
194.x: The Vaikom Satyagraha demanded access for lower castes, including Ezhavas, to the roads around the Vaikom temple in Travancore. It was a temple-entry and civil-rights movement.
194.tq: Separate the Vaikom road-access issue from the Mahad water-rights issue.
xs: Vaikom demanded **the right of lower castes to use roads around the Vaikom temple** — option **(1)**.
The **Chavdar tank** water right was **Ambedkar's Mahad** Satyagraha (**1927**).
xa: Place: **Vaikom (Travancore, Kerala)**, **1924-25**; lower castes included **Ezhavas**.
Nature: **temple entry / civil rights** (APPSC G2 **2023**).
Leaders: **T.K. Madhavan**, **K.P. Kesava Menon**, **K. Kelappan**.

194.s:
Which of the following leaders were associated with the Vaikom Satyagraha?
1. T.K. Madhavan
2. K.P. Kesava Menon
3. K. Kelappan
4. A.K. Gopalan

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
194.x: T.K. Madhavan, K.P. Kesava Menon and K. Kelappan were associated with Vaikom. A.K. Gopalan is listed with the Guruvayur Satyagraha.
194.tq: Separate leaders of the closely related Vaikom and Guruvayur movements.
xs: **T.K. Madhavan**, **K.P. Kesava Menon** and **K. Kelappan** led Vaikom — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(1)**.
**A.K. Gopalan** is linked with **Guruvayur** (**1931-32**), not Vaikom.
xa: Vaikom was backed by **Narayana Guru**; **Periyar** joined.
**Kelappan** also led **Guruvayur**.
**Gandhi** visited Vaikom in **1925**.

194.s: Periyar E.V. Ramasamy earned the title “Vaikom Veerar” because he:
o: Joined the Vaikom Satyagraha and was jailed
Led the Mahad Satyagraha in Maharashtra
Negotiated the Travancore Temple Entry Proclamation of 1936
194.x: Periyar joined the Vaikom Satyagraha and was imprisoned, after which he became known as “Vaikom Veerar”.
194.tq: Link the title to the specific action and movement rather than to a later reform.
xs: Periyar **joined the Vaikom Satyagraha and was jailed** → **"Vaikom Veerar"** — option **(1)**.
⚠ Vaikom Veerar = **Periyar**, not **Narayana Guru** (Guru only backed Vaikom).
xa: Periyar is also called the **Hero of Vaikom**.
**Mahad** (**1927**) was **Ambedkar's**.
Outcome of Vaikom: **Travancore Temple Entry Proclamation (1936)**.

194.s: What was Mahatma Gandhi’s role in the Vaikom Satyagraha?
o: He organised the Chavdar Tank Satyagraha in Maharashtra
He visited Vaikom in 1925 and negotiated with the Travancore authorities
He founded the SNDP Yogam in 1903
He led the movement in 1936 after the Temple Entry Proclamation
194.x: Gandhi visited Vaikom in 1925 and negotiated with the Travancore authorities; a compromise subsequently opened some roads.
194.tq: Identify the precise role performed by the national leader instead of attributing leadership of another movement.
xs: **Gandhi visited Vaikom in 1925** and **negotiated with the Travancore authorities** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The compromise **opened some roads**.
xa: **Chavdar Tank** = **Ambedkar's Mahad** Satyagraha (**1927**).
**SNDP Yogam** (**1903**) was inspired by **Sree Narayana Guru**.
Outcome: **Travancore Temple Entry Proclamation (1936)**.

194.s: The Vaikom Satyagraha eventually helped lead to which development?
o: Establishment of the Independent Labour Party in 1936
Formation of the Nadar Mahajana Sangam in 1910
Formation of the Justice Party in the Madras Presidency
194.x: The Vaikom Satyagraha contributed to the developments culminating in the Travancore Temple Entry Proclamation of 1936.
194.tq: Connect the movement with its later constitutional-social outcome by using the year clue.
xs: Vaikom led on to the **Travancore Temple Entry Proclamation of 1936** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **ILP** (**1936**) was **Ambedkar's** party, unrelated to Vaikom.
xa: Vaikom: **1924-25**, roads around the **Vaikom temple**.
**Gandhi's** **1925** visit brought a compromise.
Later temple entry: **Guruvayur** (**1931-32**), **Siddhantam** (**17 Dec 1933**).

194.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Vaikom Satyagraha
B. Guruvayur Satyagraha
C. Mahad Satyagraha
D. Kalaram Temple Satyagraha
194.x: Vaikom took place in 1924–25, Mahad in 1927, Kalaram Temple in 1930, and Guruvayur in 1931–32.
194.tq: Place the movements by their years, paying attention to the two events after 1930.
xs: Order: **A, C, D, B** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Vaikom 1924-25** → **Mahad 1927** → **Kalaram Temple 1930** → **Guruvayur 1931-32**.
xa: **Lakshminarayan Temple, Wardha**: **1928** (**Jamnalal Bajaj**).
**Siddhantam** (Krishna): **17 Dec 1933**.
⚠ **Mahad** was about **water rights**, not a temple.

194.s:
Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Mahad Satyagraha from the Vaikom Satyagraha?
1. Mahad concerned water rights, whereas Vaikom concerned access to roads around a temple.
2. Mahad was led by B.R. Ambedkar, whereas Vaikom involved leaders such as T.K. Madhavan and K.P. Kesava Menon.
3. Both movements took place in Kerala.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
194.x: Mahad concerned the right to draw water from the Chavdar tank in Maharashtra and was led by Ambedkar. Vaikom occurred in Travancore, Kerala; therefore statement 3 is false.
194.tq: Use the issue and location columns to reject the reversed comparison.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Mahad** = **water rights** (Chavdar tank); **Vaikom** = roads around a temple.
Statement 2 is **correct**: Mahad led by **Ambedkar**; Vaikom by **T.K. Madhavan** and **K.P. Kesava Menon**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: **Mahad** was in **Kolaba, Maharashtra**; only Vaikom was in Kerala.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: Mahad: **20 March 1927**, organised by the **Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha**.
After Mahad, INC's Anti-Untouchability Subcommittee reconstituted under **Malaviya**.

194.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes Gandhi's Andhra tour of 1932–33?
o: It collected Harijana Bhiksha and included a temple-entry initiative at Siddhantam.
It organised the Coolie Sangham exclusively for industrialists.
It established the Scheduled Castes Federation at Siddhantam.
It launched the Civil Disobedience Movement at Vizianagaram.
194.x:
During his 1932–33 Andhra tour, Gandhi collected Harijana Bhiksha and launched temple entry at Siddhantam in Krishna district on 17 December 1933.
⚠ Sources differ: Census 2011 lists a Sidhantham in Penugonda mandal, West Godavari; the 1933 tour chronology puts the 17 Dec 1933 Siddhantam visit among Krishna district stops. This key follows the notes (Krishna district).
194.tq: Combine the purpose, local campaign and place of a regional tour.
xs: On his **1932-33** Andhra tour Gandhi **collected Harijana Bhiksha** and there was a **temple-entry** move at **Siddhantam** — option **(1)**.
The **Coolie Sangham** was organised by the **communists** for **Dalit labour**, not industrialists.
xa: Siddhantam (**Krishna** district per notes): **17 Dec 1933**.
Congress track: **Harijan Sevak Sangh**.
The **Scheduled Castes Federation** (**1942**) was **Ambedkar's**.

194.s: The Coolie Sangham for Dalit labour was organised by:
194.x: The communists organised the Coolie Sangham for Dalit labour.
194.tq: Identify the organisation by the political group associated with its formation.
xs: The **communists** organised the **Coolie Sangham** for Dalit labour — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Anti-Untouchability League** was **Gandhi's** (**1932**); **Depressed Classes Mission** = **V.R. Shinde** (**1906**); **SCF** = **Ambedkar** (**1942**).
xa: Congress track: **Harijan Sevak Sangh**; temple entry at **Siddhantam**, **1933**.
Gandhi's **1932-33** tour collected **Harijana Bhiksha**.
**Kusuma Dharmanna** urged Dalits towards **socialism** (**1936**).

194.s:
With reference to the temple-entry movements, consider the following pairs:
a. Vaikom — Travancore
b. Guruvayur — Malabar
c. Siddhantam — Krishna district
d. Lakshminarayan Temple — Wardha
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
194.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Vaikom was in Travancore, Guruvayur in Malabar, Siddhantam in Krishna district and the Lakshminarayan Temple was at Wardha.
194.tq: Match each movement with its location before checking the combined code.
xs: All four pairs are **correct**: **Vaikom – Travancore**; **Guruvayur – Malabar**; **Siddhantam – Krishna district**; **Lakshminarayan Temple – Wardha**.
So **a, b, c and d** — option **(4)** is correct.
xa: Years: Vaikom **1924-25**; Wardha **1928**; Guruvayur **1931-32**; Siddhantam **1933**.
Wardha temple opened by **Jamnalal Bajaj**.
Guruvayur leaders: **K. Kelappan**, **A.K. Gopalan**.

194.s: Which statement regarding the Guruvayur Satyagraha is correct?
o: It was an Andhra movement led by Siddhantam Congress leaders.
It took place in Travancore during 1924–25.
It opened the Lakshminarayan Temple to Dalits in 1928.
It took place in Malabar during 1931–32, with K. Kelappan undertaking a fast.
194.x: The Guruvayur Satyagraha took place in Malabar in 1931–32. K. Kelappan fasted and A.K. Gopalan was associated with the movement; Gandhi asked Kelappan to end his fast.
194.tq: Separate the place and dates of Guruvayur from those of Vaikom.
xs: **Guruvayur** was in **Malabar** during **1931-32**, with **K. Kelappan** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**1924-25, Travancore** = **Vaikom**; **Wardha 1928** = **Lakshminarayan Temple**; **Siddhantam** = Andhra (**1933**).
xa: **A.K. Gopalan** was the other Guruvayur leader.
Kelappan was also a **Vaikom** leader.
Vaikom led to the **Travancore Temple Entry Proclamation (1936)**.

194.s: The Lakshminarayan Temple at Wardha was opened to Dalits in 1928 by:
194.x: Jamnalal Bajaj opened the Lakshminarayan Temple at Wardha to Dalits in 1928.
194.tq: Apply the founder-or-doer trap to a temple-entry reform.
xs: **Jamnalal Bajaj** opened the **Lakshminarayan Temple, Wardha** to Dalits in **1928** — option **(3)**.
**Kelappan** led Vaikom/Guruvayur; **Malaviya** headed the INC Anti-Untouchability Subcommittee after Mahad.
xa: **A.V. Thakkar** was secretary of the **All India Anti-Untouchability League** (**1932**).
League president: **G.D. Birla**.

194.s: After the Mahad Satyagraha, the Indian National Congress reconstituted its Anti-Untouchability Subcommittee under:
194.x: After the Mahad Satyagraha, the INC reconstituted its Anti-Untouchability Subcommittee under Madan Mohan Malaviya.
194.tq: Test the person placed in charge rather than the movement associated with the issue.
xs: After Mahad, the INC reconstituted its **Anti-Untouchability Subcommittee** under **Madan Mohan Malaviya** — option **(3)**.
**G.D. Birla** and **A.V. Thakkar** were president and secretary of Gandhi's **Anti-Untouchability League** (**1932**).
xa: Mahad (**1927**): **Ambedkar**, right to water from the **Chavdar tank**.
Also **1927**: **Manusmriti Dahan** (**25 Dec**).
The League was renamed **Harijan Sevak Sangh** (**1933**).

194.s: The Vaikom Satyagraha (1924-25) was associated with the:
194.x: Vaikom in Travancore was a temple-entry and civil-rights struggle for lower castes' use of the roads around the Vaikom temple. Khilafat was a pan-Islamic agitation; the Chavdar tank was the Mahad Satyagraha (1927); self-respect marriages began under Periyar from 1928.
194.tq: Vaikom -> Temple Entry Movement (APPSC-G2 2023).
xs: Vaikom (**1924-25**) was associated with the **Temple Entry Movement** — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC-G2 **2023**).
The **Chavdar tank** struggle was **Mahad** (**1927**); **self-respect marriages** began from **1928** under Periyar.
xa: Issue: lower castes' use of **roads around the Vaikom temple**.
Leaders: **T.K. Madhavan**, **K.P. Kesava Menon**, **K. Kelappan**.
Outcome: **Travancore Temple Entry Proclamation (1936)**.

194.s: The term “Adi” in the Adi-Andhra and Adi-Hindu movements signified which of the following?
194.x: “Adi” means original inhabitants. The movements rejected the term “Panchama” and sought a more dignified identity for Dalit communities.
194.tq: Directly identify the exact meaning of a movement-related term.
xs: **"Adi"** means **original inhabitants** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The Adi movements **rejected the term Panchama**.
xa: **Adi Andhra** = Dalits of the Andhra (Madras) region; **Adi Hindu** = Dalits of Hyderabad State.
The **1917 resolution** asked to replace "Panchama" by these names.
"Adi Andhra" (**1917**) = first Dalit identity assertion in Telugu country.

194.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Adi-Andhra from Adi-Hindu?
o: Adi-Andhra referred to tribal communities of Andhra, while Adi-Hindu referred to Dalits of Madras city.
Adi-Andhra and Adi-Hindu were names exclusively used for the same organisation.
Adi-Andhra referred to Dalits of Hyderabad State, while Adi-Hindu referred to Dalits of coastal Andhra.
Adi-Andhra referred to Dalits of the Andhra region, while Adi-Hindu referred to Dalits of Hyderabad State.
194.x: Adi-Andhra referred to Dalits of Andhra, including coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema, whereas Adi-Hindu referred to Dalits of Hyderabad State.
194.tq: Discriminate between two closely related regional labels.
xs: **Adi-Andhra** = Dalits of the **Andhra region**; **Adi-Hindu** = Dalits of **Hyderabad State** — option **(4)**.
Option (3) reverses them.
xa: Adi Andhra covers **coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema**.
Both terms were popularised by **Madari Bhagya Reddy Varma**.
Adi-Hindu groups: **Malas, Madigas**.

194.s: Who popularised the terms Adi-Andhra and Adi-Hindu and was regarded as the father of the Dalit movement in Hyderabad and Andhra?
194.x: Madari Bhagya Reddy Varma popularised both terms and is regarded as the father of the Dalit movement in Hyderabad and Andhra.
194.tq: Use the leader-title association to identify the correct personality.
xs: **Madari Bhagya Reddy Varma** popularised both terms and is the **"Father of the Dalit movement"** — option **(4)**.
**Undru Tatayya** held the **1921 Amalapuram** Sadassu; **Jala Rangaswamy** = **Adi Andhra Mahatma**; **Arige Ramaswamy** = Madiga leader.
xa: Born **1888**, Hyderabad; original name **Madari Bagaiah**.
**Manya Sangham** (**1911**) → **Adi Hindu Social Service League**.
Journal: **Adi Hindu**.

194.s: The original name of Bhagya Reddy Varma was
194.x: Bhagya Reddy Varma was originally named Madari Bagaiah.
194.tq: Test a biographical detail directly rather than the better-known public name.
xs: Bhagya Reddy Varma was originally **Madari Bagaiah** (Madari Bhagaiah) — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was born in **1888** in **Hyderabad** (some notes say **1880**).
xa: He presided over the first **Panchama Mahajana Sabha** (**1917**) — asked in **2019**.
He presided over the **All India Adi Hindu Conference**, **Lucknow, 1930**.
He opposed **child marriage**, **liquor** and the **Devadasi** system.

194.s: The early Adi-Andhra Sabha was first known as the
194.x: The early Adi-Andhra Sabha, dating to 1890, was first called the Pariya Mahasabha.
194.tq: Identify the earlier name of an organisation.
xs: The **Adi-Andhra Sabha (1890)** was first called the **Pariya Mahasabha** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Panchama Mahajana Sabha** was the first **Adi-Andhra session** of **1917**, at Vijayawada.
xa: Formative phase: **Adi Andhra Mahasabha 1917-1931**.
**Rajahmundry Nimna Jati Uddharana Sangham** was a separate body.
"Adi" = original inhabitants; rejected **Panchama**.

194.s:
The 1917 resolution of the first Adi-Andhra session included which of the following?
1. Replacement of the term “Panchama” by “Adi Andhra” in the Madras region.
2. Replacement of the term “Panchama” by “Adi Hindu” in Hyderabad.
3. Provision of special schools and wells in Dalit wadas.
4. Reservation of seats in local bodies and councils.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
194.x: The 1917 resolution sought the replacement of “Panchama” by regionally appropriate names, representation in local bodies and councils, special schools, and access to wells in Dalit wadas.
194.tq: Treat each component of a resolution as an independently testable statement.
xs: The **1917** resolution sought all four: "**Adi Andhra**" (Madras) and "**Adi Hindu**" (Hyderabad) for "Panchama", **special schools and wells**, and **seats in local bodies and councils**.
So **1, 2, 3 and 4** — option **(4)** is correct.
xa: Session: **First Panchama Mahajana Sabha**, **Vijayawada**, **4-6 Nov 1917**.
President: **Bhagya Reddy Varma**.
"Adi Andhra" came into **official use** after it.

194.s:
Consider the following statements about the early Adi-Andhra conferences:
1. The first Provincial Panchama Mahajana Sabha, the first Adi-Andhra session, was held at Mailavaram Rajayya Nataka Mandir, Vijayawada (Krishna district).
2. That first session was held in November 1921.
3. The second conference was held at Machilipatnam in 1919.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
194.x: Statement 1 is correct: the first session met at Mailavaram Rajayya Nataka Mandir, Vijayawada, in Krishna district. Statement 2 is wrong: it was held on 4-6 November 1917 (1921 is the Amalapuram Sadassu). Statement 3 is correct: the second conference was at Machilipatnam in 1919. Hence '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' drops a true statement, and options with 2 include the wrong year.
194.tq: Krishna district hub: Vijayawada 1917, Machilipatnam 1919; 1921 = Amalapuram.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: first session at **Mailavaram Rajayya Nataka Mandir, Vijayawada (Krishna district)**.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: it met on **4-6 Nov 1917**; **1921** is the **Amalapuram** Sadassu.
Statement 3 is **correct**: 2nd conference, **Machilipatnam**, **1919**.
So **1 and 3 only** — option **(2)** is correct.
xa: ⚠ APPSC-GS **2025** key: district of the first session = **Krishna**.
**1919** president: **Chilukuri Venkataswamy** — priority to **Dalit education**.

194.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Person)
(a) Bhagya Reddy Varma
(b) Guduru Ramachandra Rao
(c) Sundru Venkayya
(d) Chilukuri Venkataswamy

List-II (Role)
(i) President of the 1919 conference
(ii) President of the first Provincial Panchama Mahajana Sabha
(iii) Organiser of the first Provincial Panchama Mahajana Sabha
(iv) Chairman of the reception committee

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
194.x: Bhagya Reddy Varma was president, Guduru Ramachandra Rao organiser, Sundru Venkayya reception chairman, and Chilukuri Venkataswamy presided over the 1919 conference.
194.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes using the remaining role associations.
xs: Correct match: **a–ii, b–iii, c–iv, d–i** — option **(1)**.
