204.x: The correct order is 1907 deportation of Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh, 1908 deportation of Tilak, Aurobindo's acquittal in 1909 and his retirement to Pondicherry in 1910.
204.tq: Anchor the sequence to the years 1907, 1908, 1909 and 1910.
xs: The order is **A, B, C, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**A:** **Lajpat Rai** and **Ajit Singh** deported to **Mandalay** in **1907**.
**B:** **Tilak** sent to **Mandalay** in **1908** (6-year sedition sentence).
**C:** **Aurobindo** acquitted in the **Alipore case** in **1909**; **D:** he retired to **Pondicherry** in **1910**.
xa: Tilak was released on **16 June 1914**; he wrote **Gita Rahasya** in Mandalay.
Aurobindo was the first principal of **Bengal National College**.
Lajpat Rai went to the **USA** after **1908** and set up the **Indian Home Rule League of America (1917)**.
⚠ Both Lajpat Rai (**1907**) and Tilak (**1908**) were sent to **Mandalay** — do not mix up the years.

204.s: The Swadeshi Movement was formally launched on 7 August in which year?
204.x: The Swadeshi Movement was launched on 7 August 1905, following the partition of Bengal.
204.tq: Test the year attached to a dated movement rather than its broader phase.
xs: The **Swadeshi Movement** was launched on **7 August 1905** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It followed the **Partition of Bengal** in the same year, **1905**.
**1906** was the **Calcutta session (Naoroji)**, which passed the Swadeshi resolution; **1907** was the **Surat Split**.
xa: Calcutta **1906** resolutions: **Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education**; "Swaraj" left undefined.
The Partition was **annulled in 1911**.
APPSC-G1 **2024**: Swadeshi, Surat Split, Lucknow Pact and Home Rule all fall in the **extremist phase**.
Order check: **INC 1885 → Bengal partition 1905 → Muslim League 1906 → Surat 1907**.

204.s: Which one of the following events took place in 1911?
o: The Partition of Bengal was annulled
The Tilak Home Rule League was founded
204.x: The Partition of Bengal was annulled in 1911. Tilak was released in 1914, the Lucknow Pact was concluded in 1916, and the Tilak Home Rule League began in 1916.
204.tq: Discriminate among closely spaced chronological milestones.
xs: In **1911** the **Partition of Bengal was annulled** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Lucknow Pact** came in **December 1916**.
**Tilak's Home Rule League** was founded on **28 Apr 1916**.
**Tilak was released** from Mandalay on **16 June 1914**.
xa: The Partition itself and the **Swadeshi Movement (7 Aug)** date from **1905**.
**1908**: Tilak to Mandalay and the **Newspapers Act**.
**Besant's Home Rule League** followed in **September 1916**.
The Congress **reunion** at **Lucknow (1916)** healed the **Surat Split** of **1907**.

204.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Tilak's Home Rule League was founded on 28 April 1916.
2. Annie Besant's Home Rule League was founded in September 1916.
3. The Congress reunion and Lucknow Pact took place in December 1916.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
204.x: All three statements are correct. Tilak began his league on 28 April 1916, Besant’s in September, and the reunion and Lucknow Pact occurred in December.
204.tq: Check dates within the same year instead of treating all Home Rule events as simultaneous.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Statement 1** is correct: **Tilak's Home Rule League** was founded on **28 Apr 1916**.
**Statement 2** is correct: **Besant's** league followed in **September 1916**.
**Statement 3** is correct: the **Lucknow Pact** and **Congress reunion** came in **December 1916**.
xa: Tilak's league: president **Joseph Baptista**, secretary **N.C. Kelkar**.
**52 Home Rule branches** existed in **Andhra by 1917**.
Besant ran **New India** (the renamed **Madras Standard**) and **Commonweal (Jan 1914)**.
Under the Press Act Besant paid **Rs 2,000** security, then **Rs 10,000** more, to keep publishing.

204.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Surat Split
B. Lucknow Pact
C. Swadeshi Movement
D. Morley-Minto Reforms
204.x: The sequence is Swadeshi Movement in 1905, Surat Split in 1907, Morley-Minto Reforms in 1909 and Lucknow Pact in 1916.
204.tq: Place the events by their years before comparing the middle items.
xs: The order is **C, A, D, B** — option **(1)**.
**C:** **Swadeshi Movement**, launched **7 Aug 1905**.
**D:** **Morley-Minto Reforms** come next in the keyed order, before **B:** the **Lucknow Pact** of **December 1916**.
xa: Surat **1907** president: **Rash Behari Ghosh**; Calcutta **1906** president: **Naoroji**.
The split was **healed at Lucknow in 1916**.
**Tilak's Home Rule League (28 Apr 1916)** and **Besant's (Sept 1916)** both preceded the Lucknow Pact.
Between Surat and Lucknow: **Partition annulled (1911)**, **Tilak released (1914)**.

204.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
a. Partition of Bengal
b. Formation of the Muslim League
c. Surat Split
d. Founding of the Indian National Congress
204.x: INC 1885 (d), partition of Bengal 1905 (a), Muslim League 1906 (b), Surat Split 1907 (c), so d, a, b, c. The trap is the printed key 'b, d, a, c' (option D), which wrongly puts the Muslim League before the founding of the INC.
204.tq: 1885 INC -> 1905 partition -> 1906 League -> 1907 Surat
xs: The correct order is **d, a, b, c** — option **(1)**.
**d:** **Indian National Congress** founded **1885**; **a:** **Partition of Bengal 1905**.
**b:** **Muslim League** formed **1906**; **c:** **Surat Split 1907**.
Option (4) **b, d, a, c** puts the Muslim League before the INC's founding — wrong.
xa: ⚠ Trap: a printed key "**b, d, a, c**" exists; the true order is **d-a-b-c** (INC first).
Moderate phase: **1885-1905**; Extremist phase: **1905-1916**.
Surat **1907**: Moderates under **Gokhale** (and Mehta) vs Extremists under **Tilak**.
The **Swadeshi Movement** began on **7 Aug 1905**, the year of the partition.

204.s: The Extremists contributed to the national movement by:
o: turning nationalism into a mass movement and making Swaraj its goal
supporting permanent British control over India
restricting nationalism to educated constitutional petitioners
204.x: The Extremists broadened nationalism into a mass movement and placed Swaraj at the centre of the political goal.
204.tq: Identify the principal historical significance rather than a method or criticism.
xs: The Extremists **turned nationalism into a mass movement** and **made Swaraj the goal** — so option **(1)** is correct.
They took politics to **students, women, workers and peasants**, beyond the Moderates' **urban educated elite**.
They used **Swadeshi, boycott and national education** — so (3) is wrong; and **Swaraj** meant complete freedom, not British control — so (2) is wrong.
Restricting politics to petitions (the **3 Ps**) was the **Moderates'** method — so (4) is wrong.
xa: Extremist methods = **3 Ss**: **self-reliance, self-sacrifice, strong will**; plus mass agitation.
**Spiritual nationalism**: nation as mother goddess (**Bande Mataram**, **Bhavani Mandir**); Hindu festivals for mass contact.
**Atmashakti** (self-reliance): constructive work such as **cooperatives**.
⚠ **3 Ps** (prayers, petitions, protests) = Moderates; **3 Ss** = Extremists.

204.s: Which of the following was a criticism of Extremist politics?
o: Its religious symbolism alienated Muslims and its social outlook was orthodox.
It weakened the demand for Swaraj by supporting colonial rule.
It completely rejected all cultural symbols.
It prevented the use of boycott and Swadeshi.
204.x: The Extremists were criticised for using religious symbolism that alienated Muslims and for being socially orthodox. The Surat Split was also regarded as weakening the Congress.
204.tq: Select the option containing the recognised criticisms without reversing the Extremist programme.
xs: The Extremists' **religious symbolism alienated Muslims** and their outlook was **socially orthodox** — option **(1)**.
Tilak, for example, **opposed the Age of Consent Bill**.

They did not support colonial rule (they demanded **Swaraj**), did not reject cultural symbols (they used **Bande Mataram**, Hindu festivals), and they **championed boycott and Swadeshi** — so (2), (3), (4) are wrong.
xa: Another criticism: the **Surat Split** weakened the Congress.
Tilak made **Ganesh Utsav (1893)** and **Shivaji Jayanti (1895)** public festivals.
The Moderates, by contrast, were **pro-social reform**.
Significance: the Extremists turned nationalism into a **mass movement** and made **Swaraj** the goal.

204.s: What did students of the Machilipatnam National College wear after Annie Besant's arrest on 15 June 1917?
204.x: Students of the Machilipatnam National College wore Besant lockets after Annie Besant was arrested on 15 June 1917.
204.tq: Link the protest action with the person and triggering date.
xs: Students of the **Machilipatnam National College** wore **"Besant lockets"** after Annie Besant's arrest on **15 June 1917** — option **(1)**.
It shows the strength of the **Home Rule movement** in Andhra.
xa: Andhra had **52 Home Rule branches by 1917**.
**Besant's Home Rule League** was founded in **September 1916**; Tilak's on **28 Apr 1916**.
Besant's papers: **New India** (renamed **Madras Standard**) and **Commonweal**.
Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao = **"Andhra Tilak"**, jailed in **1908**.

204.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra in the Extremist phase:
1. Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was known as Andhra Tilak.
2. Andhra had 52 Home Rule branches by 1917.
3. Students of the Rajahmundry college wore Besant lockets after Annie Besant's arrest in 1917.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
204.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Gadicherla was called Andhra Tilak, and Andhra had 52 Home Rule branches by 1917. Statement 3 is wrong: it was students of the Machilipatnam National College who wore Besant lockets after her arrest on 15 June 1917. So '1 only' is incomplete and options with 3 are wrong.
204.tq: Andhra Tilak = Gadicherla; 52 HR branches by 1917
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Statement 1** is correct: **Gadicherla** was called **"Andhra Tilak"**.
**Statement 2** is correct: Andhra had **52 Home Rule branches by 1917**.
**Statement 3** is wrong: the **Besant lockets** were worn by students of the **Machilipatnam National College**, not a Rajahmundry college.
xa: Besant was arrested on **15 June 1917**.
Gadicherla was **jailed in 1908**.
**Bipin Chandra Pal** toured **Andhra in April 1907**.
⚠ "Andhra Tilak" = Gadicherla; Tilak himself was **"Lokmanya"** and, to **Valentine Chirol**, the **"Father of Indian Unrest"**.

205.s:
Which of the following events was associated with the tenure of Lord Minto II as Viceroy?
1. Formation of the Muslim League
2. Surat Split
3. Newspapers Act
4. Muzaffarpur case
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: Lord Minto II was Viceroy from 1905 to 1910, during which the Muslim League was formed in 1906, the Surat Split occurred in 1907, and the Newspapers Act and Muzaffarpur case occurred in 1908.
205.tq: Place several contemporaneous events within the correct tenure.
xs: All four events fall in **Lord Minto II's** tenure — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Minto was **Viceroy 1905-1910**: **Muslim League (1906)**, **Surat Split (1907)**, **Newspapers Act (1908)** and **Muzaffarpur case (1908)**.
The **Swadeshi-Boycott** movement also ran during his tenure.
xa: Minto is called the **"Father of the Communal Electorate"**.
His Secretary of State was **John Morley**; together they gave the **Indian Councils Act 1909**.
The **Simla Deputation** met Minto on **1 Oct 1906**.
Repression failed to stop protests, and both were eventually **replaced**.

205.s: Who is associated with the description 'Father of the Communal Electorate'?
205.x: Lord Minto is associated with the title 'Father of the Communal Electorate' because the Morley-Minto Reforms introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
205.tq: Link the popular epithet to the reform and Viceroy of the same period.
xs: **Lord Minto** (Minto II) is called the **"Father of the Communal Electorate"** — option **(3)**.
The **Morley-Minto Reforms (1909)** introduced **separate electorates for Muslims** with **weightage**.
**Montagu-Chelmsford** belong to the **1919** Act, which extended (not began) communal representation.
xa: Minto was **Viceroy (1905-1910)**; **John Morley** was **Secretary of State for India**.
The demand came from the **Simla Deputation (1 Oct 1906)** led by **Aga Khan**.
Exam angle: "Which Act introduced the communal electorate?" → **Morley-Minto 1909**.
⚠ UPSC notes wrongly say Minto expanded the Councils Act in **1919**; the 1919 Act was **Chelmsford's**.

205.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the offices held by Morley and Minto in connection with the Indian Councils Act, 1909?
o: Morley was the President of Congress and Minto was the Governor of Bengal.
Morley was the Viceroy and Minto was the Secretary of State.
Morley was the Secretary of State and Minto was the Viceroy.
Both Morley and Minto were Viceroys of India.
205.x: John Morley was the Secretary of State for India, while Lord Minto was the Viceroy.
205.tq: Discriminate between two closely associated authorities by office.
xs: **Morley was the Secretary of State** for India (in London) and **Minto was the Viceroy** — option **(3)**.
Hence the popular name **Morley-Minto (Minto-Morley) Reforms** for the **Indian Councils Act 1909**.
Option (2) reverses the offices; neither was a Congress president or Governor of Bengal.
xa: Minto's term as Viceroy: **1905-1910**.
**Gokhale** went to England in **1906** and met Morley to press for self-government like other colonies.
Aim of the reforms: **rally the Moderates** and **reward Muslim loyalty**.
**S.P. Sinha** became the first Indian on the **Viceroy's Executive Council** (Law Member).

205.s: The Simla Deputation led by Aga Khan III met Lord Minto on:
205.x: The Simla Deputation, led by Aga Khan III, met Lord Minto on 1 October 1906.
205.tq: Separate two closely connected 1906 dates by linking each to its event.
xs: The **Simla Deputation** led by **Aga Khan III** met **Lord Minto** on **1 October 1906** — option **(2)**.
**30 December 1906** was the founding of the **Muslim League** at **Dacca**.
**12 December 1911** = annulment of partition at the **Delhi Durbar**; **20 August 1917** = **August Declaration**.
xa: It demanded **separate electorates** and **weightage** for Muslims.
⚠ **1 Oct 1906** = Simla Deputation; **30 Dec 1906** = League founded (Dacca).
Aga Khan became the League's **first president**.
The demand was met by the **Indian Councils Act 1909**.

205.s:
The Simla Deputation of 1906 demanded:
1. Separate electorates for Muslims
2. Weightage for Muslims
3. Representation based on their contribution to the Empire's defence
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: The deputation demanded separate electorates and weightage, justifying the demand by referring to the Muslims' contribution to the defence of the Empire.
205.tq: Combine the demands with the stated justification rather than selecting only the headline demand.
xs: All three demands were made — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
It asked for **separate electorates** and **weightage** for Muslims.
Justification: their **"contribution to the empire's defence"**.
xa: Led by **Aga Khan (III)** to **Lord Minto** on **1 October 1906**.
**Weightage** = more seats than the community's population share.
The **1909 Act** granted **separate electorates with weightage** — its most critical feature.
The **Muslim League** followed on **30 Dec 1906** at Dacca.

205.s:
Consider the following statements about the All India Muslim League:
1. It was founded on 30 December 1906 at Dacca, at the session of the All-India Muhammadan Educational Conference.
2. Its formation was proposed by Nawab Salimullah of Dacca.
3. Syed Ameer Ali was its first president.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: Statement 1 is correct: the League was founded on 30 December 1906 at Dacca during the Muhammadan Educational Conference session. Statement 2 is correct: Nawab Salimullah proposed it. Statement 3 is wrong: Aga Khan was the first president; Syed Ameer Ali set up the London branch in 1908. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
205.tq: Proposer Salimullah, president Aga Khan, London branch Ameer Ali.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Statement 1** correct: founded **30 December 1906** at **Dacca**, at the **All-India Muhammadan Educational Conference** session.
**Statement 2** correct: proposed by **Nawab Salimullah of Dacca**.
**Statement 3** wrong: **Aga Khan** was the first president; **Syed Ameer Ali** set up the **London branch (1908)**.
xa: Early aims: **loyalty to the British Empire**, safeguarding Muslim interests, keeping Muslims away from the Congress.
**Jinnah** joined the League in **1913**.
The **Simla Deputation (1 Oct 1906)** preceded the League's founding.

205.s: Which one of the following was NOT an aim of the All-India Muslim League in its early phase?
o: Keeping Muslims away from the Congress
Launching an immediate armed revolt against British rule
Promoting loyalty to the British Empire
205.x: The early League aimed at loyalty to the British Empire, protection of Muslim political interests and separation from the Congress; immediate armed revolt was not one of its stated aims.
205.tq: Reject the extreme revolutionary alternative when testing an organisation's declared aims.
xs: **Launching an immediate armed revolt** was **not** an aim — option **(3)**.
The early League's aims were **loyalty to the British Empire**, **safeguarding Muslim political interests** and **keeping Muslims away from the Congress** — options (1), (2), (4).
xa: Founded **30 Dec 1906** at **Dacca**; proposed by **Nawab Salimullah**; first president **Aga Khan**.
**1912-24**: the League was dominated by **younger Muslim nationalists**.
By **1916** it allied with the Congress in the **Lucknow Pact**.
London branch: **Syed Ameer Ali (1908)**.

205.s: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 provided for which of the following electoral arrangements?
o: Election by a single national constituency
Universal adult franchise through direct elections
205.x: The 1909 reforms introduced indirect, multi-tier elections rather than direct universal elections.
205.tq: Discriminate between direct, indirect and nominated representation.
xs: The **1909 Act** provided **indirect, multi-tier elections** — option **(4)**.
It also introduced **separate electorates for Muslims** with weightage, and **elected** non-official members for the first time.
**Direct elections** at the Centre came only with the **1919 Act** — so (3) is wrong.
xa: Central Legislative Council enlarged (additional members **to 60**).
**Official majority retained at the Centre**; non-official majority in provinces.
Councils could **discuss the budget** but **not vote** on it.
**1935 Act** extended separate electorates to depressed classes, women and labour.

205.s:
With reference to the Indian Councils Act, 1909, consider the following statements:
1. The Central Legislative Council was enlarged to 60 additional members.
2. An official majority was retained at the Centre.
3. A non-official majority was provided in the provinces.
4. The Governor's veto made the provincial non-official majority ineffective in practice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: All four are correct: the 1909 Act enlarged the Central Legislative Council (additional members up to 60) but kept an official majority at the Centre, and gave the provinces a non-official majority that the Governor's veto left powerless in practice. So 1, 2, 3 and 4.
205.tq: Read constitutional composition and actual executive control together.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**1:** Central Legislative Council enlarged — additional members **to 60**.
**2:** **Official majority retained at the Centre**.
**3 and 4:** **Non-official majority in provinces**, but the **Governor's veto** left them powerless.
xa: Most critical feature: **separate electorates for Muslims** with **weightage**.
Councils could not **vote on the budget** or question **military affairs**.
**S.P. Sinha** joined the Executive Council as **Law Member**.
Aim: **rally the Moderates** + **reward Muslim loyalty**.

205.s: Which of the following powers was NOT granted to members under the Indian Councils Act, 1909?
205.x: Members could discuss the budget, ask supplementary questions and move resolutions, but they could not vote on the budget.
205.tq: Find the one power excluded from an otherwise expanded legislative role.
xs: Members could **not vote on the budget** — option **(1)**.
They **could discuss the budget**, **ask supplementary questions** and **move resolutions** — options (2), (3), (4) were granted.
They also could not question **military affairs**.
xa: **Official majority** stayed at the Centre.
Provinces had a **non-official majority**, blunted by the **Governor's veto**.
Elections were **indirect, multi-tier**.
Introduced by **John Morley** (Secretary of State) and **Lord Minto** (Viceroy).

205.s:
Consider the following statements about Satyendra Prasanna Sinha:
1. He was the first Indian member of the Viceroy's Executive Council.
2. He held the Finance portfolio on the Council.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
205.x: Statement 1 is correct: S.P. Sinha was the first Indian member of the Viceroy's Executive Council (1909). Statement 2 is wrong: he was the Law Member. Hence '1 only'.
205.tq: S.P. Sinha = first Indian, Law Member.
xs: Only **statement 1** is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
**Statement 1** correct: **Satyendra Prasanna Sinha** was the **first Indian member of the Viceroy's Executive Council** (**1909**).
**Statement 2** wrong: he was the **Law Member**, not Finance.
xa: His appointment came under the **Morley-Minto Reforms (1909)**.
Same reforms: **separate electorates** for Muslims with **weightage**.
Central council enlarged (additional members **to 60**), **official majority** retained.

205.s: Who went to England in 1906 and met John Morley to press for self-government for India on the model of other colonies?
205.x: Gopal Krishna Gokhale met Morley in England in 1906 and advocated self-government for India.
205.tq: Match the political leader with the specific constitutional initiative.
xs: **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** went to England in **1906** and met **Morley** — option **(2)**.
He pressed for **self-government like other colonies** — the Moderate goal of self-government within the Empire.
xa: The reforms aimed to **rally the Moderates** and **reward Muslim loyalty**.
At **Surat (1907)** Moderates under **Gokhale** (and Mehta) faced Extremists under **Tilak**.
Morley was **Secretary of State**; Minto was **Viceroy (1905-1910)**.
Result: **Indian Councils Act 1909**.

205.s: The Morley-Minto Reforms were introduced mainly to:
o: Rally the Moderates and reward Muslim loyalty
Transfer the capital from Delhi to Calcutta
Abolish princely states and establish a republic
205.x: Morley and Minto sought to rally the Moderates and reward Muslim loyalty through limited constitutional concessions and separate electorates.
205.tq: Identify the political purpose behind a constitutional measure.
xs: Morley-Minto Reforms aimed to **rally the Moderates and reward Muslim loyalty** — option **(1)**.
The reward was **separate electorates** with **weightage** for Muslims.
The capital moved **Calcutta → Delhi** (not Delhi → Calcutta) in **1911**; **provincial autonomy** came with the **1935 Act** — (2) and (4) are wrong.
xa: Official majority **retained at the Centre**.
Councils could debate the budget but **could not vote** on it.
**S.P. Sinha** = first Indian on the Viceroy's Executive Council.

205.s: With reference to the Indian Councils Act, 1909, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It abolished legislative councils and introduced national education.
It enlarged legislative councils and introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
It created the Muslim League at Dacca.
It reunited Bengal and ended the Surat Split.
205.x: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 enlarged the legislative councils and introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
205.tq: Identify the reform measure by its distinctive constitutional provisions.
xs: The **1909 Act** **enlarged legislative councils** and **introduced separate electorates for Muslims** — option **(2)**.
The **Muslim League** was founded separately at **Dacca** in **1906**; Bengal was reunited in **1911**; the Surat Split healed at **Lucknow 1916** — so (3) and (4) are wrong.
xa: Central council: additional members **to 60**; provincial councils also enlarged.
**Elected** non-official members for the first time; **indirect** elections.
Minto = **"Father of the Communal Electorate"**.
**1919** Act later extended communal representation to **Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans**.

205.s: The Lucknow Congress Session of December 1916 was presided over by:
205.x: Ambika Charan Majumdar presided over the Lucknow Congress Session of December 1916.
205.tq: Avoid swapping the session president with the principal brokers of the pact.
xs: The **Lucknow Congress session (Dec 1916)** was presided over by **Ambika Charan Majumdar** — option **(4)**.
**Jinnah** presided over the **League's** Lucknow 1916 session — not the Congress.
**Tilak** and **Jinnah** were the **brokers** of the Lucknow Pact; **Annie Besant** also worked for it.
xa: ⚠ Lucknow 1916: Congress president = **Ambika Charan Majumdar**; League president = **Jinnah**.
The session saw the **reunion of Moderates and Extremists** after Surat **1907**.
League side led by the **"Young Party"** (Jinnah, Ali Brothers).

205.s:
The Lucknow Congress Session of 1916 was historically significant because it witnessed:
1. Reunion of Moderates and Extremists
2. The Congress-League alliance
3. Tilak's return to the Congress fold
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: The 1916 session marked the reunion of Moderates and Extremists, Tilak's return and the Congress-League alliance represented by the Lucknow Pact.
205.tq: Identify all historically linked features of a landmark session.
xs: All three were features of Lucknow **1916** — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Reunion of Moderates and Extremists** after the **1907 Surat Split**.
**Tilak's return** to the Congress fold.
The **Congress-League alliance** — the **Lucknow Pact**.
xa: Congress president: **Ambika Charan Majumdar**; League president: **Jinnah**.
Brokers: **Tilak + Jinnah**; Annie Besant also worked for it.
**1916** = high point of **Congress-League unity**.
Limit: the two still held **separate annual sessions**.

205.s: The Muslim League delegation associated with the Lucknow Pact was led by the:
205.x: The League's Young Party, associated with Jinnah and the Ali Brothers, led the League side in the Lucknow Pact negotiations.
205.tq: Discriminate between similarly named political groupings.
xs: The League side was led by the **"Young Party"** — option **(4)**.
Its leaders were **Jinnah** and the **Ali Brothers**.
xa: **1912-24**: League dominated by **younger Muslim nationalists** whose nationalism still took a **communal** view.
Jinnah joined the League in **1913** and presided its **Lucknow 1916** session.
Congress accepted **Muslim separate electorates** — a major concession.
Pact brokered by **Tilak** and **Jinnah**.

205.s: Under the Lucknow Pact, the Congress accepted which major concession to the Muslim League?
o: Direct British appointment of Muslim representatives
205.x: The Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims, which was a major concession under the Lucknow Pact.
205.tq: Identify the specific concession rather than the general objective of the pact.
xs: The Congress **accepted Muslim separate electorates** — option **(2)**, a **major concession**.
It did not abolish communal representation — so (4) is wrong; it sought an **elected majority** in provincial legislatures — so (3) is wrong.
xa: **Weightage**: Muslims got seats above their population ratio.
**Communal veto**: no bill passed if **three-fourths** of the affected community's members opposed.
Common goal: **self-government**.
Separate electorates first came legally with the **1909** Act.

205.s: Under the Lucknow Pact, a bill concerning a particular community could not be passed if opposed by what proportion of the members of that community?
205.x: Under the Lucknow Pact's communal veto, no bill affecting a community could be passed if three-fourths of that community's members in the legislature opposed it.
205.tq: Treat a constitutional fraction as an exact figure, not an approximate majority.
xs: The communal veto required opposition by **three-fourths** of that community's members — option **(1)**.
No bill concerning a community could pass if **three-fourths** of its members opposed it.
xa: Other terms: **separate electorates** accepted, **weightage**, **self-government** as common goal.
Also: **separation of executive and judiciary**; **elected majority** in provincial legislatures.
Brokers: **Tilak** and **Jinnah** (Dec **1916**).

205.s:
Which of the following formed part of the Lucknow Pact proposals?
1. Separation of the executive from the judiciary
2. Elected majority in provincial legislatures
3. Self-government as a common goal
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: The Pact accepted self-government as its goal and included separation of the executive and judiciary and elected majorities in provincial legislatures.
205.tq: Combine institutional provisions with the shared political objective.
xs: All three were part of the Pact — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**1:** **Separation of executive and judiciary**.
**2:** **Elected majority in provincial legislatures**.
**3:** **Self-government** accepted by both as the common goal.
xa: Congress **accepted separate electorates** for Muslims.
**Weightage** and the **three-fourths communal veto**.
Limit: **separate annual sessions** continued.

205.s: Which one of the following statements about the Congress and the Muslim League in 1916 is correct?
o: The League abandoned its separate political agenda permanently.
The Congress rejected all communal representation.
They merged into a single organisation with one annual session.
They held separate annual sessions despite reaching an agreement through the Lucknow Pact.
205.x: The Congress and the League continued to hold separate annual sessions with distinct agendas even after the Lucknow Pact.
205.tq: Separate political alliance from organisational merger.
xs: They **held separate annual sessions** despite the **Lucknow Pact** — option **(4)**.
The two kept **distinct agendas**, so they did not merge (3) and the League did not drop its agenda (1).
Congress **accepted** Muslim separate electorates — so (2) is wrong.
xa: **1916** = high point of **Congress-League unity**.
Congress president **Ambika Charan Majumdar**; League president **Jinnah**.
League led by the **"Young Party"**.
Brokers: **Tilak + Jinnah**; **Annie Besant** also worked for it.

205.s: With reference to the Muslim League during 1912–1924, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It was dominated entirely by British officials.
It was led exclusively by Hindu nationalists.
It was dominated by younger Muslim nationalists whose nationalism nevertheless viewed politics communally.
It had ceased to exist as a political organisation.
205.x: During 1912–1924, younger Muslim nationalists exercised growing influence in the League. Their nationalism was still shaped by a communal view of politics.
205.tq: Distinguish a qualified description from absolute alternatives such as “entirely” and “exclusively”.
xs: During **1912-24** the League was dominated by **younger Muslim nationalists**, whose nationalism still took a **communal view of politics** — option **(3)**.
This "Young Party" (**Jinnah**, **Ali Brothers**) led the League into the **Lucknow Pact (1916)**.
xa: Jinnah joined the League in **1913**.
Early League aims (**1906**): loyalty to the Empire; keep Muslims away from the Congress.
Later milestones: **Iqbal (1930)**, **Lahore Resolution (1940)**, **Direct Action Day (1946)**.

205.s: Muhammad Ali Jinnah joined the All-India Muslim League in
205.x: Jinnah joined the Muslim League in 1913, although he was also associated with the Congress-League cooperation that culminated in the Lucknow Pact.
205.tq: Use the close-year discrimination method for a sequence of League milestones.
xs: **Jinnah** joined the Muslim League in **1913** — option **(3)**.
**1906** = League founded; **1909** = Morley-Minto Reforms; **1916** = Jinnah presided the **Lucknow League session**.
xa: Jinnah and **Tilak** brokered the **Lucknow Pact**.
He belonged to the League's **"Young Party"** with the **Ali Brothers**.
**1940**: **Lahore Resolution** demanding independent states for Muslims.

205.s: Who presided over the Muslim League session held at Lucknow in 1916?
205.x: Muhammad Ali Jinnah presided over the Muslim League session at Lucknow in 1916.
205.tq: Match the session with its presiding leader and avoid substituting later ideological figures.
xs: **Muhammad Ali Jinnah** presided the **League's Lucknow 1916** session — option **(3)**.
**Aga Khan** was the League's **first president** (**1906**); **Iqbal** gave the **Allahabad address (1930)**; **Rahmat Ali** coined **"PAKISTAN" (1933)**.
xa: ⚠ Congress president at Lucknow 1916: **Ambika Charan Majumdar**.
Jinnah joined the League in **1913**.
He co-brokered the Pact with **Tilak**.

205.s: The Lucknow Pact was negotiated principally by:
205.x: The Pact was negotiated by Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Muhammad Ali Jinnah with the Muslim League's Young Party.
205.tq: Avoid the swapped-leader trap by matching the negotiators with the Pact.
xs: The Lucknow Pact was brokered by **Tilak and Jinnah** — option **(3)**.
**Annie Besant** also worked for it, but with Tilak, not Gokhale.
xa: Tilak's return marked the **reunion of Moderates and Extremists**.
Jinnah led the League's **"Young Party"** with the Ali Brothers.
Key concession: Congress **accepted separate electorates**.
Congress president: **Ambika Charan Majumdar**.

205.s: The provision that Muslims should receive more seats than their population share in provinces where they were a minority is known as:
205.x: The Lucknow Pact provided weightage to Muslims in minority provinces, giving them representation greater than their population share.
205.tq: Discriminate between closely related constitutional terms by their operative meaning.
xs: Seats above population share for a minority community is **weightage** — option **(2)**.
The Lucknow Pact fixed a proportion of seats for Muslims **above their population ratio**.
**Communal veto** was the **three-fourths** rule on bills; **dyarchy** belongs to the **1919** Act.
xa: Weightage was first given with separate electorates in the **1909** Act.
The **Simla Deputation (1906)** had demanded weightage.
Congress **accepted** separate electorates in **1916** — a major concession.

205.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
205.x: The Surat Split occurred in 1907. The partition was annulled in 1911, the August Declaration was made in 1917 and the Swaraj Party was formed in 1923.
205.tq: Match each event with its exact year and reject shifted dates.
xs: **1907 — Surat Split** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**1911** = Delhi Durbar, **partition annulled**; **1917** = **August Declaration (20 Aug)**; **Swaraj Party** = **1923**.
So (2), (3) and (4) are mismatched.
xa: **1909** = Morley-Minto Reforms.
**1919** = Rowlatt Act, **Jallianwala Bagh (13 April)**, GoI Act.
**1920** = Khilafat and **Non-Cooperation**.
Swaraj Party: **C.R. Das** and **Motilal Nehru**, formed **1 Jan 1923**.

205.s: The August Declaration relating to India's constitutional development was made on:
205.x: The August Declaration was made on 20 August 1917.
205.tq: Distinguish the date of the declaration from the dates of later mass movements and reforms.
xs: The **August Declaration** was made on **20 August 1917** — option **(2)**.
**12 Dec 1911** = partition annulled; **13 April 1919** = **Jallianwala Bagh**; **1 Jan 1923** = **Swaraj Party**.
xa: **1919**: Rowlatt Act and the **Government of India Act**.
**1920**: Khilafat and Non-Cooperation.
The **1919 Act** introduced **dyarchy in the provinces**.

205.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
205.x: The Swaraj Party was formed on 1 January 1923 by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru, not in 1921.
205.tq: Find the shifted year in a sequence of otherwise correctly dated events.
xs: **Swaraj Party — 1921** is wrong — option **(4)**; it was formed on **1 Jan 1923**.
Founders: **C.R. Das** and **Motilal Nehru**.
The others match: **Khilafat/Non-Cooperation 1920**, **Rowlatt Act 1919**, **Jallianwala Bagh 13 April 1919**.
xa: **1917**: August Declaration (**20 Aug**).
**1911**: Delhi Durbar, partition annulled.
**1909**: Morley-Minto Reforms.

205.s: Who proposed the idea of a Muslim state in the North-West of India in the Allahabad Address of 1930?
205.x: Muhammad Iqbal proposed the idea of a Muslim state in the North-West in his Allahabad Address of 1930.
205.tq: Distinguish the early ideological proposal from the later Pakistan nomenclature and League resolution.
xs: **Muhammad Iqbal** proposed a Muslim state in the **North-West** in his **Allahabad address (1930)** — option **(3)**.
**Chaudhry Rahmat Ali** only coined the name **"PAKISTAN" (1933)**.
xa: ⚠ Muslim state idea = **Iqbal (1930)**; the name "PAKISTAN" = **Rahmat Ali (1933)**.
**1937-39**: League alleged **"Hindu Raj"** under Congress ministries.
**1940**: **Lahore Resolution**.
**1946**: **Direct Action Day**.

205.s: The name “PAKISTAN” was coined by Chaudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933 in his pamphlet titled
205.x: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali coined the name “PAKISTAN” in 1933 in the pamphlet Now or Never.
205.tq: Test the author–title association rather than the broader movement chronology.
xs: Rahmat Ali coined **"PAKISTAN"** in **1933** in **Now or Never** — option **(3)**.
The idea of a Muslim state in the NW came earlier from **Iqbal (1930)**, Allahabad address.
xa: ⚠ Do not confuse: **Iqbal** = idea; **Rahmat Ali** = name.
**Lahore Resolution (1940)**: independent states for Muslims.
**1946**: Direct Action Day; League wins Muslim seats.

205.s:
With reference to the Delhi Durbar of 1911, consider the following statements:
1. The annulment of the partition of Bengal was announced on 12 December 1911 through King George V.
2. The capital of British India was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi.
3. The annulment came along with the Morley-Minto Reforms.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: at the Delhi Durbar (12 December 1911) the partition was annulled, announced through King George V, and the capital moved from Calcutta to Delhi. Statement 3 is wrong: the Morley-Minto Reforms came in 1909. So B, C and D, which include statement 3 or omit 1 or 2, are wrong.
205.tq: 1911 Durbar = annulment + capital to Delhi; 1909 = Morley-Minto.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1** correct: partition annulled on **12 December 1911**, announced through **King George V** at the **Delhi Durbar**.
**2** correct: the capital shifted **Calcutta → Delhi**.
**3** wrong: the **Morley-Minto Reforms** came in **1909**, not with the annulment.
xa: The partition and **Swadeshi** began in **1905**.
**1907** Surat Split; **1917** August Declaration.
Lord Minto's tenure ended in **1910**.

205.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
205.x: The Lahore Resolution, demanding independent states for Muslims, was passed in 1940. Direct Action Day was in 1946 (not 1940), the Lahore Resolution was not in 1946, and Iqbal's Allahabad address was in 1930 (1933 is when Rahmat Ali coined 'Pakistan').
205.tq: 1930 Iqbal → 1933 Pakistan name → 1940 Lahore → 1946 Direct Action.
xs: **Lahore Resolution — 1940** is correct — option **(3)**.
It demanded **independent states for Muslims**.
**Direct Action Day** was **1946**, not 1940; Iqbal's **Allahabad address** was **1930**, not 1933.
xa: **1933**: **Rahmat Ali** coined "PAKISTAN" (Now or Never).
**1937-39**: League alleged **"Hindu Raj"**.
**1946**: League also won the Muslim seats.

205.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
2. The Government of India Act, 1919 provided for bicameralism and direct elections at the Centre.
3. The Government of India Act, 1935 prescribed an All-India Federation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: All three are correct: the 1919 Act introduced dyarchy in the provinces and bicameralism with direct elections at the Centre, and the 1935 Act prescribed an All-India Federation (along with provincial autonomy and dyarchy at the Centre).
205.tq: Group the distinctive features of two successive constitutional Acts.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**1:** The **1919 Act** introduced **dyarchy in the provinces**.
**2:** It gave **bicameralism and direct elections** at the Centre.
**3:** The **1935 Act** prescribed an **all-India Federation**.
xa: **1935** also gave **provincial autonomy** and **dyarchy at the Centre**.
**1909** introduced **separate electorates** for Muslims.
⚠ Montagu-Chelmsford = **1919**, not 1929 (wrong pair in APPSC-G1 **2019**).
Pitt's India Act = **1784**.

205.s:
The Government of India Act, 1919 extended communal representation to which of the following communities?
1. Sikhs
2. Indian Christians
3. Anglo-Indians
4. Europeans
205.x: The 1919 Act extended communal representation to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans.
205.tq: Check the complete membership of a constitutional category.
xs: The **1919 Act** extended communal representation to all four — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Sikhs**, **Indian Christians**, **Anglo-Indians** and **Europeans**.
xa: Separate electorates began for **Muslims** in **1909**.
The **1935 Act** extended them to **depressed classes, women, labour**.
1919 also brought **dyarchy in the provinces** and **direct elections** at the Centre.

205.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the 1909 and 1919 reforms?
o: The 1919 reforms abolished communal representation introduced in 1909.
The 1909 reforms introduced provincial dyarchy, whereas the 1919 reforms introduced Muslim separate electorates.
The 1909 reforms introduced Muslim separate electorates, whereas the 1919 reforms introduced provincial dyarchy and direct elections.
Both reforms introduced provincial autonomy in the provinces.
205.x: The Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 introduced separate electorates for Muslims, while the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms of 1919 introduced provincial dyarchy and direct elections.
205.tq: Compare the signature feature of each reform instead of swapping their dates and provisions.
xs: **1909** introduced **Muslim separate electorates**; **1919** introduced **provincial dyarchy and direct elections** — option **(3)**.
Option (2) swaps them; 1919 **extended** (not abolished) communal representation; **provincial autonomy** came in **1935**.
xa: 1909 = Morley-Minto; 1919 = **Montagu-Chelmsford**.
1919 also gave **bicameralism** at the Centre.
1935 = **provincial autonomy**, **dyarchy at the Centre**, all-India **Federation**.

205.s: The Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 are particularly associated with the introduction of:
205.x: The Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 introduced separate electorates, especially for Muslims.
205.tq: Link a constitutional reform to its distinctive provision.
xs: The 1909 reforms are linked to **separate electorates** — option **(2)**.
Separate (communal) electorates for **Muslims**, with **weightage**.
**Dyarchy in the provinces** = **1919**; **provincial autonomy** = **1935**.
xa: Minto = **"Father of the Communal Electorate"**.
1909 also gave **elected** non-official members for the first time.
**Significance**: 1909 = **legal start** of separate electorates.

205.s: The Government of India Act associated with the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms was enacted in
205.x: The Government of India Act associated with the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms was enacted in 1919.
205.tq: Distinguish the declaration year from the legislation year.
xs: The **Montagu-Chelmsford** Act was enacted in **1919** — option **(3)**.
**1916** = Lucknow Pact; **1917** = August Declaration; **1920** = Non-Cooperation.
xa: ⚠ Not **1929** — a wrong pair in APPSC-G1 **2019**.
1919 Act: **dyarchy in the provinces**, **bicameralism and direct elections** at the Centre.
It extended communal representation to **Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, Europeans**.

205.s:
With reference to the Government of India Act, 1935, consider the following statements:
1. It introduced provincial autonomy.
2. It introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
3. It extended separate electorates to the depressed classes, women and labour.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the 1935 Act gave provincial autonomy and extended separate electorates to depressed classes, women and labour. Statement 2 is wrong: dyarchy in the provinces came with the 1919 Act; the 1935 Act put dyarchy at the Centre. So A, B and D, which include statement 2, are wrong.
205.tq: Dyarchy: provinces 1919, Centre 1935.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(3)**.
**1** correct: the **1935 Act** gave **provincial autonomy**.
**2** wrong: **dyarchy in the provinces** came with **1919**; 1935 put **dyarchy at the Centre**.
**3** correct: separate electorates extended to **depressed classes, women, labour**.
xa: 1935 also prescribed an all-India **Federation**.
1919 extended communal representation to **Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, Europeans**.
1909 began **Muslim separate electorates**.

205.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the significance of 1909 and 1916 is correct?
o: 1909 marked the legal beginning of separate electorates, while 1916 marked the high point of Congress-League unity.
1909 marked the establishment of provincial autonomy, while 1916 marked the end of communal politics.
1909 marked the end of separate electorates, while 1916 marked the beginning of the Muslim League.
Both 1909 and 1916 marked phases of complete constitutional separation between Congress and the League.
205.x: The year 1909 is associated with the legal start of separate electorates, whereas 1916 is regarded as the high point of Congress-League unity.
205.tq: Use the contrast between two years to eliminate reversed comparisons.
xs: **1909** = **legal start of separate electorates**; **1916** = **high point of Congress-League unity** — option **(1)**.
**Provincial autonomy** came only in **1935**; 1909 began (not ended) separate electorates; the League dates from **1906**.
xa: 1916 brought the **Lucknow Pact**, brokered by **Tilak** and **Jinnah**.
Even in 1916 the two held **separate annual sessions**.
Separate electorates re-entered debate in **2026** commentary on religion-based voting.

205.s: Which of the following places was NOT included in Annie Besant’s Andhra tour after the Lucknow session?
205.x: The tour included Kakinada, Rajahmundry and Eluru. Vijayawada is not included among the places specified for this tour.
205.tq: Find the one location outside the stated set rather than selecting a place associated generally with Andhra politics.
xs: **Vijayawada** was not on the listed tour — option **(3)**.
Besant toured **Kakinada, Rajahmundry** and **Eluru** after the **Lucknow session**.
xa: First Telugu political prisoners: **Gadicherla** and **Bodi Narayana Rao** (**18 July 1908**).
Besant worked for the **Lucknow Pact** alongside Tilak and Jinnah.
The Lucknow session was in **Dec 1916**.

205.s: Who among the following, arrested on 18 July 1908 over a Swarajya article, are regarded as the first Telugu political prisoners?
o: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao and Bodi Narayana Rao
Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao and Mocherla Hanumantha Rao
205.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao and Bodi Narayana Rao were arrested on 18 July 1908 for a Swarajya article during the Minto-Morley repression - the first Telugu political prisoners. Konda Venkatappayya and Pattabhi Sitaramayya were Home Rule leaders; Ramayya and Basavayya were the Tenali bomb case accused (1909); Nageswara Rao and Mocherla Hanumantha Rao were associated with Andhra Patrika and Besant's tour.
205.tq: Swarajya article, 1908 → Gadicherla + Bodi = first Telugu political prisoners.
xs: **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** and **Bodi Narayana Rao**, arrested **18 July 1908**, were the **first Telugu political prisoners** — option **(2)**.
They were arrested over a **Swarajya** article.
This was part of the **repression under Minto-Morley**.
xa: **1908** also saw the **Newspapers Act** and the **Muzaffarpur case**.
Besant later toured **Kakinada, Rajahmundry, Eluru** after Lucknow **1916**.
Minto was **Viceroy 1905-1910**.

206.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Damodar and Balkrishna Chapekar shot Plague Commissioner W.C. Rand at Poona in 1897.
2. Their action was a protest against the excesses of plague-control measures.
3. Vasudev Balwant Phadke's Ramosi force was organised after the Chapekar action, in 1909.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
206.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Chapekar brothers shot Rand (and Lt. Ayerst) at Poona in 1897 in protest against plague-control excesses. Statement 3 is wrong: Phadke's Ramosi force (1879) was an earlier root, before the Chapekars. Hence only option A fits; B, C and D all include statement 3 or omit statement 1.
206.tq: Phadke 1879 comes before Chapekars 1897.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1** correct: **Damodar and Balkrishna Chapekar** shot **Plague Commissioner W.C. Rand** at **Poona** in **1897** (Lt. Ayerst also killed).
**2** correct: it was a protest against **plague-control excesses**.
**3** wrong: **Vasudev Balwant Phadke's Ramosi force** dates from **1879** — an earlier root, before the Chapekars.
xa: **1908**: **Muzaffarpur** bomb by **Khudiram Bose** and **Prafulla Chaki**.
**1909**: **Anant Kanhere** killed Nasik Collector **A.M.T. Jackson**.
**1911**: **Vanchi Aiyar** shot **Robert Ashe** at Maniyachi.
Roots of revolutionary groups: **akhadas** + secret societies.

206.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
206.x: The Bharat Mata Society was founded by Ajit Singh with Lala Lajpat Rai in Punjab, not in Bengal in 1906.
206.tq: Find the wrongly matched place and year among closely related organisations.
xs: **Bharat Mata Society — Bengal, 1906** is wrong — option **(4)**.
The **Bharat Mata Society** was **Ajit Singh's** (with **Lala Lajpat Rai**) in **Punjab**.
**Bengal, 1906** fits **Yugantar** (Barindra Kumar Ghosh).
The rest match: **Anushilan — Calcutta 1902**, **Mitra Mela — Nasik 1899**, **Abhinav Bharat — Nasik/Pune 1904**.
xa: ⚠ **Anushilan (1902)** = **P. Mitra**; **Yugantar (1906)** = **Barindra Kumar Ghosh**, its offshoot.
Mitra Mela was **renamed Abhinav Bharat** by **V.D. Savarkar**.
Ajit Singh + Lajpat Rai were **deported to Mandalay in 1907**.
**India House** (London, **1905**) = **Shyamji Krishna Varma**.

206.s:
With reference to the revolutionary organisations of the early twentieth century, consider the following statements:
1. The Dhaka branch of Anushilan Samiti was associated with Pulin Behari Das.
2. Yugantar emerged as an offshoot of Anushilan Samiti.
3. Bharat Mata Society was associated with Ajit Singh and Lala Lajpat Rai.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
206.x: Pulin Behari Das was associated with the Dhaka branch, Yugantar was an offshoot of Anushilan Samiti, and Bharat Mata Society was associated with Ajit Singh and Lala Lajpat Rai.
206.tq: Test three related organisation–leader relationships in one coded statement question.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**1:** Anushilan's **Dhaka branch** = **Pulin Behari Das**.
**2:** **Yugantar (1906)** was an **offshoot of Anushilan**.
**3:** **Bharat Mata Society** = **Ajit Singh** with **Lala Lajpat Rai** (Punjab).
xa: Anushilan Samiti: **P. (Pramathanath) Mitra**, Calcutta, **1902**.
Yugantar: **Barindra Kumar Ghosh** with **Bagha Jatin**.
The **Hardinge bomb** was attributed to **Anushilan Samiti** (UPPSC **2023** key).
Bengal journals **Yugantar** and **Sandhya** advocated violence.

206.s: Which of the following statements regarding the early revolutionary movement is correct?
o: Its secret societies developed mainly out of legislative councils.
Its activities began only after the First World War.
Its revolutionary groups grew out of akhadas and secret societies.
Its journals opposed all forms of political violence.
206.x: Many early revolutionary groups grew out of akhadas or gymnasiums and secret societies such as Anushilan and Atmonnati Samiti.
206.tq: Choose the precise cause of organisational growth rather than a broad chronological generalisation.
xs: Early revolutionary groups **grew out of akhadas and secret societies** — option **(3)**.
**Akhadas** = gymnasiums; secret societies such as **Anushilan** and **Atmonnati Samiti**.
Activity began well before WWI (Chapekars **1897**, Anushilan **1902**) — (2) wrong; journals like **Yugantar** and **Sandhya** **advocated violence** — (4) wrong.
xa: Context: heroic individual action followed the **Surat Split** and failure of mass Swadeshi.
Criticism: **not a mass movement**; **Bhavani** worship limited Muslim participation.
Earlier root: **Phadke's Ramosi force (1879)**.

206.s:
Consider the following pairs:
Society — Founder
1. Anushilan Samiti — Pramathanath Mitra
2. Yugantar — Barindra Kumar Ghosh
3. Abhinav Bharat — Ajit Singh
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
206.x: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct: P. Mitra founded Anushilan Samiti (Calcutta, 1902) and Barindra Kumar Ghosh founded Yugantar (1906). Pair 3 is wrong: Abhinav Bharat was V.D. Savarkar's; Ajit Singh led the Bharat Mata Society. So B, C and D, which include pair 3, are wrong.
206.tq: Anushilan = P. Mitra; Yugantar = Barindra; Abhinav Bharat = Savarkar.
xs: Pairs **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1** correct: **Anushilan Samiti** — **Pramathanath Mitra** (Calcutta, **1902**).
**2** correct: **Yugantar** — **Barindra Kumar Ghosh** (**1906**).
**3** wrong: **Abhinav Bharat** was **V.D. Savarkar's**; **Ajit Singh** led the **Bharat Mata Society**.
xa: Abhinav Bharat = **Mitra Mela (1899)** renamed, **1904**.
Anushilan's Dhaka branch: **Pulin Behari Das**.
Barindra wrote the manual **Mukti Kon Pathe (1906)**.

206.s: In 1907, Lala Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh were deported to Mandalay under which law?
206.x: They were deported to Mandalay in 1907 under Regulation III of 1818. The Defence of India Act came only in 1915 and the Rowlatt Act in 1919, so neither could apply in 1907; the Press Act was a press law, not a deportation law.
206.tq: 1907 Mandalay deportation = Regulation III of 1818; DIA is 1915.
xs: They were deported under **Regulation III of 1818** — option **(2)**.
**Ajit Singh + Lajpat Rai** were **deported to Mandalay in 1907**.
⚠ The **Defence of India Act** came only in **1915** — some notes wrongly name it.
xa: Ajit Singh's group: the **Bharat Mata Society** (Punjab).
The Defence of India Act was used to hang many after the **1915 Ghadar revolt**.
Lajpat Rai's later lathi-charge led to the **Saunders killing (1928)**.

206.s: In the Muzaffarpur Bomb Case, the intended target was:
206.x: Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki targeted Magistrate Douglas Kingsford at Muzaffarpur.
206.tq: Distinguish the intended target from the unintended victims and other colonial officials.
xs: The target was **Magistrate Douglas Kingsford** — option **(3)**.
**Khudiram Bose** and **Prafulla Chaki** bombed his carriage at **Muzaffarpur (Bihar)** on **30 April 1908**.
**Lord Hardinge** was the **1912** Delhi target; **James A. Scott** the **1928** target; **Jackson** was the Nasik Collector killed in **1909**.
xa: ⚠ The bomb killed **two British women** instead.
Khudiram was **hanged at 18** on **11 August 1908**; Chaki shot himself.
The police then raided the **Maniktala bomb factory** → **Alipore case**.

206.s: Which of the following correctly describes the outcome of the Muzaffarpur bomb attack?
o: Two British women were killed, Khudiram Bose was hanged and Prafulla Chaki died by suicide.
The bomb failed to explode and both accused were acquitted.
Kingsford was killed and both revolutionaries escaped.
Only Prafulla Chaki was executed after a formal trial.
206.x: The bomb killed two British women instead of Kingsford. Khudiram Bose was hanged, while Prafulla Chaki shot himself before arrest.
206.tq: Read the whole sequence carefully: target, unintended result and fate of both accused.
xs: **Two British women were killed**, **Khudiram Bose was hanged** and **Prafulla Chaki** shot himself — option **(1)**.
Kingsford escaped, so (3) is wrong; Khudiram was executed, so (2) and (4) are wrong.
xa: Khudiram, hanged on **11 August 1908** at **18**, was among the youngest martyrs.
Attack date: **30 April 1908**, Muzaffarpur (Bihar).
Khudiram Bose was born **3 Dec 1889**.
UPPSC **2021** order: Kesari (**1881**) → Khudiram executed (**1908**) → Curzon Wyllie killed (**1909**) → Al-Hilal (**1912**).

206.s: Which one of the following statements about the Alipore Bomb Case is correct?
o: It involved a raid on the Maniktala bomb factory, and Aurobindo Ghosh was acquitted.
It was related to the killing of Curzon Wyllie in London.
It concerned the Kakori train action, and C.R. Das was the chief accused.
It was conducted in Nasik, and Barindra Ghosh was acquitted.
206.x: The Alipore Bomb Case followed the raid on the Maniktala bomb factory. Aurobindo Ghosh was acquitted, while Barindra Ghosh received a life sentence; C.R. Das defended Aurobindo.
206.tq: Distinguish the place of the raid and the differing outcomes of the principal accused.
xs: The **Alipore case** followed the raid on the **Maniktala bomb factory**, and **Aurobindo Ghosh was acquitted** — option **(1)**.
**C.R. Das** defended Aurobindo; he was not an accused — (3) wrong.
**Barindra Ghosh** got **life** (Andaman Cellular Jail), not acquittal; the **Nasik** case was separate (**1909**) — (4) wrong.
**Curzon Wyllie** was killed in London by **Madan Lal Dhingra** — (2) wrong.
xa: ⚠ Alipore: **Aurobindo** acquitted (C.R. Das); **Barindra** = life.
Approver **Narendranath Goswami** was shot inside **Alipore jail**.
Aurobindo, acquitted **1909**, retired to Pondicherry.

206.s: Who defended Aurobindo Ghosh in the Alipore Bomb Case?
206.x: Chittaranjan Das, popularly known as C.R. Das, defended Aurobindo Ghosh in the Alipore Bomb Case.
206.tq: Match the legal counsel with the revolutionary case.
xs: **C.R. Das** defended **Aurobindo Ghosh** in the **Alipore case** — option **(1)**.
Aurobindo was **acquitted**; his brother **Barindra Ghosh** got **life** in the Andaman Cellular Jail.
xa: The case (**1908**) began with the raid on the **Maniktala bomb factory** after Muzaffarpur.
Approver **Narendranath Goswami** was shot in jail by **Kanailal Dutta** + **Satyendranath Bose**.
Aurobindo edited **Bande Mataram**.

206.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Alipore Bomb Case is NOT correct?
o: Barindra Ghosh was sentenced to life imprisonment in the Cellular Jail.
Narendranath Goswami was shot outside India by Madan Lal Dhingra.
Narendranath Goswami acted as an approver.
The accused were held in Alipore jail, Calcutta.
206.x: Narendranath Goswami was shot inside Alipore jail by Kanailal Dutta and Satyendranath Bose. He was not killed outside India by Madan Lal Dhingra.
206.tq: Find the swapped person and location in a case-related statement.
xs: The false statement is that **Goswami was shot outside India by Madan Lal Dhingra** — option **(2)**.
**Narendranath Goswami** (approver) was shot **inside Alipore jail** by **Kanailal Dutta** + **Satyendranath Bose**.
Options (1), (3) and (4) are true: **Barindra** got life in the Cellular Jail; accused were held in **Alipore jail, Calcutta**.
xa: **Dhingra** killed **Curzon Wyllie** in London, **1909**.
**Aurobindo** was acquitted, defended by **C.R. Das**.
Alipore case is also called the **Maniktala** case (**1908**).

206.s: Who founded the Mitra Mela in 1899, which later became associated with Abhinav Bharat?
206.x: V.D. Savarkar founded Mitra Mela in 1899. It later developed into the revolutionary organisation Abhinav Bharat.
206.tq: Use the founder–organisation association without confusing Mitra Mela with other revolutionary bodies.
xs: **V.D. Savarkar** founded **Mitra Mela (1899)** at Nasik, with brother **Ganesh** — option **(4)**.
It was **renamed Abhinav Bharat** (**1904**).
**Shyamji Krishna Varma** founded **India House**; **Barindra** founded **Yugantar**; **Sanyal** co-founded the **HRA**.
xa: In London Savarkar worked from **India House**.
Arrested in London (**1910**); failed escape at **Marseilles**.
Books: **"The Indian War of Independence, 1857" (1909)**, **"Hindutva" (1923)**.

206.s:
With reference to the Nasik Conspiracy Case, consider the following statements:
1. A.M.T. Jackson, the Nasik Collector, was assassinated by Anant Kanhere.
2. V.D. Savarkar was implicated in the case.
3. Savarkar was sentenced to imprisonment in the Cellular Jail at the Andamans.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
206.x: All three statements are correct. The assassination of A.M.T. Jackson by Anant Kanhere led to Savarkar’s implication and sentence to life imprisonment in the Andamans.
206.tq: Check all three linked facts in a conspiracy-case cluster before selecting the combined option.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**1:** **Anant Kanhere** assassinated Nasik Collector **A.M.T. Jackson** (**1909**).
**2 and 3:** **Savarkar** was implicated and got **life in the Andamans** (Cellular Jail).
xa: Savarkar's earlier groups: **Mitra Mela (1899)** → **Abhinav Bharat**.
Other cases: **Alipore 1908**, **Howrah 1910**, **Delhi 1912**.
Same year (**1909**): Dhingra killed **Curzon Wyllie** in London.

206.s: V.D. Savarkar was arrested in London in 1910. At which place did his attempted escape fail?
206.x: Savarkar’s attempted escape failed at Marseilles in 1910.
206.tq: Distinguish the place of arrest and escape attempt from other overseas revolutionary centres.
xs: Savarkar's escape attempt failed at **Marseilles** — option **(3)**.
He had been **arrested in London (1910)**.
**Stuttgart** = **Bhikaji Cama's** flag (**1907**); **Kabul** = the **Provisional Government (1915)**.
xa: He worked from **India House** with **Hardayal** and **Madan Lal Dhingra**.
He was sentenced to **life in the Andamans** in the **Nasik** case.
Books: **The Indian War of Independence, 1857** and **Hindutva**.

206.s:
Which of the following books were written by V.D. Savarkar?
1. The Indian War of Independence, 1857
2. Hindutva
3. Mukti Kon Pathe
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
206.x: Savarkar wrote 'The Indian War of Independence, 1857' (1909) and 'Hindutva' (1923). 'Mukti Kon Pathe' (1906) was Barindra Kumar Ghosh's revolutionary manual. So B, C and D, which include 3 or omit 1 or 2, are wrong.
206.tq: Savarkar: 1857 book (1909), Hindutva (1923); Mukti Kon Pathe = Barindra.
xs: Savarkar wrote **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)**.
**"The Indian War of Independence, 1857"** (**1909**) and **"Hindutva"** (**1923**).
**Mukti Kon Pathe (1906)** was **Barindra Kumar Ghosh's** manual.
xa: Savarkar founded **Mitra Mela (1899)**, later **Abhinav Bharat**.
**Andaman Jeevitam** = **Prativadi Bhayankaracharyulu**.
**The Philosophy of the Bomb** = **Bhagwati Charan Vohra**.

206.s:
Consider the following statements about the Delhi Conspiracy Case:
1. The bomb was thrown during Lord Hardinge’s state entry into the new capital, Delhi.
2. The procession passed through Chandni Chowk.
3. Lord Hardinge was killed in the attack.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
206.x: The attack took place during the procession through Chandni Chowk, and Hardinge was injured but not killed. Therefore, statements 1 and 2 are correct.
206.tq: Use the outcome trap by distinguishing injury from death.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** The bomb was thrown during **Hardinge's state entry into the new capital Delhi** (**23 December 1912**).
**2:** The procession passed through **Chandni Chowk**.
**3** wrong: **Hardinge was injured, not killed**.
xa: Planned by **Rash Behari Bose** + **Sachin Sanyal**; bomb thrown by **Basanta Kumar Biswas**.
Organisation: **Anushilan Samiti** (UPPSC **2023**).
Executed: **Basant Kumar Biswas, Amir Chand, Avadh Behari** (+ Bhai Balmukund).

206.s: Who threw the bomb at Lord Hardinge during the Delhi Conspiracy Case?
206.x: Basanta Kumar Biswas physically threw the bomb, while Rash Behari Bose and Sachin Sanyal were among those who planned the attack.
206.tq: Distinguish the planner from the person who executed the act.
xs: The bomb was thrown by **Basanta Kumar Biswas** — option **(4)**.
**Rash Behari Bose** and **Sachin Sanyal** **planned** it.
**Amir Chand** was among those **executed** in the Delhi case.
xa: Rash Behari Bose **escaped in disguise**, later to **Japan**.
Sanyal later co-founded the **HRA (1924)**.
⚠ Hardinge survived — **injured**, not killed.

206.s: Which one of the following persons escaped after the Delhi Conspiracy Case by disguising himself and later went to Japan?
206.x: Rash Behari Bose escaped in disguise after the case and later went to Japan.
206.tq: Separate the person who escaped from those executed after the trial.
xs: **Rash Behari Bose** escaped in disguise and later went to **Japan** — option **(3)**.
**Basant Kumar Biswas**, **Avadh Behari** and **Bhai Balmukund** were **executed**.
xa: The case followed the **1912** bomb at **Lord Hardinge** in **Chandni Chowk**.
Co-planner: **Sachin Sanyal**.
Organisation: **Anushilan Samiti**.

206.s: Which organisation was identified as being behind the bomb attack on Lord Hardinge in the Delhi Conspiracy Case?
206.x: Anushilan Samiti was identified as the organisation behind the Delhi Conspiracy Case attack.
206.tq: Match the incident with the organisation rather than with an individual revolutionary.
xs: **Anushilan Samiti** was behind the Hardinge bomb — option **(2)** (UPPSC **2023** key).
The **Ghadar Party** dates from **1913**, the **HRA** from **1924**; **Abhinav Bharat** was Savarkar's Maharashtra group.
xa: Anushilan: **P. Mitra**, Calcutta, **1902**.
Planners: **Rash Behari Bose** + **Sachin Sanyal**.
Bomb thrower: **Basanta Kumar Biswas**.

206.s:
Arrange the following revolutionary cases in chronological order:
A. Delhi Conspiracy Case
B. Nasik Conspiracy Case
C. Muzaffarpur Bomb Case
D. Howrah Conspiracy Case
206.x: The Muzaffarpur case occurred in 1908, the Nasik case in 1909, the Howrah case in 1910 and the Delhi case in 1912.
206.tq: Arrange the cases by their years, using the earliest event as the anchor.
xs: The order is **C, B, D, A** — option **(2)**.
xa: **Alipore (Maniktala)** was also **1908**.
**Lahore Conspiracy Case**: **1929-30**.
Howrah (Howrah-Sibpur) = **Bagha Jatin**.

206.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Muzaffarpur Conspiracy Case — Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki
Alipore Conspiracy Case — Aurobindo Ghosh and Barindra Ghosh
206.x: The Howrah-Sibpur case of 1910 was associated with Jatindranath Mukherjee, also known as Bagha Jatin, not Khudiram Bose.
206.tq: Find the swapped revolutionary in a case–participant list.
xs: **Howrah Conspiracy Case — Khudiram Bose** is wrong — option **(4)**.
Howrah (**1910**) was **Jatindranath Mukherjee (Bagha Jatin)**.
Khudiram belongs to **Muzaffarpur (1908)**; the other pairs are correct.
xa: Bagha Jatin died at **Balasore (1915)** in the **Indo-German plot**.
He co-led **Yugantar** with **Barindra Kumar Ghosh**.
Nasik **1909** = **Anant Kanhere**; Alipore **1908** = Aurobindo and Barindra.

206.s: The Indo-German, or Zimmerman, plot of 1915–17 was associated with which plan?
o: A plan to support the Simon Commission
A plan by Bagha Jatin to organise a revolt with German arms
A plan to establish a constitutional government through the Morley-Minto reforms
A plan to conduct the Chittagong Armoury Raid
206.x: The Indo-German plot involved Bagha Jatin’s plan to organise an armed revolt with German arms. He died in a gunfight at Balasore in 1915.
206.tq: Connect the conspiracy with its intended foreign assistance and leader.
xs: The **Indo-German (Zimmerman) plot 1915-17** was **Bagha Jatin's** plan of a **revolt with German arms** — option **(2)**.
He died in a gunfight at **Balasore** (**1915**).
xa: **Berlin Committee (1915)**: **Virendranath Chattopadhyaya**, **Bhupendranath Dutta**.
**Ghadar revolt** fixed for **21 Feb 1915**, betrayed.
**Kabul Provisional Government (1915)**: Raja **Mahendra Pratap**.
**Singapore Mutiny (Feb 1915)**: 5th Light Infantry.

206.s:
Consider the following statements about Vanchi Aiyar:
1. He shot Robert Ashe, Collector of Tirunelveli, at Maniyachi railway station in 1911.
2. He was captured and hanged after a trial.
3. He was linked with the Bharata Matha Association.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
206.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: Vanchi Aiyar shot Robert Ashe at Maniyachi on 17 June 1911 and was linked with the Bharata Matha Association (and V.O. Chidambaram Pillai's Swadeshi Steam Navigation agitation). Statement 2 is wrong: he shot himself after the attack. So A, B and D, which include statement 2 or omit 1 or 3, are wrong.
206.tq: Vanchi Aiyar shot Ashe, then shot himself - no trial.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(3)**.
**1:** **Vanchi Aiyar** shot **Robert Ashe**, Collector of Tirunelveli, at **Maniyachi** (**17 June 1911**).
**2** wrong: he **shot himself** — no trial.
**3:** linked with the **Bharata Matha Association**.
xa: Also linked to **V.O. Chidambaram Pillai's** **Swadeshi Steam Navigation** agitation.
Comparable: **Prafulla Chaki** also shot himself (Muzaffarpur, **1908**).

206.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Madan Lal Dhingra, part of the India House circle, killed Curzon Wyllie in 1909.
2. Bhikaji Cama unfurled the Indian flag at Stuttgart in 1915.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
206.x: Statement 1 is correct: Dhingra of the India House hub killed Curzon Wyllie in 1909. Statement 2 is wrong: Bhikaji Cama unfurled the flag at Stuttgart in 1907, not 1915. So 2 only, both and neither are wrong.
206.tq: Stuttgart flag = 1907; 1915 is the Berlin Committee / Kabul government year.
xs: Only **statement 1** is correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** **Madan Lal Dhingra** (India House hub) killed **Curzon Wyllie** in **1909**.
**2** wrong: **Bhikaji Cama** unfurled the flag at **Stuttgart** in **1907**, not 1915.
xa: India House: **Shyamji Krishna Varma**, London, **1905**.
India House hub: **Savarkar**, **Hardayal**, **Dhingra**.
**1915** abroad: **Berlin Committee** and the **Kabul** government.

206.s:
The Provisional Government of India established at Kabul in 1915 included:
1. Raja Mahendra Pratap
2. Barkatullah
3. Obaidullah Sindhi

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
206.x: Raja Mahendra Pratap, Barkatullah and Obaidullah Sindhi were associated with the Provisional Government of India established at Kabul in 1915.
206.tq: Test the composition of the provisional government without substituting Berlin Committee members.
xs: All three were in the **Kabul Provisional Government (1915)** — option **(4)**.
**Raja Mahendra Pratap**, **Barkatullah** and **Obaidullah Sindhi**.
xa: Barkatullah edited **Islamic Fraternity**.
**Berlin Committee (1915)**: Chattopadhyaya + **Bhupendranath Dutta**.
**Singapore Mutiny**: **Feb 1915**.

206.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Komagata Maru incident of 1914?
o: A ship carrying mainly Sikh passengers was refused entry into Canada and forced back to India.
A ship carried the Berlin Committee to Stuttgart for a political conference.
A ship carrying Indian troops mutinied at Singapore under Ghadar leadership.
A revolutionary vessel transported arms from Germany to Kabul.
206.x: The Komagata Maru carried 376 mainly Sikh passengers, who were refused entry into Canada and forced back to India.
206.tq: Identify the central event while separating it from the Singapore Mutiny and Berlin Committee.
xs: The **Komagata Maru** carried mainly **Sikh** passengers, refused entry to **Canada** and forced back — option **(1)**.
It carried **376** passengers (**1914**).
The **Singapore mutiny (Feb 1915)** and **Berlin Committee** are different events.
xa: Back in India, **Budge Budge** firing killed **22**.
It **radicalised the Ghadar movement**.
Canada's PM Trudeau apologised in **2016**.

206.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Komagata Maru incident:
1. The ship was forced back and reached Budge Budge.
2. Firing at Budge Budge killed 22 people.
3. The incident radicalised the Ghadar movement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
206.x: All three statements are correct. The Budge Budge firing killed 22 people and contributed to the radicalisation of the Ghadar movement.
206.tq: Test the sequence, casualty figure and consequence of one incident together.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**1:** The ship was forced back to **Budge Budge**.
**2:** Firing there killed **22**.
**3:** It **radicalised the Ghadar movement**.
xa: **376** mainly Sikh passengers were refused entry into **Canada** (**1914**).
Ghadar Party: **1913**, San Francisco (HQ **Yugantar Ashram**).
Ghadar revolt was fixed for **21 Feb 1915**.

206.s: The Ghadar revolt in Punjab in 1915 was fixed for:
206.x: The Ghadar revolt in Punjab was fixed for 21 February 1915, but the plan was betrayed and many participants were hanged under the Defence of India Act.
206.tq: Distinguish the planned date of revolt from dates of other revolutionary actions.
xs: The **Ghadar revolt** was fixed for **21 February 1915** — option **(2)**.
It was **betrayed**; many were hanged under the **Defence of India Act**.
**22 Aug 1922** = Alluri's Chintapalli attack; **17 June 1911** = Vanchi Aiyar; **27 Feb 1931** = Azad's death.
xa: Ghadar leaders: **Lala Hardayal**, Sohan Singh Bhakna, Kartar Singh Sarabha.
The **Singapore Mutiny (Feb 1915)** came under Ghadar influence.
Andhra's Ghadarite: **Darshi Chenchayya** (Nenu Naa Desam).

206.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. India House, London (1905) — Shyamji Krishna Varma
2. Ghadar Party headquarters — Yugantar Ashram, San Francisco
3. Berlin Committee (1915) — Lala Hardayal and Sohan Singh Bhakna
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
206.x: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct: Shyamji Krishna Varma founded India House in London in 1905, and the Ghadar Party's headquarters was Yugantar Ashram, San Francisco. Pair 3 is wrong: the Berlin Committee was led by Virendranath Chattopadhyaya and Bhupendranath Dutta; Hardayal and Bhakna were Ghadar founders. So A (omits 2), C and D (include 3) are wrong.

xs: **Darsi Chenchayya** (Kanigiri) was the **first and only Telugu member of the Ghadar Party** — option **(2)**.
India House was **Krishnavarma's**; the Komagata Maru was **Gurdit Singh's**; the first Ghadar president was **Sohan Singh Bhakna**.
xa: He was **arrested on suspicion**.
Autobiography: **"Nenu Naa Desam"**.
Ghadar founder **Sohan Singh** attended the **Palasa Kisan Sabha (March 1940)**.

207.s: Darsi Chenchayya was arrested on suspicion in connection with his revolutionary activities. His autobiography is titled:
207.x: Darsi Chenchayya's autobiography is titled "Nenu Naa Desam"; he was also arrested on suspicion.
207.tq: Identify the exact title associated with the person, avoiding famous but unrelated freedom-movement works.
xs: Chenchayya's autobiography is **"Nenu Naa Desam"** — option **(2)**.
**Ghadar di Goonj** was Ghadar poetry; **The Indian War of Independence** is **Savarkar's**.
xa: He was from **Kanigiri**.
**First and only Telugu member** of the Ghadar Party.
Ghadar HQ: **Yugantar Ashram, San Francisco**.

207.s: Sohan Singh, one of the founders of the Ghadar Party, attended which event in March 1940?
o: The India House convention in London
207.x: Ghadar founder Sohan Singh attended the Palasa Kisan Sabha in March 1940.
207.tq: Link the named revolutionary with the specific Andhra event and its time reference.
xs: **Sohan Singh** attended the **Palasa Kisan Sabha** (**March 1940**) — option **(1)**.
He was a Ghadar founder and its **first president**.
xa: Andhra's Ghadar link: **Darsi Chenchayya** (**Nenu Naa Desam**).
Bhakna called **Kartar Singh Sarabha** his **"General"**.
Ghadar founded **1913**, first meeting in **Oregon**.

208.s: Annie Besant was styled as the:
208.x: Annie Besant was styled the “Iron Lady of Ireland.” She was of Irish origin and later became a prominent Indian nationalist leader.
208.tq: Test the title-person association without confusing Besant's title with titles associated with Indian leaders.
xs: Annie Besant was styled the **"Iron Lady of Ireland"** — option **(3)**.
She was born on **1 October 1847** at **Clapham, London**, of **Irish origin**.
xa: In England she was a **Fabian socialist** (Fabian Society).
Joined the **Theosophical Society (1888)**; came to India in **1893**; TS **President in 1907**.
⚠ Tilak = **"Lokmanya"** / **"Father of Indian Unrest"** (Chirol); Besant = **"Iron Lady of Ireland"**.
First woman **INC president (1917)**.

208.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Tilak's newspapers is correctly matched?
208.x: Tilak founded or edited Kesari as a Marathi paper and Mahratta as an English paper; both are associated with the year 1881.
208.tq: Use the language distinction between two newspapers with the same founder and year.
xs: **Kesari** was **Marathi** and **Mahratta** was **English** — option **(1)**.
Both were started by **Tilak** in **1881**.
xa: Tilak's slogan: **"Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it"**.
Besant's papers: **Common Weal (January 1914)** and **New India** (renamed **Madras Standard**).
Tilak born **23 July 1856, Ratnagiri**.

208.s: Tilak began the public celebration of Ganeshotsav and the Shivaji festival respectively in:
208.x: Tilak began the public Ganeshotsav celebration in 1893 and the Shivaji festival in 1895. Both festivals were used to promote public mobilisation and nationalist consciousness.
208.tq: Remember the paired years in sequence and reject the reversed-order option.
xs: Tilak made **Ganeshotsav** public in **1893** and the **Shivaji festival** in **1895** — option **(2)**.
**1881** = **Kesari** and **Mahratta**; **1914** = release from **Mandalay**; **1916** = his **Home Rule League**.
xa: Titles: **"Lokmanya"**; **"Father of Indian Unrest"** (**Valentine Chirol**).
Born **23 July 1856**, **Ratnagiri**.
Released from Mandalay on **16 June 1914** after **6** years.

208.s: The Central Hindu College founded by Annie Besant in 1898 was located at
208.x: Annie Besant founded the Central Hindu College at Varanasi in 1898. It later became the core of Banaras Hindu University under Madan Mohan Malaviya.
208.tq: Distinguish the two institutions by their locations.
xs: Besant's **Central Hindu College (1898)** was at **Varanasi** — option **(2)**.
