It became the core of **BHU** under **Madan Mohan Malaviya**.
xa: APPSC-GS **2019**: TS President **1907**, first woman INC president **1917**, Central Hindu College **1898** — all correct.
**Madanapalle college** is cited for Home Rule strength in Andhra.
Besant came to India in **1893**.

208.s: Annie Besant drafted the Commonwealth of India Bill in
208.x: Annie Besant drafted the Commonwealth of India Bill in 1925 as a proposed dominion constitution.
208.tq: Use the year-based numerical distinction among related constitutional events.
xs: Besant drafted the **Commonwealth of India Bill** in **1925** — option **(3)**.
It was her draft **dominion constitution**.
xa: Her protege **Jiddu Krishnamurti** wrote **"At the Feet of the Master"**.
She became TS **President in 1907**.
**1917**: interned (June), released (Sept), **INC President** at Calcutta.

208.s: Annie Besant renamed the Madras Standard as New India after purchasing it in:
208.x: Annie Besant purchased the Madras Standard in July 1914 and renamed it New India. New India was a daily newspaper.
208.tq: Use the exact month and the newspaper's earlier name as the discriminating clues.
xs: Besant bought the **Madras Standard** in **July 1914** and renamed it **New India** — option **(3)**.
**January 1914** was her English weekly **Common Weal**.
**April/September 1916** were the founding months of the two **Home Rule Leagues**.
xa: APPSC G2 **2025** asked this twice.
⚠ Tilak was released on **16 June 1914** — the same summer.

208.s: Who described Bal Gangadhar Tilak as the 'Father of Indian Unrest'?
208.x: British journalist Valentine Chirol called Tilak the 'Father of Indian Unrest'. Curzon, Montagu and Minto were British officials who did not coin this title; Minto is called 'Father of the Communal Electorate'.
208.tq: Father of Indian Unrest = Tilak, per Valentine Chirol.
xs: British journalist **Valentine Chirol** called Tilak the **"Father of Indian Unrest"** — option **(2)**.
Tilak's popular title was **"Lokmanya"**.
**Montagu** is linked to the **August Declaration (1917)**; **Minto** is the **"Father of the Communal Electorate"**.
xa: Tilak started **Kesari** and **Mahratta** (**1881**).
He made **Ganeshotsav (1893)** and **Shivaji festival (1895)** public.
His Home Rule League: **28 April 1916**.

208.s:
With reference to Annie Besant, consider the following statements:
1. She became President of the Theosophical Society in 1907.
2. She was the first woman President of the Indian National Congress (1917).
3. She first came to India in 1907.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
208.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct (APPSC-GS 2019): she became TS President in 1907 and was the first woman INC President at Calcutta in 1917. Statement 3 is wrong: she came to India in 1893. So B, C and D, which include statement 3, are wrong.
208.tq: Besant: India 1893, CHC 1898, TS President 1907, INC President 1917.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)** (APPSC-GS **2019**).
**1:** She became **President of the Theosophical Society in 1907**.
**2:** First woman **INC President (1917)**, Calcutta.
**3** wrong: she came to India in **1893**, not 1907.
xa: Joined the TS in **1888** (**1889** in many texts).
Founded **Central Hindu College (1898)**.
Interned at **Ootacamund**, **15 June 1917**.

208.s: The All India Home Rule League of Annie Besant was founded in:
208.x: Annie Besant's All India Home Rule League was founded in Madras in September 1916. Its headquarters was at Adyar, in Gokhale Hall.
208.tq: Discriminate between the two Leagues by separating their founding places and dates.
xs: Besant's **All India Home Rule League** was founded in **Madras** in **September 1916** — option **(1)**.
HQ: **Adyar** (**Gokhale Hall**).
**Belgaum/Poona, April 1916** = **Tilak's** league.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say **1915** — her self-government campaign began then; the league itself = **Sept 1916**.
Organising secretary: **George Arundale**; ~**200 branches**.
Covered the rest of India, **including Bombay city**.

208.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the territorial jurisdiction of Tilak's Home Rule League?
o: Madras Presidency, Bengal and Assam only
Bombay city, Madras and the Central Provinces
Maharashtra excluding Bombay city, Karnataka, Central Provinces and Berar
The whole of India including Bombay city
208.x: Tilak's League operated in Maharashtra except Bombay city, Karnataka, the Central Provinces and Berar. Besant's League covered the rest of India, including Bombay city.
208.tq: Test the reversed-area trap by comparing the territorial spheres of the two Leagues.
xs: Tilak's league covered **Maharashtra (excluding Bombay city), Karnataka, Central Provinces and Berar** — option **(3)**.
**Besant's** league covered the rest of India, **including Bombay city**.
xa: Tilak's league: launched at **Belgaum** (Bombay Provincial Conference), based at **Poona**.
President **Joseph Baptista**; Secretary **N.C. Kelkar**.
Tilak's league was **better organised**; Besant's reached a **wider audience**.

208.s:
With reference to the Home Rule Leagues, consider the following statements:
1. Besant's League covered the rest of India, including Bombay city.
2. Besant's League had approximately 200 branches.
3. Tilak's League reached a wider audience than Besant's League.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
208.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Besant's League covered the rest of India including Bombay city and had about 200 branches. Statement 3 is wrong: Tilak's League was better organised, but it was Besant's that reached a wider audience. So 1 and 2 only.
208.tq: Identify the reversed comparison in statement 3 while retaining the correct geographical and numerical statements.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** Besant's league covered the rest of India, **including Bombay city**.
**2:** It had ~**200 branches**.
**3** wrong: Tilak's league was **better organised**, but **Besant's reached a wider audience**.
xa: Allied bodies: **Young Men's India Association**, **Boy Scouts Association**, **Order of Sons of India**.
Tilak's league merged into Besant's.
Andhra had **52 branches by 1917**.

208.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Office-bearer)
a. Joseph Baptista
b. N.C. Kelkar
c. George Arundale
d. B.P. Wadia

List-II (Association)
i. Secretary of Tilak's League
ii. President of Tilak's League
iii. Organising Secretary of Besant's League
iv. Treasurer associated with Besant's League

Code:
208.x: Joseph Baptista was President and N.C. Kelkar Secretary of Tilak's League. George Arundale was the organising secretary of Besant's League, while B.P. Wadia was associated with it as treasurer.
208.tq: Start from the sure pair of Joseph Baptista with Tilak's League and complete the matching.
xs: The match is **a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv** — option **(1)**.
**Joseph Baptista** = **President**, **N.C. Kelkar** = **Secretary** of Tilak's league.
**George Arundale** = **Organising secretary** of Besant's league; **B.P. Wadia** = **Treasurer** (Madras League).
xa: Madras League General Secretary: **C.P. Ramaswamy Aiyar**.
⚠ Besant was interned with **Wadia** and **Arundale** at **Ootacamund** (**15 June 1917**).
Some notes give Kelkar's initials as **N.G.**

208.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct regarding Tilak's Home Rule League?
o: It was founded by Tilak in 1914 immediately after his release from Mandalay jail.
208.x: The statement is NOT correct because Tilak's League was founded in April 1916, not in 1914. Tilak was released from Mandalay jail on 16 June 1914.
208.tq: Find the wrong year in the statement while retaining its correct founder and associated place.
xs: The wrong statement is that Tilak founded his league in **1914** — option **(4)**.
He was released from **Mandalay jail on 16 June 1914**; his league came in **April 1916** (APPSC-GS **2024**).
It was launched at **Belgaum** and based at **Poona** — (1), (2), (3) are true.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say "from Pune" or "Bombay/Deccan" for the launch.
Exact founding date: **28 April 1916**.
Some notes misdate Gadicherla's Andhra-branch post to **1914**.

208.s: Who popularised the Home Rule idea in the United Provinces and is associated with the statement, “First we are Indians, then only Muslims”?
208.x: Muhammad Ali Jinnah popularised the Home Rule movement in the United Provinces. The statement emphasised a common Indian political identity above communal distinctions.
208.tq: Link the quotation to the leader's specific regional role in the movement.
xs: **Muhammad Ali Jinnah** popularised Home Rule in **UP** — option **(2)**.
His line: **"First we are Indians, then only Muslims"**.
**Arundale**, **Kelkar** and **Baptista** were office-bearers of the leagues.
xa: Tilak's Lucknow Pact remark: **"Better two united fists than a thousand scattered fingers"**.
The **Lucknow Pact (1916)** cemented Congress-League unity.

208.s: Who organised Annie Besant's tour covering Kakinada, Rajahmundry and Eluru?
208.x: Mocherla Hanumantha Rao organised Annie Besant's tour in Kakinada, Rajahmundry and Eluru.
208.tq: Use the activity–leader association rather than a general leadership link.
xs: **Mocherla Hanumantha Rao** organised Besant's tour — option **(1)**.
After **Lucknow (1916)** she toured **Kakinada, Rajahmundry** and **Eluru**.
**Gadicherla** was **Secretary** of the Andhra branch; **Konda Venkatappayya** and **Pattabhi** were Home Rule leaders.
xa: Other leaders: **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**, **K.V. Reddy Naidu**.
Branches at **Guntur, Vijayawada, Kakinada**.
On her arrest: **"Confinement Day"** protests at **Tenali** and **Vijayawada**.

208.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Newspaper)
a. Andhra Mata
b. Desamata
c. Patakari
d. Krishna Patrika

List-II (Association)
i. Chilakamarti
 ii. Eluru
 iii. Mutnuri
 iv. Strong support to Home Rule

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
208.x: Andhra Mata strongly supported Home Rule, Desamata was associated with Chilakamarti, Patakari with Eluru, and Krishna Patrika with Mutnuri.
208.tq: Start from the sure newspaper–association pairs and eliminate codes.
xs: The match is **a–iv, b–i, c–ii, d–iii** — option **(1)**.
**Andhra Mata** strongly backed Home Rule (APPSC G2 **2017**); **Desamata** — **Chilakamarti**.
**Patakari** — **Eluru**; **Krishna Patrika** — **Mutnuri**.
xa: **Andhra Patrika** — **Kasinathuni**.
Besant's own papers: **Common Weal** and **New India**.
Andhra was one of the strongest Home Rule regions: **52 branches**.

208.s: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao was associated with which newspaper?
208.x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao was associated with Andhra Patrika.
208.tq: Use the founder or editor–newspaper association.
xs: **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** is linked with **Andhra Patrika** — option **(2)**.
**Desamata** = Chilakamarti; **Patakari** = Eluru; **Andhra Mata** = strong Home Rule backer.
xa: He was also an Andhra **Home Rule leader**.
Spelling variant: **Kasinadhuni**.
**Krishna Patrika** = **Mutnuri**.

208.s: The protests held at Tenali and Vijayawada following Annie Besant's arrest were known as
208.x: The protests at Tenali and Vijayawada following Besant's arrest were called “Confinement Day” protests.
208.tq: Recall the exact name of the protest occasion.
xs: The protests at **Tenali** and **Vijayawada** were **"Confinement Day"** protests — option **(4)**.
They followed **Besant's arrest/internment** (**15 June 1917**).
xa: Interned at **Ootacamund** with **B.P. Wadia** and **G.S. Arundale**.
Released **17 September 1917**.
Machilipatnam students wore **"Besant lockets"** (Extremist-phase notes).

208.s: *New India*, associated with Annie Besant, was originally known as which newspaper?
208.x: *New India* was the renamed *Madras Standard*.
208.tq: Test the renaming relationship rather than confusing two newspapers of the same movement.
xs: **New India** was the renamed **Madras Standard** — option **(1)**.
Besant bought it in **July 1914**.
**Common Weal** was her separate weekly (**January 1914**).
xa: APPSC G2 **2025** asked this twice.
**Andhra Mata** was a Telugu paper backing Home Rule.

208.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Andhra Home Rule movement is correct?
1. Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao translated Sarojini Naidu's Awake Mother.
2. The translation was titled Nuthana Haindava Matrigeetham.
3. Telugu pamphlets included Swarajya Paramoddesham.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
208.x: All three statements are correct. Harisarvottama Rao translated Awake Mother as Nuthana Haindava Matrigeetham and used Telugu pamphlets such as Swarajya Paramoddesham.
208.tq: Test the author, translated title and pamphlet together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**1 and 2:** **Gadicherla** translated **Sarojini Naidu's Awake Mother** as **Nuthana Haindava Matrigeetham**.
**3:** Telugu pamphlets included **Swarajya Paramoddesham**.
xa: He used **libraries as lecture venues**.
Gadicherla = **Secretary** of the Andhra branch.
Andhra had **52 branches by 1917**.

208.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the organisation of the Home Rule League in Andhra?
o: A separate Andhra branch functioned under Kanneganti Hanumanthu, with branches at Macherla and Minchalapadu.
The Andhra branch was headed by Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya, with branches only at Eluru and Nellore.
A separate Andhra branch functioned under Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao, with branches at Guntur, Vijayawada and Kakinada.
The Andhra branch was headed by Annie Besant from Vijayawada, with branches at Tirupati and Kadapa.
208.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao served as secretary of the Andhra division. Branches were established at Guntur, Vijayawada and Kakinada.
208.tq: Use the organisation–leader–branch-town combination to reject swapped leaders and places.
xs: A **separate Andhra branch** worked under **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao**, with branches at **Guntur, Vijayawada and Kakinada** — option **(3)**.
Gadicherla was its **Secretary**.
xa: **52 branches** in Andhra **by 1917**.
Leaders: **Konda Venkatappayya**, **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**, **K.V. Reddy Naidu**, **Pattabhi Sitaramayya**.
Propaganda via Telugu pamphlets such as **Swarajya Paramoddesham**.

208.s: How did Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao help spread the Home Rule movement in Andhra?
o: By organising police stations and collecting Pullari tax
By using libraries as lecture venues and distributing pamphlets
By leading the cattle-rescue action at Minchalapadu
By establishing courts and boycotting national schools
208.x: Gadicherla spread Home Rule ideas through pamphlets and used libraries as venues for lectures.
208.tq: Identify the practical method of political mobilisation from the activities of the leader.
xs: Gadicherla **used libraries as lecture venues** and **distributed pamphlets** — option **(2)**.
Pamphlets were in **Telugu** (e.g. **Swarajya Paramoddesham**).
xa: He translated **Awake Mother** as **Nuthana Haindava Matrigeetham**.
Branches: **Guntur, Vijayawada, Kakinada**.
⚠ Some notes date his post to **1914**; the leagues date from **1916**.

208.s: Annie Besant was interned in 1917 and was released in
208.x: Annie Besant was interned in June 1917 and released in September 1917.
208.tq: Distinguish the paired months of detention and release.
xs: Besant was released in **September 1917** (**17 September**) — option **(4)**.
She had been interned on **15 June 1917**.
**August 1917** = **Montagu Declaration** (**20 Aug**); **December 1917** = Andhra delegation met Montagu.
xa: Released under **INC-League pressure**.
The internment **boosted the movement** and drew in **Moderates**.
**1917**: she became **INC President** (Calcutta).

208.s: Annie Besant was interned on 15 June 1917 at which place along with B. P. Wadia and G. S. Arundale?
208.x: Annie Besant was interned at Ootacamund on 15 June 1917 along with B. P. Wadia and G. S. Arundale.
208.tq: Use the place-name anchor to distinguish the internment event from other Home Rule centres.
xs: Besant was interned at **Ootacamund** — option **(2)**.
With **B.P. Wadia** and **G.S. Arundale**, on **15 June 1917**.
xa: Released **17 September 1917**.
Montagu's remark: **"Shiva cut his wife into fifty-two pieces..."**.
Andhra reacted with **"Confinement Day"** protests.

208.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the internment of Annie Besant:
1. It aroused public outrage and strengthened the Home Rule Movement.
2. It attracted several Moderates towards the movement.
3. Besant was released under pressure from the Congress and the Muslim League.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
208.x: All three statements are correct. Besant's internment intensified public agitation, brought Moderates into the movement and ended with her release under Congress-League pressure.
208.tq: Combine the cause, political effect and release mechanism in a three-statement question.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**1:** Outrage **boosted the movement**.
**2:** It **drew in Moderates**.
**3:** Released (**17 September 1917**) under **INC-League pressure**.
xa: Interned at **Ootacamund** on **15 June 1917**.
**Montagu** commented on the folly of the internment.
Tenali and Vijayawada held **"Confinement Day"** protests.

208.s:
Consider the following statements about the Montagu (August) Declaration of 20 August 1917:
1. It was announced by Lord Chelmsford, the Viceroy.
2. It was the British answer to the Home Rule agitation and effectively blunted it.
3. It led towards the Government of India Act, 1919.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
208.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: the Declaration answered the Home Rule agitation, blunted and effectively ended it, and led to the 1919 Act. Statement 1 is wrong: it was announced by Edwin Montagu, the Secretary of State; Chelmsford was the Viceroy. So A, C and D, which include statement 1, are wrong.
208.tq: August Declaration = Montagu (Secretary of State), not Chelmsford (Viceroy).
xs: Statements **2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
**1** wrong: the declaration was by **Edwin Montagu, Secretary of State**; **Chelmsford** was the **Viceroy**.
**2:** It was the British answer to Home Rule and **blunted and effectively ended** the agitation.
**3:** It led to the **1919 Act**.
xa: Date: **20 August 1917**.
Goal: **"progressive realisation of responsible government"**.
Congress split over Mont-Ford proposals at **Bombay (Aug 1918)** under **Hasan Imam**.

208.s: The central objective expressed in the Montagu Declaration was:
o: Immediate complete independence from British rule
Progressive realisation of responsible government through self-governing institutions
Introduction of separate electorates for all communities
208.x: The Declaration promised the gradual development of self-governing institutions and the progressive realisation of responsible government by increasing Indian participation in administration.
208.tq: Choose the precise constitutional objective rather than an extreme or unrelated alternative.
xs: Its objective was the **progressive realisation of responsible government** through **self-governing institutions** — option **(2)**.
Also: **increasing Indian association** in administration.
It did not promise independence; **separate electorates** were a **1909** feature.
xa: Announced by **Edwin Montagu** on **20 August 1917**.
It led to the **1919 Act**.
It raised Andhra's hopes for a **separate province**.

208.s: The demand raised by the Andhra delegation before Montagu in December 1917 primarily concerned:
o: The transfer of the capital to Delhi
The formation of the Swarajya Sabha
208.x: The Montagu Declaration raised hopes of a separate Andhra province, and an Andhra delegation led by Nyapati Subba Rao met Montagu on 20 December 1917 to press that demand.
208.tq: Infer the regional political objective from the delegation's context.
xs: The Andhra delegation sought a **separate Andhra province** — option **(1)**.
Led by **Nyapati Subba Rao**, it met Montagu on **20 Dec 1917**.
The **Montagu Declaration** had raised these hopes.
xa: Declaration date: **20 August 1917**.
**Swarajya Sabha** came only in **1920**.
Andhra had **52 Home Rule branches by 1917**.

208.s: The Surat split of 1907 between the Moderates and Extremists was healed at:
208.x: The split that occurred at Surat in 1907 was healed at the Lucknow session in 1916.
208.tq: Use the earlier split and later reunion as first-and-last chronological anchors.
xs: The **Surat split (1907)** was healed at **Lucknow in 1916** — option **(2)**.
**Bombay 1918** was the **Hasan Imam** special session where Congress split again over Mont-Ford proposals.
xa: Lucknow also cemented **Congress-League unity**.
Reunion eased by **Tilak and Besant's** efforts.
**Gokhale** and **Pherozeshah Mehta** died in **1915**.

208.s: The reunion of the Moderates and Extremists at Lucknow was facilitated mainly by:
o: The formation of the Indian National Liberal Federation alone
Tilak and Besant's efforts, along with the deaths of Gokhale and Pherozeshah Mehta
208.x: Tilak and Besant worked for reunion, while the deaths of Gopal Krishna Gokhale and Pherozeshah Mehta in 1915 removed important obstacles to reconciliation.
208.tq: Match the reunion with its political facilitators, avoiding a later-event trap.
xs: Reunion was eased by **Tilak and Besant's efforts** and the **deaths of Gokhale and Pherozeshah Mehta** — option **(4)**.
Both deaths came in **1915**.
The **Montagu Declaration** (**1917**) and **1919 Act** came after Lucknow — so (2) is wrong.
xa: Lucknow **1916** reunited **Moderates and Extremists**.
Tilak's remark on the Pact: **"Better two united fists than a thousand scattered fingers"**.
Congress **accepted separate electorates** for Muslims at Lucknow.

208.s: Which of the following correctly describes the later fate of the All India Home Rule League?
o: Besant's League merged into Tilak's League and remained independent.
Tilak's League merged into Besant's League; in 1920 it was renamed Swarajya Sabha under Gandhi and later merged into the Congress.
It was immediately converted into the Indian National Liberal Federation in 1918.
It was dissolved at the Lucknow session in 1916.
208.x: Tilak's League merged into Besant's League. In 1920, the All India Home Rule League under Gandhi's presidency was renamed Swarajya Sabha and soon merged into the Congress.
208.tq: Track organisational transformation in sequence rather than confusing the League with a contemporary federation.
xs: **Tilak's league merged into Besant's**; in **1920** it was renamed **Swarajya Sabha** under **Gandhi** and soon merged into the Congress — option **(2)**.
So it was not dissolved at Lucknow (**1916**), nor did Besant's merge into Tilak's.
xa: Besant's league HQ: **Adyar** (Gokhale Hall).
**1920**: **Non-Cooperation** launched.
Significance: filled the gap between **Gokhale's death (1915)** and **Gandhi's rise (1920)**.

208.s: The special session of the Congress held at Bombay in August 1918 to consider the Montagu-Chelmsford proposals was presided over by:
208.x: Hasan Imam presided over the special Bombay session of August 1918, where the Congress split over the Mont-Ford proposals. Ambika Charan Majumdar presided at Lucknow (1916) and Annie Besant at Calcutta (1917); Malaviya did not preside at this special session.
208.tq: Special session 1918 Bombay = Hasan Imam.
xs: The **Bombay special session (Aug 1918)** was presided over by **Hasan Imam** — option **(2)**.
Congress **split** there over the **Mont-Ford proposals**.
**Ambika Charan Majumdar** presided at **Lucknow (1916)**; **Besant** at **Calcutta (1917)**.
xa: The proposals followed the **Montagu Declaration (20 August 1917)**.
They led to the **1919 Act**.
⚠ Montagu = **Secretary of State**; Chelmsford = **Viceroy**.

208.s: Tilak was released from prison on
208.x: Tilak was released on 16 June 1914.
208.tq: Test the exact date against nearby Home Rule chronology.
xs: Tilak was released on **16 June 1914** — option **(2)**.
He had served **6** years in **Mandalay**.
**9 January 1915** = Gandhi's return; **28 April 1916** = Tilak's league; **20 August 1917** = Montagu Declaration.
xa: **1914**: Komagata Maru; **WWI** began (from **Aug 1914**).
⚠ He did not found his league in **1914** (APPSC-GS **2024**).

208.s: The statement “Better two united fists than a thousand scattered fingers” is associated with which event and leader?
208.x: The statement is associated with the Lucknow Pact and was made by B.G. Tilak.
208.tq: Link the quotation to both its context and speaker.
xs: **"Better two united fists than a thousand scattered fingers"** = **Tilak** on the **Lucknow Pact** — option **(3)**.
It was not **Jinnah's**, **Montagu's** or **Besant's**; the Pact (Dec **1916**) sealed **Congress-League unity**.
xa: Tilak also said **"Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it"**.
Jinnah: **"First we are Indians, then only Muslims"**.
Through the Pact, Congress **accepted separate electorates** — what it had opposed in **1909**.

208.s: The remark about Shiva cutting his wife into fifty-two pieces, in the context of Annie Besant's internment, was made by
208.x: Edwin Montagu used the remark while commenting on the folly of Annie Besant's internment.
208.tq: Avoid swapping the British official with Indian nationalist leaders.
xs: The Shiva remark was **Edwin Montagu's** — option **(2)**.
It mocked the **folly of Besant's internment**.
xa: Besant interned **15 June 1917**, **Ootacamund**.
Montagu, **Secretary of State**, issued the **August Declaration (20 August 1917)**.
The internment **boosted** the movement.

208.s:
Which of the following events took place in 1915?
1. Gandhi returned from South Africa.
2. Gokhale died.
3. Tilak's Home Rule League was established.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
208.x: Gandhi returned from South Africa on 9 January 1915 and Gokhale died in 1915. Tilak's Home Rule League was established in April 1916.
208.tq: Reject the statement shifted from 1915 to 1916.
xs: **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
**1:** **Gandhi returned** from South Africa in **1915** (**9 Jan**).
**2:** **Gokhale died** in **1915**.
**3** wrong: Tilak's league came on **28 April 1916**.
xa: **Pherozeshah Mehta** also died in **1915**.
**1916**: Besant's league (Sept); **Lucknow Pact** (Dec).
**1914**: Besant's **Common Weal** and **New India**.

208.s: Which one of the following chronological sequences is correct?
o: Tilak's Home Rule League → Besant's Home Rule League → Lucknow Pact → Montagu Declaration
Besant's Home Rule League → Tilak's Home Rule League → Montagu Declaration → Lucknow Pact
Lucknow Pact → Tilak's Home Rule League → Besant's Home Rule League → Montagu Declaration
Tilak's Home Rule League → Lucknow Pact → Besant's Home Rule League → Montagu Declaration
208.x: Tilak's League was formed in April 1916, Besant's in September 1916, the Lucknow Pact was concluded in December 1916, and the Montagu Declaration was issued in August 1917.
208.tq: Place events within the same year by their months.
xs: The sequence is **Tilak's league → Besant's league → Lucknow Pact → Montagu Declaration** — option **(1)**.
**April 1916** → **September 1916** → **December 1916** → **20 August 1917**.
xa: **15 June 1917**: Besant interned.
**Aug 1918**: Bombay special session (**Hasan Imam**).
**1920**: **Swarajya Sabha**; **Non-Cooperation**.

208.s: Which one of the following pairs of quotation and leader is NOT correctly matched?
o: "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it" — B.G. Tilak
"First we are Indians, then only Muslims" — M.A. Jinnah
"Better two united fists than a thousand scattered fingers" — Annie Besant
"Shiva cut his wife into fifty-two pieces..." — Edwin Montagu
208.x: "Better two united fists than a thousand scattered fingers" was Tilak's remark on the Lucknow Pact, not Besant's. The Swaraj slogan was Tilak's, the 'first we are Indians' line Jinnah's, and the Shiva remark Montagu's on Besant's internment.
208.tq: Both 'Swaraj' and 'two united fists' = Tilak.
xs: The mismatch is **"Better two united fists..." — Annie Besant** — option **(3)**; it was **Tilak's** remark on the **Lucknow Pact**.
The others are correct: Swaraj slogan — **Tilak**; "First we are Indians" — **Jinnah**; Shiva remark — **Montagu**.
xa: Montagu's remark referred to **Besant's internment** (**1917**).
Jinnah popularised Home Rule in **UP**.
Tilak's titles: **"Lokmanya"**, **"Father of Indian Unrest"**.

208.s: Which one of the following best explains the historical significance of the Home Rule Movement?
o: It restricted nationalist activity to the major presidency towns.
It replaced the Congress permanently with the Muslim League.
It ended all political work until the Non-Cooperation Movement.
It filled the gap between Gokhale's death and Gandhi's rise, while preparing cadres and organisations for later mass politics.
208.x: The movement bridged the period between Gokhale's death in 1915 and Gandhi's rise in 1920, built countryside organisation and trained cadres who later participated in Gandhian movements.
208.tq: Choose the option that combines the movement's transitional, organisational and preparatory roles.
xs: Home Rule **filled the gap between Gokhale's death and Gandhi's rise** and **prepared cadres** — option **(4)**.
Gokhale died in **1915**; Gandhi rose in **1920**.
It built **organisation in the countryside** and trained later **Gandhian cadres**.
xa: It **shifted the movement from elite to masses**, linking town and country.
It ended with the **Montagu Declaration**, which blunted the agitation.
League renamed **Swarajya Sabha** (**1920**) under Gandhi.

208.s: Which of the following correctly represents the strength of the Home Rule Movement in Andhra?
o: It had 52 branches and was supported by the Andhra Mata and Desamata press and Madanapalle college.
It had 25 branches and was supported only by the Swarajya Sabha.
It had 52 branches but had no links with educational institutions.
It was confined to the city of Lucknow and had no Andhra presence.
208.x: Andhra was one of the strongest Home Rule regions, with 52 branches and support from Andhra Mata, Desamata and Madanapalle college.
208.tq: Check the regional number together with its associated press and educational institutions.
xs: Andhra had **52 branches**, the **Andhra Mata/Desamata press** and **Madanapalle college** — option **(1)**.
Andhra was one of the **strongest Home Rule regions**.
xa: Branches at **Guntur, Vijayawada, Kakinada**; secretary **Gadicherla**.
Besant toured **Kakinada, Rajahmundry, Eluru**.
**"Confinement Day"** protests at **Tenali** and **Vijayawada**.

208.s: Which one of the following was a major social-political effect of the Home Rule Movement?
o: It confined political participation to constitutional lawyers.
It discouraged the formation of rural branches.
It weakened Congress-League cooperation at Lucknow.
It shifted nationalist politics from an elite base towards the masses and linked towns with the countryside.
208.x: The movement broadened the freedom struggle beyond elite circles, connected urban and rural areas and prepared the ground for Gandhi's mass politics.
208.tq: Identify the broad movement impact rather than a statement that reverses its organisational role.
xs: It **shifted politics from elite to masses** and **linked towns with the countryside** — option **(4)**.
This **prepared the ground for Gandhi**.
xa: It built **organisation in the countryside** and trained **Gandhian cadres**.
Besant's league had ~**200 branches**; Andhra **52**.
Lucknow **1916** strengthened, not weakened, Congress-League unity.

208.s: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 is significant in the history of communal politics because the Congress:
o: Rejected all forms of communal representation
208.x: Through the Lucknow Pact, the Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims.
208.tq: Distinguish acceptance from later rejection or extension of a constitutional device.
xs: At Lucknow the Congress **accepted separate electorates for Muslims** — option **(3)**.
It accepted what it had **opposed in 1909** (Morley-Minto).
xa: **Lucknow 1916** also reunited **Moderates and Extremists**.
Tilak: **"Better two united fists than a thousand scattered fingers"**.
Reunion eased by deaths of **Gokhale** and **Pherozeshah Mehta (1915)**.

209.s: The Hindustan Republican Association was reorganised as the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association in:
209.x: The HSRA name dates from 1928, following the meeting at Feroz Shah Kotla in Delhi. The HRA had been established in 1924.
209.tq: Discriminate between the HRA foundation year and the HSRA conversion year.
xs: The HRA became the **HSRA** in **1928** — option **(3)**.
It was reorganised at a meeting at **Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi**, under **Chandrashekhar Azad** after Bismil's death.
**1924** = HRA founded at **Kanpur**; **1925** = **Kakori**; **1931** = executions.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say Bhagat Singh "joined the HSRA in **1925**" — in 1925 it was still the **HRA**.
HSRA goal: **socialist** revolution; "Federal Republic of United States of India".
HSRA members: **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Bejoy Kumar Sinha**, Rajguru, B.K. Dutt.

209.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Organisation or leader)
 a. HRA
 b. HSRA
 c. Bhagat Singh
 d. Chandrashekhar Azad

List-II (Association)
 i. Reorganised the revolutionary organisation after Bismil's death
 ii. Socialist revolution
 iii. Founded in 1924 at Kanpur
 iv. Credited with the founding of the HSRA

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
209.x: The HRA was founded at Kanpur in 1924; the HSRA stood for socialist revolution; Bhagat Singh is credited with the HSRA's founding; and Azad reorganised it after Bismil's death.
209.tq: Start with the certain organisation–year pair and then resolve the leader associations.
xs: The match is **a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**HRA** = founded **1924** at **Kanpur**; **HSRA** = **socialist revolution**.
**Bhagat Singh** = credited with founding the HSRA (APPSC-GS **2018**); **Azad** = reorganised it after **Bismil's death**.
xa: HRA founders: **Bismil, Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee, Sachindra Nath Sanyal** (APPSC-G1 **2024**).
⚠ Bhagat Singh was **not** an HRA founder.
HSRA formed at **Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi** (**1928**).

209.s: The stated goal of the HSRA was associated with the establishment of a:
o: Federal Republic of United States of India
209.x: The HSRA envisaged a 'Federal Republic of United States of India' and advocated socialist revolution.
209.tq: Recall the exact constitutional phrase rather than a broad substitute such as socialist republic.
xs: The HSRA aimed at a **"Federal Republic of United States of India"** — option **(1)**.
Its goal was **socialist** revolution, beyond the HRA's armed revolution for a republic.
xa: HSRA: **1928**, Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi.
Credited to **Bhagat Singh** with **Azad** and **Sukhdev**.
Shift to **socialist** ideology and **mass propaganda** (courtroom, leaflets, hunger strikes).

209.s:
Consider the following statements about the Naujawan Bharat Sabha:
1. It was founded at Delhi in 1928.
2. It was founded by Bhagat Singh, with Sukhdev as co-founder.
3. Bhagwati Charan Vohra was associated with its founding.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
209.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: Bhagat Singh founded it, co-founded by Sukhdev with Bhagwati Charan Vohra. Statement 1 is wrong: it was founded at Lahore in 1926; 1928 at Delhi (Feroz Shah Kotla) is the HSRA. So A, C and D, which include statement 1, are wrong.
209.tq: NBS = Lahore 1926; HSRA = Delhi 1928.
xs: Statements **2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
**1** wrong: the **Naujawan Bharat Sabha** was founded at **Lahore** in **1926**; **Delhi 1928** is the **HSRA**.
**2:** founded by **Bhagat Singh**, co-founded by **Sukhdev**.
**3:** **Bhagwati Charan Vohra** was also associated.
xa: Aim: mobilise **youth, peasants and workers** + fight **communalism**.
Vohra wrote **The Philosophy of the Bomb**.
Sukhdev taught at **National College, Lahore**.

209.s: The principal objective of the Naujawan Bharat Sabha was to
o: mobilise youth, peasants and workers and oppose communalism
establish a princely federation through constitutional reforms
secure separate electorates for revolutionary organisations
organise military assistance for the British during the First World War
209.x: The Sabha sought to mobilise youth, peasants and workers and to fight communalism.
209.tq: Identify the organisation from its distinctive social base and ideological objective.
xs: The Sabha aimed to **mobilise youth, peasants and workers** and **oppose communalism** — option **(1)**.
Founded **1926**, **Lahore**, by **Bhagat Singh** with **Sukhdev** (and **Vohra**).
xa: HSRA (**1928**) added **socialism** to the armed-revolt programme.
Bhagat Singh wrote **Why I am an Atheist (1930)**.
Influences: **Jallianwala Bagh (1919)**, **Nankana Sahib (1921)**, **Chauri Chaura (1922)**.

209.s: The Kakori Train Action was undertaken primarily to:
o: protest against the Trade Disputes Bill
destroy the railway line between Delhi and Lahore
obtain government treasury funds for the HRA
209.x: On 9 August 1925, the HRA looted the government treasury carried on a train near Kakori to fund its revolutionary activities.
209.tq: Identify the motive of an action rather than merely recalling its location or date.
xs: Kakori aimed to **obtain government treasury funds for the HRA** — option **(4)**.
On **9 August 1925** the HRA looted the **government treasury** on a train near **Kakori (Lucknow)**.
The **Trade Disputes Bill** protest was the **1929** Assembly bomb.
xa: **Azad** took part and escaped.
⚠ **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru** were **not** part of Kakori.
Hanged (**Dec 1927**): **Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh, Rajendra Lahiri**.

209.s: Which one of the following sets contains only those executed in connection with the Kakori Train Action?
o: Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri
Surya Sen, Ananta Singh, Ganesh Ghosh and Lokenath Bal
Jatin Das, Chandrashekhar Azad, Udham Singh and Gopinath Saha
Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru and Batukeshwar Dutt
209.x: Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri were hanged in connection with the Kakori case in December 1927.
209.tq: Group the correct case participants and exclude revolutionaries belonging to other cases.
xs: Kakori hangings: **Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri** — option **(1)**.
**Surya Sen's** group = Chittagong; **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru** = Lahore case (Dutt got **life**).
xa: Jails: **Bismil (Gorakhpur)**, **Ashfaqullah (Faizabad)**, **Roshan Singh (Allahabad/Naini)**, **Lahiri (Gonda)**.
Hanged in **Dec 1927**.
Bismil born **11 June 1897**.

209.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Kakori Train Action
B. Saunders killing
C. Central Assembly bomb incident
D. Chittagong Armoury Raid
209.x: The Kakori Train Action occurred in 1925, the Saunders killing in 1928, the Central Assembly bomb incident in April 1929 and the Chittagong Armoury Raid in April 1930.
209.tq: Place the events by their years and use the two April 1929–1930 events as the final check.
xs: The order is **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**A:** **Kakori 9 August 1925**; **B:** **Saunders, Dec 1928**.
**C:** **Assembly bomb 8 April 1929**; **D:** **Chittagong 18 April 1930**.
xa: Executions of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru: **23 March 1931**.
Azad died **27 Feb 1931**.
**Surya Sen** hanged **1934**.

209.s: J.P. Saunders was killed because the revolutionaries intended to avenge:
o: the death of Lala Lajpat Rai after the anti-Simon Commission lathi-charge
209.x: The Saunders killing was intended as revenge for the fatal injuries suffered by Lala Lajpat Rai during the anti-Simon Commission lathi-charge in October 1928.
209.tq: Match the assassination with its immediate political motive.
xs: Saunders was killed to avenge **Lala Lajpat Rai**, fatally injured in the **anti-Simon lathi-charge** (**Oct 1928**) — option **(2)**.
**Jallianwala Bagh** was avenged by **Udham Singh** (**1940**).
xa: Saunders (ASP) was **mistaken for SP James A. Scott**.
Shot by **Bhagat Singh and Rajguru** (Rajguru fired first), **Azad** covering.
The case led to the **Lahore Conspiracy Case** (trial **1929-1930**).

209.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Saunders killing is correct?
o: Michael O'Dwyer was killed in Lahore by Rajguru and Azad.
J.P. Saunders was mistakenly identified as James A. Scott, the intended target.
Charles Tegart was killed by Gopinath Saha in 1924.
Saunders was the intended target, and James A. Scott was killed by mistake.
209.x: J.P. Saunders, the Assistant Superintendent of Police, was mistakenly killed because he was taken for James A. Scott, associated with the anti-Simon lathi-charge.
209.tq: Discriminate between the actual victim and the intended target in an assassination attempt.
xs: **J.P. Saunders** was mistaken for **James A. Scott**, the intended target — option **(2)**.
Option (4) reverses them; **O'Dwyer** was killed in **London (1940)**; **Tegart** survived — Saha hit **Ernest Day**.
xa: Lahore, **Dec 1928**.
⚠ Saunders killed in place of **Scott**; Tegart's would-be killer hit **Ernest Day**.
**Rajguru** fired first.

209.s: Who fired first in the assassination of J.P. Saunders?
209.x: Rajguru fired first at J.P. Saunders, while Bhagat Singh also fired and Chandrashekhar Azad covered the retreat.
209.tq: Separate the roles of the shooter, the co-shooter and the covering revolutionary.
xs: **Rajguru** fired first — option **(4)**.
**Bhagat Singh** also fired; **Azad** covered the retreat (killing head constable **Chanan Singh**).
xa: ⚠ Notes saying Azad was "shot dead by an Indian constable" while pursuing are **wrong**.
Rajguru (Shivaram Hari) was born **1908**, **Khed** (now **Rajgurunagar**).
Rajguru was earlier in the **Seva Dal** (Varanasi).

209.s:
Consider the following statements about Udham Singh:
1. He shot Michael O'Dwyer at Caxton Hall, London.
2. The shooting took place on 13 March 1940.
3. His act was revenge for the death of Lala Lajpat Rai.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
209.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Udham Singh shot O'Dwyer at Caxton Hall, London, on 13 March 1940. Statement 3 is wrong: it was revenge for Jallianwala Bagh (O'Dwyer was the Punjab Lt. Governor); avenging Lajpat Rai was the motive of the Saunders killing (1928). So B, C and D, which include statement 3, are wrong.
209.tq: O'Dwyer -> Jallianwala; Saunders -> Lajpat Rai.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1 and 2:** **Udham Singh** shot **Michael O'Dwyer** at **Caxton Hall, London**, on **13 March 1940**.
**3** wrong: it was revenge for **Jallianwala Bagh** (O'Dwyer was **Punjab Lt. Governor**); avenging Lajpat Rai was the **Saunders** motive.
xa: Jallianwala Bagh (**1919**) also turned **Bhagat Singh** towards revolution.
Saunders killing: **Dec 1928**, Lahore.

209.s: Which statement about the 1924 attempt associated with Gopinath Saha is correct?
o: Saha shot Ernest Day by mistake while attempting to target Charles Tegart.
Saha attacked Michael O'Dwyer at Caxton Hall.
Saha shot Charles Tegart, the Police Commissioner of Calcutta, as intended.
Saha was involved in the Saunders killing at Lahore.
209.x: In Calcutta in 1924, Gopinath Saha attempted to target Police Commissioner Charles Tegart but mistakenly shot Ernest Day.
209.tq: Distinguish the intended target from the person actually killed in an attempted assassination.
xs: **Gopinath Saha** shot **Ernest Day** by mistake while aiming at **Charles Tegart** — option **(1)**.
Tegart was the **Calcutta Police Commissioner**; the attempt was in **1924**.
xa: ⚠ A parallel "wrong man" case: **Saunders** killed in place of **Scott** (**1928**).
**Udham Singh** shot **O'Dwyer** at Caxton Hall.
**1924** also: **HRA** founded at **Kanpur**.

209.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Central Legislative Assembly bomb incident of 8 April 1929?
o: Chandrashekhar Azad and Sukhdev attacked the Punjab Legislative Council.
Surya Sen and Ananta Singh attacked the Delhi Police Armoury.
Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt used non-lethal smoke bombs and distributed leaflets.
Bhagat Singh and Rajguru used lethal bombs to assassinate the Viceroy.
209.x: On 8 April 1929, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw non-lethal smoke bombs and leaflets in the Central Legislative Assembly in Delhi.
209.tq: Distinguish the Assembly action from assassination attempts and armoury raids by participants and purpose.
xs: **Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt** threw **non-lethal smoke bombs** and **leaflets** — option **(3)**.
Date: **8 April 1929**, **Central Legislative Assembly, Delhi**.
Rajguru was not involved, and the bombs were not meant to kill.
xa: Against the **Public Safety Bill** + **Trade Disputes Bill**.
Slogan **"Inquilab Zindabad"**; leaflet: **"To make the deaf hear"**.
Dutt got **life transportation** in the Assembly bomb case.

209.s: The Central Assembly bomb incident was primarily a protest against which Bills?
o: The Government of India Bill and the Rowlatt Bill
The Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill
The Trade Disputes Bill and the Indian Councils Bill
The Rowlatt Bill and the Public Safety Bill
209.x: The action protested against the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill, which were viewed as curbing civil liberties and workers' rights.
209.tq: Match the protest action with the precise legislative targets.
xs: The protest was against the **Public Safety Bill** and **Trade Disputes Bill** — option **(2)**.
These curbed **civil liberties** and **workers**.
xa: Bombs thrown on **8 April 1929** by **Bhagat Singh** and **Batukeshwar Dutt**.
They **courted arrest** to use the court as a platform.
Slogan: **"Inquilab Zindabad"**.

209.s: Which slogan was associated with the Central Assembly bomb incident?
209.x: The revolutionaries raised the slogan 'Inquilab Zindabad'. 'Do or Die' was later associated with the Quit India Movement.
209.tq: Separate slogans belonging to different phases of the national movement.
xs: The slogan was **"Inquilab Zindabad"** — option **(3)**.
The leaflet said the action was **"To make the deaf hear"**.
xa: Bhagat Singh and **Batukeshwar Dutt** threw **smoke (non-lethal) bombs**.
Date: **8 April 1929**.
Against the **Public Safety** and **Trade Disputes** Bills.

209.s:
Consider the following statements about the Central Assembly bomb action (1929):
1. The leaflet thrown said the action was 'to make the deaf hear'.
2. Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt escaped after the action to avoid a trial.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
209.x: Statement 1 is correct: the leaflet said 'To make the deaf hear'. Statement 2 is wrong: they deliberately courted arrest to use the court as a platform. So 2 only, both and neither are wrong.
209.tq: Assembly bomb strategy = court arrest, use the trial for propaganda.
xs: Only **statement 1** is correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** The leaflet said **"To make the deaf hear"**.
**2** wrong: they **courted arrest** to use the **court as a platform**.
xa: Slogan: **"Inquilab Zindabad"**.
Dutt: **life transportation**; Bhagat Singh tried in the **Lahore Conspiracy Case**.
Dutt died **1965**; cremated at **Hussainiwala**.

209.s: The second Lahore Conspiracy Case, which arose from the Saunders killing and bomb-making activities, was tried during which period?
209.x: The second Lahore Conspiracy Case was tried during 1929–1930. The first Lahore Conspiracy Case of 1915 was associated with the Ghadar movement.
209.tq: Distinguish the closely related first and second Lahore Conspiracy Cases by their dates.
xs: The **second Lahore Conspiracy Case** was tried in **1929-1930** — option **(3)**.
It arose from the **Saunders killing (1928)** and bomb-making.
The **first** Lahore case dates from **1915** — the **Ghadar** case; **1931** was the year of the executions.
xa: Executed: **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru**, **23 March 1931**, Lahore jail.
Cremated at **Hussainiwala** (Punjab).
Undertrials' **1929 Lahore jail hunger strike** for political-prisoner status.

209.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of revolutionaries who received transportation for life in the Lahore Conspiracy Case?
o: Kishori Lal, Mahabir Singh and Bejoy Kumar Sinha
Batukeshwar Dutt, Udham Singh and Surya Sen
Ram Prasad Bismil, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri
209.x: Kishori Lal, Mahabir Singh and Bejoy Kumar Sinha were among those sentenced to transportation for life. Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were executed.
209.tq: Use the sentence-category distinction instead of recalling only the principal executed leaders.
xs: **Kishori Lal, Mahabir Singh and Bejoy Kumar Sinha** got **transportation for life** — option **(1)**.
**Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru** were **executed**; **Bismil, Roshan Singh, Lahiri** were Kakori martyrs.
xa: Others transported for life: **Shiv Verma, Gaya Prasad, Jaidev Kapur, Kamalnath Tewari**.
**Batukeshwar Dutt**: life transportation in the **Assembly bomb** case.

209.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Lahore jail hunger strike of 1929:
1. It demanded political-prisoner status.
2. Bhagat Singh and Sukhdev participated in it.
3. Jatin Das was associated with it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
209.x: The hunger strike demanded political-prisoner status and involved Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Batukeshwar Dutt and Jatin Das. Therefore all three statements are correct.
209.tq: Combine the demand with the named participants and test the complete set.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**1:** The **1929 Lahore jail hunger strike** demanded **political-prisoner status**.
**2 and 3:** Participants included **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Dutt** and **Jatin Das**.
xa: **Jatin Das** died after a **63-day** hunger strike.
Hunger strikes were part of the HSRA's **mass propaganda**.
Lahore case trial: **1929-1930**.

209.s: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru, executed in Lahore jail on 23 March 1931, were cremated at:
209.x: They were cremated at Hussainiwala in Punjab. Alfred Park (Prayagraj) is where Azad died, Jalalabad Hills was the Chittagong fight, and Pentonville (London) is where Madan Lal Dhingra was hanged.
209.tq: Hussainiwala = cremation site of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru (and later B.K. Dutt).
xs: They were cremated at **Hussainiwala** (Punjab) — option **(1)**.
**Alfred Park** = Azad's death; **Jalalabad Hills** = Chittagong fight; **Pentonville** = Dhingra's hanging.
xa: Executed **23 March 1931** in **Lahore jail**.
**Batukeshwar Dutt** (d. **1965**) was also cremated at **Hussainiwala**.
Sukhdev born **15 May 1907**, Naughara, Ludhiana.

209.s: The Chittagong Armoury Raid of 18 April 1930 was led by:
209.x: The raid was led by Surya Sen, popularly known as Masterda. Ganesh Ghosh, Lokenath Bal and Ananta Singh were among his associates.
209.tq: Distinguish the principal leader from the named associates in a revolutionary operation.
xs: **Surya Sen ("Masterda")** led the **Chittagong Armoury Raid** (**18 April 1930**) — option **(3)**.
**Ganesh Ghosh, Lokenath Bal, Ananta Singh** were his **associates**.
xa: Group name: **Indian Republican Army** (also **Ambika Chakravarty**).
Fight at **Jalalabad Hills**; Surya Sen hanged **1934**.
Women: **Pritilata Waddedar**, **Kalpana Dutt**.

209.s:
Consider the following statements about the Chittagong Armoury Raid:
1. The revolutionaries cut telegraph and telephone lines.
2. They disrupted railway communications.
3. The associated fighting took place at the Jalalabad Hills.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
209.x: The operation involved cutting telegraph and telephone lines, disrupting railways and fighting at the Jalalabad Hills. All three statements are correct.
209.tq: Test the operational details together rather than only the leader's name.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**1:** They **cut telegraph/telephone lines**; they also attacked **police armouries**.
**2:** They **disrupted railways**.
**3:** Fighting at **Jalalabad Hills**.
xa: Leader: **Surya Sen**, **18 April 1930**.
**Pritilata Waddedar** led the **Pahartali European Club** raid.
Surya Sen hanged **1934**.

209.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bina Das — fired at the Bengal Governor at a convocation
Pritilata Waddedar — Pahartali European Club raid
Kalpana Dutt — sentenced to life imprisonment
Santi Ghosh and Suniti Choudhury — led the Pahartali European Club raid
209.x: Santi Ghosh and Suniti Choudhury shot the District Magistrate at Comilla. The Pahartali European Club raid was led by Pritilata Waddedar, who took cyanide.
209.tq: Separate the actions of the women revolutionaries instead of grouping all Chittagong associates together.
xs: **Santi Ghosh and Suniti Choudhury — Pahartali raid** is wrong — option **(4)**.
They shot a **District Magistrate** (Comilla).
The **Pahartali European Club** raid was led by **Pritilata Waddedar**, who took **cyanide**.
xa: **Kalpana Dutt**: arrested, **life** sentence.
**Bina Das**: fired at the **Bengal Governor** at her convocation.
All linked to Surya Sen's **Chittagong** movement (**1930**).

209.s:
Consider the following statements about Surya Sen:
1. His group in the Chittagong Armoury Raid called itself the Indian Republican Army.
2. He was hanged in 1934.
3. He was hanged in the Lahore Conspiracy Case in 1931.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
209.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Surya Sen's group (with Ganesh Ghosh, Lokenath Bal, Ananta Singh, Ambika Chakravarty) was the Indian Republican Army, and he was hanged in 1934. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1931 Lahore case executions were of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru. So A (omits 2), C and D (include 3) are wrong.
209.tq: Surya Sen: IRA, Chittagong 1930, hanged 1934.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
**1:** His group was the **Indian Republican Army**.
**2:** He was **hanged in 1934**.
**3** wrong: the **1931** Lahore executions were **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru**.
xa: Associates: **Ganesh Ghosh, Lokenath Bal, Ananta Singh, Ambika Chakravarty**.
Known as **"Masterda"**.
Raid: **18 April 1930**.

209.s: Who wrote *The Philosophy of the Bomb* as a reply to Gandhi's *The Cult of the Bomb*?
209.x: *The Philosophy of the Bomb* was written by Bhagwati Charan Vohra as a reply to Gandhi's *The Cult of the Bomb*.
209.tq: Use the author–work association while separating it from Bhagat Singh's autobiographical writing.
xs: **Bhagwati Charan Vohra** wrote **The Philosophy of the Bomb** — option **(2)**.
It replied to **Gandhi's "The Cult of the Bomb"**.
**Bhagat Singh** wrote **Why I am an Atheist (1930)**.
xa: ⚠ **The Cult of the Bomb** = Gandhi; **The Philosophy of the Bomb** = **Vohra**.
Vohra was associated with the **Naujawan Bharat Sabha (1926)**.

209.s: Bhagat Singh was born on:
209.x: Bhagat Singh was born on 28 September 1907 in the Lyallpur district, associated with Banga.
209.tq: Use the birth-date options to distinguish Bhagat Singh from other revolutionaries.
xs: **Bhagat Singh** was born on **28 September 1907** — option **(2)**.
xa: Born in **Lyallpur district** (Banga).
Hanged **23 March 1931**.
APPSC-GS **2024** keyed all four birth-date pairs correct.

209.s: Which statement correctly describes the manner of Chandrashekhar Azad's death?
o: He shot himself during a police encounter at Alfred Park.
He was shot while leading the Chittagong Armoury Raid.
He died after a 64-day hunger strike in Lahore Jail.
He was hanged at Gorakhpur Jail after the Kakori trial.
209.x: Azad shot himself during a police encounter at Alfred Park after resisting capture. He was not executed in the Kakori or Lahore cases.
209.tq: Reject the familiar execution and hunger-strike alternatives by focusing on the manner of death.
xs: **Azad shot himself** during a police encounter at **Alfred Park** — option **(1)**.
Alfred Park (now **Chandra Shekhar Azad Park**), **Prayagraj**, **27 Feb 1931**.
The **63-day** hunger strike was **Jatin Das's**; **Bismil** was hanged at **Gorakhpur**.
xa: Azad was born **23 July 1906**.
He took part in **Kakori** and escaped.
⚠ The "shot dead by an Indian constable" version is **wrong**.

209.s:
Arrange the following revolutionaries according to their years of birth, from earliest to latest:
A. Ram Prasad Bismil
B. Khudiram Bose
C. Chandrashekhar Azad
D. Bhagat Singh
209.x: Khudiram Bose was born in 1889, Ram Prasad Bismil in 1897, Chandrashekhar Azad in 1906 and Bhagat Singh in 1907.
209.tq: Fix the earliest and latest birth years first, then place the two middle years.
xs: The order is **B, A, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**Khudiram Bose 3 Dec 1889** → **Bismil 11 June 1897**.
**Azad 23 July 1906** → **Bhagat Singh 28 Sept 1907**.
xa: **Batukeshwar Dutt**: **1910**.
APPSC-GS **2024**: all four pairs correct.

209.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sukhdev taught at National College, Lahore.
2. Rajguru was earlier associated with the Seva Dal at Lahore.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
209.x: Statement 1 is correct: Sukhdev taught at National College, Lahore. Statement 2 is wrong: Rajguru was earlier in the Seva Dal at Varanasi, not Lahore. So 2 only, both and neither are wrong.
209.tq: Lahore = Sukhdev's college; Varanasi = Rajguru's Seva Dal.
xs: Only **statement 1** is correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** **Sukhdev** taught at **National College, Lahore**.
**2** wrong: **Rajguru** was in the **Seva Dal** at **Varanasi**, not Lahore.
xa: Sukhdev co-founded the **Naujawan Bharat Sabha (1926)**.
Rajguru fired first at **Saunders**.
Rajguru born at **Khed** (now **Rajgurunagar**), Maharashtra.

209.s:
Arrange the following events in the chronological order in which they influenced Bhagat Singh:
A. Chauri Chaura incident
B. Jallianwala Bagh massacre
C. Nankana Sahib incident
D. Bhagat Singh’s turn from Gandhi towards revolutionary politics
209.x: The sequence was Jallianwala Bagh in 1919, Nankana Sahib in 1921, Chauri Chaura in 1922, followed by Bhagat Singh’s turn towards revolutionary politics.
209.tq: Fix the dated events first and place the consequential change after them.
xs: The order is **B, C, A, D** — option **(1)**.
**Jallianwala Bagh 1919** → **Nankana Sahib 1921** → **Chauri Chaura 1922**.
These turned **Bhagat Singh** from **Gandhi** to **revolution**.
xa: He founded the **Naujawan Bharat Sabha (1926)**.
Credited with founding the **HSRA (1928)**.
Wrote **Why I am an Atheist (1930)**.

209.s:
Which of the following methods formed part of the mass-propaganda approach of the HSRA-era revolutionaries?
1. Use of courtroom proceedings
2. Distribution of leaflets
3. Hunger strikes
4. Exclusive reliance on secret military training
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
209.x: Courtroom proceedings, leaflets and hunger strikes were used as forms of mass propaganda. Exclusive reliance on secret military training does not represent this approach.
209.tq: Find the one extreme statement that contradicts the broader mass-propaganda strategy.
xs: **1, 2 and 3 only** — option **(2)**.
**Courtroom**, **leaflets** and **hunger strikes** were the HSRA's **mass propaganda** tools.
**Exclusive reliance on secret military training** was not part of this approach.
xa: Shift from **individual heroism** to **socialist** ideology.
Assembly bomb strategy: **courted arrest** to use the court as a platform.
**1929** Lahore jail hunger strike: **Jatin Das** died after **63** days.

209.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Andhra Pradesh angle of the revolutionary movement:
1. Salt Satyagraha prisoners from Andhra were jailed with Lahore and Meerut conspiracy convicts.
2. Some of these prisoners turned communist.
3. Krovi Lingaraju inspired youth with the examples of Alluri and Bhagat Singh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
209.x: All three statements are correct: Andhra Salt Satyagraha prisoners shared imprisonment with Lahore and Meerut conspiracy convicts, some became communists, and Krovi Lingaraju inspired youth through Alluri and Bhagat Singh.
209.tq: Verify each regional connection separately before choosing the complete combination.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**1 and 2:** Andhra **Salt Satyagraha** prisoners, jailed with **Lahore/Meerut** conspiracy convicts, **turned communist**.
**3:** **Krovi Lingaraju** inspired youth with **Alluri** and **Bhagat Singh**.
xa: **Kanuru Ramanatha Choudary** formed the **"Hindusthan Socialist Republican Army"** in **Madras** (**10 March 1933**).
Bhagat Singh was hanged **23 March 1931**.

209.s: Who formed the ‘Hindusthan Socialist Republican Army’ in Madras?
209.x: Kanuru Ramanatha Choudary formed the Hindusthan Socialist Republican Army in Madras.
209.tq: Apply the founder–organisation trap by separating Madras-based formation from other HSRA figures.
xs: **Kanuru Ramanatha Choudary** formed the **"Hindusthan Socialist Republican Army"** in **Madras** — option **(3)**.
Date: **10 March 1933**.
**Krovi Lingaraju** inspired youth; **Vohra** and **Azad** belonged to the HSRA itself.
xa: The HSRA was formed in **1928** at **Feroz Shah Kotla**.
Andhra Salt Satyagraha prisoners met **Lahore/Meerut** convicts in jail.

209.s:
Assertion (A): The HSRA represented an ideological development beyond the earlier HRA.
Reason (R): The HSRA added socialism to the HRA’s objective of establishing a republic through armed revolt.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
209.x: Both statements are true, and the addition of socialism directly explains why the HSRA represented an ideological development beyond the HRA.
209.tq: Test whether the reason explains the precise ideological difference between two organisations.
xs: **Both A and R are true** and **R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
**A:** The **HSRA** was an ideological advance on the **HRA**.
**R:** HRA (**1924**) = **republic by armed revolt**; HSRA (**1928**) **added socialism** — exactly what makes it an advance.
xa: HSRA goal: **"Federal Republic of United States of India"**.
HSRA also used **mass propaganda** (courtroom, leaflets, hunger strikes).
HRA founders: **Sanyal, Chatterjee, Bismil**.

210.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the earlier Rampa and Rekapalle rebellions?
210.x: The Rampa rebellion of 1879–80 occurred in Rampa, in the Rampachodavaram Agency of Godavari district. Rekapalle was located in Bhadrachalam taluk of Godavari district.
210.tq: Use the location comparison and eliminate the reversed place–rebellion pairs.
xs: **Rampa — Rampachodavaram agency** is correct — option **(2)**.
The **Rampa (1879-80)** revolt was in the **Rampachodavaram** agency, Godavari district.
**Bhadrachalam taluk** belongs to **Rekapalle (1879)** — so (1) and (3) swap them; neither was in Vizianagaram.
xa: Rekapalle area joined the **Madras Presidency in 1874** (APPSC **2017** key).
**1879** = "the year of the Rampa Revolution" (APPSC **2011** key).
⚠ Alluri did **not** lead the 1879-80 revolt — he was born in **1897**.

210.s:
With reference to the Rampa rebellion of 1879–80, consider the following statements:
1. Munsubdar Madhava Bhupati exploited the tribal population.
2. His policies weakened the position of the muttadars.
3. The rebellion was caused by an increase in axe tax during a famine.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
210.x: Madhava Bhupati’s exploitation of tribals and erosion of the authority of the muttadars caused the Rampa rebellion. The increase in axe tax during a famine was the cause of the Rekapalle rebellion.
210.tq: Separate the causes of the two geographically neighbouring rebellions.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1 and 2:** Munsubdar **Madhava Bhupati** (made Munsubdar **1848**) exploited tribals and **eroded the muttadars**.
**3** wrong: the **axe tax** rise in a famine caused the **Rekapalle** revolt.
xa: Rampa leaders: **Dwarabandala Chandrayya**, **Pulikanta Sambaiah**, **Karu Tammanna Dora**, **Ambul Reddy**.
**Sullivan** removed Madhava Bhupati; revolt crushed **Nov 1880**.
Chandrayya burnt **Addateegala** PS.

210.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Leader)

a. Dwarabandala Chandrayya
b. Pulikanta Sambaiah
c. Karu Tammanna Dora
d. Ambul Reddy

List-II (Rebellion association)

i. Rampa rebellion
 ii. Rekapalle rebellion
 iii. Both Rampa and Rekapalle rebellions
 iv. Neither of the two rebellions

Select the correct code.
210.x: Dwarabandala Chandrayya, Pulikanta Sambaiah and Karu Tammanna Dora led the Rampa rebellion. Ambul Reddy was associated with both the Rampa and Rekapalle rebellions.
210.tq: Start from the sure pair and identify the leader common to both rebellions.
xs: The match is **a–i, b–i, c–i, d–iii** — option **(1)**.
**Chandrayya**, **Pulikanta Sambaiah** and **Karu Tammanna Dora** = **Rampa** rebellion.
**Ambul Reddy** = **both** Rampa and **Rekapalle**.
xa: Rekapalle: Vaddagudem PS attacked on **10 July 1879**.
Rekapalle crushed **Sept 1879**; Rampa crushed **Nov 1880**.
Rampa cause: **Madhava Bhupati**; Rekapalle cause: **axe tax**.

210.s: Who among the following burnt the Addateegala Police Station during the Rampa rebellion of 1879–80?
210.x: Dwarabandala Chandrayya burnt the Addateegala Police Station during the Rampa rebellion.
210.tq: Match the specific action with the correct local leader.
xs: **Dwarabandala Chandrayya** burnt **Addateegala** PS — option **(4)**.
He was a leader of the **Rampa (1879-80)** revolt.
**Ambul Reddy** led **Rekapalle**, where **Vaddagudem** PS was attacked.
xa: Other Rampa leaders: **Pulikanta Sambaiah**, **Karu Tammanna Dora**.
Cause: Munsubdar **Madhava Bhupati**.
Addateegala was also raided in **Aug 1922** during Alluri's revolt.

210.s: The Rampa rebellion of 1879–80 was brought to an end after:
o: The axe tax was withdrawn and the rebellion ended in July 1879
Madhava Bhupati was removed by Sullivan and the rebellion was crushed in November 1880
The Madras Forest Act was repealed and the rebellion ended in November 1881
Madhava Bhupati was reinstated and the rebellion ended in September 1879
210.x: Sullivan removed Madhava Bhupati, but the rebellion was ultimately crushed in November 1880.
210.tq: Check the complete sequence of administrative action followed by suppression.
xs: **Sullivan removed Madhava Bhupati**, and the revolt was **crushed in Nov 1880** — option **(2)**.
**Sept 1879** is when **Rekapalle** was crushed; the **axe tax** was a Rekapalle grievance.
xa: Rampa revolt span: **1879-80**, Rampachodavaram agency.
Madhava Bhupati was made Munsubdar in **1848**.
The **Madras Forest Act** dates from **1882** — after the revolt.

210.s: The immediate cause of the Rekapalle rebellion was:
o: The introduction of the Madras Forest Act in the Agency areas
The dismissal of tribal leaders from government service
The increase of the axe tax on podu from 4 annas to 4–12 annas during a famine
The erosion of the authority of the muttadars by Madhava Bhupati
210.x: The Rekapalle rebellion was triggered by the increase of the axe tax on podu from 4 annas to 4–12 annas during a famine.
210.tq: Distinguish the tax-based cause of Rekapalle from the administrative cause of Rampa.
xs: Rekapalle's cause: the **axe tax on podu** raised from **4 annas to 4-12 annas** during a **famine** — option **(3)**.
**Madhava Bhupati's** erosion of the muttadars caused **Rampa**; the **Forest Act (1882)** came later.
xa: Place: **Rekapalle, Bhadrachalam taluk**, Godavari district.
Leader **Ambul Reddy**; **Vaddagudem** PS attacked **10 July 1879**.
Crushed **Sept 1879**.

210.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Rekapalle rebellion — axe tax on podu
Rampa rebellion — Vaddagudem Police Station attack
210.x: The Vaddagudem Police Station was attacked during the Rekapalle rebellion. The Addateegala Police Station was burnt during the Rampa rebellion.
210.tq: Find the action that has been transferred from one rebellion to the other.
xs: **Rampa — Vaddagudem PS** is wrong — option **(2)**.
**Vaddagudem** PS was attacked in the **Rekapalle** revolt (**10 July 1879**).
Rampa's police-station action was **Addateegala**, burnt by **Chandrayya**.
xa: Rekapalle: **axe tax**, **Ambul Reddy** — correct pairs.
Rampa: **Madhava Bhupati's** exploitation — correct pair.
Rekapalle area joined Madras Presidency in **1874**.

210.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Rampa and Rekapalle rebellions occurred in the Godavari region.
2. Ambul Reddy was associated with both rebellions.
3. Both rebellions were led by Alluri Sitarama Raju.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
210.x: Both rebellions occurred in the Godavari region, and Ambul Reddy was associated with both. Alluri Sitarama Raju led the later Rampa rebellion of 1922–24, not these earlier rebellions.
210.tq: Use the chronological distinction between the earlier rebellions and Alluri’s later revolt.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** Both occurred in **Godavari district**.
**2:** **Ambul Reddy** was in both.
**3** wrong: **Alluri** was born in **1897**; he led the later **1922-24** Rampa rebellion.
xa: ⚠ Some notes wrongly credit Alluri with the 1879-80 revolt.
**1879** = "the year of the Rampa Revolution".
Rampa leaders: **Chandrayya**, **Sambaiah**, **Tammanna Dora**.

210.s: Alluri Sitarama Raju, who led the later Rampa rebellion, was born in:
210.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju was born in 1897. Therefore, attributing the 1879–80 Rampa rebellion to him is chronologically incorrect.
210.tq: Use the birth-year check to expose an impossible attribution.
xs: **Alluri Sitarama Raju** was born in **1897** — option **(3)** (**4 July 1897**).
So he could not have led the **1879-80** revolt.
xa: Birthplace: **Pandrangi, near Vizianagaram**; ancestral village **Mogallu**.
**125th birth anniversary**: **30-ft bronze statue** at **Bhimavaram**.
Nickname **Chittibabu**; title **"Manyam Veerudu"**.

210.s:
Arrange the following rebellions in chronological order:
A. Alluri Sitarama Raju’s Rampa rebellion
B. Vasudev Balwant Phadke’s revolt
C. Khudiram Bose’s Muzaffarpur episode
D. Gulugonda tribal revolt
210.x: The Gulugonda revolt occurred in 1845–48, Phadke’s revolt in 1879, Khudiram Bose’s episode in 1908, and Alluri’s Rampa rebellion in 1922–24.
210.tq: Place events by their periods before checking the sequence of the middle items.
xs: The order is **D, B, C, A** — option **(1)**.
**C:** **Khudiram/Muzaffarpur 1908** → **A:** **Alluri's Rampa 1922-24**.
xa: Gulugonda leader: **Chinna Bhupathi** (Vizag).
**1794**: Vizianagaram — **Vijayarama Raju** killed at **Padmanabham**.
**1879** also saw the **Rampa** and **Rekapalle** revolts.

210.s: Which year is described as 'the year of the Rampa Revolution'?
210.x: 1879 is called the year of the Rampa Revolution (APPSC 2011 key) - the Rampa (1879-80) and Rekapalle (1879) revolts broke out then. 1794 was the Vizianagaram battle at Padmanabham, 1848 the end of the Gulugonda revolt, and 1922 the start of Alluri's later Rampa rebellion.
210.tq: Rampa Revolution year = 1879, not Alluri's 1922.
xs: **1879** is "the year of the Rampa Revolution" — option **(3)** (APPSC **2011** key).
**Rampa (1879-80)** and **Rekapalle (1879)** broke out then.
**1794** = Padmanabham; **1848** = end of Gulugonda; **1922** = start of Alluri's revolt.
xa: Rekapalle crushed **Sept 1879**; Rampa **Nov 1880**.
Phadke's revolt in Maharashtra was also **1879**.

210.s: The Madras Forest Act that affected the customary rights of tribal communities was enacted in:
210.x: The Madras Forest Act was enacted in 1882.
210.tq: Recall the exact year while separating the forest law from later rebellion dates.
xs: The **Madras Forest Act** was enacted in **1882** — option **(2)**.
It **reserved forests**, cutting off **podu** and **minor forest produce** rights and curbing **grazing**.
xa: It became a cause of Alluri's **Rampa rebellion (1922-24)**.
Other grievances: **begar**, the **Muttadari** system, **Tahsildar Bastian**.
Affected tribes: **Koya** and other hill tribes.

210.s: Which of the following was NOT a consequence of the Madras Forest Act, 1882, as described in relation to tribal grievances?
o: Recognition of unrestricted tribal access to minor forest produce
210.x: The Act restricted tribal access to podu cultivation and minor forest produce, and curbed grazing; it did not recognise unrestricted access.
210.tq: Choose the option that reverses the effect of a restrictive law.
xs: **Unrestricted access to minor forest produce** was not a consequence — option **(3)**.
The **1882** Act **cut off** rights to minor forest produce.
It did **reserve forests**, **restrict podu** and **curb grazing** — (1), (2), (4).
xa: **Podu** = shifting cultivation.
**Begar** = forced unpaid labour on roads.
**Tahsildar Bastian's** excesses were the spark.

210.s:
Consider the following statements about the Agency tribes and their grievances:
1. Koya and other hill tribes were affected by the reservation of forests.
2. Forest restrictions curtailed podu, or shifting cultivation.
3. The Muttadari system was associated with extortion and forced labour.
4. Begar referred to voluntary paid labour on public roads.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
210.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Begar meant forced unpaid labour, not voluntary paid labour, so statement 4 is false.
210.tq: Identify the one reversed definition in a cluster of genuine tribal grievances.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** **Koya** and other hill tribes were affected.
**2:** Forest reservation cut off **podu** (shifting cultivation).
**3:** **Muttadari** meant **extortion, forced labour**; **4** wrong: **begar** was **unpaid** forced coolie work.
xa: **Madras Forest Act, 1882**.
Spark: **Tahsildar Bastian**.
Area: agency tracts of **East Godavari and Visakhapatnam**.

210.s: Alluri Sitarama Raju was born at which of the following places?
210.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju was born on 4 July 1897 at Pandrangi, also referred to as Pandarangipeta, near Vizianagaram. Mogallu was his ancestral village.
210.tq: Distinguish the birthplace from the ancestral village and later places associated with the leader.
xs: Alluri was born at **Pandrangi (Pandarangipeta), near Vizianagaram** — option **(4)**.
**Mogallu** (West Godavari) was his **ancestral village** — some notes give it as birthplace.
**Koyyuru** = where he was shot; **Krishnadevipeta** = his tomb.
xa: Born **4 July 1897**.
Parents: **Venkataramaraju** and **Suryanarayana Amma**.
APPSC-GS **2025** asked the village; the key showed no answer.

210.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Alluri Sitarama Raju:
1. His ancestral village was Mogallu in West Godavari.
2. He was popularly known by the nickname Chittibabu.
3. Erramalli Narasimha Rao wrote his biography.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
210.x: All three statements are correct. Mogallu was his ancestral village, Chittibabu was his nickname, and Erramalli Narasimha Rao was his biographer.
210.tq: Combine closely related identity details and verify each statement independently.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**1:** Ancestral village **Mogallu, West Godavari**.
**2:** Nickname **Chittibabu**.
**3:** Biographer **Erramalli Narasimha Rao**.
xa: Title: **"Manyam Veerudu"** (APPSC **2024** key).
**1919**: hut at **Kongasingi near Krishnadevipeta**.
Born at **Pandrangi**, near Vizianagaram.

210.s:
Which of the following statements about Alluri Sitarama Raju is correct?
1. He visited Chittagong in 1921 to meet Bengali revolutionaries.
2. He respected Gandhi but believed that force was necessary.
3. He was formally affiliated to the Indian National Congress.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
210.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. He visited Chittagong in 1921, respected Gandhi and believed in the necessity of force, but he was not affiliated with the Congress.
210.tq: Use the affiliation statement as the trap while retaining the two correct ideological details.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** **July 1921** secret meeting with Bengali revolutionaries at **Chittagong**.
**2:** He **respected Gandhi** but believed **force necessary**.
**3** wrong: he was **not affiliated with Congress**.
xa: He received **guerrilla training** ideas at Chittagong.
Yet he troubled the British more than the **NCM** in that region.
Unlike Gandhian forest satyagrahas, he used **armed guerrilla war**.

210.s:
Arrange the following events associated with Alluri Sitarama Raju in chronological order:
A. Visit to Chittagong to meet Bengali revolutionaries
B. Establishment of his hut near Krishnadevipeta
C. First raid on the Chintapalli police station
D. Capture and shooting at Koyyuru
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
210.x: His hut near Krishnadevipeta dates to 1919, the Chittagong visit to 1921, the Chintapalli raid to 22 August 1922, and his death to 7 May 1924.
210.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two intermediate events by year.
xs: The order is **B, A, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**B:** hut near **Krishnadevipeta (1919)** → **A:** **Chittagong (July 1921)**.
**C:** **Chintapalli raid (22 Aug 1922)** → **D:** shot at **Koyyuru (7 May 1924)**.
xa: Last rites **8 May 1924** at **Krishnadevipeta**.
Captured by Jamadar **Kanchu Meenan**.
Shot before **Major Goodall**.

210.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gam Gantam Dora — Lieutenant of Alluri
Gam Mallu Dora — Right hand of Alluri
Gam Mallu Dora — Killed on 7 June 1924
210.x: Gam Gantam Dora was killed on 7 June 1924. Gam Mallu Dora was arrested in 1923, received a life term, was later released and won election as an MP in 1952.
210.tq: Detect the swapped fate and date among closely associated leaders.
xs: **Gam Mallu Dora — killed 7 June 1924** is wrong — option **(4)**.
**Gam Gantam Dora** was killed on **7 June 1924**.
**Mallu Dora** ("Right hand") was **arrested 1923**, got a **life term**, later won as **MP in 1952**.
xa: Mallu Dora arrested at **Nadimpalem** (**17 Sept 1923**) by **Keirns**.
**Aggiraju**: arrested **6 May 1924** at the **Maddaru** river.
⚠ **Gantam Dora** = killed **1924**; **Mallu Dora** = MP **1952**.

210.s: Alluri Sitarama Raju is popularly hailed by which title?
210.x: Alluri is 'Manyam Veerudu' (hero of the forest) (APPSC 2024 key). Andhra Shivaji was Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary and Andhra Ratna was Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya; Andhra Kesari was Tanguturi Prakasam.
210.tq: Manyam Veerudu = Alluri; nickname Chittibabu.
xs: Alluri is **"Manyam Veerudu"** (hero of the forest) — option **(2)** (APPSC **2024** key).
**"Andhra Shivaji"** = **Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary**; **"Andhra Ratna"** = **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya**.
xa: Alluri's nickname: **Chittibabu**.
Airport: **Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, Bhogapuram**.
Agency district named **Alluri Sitarama Raju district**.

210.s: The Rampa or Manyam Rebellion was principally based in which area?
o: The Gudem hills of the East Godavari Agency
