210.x: The rebellion was based in the Gudem hills, located in the Agency area of East Godavari.
210.tq: Use the location clue to separate the rebellion's operational area from other hill regions of Andhra Pradesh.
xs: The rebellion was based in the **Gudem hills** of the **East Godavari** Agency — option **(3)**.
Area: agency tracts of **East Godavari and Visakhapatnam (Gudem hills)**.
xa: Span: **January 1922 - May 1924**.
First PS attacked: **Chintapalli** (**22 Aug 1922**).
Tribes: **Koya** and other hill tribes.

210.s: Which one of the following was NOT a cause of the Rampa Rebellion?
o: Introduction of permanent settlement in the Gudem hills
Oppressive functioning of the Muttadari system
Loss of forest and podu rights under the Madras Forest Act
210.x: The rebellion was caused by restrictions on forest and podu rights, begar for road building and the oppressive Muttadari system, along with the actions of Tahsildar Bastian. Permanent settlement was not identified as a cause.
210.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the stated cluster of causes.
xs: **Permanent settlement** was **not** a cause — option **(1)**.
Causes: **Muttadari** oppression, **begar** for roads, loss of **podu/forest** rights under the **Forest Act**, and **Tahsildar Bastian**.
xa: **Madras Forest Act, 1882**.
Bastian's excesses were the **spark**.
Rebellion span: **2 years 5 months**.

210.s: The principal purpose of the first raid on the Chintapalli police station was to:
210.x: The first raid, on 22 August 1922, was undertaken to seize arms from the police station.
210.tq: Identify the immediate operational objective rather than a broader cause of the rebellion.
xs: The **Chintapalli** raid aimed to **seize arms** — option **(3)**.
It was the **first police station attacked** (**22 Aug 1922**).
xa: Then **Krishnadevipeta** and **Rajavommangi** stations were raided (**Aug 1922**).
**Annavaram** PS raided **18 Apr 1923**.
⚠ **Chintapalli** = first PS; **Panjerighat** = direct battle; **Peddagaddapalem** = first defeat.

210.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Rampa Rebellion?
o: It was confined to the coastal municipalities of Guntur district.
It troubled the British in the region more than the Non-Cooperation Movement did.
It was affiliated formally with the Indian National Congress and led through Congress committees.
It ended immediately after the imposition of the Madras Forest Act.
210.x: The rebellion troubled the British in the region more than the Non-Cooperation Movement. It was an armed tribal rebellion in the Agency area and was not formally affiliated with the Congress.
210.tq: Select the precise comparative statement while rejecting exaggerated organisational and geographical claims.
xs: It **troubled the British more than the NCM** in that region — option **(2)**.
It was **outside the Congress** and non-violence — so (3) is wrong.
It was in the **agency tracts** of East Godavari/Visakhapatnam, not Guntur municipalities.
xa: Span: **January 1922 - May 1924**.
**Assam Rifles** and **Gurkhas** reached **Narsipatnam** (**27 Jan 1924**).
Special Commissioner: **Rutherford**.

210.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: 24 September 1922 — officers Scott Coward and Heiter killed at Damanapalli ghat
6 December 1922 — Gam Mallu Dora arrested at Nadimpalem
7 May 1924 — Gam Gantam Dora killed in firing
210.x: Scott Coward and Heiter were killed at Damanapalli ghat on 24 September 1922. Mallu Dora was arrested in September 1923, Raju was shot on 7 May 1924, and Gantam Dora was killed on 7 June 1924.
210.tq: Match each event with its exact date and avoid swapping the final stages of the rebellion.
xs: **24 Sept 1922 — Scott Coward and Heiter killed** at **Damanapalli ghat** — option **(1)**.
**6 Dec 1922** = **Peddagaddapalem** defeat; Mallu Dora was arrested **17 Sept 1923**.
Raju was shot **7 May 1924**; Gantam Dora killed **7 June 1924**.
xa: Battle at **Panjerighat** (Damanghat), **Sept 1922**.
**Malabar Special Police** were behind the first defeat.
Last rites **8 May 1924**.

210.s: The first defeat suffered by Alluri Sitarama Raju’s forces at the hands of the Malabar Special Police occurred at:
210.x: At Peddagaddapalem on 6 December 1922, the Malabar Special Police inflicted Raju’s first defeat; he was wounded at Lingapuram.
210.tq: Separate the sites of the first defeat, the direct battle and the wounding.
xs: The first defeat was at **Peddagaddapalem** (**6 Dec 1922**) — option **(4)**.
Inflicted by the **Malabar Special Police**.
**Lingapuram** = where Raju was **wounded**; **Damanapalli ghat** = ambush; **Panjerighat** = direct battle.
xa: ⚠ **Chintapalli** = first PS attacked; **Panjerighat** = direct battle; **Peddagaddapalem** = first defeat.
**Rutherford** was Special Commissioner.

210.s: The Rampa rebellion extended approximately from:
210.x: The rebellion lasted from January 1922 to May 1924, approximately two years and five months, in the Agency tracts of East Godavari and Visakhapatnam.
210.tq: Use the beginning and ending months together rather than relying only on the commonly remembered year range.
xs: The rebellion ran from **January 1922 to May 1924** — option **(3)**.
About **2 years 5 months**.
xa: Area: **East Godavari and Visakhapatnam (Gudem hills)**.
First raid: **Chintapalli, 22 Aug 1922**.
End: Raju shot **7 May 1924**; **Gantam Dora** killed **7 June 1924**.

210.s: During the Rampa Rebellion of 1922-24, the direct battle between Alluri Sitarama Raju's forces and the British forces was fought at:
210.x: The direct battle with British forces was at Panjerighat (Damanghat), September 1922 (APPSC 2012 key). Chintapalli and Krishnadevipeta were police stations raided in August 1922; Koyyuru is where Raju was shot on 7 May 1924.
210.tq: Panjerighat = direct battle; Chintapalli = first raid; Koyyuru = death.
xs: The direct battle was at **Panjerighat** (Damanghat), **Sept 1922** — option **(2)** (APPSC **2012** key).
**Chintapalli** = first PS raided; **Koyyuru** = where Raju was shot; **Krishnadevipeta** = his tomb.
xa: **Damanapalli ghat** ambush: **Scott Coward and Heiter** killed (**24 Sept 1922**).
First defeat: **Peddagaddapalem**.
Also asked in APPSC G2 **2012**.

210.s:
Consider the following statements about the end of Alluri Sitarama Raju:
1. He was captured by Jamadar Kanchu Meenan.
2. He was shot on 7 May 1924 at Koyyuru before Major Goodall.
3. His last rites were performed on 8 May 1924 at Chintapalli.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
210.x: Statement 1 is correct: Jamadar Kanchu Meenan captured him. Statement 2 is correct: he was shot at Koyyuru on 7 May 1924 before Major Goodall. Statement 3 is wrong: the last rites on 8 May 1924 were at Krishnadevipeta near the Tandava river; Chintapalli was the first police station he raided. So 1 and 2 only; '1 only' misses statement 2, and options with 3 are wrong.
210.tq: Captured by Kanchu Meenan, shot at Koyyuru, last rites/tomb at Krishnadevipeta; Chintapalli = first raid.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
**1:** captured by **Jamadar Kanchu Meenan**.
**2:** shot on **7 May 1924** at **Koyyuru** before **Major Goodall**.
**3** wrong: last rites (**8 May 1924**) were at **Krishnadevipeta** near the **Tandava** river.
xa: He was shot **tied to a tree**.
Goodall is also spelt **"Gudal"**, **"Goodman"**.
⚠ Some notes say cremated, others buried; **tomb/samadhi** at Krishnadevipeta.

210.s: Which British officer was appointed Special Commissioner to crush the Rampa rebellion?
210.x: Rutherford served as Special Commissioner to crush the revolt and ordered the exile of 55 helpers; warrants were issued for 183 persons.
210.tq: Match the officer with the specific administrative post and action.
xs: **Rutherford** was **Special Commissioner** to crush the revolt — option **(4)**.
He **exiled 55 helpers** and issued **warrants for 183**.
**Goodall** = Major at Raju's shooting; **Scott Coward** = officer killed; **Keirns** = arrested Mallu Dora.
xa: ⚠ **Rutherford** appears thrice: Rampa, **Duggirala's trial** (Srikakulam), **Pedanandipadu**.
His Pedanandipadu plan to ban the **Shanti Sena** was **rejected by the Madras Government**.

210.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the end of the Rampa Rebellion:
1. Alluri Sitarama Raju was shot on 7 May 1924.
2. His last rites were performed on 8 May 1924.
3. The last rites took place near the Tandava river at Krishnadevipeta.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
210.x: All three statements are correct. He was shot on 7 May 1924, and his last rites were performed the following day at Krishnadevipeta near the Tandava river.
210.tq: Test adjacent dates and the location of the final rites as separate statements.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**2 and 3:** last rites on **8 May 1924** at **Krishnadevipeta** near the **Tandava** river.
xa: Captured by **Kanchu Meenan**; shot before **Major Goodall**.
His **tomb/samadhi** is at Krishnadevipeta.
⚠ Krishnadevipeta was also a police station raided in **Aug 1922**.

210.s: During the British campaign against the Rampa Rebellion, which officer arrested Mallu Dora?
210.x: Keirns arrested Mallu Dora. Rutherford was the Special Commissioner sent to crush the revolt, and Major Goodall was the officer before whom Alluri Sitarama Raju was shot.
210.tq: Keirns kept Mallu Dora: K for Keirns, K for kept.
xs: **Keirns** arrested **Mallu Dora** — option **(3)**.
**Rutherford** = Special Commissioner; **Goodall** = Major at Raju's shooting.
xa: Mallu Dora was arrested at **Nadimpalem** on **17 Sept 1923**.
He got a **life term**; later **MP in 1952**.
**Gam Gantam Dora** was killed on **7 June 1924**.

210.s: At which village was Kanneganti Hanumanthu killed in police firing during the Palnadu pullari movement?
210.x: Kanneganti Hanumanthu was killed in police firing at Minchalapadu during the Palnadu pullari movement.
210.tq: Distinguish the leader’s death place from the other villages connected with the same movement.
xs: **Kanneganti Hanumanthu** was killed at **Minchalapadu** — option **(2)**.
The **Palnad pullari (grass tax)** movement covered **Macherla, Veldurthi, Sirigiripadu, Minchalapadu**.
xa: Supported by **Unnava Lakshmi Narayana**.
Palnadu forest satyagraha = local version of the **NCM** call.

210.s: Who supported Kanneganti Hanumanthu during the Palnadu pullari movement?
210.x: Unnava Lakshmi Narayana supported Kanneganti Hanumanthu during the Palnadu pullari movement.
210.tq: Match the local movement leader with the person who provided political support.
xs: **Unnava Lakshmi Narayana** backed Kanneganti Hanumanthu — option **(2)**.
**Swami Ramananda Tirtha** = Hyderabad State Congress; **Mutnuri** = Krishna Patrika; **Duvvuri Subbamma** = Chirala-Perala.
xa: Unnava wrote the novel **"Malapalli"**.
He founded **Sharada Niketan, Guntur** with wife **Lakshmibayamma**.
Hanumanthu was killed at **Minchalapadu**.

210.s: The Palnadu pullari movement belongs to which period?
210.x: The Palnadu pullari or grazing-tax movement took place during 1921–22.
210.tq: Use the period to distinguish the movement from other Andhra agitations of the freedom struggle.
xs: The **Palnadu pullari** movement belongs to **1921-22** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2012** key).
It answered the **NCM** call; the **Delhi AICC (5 Nov 1921)** allowed **no-tax** campaigns.
xa: Leader **Kanneganti Hanumanthu**, killed at **Minchalapadu**.
**Pedanandipadu** no-tax: **Jan-Feb 1922**.
**1938-39**: Hyderabad State Congress satyagraha.

210.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Bezawada AICC meeting of 1921 helped put Gandhi’s programme into Andhra.
2. The Chirala–Perala municipal tax struggle was a local version of the Non-Cooperation call.
3. The Palnadu forest satyagraha was unrelated to the Non-Cooperation programme.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
210.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Palnadu forest satyagraha was also a local expression of the same Non-Cooperation call, so statement 3 is false.
210.tq: Spot the reversed relationship in the statement describing a movement as unrelated.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** The **Bezawada AICC (1921)** put Gandhi's programme into Andhra.
**2:** **Chirala-Perala** tax fight = local version of the **NCM** call.
**3** wrong: the **Palnadu forest satyagraha** was **the same NCM call**.
xa: **Delhi AICC (5 Nov 1921)**: provinces could take up **no-tax** → Guntur did.
**1921-22 Guntur** saw the NCM's most original methods in Andhra.

210.s: Who founded the Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi near Chirala?
210.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya founded the Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi near Chirala.
210.tq: Match the institution with its founder while avoiding confusion with other Andhra leaders.
xs: **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya** founded the **Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi** near **Chirala** — option **(1)**.
He resigned as professor at **Rajahmundry Government College** to promote **national education**.
**Bezawada Gopala Reddy** abolished the Chirala-Perala municipality in **1938**.
xa: Born **2 June**, **Penuganchiprolu (Krishna district)**; **1884-1929**.
Titles: **"Andhra Ratna"**, "Ramadasu".
Volunteer corps: **Ramadandu (1921)**.

210.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma — Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi
210.x: B is correct: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya led the Chirala-Perala movement (1921). A is wrong: the Ramadandu was Duggirala's volunteer corps, not Alluri's; C is wrong: Pisapati Narayana Sastri wrote Chirala Perala Vanavasam; D is wrong: Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma was the first woman jailed at Chirala-Perala, while Duggirala founded the Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi.
210.tq: Start from the sure leader–movement pair and eliminate swapped associations.
xs: **Duggirala — Chirala-Perala movement** is correct — option **(2)**.
The **Ramadandu** was **Duggirala's** corps, not Alluri's; **Pisapati Narayana Sastri** wrote **Chirala Perala Vanavasam**.
**Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma** was the **first woman jailed** at Chirala-Perala.
xa: Exodus: midnight **25 April 1921**; **13,572 of 15,326** residents left.
New camp **"Ramnagar"** outside municipal limits.
**12 women** jailed; **Duvvuri Subbamma** also arrested.

210.s: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya obtained which qualification from the University of Edinburgh in 1916?
210.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya obtained an M.A. (Hons) in Economics from the University of Edinburgh in 1916.
210.tq: Match the person with the exact qualification, subject and institution.
xs: Duggirala took an **M.A. (Hons) Economics**, **University of Edinburgh**, **1916** — option **(2)**.
He was **Secretary, Edinburgh Indian Association**.
xa: **Ananda K. Coomaraswamy** introduced him to Gandhi in London (**1915**).
Earlier: **Vandemataram** movement + **2nd Andhra Students Conference (1909)**.
After NCM: an Andhra secretary of the **Swaraj Party**.

210.s: Who introduced Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya to Gandhi in London in 1915?
210.x: Ananda K. Coomaraswamy introduced Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya to Gandhi in London in 1915 and described him as the coming man of his country.
210.tq: Apply the person-introduced-person trap to a specific political meeting.
xs: **Ananda K. Coomaraswamy** introduced him to Gandhi in **London (1915)** — option **(2)**.
He called Duggirala **"the coming man of your country"**.
xa: Duggirala: **M.A. (Hons) Economics, Edinburgh, 1916**.
Later led **Chirala-Perala (1921)**.
Joined the **Swaraj Party** (C.R. Das, Motilal Nehru).

210.s: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was also popularly known as which of the following?
210.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya, 'Andhra Ratna', was also called 'Ramadasu'. Andhra Kesari was Tanguturi Prakasam, Desoddharaka was Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao and Manyam Veerudu was Alluri Sitarama Raju.
210.tq: Separate a secondary appellation from the better-known titles of other Andhra leaders.
xs: Duggirala was also called **"Ramadasu"** — option **(3)**.
His main title: **"Andhra Ratna"**.
**"Manyam Veerudu"** = **Alluri**.
xa: His volunteer corps: **Ramadandu** (**1921**).
⚠ "**Abhinava Dandi**" = medieval poet **Ketana**, not a freedom fighter.
**Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Choudary** = "**Kavi Raju**".

210.s:
Consider the following statements about Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya:
1. He formed the volunteer corps called Ramadandu at Chirala-Perala in 1921.
2. He led the Shanti Sena in the Pedanandipadu firka.
3. He was given the title 'Andhra Ratna'.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
210.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: his volunteer corps was the Ramadandu (1921, APPSC 2019 key) and he was called 'Andhra Ratna'. Statement 2 is wrong: the Shanti Sena of Pedanandipadu was led by Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary. So A, B and D, which include statement 2, are wrong.
210.tq: Duggirala = Ramadandu; Parvataneni = Shanti Sena.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(3)**.
**1:** He formed the **Ramadandu** at **Chirala-Perala** in **1921** (APPSC **2019** key).
**2** wrong: the **Shanti Sena** at **Pedanandipadu** was led by **Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary**.
**3:** He was **"Andhra Ratna"**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **Ramadandu**, not Shanti Sena.
Veeraiah Chowdary = **"Andhra Shivaji"**.
Shanti Sena formation decided by **Guntur DCC, Dec 1921**.

210.s: The Chirala-Perala Satyagraha arose primarily because:
o: The British prohibited the Ramadandu from holding public meetings.
The villages were brought under the Forest Act and denied podu rights.
The two villages were converted into a municipality and their annual tax burden increased sharply.
The residents were forced to migrate to the Gudem hills.
210.x: Chirala and Perala were made a municipality, and the annual tax rose from Rs 4,000 to Rs 40,000, provoking the movement.
210.tq: Match the movement with its immediate administrative and fiscal trigger.
xs: Chirala and Perala were made a **municipality**, and the **tax** rose sharply — option **(3)**.
Tax rose from **Rs 4,000 to Rs 40,000** a year.
The **Forest Act/podu** grievance and **Gudem hills** belong to the Rampa rebellion.
xa: Municipality proposed **Nov 1919**, formed **Jan 1920**.
Residents: weavers and small farmers, ~**15,000**.
Municipality **abolished in 1938** by **Bezawada Gopala Reddy**.

210.s:
Consider the following statements about the Chirala-Perala movement:
1. Chirala and Perala were in Bapatla taluk.
2. The residents set up a camp called Ramnagar outside municipal limits, with a parallel all-caste assembly and an arbitration court.
3. The Ramnagar camp lasted about two years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
210.x: Statement 1 is correct: both villages were in Bapatla taluk. Statement 2 is correct: Ramnagar (Ramanagaram) outside the municipal limits had a parallel all-caste assembly and arbitration court. Statement 3 is wrong: the camp lasted about 11 months, not two years. So 1 and 2 only; every other option includes statement 3.
210.tq: Ramnagar = parallel assembly + arbitration court, lasted 11 months.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** Both villages were in **Bapatla taluk**.
**2:** **Ramnagar (Ramanagaram)** camp had a **parallel all-caste assembly** and **arbitration court**.
**3** wrong: the camp lasted **11 months**, not two years.
xa: Exodus on Gandhi's advice: **25 April 1921**.
Failure: **lack of funds**, Congress jealousy, no second line of leaders.
Gandhi wrote in **Young India** that the municipality only meant more taxes.

210.s: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was arrested on 1 October 1921 primarily because he:
o: Broke a ban on public speaking after his Berhampur speech
Organised an armed raid in the Gudem hills
Refused to pay the municipal tax
210.x: After his Berhampur speech, Duggirala was prohibited from speaking for two months. He defied the ban and was arrested on 1 October 1921.
210.tq: Link the arrest to the specific act that violated the colonial order.
xs: Duggirala **broke a ban on public speaking** after his **Berhampur** speech — option **(1)**.
After the **Andhra Mahasabha, Berhampur (Sept 1921)**, he was banned from speaking for **2** months.
Arrested **1 October 1921**.
xa: Tried by **Rutherford** at **Srikakulam**; jailed **1 year**.
⚠ Some notes place the arrest at **Trichinopoly**.
Donations: Srinivasa Ayyangar **Rs 1,000**, APCC **Rs 3,000**, Guntur DCC **Rs 250**.

210.s: Which of the following was NOT mentioned as a reason for the failure of the Chirala-Perala movement?
o: Withdrawal of support by the Ramadandu volunteers after an armed defeat
210.x: The movement weakened because of lack of funds, jealousy among other Congress leaders and the absence of second-line leaders. An armed defeat of the Ramadandu was not given as a cause.
210.tq: Identify the invented organisational explanation among the actual reasons for failure.
xs: **Withdrawal of Ramadandu volunteers after an armed defeat** was never a cause of failure — so option **(1)** is the odd one out.
The notes list three causes: **lack of funds**, **jealousy of other Congress leaders** and **no second line of leaders**.
Chirala-Perala was a **non-violent** exodus; there was no armed battle involving the **Ramadandu**.
xa: Donations were small: **Srinivasa Ayyangar Rs 1,000**, **APCC Rs 3,000**, **Guntur DCC Rs 250**.
The exodus began at midnight on **25 April 1921**; the camp **"Ramnagar"** lasted **11 months**.
The municipality was finally **abolished in 1938** by **Bezawada Gopala Reddy**.

210.s: The municipality of Chirala and Perala was abolished in 1938 during the ministry of:
o: Rajagopalachari, with Bezawada Gopala Reddy as minister concerned
Tanguturi Prakasam, with Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya as minister concerned
P. Subbarayan, with Konda Venkatappayya as minister concerned
Bobbili Raja, with Bezawada Gopala Reddy as minister concerned
210.x: The municipality was abolished in 1938 during the Rajaji ministry, when Bezawada Gopala Reddy was the Local Self-Government Minister.
210.tq: Match the administrative outcome with the correct ministry and minister instead of swapping office-holders.
xs: The Chirala-Perala municipality was abolished in **1938** under the **Rajagopalachari (Rajaji) ministry**, with **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** as minister — option **(1)**.
Gopala Reddy held the **Local Self-Government** portfolio, which covered municipalities.
**Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya** led the agitation; he was never a minister (he died in **1929**).
xa: The municipality was formed in **Jan 1920**; tax rose from **Rs 4,000 to Rs 40,000** a year.
**Gandhi** wrote in **Young India** that the municipality only meant more taxes.
After the movement failed, the **people returned** to their homes.

210.s: The book *Chirala Perala Vanavasam* was written by:
210.x: *Chirala Perala Vanavasam* was written by Pisapati Narayana Sastri.
210.tq: Use the author–work association and reject names linked with other events in the same region.
xs: ***Chirala Perala Vanavasam*** was written by **Pisapati Narayana Sastri** — option **(2)**.
**Erramalli Narasimha Rao** is the biographer of **Alluri Sitarama Raju**, not of Chirala-Perala.
**Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya** led the movement; **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** abolished the municipality in **1938**.
xa: **"Malapalli"** novel — **Unnava Lakshminarayana**; **Desabhakti Geyam** — **Gurajada Apparao**.
"**Kallumanandoy**" — **Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri**; "**Veera gandham tecchinaramu**" — **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy**.
National pledge "**Bharata Desam Naa Matrubhoomi**" — **Paidimarri Venkata Subbarao**.

210.s: Who was the first woman to be jailed in the Chirala-Perala movement?
210.x: Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma was the first woman jailed (12 women were jailed in all). Duvvuri Subbamma ('Desabandhavi') was also arrested but was not the first; Durgabai and Maganti Annapurnamma are linked to the Kakinada collection and the Tilak Swaraj Fund.
210.tq: First woman jailed at Chirala-Perala = Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma.
xs: The first woman jailed in the Chirala-Perala movement was **Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma** — option **(2)**.
**Duvvuri Subbamma** (**Desabandhavi**) was also arrested, but was not the first.
**Durgabai Deshmukh** collected **Rs 5,000** at **Kakinada**; **Maganti Annapurnamma** gave her ornaments to the **Tilak Swaraj Fund**.
xa: In all, **12 women** were jailed in the Chirala-Perala movement.
Her name is also given as **Ravuri Alivelu Mangamma**.
**Durgabai Deshmukh** founded the **Andhra Mahila Sabha** (Madras, **1937**).

210.s: The Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign of January–February 1922 was associated with which administrative unit?
210.x: The campaign was conducted in the Pedanandipadu firka of Guntur district during January–February 1922.
210.tq: Identify the precise administrative unit instead of confusing a firka with a taluka or district.
xs: The no-tax campaign of **Jan-Feb 1922** was in the **Pedanandipadu firka of Guntur district** — option **(1)**.
**Chirala-Perala** was a separate municipal-tax fight (Bapatla taluk); **Macherla** belongs to the **Palnadu** pullari movement.
xa: **18 of 19** village officers in the firka resigned (**29** in Guntur district).
The **Delhi AICC (5 Nov 1921)** let provincial committees take up **no-tax** — Guntur did.
Suspended on **11 Feb 1922** on **Gandhi's message** to **Konda Venkatappayya**.

210.s: The tax refused by the peasants of Pedanandipadu firka was the:
210.x: The campaign involved refusal to pay the January instalment of land revenue.
210.tq: Test the exact revenue item and instalment rather than the broad idea of tax resistance.
xs: The peasants refused the **January instalment of land revenue** — option **(2)**.
It was a **no-tax** campaign in **Pedanandipadu firka**, **Jan-Feb 1922**.
**Grazing (pullari / grass) tax** was the issue of the **Palnadu** movement; **municipal tax** was the issue at **Chirala-Perala**.
xa: Unique feature (1): **mass resignation of village officers**, led by Chandavolu karanam **Machiraju Ramamurthy**.
Unique feature (2): the **Shanti Sena**, decided by the Guntur DCC in **Dec 1921**.
Inquiry committee: **T. Prakasam**, **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**, **Dantu Narayana Raju** — praised it but advised waiting for **Bardoli**.

210.s: Who led the Shanti Sena in the Pedanandipadu firka?
210.x: Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary led the Shanti Sena in the firka and was also associated with the no-tax campaign.
210.tq: Distinguish the local organiser of the Shanti Sena from the leader of the village-officer resignations.
xs: **Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary** led the **Shanti Sena** in Pedanandipadu firka — option **(3)**.
**Machiraju Ramamurthy** led the **village officers' resignations**; **Konda Venkatappayya** backed the campaign and received Gandhi's suspension message.
**Dantu Narayana Raju** sat on the **inquiry committee**.
xa: Veeraiah Chowdary was called "**Andhra Shivaji**" (**APPSC 2019** key).
Formation of the Shanti Sena was decided by the **Guntur DCC** in **Dec 1921**.
⚠ **Rutherford's** plan to ban the Shanti Sena was **rejected by the Madras Government**.

210.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
210.x: Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary was known as Andhra Shivaji. Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was associated with the title Andhra Ratna, while Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Choudary was called Kavi Raju.
210.tq: Match each personality with the exact title, watching for swapped titles.
xs: **Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary — Andhra Shivaji** is correct — option **(2)**.
**Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya** was "**Andhra Ratna**", not Andhra Shivaji.
**Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Choudary** was "**Kavi Raju**"; **Machiraju Ramamurthy** was the karanam of **Chandavolu**.
xa: ⚠ "**Abhinava Dandi**" is the medieval poet **Ketana**, not a freedom fighter.
**Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao** wrote the autobiography ***Na Jeevitha Katha***.
Duggirala was also called "**Ramadasu**".

210.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
210.x: Ketana was associated with the title Abhinava Dandi, not Andhra Ratna. Andhra Ratna was the title of Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya.
210.tq: Find the swapped title by checking each personality–title pair.
xs: **Ketana — Andhra Ratna** is wrongly matched — option **(3)**.
**Ketana**, the medieval poet, was "**Abhinava Dandi**"; "**Andhra Ratna**" was **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya**.
The rest are correct: Tripuraneni — **Kavi Raju**; Veeraiah Chowdary — **Andhra Shivaji**; Duggirala — **Ramadandu** (**1921**).
xa: ⚠ Duggirala's corps was **Ramadandu**, not **Shanti Sena** (Pedanandipadu).
Duggirala studied **M.A. (Hons) Economics** at **Edinburgh** (**1916**).
After the NCM he joined the **Swaraj Party** as one of its Andhra secretaries.

210.s: Which British official attributed the village-officer resignations primarily to low pay and heavy workload?
210.x: Collector A. Gellatly attributed the resignations to low pay and workload. Revenue Board member L. T. Harris instead blamed the Congress.
210.tq: Distinguish officials by their posts and by the explanations they offered.
xs: Collector **A. Gellatly** blamed **low pay and workload** for the resignations — option **(4)**.
Revenue Board member **L.T. Harris** instead **blamed Congress** and was sent to Guntur.
**Rutherford** was deployed to Pedanandipadu; **Bastian** was the Tahsildar whose excesses sparked the **Rampa** revolt.
xa: ⚠ **Rutherford** appears thrice: Rampa **Special Commissioner**, Duggirala's trial at **Srikakulam**, Pedanandipadu.
**18 of 19** village officers in the firka resigned, **29** in Guntur district.

210.s:
With reference to the government response to the Pedanandipadu campaign, consider the following statements:
1. L. T. Harris was sent to Guntur after attributing the resignations to Congress influence.
2. Rutherford was deployed to deal with the situation.
3. Rutherford’s proposal to ban the Shanti Sena was accepted by the Madras Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
210.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Rutherford’s proposal to ban the Shanti Sena was rejected by the Madras Government, making statement 3 false.
210.tq: Use the authority-action trap: a proposed government measure was rejected, not accepted.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: **L.T. Harris** blamed **Congress** and was sent to **Guntur**.
Statement 2 correct: **Rutherford** was deployed.
Statement 3 wrong: Rutherford's plan to ban the **Shanti Sena** was **rejected by the Madras Government**.
xa: Collector **A. Gellatly** blamed **low pay and workload** for the resignations.
As **Special Commissioner** in Rampa, Rutherford **exiled 55 helpers** and issued warrants for **183**.
Rutherford also tried **Duggirala** at **Srikakulam**.

210.s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents the Congress positions during the Pedanandipadu campaign?
o: Nyapathi Subbarao supported it; T. Prakasam urged its withdrawal
Rutherford and L. T. Harris supported it; Nyapathi Subbarao opposed it
Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri opposed it; Konda Venkatappayya urged restraint
Konda Venkatappayya and Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri supported it; Nyapathi Subbarao urged restraint
210.x: Konda Venkatappayya and Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri backed the campaign, whereas Nyapathi Subbarao urged restraint.
210.tq: Compare the positions of closely associated leaders rather than their official roles.
xs: **Konda Venkatappayya and Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri supported** it; **Nyapathi Subbarao urged restraint** — option **(4)**.
**Rutherford** and **L.T. Harris** were British officials, not Congress leaders.
**T. Prakasam** sat on the inquiry committee that **praised** the campaign but advised waiting for **Bardoli**.
xa: Inquiry committee: **T. Prakasam**, **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**, **Dantu Narayana Raju**.
**Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri** also wrote the song "**Kallumanandoy**".
Withdrawn on **11 Feb 1922** after **Gandhi's message** to Konda Venkatappayya.

210.s: The Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign was suspended after the Guntur District Congress Committee received Gandhi’s message to Konda Venkatappayya on:
210.x: Gandhi’s message to suspend the campaign reached the Guntur District Congress Committee on 11 February 1922, after which the campaign ended with the Non-Cooperation Movement.
210.tq: Match the precise date with the final administrative action in the campaign.
xs: Gandhi's suspension message reached the Guntur DCC on **11 February 1922** — option **(2)**.
**5 Nov 1921** was the **Delhi AICC**, which allowed **no-tax** civil disobedience.
**6 Dec 1922** was Alluri's defeat at **Peddagaddapalem**; **7 May 1924** was **Alluri's** death.
xa: The campaign then **ended with the NCM**.
The **Bezawada AICC (1921)** put Gandhi's programme into Andhra.
Gandhi's message was sent to **Konda Venkatappayya**.

210.s:
Which of the following were unique features of the Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign (1922)?
1. Mass resignation of village officers - 18 of 19 in the firka
2. Formation of the Shanti Sena
3. Mass exodus of residents to a new camp outside municipal limits
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
210.x: Features 1 and 2 are correct: 18 of 19 village officers resigned (led by Chandavolu karanam Machiraju Ramamurthy), and the Shanti Sena was formed. Feature 3 belongs to Chirala-Perala (exodus to Ramnagar, 1921). So B, C and D, which include 3, are wrong.
210.tq: Pedanandipadu = resignations + Shanti Sena; Chirala-Perala = exodus.
xs: Features **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)**.
Feature 1 correct: **mass resignation** of village officers, **18 of 19** in the firka.
Feature 2 correct: formation of the **Shanti Sena**.
Feature 3 wrong: the **mass exodus** to a camp (**Ramnagar**) belongs to **Chirala-Perala** (**1921**).

Shanti Sena in the firka was led by **Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary**.
Guntur district saw **29** resignations in all.

210.s: In April 1921 at Kakinada, Durgabai Deshmukh collected what amount for the Congress and translated Gandhi’s speech?
210.x: In April 1921 at Kakinada, Durgabai Deshmukh collected Rs. 5,000 for the Congress and translated Gandhi’s speech.
210.tq: Test the exact amount and place associated with a contribution by a prominent woman activist.
xs: **Durgabai** collected **Rs 5,000** for the Congress at **Kakinada** in **April 1921** — option **(3)**.
She also **translated Gandhi's speech** there.
xa: Durgabai Deshmukh later founded the **Andhra Mahila Sabha** (Madras, **1937**).
**Maganti Annapurnamma** — first Telugu woman to donate all her ornaments to the **Tilak Swaraj Fund**.
**Yamini Purna Tilakam** took part in the **Guntur hartals**.

210.s: The ‘Desasevikalu’ organisation was associated with which of the following objectives?
o: Promotion of forest administration under the colonial government
Non-violent reform and propaganda for Swaraj
Armed revolutionary training and military recruitment

It was a **women's organisation within Congress**, not a forest, tax or armed body.

**12 women** were jailed at Chirala-Perala; the first was **Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma**.
**Duvvuri Subbamma** (**Desabandhavi**) was also arrested.

210.s: Who organised hartals at Guntur after Gandhi’s 1921 coastal tour?
210.x: Yamini Purna Tilakam was associated with organising hartals at Guntur after Gandhi’s coastal tour.
210.tq: Match the local action with the individual specifically connected to it.
xs: **Yamini Purna Tilakam** is linked with the **hartals in Guntur** — option **(2)**.
**Durgabai Deshmukh** collected **Rs 5,000** at **Kakinada**; **Maganti Annapurnamma** donated her ornaments to the **Tilak Swaraj Fund**.
xa: Annapurnamma also **burnt foreign goods**.
**Desasevikalu**: women's organisation within Congress for **non-violent reform** and **Swaraj** propaganda.
**Andhra Mahila Sabha** — **Durgabai Deshmukh**, **1937**.

210.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Maganti Annapurnamma — first Telugu woman to donate all her ornaments to the Tilak Swaraj Fund
Durgabai Deshmukh — founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha (1937)
Yamini Purna Tilakam — hartals in Guntur
Duvvuri Subbamma — first woman jailed in the Chirala-Perala movement
210.x: The first woman jailed at Chirala-Perala was Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma; Duvvuri Subbamma ('Desabandhavi') was also arrested but was not the first. The other three pairs are correct.
210.tq: Tilak Swaraj Fund ornaments = Maganti Annapurnamma; Andhra Mahila Sabha = Durgabai.
xs: **Duvvuri Subbamma — first woman jailed** is wrong — option **(4)**.
The first woman jailed at Chirala-Perala was **Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma**; Duvvuri Subbamma (**Desabandhavi**) was arrested later.
The other pairs are correct: **Maganti Annapurnamma** (Tilak Swaraj Fund), **Durgabai** (Andhra Mahila Sabha, **1937**), **Yamini Purna Tilakam** (Guntur hartals).

Durgabai collected **Rs 5,000** at **Kakinada** in **April 1921**.

210.s: Who was the first editor of Andhra Patrika during 1916–18?
210.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao served as the first editor of Andhra Patrika during 1916–18; Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao was its founder.
210.tq: Distinguish the founder from the first editor of the same newspaper.
xs: The first editor of **Andhra Patrika** (**1916-18**) was **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** — option **(3)**.
**Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** was its **founder**, not first editor.
**Mutnuri Krishna Rao** edited **Krishna Patrika**; **Tanguturi Prakasam** ran **Swarajya**.
xa: **Swarajya** daily began on **29 Oct 1921**.
**Desamata** — **Chilakamarti Lakshminarasimham**.
**Zamin Rythu** — **Nellore Venkataramana Naidu**.

210.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
210.x: Zamin Rythu was associated with Nellore Venkataramana Naidu. Krovi Lingaraju was associated with the Congress weekly and its 1931 sedition case.
210.tq: Find the swapped newspaper-person pair among editors and founders of Andhra papers.
xs: **Zamin Rythu — Krovi Lingaraju** is wrongly matched — option **(4)**.
**Zamin Rythu** was run by **Nellore Venkataramana Naidu**; **Krovi Lingaraju** is linked with the **Congress** weekly (**1931** sedition case).
The rest are correct: **Desamata** — Chilakamarti; **Krishna Patrika** — Mutnuri Krishna Rao; **Swarajya** — Prakasam.
xa: ⚠ **Chilakamarti** = Desamata + "**Bharata Khandambu**"; **Prakasam** = Swarajya.
**Andhra Patrika**: founder **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**; first editor **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao**.
**Krishna Patrika** was published from **Machilipatnam**.

210.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the newspaper ‘Congress’ is correct?
1. It was a weekly.
2. Madhuri Annapurnayya was associated with it.
3. Krovi Lingaraju was involved in a sedition case in 1931.
210.x: The Congress was a weekly associated with Madhuri Annapurnayya, and Krovi Lingaraju faced a sedition case in 1931 in connection with it.
210.tq: Check publication frequency, associated person and year-linked legal action together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
**Congress** was a **weekly** paper of **Madhuri Annapurnayya**.
**Krovi Lingaraju** was involved in its **1931 sedition case**.
xa: **Swarajya** (daily, **29 Oct 1921**) — **Tanguturi Prakasam**.
**Zamin Rythu** — **Nellore Venkataramana Naidu**.
**Krishna Patrika** (Machilipatnam) — editor **Mutnuri Krishna Rao**.

210.s: Who founded Sharada Niketan at Guntur along with his wife Lakshmibayamma?
210.x: Unnava Lakshminarayana founded Sharada Niketan at Guntur with his wife Lakshmibayamma for girls’ education.
210.tq: Use the founder-spouse association to identify the institution’s principal founder.
xs: **Sharada Niketan, Guntur** was founded by **Unnava Lakshminarayana** with wife **Lakshmibayamma** — option **(1)**.

210.s: Which work was written by Unnava Lakshminarayana?
210.x: Unnava Lakshminarayana wrote the novel Malapalli.
210.tq: Distinguish literary authors by matching each work with its correct creator.
xs: **Unnava Lakshminarayana** wrote the novel **"Malapalli"** — option **(4)**.
"**Bharata Desam Naa Matrubhoomi**" is by **Paidimarri Venkata Subbarao**; **Desabhakti Geyam** is by **Gurajada Apparao**.
xa: Unnava founded **Sharada Niketan, Guntur** with wife **Lakshmibayamma**.
"**Bharata Khandambu Chakkani Padi Aavu**" — **Chilakamarti Lakshminarasimham**.
***Chirala Perala Vanavasam*** — **Pisapati Narayana Sastri**.

210.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

a. Bharata Khandambu Chakkani Padi Aavu
b. Veera gandham tecchinaramu

 d. Desabhakti Geyam

Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Choudary was called "**Kavi Raju**".
National pledge — **Paidimarri Venkata Subbarao**; novel **"Malapalli"** — **Unnava Lakshminarayana**.

210.s: The national pledge ‘Bharata Desam Naa Matrubhoomi’ was written by whom?
210.x: The national pledge ‘Bharata Desam Naa Matrubhoomi’ was written by Paidimarri Venkata Subbarao.
210.tq: Test a direct author-work association using authors of other patriotic works as distractors.
xs: The national pledge "**Bharata Desam Naa Matrubhoomi**" was written by **Paidimarri Venkata Subbarao** — option **(3)**.
**Chilakamarti** wrote "**Bharata Khandambu**"; **Gurajada** wrote **Desabhakti Geyam**; **Tripuraneni** wrote "**Veera gandham tecchinaramu**".

***Chirala Perala Vanavasam*** — **Pisapati Narayana Sastri**.

210.s:
Consider the following statements about the Hyderabad State Congress:

2. Its first president was Swami Ramananda Tirtha.
3. The Nizam lifted the ban on it in 1946.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

210.tq: Combine formation, leadership and ban-lifting dates in one chronological institutional question.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
The **Hyderabad State Congress** was **formed in 1938**; first president **Swami Ramananda Tirtha**.
**Banned by the Nizam in 1938**, the ban was **lifted in 1946**.

210.s: The satyagraha of the Hyderabad State Congress in 1938 coincided with which movement?
o: The Osmania University Vande Mataram agitation

**Palnadu pullari** (**1921-22**) and **Chirala-Perala** (**1921**) belong to the NCM years, not 1938.

210.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra freedom movement:
1. The period 1921-31 is called the 'Glorious Decade' of Andhra.
2. Chirala-Perala, Palnadu and Pedanandipadu are examples of tribal armed resistance.
3. In 1921-22, Guntur saw mass exodus, resignation of officials and a no-tax campaign.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
210.x: Statement 1 is correct: 1921-31 is the 'Glorious Decade'. Statement 2 is wrong: Chirala-Perala, Palnadu and Pedanandipadu showed mass non-cooperation; it was Rampa that showed tribal armed resistance. Statement 3 is correct: these were the NCM's most original methods in Guntur. So 1 and 3 only; options with 2 are wrong.
210.tq: Mass non-cooperation = Chirala-Perala, Palnadu, Pedanandipadu; armed tribal resistance = Rampa.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **1921-31** is the "**Glorious Decade**" of Andhra.
Statement 2 wrong: Chirala-Perala, Palnadu, Pedanandipadu showed **mass non-cooperation**; **Rampa** showed **tribal armed resistance**.
Statement 3 correct: Guntur in **1921-22** saw **mass exodus**, **officials resigning**, **no-tax** campaign.
xa: Local Congress **rivalry** and **money shortage** sank Chirala-Perala.
**Gandhi's halt** ended Pedanandipadu at its peak.
Unlike Gandhian forest satyagrahas, **Alluri** used **armed guerrilla war**, yet respected Gandhi.

210.s: Which of the following current developments is associated with the legacy of Alluri Sitarama Raju?
o: The Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhadrachalam in Telangana
The Alluri Sitarama Raju University at Rajahmundry
The Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram in Vizianagaram
The Alluri Sitarama Raju Port at Kakinada
210.x: The Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport is located at Bhogapuram in Vizianagaram district and is named after him.
210.tq: Use the exact place-name association to avoid nearby-location traps.
xs: The **Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport** is at **Bhogapuram (Vizianagaram)** — option **(3)**.
The CM invited the PM to inaugurate it on **1 August 2026**.
xa: A **30-ft bronze statue** of Alluri was unveiled by the PM at **Bhimavaram** for his **125th birth anniversary**.
The Agency district is named **Alluri Sitarama Raju district**.
Alluri was born on **4 July 1897** at **Pandrangi, near Vizianagaram**.

210.s: A Guinness record associated with the Bhogapuram airport area involved:
o: The largest Kuchipudi performance by 13,000 school students
The largest tribal orchestra involving 13,000 musicians
The longest tribal marathon conducted by 13,000 athletes
The largest Dhimsa dance by more than 13,000 tribal women and girls
210.x: A Guinness record was set for the largest Dhimsa dance, involving more than 13,000 tribal women and girls.
210.tq: Match the record with the correct cultural form and participants.
xs: The Guinness record was for the **largest Dhimsa dance** by **13,000+ tribal women and girls** — option **(4)**.
It was held at **Bhogapuram** ahead of the PM's visit (**July 2026**).
xa: The airport is named after **Alluri Sitarama Raju**; inauguration invited for **1 August 2026**.
Alluri's title: "**Manyam Veerudu**" (hero of the forest).

210.s: The Agency district in Andhra Pradesh was renamed as:
210.x: The Agency district was named Alluri Sitarama Raju district in recognition of the revolutionary leader’s legacy.
210.tq: Test the official name rather than an honorific or regional description.
xs: The Agency district is named **Alluri Sitarama Raju district** — option **(4)**.
"**Manyam Veerudu**" is Alluri's **title** (APPSC **2024** key), not a district name.
xa: Alluri led the **Rampa / Manyam Rebellion**, **January 1922 - May 1924**.
His **30-ft bronze statue** stands at **Bhimavaram** (**125th birth anniversary**).
The **Bhogapuram** airport (Vizianagaram) is also named after him.

211.s: “Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi aavu” was improvised on which occasion?
o: During the Salt Satyagraha at Dandi in 1930
During Bipin Chandra Pal’s speeches at Rajahmundry in April 1907
During the Home Rule agitation in Madras in 1916
During Gandhi’s visit to Vijayawada in 1921
211.x: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham improvised the song during Bipin Chandra Pal’s speeches at Rajahmundry in April 1907.
211.tq: Lock the answer through the distinctive place, speaker and month-year combination.
xs: **"Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi aavu"** was improvised during **Bipin Chandra Pal's speeches at Rajahmundry, April 1907** — option **(2)**.
**Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham** was translating Pal's speeches when he composed it.
The song cast **India as a cow** whose milk the British were taking.
xa: His later verse: "**Bharata khandambe okka pedda bandikhana**".
Chilakamarti is called the **first Telugu national poet**; he edited **Desamata**.
The song was an APPSC **G2 2019** key question.

211.s: The later patriotic verse “Bharata khandambe okka pedda bandikhana” expressed India as which of the following?
o: A large prison under colonial rule
A prosperous kingdom protected by the British
A sacred land beyond foreign influence
211.x: The verse literally presents the Indian subcontinent as one large prison, conveying the reality of British colonial rule.
211.tq: Test the exact meaning of a quoted line rather than its author.
xs: "**Bharata khandambe okka pedda bandikhana**" shows India as **one large prison** under colonial rule — option **(1)**.
It was **Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham's** later verse, after "Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi aavu".
xa: The earlier song (**Rajahmundry, April 1907**) cast India as a **cow** milked by the British.
First Telugu national song: "**Hinduvulara ennaallee gati**".
Chilakamarti edited **Desamata**.

211.s: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham is recognised as the first Telugu national poet. Which work is associated with the distinction of being the first Telugu national song?
211.x: “Hinduvulara ennaallee gati” is recognised as the first Telugu national song, while Chilakamarti is recognised as the first Telugu national poet.
211.tq: Distinguish the poet’s title from the separately identified first national song.
xs: The **first Telugu national song** is "**Hinduvulara ennaallee gati**" — option **(3)**.
**Roshanara** (Kopparapu Subbarao) was the **first play banned** by the British; **Ekanta Seva** is the "Telugu Gitanjali".
"**Bharata khandambe okka pedda bandikhana**" is Chilakamarti's later verse.
xa: **First Telugu national poet**: **Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham**.
Often called the first nationalist song: "**The Cry of Mother India**" (**Krishna Patrika**, **15 Dec 1905**).
⚠ Per **C. Narayana Reddy**, the first is "**Melukonumi Bharata Putruda**" (**Andhra Bharati**, Oct **1909**).

211.s: Which periodical was edited by Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham?
211.x: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham edited Desamata.
211.tq: Apply the editor–periodical association and avoid confusing it with another Telugu publication.
xs: **Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham** edited **Desamata** — option **(3)**.
He is the **first Telugu national poet**.
xa: He improvised "**Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi aavu**" at **Rajahmundry** (**April 1907**).
He translated **Bipin Chandra Pal's** Rajahmundry speeches.
⚠ "**Congress**" was the paper that serialised **Chicharapidugu** (**1927-29**).

211.s: Which song, published in Krishna Patrika on 15 December 1905, is often called the first nationalist song in Telugu?
211.x: The Cry of Mother India (Krishna Patrika, 15 Dec 1905) is often called the first nationalist song. C. Narayana Reddy instead gave that place to Melukonumi Bharata Putruda (Andhra Bharati, Oct 1909). Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi aavu was Chilakamarti's verse at Bipin Chandra Pal's Rajahmundry speeches (1907), and Desamunu preminchumanna is Gurajada's song in Mutyala Saralu.
211.tq: 1905 Krishna Patrika = Cry of Mother India; 1909 Andhra Bharati = Melukonumi (C. Narayana Reddy's choice).
xs: "**The Cry of Mother India**" (**Krishna Patrika**, **15 Dec 1905**) is often called the first nationalist song — option **(1)**.
**C. Narayana Reddy** instead names "**Melukonumi Bharata Putruda**" (**Andhra Bharati**, Oct **1909**).
"**Bharata khandambu**" was Chilakamarti's **1907** song; "**Desamunu preminchumanna**" is **Gurajada's**.
xa: **First Telugu national song**: "**Hinduvulara ennaallee gati**".
**First Telugu national poet**: **Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham**.

211.s: Who wrote Japaneeyamu, which celebrated Japan’s victory over Russia in 1905?
211.x: Japaneeyamu was written by Sriram Veerabrahmam of Bandar and celebrated Japan’s victory over Russia in 1905.
211.tq: Match the world event and patriotic work with the correct author.
xs: **Japaneeyamu** was written by **Sriram Veerabrahmam** (Bandar) — option **(4)**.
It celebrated **Japan's victory over Russia (1905)**.
**Adipudi Somanatha Rao** wrote **Japan Charitra**; **Damaraju Pundarikakshudu** wrote **Panchala Parabhavam**; **Umar Alisha** wrote **Mahabharata Kaurava Rangam**.
xa: Japan Charitra was dedicated to the **Raja of Munagala**, who named his sons **Togo and Nogi**.
Japaneeyamu — Sriram Veerabrahmam was asked in the **G2 2025** match.

211.s:
Consider the following statements about Panchala Parabhavam:
1. It was written by Damaraju Pundarikakshudu.
2. It dealt with the Jallianwala Bagh tragedy.
3. Dyer was portrayed as Duryodhana.
4. Twenty-five students in Vizag were arrested for staging it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
211.x: All four statements are correct. The play concerned Jallianwala Bagh, cast Dyer as Duryodhana, was discussed in the British Parliament, and led to the arrest of 25 Vizag students who staged it.
211.tq: Treat the play, event, characterisation and consequence as separate factual components.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Panchala Parabhavam** was by **Damaraju Pundarikakshudu**, on **Jallianwala Bagh**.
It cast **Dyer as Duryodhana**; **25 students in Vizag** were arrested for staging it.
xa: The play was **discussed in the British Parliament**.
**Padmavyuham** — **Kallakuri Narayana Rao** (**1919**).
**Mahabharata Kaurava Rangam** — **Umar Alisha** (**1916**).

211.s: Which pair is correctly matched with the year of the patriotic play?
211.x: Padmavyuham was written by Kallakuri Narayana Rao in 1919. Mahabharata Kaurava Rangam was written by Umar Alisha in 1916.
211.tq: Check the author–title–year triad and reject swapped playwrights.
xs: **Padmavyuham — Kallakuri Narayana Rao — 1919** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Mahabharata Kaurava Rangam** was by **Umar Alisha** (**1916**), not Damaraju.
**Panchala Parabhavam** was by **Damaraju Pundarikakshudu**; **Japaneeyamu** by **Sriram Veerabrahmam**.
xa: Panchala Parabhavam cast **Dyer as Duryodhana**.
Japaneeyamu marked **Japan's victory over Russia (1905)**.

211.s: The lines “Desamunu preminchumanna, manchi annadi penchumanna” are associated with which poet and collection?
211.x: The lines were written by Gurajada Apparao and form part of Mutyala Saralu. The poem was published in Andhra Bharati.
211.tq: Use the poet–work pair directly; nearby nationalist poets are used as distractors.
xs: "**Desamunu preminchumanna**" is by **Gurajada Apparao**, in ***Mutyala Saralu*** — option **(4)**.
**Harijana Paatalu** is Garimella's; **Andhravali** is Rayaprolu's; **Matru Desa Sankeertanam** is Duvvuri Ramireddy's.
xa: The poem was published in **Andhra Bharati** and called the "**national anthem of Telugu people**".
Same poem: "**Desamante matti kadoi, desamante manushuloi**".
⚠ **Garimella** = "Maakoddee"; **Tripuraneni** = "Veera gandham".

211.s: Which one of the following statements correctly explains the idea expressed in the line “Desamante matti kadoi, desamante manushuloi”?
o: The nation is identified with its ruling dynasty.
The nation is represented only by its religious institutions.
The nation is defined by its geographical boundaries alone.
The nation consists primarily of its people rather than merely its soil.
211.x: Gurajada’s line means that a nation is its people, not merely its soil. It is part of the same poem in Mutyala Saralu.
211.tq: Translate the famous line into its precise underlying concept.
xs: The line means the **nation is its people, not merely its soil** — option **(4)**.
It is from **Gurajada Apparao's** "Desamunu preminchumanna" (***Mutyala Saralu***).
xa: The poem was called the "**national anthem of Telugu people**".
Gurajada made **vyavaharika bhasha** (spoken Telugu) normal.
Gurajada also wrote ***Kanyasulkam*** (staged **1893**).

211.s: The poem containing “Desamunu preminchumanna” was called the national anthem of the Telugu people. In which periodical was it published?
211.x: Gurajada Apparao’s poem was published in Andhra Bharati and came to be regarded as the national anthem of the Telugu people.
211.tq: Separate the collection, periodical and title-related details of the same poem.
xs: Gurajada's poem was published in **Andhra Bharati** — option **(2)**.
It belongs to his collection ***Mutyala Saralu***.
**Krishna Patrika** carried "**The Cry of Mother India**" (**15 Dec 1905**).
xa: Its line "**Desamante matti kadoi, desamante manushuloi**" — the nation is its people.
⚠ **Andhra Bharati** also published "**Melukonumi Bharata Putruda**" (Oct **1909**).

211.s: Who wrote the patriotic lyric “Ye desamegina ... pogadara nee talli bhoomi Bharatini”, commonly known by its title Janmabhoomi?
211.x: The patriotic lyric Janmabhoomi was written by Rayaprolu Subbarao.
211.tq: Identify the author from a distinctive line and title.
xs: The lyric ***Janmabhoomi*** ("Ye desamegina ... pogadara nee talli bhoomi Bharatini") is by **Rayaprolu Subbarao** — option **(3)**.
**Sankarambadi Sundarachari** wrote "**Ma Telugu Talliki**"; **Basavaraju Apparao** wrote "**Kollayi gattithenemi**".
xa: Rayaprolu was born in **1892**, **Guntur**.
He is the **Father of Telugu Romanticism** and founder of **Bhavakavitvam**.
His works: ***Andhravali***, ***Swatantrya Rathamu***.

211.s:
Consider the following statements about Rayaprolu Subba Rao:
1. He is called the Father of Telugu Romanticism.
2. He pioneered Bhava Kavitvam, drawing on Shelley and Keats.
3. His new concept 'Amalina Srungaram' meant heroic sentiment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
211.x: Statement 1 is correct: he is the Father of Telugu Romanticism. Statement 2 is correct: he pioneered Bhava Kavitvam drawing on Shelley and Keats. Statement 3 is wrong: Amalina Srungaram means platonic love. So 1 and 2 only; '1 only' misses 2, and options with 3 are wrong.
211.tq: Amalina Srungaram = platonic love.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: Rayaprolu is the **Father of Telugu Romanticism**.
Statement 2 correct: he pioneered **Bhava Kavitvam**, drawing on **Shelley and Keats**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Amalina Srungaram** means **platonic love**, not heroic sentiment.
xa: Rayaprolu's title: **Abhinava Nannaya** (APPSC **G2 2025** key).
He freed Telugu verse from **rigid prosody**.

211.s: Which of the following best describes Rayaprolu Subba Rao’s contribution to Telugu poetry?
o: He restored rigid prosody as the sole basis of Telugu poetry.
He replaced original verse with exclusively devotional compositions.
He moved away from translation of Sanskrit epics and introduced original, emotive verse.
He continued translating Sanskrit epics without alteration.
211.x: Rayaprolu broke with the translation of Sanskrit epics and brought original, emotive verse into Telugu. He also helped free Telugu poetry from rigid prosody.
211.tq: Choose the option that captures the complete literary change rather than an isolated label.
xs: Rayaprolu **moved away from translating Sanskrit epics** to **original, emotive verse** — option **(3)**.
He **freed** Telugu verse from **rigid prosody**, the opposite of option (1).
xa: New concept: **Amalina Srungaram** (**platonic love**).
⚠ Progressive writers like **Sri Sri** called his romanticism "**escapist**".
Main Bhava poets: **Basavaraju Apparao**, **Duvvuri Ramireddy**, **Devulapalli Krishna Sastri**.

211.s: Who described Rayaprolu’s romanticism as “escapist”?
o: Progressive writers such as Sri Sri
211.x: Progressive writers such as Sri Sri criticised Rayaprolu’s romanticism as escapist, even though he had an important role in freeing Telugu verse from rigid prosody.
211.tq: Separate later critical assessment from the poet’s own literary contribution.
xs: **Progressive writers such as Sri Sri** called Rayaprolu's romanticism "**escapist**" — option **(4)**.
**Duvvuri Ramireddy** was himself a **Bhava Kavitvam** poet, not a critic of it.
xa: Debate: **Bhava Kavitvam vs Abhyudaya** — escapist romanticism or necessary liberation of form?
Sri Sri is "**Maha Kavi**"; his work: **Mahaprasthanam**.

211.s: Who is regarded as the founder of Bhavakavitvam?
211.x: Rayaprolu Subbarao is regarded as the founder of Bhavakavitvam.
211.tq: Use direct founder recall with closely related poets as distractors.
xs: **Rayaprolu Subbarao** is the founder of **Bhavakavitvam** — option **(1)**.
**Devulapalli Krishna Sastri** and **Basavaraju Apparao** were its **main poets**, not founders.
**Gurajada Apparao** wrote ***Mutyala Saralu*** and ***Kanyasulkam***.
xa: ⚠ Devulapalli Krishna Sastri = "**Andhra Shelley**".
Rayaprolu drew on **Shelley and Keats**; he is the **Father of Telugu Romanticism**.

211.s:
Consider the following statements about Bhavakavitvam:
1. It emphasised romantic and personal emotion.
2. It included nature and love as important themes.
3. It sought freedom from classical prosody.
4. It had no patriotic strands.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
211.x: Bhavakavitvam emphasised romantic and personal emotion, nature, love and freedom from classical prosody, and it also contained patriotic strands. Therefore, statement 4 is false.
211.tq: Find the one negating statement that reverses a feature of the movement.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3 only** — option **(1)**.
**Bhava Kavitvam** stressed **romantic and personal emotion**, **nature**, **love** and **freedom from classical prosody**.
Statement 4 wrong: it **had patriotic strands** too.
xa: Founder: **Rayaprolu Subbarao**; key concept **Amalina Srungaram** (platonic love).
**Venkata Parvateeswara Kavulu** — **Ekanta Seva**, the "**Telugu Gitanjali**".

211.s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of poets identified as major poets of Bhavakavitvam?
o: Basavaraju Apparao, Duvvuri Ramireddy, Devulapalli Krishna Sastri
Gurajada Apparao, Garimella Satyanarayana, Sri Sri
Bipin Chandra Pal, Rayaprolu Subbarao, Damaraju Pundarikakshudu
Kopparapu Subbarao, Krovvidi Lingaraju, Madduri Annapurnaiah
211.x: Basavaraju Apparao, Duvvuri Ramireddy and Devulapalli Krishna Sastri are listed among the main poets of Bhavakavitvam.
211.tq: Identify the complete group by separating movement poets from associated nationalist figures and prose contributors.
xs: **Basavaraju Apparao, Duvvuri Ramireddy, Devulapalli Krishna Sastri** are main Bhava Kavitvam poets — option **(1)**.
**Sri Sri** criticised the school as escapist; **Garimella** was the people's poet of the freedom struggle.
**Kopparapu Subbarao** (Roshanara), **Krovvidi Lingaraju** (Veerabali) wrote **proscribed** works.
xa: Another main Bhava poet group: **Venkata Parvateeswara Kavulu** (**Ekanta Seva**).
Basavaraju Apparao also wrote "**Kollayi gattithenemi maa Gandhi**".

211.s: The Venkata Parvateeswara Kavulu are associated with which work, described as the “Telugu Gitanjali”?
211.x: Ekanta Seva, associated with the Venkata Parvateeswara Kavulu, is described as the “Telugu Gitanjali”.
211.tq: Match the literary group with its distinctive work and description.
xs: The **Venkata Parvateeswara Kavulu** wrote **Ekanta Seva**, the "**Telugu Gitanjali**" — option **(2)**.
**Roshanara**, **Tirugubatu** and **Veerabali** are **proscribed** works.
xa: They are among the **main poets** of **Bhava Kavitvam**.
Other main Bhava poets: **Basavaraju Apparao**, **Duvvuri Ramireddy**, **Devulapalli Krishna Sastri**.

211.s: Garimella Satyanarayana left his studies in response to whose call?
o: Bipin Chandra Pal’s call for Swadeshi
Sri Sri’s call for progressive literature
Rayaprolu Subba Rao’s call for romantic poetry
211.x: Garimella Satyanarayana left his studies in response to Mahatma Gandhi’s call during the freedom movement.
211.tq: Identify the leader associated with the decisive personal action.
xs: **Garimella Satyanarayana** left his studies at **Mahatma Gandhi's call** — option **(2)**.
He was born at **Gonedapadu**, Narasannapeta taluk (**Srikakulam**).
xa: Life: **14 July 1893 to 18 Dec 1952**.
His song "**Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu**" was **praised by Gandhi**.
He is the **first people's poet** of the freedom struggle.

211.s: Which of the following was NOT listed as a grievance in Garimella Satyanarayana’s nationalist song?
211.x: The song listed grievances such as taxes, forced labour, untouchability and the policy of divide and rule. Expansion of scientific education was not among the listed grievances.
211.tq: Find the unrelated item among the specific grievances named in the song.
xs: **Expansion of scientific education** was not a grievance in the song — option **(1)**.
"**Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu**" listed **taxes**, **forced labour**, **untouchability** and **divide and rule**.
xa: The song grew to **162 lines** and was **cyclostyled a thousand times**.
Garimella was **jailed in 1922** for **one year** for it (some notes say **6** months).

211.s: Which statement about the circulation and reception of Garimella Satyanarayana’s nationalist song is correct?
o: It was cyclostyled a thousand times and praised by Gandhi.
It was published exclusively in a British government journal.
It was printed only once and was ignored by Gandhi.
It was circulated only among literary associations after independence.
211.x: The song was cyclostyled a thousand times and was praised by Mahatma Gandhi.
211.tq: Use the distinctive circulation figure and prominent response as a paired fact.
xs: The song was **cyclostyled a thousand times** and **praised by Gandhi** — option **(1)**.
"**Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu**" belonged to the **Non-Cooperation** era.
xa: It grew to **162 lines**.
Garimella was jailed in **1922**, and later served **2.5 years RI**.

211.s: Which of the following is NOT a work or category associated with Garimella Satyanarayana?
211.x: Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu was written by Viswanatha Satyanarayana. Garimella’s works included Harijana Paatalu, anti-liquor songs, Samajika Navala and Palletullalo.
211.tq: Use the author–work association to reject a famous work belonging to another poet.
xs: **Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu** is not Garimella's — option **(3)**; it is **Viswanatha Satyanarayana's** Jnanpith-winning work.
Garimella's works: **Harijana Paatalu**, **anti-liquor songs**, **Samajika Navala**, **Palletullalo**.
xa: ⚠ Viswanatha's Jnanpith was the **first for a Telugu writer**.
Garimella inspired **Nazar**, **Subbarao Panigrahi** and **Gaddar**.

211.s: Garimella Satyanarayana is described as which of the following?
o: The first people’s poet of the freedom struggle
211.x: Garimella Satyanarayana is called the first people’s poet of the freedom struggle.
211.tq: Distinguish a popular descriptive title from titles belonging to other Telugu literary figures.
xs: Garimella is called the **first people's poet of the freedom struggle** — option **(1)**.
The **Father of Telugu Romanticism** is **Rayaprolu Subbarao**; the first Telugu Jnanpith went to **Viswanatha**.
xa: Garimella's song: "**Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu**" (Non-Cooperation era).
⚠ **Gurajada** = "Desamunu preminchumanna"; **Tripuraneni** = "Veera gandham".

211.s: Garimella Satyanarayana inspired which of the following group of writers and performers?
o: Sri Sri, Viswanatha and Unnava Lakshminarayana
211.x: Garimella inspired Nazar, Subbarao Panigrahi and Gaddar.
211.tq: Recognise the complete influence-group rather than selecting a single familiar name.
xs: Garimella inspired **Nazar, Subbarao Panigrahi and Gaddar** — option **(1)**.
He is the **first people's poet** of the freedom struggle.
xa: **Togo and Nogi** were names the **Raja of Munagala** gave his sons, after Japanese commanders.
Garimella's wife, father and grandfather **died while he was in jail**.

211.s:
Consider the following statements about Garimella Satyanarayana:
1. He was jailed in 1922 for the song 'Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu'.
2. He later served 2.5 years of rigorous imprisonment.
3. He was born at Gonedapadu in Narasannapeta taluk of Guntur district.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
211.x: Statement 1 is correct: he was jailed in 1922 (for one year; some sources say six months) for the song. Statement 2 is correct: he later served 2.5 years RI, during which his wife, father and grandfather died. Statement 3 is wrong: Gonedapadu, Narasannapeta taluk, is in Srikakulam, not Guntur. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses statement 2, and options with 3 carry the wrong district.
211.tq: Garimella = Srikakulam; jailed 1922 for the song, later 2.5 years RI.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: jailed in **1922** for "**Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu**" (**one year**).
Statement 2 correct: he later served **2.5 years RI**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Gonedapadu**, Narasannapeta taluk, is in **Srikakulam**, not Guntur.
xa: Life: **14 July 1893 to 18 Dec 1952**.
Other works: **Harijana Paatalu**, **Samajika Navala**, **Palletullalo**.

211.s:
Consider the following statements about Telugu nationalist songs:
1. 'Veera gandham tecchinaramu' by Tripuraneni Ramaswamy belongs to the Salt Satyagraha era.
2. 'Kollayi gattithenemi maa Gandhi' was written by Garimella Satyanarayana.
3. 'Ma Telugu Talliki mallepoodanda' by Sankarambadi Sundarachari later became the AP State song.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
211.x: Statement 1 is correct: Tripuraneni Ramaswamy wrote it in the Salt Satyagraha era. Statement 2 is wrong: 'Kollayi gattithenemi maa Gandhi' is by Basavaraju Apparao; Garimella wrote 'Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu'. Statement 3 is correct: Sankarambadi's song became the AP State song. So 1 and 3 only; options with 2 are wrong.
211.tq: Kollayi = Basavaraju Apparao; Maakoddee = Garimella.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 correct: "**Veera gandham tecchinaramu**" — **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy**, **Salt Satyagraha** era.
Statement 2 wrong: "**Kollayi gattithenemi maa Gandhi**" is by **Basavaraju Apparao**; Garimella wrote "Maakoddee".
Statement 3 correct: **Sankarambadi Sundarachari's** song later became the **AP State song**.
xa: ⚠ **Gurajada** = "Desamunu preminchumanna"; **Garimella** = "Maakoddee".
Basavaraju Apparao was also a **Bhava Kavitvam** poet.

211.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary — ‘Kollayi gattithenemi maa Gandhi’
211.x: Basavaraju Apparao wrote ‘Kollayi gattithenemi maa Gandhi’. Jagganna Sastri wrote ‘Bharata Swarajya Yuddham’, while Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary wrote ‘Veeragandhamu Techhinaramu’.
211.tq: Start with the sure author–song pair and eliminate swapped literary attributions.
xs: **Basavaraju Apparao — "Kollayi gattithenemi maa Gandhi"** is correct — option **(1)**.
"**Veera gandham tecchinaramu**" is by **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy**, not Jagganna Sastri.
xa: Tripuraneni's song belongs to the **Salt Satyagraha** era.
"**Ma Telugu Talliki mallepoodanda**" — **Sankarambadi Sundarachari**, later the **AP State song**.

211.s: Which of the following was the first Telugu play banned by the British?
211.x: Roshanara, authored by Kopparapu Subbarao, was the first Telugu play banned by the British.
211.tq: Use the superlative clue “first” and distinguish the action from later arrests and prosecutions.
xs: ***Roshanara*** by **Kopparapu Subbarao** was the **first play banned** by the British — option **(1)**.
**Veerabali** (Krovvidi Lingaraju, **1931**) and **Chicharapidugu** (**1927-29**) came later.
**Panchala Parabhavam** led to performers' arrest in **Vizag**.
xa: **Tirugubatu** (Muni Manikyam Narasimha Rao) was banned for "**inciting the people**".
**Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu** (Garimella, **1922**) — author jailed.

211.s: Which one of the following correctly states the year and consequence associated with Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu?
o: 1931; its author was jailed for sedition under Section 124A
No year given; its performers were arrested in Vizag
211.x: Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu is associated with 1922, and its author Garimella was jailed.
211.tq: Separate closely related years and consequences in a proscribed-literature table.
xs: **Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu — 1922; author jailed** — option **(2)**.
**1931 / Sec. 124A** fits **Veerabali**; **1927-29 / editor jailed** fits **Chicharapidugu**; Vizag arrests fit **Panchala Parabhavam**.
xa: Garimella was jailed for **one year** (some notes say **6** months).
He later served **2.5 years RI**.

211.s: Chicharapidugu was serialised during which period in Congress, and what consequence followed for its editor?
o: 1907–08; the work was banned as the first Telugu play
211.x: Chicharapidugu was serialised in Congress from 1927 to 1929, and its editor Madduri Annapurnaiah was jailed.
211.tq: Pair the publication period with the correct person and consequence.
xs: **Chicharapidugu** was serialised **1927-29** in **Congress**; editor **Madduri Annapurnaiah** was jailed — option **(2)**.
Its author was **Ramachandruni Venkatappayya**.
xa: **Veerabali** — **Krovvidi Lingaraju**, **1931**, jailed for sedition (**Sec. 124A**).
***Roshanara*** — **Kopparapu Subbarao**, **first play banned**.

211.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: Veerabali — Krovvidi Lingaraju — 1931 — jailed for sedition under Section 124A
Veerabali — Kopparapu Subbarao — first play banned by the British
211.x: Veerabali was written by Krovvidi Lingaraju in 1931, and he was jailed for sedition under Section 124A.
211.tq: Start with the sure author–work pair and verify the year and official consequence.
xs: **Veerabali — Krovvidi Lingaraju — 1931 — jailed for sedition (Sec. 124A)** — option **(1)**.
**1922 / author jailed** is Garimella's song; **1927-29 / editor jailed** is **Chicharapidugu**; **first play banned** is **Roshanara**.
xa: **Tirugubatu** — **Muni Manikyam Narasimha Rao**, banned for "**inciting the people**".
**Panchala Parabhavam** — **Damaraju Pundarikakshudu**; performers arrested in **Vizag**.

211.s: The work Tirugubatu was banned on the charge of:
211.x: Tirugubatu by Muni Manikyam Narasimha Rao was banned for “inciting the people”.
211.tq: Distinguish the stated ground for prohibition from the separate ground of sedition.
xs: **Tirugubatu** was banned for "**inciting the people**" — option **(1)**.
Its author was **Muni Manikyam Narasimha Rao**.
xa: ***Roshanara*** (**Kopparapu Subbarao**) was the **first play banned**.
**Veerabali** (**1931**) — author jailed under **Sec. 124A**.

211.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Poet)
a. Rayaprolu Subbarao
b. Gurajada Apparao
c. Viswanatha Satyanarayana
d. Unnava Lakshminarayana

List-II (Work)
i. Malapalli
ii. Andhravali
iii. Kanyasulkam
iv. Veyipadagalu

Select the correct code:
211.x: Rayaprolu wrote Andhravali, Gurajada wrote Kanyasulkam, Viswanatha wrote Veyipadagalu, and Unnava wrote Malapalli.
211.tq: Start from the sure pair and verify that every remaining work is used exactly once.
xs: Correct code: **a–ii, b–iii, c–iv, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Rayaprolu** — ***Andhravali***; **Gurajada** — ***Kanyasulkam***.
**Viswanatha** — ***Veyipadagalu***; **Unnava** — ***Malapalli*** (**1922**).
xa: Rayaprolu also wrote ***Swatantrya Rathamu***; Gurajada also ***Mutyala Saralu***, ***Desabhakti Geyam***.
Viswanatha's ***Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu*** won the **Jnanpith**, the first for a Telugu writer.

211.s: Which of the following works was written by Duvvuri Ramireddy?
211.x: Matru Desa Sankeertanam was written by Duvvuri Ramireddy. Swatantrya Rathamu is by Rayaprolu, Desabhakti Geyam by Gurajada, and Firdausi by Gurram Jashuva.
211.tq: Use direct author–work recall with works from neighbouring poets as distractors.
xs: **Matru Desa Sankeertanam** was written by **Duvvuri Ramireddy** — option **(1)**.
**Firdausi** is **Gurram Jashuva's**; **Swatantrya Rathamu** is **Rayaprolu's**; **Desabhakti Geyam** is **Gurajada's**.
xa: Duvvuri Ramireddy's title: "**Kavi Kokila**".
He was a main poet of **Bhava Kavitvam**.

211.s:
Which one of the following statements is correct regarding Viswanatha Satyanarayana’s works?
1. Veyipadagalu received the Sahitya Akademi recognition.
2. Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu won the Jnanpith.
3. Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu was the first Jnanpith-winning work by a Telugu writer.
211.x: All three statements are correct. Veyipadagalu received Sahitya Akademi recognition, while Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu won the Jnanpith and was the first such award for a Telugu writer.
211.tq: Check the separate award associations before choosing the inclusive statement option.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
***Veyipadagalu*** won the **Sahitya Akademi**.
***Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu*** won the **Jnanpith**, the **first for a Telugu writer**.
xa: Viswanatha's title is **Kavi Samrat**.
Viswanatha gave the title "**Madhurakavi**" to **Gurram Jashuva** (**G2 2012** key).

211.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
211.x: Gabbilam was written by Gurram Jashuva, not Duvvuri Ramireddy. Duvvuri Ramireddy wrote Matru Desa Sankeertanam.
211.tq: Find the swapped author–work pair among otherwise familiar literary associations.
xs: **Duvvuri Ramireddy — Gabbilam** is wrongly matched — option **(4)**.
***Gabbilam*** (**1941**) is by **Gurram Jashuva**; Duvvuri wrote **Matru Desa Sankeertanam**.
The rest are correct: Unnava — **Malapalli**; Jashuva — **Netaji Charitra**, **Christu Charitra**.
xa: Jashuva also wrote **Firdausi**.
Jashuva's title: **Navayuga Kavi Chakravarti** (**1946**).

211.s: Kanyasulkam was first staged in:
211.x: Gurajada Apparao’s Kanyasulkam was first staged in 1893.
211.tq: Separate the staging year of a drama from publication years of other Telugu works.
xs: ***Kanyasulkam*** was first staged in **1893** — option **(3)**.
It was written by **Gurajada Apparao**.
**1941** is the year of Jashuva's ***Gabbilam***.
xa: Gurajada also wrote ***Mutyala Saralu*** and ***Desabhakti Geyam***.
Kanyasulkam — Gurajada was asked in the **G2 2025** match.

211.s:
Match List-I (Work) with List-II (Author):

List-I
a. Veera Telangana
b. Nenu-Na Desam
c. Andhrula Sanghika Charitra
d. Japaneeyamu

List-II
i. Suravaram Pratap Reddy
ii. Ravi Narayana Reddy
iii. Sriram Veerabrahmam
iv. Darsi Chenchaiah

Select the correct code:
211.x: Veera Telangana is by Ravi Narayana Reddy, Nenu-Na Desam by Darsi Chenchaiah, Andhrula Sanghika Charitra by Suravaram Pratap Reddy (all in the G2 2008 match), and Japaneeyamu by Sriram Veerabrahmam (G2 2025 match). Only option A has all four right; the others swap Ravi Narayana Reddy, Darsi Chenchaiah and Suravaram.
211.tq: Social history of Andhras = Suravaram; Veera Telangana = Ravi Narayana Reddy.
xs: Correct code: **a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii** — option **(1)**.
**Veera Telangana** — **Ravi Narayana Reddy**; **Nenu-Na Desam** — **Darsi Chenchaiah**.
**Andhrula Sanghika Charitra** — **Suravaram Pratap Reddy**; **Japaneeyamu** — **Sriram Veerabrahmam**.
xa: **G2 2008** match also had **Veyyipadagalu** — **Viswanatha**.
**G2 2025** match also had **Mahaprasthanam** — **Sri Sri**.

211.s: Who was known by the title “Abhinava Nannaya” according to the commission’s key and the accepted examination reference?
211.x: The accepted examination answer is Rayaprolu Subbarao. Although another source assigns the title to Viswanatha, the commission’s key and CDI assign it to Rayaprolu.
211.tq: Resolve a source-sensitive title by remembering the examination-key convention rather than the conflicting attribution.
xs: The commission's key gives "**Abhinava Nannaya**" to **Rayaprolu Subbarao** — option **(3)**.
⚠ Some notes give it to **Viswanatha**, but Viswanatha's title is **Kavi Samrat**.
xa: **Kavi Kokila** — **Duvvuri Ramireddy**.
**Andhra Shelley** — **Devulapalli Krishna Sastri**.
**Telugu Lenka** — **Tummala Sitaramamurthy**.

211.s:
Consider the following statements about the titles of Telugu poets:
1. 'Kavi Kokila' was the title of Duvvuri Ramireddy; Vinukonda citizens also gave it to Gurram Jashuva in 1936.
2. 'Kavi Samrat' was the title of Rayaprolu Subbarao.
3. 'Andhra Shelley' was Devulapalli Krishna Sastri.
4. 'Telugu Lenka' was Tummala Sitaramamurthy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
211.x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct as per the title list. Statement 2 is wrong: 'Kavi Samrat' is Viswanatha Satyanarayana; Rayaprolu's title is 'Abhinava Nannaya'. So 1, 3 and 4 only; options with 2 are wrong.
211.tq: Kavi Samrat = Viswanatha; Abhinava Nannaya = Rayaprolu.
xs: Statements **1, 3 and 4 only** — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Kavi Kokila** — **Duvvuri Ramireddy**; Vinukonda citizens also gave it to **Jashuva** (**1936**).
Statement 2 wrong: **Kavi Samrat** is **Viswanatha**; Rayaprolu is **Abhinava Nannaya**.
Statements 3 and 4 correct: **Andhra Shelley** — **Devulapalli Krishna Sastri**; **Telugu Lenka** — **Tummala Sitaramamurthy**.
xa: **Maha Kavi** — **Sri Sri**; **Boyi Bhimanna** also received "Mahakavi".
