**Navayuga Kavi Chakravarti** — **Gurram Jashuva** (**1946**).

211.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the titles associated with Gurram Jashuva is correct?
o: He was given Navayuga Kavi Chakravarti in 1946.
He was known as Andhra Shelley.
He received Viswakavi Samrat in 1936 from Vinukonda citizens.
He received Madhura Kavi Srinatha in 1964.
211.x: Gurram Jashuva was given the title Navayuga Kavi Chakravarti in 1946. He also had the titles Madhura Kavi Srinatha in 1952 and Viswakavi Samrat in 1964; Vinukonda citizens gave him Kavi Kokila in 1936.
211.tq: Discriminate among a poet’s multiple titles by checking the title-year association.
xs: **Gurram Jashuva** was given **Navayuga Kavi Chakravarti** in **1946** — option **(1)**.
**Viswakavi Samrat** came in **1964** and **Madhura Kavi Srinatha** in **1952**.
In **1936** Vinukonda citizens gave him **Kavi Kokila**; **Andhra Shelley** is **Devulapalli Krishna Sastri**.
xa: "**Madhurakavi**" was given to him by **Viswanatha Satyanarayana**.
Jashuva's works: ***Gabbilam*** (**1941**), **Firdausi**, **Netaji Charitra**, **Christu Charitra**.

211.s: Who conferred the title “Madhurakavi” on Gurram Jashuva?
211.x: The title Madhurakavi was given to Gurram Jashuva by Viswanatha Satyanarayana.
211.tq: Identify the person who conferred a title, not merely the person who held it.
xs: **Viswanatha Satyanarayana** conferred "**Madhurakavi**" on **Gurram Jashuva** — option **(1)** (**G2 2012** key).
Jashuva's other titles: **Navayuga Kavi Chakravarti** (**1946**), **Viswakavi Samrat** (**1964**).
xa: Viswanatha's own title: **Kavi Samrat**.
**Telugu Lenka** — **Tummala Sitaramamurthy** (**G2 2012** key).

211.s: Who is popularly known by the title 'Maha Kavi' in the context of Telugu progressive literature?
211.x: Sri Sri is popularly known as 'Maha Kavi'. Boyi Bhimanna also received the title 'Mahakavi'.
211.tq: Directly associate a popular title with its principal poet.
xs: **Sri Sri** is popularly known as "**Maha Kavi**" — option **(2)**.
**Boyi Bhimanna** also received "**Mahakavi**", but Sri Sri is the standard answer.
**Gurram Jashuva** is **Navayuga Kavi Chakravarti**; **Viswanatha** is **Kavi Samrat**.
xa: Sri Sri wrote **Mahaprasthanam** (**G2 2025** match).
⚠ "**Poet of the Millennium**" is disputed: G2 2025 key — **Jashuva**; APHQ book — **Sri Sri**.

211.s: Which poet was listed by the APPSC Group 2 2025 key as the 'Poet of the Millennium'?
211.x: The APPSC Group 2 2025 key listed Gurram Jashuva as the 'Poet of the Millennium', although another answer source attributed the title to Sri Sri.
211.tq: Handle a current-exam title attribution by distinguishing competing answer references.
xs: The **APPSC G2 2025** key lists **Gurram Jashuva** as "**Poet of the Millennium**" — option **(2)**.
⚠ The **APHQ book's** answer gives **Sri Sri**; the title is **disputed**.
xa: Jashuva's other titles: **Navayuga Kavi Chakravarti** (**1946**), **Madhura Kavi Srinatha** (**1952**), **Viswakavi Samrat** (**1964**).
Jashuva's ***Gabbilam*** appeared in **1941**.

211.s: Why did nationalist songs in spoken Telugu have a wider social reach than pamphlets?
o: They were written exclusively in classical prosody
They avoided political and social themes
They were restricted to educated urban readers
They could reach villagers who could not be reached effectively by pamphlets
211.x: Songs in spoken Telugu could reach villagers more effectively than pamphlets, thereby widening nationalist communication.
211.tq: Apply the communication advantage of spoken-language literature to a social situation.
xs: Songs in **spoken Telugu** could **reach villagers that pamphlets could not** — option **(4)**.
They were not bound to **classical prosody** or to urban readers; that is exactly why they spread.
xa: **Gurajada** made **vyavaharika bhasha** normal in literature.
Garimella's "**Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu**" was **cyclostyled a thousand times**.
Progressive writers later widened the attack to **caste and class**.

211.s: Which literary development is associated with Gurajada in the growth of Telugu nationalist and progressive writing?
o: Banning all patriotic songs from public performance
Making vyavaharika bhasha a normal literary medium
Restoring exclusive dependence on classical prosody
Limiting Telugu literature to court poetry
211.x: Gurajada helped make vyavaharika bhasha, or spoken Telugu, a normal literary medium.
211.tq: Identify the specific linguistic contribution rather than a broad political claim.
xs: **Gurajada** made **vyavaharika bhasha** (spoken Telugu) a normal literary medium — option **(2)**.
He moved away from classical diction; he did not restore **classical prosody** or court poetry.
xa: His poem "**Desamunu preminchumanna**" (***Mutyala Saralu***) is the "**national anthem of Telugu people**".
His play ***Kanyasulkam*** was staged in **1893**.
Progressive writers later widened the attack to **caste and class**.

211.s: At the World Telugu Mahasabhalu, which of the following set of Jnanpith awardees was recalled along with Gurajada and Sri Sri by Chief Minister Naidu?
o: Viswanatha, C. Narayana Reddy and Ravuri Bharadwaja
Rayaprolu Subbarao, Garimella Satyanarayana and Duvvuri Ramireddy
Kopparapu Subbarao, Krovvidi Lingaraju and Muni Manikyam Narasimha Rao
Basavaraju Apparao, Devulapalli Krishna Sastri and Madduri Annapurnaiah
211.x: Chief Minister Naidu recalled Gurajada, Sri Sri and the Jnanpith winners Viswanatha, C. Narayana Reddy and Ravuri Bharadwaja at the World Telugu Mahasabhalu.
211.tq: Test the complete membership of a named group rather than one isolated name.
xs: CM Naidu recalled Jnanpith winners **Viswanatha, C. Narayana Reddy and Ravuri Bharadwaja** — option **(1)**.
This was at the **World Telugu Mahasabhalu** (**6 Jan 2026**), along with **Gurajada** and **Sri Sri**.
xa: Viswanatha's ***Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu*** won the **first Jnanpith for a Telugu writer**.
⚠ **C. Narayana Reddy** called "**Melukonumi Bharata Putruda**" (Oct **1909**) the first nationalist song.

211.s: The Bhava Kavitvam–Abhyudaya debate chiefly concerns whether romanticism was escapist or whether it:
o: Served as a necessary liberation of literary form
Eliminated all patriotic elements from poetry
Required a return to court literature
Made spoken Telugu unsuitable for public communication
211.x: The debate contrasts the criticism of romanticism as escapist with the view that it was a necessary liberation of literary form.
211.tq: Identify both sides of a literary debate and choose the precise contrasting proposition.
xs: The **Bhava Kavitvam vs Abhyudaya** debate: escapist romanticism, or a **necessary liberation of form** — option **(1)**.
Progressive writers like **Sri Sri** called Rayaprolu's romanticism "**escapist**".
Bhava Kavitvam **kept patriotic strands**, so option (2) is wrong.
xa: Rayaprolu **freed Telugu verse from rigid prosody**.
Rayaprolu is the **Father of Telugu Romanticism**; key concept **Amalina Srungaram** (platonic love).

212.s: The Abhyudaya Rachayitala Sangham, popularly known as Arasam, was formed in:
212.x: Arasam, the Telugu Progressive Writers' Association, was formed in 1943.
212.tq: Test the founding year of a literary organisation against nearby movement dates.
xs: **Arasam** (**Abhyudaya Rachayitala Sangham**) was formed in **1943** — option **(3)**.
**1936** is the **AIPWA** (Lucknow); **1970** is **Virasam** (Hyderabad).
xa: Arasam was the AIPWA's **Telugu counterpart**.
It organised the **Abhyudaya** current started by **Sri Sri's** poems.
⚠ Arasam = **progressive**; Virasam = **revolutionary** (Viplava).

212.s: Which organisation organised the Abhyudaya current associated with the beginning of Sri Sri's progressive poetry?
212.x: Arasam organised the Abhyudaya current that Sri Sri's poems initiated.
212.tq: Distinguish the progressive organisation from the later revolutionary writers' organisation.
xs: **Arasam** organised the **Abhyudaya** current started by Sri Sri's poems — option **(1)**.
**Virasam** (**1970**) is the later **Viplava** phase; **Art Lovers** (**1970**) grew into **Jana Natya Mandali**.
**Praja Natya Mandali** was a **communist cultural front** using drama and folk forms.
xa: Arasam was formed in **1943**, as the AIPWA's Telugu counterpart.
The founding text of **Abhyudaya kavitvam** is ***Mahaprasthanam*** (published **1950**).

212.s: The All India Progressive Writers' Association was founded at Lucknow in:
212.x: The All India Progressive Writers' Association was founded at Lucknow in 1936.
212.tq: Pair the organisation's founding venue with its year.
xs: The **AIPWA** was founded at **Lucknow** in **1936** — option **(2)**.
**1943** is **Arasam**, its Telugu counterpart.
xa: The founding session was **presided by Premchand**.
Through the **AIPWA** and the **AISF**, communists spread anti-British revolutionary ideas.

212.s: Who presided over the founding session of the All India Progressive Writers' Association?
212.x: Premchand presided over the founding session of the All India Progressive Writers' Association at Lucknow.
212.tq: Use the presiding-person trap in organisational history.
xs: **Premchand** presided over the AIPWA's founding (**1936, Lucknow**) — option **(2)**.
**Sri Sri** was the **Founding President** of **Virasam** (**1970**), not the AIPWA.
xa: Arasam (**1943**) was the AIPWA's **Telugu counterpart**.
Communists used the **AIPWA** and **AISF** to spread anti-British ideas.

212.s: Who is the author of the Telugu literary work *Mahaprasthanam*?
212.x: *Mahaprasthanam* was written by Sri Sri, whose original name was Srirangam Srinivasa Rao.
212.tq: Directly identify the author of a major work.
xs: ***Mahaprasthanam*** was written by **Sri Sri** (Srirangam Srinivasa Rao) — option **(3)**.
**Jashuva** wrote ***Gabbilam***; **Gopichand** wrote ***Asamarthuni Jeevayatra***; **Arudra** wrote ***Tvamevaham***.
xa: About **41** poems written **1933-47**, published **1950**; first poem ***Jayabheri*** (**1933**).
Dedicated to **Kompella Janardhana Rao**, preface by **Chalam**.
Founding text of **Abhyudaya kavitvam**.

212.s: *Mahaprasthanam* was dedicated to whom?
212.x: Sri Sri dedicated *Mahaprasthanam* to Kompella Janardhana Rao. Chalam wrote its preface.
212.tq: Distinguish the person to whom a work was dedicated from its preface writer.
xs: ***Mahaprasthanam*** was dedicated to **Kompella Janardhana Rao** — option **(2)**.
**Chalam** wrote its **preface**; **Puripanda Appalaswamy** co-founded **Sahiti Samiti** with Sri Sri.
xa: It was published in **1950**; first poem ***Jayabheri*** (**1933**).
It is the founding text of **Abhyudaya kavitvam**.

212.s:
Consider the following statements about Sri Sri's works:
1. Khadga Srushti expresses the necessity of radical, armed change.
2. Maro Prasthanam belongs to his revolutionary (post-1970) phase.
3. Anantham is a collection of the Sirisirimuvva satakam and limericks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
212.x: Statement 1 is correct: Khadga Srushti is about radical, armed change. Statement 2 is correct: Maro Prasthanam marks his post-1970 revolutionary phase. Statement 3 is wrong: Sirisirimuvva satakam and limericks are in Siprali; Anantham is his autobiography. So 1 and 2 only.
212.tq: Siprali = satakam + limericks; Anantham = autobiography.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: ***Khadga Srushti*** — necessity of **radical, armed change**.
Statement 2 correct: ***Maro Prasthanam*** — his **revolutionary (post-1970)** phase.
Statement 3 wrong: Sirisirimuvva satakam and limericks are in ***Siprali***; ***Anantham*** is his **autobiography**.
xa: ***Mahaprasthanam*** (**1950**) is the founding text of **Abhyudaya kavitvam**.
Sri Sri's title: **Mahakavi**.

212.s: Sri Sri was born at:
212.x: Sri Sri was born at Vizag on 2 January 1910.
212.tq: Directly test a biographical birthplace.
xs: Sri Sri was born at **Vizag** on **2 Jan 1910** — option **(3)**.
**Hyderabad** is where **Virasam** was formed (**July 1970**); **Lucknow** is where the **AIPWA** began (**1936**).
xa: Virasam's spark: his **Shashtipurti in Vizag** (Feb **1970**).
He co-founded **Sahiti Samiti (Vizag)** with **Puripanda Appalaswamy**.

212.s: Which intellectual influences are specifically associated with Sri Sri?
212.x: Sri Sri was influenced by the ideas of Marx and Hegel.
212.tq: Identify the stated intellectual influences from nearby literary names.
xs: Sri Sri was influenced by **Marx and Hegel** — option **(1)**.
**Premchand** presided over the AIPWA; **Gorky's** The Mother was translated by **Krovvidi Lingaraju**.
xa: Sri Sri's title: **Mahakavi**.
***Khadga Srushti*** argued for **radical, armed change**.

212.s: For which song did Sri Sri receive the National Award for Best Lyricist?
212.x: Sri Sri received the National Award for Best Lyricist for *Telugu Veera Levara* from the film *Alluri Seetharama Raju*.
212.tq: Match the award with the exact song rather than the film title alone.
xs: Sri Sri won the **National Award for best lyricist** for "**Telugu Veera Levara**" (film **Alluri Seetharama Raju**) — option **(3)**.
***Jayabheri*** (**1933**) is the first poem of ***Mahaprasthanam***; **Maa Bhoomi** is a Praja Natya Mandali play.
xa: The award is dated **1974** and called the **first National Award for a Telugu lyricist**.
He was also the **first to dub a film into Telugu** (**Aahuti**).

212.s: Sri Sri is described as the first person to dub which film into Telugu?
212.x: Sri Sri was the first to dub a film into Telugu, and the film was *Aahuti*.
212.tq: Separate a film for which lyrics were written from the film associated with dubbing.
xs: Sri Sri was the first to **dub a film into Telugu** — **Aahuti**, option **(3)**.
**Alluri Seetharama Raju** was the film whose song "**Telugu Veera Levara**" won him the lyricist award.
**Amma** is Krovvidi Lingaraju's translation of Gorky's **The Mother** (**1934**).
xa: The lyricist award (**1974**) is called the **first National Award for a Telugu lyricist**.
Sri Sri's autobiography: ***Anantham***.

212.s: Sri Sri co-founded Sahiti Samiti at Vizag with:
212.x: Sri Sri co-founded Sahiti Samiti at Vizag with Puripanda Appalaswamy.
212.tq: Test a specific co-founder relationship.
xs: Sri Sri co-founded **Sahiti Samiti (Vizag)** with **Puripanda Appalaswamy** — option **(2)**.
**Kompella Janardhana Rao** received the dedication of ***Mahaprasthanam***; **Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao** was **Vice-President of Virasam**.
xa: **Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao** co-wrote the play **Maa Bhoomi**.
Sri Sri was **Founding President** of **Virasam** (**July 1970**).

212.s:
Consider the following statements about Sri Sri's Mahaprasthanam:
1. Its poems were written between 1933 and 1947, and it was published in 1950.
2. Its first poem was Jayabheri (1933).
3. It is the founding text of the Viplava poetry of the Virasam phase.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
212.x: Statement 1 is correct: about 41 poems written 1933-47, published 1950. Statement 2 is correct: the first poem is Jayabheri (1933). Statement 3 is wrong: Mahaprasthanam is the founding text of Abhyudaya kavitvam; the Viplava (Virasam, 1970) phase is reflected in Maro Prasthanam. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses statement 2, and options with 3 are wrong.
212.tq: Mahaprasthanam = Abhyudaya (published 1950); Maro Prasthanam = Viplava.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: poems written **1933-47**, published **1950**.
Statement 2 correct: first poem ***Jayabheri*** (**1933**).
Statement 3 wrong: it founded **Abhyudaya kavitvam**; the Viplava (post-1970) phase is ***Maro Prasthanam***.
xa: About **41** poems; preface by **Chalam**.
Path: **Abhyudaya** (Arasam) → **Viplava** (**1970**, Virasam, after Srikakulam).

212.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
212.x: *Gabbilam* was written by Gurram Jashuva, not Sri Sri. *Firdausi* was also written by Jashuva, while *Asamarthuni Jeevayatra* was written by Tripuraneni Gopichand.
212.tq: Find the wrong author–work pairing.
xs: ***Gabbilam* — Sri Sri** is wrongly matched — option **(3)**.
***Gabbilam*** (**1941**) and ***Firdausi*** are by **Gurram Jashuva**.
***Asamarthuni Jeevayatra*** is by **Tripuraneni Gopichand** — correct.
xa: In Gabbilam a **bat carries a Dalit's plea to God**.
***Firdausi*** is a **laghu kavyam**.

212.s: The central image in Gurram Jashuva's *Gabbilam* is that of a bat which:
o: carries a Dalit's plea to God
212.x: In *Gabbilam*, a bat carries the plea of a Dalit to God.
212.tq: Identify the central literary image rather than the author alone.
xs: In ***Gabbilam*** the **bat carries a Dalit's plea to God** — option **(1)**.
The work is by **Gurram Jashuva** (**1941**).
The **Telangana struggle** is the theme of Arudra's ***Tvamevaham***.
xa: Jashuva also wrote ***Firdausi***, a **laghu kavyam**.
⚠ Gabbilam is **Jashuva's**, not **Sri Sri's**.

212.s: *Firdausi* by Gurram Jashuva is classified as a:
212.x: *Firdausi* is described as a laghu kavyam by Gurram Jashuva.
212.tq: Test the precise literary classification of a work.
xs: ***Firdausi*** by **Gurram Jashuva** is a **laghu kavyam** — option **(2)**.
The **psychological novel** is Gopichand's ***Asamarthuni Jeevayatra***; the **satakam** (Sirisirimuvva) is in Sri Sri's ***Siprali***.
xa: Jashuva's ***Gabbilam*** (**1941**): a bat carries a **Dalit's plea** to God.
**Boyi Bhimanna's** ***Gudisale Kalipotunnayi*** won the **Sahitya Akademi** (**1975**).

212.s: Which one of the following is NOT a work associated with Arudra?
212.x: *Gudisale Kalipotunnayi* was written by Boyi Bhimanna. Arudra's listed works include *Tvamevaham*, *Cinevali* and *Samagra Andhra Sahityam*.
212.tq: Find the work belonging to another writer in a related list.
xs: ***Gudisale Kalipotunnayi*** is not Arudra's — option **(1)**; it is **Boyi Bhimanna's** (Sahitya Akademi **1975**).
Arudra's works: ***Tvamevaham*** (**1948-49**), ***Cinevali***, ***Samagra Andhra Sahityam***.
xa: Arudra = **Bhagavatula Sadasiva Sankara Sastri**, **Sri Sri's nephew**.
Arudra translated **Veera Telangana Viplava Geethalu** from English.

212.s: Arudra was the nephew of:
212.x: Arudra, whose original name was Bhagavatula Sadasiva Sankara Sastri, was Sri Sri's nephew.
212.tq: Test a biographical relationship rather than a work–author pair.
xs: **Arudra** was **Sri Sri's nephew** — option **(1)**.
His real name: **Bhagavatula Sadasiva Sankara Sastri**.
xa: ***Tvamevaham*** (**1948-49**) is on the **Telangana struggle**.
He also wrote ***Samagra Andhra Sahityam*** and ***Cinevali***.

212.s: Which work of Tripuraneni Gopichand received the Sahitya Akademi recognition mentioned in relation to his writings?
212.x: *Pandita Parameswara Sastri Veelunama* by Tripuraneni Gopichand received the Sahitya Akademi recognition referred to here.
212.tq: Distinguish works by the same writer using the associated award detail.
xs: Gopichand's ***Pandita Parameswara Sastri Veelunama*** won the **Sahitya Akademi** — option **(2)**.
***Chaduvu*** is **Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao's**; ***Tvamevaham*** and ***Cinevali*** are **Arudra's**.
xa: Gopichand also wrote ***Asamarthuni Jeevayatra*** (**G2 2017** key).
He was the **first Director of Information of Andhra State** (**1953**).

212.s: Which novel is associated with Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao?
212.x: *Chaduvu* is the novel associated with Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao.
212.tq: Directly identify a writer–novel pairing.
xs: **Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao** wrote the novel ***Chaduvu*** — option **(1)**.
***Gabbilam*** is **Jashuva's**; ***Maro Prasthanam*** is **Sri Sri's**; ***Pandita Parameswara Sastri Veelunama*** is **Gopichand's**.
xa: Kutumba Rao was **Vice-President of Virasam** (**1970**).
**Sri Sri** was Virasam's **Founding President**.

212.s: Who wrote *Gudisale Kalipotunnayi*, which won the Sahitya Akademi award in 1975?
212.x: Boyi Bhimanna wrote *Gudisale Kalipotunnayi*, which won the Sahitya Akademi award in 1975.
212.tq: Link an award-winning work to its author and year.
xs: ***Gudisale Kalipotunnayi*** (Sahitya Akademi **1975**) was written by **Boyi Bhimanna** — option **(4)**.
Bhimanna was a **praja and abhyudaya poet**.
xa: **Gopichand's** Sahitya Akademi work: ***Pandita Parameswara Sastri Veelunama***.
Arudra's ***Tvamevaham*** (**1948-49**) is on the Telangana struggle.

212.s: Asamarthuni Jeevayatra, a psychological novel dedicated to the author's father, was written by:
212.x: Tripuraneni Gopichand wrote Asamarthuni Jeevayatra (APPSC G2 2017 key); he also wrote Pandita Parameswara Sastri Veelunama (Sahitya Akademi) and was the first Director of Information of Andhra State (1953). Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao wrote the novel Chaduvu, Arudra wrote Tvamevaham, and Boyi Bhimanna wrote Gudisale Kalipotunnayi.
212.tq: Asamarthuni Jeevayatra = Gopichand's psychological novel.
xs: ***Asamarthuni Jeevayatra*** was written by **Tripuraneni Gopichand** — option **(1)** (**G2 2017** key).
**Kutumba Rao** wrote ***Chaduvu***; **Arudra** wrote ***Tvamevaham***; **Boyi Bhimanna** wrote ***Gudisale Kalipotunnayi***.
xa: Gopichand's ***Pandita Parameswara Sastri Veelunama*** won the **Sahitya Akademi**.
He was the **first Director of Information of Andhra State** (**1953**).

212.s: Gorky's *The Mother* was translated into Telugu as *Amma* by:
212.x: Krovvidi Lingaraju translated Gorky's *The Mother* into Telugu as *Amma* in 1934.
212.tq: Directly test the translator–translation pair.
xs: Gorky's **The Mother** was translated as **Amma** by **Krovvidi Lingaraju** (**1934**) — option **(3)**.
**Narla Venkateswara Rao** wrote **Neti Russia**; **Gadde Lingayya** ran **Adarsha Grantha Mandali**.
xa: Amma — Krovvidi Lingaraju was a **GS 2019** key question.
**Arudra** translated **Veera Telangana Viplava Geethalu** from English.

212.s: Who wrote *Neti Russia*?
212.x: *Neti Russia* was written by Narla Venkateswara Rao.
212.tq: Identify the author of a world-progressive literature-related work.
xs: **Neti Russia** was written by **Narla Venkateswara Rao** — option **(3)**.
**Krovvidi Lingaraju** translated Gorky's **The Mother** as **Amma** (**1934**).
xa: Leftist and world literature publishers: **Mahidhara brothers' Viswa Sahityamala**, **Gadde Lingayya's Adarsha Grantha Mandali**.
**Maa Bhoomi** — **Sunkara Satyanarayana and Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao**.

212.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding progressive literature in Telugu?
1. Arudra translated *Veera Telangana Viplava Geethalu* from English.
2. The Mahidhara brothers published *Viswa Sahityamala*.
3. Gadde Lingayya's *Adarsha Grantha Mandali* published leftist and world literature.
212.x: All three statements are correct. Arudra translated *Veera Telangana Viplava Geethalu*, while the Mahidhara brothers and Gadde Lingayya's organisations published progressive and world literature.
212.tq: Combine translator, publisher and institution relationships in a coded statement question.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
**Arudra** translated **Veera Telangana Viplava Geethalu** from English.
The **Mahidhara brothers** published **Viswa Sahityamala**; **Gadde Lingayya's Adarsha Grantha Mandali** published leftist and world literature.
xa: **Krovvidi Lingaraju** — **Amma** (Gorky's The Mother), **1934**.
**Narla Venkateswara Rao** — **Neti Russia**.

212.s: The play *Maa Bhoomi*, staged by the Praja Natya Mandali, was written by:
o: Sunkara Satyanarayana and Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao
212.x: Praja Natya Mandali staged *Maa Bhoomi*, written by Sunkara Satyanarayana and Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao.
212.tq: Identify the correct writer pair for a progressive stage work.
xs: **Maa Bhoomi** was written by **Sunkara Satyanarayana and Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao** — option **(1)**.
**Gaddar and B. Narsinga Rao** ran **Art Lovers** (**1970**), which became **Jana Natya Mandali** (**1971**).
xa: **Praja Natya Mandali** was a **communist cultural front**; main folk form **Burrakatha**.
Gorky's The Mother → **Amma**, by **Krovvidi Lingaraju** (**1934**).

212.s: Praja Natya Mandali was primarily established as which of the following?
o: A constitutional body for local self-government
A communist cultural front for propagating ideas through drama, songs and folk forms
A peasant tribunal for settling tenancy disputes
A journal-editing committee of the CPI
212.x: Praja Natya Mandali was a communist cultural front that spread its ideas through drama, songs and folk forms.
212.tq: Identify an organisation from its function and method of mobilisation rather than from its name alone.
xs: **Praja Natya Mandali** was a **communist cultural front** spreading ideas through **drama, songs and folk forms** — option **(2)**.
Its main folk form was **Burrakatha**.
xa: Its play **Maa Bhoomi** was by **Sunkara Satyanarayana and Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao**.
**Jana Natya Mandali** (**1971**) grew from Gaddar and B. Narsinga Rao's **Art Lovers** (**1970**).

212.s: Which folk form constituted the main folk medium of Praja Natya Mandali?
212.x: Burrakatha was the main folk form used by Praja Natya Mandali.
212.tq: Use the exact traditional art form rather than a broadly related cultural performance.
xs: **Burrakatha** was Praja Natya Mandali's main folk form — option **(1)**.
The body spread communist ideas through **drama, songs and folk forms**.
xa: Its famous play: **Maa Bhoomi**.
⚠ **Arasam** (**1943**) is the progressive **writers'** body; Praja Natya Mandali is the cultural front.

212.s: Art Lovers, associated with Gaddar and B. Narsinga Rao, became Jana Natya Mandali in:
212.x: Art Lovers became Jana Natya Mandali in 1971; Art Lovers itself is associated with 1970.
212.tq: Separate two successive organisational dates.
xs: **Art Lovers** became **Jana Natya Mandali** in **1971** — option **(3)**.
Art Lovers itself was formed by **Gaddar and B. Narsinga Rao** in **1970**.
xa: **Virasam** was formed at **Hyderabad** in **July 1970**.
Older cultural front: **Praja Natya Mandali** (Burrakatha).

212.s: Which of the following works were banned?
212.x: The works *Le* and *March* were banned. *Jhamjha*, *Le* and *Viplavam Vardhillali* were listed as Virasam poetry collections.
212.tq: Distinguish the complete collection list from the separate banned-work list.
xs: **Le** and **March** were **banned** — option **(4)**.
**Jhamjha** (**1970**) and **Viplavam Vardhillali** were Virasam collections but not listed as banned.
**Maa Bhoomi** is a play; **Amma** and **Gabbilam** are a translation and a Jashuva poem.
xa: Virasam collections: **Jhamjha**, **Le**, **Viplavam Vardhillali**.
Virasam's **Founding President** was **Sri Sri**.

212.s:
Consider the following statements about Virasam:
1. Sri Sri was its founding President.
2. It was formed at Hyderabad in July 1970.
3. It is the Progressive Writers' Association of Telugu.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
212.x: Statement 1 is correct: Sri Sri was the founding President. Statement 2 is correct: it was formed at Hyderabad in July 1970 (sparked by his Shashtipurti in Vizag, Feb 1970). Statement 3 is wrong: Virasam is the Viplava (Revolutionary) Writers' Association; the progressive body is Arasam (1943). So 1 and 2 only.
212.tq: Virasam = Revolutionary (1970); Arasam = Progressive (1943).
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Sri Sri** was Virasam's **Founding President**.
Statement 2 correct: formed at **Hyderabad**, **July 1970**.
Statement 3 wrong: Virasam is the **Revolutionary (Viplava)** body; the progressive body is **Arasam** (**1943**).
xa: Spark: Sri Sri's **Shashtipurti in Vizag** (Feb **1970**).
**Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao** was its **Vice-President**.

212.s: Which sequence correctly represents the broad transition in Telugu progressive and revolutionary literary activity?
o: Virasam — Arasam — nationalist poetry — class struggle
Abhyudaya through Arasam — Viplava through Virasam — class struggle
Class struggle — nationalist poetry — Arasam — Virasam
AIPWA — Praja Natya Mandali — Arasam — nationalist poetry
212.x: The broad path ran from Abhyudaya literature through Arasam in the 1930s–40s to Viplava literature through Virasam in 1970, with Telugu poetry moving from nationalism towards class struggle.
212.tq: Arrange the movement's ideological development from earlier to later stages.
xs: **Abhyudaya (Arasam) → Viplava (Virasam) → class struggle** — option **(2)**.
Abhyudaya ran in the **1930s-40s** via **Arasam**; Viplava began in **1970** via **Virasam**, after **Srikakulam**.
Telugu poetry turned **from the nationalist to the class struggle**.
xa: Founding Abhyudaya text: ***Mahaprasthanam***; Viplava-phase text: ***Maro Prasthanam***.

212.s: Traditionalists criticised Sri Sri's free verse on the ground that it:
o: rejected all translations from world literature
was written only in classical metre
212.x: Traditionalists argued that Sri Sri's free verse destroyed the 'sweetness' of Telugu, while his supporters credited him with making Telugu poetry modern.
212.tq: Distinguish criticism from the supporters' assessment.
xs: Traditionalists said Sri Sri's free verse **destroyed the "sweetness" of Telugu** — option **(1)**.
Supporters credit him with **making Telugu poetry modern**.
xa: Sri Sri's title: **Mahakavi**; influenced by **Marx and Hegel**.
***Mahaprasthanam*** (**1950**) founded **Abhyudaya kavitvam**.

212.s: At the World Telugu Mahasabhalu, who cited Sri Sri among the greats of Telugu literature?
o: The Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu
212.x: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu cited Sri Sri among the greats of Telugu literature at the World Telugu Mahasabhalu on 6 January 2026.
212.tq: Test a current-affairs association involving a literary personality.
xs: **CM N. Chandrababu Naidu** cited Sri Sri among the greats at the **World Telugu Mahasabhalu** — option **(1)**.
The event was on **6 Jan 2026**.
xa: Sri Sri was born at **Vizag**, **2 Jan 1910**.
**Puripanda Appalaswamy** co-founded **Sahiti Samiti** with Sri Sri.

213.s: Hindu Nataka Samajam of Rajahmundry staged plays written by which of the following?
o: Dharmavaram Ramakrishnamacharyulu and Kolachalam Srinivasa Rao
Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham and Toleti Venkata Subbarao
Kallakuri Narayana Rao and Vedam Venkataraya Sastri
213.x: The Rajahmundry Hindu Nataka Samajam staged plays written by Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham and Toleti Venkata Subbarao.
213.tq: Identify the correct institutional association rather than matching playwrights merely by fame.
xs: The **Hindu Nataka Samajam, Rajahmundry** staged plays by **Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham** and **Toleti Venkata Subbarao** — option **(2)**.
**Dharmavaram Ramakrishnamacharyulu** ran his own **Sarasa Vinodini Sabha** at **Bellary**.
xa: The Rajahmundry Samajam dates to **1889**, founded by **Immani Hanumantharao**.
**Tanguturi Prakasam** and **Durga Gopalakrishnayya** acted main roles for it.
⚠ Three Hindu Nataka Samajams: **Guntur 1880-81**, **Kakinada 1885**, **Rajahmundry 1889**.

213.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Theatre company)
(a) Surabhi
(b) Sarasa Vinodini Sabha
(c) Hindu Nataka Samajam, Guntur
(d) Amateur Nataka Sabha

List-II (Founder)
(i) Erugudipati Gopalakrishnarao
(ii) Vanarasa Govinda Rao
(iii) Dharmavaram Ramakrishnamacharyulu
(iv) Kondubhatla Subramanyasastri

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
213.x: Surabhi was founded by Vanarasa Govinda Rao, Sarasa Vinodini Sabha by Dharmavaram Ramakrishnamacharyulu, Guntur Hindu Nataka Samajam by Kondubhatla Subramanyasastri, and Amateur Nataka Sabha by Erugudipati Gopalakrishnarao.
213.tq: Begin with the distinctive founder–company pairs and use elimination for the remaining combinations.
xs: Correct code: **a–ii, b–iii, c–iv, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Surabhi** — **Vanarasa Govinda Rao**; **Sarasa Vinodini Sabha** — **Dharmavaram Ramakrishnamacharyulu**.
**Hindu Nataka Samajam, Guntur** — **Kondubhatla Subramanyasastri**; **Amateur Nataka Sabha** (Nellore, **1896**) — **Erugudipati Gopalakrishnarao**.
xa: Kakinada Hindu Nataka Samajam (**1885**) — **Danavahi Hanumantharao**.
**Jaganmitra Samajam** (Vizag) — **Raja Ankitham Jaggara**.
**Hindu Natakajivaka Samajam** (Rajahmundry) — **Vaddadi Subbarayudu**; play **Venisamharam**.

213.s:
Consider the following statements about Surabhi theatre:
1. It was founded by Vanarasa Govinda Rao at Sorugu near Jammalamadugu in Kadapa.
2. Its first play was Venisamharam, staged at a landlord's wedding.
3. Its founding family were Tholu Bommalata (leather-puppet) performers who replaced puppets with live actors.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
213.x: Statement 1 is correct: Vanarasa Govinda Rao founded it at Sorugu (later renamed Surabhi), Kadapa. Statement 2 is wrong: its first play was Keechaka Vadham; Venisamharam is linked with Hindu Natakajivaka Samajam, Rajahmundry. Statement 3 is correct. So 1 and 3 only.
213.tq: Surabhi first play = Keechaka Vadham.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Vanarasa Govinda Rao**, **Sorugu** near **Jammalamadugu**, **Kadapa** (village later renamed Surabhi).
Statement 2 wrong: the first play was **Keechaka Vadham**; **Venisamharam** belongs to **Hindu Natakajivaka Samajam**.
Statement 3 correct: a **Tholu Bommalata** family replaced puppets with **live actors**.
xa: Surabhi is still a **family theatre** about **140 years** on.
Rayalaseema companies: **Surabhi** (Kadapa), **Rama Vilasa Sabha** (Chittoor).

213.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
213.x: Sarasa Vinodini Sabha was founded by Dharmavaram Ramakrishnamacharyulu at Bellary in 1886. The Guntur Hindu Nataka Samajam dates to 1880–81, Amateur Nataka Sabha to 1896, and Jaganmitra Samajam has no stated year here.
213.tq: Compare company, town and year as a three-part unit to detect a shifted date or location.
xs: **Sarasa Vinodini Sabha — Bellary — 1886** is correct — option **(2)**.
Guntur's **Hindu Nataka Samajam** is **1880-81**; **1885** is the Kakinada one.
**Amateur Nataka Sabha** (Nellore) is **1896**; **1889** is the Rajahmundry Samajam; **Jaganmitra Samajam** has no year in the notes.
xa: Sarasa Vinodini Sabha was founded by **Dharmavaram Ramakrishnamacharyulu**.
**Bellary** was an early base of Telugu theatre (then in the **Madras Presidency**).

213.s: Which event inspired the formation of Guntur’s Hindu Nataka Samajam and Nellore’s Lakshmi Vilasa Nataka Sabha?
o: The inauguration of Lalita Kala Parishad in 1956
The staging of Viplava Parivartanamu during the Non-Cooperation Movement
The first Mahasabha of Andhra Nataka Kala Parishad in 1929
The tour of the Marathi Darwada Nataka Samajam in 1880–81
213.x: The Marathi Darwada Nataka Samajam toured and pitched a tent at Rajamahendravaram in 1880–81, inspiring the two theatre organisations.
213.tq: Link the triggering event with the organisations it influenced rather than with later theatre milestones.
xs: The tour of the Marathi **Darwada Nataka Samajam** (tent at **Rajamahendravaram**, **1880-81**) inspired them — option **(4)**.
**Lalita Kala Parishad** (**1956**) and the **Andhra Nataka Kala Parishad** Mahasabha (**1929**) came much later.
**Viplava Parivartanamu** was banned during the **NCM**.
xa: Guntur's Hindu Nataka Samajam was founded by **Kondubhatla Subramanyasastri**.
Nellore's **Amateur Nataka Sabha** came in **1896**.

213.s: Which play was the first to be staged by the Surabhi theatre company, at a landlord's wedding?
213.x: Surabhi's first play was Keechaka Vadham, staged at a landlord's wedding by a family of Tholu Bommalata (leather-puppet) performers who replaced puppets with live actors. Venisamharam is linked with Hindu Natakajivaka Samajam, Rajahmundry; Gayopakhyanam is Chilakamarti's padya natakam; Kanyasulkam is Gurajada's social drama.
213.tq: Surabhi: puppeteer family turned live theatre; first play Keechaka Vadham.
xs: Surabhi's first play was **Keechaka Vadham**, staged at a landlord's wedding — option **(1)**.
**Venisamharam** belongs to **Hindu Natakajivaka Samajam**; **Gayopakhyanam** is Chilakamarti's padya natakam; **Kanyasulkam** is Gurajada's social drama.
xa: Surabhi was founded by **Vanarasa Govinda Rao** at **Sorugu** (Kadapa).
It marks the shift from **Tholu Bommalata** puppets to **live family theatre**.

213.s: Who was known by the title ‘Andhra Nataka Pitamaha’?
213.x: Dharmavaram Ramakrishnamacharyulu was known as Andhra Nataka Pitamaha, meaning ‘Grandfather of Andhra Drama’.
213.tq: Match the honorific title directly with the person who held it.
xs: "**Andhra Nataka Pitamaha**" (Grandfather of Andhra Drama) was **Dharmavaram Ramakrishnamacharyulu** — option **(1)**.
**Kolachalam Srinivasa Rao** was a Bellary writer of **historical plays**.
xa: Born **January 1853**, **Dharmavaram (Anantapur)**; died **30 November 1912**.
Wrote **30+ plays**; founded **Sarasa Vinodini Sabha** at **Bellary** (**1886**).
**Bellary Raghava** was his relative.

213.s: Kolachalam Srinivasa Rao of Bellary was known especially for writing:
o: Political pamphlets on the Non-Cooperation Movement
213.x: Kolachalam Srinivasa Rao was a Bellary playwright known for historical plays.
213.tq: Identify the playwright by his characteristic dramatic genre while rejecting absolute or unrelated descriptions.
xs: **Kolachalam Srinivasa Rao** was a **Bellary** playwright known for **historical plays** — option **(4)**.
Another historical play in the notes: **Prataparudriyam** by **Vedam Venkataraya Sastri**; dowry drama **Varavikrayam** is **Kallakuri's**.
xa: Bellary was an **early base** of Telugu theatre.
**Dharmavaram Ramakrishnamacharyulu** founded **Sarasa Vinodini Sabha** at Bellary.
**Bellary Raghava**, celebrated actor, has a Bellary theatre named after him.

213.s:
Consider the following statements about Lalita Kala Parishad, Anantapur:
1. It was inaugurated by the Governor.
2. The inauguration took place on 11 February 1956.
3. Land for it was donated by freedom fighter Kalluru Subbarao.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
213.x: All three statements are correct. Lalita Kala Parishad at Anantapur was inaugurated by the Governor on 11 February 1956, and its land was donated by freedom fighter Kalluru Subbarao.
213.tq: Check the inaugurating authority, exact date and donor as three separate components.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
**Lalita Kala Parishad, Anantapur** was **inaugurated by the Governor** on **11 February 1956**.
Its land was donated by freedom fighter **Kalluru Subbarao**.
xa: **Andhra Nataka Kala Parishad**: first Mahasabha **19-21 June 1929**, **Tenali**.
**Nandi Natakotsavams**: AP government's festival for **Telugu drama**.

213.s: Sthanam Narasimha Rao was particularly famous for portraying which of the following roles?
213.x: Sthanam Narasimha Rao was famed for female roles such as Madhuravani in Kanyasulkam and Satyabhama.
213.tq: Associate the stage actor with the characteristic roles for which the actor became famous.
xs: **Sthanam Narasimha Rao** was famed for female roles: **Madhuravani** (Kanyasulkam) and **Satyabhama** — option **(1)**.
**Kondubhatla** and **Danavahi** were founders of Hindu Nataka Samajams, not roles.
xa: **Bellary Raghava** — celebrated stage actor, relative of **Dharmavaram**.
**Tanguturi Prakasam** acted main roles for the Rajahmundry **Hindu Nataka Samajam**.

213.s: Who among the following acted in main roles for Hindu Nataka Samajam of Rajahmundry?
o: Bellary Raghava and Sthanam Narasimha Rao
213.x: Tanguturi Prakasam and Durga Gopalakrishnayya acted main roles for the Hindu Nataka Samajam at Rajahmundry.
213.tq: Match the performers with the theatre company rather than with their unrelated public identities.
xs: **Tanguturi Prakasam and Durga Gopalakrishnayya** acted main roles for Rajahmundry's Hindu Nataka Samajam — option **(1)**.
**Kalluru Subbarao** donated land for **Lalita Kala Parishad**; **Bellary Raghava** and **Sthanam Narasimha Rao** were other actors.
xa: The Rajahmundry Samajam (**1889**) staged plays by **Chilakamarti** and **Toleti Venkata Subbarao**.
Founder: **Immani Hanumantharao**.

213.s: Bellary Raghava was related to which theatre personality?
213.x: Bellary Raghava, the celebrated stage actor, was a relative of Dharmavaram Ramakrishnamacharyulu. A Bellary theatre is named after Bellary Raghava.
213.tq: Identify the family relationship instead of confusing a celebrated actor with a theatre-company founder.
xs: **Bellary Raghava** was a relative of **Dharmavaram Ramakrishnamacharyulu** — option **(2)**.
A **Bellary theatre** is named after him.
xa: Dharmavaram is the "**Andhra Nataka Pitamaha**"; founded **Sarasa Vinodini Sabha** (**1886**).
**Vanarasa Govinda Rao** founded **Surabhi**; **Erugudipati Gopalakrishnarao** the **Amateur Nataka Sabha**.

213.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
213.x: Chintamani was written by Kallakuri Narayana Rao. Vedam Venkataraya Sastri wrote Prataparudriyam, a historical play on Prataparudra.
213.tq: Find the incorrectly matched author while keeping the closely related playwright names separate.
xs: **Chintamani — Vedam Venkataraya Sastri** is wrongly matched — option **(1)**.
**Chintamani** is by **Kallakuri Narayana Rao**; Vedam wrote **Prataparudriyam** (historical, on Prataparudra).
**Gayopakhyanam** — **Chilakamarti**; **Varavikrayam** — **Kallakuri** (against dowry): correct.
xa: Chilakamarti also wrote **Prahlada Charitamu** (mythological).
**Kuliraju** — **Boyi Bhimanna** (social drama).

213.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Kanyasulkam attacks the practice of bride-price.
2. Kanyasulkam was written in spoken Telugu.
3. Varavikrayam was written against dowry.
4. Prataparudriyam is a historical play on Prataparudra.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
213.x: All four statements are correct. Kanyasulkam attacks bride-price and uses spoken Telugu, Varavikrayam opposes dowry, and Prataparudriyam deals with Prataparudra historically.
213.tq: Check each statement against the play’s theme, language and genre before selecting the complete combination.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Kanyasulkam** attacks **bride-price** and is written in **spoken Telugu**.
**Varavikrayam** is against **dowry**; **Prataparudriyam** is a historical play on **Prataparudra**.
xa: Kanyasulkam — **Gurajada Apparao**; Varavikrayam — **Kallakuri Narayana Rao**.
Prataparudriyam — **Vedam Venkataraya Sastri**.

213.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Padya natakam and social drama:
1. Padya natakam generally deals with mythological or epic themes.
2. Social drama addresses contemporary social evils such as bride-price, dowry and widowhood.
3. Padya natakam is generally presented in prose using spoken Telugu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
213.x: Padya natakam deals mainly with mythological or epic themes, whereas social drama focuses on contemporary social evils. Padya natakam uses sung verse rather than prose in spoken Telugu.
213.tq: Split the statements by comparing the subject matter and language of the two dramatic forms.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **padya natakam** is **mythological or epic**.
Statement 2 correct: **social drama** targets **bride-price, dowry, widowhood**.
Statement 3 wrong: padya natakam uses **sung verse (padyam)**; prose in **vyavaharika bhasha** is the social drama.
xa: Padya natakam examples: **Keechaka Vadham**, **Gayopakhyanam**, **Prahlada Charitamu**.
Social drama examples: **Kanyasulkam**, **Vyavahara Dharmabodhini**, **Varavikrayam**.

213.s:
With reference to Telugu dramatic literature, consider the following pairs:

List-I (Work or repertoire)
 a. Surabhi repertoire
 b. Gayopakhyanam
 c. Kanyasulkam
 d. Varavikrayam

List-II (Dramatic category)
 i. Social drama
 ii. Padya natakam

Which of the following is the correct classification?
213.x: Surabhi repertoire and Gayopakhyanam are associated with Padya natakam. Kanyasulkam and Varavikrayam are examples of social drama.
213.tq: Start from the sure pair: Kanyasulkam is a social drama, then eliminate codes containing a wrong classification.
xs: Correct classification: **a–ii, b–ii, c–i, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Surabhi repertoire** and **Gayopakhyanam** are **padya natakam**.
**Kanyasulkam** and **Varavikrayam** are **social drama**.
xa: **Padya natakam**: dialogue mainly in **verse**, mythological or epic content.
**Vyavahara Dharmabodhini** (**Veeresalingam**) is also a social drama.

213.s: Which of the following statements best describes the contribution of Gurajada to Telugu dramatic writing?
o: He restricted social drama to mythological themes and epic narratives.
He replaced live theatre with Tholu Bommalata puppetry.
He made spoken Telugu the norm for writing, thereby widening the audience.
He made sung verse the compulsory medium of all Telugu dramas.
213.x: Gurajada made spoken Telugu the norm for writing. This widened the audience for Telugu dramatic literature.
213.tq: Identify the precise contribution rather than choosing an option that reverses the language and audience relationship.
xs: **Gurajada** made **spoken Telugu** the norm for writing, **widening the audience** — option **(3)**.
His **Kanyasulkam** attacks **bride-price** in spoken Telugu.
**Surabhi** replaced puppets with live actors, the reverse of option (2).
xa: Social drama uses prose in **vyavaharika bhasha**.
Kanyasulkam — Gurajada was an **APPSC 2024** key pair.

213.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Padya Natakam?
o: A modern television drama festival conducted by the AP Government
A puppet theatre performed without any human actors
A form of Telugu theatre in which dialogue is mainly in verse
213.x: Padya Natakam is classical Telugu theatre in which the dialogue is mainly presented in verse.
213.tq: Identify the exact defining feature instead of choosing an associated theatre institution.
xs: **Padya Natakam** is classical Telugu theatre with **dialogue mainly in verse** — option **(4)**.
**Nandi Natakotsavams** are the AP government's theatre festival; puppet theatre is **Tholu Bommalata**.
xa: Its content is **mythological or epic** (**Keechaka Vadham**, **Gayopakhyanam**).
**Surabhi's** repertoire is padya natakam.

213.s:
Match List-I (Play) with List-II (Playwright):

List-I
a. Vyavahara Dharmabodhini
b. Kanyasulkam
c. Kuliraju
d. Prahlada Charitamu

List-II
i. Boyi Bhimanna
ii. Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham
iii. Kandukuri Veeresalingam
iv. Gurajada Apparao

Select the correct code:
213.x: As per the APPSC 2024 key: Vyavahara Dharmabodhini is Veeresalingam's reformist drama, Kanyasulkam is Gurajada's attack on bride-price, Kuliraju is Boyi Bhimanna's social drama, and Prahlada Charitamu is Chilakamarti's mythological play. Option B swaps Veeresalingam and Gurajada, C swaps Bhimanna and Chilakamarti, and D swaps Veeresalingam and Chilakamarti.
213.tq: Reform = Veeresalingam; bride-price = Gurajada; Kuliraju = Bhimanna; Prahlada = Chilakamarti.
xs: Correct code: **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — option **(1)** (**APPSC 2024** key).
**Vyavahara Dharmabodhini** — **Kandukuri Veeresalingam**; **Kanyasulkam** — **Gurajada Apparao**.
**Kuliraju** — **Boyi Bhimanna**; **Prahlada Charitamu** — **Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham**.
xa: Exam angle: **four-pair** play-author matching (**APPSC 2024, 2025**).
**Varavikrayam** and **Chintamani** — **Kallakuri Narayana Rao**.

213.s: Which of the following statements regarding the early role of drama companies is correct?
o: They carried social-reform themes before they carried nationalist themes.
They confined their performances exclusively to mythological subjects.
They avoided the public presentation of social issues.
They first carried nationalist themes and later adopted social reform themes.
213.x: Drama companies initially carried social-reform themes, including Kanyasulkam and Veeresalingam’s drama, before taking up nationalist themes.
213.tq: Watch for the reversed sequence trap in statements comparing reformist and nationalist themes.
xs: Drama companies carried **social-reform themes before nationalist ones** — option **(1)**.
Examples: **Kanyasulkam** and **Veeresalingam's** drama.
xa: In the **Swadeshi & NCM** years, troupes like **Jatiya Nataka Rangam** promoted swadeshi goods and national education.
Drama companies were the **main mass entertainment** of the time.

213.s: During which movement was the drama Viplava Parivartanamu published and banned?
213.x: Viplava Parivartanamu was published and banned during the Non-Cooperation Movement.
213.tq: Separate the movement associated with the banned play from other major phases of the freedom struggle.
xs: **Viplava Parivartanamu** was published and **banned during the Non-Cooperation Movement** — option **(2)**.
Exam angle: "banned during which movement" plus "who wrote it".
xa: ⚠ Author: **Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri** (**G2 2019** key) vs **Kodali Anjaneyulu** (**2018** key).
Officials watched troupes as a play reached **thousands of illiterate people in one evening**.

213.s: Why did colonial officials closely watch theatre troupes during the freedom movement?
o: A drama company could present a political idea to thousands of illiterate people in one evening.
The troupes controlled the distribution of imported goods.
The troupes were responsible for conducting elections in villages.
A drama company could legally replace the colonial administration.
213.x: Theatre could communicate political ideas before thousands of illiterate people in a single evening, making drama companies an influential medium of nationalist mobilisation.
213.tq: Apply the communication function of theatre to identify why the colonial government regarded troupes as influential.
xs: A drama company could put a political idea before **thousands of illiterate people in one evening** — option **(1)**.
So colonial officials **watched troupes closely**.
xa: **Viplava Parivartanamu** was **banned during the NCM**.
**Jatiya Nataka Rangam** promoted **swadeshi goods** and **national education**.

213.s: Which of the following statements about Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri is correct?
o: He inaugurated Lalita Kala Parishad in 1956.
He wrote Prataparudriyam as a historical play on Prataparudra.
He supported the Non-Cooperation Movement boycott of elections in 1920.
213.x: Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri was among the Andhra leaders who supported the Non-Cooperation Movement boycott of elections in 1920.
213.tq: Match the political activity with the correct individual instead of transferring a theatrical achievement to him.
xs: **Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri** supported the **NCM boycott of elections in 1920** — option **(4)**.
**Lalita Kala Parishad** was inaugurated by the **Governor**; **Prataparudriyam** is **Vedam Venkataraya Sastri's**; **Surabhi** was founded by **Vanarasa Govinda Rao**.
xa: The **G2 2019** key names him author of **Viplava Parivartanamu**.
⚠ The **2018** key names **Kodali Anjaneyulu** instead.

213.s: According to the APPSC Group 2 2019 answer key, who wrote the drama Viplava Parivartanamu, which was banned during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
213.x: The APPSC G2 2019 key gives Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri; the APPSC 2018 key gives Kodali Anjaneyulu, so learn both names with this play. Dharmavaram Ramakrishnamacharyulu was the Andhra Nataka Pitamaha, Kallakuri Narayana Rao wrote Varavikrayam and Padmavyuham, and Kolachalam Srinivasa Rao was a Bellary writer of historical plays.
213.tq: Viplava Parivartanamu: Gollapudi (2019 key) / Kodali Anjaneyulu (2018 key); banned in NCM.
xs: The **APPSC G2 2019** key gives **Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri** as author of **Viplava Parivartanamu** — option **(1)**.
⚠ The **APPSC 2018** key gives **Kodali Anjaneyulu** — learn both names.
**Dharmavaram** is the **Andhra Nataka Pitamaha**; **Kallakuri** wrote **Varavikrayam**; **Kolachalam** wrote **historical plays**.
xa: The play was **banned during the NCM**.
Gollapudi supported the **NCM boycott of elections in 1920**.

213.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Nataka Kala Parishad:
1. Its first Mahasabha was held at Tenali from 19 to 21 June 1929.
2. Kothapalli Lakshmayya served as secretary up to 1943.
3. Its magazine was titled Natya Kala and began in 1937.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
213.x: All three statements are correct: the first Mahasabha was held at Tenali on 19–21 June 1929, Kothapalli Lakshmayya was secretary up to 1943, and Natya Kala was published from 1937.
213.tq: Verify the place, date range, office-holder and publication year as separate factual elements.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
First Mahasabha of **Andhra Nataka Kala Parishad**: **19-21 June 1929**, **Tenali**.
Secretary **Kothapalli Lakshmayya** (to **1943**); magazine **Natya Kala** (**1937**).
xa: **Lalita Kala Parishad, Anantapur**: inaugurated **11 February 1956**.
Tenali companies: **Sri Rama Vilasa Sabha**, **Sri Krishna Hindu Theatre**.

213.s: Nandi Natakotsavams are organised by the Government of Andhra Pradesh primarily as a festival for which field?
213.x: Nandi Natakotsavams are the Andhra Pradesh Government's theatre festival for Telugu drama, new playwrights and artists.
213.tq: Match the festival with its field and its support for new theatre talent.
xs: **Nandi Natakotsavams** are the AP government's festival for **Telugu drama and theatre** — option **(1)**.
They encourage **new playwrights and artists**.
xa: **Nataka Vidyalayam, Vijayawada** (**1 August 1964**) trained students in dramatic arts.
**Andhra Nataka Kala Parishad** held its first Mahasabha at **Tenali** (**1929**).

213.s: Drama companies in the nineteenth and early twentieth-century social setting became effective vehicles for reform and nationalist messages mainly because they were
o: restricted to court performances for rulers and officials
limited to performances of religious rituals
the main form of mass entertainment of the time
213.x: Drama companies were the main mass entertainment of the time. Their wide reach enabled them to communicate reformist and nationalist messages to the public.
213.tq: Link the social reach of an institution with its effectiveness as a vehicle for public messages.
xs: Drama companies were **the main mass entertainment** of the time — option **(3)**.
So they became a **vehicle for reform and nationalist messages**.
xa: They reached **thousands of illiterate people in one evening**.
They carried **social-reform themes** before nationalist ones.

213.s: Surabhi is regarded as marking which transition in the history of Telugu theatre?
o: From social drama to epic poetry
From sung verse to spoken prose only
From Tholu Bommalata puppets to live Telugu family theatre
From nationalist theatre to court-sponsored performances
213.x: Surabhi marks the shift from Tholu Bommalata puppets to live Telugu family theatre. This transition is central to its significance in Telugu theatrical culture.
213.tq: Identify the first-to-last transition by matching the earlier puppetry form with the later live family theatre form.
xs: **Surabhi** marks the shift **from Tholu Bommalata puppets to live Telugu family theatre** — option **(3)**.
A **leather-puppet** family replaced puppets with **live actors**.
xa: First play: **Keechaka Vadham**, at a landlord's wedding.
Founder **Vanarasa Govinda Rao**, **Sorugu** near **Jammalamadugu** (Kadapa).

213.s: Nataka Vidyalayam, which trained students in the dramatic arts, was started at which place and on which date?
213.x: Nataka Vidyalayam was started at Vijayawada on 1 August 1964 and trained students in the dramatic arts.
213.tq: Combine the location and date, avoiding distractors formed by swapping the place or date.
xs: **Nataka Vidyalayam** was started at **Vijayawada** on **1 August 1964** — option **(2)**.
It **trained students in dramatic arts**.
xa: **Surabhi** still survives as a **family theatre**.
**Lalita Kala Parishad, Anantapur** was inaugurated on **11 February 1956**.

213.s: Which one of the following statements about Surabhi is correct?
o: Surabhi is a social drama written in prose by Gurajada.
Surabhi was a training institution established at Vijayawada in 1964.
Surabhi refers exclusively to Tholu Bommalata puppetry.
Surabhi is a family theatre tradition that still survives.
213.x: Surabhi continues as a family theatre tradition. It is distinct from Nataka Vidyalayam and is associated with live Telugu theatre.
213.tq: Distinguish the surviving theatre tradition from the training institution and the earlier puppetry form.
xs: **Surabhi** is a **family theatre** tradition that **still survives** — option **(4)**.
It is not a Gurajada drama, and the **Vijayawada (1964)** institution is **Nataka Vidyalayam**.
It **replaced** Tholu Bommalata puppets with live actors, so it is not puppetry.
xa: Still a family theatre about **140 years** on.
Rayalaseema companies: **Surabhi** (Kadapa), **Rama Vilasa Sabha** (Chittoor).

214.s: Who founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha at Madras in 1938?
214.x: The Andhra Mahila Sabha at Madras was founded by Durgabai Deshmukh in 1938.
214.tq: Use direct founder–organisation recall and distinguish the founder from other prominent women leaders.
xs: The **Andhra Mahila Sabha** (Madras, **1938**) was founded by **Durgabai Deshmukh** — option **(3)** (**APPSC 2023** key).
Not **Sarojini Naidu** or **Duvvuri Subbamma**, the usual distractors.
**Unnava Lakshmibayamma** ran **Sri Sarada Niketanam** at Guntur.
xa: The **Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha** ran **parallel** Andhra Mahila Sabha conferences, e.g. **1931 Devarakonda**.
Durgabai later got the **Padma Vibhushan (1975)**.
First chairperson of the **Central Social Welfare Board** (**1953**).

214.s: Desasevikalu was associated with which of the following?
o: The women's Gurukulam at Guntur founded in 1922
The women's wing inside the Congress during the Non-Cooperation Movement period
A women's education journal founded in 1894
214.x: Desasevikalu functioned as the women's wing inside the Congress during the Non-Cooperation Movement period.
214.tq: Discriminate between a political organisation, a journal and an educational institution by function.
xs: **Desasevikalu** was the **women's wing inside Congress** in the **NCM** period — option **(3)**.
The **1922** Gurukulam is **Sarada Niketanam**; the **1894** education journal is **Zenana Patrika**.
xa: **Sati Hitabodhini** (**1883**) and **Zenana Patrika** were founded by **Kandukuri Veeresalingam**.
**Andhra Mahila Sabha** (Madras, **1938**) — **Durgabai Deshmukh**.

214.s:
With reference to the parallel Andhra Mahila Sabha conferences conducted by the Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha, consider the following statements:
1. A conference was held at Devarakonda in 1931.
2. The Devarakonda conference was presided over by T. Varalakshmamma.
3. These conferences were conducted by the Andhra Mahila Sabha founded at Madras in 1938.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
214.x: The Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha conducted parallel Andhra Mahila Sabha conferences, including one at Devarakonda in 1931 under the presidency of T. Varalakshmamma. Statement 3 is false because the 1938 Madras organisation was a separate Andhra Mahila Sabha founded by Durgabai Deshmukh.
214.tq: Separate similarly named organisations by their sponsoring body, place and year.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)**.
Statements 1 and 2 correct: the Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha held a conference at **Devarakonda** in **1931**, presided by **T. Varalakshmamma**.
Statement 3 wrong: these were **parallel** conferences; the Madras **Andhra Mahila Sabha** (**1938**) was Durgabai Deshmukh's.
xa: Exam angle: Andhra Mahila Sabha founder = **Durgabai Deshmukh** (**APPSC 2023, 2024**).
**Sri Sarada Niketanam** monthly — **Unnava Lakshmibayamma**.

214.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Sri Sarada Niketanam monthly - Durgabai Deshmukh
214.x: Kandukuri Veeresalingam founded Sati Hitabodhini (1883) and Zenana Patrika (1894, for women's education). The Sri Sarada Niketanam monthly was Unnava Lakshmibayamma's, not Durgabai's; Sati Hitabodhini was Veeresalingam's, not Lakshmibayamma's; and the Andhra Mahila Sabha at Madras (1938) was founded by Durgabai Deshmukh, not Duvvuri Subbamma.
214.tq: Veeresalingam = Sati Hitabodhini 1883 + Zenana Patrika 1894.
xs: **Zenana Patrika — Kandukuri Veeresalingam** is correct — option **(1)**; it was for **women's education** (**1894**).
**Sri Sarada Niketanam** monthly was **Unnava Lakshmibayamma's**; **Sati Hitabodhini** (**1883**) was **Veeresalingam's**.
The **Andhra Mahila Sabha** was **Durgabai Deshmukh's**, not Duvvuri Subbamma's.
xa: **Desasevikalu** — women's wing inside Congress in the **NCM** period.
Parallel conference at **Devarakonda** (**1931**) — **T. Varalakshmamma** presided.

214.s: Sarada Niketanam at Guntur was founded in:
214.x: Sarada Niketanam was founded as a women's Gurukulam in 1922. It developed from the couple's widow asylum established in 1902.
214.tq: Separate the institution's founding year from the earlier institution that preceded it.
xs: **Sarada Niketanam** (women's Gurukulam) was founded in **1922** — option **(3)**.
**1902** is the year of the couple's **widow asylum**, which later merged into it.
**1938** is the **Andhra Mahila Sabha** (Durgabai).
xa: Founders: **Unnava Lakshminarayana** and wife **Unnava Lakshmibayamma**.
It sheltered **widows and destitute girls** and became a "**hotbed**" of the freedom movement.

214.s: Who founded Sarada Niketanam at Guntur?
o: Unnava Lakshminarayana with his wife Unnava Lakshmibayamma
T. Prakasam with K. Nageswara Rao
214.x: Sarada Niketanam was founded by Unnava Lakshminarayana together with his wife Unnava Lakshmibayamma.
214.tq: Use the founder-couple association and avoid substituting better-known reformers.
xs: **Unnava Lakshminarayana with wife Unnava Lakshmibayamma** founded **Sarada Niketanam** — option **(1)**.
The **APPSC G2 2019** key names **Unnava Lakshminarayana**.
**Veeresalingam** founded **Sati Hitabodhini** and **Zenana Patrika**, not Sarada Niketanam.
xa: Women's Gurukulam founded in **1922**; the **1902** widow asylum merged into it.
In **1902** she held the **first widow remarriage** at the asylum.

214.s:
Consider the following statements about Sarada Niketanam:
1. It was a women's Gurukulam.
2. It sheltered widows and destitute girls and provided education to girls.
3. It became a centre associated with the freedom movement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
214.x: All three statements are correct. Sarada Niketanam was a women's Gurukulam that sheltered and educated vulnerable girls and became a hotbed of the freedom movement.
214.tq: When all statements describe connected functions of an institution, verify each before selecting the comprehensive option.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
**Sarada Niketanam** was a **women's Gurukulam** (**1922**).
It **sheltered widows and destitute girls** and **taught girls**.
It was a "**hotbed**" of the freedom movement.
xa: The **1902** widow asylum later merged into it.
Lakshmibayamma took **personal responsibility** for Guntur women's part in all Congress movements.

214.s: What significant event took place at the widow asylum run by Unnava Lakshmibayamma in 1902?
o: The first widow remarriage was held there
The Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha held its Devarakonda conference there
The Andhra Mahila Sabha was founded there
214.x: In 1902, Unnava Lakshmibayamma ran the widow asylum and held the first widow remarriage there.
214.tq: Associate the reformer with the specific social-reform event rather than a later nationalist activity.
xs: In **1902**, Lakshmibayamma held the **first widow remarriage** at the widow asylum — option **(2)**.
The **Devarakonda** conference (**1931**) belonged to the Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha.
xa: The asylum later merged into the women's **Gurukulam** (**1922**).
The couple: **Unnava Lakshminarayana** and **Unnava Lakshmibayamma**.

214.s: Why did Unnava Lakshmibayamma lead the Guntur hartals during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
o: Her husband was arrested in connection with the Palnadu forest, or pullari, satyagraha
She was arrested for making salt at Chollangi
Her school was closed during the Quit India Movement
She was presiding over the Devarakonda conference
214.x: She led the Guntur hartals after her husband was arrested over the Palnadu forest, or pullari, satyagraha.
214.tq: Infer the immediate cause of a protest from the person arrested and the movement involved.
xs: She led the **Guntur hartals** after her **husband's arrest** over the **Palnadu forest (pullari) satyagraha** — option **(1)**.
**Chollangi** salt-making was **Duvvuri Subbamma's**; **Devarakonda** was presided by **T. Varalakshmamma**.
xa: The Palnadu forest satyagraha saw **8 women** arrested with **28** men.
On **9 April 1930** she led women in **Krishna and Guntur** in the Salt Satyagraha.

214.s: On 9 April 1930, Unnava Lakshmibayamma led women in the Salt Satyagraha in:

xs: **Konda Venkatappayya** was appointed **Dictator** of the Andhra Salt Satyagraha — option **(1)** (**APPSC G2 2008** key).
**Prakasam** earned "**Andhra Kesari**" in the **Simon boycott**; **Sambamurthy** toured Andhra against Simon and became **Speaker** (**1937**).
**Pattabhi** founded **Andhra Bank** (**1923**).
xa: Konda was jailed in **1930, 1932 and 1942**.
He opposed the NC resolution at the **Calcutta special session (1920)**.

215.s:
Consider the following statements about Konda Venkatappayya:
1. He co-founded Krishna Patrika (1902) with Dasu Narayana Rao and was its first editor.
2. At the Calcutta special session (1920), he supported the Non-Cooperation resolution.
3. He presided over the fifth Andhra Mahasabha session at Nellore (1917).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
215.x: Statement 1 is correct: he co-founded Krishna Patrika in 1902 and was its first editor. Statement 2 is wrong: he opposed the Non-Cooperation resolution at Calcutta (it passed 1,886-884). Statement 3 is correct: he presided over the 5th session at Nellore in 1917. So '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' misses statement 3, and options with 2 are wrong.
215.tq: Konda: Krishna Patrika 1902; opposed NCM at Calcutta 1920; CDM Dictator.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: co-founded **Krishna Patrika** (**1902**) with **Dasu Narayana Rao**; first editor.
Statement 2 wrong: at **Calcutta (1920)** he **opposed** the NC resolution (passed **1,886-884**).
Statement 3 correct: **President**, 5th Andhra Mahasabha, **Nellore (1917)**.
xa: He was **Secretary** of the first session at **Bapatla (1913)**.
Title: "**Desabhakta**".

215.s: Tanguturi Prakasam earned the title ‘Andhra Kesari’ in connection with which event?
o: The Vande Mataram agitation at Osmania University
The Simon Go Back protest at Madras in 1928
215.x: Tanguturi Prakasam came to be known as Andhra Kesari for his role in the Simon Go Back protest at Madras in 1928.
215.tq: Connect a title with the specific event that earned it, not merely with the person’s general career.
xs: Prakasam became "**Andhra Kesari**" in the **Simon Go Back** protest at **Madras** (**February 1928**) — option **(4)**.
He **defied police firing** during the boycott — not QIM or NCM (**G2 2008** and **2019** keys).
xa: Simon Commission: appointed **November 1927**, arrived **3 February 1928**.
**Bulusu Sambamurthy** toured Andhra calling for its boycott.
⚠ Some notes date Prakasam's protest **1927**.

215.s: Tanguturi Prakasam was born on 23 August 1872 at:
215.x: Tanguturi Prakasam was born on 23 August 1872 at Vinodarayunipalem, in the area now forming Prakasam district.
215.tq: Resolve a misleading alternative by checking both the year and birthplace together.
xs: **Tanguturi Prakasam** was born on **23 August 1872** at **Vinodarayunipalem** (present Prakasam district) — option **(4)**.
⚠ "**1892, Valluru**" is a known wrong option.
**Bhatlapenumarru** is **Pingali Venkayya's** birthplace.
xa: **Prakasam district** is named after him.
He was the **first CM of Andhra State**.

215.s: In 1951, Tanguturi Prakasam left the Congress along with N. G. Ranga and founded the:
215.x: In 1951, Tanguturi Prakasam left the Congress with N. G. Ranga and founded the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party. It later became associated with the Praja Socialist Party.
215.tq: Distinguish the party founded initially from the later political formation.
xs: In **1951** Prakasam left Congress with **N.G. Ranga** and founded the **Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party** — option **(3)**.
It was **later** the **Praja Socialist Party**, so option (2) is wrong.
xa: Prakasam was President of the Andhra Congress Committee **18 times**.
He was **Revenue Minister** in the **Rajaji** ministry (**1937**).

215.s: Tanguturi Prakasam was a coastal signatory to the Sribagh Pact concluded on:
215.x: Tanguturi Prakasam was a coastal signatory to the Sribagh Pact, concluded on 16 November 1937.
215.tq: Match the agreement with its exact date rather than with dates of related movements.
xs: The **Sribagh Pact** was signed on **16 November 1937** — option **(4)**.
Coastal signatories in this topic: **Tanguturi Prakasam** and **Bulusu Sambamurthy**.
**31 Mar 1921** is the **Vijayawada AICC**; **28 Mar 1955** is when **Bezawada Gopal Reddy** became CM.
xa: ⚠ Sribagh Pact = two coastal signatories here: **Prakasam** and **Sambamurthy**.
These leaders steered Andhra through **NCM, CDM, Simon boycott, Sribagh Pact** and **statehood**.

215.s: Swarajya, founded by Tanguturi Prakasam in 1921, was primarily a(n):
o: magazine edited by Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao
215.x: Prakasam's Swarajya (1921) was an English daily (APPSC 2011 key; some sources add Telugu and Tamil editions). Grama Swarajya was his separate weekly; Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao's Swarajya was a different magazine (a known trap); kisan publications from Nidubrolu were N.G. Ranga's.
215.tq: Prakasam's Swarajya = English daily (1921); don't confuse with Gadicherla's Swarajya.
xs: Prakasam's **Swarajya** (**1921**) was an **English daily** — option **(1)** (**APPSC 2011** key).
**Grama Swarajya** was his separate **weekly**.
⚠ **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao's** "Swarajya" was a different magazine.
xa: Some notes say Swarajya came in **English, Telugu and Tamil**.
**Krishna Patrika** (**1902**) — **Konda Venkatappayya** with **Dasu Narayana Rao**.

215.s:
Consider the following statements about Pingali Venkayya:
1. He was born in 1876 at Bhatlapenumarru near Machilipatnam.
2. He published his book on national-flag designs in 1921.
3. He served in South Africa during the Boer War.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
215.x: Statement 1 is correct: he was born on 2 August 1876 at Bhatlapenumarru near Machilipatnam. Statement 2 is wrong: the book on national-flag designs came out in 1916; 1921 is when he showed the flag to Gandhi at the Vijayawada AICC meeting. Statement 3 is correct: he served in the Boer War. So '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' misses statement 3, and options with 2 include the false date.
215.tq: 1916 = book; 1921 = flag shown to Gandhi at Vijayawada.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: born **2 August 1876** at **Bhatlapenumarru** near **Machilipatnam**.
Statement 2 wrong: his book on flag designs came in **1916**; **1921** is when he showed the flag to Gandhi.
Statement 3 correct: he served in South Africa in the **Boer War**.
xa: His tricolour was later adopted, with minor changes, as the **National Flag** (**G2 2019** key).
Nicknames: **Patti**, **Japan**, **Diamond Venkayya**.

215.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Pingali Venkayya is correctly matched?
o: Study of cotton varieties — Patti Venkayya
Study of national flags — Patti Venkayya
215.x: Pingali Venkayya was known as ‘Patti Venkayya’ for his study of cotton varieties. His study of Japanese led to the name ‘Japan Venkayya’, and his interest in diamonds led to ‘Diamond Venkayya’.
215.tq: Discriminate among aliases derived from different areas of study.
xs: **Cotton varieties — "Patti Venkayya"** — option **(1)**.
**Japanese** → "**Japan Venkayya**"; **diamonds** → "**Diamond Venkayya**".
His study of national flags led to a **book (1916)**, not "Patti".
xa: Pingali showed his flag to **Gandhi** at the **Vijayawada AICC** (**1921**).
Born **2 August 1876**, **Bhatlapenumarru**.

215.s: Pingali Venkayya showed his design of the national flag to Gandhi at which meeting?
215.x: He showed the flag to Gandhi at the Vijayawada AICC meeting (31 Mar - 1 Apr 1921), held at a venue named Gandhi Nagar; the tricolour was later adopted with minor changes as the National Flag (APPSC G2 2019 key). Kakinada 1923 had Bulusu Sambamurthy as Reception Committee chairman, Calcutta 1920 passed the Non-Cooperation resolution, and Tripuri 1939 saw Bose defeat Pattabhi.
215.tq: Pingali flag: Vijayawada AICC, 1921.
xs: Pingali showed his flag to Gandhi at the **Vijayawada AICC** (**31 Mar - 1 Apr 1921**) — option **(1)**.
The venue was named "**Gandhi Nagar**".
**Kakinada 1923** — Sambamurthy's Reception Committee; **Calcutta 1920** — NC resolution; **Tripuri 1939** — **Bose** beat Pattabhi.
xa: **Bulusu Sambamurthy** also attended the Vijayawada meeting.
The tricolour was adopted with **minor changes** as the National Flag.

215.s: Who chaired the Reception Committee of the Indian National Congress session held at Kakinada in 1923?
215.x: Bulusu Sambamurthy was the Chairman of the Reception Committee of the Kakinada Congress session held in 1923.
215.tq: Use the post-person association and distinguish a session organiser from a Congress president.
xs: **Bulusu Sambamurthy** chaired the Reception Committee of the **Kakinada INC session** (**1923**) — option **(3)**.
**Pattabhi** presided at **Jaipur (1948)**; **Konda** was **AICC Secretary (1923)**.
xa: Sambamurthy's title: "**Maharshi**" (ascetic Gandhian life).
He became **Speaker, Madras Legislative Assembly (1937)**.

215.s: Bulusu Sambamurthy toured the whole of Andhra primarily to mobilise public support for which of the following?
o: Boycott of the Round Table Conference
Acceptance of the Cabinet Mission Plan
215.x: Bulusu Sambamurthy toured Andhra calling for a boycott of the Simon Commission.
215.tq: Match the leader with the specific nationalist campaign rather than a similar constitutional event.
xs: Sambamurthy toured all Andhra for a **boycott of the Simon Commission** — option **(3)**.
**Prakasam** led the boycott in **Madras**.
xa: Simon Commission arrived **3 February 1928**.
Sambamurthy earlier supported the **NCM election boycott (1920)**.

215.s: Bulusu Sambamurthy held which constitutional office in 1937?
o: Speaker of the Andhra Legislative Assembly
Leader of the Legislative Council of Madras
President of the Madras Congress Committee
215.x: Bulusu Sambamurthy became the Speaker of the Madras Assembly in 1937.
215.tq: Identify the correct legislative body and avoid substituting an Andhra provincial institution for the Madras Assembly.
xs: In **1937** Sambamurthy became **Speaker of the Madras Legislative Assembly** — option **(4)**.
As Speaker he declared **Andhra state** must be formed **before** the Constitution came into force.
xa: **Prakasam** was **Revenue Minister** in the same **Rajaji** ministry (**1937**).
**Pattabhi** was **APCC President** in **1937**.

215.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the position taken by Bulusu Sambamurthy regarding the Andhra State?
o: The Andhra State must be formed before the Constitution came into force.
The formation of Andhra State should be postponed until after independence.
The Andhra State should be formed only after the Constitution came into force.
The Andhra State should be formed only after the linguistic reorganisation of all provinces.
215.x: As Speaker of the Madras Assembly, Sambamurthy declared that Andhra State must be formed before the Constitution came into force.
215.tq: Focus on the time condition in the statement; the constitutional deadline is the decisive clue.
xs: Sambamurthy declared that **Andhra state must be formed before the Constitution came into force** — option **(1)**.
He said this as **Speaker** (**1937**).
xa: **Pattabhi** wrote in **The Hindu** on the need for **linguistic states**.
The **JVP Committee** first **rejected** linguistic states.

215.s:
Arrange the following events associated with Bulusu Sambamurthy in chronological order:
A. Attendance at the Vijayawada AICC meeting
B. Support for the Non-Cooperation Movement election boycott
C. Chairmanship of the Kakinada Congress Reception Committee
D. Speakership of the Madras Assembly
215.x: The correct order is the 1920 election boycott, the 1921 Vijayawada AICC meeting, the 1923 Kakinada session and the 1937 speakership.
215.tq: Fix the dated events first and then arrange the intervening Congress activities.
xs: Correct order: **B, A, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**NCM election boycott (1920)** → **Vijayawada AICC (1921)**.
→ **Kakinada Reception Committee (1923)** → **Speaker (1937)**.
xa: He also toured Andhra for the **Simon boycott** (**1928**).
He signed the **Sribagh Pact** (**16 Nov 1937**).

215.s: In the Tripuri Congress presidential contest of 1939, Pattabhi Sitaramayya was the candidate supported by whom?
215.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya contested the 1939 Tripuri presidential election as Gandhi's candidate and was defeated by Subhas Chandra Bose.
215.tq: Use the candidate-supporter pairing, a common leader-and-deed trap in history questions.
xs: At **Tripuri (1939)** Pattabhi was **Gandhi's candidate** — option **(3)**.
He was **defeated by Subhas Chandra Bose**; Gandhi called it **his own defeat**.
xa: Pattabhi later presided over the **Jaipur session (1948)**.
He wrote **History of the Indian National Congress** (**1935**).

215.s: What was the initial position of the JVP Committee on the creation of linguistic States?
o: It rejected the idea of linguistic States at the initial stage.
It transferred the decision exclusively to the princely States.
It immediately recommended linguistic States throughout India.
It recommended linguistic States only for the Madras Presidency.
215.x: The JVP Committee, comprising Nehru, Patel and Pattabhi, initially rejected the demand for linguistic States.
215.tq: Test the committee's initial recommendation rather than its membership or later developments.
xs: The **JVP Committee** first **rejected linguistic states** — option **(1)**.
Members: **Nehru + Patel + Pattabhi**.
xa: Pattabhi had written in **The Hindu** on the **need for linguistic states**.
**Sambamurthy** demanded Andhra state **before** the Constitution.

215.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pattabhi Sitaramayya — Krishna Jilla Co-operative Bank
215.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya founded Andhra Bank, Andhra Insurance Company and the Krishna Jilla Co-operative Bank. The Simon Commission campaign is associated here with Bulusu Sambamurthy, not with Pattabhi's founding activities.
215.tq: Find the single mismatched leader-and-association pair among closely related Andhra nationalist facts.
xs: **Pattabhi — Simon Commission** is wrongly matched — option **(4)**.
The Simon boycott belongs to **Prakasam** (Madras) and **Sambamurthy** (toured Andhra).
Pattabhi founded **Andhra Bank** (**1923**), **Andhra Insurance Co.**, **Krishna Jilla Co-operative Bank**.
xa: Andhra Bank's head office: "**Pattabhi Bhavan**".
Andhra Bank (**1923**) = symbol of **Swadeshi enterprise**.

215.s: Andhra Bank was founded by Pattabhi Sitaramayya at which place and in which year?
