215.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya founded Andhra Bank at Machilipatnam in 1923.
215.tq: Combine the location and year; both must be correct to identify the answer.
xs: **Andhra Bank** was founded by Pattabhi at **Machilipatnam** in **1923** — option **(1)**.
**Kakinada 1923** was the INC session (Sambamurthy's Reception Committee).
xa: Head office: "**Pattabhi Bhavan**".
Pattabhi also founded **Andhra Insurance Co.** and the **Krishna Jilla Co-operative Bank**.

215.s: The head office of Andhra Bank founded by Pattabhi Sitaramayya was known as:
215.x: The head office of Andhra Bank was known as Pattabhi Bhavan.
215.tq: Discriminate between a founder's name and generic institutional names used as distractors.
xs: Andhra Bank's head office was "**Pattabhi Bhavan**" — option **(4)**.
The bank was founded by **Pattabhi Sitaramayya**, **Machilipatnam**, **1923**.
xa: It is seen as a symbol of **Swadeshi enterprise**.
Pattabhi was **Governor of Madhya Pradesh (1952-57)**.

215.s: Which statement best reflects the historical qualification concerning the description of Pattabhi Sitaramayya as the first Telugu president of the Indian National Congress?
o: P. Ananda Charlu and Pattabhi jointly presided over the same Congress session in 1891.
Pattabhi presided over the Congress before P. Ananda Charlu in 1891.
P. Ananda Charlu presided over the Congress in 1891, although Pattabhi is treated as the first Telugu INC president in the cited APPSC convention.
No Telugu leader presided over the Congress before independence.
215.x: P. Ananda Charlu presided over the Congress in 1891. Nevertheless, the APPSC convention identifies Pattabhi Sitaramayya as the first Telugu INC president when Ananda Charlu is not an option.
215.tq: Separate the examination convention from the strict historical qualification instead of treating similar claims as identical.
xs: Strictly, **P. Ananda Charlu** presided in **1891**; the APPSC convention treats **Pattabhi** as first Telugu INC president — option **(3)**.
⚠ Answer **Pattabhi** only when **Ananda Charlu** is not offered.
xa: Pattabhi presided over the **Jaipur session (1948)**.
At **Tripuri (1939)** he lost to **Subhas Chandra Bose**.

215.s: Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided over which session of the Indian National Congress?
215.x: Pattabhi presided over the Jaipur session (1948). At Tripuri (1939) he was Gandhi's candidate but was defeated by Subhas Chandra Bose; at Kakinada (1923) Bulusu Sambamurthy chaired the Reception Committee; the Calcutta special session (1920) passed the Non-Cooperation resolution.
215.tq: Pattabhi: lost Tripuri 1939, presided Jaipur 1948.
xs: Pattabhi presided over the **Jaipur session (1948)** — option **(1)**.
At **Tripuri (1939)** he **lost** to Bose; **Kakinada (1923)** — Sambamurthy's Reception Committee.
**Calcutta (1920)** passed the NC resolution, which **Konda** opposed.
xa: Pattabhi was on the **JVP Committee**.
He was **APCC President** in **1937**.

215.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
215.x: Desoddharaka was the title of Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, whereas Duvvuri Subbamma was known as Desabandhavi.
215.tq: Find the swapped title-person pair among closely related Andhra honorifics.
xs: **Desoddharaka — Duvvuri Subbamma** is wrongly matched — option **(1)**.
"**Desoddharaka**" was **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**, founder of **Andhra Patrika**; Subbamma was "**Desabandhavi**".
Prakasam — **Andhra Kesari**; Veeraiah Chowdary — **Andhra Shivaji**: correct.
xa: **Andhra Tilak** — **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao**.
**Andhra Ratna** — **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya**.

215.s:
Consider the following pairs of titles and Andhra leaders:
1. Desabhakta — Konda Venkatappayya
2. Maharshi — Bulusu Sambamurthy
3. Andhra Tilak — Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
215.x: Pair 1 is correct: Konda Venkatappayya was called Desabhakta. Pair 2 is correct: Bulusu Sambamurthy was called Maharshi for his ascetic Gandhian life. Pair 3 is wrong: Andhra Tilak was Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao (courage in the Vande Mataram era); Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was Andhra Ratna. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' leaves out a true pair, and the options with 3 include the false pair.
215.tq: Andhra Tilak = Gadicherla (Vande Mataram era); Andhra Ratna = Duggirala (Chirala-Perala).
xs: Pairs **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Pair 1 correct: **Desabhakta — Konda Venkatappayya**.
Pair 2 correct: **Maharshi — Bulusu Sambamurthy** (ascetic Gandhian life).
Pair 3 wrong: **Andhra Tilak** is **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao**; Duggirala is **Andhra Ratna**.
xa: Gadicherla earned it for **courage in the Vande Mataram era**.
**Desabandhavi** — **Duvvuri Subbamma**.

215.s: Who among the following was known as ‘Andhra Ratna’?
215.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was called ‘Andhra Ratna’. He led the Chirala-Perala Satyagraha in 1921 and founded the Ramadandu volunteer corps.
215.tq: Match the popular title with the leader and the associated movement.
xs: "**Andhra Ratna**" was **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya** — option **(3)**.
He led the **Chirala-Perala** satyagraha (**1921**) and founded the **Ramadandu** corps.
**Konda** — Desabhakta; **Prakasam** — Andhra Kesari; **Gadicherla** — Andhra Tilak.
xa: **Maharshi** — **Bulusu Sambamurthy**.
**Desoddharaka** — **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**.

215.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao — Ramadandu volunteer corps
215.x: Bulusu Sambamurthy was associated with an ascetic Gandhian life. Andhra Patrika was founded by Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, the Ramadandu was founded by Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya, and the Chirala-Perala Satyagraha was led by him.
215.tq: Find the sure person–episode pair and eliminate swapped associations.
xs: **Bulusu Sambamurthy — ascetic Gandhian life** — option **(3)**; hence "**Maharshi**".
**Ramadandu** and **Chirala-Perala** belong to **Duggirala**; **Andhra Patrika** to **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**.
xa: Sambamurthy was **Speaker** of the Madras Assembly (**1937**).
He chaired the **Kakinada (1923)** Reception Committee.

215.s: Tanguturi Prakasam held which of the following offices in the Rajaji Ministry of 1937?
215.x: Tanguturi Prakasam served as Revenue Minister in the Rajaji Ministry of 1937.
215.tq: Use the ministry-and-portfolio association to avoid swapping offices.
xs: Prakasam was **Revenue Minister** in the **Rajaji ministry (1937)** — option **(2)**.
In the same **1937** set-up **Bulusu Sambamurthy** was **Speaker**, not a minister.
xa: In **1946** he became **Chief Minister (Premier)** of composite Madras.
He was also Chairman, **Rajahmundry Municipality**.
**Pattabhi** was **APCC President** in **1937**.

215.s: Tanguturi Prakasam became the Chief Minister or Premier of composite Madras in:
215.x: Tanguturi Prakasam became Chief Minister, then referred to as Premier, of composite Madras in 1946.
215.tq: Use a year-based distinction between Prakasam’s Madras and Andhra offices.
xs: Prakasam became **Chief Minister (Premier)** of composite Madras in **1946** — option **(3)**.
In **1937** he was **Revenue Minister**, not CM.
xa: He later became the **first CM of Andhra State**.
In **1951** he founded the **Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party**.

215.s: Who was the second and last Chief Minister of Andhra State, serving from 28 March 1955 to 31 October 1956?
215.x: Bezawada Gopal Reddy was the second and last Chief Minister of Andhra State, holding office from 28 March 1955 to 31 October 1956.
215.tq: Use dates to distinguish successive holders of the same office.
xs: **Bezawada Gopal Reddy** was the **2nd and last CM of Andhra State** (**28 Mar 1955 - 31 Oct 1956**) — option **(3)**.
**Prakasam** was the **first** CM of Andhra State.
xa: Pattabhi became **Governor of Madhya Pradesh** (**1952-57**).
Prakasam was President of the Andhra Congress Committee **18 times**.

215.s: Who served as President of the Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee in 1937?
215.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya served as President of the Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee in 1937.
215.tq: Distinguish an organisational post from the leader’s other national offices.
xs: **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** was **APCC President** in **1937** — option **(3)**.
**Konda** was APCC president **1918-23**; **Sambamurthy** was **Speaker** in 1937.
xa: Pattabhi was **Governor of Madhya Pradesh** (**1952-57**) and a **Rajya Sabha** member.
**Prakasam** was Andhra Congress Committee President **18 times**.

215.s: Which Andhra leader served as Governor of Madhya Pradesh from 1952 to 1957?
215.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya was Governor of Madhya Pradesh (1952-57) and a Rajya Sabha member. Prakasam was Premier of composite Madras (1946); Sambamurthy was Speaker of the Madras Legislative Assembly (1937); Konda Venkatappayya was AICC Secretary (1923) and first president of the Andhra Congress Circle.
215.tq: Governor of MP 1952-57 = Pattabhi.
xs: **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** was **Governor of Madhya Pradesh (1952-57)** — option **(1)**.
**Prakasam** — Premier of composite Madras (**1946**); **Sambamurthy** — Speaker (**1937**); **Konda** — AICC Secretary (**1923**).
xa: Pattabhi was also a **Rajya Sabha** member.
He presided over the **Jaipur session (1948)**.

215.s: Which one of the following books was written by Pattabhi Sitaramayya?
215.x: ‘Feathers and Stones’, described as an Ahmednagar Fort prison diary, was written by Pattabhi Sitaramayya.
215.tq: Distinguish authorship by separating books of Pattabhi, Prakasam and Konda Venkatappayya.
xs: **Feathers and Stones** (Ahmednagar Fort prison diary) is by **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** — option **(4)**.
**Naa Jeevita Yatra** and **Chenna Nagaramu Andhra Nagaramae** are **Prakasam's**; **Andhrudyamam** is **Konda's**.
xa: Pattabhi also wrote **History of the Indian National Congress** (**1935**) and **Gandhi and Gandhism**.
Exam angle: **book-author** matching.

215.s: Which of the following works was written by Tanguturi Prakasam?
o: History of the Indian National Congress
215.x: ‘Chenna Nagaramu Andhra Nagaramae’ was written by Tanguturi Prakasam.
215.tq: Use direct author–work association while avoiding similarly grouped books.
xs: **Chenna Nagaramu Andhra Nagaramae** was written by **Tanguturi Prakasam** — option **(1)**.
**Feathers and Stones**, **History of the INC** and **Gandhi and Gandhism** are **Pattabhi's**.
xa: Prakasam's autobiography: **Naa Jeevita Yatra**.
Prakasam also wrote **Law Times** and **Monetary Systems of the World**.

215.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. ‘Naa Jeevita Yatra’ is the autobiography of Tanguturi Prakasam.
2. The autobiography consists of four parts.
3. Tanguturi Prakasam wrote all four parts himself.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
215.x: ‘Naa Jeevita Yatra’ is Prakasam’s autobiography and consists of four parts. However, Prakasam wrote three parts, while Tenneti Viswanatham wrote the fourth.
215.tq: Spot the subtle false statement created by an absolute claim such as ‘all’.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)**.
Statements 1 and 2 correct: **Naa Jeevita Yatra** is Prakasam's autobiography in **4 parts**.
Statement 3 wrong: Prakasam wrote **3 parts**; **Tenneti Viswanatham** wrote the 4th.
xa: Prakasam also wrote **Indian Monetary Systems**.
**Andhrudyamam** — **Konda Venkatappayya**.

215.s: Which of the following works is NOT associated with Tanguturi Prakasam?
215.x: ‘Andhrudyamam’ was written by Konda Venkatappayya. Law Times, Monetary Systems of the World and Indian Monetary Systems were associated with Tanguturi Prakasam.
215.tq: Find the one work belonging to a different author in a grouped list.
xs: **Andhrudyamam** is not Prakasam's — option **(3)**; it is **Konda Venkatappayya's**.
**Law Times**, **Monetary Systems of the World** and **Indian Monetary Systems** are Prakasam's.
xa: Prakasam also wrote **Chenna Nagaramu Andhra Nagaramae**.
Pingali Venkayya wrote a book on **national-flag designs** (**1916**).

215.s: Pattabhi Sitaramayya wrote articles in The Hindu on the need for:
215.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya wrote articles in The Hindu advocating the need for linguistic states.
215.tq: Identify the subject of a leader’s published advocacy.
xs: Pattabhi wrote in **The Hindu** on the need for **linguistic states** — option **(2)**.
Yet as a **JVP Committee** member he first **rejected** linguistic states.
xa: **Sambamurthy** as Speaker demanded Andhra state **before** the Constitution.
Pattabhi's **History of the Indian National Congress** came out in **1935**.

215.s: 'History of the Indian National Congress' (1935) was written by:
215.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya wrote History of the Indian National Congress (1935), as well as Feathers and Stones and Gandhi and Gandhism. Prakasam wrote Naa Jeevita Yatra and Chenna Nagaramu Andhra Nagaramae; Konda Venkatappayya wrote Andhrudyamam; Tenneti Viswanatham wrote the fourth part of Prakasam's autobiography.
215.tq: History of the INC (1935) = Pattabhi.
xs: **History of the Indian National Congress** (**1935**) is by **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** — option **(1)**.
**Prakasam** wrote **Naa Jeevita Yatra**; **Konda** wrote **Andhrudyamam**; **Tenneti Viswanatham** wrote its **4th** part.
xa: Pattabhi also wrote **Feathers and Stones** (Ahmednagar Fort prison diary).
And **Gandhi and Gandhism**.

215.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the collective historical significance of Konda Venkatappayya, Pattabhi Sitaramayya, Tanguturi Prakasam and Bulusu Sambamurthy?
o: They led Andhra-related activities connected with the Non-Cooperation Movement, Civil Disobedience Movement, Simon Commission boycott, Sribagh Pact and the demand for Statehood.
They were exclusively administrators of the Madras Presidency and did not participate in mass movements.
They were all presidents of the Indian National Congress in successive years.
They were associated only with the linguistic reorganisation of States after 1956.
215.x: These four leaders collectively guided Andhra's political activities connected with the Non-Cooperation and Civil Disobedience Movements, Simon Commission boycott, Sribagh Pact and the demand for Statehood.
215.tq: Select the option covering the full range of activities and reject the extreme word exclusively.
xs: The four led Andhra through **NCM, CDM, Simon boycott, Sribagh Pact and statehood** — option **(1)**.
Only **Pattabhi** presided over the INC (**Jaipur 1948**), so option (3) is wrong.
xa: **Konda** — **Dictator** of the Andhra Salt Satyagraha.
**Prakasam** and **Sambamurthy** — Sribagh Pact signatories.

215.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh is named after Tanguturi Prakasam?
215.x: Prakasam district is named after Tanguturi Prakasam.
215.tq: Distinguish an eponymous district from distractors formed from the names of other Andhra leaders.
xs: **Prakasam district** is named after **Tanguturi Prakasam** — option **(1)**.
He was born at **Vinodarayunipalem** in that district (**1872**).
xa: He was the **first CM of Andhra State**.
Title: "**Andhra Kesari**".

215.s: The founding of Andhra Bank in 1923 is regarded as an example of which broader idea in the Andhra nationalist context?
o: Official expansion of the Madras Government
215.x: Andhra Bank, founded in 1923, represented the spirit of Swadeshi enterprise in Andhra.
215.tq: Connect the institution with the underlying nationalist economic concept rather than its administrative location.
xs: **Andhra Bank** (**1923**) is a symbol of **Swadeshi enterprise** — option **(3)**.
Founded by **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** at **Machilipatnam**.
xa: Head office: "**Pattabhi Bhavan**".
Pattabhi also founded **Andhra Insurance Co.**

215.s: Who was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State?
215.x: Tanguturi Prakasam was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State. Bezawada Gopal Reddy was its second and last CM (28 Mar 1955 - 31 Oct 1956); Pattabhi became Governor of Madhya Pradesh; Sambamurthy was Speaker of the Madras Assembly.
215.tq: Andhra State CMs: Prakasam (first), Bezawada Gopal Reddy (last).
xs: The **first CM of Andhra State** was **Tanguturi Prakasam** — option **(1)**.
**Bezawada Gopal Reddy** was the **2nd and last** (**28 Mar 1955 - 31 Oct 1956**).
**Pattabhi** became Governor of Madhya Pradesh; **Sambamurthy** was Speaker.
xa: Earlier Prakasam was **Premier** of composite Madras (**1946**).
**Prakasam district** is named after him.

216.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indigo Revolt:
1. It took place in 1859-60, chiefly in Nadia in Bengal.
2. It was led by Digambar Biswas and Bishnu Biswas.
3. Nil Darpan, written by Dinabandhu Mitra, was translated into English by Rev. James Long.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
216.x: Statement 1 is correct: the revolt was in 1859-60 in Nadia, Bengal. Statement 2 is correct: Digambar and Bishnu Biswas led it. Statement 3 is wrong: Michael Madhusudan Dutt translated Nil Darpan into English; Rev. James Long published it. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses statement 2, and options with 3 include the false translator.
216.tq: Nil Darpan: Mitra wrote, Dutt translated, Long published.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: the **Indigo Revolt** was in **1859-60**, in **Nadia, Bengal**.
Statement 2 correct: led by **Digambar Biswas** and **Bishnu Biswas**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Nil Darpan** was translated by **Michael Madhusudan Dutt**; **Rev. James Long** only published it.
xa: ⚠ Nil Darpan = written by **Dinabandhu Mitra**, translated by **Dutt**, published by **Long**.
The **Indigo Commission (1860)** declared **Tinkathia** illegal.

216.s: Under the Tinkathia system imposed by European indigo planters, peasants were required to cultivate indigo on
216.x: The Tinkathia system required indigo cultivation on three-twentieths, or 3/20, of the peasants’ land, generally at poor prices.
216.tq: Test the exact fraction against nearby proportional distractors.
xs: Under **Tinkathia**, peasants grew indigo on **3/20** of their land — option **(1)**.
European planters forced it at **poor prices**.
xa: The **Indigo Commission (1860)** declared Tinkathia **illegal** in Bengal.
In **Champaran (1917)** Tinkathia was ended by the **Champaran Agrarian Act 1918**.

216.s: What was the effect of the Indigo Commission of 1860 on the Tinkathia system?
o: It expanded the system to all of Bengal
It made the system compulsory for twenty years
It transferred indigo cultivation to zamindars
216.x: The Indigo Commission, appointed in 1860, declared the Tinkathia system illegal.
216.tq: Identify the institutional decision that followed the agrarian protest.
xs: The **Indigo Commission (1860)** **declared the Tinkathia system illegal** — option **(2)**.
It followed the **Indigo Revolt** (**1859-60**, Nadia, Bengal).
xa: Leaders: **Digambar Biswas** and **Bishnu Biswas**.
The play **Nil Darpan** by **Dinabandhu Mitra** exposed the planters.

216.s: Which one of the following was the immediate target of the Deccan Riots of 1875?
216.x: The peasants attacked moneylenders, particularly outsiders from Gujarat and Marwar, who had seized peasant land through debt-related processes.
216.tq: Identify the actual target instead of accepting a broad but incomplete cause.
xs: The Deccan Riots (**1875**) targeted **moneylenders** — **outsiders from Gujarat and Marwar** — option **(2)**.
**Taluqdars** were the Oudh target; **indigo planters** the Bengal target.
⚠ "Uniform land tax" is an incomplete cause; the **moneylender** was the target.
xa: Under ryotwari and the **Limitation Law of 1859**, moneylenders seized peasants' land.
Outcome: **Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act, 1879**.

216.s: During the Deccan Riots, the peasants primarily attacked moneylenders’ houses and burned which of the following?
216.x: The rioters attacked the houses of moneylenders and burned their debt bonds, which represented the oppressive credit relationships.
216.tq: Test the specific action associated with the revolt rather than its general grievance.
xs: Deccan rioters attacked moneylenders' houses and burned **debt bonds** — option **(3)**.
**Indigo contracts** belong to the Bengal Indigo Revolt.
xa: The riots were in **Poona-Ahmednagar** (Maharashtra), **1875**.
The government passed the **Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act, 1879**.

216.s: The Deccan Agriculturists’ Relief Act was enacted in response to the Deccan agrarian disturbances in which year?
216.x: The Government responded to the Deccan disturbances by enacting the Deccan Agriculturists’ Relief Act in 1879.
216.tq: Distinguish the year of the disturbance from the year of the relief legislation.
xs: The **Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act** came in **1879** — option **(2)**.
**1875** was the year of the riots; **1885** is the **Bengal Tenancy Act**; **1918** the **Champaran Agrarian Act**.
xa: The **Limitation Law of 1859** had helped moneylenders seize land.
⚠ **Pabna** (**1873-76**) led to the **Bengal Tenancy Act 1885**.

216.s: The main grievances of the Oudh Kisan Sabha were directed against which practices of the taluqdars?
216.x: The Oudh Kisan Sabha addressed rent increases and begar, or forced labour, imposed by taluqdars.
216.tq: Link the regional Kisan Sabha with its specific agrarian grievances.
xs: The **Oudh Kisan Sabha** fought **rent hikes** and **begar** (forced labour) by **taluqdars** — option **(4)**.
**Indigo** and **debt bonds** belong to Bengal and the Deccan.
xa: Oudh Kisan Sabha (**Oct 1920**) — **Jawaharlal Nehru** and **Baba Ramchandra**.
**UP Kisan Sabha (1918)** — **Gauri Shankar Mishra** and **Indra Narayan Dwivedi**, backed by **M.M. Malaviya**.

216.s: Which one of the following statements correctly differentiates the Eka Movement from the Bardoli Satyagraha?
o: Eka was led by Patel in Gujarat, whereas Bardoli was led by Madari Pasi in Oudh.
Eka was under Madari Pasi and became violent, whereas Bardoli was a disciplined non-violent Congress campaign led by Patel.
Both movements were controlled directly by the Congress and remained non-violent.
Both movements were directed against moneylenders in the Deccan.
216.x: The Eka Movement of 1921–22 operated in Hardoi, Bahraich and Sitapur under Madari Pasi, became violent and remained outside Congress control. Bardoli was a disciplined, non-violent Congress campaign led by Patel.
216.tq: Use the leadership, region and method together to separate two easily confused movements.
xs: **Eka** under **Madari Pasi** turned **violent**; **Bardoli** was a **disciplined, non-violent Congress campaign** led by **Patel** — option **(2)**.
⚠ Eka was **outside Congress control**, so option (3) is wrong.
xa: Eka (**1921-22**) region: **Hardoi-Bahraich-Sitapur**; Eka means **unity**.
Bardoli (**1928**) was against a **revenue hike**.

216.s: The Eka Movement was mainly associated with which geographical area?
216.x: The Eka Movement of 1921–22 was concentrated in the Hardoi, Bahraich and Sitapur areas of Uttar Pradesh.
216.tq: Test the regional cluster rather than confusing it with the similarly named Oudh Kisan Sabha.
xs: The **Eka movement** was in **Hardoi, Bahraich and Sitapur** — option **(4)**.
**Poona-Ahmednagar** = Deccan Riots; **Kheda and Bardoli** = Gujarat.
xa: Leader: **Madari Pasi**; years **1921-22**.
It **turned violent**, outside Congress control.

216.s: The Oudh Kisan Sabha, formed in October 1920, was set up by:
o: Gauri Shankar Mishra and Indra Narayan Dwivedi
216.x: The Oudh Kisan Sabha (Oct 1920) was set up by Jawaharlal Nehru and Baba Ramchandra against rent hikes and begar. Gauri Shankar Mishra and Indra Narayan Dwivedi founded the UP Kisan Sabha (1918), backed by M.M. Malaviya; Madari Pasi led the Eka movement (1921-22); Patel and Mohanlal Pandya led Kheda (1918).
216.tq: UP Kisan Sabha 1918 (Mishra, Dwivedi); Oudh Kisan Sabha 1920 (Nehru, Baba Ramchandra).
xs: The **Oudh Kisan Sabha** (**Oct 1920**) was set up by **Jawaharlal Nehru and Baba Ramchandra** — option **(1)**.
**Gauri Shankar Mishra + Indra Narayan Dwivedi** — **UP Kisan Sabha (1918)**; **Madari Pasi** — **Eka**; **Patel + Mohanlal Pandya** — **Kheda (1918)**.
xa: Oudh grievances: **rent hikes** and **begar**.
UP Kisan Sabha was backed by **M.M. Malaviya**.

216.s: The term ‘Tebhaga’ referred to the demand of sharecroppers for:
o: One-half of the crop stored in the landlord’s godown
Two-thirds of the crop instead of one-half
One-third of the crop instead of one-half
The entire crop without payment of rent
216.x: The bargadars demanded two-thirds of the produce, reducing the landlord’s share from one-half to one-third, with storage in their own godowns.
216.tq: Watch the reversed-share trap: the demand concerns the bargadar’s share, not the landlord’s share.
xs: **Bargadars** (sharecroppers) wanted their share raised from one-half to **two-thirds** — option **(2)**.
They also wanted the crop stored in **their own godowns**.
xa: ⚠ **UPSC 2013** framed it as cutting the landlord's share from **one-half to one-third**.
Outcome: **Bargadari Act (1950)**.

216.s: Which legislation is associated with the outcome of the Tebhaga Movement?
216.x: The Bargadari Act of 1950 is associated with the outcome of the Tebhaga struggle.
216.tq: Match the movement with its later legislative outcome while rejecting earlier regional laws.
xs: The Tebhaga outcome was the **Bargadari Act (1950)** — option **(4)**.
**Bengal Tenancy Act 1885** followed **Pabna**; **Champaran Agrarian Act 1918** followed **Champaran**; the **1879** Act followed the **Deccan Riots**.
xa: Tebhaga (**1946-47**, Bengal) was led by the **AIKS/CPI**.
Its short-run failure: **limited spread** + **Hindu-Muslim rift**.

216.s: Which of the following factors contributed to the limited short-run success of the Tebhaga Movement?
o: A government ban before the movement began and a famine in Gujarat
The transfer of the movement from Bengal to Hyderabad
Limited spread and the Hindu-Muslim rift
Complete support from all zamindars and the absence of peasant participation
216.x: The movement’s short-run success was limited by its restricted spread and the Hindu-Muslim rift.
216.tq: Identify the paired outcome factors rather than confusing them with causes of other movements.
xs: Tebhaga's short-run failure came from **limited spread** and the **Hindu-Muslim rift** — option **(3)**.
It stayed in **Bengal**; it did not shift to Hyderabad.
xa: Demand: bargadars' share to **two-thirds**.
Later outcome: **Bargadari Act (1950)**.

216.s: The Telangana Peasant Armed Struggle of 1946–1951 was directed primarily against which system of rule?
o: The feudal order of the Nizam in Hyderabad State
The ryotwari system of the Madras Presidency
216.x: The struggle in Hyderabad State was directed against the Nizam’s feudal order, particularly the power of jagirdars and deshmukhs and the practice of Vetti.
216.tq: Identify the central authority and the specific system against which the movement was directed.
xs: The Telangana struggle targeted the **Nizam's feudal order** in **Hyderabad State** — option **(2)**.
Its targets: **jagirdars**, **deshmukhs** and **Vetti** (forced labour).
**Permanent Settlement** is Bengal (**1793**); ryotwari is the Madras/Deccan system.
xa: Span: **1946-51**; led by the **CPI/Andhra Mahasabha**.
Called off in **1951** after the **Indian Army integrated Hyderabad**.

216.s: Who among the following were associated with the leadership of the Telangana Peasant Armed Struggle on behalf of the Communist Party of India?
o: P. Sundarayya and Chandra Rajeswara Rao
216.x: P. Sundarayya and Chandra Rajeswara Rao were the principal CPI leaders associated with the Telangana armed struggle.
216.tq: Match the movement with its actual political leaders rather than leaders of similar peasant struggles.
xs: **P. Sundarayya** and **Chandra Rajeswara Rao** led the Telangana struggle for the **CPI** — option **(1)**.
**Biswas** brothers led the Indigo Revolt; **Dodla Ramireddy** and **Vennelakanti Raghavaiah** were Nellore anti-zamindari leaders.
xa: Sundarayya wrote **Telangana People's Struggle and its Lessons**.
**Andhra Mahasabha** President **1941-46**: **M. Suryanarayana** (**G2 2019** key).

216.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Andhra Mahasabha:
1. It initially concentrated on cultural work.
2. During the 1930s and 1940s, it moved towards leftist agrarian politics.
3. By the 1940s, it functioned as the organisational front of the Communist Party of India in the Telangana struggle.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
216.x: All three statements are correct. The Andhra Mahasabha evolved from cultural activity into a left-oriented agrarian organisation and became the CPI’s organisational front in the struggle.
216.tq: Test the transformation of an organisation across time through a coded statement question.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
The **Andhra Mahasabha** began with **cultural work**.
It moved to **leftist agrarian politics** (**1930s-40s**).
By the **1940s** it was the **organisational front of the CPI**.
xa: President **1941-46**: **M. Suryanarayana**.
The struggle set up **village soviets** after redistributing land.

216.s:
Consider the following statements about the Telangana armed struggle:
1. Doddi Komaraiah, its first martyr, was shot at Kadavendi (Jangaon) in July 1946 by the Visnur deshmukh's men.
2. Chakali Ailamma, a washerwoman of Palakurthi, defended her land against the Visnur deshmukh.
3. As per the official answer key, the memoir 'Veera Telangana - Naa Anubhavalu, Gnapakalu' was written by Mallu Swarajyam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
216.x: Statement 1 is correct: Komaraiah was shot at Kadavendi on 4 July 1946. Statement 2 is correct: Ailamma of Palakurthi resisted the Visnur deshmukh and became a symbol of the revolt. Statement 3 is wrong: the official key credits Veera Telangana to Ravi Narayana Reddy; Mallu Swarajyam was a leading woman fighter. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses statement 2, and options with 3 include the false claim.
216.tq: Veera Telangana memoir = Ravi Narayana Reddy (key), not Mallu Swarajyam.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Doddi Komaraiah**, first martyr, shot at **Kadavendi (Jangaon)** on **4 July 1946**.
Statement 2 correct: **Chakali Ailamma** of **Palakurthi** defended her land against the **Visnur deshmukh**.
Statement 3 wrong: the official key credits **Veera Telangana** to **Ravi Narayana Reddy** (**G2 2025**).
xa: ⚠ One book credits **Mallu Swarajyam**, a leading woman fighter.
Ailamma became a **symbol of the revolt**.

216.s: Which of the following was an important outcome of the Telangana Peasant Armed Struggle?
o: Land was seized and redistributed, and village soviets were established
The Permanent Settlement was introduced in Hyderabad State
Indigo cultivation was made compulsory in Telangana
The zamindari system was strengthened by the Nizam
216.x: The struggle led to the seizure and redistribution of land and the establishment of village soviets in several areas.
216.tq: Distinguish movement outcomes from the causes and institutions associated with other agrarian struggles.
xs: Land was **seized and redistributed** and **village soviets** were set up — option **(1)**.
The struggle opposed the Nizam's order; it did not strengthen zamindari.
xa: It was called off in **1951**, with **land reform** promised.
**Vetti** = forced labour under the Nizam's feudal order.

216.s: As per the APPSC Group 2 2019 answer key, who was the President of the Andhra Mahasabha during 1941-46?
216.x: The APPSC G2 2019 key gives M. Suryanarayana as Andhra Mahasabha President (1941-46), when it had become the CPI's organisational front. P. Sundarayya was a CPI leader of the armed struggle, Doddi Komaraiah was its first martyr (1946), and N.G. Ranga led the Andhra Kisan movement.
216.tq: Andhra Mahasabha President 1941-46 = M. Suryanarayana.
xs: The **APPSC G2 2019** key gives **M. Suryanarayana** as Andhra Mahasabha President **1941-46** — option **(1)**.
**P. Sundarayya** was a CPI leader; **Doddi Komaraiah** the **first martyr**; **N.G. Ranga** led the Andhra Kisan movement.
xa: By the 1940s the Mahasabha was the **organisational front of the CPI**.
**Mallu Swarajyam** — leading woman fighter.

216.s: Acharya N.G. Ranga’s agricultural labour initiative at Nidubrolu in 1923 was known as the
216.x: India’s first Agricultural Labourers’ Mahasabha was held at Nidubrolu in 1923 under the leadership of Acharya N.G. Ranga.
216.tq: Use the year and place to identify the correct organisation from closely related peasant bodies.
xs: Ranga's **1923** initiative at **Nidubrolu** was India's **first Agricultural Labourers' Mahasabha** — option **(3)**.
The **Andhra (Provincial) Ryots' Association** came in **1928**; **Rytu Zamin Sanghams** in **1931**.
xa: Nidubrolu also had the **first Kisan School in India** (**1933-34**).
**Andhra Rythu Vidyalayam, Madanapalle** (**May 1938**) — **T.N. Ramakrishna Reddy**.

216.s: In which year did Acharya N.G. Ranga found the Andhra Provincial Ryots’ Association?
216.x: The Andhra Provincial Ryots’ Association was founded by N.G. Ranga in 1928.
216.tq: Separate adjacent milestones by matching each organisation with its exact year.
xs: Ranga founded the **Andhra (Provincial) Ryots' Association** in **1928** — option **(2)**.
**1923** was the **Agricultural Labourers' Mahasabha**; **1931** the **Rytu Zamin Sanghams**; **1934** the **Rytu Sammelans**.
xa: Ranga's **Rajakeeya Pathashala, Kankipadu** (**1939**) — **G2 2012** key.
⚠ **Nidubrolu** = first Kisan School; **Kankipadu** = Rajakeeya Pathashala.

216.s: The long peasant march associated with the Andhra Kisan movement travelled from
216.x: The peasant march covered about 1,500 kilometres or miles from Ichchapuram in Srikakulam to Madras.
216.tq: Identify the route by its distinctive starting and ending points.
xs: The peasant march went from **Ichchapuram (Srikakulam)** to **Madras** — option **(2)**.
It covered about **1,500 km/miles**.
xa: Dated **1937-38**, led by **Kommareddy** and **Chalasani**.
Some notes date it **1938-39** and credit **Ranga**.

216.s: According to the Andhra Pradesh references, the peasant march from Ichchapuram to Madras was led by
o: Kommareddy Satyanarayana Murthy and Chalasani Vasudeva Rao
P. Sundarayya and Chandra Rajeswara Rao
Batchala Jagannadh Das and Vetluri Govinda Reddy
216.x: The Andhra Pradesh references name Kommareddy Satyanarayana Murthy and Chalasani Vasudeva Rao as the leaders of the march, dated 1937–38.
216.tq: Use the named leaders rather than substituting prominent figures from other peasant movements.
xs: The march was led by **Kommareddy Satyanarayana Murthy and Chalasani Vasudeva Rao** — option **(2)**.
**Sundarayya** and **Chandra Rajeswara Rao** led the **Telangana** struggle; **Biswas** brothers the Indigo Revolt.
**Batchala Jagannadh Das** led the **Munagala** peasants; **Vetluri Govinda Reddy** was at **Venkatagiri**.
xa: March: **Ichchapuram → Madras**, about **1,500** km/miles.
⚠ Some notes say **Ranga** led it (**1938-39**).

216.s: Which one of the following was India’s first Kisan School?
216.x: The Peasant Institute, or Ramanayidu Rythu Vidyalayam, at Nidubrolu was India’s first Kisan School. It was established in 1933–34 with Bharathi Devi and Ranga’s brothers.
216.tq: Distinguish the first institution from later schools and political centres.
xs: India's **first Kisan School** was **Ramanayudu Rythu Vidyalayam, Nidubrolu** — option **(1)**.
Founded **1933-34** by **Ranga**, his brothers and wife **Bharathidevi**.
**Kankipadu** (**1939**), **Kothapatnam** summer school and **Madanapalle** (**May 1938**) came later.
xa: ⚠ **Nidubrolu** = first Kisan School; **Kankipadu** = **Rajakeeya Pathashala**.
In **1934** kisan publications were issued from **Nidubrolu**.

216.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Political summer school — Kothapatnam — 1937
2. Rajakeeya Pathashala — Kankipadu — 1939
3. Andhra Rythu Vidyalayam — Madanapalle — May 1938

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
216.x: All three pairs are correct. The Political Summer School was at Kothapatnam in 1937, Rajakeeya Pathashala at Kankipadu in 1939, and Andhra Rythu Vidyalayam at Madanapalle in May 1938.
216.tq: Start from the sure place–year pairs and verify the complete set.
xs: All three pairs are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
**Summer schools** at **Kothapatnam** ran **1934-37**.
**Rajakeeya Pathashala — Kankipadu — 1939**; **Andhra Rythu Vidyalayam — Madanapalle — May 1938**.
xa: Madanapalle school was founded by **T.N. Ramakrishna Reddy**.
Another summer-school venue: **Mantena vari Palem**.

216.s: The Permanent Settlement of 1793 contributed to anti-zamindari struggles because it
o: made zamindars proprietors and reduced cultivators to the position of tenants
introduced compulsory indigo cultivation by European planters
created village soviets under peasant control
abolished zamindars and gave ownership directly to cultivators
216.x: The Permanent Settlement, introduced by Cornwallis in 1793, made zamindars owners while cultivators became tenants, creating the structural basis for later anti-zamindari opposition.
216.tq: Connect a land-revenue arrangement with its direct social and agrarian consequence.
xs: The **Permanent Settlement (1793, Cornwallis)** made **zamindars owners** and **cultivators tenants** — option **(1)**.
That was the **root cause** of Andhra **anti-zamindari** struggles.
xa: In **1937** **Rajaji** set up a **Zamindari Abolition Committee** under **T. Prakasam**.
Land reform demands led to the **Madras Zamindari Abolition Bill (1947)**.

216.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Nellore anti-zamindari struggle — Batchala Jagannadh Das
Andhra State Zamindari Peasant Association — Vetluri Govinda Reddy
216.x: Vennelakanti Raghavaiah formed the Zamin Rytu Sangam in 1930 and was associated with the paper Zamin Rytu. The other pairs assign leaders to the wrong organisations.
216.tq: Check the organisation–leader pair first and reject swapped leaders from nearby struggles.
xs: **Zamin Rytu Sangam — Vennelakanti Raghavaiah** (**1930**) — option **(2)**.
**Munagala Peasant Association** and the **Andhra State Zamindari Peasant Association** were **Batchala Jagannadh Das's**.
The **Nellore** (Venkatagiri) struggle had **Dodla Ramireddy**, **Raghavaiah**, **Vetluri Govinda Reddy**.
xa: Raghavaiah also ran the paper **Zamin Rytu**.
Film **Rythu Bidda** (**Gudavalli Ramabrahmam**) dramatised the anti-zamindari issue.

216.s:
With reference to the Munagala estate, consider the following statements:
1. It was then situated in Krishna district and is now associated with Nalgonda district.
2. Its zamindar was Nayani Venkataranga Rao.
3. The Munagala Peasant Association was associated with Batchala Jagannadh Das.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
216.x: All three statements are correct. The Munagala estate was then in Krishna and is now in Nalgonda; Nayani Venkataranga Rao was its zamindar, and Batchala Jagannadh Das was associated with its peasant association.
216.tq: Combine location, authority and organisation facts in one coded question.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
**Munagala** was then in **Krishna**, now **Nalgonda**.
Zamindar **Nayani Venkataranga Rao** (Keesaravari); peasant association under **Batchala Jagannadh Das**.
xa: Das also led the **Andhra State Zamindari Peasant Association**.
**Venkatagiri** (Nellore) was the other big anti-zamindari fight.

216.s: Who chaired the Zamindari Abolition Committee set up by Rajaji in 1937?
216.x: Rajaji set up the Zamindari Abolition Committee in 1937, and T. Prakasam served as its chairperson.
216.tq: Apply the authority–office trap by distinguishing the person who set up a committee from the person who chaired it.
xs: **T. Prakasam** chaired the **Zamindari Abolition Committee** set up by **Rajaji** in **1937** — option **(2)**.
**Nayani Venkataranga Rao** was the **Munagala** zamindar; **M. Suryanarayana** headed the **Andhra Mahasabha**.
xa: Land reform demands → **Madras Zamindari Abolition Bill (1947)**.
**Gandhi** visited **Venkatagiri** in **1933**.

216.s: The Nellore Zilla Zamindari Rytu Sangam associated with the Venkatagiri struggle was formed in 1929 by
216.x: Dodla Ramireddy formed the Nellore Zilla Zamindari Rytu Sangam in 1929 in connection with the Venkatagiri struggle.
216.tq: Match the organisation, year and leader rather than using a leader from a neighbouring struggle.
xs: **Dodla Ramireddy** formed the **Nellore Zilla Zamindari Rytu Sangam** (**1929**) — option **(1)**.
**Vennelakanti Raghavaiah** formed the **Zamin Rytu Sangam** in **1930**; **Batchala Jagannadh Das** led **Munagala**.
xa: **Vetluri Govinda Reddy** was also linked to **Venkatagiri**.
Gandhi visited Venkatagiri in **1933**.

216.s: Vetluri Govinda Reddy was associated with the anti-zamindari struggle in the
216.x: Vetluri Govinda Reddy was one of the names associated with the Venkatagiri estate struggle in Nellore district.
216.tq: Locate a leader within the correct estate rather than merely within the correct district.
xs: **Vetluri Govinda Reddy** was linked to the **Venkatagiri** estate struggle (**Nellore**) — option **(1)**.
**Munagala** belongs to **Batchala Jagannadh Das**; **Palakurthi** to **Chakali Ailamma**.
xa: Venkatagiri sangams: **Dodla Ramireddy** (**1929**), **Vennelakanti Raghavaiah** (**1930**).
**Gandhi** visited **Venkatagiri** in **1933**.

216.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
216.x: The Pabna Movement occurred in East Bengal during 1873–76. The Deccan Riots were centred in Poona-Ahmednagar, Bardoli was in Gujarat, and Tebhaga was in Bengal.
216.tq: Start from the sure region-year pair and eliminate the swapped locations.
xs: **Pabna — East Bengal** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Deccan Riots** were in **Poona-Ahmednagar (Maharashtra)**; **Bardoli** in **Gujarat**; **Tebhaga** in **Bengal**.
xa: Pabna (**1873-76**) Agrarian League — **Ishan Chandra Roy**, **Shambhu Pal**.
It was **legal and peaceful**; led to the **Bengal Tenancy Act 1885**.

216.s:
Consider the following statements about the Pabna Movement (1873-76):
1. Its Agrarian League was led by Ishan Chandra Roy and Shambhu Pal.
2. It was a movement against forced indigo cultivation, linked to Dinabandhu Mitra.
3. It was legal and peaceful and led to the Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
216.x: Statement 1 is correct: Ishan Chandra Roy and Shambhu Pal led the Agrarian League. Statement 2 is wrong: Pabna was against rent hikes by zamindars; linking it to indigo and Dinabandhu Mitra is a known mislabel (that is the Indigo Revolt). Statement 3 is correct: it was legal and peaceful and led to the Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885. So '1 and 3 only'.
216.tq: Pabna = rent hikes, peaceful, Bengal Tenancy Act 1885; not indigo.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: the **Agrarian League** — **Ishan Chandra Roy** and **Shambhu Pal**.
Statement 2 wrong: Pabna was against **rent hikes by zamindars**; indigo and **Dinabandhu Mitra** belong to the **Indigo Revolt**.
Statement 3 correct: **legal and peaceful**; led to the **Bengal Tenancy Act 1885**.
xa: ⚠ The UPSC table mislabels Pabna; it also wrongly calls **Sidhu-Kanhu** Bhil leaders (they led the **Santhals**).
Pabna ran **1873-76** in **East Bengal**.

216.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
216.x: The Telangana armed struggle occurred in Hyderabad State. Malabar was the region of the Moplah Movement; Kheda was in Gujarat, Bijolia in Mewar, and the Sanyasi Revolt in Bengal.
216.tq: Find the wrongly shifted regional label among otherwise familiar pairings.
xs: **Telangana — Malabar** is wrongly matched — option **(4)**.
The Telangana struggle was in **Hyderabad State**; **Malabar** was the **Moplah** revolt (**1921**).
The rest are correct: **Bijolia** — Mewar; **Kheda** — Gujarat; **Sanyasi Revolt** — Bengal.
xa: Moplah leaders: **Variyankunnathu Kunjahammad Haji**, **Ali Musliyar**.
Telangana span: **1946-1951**.

216.s: The Sanyasi Revolt was associated with which of the following circumstances?
o: The introduction of the Limitation Law of 1859
The demand for two-thirds of the crop by bargadars
The famine of 1770 and restrictions on pilgrimages
216.x: The Sanyasi Revolt in Bengal during 1763–1800 was linked with the aftermath of the 1770 famine and restrictions imposed on pilgrimages.
216.tq: Identify the distinctive cause rather than the region alone.
xs: The **Sanyasi Revolt** followed the **1770 famine** and **curbs on pilgrimages** — option **(4)**.
**Revenue hike** = Bardoli; **Limitation Law of 1859** = Deccan Riots; **two-thirds** demand = Tebhaga.
xa: **Permanent Settlement** came in **1793** (Cornwallis).

216.s: Who among the following was associated with the Bijolia Movement?
o: Mohanlal Pandya and Indra Narayan Dwivedi
Sitaram Das and Vijay Singh Pathik
Ali Musliyar and Variyankunnathu Kunjahammad Haji
216.x: The Bijolia Movement in Mewar was associated with Sitaram Das and Vijay Singh Pathik.
216.tq: Test the movement-leader pair while using leaders from neighbouring movements as traps.
xs: **Bijolia** (Mewar) is linked with **Sitaram Das and Vijay Singh Pathik** — option **(3)**.
**Madari Pasi / Baba Ramchandra** — UP; **Ali Musliyar / Kunjahammad Haji** — Moplah.
xa: Bijolia span: **1897-1927**, **Rajasthan**.
**Kheda (1918)** — **Patel**, **Mohanlal Pandya**.

216.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to peasant movements in Gujarat?
o: Bardoli — Baba Ramchandra and Madari Pasi
Kheda — Ishan Chandra Roy and Shambhu Pal
Bardoli — Ali Musliyar and Kunjahammad Haji
216.x: Kheda in Gujarat was associated with Patel and Mohanlal Pandya. The other pairs combine leaders from Uttar Pradesh, Bengal and Malabar movements.
216.tq: Use the region first, then verify the associated leaders.
xs: **Kheda — Patel and Mohanlal Pandya** — option **(1)**.
**Baba Ramchandra / Madari Pasi** — UP; **Ishan Chandra Roy / Shambhu Pal** — Pabna; **Ali Musliyar / Kunjahammad Haji** — Moplah.
xa: Kheda was in **1918**; **Bardoli (1928)** — Patel, against a **revenue hike**.
At Bardoli Patel earned the title "**Sardar**".

216.s:
Consider the following statements about the Moplah Movement:
1. It took place in Malabar in 1921.
2. Variyankunnathu Kunjahammad Haji and Ali Musliyar were its leaders.
3. It was directed mainly against moneylenders from Gujarat and Marwar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
216.x: Statement 1 is correct: Malabar, 1921. Statement 2 is correct: Variyankunnathu Kunjahammad Haji and Ali Musliyar led it. Statement 3 is wrong: Moplah was Muslim tenants against landlords and the British; the attack on Gujarati and Marwari moneylenders was the Deccan Riots of 1875. So '1 and 2 only'.
216.tq: Moplah = Malabar tenants vs landlords + British; moneylenders = Deccan Riots.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Malabar**, **1921**.
Statement 2 correct: leaders **Variyankunnathu Kunjahammad Haji** and **Ali Musliyar**.
Statement 3 wrong: Moplah = **Muslim tenants vs landlords and the British**; Gujarati/Marwari moneylenders = **Deccan Riots** (**1875**).
xa: Also in **1920-22**: **Awadh Kisan / Eka** movement in UP.
⚠ The Deccan rioters burned **debt bonds**; outcome the **Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act, 1879**.

216.s: The Tinkathia system in Champaran (Bihar, 1917) was ended by:
216.x: After the 1917 Champaran movement in Bihar, the Champaran Agrarian Act, 1918 ended Tinkathia there. The Indigo Commission (1860) followed the Bengal Indigo Revolt of 1859-60; the Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885 followed the Pabna movement; the Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act, 1879 followed the Deccan Riots.
216.tq: Movement to law: Pabna 1885, Deccan 1879, Champaran 1918, Tebhaga 1950.
xs: **Tinkathia** in **Champaran** (**1917**) was ended by the **Champaran Agrarian Act 1918** — option **(1)**.
**Indigo Commission (1860)** — Bengal; **Bengal Tenancy Act 1885** — Pabna; **1879** Act — Deccan Riots.
xa: Tinkathia: indigo on **3/20** of the land at poor prices.
**Kheda (1918)** in Gujarat followed soon after.

216.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the broad historical transition in Indian peasant movements?
o: From sporadic revolts against zamindars and moneylenders to Gandhian satyagraha and then organised Kisan Sabhas
From organised Kisan Sabhas to sporadic revolts and then to plantation movements
From tribal movements to exclusive urban labour movements
From revolutionary violence directly to constitutional reforms without mass participation
216.x: Before 1917, peasant movements were often sporadic revolts against zamindars and moneylenders; they later developed into Gandhian satyagraha and organised Kisan Sabhas in the 1930s.
216.tq: Recognise the chronological sequence of changing forms of agrarian mobilisation.
xs: **Sporadic revolts** against zamindars and moneylenders (pre-**1917**) → **Gandhian satyagraha** → **organised Kisan Sabhas** (**1930s**) — option **(1)**.
Pre-1917 examples: **Indigo Revolt**, **Pabna**, **Deccan Riots**; Gandhian: **Champaran**, **Kheda**, **Bardoli**.
xa: Andhra examples of the Kisan phase: Ranga's **Nidubrolu** institutions.
**Champaran** (**1917**) marks the start of the Gandhian phase.

216.s: The anti-zamindari struggles in Andhra Pradesh mentioned in connection with land reform included which of the following?
216.x: The Nellore and Munagala anti-zamindari struggles are highlighted as important Andhra-related agrarian movements. Land reform demands also contributed to the Madras Zamindari Abolition Bill of 1947.
216.tq: Identify the Andhra-specific locations rather than selecting nationally prominent movement centres.
xs: The Andhra anti-zamindari fights were **Nellore and Munagala** — option **(3)**.
**Pabna/Bijolia**, **Hardoi/Bahraich**, **Kheda/Bardoli** are outside Andhra.
xa: These, with Ranga's **Nidubrolu** institutions, are **APPSC favourites**.
Land reform demands → **Madras Zamindari Abolition Bill (1947)**.

216.s: The Madras Zamindari Abolition Bill was introduced in which year in the context of land reform demands?
216.x: Land reform demands associated with agrarian struggles led to the Madras Zamindari Abolition Bill in 1947.
216.tq: Distinguish the bill’s year from the years of the Kisan Sabha and Bargadari legislation.
xs: The **Madras Zamindari Abolition Bill** came in **1947** — option **(3)**.
**1950** is the **Bargadari Act** (Bengal).
xa: In **1937** **Rajaji** set up a **Zamindari Abolition Committee** chaired by **T. Prakasam**.
Root cause: the **Permanent Settlement** (**1793**).

217.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gothi — annual renewal fee for tenancy
217.x: Gothi referred to hereditary bonded labour in the Agency. The annual renewal fee for tenancy was nazarana.
217.tq: Identify the swapped meaning among closely related customary exactions.
xs: **Gothi — annual renewal fee** is wrongly matched — option **(4)**.
**Gothi** = **hereditary bonded labour in the Agency**; the renewal fee is **Nazarana**.
The rest are correct: **Pullari** — grazing tax; **Bedalli** — eviction; **Vetti** — forced free labour.
xa: ⚠ **Pullari** = grazing tax; **Nazarana** = renewal fee; **Bedalli** = eviction.
**Kancha paddhati**: grazing land **auctioned yearly** (Venkatagiri).
Other exactions: **forest-produce, water and cattle taxes**.

217.s: Which development intensified agrarian distress during 1929–35?
o: The abolition of all forest taxes
The conversion of all estates into ryotwari holdings
A sharp rise in crop prices
The crash in crop prices during the Depression
217.x: The Depression of 1929–35 caused crop prices to crash, intensifying agrarian distress.
217.tq: Link the economic event with its direct agrarian consequence.
xs: The **1929-35 Depression** **crashed crop prices** — option **(4)**.
Prices fell; they did not rise, and estates were not converted to ryotwari until the **1948** Act.
xa: **40%** of Andhra's land was still under zamindars at Independence.
**Pattabhi** first called for an anti-zamindari struggle in **1920**.

217.s: At the time of Independence, approximately what proportion of Andhra’s land remained under zamindars?
217.x: About 40 percent of Andhra’s land was still under zamindars at Independence.
217.tq: Recall the quantitative scale of zamindari persistence at Independence.
xs: About **40 percent** (**40%**) of Andhra's land was still under zamindars at Independence — option **(3)**.
⚠ Don't confuse with **70%** — the share of Madras Presidency zamindari land in Vizag, Nellore, the Godavaris, Krishna and Chittoor.
xa: The **1929-35 Depression** crashed crop prices.
Zamindari was abolished by the **Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948**.

217.s: Who first called for an anti-zamindari struggle in 1920?
217.x: Pattabhi first called for an anti-zamindari struggle in 1920.
217.tq: Distinguish the earliest call from later organisational leadership.
xs: **Pattabhi** first called for an anti-zamindari struggle in **1920** — option **(1)**.
**N.G. Ranga** presided over the **first anti-zamindari conference** (Venkatagiri, **Sept 1931**); **Kala Venkata Rao** introduced the **1947** Bill.
xa: **Gottipati Brahmaiah** was a leader in the **Challapalli/Munagala** struggles.
**Communists** pioneered the demand for **land to the tiller**.

217.s:
With reference to the Madras Estates Land Act, 1908, consider the following statements:
1. Inam ryots fought for abolition of inam estates under this Act.
2. The Vizag Zamindar Rythu Sabha in 1929 demanded that the Act be amended.
3. The Act itself abolished all zamindari and inamdari estates in 1948.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
217.x: Statement 1 is correct: inam ryots fought for abolition of inam estates under the 1908 Act. Statement 2 is correct: the Vizag Zamindar Rythu Sabha (3 Nov 1929) resolved to amend the Estates Land Act. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1908 Act did not abolish estates; zamindari and inamdari estates were abolished by the Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
217.tq: Separate the 1908 Estates Land Act from the later abolition legislation.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: **inam ryots** fought to abolish inam estates under the **1908** Act.
Statement 2 correct: the **Vizag Zamindar Rythu Sabha** (**3 Nov 1929**) resolved to **amend** the Act.
Statement 3 wrong: abolition came by the **Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948**.
xa: The Vizag Sabha started **Prajavani** (editor **Garimella Krishnamurthy**).
The **Jameen Ryot Mahasabha** in **1938** demanded a **Zamindari Abolition Act**.

217.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Nellore District Zamindari Rythu Sangham first met in October 1929 at the house of Bhupathiraju Venkatapathiraju.
2. The first anti-zamindari conference, held at Venkatagiri in September 1931, was presided over by N.G. Ranga.
3. The goal of the Venkatagiri conference was the abolition of zamindari.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
217.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the Nellore Sangham first met (19 October 1929) at Dodla Ramireddy's house; Bhupathiraju Venkatapathiraju was President of the Andhra Rashtra Zamindari Rythu Sangham. Statement 2 is correct: N.G. Ranga presided at Venkatagiri in September 1931. Statement 3 is correct: its goal was abolition of zamindari. So '2 and 3 only'; '3 only' misses statement 2, and options with 1 include the wrong house.
217.tq: Nellore Sangham met at Dodla Ramireddy's house; Venkatagiri 1931 = Ranga, abolition.
xs: Statements **2 and 3 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 wrong: the Nellore Sangham first met (**19 Oct 1929**) at **Dodla Ramireddy's** house.
Statement 2 correct: **N.G. Ranga** presided at **Venkatagiri**, **Sept 1931**.
Statement 3 correct: its goal was the **abolition of zamindari**.
xa: **Bhupathiraju Venkatapathiraju** was President of the **Andhra Rashtra Zamindari Rythu Sangham**.
Nellore Sangham founders also included **Duvvuri Ramakrishna Reddy** and **Nellore Venkataramana Naidu**.

217.s:
With reference to the Andhra Rashtra Zamindari Rythu Sangham, consider the following statements:
1. It was formed in August 1929.
2. Jagannadhadasu of Ganjam was associated with its founding.
3. Bhupathiraju Venkatapathiraju served as its President.
4. Mandeswara Sarma served as its General Secretary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
217.x: All four statements are correct. The organisation was formed in August 1929, with Jagannadhadasu of Ganjam associated with its formation, Bhupathiraju Venkatapathiraju as President and Mandeswara Sarma as General Secretary.
217.tq: Check each office-bearer and date before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2, 3 and 4**.
The **Andhra Rashtra Zamindari Rythu Sangham** was formed in **Aug 1929**, by **Jagannadhadasu (Ganjam)**.
President **Bhupathiraju Venkatapathiraju**; Gen. Sec. **Mandeswara Sarma**.
xa: The Nellore Dist. Sangham came on **19 Oct 1929**.
First Zamindar Rythu Sabha, North Andhra: **3 Nov 1929, Vizag**.

217.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Zamin Ryot — edited by N.G. Ranga
Rythu Bidda — written by Dodla Ramireddy
217.x: The First Zamindar Rythu Sabha in North Andhra started Prajavani, which was edited by Garimella Krishnamurthy.
217.tq: Use the publication-editor association to eliminate swapped names and places.
xs: **Prajavani — edited by Garimella Krishnamurthy** — option **(1)**.
**Zamin Ryot** was **Nellore Venkataramana Naidu's** paper; **Rythu Bidda** was **Gudavalli Ramabrahmam's** film.
Prajavani was started at **Vizag** (**1929**), not Venkatagiri **1931**.
xa: ⚠ **Prajavani** = Vizag; **Zamin Ryot** = Nellore (**March 1930**).
Venkatagiri **Sept 1931** = **first anti-zamindari conference** (N.G. Ranga).

217.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Jameen Ryot Mahasabha is correct?
o: It campaigned for the continuation of zamindari with reduced rents.
It demanded the abolition of ryotwari settlements.
It was formed to protect the rights of zamindars over forest produce.
It demanded in 1938 that the government enact a Zamindari Abolition Act.
217.x: The Jameen Ryot Mahasabha campaigned for abolition of zamindari and, in 1938, demanded a Zamindari Abolition Act.
217.tq: Separate an organisation’s abolitionist demand from opposing zamindari-era claims.
xs: The **Jameen Ryot Mahasabha** in **1938** demanded a **Zamindari Abolition Act** — option **(4)** (**GS 2023**).
It campaigned for **abolishing** zamindari, not continuing it.
xa: The **Prakasam Committee** report was completed on **7 Nov 1938**.
The abolition Act finally came in **1948**.

217.s: The rent in Gampalagudem estate was collected primarily:
o: In cash after annual auction of grazing lands
In kind, resulting in excessive extraction
Through a fixed payment of 60 seers per acre
As a renewal fee called nazarana
217.x: In Gampalagudem, rent was collected in kind rather than cash, leading to excessive extraction.
217.tq: Distinguish the mode of rent collection from other estate grievances and levies.
xs: At **Gampalagudem** rent was collected **in kind instead of cash**, causing **excessive extraction** — option **(2)** (**GS 2023**).
**Grazing-land auction** is Venkatagiri's **Kancha paddhati**; **60 seers** is the Munagala wage cut; **nazarana** is a renewal fee.
xa: **Kalipatnam**: **4,000 acres** grabbed for a project, never returned.
**Munagala** (**1938-39**): wage cut from **80 to 60 seers** per acre.

217.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Kancha paddhati in the Venkatagiri estate?
o: Waste land was seized for lanka cultivation.
Rent was collected only in harvested grain.
Grazing land was auctioned every year.
Forest land was transferred permanently to tenants.
217.x: Under the Kancha paddhati, grazing land in the Venkatagiri estate was auctioned annually.
217.tq: Match the exact local practice with its meaning.
xs: Under **Kancha paddhati**, **grazing land was auctioned every year** at **Venkatagiri** — option **(3)**.
**Lanka/waste land seizure** was the **Challapalli** grievance.
xa: **Pullari** (grazing tax) was collected at Venkatagiri **even in drought**.
The **Palemkota** revolt came on **20 Mar 1933**.

217.s:
Consider the following statements about the Venkatagiri estate agitation:
1. Venkatagiri was the second largest estate in Coastal Andhra.
2. Pullari was collected even during drought.
3. The Palemkota revolt took place on 20 March 1933.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
217.x: All three statements are correct. The estate was the second largest in Coastal Andhra, pullari was collected even during drought, and the Palemkota revolt occurred on 20 March 1933.
217.tq: Combine estate status, tax practice and a precise revolt date.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
**Venkatagiri** was the **2nd largest Coastal Andhra estate**; **pullari** was taken **even in drought**.
The **Palemkota** revolt took place on **20 Mar 1933**.
xa: **Gandhi** visited Venkatagiri on **20 Dec 1933**.
Leaders: **Ponaka Kanakamma**, **Vennelakanti Raghavaiah**, **Dodla Ramireddy**.

217.s:
With reference to the Challapalli estate agitation in Krishna district, consider the following statements:
1. Its zamindar was Yarlagadda Sivarama Prasad.
2. The agitation, from June 1930, was against the seizure of lanka and waste land and against vetti.
3. Its main grievance was a cut in the harvest wage from 80 to 60 seers per acre.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
217.x: Statement 1 is correct: Yarlagadda Sivarama Prasad was the Challapalli zamindar. Statement 2 is correct: from June 1930 the issues were seizure of lanka/waste land and vetti. Statement 3 is wrong: the 80-to-60 seers wage cut was the Munagala grievance (1938-39). So '1 and 2 only'.
217.tq: Challapalli = lanka land + vetti; Munagala = wage cut 80 to 60 seers.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: zamindar **Yarlagadda Sivarama Prasad**.
Statement 2 correct: from **June 1930**, against **lanka/waste land** seizure and **vetti**.
Statement 3 wrong: the **80-to-60 seers** wage cut was **Munagala's** (**1938-39**).
xa: Challapalli leaders: **Gorrepati Venkata Subbayya**, **Chandra Rajeswara Rao**.
Munagala zamindar: **Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao**.

217.s: Which of the following estate–agitation pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kalipatnam — 4,000 acres grabbed for a project and not returned
Gampalagudem — annual auction of grazing land under Kancha paddhati
Mandasa — forest-cutting arrests followed by police firing
Munagala — harvest wage reduced from 80 to 60 seers per acre
217.x: Annual auction of grazing land under Kancha paddhati was associated with Venkatagiri, not Gampalagudem. Gampalagudem involved rent collection in kind and excessive extraction.
217.tq: Find the swapped estate–grievance pair.
xs: **Gampalagudem — Kancha paddhati** is wrongly matched — option **(2)**.
**Kancha paddhati** (yearly grazing-land auction) was **Venkatagiri's**; Gampalagudem's issue was **rent in kind**.
The rest are correct: **Kalipatnam** (**4,000 acres**), **Mandasa** (police firing), **Munagala** (**80 to 60 seers**).
xa: Kalipatnam (**1928-39**) was led by **Bhupathiraju Lakshmi Narasimha Raju**.
Munagala zamindar: **Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao**.

217.s: Which one of the following statements about the Mandasa agitation is correct?
o: It began in June 1930 under Yarlagadda Sivarama Prasad.
It was led by the annual auction of grazing lands.
It occurred on 1 April 1940 and police firing killed five persons, including Pusumanu Gunnamma.
It concerned a wage cut from 80 to 60 seers per acre.
217.x: The Mandasa agitation occurred on 1 April 1940 after arrests for forest cutting; police firing killed five persons, including Pusumanu Gunnamma.
217.tq: Combine the date, immediate cause and consequence of an agitation.
xs: **Mandasa** (Srikakulam): **1 April 1940**, police firing **killed 5**, including **Pusumanu Gunnamma** — option **(3)**.
It began with **forest-cutting arrests**.
**June 1930 / Yarlagadda** is **Challapalli**; the **80-to-60 seers** cut is **Munagala**.
xa: Grazing-land auction (**Kancha paddhati**) belonged to **Venkatagiri**.
**Gothi** (hereditary bonded labour) was an **Agency** practice.

217.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Nellore/Venkatagiri — Yakasiri Chellamma, associated with women’s chilli-powder resistance
217.x: Yakasiri Chellamma was associated with the women’s chilli-powder resistance in the Nellore/Venkatagiri area.
217.tq: Discriminate among leaders belonging to different districts and local struggles.
xs: **Nellore/Venkatagiri — Yakasiri Chellamma** (women's **chilli-powder resistance**) — option **(1)**.
**Kalipatnam** was led by **Bhupathiraju Lakshmi Narasimha Raju**; **Gouthu Latchanna** led the **Ichchapuram yatra**.
**Ponaka Kanakamma** belongs to **Nellore**, not Srikakulam.
xa: Other Nellore leaders: **Petturi Govinda Reddy**, **Baddedi Venkatanarayana Reddy** (Gudur MLA).
Gouthu Latchanna and **Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao** petitioned the **Prakasam Committee**.

217.s: Who directed the film Rythu Bidda, released in 1939 and banned by the zamindar?
217.x: Rythu Bidda was directed by Gudavalli Ramabrahmam, released in 1939, and banned by the zamindar.
217.tq: Match a cultural work with its creator and its political context.
xs: **Rythu Bidda** (**1939**) was made by **Gudavalli Ramabrahmam** — option **(1)**.
It was **banned by the zamindar**.
**Garimella Krishnamurthy** edited **Prajavani**.
xa: **Gandhi** visited **Venkatagiri** on **20 Dec 1933**.
**Nellore Venkataramana Naidu** ran the paper **Zamin Ryot**.

217.s: Ponaka Kanakamma, named in the APPSC Group 2 2008 key, was a leader of the anti-zamindari struggle in which area?
217.x: Ponaka Kanakamma led the anti-zamindari struggle in Nellore/Venkatagiri, alongside Vennelakanti Raghavaiah, Dodla Ramireddy and Yakasiri Chellamma. Kalipatnam was led by Bhupathiraju Lakshmi Narasimha Raju; Challapalli by Gorrepati Venkata Subbayya and Chandra Rajeswara Rao; Mandasa saw the 1940 police firing that killed Pusumanu Gunnamma.
217.tq: Ponaka Kanakamma = Nellore/Venkatagiri.
xs: **Ponaka Kanakamma** led the struggle in **Nellore / Venkatagiri** — option **(1)** (**G2 2008** key).
**Kalipatnam** — **Bhupathiraju Lakshmi Narasimha Raju**; **Challapalli** — **Gorrepati Venkata Subbayya**, **Chandra Rajeswara Rao**.
**Mandasa** saw the **1940** firing that killed **Pusumanu Gunnamma**.
xa: Fellow Nellore leaders: **Vennelakanti Raghavaiah**, **Dodla Ramireddy**, **Yakasiri Chellamma**.
**Gandhi** visited **Venkatagiri** on **20 Dec 1933**.

217.s: In which year did the Madras Congress Ministry appoint the committee on the zamindari system, with C. Rajagopalachari as Chief Minister and Tanguturi Prakasam as Revenue Minister?
217.x: The Madras Congress Ministry appointed the committee in 1937. C. Rajagopalachari was the Chief Minister and Tanguturi Prakasam served as the Revenue Minister.
217.tq: Use the ministry-composition clue to identify the correct year and distinguish the Chief Minister from the Revenue Minister.
xs: The committee was appointed in **1937** by the Madras Congress ministry — option **(2)**.
**Rajaji** was CM and **Prakasam** **Revenue Minister**.
It was **formally constituted** in **Sept 1938** (**9** members) per some notes.
xa: Also called the **Estate Land / Zamindari Enquiry Committee**.
Report completed **7 Nov 1938**.

217.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Completion of the report of the zamindari enquiry committee
B. Appointment of the committee by the Madras Congress Ministry
C. Formal constitution of the committee
D. Passage of the Madras Act that became one of the early abolition laws
217.x: The correct sequence is appointment in 1937, formal constitution in September 1938, completion of the report on 7 November 1938, and the Madras Act of 1948.
217.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two 1938 committee events in their proper order.
xs: Correct order: **B, C, A, D** — option **(1)**.
**Appointment (1937)** → **formal constitution (Sept 1938)**.
→ **report completed (7 Nov 1938)** → **Madras Act (1948)**.
xa: ⚠ **Prakasam** = Revenue Minister in **1937**; **Kala Venkata Rao** = Revenue Minister who introduced the **1947** Bill.
Gouthu Latchanna's **Ichchapuram** yatra petitioned this committee.

217.s: Which of the following was the principal conclusion of the committee’s report regarding the relationship between land, the tiller and the zamindar?
o: The State alone owned the land and the zamindar had no role in revenue collection.
The zamindar was the absolute owner of the land and the tiller was only a tenant.
Land belonged jointly to the zamindar and the cultivating tenants.
Land belonged to the tiller, while the zamindar was merely a tax collector.
217.x: The report held that land belongs to the tiller and that the zamindar is only a tax collector.
217.tq: Test the precise relationship stated in the report and avoid the swapped-owner and tenant descriptions.
xs: The report held that **land belongs to the tiller** and the **zamindar is only a tax collector** — option **(4)**.
The report was completed on **7 Nov 1938**.
xa: **Prakasam** regretted it did not say outright whether **zamindari should be abolished**.
**Communists** pioneered the **land to the tiller** demand.

217.s: What did Tanguturi Prakasam regret about the report of the zamindari enquiry committee?
o: That it failed to discuss the position of the tiller
That it did not identify the zamindari areas of the Madras Presidency
That it recommended continuation of zamindari without reforms
That it did not state outright whether zamindari should be abolished
217.x: Prakasam regretted that the report did not say expressly whether the zamindari system should be abolished.
217.tq: Look for the precise limitation of the report rather than assuming that its criticism of zamindari amounted to an explicit abolition recommendation.
xs: Prakasam regretted that the report **did not say outright whether zamindari should be abolished** — option **(4)**.
It did address the **tiller** — land belongs to the tiller — so option (1) is wrong.
xa: Committee appointed in **1937** under **Rajaji** (CM) and **Prakasam** (Revenue Minister).
The **Jameen Ryot Mahasabha** in **1938** demanded a **Zamindari Abolition Act**.

217.s: Who led the yatra from Ichchapuram to submit a petition to the committee on the zamindari system?
o: Gouthu Latchanna and Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao
Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao and C. Rajagopalachari
217.x: Gouthu Latchanna and Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao led the yatra from Ichchapuram to petition the committee.
217.tq: Match the specific action and starting place with the correct pair of leaders.
xs: The **Ichchapuram** yatra was led by **Gouthu Latchanna and Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao** — option **(2)**.
They petitioned the **Prakasam Committee**.
xa: The committee's report was completed on **7 Nov 1938**.
**Mandasa** (Srikakulam) saw police firing on **1 April 1940**.

217.s: Who introduced the Madras Estates Abolition Bill on 11 November 1947?
217.x: Revenue Minister Kala Venkata Rao introduced the Bill on 11 November 1947.
217.tq: Identify the minister associated with introducing legislation rather than giving assent to it.
xs: Revenue Minister **Kala Venkata Rao** introduced the Bill on **11 Nov 1947** — option **(2)**.
**C. Rajagopalachari**, as **Governor-General**, gave assent on **2 Apr 1949**.
**Pattabhi** called for the struggle in **1920**; **N.G. Ranga** presided at Venkatagiri (**1931**).
xa: The Bill was passed by the **Madras Assembly** in **Nov 1948**.
It came into force on **7 Sept 1949**.

217.s:
Consider the following statements about the consequences of the Estates Abolition legislation:
1. It abolished zamindari and inamdari estates.
2. Tenants became direct ryots of the state.
3. Zamindars were paid compensation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
217.x: The legislation abolished zamindari and inamdari estates, made tenants direct ryots of the state and provided compensation to zamindars.
217.tq: Test the three principal legal consequences together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
The Act **abolished zamindari and inamdari estates**; **tenants became direct ryots of the state**.
**Zamindars were paid compensation**.
xa: The **1st (1951)** and **4th (1955)** Amendments shielded abolition laws.
Estates were taken over from **1950**.

217.s: The assent of Governor-General C. Rajagopalachari to the Estates Abolition law was given on:
217.x: Governor-General C. Rajagopalachari gave assent on 2 April 1949. It was the first law of independent India to receive the Governor-General’s assent.
217.tq: Separate the Bill-introduction, Assembly-passage, assent and commencement dates.
xs: **Governor-General C. Rajagopalachari** gave assent on **2 April 1949** — option **(4)**.
It was the **first law of independent India** to get the GG's assent.
**11 Nov 1947** = Bill introduced; **Nov 1948** = passed; **7 Sept 1949** = in force.
xa: Bill introduced by **Kala Venkata Rao**.
Estates were taken over from **1950**.

217.s: Which statement regarding the commencement and implementation of the Estates Abolition law is correct?
o: It came into force on 2 April 1949, while estates were taken over from 1951.
It came into force in November 1948, while estates were taken over from 1949.
It came into force on 7 September 1949, while estates were taken over from 1950.
It came into force on 11 November 1947, while estates were taken over from 1948.
217.x: The law came into force on 7 September 1949, and estates were taken over from 1950.
217.tq: Distinguish the commencement date of an Act from the later administrative takeover.
xs: The Act **came into force on 7 September 1949**; estates were **taken over from 1950** — option **(3)**.
**2 Apr 1949** is the GG's assent; **Nov 1948** the Assembly's passing; **11 Nov 1947** the Bill.
xa: ⚠ Some notes call it the "**1949**" Act, effective **1950**; its name year is **1948**.
Tenants became **direct ryots of the state**.

217.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Introduction of the Estates Abolition Bill by Kala Venkata Rao
B. Passage of the Act by the Madras Assembly
C. Assent of Governor-General C. Rajagopalachari
D. The Act came into force

Select the correct sequence.
217.x: The Bill was introduced on 11 November 1947, passed in November 1948, received assent on 2 April 1949, and came into force on 7 September 1949.
217.tq: Fix the first and last events, then place passage and assent between them.
xs: Correct order: **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**Bill introduced (11 Nov 1947)** → **passed (Nov 1948)**.
→ **assent (2 Apr 1949)** → **in force (7 Sept 1949)**.
xa: The **G2 2025** chronology: **Guntur acquired (1788)** → **Padmanabham (1794)** → Ryotwari → abolition.
Estates were taken over from **1950**.

217.s: The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, which abolished zamindari in Andhra, bears which year in its name?
217.x: It is the 1948 Act (APPSC G2 2008 PYQ: pick 1948). Trap: some sources call it the 1949 Act because it received assent on 2 April 1949 and came into force on 7 September 1949; estates were taken over from 1950; the Bill was introduced on 11 November 1947.
217.tq: Act year 1948; assent and commencement 1949; takeover 1950.
xs: The Act's name year is **1948** — option **(1)** (**G2 2008** PYQ).
⚠ Some notes call it the "**1949**" Act because assent and commencement fell in **1949**; takeover from **1950**.
**1947** is the year the **Bill** was introduced.
xa: It was the **first law** of independent India to get the GG's assent.
It abolished **zamindari and inamdari estates**.

217.s: Which Constitutional Amendments shielded zamindari abolition laws such as the Madras Act of 1948?
217.x: The 1st Amendment (1951) and the 4th Amendment (1955) shielded zamindari abolition laws from challenge. The other pairs are not the amendments that gave this protection.
217.tq: Abolition laws shielded by the 1st (1951) and 4th (1955) Amendments.
xs: The **1st (1951)** and **4th (1955)** Amendments shielded zamindari abolition laws — option **(1)**.
They protected Acts like the **Madras Act of 1948**.
xa: The Madras Act **paid compensation** to zamindars.
Tenants became **direct ryots** of the state.

217.s: Which one of the following best expresses the significance of the anti-zamindari agitations in Andhra?
o: They resulted in the establishment of the zamindari system throughout the Madras Presidency in 1948.
They led to the replacement of the Madras Presidency by a separate zamindari administration.
They helped make the Madras Act of 1948 one of the first zamindari abolition laws of independent India.
They postponed all legislation on zamindari abolition until the 1960s.
217.x: The agitations in Andhra helped create the political conditions in which the Madras Act of 1948 became one of the first abolition laws of independent India.
217.tq: Distinguish a historical significance statement from options that reverse the outcome of the movement.
xs: Andhra's agitations helped make the **Madras Act of 1948** one of the **first abolition laws of independent India** — option **(3)**.
The Act **abolished** zamindari; it did not establish it.
xa: It was the first law of independent India to get the **GG's assent** (**2 Apr 1949**).
**40%** of Andhra's land was under zamindars at Independence.

217.s: Which organisation is associated with pioneering the demand for ‘land to the tiller’ and the abolition of zamindari?
217.x: The communists pioneered the demand for land to the tiller and for the abolition of zamindari.
217.tq: Use the distinctive political demand to identify the organisation associated with it.
xs: The **communists** pioneered the demand for **land to the tiller** and **zamindari abolition** — option **(4)** (**PT365, Apr 2026**).
**Pattabhi** had first called for an anti-zamindari struggle in **1920**, but the land-to-tiller demand is credited to the communists.
xa: The Prakasam Committee also said **land belongs to the tiller**.
Agitators: **Chandra Rajeswara Rao**, **Nanduri Prasada Rao** (Challapalli/Munagala).

217.s: Approximately what proportion of zamindari land in the Madras Presidency was concentrated in Vizag, Nellore, the two Godavaris, Krishna and Chittoor?
217.x: About 70 percent of the zamindari land in the Madras Presidency lay in Vizag, Nellore, the two Godavari districts, Krishna and Chittoor.
217.tq: Identify the exact percentage before assessing the geographical grouping associated with it.
xs: About **70 percent** (**70%**) of Madras Presidency zamindari land lay in **Vizag, Nellore, the two Godavaris, Krishna and Chittoor** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **40%** is the share of Andhra's land still under zamindars at Independence.
xa: **Venkatagiri** (Nellore) was the **2nd largest** Coastal Andhra estate.
**Challapalli** lay in **Krishna**; **Kalipatnam** in **W. Godavari**.

218.s:
Consider the following statements about N.G. Ranga:
1. He was popularly called Rythu Bandhu and 'Acharya'.
2. He received the Bharat Ratna in 1991.
3. He is regarded as the founder of the Andhra Kisan movement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
