218.x: Statement 1 is correct: Ranga was called Rythu Bandhu and Acharya (also Father of the Indian Peasant Movement). Statement 2 is wrong: he received the Padma Vibhushan in 1991, not the Bharat Ratna. Statement 3 is correct: he founded the Andhra Kisan movement. So '1 and 3 only'.
218.tq: Ranga 1991 = Padma Vibhushan.
xs: **Statements 1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 3 only** is the answer.
Statement 1 is correct: **N.G. Ranga** was called **Rythu Bandhu** and **"Acharya"**.
Statement 2 is wrong: Ranga received the **Padma Vibhushan** in **1991**, not the Bharat Ratna.
Statement 3 is correct: Ranga was the **founder of the Andhra Kisan movement** (G2 2019, 2011 keys).
xa: Ranga is also called the **Father of the Indian Peasant Movement**; his full name is **Gogineni Ranganayakulu**.
Ranga's journals: **Praja Bandhu** and **Navayuga**.
Ranga's books: **Credo of World Peasantry**, **Revolutionary Peasantry**, **Fight for Freedom**.
Ranga was the first President of the **Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham (1928)** and Secretary of the **AIKS (1936)**.

218.s: Which one of the following statements regarding N.G. Ranga is correct?
o: He founded the Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham alone in 1915.
He was known as the Father of the Indian Peasant Movement.
He led the 1937 Rythu Yatra as a village association organiser.
218.x: N.G. Ranga was known as the Father of the Indian Peasant Movement. The Munagala Award was authored by Gottipati Brahmaiah, while the 1937 Rythu Yatra was led by Kommareddi Satyanarayana.
218.tq: Use the leader–title association and reject swapped deeds.
xs: **N.G. Ranga** was known as the **Father of the Indian Peasant Movement** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **Munagala Award** was authored by **Gottipati Brahmaiah**, not Ranga.
The **Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham** was founded in **1928** by Ranga with **Narasimha Devara Satyanarayana** and **Maganti Bapineedu** — not alone, not in 1915.
The **1937 Rythu Yatra** was led on the ground by **Kommareddi Satyanarayana**; Ranga launched it.
xa: **1915** is the year of the **Krishna District Rythu Sangham**, a predecessor body.
Ranga also bore the titles **Rythu Bandhu** and **"Acharya"**; he got the **Padma Vibhushan** in **1991**.
⚠ Trap: **Kommareddi** led the 1937 yatra; **Ranga** launched it on **3 July 1937**.
After WWII differences, Ranga founded the **Andhra Rashtra Kisan Congress (1943)**.

218.s: Who among the following authored the Munagala Award?
218.x: Gottipati Brahmaiah authored the Munagala Award. He was also a pioneer of the zamindari ryot movement and Secretary of the APCC.
218.tq: Match the named document with its author, guarding against swapped deeds.
xs: The **Munagala Award** was authored by **Gottipati Brahmaiah** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **Brahmaiah Award** of **15 Jan 1939** settled the Munagala dispute across **142 villages**.
**Kommareddi Satyanarayana** led the 1937 Rythu Yatra; **Nanduri Prasada Rao** led the **Kalukova Satyagraha (1938)**.
xa: Brahmaiah was a pioneer of the **zamindari ryot movement** and **APCC Secretary**.
He led the **1931 Mopidevi no-tax resolution** (Divi taluk Resettlement Mahasabha).
The Award was later broken; **Uppala Ramayya** led land occupations and **350 women** were lathi-charged.
Munagala zamindar: **Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao**.

218.s:
Kommareddi Satyanarayana is associated with which of the following activities?

1. Formation of village peasant associations in 1935
2. Leadership of the 1937 Rythu Yatra
3. Presidency of the All India Kisan Sabha in 1936

Which of the statements given above are correct?
218.x: Kommareddi Satyanarayana formed village peasant associations in 1935 and led the 1937 Rythu Yatra. The 1936 AIKS President was Swami Sahajanand Saraswati.
218.tq: Separate a leader’s documented activities from a similar organisational position.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Kommareddi Satyanarayana** formed **village peasant associations** in **1935**.
Statement 2 is correct: he led the **1937 Rythu Yatra** on the ground.
Statement 3 is wrong: the first AIKS President (**1936**) was **Swami Sahajanand Saraswati**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: the 1937 yatra was **launched by N.G. Ranga** on **3 July 1937** but **led by Kommareddi**.
The **Ichchapuram-Madras Rythu Rakshana Yatra** was compared to the **Dandi March**.
It ended with a memorandum to Speaker **Bulusu Sambamurthy**.
**N.G. Ranga** was the AIKS **Secretary** in 1936.

218.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao — Srikakulam kisan leader
2. Gouthu Latchanna — Srikakulam kisan leader
3. Gottipati Brahmaiah — Srikakulam kisan leader

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
218.x: Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao and Gouthu Latchanna were Srikakulam kisan leaders. Gottipati Brahmaiah is associated with the zamindari ryot movement and the Munagala Award.
218.tq: Use the regional association to eliminate the swapped leader.
xs: **Pairs 1 and 2** are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
**Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao** and **Gouthu Latchanna** were **Srikakulam kisan leaders**.
Pair 3 is wrong: **Gottipati Brahmaiah** was a pioneer of the **zamindari ryot movement**, APCC Secretary and author of the **Munagala Award**.
xa: **Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao** died in jail after the **Mandasa protest**.
Brahmaiah led the **1931 Mopidevi no-tax resolution**.
**Palasa** (Srikakulam region) hosted the **AIKS session** in **March 1940**, presided by **Sahajanand**.

218.s: Which of the following is NOT a book associated with N.G. Ranga?
218.x: Credo of World Peasantry, Revolutionary Peasantry and Fight for Freedom are books associated with N.G. Ranga. The Munagala Award was authored by Gottipati Brahmaiah and is not a book of Ranga.
218.tq: Find the item that belongs to the neighbouring leader rather than the named author.
xs: The **Munagala Award** is not a Ranga book — option **(4)** is correct; it was authored by **Gottipati Brahmaiah**.
**Credo of World Peasantry**, **Revolutionary Peasantry** and **Fight for Freedom** are **N.G. Ranga's books**.
xa: Ranga's journals: **Praja Bandhu** and **Navayuga**.
⚠ Trap: **Zamin Ryot** = **Nellore**; **Prajavani** = **Vizag** — not Ranga's.
The Brahmaiah (Munagala) Award is dated **15 Jan 1939** and covered **142 villages**.

218.s: Who died in jail after the Mandasa protest?
o: A leader of the AIKS at Hansi
218.x: Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao died in jail after the Mandasa protest.
218.tq: Match the individual with the specific consequence and event rather than with a similar agrarian association.
xs: **Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao** died in jail after the **Mandasa protest** — option **(2)** is correct.
He was a **Srikakulam kisan leader**, along with **Gouthu Latchanna**.
**N.G. Ranga** was jailed after the **Palasa** session, when he defied his confinement to **Nidubrolu** — he did not die in jail.
xa: AIKS remains active: it protested police action at **Hansi, Haryana** (Aug **2026**).
The **Palasa AIKS session** was held in **March 1940**, presided by **Swami Sahajanand Saraswati**.
Ranga's 1938-39 cycle rally ran from **Ichchapuram** to **Madras** against the **Madras Land Settlement Act**.

218.s: The Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham was founded in:
218.x: The Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham was founded in 1928. It merged into the AIKS in 1936.
218.tq: Distinguish the association’s founding year from the years of predecessor bodies and merger.
xs: The **Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham** was founded in **1928** — option **(3)** is correct.
**1915** was the **Krishna District Rythu Sangham**; **1923** the **Guntur and Godavari sanghams** (predecessors).
**1936** was when the Sangham **merged into the AIKS**, founded that year at **Lucknow**.
xa: Founders: **N.G. Ranga**, **Narasimha Devara Satyanarayana** and **Maganti Bapineedu**; based at **Vijayawada**.
First President: **Ranga**; first General Secretary: **B.V. Ratnam**.
It is also called the **Andhra Provincial Ryots Association, 1928**.

218.s:
Who among the following were the founders of the Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham?

1. N.G. Ranga
2. Narasimha Devara Satyanarayana
3. Maganti Bapineedu
4. B.V. Ratnam

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
218.x: N.G. Ranga, Narasimha Devara Satyanarayana and Maganti Bapineedu founded the Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham. B.V. Ratnam was its first General Secretary, not a listed founder.
218.tq: Separate founders from the later office-bearers of the organisation.
xs: The founders were **N.G. Ranga**, **Narasimha Devara Satyanarayana** and **Maganti Bapineedu** — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**B.V. Ratnam** was the **first General Secretary**, not a listed founder.
xa: The Sangham was founded in **1928**, based at **Vijayawada**, with **Ranga** as first President.
It **merged into the AIKS in 1936**.
Predecessors: **Krishna District Rythu Sangham (1915)**; **Guntur and Godavari sanghams (1923)**.

218.s: Which one of the following statements about the Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham is correct?
o: It was based at Palasa and merged into the AIKS in 1940.
It was based at Lucknow and was founded by Swami Sahajanand Saraswati.
It was based at Nidubrolu, with B.V. Ratnam as first President.
It was based at Vijayawada, with N.G. Ranga as first President and B.V. Ratnam as first General Secretary.
218.x: The Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham was based at Vijayawada. N.G. Ranga was its first President and B.V. Ratnam its first General Secretary; it merged into the AIKS in 1936.
218.tq: Test headquarters and office-bearers together, guarding against organisational swaps.
xs: The Sangham was based at **Vijayawada**, with **N.G. Ranga** as **first President** and **B.V. Ratnam** as **first General Secretary** — option **(4)**.
It merged into the AIKS in **1936**, not 1940; **Palasa** hosted the **AIKS session** of **March 1940**.
**Lucknow** is where the **AIKS** was founded (April **1936**) under **Swami Sahajanand Saraswati** — not this Sangham.
**Nidubrolu** is where Ranga was confined before the Palasa session.

219.tq: Hul began 30 June 1855, crushed 1856.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: the British failed to control the **Paharias** and invited the **Santhals** to the **Rajmahal Hills**.
Statement 2: the tract was **Damin-i-Koh**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the Hul began at **Bhognadih** on **30 June 1855** (**Hul Divas**); it was crushed in **1856**.
xa: Leaders: **Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu**, **Chand and Bhairav**, sisters **Phulo-Jhano**.
About **30,000 Santhals** proclaimed **Santhal Raj**; over **15,000** were killed.

219.s: Which of the following groups was associated with the leadership of the Santhal Hul in addition to Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu?
o: Chand, Bhairav and the sisters Phulo-Jhano
Jatra Bhagat, Govind Giri and Motilal Tejawat
Umaji Naik, Chittur Singh and Narayan Rao
Ganga Narayan, Budhu Bhagat and Tirot Sing

219.s: Which one of the following was an important cause of the Santhal Hul?
o: Oppression by zamindars, moneylenders and police
The abolition of the Khuntkatti system by the Santhals themselves
The transfer of Upper Assam to Purandar Singh
The introduction of bonded labour in Mewar
219.x: The Santhals faced oppression by zamindars, moneylenders, commonly called dikus, and the police. The Khuntkatti issue belonged principally to the Munda movement.
219.tq: Match the cause with the revolt instead of the similarly worded causes of other movements.
xs: The Hul was caused by **oppression by zamindars, moneylenders (dikus) and police** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Khuntkatti** destruction was the **Munda** (Birsa) grievance; **Purandar Singh** relates to the **Ahom** rebellion; **bonded labour** to **Govind Giri's** Bhils.

219.s: After the Santhal Hul, which one of the following developments took place?
o: Santhal Parganas became a separate district with special laws protecting tribal land.

xs: After the Hul, **Santhal Parganas** became a **separate district with special laws protecting tribal land** — option **(1)**.
The **Chotanagpur Tenancy Act** is of **1908**, not 1876.
**Munda-Manki** rule in Kolhan came via **Wilkinson's Rule (1837)**, after the **Kol** rising.
xa: The **Santhal Parganas Tenancy Act** is dated **1876** in some notes; the current SPT Act = **1949**.
The CNT Act **bars transfer of tribal land to non-tribals** and recognises **Khuntkatti** rights.
The Hul was crushed in **1856**; over **15,000** killed.

220.tq: Calculate the anniversary from the Act's year and compare the numerical options.
xs: **2026** marks **100 years** of the **Trade Unions Act 1926** — option **(3)** is correct.

xa: It came from **N.M. Joshi's March 1921** resolution.

A **nine-judge** SC Bench (**Aug 2026**) held the **1978** "industry" definition does not apply to the **Industrial Relations Code**.

220.s:

2. The decline of trade unions is traced to the collapse of the 1974 railway strike.

220.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 1974 railway strike is an example of the 1950s-70s peak. Statement 2 is wrong: the decline is traced to the collapse of the 1982 Bombay textile strike. Hence 1 only.
220.tq: 1974 railway = peak; 1982 Bombay textile collapse = decline.
xs: Only **statement 1** is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: union activity peaked in the **1950s-70s**, e.g. the **1974 railway strike**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the decline is traced to the collapse of the **1982 Bombay textile strike**.
xa: **AITUC** general secretary **Amarjeet Kaur** criticised the SC ruling on the **Industrial Relations Code**.
The Code **replaced the Industrial Disputes Act**.
**10 Left parties** protested in **Vijayawada** (Mar **2026**).

221.s: Which publication was founded and edited by Madduri Annapurnaiah?
221.x: Madduri Annapurnaiah founded and edited the Congress newspaper.

xa: Annapurnaiah was born **20 March 1899** at **Komaragiri**, **Pithapuram taluk**.

221.x: He was jailed for publishing “Chicharapidugu”, associated with the 1857 and Manyam rebellion themes.

xs: Annapurnaiah was jailed for publishing **"Chicharapidugu"** — option **(2)** is correct.

**Mother** is **Gorky's** novel (Telugu translation by **K. Lingaraju**); **Navasakti** was a socialist Telugu journal.

Jailed in the **Salt Satyagraha**, he then joined the **CSP**.

221.s:

2. He founded the Krishikar Lok Party in 1951.

In **1955** the **KLP** won **22** seats in Andhra State.

221.s: Which Andhra leader, who joined the Congress Socialist Party after being jailed in the Salt Satyagraha, was called 'Andhra Netaji'?
221.x: Madduri Annapurnaiah (b. 1899, Komaragiri) was called 'Andhra Netaji'; jailed in the Salt Satyagraha, he then joined the CSP. N.G. Ranga founded the Andhra Socialist Party; Tenneti Viswanatham presided over its 1935 session; Sundarayya was a communist leader.

Jailed in the **Salt Satyagraha**, he then joined the **CSP**.
**Ranga** founded the Andhra Socialist Party; **Tenneti Viswanatham** presided the **1935** session; **Sundarayya** was a communist.

He founded and edited the **Congress** newspaper.

221.s:
Which of the following represents the correct chronological order of the three peasant initiatives?
A. Ichchapuram–Madras peasant march
B. Raithu Rakshana Sangham
C. Guntur Peasant Protection Rally
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
221.x: The Raithu Rakshana Sangham was founded in 1934, followed by the Guntur Peasant Protection Rally in 1935 and the Ichchapuram–Madras march during 1937–39.
221.tq: Fix the earliest year first, then place the rally before the later march.
xs: Order: **B, C, A** — option **(1)**.
**Raithu Rakshana Sangham** — **1934**; **Guntur Peasant Protection Rally** — **1935**; **Ichchapuram-Madras peasant march** — **1937-39**.
xa: The **Kooli Rakshana Samiti** was formed at **Guntur** in **March 1935**.
**Andhra Rashtra Yuva Mahasabhas**: **Vizag (1935)**, **Kakinada (1936)**.
The Raithu Rakshana Sangham was **Ranga's** body.

221.s: The Kooli Rakshana Samiti was formed at Guntur in March 1935 mainly to organise:
221.x: Because the CPI was banned, leftists organised workers and farm labourers through the Kooli Rakshana Samiti, formed at Guntur in March 1935.
221.tq: Infer the organisation’s social base from its programme and political context.
xs: The **Kooli Rakshana Samiti** organised **workers and farm labourers** — option **(1)** is correct.
With the **CPI banned**, leftists used it; it was formed at **Guntur** in **March 1935**.
xa: It spread to **Vijayawada**, **Nellore**, **Tenali**, **Eluru** and **Bhimavaram**.
**Annapurnaiah** was its prominent leader.
The CPI had been banned on **23 July 1934**.

221.s: The Andhra Rashtra Yuva Mahasabhas were held at:
221.x: The Andhra Rashtra Yuva Mahasabha was held at Vizag in 1935 and at Kakinada in 1936. Annapurnaiah was prominent in these youth activities.
221.tq: Use the place–year pair and reject the reversed sequence.
xs: The **Andhra Rashtra Yuva Mahasabhas** were at **Vizag in 1935** and **Kakinada in 1936** — option **(1)**.
**Guntur (1935)** hosted the **Kooli Rakshana Samiti**; **Nidubrolu** and **Kankipadu** were **Ranga's** training centres.
xa: **Sundarayya** was joint secretary of the **Vizag Yuva Mahasabha (1935)**.
The **Andhra Communist Party** was also founded at **Kakinada** in **January 1936**.
Annapurnaiah was prominent in the **Kooli Rakshana Samiti**.

221.s: The Peasant Institute at Nidubrolu was established during 1933–34 under the leadership of:
221.x: N.G. Ranga organised the Peasant Institute at Nidubrolu in Guntur during 1933–34. It was India’s first peasant training institute.
221.tq: Match the training centre with its organiser.
xs: The **Nidubrolu Peasant Institute** (**1933-34**) was led by **N.G. Ranga** — option **(2)** is correct.
It was **India's first peasant training institute**.
**Idukallu Sadasivan** ran the **Hindupur** school; **Annapragada Kameswara Rao** was at **Tulluru**.
xa: ⚠ **Nidubrolu** = first peasant training institute; **Kothapatnam** = first political summer school (**1937**); **Kankipadu** = **1939**.

Camps were **six-week** sessions from **April** on **politics and economics**.

221.s: Which one of the following was the first political summer school and was held in the summer of 1937?
221.x: Kothapatnam in Guntur district hosted the first political summer school in the summer of 1937.
221.tq: Identify the earliest school from place and year clues.
xs: **Kothapatnam** (Guntur dist.) hosted the **first political summer school** in **summer 1937** — option **(2)**.
**Madanapalle** and **Hindupur** schools date to **1938**; **Kankipadu** to **1939**.
xa: The Madras govt **lathi-charged** it and filed cases; **Prakasam** protested.
**Ranga** and others taught there.
**Nidubrolu** (**1933-34**) was India's first peasant training institute.

221.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

School or camp — Organiser
1. Madanapalle and Mantena vari Palem — N.G. Ranga
2. Hindupur political school — Idukallu Sadasivan

221.tq: Start from the sure organiser–place pairs and check all three entries.
xs: All three pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Madanapalle** and **Mantena vari Palem** (**1938**) — **N.G. Ranga**.
**Hindupur** school (**1938**) — **Idukallu Sadasivan** (communist); **Tulluru** — **Annapragada Kameswara Rao**.
xa: **Kothapatnam** = first political summer school (**1937**).
**Kankipadu Rajakeeya Pathashala** — Ranga, **1939** (G2 2012 key).
Format: **six-week** camps from **April**.

221.s: The six-week political training camps beginning in April primarily taught youth about:
221.x: The six-week camps taught politics and economics to youth.
221.tq: Identify the programme content rather than the location or organiser.
xs: The **six-week** camps from **April** taught youth **politics and economics** — option **(4)** is correct.
They trained the cadre that later led **peasant and labour struggles** in Andhra.
xa: First political summer school: **Kothapatnam (1937)**.
First peasant training institute: **Nidubrolu (1933-34)**.
**Kankipadu Rajakeeya Pathashala**: **1939**.

o: shifted to Hyderabad after a communist ban
221.x: The Kothapatnam summer school was lathi-charged, and Prakasam protested against the incident.
221.tq: Test the distinctive consequence associated with the named institution.
xs: The **Kothapatnam** school (**1937**) was **lathi-charged**, and **Prakasam protested** — option **(4)**.
The Madras govt also **filed cases** against it.
The **Rajakeeya Pathashala** was a separate school at **Kankipadu** (**1939**).
xa: Kothapatnam was the **first political summer school**.
**Ranga** and others taught there.
It lay in **Guntur** district.

Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
1. Kothapatnam — 1937
2. Madanapalle — 1938

xs: Only pair **4** is wrong — option **(4) 4 only**; the **Kankipadu Rajakeeya Pathashala** dates to **1939**, not 1935.
**Kothapatnam — 1937**, **Madanapalle — 1938** and **Mantena vari Palem — 1938** are correct.

**Nidubrolu** institute — **1933-34**.

o: *Navya Sahitya Mala* — Vidwan Viswam and Tarimela Nagi Reddy

xs: **Udayini — N.G. Ranga** is wrong — option **(3)**; **Udayini** was edited by **Kompella Janardhana Rao**.
**Congress** — **Annapurnaiah**; **Navya Sahitya Mala** — **Vidwan Viswam**, **Tarimela Nagi Reddy**; **Pratibha** — **Sivasankara Sastri**.

221.x: N.G. Ranga was associated with *Navayuga* and *Prajamitra*.

xs: **Navayuga** and **Prajamitra** were **N.G. Ranga's** journals — option **(4)** is correct.
**Congress** was **Annapurnaiah's**; **Udayini** was **Kompella Janardhana Rao's**; **Pratibha** was **Sivasankara Sastri's**.

**Translations** also spread socialist ideas.
Ranga founded the **Andhra Socialist Party (1934)**.

221.s: Which statement about *Navasakti* is correct?
o: It was edited by Kompella Janardhana Rao and founded in 1934.
It was regarded as the first wholly socialist Telugu journal; another account identifies it as the first communist paper at Rajahmundry on 15 December 1937.
It was the Telugu translation of Gorky’s *Mother*.

xs: **Navasakti** was the **first wholly socialist Telugu journal**; another account makes it the **first communist paper** (**Rajahmundry, 15 December 1937**) — option **(2)**.
**Kompella Janardhana Rao** edited **Udayini**, not Navasakti.
**Gorky's Mother** was translated by **K. Lingaraju**.
xa: **Pratibha** — **Sivasankara Sastri**.
Ranga's journals: **Navayuga**, **Prajamitra**.
**Congress** newspaper — **Annapurnaiah**.

221.s: The CPI was banned on:
221.x: The CPI was banned on 23 July 1934.
221.tq: Distinguish the ban date from the later founding and expulsion dates.
xs: The **CPI** was banned on **23 July 1934** — option **(2)** is correct.
**January 1936** = **Andhra Communist Party** at **Kakinada**; **1940** = CSP expelled communists; **15 Dec 1937** = **Navasakti** (per CDX).

Communists who joined: **Sundarayya**, **Chandra Rajeswara Rao**, **Krovi Lingaraju**, **Gadde Lingayya**.

221.s: Why did Andhra communists initially join Ranga’s Andhra Socialist Party?
o: To establish the Forward Bloc in Andhra
To contest elections independently of the Congress
Because the CPI was banned and they were advised to work inside the Congress
To support the Quit India Movement

221.tq: Link the institutional restriction with the strategic political response.
xs: With the **CPI banned**, they were advised (by **Prof. Gout**) to **work inside the Congress** — option **(3)**.
They joined **Ranga's Andhra Socialist Party**.
They **opposed** Quit India later, so option **(4)** is wrong.
xa: Communists who joined: **Sundarayya**, **Chandra Rajeswara Rao**, **Krovi Lingaraju**, **Gadde Lingayya**.
They formally founded the **Andhra Communist Party** at **Kakinada** in **January 1936**.
The CSP nationally **expelled the communists in 1940**.

2. Chandra Rajeswara Rao was its secretary at the founding.

221.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: P. Sundarayya was its secretary when it was formally founded at Kakinada in January 1936. Hence 1 only.

xs: Only **statement 1** is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: the **Andhra Communist Party** was founded at **Kakinada** in **January 1936**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Sundarayya** was its secretary, not Chandra Rajeswara Rao.
xa: Chandra Rajeswara Rao had joined **Ranga's Andhra Socialist Party** with other communists.

221.s: The national Congress Socialist Party expelled the communists in:
221.x: The Congress Socialist Party nationally expelled the communists in 1940.
221.tq: Place the expulsion after the Andhra Communist Party’s formation and before the People’s War position.
xs: The national CSP **expelled the communists in 1940** — option **(3)** is correct.
**1936** = Andhra Communist Party at Kakinada; **1941** = communists backed the **"People's War"**.
xa: In **WWII** the communists also **opposed Quit India**, widening the break.
The CPI was banned on **23 July 1934**.
Socialists and communists worked together **1934-1940**.

221.s: Which development widened the break between socialists and communists during the Second World War?
o: The CPI was unbanned on 23 July 1934.
The communists supported Quit India and opposed the People’s War.
The socialists dissolved the Andhra Socialist Party in 1936.
The communists supported the People’s War in 1941 and opposed Quit India.

221.tq: Identify the wartime policy difference that caused the later rupture.
xs: Communists backed the **"People's War" (1941)** and **opposed Quit India** — option **(4)** is correct.
Option **(2)** reverses their stand; the CPI was **banned**, not unbanned, on **23 July 1934**.
xa: Nationally the CSP had already **expelled the communists in 1940**.
The Andhra Communist Party was founded at **Kakinada** in **January 1936**.
Communists first worked inside the Congress via **Ranga's Andhra Socialist Party**.

221.s: Tenneti Viswanatham left the Indian National Congress in which year to found the Kisan Mazdoor Party?
221.x: Tenneti Viswanatham left the Congress in 1951 to found the Kisan Mazdoor Party.
221.tq: Discriminate between closely related years in the organisational history of the socialist movement.
xs: **Tenneti Viswanatham** left Congress in **1951** and founded the **Kisan Mazdoor Party** — option **(3)**.
**1952** is the year **KMPP + Socialist Party** merged into the **PSP**.
xa: Viswanatham presided the **1935** session (Guntur) of the Andhra Socialist Party.

221.s: The Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party merged nationally with which party in 1952 to form the Praja Socialist Party?
221.x: The Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party merged with the Socialist Party in 1952, resulting in the formation of the Praja Socialist Party.

xs: The **KMPP** merged with the **Socialist Party** in **1952** to form the **PSP** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Tanguturi Prakasam** founded the **Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party** and the **Praja Socialist Party**.
xa: **1952 Madras** election (**375** seats): **KMP 35**, **Socialists 13**.
In **1953** the **PSP wanted Tirupati** as the Andhra capital (G2 2025).
**1955** Andhra election: **PSP 13** seats.

221.s:

2. Governor Sri Prakasa invited Tanguturi Prakasam to form the government.

221.x: The Praja Socialist Party wanted Tirupati to be the capital of Andhra State in 1953. Kurnool became the capital instead.

221.s: Which of the following best explains the significance of socialist organisations in Andhra?
o: They concentrated only on selecting capitals for newly formed States.
They trained cadres through summer schools and Kisan institutes, contributing later to peasant and labour struggles.
They replaced all peasant organisations with government departments.

He founded and edited the **Congress** newspaper.

o: leading the Join Indian Union movement

222.x: The Hyderabad State Comrades Association, regarded as Telangana's first communist unit, was formed in 1939. Its members included Makhdoom Mohiuddin, Raj Bahadur Gour and Syed Ibrahim.

i. Ravi Narayana Reddy
ii. Mallu Swarajyam
222.x: Veera Telangana Anubhavalu Gnapakalu is by Mallu Swarajyam (G2 2025); Veera Telangana (Na Anubhavalu) is by Ravi Narayana Reddy (G2 2008 match). The other codes swap or repeat the authors.
222.tq: 'Anubhavalu Gnapakalu' = Mallu Swarajyam; 'Na Anubhavalu' = Ravi Narayana Reddy.
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-i** — option **(1)**.
**Veera Telangana Anubhavalu Gnapakalu** — **Mallu Swarajyam** (G2 2025).
**Veera Telangana (Na Anubhavalu)** — **Ravi Narayana Reddy** (G2 2008 match).
xa: ⚠ **Anubhavalu Gnapakalu** = Mallu Swarajyam; **Na Anubhavalu** = Ravi Narayana Reddy.
**Sundarayya** wrote **Visalandhralo Prajarajyam** (**1946**).
Ravi Narayana Reddy won **Nalgonda** in **1952** with India's highest majority.

222.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: P. Sundarayya — CPI and later CPI(M)
222.x: Swami Ramananda Tirtha was a leader of the Hyderabad State Congress and led the Join Indian Union movement; he was not a CPI(M) leader. Ravi Narayana Reddy, Baddam Yella Reddy and P. Sundarayya were associated with the communist movement.
222.tq: Find the non-communist political affiliation among leaders otherwise associated with the communist movement.
xs: **Swami Ramananda Tirtha — CPI(M)** is wrong — option **(4)**; he led the **Hyderabad State Congress**.
He led the **"Join Indian Union"** movement — the **odd one out** among communists.
**Sundarayya** (CPI, then **CPI(M)**), **Ravi Narayana Reddy** (CPI) and **Baddam Yella Reddy** (CPI) are correct.
xa: Baddam Yella Reddy organised **agrarian struggles** and favoured working with the **Congress**.
⚠ Trap: **Ramananda Tirtha** = Congress, not communist.
**1964 split**: CPI (pro-Soviet) vs **CPI(M)** (pro-China).

222.s: Makhdoom Mohiuddin is best described as a
o: president of the first Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha
leader of the Hyderabad State Congress's Join Indian Union movement
founder of the Andhra Communist Party at Kakinada
poet and communist leader associated with the Comrades Association
222.x: Makhdoom Mohiuddin was a poet and communist leader associated with the Comrades Association.
222.tq: Use the combined identity of profession, ideology and organisation to avoid confusing Makhdoom Mohiuddin with other leaders.
xs: **Makhdoom Mohiuddin** was a **poet and communist leader** of the **Comrades Association** — option **(4)**.
The first Mahasabha was presided by **Suravaram Pratap Reddy**; **Join Indian Union** was **Ramananda Tirtha's**; the Kakinada founding is credited to **Sundarayya** / **Darsi Chenchaiah**.
xa: The **Hyderabad State Comrades Association** was formed in **1939** (G2 2012 key).
Other members: **Raj Bahadur Gour**, **Syed Ibrahim**.
It was **Telangana's first** communist unit.

222.s:
Consider the following statements about the 1964 split in the communist movement:
1. The CPI side included Ravi Narayana Reddy and Chandra Rajeswara Rao.
2. The CPI(M) side included P. Sundarayya and Basavapunnaiah.
3. The CPI side was associated with a pro-Soviet position, while the CPI(M) side was associated with a pro-China position.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
222.x: All three statements are correct. Ravi Narayana Reddy and Chandra Rajeswara Rao remained with the CPI, while P. Sundarayya and Basavapunnaiah went with the CPI(M); the two sides were identified respectively with pro-Soviet and pro-China positions.
222.tq: Match both leaders and ideological alignments before selecting the complete set of correct statements.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**CPI** (pro-Soviet): **Ravi Narayana Reddy**, **Chandra Rajeswara Rao**.
**CPI(M)** (pro-China): **Sundarayya**, **Basavapunnaiah**.
xa: The split came in **1964**.
Sundarayya became AP's **first Leader of the Opposition**.
National chronology: CPI banned **1934** → lifted **1942** → split **1964**.

222.s: Which communist leader won the Nalgonda seat in 1952 with the highest majority in India?
222.x: Ravi Narayana Reddy (CPI) won Nalgonda in 1952 with India's highest majority and stayed with the CPI in 1964. Sundarayya became AP's first Leader of the Opposition and joined the CPI(M); Baddam Yella Reddy organised agrarian struggles; Makhdoom Mohiuddin was a poet and Comrades Association leader.
222.tq: Nalgonda 1952 highest majority = Ravi Narayana Reddy.
xs: **Ravi Narayana Reddy** won **Nalgonda** in **1952** with **India's highest majority** — option **(2)**.
He stayed with the **CPI** in **1964**.
**Sundarayya** went to the **CPI(M)**; **Baddam Yella Reddy** organised agrarian struggles; **Makhdoom** was a poet.
xa: He presided the Andhra Mahasabha in **1941**, **1944** and **1945**.
He wrote **Veera Telangana (Na Anubhavalu)**.
Communists won **41 of 145** Andhra-region seats in **1952**.

222.s: The political significance of communist activity in Andhra is best expressed by which of the following statements?
o: It confined Andhra politics exclusively to cultural questions.
It shifted the main focus of Andhra politics from language to land.
It ended peasant mobilisation in Andhra.
It rejected the demand for Visalandhra.
222.x: The communists shifted Andhra politics from language to land through peasant mobilisation, while their social base also helped drive the Visalandhra movement.
222.tq: Identify the central political transition rather than a consequence that reverses the communist role.
xs: Communists **shifted Andhra politics from language to land** — option **(2)** is correct.
This won them **41 of 145** Andhra-region seats in **1952** and drove **Visalandhra**.
They **demanded** Visalandhra, so option **(4)** is wrong.
xa: The Mahasabha shifted to **jagirdari, vetti and taxes**.
Telangana peasants **seized land** and set up **village soviets**.
**Prakasam's** ministry fell on **15 Nov 1954** after communist-led agitation.

222.s: The CPI was banned in 1934, and the ban was lifted in:
222.x: The CPI ban imposed in 1934 was lifted in 1942.
222.tq: Distinguish the national CPI ban chronology from the separate bans concerning regional organisations.
xs: The CPI ban of **1934** was lifted in **1942** — option **(2)** is correct.
Exact dates: **23 July 1934** → **23 July 1942**.
**1946** = Hyderabad State ban; **1948** = **Prajasakti** banned.
xa: Andhra (Madras) ban: **September 1949** → lifted **October 1951**.
The **1964** split followed.
The **2nd** conference was held in **1938** at Vijayawada.

222.s: What was one political consequence of the CPI’s ‘People’s War’ line and its opposition to the Quit India Movement?
o: It cost the CPI the 1945–46 elections.
It helped the CPI win the 1945–46 elections decisively.
It led immediately to the CPI split in 1964.
It resulted in the formation of Praja Natya Mandali.
222.x: The CPI’s ‘People’s War’ line and opposition to the Quit India Movement cost it the 1945–46 elections.
222.tq: Match the political line and wartime position with their stated electoral consequence.
xs: The **"People's War"** line and opposition to **Quit India** **cost the CPI the 1945-46 elections** — option **(1)**.
The **1964** split came much later and was a pro-Soviet vs pro-China divide.
xa: The CPI ban had been lifted on **23 July 1942**.
**Prakasam** arrested communist leaders in **1946**.
The **3rd** conference (**July 1943**) was the first open conference.

222.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the first Andhra State ministry under Prakasam:
1. It fell on 15 November 1954.
2. Its fall followed communist-led agitation.
3. The CPI won 41 of 196 seats in the 1955 elections.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
222.x: The Prakasam ministry fell on 15 November 1954 after communist-led agitation. Statement 3 is false: the CPI won only 15 of 196 seats in 1955, not 41.
222.tq: Use the changed figure as the trap and compare the 1952 and 1955 electoral numbers carefully.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Prakasam's** first Andhra State ministry fell on **15 Nov 1954**.
Statement 2: it fell after **communist-led agitation**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the CPI won only **15 of 196** seats in **1955**; **41 of 145** was the **1952** Andhra-region tally.
xa: Communists shifted Andhra politics from **language to land**.
**Prakasam** had arrested communist leaders in **1946**.

222.s: Which of the following is regarded as the first officially recognised CPI publication in India?
222.x: Labour Kisan Gazette (Singaravelu) is described as the first officially recognised CPI publication in India. Navasakti (1937) was the first Telugu communist paper, Prajasakti the Andhra CPI organ (1942) and Visalandhra a daily from 1952.
222.tq: First officially recognised CPI publication = Labour Kisan Gazette.
xs: The **Labour Kisan Gazette** is the **first officially recognised CPI publication** in India — option **(3)**.
**Navasakti** (**1937**) was the first **Telugu** communist paper; **Prajasakti** a weekly from **1942**; **Visalandhra** a daily from **1952**.
xa: Navasakti: **Rajahmundry, 15 Dec 1937**, editor **Chandra Rajeswara Rao**.
Prajasakti: daily **1945**, banned **1948**.
Visalandhra inaugurated by **Tapi Dharma Rao** at **Vijayawada**.

223.s: The Communal Award of 1932 was announced by Ramsay MacDonald primarily after the failure of which event to resolve the issue of minority representation?
o: The Karachi Session of the Indian National Congress
223.x: Ramsay MacDonald announced the Communal Award in August 1932 after the Second Round Table Conference failed to reach agreement on minority representation.
223.tq: Link the announcement to its immediate political background.
xs: The Award followed the failure of the **Second Round Table Conference** over **minority representation** — option **(4)**.
It was announced by British PM **Ramsay MacDonald** on **16 Aug 1932**.
xa: It divided Indians into **11 groups**.
The **Depressed Classes** were declared a **minority** with separate electorates.
⚠ **Award** = **16 Aug 1932** (MacDonald); **Gandhi's fast** = **20 Sept 1932** (Yerwada).

223.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Communal Award of 1932:
1. It divided Indians into 11 groups for purposes of representation.
2. It recognised the Depressed Classes as a minority.
3. It provided separate electorates only for Muslims and Sikhs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
223.x: The Award divided Indians into 11 groups and treated the Depressed Classes as a minority. Separate electorates were also provided for Europeans, Indian Christians and Anglo-Indians, among others; therefore statement 3 is false.
223.tq: Find the over-restrictive statement in a list of provisions.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: the Award covered **11 groups**.
Statement 2: the **Depressed Classes** were declared a **minority**.
Statement 3 is wrong: separate electorates also went to **Europeans**, **Indian Christians**, **Anglo-Indians** and the **Depressed Classes**.
xa: Women got **3%** of seats in all provinces except **NWFP**.
Special-interest seats: **labour, landlords, traders, industrialists**.
UPPSC 2017 A/R: the Award gave each minority seats by **separate electorate** — both true, R explains A.

223.s: Under the Communal Award, what special electoral arrangement was provided to the Depressed Classes?
o: Two votes restricted to the separate electorate
A single vote in the general electorate only
No vote, but nomination to provincial legislatures
A double vote in a separate electorate and the general electorate
223.x: The Depressed Classes were given a double vote: one in a separate electorate and another in the general electorate.
223.tq: Test the exact mechanism rather than merely the existence of separate electorates.
xs: The Depressed Classes got a **double vote** — one in a **separate electorate** and one in the **general electorate** — option **(4)**.
They were declared a **minority** under the Award.
xa: **Gandhi** opposed this with a **fast unto death** from **20 September 1932** at **Yerwada Jail, Poona**.
He argued separate electorates for Dalits would **permanently divide Hindu society**.
The Pact replaced this with **reserved seats in a joint electorate**.

223.s:
With reference to the Communal Award, consider the following statements:
1. Three per cent of the seats in all provinces, except the North-West Frontier Province, were earmarked for women.
2. The Award dealt only with religious communities and made no provision for occupational interests.
3. Seats were also provided for labour, landlords, traders and industrialists.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
223.x: Three per cent of seats were reserved for women in all provinces except the North-West Frontier Province. The Award also included occupational interests such as labour, landlords, traders and industrialists, making statement 2 false.
223.tq: Pair a numerical exception with the correct list of beneficiaries.
xs: **Statements 1 and 3** are correct — option **(3) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: women got **3%** of seats in all provinces **except NWFP**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the Award also gave **special-interest** seats.
Statement 3: seats went to **labour, landlords, traders and industrialists**.
xa: The Award covered **11 groups**.
Separate electorates: **Muslims, Sikhs, Europeans, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians** + **Depressed Classes**.
Announced **16 Aug 1932** by **Ramsay MacDonald**.

223.s:
Consider the following statements about the response to the Communal Award (1932):
1. Gandhi began a fast unto death on 20 September 1932 in Yerwada Jail, Poona.
2. Gandhi argued that separate electorates for Dalits would permanently divide Hindu society.
3. The Congress formally rejected the Communal Award.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
223.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Congress neither accepted nor rejected the Award. Hence '1 and 2 only'; all other options include statement 3.
223.tq: Congress on the Award: neither accepted nor rejected.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Gandhi** began a **fast unto death** on **20 September 1932** in **Yerwada Jail, Poona**.
Statement 2: he argued separate electorates for Dalits would **permanently divide Hindu society**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **Congress neither accepted nor rejected** the Award.
xa: The Award was announced on **16 Aug 1932** by **Ramsay MacDonald**.
It gave the Depressed Classes a **double vote**.
The Pact's **reserved seats in a joint electorate** became the model for SC reservation.

223.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the constitutional history of the term 'Scheduled Castes' is correct?
o: It was first used by the Simon Commission, fixed by the Government of India Act, 1935, and the first list came in 1936.
It was first used in the Communal Award and abolished by the Government of India Act, 1935.
It was first used by Gandhi in 1932 and legally defined in 1942.
It was first used in the Poona Pact and listed in 1950.
223.x: The term was first used by the Simon Commission, fixed by the Government of India Act, 1935, and the first list was issued in 1936.
223.tq: Arrange the institutional stages of a constitutional term in sequence.
xs: "Scheduled Castes" was **first used by the Simon Commission**, fixed by the **GoI Act 1935**, first list **1936** — option **(1)**.
The **Communal Award** used the term **Depressed Classes**, declaring them a **minority**.
xa: **Art. 17** later **abolished untouchability**.
The Pact's **joint electorate with reserved seats** = model for constitutional SC reservation.
The Social Justice Ministry began a **2-year** celebration of **Jyotiba Phule's 200th birth anniversary** (Apr **2026**).

223.s: Article 17 of the Constitution is significant in the context of the Depressed Classes movement because it:
o: Provided separate electorates for Scheduled Castes
223.x: Article 17 abolished untouchability and prohibited its practice in any form.
223.tq: Match a constitutional Article with its precise subject.
xs: **Article 17** **abolished untouchability** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **Communal Award** (**1932**) was **MacDonald's**, not a constitutional article.
The **Poona Pact** gave **reserved seats in a joint electorate**, not separate electorates.
xa: "Scheduled Castes" was first used by the **Simon Commission** and fixed by the **GoI Act 1935**.
The first SC list came in **1936**.
**Jyotiba Phule's 200th birth anniversary** is being celebrated (Apr **2026**).

223.s: The reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes under the constitutional system is conceptually linked to which feature of the Poona Pact?
o: Nomination by the British Prime Minister
223.x: The Poona Pact's model of joint electorates with reserved seats became the basis for the constitutional approach to SC political reservation.
223.tq: Identify the institutional feature that carried forward into the Constitution.
xs: SC reservation follows the Pact's **reserved seats in a joint electorate** — option **(4)** is correct.
The Communal Award had instead given **separate electorates** with a **double vote**.
xa: **Gandhi's fast** (from **20 Sept 1932**, **Yerwada**) forced the change.
The Award was announced on **16 Aug 1932**.
**Art. 17** abolished **untouchability**.

224.s: The immediate political pressure that prompted the Montagu Declaration of 20 August 1917 was exerted chiefly by the:
224.x: The Home Rule Leagues created political pressure that contributed to the British declaration recognising self-government as an objective.
224.tq: Identify the immediate political force rather than the later constitutional outcome.
xs: The **Montagu Declaration** (**20 August 1917**) was prompted by the **Home Rule Leagues** — option **(2)** is correct.
It was the **first official recognition** of self-government as an aim.
The **Liberal Federation** (**1918**), **Justice Party** and **Swaraj Party** came later.
xa: Aim: **"progressive realisation of responsible government"** in India as an integral part of the British Empire.
**Montagu** + **Chelmsford** toured India in **Dec 1917**.
The **Montagu-Chelmsford Report** was announced in **July 1918**.

224.s: A 27-member Andhra delegation led by Nyapati Subbarao met Montagu at Madras to demand:
o: A separate Muslim province in South India
Abolition of the Madras Legislative Council
224.x: The Andhra delegation led by Nyapati Subbarao sought the creation of a separate Andhra province.
224.tq: Connect the delegation leader and its regional constitutional demand.
xs: **Nyapati Subbarao's** **27-member** delegation met Montagu at **Madras** for a **separate Andhra province** — option **(3)**.
p.442 of the notes gives it as **21 members**.
xa: **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** presided the **Special Andhra Mahasabha** at **Guntur** (**17 Aug 1918**).
**Krishna Patrika**: reforms = "giving with the right hand, taking with the left".
Andhra delegations seeking a separate province are a key **AP angle** of the 1919 reforms.

224.s: The Montagu Declaration of 20 August 1917 announced British policy as the:
o: immediate grant of dominion status to India
progressive realisation of responsible government in India as an integral part of the British Empire
complete independence of India within ten years
provincial autonomy with an All-India Federation
224.x: On 20 August 1917 Montagu announced the gradual development of self-governing institutions with a view to the progressive realisation of responsible government in India as an integral part of the Empire - the first official recognition of self-government as an aim. Dominion status as a goal came with the 1929 Deepavali Declaration; complete independence was never promised then; provincial autonomy and federation came with the 1935 Act.
224.tq: 1917 = 'progressive realisation of responsible government'.
xs: The Declaration aimed at the **progressive realisation of responsible government** in India as an **integral part of the British Empire** — option **(2)**.
It spoke of **gradual development of self-governing institutions**, not immediate dominion status or independence.
**Provincial autonomy** and an **All-India Federation** came with the **1935 Act**.
xa: Made on **20 August 1917**, in Parliament.
Prompted by the **Home Rule Leagues**.
First official recognition of **self-government** as an aim.

224.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the response of the Moderates to the constitutional reforms of 1919?
o: They accepted the reforms and formed the Indian National Liberal Federation in 1918.
They boycotted the reforms and formed the Justice Party.
They joined the Home Rule Leagues and demanded complete independence.
They rejected the reforms and formed the Swaraj Party.
224.x: Surendranath Banerjee and other Moderates accepted the reforms, left the Congress and formed the Indian National Liberal Federation in 1918.
224.tq: Use the founder-group and organisation pairing to avoid confusing Moderates with Swarajists.
xs: The Moderates **accepted the reforms** and formed the **Indian National Liberal Federation (1918)** — option **(1)**.
They were led by **Surendranath Banerjee** and **left the Congress**.
The **Swaraj Party** (**C.R. Das**, **Motilal Nehru**) came later and entered councils to obstruct.
xa: Some notes call it the **"National Liberation Federation"**.
**C.R. Das** + **Tilak** wanted **rejection** at **Amritsar (1919)**.
**Gandhi** + **Malaviya** wanted a **fair trial**.

224.s: At the Amritsar Congress of 1919, the reforms were described as:
224.x: The Amritsar Congress characterised the reforms as inadequate, unsatisfactory and disappointing.
224.tq: Recall the exact three-part political assessment used by the Congress.
xs: The **Amritsar Congress (1919)** called the reforms **"inadequate, unsatisfactory and disappointing"** — option **(4)**.
It was presided by **Motilal Nehru**.
xa: **C.R. Das** and **Tilak** favoured **rejection**.
**Gandhi** and **Malaviya** favoured a **fair trial**.
**Krishna Patrika**: "giving with the right hand, taking with the left".

224.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Andhra reaction to the reforms of 1919:
1. A special Andhra Mahasabha was held at Guntur on 17 August 1918.
2. It was held under the leadership of Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.
3. Krishna Patrika described the reforms as giving with the right hand and taking with the left.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: All three statements are correct. The Guntur meeting, its leadership and the Krishna Patrika description reflect the critical Andhra response to the reforms.
224.tq: Check the date, regional leader and exact contemporary description together.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The **Special Andhra Mahasabha** met at **Guntur** on **17 Aug 1918**, presided by **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**.
**Krishna Patrika** said the reforms were **"giving with the right hand, taking with the left"**.
xa: **Nyapati Subbarao** led a **27-member** Andhra delegation to Montagu at Madras.
**V. Ramadas** was elected to the **Central Legislative Assembly** (**1923**).
Madras's first **Justice Party** ministry: **Subbarayalu Reddiar**, then **Panagal Raja**.

224.s: At the Amritsar Congress of 1919, which leaders favoured giving the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms a fair trial?
224.x: At Amritsar (1919, presided by Motilal Nehru) the reforms were called inadequate, unsatisfactory and disappointing; C.R. Das and Tilak wanted them rejected, while Gandhi and Malaviya wanted to give them a fair trial. Surendranath Banerjee had already left to form the Liberal Federation (1918).
224.tq: Reject = C.R. Das + Tilak; fair trial = Gandhi + Malaviya.
xs: **Gandhi** and **Madan Mohan Malaviya** favoured a **fair trial** — option **(2)** is correct.
**C.R. Das** and **Tilak** wanted **rejection**.
**Surendranath Banerjee** had already left to form the **Liberal Federation (1918)**.
xa: Amritsar Congress (**1919**) was presided by **Motilal Nehru**.
It called the reforms **"inadequate, unsatisfactory and disappointing"**.
The **Rowlatt Act** was passed in **March 1919**.

224.s: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms were named after which two officials?
224.x: The reforms were named after Edwin Montagu, the Secretary of State for India, and Lord Chelmsford, the Viceroy of India.
224.tq: Use the name-to-office association to distinguish similarly named constitutional reforms.
xs: The reforms are named after **Edwin Montagu** (**Secretary of State**) and **Lord Chelmsford** (**Viceroy**) — option **(3)**.
**Morley-Minto** = **1909** reforms; **John Simon** chaired the **1927** Commission.
xa: The Report was announced in **July 1918**.
The Act was an **Act of the UK Parliament**.
⚠ APPSC 2019: dyarchy = **dual (not single)** government by **Montagu and Chelmsford**.

224.s: The Montagu-Chelmsford Report was announced in which month and year?
224.x: The Montagu-Chelmsford Report was announced in July 1918; it subsequently formed the basis of the Government of India Act, 1919.
224.tq: Separate the report date from the declaration date and the Act date.
xs: The **Montagu-Chelmsford Report** was announced in **July 1918** — option **(3)** is correct.
**August 1917** was the **Montagu Declaration**; **Dec 1917** the tour of India.
xa: The Report became the **GoI Act 1919**.
**First elections** under the Act: **1920**.
The **Chamber of Princes** came in **1921**.

224.s:
With reference to dyarchy under the Government of India Act, 1919, consider the following statements:
1. It was introduced in the provinces.
2. It divided provincial subjects into reserved and transferred subjects.
3. It made the provincial budget independent of the central budget.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: Dyarchy was introduced in the provinces, provincial subjects were divided into reserved and transferred categories, and the provincial budget was separated from the central budget.
224.tq: Check whether each feature belongs to provincial dyarchy rather than to the later provincial autonomy scheme.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Dyarchy** was introduced in the **provinces**, with **reserved** and **transferred** subjects.
**Provincial budgets** were **separated** from the central budget.
xa: Subjects were split into **central** and **provincial** lists.
Criticism: ministers got transferred subjects **without finance** (which stayed reserved).
⚠ UPSC notes wrongly call this **"provincial autonomy"** — that came with the **1935** Act.

224.s:
Under the dyarchical arrangement, which of the following were transferred subjects?
1. Education
2. Health
3. Local self-government
4. Law and order
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
224.x: Education, health and local self-government were transferred subjects administered by ministers responsible to the legislature. Law and order was a reserved subject.
224.tq: Find the one reserved subject and eliminate the option that includes it.
xs: **Education**, **health** and **local self-government** were transferred — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**Law and order** was a **reserved** subject, with **finance** and **land revenue**.
xa: Transferred subjects were run by the Governor + **Ministers** answerable to the **legislature**.
Reserved subjects: Governor + **Executive Council**, **not** answerable to the legislature.
In **1935** **local self-government** became a **provincial subject**.

224.s: The central legislature under the Government of India Act, 1919 was:
o: Bicameral, consisting of the Chamber of Princes and the Federal Court
Bicameral, consisting of the Council of State and the Legislative Assembly
Unicameral, consisting only of nominated members
Tricameral, consisting of the Council of State, Legislative Assembly and Provincial Council
224.x: The Act introduced a bicameral central legislature comprising the Council of State as the upper chamber and the Legislative Assembly as the lower chamber.
224.tq: Match the constitutional arrangement with the exact names of its two chambers.
xs: The centre was **bicameral**: **Council of State** (upper) + **Legislative Assembly** (lower) — option **(2)**.
The **Chamber of Princes** was a **consultative** body of rulers; the **Federal Court** came under the **1935 Act**.
xa: Assembly = **145** members (**104** elected); Council of State = **60**.
Both houses were **mostly elected**.
First President of the Assembly: **Frederick Whyte** (**1921**).

224.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the central legislature under the Government of India Act, 1919:
1. The Legislative Assembly had 145 members.
2. Of the members of the Legislative Assembly, 104 were elected.
3. The Council of State had 60 members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: The Legislative Assembly had 145 members, including 104 elected members, while the Council of State had 60 members.
224.tq: Verify each numerical detail separately before selecting the combined code.
xs: All three are correct — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Legislative Assembly** = **145** members, of whom **104** were elected.
**Council of State** = **60** members.
xa: First President: **Frederick Whyte**; first Deputy President: **Sachchidananda Sinha**.
**Vithalbhai Patel** became Assembly president after the **1923** elections.
Franchise was limited by **property, tax and education**.

224.s: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the Government of India Act, 1919?
o: Direct elections to the central legislature
Creation of the office of High Commissioner for India in London
Separation of provincial budgets from the central budget
Provincial autonomy in place of dyarchy
224.x: Provincial autonomy was associated with the Government of India Act, 1935. The 1919 Act introduced dyarchy in the provinces, along with the other listed features.
224.tq: Use the later 1935 feature as the chronological trap in a NOT question.
xs: **Provincial autonomy in place of dyarchy** was not a 1919 feature — option **(4)**; it came with the **1935 Act** (from **April 1937**).
The 1919 Act gave **direct elections**, the **High Commissioner** in **London** and **separate provincial budgets**.
xa: The **Simon Report (1930)** first recommended abolishing provincial dyarchy for **provincial autonomy**.
⚠ **Dyarchy**: **1919** = in the provinces; **1935** = provincial dyarchy abolished, Centre dyarchy never operated.
The 1935 Act also abolished the **India Council**.

224.s: The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced direct elections on the basis of:
o: Separate nomination by the Secretary of State
224.x: The Act introduced direct elections, but the franchise remained limited by property, tax and educational qualifications.
224.tq: Combine the electoral method with the qualification-based nature of the franchise.
xs: Franchise was limited by **property, tax and educational** qualifications — option **(2)** is correct.
There was no **universal adult franchise**.
xa: The **GoI Act 1919** was the **first Act** to introduce **direct elections**.
**Communal representation** was **extended** (Sikhs etc.).
First elections: **1920**, boycotted by the Congress.

224.s: Which Act introduced elected non-official members, largely through indirect and separate electorates?
224.x: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 introduced elected non-official members, largely through indirect and separate electorates. Direct elections were associated with the 1919 Act.
224.tq: Discriminate between the 1909 indirect electoral innovation and the 1919 direct elections.
xs: The **Indian Councils Act 1909** introduced **elected non-official members**, largely via **indirect and separate electorates** — option **(3)**.
**Direct elections** came with the **GoI Act 1919**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: the APPSC GS 2018 key gave **1909** for "first direct elections".
If **1919** is not among the options, mark **1909**.
**1909** = **Morley-Minto Reforms**.

224.s: If an examination question asks for the first Act associated with direct elections in India, which answer is most appropriate?
224.x: The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced direct elections. The 1909 Act introduced elected non-official members mainly through indirect and separate electorates.
224.tq: Resolve a close-option ambiguity by distinguishing direct elections from indirect elections.
xs: The **Government of India Act 1919** was the first to introduce **direct elections** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **1909** Act brought **elected** members mostly via **indirect** and **separate electorates**.
xa: ⚠ APPSC GS 2018 key gave **Indian Councils Act 1909** — mark it only if 1919 is absent.
Franchise in 1919 rested on **property, tax and education**.
Assembly: **145** members, **104** elected.

224.s: The statutory review provision of the Government of India Act, 1919 required the appointment of a commission after:
224.x: The Act required a statutory commission to review its working after ten years. The Simon Commission was appointed two years early under this provision.
224.tq: Recall the statutory interval and distinguish it from the actual early appointment.
xs: The Act required a **statutory commission after 10 years** — option **(4) Ten years** is correct.
The **Simon Commission** was appointed **two years early** (**8 November 1927**).
xa: Simon Commission = **Indian Statutory Commission** / "White Commission".
Appointed by the **Conservative (Baldwin)** government.
The Swarajist demand for review led to the **Muddiman Committee (1924)**.

224.s:
With reference to provincial dyarchy under the Government of India Act, 1919, consider the following statements:
1. Transferred subjects were administered by the Governor with the assistance of ministers.
2. Reserved subjects were administered by the Governor with the assistance of the Executive Council.
3. Local self-government was treated as a reserved subject.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: Transferred subjects, including local self-government, were administered by the Governor with ministers. Reserved subjects were handled by the Governor and the Executive Council; therefore statement 3 is false.
224.tq: Split the options by identifying the wrongly classified subject under dyarchy.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **transferred** subjects — Governor with **ministers**.
Statement 2: **reserved** subjects — Governor with the **Executive Council**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **local self-government** was a **transferred** subject.
xa: Ministers came from the **elected legislature** and answered to it.
Reserved subjects included **law and order**, **finance**, **land revenue**.
In **1935** local self-government became a **provincial subject**.

224.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Viceroy's Executive Council under the Government of India Act, 1919:
1. The Council had six members apart from the Commander-in-Chief.
2. Three of these six members were Indians.
3. All the members of the Council were elected directly by the people.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: Apart from the Commander-in-Chief, the Viceroy's Executive Council had six members, of whom three were Indians. The members were not all directly elected, making statement 3 false.
224.tq: Reject the extreme institutional claim that all members were directly elected.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
The **Executive Council** had **6** members (other than the **C-in-C**), **3** of them Indians.
Statement 3 is wrong: members were not directly elected; only the legislature was **mostly elected**.
xa: Centre: **Council of State** + **Legislative Assembly**.
**Communal representation** was extended (Sikhs etc.).
A **statutory commission** was due after **10 years**.

224.s:
With reference to dyarchy under the Government of India Act, 1919, consider the following statements:
1. Dyarchy meant a single, unified government in the provinces.
2. The scheme is named after Edwin Montagu and Lord Chelmsford.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
224.x: Statement 1 is wrong: dyarchy means dual government - reserved subjects under the Governor and Executive Council, transferred subjects under the Governor with ministers (APPSC 2019 marked 'single government' false). Statement 2 is correct. Hence 2 only.
224.tq: Dyarchy = DUAL government in provinces (1919).
xs: Only **statement 2** is correct — option **(2) 2 only**.

Statement 1 is wrong: dyarchy means **dual** government — **reserved** subjects (Governor + Executive Council) and **transferred** subjects (Governor + ministers); APPSC 2019 marked "single government" false.
Statement 2: the scheme is named after **Edwin Montagu** and **Lord Chelmsford**.
xa: Dyarchy was in the **provinces**, not the Centre.
The **1935** Act abolished provincial dyarchy; **Centre dyarchy** never operated.
⚠ UPSC notes wrongly call 1919 **"provincial autonomy"**.

224.s:
Consider the following statements about the Public Service Commission under the Government of India Act, 1919:
1. It was provided for in Section 96(C) of the Act.
2. It was set up in 1921, as soon as the Act came into force.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
224.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Public Service Commission was set up on 1 October 1926, after the Lee Commission. Hence 1 only.
224.tq: Sec. 96(C) -> PSC set up 1 Oct 1926 (after Lee Commission).
xs: Only **statement 1** is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: the PSC was provided in **Section 96(C)** (APPSC GS 2022).
Statement 2 is wrong: it was set up on **1 October 1926**, after the **Lee Commission**.
xa: The **1935** Act provided a **Federal PSC and Provincial PSCs**.
ICS exams were held simultaneously in India from **1922**.
The office of **High Commissioner for India** was created in **London**.

224.s:
Consider the following statements about the Chamber of Princes (Narendra Mandal):
1. It was a consultative body of Indian rulers.
2. It was set up in 1935 under the Government of India Act, 1935.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
224.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Chamber of Princes was set up in 1921 by royal proclamation under the 1919 reforms. Hence 1 only.
224.tq: Narendra Mandal = 1921, under the 1919 reforms.
xs: Only **statement 1** is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: the **Chamber of Princes (Narendra Mandal)** was a **consultative body of rulers**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it was created in **1921** by **royal proclamation** under the **1919** reforms.
xa: The 1935 Act's **All-India Federation** of provinces + princely states **never came into being**.
First Assembly President **Frederick Whyte** also dates to **1921**.
The **Federal Court** at Delhi came in **1937**.

224.s: Frederick Whyte and Sachchidananda Sinha were respectively associated with which offices?
o: First elected Indian President and first Chief Minister of Madras
First President and first Deputy President of the Legislative Assembly
High Commissioner for India and first President of the Legislative Assembly
First Deputy President and first President of the Council of State
224.x: Frederick Whyte was the first President and Sachchidananda Sinha was the first Deputy President of the Legislative Assembly.
224.tq: Separate similar office-holder facts by matching each person to the exact office and status.
xs: **Frederick Whyte** was the **first President** and **Sachchidananda Sinha** the **first Deputy President** of the Legislative Assembly — option **(2)**.
Whyte took office in **1921**.
xa: **Vithalbhai Patel** later became Assembly president (Speaker) after **1923**.
The 1919 Act created the posts of **President + Deputy President**.
First Madras CM: **A. Subbarayalu Reddiar** (**Dec 1920**).

224.s: The office of High Commissioner for India in London was created by the:
224.x: The Government of India Act, 1919 created the office of High Commissioner for India in London.
224.tq: Match the institutional office with the constitutional Act that created it.
xs: The **GoI Act 1919** created the office of **High Commissioner for India** in **London** — option **(2)**.
The **1935 Act** abolished the **India Council** and set up the **Federal Court**.
xa: The 1919 Act also provided a **Public Service Commission** (**Section 96(C)**).
**Chamber of Princes** was created in **1921**.
ICS exams in India from **1922**.

224.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the initial location of the simultaneous ICS examination in India?
224.x: From 1922, the ICS examination was held simultaneously in India at Allahabad and was later conducted at Delhi.
224.tq: Test the sequence of locations rather than recalling only the year.
xs: Simultaneous **ICS** exams were held in India from **1922** at **Allahabad, later Delhi** — option **(2)**.
This was one of the **FIRSTs** under the **1919 Act**; the order is **Allahabad first**, **Delhi later** — not the reverse in option **(4)**.
xa: The **PSC** was set up on **1 October 1926** after the **Lee Commission**.
The office of **High Commissioner for India** was created in **London**.
The **1935** Act provided a **Federal PSC** and **Provincial PSCs**.

224.s: In the Madras elections of 1920, which one of the following combinations is correct?
o: Congress boycotted the elections and the Justice Party won 63 seats
The Justice Party boycotted the elections and Congress won 63 seats
Both Congress and the Justice Party boycotted the elections
224.x: The Congress boycotted the 1920 Madras elections as part of the Non-Cooperation movement, while the Justice Party won 63 seats.
224.tq: Pair the political action with the correct party and election result.
xs: **Congress boycotted** (Non-Cooperation) and the **Justice Party won 63 seats** — option **(2)** is correct.
The first elections under the Act were in **1920**.
xa: **A. Subbarayalu Reddiar** became the first Chief Minister (**Dec 1920**), then the **Raja of Panagal** (**1921**).
The Justice Party held office most of **1920-37**.
The Justice Party **did not join** the Simon boycott.

224.s: The Justice Party held office in Madras for most of which period?
224.x: The Justice Party held office in Madras for most of the period from 1920 to 1937.
224.tq: Use the complete period rather than confusing it with the first ministry's starting year.
xs: The **Justice Party** held office in Madras for most of **1920-37** — option **(3)** is correct.
It won **63 seats** in **1920**, when the Congress boycotted.
xa: First Premier: **A. Subbarayalu Reddiar**; then **Raja of Panagal**.
In **1937** the Congress won; Madras premier **C. Rajagopalachari** (APHQ 2011).
Congress ministries **resigned in Oct-Nov 1939**.

224.s: The principal objective of the Swaraj Party in contesting the elections of 1923 was to:
o: Obstruct the working of the legislatures from within
Accept the reforms and cooperate with the government
Demand immediate partition of British India
224.x: The Swaraj Party, led by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru, entered the legislatures in order to obstruct colonial governance from within.
224.tq: Identify the political purpose behind entering the legislatures instead of merely recalling the party name.
xs: The **Swaraj Party** contested **1923** elections to **obstruct from within** — option **(2)** is correct.
It was led by **C.R. Das** and **Motilal Nehru**.
xa: It won about **40%** of seats.
**Vithalbhai Patel** became Assembly president (Speaker).
The **Muddiman Committee (1924)** was the British response to the Swarajists.

224.s:
Consider the following statements about the Swarajists and the 1919 Act:
1. The Swarajists won about 40 per cent of the seats in the 1923 elections.
2. The Muddiman Committee (1924) was the British response to the Swarajist demand for a review of the 1919 Act.
3. The Swaraj Party contested the 1920 elections to the Central Legislative Assembly.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Congress boycotted the 1920 elections; the Swarajists (C.R. Das, Motilal Nehru) contested in 1923. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
224.tq: 1920 = boycott; 1923 = Swarajists entered (~40%); 1924 = Muddiman.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: Swarajists won about **40%** of seats in **1923**.
Statement 2: the **Muddiman Committee (1924)** answered their demand for review.
Statement 3 is wrong: the Congress **boycotted** the **1920** elections; Swarajists contested in **1923**.
xa: Leaders: **C.R. Das** and **Motilal Nehru**.
**V. Ramadas** (Andhra) was elected to the Central Legislative Assembly in **1923**.
**Vithalbhai Patel** became Assembly president.

224.s: Who became the President, or Speaker, of the Central Legislative Assembly after the Swarajist success in 1923?
224.x: Vithalbhai Patel became the President, commonly described as the Speaker, of the Central Legislative Assembly.
224.tq: Use the office-holder trap by distinguishing the legislative leaders from the presiding officer.
xs: **Vithalbhai Patel** became **president (speaker)** of the Central Legislative Assembly — option **(1)**.
**M.A. Ansari** presided the **Madras Congress (Dec 1927)**; **C.R. Das** and **Motilal Nehru** led the Swaraj Party.
xa: First Assembly President: **Frederick Whyte** (**1921**).
Swarajists won about **40%** of seats in **1923**.
**Muddiman Committee**: **1924**.

224.s: The elections conducted under the Government of India Act, 1919 were held in which of the following years?
224.x: Elections under the Act were held in 1920 and 1923. The Congress boycotted the elections of 1920.
224.tq: Use the paired-year recall method for elections held under the same constitutional enactment.
xs: Elections under the 1919 Act were held in **1920 and 1923** — option **(4)** is correct.
The Congress **boycotted 1920** (Non-Cooperation); the Swarajists contested **1923**.
xa: In **1920** the **Justice Party** won **63 seats** in Madras.
In **1923** **V. Ramadas** was elected from Andhra to the Central Assembly.
Under the **1935 Act**, provincial elections came in **1937**.

224.s: Who became the first Chief Minister (Premier) of Madras in December 1920 after the Justice Party's victory?
224.x: A. Subbarayalu Reddiar became the first Chief Minister in December 1920; the Raja of Panagal succeeded him in 1921. Rajaji headed the first Congress ministry in 1937; P. Subbarayan was not the first premier.
224.tq: Madras 1920: Subbarayalu Reddiar, then Panagal Raja (1921).
xs: **A. Subbarayalu Reddiar** became the **first Chief Minister** (Premier) of Madras in **Dec 1920** — option **(2)**.
The **Raja of Panagal** succeeded him in **1921**.
**C. Rajagopalachari** was Madras premier under the **1935 Act** (**1937**).
xa: The **Justice Party** won **63 seats** in **1920**.
It held office most of **1920-37**.
Congress ministries **resigned in Oct-Nov 1939**.

224.s:
Consider the following statements about the appointment of the Simon Commission:
1. It was appointed by the Conservative government of Stanley Baldwin.
2. It was appointed to review the working of the Government of India Act, 1919.
3. It was appointed two years after the date fixed by the Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Commission was appointed (8 November 1927) two years early, not late. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
224.tq: Simon: Baldwin's Conservatives, two years EARLY, to review the 1919 Act.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: appointed by the **Conservative (Baldwin)** government on **8 November 1927**.
Statement 2: it was to review the **1919 Act**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it was appointed **two years early**, not late.
xa: The Act had fixed a review **after 10 years**.
Members: **7**, all British; chairman **Sir John Simon**, incl. **Clement Attlee**.
Arrived at **Bombay** on **3 February 1928**.

224.s:
With reference to the Simon Commission, consider the following statements:
1. It consisted of seven members.
2. All its members were British.
3. Sir John Simon was its chairman.
4. Clement Attlee was one of its members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: The commission had seven members, all British, with Sir John Simon as chairman; Clement Attlee was also a member.
224.tq: Verify composition, nationality, chairmanship and membership before selecting the coded option.
xs: All four are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**7 members**, **all British**, chairman **Sir John Simon**, with **Clement Attlee** among the **6** others.
xa: **No Indian member** was the reason for the boycott.
Also called the **Indian Statutory Commission** / "White Commission".
Second visit: **Oct 1928-Apr 1929**.

224.s: The Simon Commission was also known as the:
o: Indian Statutory Commission or White Commission
224.x: The Simon Commission was officially associated with the name Indian Statutory Commission and was popularly called the White Commission because it had no Indian member.
224.tq: Distinguish the formal designation from the popular descriptive name.
xs: It was also the **Indian Statutory Commission** or **"White Commission"** — option **(2)** is correct.
It was "white" as all **7 members** were **British**.
xa: Appointed **8 November 1927** by the **Baldwin** government.
Its Report (**1930**) recommended **provincial autonomy**.
It first used the term **"Scheduled Castes"**.

224.s: The Simon Commission arrived at Bombay on:
224.x: The Simon Commission arrived at Bombay on 3 February 1928.
224.tq: Separate the appointment year from the year of arrival in India.
xs: The Commission arrived at **Bombay** on **3 February 1928** (APPSC GS 2021) — option **(1)** is correct.
An **all-India hartal** and **black flags** greeted it.
**30 Oct 1928** was the **Lahore** lathi charge on **Lala Lajpat Rai**.
xa: Second visit: **Oct 1928-Apr 1929**.
Slogan **"Simon Go Back"** coined by **Yusuf Meherally** (APPSC GS 2018).
Andhra route: **Tenali - Guntur - Vijayawada - Ongole - Madras**.

224.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I (Place)
a. Lahore
b. Madras
c. Lucknow
d. Tenali and Guntur
List-II (Protest leader)
i. Tanguturi Prakasam
ii. G.V. Unnayya Sastri
iii. Lala Lajpat Rai
iv. Jawaharlal Nehru and G.B. Pant
224.x: Lahore was associated with Lala Lajpat Rai, Madras with Tanguturi Prakasam, Lucknow with Jawaharlal Nehru and G.B. Pant, and Tenali–Guntur with G.V. Unnayya Sastri.
224.tq: Start from the sure place–leader pair and eliminate codes containing incompatible matches.
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii** — option **(1)**.
**Lahore** — **Lala Lajpat Rai**; **Madras** — **Tanguturi Prakasam**.
**Lucknow** — **Jawaharlal Nehru**, **G.B. Pant**; **Tenali/Guntur** — **G.V. Unnayya Sastri**.
xa: Lajpat Rai was lathi-charged on **30 Oct 1928** and died of injuries (**Nov 1928**).
**Saunders** was shot by **Bhagat Singh** and **Rajguru** (**Dec 1928**) in revenge.
Guntur saw a **complete bandh**.

224.s: Tanguturi Prakasam acquired the title 'Andhra Kesari' in connection with which incident?
o: Baring his chest before the police during the anti-Simon Commission protest at Madras
Leading the Home Rule League in Andhra
Leading the boycott of the Rowlatt Act in Guntur
224.x: Tanguturi Prakasam bared his chest before the police during the anti-Simon Commission protest at Madras and became known as Andhra Kesari.
224.tq: Link the title to the distinctive action and place associated with it.
