xs: **Prakasam** **bared his chest** to the police at the **Madras** anti-Simon protest and was called **"Andhra Kesari"** — option **(1)**.
The **Amritsar Congress (1919)** was presided by **Motilal Nehru**, not Prakasam.
xa: Andhra anti-Simon committee president: **S. Satyamurti**.
**Bulusu Sambamurthy** toured Andhra for the boycott.
Tenali/Guntur protest: **G.V. Unnayya Sastri**.

224.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the anti-Simon Commission organisation in Andhra?
o: G.V. Unnayya Sastri presided over the committee, while M.A. Ansari toured Andhra.
Bulusu Sambamurthy presided over the committee, while S. Satyamurti toured Punjab.
Tanguturi Prakasam presided over the committee, while Lala Lajpat Rai toured Andhra.
S. Satyamurti presided over the Andhra anti-Simon committee, while Bulusu Sambamurthy toured Andhra for the boycott.
224.x: S. Satyamurti was president of the Andhra anti-Simon committee, and Bulusu Sambamurthy toured Andhra to promote the boycott.
224.tq: Avoid the swapped-person trap by matching each leader with the correct organisational role.
xs: **S. Satyamurti** presided the Andhra anti-Simon committee; **Bulusu Sambamurthy** toured Andhra for the boycott — option **(4)**.
**G.V. Unnayya Sastri** led the **Tenali/Guntur** protest; **M.A. Ansari** presided the **Madras Congress (Dec 1927)**.
**Lala Lajpat Rai** led the **Lahore** protest.
xa: Andhra route: **Tenali - Guntur - Vijayawada - Ongole - Madras**.
**Prakasam** became **"Andhra Kesari"** at Madras.
Guntur had a **complete bandh**.

224.s:
Consider the following statements about the recommendations of the Simon Commission Report (1930):
1. It recommended abolishing provincial dyarchy in favour of provincial autonomy.
2. It recommended separating Sindh from Bombay and Burma from India.
3. It recommended abolishing separate electorates.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the report recommended keeping separate electorates. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
224.tq: Simon Report kept separate electorates.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: abolish provincial dyarchy → **provincial autonomy**.
Statement 2: separate **Sindh** from Bombay and **Burma** from India.
Statement 3 is wrong: the Report recommended **keeping separate electorates**.
xa: The Report (**1930**) first used the term **"Scheduled Castes"**.
The **1935 Act** drew on the **Simon Report**, three **RTCs** and the **White Paper**.
Provincial autonomy began in **April 1937**.

224.s: The term 'Scheduled Castes' was first used in the:
224.x: The term 'Scheduled Castes' was first used in the Simon Commission Report.
224.tq: Match the exact constitutional term with the report in which it first appeared.
xs: **"Scheduled Castes"** was first used in the **Simon Commission Report** — option **(1)** is correct.
The Report came in **1930**.
xa: It recommended **provincial autonomy** and **keeping separate electorates**.
It also proposed separating **Sindh** from Bombay and **Burma** from India.
The **Nehru Report (1928)** was drafted by an **All Parties Conference** committee.

224.s: The principal reason for the boycott of the Simon Commission by Indian political organisations was that
o: it recommended the continuation of separate electorates
it was appointed after the Nehru Report
224.x: The Commission was boycotted because all its members were British and it contained no Indian member.
224.tq: Separate the immediate cause of boycott from later constitutional disagreements.
xs: The Commission was boycotted because it had **no Indian member** — option **(2)** is correct.
All **7 members** were **British**.
The **Nehru Report** came **after** it (**1928**), and the Report backed **provincial autonomy**.
xa: **Lord Birkenhead** challenged Indians to frame a constitution → **Nehru Report**.
**Motilal Nehru** chaired and **Jawaharlal Nehru** was secretary of the committee.
**Jinnah's Fourteen Points (1929)** were the League's answer.

224.s: At the Madras session of the Indian National Congress in December 1927, the decision regarding the Simon Commission was to
o: boycott it only at its first meeting
send an Indian delegation to assist it
boycott it at every stage and in every form
224.x: The Madras Congress session under M. A. Ansari resolved to boycott the Simon Commission at every stage and in every form.
224.tq: Recall the precise wording of an organisational resolution.
xs: The **Madras session (Dec 1927)** under **M.A. Ansari** resolved to boycott it **"at every stage and in every form"** — option **(3)**.
Means: no cooperation, **black flags**, **"Simon Go Back"**.
xa: The slogan was coined by **Yusuf Meherally**.
**Jinnah's League faction** and the **Hindu Mahasabha** joined the boycott.
The Commission arrived at **Bombay** on **3 February 1928**.

224.s:
Which of the following groups did NOT join the boycott of the Simon Commission?
1. Jinnah's faction of the Muslim League
2. Shafi's faction of the Muslim League
3. Hindu Mahasabha
4. Justice Party
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
224.x: Shafi's League faction and the Justice Party did not join the boycott. Jinnah's faction and the Hindu Mahasabha participated in it.
224.tq: Use organisational faction differences to identify the exceptions.
xs: **Shafi's League faction** and the **Justice Party** did not join — option **(2) 2 and 4 only**.
**Jinnah's League faction** and the **Hindu Mahasabha** joined the boycott.
xa: The **Punjab Unionists** also did not join.
The **Madras Congress (Dec 1927)** under **M.A. Ansari** called for boycott.
The Justice Party held office in Madras most of **1920-37**.

224.s:
Which one of the following correctly describes the sequence of events connected with Lala Lajpat Rai's death?
1. S. P. James Scott ordered a lathi charge.
2. Lala Lajpat Rai led a protest at Lahore.
3. Lala Lajpat Rai died of his injuries.
4. Saunders was killed by Bhagat Singh's group.
Select the correct chronological order.
224.x: Lajpat Rai led the protest on 30 October 1928, Scott ordered the lathi charge, Rai died on 17 November 1928, and Saunders was killed in December 1928.
224.tq: Fix the first protest and last revenge event, then arrange the intervening events.
xs: The correct order is **2, 1, 3, 4** — so option **(1)** is correct: protest at **Lahore**, the **lathi charge**, Rai's death, then **Saunders** killed.
**Lala Lajpat Rai** led the anti-Simon protest at **Lahore**, where the police **lathi charge** came on **30 Oct 1928**.
He **died of his injuries** in **Nov 1928**.
**Saunders** was shot in revenge by **Bhagat Singh** and **Rajguru** in **Dec 1928**.
xa: The **Simon Commission** was appointed on **8 November 1927** and arrived at **Bombay** on **3 February 1928**.
Other protest centres: **Madras** — **Tanguturi Prakasam** bared his chest; **Lucknow** — **Jawaharlal Nehru** and **G.B. Pant**.
Andhra route of the boycott: **Tenali - Guntur - Vijayawada - Ongole - Madras**; complete bandh in **Guntur**.
No Indian among its **7 members, all British** (chairman **Sir John Simon**) — the reason for the boycott.

224.s: The slogan 'Simon Go Back' was coined by:
224.x: Yusuf Meherally coined 'Simon Go Back' (APPSC GS 2018). Lajpat Rai led the Lahore protest, Prakasam the Madras protest, and S. Satyamurti headed the Andhra anti-Simon committee.
224.tq: Simon Go Back = Yusuf Meherally.
xs: The slogan **"Simon Go Back"** was coined by **Yusuf Meherally** (APPSC GS **2018**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Lala Lajpat Rai** led the **Lahore** protest and died after the lathi charge of **30 Oct 1928**.
**Tanguturi Prakasam** led the **Madras** protest, baring his chest to police.
**S. Satyamurti** was president of the **Andhra anti-Simon committee**.
xa: Prakasam earned the title **"Andhra Kesari"** for his defiance at Madras.
**Bulusu Sambamurthy** toured Andhra for the boycott.
The **Madras session (Dec 1927)** of the INC under **M.A. Ansari** resolved to boycott the Commission "at every stage and in every form".
The Commission is also called the **Indian Statutory Commission** or "White Commission".

224.s: The Nehru Report was primarily prepared in response to which of the following?
o: Lord Birkenhead's challenge to Indians to frame a constitution
The demand for a separate Muslim homeland
The failure of the Cripps Mission
224.x: The Nehru Report was prepared in reply to Secretary of State Lord Birkenhead's challenge to Indians to frame their own constitution.
224.tq: Identify the immediate cause behind a constitutional document.
xs: The **Nehru Report** answered Secretary of State **Lord Birkenhead's challenge** to Indians to frame a constitution — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was drafted by a **9-member** committee of the **All Parties Conference** (**1928**).
The **Cripps Mission** is unrelated here — the report predates it.
xa: **Motilal Nehru** was Chairman and **Jawaharlal Nehru** Secretary of the Nehru Report committee.
It was discussed at the **Calcutta session (Dec 1928)**, which gave the British a **one-year ultimatum**.
The Muslim League's reply to the report was **Jinnah's Fourteen Points (1929)**.

224.s: At which session and in which month was the Nehru Report discussed, with a one-year ultimatum to the British?
224.x: The Nehru Report was discussed at the Calcutta session in December 1928, where a one-year ultimatum was given to the British.
224.tq: Combine the event, venue and date rather than recalling the year alone.
xs: The Nehru Report was discussed at the **Calcutta session** in **December 1928**, which gave a **one-year ultimatum** to the British — so option **(2)** is correct.
The report itself was prepared in **1928** by the **All Parties Conference** committee (**9 members**).
**March 1931** was the **Gandhi-Irwin Pact**, not a discussion of the Nehru Report.
xa: Committee: Chairman **Motilal Nehru**, Secretary **Jawaharlal Nehru**.
Trigger: **Lord Birkenhead's** challenge to Indians to frame a constitution.
Response: **Jinnah's Fourteen Points (1929)** — federal constitution, residuary powers to provinces, **one-third** Muslim seats at the Centre.

224.s: Jinnah's Fourteen Points of 1929 were formulated as the Muslim League's response to which document?
224.x: Jinnah's Fourteen Points were the Muslim League's answer to the Nehru Report.
224.tq: Discriminate between closely connected constitutional documents.
xs: **Jinnah's Fourteen Points (1929)** were the Muslim League's answer to **the Nehru Report** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Nehru Report (1928)** was drafted by the **All Parties Conference** committee under **Motilal Nehru**.
The **Simon Report** came in **1930**, after the Fourteen Points.
xa: Key demands: **federal constitution**, **residuary powers to provinces**, **one-third** Muslim seats at the Centre and **separate electorates**.
The Nehru Report was discussed at the **Calcutta session (Dec 1928)** with a one-year ultimatum.
The **White Paper** was one basis of the **GoI Act 1935**, along with the Simon Report and three RTCs.

224.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents important features of Jinnah's Fourteen Points?
o: Unitary constitution, joint electorates and abolition of provincial autonomy
Federal constitution, residuary powers to provinces and separate electorates
Dominion status, nominated legislatures and universal adult franchise
Presidential government, one-third provincial seats and communal veto at all levels
224.x: Jinnah's Fourteen Points demanded a federal constitution with residuary powers to the provinces and separate electorates.
224.tq: Split the options by testing the distinctive features of a constitutional demand.
xs: The Fourteen Points demanded a **federal constitution**, **residuary powers to provinces** and **separate electorates** — so option **(2)** is correct.
They also sought **one-third** Muslim seats at the **Centre**.
A **unitary** constitution with **joint electorates** is the opposite of these demands.
xa: The Fourteen Points (**1929**) were the Muslim League's answer to the **Nehru Report (1928)**.
The Nehru Report was drafted by a **9-member** committee of the **All Parties Conference** under **Motilal Nehru**.
⚠ Do not confuse "one-third **provincial** seats" — the demand was one-third Muslim seats **at the Centre**.

224.s: The elections to the provincial legislatures held in 1937 were followed by which of the following developments?
o: The Congress won in the provinces, while the Centre continued under the 1919 structure.
The federation under the 1935 Act came into operation immediately.
The Swaraj Party returned to the legislatures for the first time.
224.x: The Congress won in the 1937 provincial elections. The Centre continued under the 1919 structure because the proposed federation never came into existence.
224.tq: Test the comparison between provincial implementation and the unformed federal Centre.
xs: After the **1937** provincial elections the **Congress won**, while the **Centre continued under the 1919 structure** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **All-India Federation** of the 1935 Act was optional for princely states and **never came into being**.
The **Swaraj Party** had already contested the **1923** elections, so 1937 was not its first entry.
xa: In **Madras**, **C. Rajagopalachari** became premier (APHQ **2011**).
**Provincial autonomy** began in **April 1937**, replacing provincial dyarchy.
The Congress ministries **resigned in Oct-Nov 1939** against India being dragged into WWII.
Further elections under the 1935 Act were held in **1945-46**.

224.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, the proposed All-India Federation was to consist of
o: British provinces and directly administered tribal areas only
224.x: The proposed federation was to include both British provinces and princely states.
224.tq: Test the composition of the proposed federal scheme.
xs: The proposed **All-India Federation** was to consist of **British provinces and princely states** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Joining was **optional for the states**, so the federation **never came into being**.
Options of provinces only or states only miss one of the two units.
xa: **Dyarchy at the Centre** was provided but **never operated**.
**Provincial autonomy** abolished provincial dyarchy and began in **April 1937**.
A **Federal Court** was set up at **Delhi (1937)**; the Act also provided a **Federal PSC** and **Provincial PSCs**.

224.s:
With reference to the federation proposed under the Government of India Act, 1935, consider the following statements:
1. Accession of princely states was optional.
2. The federation actually came into operation.
3. Dyarchy was provided at the Centre.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: Accession of princely states was optional and dyarchy was provided at the Centre. The federation never came into being, making statement 2 false.
224.tq: Separate a proposed provision from one that was actually implemented.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: accession of **princely states** to the federation was **optional**.
Statement 2 wrong: the federation **never came into being**.
Statement 3 correct: **dyarchy at the Centre** was provided, though it **never operated**.
xa: ⚠ Dyarchy: **1919** = in the **provinces**; **1935** = provincial dyarchy abolished, Centre dyarchy never operated.
Because the federation failed, the **Centre continued under the 1919 structure**.
The Act had **321 sections and 10 schedules** — the longest Act.

224.s: The Government of India Act, 1935 is notable for being the longest British constitutional Act relating to India, containing
224.x: The Act contained 321 sections and 10 schedules; it is also described in some references as having 14 parts and 321 articles.
224.tq: Use the numerical pair rather than relying on the size description alone.
xs: The GoI Act 1935 contained **321 sections and 10 schedules** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Some notes describe it as **"14 parts, 321 Articles"** — the **14** refers to parts, not schedules.
xa: Basis of the Act: **Simon Report** + three **RTCs** + the **White Paper**.
It is called the largest single source of the **Constitution's structure**.
Borrowed: **Instrument of Instructions** → **Directive Principles** (APPSC **2023**); **Federal Court** → **Supreme Court**.

224.s:
Consider the following statements about provincial autonomy under the Government of India Act, 1935:
1. It replaced dyarchy in the provinces.
2. It began in April 1937.
3. The Act retained the India Council.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: provincial dyarchy was abolished and provincial autonomy began in April 1937. Statement 3 is wrong: the Act abolished the India Council (it also created bicameral legislatures in some provinces). Hence '1 and 2 only'.
224.tq: 1935 Act abolished the India Council.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **provincial autonomy** replaced (abolished) **provincial dyarchy**.
Statement 2 correct: it began in **April 1937**.
Statement 3 wrong: the Act **abolished the India Council**.
xa: The Act also created bicameral legislatures (**Vidhan Parishads**) in some provinces.
**Local self-government** became a **provincial subject** (under 1919 it was a **transferred** subject).
Provincial autonomy was a recommendation of the **Simon Report (1930)**.

224.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Federal Public Service Commission — 1935 Act — Calcutta, 1937
Provincial Public Service Commissions — 1909 Act — Delhi, 1910
224.x: The Federal Court was established at Delhi in 1937 under the Government of India Act, 1935. The Act also provided for a Federal PSC and Provincial PSCs.
224.tq: Start from the sure institution-location-year pair and eliminate swapped authorities.
xs: The **Federal Court** was set up under the **1935 Act** at **Delhi** in **1937** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **1919 Act** created no Federal Court; the **Federal PSC** and **Provincial PSCs** came with the **1935 Act**, not the **1909** Act.
xa: The Federal Court is the forerunner of today's **Supreme Court**.
The **1919 Act** provided a **Public Service Commission** in **Section 96(C)**; it was set up on **1 October 1926** after the **Lee Commission**.
The 1935 Act also abolished the **India Council** and started **provincial autonomy** (**April 1937**).

224.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. RBI was nationalised
B. Hilton Young Commission
C. RBI started operations
D. Provincial autonomy began
224.x: The correct sequence is Hilton Young Commission in 1926, RBI operations in 1935, provincial autonomy in April 1937, and RBI nationalisation in 1949.
224.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then arrange the middle dates.
xs: The order is **B, C, D, A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Hilton Young Commission** — **1926**; **RBI started operations** — **1 April 1935**.
**Provincial autonomy began** — **April 1937**; **RBI nationalised** — **1 Jan 1949**.
xa: The **RBI Act** was passed in **1934** on the Hilton Young Commission's lines.
Provincial autonomy came under the **GoI Act 1935**, abolishing provincial dyarchy.
The **Federal Court** was also set up at **Delhi** in **1937**.

224.s: The Congress ministries resigned in October-November 1939 mainly because
o: The Muslim League withdrew support from all provincial ministries.
India was involved in the Second World War without the consent of Indian leaders.
The British abolished provincial legislatures without consultation.
The Federal Court rejected provincial autonomy.
224.x: The Congress ministries resigned in protest against India being dragged into the Second World War without Indian consent.
224.tq: Identify the political cause behind a major institutional action.
xs: The Congress ministries **resigned in Oct-Nov 1939** against **India being dragged into WWII** without Indian consent — so option **(2)** is correct.
The ministries had been formed after the **1937** provincial elections, which the **Congress** won.
The **Muslim League** did not withdraw support; instead it celebrated their exit.
xa: The League observed **"Day of Deliverance"** on **22 Dec 1939**; **Ambedkar** joined.
In **Madras**, the ministry was headed by **C. Rajagopalachari** (APHQ **2011**).
**Provincial autonomy** under the **1935 Act** had begun in **April 1937**.

224.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. C. Rajagopalachari headed the Congress ministry formed in Madras after the 1937 elections.
2. The Muslim League observed 22 December 1939 as the 'Day of Deliverance' after the Congress ministries resigned.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
224.x: Both are correct: Rajaji was the Madras premier in 1937 (APHQ 2011), and after the Congress ministries resigned in Oct-Nov 1939 the League observed the Day of Deliverance on 22 December 1939 (Ambedkar joined).
224.tq: Madras 1937 = Rajaji; Deliverance Day = 22 Dec 1939.
xs: **Both** statements are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **C. Rajagopalachari** was the **Madras premier** after the **1937** elections (APHQ **2011**).
Statement 2 correct: after the ministries **resigned in Oct-Nov 1939**, the League observed the **"Day of Deliverance" (22 Dec 1939)**.
xa: **Ambedkar** joined the Day of Deliverance.
The ministries resigned against India being dragged into **WWII**.
Under the **1919** Act, the first Madras Chief Minister was **A. Subbarayalu Reddiar** (**Dec 1920**) of the **Justice Party**.

224.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Feature of the Government of India Act, 1935)
a. Instrument of Instructions
b. Federal Court
c. Emergency powers
d. Federal scheme and Public Service Commissions

List-II (Constitutional counterpart)
i. Supreme Court
ii. Directive Principles of State Policy
iii. Emergency provisions
iv. Union-State structure and UPSC/State PSCs

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
224.x: The Instrument of Instructions corresponds to the Directive Principles, the Federal Court to the Supreme Court, emergency powers to emergency provisions, and the federal scheme and PSCs to the Union-State structure and present PSC system.
224.tq: Start from the sure pair Federal Court–Supreme Court and complete the constitutional parallels.
xs: Correct matching **a–ii, b–i, c–iii, d–iv** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Instrument of Instructions** → **Directive Principles** (APPSC **2023**); **Federal Court** → **Supreme Court**.
**Emergency powers** → **Emergency provisions** (Part XVIII); **federal scheme and PSCs** → **Union-State structure** and UPSC/State PSCs.
xa: Office of **Governor** and the Governor's address (**Sec. 63**) → Governor's address under **Art. 175/176**.
The 1935 Act = largest single source of the **Constitution's structure**.
Basis of the 1935 Act: **Simon Report**, three **RTCs** and the **White Paper**.

224.s: Section 63 of the Government of India Act, 1935 dealt with the Governor's
o: Power to nationalise the Reserve Bank
Power to appoint the Federal Court judges
Power to dissolve the Constituent Assembly
224.x: Section 63 enabled the Governor to address the provincial legislature in his discretion.
224.tq: Match a specific section with its constitutional function.
xs: **Section 63** of the 1935 Act dealt with the Governor's **address to the provincial legislature** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Under it, the Governor addressed the provincial legislature **"in his discretion"**.
**RBI nationalisation** came only on **1 Jan 1949**, not under the 1935 Act.
xa: From **1937** the speech was prepared **with ministers**; the **Constituent Assembly** kept that convention.
Today the Governor's address is under **Art. 175/176**.
Other borrowings: **Instrument of Instructions** → **Directive Principles**; **Federal Court** → **Supreme Court**.

224.s:
Consider the following statements about the Governor's address under the Government of India Act, 1935:
1. Section 63 allowed the Governor to address the provincial legislature in his discretion.
2. From 1937, the Governor's speech came to be prepared with the ministers.
3. The Constituent Assembly discarded this convention and left the address entirely to the Governor's discretion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
224.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Section 63 let the Governor address the legislature in his discretion, and from 1937 the speech was prepared with the ministers. Statement 3 is wrong because the Constituent Assembly kept that convention.
224.tq: 1937 ministries wrote the speech, and the Constitution kept the habit.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Section 63** let the Governor address the provincial legislature **"in his discretion"**.
Statement 2 correct: from **1937** the speech was **prepared with ministers**.
Statement 3 wrong: the **Constituent Assembly kept** that convention.
xa: The Governor's address today falls under **Art. 175/176**.
The office of **Governor** itself is a borrowing from the **1935 Act**.
The **Instrument of Instructions** became the **Directive Principles** (APPSC **2023**).

224.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: 1919 — Government of India Act and Rowlatt Act
224.x: The Rowlatt Act and the Government of India Act were both associated with 1919. The Partition of Bengal was in 1905, the Morley-Minto Reforms in 1909 and the Nehru Report in 1928.
224.tq: Check each year against the constitutional milestone instead of relying on a familiar title alone.
xs: **1919** saw both the **Rowlatt Act** (March) and the **GoI Act 1919** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**1905** = **Partition of Bengal** (Curzon); **1909** = **Morley-Minto Reforms** — options 2 and 3 swap them.
The **Nehru Report** was in **1928**, while **1935** = **GoI Act 1935**.
xa: **1927-28**: Simon Commission appointed / arrives; **1929**: **Jinnah's Fourteen Points**.
**March 1931**: **Gandhi-Irwin Pact**.
APPSC **2018** order: **b, d, a, c** (Partition, Rowlatt, Simon, Gandhi-Irwin).

224.s:
Arrange the following constitutional milestones in chronological order:
A. Nehru Report
B. Partition of Bengal
C. Gandhi-Irwin Pact
D. Jinnah's Fourteen Points
224.x: The correct order is Partition of Bengal (1905), Nehru Report (1928), Jinnah's Fourteen Points (1929), and Gandhi-Irwin Pact (March 1931).
224.tq: Anchor the earliest and latest milestones first, then place the 1928 and 1929 developments between them.
xs: The order is **B, A, D, C** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Partition of Bengal** (**1905**) → **Nehru Report** (**1928**) → **Jinnah's Fourteen Points** (**1929**) → **Gandhi-Irwin Pact** (**March 1931**).
xa: The Fourteen Points were the League's answer to the Nehru Report, so they must come after it.
⚠ Trap: "Gandhi signed the pact in **March 1930**" is wrong — it was **1931**.
**1909**: Morley-Minto Reforms; **1919**: Rowlatt Act and GoI Act 1919; **1935**: GoI Act 1935.

224.s: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed in:
224.x: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed in March 1931; 'March 1930' is a known trap (March 1930 was the start of the Dandi March). December 1929 was the Lahore session and August 1932 the Communal Award.
224.tq: Gandhi-Irwin Pact = March 1931.
xs: The **Gandhi-Irwin Pact** was signed in **March 1931** — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ "March **1930**" is the known trap (APPSC **2018** context) — wrong year.
xa: APPSC **2018** chronology: **Partition of Bengal**, **Rowlatt Act**, **Simon Commission**, **Gandhi-Irwin Pact** (b, d, a, c).
**1929**: Jinnah's Fourteen Points; **1928**: Nehru Report.

224.s: The criticism that dyarchy gave ministers transferred subjects without adequate financial control was based on the fact that
o: The Governor-General controlled all transferred subjects directly.
Ministers were denied legislative powers altogether.
Finance was abolished as a provincial subject.
224.x: Dyarchy was criticised because ministers controlled transferred subjects while finance remained among the reserved subjects.
224.tq: Apply the reserved-transferred distinction to an administrative criticism.
xs: Dyarchy was criticised because ministers got **transferred subjects** while **finance remained reserved** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Reserved** subjects (law and order, **finance**, land revenue) were run by the **Governor + Executive Council**, not answerable to the legislature.
**Transferred** subjects (education, health, local self-government) were run by the **Governor with ministers** answerable to the legislature.
xa: **Dyarchy** = dual government in the **provinces** under the **GoI Act 1919**.
⚠ APPSC **2019**: "dyarchy = single government" was false.
The **1935 Act** abolished provincial dyarchy and introduced **provincial autonomy**.
Another criticism: **communal electorates** were extended.

224.s: The first Justice Party ministry in Madras was associated with which pair of leaders?
224.x: The first Justice Party ministry in Madras was associated with Subbarayalu Reddiar and Panagal Raja.
224.tq: Distinguish the earlier Justice Party ministry from the later Congress ministry.
xs: The first **Justice Party** ministry in Madras was led by **Subbarayalu Reddiar** and then the **Panagal Raja** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The Justice Party won **63 seats** in **1920**; **A. Subbarayalu Reddiar** became first Chief Minister in **Dec 1920**, followed by the **Raja of Panagal** (**1921**).
**Rajagopalachari** headed the later **1937** Congress ministry in Madras.
xa: The Justice Party held office most of **1920-37**.
The Congress **boycotted** the 1920 elections (**Non-Cooperation**).
The Justice Party did **not** join the **Simon Commission** boycott.

224.s: Which one of the following was associated with the 1928 Trade Disputes and Public Safety Bills?
o: Rajagopalachari described them as the “Day of Deliverance Bills”.
Motilal Nehru described one of them as the “Slavery of India Bill”.
Ambedkar introduced them in the Federal Court.
Jinnah called both bills the “Federal India Acts”.
224.x: In the context of the 1928 Trade Disputes and Public Safety Bills, Motilal Nehru called one the “Slavery of India Bill”.
224.tq: Use the person-quotation association and reject quotations assigned to nearby leaders.
xs: **Motilal Nehru** called one of the **1928** bills the **"Slavery of India Bill"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **"Day of Deliverance"** was the Muslim League's observance of **22 Dec 1939**, not a name for these bills.
xa: These **Trade Disputes and Public Safety Bills** were recalled on **1 May 2026**.
Motilal Nehru also chaired the **Nehru Report** committee (**1928**).
With **C.R. Das**, he founded the **Swaraj Party**, which contested the **1923** elections.

225.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Butler Committee — relations of princely states with the Paramount Power
Simon Commission — review of the Government of India Act, 1919
Butler Committee — chaired by Lord Irwin
225.x: The Butler Committee was associated with Harcourt Butler, not Lord Irwin. Its purpose was to examine relations between princely states and the Paramount Power.
225.tq: Use the swapped-person trap in a commission-to-chairman pairing.
xs: The wrong pair is **Butler Committee — chaired by Lord Irwin** — so option **(3)** is the answer.
The **Butler Committee** (**1927**) was headed by **Harcourt Butler**; it is only listed under **Irwin's** viceroyalty.
Its task: examine relations between **Indian princely states** and the **Paramount Power** — pair 1 is correct.
The **Simon Commission** was to review the **1919 Act** — pair 2 is correct.
xa: **Lord Irwin** issued the **Deepavali Declaration** on **31 October 1929**.
Irwin's declaration promised a **Round Table Conference** after the Simon report.
⚠ Do not mix up the **Butler Committee** (princely states, **1927**) with the **Simon Commission** (review of the 1919 Act).

225.s:
Which of the following was NOT a condition associated with the Delhi Proposals?
1. Separation of Sindh
2. Reforms in the North-West Frontier Province and Baluchistan
3. One-third Muslim representation at the centre
4. Abolition of joint electorates
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
225.x: The Delhi Proposals supported joint electorates subject to safeguards; they did not seek the abolition of joint electorates. The other three were associated conditions.
225.tq: Identify the statement that reverses the central proposal.
xs: Only statement **4** — **abolition of joint electorates** — was not a condition — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Delhi Proposals (March 1927)** offered to **drop separate electorates** for **joint electorates** plus reserved seats.
Their conditions: **one-third** of central seats, **separation of Sindh**, reforms in **NWFP and Baluchistan**, representation by population in **Punjab and Bengal**.
xa: ⚠ **Delhi Proposals (1927)** = drop separate electorates; **Fourteen Points (1929)** = keep separate electorates.
**Jinnah's Fourteen Points** came in **March 1929** at the **Muslim League session in Delhi**.
The **All Parties Muslim Conference** (**Delhi, Jan 1929**) under the **Aga Khan** rejected the Nehru Report.

225.s: Under the Delhi Proposals of March 1927, Muslim leaders offered to give up separate electorates in favour of joint electorates subject to, among others, which condition?
o: Removal of all safeguards for Muslim-majority provinces
Complete separation of Bengal from India
225.x: The Delhi Proposals offered joint electorates in return for safeguards including one-third Muslim representation at the centre, separation of Sindh, reforms in the North-West Frontier Province and Baluchistan, and population-based representation in Punjab and Bengal.
225.tq: Recall the conditional nature of a constitutional compromise.
xs: One condition was **one-third representation at the centre** — so option **(3)** is correct.
In the **Delhi Proposals (March 1927)**, Muslim leaders offered **joint electorates + reserved seats** in place of separate electorates.
Other conditions: **separation of Sindh**; reforms in **NWFP and Baluchistan**; representation by population in **Punjab and Bengal**.
xa: The **Fourteen Points (1929)** again sought **one-third** Muslim seats at the centre, but with **separate electorates**.
The Fourteen Points also asked for a **federal constitution** with **residuary powers to provinces**.
The **Nehru Report** proposed **joint electorates** with reserved seats for minorities.

225.s: Tanguturi Prakasam earned the title ‘Andhra Kesari’ because he
o: drafted the Nehru Report in Andhra
bared his chest and dared the police to shoot during the Simon protest
organised the first Round Table Conference
led the boycott resolution at the Madras Congress session
225.x: During the Simon protest, Prakasam bared his chest and challenged the police to shoot, earning the title ‘Andhra Kesari’.
225.tq: Connect an honorific with the specific incident that produced it.
xs: During the **Madras** anti-Simon protest (**1928**), **Tanguturi Prakasam** **bared his chest and dared the police to shoot** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Police firing had killed **Parthasarathi**; Prakasam's defiance earned him the title **"Andhra Kesari"**.
The **Nehru Report** was drafted by **Motilal Nehru's** committee, and the RTCs were held in **London** — not Prakasam's work.
xa: Date of the Madras protest: **26 Feb 1928** (a printed **"2028"** is a typo); asked in APPSC GS **2022**.
**S. Satyamurthy** was President of the **Andhra Boycott Committee**.
Prakasam's moment and the Simon report's neglect of Andhra fuelled the **separate-Andhra** demand.

225.s: During the Simon Commission protest in Madras, the person killed by police firing was
225.x: Police firing during the Madras protest killed Parthasarathi.
225.tq: Identify the individual associated with a specific regional incident.
xs: Police firing during the **Madras** Simon protest killed **Parthasarathi** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**G.V. Unnayya Sastri** led protests at **Tenali and Guntur**; **Bulusu Sambamurti** toured Andhra for the boycott.
**S. Satyamurthy** was President of the **Andhra Boycott Committee**.
xa: After the firing, **Tanguturi Prakasam** bared his chest → title **"Andhra Kesari"**.
The protest was on **26 Feb 1928** (APPSC GS **2022**).
**Guntur and Ongole** showed **black flags** to the Commission.

225.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: G. V. Unnayya Sastri — protest at Tenali and Guntur
Bulusu Sambamurti — tour of Andhra for Simon boycott
Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao — Vijayawada boycott initiative
S. Satyamurthy — led the protest at Lahore
225.x: D is the wrong pair: the Lahore protest was led by Lala Lajpat Rai; S. Satyamurthy was president of the Andhra Boycott Committee. The other pairs are correct: Unnayya Sastri led protests at Tenali and Guntur, Bulusu Sambamurti toured Andhra, and Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao led the Vijayawada boycott.
225.tq: Find the wrong person-to-event pairing among closely related organisers.
xs: The wrong pair is **S. Satyamurthy — Lahore** — so option **(4)** is the answer.
**S. Satyamurthy** was President of the **Andhra Boycott Committee**; the **Lahore** protest was led by **Lajpat Rai**.
Pairs 1-3 are correct: **Unnayya Sastri** — Tenali and Guntur; **Bulusu Sambamurti** — Andhra tour; **Kaleswara Rao** — Vijayawada boycott.
xa: **Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao**, Vijayawada municipal chairman, sent a cover reading only **"Simon Go Back"**.
Municipal resolutions were passed at **Tirupati, Kurnool, Eluru, Srikakulam**.
**Lajpat Rai** was fatally injured leading the Lahore protest.

225.s: At Vijayawada, the cover sent by Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao in protest against the Simon Commission contained only the words
225.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao sent a cover bearing only the words ‘Simon Go Back’. The Vijayawada municipality also passed a boycott resolution.
225.tq: Recall the distinctive wording used in a symbolic protest action.
xs: **Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao's** cover read only **"Simon Go Back"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was the **Vijayawada** municipal chairman; the municipality also passed a **boycott resolution**.
xa: Other municipalities with resolutions: **Tirupati, Kurnool, Eluru, Srikakulam**.
**Black flags** were shown at **Guntur and Ongole**.
**Tanguturi Prakasam** led the **Madras** protest (**1928**) and became **"Andhra Kesari"**.

225.s: Black flags were shown against the Simon Commission at
225.x: Black flags were shown at Guntur and Ongole. G. V. Unnayya Sastri led protests at Tenali and Guntur.
225.tq: Distinguish locations of black-flag demonstrations from locations of organised leadership.
xs: **Black flags** were shown at **Guntur and Ongole** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Eluru, Srikakulam, Tirupati, Kurnool** instead passed **municipal resolutions**.
At **Vijayawada**, chairman **Kaleswara Rao** sent the "Simon Go Back" cover; **Tenali** saw G.V. Unnayya Sastri's protest.
xa: **G.V. Unnayya Sastri** led the protest at **Tenali and Guntur**.
**Bulusu Sambamurti** toured Andhra for the boycott.
**S. Satyamurthy** presided over the **Andhra Boycott Committee**.

225.s: The challenge issued by Birkenhead in 1927, which led to the formation of the committee for the Nehru Report, was that Indians
o: could not organise a boycott of the Simon Commission
could not agree on a constitutional scheme
225.x: Birkenhead challenged Indians to prepare an agreed constitutional scheme, leading to the All Parties Conference and the Nehru Report committee.
225.tq: Identify the cause behind the formation of a constitutional committee.
xs: **Birkenhead's** challenge (**1927**) was that Indians **could not draft an agreed constitution** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The answer was the **Nehru Report** (**August 1928**), drafted by a committee of the **All Parties Conference**.
Far from opposing **linguistic provinces** or **dominion status**, the Nehru Report itself recommended both.
xa: **Dr M.A. Ansari** presided the **All Parties Conference (1928)**.
**Motilal Nehru** chaired the **7-member committee**; **Jawaharlal Nehru** was secretary.
⚠ Trap: "**10 Aug 1929**" is wrong — the report is of **1928**.

225.s:
Consider the following statements about the Nehru Report:
1. It was drafted by a committee chaired by Motilal Nehru, with Jawaharlal Nehru as secretary, set up by the All Parties Conference under Dr M.A. Ansari.
2. It was published in August 1929.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
225.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong (a known trap): the Nehru Report came out in August 1928, not 1929. Hence 1 only.
225.tq: Nehru Report = August 1928 (1929 is the trap).
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Motilal Nehru** chaired the committee, **Jawaharlal Nehru** was secretary, under the **All Parties Conference** presided by **Dr M.A. Ansari**.
Statement 2 wrong: the report came in **August 1928**, not 1929.
xa: ⚠ Trap: "**10 Aug 1929**" is wrong; **1928** is correct.
⚠ **Ansari** presided the All Parties Conference; **Motilal** chaired its drafting committee.
The committee had **7 members**.

225.s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation of the Nehru Report?
o: Universal adult suffrage and fundamental rights
Separate electorates as the permanent basis of representation
A federal structure with a bicameral central legislature
225.x: The Nehru Report recommended joint electorates with reserved seats for minorities, not separate electorates as a permanent arrangement.
225.tq: Use the central distinction between joint electorates and separate electorates.
xs: The Nehru Report did **not** recommend **separate electorates** — so option **(3)** is the answer.
It proposed **joint electorates + reserved seats** for minorities.
It did recommend **dominion status**, a **bicameral** centre and **universal adult suffrage + fundamental rights**.
xa: Other recommendations: end of **dyarchy**, **responsible government**, a **Supreme Court**, **linguistic provinces** (incl. **Andhra**).
The **Muslim League** rejected it; **Jinnah's amendments** failed at the **Calcutta All Parties Convention (Dec 1928)**.
⚠ Separate electorates were kept by the **Simon report** and demanded by the **Fourteen Points**.

225.s:
Which one of the following combinations correctly represents recommendations of the Nehru Report?
1. End of dyarchy
2. Responsible government
3. Establishment of a Supreme Court
4. Linguistic provinces, including Andhra
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
225.x: The Nehru Report recommended ending dyarchy, establishing responsible government and a Supreme Court, and creating linguistic provinces including Andhra.
225.tq: Recognise the complete set of constitutional and administrative recommendations.
xs: **All four** were Nehru Report recommendations — so option **(4)** is correct.
**End of dyarchy** + **responsible government** (statements 1, 2).
A federal structure with a **bicameral** centre and a **Supreme Court** (statement 3).
**Linguistic provinces**, including **Andhra** (statement 4).
xa: Also: **dominion status**, **joint electorates** with reserved seats, **universal adult suffrage**, **fundamental rights**.
Report date: **August 1928**.
The **Simon report** (**May 1930**), by contrast, ignored Andhra's demand.

225.s:
Which of the following correctly describes the reaction to the Nehru Report?
1. The Muslim League rejected it.
2. Jinnah's amendments failed at the Calcutta All Parties Convention.
3. Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Chandra Bose demanded complete independence.
4. The Congress immediately accepted complete independence without an ultimatum.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
225.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Congress gave Britain a one-year ultimatum; complete independence was declared at Lahore in 1929 after the ultimatum expired.
225.tq: Identify the single false statement by distinguishing an ultimatum from its later outcome.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Muslim League rejected** it; **Jinnah's amendments failed** at the **Calcutta All Parties Convention (Dec 1928)**.
**Jawaharlal Nehru** and **Bose** wanted **complete independence**.
Statement 4 wrong: Congress first gave a **one-year ultimatum**, then declared **Purna Swaraj** at **Lahore (1929)**.
xa: The **All Parties Muslim Conference** (**Delhi, Jan 1929**) under the **Aga Khan** also rejected the report.
Jinnah's **Fourteen Points** followed in **March 1929**.
The report sought **dominion status**, which the young radicals found inadequate.

225.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Nehru Report:
1. Jawaharlal Nehru served as its secretary.
2. It recommended a Supreme Court.
3. It proposed the continuation of dyarchy in the provinces.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
225.x: Jawaharlal Nehru was the secretary and the report recommended a Supreme Court. It proposed ending dyarchy, so statement 3 is false.
225.tq: Locate the one reversed constitutional recommendation.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Jawaharlal Nehru** was **secretary** of the committee.
Statement 2 correct: it recommended a **Supreme Court** with a **bicameral** centre.
Statement 3 wrong: it called for the **end of dyarchy** and **responsible government**.
xa: **Motilal Nehru** chaired the **7-member committee**.
It recommended **linguistic provinces** (incl. **Andhra**) and **joint electorates**.
Report date: **August 1928**.

225.s: The All Parties Muslim Conference held at Delhi in January 1929, under the Aga Khan,
o: drafted the Government of India Act, 1935
resolved to boycott the Simon Commission at every stage
accepted the Nehru Report without modification
225.x: The All Parties Muslim Conference at Delhi in January 1929, presided over by the Aga Khan, rejected the Nehru Report.
225.tq: Distinguish the Muslim Conference's reaction from the earlier All Parties Conference.
xs: The **All Parties Muslim Conference** (**Delhi, Jan 1929**) under the **Aga Khan** **rejected the Nehru Report** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **GoI Act 1935** came from the Simon report + RTCs, not from this conference.
The boycott "at every stage" was not this conference's work.
xa: **Jinnah's Fourteen Points** followed in **March 1929** at the **Muslim League session in Delhi**.
The **Muslim League** also rejected the Nehru Report.
The **Nehru Report** proposed **joint electorates**, unacceptable to these Muslim bodies.

225.s: Jinnah's Fourteen Points were presented in March 1929 at the
o: Indian National Congress session at Lahore
Second Round Table Conference at London
225.x: Jinnah presented the Fourteen Points in March 1929 at the Muslim League session in Delhi.
225.tq: Match a constitutional document with its organisation, venue and date.
xs: Jinnah presented the **Fourteen Points** in **March 1929** at the **Muslim League session in Delhi** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Lahore** session (**1929**) of Congress declared **Purna Swaraj** — not the Fourteen Points.
The **2nd RTC** came later, in **Sep-Dec 1931**.
xa: Demands: **federal constitution**, **residuary powers to provinces**, **one-third** Muslim seats at the centre, **separate electorates**, Muslim-majority safeguards.
⚠ **Delhi Proposals (1927)** = drop separate electorates; **Fourteen Points (1929)** = keep them.
The **All Parties Muslim Conference** (**Jan 1929**) under the **Aga Khan** had already rejected the Nehru Report.

225.s:
Which of the following demands formed part of Jinnah's Fourteen Points?
1. Federal constitution with residuary powers vested in the provinces
2. One-third Muslim representation at the centre
3. Separate electorates
4. Safeguards for Muslim-majority provinces
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
225.x: All four were among the major demands associated with Jinnah's Fourteen Points: provincial residuary powers, one-third central representation, separate electorates and safeguards for Muslim-majority provinces.
225.tq: Distinguish Jinnah's demands from the joint-electorate provisions of the Nehru Report.
xs: **All four** demands were in the Fourteen Points — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Federal constitution** + **residuary powers to provinces**; **one-third** Muslim seats at the centre.
**Separate electorates** + **Muslim-majority safeguards**.
xa: Presented in **March 1929** at the **Muslim League session in Delhi**.
⚠ The **Delhi Proposals (March 1927)** had offered to **drop** separate electorates for joint electorates.
The Delhi Proposals also sought **separation of Sindh** and reforms in **NWFP and Baluchistan**.

225.s: Which one of the following most accurately states the significance of the Deepavali Declaration?
o: It introduced provincial autonomy and abolished separate electorates.
It accepted the demand for a separate Andhra Province and announced the Government of India Act, 1935.
It declared complete independence as the immediate constitutional objective and cancelled the Simon Commission.
It recognised dominion status as the natural goal of India’s constitutional progress and promised a Round Table Conference after the Simon Commission report.
225.x: The declaration described dominion status as the natural goal of India’s constitutional progress and promised a Round Table Conference after the Simon report.
225.tq: Choose the option that combines the two precise features of the declaration without importing later constitutional measures.
xs: The **Deepavali Declaration** called **dominion status** the **natural goal** of India's constitutional progress and promised a **Round Table Conference** after the Simon report — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was issued by Viceroy **Lord Irwin** on **31 October 1929**.
**Provincial autonomy** came with the **1935 Act**, and the Andhra demand was ignored — options 1 and 2 are wrong.
xa: The **Simon Commission report** came in **May 1930**.
The **1st RTC** began in **Nov 1930** in **London**.
Congress, instead, declared **Purna Swaraj** at **Lahore (1929)**.

225.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Deepavali Declaration:
1. It was issued in 1929.
2. It was issued by Lord Irwin.
3. It promised a Round Table Conference before the Simon Commission report.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
225.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the promised Round Table Conference was to be held after the Simon Commission report.
225.tq: Find the reversed sequence in the statement containing ‘before’ and retain the two directly established facts.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: issued on **31 October 1929**.
Statement 2 correct: issued by Viceroy **Lord Irwin**.
Statement 3 wrong: the RTC was promised **after** the Simon report, not before.
xa: It declared **dominion status** the natural goal of India's constitutional progress.
The **Simon report** followed in **May 1930**.
**Ramsay MacDonald** was British PM during all three RTCs (**1930-32**).

225.s: The Simon Commission submitted its report in which month and year?
225.x: The Simon Commission report was issued in May 1930.
225.tq: Distinguish the report date from the dates of the declaration and the Round Table Conferences.
xs: The **Simon Commission report** came out in **May 1930** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It recommended **abolishing dyarchy** → full **provincial autonomy**, keeping **separate communal electorates**.
xa: Territorial proposals: separate **Sindh** from Bombay, **Burma** from India; create an **Orissa** province.
It **ignored Andhra's demand** for a province.
The report + RTCs led to the **Government of India Act 1935**.

225.s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation of the Simon Commission report?
o: Immediate establishment of complete responsible government at the Centre
225.x: The report recommended abolition of dyarchy, provincial autonomy and continuation of separate communal electorates. Immediate establishment of complete responsible government at the Centre was not listed as its recommendation.
225.tq: Find the option that goes beyond the specific constitutional recommendations rather than merely changing one territorial detail.
xs: **Immediate complete responsible government at the Centre** was not a Simon recommendation — so option **(1)** is the answer.
It did recommend **abolishing dyarchy** → full **provincial autonomy**.
It recommended keeping **separate communal electorates**.
xa: Report date: **May 1930**.
It separated **Sindh** from Bombay and **Burma** from India, and created an **Orissa** province.
Report + RTCs → **Government of India Act 1935**.

225.s:
With reference to the territorial recommendations of the Simon Commission report, consider the following statements:
1. Sindh was to be separated from Bombay.
2. Burma was to be separated from India.
3. Orissa was to be created as a province.
4. Andhra was to be created as a province.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
225.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the report ignored Andhra’s demand for a separate province.
225.tq: Identify the one swapped territorial outcome by comparing the treatment of Orissa and Andhra.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Sindh** from Bombay and **Burma** from India were to be separated; an **Orissa** province was to be created.
Statement 4 wrong: the report **ignored Andhra's demand**.
xa: Contrast: **Oriyas lobbied** the Commission; **Andhras boycotted** it.
This neglect, along with Prakasam's **"Andhra Kesari"** moment, fuelled the **separate-Andhra** demand.
Report date: **May 1930**.

225.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the response of the Oriyas and the Andhras to the Simon Commission?
o: The Oriyas boycotted the Commission, whereas the Andhras lobbied it.
The Oriyas lobbied the Commission, whereas the Andhras boycotted it.
Both groups lobbied the Commission for their respective provincial demands.
Both groups boycotted the Commission and rejected provincial reorganisation.
225.x: The Oriyas lobbied the Simon Commission, while the Andhras boycotted it. The report supported the creation of Orissa but ignored Andhra’s demand.
225.tq: Test the paired contrast directly by checking which group lobbied and which group boycotted.
xs: The **Oriyas lobbied** the Commission, whereas the **Andhras boycotted** it — so option **(2)** is correct.
Result: the report proposed an **Orissa** province but **ignored Andhra's demand**.
xa: Andhra boycott: **Prakasam** in Madras, **black flags** at **Guntur and Ongole**, **Kaleswara Rao's** cover at Vijayawada.
**S. Satyamurthy** was President of the **Andhra Boycott Committee**.
The **Nehru Report** had backed **linguistic provinces** including **Andhra**.

225.s: The report of the Simon Commission, together with the Round Table Conferences, contributed to the enactment of which legislation?
225.x: The Simon Commission report and the Round Table Conferences contributed to the Government of India Act, 1935.
225.tq: Link the constitutional process to its legislative outcome while rejecting earlier and later Acts.
xs: The Simon report + the RTCs led to the **Government of India Act 1935** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **3rd RTC** produced the **White Paper**, then the plan for the **GoI Act 1935**.
The Commission itself reviewed the **1919** Act, so it could not have produced it.
xa: The GoI Act 1935 was passed by the British Parliament on **2 August 1935**.
Simon report (**May 1930**): abolish dyarchy → **provincial autonomy**.
All three RTCs were in **London** under PM **Ramsay MacDonald**.

225.s: Which of the following statements about the three Round Table Conferences is correct?
o: Only the Second Conference was held in London to discuss dominion status.
All three were held in Delhi under the Viceroy of India.
The conferences were convened by the Indian National Congress to draft the Nehru Report.
All three were held in London under Ramsay MacDonald to discuss the Simon Report and a federal constitution.
225.x: All three Round Table Conferences were held in London under British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald to discuss the Simon Report and a federal constitution.
225.tq: Use venue, convening authority and agenda together to eliminate substituted details.
xs: All three RTCs were held in **London** under PM **Ramsay MacDonald** to discuss the **Simon Report** and a **federal constitution** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They were not in **Delhi**, and the **Nehru Report** (**1928**) was an Indian effort before the RTCs.
xa: Congress attended only the **2nd** RTC; **Ambedkar** attended all three.
The 1st RTC agreed on a **federal structure**.

225.s:
Which of the following statements about the Third Round Table Conference is correct?
1. It was held from 17 November to 24 December 1932.
2. The Congress boycotted it.
3. It had only 46 delegates.
4. It contributed to the plan for the Government of India Act, 1935.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
225.x: All four statements are correct. The Third Conference was held in late 1932, was boycotted by Congress, had 46 delegates and helped shape the plan for the Government of India Act, 1935.
225.tq: Check the date, attendance, size and constitutional outcome as a single cluster.
xs: **All four** statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Held **17 Nov-24 Dec 1932**; **Congress boycotted** it (Jinnah too was absent).
Only **46 delegates**; it led to the **White Paper** and then the plan for the **GoI Act 1935**.
xa: The GoI Act 1935 was passed on **2 August 1935**.
APPSC **2025** match: 3rd RTC = **Congress absent again**.
**Ambedkar** and **Tej Bahadur Sapru** attended all three RTCs.

225.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First Round Table Conference — Congress represented by Gandhi
Second Round Table Conference — Gandhi as sole INC representative
Third Round Table Conference — attended by Congress under Jawaharlal Nehru
First Round Table Conference — held after the Gandhi-Irwin Pact
225.x: Gandhi attended the Second Round Table Conference as the sole representative of the Indian National Congress. Congress boycotted the First and Third Conferences.
225.tq: Start with the sure Congress-attendance pair and eliminate reversals.
xs: **Gandhi** was the **sole INC representative** at the **2nd RTC** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Congress **boycotted** the **1st RTC** (CDM was on) and was **absent** from the **3rd**.
The **1st RTC** led to the **Gandhi-Irwin Pact**, so it came before the pact, not after.
xa: 2nd RTC: **Sep-Dec 1931**, opened **7 Sept 1931**; failed on **minority representation**.
**Sarojini Naidu** and **Muhammad Iqbal** attended the 2nd RTC (APPSC G2 **2005**).
APPSC **2025** match: Gandhi-Irwin Pact = Gandhi agrees to attend the next RTC.

225.s: Dr B. R. Ambedkar attended the Round Table Conferences as a representative of the
225.x: Ambedkar participated in the Round Table Conferences as a representative of the depressed classes.
225.tq: Match the prominent delegate with the social group he represented.
xs: **Ambedkar** attended the RTCs for the **depressed classes** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He attended **all three** RTCs, along with **Tej Bahadur Sapru**.
xa: At the **2nd RTC**, Gandhi had disputes with the League and **Ambedkar** (APPSC **2025** match).
After the 2nd RTC came the **Communal Award** (**Aug 1932**).
The **1st RTC** was attended by the **Muslim League**, **Hindu Mahasabha**, **princes** and Ambedkar.

225.s: After the Second Round Table Conference, Mahatma Gandhi
o: joined the Third Round Table Conference as a British delegate
resumed the Civil Disobedience Movement and was jailed in Yerwada
formed the Muslim League to negotiate minority representation
accepted the Communal Award and retired from public life
225.x: After the Second Conference, Gandhi resumed the Civil Disobedience Movement and was imprisoned in Yerwada. The Communal Award followed in August 1932.
225.tq: Link a conference outcome with its immediate political consequence.
xs: After the **2nd RTC**, Gandhi **resumed the CDM** and was **jailed in Yerwada** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Communal Award** (**Aug 1932**) followed while he was in jail.
Congress was **absent** from the **3rd RTC**, so Gandhi did not attend it.
xa: The 2nd RTC failed on **minority representation**.
3rd RTC: **17 Nov-24 Dec 1932**, only **46** delegates.
Gandhi was the **sole INC representative** at the 2nd RTC.

225.s: The Government of India Act, 1935 was passed by the British Parliament on
225.x: The Government of India Act, 1935 was passed by the British Parliament on 2 August 1935.
225.tq: Distinguish the enactment date from the dates of the Third Round Table Conference.
xs: The **GoI Act 1935** was passed by the British Parliament on **2 August 1935** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**17 November** and **24 December 1932** are the start and end of the **3rd RTC**.
xa: The 3rd RTC led to the **White Paper**, then the plan for the Act.
Its basis: **Simon report** + RTCs.
All RTCs were in **London** under **Ramsay MacDonald**.

225.s: Which one of the following was a feature of the First Round Table Conference?
o: The Congress participated through Gandhi as its sole representative.
The Congress boycotted it, while the Muslim League, Hindu Mahasabha, princes and Ambedkar attended.
The Congress attended through Sarojini Naidu and Muhammad Iqbal.
It was attended by 46 delegates after the Communal Award.
225.x: The Congress boycotted the First Round Table Conference. Representatives of the Muslim League, Hindu Mahasabha, princely states and Ambedkar attended it.
225.tq: Test participation through the strongest conference-specific distinction.
xs: At the **1st RTC**, **Congress boycotted** while the **Muslim League, Hindu Mahasabha, princes and Ambedkar** attended — so option **(2)** is correct.
Congress stayed away because the **CDM** was on.
Gandhi as sole INC representative and **Sarojini Naidu / Iqbal** belong to the **2nd RTC**; **46 delegates** belongs to the **3rd**.
xa: 1st RTC: **Nov 1930**-Jan 1931; it agreed on a **federal structure**.
It led to the **Gandhi-Irwin Pact**.
The **Communal Award** came only in **Aug 1932**.

225.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Round Table Conferences:
1. The First Conference agreed on a federal structure.
2. The Second Conference ended in a deadlock over the minorities question.
3. The Third Conference was attended by the Congress and Jinnah.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
225.x: The First Conference agreed on a federal structure and the Second ended in a deadlock over minorities. The Congress and Jinnah were absent from the Third Conference.
225.tq: Find the false participation statement before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **1st RTC** agreed on a **federal structure**.
Statement 2 correct: the **2nd RTC** failed on **minority representation**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Congress** and **Jinnah** were **absent** from the **3rd RTC**.
xa: The 3rd RTC had only **46 delegates**.
Congress attended only the **2nd** RTC; **Ambedkar** attended all three.
All three were in **London** under **Ramsay MacDonald** (**1930-32**).

225.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to participation in all three Round Table Conferences?
o: B.R. Ambedkar and Tej Bahadur Sapru
225.x: B.R. Ambedkar and Tej Bahadur Sapru attended all three Round Table Conferences.
225.tq: Start from the sure pair involving participants present at all three conferences.
xs: **Ambedkar and Tej Bahadur Sapru** attended all three RTCs — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Gandhi**, **Muhammad Iqbal** and **Sarojini Naidu** are linked with the **2nd RTC** only.
**Jinnah** was absent from the **3rd RTC**.
xa: Ambedkar represented the **depressed classes**.
Congress attended only the **2nd** RTC.
The 3rd RTC (**1932**) had only **46** delegates.

225.s: Besides Gandhi, which of the following attended the Second Round Table Conference (1931)?
o: Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Chandra Bose
225.x: Sarojini Naidu and Muhammad Iqbal attended the Second RTC (Sept-Dec 1931), where Gandhi was the sole INC representative (APPSC G2 2005). Nehru, Bose, Patel and Azad did not attend; Motilal Nehru and C.R. Das had died before 1931.
225.tq: 2nd RTC: Gandhi + Sarojini Naidu + Iqbal.
xs: **Sarojini Naidu** and **Muhammad Iqbal** attended the **2nd RTC** — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC G2 **2005**).
**Gandhi** was the **sole INC representative** there.
xa: The 2nd RTC: **Sep-Dec 1931**, opened **7 Sept 1931** (some notes say "Nov-Dec 1931").
It failed on **minority representation**.
After it Gandhi resumed the **CDM** and was jailed in **Yerwada**.

225.s: Lala Lajpat Rai, who led the anti-Simon Commission protest in Lahore, had earlier presided over the first session of the AITUC in which year?
225.x: Lala Lajpat Rai presided over the first session of the All India Trade Union Congress in 1920.
225.tq: Connect the personality with the distinct organisational milestone and its year.
xs: **Lala Lajpat Rai** presided the **first session of AITUC** in **1920** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was **fatally injured** leading the **anti-Simon protest in Lahore**.
xa: This was recalled on **1 May 2026** for the **Trade Unions Act** centenary.
The Simon Commission report came in **May 1930**.
In Andhra, **Tanguturi Prakasam** led the **Madras** protest and became **"Andhra Kesari"**.

225.s: Which one of the following statements best explains the historical significance of Lala Lajpat Rai’s role in the anti-Simon Commission movement?
o: He led the Lahore protest and was fatally injured in the anti-Simon agitation.
He chaired the Simon Commission and drafted its report.
He represented the Indian National Congress at all three Round Table Conferences.
He secured the acceptance of Andhra’s demand by the Simon Commission.
225.x: Lala Lajpat Rai led the anti-Simon protest in Lahore and was fatally injured during the agitation.
225.tq: Use the leader–movement–consequence chain to reject options assigning him unrelated constitutional roles.
xs: **Lajpat Rai** **led the Lahore protest** and was **fatally injured** in the anti-Simon agitation — so option **(1)** is correct.
The Simon Commission was not Indian-led; Congress attended only the **2nd** RTC; Andhra's demand was **ignored** by the report.
xa: He had presided over **AITUC's first session** in **1920**.
Recalled on **1 May 2026** (Trade Unions Act centenary).
Madras counterpart: **Tanguturi Prakasam**, who bared his chest (**1928**).

225.s: The neglect of Andhra’s demand by the Simon Commission, along with Tanguturi Prakasam’s ‘Andhra Kesari’ moment, contributed to which political development?
o: The demand for a separate Andhra Province
The demand for the continuation of Burma within India
The demand for the abolition of provincial autonomy
The demand for the restoration of dyarchy in the provinces
225.x: The neglect of Andhra’s demand by the Simon Commission and Prakasam’s political role fuelled the demand for a separate Andhra Province.
225.tq: Trace the stated regional grievance to the political demand it helped strengthen.
xs: These fuelled the **demand for a separate Andhra Province** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The Simon report created an **Orissa** province but **ignored Andhra's demand**.
The report itself recommended separating **Burma** from India and **abolishing dyarchy** — the other options run against it.
xa: **Oriyas lobbied** the Commission; **Andhras boycotted** it.
**Prakasam** became **"Andhra Kesari"** at the **Madras** protest (**26 Feb 1928**).
The **Nehru Report** had backed **linguistic provinces** including **Andhra**.

226.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, the Federal, Provincial and Concurrent Lists contained, respectively, how many subjects?
226.x: The Federal List contained 59 subjects, the Provincial List 54 subjects and the Concurrent List 36 subjects.
226.tq: Use the numerical association between the three lists and eliminate options that interchange their figures.
xs: The **Federal, Provincial and Concurrent** Lists had **59, 54 and 36** items — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Federal** = **59** (largest), **Provincial** = **54**, **Concurrent** = **36** (smallest).
xa: **Residuary powers** were with the **Governor-General**.
The **Governor** had discretionary powers, e.g. the **Sec. 63** address.
The **federal scheme** is among the features borrowed into the Constitution.

226.s:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act, 1935:
1. Residuary powers were vested in the provincial legislatures.
2. The Governor-General could stop discussion and suspend proceedings on a Bill.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
226.x: Statement 1 is wrong: residuary powers were vested in the Governor-General, not the provinces. Statement 2 is correct: the Governor-General could stop discussion and suspend Bill proceedings. Hence 2 only; 1 only, both and neither are wrong.
226.tq: Under the 1935 Act the Governor-General held both residuary and blocking powers.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 wrong: **residuary powers** lay with the **Governor-General**, not the provinces.
Statement 2 correct: the **Governor-General** could **stop discussion** and **suspend bill proceedings**.
xa: Three lists: **Federal (59)**, **Provincial (54)**, **Concurrent (36)**.
**Separate electorates** were extended to **depressed classes, women and labour**.
The **Governor** had discretion too, e.g. the **Sec. 63** address.

226.s: The Government of India Act, 1935 further extended the system of separate electorates to include which of the following groups?
o: Workers, soldiers and civil servants only
226.x: The separate electorate system was extended further to depressed classes, women and labour.
226.tq: Test the exact membership of a statutory category through a closely related group-list option.
xs: Separate electorates were extended to **depressed classes, women and labour** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The 1935 Act extended the communal scheme **further** rather than ending it.
xa: The Act was called a **"Charter of Slavery"** by **Nehru**.
**Residuary powers** went to the **Governor-General**.
Congress rejected the Act and demanded a **Constituent Assembly** on **adult franchise**.

226.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Congress response to the Government of India Act, 1935 is correct?
o: Congress accepted the Act without qualification and abandoned the demand for a Constituent Assembly.
Congress accepted the Federation but rejected provincial autonomy.
Congress rejected the Act and demanded a Constituent Assembly elected on adult franchise.
Congress rejected elections and demanded restoration of dyarchy in the provinces.
226.x: Congress rejected the Act and demanded a Constituent Assembly elected on adult franchise.
226.tq: Identify the precise political demand rather than an extreme reversal of policy.
xs: Congress **rejected the Act** and demanded a **Constituent Assembly elected on adult franchise** — so option **(3)** is correct.
This became the **official Congress demand** in **1935**; **M.N. Roy** had first raised it in **1934**.
Congress did not reject elections — the **Faizpur (1936)** session decided to **contest** them.
xa: ⚠ **Lucknow 1936** (Nehru presiding) = rejected the Act; **Faizpur 1936** = contest the elections.
**Nehru**: a **"Charter of Slavery"**, "a machine with **strong brakes but no engine**".
After the polls Congress formed ministries in **8 of 11** provinces.

226.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. M.N. Roy raised the demand for a Constituent Assembly in 1934.
2. The demand became an official Congress demand in 1935.
3. The Lucknow session of 1936 rejected the Government of India Act.
4. The Faizpur session of 1936 decided to contest the elections.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
226.x: All four statements are correct. M.N. Roy first raised the Constituent Assembly demand in 1934, Congress adopted it officially in 1935, Lucknow rejected the Act, and Faizpur decided to contest the elections.
226.tq: Arrange related resolutions by person, year and Congress session.
xs: **All four** statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
**M.N. Roy** first raised the **Constituent Assembly** demand in **1934**; it became the **official Congress demand** in **1935**.
**Lucknow (1936)**, under **Nehru**, **rejected** the Act; **Faizpur (1936)** decided to **contest** the elections.
xa: The demand was for an Assembly elected on **adult franchise**.
The elections were held in winter **1936-37** in **11** provinces.
**Jinnah** called the Act "thoroughly rotten, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable".

226.s: Who described the Government of India Act, 1935 as “thoroughly rotten, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable”?
226.x: Muhammad Ali Jinnah used the description “thoroughly rotten, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable” for the Act.
226.tq: Discriminate between two well-known but different criticisms of the same Act.
xs: **Jinnah** called the Act "**thoroughly rotten, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable**" — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Nehru** called it a **"Charter of Slavery"** and "a machine with **strong brakes but no engine**".
**M.N. Roy** is known for first raising the **Constituent Assembly** demand (**1934**).
xa: Congress officially demanded a Constituent Assembly in **1935**.
The **Muslim League** later **did poorly** even in Muslim seats in the **1937** elections.
⚠ **Lucknow 1936** rejected the Act; **Faizpur 1936** decided to contest.

226.s: Who described the Government of India Act, 1935 as a 'Charter of Slavery' and as 'a machine with strong brakes but no engine'?
226.x: Jawaharlal Nehru used both descriptions. Jinnah called the Act 'thoroughly rotten, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable'; M.N. Roy first raised the Constituent Assembly demand (1934).
226.tq: Charter of Slavery / brakes no engine = Nehru; 'rotten' = Jinnah.
xs: **Jawaharlal Nehru** used both phrases — **"Charter of Slavery"** and "a machine with **strong brakes but no engine**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Jinnah** called it "**thoroughly rotten**, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable".
**M.N. Roy** first raised the **Constituent Assembly** demand (**1934**).
xa: Nehru presided the **Lucknow (1936)** session, which rejected the Act.
**Faizpur (1936)** decided to contest the elections.
Congress demanded a **Constituent Assembly** on **adult franchise** (official in **1935**).

226.s: Who led the Congress campaign in the 1937 Madras elections along with Bulusu Sambamurthy?
226.x: The campaign was led by Tanguturi Prakasam, then President of the Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee, and Bulusu Sambamurthy.
226.tq: Match the political campaign with its leading figures rather than the later ministry.
xs: The Madras campaign was led by **Tanguturi Prakasam** (**APCC President**) with **Bulusu Sambamurthy** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Madras polls: **15-20 February 1937**.
**Rajagopalachari** later became **Premier**; **Gopala Reddy** and **V.V. Giri** became ministers.
xa: The **Justice Party was wiped out**; only a few, like the **Challapalli Zamindar**, won.
The **Pithapuram Zamindar's People's Party** lost everything.
Bulusu Sambamurthy became **Speaker** in the **1937** ministry.

226.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the political outcome in the Madras Presidency after the 1937 elections?
o: The Muslim League formed the ministry under a coalition arrangement.
The Congress formed the ministry, while the Justice Party was almost wiped out.
The Justice Party formed the ministry with the People's Party.
The Hindu Mahasabha formed the ministry with the Congress.
226.x: The Congress formed the Madras ministry, while the Justice Party was almost wiped out. The People's Party of the Pithapuram Zamindar lost all its seats, and the League and Hindu Mahasabha performed poorly.
226.tq: Reject the options that assign office to parties which performed poorly.
xs: In Madras, **Congress formed the ministry** while the **Justice Party was wiped out** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Only a few Justice men, like the **Challapalli Zamindar**, won.
The **Pithapuram Zamindar's People's Party** lost everything; the **League** and **Hindu Mahasabha** did poorly.
xa: The ministry was formed on **14 July 1937** under **C. Rajagopalachari** (APHQ **2011**).
It ended **Justice Party** rule of **1920-37**.
The campaign was led by **Tanguturi Prakasam** and **Bulusu Sambamurthy**.

226.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Leader)
 a. Tanguturi Prakasam
 b. Bezawada Gopala Reddy
 c. V.V. Giri
 d. Bulusu Sambamurthy

List-II (Post)
 i. Speaker
 ii. Labour and Industries
 iii. Revenue
 iv. Local Self-Government

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
226.x: Tanguturi Prakasam held Revenue, Bezawada Gopala Reddy held Local Self-Government, V.V. Giri held Labour and Industries, and Bulusu Sambamurthy was Speaker.
226.tq: Start from the sure leader-post pair and eliminate inconsistent codes.
xs: Correct matching **a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Prakasam** — **Revenue**; **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** — **Local Self-Government**.
**V.V. Giri** — **Labour and Industries**; **Bulusu Sambamurthy** — **Speaker**.
xa: The ministry was headed by Premier **C. Rajagopalachari** (**14 July 1937**).
Rajaji's Hindi move in schools → **Periyar's anti-Hindi agitation (1937)** → withdrawn.
Prakasam was **APCC President** and led the **1937** campaign.

226.s: The introduction of Hindi in Madras schools by C. Rajagopalachari's ministry led to:
o: the merger of the Justice Party with the Congress
the resignation of the Congress ministry in 1937
Periyar's anti-Hindi agitation and subsequent withdrawal of the policy
the permanent adoption of Hindi as the sole medium of instruction
226.x: Rajaji introduced Hindi in Madras schools, but Periyar's anti-Hindi agitation in 1937 led the government to withdraw the policy.
226.tq: Follow the cause-effect chain from a policy to the political response.
xs: Hindi in Madras schools led to **Periyar's anti-Hindi agitation** (**1937**) and the policy was **withdrawn** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Hindi did not become the permanent medium — it was **withdrawn**.
The Congress ministries resigned only in **Oct-Nov 1939**, over **WWII**.
xa: Rajaji became Premier on **14 July 1937** (APHQ **2011**).
It was the **first Congress government in Madras**, ending **Justice Party** rule (**1920-37**).
Andhra ministers: **Prakasam** (Revenue), **Gopala Reddy** (Local Self-Government), **V.V. Giri** (Labour and Industries).

226.s: The provincial elections under the Government of India Act, 1935 were held in:
226.x: The elections were held in the winter of 1936-37 in eleven provinces.
226.tq: Combine the election season, years and number of provinces.
xs: The elections were held in **winter 1936-37** in **11 provinces** — so option **(4)** is correct.
