Madras voted on **15-20 February 1937**.
xa: Congress formed ministries in **8 of 11** provinces.
The **Muslim League did poorly** even in Muslim seats.
**Faizpur (1936)** had decided that Congress would contest.

226.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bengal — Unionist Party ministry under Sikandar Hayat Khan
Bengal — Coalition led by Fazlul Huq's Krishak Praja Party
226.x: In Bengal, Fazlul Huq's Krishak Praja Party formed a coalition. Punjab was associated with the Unionist Party under Sikandar Hayat Khan, while Sindh had a coalition under Allah Baksh.
226.tq: Use province-leader-party associations to reject swapped outcomes.
xs: **Bengal** had a coalition led by **Fazlul Huq's Krishak Praja Party** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Punjab** had the **Unionist Party** under **Sikandar Hayat Khan** — option 1 puts it in Bengal.
**Sindh** had a coalition under **Allah Baksh** — not a Congress majority, and not in Punjab.
xa: **Bombay**: Congress largest party, formed ministry.
Elections: winter **1936-37** in **11** provinces.
The **Muslim League** did poorly even in Muslim seats.

226.s: Which of the following statements about the Muslim League's performance after the 1937 elections is correct?
o: It performed strongly in all Muslim seats and formed ministries in every Muslim-majority province.
It did poorly even in Muslim seats, after which it alleged Hindu Raj and launched mass-contact campaigns.
It merged with the Congress in the provinces where Congress formed ministries.
It won a clear majority in Bengal and rejected mass-contact campaigns.
226.x: The Muslim League performed poorly even in Muslim seats. It subsequently alleged “Hindu Raj” and launched mass-contact campaigns.
226.tq: Trace the political consequence of an electoral setback.
xs: The League **did poorly even in Muslim seats**, then alleged **"Hindu Raj"** and launched **mass-contact campaigns** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Bengal** went to a **Fazlul Huq** coalition, **Punjab** to the **Unionists**, **Sindh** to **Allah Baksh** — not the League.
xa: In Madras too the **League + Hindu Mahasabha** did poorly.
Later the League observed **"Deliverance Day"** on **22 December 1939**.
**Jinnah** had called the 1935 Act "thoroughly rotten".

226.s: The Congress ministry formed in Madras on 14 July 1937 was headed by:
226.x: C. Rajagopalachari (Rajaji) became Premier of Madras on 14 July 1937 (APHQ 2011). Prakasam was Revenue Minister, V.V. Giri Labour and Industries Minister, and Bulusu Sambamurthy the Speaker.
226.tq: Madras 1937 Premier = Rajaji; Prakasam = Revenue.
xs: The Madras Congress ministry of **14 July 1937** was headed by **C. Rajagopalachari** — so option **(3)** is correct (APHQ **2011**).
**Prakasam** was **Revenue Minister**, **V.V. Giri** handled **Labour and Industries**, **Bulusu Sambamurthy** was **Speaker**.
xa: **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** held **Local Self-Government**.
It ended **Justice Party** rule (**1920-37**).
Rajaji's Hindi policy → **Periyar's anti-Hindi agitation** → withdrawn.

226.s: In how many provinces did the Indian National Congress form ministries after the elections held under the Government of India Act, 1935?
226.x: Congress formed ministries in eight of the eleven provinces in 1937. These included Bombay, Madras, Central Provinces, Orissa, Bihar, the United Provinces, the North-West Frontier Province and Assam.
226.tq: Use the total number as the distinguishing numerical fact.
xs: Congress formed ministries in **eight** (**8 of 11**) provinces — so option **(3)** is correct.
**July 1937**: Bombay, Madras, Central Provinces, Orissa, Bihar, United Provinces (six); later **NWFP and Assam** → total **8**.
It had a **clear majority on its own** in **5** provinces.
xa: The 5: **Madras, UP, CP, Bihar, Orissa**.
**Gandhi's advice**: hold office "**lightly, not tightly**", a "**crown of thorns**".
The ministries **resigned in Oct-Nov 1939**.

226.s: Which one of the following groups consisted entirely of provinces where the Congress secured a clear majority on its own in the 1937 elections?
o: Bombay, Madras, Bengal, Bihar and Punjab
Madras, Assam, Sindh, Bihar and Orissa
Madras, United Provinces, Central Provinces, Bihar and Orissa
United Provinces, Bombay, Punjab, Orissa and Bengal
226.x: Congress secured clear majorities in Madras, the United Provinces, the Central Provinces, Bihar and Orissa.
226.tq: Separate clear-majority provinces from provinces where Congress was only the largest party.
xs: Congress had a **clear majority on its own** in **Madras, UP, CP, Bihar and Orissa** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Bengal** (Fazlul Huq coalition), **Punjab** (Unionists) and **Sindh** (Allah Baksh coalition) were not Congress.
**Bombay** — Congress was the **largest party**, not listed among the clear majorities.
xa: In all, Congress formed ministries in **8 of 11** provinces, adding **NWFP and Assam** later.
**July 1937** ministries: Bombay, Madras, CP, Orissa, Bihar, UP.
The Madras ministry under **Rajaji** began on **14 July 1937**.

226.s: Mahatma Gandhi advised the Congress ministries to hold office:
o: firmly and permanently as a constitutional right
only until the completion of the war
lightly, not tightly, as a crown of thorns
226.x: Gandhi advised the ministers to hold office “lightly, not tightly”, describing office as a “crown of thorns”.
226.tq: Test the exact wording of a famous political expression.
xs: **Gandhi** told the ministries to hold office "**lightly, not tightly**", as a "**crown of thorns**" — so option **(4)** is correct.
The ministries indeed **resigned in Oct-Nov 1939** rather than cling to office.
xa: Congress formed ministries in **8 of 11** provinces.
Their record: **civil liberties**, **Tenancy Acts**, abolition of **begar**, **Industrial Disputes Act (1938)**.
**Harijans** got free education and other upliftment measures.

226.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the resignation of the Congress ministries:
1. The Congress ministries resigned in October-November 1939.
2. They resigned because Viceroy Linlithgow declared India a party to the Second World War without consulting Indian leaders.
3. The Muslim League observed 22 December 1940 as Deliverance Day.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
226.x: Statement 1 is correct: the ministries resigned in October-November 1939. Statement 2 is correct: Linlithgow declared India a party to the war (September 1939) without consulting Indian leaders. Statement 3 is wrong: Deliverance Day was observed on 22 December 1939, not 1940. So 1 only is incomplete, 2 and 3 only and 1, 2 and 3 wrongly include statement 3.
226.tq: Resignation and Deliverance Day fall in the same year, 1939.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the ministries **resigned in Oct-Nov 1939**.
Statement 2 correct: Viceroy **Linlithgow** declared India a party to **World War II** (**Sept 1939**) without consulting Indian leaders.
Statement 3 wrong: **Deliverance Day** was **22 December 1939**, not 1940.
xa: Some notes give the resignation as **October 1939**, others **November 1939**.
APPSC **2018** asked the reason: protest against making India a party to the war with **Germany**.
The ministries had been formed in **July 1937**.

226.s: Which one of the following was NOT a measure undertaken by the Congress ministries in the sphere of civil liberties?
o: Imposing wider bans on leftist organisations
226.x: Congress ministries lifted bans on leftist bodies; they did not impose wider bans on them. They also lifted emergency powers, released political prisoners and restored press freedom.
226.tq: Find the reversed policy among a cluster of civil-liberties measures.
xs: The ministries **lifted** bans on leftist bodies — imposing **wider bans** was not their measure — so option **(4)** is the answer.
Civil liberties record: **emergency powers lifted**, **political prisoners released**, **press freedom restored**.
xa: Agrarian: **Tenancy Acts** (e.g. UP), abolition of **begar**, **debt relief**.
Labour: **Industrial Disputes Act (1938)** + **trade-union rights**.
Harijans: **free education** + upliftment measures.

226.s:
Consider the following statements about the record of the Congress ministries (1937-39):
1. Tenancy legislation was passed, for example in the United Provinces.
2. Begar, which they abolished, was a tax on salt.
3. Free education was provided for Harijans.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
226.x: Statement 1 is correct: Tenancy Acts (e.g. UP) were part of the agrarian record. Statement 2 is wrong: begar was forced labour, not a salt tax, though it was abolished. Statement 3 is correct: Harijans got free education. So 1 and 3 only; 1 only omits statement 3, and the options with 2 are wrong.
226.tq: Begar = forced labour; remember the ministries' three agrarian steps: tenancy, begar, debt relief.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Tenancy Acts** were passed, e.g. in **UP**.
Statement 2 wrong: **begar** was **forced labour**, not a salt tax (it was abolished).
Statement 3 correct: **Harijans** got **free education**.
xa: **Debt relief** was another agrarian measure.
Labour: **Industrial Disputes Act (1938)**.
Civil liberties: political prisoners released, **press freedom** restored.

226.s: Which of the following measures best reflects the labour policy of the Congress ministries?
o: Extension of begar to industrial establishments
Recognition of trade-union rights and enactment of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1938
Abolition of all trade unions and suspension of industrial legislation
Transfer of labour legislation exclusively to the Governor-General
226.x: The Congress ministries promoted trade-union rights and enacted the Industrial Disputes Act in 1938. The other alternatives contradict the stated labour record.
226.tq: Match the policy objective with the specific labour legislation and institutional reform associated with it.
xs: Labour policy = **trade-union rights** + the **Industrial Disputes Act, 1938** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Begar** (forced labour) was **abolished**, not extended.
xa: Agrarian measures: **Tenancy Acts**, **debt relief**.
Civil liberties: emergency powers lifted, bans on **leftist bodies** lifted.
The ministries ruled **1937-39** and resigned over **World War II**.

226.s: The provision of the Government of India Act, 1935 that served as a model for the Directive Principles of State Policy was the:
226.x: The Instrument of Instructions under the Government of India Act, 1935 served as the model for the Directive Principles of State Policy.
226.tq: Test a direct source-feature relationship.
xs: The **Instrument of Instructions** of the 1935 Act was the model for the **Directive Principles** — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC **2023**).
The **Federal Court** and **separate provincial budget** are other borrowings, not the DPSP model.
xa: Other 1935 borrowings: **federal scheme**, **office of Governor**, **judiciary**, **PSCs**, **emergency provisions**.
From the **1919** Act: **bicameralism** and **direct elections** at the Centre, **separate provincial budget**.
The Act is called the **blueprint** of the Constitution.

226.s: Which one of the following sets contains only features borrowed from the Government of India Act, 1935?
o: Concurrent List, joint sitting and freedom of trade
Fundamental Rights, judicial review, impeachment and Vice-President
Federal scheme, office of Governor, judiciary and Public Service Commissions
Fundamental Duties, Five-Year Plans and ideals of justice
226.x: The Government of India Act, 1935 contributed the federal scheme, office of Governor, judiciary and Public Service Commissions, among other administrative features.
226.tq: Group the administrative and institutional provisions before considering ideological or federal borrowings from other countries.
xs: **Federal scheme, office of Governor, judiciary and PSCs** all come from the **1935 Act** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The Act also gave **emergency provisions** and administrative details.
xa: **Instrument of Instructions** → model for the **Directive Principles** (APPSC **2023**).
**1919 Act** → **bicameralism**, **direct elections**, **separate provincial budget**.
Large parts of the Constitution's structure come from the 1935 Act — hence "**blueprint**".

226.s: Which Act is correctly associated with the introduction of dyarchy in the provinces, bicameralism at the Centre and direct elections?
226.x: These three features were introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919, also known as the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.
226.tq: Recognize the characteristic three-feature combination of the 1919 Act.
xs: **Dyarchy in the provinces**, **bicameralism at the Centre** and **direct elections** came with the **Government of India Act, 1919** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **1935 Act** instead brought **provincial autonomy**, three lists and the **Instrument of Instructions**.
xa: The **1919** Act also gave a **Public Service Commission** and a **separate provincial budget**.
**1935** borrowings: **federal scheme**, **office of Governor**, **judiciary**, **emergency provisions**.
⚠ Do not confuse: **1919** = bicameralism and direct elections; **1935** = federal scheme.

226.s: The idea behind Section 63 of the Government of India Act, 1935, on the Governor's address to the provincial legislature, is carried in which Article of the Constitution of India?
226.x: Article 175 (the Governor's address) carries the idea of Section 63 of the 1935 Act. Today the speech reflects the elected ministry's policy rather than the Governor's own discretion.
226.tq: Sec. 63 grew into Art. 175.
xs: **Section 63** (Governor's address) is carried by **Article 175** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Under Sec. 63 the Governor addressed the provincial legislature "**in his discretion**".
Today the speech reflects the **elected ministry's policy**.
xa: Rows over **Governors' addresses** in **Opposition-ruled States** are traced to Sec. 63 and Art. 175 (**26 Jan 2026**).
The **office of Governor** itself is a **1935** borrowing.
The **Instrument of Instructions** became the model for the **Directive Principles**.

226.s: The Government of India Act, 1935 is often regarded as a blueprint of the Constitution of India because
o: large parts of the constitutional structure were derived from it
it introduced universal adult franchise throughout India
it abolished all forms of provincial government
it established the Constitution of India in its final form
226.x: The Act is regarded as a blueprint because large parts of the structure of the Constitution of India were derived from its institutional framework. It did not itself establish the later Constitution or universal adult franchise.
226.tq: Reject the extreme claims and select the precise structural comparison.
xs: The Act is a **blueprint** because **large parts of the Constitution's structure** come from it — so option **(1)** is correct.
Borrowed: **federal scheme**, **office of Governor**, **judiciary**, **PSCs**, **emergency provisions**.
It did not introduce universal adult franchise — Congress was still **demanding** a Constituent Assembly on **adult franchise**.
xa: **Instrument of Instructions** → **Directive Principles** (APPSC **2023**).
It brought **provincial autonomy**, which made an **Andhra** state look achievable.
**Sec. 63** → **Article 175** (Governor's address).

226.s: The present relevance of Section 63 of the Government of India Act, 1935 is most directly seen in debates concerning
o: Governors' addresses in Opposition-ruled States, along with Article 175
the composition of the Union Public Service Commission under Article 315
the appointment of the Election Commission under Article 324
226.x: Contemporary rows concerning Governors' addresses in Opposition-ruled States are traced to Section 63 of the 1935 Act and Article 175 of the Constitution.
226.tq: Link the historical provision with its modern constitutional parallel rather than with an unrelated constitutional power.
xs: Sec. 63 is seen today in **Governors' address** rows in **Opposition-ruled States**, read with **Article 175** — so option **(1)** is correct.
These rows were in the news on **26 Jan 2026**.
xa: Sec. 63: Governor addressed the provincial legislature "**in his discretion**".
Under Art. 175 the speech reflects the **elected ministry's policy**.
The Governor's **discretionary powers** under the 1935 Act included this address.

226.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Andhra angle of the Government of India Act, 1935:
1. Provincial autonomy made an Andhra State look achievable.
2. The Sri Bagh Pact (1937) closed the Coastal-Rayalaseema rift before the 1937 polls.
3. The Sri Bagh Pact was concluded at the house of Tanguturi Prakasam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
226.x: Statement 1 is correct: provincial autonomy made an Andhra State look achievable. Statement 2 is correct: the Sri Bagh Pact of 1937 closed the Coastal-Rayalaseema rift. Statement 3 is wrong: the pact was concluded at Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's house 'Sreerbagh', not Prakasam's. So 1 and 2 only.
226.tq: Sri Bagh = Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's house, 1937.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **provincial autonomy** made an **Andhra state** look achievable.
Statement 2 correct: the **Sri Bagh Pact (1937)** closed the **Coastal-Rayalaseema** rift before the polls.
Statement 3 wrong: it was signed at **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's** house **"Sreerbagh"**.
xa: **Prakasam** led the Madras **1937** campaign as **APCC President**.
First Congress government in Madras (**1937**, **Rajaji**) ended Justice Party rule of **1920-37**.
Andhra ministers in **1937**: **Prakasam**, **Gopala Reddy**, **V.V. Giri**; **Bulusu Sambamurthy** Speaker.

226.s: Which statement correctly describes the first Congress government in the Madras Presidency?
o: It was formed in 1937 under the Justice Party and ended provincial autonomy.
It was formed in 1939 under Rajaji and ended the system of separate electorates.
It was formed in 1937 under Rajaji and ended Justice Party rule that had lasted from 1920 to 1937.
It was formed in 1935 under Rajaji and ended Congress rule in the Presidency.
226.x: The first Congress government in Madras was formed in 1937 under Rajaji, bringing to an end Justice Party rule from 1920 to 1937.
226.tq: Combine the distinctive first, year, leader and preceding party rule while rejecting swapped dates and parties.
xs: The first Congress government in Madras was formed in **1937** under **Rajaji** and ended **Justice Party** rule of **1920-37** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was formed on **14 July 1937** (APHQ **2011**), not in 1935 or 1939.
1939 was the year of **resignation** (**Oct-Nov 1939**), not formation.
xa: In the polls (**15-20 February 1937**) the **Justice Party was wiped out**.
**Prakasam** became **Revenue Minister**; **Bulusu Sambamurthy** became **Speaker**.
Rajaji's Hindi move → **Periyar's anti-Hindi agitation (1937)**.

227.s: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 accepted separate electorates along with:
o: Universal adult franchise and linguistic provinces
Complete independence and abolition of legislatures
Reserved seats only for depressed classes in joint electorates
Weightage and a communal veto based on a three-fourths rule
227.x: The Lucknow Pact accepted separate electorates, weightage and a communal veto requiring a three-fourths rule.
227.tq: Test the additional conditions attached to a familiar constitutional arrangement.
xs: The **Lucknow Pact (1916)** accepted separate electorates with **weightage** and a **communal veto** (**three-fourths rule**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Weightage** = more seats than the community's population share.
Reserved seats in **joint electorates** for depressed classes came later, with the **Poona Pact**.
xa: Separate electorates for **Muslims** began with the **Indian Councils Act 1909** (Morley-Minto).
**Minto** is called the "**Father of Communal Electorate**".
The **GoI Act 1919** extended them to **Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, Europeans**.

227.s:
Consider the following statements regarding separate electorates:
1. The Government of India Act, 1919 extended them to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans.
2. The Government of India Act, 1935 gave Muslims 33% of the seats in the Federal Legislature.
3. Separate electorates ended with the Government of India Act, 1935.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
227.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 1919 Act extended separate electorates to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans. Statement 2 is correct: the 1935 Act gave Muslims 33% of Federal Legislature seats. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1935 Act extended them further, and they continued till the Constituent Assembly. So 1 and 2 only.
227.tq: Each Act widened separate electorates; they lasted till the Constituent Assembly.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **1919** Act extended them to **Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, Europeans**.
Statement 2 correct: the **1935** Act gave Muslims **33%** of seats in the **Federal Legislature**.
Statement 3 wrong: the 1935 Act **extended** them further; they **continued till the Constituent Assembly**.
xa: The 1935 Act extended them to **depressed classes (SCs), women and labour**.
The **Communal Award 1932** extended them to depressed classes; the **Poona Pact** replaced that with reserved seats.
**1909**: separate electorates for **Muslims** + **weightage**.

227.s: What was the principal change introduced by the Poona Pact in relation to the Communal Award?
o: The Muslim League was given a communal veto
Separate electorates for Muslims were abolished
Reserved seats in joint electorates replaced separate electorates for the depressed classes
Separate electorates were extended to all Europeans
227.x: The Poona Pact replaced separate electorates for the depressed classes with reserved seats in joint electorates.
227.tq: Compare the original constitutional arrangement with its replacement.
xs: The **Poona Pact** replaced the Award's separate electorates for the **depressed classes** with **reserved seats in joint electorates** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Communal Award 1932** had extended separate electorates to the **depressed classes**.
Muslims kept their separate electorates — they continued **till the Constituent Assembly**.
xa: The **GoI Act 1935** extended them further to **depressed classes (SCs), women and labour**.
**1919**: extended to **Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, Europeans**.
**1916 Lucknow Pact**: Congress accepted them, with **weightage**.

227.s: Jinnah's Point 5 in 1929 provided that:
o: Separate electorates should continue, while any community could opt for joint electorates
Separate electorates should be abolished immediately for every community
The British government should nominate all communal representatives
Only Muslims should have joint electorates
227.x: Jinnah's Point 5 supported continuation of separate electorates but allowed any community to choose joint electorates.
227.tq: Read the conditional qualification carefully instead of reducing the point to a simple yes-or-no position.
xs: **Jinnah's Point 5 (1929)**: **separate electorates to continue**, but **any community** free to **opt for joint electorates** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It did not abolish separate electorates; the **Nehru Report** had rejected them.
xa: The Nehru Report vs the **14 Points** marked the "**parting of the ways**" (**1928-29**).
**1935 Act**: Muslims got **33%** of seats in the Federal Legislature.
The **Shimla Deputation** (**1906**, Aga Khan) first demanded separate electorates.

227.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Government of India Act, 1919
B. Communal Award
C. Indian Councils Act, 1909
D. Government of India Act, 1935
227.x: The correct sequence is the Indian Councils Act of 1909, the Government of India Act of 1919, the Communal Award of 1932 and the Government of India Act of 1935.
227.tq: Arrange constitutional measures by their dates, using the earliest Act as the anchor.
xs: The order is **C, A, B, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Indian Councils Act 1909** → **GoI Act 1919** → **Communal Award 1932** → **GoI Act 1935**.
xa: The **Lucknow Pact 1916** falls between 1909 and 1919.
Each step extended separate electorates: **Muslims** (1909) → **Sikhs, Christians, Anglo-Indians, Europeans** (1919) → **depressed classes** (1932).
The **1935** Act added **women and labour**.

227.s: Which one of the following best describes the long-term political consequence of the Indian Councils Act, 1909?
o: It abolished communal representation in legislatures.
It legally institutionalised communalism and contributed to the growth of the Two-Nation Theory.
It established complete responsible government at the Centre.
It introduced universal adult franchise in British India.
227.x: The 1909 Act legally institutionalised communal representation, thereby strengthening communal politics and contributing to the emergence of the Two-Nation Theory.
227.tq: Identify the precise consequence rather than being distracted by extreme constitutional claims.
xs: The **1909** Act "**legally institutionalised communalism**" — the **seed of the Two-Nation Theory** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It gave **Muslims** separate electorates plus **weightage**; only Muslims voted for Muslim candidates.
It did not abolish communal representation — later Acts **extended** it.
xa: **Minto** = "**Father of Communal Electorate**".
The **Muslim League (1906)** came up in the run-up to 1909.
APPSC-G2 **2025**: "Which Act introduced the communal electorate?" = **Morley-Minto Reforms**.

227.s: Which one of the following Acts first introduced separate (communal) electorates for Muslims in British India?
227.x: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) introduced separate electorates for Muslims, with weightage; Minto is called the Father of Communal Electorate. The 1892 Act did not create them; the 1919 Act extended them to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans; the 1935 Act extended them further to depressed classes, women and labour.
227.tq: Introduced 1909 (Morley-Minto); extended 1919 and 1935.
xs: The **Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms)** first gave **Muslims** separate electorates — so option **(2)** is correct.
It added **weightage**; **Minto** is called the **"Father of Communal Electorate"**.
The **1919** Act **extended** them to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, Europeans; the **1935** Act to **depressed classes, women and labour**.
xa: APPSC-G2 **2025** asked exactly this: answer **Morley-Minto Reforms**.
The **Shimla Deputation** (**1906**) under the **Aga Khan** demanded separate electorates.
The **Lucknow Pact 1916**: Congress accepted them.

227.s: Who among the following was associated with the early advocacy of keeping Muslims away from the Indian National Congress in 1887?
227.x: Sayyid Ahmad Khan, along with Raja Shiv Prasad of Bhinga, promoted an anti-Congress front in 1887.
227.tq: Link the early stage of an idea with its initial advocate.
xs: In **1887**, **Sayyid Ahmad Khan** with **Raja Shiv Prasad of Bhinga** was propped up as an **anti-Congress front** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Dufferin** used him to keep **Muslims out of Congress**.
**Iqbal** (**1930**) and **Rahmat Ali** (**1933**) came much later; **Ambedkar** wrote on Pakistan.
xa: **1906**: **Shimla Deputation** (Aga Khan) → separate electorates demanded; **League** founded.
**1930**: **Iqbal's Allahabad address** — consolidated Muslim state in the North-West.
**1940**: **Lahore Resolution** — demand formalised by **Jinnah**.

227.s: The 1930 Allahabad address of Muhammad Iqbal is associated with the proposal for:
o: Immediate withdrawal of the British from India
A federation of all princely states
A consolidated Muslim state in north-western India
227.x: In his 1930 Allahabad address, Iqbal advocated a consolidated Muslim state in the north-western region.
227.tq: Distinguish an intermediate proposal from the later formal demand for Pakistan.
xs: **Iqbal's 1930 Allahabad address** (League session) proposed a **consolidated Muslim state in the North-West** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was a milestone of the **Two-Nation theory**, not a call for British withdrawal or a princely federation.
xa: **1933**: **Chaudhry Rahmat Ali** coined **"PAKISTAN"** in **"Now or Never"**.
**1940**: **Lahore Resolution**, adopted **23 March 1940**.
**1928-29**: Nehru Report vs Jinnah's **14 Points** — "parting of the ways".

227.s:
Arrange the following figures in chronological order according to their contributions to the separate Muslim homeland idea:
A. Muhammad Iqbal
B. M.A. Jinnah
C. Sayyid Ahmad Khan
D. Chaudhry Rahmat Ali
227.x: The sequence is Sayyid Ahmad Khan in 1887, Iqbal in 1930, Rahmat Ali in 1933 and Jinnah in 1940.
227.tq: Fix the first and last milestones, then arrange the middle dates.
xs: The order is **C, A, D, B** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Sayyid Ahmad Khan** (**1887**) → **Iqbal** (**1930**, Allahabad) → **Rahmat Ali** (**1933**, "Pakistan") → **Jinnah** (**1940**, Lahore Resolution).
xa: **1906**: **Shimla Deputation** under the **Aga Khan**.
**1946**: **Direct Action Day**.
**Jinnah** first worked for **Hindu-Muslim unity**, later championed the **Two-Nation Theory**.

227.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
227.x: The RSS was founded in 1925 at Nagpur by K.B. Hedgewar. The other pairs incorrectly interchange the dates, places or persons associated with the two organisations.
227.tq: Use the founder-date association to eliminate swapped organisational details.
xs: **RSS** — **1925** — **K.B. Hedgewar** is correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
The RSS was founded at **Nagpur** in **1925**, not **1915**.
**Rahmat Ali** coined "Pakistan" (**1933**); he has nothing to do with the Hindu Mahasabha.
xa: Hindu communal bodies asserted India as **Hindu territory** → reinforced the **Two-Nation Theory**.
**M.S. Golwalkar's** writing attacked nationalists for **embracing Muslims**.
**1920s** communal tension: **Shuddhi/Tabligh**, **Sangathan/Tanzim**.

227.s: The assertion that India was Hindu territory was made by Hindu communal bodies and had the effect of reinforcing which idea?
227.x: The claim that India was Hindu territory reinforced the communal conception underlying the Two-Nation Theory.
227.tq: Link an ideological claim with its broader political consequence.
xs: Hindu bodies' claim that India was **Hindu territory** reinforced the **Two-Nation Theory** — so option **(2)** is correct.

xa: **RSS**: **1925**, **K.B. Hedgewar**, **Nagpur**.
**Golwalkar** attacked nationalists for **embracing Muslims** (**11 May 2026**).

227.s: M.S. Golwalkar's writings criticised nationalists for:
227.x: Golwalkar's writings attacked nationalists for embracing Muslims.
227.tq: Test the specific target of a political criticism.
xs: **M.S. Golwalkar's** writing attacked nationalists for **embracing Muslims** — so option **(2)** is correct.
This was part of Hindu communal bodies asserting India as **Hindu territory**, which reinforced the **Two-Nation Theory**.
xa: Recalled in an op-ed of **11 May 2026**.
**RSS** was founded in **1925** by **K.B. Hedgewar** at **Nagpur**.
The **Lahore Resolution** came from the **Muslim League** (**1940**).

227.s: The Shimla Deputation of 1906 is associated with which of the following developments?
o: Acceptance of complete independence by the Congress
Demand for separate electorates and the founding of the Muslim League
Replacement of reserved seats by joint electorates
227.x: The 1906 Shimla Deputation, led by Aga Khan, demanded separate electorates, and the Muslim League was founded in the same year.
227.tq: Connect a deputation with its immediate constitutional and organisational consequences.
xs: The **Shimla Deputation (1906)**, led by the **Aga Khan**, **demanded separate electorates**, and the **League was founded** the same year — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Lahore Resolution** came in **1940**; reserved seats in joint electorates came via the **Poona Pact**.
xa: The demand was met by the **Indian Councils Act 1909**.
The **Muslim League (1906)** came up in the run-up to 1909.
**1887**: **Sayyid Ahmad Khan** used as an anti-Congress front.

227.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Nehru Report and Jinnah's response during 1928–29?
o: The Nehru Report introduced separate electorates, while Jinnah withdrew from politics
The Nehru Report created the Muslim League, while Jinnah accepted joint electorates without conditions
The Nehru Report rejected separate electorates, while Jinnah put forward his Fourteen Points
The Nehru Report adopted the Two-Nation Theory, while Jinnah supported the Lahore Resolution
227.x: The Nehru Report rejected separate electorates, and Jinnah responded with his Fourteen Points, marking a parting of the ways.
227.tq: Compare two linked constitutional positions in the same period.
xs: The **Nehru Report** **rejected separate electorates**, and **Jinnah** answered with his **Fourteen Points** — so option **(3)** is correct.
This was the "**parting of the ways**" (**1928-29**).
The **Lahore Resolution** came only in **1940**, and the League dates from **1906**.
xa: **Jinnah's Point 5**: separate electorates continue; any community may opt for joint electorates.
**1930**: Iqbal's **Allahabad address**.
Jinnah first worked for **Hindu-Muslim unity**, later championed the Two-Nation Theory.

227.s: Jinnah's political career in relation to Hindu-Muslim unity is best described as follows:
o: He initially worked for Hindu-Muslim unity and later championed the Two-Nation Theory
He remained outside all communal and constitutional politics
He first championed the Two-Nation Theory and later supported the Congress
He consistently opposed Hindu-Muslim unity from the beginning

227.tq: Test a change over time rather than a single static association.
xs: **Jinnah** first worked for **Hindu-Muslim unity** and later **championed the Two-Nation Theory** — so option **(1)** is correct.
His **14 Points** (**1928-29**) marked the "**parting of the ways**".
xa: He formalised the demand at **Lahore** (**1940**), as session president.
He raised the slogan "**Divide and Quit**" (BPSC **2025** key).
**1946**: **Direct Action Day**.

227.s: Which of the following was a feature of the communal tensions of the 1920s?
o: Shuddhi and Tabligh, along with Sangathan and Tanzim
The Swadeshi and Home Rule movements only
The Cabinet Mission and the Mountbatten Plan

227.tq: Identify the correct cluster of contemporaneous communal movements.
xs: The **1920s** saw riots and **Shuddhi/Tabligh** and **Sangathan/Tanzim** movements — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Cabinet Mission**-era clash came with **Direct Action Day** (**1946**), not the 1920s.
xa: **RSS** was founded in **1925** at **Nagpur**.
**1928-29**: Nehru Report vs **14 Points**.
**1937-39**: League campaign against "**Hindu Raj**".

227.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

227.s: Who raised the slogan 'Divide and Quit'?
227.x: The slogan 'Divide and Quit' was raised by M.A. Jinnah.
227.tq: Use the slogan-and-leader association while avoiding a swapped leader trap.
xs: "**Divide and Quit**" was raised by **M.A. Jinnah** (BPSC **2025** key) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Fazlul Huq** moved the **Lahore Resolution**; **Iqbal** gave the **Allahabad address**; **Golwalkar** attacked nationalists for embracing Muslims.

227.s: The Muslim League's mass-contact campaigns alleged that the Congress ministries were establishing:
227.x: The League's campaigns alleged that Muslims were being subjected to 'Hindu Raj' under the Congress ministries.
227.tq: Identify the exact political slogan used in propaganda.
xs: The League's mass-contact campaigns alleged "**Hindu Raj**" under Congress ministries — so option **(3)** is correct.

**1946** slogan: "a vote for the League was a vote for **Islam**".

227.s: The slogan used by the Muslim League during the 1946 elections was:
o: A vote for Congress was a vote for freedom
A vote for the League was a vote for Islam
A vote for unity was a vote for the League
A vote for Pakistan was a vote for Britain
227.x: The League campaigned in the 1946 elections with the slogan, 'A vote for the League was a vote for Islam.'
227.tq: Test exact wording of an election slogan.
xs: The League's **1946** slogan was "**a vote for the League was a vote for Islam**" — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **1946** provincial elections ran on **communal lines** (op-ed, **11 May 2026**).

227.s:
Arrange the following reports in the order in which they appeared:
A. Sharif Report
B. Muslim Sufferings under Congress Rule
C. Pirpur Report
227.x: The Pirpur Report appeared first in 1938, followed by the Sharif Report and then Fazlul Huq's Muslim Sufferings under Congress Rule in 1939.
227.tq: Arrange reports by their stated order and years.
xs: The order is **C, A, B** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Pirpur Report** (**1938**) → **Sharif Report** (Bihar, **1939**) → **"Muslim Sufferings under Congress Rule"** (Fazlul Huq, **1939**).
xa: All alleged **cruelties to Muslims** in Congress-ruled provinces.
⚠ **Pirpur** = 1938; **Sharif** = Bihar 1939; **Fazlul Huq** = "Muslim Sufferings" 1939.
**Deliverance Day** followed on **22 Dec 1939**.

227.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Muslim Sufferings under Congress Rule — Fazlul Huq
Pirpur Report — Raja Syed Mohammad Mehdi of Pirpur
227.x: Fazlul Huq authored Muslim Sufferings under Congress Rule. The Pirpur Report was authored by Raja Syed Mohammad Mehdi of Pirpur.

xa: Fazlul Huq also **moved** the **Lahore Resolution** (**1940**).
All three reports alleged **cruelties to Muslims** in Congress-ruled provinces.

227.s: All the reports listed below were primarily intended to highlight alleged:
o: Cruelties to Muslims in Congress-ruled provinces
Failures of the British military administration
227.x: The reports alleged that Muslims suffered cruelties in provinces governed by Congress ministries.
227.tq: Identify the common purpose shared by several differently titled reports.
xs: All the reports alleged **cruelties to Muslims in Congress-ruled provinces** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Pirpur (1938)**, **Sharif (1939)** and Fazlul Huq's "**Muslim Sufferings**" (**1939**) share this theme.
xa: They backed mass-contact campaigns alleging "**Hindu Raj**".
**Deliverance Day** (**22 Dec 1939**) marked the ministries' resignation.

227.s: The Muslim League observed 'Deliverance Day' on 22 December 1939 to celebrate:
o: The adoption of the Lahore Resolution
The resignation of the Congress provincial ministries
The announcement of the Communal Award
The publication of the Pirpur Report
227.x: Deliverance Day ('Day of Deliverance and Thanksgiving'), 22 December 1939, celebrated the resignation of the Congress ministries. The Lahore Resolution came in March 1940, the Communal Award in 1932 and the Pirpur Report in 1938.
227.tq: Deliverance Day = 22 Dec 1939 = Congress ministries resign.
xs: **Deliverance Day** (**22 Dec 1939**) celebrated the **resignation of the Congress ministries** — so option **(2)** is correct.

The **Lahore Resolution** came in **March 1940**, the **Communal Award** in **1932**, the **Pirpur Report** in **1938**.
xa: It capped the **1937-39** campaign against "**Hindu Raj**".

"**Divide and Quit**" was Jinnah's later slogan.

227.s: The Lahore Resolution of March 1940 demanded the establishment of independent states for Muslims in which of the following areas?
o: Only the princely states of India
227.x: The Lahore Resolution demanded independent states in the Muslim-majority areas of the north-western and eastern zones of India.

227.s: The Lahore Session of the Muslim League formally set out which political theory?
227.x: The Lahore Session of 1940 formally set out the Two-Nation Theory, treating Hindus and Muslims as separate nations.
227.tq: Use the session-to-theory association.
xs: The League's **Lahore session** (**1940**) formally set out the **Two-Nation Theory** — so option **(2)** is correct.

xa: Adopted on **23 March 1940**; called the **"Pakistan Resolution"**.
The theory's roots: **1909** separate electorates, the **"seed of the Two-Nation Theory"**.
**Iqbal's 1930** Allahabad address had proposed a Muslim state in the North-West.

227.s:

227.tq: Lahore 1940: Jinnah presided, Sikandar drafted, Fazlul Huq moved.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: adopted on **23 March 1940**.
Statement 2 correct: it was soon called the **"Pakistan Resolution"**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Sikandar Hayat Khan drafted** it; **A.K. Fazlul Huq moved** it.
xa: **Jinnah** was the session president.
JPSC **2016** key named **Sikandar Hayat Khan** as drafter.
The **Two-Nation Theory** was formally set out at this session.

227.s: Who coined the word 'Pakistan' in 1933?
227.x: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali coined the word 'Pakistan' in 1933.
227.tq: Separate the person who coined the name from those who later popularised or formalised the demand.
xs: **Chaudhry Rahmat Ali** coined **"PAKISTAN"** in **1933** — so option **(2)** is correct (MPPSC **2023**, BPSC **2017**).

227.s: The statement that communal differences would continue to trouble India so long as England remained as a third power is associated with which conclusion?

227.s: What was the principal historical significance of the system of separate electorates in British India?
o: It introduced provincial autonomy and abolished the Muslim League
It created a single national electorate based on linguistic representation
It established universal adult franchise and ended communal politics

227.tq: Identify the cause-and-effect chain linking an institutional arrangement with its wider historical consequences.
xs: Separate electorates **institutionalised religion in representation** → seed of the **Two-Nation Theory** and **Partition** — so option **(4)** is correct.

228.s:

xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.

Father **Karamchand** was **Diwan of Porbandar**; mother **Putali Bai**.
In **1893** he went to South Africa for **Dada Abdullah's** case.

228.x: Potti Sriramulu worked at Sabarmati Satyagraha Ashram.
228.tq: Distinguish an Indian associate of an ashram from foreign intellectual influences.
xs: **Potti Sriramulu** worked at **Sabarmati** (APHQ **2017**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
One source says he worked there **3 years**.
**Hermann Kallenbach** is linked with **Tolstoy Farm**; **Ruskin** and **Thoreau** were authors who influenced Gandhi.
xa: **Sabarmati (Satyagraha) Ashram** dates from **1917**.
**Kochrab Ashram** (**1915**) preceded it in Ahmedabad.
**Sevagram, Wardha** came in **1936**.

228.s: Gandhi read Unto This Last during a train journey in 1904. What did he do soon afterwards?
228.x: After reading Unto This Last in 1904, Gandhi founded the Phoenix Settlement soon afterwards.
228.tq: Link a dated intellectual influence to the immediate institutional consequence.
xs: After reading **Unto This Last** on a train in **1904**, Gandhi soon founded the **Phoenix Settlement** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Phoenix (near **Durban**) stood for **community living** and **manual labour**.
**Harijan** began in **1933** and **Sevagram** in **1936** — much later.
xa: The book was by **John Ruskin** → **dignity of labour**, **Sarvodaya**.
**Tolstoy Farm** followed in **1910**.
**Indian Opinion** began in **1903** at Durban.

228.s: Mahatma Gandhi was awarded the Kaisar-i-Hind gold medal in 1915 for which of the following services?
o: His work during the Champaran movement
His service during the Khilafat Movement
His ambulance work in South Africa
228.x: The Kaisar-i-Hind gold medal was awarded to Gandhi in 1915 for his ambulance work in South Africa.
228.tq: Test the award with its specific service rather than the better-known later campaigns.
xs: The **Kaisar-i-Hind** gold medal (**1915**) was for his **ambulance work in South Africa** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was awarded by the **British Government**.
**Champaran** came in **1917**, and the **Khilafat** campaign is when he **returned** it.
xa: He **returned it in 1920** during the **Khilafat/Non-Cooperation** campaign.
**Boer War** (**1899**): **Indian Ambulance Corps**; **1906**: **Zulu Rebellion** stretcher-bearers.
He returned to India on **9 January 1915**.

228.s: In which year did Gandhi return the Kaisar-i-Hind medal?
228.x: Gandhi returned the Kaisar-i-Hind medal in 1920 during the Khilafat and Non-Cooperation campaign.
228.tq: Distinguish the year of receiving an honour from the year of returning it.
xs: Gandhi returned the **Kaisar-i-Hind** medal in **1920** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was during the **Khilafat/Non-Cooperation** campaign.
xa: It had been awarded in **1915** by the **British Government** for **ambulance work** in South Africa.
**Young India** (English weekly) was edited by Gandhi from **1919**.
**Champaran (1917)** was his first civil disobedience in India.

228.s: Which one of the following correctly associates the early Indian satyagrahas with their principal issues?
228.x: Champaran concerned indigo, Ahmedabad concerned mill wages, and Kheda concerned remission of land revenue.
228.tq: Start from the sure issue–movement pair and eliminate swapped associations.
xs: **Champaran — indigo**; **Ahmedabad — mill wages**; **Kheda — revenue remission** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Champaran 1917** = first **civil disobedience**; **Ahmedabad 1918** = first **hunger strike**; **Kheda 1918** = first **non-cooperation**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **C – A – K** = civil disobedience – hunger strike – non-cooperation.
First satyagraha overall = **Transvaal 1906**.
First in India = **Champaran 1917**.

228.s: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas is observed on 9 January because on that date in 1915:
o: Gandhi founded the Natal Indian Congress
Gandhi returned to India from South Africa, landing at Bombay
228.x: Gandhi returned from South Africa and landed at Bombay on 9 January 1915, the date now observed as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas. The Natal Indian Congress dates to 1894, Champaran to 1917, and Kochrab Ashram was set up later in 1915.
228.tq: 9 Jan 1915 return = Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.
xs: On **9 January 1915** Gandhi **returned to India**, landing at **Bombay** — so option **(2)** is correct.
That day is observed as **Pravasi Bharatiya Divas**.
**Natal Indian Congress** = **1894**; **Champaran** = **1917**; **Kochrab** = later in **1915**.
xa: **Gokhale** advised him to spend **one year observing India**.
He received the **Kaisar-i-Hind** in **1915**.
South Africa phase: **1893-1914** (about **21 years**).

228.s: On his return to India in 1915, Gandhi was advised to spend one year observing the country before starting any mass movement. Who gave this advice?
228.x: His political guru Gopal Krishna Gokhale advised him to spend a year observing India first. Tilak, Naoroji and Tagore are not credited with this advice; Tagore is linked with the title Mahatma.
228.tq: Political guru Gokhale: one year of observation.
xs: **Gopal Krishna Gokhale**, his **political guru**, advised **one year observing India** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Tagore** is linked with the title **"Mahatma"**, not this advice.
xa: Gandhi landed at **Bombay** on **9 January 1915**.
His first Indian satyagraha came at **Champaran (1917)**.
**Kochrab Ashram** (**1915**) was his first ashram in Ahmedabad.

228.s: The Indian Opinion, started in South Africa in 1903, was published from which place?
228.x: Indian Opinion was started in 1903 at Durban in South Africa.
228.tq: Use the publication’s founding place to distinguish it from other Gandhi-associated locations.
xs: **Indian Opinion** (**1903**) was published from **Durban** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It had **English and Gujarati** editions.
**Johannesburg** is linked with **Tolstoy Farm**; **Pietermaritzburg** with the **1893** train incident.
xa: **Phoenix Settlement** was also near **Durban** (**1904**).
**Young India** — English weekly from **1919**; **Harijan** — weekly from **1933**.
⚠ **Mathrubhumi** is not a Gandhi paper (APPSC **2019**).

228.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
228.x: Harijan was a weekly started in 1933; it was not a Gujarati monthly started in 1919. Young India was an English weekly, while Navajivan was a Gujarati journal.
228.tq: Find the option that reverses both the period and nature of the publication.
xs: The wrong pair is **Harijan — Gujarati monthly started in 1919** — so option **(4)** is the answer.
**Harijan** was a **weekly** started in **1933**.
The other pairs are correct: **Navajivan** — Gujarati; **Indian Opinion** — English and Gujarati; **Young India** — English weekly.
xa: **1919** is the year Gandhi began editing **Young India**.
His autobiography was serialised in **Navajivan**.
**Indian Opinion** started in **1903** at **Durban**.

228.s: The autobiography of Mahatma Gandhi was serialised in which journal?
228.x: Gandhi’s autobiography was serialised in Navajivan, a Gujarati journal.
228.tq: Discriminate among publications by linking the work with its journal venue.
xs: The autobiography was serialised in **Navajivan**, a **Gujarati** journal — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Young India** was an **English weekly**; **Harijan** a weekly from **1933**; **Indian Opinion** was South African (**1903**).
xa: Autobiography: **The Story of My Experiments with Truth**, written in **Gujarati** (APPSC **2019**).
**Anasakti Yoga**: Gujarati rendering of the **Gita**.
**Collected Works of Mahatma Gandhi**: **100 volumes** (English), by the **Publications Division**.

228.s: Which one of the following works was written in Gujarati?
o: The Story of My Experiments with Truth
228.x: The Story of My Experiments with Truth was written in Gujarati. Songs from Prison consisted of English translations, while Young India was an English weekly.
228.tq: Separate the original Gujarati works from English translations and periodicals.
xs: **The Story of My Experiments with Truth** was written in **Gujarati** — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC **2019**).
**Young India** was an **English weekly**; **Songs from Prison** are **English translations**; the **Collected Works** are in English.
xa: It was serialised in **Navajivan**.
**Hind Swaraj** (**1909**) was also written in **Gujarati**.
Hindi version of complete writings: **Sampoorna Gandhi Vangmaya**.

228.s:
Consider the following statements about Gandhi's writings:
1. Anasakti Yoga is a Gujarati rendering of the Bhagavad Gita with commentary.
2. Songs from Prison is a collection of original Gujarati poems written at Sabarmati Ashram.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
228.x: Statement 1 is correct: Anasakti Yoga is Gandhi's Gujarati rendering of the Gita with commentary. Statement 2 is wrong: Songs from Prison contains English translations of ancient Indian religious lyrics, made in Yerwada jail. So 1 only; 2 only, both and neither are wrong.
228.tq: Songs from Prison = English, Yerwada; Anasakti Yoga = Gujarati Gita.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Anasakti Yoga** is a **Gujarati** rendering of the **Bhagavad Gita** with commentary.
Statement 2 wrong: **Songs from Prison** are **English translations** of ancient Indian religious lyrics, made in **Yerwada** jail.
xa: The Gita gave Gandhi **Nishkama karma**.
Complete writings: **Collected Works**, **100 volumes**; e-version with **Gujarat Vidyapith** (**2026**).
Autobiography written in **Gujarati**, serialised in **Navajivan**.

228.s: Which one of the following is NOT a Gandhi paper or Gandhi-associated publication listed in this context?
228.x: Mathrubhumi is not a Gandhi paper. Indian Opinion, Navajivan and Harijan are associated with Gandhi’s journalistic work.
228.tq: Use the publication-association trap to identify the outsider.
xs: **Mathrubhumi** is not a Gandhi paper (APPSC **2019**) — so option **(4)** is the answer.
Gandhi papers: **Indian Opinion** (**1903**), **Young India** (**1919**), **Navajivan**, **Harijan** (**1933**).
xa: **Indian Opinion** had **English and Gujarati** editions.
**Navajivan** serialised his autobiography.
**Young India** was an **English weekly**.

228.s: The title ‘Father of the Nation’ was used for Gandhi by Subhas Chandra Bose in which setting and year?
o: A radio address from Singapore in 1944
228.x: Subhas Chandra Bose used the title ‘Father of the Nation’ for Gandhi in a radio address from Singapore in 1944.
228.tq: Combine the giver, medium, place and year to avoid a title-only guess.
xs: **Subhas Chandra Bose** called Gandhi "**Father of the Nation**" in a **radio address from Singapore** in **1944** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1931** belongs to **Churchill's** "**half-naked fakir**" remark.
xa: "**Mahatma**" was given by **Rabindranath Tagore**.
⚠ Trap: Mahatma = **Tagore**; Father of the Nation = **Bose**; half-naked fakir = **Churchill**.
**Kaisar-i-Hind**: awarded **1915**, returned **1920**.

228.s: Who described Gandhi as a ‘half-naked fakir’ in 1931?
228.x: Winston Churchill used the expression ‘half-naked fakir’ for Gandhi in 1931.
228.tq: Test the speaker associated with a distinctive but often misattributed expression.
xs: **Winston Churchill** called Gandhi a "**half-naked fakir**" in **1931** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Tagore** gave "**Mahatma**"; **Bose** "**Father of the Nation**" (**1944**); **Gokhale** was his political guru.
xa: APPSC **2019** key accepts "Mahatma" as given in **1914**.
Bose's address was a radio broadcast from **Singapore**.
The **Kaisar-i-Hind** was returned in **1920**.

228.s: Who among the following is credited with giving Gandhi the title 'Mahatma'?
228.x: The title Mahatma is credited to Rabindranath Tagore (APPSC 2019). Subhas Chandra Bose called him Father of the Nation (Singapore, 1944); Churchill called him a 'half-naked fakir' (1931); Gokhale was his political guru.
228.tq: Mahatma = Tagore; Father of the Nation = Bose; half-naked fakir = Churchill.
xs: The title "**Mahatma**" is credited to **Rabindranath Tagore** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Bose** called him **Father of the Nation** (**1944**); **Churchill** called him a **half-naked fakir** (**1931**); **Gokhale** was his political guru.
xa: APPSC **2019** key accepts "given in **1914**".
⚠ Trap: Mahatma = **Tagore**; Father of the Nation = **Bose**.
Gokhale advised **one year observing India** before any mass movement.

228.s:
Assertion (A): South Africa is regarded as the laboratory where satyagraha was invented.
Reason (R): Gandhi developed and experimented with the method of satyagraha there in 1906.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
228.x: Both the Assertion and the Reason are true. The development and experimentation of satyagraha in South Africa in 1906 explains why South Africa is described as its laboratory.
228.tq: Test whether the historical development stated in the Reason directly explains the description in the Assertion.
xs: **Both A and R are true** and **R is the correct explanation** of A — so option **(1)** is correct.
**South Africa** is the **laboratory** where satyagraha was invented, in **1906**.
The first satyagraha opposed the **Black Act** (**Asiatic Registration Ordinance**) in **Transvaal**.
xa: Two phases: **moderate petitioning (1894-1906)**, then **satyagraha (1906-14)**.
**1913 Great March** → **Indian Relief Act 1914**.
First in India = **Champaran 1917**.

228.s: The first satyagraha associated with Gandhi was launched in which place in 1906?
228.x: Gandhi's first satyagraha was launched in Transvaal in 1906. Champaran was his first satyagraha in India.
228.tq: Distinguish the first satyagraha overall from the first satyagraha conducted in India.
xs: The first satyagraha was in **Transvaal** in **1906** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It opposed the **Asiatic Registration Ordinance** ("**Black Act**").
**Champaran (1917)** was the first in **India**; **Ahmedabad** and **Kheda** came in **1918**.
xa: **1907-08**: burning of registration certificates; first jail term **1908**.
⚠ **C – A – K** = civil disobedience – hunger strike – non-cooperation.
Same year: stretcher-bearers in the **Zulu Rebellion**.

228.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes an Andhra Pradesh connection with Mahatma Gandhi's life and legacy?
o: Potti Sriramulu was associated with Sabarmati, and Mukunda Ramarao wrote *Agamya Gamyaalu* on Andhra indentured migrants to South Africa.
Potti Sriramulu led the Transvaal satyagraha, and Mukunda Ramarao translated *Hind Swaraj* into Telugu.
Potti Sriramulu founded the Gandhi Memorial at Pietermaritzburg, and Mukunda Ramarao served as Assembly Speaker.
Potti Sriramulu wrote *Hind Swaraj*, and Mukunda Ramarao established Sabarmati Ashram.
228.x: Potti Sriramulu is associated with Sabarmati, while Mukunda Ramarao's Telugu book *Agamya Gamyaalu* traces Andhra indentured migrants to South Africa.
228.tq: Match each Andhra personality with the precise contribution or association instead of accepting swapped roles.
xs: **Potti Sriramulu** worked at **Sabarmati**, and **Mukunda Ramarao** wrote **Agamya Gamyaalu** on Andhra indentured migrants — so option **(1)** is correct.
Sriramulu's Sabarmati link is from APHQ **2017**; the book is in **Telugu** (**27 Feb 2026**).
**Hind Swaraj** was by **Gandhi**; the AP Assembly Speaker was **Ch. Ayyanna Patrudu**.
xa: **Ayyanna Patrudu** visited **Pietermaritzburg station** and the Gandhi Memorial in **KwaZulu-Natal** (**14 Sep 2026**).
About **1.5 million** Indians went on **five-year** indentures; many from **Andhra** villages.
**Sabarmati Ashram** dates from **1917**.

229.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes Gandhi's formulations ‘God is Truth’ and ‘Truth is God’?
o: ‘Truth is God’ was the earlier formulation and ‘God is Truth’ the later one.
‘God is Truth’ was the earlier formulation, while ‘Truth is God’ was the later formulation.
Gandhi rejected both formulations as incompatible.
Both expressions referred only to political freedom.
229.x: Gandhi initially used the formulation ‘God is Truth’ and later expressed the idea as ‘Truth is God’, giving truth an independent and central status.
229.tq: Discriminate between two closely related formulations by their sequence.
xs: "**God is Truth**" was the **earlier** formulation and "**Truth is God**" the **later** one — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ Trap: "God is Truth" came **first** → "Truth is God" **later**.
Gandhi did not reject them: "**Truth is my God**", he said, with religion meaning **morality, not sect**.
xa: **Truth** is the **end**; **non-violence** the **means**.
"Politics bereft of religion is a **death-trap**" — politics must be **spiritualised**.
"What is **morally wrong** can never be **politically right**" (UPPSC **2015**).

229.s: In Gandhian thought, the relationship between truth and non-violence is that
o: truth is the end and non-violence is the means
non-violence is needed only when truth cannot be established
truth is the means and non-violence is the end
229.x: Gandhi regarded truth as the ultimate end and non-violence as the means for realising it.
229.tq: Avoid reversing the means-and-end relationship.
xs: In Gandhian thought **truth is the end** and **non-violence is the means** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Gandhi: "**Means are after all everything**. As the means so the end" — means-ends purity.
xa: "My religion is based on **truth and non-violence**. Truth is my God."
"**Wrong means never take us to right ends**" (UPPSC **2015**).
Satyagraha = **satya (truth) + agraha (insistence)**.

229.s:
Which of the following correctly describes Gandhian ahimsa?
1. It applies to thought, word and deed.
2. It is a sign of weakness and inability to resist.
3. It is associated with the morally upright and strong.
4. Gandhi preferred violence to cowardice when the only alternatives were cowardice and violence.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
229.x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is false because Gandhi regarded non-violence as the quality of the strong, not a sign of weakness.
229.tq: Reject the familiar but incorrect association of non-violence with weakness.
xs: Statements **1, 3 and 4** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: ahimsa is in **thought, word and deed**.
Statement 2 wrong, statement 3 correct: ahimsa is **not a sign of weakness** but of the **strong and morally upright**.
Statement 4 correct: if the only choice is **cowardice vs violence**, he would advise **violence**.
xa: He contrasted non-violence of the **brave** with that of the **weak**.
"Non-violence is not a **garment** to be put on and off at will."
"**Poverty is the worst form of violence**" (UPPSC **2015**: persistence of poverty).

229.s: The term ‘Satyagraha’ is formed from
229.x: Satyagraha combines satya, meaning truth, and agraha, meaning insistence or eagerness.
229.tq: Test the derivation of a key technical term.
xs: **Satyagraha** = **satya (truth)** + **agraha (insistence/eagerness)** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Its English rendering was "**passive resistance**"; it means **soul force** in place of physical force.
xa: Satyagraha was born in **1906** in **Transvaal**.
⚠ Trap: satyagraha = **insistence on truth**, not "weak passive resistance".
**Swaraj** = **self-rule, self-control**, not just political freedom.

229.s:
Consider the following statements about Satyagraha:
1. Its early English rendering was 'passive resistance'.
2. It relies on physical force in place of soul force.
3. It was born in 1906 in the Transvaal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
229.x: Statement 1 is correct: it was rendered in English as passive resistance. Statement 2 is wrong: it is the reverse, soul force in place of physical force. Statement 3 is correct: it was born in 1906 in the Transvaal. So 1 and 3 only.
229.tq: Soul force replaces physical force; Transvaal 1906.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: its English rendering was "**passive resistance**".
Statement 2 wrong: it is **soul force in place of physical force** — the reverse.
Statement 3 correct: born in **1906** in **Transvaal**.
xa: Satyagraha = **satya + agraha** (insistence on truth).
Rules for satyagrahis: no **anger or hatred**, no retaliation, never **insult** the opponent.
⚠ It is not "weak" passive resistance — ahimsa belongs to the **strong**.

229.s: The Rowlatt Satyagraha of 1919 is significant in this classification because it represented the first
o: movement based exclusively on legislative action
229.x: The Rowlatt Satyagraha is identified as the first all-India mass movement in this classification.
229.tq: Identify the significance attached to a named movement.
xs: The **Rowlatt Satyagraha (1919)** was the **first all-India mass movement**, through **hartal** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Gandhi's first **hunger strike** was **Ahmedabad 1918**; local peasant struggles were **Champaran** and **Kheda**.
xa: Some notes call the **NCM (1920)** the "first nationwide mass movement".
⚠ Keep "first mass movement by Gandhi" = **Champaran** apart from "first all-India" = **Rowlatt/NCM**.
**Champaran 1917** = first **civil disobedience**; **Kheda 1918** = first **non-cooperation**.

229.s: In the Gandhian strategy, the final step is
229.x: Strike is regarded as the last step in the Gandhian strategy after other forms of resistance have been exhausted.
229.tq: Test sequence by identifying the terminal stage.
xs: The **last step** in the Gandhian method is the **strike** (UPPSC **2013** key) — so option **(4)** is correct.
Forms before it: **civil disobedience**, **hunger strike / fast**, **non-cooperation**, **hartal**, **boycott and picketing**.
xa: **Hartal**: **Rowlatt Satyagraha 1919**.
**Boycott, picketing**: **NCM** and **Swadeshi**.
**Civil disobedience**: **Champaran 1917**, **Salt March 1930**.

229.s: Which one of the following is inconsistent with the rules prescribed for a Satyagrahi?
o: Insulting the opponent to expose injustice
229.x: A Satyagrahi must never insult the opponent. The rules require non-retaliation, submission to arrest and observance of jail discipline.
229.tq: Find the option that directly violates a stated rule of conduct.
xs: **Insulting the opponent** breaks the satyagrahi's rules — so option **(3)** is the answer.
A satyagrahi must **never insult** the opponent and must have no **anger or hatred**.
He must bear assaults **without retaliation**, **submit to arrest** and follow **jail rules** — options 1, 2, 4 are rules.
xa: Ahimsa must be in **thought, word and deed**.
Satyagraha = **soul force** in place of physical force.
Gandhi's **Talisman**: recall the face of the **poorest and weakest**.

229.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the struggle with its distinctive description?
o: Rowlatt Satyagraha — first civil disobedience by Gandhi in India
229.x: Kheda (1918) is classed as Gandhi's first non-cooperation. The other pairs are wrong: Champaran (1917) was the first civil disobedience, not non-cooperation; Ahmedabad (1918) was the first hunger strike, not an all-India strike; the Rowlatt Satyagraha (1919, hartal) was the first all-India mass movement, not the first civil disobedience.
229.tq: Compare the closely related ‘firsts’ instead of recalling them in isolation.
xs: **Kheda (1918)** was the **first non-cooperation** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Champaran (1917)** was the first **civil disobedience**, not non-cooperation.
**Ahmedabad (1918)** was the first **hunger strike**; **Rowlatt (1919)** the first **all-India mass movement** via **hartal**.
xa: **NCM 1920-22** is the other non-cooperation example.
**Salt March 1930** is the other civil disobedience example.
Last step: **strike** (UPPSC **2013**).

229.s:
Consider the following statements about Gandhi's view of politics:
1. By 'religion' Gandhi meant morality based on truth and non-violence, not a sect.
2. He held that politics bereft of religion is a death-trap.
3. He favoured concentrating power in the national executive.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
229.x: Statement 1 is correct: for Gandhi religion meant morality ('Truth is my God'), not sect. Statement 2 is correct: politics must be spiritualised, as politics bereft of religion is a death-trap. Statement 3 is wrong: he favoured decentralisation, with power close to the people and local communities deciding. So 1 and 2 only.
229.tq: Gandhi: spiritualised politics + decentralised power.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: religion meant **morality, not sect** ("**Truth is my God**").
Statement 2 correct: "Politics bereft of religion is a **death-trap**" — politics must be **spiritualised**.
Statement 3 wrong: he favoured **decentralisation** — power close to the people, local communities decide.
xa: "What is **morally wrong** can never be **politically right**".
Real Swaraj = **capacity of all to resist authority when abused**.
He saw the **State** as **violence in concentrated form**.

229.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the core values of Gandhian political thought?
229.x: Truth, non-violence, compassion, simplicity, Sarvodaya and purity of means and ends are Gandhian values. Economic determinism is associated with Marxism.
229.tq: Find the concept belonging to the contrasting ideology.
xs: **Economic determinism** is not a Gandhian value — it is the basis of **Marxism** — so option **(3)** is the answer.
Gandhian core values: **truth**, **non-violence**, **compassion**, **simplicity**, **Sarvodaya**, **means-ends purity**.
xa: Gandhism's basis is **moral/spiritual**.
Marxist method: **class struggle**, **revolution**; Gandhian: **non-violence**, **change of heart**.
Property: Gandhian **trusteeship** vs Marxist **abolition of private property**.

229.s: According to Gandhi, real Swaraj would be achieved when people acquired the capacity to
o: obey every order issued by the State
resist authority whenever it is abused
replace all local institutions with a central authority
transfer political power exclusively to educated elites
229.x: Gandhi defined real Swaraj partly as the capacity of all people to resist authority when it is abused.
229.tq: Test the exact holder and exercise of political capacity.
xs: Real Swaraj comes from the **capacity of all to resist authority when abused** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Swaraj is not blind obedience nor centralised rule — it means **self-rule, self-control**.
xa: Swaraj includes the masses' capacity to **govern themselves without coercion**.
Swaraj principles incl. **swadeshi**, **ahimsa**, **satyagraha**, **decentralisation**, **education for all**.
Gandhi as **philosophical anarchist**: ideal of "**enlightened anarchy**".

229.s: Gandhi's concept of Swaraj is wider than political independence because it includes
o: self-rule, self-control and the capacity of the masses to govern themselves without coercion
freedom only from foreign economic competition
centralised rule by a single national authority
rule by a hereditary political class
229.x: For Gandhi, Swaraj meant not merely political freedom but also self-rule, self-control and the ability of people to govern themselves without coercion.
229.tq: Distinguish the broad conceptual meaning from the narrow constitutional meaning.
xs: Swaraj meant **self-rule, self-control** and the capacity of masses to **govern themselves without coercion** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was not only political freedom, and it opposed centralisation in favour of **decentralisation**.
xa: Swaraj has **eight interrelated principles**, incl. **swadeshi** and **education for all**.
Real Swaraj = capacity to **resist authority when abused**.
Gandhian individualism: **self-rule before State rule**.

229.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the interrelated principles included in Gandhi's concept of Swaraj?
229.x: Swadeshi, ahimsa, Satyagraha, decentralisation and education for all are included among the interrelated principles of Swaraj. Class dictatorship is not a Gandhian principle.
229.tq: Identify the ideological outsider in a list of principles.
xs: **Class dictatorship** is not a Swaraj principle — so option **(1)** is the answer.
Swaraj's **eight interrelated principles** include **swadeshi**, **ahimsa**, **satyagraha**, **decentralisation**, **education for all**.
xa: **Decentralisation**: power close to the people; local communities decide.
Gandhi's method is **change of heart**, not **class struggle**.
The unit of Gandhian individualism is the **individual and his conscience**.

229.s: Who regarded poverty as the worst form of violence?
229.x: Gandhi described the persistence of poverty as the cruellest or worst form of violence.
229.tq: Use the exact attribution of a distinctive quotation.
xs: **Gandhi** called **poverty the worst form of violence** — so option **(2)** is correct.
UPPSC **2015** key: the cruellest violence = **persistence of poverty**.
xa: Gandhi's **Talisman**: recall the face of the **poorest and weakest** and ask if your step helps him.
"**Wrong means never take us to right ends**" (UPPSC **2015**).
**Sarvodaya** is a Gandhian core value.

229.s: Which one of the following statements best expresses Gandhi's view on the relationship between means and ends?
o: Means are relevant only in peaceful times.
Political ends justify all available means.
The nature of the means determines the nature of the end.
Pure ends can be achieved through impure means.
229.x: Gandhi held that means are everything and that the end reflects the means used to attain it.
229.tq: Match the precise formulation of a principle rather than a familiar slogan.
xs: For Gandhi the **means determine the end**: "**As the means so the end**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
"**Wrong means never take us to right ends**" (UPPSC **2015**) — so ends never justify all means.
xa: **Means-ends purity** is a Gandhian core value.
"What is **morally wrong** can never be **politically right**".
Truth is the **end**, non-violence the **means**.

229.s:
With reference to Gandhian political ethics, consider the following statements:
1. What is morally wrong can never be politically right.
2. Non-violence may be adopted or abandoned according to political convenience.
3. Gandhi's Talisman requires consideration of the poorest and weakest person before taking a step.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
229.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because Gandhi said non-violence is not a garment to be put on and off at will.
229.tq: Find the statement that reverses an absolute ethical principle.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: "What is **morally wrong** can never be **politically right**" (UPPSC **2015**).
Statement 2 wrong: "Non-violence is **not a garment** to be put on and off at will".
Statement 3 correct: the **Talisman** asks you to recall the **poorest and weakest** person.
xa: "**Means are after all everything**."
Ahimsa is in **thought, word and deed**.
**Poverty** = the worst form of violence.

229.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Gandhism and Marxism:
1. Both envisage a stateless society as the final goal.
2. Gandhism relies on non-violence and change of heart.
3. Marxism accepts trusteeship as the basis of property relations.
4. Gandhism explains social change through economic determinism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
229.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Trusteeship is Gandhian, whereas Marxism seeks abolition of private property; economic determinism is Marxist rather than Gandhian.
229.tq: Split the options by separating shared goals from contrasting methods and bases.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: both aim at a **stateless society** — the common ground (UPSC **2020**).
Statement 2 correct: Gandhism relies on **non-violence** and **change of heart**.
Statements 3 and 4 wrong: **trusteeship** is Gandhian (Marxism = **abolition of private property**); **economic determinism** is Marxist.
xa: Marxist method: **class struggle**, **revolution**.
Gandhism's basis: **moral/spiritual**.
They share only the **stateless end**; they differ on **means**.

229.s: Gandhi's doctrine of trusteeship means that
o: the State alone should own every productive resource
private property must be abolished immediately through revolution
the wealthy should hold property as trustees for the welfare of society
wealth must be forcibly confiscated from all rich persons
229.x: Under trusteeship, the rich are not necessarily expropriated but are expected to use their wealth as trustees for social welfare.
229.tq: Distinguish a Gandhian reformist concept from revolutionary property doctrines.
xs: Under **trusteeship** the **wealthy hold property as trustees** for society; the **rich are not expropriated** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Immediate abolition** of private property through revolution is the **Marxist** position.
xa: Marxist basis: **economic determinism**; Gandhian: **moral/spiritual**.
Both share the goal of a **stateless society** (UPSC **2020**).
Preamble socialism = **Marxism + Gandhism**, leaning to **Gandhian socialism**.

229.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gandhi is called a philosophical anarchist because of his ideal of 'enlightened anarchy' and his view of the State as violence in concentrated form.
2. In Gandhian individualism, the class and its economic position form the basic unit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
229.x: Statement 1 is correct: enlightened anarchy and the State as concentrated violence make him a philosophical anarchist. Statement 2 is wrong: the unit in Gandhian individualism is the individual and his conscience (self-rule before State rule); class as the unit is Marxist. So 1 only.
229.tq: Individual and conscience = Gandhi's unit; class = Marx's.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: "**enlightened anarchy**" and the State as **violence in concentrated form** make him a **philosophical anarchist**.
Statement 2 wrong: the unit is the **individual and his conscience** — **self-rule before State rule**.
xa: Final goal: a **stateless society**, shared with Marxism.
**Decentralisation**: power close to the people.
Gandhian method: **non-violence**, **change of heart**.

229.s: The socialism mentioned in the Indian Preamble is generally understood as a blend of
o: anarchism and capitalism, with a capitalist inclination
individualism and fascism, with an individualist inclination
Marxism and Gandhism, with a Gandhian inclination
colonial liberalism and absolutism, with an absolutist inclination
229.x: The Indian conception of socialism is described as combining Marxist and Gandhian elements while leaning towards Gandhian socialism.
229.tq: Identify the correct combination in a comparative ideological question.
xs: Preamble socialism is a blend of **Marxism and Gandhism**, leaning to **Gandhian socialism** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It accepts **trusteeship**-style change rather than **abolition of private property**.
xa: Gandhism vs Marxism: same **stateless** end, different **means**.
Gandhian property idea: **trusteeship** — rich not expropriated.
Gandhi = **philosophical anarchist** ("enlightened anarchy").

229.s: Which of the following best explains the historical significance of Gandhian non-violence in the Indian national movement?
o: It replaced moral persuasion with military force.
It replaced physical force with moral force and helped make the movement a mass movement.
It made political mobilisation dependent on the colonial administration.
It restricted participation to educated urban groups.
229.x: Gandhian non-violence substituted moral force for physical force and enabled broad mass participation in the national movement.
229.tq: Connect a principle with its wider political consequence.
xs: Gandhian non-violence **replaced physical force with moral force** and made the national movement a **mass movement** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Satyagraha = **soul force** in place of **physical force**.
xa: The **Rowlatt Satyagraha (1919)** was the first **all-India mass movement**.
Methods: **civil disobedience**, **non-cooperation**, **hartal**, **boycott, picketing**.
It inspired the **Baltic Way** and **Singing Revolution** abroad.

229.s: The Baltic Way and the Singing Revolution are associated with Gandhian non-violence because they
o: created a permanent military alliance in Europe
ended colonial rule in South Asia
established a Marxist state in the Baltic region
led to the re-independence of the Baltic states in 1991
229.x: Gandhian non-violence inspired the Baltic Way and the Singing Revolution, which contributed to Baltic re-independence in 1991.
229.tq: Link a non-Indian application of an idea with its result and year.
