Which one of the following represents the correct chronological order of the events listed below?
A. Moplah uprising
B. Prince of Wales boycott
C. Chauri Chaura incident
D. Formation of the Swaraj Party
234.x: The Moplah uprising occurred in August 1921, the Prince of Wales boycott on 17 November 1921, Chauri Chaura in February 1922 and the Swaraj Party was formed in 1923.
234.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two 1921 events by month.
xs: **Moplah (Aug 1921)** → **Prince of Wales boycott (17 Nov 1921)** → **Chauri Chaura (4 Feb 1922)** → **Swaraj Party (1923)**.
xa: The **Bardoli resolution** came on **11-12 Feb 1922**; Gandhi's arrest in **Mar 1922**.
The Swaraj Party was announced **31 Dec 1922**, formed **1 January 1923**.

234.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. At Chauri Chaura on 4 February 1922, a crowd burnt the police station, killing 22 policemen.
2. Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
234.x: Statement 1 is correct: on 4 February 1922 (some sources say 5 Feb) at Chauri Chaura, Gorakhpur district, the crowd burnt the police station and 22 policemen were killed. Statement 2 is wrong: the NCM was withdrawn in February 1922 after Chauri Chaura (Bardoli resolution); Jallianwala Bagh (1919) came before the movement began. So 1 only.
234.tq: Withdrawal followed Chauri Chaura (Feb 1922), not Jallianwala.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: at **Chauri Chaura**, **4 February 1922**, the crowd burnt the police station, killing **22 policemen**.
Statement 2 wrong: withdrawal followed **Chauri Chaura**, not **Jallianwala** (**1919**), which preceded the NCM.
xa: Withdrawal: **Bardoli resolution (11-12 Feb 1922)**.
The NCM **made nationalism a mass movement** — a commonly paired true statement.

234.s: Gandhi’s first arrest by the British Government for sedition occurred when he was detained at:
234.x: In April 1919 Gandhi was stopped and detained at Palwal while proceeding towards Punjab; the incident contributed to riots.
234.tq: Separate the place of the first detention from the place of the later sedition trial.
xs: Gandhi was detained at **Palwal** — option **(2)**.
In **April 1919** he was stopped on his way to **Punjab**, which sparked riots.
xa: His later arrest was on **10 March 1922** at **Sabarmati, Ahmedabad**.
Trial: **18 March 1922**, Ahmedabad, before Judge **C.N. Broomfield**.

234.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Gandhi’s Great Trial:
1. It was held at Ahmedabad in March 1922.
2. The charge was sedition under Section 124A.
3. The charge arose from articles published in Young India.
4. Gandhi was sentenced to six years’ imprisonment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
234.x: All four statements are correct. Gandhi’s 1922 Ahmedabad trial concerned sedition under Section 124A in relation to his Young India articles and resulted in a six-year sentence.
234.tq: Verify the venue, year, legal provision, publication and sentence together.
xs: All four — option **(4)**.
Trial at **Ahmedabad**, **18 March 1922**; charge **Sedition (Sec. 124A IPC)**.
Based on three **Young India** articles; sentence **6 years**.
xa: Articles included "**Tampering with Loyalty**" and "**Shaking the Manes**".
Released in **1924** on health grounds.
Judge: **C.N. Broomfield**.

234.s: Gandhi was arrested on 10 March 1922 at which place?
234.x: Gandhi was arrested on 10 March 1922 at Sabarmati in Ahmedabad.
234.tq: Test the exact place of arrest rather than the later place of trial.
xs: Arrested at **Sabarmati, Ahmedabad** — option **(1)**.
He was arrested on **10 March 1922**, after the NCM withdrawal.
xa: ⚠ Arrest **10 March** (Sabarmati) → trial **18 March 1922** (Ahmedabad).
Sentence **6 years**; released **1924**.

234.s:
Consider the following statements about Gandhi's 1922 trial:
1. It was presided over by Judge C.N. Broomfield.
2. It came to be known as the Great Trial.
3. Gandhi pleaded guilty and asked for the highest penalty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
234.x: The trial before Judge C.N. Broomfield on 18 March 1922 was called the Great Trial; Gandhi pleaded guilty and requested the highest penalty.
234.tq: Combine the judge, conventional name and conduct of the accused in one factual set.
xs: All three — option **(4)**.
The "**Great Trial**" was before Judge **C.N. Broomfield**; Gandhi **pleaded guilty** and asked for the **highest penalty**.
xa: Gandhi said "**affection cannot be manufactured or regulated by law**".
Charge: **Sedition (Sec. 124A IPC)**; sentence **6 years**.

234.s: The statement that “affection cannot be manufactured or regulated by law” was made by Gandhi during his
234.x: Gandhi made this statement while pleading guilty during the Great Trial in 1922.
234.tq: Associate a memorable quotation with the correct historical setting.
xs: It was said at the **1922 sedition trial** — option **(4)**.
At the **Great Trial**, Ahmedabad, **18 March 1922**, Gandhi pleaded guilty.
xa: Charge: **Sec. 124A IPC**, for **Young India** articles.
Judge: **C.N. Broomfield**.

234.s: Which of the following periodicals was NOT edited by Gandhi?
234.x: The Bengalee was not Gandhi's paper; it was Surendranath Banerjea's. Gandhi's papers were Young India, Navajivan, Indian Opinion and Harijan.
234.tq: Identify the odd publication among a list of known Gandhi-edited periodicals.
xs: **The Bengalee** was not Gandhi's — option **(4)**.
Gandhi's papers: **Young India**, **Navajivan**, **Indian Opinion**, **Harijan**.
xa: His **1922** sedition charge arose from three **Young India** articles.
Articles included "**Tampering with Loyalty**" and "**Shaking the Manes**".

234.s: The Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party was announced on 31 December 1922 and formally formed on:
234.x: The party was announced on 31 December 1922 and formally formed on 1 January 1923.
234.tq: Distinguish the announcement date from the formal formation date.
xs: Formed on **1 January 1923** — option **(1)**.
It was announced on **31 Dec 1922**, after the **Gaya** session (Dec **1922**) rejected council entry.
xa: Founders: **C.R. Das (president)** and **Motilal Nehru (secretary)**.
⚠ Trap: **Jawaharlal Nehru** was not a founder (APPSC **2023**).

234.s: What was the principal difference between the pro-changers and the no-changers after the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement?
o: The pro-changers supported council entry, while the no-changers favoured constructive work and continuation of the boycott.
The pro-changers supported communal electorates, while the no-changers opposed provincial autonomy.
The pro-changers favoured complete independence, while the no-changers supported the British war effort.
The pro-changers favoured armed revolution, while the no-changers favoured princely rule.
234.x: The pro-changers, or Swarajists, sought to enter legislative councils to “end or mend” them. The no-changers preferred constructive work and continuation of the boycott.
234.tq: Compare the two groups by their stated strategy rather than by their personalities.
xs: **Pro-changers** wanted **council entry**; **No-changers** wanted **constructive work** and the boycott — option **(1)**.
Pro-changers aimed to "**end or mend**" the councils.
xa: Pro-changers: **C.R. Das, Motilal Nehru, Ajmal Khan, Vithalbhai Patel**.
No-changers: **C. Rajagopalachari, Vallabhbhai Patel, Rajendra Prasad, M.A. Ansari**.
Swarajists called the councils "**sham parliaments**".

234.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Andhra branch of the Swaraj Party?
o: Pithapuram Raja was president and C.R. Das was secretary.
V. Ramadas was president and Motilal Nehru was secretary.
Unava Lakshmi Narayana was president and Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was secretary.
Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was president and Unava Lakshmi Narayana was secretary.
234.x: The Andhra branch had Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao as president and Unava Lakshmi Narayana as secretary.
234.tq: Keep the regional office-bearers distinct from the central Swaraj Party founders.
xs: President **Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao**, secretary **Unava Lakshmi Narayana** — option **(4)**.
Option (3) reverses the two posts.
xa: The **Pithapuram Raja** formed the **People's Party** to back the Swarajists.
**V. Ramadas** won a **Central Legislative Assembly** seat from Madras in **1923**.

234.s: The People's Party was formed by the Pithapuram Raja to:
o: Conduct the no-tax campaign in Pedanandipadu
Oppose the Andhra branch of the Swaraj Party
Organise the Akali Movement in Andhra
234.x: The Pithapuram Raja formed the People's Party to support the Swarajists in the 1923 political context.
234.tq: Identify the purpose of the regional organisation from its political alignment.
xs: The **People's Party** was formed to **back the Swarajists** — option **(1)**.
Pedanandipadu's no-tax was led by **Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary**, not the Raja.
xa: Andhra Swaraj branch: president **Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao**.
Swarajists made large gains in the **1923 elections**.

234.s: Who among the following was NOT a founder of the Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party?
234.x: Jawaharlal Nehru was not a founder of the Swaraj Party. C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru were its principal founders, while Vithalbhai Patel was among its other members.
234.tq: Use the wrong-person trap by separating a prominent Congress leader from the actual founders.
xs: **Jawaharlal Nehru** was not a founder — option **(3)**.
Founders: **C.R. Das (president)** and **Motilal Nehru (secretary)**.
**Vithalbhai Patel** was a pro-changer (Swarajist).
xa: ⚠ "C.R. Das and Jawaharlal Nehru formed the Swaraj Party" is WRONG (APPSC **2023**).
It formed after the **suspension of the NCM** (APPSC **2018**).

234.s: The expression “End or Mend” was associated with the Swarajists’ strategy of
o: forming a separate party outside the Congress permanently
entering councils and obstructing colonial governance from within
234.x: The Swarajists entered the councils to expose them as sham parliaments and obstruct their functioning from within, a strategy expressed as “End or Mend.”
234.tq: Apply the slogan to the practical political strategy rather than treating it as a general objective.
xs: "**End or Mend**" meant **entering councils and obstructing from within** — option **(3)**.
Swarajists aimed to expose the councils as **"sham parliaments"**.
Permanent boycott of councils was the No-changers' stance.
xa: The **Delhi special session (Sept 1923)** allowed Swarajists to contest.
Swarajists made **large gains** in **1923**.

234.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Delhi special session permitted Swarajists to contest elections
B. Formation of the Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party
C. Gaya Congress session
D. Announcement of the Swaraj Party
234.x: The Gaya session occurred in December 1922, the party was announced on 31 December 1922, it was formally founded on 1 January 1923, and the Delhi special session followed in September 1923.
234.tq: Fix the closely spaced December–January events first, then place the September session.
xs: **Gaya (Dec 1922)** → announced **31 Dec 1922** → formed **1 January 1923** → **Delhi special (Sept 1923)**.
xa: Gaya, presided by **C.R. Das**, rejected council entry.
The party's full name: **Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party**.

234.s: The Delhi special session of the Indian National Congress held in September 1923 permitted the Swarajists to
o: withdraw from the Central Legislative Assembly
234.x: The Delhi special session in September 1923 allowed the Swarajists to contest elections. They made substantial gains in the elections held later in 1923.
234.tq: Link the special session with its specific organisational and electoral decision.
xs: It allowed Swarajists to **contest** elections — option **(4)**.
In the **1923 elections** they made **large gains**.
xa: **V. Ramadas** won a **Central Legislative Assembly** seat from Madras.
Strategy: "**End or Mend**".

234.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

List-I (Event)                         List-II (Date)
a. Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala Bagh    i. 1919
b. Treaty of Sevres                     ii. May 1920
c. Prince of Wales boycott              iii. 17 November 1921
d. Bardoli resolution                   iv. 11–12 February 1922

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
234.x: The Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala Bagh belong to 1919; the Treaty of Sevres was signed in May 1920; the Prince of Wales boycott occurred on 17 November 1921; and the Bardoli resolution was adopted on 11–12 February 1922.
234.tq: Start with the sure date pair and eliminate codes containing a shifted event.
xs: **a–i, b–ii, c–iii, d–iv** — option **(1)**.
**Rowlatt/Jallianwala — 1919**; **Sevres — May 1920**; **Prince of Wales — 17 Nov 1921**; **Bardoli — 11-12 Feb 1922**.
xa: NCM launched **1 Aug 1920**; **Chauri Chaura** on **4 Feb 1922**.
**Moplah rebellion**: **Aug 1921**.

234.s: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched on 1 August 1920, the same day on which which of the following leaders died?
234.x: Bal Gangadhar Tilak died on 1 August 1920, the day the Non-Cooperation Movement was launched.
234.tq: 1 Aug 1920: Tilak's end, NCM's start.
xs: **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** died on **1 August 1920** — option **(3)**.
Gandhi launched the NCM that day and returned his **Kaiser-i-Hind** medal.
xa: The Khilafat Committee began non-cooperation on **31 August 1920**.
The fund named after him: **Tilak Swaraj Fund**, **₹1 crore**.

234.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Congress sessions of 1920:
1. The special session at Calcutta was held in September 1920.
2. The Nagpur session was held in December 1920.
3. The Nagpur session was held before the Calcutta special session.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
234.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Calcutta special session was in September 1920 and the Nagpur session in December 1920. Statement 3 is wrong because Calcutta came first.
234.tq: C before N: Calcutta (Sept), then Nagpur (Dec).
xs: Statements **1 and 2** — option **(1)**.
**Calcutta special** — **Sept 1920**; **Nagpur** — **Dec 1920**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Calcutta came first**.
xa: Calcutta president **Lala Lajpat Rai**; Nagpur president **C. Vijayaraghavachariar**.
Calcutta passed Gandhi's resolution **1886 to 884**; Nagpur ratified it unanimously.

234.s: The Moplah rebellion in Malabar broke out in:
234.x: The Moplah rebellion in Malabar broke out in August 1921, during the Non-Cooperation Movement.
234.tq: Malabar rose in Aug 1921, a year after NCM began.
xs: The Moplah rebellion broke out in **August 1921** — option **(4)**.
**November 1921** was the Prince of Wales boycott; **February 1922** was Chauri Chaura.
xa: It was **Muslim tenants vs Hindu landlords** in **Malabar, Kerala**, and turned communal.
The **Akali movement (1920-25)** was another parallel struggle.

234.s: Chauri Chaura, where a police station was burnt on 4 February 1922, is located in which district of Uttar Pradesh?
234.x: Chauri Chaura is in Gorakhpur district, UP, where a police station was burnt on 4 February 1922, leading to the withdrawal of the NCM.
234.tq: Chauri Chaura, Gorakhpur: two Gs and a fire.
xs: Chauri Chaura is in **Gorakhpur** district — option **(1)**.
On **4 Feb 1922** the crowd burnt the police station.
xa: **22 policemen** were killed.
**Madan Mohan Malaviya** defended the accused.

234.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
1. Formation of the Swaraj Party
2. Prince of Wales boycott
3. Gandhi's arrest
4. Bardoli resolution
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
234.x: The order is the Prince of Wales boycott (17 November 1921), the Bardoli resolution (11–12 February 1922), Gandhi's arrest (March 1922) and the Swaraj Party (1923).
234.tq: Boycott, Bardoli, arrest, Swaraj: 1921, Feb 22, Mar 22, 1923.
xs: **Prince of Wales (17 Nov 1921)** → **Bardoli (11-12 Feb 1922)** → **Gandhi's arrest (Mar 1922)** → **Swaraj Party (1923)**.
xa: Exact arrest: **10 March 1922** at **Sabarmati**.
Swaraj Party formed **1 January 1923**.

234.s: The Khilafat–Non-Cooperation phase is described as the high point of:
o: Relations between the Congress and princely states
Industrial labour cooperation with the colonial government
234.x: The Khilafat–Non-Cooperation phase represented the high point of Hindu-Muslim unity during the national movement.
234.tq: Identify the specific political relationship highlighted by the movement’s significance.
xs: **Hindu-Muslim unity** — option **(3)**.
Gandhi **merged the Khilafat cause with Swaraj**.
xa: After withdrawal, unity broke and communal riots followed (**1921-27**).
Ali Brothers toured India with Gandhi.

234.s: Which of the following criticisms of the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement is correctly stated?
o: It was universally welcomed by all Congress leaders as a planned conclusion.
It was criticised only by the Muslim League after the Khilafat Movement ended.
It was opposed exclusively by the British administration.
It was criticised as sudden by Subhas Chandra Bose, M.N. Roy and C.R. Das.
234.x: The sudden withdrawal after Chauri Chaura was criticised by Subhas Chandra Bose, M.N. Roy and C.R. Das.
234.tq: Distinguish the named critics from the misleading claims of universal approval or exclusive opposition.
xs: It was criticised as abrupt by **Bose, M.N. Roy and C.R. Das** — option **(4)**.
Bose: "**sprinkling cold water**"; Roy: **weak leadership**.
xa: Marxist view: halted to avoid a **radical anti-landlord turn**.
**Swaraj in one year** remained unfulfilled.

234.s: The Marxist interpretation of Gandhi’s withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement held that it was intended to prevent:
o: A radical anti-landlord turn of the movement
The expansion of council entry by Swarajists
The formation of the Akali Dal
234.x: The Marxist interpretation argued that Gandhi halted the movement to prevent it from taking a radical anti-landlord direction.
234.tq: Link an ideological interpretation with the political-economic development it claims Gandhi sought to prevent.
xs: To prevent a **radical anti-landlord turn** — option **(1)**.
That is the **Marxist view** of the post-Chauri Chaura withdrawal.
xa: Others criticising: **Bose, M.N. Roy and C.R. Das**.
Withdrawal: **Bardoli resolution (11-12 Feb 1922)**.

234.s: Which one of the following is a current-relevance association connected with C. Rajagopalachari?
o: A statue was unveiled at Vijayawada during the Tilak Fund campaign.
A bust was unveiled at Rashtrapati Bhavan during Rajaji Utsav.
A memorial was inaugurated at Nankana Sahib under the Sikh Gurdwaras Act.
A portrait was installed at Gaya during the council-entry debate.
234.x: During Rajaji Utsav at Rashtrapati Bhavan, the President unveiled a bust of C. Rajagopalachari.
234.tq: Match the contemporary event, venue and personality without importing unrelated historical associations.
xs: A **bust** of **C. Rajagopalachari** was unveiled at **Rashtrapati Bhavan** during **'Rajaji Utsav'** — option **(2)**.
This was in **Feb 2026**.
xa: Rajaji (Madras) gave up legal practice in the NCM.
He was later a **No-Changer**.

234.s: Which of the following sets contains only Andhra-related references associated with the Non-Cooperation period?
o: Vijayawada, Pingali Venkayya, Chirala-Perala, Pedanandipadu and Palnadu
Bombay, Nankana Sahib, Bardoli, Dandi and Lahore
Calcutta, Amritsar, Chauri Chaura, Malabar and Delhi
Malabar, Nankana Sahib, Gaya, Champaran and Kheda
234.x: Vijayawada, Pingali Venkayya, Chirala-Perala, Pedanandipadu and Palnadu are the Andhra-related references highlighted for this period.
234.tq: Group the regional places and personality together and eliminate sets containing non-Andhra episodes.
xs: **Vijayawada, Pingali Venkayya, Chirala-Perala, Pedanandipadu and Palnadu** — option **(1)**.
Other sets mix non-Andhra places like **Bombay**, **Nankana Sahib**, **Malabar** and **Chauri Chaura**.
xa: Vijayawada AICC: **31 March-1 April 1921**.
Palnadu: **pullari** tax refusal; Chirala-Perala: **Ramadandu**; Pedanandipadu: **Shanti Sena**.

235.s: The AICC meeting held at Vijayawada in 1921 is particularly associated with which decision?
o: Acceptance of Gandhi's leadership of the national struggle
Formation of the Swaraj Party at Gaya
Approval of council entry as the sole Congress programme
235.x: At the 1921 AICC meeting at Vijayawada, political leaders accepted Gandhi's leadership of the national struggle.
235.tq: Distinguish a conference decision from later developments such as suspension and council entry.
xs: At the **1921 Vijayawada AICC**, leaders **accepted Gandhi's leadership** of the national struggle — option **(1)**.
The NCM was suspended only at **Bardoli (11-12 Feb 1922)**, and council entry was set aside at **Gaya (Dec 1922)**.
xa: Targets (by **30 June 1921**): **1 crore members**, **Rs 1 crore** for the **Tilak Swaraj Fund**, **20 lakh charkhas**.
**Pingali Venkayya**'s flag design (with the charkha) was endorsed by Gandhi there.
⚠ APCC meeting **January 1921** ≠ AICC session **1921** (APPSC **2023** key).

235.s:
Consider the following statements about the AICC meeting at Vijayawada (1921):
1. One of its targets was one crore Congress members.
2. One of its targets was twenty lakh charkhas.
3. The flag design of Pingali Venkayya endorsed by Gandhi there did not include the charkha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
235.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the targets (by 30 June 1921) were 1 crore members, Rs 1 crore for the Tilak Swaraj Fund and 20 lakh charkhas. Statement 3 is wrong: Pingali Venkayya's design endorsed by Gandhi had the charkha. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
235.tq: Bezawada 1921: 1 crore members, Rs 1 crore, 20 lakh charkhas; charkha flag.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** — option **(2)**.
Statements 1 and 2 correct: targets were **1 crore members** and **20 lakh charkhas** (plus **Rs 1 crore** for the Tilak Swaraj Fund).
Statement 3 wrong: **Pingali Venkayya**'s design endorsed by Gandhi had the **charkha**.
xa: Deadline for targets: **30 June 1921**.
Leaders there **accepted Gandhi's leadership**.
PM paid tribute to Pingali Venkayya on his **150th birth anniversary** (**3 Aug 2026**).

235.s: After the Nagpur session, the APCC meeting at Vijayawada in January 1921 set up Congress committees at which levels?
235.x: The January 1921 APCC meeting at Vijayawada established Congress committees at the district, taluk and village levels.
235.tq: Remember the administrative sequence from the larger unit to the village unit.
xs: The APCC set up committees at **district, taluk and village level** — option **(2)**.
This was in **January 1921**, after the **Nagpur session**.
xa: ⚠ This APCC meeting differs from the **1921 AICC** session at Vijayawada with the **1 crore - 1 crore - 20 lakh** targets.
Andhra carried out the Nagpur/Calcutta boycott of **courts, colleges and councils**.

235.s:
Consider the following statements about Gandhi's tours of Andhra in 1921:
1. His April 1921 coastal tour included Kakinada and Eluru.
2. His October 1921 tour included Kurnool, Kadapa and Tirupati.
3. The Non-Cooperation Movement in Andhra was at its peak during the April tour rather than the October tour.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
235.x: Statement 1 is correct: the April coastal tour covered Kakinada, Rajahmundry, Eluru, Machilipatnam, Chirala and Nellore. Statement 2 is correct: in October he toured Kurnool, Kadapa, Tirupati and Tadipatri. Statement 3 is wrong: the NCM was at its peak in Andhra during the October tour. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
235.tq: April = coast; October = Rayalaseema, peak of NCM.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** — option **(2)**.
1 correct: the **April 1921** coastal tour covered **Kakinada**, Rajahmundry, **Eluru**, Machilipatnam, Chirala, Nellore.
2 correct: the **October 1921** tour covered **Kurnool, Kadapa, Tirupati, Tadipatri**.
3 wrong: NCM was at its **peak** in Andhra during the **October** tour.
xa: At **Kakinada**, **Durgabai** translated Gandhi's speech and gave **Rs 5,000**.
Women leaders who emerged: **Duvvuri Subbamma, Ponaka Kanakamma, Unnava Lakshmibayamma**.

235.s: Which group of women leaders emerged prominently in Andhra during Gandhi's Non-Cooperation tour?
o: Duvvuri Subbamma, Ponaka Kanakamma and Unnava Lakshmibayamma
Durgabai, Annie Besant and Sarojini Naidu
Ponaka Kanakamma, Konda Venkatappayya and Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya
Unnava Lakshmibayamma, Garimella Satyanarayana and Durgabai
235.x: Duvvuri Subbamma, Ponaka Kanakamma and Unnava Lakshmibayamma emerged as women leaders during this phase of the movement.
235.tq: Identify the complete group of women leaders without mixing them with male organisers or other national leaders.
xs: **Duvvuri Subbamma, Ponaka Kanakamma and Unnava Lakshmibayamma** — option **(1)**.
**Konda Venkatappayya** and **Duggirala** were male Congress leaders, not part of this group.
xa: **Durgabai** translated Gandhi's Kakinada speech (**April 1921**) and gave **Rs 5,000**.
Unnava Lakshmi Narayana wrote **Nayakuralu** in jail.

235.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with the legacy of the Non-Cooperation Movement in Andhra?
235.x: The National College was established at Eluru, not Tadipatri. Pallepadu Ashram was in Nellore and Seethanagaram Ashram was near Rajahmundry.
235.tq: Check each institution against its town and identify the displaced location.
xs: **National College — Tadipatri** is wrong — option **(1)**.
The national school was **Eluru National College**; **Tadipatri** was on Gandhi's **October 1921** tour.
**Seethanagaram Ashram** (near Rajahmundry) and **Pallepadu Ashram** (Nellore) are correctly matched.
xa: Seethanagaram is now **Kasturba Ashram**.
**Ponduru Khadi** was famous; Chirala had Duggirala's **Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi**.

235.s: Which statement regarding the Seethanagaram Ashram is correct?
o: It was at Chirala and was known as Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi.
It was at Nellore and was known as Pallepadu Ashram.
It was at Eluru and became the National College.
It was near Rajahmundry and is now known as Kasturba Ashram.
235.x: The Seethanagaram Ashram was located near Rajahmundry and is now known as Kasturba Ashram.
235.tq: Distinguish similarly themed institutions by their location and later name.
xs: **Seethanagaram Ashram** was **near Rajahmundry**, now **Kasturba Ashram** — option **(4)**.
**Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi** was at Chirala; **Pallepadu** was in Nellore; Eluru had the **National College**.
xa: **Ponduru Khadi** was famous.
At **Vijayawada**, the **Prince of Wales hartal** was total.

235.s: Which place became particularly famous for Khadi during this period?
235.x: Ponduru became famous for its Khadi during the nationalist movement.
235.tq: Identify the specific place associated with the constructive programme rather than a satyagraha site.
xs: **Ponduru** was famous for Khadi — option **(4)**.
**Palnadu** and **Macherla** were linked to the Pullari satyagraha; **Pedanandipadu** to no-tax.
xa: Ponduru is in **Srikakulam**; its khadi was famed nationally.
Khadi and spinning were part of the No-Changers' **constructive programme**.

235.s:
The Andhra programme of boycott during the Non-Cooperation Movement included which of the following?
1. Courts
2. Colleges
3. Councils
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
235.x: Andhra followed the Nagpur and Calcutta programme by boycotting courts, colleges and councils.
235.tq: Recognise the complete set of institutions targeted by the boycott programme.
xs: All three — option **(4)**.
Andhra carried out the Nagpur/Calcutta boycott of **courts, colleges and councils**.
xa: **Tanguturi Prakasam** gave up his lucrative legal practice.
National institutions: **Eluru National College** and Duggirala's **Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi** at Chirala.

235.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with a national educational institution in Andhra?
o: Eluru — National College; Chirala — Duggirala's Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi
Eluru — Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi; Chirala — National College
Nellore — National College; Vijayawada — Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi
Kakinada — National College; Rajahmundry — Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi
235.x: The Eluru National College and Duggirala's Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi at Chirala were among the national educational institutions established during the movement.
235.tq: Start with the institution–town pair and reject the reversed combinations.
xs: **Eluru — National College; Chirala — Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi** — option **(1)**.
Option (2) swaps the two; neither Nellore nor Kakinada had these institutions in the notes.
xa: **Pallepadu Ashram** was in **Nellore**; **Seethanagaram Ashram** near **Rajahmundry**.
The Goshthi was founded by **Duggirala**, titled **Andhra Ratna**.

235.s: Which Andhra lawyer gave up his lucrative legal practice during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
235.x: Tanguturi Prakasam gave up his lucrative legal practice as part of the boycott of courts.
235.tq: Associate the boycott of legal practice with the lawyer who renounced it.
xs: **Tanguturi Prakasam** gave up his **lucrative legal practice** — option **(3)**.
**Konda Venkatappayya** is noted for trying to dilute the Palnadu struggle, not for giving up practice here.
xa: Prakasam's title: **Andhra Kesari**.
Andhra boycotted **courts, colleges and councils**.

235.s: During Gandhi's April 1921 tour of coastal Andhra, who translated his speech at Kakinada and donated Rs 5,000?
235.x: At Kakinada (April 1921) Durgabai translated Gandhi's speech and gave Rs 5,000. Duvvuri Subbamma, Ponaka Kanakamma and Unnava Lakshmibayamma were women leaders who emerged in the same phase, but the Kakinada translation is linked to Durgabai.
235.tq: Kakinada 1921 = Durgabai translates Gandhi
xs: **Durgabai** translated Gandhi's **Kakinada** speech and gave **Rs 5,000** — option **(1)**.
**Duvvuri Subbamma**, **Ponaka Kanakamma** and **Unnava Lakshmibayamma** emerged as women leaders on the tour, but not for the Kakinada translation.
xa: The **April 1921** coastal tour also covered Rajahmundry, Eluru, Machilipatnam, Chirala, Nellore.
In **October 1921** Gandhi toured **Kurnool, Kadapa, Tirupati, Tadipatri**.

235.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the causes of the Palnadu forest satyagraha:
1. The Forest Act of 1878 resulted in the reservation of forests.
2. Bribe-taking by forest staff added to the grievances of the people.
3. Failed rains in 1921 worsened the shortage of fodder.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
235.x: All three statements are correct. Forest reservation, corrupt forest officials and the fodder shortage caused by failed 1921 rains intensified the grievance against the Pullari system.
235.tq: Check whether all three cause-and-effect statements belong to the same local grievance.
xs: All three — option **(4)**.
**Forest Act (1878)** reserved forests; **bribe-taking forest staff**; failed **1921 rains** → fodder shortage.
xa: Pullari tax: **12 annas per cow, Rs 1.50 per buffalo, goats banned**.
Place & year: **Palnadu, Guntur district**, **1921-22** (APPSC **2012** key).

235.s:
The refusal to pay Pullari in Palnadu was accompanied by which of the following actions?
1. Social boycott of officials at Macherla
2. Driving 300 cattle into the forest without paying the tax
3. Impounding of the cattle at Minchalapadu
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
235.x: The satyagrahis boycotted officials at Macherla, drove 300 cattle into the forest without paying Pullari and had the cattle impounded at Minchalapadu.
235.tq: Link the protest method, the numerical action and the place of official retaliation.
xs: All three — option **(4)**.
**Social boycott** at **Macherla** (even Collector and SP); **300 cattle** driven in untaxed; impounded at **Minchalapadu**.
xa: ⚠ **Macherla** = social boycott; **Minchalapadu** = cattle impounded, Hanumanthu shot.
**28 men and 8 women** arrested; normalcy by **March 1922**.

235.s: Kanneganti Hanumanthu was killed in police firing during which incident?
o: The boycott of the Prince of Wales at Vijayawada
235.x: Kanneganti Hanumanthu was shot dead during the cattle-rescue action at Minchalapadu on 26 February 1922.
235.tq: Identify the leader by associating him with the specific event rather than the wider movement.
xs: Hanumanthu was shot in the **cattle-rescue at Minchalapadu** — option **(4)**.
**Macherla** was the social boycott site, not the firing.
xa: He was born in **Guntur district** (APPSC **2022** key).
The Palnadu satyagraha was the **first forest satyagraha** in Andhra (APPSC **2023** key).

235.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the roles of the persons associated with the Palnadu forest satyagraha?
o: Madabhushi Vedantam Narasimhachari imposed the Pullari tax, while Konda Venkatappayya supported tax refusal.
Unnava Lakshmi Narayana and Madabhushi Vedantam Narasimhachari studied and supported it, while Konda Venkatappayya attempted to dilute it.
Konda Venkatappayya led the cattle-rescue action, while Unnava Lakshmi Narayana opposed the movement.
Unnava Lakshmi Narayana and Konda Venkatappayya jointly ordered police firing at Minchalapadu.
235.x: Unnava Lakshmi Narayana and Madabhushi Vedantam Narasimhachari studied and backed the movement. Konda Venkatappayya tried to moderate it because the Congress had favoured social boycott rather than refusal to pay tax.
235.tq: Use the swapped-person trap carefully: distinguish supporters from the person who sought moderation.
xs: **Unnava** and **Madabhushi Vedantam Narasimhachari** studied and backed it; **Konda Venkatappayya** tried to dilute it — option **(2)**.
Venkatappayya's reason: Congress had asked only for **social boycott**, not tax refusal.
xa: Unnava was jailed and wrote **Nayakuralu**.
Hero: **Kanneganti Hanumanthu**, shot at **Minchalapadu**.

235.s: Who wrote the play *Nayakuralu* while in jail in connection with the Palnadu agitation?
235.x: Unnava Lakshmi Narayana wrote the play *Nayakuralu* while he was in jail.
235.tq: Associate the literary work with the activist who produced it during imprisonment.
xs: **Unnava Lakshmi Narayana** wrote **Nayakuralu** in jail — option **(1)**.
He studied and backed the Palnadu struggle with **Madabhushi Vedantam Narasimhachari**.
xa: Unnava was also **secretary** of the Andhra Swaraj branch.
**Konda Venkatappayya** tried to dilute the struggle.

235.s:
Consider the following statements about the Palnadu Pullari (forest) satyagraha:
1. It took place in Palnadu, Guntur district, in 1921-22.
2. It was the first forest satyagraha in Andhra.
3. Its hero, Kanneganti Hanumanthu, was born in Nellore district.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
235.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Pullari satyagraha took place in Palnadu, Guntur district, in 1921-22 and was the first forest satyagraha in Andhra. Statement 3 is wrong: Kanneganti Hanumanthu was born in Guntur district. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
235.tq: Palnadu = Guntur; Hanumanthu = Guntur-born; first forest satyagraha
xs: Statements **1 and 2** — option **(2)**.
1 correct: **Palnadu, Guntur district**, **1921-22**.
2 correct: the **first forest satyagraha** in Andhra.
3 wrong: **Kanneganti Hanumanthu** was born in **Guntur district**, not Nellore.
xa: Some notes date the Pullari rebellion from **Sept 1921**.
Hanumanthu was shot on **26 Feb 1922**.

235.s: On 5 November 1921, the Delhi AICC permitted provinces to launch which form of action?
235.x: The Delhi AICC of 5 November 1921 permitted provinces to launch civil disobedience, including no-tax campaigns.
235.tq: Associate the date with the specific expansion of the movement's programme.
xs: **Civil disobedience, including no-tax** — option **(2)**.
The **Delhi AICC** of **5 Nov 1921** allowed provinces to launch it.
xa: **17 Nov 1921**: Prince of Wales boycott; black flags in Andhra.
NCM suspended at **Bardoli**, **11-12 Feb 1922**.

235.s: The boycott of the Prince of Wales on 17 November 1921 was marked in Andhra by which form of protest?
235.x: The Prince of Wales boycott on 17 November 1921 was marked by black flags in Andhra.
235.tq: Use the symbolic colour as the clue to the nature of the protest.
xs: **Black flags** — option **(4)**.
At **Vijayawada** the **Prince of Wales hartal** was total.
xa: It followed the **Delhi AICC (5 Nov 1921)** allowing civil disobedience.

235.s:
Which of the following statements correctly represents the reactions to the suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement?
1. Subhas Chandra Bose called it a national tragedy and compared it to sprinkling cold water.
2. M.N. Roy criticised it as an instance of weak leadership.
3. Jawaharlal Nehru expressed amazement and consternation.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
235.x: All three are correct: Subhas Bose called the suspension a national tragedy, like "sprinkling cold water"; M.N. Roy blamed weak leadership; and Jawaharlal Nehru reacted with "amazement and consternation". So 1, 2 and 3.
235.tq: Match each political personality with the distinctive phrase associated with his reaction.
xs: All three — option **(4)**.
**Bose**: national tragedy ("**sprinkling cold water**"); **M.N. Roy**: **weak leadership**; **Nehru**: "**amazement and consternation**".
xa: Reason for suspension: violence at **Chauri Chaura**.
In Andhra, withdrawal dismayed satyagrahis at **Pedanandipadu** and **Palnadu**.

235.s: At the Gaya Session of the Congress in December 1922, the resolution relating to council entry was:
235.x: C.R. Das’s resolution supporting council entry was defeated at Gaya in December 1922, leading to the subsequent formation of the Swaraj Party.
235.tq: Connect the decisive session outcome with the later organisational split.
xs: C.R. Das's council-entry resolution was **defeated** (set aside) at **Gaya (Dec 1922)** — option **(2)**.
This led to the council-entry fight between Swarajists and No-Changers.
xa: NCM had been suspended at **Bardoli** (**11-12 Feb 1922**) after **Chauri Chaura**.
Bose called the suspension a national tragedy; **M.N. Roy** blamed **weak leadership**.

235.s: Who became the first woman President of the Indian National Congress, in 1917?
235.x: Annie Besant presided over the Congress in 1917 and was its first woman President. Sarojini Naidu (1925) was the first Indian woman President; Nellie Sengupta presided later (1933); Kasturba Gandhi never presided.
235.tq: First woman INC President = Besant 1917; first Indian woman = Sarojini 1925
xs: **Annie Besant** — **first woman INC President**, **1917** — option **(2)**.
In **1917** the **Home Rule flag** (**5** red, **4** green stripes) was hoisted at **Coimbatore**.
xa: That flag item was in the news (TH **19 Mar 2026**).
In **1920** the NCM was launched (Calcutta), followed by the **Nagpur session, Dec 1920**.

235.s: The Non-Cooperation Movement was suspended at Bardoli in February 1922 because of violence at:
235.x: Gandhi suspended the NCM at Bardoli (11-12 February 1922) after a mob burnt a police station at Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur district, UP. Minchalapadu and Macherla were sites of the Palnadu forest satyagraha, and Pedanandipadu was an Andhra no-tax centre; none of them caused the suspension.
235.tq: Chauri Chaura (Gorakhpur) -> Bardoli suspension
xs: Suspended because of violence at **Chauri Chaura** — option **(2)**.
**Chauri Chaura** (Gorakhpur, UP), **5 Feb 1922**: police station burnt, **21 policemen** killed (APP).
**Minchalapadu** and **Macherla** were Palnadu sites; **Pedanandipadu** an Andhra no-tax centre.
xa: Suspended at **Bardoli**, **11-12 Feb 1922**.
Nehru reacted with "**amazement and consternation**".

235.s: On which occasion did the Prime Minister pay tribute to Pingali Venkayya?
o: On 3 August 2026, on his 150th birth anniversary
On 3 August 2025, on his 149th birth anniversary
On 26 January 2026, on his 150th birth anniversary
On 15 August 2026, on his 150th birth anniversary
235.x: The Prime Minister paid tribute to Pingali Venkayya on 3 August 2026, marking his 150th birth anniversary.
235.tq: Use the exact date and anniversary figure to eliminate nearby numerical distractors.
xs: **3 Aug 2026**, his **150th birth anniversary** — option **(1)**.
He was born at **Bhatlapenumarru**.
xa: He took part in the **Vandemataram**, **Home Rule** and **Andhra movements**.
His flag design (with the charkha) was endorsed by Gandhi at **Vijayawada, 1921**.

235.s: Pingali Venkayya was born at which place?
235.x: Pingali Venkayya was born at Bhatlapenumarru.
235.tq: Test the birthplace directly and distinguish it from other Andhra locations associated with the movement.
xs: **Bhatlapenumarru** — option **(4)**.
The PM recalled this on his **150th birth anniversary** (**3 Aug 2026**).
xa: His flag design had the **charkha**.
Gandhi endorsed it at the **1921 Vijayawada session**.

235.s: The period from 1921 to 1931 is referred to in the Andhra context as the:
235.x: The period 1921–31 is described as the “glorious decade” in the Andhra context.
235.tq: Match the exact descriptive phrase with its associated time period.
xs: **Glorious decade** (**1921-31**) — option **(1)**.
It refers to leaders like **Konda Venkatappaiah**, **Duggirala**, **Prakasam**, **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** and **Pattabhi**.
xa: Titles: **Desabhakta**, **Andhra Ratna**, **Andhra Kesari**, **Desoddharaka**.
It began with the **1921** Vijayawada AICC.

235.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Leader)
 a. Konda Venkatappaiah
 b. Duggirala
 c. Prakasam
 d. Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao

List-II (Title)
 i. Andhra Kesari
 ii. Desoddharaka
 iii. Desabhakta
 iv. Andhra Ratna

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
235.x: Konda Venkatappaiah was known as Desabhakta, Duggirala as Andhra Ratna, Prakasam as Andhra Kesari, and Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao as Desoddharaka.
235.tq: Start from the sure leader–title pair and verify the remaining pairs before choosing the code.
xs: **a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** — option **(1)**.
**Konda Venkatappaiah** — **Desabhakta**; **Duggirala** — **Andhra Ratna**.
**Prakasam** — **Andhra Kesari**; **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** — **Desoddharaka**.
xa: These were "**Glorious decade**" (**1921-31**) leaders.
Duggirala founded the **Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi** at Chirala.

235.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement and its impact in Andhra:
1. The withdrawal after the Chauri Chaura incident dismayed Andhra satyagrahis.
2. The dismay occurred while the struggle was still in progress.
3. Pedanandipadu and Palnadu were associated with this Andhra context.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
235.x: The withdrawal after Chauri Chaura dismayed Andhra satyagrahis in the middle of the struggle, particularly in the context of Pedanandipadu and Palnadu. Hence, all three statements are correct.
235.tq: Separate the cause, timing and regional context before selecting the complete statement combination.
xs: All three — option **(4)**.
Withdrawal after **Chauri Chaura** dismayed Andhra satyagrahis **mid-struggle**, at **Pedanandipadu** and **Palnadu**.
xa: Hanumanthu was shot at **Minchalapadu** on **26 Feb 1922**, after Bardoli.
Palnadu reached normalcy by **March 1922**.

236.s: The Nationalist Party formed in the Central Legislative Assembly in 1924 consisted principally of
o: Swarajists, Jinnah’s Independents and Malaviya’s group
Congress socialists, revolutionaries and trade unions
Swarajists, British officials and Simon Commission members
236.x: The Nationalist Party brought together the Swarajists, Jinnah’s Independents and Malaviya’s group. It had about 70 members.
236.tq: Use the composition of the legislative bloc to distinguish it from other Congress groupings.
xs: **Swarajists**, **Jinnah's Independents** and **Malaviya's group** — option **(1)**.
It was the **Nationalist Party (1924)**, about **70** members.
xa: It **outvoted the government** and blocked the **Finance Bill**.
**Malaviya** later joined the **Responsivists**.

236.s:
Consider the following statements about the Nationalist Party in the Central Legislative Assembly:
1. It had about 70 members.
2. It outvoted the government on occasions.
3. It blocked the Finance Bill.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
236.x: All three statements are correct. The Nationalist Party used its numerical strength to outvote the government and block the Finance Bill.
236.tq: Combine membership, voting strength and legislative action in one statement set.
xs: All three — option **(4)**.
About **70** members; **outvoted the government**; blocked the **Finance Bill**.
xa: Formed in **1924** with **Jinnah's Independents** and **Malaviya's group**.
The **Muddiman Committee (1924)** followed a Swarajist demand.

236.s: Who became the first elected Indian President of the Legislative Assembly in 1925?
236.x: Vithalbhai Patel became the first elected Indian President of the Legislative Assembly in 1925.
236.tq: Distinguish the first office-holder from the first elected Indian holder of the office.
xs: **Vithalbhai Patel** — option **(3)**.
Elected (first Indian) **Speaker/President** of the Central Legislative Assembly in **1925**.
xa: He was a pro-changer (Swarajist).
The Swarajists did poorly in **1926**.

236.s:
Consider the following statements about the Swarajists in the Central Legislative Assembly:
1. Their demand for a review of the 1919 Act led to the Muddiman Committee (1924).
2. They supported the Public Safety Bill of 1928.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
236.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Swarajist demand for reviewing the Government of India Act 1919 led to the Muddiman Committee in 1924. Statement 2 is wrong: the Swarajists opposed the Public Safety Bill of 1928. So 1 only (A).
236.tq: Muddiman 1924 = review of 1919 Act; Public Safety Bill 1928 opposed
xs: Only statement **1** — option **(1)**.
1 correct: the demand for review of the **1919 Act** led to the **Muddiman Committee (1924)**.
2 wrong: the Swarajists **opposed** the **Public Safety Bill (1928)**.
xa: They walked out of the councils in **1930** after **Lahore**.
The **Nationalist Party** blocked the **Finance Bill**.

236.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Andhra Swarajist office)
a. President
b. Secretary
c. Treasurer
d. Additional associated leader

List-II (Person)
i. Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao
 ii. V. Ramadas
 iii. Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao
 iv. Unnava Lakshminarayana

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
236.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was President, Unnava Lakshminarayana Secretary, Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao Treasurer and V. Ramadas an additional associated leader.
236.tq: Start with the office-holder pairs and use the remaining person as the elimination pair.
xs: **a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** — option **(1)**.
President **Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao**; secretary **Unnava Lakshminarayana**; treasurer **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao**; **V. Ramadas** also in the branch.
xa: ⚠ **Kaleswara Rao** (president) - **Unnava** (secretary) - **Gadicherla** (treasurer).
Madras council: **B. Venkataratnam, P. Anjaneyulu, P.V. Venkatapathiraju**.

236.s:
Which of the following persons were elected to the Madras council in 1923 from the Andhra Swarajist group?
1. B. Venkataratnam
2. P. Anjaneyulu
3. P.V. Venkatapathiraju
4. V. Ramadas
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
236.x: B. Venkataratnam, P. Anjaneyulu and P.V. Venkatapathiraju were elected to the Madras council. V. Ramadas was elected to the Central Legislative Assembly.
236.tq: Separate the three Madras council members from the one central Assembly member.
xs: **B. Venkataratnam**, **P. Anjaneyulu** and **P.V. Venkatapathiraju** are listed for the **Madras council**.
**V. Ramadas** is listed separately under the Andhra branch, not the Madras council.
xa: Andhra branch: **Kaleswara Rao** (president), **Unnava** (secretary), **Gadicherla** (treasurer).
The **Kakinada Congress** was held in **1923**.

236.s: At which Congress session, held in Andhra in 1923, did local women serve as executive members and volunteers?
236.x: The 1923 Congress session was held at Kakinada in Andhra, where local women served as executive members and volunteers. Gaya (1922) was in Bihar, Belgaum (1924) in Karnataka and Nagpur (1920) in central India.
xs: Local women served as **executive members and volunteers**.
**Belgaum 1924** is known instead as the only session presided by **Gandhi**.
xa: The **Nationalist Party** formed in **1924**.
Women in Andhra also did **picketing and prohibition** work.

236.x: C.R. Das died in June 1925. His death contributed to the subsequent weakening and split of the Swarajist organisation.
236.tq: Distinguish the close sequence of years surrounding the party’s rise and decline.
xs: C.R. Das died in **June 1925** — option **(4)**.
His death led to a **party split**.
xa: **Responsivists** (**Lajpat Rai, Malaviya, N.C. Kelkar**) favoured co-operation.
Swarajists did poorly in **1926**.

236.s: The Responsivists within the Swarajist movement favoured
o: the immediate abolition of the Congress
exclusive emphasis on spinning and khadi
complete withdrawal from all legislative activity
236.x: The Responsivists favoured cooperation with the government. Lajpat Rai, Malaviya and N.C. Kelkar were associated with this tendency.
236.tq: Test the precise meaning of a faction label instead of relying on its general political impression.
xs: **Co-operation with the government** — option **(3)**.
Responsivists: **Lajpat Rai, Malaviya, N.C. Kelkar**.
xa: They emerged after C.R. Das's death in **June 1925** split the party.
The Swarajists opposed the **Public Safety Bill (1928)**.

236.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the decline of the Swarajists:
1. The party was weak on peasant issues in Bengal.
2. It became urban and legislature-bound.
3. It performed poorly in 1926.
4. It walked out of the councils in 1930 after the Lahore session.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
236.x: All four are correct: the Swarajists were weak on peasant issues in Bengal and became urban and legislature-bound, they did poorly in the 1926 elections, and they walked out of the councils in 1930 after the Lahore session. The split after C.R. Das's death in June 1925 added to the decline.
236.tq: Test multiple decline factors together, including the final council withdrawal.
xs: All four — option **(4)**.
Weak on **peasant issues in Bengal**; **urban, legislature-bound**.
Did poorly in **1926**; **walked out** of the councils in **1930** after **Lahore**.
xa: C.R. Das's death in **June 1925** caused a split.
Yet they won the **Speaker** post (**1925**) and the **Muddiman Committee (1924)**.

236.s: Which one of the following was NOT a component of the constructive programme associated with the 1920s national movement?
236.x: The constructive programme included khadi and spinning, removal of untouchability, Hindu-Muslim unity, prohibition, national schools and village panchayats. Expansion of separate electorates was not part of it.
236.tq: Identify the item outside the constructive-work cluster.
xs: **Expansion of separate electorates** was not part of it — option **(1)**.
Components: **khadi and spinning**, **national schools**, **Hindu-Muslim unity**, **removal of untouchability**, prohibition, **village panchayats**.
xa: **Ponduru (Srikakulam)** khadi was famed nationally.
Women did **picketing** and **prohibition** work.

236.s: Ponduru, in which district of Andhra Pradesh, became nationally famous for khadi?
236.x: Ponduru in Srikakulam was nationally famous for khadi. Women also participated in picketing and prohibition work in Andhra.
236.tq: Use the place–activity association and avoid replacing the district with another Andhra centre.
xs: **Srikakulam** — option **(4)**.
**Ponduru** khadi was famed nationally.
xa: Khadi and spinning were part of the **No-Changers' constructive programme**.
Women's **picketing and prohibition** work was also noted in AP.

236.s: Which of the following activities was particularly associated with women’s participation in Andhra during the constructive programme?
236.x: Women in Andhra participated in picketing and prohibition work as part of the constructive programme.
236.tq: Link a social activity with the relevant regional participant group.
xs: **Picketing and prohibition work** — option **(1)**.
The **Muddiman Committee** and blocking the **Finance Bill** were Swarajist legislative actions.
xa: At the **Kakinada Congress (1923)** women served as executive members and volunteers.
**Ponduru (Srikakulam)** khadi was famous.

236.s: Which statement best expresses the broad significance of the Swarajist and No-Changer activities during the 1922–28 lull?
o: Constructive work was abandoned after the formation of the Swaraj Party.
Council work completely replaced mass mobilisation and constructive work.
The national movement became inactive until the 1930s.
Council work and constructive work were ultimately complementary to the national movement.
236.x: The Swarajists kept the national movement active through council work, while the No-Changers sustained constructive work. These approaches were regarded as complementary and were reconciled at Belgaum in 1924.
236.tq: Compare the two approaches by their functions and identify their combined significance.
xs: **Council work and constructive work were complementary** — option **(4)**.
They kept the national movement alive in the **1922-28** lull.
xa: Swarajists and No-Changers reunited at **Belgaum 1924**.
Swarajists = council entry; No-Changers = constructive work.

236.s: Which of the following correctly represents the principal difference between the Swarajists and the No-Changers?
o: Swarajists favoured council entry, whereas No-Changers emphasised constructive work.
Swarajists supported constructive work, whereas No-Changers supported council entry.
Both groups rejected council entry and constructive work alike.
Both groups favoured cooperation with the colonial government.
236.x: The Swarajists favoured entry into the councils, while the No-Changers concentrated on constructive work and continued the boycott. Both groups were reunited at Belgaum in 1924.
236.tq: Use the central contrast in policy rather than confusing the groups’ common nationalist objective.
xs: **Swarajists** favoured **council entry**; **No-Changers** emphasised **constructive work** — option **(1)**.
Option (2) reverses them.
xa: They reunited at **Belgaum 1924**.
Constructive items: **khadi**, **national schools**, **removal of untouchability**.

236.s: The Belgaum session of the Indian National Congress (1924) is notable because:
o: It was the only Congress session presided over by Mahatma Gandhi
It adopted the Purna Swaraj resolution
It approved the suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement
It was the first session presided over by a woman
236.x: Belgaum 1924 was the only INC session presided over by Gandhi, and it reunited the Swarajists and No-Changers. Purna Swaraj was adopted at Lahore (1929); the NCM was suspended at Bardoli (1922); the first woman President was Annie Besant (1917).
xs: **Belgaum 1924** was the **only INC session presided by Gandhi** — option **(1)**.
It is the notes' **FIRST/LAST** fact for Belgaum; the other options are not linked to it in the notes.
xa: Belgaum reunited the **Swarajists** and **No-Changers**.
Council work and constructive work proved **complementary**.

237.s: The Nehru Report of 1928 was prepared by the committee of the All Parties Conference under the chairmanship of:
237.x: The committee that prepared the Nehru Report was chaired by Motilal Nehru. Jawaharlal Nehru served as its secretary.
237.tq: Distinguish the chairman from the secretary in a committee-based question.
xs: The Nehru Report committee was chaired by **Motilal Nehru** — option **(2)**.
**Jawaharlal Nehru** was its **secretary**, not chairman.
It was an **All Parties Conference** committee and asked for **dominion status**.
xa: The **Calcutta 1928** session accepted the Report with a **one-year ultimatum**.
When it lapsed, **Lahore (Dec 1929)**, under **Jawaharlal Nehru**, adopted **Purna Swaraj**.
⚠ Trap: crediting **Calcutta 1928** with Purna Swaraj is WRONG.

237.s: Who was the first to pass a Purna Swaraj resolution at the district level in Andhra Pradesh?
237.x: Bulusu Sambamurthy of East Godavari was associated with the first district-level Purna Swaraj resolution in Andhra Pradesh.
237.tq: Use the place-name clue to identify the associated Andhra leader.
xs: **Bulusu Sambamurthy** (East Godavari) passed a Purna Swaraj resolution at district level first — option **(4)**.
He got it passed at a district meeting **before Lahore**.
**Yerneni Subrahmanyam** was the only Telugu Dandi marcher; **Thota Narsayya** hoisted the flag at Machilipatnam.
xa: Sambamurthy also led the salt satyagraha at **Kakinada** (**Chollangi**).
**Lahore** passed the Purna Swaraj resolution on **31 Dec 1929**.

237.s: The Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress in December 1929 was held during the viceroyalty of:
237.x: Lord Irwin was the Viceroy of India during the Lahore Session of December 1929 and during the beginning of the Civil Disobedience Movement.
237.tq: Apply the ruler–event association trap.
xs: The Viceroy was **Lord Irwin** — option **(4)**.
Lahore (**December 1929**) was presided by **Jawaharlal Nehru**.
xa: Gandhi's **11-point ultimatum** to Irwin was dated **30 Jan 1930**.
The **Gandhi-Irwin Pact** was signed on **5 March 1931**.

237.s:
With reference to the Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress held in December 1929, consider the following statements:
1. The Nehru Report had demanded Dominion Status.
2. The one-year ultimatum given to the British at the Calcutta Session of 1928 had expired.
3. The Lahore Session accepted the Nehru Report without modification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
237.x: The Nehru Report demanded Dominion Status, and the one-year ultimatum issued at Calcutta in 1928 had expired. The Lahore Session rejected the demand for Dominion Status and adopted Purna Swaraj.
237.tq: Find the statement that reverses the decision taken at Lahore.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** — option **(1)**.
1 correct: the **Nehru Report (1928)** asked for **dominion status**.
2 correct: the **Calcutta 1928** **one-year ultimatum** had lapsed.
3 wrong: Lahore **rejected** the Nehru Report's dominion status and adopted **Purna Swaraj**.
xa: Lahore resolved that **26 January** be observed every year as **Independence Day**.
CWC was authorised to launch **Civil Disobedience**; the **RTC** was boycotted.

237.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between the Calcutta Session of 1928 and the Lahore Session of 1929?
o: Calcutta accepted Dominion Status with a one-year ultimatum, while Lahore adopted Purna Swaraj after the ultimatum expired.
Calcutta adopted Purna Swaraj, while Lahore accepted Dominion Status.
Both sessions adopted Dominion Status without any time limit.
Both sessions adopted Purna Swaraj as the immediate objective.
237.x: The Calcutta Session accepted the Nehru Report's demand for Dominion Status and gave the British one year. After the ultimatum lapsed, the Lahore Session adopted Purna Swaraj.
237.tq: Contrast the decisions of two successive Congress sessions.
xs: **Calcutta** accepted dominion status with a **one-year ultimatum**; **Lahore** adopted **Purna Swaraj** after it lapsed — option **(1)**.
⚠ Purna Swaraj came only at Lahore; Calcutta did not adopt it.
xa: Lahore's resolution was passed on **31 Dec 1929**.
The **first Independence Day** was **26 January 1930**.

237.s:
Consider the following statements about the Lahore session of the Congress (December 1929):
1. It was presided over by Motilal Nehru.
2. It resolved that 26 January be observed every year as Independence Day.
3. The tricolour was hoisted on the banks of the Ravi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
237.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the Lahore session was presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru (Motilal Nehru chaired the Nehru Report committee). Statements 2 and 3 are correct: 26 January was fixed as Independence Day (first observed on 26 January 1930) and Nehru hoisted the tricolour on the banks of the Ravi. So 2 and 3 only (C); A includes the false statement 1, B misses statement 3, D includes statement 1.
237.tq: Lahore 1929 = Jawaharlal presides; Nehru Report = Motilal
xs: Statements **2 and 3** — option **(3)**.
1 wrong: Lahore was presided by **Jawaharlal Nehru**; **Motilal Nehru** chaired the Nehru Report committee.
2 correct: **26 January** to be observed as **Independence Day**.
3 correct: Nehru hoisted the tricolour on the banks of the **Ravi**.
xa: First Independence Day: **26 January 1930**.
CWC was authorised to launch **Civil Disobedience**.

237.s: Which of the following was central among Gandhi's demands addressed to Viceroy Irwin before the Dandi March?
o: Acceptance of the Nehru Report without change
Immediate convening of the Third Round Table Conference
237.x: Abolition of the salt tax was a central demand in Gandhi's eleven-point letter to Viceroy Irwin. Irwin did not accept the demands.
237.tq: Identify the policy demand directly connected with the chosen symbol of protest.
xs: **Abolition of the salt tax** was central — option **(1)**.
It was part of Gandhi's **11 demands** to **Irwin** (letter of **30 Jan 1930**); Irwin refused.
xa: The ultimatum was sent/ignored on **2 March 1930**.
Why salt: a **universal necessity** of rich and poor; the salt tax was the most visible face of colonial exploitation.

237.s: How many followers accompanied Gandhi at the beginning of the Dandi March?
237.x: Gandhi began the Dandi March from Sabarmati Ashram with 78 followers.
237.tq: Use the exact numerical detail rather than the rounded distance or duration.
xs: Gandhi set out with **78** followers — option **(3)**.
He started from **Sabarmati Ashram** on **12 March 1930**.
xa: Route: about **240 miles (385 km)** to **Dandi** (Navsari coast).
Salt law broken on **6 April 1930**.
Only Telugu marcher: **Yerneni Subrahmanyam**.

237.s: Who was the only Telugu marcher among Gandhi's followers in the Dandi March?
237.x: Yerneni, also written Erneni, Subrahmanyam of Krishna district was the only Telugu marcher among Gandhi's followers in the Dandi March.
237.tq: Distinguish the Telugu participant in the march from Andhra leaders associated with other activities.
xs: **Yerneni (Erneni) Subrahmanyam** of **Krishna district** — option **(3)**.
**Bulusu Sambamurthy** led Kakinada; **Thota Narsayya** hoisted the flag at Machilipatnam; **Maganti Annapurna** gave her jewellery.
xa: He later founded an ashram at **Komaravolu**.
The march had **78** followers.

237.s: Yerneni Subrahmanyam, who participated in the Dandi March, later founded an ashram at:
237.x: Yerneni Subrahmanyam later founded an ashram at Komaravolu.
237.tq: Link the participant with the later institution associated with him.
xs: He founded an ashram at **Komaravolu** — option **(1)**.
He was the **only Telugu marcher** at Dandi, from **Krishna district**.
xa: **Dharasana** was Sarojini Naidu's raid site.
**Machilipatnam** saw the first Andhra salt satyagraha by **Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao**.

237.s: Why did Gandhi choose salt as the central symbol of the Civil Disobedience Movement?
o: It was produced exclusively in Gujarat.
It was used only by the urban middle classes.
It was a universal necessity and the salt tax visibly represented colonial exploitation.
It was connected with the demand for separate electorates.
237.x: Salt was consumed by both rich and poor, and the salt tax and monopoly made it a visible symbol of colonial economic exploitation.
237.tq: Choose the option that combines the social reach and political significance of salt.
xs: Salt was a **universal necessity** and the salt tax visibly represented **colonial exploitation** — option **(3)**.
It was used by **rich and poor** alike, and the **salt tax/monopoly** was the most visible face of colonial taxation.
xa: Abolition of the salt tax was central to the **11 demands**.
The CDM was the **first mass law-breaking**.

237.s: Gandhi named which person as the first successor to lead the movement after his arrest during the Salt Satyagraha?
237.x: Abbas Tyabji was designated as Gandhi's first successor after his arrest. Sarojini Naidu was named the second successor.
237.tq: Read the sequence carefully when two leaders are both associated with succession.
xs: **Abbas Tyabji** was the first successor — option **(2)**.
**Sarojini Naidu** was second, and led the **Dharasana** raid.
xa: **Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay** led women into the Salt Satyagraha.
**Kasturba Gandhi** joined protests and was imprisoned.

237.s: Gandhi began the Dandi March from Sabarmati Ashram on ____ and broke the salt law at Dandi on ____.
237.x: The march started from Sabarmati on 12 March 1930 (APPSC 2025 key) and Gandhi broke the salt law at Dandi on 6 April 1930. 2 March 1930 was when the 11-demand ultimatum was sent to Irwin, and 26 January 1930 was the first Independence Day; the other pairs mix these dates.
237.tq: Dandi: 12 March start, 6 April salt
xs: **12 March** start is the APPSC **2025** key.
**2 March 1930** was when the ultimatum was sent; **26 January 1930** the first Independence Day.
xa: ⚠ **12 March** start - **78** followers - **240 miles** - salt law broken **6 April 1930**.
Bose likened it to "**Napoleon's return from Elba**".

237.s: Who reported the beatings at the Dharasana Salt Works to the international public?
237.x: The beatings at Dharasana were reported by Webb Miller, a United States journalist.
237.tq: Test the eyewitness separately from the political leader.
xs: **Webb Miller**, a US journalist — option **(1)**.
The beatings were at the **Dharasana Salt Works** raid led by **Sarojini Naidu**.
xa: She led it after **Abbas Tyabji**'s arrest.
Other centres: **Peshawar** (Red Shirts), **Sanikatta** (Karnataka coast).

237.s: Rani Gaidinliu was associated with which movement or uprising?
o: The Naga uprising in the Manipur region
237.x: Rani Gaidinliu was associated with the Naga uprising in the Manipur region. She was arrested in 1932 and was called ‘Rani’ by Jawaharlal Nehru.
237.tq: Use the regional association to identify the movement.
xs: **Rani Gaidinliu** led the **Naga uprising** (Manipur) — option **(4)**.
She was arrested in **1932** and called "**Rani**" by Nehru.
xa: **Sholapur**: textile workers' rising, **1930**; martial law.
**Vedaranyam** was the **Rajaji-led** salt satyagraha.

237.s: The Khudai Khidmatgars organised their Civil Disobedience protests particularly in
237.x: The Khudai Khidmatgars, or Red Shirts, led non-violent protests in Peshawar and the North-West Frontier Province. The Qissa Khwani firing occurred there in April 1930.
237.tq: Associate the organisation with its regional field of action.
xs: **Peshawar and the NWFP** — option **(2)**.
**Khudai Khidmatgars / Red Shirts** were founded by **Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan** among Pathans.
xa: **Qissa Khwani** firing: **April 1930**.
**Garhwal Rifles** refused to fire on the Peshawar crowd (**1930**).

237.s: The Qissa Khwani firing connected with the Khudai Khidmatgar movement took place in
237.x: The Qissa Khwani firing in Peshawar occurred in April 1930 during the non-violent protests of the Khudai Khidmatgars.
237.tq: Discriminate between closely related movement dates.
xs: The firing was at **Qissa Khwani**, **Peshawar**, on non-violent **Khudai Khidmatgar** protests.
xa: **Garhwal Rifles** (**Chandra Singh Garhwali**) refused to fire.
The CDM brought the **NWFP** into the struggle.

237.s: Who among the following was known as the ‘Frontier Gandhi’?
237.x: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan was popularly known as the ‘Frontier Gandhi’ and was associated with the Khudai Khidmatgars.
237.tq: Use direct title–person recall.
xs: **Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan** — option **(2)**.
He founded the **Khudai Khidmatgars (Red Shirts)** in the **NWFP**.
xa: **Konda Venkatappayya** was the Andhra salt satyagraha dictator.
**Qissa Khwani** firing, **April 1930**.

237.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
237.x: Babu Genu was associated with Bombay, where he was crushed by a lorry carrying foreign cloth. Dharasana was associated with Sarojini Naidu.
237.tq: Find the wrong place associated with the person.
xs: **Babu Genu — Dharasana** is wrong — option **(3)**.
Babu Genu was crushed by a lorry carrying foreign cloth in **Bombay**, **12 Dec 1930**.
**Dharasana** is linked to **Sarojini Naidu**.
xa: **Rani Gaidinliu** — Naga uprising; **Ghaffar Khan** — NWFP: both correct.
Dharasana beatings were reported by **Webb Miller**.

237.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki — Muzaffarpur bomb case
2. Garhwal Rifles — Refusal to fire on the Peshawar crowd
3. Sholapur — Textile workers’ rising and martial law
4. Vasudeo Chapekar — Rand’s murder at Poona
237.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. The incidents belong respectively to 1908, 1930, 1930 and 1897.
237.tq: Match the incident with its participants and location.
xs: All four — option **(4)**.
**Khudiram Bose, Prafulla Chaki** — Muzaffarpur bomb, **1908**; **Garhwal Rifles** — Peshawar, **1930**.
**Sholapur** — textile rising, **1930**; **Vasudeo Chapekar** — Rand's murder, Poona **1897**.
xa: ⚠ Only **Garhwal Rifles**, **Sholapur** and **Babu Genu** belong to the CDM; the others are earlier.
Babu Genu died on **12 Dec 1930** in Bombay.

237.s: The Garhwal Rifles became notable during the Civil Disobedience Movement because they
o: refused to fire on the crowd at Peshawar
led the salt march at Vedaranyam
237.x: The Garhwal Rifles, associated with Chandra Singh Garhwali, refused to fire on the crowd at Peshawar in 1930.
237.tq: Identify the distinctive action rather than the unit’s location alone.
xs: They **refused to fire** on the **Peshawar** crowd — option **(2)**.
They are linked to **Chandra Singh Garhwali** (**1930**).
xa: The Peshawar protests were by the **Khudai Khidmatgars**; **Qissa Khwani** firing, **April 1930**.
**Sarojini Naidu** led the **Dharasana** raid.

237.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Aruna Asaf Ali — first woman president of the INC in Kanpur
Sarojini Naidu — founded an ashram at Komaravolu
Duvvuri Subbamma — led the Dharasana raid
237.x: Kasturba Gandhi participated in protests and suffered imprisonment. Sarojini Naidu led the Dharasana raid, Aruna Asaf Ali was associated with the Quit India flag-hoisting, and Duvvuri Subbamma was an Andhra leader jailed during the CDM.
237.tq: Eliminate swapped person–role pairs.
xs: **Kasturba Gandhi — protests and imprisonment** — option **(1)**.
**Aruna Asaf Ali** = **Quit India (1942)**; **Sarojini Naidu** was the first Indian woman president (**Kanpur 1925**).
**Komaravolu** was **Yerneni Subrahmanyam**'s ashram; **Duvvuri Subbamma** was jailed, not the Dharasana leader.
xa: ⚠ **Aruna Asaf Ali** = Quit India, not CDM.
**Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay** led women into the Salt Satyagraha.

237.s: Sarojini Naidu led the raid at:
237.x: Sarojini Naidu led the raid at the Dharasana Salt Works after Gandhi's arrest.
237.tq: Separate the Civil Disobedience role from the Quit India role of the same leader.
xs: **Dharasana Salt Works** — option **(2)**.
She led it after **Abbas Tyabji**'s arrest.
**Gowalia Tank** is linked to **Aruna Asaf Ali** (**1942**).
xa: Beatings were reported by **Webb Miller**.
Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman INC president (**Kanpur 1925**).

237.s: Which one of the following statements regarding women's participation in the Civil Disobedience Movement is correct?
o: Women participated only after the withdrawal of the movement in 1934.
Women joined in massive numbers, including picketing liquor and foreign-cloth shops.
Women participated only in underground revolutionary activity.
Women were excluded from protests against colonial taxes.
237.x: The Civil Disobedience Movement marked the first occasion on which women participated in massive numbers. Their activities included picketing liquor shops and shops selling foreign cloth.
237.tq: Select the option that captures both the scale and forms of participation.
xs: Women joined **in massive numbers**, picketing **liquor and foreign-cloth shops** — option **(2)**.
The CDM was the **first time** women joined on this scale.
xa: **"Kattera Udyamam"** (scissors movement) raised women's participation in Andhra.
**Paturi Balasaraswatamma** was the first woman arrested in **Nellore**.

237.s: Who was the first woman arrested in Nellore in connection with the national movement?
237.x: Paturi Balasaraswatamma was the first woman arrested in Nellore in connection with the national movement.
237.tq: Match the specific Andhra district with its associated woman activist.
xs: **Paturi Balasaraswatamma** — option **(2)**.
**Maganti Annapurna** gave her jewellery; **Palakojeti Shyamalamba** was from E. Godavari.
xa: Women jailed: **Bharati Devi Ranga**, **Digumarti Janakamma**, **Khammampati Manikyamba** (with a six-month-old baby).
**Duvvuri Subbamma** (East Godavari) was jailed in the CDM.

237.s: Who gave all her jewellery to support the national movement?
237.x: Maganti Annapurna gave all her jewellery to support the national movement.
237.tq: Identify the distinctive personal contribution rather than a political office.
xs: **Maganti Annapurna** — option **(3)**.
**Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay** led women into the Salt Satyagraha; **Duvvuri Subbamma** was jailed.
xa: Other Andhra women: **Sattaraju Mangamma** (Eluru), **Ponaka Kanakamma**.
**"Kattera Udyamam"** raised women's participation.

237.s: Which one of the following statements about Duvvuri Subbamma is correct?
o: She hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank in 1942.
She led the Dharasana raid after Gandhi's arrest.
She was an Andhra woman leader from East Godavari who was jailed during the CDM.
She was the first Indian woman president of the INC.
237.x: Duvvuri Subbamma was an Andhra woman leader from East Godavari who was jailed during the Civil Disobedience Movement.
237.tq: Reject roles belonging to other prominent women leaders.
xs: **Duvvuri Subbamma** — Andhra (**East Godavari**) leader jailed in the CDM — option **(3)**.
**Gowalia Tank (1942)** = **Aruna Asaf Ali**; Dharasana and first Indian woman president = **Sarojini Naidu**.
xa: **Paturi Balasaraswatamma** was the first woman arrested in Nellore.
**Palakojeti Shyamalamba** was also from E. Godavari.

237.s: The ‘Kattera Udyamam’ in Andhra was associated with
o: the formation of the Red Shirts
increased participation of women in the Salt Satyagraha
a campaign against the Cunningham Circular
the boycott of the Round Table Conference
237.x: The ‘Kattera Udyamam’, or scissors movement, helped raise women’s participation in the Andhra movement.
237.tq: Distinguish a local term by the social participation it promoted.
xs: **"Kattera Udyamam"** (scissors movement) **raised women's participation** — option **(2)**.
The **Red Shirts** were Ghaffar Khan's; the **Cunningham Circular** protests were in **Assam**.
xa: CDM was the first time women joined **in massive numbers**.
**Maganti Annapurna** gave all her jewellery.

237.s: The first Indian woman to preside over the Indian National Congress was:
237.x: Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman President of the Congress. She presided over the Kanpur session in 1925.
237.tq: Separate nationality from gender by comparing the first woman president with the first Indian woman president.
xs: **Sarojini Naidu at Kanpur in 1925** — option **(4)**.
She was the **first Indian woman INC president**, and also led the **Dharasana** raid.
xa: She was Gandhi's **second** successor, after **Abbas Tyabji**.
⚠ **Aruna Asaf Ali** = **Quit India (1942)**.

237.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay - led women into the Salt Satyagraha
Aruna Asaf Ali - led the Dharasana raid
Sarojini Naidu - hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank in 1942
Kasturba Gandhi - first Indian woman President of the INC
237.x: Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay led women into the Salt Satyagraha. Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank in the Quit India Movement (1942); Sarojini Naidu led the Dharasana raid and was the first Indian woman INC President (Kanpur 1925); Kasturba Gandhi joined protests and was imprisoned.
237.tq: Gowalia Tank = Aruna; Dharasana = Sarojini
xs: **Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay** led women into the Salt Satyagraha — option **(1)**.
**Aruna Asaf Ali** hoisted the flag at **Gowalia Tank (1942)**; **Sarojini Naidu** led **Dharasana** and presided **Kanpur 1925**.
**Kasturba Gandhi** joined protests and was imprisoned.
xa: These pairings are an APPSC **2025** key.
**Duvvuri Subbamma** was the Andhra woman jailed in the CDM.

237.s: Who was designated as the dictator of the Andhra Salt Satyagraha?
237.x: Konda Venkatappayya was the dictator of the Andhra Salt Satyagraha and had met Gandhi at Jambusar.
237.tq: Distinguish the overall dictator from district-level leaders.
xs: **Konda Venkatappayya** — option **(2)**.
He met Gandhi at **Jambusar**.
**Pattabhi Sitaramayya** proposed the district camps; **Kaleswara Rao** led Machilipatnam; **Prakasam** led Madras/Devarampadu.
xa: Each district had its own dictator, war council and **sibiram**.
Konda Venkatappayya also led in **Guntur villages** with **Unnava Lakshminarayana**.

237.s: The idea that every district should have its own dictator, war council and military-style camp was suggested by
237.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya suggested the organisation of one satyagraha camp, with a dictator and war council, in each district.
237.tq: Separate the organiser of the structure from the chief dictator.
xs: **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** — option **(1)**.
Each district had its own **dictator**, **war council** and a military-style camp (**sibiram**).
xa: Overall Andhra dictator: **Konda Venkatappayya**.
Pattabhi called **Machilipatnam** his **"Mecca"**.

237.s:
Consider the following statements about Salt Satyagraha camps in Andhra:
1. Seethanagaram Ashram, associated with Brahmajosyula Subrahmanyam, was called the 'Andhra Dandi'.
2. Devarampadu, called the 'Dakshina Dandi', had its camp at Tanguturi Prakasam's house.
3. Seethanagaram Ashram was the camp of West Godavari district.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
237.x: Statement 1 is correct: Seethanagaram Ashram (Brahmajosyula Subrahmanyam) was the 'Andhra Dandi'. Statement 2 is correct: Devarampadu was the 'Dakshina Dandi' with its camp at Prakasam's house. Statement 3 is wrong: Seethanagaram was the East Godavari camp; West Godavari's was Eluru National School. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
237.tq: Andhra Dandi = Seethanagaram (E. Godavari); Dakshina Dandi = Devarampadu (Prakasam).
xs: Statements **1 and 2** — option **(2)**.
1 correct: **Seethanagaram Ashram** (**Brahmajosyula Subrahmanyam**) = **"Andhra Dandi"**.
2 correct: **Devarampadu** = **"Dakshina Dandi"**, camp at **Tanguturi Prakasam's** house.
3 wrong: Seethanagaram was the **East Godavari** camp; West Godavari's was **Eluru National School**.
xa: Vizag's camp: **Vizianagaram**; Krishna's: **Andhraratna Bhavan** and **Machilipatnam**.
⚠ **"Mecca"** = Machilipatnam.

237.s: Who conducted the first Salt Satyagraha at Machilipatnam?
