237.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao conducted the first Salt Satyagraha at Machilipatnam. Pattabhi Sitaramayya called Machilipatnam his ‘Mecca’.
237.tq: Distinguish the first local satyagrahi from associated leaders.
xs: **Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao** — option **(2)**.
Pattabhi called Machilipatnam his **"Mecca"**.
**Bulusu Sambamurthy** = Kakinada; **Oruganti Venkatasubbayya** = Mylapadu; **Kalluri Subbarao** = Bellary.
xa: **Thota Narsayya ("Jenda Narsayya")** hoisted the flag at Machilipatnam.
Krishna district camps: **Andhraratna Bhavan** and **Machilipatnam**.

237.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
237.x: Kakinada was associated with Bulusu Sambamurthy at Chollangi. Oruganti Venkatasubbayya was associated with Mylapadu in Nellore.
237.tq: Find the swapped leader–centre pair.
xs: **Kakinada — Oruganti Venkatasubbayya** is wrong — option **(1)**.
Kakinada = **Bulusu Sambamurthy** at **Chollangi**; Oruganti made salt at **Mylapadu** (Nellore), **11 April 1930**.
**Guntur villages — Unnava**, **Bellary — Kalluri Subbarao**, **Vizag — Tenneti Viswanatham** are correct.
xa: Mylapadu was with **Bezawada Gopal Reddy**.
Bellary was chosen as **Rayalaseema had no coast**.

237.s: On 13 April 1930, the first salt squad from the Swarajya office at Madras was led by
o: Tanguturi Prakasam and Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao
Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao and Mutnuri Krishna Rao
237.x: Tanguturi Prakasam and Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao led the first salt squad from the Swarajya office at Madras on 13 April 1930.
237.tq: Use the date to identify the associated leaders and event.
xs: **Tanguturi Prakasam** and **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** — option **(2)**.
They led the first salt squad from the **Swarajya** office, Madras, **13 April 1930**.
xa: Prakasam's house was the **Devarampadu** camp (**"Dakshina Dandi"**).
**Nellore**'s Mylapadu salt-making was on **11 April 1930**.

237.s: Why did the Salt Satyagraha in Rayalaseema take place at Bellary under Kalluri Subbarao?
o: The Madras Government permitted salt manufacture there
Bellary was the headquarters of the Congress
The Andhra Salt Committee was based there
237.x: Rayalaseema had no coast, so Kalluri Subbarao led the activity at Bellary instead of a coastal salt-making centre.
237.tq: Apply the geographical condition to explain the choice of centre.
xs: **Rayalaseema had no coast** — option **(3)**.
So **Kalluri Subbarao** led it at **Bellary**.
xa: Coastal centres: **Machilipatnam**, **Kakinada**, **Mylapadu**, **Devarampadu**.
**Pedaganjam-Chinaganjam** was a famous salt coast.

237.s: Pedaganjam and Chinaganjam, centres on the Andhra coast during the Salt Satyagraha, were famous for:
237.x: Pedaganjam-Chinaganjam (Prakasam district) was a famous salt-making coast (APPSC 2019 key). Kalamkari is linked to Machilipatnam and Jamdani sarees to Uppada; toddy tapping is not the centre's identity.
237.tq: Pedaganjam-Chinaganjam = salt
xs: **Salt-making** — option **(2)**.
**Pedaganjam-Chinaganjam** was a famous salt-making coast (APPSC **2019**).
xa: **Devarampadu** (Prakasam dist) = **"Dakshina Dandi"**.
Bellary was used as **Rayalaseema had no coast**.

237.s: Who wrote the patriotic song ‘Bharata Swarajya Yuddham’?
237.x: Jagganna Sastri wrote ‘Bharata Swarajya Yuddham’.
237.tq: Match the literary work with its author.
xs: **Jagganna Sastri** — option **(2)**.
**Adavi Bapiraju** wrote songs in jail; **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary** wrote "**Veeragandhamu**".
xa: Veeragandhamu — APPSC **2012** key: **CDM**.
⚠ An APPSC **2019** question tied Veeragandhamu to NCM.

237.s: Adavi Bapiraju is associated with patriotic songs that he wrote
o: at the Third Round Table Conference
237.x: Adavi Bapiraju wrote patriotic songs while in jail.
237.tq: Identify the setting associated with the author’s work.
xs: He wrote songs **during imprisonment** — option **(2)**.
**Jagganna Sastri** wrote **Bharata Swarajya Yuddham**.
xa: **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary** wrote "**Veeragandhamu Techhinaramu**".
These were CDM patriotic songs.

237.s: The patriotic song 'Veeragandhamu Techhinaramu... Veerulevvaro Telpudee' by Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary is associated with which movement?
237.x: The APPSC 2012 key ties the song to the Civil Disobedience Movement. Linking it to the NCM (as an APPSC 2019 question did) is the known trap; Quit India and Vandemataram are unrelated to this song.
237.tq: Veeragandhamu = CDM, not NCM
xs: **Civil Disobedience Movement** — option **(2)** (APPSC **2012** key).
⚠ An APPSC **2019** question tied it to NCM — a known trap.
xa: Author: **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary**.
Other CDM songs: **Bharata Swarajya Yuddham** (**Jagganna Sastri**); jail songs by **Adavi Bapiraju**.

237.s: Who were the mediators associated with the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
o: Madan Mohan Malaviya and Jawaharlal Nehru
Tej Bahadur Sapru and M.R. Jayakar
237.x: Tej Bahadur Sapru and M.R. Jayakar acted as mediators in the negotiations leading to the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
237.tq: Test the mediator–event association directly.
xs: **Tej Bahadur Sapru and M.R. Jayakar** — option **(3)**.
**V.S. Srinivasa Sastri** also mediated.
xa: Signed **5 March 1931** (**Delhi Pact**).
⚠ Dating it to March **1930** is WRONG.

237.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Gandhi-Irwin Pact:
1. Gandhi agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement.
2. Gandhi agreed to attend the Second Round Table Conference.
3. Irwin agreed to commute the death sentences of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
237.x: Gandhi agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement and attend the Second Round Table Conference. Irwin did not agree to commute the death sentences of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru.
237.tq: Separate agreed terms from the specifically refused demand.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** — option **(3)**.
Gandhi agreed to **suspend CDM** and **attend the 2nd RTC**.
3 wrong: Irwin **refused** to commute the sentences of **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru**.
xa: Irwin also refused a **public inquiry** into police excesses.
Irwin agreed: release of non-violent prisoners; coastal villagers may make **salt for own use**.

237.s: The Karachi Session of the Indian National Congress held in March 1931 was presided over by
237.x: Vallabhbhai Patel presided over the Karachi Session of the Congress in March 1931.
237.tq: Link the session with its presiding president.
xs: **Vallabhbhai Patel** — option **(3)**.
The **Karachi session (March 1931)** endorsed the pact.
xa: It passed resolutions on **Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programme**.
Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru were executed on **23 Mar 1931**.

237.s:
Which of the following resolutions were passed at the Karachi Session of the Congress in March 1931?
1. Resolution on Fundamental Rights
2. Resolution on the National Economic Programme
3. Resolution accepting separate electorates for the depressed classes
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
237.x: The Karachi Session passed resolutions on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme. The National Economic Programme was drafted by Jawaharlal Nehru; separate electorates for the depressed classes were not accepted there.
237.tq: Reject the statement importing a later communal-electorate issue into the Karachi resolutions.
xs: Karachi passed **Fundamental Rights** and **National Economic Programme** resolutions, drafted by **Jawaharlal Nehru**.
The notes record no separate-electorates resolution at Karachi.
xa: President: **Vallabhbhai Patel**.
Criticism: no commutation for **Bhagat Singh**; youth disillusioned.

237.s:
Which of the following was a term agreed to by Lord Irwin under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
1. Release of non-violent political prisoners
2. Remission of fines and return of unsold lands
3. Permission for salt-making in coastal villages for personal use
4. Commutation of the death sentences of Bhagat Singh and his comrades
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
237.x: Irwin agreed to release non-violent political prisoners, remit fines, return unsold lands and permit limited salt-making. He refused to commute the death sentences of Bhagat Singh and his comrades.
237.tq: Spot the swapped term by separating Irwin’s agreements from Gandhi’s demands and refusals.
xs: Irwin agreed to **release non-violent political prisoners**, **remit fines, return unsold lands**, and let **coastal villagers make salt for own use**.
4 wrong: Irwin **refused** to commute the death sentences of **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru**.
xa: Irwin also refused a **public inquiry into police excesses**; he agreed to **withdraw ordinances**.
Gandhi agreed to **suspend CDM** and **attend the 2nd RTC**.
Mediators: **Tej Bahadur Sapru**, **M.R. Jayakar**, **V.S. Srinivasa Sastri**.

237.s: Which criticism of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact was most directly connected with the execution of Bhagat Singh and his comrades?
o: The Pact postponed the Karachi Session.
The Pact prohibited salt-making in coastal villages.
The Pact failed to secure commutation of their death sentences.
The Pact ended the system of separate electorates.
237.x: A major criticism was that the Pact did not secure commutation of the death sentences of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru, causing disillusionment among the youth.
237.tq: Match the criticism with the specific unresolved issue.
xs: The Pact **failed to secure commutation of their death sentences** — option **(3)**.
This **disillusioned the youth**.
The Pact actually **allowed** coastal salt-making, and the **Karachi session (March 1931)** endorsed it rather than being postponed.
xa: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru were executed on **23 Mar 1931**.
The Pact also gave **no police inquiry**.

237.s: Which one of the following was also associated with the Karachi Congress session of 1931?
o: Launch of the Quit India Movement
237.x: The Karachi session endorsed the Gandhi-Irwin Pact in addition to adopting resolutions on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme.
237.tq: Test the additional resolution-related association rather than the presidency alone.
xs: Karachi **endorsed the Gandhi-Irwin Pact** — option **(1)**.
It also passed resolutions on **Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programme** (drafted by **Jawaharlal Nehru**).
The **Cripps Mission** came only in **1942**.
xa: President: **Vallabhbhai Patel**.
The Pact was signed on **5 March 1931**.

237.s: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact, also called the Delhi Pact, was signed on:
237.x: The Pact was signed on 5 March 1931; dating it to March 1930 is a known trap (the Dandi March was then just beginning). 23 March 1931 is the execution of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru; 24 September 1932 is the Poona Pact.
237.tq: Gandhi-Irwin = 5 March 1931
xs: Signed **5 March 1931** — option **(2)**.
⚠ Dating it to March **1930** is WRONG.
**23 March 1931** = execution of **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru**; **24 Sept 1932** = **Poona Pact**.
xa: Also called the **Delhi Pact**; the CWC authorised Gandhi.
Gandhi then attended the **2nd RTC** (**1931**).

237.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Simon Commission appointed
B. Lahore Session adopting Purna Swaraj
C. First Independence Day
D. Gandhi-Irwin Pact
237.x: The Simon Commission was appointed in November 1927, the Lahore Session was held in December 1929, 26 January 1930 was observed as the first Independence Day, and the Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931.
237.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two 1929–30 events.
xs: **Simon Commission appointed (Nov 1927)** → **Lahore (Dec 1929)** → **First Independence Day (26 Jan 1930)** → **Gandhi-Irwin Pact (5 Mar 1931)**.
xa: The Simon Commission arrived on **3 Feb 1928**.
Dandi March: **12 Mar - 6 Apr 1930**.

237.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Nehru Report
B. Dandi March
C. First Round Table Conference
D. Withdrawal of the Civil Disobedience Movement
237.x: The Nehru Report was prepared in 1928, the Dandi March took place from 12 March to 6 April 1930, the First Round Table Conference was held in November 1930, and the Civil Disobedience Movement was withdrawn in 1934.
237.tq: Use the fixed years 1928, 1930 and 1934 to order the events.
xs: **Nehru Report (1928)** → **Dandi March (12 Mar - 6 Apr 1930)** → **First RTC (Nov 1930)** → **CDM withdrawn (1934)**.
xa: The CDM resumed in **Jan 1932**, with Gandhi arrested.
The **2nd RTC** was in **1931**.

237.s: Which one of the following chronological sequences is correct?
o: Gandhi-Irwin Pact → Communal Award → Poona Pact → withdrawal of CDM
Communal Award → Gandhi-Irwin Pact → Poona Pact → withdrawal of CDM
Gandhi-Irwin Pact → Poona Pact → Communal Award → withdrawal of CDM
Poona Pact → Communal Award → Gandhi-Irwin Pact → withdrawal of CDM
237.x: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed in 1931, the Communal Award and Poona Pact followed in 1932, and the Civil Disobedience Movement was withdrawn in 1934.
237.tq: Place events by year before distinguishing the two events of 1932.
xs: **Gandhi-Irwin Pact → Communal Award → Poona Pact → withdrawal of CDM** — option **(1)**.
Pact **5 Mar 1931**; **Communal Award Aug 1932**; **Poona Pact 24 Sept 1932**; CDM withdrawn **1934**.
xa: **1933-34**: CDM suspended, then withdrawn.
APPSC G2 **2025** order: **Chauri Chaura (1922) → Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931) → Poona Pact (1932) → Cripps Mission (1942)**.

237.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
237.x: The Communal Award was announced in August 1932, while the Poona Pact was signed in September 1932. The other pairs are correctly matched.
237.tq: Find the near-date trap between two events of 1932.
xs: **August 1932 — Poona Pact** is wrong — option **(1)**.
**Aug 1932** was the **Communal Award**; the **Poona Pact** was **24 Sept 1932**.
**Nov 1927** (Simon Commission), **5 March 1931** (Pact) and **1942** (Cripps) are correct.
xa: The Simon Commission arrived on **3 Feb 1928**.
First RTC: **Nov 1930**.

237.s:
Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the following events?
A. Chauri Chaura incident
B. Lahore Session and Purna Swaraj
C. Gandhi-Irwin Pact
D. Cripps Mission
237.x: The Chauri Chaura incident occurred in 1922, the Lahore Session in 1929, the Gandhi-Irwin Pact in 1931 and the Cripps Mission in 1942.
237.tq: Anchor the sequence to the widely separated years 1922, 1929, 1931 and 1942.
xs: **Chauri Chaura (1922)** → **Lahore / Purna Swaraj (Dec 1929)** → **Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931)** → **Cripps Mission (1942)**.
xa: This mirrors the APPSC G2 **2025** order (with **Poona Pact, 1932**).
NCM was withdrawn in **Feb 1922** after Chauri Chaura.

237.s: Which one of the following best describes the significance of the Civil Disobedience Movement as stated in relation to mass participation?
o: It was the first movement to accept separate electorates for the depressed classes.
It was confined exclusively to urban merchants and lawyers.
It was the first movement to break laws openly on a mass scale and drew women, peasants, tribals and merchants into the struggle.
It was limited to constitutional negotiations in London.
237.x: The Civil Disobedience Movement was significant as the first movement to break laws openly on a mass scale, with participation by women, peasants, tribals and merchants.
237.tq: Choose the option containing the complete significance rather than an exclusive claim.
xs: The CDM was the **first mass law-breaking** and drew **women, peasants, tribals and merchants** — option **(3)**.
Laws were broken **openly on a mass scale**.
xa: It also brought the **NWFP** into the struggle.
Its second phase (**1932-34**) failed under **repression**.

237.s: The Civil Disobedience Movement brought which of the following regions prominently into the national struggle along with wider mass participation?
o: Only the princely states of southern India
237.x: The movement brought women and the North-West Frontier Province into the struggle, in addition to its wider mass participation.
237.tq: Test the regional significance without confusing it with the movement's social groups.
xs: The **North-West Frontier Province** — option **(4)**.
The **Khudai Khidmatgars (Red Shirts)** of **Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan** led protests in **Peshawar**.
xa: **Qissa Khwani** firing: **April 1930**.
The CDM drew **women, peasants, tribals and merchants**.

237.s: The second phase of the Civil Disobedience Movement, covering 1932–1934, failed mainly because of
o: Lack of any participation by peasants
Acceptance of the Communal Award by Gandhi
The absence of a Karachi Congress Session
237.x: The second phase of the Civil Disobedience Movement, from 1932 to 1934, failed under repression.
237.tq: Match the phase with its stated cause of failure.
xs: **Repression** — option **(4)**.
The second phase (**1932-34**) began when the CDM resumed in **Jan 1932** and Gandhi was arrested.
xa: **1934**: CDM crushed and withdrawn.
The Pact was also attacked for not saving **Bhagat Singh**.

237.s: K. Kamaraj's first imprisonment was associated with the
o: Dandi March led by Mahatma Gandhi
237.x: K. Kamaraj's first imprisonment came during the Rajaji-led Vedaranyam Salt Satyagraha.
237.tq: Link the leader with the specific regional satyagraha.
xs: The **Rajaji-led Vedaranyam Salt Satyagraha** — option **(3)**.
This was recalled in a birth-anniversary tribute (**17 Jul 2026**).
xa: Andhra parallels: **Devarampadu** (**"Dakshina Dandi"**) and Seethanagaram (**"Andhra Dandi"**).
Gandhi's own Dandi March began on **12 March 1930**.

237.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Thota Narsayya — Hoisted the flag at Machilipatnam
237.x: Yerneni Subrahmanyam is associated with Dandi, not with presiding over the Karachi Session. Thota Narsayya, Konda Venkatappayya and Prakasam are correctly matched with the stated Andhra-related activities.
237.tq: Find the swapped person–role association.
xs: **Yerneni Subrahmanyam — Karachi Session president** is wrong — option **(4)**.
Yerneni was the only Telugu marcher at **Dandi**; Karachi's president was **Vallabhbhai Patel**.
**Prakasam — Devarampadu**, **Thota Narsayya — Machilipatnam flag**, **Konda Venkatappayya — Andhra dictator** are correct.
xa: Thota Narsayya was called "**Jenda Narsayya**".
**Bulusu Sambamurthy** passed a Purna Swaraj resolution at district level before Lahore.

238.s: Who was appointed by the Andhra Congress Committee as the Dictator for Andhra during the Civil Disobedience Movement?
238.x: Konda Venkatappaiah was appointed as the Dictator for Andhra and became the first leader of the Civil Disobedience Movement in Andhra.
238.tq: Use the leader–role association and distinguish the regional dictator from district-level leaders.
xs: The Andhra Congress Committee made **Konda Venkatappaiah** the **Dictator** — option **(4)**.
He was the **first leader of CDM in Andhra** (APPSC **2008** and **2017** keys).
**Kaleswara Rao** led at **Machilipatnam**; **Kalluri Subbarao** at **Bellary**; **Bulusu Sambamurthy** at **Chollangi**.
xa: Each district had its own dictator, **war council** and camp (**shibiram**).
Camps: **Guntur**, **Pallepadu Ashram** (Nellore), **Bellary** (Rayalaseema), **Vedavanam** (Madras).

238.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
238.x: The camps included Guntur in Guntur, Pallepadu Ashram in Nellore, Bellary in Rayalaseema, and Vedavanam at Prakasam's house in Madras. Krishna was not identified with the Vedavanam camp.
238.tq: Find the wrongly associated place by separating district camps from the Madras camp.
xs: **Krishna — Vedavanam camp** is wrong — option **(1)**.
**Vedavanam** was at **Prakasam's house** in **Madras**.
**Bellary** (Rayalaseema), **Pallepadu Ashram** (Nellore) and **Guntur** (Guntur) are correct.
xa: Mylapadu beach (Nellore) was run with **Pallepadu** as the centre.
Bellary leader: **Kalluri Subbarao** ("**Rayalaseema Kuruvriddhudu**").

238.s: Each district during the Civil Disobedience Movement in Andhra had its own:
238.x: Every district had its own dictator, war council and camp, known as a shibiram.
238.tq: Test the distinctive organisational structure rather than a prominent individual.
xs: Each district had its own **dictator, war council and camp** — option **(3)**.
The camp was called a **shibiram**.
xa: Overall Andhra Dictator: **Konda Venkatappaiah**.
Programme: make salt, raid salt depots, **picket foreign-cloth shops**, **cut toddy palms**.

238.s: Who led the Salt Satyagraha at Visakhapatnam and Bhimunipatnam?
238.x: Tenneti Viswanatham led the Salt Satyagraha at Visakhapatnam and Bhimunipatnam.
238.tq: Match the leader to the pair of coastal centres, not merely to a district.
xs: **Tenneti Viswanatham** — option **(3)**.
**Bezawada Gopal Reddy** = **Mylapadu**; **Dandu Narayana Raju** = **Mattapalem**; **Ravi Narayana Reddy** = **Ramachandrapuram**.
xa: First Andhra salt satyagraha: **Machilipatnam, 6 Apr 1930**.
**Kasi Viswanadham** led at **Vadarevu** (Guntur coast).

238.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
238.x: Dandu Narayana Raju led the Salt Satyagraha at Mattapalem. Ravi Narayana Reddy was associated with Ramachandrapuram, Kasi Viswanadham with Vadarevu, and Pattabhi Sitaramayya with Machilipatnam.
238.tq: Start from the sure centre–leader pair and reject swapped leaders.
xs: **Mattapalem — Dandu Narayana Raju** — option **(2)**.
**Vadarevu** = **Kasi Viswanadham**; **Ramachandrapuram** = **Ravi Narayana Reddy**; **Bellary** = **Kalluri Subbarao**.
xa: APPSC **2023** key: **Bulusu - Kakinada, Dandu Narayana Raju - Mattapalem, Kasi Viswanadham - Vadarevu, Pattabhi - Masulipatnam**.
⚠ Some explanations swap **Bulusu** and **Kasi Viswanadham**.

238.s: Pattabhi Sitaramayya described which centre as his “Mecca” in connection with the Salt Satyagraha?
238.x: Machilipatnam was associated with Pattabhi Sitaramayya, who referred to it as his “Mecca”.
238.tq: Test the distinctive epithet attached to a specific centre.
xs: **Machilipatnam** — option **(4)**.
It was the **first** Andhra salt satyagraha, **6 Apr 1930** (Krishna district).
**Chollangi** = Bulusu; **Vadarevu** = Kasi Viswanadham; **Mylapadu** = Bezawada Gopal Reddy.
xa: Other leaders there: **Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao**, **Mutnuri Krishna Rao**.
**Puranam Suri Sastry** bought the auctioned salt.

238.s: At Machilipatnam, who was injured while raising the flag at Tilak Chowk?
238.x: Thota Narsayya, popularly known as “Jenda Narsayya”, was injured while raising the flag at Tilak Chowk in Machilipatnam.
238.tq: Distinguish the person injured during flag-hoisting from those arrested or involved in the salt auction.
xs: **Thota Narsayya** ("**Jenda Narsayya**") — option **(3)**.
He was hurt raising the flag at **Tilak Chowk**, Machilipatnam.
**Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** was arrested; **Puranam Suri Sastry** bought the auctioned salt.
xa: He had hoisted the flag at Machilipatnam on **26 Jan 1930**.
**Venneti Satyanarayana** faced a lathi charge at **Rajahmundry**.

238.s: Venneti Satyanarayana was subjected to a lathi charge at:
238.x: Venneti Satyanarayana was subjected to a lathi charge at Rajahmundry.
238.tq: Separate the Rajahmundry incident from the Machilipatnam incident involving Thota Narsayya.
xs: **Rajahmundry** — option **(2)**.
**Machilipatnam** saw the lathi charge on **Thota Narsayya**.
xa: Venneti Satyanarayana was also with **Bulusu Sambamurthy** at **Chollangi** (**6 Apr 1930**).
**Berhampore firing** on satyagrahis: **15 Jan 1932**.

238.s:
Match List-I (Salt Satyagraha centre) with List-II (leader):
a. Chollangi (near Kakinada)
b. Vadarevu
c. Mylapadu
d. Bellary
i. Kalluri Subbarao
ii. Bezawada Gopal Reddy
iii. Kasi Viswanadham
iv. Bulusu Sambamurthy
238.x: Bulusu Sambamurthy led at Chollangi near Kakinada and Kasi Viswanadham at Vadarevu (APPSC 2023 key; option B makes the known swap). Bezawada Gopal Reddy led at Mylapadu beach in Nellore, and Kalluri Subbarao at Bellary since Rayalaseema had no coast (option C swaps these). Option D matches none.
238.tq: Bulusu = Kakinada; Kasi Viswanadham = Vadarevu
xs: **a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i** — option **(1)**.
**Chollangi** — **Bulusu Sambamurthy**; **Vadarevu** — **Kasi Viswanadham**.
**Mylapadu** — **Bezawada Gopal Reddy**; **Bellary** — **Kalluri Subbarao**.
xa: ⚠ Option (2) makes the known **Bulusu / Kasi Viswanadham** swap (APPSC **2023** key).
Mylapadu also had **Bomma Seshareddy**.

238.s: Which of the following was NOT part of the programme of the Civil Disobedience Movement in Andhra?
o: Establishing permanent provincial legislatures in every village
238.x: The programme included making salt, picketing foreign-cloth shops, cutting toddy palms, picketing toddy and arrack shops, and raiding salt depots. Establishing provincial legislatures was not part of it.
238.tq: Find the option outside the listed programme while checking each activity against its setting.
xs: **Permanent provincial legislatures in every village** was not in the programme — option **(2)**.
Programme: **make salt**, **raid salt depots**, **picket foreign-cloth shops** (towns), **cut toddy palms** (villages).
xa: Also **picketing toddy and arrack shops**.
**Eluru National School** volunteers joined in **May 1930**.

238.s: In the Andhra programme of boycott and picketing, cutting toddy palms was mainly undertaken in:
238.x: The programme assigned cutting toddy palms to villages, while foreign-cloth picketing was associated with towns.
238.tq: Compare the location-specific forms of action instead of treating all picketing activities alike.
xs: **Villages** — option **(1)**.
**Foreign-cloth picketing** was the town task.
xa: Toddy and arrack shops were also picketed.
**Eluru National School** volunteers joined in **May 1930**.

238.s: The Eluru National School volunteers joined the palm-cutting campaign in:
238.x: Eluru National School volunteers joined the palm-cutting campaign in May 1930.
238.tq: Distinguish the month of local participation from the month of the Dandi March.

xs: The Civil Disobedience Movement was revived in **January 1932** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Gandhi returned **empty-handed** from RTC-2; Viceroy **Lord Willingdon** struck first, arrested Gandhi and banned the Congress.
**July 1933** (3) is the opposite end — **mass CDM suspended** on **14 July 1933**.
xa: **15 Jan 1932**: firing at **Berhampur**; **8 May 1933**: Gandhi released.
**April 1934**: formally withdrawn; **1934**: Congress contested the **Central Assembly** elections.

239.s: The Karachi resolution is regarded as an important precursor to which portions of the Constitution of India?
o: Part I and the Schedules alone
The provisions relating only to the Union Public Service Commission
Part III and the Directive Principles of State Policy
The provisions relating only to emergency powers
239.x: The Karachi resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme foreshadowed Part III and the Directive Principles of State Policy.
239.tq: Link a historical resolution with its constitutional legacy.
xs: The Karachi resolution foreshadowed **Part III and the Directive Principles of State Policy** — so option **(3)** is correct.

Its political half (civil liberties, **universal adult franchise**, religious neutrality, free primary education) anticipates **Fundamental Rights**; its economic half (debt relief, **state control of key industries**) anticipates the **Directive Principles**.
xa: The resolution was drafted by **Jawaharlal Nehru**; the session was presided over by **Vallabhbhai Patel** (**March 1931**).
Similar constitutional link: the **Poona Pact** = root of reserved seats (**Arts. 330, 332**).

239.s: The Poona Pact is historically associated with the roots of reserved seats represented in the Constitution by
239.x: The Poona Pact is regarded as a historical root of the reservation of seats reflected in Articles 330 and 332 of the Constitution.
239.tq: Match the historical development with the relevant constitutional Articles.
xs: The **Poona Pact** is the root of reserved seats under **Articles 330 and 332** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It followed the RTC-2 deadlock over **separate electorates for minorities and the depressed classes**, after which **MacDonald** threatened a **unilateral award**.
xa: The **Karachi resolution** is the precursor of **Part III** and the **Directive Principles**.
**Ambedkar** was among the participants at RTC-2 (**1931**).

239.s: Which of the following pairs of post-Civil Disobedience Movement Telugu works and authors is correctly matched?
239.x: Bharat Swarajya Yuddham was written by Jagannadh Shastry, while Navayuga Gandhi was written by Damaraju Pundarikakshudu.
239.tq: Use the author-work pair and reject swapped authorship options.
xs: **Bharat Swarajya Yuddham** was written by **Jagannadh Shastry** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Navayuga Gandhi** was written by **Damaraju Pundarikakshudu**, so (2) and (3) swap the authors; **V.V. Jogayya Pantulu** (4) was the Andhra leader who assisted Gandhi at RTC-2.
xa: Both are **post-CDM Telugu works** listed in the AP angle of this topic.
Andhra leaders used RTC-2 to press for a **separate Andhra province**.

239.s: The only Round Table Conference that Gandhi attended was the:
239.x: Gandhi attended only the Second RTC, held in 1931. Listing the Second RTC under 1932 is a known trap; the First RTC (1930) was boycotted by the Congress and Gandhi did not attend the Third (1932).
xs: Gandhi attended only the **Second RTC, 1931** — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ Option (3) is the trap: listing the 2nd RTC under **1932** is wrong — it was **1931**.
At RTC-2 Gandhi was the **sole Congress representative**.
xa: Other participants: **Sarojini Naidu** (Indian women), **Muhammad Iqbal** (Muslims), **Malaviya**, **Ambedkar**, **Jinnah**, **Aga Khan**.
The conference ended in **deadlock**; **MacDonald** threatened a **unilateral award**.
Gandhi returned empty-handed in **Jan 1932** and the CDM was resumed.

240.s: Why did the Congress ministries resign in October–November 1939?
o: The British Government accepted the demand for immediate independence
The August Offer transferred defence to Congress
The Muslim League withdrew from all provincial governments
India was declared a belligerent in the Second World War without consultation with Indian leaders
240.x: Viceroy Linlithgow declared India a belligerent in September 1939 without consulting Indians. Congress ministries resigned in protest during October–November 1939.
240.tq: Identify the cause that explains the political action.
xs: Congress ministries resigned because **India was declared a belligerent in the Second World War without consultation** — so option **(4)** is correct.
In **Sept 1939** Viceroy **Linlithgow** dragged India into **WWII** without consulting Indians; the ministries resigned in protest in **October-November 1939**.
The **August Offer** (2) came only in **August 1940** and kept defence with Britain; no immediate independence was conceded (1).
xa: The League answered the resignations with the **"Day of Deliverance"** on **22 December 1939**.
**B.R. Ambedkar** joined the Day of Deliverance event in **Bombay**.
Sequence (UPPSC 2024 key): **Resignation of ministries → Ramgarh session → August Offer → Cripps Mission**.

240.s: Who joined the Muslim League's observance of the 'Day of Deliverance' in Bombay on 22 December 1939?
240.x: B.R. Ambedkar joined the observance of the Muslim League's Day of Deliverance in Bombay on 22 December 1939.
240.tq: Match the participant with the specific political observance.
xs: **B.R. Ambedkar** joined the League's **"Day of Deliverance"** event in **Bombay** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The League observed it on **22 December 1939**, celebrating the resignation of the **Congress ministries** (**Oct-Nov 1939**).
xa: The ministries resigned because India was dragged into the war **without consultation**.
Next on the timeline: **Ramgarh** Congress session (**March 1940**), then the **August Offer** (**August 1940**).

240.s: The August Offer of 1940 was made by:
240.x: The August Offer was made by Viceroy Lord Linlithgow in August 1940.
240.tq: Match the constitutional proposal with the Viceroy who announced it.
xs: The August Offer was made by Viceroy **Lord Linlithgow** in **August 1940** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It came when **Britain was losing in Europe**; **Sir Stafford Cripps** (3) led the separate mission of **March 1942**.
xa: Proposals: a **constitution-making body after the war**, more Indians in the **Viceroy's Executive Council**, a **War Advisory Council**.
It answered **Ramgarh** (**March 1940**) — ⚠ Ramgarh came BEFORE the Offer.
**Nehru** called Dominion Status **"dead as a doornail"**; Congress **rejected** the Offer.

240.s: Which of the following was NOT included in the August Offer?
o: Immediate transfer of defence to an Indian national government
An increase in Indian membership of the Viceroy's Executive Council
A representative constitution-making body after the war
240.x: The August Offer did not provide for immediate transfer of defence. It proposed a post-war constitution-making body, more Indians in the Executive Council and a War Advisory Council.
240.tq: Find the option that turns a limited proposal into an immediate transfer of power.
xs: **Immediate transfer of defence to an Indian national government** was not in the August Offer — so option **(1)** is correct.
The Offer proposed a representative **constitution-making body after the war** (4), more Indians in the **Viceroy's Executive Council** (3) and a **War Advisory Council** (2).
It kept **Dominion Status** as the goal with a **minority veto** — nothing on handing over defence.
xa: Made by **Lord Linlithgow** in **August 1940**, answering the **Ramgarh** offer.
⚠ Even the later **Cripps** plan kept **defence** and the army with **the British** in the interim.
Significance: **first official acceptance** that Indians would frame their own constitution.

240.s: The August Offer was significant because it constituted the first official British acceptance that:
o: Indians would frame their own constitution
Congress ministries could continue without wartime restrictions
The Muslim League alone represented Indian Muslims
240.x: The August Offer was the first official acceptance that Indians would frame their own constitution. The demand had been raised by M.N. Roy in 1934 and officially adopted by Congress in 1935.
240.tq: Identify the constitutional principle represented by the offer.
xs: The August Offer was the **first official acceptance** that **Indians would frame their own constitution** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It proposed a representative **constitution-making body after the war**.
**M.N. Roy** had raised the Constituent Assembly demand in **1934**; Congress made it official in **1935**.
xa: Other proposals: more Indians in the **Viceroy's Executive Council**; a **War Advisory Council**; Dominion Status as goal; **minority veto**.
Contrast: the **Cripps Mission** first conceded the **provincial opt-out** — germ of Partition.
Congress **rejected** the Offer; Nehru: Dominion Status **"dead as a doornail"**.

240.s: Which statement correctly describes the responses to the August Offer?
o: The Muslim League rejected it because it promised partition explicitly
Congress rejected it, while the Muslim League welcomed the minority veto but demanded more than it offered
Congress accepted it, while the Muslim League rejected the minority veto
Both Congress and the Muslim League accepted it without reservation
240.x: Congress rejected the August Offer, and Nehru described dominion status as 'dead as a doornail'. The Muslim League welcomed the minority veto but maintained that only partition would satisfy it.
240.tq: Compare the distinct responses of Congress and the Muslim League.
xs: **Congress rejected** the August Offer, while the **League welcomed the minority veto** but demanded more — option **(2)** is correct.
The League said **nothing short of partition** would satisfy it; the Offer had not promised partition, so (1) is wrong.
**Nehru** dismissed Dominion Status as **"dead as a doornail"**.
xa: The Offer was made by **Lord Linlithgow**, **August 1940**, when Britain was losing in Europe.
⚠ Cripps (**1942**) was also rejected by both Congress and League — for opposite reasons.
Congress responded to the war situation with **Individual Satyagraha** from **17 Oct 1940**.

240.s: The August Offer was made in response to which earlier Congress position?
o: Demand for a separate Muslim homeland
Demand for the immediate abolition of all provincial legislatures
Support for the war if a provisional national government were formed at the Centre
240.x: The August Offer responded to the Ramgarh Congress position that support for the war could be extended if a provisional national government were formed at the Centre.
240.tq: Connect the offer with the political demand it was intended to answer.
xs: The August Offer answered **Ramgarh**'s offer of **support for the war if a provisional national government were formed at the Centre** — so option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ **Ramgarh (March 1940)** came BEFORE the **August Offer (August 1940)**; the Cripps proposals (2) came only in **1942**.
xa: Ramgarh session was held in **Bihar**.
The Offer was made by Viceroy **Lord Linlithgow**; Congress **rejected** it.
Proposals: post-war **constitution-making body**, more Indians in the **Executive Council**, **War Advisory Council**.

240.s: Individual Satyagraha was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on:
240.x: Individual Satyagraha began on 17 October 1940.
240.tq: Distinguish the exact launch date from nearby wartime dates.
xs: Individual Satyagraha began on **17 October 1940** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**22 December 1939** (1) was the League's **Day of Deliverance**; **8 August 1942** (2) the **Quit India resolution**; **August 1940** (4) the **August Offer**.
xa: Gandhi launched it from **Paunar**, Wardha (also spelt "Palner").
Order of satyagrahis: **Vinoba Bhave** first, **Jawaharlal Nehru** second, **Brahma Dutt** third.
In **Bihar (1940)** it was led by **Shyam Narayan Singh**.

240.s: From which place did Vinoba Bhave commence Individual Satyagraha?
240.x: Vinoba Bhave commenced Individual Satyagraha from Paunar in Wardha.
240.tq: Match the movement's starting place with its associated district.
xs: Individual Satyagraha was launched from **Paunar in Wardha** (also spelt **"Palner"**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Acharya Vinoba Bhave** was the **first satyagrahi**; launch date **17 October 1940**.
**Ramgarh in Bihar** (4) was the venue of the Congress session of **March 1940**, not of the satyagraha.
xa: Second satyagrahi: **Jawaharlal Nehru**; third: **Brahma Dutt**.
Aim: assert **freedom of speech against the war**, not mass mobilisation.
The government arrested **Vinoba**, **Nehru** and **Patel**.

240.s: The immediate objective of Individual Satyagraha was to:
o: Mobilise the entire population for an armed revolt
Establish a provisional government at the Centre
Assert freedom of speech against assisting the British war effort
240.x: The movement aimed to assert freedom of speech and oppose the view that India should help the British war effort with men or money. Selected individuals made anti-war speeches and courted arrest successively.
240.tq: Apply the stated objective to distinguish limited protest from mass mobilisation.
xs: The aim was to **assert freedom of speech against the war** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was **not mass mobilisation** (1): selected individuals made **anti-war speeches** and courted arrest one after another.
Gandhi's line: **"It is wrong to help the British war effort with men or money."**
xa: Launched **17 October 1940** from **Paunar**, Wardha.
Satyagrahis in order: **Vinoba Bhave**, **Jawaharlal Nehru**, **Brahma Dutt**.
Exam angle: assertion-reason on why it was **"limited"** (**October 1940**).

240.s: In Bihar, Individual Satyagraha in 1940 was led by:
240.x: In Bihar, the 1940 Individual Satyagraha was led by Shyam Narayan Singh.
240.tq: Match the regional leadership with the correct movement and year.
xs: **Shyam Narayan Singh** led Individual Satyagraha in **Bihar (1940)** — so option **(4)** is correct (BPSC 2025 key).
**Brahma Dutt** (3) was the **third satyagrahi**; **Maulana Azad** (2) was a Congress negotiator with Cripps; **B.R. Ambedkar** (1) joined the League's Day of Deliverance.
xa: Launch: **17 October 1940**, by Gandhi from **Paunar**.
First satyagrahi: **Vinoba Bhave**; second: **Jawaharlal Nehru**.

240.s: In the Individual Satyagraha of 1940, the first, second and third satyagrahis were respectively:
o: Jawaharlal Nehru, Vinoba Bhave, Brahma Dutt
Vinoba Bhave, Jawaharlal Nehru, Brahma Dutt
Vinoba Bhave, Vallabhbhai Patel, Jawaharlal Nehru
Brahma Dutt, Vinoba Bhave, Jawaharlal Nehru
240.x: Acharya Vinoba Bhave was the first satyagrahi, Jawaharlal Nehru the second and Brahma Dutt the third (chosen for moral conviction, not political prominence). Patel was arrested but was not among the first three; the other options reorder the sequence.
240.tq: Vinoba -> Nehru -> Brahma Dutt
xs: First **Vinoba Bhave**, second **Jawaharlal Nehru**, third **Brahma Dutt** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Brahma Dutt** was chosen to show **moral conviction, not political prominence**.
**Patel** (3) was arrested along with Vinoba and Nehru but was not one of the first three.
xa: Launch: **17 October 1940** from **Paunar**, Wardha.
**Ongole Municipality** condemned the arrests of **Vinoba, Nehru and Patel**.
Nehru was also a **Cripps negotiator** and called Dominion Status **"dead as a doornail"**.

240.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Person)
a. Tanguturi Prakasam
b. Pattabhi Sitaramayya
c. Suryadevara Annapurnamma
d. Chilukuri Sattireddy

List-II (Place)
i. Tiruvuru
ii. Madras
iii. Nandigama
iv. Bandar
240.x: Tanguturi Prakasam was associated with Madras, Pattabhi Sitaramayya with Bandar, Suryadevara Annapurnamma with Nandigama and Chilukuri Sattireddy with Tiruvuru.
240.tq: Start from the sure person–place pair and eliminate codes containing a swapped location.
xs: **Prakasam – Madras**, **Pattabhi Sitaramayya – Bandar**, **Annapurnamma – Nandigama**, **Sattireddy – Tiruvuru** — so option **(1) a–ii, b–iv, c–iii, d–i** is correct.
All four were **arrested** at these places during Individual Satyagraha in Andhra.
xa: **Kala Venkat Rao** (APCC chief secretary) named **Mantena Venkata Raju** "Dictator" of the State Congress.
Mantena named **Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri**, the next dictator — also arrested.
**Ongole Municipality** condemned the arrests of **Vinoba, Nehru and Patel**.

240.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the organisation of the State Congress in Andhra during Individual Satyagraha:
1. Kala Venkat Rao was the chief secretary of the APCC.
2. Kala Venkat Rao named Mantena Venkata Raju as the ‘Dictator’ of the State Congress.
3. Mantena Venkata Raju named Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri.
4. Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri was also arrested.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
240.x: All four statements are correct. Kala Venkat Rao named Mantena Venkata Raju the State Congress ‘Dictator’, and Mantena in turn named Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri, who was arrested.
240.tq: Trace the sequence of authority and appointments carefully instead of treating the names as interchangeable.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Kala Venkat Rao**, APCC chief secretary, named **Mantena Venkata Raju** "Dictator" of the State Congress.
Mantena in turn named **Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri**, who was **also arrested**.
xa: Arrested Andhra satyagrahis: **Prakasam** (Madras), **Pattabhi** (Bandar), **Annapurnamma** (Nandigama), **Sattireddy** (Tiruvuru).
Several **MPs/MLAs** offered satyagraha in their constituencies; properties were **attached for unpaid fines**.

240.s: During Individual Satyagraha in Andhra, which of the following groups offered satyagraha in their constituencies and were arrested?
o: Suryadevara Annapurnamma, Chilukuri Sattireddy and the Ongole Municipality
Tanguturi Prakasam, Pattabhi Sitaramayya and several MPs and MLAs
Kala Venkat Rao, Mantena Venkata Raju and Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri only
Vinoba Bhave, Jawaharlal Nehru and Vallabhbhai Patel only
240.x: Tanguturi Prakasam, Pattabhi Sitaramayya and several Members of Parliament and Members of Legislative Assemblies offered satyagraha in their constituencies and were arrested.
240.tq: Identify the persons linked with the specific action rather than with the later protest against arrests.
xs: **Tanguturi Prakasam**, **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** and **several MPs and MLAs** — option **(2)** is correct.
Prakasam was arrested at **Madras**, Pattabhi at **Bandar**; MPs/MLAs offered satyagraha in their constituencies and had **properties attached** for unpaid fines.
The **Ongole Municipality** (1) only **condemned** the arrests; **Vinoba, Nehru and Patel** (4) were the national arrests.
xa: **Kala Venkat Rao** named **Mantena Venkata Raju** "Dictator", who named **Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri**.
**Suryadevara Annapurnamma** was arrested at **Nandigama**, **Chilukuri Sattireddy** at **Tiruvuru**.

240.s: Sir Stafford Cripps arrived in Delhi on which of the following dates in 1942?
240.x: Sir Stafford Cripps arrived in Delhi on 22–23 March 1942. The mission returned to Britain in mid-April after negotiations failed.
240.tq: Use the precise date rather than the broader month or year.
xs: Cripps arrived in Delhi on **22-23 March 1942** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He returned home in **mid-April** after talks broke down.
**22 December** (1) = Day of Deliverance (**1939**); **8 August** (3) = Quit India resolution (**1942**); **17 October** (4) = Individual Satyagraha (**1940**).
xa: Cripps was a **Labour Party** member of **Churchill's War Cabinet**.
Trigger: Japan's entry into the war; **Rangoon fell March 1942**.
Failure led directly to the **Quit India Movement (August 1942)**.

240.s: The Cripps Mission was sent to India by the British Government primarily under pressure from which combination of leaders?
240.x: The mission was sent by Winston Churchill's Government under pressure from United States President Franklin Roosevelt and China's Chiang Kai-shek.
240.tq: Match the political pressure with the correct international leaders.
xs: Churchill sent Cripps under pressure from US President **Roosevelt** and China's **Chiang Kai-shek** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Winston Churchill** (2) was the PM who sent the mission and was later **accused of sabotage**; **Linlithgow** made the 1940 August Offer.
**Maulana Azad** and Nehru (3, 4) were the **Congress negotiators**, not those who pressed for the mission.
xa: Trigger: **Pearl Harbor 1941**; Malaya, Singapore overrun; **Rangoon fell March 1942**.
Cripps: **Labour Party**, member of Churchill's War Cabinet, **"take it or leave it"** attitude.

240.s: Which one of the following developments most directly formed the immediate military background to the dispatch of the Cripps Mission?
o: The signing of the Desai-Liaquat Pact
The fall of Rangoon in March 1942 after Japanese advances
The opening of the Simla Conference
240.x: Japan's entry into the war, the overrunning of Malaya and Singapore, and the fall of Rangoon created the immediate military background to the mission.
240.tq: Identify the event that fits the stated wartime context.
xs: The trigger was Japan's entry into the war — **Rangoon fell March 1942** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Before that came **Pearl Harbor 1941** and the overrunning of **Malaya** and **Singapore**.
The **Desai-Liaquat Pact** (1) was only in **1945**; ministries' resignation (3) was **Oct-Nov 1939**.
xa: Churchill sent Cripps under pressure from **Roosevelt** and **Chiang Kai-shek**.
Cripps arrived in Delhi **22-23 March 1942**.
AP angle: rumours of Japanese bombing of **Vizag** and **Kakinada** during the mission.

240.s:
With reference to the Cripps proposals, consider the following statements:
1. India was promised dominion status after the war.
2. The Indian Union was to have the power to secede.
3. The transfer of defence control was to take place immediately.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
240.x: The proposals promised dominion status after the war and allowed the Indian Union to secede. Defence and control of the army were to remain with Britain during the interim period.
240.tq: Test the difference between a post-war promise and an immediate transfer of power.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: an **Indian Union with dominion status** after the war.
Statement 2 is correct: the Union would have the **power to secede**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **defence** and control of the army stayed with **the British** in the interim — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Constitution-making body: a **Constituent Assembly after the war**.
**Provincial option** to stay out — Pakistan conceded in principle, the **"fatal flaw"**.
A **treaty** was to protect racial/religious minorities; **Governor-General's powers retained**.

240.s:
With reference to the constitution-making body proposed by the Cripps Mission, consider the following statements:
1. Its provincial members were to be elected by the provincial lower houses acting as an electoral college.
2. The provincial lower houses were to elect members numbering one-tenth of their own size by proportional representation.
3. The representatives of the Princely States were also to be elected by the provincial lower houses.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
240.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the provincial lower houses formed an electoral college and elected one-tenth of their size by proportional representation. Statement 3 is wrong: the Princely States were to send nominees, not members elected by the provinces. So A is incomplete, and C and D wrongly include statement 3.
240.tq: Provinces elect (one-tenth, PR); princes nominate.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: members were elected by the **provincial lower houses** acting as an **electoral college**.
Statement 2 is correct: they elected **1/10th of their size** by **proportional representation**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the Princely States sent **nominees** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: The body was a **Constituent Assembly after the war**.
Exam angle: **March 1942**, Cripps's party (**Labour**), offer of **Dominion Status after the war**.
The **August Offer** had already accepted a post-war constitution-making body — for the first time.

240.s: Which provision of the Cripps proposals was regarded as the 'fatal flaw' because it could lead to the formation of separate unions by provinces?
o: The retention of the Governor-General's powers
The provincial option to remain outside the proposed Indian Union
The creation of a War Advisory Council
240.x: The proposal allowing unwilling provinces to form separate unions conceded the principle that later supported the demand for Pakistan and created the risk of balkanisation.
240.tq: Link a constitutional provision with its political consequence.
xs: The **provincial option to remain outside the proposed Indian Union** was the **"fatal flaw"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Any unwilling province/princely state could stay out and **form separate unions**, conceding **Pakistan in principle**.
Congress saw in it a **risk of Balkanisation**; it is called the **germ of Partition**.
xa: The **War Advisory Council** (3) belonged to the **August Offer**, not Cripps.
The **minority-protection treaty** (4) and the retained **Governor-General's powers** (1) were separate Cripps provisions.
⚠ The League still **rejected** Cripps: it wanted Pakistan conceded **explicitly**.

240.s:
Consider the following statements about the Cripps proposals:
1. Racial and religious minorities were to be protected through a treaty.
2. During the interim period, defence and control of the army were to remain with Britain.
3. During the interim period, the Governor-General's powers were to be curtailed in favour of an Indian cabinet.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
240.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: a treaty was to protect minorities, and defence and the army stayed with Britain in the interim. Statement 3 is wrong: the Governor-General's powers were retained. B misses statement 1; C and D include the false statement 3.
240.tq: Cripps interim = nothing changes now: defence with Britain, Governor-General's powers retained.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: a **treaty to protect racial/religious minorities**.
Statement 2 is correct: **defence** and control of the army stayed with **the British** in the interim.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **Governor-General's powers were retained** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Promise: **Dominion Status** with power to **secede**, after the war.
**Provincial option** to stay out — the "fatal flaw".
Congress objected to **no immediate transfer of power**.

240.s: Sir Stafford Cripps was a member of the
o: Labour Party and Churchill's War Cabinet
Liberal Party and Wavell's Executive Council
Communist Party and Churchill's War Cabinet
240.x: Cripps was a Labour member of Churchill's War Cabinet. Churchill sent him to India in 1942 under international and military pressure.
240.tq: Test the exact party and cabinet association instead of relying on the person's later political reputation.
xs: Cripps belonged to the **Labour Party** and was a member of **Churchill's War Cabinet** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He was criticised for a **"take it or leave it"** attitude.
xa: **Churchill** sent him under pressure from **Roosevelt** and **Chiang Kai-shek**; Churchill was accused of sabotage.
Cripps reached Delhi **22-23 March 1942**; returned **mid-April**.
Congress negotiators: **Nehru** and **Maulana Azad**.

240.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Congress response to the Cripps Mission:
1. Jawaharlal Nehru and Maulana Azad were the Congress negotiators.
2. The Congress objected to the right to secede.
3. The Congress objected that the proposals transferred power immediately instead of after the war.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
240.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Nehru and Azad negotiated, and Congress objected to the right to secede. Statement 3 is wrong: the objection was that there was NO immediate transfer of power. A is incomplete; C and D include statement 3.
240.tq: Congress wanted power now; Cripps offered it only after the war.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Nehru and Maulana Azad** were the Congress negotiators.
Statement 2 is correct: they objected to the **right to secede**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the objection was **no immediate transfer of power** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Congress also feared **Balkanisation** through the provincial option.
Gandhi called the offer a **"post-dated cheque"**; Nehru added **"on a crashing bank"**.
Failure led directly to the **Quit India Movement (August 1942)**.

240.s: The failure of the Cripps Mission was followed directly by which major movement?
240.x: The failure of the Cripps Mission directly contributed to the launch of the Quit India Movement in August 1942.
240.tq: Link the failed constitutional negotiation with its immediate political outcome.
xs: The failure of Cripps led directly to the **Quit India Movement (August 1942)** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Individual Satyagraha** (2) came earlier, from **17 October 1940**.
xa: The **Quit India resolution** was passed at **Bombay** on **8 Aug 1942**.
Talks broke down over Cripps's **"take it or leave it"** attitude and **Churchill's sabotage**.
Both Congress and League **rejected** the plan.

240.s: The Muslim League rejected the Cripps proposals because they:
o: provided for an explicit and immediate Pakistan
transferred all defence powers to the League
accepted the idea of a single Indian Union and did not explicitly concede Pakistan
abolished the right of provinces to remain outside the Union
240.x: The Muslim League opposed the proposed single Indian Union and wanted Pakistan to be explicitly conceded rather than left as an indirect possibility through the provincial option.
240.tq: Distinguish the League's objection from the Congress objections to the same proposals.
xs: The League rejected Cripps because it **opposed a single Indian Union** and **wanted Pakistan conceded explicitly** — option **(3)** is correct.
The plan only conceded Pakistan **in principle** through the **provincial option**, not explicitly (1).
**Defence** stayed with **the British** in the interim, not with the League (2).
xa: ⚠ Both Congress AND League rejected Cripps — Congress for **no immediate power**, the League for **no explicit Pakistan**.
At the **August Offer** the League had welcomed the **minority veto** but wanted partition.

240.s: Which of the following correctly describes the principal reactions to the Cripps proposals?
o: Congress rejected them for lack of immediate power and risk of Balkanisation; Churchill considered them too radical
Congress rejected them only because they promised full independence after the war
Congress accepted them as immediate independence and Churchill regarded them as too conservative
Both Congress and Churchill accepted them without reservation
240.x: Congress objected to the absence of immediate power and the possibility of Balkanisation. Churchill considered the proposals too radical, while many Indians regarded them as too conservative.
240.tq: Compare the reasons for rejection from both sides and eliminate the reversed reactions.
xs: Congress rejected Cripps for **no immediate power** and **risk of Balkanisation**, and **Churchill** found it **too radical** — option **(1)** is correct.
The plan was **"too radical for Churchill, too conservative for Indians"** — rejected by all sides.
It promised **Dominion Status after the war**, not full independence (2), and was not accepted by anyone (4).
xa: Congress negotiators **Nehru and Maulana Azad** also objected to the **right to secede**.
The **League** rejected it for not conceding Pakistan explicitly.
Result: the **Quit India Movement (August 1942)**.

240.s: Gandhi's description of the Cripps proposals as a 'post-dated cheque' was famously extended by Nehru with the words:
240.x: Gandhi called the Cripps offer a 'post-dated cheque' and Nehru added 'on a crashing bank' (some sources give the whole phrase to Gandhi, with 'failing bank'). 'Dead as a doornail' was Nehru's verdict on Dominion Status in the August Offer; the other two phrases are not tied to Cripps.
240.tq: Cripps = post-dated cheque on a crashing bank
xs: Gandhi called the Cripps offer a **"post-dated cheque"** and Nehru added **"on a crashing bank"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Some notes give the whole phrase to Gandhi, with **"failing bank"**.
⚠ **"Dead as a doornail"** (1) was **Nehru** on Dominion Status in the **August Offer**.
xa: Cripps was criticised for a **"take it or leave it"** attitude.
Gandhi on Individual Satyagraha: **"It is wrong to help the British war effort with men or money."**

240.s: Which one of the following correctly matches an event with its date?
o: Muslim League's Day of Deliverance — 22 December 1939
240.x: The Muslim League observed the Day of Deliverance on 22 December 1939. Individual Satyagraha began in October 1940, the August Offer was made in August 1940, and the Quit India resolution was passed on 8 August 1942.
240.tq: Match each event with its exact date and reject shifted dates.
xs: **Day of Deliverance — 22 December 1939** is the correct match — option **(1)**.
**Individual Satyagraha** began **17 Oct 1940**, not March 1940 (2); **March 1940** was the **Ramgarh** session.
The **August Offer** was **August 1940** (3); the **Quit India resolution** was **8 Aug 1942** (4).
xa: **B.R. Ambedkar** joined the Day of Deliverance in **Bombay**.
**Cripps Mission**: **March-April 1942**; **Cabinet Mission**: **March 1946**.

240.s: The sequence beginning with the resignation of Congress ministries and ending with the Cripps Mission is correctly represented by:
o: Resignation of ministries → Ramgarh Congress session → August Offer → Cripps Mission
Ramgarh Congress session → resignation of ministries → Cripps Mission → August Offer
August Offer → resignation of ministries → Ramgarh Congress session → Cripps Mission
Cripps Mission → August Offer → Ramgarh Congress session → resignation of ministries
240.x: The sequence was resignation of Congress ministries in October–November 1939, Ramgarh session in March 1940, August Offer in August 1940 and Cripps Mission in March–April 1942.
240.tq: Fix the first event and then place the later wartime developments.
xs: **Resignation of ministries → Ramgarh → August Offer → Cripps Mission** — option **(1)** is correct (UPPSC 2024 key).
Dates: resignation **Oct-Nov 1939**; Ramgarh **March 1940**; August Offer **August 1940**; Cripps **March-April 1942**.
⚠ **Ramgarh** came BEFORE the **August Offer** — the Offer answered Ramgarh.
xa: Next: **Quit India resolution**, **8 Aug 1942**, Bombay; **Desai-Liaquat Pact**, **1945**.
**Cabinet Mission**: **March 1946**.

240.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the resignation of the Congress ministries in 1939:
1. Lord Linlithgow declared India to be a party to the Second World War.
2. Indian leaders were not consulted before the declaration.
3. The Muslim League observed 22 December 1939 as Deliverance Day.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
240.x: All three statements are correct. Linlithgow made the declaration without consulting Indian leaders, and the League observed the Congress resignations as Deliverance Day on 22 December 1939.
240.tq: Check each statement against the cause, authority and consequence of the resignations.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
In **Sept 1939** Viceroy **Linlithgow** declared India a **belligerent** in **WWII** without consulting Indians.
The League observed **22 December 1939** as **"Day of Deliverance"**.
xa: The Congress ministries resigned in **October-November 1939** in protest.
**B.R. Ambedkar** joined the Day of Deliverance event in **Bombay**.

240.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. August Offer
B. Individual Satyagraha begins
C. Quit India incidents at Tenali
D. Royal Indian Navy Mutiny
240.x: The sequence is August Offer in August 1940, Individual Satyagraha in October 1940, Tenali events in August 1942, and the RIN Mutiny in February 1946.
240.tq: Fix the sequence using the years first and then compare events within the freedom struggle.
xs: **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)** is correct.
**August Offer**: **August 1940**; **Individual Satyagraha** began **17 Oct 1940** — two months later.
The **Quit India resolution** came on **8 Aug 1942**, so the **Tenali** incidents follow it; the **RIN Mutiny** came later still.
xa: Between them: **Cripps Mission**, **March-April 1942**.
Later: **Desai-Liaquat Pact** (**1945**), **Cabinet Mission** (**March 1946**).

240.s: The Cripps Mission reached Delhi on
240.x: Sir Stafford Cripps reached Delhi on 23 March 1942. The mission was sent by Churchill under pressure from Roosevelt and Chiang Kai-shek after Japan's advance.
240.tq: Use the exact arrival date to separate the mission from the later Quit India Movement.
xs: Cripps arrived in Delhi on **22-23 March 1942** — so option **(2) 23 March 1942** is correct.
Option (4) has the wrong year: the mission was in **1942**, not **1940**; **8 August 1942** (3) was the **Quit India resolution**.
xa: Sent by **Churchill** under pressure from **Roosevelt** and **Chiang Kai-shek**.
Background: **Rangoon fell March 1942**.
Cripps returned home in **mid-April** after talks broke down.

240.s: The Quit India resolution was passed on 8 August 1942 at:
240.x: The Quit India resolution was passed at Bombay on 8 August 1942.
240.tq: 8-8-42, Bombay: Gowalia Tank.
xs: The **Quit India resolution** was passed at **Bombay** on **8 Aug 1942** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Wardha** (1) is linked to **Paunar**, where Gandhi launched **Individual Satyagraha** in **1940**.
xa: The failure of the **Cripps Mission** led directly to Quit India.
Gandhi had used "Quit India" in **Harijan** in **April 1942**, amid rumours of Japanese bombing of **Vizag** and **Kakinada**.

240.s: The Desai–Liaquat Pact was concluded in:
240.x: The Desai–Liaquat Pact was concluded in January 1945. August 1940 was the August Offer, March 1942 the Cripps Mission and March 1946 the Cabinet Mission.
240.tq: Desai–Liaquat opened 1945, months before the war ended.
xs: The **Desai-Liaquat Pact** was concluded in **January 1945** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**August 1940** = **August Offer**; **March 1942** = **Cripps Mission**; **March 1946** = **Cabinet Mission**.
xa: **8 Aug 1942**: Quit India resolution at **Bombay**.
**22 Dec 1939**: League's **Day of Deliverance**.

240.s: The Cabinet Mission arrived in India in:
240.x: The Cabinet Mission came in March 1946. March 1942 was the Cripps Mission, January 1945 the Desai–Liaquat Pact and August 1942 the Quit India resolution.
240.tq: Cripps March 42, Cabinet March 46.
xs: The **Cabinet Mission** came in **March 1946** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**March 1942** = **Cripps Mission**; **January 1945** = **Desai-Liaquat Pact**; **August 1942** = **Quit India resolution**.
xa: Cripps arrived in Delhi **22-23 March 1942**.
⚠ Don't confuse the two "March" missions: Cripps **1942**, Cabinet **1946**.

240.s: Which one of the following correctly expresses the distinctive significance of the August Offer and the Cripps Mission?
o: The August Offer created the provincial opt-out principle, whereas the Cripps Mission introduced separate electorates.
The August Offer first conceded provincial opt-out, whereas the Cripps Mission first accepted a post-war constitution-making body.
The August Offer first accepted a post-war constitution-making body, whereas the Cripps Mission first conceded the provincial option to opt out.
Both the August Offer and the Cripps Mission rejected the idea of a post-war constitution-making body.
240.x: The August Offer marked the first acceptance of a post-war constitution-making body. The Cripps Mission first conceded the possibility of provincial opt-out, regarded as the germ of Partition.
240.tq: Compare the two proposals by assigning each distinctive concession to the correct one.
xs: The **August Offer** first accepted a **post-war constitution-making body**; the **Cripps Mission** first conceded **provincial opt-out** — option **(3)** is correct.
Option (2) swaps the two; the August Offer was the **first official acceptance** that Indians would frame their own constitution.
Cripps's opt-out is called the **germ of Partition** and the **"fatal flaw"**.
xa: The August Offer also offered a **War Advisory Council** and more Indians in the **Executive Council**.
Cripps's body: elected by **provincial lower houses** (**1/10th** of their size, proportional representation) plus **Princely State nominees**.

240.s: During the Cripps Mission, which combination of circumstances led Mahatma Gandhi to use the phrase ‘Quit India’ in Harijan?
o: The arrest of Andhra satyagrahis in Madras and Bandar; the phrase appeared in Harijan in August 1942.
The bombing of Pearl Harbor; the phrase appeared in Harijan in March 1940.
Rumours of Japanese bombing of Vizag and Kakinada; the phrase appeared in Harijan in April 1942.
The rejection of the August Offer by the Congress; the phrase appeared in Harijan in December 1941.
240.x: Rumours of Japanese bombing of Vizag and Kakinada during the Cripps Mission led Gandhi to use the phrase ‘Quit India’ in Harijan in April 1942.
240.tq: Link the event, geographical locations and publication date instead of relying on the familiar Quit India year alone.
xs: **Rumours of Japanese bombing of Vizag and Kakinada** made Gandhi use "Quit India" in **Harijan** in **April 1942** — option **(3)** is correct.
This happened **during the Cripps Mission** (**March-April 1942**).
xa: The **Quit India resolution** followed on **8 Aug 1942** at **Bombay**.
Background: Japan's entry into the war — **Pearl Harbor 1941**, **Rangoon fell March 1942**.
Andhra arrests at **Madras** (Prakasam) and **Bandar** (Pattabhi) belong to **Individual Satyagraha**, not Cripps.

240.s: The provincial opt-out conceded by the Cripps Mission was regarded as the germ of which later development?
o: The establishment of the Constituent Assembly
240.x: The Cripps Mission’s concession that provinces could opt out of the proposed union was regarded as the germ of the Partition of India.
240.tq: Connect the constitutional concession with its stated historical consequence.
xs: The Cripps provincial opt-out is regarded as the **germ of Partition** — so option **(4) The Partition of India** is correct.
It let unwilling provinces/princely states **form separate unions** — Pakistan conceded in principle.
Congress rejected it fearing **Balkanisation**; it is called the **"fatal flaw"**.
xa: The **August Offer** first accepted a **post-war constitution-making body**.
⚠ The League still rejected Cripps — it wanted Pakistan conceded **explicitly**.

241.s: The immediate failure of the Cripps Mission contributed to the Quit India Movement mainly because the Mission offered
o: A separate province for every linguistic group
241.x: The Cripps Mission failed to satisfy Indian demands because it did not offer immediate self-government. Its failure in March–April 1942 became a major cause of the Quit India Movement.
241.tq: Identify the precise deficiency in a political proposal rather than its general historical association.
xs: The Cripps Mission offered **no immediate self-government** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Its failure in **March-April 1942** became a direct cause of Quit India (UPSC 2013: launched in response to the **Cripps Proposals**).
xa: Other causes: the **Japanese advance** (Malaya, Singapore overrun; **Rangoon** fell **March 1942**) and **economic distress** (rising prices, wartime shortages).
**14 July 1942**: CWC resolution at **Wardha**; **8 August 1942**: AICC ratified it at **Gowalia Tank Maidan**, Bombay.
**9 August 1942**: leaders arrested in **Operation Zero Hour**.

241.s:
Consider the following events:
1. Fall of Rangoon
2. Overrunning of Singapore
3. Advance of Japanese forces towards India’s eastern frontier
Which of the above created an important wartime background to the Quit India Movement?
241.x: All three developments formed part of the Japanese advance in the East. Rangoon fell in March 1942, and Japanese expansion brought the war close to India’s eastern frontier.
241.tq: Recognise that multiple connected military developments contributed to the same historical cause.
xs: All three formed the wartime background — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The Japanese overran **Malaya** and **Singapore**; **Rangoon** fell in **March 1942**.
The Japanese then stood at India's **eastern frontier**, with rumours of bombing of **Vizag** and **Kakinada**.
xa: Other causes: failure of the **Cripps Mission** (no immediate self-government) and **economic distress**.
Economic distress meant **rising prices** and **wartime shortages**.

241.s: Rumours of bombing during the Japanese advance were particularly associated with which places in India?
241.x: The Japanese advance generated rumours of bombing at Vizag and Kakinada, adding to the sense of wartime insecurity in India.
241.tq: Test a specific pair of places rather than the broader military event.
xs: Rumours of Japanese bombing centred on **Vizag and Kakinada** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They arose as the Japanese, after taking **Rangoon** (**March 1942**), reached India's **eastern frontier**.
xa: At **Kakinada**, lawyers later passed a resolution **demanding Gandhi's release**.
The Japanese advance was one of three causes, with the **Cripps failure** and **economic distress**.

241.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Quit India resolutions:
1. The Congress Working Committee adopted a resolution at Wardha on 14 July 1942.
2. The Wardha resolution was proposed by Jawaharlal Nehru and seconded by Sardar Patel.
3. The All India Congress Committee ratified the resolution at Bombay on 8 August 1942.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
241.x: All three statements are correct. The CWC resolution was passed at Wardha on 14 July 1942, and the AICC ratified it at Bombay on 8 August 1942.
241.tq: Separate the preliminary CWC decision from the later AICC ratification using dates and venue.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**14 July 1942**: CWC resolution at **Wardha**, proposed by **Nehru** and seconded by **Patel**.
**8 August 1942**: **AICC, Bombay**, at **Gowalia Tank Maidan**, ratified it.
xa: Hence the names **"Wardha Resolution"** and **"August Resolution"**.
**9 August 1942**: pre-dawn arrests in **Operation Zero Hour**.
The Wardha resolution empowered **Gandhi** to lead a **non-violent mass movement**.

241.s: What authority was Gandhi given by the Wardha resolution of 14 July 1942?
o: Authority to negotiate a dominion constitution with the British Government
Authority to suspend all provincial Congress committees
Authority to form a provisional government immediately
Authority to lead a non-violent mass movement
241.x: The Wardha resolution empowered Mahatma Gandhi to lead a non-violent mass movement against British rule.
241.tq: Identify the precise power or responsibility conferred by a political resolution.
xs: The Wardha resolution empowered Gandhi to **lead a non-violent mass movement** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **provisional government** (3) was to come only **after the British left**, as the AICC Bombay resolution said.
xa: Proposed by **Nehru**, seconded by **Patel**; also called the **"August Resolution"**.
AICC, Bombay demands: **immediate end of British rule**, provisional government, **mass civil disobedience** under Gandhi.

241.s: Which of the following was NOT a demand or feature of the resolution ratified by the AICC in August 1942?
o: Mass civil disobedience under Gandhi’s leadership
Continuation of British rule until the end of the Second World War
Formation of a provisional government after the British withdrawal
241.x: The resolution demanded the immediate end of British rule, envisaged a provisional government after withdrawal and authorised mass civil disobedience under Gandhi. It did not support continuation of British rule until the war ended.
241.tq: Reject the option that reverses the central demand of the resolution.
xs: **Continuation of British rule until the end of the war** was never demanded — so option **(3)** is the odd one out.
The AICC, Bombay demanded the **immediate end of British rule**, a **provisional government after the British left**, and **mass civil disobedience under Gandhi**.
xa: The AICC met on **8 August 1942** at **Gowalia Tank Maidan**.
It ratified the CWC's **Wardha** resolution of **14 July 1942**.
Gandhi's speech there: **"Do or Die"** ("Karo ya Maro").

241.s:
Consider the following statements about Gandhi's instructions during the Quit India Movement:
1. Government servants were to resign from service immediately.
2. Soldiers were not to fire on Indians.
3. Peasants were to withhold rent from pro-government zamindars.
4. Princes were to support the people.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
241.x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: government servants were told to stay in service but pledge loyalty to the Congress. A, C and D all include the false statement 1.
241.tq: Officials: stay, but pledge loyalty to Congress - not resign.
xs: Statement 1 is wrong: government servants were to **stay in service but pledge loyalty to Congress**.

Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct: **soldiers** not to fire on Indians; **peasants** to withhold rent from pro-government zamindars; **princes** to support the people — so **2, 3 and 4 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **Students** were told they **may leave studies**.
The instructions accompanied the **AICC, Bombay** resolution of **8 August 1942**.

241.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the origin of the slogan “Quit India”?
o: The phrase was suggested by Mahatma Gandhi in Harijan in April 1942, while its coinage is generally credited to Yusuf Meherally
It was coined by Mahatma Gandhi in Young India in 1942
It was coined by Jawaharlal Nehru at the Wardha meeting in July 1942
It was first used by Subhas Chandra Bose in a broadcast from Germany
241.x: Gandhi suggested the phrase in Harijan in April 1942, whereas Yusuf Meherally is generally credited with coining it. Young India had ceased publication in 1932.
241.tq: Distinguish the person who suggested a phrase from the person generally credited with coining it.
xs: Gandhi suggested the phrase in **Harijan** (**April 1942**); its coinage is usually credited to **Yusuf Meherally** — option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ **Young India** (2) had ceased in **1932**; Gandhi's paper in **1942** was **Harijan**.
xa: The Harijan use came amid rumours of Japanese bombing of **Vizag** and **Kakinada**.
**"Do or Die"** ("Karo ya Maro") was Gandhi's slogan at **Gowalia Tank**, **8 Aug 1942**.

241.s:
With reference to the slogan “Do or Die”, consider the following statements:
1. It was associated with Mahatma Gandhi.
2. It was delivered in the Gowalia Tank speech on 8 August 1942.
3. It was announced through Young India in 1942.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
241.x: Gandhi used “Do or Die” in his Gowalia Tank speech on 8 August 1942. Statement 3 is false because Gandhi’s paper in 1942 was Harijan; Young India had ceased publication in 1932.
241.tq: Use the publication-title trap to separate a true slogan association from a false source attribution.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: **"Do or Die"** is **Mahatma Gandhi**'s, from the **Gowalia Tank speech**, **8 Aug 1942**.
Statement 3 is wrong: ⚠ Gandhi's paper in **1942** was **Harijan**; **Young India** had ceased in **1932** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Same speech: **"We shall either free India or die in the attempt"** (BPSC 2025).
"Quit India" was suggested by Gandhi in **Harijan** (**April 1942**); coinage credited to **Yusuf Meherally**.

241.s: Who said, "We shall either free India or die in the attempt"?
241.x: Mahatma Gandhi said it in his Gowalia Tank speech of 8 August 1942, the same speech in which he gave the call "Do or Die".
241.tq: It is just "Do or Die" spelt out in full.
xs: **Mahatma Gandhi** said it in his **Gowalia Tank** speech of **8 Aug 1942** — so option **(4)** is correct (BPSC 2025).
In the same speech he gave the call **"Do or Die"** ("Karo ya Maro").
xa: The **AICC, Bombay** ratified the Quit India resolution that day.
The Wardha resolution was **proposed by Nehru**, **seconded by Patel**.

241.s: The immediate arrest of the principal Congress leaders on 9 August 1942 resulted in the movement becoming
o: A movement controlled by the Muslim League
Confined exclusively to the princely states
241.x: The leaders were arrested pre-emptively on 9 August 1942. Consequently, the movement became largely leaderless and spontaneous.
241.tq: Link a political action with its immediate organisational consequence.
xs: The pre-dawn arrests of **9 August 1942** made the movement **leaderless and spontaneous** — option **(2)** is correct.
The arrests were code-named **Operation Zero Hour**.
xa: **CWC members** were held at **Ahmednagar Fort**.
