Underground leaders took over: **JP** (**Azad Dasta**), **Lohia** and **Usha Mehta** (**Congress Radio**), **Aruna Asaf Ali**.
Viceroy **Lord Linlithgow** called it the most serious rebellion since **1857**.

241.s: Operation Zero Hour during the Quit India Movement referred to
o: The pre-dawn arrest of Congress leaders on 9 August 1942
The imposition of a 21-day fast by Gandhi
The formation of Jatiya Sarkar at Tamluk
241.x: Operation Zero Hour was the pre-dawn operation through which Congress leaders were arrested on 9 August 1942.
241.tq: Match an operation name with its precise action and date.
xs: **Operation Zero Hour** was the **pre-dawn arrest of Congress leaders on 9 August 1942** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **fall of Rangoon** (1) was in **March 1942**; **Gandhi's 21-day fast** (3) was in **February 1943**; **Jatiya Sarkar** (4) was at **Tamluk**.
xa: After the arrests the movement became **leaderless and spontaneous**.
**CWC members** were held at **Ahmednagar Fort**.

241.s: Who was the Viceroy of India during the Quit India Movement?
241.x: Lord Linlithgow was the Viceroy of India during the Quit India Movement and directed the colonial response to it.
241.tq: Use the office-holder trap by distinguishing neighbouring Viceroy tenures.
xs: The Viceroy was **Lord Linlithgow** — so option **(4)** is correct.
He called Quit India the **most serious rebellion since 1857**.
xa: Repression: about **10,000 deaths**, floggings, **collective fines**, military control of cities.
Gandhi's **21-day fast** (**February 1943**) at the **Aga Khan Palace** led three members of the **Viceroy's Executive Council** to resign.

241.s: Kasturba Gandhi died in detention at Poona in
241.x: Kasturba Gandhi died in detention at Poona in 1944 while Gandhi was held at the Aga Khan Palace.
241.tq: Test a close chronological detail using neighbouring years as distractors.
xs: **Kasturba Gandhi** died in detention at **Poona** in **1944** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Gandhi was held at the **Aga Khan Palace**, where he fasted **21 days** in **February 1943**.
xa: **CWC members** were held at **Ahmednagar Fort**.
Viceroy: **Lord Linlithgow**.

241.s:
Which of the following combinations correctly describes the repression of the Quit India Movement?
1. About 10,000 deaths occurred.
2. Floggings were used by the authorities.
3. Collective fines were imposed.
4. Military control was imposed in cities.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
241.x: The repression involved approximately 10,000 deaths, flogging, collective fines and military control of cities.
241.tq: Combine numerical and administrative features of repression into a comprehensive statement question.
xs: All four are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
The toll: about **10,000 deaths**, **floggings**, **collective fines** and **military control of cities**.
xa: Viceroy **Lord Linlithgow** called it the most serious rebellion since **1857**.
Andhra collective fine: **Akividu** (W. Godavari) = **Rs 6,000**.
Exempted from fines: **Muslims**, **Christians**, **SCs**, government staff.

241.s:
Consider the following statements about Gandhi’s fast during the Quit India phase:
1. It lasted for 21 days.
2. It began in February 1943.
3. It was undertaken at the Aga Khan Palace against state violence.
4. Three members of the Viceroy’s Executive Council resigned in this context.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
241.x: All four statements are correct. Gandhi undertook a 21-day fast at the Aga Khan Palace from February 1943 in protest against state violence, and three members of the Viceroy’s Executive Council resigned in this context.
241.tq: Check duration, date, place, purpose and consequence as separate factual elements.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Gandhi's **21-day fast**, **February 1943**, at the **Aga Khan Palace**, was against **state violence**.
Its effect: **three members** of the **Viceroy's Executive Council** resigned.
xa: **Kasturba Gandhi** died in detention at **Poona** (**1944**).
**CWC members** were held at **Ahmednagar Fort**.

241.s: Who among the following organised sabotage and formed the Azad Dasta during the Quit India Movement?
241.x: Jayaprakash Narayan organised sabotage and formed the Azad Dasta during the Quit India Movement.
241.tq: Match a named underground organisation with its organiser.
xs: **Jayaprakash Narayan** organised sabotage and formed the **Azad Dasta** — so option **(2)** is correct (BPSC 2025 key).
**Ram Manohar Lohia** (1) was an underground leader who broadcast on the **Congress Radio**.
**Biju Patnaik** and **Achyut Patwardhan** (3, 4) were other underground figures.
xa: ⚠ **Azad Dasta** = **JP**; **Congress Radio** = **Usha Mehta**.
**Aruna Asaf Ali**: flag-hoisting and underground network.
Sabotage hit bridges, rail tracks, telegraph lines — especially **UP** and **Bihar**.

241.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Aruna Asaf Ali — Flag-hoisting and underground network
Ram Manohar Lohia — Underground leadership and Congress Radio broadcasts
241.x: Jayaprakash Narayan was an underground leader who organised sabotage and formed the Azad Dasta; he was not a member of the Viceroy’s Executive Council.
241.tq: Find the wrong institutional association among otherwise plausible underground activities.
xs: **Jayaprakash Narayan — Viceroy's Executive Council** is wrong: JP organised **sabotage** and formed the **Azad Dasta** — so option **(4)** is the mismatch.
The other pairs are right: **Aruna Asaf Ali** — flag-hoisting; **Lohia** — Congress Radio broadcasts; **Usha Mehta** — **Congress Radio**.
xa: Three members of the **Viceroy's Executive Council** resigned over Gandhi's **21-day fast**.
Other underground figures: **Biju Patnaik**, **Sucheta Kripalani**, **Achyut Patwardhan**, **R.P. Goenka**.

241.s: During the Quit India Movement, sabotage was especially directed against
o: Bridges, railway tracks and telegraph lines
Universities, courts and municipal libraries only
241.x: Underground activists sabotaged bridges, railway tracks and telegraph lines, particularly in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
241.tq: Identify the infrastructure targets that disrupted colonial administration and communication.
xs: Sabotage targeted **bridges, rail tracks and telegraph lines** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was strongest in **UP** and **Bihar**.
xa: **Jayaprakash Narayan** organised sabotage through the **Azad Dasta**.
Andhra: lines between **Guntur and Vijayawada** torn up; **Chirala** signal wires cut.
Tenali: the **Madras-Puri passenger train** burnt at the station.

241.s: Which one of the following statements about the parallel government at Ballia is correct?
o: It was led by Chittu Pandey and lasted for about a week
It was led by Nana Patil and continued until 1945
It was organised by the Young Congress Socialists on a ward-wise basis
It was called Jatiya Sarkar and functioned until September 1944
241.x: The Ballia parallel government was led by Chittu Pandey in August 1942 and lasted approximately one week. The other descriptions relate to Satara, Tamluk and Ahmedabad respectively.
241.tq: Apply the wrong-leader and swapped-location traps to distinguish parallel governments.
xs: The **Ballia** (UP) parallel government was led by **Chittu Pandey** and lasted **about a week** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Nana Patil** to **1945** (2) is **Satara**; ward-wise **Young Congress Socialists** (3) is **Ahmedabad**; **Jatiya Sarkar** to **Sept 1944** (4) is **Tamluk**.
xa: Ballia (**Aug 1942**) **freed Congress leaders**.
⚠ **Ballia** = shortest; **Satara** = longest.

241.s: Jatiya Sarkar, which undertook cyclone relief, school grants and paddy distribution, was established at
241.x: Jatiya Sarkar was formed at Tamluk in Midnapore, Bengal. Its activities included cyclone relief, school grants and distribution of paddy.
241.tq: Match a distinctive programme of activities with its place of operation.
xs: **Jatiya Sarkar** was set up at **Tamluk in Midnapore**, Bengal — option **(4)** is correct.
It ran **Dec 1942 - Sept 1944**, with cyclone relief, school grants, paddy distribution and **Vidyut Vahinis**.
**Satara** (1) had the **"Prati Sarkar"**; **Ballia** (3) was under **Chittu Pandey**.
xa: Satara (**Y.B. Chavan**, **Nana Patil**) was the longest, mid-**1943** to **1945**.
**Talcher** (Odisha) also had a parallel government in **1942**.

241.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Satara Prati Sarkar is NOT correct?
o: It was the longest-lasting of the parallel governments
It was established at Tamluk and remained active until September 1944
It functioned roughly from the middle of 1943 to 1945
It was associated with Y.B. Chavan and Nana Patil
241.x: The Satara Prati Sarkar was associated with Y.B. Chavan and Nana Patil and functioned from mid-1943 to 1945. Tamluk was the location of Jatiya Sarkar, active from December 1942 to September 1944.
241.tq: Find the swapped place and duration in a not-correctly-matched question.
xs: Satara's Prati Sarkar was **not** at **Tamluk**, and did not end in **September 1944** — so option **(2)** is the incorrect statement.
Tamluk's **Jatiya Sarkar** ran **Dec 1942 - Sept 1944**.
Satara (**Y.B. Chavan**, **Nana Patil**) ran **mid-1943 - 1945** and was the **longest** — (1), (3), (4) are correct.
xa: Satara ran **Nyayadan Mandals** (people's courts), village libraries, prohibition, **"Gandhi marriages"**.
APPSC 2016 asked where **"Prati Sarkar"** was formed — **Satara**.

241.s: Which one of the following was associated with the functioning of the Prati Sarkar in Satara?
o: The release of Congress leaders for approximately one week
Ward-wise taxation and policing by Young Congress Socialists
241.x: Satara’s Prati Sarkar developed Nyayadan Mandals and village libraries and also promoted prohibition and “Gandhi marriages”.
241.tq: Identify the distinctive administrative and social measures of a parallel government.
xs: Satara's Prati Sarkar ran **Nyayadan Mandals** (people's courts) and **village libraries** — option **(3)** is correct.
Freeing leaders for a week (1) = **Ballia**; cyclone relief and paddy (2) = **Tamluk**; ward-wise taxes and policing (4) = **Ahmedabad**.
xa: Satara also enforced **prohibition** and promoted **"Gandhi marriages"**.
Leaders: **Y.B. Chavan**, **Nana Patil**; mid-**1943** to **1945** — the longest.

241.s: The Kurnool (Andhra) Circular, issued on 29 July 1942 during the Quit India Movement, was drafted by whom?
241.x: The Kurnool (Andhra) Circular was drafted by Kala Venkat Rao on 29 July 1942. It was subsequently seized by the police at Kurnool.
241.tq: Use the author–document trap by distinguishing the drafter from other Andhra leaders.
xs: The **Kurnool (Andhra) Circular** (**29 July 1942**) was drafted by **Kala Venkat Rao** — option **(4)** is correct.
It was **seized by police at Kurnool**.
**Mamidipudi Venkatrangayya** (1) led the **Andhra University** resolution; **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** (3) presided over the **APCC meeting at Machilipatnam**.
xa: Pattabhi was jailed at **Ahmednagar Fort** and wrote **"Feathers and Stones"**.
**Tanguturi Prakasam** emerged as Andhra's leading figure.

241.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Place)
a. Tenali
b. Guntur
c. Bhimavaram
d. Kakinada

List-II (Incident)
i. Lawyers passed a resolution demanding Gandhi’s release
ii. Police firing on 13 August 1942
iii. Police firing on 12 August 1942 and burning of the Madras–Puri passenger train
iv. Firing on 17 August 1942 and attack on the Collectorate

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
241.x: Tenali witnessed firing on 12 August and the burning of the Madras–Puri passenger train; Guntur witnessed firing on 13 August; Bhimavaram witnessed firing on 17 August and an attack on the Collectorate; and Kakinada lawyers demanded Gandhi’s release.
241.tq: Start from the sure place–incident pairs and eliminate codes containing a swapped event.
xs: **Tenali – iii**, **Guntur – ii**, **Bhimavaram – iv**, **Kakinada – i** — option **(1)** is correct.
Tenali: firing **12 Aug 1942** (about **9** killed), **Madras-Puri train** burnt; Guntur: firing **13 Aug**.
Bhimavaram: firing **17 Aug** and attack on the **Collectorate**; Kakinada: lawyers demanded **Gandhi's release**.
xa: **Bapatla** railway station burnt; **Chirala** signal wires cut; **Tadepalligudem** post office burnt.
Rail lines between **Guntur and Vijayawada** torn up.

241.s:
In the imposition of collective fines in Andhra during the Quit India Movement, which of the following groups were exempted?
1. Muslims
2. Christians
3. Scheduled Castes
4. Government employees

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
241.x: Muslims, Christians, Scheduled Castes and government employees were exempted from the collective fines.
241.tq: Check the complete composition of the exempted groups before choosing the inclusive code.
xs: All four were exempted — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Exempted: **Muslims**, **Christians**, **Scheduled Castes (SCs)** and **government employees**.
xa: Fine on **Akividu** (W. Godavari): **Rs 6,000**.
**N.G. Ranga**'s grain was seized at **Nidudavolu**.
Muslims generally **sheltered activists**; there were **no communal clashes**.

241.s: The underground paper circulated in Andhra during the Quit India Movement carried which of the following messages?
o: Vande Mataram and Do or Die
241.x: The underground paper titled “Quit India” circulated the message “Rahasya Udyamam Saginchandi.”
241.tq: Test the exact wording of an underground publication instead of substituting a famous national slogan.
xs: The underground paper **"Quit India"** circulated **"Rahasya Udyamam Saginchandi"** — option **(1)** is correct.
**"Do or Die"** (3) was Gandhi's Gowalia Tank slogan, not this paper's message.
xa: The **Kurnool Circular** (**29 July 1942**) was drafted by **Kala Venkat Rao**.
Andhra Quit India is called the **"final, decisive event of the freedom struggle in Andhra"**.

241.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bhimavaram — Attack on the Collectorate on 17 August 1942
Chirala — Burning of the post office
241.x: Chirala was associated with the cutting of signal wires. The post office was burnt at Tadepalligudem.
241.tq: Find the location swap among closely related Quit India incidents.
xs: **Chirala — burning of the post office** is wrong: Chirala saw **signal wires cut**; the post office was burnt at **Tadepalligudem** — option **(4)**.
The others are right: **Bhimavaram** firing **17 Aug** and Collectorate attack; **Tenali** firing **12 Aug**; **Guntur** firing **13 Aug**.
xa: **Bapatla** railway station burnt.
**Kakinada** lawyers demanded **Gandhi's release**.

241.s: Pattabhi Sitaramayya was jailed at which place during the Quit India Movement, where he wrote the diary titled ‘Feathers and Stones’?
241.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya was imprisoned at Ahmednagar Fort and wrote ‘Feathers and Stones’ there.
241.tq: Use the place–work pairing and avoid confusing different colonial prisons.
xs: **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** was jailed at **Ahmednagar Fort**, where he wrote **"Feathers and Stones"** — option **(1)** is correct.
**CWC members** were held at Ahmednagar Fort.
xa: Pattabhi presided over the **APCC meeting** at **Machilipatnam**.
Gandhi was held at the **Aga Khan Palace**; **Kasturba** died at **Poona** (**1944**).

241.s: Why did the Communist Party of India oppose the Quit India Movement in 1942?
o: It considered the movement an exclusively provincial movement in Andhra.
It supported the Muslim League’s demand for Pakistan from the beginning of the war.
It supported the British war effort after Nazi Germany attacked the Soviet Union.
It had already withdrawn from Indian politics after the Civil Disobedience Movement.
241.x: The Communists opposed the Quit India Movement because, after the Nazi attack on the Soviet Union, they backed the British war effort.
241.tq: Identify the cause–attitude link rather than confusing Communist policy with the position of the Muslim League.
xs: The **Communists** backed the British war effort after the **Nazi attack on the USSR** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **CPI ban** was lifted on **23 July 1942**.
xa: The CPI then **lost heavily** in the **1945-46 elections**.
Also stayed away: **Muslim League**, **Hindu Mahasabha** and princely states.

241.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Communist Party of India after its policy during the Quit India period?
o: It did not contest the elections of 1945–46 owing to the continuation of its ban.
It formed the provincial government in Andhra after the elections of 1945–46.
It won heavily in the elections of 1945–46 because of its support for the movement.
It lost heavily in the elections of 1945–46 after opposing the Quit India Movement.
241.x: The Communist Party of India lost heavily in the 1945–46 elections. Its opposition to the Quit India Movement and support for the British war effort formed the background to its political position during this period.
241.tq: Use the electoral outcome as a chronological consequence of the party’s wartime policy.
xs: The CPI **lost heavily** in the **1945-46 elections** — option **(4)** is correct.
Its ban had been **lifted on 23 July 1942**, so (1) is wrong.
It had **opposed Quit India**, backing the British after the Nazi attack on the **USSR**.
xa: **Muslim League**, **Hindu Mahasabha** and princely states also stayed away.
**Tanguturi Prakasam** emerged as Andhra's leading figure.

241.s:
Consider the following statements about the attitude of political groups and communities towards the Quit India Movement:
1. The Muslim League stayed away from the movement.
2. The Hindu Mahasabha stayed away from the movement.
3. The princely states stayed away from the movement.
4. Muslims generally sheltered activists, and communal clashes did not occur.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
241.x: All four statements are correct. The Muslim League, Hindu Mahasabha and princely states stayed away, while Muslims generally sheltered activists and there were no communal clashes.
241.tq: Test several parallel attitudes together, including the less obvious community-level response.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
The **Muslim League**, **Hindu Mahasabha** and **princely states** stayed away.
**Muslims generally sheltered activists**; there were **no communal clashes**.
xa: The **Communists** opposed the movement; **CPI ban lifted 23 July 1942**.
Muslims were also **exempted** from the Andhra collective fines.

241.s: Which one of the following best expresses the significance of the Quit India Movement?
o: It secured immediate transfer of power before the end of the Second World War.
It was Gandhi’s first mass movement against British rule.
It was confined mainly to constitutional negotiations with the British Government.
It was Gandhi’s final mass movement and demonstrated that independence could not be postponed after the war.
241.x: The Quit India Movement was Gandhi’s final mass movement. It showed that Indian independence could not be postponed after the war.
241.tq: Choose the precise significance statement and reject claims of immediate independence or a merely constitutional campaign.
xs: Quit India was **Gandhi's final mass movement** and showed **independence could not be postponed after the war** — option **(4)**.
Leaders were arrested on **9 August 1942**, so it became **leaderless and spontaneous**, not constitutional (3).
xa: Viceroy **Linlithgow**: the most serious rebellion since **1857**.
AP angle: **"final, decisive event of the freedom struggle in Andhra"**.

241.s: In the context of Andhra Pradesh, the Quit India Movement is described as the
o: last campaign led exclusively by the Communist Party in Andhra
first constitutional campaign of the freedom struggle in Andhra
final, decisive event of the freedom struggle in Andhra
movement that began the formation of Andhra Province
241.x: In the Andhra context, the Quit India Movement is regarded as the final, decisive event of the freedom struggle in Andhra. Tanguturi Prakasam emerged as a leading figure during this phase.
241.tq: Apply the regional significance phrase exactly and avoid replacing it with a broader constitutional description.
xs: In Andhra, Quit India was the **"final, decisive event of the freedom struggle in Andhra"** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Tanguturi Prakasam** emerged as a leading figure.
The **Communists** opposed the movement, so (1) is wrong.
xa: The **Kurnool Circular** (**29 July 1942**) was drafted by **Kala Venkat Rao**.
Andhra firing: **Tenali** (**12 Aug 1942**), **Guntur** (**13 Aug**), **Bhimavaram** (**17 Aug**).

241.s: Who emerged as a leading figure in Andhra during the Quit India Movement?
241.x: Tanguturi Prakasam emerged as a leading figure in Andhra during the Quit India Movement.
241.tq: Distinguish the prominent regional figure from leaders associated with particular documents or underground work.
xs: **Tanguturi Prakasam** emerged as Andhra's leading figure during Quit India — option **(4)** is correct.
**Mamidipudi Venkatrangayya** (1) led the **Andhra University** resolution; **Kala Venkat Rao** (3) drafted the **Kurnool Circular**.
xa: **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** presided over the **APCC** at **Machilipatnam**, then was jailed at **Ahmednagar Fort**.
Quit India was the **"final, decisive event of the freedom struggle in Andhra"**.

242.s:
Consider the following statements about Individual Satyagraha:

1. Congress ministries had resigned in November 1939.
2. Individual Satyagraha followed as a limited form of protest.
3. Vinoba Bhave was the first individual satyagrahi.
4. Jawaharlal Nehru was the second individual satyagrahi.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
242.x: Congress ministries resigned in November 1939, after which limited Individual Satyagraha was undertaken. Vinoba Bhave was the first satyagrahi and Jawaharlal Nehru the second.
242.tq: Check the complete sequence of background, nature and first two participants.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Congress ministries resigned in **Nov 1939**, followed by the limited **Individual Satyagraha**.
**Vinoba Bhave** was the **first** satyagrahi and **Nehru** the **second**.
xa: Individual Satyagraha ran in **1940-41**.
**R.P.G.V. Govindan Chettiyar** (Tamil Nadu), jailed **six months** in the Individual Satyagraha, was honoured under **Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav** (**Jun 2025**).
Next phase: **Wardha CWC**, **14 July 1942**.

242.s: The period associated with Individual Satyagraha referred to in the freedom struggle was:
242.x: The limited Individual Satyagraha took place during 1940–41.
242.tq: Distinguish the limited Individual Satyagraha period from the later Quit India year.
xs: The limited Individual Satyagraha belongs to **1940-41** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It followed the resignation of the Congress ministries in **Nov 1939**.
**1942-43** (4) is the Quit India phase.
xa: First satyagrahi **Vinoba Bhave**, second **Nehru**.
**Govindan Chettiyar** was jailed **six months** in the Individual Satyagraha.

242.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding detention during the Quit India Movement?
o: Gandhi was held at Aga Khan Palace and CWC members at Ahmednagar Fort
Gandhi was held at Ahmednagar Fort and CWC members at Aga Khan Palace
Both Gandhi and CWC members were held at Tamluk
Both Gandhi and CWC members were held at Ballia
242.x: Mahatma Gandhi was detained at Aga Khan Palace in Pune, while Congress Working Committee members were detained at Ahmednagar Fort.
242.tq: Reverse the paired locations in the distractors to test precise institutional association.
xs: **Gandhi** was held at the **Aga Khan Palace, Pune**, and **CWC members** at **Ahmednagar Fort** — option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) swaps the two places — a common trap.
xa: The arrests came on **9 Aug** **1942**, the day after the **Gowalia Tank** AICC.
**Pattabhi Sitaramayya**, a CWC member, was jailed with the CWC.

242.s: The AICC session that adopted the Quit India resolution and gave the call 'Do or Die' was held at:
242.x: The AICC met at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, on 8 August 1942 and gave the call 'Do or Die'. Wardha (14 July 1942) was the earlier CWC meeting; 6 August is a wrong date found in some sources; Ahmednagar Fort was where CWC members were detained after the 9 August arrests.
242.tq: CWC Wardha 14 July -> AICC Bombay 8 Aug -> arrests 9 Aug
xs: The AICC met at **Gowalia Tank, Bombay, on 8 Aug 1942**, with the call **"Do or Die"** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Wardha** (**14 July 1942**) (2) was the earlier **CWC** meeting.
⚠ Option (3): some notes date the AICC to **6 Aug** — use **8 Aug**; option (4): **Ahmednagar Fort** is where CWC members were held after **9 Aug**.
xa: The **Andhra Circular** (**29 July 1942**) came **before** the Bombay AICC.
⚠ Some notes say "Young India" — the paper was **Harijan**.

242.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Circular:

1. It was dated 29 July 1942.
2. It was prepared before the Bombay meeting of the AICC.
3. It was seized by the police at Kurnool.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
242.x: The Andhra Circular was dated 29 July 1942, preceded the Bombay AICC meeting, and was seized by the police at Kurnool.
242.tq: Combine date, sequence and location facts in a statement-based question.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The **Andhra Circular** was dated **29 July 1942**, **before the Bombay AICC** (**8 Aug**).
It was **seized by police at Kurnool**.
xa: Author: **Kala Venkata Rao** (APPSC 2019 key).
The **APCC** met at **Machilipatnam** under **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** in the same phase.

242.s: The Andhra Circular was also known as the:
242.x: The Andhra Circular was also called the Kurnool Circular because it was seized by the police at Kurnool.
242.tq: Distinguish the official alternative name from associated Andhra locations.
xs: The Andhra Circular is also called the **Kurnool Circular** — option **(2)** is correct.
It was **seized by police at Kurnool**.
**Machilipatnam** (3) was where the **APCC** met; **Guntur** (1) saw police firing on **13 Aug**.
xa: Author: **Kala Venkata Rao**; dated **29 July 1942**.
It carried **directives for the coming movement**.

242.s: The Andhra Provincial Congress Committee met at Machilipatnam during the same phase under the presidentship of:
242.x: The Andhra Provincial Congress Committee met at Machilipatnam under Pattabhi Sitaramayya during the phase in which the Andhra Circular was issued.
242.tq: Use the person–organisation–venue combination to avoid confusing the author with the presiding leader.
xs: The APCC met at **Machilipatnam** under **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Kala Venkata Rao** (2) authored the **Andhra Circular**; **Chandra Rajeswara Rao** (4) was secretary of the **3rd Communist Conference**.
xa: Pattabhi, a **CWC member**, was jailed with the CWC.
**Unnava Lakshmi Narayana** (1) was **jailed again** in **1942**.

242.s: The Andhra Circular (Kurnool Circular) of July 1942, giving directives for the coming Quit India Movement, was prepared by:
242.x: Kala Venkata Rao authored the Andhra Circular dated 29 July 1942 (APPSC 2019 key). Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided over the APCC meeting at Machilipatnam; Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah of Kurnool stayed underground; Chandra Rajeswara Rao was secretary of the 1943 Communist conference.
242.tq: Circular - Kala Venkata Rao; seized at Kurnool
xs: The **Andhra Circular** was prepared by **Kala Venkata Rao** — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC 2019 key).

**Pattabhi Sitaramayya** (1) presided over the **APCC at Machilipatnam**; **Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah** (3) stayed **underground**; **Chandra Rajeswara Rao** (4) was **Communist Conference** secretary.
xa: Dated **29 July 1942**; **seized by police at Kurnool**.
It came before the **AICC** at **Gowalia Tank** on **8 Aug 1942**.

242.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra leaders during the Quit India Movement:
1. Pattabhi Sitaramayya, a CWC member, was jailed along with the CWC.
2. Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah of Kurnool stayed underground throughout.
3. The secret paper 'Quit India' spread the pamphlet 'Rahasya Udyamam Saginchandi'.
4. Unnava Lakshmi Narayana was jailed for the first time in 1942.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
242.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: Unnava Lakshmi Narayana was jailed again in 1942, not for the first time. A leaves out statement 3; C and D include the false statement 4.
242.tq: Watch 'again' vs 'first time' - Unnava was a repeat prisoner.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: **Pattabhi** (CWC member) jailed with the CWC; **Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah** (**Kurnool**) underground throughout; secret paper **Quit India** spread **"Rahasya Udyamam Saginchandi"**.
Statement 4 is wrong: **Unnava Lakshmi Narayana** was **jailed again** in **1942**, not for the first time — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **Mamidipudi Venkatarangayya** led the **Andhra University** protest demanding Gandhi's release.
**Chitturi Annapurna Devi** (**17**) was arrested in **Guntur** for pamphlets and picketing.

242.s: At which place did police firing on 12 August 1942 reportedly result in about nine deaths during the Quit India Movement in Andhra?
242.x: Police firing at Tenali railway station on 12 August 1942 reportedly caused about nine deaths.
242.tq: Fix the date and match it with the corresponding town rather than relying on the event alone.
xs: Police firing at **Tenali** on **12 Aug** killed about **nine** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Guntur** (4) saw firing on **13 Aug**; **Bhimavaram** (3) on **17 Aug**.
xa: The Tenali firing came three days after Gandhi's arrest on **9 Aug**.
The CWC members were held at **Ahmednagar Fort**.

242.s:
Arrange the following incidents in Andhra in chronological order:

A. Police firing at Guntur
B. Attack on the Collectorate at Bhimavaram and firing
C. Police firing at Tenali railway station

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
242.x: The incidents occurred at Tenali on 12 August 1942, Guntur on 13 August 1942 and Bhimavaram on 17 August 1942.
242.tq: Fix the earliest and latest dates first, then place the middle event.
xs: Order: **Tenali (12 Aug)** → **Guntur (13 Aug)** → **Bhimavaram (17 Aug)** — **C, A, B**, option **(2)**.
All three followed the **AICC** at **Gowalia Tank** on **8 Aug 1942**.
xa: Tenali firing killed about **nine**.
The **Andhra Circular** (**29 July 1942**) had preceded the AICC.

242.s:
With reference to the role of students and lawyers in the Quit India Movement in Andhra, consider the following statements:

1. Students of Andhra University passed a resolution demanding Gandhi’s release.
2. Mamidipudi Venkatarangayya was associated with the Andhra University protest.
3. Lawyers at Kakinada passed a similar resolution.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
242.x: All three statements are correct. The Andhra University protest was associated with Mamidipudi Venkatarangayya, and Kakinada lawyers also passed a resolution demanding Gandhi’s release.
242.tq: Test the institution, individual and parallel action as three linked but separate facts.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Mamidipudi Venkatarangayya**, history head, led the **Andhra University** protest → resolution demanding **Gandhi's release**.
**Kakinada** lawyers passed a similar resolution.
xa: **Chitturi Annapurna Devi** (**17**) was arrested in **Guntur**.
**Duvvuri Subbamma** faced a **lathi charge at Peddapuram**.

242.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Chitturi Annapurna Devi — Arrested at Guntur at the age of 17
Duvvuri Subbamma — Lathi charge at Peddapuram
Chitturi Annapurna Devi — Lathi charge at Peddapuram
242.x: Chitturi Annapurna Devi was arrested at Guntur for distributing pamphlets and picketing. The lathi charge at Peddapuram was faced by Duvvuri Subbamma.
242.tq: Find the swapped person–incident pair, a common APPSC matching trap.
xs: **Chitturi Annapurna Devi — Peddapuram lathi charge** is wrong — option **(4)** is the mismatch.
⚠ **Chitturi Annapurna Devi** = **Guntur** arrest (pamphlets, picketing) at **17**; **Duvvuri Subbamma** = **Peddapuram** lathi charge.
**Mamidipudi Venkatarangayya** — **Andhra University** protest is correct.
xa: **Vanamamalai Varadacharyulu** wrote the song **"Paradesiyulu tolagandi..."**; **Karunasree** a poem.
**Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah** of Kurnool stayed **underground**.

242.s: Which of the following pairs relating to cultural activities during the Quit India Movement in Andhra is correctly matched?
o: Kala Venkata Rao — poem on the Quit India Movement
242.x: Vanamamalai Varadacharyulu wrote or popularised the song beginning “Paradesiyulu tolagandi...”. A poem by Karunasree was another cultural contribution, whereas the other names were associated with political or underground activity.
242.tq: Match the cultural work with its creator and reject political figures used as distractors.
xs: **Vanamamalai Varadacharyulu — "Paradesiyulu tolagandi..."** is correct — option **(4)**.
**Karunasree** (1) wrote **a poem**; **"Rahasya Udyamam Saginchandi"** was the secret paper **Quit India**'s pamphlet.
**Kala Venkata Rao** (2) wrote the **Andhra Circular**; **Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah** (3) stayed **underground**.
