xs: **Azad Hind Radio** was started in **Germany** — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC 2018).
It broadcast from **Berlin**.
xa: Other German ventures: **Free India Centre** and the **Indian Legion** (Rommel's POWs).
"Netaji" was given by the **people of Germany** (UPSC notes).

243.s: Usha Mehta is particularly associated with which activity during the Quit India movement?
o: Organising the Prati Sarkar in Satara
Running the secret Congress Radio in Bombay
243.x: Usha Mehta ran the secret Congress Radio in Bombay during the Quit India movement.
243.tq: Identify a participant through her distinctive underground activity.
xs: **Usha Mehta** ran the secret **Congress Radio** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Matangini Hazra** (2) was the **Tamluk** martyr shot leading a flag procession.
xa: Underground leadership: **Jayaprakash Narayan**, **Rammanohar Lohia**.
Underground network: **Sucheta Kripalani**, **Biju Patnaik**.

243.s: Which development immediately triggered the Quit India Movement?
o: The conclusion of the Shimla Conference in 1945
The resignation of Congress ministries in November 1939 alone
Failure of the Cripps Mission in March 1942
The formation of the INA in 1943
243.x: The failure of the Cripps Mission (March 1942), which offered no immediate self-government, was the immediate trigger for Quit India. Gandhi called the Cripps offer a 'post-dated cheque' (Nehru is credited with adding 'on a crashing bank'). Shimla 1945 and the INA's 1943 revival came later, and the 1939 ministry resignations were only background.
243.tq: Distinguish the immediate trigger from earlier background developments and later events.
xs: The trigger was the **failure of the Cripps Mission (March 1942)** — option **(3)** is correct.
Gandhi called Cripps a **"post-dated cheque"** (on a failing/crashing bank).
Ministries' resignation in **Nov 1939** (2) was only background.
xa: AICC at **Gowalia Tank Maidan**, **8 August 1942**.
**9 August 1942**: leaders arrested.

243.s: Congress ministries in the provinces had resigned in:
243.x: Congress ministries resigned in November 1939 after India was involved in the Second World War without consultation with Indian leaders.
243.tq: Place the background event before the Cripps Mission and Quit India dates.
xs: Congress ministries resigned in **November 1939** — option **(3)** is correct.
**March 1942** (4) was the **Cripps Mission**; **August 1942** (2) the Quit India resolution.
xa: Next: **August Offer** (**8 Aug 1940**), then **Individual Satyagraha** (**17 October 1940**).
Quit India followed the **Cripps** failure — Gandhi's **"post-dated cheque"**.

243.s: The All India Congress Committee passed the Quit India resolution at Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay, on:
243.x: The AICC passed the Quit India resolution at Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay on 8 August 1942. The mass arrests began on 9 August.
243.tq: Distinguish the resolution date from the following day's arrests.
xs: The AICC passed it at **Gowalia Tank Maidan** on **8 August 1942** — option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes say **6 Aug** (4) — **8 Aug** is correct; **9 August** (2) is the day of arrests.
xa: **"Do or Die"** was Gandhi's call there (APPSC 2018, 2025 — Gandhi, not Bose).
Gandhi was held at the **Aga Khan Palace, Pune**; the CWC at **Ahmednagar Fort**.

243.s: Which one of the following statements regarding 9 August 1942 is correct?
o: The Wardha resolution was passed and all leaders remained free.
The INA flag was first hoisted at Moirang.
The principal leaders were arrested, making the movement leaderless and increasingly violent.
The Cripps Mission arrived in India.
243.x: On 9 August 1942, the leaders were arrested. Gandhi was held at Aga Khan Palace in Pune and the Congress Working Committee was held at Ahmednagar Fort, after which the movement became leaderless and witnessed attacks on railways, telegraphs and police stations.
243.tq: Link the date with the immediate administrative consequence rather than a different wartime event.
xs: On **9 August 1942** the leaders were arrested, making the movement **leaderless** and **violent** — option **(3)** is correct.
Gandhi went to the **Aga Khan Palace, Pune**; the CWC to **Ahmednagar Fort**.
Targets: **railways**, **telegraphs**, **police stations**; **Moirang** (2) was **14 April 1944**.
xa: **Usha Mehta** ran the secret **Congress Radio**.
Martyrs: **Kanaklata Barua** (Assam, aged **15**), **Matangini Hazra** (**Tamluk**).

243.s:
Which of the following pairs were associated with underground leadership during the Quit India Movement?
1. Jayaprakash Narayan and Rammanohar Lohia
2. Sucheta Kripalani and Biju Patnaik
3. Bhulabhai Desai and Tej Bahadur Sapru

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
243.x: Jayaprakash Narayan, Rammanohar Lohia, Sucheta Kripalani and Biju Patnaik were associated with the underground network. Bhulabhai Desai and Tej Bahadur Sapru were associated with the INA trial defence, not the Quit India underground leadership listed here.
243.tq: Separate Quit India underground workers from lawyers associated with the INA trials.
xs: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct: **JP** and **Lohia** — underground leadership; **Sucheta Kripalani** and **Biju Patnaik** — underground network.
Pair 3 is wrong: **Bhulabhai Desai** and **Tej Bahadur Sapru** were the **INA trial defence** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **Usha Mehta** ran the secret **Congress Radio**.
INA trial defence also had **Nehru**, **Asaf Ali**, **K.N. Katju**.

243.s:
Consider the following statements about the martyrs of the Quit India Movement:
1. Kanaklata Barua was 15 years old.
2. Matangini Hazra was shot while leading a flag procession.
3. Kanaklata Barua and Matangini Hazra were both associated with Tamluk in Bengal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
243.x: Kanaklata Barua was aged 15 and Matangini Hazra was shot while leading a flag procession. Kanaklata was associated with Assam, whereas Matangini Hazra was associated with Tamluk in Bengal.
243.tq: Use the location distinction to reject the otherwise attractive but overgeneralised statement.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Kanaklata Barua** was aged **15**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Matangini Hazra** was shot while leading a **flag procession**.
Statement 3 is wrong: Kanaklata was from **Assam**; only Matangini was from **Tamluk** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Both were shot while leading **flag processions**.
After **9 August 1942** the movement turned leaderless and violent.

243.s: Subhas Chandra Bose became the Supreme Commander of the Indian National Army on:
243.x: Bose assumed the position of Supreme Commander of the INA on 25 August 1943.
243.tq: Distinguish closely related dates connected with Bose's command, government and INA campaigns.
xs: Bose became **Supreme Commander of the INA** on **25 Aug 1943** — option **(3)** is correct.
**21 October 1943** (4) is the **Azad Hind** proclamation; **14 April 1944** (1) the **Moirang** flag; **18 August 1945** (2) the reported death.
xa: He had taken over the **IIL** and INA in **July 1943**.
HQ: **Singapore**, later **Rangoon**.

243.s: The first Indian National Army was organised primarily from Indian prisoners of war with Japanese help in:
243.x: The first INA was organised in South-East Asia from Indian prisoners of war with Japanese assistance. Singapore and Malaya were important centres of its formation.
243.tq: Use the geographical setting and nearby regional distractors to identify the correct theatre.
xs: The first INA was formed in **South-East Asia** (**Singapore/Malaya**) — option **(3)** is correct.
Some notes say "in **Japan**".
**North Africa** (1) supplied POWs for the **Indian Legion** in Germany.
xa: It was led by **Capt. Mohan Singh** with **Rash Behari Bose**.
About **40,000** volunteers; first division **16,300** men, after the fall of Singapore.

243.s: Who among the following were associated with the formation of the first INA?
o: Jawaharlal Nehru and Rash Behari Ghosh
Subhas Chandra Bose and C.R. Das
Capt. Mohan Singh and Rash Behari Bose
Mahatma Gandhi and Capt. Lakshmi Sahgal
243.x: The first INA was formed under Capt. Mohan Singh with the political association of Rash Behari Bose. Subhas Chandra Bose took over and revived it in its second phase in 1943.
243.tq: Apply the founder-versus-later-commander distinction instead of choosing the most famous associated person.
xs: The first INA was formed by **Capt. Mohan Singh** with **Rash Behari Bose** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **Rash Behari Ghosh** (1) was the **Moderate**, not the IIL leader.
**Capt. Lakshmi Sahgal** (4) led the **Rani of Jhansi Regiment**.
xa: **June 1942**: IIL leaders met the Japanese to set up the INA.
Second phase (**1943**): **Subhas Bose** revived the INA as Supreme Commander.

243.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the headquarters of the INA under Subhas Chandra Bose?
243.x: The INA headquarters was at Singapore under Bose and was later shifted to Rangoon.
243.tq: Watch for the reversal of the initial and later locations.
xs: INA HQ was at **Singapore**, later **Rangoon** — option **(1)** is correct.
Option (3) reverses the order.
xa: Bose took over the IIL and INA in **July 1943**.
**Imphal-Kohima campaign (1944)** ended in retreat after Japanese defeats + supply shortages.

243.s:
Consider the following statements about the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind):
1. It was proclaimed at Rangoon on 21 October 1943.
2. It declared war on Britain and the USA.
3. It was recognised by the Axis powers - Japan, Germany and Italy.
4. Its proclamation guaranteed religious liberty and equal rights.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
243.x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the government was proclaimed at Singapore on 21 October 1943; Rangoon was where the INA headquarters later moved. A, C and D all include the false statement 1.
243.tq: Proclaimed at Singapore; HQ later shifted to Rangoon.
xs: Statement 1 is wrong: Azad Hind was proclaimed at **Singapore**, **21 October 1943**, not Rangoon.
Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct: war on **Britain and the USA**; recognised by **Japan, Germany, Italy**; guaranteed **religious liberty and equal rights** — so **2, 3 and 4 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Allies recognising it: **Burma**, **Thailand**, **Philippines**, **Manchukuo**.
**Rangoon** was the INA's later HQ.

243.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andaman and Nicobar Islands under the Azad Hind Government:
1. The Andaman Islands were renamed Shaheed Dweep.
2. The Nicobar Islands were renamed Swaraj Dweep.
3. Bose hoisted the tricolour at Port Blair on 30 December 1943.
4. The islands were handed over to the Azad Hind Government by Germany.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
243.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the islands were handed over by Japan, not Germany. A leaves out statement 3; C and D include the false statement 4.
243.tq: Andaman = Shaheed, Nicobar = Swaraj; handed over by Japan.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: Andaman = **Shaheed Dweep**; Nicobar = **Swaraj Dweep**; tricolour at **Port Blair (30 Dec 1943)**.
Statement 4 is wrong: the islands were handed over by **Japan** — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: ⚠ **Shaheed** = Andaman; **Swaraj** = Nicobar.
**Jan 2026**: PM marked the **82nd anniversary** of the Port Blair flag-hoisting.

243.s:
Which of the following countries was part of the group that recognised the Provisional Government of Free India?
1. Japan
2. Germany
3. Italy
4. Thailand
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
243.x: Japan, Germany, Italy and their allies, including Thailand, recognised the Provisional Government of Free India.
243.tq: Test membership in a diplomatic group and avoid treating recognition as limited to the three principal Axis powers.
xs: All four recognised it — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Recognition came from the **Axis powers — Japan, Germany, Italy** and allies like **Thailand**.
xa: Other allies: **Burma**, **Philippines**, **Manchukuo**.
Proclaimed at **Singapore**, **21 October 1943**; declared war on **Britain and the USA**.

243.s: The INA hoisted its flag at Moirang in Manipur during the Imphal campaign on:
243.x: The INA hoisted its flag at Moirang, Manipur, on 14 April 1944 during the Imphal campaign, before retreating.
243.tq: Link a military campaign site with its precise date while separating it from Port Blair events.
xs: The INA hoisted its flag at **Moirang, Manipur, 14 April 1944** — option **(4)** is correct.
**30 December 1943** (2) was Bose's flag at **Port Blair**; **21 October 1943** (1) the Azad Hind proclamation.
xa: The **Imphal-Kohima campaign (1944)** ended in retreat after Japanese defeats + supply shortages.
INA war cry: **"Dilli Chalo"**.

243.s: The Rani of Jhansi Regiment of the INA was:
o: An all-women combat unit under Captain Lakshmi Sahgal
A women's medical unit under Aruna Asaf Ali
A civilian relief organisation under Sucheta Kripalani
A mixed military unit under Rash Behari Bose
243.x: The Rani of Jhansi Regiment was an all-women combat unit commanded by Captain Lakshmi Sahgal.
243.tq: Match the unit's character and commander rather than selecting a well-known woman freedom fighter at random.
xs: The **Rani of Jhansi Regiment** was an **all-women combat unit** under **Capt. Lakshmi Sahgal** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Sucheta Kripalani** (3) was in the **Quit India** underground network.
xa: The **IIL** was the INA's political wing.
INA motto: **"Ittefaq, Itmad, Qurbani"** (Unity, Faith, Sacrifice).

243.s: The composition of mixed INA units reflected which of the following features?
o: Separate units for Hindus, Muslims and Sikhs
A secular arrangement in which Hindus, Muslims and Sikhs ate from common kitchens
Command limited exclusively to Japanese officers
Recruitment restricted to Indian prisoners from one province
243.x: The INA maintained mixed units of Hindus, Muslims and Sikhs, including common kitchens, reflecting its secular character.
243.tq: Choose the option that directly expresses the institutional practice implied by the stated principle.
xs: INA units were **secular**: **Hindus, Muslims and Sikhs** in mixed units, eating from **the same kitchens** — option **(2)**.
Option (1) is the reverse of the mixed-unit system.
xa: INA anthem: Hindustani **Jana Gana Mana** by **Abid Hasan 'Safrani'**.
**"Jai Hind"** was popularised by Bose as a greeting **replacing communal ones**.

243.s:
Consider the following statements about the Red Fort INA trials:
1. The first trial was held at the Red Fort in November 1945.
2. Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Kumar Sehgal and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon were among the accused.
3. The defence was led by Tej Bahadur Sapru, with Bhulabhai Desai assisting him.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
243.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Bhulabhai Desai led the defence; Sapru, Nehru, Asaf Ali and K.N. Katju assisted. A is incomplete; C and D include statement 3.
243.tq: Accused: Sehgal, Shah Nawaz, Dhillon. Lead counsel: Bhulabhai Desai.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Red Fort** trials began in **Nov 1945**.
Statement 2 is correct: accused **Shah Nawaz Khan**, **Prem Kumar Sehgal**, **Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Bhulabhai Desai** led the defence, with **Sapru** assisting — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Defence team also had **Nehru**, **Asaf Ali**, **K.N. Katju**.
INA trials + the **RIN mutiny** broke the loyalty of the Indian armed forces.

243.s: The INA anthem was a Hindustani version of 'Jana Gana Mana' translated by:
243.x: Abid Hasan 'Safrani' translated the Hindustani version of 'Jana Gana Mana' that served as the INA anthem.
243.tq: Match the cultural contribution with its precise individual contributor.
xs: The INA anthem — Hindustani **Jana Gana Mana** — was translated by **Abid Hasan 'Safrani'** — option **(3)**.
**Lakshmi Sahgal** (1) led the Rani of Jhansi Regiment; **Dhillon** and **Sehgal** (2, 4) were Red Fort accused.
xa: INA motto: **"Ittefaq, Itmad, Qurbani"**.
Bose's call: **"Tum mujhe khoon do, main tumhe azadi dunga"**.

243.s: Subhas Chandra Bose was reportedly killed in a plane crash at Taipei on:
243.x: Bose was reportedly killed in a plane crash at Taipei on 18 August 1945. The circumstances of his death later became the subject of official inquiries.
243.tq: Differentiate closely spaced dates in a disputed historical event.
xs: Bose was reportedly killed in a **plane crash at Taipei, 18 August 1945** — option **(2)**.
Inquiries: **Shah Nawaz Committee** and **Khosla Commission** — died in the crash.
xa: The **Mukherjee Commission** found he **did not die** in the crash; its report was rejected.
"Netaji" was given by the **people of Germany**.

243.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Shah Nawaz Committee — 1956
2. Khosla Commission — 1970
3. Mukherjee Commission — 1999
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
243.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. The Shah Nawaz Committee was constituted in 1956, the Khosla Commission in 1970 and the Mukherjee Commission in 1999.
243.tq: Match each inquiry with its year before checking the coded combination.
xs: All three pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Shah Nawaz Committee — 1956**, **Khosla Commission — 1970**: both said he **died in the crash**.
**Mukherjee Commission — 1999**: he **did not die** in the crash; report rejected by the government (**2006**).
xa: Reported death: plane crash at **Taipei**, **18 August 1945**.
⚠ **Shah Nawaz Khan** was also one of the **Red Fort** accused.

243.s: Which one of the following correctly states the findings of the inquiries into the death of Subhas Chandra Bose?
o: The Shah Nawaz Committee alone concluded that he died in the crash; all later inquiries rejected it.
All three inquiries concluded that Bose did not die in the crash.
The Mukherjee Commission confirmed the crash theory and the government accepted its report in 2006.
Both the Shah Nawaz Committee and Khosla Commission concluded that he died in the crash, while the Mukherjee Commission concluded otherwise.
243.x: The Shah Nawaz Committee and Khosla Commission accepted that Bose died in the crash. The Mukherjee Commission concluded that he did not die in the crash, but its report was rejected by the government in 2006.
243.tq: Compare the findings across inquiries and note the later government action separately.
xs: The **Shah Nawaz Committee** and **Khosla Commission** said he **died in the crash**; the **Mukherjee Commission** said he **did not** — option **(4)** is correct.
The Mukherjee report was **rejected by the government** (**2006**), so (3) is wrong.
xa: Years: Shah Nawaz **1956**, Khosla **1970**, Mukherjee **1999**.
Reported death: **plane crash at Taipei, 18 August 1945**.
⚠ **Shah Nawaz Khan** was also one of the **Red Fort** INA accused.

243.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched?

Title or slogan — Association
o: Patriot of patriots — Subhas Chandra Bose
Father of the Nation — Subhas Chandra Bose
Netaji — Subhas Chandra Bose, as given by the people of Germany
Ittefaq, Itmad, Qurbani — Indian National Congress
243.x: The honorific 'Netaji' was given to Subhas Chandra Bose by the people of Germany. Gandhi called Bose the 'Patriot of patriots', while 'Father of the Nation' was used by Bose for Gandhi.
243.tq: Start from the sure title-person pair and eliminate swapped associations.
xs: **"Netaji"** was given to Bose by the **people of Germany** — option **(3)** is correct (UPSC notes).
**"Patriot of patriots"** was Gandhi's title **for Bose**; **"Father of the Nation"** was Bose's title **for Gandhi** (radio broadcast **1944**).
**"Ittefaq, Itmad, Qurbani"** (4) was the **INA** motto, not the Congress's.
xa: **"Jai Hind"** was popularised by Bose in place of **Bande Mataram**.
**"Dilli Chalo"** was the INA war cry.

243.s: The slogan 'Ittefaq, Itmad, Qurbani' was the motto of which organisation?
243.x: 'Ittefaq, Itmad, Qurbani', meaning unity, faith or agreement and sacrifice, was the motto of the Indian National Army.
243.tq: Test the exact official wording of a motto against nearby organisations.
xs: **"Ittefaq, Itmad, Qurbani"** was the motto of the **Indian National Army** — option **(1)** is correct.
It means **Unity, Faith/Agreement, Sacrifice**.
The **IIL** (2) was the INA's **political wing**; the **Forward Bloc** (4) was Bose's **1939** bloc within Congress.
xa: INA anthem: Hindustani **Jana Gana Mana**, translated by **Abid Hasan 'Safrani'**.
INA war cry: **"Dilli Chalo"**.

243.s: Who coined the phrase 'Quit India', while Gandhi gave the call for the movement?
243.x: The phrase 'Quit India' was coined by Yusuf Meherally. Gandhi subsequently gave the call for the movement.
243.tq: Separate the person who coined a phrase from the leader who popularised or gave the call.
xs: The phrase **"Quit India"** was coined by **Yusuf Meherally** — option **(1)** is correct.
Gandhi gave the call, having hinted it in **Harijan** in **April 1942**.
**Lohia** and **JP** (2, 3) were **underground leaders** after the arrests.
xa: Gandhi's **"Do or Die"** came at **Gowalia Tank**, **8 Aug 1942**.
**Usha Mehta** ran the secret **Congress Radio**.

243.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the slogans associated with Subhas Chandra Bose:
1. 'Jai Hind' was popularised by Bose in place of 'Bande Mataram'.
2. 'Dilli Chalo' was the war cry of the INA.
3. 'Tum mujhe khoon do, main tumhe azadi dunga' was associated with Bose.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
243.x: All three statements are correct. Bose popularised 'Jai Hind', used 'Dilli Chalo' as the INA war cry and gave the famous blood-for-freedom exhortation.
243.tq: Check each slogan against its speaker and political context before choosing the coded combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**"Jai Hind"** was popularised by Bose as a greeting replacing communal ones, in place of **Bande Mataram**.
**"Dilli Chalo"** was the **INA war cry**; **"Tum mujhe khoon do, main tumhe azadi dunga"** is Bose's.
xa: INA motto: **"Ittefaq, Itmad, Qurbani"**.
⚠ **"Do or Die"** is **Gandhi**'s, not Bose's (APPSC 2018, 2025).

243.s: The slogan 'Do or Die' is associated with:
o: Subhas Chandra Bose, as the INA war cry
Mahatma Gandhi, at the Quit India session in Bombay, 8 August 1942
Yusuf Meherally, who coined it in 1942
Bal Gangadhar Tilak, during the Swadeshi Movement
243.x: 'Do or Die' was Gandhi's call at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, on 8 August 1942. Bose's INA war cry was 'Dilli Chalo'; Yusuf Meherally coined 'Quit India', not 'Do or Die'; Tilak is linked to 'Swaraj is my birthright'.
243.tq: Do or Die = Gandhi (not Bose)
xs: **"Do or Die"** was **Mahatma Gandhi**'s call at the Quit India session, **Gowalia Tank**, Bombay, **8 Aug 1942** — option **(2)**.
Bose's INA war cry (1) was **"Dilli Chalo"**; **Yusuf Meherally** (3) coined **"Quit India"**, not "Do or Die".
xa: Exam angle: asked repeatedly (**APPSC 2018, 2025**) — answer **Gandhi**, not Bose.
Leaders were arrested the next day, **9 August 1942**.

243.s: Which one of the following statements best expresses the significance attributed to the INA trials and the Royal Indian Navy Mutiny?
o: They ended all political activity in the provinces.
They destroyed the loyalty of the British Indian armed forces to the Raj.
They resulted in the immediate abolition of the Indian National Congress.
They strengthened the loyalty of the British Indian armed forces to the Raj.
243.x: The INA trials and the RIN Mutiny demonstrated that the British could no longer rely confidently on the loyalty of the Indian armed forces.
243.tq: Apply the stated historical consequence to the broader weakening of colonial rule.
xs: The INA trials + the **RIN mutiny** **destroyed the loyalty** of the British Indian armed forces — option **(2)** is correct.
After them the **Raj could no longer trust Indian forces**.
xa: Red Fort accused: **Shah Nawaz Khan**, **Prem Kumar Sehgal**, **Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon**.
Defence led by **Bhulabhai Desai**.

243.s: The roots of the Indian National Army were traced to the Indian Independence League in which country, according to the reported historical account?
243.x: The INA’s roots were traced to the Indian Independence League in Thailand. Two leaders associated with the process died in a plane crash in March 1942 before the June 1942 conference with the Japanese.
243.tq: Test the organisation–country association without confusing it with later INA operational centres.
xs: The INA's roots were traced to the **IIL** in **Thailand** — option **(1)** is correct (**15 Jun 2026** report).
Two leaders died in a **March 1942** plane crash before the **June 1942** conference with the Japanese.
xa: In **June 1942** IIL leaders met the Japanese to set up the INA.
**Rash Behari Bose** (Japan) led the IIL; the first INA was under **Capt. Mohan Singh**.

243.s: In January 2026, the Prime Minister marked which anniversary of Subhas Chandra Bose’s hoisting of the tricolour at Port Blair?
243.x: In January 2026, the Prime Minister marked the 82nd anniversary of Bose’s hoisting of the tricolour at Port Blair.
243.tq: Use the exact anniversary figure and distinguish it from round-number distractors.
xs: In **Jan 2026** the PM marked the **82nd anniversary** — option **(3)** is correct.
Bose hoisted the tricolour at **Port Blair** on **30 Dec 1943**.
xa: Japan handed over the **Andaman & Nicobar Islands**; renamed **Shaheed Dweep** (Andaman) and **Swaraj Dweep** (Nicobar).
Azad Hind was proclaimed at **Singapore**, **21 October 1943**.

243.s: In July 2026, the All India Forward Bloc demanded an apology from the West Bengal BJP chief for referring to Forward Bloc members as:
243.x: The All India Forward Bloc demanded an apology after the West Bengal BJP chief referred to Forward Bloc members as ‘goons’.
243.tq: Recall the precise disputed expression rather than a synonymous political label.
xs: The **AIFB** objected to Forward Bloc members being called **"goons"** — option **(2)** is correct (**13 Jul 2026**).
The apology was demanded from the **West Bengal BJP chief**.
xa: Bose founded the **Forward Bloc** in **1939** after resigning the Congress presidency.
Andhra branch: **Madduri Annapurnaiah** and **Peta Bapayya**.

243.s: In June 1942, the leaders of the Indian Independence League met the Japanese primarily to:
o: Arrange the formation of the INA
243.x: The IIL leaders met the Japanese in June 1942 to set up the Indian National Army.
243.tq: Identify the immediate organisational objective behind a meeting rather than a later wartime event.
xs: In **June 1942** IIL leaders met the Japanese to **arrange the formation of the INA** — option **(4)** is correct.
The **Forward Bloc** (1) dates to **1939**; the **Congress Radio** (2) was **Usha Mehta**'s Quit India venture.
xa: The first INA: **Capt. Mohan Singh** with Indian POWs (~**40,000** volunteers).
Bose took over the **IIL** and INA in **July 1943**.

243.s: Who among the following was known as "Andhra Netaji" and, with Peta Bapayya, led the Forward Bloc in Andhra?
243.x: Madduri Annapurnaiah, called "Andhra Netaji", led the Andhra Forward Bloc together with Peta Bapayya.
243.tq: Netaji's Bloc in Andhra was led by "Andhra Netaji" Madduri.
xs: **Madduri Annapurnaiah** was **"Andhra Netaji"** and led the Andhra Forward Bloc with **Peta Bapayya** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Pattabhi Sitaramayya** (2) was the Gandhi-backed candidate Bose defeated at **Tripuri**.
xa: Annapurnaiah: born **1899**, **Pithapuram** taluk; jailed **18 months** for **"Chicharapidugu"**.
He spent **4 years** in jail during **WWII** and later edited **Jai Bharat**, **Navashakti**, **Velugu**.

243.s: Pattabhi Sitaramayya, the candidate backed by Gandhi, was defeated by Subhas Chandra Bose in the contest for the Congress presidency linked to which session?
243.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya's defeat came at the Tripuri session, the Tripuri crisis of 1939. Haripura (1938) was Bose's first presidency, and Ramgarh (1940) came after the crisis.
243.tq: Pattabhi's Tripuri defeat: Gandhi's candidate lost.
xs: Pattabhi Sitaramayya lost at **Tripuri** (**1939**) — option **(3)** is correct (APPSC 2018).
**Haripura** (1) was Bose's first presidency, the **51st** session (**1938**).
xa: Vote: **1,580** to **1,377**; Gandhi: **"Pattabhi's defeat is my defeat."**
Bose resigned (**April 1939**); **Dr. Rajendra Prasad** became President.

244.s: The INA trials at the Red Fort were conducted during which period?
244.x: The trials began in November 1945 and continued up to May 1946; the first trial commenced in November 1945.
244.tq: Distinguish the beginning and ending months rather than relying only on the year.
xs: The Red Fort INA trials ran **November 1945 - May 1946** — option **(4)** is correct.
The **first trial** began in **Nov 1945**.
xa: **12 November 1945**: **INA Day** (UPPSC 2013 key).
**21 November 1945**: **Calcutta** student protest; police firing killed **two**.

244.s: The joint trial of Prem Kumar Sahgal, Shah Nawaz Khan and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon symbolised which of the following?
o: The reconciliation of the British and Japanese armies
The division of the Indian National Army on regional lines
The exclusive leadership of the Congress
244.x: The Hindu, Muslim and Sikh identities of the three accused made their joint trial a symbol of national and communal unity.
244.tq: Infer the political significance from the composition of the accused.
xs: Trying a **Hindu**, a **Muslim** and a **Sikh** together made the trial a symbol of **unity** among communities — option **(2)**.
**Prem Kumar Sahgal** (Hindu), **Shah Nawaz Khan** (Muslim), **Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon** (Sikh).
xa: **Congress, League and Communists united** in support of the accused.
Verdict: guilty of waging war; **transportation for life** remitted by **Auchinleck** (**Jan 1946**).

244.s:
Consider the following statements about the first INA trial:
1. The accused were found guilty of waging war.
2. Their sentence of transportation for life was remitted by C-in-C Auchinleck in January 1946.
3. All three accused belonged to the same religious community.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
244.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Sahgal (Hindu), Shah Nawaz Khan (Muslim) and Dhillon (Sikh) were tried together as a symbol of unity. A misses statement 1; B and D include statement 3.
244.tq: Hindu-Muslim-Sikh trio; guilty of waging war; Auchinleck remitted.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: they were found **guilty of waging war**.
Statement 2 is correct: **transportation for life** was remitted by C-in-C **Auchinleck** (**Jan 1946**).
Statement 3 is wrong: **Sahgal** (Hindu), **Shah Nawaz** (Muslim), **Dhillon** (Sikh) — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: **Rashid Ali**'s later **7-year sentence** sparked protests (**11 February 1946**).
UPSC 2021: the three were **INA officers**.

244.s: The INA Defence Committee was set up by which organisation?
244.x: The INA Defence Committee was established by the Congress to defend the accused officers.
244.tq: Use the organisation-founder association and avoid the reaction of that organisation to the later naval revolt.
xs: The **INA Defence Committee** was set up by the **Congress** — option **(1)** is correct.
But **Congress, League and Communists** all united in support of the accused, so none acted "alone".
xa: Lead counsel: **Bhulabhai Desai** — his last major contribution.
Other lawyers: **Sapru**, **Asaf Ali**, **Sarat Chandra Bose**, **K.N. Katju**, **Jawaharlal Nehru**.

244.s: Who served as the lead counsel of the INA Defence Committee?
244.x: Bhulabhai Desai was the lead counsel of the INA Defence Committee, and this was regarded as his last major contribution.
244.tq: Distinguish the lead counsel from the other lawyers who assisted the defence.
xs: **Bhulabhai Desai** was lead counsel — option **(4)** is correct; it was his **last major contribution**.
**Sapru**, **K.N. Katju** and **Asaf Ali** (1-3) were other defence lawyers.
xa: ⚠ BPSC 2020: of **Rajendra Prasad**, **Bhulabhai Desai**, **K.M. Munshi**, **Patel** — only **Bhulabhai Desai** was counsel.
APPSC 2018: Bhulabhai Desai was **counsel, not an accused**.

244.s:
Consider the following statements about the INA Defence Committee:
1. Tej Bahadur Sapru was associated with the defence.
2. Asaf Ali was associated with the defence.
3. Motilal Nehru appeared as a lawyer in the INA trials.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
244.x: Tej Bahadur Sapru and Asaf Ali were associated with the defence. Motilal Nehru did not appear because he was dead by then.
244.tq: Test membership through a deceased-person exclusion.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: **Tej Bahadur Sapru** and **Asaf Ali** were defence lawyers.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Motilal Nehru** (and **C.R. Das**) did not appear — **dead by then** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: ⚠ UPPSC 2013 key: **Sapru**, not **Jinnah**.
Lead counsel: **Bhulabhai Desai**; also **Sarat Chandra Bose**, **K.N. Katju**, **Jawaharlal Nehru**.

244.s: INA Day was observed on which date?
244.x: INA Day was observed on 12 November 1945.
244.tq: Distinguish the commemorative date from the dates of later protests and the naval revolt.
xs: **INA Day** was **12 November 1945** — option **(3)** is correct (UPPSC 2013 key).
**21 November 1945** (1) = Calcutta student protest; **11 February 1946** (2) = Rashid Ali protests; **18 February 1946** (4) = RIN mutiny.
xa: The Red Fort trials ran **November 1945 - May 1946**.
The Calcutta firing on **21 November** killed **two**.

244.s: On 21 November 1945, student protests against the INA trials took place in which city?
244.x: Students protested against the INA trials in Calcutta on 21 November 1945, and police firing killed two persons.
244.tq: Match the protest date with its city and immediate consequence.
xs: The **21 November 1945** student protest was in **Calcutta** — option **(1)** is correct.
Police firing killed **two**.
xa: Calcutta protested again on **11 February 1946** against **Rashid Ali**'s sentence.
**INA Day** fell on **12 November 1945**.

244.s: Rashid Ali Day protests in Calcutta were held on:
244.x: The protests against Rashid Ali's sentence took place in Calcutta on 11 February 1946.
244.tq: Separate closely spaced protest dates by associating each with its event.
xs: The **Rashid Ali** protests in **Calcutta** were on **11 February 1946** — option **(2)** is correct.
They opposed his **7-year sentence** as an INA officer.
**21 November 1945** (1) was the earlier Calcutta student protest; **12 November 1945** (3) was **INA Day**.
xa: A week later, on **18 February 1946**, the **RIN mutiny** began at **HMIS Talwar**.
The first trial's **transportation for life** sentence had been remitted by **Auchinleck** (**Jan 1946**).

244.s: The Royal Indian Navy Mutiny began on 18 February 1946 among the ratings of:
244.x: The mutiny began on 18 February 1946 among the ratings of HMIS Talwar in Bombay.
244.tq: Link the date, naval vessel and city precisely.
xs: The RIN mutiny began on **18 February 1946** at **HMIS Talwar, Bombay** — option **(4)** is correct.
It spread to about **20,000 personnel**, **78 ships**, **20 shore establishments**, and also **Karachi**.
xa: ⚠ It came one day before Attlee's **Cabinet Mission** announcement (**19 Feb 1946**).
**M.S. Khan** headed the **Naval Central Strike Committee**.

244.s: Who persuaded the ratings of the Royal Indian Navy to surrender?
o: Aruna Asaf Ali and Subhas Chandra Bose
Vallabhbhai Patel and Muhammad Ali Jinnah
244.x: Vallabhbhai Patel and Muhammad Ali Jinnah persuaded the ratings to surrender. Aruna Asaf Ali supported the ratings but was not one of the two who persuaded them to surrender.
244.tq: Distinguish the supporters of the mutiny from the leaders who secured surrender.
xs: **Patel** and **Jinnah** persuaded the ratings to surrender — option **(3)** is correct.
**Aruna Asaf Ali** (1) and the **Communists** backed the revolt instead.
xa: ⚠ Congress and League flags flew together, yet both leaderships asked for surrender.
Surrender followed the events of **18-22 February**.

244.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the principal grievances of the naval ratings during the RIN revolt?
o: Demand for a separate constitution for India
244.x: The ratings struck over poor food, low pay and racial discrimination. A demand for a separate constitution was not identified as their principal grievance.
244.tq: Find the option outside the stated group of immediate service grievances.
xs: A **demand for a separate constitution** was not among the grievances — option **(3)** is the odd one out.
The ratings struck over **poor food**, **low pay** and **racial discrimination**.
xa: The mutiny began at **HMIS Talwar, Bombay**, on **18 February 1946**.
**Bombay mill + railway workers and students** joined the ratings.

244.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the scale of the Royal Indian Navy revolt:
1. It involved about 20,000 personnel.
2. It spread to 78 ships.
3. It affected 20 shore establishments.
4. It was confined exclusively to Bombay.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
244.x: About 20,000 personnel, 78 ships and 20 shore establishments were involved. The revolt also spread to Karachi, so it was not confined exclusively to Bombay.
244.tq: Reject the extreme word ‘exclusively’ while retaining the numerical details.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: about **20,000 personnel**, **78 ships**, **20 shore establishments**.
Statement 4 is wrong: the revolt also spread to **Karachi** — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: President of the **Naval Central Strike Committee**: **M.S. Khan**.
The **RIN** had been **established** in **1934**.

244.s: Who was the president of the Naval Central Strike Committee during the RIN revolt?
244.x: M.S. Khan served as president of the Naval Central Strike Committee.
244.tq: Distinguish the strike committee leader from the political leaders who negotiated surrender.
xs: **M.S. Khan** was president of the **Naval Central Strike Committee** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Patel** and **Jinnah** (2, 4) persuaded the ratings to surrender; **Aruna Asaf Ali** (3) backed them.
xa: Strike began at **HMIS Talwar, Bombay**, **18 February 1946**.
Congress and **Muslim League flags** were hoisted together.

244.s:
Consider the following statements about the RIN revolt of 1946:
1. Congress and Muslim League flags were hoisted together.
2. Bombay mill workers, railway workers and students joined the ratings.
3. Aruna Asaf Ali and the Communists backed the ratings.
4. Patel and Jinnah backed the continuation of the revolt.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
244.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: Patel and Jinnah persuaded the ratings to surrender. A, C and D include statement 4.
244.tq: Backers: Aruna Asaf Ali + Communists. Patel + Jinnah ended it.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: **Congress and League flags** together; **mill + railway workers and students** joined; **Aruna Asaf Ali** + **Communists** backed it.
Statement 4 is wrong: **Patel** and **Jinnah** persuaded the ratings to **surrender** — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Grievances: **poor food**, **low pay**, **racial discrimination**.
Events of **18-22 February**; leaders did not back a **violent revolt**.

244.s:
Consider the following statements about political reactions:
1. Congress, the Muslim League and the Communists supported the INA accused.
2. Congress and Muslim League leaders supported a violent continuation of the RIN revolt.
3. The Communists supported the RIN revolt.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
244.x: Congress, the Muslim League and the Communists united in support of the INA accused. Congress and League leaders did not back a violent continuation of the naval revolt, while the Communists supported it.
244.tq: Separate reactions to the INA trials from reactions to the RIN revolt.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Congress, League and Communists united** behind the INA accused.
Statement 2 is wrong: Congress + League leaders **did not back a violent revolt**.
Statement 3 is correct: the **Communists** supported the RIN revolt — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **Patel** and **Jinnah** persuaded the ratings to surrender.
**Aruna Asaf Ali** also backed the ratings.

244.s: Which of the following correctly describes the wider military disaffection associated with the RIN revolt?
o: The revolt was confined to civilian workers.
Only the naval ratings showed disaffection; the RIAF and Army remained unaffected.
The Army alone revolted while the Navy remained neutral.
Sections of the RIAF and Army also showed disaffection.
244.x: Sections of the Royal Indian Air Force and the Army also showed disaffection during the period of the RIN revolt.
244.tq: Avoid the exclusivity trap and identify the broader military spread.
xs: Sections of the **RIAF** and **Army** also showed disaffection — option **(4)** is correct.
Option (2) is wrong for the same reason; mill/railway workers and students also joined.
xa: **RIAF strike**: **January 1946**; **Army Signal Corps, Jabalpur**: **February 1946**.
The British relied on the **2.5-million** Indian Army — this "sword" could no longer be trusted.

244.s:
Arrange the following 1946 upsurges in chronological order:
A. Post and telegraph strike
B. RIAF strike
C. RIN revolt at HMIS Talwar, Bombay
244.x: The RIAF strike came in January 1946, the RIN revolt began on 18 February 1946, and the post and telegraph strike followed in July 1946. Every other order misplaces at least one of these months.
244.tq: Air (Jan) -> Navy (Feb) -> P&T (July)
xs: **RIAF strike** (**January 1946**) → **RIN revolt** (**18 February 1946**) → **post and telegraph strike** (**July 1946**) — **B, C, A**, option **(1)**.
The RIN revolt began at **HMIS Talwar, Bombay**.
xa: **Army Signal Corps, Jabalpur**: **February 1946**.
**19 Feb 1946**: Attlee announced the **Cabinet Mission**.

244.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Upsurge)
a. RIAF strike
b. Army Signal Corps action at Jabalpur
c. Post and telegraph strike

a. RIAF strike
b. Army Signal Corps action at Jabalpur
c. Post and telegraph strike

List-II (Date)
i. January 1946
ii. February 1946
iii. July 1946

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
244.x: The RIAF strike occurred in January 1946, the Jabalpur Army Signal Corps action in February 1946, and the post and telegraph strike in July 1946.
244.tq: Start from the sure date association and eliminate codes that reverse the sequence.
xs: **RIAF – January 1946**, **Jabalpur Signal Corps – February 1946**, **post and telegraph – July 1946** — option **(1) a–i, b–ii, c–iii**.
The RIN mutiny also came in **February 1946** (**18 February**).
xa: Sections of the **RIAF** and Army showed disaffection during the RIN revolt.
**20 February 1947**: British would leave by **June 1948**.

244.s: Why did the INA trials and the RIN revolt alarm the British authorities?
o: They demonstrated that the British treasury had gained complete control over India.
They showed that the Cabinet Mission had already formed a national government.
They showed that the Indian Army, on which the British relied, could no longer be fully trusted.
They proved that all princely states had joined the British government.
244.x: The British depended on the 2.5-million-strong Indian Army as their coercive instrument. The INA trials and the RIN revolt indicated that military loyalty could no longer be assumed.
244.tq: Connect the events to the strategic importance of military loyalty.
xs: They showed the **Indian Army**, on which the British relied, **could no longer be trusted** — option **(3)**.
The British relied on the **2.5-million** Indian Army — their "sword".
xa: The RIN mutiny "destroyed the loyalty" of the British Indian armed forces.
**Attlee** called Gandhi's role in the immediate transfer of power **"minimal"** by comparison.

244.s: According to Attlee's later assessment, which factor was more important than Gandhi's role in the immediate transfer of power?
o: The expansion of British territorial control
The success of the Simon Commission
The formation of the Indian Civil Service
244.x: Attlee regarded Gandhi's role in the immediate transfer of power as minimal compared with the loss of loyalty in the armed forces.
244.tq: Test the comparison between political influence and military loyalty directly.
xs: Attlee rated **the loss of military loyalty** above Gandhi's role — option **(4)** is correct.
He called Gandhi's role in the immediate transfer of power **"minimal"**.
xa: The INA trials + RIN revolt showed the **2.5-million** Indian Army could no longer be trusted.
Attlee announced the **Cabinet Mission** on **19 Feb 1946**.

244.s: When did Attlee announce the Cabinet Mission?
244.x: Attlee announced the Cabinet Mission on 19 February 1946; the Mission arrived in India on 24 March 1946.
244.tq: Separate the announcement date from the arrival and plan dates.
xs: Attlee announced the **Cabinet Mission** on **19 Feb 1946** — option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ That was **one day after** the **RIN mutiny** began (**18 Feb 1946**).
**20 February 1947** (4) was the declaration that the British would leave by **June 1948**.
xa: The RIN mutiny began at **HMIS Talwar, Bombay**.
Attlee saw the loss of military loyalty as decisive.

244.s: On 20 February 1947, Attlee declared that the British would leave India by:
244.x: Attlee's statement of 20 February 1947 set June 1948 as the deadline for British withdrawal. August 1947 is when power was actually transferred; March 1947 and January 1950 are unrelated to this announcement.
244.tq: 20 Feb 1947 -> leave by June 1948
xs: On **20 February 1947** Attlee declared the British would leave by **June 1948** — option **(2)** is correct.
**August 1947** (1) is not the date in the declaration.
xa: Earlier: **19 Feb 1946**, Attlee announced the **Cabinet Mission**.
Attlee called Gandhi's role in the immediate transfer of power **"minimal"**.

244.s: Which statement best reflects the historical debate concerning the events of February 1946?
o: Officials described them as a breakdown of discipline, while historians have viewed them as a nationwide uprising.
Officials described them as a purely civilian movement and historians accepted that view.
Historians rejected any connection between the events and the armed forces.
Officials and historians uniformly described them as a successful constitutional negotiation.
244.x: The events are debated as either a ‘mutiny’ or a ‘revolt’: officials emphasised breakdown of discipline, whereas historians have seen a broader nationwide uprising.
244.tq: Compare the two interpretations directly instead of treating one label as universally accepted.
xs: Officials called it a **breakdown of discipline**; historians see a **nationwide uprising** — option **(1)**.
This is the **"mutiny or revolt"** debate.
xa: Significance: the Raj's **coercive instrument** — the armed forces — **cracked**.
The **80th anniversary** was observed on **18 February 2026**.

244.s: The 80th anniversary of the Royal Indian Navy revolt was observed on:
244.x: The 80th anniversary of the RIN revolt was observed on 18 February 2026, marking eight decades since the revolt began in 1946.
244.tq: Calculate the anniversary from the original revolt year and distinguish the current commemorative date.
xs: The **80th anniversary** was observed on **18 February 2026** — option **(2)** is correct.
The revolt began on **18 February 1946** at **HMIS Talwar, Bombay**.
xa: It was revisited at India's **80th Independence Day** (**Aug 2026**) as a factor that hastened British withdrawal.
Debate: **"mutiny or revolt"**.

244.s: The wider significance of the INA trials and the RIN revolt was that:
o: The Cabinet Mission had ended all political disagreement in India.
The princely states had replaced the armed forces as the main coercive instrument.
The British had completely restored unquestioned military discipline.
The Raj's coercive instrument, the armed forces, had begun to crack.
244.x: The events indicated that the armed forces, which formed the coercive foundation of the Raj, were no longer fully reliable.
244.tq: Identify the broader institutional consequence rather than a narrow event detail.
xs: The Raj's **coercive instrument — the armed forces — cracked** — option **(4)** is correct.
The INA trials + RIN revolt showed the **2.5-million** Indian Army could no longer be trusted.
xa: Sections of the **RIAF** and Army also showed disaffection.
**Attlee**: Gandhi's role in the immediate transfer of power **"minimal"** vs the loss of military loyalty.

244.s: At India's 80th Independence Day in August 2026, which event was revisited as a factor that hastened British withdrawal from India?
244.x: The Royal Indian Navy revolt of 1946 was revisited at the 80th Independence Day as a factor that hastened British withdrawal, because the Raj's armed forces had cracked.
244.tq: The RIN revolt at 80, with India at 80.
xs: The **Royal Indian Navy revolt** was revisited at the **80th Independence Day** (**Aug 2026**) — option **(3)** is correct.
It is seen as a factor that **hastened British withdrawal**.
xa: Its **80th anniversary** was observed on **18 February 2026**.
It spread to about **20,000 personnel**, **78 ships**, **20 shore establishments**.

245.s: Sarojini Naidu was popularly known as which of the following?
245.x: Sarojini Naidu was popularly known as Bharat Kokila, or the Nightingale of India.
245.tq: Test a well-known title through direct recall.
xs: **Sarojini Naidu** was the **Bharat Kokila** (Nightingale of India) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Andhra Ratna** (3) was **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya**; **Bharatha Kesari** (4) was **Mannathu Padmanabhan**.
xa: She wrote **The Golden Threshold**.
First Indian woman **Congress president (1925)**, at **Kanpur**; first woman Governor (**UP**).
She took part in the **Dharasana raid (1930)**.

245.s: The title ‘Sardar’ was associated with Vallabhbhai Patel after which event?
245.x: Vallabhbhai Patel came to be known as ‘Sardar’ after his leadership in the Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928.
245.tq: Use date-and-event discrimination for a title.
xs: **Vallabhbhai Patel** got the title **"Sardar"** after **Bardoli 1928** — option **(1)** is correct.
He is also called the **Iron Man of India**.
xa: ⚠ Other titles: **Deshbandhu** = **C.R. Das**; **Loknayak** = **Jayaprakash Narayan**; **Bihar Kesari** = **Sri Krishna Sinha**.
**Andhra Kesari** = **Tanguturi Prakasam**, earned in the **Simon boycott**, Madras.

245.s:
With reference to the titles and associated personalities, consider the following statements:
1. Mannathu Padmanabhan was known as Bharatha Kesari.
2. Mannathu Padmanabhan founded the Nair Service Society.
3. He was associated with the Vaikom and Guruvayur Satyagrahas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
245.x: All three statements are correct. Mannathu Padmanabhan was associated with the title Bharatha Kesari, founded the NSS and participated in the Vaikom and Guruvayur Satyagrahas.
245.tq: Use a cluster of biographical statements and verify all three links.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Mannathu Padmanabhan** was **Bharatha Kesari (1959)** and **NSS founder**.
He took part in the **Vaikom and Guruvayur satyagrahas**.
xa: ⚠ **Andhra Kesari** = Prakasam; **Bihar Kesari** = Sri Krishna Sinha; **Bharatha Kesari** = Mannathu Padmanabhan.
**K. Kelappan**, the **"Kerala Gandhi"**, is also linked to the **Guruvayur** satyagraha.

245.s: Who called Gandhi ‘Mahatma’?
245.x: Rabindranath Tagore is associated with calling Gandhi ‘Mahatma’.
245.tq: Test the originator of a famous honorific.
xs: **Tagore** called Gandhi **"Mahatma"** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Bose** (3) called him **"Father of the Nation"**; **Gokhale** (1) was **Gandhi's political mentor**.
xa: Tagore also wrote **Jana Gana Mana** (APPSC 2025).
Gokhale was the **"Socrates of Maharashtra"** (APPSC 2025 correct pair).

245.s: Who first addressed Mahatma Gandhi as the 'Father of the Nation'?
245.x: Subhas Chandra Bose called Gandhi the 'Father of the Nation'. Tagore gave the title 'Mahatma'; Nehru and Sarojini Naidu are not credited with either title.
245.tq: Mahatma = Tagore; Father of the Nation = Bose.
xs: **Bose** called Gandhi the **"Father of the Nation"** — option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ **Tagore** (1) gave the title **"Mahatma"**.
xa: **Nehru** said **"The light has gone out of our lives"** on Gandhi's death (**1948**).
Bose compared the **Dandi March** to **Napoleon's return from Elba**.

245.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Andhra Kesari — Tanguturi Prakasam
2. Andhra Ratna — Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya
3. Deshabhakta — Konda Venkatappayya
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
245.x: All three pairs are correct: Prakasam earned 'Andhra Kesari' in the Simon boycott at Madras, Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was 'Andhra Ratna' and Konda Venkatappayya was 'Deshabhakta'. Options A, B and C leave out correct pairs.
245.tq: Andhra Kesari (Prakasam) is the most-asked Andhra title.
xs: All three pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Andhra Kesari** = **Tanguturi Prakasam** (earned in the **Simon boycott**, Madras); **Andhra Ratna** = **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya**.
**Deshabhakta** = **Konda Venkatappayya**.

Prakasam became the **first CM of Andhra State (1953)**.

245.s: Which one of the following pairs of person and description is correctly matched?
o: Gopal Krishna Gokhale — Socrates of Maharashtra and Gandhi's political mentor
Bal Gangadhar Tilak — Gandhi's political mentor
245.x: Gokhale was called the 'Socrates of Maharashtra' and was Gandhi's political mentor (APPSC 2025 pair). Tilak was not Gandhi's mentor; C.R. Das was 'Deshbandhu'; 'Bihar Kesari' was Sri Krishna Sinha; JP was 'Loknayak'.
245.tq: Gokhale = Gandhi's political guru; Deshbandhu = C.R. Das; Loknayak = JP.
xs: **Gokhale** — **"Socrates of Maharashtra"** and **Gandhi's political mentor** — option **(1)** is correct (APPSC 2025).
**C.R. Das** (3) was **Deshbandhu**; **Bihar Kesari** was **Sri Krishna Sinha**.
**Jayaprakash Narayan** (4) was **Loknayak**, not Deshbandhu.
xa: Gokhale founded the **Servants of India Society (1905)**.
**Tilak**: **"Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it"**.

245.s: ‘The Golden Threshold’ is associated with which author?
245.x: ‘The Golden Threshold’ was written by Sarojini Naidu.
245.tq: Distinguish literary works by their authors.
xs: **The Golden Threshold** is by **Sarojini Naidu** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Subramania Bharati** (4) was the Tamil nationalist poet; **Aruna Asaf Ali** hoisted the flag at **Gowalia Tank (1942)**.
xa: Sarojini Naidu = **Bharat Kokila / Nightingale of India**.
First Indian woman **Congress president (1925)**.

245.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. The Discovery of India — Jawaharlal Nehru
2. Annihilation of Caste — B.R. Ambedkar
3. Sarvodaya — Mahatma Gandhi
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
245.x: All three pairs are correct. The Discovery of India was written by Nehru, Annihilation of Caste by Ambedkar and Sarvodaya was Gandhi’s Gujarati rendering of Ruskin’s Unto This Last.
245.tq: Verify multiple work–author pairs and the associated literary source.
xs: All three pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**The Discovery of India** — **Nehru** (written in **Ahmednagar Fort** jail); **Annihilation of Caste** — **Ambedkar** (**1936**).
**Sarvodaya** — **Gandhi**, a Gujarati rendering of **John Ruskin's "Unto This Last"** (APPSC G1 2022).
xa: Gandhi's other works: **Hind Swaraj**, **The Story of My Experiments with Truth**, **Songs from Prison**.
**Pattabhi**: **History of the Indian National Congress**, **Feathers and Stones**.

245.s: In which place was Jawaharlal Nehru’s ‘The Discovery of India’ written?
245.x: Jawaharlal Nehru wrote ‘The Discovery of India’ in Ahmednagar Fort jail.
245.tq: Test the place associated with a major work.
xs: Nehru wrote **The Discovery of India** in **Ahmednagar Fort jail** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Yerwada jail** (1) is where Gandhi made **Songs from Prison** (translations of Sanskrit hymns).
xa: Nehru presided at **Lahore 1929**.
Nehru founded the **Independence for India League (1928)** with Bose.

245.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: A National Flag for India — Pingali
History of the Indian National Congress — Pattabhi

xs: **Feathers and Stones — Sarojini Naidu** is wrong: it is **Pattabhi**'s — option **(4)** is the mismatch.
The others are right: **"A National Flag for India" (1916)** — **Pingali**; **Hind Swaraj** — **Gandhi**; **History of the Indian National Congress** — **Pattabhi**.
xa: Sarojini Naidu wrote **The Golden Threshold**.
Pingali's flag design was endorsed by Gandhi at **Vijayawada (1921)**.

245.s: The song 'Jana Gana Mana' was composed by
245.x: Jana Gana Mana was written by Rabindranath Tagore (APPSC 2025). Iqbal wrote 'Saare Jahan se Achcha'; Sarojini Naidu wrote 'The Golden Threshold'; Bankim Chandra is a distractor not linked to this song.
245.tq: Jana Gana Mana = Tagore; Saare Jahan se Achcha = Iqbal.
xs: **Jana Gana Mana** was composed by **Rabindranath Tagore** — option **(3)** is correct (APPSC 2025).
**Muhammad Iqbal** (1) wrote **Saare Jahan se Achcha**; **Sarojini Naidu** (4) wrote **The Golden Threshold**.
xa: Tagore called Gandhi **"Mahatma"**.
⚠ **Saare Jahan se Achcha** = **Iqbal**; **Jana Gana Mana** = **Tagore**.

245.s: Gandhi's 'Sarvodaya' was a Gujarati rendering of which work?
o: Leo Tolstoy's 'The Kingdom of God is Within You'
245.x: Sarvodaya was Gandhi's Gujarati rendering of John Ruskin's 'Unto This Last' (APPSC G1 2022). Tolstoy and Thoreau influenced Gandhi but Sarvodaya is not their work; Hind Swaraj is Gandhi's own original book.
245.tq: Sarvodaya <- Ruskin's Unto This Last.
xs: **Sarvodaya** was Gandhi's Gujarati rendering of **John Ruskin's "Unto This Last"** — option **(2)** (APPSC G1 2022).
**Hind Swaraj** (4) is a separate work by Gandhi himself.
xa: Other Gandhi works: **The Story of My Experiments with Truth**, **Songs from Prison** (Yerwada jail).
Gandhi founded the **Harijan Sevak Sangh (1932)**.

245.s: The statement, ‘Generations to come... will scarce believe that such a one... walked upon this earth’, was made by whom?
245.x: Albert Einstein made this statement in tribute to Mahatma Gandhi.

xs: **"Generations to come... will scarce believe..."** was **Albert Einstein**'s tribute to Gandhi — option **(4)** is correct.
**Nehru** (3) said **"The light has gone out of our lives"** (**1948**).

**Tilak**: **"Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it"**.

xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Gandhi** said **"Sedition has become my religion"** (Dandi) and called the Cripps offer a **"post-dated cheque"**.
**Subhas Bose** compared the **Dandi March** to **Napoleon's return from Elba**.

**Nehru** on Gandhi's death (**1948**): **"The light has gone out of our lives"**.

xs: **Jawaharlal Nehru** said **"The light has gone out of our lives"** on Gandhi's death (**1948**) — option **(2)**.
**Einstein** (1) said **"Generations to come..."**; **Tilak** (3) said **"Swaraj is my birthright"**; **Bose** (4) compared Dandi to **Napoleon's return from Elba**.

Gandhi: **"Sedition has become my religion"**.

He founded the **Harijan Sevak Sangh** in **1932**.
xa: Its Vijayawada branch was headed by **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**.
Branches were at **Hyderabad and Vijayawada (1932)**.

245.x: Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in 1905. Pairing it with Motilal Nehru was the wrong pair in APPSC 2024; Lajpat Rai founded the Servants of the People Society; Gandhi founded the Harijan Sevak Sangh (1932).

**Indira Gandhi** founded the **Bal Charkha Sangh**.

245.x: Kanaklata Barua was the Quit India martyr from Assam. Tamluk is linked to Matangini Hazra; Sivaganga to Rani Velu Nachiyar; the Naga hills to Rani Gaidinliu.

245.s: The flag adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 22 July 1947 differed from the earlier design mainly because the Ashoka Chakra replaced the:
245.x: The Constituent Assembly adopted the present national flag on 22 July 1947, with the Ashoka Chakra replacing the charkha.
245.tq: Test the precise change in a familiar symbol.
xs: The **Ashoka Chakra** replaced the **charkha** — option **(1)** is correct.
The Constituent Assembly adopted the flag on **22 July 1947**.
xa: The earlier design was **Pingali Venkayya**'s, endorsed by Gandhi at **Vijayawada (1921)**.
**80th Independence Day**: CM recalled **Alluri** and **Pingali** (**16 Aug 2026**).

245.s: Potti Sriramulu undertook a fast unto death primarily for the formation of:
245.x: Potti Sriramulu undertook a fast unto death for the formation of Andhra State.
245.tq: Identify the specific political demand behind the fast.
xs: **Potti Sriramulu** fasted unto death for **Andhra State** — option **(4)** is correct.
He died on **15 Dec 1952** after **58** days.
xa: **Prakasam** became the **first CM of Andhra State (1953)**.
⚠ The **Koya** region (1) links to **Alluri Sitarama Raju**'s **Rampa** tribals.

245.s: The Rampa rebellion led by Alluri Sitarama Raju was directed against conditions associated with which legislation and practice?
o: Madras Forest Act of 1882 and forced labour
Government of India Act of 1935 and zamindari
Indian Councils Act of 1909 and indentured labour
Forest Rights Act of 2006 and bonded labour
245.x: The Rampa rebellion of 1922–24 was connected with opposition to the Madras Forest Act of 1882 and forced labour.
245.tq: Connect the movement with its immediate causes rather than its leader alone.
xs: The **Rampa rebellion 1922-24** opposed the **Madras Forest Act 1882** and **forced labour** — option **(1)**.
**Alluri Sitarama Raju** led **Koya and Jatapu** tribals; he was executed in **1924**.
xa: Other tribal leaders: **Birsa Munda** (**Ulgulan**, Chotanagpur), **Komaram Bheem** (**Gond**, "Jal-Jangal-Zameen").
**80th Independence Day**: CM recalled **Alluri** and **Pingali**.

245.s: Who served as the 'dictator' of the Salt Satyagraha in Andhra?
245.x: Konda Venkatappayya ('Deshabhakta') was the dictator of the Andhra Salt Satyagraha. Pattabhi founded Andhra Bank; Pingali designed the flag; Potti Sriramulu fasted for Andhra State in 1952.
245.tq: Andhra salt dictator = Konda Venkatappayya.
xs: **Konda Venkatappayya** was the **dictator** of the Andhra Salt Satyagraha — option **(2)** is correct.
He was titled **"Deshabhakta"**.
**Pattabhi** (1) founded **Andhra Bank**; **Pingali** (3) designed the flag; **Potti Sriramulu** (4) fasted for **Andhra State** (**1952**).
xa: **Prakasam** led salt satyagraha in **Madras** and at **Devarampadu**.
⚠ **Deshabhakta** = Konda Venkatappayya; **Deshbandhu** = **C.R. Das**.

245.s: The Andhra kisan movement and the Andhra Socialist Party were associated with:
245.x: N.G. Ranga was associated with the Andhra kisan movement and the Andhra Socialist Party; he also resigned his professorship in 1930.
245.tq: Match the regional organisation and movement with its leader.
xs: **N.G. Ranga** led the **Andhra kisan movement** and **Andhra Socialist Party** — option **(3)** is correct.
He **resigned his professorship (1930)**.
**Swami Sahajanand Saraswati** (2) led the **Bihar Kisan Sabha**; **Birsa Munda** (1) the **Ulgulan**; **Komaram Bheem** (4) the **Gond** movement.
xa: Sahajanand was the first president of the **All India Kisan Sabha (1936)**.
Komaram Bheem's movement: **1938-44**, **"Jal-Jangal-Zameen"**.

245.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I — Leader

a. Birsa Munda
b. Alluri Sitarama Raju
c. Komaram Bheem
 d. Swami Sahajanand Saraswati

List-II — Organisation or movement

i. Bihar Kisan Sabha
 ii. Munda Ulgulan
 iii. Gond movement
 iv. Rampa movement

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
245.x: Birsa Munda led the Munda Ulgulan, Alluri Sitarama Raju was associated with the Rampa movement, Komaram Bheem with the Gond movement and Sahajanand Saraswati with the Bihar Kisan Sabha.
245.tq: Start from the distinctive tribal movement names and complete the matching code.
xs: **Birsa Munda – Munda Ulgulan**, **Alluri – Rampa**, **Komaram Bheem – Gond movement**, **Sahajanand – Bihar Kisan Sabha** — option **(1) a–ii, b–iv, c–iii, d–i**.
Alluri led the **Koya and Jatapu** tribals of **Rampa**; the Ulgulan was in **Chotanagpur**.
xa: **Rampa rebellion 1922-24**, against the **Madras Forest Act 1882** and forced labour.
Komaram Bheem's Gond movement: **1938-44**, slogan **"Jal-Jangal-Zameen"**.
Sahajanand was first president of the **All India Kisan Sabha (1936)**.

245.s: Komaram Bheem is associated with which movement and slogan?
o: Bihar Kisan Sabha — ‘Swaraj is my birthright’
245.x: Komaram Bheem was associated with the Gond movement during 1938–44 and with the slogan ‘Jal-Jangal-Zameen’.
245.tq: Use the distinctive slogan to identify the movement and leader.
xs: **Komaram Bheem** led the **Gond movement** with the slogan **"Jal-Jangal-Zameen"** — option **(2)** is correct.
The movement ran **1938-44**.
**Munda Ulgulan** (1) was **Birsa Munda**'s; **Rampa** (4) was **Alluri**'s; **"Swaraj is my birthright"** (3) was **Tilak**'s.
xa: **Swami Sahajanand Saraswati** led the **Bihar Kisan Sabha**.
**N.G. Ranga** led the **Andhra kisan movement**.

245.s: Who was the first president of the All India Kisan Sabha formed in 1936?
245.x: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati of the Bihar Kisan Sabha was the first president of the AIKS (1936). N.G. Ranga led the Andhra kisan movement; Komaram Bheem led the Gond movement; Birsa Munda led the Ulgulan.
245.tq: AIKS 1936 first president = Sahajanand Saraswati.
xs: **Swami Sahajanand Saraswati** was first president of the **All India Kisan Sabha (1936)** — option **(2)**.
He also led the **Bihar Kisan Sabha**.
**N.G. Ranga** (1) led the **Andhra kisan movement** and **Andhra Socialist Party**.
xa: Ranga **resigned his professorship (1930)**.
**Komaram Bheem**: **Gond**; **Birsa Munda**: **Ulgulan**.

245.s: Which of the following comparative statements is correct regarding the national presence of leaders?
o: Prakasam and Rajaji were the only leaders with an all-India political role.
Rajaji, Prakasam and EMS had greater national presence than Gandhi, Nehru, Bose and Patel.
Southern leaders such as Rajaji, Prakasam and EMS had less national presence than Gandhi, Nehru, Bose and Patel.
Only EMS had a national presence, whereas Gandhi and Nehru were regional leaders.
245.x: The comparative assessment is that southern leaders such as Rajaji, Prakasam and EMS had less national presence than Gandhi, Nehru, Bose and Patel.
245.tq: Test the direction of the comparison and reject its reversal.
xs: **Southern leaders** — **Rajaji**, **Prakasam**, **EMS** — had **less national presence** than **Gandhi**, **Nehru**, **Bose**, **Patel** — option **(3)**.
Options (1), (2) and (4) reverse or distort this comparative note (**2 Sep 2026**).
xa: **Rajaji** led the **Vedaranyam salt march** and was **Madras premier 1937**.
**Prakasam** became the **first CM of Andhra State (1953)**.

245.s: Events marking the 154th anniversary of Tanguturi Prakasam were held in August 2026 at:
245.x: Events marking Tanguturi Prakasam’s 154th anniversary were held at Visakhapatnam and Ongole in August 2026.
245.tq: Use the paired locations as the decisive clue.
xs: Prakasam's **154th anniversary** events were in **Visakhapatnam and Ongole** (**Aug 2026**) — option **(1)**.
Prakasam was **Andhra Kesari**, a title earned in the **Simon boycott**, Madras.
xa: He led salt satyagraha at **Madras** and **Devarampadu**.
He was the **first CM of Andhra State (1953)**.

245.s: On the 80th Independence Day, the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh recalled which two leaders?
o: Alluri Sitarama Raju and Pingali Venkayya
245.x: The Chief Minister recalled Alluri Sitarama Raju and Pingali Venkayya on the 80th Independence Day.
245.tq: Identify the correct commemorative pair.
xs: On the **80th Independence Day** the CM recalled **Alluri Sitarama Raju and Pingali Venkayya** — option **(4)** (**16 Aug 2026**).
**Pingali** designed the flag endorsed by Gandhi at **Vijayawada (1921)**; **Alluri** led the **Rampa rebellion 1922-24**.
xa: Pingali was born at **Bhatlapenumarru**; nicknamed **"Jhanda Venkayya"**.
Alluri was executed in **1924**.

246.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kheda campaign:
1. Gandhi was its spiritual head.
2. Patel, with Mohanlal Pandya and Narahari Parikh, led the mobilisation.
3. It ended with the revenue increase being cut to about 6 per cent after the Maxwell-Broomfield inquiry.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
246.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 6 per cent cut after the Maxwell-Broomfield inquiry belongs to Bardoli (1928); Kheda ended with revenue suspended for poor peasants and confiscated property returned. A is incomplete; C and D include statement 3.
246.tq: Kheda = suspension for the poor; Bardoli = Maxwell-Broomfield, cut to 6%.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: at **Kheda**, **Gandhi** was spiritual head and **Patel** with **Mohanlal Pandya** and **Narahari Parikh** led mobilisation.
Statement 3 is wrong: the cut to about **6%** after the **Maxwell-Broomfield inquiry** belongs to **Bardoli** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Kheda outcome: **revenue suspended for poor peasants**; confiscated property returned.
Bardoli hike was about **30%** → cut to **6%**.

246.s: Which one of the following statements about the Borsad Satyagraha is correct?
o: It was led by Nehru in 1931 against the Salt Law.
It was led by Gandhi in 1918 against a crop failure assessment.
It was led by Patel in 1922 against the Rowlatt Act.
It was led by Patel in 1923 against a punitive tax.
246.x: The Borsad Satyagraha took place in 1923 under Patel’s leadership and opposed a punitive tax.
246.tq: Use the year–leader–issue combination to reject swapped movements.
xs: **Borsad Satyagraha**: led by **Patel** in **1923** against a **punitive tax** — option **(4)**.
**1922** (3) was Patel's **Sarabandi (no-tax) campaign**, not Borsad.
xa: ⚠ **1922 – 1923 – 1928** = **Sarabandi – Borsad – Bardoli**.
Sarabandi was led by Patel (**BPSC 2019** key).

246.s:
Arrange the following campaigns in chronological order:
A. Borsad Satyagraha
B. Bardoli Satyagraha
C. Kheda campaign
D. Sarabandi campaign
246.x: The correct sequence is Kheda (1918), Sarabandi (1922), Borsad (1923) and Bardoli (1928).
246.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the middle campaigns.
xs: **Kheda → Sarabandi (1922) → Borsad (1923) → Bardoli (1928)** — **C, D, A, B**, option **(1)**.
Kheda was the early campaign with **Gandhi** as spiritual head.
xa: Bardoli: **30%** hike cut to **6%** after the **Maxwell-Broomfield inquiry**.
Patel got the title **"Sardar"** at **Bardoli (1928)**.

246.s: The Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928 was launched primarily against which of the following?
o: A ban on the cultivation of indigo
A punitive police tax imposed after a dacoity
A substantial enhancement of land revenue despite floods and famine
Compulsory recruitment into the colonial army
246.x: The Bardoli movement opposed an approximately 30 per cent increase in land revenue imposed despite floods and famine.
246.tq: Identify the specific issue rather than the leader or year.
xs: Bardoli opposed a **land revenue** hike of about **30%** despite **floods and famine** — option **(3)**.
It was held in **1928** in Bardoli taluk (**Gujarat**, Bombay Presidency).
A **punitive tax** (2) was the issue at **Borsad** (**1923**).
xa: Outcome: hike suspended, **fresh survey**; **Maxwell-Broomfield** cut it to about **6%**.
Women joined in large numbers: **Mithuben Petit**, **Bhaktiba**, **Maniben Patel**.

246.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the method adopted during the Bardoli Satyagraha?
o: A disciplined no-tax campaign supported by a village intelligence network
An armed revolt supported by neighbouring princely states
A legal challenge before the Privy Council alone
A boycott of imported cloth without revenue refusal
246.x: Patel organised a disciplined no-tax campaign and maintained a village intelligence network during Bardoli Satyagraha.
246.tq: Distinguish the organisational method from the cause of the movement.
xs: Bardoli used a disciplined **no-tax campaign** with a **village intelligence network** — option **(1)**.
The leader was **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel** — ⚠ not Gandhi (UPPSC 2005; UPSC 2003).
xa: Issue: land revenue enhanced by about **30%**.
Women participants: **Mithuben Petit**, **Bhaktiba**, **Maniben Patel**.

246.s: The Maxwell-Broomfield inquiry, associated with the Bardoli Satyagraha, resulted in which of the following?
o: Reduction of the proposed increase to about 6 per cent after a fresh survey
Recognition of complete tax exemption for all peasants
Transfer of Bardoli taluk to a princely state
Withdrawal of the entire land revenue system
246.x: The government suspended the enhanced assessment and ordered a fresh survey; the Maxwell-Broomfield inquiry reduced the increase to about 6 per cent.
246.tq: Test the inquiry and its quantitative outcome together.
xs: The **Maxwell-Broomfield inquiry** cut the increase to about **6%** after a **fresh survey** — option **(1)**.
The government first **suspended the hike** and ordered the survey.
xa: The original enhancement was about **30%**, despite floods and famine.
Bardoli (**1928**) gave Patel the title **"Sardar"**.

246.s: Which one of the following satyagrahas was led by Vallabhbhai Patel and NOT by Gandhi?
246.x: The Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928 in Gujarat was led by Patel, not Gandhi (UPSC 2003, UPPSC 2005). Champaran, the Ahmedabad Mill Strike and the Dandi March were led by Gandhi.
246.tq: Bardoli = Patel; the usual trap is to credit Gandhi.
xs: **Bardoli Satyagraha, 1928** was led by **Patel**, not Gandhi — option **(2)** (UPPSC 2005; UPSC 2003).
Exam angle: "**which satyagraha was not led by Gandhi**".
xa: Patel's other campaigns: **Sarabandi (1922)**, **Borsad (1923)**.
At **Kheda**, Gandhi was spiritual head while **Patel** led mobilisation.

246.s:
Consider the following statements about Patel’s organisational role in the Congress:
1. He headed the Congress Parliamentary Board.
2. He ran the 1937 provincial elections under the Government of India Act, 1935.
3. He supervised Congress ministries in matters including discipline, elections and finances.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
246.x: All three are correct: as head of the Congress Parliamentary Board Patel ran the 1937 provincial elections held under the Government of India Act 1935 and supervised the Congress ministries' discipline, elections and finances. So D; A, B and C each leave out a correct statement.
246.tq: Use the institutional office to connect elections, ministries and party administration.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Patel headed the **Congress Parliamentary Board** and ran the **1937 provincial elections** under the **Government of India Act 1935**.
He supervised Congress ministries — **discipline, elections, finances**.
xa: He was **Gujarat PCC** president for **over two decades**.
Assessment: **"While Gandhi gave the moral vision, Patel was the machine"**.

246.s: The statement ‘While Gandhi gave the moral vision, Patel was the machine’ primarily highlights Patel’s
o: leadership of the Indian National Army
246.x: The statement contrasts Gandhi’s moral vision with Patel’s strong organisational and administrative machinery within the Congress.
246.tq: Interpret a descriptive political statement through its central contrast.
xs: The line stresses Patel's **organisational and administrative effectiveness** — option **(1)**.
He headed the **Congress Parliamentary Board**, running the **1937** elections and supervising ministries.
xa: **Gujarat PCC** president for **over two decades**.
Post-1947: **Home Minister**, in charge of the **States Department**.

246.s: Vallabhbhai Patel served as President of the Gujarat Pradesh Congress Committee for
246.x: Patel served as President of the Gujarat PCC for over two decades.
246.tq: Distinguish a broad duration from precise but unsupported numerical distractors.
xs: Patel was **Gujarat PCC** president for **over two decades** — option **(3)**.
He also headed the **Congress Parliamentary Board** (**1937** elections).
xa: "While Gandhi gave the moral vision, **Patel was the machine**".
He led Gujarat's peasant campaigns: **Sarabandi**, **Borsad**, **Bardoli**.

246.s: Which of the following portfolios did Vallabhbhai Patel hold in the Interim Government formed on 2 September 1946?
246.x: In the Interim Government under Nehru, Patel held the Home and Information & Broadcasting portfolios.
246.tq: Avoid swapping neighbouring portfolios in a cabinet question.
xs: In the **Interim Government** (**2 September 1946**, under Nehru) Patel held **Home + Information & Broadcasting** — option **(1)**.
After independence he was **first Deputy Prime Minister** and **Home Minister**.
xa: He ran the **States Department** with **V.P. Menon** as Secretary.
In the Constituent Assembly he chaired the **Provincial Constitution Committee**.

246.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Patel’s positions after independence:
1. He was the first Deputy Prime Minister of India.
2. He was the first Home Minister of India.
3. He was in charge of the States Department, whose Secretary was V.P. Menon.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
246.x: All three statements are correct. Patel was the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister and handled the States Department with V.P. Menon as Secretary.
246.tq: Combine first-office facts with the department–secretary relationship.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Patel was the **first Deputy Prime Minister**, also **Home Minister**.
He was in charge of the **States Department**, Secretary **V.P. Menon**.
xa: He **created** the All India Services (**IAS/IPS**).
Earlier, in the **Interim Government** (**2 September 1946**): Home + I&B.

246.s: Which of the following committees of the Constituent Assembly was chaired by Vallabhbhai Patel?
o: Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities, Tribal and Excluded Areas
246.x: Patel chaired the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities, Tribal and Excluded Areas, as well as the Provincial Constitution Committee.
246.tq: Identify the correct committee instead of a better-known committee associated with another leader.
xs: Patel chaired the **Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities, Tribal and Excluded Areas** — option **(1)**.
He also chaired the **Provincial Constitution Committee**.
xa: In the **Interim Government** he held **Home** + **Information & Broadcasting**.
Patel called the civil service the **"steel frame"**.

246.s: The description of the Indian civil service as the ‘steel frame’ of India was used by Patel to emphasise that
o: it was intended only for military administration
it could function without constitutional safeguards
if it bends, the whole structure will collapse
it should be replaced entirely by provincial services
246.x: Patel stated that if the civil service steel frame bends, the whole structure will collapse, stressing its importance to national administration.
246.tq: Complete the distinctive metaphor with its stated consequence.
