xa: Causes: **McMahon Line**, **Aksai Chin**, **Dalai Lama** asylum, **Forward Policy**.
The war came after **Chou En-lai**'s border talks (**April 1960**).
The **1962** war also derailed the **Third Plan**.

254.s: The Atomic Energy Commission was established in 1948 under the leadership of:
254.x: The Atomic Energy Commission was established in 1948 under Homi J. Bhabha.
254.tq: Direct institution–year–person association with other Nehru-era figures as distractors.
xs: The **Atomic Energy Commission** (**1948**) was under **Homi Bhabha** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Mahalanobis** is linked to the **Second Plan** model; **Krishna Menon** was **Defence Minister** in **1962**.
It was one of the institutions built in the Nehru era.
xa: **CSIR**: **1942**; its national laboratories grew under Nehru.
**IIT Kharagpur** (first IIT): **1951**.
**AIIMS** New Delhi: **1956** (AIIMS Act).

254.s:
Match List-I (Institution) with List-II (Year):
List-I
a. IIT Kharagpur (first IIT)
b. AIIMS, New Delhi
c. CSIR
List-II
i. 1942
ii. 1951
iii. 1956
Select the correct answer:
254.x: IIT Kharagpur = 1951, AIIMS New Delhi = 1956 (AIIMS Act), CSIR = 1942, so A (a-ii, b-iii, c-i) is correct. B swaps the IIT and AIIMS years; C gives AIIMS 1942 and CSIR 1956; D gives IIT 1942 and CSIR 1951.
254.tq: CSIR predates independence (1942); IIT 1951; AIIMS 1956.
xs: **a-ii, b-iii, c-i** — option **(1)** is correct.
**IIT Kharagpur** (first IIT) — **1951**.
**AIIMS, New Delhi** — **1956** (AIIMS Act).
xa: **Atomic Energy Commission** — **1948**, under **Homi Bhabha**.
**UGC** — set up **1953**, statutory **1956**.
**Rabindra Bharati**, Hyderabad — inaugurated by Nehru on **11 October 1961**.

254.s:
Consider the following statements about the University Grants Commission:
1. It was set up in 1953.
2. It became a statutory body under the UGC Act, 1956.
3. It was established as a constitutional body in 1953.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
254.x: The UGC was set up in 1953 and became statutory under the UGC Act, 1956. It was not a constitutional body.
254.tq: Distinguish the year of establishment from the year and nature of statutory recognition.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **UGC** was set up in **1953**.
Statement 2 correct: it became **statutory** under the **UGC Act, 1956**.
Statement 3 wrong: it is a **statutory**, not a constitutional, body.
xa: ⚠ UGC: set up **1953**, statutory **1956**.
**AIIMS** New Delhi also dates from **1956** (AIIMS Act).
**IIT Kharagpur**, the first IIT: **1951**.

254.s: Rabindra Bharati at Hyderabad was built to commemorate the birth centenary of Rabindranath Tagore and was inaugurated by Nehru on:
254.x: Rabindra Bharati, Hyderabad, was built for Tagore's birth centenary and was inaugurated by Jawaharlal Nehru on 11 October 1961.
254.tq: Combine purpose, place and inauguration date in a precise institutional recall question.
xs: **Rabindra Bharati**, Hyderabad, was inaugurated by **Nehru** on **11 October 1961** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was built for **Tagore's birth centenary**.
**29 April 1954** is Panchsheel; **15 August 1947** is Nehru becoming PM; **27 May 1964** is his death.
xa: AP angle: this is the topic's **Andhra/Hyderabad** link.
**December 1961**: liberation of **Goa** (**Operation Vijay**).
**1961**: **NAM** formalised at **Belgrade**.

254.s:
With reference to Indian secularism, consider the following statements:
1. India has no State religion.
2. The State remains neutral towards religions.
3. The State may intervene to reform certain social practices.
4. Indian secularism is identical to the Western model of strict separation in all respects.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
254.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 correctly describe Indian secularism. Statement 4 is incorrect because Indian secularism differs from the Western model of strict separation and permits State intervention for social reform.
254.tq: Reject the absolute comparison created by the phrase 'identical in all respects'.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(1)** is correct.
Statements 1-3: **Sarva Dharma Sambhava** — **no state religion**; State **neutral** but **may reform social practices**.
Statement 4 wrong: Indian secularism differs from the **Western model of strict separation**.
xa: **Art. 30**: protects **minority educational institutions**.
**Art. 325**: bars **religious exclusion from electoral rolls**.
**Art. 343**: **Hindi in Devanagari** official, with English for **15 years**.

254.s: Which Article of the Constitution protects the educational institutions of minorities?
254.x: Article 30 protects the rights of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions.
254.tq: Discriminate between closely related constitutional Articles by their specific subject.
xs: **Article 30** protects **minority educational institutions** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Art. 325** bars religious exclusion from **electoral rolls**.
**Art. 343** makes **Hindi in Devanagari** the official language.
xa: Indian secularism: **Sarva Dharma Sambhava**.
**No state religion**; State neutral but may **reform social practices**.
English was to continue for **15 years** under Art. 343.

254.s: Article 325 of the Constitution is significant in the context of minority rights because it:
o: prescribes Hindi in Devanagari as the official language
bars religious exclusion from electoral rolls
254.x: Article 325 prohibits exclusion from electoral rolls on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex; in this context it bars religious exclusion from electoral rolls.
254.tq: Separate Article 325 from Articles 30 and 343 by matching the provision to its function.
xs: **Article 325** **bars religious exclusion from electoral rolls** — option **(4)** is correct.
Minority educational institutions are protected by **Art. 30**.
**Hindi in Devanagari** as official language is **Art. 343**; Hindu succession came by the **Hindu Succession Act 1956**.
xa: Indian secularism = **Sarva Dharma Sambhava**.
Contrast: the **Western model** of strict separation.
English with Hindi for **15 years** (Art. 343).

254.s: Article 343 provides for which of the following language arrangements?
o: Hindi in Devanagari script as the official language, with English continuing for 15 years
Sanskrit as the official language with Hindi for 15 years
English as the sole official language of India
Hindi and all regional languages as equally official Union languages
254.x: Article 343 made Hindi in the Devanagari script the official language and provided for the use of English for 15 years.
254.tq: Combine the constitutional Article with both the script and the specified time period.
xs: Art. 343: **Hindi in Devanagari** is the official language, with **English for 15 years** — option **(1)** is correct.
English was not made the sole official language, nor were regional languages made equal Union languages.
Sanskrit has no such role in Art. 343.
xa: **Art. 30**: minority educational institutions.
**Art. 325**: no religious exclusion from electoral rolls.
Secularism: **Sarva Dharma Sambhava**.

254.s: The Indian model of secularism, under which the State has no religion but may intervene to reform social practices, is described as
o: Strict separation of Church and State
254.x: Indian secularism is Sarva Dharma Sambhava: no state religion, the State is neutral but may reform social practices. Strict separation and laicite describe the Western model; a theocracy has a state religion.
254.tq: India = Sarva Dharma Sambhava, not strict separation.
xs: Indian secularism is **Sarva Dharma Sambhava** — option **(2)** is correct.
**No state religion**; the State is **neutral** but **may reform social practices**.
**Strict separation** is the **Western model**, which India's model differs from.
xa: **Art. 30** protects **minority educational institutions**.
**Art. 325** bars **religious exclusion** from electoral rolls.
The **Hindu Code Bill** is an example of State-led social reform.

254.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar served as Labour Member of the Viceroy’s Executive Council during which period?
254.x: Ambedkar served as Labour Member of the Viceroy’s Executive Council from 1942 to 1946.
254.tq: Match the office with its specific tenure and distinguish it from his post-Independence ministerial role.
xs: Ambedkar was **Labour Member** of the **Viceroy's Executive Council** in **1942-46** — option **(4)** is correct.
**1947-1951** was his term as **first Law Minister** of free India.
He resigned in **1951** over the **Hindu Code Bill**.
xa: Law Minister in **Nehru's first cabinet** (**1947**).
Hindu Code Bill introduced in **1947**.
It sought equal rights in **inheritance, marriage, divorce** and adoption.

254.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar resigned from the Union Cabinet in 1951 primarily because which proposal was stalled and diluted?
254.x: Ambedkar resigned in 1951, on 27 September, when the Hindu Code Bill dealing with women’s rights in inheritance, marriage and divorce was stalled and diluted.
254.tq: Link the resignation to the specific legislative issue rather than to a general political disagreement.
xs: He resigned in **1951** because the **Hindu Code Bill** was **stalled and diluted** — option **(3)** is correct.
He was then **Law Minister** in Nehru's cabinet.
The Bill sought equal rights for Hindu women in **inheritance, marriage, divorce** and adoption.
xa: It was later passed in parts: **Hindu Marriage Act 1955**.
**Hindu Succession**, **Minority and Guardianship**, **Adoptions and Maintenance** Acts — all **1956**.
⚠ Marriage Act = **1955**; the other three = **1956**.

254.s: The Hindu Code Bill was primarily intended to provide Hindu women with equal rights in:
o: Employment, taxation, property registration and federal representation
Voting, citizenship, language and education only
Religious conversion, pilgrimage, temple administration and succession only
254.x: The Hindu Code Bill aimed at equal rights for Hindu women in inheritance, marriage, divorce and adoption.
254.tq: Choose the option covering all the stated subject areas of the Bill.
xs: Equal rights for Hindu women in **inheritance, marriage, divorce and adoption** — option **(4)** is correct.
The Bill was introduced in **1947** by **Ambedkar** as Law Minister.
It **stalled** and was diluted, so he **resigned** in **1951**.
xa: **Hindu Marriage Act 1955**.
**Hindu Succession Act 1956**; **Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act 1956**.
**Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act 1956**.

254.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched regarding later enactments connected with the Hindu Code Bill?
254.x: The Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act was enacted in 1956, not 1957. The other three pairings are correct.
254.tq: Check the year in each legal enactment and identify the single altered date.
xs: **Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act — 1957** is wrongly matched — option **(2)** is correct.
It was passed in **1956**.
The others are right: **Succession — 1956**, **Minority and Guardianship — 1956**, **Marriage — 1955**.
xa: ⚠ Marriage Act = **1955**; the other three = **1956**.
These Acts passed the **Hindu Code Bill** in parts.
Ambedkar resigned as **Law Minister** in **1951** when it stalled.

254.s: In Jawaharlal Nehru's first cabinet of independent India (1947), Dr. B.R. Ambedkar held the post of
254.x: Ambedkar was free India's first Law Minister in Nehru's 1947 cabinet and resigned in 1951 over the Hindu Code Bill. He had been Labour Member of the Viceroy's Executive Council (1942-46), before independence; he was not Home or Education Minister.
254.tq: Labour Member 1942-46 (Viceroy's Council); Law Minister 1947-51.
xs: Ambedkar was the **first Law Minister** in **Nehru's first cabinet** (**1947**) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Labour Member** was his earlier post on the **Viceroy's Executive Council** (**1942-46**), before independence.
He resigned in **1951** over the **Hindu Code Bill**.
xa: The Bill sought rights in **inheritance, marriage, divorce** and adoption.
**Hindu Marriage Act 1955**.
**Hindu Succession Act 1956**.

254.s: Who was appointed Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog, the successor to the Planning Commission, in the current-affairs reference cited?
254.x: Ashok Kumar Lahiri was appointed Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog, which succeeded the Planning Commission.
254.tq: Match the current appointment with the institution and its predecessor.
xs: **Ashok Kumar Lahiri** was appointed Vice-Chairperson of **NITI Aayog** — option **(1)** is correct (May **2026**).
NITI Aayog replaced the **Planning Commission** on **1 Jan 2015**.
**Nehru** chaired the Planning Commission; **Mahalanobis** gave the Second Plan model.
xa: Planning Commission: first Deputy Chairman **Gulzarilal Nanda**; last **M.S. Ahluwalia**.
Abolition announced by PM **Narendra Modi** on **15 Aug 2014**.
Planning Commission set up on **15 March 1950**.

254.s: The Indian Council of World Affairs (ICWA) was associated with which of the following events and milestones?
o: It hosted the Non-Aligned Movement summit in 1961 and marked 50 years as an Institution of National Importance.
It hosted the Simla Conference in 1947 and marked 25 years as a national university.
It hosted the Bandung Conference in 1955 and marked 15 years as an Institution of National Importance.
It hosted the Asian Relations Conference in 1947 and marked 25 years as an Institution of National Importance.
254.x: ICWA hosted Nehru's Asian Relations Conference in 1947 and marked 25 years as an Institution of National Importance.
254.tq: Pair the institution with both its associated conference and numerical milestone.
xs: **ICWA** hosted the **Asian Relations Conference (1947)** and marked **25 years** as an **Institution of National Importance** — option **(4)** is correct.
The report is dated **17 Sep 2026**.
**NAM** was formalised at **Belgrade** (**1961**); **Bandung** (**1955**) was in Indonesia — neither hosted by ICWA.
xa: Nehru's broadcast on staying independent of **power blocs**: **7 September 1946**.
**Panchsheel**: **29 April 1954**.
**Colombo Powers** sponsored Bandung.

254.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Mahalanobis strategy was criticised for neglecting agriculture.
2. Panchsheel succeeded in preventing the war of 1962.
3. The Mahalanobis strategy gave primary emphasis to industrial development.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
254.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The Mahalanobis strategy was criticised for neglecting agriculture, while Panchsheel did not prevent the 1962 war, making statement 2 false.
254.tq: Identify the reversed historical outcome in the statement about Panchsheel.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **Mahalanobis strategy neglected agriculture**.
Statement 2 wrong: **Panchsheel did not stop the 1962 war**.
Statement 3 correct: it gave priority to **heavy/capital-goods industry**.
xa: Result of the neglect: **food shortages, inflation**.
Second Plan model: **Nehru-Mahalanobis-Feldman**.
First Plan instead put **agriculture** first (**Harrod-Domar**).

255.s: Which of the following correctly explains the employment imbalance faced by Telugu people in the Madras Presidency around 1910?
o: Telugus formed about 40 percent of the population but held a disproportionately small share of senior posts.
Telugus and non-Telugus held equal shares in all government posts.
Telugus formed about 40 percent of the population and held all district-level posts.
Telugus formed less than 10 percent of the population and dominated the highest posts.
255.x: A is correct: Telugus were about 40% (2 crore) of the Madras Presidency around 1910, yet held only 8 high State jobs against 56 for non-Telugus and no District Judge posts (0 of 19).
255.tq: Compare population share with administrative representation rather than reading either figure in isolation.
xs: Telugus were about **40% (2 crore)** of the Madras Presidency around **1910** but held a **disproportionately small share of senior posts** — option **(1)** is correct.
**High jobs in the State**: Telugu **8**, non-Telugu **56**.
**District Judges**: Telugu **0**, non-Telugu **19**.
xa: Deputy Collectors: **21** Telugu vs **39**; District Munsifs: **30** vs **93**.
Telugus were lumped together as "**Madrasis**".
**Tamil dominance** of politics, education and jobs in the Madras capital fed the grievance.

255.s:
Consider the following statements regarding government employment in the Madras Presidency:
1. Telugus held 21 of the Deputy Collector posts.
2. Telugus held no District Judge posts.
3. Telugus held 30 District Munsif posts.
4. Telugus held 56 high State jobs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: Telugus held 21 Deputy Collector posts, no District Judge posts and 30 District Munsif posts. They held 8 high State jobs, while non-Telugus held 56; therefore statement 4 is false.
255.tq: Check each numerical row against the comparison table, especially the reversed final figure.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: Telugus held **21** Deputy Collector posts (non-Telugu **39**).
Statement 2 correct: **0** District Judges (non-Telugu **19**); statement 3 correct: **30** District Munsifs (non-Telugu **93**).
Statement 4 wrong: Telugus held only **8** high State jobs; **56** was the non-Telugu figure.
xa: Telugus were about **40% (2 crore)** of the Presidency around **1910**.
Education (**1915**): only **8 of 31** colleges in Andhra.
**No engineering, medical or law college** in Andhra.

255.s: In 1915, how many colleges in the Madras Presidency were located in Andhra?
255.x: Only 8 of the 31 colleges in the Madras Presidency were located in Andhra in 1915.
255.tq: Test the exact numerator from a population-distribution figure.
xs: Only **8** of the **31** colleges were in Andhra in **1915** — option **(2)** is correct.
Andhra had **163 of 583** secondary schools.
It had **no engineering, medical or law college**.
xa: Hence the **1st session, Bapatla 1913** first demanded a separate **Telugu university**.
The Tamil-dominated **Madras University** neglected Telugu.
**Andhra University** was established on **26 April 1926**.

255.s: Which of the following educational facilities was absent in Andhra in 1915?
255.x: In 1915, Andhra had no engineering, medical or law college, although it had 8 colleges and 163 secondary schools.
255.tq: Identify the absent category in a list of educational deficiencies.
xs: Andhra had **no engineering, medical or law college** in **1915** — option **(2)** is correct.
It did have colleges (**8 of 31**) and secondary schools (**163 of 583**), so options (3) and (4) are wrong.
The **2nd** Mahasabha (**1914**, Vijayawada) asked for an **engineering college**.
xa: University demand first raised at **Bapatla, 1913**; reiterated at **Vijayawada, 1914**.
Also sought: agricultural and medical colleges + a **port at Visakhapatnam**.
**Telugu medium** in secondary schools was demanded at the **3rd session (1915)**.

255.s: The political, educational and employment dominance of which group in the Madras capital intensified Telugu grievances?
255.x: Tamils dominated politics, education and government employment in the Madras capital, contributing to Telugu dissatisfaction.
255.tq: Test the dominant regional group associated with the grievance.
xs: The dominance of the **Tamils** in politics, education and jobs in the Madras capital fed Telugu grievances — option **(4)** is correct.
Telugus held only **8** high State jobs against **56** for non-Telugus.
They were lumped together as "**Madrasis**".
xa: **Revenue grievance**: surplus revenue from the **Andhra deltas** allegedly spent on **Tamil areas**.
Precedent: **Partition of Bengal 1905**, annulled **1911**; **Bihar and Orissa** separated **1912**.
**Vande Mataram movement (1905-11)** politicised Andhra youth.

255.s: The Rayalaseema leadership alleged that surplus revenue from the Andhra deltas was spent mainly on:
255.x: C is correct: a key revenue grievance was that surplus revenue from the Andhra deltas was allegedly spent on Tamil areas of the Madras Presidency.
255.tq: Identify the alleged direction of regional revenue transfer.
xs: Surplus revenue from the **Andhra deltas** was allegedly spent on **Tamil areas** — option **(3)** is correct.
This was the **revenue grievance** among the causes of the movement.
It sat alongside **Tamil dominance** in politics, education and jobs.
xa: Telugus: about **40%** of the Presidency around **1910**.
Telugus held **0** District Judge posts against **19**.
**7th session** (**1919**, Guntur) backed the province with data on the **drain from coastal Andhra**.

255.s: Which districts were the most enthusiastic supporters of the demand for a separate Andhra province?
255.x: Krishna and Guntur were the most eager supporters of the demand for a separate Andhra province.
255.tq: Separate the leading districts from the lukewarm regions.
xs: **Krishna and Guntur** were the most eager — they **led the demand** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Rayalaseema**, **Nellore** (close to Madras) and the northern districts (**Ganjam, Visakhapatnam**) were **lukewarm**.
Krishna and Guntur delegates were disappointed when **Bapatla (1913)** deferred the province resolution.
xa: The **Youngmen's Literary Association**, **Guntur** (**1903**), was the **cradle** of the movement.
The **Nidadavolu (1912)** conference joined **Guntur, Krishna, Godavari**.
Regional suspicion: Rayalaseema and Nellore saw the body as **Circars/Brahmin-led**.

255.s: Why were Nellore, Rayalaseema, Ganjam and Visakhapatnam comparatively lukewarm towards the separate Andhra demand?
o: They were close to or connected with competing administrative and regional interests.
They opposed all forms of provincial representation.
They had already become part of Hyderabad State.
255.x: Nellore was close to Madras, while Rayalaseema and the northern districts of Ganjam and Visakhapatnam were less enthusiastic for regional and administrative reasons. They were not devoid of Telugu population or opposed to all representation.
255.tq: Apply the regional comparison to explain differing levels of political enthusiasm.
xs: They were **close to or connected with competing administrative and regional interests** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Nellore** was **close to Madras**; **Rayalaseema** and the northern districts (**Ganjam, Visakhapatnam**) were **lukewarm**.
They were Telugu areas, so option (1) is wrong.
xa: Rayalaseema (**Mahanandi**, April **1913**) called the demand a "**Brahmin movement**".
The **Nellore** meeting after Bapatla called the demand "**not yet ripe**".
The **1917** district-wise vote at **Nellore** answered such suspicion.

255.s: The separation of Bihar and Orissa in 1912 demonstrated that:
o: The Madras Presidency could not be divided.
Provinces could be redrawn on linguistic lines.
Language had no role in territorial administration.
Only princely states could be reorganised.
255.x: The separation of Bihar and Orissa was cited as evidence that provincial boundaries could be redrawn on linguistic lines.
255.tq: Infer the political significance of a historical example.
xs: It showed that **provinces could be redrawn on linguistic lines** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Bihar and Orissa** were separated in **1912**.
The **Partition of Bengal** (**1905**, annulled **1911**) was the related precedent.
xa: Andhra leaders also cited **Bihar and Orissa's separate Congress circles** when asking for an Andhra PCC.
**Vande Mataram movement (1905-11)** politicised Andhra youth.
The province demand was raised from **1911** onward.

255.s: The Vande Mataram movement of 1905–1911 contributed to the Andhra movement by:
255.x: The Vande Mataram movement between 1905 and 1911 politicised Andhra youth and helped create a favourable climate for regional mobilisation.
255.tq: Match a movement with its stated social and political effect.
xs: The **Vande Mataram movement (1905-11)** **politicised Andhra youth** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **Dhar Commission** came much later (**1948**); **district-wise voting** began at **Nellore (1917)**.
A separate university was demanded only from **1913**.
xa: Precedents: **Partition of Bengal 1905**, annulled **1911**; **Bihar and Orissa 1912**.
**Swarajya** (Vandemataram era), Vijayawada — edited by **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao**.
Separate province demand raised from **1911**.

255.s: Who wrote the series of articles titled “On the present position of the Telugu people” in The Hindu in 1911?
255.x: Jonnavittula Gurunatham of the Youngmen's Literary Association, Guntur, wrote the series in The Hindu in 1911.
255.tq: Match the article series with its author and newspaper.
xs: **Jonnavittula Gurunatham** wrote the series in **The Hindu** — option **(3)** is correct.
It ran as **6 articles in 1911**; "Are Telugu people backward?" appeared on **15 April 1911**.
He belonged to the **Youngmen's Literary Association, Guntur**.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** the **APPSC G2 2017** key named "**Sitarama Sastri**"; notes give Gurunatham.
**Pattabhi Sitaramayya** also wrote in The Hindu on the case for **linguistic states**.
Gurunatham moved the first formal province resolution at **Nidadavolu, 1912**.

255.s: Which newspaper was described as the only daily from British Andhra?
255.x: Deshabhimani was an Anglo-Telugu paper from Guntur and was described as the only daily from British Andhra.
255.tq: Identify the newspaper through its distinctive status and location.
xs: **Deshabhimani** was the **only daily from British Andhra** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was an **Anglo-Telugu** paper from **Guntur**, edited by **Seshagirirao**.
**Andhra Patrika** became a daily only in **1914** and was based in Bombay, later Madras; **Andhra Advocate** was a **weekly**.
xa: **4 Feb 1910**: first call for a political meeting on Andhra problems.
**Dec 1911**: English supplement for **George V's Delhi coronation**.
It argued **Telugu culture has no protection without a government of its own** (**APPSC 2017**).

255.s: Who edited Deshabhimani and argued that the distant Madras capital and officials unfamiliar with Telugu harmed Andhra?
255.x: Seshagirirao, the editor of Deshabhimani, criticised the distance of the Madras capital and the lack of Telugu knowledge among administrators.
255.tq: Use the editor–argument association to distinguish among newspaper personalities.
xs: **Seshagirirao**, editor of **Deshabhimani**, made this argument — option **(1)** is correct.
He said the **distant Madras capital** and **administrators ignorant of Telugu** hurt Andhra.
**Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** founded **Andhra Patrika**; **Konda Venkatappayya** founded **Krishna Patrika**.
xa: Deshabhimani: Anglo-Telugu, **Guntur**, only daily from British Andhra.
**4 Feb 1910**: first call for a political meeting on Andhra problems.
**Gurunatham** wrote on Telugu backwardness in **The Hindu** (**1911**).

255.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Patrika:
1. It was founded in Bombay and later moved to Madras.
2. It became a daily in 1914.
3. Its name was chosen to popularise the word “Andhra”.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: Andhra Patrika was founded in Bombay, moved to Madras, became a daily in 1914, and helped popularise the word “Andhra”.
255.tq: Verify each newspaper attribute independently before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All **three statements** are correct — option **(4)** is correct.
Statement 1: **Andhra Patrika** was founded in **Bombay** (**9 Sep 1908**) and later moved to **Madras**.
Statement 2: it became a **daily** from **1914**.
Statement 3: its name was chosen to **popularise the word "Andhra"**.
xa: Founder: **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** ("**Desoddharaka**").
Its reply to Tamil opposition: "Tamils separating from Telugus will not harm **national unity**".
The **Sri Bagh Pact** (**1937**) was signed at Kasinathuni's Madras house.

255.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Janmabhumi — English supplement for George V's coronation
255.x: The English supplement for George V's coronation was published by Deshabhimani. Janmabhumi carried the view on 25 August 1920 that the Andhra movement could serve national unity.
255.tq: Find the swapped newspaper contribution in a closely related list.
xs: **Janmabhumi — English supplement for George V's coronation** is wrongly matched — option **(4)** is correct.
That supplement (**Dec 1911**) was published by **Deshabhimani**.
**Janmabhumi** wrote on **25 Aug 1920** that the Andhra movement can serve **national unity**.
The others are right: **Andhra Advocate** — weekly; **Krishna Patrika** — **1902**; **Andhra Patrika** — **1908**.
xa: Andhra Advocate was started by the **Vizag** district committee (**1913**).
Krishna Patrika: **Konda Venkatappayya**, later edited by **Mutnuri Krishna Rao**.
Andhra Patrika: **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**.

255.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Newspaper)
a. Deshabhimani
b. Andhra Patrika
c. Andhra Advocate
 d. Janmabhumi
List-II (Contribution)
i. Propaganda by the Vizag district committee
 ii. The Andhra movement can serve national unity
 iii. Popularisation of the word “Andhra”
 iv. Demand for protection of Telugu culture through its own government
Select the correct answer using the code below.
255.x: Deshabhimani argued for protection of Telugu culture through its own government; Andhra Patrika popularised “Andhra”; Andhra Advocate was used for propaganda; and Janmabhumi linked the Andhra movement with national unity.
255.tq: Start from the sure newspaper–contribution pairs and eliminate inconsistent codes.
xs: **a–iv, b–iii, c–i, d–ii** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Deshabhimani**: no protection for **Telugu culture without its own government**.
**Andhra Patrika**: popularised the word "**Andhra**"; **Andhra Advocate**: propaganda by the **Vizag district committee**.
**Janmabhumi**: the Andhra movement can serve **national unity** (**25 Aug 1920**).
xa: Andhra Advocate was started at the Vizag meeting under **Manda Suryanarayana** (**June 1913**).
**Krishna Patrika** (**1902**) was the voice of the Telugu districts.
**Desamata**, Rajahmundry — **Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham**.

255.s: The Telugu-medium resolution of 1915 was supported by which Tamil daily?
255.x: The Tamil daily Swadesamitran supported the Telugu-medium resolution of 1915.
255.tq: Test the cross-linguistic newspaper support rather than the Andhra newspapers themselves.
xs: The Tamil daily **Swadesamitran** backed the Telugu-medium resolution of **1915** — option **(4)** is correct.
The resolution sought **Telugu as medium of instruction** in secondary schools (**3rd session**, Visakhapatnam, **1915**).
**Deshabhimani** and **Andhra Advocate** were Telugu-cause papers, not Tamil dailies.
xa: The **3rd session** was presided by **Raja Panuganti Ramarayaningar**.
It declared a separate state of **11 Telugu districts** just and necessary.
Speeches at the 3rd session were in **Telugu**.

255.s: The Swarajya associated with the Vandemataram era was published at Vijayawada, with which person as editor?
255.x: The Vijayawada Swarajya of the Vandemataram era had Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao as its editor.
255.tq: Distinguish two newspapers with the same title by place and period.
xs: **Swarajya**, Vijayawada, was edited by **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham** ran **Desamata** (Rajahmundry).
**Mutnuri Krishna Rao** edited **Krishna Patrika**.
xa: Gadicherla presided the **7th session** (**1919**, Guntur).
He proposed **district-wise voting** at Nellore (**1917**).
**Navayuga**, Chilakaluripet — **Srinivasa Rao**.

255.s: The Andhra Patrika, founded in 1908 at Bombay and later shifted to Madras, was started by:
255.x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao founded Andhra Patrika at Bombay on 9 September 1908; it became a daily in 1914 and moved to Madras. Konda Venkatappayya founded Krishna Patrika (1902); Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao edited Swarajya (Vijayawada); Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham ran Desamata (Rajahmundry).
255.tq: Andhra Patrika = Kasinathuni, Bombay 1908.
xs: **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** started **Andhra Patrika** — option **(2)** is correct.
Founded **9 Sep 1908** in Bombay; daily from **1914**; moved to Madras.
**Konda Venkatappayya** founded **Krishna Patrika** (**1902**); **Gadicherla** edited **Swarajya**; **Chilakamarti** ran **Desamata**.
xa: Kasinathuni (**1872-1942**) presided the special **Guntur session**, **17 Aug 1918**.
The **Sri Bagh Pact** was signed at his house in Madras (**1937**).
Title: **Desoddharaka** (not Pattabhi).

255.s:
Consider the following statements about the newspaper Deshabhimani:
1. It was an Anglo-Telugu paper published from Guntur.
2. On 4 February 1910 it gave the first call for a political meeting on Andhra problems.
3. It was founded and edited by Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
255.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Deshabhimani was an Anglo-Telugu paper from Guntur and on 4 February 1910 called for a political meeting on Andhra problems. Statement 3 is wrong: its editorials were by Seshagirirao; Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao founded Andhra Patrika. So '1 only' is incomplete and the options with 3 are wrong.
255.tq: Deshabhimani = Guntur, 1910 first call, editor Seshagirirao.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Deshabhimani** was an **Anglo-Telugu** paper from **Guntur**.
Statement 2 correct: on **4 Feb 1910** it gave the first call for a political meeting on Andhra problems.
Statement 3 wrong: its editorials were by **Seshagirirao**; **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** founded **Andhra Patrika**.
xa: It was the **only daily from British Andhra**.
**Dec 1911**: English supplement for **George V's Delhi coronation**.
It argued **Telugu culture** needs a government of its own (**APPSC 2017**).

255.s: Krishna Patrika, founded on 1 February 1902 and a voice of the Telugu districts, was founded by:
255.x: Konda Venkatappayya (with Dasu Narayana Rao) co-founded Krishna Patrika in 1902, with Mutnuri Krishna Rao later as editor. Kasinathuni founded Andhra Patrika; Gadicherla edited Swarajya; Chilakamarti ran Desamata.
255.tq: Krishna Patrika 1902 = Konda Venkatappayya; later Mutnuri.
xs: **Konda Venkatappayya** founded **Krishna Patrika** — option **(3)** is correct.
He co-founded it with **Dasu Narayana Rao** on **1 Feb 1902**; **Mutnuri Krishna Rao** later edited it.
**Kasinathuni** founded **Andhra Patrika**; **Gadicherla** edited **Swarajya**; **Chilakamarti** ran **Desamata**.
xa: ⚠ Some older notes call **Mutnuri** the founder.
Krishna Patrika mocked the **Montagu-Chelmsford** scheme as "digging a mountain to catch a mouse" (**13 July 1918**).
Konda Venkatappayya's title: **Deshabhakta**.

255.s: The Youngmen's Literary Association at Guntur, founded in 1903, is regarded as the:
o: Venue of the Sri Bagh Pact
255.x: The Youngmen's Literary Association at Guntur in 1903 is regarded as the cradle of the Andhra movement.
255.tq: Recall the organisation-place-year combination associated with the movement's beginnings.
xs: The **Youngmen's Literary Association**, **Guntur** (**1903**), is the **cradle of the Andhra movement** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Jonnavittula Gurunatham** belonged to it.
The **Sri Bagh Pact** was signed in **Madras** (**1937**); the **1st Rayalaseema Mahasabha** met in **1934**.
xa: Next step: the **Nidadavolu (1912)** joint conference — first formal province resolution.
**Krishna and Guntur** were the most eager districts.
The first Mahasabha met at **Bapatla** (then in **Guntur** district), **1913**.

255.s: The joint conference of the Guntur, Krishna and Godavari districts held at Nidadavolu in 1912 is significant because it:
o: Opposed the formation of any linguistic province
Demanded a separate Rayalaseema state with Madras as capital
Passed the first formal resolution for a separate province
255.x: The Nidadavolu conference of 1912 passed the first formal resolution demanding a separate province. The resolution was moved by Gurunatham.
255.tq: Identify the significance of an early conference rather than its venue alone.
xs: **Nidadavolu (1912)** **passed the first formal resolution for a separate province** — option **(4)** is correct.
It was a joint conference of **Guntur, Krishna, Godavari** districts (in **West Godavari**).
It was moved by **Jonnavittula Gurunatham**; a standing committee was formed with **Konda Venkatappayya** as secretary.
xa: Opposed by **K.V. Reddy Naidu** and **Peddada Sambasiva Rao**.
⚠ Nidadavolu **1912** = first formal resolution; Bapatla **1913** = first numbered conference.
A separate Rayalaseema state with Madras as capital was asked only before the **Dhar Commission** (**1948**).

255.s: Who moved the first formal separate-province resolution at the Nidadavolu conference of 1912?
255.x: Jonnavittula Gurunatham moved the first formal resolution for a separate province at Nidadavolu in 1912.
255.tq: Test the person associated with a specific resolution.
xs: **Jonnavittula Gurunatham** moved the first formal province resolution at **Nidadavolu, 1912** — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes credit **Duggirala Raghavayya** and **Bhamidipati Kameswara Rao**.
**Konda Venkatappayya** was **secretary** of the standing committee; **Vinjamuri Bhavanacharyulu** presided the Guntur committee.
xa: Gurunatham wrote **6 articles in 1911** in **The Hindu**.
**Manda Suryanarayana** later moved the resolution at **Vijayawada (1914)**.
Opponents at Nidadavolu: **K.V. Reddy Naidu**, **Peddada Sambasiva Rao**.

255.s:
Which of the following persons opposed the separate-province resolution at Nidadavolu in 1912?
1. K.V. Reddy Naidu
2. Peddada Sambasiva Rao
3. Konda Venkatappayya
4. Jonnavittula Gurunatham

Select the correct answer using the code below.
255.x: K.V. Reddy Naidu and Peddada Sambasiva Rao opposed the resolution at Nidadavolu. Konda Venkatappayya served as secretary and Gurunatham moved the resolution.
255.tq: Separate opponents from the organisers and mover of the same conference.
xs: **K.V. Reddy Naidu** and **Peddada Sambasiva Rao** opposed it — **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)** is correct.
**Konda Venkatappayya** was secretary of the standing committee formed there.
**Jonnavittula Gurunatham** moved the resolution.
xa: **K.V. Reddy Naidu** later proposed the name "**Telugu Viswavidyalayam**".
Nidadavolu (**1912**) = first formal separate-province resolution.
It was a joint conference of **Guntur, Krishna, Godavari**.

255.s: Who was the president of the Andhra Mahasabha Committee at Guntur?
255.x: Vinjamuri Bhavanacharyulu was the president of the Andhra Mahasabha Committee at Guntur, while Konda Venkatappayya was its secretary.
255.tq: Discriminate between president and secretary within the same committee.
xs: **Vinjamuri Bhavanacharyulu** presided the Andhra Mahasabha Committee at **Guntur** (**1912-13**) — option **(2)** is correct.
He was the **first municipal chairman of Guntur**.
**Konda Venkatappayya** was its **secretary**; **Manda Suryanarayana** presided the **Vizag** meeting.
xa: **Guthi Kesava Pillai** presided the Rayalaseema meeting at **Mahanandi** (April **1913**).
Manda Suryanarayana was **Vizianagaram** municipal chairman.
The Vizag meeting started the weekly **Andhra Advocate**.

255.s:
Consider the following statements about the Vizag district meeting of June 1913:
1. It was presided over by Manda Suryanarayana.
2. It started the weekly Andhra Advocate.
3. Its president was the first municipal chairman of Guntur.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
255.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Manda Suryanarayana presided and the meeting started the weekly Andhra Advocate. Statement 3 is wrong: Manda Suryanarayana was the Vizianagaram municipal chairman; Vinjamuri Bhavanacharyulu was the first municipal chairman of Guntur. So '1 only' is incomplete, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include statement 3.
255.tq: Vizag 1913 = Manda Suryanarayana (Vizianagaram) + Andhra Advocate; Guntur chairman = Bhavanacharyulu.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **Vizag** meeting (**June 1913**) was presided by **Manda Suryanarayana**.
Statement 2 correct: it started the weekly **Andhra Advocate**.
Statement 3 wrong: Manda Suryanarayana was **Vizianagaram** municipal chairman; **Vinjamuri Bhavanacharyulu** was Guntur's first.
xa: Manda Suryanarayana moved the province resolution at **Vijayawada (1914)**.
He was **Andhra Mahasabha president 1941-46** (PYQ).
His **2 Sept 1921** university resolution was accepted.

255.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Youngmen's Literary Association at Guntur
B. Nidadavolu joint conference
C. Mahanandi Rayalaseema meeting
D. Vizag district meeting
255.x: The events occurred in 1903, 1912, April 1913 and June 1913 respectively.
255.tq: Anchor the sequence with the 1903 event and distinguish the two 1913 meetings by month.
xs: The order is **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)** is correct.
A: **Youngmen's Literary Association**, Guntur — **1903**; B: **Nidadavolu** — **1912**.
C: **Mahanandi** Rayalaseema meeting — **April 1913**; D: **Vizag** district meeting — **June 1913**.
xa: Mahanandi (under **Guthi Kesava Pillai**) called separation impractical — a "**Brahmin movement**".
Vizag started the weekly **Andhra Advocate**.

255.s:
Consider the following statements about the district meetings held after the Bapatla conference of 1913:
1. Meetings in Guntur, Vijayawada, Godavari and Chittoor backed a separate Andhra.
2. The Nellore meeting considered the demand 'not yet ripe'.
3. The Vizag meeting opposed a separate Andhra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
255.x: Statement 1 is correct: Guntur, Vijayawada, Godavari, Vizag and Chittoor meetings backed a separate Andhra. Statement 2 is correct: Nellore said the demand was 'not yet ripe'. Statement 3 is wrong: the Vizag meeting also backed it. Hence '1 only' is incomplete, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.
255.tq: After Bapatla, only Nellore held back ('not yet ripe').
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: meetings in **Guntur, Vijayawada, Godavari, Vizag, Chittoor** backed a separate Andhra.
Statement 2 correct: **Nellore** called it "**not yet ripe**".
Statement 3 wrong: the **Vizag** meeting also backed it.
xa: Bapatla had **deferred** the province resolution.
The **2nd** session (**Vijayawada, 1914**) passed it.
Nellore later hosted the **5th** session (**1917**), with **district-wise voting**.

255.s: Who served as the secretary of the standing committee formed after the 1912 Nidadavolu conference?
255.x: Konda Venkatappayya served as secretary of the standing committee formed after the Nidadavolu conference.
255.tq: Test the specific office-holder rather than the better-known president of a later session.
xs: **Konda Venkatappayya** was secretary of the Nidadavolu standing committee — option **(4)** is correct.
**Nidadavolu (1912)** passed the first formal province resolution.
**Nyapati Subba Rao** presided the **2nd** session; **Manda Suryanarayana** the Vizag meeting.
xa: Konda was also secretary of the **Guntur** Andhra Mahasabha Committee.
Secretary of **Bapatla (1913)** (**APPSC 2022** key).
Co-founded **Krishna Patrika** (**1 Feb 1902**).

255.s:
With reference to the early demands of the Andhra movement, consider the following statements:
1. The demand for a separate Andhra province was raised from 1911 onwards.
2. The demand for Telugu as the medium of instruction in secondary schools was raised at the third session in 1915.
3. The demand for a separate university was first raised at the second session in 1914.

xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the separate province was raised from **1911** onward.
Statement 2 correct: **Telugu medium** in secondary schools — **3rd session, 1915**.
Statement 3 wrong: the university was first demanded at the **1st session, Bapatla 1913**; the **2nd** (**1914**) reiterated it.

Reason: Tamil-dominated **Madras University** neglected Telugu.
**Andhra University** established **26 April 1926**.

255.s: Which one of the following was NOT among the principal opponents of the separate Andhra province proposal?
255.x: V. Satyanarayana supported the proposal. Nyapati Subba Rao, Mocherla Ramachandra Rao and Ganti Venkataramayya opposed it.

xs: **V. Satyanarayana** was not an opponent — he **supported** the resolution — option **(2)** is correct.
The mover was **Vemavarapu Ramadasu Pantulu**, supported by V. Satyanarayana.
Opposed by **Nyapati Subba Rao**, **Mocherla Ramachandra Rao**, **Ganti Venkataramayya**, M. Adinarayanaiah.
xa: **B.N. Sarma** felt the demand might do "**more harm than good**".
Outcome: **Krishna Rao's amendment** — collect public opinion, take up at next conference.

255.s:
With reference to the early resolution for a separate Andhra province, consider the following statements:
1. Krishna Rao's amendment provided for collecting public opinion and taking the matter up at the next conference.
2. A committee under Pattabhi Sitaramayya was set up to carry out this decision.
3. The province proposal was moved by Nyapati Subba Rao.

255.x: Statement 1 is correct: Krishna Rao's amendment was to collect public opinion and take it up at the next conference. Statement 2 is correct: a committee under Pattabhi Sitaramayya was set up for this. Statement 3 is wrong: the proposal was moved by Vemavarapu Ramadasu Pantulu; Nyapati Subba Rao opposed it. So '1 only' is incomplete, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include statement 3.
255.tq: Mover = Ramadasu Pantulu; opponents include Nyapati Subba Rao; outcome = Krishna Rao's amendment + Pattabhi committee.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Krishna Rao's amendment** — collect public opinion, take it up at the next conference.
Statement 2 correct: a committee under **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** was set up to carry it out.
Statement 3 wrong: the mover was **Vemavarapu Ramadasu Pantulu**; **Nyapati Subba Rao** opposed it.
xa: Krishna and Guntur delegates were **disappointed** by the deferment.
President **B.N. Sarma**: "**First we are Indians, then we are Andhras.**"
The resolution passed at **Vijayawada** in **1914**.

255.s:

2. Lifting the ban on the entry of Telugus into the Army
3. A fund for technical training abroad

255.x: The Bapatla agenda included an English paper, removal of the ban on Telugus entering the Army and a fund for technical training abroad. Immediate establishment of a separate province was not listed as an agenda item.

xs: Items **1, 2 and 3** were on the agenda — option **(1)** is correct.

255.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because B.N. Sarma presided over the first session; Nyapati Subba Rao presided over the second session.

xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: held at **Bapatla**, then in **Guntur** district.
Statement 2 correct: delegates came from **Hyderabad, Warangal, Nagpur**.
Statement 3 wrong: **B.N. Sarma** presided; **Nyapati Subba Rao** presided the **2nd** session.

About **800 delegates and 2,000 visitors**.

255.s: What was the principal position taken by B.N. Sarma regarding the demand for a separate Andhra province at the first Andhra Mahasabha?
o: It should be achieved only through armed struggle.
It should be pursued immediately through constitutional agitation.
It was essential before any work for Andhra uplift could begin.
It might do more harm than good at that time.

He urged **loyalty to the British** and joint work for Andhra's uplift — not immediate agitation.

His motto: "**First we are Indians, then we are Andhras.**"

255.s: Which one of the following statements correctly reflects B.N. Sarma's approach at the first Andhra Mahasabha?
o: He argued that Andhra interests were superior to Indian interests.
He rejected cooperation with the British and demanded immediate independence.
He advocated loyalty to the British and joint work for Andhra uplift.
He opposed educational and economic work for Andhra.

xs: **B.N. Sarma** advocated **loyalty to the British and joint work for Andhra uplift** — option **(3)** is correct.
He put Indian identity first: "**First we are Indians, then we are Andhras.**"
He called a separate province premature — "**more harm than good**".
xa: He was a member of the **Madras Legislative Council**.
He founded the **Andhra Rajakeeya Samiti** (**1917**).
The province resolution was **deferred** at Bapatla.

255.s: The statement “First we are Indians, then we are Andhras” is associated with:
255.x: The statement expressed B.N. Sarma’s emphasis on Indian identity before regional identity.

xs: "First we are Indians, then we are Andhras" is linked to **B.N. Sarma** — option **(4)** is correct.

**Vemavarapu Ramadasu Pantulu** **moved** the province resolution; **Nyapati Subba Rao** opposed it; **Konda Venkatappayya** was secretary.

Vemavarapu Ramadasu Pantulu — Moved the separate-province resolution
Unnava Lakshminarayana — Presided over the first session

xa: The resolution was supported by **V. Satyanarayana**.

Ramadasu later **seconded** Manda Suryanarayana's resolution at **Vijayawada (1914)**.

Consider the following statements about the first Andhra Mahasabha:

xs: The **3rd session** (**May 1915**, **Visakhapatnam**) declared a separate state of the **11 Telugu districts** **just and necessary** — option **(3)** is correct.
It was presided by **Raja Panuganti Ramarayaningar**.
The demand to include **Madras city** was rejected later, at the **5th** session (Nellore, **1917**).
xa: It also sought **Telugu medium** in secondary schools; speeches were in **Telugu**.
**Swadesamitran**, a Tamil daily, backed the Telugu-medium resolution of **1915**.
Order of sessions: **Bapatla, Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Nellore, Kadapa**.

255.s: Which one of the following was a major resolution of the third Andhra Mahasabha session?
o: Introduction of Telugu as the medium in secondary schools
Transfer of Andhra University to Visakhapatnam
Creation of a separate Andhra Congress circle
Reservation of seats exclusively for Brahmins
255.x: The third session at Visakhapatnam supported Telugu as the medium of instruction in secondary schools and the use of Telugu in speeches.
255.tq: Match the educational reform with the correct session rather than a later Congress-related demand.
xs: The 3rd session resolved on **Telugu as the medium of instruction in secondary schools** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was held at **Visakhapatnam** in **May 1915**.
The separate Andhra **Congress circle** was demanded at the **4th** (Kakinada, **1916**); AU moved to **Visakhapatnam** only in **Dec 1928**.
xa: The session reiterated the province: **11 Telugu districts**.
President: **Raja Panuganti Ramarayaningar**.
The Tamil daily **Swadesamitran** backed the resolution.

255.s: The demand for a separate Andhra Congress circle was made at the fourth Andhra Mahasabha session held at:
255.x: The fourth session was held at Kakinada in May 1916 and demanded that the AICC create a separate Andhra Congress circle.
255.tq: Link the organisational demand to the correct venue and session.
xs: The separate Andhra Congress circle was demanded at the **4th session**, **Kakinada** — option **(2)** is correct.
It was held in **May 1916** under **Mocherla Ramachandra Rao**.
**Nellore** hosted the **5th** (**1917**), **Kadapa** the **6th** (**1918**), **Guntur** the **7th** (**1919**).
xa: **C.V. Narasimha Raju** moved a **fully autonomous province** there.
A women's session (**8 May 1916**) under **Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi**.
The **AICC** at **Lucknow 1916** examined the demand but took no decision.

255.s: Who moved the resolution for a fully autonomous Andhra province at the fourth Andhra Mahasabha session?
255.x: C.V. Narasimha Raju moved the resolution demanding a fully autonomous Andhra province at the Kakinada session of 1916.
255.tq: Apply the person-and-deed trap by separating the mover from the session president.
xs: **C.V. Narasimha Raju** moved the fully autonomous province resolution at **Kakinada (1916)** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Manda Suryanarayana** moved the province resolution at **Vijayawada (1914)**.
**Konda Venkatappayya** presided the **5th** session (Nellore, **1917**); **Kasinathuni** presided the special **Guntur** session (**1918**).
xa: The 4th session was presided by **Mocherla Ramachandra Rao** ("**Gokhale of South India**").
It asked the AICC for a separate **Andhra Congress circle**.
Women's session: **8 May 1916**.

255.s: At the fifth Andhra Mahasabha session, the province resolution was passed through:
o: A unanimous vote of all delegates
A vote restricted to members of the AICC
District-wise voting, with one vote for each district
A referendum among the people of Madras city
255.x: At the Nellore session in 1917, the province resolution was passed through district-wise voting, with one vote allotted to each district.
255.tq: Test the distinctive voting procedure rather than merely the session venue.
xs: At the **5th session** the province resolution passed by **district-wise voting** (**one vote per district**) — option **(3)** is correct.
**480** of **740** delegates came from **Nellore**, so **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** proposed this method.
It was held on **1 June 1917** at **Nellore** under **Konda Venkatappayya**.
xa: The session **rejected the demand to include Madras city**.
It was the **6th** session (**Kadapa, 1918**) that passed the province **unanimously**.
The **1917** district-wise vote answered **Circars/Brahmin-led** suspicion.

255.s: The sixth Andhra Mahasabha session held at Kadapa in May 1918 is notable because the province resolution was:
o: Replaced by a demand for Madras city
Deferred for consideration by the AICC
255.x: The sixth session at Kadapa passed the demand for an Andhra province unanimously.
255.tq: Use the decisive wording to distinguish unanimous approval from earlier procedural disputes.
xs: At the **6th session** (**Kadapa**, **May 1918**) the province resolution was **passed unanimously** — option **(4)** is correct.
It was presided by **Nemali Pattabhi Rama Rao**.
The **Andhra Provincial Congress Conference** met alongside.
xa: ⚠ Nemali Pattabhi Rama Rao **opposed** the demand in **1916** but switched to support at Cuddapah in **1918**.
The **5th** session (**1917**) had used **district-wise voting**.
Kadapa is the last of the order **Bapatla, Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Nellore, Kadapa**.

255.s: Which conference met alongside the sixth Andhra Mahasabha session?
255.x: The Andhra Provincial Congress Conference met alongside the sixth Andhra Mahasabha session at Kadapa in May 1918.
255.tq: Identify the associated organisation rather than confusing it with a regional Mahasabha.
xs: The **Andhra Provincial Congress Conference** met alongside the 6th session — option **(3)** is correct.
The 6th session was at **Kadapa** in **May 1918**, under **Nemali Pattabhi Rama Rao**.
The **Rayalaseema Mahasabha** was formed only in **1934**; the **Madras Provincial Conference** had **refused** the province question in **May 1915**.
xa: The **Andhra Congress Committee** was formed on **22 January 1918**.
The province resolution passed **unanimously** at Kadapa.
First president of the Andhra Congress Committee: **Nyapati Subba Rao** (notes).

255.s:
Arrange the following Andhra Mahasabha sessions in chronological order:
A. Session at Kakinada
B. Session at Bapatla
C. Session at Kadapa
D. Session at Visakhapatnam
255.x: The sessions occurred at Bapatla in 1913, Visakhapatnam in 1915, Kakinada in 1916 and Kadapa in 1918.
255.tq: Arrange the venues by their session years, using the earliest and latest events first.
xs: The order is **B, D, A, C** — option **(1)** is correct.
B: **Bapatla** — **1913**; D: **Visakhapatnam** — **1915**.
xa: **Vijayawada** (**1914**) came between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam.
**Nellore** (**1917**) came between Kakinada and Kadapa.
**Guntur** (**1919**) hosted the **7th** session.

255.s:
Consider the following statements about the seventh Andhra Mahasabha session:
1. It was held at Guntur in 1919.
2. It was presided over by Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao.
3. It backed the province demand with data on the drain from coastal Andhra.
4. It passed the province resolution through district-wise voting.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: the 7th session was at Guntur in 1919 under Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao and backed the province with data on the drain from coastal Andhra. Statement 4 is wrong: district-wise voting was used at the 5th session, Nellore 1917. So '1 and 2 only' is incomplete, and '2, 3 and 4 only' and '1, 2, 3 and 4' include statement 4.
255.tq: District-wise voting = Nellore 1917 (5th); Guntur 1919 (7th) = drain data.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)** is correct.
Statements 1-3: the **7th** session, **Guntur**, **1919**, under **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao**, backed the province with data on the **drain from coastal Andhra**.
Statement 4 wrong: **district-wise voting** was used at the **5th** session (Nellore, **1917**).
xa: Gadicherla himself proposed district-wise voting at Nellore.
He edited **Swarajya**, Vijayawada.
His **1924** bid for the APCC presidency was defeated.

255.s: The special Andhra Sabha held at Guntur on 17 August 1918 protested that:
o: The Montagu-Chelmsford proposals did not provide for an Andhra province
The AICC had rejected Telugu as a medium of instruction
The Andhra Provincial Congress Conference had been dissolved
Madras city had been included in the Andhra province
255.x: The Guntur special session protested that the Montagu-Chelmsford proposals made no provision for an Andhra province.
255.tq: Identify the precise grievance associated with the special session.
xs: The special **Guntur** session (**17 Aug 1918**) protested that the **Montagu-Chelmsford proposals had no Andhra province** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was presided by **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**.
The **Montagu-Chelmsford Report** (**July 1918**) had no Andhra provision.
xa: There **Pattabhi** proposed an **All-India Linguistic States Conference**.
**Krishna Patrika** mocked the scheme as "digging a mountain to catch a mouse" (**13 July 1918**).
**Dec 1918**: a delegation went to **London**; **Mocherla Ramachandra Rao** submitted a memorandum.

255.s: Which of the following correctly gives the venues of the second, third, fourth and fifth sessions of the Andhra Mahasabha respectively?
255.x: The second through fifth sessions were held at Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam, Kakinada and Nellore respectively.
255.tq: Track the session number separately from the year and venue.
xs: **Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Nellore** — option **(2)** is correct.
**2nd**: Vijayawada (**11 April 1914**); **3rd**: Visakhapatnam (**May 1915**).
**4th**: Kakinada (**May 1916**); **5th**: Nellore (**1 June 1917**).
xa: Exam angle: match **session - venue - president**.

255.s:
Consider the following statements about the fourth Andhra Mahasabha held at Kakinada in 1916:
1. It was presided over by Mocherla Ramachandra Rao, called the 'Gokhale of South India'.
2. A women's session was held under Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi.
3. It rejected the demand to include Madras city in the proposed province.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
255.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Mocherla Ramachandra Rao ('Gokhale of South India') presided at Kakinada, and a women's session on 8 May 1916 was held under Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi. Statement 3 is wrong: the demand to include Madras city was rejected at the 5th session, Nellore 1917. So '1 only' is incomplete and the options with 3 are wrong.
255.tq: Kakinada 1916 = Mocherla + women's session; Nellore 1917 = district-wise voting, Madras city rejected.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Mocherla Ramachandra Rao** ("**Gokhale of South India**") presided at Kakinada.
Statement 2 correct: a women's session on **8 May 1916** under **Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Madras city** inclusion was rejected at the **5th** session (Nellore, **1917**).
xa: **C.V. Narasimha Raju** moved a **fully autonomous province** at Kakinada.
Kakinada sought a separate **Andhra Congress circle** from the AICC.
⚠ Mocherla had **opposed** the province resolution at **Bapatla (1913)**.

255.s: Who was the first Telugu person to preside over a session of the Indian National Congress?
255.x: P. Anandacharlu was the first Telugu person to preside over a session of the Indian National Congress.
255.tq: Directly identify the person associated with the distinction.
xs: **P. Anandacharlu** was the first Andhra to preside over the INC — option **(3)** is correct.
He presided the **7th session**, **Nagpur**, **1891**.
**Pattabhi Sitaramayya** presided later, at **Jaipur, 1948**; **P. Rangaiah Naidu** and **Nyapati Subba Rao** were delegates at the **1885** session.
xa: ⚠ **APPSC G2 2011** key named **Pattabhi** "first Telugu person" — read the wording.
Anandacharlu (**Chittoor**) was earlier Secretary of the **Madras Mahajana Sabha** (**1884**).
**1885 Bombay session** had **72** members.

255.s: The 7th session of the Indian National Congress, presided over by P. Anandacharlu, was held at:
255.x: The 7th session of the INC was held at Nagpur in 1891 under the presidency of P. Anandacharlu.
255.tq: Link the session number with its venue rather than its president alone.
xs: The **7th** INC session under **P. Anandacharlu** was at **Nagpur** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was held in **1891**.
**Jaipur** (**1948**) was Pattabhi's session; **Calcutta** (**1886**) had **21 Andhras out of 408**.
xa: Anandacharlu was from **Chittoor**.
He was the **first Andhra INC president**.
**1892**: **Krishna District Congress Committee** formed (first meeting at **Guntur**).

255.s: Who was the first president of the Andhra Provincial Congress Committee, whose presidential term is given as 1918–1923?
255.x: C is correct as keyed: the APPSC G2 2011 key names Konda Venkatappayya the first APCC president, with his presidency given as 1918-23. Note that other sources name Nyapati Subba Rao first president of the 1918 Andhra Congress Committee, with Konda Venkatappayya as first secretary.
255.tq: Discriminate between the first committee president and the first president of the separate Andhra Congress Committee.
xs: As keyed, **Konda Venkatappayya** was the first APCC president, his presidency given as **1918-23** — option **(3)** is correct (**APPSC G2 2011** key).
He was also the **first secretary** of the Andhra Congress Committee.
**Pattabhi** and **B.N. Sarma** are not named as first president.
xa: ⚠ The notes name **Nyapati Subba Rao** first president of the Andhra Congress Committee (**1918**), with Konda Venkatappayya as **first secretary**.
The committee was formed on **22 January 1918**.
It was the **first major victory** of the Andhra movement.

255.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the formation of the separate Andhra Congress Committee:
1. It was formed on 22 January 1918.
2. Nyapati Subba Rao was its first president.
3. Konda Venkatappayya was its first secretary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: All three statements are correct. The separate Andhra Congress Committee was formed on 22 January 1918, with Nyapati Subba Rao as president and Konda Venkatappayya as secretary.
255.tq: Check the date, office-holder and office separately before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All **three statements** are correct — option **(4)** is correct.
Statement 1: formed on **22 January 1918**.
Statement 2: first president **Nyapati Subba Rao**.
Statement 3: first secretary **Konda Venkatappayya**.
xa: Formed through **Pattabhi Sitaramayya**, **Konda Venkatappayya**, **Tilak**.
The **Calcutta Congress (1917)** had accepted the demand.
⚠ The **APPSC G2 2011** key names **Konda Venkatappayya** first president.

255.s: The demand for a separate Andhra circle was taken to the All-India Congress Committee by which session of the Andhra Mahasabha?
o: The special session at Guntur in 1918
255.x: The fourth Andhra Mahasabha in 1916 took the demand to the AICC, which referred it to the provincial bodies in December 1916.
255.tq: Link the organisational demand with the specific Mahasabha session and year.
xs: The **4th session (1916)** took the demand to the **AICC** — option **(1)** is correct.
The 4th session was at **Kakinada**.
The **AICC** referred it to provincial bodies in **December 1916**.
xa: **Lucknow 1916**: AICC examined it, **no decision**.
**Calcutta Congress (1917)** accepted it.
Committee formed **22 January 1918**.

255.s: At Lucknow in 1916, the All-India Congress Committee, while examining the Andhra demand,
o: rejected the demand as harmful to national unity
referred the demand to the Montagu-Chelmsford Committee
examined the demand but took no decision
accepted the demand and immediately formed Andhra Province
255.x: The AICC examined the demand at Lucknow in 1916 but took no decision. Pattabhi Sitaramayya pressed the demand there with Tilak’s support.
255.tq: Distinguish examination of a proposal from its acceptance or rejection.
xs: At **Lucknow 1916** the AICC **examined the demand but took no decision** — option **(3)** is correct.
Some notes say **Pattabhi** pressed it there with **Tilak's** support.
It was then referred to provincial bodies in **December 1916**.
xa: The **Calcutta Congress (1917)** accepted the demand.
The **Andhra Congress Committee** was formed on **22 January 1918**.
Stance timeline: **1915** provincial conference refused; **1916** Lucknow no decision; **1918** separate committee.

255.s: Which of the following was a reason advanced by the Andhras for demanding a separate Congress circle in 1914?
o: The Simon Commission had recommended abolition of provincial committees.
Although 256 Andhra delegates attended the Madras Congress, none was placed on the Working Committee.
The Montagu declaration had excluded all Telugu-speaking areas.
The Andhra delegates were denied admission to the Congress session.
255.x: At the 1914 Madras Congress, 256 Andhra delegates attended, but no Andhra member was placed on the Working Committee. Tamils also blocked an Andhra resolution.
255.tq: Use the distinctive numerical detail to identify the correct cause.
xs: At the **1914 Madras Congress**, **256 Andhra delegates** attended but **none was on the working committee** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Tamils blocked an Andhra resolution** there.
The **Simon Commission** (**1928**) and the **Montagu declaration** (**1917**) came later.
xa: **May 1915**: the Madras Provincial Conference **refused** to discuss the province question.
Precedent cited: **Bihar and Orissa's** separate Congress circles.
The **4th Mahasabha** (**1916**) took the demand to the AICC.

255.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Andhra movement between 1921 and 1935 is NOT correct?
o: Moderates such as Radhakrishnan, Sir Vijaya and C.R. Reddy kept the Mahasabha going.
The Congress in office in Madras had already completely taken over the demand in 1921.
The movement merged into Gandhian mass struggles.
The phase was described as ‘Swarajya within Swarajya’.
255.x: The Congress in office in Madras took over the demand from the declining Mahasabha only from 1946 onwards. The other statements correctly describe the 1921–1935 phase.
255.tq: Find the statement that shifts a stated development to the wrong period.
xs: The claim that **Congress in office in Madras took over the demand in 1921** is NOT correct — option **(2)** is correct.
Congress took over the demand only from **1946 onwards**, from the declining Mahasabha.
**1921-35**: the movement **merged into Gandhian mass struggles** ("**Swarajya within Swarajya**").
**Moderates** — **Radhakrishnan**, **Sir Vijaya**, **C.R. Reddy** — kept the Mahasabha going.
xa: **Special Andhra Sabha, Madras, 1931**: president **Kadapa Koti Reddy**.
**Silver Jubilee session, Vijayawada, 1937**: president **Kadapa Koti Reddy**.
**Sir Vijayanand** presided at **Visakhapatnam**, **November 1941**.

255.s:
Consider the following statements about Pattabhi Sitaramayya:
1. He presided over the Jaipur session of the Indian National Congress in 1948.
2. He lost the 1939 Tripuri presidential contest to Subhas Chandra Bose despite Gandhi's backing.
3. He was the first Andhra (Telugu) person to preside over an INC session.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
255.x: Statement 1 is correct: he presided at Jaipur in 1948. Statement 2 is correct: he lost at Tripuri (1939) to Subhas Bose though Gandhi backed him. Statement 3 is wrong: the first Andhra to preside was P. Anandacharlu (7th session, Nagpur, 1891). So '1 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include statement 3, and '2 only' leaves out statement 1.
255.tq: First Andhra INC president = Anandacharlu 1891, not Pattabhi.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Pattabhi** presided at **Jaipur** in **1948**.
Statement 2 correct: he lost the **1939 Tripuri** contest to **Subhas Bose** despite Gandhi's backing.
Statement 3 wrong: the first Andhra to preside was **P. Anandacharlu** (**7th session, Nagpur, 1891**).
xa: ⚠ The **APPSC G2 2011** key named Pattabhi "first Telugu person" — read the wording.
Pattabhi was president of the **JVP Committee**'s **Jaipur** AICC session (**Dec 1948**).
**N. Sanjiva Reddy**: INC president **1960-62**.

255.s: N. Sanjiva Reddy served as President of the Indian National Congress during:
255.x: N. Sanjiva Reddy served as Congress President from 1960 to 1962.
255.tq: Distinguish the exact two-year tenure from nearby chronological ranges.
xs: **N. Sanjiva Reddy** was INC president in **1960-62** — option **(3)** is correct.
He was the first **Deputy CM** of Andhra State.
He beat **N.G. Ranga** in the April **1951** APCC election by **5** votes.
xa: He later became **President of India**.
⚠ He was **not** a member of the **JVP Committee** (**APPSC 2021**).
Before the **Dhar Commission** he spoke for **20** Rayalaseema MLAs.

255.s: The Congress session held at Kakinada in 1923 was presided over by:
255.x: Maulana Mohammed Ali presided over the Congress session held at Kakinada in 1923.
255.tq: Match the Andhra venue and year with its presiding president.
xs: The **Kakinada session, 1923** was presided by **Maulana Mohammed Ali** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was one of the Congress sessions held in Andhra.
**Pattabhi** presided only in **1948** (Jaipur).
xa: **AICC at Bezawada (Vijayawada), 1921**: **Tilak Swaraj Fund**.
⚠ Kakinada also hosted the **4th Andhra Mahasabha** (**1916**).
**1921-35**: "**Swarajya within Swarajya**".

255.s: The principal financial objective associated with the 1921 AICC meeting at Bezawada was the collection of funds for the:
255.x: The AICC meeting at Bezawada in 1921 was associated with the Tilak Swaraj Fund.
255.tq: Separate two related events at the same meeting by identifying the named fund.
xs: The **1921 AICC at Bezawada (Vijayawada)** was linked to the **Tilak Swaraj Fund** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **Pingali Venkayya** showed his flag design to Gandhi at the same Bezwada AICC session (**1921**).
The notes link no other fund to it.
xa: **Kakinada session, 1923**: **Maulana Mohammed Ali**.
**Nagpur, December 1920**: PCCs reorganised on linguistic lines.
**1921-35**: the movement merged into **Gandhian mass struggles**.

255.s: The Krishna District Congress Committee, whose first meeting was held at Guntur, was formed in:
255.x: The Krishna District Congress Committee was formed in 1892, following the suggestions of the 1885 Congress session; its first meeting was held at Guntur.
255.tq: Use the exact year rather than the year of the Congress session that inspired it.
xs: The **Krishna District Congress Committee** was formed in **1892** — option **(4)** is correct.
Its first meeting was at **Guntur**, on suggestions of the **1885** session.
**1885** = Bombay session; **1886** = Calcutta session; **1891** = Anandacharlu's Nagpur session.
xa: **1885 Bombay session** (**72** members) had Andhra delegates incl. **Nyapati Subba Rao**.
**1886 Calcutta**: **21 Andhras out of 408**.
**P. Anandacharlu**: first Andhra to preside (**1891**).

255.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Madras session blocked the Andhra resolution
B. Lucknow session took no decision on the Andhra province
C. A separate committee was formed on the issue
D. Provincial conference refused the Andhra demand
255.x: The sequence was Madras in 1914, the provincial conference in 1915, Lucknow in 1916, and formation of a separate committee in 1918.
255.tq: Anchor the sequence to the four successive years 1914, 1915, 1916 and 1918.
xs: The order is **A, D, B, C** — option **(1)** is correct.
A: **1914 Madras Congress** — Tamils blocked the Andhra resolution; D: **May 1915** provincial conference refused.
B: **Lucknow 1916** — no decision; C: **1918** — separate committee formed (**22 January 1918**).
xa: The **Calcutta Congress (1917)** accepted the demand.
First president **Nyapati Subba Rao**; first secretary **Konda Venkatappayya**.
It was the **first major victory** of the Andhra movement.

255.s: The reorganisation of the Provincial Congress Committees on linguistic lines was undertaken at the:
255.x: The Congress reorganised its Provincial Congress Committees on linguistic lines at the Nagpur session in 1920. Linguistic provinces had therefore been a Congress commitment since the 1920s.
255.tq: Distinguish the organisational decision at Nagpur from later constitutional debates.
xs: PCCs were reorganised on linguistic lines at the **Nagpur session, 1920** — option **(2)** is correct.

**Jaipur** hosted the **Dec 1948** AICC session that set up the **JVP Committee**.
xa: "PCCs after **1920** were based on linguistic regions" (**APPSC 2016**).
The **Nehru Report (1928)** advocated linguistic provinces in line with this.
Andhra (**1953**) was the first to claim the promise.

255.s: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the Nagpur Congress session of 1920?
o: The membership fee was reduced to four annas.
Provincial Congress Committees were reorganised on a linguistic basis.
An AICC of 350 members and a Congress Working Committee were provided for.
The goal of complete independence by armed means was adopted.
255.x: The Nagpur session changed the goal to Swaraj by peaceful and legitimate means, not complete independence through armed struggle. The other three features belonged to the reorganisation adopted at Nagpur.
255.tq: Find the one statement that reverses the session’s constitutional and political programme.
xs: **Complete independence by armed means** was NOT a Nagpur feature — option **(4)** is correct.
Nagpur (**December 1920**) cut the membership fee to **4 annas**.
It reorganised **PCCs on linguistic lines**.
It created an **AICC of 350** + a **Congress Working Committee**.
xa: Nagpur was presided by **C. Vijayaraghavachariar**.
The Andhra PCC (formed **1918**) became a **regular linguistic unit**.
The **Calcutta special session (September 1920)** accepted non-cooperation.

255.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the Congress sessions of 1920?
o: Calcutta special session — C. Vijayaraghavachariar; Nagpur session — Lala Lajpat Rai
Calcutta special session — Lala Lajpat Rai; Nagpur session — C. Vijayaraghavachariar
Calcutta special session — Konda Venkatappayya; Nagpur session — Lala Lajpat Rai
Calcutta special session — B.N. Sarma; Nagpur session — C. Vijayaraghavachariar
255.x: Lala Lajpat Rai presided over the Calcutta special session in September 1920, while C. Vijayaraghavachariar presided over Nagpur in December 1920.
255.tq: Pair each session with its correct presiding officer before checking the code.
xs: **Calcutta special session — Lala Lajpat Rai**; **Nagpur — C. Vijayaraghavachariar** — option **(2)** is correct.
Calcutta (**September 1920**) accepted non-cooperation by **1886 to 884**.
Nagpur (**December 1920**) reorganised PCCs on linguistic lines.

Nagpur: **AICC of 350**; fee **4 annas**.
**B.N. Sarma** presided the **1st** Andhra Mahasabha (**1913**), not a 1920 Congress session.

255.s: Which statement regarding the Andhra delegates at the Calcutta special session of 1920 is correct?
o: Konda Venkatappayya presided over the session and cast the deciding vote.
No Andhra delegate attended the session.
All Andhra delegates voted in favour of non-cooperation.
About 30 Andhra delegates, including Konda Venkatappayya, voted against non-cooperation.
255.x: About 30 Andhra delegates, including Konda Venkatappayya, voted against the non-cooperation proposal at the Calcutta special session.
255.tq: Test the regional voting detail rather than the general session outcome.
xs: About **30 Andhra delegates**, incl. **Konda Venkatappayya**, **voted against non-cooperation** — option **(4)** is correct.
The session was presided by **Lala Lajpat Rai**, not Konda Venkatappayya.
Non-cooperation was accepted by **1886 to 884**.
xa: The Calcutta special session was in **September 1920**.
**Nagpur, December 1920**: PCCs reorganised on linguistic lines.
Konda Venkatappayya later became the **first CDM leader in Andhra**.

255.s: The Nehru Report of 1928 advocated linguistic provinces in accordance with the:
255.x: The Nehru Report advocated linguistic provinces in line with the reorganisation of Provincial Congress Committees undertaken in 1920.
255.tq: Link a constitutional recommendation to the earlier organisational precedent it followed.
xs: The **Nehru Report (1928)** advocated linguistic provinces in line with the **1920 reorganisation of PCCs** — option **(1)** is correct.
The PCCs were reorganised at **Nagpur, 1920**.
Linguistic states were thus a Congress promise **since the 1920s**.
xa: **1928**: **A. Kaleswara Rao** reminded the Madras Council of the delay.
The **Simon Commission** toured in **1928**, boycotted by Congress.
The **Montagu-Chelmsford Report** (**July 1918**) had no Andhra provision.

255.s:
With reference to the Andhra Provincial Congress Committee, consider the following statements:
1. It had already been formed in 1918.
2. After the Nagpur session it became a regular linguistic unit.
3. It functioned along with Karnataka and Maharashtra linguistic units.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: All three statements are correct. The Andhra PCC was formed in 1918 and was regularised as a linguistic unit after Nagpur along with Karnataka and Maharashtra.
255.tq: Use the timeline to verify both the prior formation and later regularisation.
xs: All **three statements** are correct — option **(4)** is correct.
Statement 1: the Andhra PCC was formed in **1918**.
Statements 2 and 3: after Nagpur (**1920**) it became a **regular linguistic unit**, with **Karnataka** and **Maharashtra**.
xa: The Andhra Congress Committee was formed on **22 January 1918**.
This showed early **Congress commitment to linguistic provinces**.
**6th Mahasabha** (Kadapa, **1918**): the **Andhra Provincial Congress Conference** met alongside.

255.s: Who moved the separate-province resolution in 1917?
