Statement 1: correct — PCCs were reorganised on **linguistic lines** at **Nagpur, 1920**.
Statement 2: correct — the Government **accepted the principle in 1947**.
Statement 3: wrong — it **delayed acting** on it; Andhra came only on **1 October 1953**.
xa: The **Nehru Report (1928)** advocated linguistic provinces.
The Andhra PCC (formed **1918**) became a regular linguistic unit.
Exam angle: "PCCs after 1920 were based on linguistic regions" (APPSC 2016).

255.s: What was the significance of Jawaharlal Nehru's declaration of November 1947 regarding linguistic states?
o: He accepted only the division of the Madras Presidency
He announced the formation of Andhra State immediately
He withdrew support for linguistic reorganisation completely
He declared support for linguistic states, although immediate reorganisation was not undertaken
255.x: In November 1947, Nehru declared support for linguistic states, but immediate reorganisation did not follow.
255.tq: Distinguish a political declaration of support from immediate implementation.
xs: In **November 1947**, Nehru **declared support for linguistic states**, but immediate reorganisation did not follow — option **(4)** is correct.
Andhra was announced only on **19 December 1952**, after **Sriramulu's** death.
xa: The declaration **raised hopes**.
On his **1948 Visakhapatnam** visit, Nehru promised a committee.
The Centre **accepted the principle in 1947** but went slow, fearing for **national unity** after Partition.

255.s: The Linguistic Provinces Commission was appointed by the Constituent Assembly on
255.x: The Linguistic Provinces Commission, also known as the Dhar or Dar Commission, was appointed by the Constituent Assembly on 17 June 1948.
255.tq: Distinguish the appointment date from the later Draft and JVP dates.
xs: The **Linguistic Provinces Commission** (Dhar/Dar) was appointed on **17 June 1948** — option **(3)** is correct.
**21 February 1948** is when the Draft Constitution was published (Andhra dropped); **December 1948** is when it **reported**.
xa: Appointed by the **Constituent Assembly** President, **Rajendra Prasad**.
Members: **S.K. Dhar** (chair), **Dr. Panna Lal**, **Jagat Narayan Lal**.
Report **10 Dec 1948**, published **13 Dec**.

255.s: Which one of the following was NOT a member of the Linguistic Provinces Commission appointed in 1948?
255.x: The Commission consisted of S.K. Dhar, Dr Pannalal and Jagat Narayan Lal. Pattabhi Sitaramayya was a member of the later JVP Committee.
255.tq: Find the person belonging to the neighbouring committee rather than the named body.
xs: **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** was **not** on the Dhar Commission — he was on the **JVP** Committee — option **(4)** is the answer.
The Commission: **S.K. Dhar** (chair), **Dr. Panna Lal**, **Jagat Narayan Lal**.
xa: JVP = **Jawaharlal Nehru**, **Vallabhbhai Patel**, **Pattabhi Sitaramayya**.
⚠ **N. Sanjiva Reddy** was **not** a JVP member (APPSC 2021).
⚠ **Dar** = Constituent Assembly; **JVP** = Congress.

255.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra in the Draft Constitution:
1. Andhra was included in the First Schedule of the Draft.
2. Andhra was dropped from the Draft published on 21 February 1948.
3. The deletion followed objections from Tamil and Kannada areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: All three statements are correct. Andhra was initially in the First Schedule of the Draft, but it was omitted from the Draft published on 21 February 1948 after Tamil and Kannada objections.
255.tq: Check the complete sequence of inclusion, deletion, date and cause.
xs: All three statements are correct — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
Statement 1: Andhra was in the **First Schedule** of the Draft.
Statement 2: it was **dropped** from the Draft published **21 Feb 1948**.
Statement 3: the deletion followed **Tamil and Kannada** objections.
xa: The **Constituent Assembly** kept only the pre-Independence provinces.
The Dar Commission came on **17 June 1948**.
The Constitution of **26 January 1950** had **no Andhra state**.

255.s:
Consider the following statements about the JVP Committee:
1. It was constituted at the Jaipur AICC session in December 1948.
2. Pattabhi Sitaramayya was its president.
3. Its report was submitted in 1949.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: The JVP Committee was constituted at the Jaipur AICC session in December 1948, with Pattabhi Sitaramayya as president, and submitted its report in 1949.
255.tq: Combine the committee's venue, office-holder and report year to identify the complete statement set.
xs: All three statements are correct — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
Statement 1: set up at the **Jaipur** AICC session, **December 1948**.
Statement 2: **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** was its **president** (he presided the Jaipur session).
Statement 3: report in **April 1949** to the **CWC**.
xa: Members: **Nehru, Patel, Pattabhi** ("Three Ministers Committee").
Report: Andhra possible **if Madras city was given up**.
Some questions say "**Jaipur, 1949**".

255.s: The JVP Committee recommended that the demand for Andhra could be considered if the claim to which city was given up?
255.x: The JVP Committee stated that Andhra could be considered if its claim to Madras city was relinquished.
255.tq: Distinguish the disputed metropolitan city from the proposed Andhra capital and other Telugu cities.
xs: The JVP Committee said Andhra could be considered **if its claim to Madras city was given up** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Kurnool** became the capital and **Guntur** got the High Court only in **1953-54**.
xa: Report **April 1949**: postpone new provinces — security, unity, economic prosperity first.
"If public opinion is **insistent and overwhelming**, we as democrats have to submit to it."
This "**Andhra exception**" (minus Madras) became the formula used in **1953**.

255.s: Which one of the following best reflects the recommendation of the JVP Committee regarding the creation of new provinces?
o: Creation of provinces solely on financial criteria
Postponement of the creation of new provinces
Merger of all Telugu areas with Hyderabad
Immediate creation of all provinces on a linguistic basis
255.x: The JVP Committee recommended postponing the creation of new provinces, while allowing Andhra's claim to be considered subject to giving up the claim to Madras city.
255.tq: Identify the committee's cautious recommendation rather than the later outcome of Andhra State formation.
xs: The JVP Committee recommended **postponing the creation of new provinces** — option **(2)** is correct.
It rejected **immediate linguistic reorganisation**, putting **security, unity and economic prosperity** first.
xa: It **reaffirmed the Dhar** report.
Exception: **Andhra** could be formed if the Madras claim was dropped.
**CWC** then recommended Andhra **without Madras city**.

255.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the JVP Committee's report:
1. It reaffirmed the general approach of the Dhar Commission.
2. It placed security, unity and economic prosperity above immediate linguistic reorganisation.
3. It stated that overwhelming public opinion could not influence democratic decision-making.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: The report reaffirmed the Dhar approach and prioritised security, unity and economic prosperity. It also recognised that insistent and overwhelming public opinion would have to be respected, making statement 3 false.
255.tq: Identify the statement that reverses the report's qualification about democratic public opinion.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1: correct — the report **reaffirmed Dhar**.
Statement 2: correct — it put **security, unity, economic prosperity** first.
Statement 3: wrong — it said if public opinion is "**insistent and overwhelming**, we as democrats have to submit to it".
xa: Report submitted **April 1949** to the **CWC**.
**T.T. Krishnamachari**: neighbouring states would also have to consent.
Madras government + **Tamil Nadu Congress** agreed to Andhra without Madras.

255.s: T. T. Krishnamachari added which qualification to the proposal for creating Andhra?
o: The Andhra demand should be decided by referendum in every district
The approval of the Governor-General alone would be sufficient
The approval of neighbouring states would also be necessary
The consent of the British Cabinet would be necessary
255.x: T. T. Krishnamachari stated that neighbouring states would also have to consent to the creation of Andhra.
255.tq: Ask which authority or group was specifically associated with the additional qualification.
xs: **T.T. Krishnamachari** added that **neighbouring states would also have to consent** — option **(3)** is correct.
No referendum or Governor-General's approval figures in the notes.
xa: **CWC**: Andhra **without Madras city**.
T.T. Krishnamachari was a **Tamil** member of the **Partition Committee**.
⚠ Some notes name him as Partition Committee chairman — **wrong**; it was **Kumaraswamy Raja**.

255.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to the three-member committee associated with linguistic provinces?

1. Jawaharlal Nehru — Member
2. Vallabhbhai Patel — Member
3. Pattabhi Sitaramayya — Member
4. N. Sanjiva Reddy — Member
255.x: The three members were Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel and Pattabhi Sitaramayya. N. Sanjiva Reddy was not a member.
255.tq: Use the membership-composition trap by identifying the outsider in the list.
xs: **1, 2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**: the JVP members were **Jawaharlal Nehru**, **Vallabhbhai Patel**, **Pattabhi Sitaramayya**.
**N. Sanjiva Reddy** was **not a member** (APPSC 2021 trap).
xa: Called the "**Three Ministers Committee**".
Set up by **Congress** at **Jaipur**, **December 1948**.
⚠ The **Dar Commission** members were **S.K. Dhar**, **Panna Lal**, **Jagat Narayan Lal**.

255.s: What did the Congress Working Committee recommend after the JVP report regarding the creation of Andhra State?
o: No linguistic state should be formed until after the States Reorganisation Commission.
Andhra should be merged with Rayalaseema and Hyderabad immediately.
Andhra should be formed without Madras city.
Andhra should be formed with Madras city as its capital and half the city shared with Tamil areas.
255.x: The Congress Working Committee recommended forming Andhra without Madras city. The Madras government and Tamil Nadu Congress accepted this position, while Andhra Congress wanted half of Madras town.
255.tq: Test the exact institutional recommendation and avoid confusing it with the Andhra Congress demand.
xs: The **CWC** recommended Andhra **without Madras city** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **Madras government** and **Tamil Nadu Congress** agreed; the **Andhra Congress** wanted **half of Madras town**.
xa: This followed the **JVP** report of **April 1949**.
The Madras **Partition Committee** followed (Cabinet decision **7 Dec 1949**).
**P.S. Kumaraswamy Raja's** government accepted Andhra on **JVP terms**.

255.s: The JVP Committee was constituted in December 1948 by the
255.x: The JVP Committee was constituted by the Congress in December 1948. Its members were Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel and Pattabhi Sitaramayya.
255.tq: Apply the ‘who constituted the body?’ test to distinguish two related committees.
xs: The **JVP Committee** was set up by the **Indian National Congress** (Jaipur, **December 1948**) — option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ The **Constituent Assembly** appointed the **Dar Commission** (**June 1948**).
xa: Members: **Nehru, Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya** (president).
Report **April 1949**: postpone new provinces.
Commission sequence: **Dhar (1948)** → **JVP (1948-49)** → **Wanchoo (1953)** → **SRC (1953-55)**.

255.s: The committee formed by the Madras Government under Chief Minister P.S. Kumaraswami Raja was primarily concerned with:
o: Selecting the first Governor of Andhra State
Dividing the assets and liabilities between Madras and Andhra
Drafting a constitution for Andhra State
255.x: The committee was constituted to divide assets and liabilities between the proposed Andhra region and Madras. It failed because Madras leaders refused to surrender Madras city to Andhra.
255.tq: Identify the purpose of the committee before examining why it failed.
xs: The **Partition Committee** under CM **P.S. Kumaraswami Raja** was formed to **divide assets and liabilities** — option **(3)** is correct.
It also handled **administrative arrangements** and the **six Bellary taluks**.
xa: Madras Cabinet decided on it on **7 Dec 1949**.
Report **4 Jan 1950**; **Prakasam** wrote a separate report.
It **failed**: Madras leaders refused to let **Madras city** go to Andhra.

255.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Andhra State movement is correct?
o: The Constitution itself fixed 1 October 1953 as the date of Andhra State formation.
The Andhra State was formed before the Constitution came into force.
The Constitution of 26 January 1950 already included a separate Andhra State.
The Constitution of 26 January 1950 did not include a separate Andhra State.
255.x: There was no separate Andhra State in the Constitution as it came into force on 26 January 1950, although the Partition Committee had proposed that date in its deliberations.
255.tq: Watch for the false constitutional assumption created by a proposed date.
xs: The Constitution of **26 January 1950** did **not** include a separate Andhra State — option **(4)** is correct.
Andhra State came on **1 October 1953**, after the Constitution — by the **Andhra State Act** (assent **14 Sept 1953**), not the Constitution.
xa: The **Partition Committee** had proposed forming Andhra on **26 Jan 1950** — not implemented.
The **Andhra Mahasabha** too demanded the state by **26 January 1950**.
Andhra = **first state formed on a linguistic basis**.

255.s: Who was the leading champion of Andhra separation among the Madras Chief Ministers listed below?
255.x: T. Prakasam, Chief Minister during 1946–47, was the leading champion of Andhra separation and submitted a separate report to the Partition Committee.
255.tq: Match the political stand with the correct Chief Minister and tenure.
xs: **T. Prakasam** (CM **1946-47**) was the **leading champion** of Andhra — option **(3)** is correct.
**Kumaraswamy Raja** chaired the Partition Committee; **Rajagopalachari** made anti-Andhra statements.
xa: Prakasam filed a **separate report** in the Partition Committee (**4 Jan 1950**).
Title: **Andhra Kesari**; first CM of Andhra State (**1 Oct 1953**).
Book: "**Chenna Nagaramu Andhra Nagaramae**".

255.s: Which Madras Chief Minister chaired the Partition Committee constituted in 1949?
255.x: P.S. Kumaraswamy Raja, Chief Minister of Madras from 1949 to 1952, chaired the Partition Committee.
255.tq: Use the office-holder trap by separating the committee chairman from the committee members.
xs: **P.S. Kumaraswamy Raja** (Madras CM **1949-52**) chaired the Partition Committee — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes say **T.T. Krishnamachari** — wrong (APPSC G2 2025 key = Kumaraswamy Raja).
xa: Andhra members: **T. Prakasam**, **Kala Venkatrao**, **Bezawada Gopala Reddy**, **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy**.
Tamil members: **T.T. Krishnamachari**, **C. Rajagopalachari**, **Madhava Menon**.
Report: **4 Jan 1950**.

255.s: Which one of the following statements about C. Rajagopalachari's position is correct?
o: He was the leading champion of a separate Andhra during 1946–47.
As Premier in 1937, he included Rayalaseema in his cabinet and supported Andhra separation.
As Premier in 1937, he left Rayalaseema out of his cabinet and later made anti-Andhra statements.
He chaired the Andhra Partition Committee and submitted a separate Andhra report.
255.x: C. Rajagopalachari left Rayalaseema out of his cabinet as Premier in 1937 and later made anti-Andhra statements. He served as Madras Chief Minister from 1952 to 1954.
255.tq: Use the person-with-deed trap and identify the precise political position.
xs: **Rajaji**, as **1937** Premier, left Rayalaseema out of his cabinet and later made **anti-Andhra statements** — option **(3)** is correct.
The 1946-47 champion was **T. Prakasam**; the Partition Committee chair was **Kumaraswamy Raja**.
xa: He was Madras CM **1952-54**.
He opposed sharing **Madras** (later **Kamaraj** too).
The 1937 cabinet snub **deepened** the regional rift.

255.s: Which of the following was NOT a task of the Madras Partition Committee?
o: Drafting the Constitution of the Republic of India
Consideration of the six Bellary taluks
255.x: The committee dealt with division of assets, administrative arrangements and the six Bellary taluks. Drafting the Constitution of India was not its task.
255.tq: Find the unrelated constitutional function among the committee's administrative responsibilities.
xs: **Drafting the Constitution of India** was **not** a Partition Committee task — option **(1)** is the answer.
Its tasks: **division of assets**, **administrative arrangements**, the **six Bellary taluks**.
xa: Formed by CM **P.S. Kumaraswami Raja**; Cabinet decision **7 Dec 1949**.
Report **4 Jan 1950**.
Later, **Bellary taluk** went to **Mysore** on **Justice L.S. Misra's** report.

255.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the Andhra members of the Madras Partition Committee?
o: T. Prakasam, Kala Venkatrao, Bezawada Gopala Reddy and Neelam Sanjiva Reddy
T.T. Krishnamachari, Bhaktavatsalam, Madhava Menon and C. Rajagopalachari
P.S. Kumaraswamy Raja, T. Prakasam, Rajaji and N. Sanjiva Reddy
Kala Venkatrao, Bhaktavatsalam, Bezawada Gopala Reddy and Madhava Menon
255.x: The Andhra members were T. Prakasam, Kala Venkatrao, Bezawada Gopala Reddy and Neelam Sanjiva Reddy. The other named members belonged to the Tamil side or chaired the committee.
255.tq: Separate the two regional groups before selecting the complete membership set.
xs: The Andhra members were **T. Prakasam**, **Kala Venkatrao**, **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** and **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** — option **(1)** is correct.
**T.T. Krishnamachari**, **C. Rajagopalachari**, **Madhava Menon** (and **Bhaktavatsalam** per CDX) were the **Tamil** members.
xa: Chairman: **Kumaraswamy Raja**.
**Kala Venkatarao** drafted the "**Kurnool Circular**" (APPSC 2018).
**Prakasam** wrote a **separate report**.

255.s: What was the principal difference between T. Prakasam's position and the majority position in the Partition Committee?
o: Prakasam supported Madras as the capital, while the committee rejected Andhra State altogether.
Prakasam opposed any separate Andhra, while the committee supported it.
Prakasam demanded Rayalaseema be excluded, while the committee demanded its merger with Hyderabad.
Prakasam wrote a separate report, while the committee otherwise agreed on forming Andhra on 26 January 1950.
255.x: The committee agreed on the formation of Andhra on 26 January 1950, but T. Prakasam submitted a separate report reflecting his distinct position.
255.tq: Compare the dissenting report with the committee's common recommendation.
xs: **Prakasam wrote a separate report**, while the committee agreed on forming Andhra on **26 Jan 1950** — option **(4)** is correct.
The plan was **not implemented**: Madras leaders refused to let **Madras city** go.
xa: Report dated **4 Jan 1950**.
The Constitution of **26 Jan 1950** had **no Andhra state**.
Prakasam was the **leading champion** of Andhra among Madras CMs.

255.s: The Andhra Mahasabha demanded that Andhra State be formed by:
255.x: The Andhra Mahasabha demanded the formation of Andhra State by 26 January 1950.
255.tq: Distinguish the movement's demanded deadline from later actual reorganisation dates.
xs: The **Andhra Mahasabha** demanded the state by **26 January 1950** — option **(1)** is correct.
**1 October 1953** = Andhra State formed; **1 November 1956** = Andhra Pradesh.
xa: The **Partition Committee** too agreed on **26 Jan 1950** — not implemented.
**Swami Sitaram's** fast (**1951**) demanded the state by **2 October 1951**.
**1949**: the **Visalandhra Mahasabha** was formed for all Telugu areas.

255.s: Swami Sitaram, who undertook a fast for a separate Andhra State in 1951, was also known as
255.x: Swami Sitaram was the popular name of Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri, a Gandhian associated with the Andhra movement.
255.tq: Use the direct identity link between a popular name and the full name.
xs: **Swami Sitaram** was **Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri (Sastry)**, a Gandhian — option **(3)** is correct.
**Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** founded **Andhra Patrika**; **Konda Venkatappayya** co-founded **Krishna Patrika**; **Jonnavittula Gurunatham** wrote the **1911** series in **The Hindu**.
xa: His fast: **15 August to 20 September 1951**, **35 days**.
He led the **palm-tree cutting** campaign in the **Civil Disobedience Movement**.
⚠ **Swami Sitaram** = **35 days** (1951, ended by **Vinoba Bhave**); **Potti Sriramulu** = **58 days** (1952, died).

255.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Swami Sitaram's fast:
1. He undertook the fast for a separate Andhra State.
2. The fast lasted for 35 days.
3. It was undertaken in August 1953.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: Swami Sitaram fasted for a separate Andhra State for 35 days in 1951, not 1953. Therefore, statements 1 and 2 are correct.
255.tq: Split the statements by checking the year against the established chronology.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1: correct — he fasted for a **separate Andhra State**.
Statement 2: correct — the fast lasted **35 days**.
Statement 3: wrong — it ran **15 August to 20 September 1951**, not 1953.
xa: Demand: Andhra state by **2 October 1951**.
Madras city's status to be settled within **three** years.
It ended on **Acharya Vinoba Bhave's** appeal — empty assurances, no gain.

255.s: Which one of the following was NOT a demand associated with Swami Sitaram's 1951 fast?
o: Settlement of Madras city's status within three years
Immediate merger of Telangana with Andhra State
Formation of Andhra State by 2 October 1951
Neither Andhra nor Tamil interests controlling Madras city during the interim
255.x: The demands concerned the formation of Andhra State, settlement of Madras city's status, and an interim arrangement over the city. Merger of Telangana was not one of the stated demands.
255.tq: Find the option outside the specific demand set.
xs: **Immediate merger of Telangana** was **not** one of Swami Sitaram's demands — option **(2)** is the answer.
His demands: Andhra State by **2 October 1951**; Madras city's status settled within **three years**; **neither side** to control Madras meanwhile.
xa: Fast: **35 days**, **15 August to 20 September 1951**.
Ended on the appeal of **Vinoba Bhave**.
**Nehru criticised** the fast.

255.s: What was one important consequence of the failure to secure gains after Swami Sitaram ended his fast?
o: Confidence in the Congress leadership among Andhras was weakened
Madras became a shared Union Territory
The Andhra movement immediately achieved a separate state
The Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party was dissolved
255.x: The fast ended without gain, which hurt Andhra confidence in the Congress leadership and weakened the movement temporarily.
255.tq: Trace the stated cause-and-effect relationship instead of selecting a later political outcome.
xs: The fast ended with no gain and **Andhra confidence in the Congress leadership was hurt** — option **(1)** is correct.
The movement was also **weakened for a time**; Andhra State came only on **1 October 1953**.
xa: **Nehru** criticised the fast.
Context: **Prakasam and Ranga** had left Congress to form the **Kisan Mazdoor (Praja) Party**.
**Potti Sriramulu's** fast followed in **1952** (**58 days**).

255.s: Swami Sitaram had earlier led which campaign during the Civil Disobedience Movement?
255.x: Swami Sitaram was a Gandhian who had led the palm-tree cutting campaign during the Civil Disobedience Movement.
255.tq: Link the leader with the specific campaign rather than a general Gandhian activity.
xs: Swami Sitaram led the **palm-tree cutting** campaign in the **CDM** — option **(4)** is correct.
He was a **Gandhian**, **Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri**.
xa: ⚠ **Temple-entry** fasts belong to **Potti Sriramulu** (**1946**, Nellore Venugopala Swamy temple).
Sitaram's statehood fast: **35 days** in **1951**.
⚠ **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** led the first **salt squad** from the Swarajya office, Madras (**13 April 1930**).

255.s:
Consider the following statements about the political context of Swami Sitaram's fast:
1. Sanjiva Reddy defeated N.G. Ranga in the April 1951 APCC election.
2. Sanjiva Reddy's margin of victory was five votes.
3. Prakasam and Ranga subsequently formed the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: All three statements are correct: Sanjiva Reddy defeated N.G. Ranga by five votes, after which Prakasam and Ranga left to form the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party.
255.tq: Check the linked sequence of election result, margin and subsequent political action.
xs: All three statements are correct — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
Statement 1: in the **April 1951** APCC election, **N. Sanjiva Reddy** (backed by Pattabhi) beat **N.G. Ranga** (Prakasam's candidate).
Statement 2: the margin was **5 votes**.
Statement 3: **Prakasam and Ranga** then left to form the **Kisan Mazdoor (Praja) Party**.
xa: The split (**Prakasam and Ranga vs Pattabhi and Sanjiva Reddy**) **delayed the state**.
Swami Sitaram fasted **15 August to 20 September 1951**.
**Leadership splits** — **Circars vs Rayalaseema**, **Prakasam vs Pattabhi** — repeatedly slowed the movement.

255.s: On whose appeal did Swami Sitaram end his fast in 1951?
255.x: Swami Sitaram ended his fast on the appeal of Vinoba Bhave.
255.tq: Test who intervened in ending the fast.
xs: Swami Sitaram ended his fast on the appeal of **Acharya Vinoba Bhave** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Nehru** criticised the fast rather than ending it.
xa: The fast gave only **empty assurances**, no gain.
It lasted **35 days** (**1951**).
⚠ **Potti Sriramulu** did not end his fast — he died on the **58th day** (**15 December 1952**).

255.s: Which political rivalry is identified as having delayed the formation of Andhra State?
o: Prakasam versus Pattabhi and Ranga versus Sanjiva Reddy
B.N. Sarma versus Guthi Kesava Pillai and Prakasam versus Nehru
Sitaram versus Sriramulu and Ranga versus Rajaji
Jinnah versus Sastri and Nehru versus Patel
255.x: Rivalries between Prakasam and Pattabhi, and between Ranga and Sanjiva Reddy, delayed the formation of the state.
255.tq: Select the complete paired relationship rather than a single name.
xs: **Prakasam and Ranga vs Pattabhi and Sanjiva Reddy** — the group rivalry that **delayed the state** — option **(1)** is correct.
It came to a head in the **April 1951** APCC election, which **Sanjiva Reddy** won by **5 votes**.
xa: **Prakasam and Ranga** then formed the **Kisan Mazdoor (Praja) Party**.
⚠ **Jinnah** and **V.S. Srinivasa Sastri** were **allies** in opposing Sarma's **1918** resolution, not rivals.
The **Circars vs Rayalaseema** split also slowed the movement.

255.s: Potti Sriramulu's ancestral village, as identified in the available account, was:
255.x: Gajula Dinne in Nellore district is identified as Potti Sriramulu's ancestral village. Mylapore was associated with the later venue of his fast, not his ancestral village.
255.tq: Distinguish a person's ancestral place from the place of a later political event.
xs: Potti Sriramulu's ancestral village was **Gajula Dinne**, **Nellore district** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Mylapore** was where **Bulusu Sambamurthy** housed him for the **1952** fast; he was born in **Madras**.
xa: Born **16 March 1901**, **Arya Vysya** family.
Nellore was renamed "**Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore District**" (**2008**).
He left his **railway job** after his wife and mother died.

255.s: Potti Sriramulu was born on 16 March 1901 in a family belonging to which community?
255.x: Potti Sriramulu was born on 16 March 1901 in an Arya Vysya family. His ancestral village was Gajula Dinne in Nellore.
255.tq: Test a precise biographical detail carried in the heading and introductory account.
xs: Potti Sriramulu was born in an **Arya Vysya** family on **16 March 1901** — option **(4)** is correct.
Born in **Madras**; ancestral village **Gajula Dinne**, Nellore district.
xa: Some notes give **15 March**; older notes **15 March 1901 or 1911**.
125th birth anniversary: **16 March 2026** — **58-foot** "**Statue of Sacrifice**", **Sakhamuru Park, Amaravati**.
Titles: **Amarajeevi**; "**Andhra Martyra Martanda**".

255.s: Which one of the following best explains why Potti Sriramulu left his railway job?
o: He resigned after the deaths of his wife and mother
He was appointed to the Madras Legislative Assembly
He left to join the Communist movement
He was dismissed for participating in the Civil Disobedience Movement
255.x: He left his railway employment after the deaths of his wife and mother and subsequently devoted himself to Gandhian constructive work.
255.tq: Link a biographical cause with the subsequent life choice.
xs: He **left his railway job after the deaths of his wife and mother** — option **(1)** is correct.
He then took up Gandhian work — not the **Communist** movement.
xa: He met **Gandhi** during the **Salt Satyagraha**; about **3 years at Sabarmati Ashram**.
Took part in **Non-cooperation**, **Salt Satyagraha**, **CDM**, **Quit India**; jailed several times.
**Gandhi (Madras, 1946)**: with **10-12** such patriots he would have won Swaraj long ago.

255.s:
Consider the following statements about Potti Sriramulu's Gandhian life:
1. He spent about three years at Sabarmati Ashram.
2. He did constructive work at the Komaravolu and Angaluru ashrams and in the Village Seva Sangam.
3. His constructive work included khadi, prohibition and Harijan uplift.
4. He was born in Nellore town, his ancestral village.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: about 3 years at Sabarmati; Komaravolu and Angaluru ashrams and the Village Seva Sangam; khadi, prohibition, Harijan uplift (and Hindu-Muslim unity). Statement 4 is wrong: he was born in Madras; his ancestral village was Gajula Dinne in Nellore district. So '1 and 2 only' is incomplete, and '2, 3 and 4 only' and '1, 2, 3 and 4' include statement 4.
255.tq: Born Madras, roots Gajula Dinne (Nellore); 3 years Sabarmati.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: correct — about **3 years at Sabarmati Ashram** (APPSC G2 2017).
Statements 2 and 3: correct — **Komaravolu** and **Angaluru** ashrams, **Village Seva Sangam**; khadi, prohibition, **Harijan uplift**.
Statement 4: wrong — he was born in **Madras**; his ancestral village was **Gajula Dinne**, Nellore district.
xa: His work also covered **Hindu-Muslim unity**.
Earlier fasts were for **Harijan** causes; the **1952** fast was his only one for statehood.
**Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University** is in **Hyderabad**.

255.s: The earlier fasts of Potti Sriramulu were primarily undertaken for which cause?
o: Demand for prohibition in Madras Presidency
255.x: His earlier fasts were undertaken for Harijan causes, including temple entry and Harijan welfare. The 1952 fast was his only fast for statehood.
255.tq: Separate the earlier Harijan fasts from the later statehood fast.
xs: His earlier fasts were for **Harijan causes** — including **temple entry** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **1952** fast was his **only fast for statehood**, so (3) is wrong for the earlier ones.
xa: **1946**: Nellore **Venugopala Swamy temple** — Harijan entry.
**1948**: **29 days**, **Wardha** — Harijan Day.
**1949**: **28 days** (January) — **Gandhi Smarak Din**.

255.s: What was the stated outcome of Potti Sriramulu's 1946 fast of 19 days?
o: A demand for a temple-entry law for Harijans
The establishment of a university in Nellore
The observance of Gandhi Smarak Din
255.x: The 19-day fast in 1946 was connected with the demand for a law permitting temple entry for Harijans.
255.tq: Distinguish two 1946 fast-related entries by their stated outcome.
xs: The **1946** fast of **19 days** sought a **temple-entry law for Harijans** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Gandhi Smarak Din** came from the **28-day** fast of **January 1949**.
xa: Another **1946** fast at the Nellore **Venugopala Swamy temple** won **Harijan entry** (CDX **10** days; APP **23** days).
**1948**: **29 days**, **Wardha** — Harijan Day and **₹1 crore**.
His only statehood fast: **1952**, **58 days**.

255.s: Potti Sriramulu's 29-day fast at Wardha in 1948 was associated with which combination?
o: Harijan Day and a grant of one crore rupees
Temple entry and the formation of Andhra State
Gandhi Smarak Din and the creation of Rayalaseema
Prohibition and the establishment of Andhra University
255.x: The Wardha fast in 1948 was associated with the observance of Harijan Day and a grant of one crore rupees. Madras also marked Harijan Welfare Day on the thirtieth of every month.
255.tq: Match the duration and place of a fast with its distinctive outcome.
xs: The **1948 Wardha** fast of **29 days** led Nehru to declare a **Harijan Day** and **₹1 crore** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Gandhi Smarak Din** came from the **1949** fast; **temple entry** from **1946**.
xa: **Madras** marks **Harijan Welfare Day** on the **30th** of every month (APP).
**1946**: **19 days** — temple-entry law for Harijans.

255.s: The 28-day fast undertaken by Potti Sriramulu in January 1949 resulted in the observance of which day?
255.x: The 28-day fast in January 1949 was associated with the observance of Gandhi Smarak Din.
255.tq: Test the year-and-outcome association from a chronological fast table.
xs: The **28-day** fast of **January 1949** led to observance of **Gandhi Smarak Din** — option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ **Harijan Welfare Day** (30th of every month, Madras) is linked to the **1948 Wardha** fast.
xa: **Andhra State Day** was **Diwali 1937** — unrelated to his fasts.
**1948**: **29 days**, **Wardha** — Harijan Day + **₹1 crore**.
**1946**: **19 days** — temple-entry law demand.

255.s: On 19 December 1952, Jawaharlal Nehru announced that Andhra State would be formed from:
o: Telangana and the coastal districts of Madras Presidency
The undisputed Telugu-speaking areas, excluding Madras city
All Telugu-speaking areas including Madras city
The entire Madras Presidency excluding Rayalaseema
255.x: Nehru announced that Andhra State would be formed from the undisputed Telugu areas, while Madras city would be excluded.
255.tq: Separate the accepted Telugu areas from the specifically excluded Madras city.
xs: On **19 December 1952**, Nehru told Parliament Andhra would be formed from the **undisputed Telugu areas, excluding Madras city** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Telangana** joined only in **1956** (Andhra Pradesh); Madras city was never included.
xa: ⚠ **19 December** is often misgiven as Sriramulu's death — he died on **15 December 1952**.
**25 March 1953**: Nehru — "**No question**" of Madras as the capital.
Andhra State formed **1 October 1953**.

255.s: Potti Sriramulu began his final fast at the house of:
255.x: Although the fast initially began at the St. George's Fort gate, Bulusu Sambamurthy moved Sriramulu to his house in Mylapore, which is generally given as the venue.
255.tq: Distinguish the initial location from the recognised venue of the fast.
xs: Sriramulu fasted at **Bulusu Sambamurthy's** house in **Mylapore** — option **(3)** is correct.
He first began at the **St. George's Fort gate** (CDX); Sambamurthy then moved him to his house — the venue in most notes.
xa: Start: **19 October 1952**, Madras.
Plan disclosed to friend **V. Lakshminarayana** in **September 1952**.
**Bulusu Sambamurthy** was a **coastal signatory** of the **Sri Bagh Pact**.

255.s: Potti Sriramulu's final fast lasted for:
255.x: The final fast is recorded as lasting 58 days. Some accounts mention 56 days, but the specified exam-oriented figure is 58 days.
255.tq: Give priority to the stated standard figure when nearby numerical variants are distractors.
xs: The final fast lasted **58 days** — option **(3)** is correct.
Some notes say **56** days; **29 days** was his **1948 Wardha** fast.
xa: Start **19 October 1952**; death **15 December 1952**.
⚠ **Swami Sitaram's** fast = **35 days** (**1951**).
The **58-foot** "Statue of Sacrifice" echoes the **58-day** fast.

255.s: Which one of the following statements about the aftermath of Potti Sriramulu's death is correct?
o: The States Reorganisation Commission was dissolved after his death
The Congress rejected the demand for a separate Andhra State
There were riots and police firing in which seven persons died, followed by Nehru's announcement of Andhra State
The Madras Government immediately accepted Madras city as the capital of Andhra
255.x: Sriramulu's death was followed by riots and police firing in which seven people died. Nehru announced the formation of Andhra State in Parliament on 19 December 1952.
255.tq: Select the option combining the immediate consequence with the subsequent governmental response.
xs: His death sparked **riots**; police firing at **Anakapalli** killed **7**; Nehru then announced Andhra State — option **(3)** is correct.
The **SRC** came **after** this (**Dec 1953**), and Madras was **excluded**, not made Andhra's capital.
xa: **Hartals, demonstrations, riots**; railway stations, post offices attacked.
MLA **Tenneti Viswanatham** and MLC **P. Sitaramayya** resigned.
Announcement in Parliament: **19 December 1952**.

255.s: Potti Sriramulu sought the formation of a state comprising which of the following areas?
o: The Telugu-speaking districts along with the entire Madras city area
The Telugu-speaking districts of Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema
255.x: Potti Sriramulu demanded a separate state consisting of both Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema. The question of Madras city was left for later negotiation.
255.tq: Test the territorial scope directly and distinguish the core demand from the disputed city question.
xs: Sriramulu sought a state of the Telugu districts of **Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Madras city** was left to **later negotiation** (APPSC 2019).
xa: His condition on Madras: a **Chief Commissioner's (C-class) state** by agreement.
Andhra State (**1953**): **Coastal Andhra (7)** + **Rayalaseema (4)** districts.
⚠ **Swami Sitaram's** 1951 demand: Madras's status settled within **three years**.

255.s: Which one of the following was NOT one of the three conditions associated with Potti Sriramulu's demand?
o: Madras city should become a Chief Commissioner's State by agreement
The Andhra State should include the whole of the Madras Presidency
The Centre should announce the formation of Andhra State immediately
255.x: The three conditions concerned immediate announcement, unity among Andhra leaders and making Madras a Chief Commissioner's State by agreement. Inclusion of the entire Madras Presidency was not a condition.
255.tq: Find the option that goes beyond the precise three-condition formulation.
xs: Inclusion of **the whole Madras Presidency** was **not** a condition — option **(2)** is the answer.
The **three conditions**: Centre to **announce Andhra State at once**; Andhra leaders to **stay united**; **Madras city** → **Chief Commissioner's (C-class) state** by agreement.
xa: The C-class arrangement was also called a "**free state**".
On the **50th day**, Nehru offered Andhra **without Madras** if all parties agreed.
He died on the **58th day**.

255.s: On the 50th day of Potti Sriramulu's fast, Jawaharlal Nehru offered to form Andhra State subject to which condition?
o: Andhra should accept Madras as its capital
Rayalaseema should be excluded from Andhra State
The demand should be referred to the States Reorganisation Commission
Andhra should be formed without Madras if all parties agreed
255.x: On the fiftieth day, Nehru offered to form Andhra without Madras, provided all parties agreed. Sriramulu rejected the offer and distrusted a later telegram.
255.tq: Use the specific condition attached to a political offer as the key discriminator.
xs: On the **50th day**, Nehru offered Andhra **without Madras if all parties agreed** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Sriramulu rejected** the offer and distrusted a later telegram.
xa: ⚠ The **JVP** formula (**1948**) had also required dropping the Madras claim.
He died on **15 December 1952** (**58th day**).
**19 December 1952**: Andhra announced, excluding **Madras city**.

255.s: Which of the following correctly describes the public reaction after Potti Sriramulu's death?
o: There were no major disturbances outside Madras city
The reaction was confined to the Andhra Legislative Assembly
The Madras Government immediately declared a state of emergency throughout India
Hartals, demonstrations and riots occurred across Andhra
255.x: His death led to hartals, demonstrations and riots across Andhra. Railway stations, post offices and offices were attacked.
255.tq: Distinguish the broad regional reaction from narrowly confined alternatives.
xs: His death led to **hartals, demonstrations and riots across Andhra** — option **(4)** is correct.
Railway stations, post offices and offices were attacked — far beyond Madras city.
xa: Police firing at **Anakapalli** killed **7**.
The **Madras Mail** editor compared his sacrifice to **Christ's**.
His death "**forced the Centre's hand**" → Andhra → **SRC** → **States Reorganisation Act 1956**.

255.s: Who resigned in protest following the public reaction to Potti Sriramulu's death?
o: Burgula Ramakrishna Rao and N. Venkatramayya
Neelam Sanjiva Reddy and C.M. Trivedi
T. Prakasam and Bezawada Gopala Reddy
255.x: MLA Tenneti Viswanatham and MLC P. Sitaramayya resigned in protest.
255.tq: Use a paired-person recall question with office-based distractors.
xs: MLA **Tenneti Viswanatham** and MLC **P. Sitaramayya** resigned — option **(4)** is correct.
**T. Prakasam** became Andhra State's **first CM** in **1953**; **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** became **Deputy CM**; **C.M. Trivedi** became Governor.
xa: **Tenneti Viswanatham** later sat on the advisory committee with **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** to **Special Officer Trivedi**.
Police firing at **Anakapalli** killed **7**.
Nehru's announcement followed on **19 December 1952**.

255.s: The editor of which newspaper compared Potti Sriramulu's sacrifice to that of Christ?
255.x: The editor of The Madras Mail compared Potti Sriramulu's sacrifice to the sacrifice of Christ.
255.tq: Test the exact newspaper-person association rather than the wider event.
xs: The editor of **The Madras Mail** compared Sriramulu's sacrifice to **Christ's** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Andhra Patrika** (**Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**) and **Deshabhimani** (Guntur) were earlier Andhra-cause papers.
xa: Title after death: **Amarajeevi** (Immortal Martyr).
**Hartals** and **riots** followed across Andhra.
⚠ **The Hindu** carried **Jonnavittula Gurunatham's** **1911** articles.

255.s: Potti Sriramulu, honoured with the title 'Amarajeevi', died on the 58th day of his fast. The date of his death was:
255.x: Sriramulu began his fast on 19 October 1952 and died on its 58th day, 15 December 1952, earning the title 'Amarajeevi'. 19 December 1952 is the date of Nehru's announcement in Parliament (a common trap), and 1 October 1953 is the formation of Andhra State.
255.tq: 19 Oct start - 15 Dec death - 19 Dec announcement - 1 Oct 1953 state.
xs: **Amarajeevi** Potti Sriramulu died on **15 December 1952**, the **58th day** — option **(2)** is correct.
**19 October 1952** = fast began; **19 December 1952** = **Nehru's announcement** (common trap); **1 October 1953** = Andhra State formed.
xa: Some notes say **56** days.
Exam angle: **19 Oct** start, **15 Dec** death, **19 Dec** announcement, "**58 days**".
Venue: **Bulusu Sambamurthy's** house, **Mylapore**.

255.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Potti Sriramulu began his final fast
B. Nehru announced the formation of Andhra State in Parliament
C. Potti Sriramulu died
D. Justice K.N. Wanchoo was appointed
255.x: Sriramulu began his fast on 19 October 1952 (A), died on 15 December 1952 (C), Nehru announced Andhra State in Parliament on 19 December 1952 (B), and Wanchoo was appointed on 7 February 1953 (D). The other orders misplace the Wanchoo appointment or put the announcement before the death.
255.tq: Fast 19 Oct -> death 15 Dec -> announcement 19 Dec 1952 -> Wanchoo 7 Feb 1953.
xs: The order is **A, C, B, D** — option **(1)** is correct.
**A**: fast begins **19 October 1952** → **C**: death **15 December 1952**.
**B**: Nehru's announcement **19 December 1952** → **D**: **Justice K.N. Wanchoo** appointed **7 Feb 1953**.
xa: Wanchoo report: **25 Mar 1953** (some notes **23 March 1953**).
Act introduced **10 Aug 1953**; President's assent **14 Sept 1953**.
Andhra State formed **1 October 1953**.

255.s: The committee headed by Justice K.N. Wanchoo was appointed on:
255.x: Justice K.N. Wanchoo was appointed on 7 February 1953 to report on the implications of the proposed Andhra State.
255.tq: Use exact-date discrimination among closely related Andhra movement events.
xs: **Justice K.N. Wanchoo** was appointed on **7 February 1953** — option **(2)** is correct.
**19 December 1952** = Nehru's announcement; **19 October 1952** = start of Sriramulu's fast.
xa: Wanchoo was **Chief Justice, Rajasthan HC**; a **single-member** committee.
He reported on the **implications** of forming Andhra.
Report dated **25 Mar 1953** (some notes **23 March 1953**).

255.s: Justice K.N. Wanchoo submitted his report on the proposed Andhra State in:
255.x: Wanchoo submitted his report in March 1953. Sources give differing exact dates within March, so the month is the reliable point.
255.tq: Choose the reliable time unit when exact dates are uncertain.
xs: Wanchoo reported in **March 1953** — option **(1)** is correct.
Notes date it **25 Mar 1953**; some say **23 March 1953** — either way, March.
xa: He was appointed on **7 Feb 1953**.
The Centre accepted his report **except on Bellary** (he had suggested the whole district go to Andhra).
**25 March 1953**: Nehru — "**No question**" of Madras as the capital.

255.s: Which statement correctly reflects the decision regarding Madras city in the formation of Andhra State?
o: Madras was made a Chief Commissioner's State under the Act
Madras was made the permanent capital of Andhra State
Madras was declared a joint capital of Andhra and Tamil areas
There was no question of making Madras the capital of Andhra State
255.x: The decision leading to Andhra State made it clear that there was no question of Madras being its capital.
255.tq: Distinguish the rejected capital claim from proposals concerning Madras's separate status.
xs: Nehru announced (**25 March 1953**) there was "**No question**" of **Madras** as the capital — option **(4)** is correct.
Madras city was **excluded** and stayed with Madras State; it was not made a C-class state.
xa: Andhra's capital became **Kurnool** (temporary).
⚠ Sriramulu's **C-class state** idea for Madras was **not** adopted.
Losing Madras left the new state "**administratively and economically orphaned**".

255.s: Which of the following correctly describes the final territorial adjustments concerning Bellary?
o: The entire Bellary district was added to Andhra State
Bellary taluk went to Mysore, Rayadurg to Anantapur, and Adoni and Alur to Kurnool
Bellary taluk went to Kurnool and Adoni to Mysore
Rayadurg and Alur were transferred to Hyderabad State
255.x: The Centre accepted Justice Mishra's report: Bellary taluk went to Mysore, Rayadurg was added to Anantapur, and Adoni and Alur were added to Kurnool.
255.tq: Match each territorial unit with its final destination and avoid reversing the transfers.
xs: **Bellary taluk → Mysore**, **Rayadurg → Anantapur**, **Adoni and Alur → Kurnool** — option **(2)** is correct.
Wanchoo had suggested the **whole district** go to Andhra, but the Centre did not accept that.
xa: Bellary taluk went to Mysore on **Justice L.S. Misra's** report.
**Siruguppa, Hospet, Sandur, Harpanahalli, Hadagali** also went to **Mysore**.
The **Partition Committee** had earlier considered the **six Bellary taluks**.

255.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the dates connected with the Andhra State Bill and the formation of Andhra State?
o: Introduction—10 August 1953; assent—14 September 1953; formation—1 October 1953
Introduction—14 September 1953; assent—10 August 1953; formation—1 October 1953
Introduction—10 August 1953; assent—1 October 1953; formation—14 September 1953
Introduction—1 October 1953; assent—14 September 1953; formation—10 August 1953
255.x: The Bill was introduced on 10 August 1953, received assent on 14 September 1953, and Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953.
255.tq: Order the legislative process by introduction, assent and commencement rather than by memorising isolated dates.
xs: **Introduced 10 Aug 1953 → assent 14 Sept 1953 → formed 1 October 1953** — option **(1)** is correct.
The other options jumble these three dates.
xa: Passage: **Madras Assembly → Lok Sabha → Rajya Sabha**.
Andhra = **first linguistic state** of independent India.
⚠ **1 Oct 1953** (Andhra State) vs **1 Nov 1956** (Andhra Pradesh).

255.s:
Consider the following pairs regarding the districts of Andhra State in 1953:
1. Coastal Andhra — 7 districts
2. Rayalaseema — 4 districts
3. Total districts — 11
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
255.x: The Coastal Andhra region had seven districts and Rayalaseema had four, making a total of eleven districts.
255.tq: Break the regional total into its two component figures before selecting the coded option.
xs: All three pairs are correct — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
**Coastal Andhra (7)**: Srikakulam, Visakhapatnam, East and West Godavari, Krishna, Guntur, Nellore.
**Rayalaseema (4)**: Chittoor, Cuddapah, Anantapur, Kurnool — **11** in all.
xa: Plus the **Bellary taluks** (some notes say "**12 districts**").
**Vizianagaram** and **Prakasam** districts did not exist yet.
Exam angle: **1 Oct 1953** and the **7 + 4** split.

255.s: Which one of the following was NOT included among the districts of Andhra State at the time of its formation?
255.x: Vizianagaram district did not exist at the time of Andhra State formation. Nellore, Kurnool and Chittoor were included.
255.tq: Find the later-created district among the districts belonging to the 1953 arrangement.
xs: **Vizianagaram** did not exist when Andhra State was formed — option **(4)** is the answer.
**Nellore** (Coastal), **Chittoor** and **Kurnool** (Rayalaseema) were among the **11** districts.
xa: **Prakasam** district too did not exist yet.
Coastal Andhra **7** + Rayalaseema **4**.
**Rayadurg** joined **Anantapur**; **Adoni and Alur** joined **Kurnool**.

255.s: The Bellary taluks that were associated with the formation of Andhra State were ultimately transferred to:
255.x: D is correct: Siruguppa, Hospet, Sandur, Harpanahalli, Hadagali and Bellary taluk itself (on Justice Misra's report) went to Mysore. Only Rayadurg (to Anantapur) and Adoni and Alur (to Kurnool) went to Andhra.
255.tq: Use the territorial-transfer trap by distinguishing the transferred taluks from the excluded Madras city.
xs: The Bellary taluks went to **Mysore State** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Siruguppa, Hospet, Sandur, Harpanahalli, Hadagali** and **Bellary taluk** (on **Justice L.S. Misra's** report) → Mysore.
xa: Only **Rayadurg** (→ **Anantapur**) and **Adoni and Alur** (→ **Kurnool**) went to Andhra.
Announced by Nehru on **25 March 1953**.
Wanchoo had suggested the **whole district** for Andhra.

255.s: Who inaugurated Andhra State at Kurnool?
255.x: Jawaharlal Nehru inaugurated Andhra State at Kurnool.
255.tq: Distinguish the inaugurating national leader from the constitutional authorities associated with state reorganisation.
xs: **Jawaharlal Nehru** inaugurated Andhra State at **Kurnool** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Rajendra Prasad** was President of the **Constituent Assembly**; **Rajagopalachari** was Madras CM (**1952-54**) and anti-Andhra.
xa: Formed **1 October 1953**, carved out of **Madras State**.
First CM **T. Prakasam**; Governor **C.M. Trivedi**.
Capital path: **Kurnool (1953) → Hyderabad (1956) → Amaravati**.

255.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Site)
a. Kurnool
b. Tirupati
c. Vijayawada/Guntur

aList-II (Supporter)
i. Communists
 ii. Congress, Prakasam's group and Rayalaseema leaders
 iii. Krishikar Lok Party

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
255.x: Kurnool was supported by Congress, Prakasam's group and Rayalaseema leaders; Tirupati was associated with the Krishikar Lok Party; and Vijayawada/Guntur was supported by the Communists.
255.tq: Start from the sure regional association and eliminate incompatible codes.
xs: **a–ii, b–iii, c–i** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Kurnool** — Congress, **Prakasam's** group, **Rayalaseema** leaders (Sreebagh Pact).
**Tirupati** — **Krishikar Lok Party**; **Vijayawada/Guntur** — **Communists** (**Puchalapalli Sundarayya**).
xa: ⚠ Some notes give **Praja Socialist Party** for Tirupati — follow the key (**Krishikar Lok Party**, APPSC G2 2025).
The Krishikar Lok Party **changed its stand** during the Assembly session.
Vote: **Kurnool 79** vs **Vijayawada 53**.

255.s:
With reference to the Madras Assembly vote on the capital of Andhra State, consider the following statements:
1. Kurnool secured 79 votes against 53 for Vijayawada.
2. Kurnool's victory was helped by five non-Andhra votes.
3. T. Prakasam voted in favour of Kurnool.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
255.x: Statement 1 is correct: Kurnool won 79 to 53, a margin of 26. Statement 2 is correct: five non-Andhra votes helped Kurnool. Statement 3 is wrong: Prakasam did not vote (and 6 members were absent). So '1 only' misses statement 2, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include statement 3.
255.tq: Remember 79-53 (margin 26), five non-Andhra votes, Prakasam did not vote.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: correct — **Kurnool 79**, **Vijayawada 53**, a margin of **26**.
Statement 2: correct — **five non-Andhra votes** helped Kurnool.
Statement 3: wrong — **Prakasam did not vote**; **6** members were absent.
xa: Kurnool was a **temporary** capital.
High Court went to **Guntur** under the **Sreebagh** balance.
**Communists** backed **Vijayawada**.

255.s: In June 1953, the Andhra MLAs met under the leadership of:
255.x: The Andhra MLAs met in June 1953 under T. Prakasam to consider the capital question. Congress, Prakasam's group and N.G. Ranga's Krishikar Lok Party initially agreed on Kurnool.
255.tq: Match the political meeting with its presiding leader.
xs: In **June 1953**, Andhra MLAs met under **T. Prakasam** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Congress**, **Prakasam's socialist group** and **N.G. Ranga's Krishikar Lok Party** first agreed on **Kurnool**.
xa: **Puchalapalli Sundarayya** led the **Communists**, who backed **Vijayawada**.
**P.S. Kumaraswami Raja** chaired the **1949** Partition Committee.
Final vote: **Kurnool 79**, **Vijayawada 53**.

255.s: Andhra State, the first state of independent India formed on a linguistic basis, came into existence on:
255.x: Andhra State was carved out of Madras State on 1 October 1953 as the first linguistic state, with Kurnool as capital. 15 December 1952 is Potti Sriramulu's death; 26 January 1950 is when the Constitution came into force without an Andhra State; 1 November 1956 is the formation of Andhra Pradesh.
255.tq: 1 Oct 1953 = Andhra State; 1 Nov 1956 = Andhra Pradesh.
xs: **Andhra State**, the first linguistic state, was formed on **1 October 1953** — option **(2)** is correct.
**15 December 1952** = Sriramulu's death; **26 January 1950** = Constitution, with no Andhra; **1 November 1956** = **Andhra Pradesh**.
xa: Carved out of **Madras State**; capital **Kurnool**.
It opened the way to the **SRC** (**Dec 1953**).
Firsts: CM **Prakasam**, Governor **C.M. Trivedi**, Speaker **N. Venkatramayya**.

255.s: T. Prakasam was associated with which of the following combinations?
o: Partition Committee, Kisan Mazdoor Party and first Chief Minister of Andhra State
Dhar Commission, Andhra Congress Committee and first Governor of Andhra Pradesh
JVP Committee, Swarajya and first Speaker of Andhra State
Visalandhra Mahasabha, Andhra Kesari and first president of Andhra Congress Committee
255.x: T. Prakasam served on the Partition Committee, formed the Kisan Mazdoor (Praja) Party with Ranga in 1951, and became the first Chief Minister of Andhra State on 1 October 1953.
255.tq: Combine three roles and reject options that swap institutions or offices.
xs: **Prakasam**: **Partition Committee** member, co-founder of the **Kisan Mazdoor (Praja) Party** (**1951**), **first CM of Andhra State** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **first president of the Andhra Congress Committee** was **Nyapati Subba Rao**; Prakasam was never on the **Dhar** or **JVP** bodies.
xa: He wrote a **separate report** in the Partition Committee (**4 Jan 1950**).
Title: **Andhra Kesari** — also the name of **Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao's** paper (**1904**).
His government fell over **liquor prohibition** (**Nov 1954**).

255.s: Who was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State?
255.x: Tanguturi Prakasam Pantulu was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State and headed a coalition government.
255.tq: Directly test the first office-holder and distinguish him from the succeeding Chief Minister.
xs: **Tanguturi Prakasam Pantulu** was Andhra State's **first CM**, heading a coalition — option **(1)** is correct.
**Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** was **Deputy CM**; **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** became CM after the **1955** mid-term poll.
xa: Prakasam's ministry fell in **Nov 1954** over **liquor prohibition**.
**President's rule** followed, then the **1955** poll.
⚠ **Burgula Ramakrishna Rao** shifted to favour merger in **1954**.

255.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched in the first Andhra State government?
255.x: C.M. or Chandulal Madhavlal Trivedi was the Governor. N. Venkatramayya was Speaker, Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was Deputy Chief Minister and T. Prakasam was Chief Minister.
255.tq: Start with the sure office-holder and eliminate swapped constitutional positions.
xs: **Governor — C.M. (Chandulal Madhavlal) Trivedi** is correctly matched — option **(1)** is correct.
**Speaker** = **N. Venkatramayya**; **Deputy CM** = **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy**; **CM** = **T. Prakasam**.
xa: **Trivedi** was earlier the Centre's **Special Officer** for setting up the state.
**Bezawada Gopala Reddy** presented the **1955-56** budget (APPSC GS 2021).
**Speaker in 1956**: **Laxmi Narasimham**.

255.s: Which statement regarding the legislature of the first Andhra State is correct?
o: It had a Legislative Council but no Legislative Assembly
Its Assembly consisted of members elected to the Madras Assembly in 1952, and it had no Legislative Council
Its members were nominated entirely by the Governor
It was formed through a fresh election held in October 1953
255.x: The Andhra Assembly consisted of members elected to the Madras Assembly in 1952. Andhra State did not have a Legislative Council.
255.tq: Test legislative composition and the absence of a second chamber together.
xs: The Assembly consisted of members elected to the **Madras Assembly in 1952**, and there was **no Legislative Council** — option **(2)** is correct.
No fresh election was held in **October 1953**; the first mid-term poll came in **1955**.
xa: **1955** poll: **United Congress front** (Congress + **Krishikar Lok Party** + **Praja Socialist Party**) beat the **Communists**.
**Bezawada Gopala Reddy** then became CM.
High Court at **Guntur**, set up **5 July 1954**.

255.s: Arrange the following in chronological order: A. T. Prakasam became Chief Minister of Andhra State; B. Prakasam's ministry fell; C. Mid-term election was held; D. Bezawada Gopala Reddy became Chief Minister.
255.x: Prakasam became Chief Minister on 1 October 1953, his ministry fell in November 1954, the mid-term poll followed in 1955, and Gopala Reddy then became Chief Minister.
255.tq: Fix the first and last events, then place the fall of the ministry before the mid-term poll.
xs: The correct order is **A, B, C, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**A:** **T. Prakasam** became the first CM of Andhra State on **1 Oct 1953**, heading a coalition.
**B:** His ministry fell on a no-confidence defeat in **Nov 1954**, over the **liquor-prohibition** controversy.
**C, D:** The **mid-term poll** followed in **1955**, after which **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** (Congress) became CM (1955-56).
xa: **President's rule** was imposed after Prakasam's ministry fell in **Nov 1954**.
⚠ Some notes put the fall of Prakasam's government in **1955**; the no-confidence defeat was **Nov 1954**.
Prakasam's title was **"Andhra Kesari"**; the first Deputy CM was **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** (later President of India).
Andhra State had **no Legislative Council**; its members had been elected to the Madras Assembly in **1952**.

255.s: Before the merger in 1956, which combination was correct?
o: Andhra State CM—B. Gopala Reddy; Speaker—Laxmi Narasimham
Andhra State CM—Burgula Ramakrishna Rao; Speaker—N. Venkatramayya
Andhra State CM—T. Prakasam; Speaker—Laxmi Narasimham
Andhra State CM—N. Sanjiva Reddy; Speaker—Burgula Ramakrishna Rao
255.x: Immediately before the 1956 merger, B. Gopala Reddy was Chief Minister and Laxmi Narasimham was Speaker of Andhra State. Burgula Ramakrishna Rao was Chief Minister of Hyderabad State.
255.tq: Compare the final office-holders of Andhra State with those of Hyderabad State.
xs: Before the **1956** merger, the Andhra State CM was **B. Gopala Reddy** and the Speaker was **Laxmi Narasimham** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**T. Prakasam** was the first CM (from **1 Oct 1953**), not the CM at the time of the merger.
**N. Venkatramayya** (Nallapati Venkatramaiah) was the **first** Speaker, not the Speaker in **1956**.
xa: **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** became CM after the **1955 mid-term poll** and presented the **1955-56 budget**.
First Governor of Andhra State: **C.M. (Chandulal Madhavlal) Trivedi**, earlier the Centre's **Special Officer** for setting up the state.
First Deputy CM: **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy**, later President of India.
The 1956 merger came with the **Gentlemen's Agreement** — cabinet ratio **60:40** (Andhra : Telangana).

255.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 1955 mid-term election in Andhra State:
1. It was held after the fall of the ministry headed by Tanguturi Prakasam.
2. The Congress contested in alliance with the Krishikar Lok Party and the Praja Socialist Party.
3. The United Congress front contested against the Communists.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: All three statements are correct. The election followed the fall of Prakasam's ministry, and the Congress, Krishikar Lok Party and Praja Socialist Party formed the United Congress front against the Communists.
255.tq: Test the complete alliance structure by checking the election context, constituent parties and principal opponent together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Statement 1 — correct:** the **1955** mid-term poll was held after **Prakasam's** ministry fell (no-confidence, **Nov 1954**).
**Statement 2 — correct:** the **United Congress front** = Congress + **Krishikar Lok Party** + **Praja Socialist Party**.
**Statement 3 — correct:** the front's opponent was the **Communists**; the front won.
xa: After the win, **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** became CM.
**N.G. Ranga's Krishikar Lok Party** had backed **Tirupati** as capital in 1953; the **Communists** (Puchalapalli Sundarayya) backed **Vijayawada / Guntur**.
Prakasam's government lost its majority over the **liquor-prohibition** controversy.

255.s:
Consider the following statements about the High Court of Andhra State:
1. It was located at Guntur, while the capital was at Kurnool, following the Sri Bagh Pact balance.
2. It was set up on 5 July 1954.
3. Until it was set up, the Madras High Court served Andhra State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: All three are correct: the High Court was placed at Guntur (Coastal Andhra) with the capital at Kurnool (Rayalaseema), as in the Sri Bagh Pact; it was set up on 5 July 1954; and the Madras High Court served Andhra in the interim. Any option leaving out a statement is incomplete.
255.tq: Capital Kurnool + High Court Guntur (1954) - APPSC G2 2008, 2025.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Statement 1 — correct:** High Court at **Guntur** (Coastal Andhra), capital at **Kurnool** (Rayalaseema), following the **Sreebagh Pact** balance.
**Statement 2 — correct:** the High Court was set up in **1954**, on **5 July 1954**.
**Statement 3 — correct:** the **Madras High Court** served Andhra in the interim.
xa: The **Sri Bagh Pact (16 Nov 1937)** put the **Capital and High Court in separate regions**, with Rayalaseema getting first choice.
Exam pair: **"capital Kurnool, High Court Guntur"** (APPSC G2 2008 and 2025).
In the Madras Assembly vote on the capital, **Kurnool 79** beat **Vijayawada 53**; Kurnool was a **temporary** capital.

255.s: Who presented the 1955-56 budget of Andhra State?
255.x: Bezawada Gopala Reddy presented the 1955-56 budget of Andhra State (APPSC GS 2021 key); he became CM after the 1955 mid-term poll. Prakasam was the first CM, Sanjiva Reddy the Deputy CM, and Tenneti Viswanatham sat on Trivedi's advisory committee.
255.tq: Budget 1955-56 = B. Gopala Reddy.
xs: **B. (Bezawada) Gopala Reddy** presented the **1955-56** budget of Andhra State (APPSC GS 2021 key) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**T. Prakasam** was the first CM; **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** was the Deputy CM.
**Tenneti Viswanatham** sat on Trivedi's advisory committee (with Sanjiva Reddy) and later resigned as MLA over Sriramulu's death.
xa: Gopala Reddy became CM after the **1955 mid-term poll**, won by the **United Congress front**.
Gopala Reddy was also an Andhra member of the **1949** Madras **Partition Committee**, and a coastal signatory of the **Sri Bagh Pact**.
First Governor: **C.M. Trivedi**; first Speaker: **N. Venkatramayya**.

255.s: In which year was Nellore district renamed Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore District?
255.x: Nellore district was renamed Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore District in 2008 by the government headed by Chief Minister Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy.
255.tq: Test a renaming year with closely spaced alternatives.
xs: Nellore was renamed **"Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore District"** in **2008** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The renaming was done under CM **Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy**.
xa: Sriramulu's ancestral village was **Gajula Dinne**, in Nellore district; he was born in Madras on **16 March 1901**.
**Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University** (Hyderabad) is also named after him.
His titles: **Amarajeevi** (Immortal Martyr) and "Andhra Martyra Martanda".

255.s: Which university bears the name of Potti Sriramulu?
255.x: Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University in Hyderabad is named after him.
255.tq: Distinguish the commemorative institution from other Andhra universities.
xs: **Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University**, Hyderabad, is named after him — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Andhra University** was set up in **1926** (first VC **C.R. Reddy**); **Sri Venkateswara University**, Tirupati, was founded in **1954**.
xa: Nellore was renamed **"Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore District"** in **2008**.
The **58-foot** bronze **"Statue of Sacrifice"** stands at **Sakhamuru Park, Amaravati**, unveiled on **16 March 2026**.
His death fast lasted **58 days** — **19 Oct** to **15 Dec 1952**.

255.s: Which of the following is a title associated with Potti Sriramulu?
255.x: Potti Sriramulu is known by the title Amarajeevi, meaning Immortal Martyr. He is also associated with the title “Andhra Martyra Martanda.”
255.tq: Test an exact honorific while using titles associated with other Andhra leaders as traps.
xs: Potti Sriramulu is known as **Amarajeevi** (Immortal Martyr) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Andhra Ratna** = **Duggirala Gopalakrishnaiah**; **Desoddharaka** = **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**; **Andhra Kesari** = **Tanguturi Prakasam**.
xa: His other title: **"Andhra Martyra Martanda"**.
He got the title after dying on the **58th day** of his fast, **15 December 1952**.
⚠ **Andhra Kesari** is also the name of **Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao's** paper (**1904**).
**Deshabhakta** = Konda Venkatappayya; **Swami Sitaram** = Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri.

255.s:
Consider the following statements about the 'Statue of Sacrifice' of Potti Sriramulu:
1. It is a 58-foot bronze statue at Sakhamuru Park, Amaravati.
2. It was unveiled by Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on 16 March 2026.
3. It was unveiled on Potti Sriramulu's 100th birth anniversary.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
255.x: Statement 1 is correct: 58-foot bronze statue at Sakhamuru Park, Amaravati. Statement 2 is correct: unveiled by CM Chandrababu Naidu on 16 March 2026. Statement 3 is wrong: 16 March 2026 was his 125th birth anniversary (born 16 March 1901). So '1 only' is incomplete, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include statement 3.
255.tq: 58 feet = 58-day fast; born 1901, so 2026 = 125th anniversary.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
**Statement 1 — correct:** a **58-foot** bronze statue at **Sakhamuru Park, Amaravati**.
**Statement 2 — correct:** unveiled by CM **Chandrababu Naidu** on **16 March 2026**.
**Statement 3 — wrong:** **16 March 2026** was his **125th** birth anniversary (born **16 March 1901**), not the 100th.
xa: Memorial park of **6.80 acres**, about **₹150 crore**; **26 t** bronze + **42 t** iron.
Built by the **Amarajeevi Potti Sriramulu Memorial Trust**; phase 2 adds a **museum, auditorium** and skill centre.
The 58-foot height echoes his **58-day** fast of **1952**.

255.s: Which of the following periodicals was associated with Nyapati Subba Rao?
255.x: Nyapati Subba Rao was associated with the monthly periodicals Vaijayanti and People's Magazine.
255.tq: Use nearby newspaper names as plausible distractors.
xs: **Nyapati Subba Rao** brought out the monthly **Vaijayanti** (and **People's Magazine**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Andhra Kesari** was founded by **Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao** (**1904**, Rajahmundry).
**Swarajya** (Vijayawada) was edited by **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao**; **Desamata** (Rajahmundry) by **Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham**.
xa: Nyapati Subba Rao (Rajahmundry) attended the **1885** INC session and was INC General Secretary.
He presided the **2nd Mahasabha, Vijayawada 1914**, and led the delegation to **Montagu** (**20 Dec 1917**).
**First president, Andhra Congress Committee (1918)**; titles **Rajabahadur** and **Padyavinoda**.

255.s:
Consider the following statements about Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao:
1. He founded Andhra Kesari in 1904 at Rajahmundry.
2. He wrote Andhrula Charitra.
3. He founded the Andhra Patrika.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao founded Andhra Kesari in 1904 and wrote Andhrula Charitra. Andhra Patrika was associated with Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.
255.tq: Find the wrong person linked with a newspaper.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
**Statement 1 — correct:** **Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao** founded **Andhra Kesari** in **1904**, Rajahmundry.
**Statement 2 — correct:** he wrote **Andhrula Charitra**.
**Statement 3 — wrong:** **Andhra Patrika** was founded by **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** (**9 Sep 1908**, Bombay).
xa: He founded the **Vijnana Chandrika Mandali** (**1906**) with **Komarraju Lakshmana Rao**.
He also founded the **Balabharati Samithi** (**Feb 1907**).
⚠ **Andhra Kesari** is also the title of **Tanguturi Prakasam**.

255.s: Who founded the Vijnana Chandrika Mandali in 1906 along with Komarraju Lakshmana Rao?
255.x: Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao founded the Vijnana Chandrika Mandali in 1906 with Komarraju Lakshmana Rao.
255.tq: Test a co-founder relationship.
xs: **Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao** founded the **Vijnana Chandrika Mandali** in **1906** with **Komarraju Lakshmana Rao** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Nyapati Subba Rao** ran **Vaijayanti**; **B.N. Sarma** presided **Bapatla 1913**; **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** founded **Andhra Patrika**.
xa: Veerabhadra Rao founded **Andhra Kesari** (**1904**, Rajahmundry) and wrote **Andhrula Charitra**.
He also founded the **Balabharati Samithi** (**Feb 1907**).

b. Nyapati Subba Rao
c. Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao
 d. B.N. Sarma

xs: **a–iii, b–iv, c–ii, d–i** — option **(1)** is correct.

255.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gokhale of South India — Mocherla Ramachandra Rao
255.x: Desoddharaka was the title of Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, not Pattabhi Sitaramayya.
255.tq: Use the known confusable title-person pair to find the mismatch.
xs: **Desoddharaka — Pattabhi Sitaramayya** is wrongly paired — so option **(2)** is the answer; **Desoddharaka** = **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**.
**Mocherla Ramachandra Rao** = **"Gokhale of South India"** (presided the 4th Mahasabha, **Kakinada 1916**) — correct.
**Andhra Ratna** = **Duggirala Gopalakrishnaiah**; **Deshabhakta** = **Konda Venkatappayya** — both correct.

**Andhra Kesari** = Tanguturi Prakasam; **Amarajeevi** = Potti Sriramulu.
**Rayalaseema Kuruvriddhudu / Pitamaha** = Kalluri Subbarao; **Jenda Narsayya** = Thota Narsayya Naidu.

255.s: The title ‘Rayalaseema Kuruvriddhudu’ or ‘Pitamaha’ is associated with:
255.x: Kalluri Subbarao was known as Rayalaseema Kuruvriddhudu or Pitamaha.
255.tq: Test regional honorifics directly.
xs: **Kalluri Subbarao** was called **Rayalaseema Kuruvriddhudu / Pitamaha** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri** = **Swami Sitaram**; **Jenda Narsayya** = **Thota Narsayya Naidu**; **Mocherla Ramachandra Rao** = "Gokhale of South India".
xa: Kalluri Subbarao led the **Salt Satyagraha in Bellary**.

255.s: Who was popularly known as Jenda Narsayya?
255.x: Thota Narsayya Naidu was popularly known as Jenda Narsayya.
255.tq: Match the exact title with the person rather than a similar leader.
xs: **Thota Narsayya Naidu** was known as **Jenda Narsayya** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Duggirala Gopalakrishnaiah** = **Andhra Ratna**; **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** = **Desoddharaka**; **Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri** = **Swami Sitaram**.
xa: **Deshabhakta** = Konda Venkatappayya; **Andhra Kesari** = Tanguturi Prakasam.
**Amarajeevi** = Potti Sriramulu; **Rayalaseema Kuruvriddhudu** = Kalluri Subbarao.

255.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Nyapati Subba Rao — Rajabahadur and Padyavinoda
255.x: Nyapati Subba Rao held the titles Rajabahadur and Padyavinoda. Andhra Ratna was Duggirala Gopalakrishnaiah, Desoddharaka was Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, and Amarajeevi was Potti Sriramulu.

xs: **Nyapati Subba Rao — Rajabahadur and Padyavinoda** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.

xa: Nyapati Subba Rao ran the monthlies **Vaijayanti** and **People's Magazine**.
He presided the **2nd Mahasabha, Vijayawada 1914**, where the province resolution was passed.
**First president, Andhra Congress Committee (1918)**; led the delegation to **Montagu** on **20 Dec 1917**.

255.s: On 6 February 1918, B. N. Sarma moved a resolution in the Imperial Legislative Council relating to which of the following?
255.x: B. N. Sarma moved the resolution for the creation of linguistic provinces in the Imperial Legislative Council on 6 February 1918.
255.tq: Use the date–mover–subject combination to identify the correct resolution.
xs: On **6 Feb 1918**, **B.N. Sarma** moved a resolution for **linguistic provinces** in the Imperial Legislative Council — so option **(3)** is correct.
Supported by **K.V. Rangaswami Ayyangar**; opposed by **Jinnah** and **V.S. Srinivasa Sastri**.

255.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
255.x: The Dhar Commission functioned during 1948. The JVP Committee belonged to 1948–49, the Visalandhra Mahasabha was formed in 1949 and the States Reorganisation Commission was appointed in December 1953.

255.tq: Test a leader's change of position rather than merely identifying his office.
xs: In **1954**, **B. Ramakrishna Rao** shifted to favour the **merger** of Telugu areas — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Kurnool Circular** was drafted by **Kala Venkatarao**, and the **Dhar Commission** was chaired by **Justice S.K. Dhar** — not by him.
xa: Burgula Ramakrishna Rao presided the **Nizam Andhra Mahasabha** session at **Devarakonda (1931)**.
The **Visalandhra Mahasabha** (for all Telugu areas) was formed in **1949**.
The **SRC** (Fazal Ali) was set up in **Dec 1953**.

255.s: The States Reorganisation Commission appointed in December 1953 is associated with which of the following persons?
255.x: The States Reorganisation Commission appointed in December 1953 is identified with Fazal Ali.
255.tq: Apply the person–institution association while avoiding similarly placed Andhra leaders.
xs: The **States Reorganisation Commission** (Dec 1953) is identified with **Fazal Ali** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Kala Venkatarao** drafted the **Kurnool Circular**; **Kadapa Koti Reddy** presided the **1937** Silver Jubilee session; **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** founded Andhra Patrika.
xa: SRC members: **H.N. Kunzru** and **K.M. Panikkar**; announced **22 Dec 1953**.
The SRC led to the **States Reorganisation Act 1956**.

255.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Dhar Commission was followed by the JVP Committee.
2. The Madras Partition Committee functioned during 1949–50.
3. The Wanchoo inquiry was conducted during February–March 1953.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: All three statements are correct. The sequence included the Dhar Commission and JVP Committee, the Madras Partition Committee in 1949–50 and the Wanchoo inquiry in early 1953.
255.tq: Check the dates of successive commissions and inquiries rather than relying only on their names.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Statement 1 — correct:** **Dar Commission** (Jun-Dec **1948**) was followed by the **JVP Committee** (Dec 1948, report April 1949).
**Statement 2 — correct:** the Madras **Partition Committee** worked **Dec 1949-Jan 1950**, reporting on **4 Jan 1950**.
**Statement 3 — correct:** the **Wanchoo** inquiry ran **Feb-Mar 1953** (appointed **7 Feb 1953**, report **25 Mar 1953**).
xa: Partition Committee chairman: **Kumaraswamy Raja**, Madras CM (APPSC G2 2025 key).
**Justice K.N. Wanchoo** (Chief Justice, Rajasthan HC) was a **single-member** committee.
⚠ **Dar** = appointed by the **Constituent Assembly**; **JVP** = appointed by **Congress**.

255.s: Which one of the following distinguishes the Andhra Mahasabha of the Madras Presidency from the Nizam Andhra Mahasabha?
o: The former began at Bapatla in 1913, whereas the latter began at Jogipet in 1930.
The former began at Jogipet in 1930, whereas the latter began at Bapatla in 1913.
Both began at Bapatla in 1913 and had the same first president.
Both began at Jogipet in 1930 but pursued different educational aims.
255.x: The Madras Presidency organisation began at Bapatla in 1913 under B.N. Sarma, while the Nizam Andhra Mahasabha began at Jogipet in 1930 under Suravaram Pratapa Reddy.
