255.tq: Split the comparison by date, venue and first president.
xs: The **Andhra Mahasabha** began at **Bapatla in 1913**; the **Nizam Andhra Mahasabha** at **Jogipet (Medak) in 1930** — so option **(1)** is correct.
First presidents differ: **B.N. Sarma** (Bapatla) vs **Suravaram Pratapa Reddy** (Jogipet).
Aims differed: a **separate Andhra province** vs **Telugu culture, education and reform** under the Nizam.
xa: Nizam Andhra Mahasabha later sessions: **1931 Devarakonda** (Burgula Ramakrishna Rao), **1934 Khammam**, **1935 Siricilla** (Madapati Hanumantha Rao).
Andhra Mahasabha later sessions: **Vijayawada**, **Visakhapatnam**, **Kakinada**, **Nellore**.
The Nizam body's sessions also held women's conferences (**Andhra Mahila Sabha**).

255.s: The Visalandhra Mahasabha, formed in 1949, was intended to represent the demand for a state comprising:
o: The Telugu and Tamil-speaking areas jointly
255.x: The Visalandhra Mahasabha was formed to advocate the integration of all Telugu-speaking areas.
255.tq: Distinguish the geographical scope of an organisation from the narrower regional demands.
xs: The **Visalandhra Mahasabha** (**1949**) stood for a state of **all Telugu-speaking areas** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was formed after the **Dar Commission** and **JVP Committee** (**1948**).
xa: In the APPSC G2 2025 order: **Dhar → Visalandhra Mahasabha → Sitaram's fast → SRC**.
The Andhra State of **1 Oct 1953** had only **11** districts (7 coastal + 4 Rayalaseema) — not all Telugu areas.
**B. Ramakrishna Rao** shifted to favour merger in **1954**.

255.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Swami Sitaram's fast for Andhra State
B. Dhar Commission
C. States Reorganisation Commission
D. Formation of the Visalandhra Mahasabha
255.x: The Dhar Commission came in 1948 (B), the Visalandhra Mahasabha was formed in 1949 (D), Swami Sitaram fasted in August-September 1951 (A), and the SRC was set up in December 1953 (C). This is the order keyed in APPSC G2 2025; the other options misplace Visalandhra or the SRC.
255.tq: Dhar 1948 - Visalandhra 1949 - Sitaram 1951 - SRC 1953.
xs: The order is **B, D, A, C** — option **(1)** is correct (APPSC G2 2025 key).
**B:** **Dhar Commission**, Jun-Dec **1948**. **D:** **Visalandhra Mahasabha**, **1949**.
**A:** **Swami Sitaram's** fast, **15 Aug-20 Sep 1951**. **C:** **SRC** (Fazal Ali), **Dec 1953**.
xa: Swami Sitaram (**Gollapudi Sitarama Sastry**) fasted **35 days**; ended on the appeal of **Vinoba Bhave**.
⚠ **Swami Sitaram** = **35 days** (1951); **Potti Sriramulu** = **58 days** (1952, died).
Between them: the Madras **Partition Committee** (Dec 1949-Jan 1950) and the **Wanchoo** inquiry (Feb-Mar 1953).

255.s: The formation of Andhra State in 1953 is historically significant because it was regarded as the:
o: first state created by merging all Telugu-speaking regions
first linguistic state formed after Independence
first state formed exclusively on a religious basis
first state formed under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956
255.x: Andhra State was the first state formed on a linguistic basis after Independence and became the precedent for wider reorganisation.
255.tq: Distinguish the first linguistic state after Independence from the later nationwide reorganisation of 1956.
xs: Andhra State (**1 October 1953**) was the **first linguistic state** formed after Independence — so option **(2)** is correct.
It did **not** include all Telugu areas — **Madras city** was excluded and Telangana joined only in **1956**.
It was formed before, not under, the **States Reorganisation Act 1956**.
xa: Carved out of **Madras State**; capital **Kurnool**, inaugurated by **Nehru**.
**11 districts**: 7 Coastal Andhra + 4 Rayalaseema.
It opened the way to the **SRC** (Fazal Ali, announced **22 Dec 1953**).

255.s: The formation of Andhra State in 1953 is commonly described as the “Andhra exception” because it:
o: allowed Madras to become the capital of a separate Andhra State
created a state without any elected legislature
reversed the decision to use language as a basis for state formation
opened the way for the States Reorganisation Commission and nationwide linguistic reorganisation
255.x: Although the Dhar Commission and JVP Committee were cautious about linguistic states, the Andhra exception paved the way for the SRC and broader linguistic reorganisation.
255.tq: Identify the historical consequence rather than merely recalling the event itself.
xs: The "**Andhra exception**" opened the way to the **SRC** and nationwide **linguistic reorganisation** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Dhar** and **JVP** both rejected language as a basis, yet JVP's Andhra exception (**minus Madras**) became the formula used in **1953**.
So it did not hand Madras to Andhra, nor reverse the linguistic principle.
xa: **Potti Sriramulu's death** forced the Centre's hand → Andhra → **SRC (Dec 1953)** → **States Reorganisation Act 1956**.
JVP's report (**April 1949**): Andhra could be formed **if Andhras gave up Madras city**.
SRC members: **Fazl Ali**, **Kunzru**, **Panikkar**.

255.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the sequence of bodies and commissions associated with linguistic reorganisation?
o: JVP Committee → Dhar Commission → Wanchoo Committee → Fazal Ali Commission
Dhar Commission → JVP Committee → Wanchoo Committee → Fazal Ali States Reorganisation Commission
Wanchoo Committee → Dhar Commission → JVP Committee → Fazal Ali Commission
Dhar Commission → Wanchoo Committee → JVP Committee → Fazal Ali Commission
255.x: The sequence was Dhar Commission in 1948, JVP Committee in 1948–49, Wanchoo in 1953 for Andhra, and the Fazal Ali SRC in 1953–55 for all India.
255.tq: Fix the earliest commission first and then place the Andhra-specific and all-India bodies.
xs: The sequence is **Dhar → JVP → Wanchoo → Fazal Ali SRC** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Dhar Commission** (**1948**, CA-appointed) → **JVP** (**1948-49**, Congress).
**Wanchoo** (**1953**, Andhra only) → **Fazal Ali SRC** (**1953-55**, all India).
xa: SRC members: **H.N. Kunzru** and **K.M. Panikkar**.
**Justice K.N. Wanchoo** was appointed on **7 Feb 1953**; report dated **25 Mar 1953**.
⚠ **Dar** = appointed by the **Constituent Assembly**; **JVP** = by **Congress** at **Jaipur**.

255.s: The States Reorganisation Commission announced on 22 December 1953 was associated with which combination?
o: Fazal Ali, H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar
K.N. Wanchoo, H.N. Kunzru and Pattabhi Sitaramayya
Fazal Ali, Neelam Sanjiva Reddy and K.M. Panikkar
P.S. Kumaraswami Raja, Fazal Ali and H.N. Kunzru
255.x: The SRC was headed by Fazal Ali, with H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar as members.
255.tq: Start with the sure chairman-member combination and eliminate bodies connected with Andhra alone.
xs: The SRC (announced **22 Dec 1953**) = **Fazal Ali**, **H.N. Kunzru** and **K.M. Panikkar** — option **(1)** is correct.
**K.N. Wanchoo** led the **1953** single-member Andhra inquiry; **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** was on the **JVP** Committee.
**P.S. Kumaraswami Raja** chaired the Madras **Partition Committee**; **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** was not on the SRC.
xa: The SRC led to the **States Reorganisation Act 1956**.
Its path was opened by the formation of **Andhra State** on **1 Oct 1953**.
⚠ **N. Sanjiva Reddy was not a member** of the JVP Committee either (APPSC 2021).

255.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Andhra movement during 1913–1920 is correct?
o: It began only after the formation of Andhra State in 1953.
It opposed the use of Telugu in education and administration.
It combined demands for an Andhra State, Andhra University, development of Telugu and cultural revival.
It was confined exclusively to the demand for a separate province.
255.x: The period 1913–1920 was the propaganda phase, with four broad objectives: Andhra State, Andhra University, Telugu development and cultural revival.
255.tq: Prefer the option that captures the full set of objectives rather than an exclusive single-purpose claim.
xs: The **1913-20** propaganda phase combined **Andhra State**, **Andhra University**, development of **Telugu** and **cultural revival** — option **(3)** is correct.
It began long before **1953** (Bapatla **1913**), and it **promoted** Telugu — e.g. **Telugu medium** in secondary schools (**1915**).
It was not only about a province — the **first** session (Bapatla) also demanded a **separate university**.
xa: **Bapatla (1913)** "sowed the seeds" of the movement — the first organised Telugu platform.
Bapatla agenda: an English newspaper, lifting the **ban on Telugu entry into the Army**, a fund for technical training abroad.
The **1914 Vijayawada** session passed the province resolution.

255.s: The annual resolutions and memorandums of the Andhra movement were important mainly because they:
o: transferred the Andhra capital permanently to Hyderabad
replaced the demand for linguistic states with a demand for religious provinces
ended the demand for a separate Andhra province after 1913
kept the Andhra issue on the national agenda until the formation of Andhra State in 1953
255.x: Repeated resolutions and memorandums ensured that the Andhra problem remained before national political authorities until Andhra State was formed in 1953.
255.tq: Choose the option expressing the cumulative political effect of repeated resolutions.
xs: The annual resolutions and memorandums kept the "**Andhra problem**" on the national agenda until **1953** — option **(4)** is correct.
The capital went to **Kurnool (1953)**, then **Hyderabad (1956)**; the demand was for **linguistic** provinces, never religious ones.
xa: Examples: **B.N. Sarma's** Imperial Council resolution (**6 Feb 1918**); **Mocherla Ramachandra Rao's** London memorandum (**Dec 1918**).
Council of State bids in **1925**, **1926** and **1927** (Ramadasu Pantulu) all failed.
**1931**: the Andhra resolution was handed to **Gandhi** for the **2nd RTC**.

255.s: The district-wise voting adopted at the fifth Andhra Mahasabha session was primarily a response to criticism that the organisation was:
o: controlled by Tamil settlers in Madras
opposed to the use of Telugu in public life
dominated by Circars and Brahmin interests
255.x: Rayalaseema and Nellore leaders criticised the Andhra Mahasabha as a Circars- or Brahmin-led body; district-wise voting was adopted in response.
255.tq: Match the institutional change with the specific regional criticism that caused it.
xs: Rayalaseema and Nellore leaders saw the Mahasabha as **Circars/Brahmin-led**; **district-wise voting** (**1917**) answered this — option **(4)** is correct.
At Nellore (**1917**), of **740** delegates **480** were from Nellore → **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** proposed one vote per district.
xa: The **5th session (Nellore, 1917)** was presided by **Konda Venkatappayya**; it rejected the demand to include **Madras city**.
The **Mahanandi** meeting (**April 1913**, Guthi Kesava Pillai) had called the movement a **"Brahmin movement"**.
Leadership splits — **Circars vs Rayalaseema**, **Prakasam vs Pattabhi** — repeatedly slowed the movement.

255.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the early milestones of the Andhra movement?
o: Bapatla 1912—first formal resolution; Nidadavolu 1913—first numbered conference; Vijayawada 1914—first Congress session
Nidadavolu 1912—first Andhra Mahasabha; Bapatla 1913—first Congress circle; Vijayawada 1914—first university session
Vijayawada 1912—first formal resolution; Bapatla 1913—first linguistic PCC; Nidadavolu 1914—first Andhra Mahasabha
Nidadavolu 1912—first formal resolution; Bapatla 1913—first numbered Andhra Conference; Vijayawada 1914—first session called Andhra Mahasabha
255.x: Nidadavolu in 1912 saw the first formal resolution, Bapatla in 1913 was the first numbered Andhra Conference, and Vijayawada in 1914 was the first session called Andhra Mahasabha.
255.tq: Keep the three places and years aligned before comparing the labels attached to them.
xs: **Nidadavolu 1912** = first formal resolution; **Bapatla 1913** = first numbered Andhra Conference; **Vijayawada 1914** = first session called **Andhra Mahasabha** — option **(4)**.
The other options jumble the places and years; Bapatla was **1913**, not 1912.
xa: **Nidadavolu (1912)** was a joint conference of **Guntur, Krishna, Godavari**; resolution moved by **Jonnavittula Gurunatham**.
**Bapatla** president: **B.N. Sarma**; **Vijayawada 1914** president: **Nyapati Subba Rao** (province resolution passed).
The Youngmen's Literary Association, **Guntur (1903)**, was the cradle of the movement.

255.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First Andhra INC president — Nyapati Subba Rao, 1918
First Andhra Congress Committee president — Anandacharlu, 1891
First Andhra Congress Committee president — Tanguturi Prakasam, 1953
255.x: Anandacharlu was the first Andhra INC president in 1891, whereas Nyapati Subba Rao was the first president of the Andhra Congress Committee in 1918.
255.tq: Test the two similar leadership titles separately rather than treating them as identical offices.
xs: **P. Anandacharlu** (Chittoor) was the first Andhra to preside over the INC — **7th session, Nagpur, 1891** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Nyapati Subba Rao** (**1918**) was the first president of the **Andhra Congress Committee**, not of the INC.
**Tanguturi Prakasam** was the first **CM** of Andhra State (**1953**).
xa: Anandacharlu was earlier Secretary of the **Madras Mahajana Sabha** (**1884**).
⚠ APPSC G2 2011 key named **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** as "first Telugu person" to preside — he presided **Jaipur, 1948**.
**N. Sanjiva Reddy** was INC president **1960-62**.

255.s: Which of the following best explains why the Andhra movement was repeatedly slowed before 1953?
o: The immediate acceptance of the Andhra demand by the Central Government
Leadership and regional splits, including Circars–Rayalaseema and Prakasam–Pattabhi divisions
The unanimous opposition of all Telugu-speaking districts to a separate state
The absence of any demand for linguistic organisation within Congress
255.x: Factional divisions between regions and leaders, notably Circars versus Rayalaseema and Prakasam versus Pattabhi, repeatedly weakened the movement.
255.tq: Identify the internal political cause rather than an absolute or externally imposed explanation.
xs: Leadership and regional splits — **Circars vs Rayalaseema**, **Prakasam vs Pattabhi** — repeatedly slowed the movement — option **(2)** is correct.
The Centre was **cautious**, not accepting: **Dhar** and **JVP** both rejected language as a basis.
Congress had promised linguistic PCCs since **1920**, and Telugu districts were divided, not unanimous.
xa: Delay was blamed on Centre caution after **Partition** + Andhra factionalism.
**April 1951**: **N. Sanjiva Reddy** beat **N.G. Ranga** for APCC by **5** votes → Prakasam and Ranga left to form the **Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party**.
The university seat/jurisdiction row left lasting **Rayalaseema** resentment → the **Sri Bagh Pact**.

255.s: The provisions of the Sri Bagh Pact continue to be cited particularly in contemporary debates concerning:
o: the status of the Telugu language in the Union List
the creation of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council
the merger of Andhra with Maharashtra
Rayalaseema’s capital, High Court and irrigation concerns
255.x: The Sri Bagh terms concerning capital, High Court and irrigation remain important in Rayalaseema-related debates.
255.tq: Group the three linked provisions under the region whose interests they addressed.
xs: The **Sri Bagh** terms on **capital, High Court and irrigation** are still cited in Rayalaseema debates — option **(4)** is correct.
The pact (**16 Nov 1937**) put **Capital and High Court in separate regions**, Rayalaseema choosing first.
xa: Irrigation clause: **priority to Rayalaseema** in Krishna, Tungabhadra and Pennar waters for **10 years**.
University clause: AU centres at **Waltair and Anantapur**.
Signed at **'Sri Bagh', Madras**, the house of **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**.
⚠ **Sri Bagh** = **1937**, Coastal-Rayalaseema; **Gentlemen's Agreement** = **1956**, Andhra-Telangana.

255.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Andhra University is correct?
o: Its university struggle contributed to the growth of a distinct Telugu intellectual identity.
Its location had no connection with regional political concerns.
It was established only after the formation of Andhra State in 1953.
It was intended exclusively for technical education in Rayalaseema.
255.x: The struggle over Andhra University helped build a distinct Telugu intellectual identity and is regarded by many as a forerunner of the Andhra State movement.
255.tq: Recognise the broader cultural significance of an institutional demand.
xs: The **university fight** built a distinct **Telugu intellectual identity** and is seen as a forerunner of Andhra State — option **(1)** is correct.
Its seat was deeply political: the location dispute deepened the **Circars-Rayalaseema** rift.
It was established in **1926** (not after 1953), as a general university for Telugu people.
xa: Andhra University Act passed under the **Justice Party** government; established **26 April 1926**, HQ **Vijayawada**.
Seat shifted to **Visakhapatnam** (Dec **1928**) after **C.R. Reddy's** report; inaugurated at Waltair on **5 Sept 1930**.
First VC: **C.R. Reddy** (1926-1931); **S. Radhakrishnan**, 1931-1936.

255.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with present-day higher education in Rayalaseema?
o: Central University of Andhra Pradesh — Anantapur
Yogi Vemana University — Kurnool, established in 1953
Central University of Andhra Pradesh — Kadapa, established in 1926
Yogi Vemana University — Amaravati, established after the 2014 Act
255.x: The Central University of Andhra Pradesh is located at Anantapur and was set up after the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014. Yogi Vemana University is at Kadapa and was established in 2006.
255.tq: Check both the location and the institutional history before accepting a match.
xs: The **Central University of AP** is at **Anantapur** — option **(1)** is correct.
It came after the **AP Reorganisation Act 2014**; campus funds were released in **Mar 2026**.
**Yogi Vemana University** is at **Kadapa** (**2006**), not Kurnool or Amaravati.
xa: **Sri Venkateswara University**, Tirupati (**1954**) answered an old Rayalaseema grievance.
The **1st Rayalaseema Mahasabha** (**1934**) demanded a separate university at **Tirupati**.
Sri Bagh (**1937**) promised an AU centre at **Anantapur**.

255.s: Which one of the following correctly states the significance of Kurnool becoming the capital of Andhra State in 1953?
o: It was selected after Andhra retained Madras city.
It was selected as the capital of the entire Madras State.
It became the capital because the new state, having lost Madras, had to use the relatively undeveloped town of Kurnool.
It was chosen as the permanent capital under the 1956 States Reorganisation Act.
255.x: The loss of Madras left the new Andhra State administratively and economically weak, requiring it to use the relatively undeveloped town of Kurnool as its capital.
255.tq: Link the capital choice to the political and economic consequence of losing Madras.
xs: Having lost **Madras**, the new state was "administratively and economically orphaned" and had to use undeveloped **Kurnool** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Madras city was excluded** from Andhra; Kurnool was only a **temporary** capital, not chosen under the **1956** Act.
xa: Madras Assembly vote: **Kurnool 79** vs **Vijayawada 53**, helped by **five non-Andhra votes**.
Kurnool suited the **Sreebagh Pact**: capital in Rayalaseema, High Court at **Guntur**.
Capital path: **Kurnool (1953) → Hyderabad (1956) → Amaravati**.

255.s: The AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 is associated with which provision?
o: Abolition of the statutory concept of a state capital
Affirmation of Amaravati’s permanent statutory position as the capital
Transfer of Andhra Pradesh’s capital to Hyderabad
Recognition of Kurnool as the permanent capital of Andhra Pradesh
255.x: The AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 affirms Amaravati’s permanent statutory position as the capital of Andhra Pradesh.
255.tq: Use the exact statutory effect instead of confusing historical and current capitals.
xs: The **AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026** affirms **Amaravati's** permanent statutory position as capital — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kurnool** was the temporary capital of Andhra State (**1953**) and **Hyderabad** came in **1956**.
xa: The **58-foot** "Statue of Sacrifice" of Potti Sriramulu stands at **Sakhamuru Park, Amaravati**.
Deputy CM **Pawan Kalyan**: A.P. still grapples with its capital question.
The **Central University of AP** at **Anantapur** followed the **AP Reorganisation Act 2014**.

255.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the reported present performance of the Telugu Ganga project?
o: It has been abandoned because Rayalaseema has no irrigation grievance.
It supplies irrigation only to coastal Andhra and no water to Chennai.
It can barely irrigate about 20,000 acres despite the larger intended command area.
It irrigates nearly 2.75 lakh acres as originally intended.
255.x: The project was intended for 2.75 lakh acres and Chennai water supply, but it was reported to be barely irrigating 20,000 acres.
255.tq: Compare the intended figure with the reported actual performance.
xs: **Telugu Ganga** barely irrigates about **20,000** acres — option **(3)** is correct.
It was meant for **2.75 lakh acres** plus **Chennai** water — so options 2 and 4 are wrong.
xa: It is a live **Rayalaseema irrigation grievance**.
Sri Bagh (**1937**) gave Rayalaseema **priority** in Krishna, Tungabhadra and Pennar waters for **10 years**.
The **1937 Silver Jubilee** session demanded safeguards in **Cabinet, Irrigation and Capital**.

255.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the 2026 Andhra University centenary observance is correct?
o: The centenary commemorates the period 1926–2026 and was associated with an announcement of ₹500 crore support.
The centenary marked 1913–2026 and announced ₹150 crore for a Potti Sriramulu memorial.
The university was founded in 1953 and the centenary was celebrated at Kurnool.
The centenary programme excluded any proposal for international ranking improvement.
255.x: Andhra University’s centenary covers 1926–2026, and the State announced ₹500 crore to help it enter the global top 100.
255.tq: Match the centenary period with the correct funding and institutional objective.
xs: AU's centenary covers **1926-2026**, and CM Naidu announced **Rs 500 crore** — option **(1)** is correct.
The money aims to push AU into the global **top 100**, so option 4 is wrong.
**₹150 crore** relates to the Potti Sriramulu memorial; AU was founded in **1926**, not 1953.
xa: Theme **"Century of Excellence"** (**27 Apr 2026**); chief guest Vice-President **C.P. Radhakrishnan**.
Governor **S. Abdul Nazeer** credited founding VC **Cattamanchi Ramalinga Reddy**.
AU was established on **26 April 1926**; HQ first at **Vijayawada**.

255.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: N. Venkatramayya — first Speaker of Andhra State
C.M. Trivedi — first Governor of Andhra State
Sanjiva Reddy — first Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra State
Cattamanchi Ramalinga Reddy — first Governor of Andhra State
255.x: Cattamanchi Ramalinga Reddy was the founding Vice-Chancellor of Andhra University, not the first Governor of Andhra State. C.M. Trivedi held the latter position.
255.tq: Find the swapped office-holder in the otherwise familiar set of pairings.
xs: **Cattamanchi Ramalinga Reddy** was AU's founding **VC**, not first Governor — so option **(4)** is the wrong pair.
First Governor: **C.M. Trivedi**; first Speaker: **N. Venkatramayya**; first Deputy CM: **Sanjiva Reddy** — all correct.
xa: C.R. Reddy was VC **1926-1931** and again **1936-1949**; he drafted the AU bill.
C.R. Reddy coined **"City of Destiny"** for Visakhapatnam.
First CM: **Prakasam**; Trivedi was earlier the Centre's **Special Officer** for setting up the state.

256.s:
Consider the following statements about the Wanchoo Committee:
1. It was a single-member committee headed by Justice Kailas Nath Wanchoo, Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court.
2. It was appointed on 7 February 1953.
3. It submitted its report on 25 March 1953.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
256.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Wanchoo, Chief Justice of the Rajasthan HC, was the single member, appointed 7 Feb 1953. Statement 3 is wrong: the report came on 23 March 1953; 25 March 1953 was Nehru's announcement. So 'all three' (D) and options leaving out statement 2 (A) or including 3 (C) are wrong.
256.tq: 23 March = report; 25 March = Nehru's announcement. Single member, Rajasthan HC.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
**Statement 1 — correct:** a **single-member** committee — **Justice Kailas Nath Wanchoo**, **Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court**.
**Statement 2 — correct:** appointed on **7 Feb 1953**.
**Statement 3 — wrong:** the report came on **23 March 1953**; **25 March 1953** was Nehru's announcement.
xa: Mandate: **boundary division**, **financial settlement**, **asset distribution**, administrative arrangements.
Trigger: Nehru's **19 Dec 1952** statement after **Potti Sriramulu's** death.
⚠ His recommendation to work from **Madras** for **3-5 years** was **not** accepted.

256.s: Which one of the following was NOT included in the terms of reference of the Wanchoo Committee?
o: Determination of the permanent capital of India
256.x: The committee dealt with boundary division, financial settlement, asset distribution and administrative arrangements. Determining the permanent capital of India was not within its mandate.
256.tq: Find the unrelated item among subjects belonging to the committee’s actual mandate.
xs: Fixing the **permanent capital of India** was not Wanchoo's job — so option **(1)** is the answer.
Its mandate: **boundary division**, **financial settlement**, **asset distribution** and administrative arrangements.
xa: Wanchoo = **single member**, **Chief Justice, Rajasthan High Court**; appointed **7 Feb 1953**.
On the capital, it only suggested Andhra work temporarily from **Madras city for 3-5 years** — rejected by Nehru.
The earlier **Partition Committee** (**1949-50**, **Kumaraswamy Raja**) had first been asked to work out the asset split.

256.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Nehru’s statement following the death of Potti Sriramulu
B. Appointment of the Wanchoo Committee
C. Submission of the Wanchoo Committee report
D. Nehru’s announcement on the capital of Andhra State
256.x: The sequence was 19 December 1952, 7 February 1953, 23 March 1953 and 25 March 1953.
256.tq: Use the first and last dates to place the intermediate committee events correctly.
xs: The order is **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)** is correct.
**A:** Nehru's statement after Sriramulu's death — **19 Dec 1952**. **B:** Wanchoo appointed — **7 Feb 1953**.
**C:** Wanchoo report — **23 March 1953**. **D:** Nehru's capital announcement — **25 March 1953**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes give **25 March** as the report date — that was really Nehru's announcement.
The **25 March** announcement: capital inside Andhra, temporary capital to be decided **before 1 July 1953**.
Result: **Kurnool** became the temporary capital.

256.s: What temporary arrangement for the Andhra Government was recommended by the Wanchoo Committee?
o: It should function from Kurnool permanently.
It should function from Madras city for three to five years.
It should function from Guntur for ten years.
It should function from Bellary until 1956.
256.x: Because Andhra lacked capital infrastructure, Wanchoo recommended that the Andhra Government work temporarily from Madras city for three to five years.
256.tq: Test the recommendation through its duration and location, both of which are vulnerable to reversal.
xs: Wanchoo recommended the Andhra government work temporarily from **Madras city for 3-5 years** — option **(2)** is correct.
Reason: the new state **lacked capital infrastructure**.
**Kurnool** became only a **temporary** capital, and **Guntur** got the **High Court** (**1954**) — not the seat of government.
xa: The Centre **did not accept** this: Nehru (**25 March 1953**) ruled out Madras as capital.
⚠ **Wanchoo** = Madras for **3-5 years**; **Nehru** = capital inside Andhra → **Kurnool**.
The Andhra **PCC** had wanted **half of Madras town**.

256.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Nehru’s announcement of 25 March 1953:
1. Madras was ruled out as the capital of Andhra State.
2. The capital had to be located within Andhra.
3. A temporary capital was to be decided before 1 July 1953.
4. Some offices could continue in Madras for a period.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
256.x: All four statements correctly describe Nehru’s 25 March 1953 decision. It rejected Madras as the capital while permitting a temporary arrangement and limited continuation of offices in Madras.
256.tq: Check each administrative condition separately before selecting the complete combination.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Statements 1, 2 — correct:** "no question" of **Madras** as capital; the capital must be **inside Andhra**.
**Statement 3 — correct:** a **temporary** capital to be decided **before 1 July 1953**.
**Statement 4 — correct:** some offices could stay in **Madras** for a while.
xa: Outcome: **Kurnool** = temporary capital.
The Assembly was formed from members elected to the Madras Assembly in **1952**; **no Legislative Council**.
Nehru also said **Bellary** district court would serve **Adoni, Alur and Rayadurg** for the time being.

256.s: Who served as the Special Officer for the initial administrative arrangements of Andhra State?
256.x: C. M. Trivedi served as the Special Officer. Neelam Sanjiva Reddy and Tenneti Viswanatham were members of his advisory committee.
256.tq: Distinguish the principal office-holder from members of the advisory committee.
xs: **C.M. Trivedi** was the **Special Officer** for setting up Andhra State — so option **(3) M. Trivedi** is correct.
**Justice Kailas Nath Wanchoo** headed the single-member **Wanchoo Committee** (**1953**), not the special office.
xa: Wanchoo was **Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court**; **Justice Mishra** (Hyderabad HC) held the **Bellary** inquiry.
The **Partition Committee** (**1949-50**) was chaired by **Kumaraswamy Raja**.

256.s: Which of the following correctly compares the positions taken on Madras city?
o: Wanchoo recommended Madras as the permanent capital, whereas Nehru accepted the recommendation unchanged.
Nehru accepted Madras as the permanent capital, whereas the Andhra PCC wanted Kurnool.
The JVP Committee supported Andhra’s claim without conditions, while Wanchoo rejected any temporary arrangement.
The Andhra PCC wanted half of Madras town, whereas Wanchoo recommended Madras as a temporary headquarters for three to five years.
256.x: The Andhra PCC demanded half of Madras town, while Wanchoo recommended Madras as the temporary headquarters for three to five years. Nehru later rejected Madras as the capital.
256.tq: Compare recommendations across bodies and distinguish a temporary headquarters from a permanent capital.
xs: The **Andhra PCC** wanted **half of Madras town**; **Wanchoo** suggested Madras as temporary HQ for **3-5 years** — option **(4)** is correct.
Wanchoo never proposed Madras as the **permanent** capital, and **Nehru** rejected even the temporary idea (**25 Mar 1953**).
The **JVP Committee** was conditional: Andhra only if Telugus gave up **Madras**.
xa: Nehru: capital must be **inside Andhra** → **Kurnool**.
JVP's report date: **April 1949**.

256.s: The JVP Committee’s position in April 1949 regarding Andhra and Madras was that:
o: Madras should be divided equally between Andhra and Mysore.
Andhra could be formed only if the Telugus gave up their claim to Madras.
Andhra should receive half of Madras town.
Madras should become the temporary capital of Andhra for five years.
256.x: The JVP Committee held that Andhra could be formed only if the Telugus relinquished their claim to Madras.
256.tq: Identify the conditional recommendation rather than confusing it with the Andhra PCC or Wanchoo position.
xs: JVP (**April 1949**): Andhra only if the Telugus **gave up their claim to Madras** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Half of Madras town** was the **Andhra PCC's** demand; Madras as temporary HQ (**3-5 years**) was **Wanchoo's** idea.
xa: Nehru (**25 Mar 1953**) rejected Madras as capital → **Kurnool**.
Stand sequence on Madras: **JVP (1949)** → **Wanchoo (1953)** → **Nehru (25 Mar 1953)**.

256.s: Which description best reflects the financial and administrative position of the newly formed Andhra State?
o: It had no need for an asset division with residual Madras.
It possessed a developed capital and a major commercial centre.
It was administratively and economically orphaned, lacking a developed capital and commercial centre.
It had inherited the entire financial surplus of residual Madras.
256.x: The new state lacked both developed capital infrastructure and a commercial centre and was described as administratively and economically orphaned.
256.tq: Choose the precise combined description rather than an exaggerated or reversed financial claim.
xs: Without a capital or commercial centre, Andhra was "**administratively and economically orphaned**" — option **(3)** is correct.
It **did** need an asset division: assets and administration were split between **Andhra** and **residual Madras**.
xa: For lack of capital infrastructure, Wanchoo proposed **Madras city for 3-5 years**; Nehru chose a capital inside Andhra (**Kurnool**).
The **Partition Committee** (**1949-50**) first worked on the asset split.
⚠ Compare **2014**: assets split by **location**, debts by **population** → AP carried a heavy debt share.

256.s: Which body had first been asked during 1949–50 to work out the division of assets between Andhra and residual Madras?
256.x: The Partition Committee of 1949–50 was first entrusted with working out the division of assets between Andhra and residual Madras.
256.tq: Identify the correct body by matching it with the function assigned to it.
xs: The **Partition Committee** (**1949-50**) was first asked to work out the **asset split** — option **(4)** is correct.
The **Wanchoo Committee** came later (**1953**); the **Tungabhadra Board** came under the **Andhra State Act 1953**.
The **JVP Committee** (**April 1949**) dealt with whether Andhra could be formed, not the asset split.
xa: Chairman: **Kumaraswamy Raja**.
It also covered "**administrative arrangements**" for the new state.
Wanchoo's mandate: **boundary division**, **financial settlement**, **asset distribution**.

256.s: The Partition Committee associated with administrative arrangements for the new Andhra State was chaired by:
256.x: The Partition Committee of 1949–50, associated with administrative arrangements for the new state, was chaired by Kumaraswamy Raja.
256.tq: Match the committee with its chairman while avoiding substitution by a later committee head.
xs: The **Partition Committee** (**1949-50**) was chaired by **Kumaraswamy Raja** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Justice Wanchoo** headed the **1953** single-member committee; **C.M. Trivedi** was the **Special Officer**.
xa: The Partition Committee first worked out the **asset split** and **administrative arrangements**.
Wanchoo (appointed **7 Feb 1953**) later took up **financial settlement** and **asset distribution**.

256.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the High Court arrangements after the formation of Andhra State:
1. The Madras High Court retained jurisdiction until the site of the Andhra High Court was decided.
2. The Andhra High Court was established in 1954.
3. The Andhra High Court was established at Guntur.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
256.x: All three statements are correct. The Madras High Court continued jurisdiction temporarily, and the Andhra High Court was established at Guntur in 1954.
256.tq: Separate the interim jurisdiction of the old court from the establishment details of the new court.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Statement 1 — correct:** the **Madras High Court** kept jurisdiction until the Andhra HC site was decided.
**Statements 2, 3 — correct:** the Andhra High Court was set up at **Guntur** in **1954**.
xa: **Bellary district court** was to serve **Adoni, Alur and Rayadurg** for the time being (Nehru, **25 Mar 1953**).
Capital: **Kurnool** (temporary); High Court: **Guntur**.

256.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
256.x: Rayadurg taluk went to Andhra and was included in Anantapur district. Adoni and Alur went to Kurnool district, while Bellary, Hospet and the other listed areas went to Mysore.
256.tq: Start with the sure district allocation and reject options that reverse the territorial division.
xs: **Rayadurg taluk → Andhra (Anantapur district)** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**Bellary taluk** went to **Mysore** (Justice Mishra's report), not Kurnool.
**Hospet** went to **Mysore**; **Adoni** went to **Andhra (Kurnool district)**.
xa: **Adoni and Alur** → **Kurnool** district.
**Siruguppa, Hospet, Sandur, Harpanahalli, Hadagali** → **Mysore**.
After the split, **Tungabhadra** works were shared between **Andhra** and **Mysore**.

256.s: The decision to assign Bellary taluk to Mysore was based on the report of:
o: Kumaraswamy Raja, Chairman of the Partition Committee
M. Trivedi, Special Officer of Andhra State
Justice Mishra, Chief Justice of the Hyderabad High Court
Justice Wanchoo, Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court
256.x: Bellary taluk was assigned to Mysore on the basis of Justice Mishra’s report. Justice Mishra was the Chief Justice of the Hyderabad High Court.
256.tq: Use the wrong-person-for-the-deed trap by matching the report with its author and office.
xs: **Bellary taluk** went to **Mysore** on the report of **Justice Mishra**, **Chief Justice, Hyderabad High Court** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Wanchoo** (Rajasthan HC), **Kumaraswamy Raja** (Partition Committee) and **C.M. Trivedi** (Special Officer) did not decide Bellary taluk.
xa: Mishra's hearings: **1-15 May 1953**.
**Rayadurg** → Anantapur; **Adoni, Alur** → Kurnool.
The **Tungabhadra Board** was set up under the **Andhra State Act 1953**.

256.s: The Sreebagh Pact of 1937 promised priority for irrigation in Rayalaseema and Nellore on which rivers?
o: Krishna, Godavari and Pennar only in coastal Andhra
256.x: The Sreebagh Pact promised priority for irrigation in Rayalaseema and Nellore on the Tungabhadra, Krishna and Penna for ten years or as needed.
256.tq: Recall the exact three-river combination instead of selecting a nearby river group.
xs: The **Sreebagh Pact** (**1937**) gave **Rayalaseema** and **Nellore** irrigation priority on the **Tungabhadra, Krishna and Penna** — option **(2)** is correct.
Godavari, Vamsadhara, Bhima and Kaveri were not in the pact's clause.
xa: The priority was for **10 years** or as needed.
The **Andhra State Act 1953** set up the **Tungabhadra Board** to manage the works.
Today the Centre plans a **high-level committee** on Tungabhadra disputes among **AP, Telangana and Karnataka**.

256.s: The irrigation priority under the Sreebagh Pact was intended to operate:
o: Until the formation of Andhra State only
For ten years or as needed
256.x: The Pact provided priority for ten years or as needed, rather than prescribing either a permanent arrangement or a fixed five-year period.
256.tq: Distinguish a fixed duration with a qualifying phrase from absolute or permanent claims.
xs: The Sreebagh irrigation priority was for **10 years** or as needed — option **(4)** is correct.
It was neither permanent nor for five years only.
xa: Rivers: **Tungabhadra, Krishna and Penna**; beneficiaries: **Rayalaseema** and **Nellore**.
Pact year: **1937**.
After the **Bellary** split, Tungabhadra works were shared between **Andhra** and **Mysore**.

256.s: What institutional arrangement followed the division of Bellary in relation to the Tungabhadra project?
o: The project works became shared by Andhra and Mysore, and a Tungabhadra Board was established under the Andhra State Act, 1953.
The project was transferred entirely to Mysore.
The project was placed under the Madras High Court.
A board was established under the Sreebagh Pact of 1937 alone.
256.x: After Bellary was divided, the Tungabhadra works became shared between Andhra and Mysore. A Tungabhadra Board was set up under the Andhra State Act, 1953 to manage the works.
256.tq: Link the territorial change to its institutional consequence and reject the swapped legal basis.
xs: After the **Bellary** split, Tungabhadra works were shared by **Andhra** and **Mysore**, and a **Tungabhadra Board** was set up under the **Andhra State Act, 1953** — option **(1)**.
The **1937 Sreebagh Pact** only promised irrigation priority — it set up no board.
xa: **Bellary taluk** and **Hospet** etc. went to **Mysore**; **Adoni, Alur, Rayadurg** to Andhra.
On **26 Jun 2026**, **C.R. Patil** opened **33 new gates** of the **Tungabhadra dam** with three CMs present.
A **high-level committee** is planned for **AP, Telangana and Karnataka** water disputes.

256.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the 2014 bifurcation arrangements?
o: The Sheela Bhide Committee dealt with employee allocation and the Kamalanathan Committee dealt with capital.
The Section 6 expert committee dealt only with High Court jurisdiction.
The Kamalanathan Committee dealt with employees, while the Sheela Bhide Committee dealt with Schedule IX institutions.
Both committees dealt exclusively with Tungabhadra water sharing.
256.x: The Sheela Bhide Committee dealt with Schedule IX institutions, the Kamalanathan Committee with employees, and a separate Section 6 expert committee examined the capital issue.
256.tq: Match each panel with its specialised subject and reject swapped committee functions.
xs: **Kamalanathan Committee** = **employees**; **Sheela Bhide Committee** = **Schedule IX institutions** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **Section 6** expert committee dealt with the **capital**, not the High Court.
None of these panels dealt with **Tungabhadra** water.
xa: In **2014**, assets were split by **location** and debts by **population** → AP carried a heavy debt share.
⚠ For **1953**, the matching panels were the **Partition Committee** (**1949-50**) and the **Wanchoo Committee**.

256.s: In the 2014 bifurcation, which method of division contributed to Andhra Pradesh carrying a heavy share of debt?
o: Assets were divided by location and debts by population.
Assets were transferred to the Union and debts were cancelled.
Assets were divided by population and debts by location.
Both assets and debts were divided equally between the two states.
256.x: Assets were divided by location, whereas debts were divided by population. This arrangement resulted in Andhra Pradesh carrying a heavy debt share.
256.tq: Track the reversed comparison between the basis for dividing assets and the basis for dividing debts.
xs: In **2014**, assets were divided by **location** and debts by **population** — option **(1)** is correct.
This left **Andhra Pradesh** with a heavy debt share.
xa: **Sheela Bhide Committee**: **Schedule IX** institutions; **Kamalanathan Committee**: employees.
**Section 6** expert committee: capital.
⚠ In **1953**, too, the new state was "**administratively and economically orphaned**" after losing Madras.

256.s: Which of the following statements relates to the contemporary Tungabhadra water-dispute context?
o: The Centre planned a high-level committee to settle disputes among Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka.
The Union Jal Shakti Minister closed all gates of the Tungabhadra dam in June 2026.
The issue was settled through the Wanchoo Committee in 1953.
The dispute involved only Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
256.x: The Centre planned a high-level committee to address Tungabhadra water disputes involving Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka. The 1953 Wanchoo Committee was unrelated to this contemporary dispute.
256.tq: Separate a current institutional development from the historical committee and identify the correct states involved.
xs: The Centre plans a **high-level committee** on **Tungabhadra** water disputes among **AP, Telangana and Karnataka** — option **(1)** is correct.
**C.R. Patil** **opened** **33 new gates** of the dam (**26 Jun 2026**), not closed them; Tamil Nadu is not a party.
The **1953 Wanchoo** Committee dealt with Andhra's formation, not this dispute.
xa: Under the **Andhra State Act 1953**, a **Tungabhadra Board** was set up.
The **Sreebagh Pact** (**1937**) gave Rayalaseema and Nellore priority on the **Tungabhadra, Krishna and Penna**.

257.s: Which was the first Telugu newspaper, established in 1835 at Bellary and run by Christian missionaries?
257.x: Satyadoota, established in Bellary in 1835, was the first Telugu newspaper and was run by Christian missionaries.
257.tq: Recall the earliest publication through its year, place and institutional association.
xs: **Satyadoota** (**1835, Bellary**), run by **Christian missionaries**, was the first Telugu newspaper — option **(4)** is correct.
**Vrutantini** came in **1838** (Mandigala Venkataraya Sastri); **Hitavadi** in **1841** (Edmund Park).
**Vartamana Tarangini** (**1842**, Madras) was the first Telugu paper started by a Muslim (**Syed Rahamatullah**).
xa: ⚠ **Satyadoota** = first Telugu paper (Bellary); **Hitavadi** = first **printed in Andhra**.
**Andhra Prakasika** (**1885**) = first **political** journal in Telugu.
**Desabhimani** = the **only Telugu daily** in British Andhra.

257.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
257.x: Vrutantini dates from 1838 and was associated with Mandigala Venkataraya Sastri. The other pairs contain swapped years, places or persons.
257.tq: Start from the sure year–editor pair and eliminate swapped associations.
xs: **Vrutantini — 1838 — Mandigala Venkataraya Sastri** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Hitavadi** = **1841**, **Edmund Park**; **1835** and the missionaries belong to **Satyadoota**.
**Tattvabodhini** = **1864**, **Madras Veda Samaj**; **1842** and **Syed Rahamatullah** belong to **Vartamana Tarangini**.
**Purushartha Pradayini** = **1872**, **Machilipatnam**, not 1864.
xa: Tattvabodhini supported **widow remarriage**; Purushartha Pradayini carried articles **both for and against** it.
By **1905**, there were about **20 Telugu journals**, incl. Andhra Prakasika, Sasilekha, Krishna Patrika, Desabhimani, **Rasikollasini**.

257.s: Which Telugu newspaper was the first to be printed in Andhra?
257.x: Hitavadi, associated with Edmund Park and dated 1841, was the first Telugu newspaper printed in Andhra.
257.tq: Distinguish the first Telugu newspaper from the first one printed in Andhra.
xs: **Hitavadi** (**1841**, **Edmund Park**) was the first Telugu newspaper **printed in Andhra** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Satyadoota** (**1835**) was the first Telugu paper overall, but at **Bellary**.
**Vartamana Tarangini** (**1842**) and **Tattvabodhini** (**1864**) were both from **Madras**.
xa: ⚠ **Satyadoota** = first Telugu paper; **Hitavadi** = first printed in Andhra.
**Vrutantini** (**1838**) — Mandigala Venkataraya Sastri.

257.s:
Consider the following statements about Vartamana Tarangini:
1. It was started on 8 June 1842 at Madras.
2. Syed Rahamatullah was associated with its beginning.
3. It was the first Telugu paper started by a Muslim.
4. After 1843, it passed to Puvvada Seshagiri Rao.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
257.x: All four statements are correct. Vartamana Tarangini was a weekly begun at Madras in 1842 by Syed Rahamatullah, the first Telugu paper started by a Muslim, and later passed to Puvvada Seshagiri Rao.
257.tq: Verify date, place, distinction and ownership change as separate elements of one publication profile.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Statements 1, 2 — correct:** started **8 June 1842** at **Madras** by **Syed Rahamatullah**.
**Statement 3 — correct:** the **first Telugu paper started by a Muslim**.
**Statement 4 — correct:** after **1843** it passed to **Puvvada Seshagiri Rao** and got its own press.
xa: It was a **weekly**.
Earlier papers: **Satyadoota** (**1835**), **Vrutantini** (**1838**), **Hitavadi** (**1841**).
**Tattvabodhini** (**1864**, Madras) came from the **Madras Veda Samaj**.

257.s:
Consider the following statements about early Telugu journals and widow remarriage:
1. Tattvabodhini, published at Madras in 1864 by the Madras Veda Samaj, supported widow remarriage.
2. Purushartha Pradayini, published at Machilipatnam in 1872, carried articles only against widow remarriage.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
257.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Purushartha Pradayini carried articles both for and against widow remarriage. So only 1 (A); B, C and D all depend on the false statement 2 or deny the true statement 1.
257.tq: Veda Samaj's Tattvabodhini = for; Purushartha Pradayini = both sides.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
**Statement 1 — correct:** **Tattvabodhini** (**1864**, Madras, **Madras Veda Samaj**) supported widow remarriage.
**Statement 2 — wrong:** **Purushartha Pradayini** (**1872**, Machilipatnam) carried articles **both for and against** widow remarriage.
xa: **Veeresalingam's** journals included **Vivekavardhani (1874)** and **Sati Hitabodhini (1883)**.
Women's-cause papers: **Hindu Sundari** (**1902**) and **Sri Savitri** (**1904**).

257.s:
Arrange the following journals of Kandukuri Veeresalingam in chronological order of their commencement:
A. Satyasamvardhini
B. Vivekavardhani
C. Sati Hitabodhini
D. Hasyasanjivani
257.x: Vivekavardhani began in 1874, Hasyasanjivani in 1876, Sati Hitabodhini in 1883 and Satyasamvardhini in 1891.
257.tq: Fix the earliest and latest dates first, then arrange the middle publications.
xs: The order is **B, D, C, A** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Vivekavardhani** (**1874**) → **Hasyasanjivani** (**1876**) → **Sati Hitabodhini** (**1883**) → **Satyasamvardhini** (**1891**).
xa: Later journals: **Zenana Patrika** (**1894**) and **Satyavadini** (**1905**).
Veeresalingam had **his own press from 1876**.
He also ran **Chintamani** with **Nyapati Subbarao**.

257.s: Which one of the following statements about Veeresalingam's press activities is correct?
o: He established his own press only after 1905.
He did not possess a press and published only through missionary presses.
He established his own press in 1876.
His own press preceded all his journals and was established in 1870.
257.x: Veeresalingam had his own press from 1876.
257.tq: Identify the precise year associated with an institutional development, not merely a publication year.
xs: Veeresalingam had **his own press from 1876** — option **(3)** is correct.
His first journal, **Vivekavardhani**, came earlier, in **1874** — so the press did not precede all his journals.
xa: **Hasyasanjivani** also began in **1876**; **Sati Hitabodhini** in **1883**.
Later: **Satyasamvardhini** (**1891**), **Zenana Patrika** (**1894**), **Satyavadini** (**1905**).

257.s: Who was the editor of Andhra Prakasika, published in 1885?
257.x: A.P. Parthasarathy Naidu was the editor of Andhra Prakasika, which was published in 1885.
257.tq: Use direct editor–publication recall and distinguish similar Andhra newspaper names.
xs: **A.P. Parthasarathy Naidu** edited **Andhra Prakasika** (**1885**) — option **(4)** is correct.
**Mutnuri Krishna Rao** edited **Krishna Patrika**; **Devaguptam Seshachalapati Rao** ran **Desabhimani**; **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** founded **Andhra Patrika**.
xa: Andhra Prakasika was the **first political journal in Telugu**.
By **1905**, it was one of about **20 Telugu journals**.

257.s: Andhra Patrika was initially published from which place and in which year?
257.x: Andhra Patrika was started at Bombay on 9 September 1908 by Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.
257.tq: Separate the original publication place and year from the later shift and change to a daily.
xs: **Andhra Patrika** began at **Bombay** on **9 Sept 1908** — option **(3)** is correct.
It moved to **Madras** later, and became a **daily in 1914** — so options 1 and 4 mix up the facts.
**Vijayawada, 1907** is Gadicherla's **Swarajya**.
xa: Founder: **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**; it **promoted Gandhian ideas**.
He also ran the literary monthly **Bharati** (**1924**).
APPSC GS 2025 pair: **Andhra Patrika – Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**.

257.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Andhra Patrika?
o: It was a daily from its inception and opposed Gandhian ideas.
It began as a weekly, became a daily in 1914 and promoted Gandhian ideas.
It began as a monthly at Madras and became a weekly in 1914.
It was founded at Machilipatnam by Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao.
257.x: Andhra Patrika began as a weekly, became a daily in 1914 and promoted Gandhian ideas.
257.tq: Test the sequence of publication format and ideological orientation together.
xs: **Andhra Patrika** began as a **weekly**, became a **daily in 1914** and **promoted Gandhian ideas** — option **(2)** is correct.
It started at **Bombay** (**1908**), not Madras or Machilipatnam, and was founded by **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**, not Gadicherla.
xa: **Krishna Patrika** was the paper founded at **Machilipatnam** (**1 Feb 1902**).
**Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** founded the Telugu **Swarajya** (**1907**, Vijayawada).

257.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
257.x: Andhra Prabha was associated with the Indian Express group and Ramnath Goenka; Narla Venkateswara Rao was a noted editor. Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao founded Andhra Patrika.
257.tq: Find the swapped founder or editor among closely related Andhra newspapers.
xs: **Andhra Prabha — Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** is wrongly matched — option **(1)**; Andhra Prabha was an **Indian Express group** paper (Ramnath Goenka).
**Desabhimani — Devaguptam Seshachalapati Rao**, **Zamin Ryot — Nellore Venkatarama Naidu**, **Swarajya — Gadicherla** are all correct.
xa: **Narla Venkateswara Rao** was a noted editor of Andhra Prabha (**1938**, Madras).
Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao founded **Andhra Patrika** (**1908**) and **Bharati** (**1924**).
Desabhimani began as **Krishnavrittantini**; Zamin Ryot wrote on **peasant issues**.

257.s:
Consider the following statements about the newspapers named Swarajya:
1. Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao's Telugu Swarajya was started in 1907 at Vijayawada.
2. Gadicherla's Swarajya was earlier named Krishnavrittantini.
3. Tanguturi Prakasam's Swarajya was a separate English daily from Madras.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
257.x: Statement 1 is correct (Vijayawada, 1907). Statement 2 is wrong: Swarajya was earlier named Sri Venkateswara Patrika; Krishnavrittantini was the earlier name of Desabhimani. Statement 3 is correct: Prakasam's Swarajya was a separate English daily from Madras. Hence 1 and 3 only; A omits 3, C and D include the false 2.
257.tq: Two Swarajyas: Gadicherla's Telugu (Vijayawada 1907, ex-Sri Venkateswara Patrika) vs Prakasam's English daily (Madras).
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
**Statement 1 — correct:** Gadicherla's Telugu **Swarajya** began in **1907** at **Vijayawada**.
**Statement 2 — wrong:** it was earlier **Sri Venkateswara Patrika**; **Krishnavrittantini** was the earlier name of **Desabhimani**.
**Statement 3 — correct:** **Prakasam's Swarajya** was a separate **English daily** from **Madras** (APPSC GS 2021 key).
xa: Gadicherla's Swarajya was **militant nationalist**; he was jailed for editorials such as **"Veerabali"**.
APPSC GS 2025 pair: **Swarajya – Gadicherla**.

257.s: Zamin Ryot, published from Nellore, was particularly associated with writing on which subject?
257.x: Zamin Ryot was published from Nellore and was associated with Nellore Venkatarama Naidu; it wrote on peasant issues.
257.tq: Link a newspaper to its distinctive subject focus rather than to its editor alone.
xs: **Zamin Ryot** (Nellore) wrote on **peasant issues** — option **(4)** is correct.
Founder: **Nellore Venkatarama Naidu**; it served the **peasant / anti-zamindari** movement.
Widow remarriage was the theme of **Tattvabodhini**; mother-tongue education was backed by **Swadesamitran** (**1915**).
xa: **Navasakthi** = first fully **socialist** Telugu journal; **Prajasakthi** = first **communist** one.
**Andhra Mata** = paper of the **Home Rule** movement.

257.s: Krishna Patrika was first published on 1 February 1902 at:
257.x: Krishna Patrika began publication on 1 February 1902 at Machilipatnam.
257.tq: Distinguish the journal’s place of origin from the later centres of other Telugu newspapers.
xs: **Krishna Patrika** began on **1 Feb 1902** at **Machilipatnam** — option **(1)** is correct.
Founders: **Konda Venkatappayya and Dasu Narayana Rao**.
xa: Its most famous editor: **Mutnuri Krishna Rao**.
Its office was a meeting point for freedom fighters.
**19 Jul 1913** cartoon: **Rayalaseema** as an **iceberg** blocking the "Andhra Movement" ship.

257.s: Krishna Patrika was founded at Machilipatnam on 1 February 1902 by which pair?
o: Konda Venkatappaiah and Dasu Narayana Rao
Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham and C.Y. Chintamani
Mutnuri Krishna Rao and Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao
Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao and Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao
257.x: Krishna Patrika was founded on 1 February 1902 by Konda Venkatappaiah and Dasu Narayana Rao at Machilipatnam.
257.tq: Combine the date with the founder pair rather than relying on the later editor’s name.
xs: **Konda Venkatappaiah and Dasu Narayana Rao** founded **Krishna Patrika** (**1 Feb 1902**, Machilipatnam) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Mutnuri Krishna Rao** was its later, most famous editor; **Gadicherla** founded **Swarajya**.
**Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham** ran **Manorama** and **Desamata**; **Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao** ran **Andhra Kesari**.
xa: APPSC GS 2025 pair: **Krishna Patrika – Konda Venkatappayya**.
**30 Nov 1912**: Krishna Patrika wrote that strengthening the nation begins with the Andhra movement.

257.s: Who is regarded as the second and most famous editor of Krishna Patrika, largely responsible for its success?
257.x: Mutnuri Krishna Rao was Krishna Patrika's second and most famous editor and was largely responsible for its success (APPSC GS 2024). Konda Venkatappayya and Dasu Narayana Rao founded it in 1902; Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao founded Andhra Patrika.
257.tq: Founders of Krishna Patrika = Konda + Dasu; famous editor = Mutnuri.
xs: **Mutnuri Krishna Rao** was Krishna Patrika's **second and most famous editor**, "largely responsible for its success" — option **(2)** (APPSC GS 2024).
**Konda Venkatappayya** and **Dasu Narayana Rao** were its **founders** (**1902**).
**Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** founded **Andhra Patrika** (**1908**).
xa: Krishna Patrika's office was a meeting point for freedom fighters.
It backed the **Vandemataram / Swadeshi** movement.
Its **11 Apr 1914** editorial and **19 Jul 1913** iceberg cartoon backed the Andhra movement.

257.s: Who was the editor associated with Bharati, the literary monthly started in 1924?
257.x: Bharati, a literary monthly started in 1924, was associated with Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.
257.tq: Match a journal with its editor while separating literary journals from political newspapers.
xs: **Bharati** (**1924**), a literary monthly, was run by **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Suravaram Pratapa Reddy** ran **Golconda Patrika**; **Jayanti Ramayya** the **Andhra Sahitya Parishad Patrika**; **Kokkonda Venkataratnam** **Andhra Bhasa Sanjivani**.
xa: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao also founded **Andhra Patrika** (**9 Sept 1908**, Bombay).
**Manorama** (**1906**) and **Desamata** (**1910**) — Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham.

257.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Andhra Bhasa Sanjivani — Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham
Andhra Sahitya Parishad Patrika — Jayanti Ramayya
257.x: Andhra Bhasa Sanjivani was associated with Kokkonda Venkataratnam, who introduced the editorial column. Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham was associated with Manorama and Desamata.
257.tq: Locate the swapped editor among a cluster of journal–editor pairs.
xs: **Andhra Bhasa Sanjivani** was **Kokkonda Venkataratnam's**, not Chilakamarti's — option **(1)** is the wrong pair.
**Andhra Sahitya Parishad Patrika — Jayanti Ramayya**, **Manoranjani — Kallakuri Narayana Rao**, **Golconda Patrika — Suravaram Pratapa Reddy** are correct.
xa: Andhra Bhasa Sanjivani **introduced the editorial column**.
**Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham** ran **Manorama** (**1906**) and **Desamata** (**1910**).
**Chintamani** — Veeresalingam and **Nyapati Subbarao**.

257.s: Which journal did Gurajada Appa Rao attempt in 1896?
257.x: Gurajada Appa Rao attempted Prakasika in 1896.
257.tq: Associate the individual, journal title and year without confusing it with Andhra Prakasika.
xs: **Gurajada Appa Rao** attempted **Prakasika** in **1896** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Bharati** (**1924**) was Kasinathuni's; **Manorama** (**1906**) was Chilakamarti's; **Andhra Bhasa Sanjivani** was Kokkonda Venkataratnam's.
xa: ⚠ Do not confuse **Prakasika** (**1896**) with **Andhra Prakasika** (**1885**), the first political journal.
**Manoranjani** (**1910**) — Kallakuri Narayana Rao.

257.s: The article 'Are Telugu people backward?' reported which comparison?
o: 56 Andhras to 8 non-Andhras in civil services, and 19 to 0 in the judiciary
19 non-Andhras to 0 Andhras in civil services, and 56 to 8 in the judiciary
8 non-Andhras to 56 Andhras in civil services, and 0 to 19 in the judiciary
56 non-Andhras to 8 Andhras in civil services, and 19 to 0 in the judiciary
257.x: The article reported 56 non-Andhras to 8 Andhras in the civil services and 19 non-Andhras to no Andhras in the judiciary.
257.tq: Guard against reversed comparisons in numerical statement questions.
xs: "Are Telugu people backward?" reported **56 non-Andhras to 8 Andhras** in civil services and **19 to 0** in the judiciary — option **(4)** is correct.
The other options reverse the figures or swap services and judiciary.
xa: It appeared in **The Hindu** on **15 Apr 1911**, by **Jonnavittula Gurunatham**.
He wrote **6** articles in **1911**; Telugu papers demanded a separate state from **1911**.
Opposing view: the **"Viswamitra"** letter in The Hindu (**29 Aug 1912**) asked where Andhra would find officers.

257.s: Which newspaper stated on 30 November 1912 that strengthening the nation begins with the Andhra movement?
257.x: Krishna Patrika made this statement on 30 November 1912 in support of the Andhra movement.
257.tq: Link a dated editorial statement to the correct newspaper.
xs: **Krishna Patrika** wrote on **30 Nov 1912** that strengthening the nation begins with the Andhra movement — option **(3)** is correct.
**Janmabhumi's** similar article (national unity) came on **25 Aug 1920**.
xa: Krishna Patrika's **19 Jul 1913** cartoon showed **Rayalaseema** as an **iceberg** blocking the ship.
Its **11 Apr 1914** editorial also backed the movement.
**The Hindu** ran both Gurunatham's articles and the opposing **"Viswamitra"** letter.

257.s: The cartoon published on 19 July 1913 in Krishna Patrika depicted which image?
o: Telugu people as an iceberg opposing national unity
Madras as a ship carrying the Andhra Mahasabha
Rayalaseema as an iceberg blocking the ship of the Andhra Movement
Andhra as a bird emerging from a cage
257.x: The cartoon depicted Rayalaseema as an iceberg blocking the ship labelled 'Andhra Movement'.
257.tq: Test the distinctive visual metaphor rather than the newspaper's general ideology.
xs: The **19 Jul 1913** **Krishna Patrika** cartoon showed **Rayalaseema** as an **iceberg** blocking the "**Andhra Movement**" ship — option **(3)** is correct.
It pictured Rayalaseema's resistance, not the Telugu people or Madras.
xa: Krishna Patrika's **30 Nov 1912** line: strengthening the nation begins with the Andhra movement.
Founded **1 Feb 1902**, **Machilipatnam**; most famous editor **Mutnuri Krishna Rao**.

257.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding newspaper support for the Andhra movement?
o: The Hindu — supported the movement without any opposing contribution
Swadesamitran — opposed mother-tongue education at the Third Andhra Mahasabha
Janmabhumi — published its special article on 25 August 1912
Desabhimani — urged Telugu papers to write on Andhra affairs instead of world politics
257.x: Desabhimani urged Telugu papers to focus on Andhra affairs rather than world politics. Swadesamitran supported mother-tongue education, Janmabhumi's special article appeared on 25 August 1920, and The Hindu also carried an opposing contribution.
257.tq: Find the correctly matched newspaper and statement while rejecting date and viewpoint reversals.
xs: **Desabhimani** urged Telugu papers to write on **Andhra affairs** instead of world politics — option **(4)** is correct.
**Swadesamitran** (Tamil) **backed** mother-tongue education at the **3rd Mahasabha** (Visakhapatnam, **1915**).
**Janmabhumi's** article came on **25 Aug 1920**, not 1912; **The Hindu** also carried the opposing **"Viswamitra"** letter.
xa: Desabhimani = the **only Telugu daily** in British Andhra; founder **Devaguptam Seshachalapati Rao**.
It began as **Krishnavrittantini**.

257.s: Which of the following groups consisted entirely of publications that supported the movement for a separate Andhra?
o: Andhra Patrika, Krishna Patrika, Desabhimani, Desamata and Darbar
The Hindu, Viswamitra, Swadesamitran and Desamata
Krishna Patrika, The Hindu, Modern Review and Viswamitra
Desabhimani, Zamin Ryot, The Hindu and Hindusthan Review
257.x: Andhra Patrika, Krishna Patrika, Desabhimani, Desamata and Darbar were listed as supporters of the separate Andhra movement.
257.tq: Screen each group for a known opposing paper or publication not listed as a supporter.
xs: **Andhra Patrika, Krishna Patrika, Desabhimani, Desamata and Darbar** all supported a separate Andhra — option **(1)** is correct.
The **"Viswamitra"** letter in The Hindu (**29 Aug 1912**) **opposed** the demand, so options 2 and 3 fail.
**Zamin Ryot** is not among the listed supporters.
xa: Outside support: **The Modern Review**, **Hindusthan Review**, **London Review of Reviews**.
**Janmabhumi** (**25 Aug 1920**): the Andhra movement strengthens national unity.

257.s: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was popularly known as the 'Gagging Act'. Who repealed it, and in which year?
257.x: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878, popularly called the Gagging Act, was repealed by Ripon in 1882.
257.tq: Pair the enactment with the correct repealing authority and year, avoiding near-date traps.
xs: The **Vernacular Press Act, 1878** ("Gagging Act") was repealed by **Ripon** in **1882** — option **(3)** is correct.
**1878** is when the Act was passed, not repealed.
xa: This was the background to the growth of Telugu nationalist papers.
Gadicherla was jailed with a heavy sentence for **Swarajya** editorials such as **"Veerabali"**.

257.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding newspapers associated with movements in Andhra:

List-I (Movement)

a. Vandemataram/Swadeshi movement
b. Peasant or anti-zamindari movement
c. Socialist movement
d. Communist movement

List-II (Newspaper)

i. Zamin Ryot
ii. Prajasakthi
iii. Navasakthi
iv. Krishna Patrika, Swarajya, Desamata, Andhra Kesari and Navayuga

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
257.x: The Vandemataram/Swadeshi movement was supported by Krishna Patrika, Swarajya, Desamata, Andhra Kesari and Navayuga. Zamin Ryot supported the peasant or anti-zamindari movement, Navasakthi was associated with socialism, and Prajasakthi with communism.
257.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with mismatched movement–newspaper associations.
xs: **a–iv, b–i, c–iii, d–ii** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Vandemataram / Swadeshi:** Krishna Patrika, Swarajya, Desamata, **Andhra Kesari**, Navayuga.
**Peasant / anti-zamindari:** **Zamin Ryot**; **Socialist:** **Navasakthi**; **Communist:** **Prajasakthi**.
xa: **Home Rule** paper: **Andhra Mata** (APPSC G2 2017 key).
**Andhra Kesari** was **Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao's** paper (Rajahmundry); **Desamata** was also from Rajahmundry.
Women's cause: **Hindu Sundari** (**1902**), **Sri Savitri** (**1904**).

257.s:
Match the following women-oriented publications with the years associated with them:

a. Hindu Sundari
a. 1902
b. Sri Savitri
b. 1904

Which of the following is correct?
257.x: Hindu Sundari was associated with the year 1902, while Sri Savitri was associated with 1904.
257.tq: Match each publication with its specific year before checking the combined option.
xs: **Hindu Sundari — 1902**; **Sri Savitri — 1904** — option **(1)** is correct.
Both served the **women's cause**; **1835** is the year of **Satyadoota**.
xa: **Tattvabodhini** (**1864**) supported **widow remarriage**.
**Veeresalingam's** women-oriented journals: **Sati Hitabodhini** (**1883**), **Zenana Patrika** (**1894**).

257.s: Jaya Bharat holds which distinction in the history of Telugu journalism?
o: It was the first fully socialist Telugu journal.
It was the first Telugu journal published after independence.
It was the only Telugu daily of British Andhra.
It was the first Telugu newspaper published in Bellary in 1835.
257.x: Jaya Bharat was the first Telugu journal published after independence. The other options describe other papers: Navasakthi was the first fully socialist Telugu journal, Desabhimani the only Telugu daily of British Andhra, and Satyadoota (Bellary, 1835) the first Telugu newspaper.
257.tq: Discriminate among publications by their precise historical distinction rather than by their broad association with Telugu journalism.
xs: **Jaya Bharat** was the **first Telugu journal published after independence** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Navasakthi** = first fully socialist Telugu journal; **Desabhimani** = only Telugu daily of British Andhra.
**Satyadoota** = first Telugu paper (**1835, Bellary**).
xa: **Prajasakthi** = first communist Telugu journal.
**Andhra Prakasika** (**1885**) = first political journal in Telugu.
**Vartamana Tarangini** = first Telugu paper started by a Muslim.

257.s: Which Telugu newspaper is associated with the Home Rule movement in Andhra?
257.x: Andhra Mata was the paper of the Home Rule movement (APPSC G2 2017 key). Zamin Ryot wrote on peasant issues, Navasakthi was the first fully socialist Telugu journal, and Jaya Bharat was the first Telugu journal after independence.
257.tq: Home Rule -> Andhra Mata.
xs: **Andhra Mata** was the **Home Rule** paper (APPSC G2 2017 key) — option **(3)** is correct.
**Zamin Ryot** = peasant issues; **Navasakthi** = socialist; **Jaya Bharat** = first Telugu journal after independence.
xa: **Vandemataram / Swadeshi** papers: Krishna Patrika, Swarajya, Desamata, Andhra Kesari, Navayuga.
**Prajasakthi** = first communist Telugu journal.

257.s: Which of the following best describes the wider significance of the press in the Andhra region during the freedom movement?
o: It opposed both the national movement and the demand for a separate Andhra.
It confined its activities exclusively to literary publishing and avoided political issues.
It spread the national movement and built support for the demand for a separate Andhra.
It functioned only as an instrument of the colonial administration.
257.x: The press performed a dual role: it spread the national movement and also built support for the separate-Andhra demand.
257.tq: Identify the option that combines both stated functions instead of accepting an extreme exclusive claim.
xs: The press **spread the national movement** and **built support for the separate-Andhra demand** — option **(3)** is correct.
Papers like **Krishna Patrika**, **Andhra Patrika** and **Desabhimani** were openly political, not colonial or purely literary.
xa: Newspapers also gave rise to **reading rooms and libraries**.
Telugu papers demanded a separate state from **1911**.
**Janmabhumi** (**25 Aug 1920**): the Andhra movement strengthens national unity.

257.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the social impact of newspapers in the Andhra region:
1. Newspapers gave rise to reading rooms.
2. Newspapers contributed to the development of libraries.
3. Newspapers had no role beyond reporting political events.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
257.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: newspapers gave rise to reading rooms and libraries. Statement 3 is false because their influence extended beyond merely reporting political events.
257.tq: Reject the restrictive statement and select the combination containing the two wider social effects.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
**Statements 1, 2 — correct:** newspapers gave rise to **reading rooms and libraries**.
**Statement 3 — wrong:** the press also **spread the national movement** and built support for a **separate Andhra**.
xa: First political journal: **Andhra Prakasika** (**1885**).
Only Telugu daily of British Andhra: **Desabhimani**.

257.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Andhra Prakasika — first political journal in Telugu
2. Desabhimani — only Telugu daily in British Andhra
3. Satyadoota — first Telugu journal published after independence
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
257.x: Pair 1 is correct: Andhra Prakasika (1885) was the first political journal in Telugu. Pair 2 is correct: Desabhimani was the only Telugu daily in British Andhra. Pair 3 is wrong: Satyadoota (1835) was the first Telugu newspaper; Jaya Bharat was the first Telugu journal after independence. Hence 1 and 2 only.
257.tq: First political journal = Andhra Prakasika; only daily = Desabhimani.
xs: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
**Pair 1 — correct:** **Andhra Prakasika** (**1885**) = first political journal in Telugu.
**Pair 2 — correct:** **Desabhimani** = only Telugu daily in British Andhra.
**Pair 3 — wrong:** **Satyadoota** (**1835**) was the first Telugu newspaper; **Jaya Bharat** was the first after independence.
xa: Andhra Prakasika's editor: **A.P. Parthasarathy Naidu**.
Desabhimani's founder: **Devaguptam Seshachalapati Rao**; it began as **Krishnavrittantini**.
**Hitavadi** (**1841**) = first Telugu paper printed in Andhra.

258.s:
Mutnuri Krishna Rao transformed Krishna Patrika primarily into a:

1. Political weekly
2. Centre for freedom fighters
3. Commercial banking journal
4. Hub of political awakening
258.x: Mutnuri Krishna Rao made Krishna Patrika a political weekly and a hub for freedom fighters, which made it a centre of political awakening (1, 2 and 4). It was never a commercial banking journal, so 3 is wrong.
258.tq: Find the statement that changes the political character of the institution into an unrelated activity.
xs: **Mutnuri Krishna Rao** made Krishna Patrika a **political weekly**, a **hub for freedom fighters** and of **political awakening** — option **(2) 1, 2 and 4 only**.
Item 3 is wrong: Krishna Patrika was never a **commercial banking journal**.
xa: In **1907**, Mutnuri called extremist leaders to visit Andhra.
**Bipin Chandra Pal** toured Andhra in **April 1907** — Kakinada (**17** Apr) and **five** lectures at Rajahmundry (**19-24** Apr).
Editors made journalism a tool of political awakening that also publicised the **library movement**.

258.s: In which year did Mutnuri Krishna Rao call upon extremist leaders to visit Andhra?
258.x: Mutnuri Krishna Rao called upon extremist leaders to visit Andhra in 1907.
258.tq: Use the year as the decisive clue while rejecting nearby movement years.
xs: Mutnuri Krishna Rao called extremist leaders to visit Andhra in **1907** — option **(2)** is correct.
The result was **Bipin Chandra Pal's** tour of **April 1907**.
xa: Pal lectured at **Kakinada** on **17** Apr 1907 and gave **five** lectures at **Rajahmundry**, **19-24** Apr.
⚠ Some notes say Mutnuri organised the tour; the **G2 2011 key** credits **Gadicherla** — know both.
The **Bala Bharati Samithi** was founded at Rajahmundry in **Feb 1907**.

258.s: Which extremist leader toured Andhra in April 1907, lecturing at Kakinada and delivering five lectures at Rajahmundry?
258.x: Bipin Chandra Pal toured Andhra in April 1907 (Kakinada on 17 April, Rajahmundry 19-24 April) after Andhra leaders invited extremist leaders. Tilak, Lajpat Rai and Aurobindo did not make this tour. Some sources credit Mutnuri Krishna Rao with organising it; the APPSC G2 2011 key credits Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao.
258.tq: 1907 Andhra tour = Bipin Chandra Pal; organiser per G2 2011 key = Gadicherla.
xs: **Bipin Chandra Pal** toured Andhra in **April 1907** — option **(4)** is correct.
He spoke at **Kakinada** (**17** Apr) and gave **five** lectures at **Rajahmundry** (**19-24** Apr), at **Mutnuri's** invitation.
xa: ⚠ Trap: some notes say Mutnuri organised the tour; the **G2 2011 key** credits **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao**.
The **1907 Rajahmundry College** incident got Gadicherla blacklisted from government jobs.
**Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao** co-founded the **Bala Bharati Samithi**, Rajahmundry, **Feb 1907**.

258.s:
Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao is associated with which of the following publication years?

1. Andhra Patrika — 1908
2. Bharati — 1924
3. Krishna Patrika — 1907
4. Swarajya — 1907
258.x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao founded Andhra Patrika (1908) and Bharati (1924). Krishna Patrika was founded in 1902 by Konda Venkatappayya and Dasu Narayana Rao, and Swarajya (1907) was Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao's paper. Hence 1 and 2 only.
258.tq: Split publication years from the editor–paper associations to catch cross-pairing.
xs: Only items 1 and 2 fit — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**: **Andhra Patrika** (**1908**) and **Bharati** (**1924**).
**Krishna Patrika** was **Mutnuri Krishna Rao's** paper, not his.
**Swarajya** (**1907**) was **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao's**.
xa: Kasinathuni also set up the publishing house **Andhra Granthamala**, named to popularise the word "Andhra".
He lived **1867-1947**; title **"Desoddharaka"**.
The **Sreebagh Pact** was signed at his Madras house on **16 Nov 1937**.

258.s:
Which of the following statements about Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao is correct?

1. He lived from 1867 to 1947.
2. He was known by the title ‘Desoddharaka’.
3. His business wealth was put to public use in accordance with the idea of Gandhian trusteeship.
4. His Amrutanjan business helped fund his public work.
258.x: All four statements are correct. Nageswara Rao (1867-1947) was titled Desoddharaka, and in the spirit of Gandhian trusteeship he used the wealth of his Amrutanjan business to fund his public work.
258.tq: Treat dates, titles, ideology and financial support as separate factual checks.

259.s: Who was the first president of the Andhra Desa Library Association?
259.x: Mocherla Ramachandra Rao was the first president of the Andhra Desa Library Association.
259.tq: Distinguish the first president from the two secretaries and the conference organisers.
xs: **Mocherla Ramachandra Rao** was the ADLA's first president — option **(2)** is correct.
