Match List-I with List-II regarding Hyderabad Congress resolutions:
List-I (Date)
a. June 1953
b. 1954
c. 8 July 1954
d. November 1955
List-II (Decision/Event)
i. Telangana convention backed a separate Telangana
 ii. Hyderabad PCC delegation met the SRC
 iii. Resolution for dividing Hyderabad State into three parts
 iv. Earlier resolution was rejected and territorial representatives agreed on Maharashtra and Karnataka
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
262.x: In June 1953 the Hyderabad Congress Committee proposed three divisions; in 1954 that resolution was rejected; on 8 July 1954 the PCC delegation met the SRC; and in November 1955 Harishchandra Heda supported separate Telangana.
262.tq: Start with the exact 8 July date and then arrange the remaining resolutions by year.
xs: Correct match: **a–iii, b–iv, c–ii, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**June 1953**: divide Hyderabad State into three; **1954**: that resolution set aside, Marathwada to Maharashtra and Kannada areas to Karnataka.
**8 July 1954**: Hyderabad PCC delegation to the SRC; **Nov 1955**: Telangana convention backed separate Telangana (**Heda**).
xa: The June 1953 three parts: **Visalandhra, United Maharashtra, United Karnataka**.
The 1954 delegation sought a Telangana of **60,000 sq miles** and **Rs 17 crore** revenue.
Delegation members: **Harishchandra Heda, J.V. Narsing Rao, Arige Ramaswamy**.

262.s: Which of the following was included in the Hyderabad PCC delegation’s proposal of 8 July 1954?
o: A self-sufficient Telangana comprising nine districts, Bastar, parts of Chanda and Telugu areas of Marathwada and Karnataka
A united Andhra State including all of Maharashtra and Karnataka
A separate state consisting only of the nine coastal districts
A Telangana limited to Hyderabad city and its suburbs
262.x: The delegation proposed a self-sufficient Telangana of nine districts along with Bastar, parts of Chanda and Telugu areas of Marathwada and Karnataka.
262.tq: Check the exact territorial composition of the proposed unit.
xs: The delegation sought a **self-sufficient Telangana** of **nine districts** + **Bastar**, parts of **Chanda** and Telugu areas of **Marathwada and Karnataka** — option **(1)**.
It met the SRC on **8 July 1954**.
xa: Proposed size: **60,000 sq miles**, **Rs 17 crore revenue**.
Members: **Harishchandra Heda, J.V. Narsing Rao, Arige Ramaswamy**.
Same day, the **Warangal Congress meeting** noted the Hyderabad government had **no official opinion**.

262.s: Why was it argued that Telangana could exist as a separate state?
o: It had no revenue surplus and therefore required immediate merger.
It had higher per capita income and revenue than Andhra State and was therefore considered economically viable.
It had already been declared a separate state by the States Reorganisation Commission.
Its population was larger than that of every other region in India.
262.x: The argument for separate Telangana was based on its higher per capita income and revenue compared with Andhra State, making it economically viable on its own.
262.tq: Connect the economic indicators with the political conclusion drawn from them.
xs: Telangana had **higher per capita income and revenue** than Andhra State, so it was seen as **economically viable** — option **(2)**.
The SRC recommended a separate Telangana only **initially**, to be reconsidered after **1961** — it did not declare one.
xa: Telangana's revenue surplus fear led to the clause: **surplus spent only in Telangana**.
SRC: merger only with **two-thirds** of the Telangana legislature.
Nehru's "**Andhra imperialism**" remark (**Oct 1953**) boosted the separate-Telangana camp.

262.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee resolution at Kurnool
B. Formation of the Visalandhra Mahasabha
C. Hyderabad PCC delegation met the SRC
D. Telangana convention supported separate Telangana
262.x: The Visalandhra Mahasabha was founded in 1949; the APCC Kurnool resolution occurred on 30 September 1953; the Hyderabad PCC delegation met the SRC on 8 July 1954; and the Telangana convention took place in November 1955.
262.tq: Place the 1949 event first, then use the stated dates to order the later events.
xs: Correct order is **B, A, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**B** Mahasabha founded (**26 Nov 1949**) → **A** APCC Kurnool (**30 Sep 1953**) → **C** PCC delegation to SRC (**8 July 1954**) → **D** Telangana convention (**Nov 1955**).
xa: The **1st** Mahasabha session was at **Warangal**, **12-13 Feb 1950**.
The **2nd** Mahasabha was at **Hyderabad**, **13-14 Jun 1954** (President **Sri Sri**).
**Harishchandra Heda** backed a separate Telangana at the **Nov 1955** convention.

262.s: Who among the following supported a separate Telangana at the Telangana convention held in November 1955?
262.x: Harishchandra Heda supported the demand for a separate Telangana at the November 1955 Telangana convention.
262.tq: Match a leader with the specific forum and position associated with him.
xs: **Harishchandra Heda** backed a separate Telangana at the **Nov 1955** convention — option **(4)**.
**Bezawada Gopala Reddy** and **Burgula** signed the **Gentlemen's Agreement** for merger.
xa: Heda was also part of the Hyderabad PCC delegation to the **SRC** (**8 July 1954**).
⚠ One note spells him "Harishachandra Deda".
Other separate-Telangana voices: **Marri Chenna Reddy**, **Mahadev Singh** (PSP).

262.s: What did the States Reorganisation Commission recommend in paragraph 386 regarding Telangana?
o: Immediate merger with Andhra without conditions
A separate Telangana state initially, with reconsideration after the 1961 elections and merger only with a two-thirds majority of the Telangana legislature
Merger only after a referendum in Madras
Permanent continuation of Hyderabad as a multilingual state
262.x: The SRC recommended that Telangana remain separate initially, that the issue be reconsidered after the 1961 elections, and that merger require a two-thirds majority in the Telangana legislature.
262.tq: Retain all conditions in a recommendation instead of selecting only its headline.
xs: SRC (**1955, para 386**): **separate Telangana initially**, reconsider after the **1961** elections, merger only with **two-thirds** of the Telangana legislature — option **(2)**.
It did not recommend immediate unconditional merger or a permanent multilingual Hyderabad.
xa: SRC members: **Fazl Ali** (chair), **H.N. Kunzru, K.M. Panikkar**.
Also: **Raichur, Gulbarga** → Mysore; **Marathwada** detached.
The wait-till-**1961** formula foreshadowed later separate-Telangana demands.

262.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Event)
a. Nehru announced the States Reorganisation Commission in the Lok Sabha
b. States Reorganisation Commission was constituted
c. Report of the Commission

d. Visalandhra Mahasabha was founded
List-II (Date/Year)
i. 1949
 ii. 22 December 1953
 iii. 29 December 1953
 iv. 1955
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
262.x: Nehru announced the Commission on 22 December 1953; it was constituted on 29 December 1953; its report came in 1955; and the Visalandhra Mahasabha was founded in 1949.
262.tq: Start from the sure date and complete the chronological pairs.
xs: Correct match: **a–ii, b–iii, c–iv, d–i** — option **(1)**.
SRC announced by **Nehru** on **22 Dec 1953**; constituted **29 Dec 1953**; report **1955**; Visalandhra Mahasabha founded **1949**.
xa: SRC constituted by Home Ministry Resolution **53/69/53**.
Members: **Fazl Ali** (chair), **H.N. Kunzru, K.M. Panikkar**.
Hyderabad Assembly vote on the report: **103** for, **29** against, **15** neutral.

262.s: Who among the following was NOT a member of the States Reorganisation Commission?
262.x: Fazl Ali, H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar were the members of the States Reorganisation Commission. Harishchandra Heda was associated with Telangana political resolutions, not with the Commission.
262.tq: Identify the person outside the formal membership list.
xs: **Harishchandra Heda** was not an SRC member — option **(3)**.
SRC members: **Fazl Ali** (chair), **H.N. Kunzru, K.M. Panikkar**.
Heda was in the Hyderabad PCC delegation to the SRC and backed separate Telangana (**Nov 1955**).
xa: SRC announced **22 Dec 1953**, constituted **29 Dec 1953**, report **1955**.
⚠ **Fazl Ali** = SRC; **Wanchoo** = Andhra State problems; **Pataskar** = Andhra-Madras border.
BRS leader **K.T. Rama Rao** (**Jan 2026**) cited the **Fazal Ali Commission**'s recommendation.

262.s: Which of the following territorial changes was recommended in relation to Hyderabad State by the States Reorganisation Commission?
o: Raichur and Gulbarga to Andhra, and Marathwada to Mysore
Marathwada to Andhra, and the Kannada areas to Telangana
Raichur and Gulbarga to Mysore, and Marathwada to be detached
262.x: The Commission recommended that Raichur and Gulbarga go to Mysore and that Marathwada be detached from Hyderabad State.
262.tq: Test the direction of territorial transfers without reversing the recipient regions.
xs: SRC: **Raichur and Gulbarga to Mysore**, and **Marathwada** to be **detached** — option **(3)**.
Telangana was to continue initially as a **separate state**.
xa: Reconsider after **1961** elections; merger only with **two-thirds** of the Telangana legislature.
On **1 Nov 1956**, Kannada areas of Hyderabad went to **Mysore** and Marathi areas to **Bombay**.
Telugu, Kannada and Marathi areas of Hyderabad State agreed to partition.

262.s: The Hyderabad Legislative Assembly debate on the States Reorganisation Commission report recorded how many votes in favour of Visalandhra?
262.x: Of the 147 members who voted, 103 voted in favour of Visalandhra, 29 against it and 15 remained neutral.
262.tq: Distinguish the votes in favour from the total membership and the other voting categories.
xs: **103** members voted for Visalandhra — option **(3)**.
Of **147** who voted, **29** were against and **15** neutral; total members **174**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes print **153** for; **103** is the figure that adds up to **147**.
SRC report came in **1955**.
SRC had wanted merger only with **two-thirds** of the Telangana legislature.

262.s: Which of the following correctly describes the legal status given to the Gentlemen's Agreement in connection with the formation of Andhra Pradesh?
o: It remained only a private political understanding without statutory support
It was enforced through the Andhra State Act, 1953
It was incorporated into the Constitution as a separate Schedule
It was given constitutional backing through Article 371(1) and the 1958 Regional Committee Order
262.x: The Gentlemen's Agreement's Regional Committee for Telangana was given constitutional backing through Article 371(1) (inserted by the Seventh Amendment, 1956) and the Andhra Pradesh Regional Committee Order, 1958. It was more than a private understanding, but it was neither a separate Schedule nor part of the Andhra State Act, 1953.
262.tq: Identify the correct legal instrument instead of confusing constitutional, statutory and political arrangements.
xs: The Agreement got constitutional backing through **Article 371(1)** and the **1958 Regional Committee Order** — option **(4)**.
Article 371(1) came via the **7th Amendment, 1956**; it was not a separate Schedule or part of a 1953 Act.
xa: The **Regional Committee** was appointed by the **President**, constituted in **1958**.
Wound up after the **32nd Amendment (1973)** removed AP from Art. 371(1).
Root flaw: mostly **political assurances**, not constitutional mandates.

262.s: The Gentlemen's Agreement was signed at which of the following places?
262.x: The agreement was signed at Hyderabad House in New Delhi. Some accounts refer to the venue as Hyderabad Guest House, Delhi, but the commonly recorded venue is Hyderabad House.
262.tq: Use location-based recall while distinguishing the venue from the place represented by the agreement.
xs: The Gentlemen's Agreement was signed at **Hyderabad House, New Delhi** — option **(4)**.
Some notes call it "**Hyderabad Guest House, Delhi**".
xa: Date: **20 February 1956**.
The CMs had agreed to merge at the same venue on **22 Oct 1955**.
Signed by **8 leaders** — **4** from Andhra and **4** from Telangana.

262.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with reference to the signatories associated with the Gentlemen's Agreement?
o: Bezawada Gopala Reddy — Chief Minister, Andhra State
Burgula Ramakrishna Rao — Deputy Chief Minister, Hyderabad State
K.V. Ranga Reddy — Chief Minister, Andhra State
J.V. Narsing Rao — Andhra PCC President
262.x: Bezawada Gopala Reddy was the Chief Minister of Andhra State. Burgula Ramakrishna Rao was Chief Minister of Hyderabad State, K.V. Ranga Reddy was its Deputy Chief Minister, and J.V. Narsing Rao was Hyderabad PCC President.
262.tq: Start from the sure person–office pair and eliminate swapped regional posts.
xs: **Bezawada Gopala Reddy — CM, Andhra State** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Burgula** was **CM** (not Deputy CM) of Hyderabad State; **K.V. Ranga Reddy** was **Deputy CM, Hyderabad**.
**J.V. Narsing Rao** was **Hyderabad PCC President**; the APCC President was **Alluri Satyanarayana Raju**.
xa: Other Andhra signatories: **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** (Deputy CM), **Gouthu Latchanna**.
Other Telangana signatory: **Marri Chenna Reddy** (minister).
⚠ **Tanguturi Prakasam** was **not** a signatory (APPSC GS 2018).

262.s: Which of the following persons was NOT a signatory associated with the Gentlemen's Agreement?
262.x: Tanguturi Prakasam was not a signatory. Gouthu Latchanna, Alluri Satyanarayana Raju and J.V. Narsing Rao were among the listed signatories.
262.tq: Find the one outsider in a list of regional signatories.
xs: **Tanguturi Prakasam** was not a signatory — option **(3)** (APPSC GS 2018).
**Gouthu Latchanna** and **Alluri Satyanarayana Raju** signed for Andhra; **J.V. Narsing Rao** for Telangana.
xa: Andhra: **Bezawada Gopala Reddy**, **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy**, Gouthu Latchanna, Alluri Satyanarayana Raju.
Telangana: **Burgula**, **K.V. Ranga Reddy**, **Marri Chenna Reddy**, J.V. Narsing Rao.
Signed **20 February 1956**, **Hyderabad House, New Delhi**.

262.s: Which one of the following pairs relating to later positions is correctly matched?
o: Burgula Ramakrishna Rao — Governor of Kerala and later Uttar Pradesh
K.V. Ranga Reddy — Governor of Kerala
Marri Chenna Reddy — Minister of Irrigation and Electricity in 1956
J.V. Narsing Rao — Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh in 1978
262.x: Burgula Ramakrishna Rao served as Governor of Kerala from 1956 to 1960 and later as Governor of Uttar Pradesh from 1960 to 1962.
262.tq: Use the swapped-office trap in later-career matching.
xs: **Burgula Ramakrishna Rao** became Governor of **Kerala** (**1956-60**), then **Uttar Pradesh** (**1960-62**) — option **(1)**.
**K.V. Ranga Reddy** became the **First Deputy CM** of Andhra Pradesh.
**J.V. Narsing Rao** was **Irrigation and Electricity** minister (**1956**); **Marri Chenna Reddy** was CM in **1978**.
xa: Chenna Reddy was CM of Andhra Pradesh in **1978** and **1989**.
Burgula was the **first** and **last** elected CM of Hyderabad State.
The first CM of AP was **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy**.

262.s: The Gentlemen's Agreement signed on 20 February 1956 was signed by:
o: 8 leaders, 4 from Andhra and 4 from Telangana
4 leaders, the CMs and Deputy CMs of both states only
262.x: Eight leaders signed, four from each region: Bezawada Gopala Reddy, Neelam Sanjiva Reddy, Gouthu Latchanna and Alluri Satyanarayana Raju for Andhra; Burgula Ramakrishna Rao, K.V. Ranga Reddy, Marri Chenna Reddy and J.V. Narsing Rao for Telangana. The CMs and Deputy CMs were only four of the eight; 6 and 10 are wrong counts.
262.tq: 4 + 4 = 8; Prakasam not among them
xs: **8 leaders, 4 from Andhra and 4 from Telangana** signed — option **(1)**.
Andhra: **Bezawada Gopala Reddy, Neelam Sanjiva Reddy, Gouthu Latchanna, Alluri Satyanarayana Raju**.
Telangana: **Burgula, K.V. Ranga Reddy, Marri Chenna Reddy, J.V. Narsing Rao**.
xa: Venue: **Hyderabad House, New Delhi**.
Not a signatory: **Tanguturi Prakasam**.
It was given backing through **Article 371(1)** and the **1958** Regional Committee Order.

262.s: Which one of the following was NOT a safeguard provided for Telangana under the Gentlemen's Agreement?
o: Sales of agricultural land in Telangana were to be controlled by the Regional Council
All cabinet portfolios were to be permanently reserved for Telangana
Telangana's surplus revenue was to be spent only in Telangana
Urdu was to continue in Telangana's administration and courts for five years
262.x: The agreement did not reserve all cabinet portfolios permanently for Telangana. It provided a 60:40 cabinet arrangement, representation in key portfolios and other regional safeguards.
262.tq: Find the absolute and overextended claim among safeguards that were actually limited or proportionate.
xs: **All cabinet portfolios permanently reserved for Telangana** was not a safeguard — option **(2)**.
The Agreement gave a **60:40** cabinet share and at least **two** key portfolios to Telangana.
Land sales control by the **Regional Council**, **surplus spent only in Telangana**, and **Urdu** for **5 years** were real safeguards.
xa: At least **one Muslim** minister from Telangana.
Education: priority or at least **one-third** of technical seats.
Prohibition was left to **Telangana legislators**.

262.s:
Consider the following statements regarding financial safeguards for Telangana under the Gentlemen's Agreement:
1. Common administrative costs were to be shared proportionately.
2. Telangana's surplus revenue was to be spent only in Telangana.
3. The financial arrangement was to be reviewed after five years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: All three statements are correct. The agreement provided proportionate sharing of common expenditure, exclusive use of Telangana's surplus in Telangana and a review after five years.
262.tq: Check each statement against the separate components of a financial safeguard before selecting the combined option.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: common **administrative expenditure** borne **proportionately**.
Statements 2 and 3: Telangana's **surplus spent only in Telangana**, **reviewed after 5 years**.
xa: Alleged later violation: promise to spend the Telangana surplus only on Telangana was **ignored**.
Fear behind it: Telangana's **revenue surplus** would not be spent on Telangana.
Urdu clause also had a **5-year** term.

262.s: Under the educational safeguards of the Gentlemen's Agreement, Telangana students were to receive which of the following benefits in technical institutions?
o: Admission only through a separate entrance examination
Exactly one-half of all seats irrespective of institutional capacity
Priority in admission or at least one-third of the seats, whichever was more favourable
Admission exclusively in institutions established after 1956
262.x: The agreement protected existing educational facilities and provided Telangana students admission priority or at least one-third of the seats in technical institutions, whichever was more favourable.
262.tq: Match the precise safeguard, especially the alternative wording 'whichever is more favourable'.
xs: Telangana students got **priority in admission or at least one-third of the seats**, whichever was more favourable — option **(3)**.
Existing educational facilities in Telangana were also protected.
xa: Fear: Coastal Andhra's more advanced educational position would dominate.
Domicile rule for recruitment: **12 years** of residence.
Later, **Article 371D** (**32nd Amendment, 1973**) gave equitable opportunities in public employment and education.

262.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Services — Proportionate retrenchment and recruitment according to population ratio under domicile rules
Land — Exclusive power of the Union Government over agricultural sales
Urdu — Abolition from Telangana administration immediately after the agreement
Prohibition — Uniform compulsory prohibition throughout Andhra Pradesh
262.x: The services safeguard provided for recruitment according to population ratio under domicile rules and proportionate retrenchment from both regions. The other pairs contradict the agreed provisions.
262.tq: Start from the sure services pair and eliminate options that reverse or exaggerate the safeguard.
xs: **Services — recruitment by population ratio and proportionate retrenchment** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Land** sales were controlled by the **Regional Council**, not the Union; **Urdu** was kept for **5 years**, not abolished.
**Prohibition** was left to Telangana legislators, not made uniform.
xa: Domicile rule: residence of **12 years** (some notes say 15).
Cabinet: **60:40**; at least **one Muslim** minister from Telangana.
Separate Telangana PCC till **1962**.

262.s: The domicile safeguard associated with recruitment in Telangana required residence for how many years?
262.x: The agreed safeguard referred to Mulki or domicile rules requiring 12 years of residence for recruitment in Telangana.
262.tq: Separate the exact numerical requirement from nearby duration figures used in related provisions.
xs: The domicile safeguard required **12 years** of residence — option **(3)**.
⚠ Some notes say **15 years**; the original **Mulki rules** required about **15 years**.
**5 years** is the Urdu/finance review period; **10 years** the Regional Committee review.
xa: Mulki rules: from **1888**, tightened by the Nizam's farman of **1919**.
Alleged violation: posts reclassified as "**state-cadre**" or "**unreserved**".
The local-cadre system under **Art. 371D** descends from this domicile clause.

262.s:
Consider the following statements about the safeguards for Telangana under the Gentlemen's Agreement (1956):
1. Urdu was to be kept in Telangana's administration and courts for ten years.
2. Sales of agricultural land in Telangana were to be controlled by the Regional Council.
3. The question of prohibition in Telangana was left to the Telangana legislators.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
262.x: Statement 1 is wrong: Urdu was to be kept in Telangana's administration and courts for five years (then reviewed by the Regional Council), not ten. Statement 2 is correct: the Regional Council controlled agricultural land sales in Telangana. Statement 3 is correct: prohibition was left to Telangana legislators. Hence '2 and 3 only'; options with statement 1 (1 and 2, 1 and 3, all three) are wrong.
262.tq: Urdu = 5 years, land = Regional Council, prohibition = Telangana legislators; spot the changed number.
xs: Statements 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 2 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 wrong: **Urdu** was kept in Telangana administration and courts for **5 years**, not ten.
Statement 2: sale of **agricultural land** in Telangana controlled by the **Regional Council**; Statement 3: **prohibition** left to Telangana legislators.
xa: After 5 years the Urdu clause was to be reviewed by the **Regional Council**.
Finance clause also reviewed after **5 years**.
Regional Committee itself was to be reviewed after **10 years**.

262.s: The cabinet composition agreed under the Gentlemen's Agreement was based on which ratio between Andhra and Telangana?
262.x: The finally agreed cabinet share was 60:40 between Andhra and Telangana. It was also provided that at least one Muslim minister would be included from Telangana.
262.tq: Prefer the precise percentage ratio when both a simplified ratio and a rounded formulation may appear in sources.
xs: The cabinet share was **60:40** (Andhra:Telangana) — option **(4)**.
⚠ Older notes print **3:1**; keyed answer = **60:40** (APPSC G2 2025).
xa: Also put as "Telangana at least **40%**".
At least **one Muslim** minister from Telangana.
At least **two** of Home, Finance, Revenue, Planning & Development, Commerce & Industry to Telangana.

262.s:
Consider the following statements about political safeguards under the Gentlemen's Agreement:
1. The Chief Minister and Deputy Chief Minister were to be from different regions.
2. If the Chief Minister belonged to Andhra, the Deputy Chief Minister was to belong to Telangana, and vice versa.
3. At least two among Home, Finance, Revenue, Planning and Development, and Commerce and Industry were to be allotted to Telangana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: All three statements correctly describe the political safeguards. The agreement also provided for at least one Muslim minister from Telangana and a 60:40 cabinet share.
262.tq: Read the political safeguards together and verify both the reciprocal rule and the specified portfolio list.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
CM and **Deputy CM** from **different regions** — if CM from Andhra, Deputy CM from Telangana and vice versa.
At least **two** of **Home, Finance, Revenue, Planning & Development, Commerce & Industry** to Telangana.
xa: ⚠ **Sanjiva Reddy** did not appoint a Deputy CM, calling the post a "**sixth finger**".
Cabinet share **60:40**; at least **one Muslim** minister from Telangana.
The Deputy CM breach fed the **1969 Jai Telangana** agitation.

262.s: Which of the following was the proposed institutional safeguard specifically intended for Telangana?
o: A separate Supreme Court bench with exclusive jurisdiction
A Union Territory administration under the President
A statutory Regional Council or Committee
A permanent bicameral Parliament for Telangana
262.x: The agreement provided for a statutory Regional Council or Committee for Telangana. The other institutions were not part of the agreed safeguards.
262.tq: Identify the institution actually created for regional protection rather than choosing unrelated constitutional bodies.
xs: A **statutory Regional Council or Committee** for Telangana — option **(3)**.
It was given footing under **Article 371(1)** and constituted in **1958**.
xa: Powers: **development planning, irrigation, agriculture, industry, education, public health, recruitment, prohibition**.
Disputes with the state government went to the **Centre**.
The Regional Committee was provided by the **Gentlemen's Agreement** (APPSC GS 2019).

262.s: The separate Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee contemplated under the agreement was to continue up to which year?
262.x: A separate Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee was provided for up to 1962, while the Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee did not object to this arrangement.
262.tq: Use the end-year clue to distinguish a party-organisation safeguard from the broader political provisions.
xs: A separate Telangana PCC was to continue till **1962** — option **(3)**.
The **Andhra PCC** did not object.
xa: **1958** is when the Regional Committee was constituted.
**J.V. Narsing Rao** was the **Hyderabad PCC President** who signed the Agreement.
⚠ The notes count **ten provisions** or **fourteen points** — same content, different grouping.

262.s: The earlier resolution of the Andhra Assembly under Chief Minister Bezawada Gopala Reddy related to giving Telangana priority and population-based allocations in which areas?
o: Defence, foreign affairs, currency and communications
Language, forests, ports and public health only
262.x: The Andhra Assembly resolution supported Telangana priority and population-based allocations in jobs, education, irrigation and development.
262.tq: Recall the complete cluster of subjects rather than selecting a list containing Union subjects.
xs: The resolution gave Telangana priority and population-based allocations in **jobs, education, irrigation and development** — option **(4)**.
It was a **unanimous** resolution under **CM Bezawada Gopala Reddy**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes date it **25 Nov 1953**; it belongs to **1955**, after the SRC report.
The **Andhra Legislature (Kurnool)** later passed the merger unanimously.
Bezawada Gopala Reddy became CM after the **1955** mid-term polls.

262.s:
Consider the following statements about the Telangana Regional Committee:
1. It consisted of elected representatives from Telangana.
2. All Telangana ministers except the Chief Minister were ex officio members.
3. Disputes between the Committee and the State Government were to be referred to the Centre for final decision.
4. Its working was to be reviewed after ten years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: All four statements are correct. The Committee represented Telangana legislators, included Telangana ministers other than the Chief Minister ex officio, referred disputes to the Centre and was subject to review after ten years.
262.tq: Check composition, dispute settlement and review clauses separately before selecting the complete combination.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Members were Telangana legislators; all Telangana ministers **except the CM** were **ex officio** members.
Disputes with the state government went to the **Centre**; review after **10 years**.
xa: Appointed by the **President** under **Article 371(1)**; constituted **1958**.
⚠ Some notes: all elected Telangana MLAs were members.
**1968:** extended for five years; wound up after the **32nd Amendment (1973)**.

262.s: Which of the following was NOT among the subjects assigned to the Telangana Regional Committee?
262.x: The Committee dealt with regional matters such as planning, irrigation, agriculture, industry, recruitment, health, education and prohibition. Foreign affairs was not among its subjects.
262.tq: Find the subject outside the regional administrative and developmental sphere.
xs: **Foreign affairs** was not a Regional Committee subject — option **(4)**.
Its subjects: **development planning, irrigation, agriculture, industry, education, public health, recruitment, prohibition**.
xa: Disputes with the state government → **Centre** for final decision.
Land sales in Telangana were also under Regional Council control.
It was reviewed after **10 years**.

262.s: Which of the following statements regarding the later history of the Telangana Regional Committee is correct?
o: It was extended for five years in 1968 and wound up after the 32nd Amendment in 1973.
It was extended for ten years in 1968 and abolished by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.
It was abolished in 1968 after the 32nd Amendment.
262.x: The Committee was extended for five years in 1968 and was subsequently wound up after the 32nd Amendment in 1973 removed Andhra Pradesh from Article 371(1).
262.tq: Link the extension, constitutional amendment and final consequence in sequence.
xs: It was **extended for five years in 1968** and **wound up after the 32nd Amendment in 1973** — option **(1)**.
The **32nd Amendment** removed AP from **Art. 371(1)**; it did not abolish the Committee in 1968.
xa: The same **32nd Amendment, 1973** (Six-Point Formula) inserted **Article 371D**.
⚠ One note says "**33rd**" — wrong.
The Committee was constituted in **1958**.

262.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the fate of the Deputy Chief Minister’s post under Sanjiva Reddy?
o: Sanjiva Reddy appointed a Telangana Deputy Chief Minister immediately.
Sanjiva Reddy did not appoint a Deputy Chief Minister and described the post as a “sixth finger”.
Sanjiva Reddy retained the post but transferred its powers to the Regional Committee.
The post was abolished by the 32nd Constitutional Amendment before the formation of Andhra Pradesh.
262.x: Sanjiva Reddy did not appoint a Deputy Chief Minister and dismissed the post as a “sixth finger”. This breach contributed to the grievances that led to the 1969 Jai Telangana movement.
262.tq: Use the exact action and quoted description to distinguish the event from later constitutional changes.
xs: **Sanjiva Reddy** did not appoint a Deputy CM and called the post a "**sixth finger**" — option **(2)**.
The Agreement had said the CM and Deputy CM should come from **different regions**.
xa: This breach fed the grievances behind the **1969 Jai Telangana** agitation.
Other alleged violations: non-locals recruited into Telangana posts; Telangana **surplus** not spent in Telangana.
**K.V. Ranga Reddy** is remembered as the **First Deputy CM** of Andhra Pradesh.

262.s: Large-scale recruitment of non-locals into Telangana posts during the late 1950s and 1960s was alleged to violate which provision of the Gentlemen's Agreement?
262.x: The allegation concerned violation of the domicile and employment protection promised to Telangana. Recruitment of non-locals into Telangana posts was cited as the grievance.
262.tq: Match the alleged action with the specific violated clause.
xs: Recruiting non-locals into Telangana posts was alleged to violate the **domicile and employment protection** clause — option **(4)**.
The Agreement reserved Telangana recruitment by residence of **12 years** (Mulki/domicile rule).
xa: Mulki rules were bypassed by reclassifying local posts as "**state-cadre**" or "**unreserved**".
Other alleged violations: Telangana **surplus** not spent in Telangana; **Deputy CM** post not filled.
Root flaw: **political assurances**, not constitutional mandates → **1969 Jai Telangana** agitation.

262.s: Mulki rules were alleged to have been bypassed by:
o: Transferring the capital from Hyderabad to Kurnool
Creating a separate High Court at Guntur
Reclassifying local posts as state-cadre or unreserved posts
262.x: The alleged method of bypassing the Mulki rules was to reclassify local posts as state-cadre or unreserved posts.
262.tq: Identify the administrative device used to evade a protective rule.
xs: Mulki rules were allegedly bypassed by **reclassifying local posts as state-cadre or unreserved** — option **(4)**.
The capital moved from **Kurnool** to **Hyderabad** (not the reverse), and the **Guntur** HC (**1954**) belonged to Andhra State.
xa: Mulki rules: from **1888**, tightened **1919**; residence of about **15 years**.
Agreement domicile period: **12 years** (some notes say 15).
Later fix: **Article 371D** local cadres (**32nd Amendment, 1973**) and the **Presidential Order 1975**.

262.s: Which one of the following was the alleged violation concerning the Telangana revenue surplus?
o: The surplus was to be transferred only to the Union Government but was retained by Telangana.
The surplus was to be spent only on Telangana but this assurance was ignored.
The surplus was to be divided equally between the two High Courts but was used for education.
The surplus was earmarked exclusively for Andhra State but was spent in Hyderabad.
262.x: The Agreement promised that Telangana's revenue surplus would be spent only on Telangana, but this political assurance was alleged to have been ignored.
262.tq: Use the precise promise-versus-violation comparison.
xs: The Telangana **surplus was to be spent only on Telangana**, but this assurance was **ignored** — option **(2)**.
The finance clause also said common administrative costs be borne **proportionately**, reviewed after **5 years**.
xa: Fear behind it: Telangana's **revenue surplus** would not be spent on Telangana.
Separate-Telangana argument: Telangana had higher **per capita income** and **revenue** than Andhra State.
Criticism: safeguards (**Deputy CM post**, **surplus funds**, **Mulki rules**) were weakly enforced.

262.s: The grievance arising from the alleged violations of the Gentlemen's Agreement contributed to which movement?
262.x: The alleged violations, especially concerning employment, domicile and revenue surplus, contributed to the Jai Telangana agitation of 1969.
262.tq: Link the political grievance to its later movement.
xs: The grievance over violations produced the **Jai Telangana agitation of 1969** — option **(1)**.
The **Mulki agitation** was in **1952** (before the Agreement); **Visalandhra** was the pro-merger movement.
xa: Later settlements: **1969 Eight-Point**, **1973 Six-Point**, **371D** built on the Agreement's safeguards.
**Telangana Praja Samithi** formed in **1969** (president **Marri Chenna Reddy**); merged with Congress **Sept 1972**.
Telangana was finally carved out in **2014**.

262.s: Article 371(1) provided constitutional footing to which institution in Andhra Pradesh?
262.x: Article 371(1) gave constitutional footing to the Regional Committee in 1958.
262.tq: Match the constitutional article with the institution it supported.
xs: **Article 371(1)** gave constitutional footing to the **Regional Committee** (**1958**) — option **(1)**.
The **AP Administrative Tribunal** comes under **Article 371D** (**32nd Amendment, 1973**).
xa: The Regional Committee was appointed by the **President**.
**1968:** extended for five years; wound up after the **32nd Amendment** removed AP from Art. 371(1).
Article 371(1) came via the **7th Amendment, 1956**.

262.s:
Consider the following statements about Article 371D:
1. It is associated with the Six-Point Formula.
2. It provides for equitable opportunities in public employment and education.
3. It provides for local cadres and an Andhra Pradesh Administrative Tribunal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: All three are correct: Article 371D, inserted by the 32nd Amendment (1973) to implement the Six-Point Formula, provides equitable opportunities in public employment and education, local cadres and the AP Administrative Tribunal.
262.tq: Test the full scope of a constitutional provision rather than its article number alone.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Article 371D came by the **32nd Amendment, 1973**, implementing the **Six-Point Formula**.
It provides **equitable opportunities in public employment and education**, **local cadres** and the **AP Administrative Tribunal**.
xa: ⚠ One note says "**33rd**" Amendment — wrong.
**Presidential Order 1975**: AP Public Employment (Organisation of Local Cadres and Regulation of Direct Recruitment) Order.
**APRA 2014, Section 97** extended 371D to "the State of Andhra Pradesh or the State of Telangana".

262.s: The Presidential Order of 1975 relating to Andhra Pradesh primarily concerned:
o: Transfer of the Andhra High Court to Amaravati
Creation of a separate Legislative Council for Telangana
Organisation of local cadres and regulation of direct recruitment
Division of the Krishna and Godavari rivers
262.x: The 1975 Presidential Order was the AP Public Employment (Organisation of Local Cadres and Regulation of Direct Recruitment) Order.
262.tq: Identify the official subject of the Presidential Order instead of a neighbouring state issue.
xs: The **Presidential Order 1975** is the AP Public Employment (**Organisation of Local Cadres and Regulation of Direct Recruitment**) Order — option **(3)**.
The High Court moved to **Amaravati** only on **1 Jan 2019**.
xa: It flows from **Article 371D** (**32nd Amendment, 1973**).
**May 2026:** AP Personnel Department finalising mapping of **zones and multi-zones** under this order.
The system traces back to the **1956** Agreement's domicile clause.

262.s: Section 97 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 extended Article 371D to:
o: The State of Andhra Pradesh or the State of Telangana
Only the State of Andhra Pradesh
262.x: Section 97 extended the operation of Article 371D to the State of Andhra Pradesh or the State of Telangana.
262.tq: Test the exact statutory subject and avoid the only-one-successor-state trap.
xs: **Section 97** of **APRA 2014** extended Art. 371D to "**the State of Andhra Pradesh or the State of Telangana**" — option **(1)**.
So it covers both successor states, not only one.
xa: Article 371D: **32nd Amendment, 1973** (Six-Point Formula).
Hyderabad was AP's capital from **1956** until the **2014** bifurcation.
AP Assembly (**28 Mar 2026**) asked the Centre to name **Amaravati** in **Section 5(2)** of APRA 2014.

262.s: Article 371D of the Constitution, relating to Andhra Pradesh, was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment?
262.x: Article 371D was inserted by the 32nd Amendment, 1973, implementing the Six-Point Formula. The 33rd is a common wrong answer (some sources print it); the 31st and 42nd Amendments dealt with other matters.
262.tq: Six-Point Formula -> 32nd Amendment (not 33rd)
xs: Article 371D was inserted by the **32nd Amendment, 1973** — option **(3)**.
⚠ One note prints "**33rd**" — wrong.
xa: It implemented the **Six-Point Formula**.
It provides local cadres and the **AP Administrative Tribunal**.
The same **32nd Amendment** removed AP from **Art. 371(1)**, ending the Regional Committee.

262.s:
With reference to the formation of Andhra Pradesh in 1956, consider the following statements:
1. The 11 districts of Andhra State were merged with the nine Telugu-speaking districts of Hyderabad State.
2. The Kannada-speaking areas of Hyderabad State were transferred to Mysore State.
3. The Marathi-speaking areas of Hyderabad State were transferred to Bombay State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: All three statements are correct. Andhra Pradesh was formed by merging the 11 districts of Andhra State with the nine Telugu-speaking districts of Hyderabad State, while the Kannada and Marathi areas went to Mysore and Bombay respectively.
262.tq: Use the regional-transfer pattern and verify each linguistic area separately.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**11 districts of Andhra State** + **9 Telugu-speaking Telangana districts** formed AP on **1 November 1956**.
**Kannada** areas of Hyderabad went to **Mysore**; **Marathi** areas to **Bombay**.
xa: Law: **States Reorganisation Act, 1956**; basis: **linguistic reorganisation** (APPSC GS 2023).
Andhra State = **Coastal Andhra + Rayalaseema**.
Preceded by the **Gentlemen's Agreement** (**20 Feb 1956**).

262.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the political steps preceding the formation of Andhra Pradesh:
1. The Andhra Legislature met at Kurnool and unanimously resolved in favour of the merger.
2. Both the Andhra and Hyderabad ministries resigned to facilitate the formation of the unified state.
3. The merger was opposed by the Andhra Legislature through a divided vote.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Andhra Legislature unanimously supported the merger at Kurnool, and both ministries resigned; statement 3 is false.
262.tq: Find the single reversal in a question about unanimity and ministerial resignation.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: the **Andhra Legislature (Kurnool)** passed the merger **unanimously**.
Statement 2: **both ministries resigned** in **1956** for the unified state; Statement 3 is false.
xa: Andhra CM at merger: **Bezawada Gopala Reddy**; Hyderabad CM: **Burgula Ramakrishna Rao**.
Hyderabad Assembly vote on the SRC report: **103** for, **29** against, **15** neutral.
First CM of the new state: **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy**.

262.s: Which city became the capital of Andhra Pradesh in 1956, replacing Kurnool?
262.x: Hyderabad became the capital of Andhra Pradesh in 1956, replacing Kurnool, which had served as the capital of Andhra State from 1953 to 1956.
262.tq: Distinguish the new unified-state capital from the earlier Andhra State capital.
xs: **Hyderabad** became AP's capital in **1956**, replacing **Kurnool** — option **(2)**.
Kurnool had been the Andhra State capital (**1953-56**), chosen in the spirit of the **Sri Bagh Pact**.
xa: SRC: Hyderabad would solve Andhra's **permanent-capital** problem.
The Andhra State High Court sat at **Guntur** (**1954**).
Today's capital: **Amaravati**; the **AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, 2026** (Amaravati sole capital) passed the **Lok Sabha**.

262.s: Which of the following was a reason for selecting Hyderabad as the capital of the new Andhra Pradesh?
o: The SRC considered that it would solve Andhra's permanent-capital problem and it had ready administrative infrastructure.
It had already been the capital of Andhra State since 1953.
The Sri Bagh Pact expressly transferred the capital from Hyderabad to Kurnool.
It was the smallest city with limited administrative facilities.
262.x: The SRC noted that Hyderabad could solve Andhra's permanent-capital problem, and it was the largest city with ready administrative infrastructure. Visalandhra Mahasabhas had also demanded Hyderabad as capital.
262.tq: Identify the combined administrative and political rationale rather than a false historical sequence.
xs: The **SRC** said Hyderabad would **solve Andhra's permanent-capital problem**, and it had **ready administrative infrastructure** — option **(1)**.
Andhra State's capital since **1953** was **Kurnool**, not Hyderabad.
Hyderabad was the **largest** city, not the smallest.
xa: The Visalandhra Mahasabhas had demanded Hyderabad as capital.
Kurnool was chosen in the spirit of the **Sri Bagh Pact**.
Hyderabad remained capital until the **2014** bifurcation.

262.s: Who inaugurated Andhra Pradesh on 1 November 1956?
262.x: Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru inaugurated Andhra Pradesh on 1 November 1956, with Hyderabad as its capital.
262.tq: Identify the national leader associated with the inaugural event.
xs: **Jawaharlal Nehru** inaugurated Andhra Pradesh on **1 Nov 1956**, with **Hyderabad** as capital — option **(3)**.
**Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** became the first CM; **Burgula** was the outgoing Hyderabad CM.
xa: First Governor: **C.M. Trivedi**.
Nehru had earlier called Visalandhra "**Andhra imperialism**" (**Oct 1953**).
AP was the first state formed under the **SR Act 1956**.

262.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
262.x: Dasarathi wrote “Enni Naalla Swapnamidi”, while Kaloji wrote “Emaanandam ... Eenadu”.
262.tq: Use author–title discrimination between two contemporaneous literary references.
xs: **Dasarathi** wrote "**Enni Naalla Swapnamidi**" — option **(3)**.
**Kaloji** wrote "**Emaanandam ... Eenadu**"; both celebrated the **1956** formation.
xa: ⚠ **Kaloji** first supported, later opposed the merger.
**Visalandhralo Prajarajyam** (**1946**) = **Sundarayya**.
**The Emergence of Andhra Pradesh** = **K.V. Narayana Rao**.

262.s: With reference to the naming of the state formed on 1 November 1956, which one of the following is correct?
o: The name 'Visalandhra' proposed by the Communists was adopted
The draft Bill's name 'Andhra Telangana' was finally replaced by 'Andhra Pradesh' through the Seventh Amendment Bill in the Lok Sabha
The name 'Andhra Pradesh' was fixed by the Gentlemen's Agreement
The name 'Andhra Telangana' was retained until 1973
262.x: The draft Bill used 'Andhra Telangana' and the Communists proposed 'Visalandhra', but the Seventh Amendment Bill in the Lok Sabha (10 Aug 1956) settled on 'Andhra Pradesh'. The Gentlemen's Agreement did not fix the name, and 'Andhra Telangana' was never the state's name.
262.tq: Draft: Andhra Telangana; CPI: Visalandhra; final: Andhra Pradesh
xs: The draft Bill's "**Andhra Telangana**" was replaced by "**Andhra Pradesh**" through the **7th Amendment Bill** in the Lok Sabha — option **(2)**.
"**Visalandhra**" was the Communists' proposal, not adopted.
xa: Date of the Lok Sabha change: **10 Aug 1956**.
The state was formed on **1 November 1956** under the **SR Act, 1956**.
The **Gentlemen's Agreement** (**20 Feb 1956**) dealt with safeguards, not the name.

262.s: Andhra Pradesh was formed on 1 November 1956 under which law and on what basis?
o: Government of India Act, 1935; religious composition
Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014; economic viability
262.x: AP was formed under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, on the basis of linguistic reorganisation (APPSC GS 2023), merging Andhra State with the Telugu districts of Hyderabad State. The Andhra State Act created Andhra State in 1953; the 1935 Act and APRA 2014 belong to other events.
262.tq: 1 Nov 1956 = SR Act 1956 = language
xs: AP was formed under the **States Reorganisation Act, 1956**, on the basis of **linguistic reorganisation** — option **(2)** (APPSC GS 2023).
**Andhra State** was formed earlier, on **1 Oct 1953**; **APRA 2014** dealt with bifurcation.
xa: It merged **11** Andhra districts with **9** Telangana districts.
AP = the first major linguistic state, uniting Telugu-speaking areas for the first time.
Inaugurated by **Nehru**, **1 Nov 1956**.

262.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched in respect of the first office-holders of Andhra Pradesh formed in 1956?
o: Chief Minister — Neelam Sanjiva Reddy; Governor — C.M. Trivedi
Chief Minister — Bezawada Gopala Reddy; Governor — Burgula Ramakrishna Rao
Chief Minister — Tanguturi Prakasam; Governor — C.M. Trivedi
Chief Minister — Neelam Sanjiva Reddy; Governor — Kashinatha Rao
262.x: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy became the first Chief Minister and C.M. Trivedi was the first Governor of Andhra Pradesh after its formation in 1956.
262.tq: Match each constitutional office with the correct first holder and reject pre-merger office-holders.
xs: First CM **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** and first Governor **C.M. Trivedi** — option **(1)**.
**Bezawada Gopala Reddy** was the last CM of Andhra State; **Prakasam** was its first CM; **Kashinatha Rao** was the Hyderabad Speaker.
xa: First Speaker: **Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao**; Deputy Speaker: **Kalluri Subbarao**.
First Leader of Opposition: **Puchalapalli Sundarayya**.
**C.M. Trivedi** = first Governor of both Andhra State and AP.

262.s: Which one of the following pairs relating to the pre-merger states is NOT correctly matched?
o: Andhra State — Bezawada Gopala Reddy as Chief Minister at the time of merger
Andhra State — Laxmi Narasimham as Speaker at the time of merger
Hyderabad State — Burgula Ramakrishna Rao as Chief Minister at the time of merger
Hyderabad State — Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao as Speaker at the time of merger
262.x: The pair in option d is incorrect. Kashinatha Rao was the Speaker of Hyderabad State at the time of merger; Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao became the first Speaker of Andhra Pradesh.
262.tq: Identify the wrong office-holder by distinguishing pre-merger Speakers from the first Speaker of the unified state.
xs: **Hyderabad State — Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao as Speaker** is wrong — option **(4)**.
Hyderabad State's Speaker was **Kashinatha Rao**; Kaleswara Rao became the **first Speaker of AP**.
The rest are right: Andhra — **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** (CM), **Laxmi Narasimham** (Speaker); Hyderabad — **Burgula** (CM).
xa: Kaleswara Rao founded the **Visalandhra Mahasabha** (**1949**).
Burgula headed the elected government of **1952**.
First Council Chairman: **Madapati Hanumantha Rao**.

262.s: Who was the first Leader of the Opposition in the newly formed Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly?
262.x: Puchalapalli Sundarayya was the first Leader of the Opposition in the newly formed Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly.
262.tq: Use office-specific recall rather than confusing party and ministerial positions.
xs: **Puchalapalli Sundarayya** was the first Leader of Opposition — option **(1)**.
⚠ First Speaker = **Kaleswara Rao** (Mahasabha founder); first Leader of Opposition = **Sundarayya** (coined Visalandhra).
xa: Sundarayya later became first General Secretary of **CPI(M) (1964)**.
**1962** elections: Congress **177** seats; Communists over **50**.
**K.V. Ranga Reddy** = First Deputy CM of AP.

262.s: The first Chairman of the Legislative Council of Andhra Pradesh was:
262.x: Madapati Hanumantha Rao was the first Chairman of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council.
262.tq: Separate the Council chairmanship from Assembly speakership.
xs: **Madapati Hanumantha Rao** was the first Legislative Council Chairman — option **(2)**.
**Kalluri Subbarao** was Deputy Speaker; **Kaleswara Rao** the Speaker; **J.V. Narsinga Rao** a minister.
xa: The Council was constituted in **1958** with **90** members under **N. Sanjiva Reddy**.
Madapati Hanumantha Rao called the Visalandhra idea **50 years** old (**1954**).
First Governor: **C.M. Trivedi**.

262.s: The Congress strength in the newly formed Andhra Pradesh was calculated as:
o: 79 seats from Telangana and 140 from Andhra, totalling 219
40 seats from Andhra and 119 from Hyderabad, totalling 159
40 seats from Hyderabad and 119 from Andhra, totalling 159
90 seats from Hyderabad and 79 from Andhra, totalling 169
262.x: The Congress had 40 seats from Hyderabad in 1952 and 119 from Andhra in 1955, giving a total strength of 159.
262.tq: Check both components and the total instead of accepting a reversed regional figure.
xs: Congress had **40** seats from **Hyderabad** (**1952**) + **119** from **Andhra** (**1955**) = **159** — option **(3)**.
Option (2) swaps the regions; **79** was the 1957 Telangana poll and **90** the Council size.
xa: **1957:** elections only in Telangana — **79** members.
**1962:** Congress **177** seats.
**1983:** TDP **202** seats — first non-Congress government.

262.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with a portfolio in the first Andhra Pradesh cabinet?
o: Kasu Brahmananda Reddy — Irrigation and Electricity
262.x: Bezawada Gopala Reddy held the Finance portfolio. D. Sanjivayya handled Labour, Kasu Brahmananda Reddy Local Bodies, J.V. Narsinga Rao Irrigation and Electricity, and Mehdi Nawaz Jung Cooperation.
262.tq: Use the swapped-portfolio trap among members of the same cabinet.
xs: **Bezawada Gopala Reddy — Finance** is correct — option **(1)**.
**D. Sanjivayya** = **Labour**; **Kasu Brahmananda Reddy** = **Local Bodies**; **J.V. Narsinga Rao** = **Irrigation and Electricity**; **Mehdi Nawaz Jung** = **Cooperation**.
xa: CM: **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** (Srikalahasti, Chittoor).
Sanjivayya became CM on **11 Jan 1960**; Brahmananda Reddy in **1964**.
Mehdi Nawaz Jung had backed Visalandhra (educated Muslim support).

262.s: In 1957, the second general elections for the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly were held only in:
o: Both regions simultaneously with equal seats
262.x: The second general elections in 1957 were held only in the Telangana region, where 79 members were elected.
262.tq: Test the regional limitation of an election rather than the total-state assumption.
xs: The **1957** elections were held only in the **Telangana region** — option **(2)**.
**79** members were elected.
xa: Andhra had already voted in the **1955** mid-term polls (Congress **119**).
Hyderabad's Congress members dated from **1952** (**40**).
**1962:** Congress **177** seats; Communists over **50**.

262.s: The Legislative Council of Andhra Pradesh was constituted in 1958 with:
262.x: The Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council was constituted in 1958 with 90 members during the tenure of N. Sanjiva Reddy.
262.tq: Separate the Council's membership figure from Assembly and regional election figures.
xs: The Legislative Council was constituted in **1958** with **90** members — option **(2)**.
It was under CM **N. Sanjiva Reddy**; first Chairman **Madapati Hanumantha Rao**.
xa: **79** = members elected in Telangana (**1957**).
**159** = Congress strength at formation.
**1958** is also when the **Regional Committee** was constituted.

262.s: The High Court of Andhra Pradesh began sitting at Hyderabad from:
262.x: With the formation of the new state, the High Court of Andhra Pradesh sat at Hyderabad from 5 November 1956.
262.tq: Distinguish the state's formation date from the High Court's actual sitting date.
xs: The High Court of AP sat at **Hyderabad** from **5 Nov 1956** — option **(4)**.
**1 November 1956** was the state's formation day, not the High Court's.
xa: **Andhra State HC**: **1954**, at **Guntur**.
After bifurcation it moved to **Amaravati** on **1 Jan 2019**.
Hyderabad was capital from **1956** until **2014**.

262.s: After bifurcation, the High Court of Andhra Pradesh moved to Amaravati on:
262.x: After bifurcation, the Andhra Pradesh High Court moved to Amaravati on 1 January 2019.
262.tq: Use close-date discrimination for post-bifurcation institutional changes.
xs: The AP High Court moved to **Amaravati** on **1 January 2019** — option **(3)**.
It had sat at **Hyderabad** from **5 Nov 1956**.
xa: Andhra State HC: **1954**, **Guntur**.
**2026:** AP capital **Amaravati**; Governor **S. Abdul Nazeer**.
AP Assembly (**28 Mar 2026**) asked to name **Amaravati** in **Section 5(2)** of APRA 2014.

262.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Establishment of the Andhra State High Court at Guntur
B. High Court of Andhra Pradesh began functioning at Hyderabad
C. Common High Court for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
D. Separate High Court of Andhra Pradesh began functioning at Amaravati
262.x: The sequence is 1954, 1956, 2014–2018 and 1 January 2019 respectively.
262.tq: Fix the first and last dates, then place the formation of Andhra Pradesh and the common court between them.
xs: Correct order is **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**Guntur** (**1954**) → **Hyderabad** (**5 Nov 1956**) → common High Court after the **2014** bifurcation → **Amaravati** (**1 Jan 2019**).
xa: Guntur HC belonged to **Andhra State** (formed **1 Oct 1953**, capital **Kurnool**).
AP was formed on **1 November 1956**.
**APRA 2014, Section 97** extended Art. 371D to both successor states.

262.s: Who served as Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh immediately before the imposition of President’s Rule in January 1973?
262.x: P.V. Narasimha Rao served as Chief Minister from 1971 until President’s Rule began on 18 January 1973.
262.tq: Use the tenure boundary to distinguish adjacent Chief Ministers.
xs: **P.V. Narasimha Rao** (**1971-73**) was CM just before **President's Rule** (**18 Jan-10 Dec 1973**) — option **(2)**.
**Kasu Brahmananda Reddy** preceded him (**1964-71**); **Jalagam Vengala Rao** came after (**1973-78**).
xa: PVNR later became **Prime Minister** (**1991-96**).
**Marri Chenna Reddy** followed Vengala Rao on **6 Mar 1978**.
PYQ order (2025): **Sanjivayya → Brahmananda Reddy → PVNR → Anjaiah**.

262.s: Which Chief Minister was in office when the Telugu Desam Party was founded on 29 March 1982?
262.x: The Telugu Desam Party was founded on 29 March 1982 during the tenure of Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy.
262.tq: Place the party’s founding date within the correct Chief Ministerial tenure.
xs: The TDP was founded on **29 March 1982** during **Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy**'s tenure — option **(1)** (APPSC G2 2019).
Bhavanam was CM **24 Feb-20 Sep 1982**; **Kotla** followed, and **NTR** came only in **Jan 1983**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes print **29 May 1982** — wrong.
TDP won **202** seats in **1983**, within about **nine months** of founding.
**T. Anjaiah** preceded Bhavanam (**1980-82**).

262.s: Who was the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh immediately before N.T. Rama Rao assumed office in January 1983?
262.x: Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy served from 20 September 1982 until January 1983, immediately before N.T. Rama Rao became Chief Minister.
262.tq: Use the last pre-1983 succession link to identify the correct office-holder.
xs: **Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy** (**20 Sep 1982-Jan 1983**) was CM just before NTR — option **(2)**.
**Bhavanam** preceded Kotla; **Nadendla** came after NTR (**16 Aug-16 Sep 1984**).
xa: NTR sworn in **9 Jan 1983** at **Lal Bahadur Stadium**.
**4 CMs in 4 years** (Chenna Reddy, Anjaiah, Bhavanam, Kotla) → fatigue that helped the TDP.
Kotla was CM again in **1992-94**.

262.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding Damodaram Sanjivayya?
1. He was the second Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh.
2. He became Chief Minister on 11 January 1960.
3. He later became President of the Indian National Congress.
4. He was never defeated in an election.
262.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is incorrect; the claim that Damodaram Sanjivayya was never defeated in an election is the false statement.
262.tq: Identify the incorrect biographical claim among several true details.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**Damodaram Sanjivayya** was the **second CM** of AP, from **11 Jan 1960**, and later **AICC President**.
Statement 4 wrong: "**never defeated in an election**" is the incorrect statement (APPSC G2 2008).
xa: He was India's first **Dalit (Harijan) CM**.
He was **Labour** minister in the first AP cabinet.
⚠ **AICC President** = both **Sanjiva Reddy** (1960) and **Sanjivayya**.

262.s:
Consider the following statements about Chief Ministers of united Andhra Pradesh:
1. Nadendla Bhaskara Rao had the shortest tenure, about 31 days in August-September 1984.
2. N.T. Rama Rao had the longest continuous tenure as Chief Minister, from 1983 to 1989.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
262.x: Statement 1 is correct: Nadendla Bhaskara Rao served 31 days (16 Aug-16 Sep 1984), the shortest tenure. Statement 2 is wrong: the longest continuous tenure in united AP was N. Chandrababu Naidu's (1995-2004); NTR's spell was broken by Nadendla in 1984. So '1 only' is right; '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' are wrong.
262.tq: Shortest = Nadendla (31 days, 1984); longest continuous = Naidu (1995-2004).
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: **Nadendla Bhaskara Rao** had the **shortest tenure — 31 days** (Aug-Sep **1984**).
Statement 2 wrong: the **longest continuous tenure** was **N. Chandrababu Naidu** (**1995-2004**); NTR's spell was broken by Nadendla in **1984**.
xa: Nadendla was sworn in **16 Aug 1984** under Governor **Ram Lal**; NTR restored **16 Sep 1984**.
**First non-Congress CM**: **N.T. Rama Rao** (**1983**).
Nadendla died in Hyderabad, **April 2026**, aged **90**.

262.s:
Which of the following statements about the early political history of Andhra Pradesh is correct?
1. All Chief Ministers up to January 1983 belonged to the Congress.
2. N.T. Rama Rao was the first non-Congress Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh.
3. Congress rule continued uninterrupted from 1956 until 1983.
4. The first non-Congress Chief Minister was Nadendla Bhaskara Rao.
262.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because N.T. Rama Rao, not Nadendla Bhaskara Rao, was the first non-Congress Chief Minister.
262.tq: Reject the swapped-person trap in a political succession statement.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
All CMs up to **Jan 1983** were Congress; rule was uninterrupted **1956** to **1983** (APPSC G2 2008).
**N.T. Rama Rao** (**1983**) was the first non-Congress CM, so statement 4 (**Nadendla**) is wrong.
xa: **1983** ended over **26 years** of Congress rule.
TDP won **202** seats in **1983**.
Nadendla had been NTR's **Deputy CM** before his **1984** takeover.

262.s: Which group of four Chief Ministers represents the successive administrations through which Congress changed four Chief Ministers in four years before the rise of the Telugu Desam Party?
o: M. Chenna Reddy, T. Anjaiah, Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy and Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy
Jalagam Vengala Rao, P.V. Narasimha Rao, M. Chenna Reddy and N.T. Rama Rao
Kasu Brahmananda Reddy, P.V. Narasimha Rao, T. Anjaiah and N.T. Rama Rao
M. Chenna Reddy, Nadendla Bhaskara Rao, Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy and Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy
262.x: The four Congress Chief Ministers were M. Chenna Reddy, T. Anjaiah, Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy and Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy. Their rapid succession contributed to political fatigue before the TDP emerged.
262.tq: Select the complete and correctly ordered succession set.
xs: The four were **M. Chenna Reddy, T. Anjaiah, Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy and Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy** — option **(1)**.
Their rapid succession created fatigue that helped the **TDP**.
**NTR** and **Nadendla** were not part of this Congress run; **Vengala Rao** and **PVNR** came earlier.
xa: Chenna Reddy: **6 Mar 1978**; Anjaiah: **11 Oct 1980**; Bhavanam: **24 Feb 1982**; Kotla: **20 Sep 1982**.
**1 Jan 1978:** **Indira Gandhi** formed **Congress (I)**.
TDP founded **29 March 1982**.

262.s:
Arrange the following Chief Ministers in chronological order of assuming office:
A. Jalagam Vengala Rao
B. M. Chenna Reddy
C. T. Anjaiah
D. Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy
262.x: Jalagam Vengala Rao assumed office in 1973, followed by M. Chenna Reddy in 1978, T. Anjaiah in 1980 and Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy in February 1982.
262.tq: Arrange the administrations using their tenure years and transition dates.
xs: Correct order is **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**Jalagam Vengala Rao** (**1973**) → **Chenna Reddy** (**6 Mar 1978**) → **T. Anjaiah** (**1980**) → **Bhavanam** (**24 Feb 1982**).
xa: Vengala Rao followed **President's Rule** (**18 Jan-10 Dec 1973**).
**Kotla** followed Bhavanam on **20 Sep 1982**.
Chenna Reddy was CM again in **1989-90**.

262.s: Who was the first Dalit Chief Minister in India, taking office in Andhra Pradesh on 11 January 1960?
262.x: Damodaram Sanjivayya, the second CM of Andhra Pradesh, became India's first Dalit CM on 11 January 1960 and later became AICC President. Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was AP's first CM (1956-60); Brahmananda Reddy (1964) and Anjaiah (1980) came later.
262.tq: Sanjivayya: 2nd AP CM, 1st Dalit CM, later AICC President
xs: **Damodaram Sanjivayya** became India's first **Dalit CM** on **11 Jan 1960** — option **(1)**.
**Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** was AP's first CM (**1956-60**); **Brahmananda Reddy** (**1964**) and **Anjaiah** (**1980**) came later.
xa: Sanjivayya was the **second CM** of AP and later **AICC President**.
⚠ Trap: "never defeated in an election" is the incorrect statement about him.
Sanjiva Reddy returned as CM in **1962-64**.

262.s:
Arrange the following Chief Ministers of Andhra Pradesh in the order in which they first took office (PYQ 2025):
1. P.V. Narasimha Rao
2. Damodaram Sanjivayya
3. T. Anjaiah
4. Kasu Brahmananda Reddy
262.x: Sanjivayya (1960), Kasu Brahmananda Reddy (1964), P.V. Narasimha Rao (1971), T. Anjaiah (1980). Putting Brahmananda Reddy before Sanjivayya, PVNR before Brahmananda Reddy, or Anjaiah before PVNR breaks the order.
xs: Correct order is **2, 4, 1, 3** — option **(1)**.
**Sanjivayya** (**1960**) → **Kasu Brahmananda Reddy** (**1964**) → **P.V. Narasimha Rao** (**1971**) → **T. Anjaiah** (**1980**).
xa: Brahmananda Reddy's 2nd term began **6 Mar 1967**.
President's Rule: **18 Jan-10 Dec 1973**, after PVNR.
Anjaiah: **11 Oct 1980-Feb 1982**.

262.s: Who formed the Congress (I) on 1 January 1978?
262.x: Indira Gandhi formed Congress (I) on 1 January 1978, while Brahmananda Reddy led the rival Reddy Congress.
262.tq: Distinguish the founder of a faction from the leader of the rival faction.
xs: **Indira Gandhi** formed **Congress (I)** on **1 Jan 1978** — option **(1)**.
**Brahmananda Reddy** led the rival **Reddy Congress**.
xa: **1978** elections: Congress (I) under **Chenna Reddy**.
**Madan Mohan** was convener of the **Telangana Praja Samithi** (**1969**).
**26 Feb 1984:** Chenna Reddy formed the **National Democratic Party**.

262.s: The three-tier Panchayat Raj system was implemented in Andhra Pradesh on 1 November 1959 under which Chief Minister?
262.x: The three-tier Panchayat Raj system was implemented in Andhra Pradesh on 1 November 1959 under N. Sanjiva Reddy. Rajasthan was the first State to implement it on 2 October 1959.
262.tq: Separate the Andhra implementation date and Chief Minister from the earlier Rajasthan milestone.
xs: Panchayat Raj came to AP on **1 Nov 1959** under **N. Sanjiva Reddy** — option **(2)**.
⚠ **Rajasthan** was first (**2 Oct 1959**); AP second.
xa: Based on the **Balwant Rai Mehta** report, approved by the **NDC** in **1958**.
NTR introduced the **Mandal system** from **1985**.
The Legislative Council (**1958**, **90** members) was also under Sanjiva Reddy.

262.s: The Balwant Rai Mehta report was associated with which institutional development?
o: Implementation of the three-tier Panchayat Raj system
Reservation of 44 per cent seats for Backward Classes
Introduction of the Mandal system in Andhra Pradesh
262.x: The Balwant Rai Mehta report, considered by the National Development Council in 1958, was associated with the three-tier Panchayat Raj system.
262.tq: Identify the institutional reform linked to a committee report rather than a later NTR-era measure.
xs: The **Balwant Rai Mehta** report led to the **three-tier Panchayat Raj** system — option **(2)**.
The **Mandal system** was NTR's (from **1985**); **44%** BC reservation was an NTR social measure.
xa: **NDC** considered it in **1958**.
Rajasthan **2 Oct 1959**; AP **1 Nov 1959**.
NTR was chairman of the **National Front**.

262.s: Which one of the following correctly describes NTR-era local-body reforms?
o: The Mandal system was introduced from 1985, and a two-thirds majority was newly prescribed in 1983.
The Mandal system was introduced from 1978, and no-confidence motions were abolished in 1983.
The Mandal system was introduced in 1983, and a three-fourths majority was substituted in 1985.
The Mandal system was introduced from 1985, and a simple majority was allowed for specified no-confidence motions in 1983.
262.x: NTR introduced the Mandal system from 1985 and, in 1983, permitted a simple majority for no-confidence motions against Zilla Parishad vice-chairmen instead of the earlier two-thirds majority.
262.tq: Compare the old and new majority requirements while keeping the two reform years distinct.
xs: NTR introduced the **Mandal system from 1985** and in **1983** allowed a **simple majority** for no-confidence motions against **Zilla Parishad** vice-chairmen — option **(4)**.
The earlier requirement had been **two-thirds**, so (1) reverses it.
xa: Three-tier Panchayat Raj in AP: **1 Nov 1959**.
NTR initiatives: **Rs 2/kg rice** (**14 Apr 1983**), **Dharma Mahamatra** (first holder **N. Vittal**).
**44%** BC reservation and equal property rights for daughters.

262.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: 1957 — Elections in Telangana only, covering 79 seats
1989 — TDP formed the first non-Congress government
262.x: The 1957 elections were held only in Telangana and covered 79 seats. The 1962, 1978 and 1989 results have been incorrectly interchanged in the other options.
262.tq: Find the accurately paired year and election detail among reversed party results.
xs: **1957 — elections in Telangana only, 79 seats** is correct — option **(2)**.
**202** seats was the TDP in **1983**, not 1962; Congress won **177** in **1962**.
**1978** = Congress (I) under Chenna Reddy; **1989** = TDP defeated, Congress returned.
xa: **1985:** TDP won the mid-term polls.
First non-Congress government: TDP, **1983**.
Congress strength at formation: **159**.

262.s:
Consider the following statements regarding elections in Andhra Pradesh:
1. In 1962, Congress won 177 seats and the Communists won more than 50 seats.
2. In 1978, Congress (I) came to power under Chenna Reddy.
3. In 1985, the Telugu Desam Party won the mid-term election.
4. In 1989, the Telugu Desam Party was defeated and Congress returned.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: All four statements correctly state the recorded election outcomes for 1962, 1978, 1985 and 1989.
262.tq: Verify the sequence of party victories and defeats across successive elections.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**1962**: Congress **177**, Communists over **50**; **1978**: Congress (I) under **Chenna Reddy**.
**1985**: TDP won the mid-term; **1989**: TDP defeated, Congress returned.
xa: Mid-term polls of **28 Dec 1984** followed the 1984 crisis; NTR sworn in again **9 Mar 1985**.
**1957:** only Telangana voted (**79** seats).

262.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the first electoral performance of the Telugu Desam Party?
o: It won 202 seats in 1985 and formed the first Congress government.
It won 177 seats in 1983 and formed a coalition government.
It won 202 seats in 1983 and formed the first non-Congress government in Andhra Pradesh.
It won 79 seats in 1983, all from Telangana.
262.x: The Telugu Desam Party won 202 seats in the 1983 election and formed the first non-Congress government in Andhra Pradesh.
262.tq: Use the distinctive seat tally and the political consequence together to reject swapped election results.
xs: The TDP **won 202 seats in 1983** and formed the **first non-Congress government** — option **(3)**.
**177** was Congress's 1962 tally; **79** the 1957 Telangana poll.
xa: TDP founded by **NTR** on **29 March 1982**; won within about **nine months**.
Campaign: **Telugu self-respect** (Telugu Atma Gauravam), "**Chaitanya Ratham**".
NTR sworn in **9 Jan 1983**, cabinet of **15**; **Nadendla** Deputy CM.

262.s: Who among the following was the Deputy Chief Minister in N.T. Rama Rao’s initial cabinet?
262.x: Nadendla Bhaskara Rao served as Deputy Chief Minister in N.T. Rama Rao’s initial cabinet.
262.tq: Test the office-holder directly while using nearby Andhra political figures as plausible distractors.
xs: **Nadendla Bhaskara Rao** was **Deputy CM** in NTR's first cabinet (**9 Jan 1983**) — option **(2)**.
**Chenna Reddy**, **Sanjivayya** and **Sanjiva Reddy** were earlier Congress CMs, not NTR's ministers.
xa: NTR's first cabinet had **15** members, sworn in at **Lal Bahadur Stadium**.
⚠ **Nadendla** = Deputy CM (**1983**) → CM for **31 days** (**1984**) under Governor **Ram Lal**.
Nadendla later formed the **Democratic Telugu Desam** (**1984**).

262.s: Who was the first holder of the office of Dharma Mahamatra, associated with the anti-corruption initiative during the NTR period?
262.x: N. Vittal was the first holder of the Dharma Mahamatra office associated with the anti-corruption initiative.
262.tq: Match an unusual office title with its first office-holder.
xs: The first **Dharma Mahamatra** (anti-corruption) was **N. Vittal** — option **(4)** (APPSC G2 2017).
**Madan Mohan** was the **Telangana Praja Samithi** convener (**1969**); **Nadendla** was NTR's Deputy CM.
xa: Other NTR measures: **Rs 2/kg rice** (**14 Apr 1983**), **15-point development plan** (**10 Apr 1983**).
Ban on private practice by government doctors: **28 Apr 1983**.
First **Women's University** at **Tirupati**.

262.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the first Women’s University associated with the NTR period?
262.x: Tirupati had the first Women’s University referred to in the NTR-era reforms.
262.tq: Test the exact location of a named institutional initiative.
xs: The first **Women's University** of the NTR period was at **Tirupati** — option **(4)**.
It was one of NTR's initiatives after the **1983** victory.
xa: **Dharma Mahamatra**: first holder **N. Vittal**.
Social measures: **equal property rights for daughters**, **44%** BC reservation.
**Sri Rama Pada Sagar** (stage II): foundation **5 May 1983**.

262.s:
Consider the following statements regarding social and educational reforms during the NTR period:
1. Equal property rights for daughters were included among the social initiatives.
2. A 44 per cent reservation was provided for Backward Classes.
3. A Buddha statue was installed in Hussain Sagar.
4. Vocational education was introduced in schools.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: All four statements are listed among the social and educational initiatives of the NTR era.
262.tq: Treat each item in a reform list as an independent statement before choosing the complete combination.
xs: All four are NTR-era measures — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Equal property rights for daughters** and **44%** **BC reservation**.
**Buddha statue in Hussain Sagar** and **vocational education in schools**.
xa: First **Women's University**: **Tirupati**.
From **1985**: **Mandal system** introduced.

262.s:
Consider the following statements about the Telugu Desam Party:
1. It was founded by N.T. Rama Rao on 29 May 1982.
2. Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy was Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh when it was founded.
3. It campaigned on the slogan of Telugu self-respect (Telugu Atma Gauravam), using the 'Chaitanya Ratham'.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the TDP was founded on 29 March 1982, not 29 May (a known misprint). Statement 2 is correct (APPSC G2 2019). Statement 3 is correct. So '2 and 3 only'; every option containing statement 1 is wrong.
262.tq: TDP: 29 March 1982, under CM Bhavanam
xs: Statements 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 2 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 wrong: TDP was founded on **29 March 1982**; **29 May 1982** is a known misprint.
Statement 2: CM at the time was **Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy** (APPSC G2 2019); Statement 3: **Telugu Atma Gauravam** slogan with the "**Chaitanya Ratham**".
xa: TDP won **202** seats in **1983**, about **nine months** after founding.
NTR sworn in **9 Jan 1983**; first non-Congress CM.
Bhavanam's tenure: **24 Feb-20 Sep 1982**.

262.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the political crisis of August–September 1984:
1. Governor Ram Lal dismissed N.T. Rama Rao’s government while NTR was in the United States for medical treatment.
2. Nadendla Bhaskara Rao was sworn in as Chief Minister on 16 August 1984.
3. Nadendla Bhaskara Rao resigned on 16 September 1984, after which N.T. Rama Rao was restored.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: All three statements are correct. The dismissal by Governor Ram Lal led to Nadendla Bhaskara Rao’s short-lived ministry and NTR’s restoration after Nadendla resigned.
262.tq: Link the governor’s action, the replacement ministry and the restoration in a single event sequence.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
With NTR in the **US** for treatment, Governor **Ram Lal** dismissed his government (**Aug 1984**).
**Nadendla** sworn in **16 Aug 1984**; after a statewide agitation he resigned and NTR was restored on **16 Sep 1984**.
xa: Nadendla's **31 days** = the **shortest tenure** of any AP CM.
It was the first **coup-style takeover** in the state.
Outcome: **anti-defection law** (**52nd Amendment, 1985**).

262.s: The 1984 dismissal of N.T. Rama Rao’s government was widely regarded as which of the following in Andhra Pradesh politics?
o: The first division of the ruling party
The first coalition experiment in the State
The first coup-style takeover in the State
The first invocation of President’s Rule in the State
262.x: The dismissal and replacement of NTR’s government in August 1984 was described as the first coup-style takeover in the State.
262.tq: Identify the exact political characterisation rather than a broadly related constitutional event.
xs: The **1984** episode was the **first coup-style takeover** in the state — option **(3)**.
President's Rule had already been used in AP (**18 Jan-10 Dec 1973**), so it was not the first President's Rule.
xa: Governor **Ram Lal** dismissed NTR's government while he was in the US.
Nadendla sworn in **16 Aug 1984**; NTR restored **16 Sep 1984**.
It is a textbook case of **Governor's discretion misused**, shaping **Sarkaria Commission** debates.

262.s: Which constitutional development was associated with the political crisis involving N.T. Rama Rao and Nadendla Bhaskara Rao?
262.x: The episode contributed to the anti-defection law enacted through the 52nd Constitutional Amendment in 1985.
262.tq: Match the political consequence with the correct constitutional amendment number and year.
xs: The crisis led to the **anti-defection law** — the **52nd Amendment, 1985** — option **(1)**.
It followed **Nadendla Bhaskara Rao**'s **1984** takeover with defecting legislators.
xa: NTR sworn in again on **9 Mar 1985** after the **28 Dec 1984** mid-term polls.
Other constitutional links in this topic: **Article 371D** (**32nd Amendment, 1973**).
⚠ "33rd" for 371D is a known wrong answer.

262.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. N.T. Rama Rao was sworn in again as Chief Minister.
B. Nadendla Bhaskara Rao was sworn in as Chief Minister.
C. Indira Gandhi was assassinated.
