D. Mid-term elections were held.
262.x: Nadendla Bhaskara Rao was sworn in on 16 August 1984, Indira Gandhi was assassinated on 31 October, mid-term polls were held on 28 December, and NTR was sworn in again on 9 March 1985.
262.tq: Fix the first event by its August date and then distinguish the October, December and March events.
xs: Correct order is **B, C, D, A** — option **(1)**.
**Nadendla** sworn in (**16 Aug 1984**) → **Indira Gandhi** assassinated (**31 Oct 1984**) → mid-term polls (**28 Dec 1984**) → NTR sworn in again (**9 Mar 1985**).
xa: NTR was restored on **16 Sep 1984** before the mid-term polls.
The **1985** swearing-in was NTR's **3rd**.
TDP won the **1985** mid-term; it was defeated in **1989**.

262.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Leader)
a. Neelam Sanjiva Reddy
b. P.V. Narasimha Rao
c. Damodaram Sanjivayya
d. N.T. Rama Rao
List-II (National office)
i. Prime Minister of India
ii. Chairman, National Front
iii. President of India
iv. AICC President

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
262.x: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was President of India, P.V. Narasimha Rao was Prime Minister, Damodaram Sanjivayya was AICC President, and N.T. Rama Rao was Chairman of the National Front.
262.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes containing a swapped national office.
xs: Correct match: **a–iii, b–i, c–iv, d–ii** — option **(1)**.
**Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** = **President of India**; **P.V. Narasimha Rao** = **Prime Minister**.
**Damodaram Sanjivayya** = **AICC President**; **N.T. Rama Rao** = Chairman, **National Front**.
xa: Sanjiva Reddy was elected President in **1977**; AICC President in **1960**.
⚠ **AICC President** = both **Sanjiva Reddy** and **Sanjivayya**.
PVNR was Prime Minister **1991-96**.

262.s: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was elected President of India in which year?
262.x: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was elected President of India in 1977. He had earlier served as AICC President in 1960.
262.tq: Separate the year of the national constitutional office from the year of party leadership.
xs: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was elected **President of India** in **1977** — option **(3)**.
**1960** was when he became **AICC President**.
xa: He was the **only Janata candidate** to win in AP in **1977**.
He was the **first CM** of Andhra Pradesh (**1956-60**) and again **1962-64**.
Panchayat Raj came to AP under him (**1 Nov 1959**).

262.s: Which statement is correct regarding Neelam Sanjiva Reddy’s 1977 electoral significance?
o: He was elected Chairman of the National Front in 1977.
He won the first election to the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly in 1977.
He was the only Congress candidate to win in Andhra Pradesh in 1977.
He was the only Janata candidate to win in Andhra Pradesh in 1977.
262.x: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was the only Janata candidate to win in Andhra Pradesh in the 1977 election.
262.tq: Use the party label and state-specific distinction to catch a reversed political association.
xs: In **1977** Sanjiva Reddy was the **only Janata candidate to win in Andhra Pradesh** — option **(4)**.
The **National Front** chairman was **N.T. Rama Rao**.
xa: He was elected **President of India** the same year (**1977**).
He was AICC President in **1960**.
As CM he did not appoint a Deputy CM, calling it a "**sixth finger**".

262.s: The Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956 is significant because it
o: adapted the Sribagh Pact model of settling regional apprehensions through a moral agreement
replaced the Constitution with a regional pact for Telangana
abolished the Mulki rules throughout Hyderabad State
provided for the immediate creation of a separate Telangana State
262.x: The Gentlemen's Agreement followed the Sribagh Pact's approach of addressing regional fears through a moral and political understanding rather than through a constitutional settlement.
262.tq: Identify the central significance rather than a later consequence.
xs: The Agreement **repeated the Sribagh Pact model** — settling regional fears by a **moral pact** — option **(1)**.
It did not create a separate Telangana or abolish Mulki rules; it protected **Mulki/domicile** recruitment.
xa: It was the written basis of the **1956** merger.
Later settlements: **1969 Eight-Point**, **1973 Six-Point**, **371D**.
**Kurnool** was chosen as Andhra State's capital in the spirit of the **Sri Bagh Pact**.

262.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the safeguards associated with the formation of Andhra Pradesh:
1. Telangana apprehensions during 1953–56 contributed to the inclusion of written safeguards.
2. The safeguards possessed complete constitutional enforcement.
3. Their later dilution contributed to the 1969 agitation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The safeguards were political assurances and lacked constitutional enforcement, so statement 2 is false.
262.tq: Find the one overstatement among otherwise precise historical statements.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: apprehensions of **1953-56** meant the merger came with **written safeguards**.
Statement 2 wrong: they were **political assurances without constitutional teeth**; Statement 3: their dilution led to the **1969** agitation.
xa: Weakly enforced safeguards: **Deputy CM post**, **surplus funds**, **Mulki rules**.
The **Regional Committee** alone got backing under **Art. 371(1)** (**1958**).
Telangana was carved out in **2014**.

262.s: Which of the following safeguards associated with the Gentlemen's Agreement was considered weakly enforced and later became a focus of regional discontent?
o: The abolition of the State Legislature, land revenue and taxation
The replacement of Telugu by Urdu as the official language
The creation of a separate Governor, High Court and Public Service Commission
The Deputy Chief Minister post, surplus funds and Mulki rules
262.x: The Deputy Chief Minister provision, protection of surplus funds and the Mulki rules were among the safeguards regarded as inadequately enforced.
262.tq: Use a grouped-list question to identify the complete set of related safeguards.
xs: The **Deputy CM post**, **surplus funds** and **Mulki rules** were weakly enforced — option **(4)**.
Urdu was to be kept for **5 years** in Telangana, not to replace Telugu.
xa: **Sanjiva Reddy** did not appoint a Deputy CM ("**sixth finger**").
Mulki rules bypassed by reclassifying posts as "**state-cadre**" or "**unreserved**".
Result: the **1969 Jai Telangana** agitation.

262.s:
Consider the following statements about the later constitutional and administrative legacy of the Gentlemen's Agreement:
1. The Eight-Point Formula of 1969 was connected with the later Telangana settlement process.
2. The Six-Point Formula of 1973 was unrelated to regional safeguards.
3. Article 371D and local-cadre arrangements reflect the legacy of the Agreement's domicile-related protection.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The Six-Point Formula of 1973 was also part of the subsequent regional-safeguard framework, making statement 2 false.
262.tq: Separate a genuine institutional legacy from a reversed description.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 3 only**.
Later settlements — **1969 Eight-Point**, **1973 Six-Point**, **371D** — build on the Agreement's safeguards.
Statement 2 wrong: the **Six-Point Formula** led to **Article 371D** (**32nd Amendment, 1973**), a regional safeguard.
xa: AP's local-cadre and zonal recruitment under **Art. 371D** descends from the domicile clause.
**Presidential Order 1975** organised local cadres.
**May 2026:** zones and multi-zones being re-mapped.

262.s:
With reference to recent political statements concerning the merger and bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. K. T. Rama Rao blamed the Congress for merging Telangana with Andhra Pradesh despite the Fazal Ali Commission's recommendation.
2. Tejasvi Surya compared the 2014 division with Partition in a parliamentary remark.
3. The latter remark led to protests in Telangana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: All three statements are correct. K. T. Rama Rao made the criticism in January 2026, while Tejasvi Surya's April 2026 remark drew protests in Telangana.
262.tq: Combine closely related current-affairs statements and verify each name, event and consequence.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**BRS** leader **K.T. Rama Rao** (**Jan 2026**) blamed Congress for the merger despite the **Fazal Ali Commission**'s recommendation.
**BJP** MP **Tejasvi Surya**'s **April 2026** remark compared the **2014** division with Partition → protests in Telangana.
xa: Protests in Telangana: **5 Jan** and **17 Apr 2026**.
The SRC (**Fazl Ali**) had recommended Telangana as a **separate state first**.
The SRC wanted merger only with **two-thirds** of the Telangana legislature.

262.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation is correctly matched?
o: Capital — Amaravati; Governor — S. Abdul Nazeer; Chief Minister — N. Chandrababu Naidu
Capital — Hyderabad; Governor — K. T. Rama Rao; Chief Minister — Tejasvi Surya
Capital — Amaravati; Governor — N. Chandrababu Naidu; Chief Minister — S. Abdul Nazeer
Capital — Kurnool; Governor — Nadendla Bhaskara Rao; Chief Minister — K. Pawan Kalyan
262.x: The current Andhra Pradesh capital is Amaravati, and the Governor and Chief Minister are S. Abdul Nazeer and N. Chandrababu Naidu respectively.
262.tq: Start with the sure office-holder and check whether the capital and remaining offices align.
xs: **Capital Amaravati**, **Governor S. Abdul Nazeer**, **CM N. Chandrababu Naidu** — option **(1)**.
**Hyderabad** was capital only till **2014**; **K.T. Rama Rao** is a **BRS** leader; **Pawan Kalyan** is **Deputy CM**.
xa: Naidu heads the **NDA** coalition (**Jun 2026**).
Naidu had the longest continuous tenure in united AP (**1995-2004**).
The AP High Court moved to **Amaravati** on **1 Jan 2019**.

262.s:
Consider the following developments concerning Amaravati and the capital of Andhra Pradesh:
1. The Andhra Pradesh Assembly passed a resolution on 28 March 2026 requesting that Amaravati be named in Section 5(2) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.
2. The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, 2026 making Amaravati the sole capital was passed by the Lok Sabha in June 2026.
3. The amendment made Hyderabad the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The 2026 amendment concerned making Amaravati the sole capital, not Hyderabad, so statement 3 is false.
262.tq: Catch the reversed capital claim in the final statement.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: AP Assembly resolved on **28 Mar 2026** to name **Amaravati** in **Section 5(2)** of **APRA 2014**.
Statement 2: the **AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, 2026** (Amaravati sole capital) passed the **Lok Sabha** in **Jun 2026**; Statement 3 wrong — it was **Amaravati**, not Hyderabad.
xa: Hyderabad was capital from **1956** until the **2014** bifurcation.
Before Hyderabad, **Kurnool** was the Andhra State capital (**1953-56**).
The AP High Court sits at **Amaravati** since **1 Jan 2019**.

262.s: The dismissal of N. T. Rama Rao's government in 1984 is significant in Indian constitutional discussions because it
o: became a textbook example of the alleged misuse of gubernatorial discretion and influenced later Sarkaria Commission debates
resulted directly in the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh in 2014
established the first linguistic state in India
abolished the office of Governor in Andhra Pradesh
262.x: The 1984 dismissal is cited as a classic instance of gubernatorial discretion being misused, and it contributed to later debate examined by the Sarkaria Commission.
262.tq: Distinguish the constitutional significance of an event from its later political consequences.
xs: The **1984** dismissal is a textbook case of **Governor's discretion misused**, shaping later **Sarkaria Commission** debates — option **(1)**.
It had nothing to do with the **2014** bifurcation or the first linguistic state (AP itself, **1956**).
xa: Governor: **Ram Lal**; NTR was in the **US** for treatment.
Nadendla's **31 days** (**16 Aug-16 Sep 1984**).
It led to the **52nd Amendment, 1985** (anti-defection law).

262.s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents the political leadership of Andhra Pradesh in June 2026?
o: N. Chandrababu Naidu as Chief Minister and K. Pawan Kalyan as Deputy Chief Minister
K. Pawan Kalyan as Chief Minister and N. Chandrababu Naidu as Deputy Chief Minister
Nadendla Bhaskara Rao as Chief Minister and K. T. Rama Rao as Deputy Chief Minister
S. Abdul Nazeer as Chief Minister and N. Chandrababu Naidu as Deputy Chief Minister
262.x: In June 2026, N. Chandrababu Naidu was Chief Minister heading the NDA coalition, with K. Pawan Kalyan as Deputy Chief Minister.
262.tq: Separate constitutional office-holders from political coalition partners and the Governor.
xs: **N. Chandrababu Naidu** CM and **K. Pawan Kalyan** Deputy CM — option **(1)** (**Jun 2026**).
Naidu (TDP) heads the **NDA** coalition; **S. Abdul Nazeer** is Governor, not CM.
xa: Capital: **Amaravati**.
**Nadendla Bhaskara Rao** died in Hyderabad in **April 2026**, aged **90**.
Naidu's first long term: **1995-2004**.

263.s:
Under Article 3 of the Constitution, Parliament may by law:
1. Form a new State.
2. Increase or diminish the area of a State.
3. Alter the boundaries or name of a State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: Article 3 empowers Parliament to form new States and to increase or diminish the area, alter the boundaries, or change the name of any State.
263.tq: Test the full constitutional power list by checking whether any item has been wrongly excluded.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Under **Article 3**, Parliament may **by law** **form a new state**, **increase/diminish** its area, and **alter the boundaries or name** of a state.
xa: **Article 2** = admission of new states/territory from outside (e.g., **Sikkim**, **36th Amendment**).
**Article 4**: such a law is **not an amendment** under **Article 368**.
The **AP Reorganisation Act 2014** was made under **Article 3**.

263.s: A law made under Article 3 for reorganisation of States is passed by Parliament by:
o: A two-thirds majority of all State Legislatures
263.x: A law under Article 3 requires only a simple majority in Parliament and is not a constitutional amendment under Article 368 by virtue of Article 4.
263.tq: Discriminate between the simple-majority procedure and the special-majority procedure for constitutional amendments.
xs: An Article 3 law is passed by a **simple majority** — option **(2)**.
By **Article 4** it is **not an amendment under Article 368**, so no special majority is needed.
xa: The bill needs the **President's prior recommendation**.
The President **refers** it to the affected state legislature; its views are **not binding**.
Time limit for views added by the **5th Amendment 1955**.

263.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Article 2 — Admission or establishment of new States
Article 2 — Alteration of the name of an existing State
Article 3 — Admission of a foreign territory as a new State
Article 4 — Laws under Articles 2 and 3 deemed amendments under Article 368
263.x: Article 2 deals with the admission or establishment of new States. Article 3 concerns the formation or alteration of existing States, while Article 4 excludes such laws from being treated as amendments under Article 368.
263.tq: Separate the closely related Articles 2, 3 and 4 instead of relying on the common word ‘State’.
xs: **Article 2 — admission or establishment of new States** is correct — option **(1)**.
Changing a state's **name** is under **Article 3**, not Article 2; Article 3 does not deal with admitting foreign territory.
**Article 4** says such laws are **not** amendments under **Article 368** — option (4) reverses it.
xa: Example of Art. 2: **Sikkim** (**36th Amendment**).
⚠ Trap: some notes say APRA 2014 was under **Article 2** — wrong; it was **Article 3**.
Art. 3 bills pass by **simple majority**.

263.s: Is a reference to a Union Territory Legislature required when Parliament considers a Bill under Article 3?
o: Only with the approval of the Supreme Court
No, Article 3 requires reference only to the affected State Legislature, not to a Union Territory Legislature
Yes, but only when its boundaries are altered
263.x: No reference to a Union Territory Legislature is required under Article 3. The constitutional reference is to the Legislature of the affected State.
263.tq: Identify the exception to the State Legislature reference requirement.
xs: **No** — Article 3 needs reference only to the **affected State legislature**, not to a Union Territory legislature — option **(2)**.
Notes: views **not binding**; no fresh reference for each amendment to the bill; **no reference for a UT**.
xa: Introduction only on the **President's recommendation**.
Time limit for views added by the **5th Amendment 1955**.
Passed by **simple majority**.

263.s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 was enacted primarily under which Article of the Constitution of India?
263.x: The Act was enacted under Article 3, which empowers Parliament to form a new State out of an existing State. Article 2 deals with admission or establishment of new States.
263.tq: Distinguish the closely related constitutional provisions rather than relying on the subject of the legislation alone.
xs: APRA 2014 was enacted under **Article 3** — option **(1)**.
With **Arts. 3 and 4**, **no Art. 368 amendment** was needed.
⚠ **Article 2** deals with admitting new states/territory from outside — a common wrong answer.
xa: President's assent: **1 March 2014**; appointed day **2 June 2014**.
Telangana became the **29th state**.
Structure: **12 Parts, 108 Sections, 13 Schedules**.

263.s:
Consider the following statements regarding a Bill under Article 3:
1. It can be introduced only on the recommendation of the President.
2. The President refers it to the affected State legislature for its views.
3. The views of the State legislature are binding on Parliament.
4. It is passed by a simple majority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The views of the affected State legislature are sought but are not binding on Parliament.
263.tq: Identify the non-binding consultation statement among procedural conditions.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 4 only**.
Statement 1: introduced only on the **President's recommendation**; Statement 2: referred to the **affected state legislature**; Statement 4: **simple majority**.
Statement 3 wrong: the state legislature's views are **not binding**.
xa: Time limit for views: **5th Amendment 1955**.
No reference is needed for a **UT**.
Criticism of APRA 2014: passed **without the state assembly's consent**.

263.s: The provision requiring the State Legislature to express its views on an Article 3 Bill within a period specified by the President was added by the
263.x: The time limit for the affected State Legislature to express its views on an Article 3 Bill was added by the 5th Amendment, 1955. The 1st Amendment (1951) dealt with other matters, the 7th Amendment (1956) implemented the States reorganisation, and the 36th Amendment (1975) made Sikkim a State.
263.tq: Art 3 reference time limit = 5th Amendment 1955; views are still not binding.
xs: The time limit for the state's views was added by the **5th Amendment, 1955** — option **(2)**.
The **36th Amendment** relates to **Sikkim** (Art. 2 admission), not Article 3 procedure.
xa: The views remain **not binding** on Parliament.
No fresh reference is needed for each amendment to the bill.
**Article 4**: such laws are not Art. 368 amendments.

263.s: Bombay State was bifurcated into Maharashtra and Gujarat in 1960 mainly following the:
o: Akali Dal and Punjabi Suba movements
263.x: The Samyukta Maharashtra and Mahagujarat movements led to the division of Bombay State into Maharashtra and Gujarat on 1 May 1960.
263.tq: Match a reorganisation outcome with the movements that demanded it.
xs: Bombay was split into **Maharashtra and Gujarat** (**1960**) after the **Samyukta Maharashtra and Mahagujarat** movements — option **(1)**.
The law was the **Bombay Reorganisation Act 1960**.
xa: It was a **linguistic** reorganisation, like Andhra **1953**.
**1966:** **Punjab Reorganisation Act** created **Haryana**.
**1963:** **Nagaland**, first NE state with full statehood.

263.s: The Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966 resulted in which of the following arrangements?
o: Punjab was divided into three States, with Chandigarh transferred to Delhi.
Punjab and Haryana were created; Chandigarh became a Union Territory and shared capital.
Haryana and Gujarat were created; Chandigarh became part of Maharashtra.
Punjab was merged with Himachal Pradesh; Chandigarh became the sole capital of Haryana.
263.x: The 1966 reorganisation divided Punjab into Punjab and Haryana, while Chandigarh was made a Union Territory and served as their shared capital.
263.tq: Test the complete institutional consequence rather than only the names of the new States.
xs: The **Punjab Reorganisation Act 1966** created **Haryana**; **Chandigarh** became a **UT** and **joint capital** — option **(2)**.
Punjab's hill areas went to **Himachal Pradesh**.
xa: ⚠ HP became a **state** only in **1971**, not **1966**.
**Gujarat** came from Bombay in **1960**, not from Punjab.
Ascending order (APPSC 2018 key): AP (**1953/56**) → Haryana (**1966**) → Chhattisgarh (**2000**) → Telangana (**2014**).

263.s: Which one of the following states was created in 1963 and was the first North-Eastern state to receive full statehood?
263.x: Nagaland became a state in 1963 and was the first North-Eastern state granted full statehood. The State of Nagaland Act was enacted in 1962.
263.tq: Separate the year of the Act from the year of state inauguration.
xs: **Nagaland** (**1963**) was the first NE state to get full statehood — option **(4)**.
Its Act is the **State of Nagaland Act 1962**; some notes date it to 1962.
**Manipur, Tripura, Meghalaya** came in **1972**; **Mizoram** in **1987**.
xa: Nagaland was the first NE state carved out of **Assam** (APPSC 2025).
It was formed on an **ethnic/tribal** basis.
**1971** NE Areas (Reorganisation) Act made **Mizoram** and **Arunachal** UTs.

263.s: Which of the following states became a full-fledged state in 1971 under the State of Himachal Pradesh Act, 1970?
263.x: Himachal Pradesh attained statehood on 25 January 1971 under the State of Himachal Pradesh Act, 1970.
263.tq: Use the Act year and statehood year as a paired chronology clue.
xs: **Himachal Pradesh** became a state on **25 Jan 1971** under the **State of Himachal Pradesh Act 1970** — option **(4)**.
**Haryana** dates from **1966**; **Meghalaya** from **1972**.
xa: ⚠ In **1966** HP only got Punjab's **hill areas**.
**Chandigarh** became a UT and joint capital in **1966**.
**Goa** became a state in **1987**.

263.s:
Arrange the following states in chronological order of their formation:
A. Gujarat
B. Nagaland
C. Haryana
D. Himachal Pradesh
263.x: Gujarat was formed in 1960, Nagaland in 1963, Haryana in 1966 and Himachal Pradesh in 1971.
263.tq: Place the first and last events, then resolve the middle years.
xs: Correct order is **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
xa: **1972:** Manipur, Tripura, Meghalaya.
**1987:** Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa.
**2000:** Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand, Jharkhand.

263.s: Manipur, Tripura and Meghalaya attained statehood in 1972 under which enactment?
263.x: Manipur, Tripura and Meghalaya became states in 1972 under the North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971.
263.tq: Start from the sure law-state association.
xs: **Manipur, Tripura and Meghalaya** became states in **1972** under the **North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971** — option **(2)**.
The same Act made **Mizoram** and **Arunachal** UTs.
xa: Mizoram and Arunachal became states in **1987** (Acts of **1986**).
**Meghalaya** = ethnic/tribal basis.
**Nagaland Act 1962** → statehood **1963**.

263.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Arunachal Pradesh — State of Arunachal Pradesh Act, 1986
263.x: Sikkim became a state in 1975 through the 36th Constitutional Amendment. The other three pairs are correctly matched with the relevant Acts.
263.tq: Find the mismatched law-state pair rather than relying only on the year.
xs: **Sikkim — State of Sikkim Act, 1987** is wrong — option **(1)**.
Sikkim came in under **Article 2** through the **36th Amendment**.
**Goa** (State of Goa Act **1987**), **Arunachal** and **Mizoram** (Acts of **1986**) are correctly matched.
xa: All three of Mizoram, Arunachal and Goa became states in **1987**.
**Article 3** covers forming states from existing ones.
**2019:** J&K and Ladakh became UTs.

263.s: Goa became a state in which year?
263.x: Goa became a state in 1987 under the State of Goa Act, 1987.
263.tq: Separate Goa’s 1987 statehood from the 1986 Acts relating to Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh.
xs: **Goa** became a state in **1987** — option **(3)** (State of Goa Act **1987**).
**1986** is the year of the Mizoram and Arunachal Acts; **2000** the year of Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand, Jharkhand.
xa: **Mizoram** and **Arunachal Pradesh** also became states in **1987**.
Current count: **28 states and 8 UTs**.
**Telangana** (**2014**) is the **29th** state created at the time.

263.s:
Arrange the following states in the order of their formation:
A. Chhattisgarh
B. Uttarakhand
C. Jharkhand
D. Telangana
263.x: Chhattisgarh was formed on 1 November 2000, Uttarakhand on 9 November 2000, Jharkhand on 15 November 2000 and Telangana on 2 June 2014.
263.tq: Use the day-month sequence for the three states formed in 2000 before placing Telangana.
xs: Correct order is **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**Chhattisgarh (1 Nov 2000)** → **Uttarakhand (9 Nov 2000)** → **Jharkhand (15 Nov 2000)** → **Telangana (2 June 2014)**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes give **8 Nov 2000** for Uttarakhand.
The **2000** states came from **MP, UP, Bihar** Reorganisation Acts.
They were based on **tribal/regional backwardness**, not language.

263.s: According to the commonly cited date, Uttarakhand was formed on:
263.x: The commonly cited date for the formation of Uttarakhand is 9 November 2000. Some other reference material gives 8 November, making this an important date distinction.
263.tq: Handle conflicting close dates by identifying the convention specified in the question.
xs: Uttarakhand was formed on **9 November 2000** — option **(3)**.
⚠ Some notes give **8 Nov 2000**.
**1 Nov 2000** = Chhattisgarh; **15 Nov 2000** = Jharkhand.
xa: Uttarakhand was carved from **UP**.
Basis: **regional backwardness/administrative**, like **Telangana**.
1 November is also AP's formation day (**1956**).

263.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the bases of state formation:
1. Andhra Pradesh was associated with the linguistic principle.
2. Nagaland was associated with an ethnic or tribal basis.
3. Telangana was associated with regional backwardness and administrative considerations.
4. The states created in 2000 were formed solely on linguistic grounds.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the 2000 states were created on grounds of tribal and regional backwardness, not language.
263.tq: Reject the extreme word 'solely' while comparing different bases of reorganisation.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**Andhra** = **linguistic**; **Nagaland** = **ethnic/tribal**; **Telangana** = **regional backwardness/administrative**.
Statement 4 wrong: the **2000** states were created on **tribal and regional backwardness**, **not language**.
xa: Other ethnic/tribal states: **Meghalaya**, **Jharkhand**, **Chhattisgarh**.
Linguistic: Andhra **1953**, the **1956** wave, Maharashtra-Gujarat **1960**.
Newer basis: **size + governance** (mega-states like **UP**, **240 million+**).

263.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (State or group)
a. Andhra State
b. Maharashtra and Gujarat
c. Nagaland
d. Telangana

List-II (Year)
i. 1960
ii. 1963
iii. 1953
iv. 2014

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
263.x: Andhra State was formed in 1953; Maharashtra and Gujarat in 1960; Nagaland in 1963; and Telangana in 2014.
263.tq: Start from the sure state-year pair and eliminate codes containing a misplaced year.
xs: Correct match: **a–iii, b–i, c–ii, d–iv** — option **(1)**.
**Andhra State** **1953**; **Maharashtra and Gujarat** **1960**; **Nagaland** **1963**; **Telangana** **2014**.
xa: ⚠ Nagaland's Act is of **1962**; statehood **1963**.
Telangana was born on **2 June 2014**.

263.s: The formation of Maharashtra and Gujarat in 1960 was associated with which legislation?
263.x: Maharashtra and Gujarat were formed in 1960 under the Bombay Reorganisation Act.
263.tq: Match the State formation with the correct legislation.
xs: Maharashtra and Gujarat were formed under the **Bombay Reorganisation Act 1960** — option **(3)**.
The **Punjab Reorganisation Act** (**1966**) created Haryana; the **SR Act** was **1956**.
xa: Movements behind it: **Samyukta Maharashtra** and **Mahagujarat**.
It was a **linguistic** reorganisation.
Pending demand from Maharashtra: **Vidarbha**.

263.s: Which of the following States were created in 2000 primarily on grounds of regional backwardness rather than language?
263.x: Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand and Jharkhand were created in 2000, with regional backwardness being an important consideration rather than linguistic identity.
263.tq: Use the basis of reorganisation to distinguish the 2000 States from linguistic States.
xs: **Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand and Jharkhand** (**2000**) were based on **tribal/regional backwardness**, not language — option **(3)**.
**Maharashtra, Gujarat** (**1960**) were linguistic; **Mizoram, Goa, Arunachal** came in **1987**.
xa: Dates: Chhattisgarh **1 Nov 2000**, Uttarakhand **9 Nov 2000**, Jharkhand **15 Nov 2000**.
Parent states: **MP, UP, Bihar**.
**Telangana** also falls under regional backwardness/administrative basis.

263.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Formation of Andhra Pradesh
B. Formation of Telangana
C. Formation of Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Uttarakhand
D. Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh became Union Territories
263.x: Andhra Pradesh was formed in 1956, the three States in 2000, Telangana in 2014, and Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh became Union Territories in 2019.
263.tq: Use the decade gaps to establish the sequence from 1956 through 2019.
xs: Correct order is **A, C, B, D** — option **(1)**.
**AP** (**1956**) → **Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand** (**2000**) → **Telangana** (**2014**) → **J&K and Ladakh UTs** (**2019**).
xa: J&K and Ladakh became UTs from **31 October 2019** under the **J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019**.
J&K's **Legislative Council** was abolished; **Ladakh** has no legislature.
Common **High Court of J&K and Ladakh**.

263.s: Telangana came into existence as the 29th State of India on
263.x: Telangana was formed on 2 June 2014 under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, as the 29th State. The other dates are distractors: 1 November is the old AP formation day and 2 October is Gandhi Jayanti.
263.tq: Telangana = 2 June 2014 = 29th State.
xs: Telangana became the **29th state** on **2 June 2014** — option **(2)**.
**1 November** is AP's old formation day (**1956**).
xa: President's assent to APRA: **1 March 2014** (APPSC 2025 key).
⚠ Trap: "came into effect **2 March 2014**" is wrong.
**Section 10**: First Schedule entry **"29. Telangana"**.

263.s: Which one of the following is NOT listed among the active demands for the creation of new states?
263.x: Vidarbha, Gorkhaland and Bundelkhand are listed as active demands. Konkan is not included in that list.
263.tq: Find the outsider in a list of named regional statehood demands.
xs: **Konkan** is not among the listed active demands — option **(2)**.
Listed: **Vidarbha, Harit Pradesh, Purvanchal, Bodoland, Saurashtra, Gorkhaland, Bundelkhand**.
xa: Gorkhaland is handled through the **GTA** (**2011**).
**Subhash Ghisingh** founded the **GNLF** in **1980**.
Newer basis for states: **size + governance**.

263.s: The demand for Gorkhaland is handled institutionally through the:
263.x: The Gorkhaland demand is handled through the Gorkhaland Territorial Administration (GTA).
263.tq: Match the regional demand with its specific administrative mechanism.
xs: Gorkhaland is now handled through the **Gorkhaland Territorial Administration** (**GTA**, **2011**) — option **(1)**.
Earlier body: **Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council** (**1988**).
xa: **1907:** **Darjeeling Hillmen's Association** sought separation from Bengal.
**1980:** **Subhash Ghisingh** founded **GNLF**, coined "Gorkhaland".
**Bodoland** is a separate pending demand.

263.s: Which of the following was identified as a newer basis for considering the creation of states?
o: Replacement of all regional languages by Hindi
Size and governance concerns relating to mega-states
Exclusive conversion of Union Territories into states
263.x: Size and governance are identified as newer considerations, since very large states such as Uttar Pradesh may become unwieldy to administer.
263.tq: Apply the governance rationale to the example of a mega-state.
xs: The newer basis is **size and governance** of **mega-states** — option **(2)**.
States like **UP** (**240 million+**) are seen as unwieldy (**Feb 2026**).
xa: Older bases: **linguistic**, **ethnic/tribal**, **regional backwardness/administrative**.
Active demands include **Harit Pradesh**, **Purvanchal** and **Bundelkhand** (from UP's regions among others).
**Telangana** and **Uttarakhand** = regional backwardness.

263.s: Who founded the Gorkha National Liberation Front and coined the term ‘Gorkhaland’?
263.x: Subhash Ghisingh founded the GNLF in 1980 and coined the term ‘Gorkhaland’.
263.tq: Match the movement, organisation and founder without confusing them with later administrative bodies.
xs: **Subhash Ghisingh** founded the **GNLF** (**1980**) and coined "**Gorkhaland**" — option **(1)** is correct.
The demand goes back to the **Darjeeling Hillmen's Association**, which sought separation from **Bengal** in **1907**.
xa: **Gorkhaland** is one of the active demands, with **Vidarbha**, **Bodoland** and **Bundelkhand**.
**1988:** **Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council**.
**2011:** **Gorkhaland Territorial Administration** (GTA).

263.s:
Arrange the following developments in the Gorkhaland movement in chronological order:
A. Formation of the Gorkhaland Territorial Administration
B. Demand by the Darjeeling Hillmen’s Association
C. Foundation of the GNLF and coinage of ‘Gorkhaland’
D. Formation of the Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council
263.x: The sequence is 1907 demand, 1980 foundation of the GNLF and coinage of ‘Gorkhaland’, 1988 formation of the Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council, and 2011 formation of the Gorkhaland Territorial Administration.
263.tq: Place the first demand and final administrative arrangement first and last, then order the two intermediate developments.
xs: Correct order is **B, C, D, A** — option **(1)**.
**Darjeeling Hillmen's Association** (**1907**) → **GNLF** (**1980**) → **Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council** (**1988**) → **GTA** (**2011**).
xa: GNLF founder: **Subhash Ghisingh**.
The GTA is the **current** mechanism handling the demand.
Other pending demands: **Vidarbha**, **Bodoland**, **Saurashtra**.

263.s:
Match the State with the principal basis of its formation:
a. Andhra (1953)
b. Meghalaya
c. Uttarakhand
1. Regional backwardness / administrative
2. Linguistic
3. Ethnic / tribal
263.x: Andhra (1953) was the first linguistic State; Meghalaya (like Nagaland, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh) was formed on an ethnic/tribal basis; Uttarakhand (like Telangana) on regional backwardness/administrative grounds. The other codes mix up these bases.
263.tq: Linguistic = Andhra; tribal = Nagaland/Meghalaya/Jharkhand/Chhattisgarh; backwardness = Uttarakhand/Telangana.
xs: Correct match: **a-2, b-3, c-1** — option **(1)**.
**Andhra (1953)** = **linguistic**; **Meghalaya** = **ethnic/tribal**; **Uttarakhand** = **regional backwardness/administrative**.
xa: Other ethnic/tribal: **Nagaland**, **Jharkhand**, **Chhattisgarh**.
Other regional/administrative: **Telangana**.
Meghalaya became a state in **1972**.

263.s: The Mulki rules originated in:
263.x: The Mulki rules originated in Hyderabad State in 1888, during the rivalry between Mulki and non-Mulki groups in the Nizam's bureaucracy.
263.tq: Test the origin by matching the rule with its original State and year.
xs: The Mulki rules originated in **Hyderabad State in 1888** — option **(1)**.
They came out of the **Mulki vs non-Mulki** rivalry in the Nizam's bureaucracy (**Salar Jung II** era).
xa: **1919 Nizam's Farman** made them stricter.
Nizam's rules = **15 years** of residence.
The Mulki question runs from **1888 to 2014**.

263.s: Under the original Mulki rules of 1888, an outsider could be appointed to a State post only with the permission of the:
263.x: The 1888 rules reserved State posts for local residents, while an outsider required the permission of the Prime Minister, or Diwan, for appointment.
263.tq: Use the authority-holder trap in an administrative-history question.
xs: An outsider needed the permission of the **Prime Minister (Diwan)** — option **(1)**.
From **1919** the stricter rule required the **Nizam's personal permission**.
xa: Purpose: local residents to get **State posts**.
Origin: **1888**, **Salar Jung II** era.
The **1919** Farman aimed to curb **unemployment among locals**.

263.s: The 1919 Nizam's Farman made the Mulki rules stricter by requiring outsiders to obtain:
o: A certificate from the Girglani Commission
The personal permission of the Nizam
The approval of the Hyderabad Legislative Council
The permission of the Prime Minister of India
263.x: The 1919 Farman required outsiders to obtain the Nizam's personal permission, strengthening the protection of local employment.
263.tq: Separate the 1888 Diwan-permission rule from the stricter 1919 requirement.
xs: The **1919 Nizam's Farman** required outsiders to get the **Nizam's personal permission** — option **(2)**.
The **Girglani Commission** came only in **2001**.
xa: Under the **1888** rules, the **Prime Minister (Diwan)** gave permission.
Aim: curb **unemployment among locals**.
Mulki = **15 years** continuous residence (Nizam's rules).

263.s: In the context of the Nizam's Mulki rules, the term 'Mulki' referred to a person who had:
o: Served in the Nizam's army for fifteen years
Obtained a recommendation from a local zamindar
Completed a fixed period of continuous residence in the State
Been born only in Hyderabad city
263.x: A Mulki was defined as a person who had completed a fixed period of continuous residence in the State. Under the Nizam's rules, the period was 15 years.
263.tq: Distinguish a residence qualification from birth, service or official recommendation.
xs: A **Mulki** was a person with a **fixed period of continuous residence** in the State — option **(3)**.
Under the Nizam's rules the period was **15 years**.
xa: ⚠ **15 years** = Nizam's rules; **12 years** = Gentlemen's Agreement (some notes give 15).
**Oct 1972:** Supreme Court upheld the Mulki Rules (**Director of Industries v. V. Venkata Reddy**).
**1973:** Mulki Rules repealed under the **Six-Point Formula**.

263.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Nizam's Mulki rules from the domicile proposal associated with the Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956?
o: The Nizam's rules referred to 12 years' residence, whereas the 1956 proposal referred to 15 years' residence only.
The Nizam's rules referred to 15 years' residence, whereas the 1956 proposal referred to 12 years' residence.
Neither system used residence as a qualification.
263.x: The Nizam's rules used a 15-year continuous residence requirement, while the 1956 Gentlemen's Agreement suggested domicile rules such as 12 years' residence.
263.tq: Compare the two closely related residence requirements instead of merging them into one rule.
xs: Nizam's rules: **15 years**; Gentlemen's Agreement: **12 years** — option **(2)**.
Option (1) reverses the two figures.
xa: ⚠ Some notes give **15 years** for the Agreement too.
Gentlemen's Agreement signed **20 Feb 1956**.
**1969 Jai Telangana** sought implementation of Mulki safeguards.

263.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with an alleged violation of the 1956 safeguards?
1. Mulki rules — Recruitment of non-locals in large numbers
2. Revenue surplus — Diversion away from Telangana
3. Telangana Regional Committee — Safeguards could not be enforced in court
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
263.x: All three pairs are correct: non-locals were alleged to have been recruited, Telangana’s revenue surplus was allegedly diverted, and the political safeguards were considered unenforceable in court.
263.tq: Match each safeguard with its corresponding alleged violation before selecting the code.
xs: All three pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Mulki rules**: non-locals recruited in large numbers; **Revenue surplus**: diverted, fiscal centralisation.
**Regional Committee**: safeguards were political promises and **could not be enforced in court**.
xa: Local posts were reclassified as "**state-cadre**"/"**unreserved**".
Flashpoint (**1968**): sub-committee extended for **five years**; Centre asked to extend Mulki rules.
Result: **Jai Telangana** (**1969**).

263.s: The safeguard that required Telangana’s revenue surplus to be spent only in Telangana was associated with the:
263.x: The Gentlemen’s Agreement of 20 February 1956 included the safeguard that Telangana’s revenue surplus should be spent only in Telangana.
263.tq: Identify the named agreement behind a specific financial safeguard.
xs: The surplus-spending safeguard came from the **Gentlemen's Agreement** (**20 Feb 1956**) — option **(1)**.
The **Mulki rules** dealt with jobs, not revenue.
xa: Alleged violation: surplus **diverted**; fiscal centralisation.
The **Eight-Point Formula** (**1969**) set up a special committee on **Telangana surplus funds**.
The Regional Committee was to supervise **development, recruitment, education**.

263.s:
The Telangana Regional Committee was intended to supervise matters relating to:

263.x: The separate Andhra flag was hoisted on 10 December 1972; P. V. Narasimha Rao resigned and President's Rule began on 18 January 1973.
263.tq: Fix the sequence by comparing the two events dated in December 1972 and January 1973.
xs: **Flag hoisted (10 Dec 1972) → P.V. Narasimha Rao resigned (18 Jan 1973) → President's Rule began** — option **(1)** is correct.
President's Rule began the same day the CM **resigned**, **18 Jan 1973**, so it cannot come before the resignation.
xa: President's Rule ended **10 Dec 1973**; **Jalagam Vengala Rao** became CM.
The trigger was the **October 1972** SC ruling upholding the **Mulki Rules**.
⚠ **10 Dec** twice: flag **1972**, end of President's Rule **1973**.

263.s: The inclusion of Assistant Surgeons and Engineers under the Mulki rules in 1972 led directly to the:
263.x: The Five-Point Formula of 27 November 1972 brought Assistant Surgeons and Assistant Engineers under the Mulki rules, adding fuel to the Jai Andhra agitation that had followed the October 1972 Supreme Court judgment upholding the Mulki Rules. The 1969 agitation and the 1956 Gentlemen's Agreement came earlier.
263.tq: Link the immediate administrative cause to the resulting movement.
xs: Bringing **Assistant Surgeons** and **Assistant Engineers** under the Mulki rules (**27 Nov 1972**) **added fuel** to the **Jai Andhra** agitation — option **(4)** is correct.
The **Gentlemen's Agreement** (**1956**) and the **1969** Telangana agitation came earlier.
xa: Jai Andhra's immediate cause: the SC ruling of **October 1972** upholding the **Mulki Rules**.
**Indira Gandhi** ruled out a separate Andhra State.
⚠ The **Greater Rayalaseema** demand belongs to the **2014** bifurcation debate.

263.s: The President's Rule imposed in Andhra Pradesh on 18 January 1973 is significant because it was
o: the first President's Rule in the State since its formation
imposed under Article 360 for a financial emergency
the second spell of President's Rule after one in 1969
imposed to implement the Eight-Point Formula
263.x: After P.V. Narasimha Rao resigned on 18 January 1973 amid a breakdown of law and order during Jai Andhra, President's Rule lasted until 10 December 1973 - the first in AP since the State was formed. Article 360 concerns financial emergency; there was no President's Rule in 1969; the Eight-Point Formula (1969) is unrelated.
263.tq: First PR in AP = 18 Jan 1973 to 10 Dec 1973 (~11 months), Jai Andhra.
xs: President's Rule from **18 January 1973** was the **first in AP since its formation** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was imposed for a **breakdown of law and order** during Jai Andhra — not a financial emergency, and there was none in **1969**.
xa: It lasted till **10 Dec 1973** (about **11 months**).
CM **P.V. Narasimha Rao** resigned the same day.
The **Eight-Point Formula** belongs to **1969** — unrelated.

263.s: Under the Six-Point Formula, which arrangement was intended to address grievances of government employees?
o: A common police force for both successor states
A committee to select the capital at Amaravati
A committee to settle their grievances
A separate state for Coastal Andhra
263.x: The third point of the Six-Point Formula provided for a committee to settle government employees’ grievances.
263.tq: Identify the administrative remedy from the stated problem.
xs: Point 3 of the **Six-Point Formula**: a **committee to settle government employees' grievances** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Amaravati** and successor-state police belong to **2014-15**, not **1973**.
xa: Point 1: **Mulki Rules and TRC abolished**.
Point 2: **local preference** in non-gazetted posts; **6 zones**; **AP Administrative Tribunal**.
Point 4: backward-area development via a **State Planning Commission**.

263.s: The Six-Point Formula provided for backward-area development through:
o: An Administrative Tribunal with zonal committees
A State Planning Commission with local sub-committees
A Central University with local sub-committees
The Telangana Regional Committee with district committees
263.x: Backward-area development was to be addressed through a State Planning Commission with local sub-committees.
263.tq: Distinguish planning institutions from tribunals and regional bodies.
xs: Point 4: backward-area development through a **State Planning Commission with local sub-committees** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **Administrative Tribunal** dealt with service disputes; the **Central University** with education (**Art. 371E**); the **TRC** was **abolished**.
xa: Point 5: local preference in **admissions** → **Central University, Hyderabad**.
Point 6: constitutional amendment → **32nd Amendment**, **Presidential Order 1975**.
Proposed **21 Sep 1973**; approved **18 Dec 1973**.

263.s: Article 371E, associated with the Six-Point Formula, provides for:
o: Local cadres and six administrative zones
A State Planning Commission for backward areas
263.x: Article 371E provides for the establishment of a Central University at Hyderabad. Local cadres and zones are associated with Article 371D.
263.tq: Separate the closely related constitutional articles 371D and 371E.
xs: **Article 371E** provides for a **Central University** at **Hyderabad** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Local cadres**, **zones** and the **AP Administrative Tribunal** come under **Art. 371D**.
xa: Both were inserted by the **32nd Amendment** (in force **1 July 1974**).
**State Planning Commission** = Six-Point Formula's backward-area body.
Exam angle: which article gave the Central University — **371E**.

263.s:
Consider the following statements about Article 371D:
1. It is associated with local cadres and zonal arrangements.
2. It is connected with the Andhra Pradesh Administrative Tribunal.
3. It established the Central University at Hyderabad.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Central University at Hyderabad is associated with Article 371E, not Article 371D.
263.tq: Use the article-number distinction to reject a swapped provision.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: correct — **Art. 371D** covers **local cadres** and zonal arrangements.
Statement 2: correct — it provides the **AP Administrative Tribunal** (service disputes taken out of the High Court).
Statement 3: wrong — the **Central University** is under **Art. 371E**.
xa: Art. 371D: **equitable opportunities** in public employment and education.
Under it, the **Presidential Order 1975** created **6 zones**.
**APRA 2014 Sec 97** extended **Art. 371D** to Telangana.

263.s: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the Six-Point Formula of 1973?
o: Continuation of the Telangana Regional Committee
Local preference in non-gazetted posts and admissions
263.x: The Six-Point Formula abolished the Telangana Regional Committee. It provided for a Central University at Hyderabad, an Administrative Tribunal and local preference in specified posts and admissions.
263.tq: Watch for the reversal of an institution that was abolished rather than continued.
xs: **Continuation of the TRC** was **not** a feature — the Six-Point Formula **abolished** it — option **(3)** is the answer.
It did provide an **Administrative Tribunal**, a **Central University** at Hyderabad and **local preference** in non-gazetted posts and admissions.
xa: TRC dissolved on **1 Jan 1974**.
Mulki Rules abolished with the **TRC's consent**.
The formula ended **Jai Andhra** and brought about **two decades** of relative peace.

263.s: The Jai Andhra movement of 1972–73 was triggered by the Mulki rules and was called off on:
263.x: Jai Andhra was called off on 1 October 1973, after the Centre proposed the Six-Point Formula on 21 September 1973. 10 December 1972 is when the separate Andhra flag was hoisted, 18 January 1973 is when President's Rule began, and 18 December 1973 is when the Six-Point Formula was approved.
263.tq: Separate the trigger, the date of calling off and the later formal settlement.
xs: Jai Andhra was **called off on 1 October 1973** — option **(4)** is correct.
**10 Dec 1972** = Andhra flag hoisted; **18 Jan 1973** = President's Rule began; **18 Dec 1973** = Six-Point Formula approved.
xa: The Centre proposed the formula on **21 Sep 1973**.
⚠ PYQ: the agitation was ended by the **Six-Point Formula** — not repression.
The movement ran from **1972** into **1973**.

263.s: The Jai Andhra agitation of 1972-73 was finally brought to an end by
o: the abolition of the Mulki Rules alone
the Six-Point Formula proposed by the Central Government
the Eight-Point Formula of Indira Gandhi
263.x: Jai Andhra ended with the Six-Point Formula proposed by the Centre on 21 September 1973. Neither repression nor the abolition of the Mulki Rules by itself ended it (the PYQ trap); the Eight-Point Formula belongs to the 1969 Telangana agitation.
263.tq: Jai Andhra ended by = Six-Point Formula (21 Sep 1973), not repression or Mulki abolition.
xs: Jai Andhra was ended by the **Six-Point Formula proposed by the Central Government** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ PYQ trap: **neither repression nor abolition of the Mulki Rules** alone ended it; the **Eight-Point Formula** was for **1969**.
xa: Proposed **21 Sep 1973**; agitation called off **1 Oct 1973**.
It got constitutional backing via the **32nd Amendment** (**Art. 371D, 371E**).
It still governs AP's **local cadres**.

263.s: The 32nd Constitutional Amendment Act, which inserted Articles 371D and 371E, came into force on:
263.x: The 32nd Constitutional Amendment Act was enacted in 1973 and came into force on 1 July 1974.
263.tq: Use the year-and-date distinction carefully instead of treating enactment and commencement as identical.
xs: The **32nd Amendment** (Art. **371D** and **371E**) came into force on **1 July 1974** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was the **1973** amendment that gave effect to the **Six-Point Formula**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say **33rd** Amendment — wrong; PYQ key = **32nd**.
**Presidential Order** on local cadres: **1975**.
Exam angle: APHQ **2019** asked which amendment brought in the Six-Point Formula.

263.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 371D:
1. It provides for equitable opportunities in public employment and education for different parts of Andhra Pradesh.
2. It permits the organisation of local cadres and the fixing of local areas for direct recruitment and admissions.
3. It places all service disputes within the exclusive jurisdiction of the High Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Article 371D provided for an Administrative Tribunal for service disputes, taking them out of the High Court's jurisdiction.
263.tq: Find the wrong statement by checking the authority assigned to service disputes.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1: correct — **equitable opportunities in public employment and education**.
Statement 2: correct — **local cadres** and **local areas** for direct recruitment and admissions.
Statement 3: wrong — an **Administrative Tribunal** took service disputes **out of** the High Court's jurisdiction.
xa: The President acts through a **Presidential Order**.
⚠ **Art. 16(3)**: only **Parliament** may prescribe residence requirements; **371D** = special route for AP.
Inserted by the **32nd Amendment**.

263.s: Article 371E of the Constitution enables Parliament to establish which of the following in the State?
263.x: Article 371E empowers Parliament to establish a Central University in the State, represented by the University at Hyderabad.
263.tq: Test the precise constitutional function attached to the Article.
xs: **Article 371E** lets Parliament establish a **Central University** in the State — option **(1)** is correct.
That is the **University at Hyderabad**.
xa: ⚠ The **Administrative Tribunal** comes under **Art. 371D**.
Six-Point Formula point 5: local preference in **admissions** → Central University.
**32nd Amendment**, in force **1 July 1974**.

263.s:
With reference to residence requirements for public employment, consider the following statements:
1. Article 16(3) empowers only Parliament to prescribe residence requirements.
2. Article 371D provides a special constitutional route for Andhra Pradesh.
3. The President alone can prescribe residence requirements for every State under Article 16(3).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Article 16(3) refers to Parliament, while Article 371D is the special route for Andhra Pradesh.
263.tq: Use the authority trap by distinguishing Parliament's power from the President's role.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: correct — **Art. 16(3)**: only **Parliament** may prescribe residence requirements.
Statement 2: correct — **Art. 371D** is a **special route** for AP.
Statement 3: wrong — Art. 16(3) speaks of **Parliament**, not the President.
xa: In **1969** the SC struck down the **1957** Act's Telangana clause under **Art. 16(3)** (residence for only part of a State).
Art. 371D works through a **Presidential Order** (**1975**).
⚠ **1969 vs 1972**: residence law struck down vs **Mulki Rules** upheld.

263.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional position of education admissions after the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: Article 371D was abolished for both States immediately after bifurcation.
Article 371D was replaced by Article 371J for both States.
Admission quotas were continued permanently only in Andhra Pradesh.
Existing admission quotas under Article 371D continued for ten years and Article 371D was extended to Telangana.
263.x: The Act continued the existing admission quotas under Article 371D for ten years and extended the operation of Article 371D to Telangana.
263.tq: Distinguish continuation and extension of a provision from abolition or replacement by another Article.
xs: After **APRA 2014**, existing admission quotas continued **for 10 years** and **Art. 371D was extended to Telangana** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Sec 95**: equal access to **higher education** for **10 years**; **Sec 97**: **Art. 371D** extended to Telangana.
xa: **Part XII** covers amendment of **Articles 371D and 168** (APPSC 2022).
**Art. 168**: Telangana's Legislative Council.
AP's **Public Employment Order-2025** rebuilt the 371D system as **6 zones and 2 multi-zones**.

263.s: The Six-Point Formula received constitutional backing through the insertion of:
263.x: The 32nd Amendment Act, 1973 inserted Articles 371D and 371E to provide constitutional backing for the Six-Point Formula.
263.tq: Discriminate among neighbouring constitutional article numbers.
xs: The **Six-Point Formula** got constitutional backing through **Articles 371D and 371E** — option **(2)** is correct.
Inserted by the **32nd Amendment** (**1973**), in force **1 July 1974**.
xa: **371D**: local cadres, zones, **AP Administrative Tribunal**.
**371E**: **Central University** at Hyderabad.
⚠ **Art. 370** is J&K's — revoked before the **J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019**.

263.s: Articles 371D and 371E relating to Andhra Pradesh were inserted by which Constitutional Amendment?
263.x: The Thirty-second Amendment of 1973 gave effect to the Six-Point Formula and inserted Articles 371D and 371E.
263.tq: Reject the nearby but incorrect 33rd Amendment and recall the exact amendment number.
xs: **Articles 371D and 371E** were inserted by the **32nd Amendment** — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes say **33rd** — wrong; **36th** Amendment admitted **Sikkim** under **Article 2**.
xa: It gave effect to the **Six-Point Formula** (APHQ PYQ 2019).
In force **1 July 1974**.
Exam angle: amendment number (**32nd**), President's Rule (**Jan 1973**), **371E** for the Central University.

263.s: Which of the following statements regarding local cadres is correct?
o: Local cadres abolished all forms of direct recruitment.
Local cadres applied only to educational admissions and not to public employment.
Posts could be organised district-wise, zone-wise or multi-zone-wise, with direct recruitment reserved for locals of the area.
All posts were reserved exclusively for persons born in the concerned district.
263.x: Local cadres could be organised district-wise, zone-wise or multi-zone-wise, and direct recruitment was reserved for locals of the relevant area.
263.tq: Apply the definition to distinguish residence-based local recruitment from birth-based exclusivity.
xs: Under local cadres, posts were organised **district-wise, zone-wise or multi-zone-wise**, with **direct recruitment reserved for locals** of that area — option **(3)** is correct.
They covered public employment as well as admissions — they did not abolish direct recruitment.
xa: The Order: **AP Public Employment (Organisation of Local Cadres and Regulation of Direct Recruitment) Order, 1975**.
**6 zones** — decentralised, equitable recruitment.
**GO 610** (**1985**) sought to repatriate non-locals appointed in violation of the Order.

263.s: After the reorganisation of Andhra Pradesh in 2014, which zones of the undivided State were retained by Andhra Pradesh for its 13 districts?
263.x: After 2014, Andhra Pradesh retained Zones I to IV for its 13 districts; Zones V and VI related to the Telangana region.
263.tq: Test the boundary of the retained range rather than recalling an individual district.
xs: After **2014**, AP kept **Zones I-IV** for its **13 districts** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Zones V and VI** were the **Telangana** zones.
xa: **Zones I-III** = Coastal Andhra; **Zone IV** = Rayalaseema.
New system: **6 zones and 2 multi-zones** (Cabinet, **April 2026**).

263.s:
With reference to the revised Andhra Pradesh Public Employment Order-2025, consider the following statements:
1. The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet approved six zones and two multi-zones.
2. The revised arrangement was approved in April 2026.
3. The Department of Personnel completed the final mapping in May 2026.
4. A multi-zone restricts candidates to posts available only within their own zone.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: Six zones and two multi-zones were approved in April 2026, and final mapping was completed in May 2026. A multi-zone enables candidates from adjacent zones to compete for a wider set of posts, so statement 4 is false.
263.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the practical effect of a multi-zone.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)** is correct.
Statements 1 and 2: correct — the AP Cabinet approved **6 zones and 2 multi-zones** in **April 2026**.
Statement 3: correct — the **Department of Personnel** completed final mapping in **May 2026**.
Statement 4: wrong — a **multi-zone** lets candidates from **adjacent zones** compete for a **wider** set of posts.
xa: This is the **AP Public Employment Order-2025**.
It rebuilds the **Art. 371D** local-cadre system.
AP now has **28** districts (**2025**), incl. new **Polavaram** and **Markapuram**.

263.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the zonal system under the 1975 Order in undivided Andhra Pradesh:
1. Zones I to III comprised Coastal Andhra.
2. Zone IV comprised Rayalaseema.
3. Zones V and VI comprised Telangana.
4. Hyderabad was included in Zone V.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: Zones I to III were in Coastal Andhra, Zone IV was Rayalaseema, and Zones V and VI were in Telangana. Hyderabad was included in Zone VI, not Zone V.
263.tq: Find the single reversed classification in an otherwise familiar regional grouping.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(1)** is correct.
Statements 1-3: correct — **Zones I-III** Coastal Andhra, **Zone IV** Rayalaseema, **Zones V-VI** Telangana.
Statement 4: wrong — **Hyderabad** was in **Zone VI**, not Zone V.
xa: Zone V: **Adilabad, Karimnagar, Warangal, Khammam**.
**Girglani** found large violations especially in **Zone VI - Hyderabad**.
The zones came from the **Presidential Order, 1975**.

263.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the zones of undivided Andhra Pradesh under the 1975 Order:

List-I (Zone)
a. Zone I
b. Zone II
c. Zone III
d. Zone IV

List-II (District group)
i. Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore
ii. Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam
iii. Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur and Chittoor
iv. East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
263.x: Zone I consisted of Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam; Zone II of East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna; Zone III of Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore; and Zone IV of Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur and Chittoor.
263.tq: Start from the sure coastal pair and eliminate the codes with mismatched zone groups.
xs: **a–ii, b–iv, c–i, d–iii** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Zone I**: Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam; **Zone II**: East Godavari, West Godavari, Krishna.
**Zone III**: Guntur, Prakasam, Nellore; **Zone IV**: Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur, Chittoor.
xa: **Zone V**: Adilabad, Karimnagar, Warangal, Khammam.
**Zone VI**: Hyderabad, Ranga Reddy, Nizamabad, Mahbubnagar, Medak, Nalgonda.
After **2014**, AP kept **Zones I-IV**.

263.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched under the zonal classification of undivided Andhra Pradesh?

1. Zone V — Adilabad, Karimnagar, Warangal and Khammam
2. Zone VI — Hyderabad, Ranga Reddy, Nizamabad, Mahbubnagar, Medak and Nalgonda
3. Zone IV — Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore
4. Zone II — Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur and Chittoor
263.x: The districts listed in statements 1 and 2 correctly belong to Zones V and VI respectively. Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore belonged to Zone III, while Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur and Chittoor belonged to Zone IV.
263.tq: Use the zone number to detect swapped district groups.
xs: Pairs **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)** is correct.
**Zone V** = **Adilabad, Karimnagar, Warangal, Khammam**; **Zone VI** = **Hyderabad, Ranga Reddy, Nizamabad, Mahbubnagar, Medak, Nalgonda**.
Pair 3 wrong: **Guntur, Prakasam, Nellore** = **Zone III**; pair 4 wrong: **Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur, Chittoor** = **Zone IV**.
xa: **GO 610** (**30 December 1985**, **N.T. Rama Rao**) sought to restore local posts to Telangana candidates.
**Girglani Commission**: constituted **2001** by **Chandrababu Naidu**; report **2004**.
⚠ **GO 610** = **NTR, 1985**; **Girglani** = **Chandrababu Naidu, 2001-04**.

263.s: GO 610 was issued primarily to:
o: Introduce the Mulki rules in Hyderabad State
Repatriate non-local employees appointed in violation of the Presidential Order and restore posts to Telangana locals
Create six local zones for the first time
263.x: GO 610 sought to repatriate non-local employees appointed contrary to the 1975 Presidential Order and restore local posts to Telangana candidates.
263.tq: Test the purpose of an executive order through the action it required.
xs: **GO 610** was issued to **repatriate non-local employees** appointed in violation of the **1975 Presidential Order** to their own zones and **restore local posts to Telangana** candidates — option **(2)**.
The **Mulki rules** go back to **1888** in **Hyderabad State**, not to GO 610.
**Six zones** were created by the **Presidential Order, 1975**; the **University at Hyderabad** came from **Art. 371E** (32nd Amendment).
xa: GO 610 was issued on **30 December 1985** by the **N.T. Rama Rao** (TDP) government.
Its **weak implementation** led to the one-man **Girglani Commission** (**2001**, report **2004**).
The **1975 Order** set **Zones V-VI** for Telangana, with **Hyderabad in Zone VI**.

263.s: GO 610 was issued on 30 December 1985 by the government headed by:
263.x: GO 610 was issued on 30 December 1985 by the N.T. Rama Rao-led TDP government.
263.tq: Combine the exact date with the issuing authority to avoid a swapped-leader trap.
xs: GO 610 was issued on **30 December 1985** by the **N.T. Rama Rao** (TDP) government — option **(4)**.
**Chandrababu Naidu**'s government constituted the **Girglani Commission** in **2001**, not GO 610.
**Kakani Venkataratnam** and **B.V. Subba Reddy** were Congress leaders of the **Jai Andhra** agitation (1972).
xa: Purpose of GO 610: **repatriate non-local employees** appointed against the **1975 Presidential Order** and restore local posts to Telangana candidates.
Chronological PYQ order: **Jai Telangana** → **Jai Andhra** → **32nd Amendment** → **GO 610** → **Girglani Report**.

263.s: The Girglani Commission was constituted in 2001 by the government headed by:
263.x: The one-man Girglani Commission was constituted in 2001 by the Chandrababu Naidu government and submitted its report in 2004.
263.tq: Use the government-commission association rather than confusing the commission with GO 610.
xs: The **Girglani Commission** was constituted in **2001** by the **Chandrababu Naidu** government — option **(4)**.
**N.T. Rama Rao**'s government had issued **GO 610** in **1985**.
**Kakani Venkataratnam** led **Jai Andhra**; **M. Venkaiah Naidu** took part in it as a **student leader**.
xa: It was a **one-man commission** of **J.M. Girglani**; report in **2004**.
It found large-scale violations of the **Presidential Order** and **GO 610**, especially in **Zone VI - Hyderabad**.
The commission was set up because of the **weak implementation** of GO 610.

263.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Girglani Commission:
1. It was a one-man commission headed by J.M. Girglani.
2. It examined violations of GO 610 and the 1975 Presidential Order.
3. It found large-scale appointment of non-locals in Telangana zones, especially Zone VI or Hyderabad.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: All three statements are correct. The commission headed by J.M. Girglani examined violations and highlighted large-scale non-local appointments in Telangana zones, particularly Zone VI.
263.tq: When all statements describe distinct findings of the same commission, verify each independently before choosing the complete combination.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: it was a **one-man commission** of **J.M. Girglani**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: it examined violations of **GO 610** and the **1975 Presidential Order**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: it found large-scale appointment of non-locals in Telangana zones, especially **Zone VI - Hyderabad**; so **1, 2 and 3** — option **(4)**.
xa: Constituted in **2001** by the **Chandrababu Naidu** government; report in **2004**.
**GO 610** was issued on **30 December 1985** by the **N.T. Rama Rao** government.
After **2014**, disputes over Mulki rules and GO 610 complicated the **division of employees** between AP and Telangana.

263.s: The weak implementation of which measure led to the constitution of the Girglani Commission?
263.x: GO 610 was weakly implemented, leading to the constitution of the Girglani Commission to examine continuing violations of the Presidential Order and GO 610.
263.tq: Trace the institutional consequence of inadequate implementation.
xs: The **weak implementation of GO 610** led to the **Girglani Commission** — option **(4)**.
The **Mulki rules** date to **1888**; the **32nd Amendment** (1973) inserted **Art. 371D/371E**; the **Gentlemen's Agreement** (1956) gave Telangana safeguards — none of these led to the commission.
xa: GO 610 (**1985**, **NTR**) sought to repatriate non-locals appointed against the **1975 Presidential Order**.
Girglani Commission: **2001**, **Chandrababu Naidu** government, report **2004**.
Disputes over non-local appointments continued even under the constitutional **zonal system**.

263.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: 1972 — Supreme Court upheld the Mulki Rules and Jai Andhra agitation followed
263.x: The Srikrishna Committee submitted its report in 2010, not in 2001. The year 2001 is associated with the founding of the TRS by K. Chandrasekhar Rao.
263.tq: Find the wrong year-person or year-event pairing.
xs: **"2001 — Srikrishna Committee report"** is NOT correctly matched — option **(3)**; the **Srikrishna Committee** reported on **30 Dec 2010**.
**2001** is the year the **TRS** was formed by **K. Chandrasekhar Rao**.
The other pairs are right: **1969** Jai Telangana; **1972** SC upheld Mulki Rules → **Jai Andhra**; **1956** Gentlemen's Agreement safeguards.
xa: The Srikrishna report gave **six options**.
Other milestones: KCR's fast → Centre's announcement **Dec 2009**; **Million March** **Mar 2011**; **Sakala Janula Samme** **Sep-Oct 2011**; **CWC** resolution **July 2013**.
Telangana was formed on **2 June 2014**.

263.s:
Arrange the following events relating to the separate Telangana movement in chronological order:
A. Formation of the Telangana Rashtra Samithi
B. Centre's announcement after K. Chandrasekhar Rao's fast
C. Srikrishna Committee report
D. Million March
263.x: The Telangana Rashtra Samithi was formed in 2001, the Centre's announcement followed in December 2009, the Srikrishna Committee report came in December 2010, and the Million March occurred in March 2011.
263.tq: Fix the sequence using the formation year first and the event months at the end.
xs: The correct order is **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**TRS formed** (**2001**) → **Centre's announcement after KCR's fast** (**Dec 2009**) → **Srikrishna report** (**Dec 2010**) → **Million March** (**Mar 2011**).
xa: **Sakala Janula Samme**, a general strike of about **42 days**, followed in **Sep-Oct 2011**.
The **CWC resolution** for Telangana came in **July 2013**.
The Srikrishna Committee's report (**30 Dec 2010**) gave **six options**.

263.s: Who founded the Telangana Rashtra Samithi, and in which year was it formed?
263.x: The Telangana Rashtra Samithi was formed in 2001 by K. Chandrasekhar Rao.
263.tq: Match the movement organisation with its founder and formation year.
xs: The **TRS** was formed by **K. Chandrasekhar Rao** in **2001** — option **(2)**.
**2009** is the year of the Centre's announcement after KCR's fast; **Indira Gandhi**'s 1969 link is the **8-point formula**; the **Telangana Praja Samithi** belongs to **1969**.
xa: After the TPS merged with the **Congress**, the statehood demand stayed dormant until **TRS (2001)**.
The **Million March** at Tank Bund came in **Mar 2011**.
Telangana became the **29th state** on **2 June 2014**.

263.s: Sakala Janula Samme, associated with the separate Telangana movement, was:
o: An eight-point formula announced in April 1969
A parliamentary resolution adopted in July 2013
A one-day march at Tank Bund during March 2011
A general strike lasting approximately 42 days during September–October 2011
263.x: Sakala Janula Samme was a general strike that lasted approximately 42 days during September–October 2011. The Tank Bund march was the Million March, held in March 2011.
263.tq: Distinguish the prolonged general strike from the one-day Million March.
xs: **Sakala Janula Samme** was a **general strike** of about **42 days** in **Sep-Oct 2011** — option **(4)**.
The **Tank Bund** march of **Mar 2011** was the **Million March**.
The **8-point formula** was Indira Gandhi's of **11 Apr 1969**; **July 2013** was a **CWC resolution**.
xa: The **TRS** was formed in **2001** by **K. Chandrasekhar Rao**.
The **Srikrishna Committee** reported on **30 Dec 2010** with **six options**.
Telangana was born on the appointed day, **2 June 2014**.

263.s: The Million March associated with the Telangana movement was held at Tank Bund in:
263.x: The Million March was held at Tank Bund in March 2011.
263.tq: Use the location as the anchor and distinguish its date from the neighbouring movement events.
xs: The **Million March** at **Tank Bund** was held in **March 2011** — option **(4)**.
**Dec 2009** = Centre's announcement after KCR's fast; **Dec 2010** = Srikrishna report; **July 2013** = CWC resolution.
xa: **Sakala Janula Samme**, a ~**42-day** general strike, followed in **Sep-Oct 2011**.
The **TRS** was formed in **2001** by **K. Chandrasekhar Rao**.
The **Srikrishna Committee** (Justice **B.N. Srikrishna**) gave **six options**.

263.s:
Which event occurred latest among the following?

A. Formation of the Telangana Rashtra Samithi
B. Srikrishna Committee report
C. Sakala Janula Samme
D. Congress Working Committee resolution for Telangana
263.x: The Congress Working Committee resolution for Telangana was adopted in July 2013, later than the TRS formation in 2001, the Srikrishna Committee report in 2010 and Sakala Janula Samme in 2011.
263.tq: Identify the latest event by comparing the years before comparing the months.
xs: The latest is the **Congress Working Committee resolution** for Telangana (**July 2013**) — option **(4)**.
Earlier ones: **TRS** formed **2001**; **Srikrishna report** **Dec 2010**; **Sakala Janula Samme** **Sep-Oct 2011**.
xa: The **Million March** at Tank Bund was in **Mar 2011**.
Centre's announcement after **KCR's fast**: **Dec 2009**.
The AP Reorganisation Act got **President's assent** on **1 March 2014**; Telangana formed **2 June 2014**.

263.s: Which of the following correctly describes the outcome of the Greater Rayalaseema demand?
o: It was not accepted, and the region remained in residuary Andhra Pradesh.
It was accepted through the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.
It led to the creation of a fourth capital at Anantapur.
It resulted in Rayalaseema becoming a separate State in 1973.
263.x: The separate-state demand raised by Rayalaseema activists during the bifurcation debate was not accepted; Rayalaseema remained part of residuary Andhra Pradesh.
263.tq: Test the actual outcome against plausible but unsupported institutional outcomes.
xs: The **Greater Rayalaseema** demand was **not accepted**, and the region **remained in residuary Andhra Pradesh** — option **(1)**.
It was a separate-state demand from **Rayalaseema activists** during the **bifurcation debate**.
xa: The Act's **Sec 46** gave a **backward-area package** for **Rayalaseema** and **North Coastal AP**.
Under the **1975 Order**, Rayalaseema formed **Zone IV** (Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur, Chittoor).
**Jai Andhra** (**1972**) was a counter-agitation in **Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema** against the Mulki Rules.

263.s: The Committee on Telangana (2010), which examined the demand for a separate Telangana State and gave six options in its report of December 2010, was chaired by
263.x: Justice B.N. Srikrishna chaired the 2010 Committee on Telangana, reporting on 30 December 2010 with six options. Wanchoo gave legal opinion under the 1969 Eight-Point Formula; Sivaramakrishnan chaired the 2014 AP capital committee; Girglani headed the 2001-04 one-man commission on GO 610.
263.tq: Srikrishna = Telangana 2010, six options; Sivaramakrishnan = capital 2014.
xs: The **Committee on Telangana (2010)** was chaired by **Justice B.N. Srikrishna** — option **(2)**; report **30 Dec 2010**, **six options**.
**Justice K.N. Wanchoo** gave a legal opinion on job safeguards under the **8-point formula** (1969).
**K.C. Sivaramakrishnan** headed the **Expert Committee on AP capital** (Sec 6); **J.M. Girglani** headed the one-man commission on **GO 610**.
xa: The committee studied the **separate-Telangana demand**.
⚠ Srikrishna report = **2010**; **2001** = **TRS** founded by **K. Chandrasekhar Rao**.
The **Million March** (**Mar 2011**) and **Sakala Janula Samme** (**Sep-Oct 2011**) came after the report.

263.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, the broad population ratio used for apportionment of assets and liabilities between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana was:
263.x: The broad population ratio used for apportionment was 58.32:41.68 between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana respectively.
263.tq: Read ratio options in the stated order—Andhra Pradesh first and Telangana second—before comparing the figures.
xs: The population ratio was **58.32 : 41.68** (AP : Telangana), from **Census 2011** — option **(3)**.
It is defined in **Part I** (Preliminary) of the Act.
xa: **Liabilities/debt** are divided by this **population ratio**; **assets** by **location**.
The same ratio was used for the **judges' salaries** of the common High Court.
**Power** was split by the **last 5 years' average consumption**.
**Outcome:** AP with **58%** of population got about **46%** of revenue and power.

263.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha.
B. The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Bill was passed by the Rajya Sabha.
C. The President gave assent to the Act.
D. Telangana came into existence as the appointed day arrived.
263.x: The Lok Sabha passed the Bill on 18 February 2014, the Rajya Sabha on 20 February, the President gave assent on 1 March, and Telangana came into existence on 2 June 2014.
263.tq: Fix the legislative sequence first—Lok Sabha before Rajya Sabha—then place assent before the appointed day.
xs: The order is **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
