**Lok Sabha** passed it on **18 Feb 2014**, **Rajya Sabha** on **20 Feb 2014**, **President's assent** on **1 March 2014**, and Telangana was born on the **appointed day**, **2 June 2014**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: "came into effect **2 March 2014**" is wrong; the Act took effect on the appointed day **2 June 2014**.
The constitutional basis was **Article 3**, not Article 2.
Telangana became the **29th state**.

263.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the date of presidential assent from the appointed day under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: Assent was on 2 June 2014, whereas the appointed day was 1 March 2014.
Assent was on 1 March 2014, whereas the appointed day was 2 June 2014.
Both assent and the appointed day were on 1 March 2014.
Both assent and the appointed day were on 2 June 2014.
263.x: The President gave assent on 1 March 2014. The appointed day, on which Telangana was formed, was 2 June 2014.
263.tq: Separate the legal milestone of assent from the operational milestone of the appointed day.
xs: **Assent** was on **1 March 2014**, and the **appointed day** was **2 June 2014** — option **(2)**.
Telangana was **born on the appointed day**; option (1) swaps the two dates.
xa: Lok Sabha / Rajya Sabha passed the Bill on **18 / 20 Feb 2014**.
⚠ Some notes give "in force from **2 March 2014**" — treated as a trap.
The Act has **12 Parts, 108 Sections** and **13 Schedules**.

263.s: At the time of its formation, Telangana was the _____ State of India.
263.x: Telangana became the 29th State of India when it was formed on 2 June 2014.
263.tq: Use the formation event and the rank as a paired current-history fact.
xs: Telangana was the **29th** state of India — option **(2)**.
**Sec 10** amended the **First Schedule**, adding **"29. Telangana"**.
xa: Telangana (**2014**) is the **youngest** state.
After the **J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019**, the count is **28 states and 8 UTs**.
Telangana was formed on **2 June 2014**.

263.s:
With reference to the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, consider the following statements:
1. It required an amendment under Article 368 of the Constitution.
2. Section 10 added Telangana as entry 29 in the First Schedule.
3. The Act was made under Articles 3 and 4.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is false because the Act was enacted under Articles 3 and 4 and did not require an Article 368 amendment.
263.tq: Split the options by testing the Article 368 trap against the specific provisions of the Act.
xs: Statement 1 is **wrong**: under **Arts. 3 and 4**, **no Art. 368 amendment** was needed (Art. 4 says such a law is not an amendment under Art. 368).
Statement 2 is **correct**: **Section 10** added **Telangana as entry 29** in the **First Schedule**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: the Act was made under **Articles 3 and 4**; so **2 and 3 only** — option **(2)**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: some notes say **Article 2** — wrong; Art. 2 = admitting new states/territory from outside (e.g., **Sikkim**).
An Art. 3 bill needs the **President's recommendation** and passes by **simple majority**.
The state legislature's views are **not binding**.

263.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Part I of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: Preliminary provisions, including definitions and the population ratio based on Census 2011
Apportionment of assets and liabilities between the two States
Reorganisation of the State and formation of Telangana
Legal and miscellaneous provisions, including amendments to Articles 168 and 371D
263.x: Part I contains the preliminary provisions, including definitions and the population ratio of 58.32:41.68 based on Census 2011.
263.tq: Use the subject of the Part to eliminate provisions belonging to neighbouring Parts.
xs: **Part I** = **Preliminary**: definitions and the **population ratio 58.32 : 41.68** (Census 2011) — option **(1)**.
Assets and liabilities = **Part VI**; reorganisation and Telangana's formation = **Part II**; legal and miscellaneous = **Part XII**.
xa: Part I covers **Sections 1-2**.
**Part II** (Sections **3-11**) was the **APPSC 2023** key.
The Act has **12 Parts, 108 Sections** and **13 Schedules**.

263.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Parts of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014:
1. Part III deals with representation in the Legislatures.
2. Part IV deals with the High Court.
3. Part VI deals with apportionment of assets and liabilities.
4. Part VIII deals with provisions as to services.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: All four statements are correct. Parts III, IV, VI and VIII cover legislatures, the High Court, assets and liabilities, and services respectively.
263.tq: Check each Part-subject pair independently before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Statement 1 **correct**: **Part III** = Representation in the Legislatures.
Statement 2 **correct**: **Part IV** = High Court (Sections **30-43**).
Statements 3 and 4 **correct**: **Part VI** = Apportionment of Assets and Liabilities; **Part VIII** = Provisions as to Services — so **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
xa: **Part V** = Authorisation of Expenditure and Distribution of Revenues; **Part VII** = Certain Corporations.
**Part IX** = Water Resources (**84-91**); **Part X** = Infrastructure and Special Economic Measures.
**Part XI** = Access to higher education; **Part XII** = Legal and miscellaneous.

263.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Part)
 a. Part V
 b. Part VII
 c. Part IX
 d. Part X

List-II (Subject)
 i. Infrastructure and Special Economic Measures
 ii. Provisions as to Certain Corporations
 iii. Authorisation of Expenditure and Distribution of Revenues
 iv. Management and Development of Water Resources

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
263.x: Part V concerns expenditure and revenue distribution; Part VII concerns certain corporations; Part IX concerns water resources; and Part X concerns infrastructure and special economic measures.
263.tq: Start from the sure Part-subject pair and eliminate codes containing a misplaced subject.
xs: Correct matching: **a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Part V** = **Expenditure and Distribution of Revenues**; **Part VII** = **Certain Corporations**; **Part IX** = **Water Resources**; **Part X** = **Infrastructure and Special Economic Measures**.
xa: Part IX covers Sections **84-91**, including the **Apex Council** and **KRMB/GRMB**.
**Part VI** (Sections **47-67**) = Apportionment of Assets and Liabilities.
**Part VIII** (Sections **76-83**) = Provisions as to Services.

263.s: The provisions relating to amendments of Articles 168 and 371D of the Constitution are contained in:
263.x: Part XII contains legal and miscellaneous provisions and amends Articles 168 and 371D.
263.tq: Match the constitutional amendment with the appropriate concluding Part of the Act.
xs: Amendments of **Articles 168 and 371D** are in **Part XII** (Legal and miscellaneous) — option **(4)** (**APPSC 2022** key).
**Part IX** = Water Resources; **Part X** = Infrastructure and Special Economic Measures; **Part XI** = Access to higher education.
xa: Part XII also holds **Sec. 108** — removal of difficulties.
**Art. 168** change concerns the **Telangana Legislative Council**.
**Sec 97** extended **Art. 371D** to Telangana.

263.s: Which Part of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 deals with the 'Reorganisation of the State of Andhra Pradesh', including formation of Telangana, the common capital and the Governor?
263.x: Part II (Sections 3-11) covers the reorganisation itself: formation of Telangana, the common capital and the common Governor (APPSC 2023 key). Part I is preliminary (definitions, population ratio), Part VI is apportionment of assets and liabilities, and Part XII holds legal and miscellaneous provisions such as amendments of Articles 168 and 371D.
263.tq: Part II = Reorganisation of the State; Part XII = Art 168/371D amendments.
xs: **Part II** — **Reorganisation of the State of Andhra Pradesh** (Sections **3-11**) — option **(2)** (**APPSC 2023** key).
**Part I** = Preliminary; **Part VI** = assets and liabilities; **Part XII** = legal and miscellaneous (amendment of **Arts. 168, 371D**).
xa: **Sec 3** = formation of Telangana; **Sec 5** = Hyderabad common capital up to **10 years**.
**Sec 6** = Expert Committee on new capital; **Sec 7** = **Common Governor**.
**Sec 8** = Governor's **special responsibility** in the common capital.

263.s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 consists of
263.x: The Act has 12 Parts, 108 Sections (Section 108 is the removal-of-difficulties clause) and 13 Schedules (the Thirteenth lists the institutions and infrastructure promised to AP). The other combinations alter one or more of these numbers.
263.tq: APRA 2014 = 12 Parts / 108 Sections / 13 Schedules.
xs: The Act has **12 Parts, 108 Sections and 13 Schedules** — option **(1)**.
**Sec. 108** is the **removal of difficulties** clause.
xa: The **Thirteenth Schedule** (Sec. 93) lists central institutions and infrastructure promised to AP.
**Ninth** Schedule = PSUs/corporations; **Tenth** = State institutions; **Eleventh** = irrigation projects; **Twelfth** = coal, oil & gas, power.
**Part II** (Sections **3-11**) is the reorganisation itself.

263.s:
Consider the following pairs regarding the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014:
1. Section 6 — Expert Committee on a new capital for Andhra Pradesh
2. Section 8 — Governor's special responsibility in the common capital
3. Section 10 — Telangana added as Entry 29 in the First Schedule
4. Section 97 — Extension of Article 371D to Telangana
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
263.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Sections 6, 8, 10 and 97 respectively deal with the capital committee, the Governor's special responsibility, Telangana's entry in the First Schedule and extension of Article 371D.
263.tq: Verify each section–subject pair independently before selecting the comprehensive combination.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(3)**.
**Sec 6** = **Expert Committee** on new AP capital; **Sec 8** = **Governor's special responsibility** in the common capital.
**Sec 10** = **Telangana as entry 29** in First Schedule; **Sec 97** = **Art. 371D extended** to Telangana.
xa: **Sec 5** = Hyderabad **common capital** for up to **10 years**; **Sec 7** = **Common Governor**.
**Sec 90** = **Polavaram** a **national project**.
**Sec 94** = fiscal support, special development package and **Central support for the new capital**.

263.s:
The Governor's special responsibility in the common capital under Section 8 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 included which of the following?
1. Law and order
2. Internal security
3. Vital installations
4. Government buildings
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
263.x: Section 8 assigned responsibility for law and order, internal security, vital installations and government buildings in the common capital. The Governor was to act in individual judgment after consulting Telangana's Council of Ministers.
263.tq: When a provision contains a complete list of responsibilities, test whether the option preserves all listed elements.
xs: All four — **law and order, internal security, vital installations, government buildings** — option **(4)**.
Under **Sec 8**, the Governor acts in **individual judgment** after consulting **Telangana's Council of Ministers**.
xa: **Sec 7** = **Common Governor** for both states, for a period the President decides.
**Sec 5** = Hyderabad **common capital** for **not more than 10 years**.
Hyderabad's **10-year** joint-capital period ended in **June 2024**.

263.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Section 90 — Polavaram declared a national project
Section 50 — Recovery of tax arrears by place of assessment
Section 56 — Tax refunds by population ratio
Section 94 — Extension of Article 371D to Telangana
263.x: Section 94 deals with fiscal support, including tax incentives, a special development package for backward areas and Central support for the new capital. Article 371D was extended to Telangana under Section 97.
263.tq: Find the swapped provision by comparing each section with its neighbouring subject in the statutory scheme.
xs: **"Section 94 — Extension of Article 371D"** is NOT correctly matched — option **(4)**; **Art. 371D** was extended to Telangana by **Sec 97**.
**Sec 94** = fiscal support: tax incentives, **special development package** for backward areas, **Central support for the new capital**.
The others are correct: **Sec 90** Polavaram national project; **Sec 50** tax arrears by place of assessment; **Sec 56** refunds by population.
xa: ⚠ **Sec 50** = arrears (place of assessment); **Sec 56** = refunds (population).
**Sec 95** = equal access to **higher education** for 10 years.
**Sec 84-85** = **Apex Council** and **River Management Boards**.

263.s: The Apex Council and the Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards are provided for under which sections of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
263.x: Sections 84 and 85 provide for the Apex Council and the Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards respectively.
263.tq: Use paired-number recall for consecutive statutory provisions dealing with related water-management institutions.
xs: The **Apex Council** and the **Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards** are under **Sections 84-85** — option **(4)**.
**Sec 90** = Polavaram; **Sec 94** = fiscal support; **Sec 95** = higher education; **Sec 97** = Art. 371D extended.
xa: Part IX (Water Resources) covers Sections **84-91**.
The **Apex Council** is chaired by the **Union Water Resources Minister** with both CMs.
**Krishna and Godavari** are the most contentious rivers (**APPSC 2025**).

263.s: Section 95 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 provides for:
o: Tax refunds according to population ratio
A common High Court at Hyderabad
Equal access to higher education for ten years
263.x: Section 95 provides for equal opportunities for quality higher education to students in the successor States for a period of ten years.
263.tq: Separate education, taxation, judiciary and water-management provisions by their operative subject.
xs: **Sec 95** = **equal access to higher education** for **10 years** — option **(4)**.
**Tax refunds** by population = **Sec 56**; **common High Court** = **Sec 30-31**; river management = **Sec 84-85**.
xa: **Part XI** of the Act deals with **access to higher education**.
**Sec 97** extended **Art. 371D** (education and employment opportunities) to Telangana.
The **13th Schedule** promised AP an **IIT**, **NIT**, **IIM**, **AIIMS** and central + tribal universities.

263.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Section)
A. 26
B. 46
C. 84-85
D. 90

List-II (Provision)
I. Polavaram as a national project
II. Finance Commission award, grants and backward-area package
III. Delimitation of Assembly constituencies
IV. Apex Council and River Management Boards

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
263.x: Section 26 concerns delimitation; Section 46 concerns the Finance Commission award and related grants; Sections 84-85 concern the Apex Council and River Management Boards; and Section 90 concerns Polavaram.
263.tq: Start from the sure pair Section 90–Polavaram and eliminate codes that do not preserve it.
xs: Correct matching: **A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I** — option **(1)**.

**Sec 26** = **delimitation**; **Sec 46** = **Finance Commission award**, grants and backward-area package; **Sec 84-85** = **Apex Council and River Management Boards**; **Sec 90** = **Polavaram national project**.
xa: Sec 26 promised Assembly seats **175 → 225** (AP) and **119 → 153** (TG), subject to **Art. 170** — not yet done.
Sec 46's backward-area package covers **Rayalaseema** and **North Coastal AP**.
Polavaram's original name: **Ramapada Sagaram**, proposed by **Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy**.

263.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.

List-I (Section)
 a. Section 3
 b. Section 5
 c. Section 6
 d. Section 8

List-II (Subject)
 i. Governor's special responsibility for security
 ii. Formation of Telangana
 iii. Expert committee on a new capital for Andhra Pradesh
 iv. Hyderabad as common capital

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
263.x: Section 3 dealt with formation of Telangana; Section 5 with Hyderabad as common capital; Section 6 with the expert committee on a new capital for Andhra Pradesh; and Section 8 with the Governor's special responsibility for security.
263.tq: Start from the sure section–subject pairs and eliminate codes with swapped provisions.
xs: Correct matching: **a–ii, b–iv, c–iii, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Sec 3** = **Formation of Telangana**; **Sec 5** = **Hyderabad common capital**; **Sec 6** = **Expert committee** on new AP capital; **Sec 8** = **Governor's special responsibility**.
xa: ⚠ **Sec 3** = **10 districts** in one note, **9 districts** in another.
**Sec 7** = **Common Governor**; **Sec 10** = Telangana as entry **29**.
The Sec 6 committee was chaired by **K.C. Sivaramakrishnan** (report **Aug 2014**).

263.s: Under the original arrangement provided by Section 5 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, Hyderabad was to serve as the common capital of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana for a period not exceeding:
263.x: Section 5 provided for Hyderabad to be the common capital of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana for a period not exceeding ten years.
263.tq: Use the specific statutory time limit rather than confusing it with other transitional periods.
xs: Under **Sec 5**, Hyderabad was the common capital for **not more than 10 years** — option **(2)**.
That **10-year** joint-capital period ended in **June 2024**.
xa: The **AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026** amends **Section 5** → **Amaravati** sole, permanent capital, **with effect from 2 June 2024**.
It followed the AP Assembly resolution of **28 Mar 2026**.
**Amaravati** was chosen in **2015** (~**33,000 acres** land pooling).

263.s: The tax arrears of the reorganised States were apportioned according to:
o: The place of assessment under Section 50
The location of assets under Section 53
263.x: Tax arrears were apportioned according to the place of assessment under Section 50. Tax refunds, in contrast, were apportioned according to population under Section 56.
263.tq: Discriminate between tax arrears and tax refunds before selecting the section.
xs: **Tax arrears** were apportioned by **place of assessment** under **Section 50** — option **(2)** (**APPSC 2023** key).
**Tax refunds** go by **population** under **Sec 56**; location-based division of units is the **Schedule IX** rule under **Sec 53**.
xa: ⚠ **Sec 50** = arrears (place of assessment); **Sec 56** = refunds (population).
AP's loss on refunds: about **₹3,900 crore** (**14th FC**).
**Assets** by **location**; **liabilities** by **population ratio 58.32 : 41.68**.

263.s: Which Article of the Constitution was amended in relation to the Legislative Council of Telangana?
263.x: Article 168 was changed in relation to the Legislative Council of Telangana. Article 371D was extended to Telangana separately.
263.tq: Distinguish the constitutional provision concerning State legislatures from those concerning Assembly delimitation and High Courts.
xs: **Article 168** was amended for the **Telangana Legislative Council** — option **(2)**.
**Art. 371D** was extended to Telangana by **Sec 97**; **Art. 170** governs the Assembly seat increase; **Art. 214** concerns AP's separate High Court.
xa: Legislative Council seats: AP **58** (some notes: **50**), Telangana **40**.
Amendment of **Articles 371D and 168** is in **Part XII** (**APPSC 2022**).
Assembly seats: AP **175**, Telangana **119**.

263.s: Under Section 30, the High Court at Hyderabad was to remain common until:
o: The Legislative Council of Telangana was constituted
A separate High Court for Andhra Pradesh was established under Article 214
The expiry of ten years from the appointed day in every circumstance
263.x: Section 30 provided for the common High Court at Hyderabad until a separate High Court for Andhra Pradesh was established under Article 214. The Andhra Pradesh High Court was later located at Amaravati.
263.tq: Identify the triggering legal condition rather than an assumed fixed period.
xs: Under **Sec. 30**, the **High Court at Hyderabad** stayed common until AP's own High Court was set up under **Article 214** — option **(2)**.
**Art. 168** concerns the Telangana Council; the ten-year limit belongs to the **common capital** (Sec 5), not the High Court.
xa: Judges' pay was shared in the **population ratio**.
AP's High Court was later located at **Amaravati**.
**Part IV** (Sections **30-43**) deals with the High Court.

263.s: The salaries of judges of the common High Court were to be shared between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana in which ratio?
263.x: The judges’ salaries of the common High Court were shared according to the population ratio of Andhra Pradesh to Telangana, namely 58.32:41.68.
263.tq: Apply the general population-ratio rule to the specific expenditure item.
xs: Judges' salaries of the common High Court were shared in the population ratio **58.32 : 41.68** — option **(1)**.
This **population ratio** (**Census 2011**) is set in **Part I** of the Act.
xa: **Liabilities/debt** are also divided by population ratio; **assets** by **location**.
**Power** is divided by the **previous five years' average consumption**.
The common High Court was at **Hyderabad** under **Sec. 30**.

263.s: Which of the following pairs correctly gives the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha seats allocated to Telangana respectively?
263.x: Telangana was allocated 17 Lok Sabha seats and 7 Rajya Sabha seats. Andhra Pradesh was allocated 25 Lok Sabha and 11 Rajya Sabha seats.
263.tq: Read the two Houses separately and avoid interchanging their figures.
xs: Telangana got **17 Lok Sabha** and **7 Rajya Sabha** seats — option **(1)**.
**25** Lok Sabha and **11** Rajya Sabha seats went to **AP**.
xa: Assembly: AP **175**, Telangana **119**.
Legislative Council: AP **58** (some notes: 50), Telangana **40**.
**Sec 26** promised Assemblies of **225 (AP)** and **153 (TG)** — not yet done.

263.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents the Assembly seats allocated to the successor States?
263.x: The initial allocation was 175 Assembly seats to Andhra Pradesh and 119 to Telangana. The figures 225 and 153 refer to the proposed future increase under Section 26, which has not yet been implemented.
263.tq: Distinguish the existing allocation from the proposed future strength.
xs: AP got **175** and Telangana **119** Assembly seats — option **(2)**.
**225** and **153** are the **Sec 26** proposed increase, subject to **Art. 170** — **not yet done**.
xa: Lok Sabha: AP **25**, Telangana **17**; Rajya Sabha: AP **11**, Telangana **7**.
Legislative Council: AP **58**, Telangana **40**.
**Art. 168** was amended for the **Telangana Council**.

263.s: Which one of the following was a consequence faced by the residuary State of Andhra Pradesh after reorganisation?
o: It lost Hyderabad and faced revenue deficits.
It became responsible for the entire Telangana public debt.
It acquired all districts of the former State of Hyderabad.
It retained Hyderabad and obtained a revenue surplus.
263.x: The residuary State of Andhra Pradesh lost Hyderabad, a major revenue-generating centre, and faced revenue deficits after bifurcation.
263.tq: Apply the territorial and fiscal consequences together rather than treating them as separate facts.
xs: Residual AP **lost Hyderabad** and **faced revenue deficits** — option **(1)**.
**Debt** was split by **population ratio**, so AP did not take all of Telangana's debt; Hyderabad went to Telangana.
xa: AP with **58%** of the population got about **46%** of revenue and power.
AP's loss on tax refunds was about **₹3,900 crore** (**14th FC**).
**Special Category Status** was a PM's assurance in the **Rajya Sabha**, not in the Act.

263.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the basis of apportionment under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: Power — average consumption of the previous five years
263.x: Power was apportioned on the basis of the average consumption during the preceding five years. Assets were divided by location, liabilities by population, and tax arrears by place of assessment.
263.tq: Compare each item with its distinct apportionment basis.
xs: **Power** — **average consumption of the previous five years** — option **(3)**.
**Assets** go by **location** (not population); **liabilities** by **population** (not location); **tax arrears** by **place of assessment** (Sec 50).
xa: **Tax refunds** by population — **Sec. 56**.
Population ratio: **58.32 AP : 41.68 TG**.
AP was left with **46%** of power vs **58%** of population.

263.s: Under which Section were tax refunds apportioned according to population?
263.x: Section 56 provides for apportionment of tax refunds according to population.
263.tq: Use the section-number association for a specific financial provision.
xs: **Tax refunds** were apportioned by **population** under **Section 56** — option **(1)**.
**Sec 50** = arrears by place of assessment; **Sec 26** = delimitation; **Sec 66** is cited by AP on unlisted institutions.
xa: AP's loss on refunds: about **₹3,900 crore** (**14th FC**).
⚠ **Sec 50** = arrears (place); **Sec 56** = refunds (population) — **APPSC 2023** keyed Section 50 for arrears.
Liabilities follow the **58.32 : 41.68** population ratio.

263.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Schedule)
 a. Ninth Schedule
 b. Tenth Schedule
 c. Eleventh Schedule
 d. Twelfth Schedule
List-II (Subject)
 i. Irrigation projects
 ii. Coal, oil, gas and power
 iii. State institutions
 iv. Public sector undertakings and corporations

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
263.x: The Ninth Schedule covers PSUs and corporations, the Tenth State institutions, the Eleventh irrigation projects, and the Twelfth coal, oil, gas and power.
263.tq: Start with the sure institutional pairs and eliminate codes that repeat a subject incorrectly.
xs: Correct matching: **a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii** — option **(1)**.
**Ninth** = **PSUs/corporations**; **Tenth** = **State institutions**; **Eleventh** = **Irrigation projects**; **Twelfth** = **Coal, oil & gas, power**.
xa: **Thirteenth** = education and infrastructure promises (Sec. **93**).
Ninth Schedule companies divided under **Sec 53**: units by location, HQ by population ratio.
Unlisted Ninth/Tenth bodies are disputed — AP cites **Sec. 66**.

263.s: The railway zone referred to in the Thirteenth Schedule is now known as:
263.x: The railway zone included among the infrastructure promises in the Thirteenth Schedule is now South Coast Railway.
263.tq: Use the exact official name instead of a geographically similar distractor.
xs: The railway zone in the **13th Schedule** is now **South Coast Railway** — option **(2)**.
It became fully operational as the **18th zone** from **1 June 2026**.
xa: HQ **Visakhapatnam**; divisions **Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada, Guntakal, Guntur**.
The 13th Schedule (Sec. **93**) also promised a **steel plant**, **port** and **metros**.
Its education promises: **IIT**, **NIT**, **IIM**, **AIIMS**, central + tribal universities.

263.s:
The Thirteenth Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 included provisions relating to which of the following?
1. IIT, NIT, IIM and AIIMS
2. Central and tribal universities
3. A new railway zone, steel plant, port and metros
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: The Thirteenth Schedule included institutions such as IIT, NIT, IIM and AIIMS, central and tribal universities, and infrastructure proposals including a railway zone, steel plant, port and metros.
263.tq: Treat every item in a statutory schedule as a separate checklist entry.
xs: All three are in the **Thirteenth Schedule** (Sec. **93**) — option **(4)**.
It lists **IIT, NIT, IIM, AIIMS**, **central and tribal universities**, and a **new railway zone, steel plant, port and metros**.
xa: The railway zone is now **South Coast Railway** — **18th zone**, HQ **Visakhapatnam**.
**Sec 94** separately gives **Central support for the new capital** and a backward-area package.
**Ninth** Schedule = PSUs; **Tenth** = State institutions.

263.s: Under Section 53 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, the division of Government companies and corporations under Schedule IX was based on:
o: Population ratio for units and location of headquarters
Location of units and population ratio for headquarters
Revenue contribution of each district alone
Equal division of all units and headquarters
263.x: Schedule IX units were divided according to location, while headquarters were divided according to the population ratio.
263.tq: Apply the two-part rule separately to units and headquarters.
xs: Under **Sec 53**, **Schedule IX** companies were divided with **units by location** and **HQ by population ratio** — option **(2)**.
Option (1) reverses the two bases.
xa: Population ratio: **58.32 : 41.68** (AP : TG).
**Tenth Schedule** = State institutions; unlisted bodies are disputed — AP cites **Sec. 66**.
General rule: **assets** by **location**, **liabilities** by **population**.

263.s:
Consider the following statements regarding apportionment under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014:
1. Assets are apportioned according to location.
2. Liabilities and debt are apportioned according to population ratio.
3. Tax arrears are apportioned according to place of assessment.
4. Tax refunds are apportioned according to population ratio.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: All four statements are correct. The relevant bases are location for assets, population for liabilities and refunds, and place of assessment for tax arrears.
263.tq: Build the answer by checking each row of the apportionment framework.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Assets** by **location**; **liabilities/debt** by **population ratio** (**58.32 AP : 41.68 TG**).
**Tax arrears** by **place of assessment** (**Sec 50**); **tax refunds** by **population** (**Sec 56**).
xa: **Power** was split by the **average consumption of the previous five years**.
AP's loss on refunds: about **₹3,900 crore** (**14th FC**).
Schedule IX companies (**Sec 53**): units by location, HQ by population ratio.

263.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026:
1. It amended Section 5 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.
2. It made Amaravati the sole, permanent capital of Andhra Pradesh with effect from 2 June 2014.
3. It followed an Andhra Pradesh Assembly resolution of 28 March 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
263.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 2026 Act amended Section 5 (the capital provision). Statement 2 is wrong: Amaravati is the sole, permanent capital with effect from 2 June 2024 (when Hyderabad's 10-year common-capital term ended), not 2 June 2014, the appointed day. Statement 3 is correct: it followed the Assembly resolution of 28 March 2026. So only 1 and 3 are correct; every option containing 2 is wrong.
263.tq: 2 June 2014 = Telangana born; 2 June 2024 = Amaravati sole capital (after Hyderabad's 10 years).
xs: Statement 1 **correct**: the 2026 Act amends **Section 5** (the capital clause).
Statement 2 **wrong**: **Amaravati** is sole, permanent capital **with effect from 2 June 2024**, not 2 June 2014 (the appointed day).
Statement 3 **correct**: it followed the AP Assembly resolution of **28 Mar 2026** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Original **Sec 5**: Hyderabad common capital for **not more than 10 years**; that period ended in **June 2024**.
**Amaravati** was chosen in **2015** (~**33,000 acres** land pooling).
The **AP High Court** (order of **3 March 2022**) struck down the **CRDA Repeal Act** and upheld Amaravati as the only legal capital.

263.s:
Consider the following statements about committees linked to the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh:
1. The Committee on Telangana (2010), chaired by Justice B.N. Srikrishna, gave its report in December 2010 with six options.
2. The Expert Committee on the AP capital under Section 6, chaired by K.C. Sivaramakrishnan, recommended a 'super capital'.
3. The GN Rao Committee and the BCG study formed the basis of the three-capitals plan of 2020.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
263.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Srikrishna Committee reported in December 2010 with six options. Statement 2 is wrong: the Sivaramakrishnan Expert Committee (report August 2014) opposed a 'super capital'. Statement 3 is correct: the GN Rao Committee and BCG study underpinned the 2020 three-capitals plan. Hence 1 and 3 only; options including 2 are wrong.
263.tq: Sivaramakrishnan = Sec 6 capital committee, against a super capital; GN Rao + BCG = three capitals.
xs: Statement 1 **correct**: **Justice B.N. Srikrishna**'s committee reported in **Dec 2010** with **six options**.
Statement 2 **wrong**: the **K.C. Sivaramakrishnan** Expert Committee (**Sec 6**) **opposed a "super capital"**.
Statement 3 **correct**: the **GN Rao Committee + BCG study** were the basis of the **three-capitals plan (2020)** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: The Sivaramakrishnan committee reported in **Aug 2014**.
The three-capitals plan **failed in court** in **2022**.
**Amaravati** was chosen in **2015**.

263.s: Amaravati was selected as the capital of Andhra Pradesh in 2015 after land pooling involving approximately:
263.x: Amaravati was chosen in 2015 after land pooling involving approximately 33,000 acres.
263.tq: Use the middle-value numerical trap for approximate figures.
xs: **Amaravati** was chosen in **2015** with land pooling of about **33,000 acres** — option **(1)**.
Another note puts the pooling at **33,000-34,000 acres**.
xa: The **three-capitals plan (2020)** failed in court in **2022**.
The **AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026** makes **Amaravati** the sole capital from **2 June 2024**.
The Sec 6 **Expert Committee** under **K.C. Sivaramakrishnan** reported in **Aug 2014**.

263.s: The three-capitals plan of Andhra Pradesh, associated with 2020, failed in court in:
263.x: The three-capitals plan introduced in 2020 failed in court in 2022.
263.tq: Separate the year of proposal from the year of judicial outcome.
xs: The **three-capitals plan (2020)** failed in court in **2022** — option **(4)**.
The **AP High Court** order of **3 March 2022** struck down the **CRDA Repeal Act** and upheld **Amaravati** as the only legal capital.
xa: The plan was based on the **GN Rao Committee + BCG study** and backed by the **YSRCP**.
**Amaravati** was chosen in **2015** (~**33,000 acres**).
The **2026 Amendment Act** amends **Section 5** to make Amaravati the sole, permanent capital.

263.s: Which rivers constitute the principal subject of dispute between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana after bifurcation?
263.x: The Krishna and Godavari are the principal rivers involved in post-bifurcation water-sharing disputes between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
263.tq: Use direct identification of the central factual pair.
xs: The most contentious rivers are the **Krishna and Godavari** — option **(3)** (**APPSC 2025**).
They are managed by the **KRMB and GRMB** under an **Apex Council**.
xa: The **Apex Council** is chaired by the **Union Water Resources Minister** with both CMs.
The **Polavaram-Banakacherla link** (Godavari → Krishna → Penna) is opposed by Telangana.
Boards are provided under **Sec 84-85** of the Act.

263.s: Which of the following statements regarding Section 108 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act is NOT correct?
o: It empowers the Central Government to remove difficulties.
The absence of binding force in the mechanism has been raised as a complaint.
It provides a mechanism for dealing with difficulties arising from reorganisation.
It imposes fixed deadlines for every action required to resolve disputes.
263.x: Section 108 empowers the Centre to remove difficulties, but it and the related expert committees do not prescribe deadlines or possess binding force.
263.tq: Find the statement that adds an unsupported absolute procedural requirement.
xs: The NOT-correct statement is that Sec 108 **imposes fixed deadlines** — option **(4)**; it has **no deadlines or binding force**.
**Sec 108** lets the **Centre remove difficulties** arising from reorganisation; the lack of binding force is a complaint.
xa: Sec. 108 sits in **Part XII** (Legal and miscellaneous).
The **expert committees** under the Act also have **no deadlines or binding force**.
Another complaint: **Special Category Status** was only a PM's assurance in the **Rajya Sabha**.

263.s: At the time of bifurcation, Andhra Pradesh was left with approximately what share of power despite having about 58 per cent of the population?
263.x: Andhra Pradesh was left with about 46 per cent of the power, although it had approximately 58 per cent of the population.
263.tq: Link the numerical outcome with the contrasting population figure.
xs: AP was left with about **46 per cent** of power against **58%** of population — option **(1)**.
**Power** was split by **average consumption of the previous five years**.
xa: AP with **58%** of population got about **46%** of revenue too.
Population ratio: **58.32 : 41.68** (AP : TG).
Residual AP **lost Hyderabad** and faced **revenue deficits**.

263.s: The proposed Polavaram–Banakacherla link is described as following which sequence of rivers?
263.x: The proposed link is described as transferring water from the Godavari to the Krishna and then to the Penna.
263.tq: Read the sequence direction carefully rather than merely identifying the rivers.
xs: The **Polavaram-Banakacherla link** runs **Godavari → Krishna → Penna** — option **(2)**.
Telangana says it breaks the **AP Reorganisation Act** and the **GWDT Award (1980)**.
xa: **Krishna and Godavari** are the most contentious rivers (**APPSC 2025**).
**KRMB and GRMB** work under an **Apex Council** (**Sec 84-85**).
**Polavaram** was declared a **national project** under **Sec 90**.

263.s: The objection raised by Telangana to the Polavaram–Banakacherla link is that it allegedly violates which of the following?
o: The River Boards Act and the Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal Award, 1973
The Inter-State Water Disputes Act and the Sarkaria Commission Report
The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act and the GWDT Award, 1980
The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 and the Bachawat Commission Award
263.x: Telangana has argued that the link violates the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act and the Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal Award of 1980.
263.tq: Match the dispute with the exact legal instruments named in it.
xs: Telangana says the link violates the **AP Reorganisation Act** and the **GWDT Award, 1980** — option **(3)**.
The link carries water **Godavari → Krishna → Penna** (**Jul 2025**).
xa: The **Apex Council** is chaired by the **Union Water Resources Minister** with both CMs.
Telangana wants time-bound closure of Act issues and its **Krishna** rights.
Deputy CM **Bhatti Vikramarka** raised this with the Centre (**Aug 2026**).

263.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the original name of the Polavaram project is correct?
o: It was originally known as Polavaram Sagaram and was proposed by Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy.
It was originally known as Ramapada Sagaram and was proposed by Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy.
It was originally known as Ramapada Sagaram and was proposed by Arthur Cotton.
It was originally known as Godavari Sagaram and was proposed by K. L. Rao.
263.x: The original name was Ramapada Sagaram, and the proposal was associated with Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy. Arthur Cotton and K. L. Rao are incorrect attributions in this context.
263.tq: Separate the correct project name from the commonly substituted names of other engineers.
xs: Polavaram's original name was **Ramapada Sagaram**, proposed by **Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy** — option **(2)**.
⚠ Trap: it was **not** proposed by **Arthur Cotton** or **K.L. Rao**.
xa: **Sec 90** declared **Polavaram** a **national project**.
The **Polavaram Ordinance, 2014** moved **seven mandals** of **Khammam** to AP.
**Polavaram** is one of AP's new districts in the **2025** count (with **Markapuram**).

263.s: Which of the following correctly describes the position regarding Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh?
o: It was granted through the Polavaram Amendment Ordinance, 2014.
It was an assurance given by the Prime Minister in the Rajya Sabha and was not included in the Act.
It was expressly enacted as a provision of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.
It was recommended by the Srikrishna Committee in December 2010.
263.x: Special Category Status was an assurance given by the Prime Minister in the Rajya Sabha, not a provision of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act. Andhra Pradesh has stated that the assurance was not fulfilled in full.
263.tq: Distinguish a political assurance from a statutory provision.
xs: **Special Category Status** was an **assurance by the PM in the Rajya Sabha**, **not in the Act** — option **(2)**.
AP says it is **not fulfilled in full**.
xa: The **Polavaram Ordinance, 2014** dealt with transfer of Khammam villages, not SCS.
The **Srikrishna Committee** (Dec 2010) gave **six options** on Telangana.
**Sec 94** of the Act gives tax incentives and a **special development package** for backward areas.

263.s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Ordinance, 2014 amended which provision in order to transfer certain areas to Andhra Pradesh?
263.x: The 2014 Amendment Ordinance amended Section 3 and transferred seven Khammam mandals in the Polavaram submergence area to Andhra Pradesh.
263.tq: Use the section-number clue together with the specific legislative action.
xs: The **AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Ordinance, 2014** amended **Section 3** — option **(4)**.
It moved **Khammam** villages in the Polavaram submergence zone (**G.O.Ms. No. 111, 27 June 2005**) to AP.
**Sec 26** = delimitation; **Sec 50** = tax arrears; **Sec 84** = Apex Council.
xa: **Seven mandals** were moved; **Bhurgumpadu villages** also kept in AP.
**Sec 3** = formation of Telangana (**10 districts** in one note, **9** in another).
**Sec 90** = **Polavaram national project**.

263.s:
With reference to the Polavaram Ordinance, consider the following statements:
1. Seven mandals of Khammam in the Polavaram submergence area were moved to Andhra Pradesh.
2. The Bhurgumpadu villages were retained in Andhra Pradesh.
3. The Ordinance transferred the entire Khammam district to Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Ordinance transferred seven specified mandals and retained the Bhurgumpadu villages in Andhra Pradesh; it did not transfer the entire Khammam district.
263.tq: Reject the overbroad statement by distinguishing specified territorial transfers from an entire district transfer.
xs: Statement 1 **correct**: **seven mandals** of **Khammam** in the submergence zone moved to AP.
Statement 2 **correct**: the **Bhurgumpadu villages** were also kept in AP.
Statement 3 **wrong**: only specified submergence-zone villages moved, **not the entire district** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: The Ordinance amended **Sec. 3** of the Act.
Submergence zone defined by **G.O.Ms. No. 111, 27 June 2005**.
Under the **1975 Order**, Khammam was in **Zone V**.

263.s: Following the constitutional status of Jammu and Kashmir as a Union Territory in 2019, India has:
263.x: After Jammu and Kashmir ceased to be a State and became a Union Territory in 2019, India has 28 States and 8 Union Territories.
263.tq: Account for the change in status of Jammu and Kashmir before selecting the present total.
xs: After J&K became a UT in **2019**, India has **28 states and 8 UTs** — option **(2)**.
The **J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019** split it into two UTs — **Jammu and Kashmir** and **Ladakh**.
xa: The split took effect from **31 October 2019**.
It followed a presidential order under **Art. 370** revoking special status.
Telangana (**2014**) was the **29th state** at its formation.

263.s: The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 resulted in the creation of which two Union Territories?
263.x: The 2019 Act reorganised the former State of Jammu and Kashmir into the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh.
263.tq: Use the paired-territory identification method for a reorganisation statute.
xs: The **J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019** created the UTs of **Jammu and Kashmir** and **Ladakh** — option **(4)**.
**Chandigarh** became a UT in **1966** (Punjab Reorganisation); **Himachal Pradesh** is a state (**1971**).
xa: In force from **31 October 2019**; all constitutional amendments apply w.e.f. **5 Aug 2019**.
**Ladakh** has no legislature; J&K has a **Legislative Assembly** of the UT.
Common **High Court of J&K and Ladakh**.

263.s: The reorganisation of the former State of Jammu and Kashmir into the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh took effect on:
263.x: The two Union Territories came into existence on 31 October 2019.
263.tq: Separate the date of the constitutional order from the date on which the new Union Territories came into existence.
xs: The two UTs came into being on **31 October 2019** — option **(3)**.
**5 Aug 2019** is the date from which all constitutional amendments apply to J&K.
**27 Dec 1970** is when **Indira Gandhi** dissolved Parliament.
xa: The split followed the presidential order under **Art. 370**.
Count since then: **28 states and 8 UTs**.
J&K's **Legislative Council** was abolished.

263.s:
Which of the following statements about the constitutional position after the reorganisation of Jammu and Kashmir is correct?
1. The former State Legislature, including its Legislative Council, was abolished.
2. The Legislative Assembly of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir replaced the former State Legislature.
3. Ladakh was provided with a legislature under the 2019 Act.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
263.x: The former State Legislature and its Legislative Council were abolished, and Jammu and Kashmir now has a Legislative Assembly as a Union Territory. Ladakh has no legislature.
263.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the institutional comparison between Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh.
xs: Statement 1 **correct**: the **State Legislature**, including the **Legislative Council**, was **abolished**.
Statement 2 **correct**: it is now the **"Legislative Assembly of the UT of J&K"**.
Statement 3 **wrong**: **Ladakh has no legislature** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: The two UTs exist from **31 October 2019**.
Judiciary: a common **High Court of J&K and Ladakh**.
All constitutional amendments apply w.e.f. **5 Aug 2019**.

263.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Formation of Telangana
B. Founding of the TRS
C. Jai Telangana agitation
D. Srikrishna Committee report
263.x: The correct sequence is 1969 Jai Telangana agitation, 2001 founding of the TRS, 2010 Srikrishna Committee report, and 2014 formation of Telangana.
263.tq: Place the first and last events, then arrange the middle dates.
xs: The order is **C, B, D, A** — option **(1)**.
**Jai Telangana** (**1969**) → **TRS founded** (**2001**) → **Srikrishna report** (**30 Dec 2010**) → **Telangana formed** (**2 June 2014**).
xa: The 1969 agitation was led by the **Telangana Praja Samithi**, with **Marri Chenna Reddy**.
The **Million March** came in **Mar 2011**; **CWC** resolution **July 2013**.
The Mulki question runs from **1888 to 2014**.

263.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
263.x: The Six-Point Formula belongs to 1973. The 1985 event was the issuance of GO 610 to correct violations of the Presidential Order.
263.tq: Find the mismatched year by separating the constitutional compromise from its later implementation measures.
xs: **"1985 — Six-Point Formula"** is NOT correctly matched — option **(4)**; the Six-Point Formula was **1973**.
**1985** = **GO 610**, to correct violations of the Presidential Order.
The others are right: **1975** Presidential Order on local cadres; **1969** Jai Telangana; **1972** Jai Andhra.
xa: **1956 (20 Feb)**: Gentlemen's Agreement; **2001-04**: Girglani Commission.
The Six-Point Formula led to the **32nd Amendment** — **Art. 371D**.

263.s: The Jai Telangana agitation of 1969 primarily demanded:
o: Implementation of Mulki safeguards and a separate State
Merger of Telangana with the Madras State
Repatriation of all Andhra employees to Hyderabad State
Abolition of all local cadres in Andhra Pradesh
263.x: The 1969 Jai Telangana agitation was centred in Telangana and demanded implementation of Mulki safeguards along with a separate State.
263.tq: Link the movement with both its region and its principal demand.
xs: **Jai Telangana (1969)** demanded **implementation of Mulki safeguards / a separate State** — option **(1)**.
It was led by the **Telangana Praja Samithi** and **Marri Chenna Reddy**.
xa: ⚠ **1969** = Telangana **for** Mulki rules; **1972** = Andhra **against** Mulki rules.
It began as a **student strike in Khammam, January 1969**.
**Over 360** students and agitators were killed — the **Telangana martyrs of 1969**.

263.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Girglani Report
B. Jai Andhra agitation
C. GO 610
D. Jai Telangana agitation
E. 32nd Constitutional Amendment
263.x: The correct sequence is Jai Telangana agitation (1969), Jai Andhra agitation (1972), 32nd Amendment (1973), GO 610 (1985), and Girglani Report (2004).
263.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the constitutional and administrative measures between them.
xs: The order is **D, B, E, C, A** — option **(1)**.
xa: The **1975 Presidential Order** on local cadres came between the 32nd Amendment and GO 610.
**GO 610** = **NTR**; **Girglani** = **Chandrababu Naidu**.
The **Srikrishna Committee** report followed in **Dec 2010**.

263.s: The Six-Point Formula and the 32nd Constitutional Amendment represented which of the following in the sequence of regional developments?
o: A movement against the Mulki Rules followed by their complete abolition
The final report of the Girglani Commission
The first demand for a separate Telangana State
A compromise following the Jai Telangana and Jai Andhra agitations
263.x: The Six-Point Formula of 1973 and the 32nd Amendment represented a compromise after the regional agitations concerning Mulki safeguards.
263.tq: Place a constitutional settlement in its political sequence rather than confusing it with an agitation.
xs: The **Six-Point Formula** and **32nd Amendment** (**1973**) were a **compromise** after the **Jai Telangana** and **Jai Andhra** agitations — option **(4)**.
The 32nd Amendment inserted **Art. 371D** (local cadres, zones, Administrative Tribunal) and **371E** (central university).
xa: The **1975 Presidential Order** on local cadres followed as implementation.
⚠ **1969** Telangana was **for** Mulki rules; **1972** Andhra was **against** them.
The **Girglani Commission** came later (**2001-04**).

263.s: The South Coast Railway, operational from 1 June 2026, has its headquarters at:
263.x: South Coast Railway became operational on 1 June 2026 as India's 18th railway zone, with headquarters at Visakhapatnam.
263.tq: Separate the headquarters from the listed divisions, which include Guntakal, Guntur, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam.
xs: **South Coast Railway** has its HQ at **Visakhapatnam** — option **(4)**.
**Vijayawada**, **Guntur** and **Guntakal** are its **divisions** (with Visakhapatnam).
xa: It became fully operational as the **18th zone** from **1 June 2026**.
It was promised in the **APRA** (**13th Schedule**).
The 13th Schedule also promised a **steel plant**, **port** and **metros**.

263.s: Hyderabad's period as the joint capital of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana ended in:
263.x: The ten-year joint-capital period of Hyderabad ended in June 2024.
263.tq: Distinguish the fixed duration from the date on which the period actually ended.
xs: Hyderabad's **10-year** joint-capital period ended in **June 2024** — option **(4)**.
**Sec 5** made Hyderabad the common capital for **not more than 10 years** from **2 June 2014**.
xa: The **2026 Amendment Act** made **Amaravati** sole capital **with effect from 2 June 2024**.
**Sec 8** gave the Governor **special responsibility** in the common capital.
**Amaravati** was chosen in **2015**.

263.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a criticism of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: It transferred the entire public debt to Telangana.
It denied Andhra Pradesh any share in the revenue of the undivided State.
It was passed without the consent of the State Legislative Assembly.
It was passed only after obtaining the binding consent of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly.
263.x: A major criticism was that the Act was passed without the consent of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly. The reorganisation also involved revenue and debt-sharing arrangements rather than the complete transfer of either to one State.
263.tq: Identify the precise criticism and reject absolute statements about consent, revenue and debt.
xs: The Act was **passed without the state assembly's consent** — option **(3)**.
**Debt** was split by **population ratio**, not transferred wholly to Telangana; AP did get a revenue share (about **46%**).
xa: Under **Art. 3**, the state legislature's views are **not binding**.
Telangana wants time-bound closure of pending Act issues and its **Krishna** rights.
**Sec 108** and the expert committees have **no deadlines or binding force**.

263.s: The number of districts in Andhra Pradesh changed in which of the following sequence between 2014 and 2025?
263.x: Andhra Pradesh had 13 districts in 2014, 26 in 2022 and 28 in 2025.
263.tq: Arrange successive administrative changes in their time sequence.
xs: The new districts in **2025**: **Polavaram** and **Markapuram**.
xa: After **2014**, AP kept **Zones I-IV** for its **13 districts**.
Current local-cadre system: **6 zones and 2 multi-zones** (**AP Public Employment Order-2025**).
AP area: **1,60,205 sq km**; coastline **974 km**.

263.s: Which two districts were identified as new additions in the 2025 district count of Andhra Pradesh?
263.x: Polavaram and Markapuram were identified as the new districts in the 2025 count, which took the total to 28.
263.tq: Discriminate between newly identified districts and established cities or districts.
xs: The new districts in the **2025** count are **Polavaram** and **Markapuram** — option **(1)**.
xa: AP had **13 districts** in **2014**.
AP's population: **4.96 crore** (**2011**).
Capital **Amaravati**; CM **N. Chandrababu Naidu**; Governor **S. Abdul Nazeer**.

263.s:
Consider the following statements about the Telangana movement:
1. It was the first mass movement to place separate statehood prominently on the political agenda.
2. Its broad sequence involved students, followed by a political party and then a central formula.
3. A similar sequence was visible during the movement of 2001–2014.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: All three statements are correct. The movement was significant for making separate statehood a major political issue, and its student-party-central formula sequence was repeated in 2001–2014.
263.tq: Test the significance, sequence and later recurrence of a movement together.
xs: Statement 1 **correct**: it was the **first mass movement** to put separate statehood on the political agenda.
Statement 2 **correct**: sequence **students → party → central formula**.
Statement 3 **correct**: the sequence was repeated in **2001-14** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: It led to the **first President's Rule** in AP.
The **Six-Point Formula** brought roughly **two decades** of relative peace between regions.
**Prof. K. Jayashankar** is widely called the movement's ideologue.

263.s: Prof. K. Jayashankar, associated with the Telangana movement, was a former Vice-Chancellor of:
263.x: Prof. K. Jayashankar was a former Vice-Chancellor of Kakatiya University and was widely regarded as the ideologue of the Telangana movement.
263.tq: Use the person–institution association to distinguish prominent regional figures.
xs: **Prof. K. Jayashankar** was a former VC of **Kakatiya University** — option **(2)**.
He was active in the **1952** and **1969** agitations and is widely called the **ideologue** of the Telangana movement.
xa: He came up in the **'Jatipita'** title debate (**Feb 2026**).
The **1969** agitation began with a **student strike in Khammam**.
Telangana (**2014**) = youngest (**29th**) state.

263.s: The 1969 agitation and the 1972 Jai Andhra counter-movement were followed by which combination?
o: The States Reorganisation Act and Article 370
263.x: The two regional agitations were followed by the Six-Point Formula in 1973 and Article 371D, which provided the constitutional basis for local cadres and related arrangements.
263.tq: Pair the political settlement with its constitutional provision.
xs: The two agitations were followed by the **1973 Six-Point Formula** and **Art. 371D** — option **(1)**.
**Art. 371D** (32nd Amendment) still governs AP's **local cadres**.
xa: The **32nd Amendment** also inserted **Art. 371E** (Central University, Hyderabad).
It came **in force** on **1 July 1974**.
⚠ Some notes say **33rd** Amendment — wrong; PYQ key = **32nd**.

263.s: Which of the following is the most appropriate criticism of the constitutional zonal system associated with Article 371D?
o: It completely ended all disputes over local appointments.
It applied exclusively to railway recruitment.
Disputes over non-local appointments continued despite the system.
It abolished the principle of regional equity in public employment.
263.x: Although the system replaced political assurances with constitutional zoning, disputes over non-local appointments continued, including issues associated with GO 610 and the Girglani Commission.
263.tq: Reject absolute claims and identify the continuing limitation of an institutional arrangement.
xs: **Disputes over non-local appointments continued** despite the zonal system — option **(3)**.
Examples: **GO 610** (**1985**) and the **Girglani Commission** (**2001-04**).
xa: The constitutional zonal system **replaced political assurances**.
Local-cadre rules trade off **merit and mobility** vs **regional equity**.
Art. 371D system now rebuilt as **6 zones and 2 multi-zones** (Cabinet approval **April 2026**).

263.s: The long-running Mulki question is described as extending from:
263.x: The Mulki question is traced from 1888 to 2014 and is linked with the 1969 and 1972 agitations, Article 371D, GO 610 and bifurcation.
263.tq: Use the distinctive beginning and ending years to identify the historical span.
xs: The **Mulki question** runs from **1888 to 2014** — option **(4)**.
It connects the **1969** and **1972** agitations, **Art. 371D**, **GO 610** and **bifurcation**.
xa: Mulki rules originated in **1888** in **Hyderabad State** (**Salar Jung II** era).
The **1919 Nizam's Farman** made outsiders need the **Nizam's personal permission**.
⚠ **15 years** residence = Nizam's rules; **12 years** = Gentlemen's Agreement.

263.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the principal tension in local-cadre rules?
o: They apply only to private-sector employment.
They make merit irrelevant in public employment.
They replace regional equity entirely with unrestricted mobility.
They balance merit and mobility against regional equity.
263.x: Local-cadre rules involve a trade-off between merit and mobility on the one hand and regional equity on the other.
263.tq: Apply the policy principle to the competing objectives rather than choosing an absolute statement.
xs: Local-cadre rules **trade off merit and mobility** vs **regional equity** — option **(4)**.
They reserve direct recruitment for **"locals"** of an area under **Art. 371D**.
xa: Posts are organised **district-wise / zone-wise / multi-zone-wise**.
**Multi-zone:** candidates from adjacent zones compete for a wider set of posts.
⚠ **Art. 16(3)**: only **Parliament** may prescribe residence requirements; **Art. 371D** is AP's special route.

263.s: Which of the following correctly states the present profile of Andhra Pradesh given in the 2026 reference?
o: Capital Amaravati, area 1,25,000 sq km and coastline 650 km
Capital Visakhapatnam, area 1,60,205 sq km and coastline 974 km
Capital Hyderabad, area 1,60,205 sq km and coastline 974 km
Capital Amaravati, area 1,60,205 sq km and coastline 974 km
263.x: The stated 2026 profile gives Amaravati as the capital, an area of 1,60,205 square kilometres and a coastline of 974 kilometres.
263.tq: Check the capital, area and coastline as a combined profile and reject one-variable substitutions.
xs: AP's **2026** profile: capital **Amaravati**, area **1,60,205 sq km**, coastline **974 km** — option **(4)**.
**Hyderabad**'s joint-capital period ended in **June 2024**; **Visakhapatnam** is the **South Coast Railway** HQ, not the capital.
xa: AP's coastline is the **second longest**.
Population **4.96 crore** (**2011**).
Governor **S. Abdul Nazeer**; CM **N. Chandrababu Naidu**.

264.s: Naxalbari is located in the Siliguri sub-division of which district and State?
264.x: Naxalbari is in the Siliguri sub-division of Darjeeling district in West Bengal.
264.tq: Use the precise sub-division–district–State geographical chain.
xs: Naxalbari lies in the **Siliguri** sub-division of **Darjeeling** district, **West Bengal** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Srikakulam** (AP) was the site of the separate **Srikakulam Girijan struggle (1968-70)**, not Naxalbari.
xa: The **Naxalbari uprising** was a peasant uprising of **March-May 1967**.
It was led by **Charu Majumdar** and **Kanu Sanyal**; its slogan was "**Land to the tiller**".
⚠ Do not confuse: Naxalbari = **West Bengal (1967)**; Srikakulam = **Srikakulam Agency, AP (1968-70)**.

264.s: Which slogan was associated with the Naxalbari uprising?
264.x: “Land to the tiller” was the slogan associated with the Naxalbari peasant uprising.
264.tq: Recall the movement-specific slogan rather than a general nationalist slogan.
xs: The slogan of the Naxalbari uprising was "**Land to the tiller**" — option **(3)** is correct.
Its related line "**Ballot to Bullet**" rejected the **CPI(M)'s parliamentary path**, so "Inquilab through elections" is the opposite of its stand.
xa: Causes of Naxalbari: **land concentration**, **failed land reforms** (zamindari abolition, ceilings, tenancy) and **exploitation of tribals**.
The movement later put **land to the tiller** and **tribal land alienation** at the centre of AP politics.
Naxalbari: **Siliguri** sub-division, **Darjeeling**, **West Bengal**, **March-May 1967**.

264.s: The expression “Ballot to Bullet” indicated the rejection of:
o: The Chinese model of guerrilla warfare
264.x: The “Ballot to Bullet” line rejected the CPI(M)’s parliamentary path and favoured armed revolutionary struggle.
264.tq: Distinguish the rejected parliamentary route from the alternative guerrilla strategy.
xs: "**Ballot to Bullet**" rejected the **CPI(M)'s parliamentary path** — option **(1)** is correct.
The movement in fact embraced the **Chinese-model protracted guerrilla war** and **land redistribution** ("Land to the tiller"), so options (2) and (4) are wrong.
xa: The **CPI(ML)** was formed in **1969** and saw the Indian state as **semi-feudal**.
Its founder was **Charu Majumdar** (with **Kanu Sanyal**), based in **West Bengal**.
⚠ **Srikakulam** began under the **CPI(M)** and shifted to the **CPI(ML)** in **1969**.

264.s:
Consider the following statements about the CPI(ML):
1. It was formed in 1969.
2. It viewed the Indian State as semi-feudal.
3. It followed the Chinese-model concept of protracted guerrilla war.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
264.x: All three statements are correct. The CPI(ML) was formed in 1969, described India as semi-feudal and followed the Chinese-model strategy of protracted guerrilla war.
264.tq: Verify the formation year, ideological assessment and strategic doctrine as a single cluster.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **CPI(ML)** was formed in **1969**.
Statement 2 is correct: it saw the Indian state as **semi-feudal**.
Statement 3 is correct: it followed the **Chinese-model protracted guerrilla war** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: CPI(ML) founder: **Charu Majumdar** (with **Kanu Sanyal**); base **West Bengal**.
The **AP extremist CPI(ML) wing** (1967 split) was led by **Tarimela Nagi Reddy**, Chandra Pulla Reddy, Kolla Venkaiah and Nagabhushana Patnaik.
**People's War Group (PWG)**: **Kondapalli Seetharamaiah**, **1980**; **CPI (Maoist)**: PWG-MCC merger, **2004**.

264.s: Which of the following was NOT identified as a cause of the Naxalite movement?
o: Failure of land reforms, including tenancy reforms
Universal success of zamindari abolition and land ceilings
264.x: Land concentration, failed reforms such as zamindari abolition, ceilings and tenancy reforms, and tribal exploitation were identified as causes. Universal success of these reforms was not a cause.
264.tq: Reject the option that reverses the stated land-reform failure.
xs: **Universal success of zamindari abolition and land ceilings** was NOT a cause — option **(2)** is correct; the causes were their failure.
The notes list **land concentration**, **failed land reforms** (zamindari abolition, ceilings, tenancy) and **exploitation of tribals** as causes.
xa: The Naxalbari slogan was "**Land to the tiller**".
In AP, **Regulation 1 of 1970** tightened the **AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation** to stop tribal land passing to non-tribals.
**Srikakulam** was a tribal-peasant uprising against **landlords, moneylenders and forest officials**.

264.s: The Naxalbari peasant uprising of March-May 1967 was led by
o: Tarimela Nagi Reddy and Chandra Pulla Reddy
264.x: Charu Majumdar and Kanu Sanyal led the Naxalbari uprising in Darjeeling district. Nagi Reddy, Pulla Reddy, Venkaiah and Patnaik led the 1967 Andhra extremist wing; Kondapalli Seetharamaiah founded the PWG in 1980; Vempatapu Satyam is linked with Srikakulam.
264.tq: Naxalbari 1967 = Charu Majumdar + Kanu Sanyal.
xs: The Naxalbari uprising (**March-May 1967**) was led by **Charu Majumdar and Kanu Sanyal** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Tarimela Nagi Reddy**, **Chandra Pulla Reddy**, **Kolla Venkaiah** and **Nagabhushana Patnaik** led the **AP extremist CPI(ML) wing** (1967 split).
**Kondapalli Seetharamaiah** founded the **PWG** in **1980**.
xa: **Kanu Sanyal** with **Tarimela Nagi Reddy** also spread the **Srikakulam** struggle.
⚠ Some notes misprint Kanu Sanyal as "**Kasu Sanyal**".
Charu Majumdar went on to found the **CPI(ML)** in **1969**.

264.s: The Srikakulam Girijan struggle is generally placed in the period:
264.x: The Srikakulam Girijan struggle is generally dated to 1968–70, although 1968–69 is also used in some references.
264.tq: Distinguish the standard period from nearby movement and Emergency dates.
xs: The Srikakulam Girijan struggle is placed in **1968-70** — option **(4)** is correct (PYQ key).
⚠ Some notes give **1968-69**; **1975-77** is the **Emergency**, when Naxalite cadres were killed in alleged encounters.
xa: It took place in the **Srikakulam Agency** against landlords, moneylenders and forest officials.
Tribes involved: **Savaras (Soras)** and **Jatapus**.
It began under the **CPI(M)** and shifted to the **CPI(ML)** in **1969**.

264.s: The Srikakulam Girijan struggle was primarily a tribal-peasant uprising against:
o: Municipal authorities, contractors and port officials
Industrial workers, traders and railway officials
Colonial soldiers, zamindars and missionaries only
264.x: The uprising in the Srikakulam Agency was directed against landlords, moneylenders and forest officials.
264.tq: Identify the correct combination of immediate rural and forest-area adversaries.
xs: Srikakulam was a tribal-peasant uprising against **landlords, moneylenders and forest officials** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was fought in the **Srikakulam Agency** (tribal hills), not in towns, factories or ports.
xa: Tribes: **Savaras (Soras)** and **Jatapus**; period **1968-70**.
Later the **Girijan Cooperative Corporation (GCC)**, **Visakhapatnam**, procured minor forest produce to free tribals from **moneylenders**.
Outcome: suppressed by the State, but it seeded the **Naxalite movement** and revolutionary literature in Andhra.

264.s: Which of the following tribal communities were associated with the Srikakulam Girijan struggle?
264.x: The principal tribal communities associated with the struggle were the Savaras, also called Soras, and the Jatapus.
264.tq: Discriminate between the named Srikakulam tribes and other tribal groups of India.
xs: The tribes of the Srikakulam struggle were the **Savara (Sora) and Jatapu** — option **(3)** is correct.
The notes name only these two tribes for Srikakulam.
xa: The struggle was in the **Srikakulam Agency**, **1968-70**.
Leaders who spread it: **Kanu Sanyal** and **Tarimela Nagi Reddy**.
Target: **landlords, moneylenders and forest officials**.

264.s:
Consider the following statements about the political course of the Srikakulam struggle:
1. It began under the CPI(M).
2. It shifted to the CPI(ML) in 1969.
3. Kanu Sanyal and Tarimela Nagi Reddy are named as having spread the struggle.
4. It was led from the beginning by the CPI(ML) formed in 1969.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
264.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The struggle began under the CPI(M) and shifted to the CPI(ML) in 1969; therefore, it was not led by the CPI(ML) from the beginning.
264.tq: Track the organisational transition and reject the overbroad ‘from the beginning’ claim.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: Srikakulam began under the **CPI(M)**.
Statement 2 is correct: it shifted to the **CPI(ML)** in **1969**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Kanu Sanyal** and **Tarimela Nagi Reddy** spread it.
Statement 4 is wrong: the CPI(ML) was formed only in **1969**, so it could not lead from the start — answer **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: PYQ key: the "**1967** Srikakulam uprising" started under the **CPI(M)**.
The **CPI(ML)** saw the Indian state as **semi-feudal** and followed Chinese-model protracted guerrilla war.
Tribes: **Savaras (Soras)** and **Jatapus**.

264.s: Which one of the following best describes the immediate historical significance of the Srikakulam Girijan struggle?
o: It led directly to the formation of the Greyhounds in 1989.
It was suppressed by the State but seeded the Naxalite movement and revolutionary literature in Andhra.
It ended all tribal land conflicts in Andhra Pradesh through a constitutional settlement.
It established the CPI(ML) as the sole recognised political party in Andhra Pradesh.
264.x: The struggle was suppressed by the State, but it helped seed the Naxalite movement and revolutionary literature in Andhra.
264.tq: Choose the option that captures both suppression and longer-term political and cultural impact.
xs: Srikakulam **was suppressed by the State but seeded the Naxalite movement and revolutionary literature in Andhra** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **Greyhounds** came much later (raised **1989**), and the struggle did not end tribal land conflicts.
xa: It made AP a core base of **Indian Maoism**.
It reshaped Telugu literature via **Virasam (1970)** and **Jana Natya Mandali (1971)**.
State response included **Regulation 1 of 1970**, tightening the AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation.

264.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Organisation)
 a. CPI(ML)
 b. AP extremist CPI(ML) wing
 c. People’s War Group
 d. CPI (Maoist)

List-II (Founder or origin)
 i. Merger of PWG and MCC
 ii. Charu Majumdar with Kanu Sanyal
 iii. Kondapalli Seetharamaiah
 iv. Tarimela Nagi Reddy, Chandra Pulla Reddy, Kolla Venkaiah and Nagabhushana Patnaik

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
264.x: CPI(ML) is associated with Charu Majumdar and Kanu Sanyal; the AP extremist wing with the four Andhra leaders; PWG with Kondapalli Seetharamaiah; and CPI (Maoist) with the PWG–MCC merger.
264.tq: Start with the sure founder–organisation pairs and then complete the code.
xs: Correct match **a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i** — option **(1)**.
**CPI(ML)** — **Charu Majumdar** with Kanu Sanyal (**1969**); **AP extremist wing** — **Nagi Reddy**, Pulla Reddy, Venkaiah, Patnaik (**1967**).
**PWG** — **Kondapalli Seetharamaiah** (**1980**); **CPI (Maoist)** — merger of **PWG and MCC** (**2004**).
xa: PWG's stronghold was **North Telangana** in Andhra Pradesh.
CPI (Maoist) operates across the **Red Corridor**.
The **PWG was banned** in AP in **1992**.

264.s: The People’s War Group was founded by Kondapalli Seetharamaiah in:
264.x: Kondapalli Seetharamaiah founded the People’s War Group in 1980.
264.tq: Separate the PWG formation year from the CPI(ML), split and merger years.
xs: **Kondapalli Seetharamaiah** founded the **People's War Group** in **1980** — option **(3)** is correct.
**1967** = AP extremist CPI(ML) wing; **1969** = CPI(ML); **2004** = CPI (Maoist) from the PWG-MCC merger.
xa: The PWG's base was **Andhra Pradesh**, with **North Telangana** as its stronghold.
The **PWG was banned** in AP in **1992**.
Government-Maoist peace talks were held in Hyderabad in **October 2004** under the **YSR** government.

264.s:
Arrange the following organisations or developments in chronological order:
A. Formation of CPI (Maoist)
B. Formation of CPI(ML)
C. Formation of People’s War Group
D. Formation of the AP extremist CPI(ML) wing
264.x: The AP extremist CPI(ML) wing dates to 1967, CPI(ML) to 1969, PWG to 1980, and CPI (Maoist) to 2004.
264.tq: Fix the earliest and latest dates first, then place the 1969 and 1980 developments.
xs: Correct order **D, B, C, A** — option **(1)**.
xa: CPI(ML) founder: **Charu Majumdar** (with Kanu Sanyal).
PWG founder: **Kondapalli Seetharamaiah**.
CPI (Maoist) came from the merger of **PWG and MCC**.

264.s: The Revolutionary Writers’ Association, popularly known as Virasam, was founded on:
264.x: Virasam was founded on 4 July 1970 in Hyderabad.
264.tq: Distinguish the founding date from the February 1970 pamphlet episode and later cultural organisations.
xs: **Virasam** was founded on **4 July 1970** in **Hyderabad** — option **(4)** is correct.
**1-2 Feb 1970** was **Sri Sri's 60th-birthday** celebration at **Vizag**, where the seed pamphlet was distributed — not the founding.
xa: The pamphlet challenging writers was distributed by **Andhra University** students.
Founding president: **Sri Sri**; vice-presidents: **Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao** and **Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry**.
First meeting: **Khammam (1970)**; first revolutionary poetry collection: **Jhamjha (1970)**.

264.s: Which pair correctly identifies the vice-presidents of Virasam at its founding?
o: Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao and Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry
264.x: Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao and Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry were the founding vice-presidents of Virasam.
264.tq: Discriminate the office-holders from the president and associated cultural-body founders.
xs: Virasam's founding vice-presidents were **Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao and Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Sri Sri** was the founding **president**; **Narsinga Rao and Gaddar** founded **Art Lovers**; **Charu Majumdar and Kanu Sanyal** led Naxalbari.
xa: Virasam was founded on **4 July 1970**, **Hyderabad**.
Seed: pamphlet at **Sri Sri's 60th-birthday** celebrations (**1-2 Feb 1970, Vizag**).
First meeting at **Khammam (1970)**.

264.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First revolutionary poetry collection — Jana Natya Mandali, 1971
Art Lovers — Sri Sri and Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry
Jana Natya Mandali — founded in 1967 by Charu Majumdar
264.x: The first Virasam meeting was held at Khammam in 1970. Jhamjha was the first revolutionary poetry collection, while Art Lovers was associated with B. Narsinga Rao and Gaddar.
264.tq: Find the one correctly matched event and reject swapped cultural organisations and names.
xs: **First Virasam meeting — Khammam, 1970** is correctly matched — option **(2)**.
The first revolutionary poetry collection was **Jhamjha (1970)**, not Jana Natya Mandali.
**Art Lovers** was founded by **B. Narsinga Rao and Gaddar**, and became **Jana Natya Mandali** in **1971** — not linked to Charu Majumdar.
xa: Virasam: founded **4 July 1970**, **Hyderabad**; president **Sri Sri**.
Vice-presidents: **Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao** and **Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry**.
Seed pamphlet by **Andhra University** students at Sri Sri's **60th-birthday** (Vizag).

264.s: The first revolutionary poetry collection associated with this literary movement was:
264.x: Jhamjha, published in 1970, is identified as the first revolutionary poetry collection.
264.tq: Distinguish the title of the poetry collection from names of organisations and slogans.
xs: The first revolutionary poetry collection was **Jhamjha (1970)** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Virasam** is the writers' body (**1970**), **Art Lovers** a cultural troupe (**1970**), and "**Ballot to Bullet**" a political line — none is a poetry collection.
xa: First Virasam meeting: **Khammam (1970)**.
**Art Lovers** (B. Narsinga Rao and Gaddar) → renamed **Jana Natya Mandali (1971)**.
Virasam's founding president was **Sri Sri**.

264.s: Who was the founding president of the Revolutionary Writers' Association (Virasam), formed in Hyderabad on 4 July 1970?
264.x: Sri Sri was Virasam's founding president; the seed was a pamphlet handed out by Andhra University students at his 60th-birthday celebrations in Vizag in 1970. Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao and Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry were vice-presidents; Gaddar was with Art Lovers / Jana Natya Mandali.
264.tq: Virasam: president Sri Sri; VPs KoKu + Ravi Sastry; JNM = Gaddar.
xs: **Sri Sri** was Virasam's founding president — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao** and **Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry** were vice-presidents; **Gaddar** co-founded **Art Lovers** (later Jana Natya Mandali).
xa: The seed was a pamphlet distributed by **Andhra University** students at **Sri Sri's 60th-birthday** celebrations (**1-2 Feb 1970, Vizag**).
First meeting: **Khammam (1970)**; first collection: **Jhamjha (1970)**.
Through Virasam and **Jana Natya Mandali**, Srikakulam reshaped **Telugu literature**.

264.s: Integrated Tribal Development Agencies (ITDAs) were set up under the Tribal Sub-Plan from:
264.x: ITDAs were set up under the Tribal Sub-Plan from the Fifth Plan, beginning in 1974–75.
264.tq: Link the institutional arrangement with the correct Five-Year Plan and starting year.
xs: **ITDAs** were set up under the **Tribal Sub-Plan** from the **Fifth Plan (1974-75)** — option **(3)** is correct.
ITDA = **Integrated Tribal Development Agency**, for tribal development.
xa: **AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation** was tightened in **1970** (**Regulation 1 of 1970**) to stop tribal land passing to non-tribals.
**Girijan Cooperative Corporation (GCC)**, **Visakhapatnam**, procures minor forest produce and supplies essentials.
These measures followed the movement putting **tribal land alienation** at the centre of politics.
