264.s: The Girijan Cooperative Corporation headquartered at Visakhapatnam primarily:
o: Administers peace talks between the government and Maoists
Investigates alleged encounter killings during the Emergency
Conducts anti-Naxal operations and trains Greyhounds personnel
Procures minor forest produce and supplies essentials to reduce tribal dependence on moneylenders
264.x: The Girijan Cooperative Corporation procures minor forest produce and supplies essential goods, helping free tribals from moneylenders.
264.tq: Match the institution with its economic function and reject security or inquiry functions.
xs: The **GCC**, **Visakhapatnam**, **procures minor forest produce and supplies essentials**, freeing tribals from **moneylenders** — option **(4)** is correct.
Encounter killings were probed by the **Bhargava Commission (1977)**; anti-Naxal operations are the **Greyhounds'** job; peace talks were held by the government in **2004**.
xa: **ITDAs** came under the **Tribal Sub-Plan** from the **Fifth Plan (1974-75)**.
**Regulation 1 of 1970** tightened the AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation.
Srikakulam was directed against **landlords, moneylenders and forest officials**.

264.s: Which of the following correctly reflects the impact of the movement on political priorities?
o: It removed land issues from tribal politics and focused exclusively on urban labour.
It placed land to the tiller and tribal land alienation at the centre of politics; Dalits within it later concentrated on land struggles.
It opposed all land redistribution and cooperative institutions.
It treated land alienation as solely a cultural issue without an economic dimension.
264.x: The movement placed land to the tiller and tribal land alienation at the centre of politics, and Dalits within it later concentrated on land struggles.
264.tq: Select the comprehensive statement that preserves both the general and Dalit-related land dimensions.
xs: The movement **placed land to the tiller and tribal land alienation at the centre of politics**; **Dalits** within it later concentrated on **land struggles** — option **(2)** is correct.
It did not drop land issues or oppose redistribution — its very slogan was "**Land to the tiller**".
xa: Responses: **Regulation 1 of 1970** (land transfer), **ITDAs** (Fifth Plan, **1974-75**), **GCC** (Visakhapatnam).
Causes: **land concentration**, failed land reforms and **exploitation of tribals**.
Literary impact: **Virasam** and **Jana Natya Mandali**.

264.s: The AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation was tightened in 1970 (Regulation 1 of 1970) mainly to
o: stop land in Scheduled Areas passing from tribals to non-tribals
set up Integrated Tribal Development Agencies
allow procurement of minor forest produce by the GCC
abolish zamindari in the Srikakulam Agency
264.x: Regulation 1 of 1970, a response to the tribal unrest, barred transfer of land in Scheduled Areas from tribals to non-tribals. ITDAs came under the Tribal Sub-Plan from the Fifth Plan (1974-75); minor forest produce procurement is the Girijan Cooperative Corporation's work; zamindari abolition was not the Regulation's purpose.
264.tq: Regulation 1 of 1970 = no tribal-to-non-tribal land transfer (LTR).
xs: **Regulation 1 of 1970** was meant to **stop land in Scheduled Areas passing from tribals to non-tribals** — option **(1)** is correct.
**ITDAs** came under the Tribal Sub-Plan from the **Fifth Plan (1974-75)**; procuring minor forest produce is the **GCC's** work.
xa: The **GCC** is at **Visakhapatnam** and frees tribals from moneylenders.
The movement made **tribal land alienation** a central political issue.
Srikakulam tribes: **Savaras (Soras)** and **Jatapus**.

264.s: The Greyhounds, raised in 1989, is best described as which of the following?
o: A paramilitary unit under the Ministry of Home Affairs
A dog squad attached to the Forest Department
An elite anti-Naxal special police force of the Andhra Pradesh Police
A Central disaster-response force trained for flood rescue
264.x: Greyhounds is an elite anti-Naxal special police force unit of the Andhra Pradesh Police, raised in 1989. It is not a dog squad or disaster-response unit.
264.tq: Use the exact institutional description and reject look-alike options.
xs: The **Greyhounds** is an **elite anti-Naxal special police force of the Andhra Pradesh Police**, raised in **1989** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is a police special forces unit — **not a dog squad** or a **disaster unit**.
xa: Under DGP **H.J. Dora** (**1996-2002**) it neutralised top Naxalite leaders; **over 1,200 cadres** surrendered (**1998-2001**).
Post-bifurcation **Greyhounds Training Centre**: **Anandapuram** (near Visakhapatnam), under **Sec. 9** of the AP Reorganisation Act, **2014**.
The **PWG was banned** in AP in **1992**.

264.s: The People's War Group (PWG) was banned in Andhra Pradesh in:
264.x: The PWG was banned in Andhra Pradesh in 1992.
264.tq: Fix the year by distinguishing the ban from the formation and policing milestones.
xs: The **PWG was banned** in Andhra Pradesh in **1992** — option **(2)** is correct.
**1989** = Greyhounds raised; **1996** = start of H.J. Dora's term as DGP; **2004** = Hyderabad peace talks / CPI (Maoist).
xa: The PWG was founded by **Kondapalli Seetharamaiah** in **1980**.
PWG merged with MCC to form the **CPI (Maoist)** in **2004**.
Peace talks: **October 2004**, Hyderabad, **YSR** government.

264.s: Government–Maoist peace talks were held in Hyderabad in October 2004 during the tenure of which government?
264.x: Government–Maoist talks were held in Hyderabad in October 2004 during the YSR government.
264.tq: Match the event, place, month and government rather than relying on the year alone.
xs: Government-Maoist peace talks in Hyderabad in **October 2004** were held under the **YSR government** — option **(3)** is correct.
2004 was also the year the **CPI (Maoist)** formed from the **PWG-MCC** merger.
xa: The **PWG was banned** in AP in **1992**.
Earlier, under DGP **H.J. Dora** (**1996-2002**), **over 1,200 cadres** surrendered (**1998-2001**).
National toolkit includes **rehabilitation** for surrendering cadres + **dialogue**.

264.s: After bifurcation, the Greyhounds Training Centre was built at:
o: Warangal near the North Telangana stronghold
264.x: The post-bifurcation Greyhounds Training Centre was built at Anandapuram, near Visakhapatnam.
264.tq: Test the precise location and distinguish it from other Naxalite-affected areas.
xs: The post-bifurcation **Greyhounds Training Centre** was built at **Anandapuram near Visakhapatnam** — option **(4)** is correct.
It was built under **Sec. 9** of the **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014**.
xa: It is credited with sharply reducing Naxal activity in **Alluri Sitharama Raju** and **Parvathipuram Manyam** districts.
These districts lie along the **Odisha-Chhattisgarh** borders.
The Greyhounds were raised in **1989** as AP's elite anti-Naxal police force.

264.s: The Greyhounds base at Anandapuram is associated with securing the Left-Wing Extremism corridor in which districts?
o: Alluri Sitharama Raju and Parvathipuram Manyam
264.x: The Anandapuram Greyhounds base is credited with securing the LWE corridor in the Alluri Sitharama Raju and Parvathipuram Manyam districts along the Odisha–Chhattisgarh borders.
264.tq: Use the paired-district clue and avoid substituting neighbouring Andhra districts.
xs: The Anandapuram base secures the LWE corridor of **Alluri Sitharama Raju and Parvathipuram Manyam** — option **(1)** is correct.
These districts lie along the **Odisha-Chhattisgarh** borders.
xa: The training centre was built under **Sec. 9** of the **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014**.
Anandapuram is **near Visakhapatnam**.
Ex-DGP **H.J. Dora**, who led the Greyhounds during the PWG peak, died in **March 2026**.

264.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the major components of the national toolkit for addressing Naxalism?
o: Exclusive reliance on military rule without dialogue
Development of roads and mobile towers
264.x: The national toolkit includes intelligence-led operations, stronger state police, rehabilitation, dialogue, and development of roads and mobile towers. Exclusive reliance on military rule is not included.
264.tq: Find the option that reverses the combined security, rehabilitation, dialogue and development approach.
xs: **Exclusive reliance on military rule without dialogue** is NOT in the national toolkit — option **(1)** is correct.
The toolkit includes **intelligence-driven operations** + stronger state police, **rehabilitation** + **dialogue**, and **roads and mobile towers**.
xa: AP example: under DGP **H.J. Dora**, intelligence-led policing secured the surrender of **over 1,200 cadres (1998-2001)**.
Dialogue example: Government-Maoist talks in **Hyderabad**, **October 2004**.
The **Greyhounds** (raised **1989**) are AP's elite anti-Naxal force.

264.s: During the Emergency period, many Naxalite cadres in Andhra Pradesh were killed in alleged encounters during:
264.x: Many Naxalite cadres were killed in alleged encounters in Andhra Pradesh during the Emergency, 1975–77.
264.tq: Separate the Emergency period from the Srikakulam struggle and PWG formation dates.
xs: During the **Emergency (1975-77)** many Naxalite cadres in AP were killed in alleged **"encounters"** — option **(1)** is correct.
**1968-70** is the **Srikakulam** struggle, not the Emergency.
xa: The **Bhargava Commission** (**1977**) inquired into these encounter killings.
It was headed by **Justice Vashist Bhargava**.
The **PWG** was later **banned** in AP in **1992**.

264.s: The Bhargava Commission was set up in 1977 to inquire into:
o: The reorganisation of Andhra Pradesh districts
Alleged encounter killings of Naxalite cadres in Andhra Pradesh
The procurement activities of the Girijan Cooperative Corporation
264.x: The Bhargava Commission, headed by Justice Vashist Bhargava, was set up in 1977 to inquire into alleged encounter killings during the Emergency.
264.tq: Match the commission with its subject of inquiry and its historical context.
xs: The **Bhargava Commission (1977)** inquired into **alleged encounter killings of Naxalite cadres in Andhra Pradesh** — option **(2)** is correct.
The killings took place during the **Emergency (1975-77)**.
xa: It was headed by **Justice Vashist Bhargava**.
The **CPI(ML)** was formed in **1969**, under **Charu Majumdar**.
The **GCC** (Visakhapatnam) procures minor forest produce — unrelated to the commission.

264.s: Who headed the Bhargava Commission?
264.x: The Bhargava Commission was headed by Justice Vashist Bhargava.
264.tq: Use the commission-name and chairperson pairing rather than importing unrelated judges.
xs: The Bhargava Commission was headed by **Justice Vashist Bhargava** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was set up in **1977** to inquire into encounter killings of Naxalites in AP.
xa: The killings occurred during the **Emergency (1975-77)**.
Later state responses: **Greyhounds** (**1989**), **PWG ban** (**1992**).
Peace talks: **October 2004**, Hyderabad.

264.s: Which one of the following statements best expresses the wider significance of the Srikakulam movement for Andhra Pradesh?
o: It made Andhra Pradesh a core base of Indian Maoism and reshaped Telugu literature through Virasam and Jana Natya Mandali.
It ended all Maoist activity in Andhra Pradesh after 1970.
It led only to the creation of a police training institution and had no social impact.
It remained confined to a short electoral campaign with no literary influence.
264.x: Srikakulam helped make Andhra Pradesh a core base of Indian Maoism and influenced Telugu literature through Virasam and Jana Natya Mandali.
264.tq: Choose the option that combines the political and literary consequences without using an absolute claim.
xs: Srikakulam **made Andhra Pradesh a core base of Indian Maoism** and **reshaped Telugu literature** through **Virasam** and **Jana Natya Mandali** — option **(1)** is correct.
Maoist activity did not end after 1970 — the **PWG (1980)** and **CPI (Maoist) (2004)** followed.
xa: **Virasam** was founded on **4 July 1970**, Hyderabad; president **Sri Sri**.
**Art Lovers (1970)** → **Jana Natya Mandali (1971)** (B. Narsinga Rao and Gaddar).
AP angle: the **Greyhounds** base at **Anandapuram** secures the **ASR** and **Parvathipuram Manyam** LWE corridor.

264.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Greyhounds operations under DGP H.J. Dora:
1. H.J. Dora served as DGP during 1996–2002.
2. Greyhounds neutralised several top Naxalite leaders during this period.
3. More than 1,200 cadres surrendered during 1998–2001.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
264.x: All three statements are correct. H.J. Dora was DGP from 1996 to 2002, Greyhounds neutralised several top leaders, and over 1,200 cadres surrendered during 1998–2001.
264.tq: Check the linked office, operational outcome and surrender figures together.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **H.J. Dora** was DGP during **1996-2002**.
Statement 2 is correct: the **Greyhounds** neutralised several top Naxalite leaders under him.
Statement 3 is correct: **over 1,200 cadres** surrendered in **1998-2001** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: H.J. Dora led the Greyhounds during the **PWG** peak and died in **March 2026**.
The Greyhounds were raised in **1989**; the **PWG was banned** in **1992**.
Training centre: **Anandapuram** (near Visakhapatnam), **Sec. 9**, AP Reorganisation Act **2014**.

264.s: The Greyhounds base at Anandapuram in Andhra Pradesh secures the Left Wing Extremism corridor of which districts?
o: Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR) and Parvathipuram Manyam
264.x: The Greyhounds base at Anandapuram secures the LWE corridor of the Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR) and Parvathipuram Manyam districts in north coastal Andhra Pradesh.
264.tq: Anandapuram guards the northern Agency hills: ASR + Manyam.
xs: The Anandapuram base secures the LWE corridor of **Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR) and Parvathipuram Manyam** — option **(4)** is correct.
These districts border **Odisha-Chhattisgarh**; the other district pairs are not named in the notes.
xa: The base is the post-bifurcation **Greyhounds Training Centre**, built under **Sec. 9** of the **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014**.
Anandapuram is **near Visakhapatnam**.
The **Greyhounds** are AP Police's elite **anti-Naxal special police force**, raised in **1989**.

265.s: The Karamchedu massacre of Dalits took place in which district?
265.x: The Karamchedu massacre occurred in Prakasam district on 17 July 1985.
265.tq: Apply the event–district location pair.
xs: The **Karamchedu** massacre of Dalits took place in **Prakasam** district — option **(4)** is correct.
It is dated **17 July 1985** (one source says **1982**).
**Guntur** is the district of the **Chunduru** massacre (**6 Aug 1991**); **Nellore** is linked with the anti-arrack movement.
xa: After Karamchedu, Dalits broke away from the **Congress and Communist parties** and formed **independent Dalit Mahasabhas**.
The **AP Dalit Mahasabha** was founded in **1985** by **Katti Padmarao** (Bojja Tarakam also a founder).
⚠ **Karamchedu** = **Prakasam**, 1985; **Chunduru** = **Guntur**, 1991.

265.s: The Chunduru massacre occurred on 6 August 1991 in which district?
265.x: The Chunduru massacre occurred on 6 August 1991 in Guntur district.
265.tq: Combine the date with the correct district to avoid event-location reversal.
xs: The **Chunduru** massacre (**6 Aug 1991**) occurred in **Guntur** district — option **(3)** is correct.
**Prakasam** is the district of the **Karamchedu** massacre (**17 July 1985**).
xa: ⚠ **Karamchedu** = **Prakasam**, 1985; **Chunduru** = **Guntur**, 1991.
1991 was also the year the **anti-arrack movement** began at **Dubagunta**, **Nellore**.
Leaders of modern Dalit assertion include **Katti Padmarao**, **Gaddar**, **Manda Krishna Madiga** and **Jupudi Prabhakar Rao**.

265.s: Which of the following developments followed the Karamchedu incident?
o: Dalits formed independent Dalit Mahasabhas after breaking away from Congress and Communist parties.
Total prohibition was imposed across Andhra Pradesh.
The Mandal Commission was immediately constituted.
The MRPS was founded at Eedumudi.
265.x: After Karamchedu, Dalits broke away from the Congress and Communist parties and formed independent Dalit Mahasabhas.
265.tq: Identify the political consequence directly linked to the event.
xs: After Karamchedu, **Dalits broke away from the Congress and Communist parties** and **formed independent Dalit Mahasabhas** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Total prohibition** came only in **1995**, after the anti-arrack movement — not a result of Karamchedu.
xa: Karamchedu: **Prakasam** district, **17 July 1985**.
The **AP Dalit Mahasabha** (**1985**) was founded by **Katti Padmarao**; **Bojja Tarakam** was also a founder.
Precursors: **Bhagya Reddy Varma's** Adi-Andhra conference (**1919**) and **Kusuma Dharmanna's** Adi-Andhra Mahasabha (**1936**).

265.s: Which one of the following is NOT associated with modern Dalit assertion in Andhra Pradesh?
265.x: Kaka Kalelkar chaired the First National Backward Class Commission and is not listed among the leaders of modern Dalit assertion in Andhra Pradesh. Katti Padmarao, Manda Krishna Madiga and Endluri Sudhakar are associated with that assertion.
265.tq: Find the outsider in a group of movement leaders.
xs: **Kaka Kalelkar** is NOT listed among leaders of modern Dalit assertion in AP — option **(1)** is correct.
The listed leaders are **Katti Padmarao**, **Gaddar**, **Manda Krishna Madiga**, **Jupudi Prabhakar Rao**, **Endluri Sudhakar** and **Boyi Bhimanna**.
xa: **Katti Padmarao** founded the **AP Dalit Mahasabha** (**1985**).
**Bojja Tarakam** was also a founder of the AP Dalit Mahasabha.
The **MRPS** is named among the bodies of caste assertion that reshaped AP politics.

265.s: Who founded the Andhra Pradesh Dalit Mahasabha?
o: Katti Padmarao, with Bojja Tarakam also recognised as a founder
265.x: The Andhra Pradesh Dalit Mahasabha was founded in 1985 after Karamchedu, with Katti Padmarao identified as its founder and Bojja Tarakam also recognised as a founder.
265.tq: Handle a multiple-founder distinction without reducing it to a single-name association.
xs: The AP Dalit Mahasabha was founded by **Katti Padmarao**, with **Bojja Tarakam** also recognised as a founder — option **(3)** is correct.
**Bojja Tarakam alone** is wrong, and **Manda Krishna Madiga** and **Gaddar** are other leaders of Dalit assertion, not its founders.
xa: It was founded in **1985**, after the **Karamchedu** massacre (**Prakasam**).
Precursors: **Bhagya Reddy Varma** (Machilipatnam, **1919**) and **Kusuma Dharmanna** (Vizianagaram, **1936**).
AP's Adi-Andhra leaders were inspired by Phule's **Satyashodhak Samaj (1873)** and Periyar's **Self-Respect Movement**.

265.s: The Andhra Pradesh Dalit Mahasabha was founded in which year?
265.x: The Andhra Pradesh Dalit Mahasabha was founded in 1985, following the Karamchedu incident.
265.tq: Match the organisation with its founding year.
xs: The **AP Dalit Mahasabha** was founded in **1985** — option **(2)** is correct.
It followed the **Karamchedu** massacre (**17 July 1985**); **1991** is Chunduru, and **1982** is a variant date some notes give for Karamchedu.
xa: Founder: **Katti Padmarao**; **Bojja Tarakam** also a founder.
After Karamchedu, Dalits left the **Congress and Communist parties** to form independent Mahasabhas.
**Chunduru** massacre: **6 Aug 1991**, **Guntur**.

265.s:
Consider the following statements about precursors of the AP Dalit Mahasabha:
1. Bhagya Reddy Varma's Adi-Andhra movement held its Machilipatnam conference in 1919.
2. Kusuma Dharmanna's 1936 Adi-Andhra Mahasabha was held at Machilipatnam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
265.x: Statement 1 is correct: Bhagya Reddy Varma's conference was at Machilipatnam in 1919. Statement 2 is wrong: the 1936 Adi-Andhra Mahasabha of Kusuma Dharmanna was held at Vizianagaram. So only 1; B, C and D are therefore wrong.
265.tq: 1919 Machilipatnam = Bhagya Reddy Varma; 1936 Vizianagaram = Kusuma Dharmanna.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Bhagya Reddy Varma's** Adi-Andhra conference was at **Machilipatnam** in **1919**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Kusuma Dharmanna's** **1936** Adi-Andhra Mahasabha was at **Vizianagaram** — so **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: The **1919 Machilipatnam** conference demanded abolition of the **Jogini and Devadasi** systems.
⚠ **1936** = Kusuma Dharmanna (Vizianagaram) **and** the **All India Kisan Sabha**.
These two Adi-Andhra bodies are the **precursors** of the AP Dalit Mahasabha (**1985**).

265.s: The Anantharaman Commission of Andhra Pradesh is correctly described as the commission that:
o: Checked whether minorities were included in the BC list in 1982
Was the first AP Backward Class Commission and grouped BCs into A–D categories
Granted constitutional status to the NCBC
265.x: The Anantharaman Commission, functioning during 1968–70, was the first AP Backward Class Commission and grouped BCs into A–D categories.
265.tq: Identify the commission from its distinctive function and period.
xs: The **Anantharaman Commission** (**1968-70**) **was the first AP Backward Class Commission** and **grouped BCs into A-D** — option **(2)** is correct.
Checking whether minorities were in the BC list was the **Muralidhar Rao Commission** (took charge **27 Jan 1982**).
xa: ⚠ FIRST AP BC Commission = **Anantharaman**, not Muralidhar Rao.
Muralidhar Rao combined BC, ST and religious-group populations as **29.08%**, leading to a big rise in the reservation quota.
**86 castes** are recognised as BCs in Andhra; Telangana has a separate list.

265.s: Which function was associated with the Muralidhar Rao Commission?
o: It introduced the A–B–C–D categorisation of Scheduled Castes.
It examined whether minorities were included in the Backward Class list.
It imposed prohibition throughout Andhra Pradesh.
It conducted the first national survey of OBC population.
265.x: The Muralidhar Rao Commission examined whether minorities were included in the Backward Class list.
265.tq: Match the commission with its precise terms of reference.
xs: The **Muralidhar Rao Commission** **examined whether minorities were included in the Backward Class list** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **A-D** grouping of BCs was the **Anantharaman Commission's** work (the first AP BC Commission, **1968-70**).
xa: Muralidhar Rao took charge on **27 Jan 1982**.
It combined BC, ST and religious-group populations as **29.08%**.
Its report led to a big rise in the State's **reservation quota**.

265.s: How many castes were recognised as Backward Classes in Andhra, with a separate list maintained for Telangana?
265.x: Eighty-six castes were recognised as Backward Classes in Andhra, while Telangana had a separate list.
265.tq: Check the exact count and the territorial qualification together.
xs: **86 castes** were recognised as BCs in Andhra, with a separate list for Telangana — option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ Do not reverse the digits — **68** is not the count.
xa: The first AP BC Commission was the **Anantharaman Commission** (**1968-70**), which grouped BCs into **A-D**.
The **Muralidhar Rao Commission** took charge on **27 Jan 1982**.
After **Mandal**, OBC and Dalit movements split over **sub-categorisation**.

265.s:
Consider the following statements about Bhu Poratam:
1. It was jointly launched by the CPI and CPI(M) in Andhra Pradesh.
2. It was launched in 1997.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
265.x: Statement 1 is correct: Bhu Poratam was a joint CPI-CPI(M) land struggle. Statement 2 is wrong: it was launched in 2007, not 1997. Hence 1 only; options B, C and D wrongly accept the 1997 date or reject the CPI-CPI(M) link.
265.tq: Bhu Poratam = CPI + CPI(M), 2007.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Bhu Poratam** was jointly launched by the **CPI and CPI(M)** in AP.
Statement 2 is wrong: it was launched in **2007**, not 1997 — so **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Aim: occupy and distribute **government and surplus land** to the landless.
It continues the Communist **tenancy and land campaigns of 1956-69**.
⚠ **1997** is the year prohibition was lifted in AP.

265.s: The principal objective of Bhu Poratam was to occupy and distribute which land to the landless?
265.x: Bhu Poratam sought the occupation and distribution of government and surplus land to landless people.
265.tq: Identify the precise scope of land targeted by the campaign.
xs: Bhu Poratam aimed to occupy and distribute **government and surplus land** to the landless — option **(1)** is correct.
The notes name no forest, temple or private land as its target.
xa: Launched jointly by the **CPI and CPI(M)** in **2007**.
It continued the Communist **tenancy and land campaigns of 1956-69**.
The **AIKS** (founded **1936**) was one of the mass organisations the CPI worked through.

265.s: Bhu Poratam continued which earlier Communist tradition in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Industrial strikes and railway campaigns of 1942–45
265.x: Bhu Poratam continued the Communist tradition of tenancy and land campaigns carried out during 1956–69.
265.tq: Link a later movement with its stated historical continuity.
xs: Bhu Poratam continued the Communist **tenancy and land campaigns of 1956-69** — option **(2)** is correct.
The anti-arrack movement began only in **1991** and was led by rural women, not the Communist parties.
xa: Bhu Poratam: **CPI and CPI(M)**, **2007**.
Its aim was to distribute **government and surplus land** to the landless.
The **power tariff agitation (2000)** was another Left-farmer protest, against electricity tariff hikes.

265.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. N.G. Ranga founded the Indian Peasants' Institute at Nidubrolu in 1933.
2. N.G. Ranga was one of the founders of the All India Kisan Sabha in 1936.
3. The All India Kisan Sabha was one of the mass organisations through which the Congress worked.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
265.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Ranga founded the Nidubrolu institute (1933) and co-founded the AIKS (1936). Statement 3 is wrong: the AIKS was a mass organisation of the CPI, not the Congress. So A; B, C and D all include the wrong statement 3.
265.tq: Nidubrolu 1933, AIKS 1936, AIKS worked for CPI.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **N.G. Ranga** founded the Indian Peasants' Institute at **Nidubrolu** in **1933**.
Statement 2 is correct: he was a founder of the **All India Kisan Sabha** (**1936**).
Statement 3 is wrong: the AIKS was a mass organisation of the **CPI**, not the Congress — answer **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: ⚠ **1933** = Nidubrolu institute; **1936** = Kisan Sabha — both **N.G. Ranga**.
**1936** was also the year of **Kusuma Dharmanna's** Adi-Andhra Mahasabha at **Vizianagaram**.
N.G. Ranga is described as a **peasant leader**.

265.s: The power tariff agitation of 2000 was directed against which issue?
o: Auction of arrack shops under prohibition policy
Hikes in electricity tariffs under power-sector reforms
265.x: Left parties and farmers protested electricity tariff hikes introduced under power-sector reforms during the 2000 agitation.
265.tq: Connect the agitation with the policy issue that triggered it.
xs: The **2000** power tariff agitation was against **hikes in electricity tariffs under power-sector reforms** — option **(4)** is correct.
It was led by **Left parties + farmers** in **Hyderabad**.
xa: Police opened fire at **Bashir Bagh, Hyderabad**, on **28 Aug 2000**.
Another Left-led campaign was **Bhu Poratam** (**CPI and CPI(M)**, **2007**).
Arrack auctions were the target of the separate **anti-arrack movement** (**1991**).

265.s: The Bashir Bagh firing associated with the power tariff agitation took place on:
265.x: Police opened fire at Bashir Bagh in Hyderabad on 28 August 2000 during the power tariff agitation.
265.tq: Combine the incident, date and location before choosing.
xs: The **Bashir Bagh** firing took place on **28 Aug 2000 in Hyderabad** — option **(1)** is correct.
**27 Jan 1982** is when the Muralidhar Rao Commission took charge; **1 Oct 1993** is arrack prohibition; **6 Aug 1991** is the Chunduru massacre.
xa: The agitation, by **Left parties + farmers**, protested **electricity tariff hikes** under power-sector reforms.
Its year: **2000**.
Other Left-led land struggle: **Bhu Poratam (2007)**.

265.s: The anti-arrack movement in Andhra Pradesh began in 1991 at which place?
265.x: The movement began in 1991 at Dubagunta village in Nellore district.
265.tq: Use the location-specific direct-recall approach.
xs: The anti-arrack movement began in **1991** at **Dubagunta village in Nellore district** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Nidubrolu** is linked with **N.G. Ranga's** Indian Peasants' Institute (**1933**); **Chunduru** is the **1991** massacre site in **Guntur**.
xa: Leader: **Vardhineni Rosamma**, with rural women.
It grew out of **"Aksharajyothi"** adult-literacy classes.
1930s precursor: **Kallur Subbarao's** anti-liquor and Swadeshi movements in the **Dattamandalas** (**Rayalaseema**).

265.s: The anti-arrack agitation of 1991 emerged primarily from discussions held in which programme?
o: Workers' education classes under the Kisan Sabha
265.x: Women discussed the effects of men's arrack drinking during Aksharajyothi adult-literacy classes, which helped initiate the agitation.
265.tq: Identify the immediate institutional origin of a movement.
xs: The agitation grew out of **"Aksharajyothi"** **adult-literacy classes** — option **(1)** is correct.
The lessons led women to discuss men's **arrack drinking**, **debt**, **domestic violence** and men missing work.
xa: Origin: **1991**, **Dubagunta**, **Nellore**.
Methods: women closed arrack shops and stopped auctions using **broomsticks and chilli powder**.
Outcome: **arrack prohibited** in AP on **1 Oct 1993**.

265.s: Who was the prominent woman leader of the Dubagunta anti-arrack movement?
265.x: Vardhineni Rosamma of Dubagunta was a prominent leader of the anti-arrack movement.
265.tq: Test the leader associated with the specific locality and movement.
xs: **Vardhineni Rosamma** of **Dubagunta** led the anti-arrack movement — option **(1)** is correct.
**Bhagya Reddy Varma** (**1919**) and **Kusuma Dharmanna** (**1936**) led Adi-Andhra bodies; **Jupudi Prabhakar Rao** is a Dalit assertion leader.
xa: The movement began in **1991** in **Dubagunta village, Nellore district**.
It was led by **rural women**.
It is one of India's most successful **women-led movements**.

265.s: Which of the following best describes the immediate demand of the anti-arrack movement?
o: Stopping the sale and auction of arrack
Abolition of land revenue and tenancy
265.x: The movement demanded an end to the sale and auction of arrack.
265.tq: Match the movement with its central demand rather than its method of protest.
xs: The movement's demand was **stopping the sale and auction of arrack** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Electricity tariffs** were the issue of the **2000** power tariff agitation, not the anti-arrack movement.
xa: Women **closed arrack shops** and **stopped arrack auctions**.
It spread from **Nellore** to the whole State.
Outcome: **arrack prohibited** from **1 Oct 1993**; **total prohibition** in **1995**.

265.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to prohibition in Andhra Pradesh in chronological order:
A. Prohibition was lifted.
B. Arrack was prohibited in Andhra Pradesh.
C. Total prohibition was imposed across the State.
265.x: Arrack was prohibited on 1 October 1993, total prohibition followed in 1995, and prohibition was lifted in 1997.
265.tq: Use the first-middle-last sequence to order closely related years.
xs: Correct order **B, C, A** — option **(1)**.
**Arrack prohibited** (**1 Oct 1993**) → **total prohibition** across the State (**1995**) → **prohibition lifted** (**1997**).
xa: The 1995 prohibition was later "**largely abandoned**".
The trigger was the **anti-arrack movement** of **1991** at **Dubagunta**, **Nellore**.
It grew out of **Aksharajyothi** adult-literacy classes.

265.s:
Which methods were notably used by women during the Anti-arrack movement?
1. Closing arrack shops
2. Stopping arrack auctions
3. Using broomsticks and chilli powder
4. Conducting legislative elections
Which of the statements given above are correct?
265.x: Women closed arrack shops and stopped arrack auctions, using broomsticks and chilli powder. Legislative elections were not a stated method of the movement.
265.tq: Find the one unrelated activity among concrete movement methods.
xs: Women **closed arrack shops**, **stopped arrack auctions** and used **broomsticks and chilli powder** — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
**Conducting legislative elections** is not a method the notes mention.
xa: The movement was led by **rural women**, with **Vardhineni Rosamma** as leader.
It began in **1991** at **Dubagunta**, **Nellore**.
Demand: stop the **sale and auction of arrack**.

265.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the geographical spread of the Anti-arrack movement?
o: It remained confined to Dubagunta village.
It spread from Machilipatnam to Madras Presidency.
It began in Hyderabad and spread only to Telangana.
It spread from Nellore to the whole State.
265.x: The movement spread from Nellore district to the whole of Andhra Pradesh.
265.tq: Test the movement’s origin-to-spread pattern using nearby geographical distractors.
xs: The anti-arrack movement **spread from Nellore to the whole State** — option **(4)** is correct.
It did not stay confined to **Dubagunta** village, where it began in **1991**.
xa: Outcome: **arrack prohibited** in AP on **1 Oct 1993**.
**Total prohibition** followed in **1995** (later abandoned); prohibition lifted in **1997**.
It is one of India's most successful **women-led** movements.

265.s: The Anti-arrack movement is regarded as one of India’s most successful movements led by which group?
265.x: The anti-arrack movement began in Dubagunta (Nellore) in 1991, led by rural women from the Aksharajyothi literacy classes, and is regarded as one of India's most successful women-led movements.
265.tq: Match the movement’s significance with its principal social constituency.
xs: The anti-arrack movement was led by **rural women** — option **(1)** is correct.
It is regarded as one of India's most successful **women-led movements**.
xa: The women came from **Aksharajyothi** adult-literacy classes.
Their methods: **broomsticks and chilli powder** to close shops and stop auctions.
Leader: **Vardhineni Rosamma** of **Dubagunta**, **Nellore**.

265.s: Which one of the following best expresses the broader significance of the social movements discussed in Andhra Pradesh?
o: They replaced all electoral politics with peasant organisations.
They were confined exclusively to urban industrial workers.
They shifted politics from a national-movement elite orientation towards caste, gender and class assertion.
They ended all political contestation based on caste and class.
265.x: These movements broadened the political arena from the national-movement elite towards caste, gender and class assertion through organisations such as Mahasabhas, MRPS and women’s anti-arrack groups.
265.tq: Select the option that captures the common political significance without using an absolute claim.
xs: The movements **shifted politics from a national-movement elite** orientation **towards caste, gender and class assertion** — option **(3)** is correct.
Examples: the **Mahasabhas**, the **MRPS** and the **anti-arrack women**.
xa: Debate: after **Mandal**, OBC and Dalit movements split over **sub-categorisation**.
The **1995** prohibition was later "**largely abandoned**".
**200th birth anniversary of Jyotirao Phule** commemorated on **11 April 2026**.

265.s: Which pair of movements influenced the Adi-Andhra leaders in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Bhu Poratam and Power Tariff Agitation
265.x: Phule’s Satyashodhak Samaj, founded in 1873, and Periyar’s Self-Respect Movement influenced the Adi-Andhra leaders.
265.tq: Match the ideological influences with the social movement they inspired.
xs: Phule's **Satyashodhak Samaj** (**1873**) and Periyar's **Self-Respect Movement** inspired AP's Adi-Andhra leaders — option **(1)** is correct.
**Bhu Poratam** (**2007**) and the **power tariff agitation** (**2000**) came long after the Adi-Andhra bodies.
xa: The **200th birth anniversary of Jyotirao Phule** was commemorated on **11 April 2026**.
Adi-Andhra leaders: **Bhagya Reddy Varma** (Machilipatnam, **1919**) and **Kusuma Dharmanna** (Vizianagaram, **1936**).
These bodies were the **precursors** of the Dalit movement.

265.s: Which statement correctly reflects a debate following the Mandal Commission period?
o: Sub-categorisation was rejected by every Dalit organisation.
All OBC and Dalit organisations merged into one movement.
The debate centred exclusively on prohibition in Andhra Pradesh.
OBC and Dalit movements split over the issue of sub-categorisation.
265.x: After Mandal, divisions emerged between OBC and Dalit movements over sub-categorisation.
265.tq: Identify the stated political consequence without extending it into an absolute claim.
xs: After **Mandal**, **OBC and Dalit movements split** over **sub-categorisation** — option **(4)** is correct.
They did not merge, and the debate was not about prohibition.
xa: Another debate: the **1995** prohibition was later "**largely abandoned**".
The movements shifted AP politics towards **caste, gender and class** assertion.
The **MRPS** is named among the bodies of this assertion.

266.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Organisation)
a. Andhra Mahila Sabha
b. Progressive Organisation of Women
c. Stree Shakti Sanghatana
d. Mahila Dakshata Samiti
List-II (Year)
i. 1978
ii. 1937
iii. 1990
iv. 1974
Choose the correct answer using the code given below.
266.x: Andhra Mahila Sabha was founded in 1937, POW in 1974, Stree Shakti Sanghatana in 1978 and Mahila Dakshata Samiti in 1990.
266.tq: Start from the sure year–organisation pair and eliminate codes containing inconsistent matches.
xs: Correct match **a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii** — option **(1)**.
**Andhra Mahila Sabha** — **1937**; **POW** — **1974**; **Stree Shakti Sanghatana** — **1978**; **Mahila Dakshata Samiti** — **1990**.
xa: Andhra Mahila Sabha founder: **Durgabai Deshmukh**.
Stree Shakti Sanghatana: **Vasantha Kannabiran**, **K. Lalita** and others, Hyderabad.
Mahila Dakshata Samiti: **Suman Krishnakant**, branches in **Vizag** and **Chittoor**.
⚠ **1964** = two Communist women's bodies after the CPI split.

266.s:
Consider the following statements about women's organisations in Andhra:
1. The Andhra Mahila Sabha was founded by Durgabai Deshmukh.
2. The Andhra Mahila Samakhya and the AP Mahila Sangham were two Communist bodies formed after the CPI split of 1964.
3. The first State women's Mahasabha was organised by Communist women in 1964.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
266.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the first State women's Mahasabha was organised by Communist women in 1947, not 1964. So A; B, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
266.tq: Two Communist dates: 1947 first Mahasabha, 1964 split into two bodies.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Andhra Mahila Sabha** was founded by **Durgabai Deshmukh** (**1937**).
Statement 2 is correct: **Andhra Mahila Samakhya** and **AP Mahila Sangham** were two Communist bodies after the **1964** CPI split.
Statement 3 is wrong: the first State women's **Mahasabha** was in **1947**, not 1964 — answer **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: **POW** (**1974**) was formed by radical-Left women activists in Hyderabad.
**Stree Shakti Sanghatana** (**1978**): **Vasantha Kannabiran** and **K. Lalita**.
Durgabai Deshmukh was the first chairperson of the **Central Social Welfare Board (1953)**.

266.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched?
1. Progressive Organisation of Women — Radical-Left women activists, Hyderabad — 1974
2. Stree Shakti Sanghatana — Vasantha Kannabiran and K. Lalita — 1978
3. Mahila Dakshata Samiti — Suman Krishnakant — 1990
4. Abhyudaya Mahila Samstha — Malladi Subbamma — family counselling
Select the correct answer using the code below.
266.x: All four pairings are correct. Abhyudaya Mahila Samstha was associated with family counselling and Malladi Subbamma; no year is specified for it.
266.tq: Verify each organisation against its activist base, founder or activity before selecting the complete combination.
xs: Pair 1 is correct: **POW** — radical-Left women, Hyderabad — **1974**.
Pair 2 is correct: **Stree Shakti Sanghatana** — **Vasantha Kannabiran** and **K. Lalita** — **1978**.

Pairs 3 and 4 are correct: **Mahila Dakshata Samiti** — **Suman Krishnakant** (**1990**); **Abhyudaya Mahila Samstha** — **Malladi Subbamma**, family counselling — answer **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
xa: Mahila Dakshata Samiti had branches in **Vizag** and **Chittoor**.
**Andhra Mahila Sabha**: **Durgabai Deshmukh**, **1937**.
The first State women's **Mahasabha** was held by Communist women in **1947**.

266.s: Who was the editor of the Telugu feminist magazine Bhumika, founded in 1993?
266.x: Bhumika was founded in 1993 and its editor was Kondaveeti Satyavathi.
266.tq: Distinguish a journal’s editor from activists, reformers and political leaders listed in the same field.
xs: **Bhumika** (**1993**) was edited by **Kondaveeti Satyavathi** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Kandukuri Veeresalingam** ran the earlier journals **Janana** and **Satihita Bodhini**; **Pratibha Bharati** was the first woman Speaker; **Vasantha Kannabiran** co-founded Stree Shakti Sanghatana.
xa: Bhumika is a **Telugu feminist magazine**.
Veeresalingam's journals promoted **women's education** and **widow remarriage**.
Feminist bodies of the time: **POW (1974)**, **Stree Shakti Sanghatana (1978)**.

266.s: Which of the following statements about earlier feminist publishing and reform is correct?
o: Satihita Bodhini was an SHG federation started in 2000.
Bhumika was founded by Kandukuri Veeresalingam in 1883.
Janana and Satihita Bodhini were associated with Kandukuri Veeresalingam and promoted women’s education and widow remarriage.
Janana was the official journal of the Central Social Welfare Board.
266.x: Kandukuri Veeresalingam’s Janana and Satihita Bodhini promoted women’s education and widow remarriage. Bhumika was a later Telugu feminist magazine founded in 1993.
266.tq: Reject the wrongly dated or wrongly attributed journal by checking the reformer–publication association.
xs: **Janana and Satihita Bodhini** were **Kandukuri Veeresalingam's** journals and **promoted women's education and widow remarriage** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Bhumika** was founded in **1993**, edited by **Kondaveeti Satyavathi** — not by Veeresalingam.
xa: Veeresalingam's journals are the **earlier model** of feminist publishing.
The **Central Social Welfare Board** (**1953**) had **Durgabai Deshmukh** as its first chairperson.
SHG economics in AP: **DWCRA** and **IKP**.

266.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Durgabai Deshmukh was the first chairperson of the Central Social Welfare Board, in 1953.
2. Sharda Mukherjee became the first woman Governor of Andhra Pradesh in 1999.
3. The Hindu Succession (AP Amendment) Act came before Andhra Pradesh got its first woman Speaker of the Legislative Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
266.x: Statement 1 is correct (1953). Statement 2 is wrong: Sharda Mukherjee became Governor in 1977; 1999 is the year Pratibha Bharati became the first woman Speaker. Statement 3 is correct: the Act is of 1986, the first woman Speaker came in 1999. So B; A, C and D include the wrong statement 2.
266.tq: Order: CSWB 1953, Governor 1977, AP Act 1986, Speaker 1999.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Durgabai Deshmukh** was the first chairperson of the **Central Social Welfare Board (1953)**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Sharda Mukherjee** became the first woman Governor of AP in **1977**, not 1999.
Statement 3 is correct: the **Hindu Succession (AP Amendment) Act** is of **1986**; the first woman Speaker came in **1999** — answer **1 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **Pratibha Bharati** was the first woman **Speaker** of the AP Assembly (**1999**).
The **1986** AP Act gave daughters **coparcenary rights** — well before the Central amendment of **2005**.
Durgabai Deshmukh also founded the **Andhra Mahila Sabha** (**1937**).

266.s: Pratibha Bharati became the first woman Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly in which year?
266.x: Pratibha Bharati became the first woman Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly in 1999.
266.tq: Use chronological discrimination among the years of women’s political milestones.
xs: **Pratibha Bharati** became the first woman **Speaker of the AP Legislative Assembly** in **1999** — option **(3)** is correct.
**1977** = **Sharda Mukherjee**, first woman Governor; **1986** = Hindu Succession (AP Amendment) Act; **2005** = the Central amendment.
xa: **Durgabai Deshmukh**: first chairperson of the **Central Social Welfare Board (1953)**.
**Muthulakshmi Reddy** campaigned against **Devadasi** dedication.
**Ammannaraja** moved the **1937** anti-dedication bill in the Madras Assembly.

266.s:
Consider the following pairs of law and year:
1. Madras Devadasis (Prevention of Dedication) Act - 1947
2. AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act - 1988
3. Dowry Prohibition Act - 1988
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
266.x: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct: the Madras Act is of 1947 and the AP Devadasis Act of 1988. Pair 3 is wrong: the Dowry Prohibition Act is of 1961. So A; B, C and D include the wrong pair 3.
xs: Pair 1 is correct: **Madras Devadasis (Prevention of Dedication) Act** — **1947**.
Pair 2 is correct: **AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act** — **1988**.
Pair 3 is wrong: the **Dowry Prohibition Act** is of **1961** — answer **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: NCRB **2023**: about **15,000 dowry cases** and **6,100 dowry deaths**.
**Ammannaraja's** **1937** anti-dedication bill followed **Muthulakshmi Reddy's** campaign.
The **1919 Machilipatnam** Adi-Andhra conference demanded abolition of the **Jogini and Devadasi** systems.

266.s: The 1919 Machilipatnam Adi-Andhra conference demanded the abolition of which systems?
266.x: The 1919 Machilipatnam Adi-Andhra conference, associated with Bhagya Reddy Varma, demanded abolition of the Jogini and Devadasi systems.
266.tq: Link a conference with its specific reform demand rather than with later legislation.
xs: The **1919 Machilipatnam** Adi-Andhra conference demanded abolition of the **Jogini and Devadasi systems** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was led by **Bhagya Reddy Varma**.
xa: **Muthulakshmi Reddy** campaigned against Devadasi dedication; **Ammannaraja** followed with a **1937** bill in the Madras Assembly.
Laws: **Madras Devadasis** Act (**1947**); **AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act** (**1988**).
⚠ Same **1919** conference, two names: **Bhagya Reddy Varma** led it, at **Machilipatnam**.

266.s: Which sequence correctly reflects the background to Devadasi abolition efforts?
o: Muthulakshmi Reddy’s campaign, followed by Ammannaraja’s 1937 anti-dedication bill in the Madras Assembly
Ammannaraja’s campaign, followed by Muthulakshmi Reddy’s 1947 bill in Andhra Pradesh
The 1988 AP Act, followed by the 1919 Machilipatnam conference
The 1961 Dowry Prohibition Act, followed by the 1937 anti-dedication bill
266.x: Muthulakshmi Reddy’s campaign was followed by Ammannaraja’s 1937 anti-dedication bill in the Madras Assembly.
266.tq: Track the reform campaign and bill in sequence, while rejecting reversed dates and jurisdictions.
xs: **Muthulakshmi Reddy's** campaign was followed by **Ammannaraja's 1937 anti-dedication bill in the Madras Assembly** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **1919** Machilipatnam conference came long before the **1988** AP Act, and the **1937** bill came before the **1961** Dowry Act — so options (3) and (4) reverse the order.
xa: **Madras Devadasis (Prevention of Dedication) Act**: **1947**.
**AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act**: **1988**.
**Bhagya Reddy Varma's** **1919** conference demanded abolition of the **Jogini and Devadasi** systems.

266.s: Which of the following figures was recorded by NCRB for dowry cases and dowry deaths in 2023?
o: About 6,100 dowry cases and 15,000 dowry deaths
About 15,000 dowry cases and 4,41,534 dowry deaths
About 4,41,534 dowry cases and 15,000 dowry deaths
About 15,000 dowry cases and 6,100 dowry deaths
266.x: NCRB recorded about 15,000 dowry cases and 6,100 dowry deaths in 2023.
266.tq: Do not reverse paired statistics; match each figure with its correct category.
xs: NCRB recorded **about 15,000 dowry cases and 6,100 dowry deaths** in **2023** — option **(4)** is correct.
**4,41,534** is the NCRB figure for total **crimes against women** in **2024**, not dowry.
xa: The **Dowry Prohibition Act** dates from **1961**.
⚠ Don't swap the two: cases (**15,000**) > deaths (**6,100**).
AP's **181 Women Helpline** has run since **2016**.

266.s: What was the principal significance of the Hindu Succession (AP Amendment) Act, 1986?
o: It reserved one-third of Assembly seats for women.
It established the Central Social Welfare Board.
It abolished the Devadasi system in Andhra Pradesh.
It gave daughters coparcenary rights in joint family property.
266.x: The 1986 Andhra Pradesh amendment gave daughters coparcenary rights in joint family property, well before the Central amendment of 2005.
266.tq: Match a legislation with its precise legal effect and distinguish it from reservation laws.
xs: The **Hindu Succession (AP Amendment) Act, 1986** **gave daughters coparcenary rights in joint family property** — option **(4)** is correct.
One-third reservation came from the **73rd and 74th Amendments (1992)**, for local bodies, not Assemblies; the Devadasi system was dealt with by the **1988** AP Act.
xa: ⚠ AP acted in **1986** — well before the Central amendment of **2005**.
The **Central Social Welfare Board** dates from **1953** (first chairperson **Durgabai Deshmukh**).
The first woman Speaker of the AP Assembly, **Pratibha Bharati**, came in **1999**.

266.s:
Consider the following statements about women's reservation in local bodies:
1. The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments were enacted in 1992.
2. Article 243D(3) reserves at least one-third of seats for women in Municipalities, and Article 243T does so in Panchayats.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
266.x: Statement 1 is correct: both amendments date from 1992. Statement 2 is wrong because it reverses the Articles: 243D(3) covers Panchayats and 243T covers Municipalities. So 1 only; B, C and D accept the reversed Articles or reject the 1992 date.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **73rd and 74th Amendments** were enacted in **1992**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it reverses the Articles — **Art. 243D(3)** covers **Panchayats** and **Art. 243T** covers **Municipalities** — answer **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: They reserve **at least one-third** of seats for women.
The **Constitution (131st) Amendment Bill, 2026** on women's reservation was **defeated** in **April 2026**.
As of **Aug 2026**, the women's reservation Act is still not in force — tied to **delimitation**.

266.s: What happened to the Constitution (131st) Amendment Bill, 2026, which sought to accelerate implementation of women’s reservation by redistributing Lok Sabha seats?
o: It was referred to the Central Social Welfare Board.
It was withdrawn after the 73rd Amendment.
266.x: The Constitution (131st) Amendment Bill, 2026 was defeated in April 2026.
266.tq: Test the fate and purpose of a recent constitutional proposal without confusing it with an enacted amendment.
xs: The **Constitution (131st) Amendment Bill, 2026** was **defeated in April 2026** — option **(3)** is correct.
It sought to speed up women's reservation by **redistributing Lok Sabha seats**.
xa: As of **Aug 2026**, the women's reservation Act is still not in force — tied to **delimitation**.
Local bodies already have **one-third** reservation via the **73rd and 74th Amendments (1992)**.
**Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan** (**Jun 2026**) builds leadership of women elected representatives.

266.s: Which sequence best represents the broad evolution of the women’s movement in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Reform bodies, Left and autonomous groups, mass action, SHG economics
SHG economics, reform bodies, mass action, princely-state administration
Mass action, constitutional courts, reform bodies, military organisations
Autonomous groups, colonial administration, SHG economics, reform bodies
266.x: The movement moved from reform bodies such as Andhra Mahila Sabha to Left and autonomous groups, then to mass action such as Anti-arrack and SHG-based economic activity.
266.tq: Arrange movements by their broad institutional and social progression rather than by isolated dates.
xs: The evolution was **reform bodies** → **Left and autonomous groups** → **mass action** → **SHG economics** — option **(1)** is correct.
Reform body: **Andhra Mahila Sabha**; Left/autonomous: **POW**, **Stree Shakti Sanghatana**; mass action: **anti-arrack**; SHG: **DWCRA**, **IKP**.
xa: Andhra Mahila Sabha: **Durgabai Deshmukh**, **1937**.
POW: **1974**; Stree Shakti Sanghatana: **1978**.
SHG economics in AP is represented by **DWCRA** and **IKP**.

266.s: Which initiative was launched to build the leadership skills of women elected representatives?
266.x: Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan was launched to build leadership skills among women elected representatives.
266.tq: Match a programme with its stated target group and purpose.
xs: **Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan** was launched to build the leadership skills of **women elected representatives** (**Jun 2026**) — option **(3)** is correct.
**Mahila Dakshata Samiti** is a women's body (**Suman Krishnakant**, **1990**); **Aksharajyothi** was the adult-literacy programme behind the anti-arrack movement.
xa: Women's-quota implementation was still disputed in **Aug 2026**.
**73rd and 74th Amendments (1992)** reserved at least **one-third** of local-body seats for women.
AP: **One Stop Centres** in all **26 districts** (**22,692** cases handled).

266.s:
Which of the following statements about women-oriented support services in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
1. One Stop Centres function in all 26 districts.
2. The 181 Women Helpline has operated since 2016.
3. Andhra Pradesh has 28 Shakti Sadans.
4. Beti Bachao Beti Padhao covers all 26 districts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
266.x: All four statements are correct: One Stop Centres cover all 26 districts, the 181 helpline has run since 2016, there are 28 Shakti Sadans, and BBBP covers all 26 districts.
266.tq: Check each numerical coverage claim before choosing the complete combination.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: **One Stop Centres** in all **26 districts**; **181 Women Helpline** since **2016**.
Statements 3 and 4 are correct: **28 Shakti Sadans**; **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao** covers all **26 districts** — answer **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
xa: One Stop Centres have handled **22,692** cases (APSES **2024-25**).
⚠ **Trap:** APSES dates BBBP from **2006**; the scheme was launched in **2015**.
**Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan** (**Jun 2026**) trains women elected representatives.

266.s: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, which now covers all 26 districts of Andhra Pradesh, was launched in
266.x: BBBP was launched in 2015. The AP Socio-Economic Survey wrongly dates it from 2006 - the exam trap. 2011 is a Census year and 2016 is when the 181 Women Helpline began in AP.
xs: **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao** was launched in **2015** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **Trap:** the AP Socio-Economic Survey (APSES) dates it from **2006**.
**2016** is when AP's **181 Women Helpline** began.
xa: BBBP covers all **26 districts** of AP.
AP has **28 Shakti Sadans**.
**One Stop Centres** in all 26 districts have handled **22,692** cases.

267.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Nataka Vidyalayam of the Andhra Nataka Kala Parishad was set up at Vijayawada in 1964 for training in drama.
2. The International Telugu Institute was established in 1975.
3. Ravindra Bharathi, Hyderabad, was built in 1961 for Gandhi's birth centenary.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
267.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Ravindra Bharathi (1961) was built for Tagore's birth centenary, not Gandhi's. So A; B, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
267.tq: Ravindra Bharathi = Rabindranath Tagore centenary, 1961.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Nataka Vidyalayam** (Andhra Nataka Kala Parishad) opened at **Vijayawada** on **1 August 1964** for drama training.
Statement 2 is correct: the **International Telugu Institute** dates from **1975**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Ravindra Bharathi** (**1961**) was built for **Tagore's** birth centenary, not Gandhi's — answer **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: ⚠ Ravindra Bharathi's inaugurator: **APPSC G2 2017 key** gives **Dr S. Radhakrishnan**; a PYQ book gives **Jawaharlal Nehru** — follow the official key.
**AP Sahitya Akademi** was set up in **1957**.
**1975** is also the year of the **first World Telugu Conference** at **Hyderabad**.

267.s:
With reference to national cultural academies, consider the following statements:
1. Sangeet Natak Akademi was the first national arts academy.
2. Sangeet Natak Akademi was inaugurated by Rajendra Prasad.
3. Sahitya Akademi is a statutory body.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
267.x: Sangeet Natak Akademi was the first national arts academy and was inaugurated by Rajendra Prasad. Sahitya Akademi was established as a society, not as a statutory body.
267.tq: Identify the false institutional-status statement before using the coded options.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Sangeet Natak Akademi** was the **first national arts academy**.
Statement 2 is correct: it was inaugurated by **Rajendra Prasad** on **28 January 1953**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Sahitya Akademi** is a **society, not statutory** — answer **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Sahitya Akademi was set up in **1952** but inaugurated on **12 March 1954**.
**Lalit Kala Akademi**: **1954**.
⚠ The State-level **AP Sahitya Akademi** came in **1957**.

267.s:
Arrange the following national cultural institutions in chronological order of their establishment or setting up:
A. Lalit Kala Akademi
B. Sahitya Akademi
C. Sangeet Natak Akademi
D. Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University
267.x: The Sahitya Akademi was set up in 1952, Sangeet Natak Akademi in 1953, Lalit Kala Akademi in 1954, and Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University in 1985.
267.tq: Fix the earliest and latest institutions first, then distinguish the middle years.
xs: Correct order **B, C, A, D** — option **(1)**.
**Sahitya Akademi** set up **1952** → **Sangeet Natak Akademi** **1953** → **Lalit Kala Akademi** **1954** → **Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University** **1985**.
xa: ⚠ Sahitya Akademi was set up in **1952** but inaugurated only on **12 March 1954**.
Sangeet Natak Akademi was inaugurated by **Rajendra Prasad**.
The Telugu University absorbed the **State akademis** and the **International Telugu Institute**.

267.s: In 1985, the State akademis were merged into which institution by the NTR Government?
267.x: In 1985, the NTR Government merged the State akademis into the newly established Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University.
267.tq: Identify the institution created through restructuring rather than the pre-existing cultural bodies.
xs: The **NTR** government merged the State akademis into the new **Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University** (**1985**) — option **(2)** is correct.
It also absorbed the **International Telugu Institute** (**1975**); **Ravindra Bharathi** is an auditorium (**1961**) and **Sangeet Natak Akademi** a national body.
xa: **AP Sahitya Akademi** (**1957**) promoted Telugu literature, translation and awards.
**Nataka Vidyalayam**, Vijayawada: **1 August 1964**.
The International Telugu Institute is an **APPSC 2019** key.

267.s: The Andhra Pradesh Sahitya Akademi, set up to promote Telugu literature, translation and awards, was established in
267.x: The AP Sahitya Akademi was set up in 1957. The national Sahitya Akademi was inaugurated in 1954; Ravindra Bharathi was built in 1961; the International Telugu Institute dates from 1975.
267.tq: AP Sahitya Akademi 1957; merged into Telugu University 1985.
xs: The **AP Sahitya Akademi** was set up in **1957** — option **(2)** is correct (PYQ).
**1954** = national Sahitya Akademi inaugurated; **1961** = Ravindra Bharathi; **1975** = International Telugu Institute.
xa: ⚠ Sahitya Akademi: set up **1952**, inaugurated **1954**; AP Sahitya Akademi = **1957**.
In **1985** the NTR government merged the State akademis into the **Telugu University**.
The national **Sahitya Akademi** is a **society**, not a statutory body.

267.s: According to the official APPSC Group 2 (2017) answer key, Ravindra Bharathi in Hyderabad was inaugurated by
267.x: The APPSC G2 2017 key gives Dr S. Radhakrishnan; an AP History PYQ book gives Jawaharlal Nehru, but the official key is followed. Rajendra Prasad inaugurated the Sangeet Natak Akademi; the hall was built for Tagore's birth centenary (1961), not opened by him.
267.tq: Ravindra Bharathi (1961): follow APPSC key = Radhakrishnan, not Nehru.
xs: The official **APPSC G2 2017** key gives **Dr S. Radhakrishnan** — option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ The AP History PYQ book gives **Jawaharlal Nehru**; follow the official key.
**Rajendra Prasad** inaugurated the **Sangeet Natak Akademi**; the hall honours **Tagore's** birth centenary.
xa: Ravindra Bharathi, **Hyderabad**, dates from **1961**.
Sangeet Natak Akademi was inaugurated on **28 January 1953**.
The **International Telugu Institute** came in **1975**.

267.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Conference)
A. First World Telugu Conference
B. Second World Telugu Conference
C. Third World Telugu Conference
D. Fourth World Telugu Conference

List-II (Venue)
1. Tirupati
2. Mauritius
3. Hyderabad
4. Kuala Lumpur

Choose the correct answer using the code below:
267.x: The First Conference was held at Hyderabad, the Second at Kuala Lumpur, the Third in Mauritius and the Fourth at Tirupati.
267.tq: Start from the sure venue of the First Conference and complete the one-to-one matching.
xs: Correct match **A-3, B-4, C-2, D-1** — option **(1)**.
First — **Hyderabad** (**1975**); Second — **Kuala Lumpur** (**1981**); Third — **Mauritius** (**1990**); Fourth — **Tirupati** (**2012**).
xa: The first conference was called **Prapancha Telugu Mahasabhalu**.
Its year **1975** is asked repeatedly — also the year of the **International Telugu Institute**.
Kuala Lumpur is in **Malaysia**.

267.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Second World Telugu Conference — Kuala Lumpur, 1981
267.x: The Fourth World Telugu Conference was held at Tirupati in 2012, not at Vijayawada.
267.tq: Find the single altered venue while retaining the correct year.
xs: **Fourth World Telugu Conference — Vijayawada, 2012** is NOT correct: it was held at **Tirupati** — option **(1)**.
The other pairs are correct: Third — **Mauritius, 1990**; Second — **Kuala Lumpur, 1981**; First — **Hyderabad, 1975**.
xa: First conference = **Prapancha Telugu Mahasabhalu**.
**1975** = first conference **and** the International Telugu Institute.
A new **Telugu Mahotsavam** is to be held **annually** (announced **July 2026**).

267.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. International Telugu Institute — 1975
2. Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University — 1985
3. Ravindra Bharathi — 1961

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
267.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. The International Telugu Institute was established in 1975, Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University in 1985, and Ravindra Bharathi in 1961.
267.tq: Check each institution against its establishment year before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Pair 1 is correct: **International Telugu Institute** — **1975**.
Pair 2 is correct: **Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University** — **1985**.
Pair 3 is correct: **Ravindra Bharathi** — **1961** — answer **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: The Telugu University absorbed the State akademis and the **International Telugu Institute**.
Ravindra Bharathi was built for **Tagore's** birth centenary.
**AP Sahitya Akademi**: **1957**.

267.s:
Match the following newspapers with their founders:

A. Andhra Jyothi
B. Eenadu
C. Udayam
D. Sakshi

1. Ramoji Rao
2. Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy
3. K.L.N. Prasad
4. Dasari Narayana Rao

Choose the correct answer using the code below:
267.x: Andhra Jyothi was founded by K.L.N. Prasad, Eenadu by Ramoji Rao, Udayam by Dasari Narayana Rao and Sakshi by Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy.
267.tq: Use the founder–newspaper pair as the anchor and reject swapped-founder options.
xs: Correct match **A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2** — option **(1)**.
**Andhra Jyothi** — **K.L.N. Prasad**; **Eenadu** — **Ramoji Rao**; **Udayam** — **Dasari Narayana Rao**; **Sakshi** — **Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy**.
xa: Years: Andhra Jyothi **1960**, Eenadu **1974** (Visakhapatnam), Udayam **1984**, Sakshi **2008**.
⚠ FIRST communist Telugu journal = **Prajasakti**; FIRST after Independence = **Jaya Bharat**.
Pre-1956: **Kasinadhuni Nageswara Rao's** **Andhra Patrika** and **Bharati (1924)**.

267.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Jyothi was launched in 1960.
2. Eenadu was launched from Visakhapatnam in 1974.
3. Sakshi was launched in 2008.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
267.x: All three statements are correct. Andhra Jyothi was launched in 1960, Eenadu in Visakhapatnam in 1974, and Sakshi in 2008.
267.tq: Verify the newspaper year and, where given, the place of launch before choosing the code.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Andhra Jyothi** — **1960**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Eenadu** — **Visakhapatnam**, **1974**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Sakshi** — **2008** — answer **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: Founders: **K.L.N. Prasad** (Andhra Jyothi), **Ramoji Rao** (Eenadu), **Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy** (Sakshi).
**Udayam** (**1984**) was founded by **Dasari Narayana Rao**.
**Prajasakti** was the first communist Telugu journal.

267.s: Which of the following statements regarding early Telugu journals is correct?
o: Andhra Patrika was the first communist Telugu journal and Prajasakti was launched after Independence.
Prajasakti was the first communist Telugu journal and Jaya Bharat was the first Telugu journal after Independence.
Bharati was the first Telugu journal after Independence and Andhra Patrika was founded in 1956.
Jaya Bharat was founded before Independence and Bharati was the first communist Telugu journal.
267.x: Prajasakti was the first communist Telugu journal, and Jaya Bharat was the first Telugu journal after Independence. Andhra Patrika and Bharati (1924) were Kasinadhuni Nageswara Rao's pre-1956 publications, so the other options misattribute them.
267.tq: Distinguish the superlatives and historical sequence of the early Telugu journals.
xs: **Prajasakti** was the **first communist Telugu journal** and **Jaya Bharat** the **first Telugu journal after Independence** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Andhra Patrika** and **Bharati (1924)** were **Kasinadhuni Nageswara Rao's** pre-1956 publications — not communist, not post-Independence firsts.
xa: Post-1956 papers: **Andhra Jyothi (1960)**, **Eenadu (1974)**, **Udayam (1984)**, **Sakshi (2008)**.
**Eenadu** was launched from **Visakhapatnam** by **Ramoji Rao**.
⚠ FIRST communist = Prajasakti; FIRST after Independence = Jaya Bharat.

267.s: Rayaprolu Subbarao received the Sahitya Akademi Award for which work?
267.x: Rayaprolu Subbarao received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1965 for Misra Manjari.
267.tq: Match the author with the specific award-winning work rather than with a better-known Telugu title.
xs: **Rayaprolu Subbarao** won the **Sahitya Akademi** award in **1965** for **Misra Manjari** — option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ **Gabbilam** is **Gurram Jashuva's** work, and his award was **not** for Gabbilam (PYQ 2025).
xa: **Gurram Jashuva**: Sahitya Akademi **1964**; **Padma Bhushan 1970**; nominated **MLC 1964**.
Other awardees: **C. Narayana Reddy** and **Ravuri Bharadwaja**.
Sahitya Akademi Award now: **Rs 1 lakh**, **24 languages**.

267.s: At the Ugadi 2012 Telugu Velugu awards, who was associated with literature and who with painting, respectively?
267.x: C. Narayana Reddy received the Telugu Velugu award for literature, while Bapu received it for painting.
267.tq: Split the paired categories first, then assign the two personalities.
xs: At the **Telugu Velugu awards (Ugadi 2012)**, **C. Narayana Reddy** was honoured for **literature** and **Bapu** for **painting** — option **(1)** is correct.
Option (3) reverses the two; **Gurram Jashuva** and **Ravuri Bharadwaja** are other Sahitya Akademi names.
xa: C. Narayana Reddy is also a **Sahitya Akademi** awardee.
**Rayaprolu Subbarao**: Sahitya Akademi **1965** for **Misra Manjari**.
AP cultural awards (**Jul 2026**): **Ugadi Kala Ratna**, **Kandukuri**, **Telugu Language** and **Gurram Jashuva** awards.

267.s: The Sahitya Akademi Award currently carries which combination of languages and prize amount?
267.x: The Sahitya Akademi Award covers 24 languages—22 Eighth Schedule languages along with English and Rajasthani—and carries Rs 1 lakh.
267.tq: Distinguish the language count and prize amount from figures associated with other awards.
xs: The Sahitya Akademi Award now covers **24 languages** and carries **Rs 1 lakh** — option **(4)** is correct.
The 24 = **22** Eighth Schedule languages + **English** + **Rajasthani**.
**Rs 15 lakh** is the **Dadasaheb Phalke** prize money.
xa: The Sahitya Akademi was set up in **1952** and inaugurated on **12 March 1954**.
It is a **society**, not a statutory body.
Telugu winners: **Gurram Jashuva** (**1964**), **Rayaprolu Subbarao** (**1965**, Misra Manjari).

267.s:
Which of the following statements about Gurram Jashuva is correct?
1. He received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1964.
2. He received the Padma Bhushan in 1970.
3. Gabbilam received the Sahitya Akademi Award.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
267.x: Jashuva received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1964 and the Padma Bhushan in 1970. Gabbilam itself did not receive the Sahitya Akademi Award, making statement 3 false.
267.tq: Use the negative trap in the final statement to separate the poet’s award from the work’s award.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Gurram Jashuva** won the **Sahitya Akademi** award in **1964**.
Statement 2 is correct: he got the **Padma Bhushan** in **1970**.
Statement 3 is wrong: his award was **not** for **Gabbilam** (PYQ 2025 trap) — answer **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Jashuva was also a nominated **MLC** in **1964**.
⚠ **1964** = Nandi Awards instituted **and** Jashuva's Sahitya Akademi + MLC.
A **Gurram Jashuva award** is among AP's cultural awards (**Jul 2026**).

267.s: Which statement regarding the Nandi Awards is correct?
o: They are theatre awards instituted by the Government of India in 1969.
They are national literary awards instituted in 1952.
They are Andhra Pradesh Government awards for films, television and drama, instituted in 1964.
They are awards exclusively for Telugu newspapers, instituted in 1975.
267.x: Nandi Awards are Andhra Pradesh Government awards for films, television and drama, instituted in 1964.
267.tq: Use the awarding authority, fields and year together to reject swapped-award descriptions.
xs: The **Nandi Awards** are the **AP government's** awards for **films, TV and drama**, instituted in **1964** — option **(3)** is correct.
They are not central-government awards, not literary, and not for newspapers.
xa: The previous **YSRCP** government let the Nandi and **Kandukuri Veeresalingam** Awards lapse.
The coalition government announced revival of Nandi Awards and **Nandi Natakotsavams** (**Mar 2026**).
⚠ **1964** = Nandi Awards **and** Jashuva's Sahitya Akademi + MLC.

267.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the Telugu recipients of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award?
267.x: B.N. Reddy, Akkineni Nageswara Rao and K. Viswanath are among the Telugu recipients of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award. Dharmavaram Ramakrishnamacharyulu is associated with Telugu theatre, not this list of film awardees.
267.tq: Use the domain distinction between Telugu cinema awardees and theatre personalities.
xs: **Dharmavaram Ramakrishnamacharyulu** is NOT among the Telugu Phalke awardees — option **(1)** is correct.
Telugu awardees: **B.N. Reddy**, **L.V. Prasad**, **B. Nagi Reddy**, **Akkineni Nageswara Rao**, **D. Ramanaidu** and **K. Viswanath**.
xa: Phalke prize: **Swarna Kamal**, shawl + **Rs 15 lakh**.
The cash was raised from **Rs 10 lakh** in **2024**.
The State's own film awards are the **Nandi Awards** (**1964**).

267.s: Which of the following correctly reflects the recent position regarding Andhra Pradesh cultural awards and festivals?
o: The Telugu Language Awards were discontinued from 29 August.
The Kandukuri Awards and Nandi Awards were permanently abolished by the coalition government.
Nandi Natakotsavams were replaced exclusively by the National Theatre Festival.
The Kandukuri Awards were revived, while revival of Nandi Awards and Nandi Natakotsavams was announced.
267.x: The coalition government revived the Kandukuri Awards and announced the revival of the Nandi Awards and Nandi Natakotsavams. The previous government had allowed these awards or festivals to lapse.
267.tq: Track the change from lapse to revival and distinguish announcement from abolition.
xs: The coalition government **revived the Kandukuri Awards** and **announced revival of Nandi Awards and Nandi Natakotsavams** (**Mar 2026**) — option **(4)** is correct.
It was the previous **YSRCP** government that let the **Nandi** and **Kandukuri Veeresalingam** Awards lapse — they were not abolished by the coalition.
xa: Nandi Natakotsavams are to be revived "on a grand scale" (**27 Jul 2026**).
**Telugu Mahotsavam** is to be held **annually** (Minister **Kandula Durgesh**).
The **National Theatre Festival** is a separate Sangeet Natak Akademi event (**15 July 2026**).

267.s: The cash component of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award was raised in 2024 from ₹10 lakh to:
267.x: The cash prize was increased from ₹10 lakh to ₹15 lakh in 2024.
267.tq: Quantitative recall using nearby monetary values.
xs: The Phalke Award cash was raised from **Rs 10 lakh** to **Rs 15 lakh** in **2024** — option **(2)** is correct.
The award also carries a **Swarna Kamal** and a shawl.
xa: Telugu awardees: **B.N. Reddy**, **L.V. Prasad**, **B. Nagi Reddy**, **Akkineni Nageswara Rao**, **D. Ramanaidu**, **K. Viswanath**.
⚠ Don't confuse with the **Sahitya Akademi** award: **Rs 1 lakh**.
AP's own film/TV/drama awards: **Nandi Awards** (**1964**).

267.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the current cultural initiative?
o: National Theatre Festival — exclusively at one venue
Telugu Language Awards — to be held on 15 July
Telugu Mahotsavam — to be held annually
267.x: Telugu Mahotsavam was announced as an annual event. Telugu Language Awards are associated with 29 August, and the National Theatre Festival is being held across 150 locations.
267.tq: Separate the dates, scale and status of the different current cultural initiatives.
xs: **Telugu Mahotsavam — to be held annually** is correctly matched — option **(3)**.
The **National Theatre Festival** runs at **150** locations, not one venue; **Nandi Natakotsavams** are being revived, not discontinued.
xa: Telugu Mahotsavam was announced at **Undavalli Caves**, **July 2026**, by Minister **Kandula Durgesh**.
The National Theatre Festival (**15 July 2026**) marks **150 years** of **Vande Mataram**; two AP plays were selected.
Nandi Natakotsavams to be revived "on a grand scale" (**27 Jul 2026**).

267.s: Which one of the following is NOT listed among the Andhra Pradesh cultural awards?
267.x: Ugadi Kala Ratna, Kandukuri, Telugu Language and Gurram Jashuva awards are listed among Andhra Pradesh cultural awards. Lalit Kala Akademi is a national cultural academy, not one of the listed Andhra Pradesh awards.
267.tq: Distinguish a state award list from the name of a national academy.
xs: **Lalit Kala Akademi Award** is NOT among the listed AP cultural awards — option **(3)** is correct.
**Lalit Kala Akademi** (**1954**) is a **national** academy.
The AP awards (**Jul 2026**) are **Ugadi Kala Ratna**, **Kandukuri**, **Telugu Language** and **Gurram Jashuva** awards.
xa: The **Kandukuri Awards** were revived by the coalition government after lapsing under the **YSRCP** government.
The **Nandi Awards** (**1964**) are AP's film, TV and drama awards.
National akademis: Sahitya (**1952**), Sangeet Natak (**1953**), Lalit Kala (**1954**).

267.s: The announcements concerning Telugu Mahotsavam and the revival of Nandi Natakotsavams were associated with which Minister and location?
o: Abul Hasan Tana Shah at Kuchipudi village
267.x: The announcements were associated with Minister Kandula Durgesh and the Undavalli Caves location.
267.tq: Match the contemporary initiative with the responsible minister and reported location.
xs: The announcements were made by Minister **Kandula Durgesh** at **Undavalli Caves** — option **(1)** is correct.
They were made in **July 2026**.
xa: **Telugu Mahotsavam** is to be held **annually**.
Nandi Natakotsavams to be revived "on a grand scale" (**27 Jul 2026**).
The coalition government had already revived the **Kandukuri Awards**.

267.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the recent cultural initiatives in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Nandi Natakotsavams are proposed to be revived along with an annual Telugu Mahotsavam.
The initiatives concern only Kuchipudi and exclude folk forms.
Nandi Natakotsavams are proposed to be discontinued permanently.
The Telugu Mahotsavam is intended only for urban theatre groups.
267.x: Andhra Pradesh announced an annual Telugu Mahotsavam to revive several folk and theatre forms, and Nandi Natakotsavams are also proposed to be revived.
267.tq: Distinguish revival measures from discontinuation and identify the scope of the cultural programme.
xs: **Nandi Natakotsavams are proposed to be revived** along with an **annual Telugu Mahotsavam** — option **(1)** is correct.
The Natakotsavams are to be revived "on a grand scale" (**27 Jul 2026**) — not discontinued.
xa: Telugu Mahotsavam: announced at **Undavalli Caves**, **July 2026**, Minister **Kandula Durgesh**.
The **Nandi Awards** (films, TV, drama; **1964**) are also to be revived.
The previous **YSRCP** government had let the Nandi and Kandukuri Awards lapse.

267.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Theatre Festival of the Sangeet Natak Akademi:
1. It was scheduled for 15 July 2026.
2. It was planned across 150 locations.
3. Its theme was connected with 150 years of Vande Mataram.
4. Two plays from Andhra Pradesh were selected.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
267.x: All four statements are correct. The festival was scheduled for 15 July 2026 at 150 locations in connection with 150 years of Vande Mataram, with two Andhra Pradesh plays selected.
267.tq: Check the date, number of locations, commemorative theme and state representation independently.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the **Sangeet Natak Akademi** festival was set for **15 July 2026** at **150** locations.
